_childDocuments_.review: Umurangi Generation oozes personality.The game revolves around taking photographs using a quick to pick-up FPS control scheme. The tutorial is quirky and does a great job of getting you started, and the objectives are laid out clearly for you when you jump in. You unlock lenses and other features by completing objectives and progressing through the game. It doesn't force traditional photography rules like 'power of thirds' or anything like that so it's not too intimidating to get into. However, you could absolutely implement these rules into a casual playthrough and get a lot of extra fun out of it.Obviously, if your game revolves around photography you have to make sure the visuals are good, and this game delivers. No, you're not getting a super realistic high poly simulation with ray tracing, advanced hair physics and a 4D see it, smell it, breath it kind of experience. What you are getting is an incredibly stylish cel-shaded world and levels that compliment that technique - from urban city rooftops with red sunset skylines, to neon-lit edgy inner city night-time scenes. The developers have put their own humour into the art in the environments and it teases themes about troubles in the real world. Combining this with the 90's house / synthwave soundtrack gives the game a very underground 'f*** the system' kind of vibe.I don't have much bad to say about the game. Collision jumping onto things / hitting sloped objects can be a bit awkward but it's so minor that it's barely worth mentioning. You can stack jumps in quick succession before launching to get unintended height (think Doom Eternal speedruns) but I actually like this quirk, it doesn't affect normal gameplay whatsoever. For the aesthetic of the game, the replay value and the personality this game has, I would absolutely recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Umurangi Generation

_childDocuments_.review: Video:Text:The Photo Mode, a fun little distraction for the People who are stuck in a situation where they want to make good Pictures but lack the equipment or their surroundings are kind off…boring. It has been around for a while, enjoying growing popularity. My interest in it can be traced back to Alan Wake with it’s no HUD Option, which I highly recommend trying out. Now we’re getting titles exploring the Photography Part a bit more, dropping you in a Place with a Camera and tasking you to get certain pictures. This is also where Umurangi Generation falls into only stringing those Photo Ops together with a Narrative and an impressive Set of Options to make those Pictures look exactly like how you want them to. That alone is pretty impressive but is it enough to make this a compelling buy for 15 Bucks/12,50 Eurobucks?Umurangi Generation takes place in the Walled-of City of Tauranga, New Zealand, sometime after 2047. You’re an unnamed Courier, working for the Tauranga Express. Throughout the Game you will be send to various locations to complete Deliveries and take Pictures while you’re at it, as the Events, surrounding a Kaiju Situation, unfold around you. The Game takes the Route of only telling you the Story with the environment and Newspapers scattered around, meaning you actively have to look for the Story. While good for the most part and very fitting for a game about exploring Photography, I would have liked to get a Newspaper Print after a completed delivery, where you could see how the People get along with that whole Kaiju thing hanging over them and get a better picture of the world.The Visuals evoke a Neo-Noir Style. With Simplistic faces, jagged Models and an intentionally lower texture quality. It is a more unique Art-Style which has a very appealing quality to it. Sadly, the game isn’t optimized very well. In the more populated Areas, the framerate tends to go down very often, which can get one out of the experience. There is also a Problem with environmental Variety. If you prefer Landscapes besides the Concrete then sadly, you’re out of Luck as there are next to no Landscape Levels, you’re gonna have to live with Walls, Walls, Walls. This is something that DLC has to solve later on.As it is a Game about Photography you’re only Equipped with a Camera and are tasked with taking certain Pictures that include things like “2 Boomboxes” or “a Skull and a Knife”. How you want to take those pictures is up to you. Many of those tasks can be completed any way you see fit while some require a certain distance or a specific Lens when taking the Picture. On Top of that there are Bonus Objectives, like “Recreate this Postcard”, “Take a picture with all your Friends in it” or “Finish the Level within a 10 Minute Window”. Completing all these nets you new Equipment, like Lenses or Camera Upgrades to give your Pictures a new touch and make it easier for you to complete Objectives, so it’s recommended to go ahead and finish everything first before moving on which, with a constant 10 Minutes Limit for Delivery, kind-of becomes a Mad Dash, where you will have to throw away your Artistic Sense to reach all those Bonus Objectives in time. If you just want to run through everything you will also be done with all 9 Levels in about 2 Hours and be bored afterwards, so bringing in a Creative Potential is required for long term enjoyment as that ties to the game’s main selling point and it’s best feature. When you take a Picture, you can customize it with various filters that you unlock during the game, which open up the possibilities for your Pictures more and more. Soon your Pictures can turn from regular looking to out there experiences and that is when the fun begins.The Soundtrack itself is pretty damn good. The Composer, Youtuber ThorHighHeels under the Alias Adolf Nomura, made a very good Soundtrack that fits very well into the Style of the Game. The Main Issue lies with the Implementation of it. A couple of Songs have already been in other Albums of the Composer and sometimes don’t seem to fit well with the Scenario of the Level, giving it rather more of a Playlist-Feeling than adding to the Atmosphere. A longer custom-made Track with a Separate Option on subsequent visits would have helped out with giving that first Playthrough more of an oomph.Umurangi Generation is a game with heart and a solid game about Photography that I, as a Photo Mode Enthusiast, really enjoyed. It has some issues in terms of Variety and you should also be ready for the jank that comes with One-Man Development, which can get one out of the Flow but if you enjoy taking pictures and want to explore it with a set of Creative tools, Umurangi Generation is a recommendation at full Price. If you’re new to Photography or are still undecided you should try out the Demo first and see for yourself. But I want to say one thing:

_childDocuments_.review: I love it when games leave it up to the players to decide how much they want to engage with the underlying themes and the mechanics. On a basic level, you can just stroll through lively environments, complete bounties by shooting photos of some birds here or some plants and boomboxes there with varying lenses and listen to mellow alternative, jazzy hip hop and trip hop tunes. The next level is looking for those rare shots, squeezing in one more bird by slightly tilting the camera to fulfil the objective from an unusual vantage point or perspective, and colorgrading them to your liking and aesthetic vision afterwards. And the third and final level is engaging with the incredible story and concept told through visual cues, ephemera and underlying concepts, delving into the conflict at the heart of the game and drawing your own conclusions. And that's where Umurangi Generation is the most rewarding for me. Someone else might have a total different take on what makes the game fun and engagig. And that's the beauty of it all.

_childDocuments_.review: CHANGED TO NOT RECOMMENDED**Human vs Human gameplay = Sometimes fun, but frustration because of lack of control hurts the experience****Human vs CPU or human vs human gameplay on expert = Broken (You can't even swing at most shots coming at you, even if the ball is hit right next to you)**Here is some human vs human gameplay. Nadal vs Federer (I am Nadal) - This is on Very Hard difficulty**Some major problems exist with the gameplay**The give ups happen constantly even if you are within arms reach to hit the shot, this is an AO2 special, and just like on AO2, it happens when trying to return serves or return shots back during rallies. These are CANNED points, they are points that happen no matter what whether you anticipated properly or not, whether you his the button at the right time or not. You will also get consistently frustrated at not being able to make it to balls you should be able to get to, that you see players get to all the time in real life.Lack of control in a sports game, feeling helpless because of faulty core game mechanics, is what truly makes this game not recommended. The graphics are solid, the atmosphere/SFX are good, and the ball speed outside of expert mode makes sense...  but the constant being forced to give up really hurts the game. Also, the player foot speed not matching the ball speed, and being forced forward to hit the ball (Stabbing at it) when you are not intending to do so. If you are buying this game for local coop, local against, or to play the CPU on the lower levels, the game CAN be a fun at times. Looking to play online against other humans? Sure, that may be fun at times as well. But you also may have a negative experience more often than not, which is why I can't recommend the game at this time.On expert mode  (ether human vs human or human vs CPU), the game is broken. You can't even swing most of the time, your player with just stumble or not do anything at all when the ball is hit back to you. Expert level is broken, and I imagine that this could impact your play in the career mode. Human vs human on expert is also a nightmare in lack of control, as you are stuck giving up CONSTANTLY without even being given the chance to swing.*I also think the card system is not necessary, and gives players artificial boosts which compromise the integrity of the matches. This doesn't belong in a tennis game, and neither does pack opening. Going down this road is a slippery slope, and reminds me of the MyTeam/Ultimate team modes, and overall artificial boost gameplay (unbalanced, not skill based) with 2K and EA Sports games. These card systems and artificial boosts are ruining sports video games.*With that out of the way, I wanted to talk about some of the poor reviews on here where they talk about the ball speed being too fast, have you ever watched a real match? This is the best ball speed they have had since Top Spin 4, but the pace is actually better at times in TWT2. I say this when playing WITHOUT artificial boosts, human vs human, or human vs CPU on levels lower than expert.Devs: PLEASE do not patch the ball speed overall, it actually makes sense and gives the matches the action it should have. You need to fix expert difficulty, but the pace overall otherwise in human vs human and human vs cpu on lower levels is just fine. The player movement itself needs to be smoother and match the ball speed, giving the user the proper amount of control.Baseline play is overall solid when you are not being forced to give up or being forced to stab at the ball, but coming to the net could use some work. It feels sluggish and delayed trying to get to the net.There is an issue where when you play two players locally, your players never switch sides. I was one player, and I was ALWAYS on the bottom on the screen for every game. Even when I switched (pre match) to have player 2 be on the bottom, I was still on the bottom for the entirety of the match. This is something the developers will need to patch.This game feels more realistic, with better animations than AO2, and less being DRAGGED into different directions (Canned animations) than TWT1.However, lack of control, feeling of helplessness makes the consumer not want to play again. When frustration overrides fun, it is time to put the game down.I wish this game had the player creation/sharing feature of AO2, but I may try to mod the game (Wish me luck). I also recommend the game more for human vs human, or human vs cpu on the lower levels, NOT for those who want to play on expert right away, because right now that difficulty is broken.I have been playing tennis video games, and watching tennis since the early 90s. I have most of the tennis games ever made (From Super Tennis, to Grand Slam Tennis, to all the Top Spins, Virtua Tennis, etc). It's troubling to me that tennis games a decade and more older have far better feel on the sticks, more control for the user, giving the user a far better experience and sense of true competition.The developers need to focus on giving the user CONTROL. Until that happens, this review will remain not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Better than the reviews suggest by far, however they are somewhat accurate in their complaints, and I think some dev work on it could help improve it. Even as-is I think it's good as a tennis game past the initial hump, and as a game in general I think it's passable.Specific points: 1. "I can never release the button at the right time, it's random!" The timing mechanic is difficult to grasp, because it is "release a button 'at the right time'" ..with not enough feedback on when the 'right time' really is, because it depends on the specific animation picked - so how close you are to the shot, how fast it is, how far up you'll contact the ball, etc. Personally, I think a tutorial mode/tennis school mode where there is some direct feedback like a glow/shading at the right time to let go would work; think of it as a coach talking you through it and practicing the drill in this mode.I have seen people get it in a single session, becoming suddenly experts at hitting the right timing. But it took me literally 6+ hours before I started getting it somewhat consistently, and by the point I write this I tend to hit 90+% of my shots good or perfect (except volleys which I almost never get to practice). It was frustrating and I did consider dropping the game a couple times. No workaround for players I can think of beyond just trying to lower your expectations for 3-5 matches and trying your best to just hit the right timing on every ball and not caring about losing during that.2. "It's like my player doesn't even try to hit the ball, he just gives up!"There's two input phases: movement and swinging, and there isn't enough feedback on when one ends and the other one starts. Secondary to that, while moving you use the same stick/movement buttons to move in a direction.. that you also use to aim while swinging. Seeing as how tennis is a lot of running left in order to then hit it to the right, if you can't figure out early when the movement phase is over and you're now mid-swing, then you have a very short amount of time to move the stick to the other direction and also work on your timing. Even with how much I've played, I can't tell exactly what triggers the swing phase to start exactly (seems to be distance from the point at which the ball would enter your strike zone - so if you run towards where the ball hits the ground, you won't start swinging because there's no way to pick it up so low except a weird half-volley - however it seems to depend on the animations it COULD choose, so for example volleys are harder to trigger because there's fewer animations it could use and less time for it to trigger in), but I only rarely mis-step now.Personally, I can't think of a good solution to this. More variety in the animations, especially around the situations that have little time to react like volleys or shots aimed straight at the player/that need the player to stretch for it, would mitigate it a bit if they become a bit more likely to trigger early? I think it's not bad enough as is to be a problem if you adjust your tactics a bit, step back well behind the baseline more to give yourself room, and accept that some balls you'll just not be able to grab (as happens in real life).This was the main reason I kept messing up in Career mode, as it seemed I could win receiving games consistently once #1 was done, but I kept losing my service games...because after serving I wasn't stepping back behind the baseline to give myself time.. and because I wasn't trying to run right to the ball (through the animation start) because I would start aiming too early (usually before the animation started) meaning I just stepped the wrong way from the ball.. even though I wasn't intending on moving, but instead aiming. As a workaround to the players, play 3-5 games where you won't charge any shots and hit "precision" shots instead where you just tap the button at the right time and don't worry about aiming initially. You should start seeing when the animation is starting (and locks you in) and you can start aiming then, instead of worrying about holding the right shot button down to charge it early while also moving/aiming and timing.3. "Shot choice is boring/simple", "Career is boring", "Impossible to do aces", "Unbalanced", "Cards are dumb/boring/not realistic" etc.These are likely fair criticisms to some extent or another. Some seem bugs, some seem areas where they haven't invested a lot of effort into, and some are just game design that doesn't mesh with everyone. The bugs hopefully should get fixed, and if not then at least they're not terribly disruptive. I don't think any of them are likely to apply to a majority of people as actual negatives, so just watch some gameplay of it and see if you agree with them or not, then skip the game if so.

_childDocuments_.review: My first look/overview can be found hereHaving only played for just over an hour, I have to say there was more I disliked than enjoyed about the game. The game seems to want to force your player into animations even if you don't press a button. This combined with the timing elements of shots means it's impossible to get into a rhythm.  As an example, if you tap the button you do a weaker more accurate shot, if you hold down the button you do a more powerful shot. The key to this is timing. However, because the animation of your swing can begin before you press a button it often makes you react. Forcing you to press the button before you expected or release later than you wanted. I have no doubt with some practice you could overcome this issue. Playing as a created player with low stats means you either hit the ball out or hit the net unless you get the timing right, whereas the better players can compensate for the bad timing with there stats. This makes the career mode a real chore until you have played much more to learn the timing. Hard work will most likely pay off here. Lastly, the game features a card mechanic, it seems to be bolted in to offer a way to make money. Giving stat boost or weakening opposition. Because it's so strange I cannot help feeling this has been added as a cash grab. Additionally, the devs sent me a key for a legends pack and official tournaments and stadiums which stings a bit if you were required to buy these to get the realism that should be in the base gameadditionally some gameplay from the legendary players can be found here

_childDocuments_.review: This game was just okay. Although I don't have that much time on the game, I will try to give the most in-depth review that I can based on some of the things that I saw while playing it. Most of these will be comparisons to Topspin 4 but hope this helps for people that may be on the fence. Pros-Forehand and two handed backhand groundstrokes look good and the developers did a great job with the actual players animation.Volleys are much smoother than topspin and is a big upgrade in my opinion.The game plays much quicker than topspin 4 which makes it feel more realistic.Has a lot of the current players to pick through so you can play with the modern young players.Cons-The one handed backhand animation is not realistic and you can abuse the short angle shot that drifts off the court to hit a winner about any time. Non existent backhand slice animation (It looks like you are just blocking the ball at the baseline).Player occasionally will not even try to hit a ball that is coming right at him/her.Should be aces out wide on the deuce side come back almost unreturnable from the CPU.You can abuse the movement by stopping and sprinting to change direction instantly. Not fully licensed.No Djokovic.Clunky movement on clay. Doesn't really feel like you're on clay. NeutralTiming is much different than topspin 4. Just something that you'll have to adjust to but neither a good or bad thing. Very hard to ace someone even if you hit the line down the T or out wide. Just means you'll be forced to win more rallies. Playing on expert, you will get aced quite a bit at first but it's enjoyable that you have to actually read the player to guess their serve. Although this game was not my favorite, it was not as bad as some people make it out to be. It's not unplayable but for the price that it is, it wasn't a good enough game to warrant me keeping it. If you are a hardcore tennis fan that needs their tennis video game fix, then this game will work and you'll have fun along with a little bit of frustration. If you are on the fence I would say try it out and if not for you then refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: Initial Impression - A joyless career mode that I'm just not having any fun playing.I am actually a big fan of AO by the same devs, and even got a little bit of fun out of the patched up TWT... but this feels joyless - such a shame as I really wanted to like it. Technically it's far better at launch that TWT (not hard I know) but even then, I've had one crash to desktop in 90 mins played. I can see remnants of the AO player creator but its a cut down experience with less flexibility and customisation options. Some of the AI opponents look terrible in close ups - not just dodgy shadows but deformed faces. However, the overall look of the game is OK from the game play camera and general presentation is good. Its the career mode that's killing the game for me - this game requires very precise timing which is made worse by your players initially very low stats. The animations also seem a little out of sync with the button presses, making learning the timing even harder. Thus even on easy modes, every shot has to be perfect to have any chance of winning and gaining xp and gold to upgrade... meaning it throws you into a terrible grind from the first match. Losing constantly as you learn how to play is not fun and strangely, not something I experienced with TWT or either AO game. Unless some sort of balance patch is coming, I'm struggling to find the will to carry on playing / improve my timing for a game where the core game mode is not really fun to play at even the lowest settings. Happy to update this review if the timing starts to 'click' once my player stats have improved or its patched but at the moment, its a thumbs down for me from a game play / fun perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: I will add to my review as they are having a sale now. That's all.The following is my original review, on October 3, 2020.-------If you're looking for a "", I wouldn't recommend this game. Possibly, it will get a drastic update and get better, but at this time (October 2, 2020), it won't satisfy you. Right now, it's more of an outrageous rhythm game, than a tennis simulator.Watch a video of someone playing this game on YouTube or something else. 10 minutes is better than 5 minutes, and 20 minutes is better than 10 minutes. And if you don't feel strange with the way this game behaves, then congratulations, you deserve to keep thinking. On the other hand, if you feel strange, you should not buy it.- - -There are numerous complaints about this game in my 11 hours of play. I will focus on 3 of them here.* The use of words in this text *player = a player of the video gameathlete = a tennis player in a screen- - -This is something that has particularly bothered me. There are frequently times when an athlete's racket swing and the trajectory of the ball being hit out is clearly incorrect. For example: a heavy-topspin-ball like Nadal, from a slice swing. And a very powerful shot like Del Potro, from just barely touch the ball.The point is, you can't anticipate the ball by looking at the stance of the swing. Anticipating your opponent's aim from the preliminary movement is the basis of most competitive sports (and good athletes hide the preliminary movement or deliberately fake it).In tennis, if you run after a drop shot is hit, you couldn't return the ball. You have to run as soon as you notice to do so. "My opponent is about to hit a drop shot!"In this game, you can't do it because the drop shot occasionally comes from a typical topspin swing that is powerfully scraped up from underneath.- - -There is not much that can be controlled. It's not the lack of commands. It's that there isn't much room for us, the game players, to intervene.If you tilt the stick in the direction to the ball, the athlete will start swinging on his own. We can't tell them how to hit it. Against a weakly launched chance ball, my athlete dash forward and return with a half-volley for some reason. Why not just hit a power shot calmly at shoulder or waist height!This game is a rhythm game that you have to press the buttons at the right time while watching inexplicable balls and unintelligible athlete's actions.You can barely control not only the shot, but even the movement. Repositioning after you hit the ball?  There is no need. The moment you tilt the stick to either side, the player will start swinging. If the ball is within his catching distance,  he will catch up on his own.Moreover, there is virtually no penalty for tilting the stick to the opposite direction. So, if you shake the stick with a clatter to the left and right at the moment the opponent hits, my athlete will start swinging. Yeah, this technique is so realistic it's like doing a split step!- - -I'm sure many other reviewers have written about this as well, I'm also negative about this system. Even if we have to continue to use this system, I hope that it will be changed so that the display can be turned off as an option. The glittery card display breaks the realistically calm screen atmosphere.- - -I'll write again. If you're looking for a "", I wouldn't recommend this game for now. However, I wish it will get better. Thank you for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes, at the time of this review, I only have 40 minutes played, but I can most definitely say, that this game, is a great game. AO Tennis 2 is a fantastic tennis game, but it's more friendly and easy to get used too. Tennis World Tour 2, has a more realistic feel and it's a lot harder to master, even on its most easiest difficulty. The graphics are incredible. Just like I stated on AO Tennis 2's review, it's a shame, that Top Spin 4 nostalgic freaks are giving this game a thumbs down. It's time to move on, and accept things as what they are, this game a long with AO Tennis 2, are far superior than Top Spin 4. _childDocuments_.review: I have been a tennis fan my whole life: I have played Virtua Tennis, Top Spin, Grand Slam Tennis, Dream Match Tennis Pro, and Tennis Elbow. Having played TWT2 game for an hour after buying it, I can say it's just not worth the money at all for the features you gain. I chose to buy this over AO Tennis because I really prefer the realistic and deep learning curve that Top Spin or Tennis Elbow provided, yet this one is nowhere near their caliber at all if you are looking for realistic and rewarding gameplay. It felt really wonky, buggy, and unpredictable to the point where it's no longer skill-based sometimes because CPU players would throw shots that won't let you retrieve it even if your positioning is right there. There were no slice animations on the backhand side of the players sometimes, which made it so weird and disengaging as if the shot type mechanism doesn't matter. The player movements were so buggy as if they could min-teleport. I found net volleys and power slices to easily drive winners, which again is really weird for me. Finally, what turned me off the most, was the nonexistent online mode. I only managed to have matched with someone, and the match was laggy, so my opponent quit the match. For the price, these fundamental things I expected from it were not met. Overall, you are better off getting Tennis Elbow for PC unless you are really dead serious on official licensing of players and some tournaments. Top Spin 4 is still the greatest tennis video game that has official licensing to tournaments and players.

_childDocuments_.review: I've chosen negative as there are just too many little things wrong with the game. Not enough 'lets', no 'net cords' whatsoever and not enough shots hit into the net in general. The net doesn't feel threatening.- Serving is too easy. My 1st serve percentage is always over 95%.- Impossible to serve an ace though unless playing with Safin, who no matter if it's 1st, or a rare 2nd serve, I can bomb down 148mph serves. (nowhere near enough threat of double faulting as the serving system is too easy)- The game defaults the difficulty to 'normal' for every career mode match. So it's down to memory to change the difficulty in game before the opening point of every match.- Animations and responsiveness are improved but still not quite good enough. _childDocuments_.review: There's some potential but overall it's a mess... again.- Shots frequently still don't match the input. You'll get a slice shot when you've press for top spin or a flat shot when you want a slice etc. and this happens even when you've supposedly timed the shot as "good" or "perfect".- Pro players seemingly have no identity or specific animations other than Nadal. Even Federer has a generic serve and swings, and NO ONE has realistic or personalised celebrations. For a game that wants to present itself as a tennis "sim" this is simply unforgivable. You want to feel like you are these players and the character model just looking (a bit) like them isn't enough. Federer with a massive, cheesy (and terrifying) smile after winning a point just looks so, so wrong.- Net play is completely broken. If you go to the net you will be passed, regardless of the difficulty level or who you're playing against, because the game simply does not respond to input at the net whatsoever. I've played just under 4 hours and haven't been able hit one volley at the net, nor has an animation even been initiated to lunge for the ball as it passes.- Similar to above, all too often your player will simply refuse to respond to a ball when moving side to side at the baseline that falls close enough that you realistically should be able to at least lunge for it and make some sort of play. Completely unresponsive.- The AI seems incapable of getting above 40% first serves in, regardless of who you're playing against or what difficulty the game is on. Fault after fault.- Impossible to hit aces even using the best players. I haven't yet managed a single one on my time with the game.- Single handed backhand animations are honestly beyond abysmal. Similar to my first point, you'll try and play a top spin backhand and it'll hit some bizarre looking, dodgy slice that looks completely unnatural and unrealistic.- Ball physics at times are completely nonsensical in terms of trajectory and velocity. One minute you'll hit a top spin forehand that looks great, the next you're playing a strange, lunging volley that somehow goes into super speed with heavy top spin despite the animation not matching this at all.- They may have "doubled" the animations, but it's still nowhere near enough and the game still completely lacks any real fluidity. You'll see the same animations over and over again (as well as ones that make literally no sense considering the button you've pressed, as above) and players will awkwardly transition from one shot/position to the next in an unrealistic way.- The sound is still sub-par. Crowds don't react to some winners and generally are still underwhelming and, seriously, how hard/expensive could it be to just pay some decent, professional umpires and line judges to record for the game? Because they still sound AWFUL. Again, it ruins the immersion of it all. - Zero customisation. It's 2020 and yet we can't create and share courts/arenas/tournaments/players and we can't edit pro players stats and overall ratings to our liking. AO Tennis manages it, so why can't Tennis World Tour? It completely takes away from the realism and how replayable the game is, especially considering the base game without DLC has ZERO official tournaments and a number of huge omissions in the roster such as Djokovic, Serena Williams, Naomi Osaka etc.Overall I'd give the game 4/10 so far, at a push. Unless there's huge improvements to the responsiveness, animations and content via patches (here we go again) then it's yet another failed tennis game.

_childDocuments_.review: I experienced the same terrible performance issues in this game on Windows 11 as I did with another game developed by Big Ant Studios called AO Tennis 2. In Windows 10, I could play AO Tennis 2 at a full 60fps with an RTX3080 and i9-9900k processor in 4k resolution. However, in both AO Tennis 2 and Tennis World Tour 2, the frame rate dives down into the 30s-40s in Windows 11 with shadows enabled, even with an RTX4080 and i9-14900k processor. In both games, the only way I can get 60fps at 4k resolution in Windows 11 is to completely disable shadows, which looks awful. Tennis World Tour 2 is also way too similar to AO Tennis 2. I have no idea why a developer would make two very similar tennis games like this. However, the difficulty in Tennis World Tour 2 seems excessive compared to AO Tennis 2. I was constantly getting aced by opponents with my shots going out of bounds way too often, even on so-called "very easy" difficulty. This game also uses a timing based shot system that is not fun and a convoluted card-based skill system where you are encouraged to spend money to buy more cards. In fact, right off the bat the first thing you are shown is how to purchase more cards. Overall, I did not enjoy my time spent with this game so I cannot recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I was highly disappointed with Tennis World Tour 2. The game fails to deliver on many fronts, and falls far short of expectations.The controls are clunky and unresponsive, making it nearly impossible to execute even basic shots accurately. The AI opponents are still predictable, and the game's difficulty level remains poorly balanced, making it either too easy or too difficult at times.The graphics have not improved since the first game and are still lackluster, with stiff and unnatural character animations. The game also still lacks content, with only a limited number of courts and players available.The career mode is still shallow and unengaging, offering little motivation to progress through the ranks. _childDocuments_.review: Update after April 23, 2021 patch:The game is approaching Top Spin 4 levels now. It's not quite there in some areas (online netcode is a bit shaky and the variety of tactics usable in rallies is still pretty low), but in most aspects it's now a pretty good tennis game. I'm definitely impressed by the level of improvements and support the game has gotten.The custom animations for the players are a really nice touch that makes exhibition mode much more appealing. Graphics have definitely seen a big boost since launch which is unexpected but nice. I'm super happy to finally see the white on-court advertisement boards replaced. Compared to the version of the game that launched it's unrecognisable, really,My final large gripe...when I play my friend online and we want to play a womens/mens exhibition match it would help to remove the timer that forces us to choose our players within 30 seconds, it's just not enough time to browse through the stats and make a decision. And it would also help to have all the female players grouped together, separately from the male players, as it can be really hard to spot the player you're looking for at the moment. Also,,,the game still crashes fairly often on PC and Xbox...like 1/10 matches the game crashes :(My original review: Best tennis game we've had since Top Spin 4, unfortunately. detailed_description: While walking with your brother, everything turns into horror and drags the hero into a series of terrible events. Your brother has been kidnapped, and you are left face-to-face with an ominous forest filled with dangers and strange creatures. Solve the puzzles that you meet on the way, do not let yourself be caught, and save your brother! Find out the dark story that befell the once-calm and peaceful forest, turning it into a creepy place filled with evil. Perhaps it is you who will be able to solve all the secrets of the forest and save the peaceful creatures? 1. Creepy atmospheric puzzle 2. Elements of a classic quest: collect items and use them in a wide variety of cases. 3. But this is not only a quest, you will have to hide, run away, jump high, and even ... learn to play the reedpipe! 4. A truly creepy soundtrack and beautiful 2D art will take you to a dark tale and give you few unforgettable hours!

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is a hand-drawn, short and sweet adventure game that is sure to appease adventure, puzzle and horror fans alike. Whilst only lasting a few hours, the lurid, yet strangely charming illustrations and simple gameplay make it a title that is difficult to dislike and shouldn't be avoided due to its low playtime. + Macabre hand-drawn illustrations with a quirky, almost cute twist.+ Logical answers to puzzles but be warned you will die ... + Melancholic atmosphere and eerie sound effects.+ Varied gameplay, hide, run, solve puzzles and most importantly, don't get caught!+ Steam achievements.- At approximately 2 hours long, it left me wanting more. The developers behind Creepy Tale have extreme potential and I hope to see more releases from  in the future to fill this void. The story begins with the young unnamed protagonist taking a leisurely stroll in the woods with his brother, innocently collecting mushrooms. Before long, tragedy strikes, and the brother is dragged off into the abyss by sinister looking beasts from another world. The once peaceful forest is then transformed into a nightmare, filled with evil that our hero must navigate and overcome to save his brother and ultimately restore serenity to the land.  Explore the mysterious forest, meet some relatively friendly and some not-so-friendly inhabitants, solve puzzles and most importantly of all, avoid getting caught or falling victim to the many death traps scattered throughout the map. As a 2D sidescroller, only A + D are used to navigate, with Z being the 'use' button. Whilst these controls cannot be remapped, the title does have full controller support. Some items can be difficult to spot, but they are typically found within a small radius and I never found myself unable to proceed due to this. The puzzles are logical and relatively simple, with codes/instructions to combinations being found nearby and there is little to no backtracking involved.The handful of enemies are crafted brilliantly and succeed in making players feel uneasy, especially combined with the creepy sound effects. The protagonist must outwit them by either hiding in nearby cupboards, chests or even in plants! Typically, direct confrontations lead to death as we cannot outrun the monsters if we get too close, but the forgiving save system prevents this from becoming frustrating. Nevertheless, it's very straightforward and even if it takes a death or so, what I was required to do would always soon become apparent. The hand-drawn artwork is Creepy Tale's defining feature and it does really shine. Its overcast and bleak colours accentuate this ominous world, highlighting the drab atmosphere brilliantly. The enemies allude a frightening aura, yet also appear to belong in children's storybooks, with their overly peculiar appearance.It is stated on the store page that it features a 'truly creepy' soundtrack and indeed it does. There is no dialogue, but it makes up for this with its excellent use of sound, building a ghostly atmosphere. The forest is devoid of life and the sound helps to portray this sense of loneliness well. The eerie gasps, sneers and heightened effects when an enemy sees a player can all be defined by the games title, creepy! It is not scary like in the traditional horror sense but is a form of story-book dread that many can appreciate.Yes! It is adequately priced at $AU7.50 and for fans of the genre, it is a difficult title to dislike. Clocking in at approximately 2-3 hours of playtime, it is a short-lived, but enjoyable experience that I do not regret playing. I look forward to the release of other similar titles by the same Indie developers' and I see much potential in their work. This review copy was provided to the OCG-Curations curator.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing it I was actually a bit torn about this short little 2D-puzzle-adventure. On the one hand I really wanted to like it. It’s got simplistic, yet charming, hand-painted graphics which with their depressive brown color palette definitely manage to give the game a dark Brothers Grimm feeling, and the eerie music adds to that creepy tale vibe. But on the other hand there were also a few points I had my gripes with. Now, you have to know that I played with tips turned off (this function can be found in the settings menu at the start), but I didn’t know this at this point.With tips turned off, one of the biggest problems I encountered probably were the hitboxes in my opinion. You were often even standing at the right spot, but nothing happened, and then the character just shrugged/wondered in a too long animation (which mostly resulted in the monsters catching you). And what didn’t make it easier, it was often cryptic what the game wanted you to do. Sometimes mechanics weren’t obvious (like being able to take something off a table or having to jump on the bed to search a cushion), sometimes items you needed were hidden in a pixel-hunting tradition, or sometimes you had no clue what the problem actually was or what was required next. I was just too often stupefied for my taste and a few times even had to resort to a guide. I guess a few more visual clues would have helped in that regard.Like I said, after playing I noticed the tips function for the first time. This tips function adds kind of big interaction symbols that pop up wherever you go. I can’t really say now afterwards how these will influence your gaming experience. I guess it makes a lot of stuff way easier, especially searching for items. On the other hand it kind of simplifies a lot too much in my opinion, and most importantly it somehow breaks the immersion. I would have actually wished that there would have been a mixed option of both ways, like no clues, but pressing a button for some hotspots if you’re stuck.Anyway, apart from those little flaws I experienced, and no matter what play-style you prefer, I do still clearly recommend this, if even for the visuals and the atmosphere alone, because you can see that the 2 devs were people who just love dark fairy tales, and they definitely managed to do an interesting game which encompasses everything I normally adore in all small indie productions. It’s also easy to 100% achievement-wise, and keeping the low price in mind, the question of buying it probably is a no-brainer. So nevertheless, personally I’m looking forward to Creepy Tale 2 and hoping for a few enhancements there.

_childDocuments_.review: is a short indie puzzle platformer that is fairly priced and rather enjoyable as well. The puzzles are fairly straight forward and the story told is unexpected and quite interesting. The most outstanding aspect of the game is the hand-drawn artwork, which is just incredible.The game is in a series of 8 episodes that tell of a story without using any words. There are three chapters, and the breakdown is 3/3/2 in terms of episodes. The breaking up of the episodes are completely arbitrary. While there is only one puzzle in each of the first two episode, the subsequent episodes have usually more than one simple puzzle.The game does not rely on difficulty of puzzles to make the game artificially longer. The puzzles are fairly straight forward, but are neat in their own way. If you are interested in the game, you should definitely check it out and do not watch any videos that exist for this game, because presumably you will run across some spoilers.It's a class point and click game with a small amount of platforming, which is very easy. But still, I know some people cannot do the left and right handed coordination of things well and just simple jumping around in platformers are too much, so this game would not be for those individuals.I have a video of the game uploaded and linked to Steam contents page, but I won't give a link here, as I mentioned, I really don't want to provide any spoilers for people who are reading this.You can play with the keyboard or with a controller. I think you should definitely use a controller for this game.Really nice style and hand-drawn artwork is really awesome.Very fitting, pretty nice.If you don't mind a tiny bit of platforming and enjoy hand-drawn artwork and some pretty neat little puzzles (each one practically fits on one screen--few exceptions).Totally fair with a base price of $4.99 US and currently during its launch week, there's a 20% discount.  is a really great little indie title with a tiny amount of platforming but the gameplay revolving around a set of fairly straight forward puzzles and its main draw coming from the artwork in its hand-drawn style that's really quite fantastic. The story told through the art is pretty neat too.The game takes about 2-2.5 hours to complete. Most of the achievements are optional, and a few will unlock with the story development. They are pretty easy to get for people going after the achievements.This game is very much worth your money and your time, so check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a bit torn about recommending , but its "only" con - , is an integral part of the game, as it's a 2D side-scrolling puzzle game with light platforming. I shouldn't need hints to tell what I can interact with or not. Instead of solving puzzles, I mostly hunted for interactable pixels to interact. Some interactable items were obvious, others not soo much. Far too many times I found myself clicking on what looked important, only to get a ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ from my character. The puzzles were simply poorly designed (not all, but a large majority), requiring trial and error, which is never fun, especially when it involves you dying over and over. They inadequately convey what you need to do to advance (or not at all) and rely on this (un)fun concept for that "aha" moment, or rather "please let this be it" moment in the case of . The presentation is superb and sadly the only thing I can praise. It delivers a bleak and mysterious world, with danger lurking at every corner, accompanied by an outstanding soundtrack.So, what is my final verdict in the end? Even if it had a couple of decent moments, the large part of the game (that is already extremely short) was unenjoyable. The trial and error based puzzles weren't fun, nor was the constant death that accompanied them. When puzzles work, and the game was clear with what it expects from me, it was fun. I was fully immersed in this dark, dreary and dangerous world, and the "aha" moments when you find the solution felt genuine. But then those puzzles that require you to know the answer beforehand take over, shattering my immersion, as the only thought going through my head is "What did I do wrong this time!". When I write my reviews, I always ask myself a simple question - Did I enjoy playing this game? No, I didn't enjoy my time .

_childDocuments_.review: I feel pretty bad not recommending this game because the potential is definitely , I just really disliked the execution of it. There is a storyline to the game, but it is definitely not narrative-driven (which is fine, I just think it's worth mentioning). Instead, the game is probably best categorised as a puzzle game. I love puzzle games, I particularly enjoy indie puzzle games, and I thought the design of this game looked right up my alley. What I was met with were a) puzzles that made zero sense (I'm legitimately confused how people figured some of them out because even after watching a guide, I don't know how people knew what to do) b) finicky controls and c) frustrating interactions when it came to playing after a death.As an example for a), there is a puzzle in the game where there are hundreds of possible solutions. You know what I don't want to do? Try hundreds of different solutions. If that wasn't annoying enough, after you do it once, you have to do it  with a different solution (and it's not even clear that that's what you need to do!). Now, this wouldn't be so bad if maybe there was a hint somewhere, anywhere in the game that indicated what the possible combination might be to narrow it down and that you have to do it three times, but as far as I'm aware, there isn't. This type of puzzle where you just kind of have to brute force it (or look up a guide...) occurs several times in the game, and at that point, it's not really a puzzle IMO.For b) there were countless times when I would want to do something (pick something up, hide, etc), and it's almost like there were two different interactions I could have with one particular object. Depending on exactly where I was standing, one option might become the only one available. This meant that there were many times in which I thought I had explored an entire area but evidently hadn't because although I stood 1-20 pixels away from an item, and 22-500 pixels away from an item, I didn't stand 21 pixels away from an item, and 21 pixels away from the item is the only distance in which you are able to pick the item up. Otherwise, I got a different interaction with the item. For c) there were several times in which I died and lost only some items. What was annoying about this was it wasn't like I lost my most recently accrued items which would probably make the most sense. Instead, I might have been in three different areas trying to get various objects, and would lose one item from the first area, all of them from the second area, and then have all the items I got in the third area. It makes no sense to me how this game was saving my progress. All of that being said, the design of the game is very good. The art style is nice and the theme is on point. I just can't recommend this game given the gameplay itself, but am curious to know if Creepy Tale 2 improved on these things.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if this puzzle-platformer was $10, I would have no problems recommending it. It kinda reminds me of Limbo just because you tend to die a lot - it looks like a game for kids, but the deaths can be a little disgusting, like impaling yourself on the spikes or getting your face chewed out. Overall the game is just very enjoyable, nice animation, and the majority of the puzzles were creative and fun to do. I managed to finish it slightly under 3 hours, with a few missing achivements, so about 3 hours of content. There is some platforming involved, nothing too difficult though, especially compared to Limbo. Some moments in the game were funny, and the ending was very satisfying as well. You can use the controller to play it, but the buttons are preset (I used xbox-one). Some of the puzzles were not necessarily logical, but they were not hard, I just had to think in a surreal kind of way to understand them. There is one thing I disagree with the developer, they removed any indication for interactable items to make the game more difficult, so you have to use your eyes and scan the environment. It's not a huge problem because there are only so many things that can grab your attention, but I don't see the point of me humping every inch of the game just to make sure. There was only one puzzle that I did not like, the one on the chessboard, if there is logic to it, it could be interpreted in multiple ways, I solved it by luck. + I thought most of the puzzles were unique and fun + nice animation, enjoyable occasional humour + some optional achievements I encountered a few glitches, some forced me to replay the short episodes (I already posted the details in the forum). You have the option to restart from each episode so it's not a huge problem as the episodes are 10-20 minutes if you know nothing about them. So it delayed me by 10 minutes at most. Personally, I think you should have icons for things that you can push or pick up, but the game has decent visual clarity so it's not too hard either way.One of the better cheap games in my recent memory, it's comparable to many similar games in a $10-15 range. It made me laugh many times, and I thought most of the puzzles were very creative. Loved everything that happens in the last chapter ;), I did not expect that.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: MILD SPOILERS Creepy Tale is an absorbing, beautiful, and unique short game that left me wanting more. In this case, that's not a particularly good thing.  As several critics have pointed out, it usually takes an average gamer 2 hours to finish.Although what they don't tell you, however, is that it's generally only a 30 minute playthrough with this beta-game when you already have everything figured out before starting. The 2-hour duration is more than likely experienced because of the frustratingly unintuitive puzzles you'll encounter on your first attempts, whose sole purpose, it seems, are to waste the player's time.I'm not even kidding... some of the puzzles aren't even puzzles, because a puzzle is using information you have and pairing it with information you'll receive. Information you know how to apply with the plot elements already thrown at you.It doesn't have to be done with ease or with immeasurable difficulty, but there should be a connection with everything you do. This game is largely comprised of just random guesswork supported on top of a wildly unclear story.The story itself isn't all that confusing, it just doesn't go any deeper than giving you the bare minimum of what it's offering. Which, it seems, is just a creepy atmospheric short game with just about zero backstory. I understand that this isn't the full game and so it certainly makes sense to go easier on it because of this fact.However, if the full game is also going to feature more of the same frustratingly unintuitve puzzles that are geared towards being random button and item combinations to progress onward, I probably won't buy it.This review isn't for the full and finished game, but the one I played that's currently available on Steam. My philosophy is thus: If you charge money for a game, even if it's really short and may not even be the full game that was hyped on social media, I'm still allowed to criticize it.I just feel that it really is that simple.    As creative writing informs us, a story should "show" and not "tell". What they mean is that you can "tell" when appropriate in the right setting/environment in your story -- not just to omit it entirely from your narrative, which is what Creepy Tale seems to do with this literary advice. As I said, it's beautiful. The hand-drawn visuals grabbed me immediately. The sound design is on another world: monsters growling angrily, opening hundred year-old doors whose hinges have rusted, bouncing on enormous purple mushrooms, grabbing buttons on the ground, and playing ceremonial wooden flutes: 100% engrossed by the sounds that these interactions produce. Just beyond words. I was particularly fond of the sound for collecting water from an old tin bucket. That's just *chef kiss*. Wow. So, so good.  The soundtrack was also pretty cool, albeit not as immersive: it mostly consisted of either a few darkly emotional piano chords played on a loop, airily atmospheric synths (typically paired with an occasional FruityLoops orchestral thing), or this celestial-sounding bright chorus effect smeared on digitized vocals that kept growing in loudness every half minute. Gotta be honest, the celestial/chorusy vocal track eventually got on my nerves. It was delightfully creepy when the vocals were just droning quietly in the background, but then it gets deafening after a while and I just have to mute it.  And I don't want to turn the volume down all that much, because then I'll probably miss all the charming little noises that this game has up its sleeve. You have amazing sound design -- why bloody ruin it with tracks that drown everything else out? If anyone from the team that made this game reads this, can you please consider what I said for an update/patch?I have sound-loudness sensitivities and that really took me out of the experience.  This sells for more than $2.50 ($4.99) -- I just so happened to catch it during when it was on sale. Now, it's most certainly a looker (as we had already established), but can anyone genuinely justify paying more than $2.50 for an annoyingly short game whose "puzzles" will make you want to furiously punch your pillow and scream your lungs out at God?  I can potentially see this as a $2.50 short indie game, as most of the money appears to have been lovingly spent on its visuals and art direction. But anything more than that, and I'm not sure I'd agree with the price, sorry. And while I'm at it, I might as well explain my problem with the puzzles it has.Many of them are dependent on you noticing that an item is supposed to be grabbed and used in combination with other items and environments to progress onward.One critic said that the grabbable items were "easily found" (or something like that) when in actuality they're pretty much all drably colored which frustratingly matches the background and other non-grabbable items in your immediate vicinity.Many of the roots, leaves, twigs, and mushrooms on the ground can't be grabbed while the ones that you are supposed to grab don't have any distinct features to tell them apart. At times it doesn't even seem like that's what you're meant to do. But then you find out what needs to be done and you feel like an absolute moron for the rest of the game. Fun. I can *somewhat* (and I mean somewhat) understand the logic of picking up a nondescript branch from the ground andusing it as a lever to lower the bridge deck that a monster patrols to drop it in to the water for a classy escape. (Getting there took some time, but it was beatable with some trial and error.)But the wonderful "mushroom part" I had no shame whatsoever in looking up how to beat. Basically, you're supposed to put mushrooms in a cauldron in the right order and serve it to a witch.If done correctly, the witch dies, leaving you with the key to the door that takes you outside. I was clueless here. One mushroom makes the concoction fizz a blue color upon throwing it in first, but I didn't know that there were other mushrooms that made the brew also fizz and change different colors. There's literally an achievement for adding the wrong mushrooms three times in a row, and I got that on my first try. I dumped the stuff into the witch's boiling cauldron but nothing happened.I then went up to inspect the scene after trying to blindly poison her and she lovingly ate my face without hesitation. So cool.I thought that if anything in this game was going to be a genuine puzzle, it most certainly would be this. But, no. The mushrooms that you need to use have to be thrown in in the right order and there's almost zero similarities between them. Eventually I could probably guess the right order, but that just sounds unbearably tedious. Because it is. Who wants to do that? Now, the trailer for the full game/Creepy Tale 2 indeed looks superb, but I'm waiting to jump on it after seeing its Lets Plays from the gaming community on Youtube first. Just a few glances to see if it's anything worth checking out without having much ruined. Would I recommend this game? Honestly...  I don't know. If you don't mind how unintuitive its puzzles are because the art style's uniqueness would make up for this if you're that type of person, then go for it.  (Definitely for those who like games with a charming, hand-drawn feel.) It's not expensive and the areas you need to explore aren't big.But for me, that doesn't matter: its story was predominately ambiguous and for the most part wasn't interesting enough to keep my attention. Let's see how the Creepy Tale 2 fares.

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is a 2D puzzle game that tells its story, not through narrative or dialogue, but through its enigmas and over the course of eight episodes. It's about two brothers who find themselves in an evil forest, full of fantastical creatures, eerie monsters, and nasty witches. Your brother gets kidnapped, and it's up to you to rescue him from the clutches of these diabolical fiends, but finding him won't be that easy. The ideas behind the game, including the art direction and soundtrack, are all inspired by the wonderful works of Grimm's Fairy Tales; a classic anthology of frightening tales for children.The atmosphere of this title is absolutely solid. Everything from the wispy, hand-drawn backgrounds to the muted colors, drab tones, and abundance of fog. It all just makes a very strong, rainy autumn day vibe come alive. The art style really nails the Grimm's Fairy Tales inspiration, as you'll find similar artistry in the illustrated versions of most books. The monsters are also as creepy as they are cute, and they seem to draw heavily from another great classic children's book, Where the Wild Things Are. Additionally, the soundtrack is subtle and blends everything together, with a haunting main melody that may just end up lingering in your head even after you've completed your Creepy Tale adventure.Although the visuals are the major appeal to this release, the puzzles are what the gameplay centers around, and boy oh boy are they good. They're not too hard, they're not too easy, and they do require some critical thinking to overcome. Not only is your brain going to be tickled, but the enigmas are ingenious and they don't rely on the boring tried-and-true formulas that so many puzzle games, especially those with a horror theme, default to these days; such as pipes, valves, sliders, circle images, etc. There are eight episodes to devour, split into three chapters, and without any guides you're looking at about 2-3 hours for completion. If you suck at even the simplest of puzzles like me, a guide will get you through in about an hour and a half.No matter how you choose to play Creepy Tale, guided or not, you're going to have a good time. It's a simple little title with well thought-out puzzles, and an outstandingly well done atmosphere that certainly does stay true to the main inspirations that it was born from. It's best played on a dreary day in the fall, sipping coffee or your favorite warm beverage, while watching the leaves fall, and just remembering when life was a little bit easier and carefree. Fans of puzzle games in particular will be truly satisfied here, since the puzzles are fun and unique, while straddling the fine line between challenging and overly complex.The Horror Network  |  Click for Gore

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy taleCreepy tale is an interesting puzzle platformer with a rich story. The game delivers a great 2D platformer experience with befitting music and sound effects.The story starts off with two brothers who decided to go collect mushrooms from an unknown part of the forest. What seemed to be a nice brotherly moment of peace and comfort was soon to be proven wrong.Something happened; there’s a sudden noise. My brother has been kidnapped by a monster, his basket of mushrooms wasted on the floor.Being afraid and alone, I decide to go after the monster into the forest, in the hope of finding my brother. This forest seems so ominous and uncanny, full of weird structures and creatures. Moving forward, I try to puzzle things together and track down my missing brother.  While going through the forest, mysterious creatures start to appear, some of which are peaceful and scared of my presence, while others are hostile, ready to come after me given the chance. I continue, passing one obstacle after another, passing sleeping monsters, climbing bean stalks, figuring out puzzles, and trying to find my brother.  The grim atmosphere compliments the game nicely, and the well-chosen music fits the gameplay experience nicely. Although the 2D art style in Creepy Tale is nothing new, Creepy Tale’s creators have done a such a good job with the style that I didn’t even consider the fact that I had played such 2D styled games before; the game felt that unique. Now let’s talk about the gameplay . . . I must say the base game is solid for this short yet very interesting indie title. The basic movement keys are there W, A, S, D but also arrow keys for some reason. There are keys for interactions with items in place, though these keys are not changeable. The gameplay felt very smooth with consistent frame rates without any issues. However, I faced quite a few other issues:  achievements are not working, key registrations are bad and I’m getting a weird lag which caused me to be caught by the witch in the cabin a lot; I really had a bad time getting past her.Interacting with an item in a rush didn’t work because the key didn’t register, or maybe that’s how it’s supposed to be, which is also weird and wrong if it’s not a technical issue. As this is a platformer there shouldn’t be any lag while running, jumping, and interacting with items. The quality of graphics was high, well-polished and complimented the story and gameplay extremely well. Nothing catches the eye like good render quality, which was consistent throughout the world.It seems like check points are placed with every correct action performed by the player, which is a very good thing in a platformer game. Although this was supposed to be a horror game, it actually turned out to be more creepy rather than a full-blown horror game.  I didn’t feel scared a single time throughout my entire gameplay, but I did feel really creeped out quite a few times. The monster and the main protagonist designs are well made and fit the theme of the game perfectly.Puzzles, though easy to complete, felt again and again as though there were too many unnecessary steps added to the gameplay and puzzles, which just added an element of annoyance. The game is very interesting and addictive, although I faced quite a few issues as I mentioned before, and there are quite a few genuine annoyances, but I could see myself coming back to this game for more.Positives: + Short yet rich story+ Solid base gameplay+ Common yet well-implemented game design+ Great music and sound effects that fit the theme perfectly+ Check point saved with every correct action + Well-designed main protagonist and monsters+ Easy puzzles + Atmospheric Negatives: -  Repetitive at times-  Though the puzzles were easy, there were quite a few unnecessary steps added to them-  Short game -  Key registration latency -  Achievements didn’t seem to workOverall, considering all aspects of this game, I must say was very interested with this story-rich, short Indie platformer. 8/10Key provided by the developer/publisher for review purposes. Any opinions expressed are entirely my own!

_childDocuments_.review: A trip to the forest for mushrooms results in the abduction of one of the brothers, and now the second of them will have to go through a series of trials in order to save his relative. The game has a very interesting mood - it is both relaxing and fairy, but at the same time quite gloomy. In many respects this is facilitated by the visual style, in which muted gray tones very successfully coexist with interspersed with bright colors. Watching this spectacle is incredibly nice, you really immerse yourself in the atmosphere of a frightening fairy tale, perceiving the gameplay in a completely different way. Of course, do not over-praise the game, it is still an indie game created using a very limited amount of resources, but they are really used to good use. A variety of puzzles is also very pleasing, here you have puzzles using physics, and traditional puzzles, many of which are solved in several stages. The only thing I would like for some clearer recognition of the objects used, some of them are very difficult to find. There is logic in all riddles; sooner or later you come to their solution in a natural way, which is very important for games that focus primarily on this element. The creators managed to very organically weave the universe of games and puzzles, so that they seem like a completely natural part of the world. The plot of the game ... Let's just say it exists and that’s enough."Creepy Tale" is a charming little fairy tale that lures a player into a dark forest full of dangers and worries. In the gingerbread houses here, the hero is not fed with sweets, but eaten himself, so you need to be brave and think faster.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved so many aspects of Creepy Tale but I wasn’t a fan of many of the puzzles overall and in a puzzle game that is kind of a problem. I found much of the time I was beating the puzzles by trial and error or luck and not because they made any logical sense to me. There were some good ones early on like when you have to figure put how to poison a witch but many of the ones after that I felt my self asking “how should I have reasonably known that ?”. Most of the time it was trial and error until I figured it out but I still don’t know why the correct solution was correct. The game board puzzle is a great example of this. The art is gorgeous and has a great theme to it. The lack of voice acting works for this game much how it did for the game Brothers. The story, while a bit unexplored, was interesting for what it was. The sound effects and music were well done.	I played Creepy Tales on Linux. It never crashed on me and I didn’t notice any glitches. Alt-Tab didn’t work. There was an auto save system and the worst part was the game gave no indication when it saved. The save points weren’t terribly spaced apart but a save icon would have been nice or even better a manual save system. You can’t edit controls either. This wasn’t a huge deal as I don’t mind the defaults but it still would have been nice to have the option. The game ran fairly well on the lower end system I used but there was some lag when the game would drop to the 40’s for frame rate here and there. There are no graphics options at all aside from resolution. My Logitech F310 game pad worked without issue although it was limited to using the thumb sticks due to the dpad not working. Game Engine: UnitySave System: AutoDisk Space Used: 1.57 GBInput Used: Logitech F310Resolution: 1080PCPU Usage: 6-16 %RAM Usage: 2.8-3.6 GBFrame Rate: 40-75 (My refresh rate)	I wanted to like Creepy Tale more than I did because I can see a lot of effort went into it and I did enjoy aspects of it.  Sadly I just couldn’t get into the puzzles and that is probably more of a personal issue than the sign of a bad game as many people I know loved the puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: 1.6h (100% achievement, finished the game) No. Yes (~11 achievements). No. is a short adventure game where you have to survive from creatures that want to eat you.- Unique gameplay that relies on trial and error- Checkpoints through chapter select- Sometimes it can be confusing what the game wants you to doIntel Core i5-9300H 2.40GHz, 8GB RAM, NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650The setting in  looks like the medieval era with the dominant use of brown color and simplistic, yet realistic-looking characters. Despite the usage of brown colors, it's still easy to distinguish objects from the backgrounds due to the darker color. Moreover, the monster design also goes well with the artistic style to set the atmosphere. is a game of trial and error. It's a game without words, where you need to figure out what the game wants. It consists of 8 chapters, each focusing on a location and how the main character has to escape from the danger that lurks in it. It's mostly about monsters that eat you whenever they see you, although there are also other things.You need to pick up objects and use it to other objects. If you enable the hints in the options, they will be highlighted, or you can just spam the interact button to find anything interactable. It's easy to do so since you control your character with a keyboard instead of a mouse. Sometimes, it's not clear what the game wants you to do. You might not pick up some objects because they are too small and not noticeable from the background, or you might not understand that a certain object can be used in a certain way since the items are only available in this game - things like that end up forcing you to do trial and error, and failure means death. You need to restart the chapter again, although luckily, checkpoints will be there to save your time most of the time.I like how it gives you the sense of creepiness at the beginning; the thought of a monster coming out and eating you can be scary, although that feeling will disappear as you play. The monsters will not be as scary anymore, although the creepiness will still be there even just a little bit. It really stands up to its title. Puzzles are also available from time to time. You might need to do trial and error to either solve or figure out the rules. Sometimes, the rule can be so obscured that you won't know unless you already know the answer.I finished the game in 1.6h. I admit that I used a guide to bypass some solutions since the game can be cryptid at times, and it can be exhausting to redo with trial and error. When these kinds of things happen, I end up getting annoyed at the game since it's more like figuring out what the game wants rather than actually playing. And that's what I felt most of the time. Luckily, the game is short and the transition between the annoying puzzles and the ones I could figure out is quite scarce. is a game with a unique, creepy atmosphere. It's a game that tests your ability to figure out what you should do without words, and pay attention to your surroundings. It might be annoying to figure out what the game wants, but the gameplay and presentation itself help to make the game enjoyable. Moreover, the short length does well to contain my patience. I could recommend it to those who like games with a unique atmosphere, although do buy it on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay... this looks like a hobbyist game, or a game circle/club gotten together to build a game. Very very short.. and not much of a story to tell but rather a concept of the story itself.The creepy art style aren't bad, but not very original as we can see a lot of these going on in other game. So it's definitely not a "own-style" original... And even though the art style suggested this is a point and click adventure, it's not... it's made using a platformer engine... so yeah, it's more a puzzle solving platformer which doesn't really require much of a parkour skill.And the puzzles... are bad... one of those that doesn't have a proper logical answer, but rather needs you to "find" the answer by random button smashing near objects (if this is actually point and click it would be much easier and less frustrating)... jumping off a tower is the solution to get across... this is what you will be getting a lot in this game. Testing out every objects and items and without even needing a puzzle solving skill in the end, you will reach your goal...The game can be done in less than an hour.. but those long long hours we see in the reviews are mainly because this game do card drops... so yeah... idle and keep the game on for card drops... and that gives a wrong idea of how long this game actually is...I'd have given a neutral rating for this but since we can't do that here on steam... i am giving a thumbs up for an attempt of making a creepy game. But don't really recommend it at full price at all. It's totally not worth it. Might not even worth it for some as free game imo... So if you want to support the indie developer on their work, buy it, just don't expect it to be good.

_childDocuments_.review: Short story about a boy trying to find his brother who has been kidnapped by monsters. _childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Kind of surprising game. I loved the creepy undertones that brought to mind the themes found in the original Grimm's Fairy Tales. _childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It has a good creepy setting and premise but the puzzles are far too obscure or nonsensical for the game to be enjoyable.  The simple story, art style and music makes it feel like a Grimm Fairy Tale (complete with a shocking and moral ending) and the animations are well done, but I never felt as though I solved a puzzle beyond trying everything with everything else.  The game is pretty unforgiving with death coming frequently and as you are forced to repeat some sections multiple times, it just becomes tedious and boring.  The very short play time is extended by earning achievements, but not by much and although overall, I was disappointed by it.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It was a pleasant couple of hours of gameplay. A few of the puzzles are legitimately challenging and I felt no shame having to get a hint or two, to keep my relaxation steady. The game looks and sounds like an old German fairytale told as a lullaby which really made it stand out from the competition.  This is a game I wouldn't mind revisiting after a year or two.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale
