_childDocuments_.review: It is essentially a puzzle platformer. heavy on the puzzle side.It looks nice, plays well and has a touch of humour.In the end, whether you enjoy your time or not, will come down to the puzzles. The game is made of three different types of puzzles. Logic based, environmental clue based, and those of complete guesswork. At a guess, I will say the game is evenly split between them. My least favourite type of puzzles are based on guesswork. So, based on that I did not enjoy 33 percent of my time playing through the game. I'm surprised I was able to solve all the puzzles without 'external help'.There's no hand holding,  Although sometimes you can look for tiny clues by what the protagonist glimpses at as you walk around. Figuring out what to do and how to solve the puzzles can be a real 'head-scratcher'.  Therefore, you do need to figure out what the developer was thinking and then solve it exactly as the developer wanted you to.It's a relatively short game. If you knew the solutions to the puzzles you could get through it within two hours. I got stuck on three certain puzzles which kept me engrossed for an extra hour.I would only recommend this game to people looking for a tough puzzle game. If you are only wanting 'logic based' or 'clue based' puzzles then this game is not for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is a short puzzle adventure set in a spooky mystical world. Without going into detail, the story is simple yet interesting. There is no dialog but rather the story is told through actions and the occasional thought bubble. The controls are very basic, so much so that can take some getting used to and can be frustrating at first. The achievements are not too difficult to get, though you will likely have to replay certain parts to get them all. Luckily, you can access any section of the game in the main menu once completed.  I overall enjoyed the game considering it was only a few dollars. I recommend picking it up on sale like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A cute little puzzle game with minor platforming elements. _childDocuments_.review: It's a bit difficult to rate this game and decide if I recommend it. There are pros and cons. I'm closer to liking this game than to dislike it because I've had some fun playing it. So... What do we have here? It is a short story with a creepy atmosphere all over the place, where you need to save your brother (and the whole world) from Evil. The story is not long, but quite enjoyable. It took me 2 hours to finish it with all of the achievements. The drawing style, characters and atmosphere are quite nice. Controls are few. You can use a keyboard or controller, which you prefer. For me, the controller was not working, and that's disappointing. Autosave. You can replay any chapter again. Only one (happy) ending, so no bad endings for the players here. The story is simple. Sometimes I was lost in what to do and why is it going on like that, still it was interesting to play. Can't say that I would play this game more than once, but for one-time play - it is a nice choice. What I, personally, like the most is the atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This game is going into my “Won’t Play” folder, which is my folder for games I either did not finish or would never play again. _childDocuments_.review: I liked the game. The art and atmosphere are excellent, very good mix of simple and childish (in a good way) with horror and subdued but dark material. The death scenes remind me a lot of Inside, where you won't see any gushing blood or gore, but it still makes you wince with impact. A couple of the puzzles felt like I was just mashing the interact button with anything I could find until I found the right combination, and after I got the solution I still felt like they were pretty unlikely to be solved by actually figuring them out rather than guessing. It is very difficult to tell what is part of the scenery and what might be an object you can interact with, so I found myself doing the step-try interact-step-try interact dance. The controls are not super well tuned either, there was one point in particular where I had to enter a door at a certain time to avoid a monster and the interact button would repeatedly just fail to do anything. That said, this is not a platformer, so it's not that big of a problem but may cause you a few extra deaths. I picked it up on sale and feel it was a good buy. Not sure if I would recommend it at full price unless you really like the art style and rarely suffer frustration from the issues I mentioned. I'm glad they're making a part 2 but hope they tune the controls a little better and polish the puzzles slightly more.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The platforming sections are brief, but made frustrating by the terrible controls. It's fairly buggy, got stuck in scenery a couple of times and had to restart. Some of the puzzles are good, but there are far too many that seem to rely on trial and error, padding the playtime out.The art direction is nice and the soundtrack is probably the best part of the game. It's not the the worst game I've every played, but I honestly don't think that I could recommend it to anyone. Unless it's like $0.50 or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent little horror/puzzle game with simple mechanics and intuitive riddles. The presentation is very cosy and spooky and polished. _childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game, but fairly short. Just don't come in expecting anything crazy and you'll probably be more than satisfied for the price. While never actually scary or frightening, the game does build with success a certain atmosphere of tension and dread, borrowing inspiration from the stories of the Grimm Brothers to flesh out the world. The story is simple and left mostly ambiguous, with further details provided in the sequel for those left wanting more and interested in delving deeper. Puzzles are not hard, and there's even a built-in hint system for when things get confusing. To wrap it up, it's easy to get 100% achievements for good-ol' lovers of completionism.

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is an adventure game controlled exclusively by keyboard (or possibly controller, haven't tried it). The atmosphere is exactly like the store description says, creepy and reminiscent of Brother Grimm tales.The art style totally fits the style, though animations are a bit simplistic.The music is non-intrusive and fits the vibe well. I noticed a bug with how the music was triggered once, but it's no big deal for me.Now the most important part: the puzzles.Pros:* More often than not it is not hard to understand what has to be done* The puzzle design is pretty diverse and it didn't feel like I have to do the same thing over and over again* There is no complicated inventory dependence. So, like in many point-and-click adventures you never end up in a situation where you have an inventory full of items and out of frustration go around and try to use every item on every object to progressCons:* The interactable and pickable items frequently do not stand out or are highlighted in any way. They blend with the environment. As a result at times I had to walk around an area clicking the action button every step of the way to find what I missed* There are few puzzles with moon logic* There is one puzzle where a hostile NPC walks around, and you have to do some stuff in that area to progress, while evading the NPC. Due to how the NPC moves, unless you know exactly what to do, this puzzle is more about an annoying trial and error to find the correct sequence of actions than about, well, being a puzzleOverall I would recommend this game to any adventure / puzzle game enthusiasts. It's short enough so that the cons can be more or less overlooked. For people who are not fans of the genre the game may be more frustrating than fun though.

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale Review: A Hauntingly Beautiful Experience (11/10)Creepy Tale is a masterclass in blending eerie storytelling with captivating visuals, earning a well-deserved 11/10 in my book. From the moment you dive into its unsettling world, you're greeted with a rich atmosphere that immerses you in a haunting fairy tale.The art style is one of the game's standout features. Each scene is beautifully crafted, with a distinctive aesthetic that draws you in and keeps you on edge. The dark, whimsical landscapes are both enchanting and foreboding, perfectly complementing the narrative's tone.The gameplay mechanics are intuitive yet engaging, with puzzles that challenge your mind without feeling overly frustrating. Each puzzle feels like a natural part of the story, enhancing your connection to the characters and the unfolding plot. The sound design is equally impressive; the eerie soundtrack and ambient noises create an unsettling tension that keeps you invested in every moment.What truly sets Creepy Tale apart is its storytelling. The narrative is rich with depth, exploring themes of loss, bravery, and the unknown. The characters are well-developed, and their journeys are compelling, making you genuinely care about their fates.Overall, Creepy Tale is not just a game; it’s an experience that lingers long after you've played. If you appreciate beautifully crafted indie games that deliver both a visual and emotional punch, this is a must-play. I can’t recommend it highly enough—an easy 11/10!
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Charmingly creepy, short game with at times eccentric puzzle solutions.I can recommend this game for the atmosphere and story. It is expanded upon in the sequel(s), but your protagonist achieves his goal by the end of the game so you don't need to worry about having to buy another game to get get closure. (I'm not entirely sure if this warrants a spoiler warning considering that you can see that for yourself relatively fast if you know what you're doing, haha).Length: My core playtime was about an hour, but that's mostly owed to the fact that I already owned and completed the game on Switch, and thus roughly remembered what I had to do. Since the Switch version doesn't have achievements, I did have to go hunting for some of them since I wasn't aware of them.Art: Well, you can see from the screenshots and trailer what you've got to expect. I find the style unique in its own right and it hits the right spot between being simple enough to not distract from anything but still detailed enough to get the terror across, if that makes sense. This setting is not your Disney-esque fairy tale, and the imagery is reflecting that.Sound: The soundtrack works great in supporting the atmosphere. For lack of even more suitable words, it certainly is as creepy as the game title would have you believe. Perfect for spooky season or whenever you need to rattle your nerves a bit.Story: Enough vagueness to get your creative juices flowing in terms of trying to understand the rules of this world. Expanded upon in sequel(s), as mentioned above. Everything is told solely through imagery and sounds, there is no text or dialogue in this game.Puzzles: A lot of trial and error at times, but generally not too punishing if you mess up (except for one chapter that requires a long sequence of events and that can indeed be frustrating if you mistime or misclick). And if you're absolutely stumped, there are guides available.(I saw there is an option to toggle interactable objects or something like that, which should help when you get stuck also, but I didn't try that out for myself so I can't say how big or little help this is.)Achievements: Can generally be gotten during the first playthrough. But feel free to fully enjoy the story before looking up a guide to make sure you don't miss any, as you can select any chapter from the main menu after you started/completed it. There is only one achievement where I'm not sure if it has to be done in one sitting as it spans 3 chapters, but they're all relatively short so even if you do have to replay, you don't lose a ton of time here.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A very short point and click style game (though you don't actually point and click, you use either WASD or arrow keys). You hunt through a creepy forest looking for your brother. I like the art style and atmosphere, it really delivers on that. If you enjoyed flash games or other free story games, this is very much like that but more polished. The sound design is good as well with appropriate sound cues and music. The puzzles are sometimes a bit obtuse, where you can easily get stuck because you didn't find the right item hiding somewhere (like, for example, there is a spot with 3 mushrooms and only one is interactable, so if you tried one of the non-interactable mushrooms first you may well miss the one you need). Overall though, because each area is small with only a few items in each, it does not take too long to just brute force your way through. I think it was a good idea to keep the various puzzle areas completely seperate, so you never feel like you missed something and there is never any back tracking. Overall the gameplay is just ok, nothing really out of the ordinary.My only real complaint is that it is too short. You can beat it in about an hour. That is a bit short, even for $5, but on sale it is well worth it. Bottom line, if you enjoy the art style buy it on sale, you will have a good time.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks nice, but for a game that has platforming, the platforming controls are kind of floaty, and you can't jump down from platforms, Also, even though I use a controller, the default keyboard controls are very weird, as if the dev had never played any game on a keyboard before (arrow keys + space, okay, but then the letter 'y' which becomes 'z' on qwerty keyboards, making it awkward for anyone without a controller (which I think is not a good decision for an adventure game without mouse control). Also, if you do have a controller, you can't turn off the vibration. Or adjust much of anything, option-wise in general. There's a review by an user named 'xOrbOfDeception' here on Steam that describes the control issues in greater detail. Also, the most annoying part are moon logic puzzles, which there are far too many of considering how short this game is. It really captures the feel of John Kenn artwork very well, but the gameplay becomes needlessly annoying as a consequence of the factors I mentioned. And that's the most important thing for a game, in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: It was interesting enough that I ended up playing it through to the end the first time I started it. Sure, it was the first and the last time I started it, but puzzle games aren't exactly famed for their replayability (and I don't love Steam achievements THAT much).The music set a nice tone, the visuals were successful enough, if a bit Adobe Flashy, but most importantly the puzzles were generally engaging. I didn't often find myself questioning the logic, and I seldom had to click around randomly just to see what works. There were only two occasions where I thought the clues were woefully inadequate (looking at you, tree), which is definitely more of an indication of decent design than any spectacular cognitive abilities on my part. I also found there to be a nice mix between puzzle and platformer. The platform element was more seasoning than meat, but it broke up the monotony. All in all, I'd give this a soft recommendation. _childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is a Nintendo Switch game that somehow is also on Steam, but from all appearances this is designed specifically for handheld gaming devices.  Once more the public domain has been pillaged, this side scrolling adventure game with hand drawn art has you loosely following the Brother's Grimm and their dark fairy tales.  Gameplay and puzzle solving requires a lot of trial and error, life is cheap and returning to checkpoints will be a frequent experience. One important note is that even though this is an amateur project, it does seem to be sincerely and genuinely made.  I couldn't find any flipped assets, plagiarism or any other kind of insincere actions from the developer, but unfortunately genuine intentions alone are not enough to produce a brilliant PC gaming experience.The game is very very short and can be finished in 2 hours.  Developers have at least some responsibility to provide enough content to make a game last more than 2 hours if they're serious about providing something of value to gamers.  There's less content here than some free game demos.Unfortunately there's a number of technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.While there are options to change the resolution for the game, all this does is scale up the simplistic 2D art assets used to make the game, which makes little or no difference to the graphics quality.  Without any other substantial graphics tweaks, it's not possible for gamers to improve the lacklustre 2D visuals.The game is comprised of "okayish" hand drawn 2D illustrations instead of professional looking 3D game assets.  It's unclear if this is due to lack of budget to arrange someone who can create graphical assets properly, or lack of talent.  Regardless, the overall visual quality of the game is very low, beneath what PC gamers have come to expect in this era of cutting edge photorealistic 3D graphics.Because this is designed for handheld/portable gaming appliances, it carries a number of deliberate design deficiencies.  Compromises were made to cater to the low power handheld gaming appliances that the game was designed for.  These are unfortunate compromises and limitations that PC gamers shouldn't be forced to accept, but it's evident that PC was a second thought for the mobile game developers.  The game is deficient as a result of these choices, and would have been so much better without the handicaps that designing games for low power handhelds forces upon a game.  While this might run well on a Steam Deck, we must remember the vast majority of gamers here are gaming on PC.These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.So, should you buy this game?  Is this one of the best of the 100,000+ games on Steam?Creepy Tale has the ridiculous, laughable price of around $5 USD, it's not worth it given the defects and shortcomings with the product, especially considering the sheer number of completely free, much higher quality games on Steam.  For comparison, the $5 asking price for this game could get you games like the "Tomb Raider" remake, "Mass Effect 3" or "Fallout 4".  Quality, professionally made games like those are frequently on sale cheaper than this.Unfortunately Steam reviewers aren't presented with a "Maybe" option... if they did, that's what I'd choose.  This isn't a completely bad game, but it's also not one of the best.  As always, if you read my review and you can overlook the negatives I've called out, or they just aren't important to you, then by all means go ahead and buy this.

Loved the art style (it's whimsy-horror, so if you're into that real Tim Burton/Coraline style art, this is right up your alley.) The puzzles are definitely quite abstract/intuitive, but I only struggled with the mushrooms and librarian. Otherwise it was a delight to play and prompted me to buy the whole trilogy!
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Very interesting story and visuals! I've always been fascinated in horror, and have always enjoyed puzzles so this was very enjoyable! Plenty of guides available if you get stuck on anything such as achievements or story progression. Would recommend, though much more worth it when on sale. Still, a very enjoyable horror puzzle game!
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, was that a waste of time...First of all, it should've been called "Tale" because this thing is NOT creepy in the slightest.The controls are clunky and very poorly thought out (using Z as the action key is a joke, considering that probably most people play this on WASD).The sound effects are ridiculous and completely ruin the already weak "creepy mood" of the game.The puzzles are annoying, relying entirely on a trial and error method. There is literally no hint on what to do, leaving you to click EVERYWHERE without any guidance. Sure, you can turn on tips in the settings, but they're still not really helpful in most cases.Based on the unique graphics, I expected something much more immersive, atmospheric, and, first of all... fun.Overall, it's a wasted potential. I don't recommend it unless it's on a -90% sale, and even then, think twice before buying this... thing.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun little diversion,  really delivers on vibes, art & music, and task variation. I found the controls to be really clunky (A+D didn't work, so I used the arrow pad; Z to interact; space bar to jump; X for special object), like this game was poorly mapped to PC from some platform that used a controller. Just as I was getting used to it, the game ended.As some other reviewers have said, one of my biggest gripes with this game is that there's very little direction for what needs doing. It's a delicate balance in games like these to lead the player but not too much. Unfortunately,  errs on the side of "too nebulous."  This is ameliorated by the "show tips" checkbox in the Settings menu, which shows up an icon above your character's head when something can happen... but it still doesn't give any indication of WHAT should happen. Also, there are a lot of hotspots that do absolutely nothing, which... certainly is a choice.I died a lot, which is to be expected in these sorts of trial-and-error games. Ope, that ended in death. Let's try something else, since the game helpfully restarted me right before that challenge! A couple ways to die even give you an achievement! Embrace the death.The story, such as it is, felt much more like a prototype than a fully-fleshed-out tale, so the summary which says "Find out the dark story that befell the once-calm and peaceful forest..." is a bit of an overstatement.All in all, it's a pleasant diversion. I wish there were more, which earns it a Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere is good, and the puzzles are challenging. I think I resorted to online help for one or two steps due to the latter. Took me about 2 hours to fully complete. Replay-ability is accentuated by the game letting you choose specific chapters to return to as opposed to making you start all over. Another thing to note is a lack of voice acting or text dialogue, though, the story did just fine without. A highlight chapter for me was the witch's hut due to the tension I felt to solve the puzzle without getting caught.Overall, I enjoyed this puzzle game.

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting little game... it's the characters in these types of games that make them fun and the creepy dudes have their own personalities, which does the job well... keeps the interest going. Only a couple of hours long, but a fun, if sometimes frustrating experience.... timing and order is key to this game, get it wrong and your blood pressure goes up!But it's a decent story, great sound and graphics, a well developed game.Why are there always  in these types of games? _childDocuments_.review: A very sweet fun game. It's like playing a comic strip both in style and how everything moves left to right as you progress. A lot of the color is drab, but that just enhances the things that come into full color as you play. The style is like living line drawings filled with watercolor that moves. The mechanic of monsters coming to life when they get touched by colorful butterflies is playful and unique. The mechanics of how to play are also unique and unexpected at times. I needed help on a couple puzzles, but if you use what you find, you'll eventually figure things out. There are also ghosts in the background that let you know where there is something special to do. Probably like a lot of puzzle games, instead of dying, you just fall down and reset to the beginning of the most recently cleared area. Instead of a negative feeling when failing a section, I felt more like I wanted to figure out what I could do different next time, or what did I miss. If you liked the original book "Where the wild things are", you will probably love this.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is effective, there is no doubting that. It is as insidious as they come, and that comes from its art, world and characters. Eager to play its sequel in the hope that it expands more. But, Creepy Tale fumbles whenever it asks you to do anything. Too often, it resorts to puzzles that are clumsy and illogical, with a parade of deaths as the punishment.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This nice little puzzle adventure is based very much on the art of John Kenn Mortensen, a danish artist who draws dreamlike creepy monster scenarios entirely on post-it notes. Here we see these pictures come to life in a little tale of two brothers looking for mushrooms in the woods. One of them gets kidnapped by monsters and so the other one sets out on an eerie little journey to save him. The puzzles are for the biggest part not very difficult to solve, but sometimes they can be a bit obscure, mostly because it is not always clear with which objects in the scenery you can interact, but it never got frustrating and overall I enjoyed it a lot. The game is quite short - it can be solved in about one hour -, but I loved the art style and overall fairy tale like spookiness very much.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished Creepy Tale and I've gotta say, it's really eerie but the most creepy part isn't the art or characters chasing you, it's the puzzles,object interaction and platforming. That's the real nerve breaker right there, as some  puzzles are just trial and error (I was playing with  Tips/Hints on off).Art itself is a very double-edged sword here. While I really love it, it also makes it hard to notice on some parts what objects are actually interactable.Overall the game itself is super short,  if you use a walkthrough or just speedrun it you'll finish it under an hour. For me since it was my first time, I took it slow, exploring everything I could while also dying a fair bit and I still finished it in just over 2 hours. Story itself has some serious holes (which I hope are explained in the sequels) like for example: Who was that little girl that mind-controlled the Ewoks? You know nothing of her except that she mixed some conconction together and posesses some magick powers. Keep in mind she plays quite a big role in this game. So yeah, super disappointed in the game's lore so far, that's why I just made my own as of writing this.✅ Beuatiful art style✅ Nice characters ✅ Easily achievable trophies  ( EZ and fast plat)✅ Chapter Selection is a blessing❌ Some puzzles are meh❌ Pricey❌ Object interaction is a bit of a mystery ❌ Story has some serious holes★★☆☆☆ It's short but sweet and I recommend it only while it's on sale.So go on ahead and explore the forest. Just be mindful of your surroundings because your flute will get smashed to pieces by a music-hating tree, soon afterwards you'll feed a magic carrot to Chewbacca and actually take control over him then proceed to engage in windpipe massaging the Ewok (professionally known as a front choke hold) like a fuzzy Krav Maga master.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The only thing I like about this game is its art style, which isn't even original as it is obviously based on the work of artist John Kenn Mortensen, and is pretty much the only reason I bought the game. The gameplay is a poor mix of platforming, stealth and point n clickish puzzles. The platforming is bad as the controls are pretty loose and the puzzles don't make much sense and have very few clues. Also, it's hard to tell which objects can be interacted with as they pretty much blend in with the surroundings and there's no indicator of sort, such as flashing or a marker appearing to let you know if they are interactable when you approach them. Instead, if you press the 'interact' button when you're on a spot with nothing to interact with, your character will perform a sluggish shrug motion, which is annoying enough when you have to trial-and-error towards finding some elusive object, and absolutely infuriating during the stealth sections of the game (which are the worst sections of the game for me) where you have to act quickly to sneak past enemies.The game is short, which might just be a good thing due to its poor gameplay. There's also no proper dialogue in this game, for better or worse.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: It's ok. It'd be a recommend on sale from me, and only if you like linear puzzle games that go for atmosphere over gameplay. Its definitely not for kids due to the way the last chapter is resolved with the girl, but it's not overly creepy either. More like an un-modernised fairy tale. The stylised graphics and atmosphere are well done. It is very short though (far less than my play time as it was left running in the background for a while), and has no replayabilitiy. The game has only a single way through which I found a bit frustrating/annoying at times, and a few of the puzzles just seemed like trial and error which isn't really my idea of fun  (examples below the spoiler tag). My advice is if you get really stuck anywhere or don't want to deal with that, just check a playthrough on youtube. SPOILERISH THINGS BELOWFor example you'd outrun a monster, go to pull up a plank behind you, but then just stand and be caught because that wasn't how the game wanted you to solve that puzzle. Maybe I missed a clue, but some seemed like trial and error like which dream catcher to select, or what order to move the disks for the butterfly passage. I worked them out with trial and error, but there really should have been clues instead. I checked youtube over the flute puzzle. I still can't work out why the tree would care about objects it can't even see, but you need to interact with all to pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Terror Meter 2/10Narrative Intrigue 3/10Visuals 7/10Difficulty 1/10Length <1hrCreepy Tale is a 2D Side Scrolling Puzzle game with Grimm Dark visuals, the player has to chase after their kidnapped brother to free him from the monsters that kidnapped him.Creepy Tale is a puzzle game, with each location the player will need to use their wit to find all the items they need. Think of each separate location as its own self-contained puzzle, with the player being able to find, or have on hand all items that they will need to complete the puzzle in the area. The challenge comes from puzzles being multi steps, and will require the player to plan out the puzzles in order to avoid enemies. Some puzzles later in the game are a bit annoying and require trial and error to get through.The puzzles can be difficult, but as long as you remember that everything that can be interacted with is part of the puzzle. During my playthrough at multiple points I ignored things that could be interacted with, not realising that the item had purpose.Overall the visuals were great, it really reminds me of the Grimm brother visuals. The puzzles were complex enough and did require some thought and multiple tries to get right, while the items you need to complete are really easy to find. Will definitely recommend the game, and will play the sequels when I get the chance.If you are having difficult with Creepy Tale, then my playthrough is below:Should you find the review helpful, you can find more games I recommend on my Curator Page:

_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Lovable art style, decent graphic, and a fairly creepy story. But the puzzle designs in this game lies amid controversy. Most of them were quite ordinary, but some made no sense. A complete random, if you will. The game even has this achievement if you can lucky-guess and complete a certain puzzle within a limited number of try. It was a vexing experience for some, understandably. But you might find fun in trying to solve them. Also, in a sense, it kinda captured the literal cluelessness of the protagonist we are playing as. Another issue about this game is that many things were leading the players astray. A character seemingly too poignant to ignore but actually didn't have any role in the game, or a puzzle which did not contribute to any story progress, for example. Time and endeavor-consuming. Still, the game is to me an enjoyable quest. Much less creepy than first anticipated. The creepiest height the game can goes to is in the end of the story, and with tremendous help from the soundtrack. P.S. I saw that the developer team has released their second game: Creepy Tale 2. Not a sequel, but a new story altogether. The two games, if not mistaken, are 4 years apart. We will see how the series fares.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game on a big sale (I think it was around -70%). If you could grab it on sale, do it :)It's really short (you could complete it in a couple of hours), has some interesting puzzles.What I like the most: game art style, music and general atmosphere. If you play it in the evening in a dark room without lights on, you'll totally experience it. For the price I paid (it was around 1$ with some extra), I think that was a really cool experience. Plus Steam achievements, some are fun to get.What could potentially be a drawback - controls. You can do only couple of things(like walk, jump, interact) and sometimes you have to come really close to objects to interact with them.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little game overall.  I picked it up on sale because I liked the artwork and the "Grimm's Fairytales" motif. With that in mind, I was very satisfied.The puzzles can be tricky, but the levels are small enough that trial and error should see you through. There are a few instances where you need to maneuver quickly and precisely, so expect to use platformer skills in conjunction with the problem-solving. I'm proud to report that I didn't need any walkthrough guides to finish.The game is short at less than three hours overall.  I don't expect to replay it, but you can skip between chapters if you are compelled to hunt for achievements.  I would've liked a better soundtrack to pair with the charming graphics.  I'll keep an eye out for the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is short and sweet, and so is the review :)This is a wonderfully enjoyable, and delightfully grim/grotesque yet simultaneously whimsical point and click "horror" game.  I put horror in quotes because, despite the dark faerie tale (Grimm-like) ambience/art work/aesthetic design, there is nothing really scary or horrifying about the game.  It's just plain fun.The gameplay is fun and straightforward, with an absence of the usual galaxy-brain puzzle solutions that tend to plague point-and-click adventure games (almost everything is very easy to figure out, and you may not ever need a walkthrough to progress, although you may want one for a couple of more arcane achievements).The music is....fine (nothing extraordinary, but certainly not bad) but the sound design is pretty sweet, if too sparse for my liking.The graphics aren't awe-inspiring in terms of complexity, but they absolutely are appropriate to the genre and the setting, so I was quite impressed with them overall due to the solid art-design.I can highly recommend this very short, but very enjoyable game, and I am very pumped about the next game this team puts out.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics in the game are great, the atmosphere is there but I got so frustrated in the short time I tried to play it.  Simply escaping the house required exact mouse positions and advancing to the next underground section became too much.  I'm sure this is a great game but I just struggled.  I think the devs should have made the first part super easy to get people hooked.  Who knows I may revisit it in the future and possibly change this review.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: What a nice little game! A real gem!Really, I did not expect too much, and was pleasantly surprised. Controls are very simple, the puzzles not always intuitive and the playtime is short (2 hours maybe). But the whole game lives from the beautiful really creepy atmosphere, the lovely drawn environments and art design. For the 2 hours it lasted, I was completely sunken in. Thank you devs, looking forward to the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome little creepy game! I was instantly excited to play since I could clearly see the inspiration from John Kenn Mortensen and it did not disappoint. They take on his style, so it's not really that scary, mostly kinda silly. It's a simple point and click and is honestly pretty short. I finished the game and went back for all the achievements and I haven't even received all the card drops. Some of the details/items are pretty small so you might miss what you're supposed to be doing next. For some that might be frustrating or it might be part of the challenge. Since it's only a couple bucks I'd say it's worth the play! I will definitely pick up the second game when it comes out!
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good game. About 2 hours of game play. the story was good, and I very much enjoyed coming across the nice (or at least passive) "monsters". The ending had a good twist, and the moments leading up to it were pretty satisfying. Only complaint I really have is just that for most of the puzzles, it's just trial and error. there wasn't really a pattern (at least that I could tell) to them, so that was a bit frustrating. other than that though, I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy Tale is a short, but great horror, fairy tale like game. Now then let’s get into the story.Two brothers picking mushrooms in a foggy forest, until one of them goes after a butterfly and it leaves the other brother to have to go find him.Okay now let's get into the likes. The graphics are good yet simple; this game proves you don’t need fancy graphics to create a great game. the art style is very good and it's creepy and kind of beautiful as well, remind me of the Hansel and Gretel games on Newgrounds, it also reminds me of art by John Kenn Mortensen.The story is good and spooky with some nice surprises; it all so has a dark Fairy Tale feel to it.The game has a great foreboding atmosphere and also have a nice a Fairy Tale feel. Some of the death animation is gruesome and good.The music is really good and fits the game well; the price is also fair for such a short game.Okay now let's get into the dislikes. Jumping and landing on the right spot can be kind of a pain sometimes it just feels a bit too floaty.All right then with that all said and done with Creepy Tale is a short, but great horror, fairy tale like game. With a lot to love like a very good and creepy art, a good and spooky story and a great foreboding atmosphere. So if you're looking for a horror game that has that nice creepy dark fairytale feel to it I highly recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good one. Some of the puzzles can be frustrating at first but after you get the hang of it, it's a really nice short game with a unique art style and simple controls. It is a bit too violent for children in a couple of places but don't misunderstand, it's not a combat game at all. Very much looking forward to the sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: A short yet fun little adventure. I played this in my dimly-lit living room with a group of friends and we all had fun shouting at the tv as we tried to solve the puzzles that drive this game. The inspiration in character design taken from the artwork of John Kenn Mortensen is a nice touch.Overall a nice little puzzle game. Recommended for a few hours of spooky fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Creepy tale is exactly what it says on the tin: The narration of a fairy tale immersed in a creepy and eerie atmosphere. The game is a simple puzzle-platformer with linear progression, in which you solve a number of puzzles to progress. Bonus for old-school puzzle-solving style: You are not led by the hand on how to solve the puzzles and no hints are given, so trying to understand what the puzzle is and how to solve it is part of the puzzle-solving process. Albeit very short (gameplay time < 3h), the game is fun and memorable due to its distinctive style of graphics, and prices accordingly. Hopefully the primer for a more expansive sequel.Would recommend.6.0/10
_childDocuments_.name: Creepy Tale

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game was interesting and I did enjoy the story. The minimalist art style, and game over all, really worked with the narrative, it didn't need more fancy animations or epic effects.One thing for me was using "Z" and "X" for actions as it was a bit awkward. Especially when using A-D keys to walk, less when using the arrow keys.4,99€ is not too much for the game, but it would definitely be more worth buying the game when it's on sale. I got the game in a Humble Bundle bundle and I'm glad I did. It was 1,5 hour of an interesting game. There is definitely a chance of me replaying the game sometime in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game very much. The visual storytelling here is something even AAA game devs and movie directors can learn from. The art style is interesting and endearing and the puzzles, while a little hard, isn't so hard that it turns me completely off from the game. I had to look up a video once or twice, but it's nothing compared to some of the esoteric puzzles I've encountered in other games.I can recommend this to anyone of any kind of video game pursuit. While short (I completed the game in 2 hours, and that's my first run with all the pauses and hiccups and mind-blank moments), it is fairly priced and provides more value than the price point would indicate.

name: Unravel
detailed_description: Unravel introduces Yarny — a new, lovable, and endearing character made from a single thread of yarn that slowly unravels as you move. Inspired by the unique and breath-taking environments of Northern Scandinavia, Unravel is a visually stunning, physics-based puzzle platformer. Using yarn to swing from tree branch to tree branch or hitch a ride on a flying kite, no feat is too big. Yarny is brought to life as the representation of the ties that bind loved-ones together. Embark with Yarny on a seemingly larger-than-life adventure to reconnect the long-lost memories of a family. Told completely without words, experience an exciting and heartfelt story about love, hope, and the journey of life. Game Features: Environment. Inspired by the breath-taking, lush environments of Northern Scandinavia, traverse nature’s beauty as well as the dangers that it has in store. Puzzles . Using Yarny’s thread, interact with the environment to swing across a tree gap or hitch a ride on a flying kite, no feat is too big. The tools may be simple but they have ability to accomplish complex puzzles. Underlying Story. Unlock a heartfelt story re-connecting the memories of a long lost family. The tale is told completely without words, and Yarny is the bond that ties everything together.

_childDocuments_.review: Just from the first level I'm in love. Unravel is a fun, beautifully made game with an amazing soundtrack. It's similar to any other platformer with its own quirks. As yarny, you are constantly unravelling but there are bits of yarn around the world to keep you going. You use your tail as a bridge, a slingshot, a rope, etc to get where you need to go, and solve the puzzles along the way.Absolutely beautiful game, cannot reccomend it more.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel is a cute and heartwarming platformer-puzzle game from EA. It's weird that EA released such a game but it's a very pleasant surprise.You play as a yarn-boy or whoever that being is. The gameplay consists of platforming sections and puzzles. Although the game might seem like a casual game from first sight, in reality it's quite challenging, especially if you go after achievements. Puzzles are not hard but require you to use your head a little. Platforming sections for the most part are pretty easy but at the same time they're very easy to mess up. The game is physics based and a lot depends on your momentum when you swing so it's easy to fall down. There are some places which could really be hard for someone who is not used to platformers.The game is pretty long, especially if you do every achievement. You will need to replay the levels for that. Finding secrets adds another layer of difficulty since they are well hidden and sometimes require risky actions.Level design is great. Each level is fresh and feels completely different. Both gameplay and scenery changes in each level. While one level may require more swinging through a beautiful scenery to not drown another one might involve balancing on a branch floating on water and avoiding mosquitoes or flying while holding on a kite.The controls and the game itself plays slightly similarly to Little Big Planet. I don't know, it reminds me of that game.There could be times when the character doesn't do what you wanted but it's more on you to timing your jump wrongly and underestimating the distance and momentum.Graphically this game is gorgeous. The levels look like from a Pixar movie and animations of the main character and some other beings/objects is really good. The whole game is a real eyecandy.Ultrawide  works with a simple fix and it looks even better.I have no problems with performance, game runs very smoothly on 3700x, 32gb, 2070s at 3440x1440.Sound is on par with the visuals. Music is wonderful and the ambient sounds on levels are believable. This is a wonderful game for people who enjoy platformers with some puzzles. It looks beautiful, gameplay is fun so you shouldn't miss this little gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Ah Unravel, potentially THE most frustrating game i played this year, where do i start with this one? Some backstory: since EA decided to deeply discount the second game before this one, i got & finished Unravel 2 first, and i remember it being enjoyable but still a bit disappointing since i mainly got it to to play with a friend only to discovered later that its local coop only which is a big shame (but i guess that was on me for not doing my homework before). i still feel like finishing that one solo really affected how much i could've enjoyed it, but alas, it was still good enough for me to justify buying Unravel 1, thinking i'll surely like that one a lot more with it being a solo experience, but boy oh boy how wrong i was.. Unravel 1 might be my first game ever that i bought directly from the steam store and deeply regret not refunding it when i was able to, why you might ask?simple, because of the terrible puzzles & poor level design, according to google this game has 12(?) levels, i hated it by the 3rd one (the swamp level) and i'm close to giving up on it altogether by the 5th(?) level (the one with falling rocks) some puzzles are intuitive and straight forward, others are pure frustration, nobody enjoys being stuck with little to no direction on what to do next, nobody enjoys random unpredictable physics..The story is close to non existent, can't say i had a chance to properly pay attention to those visions and the meaning behind them with how bad the level design is, but i probably wouldn't have minded it had i enjoyed the rest of the game.The one saving grace for Unravel 1 is the art style, i absolutely love it, and its one of the 2 reasons i kept pushing through to see the ending (the second one being wanting to get at least some of my money's worth), but i'm not sure it'll be able to carry me all the way through though, we shall see i guess.Unless you have a high tolerance for frustrating puzzles you're probably better off skipping this one and buying the second one instead.Giving it a 5/10 just cuz i can still see there was a lot of passion behind this project.

_childDocuments_.review: In case you didn't know, vemod describes a tranquil atmosphere of longing and sorrow over something one feels has disappeared and been lost, like a melancholic and mournful state filled with tender yearning. Growing up in a rural part of Sweden this game truly found a way to burrow itself inside and tender up a heart hardened by loot boxes and live services of today.. Unravel follows a little yarnie traversing rustic landscapes searching for memories of what once was. It is a beautiful little puzzle platformer where your resource is yarn and you use it to swing, drag and bungee yourself through a modest landscape filled with various obstacles. The gameplay is simple yet rewarding and during my playthrough I never encountered anything that took me away from the reverie. The game really nails the atmosphere and the environments are really evoking memories of my own childhood, which in a way is a bit spooky.. The pure coziness of the Scandinavian cottage core hub mixed with the various landscapes makes for a varied journey while never getting over the edge on nostalgia. So far so good! But I have not even mentioned the music yet. This soundtrack is magnificent, and even if you never play the game look up the soundtrack on a random streaming service. It perfectly encapsulates the haunting beauty that the game's story slowly reveals and to this day this is a soundtrack I recommend to anyone wanting to hear the soul Swedish folk music. In the end this is a great game and one that I recommend with all my heart. The only caveat is that it is tied to the horrendous EA-platform, but if you can tolerate that, this is a true treasure.

_childDocuments_.review: Dang, I’m crying over a ball of yarn… what am I doing with my life?!?!Unravel is probably one of my most cherished gaming memories. I remember playing it with my late younger brother, taking turns (since the first game was only 1-player). It’s a shame we never got to play the second game together. I’m glad that other people are playing this great series that we loved.This game affected me a lot, and not just because of my brothers passing. You see, I live in Sweden and I love it, so I could really see my own childhood in this game. Everything touched me. I was in my teens when I first played it and this game made me think of what I want my own children to experience in their own childhood. Too bad I’ve never had any real world interaction  with a woman. I thought it was unique in what it tried to do. The main aspect of Unravel is its story, and it uses the full power of gaming medium in order to tell it. Story is told through text. It is told through photos. It is told through music and the levels themselves. And each level has a theme which resonated with me. The game made me feel like any game rarely has: some levels were joy, some levels were grief, and it all translated through details and levels in the game.I didn't have half the problems with the platforming everyone else seemed to. I hate when people say this kind of thing, but maybe you guys just weren't very good at it. Once you figured out what you were supposed to do, the puzzles were pretty trivial, which is a sign of a good puzzle.I also think it's telling that everyone mentions the art style, graphics, and platforming, but not the story or message of the game. I can't think of another game that nailed a feeling and a message so well, and they did it without a single line of dialogue. That is a tremendous artistic achievement, but most hardcore gamers don’t recognize it when it smacked them in the face, because they thought the platforming was wonky, and that's all that matters.These impressions might seem overly positive, but that's really how I feel about the game: absolutely love it.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Till date we have seen many strange characters in different games. But Yarni has many differences from other characters. A character made of several meters of red wool yarn.Human damage to the environment is one of the important points that were discussed in the game.The badges that Yarny sticks on the photo album and in this way, all the pictures come alive again and you can watch them. In the game, you don't even hear a word of dialogue and the story does not follow a specific goal except to review memories. The memories reviewed in the game are not actually the personal memories of their owners. Maybe all these memories are common memories of many of us. Excursion in nature can be an example of this claim. Another thing that the creators paid special attention to is depicting the beauty of the world. In addition to this issue, we witnessed many bitter and sweet events in the stages of the game. Human damage to the environment is also one of the important points that were discussed in the game. The artistic view of the game stage designer should not be neglected, which depicts nature in the most beautiful way in the beginning stages of the game, and then goes to the dark and bitter stages of the game. This issue makes the constructive protest against human's disregard for the environment more visible and the audience is affected.The puzzles of the game are very creatively designed at first and make you think. Then you should try to open the way for yourself and pass the puzzle by using different applications of the thread wrapped around the Yarni. Another thing about puzzles is that they use the laws of physics. All objects are designed with real physics and have a specific weight. This makes you think about shaking different objects and how to use them before solving the puzzles so that you can make a better decision.The puzzles in the game are a bit challenging at first and you may get stuck in them for a while. But as the game progresses, the creativity in their design loses its color and face. In fact, most of the puzzles follow the same rules and just look different. By solving a few puzzles, you will learn everything and easily cope with the next puzzles. Unfortunately, this issue seriously affects the game and fans of this genre will definitely be disappointed by Unravel. Because as we get closer to the end of the game, the game becomes easier and its initial feeling disappears. Another interesting point is the lack of stability in the rules of the game. It's really surprising why sometimes the game doesn't follow its own rules!Sometimes the thread runs out for no reason, and this shows that the game is designed to be very linear, and you will have no choice but to follow the path set by the game's stage designer. Sometimes it happens that the jumping platform is not created by tying two close points together and the thread becomes loose. Another negative thing we saw in the game was its not so powerful platformer elements. Except for hanging from the tree branch and the designated points and finally jumping forward, no other point can be seen.At all stages, the distant scenery can be seen in the background of the picture, and it is even fun to watch them.Game environments are designed from real places located in Sweden. The most important thing that comes to mind at first glance is the slight difference between the game and real environments. All the scenery is designed in high detail and you will feel it.The developer studio has really done everything in the field of visuals. In all the moments of the game, you can hear soft music and listening to music. The music of the game is really relaxing and has greatly increased the artistic value of the game. In happy stages, we play one type and in dark stages with another type of music, which strengthens the feeling of loneliness and fear in the audience.Unravel is a good and very valuable game, but some factors have worked together to make it not a masterpiece. The effort made by the production team for the visual design of the game is very commendable, but I wish the same effort and creativity were spent on the gameplay and puzzle design of the game to see a more perfect work. By recalling the memories in your heart, Unravel also leaves a good memory in the mind of the audience, and you will remember the tour in its environments for a long time. Sometimes you get lost watching it, sometimes you laugh and sometimes the dark world of the game makes you think.

_childDocuments_.review: I only remembered something about this game due to the E3 presentation but never got to play it.So, now it was the time, and it was totally worth it. It's a rather short game unless you wanna 100%.You play as Yarny, the little yarn made dude that will be your character through the game, solving puzzles and platforming activities with his yarn-based movesets, unraveling the story as you progress.Story/messsage wise, I think it's pretty touching, and it really makes me happy that games like this exist, that it's clear that are made out of passion, creativity and just wanting to show the world what you have in your mind.Presentation is great, visuals are really nice and have aged well, music and sounds provide excellent atmosphere and vibes to it, and Yarny itself is animated really well, full of little details and reactions to multiple things through the world, making it feel alive. Difficulty isn't as low as you sometimes expect from these kind of titles, and there is some trial and error involved. Some levels can be a bit frustrating but nothing that took me more than 5 minutes to figure out, so I don't think it's really important.A little hidden gem probably, since it's not really one of those games that it's talked about, but if you like games that give you feels, and like physics based puzzles and platforming, I would totally recommend you to give it a try.

The concept on paper sounds interesting - you're a yarn character that can lasso and climb stuff and you can only go so far until you run out of yarn. _childDocuments_.review: No loose threads here. Story:You play as Yarny, a crochet character that lives inside the home of an elderly woman. Exploring the house you travel to locations that are significant to the woman and relive her memories, both happy and sad as you try to track down yarn badges belonging to her memory album.There's not a single audible piece of dialogue spoken in Unravel, yet the story it tells through visuals is quite poignant and filled with both happiness and sadness. It's not groundbreaking by any means, but the way it's done is actually fairly impressive and I genuinely loved the story. Graphics:Visually Unravel is a pretty impressive game. The environments of the game are going for that photorealistic look although they're not quite there yet. With Yarny's cartoonish, once you start playing it looks a bit off, but once you get into it, the world looks great. Just his design overall is great and I fell in love with the cute fellow immediately and his characteristic animations are top notch.The amount of different environments and the different varieties ranging from a sea shore, the woods and incredibly dangerous factories. Just how distinct each area, is a major plus and I loved exploring each level and finding secrets is just a ton of fun. Audio:The audio design is also great across the board. I'll start off with the soundtrack, because the orchestral music you hear throughout your journey is great and there's some really cool ambient tracks that sound upbeat and fun and then when the game turns serious, the somber tracks are just as good.The other sound effects are pretty decent, although the score takes the center stage here. The world around you does make noise, like birds chirping, snow falling off branches, the rain pouring onto the ground. It's all great stuff and mixed with the music it definitely builds a great atmosphere for each level.Gameplay:Unravel is a puzzle platformer where your main goal is to reach the end of the level and collecting the badge, however as a small guy made out of yarn you will have to use your wits to survive. So it's a very standard platformer, but there are a few different moves you have at your disposal and I'm talking about your yarn lasso. Around the world you will find red bows which allow you to throw a lasso onto them and that will make you swing across gaps or dangerous areas. Also you can build bridges between two points so you can use it as a trampoline or to move items which help you later down the line, like building a platform. The puzzles usually range from how can you clear a path to proceed and the puzzles are usually pretty simple in their design, with only a few of them actually stumping me and even then you're not going to get stuck on them. Also the checkpoints extend your yarn, cause you can actually  get to a point where you can't proceed through the level because you're going to wear out the yarn. So the gameplay is overall really fun, but there are a few issues. First of all connecting bridges is a bit finnicky and using them is also pretty janky. Sometimes you will hold down the jump button, but you'll find yourself not able to jump because you have to find a sweet spot to do it from and it gets annoying when you're dangling from an instant death pit. There's also minor issues with Yarny not wanting to push items when they are colliding with something. There's one level where you have to pull something up a log and it got stuck in a certain way where you had to sort of fiddle with your positioning to get that thing  and again you're doing this over an instant death spot. The swinging is also a bit hit or miss. It works incredibly well for the most part and is actually quite a fun move and if you pull it off correctly, you can build off crazy momentum. However you can land on it incorrectly and you'll get yourself killed so chaining them together is not a good idea, just take it slow. Verdict:The EA Originals program has so far been absolutely great and I can't believe that it took me that long to get to it. It's a genuinely fun game that is challenging, fun and has an emotional story all wrapped in a neat package. If you want a fun platformer give Unravel a shot, you won't be disappointed. Final Rating:9/10Pros:+ Story is emotional without uttering a single word + Great orchestral soundtrack + Incredibly fun gameplay, that is both simple and challenging + Tons of different and amazing looking environments Cons:- Some of the gameplay mechanics, especially the bridges are incredibly finnicky and will wind up getting you killed. _childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty, atmospheric, and even emotional puzzle platformer. The game only hits the feels if you are paying attention to the ghostly images and the pictures you unlock as you play through it. Though not nearly as emotional of an experience as Brothers:a tale of two sons this will get you there if you let it and invest the mind space for it.Unravel is a PS3 era game so some of the visuals are a little lacking by today's AAA standards but this was never a AAA game to begin with. Said, the visuals of this game stand up very well which in my mind is mostly due to the fact that the graphics are a bloomy and generally artistic type style instead of trying to be ultra realistic.The game is relatively short and can be finished in a single sitting if you put your mind to it, but it would take most of your day in order to play through it. Despite it being short, it is well worth the time investment for the payoff.The puzzles themselves in this puzzle platformer are mostly pretty straightforward, and I only found myself getting stuck three or four times badly throughout the entirety of this game. Though, the worst time getting stuck took maybe 20 minutes to figure it out.I played this game entirely through for the first time on my steam deck, I was able to fully and completely crank all graphic settings to the maximum and run at a native resolution and still achieve a smooth solid 60 frames per second. This type of game is perfectly suited for the steam deck and it's slightly anemic APU. I also played this over the course of several days while laid up and on full bed rest in a skilled nursing facility following a rather severe car accident. It was nice to be able to distract myself in short bursts completing one picture, similar to the paintings in Mario 64, at a time and being able to easily take bite-sized chunks out of the game every time I played.For my dime, the game may not necessarily be worth the full $20 that it costs currently on steam. However, if you get it in a humble bundle or have had it in other bundles with other games that you would like to play it could be a real solid value in the end. Overall, I would give this game a solid recommendation for people who would enjoy puzzle platformers but aren't necessarily experts at super complicated ones.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tough one to review, as it's simultaneously one of the most enjoyable games I've played recently, and yet also one that makes me want to barf so much that I'm not sure if I'll ever finish it.It's a wordless narrative, and it aims to evoke a heartfelt sentimental response. The bright colours, the melodramatic music, the snapshots of peoples lives that are revealed. It's all meant to add up to this thing of great import; those moments of light and darkness as we strive for happiness in this crazy, mixed up world, and it misses no attempt to shove this profundity in your face. It gets a bit much after a while, particularly with the music.The game-play is excellent. A puzzle-platformer that builds from seemingly gentle beginnings  into a fairly challenging mix of wits and well realised reflex driven action sequences. While it may not be super focused on the latter, it does have more than a few genuinely exciting turns where it's channelling the likes of Ori And The Blind Forest to deliver a thrilling change of pace.On the other side of it, you have a well constructed set of simple tools, and then the level design to push your understanding of them to a pleasantly mentally taxing degree. The premise is simple: You're a sentient thingy-ma-jig made out of wool, and to get around requires you unravelling your fabric. 'Unravel' by name, unravel by nature.There are hook objects in the environment, and for certain ones a connective bit of your wool stretched between them makes for a bouncy platform for higher jumping, or can be used as a bridge to move environmental objects around the area. You can pull objects by lassoing them (if they have a hook) and push them about. And finally you can use your fabric as a grapple and swing about. Every time you attach to one of these grapple points it shrinks your mass a little, and eventually you will run out of thread. You can find points that replenish your mass, but getting to them is still part of the puzzle, and once you do: it's a question of how much further you can now go. The previous stage of the puzzle will be closed off in some cases, as the hook acts like a check-point. Though that doesn't mean you're entirely done when it comes to it being incorporated into the final stages of the puzzle sequence.I did on occasion have to restart a few of the puzzles, as whilst progress through the level is generally not too tricky, there are collectables to get which require thinking ahead several more steps. As the solution allows for no error in timing and may incorporate further physical involvement of a much more dexterous nature.  Without having finished it I can't say if there's any reason to bother collecting these items, other than being a completionist or enjoying the extra challenge they provide. So now we get to why I may never finish this. I'm a crochet-ty old git and the tone of it is a bit sickly sweet for my tastes, with the overbearingly schmaltzy music that's initially rather lovely but soon becomes tedious as it's just loops throughout the level. Dramatic chase sequences have appropriately stirring tunes, so it's not that it lacks variety or great audio. Just that the main ambient track felt like it was constantly going "do you feel something? no? what if I do this? do you feel something now? no? what if I do this, or this? do you feel something now? please, please, please, pretty please with super sugary icing and juicy cherries on top, please feel something" Urgh....alright, dang it! Stop needling me game! I do feel something....and that is annoyance at how desperate this is to communicate it's theme. It's cloying to me, rather than sweet, as it's not very subtle.Graphically I think it's gorgeous, and it ran smoothly with responsive game-play. Taken just as a game I thought it was great. But the theme's behind it were a bit "meh" for me. I'm not like "bah, humbug!" at explorations of spiritual or emotional matters, yet there's a line where I start to feel myself disconnecting if it gets a bit sappy, and 'Unravel' crossed that line. As a yarn it just isn't that compelling for me personally. I like the material it's cut from, but not the way it's been tailored.But if you've played a game for 7 hours and have mostly enjoyed it, then even though I can't ultimately bring myself to finish it, it's still a recommended. Especially since anyone who isn't cranky like me won't find it anywhere near as nauseating. I've got a good idea that it has to be close to completion at this stage, and feel that it is worth the money for 8 or 9 hours of pretty darn good game-play. To get all of the hidden items would probably add on a few more hours, as I do know I've missed at least 10 or so and that was while trying to be thorough. If you miss them on a first go through a level, then you can repeat stages later. All previously found items don't need doing again, however: the stage does. They're not overly long, but without knowing if these items actually change anything I don't have the compulsion to solve some of the puzzles that have me stumped as to the solution. Especially when I know that taking a break and coming back to them later means repeating stuff I've already done.Whilst the game itself is compelling, the narrative (such as it is) is not much of a reason to persist, and I can't separate the two when the latter is so prominently woven into the experience through it's visuals, sound and tone.If you found this review to be helpful, then why not check out my curators page:

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel is a cute little platformer about memories and family bonds, told entirely without dialogue. You play as Yarny, a small little creature made out of yarn, as you explore the world trying to reconnect these memories, filling out a photo album along the way.The gameplay is pretty simple, and mostly physics based, as you have to solve different puzzles in each chapter. Yarny has the ability to extend a string of yarn out of his body to reach into certain spots, whether to swing across branches, or to grab otherwise unreachable objects. Being made out of a single thread of yarn, he needs to keep getting extra yarn, and the spots with this yarn act as checkpoints throughout the game. The game itself seems pretty forgiving with the positioning of the checkpoints, as they're usually not that far apart. However, having gone for the "Not So Fragile After All" achievement, which requires you to complete each level without dying, I can say that the game does present some issues in regard to difficulty, as it feels to be all over the place (the "middle" levels seem to be the hardest in the entire game); now, if you don't mind about achievements, you probably won't have as much issue with dying a couple times per level.Aesthetically speaking, the game looks wonderful. I can't quite say what it is, but it has this kind of relaxing, or nostalgic atmosphere; it's not without its dark moments, though, as during some levels you see Yarny go through some frightening places for a little yarn creature; his expression says it all. The soundtrack is also a strong point of the game, and it makes a great job at accompanying each section.All things considered, even though I got personally frustrated at times, when going for the no deaths achievement, I can still look at this game and say that it's a nice experience, which I can easily recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel is a game that I can't help but love, even after all it's shortcomings.This game has issues, the puzzles are frustrating sometimes, and some just flat out don't work properly, the levels can feel boring, and many sections in general feel annoying to play; or like a chore. Also, it's short, with me putting in 6 hours of playtime to beat it, not going for all the secrets, and struggling on a good amount of sections.However, I just can't bring myself to hate this game. It's obviously such a personal project for the development team, and there's so much heart and soul poured into this game.I would recommend picking this up, but I would say look forward to the last 2 or 3 levels of the game. In my opinion, that's where the game peaks. When they focus more on the incredible environments, story, platforming, and just interesting sections, instead of throwing 5 puzzles in a level for you to solve, the game is at it's absolute highest, and feels like the vision of it gets realized properly.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a gorgeous game, possibly the best-looking and most stylish I played that I can remember right now. However, I might be wrong because it's also mind-numbingly frustrating in certain respects. Controls are hit-and-miss sometimes, there are areas that are just plain infuriating (the final level especially is an exercise in "What were they thinking?") - and you're not given a lot of pointers either (think "flat design", but in an environment that requires you to quickly react else you're dead).As said, the game's looks are top-notch, music is fine if you can stand violins, and I'm sure Sven and Ulla-Britta were well-meaning when they made this (I'll disregard this being published by EA). The game should be likeable, and I really tried to like it but ultimately was glad I was finally over with it.Gotta give it a thumbs-down lacking a neutral rating.

_childDocuments_.review: i review games on steam after i 100% complete them! check out my reviews to see all the games i have completed!unravel is a puzzle/platformer developed by coldwood interactive and published by EA. originally announced at e3 2015, in december of that year EA announced that the game would launch worldwide in february 2016 for PC, PS4, and xbox one. unravel focuses on yarny, a creature made of red yarn. they explore the world, using yarn from their body in order to pull, swing, and solve puzzles of varying complexity. visually, the game looks pretty good but not mind-blowing, even for a 2016 title. one big flaw with the visuals is that i, as well as others, had problems figuring out if something was supposed to be part of the foreground or in the background. it's not intuitive and leads to a guessing game for what you can actually use or not.fundamentally, it's a neat little idea, but there are even more flaws with the gameplay. there's loads of inconsistency throughout in regards to the physics and mechanics, as well as general issues with level design. even simple things like purposely slowing down the player or limiting movement during simple walking sections that are flat out not enjoyable. the gameplay itself can also become tedious and repetitive, and is saved only by the heart-warming story that comes with playing through the game. if you weren't able to buy this for $2 or 90% off, then i'd be a lot more disappointed but at that price point i can't complain for what is truly a solid puzzle/platformer. i'm excited to eventually jump into the sequel as i hear that is a lot better than the original.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really cute game about your character, Yarny, who is made of yarn, embarks on a major adventure to find all the collectibles and return home. This game is a physics-based puzzle platformer with loads of obstacles you have to overcome. Yarny cannot swim, if the wind is too bad, he will blow away and he cannot fall from heights or he will die. The emotions that go with this game are portrayed perfectly where Yarny shows memories, bonds between family members that are built and lost. This makes the game extremely realistic and you feel a sense of relief with Yarny when the game is completed. This game is visually stunning with great graphics and art style. The attention to detail is unreal. I also did not have any major frame drops and was able to complete the full game in just over 7 hours.  The music and interactive sounds of this game is quite lovely and fitting. Some of the levels had me sitting on the edge of my seat and the music made it even better. The gameplay mechanics were really easy to get used to, especially while using a controller. If you get used to the mechanics the puzzles are quite easy, however some of them you have to do a few times to get it perfect.Clearly a lot of love and dedication was put into this game.I personally would recommend this game for any gamer, no matter what type of genre games you prefer.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. It was so quaint. Swinging from branch to branch is so fluid and fun, and the puzzles are pretty easy. If you want to get all the achievements, then it's not quite so easy, but not a tearing-your-hair out experience either! I really enjoyed 100%ing this game.One quite big reason to not get this game, however, is that in low lighting parts of levels, the game can get unplayably laggy and the screen will flicker. I have a 1660Ti so I'm certain my GPU isn't the issue here. I've found that a way to ease it is to tab out for two minutes and then it becomes playable again. Oddly, I only got the issue towards the end of the game, but had it in earlier chapters when I later returned to them.The game is very cheap, especially on sales, so despite this (quite major) gripe, I'd definitely recommend this game. Perhaps you won't have the same issue I did.
