_childDocuments_.review: I have been aware of Unravel's existence for a long time. I most likely saw it when watching an E3 live stream. However, I have never given this game a thought at the time as I was not interested in this type of game. However, recently, I have been playing indie and experimenting with new types of games. Therefore, I watched the IGN review to see if it was worth playing. I purchased this along with Unravel Two.This game came with a cute character design along with a realistic world. This helped bring the character to life and helped to create a bond between me and Yarny (who is the playable character). Yarny would also have different ways they would move depending on the situation. For example, at the start of the game Yarny moves freely and without an issue but when the story and mood get darker Yarny walks slower with their arms crossed. This helped to show how Yarny was feeling. Along with the music, this character-building worked perfectly.The puzzles that Yarny comes across are like no other game I have ever played. As Yarny is made of yarn, you must use the most efficient way to get around obstacles as possible. If Yarny uses too much yarn, yarny will start to become unstable and not be able to reach any further as there is no yarn left. I found this fun as it meant that the puzzle was not just a fact of getting to the end but was about the journey throughout the area. Also, Yarny can climb up their yarn, grapple onto anchor points and tie their yarn to the anchor points. Most interestingly, tying the yarn to the anchor points was most useful as this could be used to make a trampoline or to have an extra security meaning if Yarny was to fall, then they could stop themselves falling.Although this was not important in the grand scheme of things, I felt like the story needed some work. This was told in pictures that would appear throughout the levels. This meant that it was up to the player to figure out what the story was attempting to show. Sometimes this was unclear but the music helped to portray how the game was supposed to make me feel. This did not take away any enjoyment from the game.In conclusion, I enjoyed Unravel due to the gameplay, lovely scenery and great soundtrack. I felt like the story needed a bit of work but did not take away anything from the game. I also felt like at some points the game could get slightly repetitive. I feel like this game is worth playing if you like games in the puzzle platformer genre but I feel like there are better games than this with a better story.

_childDocuments_.review: Easiest game to review ever. It can be summed up with one word: beautiful. You can also add words like sad, deep, fun, and cute, but beautiful truly sums it up.This is a piece of art that proves games can convey so much. The game doesn't even use words, aside from the titles in the journal-like notebook. The gameplay, soundtrack, artwork, story, character, puzzles, and mechanics are all beautiful. Everything is beautiful in this game, and it's rare that I can say I have nothing to complain about. It's clear from the beginning that this will be a flawless experience. It's evident that heart was put into this game, especially in a time when other types of video games might offer easier profit.This game blew my mind and left me sad, contemplating life's meaning and worth. My eyes were wet by the end, and I barely managed not to cry.For achievement hunters: the game has 26 achievements, with some really, really frustrating to obtain. It was not the easiest completion of a game I've done. It was actually quite hard. So expect it if you want to go that road.To the developers, I appreciate and thank you, along with the publisher, for this experience. Please don't stop making games like this. And if you're a developer, in any field of game development, and you read this, consider creating content like this. Content you can look back on and be proud to have been part of the team that made it.

_childDocuments_.review: I saw a review where someone basically said that they didn't enjoy the game because after the first three levels, it gets really hard. They are not wrong about the game getting harder as it progresses. That's a pretty typical formula for games, after all. What they are wrong about is that the progression of difficulty makes the game less enjoyable. I think it makes it far more enjoyable.The first few levels are for finding your legs and figuring out how to use all the controls. After that, you're actually applying the controls in various ways where you have to figure out for yourself what will work and what won't. This isn't a game that explains every puzzle to you or stops you from experimenting with different options (within reason. It is still a linear game, not a sandbox). It does a great job of letting you feel like you're exploring a world even though you're following the path that they want you to. The graphics for this game are absolutely stunning. They make the world that much more immersive. The plot is fairly simple, but still evocative as you restore memories from the family whose house you're in as you look at their photos. If you're a fan of puzzles, physics-based, or platformers in any regard, then I think you'll probably enjoy this game. It's also a fairly quick play, It took me about 7.5 hours, including putting in a little extra work to find/get some of the collectibles.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, it's beautiful and heartwarming. I love the idea of a game about creating and keeping memories close to you.I personally felt very close to the game as I've been brought up in a family that loves mountain hiking and folk music, some of the scenes in the game reminded me of things I forgot from when I was very young.To conclude, I loved the gameplay, the music, the nostalgia, the gorgeous Swedish landscapes, and I definitely recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Take care of your elders. Great game. Visuals are great. Gameplay is creative. Art concept is great. Everything about this game is so simple and simply everything is so great. I mean, simplicity at it's best here. You don't need AAA budgets to create something big and this much impactful. I normally dislike EA pretty much but this time, they nailed it by supporting the producers.Also all credit goes to Coldwood Interactive either.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: When Unravel was first revealed by EA it was game that I was interested in right away. First because it looked beautiful and two it was definitely not a typical EA type game. Having now picked it up during the winter sale along with the sequel I can say I'm happy with my purchase. The game is definitely beautiful to look at while playing and the music is also pretty good. The platforming/puzzle are also fun. I've had trouble figuring out some of them at first but eventually figure out how to proceed. If you enjoy platformers and puzzle solving this is the game for you
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: super chilled ( sometimes harder than you think especially for secrets) awesome looking and sounding puzzle platformer.really enjoyed this, the physics are solid and act exactly like you expect which makes it so satisfying navigating the way through each level.now going straight onto unravel 2, out of library of 500+ mostly not played games, I'm seriously glad I picked these up to unwind with (pun intended ), just shy of 11 hours to end credits but so much more to find still.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. It's really hard to love something that comes from EA aside from the things that Respawn develop. But this game is worth installing the origin software that i really hate. I remember when this game announced in E3 and the developer crying and I knew in that moment that I will play it. The story heartwarming, the gameplay is fun and relaxing. Thanks for this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel was a lot better than I was expecting. I only played it because it comes with EA Play but I would buy this even if I didn't have EA Play.     The soundtrack... I don't even know, I have no words to explain how outstanding it is.     The puzzles too, they were extremely hindering at times. Usually when it comes to this I'll look to YouTube for help, but for this game I didn't. This game kept me playing until I solved it myself. It felt good. This... this game changed me... I am a new man!
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: You should try out this game if you're into platformers and puzzles. The art style and graphics is incredible, especially for 2016. The music on this game is also top notch and matches the vibe perfectly. It can however get a bit repetitive at times and some puzzles can be frustrating and not be entirely logical. If you're planning on playing Unravel 2 with a friend, this is probably a good warmup. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and sometimes emotional journey through the Swedish nature. The game has pretty low difficulty, and combined with the beautiful environments, it ends up being a nice and relaxing play (some puzzles can get a little bit challenging towards the end, but that is not generally the case).It seems that a lot of love has been poured into Yarni, and it shows from the very first minute. It put a smile on my face, and that is always a nice feeling.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: This is a gorgeous game with a beautiful storyline, and I love everything about it... except for the controls. As a gamer who doesn't like using a controller and relies on mouse and keyboard, I find the controls incredibly frustrating to use. I wish they'd gone a different way with it for players like me.I will continue to play and try to finish the game so I can play the next one, but if I wasn't such a sucker for knitting and the visuals, the controls would have potentially made me get a refund. Which is a shame, because it really is the only downside for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't do this game justice with a rushed review, so I'll try again to express how great it is. You will often find yourself just standing still and admiring the graphics and the music, and that's ok, enjoy it! You uncover a moving tale by exploring environments and discovering memories that end up as photos in a family album. Finding connections between these images and constructing a story around them was just as fun and satisfying as completing string puzzles. Because the game leans more towards puzzles than platforming, although they are not that difficult, it's understandable because it doesn't aim to be a masterpiece in precision and logic, but rather to convey a powerful message using amazing visuals while forcing you to think about progressing further, but just enough to keep you engaged.It's an old game by now, with a succesful co-op sequel, but I'll still call it my GOTY.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful little puzzler in a similar vein to Limbo and Inside in that the story (in this case) literally takes place in the background and it's very much up to the player to try to interpret what it all means.  I'm not really a fan of this method of story telling and it's easily ignored if it's just not gelling with you.I made the mistake of playing through Unravel 2 first and I'm finding it a little frustrating coming back to this one  The controls in the second game feel more refined and intuitive than they do here (which is probably to be expected) and in some sections, particularly those involving water, prepare to be annoyed when "the little red man" doesn't seem to want to do what you want him to do.Anyway, overall a worthwhile buy especially if you appreciate games that feel like a work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: This game is cute, charming, relaxing and easy on the eyes, with both its story and backstory heartwarming. Not only do I enjoy playing this game, I enjoy watching playthroughs of the game ala "Jacksepticeye" and others. Unravel - and its sequel "Unravel Two" - might not be for everyone, but I do recommend this game, if not at most giving it a chance
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game to play it with my sister.I am normally accustomed to different platforming Games, but this game is perfect, to play with a relative beginner.I let her play most passages, but when she needs help, I can take control in and help her.The Atmosphere is very nice and everything looks very pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Fantastically designed world with many different levels. Extraordinary detail and objects' variety. You will find a bunch of high-poly models with great dirty and rusty textures on them. Render quality is at the top level too.- Superb artistic approach. Everything is pure art, from the colors to the lighting. It is an immersive fairytale world.- Although the story initially seems to be simplistic and childish, it isn't. It manages to keep you interested till the end. The story gave me some strong emotions without seeing them coming. The memories and photos you collect are romantic without being weepy or cliché.- It packs some clever puzzles of easy to medium difficulty. Although you will mostly tie and untie threads you won't get bored at all.- The rhythm of the game is great. Where it is relaxing for a while and you must solve a puzzle, then you have to run because a bird attacked you. Great changes of speed that never let you get bored.- Nice gameplay mechanics. The main character is responsive and everything works fine. The actions are few, so you will quickly get used of them.- Great smooth animations. Your character performs a big variety of moves that change depending the terrain you are on. The environment and the animals have very natural animations too.- Physics feel so natural. Good job.- The music is fantastic. Every level has a different track. It fits perfectly to the rhythm and the visual aesthetics.- Nice cinematic approach. It transforms the game to an interactive 3d movie. Good camera movement. Cool overall direction.- The animals you meet are really well-crafted. The environment feels more alive with them in it. They are funny too.- The red budges you collect (if you choose so) give an extra challenge. Nice addition.- The main character is adorable and unforgettable.- If you had a hard day, just calm and play Unravel. It is so relaxing.The bad- I found  the bokeh and bloom effects way too much. They make everything at the background so blurry and shiny. Sometimes they ruin the atmosphere.- There is an annoying flickering at some models. Not everywhere but often enough.- Every time you want to change level you have to walk (and climb) the same room. Again and again. After a while it becomes extremely boring.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: A very polished and beautiful game, with a unique spin on platforming. Varied environments and emotional moments, which make for a compelling and challenging journey echoing life itself. I was so impressed! The team really put their heart and soul into this project and it really shows. Totally recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: I've never cried so much after a game, and I do that often. Unravel is masterpiece, by art, by music, by story and story arc, by composition, by design and by conscious procedural rhetoric. We can speak about catharsis here. If You have sensitive soul and grew up in a small village, this game will break your heart and put it together again.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: For a game about adorable little yarn creature that runs around and collects yarn pins, there are sure lots of things trying to kill you. Sometimes it feels more like you are playing Limbo 2 with the amount of ways Yarny dies (most of which are odd because he is made of, well, yarn.) Plus there are occasional physics bugs that force you to restart the level from the beginning, but these are rare. Nonetheless, it is very fun little game with beautiful scenery that doesnt overstay it's welcome and keeps things fresh each level.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: I had already played this on the Xbox One way back but I definitely wanted to play this again. This game is truly an experience despite its short playthrough. There are collectibles you can find in each level to add onto your time but the game itself isn't too long and not too short. This is one of the few games that really has me thinking and gets me in the feels, especially towards the end of the game. The visuals are insanely good, it is like watching a little yarn creature in a real life environment. The environments are really detailed on max settings and i'm always shocked how good it looks. If you want a game where you can relax, solve a few puzzles using things around you in the game, this is the one to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel is a gorgeous work of art that tells a nice story about a family's memories from the perspective of a yarn character sewn by the grandma. Although a bit short, many of the levels are breathtaking to experience and the puzzle platforming rarely becomes a nuisance. It is well worth a playthrough and there's not many games like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: A very gorgeous game that oozes passion. As a fellow made of yarn, you make your way through the beautiful (and often daunting) swedish landscape. The graphics and general visual design are the star of the show here: everything looks amazing and every single level is just full of detail and packed with visual glee.When it comes to gameplay, Unravel is the standard platformer with a small twist: since you are made of yarn, you can use it as a lasso to swing yourself over gaps, or tie knots to create bridges and small trampolines. You also only have a limited amount of yarn available, so the challenge becomes reaching the next bundle of yarn to "refill" your body. Those also act as checkpoints.The game also features some simple puzzling, none of which is too difficult due to the somewhat limited amount of things you can do anyway (though there were two or three headscratchers). The game works well most of the time. Its not quite all sunshine in the swedish landscape though. Some of the platforming challenges are a little frustrating, as the  lasso swing mechanic does not always work well with the physics of the game. Still, the checkpoints are very forgiving and it usually only takes a few tries. You cant really get angry at this cute game anyway. The music consists mostly of violins and while very engrossing at first, by the end of the game you are fine with not hearing a violin for quite a while. Still, the soundtrack fits and is atmospheric enough.Overall this is a somewhat short (around 5 hours or so) must play for anyone who likes platformers and games with gorgeous visual design.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: This game has become my new favorite. I love puzzle games and this one is cute and has its challenges. You are this little Yarn Demon and you are going through memories to find photos and little yarn ornaments. During the Memories you are faced with puzzles, challenges, and the over all environment. Your yarn is your life line it can run out or break. This game was very well thought out on how to interact with everything around you. I wound up getting the second one as well which is 2 player and my family just loves it as much as I do.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting for a few years to get around to buying it, Unravelled finally appeared in the Steam store a few weeks ago, along with it's co-op based sequel in a bundle for the sweet price of $15 (from memory). After finishing Gorogoa a few weeks ago, I wanted to play another short puzzler with loads of charm. Unravelled delivered in spades!The game starts with an old lady reminiscing about her life, but with an empty photo album. That's where you come in - a bright red doll made of wool. Your job is to revisit various places where her memories took place and recover the treasures left behind.Right off the bat, the game just exudes charm. Not only does the sombre folk music set the tone, the programmers managed to have your little woollen doll display emotion without saying a word. You can easily see joy, fear, sadness, surprise... the whole gamut, just by the shape of the eyes and the doll's posture. To get around the game you'll lasso and swing between various pieces of furniture, nails, fences, posts, and anywhere else that red bits of fuzz are found. You'll need to do this in the relative safety of the house to get to the different levels, accessed by photos located around the home. Venturing outside, tying your string to two items creates a trampoline, allowing you to explore other areas to find the occasional secret item to add to the photo album.The game itself isn't overly tricky. The puzzles are easy enough to work out without having to resort to a guide, although some solutions can involve a little lateral thinking (although one of the more tricky puzzles isn't as tricky to any aussie during Swooping Season :-) ). That being said, the final level had me rage quit after being sent back to a save point dozens of times before I was halfway through it. As you finish a level, the photo album fills another chapter and gives some context to the level you just played.The game is fairly short. I started playing it occasionally at night during the week after work two and a half weeks ago and took me about 11 hours all up to complete. Totally worth the wait from when I first saw this game back in 2015.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly, If your having crashing issues with the game either starting up.. or for me was when i was trying to enter a picture(level). After some researching, seeing a posted fix from other people having the same issues. It was a windows media player codec conflict. I uninstalled the codec i had, installed K-lite standard codec, and it never crashed again.Secondly you'll need to create or link your origin account to steam to play, which is kind of lame, but seems that's how EA games are gonna be. I don't like or use origin for anything, but if that's whats required for me to play the EA games I want on steam, so be it. I set up origin to run minimized and disabled the in-game overlay.Lastly, the game is beautifully done, backdrops are amazing. It's a fun experience. Puzzles are nothing super difficult, but needed some thought. for me it was kinda like if Limbo was in a bright, much lighter atmosphere.Edit- I bought this on sale bundled with Unravel 2 for like 10 bucks or something. Worth it for sure on sale.. not sure about full price...
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: This game is OK. It has a decent concept and the gameplay is generally good. BUT there are two major let downs.1. Origin seems much more annoying to deal with in this game than it does in any of the other EA titles I've played recently. It's 2020. We shouldn't have to deal with this.2. the checkpointing doesn't seem to work. If I quite and reload a level, even if I pass a swirly checkpoint, it places me much further back, which is very annoying and makes it difficult to leave and return later.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fantastic game, I highly highly recommend it.I see in a lot of the negative reviews that they couldn't figure out how to get into a level, or beat some part of the game, and I beg you, please do not listen to those reviews. Anybody who cannot beat this game is either about 8 years old, or incredibly stupid. It's not an easy game, but it's absolutely not impossible. there are so many games I can think of that are much more difficult than this game. This is NOT the Dark Souls of 2D platformers.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: A chill and relaxing game to play on your own. I give the developer so much respect when he came up on stage of E3 2016. He looked so nervous, but he was so wholesome. He even had his own Yarny doll. I immediately wanted to support him, And I got the game on ps4, 4 years later on steam and I still enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel is a really good puzzle platformer. You play as Yarny, a magical Yarn creature trying to bring the family together by collecting memories of them. The objective of the game is to collect secrets and get the memory (in the form of a stitch pattern) at the end. The odd thing is that the play time is less than 7 hours to completion. Gameplay-wise, best to use a controller. RT for shooting your string, LT for hanging onto said string, Square to tie the string down (mostly to make springboards).Conclusion, do try Unravel. However, note that <1% of all the accounts actually completed the game. The puzzles are not easy.1. Puzzle DesignI loved it. The whole string mechanic was lovely.2. GraphicsFantastical. I loved 3. Interesting MechanicsThe acorn turning into a snowball, the freezing winds blowing you off, the ravens attacking you from the background,1. Short, too Short7 hours gameplay.2. The Bucket From The Well Has a BugIt is possible to drop the bucket in the well, resulting in a incomplete game.1. Maybe a Few More Stages?The dark room in the back would have been great to add a few more levels to round up the play time to 10 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: As you complete levels you piece together the story line, which builds emotional momentum throughout the game play. The mechanisms and physics of the game are simple, but well thought out with lots of adventure and puzzle elements. The music is wonderful as well (gives the game an almost Irish twist). I would label this game Buddhist, in that the journey is actually more important than the destination and you gather that by the end of your experience. There is a sequel and I will definitely give it a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended on sale.As usual, unity-like frustrating controls are present. But the style is pretty, the music is fitting and soothing, so this is a good game for relaxing.The most amusing part for me were the credits. 10 people, that actually made the game (honestly, other similar indy games are made with just two people), but those people are then complemented with about 100 people from EA, which noone of us are capable to understand what were actually doing. This clearly allows us to understand, why EA is such a cash grab entity.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: A stunning game, after 4 hours of playing I'm loving it more and more. The music is wonderfully calm yet atmospheric when it needs to be without being OTT. The game play itself is simple yet I find myself challenged to just the right level throughout. A genius concept for a storyline and a beautiful game to play, both audibly and visually - a moment of calm in this crazy pandemic era world.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and art style is wonderful.Really like the vibe of the game.Makes me happy.A lot of negative reviewes says that the puzzles are bad but I think they are really good.Music is also good.PC controls are bad but I used my Switch Pro controller so it's fine.Mechanics are cool.Love the dynamic enviorments
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game with beautiful audiovisual style, depicting the scandinavian nature and decaying buildings and machinery. Gameplay is based on physics of the yarn trailing bahind the player character. It is very smooth and I never got stuck up for long trying to figure how  to continue. The story is fragmentary, more about setting the mood. It is filled with nostalgia, melancholy and, in the end, hope.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: A combination of puzzler and sidescrolling platformer with beautiful visuals and folk music-like background music. Unfortunately it's a recurring problem that the character gets stuck in the air after using lasso to attach somewhere. It can be temporarily helped, but keeps occuring again and again after the first instance, and most of the time seems to require a restart of the game to actually be resolved. Still would recommend for puzzle lovers and casual gamers.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel offers players a journey in the shoes of Yarney, a sweet little character made from yarn as he goes on adventures through diverse, stunning, dangerous, puzzle filled environments. With beautiful graphics and filled with stunning environments to explore, with the addition of new and interesting gameplay mechanics and a nice accompanying soundtrack, (though can sound repetitive in some areas) Unravel is a fun and touching storytelling experience that's sure to pull on your heart strings. 9.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Before this game I didn't know red yarn was all over the place. This game taught me the true meaning of red yarn and how much you use. Thank you!Other than that, the game is fantastic. Kinda reminds me of "Little Big Planet" in a way. Love how you can interact with certain objects and swing around the trees. The level designs only gets better the further you get in the game. So many screenshots can be taken in the game itself, and they're perfect for your profile showcase's. Can't wait to finish the game out and play the second version, and just maybe... co-op with someone.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: This game is visually beautiful! Amazing details! If you like the outdoors then you'll love the visual. For me, the game was very contemplative and relaxing. 2 or 3 levels weren't very relaxing but I don't want to spoil it for you.A couple of puzzles/sections are quite challenging but not frustratingly so. The game isn't very difficult to finish. I have yet to gather all of the hidden objects, tho. I do wish that there were more "boss" fights.Side note:Have to install Origin and create an account with EA.Also have to be online to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics, animations and controls are really good. Calm, relaxing soundtrack. The puzzles/gameplay is fine. Haven't finished it yet so can't say much about the story. No bugs or technical issues yet. Based on the average time to beat the game, I wouldn't say it's worth the full price, but at 50% off it's fine. Shame it requires Origin though, that and no achievements almost made me avoid buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the entire story of this game when I got it a few years ago on the Xbox One. This game is absolutely fantastic and I cannot wait to play it all over again. The gameplay is simple, the visuals are amazing, and the music is absolutely perfect. A tad annoyed it made me install Origin just to play it, but I can look past that for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel

_childDocuments_.review: Yarny's mission is to mend broken bonds and the yarn represents the love and connection between people. The player will use Yarny's thread to do things such as swinging across gaps or rappelling down trees. Te game will also challenge gamers to use the thread in clever and creative ways. [Electronic Arts]

name: Unravel Two
detailed_description: PLAY ON STEAM USING THE REMOTE PLAY TOGETHER FEATURE When you cut ties to the past, new bonds form. In Unravel Two, create a Yarny of your very own. Then build relationships with other Yarnys in local co-op or as a single player, fostering friendship and support as you journey together. Begin your adventure in a cold and imposing land, then watch your surroundings blossom with new life as you chase the spark of adventure. Dive into an immersive story filled with energy, exuberance, inspiration — even monsters. Approach every challenge with positivity and fearlessness to awaken the world around you, and discover an unbreakable bond between friends. Key Features: Two Yarnys – always! Form a bond with friends and other players in seamless local co-op. Support each other as you solve tricky trials and seamlessly traverse enchanting worlds together. Or, as a single player, create two Yarnys of your own and unlock special abilities along your adventure. World of wonders. Inspired by real Scandinavian locations, navigate beautiful natural landscapes and complex urban environments, seeing it all through the eyes of Yarny. As you progress, watch your world flourish and evolve, opening fresh challenges and spaces to explore. Playful problem solving . Uncover a variety of ways to play. Jump, slide, swing and run faster than ever to chase the spark that connects you to others as you travel within a world of challenges and adventures. Heartfelt storytelling. Enter a world where unique emotions manifest into friendly characters, fulfilling relationships and even intimidating monsters. How will you use hope and love to defeat doubt and fear? Connect to an engaging and dramatic story that demonstrates the power of positivity in the face of uncertainty.

Unless you can be at the same room or stream the game to your friend via Parsec or Steam Remote etc, there is no way to play it together. I was a bit disappointed by the co-op part, but it's a good game in everything else. Interesting locations, modern graphics, enjoyable gameplay and etc and etc. The soundtrack lines up with everything else pretty well.7.5 / 10

My only gripe is lack of ultrawide (CRG9) support.”10 year old daughter says: “I like it because it’s fun to play with my sister and really fun to figure out how to go through all the obstacles.”7 year old daughter says: “I like how its adventurous and that each level is new and mysterious. _childDocuments_.review: Requires a controller to play with someone, so if you are on PC without it - u need emulators on both computers you gonna play. I used Jocys. But the fact of the need to set everything up(and figure out it first) almost made us delete and get a refund. Glad we did not. The game is fun to play for anyone who can overcome the hassle of setting up controller emulator on PC.A quick guide to play on PC:1. You don't need to buy the game on both PCs, one game copy is sufficient.2. You will need to install Origin.3. Install controller emulator on both devices if you don't have a controller. I used Jocys.4.Make sure it is visible in steam. Go steam>settings5. Run the game, right click on ur friend in steam and invite to steam remote play.6. Make sure you have different controllers assigned and keyboard of your friend is not active in the window you will see. Should be good to go after. If you lost feed at some point, try restarting the game on both computers - works for us.UPD:Made a guide with screenshots:

_childDocuments_.review: This review includes both Unraveled and Unraveled 2.  I played them back to back, but played #2 first, solely for the Couch Coop with my wife.  Wow, both of these games are insanely immersive.  The graphics, and the music is top notch beautiful.  The biggest difference between the two is the Coop of #2.  The levels are not terribly hard but are just hard enough.  Unraveled 2 also had+ Better and More Consistent Movement+ More Carefree Swinging+ Carry your teammate+ Bonus Challenge Levels.  (Hard)After finishing #2,  I went back and played the first one.  Almost immediately, I noticed two things.  The puzzles were harder, and you died a lot.  In fact, I know we died here and there in #2, but I didn't notice it like I did in #1.  About half way through the second chapter, it dawned on me what this game really was.  It's basically Limbo with beautiful imagery, music, and a lasso.  If you enjoyed Limbo, or Little Nightmares, this is an easy recommend.  I got both games on sale for  a little less than $10 and got about 25 hours between the two games.  So that seemed like a good deal.  I enjoyed both of them, but if you don't have a coop partner, the better game is the first one.  The first one has better puzzles and there are more of them.Only ConRequires Origin to play.  It's a minor ding, but that crap shouldn't be necessary for games bought on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: While the first  (released in 2016) offered a purely singleplayer-experience featuring a protagonist made out of yarn (“Yarny”), its 2018-sequel set out to take things even further: while still offering a singleplayer option,  can also be played together via couch coop (although this can be taken online using Steam Remote Play as well). And as it turns out, the resulting game makes  a prime option to introduce someone unfamiliar with the genre to platforming games.But let’s start with a quick overview:  tells the tale of two Yarnys, adorable-looking beings made out of yarn and permanently connected via a thread. In a 4 to 5h story told without any dialogue, the two Yarnys set out on an adventure in Sweden and explore forests, villages, rivers and more. To pass obstacles in their way, the Yarnys can use their yarn to perform various activities, like swinging from a branch or building a makeshift trampoline. Surprisingly, the game never really runs out of obstacles that force players to use their yarn abilities in new ways – even in the final level  still introduces new ideas to play around with.That said,  clearly was made with more casual/younger players in mind. As such, many of the obstacles/jumping puzzles you encounter are offering their solution at first glance. Additionally,  also offers a hint system as well as the option to slow down time at the press of a button, if the platforming proves too challenging. Finally, as the Yarnys are – as mentioned – always connected via a thread of yarn, it’s usually enough for one player to pass the platforming sections – as they can simply pull up the other player using said interconnected thread of yarn.That doesn’t mean that  doesn’t offer any challenge to more experienced players at all. There are optional challenge levels, which can be significantly harder, as well as gold medals for completing levels under a certain time limit & without dying once. However, the strength of  lies in its ability to offer a coop experience that even players of different skill level can participate in.Why? Apart from the hints and slow-motion,  also offers the Yarnys the ability to merge together. That means even if all other option to make the experience easier fail, one player can simply merge with the other and let themselves be carried throughout the jumping puzzle (for example). Yes, there are obstacles that can only be passed while both players are doing something (e.g. one is distracting an angry bird while the other one is using the distraction to sneak past it). But during my playthrough, me and my partner always had ways to help each other out if one of us was struggling.The other reason why  is perfect for introducing someone to platforming is its charm. With adorable protagonists, lovely music and charming graphics showcasing Sweden from a new (read: small) perspective,  is simply a delight to look at – be it for adults or children. There are some slightly less peaceful levels, like sneaking through a factory full of machines and steam, but even these should be okay for older children (6+).  Simply put,  is an incredible charming game to play with someone who doesn’t usually play videogames. But even players of higher skill level should have fun in this great, albeit short, experience. While I wouldn’t recommend  at its full price considering its length, definitely grab this one on sale if you’re looking for some light coop puzzle-platforming fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Picked up this game with the 50% off for myself and my 10 year old daughter to play as she has wanted this game for awhile.  She did most of the first one, I did very little of it out of frustration as I seemed to not know what to do.  This second one is a huge improvement, it is fun, fast paced, easier to figure out what to do next and the graphics are truly amazing.   The pigeons look real!  Movement and controls are smooth and responsive, if you didn't make the jump you didn't do it right.  She has motored through it on solo and is unhappy she has seemed to have reached the end, so looks like it might not be as long as it should be.  However, playing with someone else is really really fun, especially with a giggling 10 year old which in light of that, this game could be geared to much younger people.  She had no trouble figuring out the puzzles and was teaching me!  The checkpoint system is fantastic, it saved us many times, achievements are so-so.  The most frustrating thing is its connection with Origin, took awhile to get things synced properly.  Origin can't seem to get people to buy from them so forcing this through Steam is kinda dirty pool to me.  But coop does work nicely and I laughed my butt off the whole time.  Only a couple of hours in but can't wait to play again tonight, can't see me wanting to play solo, it really is a true coop game.  My hopes are there will be additions to the game to come, it seems short so be sure to get it on sale.  Entertaining and family friendly so far, using a controller seems to be best.  Fun one to pick up but do not pay full price, I can't say it would be worth double.  Still a thumbs up from me.

You play as a little man of wool climbing, swinging, solving puzzles with you friend, all while avoiding getting burnt, crushed, drowned, or eaten by chicken/fish. _childDocuments_.review: I’m a big fan of games that let you hug.This is a brilliant game. One of the few my wife’s boyfriend will play with me.Gave it to my daughter when she turned 7 a couple of weeks ago and we’re playing through it right now. So much fun to play together with your kids as it’s so calm and serene and they can take their time solving the puzzles and hitting the right spots for the jumps and swings.This is a great game for two people who are at different levels of ability. In most cases, if one player can nail the platforming, the other player can either hop on and ride along, or can climb the connecting rope to get there instead of jumping. Can not recommend this enough as the next stepping stone for your kids once they can handle Kirby or Yoshi. The fact that it takes two players but all puzzles can be solved with one player stationary is key for my little one to enjoy it. Really loved playing this with my 7 year old. She’s up for adoption now though.Story wise there’s something there but it’s too vague and difficult to put together. The Souls series had a vague approach to their story, but in-game descriptions and dialogue helped piece it together, leaving only a few gaps here and there for player interpretation.With Unravel I’m left wondering just what these devs were going for. I can tell there’s something there but I can’t even begin to figure it out. Simply put, I have the same feeling for Unravel as I do Death Stranding. I have no idea what the f*ck is going on but I love it. At the end I mostly ignored the seemingly sad story and my wife’s boyfriend and I just laughed at our little yarn dudes.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel Two is a cute, wonderful, small game. It can be played both solo and in co-op. I would highly recommend playing the game with a spouse or with kids. It could be a great bonding experience. 	The gameplay is solid. Controls feel very responsive and fluid. Swinging on ropes and building momentum while in the air is satisfying. Puzzles are interesting and engaging. Platforming sections might take couple of tries but they are perfectly doable. Each challenge is designed both for co-op and solo play, which is great. Players interested in harder challenges can try out bonus levels which offer harder puzzles and very difficult platforming areas.	Graphics and music are beautiful and only add to this wonderful experience. The story is a subject open for interpretation. For this reason some people will completely ignore it while others might find it endearing. 	Playing this game with my wife was a fantastic decision. We have not only finished every level but we also acquired a gold medal for a speedrunning challenge in each level. This was quite a tremendous task, with many fails and arguments. But for every argument we had, the triumph after finally acquiring a gold medal felt more powerful. I am grateful for this experience.	We recommend this game.If you are interested in a longer video version of this review, containing details of our speedrun then check out my youtube channel:

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel Two focuses on creating puzzles that utilize yarn-based mechanics, perhaps to use the theme that was at best an unrealized idea from the first Unravel. The clunky controls of Unravel are thankfully fixed, and the result in Two makes for some really playable puzzles. However, Unravel Two completely abandons the story. While the puzzles certainly added variety to the Unravel series, these improvements were insufficient to make a good game. There is no emotional connection, no point to the atmosphere, no reason for the enemies that kill the yarn creatures. The puzzles are also somewhat ruined by a glittering firefly that always tells you exactly what to do to solve every puzzle.  To bring some challenge back into the game that was stolen by that spoiler-giving firefly, many solutions require speed or reflexes or skillful dodging of enemies rather than contemplative puzzling.As we played through this game, we kept having so many "why?" moments. Why are there now two yarn creatures? Why am I watching memories of children getting chased by adults and then start a forest fire?  Why is the lighthouse being attacked by Satan's demons!?  Then the credits rolled and it all made sense.  The developer proudly announced "we tried to move away from conventional hierarchies and let consensus rule."  In effect, this game has no vision, no creative direction, and no purpose.  The game shows a severe lack of a director to weed out good ideas from the great ideas.  The result is an ill-conceived mess that makes no sense.

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel Two is a coop platformer game, which you can play it alone too, and your goal is to go into memorise and get energy for the lighthouse.I played this game in coop mode, so my opinion will based on that.Graphically this game is wonderful. All of the "outside" areas (Forest, Campsite, Lumberyard etc.) are beautiful! Also the underground parts looks good, but for me some "inside" are looked bit boring comparing to the other ones. Animations are looking good too, but game has visual bugs like characters getting inside each other, sometimes the string goes in to props or in the ground or few effects looks off, but this is just nitpicking.Controls are pretty easy to memorize. You can play the game with keyboard and controller, but the game itself wants you to play with controller, but it's really whatever. Besides the direction keys, you need to use 3 different action button and the jump button. There is a button for slowning down time, but we never used it, also there are buttons for hints and tips, but that's really it. Also, there are emote buttons too. It's responsive and works really good!Music and sounds is also a bright point in the game. All of the places in the game has an unique music and also different ares in the places has different music again. These are really fits for the current scene and situation. Sounds effect are also good to listen, not annoying in long term.The gameplay is pretty straight forward. You start from the beginning of the level and you go till the end with the other character or with your partner. You have to do lot of jumping or normal puzzles to get through different places and there are fast action parts on the map, where you can't really think what you need to do, but you need to do it. This is really well mixed, there are no boring bits or feeling that some parts are longer than it should be. Also you can collect... we call those "coins", because it sounds that when you picking it up, and if you collect all of that, you can see a picture in the lighthouse. Also if you finish the map, you see one or two pictures too, related to the map.You can also customize your character, change it's colors. There are challanges for the levels and also there are challange levels to the related levels, which are indeed hard, and we will look into those more hopefully. If you finish those, you get more character parts.The game's difficulty is really mixed. The first 2 levels were pretty easy, but later all of the levels had a harder part or parts where you need to think more. I didn't mind it and it didn't felt annoying at all. The game is not too long, if you focus on the story, you can complete it in 7 hours but there are challanges too.The game is really fun to play, but I can only recommend to play this with a partner, alone is not that interesting in my opinion. As I wrote before, things looks good in it, and some parts are challanging, some parts are not really. I recommend to buy the game if it's on sale, or buy EA Play and try the game with that. Remote play is a bit interesting to play with, because I didn't find a way to play the game with keyboard only. I had to play with controller and my partner was able to play with keyboard, but I probably missed something.Good game, I can recommend it for some fun time!

_childDocuments_.review: First thing to know: if you have any issues with Steam Remote Play due to the Origin implementation, use Parsec instead. _childDocuments_.review: I just wanted to be a little piece of wholesome yarn with my friend online and now I'm left sitting here with nothing more than a ball of shattered dreams and $7 poorer.Starting game. Realise instantly that the key bindings are automatically mapped to the ARROW KEYS and not WASD like every other game ever. When I try and change the key bindings on my keyboard, it refuses to recognise the alt arrow keys so I have to dig out my old keyboard to even navigate the menu. Fine. I really really wanna be a little piece of wholesome yarn with my buddy, so I dig it out of the back of my closet where I stashed it. FINALLY am able to actually play the game. Amazing. Start playing through tutorial, waiting for the point where I can join games with my buddy. It isn't happening. He googles it and finds out that it's COUCH CO OP ONLY. But the game description tags have "coop" and "local coop" separately, shouldn't that mean we can play together on 2 separate computers? It means "Remote Play Together" is the only way to make it work from 2 separate computers? GREAT. So we BOTH bought a game that only one of us had to buy. He puts in for a game refund. I just wanna be a little piece of wholesome yarn with my buddy. THAT'S ALL. WHY IS THIS TAKING SO LONG?!Finally, FINALLY, have things sorted out. I invite him to Remote Play Together in my game. He offhandedly mentions that in his previous googling, it specifies that you absolutely positively HAVE to have at least one game controller for the game to be coop playable. You can't both be using keyboards to play. On a PC game, you can't both be using keyboards. NEITHER OF US have a controller that works with our PC, we have keyboards like normal regular people. So after a half an hour of hunting down my old keyboard and googling the stupidly confusing hurdles that this game presents to an average pair of PC gamers, I CAN'T BE A LITTLE BALL OF WHOLESOME YARN.I am left sitting here, at the end of my rope, absolutely GUTTED and now contemplating dropping the $40 to buy It Takes Two like every single streamer is doing right now. Because THAT GAME doesn't hate PC users. This one clearly does.

_childDocuments_.review: You've seen, played and experienced everything, so you expect more from the second installment than just chewing on a two-year-old morsel. Unfortunately, you won't get much more. Respectively, you get one thing that looks great: you can play all of Unravel Two in local co-op with a friend.There are two figures on the screen at once. They both bounce, they both solve logic puzzles, they help each other and sometimes they get in each other's shoes. And in two it is, quite unsurprisingly, a lot of fun.Unravel Two will take you somewhere around five, maybe seven hours. Depending on how much you get stuck on the more challenging passages, of which there are quite a few. The peculiar pace of the game will not make it easier for you to pass through a beautiful landscape with a too blurry background. In the first half, it is a really simple, accessible hopscotch, where you don't solve much and go on autopilot.And it's fine. For connoisseurs of the first game, it's not about anyone's discovery fun, the game doesn't even try to do anything else, but you won't get bored. Then comes an imaginary record scratch and the game suddenly swings into an uncompromising hardcore platformer, where the difficulty of hopping does not match the difficulty of puzzles.

_childDocuments_.review: Tangled with a partner.Story:In Unravel Two you play as not one, but two Yarny's. After a nasty shipwreck you find yourself stranded on a small island, with your thread cut off, you bind yourself to another Yarny that has lost his strand as well. You take shelter in a nearby Lighthouse and explore the memories of two kids that escaped from an orphanage. The story this time around isn't nowhere near as good as the previous game, but still has some really nice themes that mesh well with the tone of the game. The themes of connection are genuinely heartwarming and I especially loved the closing credits with the heartfelt note by the developers which made the experience that much more poignant.Graphics:The art style is pretty much the same as the first Unravel game just a lot more refined. There's less levels, but they're connected by multiple different environments. So for example you explore the area near the orphanage and then progress into the city streets or explore someone's backyard and then move onto the forest behind it. The realistic nature of the graphics, does wonders to translate the Swedish nature into game form. I also have to mention Yarny again. I absolutely loved his design in the first game, he's an adorable little guy and now there's two of them and their characteristics are adorable as they're animated very well, like hugging and high fiving each other after a very stressful situation. Also you can customize them in a menu and you unlock more by rescuing other Yarny's and there's some really cool looking options to personalize your own Yarny. Audio:The audio design is also incredibly top notch. The soundtrack is very similar to the first game as it has somber music in the more dramatic moments of the game, cheery music in the happier moments and intense music when you're going through the more intense moments of the game. The music sounds like it could have been stripped straight out of the first game, but it's definitely new. Not say that it's a bad thing, because it's definitely not, as the music is really good matching the tone of the first game.There's of course other sound effects that you encounter while going through this adventure, but again it's not the main focus here. There's machine whirring, nature noises like birds water running etc. It again makes each level feel unique from an atmosphere standpoint and I loved each level because of it. Gameplay:Unravel Two is essentially the same game as the first as it's a physics based platformer where you solve puzzles, do some platforming, but this time around you have another Yarny tagging along for the ride. So I'll quickly go through the main gameplay. The gameplay is a lot more refined this time around. Most of the gameplay mechanics make a comeback this time around as in swinging with your yarn lasso, creating bridges with your stands to move items and using them as a trampoline and of course you're still avoiding enemies that want to kill you. Also the new wall jump move is also really satisfying to use, with a minor negative being that it's not really clear what walls you can wall jump off sometimes, which will lead into your death a few times,Most of my issues from the first game have been addressed. The swinging especially feels a lot more responsive and linking them together is a lot for satisfying, because unless you really mess up, the momentum you build up will be kept between swings. The bridges are also used to a minimum, but they work much better because you don't have to find a sweet spot, all you do is stand on it and press jump and it will launch you into the sky. So let's talk about the biggest change which is the second Yarny. I was at first worried playing this solo as controlling two characters at the same time is a rather complex thing to pull of correctly, but I never felt that I was dragged by the other character. You can carry the second Yarny on your back when you're just running around and platforming and detach yourself from him when it's time to solve puzzles. You can use the second character as an anchor point between platforms and as block  to keep certain platforms from moving.The puzzles themselves are fine and just slightly harder than the first game, but nothing that will stump you. Some of them might look scary on the surface, but once you figure out how to make those pieces move it all will click in your brain and the solution will follow close behind. There's also a bunch of bonus levels, which are much harder than the main levels and they will really test your skill as they are much harder than anything from the main story of both games, so there's definitely more value here for those who want a bit more after wrapping up the game.However one big negative is that there's no Online Co-Op. I get that the themes are about connection and I'm glad there is local co-op, but I wish the developers could have added an online mode for those with friends that are not capable to sit down for a 5 hour journey at your house. Verdict:Unravel Two is a great sequel and is much better than the first game. Fun new gameplay mechanics, refined old mechanics and everything else that already worked in the previous game comes back much stronger here. There are a few minor issues, but they are nothing compared to the top notch quality of the game.Final Rating:9.5/10Pros:+ Yarny is back and brought a friend you can customize to your liking.+ Fun new gameplay mechanics and refined old ones+ Tons of cool environments + Really good audio design + Provides both a casual and challenging experience for those seeking one outCons:- Story is slightly weaker this time around- No Online CO-OPIf you liked this review please consider joining  and

_childDocuments_.review: I adore Unravel Two, simply. Allow me to elaborate:So I guess we're all here from Unravel I(which if you haven't played, you definitely should/ have to), so we already know the ropes of this game.Unravel Two also took place in Sweden(my goat country), and told a different story from Unravel I, while also strongly upscaling Unravel I's graphics by several degrees. You think Unravel I is beautiful? Unravel Two is Breathtaking. Every minor detail was taken care of with love. It's like the Toy Story of video game, you get to see the miniature world of things that we humans are incapable of perceiving: things like a pinecone, a cog, a stone, a broken branch, and even an animal like a pike. You get to see all that from the perspective of a tiny yarn doll. Excellent creativity, that. Graphically speaking, this game is 10 out of 10. Forget all about the nitpicking of AAA titles, you come here to feel.I wouldn't delve into the story too much, since I don't feel personally connected to it(I'm still hung up on Unravel I's story), but I do enjoy it, and think about it often.The music in this game is as good as the first one, maybe even better than a few notches. Tracks like "Problem Solving" and "Let it All Out" really brought out the talent of the musician, Frida Johansson(Oh I so love her with all my heart). Play the game, and enjoy the music. Finally, about technicalities and price. I bought it on sale, and so should you. It's optimized very well and runs with absolutely no bugs whatsoever. Yes, it's a goodie.Conclusion: Yes, buy and play it, and tell others about it. Share the soundtrack, share the love. Be the positive gamer you want to see in the world.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has excellent movement and tight controls and the good pretty much stops there. Levels are exceptionally long and drawn out, repeating the same kind of puzzle ad naseum, for level after level with zero new mechanics ever introduced. The puzzles get more difficult to solve or more precise to complete, but in variety and imagination nothing changes. Though this game is couch co-op, a lot of rooms are best completed with one person riding on the other's back since having both people make it through a challenging section is exponentially harder than having only one person make it through.There don't seem to be any secrets in this game or meaning for collection. Every once in a while you'll see a sparkly thing you can jump into and it plays this dramatic sound as you pick it up but they don't actually do anything and I'm not sure if the game even tracks your getting them. The highlight of the game comes in the form of challenge levels, which show far more creativity than the regular levels. These challenge levels are the only way to actually unlock new content in this game, in the form of costume choices, but the actual variety in costumes is so low as to be comical. You'll unlock 20 pairs of nearly identical eyes, and 20 garments that cover, in great detail, the range between "long shirt" and "short dress." You'll also get 6 different shades of nearly identical reds, although you don't have to unlock those, you get all the colors from the start.

I was always more interested in the subtlety of the two Yarny’s relationship to become too intrigued by the human element.With a gorgeous world to travel through and some lovely puzzles to solve, Unravel Two can be a perfect game to enjoy alone or with friends. The movement is similar to the original with only a couple of new moves to help you progress, there isn’t loads of new features, but that doesn’t make it dull. Even though you’re limited to what you can do, there are many ways to use what you’ve got, making it more of the same, however, if that’s what you loved about the first then you’re in for double the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: As a "more of the same" sequel Unravel Two does its job, but it's nothing great compared to the first one which I consider the best. Graphics, art, level design and soundtrack are still great, but due to the lack of online co-op I played it as a single player game and maybe that's the problem. Switching between two Yarnys just to solve puzzles often interrupts the flow, while having another real person playing as one of them would add much more dynamism and fun to the gameplay. Yes, the game supports remote play together, but that's a Steam feature and it's not as good as having a online co-op mode. The story narrated in the background is a basic tale of child abuse that doesn't get you engaged, with some parts unclear and the morale being literally written at the end.In conclusion, Unravel Two is a good game for kids and families or if you can play it with a friend.As a solo experience you will like it but also get slightly disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: (READ ALL FOR ALL INFORMATION)If you guys are wondering"how do i play co-op with this game on a PC" its very easy!! First of all, you need two computers for this to work. I know it says co-op split screen but that only works with controller ..Then you need to buy the game on one of the computers. The next step is very simple...you need to be in the game for this to work...Do not start playing the game until they join...Next click shift and tab, and right click on the friend who you want to play with then click remote play with... The graphics wont be great on the friends computer because they don't have the game but it will still be fine..Then just start a game and it should work if it doesn't i'm sorry.... A flaw about this is you cant control both of them at the same time your going to have to take turns, and once you get used to it, it is very fun! The last  step your gonna have to do to get the game running is make a Origin account if you have one great just get it running and then click play in steam...If you don't have one set one up and then open Origin and click play in steam...If you have any questions ask me bellow in the comments. Hope you have fun with the game!!  This is a very very fun and funny game to play with friends!!
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: After Unravel comes this, but I actually played this one with a friend first. Because of the two characters joined thread it became easy to move more freely and cover more areas without getting stuck like its previous title. The graphics quality was as amazing as the previous game and I loved it. The brainstorm and skills you can apply to this game is really great for enjoying. Either play together or hitchhike on your friend where you cant make it was a great option and innovative.Unlike any other game I have played before this was a completely new experience and the story was good too. With every level you can watch the story unfold like its previous game. I enjoyed this with my friend and I hope you guys can try it someday too, have fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

(Directed to some comments wich claim lack of instructions.)Worth the money. (Bought at 10€)The negative part was the mandatory Origin installation...
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Unravel you will like playing Unravel Two as well. The formula hasn't changed, still a fun to play platformer with excellent level design and picturesque graphics, The strongest side of this installation is the option to play together in coop, which is a lot of fun and works very well with the game mechanics. The puzzles are not too challenging and it is more about the jumping that can pose some challenge, but in the end both aspects are very satisfying. The weakest part of the game for me is the storytelling, which is not very clear and a bit confusing, as one is not sure what the story is exactly about and where it is aiming. Maybe it is just me, but some explicit storytelling would surely benefit the game, this was better handled in Unravel. Overall if you enjoy well crafted platformers with lightweight puzzle solving and a lot of jumping around with a partner I can surely recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: We played this game as a couple! The mechanics were ingenious. The piggy backing, the tether, the lasso... The nicest thing was the mechanics also supported the overall feel of the game. You had to cooperate with your partner but the mechanics were designed so that you never felt held back. We also liked the length of the game. It wasn't too long, and ended just when we were starting to feel it was time.The game works fine in Linux through proton.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really warm experience, albeit frustrating at times. _childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game, with beautiful graphics. Played it Co-op, which seems to be the way to go. _childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: After tries upon tries it finally started without Denuvo crashing Origin and the game before even showing the EA logo video.The tutorial level offered a light hearted platform puzzler with marvelous graphics with themes from Swedish nature.Suspecting that the game starting was just a coincidence I quit and watched a Youtube video about how American police uses chemical weapons against its own citizens that if used in war would be a warcrime, just to let me think about something else and let the game unload fully from the RAM.I also tried to start the original Unravel, but it still crashes before the EA logo video shows.Still later I tried starting Unravel Two again, and it didn't. Don't get me wrong, there were the same disk activity as when it crashed or started earlier, but nothing else happened. So I tried to restart Steam and Origin. Steam let me force a shutdown, but Origin only opened a pop up saying it couldn't be shut down because Unravel Two was running.How about using the Task Manager to kill any Unravel Two processes? That would have been great if the Task Manager could be started and wasn't blocked by Origin and/or Denuvo. Taskkill from a command prompt would have worked if the command prompt wasn't also blocked and couldn't be started.Googling other ways to kill tasks had to be done on my phone as Chrome couldn't open anything in new tabs.Logging out wasn't possible, restarting or shutting down my computer was also blocked along with most other functions on my computer. The only way to restart was the janitor reset, holding down the power button until the hardware shuts down the power and then turning the computer on again.I can not in good concience recommend this beautiful light hearted game until EA gets their act together and stops breaking games by adding Origin and Denuvo DRM on top of the DRM when publishing games on other platforms with their own DRM built in, such as Steam.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible game. I’ve been playing this with my 5 year old, as well another adult. The graphics are beautiful. The auto-save checkpoints is amazing. The puzzles are adequately challenging, and if you get stuck and want a hint - there’s a button for that. Most of it is fairly intuitive, but I’ll admit there were a few solutions my 5 year old saw that I did not. With that being said, one person can mostly (literally) carry the team, but not completely. Once one player successfully navigates an obstacle, you can pull the second player up to you. This is hands down my favorite feature of the game. However, you regularly encounter obstacles where you absolutely must rely on the second player. Another of my favorite features is the ability to slightly slow down time (it's an on/off option). This tremendously helps those who may not be as quick on the controller. I also like that the characters don’t “run into” each other (you run through each other without a physical interaction). There’s probably a word for whatever that is (or whatever it isn’t?).This is the best 2 player family game I’ve ever played, it can also be played solo. The Challenge Levels are very challenging.I ran into a very annoying issue with the EA launching not making the game full screen, but after force ending task and closing/reopening Steam a few times I could get it to work.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoyed the first one, you will enjoy this one as well. The puzzles are fun but less challenging and the 2 player mode is quite fun as well. It's rare to get couch co-op games nowadays. If you're an achievement hunter, the medals are quite hard to earn. A 6-7 hour game if you're not going for 100%. 100% will take from 15-20 hours depending on your skill. Music, art-style and atmosphere is still at a high level same as the first one. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely co-op platformer. Pretty graphics, relaxing music and nice puzzles. There are also collectables to find throughout your journey. The only downside is having to install an app so both players can use a controller (DS for Windows), it's too tricky to play on keyboard/mouse. Steam's remote play together works fine, but the 2nd person's view can become blocky due to video compression issues. It would be better if the game gave a friends pass on purchase (like It Takes Two) to avoid this. Overall recommended, it's a really nice co-op game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Although it tries to live up to it's predecessor it sadly falls short. What little story there was for me in my short time playing, (which I heard ends up being quite short anyway upon completion) got smothered by the linear puzzles, some of which I found quite frustrating. This was partly due to the level design being flawed with some of solutions disguised as part of the background. The gameplay was further rendered challenging with the addition of lethal spectres which broke the enjoyment of the journey for me, as well as being somewhat world breaking. It does provide the player with optional hints should they become stuck but personally this resulted in pulling me out of the experience on the occasions I found myself using them. I also found the world a bit dull and no where near as beautiful, eye catching and diverse as it's predecessor. There is the addition of optional challenge levels which some may find enjoyable if that's your thing. It can be played as co-op which may be more enjoyable, although it's only local at the writing of this review. There is also, as of yet, no achievements. Overall it just failed to deliver and build upon what made the prior title stand out. 4/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for an inexpensive game that I could play on my own and this has been great so far. (Got it on sale!) The objective of the game kind of reminds me a little of It Takes, except you don't need a partner. Which is kind of exactly what I was looking for. It's different from It Takes Two because the story line isn't quite as involved, less cut scenes (so far), and it's side scrolling. The puzzles aren't as tricky either, but that's totally fine for me because I think I'd get stuck a lot on It Takes Two by myself. LolI love the graphics and the music is actually pretty relaxing. I wish there was a little more variety in the music, but it does change up a fair amount. Controls are smooth, even on keyboard and so far the objectives haven't been super difficult. If you get stuck then the hints are great because they don't give it completely away with the first hint so you can see if you're at least on the right track without knowing exactly what to do. Not to mention the characters are actually super cute. I see a lot of people were disappointed that it's only local co-op and not online, but I definitely recommend this game for solo play!
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fine if you are looking for something to fill your time with a friend or partner. Just don't expect a story-rich plot or honestly a plot you can even follow. It's very much you play to play the game and then stare confused at what is happening in the background from time to time. The game play is fairly straight forward and relatively easy to work-through puzzles. However, there is an occasional part that will have you so worked up because you keep dying no matter what you do until that one god-sent moment you make it past. Also, playing this game with steam's remote play together is the most tedious and confusing system that took at least 5 minutes each play to work out. Overall a decent game that I spent 5 hours on and will never look at again.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Bought this game to play with my wife and it has been wonderful! The look of the game and the music are both beautiful and feel like you are playing through a work of art.  We liked that we could customize the shape and color of our yarn dudes! Some of the first challenges, which involved jumping to narrow ledges, and swinging, were hard for her. However, the game lets you slow down time to make these movements easier.  Now we are both moving through the levels much more efficiently, and haven't needed to slow time as often.  Really creative puzzles and teamwork!  And more relaxing than Lego LOTR and Castle Crashers (which have been our other games)    :-)Forgot to mention,  I have a wired X-box 360 controller, and a cheap LG F310 controller that I got at Target for $20.  Plugged them both into my PC and was able to play without issue. With other games I have had to restart the computer to get the controllers to work.
