Also, I purchased the game for both of us which was also a waste of money. -1/10, I wouldn't recommend. A real bummer.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Baby's first puzzle platformer is a beautiful bore.I suppose if you've never played this genre of game before this might be mildly interesting. But for anyone who can put two and two together this game offers nothing but tiny speed bumps in your pursuit to "go right" and finish each level. None of the puzzles require more than a few seconds to figure out as you blaze through the different environments on your quest to, well, get to the end. See, there's not much of a story here. There's some family drama unfolding in the background in the form of apparitions but you don't interact with them in a meaningful way. As far as mechanics go, "Yarny" can use a grappling hook, create a makeshift trampoline between two hooks, and wall jump. That's about it. The inclusion of a second Yarny does slightly increase the complexity of the puzzles as a secondary grapple point.. This game may be unfortunately timed as I had just finished playing the absolutely brain-tickling , a feat  could not accomplish.And to be clear I did play this with two players. It just meant there were two bored players instead of one. Which brings up another cardinal sin: Unravel two does not support 2 controllers. It's keyboard + Controller. Playing a platformer on a keyboard is bad enough, but the game also refuses to save any keybinds you might reassign if you don't like the defaults.I will say it's a pretty game. There are some lovely fire, smoke, and water effects. But like a beautifully gift wrapped pair of socks, what's inside is merely functional, not exciting. Once you factor in the need to install the dreadful EA Origin (a colossal headache) I see no reason to play this game.EDIT: I played the game to completion. The story mode, as expected, is more like a walking simulator than a real game. There are only 3-4 sections that require some thought. However the challenge levels are actually very good and what is what I had hoped the main game would be like. There are 20 in total and most of them are good to excellent. These took around 2-3 hours to complete. They do significantly improve my impression of the game, and were at least one of Origin, the lack of dual controller support, or the dull main story fixed I could be convinced to give this game a marginal thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: False Advertising.Be warned 'Remote Play Together' is a lie. The other 'player' cannot actually participate in gameplay; they can only watch the host play the game by controlling both characters; actually playing together is possible only in local co-op. (I know, that's completely insane, and yet here we are).Bear the fact that the Steam page lies to you in mind before purchasing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: My friend and I both purchased Unravel Two with the intent of playing co-op which turned out to be a $2.69 CAD mistake. Turns out there is no online co-op and instead the game utilizes one of the worst things ever, Steam Remote Play. We tried for roughly 30 minutes on my copy of the game to get it working with both of us using a controller and had no success.We quickly switched to his copy and like magic (crappy magic at a five year old's birthday) it started working. I'd get a few frames here and there which made some of the platforming sections difficult, but thankfully there's an awesome feature where you can just let your friend play the game while you do nothing. This made the final mission really epic while I watched my friend clear obstacles in 11 fps. Here's the kicker... I tried refunding my copy but for some reason it shows me having 4.8 hours recorded while my friend has 4.7. What? I closed my game after 30 minutes. Very uncool.Here's hoping we can bring three or four friends along for the ride in Unravel Three and Four. But if there's no online co-op, you can count me out!
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Don't play this game for the story - there isn't much going on. The game's strengths lie in it just being a decent cooperative couch game. _childDocuments_.review: Unravel 2 is like that friend who shows up unexpectedly at your doorstep with a giant ball of yarn and says, "Let's get tangled up in some mischief!" Except, in this case, the mischief involves controlling adorable little yarn creatures on a quest through stunning landscapes.The gameplay itself is a masterclass in cooperative gaming. If you've ever tried to coordinate with someone in real life while holding onto both ends of a piece of string, you'll know the struggle is real. But Unravel 2 takes that struggle and turns it into a beautifully choreographed dance of teamwork and frustration. It's like a knitting circle where everyone's trying to finish the same sweater, but some joker keeps unraveling it every five minutes.The puzzles range from pleasantly perplexing to "I swear this level was designed by a sadistic cat who just learned how to knit." But fear not, because the satisfaction of finally untangling that mess you've been wrestling with for the past hour is second to none. It's like solving a Rubik's Cube made entirely out of yarn, except when you mess up, instead of colors, you just get a bigger knot.Unravel 2 is a charming, challenging, and downright adorable experience that's guaranteed to tie you up in knots (both figuratively and literally). Just make sure you have plenty of patience, a good sense of humor, and maybe a spare ball of yarn for when you inevitably throw yours across the room in frustration.I enjoyed playing this game with my partner a lot. No ball of yarn has been thrown, I promise.

Unbelievable. Instant refund.

The story is told without cut-scenes, much life Half-Life and Portal handle storytelling. The graphics are amazing, my FPS has never dropped below 63 while running and the game is still breathtaking. If you're like me, you don't like googling how to beat games, especially puzzle games, the game has a built in OPTIONAL hint system for those who are stuck, I love how it's optional because those who want more of a challenge can play through without hints and those who re playing for story and are stuck can easily move on to the parts of the game they enjoy. You either have to find that sweet spot and get it right in one go or retry over and over and over again. The margin of success is thinner than a strand of hair, being absolutely necessary to finish the entire challenge levels in one go, given there's 20 of them, even though there's slow motion option, it's hard to get through. I honestly quit the challenges midway and started focusing on finishing the main story levels first and later try out challenges. _childDocuments_.review: I bought Unravel 1 and 2 together. After playing the first one for an hour I knew these weren't games for me, but I waited too long to return them, so I went ahead and played them since I was stuck with them. I didn't like Unravel much at all. However, I did like Unravel 2... at least at first. The sequel is more fun to play; having two yarnys to manipulate is a lot of fun. The controls are better; it's a lot less frustrating to do the things that you want to do with your character in this game versus the first one. The graphics are every bit as good as the first game; they are both beautiful. The music is better. This game is more challenging. I like that the sequel has multiple save slots. But that's where my praise ends because the negatives outweigh the positives for me (see below). The bottom line is that I think the first Unravel is a better game simply because it doesn't have the issues that this one has. I stand by that even though I didn't dislike playing the sequel as much as I did the first game.These are my issues with Unravel 2:1) Both of these games require the use of EA's Origin game launcher. If I had know that beforehand, I wouldn't have bought them.2) The multiplayer doesn't work the way one would expect on a PC. It's complicated to play this game with online multiplayer, but it is possible. Local multiplayer works fine, but you're not allowed to have a dual controller setup on PC; one player must use a keyboard. This forced input setup turned this into a single player game for me. 3) Some of the bonus stages are brutally difficult. This would be a positive for a "hardcore" gamer, but this is a real turn-off to a "casual" gamer. A couple of these stages made me hate the game (yes, I did complete them all). There's almost no point to complete these stages other than unlocking Yarnys that only add cosmetic options to use when you are basically done with the game. You don't even get an achievement for completing them all. No, you have to complete them all in 45 minutes. And not 45 minutes total best times, but complete all 20 stages in 45 real-time minutes including the time it takes you to move between the stages which aren't located in the same room of the main hub (the Lighthouse). And if you have slow load times, that also counts as part of the 45 minutes.4) The story is weird. And not weird in a good way; it's weird in that I-have-no-clue-what-is-going-on way. I can't even begin to understand the ending. I was left confused and dumbfounded when I finished the game. I kept hoping that things would be explained by the ending, but nope. There's no final "boss" (not that there needs to be one, but it could have helped). The way things end make it feel like the game is unfinished. If the story had made any sense, I might have had an emotional connection to this game and been more forgiving about my gripes with it. I did not enjoy playing the first game, but I have to admit the ending was touching. 5) The levels are way too long. Each level took me between 30-45 minutes to get through the first time (granted I was hunting the collectibles). It wasn't a good feeling when they kept dragging on. They are so long that I didn't want to play them again. These levels aren't seamless like the first game, so they could have been broken up into stages so that you could go back and only play certain parts without having to go through the entire level.6) The main hub (the Lighthouse) is far more complicated to get around than it needs to be. It was fun to explore at first, but you could easily forget where things are located when trying to revisit them, and some areas are tricky to get to.  It's a creative design, but horribly impractical.7) I don't know what the point of the collectibles are in this game. There's not even an achievement for collecting them all.  I got them all, but I have no idea what they unlocked. I am pretty sure that rescuing the yarnys in the bonus stages are what added the options for the character customization. I also think that the collectibles lost their charm in this game for being sparkly stars instead of buttons like the first game. The last collectible in the game is impossible to see at normal speed; I couldn't even see it when using a guide, I just got lucky that I was able to grab it.8) When you try to select the eyes to customize your character, the stupid yarnys would always turn their heads so that I couldn't see what the eyes looked like that I was try to select, AND you can't rotate the head yourself.  It was rather annoying for being something so insignificant to the game.

_childDocuments_.review: ‏Unravel 2 is a charming and heartwarming puzzle-platformer that invites players to embark on a captivating journey as endearing yarn creatures. Developed by Coldwood Interactive, this sequel to the beloved Unravel introduces a delightful co-op experience, allowing players to unravel the game's mysteries together. With its breathtaking visuals, touching narrative, and inventive gameplay mechanics, Unravel 2 weaves a truly unforgettable adventure.Unravel 2 takes place in a stunning world filled with picturesque landscapes, from lush forests to towering cliffs and bustling urban environments. The attention to detail in the environment design is awe-inspiring, immersing players in a vibrant and immersive setting. Each level feels like a work of art, with its own distinct style and atmosphere. The use of lighting, color palettes, and environmental effects adds depth and beauty to every scene, creating a visually mesmerizing experience.The narrative of Unravel 2 is a touching tale of friendship, resilience, and personal growth. The game beautifully conveys its story without the use of words, relying on subtle gestures, emotions, and visual cues. As players guide the adorable yarn characters through their journey, they witness moments of joy, discovery, and even sorrow. The narrative unfolds organically, evoking a range of emotions and leaving a lasting impact.Unravel 2 introduces a new dimension to the gameplay with its cooperative multiplayer feature. Players can join forces with a friend or control both yarn creatures simultaneously in solo play, allowing for unique and engaging puzzle-solving mechanics. Cooperation and communication are key as players must work together to overcome obstacles, swing across chasms, and unravel complex puzzles. The seamless integration of co-op mechanics enhances the overall experience, fostering a sense of teamwork and camaraderie.Unravel 2 offers a delightful mix of puzzles and platforming challenges that keep players engaged throughout their adventure. The puzzles range from clever physics-based conundrums to intricately designed environmental puzzles, requiring both logical thinking and dexterity to solve. The platforming segments are equally enjoyable, with precise controls and well-designed levels that offer a satisfying balance of exploration and skill-based traversal. The gradual increase in difficulty ensures a rewarding sense of accomplishment with each successfully completed challenge.The enchanting soundtrack of Unravel 2 perfectly complements the game's atmosphere, evoking a range of emotions as players progress through the story. The music beautifully captures the whimsical and heartfelt moments, enhancing the sense of wonder and immersion. From gentle melodies to lively tunes, the soundtrack immerses players in the world, creating a captivating audio experience that further elevates the gameplay.Unravel 2 is a delightful co-op adventure that weaves together breathtaking visuals, a heartfelt narrative, innovative gameplay mechanics, and enchanting sound design. The game's seamless co-op integration and intricate level design make it a joy to play with a friend, fostering a sense of connection and collaboration. Whether you're drawn to its charming aesthetics, compelling storyline, or captivating puzzles, Unravel 2 is a masterpiece that tugs at the heartstrings and leaves a lasting impression.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid physics-based puzzle platformer with a nice, soothing soundtrack. Unlike Unravel 1, you control 2 yarns at once ( or play in co-op mode with a friend), This results in puzzles that are solved in a very organic way. I appreciate that the puzzles are not too challenging and they are mostly used to showcase the satisfying physics-based platforming that you can do in the game. Also, the game has really nice looking graphics. The simple act of traversing through the highly-detailed environments is a joy.My only criticism is that the levels, the environments are a bit too similar to each other. They could definitely use some more variety.8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: A very, very special game that improves in a lot of smart ways upon the original Unravel. Unravel 1 had less intuitive (and more punishing) puzzle design and felt like it dragged on too long as a result. Unravel 2, on the other hand, has an emphasis on incredibly inventive cooperative platforming and feels perfectly paced.Unravel 2 is wonderful as a singleplayer experience, though there's something really meaningful about playing through it with a loved one or significant other. I did so via Steam remote play (a fantastic Steam feature more people should check out!) and had a magical time. Thank you, EA, for funding Unravel 2, and thank you, Coldwood, for making it a reality. The world's a better place because Unravel 2 is in it.

_childDocuments_.review: We enjoyed this game, yet have given it a Thumbs Down for some very good reasons.  It was purchased purely for the 2 player co-op.  I'm a seasoned gamer and my partner dabbles, so the mechanics of this game allowed me to help her through the difficult bits, just as advertised.  This gameplay is great...However, there were some things we found annoying, which leads to the Thumbs Down.  The story mode is far too short.  It took us less than 8 hours to complete the story :(  We felt the story was too easy.  Then there are all bonus levels which are incredibly difficult and repetitive.  Like, you'll die in the first 15 seconds and find yourself repeating this over and over and over - to the point where you're not having fun.  Most of the bonus levels can't be completed if one of your team hasn't developed "controller thumbs" yet.But the thing is, it's like these bonus levels WERE supposed to be part of the story game, yet they decided to cut the story/development time short and just dump in some really short bonus levels that are incredibly difficult - The difficulty is not reflective of the main story game play.  It was this reason we felt cheated.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of negative reviews come from not being able to play the game online with friends or having some problems with the controls. _childDocuments_.review: == Update of 2021.09.19 ==The summer seems to be over here. So, I returned to the game today to see if anything has changed at all, and to my surprise, after the game launched and the Origin client updated, I found out that I can control each of the two characters using one Steam controller in a local co-op game. At last!This solves my main complaint, and makes the game playable. It is not yet possible, however, to launch the game while Steam is in the Family View mode. I believe it to be in Steam's hands, not Origin's, to fix their API to make it take this case into consideration. I will keep the recommendation as Downthumb for now, until the children play it extensively and make sure all is alright, and until Steam fix their API. == Update of 2021.05.19 ==I can now run the game, after having solved some of the technical hurdles that had prevented us from testing the game, which are:1 Overcoming the twisted, enforced, buggy process of complying with the double DRM, by linking my Steam account to an Origin account that I created.2 Solving the  by disabling the "winegstreamer" library in Proton, using winecfg via protontricks (some people suggest deleting the video files, since they are only for intros and cut scenes. I didn't attempt this, because I do not like doing so.)3 Finding out that the game cannot be launched while Steam is in Family View mode. It seems that in family view some APIs pertaining to account authorisation/authentication are not accessible, and that causes the double DRM process to fail. This seems to be irrelevant to many, but to me, the reason I got the game is for my children to play it together. Now I need to launch it for them every time, because there are other games not in the family view that I do not want them to be exposed to yet.What remains now is:* Figuring out how to enable local co-op, which is what is intended by the tag "Shared/Split Screen Co-op", i.e having two players playing the game on the same device on the same Steam account using two sets of controllers, where each player controls a character. Several users in the forums confuse that with inviting a friend to play over remote-play, which is not the same at all. Now I'm beginning to doubt that it is possible at all, or at least in Steam.== Initial review ==Believe it or not: I never yet played this game!The 14 hours+ logged by Steam is the time during which the game application managed to stay in memory, invisible to me, after having crashed.So far, I struggled for a couple of hours to make the compulsory Origin registration work on my Linux, after which came the immediate crashes after launch. I have yet to implement a solution.The only reason I have this is that it appeared to be a pleasant-looking, interesting and fun collaboration game that my kids could enjoy playing together, as I’m always searching for this kind of games. I resisted the urge to not get involved with EA, but alas!Double DRM is synergetic failure; a failure greater than the sum of its failing parts. It should not exist.So until I get this properly running, it will remain in the red zone.Anyhow, the kids are content with Ibb & Obb, Pikuniku, Biped, and the likes, in addition to Deru, Death Squared, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately an absolutely underwhelming experience imho.I fell in love with the first Unravel on which I have spent more than 5 hours. Unravel 2 on the other hand does nothing the original didn't already do any better. It is shorter, simpler (not necessarily easier), and generally just less interesting.The "coop" mechanic in which you simply control 2 characters feels forced and unneeded and rarely is used for anything interesting. Mostly swinging. Swinging is still fun, the graphics are still phenomenal and the music is still chilling, but the gameplay just got on my nerves from the first minute on. Unravel 2 takes about 2 to 3 hours at most to complete. Then you have some challenge missions. The "story" is...I dunno what it is. I was kinda in love with the first game's story. It was visual story telling and made sense. The central hub was also a charming place with puzzles of its own. The hub in Unravel 2 is just "go from A to B". I don't really get any of it.If you desperately want to feel like Spiderman light you may get this on sale. But then again, you might just buy Unravel 1 and have more fun with that. Yarny was special...now there are unlimited Yarnys. Not sure how exactly they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ this up.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game but I can't recommend it. It's more fun than the first, that's for sure. Unfortunately, even with a decent spec and cooling set up this game makes my CPU and GPU heat up hotter than any other game I've ever played, Steam or otherwise. Hell, it might have actually started steaming at one point. The temperature gauge just read "Death Valley in mid-July, hope you backed your s**t up." Even on potato settings it was hot enough to make french fries, just saying.You can do "online co-op" but it's remote play so either person can fully control both characters no matter if someone is currently playing them, and I'm not going to even try to be mature or constructive about this- it was a really stupid idea that not only brings nothing to the table but actually detracts. If you switch characters or one person accidentally smacks their own controller/keyboard then your character moves or, say, may fall to their death because the person hit a button and you let go of the yarn. You pretty much have to have an agreement and a lot of patience not to touch your controller while the other person is playing, all that said one character is allocated waaaaaaaaaaaay more responsibilities and movements than the secondary character, which is really not fun for the 2nd person who just sits there aside from 2 or 3 little assists. All that said, it's a fun, neat game to play solo, the wall jumping and making the yarn restriction based upon the distance between the two characters was a great decision.I'm writing this review because there was an update that came out recently but absolutely no patch notes on their website, store page, forum, Twitter, nothing indicating what they fixed or changed. I'd honestly be interested in finishing this game if I wasn't convinced it was going to burn my house down a minute into game play. Be happy to update my review one day, or maybe try playing it again once I figure out what the hell they updated.Edit: Oh look at that, the 2nd game patch since my review and they still never released any patch notes about either of them and now the game just crashes. So yeah, I'm not finishing it. Just gonna delete it. Don't buy this game.

The objective of the game is to solve puzzles by navigating a ball through a maze-like level. The levels start out relatively simple, but as you progress through the game, they become more complex and difficult to solve. This game will keep you on your toes, and you will need to think creatively to find the solution to each puzzle.One of the best aspects of Urnavel TWO is the Steam Achievements. The game has an extensive list of achievements, many of which are very hard to get. This adds a layer of challenge to the game, as you will need to master each level to unlock all of the achievements. For gamers who love a challenge, Urnavel TWO will definitely satisfy.The graphics of Urnavel TWO are simple yet beautiful. The levels are colorful, and the animations are smooth and fluid. The music is also a standout feature of the game, with a relaxing and soothing soundtrack that will help you focus on solving the puzzles.In conclusion, Urnavel TWO is an excellent puzzle game that will challenge your brain and keep you entertained for hours. The Steam Achievements add an extra layer of challenge to the game, making it a must-play for gamers who love a challenge. The graphics and sound design are also top-notch, making Urnavel TWO a complete package. If you're a fan of puzzle games, Urnavel TWO is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: a sequel to the critically acclaimed Unravel and builds on its predecessor's heartfelt storytelling and inventive gameplay with a focus on cooperative play.The game follows two Yarnys—small, yarn-based creatures—as they embark on a journey through a series of beautifully crafted environments. The cooperative gameplay is a standout feature, allowing two players to work together to solve puzzles and navigate the game's levels, which requires coordination and teamwork. For solo players, the game can be enjoyed with a single Yarny that can switch between two forms, though the cooperative experience shines brightest.Visually, Unravel Two is stunning, with its detailed and imaginative settings that bring the natural world to life in a whimsical and artistic manner. The puzzles are creatively designed, balancing challenge with the satisfaction of solving them. The game's narrative, while minimalistic, is poignant and complements the serene atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking for something to play with my daughter after beating It Takes Two, which was our first real coop video game together. I have this weird thing where I crave novelty so replaying games I remember is always a pretty big bore for me. Fortunately, I discovered Unravel 2!What a wonderful and refreshing surprise, and a steal too when I got it on sale for $5! It's definitely worth full price though as my 9 year old had a wonderful time playing it. She doesn't like fighting games as much as my son so this kind of non-combat co-op puzzle game suits her just fine.The level designs are wonderful, the music, ambiance and everything is just so well put together. This is the kind of game I believe AAA developers are no longer capable of making, especially if they've been bought out by one large software conglomerate or another. And get this, I'm here on the tail end of 2024 playing a game made in 2018 and it doesn't feel dated at all. I highly recommend playing this with your little ones to help them exercise that puzzle muscle. I'm a firm believer that the family that games together, stays together. It also helps teach the little ones the excitement and feeling of working together like a well oiled machine.My daughter wants to add: "This game is really high quality and a lot of fun. It is very realistic and very adventurous. That is all I want to say." +1

You need to work well together and sometimes you are the reason that your partner cannot get over an obstacle. The puzzles range from pleasant to frustrating, but the satisfaction of finally finishing a level is unreal.This is a great co-op game for players who enjoy puzzle platformers. The first installment was slower and more contemplative, whereas this one is strongly action-oriented and  the story doesn't make much sense.Solid co-op game nevertheless.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Does not support 3rd party controllers and the co-op is based on steam remote play which has been an absolutely horrible experience to pull off - it takes longer to get the game going than actually playing it, AND it basically works with your friend needing to join and interact with your stream remotely. Slightly not-so-okay internet connection? Too bad, the game is unplayable. There is no local co-op, meaning you cannot both sit at one computer AND there is no online co-op, meaning you cannot play on entirely different devices either, forcing you to play in a state of uncertainty whether it will be possible, not to even mention fun. So you need an official console controller if you wanna go down that route, HOWEVER there are slots for controllers, which if switched, makes the controller unusable until the game is restarted. No clue whether this is Steam, EA or their collaboration, but so far this has been quite possibly the worst of the worst experiences of any co-op gaming I've had. While this looks like a cute little game there simply isn't anything to recommend because it doesn't work more than it does.

_childDocuments_.review: I played Unravel Two first, before Unravel, and thoroughly enjoyed it co-op.  It reminded me of Little Big Planet on the PS3, which I also loved.The puzzles were great; not so difficult that you'd have to lookup a walk-through, but not too easy either.  Somewhat of a "think outside the 9 dots" puzzle at times, which I enjoy.  The graphics were astonishingly beautiful.Near the end, it became much more difficult in terms of dexterity, but with the "jump on my back" feature, the less dexterous player is still able to progress.  At times I almost thought I would have to give up in frustration at the difficulty level, but then there is also a "slow time" option which I found surprisingly helpful too.The co-op game is relatively short, but it also comes at a very low price tag, so well worth the money if you enjoy platform puzzlers.  I'm hoping they come out with Unravel 3, because I'll definitely be buying it.

_childDocuments_.review: A great single player game but there's a few odd choices that might make co-op less enjoyable.For starters, there's much more of an emphasis on story, with long cutscenes. Usually when I play co-op I prefer to just get to the action. The levels are also really long so make sure you both have time set aside.The puzzles and platforming are really solid though. Controlling two characters lets the game get really creative with these. It plays really well as a single player game too, aside from sections with enemies and platforming at the same time. Those are a bit trickier to manage but they're still very doable. Most the time, you can just carry the other character and it plays just like the original. But you can also play them individually and just swap between them when needed.My only complaints are I didn't like the story as much in this one, and it's greater emphasis meant I was just being bored when it was on screen. There's also abstract enemies now. They don't really fit the mostly realistic feel of the original. But these are minor gripes. It's still a very enjoyable experience. Overall it's a slight step down from the original but it's still a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: This is hands down, one of the best games I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing. It is a literal masterpiece, and definitely conveys and brings out the emotions that the team behind it intended. The simplicity and beautiful story puts this game FAR above most modern triple A titles. I wish development teams would take notes from a product like this, and realize that there doesn't need to be a ton put into a title to make it successful. Bought this game never playing the first one, and I was very impressed. Ended up playing through steam remote play, so only one purchase of the game was needed in my case for co-op.The environment in this game is incredible, and the development team should be proud of the work they have produced. Attention to detail was very obvious, and we mentioned cool little features like the environment moving from our running or interacting with it throughout the entire playthrough. It ran very smoothly, and thankfully enough, there were no bugs that were run into, so this is a sigh of relief, especially considering the day and age that we're in with games releasing with TONS of bugs. The story was beautiful, and the little challenges weren't too hard, and super forgiving if you tend to mess up, or have a hard time with jumping puzzles and puzzles in general. It's a nice relaxing time when playing with a good friend, as you can just take an evening to chill out and enjoy a comfy title.Anyone that is thinking about buying this game should definitely do so. I hold games to a very high standard, and hardly ever review something, but I felt that after the experience I had in this game...the devs and teams behind it deserve nothing less than a positive review. Incredible game, please make sure to stick to this quality all the time, it is much appreciated by your playerbase.

_childDocuments_.review: "Unravel Two" is more than just a game; it's a delightful experience that my 7-year-old daughter and I have cherished. From the moment we picked up the controllers, we were hooked, and here's why:The split-screen cooperative gameplay is a stroke of genius. It strikes that sweet spot in difficulty, offering both a challenge and a sense of accomplishment for both generations. The best part? When things get tough, I can handle the tricky bits, and my daughter can tackle the easier parts – a perfect teamwork dynamic. The puzzles in "Unravel Two" are like a perfectly knitted scarf – intricate, yet never overwhelming. The game's pacing ensures that every puzzle feels just right, making our journey through it an absolute joy. The graphics are a feast for the eyes, with every level resembling a mini work of art. The attention to detail is astounding, and it's impossible not to be captivated by the enchanting world of Yarnys. The music, too, complements the visuals beautifully, setting the mood for a heartwarming adventure.In a world filled with games, "Unravel Two" stands out as a heartwarming gem that's perfect for families and friends alike. It's a tale of yarn and adventure, where teamwork, laughter, and shared accomplishments reign supreme. So, grab your controllers, unite your Yarnys, and prepare for an unforgettable journey that's sure to warm your heart."Unravel Two" – where love, laughter, and puzzles intertwine seamlessly.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is not a bad game...but it isn't great either. A single run through of the game took approx 4 hours. There are medals to earn by not dying and beating specific times on each level as well as separate challenge levels that unlock appearance items. If we had done these extra bits I imagine it could easily have taken two or three times that long.It is great that the game doesn't require two copies of the game to play co-op. It instead uses Steam Remote play.I found the game vague and a bit clunky. My partner and I only had the vaguest sense of what the story was supposed to be. Looking up the plot online filled in many gaps that I just simply don't know how else you would know unless you googled it. There is a golden light that spells out for you the path you need to take to progress in every room. Took a bit of the problem solving fun out of it. The game relies heavily on swinging and momentum, which didn't work very smoothly. about 35% of the time I found myself dangling and having to awkwardly reposition or fight to get swinging again. Overall I do not regret playing the game. But I would only recommend others pick it up if there is a good sale going on at the time of purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Just like Unravel, a magical adventure that I would recommend to anyone.It does a good job of being a sequel by introducing some new mechanics on top of the old ones – wall-sliding, no fall damage, swimming, and of course the second player. Surprisingly, it feels completely normal to play this singleplayer, so don't worry about that. Some of the issues of the first game are fixed here – there were far fewer unintuitive puzzles (the hint system was a good idea; I only used it once but it really helped in that one puzzle), far fewer annoying deaths due to the character being "unreasonably weak" of the platforming not working. Apart from a few bruh moments my experience was great and very immersive. Oh, and there's a bunch more stuff to do after you finish the main game as well – challenges, time trials, secrets, cool stuff like that. More than in Unravel.As for the story, well, if you've played the first game you know these people know how to tell an emotional story — without any words, in fact. Coldwood really care about their games and that demands respect. I would truly, honestly call this game one of the masterpieces of the video game art form.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: Sooo... After playing through the more than perfect first part short after release and 100%ing it yesterday it was time for part two. Expectations were high and disappointment even higher. Girl and me loaded up the game, which ALWAYS starts in a window. [First wtf] Then we realized, no online coop, only local or remote play (so no achievements for the client). In a game where even the boxart highlights the two player focus [Second wtf] Even with remote play and two seperate pcs in use, at least one player has to use a controller. [Third wtf] The settings only show a pic of a xbox controller. No matter what controller is connected, the game gives you xbox button promts and no config. [Fourth wtf. Espacially as in Unravel 1, which is older than the console itself automatically detected my switch controllers and gives according on screen icons]When remote playing the game gets confused with what button promts to give. Even as keyboard user you're sometimes told to press yxab and vice versa press shift, ctrl, l and what ever on the controller.After a way too long time we managed to get remote play, input devices and the ea launcher [Why use steam AND former origin?] more or less to work and started playing. Roughly ten minutes up to the first client crash. In total 18 crashes in 10 hours. No idea why, client game just closed.We tried to ignore our raising frustration levels and focus on experience the actual gameplay. And the core mechanic with using one player as the anchor point so the other can rope around is pretty nice, even not used that often.But.. Honestly.. Everything else feels like all the great details that made the first game so incredibly awesome were given a 180 degree turn. Where the first game had this deep picture based story this one has some shallow story about two kids fleeing from some evil adults. Who are they? What happened? From what place and people are they running away? After finishing the game I googled the story because we had no idea, what the game was about and all I could say about it is 'hm'. The whole world feels so random and blunt. Platforming over random rooftops, through factory like mazes with lava traps or a suddenly burning forest. But what should this mario level present? Where are we? Why are we here? Because some super blury silouettes ran that way.Where is all the creativity, the diversity, the innovation gone? Little details like Yarny beeing scared from a butterfly, an elk walking through the background and luring all those mosquitos of you, you unexpectibly starting a ride on a tricycle because you had to climb it to reach a doorhandle, details, decoration, and and and In general, not a single setting, puzzle, character, event, or anything gave me even half of that joy the first game did. It's all just 'do this, because the game tells you to'. I'm missing the feeling of exploring a world, because I want to. Not even the controls are as smooth as they had been. All in all it feels like big boss EA said 'first one brought money, make another one, and be finished tomorrow'. So there just wasn't enough time for depth.Last thing, the achievements. For me, achievements are like side quests but here it's more like Dark Souls. For all levels: 'Beat the level without dying' or 'Beat the game in bloody pro level speedrunning time'. And 'beat all 20 bonus levels in a continuous streak of max 45 minutes'. At least there are a few little creative (still brutal) ones like 'dodge the fish five times'But the moment I quit the game for good was when trying 'falling with style'. You have to play through half the level to get to the spot, where you're supposed to do some rope skill challenge. Takes quite some time but wouldn't be too bad.. if there wasn't an unavoidable checkpoint you will hit, before knowing if you'd jumped correct and earned the achievement or not.So if you miss the jump, you have to do the first twenty minutes of the level again and watch the unskippable cutscenes again and again.So.. yes.. I expected the game to be very different and I'm disappointed. I really hope, there will be a third part to the series with the old charme. You showed us what perfection and genius you can do. Please show us again.

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel Two is an excellent and, sometimes, challenging co-op platformer. The game starts off with putting you through a short tutorial before pushing you further through the story. The gameplay is fun and they've accounted for the amount of times you or your co-op partner will die or miss jumps with a mechanic where you can pull your partner up by your connected string. However, if you're wanting a cohesive plot or story to the game, there really isn't one outside of the power of teamwork? The plot is very vague and honestly seems to detract from the overall quality of the game. However, the game is excellent for platforming and is a triumph for the genre. The gameplay is fun and challenging enough for even experienced gamers, and I would highly recommend it for that reason alone.

_childDocuments_.review: "The developers were very understanding when they added accessibility options for players who are not familiar with gaming. They added the option to use slow motion, which can be toggled on and off without any consequences at any stage of the game, making difficult parkour stages easier when needed. They also added useful hints for every puzzle, allowing a wide range of ages to play and enjoy the game. The game's aesthetics are beautiful, and the platforming is well-designed. There are also available challenges for those who need more gameplay and like to test their skills. The quantity and level of challenges are adequate, and overall the game is fun and recommended, especially when you want something to play with a friend or sibling on the same device."

_childDocuments_.review: I've had steam for over 10 years at this point. I've played a couple games in that time. I've never felt the need to write a review. I felt like the reviews that I saw under a game said what needed to be said before/after playing the game. Unravel two is bad. The physics are inconsistent, the story is completely incoherent and unrelated to the gameplay, the gameplay itself is frustrating at times (especially the last level, where ), and I simply did not have fun while playing this game. There was no character growth, no actual sense of urgency when the game was trying to  that a situation was urgent (with the sound or implied threat of enemies or danger), no reason to care for anything that happens to the characters you play as or the "story" that happens in the background of this game. There was maybe one or two interesting puzzles and the graphics were decent but beyond that, this game was agonizing to sit through. If you're looking for a platformer, just play Ori or Little Nightmares. If you want a game to play splitscreen with someone close to you, play It Takes Two or A Way Out or Shovel Knight or Stardew or any other highly rated game. This game does not deserve to be rated as highly as it was and I couldn't agree less with its current review score. Bad time, please don't play. xoxo

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel Two is a fantastic sequel that improves on everything that made the first game great. The addition of a second character and cooperative gameplay adds a new level of depth to the game's puzzle-solving mechanics. The game's visuals are once again stunning, with even more vibrant environments and a wider range of settings. The game's controls are smooth and responsive, making for an enjoyable experience. The game's soundtrack is also excellent, providing a calming and soothing feel that's perfect for the game's atmosphere. _childDocuments_.review: - The graphics are quite good, or at least the narrow slice within the fully-rendered depth of field that contains the player characters is. Objects in the foreground and background are blurrier than their respective distances should dictate, so it can be a little hard to look at until your eyes adjust- Beyond the partially fancy graphics, the most impressive part of the game is the yarn physics. Sure, it's a little floaty, but the realistic way that you can see gravity and tension modeled for the string connecting the two characters is really cool- The music was fairly good. Lots of orchestral arrangements like you tend to see from these mega-publisher prestige arthouse entries. If I could make sense of any aspect of the story happening in the background, I might understand why the score is so emotionally charged- Speaking of the story, I have no idea what's going on with the plot. Why do those adult ghosts hate those kid ghosts so badly? It honestly makes no sense when you're just playing as a couple of yarn people bouncing around and solving puzzles in the foreground- I suspect the story is intentionally vague, but then why make it so dire and frantic? The first Unravel handled this much more effectively by portraying little heartfelt family vignettes in the background instead. The journey of the characters through the seasons reflected the aging and maturing of a family. It was thoughtful and poignant. The whole experience of Unravel Two, conversely, is incredibly discordant and awkward- I like how the background ghosts' irrelevant plot sometimes affects the environment your puzzle solving. This intriguing blend of story and gameplay would have been dramatically more impactful if the narrative made even a crumb of sense- Impenetrable plot aside, the gameplay works well from a mechanical perspective. Swinging, jumping, and bouncing all feel natural outside of some slight floatiness- Unfortunately, the puzzles feel like a step back from the first game in terms of complexity. If you're playing with a friend, you will absolutely blaze through this game without having to think too hard- The platforming aspects of the game also fail to present many challenges, though more than the puzzles do, at least- The gameplay isn't though devoid of rewards, thankfully, though really enjoying the game does require a second player. Absolutely nailing a puzzle that requires some platforming chops while in perfect sync with whichever friend/spouse/partner/sibling/pet you're playing with does feel pretty great- After being left with a pretty good impression of the first game, Unravel Two was a little bit of a letdown- I played the game with my wife, who enjoyed the game much more than I did. Maybe take some of my negativity with a grain of salt- The game ran well, at least, though you'll have to deal with EA's launcher- . Very soft recommend. The game is a passably enjoyable multiplayer experience if you can ignore the pointless background story and forget that the first Unravel is a superior experience. I don't think I would recommend Unravel Two for the solo player since playing alone would obviate the game's major redeeming quality

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel Two is a puzzle-platformer game developed by Coldwood Interactive and published by Electronic Arts. It is a sequel to the popular game Unravel, and it features a new storyline and gameplay mechanics.The game's main character is Yarny, a small creature made of yarn, and in Unravel Two, players control two Yarnys as they navigate through various environments, solving puzzles and overcoming obstacles together. The game's story is a heartwarming tale about friendship and teamwork, and it is presented through beautiful cutscenes and narration.One of the most impressive aspects of Unravel Two is its level design. The game's environments are stunningly beautiful, with a vibrant color palette and attention to detail that makes each level feel unique and alive. The game's puzzles are cleverly designed, and they require players to use both Yarnys' abilities to solve them.Another standout feature of Unravel Two is its cooperative gameplay. The game can be played alone, but it is designed for two players, either locally or online. Players must work together to solve puzzles and overcome obstacles, and the game's mechanics are designed to encourage communication and collaboration between players.The game's soundtrack is also a highlight, with a beautiful and emotional score that enhances the game's storytelling and atmosphere.One potential downside of Unravel Two is its difficulty level. While the puzzles are cleverly designed, some players may find them to be too easy or not challenging enough.Overall, Unravel Two is a beautiful and enjoyable puzzle-platformer that offers a heartwarming story, stunning graphics, and engaging cooperative gameplay. If you enjoyed the first Unravel game or are a fan of puzzle-platformers in general, Unravel Two is definitely worth checking out.

_childDocuments_.review: 'Unravel two' is a wonderful sequel to my favorite puzzle platformer game of all time 'Unravel'. The game does some new and innovating things compared to it's predecessor that make it stand out rather than feeling like more of the same. It keeps the lovely charm that the first game had but spices it up by (as the tittle of the game suggests) making you control two yarnys! This isn't just a half-baked coop feature, no no, the whole game and every puzzle is decided with two yarnys in mind! This makes the gameplay very different from the previous game, since you no longer have a guaranteed safety line but rather need to look out for two yarnys at the same time! This makes movement super smooth once you got it down, making flips across water and fire alike. i personally found the levels even more fun in unravel two due to these new movement mechanics & puzzles, which were a joy to figure out. Visuals are also (somehow) even better! The soundtrack, while not as good as the previous game is still masterful and really makes you all the more invested into the world of unravel. Lastly the story is in my opinion the only thing were unravel two is noticably worse than the first game. It just wasn't told as well as the first game so it didn't have that same impact or feeling of nostalgia. Still the game is a blast to play and a recommendation to anyone who loves a good puzzle platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: If you are a fan of side-scrolling puzzle platformers like Limbo, Inside and Little Nightmares, you will enjoy the Unravel games. While the second game's story doesn't quite have the same emotional punch as the first, the graphics and gameplay are greatly improved. The tediousness of the first game has been smoothed out and it feels much cleaner to play, with a better checkpoint system, easier backtracking and no fall damage or drowning. The levels are significantly longer to compensate for having fewer of them, which was a bit of a disappointment. I enjoyed the variety in the first game's levels, which each felt unique in their style and gimmicks. However, I do understand the need to simplify things to make it compatible with multiplayer. The puzzles were also simpler, with the more complex ones being moved into the challenge section, which I do not mind for the sake of making completing the story less frustrating. Overall, it is an improvement to the first game, but was a tad lacking in the story department.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to believe how much the artistic direction changed between Unravel and Unravel Two. While the first game was an atmospheric and nostalgic platformer for adults with gorgeous and memorable world design and beautifully authentic yarn physics, Unravel Two is an action platformer for kids, with still beautiful but rather uninspired and forgettable world design, and horribly unrealistic physics. There's nothing wrong with games for kids as such, but the shift in direction is staggering, and unfortunately this game had much less value for me than the original. The background storyline was so background that I barely registered it, the difficulty in the main story was nonexistent, and the game was actually significantly shorter than the original. What ultimately saved the game for me were the optional challenges at the end, which provided almost as much playtime as the main story, and actually exploited the physics and puzzle potential of the two-Yarny format.To summarise, Unravel Two would probably be amazing fun for a couple of kids in co-op, but for me (a young adult looking for immersion and engagement), it was overall rather unentertaining.

_childDocuments_.review: I was so excited when EA announced on Saturday that there was going to be a new Unravel and even more excited when I got to buy it straight away. It is an absolutely beautiful game, as good as if not better than the first. The platforming is improved in my opinion, the puzzles are more varied, the tutorial more in-depth (OK maybe a little long) - and the spark that guides you is perfect. BUT the best thing is I get to play this with my 8 year old daughter. With Unravel 1 we played separately - each finishing the whole game in separate play sessions. In Unravel 2 we play together, sometimes we race each other, but all of the time we figure the puzzles out together, deciding what role each of us will play in solving the puzzle - and we laugh at the situations we get ourselves into. And we help each other, I am not as good as her at the side to side jumping - so often she grabs me on my back. It's super fun. The game can be played like that all the way through but we prefer to play in co-op. We love the music and the settings to. And now we are on the bonus levels. it is a wonderful game.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommend for co op lover but have a lot of pro and cons.7 Chapter with around 30 mins for each.Controller:Can play with friends but a lot limitation, such as 1 player as keyboard 1 player as controller in same machine or remote play together. It recommend controller but unable to link 2 controller in same machine.Control part is not user friendly and not support online feature.Story:Story is not complete as I not really understand the whole story after complete the games. Need to guess as no word and explaining given.Gameplay:There is some interesting part as two player is link each other, can pull each other and at certain point, it actually easier to combine as 1 to get through the level.The level difficulty is not balance as some level (chapter 5 onward) is quite difficult as compare to previous level.Sometime It will become easier as we can combine so only one player need to pass through.But the cons is, another player will feel boring and if play separately, the difficulty become double.It is like the core value which the developer want to present, we should help each other and go through the difficulties together. If we not helping each other, it will only become more difficult?Overall it is very special design just the difficulty level might be high for average player and achievement without die??Recommend for co-op lover and someone who love to challenge your finger.

_childDocuments_.review: First played on Steam Remote Play.[STORY]There are two stories... probably. At least that's how I understand it. First one is quite "understandable" - second one? Please, explain.[DIFFICULTY]From 7 chapters, only last one has "demanding" puzzles.Most of the times I felt that my time is wasted on some sections that lead from one part of the map to another or waiting for enemies to go away, especially when you are out of theirs range.^ Most of the times, game doesn't need two players, so you may connect to your partner and rest a little bit - maybe doze off while your partner is struggling with some "parkour" part.[NEGLIGENCE]Enemies, collectibles and needs-two-in-two-separate-places-puzzles are made... aren't really made. Enemies look a bit like black stains with red/white marks, collectibles and other indicators are just white particles. You could made buttons for puzzles, anything for collectibles - but I suppose it was "whatever" for developers "story doesn't play the role anymore".[BUGS]Sometimes, you may have a bug that you cannot carry a friend - so you need to go a little bit farther and come back to be able to carry.[OVERALL]For me, it looks like a "technological" demo - we made progress with graphics, music and that's all. If you search for investment of your precious time, you probably should search for the first part of this game... or think about "It takes Two" - at least there, you have more space filled with content.

Extra challenge levels are reasonably hard and fun tooThe only complaint from me on this game is the (imo) intense vibration in my controller every time I die in the game. I dislike controller vibrations; it takes my focus out of the game and I feel uncomfortable with it (sensory sensitivity). Biggest problem when I keep dying in the harder challenges and I have to throw down the controller or restart checkpoint asap, or else I will feel the wrath of the controller. _childDocuments_.review: Overall, I would say that this was a better experience than the first Unravel. This was largely thanks to the improved gameplay. The addition of being able to have two players instead of only one was perhaps the best new feature for me. Having two players brought an additional depth layer to the game, especially when in comes to puzzle complexity. This time around the puzzles were much more versatile and clever than they were in the first game. In addition, the additional challenge levels contained some nice puzzles and platforming challenges. Wall jumping was also a welcome feature.However, compared to the first game, the story was much worse this time around (and it wasn't particularly great in the first game, either). Also, I was very disappointed that the level of detail in the environments and textures was worse than it was in the first game (two years older). Even though the camera angle was further away from the environment than it was in the first game (due to having two players this time around), it still doesn't mean that the developers should become more lazy when creating their levels. This was particularly disappointing for me, since the attention to detail in the evironments was the first game's most impressive part.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. The graphics have excellent lighting, depth and focus. The style makes you feel small against the world, and ever so more in touch with its every branch. The soundtrack is lovely, it sparks many emotions that speak in a low voice. The story unfolds with your hooks and swings, as you follow the footsteps of the protagonists, as you traverse the objects that bear their memories. Music, lighting and environment combined change in symphony to shift the flow from worry to calmness to joy and back. The experience concludes with a beautiful message, a lesson to remember, learnt through your very movements.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: A short and honest review of UNRAVEL TWOEven though the essence that made the first game a hidden jewel isn’t completely here, “Unravel 2” is a very sweet and brief experience worth having, especially along with a friend or a loved one. Co-op is a really welcome addition this time around, but unfortunately it comes with the sacrifice of the highly emotional story the first game beautifully told. It’s clear the developers had good intentions with this second entry and its message of unity and understanding, but it just doesn’t hit all the notes. Anyway, in the “gamey” side: controls are smooth and level design is ingenious yet simple. Long gone are the sometimes cruel and frustrating puzzles “Unravel” 1 had, at least in story mode, as there are many challenges to get some extras here… not very worth doing that, though. With little to none replay value (unless you want to do some speedrunning) and a lack of impactful moments (again, the first game had), I don’t see myself coming back to “Unravel 2” anytime soon. Maybe one day, with someone in the same room (or via remote play) to spend some time and/or when there are no other (lots of) titles waiting to be experienced.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this review with 0 minutes playing this alone, I have no idea what it's like alone. This is a quite clever puzzle sidescroller. I'm a big fan of coop games in general, so maybe I'm just a bit biased but I really enjoyed all the mechanics, and the story was similarly good to the first game. Not heavy, but adds to the game. It's not as complex as portal or story oriented as Way Out, and not as fancy as It Takes Two, but definitely interesting, and it got me good.  The same but better. The jumping mechanic is different, but makes sense. There is no thread behind, only the two of you connected, which opens new possibilities. It's a bit trickier than the first one, especially the bonus levels, I haven't finished any of them yet, but they are really hard imo. Aesthetics are still marvelous. If you liked the first one, you're gonna love this one too.

_childDocuments_.review: Me and a friend of mine wanted to play this game, but something that is not made clear is that you actually can't legitimately play the game online, there's only local co-op. No worries you'd say, for that reason there is Remote Play Together, and you'd be right, the only problem is that the game doesn't work with RPT either... I send my buddy the link, he joins and then it says he doesn't have an output, even though he's got a mouse and keyboard, we both have controllers too, so we tried all four possible combinations (me with a controller and him with a keyboard, him with a controller me with a keyboard, both with keyboards and both with controllers) nothing works! So I read somewhere that Unravel 2 is technically still an Origin game(hence why you have to run origin to run the game) and Origin does not support RPT. So basically there is no way you can play this game online. Very disappointing. Don't bother playing it unless you actually live with the person you wanna play with or you have the opportunity to have your friends come over. This game is in no way PC-friendly.
_childDocuments_.name: Unravel Two

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a fun, short couch co-op game to play for a whole afternoon with a friend or partner, this is one of them.[Played together with my husband, both using controllers]I didn't play the first Unravel game, but you don't really need to play the first game to get the fun out of this one. It's all about the puzzles and working together with your partner/friend to solve them. Although it is said that you can play it as single player as well, I haven't yet tried playing it solo, but I bet it can be entertaining and challenging as well.There's no dialogue, but the narrative combined with the music and stunning visuals can make an immersive experience as you play. The whole ambient of the game can get quite sad and dark, with bits of light and relieve as you advance the story. It's quite cute to see how these little yarn characters interact with this world as you swing your way out of danger.As for the puzzles, they are challenging enough to enjoy throughout the game and to not frustrate you if one of you gets stuck.Overall, is a fun, although short, game to spend some quality time with friends and family.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love Unravel and Unravel Two. I have played them before already on Origin, before it arrived on the Steam Store.I love the Yarny people! I found the way the two Yarnies can merge into one (to move around more easily) to be rather clever and practical!The game, like the first one, is gorgeous! _childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Underwhelming, but grab it on sale if you love co-op and artsy games, it has its moments, and the co-op grappling / swinging mechanics are awesome.Completed the game with my partner.  I feel like critiquing hard about what's wrong first, because what's right is so good and really feels squandered.The devs put a message in the game that they are proud that the game was designed by committee.  It really shows - in a bad way. The art style, story, and gameplay all get you hooked - and there are some great moments for all 3, but it remains directionless and there is no big climax, either for the gameplay or story.Storywise, you're left never feeling sure what the concurrent storylines were all about, nothing is explained, some "things" are introduced at the end, and left us with the impression that it was mostly all for show and was never really going anywhere in the first place, (much like the "Lost" series).Gameplaywise, it's extremely unique and satisfying, but never really gets challenging, except for the bonus levels, which spike up in difficulty and frustration so hard, with long stretches of difficulty and no checkpoints.  Somewhere between those two extremes I think there's a lot of fun to be had.And the flow of the gameplay; it peaks in the middle with a really exciting sequence, and then starts to wind down again, and finishes very weakly. After what they showed us in the middle, it felt unfinished - no big challenge, no climax, no "boss fight" that ties into the concurrent story, just ends on an easy level like any of the other levels...It's this design by committee that leaves things feeling like a bunch of features rattled up in a can and poured out in a sequence that doesn't have any high level flow directing you through an experience, an adventure. it's clear there's no consistent high level vision over how the player moves through the experience. Hierarchies have a purpose, they're not some big bad evil thing to be avoided.  They exist in nature for a reason; they're a very good filtering process.  In any creative effort, you need one or a few people with a consistent high level vision to steer the ship while everyone else is focused on their respective tasks, doing a great job on the details, but unable to see the big picture clearly. Likewise, the people at the helm can see the big picture because their minds are uncluttered by the details. The human brain can only focus on so much at once. This is just how it is. It's natural, and useful. Together we create big, detailed experiences for people to lose themselves in.Extremely beautiful, with a photorealistic look at times.  Even that loading screen which is just the dawn sky reflected in a rippling lake, is mesmerising.  The cutscenes set the bar a bit high with how soft the wollen characters look, which is a little disappointing when the actual gameplay graphics kick in, nevertheless, the woolen string physics look amazing and very believable.  The scenery is amazing to stare at and some times you want to move through slowly and admire it, even though the platforming sequences seem to encourage some quick swinging moves, though this doesn't happen too often.The "yarnies" story seems non-existant, and the cinematic for them at the end really comes out of nowhere, but watching the adventure the 2 kids are going through, playing out in the background scenery of the levels as you play the game itself, is a really cool idea.  Sometimes the gameplay paralells the kids adventure in a way, which really makes you feel it's all building up to something. Shame it never seems to tie together (lol) in a meaninful way by the end.  It just leaves you hanging by a thread (sorry, this is too easy...).Seriously that string physics gameplay where you have to combine grappling, swinging, and "belaying" each other, rock climbing style, so that one holds while the other swings, is so damn cool. We had some really satisfying moments, some part of the gameplay, some seemingly emergent because of the way these physics features fluidly combine together. You feel like a bad-ass, or Spider-Man, in some sequences, flipping through the air between grappling points in sequence, to land safely with the grace of an expert acrobat.  There is nothing like this in any other game I've played.There are some "chase" sequences which are genuinely exciting and entertaining, and had us laughing out loud at the different ways we were dying and trying to keep ahead. Again, as mentioned, it's a shame they saved nothing like this for the end of the game. It really ends on a low after some of the exciting moments in the middle.See the TLDR at the top. Hop you enjoy it. Maybe the devs will make a 3rd co-op game in the series, and designate a vision holder for the experience this time.

_childDocuments_.review: ✅ Presents a unique gameplay based around controlling two yarn creatures connected with a thread.✅ Very nice and detailed graphics quality, textures, lighting and animations. Better than the previous game.✅ Almost No-GUI gameplay! The game world is your GUI.✅ Part logic, part physics based puzzles.✅ Puzzles and levels have some twists and turns that make the experience fresher at times.✅ Very nice, melancholic, fitting and dynamic soundtrack. Music changes depending on the action on the screen. I liked the soundtrack from the first Unravel more.✅ Frequent save checkpoints. More frequent than in the previous game, so it's a bit faster to repeat a challenge. You can also resume a level from last checkpoint if you quit mid-level.✅ The levels can be quite lengthy, depending on how good you are in solving the puzzles.✅ Silent no-words gameplay and cinematics. Doesn't require any language learning, except for the menu and parts of the levels, where the basic mechanics are explained. Not counting if you want to use hints.✅ Simple and intuitive controls. Played on an Xbox 360 Controller.✅ Gameplay is more dynamic than in the previous game. The controls are also more flexible and easier.✅ Built-in hint system and gameplay easing mechanics that help make the harder parts easier for some people. You won't get stuck!✅ The hint reminders, hint system, and gameplay easing mechanics are optional and can all be turned off in the menu.✅ Optional Advanced Challenges for people for whom the base game was too short and too easy.✅ Playable on my integrated Intel HD Graphics 4600, but works slower than the previous game (I play in 1280x720, 33 fps average, 12 fps minimum. Previous game ran at 1600x900, 46 fps average, 32 fps minimum).✅ The cost is very low, especially during a discount and even lower in a bundle with Unravel (at least in my country). Totally worth it!❌ Uses the Denuvo anti-tamper DRM.❌ Requires the Origin Client to launch every time when launching the game.❌ Requires pairing your Steam account with your Origin account before launch. This can cause problems with launching the game for the first time afterwards and needs restarting both Steam and Origin game clients to fix it.❌ The game crashed often after loading a level and one time near the end of a level. Thankfully you can resume your level from the last checkpoint.❌ In-game cinematics can cause some conflict with your installed Codecs, and can prevent you from launching the game and playing, if you have bad luck. It might be worth it to uninstall any codec pack you installed and install only the Standard K-Lite Codec Pack to avoid conflicts. This can happen in some other games as well.❌ Some of the thread management mechanics are gone compared to the previous game. Most probably to keep the gameplay more dynamic and faster. This makes it a little less varied compared to Unravel.❌ Levels are more similar to each other than those in Unravel. There is overall less variance in gameplay and mechanics. Especially the physics aspect is smaller. There is also less levels. ❌ Lots of speedrunning and "do not die" achievements, requiring you to complete all levels as fast as you can with no mistakes and breaks. Only for people who have coffee instead of blood in their veins.❌ Has a co-op achievement.❌ I didn't particularly like the narrative and story inspirations. This aspect was somehow done better in Unravel, where you feel more connected and immersed. This game feels more arcade, more generic.❌ You cannot turn off the big bokeh (blur) effect. This just means that ~90% of what you see on screen will be permanently blurred. Previous game had the same no-option problem. I know that this is a photo-lens-like effect that at the same time serves to focus your eyes on the action (and hide low-quality graphic assets), but it would be nice if there was an option for anyone who doesn't like performance loss and blurry games to disable it. It's nice for Photo Mode and static photos, but a game is not a photo. Also a simple slider to adjust its strength would have been nice.❌ Even the easy optional Advanced Challenges are sometimes too hard. Very small % of people will have the patience to do them all.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh. This game has an excellent engine, feels smooth, but is utterly marred by poor level design.For context, I played this game with a friend. _childDocuments_.review: Really nice 2 player local co-op experience on offer here. If you're looking for something for a couch co-op setting, this is definitely worth getting.Don't let the somewhat generic vibe of the promotional material put you off.The player-player interplay in the physics puzzle based gameplay loop is top notch enjoyable, well thought and fleshed out, and thoroughly addictive.Plus the graphics, while not technically too over the top amazing (in 2020) and being somewhat understated, are still really beautiful and do an excellent job at giving an immersive macro zoom vibe to the trip through the gameworld. The art direction is good enough that this seems like something that'll age well.The story, while decidedly background fare that never gets in the way of the flow of the gameplay - which is actually a good thing - nevertheless provides for a bit of intrigue to the goings on that the player controlled characters have to find their way through.If you enjoyed Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons, you're likely to enjoy this, and vice versa - it's a good shout to check that game out if you enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Unravel 2 is a fantastic puzzle platformer. The objective of the game is to get to the end of the stage. Use string physics to solve obstacles and keep on moving forward. Gameplay-wise, controller is best. PS configuration. Square to tie a knot, X to jump, O to unravel knots, Triangle to switch character/ Hold Triangle to get your buddy to hop on your back. LT to hold onto your string, RT to toss your string. Only in the last stage will you get to use the most basics of basics, double jumping and wall climbing. Conclusion, do try Unravel 2. Sadly, the main campaign lasted only 4.7 hours. Even for such a short game, only 1.5% of all copies sold actually completed the main campaign so it's meant for an ultra-niche audience who can appreciate complex physics puzzles. I suspect the game is ONLY designed for controller and that keyboard is just unplayable.1. Beautiful puzzlesI loved figuring them out.2. Nice EnvironmentYou made a nice world using the PhyreEngine. PhyreEngine is a free to use game engine from Sony Interactive Entertainment, compatible with PlayStation 4, PlayStation 3, PlayStation VR, PlayStation Vita, PlayStation Portable, Microsoft Windows (for OpenGL and DirectX 11), Google Android and Apple iOS. PhyreEngine has been adopted by several game studios and has been used in over 200 published titles.1. Short, Way Too ShortThis may have affected how players viewed the game. It's so short.

Key Features Discover a world worth exploring. Run, climb and glide your way through a dark Nordic forest and explore its living, breathing ecosystem filled with secrets and mystical creatures. _childDocuments_.review: Fe's biggest strength is probably its biggest weakness.When I started playing Fe, I was enthralled with a childlike sense of wonder and curiosity, but that wonder and curiosity unfortunately led to frustration; Fe barely tells you what to do to move forward, and the solution to problems seems very vague most of the time. The game does a very poor job of teaching you how to play it. Your character controls pretty sluggishly, which further adds to the tedium, but from the small amount of the game I've played so far there's some very cool moments and solving the problems the game throws you leads to some pretty great 'a-ha!' moments.The game is a visual and audio treat, but it's important to know what you're getting yourself in for before you buy.It pains me to slap a 'do not recommend' on this game, because I'm intending on playing this through to the end, and I am really enjoying it so far, I just don't feel like it's the sort of thing the average gamer would enjoy.UPDATE:Game is fantastic. Buy it.
