_childDocuments_.review: Many reviews of this game are misleading. Yes, it's cute, and yes, it's for the most part an exploration game with some metroidvania elements. But I wouldn't call it “calm" because unfortunately it's also a mediocre and frustrating 3D platformer set in a world that is more often repetitive than delightful. I finished the game, but honestly I started to get quite annoyed with it at the mid-point.Most annoying is the map: it's incredibly unhelpful and does little to get a sense of the rather large world and how it's interconnected. It would be great if we could see all the various collectibles, but instead we get vague, permanent markers for the main-quest items. I had zero desire to go and find all the collectibles after I finished the game, which is rare for me.As for those collectibles, it might take you a few hours of play until you realize which items are unnecessary and which move the story forward. The game generally does a poor job at signalling what exactly you are supposed to do. There is a built-in hint system of sorts that at least tells you where to go, and I strongly recommend using it all the time and following it exactly in order to avoid confusion and keep the story plodding forward. Of course, this mechanic makes exploration unnecessary, and that leads us to the essential problem with : the game doesn't seem to understand how to weave exploration with storytelling.It's also not a very easy game. The 3D platforming sometimes requires some precision and a bad jump can send you way back to try the whole sequence all over again. There are also enemies that can kill you, which will also send you back. It's anxiety-inducing, neither calm nor peaceful.Finally, it's worth mentioning that the game has a very innovative musical mechanic. Alas, it is also disappointing, as it involves fine-tuning loudness and nothing very musical at all. It feels like a wasted opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little gem. Fe is probably one of the cutest indie games for me by far. It's relatively short and it can be finished in 4-5 hours, maybe more if you're looking for 100% but it's relaxing and story is beautiful. Reminds me of games like AER Memories of Old and The First Tree in terms of artstyle. Fe reminds me of Ori, but it's unique in its own way. You play as a fox-like creature singing to communicate with other animals and learning their language to unlock new abilities. And music is what really stands out in this game, especially the ending is really touching. Well made platforming and puzzles. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Take a walk in this magical forest shrouded in mystery as you communicate with its inhabitants to help save the forest from an enemy that wants to silence everything.  is a cute Jump-N-Run Plattformer with beautiful art style, minimalistic story telling and fun game mechanics. You play as a fox-like creature singing to communicate with other animals that will assist you to overcome obstacles by activating the forest fauna. Helping out the friendly animals in the forest will eventually net you the same singing abilities (different creatures sing in different languages). Hidden gems are scattered through the forest and are used to unlock new traversing abilities. The game can be completed within 5 to 7 hours and further extended by collecting all the gems. The only negative is the backtracking without the option to load in an already completed area. [8/10]

_childDocuments_.review: This game reminds me a little of what would happen if you crossed Spore with Spyro, and added a dash of Journey. The 3D platforming is a lot like Spyro, the story is whimsical and interpretive (if you love coming up with game plot theories, you'll love this game), and the interactions with the other creatures of the forest feel similar to Spore's creature stage (albeit less annoying and buggy.) The art style is gorgeous, there is no annoying tutorial or follow-the-dotted-line gameplay or intrusive HUD (although there is a map you can access with tab if you get lost) and the music and sound design is pleasant and natural.Speaking of bugs though, there was a bug that almost prevented me from achieving 100% shard completion in one of the zones. A set of flowers wouldn't activate for me, and I had to overcome it via an in-game workaround that clearly wasn't the intended solution. And once you unlock the final ability, there isn't much else to do in the game except finding all the glyphs, and most of them are copy pasted and not much fun to look for.This game could've benefited nicely from some time trials, races or a couple of interesting side quests for some end-game that would've made collecting all the abilities worth it. Also beware that this game will install Origin on your PC. If you have a Nintendo Switch though, you can circumvent it by buying the game on there.At the time of writing, this game is somewhat underground (probably thanks to zero attempts at advertising), but it's definitely 100% worth playing. I hope more unique games like this are released.

_childDocuments_.review: This is another review that really pains me to make, much like my review for HK. If Steam offered a mixed or indifferent option I would pick that in a heartbeat. I genuinely do not know if a thumbs up or a thumbs down is better. I adore this game and have even made some content inspired by it, but given the circumstances, I think it's better to post a negative than a positive. I can say now that the product  It was worth what I paid for it and if you want to try it, absolutely do.It's a great game, unique, charming, captivating, but behind all of that lies a borderline nonsensical story and mechanics that should've really been expanded upon because they feel too shallow. Overall, if I had to briefly describe Fe, I would describe it as "a hint of something". Fe opens the door for such great potential yet does not expand on it, it defines the space needed for a beautiful story and unique game, yet only scratches the surface of this space. It is as if it fears going any deeper would damage it.Everything in it feels shallow, the gameplay, the story... Everything is so unique but they fail to really make it meaningful. Still - it left its mark on me and was very memorable, it brings warm memories to think of, so if someone asked me whether or not I thought the gameplay and story were OK, there would be no answer, it simultaneously is and isn't.The story is by far the most problematic bit of the game and is where most of my gripes sit. It is not well established, and it is confusing - especially the ending. I don't want to say much about it, but it feels like the ending was left up to someone that had no knowledge of the product ahead of time, they were told "statue looking things want to use their magic to ascend or something" (don't worry, that is not a spoiler, it is not entirely accurate). It makes zero sense whatsoever with context to the rest of the game and the game's storytelling does not do a good job of going into why. For the first time in a while the ending of a game has left me feeling almost concussed, wobbling about in a fit of confusion without any closure as to what just happened or why. Is it even a story?.. If they had used the entire game's current story for a hypothetical exposition, then maybe it would have been orders of magnitude better, because it would create a wonderous mystery to solve. What was  motive?The world is another mild problem. Fe goes on about this forest that you are supposed to save, but of all the seasons to pick, they chose winter. This is a bit of a nitpick, I know, but hear me out: They wanted to outline this "beautiful world" yet chose the season with the most dull colors, with the least room for any sort of environmental specialties. If they had gone with spring or summer they could have used a much wider color palette. While the graphics of a game don't really define it, the artstyle does, and their choice of season inadvertently shot themselves in the foot by only allowing them to use cold colors. The only time you see warm colors like red, orange, and yellow are in negative circumstances, save for a single memorable type of plant, and a very specific location that makes up 10% of the game. Everything feels so limited, compressed almost.For some positives? The music is pretty great. It fits the environment super well and captures the mood of what is going on quite nicely. I will definitely be listening to this in my spare time. Additionally, the mechanics were fresh, something I had not seen used as a primary mechanic before. The environment, while bland, is still nice. It's a neat place to be and it has some cool bits and pieces to it that make it special. The world was not ugly by any means and I think that the design of the map should be recognized positively.In general, the game was neat. It was charming, it was different than the rest, but it was empty, it was a husk. It leaves me hungry for more not out of curiosity but out of longing for something that could have been. It's a neat game, but I can't see myself telling people it's one of those games you really need to play, hence why I decided to reluctantly go with a -1.

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a 3D metroidvania with a beautiful art style and aesthetic, and minimalistic story telling. While I tend not to be a fan of games with such minimalistic stories, Fe still manages to do a good job in its presentation. The story begins with your character, a small fox-like creature, landing in a forest. You quickly learn that you can communicate with other creatures by singing, and that there's some robot-like creatures trying to silence the forest. As I said, it's a pretty minimalistic story (there's no dialogue, no backstory, nothing like that), but going into more detail might still spoil some things.As for the gameplay, like I mentioned, it's similar to a metroidvania, meaning that there's a huge interconnected world for you to explore, though new regions open as you unlock new abilities. In this case, there's only two abilities that are necessary to beat the game, while the "voices" you learn from specific creatures are all needed (and also open paths). It's an interesting mechanic, though it can be frustrating at times, since the game doesn't go into depth explaining how the singing mechanic works. The platformer can also become annoying at times, but nothing too serious.I already mentioned the aethetics of the game, and I still must repeat myself, it looks gorgeous. It has a distinctive art style, though the soundtrack seems to be minimal; then again, it makes sense, as they wouldn't want it to take over the singing aspect of the game. Something I forgot to mention when talking about the story (as it's related to that) is that, at certain points, there's some amazing setpieces, a moment in particular during the early portion of the game felt really good.Finally, I'll add that it's a very short game, though enjoyable. However, I feel the game has some unnecessary padding after beating it. Like many metroidvanias, there's collectibles to collect, three types, of which two are required for achievements. While one of said types can be easily collected during the story (and even if you miss some, they can be easily found afterwards), the other type, the crystals, are much harder to find. The crystals are required to unlock abilities, but in order to find some of them, you can be forced to do lots of backtracking. Another complaint would be that, after getting all crystals, you unlock the final ability, one which would've been really useful when tracking down collectibles, but at that point in the game, feels meaningless, as there's no further content to enjoy, other than travel around the game's world.So, in conclusion, do I recommend this game? Yeah, I think so. It's not really a bad game, and the achievements, while a bit time consuming, are easy enough (even more so if you use guides). Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for the worst FPS game experience of your life, then Fe is an absolute must-play. Just kidding—this isn't even an FPS, but honestly, after playing it, I almost wish it were. This indie title from Zoink! was marketed as an eco-friendly, charming platformer, but let's be real—charm can only get you so far when your gameplay is more lifeless than the robotic enemies you occasionally encounter.For a game that was supposed to be about exploration, it sure makes getting lost feel like a chore. The controls are about as smooth as sandpaper, making the platforming sections feel more like a punishment than an adventure. And don't even get me started on the singing mechanic, which is meant to connect you with nature but ends up feeling like you’re trying to tune a broken radio.Visually, Fe is... fine, I guess? It’s like staring at a postcard for hours—nice at first, but eventually, you just want to move on. The color palette is pretty, but after a while, everything just blends into one big, indistinguishable blur. If you’ve seen one glowing tree, you’ve seen them all.If the clunky gameplay and underwhelming visuals of Fe didn’t already put you off, how about the fact that it uses Denuvo? That’s right, this charming little indie game comes with the heavyweight DRM usually reserved for AAA titles. Because nothing says "immersive forest adventure" like having your CPU performance throttled by an invasive anti-tamper system. If you weren’t already frustrated by the awkward controls and lackluster mechanics, Denuvo might just be the final nail in the coffin.In the end, Fe tries to be deep and meaningful, but it's about as shallow as a kiddie pool. The narrative is barely there, and what little story it has feels more like an afterthought. So if you’re in the market for a game that tries too hard to be artsy without actually being fun, then by all means, give Fe a go. Just don’t say I didn’t warn you.

_childDocuments_.review: All in all, Fe's got a pretty face but a boring personality. Fe is an exploration game incorporating a musical mechanic, a lot of atmosphere, and pretty graphics. It's a very nice looking 3D platformer full of unique environments and creatures, as well as pleasing-to-the-eye colour coordination. This game had a lot of potential but it unfortunately fell short for me. I like finishing things, but I didn't complete this game. In fact, I didn't even play it enough to collect all the possible trading cards I could from it. While it is an exploration game, Fe does a poor job at giving you an objective to actually go off of to make any progress in the game. Even the map is of little help in this regard, only giving a very vague idea of where you are and where you need to go without accounting for anything in between. There is a built-in hint system that acts as a guide, but this also pretty much throws the exploration aspect of the game right out the window. The musical mechanic could have been great; something new and different or interesting. It wasn't any of these things, and turned into one of the main reasons I stopped playing the game altogether. All it was, to put it simply, was finding different notes here and there, then using the one specific note that worked on whatever you were trying to interact with, and screaming that note at whatever it was. A plant? Another animal? You screamed that note together until you got what you wanted. That's it. The pitches in the game were irritating for me to say the least, and I couldn't take much more of it. The final failure for this game in my personal opinion was the utter lack of any form of a story. I understand that there weren't cutscenes or bits of actual dialogue to drive it, but don't try to use that as an excuse. Inside, Limbo, Abzu, Little Nightmares, I could go on and on. For me, Fe lacked a story.

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a cute little hidden gem similar to AER Memories of Old with a great soundtrack and atmospheric visuals. It's a bit on the shorter side for a game of this price, but overall I would recommend it (on sale). TLDR, its a strong 7/10 with my issues being pretty minor. I love the concepts, gathering the different voices and the color changes to show you which voice is needed made the game for me. The main lil guy is also cute, and the designs of the other animals are as well (the lizards were my favorites). When you face the enemies, it really reminded me of the "Silent Realm" levels in Zelda: Skyward Sword with the Guardians, especially with how your only choice really was to run and hide. Them searching for you with a specific FOV gave a similar feeling of being hunted with no defenses. For Achievements, it only adds on about 2-4 hours max of collectible hunting and a possible second playthrough if you locked yourself out of one of the missable ones. Easy, simple, nothing too challenging. A good game to add to the completion list. The story is told through "visions" and zero voice acting, which makes it a bit harder to understand. If you're interested in the story, you have to really dig for it or just watch some guy with a cool voice explain it to you on youtube. The controls were also a bit challenging, especially the singing mechanics (I literally just wiggled my mouse around until it worked lmao) and the fact that you cant really change them makes it worse. Would recommend a controller, but as someone who hates controllers it was manageable. Another downside for me is the "open world" as it is pretty sparse of things to do. The game doesn't hold your hand, and you can spend quite a while trying to figure out what to do or where to go. The collectibles are also a pain, and it was the last achievement I got. I disliked how the abilities were locked behind the number of collectibles you got, but it did provide somewhat of an incentive (however I completed the game well before getting all the gems). Its cute and fun for a single playthrough, however I struggle to find a reason to come back to it in the future. Possibly the biggest con for me is the inclusion of the "Origin" EA Play whatever its called service which is mandatory to play this game. I personally hate it so much when companies still require you to download their service to use a steam product, and this game is sadly an EA game. I had no issues (other than being annoyed) having origin running at the same time, but I have heard horror stories of people simply being unable to play due to this requirement.

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved this game and definitely recommend to anyone looking for something chill, pretty, and easy. The graphics are beautiful and the game runs very smoothly. The little creatures are adorable and the songs you eventually learn from each one to progress through the lands feels good to play through. The ethereal look of each area is really one of my favorite parts. It just feels like a living in a fairy tail. Lizzyboys are freaking precious and them following me around to do the bouncy flowers was one of my favorite parts of the game, too. Its hard to pick a favorite creature. The giant ones are just as beautiful as the small ones are adorable. It wasn't too hard to get all of the achievements either.The only thing i'd change about this game is adding some kind of journal to keep up with which crystals you have collected or haven't collected (and maybe the hieroglyphics). I expected to gather more crystals by just doing a normal play through of the game but i had 30ish to collect in the end game. I spent a lot of time running around confused. At that point i had no idea which ones i did or didn't have. I followed EAs guide to find them all after i finished the story. EAs guide is a little messed up by saying some crystals belong in an area they don't belong in, and some instructions are a little too vague (more pics would be nice). That made finding a few crystals very difficult because i just didn't know which guide to look at for them. I found them all in the end but it took unnecessarily long.I guess one more thing i would change is the last ability. I'm not really sure what the point of it is. By the time you get it, you're tired of searching the lands from crystal hunting and there's nothing left to gain from being able to fly. I guess its cool if you just want to keep roaming around though. But tbh i just logged off immediately after getting it lol.Aside from crystal hunting being a little tedious, its a lovely little game, definitely check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: I mulled for a long time on whether or not to recommend and in the end my conclusion is: I'm conflicted.This game is really pretty to look at, with the colour schemes and designs, but there's also a level of block potato-quality which stops me from being able to call it gorgeous or anything of that sort. There has been something of an effort to teach the controls as you go along and without long blocks of explanation or dialogue, but the end result is somewhat confusing, with some combos being very difficult to work out and strange manipulations of the controller necessary to do multiple things at once at times.I got all of the crystal helmets, which were supposed to be giving me backstory, and I'm *still* not entirely sure what the end was. I could tell that there was some sort of twist, but it didn't actually explain or clarify what had happened before that twist point. The creatures are charming, especially the little lemur-like thing that is called a Fe, but the use of songs/language to manipulate the area around you stops being quite so cute when you end up screaming at a series of flowers for two minutes straight in order to get high up enough to have a chance at getting a crystal. Note: a chance. I'm not bad with platformers and I'm pretty completionist, but I just could not get the last dozen or so crystals because of a couple of complicated, timed puzzles and platforming sections which were beyond my reach - jump a half-second too late or a few pixels too low and you have to do considerable work to reset.

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a pretty solid take on a 3D platformer with metroidvania elements. One comparison that comes to mind is between Fe and the 2D Ori and the Blind Forest (Definitive edition), as both games use a considerable amount of linear metroidvania, comparable price points, and awesome orchestral music. The characters and environments in Fe even look somewhat like those Ori, but the story and game play are drastically different here. Ultimately, this game is pretty good, but Fe feels much more underdeveloped in certain aspects.Like Ori, Fe guides the player to a degree (more than in Ori if you leave map markers on), but there is still a bit of exploration and cool puzzle solving to be done, as well as interesting upgrades that you acquire in a linear progression across a non-linear map. Tree climbing can be neat, yet a little clunky at times; however, there's a way to get pretty consistent climbs to the very top of trees without accidentally jumping off. The need to communicate to animals with different languages throughout the game is a great game loop, and the diversity in how animals behave will keep you engaged. Areas are themed like in Ori, and honestly the environments are cool enough to my liking. Saving/encountering the leaders of the different animal types is actually cool, but things come across as a little rushed in some parts (. This said, a lot of moments have been really cool and enjoyable. I didn't attempt 100%, but I am sure it would be interesting to try to find the shards required to do so, and unlock the remaining optional abilities this way.Also like in Ori titles, stealth has its place in the game play, but to a much greater degree than in Ori. However, the stealth part of the game has limited variety (). The silent ones are those you hide from in stealth sections. You only encounter two types of enemies from this group, so it feels pretty lazy in terms of stealth variety. The AI of the silent ones is pretty dumb too, since they often lack object permanence and usually forget about you once you jump into a bush. This takes us to the half-baked lore the game offers. You can pick up collectables that give you the perspective of the silent ones. These end up being largely repetitive and uninformative with exception of a few of these. Hence, it might be more worthwhile to skip these items, since they just lead to loss of time for the most part. By the time the ending comes in, you're not left with much sense of why the silent ones did what they did in the first place. Some players have made an effort to make sense of it, and to a degree, it makes some sense, but you're still left with more questions (. The game ends pretty abruptly and ends up being underwhelming and disappointing (). Do I recommend this? Yes, but I can't say it's quite the quality of platformers like the Ori games (or beloved triple A 3D platformers), as it just feels too empty in some respects. I take similar issue to the buggy 3D game, Blue Fire (which poorly borrows a lot from the 2D masterpiece, Hollow Knight). That said, the only "bug" I had in Fe was some difficulty in getting the game to communicate with my xbox one controller on the title screen, but it was fine otherwise. In my opinion, 3D metroidvania-esque games end up having more quirks than 2D ones, but we still need more devs to try working on games like these, because they can be really enjoyable, and I liked this one quite a bit.

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a truly gorgeous game. The minimalist art design is charming, the color palettes are very appealing, and the music is simple yet stunning. Every element of the game comes together to create an immersive experience. Virtually any individual screenshot of this game could be framed as art due to the expressive nature of the game’s world. Although Fe is by no means a hard game, it doesn’t hold your hand through the journey of discovery. Ultimately your goal is to explore the world to progress and piece together a story that is told through visuals alone. Not a single word is spoken throughout. There are several spots where the music compliments the story for emphasis and to enhance the already memorable set pieces. Without spoiling too much, the first time climbing the deer spirit is a breathtaking feast for the eyes and ears. The ending of the game is similarly fantastical, but that should be experienced to understand what I mean. If the game seems too simplistic, bear in mind that it will not overstay its welcome. The game is very short and can reasonably be completed is a few hours. Shooting for completion will see you exploring and conquering creative environmental puzzles that, while not necessary to complete the game, are a welcome addition. I only have two complaints with the game. First is that there does not seem to be any kind of fast travel system. Even after completing the story, you still have to manually go everywhere, which can make hunting down pink crystals you may have missed feel like more of a chore. This is a bigger problem for completionists, but it would have been helpful for the average player as well. There's no reason to not have a quick travel system in the post-game at least. My other complaint is that you need to be logged into an EA account to play this game. It really feels like an unnecessary restriction for a single player game. Overall, Fe is an experience that anybody with a taste for 3D Metroidvanias and/or artful expression in video games can find enjoyment. Definitely try it out if you can.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice platforming game with an emphasis on exploration. There's no combat, and no dialogue. I don't think this is a good kid's game despite the graphics being very childlike. The main reason is that it's just not very intuitive and hard to figure out. Once you know how to play it, it's easy, This is more of a relaxation game. The world is really mellow, and while there are enemies in the game, you don't really fight them other than yanking a crystal off of the back of one enemy type. The music and graphics relax you as you venture deeper into this world and discover the story, but the game is full of irritating platforming that gets almost unacceptable if you try to complete it 100%. Basically, you find pink crystals to unlock new abilities. You never get a double jump, so you are always trying to climb trees to find the vantage point necessary to use the glide ability that you eventually get. Gliding around the map is a lot of fun. Beyond that, you won't get any other abilities until after you beat the game, but by that point they're pretty useless. The main ability that doesn't involve movement is the ability to sing. You can sing to communicate with animals and make flowers bloom to create springboards or allow you to float upwards. This is a really nice game mechanic and it emphasizes the story element as you connect with more animals and learn their language. The game itself isn't very long, though, and if you want to 100% complete it you have to collect a bunch of pink crystals. This is where the game gets frustrating because even if you know where the crystals are you have to spend 15 minutes figuring out which tree or bridge you need to float across to access it. If you get all of the crystals you get the ability to fly infinitely. This is great but it's entirely useless since by the time you get it you've already accomplished everything the game has to offer. Overall, I really liked the experience of Fe, but I felt it somewhat overstayed its welcome. The crystal collecting is ridiculously frustrating and its in comparison to a game that otherwise has extremely simple, albeit eloquently done, platforming segments. It's the complexity of the environments that ultimately makes it worth recommending, even though at times it gets frustrating because you have to backtrack and circle around places, or you might screw up trying to access one area only to find you needed to take an alternate area. Couple that with some really nice set pieces like a gigantic deer you can climb up and the overall experience is very interesting even though the game play is pretty shallow.

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a wordless, noncombat exploration game featuring an eponymous Fe, trying to uncover what has happened in its world with hulking monstrosities capturing all the innocent animals.The aesthetic of this game is lovely. Even though it's very muted, the world is beautifully rendered and is compelling to study from a clifftop or treetop. This is always important in an exploration game. There are so many nooks with little secrets to find, and the game provides you with many ways to move about.The movement can be a bit clunky at times, but since this is a noncombat game, that's usually not a huge deal, and while it is possible for the enemies to capture you, which is basically this game's version of "death", you have to know to be evasive, use terrains to your advantage, and find the best way to navigate. There are admittedly points where the clunkiness can make jumps, for instance, kind of frustrating, but the game is so charming that you'll stick it out. Of course, the most challenging movements are for extras, so they're not strictly necessary.Because the story is wordless, there are certain moments where you assume control of one of the hulking things for an alternate point of view at a different point in time. These are not extensive sections, but they provide an interesting and not unwelcome break from the usual gameplay.That said, because this is a noncombat exploration-oriented game, this is not a generally stressful game to play. As long as you are out of sight of the enemies, you can really take your time.Fe was a lovely game that drew me in to play through to the end. I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for an aesthetic indie game in a wonderful world, just want to play through the story and be surprised by the ending - this is the game for you!If you're a perfectionist like me wanting to get all the achievements - don't do it. I've played the story in less than a few hours and it has taken me at least double the time to get all the achievements - but one of them didn't even work since one of the helmets glitched for some reason... I'm too tired of all the work to collect the stuff for it again in a new save file. So now I'm stuck at 11/12 achievements and grumpy about it...(If anyone has a save file with 11/12 helmets collected...gimme please? owo)Long story short:Story and aesthetic are great! The collectibles are terrible!
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: The scenery is beautiful, not the mention the flow from the plants. The character Fe is really cute.It's a nice game full of relaxation but not aways. For me, anytime bumping into a Silent One was terrifying.It isn't always clear what you are suppose to do or where you are suppose to go. You bird friends guiding the way are very helpful in this or else I would have been stuck for a long time.It's not hard to 100% complete but it will take some time to get all the crystals.A great game, especially with the sale price I got it for.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game to get lost in and nice concept. I'd like the map to be more detailed, though. I think I'm just not enough of an "experienced" gamer (in open world games especially) to roam confidently in this game's world. In the beginning, it is quite clear what should happen, but after that I'm a bit lost. This also has to do with the fact that there is no text/ voices - which, on the other hand, fits the mysterious, fantastic atmosphere. I look forward to return to it later!
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: this game has some great concepts and the controls are amazing, the way you have to put certain pressures on the RT to learn a different language or connect with other life is such a cool gimmick. and the platforming is really unique and fun.i haven't got to far yet, these are first impressions because i'e played for 2 hours but so far i'm loving the game and cant wait to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a very unique game. Its geometric artistry is absolutely gorgeous as for the game its self...Its one of those games that you love to hate. The storyline is a bit interpretive. Personally to be able to function correctly I had to use both keyboard and controller. The fact that you have to 100% the game to unlock the finally skill :?...Im not sure what the thought process was on that one. That being said It is a fun and interesting game worth what you pay for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent game. The design is dark, but it hides its beauty. The progression system is also reminiscent metroidvanias, unlock a power up before going a certain direction. The story is up to you to decipher, but the gameplay itself can be confusing. There is little to no handholding and the "stealth" is not good. At least the traversal is fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game for around $6 on sale and what a steal that was - I thoroughly enjoyed it. I'll confess I was confused about the story, and there was a learning curve in the beginning, but by the time I reached the area with the giant deer I was sold. It's just so beautiful - the artwork is wonderful, as is the music. I thought the game mechanics were quite good and original. It's very atmospheric and quite relaxing to play - perfect for unwinding after a day of work. There is no direct combat. If you like 3D platforming games, give this a try. If you get it on sale it's one of the best deals around.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: It's not bad, but kinda "meh" puzzle platformer.Very pretty and atmospheric. Maybe a bit too colorful in same areas.Story is alright I guess, but the camera drove me insane at times and the scenery gets repetitive and 'samey'. It doesn't help if you want to collect everything as the areas are quite large and well as mentioned.... everything looks the same.Maybe I'll return one day as the game apparently let's you finish collecting after the story is over so you don't have to restart from scratch if you're a completionist, which was nice.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: I've put 10-11 hours into Fe and another 1 or so into exploring/completionist hunting after the game was nominally complete. I didn't get 100% of the Steam achievements, but did finish the second, more thorough tier of secrets (in the Doom sense.)Interesting game, although at times hard to follow the story or understand the next objective. Great for casual players and new gamers: it autosaves very often, mistakes are "free" and cost only time, and can always be paused or exited without going backwards / losing progress even within a boss fight. The hardest parts for me were some long platforming sequences that had issues with questionable camera autoaim logic (e.g. you'd jump while aiming "forward" but actually spiral to the side too quickly to recover.) The hardest parts for a novice gamer would be all the (not unreasonable, but not newbie-friendly) expectations that veteran video game enthusiasts take for granted; knowing to look for hints, secret areas, interaction opportunities, or unintuitive game mechanics.Clearly a lot of heart was put into the game by its developers, and I'm giving it a solid 8 out of 10 on my uncommonly harsh scale, where even a perfect game doesn't merit a 10 unless it goes above and beyond with art, creativity, or gameplay innovation and has no equal in the genre. Worth a play for patient players looking for a wholesome experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: It was kind of a pleasing experience. Visually it is pretty and gameplay was fun. Story on the other hand kind of confusing - I couldn't connect with the main character - sadly.  Achievement hunting was sort of pain due to the collectibles hunting - just no idea where exactly to look at since they don't show up on the map - even when collected so not sure where to look at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently few people played this game, and this is very sad. Fe is a very nice game with nice visuals and sound design. I won't tell about the story 'cause it's a very short game (6-8 hours of gameplay storywise; less if you know how to locate yourself on the map). It's cute, fun and quick to play! I truly recommend, easily one of my favourites.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: An incredibly cute game where you truly feel like a little critter from another dimention not so different from ours. Creatures interact with each other in surprising ways and make up a truly living world. If you play this game dont forget that it indie and it comes with some technical drawbacks but the innovation and originality make it worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a stunning game full of discovery, wonder, suspense and mystery. What I really love about the game is the lack of dialogue or the lack of traditional dialogue. You can't gripe about the music either. Simply lovely. I almost wrote the game off but it reminded me so much of "Ori" in which you need to explore or back track to discover secrets, items and solve mysteries. Once I started playing I couldn't put the controller down. Simple controls and a pretty nice casual, relaxing game where the soundtrack is affected by your progression.I recommend getting Fe on sale if you can though it's not expensive originally and is probably a 6 to 8 hour game off the bat with an extra 2 if achievement hunting. If you are into exploring, discovery, and a not too challenging achievement hunting then Fe is the game for you so pick it up full price or on sale. Either way You will not be disappointed.I give Fe an 8.5 out of 10
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a great game, you are shown a cut scene at the beginning to get an understanding of who you are, and you quickly learn what your purpose is right after as you go after a deer and begin a very long journey, some areas are tricky and a bit confusing but once you've walked around them time and time again you start to see things you didn't the first time. I'm sad that the last two abilities aren't needed to complete the game, because they would have been super helpful and cool to have while avoiding/running out the bad guys of the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a very relaxing cute 3D adventure where you play a... wolfcub...?What made the game fun for me was the environment and the interaction with the animals.Also the little quests like rescuing chicks was fun. The music in my opinion was fine. it didn't really stand out to me, but it gave the game this calm impression. Which was nice. I played this with a controller so I can't speak about the control usage with keyboard and mouse, but with a controler it was easy.What I didn't quite like was the search for jewels(?). The look of the game didn't make it inviting for me to go exploring, but this will depend on the player.Overall I would recommend to play the game if you want to play something chill and not heavy.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Quite liked this game, right up until the part where I didn't get my achievements for finishing it and some other collectibles I did get. If you're into games like the Ori series or mario 64 or enjoy exploring an open 3D world and solving some fun, not too hard puzzles in a relatively peaceful yet intruiging setting, then this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: A good 3d adventure game, especially for the price. It's a collectathon and some puzzles mixed in, with an emphasis of a platformer. The progression of the game has a nice feel and has you revisiting old locations to pick up items once you have learned new abilities later in the game. There is no combat in the game, just stealth to sneak past enemies but enemies are not too common. The gameplay is more about exploration.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Charming but vague.These words describe Fe perfectly, both its pros and cons.Along first 5 minutes of the game you might find yourself thinking to be playing something quite familiar. There's the clear reason for it: fairy vibes of  in here are very transparent. While taking, perhaps, the best part of its reference -- the visual and the setting -- devs at  kinda forgot to make the goals more comprehensible and the puzzles more involving and less repeatable.However, Fe manages to find its way to be distinguished in the best way -- both with the spirit and concepts of the game through its  (if you played it already, I hope you get the pun).This might be not the one you'd like to get back to once again after you finish it, but it's definitely worth trying at least once.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a atmospheric adventure game, and a good one at that. Though it is a game with elements of platforming and solving clues the game gives you, which could be annoying to some people. So it is advised that you approach it with that in mind.Overall it's charm is also it's flaws due to the fact that this is an adventure game, It's not a game that have focus on making gameplay satisfying. but rather has an approach of making the game with it's atmosphere as it's selling point. So if you are not sold on the atmosphere this game has, I think you'll dislike it. But if you do, I highly recommend playing this game. and better yet it's free with EA play. Which meant you can play this game for lower than it's normal price with EA play if you don't care about owning and playing this again in years later.I would not skip this one if you like game with heartwarming atmosphere with gorgeous visual. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most beautifull game, I have ever played. Highly recommendable because of its mysterious lore and easy but still tricky gameplay. There is a lot to find and explore in this wonderfull world full of magic creatures and plants. My only problems are, that there arent any dialogues so you kinda have to figure out yourself, what happend in this place and what the whole story of the forest is. Another negative point is, that there isnt a sequel yet, what I really hope for, because I absolutely love the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: At first you don't really know what's going on, but that only helps you get deeper into the role of our protagonist. He doesn't know what exactly is happening but wants to help all the animals that live in the forest with him.It's quite easy to understand the mechanics of the game, although the camera, if you play with mouse and keyboard, can drive you crazy.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very charming game. It's short if you zoom through it, but its very fun to just poke around and explore. Movement feels satisfying, and the mechanic of singing to the other animals is so unique and well done. I think its well worth the price. I liked the story, it took me two play-throughs to really "get", but I didn't mind, the first run was getting used to how the game works, and where everything is, the second was to just really absorb the story and find all the little hidden things. Overall I recommend it, its cute, unique, and well made.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't know anything about this game, so I wasn't sure what to expect, it looked like a chill game that looked very pretty, and it sure was, I really like the visual style, every location is beautiful, the gameplay is simple but fun, the language mechanic to interact with the nature fits the game very well. The game feels chill and relaxing to play, and there are many things to collect. Maybe it would've been good to include a way to track all the collectibles, you can track one, but the other 2 you have no help at all, and some are very hard to find.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: My initial gripe with this game is that there is no real explanation of how to play, what the purpose or the goal of the game is. I actually restarted the beginning section a few times to make sense of the main mechanic of the game singing in tune with the plants. Once I understood you need to move your mouse slowly to change the pitch to match, and once I started diving into the game to find what I can and can't sing and connect with, then and only then did everything sort of piece together and I really started enjoying it. I really like how you slowly build up your languages with different species and plants and you begin to access more abilities and ways to navigate around the world. It's a neat concept and once you get over the initial I'm not sure what I'm doing or what the game is about you begin to get immersed into this world.It's certainly one of the most unique indie games I've played, but I'm glad I did play it as I enjoyed it very much. Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty boring game, not much of a platformer, it's more like a stealth walking sim. You do unlock new "abilities" like in a metroidvania game, but there's not much to use them on, other than progressing trough the next story section they unlock and there's not much point in gathering the collectibles either. The graphics look nice on pictures but it's really straining on the eyes when actually playing it and since everything is so simplistic and same colored everywhere it's nigh impossible to tell where you are, making getting the collectibles even more of a chore, the barren map doesn't help much either.I also often got stuck on the jagged polygonal terrain which resuletd in me getting caught in stealth sections.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: very cool cant wait to beat it but it looks like maybe 6 to 7 hours of gameplay from what ive seen i love the puzzles and all the fun little and slightly... big creatures artwork top scores nice enemies and allies and it feels kind of free with a good sense of direction i highly reccomend this game to all
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Better than I thought it would be. The colorful nature settings are reminiscent of Meadow (the 2016 mmo), and the gameplay, while simple, is fun it if you want to explore the environments at your own pace. Fe's story is told entirely through images instead of text, and despite the fact that I didn't really understand what was going on, it still managed to leave an impact on me by the end through imagery and audio alone. The game's music is great throughout, but it becomes especially powerful in the last area, where it intensifies the closer you get to the finale.Fe has no combat, but instead has stealth sections that require sneaking around enemies in your path. There aren't too many of these compared to the platforming, so I would put Fe primarily in the 3d platformer genre, but one unique mechanic it does introduce is singing. Your cute little fox-like creature can sing to ask other animals for help using vocals that range from "nice and evenly pitched" to "cat gargling soap underwater". These sounds can become strange and annoying to listen to, but it's worth it when you successfully gather up an army of animal followers, or free a trapped creature and send it on its merry way.Overall, Fe had a kind of magical atmosphere to it that only got stronger for me the more I played. It's not a game for everyone, but if you like animal adventures with minimal dialogue like Meadow or Rain World, I would recommend checking Fe out when it's on sale. $20 might be too much considering how short it is (4-5 hours for a blind playthrough), but for the $5 I spent on it, the experience was 100% worth it. Fe does have some replayability in the form of collectibles, but even without those, I can easily see myself coming back for more replays.Edit: the final ability you get for collecting all the shards is very fun and worth getting to complete the post-gameEdit2: someone mentioned motion sickness - I get awful motion sickness playing certain games, but this isn't one of them. It is something to pay attention to, but no, it isn't a guarantee with Fe
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ok, very short and starts very slowly. Had I not known how short it was short I probably wouldn't of continued to play it, I am glad I did though, once the game gets going and you become accustomed to the platforming using the abilities you gain, it is rather fun and relaxing. At a surface level the story is up to you to decide what you want from it, there is no verbal or written dialog, you play as a small animal in a small open world that has been taken over by evil creatures, in order to gain control of the world back you have to sneak around, completing small gathering and platforming puzzles. I wont spoil the way things unfold but its interesting enough if you pay attention. Due to the lack of dialog at times you will be wondering where to go, you are guided by a glowing bird and there is a world map vaguely showing you where you should go next. The real draw here (no pun intended) is the art style, its rather unique and beautiful along with a great sound track, although the singing the animals do is rather annoying and fairly constant as its is how you control your abilities, which is a shame. Overall the game is flawed but short, interesting and pretty enough to have play through.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the greatest game I've played. It was really sweet, calming, cute, funny and sad. Each of the soundtrack was amazing. I loved every bit of It including the storyline. I love the design and how the puzzles are created. However, the graphics got me slightly nauseous but nothing I can't deal with!Overall; 9/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: So I got this game with the ea play subscription and I like these type of small action adventure games so I gave it a try. The game turned out to be pretty good actually. It has a really cool and intresting story and the graphics are cool and different than other games. Also the music is so freaking good. Seriously this game could have easily gotten an award for its music. I don't know if I would have gave 20$ for this game as it is really small. The story is about 6-7 hours and I played around 11 hours in order to get all the achievements. But it is definetly worth playing. I would recommend buying ea play and playing it through there.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played just below an hour of this game. It's beautiful, that's for sure, and takes after classic platformers sans the double jump. Its downfall comes in its art direction and lack of meaningful UI. When everything is beautiful nothing is a clear way forward. In the beginning, you're supposed to follow a deer, but the deer remains the same purple as the forest around you, not indicating it as any point of interest. For a long-time game player you will automatically follow it because its the only thing moving. For a new game player without that instinct this will likely be an impossible task and the player will just wander as soon as the deer is out of sight (and it was a lot). Then, even AS a long-time game player, I found myself constantly going for glowing balls of yellow thinking they were collectibles of some kind. They're just flowers with a middle that's brighter and higher contrast than their stems, making them LOOK like points of interest, and I doubt they intended that. Then, in the cases where they actually show you the controls (as they do this sparsely, not at the beginning), some of the buttons are unclear. When they wanted you to press tab they didn't show the tab button, they showed a vague button somewhat of it's shape, and there are several buttons on a keyboard that look that way.Those are mostly nitpicks and could be fixed with a more senior art game designer. The game itself is still very pretty, though I get the feeling I've seen it all before with better, more spiffied up indie titles, like Journey and Abzu. But it's still a solid little platformer that clearly had love put into it. Give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: I look at this game and wonder why it hasn't done very well. I'd say it's a masterpiece of a game. Everything from the gameplay to the character design to the music is absolutely beautiful. In all honesty, this is my happy place.I first played this game on Xbox. I loved it then, and I love it now. I picked it up on sale.Some people might complain about the art style. I happen to love the minimalistic atmosphere the game has, combined with its surreal aspect.It's a pity that this game has been ignored for so long. Two years, and it only has a couple hundred reviews. If this game had the same sort of advertising that a triple A game had, this game would be one people would talk about.Do I recommend this game? absolutely from the bottom of my heart.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: This game has super graphics and beautiful background music. For everyone who likes easy puzzles while enjoying good melodies this game is the perfect choice.  Unfortunately some puzzles can be shortened much too easily by simply climbing up and down. There is a story but you have to search every corner of the game to understand it. But all creatures are cute, the controls are very comfortable and it's worth playing the game if you have enough time to enjoy it. The story is also short, you can play it for 7 hours and as I said before, take the time to sit back and enjoy the graphics, music and cute animals.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: I originally found this game because I was looking for something relaxing to play after a long day. I was drawn in by this sense of wonder and its beautiful looks but somewhat unsure because of some reviews. Despite positive, many reviews pointed out that it doesn't really tell you what to do and that it can be somewhat janky, however I did not find this to be the case at all. The game does gives you the basics, points you in a general direction and its pretty intuitive once you know what you can do. I actually like that it isn't very direct, this way you can explore more (and get lost more) and actually have to pay some attention to what is happening. Truth is, if you dont pay attention, you'll miss out on so much of the story because there's no dialogue, its entirely depicted in visuals and sounds.Overall, the game is gorgeous, the soundtrack is lovely and the gameplay is smooth. It's exactly what I was looking for and I'm very glad I took a chance.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: Fe is a very beautifully styled puzzle game with calm cute elements, a lot of blooming light colours in dark environments and a relaxing atmosphere if you are ok to just wander in a park, listen to the hum, go mushroom hunting all the while trying to figure what the game is on about. Maybe the hart you chase knows. However the big downside is the Origin install, account setup etc from EA. Origin has a notorious habit for running poorly and if they could decouple Fe, a unity game from Origin that might actually make the first 30 min playable (rather than buggy Origin-ness) followed by finally being able to play the game eventually.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't the type of game I usually look for, or play. It was however a nice break from the fps / mmo / action games I usually lean to. The art and music in Fe are amazing. You play a little singing foxdogthing and save a magical forest. Almost everything in Fe seemed very original and stands out from other games that are in this genre... whatever that is anyway. An adventure game? Pretty cool, worth it for sure if you catch it on a good sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: This isn't a game. It's a . Everything in it - the music, the art style, the creatures - is gorgeous. Despite lacking any dialogue, I knew how every creature felt or what their intentions were. I always instinctively knew what to do and how things worked. I could just relax and immerse myself into this world, and everything made sense.
_childDocuments_.name: Fe

_childDocuments_.review: In Fe, players are enchanted by the natural surroundings as they uncover secrets, complete side quests, and meet the mystical creatures of the forest. Players climb, glide and dig as they voyage through the open experience meeting, interacting and rescuing plants and animals from the Silent Ones, the machine antagonists that are threatening the forest. Through unparalleled freedom of exploration in a world full of discoveries to uncover, players become Fe and never want to leave. [Electronic Arts]

name: Sea of Solitude
detailed_description: When humans get too lonely, they turn into monsters… Sea of Solitude takes you on a personal journey of a young woman’s loneliness. Set sail across a beautiful and evolving world where nothing is quite what it seems. Meet fantastical creatures and monsters, learn their stories, and solve challenges. Explore a flooded city by boat, on foot, or by swimming through the water itself. Dare to look what lies beneath the surface, in a haunting struggle of darkness and light, and discover what it truly means to be human. Key features An emotional journey — Sea of Solitude embarks players on a nuanced and intimate action-adventure, experienced through the mind of Kay, as she struggles to overcome her loneliness. Players must help Kay see below the surface and beyond, guiding her through her Sea of Solitude in this deeply touching tale of darkness and light. A metaphorical world — As her journey evolves, Kay’s dark and stormy environment begins to transform, with light and color shining into the world. Water levels rise and fall to reflect her own state of mind, transforming the flooded city landscape into new areas for the player to explore with new challenges to face. Face the monsters within — Encounter fantastical creatures, solve puzzles, and rid the world of tainted memories. Meet a variety of beautiful and terrifying monsters, each with their own struggles of loneliness to tell. Through confronting these monsters, Kay will not only learn more about them, but also herself and what it means to be human. An EA Original — EA Originals helps shine a light on some of the most passionate, independent, and talented game studios across the globe. Discover innovative and unforgettable gaming experiences from highly creative game makers who love to enchant and inspire.

_childDocuments_.review: Short Story (like 5 hours when you try to get all Collectables/ Achievements)But nice Atmosphere and unique GraphicsHow much Lonelyness & Emptyness can a person resist. How many problems like a younger Brother bullied, a Workaholic Dad that things Money is more value than Time with Family or a Mother that has no other Target to make others happy .Kay really get through alot in short time, nearly never gives up. Fights till the end of her powers. Cant win everything. In this hard times, think on the Persons, that has no one instead of the People that already have enough people around them. So no one feels lost & gets lost with a terrible Decision.I hope there will be a second Sea of Solitude someday. Hope you enjoy the Game like me.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a bunch of short little 5 hour games or under now that you can play on the EA 5 bucks a month deal.  This game and Unravel 1 and 2 etc.   If you pick up the monthly pass to play these games you will knock them out in a single session or a week at most and will still have 3 weeks left to download and play a bunch of other neat games.  Sea of Solitude is a once and done game for me so it is a perfect candidate for the monthly pass.  But we are not here to talk about whether the EA pass has value or not we are here to talk about this game.  So what can I tell you about it?  Unfortunately not a lot.  Spoilers.Did you like the game Submerged?  As in did you like very chilled exploration, no combat and a heartwarming story?  If yes then Sea of Solitude take a page or two from that game and does its own thing with it.  Do you like giant monsters and a lot of voiced dialogue with no lore to read?  Again, you might want to play this.____________+  beauty is not only skin deep and just on the surface.  This game is very beautiful to get lost in.  I really feel for the characters.  I loved the flooded city in the daytime where you can peer down through the crystal clear water to see the remains of trams, shops and hotels.  I was sucked in when darkness came and the seas were now filled with terror.+  price.  Played through the EA monthly pass, this game is amazing value.  I paid 12 bucks and got 5 hours out of it.  But I do like to take my time.  You might be able to crush this game in 3 or 4 hours, in which case the 20-odd bucks asking price is too much in my opinion.+  story.  I won't say anything about the story and I don't recommend you finding out anything about the story because that is really what you are paying for here.  Go in blind and begin your journey as I did....as a monster with huge red eyes, floating adrift in the ocean with amnesia.+  creepy.  The monsters are really well conceived and presented.  They are giant, overpowering and  carry their own weight.  I was always looking forward to seeing the monsters evolve and to imagine what was coming next.____________-  EA Origin.  I mean, come on.  It has Steam achievements.  It has Steam trading cards.  You can buy it right here on Steam.  It is not some kind of exclusive game.  So why the hell do I need to run it through Origin?  Dumb.-  angsty.  the story cranks the teenage angst up a little too high for my liking.  It borders on cringe at some points but overall I was really digging the story and let the overcooked parts slide.-  ending.  "Tickets ple----okay we're here." I really expected more closure or something bigger.  I guess that's just my own expectations' fault and not the game but they did seem to be pushing towards something and I feel like they just let it putter out towards the end.   - HARD TO PORT!  I MEAN STERN!   NO....GO BACK TO PORT....GAHHH, SCREW IT.  Just back up slowly and let the camera rotate into the optimal angle.  The boat controls are not great.-exploration training wheels.  There seems to be this big city to explore but it feels railroaded like a Mass Effect 1 building mission.  The game begins quite open, or at least seems that way and then becomes narrower and narrower as you progress.____________So Sea of Solitude has a lot going for it.  It dabbles in a lot of social and mental issues that affect us all and for the most part it does a really good job.  Its a very casual adventure game that some gamers might abhor but for those of us that don't want to git gud all the time will enjoy its soft pace and easy adventuring.

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to talk about this game without spoiling so be wary of that, I'd also recommend playing through this game with subtitles off and voice volume off, I'll explain shortly after a quick intro.You play as Kay, a 20 year old struggling with family and relationship issues, the game’s visuals are an expression of the ups and downs of her own and other peoples emotions  and the monsters manifested from her thoughts and the monster versions of her peers in their toxic states.For me, this game has some glaring issues, mainly to do with how it plays its metaphors and symbolism along with its sub-par script and voice acting. These two tend to go hand in hand in bringing the experience down. The game seems to struggle to know what it's aiming for and there seems to be conflict between creative aspect.The game has some moments where visual storytelling shines through and I really enjoyed these moments,  however Kay (and other characters) can't seem to shut up about stating the obvious,  the first 20 minutes of the game I was screaming at Kay to shut up to let me experience and infer rather than her saying what had just happened or not letting me figure out for myself.Even from the get-go if you fire a flare into a wall Kay states it cannot go through when you can clearly see it explodes on impact and doesn't go through. Flares being a guide to the next location or objective you need to go to. Also when interacting a light copy of herself to aim at a monster Kay is clearly screaming and it's hurting, when leaving the copy Kay states "that hurt so much" in the fasted, blandest delivery possible; not out of breath, not exhausted, no emphasis at all to just what happened.This is worsened since in some points of the game you need to listen to audio cues that are voice lines  which is infuriating since that (along with the fact that there are some long pauses that allow for dialogue) does make that recommendation of playing without any voice lines present a little harder but I believe the dialogue brings the experience down a lot.On top of this the voice acting isn't great. As stated prior some lines are delivered very poorly, especially in context to what's going on in-game. If it wasn't for the stating of the obvious annoyance I would recommend just playing with subtitles for context; but unfortunately, the mix of bad voice acting with the less than ideal script leaves dialogue feels fake and forced. It makes Kay come off as more annoying than relatable with her issues, since she just comes off as incomprehensible.I know I've just bashed this game but I still have a soft spot for it, the visual style is amazing, it really shines and overall I enjoyed the story and the way it was told. The mechanics and gameplay are very simple but pleasing, typically consisting of the red light green light system for a lot of interaction with monsters and minor puzzle-like aspects. There are moments where visual storytelling is used to a very admirable degree during the game, and if I just ignored how what I just discovered was repeated to me I was enjoying how I was learning about Kay's story and what everyone was going through.

_childDocuments_.review: EA is usually known for two things: microtransactions and more microtransactions. As a result, many gamers overlook their EA Original lineup, which features unique indie titles. One such is .It's always amazing to see developers find creative and unique ways of tackling themes surrounding mental health issues. Some succeed, some fail. Sadly,  falls in the latter camp. It fails for a couple of reasons. First, the . Instead of providing a more in-depth commentary on a particular issue, it opts for quantity over quality. As a result, it only skims over them and does a rather shallow take that boils down to  and . Another glaring issue is the lack of character growth and development for Kay, the game's protagonist. There's no significant change in her behaviour throughout the story. Doing things your way and claiming it's the correct way, from both your and the other persons perspective, comes off as arrogant. Also, apologizing doesn't magically erase the memory of your previous actions.Up next is the abysmal delivery of  moments. They are delivered through flying  orbs.  Use all the tools this medium offers and portray what you demand we visualize instead. This ties in with how the game "evokes" emotional response from you. Let's take a look at . The story does a great job of developing the bond between the Titan BT and its pilot, Cooper (You), as they try to stop the bad guys. I wasn't told - "Oh, Cooper and BT did this, so they are best bros". No. I was there, experiencing it all, which led to me genuinely caring for BT. So, what does  do? Does it:orIf you guessed B, a  will arrive at your location shortly. This is my biggest gripe with the game. How can a story-driven game get this essential part so wrong? I won't feel lonely, sad or depressed because you tell me. Make me feel that by playing your game. The sad part is, the first 2 minutes show a glimpse of this, but it's never again replicated in the entire game.And the final nail in the coffin - . I don't want to sound harsh, but Kay's voice actor, in particular, was awful. Her delivery was devoid of emotion, almost robotic. Simply put, RoboCop expresses more emotion than Kay.The majority of your time will be spent on foot, traversing the empty world, doing the same two puzzles over and over, with a rare fun boat or platforming section. There is also no incentive to explore off the beaten path. Nothing interesting lies in some dark corner of the map, just useless collectables that dont expand the story in any way. The platforming was surprisingly good but almost non-existent for whatever reason. Controls are responsive and precise. It wasn't complex, you can only jump and grab ledges, but it was still enjoyable. There is also no fall damage, so there is no need for caution during these rare platforming sections. I wish they created more platforming sections akin to the Chameleon one, where you aren't just going up/down a ladder or swimming to a new roof. While you cant die by fall damage, the game still has enemies that can kill Kay - ghosts and the mermaid. You encounter the mermaid early, and from that point on, anytime the sky is dark, she patrols the water. Even if out of sight, as soon as you get in the water, she comes gunning for you. The ghosts only show up during certain sections and boss battles. Kay can't hurt them, so you have to find something in the environment that can and activate it by firing a flare from your hand.Besides walking and light platforming, there are also puzzles for you to solve. They offer no challenge whatsoever. If you dont know where to go next, simply fire up a flare that shows you da wae. The biggest problem I had with the puzzles was their copy and paste design. There are two-three types of puzzles that repeat over and over. A few more unique puzzles would have made the gameplay much more enjoyable. As it is now, it gets monotonous rather quickly. The visuals are the reasons it caught my attention in the first place. The monsters design is excellent. They each represent certain issues, reflected by their design. I especially loved the mermaid. Those menacing glowing red eyes, fixed on you as she passes by, always gave me the chills. The soundtrack was ok, not something that stuck to memory, and I have no intention of relistening to any tracks from the OST. While I prefer a strong story over gameplay,  manages to fail at both. The personal story about mental issues doesn't offer anything beyond superficial comments. Coupled with bad dialogue and voice acting, monotonous and tedious puzzles, only boredom and disappointment in this sea await you.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude has a very deep and dark subject matter which explores mental illness well. It also addresses the horrible effects of bullying on young people in a realistic manner. The art style and graphics for this game are lovely, the lightning is great and the colours throughout the game were fantastic. The gameplay wasn't anything unique or special, though it did have some good moments. the story wasn't anything special either, although I can really appreciate the purpose behind the games narrative. The voice acting could be much better, and the emotions behind a lot of the characters/voices seemed very straightforward without too much depth. The game is also a little short, 2-4 hours for an average playthrough. The designs for the game, specifically the monsters, are amazing and there were a lot of moments where i felt really intimidated getting into dangerous situations with them. I feel there's not really anything too amazing that stands out about this game to make it innovative or unique, except it's subject matter and how it handles it, but i do feel that it's still a good indie game and should be experienced!

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude is a beautiful game about loneliness, about overcoming those feelings and learning when to let go. The story follows Kay, a young woman who finds herself turned into a monster, standing on a boat in the middle of a storm. As she tries to finds answers, she discovers this sea she finds herself in is inhabited by more monsters, each with their own problems and struggles. It is, above all, a story about overcoming loneliness, as I mentioned earlier.The game world is beautifully designed. What starts as a dark sea in a stormy night quickly reveals an entire underwater city, which you can explore as you progress through the story, and the water levels fall and rise. During the bright moments in the story, the city itself looks beautiful; the environments are very well design, not to mention the game's art style adds to the beauty of it. Of course, during the dark moments in the story, the city feels threatening. Overall, a fantastic design.Gameplay is very simple. Through most of the game you'll be navigating your boat, or traversing across the rooftops and streets of the city, swimming at times. There aren't many enemies, or combat encounters for that matter; Kay herself isn't a fighter, instead relying on light to guide and protect her. The most constant threat is the whale, a giant monster that lurks the water at dark, threatening to eat Kay if she reaches her. Personally, I like the fact that the game's gameplay is rather minimal, and I enjoyed the simplicity of exploring this abandoned city, listening to the monsters' stories.Overall, I can say I really enjoyed Sea of Solitude. It's not a very long game, yet it manages to provide a beautiful story in a beautiful world, so I recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a very interesting premise but falls flat taking full advantage of it. I'm over half way through the game, but now it feels like a chore. The game focuses on mental health, with an emphasis on "loneliness" but that is not expressed through gameplay, instead its only inferred to explain how "everyone has issues but has no one to talk to". as a result I feel the gameplay is lacking.It's repetitive, go from point A to point B and avoid monsters, its removed any tense feelings I had in avoiding monsters. Sometimes they change the way you have to approach an objective, but at that point it only becomes an annoyance. This is not a stealth or a puzzle game because you can't hide from the monsters and it's not a puzzle just timing when you should move or not.Design wise the monsters and world are very well made. They fit with the story and I did enjoy looking around the sea world. I think it's the biggest strong point of this game.The writing is cliche and the voice acting doesn't sound believable. As a result the dialogue in the game is pretty awkward. I'm distracted whenever someone talks just because it pulls me out of the atmosphere it's so good at setting.It's not a bad game, but it is mediocre. I respect its approach to mental health, but as a game it doesn't do enough to keep me wanting to play. If the focus on loneliness and mental health are all you need, then I would recommend it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Emotionally empty "deep" game about how everything will turn out fine if you just really, really listen to people's problems! I'm not sure if the main character was deliberately set up to be the most insufferably annoying protagonist I could imagine, or not, but either way, I honestly didn't feel anything throughout this "experience" besides general contempt for everybody involved.As somebody suffering from social anxiety and loneliness, I'd have thought I could relate to the themes in this game, but nope... it seems completely removed from reality. I think I started losing interest in the story pretty early on, during the "bullying" section... it's like somebody whose only idea of how reality works is based on Hollywood movies is trying to write a sob story. Pretty much sets the tone of the rest of the game, which is just replaying boring stereotype after boring stereotype without conveying anything resembling real human emotions or struggles.Overall, it feels like it comes close to setting the stage for a bunch of important life lessons and then steps two inches short of the conclusion to throw those lessons in the trash by magically fixing everything instead and making sure the main character learns nothing. *shrug*P.s. THIS IS AN EA ORIGIN GAME AND DOES NOT RUN NATIVELY. I only learned that after my refund period was over. You should absolutely not support this scummy company. It's also horribly broken on a technical level, it's a console game through and through, which wouldn't be so bad if the PC controller support actually worked. At least for me, it didn't recognize my controller.
