From that point on you are on the journey.I would say there were some unique takes on mental health struggles and it didn't feel generic, there were also two twists I didn't expect which I found enjoyable. One feature I felt it conveyed very well as a game is the fact that nobody is perfect, without saying those words once throughout the game.I Think it's a worthwhile experience to play through, although I don’t think it's worth twenty euro, it's simply too short, a much more reasonable price would be between the five to ten euro ballpark.So either get it on sale, or get it for free through EA Pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my play-through of it. It's a pretty simple game. TONS of symbolism used to get several messages across regarding mental health and lonelines. All in all a good interactive experience to show and not tell what it means when someone says "The only person who can help you is yourself. Accept all of you."Game-play is still a little buggy in some areas, but nothing game breaking. The game-play is very simplistic but tries to do what it can to prevent it from becoming too repetitive. If you've played a platformer or two before you could clear this game in under 4 hrs.The audio design isn't anything too amazing. It's above average and fully voice acted but could have been utilized more than it was to evoke emotion during key areas of the experience.The art is all phenomenal! Fantastic visual design throughout the entire experience. Symbolism and characters are all amazingly created and the animation is pretty decent! Created a fantastic world which really brought the whole experience together.This is where people may disagree with me as everyone handles loneliness differently. But I think the story is fantastic. I believe the purpose of the game is to express that loneliness comes in many different forms and was the creator's attempt at visualizing their experience with mental illness in a way which helped those who don't deal with mental illness regularly get an understanding of it, while hopefully reaching out to those who do experience loneliness and mental illness with a message. Based on the other reviews it seems like this game has been able to really help some people and become a turning point, which to me says it's an effective story. For those who disagree, look deeper into yourself and what the game is trying to tell you. If you still don't relate, I hope you can find another outlet!Found out they're planning on releasing a "director's cut" edition with a longer story that goes deeper into it so that might be neat. It also was a game that made me feel, which is rare. So that's cool!

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know why people are complaining about the voice acting--it's more than fine! I see people comparing it to RiME (check out my review for that game if you'd like), and I don't think I'd agree, other than the fact both games heavily use symbolism to convey their plot. I preferred this game. Whereas RiME paints a beautiful world it undercuts with the reveal at the ending, Sea of Solitude appropriately sets the "it's all symbolic" tone from the get go, which I preferred. The graphics are simple and beautiful, the water effects look great, even if they behave a little more like Jell-O than water. The plot was a typical dive into depression, but the way the game used the symbolic world to explore the thought processes and source of depression was incredibly well done.I picked it up for 7 bucks and let me say it was a steal at that price, even though it's only about 3-4 hours long (I played in offline a little bit for my run). Check this one out if it looks interesting, it IS interesting, and doesn't overstay its welcome. P.s. watch Lumps Plays on YouTube

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude offers a unique and moving experience that explores complex emotions through an atmospheric, beautifully crafted world. The game stands out for its art direction, with a surreal, flooded city that feels alive and deeply connected to the journey you’re taking. The world is constantly shifting, reflecting both light and dark, and invites you to explore while immersing you in its hauntingly beautiful scenery.The visuals and story-driven elements are where Sea of Solitude truly shine. The game feels like a journey of self-discovery, communicated through powerful visuals, colors, and sounds. It’s an experience that invites introspection and offers a sense of connection, making it more than just a typical adventure game.However, the camera controls are a bit clunky at times. Especially during faster or more confined moments, the camera can be difficult to manage, which disrupts the otherwise smooth flow. Thankfully, the game’s emotional depth and stunning environment are more than enough to keep you engaged and make the journey worthwhile.Rating: 8/10 – An emotional, beautifully crafted experience, even if the camera needs some refinement.

I think the voice acting was the main reason it was hard for me to get into the story as I personally think it was pretty bad, except for one character we meet at the end. As for the actual gameplay it feels very lacking. Many of the things felt repetitive and also kind of unnecessary. _childDocuments_.review: If you like Gris you might like this, too.I don't know how I got so many of these "basically a walking simulator art project that has some allegorical mumbo-jumbo about emotions" on my Steam wishlist. I've quickly discovered that they aren't really for me, though they seem to have a pretty enthusiastic audience. Even though they aren't really for me, I can sometimes see the appeal. Something like Gris has stunning artwork. Other times they do a great job of evoking the feels.But I struggle to find much good to say about Sea of Solitude. The graphics have some appeal but are hamstrung by the water effects feeling off and janky. And the whole thing is about a submerged city, so the water effects being off is a big negative. But the real problem is that voice acting just isn't up to the task. And it isn't helped by amateurish writing."Actually, the first time we came to this cafe was 9 months before you were born.""Mama!""Sometimes I forget you're only 12 years old."Just. So. Clunky.The entire section about bullying just falls flat. And, as I often find with these kinds of games, their attempts at being vague & obscure just mean I have no emotional connection to anyone. In a matter of minutes you are told, via clunky voice over exposition, that you have a brother and you didn't pay enough attention to notice he was being bullied.You come to a game like primarily for the feels and this one just doesn't deliver.

_childDocuments_.review: Somethings are very strong, while other things are just as bad. Wish it held back on holding our hands and focused even more on the beautiful environments and character design.I like how linear the game is and certain scenes are definitely quite strong, but there's a lot of corny writing and at times the sound design is downright unfinished.I did enjoy this though. It's just that there's a lot more potential and a ton more room for nuance (surface level metaphors =/= nuance).If you're interested, buy it! A lot of care was definitely put into this.

Some minor collectibles if you wanna 100%.Broken up into levels with enough auto saves to play in smaller chunks ( i play before work a bit each day)Forgiving platforming / challengesCreative character designs though a few tedious spots (the ghost girls  in wolf area are janky, short hopping while running makes you go faster)It comes in at 3 hours for me, buy it on sale if you're worried about the duration, but I was glad I got to experience this game. _childDocuments_.review: Nice little game with a graphic style that reminds of Journey or Sky Children of Light. The gameplay is simple and fluid. Story-wise, SAS shows the poison of human relationships, the nuclear family and bullying in a metaphorical and not so profound way. It's rare to see a female protagonist deal with such issues, but also not really surprising.  The lack of choices and the simple puzzles make this game to a little movie we walk through.

_childDocuments_.review: An awesome game with a moving story.  It's a bit mouse hungry which makes it hard to play windowed and put the window where you want it, and there was one puzzle early on that I had a hard time with because the solution involved moving the mouse to the left, which didn't appear to do anything.  I'm still really glad I bought this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of solitude is a prime example of video game artistry. This is the reason I am a gamer. Cheap thrills only go so far. SOS is intentionally an intimate and theraputic masterpiece. The black fur and blood orange eyes of Kay draw you into a relatable dilemma of struggle not to drown in a sea of solitude. With fresh, pseudo combat dynamics an immersive world to explore and emotion provoking writing, this game goes straight to the fav list easily. So good.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game originally on the Nintendo Switch, but I wanted to play it again on the PC because it's so good. I struggle with mental illness, so any game involving me attacking the demons of mental illness is always an automatic like for me. I find the main character and her struggles to be relatable. She is trying to navigate a treacherous and frightening world while trying to cling unto hope in the form of this girl that radiates light. The environments and soundtrack are both so beautiful. I love this game

_childDocuments_.review: A quick game that is very rough around the edges but if it's on a good sale I'd recommend it. I got it for £5 and feel like I got my money's worth, much more and I probably wouldn't. The story is nice but nothing groundbreaking, but there's just enough in it + some collectables to make you want to stick around. The main drawback is honestly the controls which are super clunky, particularly the camera control can be really bad at times which almost made me quit at the start. That said it's clear this is a labour of love that has some nice moments to endear you in a short experience that doesn't overstay it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: I gave it "thumbs up" but it's actually more of a "meh". It starts very promising and has some very beautiful scenes, but all in all it looks more like a very short final project of some students. The voice acting is mediocre at best, specifically for the main character (who doesn't totally sound like native speaker) and the dad. And well, the story is a bit too much cliché. Like everybody and his dog has mental issues here without any real reason for it. I was also confused by the mixture of German words on buildings with American elements (the family house etc.).What annoyed me most was the totally messed up steering of the boat and that looking around with the mouse was permanently overruled by some angle the game wanted to force on me. Also, there are quite a few somewhat annoying sequences where you need to avoid a monster or run from flying nightmare girls (or whatever).I needed less than 4h to finish this but when I tried to exit it the first time, the Escape key didn't respond. So I needed to shut down the process externally.So, yeah, I got in on sale and it wasn't horrible, actually I enjoyed it here and then. But it's definitely not something you would wholeheartedly recommend to absolutely everybody.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game! Heartfelt and relatable where it had me crying at the end without even consciously understanding why. I think this game just reflects the human condition and characterizes the confusion, anger, and despair that can result. The issues we face don't always make sense, in the moment or otherwise, and sometimes that is part of the process as well. Anyway, this was a quick play for me just a little over 4 hours. I will say I wish I would have taken to exploring earlier on rather than just following checkpoints. Not that I think not having collected everything detracted from the gameplay. Music was absolutely wonderful and coincided with the visuals very nicely.Not that this game needs a sequel because I think it ended nicely, but I could see a separate storyline following this style that I would love to see!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: A chain of unforeseen events can start when there's a lack of communication and understanding between one another and especially between members of the family, so start talking.This game delves deep into it and shows that how negatively it effects everyone connected to the incident directly or indirectly. There are other personal and social issues highlighted as well like bullying, mistrust, unchecked bottled up emotions, and so on.Takeaway: Keep your chemicals in check.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: Aside from this game being a bit buggy and visually glitchy, I found it to be a very moving and enjoyable game! Yes.. I might have adjusted the dialogue a bit (looks like it was translated?), and perhaps changed up the voice acting or removed it altogether. Overall the gameplay was very simple, stylistically it was enjoyable, and the messages surrounding mental health were obvious and well presented in a very artistic fashion. Does this have the best graphics? No.Is the combat challenging? Not really.Does it have a good story that anyone suffering from mental health issues can probably relate to? Absolutely. This is not a game to take seriously, but one to enjoy for retrospection. Just enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude left me with mixed feelings. The story is pretty much personal and familial drama. It's interesting and very adult oriented. Yet the game is somewhat childish and simple. It's like it is stuck between two worlds and not really that deep in terms of gaming. The graphics are pretty good and the animations are amazing. The sounds are great, especially the voices. Music is not bad either. It's a nice game with a good story but the gaming side is kind of conventional. I like the ending a lot.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good: 7.5/10. Pros: - good music and it really complements the atmosphere. - deep and compelling story. Very moving and honestly provides an in-person pov on how depression, suicide, breakups, divorce, etc. works and how it affects people all around you; not just yourself. - decent graphics. Wished there was a setting to play at higher fps instead of a constant 72. Maybe there was but I couldn't find it. - cute ass monsters (at the end)- colour usage as a motif and for symbolism was just *chefs kiss*Cons: - some small minor mechanical bugs. I found some movement issues when it came to the children. Perhaps that was just my controller... - voice acting is kinda sub-par. It's functional but it's not that amazing. Some parts sounded pretty static and not at all moving while other parts were mediocre at best. It's not even a "scary" game. There are some scenes that are somewhat a little scary but it's really not that scary. There aren't even really any jumpscares or creepy things chasing you (besides the whale, kids, imps). So yeah, if you're concerned about that, dw, it's not a horror game.

_childDocuments_.review: Two things before I get into my feelings about the game itself. The keyboard and mouse controls are hot garbo, if you play this game you need a controller or it's really not worth playing. You need origin if you want to play that. I don't like that I REQUIRE Origin to play it. But it's not a deal breaker for me.As for the content of the game itself. It has really good visuals, and it is a bit stressful as you try not to get one shot by the aquatic monster that is constantly taunting you. That being said, it's pretty easy, the only times I died was due to clunky controls, they're not awful, but if you die, it'll most likely be the controls at fault. I also felt that the 'message' is kinda, very heavy handed. I'm going to get into spoilers for each section after this, There are 12 chapters, and about four separate sections and the game itself will take you just under 3 hours. I beat the game but did not get all the trophies.The gameplay itself (USING A CONTROLLER) is fine, it's really simple there are basically two modes, the first one being in your boat, which I enjoyed driving it around, you just drive it around a few obstacles here and there, but it's fun. The platforming sections are okay, nothing to write home about really, you can jump and walk around, I feel like there should have been faster movement. Besides the jumping and moving you have a flare that you can fire, which is mostly used to tell you where to go. Then you get an interact button, or a 'look towards monster' to know where it is.Potential spoilers after this point.Chapter 1 is tutorial and introduction, chapter 2-4 follows your character learning about the issues Kay's brother had, that Kay ignored. Again the visuals were really good, and they fit the narrative very well. It's a bit silly how Kay treats her brother, but not completely unbelievable.Chapter 5-8 is about Kay's parents relationship, I wasn't a fan at first, again very heavy handed with pushing the messages it has to tell you, I was kind of rolling my eyes for a while, but at the end of the section during the boss fight, something about it made me change my feelings, while still heavy handed it kind of surprised me with how they decided to end the conflict between them.Chapter 9-10 sees you dealing with your boyfriend and relationship with, at first I was worried that he was just going to be an abusive jerk and Kay had to just see it, but I was glad that it didn't go that route, instead of him just being a scumbag he just needed to work on himself, and wants to not have to lean on Kay, I thought it was really sweet that he tells Kay to take care of herself at the end. She really just needed to let go. It's hard to me because I was happy he was willing to separate to work on himself, but it's also really hard for me to not want them to work it out together.Chapter 11-12 is about Kay working on herself, I liked it, especially the start of it when Kay feels isolated and alone. It ended okay, it's a decent message. I think this game would be an okay game for beginner gamers.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: This game is a great buy <$10 if you like story driven games. Expect only 3-5 hours of gameplay.Price: for the full $20 list price I would expect more that this game doesn’t have.  To start, start to finish with collectibles is 5 hours, without collectibles is around 3-3.5 hours.  The graphics and gameplay do not warrant $20.  Storyline: The concept I love.  The concept is based on mental illness within oneself and one’s family and friends.  The mental illnesses are dynamic between characters.  The flaw in the storyline is that you get to know the mental illnesses really well but with zero background on the characters so it comes off as shallow and rushed due to gameplay length and lack of character background/immersiveness.  An example is with the father/mother relationship. Throughout the length of the game the father is painted as a rather horrible person.  I do not believe this was the games intention but it comes off this way with only about 5 minutes of dialogue showing the mother’s issues with zero referencing back to it and maybe 1.75 hours showing the fathers issues. Graphics: The artistry that expresses the concept is amazing.  Not in a graphics quality way, just pure aesthetics.  The monsters are really the high note in the design and gameplay.  They are genuinely terrifying and expressive and are the most exciting parts of the game. Gameplay: the gameplay is rather uninteresting but keeps you seated to experience the story.  It is good for a story driven game.

There were a few things that really took me out of it, and one of those things is the voice acting. Not everyone sucked, but a lot of the time the line delivery was so flat it just made me laugh. Of course, this wouldn't have been much of a problem if the writing was good enough to make me ignore that little detail. Sadly, all I could think while playing it was how painfully unsubtle it was.For example, one chapter was about  I'm sure not everyone will have a bad experience with this game. I'd say the gameplay was pretty fun, if a bit easy. It's just a shame I couldn't get invested in the story no matter how hard I tried.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: is a deeply personal game, dealing with a common, but heavy topic. It’s touching and bare, with its symbolism clear but meaningful all the same. In some ways it feels as if you’re reading something you shouldn’t. It’s quite likely that the story is taken from the writer’s real life, but overall this only enhances the impact of the game. is about broken relationships with your loved ones and yourself. Differing expectations, a failure to communicate, unexpected interest – the game incorporates it all in a surprisingly cinematic and enjoyable package. The gameplay is simple and puzzles are minimal, but tight controls and some OK platforming are enough to hold interest as you explore the main character’s mistakes in her life and how she works past them, both for the betterment of others and eventually herself.At risk of spoilers, my favorite thing about the writing is how it avoids a savior complex. The story certainly could have led that way, but enough maturity is displayed that this attitude is seen to its eventual consequence. With this, I’d recommend . There are a number of games that deal with mental health and toxic relationships, but this presentation is polished and presented in a innovative mold.

Like. wow. also, whoever mixed the audio for this game did a great job.Game isnt going to be for everyone but if you enjoy single player story games like When The Darkness Comes, Limbo, or Journey, then maybe you'll enjoy it. Though I may advise to wait until it is on sale. Overall 7/10. Cute game to play on a lonely night in. It'll make you reflect.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: This was a great story game. This is a good one for anyone, whether you've had to deal with mental issues or not. Truly in my eyes, its not even just depression in its definition, I feel it explores the regular weak moments we all have, from not wanting to get out of bed, to violent bullying. Making us all a bit more aware. Kay thinks her life is great, until slowly, shes surrounded by water, a metaphor of course, and within and around it are monsters, helping Kay defeat them, you get attached. I cried at the end. I don't want to spoil anything, but basically if you can't help but enjoy a good story that puts a golf ball in your throat, and gets you super emotionally invested, this is your game. I was Kay, for 6.8 hours. Tips: You can make the seagulls move and fly after you shoo them. I'm sure most of you figured this out, but for the new players or anyone who missed it, there ya go. Also, I about cried when those damn other "me's" we're taking that piece away from me repeatedly and I could NOT get to the damn ice door to melt it in time, they were so fast. (when you get there you'll know, trying to not spoil) anyway, just keep jumping like a nut out of the bag, make sure you take that split second to adjust the camera when needed because you won't go as fast if your backwards, and also, stand in the center ready to run slightly to the right, they always stop in the same spot and i didn't realize that until I hit the one in front EVERY time. Like I said, I almost cried in futility, but gull dang it, I did it. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a mixed experience. It is a story message-driven game, with functional gameplay that is more interested in providing the means for the message and narrative rather than innovate or provide memorable gameplay.Without harming or hurting anyone, I could say that this could have been a visual novel and would have managed to deliver the message as good as the game does, without the gamification, but I also understand that without doing a compelling game, people won't pick it up to explore the story.Sea of Solitude tries to convey it is more a personal journey and is fitted for teenagers or young adults, who feel alone, anxious, and think too much about themselves instead of listening to the world around them. It also emphasizes the Resistance To Change, and that sometimes is better to let go and let people grow themselves instead of being in their face always.A good book to accompany the latter lesson is the War of Art -> Steven PressfieldThe game has short chapters which try to convey the following messages/lessons: Listening/Caring about Others, Letting Go, Letting People Evolve/Figure stuff for Themselves, It is not always about you, Change faces resistance and will hurt you and it comes from Within You, Trust yourself the people around you, and that you are never alone.I have to say that the clarity of the messages is sometimes minimized by the game itself and that sometimes the dialogue/or gameplay becomes so tedious that it ruins the next anchor point.I understood that the game had its dialogue rewritten and reinterpreted, so at least I didn't see it at its worst, but it's still lackluster sometimes.Sometimes the game tries to transmit too much information/lessons instead of keeping true to the chapter ideas.The gameplay is there, but it doesn't manage to offer anything substantial, any innovation, or anything new. There is a small open world in the initial chapters that only serves for the existence of people to collect seagulls and letters. Later chapters get diminished in quantity, and it really manages to convey the message a bit better. In fact, the game's last chapters are generally better being shorter and smaller than the bigger previous ones.Also, the game has repetitive and boring tasks, that have been extended for the dialogue to be more spaced out and feel loner. But in fact, for me, the spaced-out dialogue which requires doing the same task again, to receive another line of dialogue, breaks the heart of the game.Don't get me wrong it is not super tedious, and they are not long, but it is basically the same thing 3 or 4 times, without challenge or change, just relocations.I really believe that if shortened, condensed, the game would have managed to convey the message and make it even more approachable than what we got today.The gameplay has swimming, rowing, platforming elements, small and easy puzzles. It cannot be defined as a genre, and while I could compare it to the mixing of things in Brothers: A Tale of Two Souls, this game is way less than that. (could erase this comparison)Sea of Solitude is a mixed bag, the gameplay is just plain and boring, nothing to recommend, and could say that some of the character and art direction looks good, that is the best I could say, the story and message trying to present are great but not that good exposed or delivered but you can still identify them and learn something.I advise people to get the game on a sale, 4.99 E - 9,99 E (at max).- I recommend completing the game in 1 sitting or at least in the same day, or at worst one day after another - The game usually takes about 3 to 4 hours, and while it could be a bit much for a single sitting, to convey the message you need to be aware at what is happening in the game. The game sometimes is a bit too long, some moments are elongated without any positive effects to the game. The same dialogue could have been delivered without tedious repetitive moments- The game requires Origin... sorry- I recommend playing the game with a controller, preferably a rumble one- Don't overstress about the collectibles unless you are a Completionist, they don't offer any meaningful value- The game is fairly easy, so it shouldn't take you much effort to beat, as it is more focused on delivering the story- To improve the experience, play the game when you are calm and if possible at a time when you would not be interrupted. Try to be present in the game.- Preferable age period is older teenagers or young adults

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit this was actually quite scary at points, particularly around the beginning. As it went on, the horror factor transitions to the emotional side. I love how they explored themes of both interpersonal and self mental health. I love how it looks - the monsters' models especially were impressive and compelling. I love the sound design, music and all. Okay, some of the voice acting isn't particularly immersive, but just because they aren't native English speakers doesn't mean they should be immediately discounted. I thought it was still great for the most part.The game mechanics weren't particularly interesting, but did require at least some thought. It's not all just mindless running from A to B, and the environment is enjoyable to just exist in. The collectables definitely should have been looked at further, though. Their consistency throughout the game is terrible - whenever I would take time to explore would result in finding nothing in empty but traversable parts of the map. Having to watch the seagull fly away every time was a little much, especially as it doesn't reveal much more information from the different viewpoint. Also I don't appreciate the achievements that are to farm deaths in different ways.Cool game, though I'd probably want to get it at 50% off or more for its ~movie length. I would definitely recommend playing this if you pick up the EA play subscription at all (as I did).

_childDocuments_.review: It's more depressing knowing a team of people worked on this than the game itself. At the end of the day, someone thought this was ok to sell for money, and because of that it deserves to be shunned.This game is a rare gem in the worst way possible and is a perfect example of what not to do in game development. It shows how good games are really just a bunch of little things all layered on top of each other that make them truly special.If you've ever played Ico or The Last Guardian, this game is the furthest thing from those titles and I'm ashamed for even comparing them. I don't know what they were thinking putting voice acting into this when it's 90% of the content and all of it is bad. Just because you have a 'story' doesn't mean 3 hours of exposition and nothing for gameplay makes it worthwhile.Just a few standout reasons why this game is just bad:-Writing that makes fortune cookies look like Tolkien.-Embarrassing voice acting and robotic, unbelievable characters.-Collecting bottles and shooing seagulls for collectibles that add literally nothing wow!-Animations that often jank and feel rushed.-Footprints don't even match where your character is walking.-Game crashed during a cutscene which made it way funnier. This has actually been the only positive so far.I feel obligated to finish playing to see how much worse it gets. I truly have no idea how this game has an 87% Very Positive rating on Steam other than people having no standards.I will give some props to the level designer though for doing a good job of making environments that are at the very least not a complete slog.

_childDocuments_.review: If you have depression or anxiety, you SHOULD play Sea of Solitude. You play Kay, a young woman on the verge of transforming into one of the many monsters that haunts a flooded coastal town. Each monster represents either someone in Kay’s life or a portion of her psyche. Most of the adventure is spent boating around, following the objective marker, basic 3D platforming, and avoiding enemies. While this is happening, Kay will interact with the monsters and monologue about her experiences. In a lot of ways, Sea of Solitude is a walking simulator done right because there’s a constant sense of danger and dread, but you’re powerless to do anything about it. One of the best examples of this oppressive atmosphere is the setting itself. When Kay approaches a depressive episode, the colors fade, the sky turns black, the ocean turns rough and monsters swarm the waters. As you platform between rooftops, the water will occasionally come so high that the monsters swoop in on you if you can’t find high ground. It adds that extra dash of personality and challenge that could have easily been missed if they had the monsters patrol in circles without reason. The boss fights, on the other hand, are rough around the edges. There are three and they’re all some variation of run in circles until the dialogue finishes and the fight is over. Bear in mind, the writing, music, and visuals for these sequences is excellent, which makes up for what is otherwise a very simple 3D platformer. The allegories here are carefully chosen in design and environment, making for literary themes that are fascinating and easy to grasp. If I had to point to a weak point, it would be the voice acting. I do not mean the accents here. What I mean is that in a lot of cases Kay’s inflection doesn’t carry the right tone and urgency, even when the monsters talking to her do. This is especially noticeable with the dragon monster and the octopus monster whose parts are probably the storytelling highlight of the whole adventure. Sea of Solitude clocks in at just 3 hours, but the story it tells and the way it tells it kept me captivated for every single minute. If you or someone you know has ever struggled with depression, I would highly recommend playing Sea of Solitude.

_childDocuments_.review: There seems to be a very noticeable divide in the reviews for this game. By no means is Sea Of Solitude a perfect game and likewise, it's not a bad game at all.  There are a couple of things overall that tend to hinder the game that keeps me from enjoying the game more. First and foremost the voice acting is a bit lackluster but this is probably because of a noticeable language barrier. Many times I would notice very odd phrasing with some of the sentences that made me re-read some lines. This isn't a deal-breaker at all but it can be very noticeable at times. Compounded with very basic explanations of the story and character development. Kept me from becoming more invested in the main story but I can see the vision of the tale.  That being said I enjoyed the game overall quite a bit, to be honest. Now for everything that I believe the game does very well at. The first half was by far my favorite aspect of my experience. Due in part to gameplay, layout, and overall visuals/design, I felt was pretty damn on the mark. Between cruising through a submerged town, some basic puzzle-solving, and an easy to understand layout. Every aspect at the beginning of the game was well thought out and the pacing at least for me was perfect. However, once you're out of the town and onto the next part this starts to fall apart. Levels become more basic in their construction and it just feels like a lack of planning. By the end, this becomes a lot more evident as everything is being wrapped up. Onto something, I found to be a lot more interesting by far had to be the visuals. The metaphors and symbolism displayed I felt were on-point representations of the story and helped everything along. You can easily tell that the fish that follows you throughout is the depression that lingers no matter how much you help others. Each sub-story of the characters always had a unique representation without being uniform. Overall it makes for a decent experience with a run time of around 2.5 - 3 hrs. The most surprising aspect of the Sea Of Solitude was the publisher, EA. I'd like for EA to have more of these titles like we use to see. If they ever get back into supporting unique individual games we might see another Mirrors Edge, Dead Space, or Titan Fall. 68/100

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of games that explore facets of the human condition or psyche in interesting, thoughtful and engaging ways. Sea of Solitude accomplishes this in a manner that is true to the nature of emotions it evokes and situations that (for me at least) provoke thought about how people interact. It's not always a pleasant journey, a good bit of it can be uncomfortable but then such is life at times. This game however is a journey, a process that moves the player not just through situations for the sake of doing so but with an eye towards understanding them and resolving them and it's that conflict resolution aspect that brings things full circle and makes for a complete and compelling experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Players nowadays think that "Mental Health = Good Game". This isn't always the case. There are other mental health games, like  and , which feature good story telling and gameplay. , on the other hand, is weak on both aspects.Gameplay is mainly walking/sailing around. When you get lost, you throw a magical flare which flies towards your next objective. This objective features a magical doppelganger of the player character; you interact with this clone, who then fires a laser beam towards a big shadow monster, resulting in the opening of a new location. You explore this location, rinse and repeat. Sometimes you get chased by these monsters but that's all the tension  you're gonna get.Narration is pretty weak. Your character starts the game feeling lost and hopeless. The first two characters you meet, the shining doppelganger and the shadow monster, pretty much look exactly like you and tell you vague things like "I know who you are" and "You're worthless", and thus you know from the start that there is a mental health / identity crisis twist somewhere in the story.And that's about it. You walk around, touch objects in the environment, occasionally avoid monsters, and in the end 'learn to accept yourself'. This game lacks powerful, touching, cathartic moments to reinforce its message. And you don't feel like you EARN your game progress because the Flare Mechanic and environment highlights pretty much solve your problems for you.I only played this game because it is bundled with EA Play, and I thought, based on cover art, that this game will feature Cthulhu eldritch mythos, which deal with mental health way better than this game.

_childDocuments_.review: is about struggling with mental health, self-image, emotional maturity/growth, and how it affects those around you (family, relationships, and otherwise). It tackles these themes in an artistic fashion with consistent scenes that take your breath away, both through its visuals and score. While the topics it covers aren't necessarily novel, they are core to the human experience, and thus games like these can always help someone learn about themselves or grow. Overall a fun experience with the exception of the unexpected difficulty spike in Chapter  (though maybe it was just me since some online walkthroughs seemed to have no trouble with it). Definitely a must-play if you enjoy similar emotional experiences that tackle dark subject matter.

_childDocuments_.review: The style of the game looks very nice while also being somewhat unique.It helps very much that the level design is most times also creative and that the characters in the game also look very beautiful in the game style.The story which is probably the main selling point when deciding to play this game can cut very deep or not at all - it is a very specific story but I guess there are many that can at least partly empathize with it.In short and very generic the story is about a depressed girl (that has/had a boyfriend) with a younger sibling and with parents that also struggle with the question if they should split up.I could often "feel" what the girl and other characters were feeling even though it was sometimes presented a bit plain and quick but its a difficult topic and the game is very short.I never really felt that the game is trying to show/berate you how to handle such situations but rather show in a linear story how the girl is able coping with her feelings/situation.It is clear that because of the very specific setup this game will not appeal to the mainstream audience so I applaud the effort that still went into making this game.Things that are negative are that there were 2-3 times where I struggled a bit in where to go next (nothing major), there were 5-10 clearly visible visual glitches when switching between cutscene and the level and that the mouth flips for monster characters but also the main characters are often very off or none existing.It is a solid 2-3h game if you do not go achievement hunting and are interested in the topic (probably even have parallels to the girl yourself to be a bit invested in the story) so keep that in mind before paying a high price.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful and emotional, and sort of reminds me of a mature version of Inside Out (that Pixar cartoon) for teens and young adults. I would say though, I was told this game was about overcoming loneliness, which it is not, and is terribly named for that reason. It's not really about loneliness at all, other than maybe facing your emotional burdens on your own rather than relying on others to "fix" you. If you're looking to explore the depths of loneliness, especially as an adult during covid, this is not the game for you. If you're a teen or young adult looking for some self-reflection and a gorgeous artistic and emotional growth experience, you've found your game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude is a very emotional and heavy game. At first, I always searched for a reason not to play it because I felt like if it was not the right time for it. Today I did and I am very glad about it. Its story is somewhat beautiful, dark but also so realistic. Based on real-life issues and events. You will find yourself in some of those Events for that I can guarantee. Combined with its beautiful and smooth graphics your journey is full of joy for your eyes. The gameplay is easy and simple but also very flawless. It was clear to me that such a game won't last long, even with the collectibles in it, I only needed 3.6h but those were enough. But my honest opinion is that if you have not collected everything, I did not really feel like going back in the levels and collect them because it will sort of ruin the experience you will have and also the feelings you get in this game. I can recommend this to everyone who is out for some good and emotional story telling. But don't play this game if you feel sad or not well because this game is heavy.+ A story well done+ Stunning graphics+ Simple and smooth gameplay+ Emotional and realistic- Short play time but this is more than okay- Collectibles should not lure you back in to the levels
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game, I beat it within a bit less than 3 hours (and I died quite a bit). The length isn't important, though, as the story still maintains and carries itself beautifully. For those critiquing this game for being 'flat' or 'naive' I think it is important to note that holding your own view of depression or saying someone else's experiences of depression and loss as being the two descriptor words above is both calloused and cruel in their own ways. The game is both eloquent and somber in its own ways, acutely portraying both pain and the hardest lessons we have to learn: In the end, no matter how much we try to fix everyone else -- we can't sometimes and that's okay, alongside the lesson that in the end, the only person who can help you is yourself.  The music, scenery and imagery used to convey both pain and relief is amazing. This game was a truly heartwrenching and enjoyable trip.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: Visually very pretty and aesthetically appealing, the main reason why I bought it. The constant voice over leaves too little up to interpreting the surreal images and apart from the poor delivery, with voice actors that dont seem comfortable enough with the english language, at times much needed nuance is missing, making the struggles almost seem petty and the protagonist whiny. There's this weird air around not just criticism of passionate work but especially one around delicate topics like mental health. But neither in comparison nor on its own do i think its worth recommending for the emotional experience.I don't want to "punish" the emotional investment or bravery of the team to process and lay bare their experience, but rather the execution and maybe also why this had to be a video game and not an animated short. In the end I am here because i wanted to play a game

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games I've played all year.Great storytelling,interesting game mechanics,really solid platforming,amazing soundtrack and visuals.It's tackling some very delicate but nonetheless important topics, which makes this game all the more fascinating.All around a very good game for little money on sale. _childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude is an unusual game. I can't precisely describe what genre it is. It doesn't have the same feel as a platformer, though it has some platforming elements. I can't call it a horror game, despite that one level and the fact that most of the characters are monsters. The closest I can get is a psychological or philosophical game.The game didn't seem particularly difficult. I think it wouldn't be as good as sit is if it were. Instead, it tries to make you think and feel. The story of how a girl deals with her loneliness, and the relationships she has with those around her. It talks of how she didn't notice things while she was wrapped up in her world. It tells of how some people need to let go of things some times. And in the end, it talks of accepting yourself, flaws and ideas alike.I think because of this approach the game was beautiful in the end. A great deal of the time the game felt pretty dark. A great deal of the time, the game was dark. Themes of bullying, abuse, neglect, and loneliness pervade the entire game. But there are also themes of reconciliation, love, friendship and others as well to combat (sometimes literally) these dark themes.A great deal of the game is open to interpretation. Why is X this way? Why did Kay do Y? Why were some monsters portrayed differently? You get to decide that. In the end, this is a game well worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: Touching. Imo this is not about playing a random game for having fun. This is about story: how things, thoughts, relations and insights around depression evolve. Gameplay is not important, it just supports the visual language around the touching narration. I really liked it a lot but not in a fun way - it left me here thoughtful and kind of sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Developed by Jo-Mei Studios, Sea of Solitude is an adventure game set in the mind of the depressed protagonist Kay. Envisaging her loneliness as an endless sea flooding a city, you are to guide her through her memories, help her to piece together what happened to cause her to come here, why she's a monster and how she can regain her humanity. Along the way, you will meet different aspects of Kays personality and other family members, many of them also represented as shadowy-red-eyed monsters.Throughout your quest to piece together Kays memories and explore the sources of her guilt and depression, you will re-live the aspects of Kays past that led her here. From her feelings of guilt over her ignorance of her younger brothers suffering at the hands of bullies in school, her feelings of blame and confusion over her parents constant arguments and subsequent divorce and her sense of helplessness at the emotional isolation from her boyfriend, each of these is re-told as a voice over throughout the course of each sections particular challenge in order to get to the particular monster representing that family member.Her brother is depicted as a large bird, her father and mother as a fire-breathing chameleon and a vast Kraken respectively and her boyfriend as a thinly masked wolf these monsters are only initially portrayed as menacing. Over the course of the game, as Kay begin to piece things together, they are shown to not be monsters at all, just human.The main threats throughout the game is a sea monster, also shadowy and red-eyed to highlight its connection to Kay, who constantly torments her and a mop-haired giant who constantly blocks her way using shells and who also weighs in with its own psychological abuse. Again, over the course of the game, these will be revealed to have their own reasons for existing and acting they way they do.I'll just take a brief aside here to critique this as a game. I feel slightly uncomfortable doing so as it almost seems tacky and insulting to criticise the mechanics of a story that's a emotional and forthrightly personal as this one. As the review on Destructoid said perfectly on this "putting a score on this feels like being allowed to read a relatives diary only to give it a thumbs up or down". But thankfully the game, for the most part, is really well put together. Firstly the visuals are excellent. The hint of cell-shaded artwork along the wonderful water effects is contrasted brilliantly by the design of the monsters. They strike that perfect balance of menacing and vulnerable and it plays perfectly into their characterisation. The controls are simple and effective. They flow nicely and are never a hinderance to the gameplay. Some of the game physics can be quite janky such as when jumping into water, often Kay will fall through the first metre or so of water before the engine realises she's in water and starts her swimming. This can lead to a number of annoying deaths at the hands of the aforementioned sea monster. These occurrences are few and far between however and don't spoil the overall feeling or tone.The different section challenges can be onerous however. The primary aim of the sections is for Kay to absorb the bad and toxic memories into her orange backpack and this involves sometimes unlocking the memories by finding other glowing pieces of it or by eradicating any number of shadowy "ghosts" that will try to prevent you from accessing the memory. Some of these can go on for a bit and the number of fetch quests can get a little tedious. In particular I found the mask recovery sections to go on for a while and the whole concept of having to outrun the witches or they'll take the piece all the way back to the start was a source of some frustration. But, on the whole, these do not undermine the game or its message.And that message is a vital one. Through Kay we get to see her learning the various lessons her life has thought her and how she can use them to help become a better person. Through her brother she learns the value of listening and being there for someone. Through her parents she learns that not everything is her fault and  there are some things she can't control and through her boyfriend we see her past trauma come full circle as her struggles to keep a toxic relationship together consume her and she learns that there are some times when letting go is the only way forward. Ultimately, Sea of Solitude is the product of someone laying their struggles bare for others to see. It's an intensely personal story and its ability to grip you as a player depends purely on how you react to how the narrative is portrayed. If you're someone who can empathise then this game will reach you on so many levels. The game is careful to state that the solutions to Kays issues are specific to her and are not to be applied to others. I do think that one of the games core messages that when we are struggling, trusting and relying on others is the best way out, no matter how painful it may seem. It reminds me of the most poignant line from the excellent book The Boy, The Mole, The Fox and the Horse by Charlie Mackesy.The Boy asks the Horse "What's the bravest thing you've ever said?""Help" says the Horse.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Solitude is a third-person adventure game with some platforming, with simple yet very nice looking, colorfull graphics.You play as a girl that is going through a tough situation in her family, mainly her parents. The story is told through voices in mains characters heard, sort of flashbacks of previous conversations between her and her parents, little brother or even boyfriend. Its as straightforward as it gets, you play, keep going, you enter an area, listen to a talk between someone and move on.The game has some creepy parts especially at the start.You can also go out of your way to do certain things like scare away birds or collect messages in bottles, but its purely for achievements and it doesnt change the story in any way, shape or form.The negative things about this game can be the voice acting, its a double-edged sword, the writing feels a bit off but the voice actors did a good job. And then the camera, which is something you will fight a lot because it doesnt really like to cooperate.Overall, this game feels like a hidden gem, but maybe thats just me. Its a fun experience and it looks damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely one of the most beautifully designed and greatest story driven indie games I have ever played. The raw emotion derived from the art style, the soundtrack, and plot warranted a replay for me as well as forcing a couple of my friends to sit down and work their way through this three hour game. There is something emotionally derivative that everyone can take away from playing this game, and everyone SHOULD play this game. I wasn't expecting to feel such raw emotions when I picked this game up, but I feel lucky that I did, and it is a story that I will carry with me forever. I highly recommend playing through this game and then watching the story developer's TED talk on Youtube. It is both rewarding and illuminating.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the art style and the concept.Jo-Mei Games didn't choose a simple topic for their game, but it worked for me, even if it seems bumpy here and there and the story does not seem completely linked to the game mechanics.Unfortunately, the voices repeatedly threw me out of the gaming experience, not because they were inherently bad, but because they didn't fit the game and the characters for me. (But that also feels like whining at a high level.)But overall, it was a very good gaming experience for me. The sound was great and I kept stopping to admire the surroundings. I could concentrate on the story and didn't have to get frustrated over overcomplicated mechanics and quests. I will play it again.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty excited for this, but I do feel pretty let down. _childDocuments_.review: If you want a game the explores the concepts of mental health and personal growth, and can over look minor game composition issues, then I highly recommend purchasing if the game is on sale.I bought sea of solitude on a whim during a sale, mostly because I saw it during the EA E3 Press Show a few years back, I was interested at the time but never got it due to origin exclusivity. Don't expect ridiculously world changing game mechanics here, and don't trust the awful EA trailers making this game look like it's for edge lord emo kids because it's nothing like that. You play as a girl named Kay, trapped in a reality (most likely of her minds creation), and she is alone in the flooded ruins of a city. Whilst there are platform/adventure game elements, this game is  and focuses mostly on the journey of Kay through mental issues and her personal growth towards self-actualisation and positive changes toward her mental state.Pros:+ Narrative (though heavy handed at some points it's message shines through brightly)+ Visuals (Art design is beautiful, especially for monsters )+ Water (The Sea itself is like it's own character + World Design (Cons:+ Writing (The writing can be a tad iffy and unbelievable at some points, there was one moment where I audibly laughed )+ Voice acting (From the word go the voice acting was like being slapped around the face with a stinky fish though I was able to look past this as the narrative pulled me in more, but I still found it hard to place the voices with characters, especially that of Kay)+ Cutscenes (An extension of voice acting problems, maybe it's to do with translation but, Kays mouth and some of the mouths of the monsters did not move in sync with their dialogue and that hurt me for a game so narratively focused, I didn't expect masterwork but an attempt would have improved the hook)Keep in minds:+ Narrative Engagement (I feel like for someone who hasn't experienced mental health issues in the past, it may be potentially quite hard to engage properly with the story, so please keep this in mind)+ Gameplay (Nothing amazing, very basic platforming without much challenge which for me was fine for a small 3 hour title, but I have seen others complaining that it didn't interest them enough)+ Collectables (Two kinds of collectable objects: Bottles and Birds. Bottles are great and tie into the narrative of the world and Kays journey  Birds are fun to shout at and scare off, they always fly towards the next objective it seems, but don't really offer much reward.+Spooky Bois (There is a big spooky boi that wants you as a snack if you fall in the water, you have time to get out so just make sure timing is on point and you will be fine. Take note however, that if you don't like sharks then this thing may make you want to insta-quit and I wouldn't blame you, but you're missing out if you do)I hope this review can help anyone who is on the fence about this buy, and I definitely recommend a purchase of under £7 or your regional equivalent. It's a 3 hour journey that I don't regret investing in <3

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautifully crafted game that explains mental illness and toxic relationships that people can have with one another. It tackles depression well and the healing process that it takes to overcome or at least cope with it. I highly recommend playing it if you experience confusing emotions and have difficulty working through them or if you know someone else who experience this and wish to understand them more.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Solitude

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous and moving gaming experience. As you can see by my play time, this is by no means a long game, but it is a beautiful one. The animation and low difficulty (challenges are confined to monster evasion and some mild platforming) make it feel like a playable animated movie. In a word, this game is healing. From the visuals to the flowing music and emotional German-accented voice acting, this game really feels like a journey of self-discovery. Be warned though, it covers some heavy mental health grounds, so this isn't a walk in the park. Strongly recommended for fans of narrative art games.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's keep it short and simple.Well... (-): If you want something complicated and a real challenge, I guess you will be disappointed. It's also kinda short sadly... not regarding the seagulls and the bottles. (collectables)But (+): It's beautifully designed, and most definately a game that focuses on the story not complicated game mechanics. (Might be a - to some people)The voice actors did a good job too in my oppinion, although some might say otherwise.A few thoughts (-/+): The topics Sea of Solitude revolves around might not be for everyone. I'm pretty sure there are people out there who just plainly won't like it because of that. I for my part know some of these things quite well and I really appreciate the effort the developers put into this little gem to visualize some, let's say: not so nice, feelings, emotional states and situations one can find him/herself in. Maybe I'm a bit of a crybaby but some of the memories you collect really touched me and where kinda uncomfortable.All in all: I loved it. It's beautiful, the level and character design is quite neat and Kay is a nice main-character. It was touching as well so... for my part, I got what I was hoping for. Also I think for the price you can't go wrong if you know what to expect and if you are into more emotional and story-driven games.

_childDocuments_.review: We all have our inner demons and have struggled with something in our lives and that's what this game masterfully displays. There is at least one part of this game that anybody who plays it can relate too. For me personally Jack's part hit the closest to home. This game is an extremely correct and metaphorical display of what it's like to struggle with inner turmoil and yet try your hardest to fix it and to make everything okay. This game may not be very long (took me about 4.8 hours to beat it) but it's definitely worth every penny to me. A masterfully made game with extremely cool gameplay and a premise that not a lot of games touch upon, 10/10 excellently made.

_childDocuments_.review:
When humans get too lonely, they turn into monsters 

Sea of Solitude takes you on a personal journey of a young woman's loneliness. Set sail across a beautiful and evolving world, where nothing is quite what it seems. Meet fantastical creatures and monsters, learn their stories, and solve challenges. Explore a flooded city, either by boat, on foot, or by swimming through the water itself. Dare to look what lies beneath the surface, in a haunting struggle of darkness and light, and discover what it truly means to be human. 

KEY FEATURES 

- AN EMOTIONAL JOURNEY Sea of Solitude embarks players on a nuanced and intimate action-adventure, experienced through the mind of Kay, as she struggles to overcome her inner loneliness. Players must help Kay see below the surface and beyond, guiding her through her Sea of Solitude, in this deeply touching tale of darkness and light. 

- A METAPHORICAL WORLD As her journey evolves, Kay's dark and stormy environment begins to transform, with light and color shining into the world. Water levels rise and fall to reflect her own state of mind, transforming the flooded city landscape into new areas for the player to explore, with new challenges to face. 

- FACE THE MONSTERS WITHIN Encounter fantastical creatures, solve puzzles, and rid the world of tainted memories. Meet a variety of beautiful and terrifying monsters, each with their own struggles of loneliness to tell. Through confronting these monsters, Kay will not only learn more about them, but also herself, and what it means to be human.

name: Partisans 1941
detailed_description: A new approach to the stealth tactics genre: Partisans 1941 combines stealth, action, resource management and base-building elements. Take control of a group of Partisans resisting the German occupation Eastern Front during World War II. Plan and initiate combat your way. Use tactical pause, study the environment and choose the best position to set up an ambush. Build up your resistance camp hidden deep in the woods and find allies to join your cause. Form squads of unique Partisans and undertake diverse missions to undermine enemy forces and infrastructure, while securing resources desperately needed to sustain the resistance. Experience a dramatic and unique chapter of World War II and become a Red Army commander behind enemy lines. Features Fresh approach to the stealth tactics genre. A new way to play real time tactics - mix of combat, stealth, ambushes and a variety of special items to bring chaos to the enemy ranks. Choose your own way of completing each mission. Lead a squad of Partisans. Build a squad of your choice and level up your Partisans. Use your character’s strengths to find the right solution to different situations. Find and recruit new resistance members. Experience the life of a resistance group. In between missions you witness the routine of a Partisan’s life - develop your base, prepare for the next assignments, ensure you have the resources for the Partisan’s survival. Keep your troops motivated. A different perspective on WW II. Experience the story of fierce resistance against ruthless German occupation on the Eastern Front. See the story and motivation of different people joining the Partisan resistance, military as well as common folk. Background and Story As red army commander Alexey Zorin you escape a Nazi prison camp. Gather a Partisan squad from soldiers left behind enemy lines and locals. Live with your squad all the way from small sabotage missions to attacks on the occupational forces’ authority. Play a leading role in an operation initiated by Red Army staff quarters and conducted by all Partisan teams in the area: A strike on the German forces’ supply lines for the frontlines, with the goal of buying additional time for the defenders of Leningrad to prepare against the German attack.

_childDocuments_.review: I received an early review key from the developers. I love real-time strategy games like Commandos, Desperados, and Shadow Tactics (I played the first two during my childhood). [This game was played through Steam]If you like killing Nazis, playing as the resistance, using stealth and advanced planning to succeed against overwhelming odds, killing Nazis, real-time strategy, World War 2, and killing Nazis, then you will really enjoy this game.The aesthetics are great - there is a lot of detail in each level and every different weapon is visible on your Partisans. The combat effects are nice, especially when you set up several mines and tripwires before tossing a grenade to lure your enemies to their deaths. The voice acting is good - your Partisan group is large and you will interact with a number of NPCs throughout the game. I enjoyed the music and sound effects and felt they were an appropriate fit for pumping up the Soviet resistance during WWII. I particularly liked how you could hold ALT to view all interactable (usually loot) objects and enemies within your field of vision; you can also see inside buildings, which is great for setting up optimal breaches. You will use a keyboard and mouse to play - the controls are straightforward, but remember that right mouse button on enemies shows their field of view, and F1 toggles all of your Partisans (in case you sped through the tutorial and tooltips like me lol). There are three difficulties - the Hard setting removes in-game saving, prevents tactical mode from slowing down time, and adds the risk of Partisans bleeding out when they are knocked down and untreated - I strongly recommend playing on Normal first. I tried all three and found Easy and Normal to be the most enjoyable because planning ambushes in tactical mode was so satisfying, however, Hard forces you to adopt a more cautious playstyle, which I also found very exciting. The tutorial and tooltips are very helpful at getting you accustomed to the game. I would say the difficulty ranges from moderate to extreme depending on your experience with real-time strategies - stealth is definitely a preferred playstyle in this game, especially on harder difficulties; trying to clear a level Rambo-style was challenging even on Easy. You lead a team of Soviet Partisans resisting the German invasion by sabotaging tanks, bombing key bridges, and liberating local villages. Between missions you are presented with the overworld, where you can develop your base by constructing workshops (for homemade bombs and meds), food facilities (increase food-collecting activities), and other necessities. Members of your party can also be sent out on different operations, earning resources, experience and (occasionally) morale boosts (improve shooting accuracy and ability cooldown). Every “turn,” you will have to ensure you have enough food for your Partisans, however, I found this to be easily manageable with all the activities you can do. I strongly recommend you build the weapon workshop as soon as possible because the upgrades are extremely helpful (ex: silencer that reduces weapon noise radius). During the story missions, you will load into maps of varying sizes with a number of objectives. So far, I’ve only encountered one scenario that had a timed aspect. Stealth is definitely preferred because there are always many enemies in each level - and later ones have the possibility of reinforcements arriving if you trigger alarms. Each Partisan has unique skills - Commander Zorin (the main character) has a one-hit kill throwing knife (you can upgrade the range, but it is still very short), and Valentina has a sniper shot that can eliminate any enemy even when they are behind cover (limited uses per mission). Sanek has the most interesting ability because he can disguise himself and walk past enemies - later, he can even distract people by talking to them, averting their visual range so your other Partisans can sneak by. I personally enjoy taking Sanek and Valentina with me into all missions because of their drastically different playstyles. Pro tip: INVEST IN SANEK’S FENCE CLIMBING ABILITY. It pays off in future missions, trust me. Loot is king in this game. You will likely be doing a lot of inventory management, so consider picking the backpack (inventory capacity) upgrade if one of your Partisans has that available. There are tiers for the weapons, and most of the gold weapons I’ve found were behind high fences that you would not be able to reach without the associated skill. The higher tier weapons also have more room for weapon mods, so try to find these whenever you can.Combat can get very intense and careful planning is the key to success. You can switch to tactical mode (which slows down time in Easy and Normal difficulty) to queue simultaneous orders amongst your Partisans - a fun example of setting up ambushes involved me killing a Nazi with Zorin’s knife throw while Sanek walked past a group huddled around an explosive barrel in his disguise (so he could ignite it with a close-ranged shotgun blast) and two other squad members prepared to lob grenades. Speed and flanking is also very powerful in this game, so try to outmaneuver the enemy and purchase related skills (ex: take less damage while sprinting, increased sprint stamina). Traps and chokepoints/killzones work very well - arm a narrow space with trip mines and bottles (enemies will pick them up and investigate) or have a group chase you into a tight area where your Partisans are waiting behind cover (reduces damage taken) and watch them light everyone up. I’ve had a lot of fun with the game, however, I’ve noticed very minor quality of life features I think the devs can easily improve - specifically, the inventory management. To date, in order to compare weapon stats you need to right click the unequipped gun and select “to compare;” in other similar games, you would be able to see most stats by just hovering over each item. Continuing, to see more details about each piece of gear, you need to right click and select “information.” My issue with this current system is that the information boxes are extremely sensitive - if you move your mouse away too much it will disappear and you’ll have to click everything again. A second thing I noticed is that the enemy AI seems to occasionally change behavior if you load from the same spot - for example, I have a quicksave right before a Nazi investigates a dead body and runs into the bush I was hiding in. Sometimes, I will load the save and the enemy will already know where I am or a different Nazi will be alerted (I’ve tested this a lot on stream). For some, this may be refreshing because it makes the AI unpredictable; for others, they may not like this variance because they’d like for their strategies to be precise. I personally have no preference, and this would not be a problem on Hard difficulty since you cannot save in-game anyway. Overall, Partisans 1941 is extremely fun and I am happy with the inclusion of the overworld where you can construct different things and send your squad members on varying operations. If you like real-time strategies, challenging scenarios, stealth, and tactics, then you should definitely check out this game!Highly recommend!Cheers,DJSF For more reviews, .If you'd like to support me, please visit . Thank you for your consideration. Commandos, Desperados, Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game and it was quiet interesting experience. If you like Commandos, Desperados, etc.. you should buy it and give it a try.I believe that if devs release another game and fix the mentioned issues it could easily be a 9 or a 10.Pros:- Interesting setting and story- Variety of maps and objectives- Camp system (build buildings, go to missions for certain resources,etc..)- Hero system (skills, upgrades,etc..) - you also get to select which ones to bring into battle- Inventory system which allows you to equip whatever you want to suit your gameplay- More action than similar games (maybe that's not positive depending on point of view)Cons- Various small annoying issues/bugs that could have been easily fixed with some QoL fixes- Inventory system has some really annoying issues and the whole "extra" stuff you find it makes game really annoying to manage at times- Camp system although it's a nice addition compared to others, I think it could have bee really great. After you build the basic buildings there's really not much else you can do- Weapon upgrading ; again a nice system but could have been easily improved to be even more great and offer more customizations- Skill system; again a nice addition but many skills are similar to others - Moral mechanism; seemed like a nice idea but you tend to forget as you progress the game. Maybe if it could have been more complex e.g. with consequences on missions it would have been better.- You can select 3 heroes in each missions (with some exceptions) which imo is really bad, cause certain characters are left unplayed- Last mission (wayyy too easy and small for final one) -> also it's final mission you should have been able to select the whole squad!

Few things to be aware are: enemy AI sometime is just stupid, I had few enemies get stuck at a door, sometimes you will kill 1 enemy out of 3 patrolling area and remaining 2 don't seem to be bothered their friend went missing. UI issues when there is too many bodies on a floor. If you stack to many bodies in one area UI gets crazy and it's hard to pick up weapons or bodies. Save issues: sometimes save states glitch if you save a game while carrying a body this body will be dropped on floor on load which can lead to obvious problems if you don't notice. Occassionaly on load enemies enter search state for some reason and start looking for you it's very random as reloading same save works fine next time. Over all 7/10 good start into a stealth genre and I would buy thier next title for similar price I got this one if they release more hopefully with better polish.

_childDocuments_.review: Even if you are fan of the tactics genre, you may be disappointed with Partisans 1941. The mission quality is a mixed bag as they are not fully fixed to specific characters, rather than being crafted around their respective abilities (which you may not even fully unlock by the end). This means that the missions are open to more generic tactics gameplay, leading to a sense of repetition. Further to this, you can take characters on a mission only to realize afterwards they were a poor choice for the circumstances.Outside of the missions there is a basic partisan camp management system, which allows for a bit of a breather and character interactions to progress the story. While I like the idea, the system is only surface level, slowing down the experience as you collect and sort food and supplies. There is also a moral mechanic, but I completely forgot about it early on (as long as you do the available moral tasks and don't steal from the locals, you'll encounter virtually zero challenge with the mechanic).Overall I did enjoy my time with Partisans, but is does have numerous shortcoming which hinder the experience. Under-baked mechanics, AI bugs, UI usability issues, and general lack of polish make it hard to recommend over alternatives like Blades of the Shogun or Desperados III. Worth a try if you're itching for more tactics gameplay, just know that others have done it better.
