_childDocuments_.review: You take control of a group of Partisans (a military force formed to oppose control of an area by a foreign power) to fight against the occupying German forces during World War II.You start off alone but soon meet up with other resistance members. Each mission involves you planning a strategy to reach a certain location, usually by overcoming the enemy, but remember you are massively outgunned by the Germans, so instead of going in guns blazing, the main game involves stealth, patience and trying to set up an ambush.The first thing you will notice are the graphics, they are incredibly detailed, you also get a choice of language for the enemy, so they can speak in German or English depending on your preference, or if you want subtitles. This all adds to the realism of the game. Once you get past the looks you have to deal with the controls. I hated the control system. I admit I am a console gamer at heart, but I have also been playing computer games since the 1980s, so I do not fear a mouse and keyboard. I would hope in future they at the very least offer a simplified control system that is more user friendly. I also hope they have in place a better hints system and a better tutorial. The onscreen hints and suggestions just seem to blend into everything else on the screen and I found that it just didn't really help.Now once I got past the terrible control system, I then had to deal with the camera view, now maybe I didn't figure out how to make it automatically follow your main character, but as far as I can see you have to manually control the view as well, so while trying to plan out your next step you are forever trying to get the screen centred or facing the direction you want, and then instead of having a solid isometric view, the camera also can swing around, which in theory is a good thing as it allows you to see things better, but I found it just makes life harder. When playing a game I hate having to keep looking down at the controls. So I just found it frustrating and time wasting, when a much simpler camera view would just make life easier and the game more enjoyable.Once you get past these issues, the game itself is actually quite good, the stealth aspect is fun, whether it is sneaking up behind someone and putting them in a choke hold, or throwing a knife or shooting someone with a rifle, get it right and it all feels very good, get it wrong and luckily you can revert to a quick save and try again.I think if you are already a fan of these types of games on a PC then you will very much enjoy this, however if you are a console gamer like me, you will probably find the whole control system a bit of a nightmare.The GoodEverything looks great, and the game itself is a fun, if a bit overdone in the gaming market.The BadThe controls, the camera.SummaryThe game has a lot of potential, I expect the game will get constant improvements and hopefully if the game makers listen to the players, they can fix the issues I mentioned. If they ignore the complaints and just push the game to the niche market who already plays these types of games, then that would be a mistake.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game in the same style of Commandos or Desperados (or Shadow Tactics), albeit with simpler mechanics:* There is no concept of height, no towers, no high ground with better visibility* Enemies don't go looking for their suddenly missing comrades, they just keep patrolling their paths, even if you lure dogs away from three-party patrols and kill them, the patrols will just go about their business as if they never had a dog* Your partisans aren't as specialized as your characters in the other mentioned games are. Most skills are interchangeable with just a few being character-specific. Eventually I found myself using the same three partisans over and over as one can lure people out by whistling and one can then kill them quickly by throwing knives. All the other partisans and their skills are basically redundant.It also has A LOT of bugs. All of which I could work around:* Sometimes the camera gets locked in one place of the map. This happened to me during the prison mission when one partisan was still outside the compound. The camera would lock on them after another partisan triggered the cutscene inside and couldn't be moved. Only solution is to reload a savegame and move the partisan inside before triggering the cutscene.* Enemies will sometimes stop dead in their tracks and stop patrolling. Saving and reloading can fix this.* In some missions, you cannot lure people out of rooms as they won't find the door. They will just run into the wall next to the door and then return to their business. * Enemies can often see you through closed doors.* Sometimes enemies will randomly start searching for you with no apparent reason. This is especially frustrating when there are achievements that require you not to trigger alarms.* Several achievements seem to be broken. For example, I finished the game and thereby destroyed the train gun, yet didn't get the achievement. Same for multiple "finish mission without being found" and "don't trigger an alarm" achievements. I carefully watched not to do those things, yet never got the achievement. Also didn't get the one about completing the whole group nor the "kill three people with one landmine", despite doing that several times.* Often the roofs of buildings don't disappear when they should, making planning with people inside rooms difficult* Skill radiuses don't respect elevated territory or work inside rooms. Especially when luring people out of rooms, you need to see the radius of the whistle skill. It will show on the outside but not on the inside. Some things are a bit odd in terms of gameplay for a game in this genre:* Some missions require you to fend off waves of enemies. You don't know this in advance and hence cannot plan ahead (by choosing and equipping the right partisans for example). These situations just randomly happen and you're in luck if you brought enough mines along to deal with this quickly. Otherwise these situations are a total pain to deal with.* Between the missions there is some X-Com style base building and chore-running that you need to feed your partisans. This doesn't really add to the gameplay and quickly becomes tedious. Just as chores are. * For a game that considers saving and reloading part of its gameplay, loading takes a heck of a long time. * You cannot replay individual missions after finishing the game. If you don't create a single save per missions (which I didn't for most of the game as it wouldn't let me before the first hotfix), you cannot go back to them after the campaign is done.* It it sometimes extremely hard, if not impossible, to interact with something in the world. If you pile multiple corpes over another, interacting with one in particular becomes insanely finicky. Same for boxes and cabinets. Also it is close to impossible to plant mines or tripwires among corpses as the corpses apparently have higher interaction precedence. I still recommend the game to both lovers of the genre and newcomers. It's really fun to play, challenging but not unfair and tells a nice story that I enjoyed following. Most the bugs and quirks will surely be fixed soon and I can totally see myself come back to the game in a few months to play it again and see how it developed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun stealth real time tactics game with elements of base building, resource management, and character growth. What sets this game apart from others in the genre is its great usage of the historical setting. The characters are authentic to the time period and the story is believable given the premise of being partisan resistance fighters. Partisans 1941 successfully captures the grim and desperate atmosphere of the Eastern Front during World War II and showcases the barbaric nature of fascism.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set is 1941 in the Eastern Front and we control a group of partisans within the front.This is a game similar in style to Commandos, Desperados and Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun. If you like those games you are sure to like this one.Besides being similar to those, it brings in a number of novel concepts such as a sort of resource management to keep the partisan group afloat and morale high. Furthermore, the shooting in this game has mechanics slightly more refined than in the titles that were mentioned and the game is designed around the player frequently setting up ambushes and shooting down enemy patrols. There are a number of weapon types with different ranges and firing rates, but if you play on normal just about any bullet can be fatal or cause injury on your partisans. This leads to short and tense shootouts wherein distance to the target defines how likely you are to hit, and cover decreases the chances of being hit.This game also incorporates a skill system wherein each character has a number of skills they can get as they level up, but these are all different for each character. The characters each have specialisations, but there is slight intersection. This also means the levels are design to be beatable in multiple ways rather than being incredibly tight puzzles such as those found in Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3.I'm a fan of all these things, however, the game is a bit clunky in the controls and responsiveness of the menus. I've also heard reports of bugs and other issues. However, the developers are working on fixing these, and I personally have not experienced anything that'd bother me more than the old Commandos games, so I am greatly enjoying my experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Man, i love it when games force me to use stealth for a mission and have the enemies alert themselves of my presence 0.02 of a second before i executed them. As if that wasn't ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ enough, IT WAS THE LAST ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ENEMY OF THE MAP.WHY DO I HAVE TO BE STEALTHY AGAINST THE LAST ENEMY ON THE MAP???????Partisans is a commando-inspired RTS with elements of management of a russian insurgency in german-occupied USSR. What i said above is a good enough taste of what kind of "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!" moment you will experience playing this game. Sadly it is full of them. The game runs like absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ turd. No, really, my computer aint too nice or anything but the game looks like ♥♥♥♥ and it cant hit 30 FPS on the main menu. Its seriously strange.That being said i stil strongly recommend this game, i think its fantastic, i never intended to refund it even when i got frustrated with it and i plan to play it to completition.Before you decide to buy it or not, however, i believe that if you work on UI or UX design you -HAVE- to play this gameThis game is the PERFECT example of how NOT to design an UI. No, graphically its fine, it looks pretty, simple, and its functional, menus aren't hidden, there are nice audio cues for anything you click.The issue is the "interactive" part. "What weapon is that?" "What ammo is that?" "What's that item?" You think any logical rational human being would just let you hover the mouse above the icon, maybe if they were a bit mean they would make you leave the mouse there for a few seconds before the info menu would pop up. But no, you have to right click every item- No. You dont JUST have to right click on them, that would be too nice, you have to right click on them to open up the popup menu for the item and click on "information" to get even the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ nametag. If that doesn't sound annoying, similar weapons of different factions like the Kar98k and the Mosin nagant have an almost identical symbol (no, not identical, but close enough to mistake them) some bullet symbols for different calibers are the very ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ same, and having to click on "information" all the time just to see  WHAT THE ♥♥♥♥ did you just pick up gets annoying quickly.The game is FULL of weird awful UX design choices like that that just make the experience an absolute annoyance, even 20 years ago many games knew better than to do some of the things Partisans does. It also has some bugs here and there.You CANNOT drop items into the ground for some reason. Once you pick them up, if you want them out you MUST destroy this. You can, however, trade itemsbetween characters, but this still presents an issue; you see, characters have 2 weapon slots, and weapons are big and occupy a ton of space. If a character with an empty weapon slot has a full inventory, and another one with 2 weapon slots has the gun in his inventory, you end up in this retarded situation where you would love to re-organize the inventory of both characters, but you cant, since you cant drop items and you cant transfer items directly into the weapons slots, only inventory slots, you are screwed out of picking up more items OR you have to destroy them to move the weapon.My last complaint has to do with the hitbox detection for the mouse, i pity whoever has to click somewhere in a space between objects, or click on a crate next to a door, because you will have to play with the camera a fair bit just to click on what was obviously an open space for the game to recognize what you wanted to do.Is this the best commando-like game? No, i think that shadow tactics is a frankly better one, but if you still want the part where you ambush a bunch of nazis in a firefight, i dont know any game that does it better, and even with all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that you have to go through sometimes, i still think that the game is a blast.The game is also not getting updated anymore. _childDocuments_.review: Partisans 1941 at its best is a fun, challenging tactics game in a unique setting, but at its worst is a buggy, frustrating stealth game where the lack of polish outshines the game's pros. It's a game that doesn't quite realize its potential but still provides an entertaining experience. Unless you already know you like real-time tactics games, and really enjoy a WWII Eastern European setting, I'd wait to buy the game on sale, where it's definitely worth the price.-Systematically wiping out squads of enemies or preparing a makeshift defense to hold off waves of enemies with only 3-4 characters or 'partisans' are very satisfying. Once you get the timing down, synchronizing your units' actions is rewarding.-The game gives a decent amount of tools to take on missions, while also implementing an inventory management system that makes you prioritize what's worth picking up between in-mission items and food/supplies that help feed your partisans, improve your base, and create make-shift items and weapon upgrades. You won't be able to pick up everything you find. I normally don't enjoy inventory management but I think it enhanced the game in this case.-Each partisan has customizable skills with their own strengths, deficiencies, and unique skills. Some units can more easily sneak around, some are better at stealthily eliminating enemies, and some units have special combat abilities for quickly wiping out squads. Partisans will have their shortcomings you can't change, so you'll want to assess which are best suited for stealthier versus combat-heavy missions. -As far as strategy games go, Partisans 1941 is relatively brief. I played on  and it was my first time playing this genre of tactics game, and it took me about 18-22 hours. More experienced players, or anyone playing on easy, will probably have a quicker play-through.-The voice-acting is immersive, none of which is in English. As a non-Russian speaker, I can't fully access the quality of the voice-acting, but it sounds authentic and believable, nothing ridiculous or over the top. It makes you feel like you're actually fighting on the Eastern Front.-The gameplay mostly strikes the right balance between stealth and combat. Actively engaging in shootouts will quickly deplete your characters' limited ammo until last few missions, but the game isn't afraid to throw overwhelming numbers against you to force careful planning and quick reactions to survive engagements. -The characters have just enough of a personality to feel human, with a few short dialogues between missions, but don't expect to become majorly attached to them.-There are a few opportunities for 'environmental' kills and events that spice-up missions. -The game does not whitewash the horrors of war inflicted upon civilians. The game won't show you anything especially graphic but you do feel the brutality of the occupation. While the plot is pretty barebones, theses moments provide decent story motivation for the player and characters (mostly).  -It feels like this game needed much more play-testing before launch, particularly for finding bugs. Too often characters will accidentally (not) pick-up bodies, inadvertently leave cover, or aim at target well outside their weapon's range. Plenty of times you think you're moving a group of units into bushes (which conceal your units) only for one of them to be standing outside the bushes and give away your position. Some character's abilities are bugged and alert your enemies when ordinarily you'd think it wouldn't. Other times a unit will take a terrible route to a destination (I don't think you can set waypoints). -The worst implementation issue is when loading a quick-save during a mission (which new players will likely be doing a lot). Instead of reloading everything as it was, enemies will instead be at the beginning of their patrol route. I've even seen enemies seemingly come back to life off a quick-save, or already start on alert. You can mitigate this partially by quick-saving before starting a careful maneuver, but its still an inconvenience in a game where precision is critical. -The cover system is very haphazard. Objects you'd think would serve as cover, like walls near open doorways, aren't. This can make some of the battles inside buildings unintentionally difficult without liberal use of grenades.-The fact I am experiencing these issues two years after the game's release means they aren't getting fixed. The player can learn to play around them, but proceed at your own peril.-The music is completely forgettable to nonexistent. It's not a dealbreaker but a strong score would have given the latter missions, particularly the finale, a bigger emotional punch. -The story itself doesn't feel like it ever escalates. I mentioned liking the characters and mature themes, but the way the story's portrayed, the characters never meaningfully develop past their couple character traits. There's no emotional conflict between the characters or over the story's events, and despite the crimes perpetrated against the civilian population, it feels like your partisans respond almost flatly and matter-of-factly, which feels out-of-place when the game literally shows pits full of corpses and children wondering where their parents are. This feels like a big missed opportunity even if strategy games don't always emphasis story and atmosphere.-The final mission, while a good test of the player's skill, ultimately falls flat. It's combat-centric and suffers the most from the half-implemented cover system, especially for indoor fights. The mission itself almost feels inconsequential. There's barely any build-up, no comments from the character's before or during the mission about how this is a turning point and decisive battle, and once the mission concludes the game just...ends. All you get is a letter with some game stills that says 'good job' and 'the Soviet people will always fight back'. Nothing about the German occupiers retreating, no in-game ramifications of your success, not even one-line character endings. The complete lack of a payoff makes the mission feel tacked on. The penultimate mission, which have well-established stakes from earlier missions, comes across as a more fitting end to the campaign. It's another aspect of the game that feels disappointing and underdeveloped.The game is on sale for six USD at the time of writing. At that price, the entertainment value is excellent. But for anyone on a tight budget or thinking of buying the game at full price, I'd recommend looking elsewhere or waiting for a sale. The game's shortcomings don't diminish the joy I felt when a carefully planned mission goes off smoothly, but the underdeveloped gameplay elements, story, and music leaves much to be desired that I hope is addressed in a sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played very few games which have earned the right to mention the Holocaust in their story. WW2 games are so often indulgent, desensitizing, gentrification of the most atrocious period of European history. Partisans 1941 is such a game that deals with its subject manner in a way that's tactful, honest, inglorious, and grim, thus following through on the seemingly insurmountable challenge of merely mentioning the Holocaust within the context of an action-entertainment product. If one gets invested in the story (not for everyone because it unfolds slowly within a very drab and solemn atmosphere), one finds that they grown sincerely dedicated to the tragic fate that the partisans find themselves in. You gain personal attachments to the characters; a little boy weilding a shotgun that's bigger than him, a busybody nurse who's compassion is a sacred blessing as well as lethal curse, a wandering assasin who's committed his life to satiating his bottomless thirst for bloody vengence, all these personalities and more become trusty companions, fulfilling unique roles and bearing unique and complex interpersonal burdons. This dark and haunting atmosphere is not for everyone. Some people will be put to sleep by it. As for myself, a huge history buff, this game scratches a kind of itch which most other WW2 games can't. The gameplay is truly engaging, immersive, and even hypnotic. When truly on a roll, the player may feel truly in touch witht that primal, hunting instinct. Looking at a map full of 80 nazis then, an hour later, seeing a graveyard full of 80 dead nazis, knowing that YOU made that happen with 3 Russians (one with a broken arm and having used around 200 rounds and a knife), you feel a sense of power that can't be accomplished through button mashing or spraying and praying. You have to get creative, take a breath and assess the situation, use your loot resourcefully, backtrack and try again, and otherwise engage in mentally engaging tactical executions. It isn't all just winding a clock though. Sometimes, timing things just right is what's needed to get out of a situation. That said, like sex, once things get going and the stealth gloves come off, that's when the real fun begins. The action is like nothing else. It is so damn exhilarating. Firefights may last only 1 minute or so. However, in that time frame, you're still required to make quick and decisive decisions. The character animations as they duck in cover, change stances to reload, and sprint across firing lanes heightens the stakes and offers a sight for the player to behold. This cycle of silence and caution which suddenly explodes into raw, unhinged fun violence is extremely rewarding. Even more rewarding when your play unfolds perfectly and you can just sit back and enjoy as the Nazis hit the floor. What looked like 15 nazis initially turning into 15 dead ones in 5 seconds as the smoke clears is like no feeling you can get from and RTS or sniper elite. That said, There is a massive issue with bugs in this game. It is severe. So severe that one may lose or need to restart missions simply due to bugs. Bugs are usually just annoyances, but in a STEALTH game that requires precision at its core is irredeemable and unacceptable. The game takes an EXTRAORDINARY amount of patience to play. Add bugs to that and you can imagine why this game will not appeal to 90%  of players.

_childDocuments_.review: * Graphics look pretty good and fitting, despite simple style. If anything, palette's a bit too brownish.* Sounds and music are nice. * Basebuilding/filler part is a nice breather between long-ish missions. Campfire stories give characters some much-needed personality, too.* Missions are tight, yet challenging. Not overly long like with other games in this genre.* I do like the setting and even story. Russian villagers, partisans and their struggle against nazis and collaborationists is a welcome fresh breeze in game industry.* A possiblity to sometimes solve a problem with guns reduces fatigue and boredom such games usually cause.* Not too many nasty mission objectives with timer or curveballs. Hate when games do this; you think you've won, and now defend against a tank or something. Few tricker missions exist, but it's not too bad. * Pacing feels about right* Characters sound too much like politruks giving speech. While it's probably accurate due setting, still reads too much like a marxist propaganda novel. I'd rather see Morozov get drunk and into fight or something, for a change. I don't think anyone's proper and moral communist after having just cut throats of 30+ enemy soldiers.* If you're doing English voiceover for a slav-setting game, don't employ . The  brit accent sounds totally out of place. * UI is absolute garbage, especially anything related to inventory management. Even simplest of things, like hover-tooltips or "replace inventory item with that's on the dead soldier" or auto-stacking ammo and tools doesn't exist. It's needlessly annoying and stupid.Entire inventory system does what I hate most about games; . It's not a challenge, not a puzzle, not important to the plot or setting, not anything interesting. Just a stupid, complex chore that this game doesn't need. Why do I have to spend tens of minutes managing broken gun parts and tobacco leaves in inventories? Why can't game just say "you picked up some useful stuff, laid it aside and took it back to camp after the mission". I don't need to actually carry all this trash around, is this a homeless simulator or what?* Commandos-style games have usually a kill loop for every character. Throw cigarettes, wait, throw knife. Lay trap, play flute, wait. And so forth. But it doesn't seem to exist here  until you hire Morozov. You can't  bottles for some weird reason, and bottles disappear if enemy gets to them, you have to manually count and collect rocks, this is all so needlessly complicated and useless, why do this? Morozov is only character with (almost) reliable kill loop, so you'll be using him until the end of the game. In other words, characters could use more variety and actual design. At least Sanek can kill knocked-out guards. If that also didn't exist, I'd be quite bad.* Most characters feel pointless. I tried, but couldn't find their quirks (a medic/sniper, a fast runner/acrobat, an... old man? etc) very fun (or useful). It was all Sanek and Morozov due their reliable, practical skills. * Gunplay feels badly implemented. I mean, there's gun skills and tons of guns, but using guns is so punishing  and random that it feels pointless. Almost like this game doesn't know what it wants to be. That said, stealth part is really good so I'm not sure if it's really a problem. I just don't use guns, unless game really forces me to (that dreaded village defense mission).Feels like there's more problems than good, but the good outweighs the bad. This genre needs more games like this and Partisans 1941 can stand proudly next to classics and modern takes of the genre. Totally worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game because it is not bad game as such , it just has too many interface issues and gets repetitive after a full play through.  Also sort of half-way through the game then the camp menus and the load game menu becomes laggy / less responsive.Game offers stealth approach to most tasks and is manageable to play most of the time - I played my (first) play through on easy.   But to try to be more interesting/challenging then the game will throw you 'curve balls' or suddenly at a few places become unreasonably difficult !   Also some things (or ways to do things) in some missions can only be done if you brought the character that can do that  (e.g. I had a mission where I could not pick up all loot.)The game has a lot of interface issues (that becomes apparent on a play through) where especially navigation on map with mouse becomes a pain, especially edge-scrolling and the fact that it's so utterly poorly defined where and where not that characters can go on the outskirts on the map !On camp/base then something on the head of one character frequently got in the way of clicking on other things , just as on map then trying to click the I(inventory) button down right would suddenly send you to a place on map rather than open inventory because one needs to make sure that the I lights up before clicking.Further more trying to get item back after use and picking up bodies in game can sometimes be a problem  which , in this type of game , sometimes is a major problem since so much depends on timing.Lastly , the whole inventory both for crew and in camp needs some work.  E.g. items do not auto-stack in crew inventory , meaning  that you will have to spend a lot of time stacking ammunition and other things to free space in inventory.  At camp inventory then ,IMO, things are not that greatly marked as to differentiate between the good the bad or the best of an item type  (e.g. burn outs , normal or good quality) , also modded items ought to be better marked.  In short then if you got a lot of items then it's often a pain to find the best items !Don't get me wrong , it's not a bad game as such there is just annoyances and it becomes repetitive because of the (in the end) rather limited options of doing  things - at least stealth wise..P.S.One will have to push the ALT key to be able to highlight enemies near.  Personally I wish that one could turn that on permanently as I would sit with the ALT key pushed most of the time !

_childDocuments_.review: Just approaching end of the campaign, but I have to say this game has been fantastic. Would recommend it to anyone that loves these kind of tactical action games with huge stealth elements to it.Starting from playable characters. All of them have their own little backstory that makes them interesting and not just some random Partisan that joined you. Also each of them has their own unique abilities that makes them more valuable in certain situations, thus allowing you to build team compositions for missions in the way you want (with few mission exceptions). If you want full stealth, well why not? it's very much possible. All out attack? sure, just take characters that focus on guns. In general gameplay is really good. As mentioned before, game gives you a lot of freedom to do missions in few different ways, and that really allows every character to shine. I've mostly focused on stealth myself since it's really fun, but you can do it in your own way. Gunplay is realistic in a way that weapon choice really matters depending on the situation, and distance is so so important. Smart positioning is also key. Enemies have quite a smart AI and won't be fooled too easily, so you have to play your actions nicely. They also make use of explosives and mines, just as you do, and have dogs to find you in hiding spots, which is a cool little detail.Between the missions you are at your base chilling and making plans about the future missions. Game always provides random dialogues there so you can learn a thing or two about characters and their story, as well about what's going on in Russian during those months. There's missions you co do while at base too, that reward you with resources, food and equipment. Nothing groundbreaking but gives you something to do at least.My main gripe with the game is the fact that in some situations, lack of keybinds shown, especially in base. So you have to use your mouse to navigate, select and then exit again. Kinda weird that but cause rest of the game is really good, I can look past it.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I recommend this game to people who love the genre. It have some interesting pivots from the typical tropes that I like, however they aren't always well implemented. For those wanting to get a first taste in the genre I'd recommend the much more polished games like Desperado III or Shadow Tactics.Pro's: *The non-stealth combat is actually fun and engaging. I honestly think there's a better game buried within focused on using their combat mechanics across larger and more expendable squads.*Killing lots of Nazi'sCon's: *The story and character building is as basic as it comes.  *Glitchy. It's frustrating when you have to completely change how you are fighting through a mission because enemies are stuck on doors or just flat out see through them.*It's not always clear when attacking an enemy squad with combat will result in the entire base falling on you or just an isolated skirmish. Why does getting caught put the entire base on alert and effectively end the mission but shooting at them doesn't?*The inventory and menu system needs a revamp badly. Highly frustrating at times, particularly in-between missions.Neutrals: *The overarching "meta game" of collecting resources and materials is a great idea, but it's implemented in a way that makes it mostly pointless filler. Upgrading weapons is nice, but feels pointless when some late-game key missions require stealth.*The skill system is a good idea, but ultimately not particularly impactful as there are key skills (weapon updates, abilities) and non-key skills like sprinting, backpack space, etc. And you really only level up enough to get the key skills.

_childDocuments_.review: This is just a very good isometric tactical/stealth game made with low/mid budget. It does not reinvent the genre, but is definitely a good contribution thereto. Definitely recommended for the fans. The enemies' AI is surprisingly credible, which provides an interesting challenge at least for a single playthrough. When stealth is not an option, the ensuing firefights are very fast, brutal and satisfying. It forces you to carefully plan and prepare for every engagement (if you can't win by stealth only), and will usually punish you for going in all guns blazing. But even if your plan carefully laid out somehow misfires, the positive outcome is still possible, which is oddly satisfying. Characters are decently written and voiced (for this kind of game) and feel actually perceivable. The "base management" mechanic is purely a placeholder, and feels unnecessary and superfluous. The game would barely lose anything without it.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who's thoroughly enjoyed similar games to this (Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, and Desperados III), I picked this up during the summer sale expecting an awesome experience, especially since I enjoyed the demo of this game back before the full game was released. However, in practice, the game feels much less satisfying than similar titles, with an uninspiring and boring story.  The first issue i have with the game is just how RANDOM it is. you only have a random chance to avoid hits when in cover, you have a random chance to hit enemies based on distance (you can even miss shots point blank if you're unlucky), you have a random chance to completely blow your cover when trying to stealth kill certain enemies if you don't have the skills for it. All of this randomness combined just made me feel like the only way I could properly complete a mission is if i save-scummed constantly. Second, not only is the story bland and uninteresting, but the characters are rather boring both in terms of personality and in terms of their skill sets. You simply throw them a gun they're a little bit better with and MAYBE they get a unique skill or two. As of the time I gave up on trying to enjoy this game, the only unique skills I had were the main character's throwing knife, and a child's abilities to disguise and to stun enemies with a slingshot (which was borderline useless, as you had to kill them before they woke up or your cover would be blown. Basically a worse throwing knife). Additionally, most missions I played forced me to stay completely undetected and/or never fire my weapons, which meant that the only way I could safely navigate the missions was by spamming the throwing knife and disguise abilities, while my third character sat there doing absolutely nothing the entire time as they were useless in terms of their skill set. What's the point of having so many weapon skills in the character's skill trees if you can't even use them most of the time? Overall, I would not recommend this game to anyone, as much better versions of this game exist already. TL;DR: Just play Shadow Tactics or Desperados III instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclaimer: I have not completed Partisans 1941I had high hopes for Partisans 1941 but was unfortunately disappointed by the playstyle encouraged by the game's mechanics. To put it simply the game requires a lot of trial and error, a lot of "save scumming" to progress through the levels. This makes the game quite slow to play as players will find that they'll have to repeatedly load previous saves due to information not conveyed effectively by the game.Another problem with Partisans is that the controls themselves are not really that ideal. It isn't always super clear which character you have selected and on numerous occasions I've accidentally moved a character that I thought I didn't have selected and had my cover blown. It's almost as if the game pushes you to use the number keys to select your units instead of with the mouse. There's also the fact that anytime one of your units are spotted the enemy instantly knows the positions of the rest of your units even when seperated.Furthermore I'm disappointed by the lack of small-scale limited missions. There's no opportunity to set up small, isolated ambushes, raids etc. Every mission is a large setpiece with a unique objective. While this is good as it means variety it also means that each level plays out the same, stealth kill every enemy before going loud for the last three opponents.

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY WANTED TO LIKE THIS GAME. I really, really wanted to like it. I wanted to like it so much that I'm still listing it as "recommended," because it's clear how much effort the developers put into it. Especially the artists and character designers. I do not regret my purchase, because this type of game is ambitious.But, in its current state, it just simply isn't a good game.The demo was fascinating, but I had hoped that the incoherent control scheme would have been ironed out by release. You left click some things, you right click other things. You click to place a mine but it doesn't work. You click to heal yourself but it doesn't work. You click to open a door but it doesn't open. Or it opens and it closes again. Or it opens, and you walk through it while it closes, but you're outside of it again.Maybe I just don't "get it," but the stealth mechanic doesn't actually work in practice. If you attempt to stealth kill someone from behind, even if they are nowhere near the other enemies, you receive full aggro. Hiding in things and popping out to ambush/flank enemies doesn't "feel" like it's working right. Aggro changes and my hidden characters usually get immediately taken down. Also, there's no point in hiding bodies (since nobody will find them, as they were all already alerted).The art in the game is excellent, but the visual settings are piss poor. The game is totally blurry. I had hoped the full game would come with any graphics settings, but... there is only one, and it makes the game look worse...?Finally, not being able to save at key points in missions, precisely at points the game is most likely to have bugs and fail to interpret commands correctly, often means losing the mission and becoming aggravated.It's one thing to "lose" when the player feels they could have done better. It makes the player want to try again. But, losing a mission because the player felt they were fighting the controls is a horrible thing. It's bad design.Partisans 1941 has a lot of good things going for it, though.* The voice acting. Also, nice touch on including an interpreter at the beginning of the game.* The story is really exciting. I want to play more (but don't want to deal with the controls).* The characters (the initial three Partisans, at least) are brilliant. A lot of love went into making them.* The environments. If only the game played as expected, these maps would have really been able to shine.* Tactical Mode is a great idea, and well-executed (though the fun is barred by bad gameplay).* The Base provides a good moment of respite between missions. I almost wish it was the whole game.Really wish I could like this game. I'll keep trying to swing at it and see if the story holds up all the way through. I can't imagine the gameplay changing drastically enough that it will hit the mark, but maybe the story will be memorable enough that I remember it a couple years from now, and remember how much potential it had.Again, kudos to the artists, the sound engineers and the writers. You'll get it next time.

I think there are so many quality of life additions that could be made. To name a few: an "autofill" option in camp rather than having to assign the same partisans to the same jobs every day. The placement of bottles is a bit buggy, sometimes you can place them from a small distance, other times your partisan has to move to the exact spot. Inventory management is a total mess, and gets quite frustrating... luckily if you are using knives you really don't need to loot anything to win the game. Oh yeah, and enemies are really really bad at using doors.I didn't encounter any game breaking bugs or issues.Overall its an enjoyable game - if a little tedious at times, and if you like the genre definitely worth playing. 6.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Partisans 1941 is a difficult, rewarding stealth game with very refreshing gameplay mechanics. You micromanage a small Guerrilla force, picking off guards with a wide variety of clever tools and tactics. The devs provide a plethora of methods for getting the job done, and exploring these in quick, coordinated attacks is half the fun. This is NOT a game where you can rip through a mission with brute force alone, surpassing stealth and ambushes. If your partisans are ever caught in the open, without cover, they get ripped to shreds immediately.  Gameplay is slow and deliberate and I love it. _childDocuments_.review: Great real time tactics/strategy/rpg game.Essentially the game is split into two. There's the main game: you command your partisans to sneak, stab, shoot, ambush, distract, bomb, explode, misdirect, etc. For this mission you (usually) pick up to 3 partisans (although the commander is always part of the battle, so really you only pick two). Each partisan is somewhat unique with unique skills, abilities, etc that you unlock with exp your team earns through kills, completing objectives, etc. Note: if any of your team mates are spotted then your entire team will shoot at whatever enemies are near them. So if one person is spotted, your team mates hiding in bushes but behind zero cover might accidentally get themselves naded/shot to death. That being said I loved playing this game, especially trying to find creative ways to unalive every single enemy on a map.on your team of partisans you get:You got the expert doctor who is also a sniper, the old man living in the woods with his shotguns and traps, the star athlete than can operate machine guns and sub machine guns very effectively, the kid who is also a master of disguise/ knocking people out, the sketchy commissar who stabs and uses enemies as human shields, etc.While on mission you also scavenge for supplies. Your ammo/ weapons are limited by what you find on the field of battle and on side missions at home base (more on that later) and every character has a limited backpack space (although for the most part with careful inventory management you can usually carry nearly everything you find on a battlefield).Between battles you manage your partisan camp. This mostly consists of selecting construction projects, assigning partisans to do household chores/gather food, etc. You can also send them on side missions. These side missions will have a description like "raid the truck convoy", "propaganda", etc. You have a likelihood of success on this missions written as a percentage and higher level partisans increase this percent. These side missions are automatically played out and usually reward you with ammo, supplies, explosives, higher tier guns, etc that you can then bring with you on missions.There's also a morale mechanic that's never fully explained in the tutorials:  if your team has a higher morale they do everything faster and better: abilities, shooting, etc. You gain morale from some specific side missions and you lose morale when you rob supplies from the local population (items that are in red when you scavenge). That being said, I really enjoyed playing the game. Its a neat concept, would be cool to see how they could improve upon it. I really wish they used this concept in other types of settings. Highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: I was naturally interested in , as real-time tactics games based on  are quite rare lately, especially when they offer a bit more unique view on skirmishes behind the enemy lines rather than on commanding the . In the end, it surprised me how I was thrilled to start a new mission each time, but my enthusiasm went a bit down due to constant performance issues and occasional minor bugs. As if we could not get a decently done game in all aspects lately. is in its full swing.  and their allies cut deep into the Soviet territory, on their quick way towards , and oil fields. However, the plot takes place behind the enemy lines, where commander  tries to form a partisan group. His goal is simple: sabotage Axis forces as much as possible, which would help his comrades on the battlefield. So, get your ushanka, papashka, and a bit of vodka because we will need them for some time.While a simple plot like this is enough for such a game, I would expect that the characters on which the game focuses would have more depth and that their relationships would develop during the campaign. Unfortunately, all the characters just fulfill the basic character tropes without bringing anything new to the table. There is an over-enthusiastic kid, a commander who gets along with everyone, a woman in the role of a caring medic, and so on. I found myself rolling my eyes a few times as I successfully predicted the dialogues’ outcome based on the characters’ personalities.Nevertheless, the plot still manages to provide a decent amount of motivation for finishing it, as Germans often take revenge on innocent civilians, so, as a good samaritan, I have to help these poor souls. An addition of which I am fond of is  forces, which consist of Russian turncoats, so you even have to fight your own kind. There are also a lot of collectables, presented by authentic newspaper, letters, and photos, from which you can learn a bit more about this conflict, which is something I appreciate a lot.Even though the plot is a mixed bag, the gameplay itself makes up for it. I finished the game’s campaign in about twenty-five hours, playing it rather stealthily with a few gunfights. If you are familiar with other games from this genre, such as , you will feel right at home. You have to plan your next steps carefully, or your beloved partisans will end up eating dirt. Enemies always outnumber you, so patience is the key to successful sabotage. Your main objectives are something you would expect: killing commanders, destroying Germans’ stuff, and so on. It is both hard and enjoyable to get to these targets.You always choose up to three partisans before each mission, allowing you to equip them with various weapons, grenades, mines, medical items, and other accessories. However, each partisan has a bit different and unique skills, so you want to give certain weapons, like shotguns, to someone who is suited for it. As I preferred a stealthy approach, I chose a partisan who can whistle to attract enemies, while the other one kills them with throwing knives. Various skills like these allow you to combine them in action, making the game very satisfying to play.Even though you can hide in bushes or behind obstacles, stealth is not always that easy. Sounds are as important as your visibility, and enemies can even hear the bodies which fall on the ground. The bodies also have to be hidden from their sights. Later on, there are often dogs that can sniff you out, and I had quite a lot of troubles with them. Also, Nazi officers control the numbers of their soldiers and can start an investigation even if only one is missing. The last thing that I found interesting about stealth is that not every partisan is capable of performing quick melee stealth kills. While a trained soldier does not have a problem with slicing enemies’ throats, a boy or female medic struggle with it. That does not make them useless, as they are useful in different situations.However, open combat might be inevitable at some point, and being careful during gunfights is even more important, as it might turn into a slaughterhouse within a few seconds. The AI tends to take cover a lot, tries to flank you, or use grenades to lure you out from cover. They also love to call for additional reinforcements, which is overwhelming for your tiny but brave group. Using firearms does not always lead to a massacre, as you can set up ambushes by spacing out your partisans and placing a few mines. And witnessing the successful outcome is just delightful to watch.Missions are not the game’s only content, as you have to manage a camp between them. You have to gather food and upgrade materials there, which is important for your crew’s survival and upgrading your equipment and the camp. There are also several tasks, which partisans do automatically. It reminds me of , although it is simpler, and the game’s main focus is still the missions, yet it is a great addition. Overall, I loved all the Partisans 1941’s gameplay aspects. Each mission is a bit harder, providing new challenges to overcome. It does not give you anything for free, but it is also fair.What  excels in is the atmosphere of the gritty Soviet lands, as it looks quite realistic with a bit of cartoony style in characters’ appearance. Despite being set in one region, it still manages to provide the environmental variety, from muddy villages and swamps to train stations and fortresses. It is not only the visuals, as all the sounds and soundtrack just absorbed me into this game.To make your experience even more immersive, I recommend switching to Russian voice acting, which you should do anyway because the English one is terrible. Germans are not affected by that, as they always speak in their native language. Even though I hate Nazis with passion, I find censoring svastika as a bit hypocritical decision, especially as the game shows other questionable symbols and hints on Nazi war crimes all the time.Unfortunately, the worst aspect of this game is its optimization. I tested the game with an , running at high settings, at , at  resolution. With such a framerate, it is sometimes a bit unpleasant to play, and four missions did not even go above 20 frames at all! I also encountered a few minor bugs, such as not being to loot items until finding the right camera angle. Admittedly, the developers work on fixes with passion, and several bugs got fixed during my playthrough. excels in its gameplay and atmosphere, which I enjoyed so much that I can overlook horrendous optimization. While I am giving it a positive rating, you should reconsider whether to wait with your purchase. Nevertheless, fans of the real-time tactics genre should definitely give it a try sooner or later.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has many technical issues:- way too long load times, even from an M.2 SSD (and you'll be reloading a lot)- quicksave doesn't always save the game, even though it says it does- after load the gamestate isn't always the same as it was when you saved it, eg. loot disappears, closed doors are open or vice versa etc.- steam achivements don't always trigger- vision cones don't work right- AI enemies change their routine when you get near them, even though they aren't "officially" aware of your  presence- the list goes on, there's just too much to list.With all that being said... it is a fun game, if you can get past the problems. The gameplay gets the tactical stealth formula right, every kill is satisfying, and the combat strikes a good balance between chaotic and tactical. The atmosphere is really nice, it does a good job of painting the eastern front of WW2 (or more like behind the front,) which is often sadly underrepresented in games. The characters are likeable if one-dimensional, and the story is predictable but still draws you in. The dialog is cheesy, with a professional but not great Enlish VO, but it all adds up to a consistent experience, that maybe mimics a Soviet propaganda movie, with the devilish Nazi villains and the overidealized heroic partisans.Conclusion: if you like Commandos-like games, interested in the eastern theater of WW2, AND they fix the bugs (I played on V1.01,) then it's worth a buy.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent game marred with issues. Partisans 1941 could have been the modern Commandos successor I've been waiting for, but no. It's far too unpolished and sloppily designed to earn that pedigree. I still enjoyed my time with the game, but it left me unsatisfied and just made me wanna play Commandos again.The presentation is top notch. I'll give it credit. It's a beautiful game. I'd say it's not as vibrant as Desperados 3, but it has higher graphical fidelity. The character models are all very detailed and recognizable from afar. The game's muted color scheme adds to the bleak tone. Levels are decently sized and detailed. Voice acting is meh. The English voices are especially mediocre. There's not much to say about the soundtrack either. It's forgettable, but fitting. Performance on the other hand is spotty at best. Numerous levels dip below 60 FPS into the 30s. This is not the worst the technical issues get.The gameplay is the highlight here. Every character has a unique ability to differentiate themselves from one another. However, they must be unlocked in a skill tree where most of the skills are the same between each character. The stealth gameplay will be familiar with anyone whose played Commandos or Desperados. You can hide bodies, pause with the space key, set traps, and die very quickly. The big difference here is that combat is an option. In a few sections, combat is inevitable and it's actually quite good. All characters' loadouts are customizable with a proper inventory system. Injuries can be sustained from combat which can affect overall accuracy or movement speed. There's a cover system as well. The way combat and stealth synergize here is great and my favorite aspect of the game. Utilizing stealth to whittle down enemy squads and setup advantageous positions for shootouts was fun. This is more than I can say for the camp management.For a game with so many playable characters, the fact that most missions only allow up to three characters to be brought and one of them is almost always Commander Zorin is a backwards design decision. Considering you don't know the objectives, map layout, and enemy types before entering the mission, you just end up using the same squad for every mission. I never used the old man even once outside of the mission where he's rescued. Camp management is boring and repetitive. Just keep the food in the positive and you'll never lose morale. I've never seen morale go down even once. I built every optional building long before the final mission and almost never crafted anything since you can get them from missions or base operations. The only resource I needed was XP.The story is virtually nonexisting. I can give you a general premise, but I could not recite the "plot" of Partisans. There are no memorable characters. None of them have any personality or catchy one liners. There's almost no villain. There's few cutscenes. To be honest, most of the missions were kinda forgettable. Most of them look the same since there all in some forest-y area with tons of bushes to hide in. The few instances of rainy levels and a snowy level were welcome changes of pace. I liked the prison break level as well. However, these levels have no story. They all just feel like video game levels with a brief description to give context and nothing more. The game's not even that hard. I didn't even realize I was playing the final mission when I started it and it was an awful mission. All that effort for a little speech and an abrupt fade to credits.And then there were bugs. This game still needs patches. I'm baffled at the level of unpolish here. Characters holding their knife as if it were a rifle. Enemies spotting me and attacking through walls. Characters running in a circle in place. Enemies getting alerted from spotting hidden bodies they were nowhere near to. One of my manual saves was mysteriously deleted. The game crached once on me. UI prompts would not work as they should. Body carrying animations would glitch. Assassination animations wouldn't play as they should. Characters wouldn't shoot through open doorways, but enemies would still shoot them back. There are a lot of bugs here.Commandos 2 was buggy as well, but it was also an extremely ambitious game with a lot of depth and imaginative design. A genuine diamond in the rough. Partisans 1941 feels like a familiar concept shoddily executed. I'm sorry, but this has nothing on the excellent design of Mimimi's brilliant trio of Shadow Tactics, Shadow Gambit, and the G.O.A.T., Desperados 3. It's a shame that the devs didn't give this game enough love to fix these issues. As it stands, it's one of the better titles in this niche sub-genre of Commandos-likes, but not one of the best. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: After wild west comeback in the form of the third Desperados, with which their creators followed up on the five-year-old battles in the early Japanese modern era, here we have battles on the fields of World War II again after many years. Not from Mimimi, but from Russian developers Alter Games, under whose baton we will fight on the Eastern Front in the shoes of Soviet partisans. Fighters who often lost everything and their only chance was to connect with colleagues with a similar cruel fate. Personally, I welcomed this thematic focus, which I took at least as a pleasant change after the battles in the western ranks.The plot of the game takes place mainly in the fall of 1941, when Nazi Germany has been conquering the Soviet Union for some time. Right at the beginning, you get to know the main character, who is Alexei Zorin. It is about a soldier whose commander was shot by the Nazis and placed in a concentration camp together with his other comrades. After a casual conversation with the Nazi guards, your hero is consigned to near-certain death by firing squad, but he wouldn't be a proper Soviet hero if he didn't run away from the gravedigger's shovel. After defeating the guard, you will subsequently escape from the concentration camp and the guerrilla campaign can begin. Soon after the escape, you meet two more partisans and find refuge in a makeshift camp somewhere in the dense Russian forests, from which you will send your partisans on missions. You will fight both in endlessly overgrown forests and in cities, fields, villages (often mercilessly burned by the Nazis), train stations, prisons, blowing up railway bridges, sabotaging enemy convoys and the like. As you progress through the story, the guerrillas in your ranks will increase. In the end, you will have a choice of perhaps ten characters, each of which is suitable for something different. Wounded men will take charge of submachine guns, shotguns, and light machine guns, while the weaker sex, on the other hand, will focus more on pistols, stunning and healing wounded comrades.The game takes the best of the Commandos series and Robin Hood: Legend of Sherwood. During your campaign, you will therefore primarily fulfill the main missions, but also take care of the activity outside of them in your camp. In it, you will be tasked mainly with procuring food and wood from the forest, as well as, just like in Sherwood Forest, making raids on enemies moving near your camp site. The reward for their successful completion will be looted resources or weapons. You will also be able to visit the local villagers and increase your morale and your battle reputation by your presence, speech and above all your actions. It will affect your overall performance on the battlefield, when with its highest level you will be fast, accurate, durable, and in the case of the lowest level of morale, completely helpless. You will also be able to build buildings in the camp that will increase your food production through, for example, its heat treatment or fishing. New in the game is the RPG system, where each partisan gains points for their technological progress for completing missions and ambush missions. Each of the characters has unique abilities that others cannot learn, but at the same time they all have the opportunity to learn some abilities. For example, one partisan wields shotguns, another submachine gun, a third knife, another can heal quickly, and so on.I don't find the game's graphics to be stunning at the time of release. It's basically the same quality as five years ago when some of you were trying to defend the Shogun of the Empire in Shadow Tactics. So its quality does not disappoint, but it does not inspire either, and I daresay that it could have been better in 2020. Even worse is the gameplay, especially during firefights or when you're trying to escape your pursuers through a dense forest. I find the gunfights quite unlucky, when the opponent practically has no chance to hit you when you are covered behind obstacles (not even snipers) and, on the contrary, basically takes you down in one or two shots when you are not taking cover, even if you are hidden in the bushes. You'll curse uneven terrain or dense trees about retreating from combat. You will often get stuck and the character will simply not find a suitable path on its own, but you will have to click the mouse again. Again, the alpha and omega of play is cover, otherwise you will be after you very quickly. Enemies will also throw grenades at you, and really run away from them immediately, otherwise it's up to you. The last thing that personally bothered me a lot was the amount of collected objects, which as the game progressed, not only your guerrillas (of which you could choose a maximum of three for each mission) were not able to take them all, but despite the voluminous storage in the camp there was nowhere to put them later. Not to mention the graphics, where the bulk of your stuff is only represented by white outlines. This makes managing looted weapons and ammo quite annoying. The controls are also not the friendliest and seem quite clunky. At the very end, I was confused by censorship, when instead of flags with swastikas, you see flags with crosses in the game.Despite the aforementioned ailments, I had a great time playing the game. In a total of fifteen missions, I tried all kinds of combat tactics, including, for example, setting explosive traps, mines, spraying enemies with a salvo from an ambush machine gun, luring enemies away using whistles, disguises, and the like. The Russian developers got it right and Commandos definitely has a capable successor, and once you get used to the aforementioned gameplay flaws, you'll start to more or less ignore them and enjoy the battles on the Eastern Front, because the campaign is really well done. Compared to, for example, the third Desperados, in the game you will see the narration of events in the form of period documentary (color) reports. Sometimes you will also witness some kind of video, although here it is more like footage from the game. If you like WWII and want to fight on the Eastern Front, Partisans 1941 might be the right choice for you. Despite some shortcomings, it is still an above-average game that will keep you entertained for dozens of hours. And for an authentic experience, I recommend setting the dubbing to Russian, because any other will deprive you of the atmosphere of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: At first it seems that the creators really want to be the new Mimimi Games, but this impression quickly dissipates, because they immediately offer many interesting things that create the obvious face of their game. To be honest, this game is much more real Commandos than the recent «Commandos 2 - HD Remaster», truly the spiritual successor to this great game. Real-time tactics, telling about the frightening time of the beginning of the Great Patriotic War, when Nazi troops of Germany treacherously attacked the Soviet Union. The player will have to take control of a detachment of partisans, gradually growing into a full-fledged military force, beating the enemy with inexorable methods. What is especially pleasant - we not only participate in direct partisan operations, but we ourselves equip life at our base, plan to supply the detachment with food, materials, create new buildings that help to more effectively survive difficult everyday life. All this skillfully alternates, so there is no time to get bored, and the gameplay becomes much more unusual.The game is skillfully distinguished by one feature that you do not immediately feel, but after understanding it, you begin to experience emotions in a completely different way. The game world is completely insecure. You cannot endlessly hide in the bushes, knocking out enemies one by one, even if the enemies will not find you there easily, but German Shepherds can easily sniff out your trail, exposing your shelter. You cannot headlong into open combat, enemies with much more powerful weapons will blow you away in no time, so you start thinking like a partisan - to plan ambushes, engage in open firefights, only by correctly placing your fighters in good cover, use laying mines on patrol roads or approaching routes of possible reinforcements, think over all your moves in advance. The feeling of constant anxiety will become your main companion, fleetingly letting go only during gatherings in a partisan camp. And it all becomes a huge win for the game.What pleases even more is the humanity with which the writers reacted to their characters and story. The heroes are very convex, their emotions are natural and understandable to the player, they are not just cardboard dummies, but real characters. Fetisov and Mellenberg turned out to be a little stereotyped, but not to say that they were especially critical. Russian dubbing of characters is generally great, I advise you to play with him and subtitles, I have not heard such an excellent performance for a long time, a deep bow to each of them for their excellent work. I sincerely empathized with each character, and at some point I wanted the developers to use their rights more often and force them to play for different characters, and not just for your favorite three of heroes. On assignments, you can find various interesting interactions, and I would like it to be even more. Much more, as well as additional quests. After all, when the locals share with you the location of the caches with weapons, the routes of the occupiers, while still telling their story, this is just an invaluable feeling of the completeness of the world. The player can also find a lot of real archival materials telling about the exploits of the partisans of those years, and also get acquainted with the famous guide to guerrilla warfare.The difficulty is extremely high, the enemies are smart and do not allow you to relax. The gameplay at the maximum difficulty level generally requires a brutal expenditure of forces. Yes, the game still needs to be polished, especially the famous Doors, which are almost more insidious here than the SS men, living their absolutely special door life. I met a critical bug only once - in Prison, when the game stubbornly failed my mission when Morozov hit a certain point in a location near the prison cells, and this place had to be defeated in very clumsy ways, moving towards the goal almost by a millimeter. And after polishing, the game should finally shine the way it deserves. My personal big thanks to everyone who made this game, you did not shame the memory of the winners in that war. There should be more of these games, I am absolutely delighted.

_childDocuments_.review: A great little strategy game that I expected to be like all the others, just another XCOM (which is why I bought it) but it turned out to be a bit different! Implementing it's own clever mechanics & enjoyable combat. There are some bits that bring it down though, the autosave system is QUITE frustrating since it essentially doesn't exist. So if you're not playing on Hardcore and you forget to save...you're playing on Hardcore. It's extremely annoying to have all my careful stealth work undone and then have to rush back through the mission to get to the fresh, new enjoyable part again. A few other things like the skills in the skill tree (they're pretty lame & identical) could be improved. There's also NO confirm options either. So if you go to split and item and accidentally click discard instead, it's gone! Quite annoying. You know when XCOM tells you you'll cause friendly fire? This game just lets you make that mistake which is a way is good cause it makes you think about your actions but when it's a simple misclick that brings my Sanek out of disguise in front of the whole german compound, causing him to die and the rest of my squad to be discovered and suffer the same fate causing me to have to redo the ENTIRE MISSION!...it can be frustrating.I swapped a few times between leaving a good or negative review but honestly I still very much enjoy this game and I'll be playing it through to it's completion and then some. So if they can make these QoL changes, this game will be fantastic!

_childDocuments_.review: Almost every mission I've played so far has had a segment where the mission automatically fails if you get spotted. This awful, outdated design choice combined with several small bugs and other strange design choices (doors almost never open correctly on your first try, taking too long to stealth kill a guard will count as you being spotted even if the guard is out of sight/hearing range of anyone else, trying to throw a rock will sometimes make your character run directly to where you wanted him to thrown) make the mandatory stealth portions of the game a tedious mix of trial and error and hoping the game doesn't decide to screw you over.Wouldn't even consider recommending this at least until the bugs are fixed but even then, the mandatory stealth sections are enough to turn me off. My only regret is that I kept playing this in the hopes that things would get better long enough to make it so I can't refund the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Comrades of the Motherland,As we stand on the precipice of history, our nation faces its greatest trial yet. In 'Partisans 1941', we are called upon to embody the spirit of resistance and wage a relentless struggle against the fascist invaders who seek to trample our homeland underfoot.This game, a testament to the indomitable will of the Soviet people, places us in command of a ragtag band of partisans, united in their determination to defend their land and their way of life. From the dense forests of Belarus to the snow-capped peaks of the Caucasus, we will wage guerrilla warfare against the Nazi oppressors, striking fear into the hearts of our enemies and inspiring hope in the hearts of our comrades.But make no mistake, comrades, this will not be an easy fight. The fascist war machine is formidable, its forces vast and relentless in their pursuit of conquest. We will face overwhelming odds, and the sacrifices we make will be great. But we must never waver in our resolve, for the fate of our nation hangs in the balance.In 'Partisans 1941', every decision we make will have consequences, and every action we take will shape the course of history. We must use all our cunning and resourcefulness to outmaneuver the enemy, striking swift and decisive blows against their supply lines and infrastructure.But it is not just the tactical aspect of the game that impresses. The attention to detail, from the authentic weapons and uniforms to the stunningly realized landscapes, serves as a poignant reminder of the real sacrifices made by our brave soldiers and partisans during those dark days of war.So I call upon you, my fellow countrymen, to rise to the challenge before us. In 'Partisans 1941', we have the opportunity to rewrite the history books, to turn the tide of battle in favor of the Motherland. Together, we will stand as one, united in our defiance against tyranny and oppression.For the glory of the Soviet Union!Comrade Stalin

_childDocuments_.review: Partisan 1941 is a real time tactics where you control a group of partisans resisting against invading Nazi force. For what was seemingly a Commando clone, Partisan shuffled up the system to accommodate a more combat-oriented gameplay and light role playing system. The result is a fun, flexible system that encourages more adaptive playstyle than almost strictly stealth focused gameplay of Commando likes.   The main bulk of your time will be spent on missions. It’s where your partisans will stab, shoot, or blow up nazis. In this segment, you choose 3 Partisans of your choice, and thrown into the level. The freedom given in tackling the levels is quite satisfying. With one or two exceptions, players are given goals such as eliminating certain enemies or rescue missions or gathering intel. Combat works similar to real time isometric RPG. if you choose partisan(s) and click on enemies, they will attack with their equipped weapons. Cover and positioning matters as these are the key to casualty-free combat. The real time element actually feels refreshing especially when you see your plan unfold. In turn based games like xcom, time basically stops until either player or AI take actions, resulting in unlimited moments to think about your next move. In Partisans, your survival in combat depends on how you react to the events happening on-screen. The addition of slow-mo also will help you, but the clock will still tick, so a fast response is still needed. One of my best example was using my SMG unit to drew fire while my shotgun wielder ambushed them. Another squad were closing in to ambush my SMG, so i threw a grenade on them with my 3rd character, got 2 of them while 1 ran and i killed them with a melee attack. It’s not a perfect system, as sometimes cheese just happens on its own. I’ve killed like a dozen units with a single grenade because the enemies were clumping on the screen and reacted poorly. They usually ran from grenades, but it might be a glitch that the crowd didn’t disperse and the explosion caught all of them at once. Overall when it’s working as intended, the combat is brilliant and fun. When it doesn’t it either can lead to funny, cheesy moments or just reload from your save before you engage. Discretion is another option when going through a level. Detection is based on 2 factors: vision and sound. Each enemy has a vision cone, and each action made by your character such as running, or shooting a gun produces sound. If you are either seen or heard, enemies will send one or more squads to investigate for a time. If you are detected during this time, combat will ensue and you will be on a disadvantage. Stealth-kill is directly related to melee skill. With high melee skill, you can take out higher-ranked enemies silently and quickly. If your character’s melee skills are low, you can kill regular soldiers easily. If you try to take on an officer, your partisan will make a lot of noise as the victim struggles that will ensue instant detection unless the surrounding area is clear of enemies.Maximum melee skills are also only owned by certain characters. The decision of who you bring during missions will affect your style as each character has their own forte. Each character has 2 types of skills: unique and generic. Generic skills are shared between other characters like gun skill or carry capacity, but each also has their own unique ability. One character specializes in stealth and has the skill to lure enemies out and take them out silently. One specializes in machine guns for suppression or crowd control, et cetera. All these factors meld together into a flexible, fun gameplay. To be honest, it’s a part of the gameplay that can be easily omitted and wouldn’t change anything for better or worse. In between missions, you have to manage your partisan’s camp. Each day will consume food for each member of the resistance. There are daily tasks that you’ll assign to each member, each have different functions. Some will raise the soldier’s morale (which determine their effectiveness), some will get you resources or food. There are some “off-screen” missions that basically can give you extra XP or equipment. The problem is the system is really shallow. You will basically never run out of resources as long as you spread the tasks evenly. The only useful part about the base is, you can spend resources and assign characters to craft usable items like health packs or grenades.The game’s performance leaves a lot to be desired. In later, bigger levels the game runs at 40-50 FPS. The game visual isn’t technically demanding so it should have been better. It doesn’t really distract your gameplay experience since the game doesn’t depend much on quick reflexes. As for bugs, per v1.03 minor bugs still exist such as weird enemy behavior and overall lack of polish. My main complaint is how cumbersome the UI is, especially the inventory screen. Organizing your equipment feels like a chore because you have to click right for a drop-down menu to show weapon stats instead of a floating bubble that automatically appears when you hover over the items. This game doesn’t have zillions of polygons nor fancy shaders and effects but strong art direction glued the pixels on the screen very well. For example the muted color palette reflects well on the game’s setting of early wintry russia. Aesthetics wise, I have no problem but functionally, some parts of the design can be confusing. With some characters, especially those who wear similar clothes and body type, it’s sometimes hard to distinguish them on the screen unless you click on them. The sound is acceptable across all boards. Sound effects, voice acting, music does all it’s job enough. Partisans 1941 shakes the formula of real time tactics games enough that it is quite worthy of your time. Some of the edges are rough, but if you are a fan of commandos and the like and looking for something similar yet different, i cannot recommend this enough.
