_childDocuments_.review: I put this game down in frustration when it first came out because I was struggling to come to grips with its mechanics, which are more punishing than I am typically used to in games that emphasize stealth. But I picked it up again to give it another try, and it's grown on me much more now. I wasn't a huge fan of the missions where you instant lose when you get spotted, but the game does have a generous quicksave system. I initially didn't like this because it felt like I was being encouraged to do extreme save-scumming through every mission (since they tend to be quite involved and it would be a pain to restart), but I've now grown to appreciate it as a tool for you to set your own checkpoints. It only breaks the immersion if you use it every few seconds, and it is nice to have it there to encourage taking more risks and trying new things, because you can reload very quickly. So in the end it did end up enhancing my experience. I think also just playing better and learning to wrap my head around the mechanics has made me enjoy the challenge more. The game is not forgiving mechanically, but it is cool to pull off plans and maneuvers that require split-second timing and precision. The tactical pause feature is very nice that way. All in all, I've changed my negative review to positive after giving it another go, and I do recommend trying it out!

_childDocuments_.review: Really good fun game. It had a few issues with doors, prior to the patch, that lots of reviews mention. This is now resolved and they don't flap/open close etc. The levels are well thought out and require some thinking about. One of the things I really liked was the ability to choose different characters for the missions. You normally have one you have to use, but you can use any of the others you already unlocked. I definitely had a favourite, so will play again, without using that character, which then changes your whole strategy for the missions. You can't just open fire and expect to win against more than 5 or 6 guards. I see lots of people complaining about this, but this is as I would imagine real life would have worked out back then.TIP - Equipment is persistent from level to level, so every bullet/grenade is really important. Don't waste them. Again this is lifelike as Russian soldiers were often sent to the front with just 5 bullets. Definitely recommend if you liked Commandos or the Minimi Games titles.

_childDocuments_.review: I was actually very excited for this game from having seen the demo, since I've been itching for a good Commandos like experience for a while. While Desperados 3 and Shadow tactics are fun, was kinda sad we haven't gotten a WW2 one until now.Okay, so what I played so far the game is rather enjoyble. It has this mixture of Commandos 2, meets Darkest Dungeon, Desperados 3/Shadow Tactics and I'd say Men of War. The Commandos 2 part comes from sneaking behind enemy lines, having a squad of soldiers, inventory stuff and being able to loot bodies and other items. Darkest Dungeon is the whole base building part and managing ones resources, plus sending your partisans on side missions to get food, ammo, parts or raise morale, while from Men of war it has the cover mechanics and I wanna say the distance shooting. While from DS3/ST it borrowed the mechanic of freezing time and letting you issue individual orders for your troops.Now, I'm currently on mission 2 and I don't know how much the game racks up it's difficulty from there, but from what I saw the 2nd mission is gonna be a fun challenge. The game however isn't without it's flaws, for some reason the keyboard camera controls aren't working as they should, which isn't an issue as I just switched to oldschool of using a mouse, however this could be a problem for others. An I did run into a couple of glitches of characters getting stuck in doors or on geometry. So, I hope these things will get patched.Can I recommend this game? Well, if you enjoyed Desperados 3 and Shadow Tactics, I'd say yes, and if you're a fan of the Commandos series you will prob also enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Naturally you're going to compare this to Shadow Tactics and Desperados due to it's obvious similarities. There's hits and misses when doing that.Engaging open-fire is an interesting additional to the predominately stealth-based genre. Sometimes it's the best, and most efficient, way to tackle a problem. It's also nice to have the option. Getting spotted doesn't always mean a loaded save. However I do wish they explored this approach a bit further. There's very little to do once you're in a fire-fight. Leaving cover is risky, and slow, and you'd wished you'd set up someone on a flank before engaging (which kind of defeats the purpose of why I liked it as a stealth-alternative, if I'm utilizing stealth to establish position I might as well utilize that same stealth to kill). Additionally with a percentage-based hit-chance on enemies, missing may result in them having time to reach cover themselves, further reducing your success rate and forcing you to painstakingly re-position mid-fight (I can't stress how bad an option this is), or load a save.As part of this open-combat system however, is the nice addition of equipment and load-outs (something you don't see from Shadow tactics/Desperados). Having different weapon choices, and multiple different utility options, is a nice touch.Rolling with the positives; I thought the 'base section' in between missions was added value. Choosing some automated assignments/missions to gain rewards, of which you can decide is most beneficial, is a good addition.There's some annoying tech issues regarding UI at higher resolutions/aspect ratios. My normal fixes weren't applicable either. Playing windowed was tolerable, but you don't necessarily want to play a video game to 'tolerable standards'.Also a really bad design decision regarding saving plagued my missions. You cannot save during certain character actions. Some make sense, some do not. This however was not a gripe I ever experienced with Shadow tactics or Desperados. For example; you cannot save when one of the characters is utilizing a disguise. This is extremely painful as he moves at a significantly reduced speed while disguised, and you ultimately want to save after you've got him in a position to distract somebody (while disguised) before initiating a kill command with another character. This leads you to need to not only think about how you're going to execute a stealth-kill, but also think about where you can hide the disguised character so that you can de-disguise without being spotted, save, stay safe while waiting for disguise to come off cooldown, before going back into position. Unnecessary and a real headache considering how I felt the few missions I did in my short playtime leaned heavily on this ability.With Shadow Gambit being released with Overwhelmingly Positive reviews, and considering the substantial discount I got, I'm happy to give this a miss.

Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the mother of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: I kept my original review at the bottom because someone was upset that I reviewed the game with 8 hours played.  I felt like 8 hours was enough to have a reasonable opinion about the gameplay and mechanics, but I told them I'd finish the game and update my review anyway.My opinions haven't really changed since my original review, and if anything, they further cement my problems with the game.- Stealth is just too good in this game, and the lack of variety in stealth is what makes it get quickly stale.  What doesn't help at all is that the enemy AI is quite dumb and predictable. Every single enemy in the game does one of two things: stand in one spot and only look in one direction, or walk a route where they will inevitably look left, then straight, then right, and they may finally repeat that looking pattern a couple more times before moving elsewhere.  It doesn't really feel all that cool or rewarding, which is a shame because I'm a fan of stealth.  If you're hoping for something even remotely close or interesting to your favorite stealth games, this isn't it.- The only thing I'll slightly change is that gunplay *can* feel decent if your character skills have weapon accuracy maxed and the weapon has an accuracy upgrade.  There's a few other things that can affect accuracy such as injuries, but until your weapon accuracy situation is in the best state it can possibly be in, it's just not that good.  It's worth mentioning that even when your weapon accuracy is the best it can be, it's still completely inferior to stealth.  There aren't many missions where stealth can't be used at all, either.Additionally, here's some glitches and general frustrations I came across.  No spoilers ahead.- One time when my partisan was downed, their body teleported across the map.- Sanek's disguise ability makes it so you can't save the game because "the character is busy".  However, there was a time where after he was no longer disguised, the game insisted that he was still "busy".  I tried putting the disguise back on and then removing it again, but still the same issue.  My only way of fixing this was loading to an earlier save, which is frustrating.- During one mission where you need to kill an important enemy, the important enemy runs off to a nearby village.  During one of my attempts, the important enemy started to casually walk in the middle of a firefight towards the area he just ran away from.  This is not expected behavior, as he's supposed to stand until we engage in a cutscene with him.- If you're in the enemy cone of vision, they start to get suspicious (which is expected).  You can do just about any action without immediately alarming them while in their vision.  You can throw a grenade, throw a rock, heal yourself, and it's no issue.  You know what is an issue?  Placing a harmless bottle on the ground.  Placing a bottle on the ground in their cone of vision IMMEDIATELY alerts all nearby enemies.  Let me emphasize that you can throw a grenade in their vision, but not place a harmless bottle.- Mission failed screen has been completely unresponsive a few times, causing me to quit the game completely to fix it.- I've had partisan #1 stuck in the reviving animation if they happen to get downed while reviving partisan #2.  This also caused the partisan #2 to be 100% incapable of being revived (which is never supposed to happen).  Additionally, if you revive partisan #1, they will be perpetually in that same reviving animation, and totally unable to commit any actions other than gliding across the ground.  Had to load a different save to fix this.- You can actually throw grenades over the walls of an adjacent room, even though the walls clearly go all the way up to the ceiling.  May take a few tries to get the height and angle right, also assuming the wall isn't too high.  One particularly egregious example of this is killing the final important enemy in the final mission.- One mission has you running away from a ton of soldiers who are actively trying to find you.  Once you get to the exit, a cutscene plays.  However, I started to hear gunfire unrelated to the cutscene.  I quickly realized that the cutscene is just playing over the mission I was just in, and my partisans were not teleported to a safe location.  They were actually fighting even though I reached the exit.  My partisans died, and I saw a "mission failed" screen while the cutscene was still playing.  Moments later, I saw a "mission successful" screen placed over top of the "mission failed" screen, which is all still placed over the cutscene.  This is confusing, annoying, and inexcusable.- There are a few other glitches or annoying things, but the ones above were particularly annoying.I do have a few nice things to say about the game.- Voice acting was pretty okay.- Between story missions, you can assign partisans to do some base missions for gathering resources.  This is a nice extra touch to the game, though it definitely could have been fleshed out more.Overall, I still cannot recommend this game.  Most of the game felt okay, but the actual gameplay is where it truly fell short.  It felt boring, unrewarding, and more of a chore than anything.===ORIGINAL REVIEW===I wanted to like this game so much, but the combat is so bad.  Stealth is king in this game, but enemy routes are the same 100% of the time.  This makes for somewhat bland and not-so-creative gameplay.  Stealth really just consists of sneaking up behind an enemy, knifing them, and then hiding their body.  Seems fairly simple (and it is), but it gets really repetitive.  To be honest, stealth is likely too good, and in stark contrast to awful gunplay.  What's really annoying is that if you're caught, all nearby enemies suddenly know your position on the map, no matter what.  Really bizarre oversight and frustrating to experience.  Gunplay feels so bad.  After the first few missions, enemy soldiers tend to have great accuracy while your accuracy is still mediocre.  You can use cover to make enemy accuracy go down a bit, but it ultimately feels like you're always at a disadvantage.  You could argue that you're going against trained soldiers, but the repetitive stealth is just not that fun to make up for that.  You can upgrade your accuracy for certain guns and other skills, which can help a bit, but not enough in my experience.For anyone claiming this is like XCOM or Fallout, that is a completely mistaken comparison.  Combat is real-time in this game, whereas that isn't the case with XCOM and classic Fallout games.  Combat becomes far too chaotic if you're not prepared for it, and your squad will likely die unless you had intentionally engaged in a gun fight.  If you think you can quickly micro-manage your squad in the middle of a gunfight like an RTS game, it's really not that effective.The story is otherwise alright and the aesthetics are cool, but the gameplay is just not there for me.  I've tried coming back to this game a couple of times now, but I just can't get myself to enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sort of like if Desperados III and XCOM had a premature baby. You're about to read a lot of complaints, but I did enjoy this game quite a bit.This game is a buggy and unpolished mess. I played through on normal, and the bugs were so numerous and frequent that I think I might have smashed my monitor to pieces if I had been playing on the hardest difficulty (where you can't save during tactical missions). The most prominent bugs for me were: 1. The game struggled to constrain the mouse cursor within the game window, so the cursor would constantly fly off to another monitor. I could temporarily fix this by pausing the game, but the bug would consistently return a few minutes later. 2. Characters will occasionally get permanently stuck on objects like boxes and walls. If this happens to one of your partisans, it almost always requires loading a save as most missions can only be finished by moving your entire squad to a specific area on the map. If a a Nazi gets stuck on something, it will cause them to sort of phase out of existence and become untargetable by most weapons and abilities. The only methods I've found to correct this situation is to intentionally run into the stuck NPC's view cone, or to spend a usage of an AOE kill ability (like Massacre). Either of these bugs occurring on the hardest difficulty is likely to force a full mission restart.The game also generally runs pretty poorly for no clear reason. There's also a huge list of bizarre design choices such as:Completely randomized loot on most enemies and boxes.Vague or sometimes inaccurate descriptions for skill tree abilities (this seems at least partially due to the somewhat lazy English translation).Some skills are borderline useless (Strength, Inspiration II) while others are completely overpowered (Whistle II, Body Shield).Not allowed to drop food / supply items after picking them up.Partisans that can specialize in rifles are generally far better in combat than other partisans. The economy and progressions systems feel very off. Everything that costs supplies feels insanely expensive, and the utility of many base buildings is questionable at best. There's also no explanation for what a building does or how it works until you build it. Despite all these issues, I enjoyed this game. There aren't a lot of serviceable games like this, so I'm willing to accept a considerable amount of jank. If you enjoyed Desperados III / Shadow Tactics, this might scratch that sort of itch, but it's definitely nowhere near as satisfying.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid, aesthetically pleasing entry in the real-time tactical genre. Unlike many, however, stealth is important but not crucial, allowing for a refreshing option to go in guns blazing if you want. The influence of Mimimi games is strong, which is a good thing, though it lacks polish in enough ways that the difference in quality is noticeable. Still highly recommended for fans of the genre!-Art, Aesthetic, Setting:  Fantastic. Perfect for this type of game.-Character Design:  They look awesome! Their backstories are interesting and believable, though sparsely exhibited and not terribly complex.-Level Design:  Impressively large, complicated, and non-linear. There are many ways to approach a given situation, which matters a lot considering that each character has their own skill trees and special abilities.-Sound Design:  Crisp, clear, fitting, and just enjoyable.-Mechanics:  While generally competent and satisfying, some special abilities are vastly better than others or simply redundant. Implementation and NPC behaviour is a bit inconsistent. This is mitigated by the effective quicksave option, but it feels a bit sloppy sometimes.-Interface:  Inventory management, item comparison, and click hitboxes are all a pain.-Length:  There’s plenty of gameplay, but without a really engaging story it feels a bit long.-Voice Acting:  Most are decent/good, but a few are stellar, especially Trofim, Nikitin, and Morozov.EDIT:  Original quickshot review below.It's good! I think some negative reviews make the mistake of comparing this to the Mimimi games (Desperado, Shadow Tactics), from which it copies many elements, especially the mission UI, but this game has a different playstyle and aesthetic. It's not as polished, but it stands well on its own. If you enjoy this genre, this game is a worthy entry, with plenty of variety and fun. It also allows a little more playstyle flexibility than most in the genre, which mostly focuses on stealth. It's very important here, but there are way more opportunities to pick a firefight if you want.

_childDocuments_.review: Vodka Tactics: Blades of the Commissar This game is really very, very similar to Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, up to the animation of stealth kills. Which is honestly great - because the former is one of the best stealth RTS games. But instead of shinobi clan, here you will lead a band of partizani fighting nazis.Pros:-Very interesting stealth actions-Deep, realistic and lovable characters-Amazing voicing - germans speak german, russians speak russian, yet you get subtitles in english. That is so much better for a game like this than your typical "fake accents" or "everybody speaks US english". Glad they went with this option-Atmosphere is very fitting-Music is great for background, nothing special - but you will not tire of it even after many hours.-A bit of base managementCons:-Linearity. This is by no means an XCOM-like game. Here it is more story-driven, same as Shadow Tactics. You sometimes can complete (or not) side quests, but for the most part you are only and observer here. Also, companions you recruit are fixed, so not much choice in that-Some frequent bugs with clipping terrain and "stuck" characters, but save often and that shouldn't be a problemOverall: 9/10, great tactical game, albeit a bit linear. But if you don't mind and just want hardcore stealth-oriented tactical game - buy this. Also, must buy if you liked Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun.

_childDocuments_.review: Already put in some good hours into the game so far and all in hard mode (no saves). Couple of things to say here:Good things:1) Decent story. Keeps me engaged and it's big chilling to see the campfire interactions after every mission. 2) Fun combat, and devs did a good job in making gunfights a completely viable approach many situations. Assuming you don't attempt to shoot literally every enemy you see, you'll get enough ammo and explosives to play with. 3) Cool skill system. Makes very noticeable impact in how you decide to play the game.Bad things (and some are really really bad):1) Overall character control is atrocious. In a world where Commandos, Desperados, and Shadow Tactics exist, there is absolutely no excuse for how bad and clunky character control is in this game. Things that I was taking for granted in the original Commandos, RELEASED IN 1998, are somehow broken in this game. Specifically:a) If you issue a kill command with your knife (to include zorin's knife throw) and the enemy soldier moves, your character will just walk there, sit still, and get shot. In most cases any movement from the enemy will flat out cancel your command. Your characters don't like to follow the enemy for the kill for whatever reason. It's rage inducing at times as a player and it points toward laziness from the dev side. Like, come on guys, people were getting this right 15 years ago.b) Game does not like it when you have multiple commands going out to different characters at the same time. Works in most cases, but happens enough to be noticeable.c) Object placement's range is a random dice roll. All those games above will give you a range indicator of how far you can place that bottle of wine away from your character, for example. This game? none of that. And worse yet, it isn't consistent. You can place a bait bottle like 2 bodies out from the bush you're in one time and can't place it outside the bush the next. d) Your left click does waaaaaaaaay too much. You accidentally click on a body? You moving that sucker. It gets insanely obnoxious when  you're playing around tight spaces or small brushes when you're trying to both hide the bodies and your own character. other games would have you held down Ctrl or something to pick them up or to inspect inventory. Simple solution, but it makes the game smooth. Not only that, some genius had the idea of packing at least 2 huge selectable buttons when you mouse over the bodies. Like, which genius UI designer was it who thought that was a good idea?2) Moving on from the controls, the stealth/hidden system isn't very clearly defined. It's not buggy (too much), but what you do to stay not detected or not (sometimes a specific criteria for finishing a mission) is not very clear cut. If, say, you use an infantry mine to blow up a patrolling squad with a dog, as long as no one saw the soldiers dying, enemy who can hear the explosion ran there to inspect, try to find you, and then walk away. IT DOESN'T break your stealth. But, if you gun down a lone guy in a random ass corner of the map and no one else is around? You're detected. If you kill someone with a knife, ran away to the other side of map, and then the body gets spotted? You're detected. On top of that, as others have pointed out before me, they're really good at running toward you, no matter where you are. If you run sufficiently far away they'll stop after a bit so it's not that bad though.3) Game is bug infested. Characters got stuck in the middle of trees, pathing gets messed up, etc. You name it, they got it. I got a current bug right now where Zorin wouldn't fire his rifle after a mission. Went online to look for it, and lo and behold the error was mentioned A YEAR AND A HALF AGO. None of the fixes that worked then work now either. Devs somehow managed to patch the fixes out but not the bug. Brilliant.I love pain, so I'm still playing it, but I cannot actually recommend this game for anyone else, whether they're a fan of the genre or if they're just starting out. The competing games are just so much better.

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely leave reviews. This game is such a mixed bag. I've had a lot of fun playing it, it's also a really frustrating game. The launch of this game was incredibly poor (the first patch completely broke everyone's save game files, we got them back but it took a few days). There are a hundred little usability issues that feel like death by a thousand cuts. It's playable, and not just barely, but some of the issues are really frustrating. There's workarounds for pretty much all of the issues, which is why I was able to play all the way through and beat it. The mechanics are interesting and fun. There's a lot of wasted potential though. For instance the camp mechanic feels like it could have been really interesting but by the end of the game I was basically just cruising through it.If you're looking to buy this game wait- give it maybe a few months before the patches come out to fix some of these issues. It does seem like the developers care. They're responsive on discord. You can feel the passion in the game and it's very aesthetically pleasing and the characters are all really well-crafted. I don't regret buying this game, however I wish I would have waited a few months to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game it self is kinda cool. You have solid graphics and even sound is not bad. But what does not work with this game is the play-ability. I will not be talking about bugs because I guess there are plenty posts about that. First of all what I do not like is to have only three partisans you can use per mission. And in very most cases you will have pre-selected partisans you can use and you can't change that. So you have different partisans with different roles and abilities and you level them up (via automated missions) but you can't use them because the game won't let you to use them. This is the game killer that want's you to stop playing or not even trying. If I knew that before I bought the game I wouldn't be writing a review right now.The second thing that deserves to be pointed out is the base upgrade. So you waste tons of resources on base upgrade so that at the end you can't do anything with it. You build a kitchen, a hen house, med tent, workshop, a watch tower for hunting and that's about it. You build several buildings to produce food and while doing that you need to use partisans you can bring them on the mission because they are somekind of a NPC. They don't even get experience points. Anyway with all the resources you pour into the base yoou don't even have a decent armory to make you bullets. You can make some homemade grenades and mines (that are way less powerfull) and ou can upgrade your weapons. But then again how many weapons can you upgrade when you can use only three partisans at the time? Exactly!The third thing are rewards. Oh man I've seen pretty bad games with awful rewards, but this game is even worse. On a dead Nazi soldier you find an empty shell. That's your loot. You transform empty bullet shells into the resources but that doesn't help you much since you can't make anything useful.  In this game German army is the poorest army in WW2, even poorest than the Soviet Union at that time. If you are lucky you can find a whole bullet on a dead soldier.The fourth and the last thing are the missions, tips, quality of life in general. Missions are poorly explained. So partisan unit is small and agile, meaning you don't carry unnecessary explosives, grenades and bullets.  Stealth is your strongest weapon. But during the mission there are times when mission is extended and you can't stealth and you need to defend from all sides multiple times. Which is fine but there could be an information to bring extra bullets. The junk you carry in your backpack has no tool tips like most games do. You need to to clicking and clicking to get the information what's all about. The same goes for weapons and stuff. When you save a game, I don't understand why I need to click "return" and why is escape button not working? When there is an confirmation to send out partisans why is pressing "enter" not enough? I won't even go into the awful leveling mechanics and experience points gaining. _childDocuments_.review: If you liked Commandos back in the day, or you like stealthy turn-based tactical games, then Partisans 1941 is enjoyable enough. And a little addictive. (It's not turn-based but these games still kinda play like ones in a way.) I never quite liked Shadow Tactics. That game never brought back fond gaming memories in the same way Partisans does. Much like in Commandos, you lead a small, isometric team against the Nazis, only this time it's partisans on the Eastern front rather than a ragtag crew of commandos on the Western front. Very much in-character too, if we put it that way. It's all WWII Eastern rethorics and ethos this time, a novel experience for a Western gamer.Clearly a hommage to Commandos, Partisans 1941 include sneaking around enemy 'cones of vision' since taking on too many enemies in a firefight is a very bad idea, much as it was back then (I'm not only referring to Commandos). But then the devs also threw a mini resource management game and RPG elements on top. It doesn't add all that much to the game experience, but it's a little extra on top of a game idea that is over 20 years old by now. But still works just fine.I read some complaints in other reviews here about the interface being clunky. It's not too bad really. Besides, it's NOTHING against how Commandos was. Commandos was sort of retro already back when it was released and, boy, was it clunky! But that never mattered. It was fun anyway. Here, due to significantly larger maps and more complexity, the game becomes more unpredictable. You end up quicksaving your way through basically every move you do, at least if you go the full stealth route for the achievements, but as opposed to Commandos you never really save yourself into a corner since there are three quicksave slots (plus you can do hard saves as well). You try something, screw up, reload, try something else, screw up, reload, try a third approach, phew, it worked, better save immediately! That's how it plays. Playing through a map takes a little time and that seems to be the intention.The one thing Partisans lack compared to Commandos is that humorous charm that made the latter game so irresistible even during its most frustrating moments. It was like one of those old WWII movies back when wars were still portrayed like an adventure on the silver screen. But with Partisans it's like it can't quite make up its mind whether it's a dead serious game or not. It's sort of strung up in between Commandos, on the one hand, and on the other hand a movie like Come and See, portraying the real horrors of the Eastern front from the civilian perspective.

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying this game immensely. For starters, it's very interesting to not take the role of "the west" (or the Allies or whatever is appropriate for the game in question). The story, the characters, it's all good, but I find myself mostly coming back to see whether I can stealth kill every enemy.There are a few minor bugs people have mentioned elsewhere, but nothing I found too game breaking. Sometimes I have to move a body before I can loot it, ok. Sometimes I tell a character to place a mine or distraction item and they just don't do it. _childDocuments_.review: This would be my very first negative review on steam.Before I start, I would like to point out that this game was gifted to me. _childDocuments_.review: Let me start out by saying that I do not think this is an objectively bad game. It's has a lot of cool ideas and mechanics. However there are a few big issues that really make it hard for me to recommend to anyone. I enjoy the setting and the overall concept for the game. The base management, character skill trees and inventory management, and unique character skills are all done fairly well while not super complex. My biggest issue with the game has to be the cover system. There are so many areas where it would make sense to be able to use as cover in combat yet you can't. Doorways, wall breaches, and even some corners of buildings are not counted as cover in combat. The games pickiness in what it allows you to use as cover limits your tactical options and is very frustrating. I really want to like this game but that alone is enough to kill it for me.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Commandos 2 and Desperados you will probably like this game, too. The characters have different abilities, but they are not as remarkable or distinguished as in the other comparable games. One big difference, though, is that open fire fights are sometimes even encouraged, and the game provides a cover mechanic and it is a lot of fun seeing a plan unfolding when you circumvented the enemies and flank them from all sides. This is where the game really shines, though the RNG factor is quite high, meaning the outcome from these firefights can be vastly different. I had fun with the game for the time it lasted, I wished the devs would polish it a bit more, if there is any DLC, I will surely be there to play it.

_childDocuments_.review: Most difficult game I've played in a long time.... Most people reading this are either from Humble Bundle, or a fan of RTS- so two audiences, only one of which I'm a part of.I abhor RTS games, X-Com games, 4X, whatever the hell genre this game is... Controlling multiple characters at the same time, each with "unique" abilities, etc... Stealth is the name of the game... It should be Tom Clancy's PartiCell 1941... I'm on the..... 3rd?? Mission of the game? After 6 hours of playing... And dying..  And playing, and getting spotted, and playing and getting spotted, and quicksaving after every single stealth takedown I make when I remember to which unfortunately is VERY RARELY... So the game is generous with saves, unless you're on the hardest difficulty, in which case you can't save.. I'm on THE EASIEST difficulty and there's something "off" about the enemy placement...Every level feels like it's setup in AN INCREDIBLY specific way, with a specific path to take, masquerading as a game you can make infinite choices in... Quickly you will realize you have NO FREEDOM, until I assume later in the game when you can finally craft different things that will help.... Well for my first six hours I've been wandering bush to bush, placing a non-infinite amount of bottles on the ground, throwing a rock, luring one guard away from 3 to an area that looks like a vision dead zone only to realize, "Nope, that one guard literally across the camp turns his head at such an unfortunate time, while another one looks at the exact same spot the second the other turns his head away... Ok, so... Can't do that...It's a puzzle game of trial and error... Which guard do the devs want me to take out next, and WHAT do I have to do to get him out of the line of sight of quite literally 7 other guards, scattered across the camp, whose vision cones are sweeping across the entire camp, (and your planned target) incessantly.. It's also all in Russian with subtitles..... This is not a game who's story I care about, it's NOT INTERESTING, it's INCREDIBLY cliche so far, but again, I'm only on Mission 3, I've just been playing with the same 3 characters the ENTIRE time.. The dialogue is beyond sub-par... ANY of the characters you meet/play as/control could die in the story and I wouldn't even think twice... Even the chipper young enthusiastic, "I wanna face the world" 14 year old kid who's immediately on your team. I actually DO hope he gets killed off, that's how unsatisfying his interactions are... Main protagonist "badass" is too generic to even be worth discussing.. He's the Commander of a former something in the Soviet Union, it truly doesn't matter at all.. Ok so the story is terrible, the dialogue in general is hair-pulling... Music? Well, there isn't really any gameplay soundtrack, so that's not worth mentioning....What else? I can't say.. I would like to give more insight into what the game has to offer, but after more than 6 hours, and such a slow burn, I can neither recommend this nor discourage, so I'm going to give the benefit of the doubt towards people who like these types of games. If you think 6 hours of studying patrol patterns and struggling to work your way through, (not joking) 30 Germans with a knife, and if you're spotted you immediately fail and go back to the last save point- (which could be the beginning of the level multiple times if you're like me.... At some point you just start speedrunning the damned missions because you're so fed up, which leads to more mistakes, which ultimately leads to an Alt-F4 after a few good hours..) If all that sounds frustrating and NOT your cup of tea, I'd stay away...If you have more experience controlling multiple incredibly vulnerable characters through swarms of enemies without being alerted, yet still needing to kill them through the use of the same exact way of luring them with a shiny bottle of rum they all say "It must be my Lucky Day!" when they spot and walk over to it, by throwing a rock to get their attention to look towards, and then stealth killing them from a bush like you did to the last 10- if this is your genre, you may have fun with this... The atmosphere is good. I like the period. I like the idea behind the game... So even after what seems like a scathing review, the passionate anger and hatred I feel for this game kinda makes me want to keep playing and see if your characters EVER become viable, or if you're CONSTANTLY in a state of glorified Puzzle solving.. You can craft different items, I just built the workshop at your camp you fix up.... But after a couple nights (one of which is dedicated to healing injuries and food) you're forced to go on a mission when all ya really wanna do is a random Task that came in that gives you supplies and XP. Overnight... But no you needed to heal and fish. And now you gotta go do a mission that takes, in my case, and I can't help but imagine many others also, roughly 2 hours to finish... It's not as chill of a game as I'd thought... I would have liked very little brain work, but alas that's not the case... And the fact that I can't listen to the story, I have to read subtitles of the characters speaking Russian is also INCREDIBLY annoying.. The story is already so uninteresting, at least let me check my phone... Why does it take Russians 25 seconds to say "The Fascists have a tank. Blow it up.." Ok, so after reading that, can you skip thru phrases like Fallout, or Pokemon, or literally any other game with dialogue? No but you can hold space and skip the ENTIRE dialogue, which at the end of the day, seems less and less like you're missing out on ANYTHING of value.. I'm going to beat this 3rd mission.... I may even move on to the 4th mission... After Mission 4, I will have about 10-15 hours in the game, and I may update my review accordingly. If this isn't your genre, do not buy it.. If you like X-Com style games, I'd read a different review from someone qualified in the genre... If you received it in your HB like myself, and you're wondering whether it's worth booting up..... That's why I have to leave a Thumbs Up.. It's worth booting up to see if it's for you. Some games you play and they just aren't for you.. Some games you play and you realize "This is a BAD GAME, and the majority of sane people will ALSO think this is a terrible game.." Others leave you feeling confused yet open to the idea that there could be an audience for this.. This game is the latter for me...I can't help but feel like this is a good game for the right people, and an "okay" game for someone to try out who's not big on awkward camera angles and games anywhere under the genre of "Strategy." Feel free to comment, check me, correct me, and even give pointers if you think there's something I'm obviously missing in terms of being successful.. I could CERTAINLY use them.. But if you disagree that Sanek is the most annoying "Side-Protagonist" in any game you can imagine to date, I'll probably disable comments because I want the conversation to be fruitful, not full of sociopaths. And if you think Sanek is charming, you're unstable, and very likely *dangerous* like a *rattlesnake..*

_childDocuments_.review: EXTREMELY impressed with this game! Been streaming this for 2-4 hours at a time, and loving every single moment of it. This scratches that itch that Commando's left behind (I didn't play the HD remake as it was buggy). From huge maps, with insane amounts of enemies and different enemy types and plenty of variations on how you approach missions.I will start with the cons,- Tiny bugged animations (using a mounted machine gun)- "Sometimes" characters take a none planned long route and run in front of enemies if you don't micro manage- English voices for playable characters, no accents just straight up out of London (Germans speak German and well etc)         - To clarify, I think they did this to show the characters don't really speak German and they are foreign / make you            dislike them more.- Censorship (makes sense in 2020)Pros!- Very large missions which can take hours- Large selection of playable partisans with unique skills- LOTS of missions ( still got many more to play - i think)- Graphics are acceptable- No lag, or noticed any game breaking bugs- Lots of voluntary tasks to do, added items like turning power off, luring dogs away, disabling alarms, making trains drive off etc.- Base and army management- Micro management of resources- Tarkov style equipment / ammo / kit distribution among players- 101 ways to kill everyone- mini missions between main campaign missions to do- Skill / level ranks with additional unlockable items / characteristics and kill methods.This game genuinely put the effort in to make it solid, working and enjoyable. This is not rushed nor is this quick and easy to play, careful planning and save/load is MUST. Other than some tiny polishing bits, this game is pretty much Commandos 3 reborn with some things missing but lots of things added. If you like Desperados III, Commandos (any) or Shadow Tactics, you will surely enjoy and like this game!9.5 / 10Feel free to watch below for live game play or previous play throughs!

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly like the game.  Though, the DLC leaves much to be desired, the game, itself, is plenty worth it.  Gameplay reminds me of Blades of The Shogun.  Isometric, stealth-focused gameplay.  Mission-oriented.  Though, I do wish the game was longer...  Or that there were simply more missions.  Perhaps an "endurance" mode?  Just see how many missions you can go?  Though, I suppose that, eventually, you'll run out of maps and missions...Ah, one thing I expected to happen, yet never did, was a raid on the Partisan camp, itself.  I expected, at some point, to lose everything in it, and have to start, more or less, from scratch again.  Plus building the base myself, hand-picking locations for things as to prevent it from being found, and if it is found, to have defenders ready to protect it...  A bit of a missed opportunity, but I guess it would be a bit of a hassle, to make.Honestly, they could release MANY more of these games.  Playing as Polish, French, Italian [During the Civil War in Italy], Czech, Albanian, and Jewish, even German Partisans?  Honestly, they could make so bloody many of these...The Polish one, alone, has so many heartbreaking ups and downs.  Fighting both the Russians and the Germans...  Then the Germans exclusively...  Russia then helps them, but ends up betraying them, and executing many Partisan groups so that they may conquer Poland again...!  Could make a three game series on Poland alone.

_childDocuments_.review: 9/10 - Excels in the Real Time Tactics with slow/pause genre+ Fantastic tactical espionage+ Hybrid blend of battles and strategy layer la-xcom is much appreciated even if limited+ Guns blazing or bush camping gives you options on how to achieve goals+ Heavy stealth push as a strategy great number of missions forcing stealth to support the narrative+ Beautiful engine with fantastic complimentary UI+ Excellent setting drawing on the vast history of the period and actual partisans+ Slavic game made with care - wonderful usage of Russian, Ukrainian and German throughout+ Gameplay is an improved polished marauder/JA/shadow tactics mix providing emergent combos+ AI well done in both stealth and combat modes+ Different settings/foes force tactical flexibility and usage of skills/tools+ Memorable characters well done from being nameless caricatures+ Expansive number of skills, weapons, utilities and maps+ True to time period Soviet propaganda/dialog~ Game drags if you try to wipe out all enemy forces- XP progression uneven with some events giving you 100 fold of enemy kills- Engine stable but slow and stutters often- No real usage of multiple characters as usually one or two can brutalize all problems- Can stealth most of the game - wish there were more levels geared for combat- Some skills overpowered; balance issuesExtremely satisfied with my experience - highly recommended for TBT/RTT fans or anyone that likes the setting

_childDocuments_.review: This is a strategy game similar to the old Commandos but without the deep strategy and gimmicks. As almost every Daedalic Game it has a lot of things but lacks of depth. It's not a flaw it's just like they do everything. Game has a good story, solid mechanics (even if they are a bit repetitive).Now why the negative review? There are two major issues which made the game unplayable and unfun, unless you savescum a lot.First, and this is a VERY stupid issue, putting common \ powerful \ elite enemies in a realistic strategic game is dumb as hell, almost as dumb as "weapon rarity", which is in game but whatever.A bullet is a bullet, doesn't matter if you are a common grunt or the general of the SS. This is WW2 not modern warfare, if I shoot you hitting 100% you die, no matter your grade or how much experience in the army you have.During gunfights, even if you ambush them, under cover and the guy is on plain sight you STILL have to hit him a lot of times before elite enemies die. This is stupid. Normal grunts usually die in one hit, from silver and over its like they are bulletproof.The second issue is the fact that cones of vision and hearing ranges are completely bonkers and they will screw you around. I can't stress enough how much this is important in this kind of game.There is absolutely randomness on when it does happens. A patrol with a dog can ignore the corpse you left far from them and the fourth time they do the same route they find it, and you are far in the map cause you thought "ok that’s fine they will not find it”.Also enemies can see trough a 20x20 window near the roof and spot a corpse you left on the floor. Height differences are completely ignored, even if you clearly see the cone of vision ignoring that zone.Hearing is absolutely random, a corpse falling alert people over solid concrete walls on time, another time is ignored by the guy at 2m from them.This stuff can't happen in those games. Playing on hard or without a finger on the quick save is impossible, there is too much uncertainty on how things works that makes this game a pain to play. You can be the best master planner in the universe, something will screw up.In the end I kept playing but some missions are excruciatingly painful for this issue.It’s not a bad game but needed more fixing and design competence.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: MAN! I really do wish i enjoyed Partisans 1941 and got to finish it BUT the more i played it, the more i become annoyed with the game cause of lot of bugs, some missing features and how badly optimization it is.I like how the game starts and introduces you to your Partisans and camp to handle but with time you realize that that camp is just same repetitive stuff you got to do. You send someone for food, some to get ammo, XP, and materials for few days before a new mission starts, The weapons i got *at least* from those were actually more bad than what you get yourself from inside the actual missions. Other issue is that this game runs like sh*t in some missions. Some missions you get solid 60+ FPS without any issues while in others it is 10-25fps (  been some example ). Really disappointed on the Developers for abandoning the game rather than fix it And the Bugs, OMG! the Bugs there are a crap ton of them in this game so let me mention some of them: - You order a partisan to place a mine, the character goes to the location and does nothing, you need to press again so he does it - You kill someone in enemy view. They go alerted and start searching for you. They fail and return back to their routine, you save and if you load it again, they will AGAIN get alerted and start searching. The AI in this game is super dumb most of the times. - The icons to pick up a body or something is super confusing too, sometimes it works and sometimes it does not - The mouse lag in Inventory is god awful. Sometimes unbearable even, you drag something and have to wait a sec or 2 before moving other stuff - If you issue a kill command with your knife (to include zorin's knife throw) and the enemy soldier moves, your character will just walk there, sit still, and get shot. Other cons include: - Unfinished Base Building- Bad Weapon stat system- I apologize but the English VA is bad in this game, If you know Russian i would highly recommend playing on that - Stealth potions of this game actually sucks - The controls cannot be changed. They can be viewed in the settings but not changed at all.- GOD AWFUL OPTIMIZATION. Low FPS in some missions and random fps jumps everywhere in the game.But credits where credit is deserved. The story was pretty ok, the character were interesting with unique abilities and the ( Russian ) Voice acting was excellent as well, Maps were fun and good layout, The few cutscenes were interesting to watch, the game-play is the strongest part of this game TL;DR i would only highly recommend getting this game if you are super die hard fan of Commandos or Desperados or Shadow tactics game and can bare with bugs and optimization issues. Rest it's a pass from me

_childDocuments_.review: Personal Rating: 8.5 / 10So cool. I never understood why the commandos series did not have any decent follow ups. Partisans moved up and fullfilled every expectation. A cool mix of "be a sneeky hidden bastard", "be a silent stalker-killer" and "all guns blazing" choices (in most cases more than one option works fine) to accomplish the missions leaves noone behind being annoyed because again all you have to do is stay hidden while you obviously prefer to kill those bloody fascist pigs. Each character can be "modified" by boosting certain personal skills but unlike commandos each character is pretty much able to do anything the others can do too (but a little slower / less accurate). Thus that annoying each character is a specialist thing i always disliked while playing commandos got removed. Awesome!Between the missions you'll find a little part of "manage your partisan camp" but it is only a small part, easy to handle and it provides some nice options like building workshops to create certain items or improve your equipment. So this management section does not bother at all. Instead it creates a little bit of an impression that being a partisan has been more about surviving every day instead of fighting the enemy each day in close combat.Finally Partisans is an awesome follow up to my beloved commandos series with hopefully more parts to follow.What i certainly would love to see would be that your decisions have consequences. Like if you do not kill the enemies or use less force the enemy forces could be a little more relaxed thus being less cruel towards the civil population. This could lead to more civilians being friendly with the enemy and reporting the partisans if they spot them. Thus making it harderer to rely on being sneeky only.While on the other hand kiling the enemies would lead to more /more alert and brutal enemy troops while the suffering civilians are more likely to help or at least being silent about your position.Just like during WWII when in many parts of the sowjet empire german troops at first  were greeted as liberators from stalins reign of terror. That drastically changed when the front troops moved on and the race war started.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea of a game, however gameplay is far too frustrating to be uniquely fun in most mission scenarios.Main problem is the stealth and auto-save system. The auto-save system is basically non existent and only auto-saves at the beginning of most missions.Stealth is a huge pile of nit-picks that they combine into one big mess.- Enemies that spot you immediately hive-mind all the other enemies before they even get a word out, this basically means clutch stealth moves will not work.- Stealth only missions are a pain as the hive-mind of the enemies mean you will be trial and erroring and quick-saving 50 times every stealth mission- When your partisan stealth kills an enemy it makes a bit of sound, however if the enemy is a level 2 or higher in difficulty for the partisan to stealth kill, it counts as alerting the enemy even if they are the ONLY ONE there. This fails stealth missions even though the enemy is going to die. I made the mistake of only leveling one partisan's melee kill efficiency at the beginning of the game and not ranking the others (one of which cant even stealth kill but has other ways of distracting the enemy). This made things horrendous to deal with as there is no way to reset skills and for the entire mission until I got to a certain checkpoint which allowed us to be spotted, only 1 partisan was able to kill anyone the entire time because if anyone else did so it would fail the mission despite the only person seeing us was the last guy who was in the process of being stealth killed via an animation. - Enemies seem far too perceptive to the point I cannot tell if its a bug or a feature. The enemies may sometimes just immediately be alerted to a bright red ! without even looking your direction or even filling up a yellow ! above their heads. - There is a lack of variety to stealth mechanics that assist you in missions especially early on, you have bottles, rocks, and one character who can throw a knife a short distance away. You can also hide in certain basements or outhouses and in bushes to get around the enemy, however moving partisans past an enemy is a pain if you have to do it one at a time when killing the enemy isnt an option. Rocks can be hard to come by and are not recoverable when used, same with bottles. The only other option to stealth is to sneak around the enemy as some scenarios make it impossible to take anyone out without being seen. Unfortunately since the game heavily relies on stealth and resource preservation, the stealth mechanics cause a great deal of frustration especially when it is a requirement in missions that will instantly fail you if you are spotted for .1 seconds. Because of this I cannot recommend it as it is a large part of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I both loved and hated this game, and it ended with me ragequitting like 4/5 of my way through. Let me tell you why.So it's the same 'commandos' type of thing you already know about. No secrets there. A good reimagining of it though. Very good actually. The mood and scenarios are well designed, there is a good combination of stealth with a few firefights here and there that feel satisfactory - you know you are not supposed to shoot your way through, sometimes (rarely) it is mandatory but most of the time you can and should avoid it. The uniqueness is the deviousness of the thing. Tripwires, tripmines, makeshift mines, a bear trap.... you can really use some intellingent ways to kill the enemies which feel very rewarding when they work. And if you plan to use your guns, you can position your guys in a way as to, when they finally open fire, the enemies are in such a killbox that everyone is mowed down with a few bullets and that is it. When those things work the sense of satisfaction is great, that's what you expect in an intelligent game. The stealth parts are great to, tho I must say, I mainly always do the same thing, I use my knife-throwing guy combined with my whistle guy whenever I can. Also there is this simple 'base management' thing inbetween missions where you have a stash of weapons, you can craft a few things etc. Like the awesome SILENT STORM (but not nearly as awesome as that... how could it be?). However .... What made me mad is this: So the game kinda tells you, "allright go stealth if you wish, or go brute and shoot it out if you want, just know the first is the right way to do it. But the second one is there for you to do too". Only.... the game spits in your face when it comes to ammo. You see, you loot corpses and the eventual ammo box, but ammo is SO DAMN SCARCE!!!!! I mean it man, you can place a tripwire bomb in  the middle of the road, kill a german patrol of five soldiers - all carrying machineguns! - then search them to gather a grand total of THREE MACHINEGUN BULLETS! THREEEEEE!!!!!!! I AM NOT EVEN EXAGERATING! And it is always like that. Ammo is so ridiculously scarce, you hardly see the point in putting guns in your soldier's hands. I know you are supposed to go stealth as much as you can but that is more than unbalance, that's just bad game design, because there may be times, however rare, that things are going to get hot and you know you can't count on firepower because you simply won't have the ammo for it. I mean it, it is  VERY ENERVING to act like a beggar for bullets all the way through the game, it feels like a bullet hoarding game above everything else. The developers screwed things up here considerably, if ammo was more readily available all over the map, as it should in a place swarming with soldiers, one could gather a lot of it, use it a lot, even if to soon see that it doesnt pay off to use the brute way all the time. But when it really becomes necessary, which it does sometimes... you would have it damn it! That is the problem right there: when you need it, even if you've been hoarding it like Smaug, you don't have enough. Ever. Even nearing the last missions.Case in point. Nearing close to the last mission, and gathering/sving carefully as much ammo as I possibly could, spending it only very sparingly, I was doing a mission with a guy with a rifle and 200 bullets, and two guys with machineguns and ~80 bullets each (all of which I have been painstakingly saving through the last 10 missions!). Thats like two full salvos each, so not much, perhaps some 10 or fifteen seconds of fire and that's it, you're out of ammo. Then this "fend off the attacks!" type of challenge begins. Ok, let's try to be smart about it. I set up tripwires and mines around a chokepoint, position them in smart places, and manage to fend off one frontal attack, then a latteral attack, then another. There was a fixed machine gun I could use so that helped to defeat the first attacks in a smart, ammo-conserving manner. However, they do were shooting a bit so ammo was dropping. THEN ALL THE SUDDEN.... FIVE OR SIX SIMULTANEOUS ATTACKS FROM ALL SIDES, some 20 foes or more, and I was there with two guys having 30 machinegun bullets each having to blast away in all directions, which is perhaps 10 seconds of fire, being attacked from all sides. Needless to say, in a matter of seconds the machinegunners were out of ammo and they were dead.I immediatelly said ON NO FUDGE THIS SHEITTE, ragequit and uninstalled the game. Because that's when being a beggar about bullets all over the past 12 or 15 missions made me realize it was all for nothing if there was to be a situation where I, for once, really needed to use firepower. Well... to sum things up, this game deserves 5 stars but I will give it only 2.5. It will imediatelly rise to 5 if they multiply the amount of available bullets on the map by a factor of 10, so that you can actually have it and use it if the need arises.

_childDocuments_.review: Partisans 1941 is a damn nice recall to the golden days of tactical RTS games like Commando's Desperados and my personal favorite, Robin Hood the Legend of Sherwood. Interestingly crafted missions, objectives and challenges all within the context of WW2 inviting one to explore their own brand of play style and tactical approach. Personally being a Stealth fanatic, I am more than satisfied. Few issues I came across,1.) The characters could use some more fleshing out, not in terms of writing but in terms of game play where as a stealthy approach you would be using only 2 characters with knifes while the rest with their gun based abilities become redundant unless the game forces you to all out fight. Guns blazing moments are few and far between.2.) The stealth features can be glitch out at times when enemies notice you through and this leads to entire screw up of your perfect stealth run.3.) The games forest based HQ or HUB could use with some more features like tasks to gather intel for your next mission which in turn significantly changes how things unfold and this creates some form of replaybility and experimentation.Overall I feel Partisans true to its name and concept encourages more of stealth play and on that note it does deliver. Good fun if you enjoy this kind of thrill.

_childDocuments_.review: No children should fight in a war and no old man should ever see it  twice in one life.Yet, in Partisans 1941 it will happen as you command a group of different resistance members. I would not call them all soldiers because they are not. They are survivors from a war nobody wanted and it's your job to weaken the enemy by taking part in different missions with a good map variety as well diferent objectives with some good optional ones as well.The approach in each mission is really up to you. Full stealth using only your knife during an entire mission, gun-crazy with a variety of rifles, handguns and SMS or an even louder approach with grenades and mines. However the game really shines when you decide to go full stealth or at least stealth without being found (like many games, an yellow exclamation point means they know something's up, a red one means you've been found). I found out the best combo is full stealth with luring techniques. For instance you can use one character to whistle to lure a soldier and another one to use a throwing knife on him making a good combination. You can also create noises or even let a fallen body on a visible way to lure more enemies and when all of them are grouped you toss a grenade or even better a mine right next to that fallen body for maximum damage with a use of a single item.During the game you have more tasks then simply carrying on with these missions. You don't have a base so you will have to build one. For that you will need resources so try to scavange when possible the houses, boxes and closets to find these supplies needed to build a better settlement. You keep what you got after each mission and you have a storage to keep the items so grab what you can so you can have a bigger variety of weapons for different sorts of missions.  As you progress, you will be able to improve and craft weapons as well having a place to smoke food and other surviving necessities. During early in the game I always felt I was a bit short of supplies and food but don't worry, you'll have just enough to get by another day. I believe this is intentional because when you are on the run there's not plenty of food and resources so you need to work with what you can.Speaking of resources you can also find food during your mission but pay attention to what you loot. An icon with a red color means you are about to steal from your own people. While food is critial for your own survival, to steal from your own will decrease your morale. A low morale score will have an impact on the performance of your members. Just stick to scavaging everything you can and leave the rest for those who have even less than you. After all, everyone is a victim of this invasion.After each mission you have some tasks to do in your settlement and stories to listen from your group. These make a nice change of pacing, an opportunity to slow down, calm down, get to know a bit more about each one and a chance to organize your things before going to the next mission. Rumours will also arrive at your settlement, you will read about patrols getting more frequent, soldiers now using more dogs to detect explosives and other intel that puts you inside the world in a more real form.Day and night cicles will have an effect on your enemie's vision so use the darkness of night wisely when available and during day missions don't be afraid of trying different strategies. You can try to kill as little as possible going straight to the goal or go for a more secure but time investing path which focus on eliminating all your enemies in order to sacavanger for supplies freely. Make good use of "accidental" kills when possible. Perhaps that perfect pile of wood is just a push away from falling on a patrol of 3 soldiers, making the perfect "accident" to solve your upcoming path. No matter your playstyle there's plenty of good fun to be had and liberty on how you decide to approach each scenario.

_childDocuments_.review: This game could be good, yet it is hindered by poor UI and AI. It is further missing many standard QoL features typical of games of this type. You cannot, for instance, sort your stored inventory by type, and the inventory screen causes severe stuttering for me mid-game now that I have quite a bit of stuff in there.Clicking on things is a nightmare as your partisans either ignore you or do something entirely unexpected, often to the detriment of the their lives and the mission. The AI.. there is an illusion present wherein the AI seems pretty cool, until one of your partisans catches their attention. Then, suddenly, every enemy knows exactly where every partisan is hiding. They turn almost immediately and start firing at partisans behind them, who are in cover and hiding, as if they knew they were there the whole time.Setting all that aside, the game play can be fun, the story entertaining, and the art and visuals pleasing. In truth, I wish there was a 1-5 star system or a neutral option rather than thumbs up or down. Sadly, given only these two options, I must give it a thumbs down. Get it on sale, but be prepared to save and reload regularly as you account for the poor pathfinding, difficulty getting your partisans to do what you want when you want, and try to play what could have been a pretty good game rather than the frustrating and flawed gem we have now.

_childDocuments_.review: Partisans is a good game, but it isn't a flawless game. Controlling the actions of your partisans can be complicated. It is probably meant to be easy and/or controller friendly, but in reality it is annoying to use and sometimes flat out impossible. Also, vision cones don't always accurately show what the AI can see. The game generally does a good job explaining various mechanics, but it isn't always clear how various mechanics actually work for various types of enemies. Trial and error seems to be required and if things do go wrong, there is a plethora of options to go 'loud'. The missions are engaging and fun to play. Level design makes sense and, with the exception of some later ones, does not feel 'bloated' like desperados III. The story is garbage Russian revisionist history. Jewish people don't seem to exist. Partisans are portrayed as white knights in shining armour. Germans are portrayed as sadistic, evil brutes. The painful irony is that the protagonist would have been a victim of the Gulag system after the war since he starts the game as a POW. The Soviet brutality is not even mentioned in passing. The commissar who makes his appearance later on is portrayed as a grizzled fighter rather than the useless waste of space commissars usually were in historical reality. (Their sole job was to keep the fighting men ideologically 'pure' and loyal to Stalin. They were the ones ratting out people, for both real and imagined failings.) Apart from this, the story is apallingly bad as a story. The game doesn't need the story, though. Partisans has some rpg elements to it, as well. Your partisans level up along the way and you get to loot weapons, food and equipment during the missions. You have to build your base as well and manage food and morale. It is largely meaningless. It is easy to manage. It is a nice touch you need to loot everything you need, as it adds an authentic touch. Partisans wouldn't be normally in any kind of position to receive supplies. This aspect could be very interesting, but it needs more than a little bit of work. Especially the fact that killed soldiers drop random loot rather than the weapon they use is absolute nonsense. What makes this game great regardless of the above is the fact both stealth and guns truly work. If you want to ambush patrols with grenades and smg's: you can do so. If you want to sneak your way through, this works too, with some notable exceptions. The game is at its worst when large numbers of enemies are spawned and thrown at you in waves. (Easily dealt with through mines.) The combat relies heavily on cover. The AI is more than capable and should not be underestimated. As most commandos type games, nobody seems to care much if fellow soldiers disappear one by one. Officers do mind, though, and following searches can quickly escalate to nasty gun fights. Ultimately, as an avid commandos fan, I loved playing my way through the missions that despite the cringe worthy story nearly always feel meaningful. I just wish there were a few more missions to play through. Despite the fact I am a slow and careful player who combes through every nook and cranny, I finished the game in under 40 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun, albiet really difficult and the AI can be kind of stupid and variable beyond belief, as well the enemies are often alerted to your forces positions during attack despite seeing no one.Unfortunately my game glitched during the last mission and only one of my characters will move. The other two are stuck and won't move until attacked, which is an impossible scenario in a stealth game. I'd hoped to finish the game by tonight but I guess not. TLDR: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that you'd give a "mixed" review.Partisans strives to be like Commandos, Desperados or even Shadow Tactics (which is from the same publisher incidentally), which are the pinnacle in this genre.However, it fails to achieve this level of greatness, yet it's still fun to play through for the most part.The main meat of the game are of course the missions, 15 in total (+ some standalone missions if you want to). In between you will "manage your base", which is nothing to really highlight. You have to gather food and supplies, raid enemy encampments automatically to get weapons and ammo, craft basic explosives, etc.Each partisan you gather during your playthrough has his or her own skill tree, is better with certain weapons, better at stealth or just a mean killing machine.Gameplay, however, revolves around stealth for the most part. You CAN go in guns blazing, but that's risky, since alarming one guard often alarms the entire map, meaning you have to contend with 50+ enemies, and you're just going to be outgunned, even with heavy weapons and grenades. Your partisans will also get injured (they can't die, unless all of them die). Since ammo is rather scarce this isn't the preferred way of playing the game, but sometimes open conflict is unavoidable, so cover is important, since it reduces the chance to be hit by a lot. Especially SMGs are totally useless in these sort of situations though, since you'll just burn through ammo without hitting anything.I'd always favour the dedicated melee characters, with which you can lure enemies and take them out rather easily. Unless the enemy AI just decides to not give a ♥♥♥♥ about it. This game follows a very peculiar design choice, in which enemies will not always follow set paths, but do whatever they want. This is especially noticeable when you load a quick save and realize the enemy has done something completely different than last time ... or that time has skipped forward 2 to 3 seconds for no apparent reason (I can only explain this by believing the game isn't synced with the actual loading times). This leads to you doing the exact same thing with wildly different outcomes. Especially terrible are the "don't get spotted" missions, where it's sometimes enough for an isolated enemy to see you for a fraction of a second before he dies. You have to time your kills absolute perfectly, unless you want the whole camp to be alerted. To make it short: There is a disconnect between what is happening on screen and what is happening behind closed curtains. Also, screw the dogs.The AI has another problem though. It's just plain stupid. I've had enemies see a corpse, freak out and immedietaly know where I am, despite having no way of knowing where I am. In other instances they didn't find me at all, despite a dog literally standing 1 feet away from me and having me sniffed out, only to completely freak out again when they "discover" the corpse AGAIN (happened after a load ... you'd think they'd at least remove the body or that they'd stay alert forever). I've also had enemies just not react to my lures ... enemies that suddenly turn around though they've never done that before ... and enemies that just run into a wall, all agitated, only for me to kill them all in bewilderment with 1 of my guys, who can kill several at once.Level layout is generally good, but missions always end up being played the same way: Sneak from bush to bush and kill isolated enemies. In Shadow Tactics for example you have different characters that can fulfill different roles, in Partisans I often needed 2 guys to do the job 1 guy should be able to. I've also frequently had commands not register and my guys generally doing whatever they wanted.Atmosphere and the, I guess, original Russian language is superb though, even the German Russian accents. Most of it is flawless, which considering Daedalic is a German company I'd expect (when it comes to German). Overall a pretty decent game for the asking price. But nothing you will play more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: I came to fight Nazis, but the greater foe was the UI.Out of every 10 reloads, at least half are due to an action that was prevented or enabled by a UI that, two dozen hours in, I still haven't gotten the hang of.  I wanted to like this game, with its cool concept and squad-stealth RPG aspirations, but the lack of polish across the board keeps this from shining like it should.  In increasing order of pettiness: it also crashes, the pathfinding is 1990's level, and all the Soviets are British.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: After 40 hours, I have not finished the game yet but I already plan to get the DLC for extra missions and to support the developpers. I'm very happy to see such a polished and high quality game on the topic of the Great Patriotic War. Contrary to games like "Commandos", the context and story of this game will make you really care about your partisans. As with real-life partisans, you will see that the characters come from different social or ethnic backgrounds, and they don't even always have the same political views, but they are all working together and fighting for their motherland. To better enjoy the game, I strongly recommend foreigners to play with the original voices in Russian rather than English dubbing. I really hope the developpers will release a sequel to "Partisans 1941", in the future, but I'm already very grateful to them. Большое спасибо !
