_childDocuments_.review: Partisans 1941 is game that will make you tired after couple hours of playing. There are many reason why this game is not good. I'll try to make it as short as I can. Developers tried to create an interesting plot, but there was nothing special. The thing that I actually liked is that developers tried to make characters interesting and have a background story with biography.Every playable character has it special ability, that allows you to attack the enemies in various ways, which, allows you to kind of use different play styles.The game provides a good atmosphere, where is shown the soviet union during which, the Germany attacked and occupied the territories. The music that is the same and annoying, yet kind of classic for that time also conveys that atmosphere, but definitely not the mood.There are not many games with this genre. Again, we know Commandos series, shadow tactics etc. so I always give a chance to games like this. Developers created a game with the niche genre.The first reason is the amount of game bugs this game has. It was a big pain playing it. Sometimes, textures would start having a seizure, sometimes other stuff.The second reason is how the game is optimized... deplorable. The game sometimes runs 60 fps when it wants, sometimes it runs 20-30 fps. I noticed that it happened on exactly the same locations. I turned on the fps counter and when I looked at the map it showed me (you won't believe) over 42 000 FPS. The game has a lovely feature of randomly crashing, so if you didn't do a quick save, you will lose your playthrough.Clunky control, where characters do not do the things you directly ask them to do. Sometimes, they just do whatever the hell they want. You press the place where you want him to stand? Well this idiot will pick up a dead body. You want the guy to reload the weapon? Sometimes, he doesn't feel like to do that. There are way too many similar situations.I really did not like the way, there are dialogues. I played in russian language, since I know it pretty well, so why wouldn't I play the game about soviet partisans in russian. This game feels such a big time propaganda... I did not like it.The soundtrack of the game is poor and not memorable. I actually remember only 1 soundtrack, that is pretty annoying and still playing in my head. Commandos, the game that was developed in 2001, had more than 25 music, that I still remember to this day. Boring level design, most of the missions and maps were not memorableLooting system has not meaning in this game as once you get couple weapons, you really do not need to spend your time in checking what is the difference between weapons, it just does not matter, because they are all the same. The difference is that the good quality weapon of course is better, but once you get it, you do not need to loot.Not a good game, because I honestly, did not enjoy most of the aspects of the game, because of the things that I remembered, was the negative experience. Luckily, I bought it with discount. NOT RECOMMENDED3/10

_childDocuments_.review: A very fun RTT, strategy, WWII, stealth game. You, a Army Commander are taken behind enemy lines as a prisoner of war. You escape certain death and sneak your way to some partisans. You lead your team to guerilla warfare against the occupying German forces. A very good game with great art style. Great interface, graphics and story. Well worth any price they have it at.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: My overall recommendation is rather neutral, it started out fantastic but overtime a few things that are done VERY VERY POORLY and lead to huge frustration:- Map design/camera: Pathing extremely poorly reflected to the user. There are times where you see a gap where they supposedly can go through, instead they go around the map because the "path" is actually artificially blocked by the level designer with some small boxes. (you can see the paths in "tactical mode" but realistically you will not use it everytime you issue an order)- Stealth ONLY missions: why do they even exist? Lets be clear, you INSTANTLY get "Game Over" the moment you use guns/grenades, or a body is discovered. This is the biggest reason I do not want to replay this game ever again, stealth is fun at first; after a few missions, you realize you can only bait-kill-hide body one enemy at a time.I want to play the game my way, this is reflected in the skill trees of every characters, they all have stealth skills and gun skills. it's a chore/grind to go through groups of enemies placed at chokepoints for artificially prolonging the missions.- Inconsistent AI response: AI responds/pathing is different everytime the same action is done. There is no real way for the player to strategize, but to experiment with quick save/load- inventory UI/management: for example, why same ammo doesn't get grouped and stacked automatically but have to be done manually? Why can I not discard junks later to make space?This management is extremely annoying and tedious- Cover: sometimes you click where you want them to take cover and they take the wrong side.- Controls: additional key bindings need to be in options- Camera: additional free-camera movements is REALLY NEEDED, you can't see how the enemy detects you through 2 windows until they did because you CANNOT tilt the camera much lower.- And I feel like they can tell me beforehand when some missions are totally pure gunfights or pure stealth (if you get detected it's game over), so I bring the characters with correct skills and correct equipments!! (like loads of stones/bottles? or med kits?)But I really love some aspects in this game.The graphics are great.The optimization is great except one minor issue I encountered in 8 hours.The voice acting is phenomenal. I use Russian voices.The gameplay is solid for the most part, albeit sometimes frustrating, but it's SP game with savescumming.The minor base-managing, level-up for skills RPG elements are also fun.Indie game being what it is, there are much polishing to do still.

_childDocuments_.review: Great tactical game, allows more freedom than commando's or shadow tactics which tend to be quite restrictive and require you to play a certain way. _childDocuments_.review: I am only 8 hours in the game but what I've seen is damn impressive. Typical guerilla war game is either us destroying everything with our small squad, or stealth puzzle game. This game definitely gives the vibe of the second type, plus given recent success of Desperados 3 and Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun, it only makes more sense.However, these games somehow managed to marry both types, giving you a sandbox experience. You like to set up ambushes, put mines around you and shoot from an advantageous position? Go ahead! You want to sneak by most of the guards? Possible too! The best part, I think, is that you can pick your squad for every mission: they give you a clue what to expect there, and some missions require stealth/assault, but overall you are free to go as you please.Base management is also very nice so far: I like that you can't buy anything, so I have to choose between a chance for a better gun or to get more resources to improve existing ones. So, if you are into tactical stealth games + something like Men of War, definitely get this game. It has some bugs, and many QoL things are missing, but nothing gamebreaking.I am just really excited as we don't often get games of such genre!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like XCOM, you'll probably like this. If you like Hitman, you'll probably like this. Partisans plays out sort of like a blend of those two formulas (though it takes place in real time, not turn-based like XCOM). It is not as hardcore (no permadeath; if your partisans die you get a game over and must reload a save) but the same ideas are present.The game is oriented towards stealth, but open combat is a viable option as well. A weird thing to grapple with is that enemies 50 feet away are not alerted to your explosions and gun battles, so you can remain "undetected" despite the fact that you blew up 5 Nazis with a mine and left their bodies in the road. And the AI doesn't really stop to think why their fellows seem to be going missing one by one - an officer turns his back for one minute and just like that his crony is gone. Oh well, nothing to see here. A little weird, but these levels are so big that it would be pretty much impossible to remain truly undetected the whole time. And playing that way would bias your gameplay towards only 1 or 2 partisans and their particular skills (knife throwing, choloroform). So it's good that there is still a place for the character who can mow down a dozen Nazis at once with a machine gun.

_childDocuments_.review: Partisans 1941 – Guerrilla Warfare at Its Finest! 🎖️🌲Partisans 1941 drops you straight into the heart of World War II, where stealth, strategy, and a bit of guerrilla magic collide! This real-time tactics game is like a thrilling chess match where your pieces can sneak, ambush, and outsmart the enemy. 🕵️‍♂️⚔️As an army commander behind enemy lines, you’re not just playing with numbers; you’re crafting a team of diverse partisans, each with their own unique skills and stories. Whether it’s planting traps, laying low in the shadows, or launching surprise attacks, every decision counts! 💥🌿The immersive environments beautifully capture the tension of the Eastern Front, and the tactical gameplay keeps you on your toes. _childDocuments_.review: Formula of the game: Shadow Tactics + WW2 setting + Russian "Great Patriotic War" propagandistic narrative + "quality" of Russian gamedev.This game was clearly aimed at Russian audience first and foremost, it has soul and atmosphere, and those are something that got the most love from the devs. Russian voice actors did a fantastic job, so did the artists and the composer. If I were revieving this in Russian, I'd probably have given it a thumbs up after all.And yet, if one refrains from aforementioned subjectivity and evaluates this game for what it is, things are much less pleasant.1) Very buggy and unpolished, with bugs ranging from mild annoying to major feature-breaking ones.2) Nonexistent balance, with some characters having lots of OP abilities at once, and others being absolutely useless.3) Totally dumb AI which makes laying huge minefields on every level your main tactic - make some noise and whole level will happily run into these, in a nice tighly packed groups of 5+ enemies, no less!4) Stealth is broken at worse and frustrating at best, meaning the most non-annoying way to play is to kill everyone on the level - meaning no replayability.5) Game is pretty short and mechanics like base management are only there to artificially extend the playtime.6) The story is pretty generic, no love given towards character development or similar. Instead, there's a lot of "patriotic" black-white propaganda, like the game going out of its way to make you hate polizei (your own people) more than Nazis and to actually force you to kill all of them, either giving you xp for that or outright making that your level objective. Polizei are exclusively presented as looters, thieves and murderers, which is ahistorical and makes no sense. Long story short, while the game copied gameplay and features of games like Shadow Tactics diligently, it is much less polished&balanced, and you are not likely to enjoy it unless you're a Russian player with a thing for the atmosphere and the narrative.

_childDocuments_.review: I want to recommend this game, but I can't in good conscious. There are so many little problems that are completely unacceptable for a real time tactics game that it just ruins the experience.tl;dr There are a ton of bugs; bad gameplay mechanics; glitchy and poorly designed AI; and poor performance. I do not recommend Partisans 1941.There are two distinct parts to this game: combat/tactics, and base-building.This is where the core of the game lies. You are a Russian partisan group behind enemy lines during the invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941. Your goal is to kill german soldiers and those that work with them (Polizei in the game). You also have missions around stealing information, blowing up bridges, etc.Not sure:Between missions you go back to your base and can do things like:I really want to like this game. I have played RTT games on and off for a while and the setting for this one is fun. However, this is poorly implemented with lazy AI development and obvious problems with performance and bugs. The AI is far too rigid and doesn't include anything beyond "AI sees you". No object permanence, no change in routines, no background events, etc.I will likely keep playing the game through because I can't return it at this point, but ultimately I do not recommend this game for others.

_childDocuments_.review: The main premise the devs had for it is you use a combination of stealth and combat to finish your missions, but that is utterly wrong. Because the correct answer is you can only use stealth and getting into combat is not rewarding and utterly detrimental to your success. - Going stealth is always better. If you fire a single shot almost entire map will rush to your position, the germans are much better at shooting your guys vs. your guys ability to shoot them back. Which makes sense to a degree, because they are a professional army but its a bit ridiculous to see your partisan with shotgun repeatedly failing to hit someone 5 meters infront of them outside of cover. Even if you somehow miraculously manage to survive you will get hard to cure injuries, wounds. So only time you might want to get in combat is when you almost cleared the entire map.- Maps arent designed well. To compare, in shadow tactics blades of shogun, maps are designed like a puzzle that you have to solve. You will need to use the correct char at the correct time and sometimes multiple characters in combination to make it work. And you gain satisfaction of solving a hard puzzle when you managed to overcome it. In this game its not much of a puzzle but more like finding the starting point of a knot. After finding it you just rip it open by mindlessly following that path. Killing and passing by soldiers one by one easily.In short, this is a game that tried to have a hybrid gameplay but failed at both of them.  Not recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love this game but there are too many flaws in the gameplay that make it really hard to play and not in a good way.1. The detection system is bad. It is hypersensitive and enemies sometimes even see through walls. On other occasions they don't detect the characters at all, even when they're right in front of them. This makes stealth missions (of which there are a few) almost unplayable.2. The ammo is highly limited, which can be a good thing if balanced otherwise but in most cases it's not even worth using guns at all and just rely on things like knife throwing or explosives which have a 100 % chance to hit and in the case for knifes are even unlimited and in the case of explosives are usually abundant.3. The food system is not very well implemented and it takes a while to get used to as it's not explained properly. To get more food you can either just rely on the 1 x free food gathering per day or you can build a kitchen. If you build a kitchen, not only does it take time and resources but also you'll have to spend food to get food.4. The pathfinding of your characters is atrocious. They'll rather run around three corners directly into enemy sight instead of the slightly longer way around enemies. That would be fine if the characters would be controlled more directly. But this way you have to rely on the terrible pathfinding.4.5 Related to the pathfinding is that sometimes when you select more than one character to be in the same spot behind cover for example, one character will stay behind the cover while the other just runs to the other side. You can't be more precise because you can't really scroll in too much. 5. Abilities are incredibly unbalanced. While most of them are quite cool ideas, they're not very well executed. The already mentioned knife throwing is a guaranteed one hit kill if you're close enough (and again you have to rely on the terrible pathfinding here) which is unlimited as long as you don't forget to pick up your knife (makes sense eh?). Well that logic applies to most ablities, you have a certain cooldown and you can use it afterwards again. BUT WAIT, without telling it in the skill description some of the ablities have limited use. This might not be too bad if it was limited use per mission and it would have to "recharge" again until you leave for the partisan camp but no, they're limited use per character until the end of the game. 3 uses of the same ability you didn't even know had a cooldown? Well you're out of luck now, can't use the ability anymore.6. The "natural" boundaries in the maps not only feel incredibly unnatural and generally bad. The characters can perform all kinds of stunts but are completely incapable when they're supposed to go up the slightlest of slopes.7. The AI is just weird and overpowered, no matter the difficulty really. I appreciate some challenge but I want it to feel fair which it doesn't here. The AI always exactly knows where you are when one character has been seen by anyone, even if the reporter is being killed before they can shoot. This also ties in with the problem that using guns to quickly take out enemies is essentially useless because, even when enemies are outside of hearing range, they still will know what happened. Additionally enemies often manage to onehit characters, even if the characters are in cover.It's obvious that enemies aren't characters like the player characters and more random number generators, which I always dislike in games.The game has a lot of potential but it is very much unpolished and I doubt it can be fixed, even if the devs wanted to. It's not like the game feels like a cashgrab, it definitely has potential and the setting is somewhat unique.

_childDocuments_.review: It is quite interesting to find the way to clear each map. Setting and history is also very good.As for the bugs, I encountered 2 of them: 1) got achievement of killing 3 enemies with 1 mine by killing 1 enemy and 2 partisans (my mistake, but got the achievement); 2) on the map where we should find grandfather of Sanek, in the top (where secret loot is), while going back, partisans cannot move in one corner (just tell them run from secret loot to the plane, you'll see). Update: bonus missions in DLS do not fit the story, as there are no camp, only partisans to select and limited number of skills. From my opinion, it is not good.In total, I really like the game!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is very buggy and is also poorly optimized. And yet I reccomend it to people who love this genre because if you can overlook the issues, you'll surely enjoy the game. While Mimimi has the Desperados series covered, this is still the best alternative to the Commandos series in recent times. The game uniquely gives you some control over how to develop your squad members, whom to bring to which mission, and what resources to bring to the mission. It also has a camp-management feature. And thankfully, despite the several bugs, very few are game-breaking. In fact, the only kinda-game-breaking bug that I have found is that some choices are not reset after you reload a save. This might affect how many times you can use sepcial skills of the Partisans, which are limited use, and might prevent you from using the skill you wanted in any given situation. In most cases, you can switch to an alternative path, unless the mission requires stealth and your stealth skills are bugged out (i.e. disabled). Given the overall positive recenption of the game, it is a pity that the developers abandonned this promising game in such a poor state.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this game up on sale and I can only encourage other people to do so as I really enjoyed it for a game I picked up under £4. There are some bugs and other issues in game but for the price you pay when on sale, you can easily get over them and keep on keeping on!The campaign has a good number of missions and when playing them on hard, you will defiantly be challenged as you cannot save your progress mid mission when playing on hard.There is also a missions part of the game which but I am yet to play through these.If you like top down strategy games and can spare a few quid when on sale, I would highly recommend this game...here's hoping to a Partisans 2!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I love this type of game set in the WWII era. I played the hell out of Commandos back in the day. I lasted about 30 minutes in this game. I just could not over the frustrating camera controls. WHY can't you use the mouse and the Q/E keys to control the camera. I hate the W,A,S,D option to control the camera, I like to use the mouse. So yes there is an option to use the mouse to control the camera, but now with that option, you can't rotate the camera? Thats just crazy. I want to play this game, but too frustrating with the wonky controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: I have two complaints:1) Easy Mode as well as the other difficulties should have the correct resource scaling. It seems that despite the difficulty, you'll never have enough ammo. I find or earn a lot of guns only to have them sit in the camp's inventory due to a chronic lack of ammo. I get the simulation of being a rag-tag bunch of guerrillas having to scrounge around for scraps and pennies, but is it too much of an ask that when I knife kill a German or Polizei that I can loot ALL of the ammo on them? Even worse, on some missions where I clean sweep the entire map I'm rewarded to find no secret armory or stash and no central supply depot? Would be really cool to make munitions runs or something, you know, or re-visit previously cleared locations to do so after the battle.2) Probably the first time I've seen every single enemy unit with laser-eyed X-ray vision and wall hacks that immediately run to my Partisans hidden in a bush or hidey-hole the very millisecond they see something suspicious. I highly doubt there's coding for the enemy AI to enter an "alarm phase" or "searching mode" at all. It just skips straight into: "here's where the player is; engage in shootout." At no point did it feel like: "Welp. Gotta hide until they either give up or clear the area so I can sneak past." Instead it's always: *quick load*. This wouldn't be so bad of a problem (although still an incredibly annoying one) if I had the AMMO to survive a shootout.  I get that punishing stealth game blah blah blah, but many other (better!) stealth games have a smarter AI behavior like Sniper Elite, Crysis, Metal Gear Solid, even Thief and The Dark Mod. In those games, if you make a mistake you can still salvage the situation if you simply avoid getting spotted again and wait for the AI to cool off or instead work around the enemy that's now suspiciously searching for you. But having the AI home in on your EXACT position like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ JDAM despite not ever seeing you hiding in a bush is incredibly frustrating and not fun. Minor flub = instantaneous game-ending failure with no chance to recover the situation is not fun. At this point it's not really a stealth game, but a Quick Save/Load Simulator.Russian voice acting sounds fine tho...
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good stealth title in the style of the Commandos series, set in the Soviet Union on the Eastern Front of World War II. It manages to handle such a bleak time in history with care, showing the depravity of the Nazi regime while not coming across as just an ultra nationalistic romp on the Soviet side that a lot of war films and media tend to do. You are partisans, guerrilla fighters trying to survive and push the fascist invaders out. I highly recommend using the native language with subtitles for immersion, as it's weird having Soviets with English accents and Germans well, not speaking German.Over the course of the game you'll get around eight partisans over the course of the campaign who all have different strengths to help you on your mission. You'll be scavenging for resources and eventually have a home base of your own where you gather food, go out on reconnaissance and craft needed supplies and even upgrade your weapons. There's even a level up system and since you do get experience per kill, it can be worth it to kill as many guards and collaborators as you can, though the experience does provide diminishing returns for balance reasons. Plus in stealth games I find it usually better to get rid of as many enemies as you can to avoid yourself headaches later in a mission.One nice thing about this game is you have the option to 'go loud' in shootouts if you end up being detected though it's highly recommended to do this towards the end of a mission once you've thinned out their ranks. You are often outnumbered and out gunned and can get injured and killed quite easily. You can slow down time to coordinate the perfect ambush. I can't describe how satisfying it is throwing grenades, setting up mines and tripwires and mowing down your enemies with surgical precision. Then slipping away like you were never there.It's a bit buggy however and the dlc is definitely in a rougher quality than the main game. Definitely worth checking this game out as I think this game is a hidden gem. As with all stealth games, quick save and quick load are your friend. Good luck and good hunting.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game, with a gameplay just like classics such as Shadow Tactics and Desperados III, but with much more stealth. You have to be patient to play Partisans, cause almost always you will just walk, crouched, from one hidding spot to another, mapping the place carefully to make kills one-by-one. It's really challenging. I also liked the ambience, the russian and german chats, the storytelling, the design choices...can´t recommend enough to all RTT players.

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: It is a Commandos game mixed with kindergarten version of XCOM.Is it good? Yes.Does it worth it? Yes.It is short, ~20 hours ehen playing mostly stealth.Could it be better? Yes.Will play again? After I replay Desperados 3, Commandos (all except 4), Shadow Tactics, I will play Partizan 1941 again. It is in the cycle.давай? да.Am I Russian? No.If you want stealth it is as good as commandos.If you play wanna shoot people, action is better than commandos 3Is it buggy? Hell yeah.- Once one of my character looked like shooting but did not shoot at all. Rifle was jammed even though the game does not have such mechanic.- All of the dogs, anywhere in the map start to search you if any dog starts to search you.- One time a dead body decided to get under a box after quickload, which became uncarriable.  - Officers get confused after quickload.- Some assets are not translated from Russian. Seen only twice in 20 hours and didn't effect the game.Played the game in normal mode:What I liked:- I like games with operations with small teams with different abilities.- Liked the character development.- Liked the behaviours of different enemies.(Especially dogs and officers)- Liked real time fights of this game even though I didn't like the games with similar real time fights(Tyranny Pathfinder Kingmaker).What I did not like:- I only played with 3 characters and didn't need to use others. - Injuries do not have any affect at all after the mission.- Always had more than enough food and supply, the game would be the same without these.- Morale never dropped from very high.- Watching the camp gives satisfaction while the actions that we can do at the camp feels like empty.- Some assets are not ready, one of the enemy commander(forgot the name of the character) had a portrait with graphic quality of Wolfenstein 3D(1992). Conclusion:I liked it, I would like it even more if the game would force me to use other characters. Also actions in the camp and resources should affect the game more. I believe they wanted to make is as good as XCOM about resources and decisions etc. but they needed to release the game so they left it like a kindergarden version of XCOM. Bugs will be fixed. They were not affecting the gameplay that much anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome real time tactical game with huge focus on stealth. The mechanics of the game are truly fun and sometimes make you feel like you are playing a sandbox tactical game in which you just kill german soldiers in a way YOU want and YOU prefer. You can kill everyone without them even noticing you, go guns glazin' style and just shoot everyone, set traps and make them try to find what that was while you sneak behind their backs and so much more. It is really awesome how rich the tactical side of this game is. One of the best things the game offers is the  that slows time and lets you choose what to do with each of your partisans. The game has a big potential for replayability with it's many ways of achieving a goal of a mission (the tactics, the skills of the partisans or the selection of partisans you made in the beginning of the misson). Every partisan has something unique...but I think that everyone will have their most favourite set of 3 partisans like I do. The pre-missoin phases inside the camp is a nice way of gaining resources and experience even tho later in the game it is the "boring" part of the game. I was able to find quite a lot of bugs for this kind of a game but nothing too serious. The only thing I really hate about this game is tha fact that you have to buy a 10€ DLC to be able to play a defence game mode...Over all I give Partisans 1941 solid

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets worse the more you play it. There are characters that get stuck in bushes after cutscenes. Items that can't be pick up after being placed. Characters falling in the water and getting stuck in the water. You have bandages that you can't use sometimes too for no reason, even though you want to heal your almost dead partisans.The enemy knows exactly where you are if put them on red alert, even if you are far, far away from them and hiding. They literally run you down no matter where you go or may be hiding. This means throwing a grenade and then running to a hiding spot, unseen the whole time, while your whole team is no where near the scene, also hiding, is not a valid option; they'll all get outnumbered in seconds by every soldier on the map and killed instantly that way. In other words, guerilla warfare is not something you can do in this game, even though these partisans seem willing and equipped to do that in this game. It's either full stealth or epic firefight.There's inconsistencies in the gameplay. Sometimes your character will go for the stealth kill no problem. Other times they get really close to the enemy and start shooting, get into melee combat instead or stand there, both ways sounding the alarm. Same with enemy vision. Some enemies don't see you in their cone and you know its safe. Other times they 'see you' and sound the alarm, even though the enemy cones clearly don't see your character. Things are also unclear. At the camp, the missions have a supply icon of 50. I have 30 supplies and want more supplies. I go on the mission. The next day I neither earn nor lose supplies, even though I succeeded in the mission. Why is that supply Icon of 50 there if I neither lose nor gain 50 supplies by completing it? Missions you play are also unclear. In the tank mission, the captain doesn't mention that we need a bomb, or that we need to find one, meaning you're going to spend a lot of time confused and roaming the map wondering how and where you get a bomb for the tank. Same with the mission with the blonde partisan woman where you have to find the village chief. You find him, you get in his face, you're there again confused for a while not knowing that you have to kill the all the enemies here and there around him to interact with him. The player still has to figure out what you need to do in the mission even though there are mission objectives written out. Basic features that you may have seen in other games like Desperados 3 or Shadow Tactics are also missing here. The radius of how much noise your weapons make are unknown to you, meaning you have to guess and test yourself if others will hear your guns, knives and explosions. The camera also gives you the choice to either have the ability to rotate the camera with Q E or to move the camera up-down-left-right with the mouse. You can't pick both, but the game would be smoother with both. It's yes or no one or the other. Characters that get shot next to or on top of another body will pretty much die because the revive button is the same as the pick up button, the loot button and the cover button. So once the enemies that shot him go away and you get to him, the guy is going to do die before you can pick up all the bodies around him and put them somewhere else. This is the mechanic that will piss you off the most and drive you away from the game out all these issues.All of this along with playing it on hard mode, which gives you zero saves for usually hour long missions and you have a progressively frustrating and raging experience. You're going to spend hours and days on single missions since it's already natural to mess up on top of all these issues hindering you. You have to do the missions over and over until you get it down perfect, with no characters stuck in place bugs, no pointless deaths because you can't click on your dying teammate, and more (There are still more bugs and problems I didn't mention on top of what I already listed).The game is still fun, being able to customize character equipment, immersing yourself in a chill, stealth experience thanks to the music and style, being on edge which bullet will hit who during the occasional firefight, and simple management at your base. Unfortunately, I would not recommend this game to others to experience this rage inducing jank. In fact, as much as I like this game and genre and want to complete a single playthrough, my interest is dying because of the above issues cockblocking the completion of my endless attempts playing the same missions (the big betty mission especially). After dozens of hours, days in a row playing through the same mission then having to start over just because of something like a body on my partisan being in the way reviving him in time, just because he got caught at the end of the mission picking up a body. Your temper will explode too when this happens to you. Game's been out for about two years too from this review, so I would assume most if not all of these issues should have been fixed by now. Find a different game or heed my warning please. Thanks for reading my review.

_childDocuments_.review: Quite honestly, this is a brilliant game idea executed to near perfection. It is as though XCOM was turned into a real-time, stealth-based World War II guerilla simulator. I thoroughly have enjoyed the stealth mechanics in this game. The first time I pulled off a double stealth execution from some bushes and then quickly dragged the bodies to a hiding spot before an approaching patrol noticed anything was awry was extremely satisfying.The missions are engaging, interesting and unique; however, this may be my one source of grievances. This game forces you to play how it wants you to. Most missions, thus far, dictate how you approach everything. I cannot choose to only ambush small patrols, or liberate prisoners from Nazi camps. Every mission is dictated, scripted and imposed upon the player-- practically railroading you into a specific style of play.An additional area that feels slightly lackluster is the Partisan camp. The resource management aspect of the game, and assigning various tasks to Partisans feels somewhat shallow. It is almost if I am just given the facade of having real control over this band of fighters. Despite the negatives detailed above, this a great game with good bones. If I were able to choose how my group of guerilla soldiers fought, where they fought, and when they fought, this may be the perfect game. I look forward to future iterations or any updates for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: A decent enough Commandos-like if that's what you're looking for.Be aware that this is much closer to the original Commandos than it is to games like Shadow Tactics, that have done huge work to refine the formula in terms of systems, UI design and enemy AI. If you've played some of those more modern games, you may have been spoiled and could find it difficulty to go back to something like Partisans, which is rather rough around the edges.The base management layer of the game is barely worth mentioning. It scarcely affects anything and quickly becomes an unnecessary exercise in clicking just to get to the next mission.The biggest shortcomings to be aware of are the UI and the enemy AI. On the UI front, controls are fiddly, and the outcome of your actions is often unclear. Sometimes you'll be detected for unknown reasons, and the game does little to show you things like sound raidus *before* you take an action. That means there's lots of trial and error involved.The enemy AI is just straight up bad. On finding an enemy corpse, sometimes they'll telepathically know exactly where all your partisans are, others they'll just stand there like idiots until the alert timer runs down. They also straight up can't handle indoor environments, regularly getting stuck in doorways, but thankfully most of the game takes place outside. This dodgy AI also makes the forced stealth sections a chore.The really interesting twist here is that, unlike most games in the genre, combat is actually a viable option. When things get loud, the game actually handles tactical, cover-based combat pretty well. It just adds  a bit of welcome variety to proceedings.All in, killing your way through maps full of Nazis is as satisfying as it's ever been, bugs and shonky AI aside.

_childDocuments_.review: The core gameplay concept can be described as " meets ". I love it. On most missions, the game lets you decide whether to take the stealthy approach or let the guns speak. I like to combine both approaches... quietly take out the ones that would outflank you once the bullets fly, then carefully take up covered positions around the rest of them and finally take 'em down in a crossfire. Gunfights are very dynamic and positions have to be changed when enemies try to outflank you or find cover of their own, which keeps you on the edge of your seat until the last enemy drops dead.The game may not be perfect - inventory management can get a little tedious sometimes and the whole base building thing doesn't seem fully developed, but the core gameplay is great fun.

I would suggest to enlarge the tooltip text and have a bit more tooltips so the userd doesnt have to figure out what an icon means.I rarely get sucked into games and this one was just an absolute joy to play so far (19 hours). 100% worth the buy and i will be buying the DLC as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome - buy it!Why?If you enjoyed playing Commandos back in the day, then this is the closest thing you're going to see to a fully modernised sequel.This is the 3rd game in the same genre from Daedalic after Shadow Tactics - Blades of the Shogun and Desperados III. If you enjoyed either of those then you're going to enjoy this.For me this is the best real-time tactics game Daedalic have released so far. It goes further than their previous titles by adding in a home base where you can build up your camp, make food, modify weapons and go on interim missions to gain resources for crafting. Now this aspect of the game isn't very developed as yet and is a bit simplistic, but it adds a new dimension to the genre and gives the campaign missions a feeling of continuity as the resources and weapons that you scrounge during a mission can be taken back to base and shared among your group of partisans.The graphics are excellent, although I'd like the zoom to be able to zoom in a little closer.Controls are pretty good, though as usual with these games the characters don't always do eaxctly what you tell them and they sometimes go loud when you don't intend them to. However in Easy and Normal modes you can save and load at any time and the save/load times are very quick so it's easy to re-load a save if it all goes pear shaped.I'm not a big fan of story based games, but the story in this one is pretty good. Historical accuracy is also good.This is one of those games where I felt trult saddened when it ended, that I will miss the game characters now that the war is over and it'd be great to see a sequel to this.Any negative reviews that tell you "just play Shadow Tactics" or "just play Desperados III" - ignore them. Play all three!

_childDocuments_.review: This review was difficult, as I honestly love real-time strategy ever since playing the original Commandos. This game is an easy recommend for any fans of the genre who enjoy the old school tactics games. It's a much harder sell for literally anyone else.The main issues I had:- The folks making this game are really on to something with the mini basebuilding and character level ups going on. Unfortunately it's so shallow that it might almost not have been included at all. If made into a meaningful system that really feeds back into the missions, this would be really good. As things stand it's just more clicking you go through to get to the next mission.- Having a bit stronger focus on action and not always having to avoid shootouts is a great idea. Unfortunately it's incredibly unbalanced. Additionally I feel that you either go full XCOM and turn your characters into disposable pieces on the chess board (would be so fitting for a war game!) or you make them a bit more balanced. I think Desperados or Shadow tactics got the character balance much better.- Enemy behavious seems a bit weird at times. For example when you kill two enemies with a knife from the back and are just a split second off, everyone is alarmed immediately. This could be made so much better with a small grace period (again, Shadow Tactics and Desperados do that). On the other side you can literally kill a guard with a throwing knife from a bush and just run away unseen with enemies basically forgetting about the knife-throwing busches after about 30 seconds.- It's impossible to see at a glance what range skills and items have. Please just give me a radius when I select a grenade or a throwing knife to see what my range looks like.- Maybe I missed it in the tutorials but I missed a feature to mark a place in order to check if an enemy can see that. The original Commandos even had that and I feel it's necessary.- Some verticality would have been awesome. I don't mind sneeking around forests and farmsteads or through enemy controlled train stations, but please at least let me get my sniper up into a snipers nest on a barn roof or allow some of my characters to climb up some vines into a window or something. This was a feature Commandos 2 had more than a decade ago.- The game still feels a bit glitchy at times. It's unfortunate, since you really have to save every 10 seconds in case something happens.Despite all of this I still played the game from start to finish, but I don't think I'll ever circle back to it in the same way I do with Shadow Tactics or Desperados. It's such a shame as I love the genre and really appreciate the effort. I just don't think that this game is really good for anyone but the ones who can look beyond its flaws and missed chances.

_childDocuments_.review: It is impossible to give a definitive answer to what makes an artistic product good, but it seems to me, tonal coherence of various components is a good starting point. This is the most important reason why I can wholeheartedly recommend this game. Right from the opening sequence Partisans 1941 is very clear in what manner it is going to depict the partisan activity, and not a single component here disagrees with the others.When it comes to Soviet World War II Cinema the existence of two different camps is quite evident. On one hand there are war movies, such as Ballade o soldate (Ballad of a Soldier), or Jariskatsis mama (Father of a Soldier). Soviet war movies are slightly revanchist, but still hopeful of rebirth with an optimistic outlook on human psyche, even during one of the most barbaric invasions of recent history. On the other hand, there are partisan movies, such as Voskhozhdenie (The Ascent), or Idi i smotri (Come and See). There is an irremissible sombreness in partisan movies, usually depicting the barbaric actions of the Nazi war machine fully and we see that not even the Soviet people can be defined as "good".Partisans 1941 takes partisan movies, depicts the barbarism like they do but also adds optimism and revanchism of war movies to the mix. This works very well from a narrative standpoint, considering Alter Games are on unbroken land here, with their debut game as well. It is refreshing to have hopefulness, determination, a leader that you can look up to in a work about partisans. It fills the player with a sense of appreciation towards the countless partisans operating during the most horrifying and oppressive invasion in recent history. The gaming medium is perfect for this. Characters can talk about taking the war to the Nazis in any other medium, but player agency, the manner in which you will carry it out, especially with the various special skills and varied partisans this game offers is what makes it so satisfying. Having a choice between rushing a Nazi with a knife in your hand (Morozov) or picking his head from distance with a fully upgraded AVS-36 (Valya) or making him eat lead through a wall with your buckshot (Trofim) and many other options that benefit from different abilities complementing each other massively differentiates this from other media.Even then, the first thing that grabbed my attention was not gameplay mechanics, but how good our main character (probably inspired by real life partisan commander Simcha Zorin) looked. He is clean shaven with hair like he just left the most fashionable barber shop in Byelorussia five minutes ago, with a determined look in his eyes that says I will eliminate every single Nazi from Minsk to Staroe Selo. The thousand-yard stare, the downtrodden look, the desperation from hunger and cold so associated with the partisans does not have a place here. This goes for every character. They look, talk and act like they have the hindsight to know these days will pass like any other and they will emerge victorious.As I said, Partisans 1941 is a game where nothing is out of place tonally, and this extends even to the colour scheme. If you have played one of the numerous WWII FPS's taking place in the Eastern Front, you will already be accustomed to the yellowness of wheat, greenness of pine trees and brownness of the earth. How the game changes this well established formula is subtle, but effective. Brightness and intensity of every colour is slightly increased in comparison to usual, and a small amount of shading applied to borders of every object makes them more pronounced. These small changes give the usually depressing Soviet countryside a much more humane appearance.As a final layer of finish, the OST is composed with the same design perspective that is present in other areas. The music you'll hear the most, that plays whenever you're in camp is in the same vein. It's slow tempo, but the notes are crisp and distinguishable, in contrast with the melancholic vocal accompanying it, fully embracing the duality.Of course, as both a debut game and an indie game, Partisans is far from being perfect. UI is sometimes buggy and unresponsive, especially in inventory and picking up items/bodies. It is obvious to see the game was designed with stealth options as a priority. The enemy AI can get really stupid and there will be no way to predict if they will function or not in a firefight. Camp management starts out interesting for one or two missions, but gets repetitive fast. If you have a completionist streak, you'll find that scouring every map to remove every Nazi from existence gets tiresome in larger levels, especially when they start to call in reinforcements. Nevertheless, when it works, it works really well. The excitement and subsequent relief of a well-executed stealth attack with combined partisans is a feeling that is rarely replicated in gaming and usually passes as a high point of a game, here these opportunities are dime a dozen. The planning it takes to silently kill a dog and its handler, usually a mid-tier enemy in most games, is rewarding thanks to the multiple approaches you can take. If you can handle some minor jank (and nothing good ever happens without some minor jank), Partisans 1941 is a game that exactly knows what it wants and achieves what it wants and this is nothing to be scoffed at in these times.Punch a Nazi out, stab a Nazi in/10

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I have really enjoyed the game. It doesn't quite feel as polished as some other squad tactics games I've played recently, like Stealth Tactics or Desperados 3, but it's still fun to play. The stealth mechanics feel good. Character's individual abilities aren't quite as varied as Desperados 3, but they are effective. One thing I do appreciate about the game is that open conflict feels effective. It's nice to be able to set up an ambush or place my squad in different areas and be confident that they can effectively attack and defend against a group of enemies and take them all out. The addition of managing a camp adds some nice diversity to the gameplay. Of course, the WWII setting is interesting, though I do wish the game would have had a little more genuine history involved, such as more actual battles and places instead of the more generic missions and context the game gives you. If you enjoy games like the ones I mentioned, this should please you.

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game as I love RTS (Real Time Tactics) games. Surely this game has potential but it seems unfinished, as if it was a beta. Here's a few features that are lacking/need refurbishing:- Very slow gameplay (characters feel sloppy and somewhat out of control).- Unbalanced character control (Hard to place characters at desired location).- Limited tactical mode (Once in tactical mode you can either do nothing, or do chosen actions immediately, you cannot leave tactical mode with actions pre-selected).- Enemies reactions vary greatly. Either really slow, really fast, or non-responsive.- Game is mainly based on stealth, while this is a great feature, over using it is boring.- Short grace periods for actions executed.- Reveal area field of view is not necessary. All enemies and map should be visible at all time like Desperados and Shadow Tactics- Camp not necessary the game should be mainly based on story and not building. (Building is good for strategy games only, RTS you act live as it is with what you get).- Looting is a nice feature back from Commandos, but keeping the game limited to few skills per character is better. (Look Desperados and Shadow Tactics)- Active items should have a visible usage range and noise range.- Enemy view cones should have dark zones for stealth- Stealth should be an option and not an automatic feature when approaching enemy.- Camera rotation is disabled when using Custom control settings.- Map ends with pitch black area as if there is no further world to explore (not pleasing to eye, should end with a fog lighter in color to the rest of the world).Overall, to Me this game seems like an unfinished project that needs to be cleaned up. I have played for the first 3 or 4 missions and I'm not eager to go back to finish this game.

_childDocuments_.review: When commander Zorin and his subordinate Fetisov manage to escape a POW camp in the opening days of the Eastern Front and embark on a journey of resistance, little did they know that they were laying the foundations of a veritable partisan cell. What initially amounted to a struggle for survival and hopefully getting to know about the state of the war ended up in evolving into makeshift reprisal against the invaders and eventually, coordinated retaliation against the occupiers. It is a tale that seeks to embody the experience of resistance in the occupied Soviet Union throughout the lens of a made-up partisan cell that, however, is inspired in the real-life feats and experiences of partisans in the war. This is delivered in the form of an isometric RTS, much like Commandos, which puts you in the shoes of this band of resistance fighters bent on thwarting the conqueror's advance into their land.This partisan cell, comprised of an ever-growing cast of characters that join your ranks the more you progress in the story, gathers around a forest encampment which you can buiild, enhance and from where you can plan your next step. When not in a mission, this makeshift encampment is your HQ, where you may take inventory of items in your storage, send members on off-screen missions to gather resources (you have to feed and heal your partisans) and XP, which they use to level up. This is where you will spend most of the time between main missions and serves as a relief of sorts after tense levels.And speaking of missions: Partisans borrows heavily from Commandos, and rightly so: Commandos defined an era in isometric RTS-gaming. But whereas Commandos relies heavily on stealth and tip-toeing around enemy patrols, Partisans is all about positioning your soldiers behind cover, awaiting for the precise moment to strike an unwary patrol. Whereas Commandos emphasises avoiding large-scale pitched battles, Partisans compels you to engage in them. For whereas commandos in real life dealt with espionage, information theft and such, Partisans dealt primarily with sabotage and ambushes, so while at first glance one might be tempted to draw parallels between them, there is a stark difference at heart, and that is Partisans' focus on sheer, raw action. Admittedly, you may stealth your way through the entire game (as I did), but playing it guns blazing on a second run is as much fun as carefully picking stray soldiers and hiding them in bushes. And that is one of the highlights of Partisans 1941: you have so much agency over how each level and encounter plays out, that the replay is value is significant.There is also a factor which is difficult to measure, but which this game nails perfectly well and that is the  factor. The struggle for the survival of Russia, of the Motherland feels  . The missions, combat, the objectives, everything is beautifully crafted to immerse us in the harsh and grim reality of the Eastern Front in 1941 and succeeds brilliantly in crafting the narrative that follows the despair that plagued the opening days of Operation Barbarossa, to the jubilant confidence that followed the reversal of the tides of war after German forces were stopped before Moscow. You feel part of that struggle in a most unique way, and throughout dialogues, events and in-game newspaper articles you feel part of the war and immerse yourself in this fight for life and death.Speaking of whichi, note that the game is called "Partisans 1941" for a reason: the game takes place  during 1941, so you will not get to participate in the Fall of Berlin or even the Battle of Stalingrad, but it is preceisely this focus on 1941, the first year of the War in the Eastern Front, that makes it such a polished experience: by carefully narrowing down the scope of the game and seeking not to be overly ambitious, the devs deliver a solid and fresh take on such a scantly visited episode of the war: the year 1941 in the Eastern Front, with all that the ebbing and flowing of the tide of war entailed It is a game rich with significance and it is powerful in delivering the message of despair, resistance and ultimately, hope in the face of insurmountable odds.For all the power of its premise, the game could use some polishing on some elements of its storyline: characters are bland and rather one-dimensional: Soviets are good guys and the Germans -and their supporters- are deviously evil. Admittedly, it would be difficult to think of the Germans in the Eastern Front of anything rather than barbaric, but overlooking the brutality of the Soviets themselves (especially when a Commissar comes into play later in the game) makes this game seem like a veiled tool of propaganda. While useful for the life-or-death struggle narrative, it feels weak and lazy at times to come up with such one-dimensional characters in a game that otherwise is beautifully and painstakingly crafted to depict real-life events as truthfully as possible. Moreover, while most of the missions are rather solid (and there are indeed some truly remarkable ones), there are a few which are rather bland and suffer from poor level design. Thankfully these are the minority among a brilliant selection of maps -and brilliant there are indeed: train station map, I am looking at you!- but they detract from the experience of an otherwise perfectly-crafted game. Sound effects, moreover, do their job perfectly well, but voice acting can come across as rather bland and boring, and the musical score is unrepentantly forgettable.Having said that, the game is a solid entry on a somewhat overlooked theater of the bloodiest war of all-time, and is a fresh -if biased- outlook on the often forgotten Soviet experience, and it does so in a way that feels as epic as Russian war movies -such as Brest Fortress- feel. And for that I cannot help but commend it.7.5/10TL;DR: Solid game that sports remarkable dynamics and surpisingly great gameplay with abundant margin for replayability, but suffers from rather bland characters and storyline. Visuals are good, sound is acceptable and music, remarkably forgettable. No game makes you say "Вставай, страна огромная!" like this.

_childDocuments_.review: PROS:- Satisfying stealth 'puzzle' encounters (when they work)- Skills which feel overpowered in how easy they seem to make encounters (at first)- Nice, albeit distracting voice acting. The "Russians" are british in the English VO, and that's a strange choice. Still, english actors gave a strong performance.- Lasts 15-30 hours (would be 15, but see first CON...)CONS:- It's broken as ♥♥♥♥. Far, FAR too often did I trigger an alarm over something that wasn't my fault. A partisan fired his pistol while quietly escorting a hostage. A grenade is thrown through a wall. An enemy's expected patrol freezes in an inopportune location. A body can't be picked up because of the way it fell.- The Russian VO sounds like the actors were extremely, extremely bored. I appreciate the option for Russian VO since it should fit better, but their performance wasn't believable.- No autosaves, so get used to F5'ing after every successful kill, else you may fail due to a bug listed above.- The game gives you tons of ammo, but heavily implies you should be near 100% stealth with silent melee takedowns and body hiding. When gunfights break out, they just don't feel as satisfying since they happen so quickly.Right now, I just cannot recommend the game in this state. I personally played all the way through, and enjoyed a fair amount of it, but I'm also a stubborn S.O.B. and I couldn't see most other players hitting their head against the same brick wall I did for "enjoyment" considering the state the game is in.Honestly, I'm not sure how many of the bugs can be patched out, and how many problems are inherent to the core game design. Pathfinding is bad, left clicking to open something may order a partisan out of cover and blow the whole thing.No, there's no sequel bait, but honestly I WOULD play a sequel or otherwise successor to this game, given the devs learn from some missteps.

_childDocuments_.review: If you play this game after commandos/shadow tactics/desperados - you will be disappointed.There are so many bugs in the game, the engine actually crashed a few times. When items are passed from one character to other (in base), they overlap in the same square of the backpack and needs to taken apart. If you kill an enemy using a trap, the body cannot be picked up and the trap cannot be picked up. When the game is completed and the Credits  to roll, the game hangs!!!. There are more, but I'm not the testing department for the game, so I will stop listing.Even if you ignore the bugs and want to explore the game content (as I did), you will find that there are too few abilities and the game is quite clunky. Items cannot be dropped to be picked up later. There is a  option, which simply deleted the item. If you pick up a weapon and now your backpack is full, you cannot equip that weapon, because the already equipped weapon cannot be dropped or swapped (if it is a smaller weapon) or even deleted using "discard" option. Skills once taken cannot be reset (you don't know which new characters will be introduced and what skills they might have, so you might level some redundant skills and may want to reset it later). Enemy cone of vision moves so slowly, it is not even a challenge. The night missions are a cake walk.The concepts they  to implement are not bad though. It is not 100% stealth, you can switch to combat way of playing. There are hit chances, crit chances involved in the outcome of an engagement in such combats. Tactical pause to queue actions on different characters is a nice feature (like in shadow tactics/desperados).In conclusion - if you are looking for a game similar to shadow tactics / desperados / commandos - this is it. If you are looking for a game that you can enjoy as much as those - this it DEFINITELY NOT it. The bugs and the clunky gameplay really takes it all out of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game of course will remind you of the Commando franchise but with enough differences to make it still feel fresh.One thing that I am sucker for in games is when you have a base of operations that you see visually improve as you progress.   This has that feature although not as well done as say the Division series.   In this game as you improve your base you are offered more options for your troops to do in their down time when they aren't out on mission.The roles of the characters aren't as strict as the Commando series but you will have characters that are better with specific weapons.One minor criticism of the game is that you find that you rely mostly on your main character that has the knife throwing ability.   He will be used to slowly carve down the number of enemies before it is safe for a group attack.   Perhaps this changes later in the game and I just haven't recruited enough Partisans yet.There is a lot of stealth in this game be warned.   Call of Duty teenagers may wish to think hard about buying this game.  Expect a lot of crawling in the bushes, silent knife kills, hiding of the bodies, and looting the corpses.   If that is your bag of tea then this game is very highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. But some problems in the core gameplay mechanics and UI makes this game far from a great stealth/tactics game. CONS: - Too much uncertainty. Especially in the enemy AI. The differences between the enemies are not clear. Some enemies can spot you in an instant. After some time you start playing trial and error. This is the opposite of stealth. I believe the main audience of this game genre will not like this. - Enemies outside can see you while you are inside a building: I believe that buildings should be a safe zone. This adds an extra layer to uncertainty.- There is no use of using guns: Guns have a hit probability depending on distance and cover. I rarely get a single shot kill even if it says above 75% hit chance. Also guns make noise as expected in these style of games like Desperados or Shadow Tactics. But you don't have a clue of who will hear the shot. A simple UI would show that. Uncertainty, uncertainty...- Patrol path for some enemies are too long: You kill an enemy, then 5 minutes later patrols somehow find that enemy you killed and find you afterwards. 5 mins of gameplay is gone. There is no game speed increase button as in Desperados 3. - Enemies are not distinguishable from the background: I have to press ALT key constantly to highlight the enemies. This kills the stealth game feel.- CONTROLS: This problem is huge. Selecting a character shouldn't be this complicated. If 2 of your characters are close to each other, then it is impossible to select the one you want. PROS:- Base building: Between missions you upgrade your base with the materials you collected during missions.- RPG Character development: You chose and unlock certain abilities and improve as your characters level up. - Quick SAVE / LOAD: This is really quick. Final thoughts: This is not a bad game. There is too much of everything. Some AI changes, UI/Control improvements and some simplification would make this game a masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: Here are some of the problems I found in 3 hours of playing:The AI in this game is beyond just dumb:if the enemies see a body killed with environmental they will instantly go agro(which fails you on stealth missions) but if they see the environmental kill happen they will just investigate. Another great example is that one of the characters can disguise himself by putting his hands in his pockets(not even a joke) and you can do this in front of the guards, and they will stop suspecting you, just imagine seeing this kid carrying a mossin and after seeing him put it on his back and proceed to put his hands in his pockets you'll think "oh, he's just a kid"There are also some game-breaking bugs:your characters will sometimes forget their unlocked skills and there is nothing you can do, the skill will still be bought they just won't use it.Sometimes your characters will randomly attack enemies, thus alerting them.Enemies can sometimes see you while you're hiddenthe game also has a lot of mechanics problems:you can't save if your character is disguisedthe main keybinds do multiple things and sometimes this causes problems, for example both "cancel action" and "view the view cone of an enemy" are the same button (and sometimes even makes the character walk there)Just get Desperados way better in every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so much, I love this type of game from when I used to play commandos on the Playstation. Unfortunately this game is an unpolished mess that can't make its mind up what it wants to be. Shadow Tactics and Desperado's 3 are just so much more polished. For example a classic tool in these games is the ability to mark an area on the ground and it tells you if someone can see the area, it's completely missing here so that kinda sets the tone and lowers the expectations!This game is pretty unique in one aspect and that’s the gun battles, you can get into some pretty good battles and the characters fight autonomously. Which is pretty cool and a USP, the trouble is the game doesn’t realise this and forces you to the infamous ‘don’t be detected missions’ which are simply put; awful. I’m sure some developer somewhere thought one day that it was a great idea to have people play the game and not be detected at all or it automatically ends the mission, clearly they never played assassins creed and listened to the feedback of ‘which ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thought this was fun?’ they should have stuck to the battles throughout and just capitalised on those missions designs as they are superior and far more funAs for the characters, there are too many. I think I ended up with 8 of them, and throughout the main story you can only choose 3 to come with you on each mission, I’ve no idea why there are so many, they are simply not required and this means many just get forgotten about and unused, not to mention 1 dude is mandatory on all the missions bar one so you only get to choose from 2 of the massive roster!I did encounter a few bugs too, characters not placing mines and will just stand there, and an infuriating bug which means when you quicksave, the quickload state moves the enemy characters around! _childDocuments_.review: Worth your while if you are a fan of Commandos style tactics-games. Ideally get it on sale as the technical side leaves a lot to be desired. If you can't stand communisits don't play.PROS- Most of the missions are wonderfully designed, great looking, with multiple ways to complete your objectives. They're not too long nor unreasonably difficult. Mission 14 is genuinely a masterpiece of non-linear stealth action.- Soundtrack and sound overall is very good and atmospheric, good weapon sounds and nice ambience. Visuals have a nice artstyle and are overall very pleasant.- Characters are reasonably well balanced, they all offer different flavours and unique approaches to missions. Cracks in their balancing appear only at very late game or at higher difficulties.MIX- Story is pretty much non-existent as there isn't an overarching plot. The characters don't go through arcs or change, although for this type of a game it isn't much of an issue. You are given missions to complete and that's it. Extra interactions between characters would've been nicer though.- The camp managment side is very barebones, you get most of your camp upgrades very early and after that there isn't much to do. Also the camp UI is kind of messy and you never get quite used to it.- The game feels like playing through a Yuri Ozerov movie, it very much uses USSR WW2 propaganda, the Partisans are all super heroic, the Germans are all super bad and there are one-liners straight out of propaganda posters. Now this might be on purpose to create an atmosphere reminiscent with what the state media would portray the war as, shortly after it's end (think post-war US WW2 movies). Or the developers genuinely believe this and are old-school USSR apologists. Either way be warned, it might rub some people the wrong way.CONS- The game doesn't have fully customisable graphics, you cannot choose textures, objects and post processing individually, you can only chose low. medium and high presets, that's it.- The inventory is total crap, not the idea, but the implementation. The game will scream at you that you don't have anymore space but you actually do, you just have to make it manually. Items of the same type often won't autmoatically stack together, so you get three incomplete stacks of the same ammo instead of one full stack. You cannot reload your guns in the inventory by dragging ammo onto them, you have to unload the gun and then put it into the Partisans hands. Every time you move an item or change a weapon the game lags. The auto sorting is almost useless as it sorts very strangely and makes a mess. The icons are very difficult to read at first glance, you will confuse different ammo types till the very end.- There are many moments where the game hiccups and you'll have no idea why, it's classic Slav-jank. 'Cause I'm a Slav myself I don't really mind and just use the F5 button religiously as I was taught, but it's noticeable enough to where it can be sometimes frustrating.- The last 2 missions are exactly the opposite of why I liked the game. They are very linear, ball bustingly hard and feel like you need to cheese to finish them. Absolutely appalling ending to an otherwise good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Action-based tactical RPGs are a mixed bag that can vary greatly in quality from one title to the next. For every Desperados III or Broken Lines, there are at least a dozen others that miss the mark. Character balance, map design, and variety all play a huge role and one slip-up in any of these can lead to disastrous results that reverberate throughout the experience.Partisans 1941 succeeds at fitting the requirements to be a worthy addition to the genre. Gameplay is smooth, mostly unique skill trees keep leveling up exciting across your cast of characters, and the story overall is one that you can find yourself getting caught up in before you know it. Just make sure that you’re prepared for a story based in occupied territory during World War II and all that it entails.Partisans 1941 puts you into the boots of Captain Alexey Zorin, a Soviet officer whose command was captured by the invading German forces. His story begins as he pulls off an escape attempt from a prison camp. The first of his allies, experienced Sergeant-Major Nikolay Fetisov and fourteen-year-old Alexander Kuzmin, are recovered during the chaos. Once they’ve made it to safety, you’ll guide them as they engage in guerilla warfare to bring the hurt on the occupiers that threaten their country by engaging in stealth missions, maintaining and upgrading a secret base camp, and interacting with the victims of the occupation to gather information, equipment, and co-conspirators.The story is suitably dark for the setting, though I never found it to get to the point that I would warn someone who had a passing grasp of the events of World War II. Blood and gore is limited, violence during gameplay is no worse than any other similar title in the genre, and overall, it tends to be the story of successful underdogs facing off against an overwhelming enemy. Encountering new allies is exciting and overcoming the enemy with many small victories is fulfilling. One of the first missions of the title is one where your squad sneaks into an enemy structure to permanently remove a tank that was left behind for repairs from the German armory.One of my favorite parts of any RPG is leveling up my characters. Partisans 1941 has an enjoyable system in this regard as each character in your unit is unique. Though many skills are shared by some characters, such as rifle proficiency or increased defensive bonuses from cover, each tree feels unique enough to warrant consideration for who is the best man or woman for the job prior to going out on a mission. Right off of the bat, your squad grows to three characters that form your starting unit. Captain Zorin specializes in swift movement and quiet ambushes with his trusty knife, Sergeant-Major Fetisov is an all-around classic infantryman with a strong leaning toward using loud firearms and grenades, and young Kuzmin can become particularly capable of sneaking around in plain sight as long as he’s careful not to draw suspicion to himself. As your party continues to grow, you’ll gain even more variety that will allow you to tailor how you take on your missions going forward.Progression also takes place on the equipment front. Defeating enemies will often have them drop items that you can use to your advantage and these come in quite a variety. As you might expect, weapons are of the utmost importance and you’ll need both them and their related ammunition to be able to take your foes head-on. However, weapons are only a part of what’s available to aid you in your strategy here and a particularly stealthy, tactical approach will likely make it so that you don’t need as much ammo as you find. Everything from rocks to medkits to vegetables, eggs, and cheese will be looted from those you defeat, and maybe even the homes of the locals if you’re particularly desperate. Rocks find their use in making noise and causing a distraction to enemies who aren’t on alert, medkits and their associated items will keep your squadmates in the fight after sustaining injuries, and food and other supplies that aren’t immediately useful will add to the resources back at your base, granting you the ability to significantly improve its functioning. This will not only make it easier for your partisans to survive, but also to thrive in their opposition of the occupiers.Partisans 1941 is a challenging tactical action game that will keep veterans of the genre on their toes, especially if they’ve upped the difficulty. Quick saves and loads are still the order of the day here for many of us and will allow you to make some mistakes along the way and still be able to enjoy the game even if you aren’t one of the experts rolling up who are prepared to free the Soviet Union on their self-enforced ironman mode. The story and characters within it are interesting and only a few small areas feel as if they’re a little odd, such as German soldiers speaking with an accent but Soviet speaking perfect English.Overall, Partisans 1941 is a solid addition to the genre and one that I can easily recommend to anyone who enjoys similar titles. Though it doesn’t innovate as often as I would’ve liked, it checks all of the boxes for a game that will keep you entertained by what you already enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Commandos style real time strategy game focused around a Russian resistance group in 1941. A larger focus on being able to engage in direct combat than most games like this, as stealth or avoiding kills is rarely required, weapons of different qualities can be found and upgraded as well as traps and grenades. Characters gain experience from kills, objectives completed, and side missions you assign them at your camp between stages and can learn new abilities, passive skills, or increase their hit chance with weapons. Between missions you have a camp where you can assign characters tasks like missions to get them XP or to gain equipment, tasks to gain food or resources, building mines or grenades, etc. A lot of elements never amount to much, your morale should always be at max so that's never a thing that matters, getting food is never really a problem, upgrading weapons and crafting explosives feels like an afterthought, all the looting is just time consuming.Bigger problems with the game are that Desperados 3 added the thing most needed in this genre, a fast forward button, and that's always going to be missed. Unbalanced, enemies are never set up in a difficult way that really requires you to use skills of multiple characters, some very overpowered abilities. Not a great idea to go for achievements requiring stealth as what actually counts as detection can be buggy and completing main objectives can just alert anymore for no reason. It doesn't know how to handle height or cover when it comes to your enemies cones of view and having no difference between things that are standing, crouching, or on the ground is unfortunate. If you go for a more combat focused playthrough one of the biggest bugs is that they just won't reload guns and if you manually do it they go through the animation but nothing happens (opening inventory and unequipping and reequipping seems to get it working again). You can go into a time slowed mode where you can issue commands to all your characters to try to sync up actions but you really can't do things like have them move in together to each stealth kill an enemy as your window between an alert going off is probably around one second and it is one of the kind of games where it doesn't matter if an enemy is able to say/yell/radio/etc a warning because the alert comes the second they see anything (even if that something is the knife flying through the air to kill them).If you really like the genre there is some enjoyment to be had and I can recommend it but it falls a bit short in many areas always staying around just being an average title at best.Screenshots:
