_childDocuments_.review: This game is similar to the other stealth strategies: Commandos, Desperados, Shadow Tactics. Unfortunately it doesn't come up anywhere near them.There are very few games in this genre, so any new stealth experience is welcome.The game is innovative in that it has a resource management system, you can even upgrade your weapons.There is a lot of character banter in between the missions,The graphics is just plain bad. Even on a semi-high end machine it looks horrible - see some screenshots. I know this is generally a thing with Daedalic games, but still it's big con. Competing games such as Desperados and Shadow Tactics also aren't top end graphics, but there the environments are clean, everything is easy to spot etc.Game systems just don't work. Resource management system is just bothersome and not fun - it's merely chore that doesn't give you any new options. At best you can construct makeshift mines and grenades. It also comes with rather tedious inventory management. Combat is also not that fun - both parties take cover and then they roll chances to hit (sometimes it's sprinkled up with a grenade or so, though). Even the RPG part is bland - your partisans have very similar skills and play largely the same.Unfortunately it's not really easy to enjoy the combat part, because the controls are pretty unresponsive. You often misclick due to messy graphics or poor UI, your partisans sometimes just randomly stop walking, sometimes they start running on doubleclick and sometimes they don't.. it feels kinda random even after about 10 hours into the game.I could go on rambling about a lot more, but let's go straight to the conclusion.Why would you get this game? If you like the stealth strategy genre, just avoid this and instead go play Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3 again. Even though you've probably played it twice already, it will still be more fun than Partisans 1941.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great, interesting and tactical. ..but it doesn't go all the way to the finish. The reason I give this a thumbs down and a refund is because it lacks certain features and has bugs that makes this game not fun to play. Like, the enemy LOS is ridiculous. I know the germans are "übermenschen" but having x-ray vision and the ability to see through walls, logpiles and barrels is something that is more annoying than fun. How can a cart that has wheels hide squad members more than a pile of logs or 5 barrels that looks like they're close enough to hide at least 2 people? Also, the enemies can slightly bend their vision around objects, they can even look through civilians...The game do also lack the ability to prone. If I were to do an ambush against a small enemy squad, I would want to have someone inside a house, someone behind a cart and someone laying down behind a fallen tree. What's the problem here? You can't lay down behind the tree because the enemy can see through it but it offers cover... Instead you have to stay in the bushes and run out to that tree, risking the life of a squad member who probably won't be able to kill anyone... I know, the fallen tree is on the gound and the enemies can see over it, but what if there's an uneven terrain, like a hole next to the tree, or a ditch, then you should have some cover until the enemies stands next to that tree. The game also does strange stuff. I had a shotgunner who broke his arm by doing basically nothing. Seriously? If you like this, well, go ahead and buy it. It has the potential to be something bigger, something better but in its current state, it's not. An interesting thing would to have this gameplay set in France as the french resistance, Norway or in Poland to name a few with some urban and some countryside generated maps. Instead of having it with set missions, I would've loved to see random generated missions where you have to free prisoners, killing or kidnapping officials/officers or destroy enemy stuff to keep the enemy busy with everything else than hunting down resistance fighters or fighting the Allied/Russian forces. There's a lot of ways to go instead of 15 missions, which sounds like nothing tbh.Also, you unlock the achievement "War never changes" after killing like 3 enemies, and it has the requirement to kill 100 enemies. Good job!

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that could seriously benefit from a "definitive edition". The partisan theme feels really unique compared to other games in the Real Time Tactics genre and the seamless stealth-to-gunfight system makes you feel like you're not just a war ninja but an actual soldier too! On the other hand, after the incredible Desperados 3 this is a step down in production quality. Voice acting is minimal, the mouse movement feels floaty, the UI buttons are too small, graphics options are next to none, the cover options are strangely picky and not being able to play with a gamepad is a buzzkill. So yeah, its great that the RTT genre is kickin' but a definitive edition would be great for this game!

_childDocuments_.review: It's an okay tactics game, but what forced me to stop wanting to play is the absolutely weird AI of the enemies that suddenly become heat seeking cruise missiles for everyone that _wasnt_ yet spotted as soon as one of your guys gets caught or at the very least, seen. _childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a lot of fun. Be warned this is a very difficult and unforgiving gameI really enjoy the story, the writing, the characters, and the gameplay is a LOT of fun. I'm a bit disappointed this is a very linear game; I was kinda hoping for something more dynamic, but it's fun nevertheless.My main gripe is that, for a game where you're always at a disadvantage and where stealth is essential, some of the controls can be frustratingly wonky. Especially bad is trying to pick up a body; I've had incidents where I have maybe ~5 seconds to pick up a body and run with it before I'm spotted. Far too often, despite clicking directly on the 'pick up body' button, the game instead has my character walk around aimlessly or lean against cover instead of grabbing the body.Very frustrating since seconds matter so much.Still, I'd recommend this. Just be vigilant about where you're clicking, and exploit the ability to slow time!

_childDocuments_.review: I played a quite small amount of time with this game, but I could tell very quickly that I was not going to enjoy it. If you like games like Men of War, Graviteam Tactics, or XCOM, it is somewhat likely that you will hate this game. The main reason being the combat. The shooting is like if XCOM was in real time and it just feels wrong. Where in an XCOM game your success is really only down to your positioning, it is here based on how fast you can click. Additionally, RNG is present in both of these games but here since it is in real time it seems wrong that a point blank shot is either a miss or only a wound. The realistic setting adds to this feeling, as you see what seem to be real soldiers fire what seem to be nerf guns for all the effect they have. Its like Company of Heroes but without the chaotic fun of the large scale battles. The guns are just bad. And that is what made me refund it.

_childDocuments_.review: I tried, but I just can't. Inventory is clunky to manage and unintuitive to use. Windows won't adjust to screen size, leaving text unreadable and off screen. Inventory item information doesn't pop up automatically, so you'll find yourself right clicking every single item to figure out what it's name is, what it does, and where to equip it. Characters all engage in combat immediately and are in constant agro until you take manual control and stop them. Hit chance isn't calculated for new spots, so trying to gain a new vantage point is guess work as to effectiveness. Voice acting is mediocre, camera doesn't ever zoom in far enough to really get a close look at what's going on, stealth feels forced. Combat is bad, story is bland at two and a half hours in, stealth is hamfisted at best, and even the UI, inventory and leveling all feel uninspired, unintuitive, and rushed. If you want a good isometric, just go buy Wasteland 3. This one is gonna get a solid no from me.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: brilliant gameplay + bad controls and horrendous UX.The core gameplay is similar to but also different from Desperados/Shadow Tactics. If you are looking for D/ST here, this game might disappoint you. But it's definitely worth giving it a chance. Desperados 3 is probably my favourite game of all time. I was slightly disappointed that Partisans is different, but this game totally works as its own. It's a mixture of stealthy skill combos and tactical ambushes.Stealth is not as deep as D/ST, but overall the options are wider here. There are also levelups, new skills to learn, existing ones to boost. More logical item usage.The more action packed ambushes are not just braindead shootouts either. Start a not very well thought-out ambush and you quickly need to realise that enemy is way better equipped and trained than you partisans.There is also some HQ management between missions. I'm usually not a fan of this, but I liked it here. It's simple with some meaningful choices and revolves around you characters. What makes this not a brilliant game for me is the bad controls and VERY bad UX. Some of the usability issues are just horrendously bad. I can totally see how these could ruin the game for someone. I liked everything else so much that I managed to put up with them, but they've bothered me and hindered my enjoyment to the very end.Without these issues this could be a game of the year contender for me (of whichever year). Sadly, it is only a really really good game thanks to these.Would I recommended it? Not wholeheartedly. If you like stealthy and or tactical gameplay, give it a try and please be prepared that it might not always be very user fiendly.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: don't bother getting this for anything more than $10, this game feels like it's still in early access/beta phase.I have very little time on the game itself, so I imagine there's way more mechanics to introduce.  The problem?  Literally EVERY SINGLE mechanic that has been introduced in the first hour and a half falls flat and I do not have high hopes going forward.  Even the simplest of mechanics are horribly unpolished and every single menu has been a pain to navigate.  Here's the breakdown:Game runs slightly worse than alright.  There's no way that I get more FPS on games like MGS:V or DMC:V than this game on 1440p.  Somehow the optimization isn't all there, and I turned down graphic options considerably just to get it somewhat decent (60FPS).  Even then, there's still AWFUL input delay and that includes simply moving the cursor.  It just feels sluggish and heavy to run for no reason.Gameplay is stiff and VERY CLEARLY unpolished.  Enemies are way too fast at reacting on normal difficulty, you can throw a knife at an enemy and his buddy will IMMEDIATELY return fire regardless if he recognizes your location or not.  This happened literally multiple times and I was able to recreate it:  my characters are behind cover AND HIDDEN, throw a knife at an enemy. Now, after throwing the knife, obviously it's a silent kill right?  No way the enemy should know where it could be coming from, especially with one of my characters hidden in a bush.  Enemy drops dead, his buddy next to him IMMEDIATELY fires into the bushes and kills one-shots my character from full health.  Huh?  It wasn't even the same character that threw the knife, how is that even possible?Accessing context menus or clicking interaction prompts just feels inconsistent.  Even the most basic actions like picking up a body or opening doors is inconsistent.  On top of that, controls in every single menu is GARBAGE.  There's no situation in any game ever where I thought "Hey, if I right-click, I want to close all the windows I have open."  The menus need a massive QoL overhaul, it's actually unbearable for me to even try anymore.  The voice acting is actually extremely unimpressive and very immersion-breaking.  I understand it's hard to find good voice talent, but at least TRY to get an accent going for these Soviet soldiers.  It makes no sense that I'm hearing a VERY non-Russian accent in the Soviet countryside.There's an inventory management system.  You can't rotate items.  It's 2020, while this is a (somewhat) minor point, I find it hard to believe no one addressed this extremely inconvenient point.Every context menu, every interaction, all of it feels unintuitive and inconsistent across the board.  I'm actually having a hard time finding something that I appreciate in this game when this game can't even get the most basic things right.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good, kind of a Shadow Tactics clone with character progression and rpg elements.It is, however, incredibly buggy and inconsistent in its behavior. Most of the skills do not work as intended and for a stealth game, almost every creative approach leads to a gunfight in which your partisans will probably win. It is challenging, but mostly because of the bugs and the requirement for cheesing to avoid some glitches and weird bugs. For example, in a mission in which you need to sabotage anti air guns and kill it's crews, the whole camp started looking for me in an infinite loop before I even moved my characters, and it happened again after I've killed the first crew, hiding their bodies perfectly well. I was questioning myself until the 20th reload that I've found out they weren't even looking for me in a place I've been to, but in the other side of the camp, which I've had no access to yet.Oh and I want to point out the extremely horrible voices and anime style cliches of the characters. _childDocuments_.review: score 7/10 - Russian take on Commandos where a throwing knife is much more powerful than a Mauser, where a bottle of vodka distracts better than anything.TLDRPartisans is a spiritual clone of Commandos with elements of Shadow Tactics and some base building and character progression elements. At its core it is 2.5D tactical real time strategy with an emphasis on stealth where you generally control 3 partisans per mission. Sure, you can equip your partisans with weapons and even upgrade them, set up choke points and traps for Nazi patrols, but stealth is just much more efficient. The actual gunfire engagements do feel unbalanced and quite buggy where AI won’t react to a landmine going of with a loud bang if they are 20+ meters away.From the stealth mechanics point of view the game does encourage planning and combining of your squad skills. Occasional bugs and glitches do affect the game, but all in all will not prevent you from enjoying the game. The challenges that the maps present are not huge though, planning, timing and having your best team on the map will make it easy with only occasional need for quickloads.The story is non-existent – for motherland and for Stalin, let’s kill as many Nazis as we can and sabotage them. Occasional campfire discussions are aimed to create an authentic atmosphere, but they are so badly done that I rather not have them at all. Historical notes on the other had (you recover these during missions) do give you some glimpses of the war on the Soviet front.Base-building is redundant, it is there to pass some time and also give you an option to upgrade weapons and manage your inventory, but otherwise it is so easy that I did not even notice any challenges with food and supply management (you loot enough during campaign missions and basebuilding auto missions).In overall the game is solid, it has its flaws and is certainly few steps behind Shadow Tactics or Desperados 3, but otherwise it is worth your wile if you are a fan of the genre, and common, ‘killing Nazis is always fun’ as per William "B.J." Blazkowicz.P.S.For more grumpy reviews follow me as curator at

_childDocuments_.review: At first I drew attention to this game not because of the gameplay, but because it told the story about german invasion in an unusual way (unusual for modern movies, games and books in Russia and western world as well). The Nazis are shown as Nazis: thea are shooting women, children and prisoners, taking hostages, burning and plundering villages. They are not shown as reflective cultural "europeans" who are sometimes forced to do terrible things (as in modern Russian films). Collaborators are shown as scum and opportunists who take advantage of the occupation for personal gain. And Soviet partisans are shown as heroes who have no questions about their duty to fight for their motherland (again, not like in modern Russian films). Some of the heroes are directly communists or Komsomol-member, and this fact is not hushed up or shyly avoided (again, not like... ). Essentially they are fighting for Soviet power and for the legacy of the October Revolution (while in modern films the heroes fight at best for "Russia", but more often "for themselves" or "for the girl").Such a straightforward look is inherent in old Soviet books and films about the war, in each letter of which there is more truth than in all modern rubbish.Born in the Voronezh region, as a child, I listened to stories about the occupation, about how the Wehrmacht soldiers put children on their armored vehicles so that the partisans would not fire at it, and arranged mass executions for every successful partisan action. In these stories of my great-grandfathers, old soldiers and old partisans, there was also no reflection about why they fought: they fought for Soviet power against the Nazis, period.Therefore, I bought this game without paying attention to the quality. To my surprise, the quality is quite decent. In terms of gameplay, this is a retro game "Commando look alike". Missions take place on fairly large maps with dozens of enemies, and as a rule, you need to kill most of them or all of them with a group of 3-4 partisans. As with all such games, most of the time you bypass the "cones of view", hide in the bushes and throw knives. Most maps can be passed stealthily (through the bushes with a knife) or loudly (with shooting and explosions). Some characters are more suitable for a stealthy style of play, and some for a more straightforward style. As usual in such games, the player gets used to one favorite technique: for me it was the main protagonist's throwing knife, which accounted for two thirds of frags.The difference between this game and other "commandos" clones in two things. Firstly, this is the base management, but it is essentially purely cosmetic. The second is the loot, inventory and weapon system. Which makes the game more similar to the "Men of War" series: each partisan can take any weapon in his hands, ammo and grenades can run out and they must be counted. The combat system is again similar to "Men of War" and is based on covers. Clashes are usually fleeting and brutal, partisans die quickly enough under the crossfire or in open areas. Therefore, to win, you first have to crawl through the bushes with knives thoroughly in order to reduce the number of enemies.I have not encountered a single bug during the game, perhaps because I played it six months after the release. Control, camera are familiar to fans of "commandos" clones. The only drawback of the game is that it is relatively short and released DLС does not fix the matter.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: If you genuinely anticipated for a good Commandos Game since Commandos 2: Men of courage, this is the game for you, as a fan of Commandos 2 I can tell you that Partisans 1941 is the dream spiritual sequel to one of my favourite games of all time since there was basically no good Commandos game after the second instalment.Hiding inside of bushes, catching enemies off guard, knifing them, blowing up a crowd of disrupted Nazis, tripwire bombs and traps, this game has it all, the icing on the cake however, this game takes the guerrilla warfare aspect of a classic commandos game and pushed it to a new height with its designs, using bullet time and giving characters unique quick kill abilities, this game lets you pull off tons of fun guerrilla tactics on groups of enemies.You can level up your characters according to your play style, be it stealth focused or urban fighting focused, the maps are designed in a way that each area of enemies can be approached from multiple angles, the environment and ambient takes you to a war-torn eastern front, where you defend and avenge your motherland with a group of partisan comrades, you can also change the game audio to Russian for authenticity, there are also some interesting touches to put emphasis on what it could be like to survive in the desolate lands of Nazi occupied parts of soviet Russia.The weapon sounds and physics are also very satisfying, inventory management can be a bit tedious but I do not hold that against the game as careful logistics is an important aspect of warfare, the characters are well written and much information are provided to inform the player on what goes on in Soviet Russia during the Nazi invasion, a over all well rounded and well iterated urban tactics game set in WW2.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Desperados / Commandos remake with a different setting and added base building / crafting. It lacks features and depth Commandos and Desperados had, but the story line / setting of Partisans is better. But since there is the base management/ crafting in the game, you have to loot every corner of the map to thrive, which makes the game tedious. If you have finished either Commandos or Desperados, Partisans is no challenge to you, not even on highest difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, first off I'll say that though I'm rating this game positively that does not mean it isn't without it's flaws, some minor, some major.First off, the game can be glitchy still. Some times my team got spotted without clear reason why or sometimes when I stealth-killed a pair of enemies at the same time they still somehow set off an alert. And at some points my team got shot through solid building walls.Second, the lit up areas in nighttime missions are some times bigger than they seem. Sometimes this makes sense because the light is  seemingly cast in 3D from what I can tell. But other times someone was standing away from a lit up area's source and still be lit up according to the game.A marker on the mouse to show what is or isn't considered lit up or being able to highlight could help considerably in a potential sequel.Furthermore, outside of a few mission the most partisans you'll be able to control in a mission will be 3 which feels fitting at the start of the game but when the final level is just with 3 as well it feels underwhelming.And lastly some things you'll only learn the hard way since the tutorials won't mention it like how the highest ranked enemies will check up on their subordinates and will start a search for you if they find anyone is missing.Beyond those and perhaps some other things I still mostly enjoyed my time with this game even if I found it a bit wanting at times.Hope that it'll get a (spiritual) sequel at some point with these issues fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: One of my all time favourite games. Period. I knew I would like this game the moment I was introduced to it and its' concept. When I first played it I fell in love. There is so much about this game I could rant about, so I will.Conceptually I love this game. I have always had a love for media around Partisans, what little there is. So any work that shines light on this under-explored topic gets an immediate win in my book. Partisans 1941, makes me feel like a partisan. Some people don't like the resource management, I can understand that, but I am not one of those people. I love the feeling of accruing weapons and materials for my partisans. Finding ways to conserve my resources while still getting as much use as possible. The Inventory UI is quite the mess though. I do hope if Alter have any plans to continue support for Partisans 1941, that they rework it. The tactical and stealth aspects of the game are really well done and fun; however I do have some complaints. The time delay between an enemy spotting you and them bursting to action is far too unforgiving. I don't want it to be too forgiving, because then it wouldn't be as challenging. The challenge of this game is a large part of the fun for me. Now admittedly this isn't too big of a problem in most missions; except stealth only missions, where if you don't  deal with the target who saw you then it's game over. On hard this can make stealth missions agonizingly tedious as you run through the same guards to get back to the point you were previously at, over, and over. Outside of stealth only missions however I don't find this too much of an issue, as you are usually able to eliminate a target before they can sound any alarms. I touched on this before, but the difficulty of this game is one of my favourite aspects. This game can be  on hard. Perfect coordination and planning between your characters is required. It is punishing; without feeling undeserved. When I get a mission fail, it's  always because I mess up. I would genuinely recommend that players looking for the proper Partisans 1941 experience play on hard. On normal I was enjoying the game. On hard; I was  it. On hard, your Partisans are F*cked if you don't use proper positioning. On normal I was able to savescum my way to perfect stealth runs, where I only used melee and stealth abilities. Hard made me realise that a properly set up ambush is not only more effective at times, but more Partisans is a pretty intensive game, my rig can run it relatively well, but on some of the bigger maps with lots of enemies, I will find frame rate drops. I don't hold this too much against the game however; because the resulting artwork and style of the environments, characters, and enemies is work every lost frame to me. Would I take a better optimised game? In a heart beat. Would I take it at the expense of the games graphics? Probably not. If you own the art book for this game, and have looked at it, you will understand the care put into the creation of the environments. Not just from a level design aspect, but also the care put into the design of buildings to make them as immersive and accurate to the setting as possible. The one area I find the Graphics lacking is in the character models, even on the highest settings the characters are weirdly blurry and hard to make out. Which is a shame because I rather like the characters. speaking of. The characters are an area I think are rarely spoken of in this game. Possibly because it's not exactly what you come to an RTT game for, but I find that the personalities of the characters all shine through without becoming shallow and one-note. The writers managed to make each character feel rather distinct without falling to just making simple character quirks and playing them up. Show me a character from this game and I could describe their personalities to you, because they stick out to me that well. However that may be saying more about me admittedly.Another underappreciated aspect of the game, Vladislav Isaev and Elena Isaeva did a wonderful job on this score. It's one you likely won't notice, especially if you play on low volume or with music off. As someone who owns the soundtrack however I must say it is so atmospheric and immersive. It reminds me a lot of Halo ODSTs soundtrack. Give it a listen if you have it.All-in-all, I think Partisans 1941 is a brilliant game. One of my favourites of all time. It is one of two games I have bought the Supporter pack for. The other being Barotrauma. I do not regret a single dollar. Quite the opposite, if I had, had the money, I would have bought this game at full price instead of on sale. Seeing as I did not however, I am glad I bought this game, and its' extended edition.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally finished the game, and decided to edit my initial review and change it to a positive one.The game is not perfect, with a clunky 1990's like UX. The about 10 partisans you  get to choose from also vary in their skills, and while most feel generic, 2 or 3 are overpowered and give u no reason to choose anyone else. The base management option is kinda pointless. You will never really run out of food, and there's no reason to craft weapons 99.99% of the time.There are however 2 main reasons that make this game a very good one after all:1. The game provides an excellent blend between stealth and real time combats. You can outtake the enemies silently or ignore them. You can also ambush and fight them with guns and grenades. Neither of the options feel too repetetive (even though the stealth option gets a bit too easy once you get the whisteling thief). I think the devs here actually managed to build a more complete experience than you get from Desperados 3, which feels more puzzelish with sometimes one way to do things.2. The characters are diverse, and represent the soviet society with its struggles and issues pretty weel. Unlike what it may seem in the beginning, this game akcnowledges USSRs issues, and doesnt hide them behind layers of propaganda. Sure, you play the good guys defending their homeland, but its clear, for example, no one likes the NKVD officer.It takes time for things to start working, but at the end i think it worths it

_childDocuments_.review: The game is okay, mostly. Compared to e.g. commando's I like how there is less punishment and even a bit of satisfaction reward for setting up ambushes and then having a shootout, provided you can get yourself in a good position ... which is where the main problem starts.The controls are terrifyingly bad. You will find yourself clicking on things and characters doing something else. Or just nothing at all because you are actually supposed to click on the little icons that appear when you hover over a target. Or they will switch to their loud weapon when you're not paying attention and you try to sneak up on someone and they will grab their gun and alert the entire map. Or when moving as a group 2 people will stay on one side of the fence while the other will happily run around and get shot. When there are multiple click-targets over each other I can guarantee you that you will pick the wrong one.There doesn't seem to be any logic in getting shot vs getting a wound. I've had one of my guys get shot once and get wounded while I had another one at only a sliver of health left and he was fine.Even something like sorting your inventory doesn't work like you would expect. What it does is compress empty spots. What it doesn't do is put the same type of ammo next to each other in a neat little row. It doesn't really matter for the gameplay but it just.. bothers me.I paid 6 currency units for this. Because of that I am not going to feel ripped off. Just disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is actually good, but I couldn't bother to finish it due to several bugs that made it annoying to play.Of course, it has a good premise: upgrading your partisans, bit of base-building, inventory management. but clunky controls (left click to walk, right click to cancel...), and the bugs... OH, THE BUGS.- Skills stopped working randomly.- You just can't click properly on a corpse to retrieve items or your knife. You have to move the bodies around in order to properly click on the icons.- Sometimes you order your partisan to build a trap, your partisan would go to that place and...... nothing happens. They just stay there, doing nothing, and you can't move them either. You have to cancel the order and repeat the order to build a trap. Then the dog notices you and you should reload a game due to a bug.Among other things that made it annoying to play, like, guards outside the screen can't hear an EXPLOSION. It made me feel like I was cheating: putting a explosive trap and wait for a patrol to step on it, and every other guard on the game just keep doing their business. Why, WHY, IN THE NAME OF THE GOOD LORD, stones are a PRECIOUS limited resource? Seriously!And, the resource management at base is... I'm sorry, its just plain stupid. Like, you should spend 10 food, to get 20 food, or you could just go hunting/fishing and get 15 food. And fishing you can go as soon as the game starts. Only late at the game you can smoke 10 food to get 20, which sounds......... counterintuitive.Like I said, it is a good game. But half way through it, bugs got so annoying that killed my will to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Since commandos 2 is my most favorite game. This game really hit that sweet spot. Although I played Desperados 3 and Shadow tactics: Blades of the Shogun, they didn't have the loot system that commandos had. Partisans 1941 is overall a pretty cool game. For sure recommend. Just want to share my frustrations, but by no means they should stop you from playing this cool game (Maybe the devs will see it and get a new idea for something):1. Not super polished, some moments are frustrating, especially when you try to loot a box and the clicker cannot hit the hit-box.2. The base aspect is pretty cool, especially early on. After mid-game you have more resources than you can spend on. So you just spend a few days farming food or doing side activities. Really gets boring quick.3. I feel like there are 4 partisans who are OP (in terms of usefulness) and the others who are just kinda trash. For example all the melee guys are very useful, especially since most late-game missions require you to not be found. Morozov (this guy lures enemies and jumps on the with his knife(SUPER USEFUL)). While the old guy or the spy kid or even the nurse, they don't bring as much value. Those characters are cool for the story, not so for the game-play4. Some enemy logic is kinda missing. Some enemies don't move from their room, even if you throw grenades into the nearby room. 5. A thing that is missing for sure is when you melee kill someone, you cannot instantly pick him up. The animation shows that you picked him up, but the game still counts that he fell from being killed and made sound hitting the floor. This is that thing that probably should have been addressed.6. Most missions (especially late-game ones) kinda require you to use grenades. Like 6-7 enemies are grouped in a tiny room toughener. Of-course you can lure them 1 by 1, but instead you can simply throw a grenade and you are done. If enemies had more patrolling AI that would be awesome. Instead of them just chilling in 1 room forever.7. Some maps are ridiculously small. I probably always compare to Commandos 2 (which I shouldn't do). But when a map takes you 10min to beat (without speed running) it kinda feels lackluster. 8. The storage in your base is buggy once it has lots of items. You cannot properly click on things for them to work.The awesome parts:1. Abilities of some chars really feel strong and you enjoy using them2. The story is pretty cool and makes a lot of sense3. Voice acting (I was playing with Russian audio) is just so rich4. Base aspect is a pretty unique twist for this genre. Works okay overall5. Maps are very nice looking 6. Enemies are not put in a crazy tight way. You can always find that stealth undetected approach pretty easilyThank you dear Devs for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll probably finish it later, but the game doesn't feel fun or plays good at all.While most things can be acceptable in my opinion, the fact that I have input issues in a strategy game together with weird AI and a janky UI interaction just makes the game hard to enjoy.Let's bash on the enemies for now. The enemies will know where you are as soon as you throw a grenade. They will then proceed to hunt you down, always know where you are and will follow you through bushes and any obstacle you can put in between. They might eventually stop chasing you and go into search mode, but you've probably crossed the entire play area before that happens. You're guaranteed to lose almost all firefights since your accuracy is chance based and the enemy is very aggressive. Remember that flanking is very difficult, because they will know where the guy is that you've been hiding in a bush. The game seems to encourage you to play everything stealth which I typically enjoy (played both commandos and og men of war, but will sometimes put you into situations where combat is forced and therefore not fun.Let's move on to both UI and object/world interaction with your characters.While I don't hate much about the UI, there are some issues I sometimes faced. Most of them come down to interaction with objects or corpses for looting or moving them. I'd argue that most of the things I dislike are more personal, but there are definitely some adjustments that could be made for a better quality of life. Where I do have issues is that there are times that my characters seem to not respond properly to what I want them to do.This last part is purely my own opinion. I don't see or feel the need for the campsite. It feels like it's there to tell some bits of story and pad out the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Partisans 1941

_childDocuments_.review: In short it´s more combat and narrative oriented 3D Commandos in Russian. The Eastern Front - and especially the partisan efforts against operation Barbarossa aren´t usually the scenarios that are depicted in video games and that worked great as a backdrop for the game and the building of your troops and equipment and the plot through the campaign felt realistic enough. The main difference to Commandos (I don´t think you can talk about this game without mentioning Commandos) is that has a real plot and real characters - even though you probably end up using 3-4 same characters over and over.As a Finn it was interesting to see the Finnish portrayed as the evil Axis who perish in the hands of partisans of Karelia and the main character is said to have risen in his rank in the Finnish/Winter War. All in all a pretty good game with, most of complaints I can think of are of the game stability and towards the end I was keeping my fingers crossed it won´t brake before the end. Also the base building part seemed too bare boned and I´m not sure if the food count worked properly. Maybe some balancing could be done as you can only choose 3 partisans per mission and most of them just end up sitting in the camp. I don´t think chose the medic even once. Towards the end your characters become pretty much terminators and you can decimate legions of nazis with ease if you just have enough grenades and mines and the only thing stopping total carnage is lack of ammunition. Speaking of carnage - there should have been more gore in my taste to make the war hell. If you like real time tactics, guerilla warfare and world war 2 I highly recommend to give it a shot.

Overal a very fun and challenging game that sticks close to the gameplay of it's Pappenheimers and well wurth playing if you enjoyed those.

_childDocuments_.review: The worst human conflict in history has arrived at the doorstep of the Soviet Union. Pacts, non-aggression agreements and an adventurous albeit misguided expedition into Finland has not prepared the USSR fully for what has showed up with a deadly blade at its throat. The Motherland has been invaded on every front. The industrial heart of the USSR, Ukraine, has been seized by the Germans and Belarus is facing endless purges of villages. The Red Army leadership, having just narrowly survived the Great Purge, is forced to retreat to the cities of Leningrad, Moscow and Stalingrad. The Third Reich holds the industry hostage, but now - they must grasp the lifeblood of the nation. The tendrils of German fascism pierce like a bayonet into the iron heart of the USSR and as the Red Army reorganizes for a desperate defense, for an eventual desperate push, they must rely on the partisans left behind.Anyone who believes themselves too small to make a difference, have never tried to sleep in a humid room, on a summer night, with a single fly buzzing around them. The partisans are greatly outnumbered and many of them lack the ideological loyalty of the Red Army. The feared insurgents that strike the vulnerable veins and arteries of the invading German plunderer are motivated instead by a renewed civic nationalism and a loyalty to freedom from life under occupation. If one is incapable of fighting formally for their country, at the very least they can die for it.The Second WWII/Great Patriotic War has become a biblical event in the modern world, especially for the former Soviet Bloc. To this day, its imagery, heroic tales and also the unspeakable horrors that occurred during the Eastern Front, have forever remained a stronger creation myth to the modern Russian people than the story of Adam and Eve. In much the same way how the Pacific War of the same conflict had forever changed the geography of Far Eastern Nations and created today, the major powers of the Pacific that stand now, much of Eastern Europe remembers this war with equal amounts horror, sorrow and also appreciation for a generation of men, women and even children, who endured the endurable and overcame arguably one of the greatest armies of mankind. But not everyone had a choice. Whether it be forced recruitment, conscription, "moral obligation" or merely survival, humanity's greatest conflict is home to some of humanity's greatest stories. Are all of them true? Unlikely, but as humans, we cherish the ideal stories just as much as we mourn the reality. Truly, the second world war was a behemoth meeting of superpowers and often, a lot of what lead up to it was nearly nonsensical, but almost fated by the fact that the world only tolerates one superpower at once. The war of Germany against Eastern Europe was two spheres of civilization clashing. At an immense and great cost, Stalin's communism had turned the USSR into a superpower by the end of the war and Hitler already had a mountain of corpses and destruction from the last war to build a similar beast out of the remnants of Germany.Ignoring the political ramifications of those, today, who assert a modern revisionist soviet identity (in reality, a civic Russian nationality that ignores the significance of other nationalities of the 'near abroad') - this game is really about a nation, that was composed not just of Russians, but Kazakhs, Ukrainians of a much broader and stronger identity than merely 'communist', etc who fought off an invasion and in turn, had to become beasts themselves. The USSR is not sinless, but this game exists not to critique the USSR as much as it is to be fun.The game is Russian jank, so there will be immense headaches. But the characters, of a variety of backgrounds and spoken languages (play this game in the Russian dub, obviously) are distinct enough to make missions a nightmare or a breeze. Personally, my preferred character selection actually made this game overwhelmingly easy, especially after I got a former prisoner with a whistle-lure and rib-shank ability. The later stages of the game became less about trial, error and patience and more about patience, as I expertly maneuvered partisans to attack in synchronized stealth ambushes.The game allows you to go loud fairly often and whether you are fighting locals who have sold out their country to work for Germany or the elite infantry of the SS, the ability to actually pause combat and orchestrate your coordinates attacks mid firefight in a nearly RTS way, gives the game incredible leverage for when ♥♥♥♥ goes south. However, some levels are timed and have insta-fails for breaking stealth in certain sections. These are simultaneously the best and worst missions by far. The first stealth only mission was entirely garbage, but there is a part where you enter a Dulag (don't worry, the loading screens, despite last less than a second, will give you the definition of this almost every single time while playing) and it is by far some of the most fun I've had in a game of this sort in a long time.The UI scaling is complete trash, a lot of the UI itself is hostile to the user and sorting ammo is a screaming nightmare. If you try and play too casually, your partisans will waste ammo in an engagement a literal 14 year old with a double-barrel hunting shotgun could accomplish with some coordination and the path finding is somehow worse than Warhammer 40k's first Dawn of War. Moving groups all at once rather than individually will sometimes result in an ambitious partisan, often unsuccessfully, sneaking between the gaps of standing German SS soldiers or moving around a building, sometimes through a building, in clear view of the entire German army. The door system is atrocious and combined with the fact the game mandates constant save scumming, you sometimes end up wasting a lot of time setting up for a simple scoop-and-poop house raid, only to be playing the RNG game of "will the German with his 360 degree Naruto side character vision see me through this wall as I stab his boyfriend", and that is IF you don't happen to open the wrong door, revealing your entire team to the German garrison like they had just won a gameshow and their prize is relentlessly murdering you instantly with submachine gun fire.I had a glitch on the mission Bertha, where I was not able to leave due to a dog stuck in the corner of the map, alert at nothing at all. After killing the dog, I was able to leave, but I had killed at least 20 guards in the process of getting to him, then had to move all of their bodies into bushes. It was a pain in the ass.During the Dulag escape, I also had to carry a comrade to a BTR for an escape, but during a reload of a save, he was swapped out for a random dead body for some reason and I had to run aaaaaaall the way back to the second floor of the prison and then carry him aaaaaall the way back to the BTR, while being slow as ♥♥♥♥ and dodging patrols with dogs and numerous sentries. It was boring to say the least.The game has a low stakes, but strangely addicting camp management system that is mostly for show, but really, I loved it and the dialogue between the characters is surprisingly sharp.A mix between Soviet war dramas and Partisan horrors-of-war films, this game is solid. I recommend playing it if you have high patience and a lot of experience with similar games. The publishers also released Shadow Tactics, I believe, but they also released Golum, so buying a game from them is always a gamble. I am unfamiliar with the Russian developers themselves, as their page link on the steam store is defunct and it seems now this game is abandoned.Other than a few glitches, on the cheap side, you should totally get this game for the sole fact you can send a 14 year old and a convicted, alcoholic criminal on a mission to stab people in the woods. Making it the most realistic depiction of Slavic life.

name: Severed Steel
detailed_description: Severed Steel is a single-player FPS featuring a fluid stunt system, destructible voxel environments, loads of bullet time, and a unique one-armed protagonist. It's you, your trigger finger, and a steel-toed boot against a superstructure full of bad guys. Chain together wall runs, dives, flips, and slides to take every last enemy down. Key Features A Unique Fighter Play as Steel, a nimble, one-armed sharpshooter on a mission. There is no reloading – pick your shots well and be ready to pry a loaded weapon from your enemies' cold dead hands. Stylish Combat Dodge bullets, leap off walls, slide kick, throw weapons – do whatever it takes to come out on top in intense and frenzied firefights. Fully Destructible Environment Punch through thick concrete with .50 cal slugs, or make big holes in things with your arm cannon. Carve your own path through completely destructible levels. Dynamic AI No two battles are the same thanks to dynamic, unscripted, squad-based AI. Firefight Mode Chase high scores and fast times for leaderboard acclaim in this arcade-styled mode. Features 42 levels, each with their own sub-challenges, and over 20 unlockable, game modifying 'Mutators'. Campaign Mode Blast through six compact story chapters as you battle against the forces of nefarious mega-corporation, EdenSys. Finish the campaign and want more? Try New Game + mode which mixes up the campaign for a fresh playthrough. Rogue Mode Severed Steel with Rogue-lite elements. Click the Rogue Steel button on the main menu to start a short, randomly generated, 10 level campaign. Features unlockable perks, skins, and more. Accessibility A range of adjustable settings for features such as difficulty, visuals, audio, controls, navigation, and more. Level Editor (with Steam Workshop support) Build levels and share them with the community. Note: This feature is in beta and will continue to be updated post-launch.

_childDocuments_.review: PLAY THIS GAMEfor those on the fence this game has about an hour and a half of actual campaign but it's pulse pounding the entire time. After my playthrough I felt worn out.This game is what I affectionately call "F.E.A.R's EDGE" because of the obvious inspirations from the games F.E.A.R and Mirror's Edge. The game is a fast, violent, arcadey trick shooter that has the ability to slow down time so you can land those perfect matrix style flip shots through the air or hang up side down and spin around like its a John Woo film. The mechanics let a casual player have a great time, and speedrunners and score attackers have a brilliant kill-chaining tryhard-fest. The game is overall pretty decently difficult but I would say it's fair over all. There were very few times I died where it wasn't my own fault. My only legitimate criticisms are: Sometimes when I click LMB or RMB during a dive it seems unresponsive. it worked like 90% of the time, but I can only imagine a world where it works 100% of the time so I can truly pop off.The story is HELLA ambiguous that only really displays the plot through these short motion graphics. I want to know more about what is going on and where things are going and what happen and there isn't really anything to grab onto here. Lastly the Campaign is only about an hour and a half. The game play is so good I was hoping for at least another 3 hours of content at least. I do appreciate the arcadey mode (Firefight) to be able to revisit levels with new gear and variants and modifiers. I just have no idea why the levels would be locked behind a separate leveling meter after you already beat the game in story mode. Seems a tad Extra. in the end this is a game about the gameplay so for that this gets a very high recommendation from me.I will definitely be all up in the workshop trying out some of these levels people come up with. I am very hungry for more content!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really conflicted on this game.Severed Steel is a perfectly competent FPS, nothing it does is bad, per-se, it's just quite shallow.Its unique mechanics are all fun and satisfying to use, but are very simple and mostly have single uses.Its style system seems interesting but the way it's executed makes it play like ticking off a checklist.Its parkour system links your survivability to staying mobile, but chaining together the same two or three moves makes you practically invincible and the movement around it is floaty and un-inspiring.Its enemies are very simple and all but two of them are killed with a single headshot from any weapon.Its guns are varied and interesting but mostly feel interchangeable as you automatically pick up and equip new ones.Its visuals are unique and interesting in a lot of ways, but feel very "Unity default" when you look closer.I'm sure there's depth to this game I'm not aware of, but from what I see it can't be very much.Overall, a solid, fun game to get on sale, but not one I'm drawn to spend much time on.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is something I've been on board with with since the demo. The premise is simple, the dev is cool and the gameplay is tight - mostly.Something unique to my current version is a number of occasions where weapons and abilities simply haven't fired, and in a game this heavily tied to twitch reponses that's often a death sentence. It could just be a problem with my mouse driver but I haven't noticed it elsewhere.In any case, I still give this game a hearty recommend, since I've still made it to the last level and what a variety of levels there is! Some of it is more story related, some of it is weird and creepy (START. THE. RELAXATION. PROCESS.) and some of it is just balls-to-the-wall weird fun which requires no justification. There's train levels, scaling buildings, a disco fight, a giant mech boss and a garden hedge maze you can burn through with a flame-thrower.At the very least, grab the demo, give it a whirl, and blow up some walls to the dulcet tones of that bangin' soundtrack.

_childDocuments_.review: i havent posted any formal reviews before and havent played this game that much, but nevertheless (theres a little razzle dazzle™ for ya) i'll share my critiquesalso, certainly important to specify i play on very low graphics settings, so things i say about polish are likely wrong1. Slow motionslow motion is a near limitless rescource if you have any idea what you're doing, as during dives it never runs out, and there is no limit to dive spamming, and kills give a large amount of it. combining slow motion and tricks definitely makes you feel like a badass in large combat situations, but if you are un-immersed for whatever reason it feels sluggish and spammy2. "Luck"the luck meter is an interesting take on the healthbar, trying to replace the whole "supersoldier" vibe, and allowing health on kill to still be immersive and fun, however due to the ability to spam slow motion, the fact that during dives you take no damage, and the small maximum health, makes a system that feels very unfair.3. Responsea large amount of features arent very responsive, the arm cannon, hits, kills, getting hit, getting killed, movement, all of them simply not having enough polish to make it feel natural4. Weapons and Enemiesfinally something i can not be 99% negative about, the weapons feel amazing, they're fun, you get many options, and despite the large amount of options the fact you have to grab new ones every so often gets you a feel for the arsenal. the kick and arm cannon generally dont seem that good of options for general use but i can see why from a game design perspective. the enemies (technically) drop small amounts of ammo with a low capacity forces you to constantly kill and get close up5. objectivesdestroy, find, kill, that's it. maybe move around a bunch but not much to sayoverall? good game, imo needs more work

_childDocuments_.review: Short but brilliant in its simplicity. Levels represent a collection of arenas with basic objectives: push buttons, destroy objects, kill enemies. It is too short to get old, and it provides replay value with New Game+, Firefight, and Rogue modes.Enemies do not take much to go down and flinch when damaged, unless it is a rarely encountered heavy with a weak spot on his back. Enemies are also a bit trigger-happy - they start spraying even before they start tracking the player character. Additionally, it is somewhat annoying to see them spawn out of thin air sometimes, but it does keep the player on move.In addition to a familiar selection of firearms and the hole-punching arm-fitted cannon, the player character can slow down time, dive, slide, kick, run along the walls, and steal enemy weapons when close enough. Movement abilities make the player dodge all bullets, so performing them often is vital at higher difficulties (these modes are for fun only and seem to have no associated achievements)

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, this is a movement shooter about feeling stylish. The movement abilities, the destructible environments, and all the FPS mechanics are streamlined and simplified so you can focus on having fun. No reloading or aiming down sights; the game focuses instead on you moving around like crazy and jumping from enemy to enemy, stealing their weapons in the process. It's so fun to go soaring in the air, blast a hole through a wall, and thread the needle through your own destructive shortcut, or to slide on the ground, build up speed down a staircase, and crash into a group of enemies like bowling pins. The campaign is really short, around 2 hours, and your mileage with the high-score chasing Firefight mode will vary. My large hour count is from the extremely grindy achievements (completing 25 runs!) for the "roguelike" mode, which was basically just a randomized playlist of 10 levels with a very small pool of gameplay modifiers. Still! The game kicks ass, and I got it at 90% off, which was a great deal. I would recommend waiting for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you enjoy games like SuperHot and movement shooters, "Severed Steel" is definitely worth your attention.Severed Steel combines Titanfall-style movement with a slow-motion mechanic reminiscent of SuperHot, which was clearly an influence. The game's highlight is its stunt system, allowing you to slide, dive, and wall-run to avoid damage. This system, while straightforward, offers a high skill ceiling, enabling you to chain movements together and navigate levels with increasing speed. The game also features a slow-motion meter that refills with each kill and doesn't deplete while performing stunts, encouraging a fluid and highly mobile style of play. You can chain wall runs into kick-slides, snatch weapons directly from enemies' holsters, and dive behind them in slow motion to unleash a flurry of bullets.Despite the game's lack of diverse enemy types—offering only a few that behave similarly—the campaign remains engaging and concise, ensuring it doesn't overstay its welcome. The level design is generally strong, providing plenty of tactical options for movement and interaction within destructible environments. However, some levels do feature objectives that are frustratingly difficult to locate. This was never too much of a problem however, as each level is entirely destructible!For Steam Deck owners, I played this one entirely on the deck, and it feels like it was tailor made for it. Pump the graphics up (tick simple lighting and particle effects though) and you can run this at over 75fps minimum, more likely ~80fps. The game feels like it was built for gyro controls, which I found incredibly satisfying to use - I recommend binding gyro to your slow-motion button (left trigger by default) but otherwise leaving your right thumbstick/trackpad as a normal joystick.Overall, this game comes highly recommended from me.

_childDocuments_.review: KILL THEM ALL.Severed Steel is like a beautifully stylish amalgamation of the fast-paced frenetic action of DOOM, the futuristic and neon-infused aesthetic of Ghostrunner, the environmental destructibility of Red Faction or Battlefield, and the slow-mo bullet time mechanics pioneered by Max Payne, all set to a pumping soundtrack a la Hotline Miami, where the BPM never drops below 100. With a simple yet addictive gameplay loop, Severed Steel offers tons of replay value even after you've completed its short but sweet campaign.The game has you play as Steel, a mute, one-armed woman hell-bent on killing anything and everything in her way to... something. Admittedly, Severed Steel is very light on plot and story, but, like the particles and shell casings you leave behind as you rampage your way through its many levels, there are enough little sprinklings for you to piece together a larger narrative. As mentioned, the gameplay loop is very simple, but very addicting. You start each level with a simple objective (see above) and how you accomplish that objective is up to you. Of course. you'll have dozens of faceless, heavily-armed goons standing in your way, but let's just say they won't be standing for long. You learn early on how to traverse the world of Severed Steel, using jumps, double-jumps, wall-runs, dives, and slides to get the drop on your enemies as you gracefully fly through each level. There's a good sense of variety throughout the game, as some levels are centered around verticality, requiring you to ascend higher and higher towards your objective, while others aim to evoke a sense of claustrophobia, locking you into tight corridors overflowing with enemies. Like the aforementioned DOOM and Ghostrunner, there are several ways to get across each level, and like DOOM and Ghostrunner, staying still almost always spells certain death.Severed Steel should really be called "Stylish Steel," as simply running around each level and killing enemies isn't always the ideal path to victory. The levels are designed to allow you the freedom to use the game's exaggerated physics to your advantage in a number of ways. For example, a typical encounter may see you jump, shoot an enemy, double-jump and spin around 180 degrees to shoot another enemy, then turn another 90 degrees, dive through a window, steal another enemy's weapon out of their hands, and finally land in a slide where you shoot the enemy whose weapon you just stole... with their own weapon! You're also going to want to use your slow-mo ability as often as possible, as this can help with precise aiming as well as chaining together multiple kills in a single move. While the campaign doesn't feature an arcade-style mode, you are encouraged to come up with your own stylish ways of dispatching your foes - experimentation is key!The enemy and weapon variety will also change how you approach Severed Steel's many levels, as some enemies can only be harmed by hitting a particular weak point, while others are more bullet sponges and will require several rounds to put down. You'll be swapping weapons quite frequently, as most weapons have limited ammo counts and will quickly *click* empty, requiring you to grab another one to continue the fun. Most weapons will be pistols and machine guns, but there are also explosive weapons, sniper rifles, and even a flamethrower. Another part of your arsenal that you acquire early on is your Arm Cannon, a customizable special weapon that acts as a 'get-out-of-jail-free' card in many of the game's more tense situations. Not only can the Arm Cannon melt away enemies like they're warm butter, but it can also alter the geometry of the levels. Point the Arm Cannon at any wall, walkway, door, etc, press FIRE, and watch a hole take the place of whatever solid object was once there. This can be used to create shortcuts through walls, and even bring enemies who are above you down to your level, much to their chagrin. Ordinary weapons can also punch holes in the levels' physicality, so take some time to wander through each level before proceeding and bask in the beauty of Severed Steel's destruction physics.Beyond the campaign, there's also a New Game + mode, an arcade mode called Firefight, and daily challenge levels to keep you on your toes. There are also several modifiers to the game, which can increase/decrease difficulty, give you different versions of your Arm Cannon, give you different starting weapons, etc. I'm 6 hours into the game at the time of writing this review, and I know I easily have another 6-8 in me.Despite the fast and frenetic nature of Severed Steel, it's an overall approachable and highly entertaining experience that encourages experimentation, rewards stylish play and engagement with its many mechanics, and provides so much more to do even after you think you've seen and done it all. Definitely one of the best first-person shooters of our time.

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Description:-Severed Steel is an insanely high octane, badass fps w/ top of the line visuals and a killer soundtrack.  It feels like Max Payne, Red Faction, and Fear had a beautiful love child.  It's still in early access, so it may be a bit light on content, but the content that is offered is extremely well polished and so much fun.*Notes:-As of Jan 2022, I have played for about 7 hrs.  I played on the Severed Steel difficulty and completed the 6 chapters that are available.  I also messed around w/ the Firefight mode for about 45 minutes.  This is a game that is intended to be played many times over.  There is an N+ mode which allows you to add modifiers from the Firefight mode into the campaign levels.What's Good:-The star of the show is the slowmotion.  This feels like a modern version of the slowmo from Max Payne but put into a fps.  It's by far the most interesting mechanic introduced.  You don't have unlimited use of it, so using it strategically is very important.  Not only is it extremely fun to blast a dozen enemies while in slowmo, but it's extremely rewarding when you find out the best way to use slowmo to your advantage and survive an onslaught.  -This is one of the most visually impressive fps that I've ever played.  Very few games look this sleek, modern, and clean visually.  The devs used a lot of bright colors in front of dark backdrops that make all of the colors really pop.  The clean visuals are the perfect complement to the ridiculously fast and chaotic nature of the moment to moment gameplay.  Every piece of the environment is destructible which reminds me a lot of Red Faction.-As impressive as the visuals are, they wouldn't matter if the moment to moment combat wasn't engaging, challenging, and fun.  Fortunately, this is another area this game rises above.  This is such an incredibly fun game.  There isn't as much depth as some other fps shooters out there, but the fun factor here is extremely high.  I have loved every second of my 7 hrs playing.  It's extremely addictive and I could see myself playing this for many years to come. -Moving, jumping, using slowmo, using the hand cannon, and shooting all feel fluid and very well polished.  Putting together all of these different elements is not easy, but Severed Steel makes it work really well.  You can't approach this game the way you would a typical fps.  You have to learn when to jump, when to slide, how frequently to use the slowmo, and quickly land headshots right before stealing an enemies weapon.  If you try to stay in one place for even a few seconds, you will probably die, so get ready to move!-The soundtrack is absolutely top tier!  There are lots of different tracks, with tons of variety.  The songs feels like they were ripped straight from a John Woo movie and fit the tempo of this game perfectly.Could Use Some Changes:-The biggest complaint from just about every review is the lack of content.  I personally see no problem w/ what is available.  I found the Severed Steel difficulty to be quite challenging.  I died a lot, as it took me over 6 hrs to complete the first 6 chapters.  I think too many ppl were expecting a more typical fps experience w/ a 15-20 hr campaign.  They are planning to add more content, but as of now, there are only 6 chapters.-As fun and challenging as this game is, this isn't Doom Eternal.  The skill ceiling is not as high here.  Yes, there is plenty of strategy involved when playing this, but sometimes the slowmo can be a get out of jail free card once you become really competent utilizing this mechanic.  -I wasn't very impressed w/ the bosses at all.  I think this was the biggest disappointment for me personally.  They feel like kind of an afterthought.Thoughts:-This was such a fun experience!  I'm really excited to see what future levels look like and how they implement more interesting mechanics.  The hand canon has a couple of variations so I could see the devs adding a few more perks which mixes levels up quite a bit.  I'm looking forward to spending some more time messing around w/ the Firefight mode.  I think there is a lot of potential for really interesting and challenging experiences once I unlock all of the modifiers.Consensus:-Solid Game (Tier 3 and makes up 35% of my reviews).  Severed Steel is beauty and chaos rolled into one well polished package.  If you grew up playing games like Max Payne or Red Faction, then you'll probably have a blast w/ this one.  If you are expecting a more traditional fps experience, then you may be disappointed w/ Severed Steel.  Take that into consideration before adding this to your library.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is quite an amazing FPS that takes inspiration from F.E.A.R., Red Faction, and even Stranglehold, blending the elements into a super brisk shooter with a lot of replay-ability.From F.E.A.R. and Stranglehold, you get a slow-mo ability that lets you relish in the destruction and mayhem you've caused, while also really feeling in control despite the odds. The enemies have their own radio chatter that The AI also reacts differently each play-through, causing some unpredictable plays each time. Furthermore, there's parkour that allows interacting with the entire level. You are able to wall-run, slides, dives and even wall-jumping. Combine this with a destructible environment, it can make each level into your own playground as you go circles around the enemy.And lastly, from Red Faction, there's a destructible environment to plow your way through with explosives and even a second ability that comes into play. So being able to blast a hole under the floor of an enemy, only to welcome them with a hail of buckshot or bullets, is going to be satisfying and silly. It also aids in the platforming at times as well.In addition, there's a map creator with Steam Workshop in order to experience the game in a different light. It is great fun to see what the community can cook up to test your skills. And both campaign and firefight modes are expanded upon with different loadouts and mutators that can be unlocked (like Floor is Lava and Big Head mode!)Unfortunately the game is quite short with the levels that can sort of blend together (yet very replayable). The super fast speed and chaotic nature of the game can be disorienting at times, especially when doing a flip.But if you're looking for an FPS that can make you feel like an agile killing machine, this is very much an experience that few have been able to replicate.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel, in the world post-John Woo, SUPERHOT, Max Payne, and the Maxtrix movies, is a game the leans heavy into its influences and creates something unique. The fluid of combat is addicting and fun while the soundtrack creates the rhythm in which you're sliding, diving, wall running, and maiming. I don't know what kind of techno-hoodoo they used but somehow the soundtrack would line up with my headshots. If that's coincidence or not has yet to remain to be seen. My biggest complaint would come from the wall running and double jumping as they felt janky and I think that may be me having issues coming from Ghostrunner where wallrunning felt more fluid. A smaller complaint is that environments are starting to blur inside my head and I don't recall what levels I did except for the night club and fighting the CEO. All and all if you're looking for a good bullet time shooter where you're a ballerina of bullets and carnage, this would be for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Did you ever wonder what if Max Payne was a woman who lost her arm and she was taking acid instead of painkillers? Severed Steel is exactly that.It's a high-octane movement shooter that rewards the player for perfoming stunts like diving, sliding and wallrunning with invincibility and infinite slow-mo. Don't expect tactiful gunfighs like in F.E.A.R. where you use slow-mo mostly when you feel overwhelmed, here you throw yourself at your enemies to live. You can't sidestep individual bullets like in Max Payne or Super Hot, you have rely on stunts to dodge. Healing is done by killing people, so it's like Doom but without the middle-man.Since your arm is replaced with a canon, you can't reload. Instead you constantly pick up a fresh gun from fallen enemies (or steal from a still breathing ones). Mentioned canon is able to blow holes in the fully destructable levels, letting you make new routes on the fly.The main campaign is roughly 60 minutes and it's mostly great. Mostly, because the last couple of levels are centered around the level destruction and it hurts the flow a lot. Main sauce is in firefights, that are campaign levels with sole goal of killing everyone. Mutators let you spice it up a bit, make it harder, easier or sillier. There's also a level editor (currently in beta), so potential is unlimited.To me, Severed Steel to Ultrakill is what Bayonetta to DMC. I personally enjoy Severed Steel more due to the freedom of movement it allowes. Did I mention when in the air you can freely move your camera, letting you shoot enemies while upside down? It might feel confusing at first, untill you realize that slow mo gets even slower, giving you sweet time to line up that headshot and look absolutely badss while doing so.My verdict is BUY THIS GAME RIGHT NOW.On the side note, I recommend turning off Bloom in graphics setting, because otherwise your eyes will hurt every time you go into slow mo.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This game slaps.I could sell you on it by citing its inspirations or comparing it to other games, but its not sufficient.You have slomo, guns, sliding, diving, and can break through the walls. Beating a level in less than a minute because of clever positioning of shots in the level is a great feeling.Highly recommend, especially for the price, very high replayability with the extra modes.

_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is kind of short, but that is no showstopper. Plenty of great games are short because they manage to fit all they need in those hours (for a few well-known - Flower, Journey, all of Freebird games). The strength of those other games lies in the fact they have a complete package (an experience, however much I hate the word) to offer. Severed Steel does not...The game has reasonable presentation - a rather good soundtrack and decent (far from great, but manageable) graphics.What breaks the charm, though, is the lack of... Anything besides slo-mo. In its current state Severed Steel looks like a rough pre-alpha tech demo for an early 2000s game engine. There is no plot, there is no level design to speak of (it's all very simplistic and boxlike), there is no atmosphere or reason. Nothing besides shooting bad guys is slo-mo. And destructible levels, yes. You can destroy the levels around you.And the slo-mo itself is also pretty mediocre. Initially it feels very floaty and devoid of friction, so it's hard to gauge where you're going to land or what you can catch on. You just slowly fly left and right or up and down (and you have to, to avoid enemy gunfire), while shooting enemies. Max Payne, Ghostrunner and whatever else used slo-mo as a tool among others. Severed Steel used slo-mo as the main mechanic and that gets boring prety fast.The combat overall feels nice - you can kick enemies and automatically pick up guns, but, again - the entire thing is pure sugar, not frosting on a tasty cake.I feel like I have to specifically mention it again - there is no plot or explanation. There are hand drawn cutscenes without text and there are different in-game objectives (some of those feel like a pathetic attempt at... humor?) from "Kill them all" to "Destroy this or that thing", "Meet 6 cool guys" and "Engage in stress relief excercise". Those do not require any special action. Just slo-mo through a few dozen dudes and reach a point. Quite meh.The firefight mode is there, but... What incentive is there to play it?
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is gives you what you want, if what you want is a fast paced arena shooter with great mobility options and slow mo effect. The only way to heal is to kill, the only way to get more slow mo is to kill, and the only way forward is to kill. One thing that made this game for me is the unlocked camera while in the air in addition to the increased slow mo effect the more extreme your angle is. If you are fully inverted time slows to a near stand still giving you some time to take in everything that is happening. Also you have a plasma gun attached to your arm letting you blow up walls and enemies. This gives you so many options as to how to you want to approach any given room. The speed of the player reminds me of Quake back in the day, the way they give you instructions is SUPERHOT, but the mixing of mobility and slow mo really makes this game something special. The game is short and sweet. If you only play the games for their campaigns I could see the game being too short for you but its a game I keep coming back to. Couldn't recommend this game any higher.

_childDocuments_.review: I started with the demo, and the first few levels of this game definitely had me wondering if I would enjoy it, messing around with the movement mechanics and getting used to the flow of the game. I had this feeling I'd probably play through the demo and call it good, because everything just seemed a little weird. Then I got to the first level with actual combat, and at first I really thought I was just going to drop it, but when the music kicked in, I knew I had to at least get through the demo. After a few tries trying to understand the flow of combat, something clicked, and all of a sudden I knew that this would be one of my favorite games I've ever played. Fast forward 5 hours to 4 A.M. and I had beat the game in one sitting, because it was just that addicting, The only time I had closed the game was to buy the full game after I beat the demo. Only complaints being the slide and dive can be a little weird/janky to use at times, and I ran into two bugs with the slide, one of which I had to fix by resetting the level. Easy 9.5/10, felt like a $25 five hour high.

_childDocuments_.review: What do you get when you mix the movement of Titanfall 2, the time slowdown of Max Payne, and the arena based levels from SUPERHOT? you get Severed Steel, a super fast fps where every cool thing that you can do makes you invincible, such as wall running, diving, and even front flips. Using the invincibility mechanic along with the time slowdown and the fully destructible areas gets you pulling off some incredibly cool and satisfying kill combos witch keeps your health and slowdown replenished. Some of the negatives are the short campaign along with it's almost non existent story and how fast the game is making it rely heavily on time slowdown causing it to be incredibly difficult to play without it. Overall I found the game incredibly fun and have already started the new game +, something I rarely do after finishing a game. If you liked any of the games I mentioned above I would expect you to have a blast playing Severed Steel.
