_childDocuments_.review: I’ve long had this dream game in my head of a free flowing parkour fps arena shooter that has so much style to it. Little did I know that someone had already just recently done it. To me, this is as close to a perfect parkour fps game as you can get. From the extremely open ended combat that allows for so much experimentation, constant weapon swapping to encourage aggression, varied and packed levels, and so much love poured into it; it’s amazing. My only gripe is that I wish the story was better told. While it has hints of something going on; I could barely follow what was happening. Still, with gameplay this good, it really doesn’t need to worry. Can’t recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This game grants you one of the closest experiences to roleplaying Neo from the Matrix that I have ever played, period.You have bullet time mechanics, wall running, sliding, diving, and even somersaulting and level destruction. Truly an amazing experience. Also seems to have lots of re-playable value with the firefight and rogue-light modes, and lets you have a "head-empty, shoot some baddies while being badass" gaming session. One of the  moments that stuck with me in the game was when I entered one of the firefight levels and one of the challenges was something along the lines of "Get 3 headshots while upside down", which made me scratch my head at first wondering how to even attempt that, but was my first foray into discovering that you are granted 360 degree camera control and can literally "flip" while using the dive mechanic, letting you jump over enemies and plug them in the head or in the back while you were flying over them. Although, I must say that some of the levels can be disorienting, especially with the lighting (some levels are REALLY dark, and have sparse, bright neon lights here and there), and constant flipping and dashing around. It plays smoothly, but I definitely would not recommend playing this while heavily drunk/under the influence, I can forsee it getting nauseating, fast. Also, if you are expecting some form of story or lore, don't get too excited over this one. There is an overarching story to the campaign, but it's nothing much and isn't too inspired. Go into the game expecting an action experience with minimal to no plot, just shooting baddies.If you see this on sale, definitely pick it up to give it a try, one of the more refreshing and entertaining shooting experiences of recent memory that I've had. If you liked SUPERHOT and how badass it made you feel, but wanted a more involved and faster-paced action-shooting experience, this is it.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a game with a story line and immersive dialogue, DO NOT BUYIf you are looking for a challenging game at the highest possible difficulty in a solo play fashion, BUY THIS GAME.Playing this game at anything besides the highest level of difficulty means you will more than likely finish it within 3 hours and make it a complete waste of money and time. If you are not a boomer gamer, and actually look for a challenge I recommend playing this game at the MOLTEN STEEL difficulty level. The mechanics feel a bit wonky at first, however you will soon learn that it doesn't really give you a terrible experience in the long-run.Just keep this in mind, any game can be short if you play in easy difficulties. Play this game at the MOLTEN STEEL level and I promise you it will be worth the purchase. Firefights are also a fun challenge setting as well after completing the campaign missions.All-in-all:Storyline is dogsh*t, I have no idea what I just played through.Mechanics and game-play are fun AF.For $22, it was worth the 8 hours of entertainment.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: game is a high octane action packed run n gun with super fun combat. my only issue was that without relying too much on the slow mode and stunts, the game can be very hard (unless you have amazing aiming skills). I wouldn't recommend it at full price since the story mode is only 2.5 hours long but if you can catch it on sale, its a definite yes for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Never have I ever felt like such a badass in a game before, and I've played Doom Eternal.The movement is amazing once you get the hang of it after like 2 minutes, slowing down time is so much fun especially getting headshots through time slowdown too, and the wall running is really well done.Taking guns off enemies is fluid and easy to do in a moment of panic when you have no ammo for your current gun, Kicking enemies is the only slight issue I have in that it feels a little rough for me but I can deal with it.The Music is really really good and not music I thought could go with a game like this but it was pulled off amazingly and will even give you more money and get the soundtrack just to support you.The game also runs almost flawless even with raytracing on at 120 fps, sometimes with grenade launchers and lots of explosions can cause hitches but its rare.All the graphics and hud options to chose from is really good to include, the default fov is great and has a slider to adjust it.Just finished the game and with a playtime of almost 2 hours and i'm fine with that as there is firefight mode and steam workshop, would love to see maybe free and paid dlcs in the future, its fine if there isn't but it would be great.So far this could be my game of the year, if the Developer is reading this I don't care how short the game is, the game play for me is 10/10.You created a really fun game and for me you will get my steam nomination at the end of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: fun actiony game. offers similar gameplay to ultrakill but differs in a few major ways.the enviroment is shapeable, though thats of limited utility at times as the arm cannon and grenade launcher are usually otherwise occupied dealing with other issues or out of ammo.enemies are considerably more aggressive and dangerous, maybe a bit too aware as well. often i'll attempt a flank through a wall or glass pane only for the enemy to begin shooting and then instantly face me. sure they aren't accurate, but their time to kill (me) is relatively fast, and the punishment for death is starting over.diving is a mechanic you don't see often, its effectively another jump that has mostly horizontal movement that seems to disable for the most part your ability to wallrun, effectively making it a self unlife button near pits. don't really recommend using it often.bullet time is a fun mechanic as ever, but i think the game is over centralized around it at the moment, being able to hit an enemy while moving considerably faster than most any shooter without decreasing their speed by a factor of  10 or so deserves a greater reward than them simply being dead in my opinion.on the positive however, the game players well, feels mostly good, looks great and is a ton of fun, i just think the above if solved could lead to a much better overall package that would leave a much stronger impression. by and far id say changing the enemy ai is the number 1 thing i want. i wouldn't  say i want this to be a stealth game, but id like enemies act less like automated moving turrets that all get alerted at once and more like humans dealing with an extremely fast handicapped person. i'd like to draw extra attention to the fact that any gunshot turns the remainder of the map into an extended gunfight, i think thats a bad thing more than a good.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent adrenaline shooter ! Good level design working well with the voxel-breaking mecanic, good gunfeel, confortable controls and excellent soundtrack ! The difficulty may be inconsistent on some levels but you can it change anytime. Surprisingly well optimised, running like a charm on my POS laptop.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: If Titanfall, John Woo films, Cyperpunk all got mixed in a big pot with acid you'd get this game. The combat is 200mph, the gunplay is chaotic, but precise, you feel the weight of every jump, slide, slowdown, and shot and carefully weigh up those micro decisions in every room, and every gunfight. There is very little to complain about, the main issue is it's story being only 2 hours long.This is  the most fun I've had in a shooter since Doom Eternal, but I want more! On sale, its worth a punt if you like arena/movement shooters and destroying your brain
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Some of the most satisfying gunplay I've ever encountered in a game, and the best one that includes slow-mo. F.E.A.R. ran so Severed Steel could fly--at a wall, kick off it, then backflip over an enemy and headshot him, flawlessly transition into a slide on the ground, stealing another enemy's gun while you throw them off balance, and blowing their brains out from behind before they even have time to glance over their shoulder.The dev is still adding content and clearly passionate about the game. The visual style is very distinctive--but for those who might experience eye-strain from bloom and the like, there's options to turn effects down, or disable certain elements (even those of the HUD) altogether, something that I, as someone with chronic migraines, really appreciate being an option.The story isn't really much more than a way to get you from one level to the next, but then that's not what you're here for; you're here to get your dose of adrenaline as you slaughter your way through three dozen unlucky goons in under a minute because you don't have time for their shenanigans, you've got places to be and people to kill. And that's exactly what Severed Steel delivers--and then some.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most fun shooters I've played in a while. The DnB soundtrack is entrancing, and liberal supply of slowmo makes it less exhausting than something like Ultrakill. Despite being a high-octane run n gun, it can be oddly relaxing. The graphical style is wonderful and the fully-destructible environments make for a different experience each time you play. The main campaign has plenty of levels and there are tons of bonus levels on top of that. It also has two additional modes. It's just so good.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Believe me, every single time you hit that slowmo button you will feel amazing. Sliding below a desk, shooting enemies on the knee, diving through small gaps on the wall then jumping over a group and landing headshots UPSIDE-DOWN while there's this amazing EDM track playing in the back setting the rythm... I needed that, this game reminded me that games are supposed to be fun.If you really want to extend the experience try the hardest difficulty, where the pacing of the game changes completely, becoming a combat puzzle where you'll have to execute everything perfectly in order to beat the levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is the only time where you're allowed to say it feels great to play one handed. This is in reference to the main characters having a cannon in her left hand to deform the level to allow so much creative freedom in one of the best fast-paced movement shooters that is becoming a new sub-genre. If you haven't already bought this game, you're missing out on a great blend of slow-mo action that fans of Max Payne, Fear and Titanfall fans would have wet dreams of. It's the new standard for this sub-genre. Many updates have come out further to add value since I played in it 2022, like a new rogue-like mode, more missions, and dual-welding. It even has New Game+ that re-tweaks the enemy placements if you thing the game is too short and don't want to do it's rogue-like mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, the movement is amazing and might be my favourite movement in any video game. If you like Ultrakill, Trepang or any game of that sort, do try this game out. Story is a decent length, not too long, not too short but is still on the short side, however there's tons of challenges and different maps to play through, a gamemode where it's different every time, all that good stuff. Amazing game, I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel has to be one of the most fun games I've played in a while. Great gameplay with an amazing soundtrack, however, its VERY short (~6 hours for a complete playthrough) The best way I can describe this game is ghostrunner mixed with superhot and a dash of portal lol If you're on the fence, I'd highly recommend jumping the gun and getting it.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This game makes you feel like an absolute badass. It is so much fun to just slide, jump, and bullet time shoot enemies. If you want to feel like a super cool, ultimate unstoppable badass fighting hordes of enemies with SUPERHOT like mechanics but even better, this is the game for you. I 100%'d the game in 49 hours, and I don't regret it at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome! Every level feels like the last. The gameplay is smooth and fulfilling. All cutscenes are skippable. The levels may be a bit long, but you can then do an easier mode. Also, you get to kill a CEO and burn his mansion. How cool is that? Also, lots of custom levels like in Prodeus (I got that on GOG)
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: One of the shorter games I've played but definitely one of the best games I've ever played. The slow down is smooth, the shooting is extremely well done. (Although there are a few times where it feels like I shouldn't have killed an enemy, but that's ok cause the game is still phenomenal). The graphics are insanely beautiful, even on low end computers. Speaking of low end computers it plays really well on my crappy laptop, I never once experienced any frame skipping or resolution errors.Overall 9/10 amazing game, good job devs. Highly recommend

_childDocuments_.review: What a fantastic game! Mixes old school shooting with destructible environments, parkour and bullet time. The game is very easy to pick up but harder to master. At first I was falling off things & dying regularly. After half an hour or so, having mastered the movement skills, the game becomes a real joy to play. The number of ways to reach your enemies, steal their weapons and kill them is nearly endless. The flow of combat is incredible which makes the game incredibly satisfying to play.Graphics are sylized but very pleasing and have a great aesthetic. Gun sounds are satisfying and the game has a very suitable sound track.The game has a relatively limited number of maps but replayability is off the charts making the game superb value for money. There's even custom maps with mutators which makes replayability even higher. Severed Steel is highly recommended for FPS fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: A mix between Superhot and FEAR. From the former you get spending most of your time in slow-mo managing your positioning, ammo and enemy placement to stay alive and effective. From the latter you have the focus on spectacle (and slow-mo obviously). The environment is destructible so you can flank enemies or skip some parts of the level.The levels themselves are small most of the time so you are engaged enemies in close quarters which, combined with your moveset, gives you different ways to deal with them. You can slide under everybody, dive through them, or wallrun across the whole level. Or combine it all fluidly one into another.The main campaign is rather short (2-3 hours). So you have other options to spend your time on: new game+, firefight mode (kill-them-all on campaign maps with different challenges), bonus maps from community, and rogue-like mode where you run through 8 or 10 maps with random buffs (and debuffs) you can choose from.Give it a try if you like fast-paced shooters.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: So fun! It's like Super Hot, Neon White, and Hotline Miami mixed together. So many moments where you are doing some absolutely awesome gun acrobatic Matrix type ♥♥♥♥ and the music is hitting just right. And destructible voxel environments! If I ever made a game, I would want to make something as cool as this. Awesome!

It is extremely fun to play, though, and I like trying to place on the leaderboards for these kinds of games so I love it. My only real criticism would be to add more categories to the scoreboards like with mutators on like floor is lava, and maybe a couple more multipliers for a little more nuance in the scoring system like kills without slo-mo, and higher consecutive kill multipliers.Highly recommended! Hopefully modding will enhance the experience as well.

The basic difficulty feels a little too easy sometimes but there's lots of replayability and difficulty modifies, and perhaps most importantly, it's just damn fun to slide into a room, spring into a dive, and shoot four guys in the back with a shotgun before blowing a hole in the floor to move on.

_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: To put it in as little words a possible; this game is if max payne (The character) had a messy night with titan fall (The physical game disk) and got titan fall pregnant with severed steel as their baby.To put it in a more articulate way; this game reminds me of games of yesteryear, in that the main focus is to give you an enjoyable gameplay experience, without deepthoating you with hours of cut-scenes and a convoluted story neither you nor I care for. Even with all that said, the story that is there is actually pretty good, albeit grossly overshadowed by the stellar gameplay. Furthermore, to touch upon the gameplay, it is so beautifully unique, with a very creative implementation of bullet-time, in which it only recovers (On normal difficulty or higher, if I remember) when you get kills, and same goes as for health re-gen. And to believe that I haven't even talked about the movement! Not only do you have a very satisfying dive, in which you can activate slow-mo to get some awesome action shots, but you also get wall-running and sliding! This game is most certainly a must-play for fans of ultra-kill, max payne, titan fall and the like! It also helps that this game often goes on sale for dirt cheap, so there's not really any reason to not buy this gem!

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★☆☆ (3/5)You snooze, you lose.The game introduces a fresh idea, allowing you to remain invulnerable as long as you move in a parkour style, and although the enemies are relatively simple, they are always trying to overwhelm you. The levels are quite different and destructible, opening the door to exploring new strategies. Unfortunately, despite finishing the campaign, I still found myself fighting the controls more than the enemies, and the review is biased because of that. Players who can master the controls will find the game more enjoyable than I did. Worth at a discount.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has me hooked. I've only had it a few days, but I already have 9 hours clocked and it hasn't gotten stale. It takes a little time to get used to, but by the end you'll be sliding and flipping around blasting heads with a myriad of fun, unique weapons. The visuals and soundtrack give the game a great style and vibe also. If you like high testosterone gameplay that makes you feel like john wick, Severed Steel will scratch that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale for 3 dollars but would happily pay the full amount after seeing what is on offer here.This is one of the most satisfying shooters I have ever played. The combat is so fast and chaotic but the game gives you just the right amount of control to make you feel like a badass each time you clear a floor.The campaign can be beaten in about 2 hours and I think it properly ramps up in intensity as you go. There are not many new mechanics after the first handful of missions, but variety is introduced through new level layouts and weapons. The real game starts after the campaign though. Besides a new game plus there is a firefight mode that lets you chase high scores and challenges you to try new strategies and a roguelike mode that has you run through a handful of campaign missions again with some interesting buffs as you go. On top of that there are a handful of bonus missions and unlockable weapons and modifiers that can be applied to any mode to make it more challenging or interesting to replay.The campaign may be short, but if this is your type of game there are dozens of hours of fun to be had here.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game, ESPECIALLY so at the 5 bucks I got it on sale for. Super short, finished in 2 hours, just within refund time (which for the sake of the developer, I hope you don't do) but jam packed with great visuals, great music, and great gameplay. There's also other gamemodes (roguelite mode, new game +, etc.) and custom maps I haven't even tried yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Ten guards wait at the door, preparing for the enemy who their colleagues radioed in about seconds before. They wait patiently, not taking the risk. Surely she is doomed; there are ten of them and one of her!Suddenly the wall to the right explodes and she jumps through, assault rifle blazing killing four men before they even figured out what happened.The jetpack troop fired his shotgun at her 3 times, but not before she dives under a desk. In one motion she then slides into him, breaking his legs and grabbing his weapon before turning it on three other soldiers.The heavy soldier fires a grenade, but misses. She kicks the gun from his hands and then fires off the remainder of the shells into him.Finally the shield user bum rushes her knowing his shield will keep him covered.She jumps, flips over him, reaches toward his belt, grabs his pistol before finally shooting one round into the back of his head before she hits the ground.Room clear! NEXT!Severed Steel is one of the most effortlessly stylish FPS games made in the past few years, combining huge chunks of Hotline Miami with F.E.A.R. all wrapped up with a chaotic parkour system in (almost) fully destructible environments. When it comes to short, sharp FPS action games you have an absolute gem on your hands with Severed Steel, albeit a really short one.What we have here is one of the new breed of, due to a lack of better term, “spectacle FPS” games; titles like Doom Eternal or Ultrakill that focus more on moment-to-moment resource management fighting enemies in small arenas with an absolute focus on the action and little else. Everything in Severed Steel is about the kinetic action and fluid movement from gunfight to gunfight, and while it lacks any other major elements it does not need them. With this in mind if you want a long game with depth and an interesting story, then Severed Steel will likely not be of interest.For those who do crave more ultraviolence however, Severed Steel differentiates itself from its peers mostly via its pacing. Like its peers like Ultrakill, Severed Steel sees its protagonist Steel fighting masses of enemies in small, boxy arenas and can only progress once a simple objective is completed, such as kill everyone or destroy a terminal etc… However Severed Steel presents virtually all characters in game, protagonist included, as a glass cannon: If someone is in the arena, they will likely go down in five shots at the most. All firefights will all foes are brief and brutal, with the average foe being taken down usually in one headshot and whole groups of enemies being wiped out in roughly five seconds flat. This combined with Steel’s inability to reload - she only has one arm - means she will move from group to group discarding empty weapons and grabbing new ones as she goes along. In this regard is sort of feels like a first-person Hotline Miami, focusing on very little downtime and fast respawns if you die.  Unlike Hotline Miami however Steel has a couple of tricks up her single sleave to help not turn this into a dying simulator: Bullet time and parkour.The bullet time in Severed Steel is more akin to that in F.E.A.R. or Max Payne than Super Hot; a button based move that lasts as long as you use it and is limited in its usage. Here Steel can slow time down for short bursts and wipe out numerous enemies at once, both enhancing her (real time) aiming as well as allowing her to predict incoming shots easier. Also like F.E.A.R. she has a number of movement enhancing moves such as slides and dives combined with more modern techniques such as mantling, wall running and double jumps. This all makes for a character that, while fragile, is so versatile in how she can take out foes that it not only opens up for numerous ways to fight her opponants as well as getting the drop on them. See a room that is chock full of enemies? Run up the wall to the space above them, blow a hole in the roof with your plasma cannon arm and then drop in from above and then shoot them in slow motion while falling upside down before sliding in and kicking the last guy in the face. It all adds up to make for one of not only one of the most fun combat experiences in a shooter in the past few years, but it also looks so absurdly stylish that videos of your performance (even when playing bad) are superb YouTube B reel fodder to make you look as cool as possible while playing.Oh yeah! Plasma cannon for an arm. You can blow holes in any wall due to the voxel based sectors in the game. Why use doors when you can make them?So with all this gushing praise, why is this not one of the most beloved FPS games from the past huge glut of shooters?Severed Steel is short. 3 hours short to be precise. While it absolutely wastes no time in what it does, it is such a blunt title that you will likely polish it off in one sitting. Granted the way it is structured means it is made to play through multiple times, each time trying to better yourself, but since there is no scoring system it is hard to grade yourself as you go. Considering the price point this really does sink Severed Steel down a lot, which is unfortunate as it is so damn good in the short time it gives you, its just a shame its not better value.Another issue is performance. Since the environment is voxel based it chokes CPUs and GPUs resulting in sub-optimal frame rates. Even with the Bullet time in game, FPS games are utterly framerate dependent and considering that I was dropping to well under 60 at times, that is not the best thing to have happen.To conclude, Severed Steel is an absolute joy for the short time it goes on. If it were a bit longer perhaps it would not work, but even then it does feel like you are being short changed considering its price point.Avoid at full price, but once it goes on sale this is, imo, more fun than Doom Eternal! Keep an eye on it!
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This is a FANTASTIC game. Rarely does a game's systems work so well together. I don't think this game contains a single bad part. The movement is extremely fun, and I love the way you can spin the camera around 360 degrees while diving. The guns sound, and feel great. The sound design in general is extremely satisfying. That includes the music, which is just perfect. It really gets your blood pumping. When I can feel my heart beating while playing a game, that's how I know it's great.If I had one criticism, it would be that the performance can REALLY chug when you enable ray traced lighting. However, that's just the RT experience, especially with a Radeon card. The resolution scaling performs well, however, which is good.I definitely recommend, even if it's not on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: If you like the punchy, second-to-second action of games like Hotline Miami or SUPERHOT, this game will be right up your alley. It's got slick, stylish movement that invites you to show off between the carnage. It's got rich music that punctuates the action and makes the incredibly fast pace feel all the more thrilling. Skill comes not just from staying oriented and landing your shots while taking full advantage of the true 360 degree turning, but from being in your element in each level, taking advantage of every wall, ledge, and window. It's been a long time since I've felt so liberated in a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: super fun game! don't try to play it like superhot or ghostrunner - this game is it's own thing. the story isn't the main point of the game but the campaign is still good, and it sets you up for firefight fairly well.(to the devs: we need a way to play back-to-back firefight levels!! unless you play with the triple threat mutation the firefight levels seem so short.)
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine, very mechanically sound but it just didn't click for me. Combat feels weightless in a way that is difficult to explain and the challenge of moment to moment gameplay is either extremely easy or extremely quick death. _childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is what you get when you mix Quake, Titanfall 2, Hotline Miami, F.E.A.R. and Max Payne. It's hard for me to find negatives when it's easily one of the most fun shooters of the past few years and will more than likely be in the Top 15 Shooters of the 2020s.For starters, the soundtrack is a blast. It's pretty much entirely old-school Jungle/Drum and Bass with a slight modern touch to it, very fitting beats for the nearly non-stop action. The controls are great and you have unlimited freedom in your movement, weapons are satisfying to use and the voxel system allows for carnage that completely destroys every level.I found the campaign to be a bit too short, finishing it in just a few hours, but almost all levels in the 6 chapters are very well designed, and there's a New Game+ mode to boot. Severed Steel also accompanies a Firefight mode that's a series of levels where you must kill a certain amount of enemies to get the highest score, completing different challenges to increase your multiplier. It's pretty fun. The third main mode is a randomly generated 10 levels run with roguelike elements.Overall, the game is addicting and very replayable, specially thanks to a level editor and Workshop support.There are two main issues with the game for me. The visuals are pretty, but both Screen Space Reflections and RTX Reflections are extremely distracting. The art style and level design make so these reflections become visual noise that can get in the way of your gameplay. Make sure to turn them off.Also, while the game runs great, it has an odd issue where the game does not recognize your mouse inputs, which is a huge deal in a fast paced game like this. I managed to fix this by right-clicking the game's .exe, going to properties -> compatibility, checking "Disable fullscreen optimizations" and playing the game on exclusive fullscreen instead of borderless.All in all, Severed Steel is a game that was well worth keeping an eye on for the past few years. The team did a fantastic job blending all of its influences together, and it proudly wears them on its sleeves. I'd recommend Severed Steel to anyone that's a shooter fan and to every person out there that is craving some John Woo inspired action.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a mix of mostly three games: Quake, Mirror's Edge and F.E.A.R From Quake it takes main gameplay loop based on short 2-5 minute levels with simple "button-key-door-kill everyone" objectives and a story which is delivered mostly through text file in game folder which you must download separately as a part of artbook. There also some black and white mute animatics which aren't tell you much but remind me of Homeworld. The Dev himself said he took inspiration from The Specialists Half-Life mod though. Other than that and environmental storytelling there won't be much in terms of narrative to speak of. From Mirror's Edge it takes a large emphasis on movement, wallruns and various jumps/dashes/slides/kicks. There are multiple melee attacks and player's character can move rather fast. Just like in ME player cannot collect ammo or reload their gun, only throw and swap for another one. From F.E.A.R it takes non-linear levels, enemies which are squad based and act rather smart, and a lot of smoke/sparks/glass shards/dust which levels get generously filled with as they get destroyed by enemies' and player's fire. Main campaign is the least game can offer, it's rather short and milquetoast, I recommend getting straight into Firefight and Rogue Steel modes as they can be much more fun, they are highly customizable (as well as game settings in general by the way) and can be adjusted to be easier, harder, more chaotic with many mutators which you unlock as you play more these gamemodes. There also are custom levels and whole custom campaigns as well as level editor so check out a workshop. Also there is a cannon, a multiple cannons actually. You can use it as a panic button when out of ammo, you can use it to break the walls and floors to make a shortcuts and break sequences as a speedrunner, you can swap it for  gravity gun, laser cutter or flamethrower if you want something else more suitting for your tactics. By the way soundtrack is easy one of the best things I've listened to in this year. This kind of ethereal breakbeat/dnb and synthwavish beats does a good service in conveying this shiveringly bleak futuristic scifi mood game has. Listen to some Molten Steel, New World Order, Bellona, An Argument for Humanity, Code Heist, Death from Above, Bilderberg Group, A Thousand Mirrors, Flying Too Close to the Sun, Dead Sky on Youtube for example.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is great fun and definitely worth your time if you like stylish shooters. It looks nice with very destructible environments, I love the synthwave soundtrack, and the core gameplay loop is just so fun to do.The core gameplay loop is a bullet time stylistic shooter. You will run, wall run, slide, dive, and any combination of to traverse levels and kill enemies while utilizing a VERY generous bullet time mechanic as it is infinite during any of the advanced movement mechanics. Your character has one arm, so any weapon you find is only good for whatever is left in the magazine but you can easily disarm enemies or even steal their backup from their holster in a pinch. Enemies are aggressive and deadly accurate, unless you are in the middle of conducting one of the advanced movement mechanics, which chaining them will become absolutely essential upon playing on higher difficulties where you have less health and more aggressive enemies. Upon a point in the campaign or through firefight you will obtain an arm cannon with a variety of different uses which will change how you play. Anything from a standard energy blast that can carve through levels and delete enemies on direct hit to a literal gravity gun where you can use physics objects in game as weapons or even shields. They all have their place in any playstyle and can all be formidable in the right players arsenal. There is full freedom in movement so you can do a backflip while flying through the air to get those sweet inverted headshots.Story? I completed the campaign and I had no idea what was going on the entire time as I was too busy having my happy murder fun time for about 2 hours. The bread and butter of this game is Firefight where they drop you in a level with a set amount of enemies and you try to kill them all while completing separate challenges to unlock more things to use in Firefight mode, such as different starting weapons, arm cannon modes, and some cosmetics (despite you never really seeing your cosmetics in game anyway). Challenges will range from things like kills while wall running or sliding, stealing weapons out of holsters, amongst others that will vary up the way you play each level if you want to unlock the gear you want.There's also Rogue Steel where they generate a campaign for you while you pick modifier cards between levels for buffs or for increases in your score multiplier which also act as difficulty modifiers which will do anything from reduce your health by half, to making certain enemies only killable through headshots or weak spot hits, making bullet time not slow down time as much, or even having bullet time not be infinite during advanced movement and only replenished through kills. Each card adds a certain wild card element and can easily keep you playing for multiple runs, and unlike other rogue-like modes it does not end on death, as you just restart that level and keep trying until you succeed. Very niche title, but it is very fun and easy to lose track of time while playing. A couple things to be on the lookout for:There's not a very good indication on when you've taken damage until you are at critical health, and weapons do have cones of fire despite what the reticle might have you believe. Certain weapons are good for range, others are monstrous up close so it would be cool if there was a testing area where you can test the games different weapons and mechanics so you're not trying to figure out which ones you like while playing the game itself.

_childDocuments_.review: Fear, Max Payne, Mirror's Edge, Superhot, Syndicate, and Titanfall 2 all wrapped up in one. Gameplay & Campaign is pretty simple. Kill, do a simple objective like shoot or blow up something, leave. Rinse and repeat. Normally that would be repetitive as hell, but with this game it oozes style and choice with the level and gameplay design. Combined with the simple mechanics of invulnerability while wallrunning, sliding, jumping, or diving, it gives the player a massive amount of choice on how to tackle the level and style upon the enemy. On top of slow mo, it creates a mix of extremely fast or as slow as you'd like gameplay to style and vibe to with the violence and music. Less than halfway through you also get another ability to shoot through objects or walls, which continues to give creativity to the player on how they combo or get to their next firefight/objective to keep up the fast pace. The games controls are extremely tight for what they are, diving and wallrunning feel extremely snappy, sliding through lower objects works extremely well, and things like wallkicking to gain height up a wall or towards the celling is a fantastic addition when combining other techniques. Diving on carts or over tables John Woo style while throwing yourself out windows or off of trains at high speed never gets old when it's up to the player of how they get to and finish each firefight. Enemies are relatively simple but not overly OP or dumb. They walk the fine line of being dangerous if you're not taking advantage of the games mechanics, while also not being able to just insta snap and kill you if you come into their sightline. Messing with them in ways like kicking away their shields, taking off their sidearm while sliding past them, or shooting your arm cannon to blow up the ground from under their feet and have them fall off the map is just a few ways to mess with them. Like Fear, they group up and are intelligent enough to keep chasing you at all times, but combined with your constant movement from floor to floor & room to room, it creates a sense of natural firefights and not just static spawns.Music is fantastic, and sounds pretty dynamic. Not so much like Hotline Miami, but Dyad is a really good comparison. Visuals are also not overly realistic due to the cell shading; but have lots of neon colors, bright whites, dark blacks, very saturated in all the right ways with great SFX & Recoil to back it up inbetween the beats of the music. Campaign took me around 3-3.5 hours on Hard difficulty, and the rest of the content is side stuff like Firefight which is the story maps with unique mutators or challenges to go along with them, or custom user maps. That being said, is $25 worth it? Considering stuff like Balan Wonderland was $60, or even things released 10 years ago were okay with stuff like 4 hour SP campaigns worth $60 on release, I think it's well worth it, especially on a sale. It also has a NG+ option with new remixed enemy spawns which is already a step up from other faster paced action shooters like Bright Memory. I don't look at how long a game takes me to get through, but how much I enjoyed and how memorable it is with what content is given, and how the game either fails or succeeds at what its trying to do. With that said, I find what it goes for to be a complete success, and I will be comparing and hoping a lot of other fast paced shooters take notes of this title. It may be short, but it's so in depth with its mechanics and satisfying gunplay that it's easy to have you hooked into its spectacle even on repeat attempts and playthroughs. Here's hoping they keep releasing some content & more varied maps, weather effects, or other things they feel like. Or if I'm greedy then some sort of Style Meter that was in the something like the original Bright Memory. But even with what's already in the game, it's an amazing FPS experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. That was the most insane 1.5 hour game I've ever played. When you're playing a game and say, "this is the last level", and then you just *keep playing* because it's that fun? Special time. Presentation: Levels are simple texture wise because almost everything is destroyable, which plays excellently with your arm cannon once you start breaching and clearing walls like an Ultrakill swat member. Music is fantastic, the enemies are easy to see with their red glow. The cutscenes are minimal, stop motion comic book like design, and look good.Story: Not much, but for this type of game that's perfectly fine. There's the main character's drive to get revenge, some betrayal, and then escaping. Any more story might have actually distracted from the main selling point:Gameplay: Wonderful slow motion gameplay that actively encourages you to double jump, slide, and launch yourselves into  enemies and through windows. Once I realized that, in slow motion, you can *turn yourself upside down while aiming to shoot someone in the back?* I knew I loved this game. The feeling of constantly moving and blasting while grabbing new guns is insanely addicting.Hearty recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is a fantastic movement shooter with an excellent soundtrack. Whether it's the super smooth movement or the solid visuals, Severed Steel manages to be a very enjoyable experience. Moreover, the bullet time mechanic, enemy placement, and level design make Severed Steel's gameplay unique and addictive. However, as much as the game does right, it does have two major problems: the lack of content and the high price. _childDocuments_.review: How to win (at its namesake difficulty):Step 1: Are there red lines (stunt indicator) on your screen?Yes -> shoot baddies (don't worry, you're currently invulnerable)No -> mash Space, Ctrl, Shift till there areRepeat Step 1 till you win.It's not bad, it's just... not fun, either. To be more constructive in my criticism, the three "stunts" (slide, jump+wallrun, lunge) currently feel redundant, since only one of them tends to be possible at any one time. You can't really transition between them without touching the ground (instead of being able to, say, lunge towards a wall, wallrun, jump off it, and slide into an enemy), which kills the pacing. Furthermore, the camera is prone to gimbal-lock while lunging, which is very disorienting and effectively forces you to land before you can resume shooting.Both the melee and time-slow mechanics feel very "jarring" compared to games that did them well (Doom Eternal and Ghostrunner, respectively), though seeing as I can't describe specifically why, I'll withhold my criticism of those aspects.For what it's worth, I enjoyed both the auto-pickup and empty-weapon-throw mechanics, and I think the game could be a lot of fun if the controls were more polished. I'll give it another shot next year (or on the next major update)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute must purchase even if you only have a modicum of interest in shooters. Max Payne showed us how rad bullet time can be and Greylock Studio took that and ran with it - resulting in one of the best action games on Steam. The gunplay feels crisp and intuitive and the wanton destruction don't feel gratuitous and instead often times it can play a critical role in how you progress through a mission. My favorite mission by far one the one placed in the city where you can leap from a roof top shoot through the roof of another building, plunge yourself through the newly formed hole in said roof, and drop kick your target before he even has a chance to turn around.The campaign isn't overly long but it is just nonstop fun and intense action. Once you have finished the main story however, you find out that it's quite literally just the beginning of the game. There are countless challenges and modes you can play until you really feel like you've had your fill. There's a really fun rogue-lite game mode called Rogue Steel where you get different power-ups between missions and the further you get, the more unlocks you acquire allowing you to start runs with an even more broken loadout than before. On top of Rogue Steel, you have not only mods available on the Steam Workshop to really add to the copious amounts of content, but there's even a built in level editor which feels rather intuitive that allows you to create your own challenges and share them with friends. The game is often found in bundles on sites like Fanatical and GreenManGaming, but even on steam the game will go on sale for as low as $2.49 and at that price, you are doing yourself a complete disservice not giving it a try. I highly recommend this game!

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is the love child of The Matrix Hallway scene and Action Half-Life Mod painted with surreal cyberpunk aesthetics and amped up with a great electronic soundtrack. At least if you are willing to give it a bit to click. The game can be a bit overwhelming and feeling "off" at the beginning, but once you understood the gameplay mechanics it really is a blast to play. It comes with a ~5 hours long campaign, five difficulty levels and a Firefight mode that offers over 40 additional challenge levels where you can set your own rules (modifications), arrange them in playlists and share high scores with online folks. There even is a level editor, which is still in Beta though. For the asking price of just 20€ you certainly get a lot of content and awesome gameplay. Highly recommended for anyone remotely interested in a fast-paced, stylish cyberpunk shooter.

_childDocuments_.review: Ignore the time played at the posting of this review, I played the demo extensively on the hardest difficulty.  Shattered steel is a one of a kind mashup of all the tropes of modern shooters, hitscan enemies, slow motion, and sliding; however it manages to combine all of these into some extremely fun gameplay by tilting the playing field hapazardly.  Your enemies can kill you in a single shot(on molten steel) and you cannot be hit while doing stunts.  This imbalance fuels the gameplay loop of shattered steel wonderfully; you must keep moving and keep aware lest your enemies tag you once.  The slow-motion mechanic is welcome, the game would be far too fast paced without it.  There has been some discussion on the brevity of this game but I believe that the developer "intended" the game to be played/replayed on the harder difficulties, this causes you to replay levels a handful of times to find the best route for your playstyle.  The control have some... jank to them, but it is incredibly rewarding to learn how to use said jank to your advantage, the prime example of which that I can think of is controlling your motion through the air by pressing the dive key while moving in the direction you want to go, followed by pivoting your camera around to take shots at enemies, it sounds simple on paper but its a far cry from the standard "your character only shoots in one direction and moves around in one of 8 directions." I replayed the demo levels dozens of times on the hardest difficulty and it felt fantastic to beat it each time, I strongly recommend you play on the molten steel if you can handle it, the game feels more complete this way.Highly recommend, good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is a flashy, fast paced mobility FPS that plays well, has a great aesthetic and soundtrack, and makes you feel pretty cool as you play it.  The gimmick - that you've only got one hand - means that rather than the conventional gameplay loop of scavenging ammo for your weapons, you're in a constant cycle of grabbing weapons from enemies (alive or dead), emptying the clips, then literally throwing them away to get new ones.  All the while you're doing flips, slides, wallruns, dives, kicks, and making liberal use of slow-motion to do tricks and survive large waves of enemies with limited health.  You do get an arm cannon as you progress that not only provides additional firepower, but can blow holes in the terrain for movement or strategic purposes.The value proposition of Severed Steel is going to depend in large part on how you enjoy single player FPS games.  The campaign itself is short, about 2-3 hours (and New Game+, while harder, takes probably less time as you've got your bearings by then).  If that's all you're here for, then full price is definitely hard to justify, though it'd still be worth looking at on sale.  Severed Steel does have a variety of extra modes, however, that - if they're up your alley - are where a lot of extra value comes from.  There's short roguelike campaigns of 8-10 stages with a variety of modifier cards being applied as you go, ranging from beneficial to hazardous (ex. the floor is lava).  There's challenge stages where you're going for a high score by chaining multiple tricks and kills together while dealing with optional objectives.  There's even daily leaderboard challenges.  If you're inclined to poke at these extra modes to unlock extra cosmetics, gameplay mutators, and so forth, then there's a lot of extra meat to the game and potentially a lot of extra hours.If the trailer interests you then you'll have a good time, just decide where you're going to land on the price-to-value spectrum and purchase accordingly.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is a fast paced, frenetic and at times even frantic first person shooter that is both good and, well, I wouldn’t say bad, but mediocre maybe. Maybe?The game contains an actual story, told by slightly animated cartoony cutscenes, but it’s not what the game’s about. This game is all about shooting people in the most stylish of ways. This sort of gameplay has some pros and cons, however.First let me start by saying the game will really make you feel like a badass when you get in a specific kind of flow. The levels aren’t long, they usually take around five minutes to complete, and you can take a bit of damage before a level finally resets. It all works fine with the exception of one thing: the presentation leaves a lot to be desired. A lot.Let me start with the user interface. The objective is listed in the upper right corner which is normal and perfectly fine, but the marker on your screen is dark red which makes it hard to see and/or find at times because a) it’s frenetic and fast paced and b) the environments are actually kind of dark so it blends in easily. Then there are the messages that pop up whenever you make a kill (like headshots). In my few hours of playing I’ve only been able to read it a couple of times and that was when time was slowed down (and even then I wasn’t able to read it entirely). If you don’t slow it down it pops up and is almost instantly gone which feels very unsatisfying. This also applies to the tutorial where messages quite quickly disappear, even when you still have to perform a certain action. It leaves a bad impression even if you take the game’s design philosophy into consideration. There are always things that need a (little) different touch.When you get killed there’s also no message whatsoever. The screen indicates when you get hurt, and the colors get more intense the more you get hit, but you usually have no clue when enough is enough with the game’s rapid tempo. When you die all you get a black screen and then you reload from the start. It’s frustrating because you have no idea when to exactly retreat or take it easy. There is a clover in the lower right corner that I think acts as your health status, but it’s never explained and I literally just saw it a few minutes before reaching the end of the game. It’s just poor design, especially as far as the user interface is concerned. Sure, the levels take just a few minutes to complete, but that’s no excuse.Other than that the menus are somewhat simplistic, but they get the job done.The gameplay consists of shooting enemies and objects relevant to the mission. You’ll do this with the help of several moves: you can slide, dive, (double) jump, wallrun, kick, shoot, throw, destroy walls and slow down time. The last one is necessary to make precision shots like headshots and to slow down all of the chaos and the kick is very useful for enemies with shields or close combat in general. Just don’t expect a Bulletstorm kick here. The others speak for themselves I think, but sliding, diving and wallrunning all won’t let you take any damage. So it’s essential to keep moving and mixing up those moves as you move through the levels. There’s also a missile that you can point towards any wall and that way make a hole in it. Useful if you want to drop enemies, move forward (sometimes you’re required to destroy something in order to progress) or make a shortcut to an enemy for an easier kill. The objectives themselves usually consists of shooting objects, making holes (or a combination of those two) and killing all of the enemies. A little simplistic, but it works.You always start with a gun, but guns can also be acquired by taking them from enemies. Whenever a gun is empty you can throw it and if you’re tactical or lucky kill an enemy with it. Guns that are empty are marked with an ‘x’. If you walk over another gun that is the same you’ll automatically pick up the required ammo and otherwise you can pick up other weapons from dead enemies that will quickly fill the floors of the levels, like a flamethrower or SMG.There are six chapters for a total of two to three hours of gameplay. After that there’s the Firefight Mode which acts as some sort of arcade mode, but with challenges. Finishing a map in Firefight also unlocks new maps, weapons and mutators to play around with. Fun enough, but the few maps I played weren’t very addicting to me.The graphics are simple to the point that they’re basically only made out of basic geometry, with here and there a bit of furniture or a PC hanging around. It would’ve been nice if you could’ve used the environment more for making kills (not talking about the missiles here), but alas. Since the environment is made of voxels it’s naturally easier to destroy. Fire, bullets, missiles all make holes in the environment. It’s cool and it looks so simple, but it also explains why it looks so simple. Otherwise it wouldn’t have been possible to do this in an easy way. The lighting of the levels is fine as long as you don’t expect too much of it. The characters have enough detail to make them stand out. In fact, they seem to have the most detail of all.There’s no voice acting except for some yells by enemy soldiers. These are okay. The main character isn’t voiced. The sound effects are pretty good and clear, and the music is more up tempo/faster paced. It’s not my style, but I guess it gets the adrenaline flowing during hectic moments.I got stuck into the floor of the map once, but other than that I experienced no bugs or issues.With a little more polish and consideration Severed Steel could’ve been a really awesome little game. As it stands now it’s a fairly good game with some frustrating and questionable design choices. The action is spot on, when you get into the right flow that is. Unfortunately this not only depends on you as a player, but also on the game itself. Still, it’s a game that can, and probably will at least once, make you feel like a total badass. I don’t think it’s worth the current price, but if you can get it in the €10 range it’s a good deal.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel has an excellent parkour system with wallrunning, diving, sliding and double jumping. Comboing them together is the main gameplay mechanic since you are invulnerable when you do so as well as giving infinite slowmo. Pretty much as soon as you stop you die; so keep moving!You have a slowmo meter which is quite generous which does not deplete when you are parkouring and refills when you score a skill, meaning that you can go through a level entirely in slow motion. It helps you accomplish daring stunts and incredible trick shots which make you feel very stylish and powerful.A voxel-based destruction system means that most surfaces can be destroyed. You can shoot enemies through walls or create new shortcuts. Explosive weapons are a treat to use because of their destructive power.There is no way to reload your weapons and you can only carry one at a time, meaning that you constantly swap for new guns. There are quite a few in the game, some more memorable than others, but overall the arsenal is very diverse.The singleplayer campaign consists of many smaller levels strung together. Every level has one or a few objectives to complete and they mostly consist of destroying a thing, getting to a place or killing all enemies, but there are some more creative objectives as well. Each level only takes a few minutes at most but generally requires several attempts. There is a loose story told through silent cut-scenes, which neither grabbed me nor ruined the pace.I played on the “Severed Steel”-difficulty and it felt fair and balanced. You do die very quickly and at first it felt overwhelmingly hard, but as soon as you get a hang of what the game wants from you it flows quite nicely. Levels are short and resets are fast meaning that death is only a short setback. I recommend choosing a mode that you find challenging since individual levels and the game are very short, meaning that it never gets frustrating. There is a stark neon aesthetic throughout and the UI as well as the general art style can be quite arcadey. I turned down many of the effects to get a cleaner look and less visual noise since it was otherwise too overwhelming.The sound design is punchy and effective. Explosions have a nice thud, weapons sound distinct. Audio queues are used well and are not downed out amidst the noise. Enemy chatter is distorted in a way very reminiscent of F.E.A.R. The music is high tempo EDM with a good amount of different tracks that overall improved on the feel and sense of speed of the game.

And with the never ending slowmo aiming will never be a problem, plus you also heal on every kill so the combat isn't rewarding unless you're a smoothbrain who enjoys guaranteed headshots the game. UI gives impression of poor and rushed (just like everything else in the game), and is confusing at times. The music is like someone searched for 'best drum and bass jungle' from Youtube and hit play but drum and bass wasn't really a thing yet so it ends up being really under the bar.It's someones clunky shooter game hobbyist project (which is totally fine and valid) but not a $20€ masterpiece (or even good) fps game. And for some reason everyone is too afraid of admitting that.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome game, if you've ever replayed the same checkpoints in F.E.A.R over and over, enjoyed time trials in Mirrors Edge and ghostrunner, and wish Remedy would make a Max Payne again, this is for you. 9/10Voxel graphic destruction, RTX, and a high level of polish for an indie title. Played Campaign once on Tempered Steel (Easy/Normal), got to level 60 doing firefight on Severed Steel (the way it's meant to be played!) then replayed Campaign on Severed. Easy 8-10 hours of pure gameplay. Everything flows together very well and is a blast to play. Runs great on r5 5600x and EVGA RTX3080FTW3. Some slowdown with triple enemies in the portal level, but that's to be expected cause that is FREAKIN WILD!Great soundtrack from Floating Door, fits the game very well. Goes excellent with other electronic music as well, makes it a perfect quick game to drop into.Lots of QOL settings; after I beat the campaign, I turned off all the HUD elements except for crosshair and enemy outlines. Definitely suggest doing the same, it makes it seem almost like prerendered gameplay. Weapons have convenient lights on them to indicate ammo and you almost never run dry of cannon ammo anyways.One thing I would like to see (AKA why it's not a perfect 10): Melee weapons and dismemberment. The up close play is pretty dope, most of the kicks you could do in FEAR you can do here, but they... lack impact somewhat? 9/10 times the best option up close is to take their sidearm and headshot them then dive away. You can gain some height from drop kicking heads and if you're fast enough you can oneshot with a slide kick, but you aren't going to kung fu a whole room of enemies. Not without trying a couple times at least.Support this Developer! Support this Game! Support Community Mapmakers!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: The game is incredible and extremely addicting and you should definitely pick it up. I decided to pick this game up because it looked right up my alley, and I was getting major Hotline Miami and Katana Zero vibes from the trailer alone. The gameplay is incredibly satisfying and even just in the tutorial it seemed like everything clicked, I really felt like I was a crazed ninja dashing around and confusing my masked opponents. The movement in this game is incredible, it's reminiscent of Mirror's Edge but it also feels like something you'd find in a momentum-based Sonic fangame. The gunplay is also extremely fun, although I do feel like it is what will turn most players away because of how challenging it can be. Due to the extremely fast default movement speed it's hard to line up your shots, and the game feels a little clunky when you try to slow down. However, the bullet-time mechanic does wonders to remedy this, it also allows you to pull off some incredibly stylish movie level stunts. The fact that slow-mo and health regen with every kill allows you to keep up the pace and keep pushing forward without having to stop to let it refill on a cool-down or something, in fact stopping/slowing down will almost certainly get your head taken off of your shoulders. Once you unlock the arm-cannon the game really opens up. You gain the ability to blow a hole in surfaces and absolutely demolish your opposition. This one simple mechanic is what truly propels this game into greatness with how versatile it can be. This game has a lot going for it and I feel like it's really something special, if you have the spare cash and a few hours to spare you should absolutely pick it up.

_childDocuments_.review: Campaign is pretty short but it gives you a good sense of how to play the game. Recommend starting with Severed Steel Difficulty if you have played movement games before. Learning curve is good and I think most players will find Severed Steel challenging but not frustrating.After you learn on the campaign, do some of the firefight missions. These are plenty fun and the challenges make them much more enjoyable. The real game starts with the Rogue campaign. I only played one, but so far it was a big treat. It changes up the dynamic so much and really refreshes the game.Pros: Simple, fun gameplayAll the guns are useful and you wont find yourself feeling rewarded for only using a particular typethe bullet time mechanic is fair enough and enables some sick setups.Music and art are tremendous.Cons:Melee is a bit clunky. You are pretty much penalized for using it because most enemies require more than one hit unless you have a lot of speed. The only time you will find yourself wanting to use it is when you are out of ammo really. Maybe better players will be more strategic about meleeing enemies to preserve ammo but the average person is going to be annoyed with how useless it feels. The weakness of melee really begins to show itself in the rogue campaign, where using it becomes more important for certain perks.Story: pretty much nonexistent which is fine but a little bit of writing would have been nice to explain the cutscenes.Chaining stunts together is a bit difficult. You pretty much end up the Dive-slide pattern and wall running is kind of an afterthought. Part of the reason is that it is very difficult to cancel a dive, unlike a slide, in mid air to chain to a wall.Bullet time makes the game a bit too easy. Once you realize it is unlimited during stunts, the game sort of takes care of itself. A bit more creative in limiting it would have made the game a bit more fun I think. The rogue campaign addresses this so it's not too big of an issue. The bulk of the time spent in this game will be in rogue campaign anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun arcade style action-fps-shooter. You can slow down time, wallrun, kickslide mid air, dive through glass or holes you make in the destructible map. The game is on rails, but feels free. The experience feels balanced and the challenge can ramp up quickly if you run out of ammo or slomo. Tons of challenge modes and it still has support with updates and new content. The game throws you right into the action with very little downtime. Highly recommend!There are some downsides/improvements I'm looking out for, such as...Campaign is very quick. You move so fast in levels and even menus that it can quickly drain your excitement just to keep up. Would be nice to have it slow down a bit to show more cut scenes, enjoy the scenery, or single enemy fights that requires more strategy than shooting in the head or bright back.I wish there were specific sliders for settings like slomo instead of just difficulty and mutators. It is a score-arcade based game so I get why they limit the customization. But this is a missed opportunity to give the player more freedom.The melee is janky, when the kick connects it's fun, but it pushes you back when you want to constantly move forward. Arm cannon melee is awful. I reallllly wish there was a sword/slash/dashing melee move aside from the weak flying sidekick/slide.Camera sometimes goes nuts, can suddenly turn your stomach. I also wish there was a 3rd-Person perspective option. Or more camera smoothing.Even though the camera can give a little motion sickness after extended play time. I also wish there were random stunts/flips you can do. It feels like you should be able to parkour and flip tricks like in the matrix. The movement is dope, but the potential for more is greater.New Rogue mode is my favorite addition, but also feels like they are holding back the potential of cards that could have easily been launch mutators. Could go much more over the top without feeling too imbalanced. Cards give you starting weapons, extra jumps, shockwave on landing, exploding headshots or gun throws, different arm cannons, negatives for score multipliers like health and ammo, and enemies level up/get a little bit tougher. I was hoping/expecting things more like, a dashing melee :p, burning bullets, spread bullets, teleportation, hand beams, and more passives like see through walls, or more enemy buffs that give them more abilities/weapons/difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Momentum. That is what the entire game pivots around. It's about lots of things happening in a handful of seconds, and making them digestible via bullet time toggle. The means of movement are diving, sliding and wallrunning, all with their own positives and negatives, but they all make you invulerable to damage. Gauging what's best at any given moment is how you find harmony with the game's momentum, and the absolute worst thing you can possibility do in any situation is just stand still. You are a shark; you are unstoppable, lethal, and dead if you stop moving.Weapons are an expendable commodity. There's a decent variety and they can't be reloaded. Empty one out onto a target, dive over the next target while grabbing his sidearm, shoot him with it, throw it to stagger another nearby target, pick up a weapon, and keep blasting. It's all about rapid decision making that's made extremely accessible by bullet time. Holding down RMB actives slo-mo that can be used to get your bearings and line up moving shots - and it's a satisfying feeling. It's a resource bar that depletes, but recovered by making kills, so it's an "economy" of using bullet time in order to "buy" more bullet time than you spent.This on its own would be modestly fun. But an extra dimension is added into the mix with  An arm cannon early in the campaign will let you blow holes in surfaces. It enables a completely fresh, frenetic navigation where you're opening your own shortcuts and effectively "weaselling" your way out of tight spots to keep the pace going. It's what makes an otherwise merely neat game suddenly ingenius, and giving all kinds of speedrunning possibilities with seeing just how fast it can let you complete a level.Speed is however, probably the game's simultaneous weakness. There's about 42 levels in the campaign (and a couple really cool bonus levels) of which most can be completed in 2 minutes or less, and the campaign can  be finished in 3 hours. To call it "light on storytelling" would oversell it. It's more like just a variety of rapid levels stringed together semi-cohesively by moment-to-moment objectives and the occasional still-frame cutscene. It's hard to ascertain the story unless you download the free digital concept artbook. I mean, how would anyone have known the protagonist is a clone soldier? Or that the game takes place in a dystopic future where the world is segregated by 3 mega-corps who run underground cities maintained by a cloned labor force? Nothing in the game hints towards these things whatso-freaking-ever. It might even just be leftover retcons from the development's storyboarding. Who knows.So, storytelling is not even taking backseat, but gagged in the trunk as an unwilling passenger begrudgingly taken along for the ride.It's not something I think can be fixed without some fundamental changes/additions to level structuring that may hurt the game's rapid momentum, and maybe should simply be taken as a nature of the beast. It's fast, mindless fun relying in the most momentary decision-making skills to do stylish gun parkour, and has a well-equipped arcadey mode (called "Firefight") that makes the absolute most of what's on offer.There's a demo that can easily sell on you on whether or not you'll fall in love with it, and if you do, you'll play it for more than just its bite-sized campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is an electrifying and heart-pounding shooter. The game's unique focus on acrobatics and fluid movement sets it apart from the rest, making it a must-try for fans of the shooter genre.The gunplay in Severed Steel is undeniably the star of the show. The arsenal of weapons at your disposal feels satisfyingly weighty and distinct, each packing a punch and providing a different strategic advantage. The destructible environments add an extra layer of excitement, as you can unleash chaos on your enemies while creatively utilizing the surroundings to your advantage.The acrobatics mechanics are a game-changer, giving you an exhilarating level of control over your character's movements. The ability to slow down time during mid-air stunts and pull off awe-inspiring maneuvers feels empowering and stylish. It's a refreshing twist on the traditional shooter formula and keeps you engaged throughout each heart-pounding encounter.However, there's one aspect of Severed Steel that left me wanting more: the campaign length. While the action is a blast from start to finish, the campaign felt a tad too short for my liking. Just as I was fully immersed in the world and the intricacies of the story, it came to an abrupt end, leaving me hungry for more content. The developers have done a remarkable job crafting a captivating universe, and I can't help but wish there was more of it to explore.Despite this minor drawback, Severed Steel is an absolute thrill ride that should not be missed. Its intense gunfights, acrobatic ballet, and unique gameplay mechanics create an experience that's both addictive and refreshing. If you're a fan of high-octane action games that challenge you to think on your feet, Severed Steel will undoubtedly scratch that itch. Just be prepared to savor the experience, as you might find yourself wishing for a bit more campaign goodness.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing marriage of multiple games and genres (Max Payne, F.E.A.R., Mirror's Edge, SUPERHOT, Titanfall 1/2, ULTRAKILL) while still being its own thing. Runs and plays incredibly great and the voxels don't detract from the experience, one of the most fluid ways to play out your John Woo / Wick fantasty. I don't think I can name a title that does backflips, upside down shooting, climbing by kicking your feet and making voxel dents or wallrunning quite as well, nevermind being able to shoot through walls like in Teardown for creative shortcuts. A lot of pro customiseability and accessibility sliders. The main campaign is short but infinitely replayable, if running through it again doesn't quite do it for you there is a roguelike mode that you can again customise and make it as accessible as you like. Some meta upgrades in Fireright are a bit of a slog to go through and the recent community pre-packaged maps are not very well balanced but they're there if you want to scratch the itch of more highly mobile robot lady. Had to add this here out of spite, but if Trepang2 didn't do it for you, hopefully this will, like it did for me.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Fast and badass. Kick baddies, snatch guns, chain slow-mo kills, breach a door/wall, and just generally disregard the whole concept of "limitations." Workshop included.Severed Steel takes the best of Max Payne and Titanfall and puts it in one neon-soaked package. Use wall runs, wall kicks, wall DESTRUCTION, and double jumps, in conjunction with slides, dives, weapon snatches, and slow-mo, to become an unstoppable whirlwind of bullets and mayhem; and do it all to pumping techno beats. Enemies are (mostly) highlighted in red when visible, so target ID is fast and easy, meaning you can shoot exactly who you need to in a flash. There are plenty of weapons in the categories of pistol, shotgun, SMG, assault rifle, grenade launcher, and more I probably haven't seen yet. Additionally, you get an explosive arm cannon for when that wall in front of you just shouldn't be there, or that shield is just too inconvenient to go around.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Superhot + Max Payne/Stranglehold. Severed Steel offers a thrilling two to three hour campaign and is heavy on bullet time and a variety of guns. If you like bullet time in your games, it's a must-have experience. Gameplay here is more akin to a traditional FPS than Superhot while keeping a very arcade-like feel. Levels are well designed and keep the action flowing. You can kick, slide, dive and wall run for moments of invulnerability and cool. Walls can be destroyed which opens up the gameplay. I really like how the dive mechanic feels here and it makes the FPS perspective feel fresh when diving over top of enemies--you really get the sense that you're doing a full-flip and in bullet time it's hard not to feel like a moment out of The Matrix. Graphics aren't going for realistic and fully textured while they do have a lot more to offer than Superhot and it has a nice neon-style. There's a new game plus and campaign generator with rogue lite elements. This campaign seems to randomly string together levels from the main campaign and I'm not sure if there's any new levels thrown in. Main campaign is satisfying enough for me, and I really enjoyed it!

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is another solid addition to the movement shooter genre, with a few game play and design aspects that give it its own style. First and foremost, the game play is the star of the show, while there is technically a "story" it is essentially just a quick handful of static images between chapters, this is completely fine in my opinion as this fast paced arcadey style of fps is often best when not bogged down by its narrative. The movement, gunplay, and general combat is all super solid and satisfying when you get in the groove. A couple of things took a little bit of getting used to, like having both a crouch/slide and a dive took a bit of work(and a swap of their binds) to really get down, but once you do it feels super cool to pull off some action movie stunts like diving through a window in slow mo, turning around to shoot a guy behind you then slide tackling another guy, sliding under a table and taking out a third guy with the second guy's gun. Speaking of which, another thing that takes a little getting used to is not being able to reload, I thought it would be harder to deal with, but I got used to it pretty fast, and things like beaming people in the head with empty guns and stealing enemies sidearms really adds to the action movie vibes. Both firefight mode and rouge steel mode(rougelike mode) are also nice options for adding longevity to the game. The unlock-able gameplay modifiers and different canon arms is nice way to add some variety and challenge too. It would be cool to see the rougelike mode refined further so that you could sort of have "builds" like in most other games in the genre, but I liked the concept of having to choose a debuff for a higher point modifier and the risk reward involved in that, and all things considered it's a bonus mode that's still fun to play regardless so I can't complain.It's a little bit like Super Hot and Hotline Miami had a baby that does parkour. Overall would definitely recommend if you want some super solid single player fps game play.
