_childDocuments_.review: Great Matrix simulator with some amazing electronic music. A number of games have done this before, like GTTOD, Titan Fall, Maximum Action, so on and so forth, but Severed Steel really amps the game with the very simple but extremely effective addition of amazing music. Another great addition is RTX for Nvidia cards, although not entirely optimized, RTX on adds a level of immersion i haven't experienced before in a game like this. The $25 price tag is a mixed bag however. On one hand, i see the effort done here in all aspects to bring us a truly unique experience, on the other, its a one trick pony with little change other than the complete destruction of environments. If i would to put it into laymen's terms, it would be the Call of Duty of this genre. Not pushing the genre to new heights, but perfecting what is already here.Severed Steel is 100% a buy if you're into parkour shooters of any type. The music, the style, the gameplay, all add up to a perfect experience in a genre that is picking up steam recently. I look forward to more from this title and the developers to see whats next.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is a mix of FEAR and Mirror's Edge that offers a combat sandbox that is a lot of fun if you're willing to play around with weapons and mutators on offer.  PROS:-Combat is fun in a 'simple to understand but hard to master' sort of way. Also many ways to feel like a total badass such as: -Stealing guns from an enemy's holster. -Flipping upside down before nailing a headshot. -Using the gravity gun to catch an enemy grenade and fling it back at them.-Controls are smooth and it is easily to pull off stunts such as wall-running, sliding, and flipping.-A varied arsenal that is fun to play around with, with a variety of machine guns, shotguns, pistols and explosive weapons. -Difficulty can be tuned from 'basically cheating' to 'hardcore' and anything in between.-Dope soundtrack.-The amount of free content Severed Steel has received is incredible. We've had additions such as a Roguelike mode, weapon skins, new scoring, and akimbo weapons added all within a year WHILST the team is working on another game. -Updates still coming even though the devs are working on a new game. They are smaller QoL updates, but they're still appreciated and show how much the devs truly care. MEH:-Some people will say this game doesn't have a lot of content, but I feel that depends on how you look at it. If you compare this to something such as Skyrim then sure, it 'lacks content', but there is still a lot to offer if you're willing to play around with mutators, New Game+, workshop. I'd also argue that Severed Steel makes for a great 'game between games'. The sort of thing you play when you don't want to think too much about plot and just wanna take a few minutes to feel like a badass mowing down henchmen. -It is visually simplistic, especially with the voxel environments, but that sort of works as the game is rather fast paced and knowing what you're looking at is important as you have to make split-second decisions.BAD:-Can only shuffle playlist during Firefi-SCRATCH THAT. You can now shuffle music whenever and put in your own music.

_childDocuments_.review: 15 minutes after booting the game, my mind was blown. The smoothness of the movement, the crisp and orgasmic gunshot sounds, and everything about the visuals - straight up fire. The gameplay is extremely fun, and also pretty simple. It's just about constantly moving, sliding, double jumping, wall running, diving. And of course, the satisfying slow-motion. Level design is also really good, pretty varied. Some are more vertical, some are more horizontal, some are just only small platforms you have to stay on top of. So it keeps the gameplay fresh in that regard, as the challenges gets pretty varied. Though what I would say is a shame is that there's not much when it comes to enemy types. There's a few, but honestly, not too memorable at least for me when it comes to function and what they're forcing you to do. I expected more as there is so much moves you can do, and so little that the enemy can. But overall, it's really fun, it did not really hinder the fun and engagement I was getting. _childDocuments_.review: This game is really fun.  Fun and fluid combat with levels that inspire learning enemy placement and then taking them all out in one fluid, slo-mo moment.  The voxel environment and destruction mechanics work really well for dynamic decision-making.  The game is short, but worth your time.  However, the quality of the game drops off drastically in the last few levels.  Levels become less inspired, opting for big open arenas where the destruction plays less of a role in combat and more of a transitionary tool between firefights.  The game also has a massive difficulty spike in the end.  So massive that I had to bump down from the game's "default" difficulty all the way to the easiest, and it was STILL so difficult that I didn't engage with the game and instead exploited the AI to win.  The problem is that you're taught by the game's mechanics to dodge in and out of cover, while understanding enemy placement.  Then, the last few levels throw you in big arenas with very little cover and every enemy spawns in large amounts by teleportation.  No time to learn enemy placement and with hardly any cover, every firefight turns into an aim-trainer shootout.  No longer able to break enemy sight leads to a lot of frustration and what feels like unfair difficulty, as 30 enemies in an arena vs you with no cover means a lot of deaths that are all looking the same.Though I am complaining a lot, I really like this game.  The solid first 98% of the game is great and I had a lot of fun.  It's just those last 4-5 levels that feel cheap and don't work with the rest of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write a lot of reviews, but I felt I needed to for this game.Severed Steel absolutely nails the gameplay. It's the best FPS I've ever played. The movement system has a slight learning curve, but once you adjust to it the game makes you feel like a vengeful god. You spend nearly every second of each level perpetually in combat, spreading an acrobatic swathe of death and destruction across the tron-esque environments that crumble around you over the course of an engagement. This feeling of power is carefully balanced with the efficacy of the AI, which will chew you to pieces if you don't lean in to the action move star role. If you like games where you shoot things then you owe it to yourself to pick this up. In my opinion, this is the new golden standard for FPS.My only real complaint would be the amount of content currently in the game. I finished the campaign on the recommended difficulty setting in about 2 hours. The developers have responded to other reviews critiquing the length of the game by claiming that the game is highly replayable due to the firefight mode. This is essential an arcade mode where you play the same maps again but try to chain combos together. If high scores and gameplay mutators are your thing then you might agree, but personally I didn't find it that engaging. I don't think it really has the depth right now to justify claiming it's the bulk of the game, at least in regard to the asking price. To sum up my thoughts, I'd say Severed Steel is a ton of quality without much quantity. There's lots of potential here and I really hope this game continues to be expanded. I'd love to see a sort of horde mode modifier with respawning enemies. It's really a personal judgement if the gameplay is enough to justify the price of admission but considering the size of the team who made this game and the quality of the result I'd say it does. If the worst complaint you can leverage against something is that there isn't enough of it, that's pretty high praise.

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is an arcade FPS game with core gameplay revolving around bullet time and a high-agility movement system. You can slide, dive and wall jump your way around levels while killing dozens of enemies in real time or slow-mo. Kills re-fill your bullet-time meter and your health, so as long as you keep gunnin em down you're essentially invincible and the Flash. Severed Steel features a campaign mode, new game+ mode and a firefight mode. Firefight mode is a challenge mode where you can play levels from the campaign or from the Steam workshop with your choice of weapons and mutators. It also includes a level editor so that you can create your own maps and upload them on the workshop.+Good, neon-soaked visuals+Great gunplay with a fair variety of different weapons +Fun parkour-ish movement system that rewards you for constantly being on the move +Bullet time is great fun and even if you're using it constantly the game still offers quite the challenge+New game+ offers a significantly increased challenge+Firefight mode has a level up system and plenty of unlocks to encourage you to spend time in it+The devs have been adding more content since launch+/-No reloads, once you're out of ammo you can throw your gun to stun an enemy but then you need to find a new one. It definitely helps keep the pace high but I did sometimes wish I could have held on to a weapon I particularly liked for a bit longer+/-Base price of $25 is a little high imo, but the game has already been bundled a couple of times and can be found on sale for $10 pretty easily. I think $15 or less is a great price to pick this up at-The voice lines of the enemies can be a little annoying, it's mostly just them swearing at you with the same voice line, though it's not that noticeable in slow-mo-There are a few times where you'll face an enemy or obstacle with a thick health bar, these are mostly fine, but there's one boss fight in the game (as in, there's only one) that felt really out of place to me and wasn't all that funOverall, this game is an absolute blast and I can definitely see myself returning to it as new updates drop or just to keep mopping up the content I have left after finishing the campaign. If you're into FPS games heavy on bullet time, this is an easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ banger of an FPS. One of Steam's hidden gems.Wall running, dolphin-diving, sliding, borderline infinite slow-mo, low health and ammo, constant need to swap your weapons, coupled with the ability to break through pretty much any wall, roof or floor on a level, create a gameplay loop, where you are forced to think fast and react quickly to a constantly changing environment around you. Add to that a pretty good enemy AI, which adapts to your actions relatively well, and top it off with a trance-dnb soundtrack, and you get a high octane action filled FPS, which can easily put you in a "flow" state and make the time fly by super fast. The story is incredibly simple and is mostly there just to give context to whatever is happening during gameplay, which is the main (and I would say the sole) focus of the game. There are plenty of things to do after you finish the campaign: higher difficulty levels, ng+, challenge mode, as well as custom maps. Plenty of reasons to stay in the game and keep playing around with mechanics. If you like fast-paced shooters, which can offer some hardcore gameplay and don't focus on the story, you will most likely have a lot of fun with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: These days, bullet time/movement indie shooters are everywhere. There something about slowing down time to blast an enemy mid-wall run that’s compelling. No firefights are the same when you can traverse terrain with freedom of movement and slow down time to create a create a visual and audio treat. Severed Steel serves up this type of combat with a unique visual style, a bangin sound track, and replay ability that is rare in the FPS genre. Severed Steel is not a game that you’ll just play the campaign and never come back to. Its campaign is good, offering up great level design and visually popping environments. But its real value is in its randomly generated mini-campaigns that’ll keep you coming back for more. Some levels in the 8 mission campaigns are just wild, randomly generated things that keep you on your toes. Others are recycled from the story campaign with different enemy types and objectives. These mini campaigns keep the games’ compelling combat fresh, and offer true value and replayability to the player. The game’s gunplay and combat are good! Its hard to mess up a bullet time/movement shooter, but the game innovates and keep the combat frantic with the game’s one magazine rule. Each weapon in the game has only one magazine, and when it runs out, you’ll throw the weapon and pick up a new one. It makes you think about spending ammunition and what your next move Is going to be if you’re running low on rounds in the magazine. The game has relatively low TTK, so it can be punishing but fair, since bullet time helps you kill enemies to regain health.The game environments are cool! Not only do they have a unique look and style, but they offer cool gameplay opportunities, as they are fully destructible. Making holes in walls, floors, and ceilings, offer move movement paths to tackle challenging levels and enemies. Weapon selection is varied and good! The sound track is excellent. Not usually my kind of music, but its very good. I’m not done with Severed Steel, but I recently finished its main campaign and with its new akimbo update out (very fun btw) it seemed like a good time to review. I would recommend this game if you enjoy unique shooters that offer great single player replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome, but as everything this cool it has a big drawback. The controls are great. The character feels very responsive even in the air, you can do flips, kicks, slide kicks, double jump, wall run, wall climb (this one is pretty useless tho) and even vault. Picking up weapons is fast, shooting is very responsive and it just feels very good to chain all of these and dance around the enemies. The gameplay is very satisfying. Since you can't reload you are more or less forced to use all weapons and learn their quirks. Sure we all have a favourite but when it runs out of bullets anything is better. All guns feel great, headshots are always a one shot from anything (except when not) and even if not, the feedback the game gives you when killing an enemy tells you when to jump onto the next one.  The slowmotion is basically the way to play it, you have to kill enemies to refill it but during acrobatics it is unlimited, so you'll jump, slide and vault around to survive. Without slowmo enemies are pretty fast but maybe it's my own skill issue. All encounters are extremely fun and rarely make you say "that's BS", more like a skill issue. The screams of the enemies, the music blasting as you blast the poor bots, and the level destruction make it so damn addictive, and you can always tell where there's been a fight. You can even create your own paths by making a huge hole in walls, ceilings, and even the floor. However this is the thing that'll dissapoint almost everyone: The content.You have campaign and campaign+ which are pretty short and not really THAT dynamic since all enemies and their spawns seem to be pre selected, they are here to be played the first time and have some sort of difficulty curve. Then there's the firefight gamemode which I really haven't played because of the next mode.Rogue Steel is a rogue-lite mode with 10 randomly selected maps, mostly from the campaign and others exclusive to this mode, and random objectives like killing all enemies or destroying a console. Luckily the more levels you play the more and harder enemies spawn so the encounters aren't always the same.After every level you have to choose a modifier, either a buff or a debuff. You can make pretty OP stuff like guns with only one bullet, but that last bullet is explosive and you get one back for every enemy killed. Or you can get screwed and have less health, harder enemies and limited slowmo.Even though this mode makes this game pretty replayable, I've seen everything it has to offer and a bit more at just 20Hs. Sure there are steam workshop maps but that's like 5 more hours at most.If you want a great feeling game, and a couple hours of fun then pick this up. This game is very good.

_childDocuments_.review: This Game slaps. + the soundtrack slaps 2. Works fab on steam deck and has loads of optimisation/accessibility options. A True Movement shooter with every in game mechanic supporting this: Movement abilities such as wall running, sliding, kick flipping, diving = Skills = Near unlimited bullet time while performing them. 360 degree aiming = Wanna aim mid back flip in slow mo? You can do that. Arm cannon to go through walls and baddies to get more flow and movement = youbetchya + A super sticky movement system: Check! Nothing about this game is a drag. It achieves super stylistic play that is only limited by your imagination, without the modern trope of having to switch weapons every 2 seconds. And when you do need to find a new gun, stealing weapons/ throwing weapons is fun + easy and there's lots of variety. I once Wall ran and then kicked off another wall into a backflip killing 3 bad guys mid flip and it totally felt like that scene in the matrix. Score 9/10 - only negative is that there isn't a way to save progress on the rogue like element of the game. + this is the only bullet time game that can make up for Trepang 2's delay.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is life itself, injected into your veins while you race at the speed of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ light down narrow corridors, vaulting an enemy and popping a bullet into their now bloodied cranium. I imagine this is what cocaine feels like or speed maybe, I don't take drugs (okay maybe once) so I'll leave it up to you. I have to say HOW MUCH I love this games movement systems, and how it encourages fast play and constant enemy engagement with health regen tied to it and weapons with limited ammo necessitating the need for finding another instantly. But it also provides a handicap of sorts for those that can't play at those comically insane speeds with the Time Slowdown. That feeling of chaining together jump into vaults over a shielded enemy and pumping a slug into him upside down is a chaotic wonder and never got old. Every single bullet feels impactful, much in line with how  was all those years ago, the game rewards you for precision. The resurgence of the "boomer shooter" subgenre is a fantastic relief man. Starting with  2016 reboot and hitting new levels of insanity with New Blood's .  slaps those games together, with all their craze and with a little less blood, and becomes a new kind of movement shooter. Despite it's short campaign length, it becomes a lasting experience I'll soon want more of. And it seems post launch support has been grand, with a plentiful amount of post story content in the form of Firefight and NG+.A wholly impressive showcase, I'll most definitely be playing Greylock's next title.

_childDocuments_.review: So, I got this game on 14th of July 2023 and this game sucked me in so much, that on 19th of July 2023 I finished all the achievements. Some were grindy, some hard, but damn, this game is absolute blast. this game slaps hard af. Movement shooter that is so much fun. To simply describe it. Imagine Titanfall and FEAR having a child. Wall running, sliding, double jumping, slow mo and destructible world. About 100 guns are in this game, arm cannon and also so much customization for gameplay. has short simple story, set in sci-fi, neon, cyberpunk styled corporation with soundtrack that perfectly sets the mood and atmsphere of the game. Simply said you got ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by the corpo's and you are having your revenge rampage againts the corpo that has wronged you. Corpo's PMC are trying to stop you. You'll see action in industrial complexes, offices, clubs, flats, prison, labs, basically anything that you imagine. But damn, the visual design of levels is awesome. You'll go through so many levels with different designs that it never feels same or reused. Only negative is that campaign is short, but here comes the main dish. of this game is insane. Campaign is just appetizer, It's just the starter. There's also Bonus campaigns made by devs and fans and also You can replay campaign with New Game+ but what you seek  are .Modifiers are the main thing. Game offers two additional game modes.  is gamemode which unlocks you some modifiers by completing campaign missions with challanges that the devs set in place. The  second additional game mode is . Rogue is basically rogue lite gamemode in which you play campaign maps in random order with random modifiers being chosen by you and by the game. You unlock those modifiers to be used in campaign and in Firefight by playing Rogue mode. You also unlock cosmetics for your character and arm cannon.Just to give you an idea of what those modifiers are like. Few examples:Floor is lava - exactly what is says, floor is lava and gives you dmg. You will only wall run, jump and dive to avoid floor.Explosive doors - doors explode in contact with enemy, so kick them in their face.One Bullet - every gun has one bullet, so you really wanna aim for the head and if you miss, just throw the empty gun at the enemy.Explosive guns - Thrown guns explode on contact. Guns are important and this game nailed them. So many different guns. Pistols, shotguns, rifles, SMG's, assault rifles, flamethrowers, grenade launchers, current guns, sci-fi guns, wild west guns, world war guns. So much choice but shotguns are probably the strongest ones, using them makes it easy and also high calliber guns are pretty much strong. Guns feel amazing to use and really feel punchy.Theres also the  In one hand you wield the guns you steal from enemies and your 2nd arm is replaced with a sci-fi cannon. It shoots orb of energy that kills enemy or destroys parts of the map. It is mostly used for destroying walls, roofs or anything you need to get through but it has limited uses. So killing enemies is required to fuel the cannon. It's mostly used for making new paths on the map, but there are many versions of the Arm Cannon. to give you an example of what you can expect. There's Laser cutter, which is Arm Cannon that instead of energy orbs shoots laser beam cutting through wall, not so effective to make a path but effective for killing enemies through the walls. Theres many other versions that also have their own modifiers making the gameplay with it more varied. With all the modifiers you can play easy game or run a gauntlet. Basic solid fast paced gameplay filled with constant wallrunning, jumping, diving, slaughtering enemies, throwing used guns on enemies and stealing theirs is just an awesome cocktail of gameplay mechanics with so many details that are really fun to find out by just experimenting with game. Replayability is awesome. Did 100% basic game. Now I'm gonna jump on workshop content.GJ devs, you are the best. This game is so far the most positive surprise I have experienced this year.Anyone else reading this. Buy the game. You'll have tons of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if SUPERHOT and the original Mirror's Edge had an illegitimate kid who grew up listening to breakcore and watching old John Woo movies.This game is a blast to play. The movement, combat, and destruction all flow into each other seamlessly to create a core gameplay loop that just feels good in your bones to experience. Seriously, it's tight as hell.Though this also proves to be a bit of a problem with Severed Steel - the gameplay loop leaves you hungering for more, but there's only so much. The campaign is over in a few hours, and your main options for replay value are either repeating individual levels from the campaign in a deathmatch mode or community-made campaigns that vary from too easy to too hard with no in-between.To the devs' credit, they DID attempt to remedy this by introducing a roguelike mode where you're still repeating a playlist of campaign levels, but you also get modifiers that change the experience with each level completed. But after unlocking all the cards it began to feel a little like a giant grind to me - maybe this is just a flaw in my psychology when I see rare cosmetics in video games and decide I want them at all costs.It would be smart to add more cards to the roguelike mode, especially if they're cards that cater to goofy shenanigans like with items in Risk of Rain, or to add a means of playing randomly generated levels for infinite new things. But adding new items requires a massive creative effort, and randomly generated levels are often not very fun, so for now it's all good.All things considered, though, hella worth the price tag. Woo!

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. A paradigm example of how to take an idea (F.E.A.R, in this case) and build upon it into something wholly unique. The 3D, movement-based combat, with health and AP regained from kills, and no ammo resupplies for weapons make it feel like you are a neutrino dashing about the world. It's addictive. My only minor gripes are as follows: The level manipulation mechanics introduced with the arm cannon are a fun gimmick, but it was never fully taken advantage of in the level design. There were a couple times (like destroying a house or digging a path) where you were expected to use it, and you're always free to in combat, but generally I found its utility was never needed much. I would've loved to see combat arenas where you were expected to navigate using the cannon to survive. My second little ♥♥♥♥♥♥ is that I felt like the diving and sliding mechanics didn't have the best compatibility between each other. I found that I would almost always be chaining dives or chaining slides one after another, but transitioning between the two rarely worked as well for me. Being able to organically transition between slide and dive then slide again during the same jump would've been really cool. Otherwise, the movement based combat of this game is stellar. I was absolutely hooked and would highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I enjoyed a shooter game this much since DOOM 4 came out. There isn't much story to it, but it also features multiple modes with their own challenges. Lots of weapons, basically unlimited maps thanks to the level editor, and a great soundtrack as well. The destruction in some maps and/or with modifiers can get really intense though, so don't let the requirements fool you, a good CPU is a no-brainer for this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥, this game is brutal! , that is. If the game not even giving you a use key to open doors (kicking them in is the only way, including an instant kill for whoever's unfortunate enough to be in the door's way) wasn't obvious, let me tell ya, it's pure unadulterated badassery! The levels are built more like deathmatch arenas than singleplayer levels, with doors, catwalks & teleporters giving your assaulters more than enough opportunities. Pretty much the first thing you do in a level, be it kicking open a door, firing a gun or kicking someone's skull into oblivion and all hell breaks loose. And here's where the fun begins! Shooting is fun all right but if do so merely running around the place on the solid floor, you won't have any fun here neither success. Obviously, there's no regenerating health either, you gotta kill to stay alive which only helps to direct shootouts here into that delightful high-octane action flow.Your main means to avoid damage, getting around and last but not least, having fun, is stunts. Run up the wall, jump into a dive while diving in slow-motion, empty your magazine into a couple guys, land, slide into that shielded prick intead of even bothering trying to flank him, snatch his gun out of his still-living hands, empty said gun into said shielded prick. All of this in slow-motion of course which is badly needed as the game's pace is the best kind of brutal indeed.The game's clear visuals helps great assessing any given combat situation. _childDocuments_.review: Can I get a developer's response to this one? Because I'm really curious about something. For me, this game feels like as if somebody looked at Titanfall 2 and said "what if me made something like that, but with better air control, simplistic level design to allow more movement and clean, easy to read graphics". Was that your intention? Because if it was, no doubt you succeeded.Let's get negatives out of the way first. Yes, this game is short, pretty repetitive, a bit janky, too easy even on higher difficulties and kinda feels more like a tech demo rather than an actual finished product. But that doesn't change the fact that I absolutely love it, it's a ton of fun to play and it just clicks right. Movement is fluid and very responsive, although a bit rough around the edges (for example it's very easy to glitch into the stairs while sliding or fall down like a sack of potatoes while jumping because your character does a flip you didn't intent to do), but none of it is game-breaking. Your mobility is just absurd and I love abusing various mechanics and ripping through enemies like it's nothing. The addition of destructive environment is also really cool, adding another layer of depth to the gameplay. It's especially handy during speedruns. And let me say - I've never even tried speedrunning anything, but in Severed Steel, almost every map is a short and fun speedrun challenge which I thoroughly enjoyed. If you know what you're doing, you can just melt the ceiling here, abuse walljumping there, shoot your objective through the wall and boom, you've skipped an entire level in about 15 seconds. Very smart design choice to include shortcuts like that. Another thing I'd like to mention is the variety of arenas. It's not just medium-sized industrial spaces you see in the beginning, there are also trains, multi-leveled apartment complexes, forests, small cities, mansions, portal arenas... Almost every map plays a bit differently than the last.After you finish the game, you can try out Firefight mode with different mutators, modes, challenges, high scores to beat, etc. I understand that some people may not find it particularly interesting and just call it quits at this point, but I'm still having a blast. The only annoying thing is that some levels (with the addition of Triple Threat mutator) turn into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ slideshow after a couple of minutes, which is just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and needs to be fixed.Overall, a great game, even if a bit mindless.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start off by addressing the most important criticism of the game(albeit one I disagree with): Yes, the base campaign is short. However, it kind of ignores the rest of the game: Severed Steel not only has a NG+ mode which has a higher difficulty, it also has numerous bonus campaigns, a firefight score attack mode, and a roguelike-style mode which are all pretty interesting and fun to play through. There's also a lot of unlockables for each of these modes, including new arm cannons, new starting weapons, modifiers, and even cosmetics(Although admittedly, the latter is something that's kinda pointless, it's still neat/cute to see). You can say it's short but that's like saying Superhot is short: Technically true but ultimately it misses the whole point of the game.With that said, Severed Steel is a pretty fun game. The destructible environments mean you can approach each level in a variety of ways: There were many times where I would use my arm cannon to make a hole in the ceiling to drop an enemy down and take his gun, or blasting open a wall while wall running to get the drop on a group that was focused on the windows. There's plenty of weapons, and none of them in particular feel pretty bad, although a number of them do feel pretty similar. The heavier weapons like the shotguns and the grenade launcher feel pretty satisfying, and the gimmicks that are there for the weapons(Like Snipers having insane punch-through, letting you shoot through walls) are fun to make use of.The environmental design is top notch. Even with as fast paced of a game as it is, I didn't find myself getting disoriented or lost at all, and it's usually pretty easy to see the next objective. Something in particular that I liked was the color design, they did a lot of work in making sure the levels popped out, even in something like a basic office. The soundtrack for this game is also pretty praise-worthy(And I love that you can see the name of each track just by pausing the game, a feature I now wish every game had and I don't know why it's-as far as I'm aware-never been done elsewhere), with a bunch of high-tempo music that really fit the atmosphere of the game.It's definitely not perfect: While navigating levels was fine, sometimes the game can feel a bit disorienting when mid-combat. I found myself getting a bit lost originally and accidentally doing flips which was the main source of my confusion(Although now I do them on purpose for shiggles. Because seriously, how many other FPS games let you actually flip upside down to shoot someone?). I also do feel like 1 of the levels in particular that make use of the destructible environments can be a little frustrating(Because it requires recharging your arm cannon at least once to blast through each wall, which means blasting and then breaking off to recharge so you can go back and keep blasting. It kind of hurts the whole feel of the pacing), but it's a pretty minor speedbump. Besides that, my time with Severed Steel has been almost 100% positive.I got the game for $10 during a sale, but I do feel like it's honestly worth full price. It's an incredibly fun FPS that oozes style, and probably one of the most fun FPS titles I've played in recent years. Just keep in mind that the majority of the game's 'meat' is in its replayability through the various modes it has on offer, along with the Steam Workshop for custom level sharing(and a level editor to make your own maps if that's your thing!).

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel blends so many classics perfectly. You get the wall running and speed of something like Ghostrunner, the bullet time of something like Max Payne, with a flair of Superhot. Each level is small, tight and focused. There's not much story here and you can probably complete the campaign in about 2 hours. That being said, you'll want to play for way more than 2 hours. The gameplay loop is so fun and so satisfying with tons of challenges, a new game+, and plenty of things to do. Completing every mission leaves you feeling like a cyborg John Wick on cocaine.On top of an amazing gameplay loop, the visuals are stunning. They go with a bright neon visual for the most part. Everything is so colorful and fits an amazing aesthetic. The music is also top notch. There's a pretty good amount of enemy variety and lots of weapons you can have fun with. Complete the game and come back for more with mutators to make things even more interesting! This is definitely a must buy in my opinion. My only two complaints, and they're minor are the kicking can feel a bit awkward at times and just the lack of a full speed replay at the end of every stage. Superhot did that and it felt awesome seeing everything happen in real time so you can see how much of a bad ass you were. I want to see the same thing here so I can watch myself do flips and land several head shots back to back to back in a second of real time.I really cant' recommend this game enough, it's an absolute blast where the devs clearly focused on just a couple of things and perfected them all. A lot of games will try to do a lot of things and just make sure they're all OK or pretty well done while this game focuses on a few and makes sure they're all perfect. Well done devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly one of the most exhilarating experiences I've had in a first person shooter. Probably the most fun I've had since superhot came out. _childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is like if you took the protagonist from Mirror's Edge, gave her the Metroid arm cannon along with a mile long bump of speed, and told her to kill everything in sight while doing so with the movement of Titanfall + the dive from Mario 64 + the obligatory bullet time since every movement shooter needs one of those nowadays. It's even in destructible voxels which I've been a crippling addict of since Teardown. The sheer amount of inspiration from other games feels like the components will inevitably have friction between them yet it is absolutely seamless.     The story is 5 still frames because there doesn't need to be a story. The graphics are non-existent because it doesn't need good graphics. All it needs is move and shoot which it does flawlessly, even better than its inspiration mind you. In Mirror's Edge, Faith could barely get to a jog without having to do something that loses all momentum while somehow dodging a billion bullets flying at her. In Severed Steel, you can go from zero to a thousand right into a newly formed cavity in someone's face. In Titanfall 1&2, you are given incredible movement options only for the game to not penalize you for playing it like a normal shooter. In Severed Steel, you need to constantly be doing stunts in order to not have your body not be comprised of more lead than flesh in the span of 2 seconds. I can go on.     For the first 15 minutes you will feel like a fish out of water trying to work out how to move without losing all spacial awareness, but when it clicks, god does it click. You can kick under a door, slide under a table, pick off some enemy's shins, run out of ammo with one enemy left, throw your empty gun at him, steal his gun, and shoot him with it. You can kick an exploding object at an armored enemy, blast him into bits, shoot at his gun to flick it into the air, dive through the air to pick it up, dispatch the remaining enemies in the room while wall running, and blast a hole in the wall for a quick exit. You can double jump, drop kick an enemy, kick the wall to gain some height, and shoot every enemy in the room while upside down. Words do not do these scenes justice and neither does seeing a video do so either. It can only be experienced to fully appreciate.     In my personal opinion, the best maps in the game are those that have some open parts, some small parts, and an objective that isn't just "kill everyone." For example, the train levels were some of my favorite maps since it is all about this open space of outside the two trains with the small cabins of each train that can be breached into along with the objective of destroying the controls at the front of the trains. This is much more open ended level design that encourages creative freedom in how you approach the level. Take this in contrast to the levels where there is just a big empty warehouse of snipers which does not cater to the move set at all.     Very few games (Celeste, Teardown, People Playground) are as ripe for map creation as Severed Steel is. Luckily there is a team of very passionate map makers that produce many times the campaign's maps on a regular basis. There are also a variety of different modes all about playing maps and getting the best scores by killing everyone quickly with a Tony Hawk's Pro Skater type variety scoring system.     Overall while I do take issue with some of the map designs, some fairly weak audio design, clipping into your own character, and a laughably easy boss randomly thrown in there, Severed Steel sets out to do a few things that many have done before and does it in such a way that few others can match.TLDR: 0/10 no grapple hook

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is the good stuff! Damn, man! What a ride this is! I need to take a break. this game is pure adrenaline, so intense!I very much like how this is put together. Movement options with double jump, wallrun, dodge, slide, wallrun resets double jump and melee kicking is like rocket jumping off a wall. The Slow-Mo and how the big white letters tell you what to do strongly remember me of SUPERHOT. The Tron-like graphics remind me of GTTOD. Fitting headbang synthwave beat. I very much like it that the track does play on when you die and retry. The gameplay is very fast-paced and very fluid and fair. I always felt that I should have done something different when I died and not the game. It telegraphs all informations very good and while the enemies react pretty fast (depending on the difficulty setting / can be changed) with the right use of slow-mo it's so cool to take out all of them. Slo-mo is very important, because the game is so fast and enemies react so fast that slo-mo is the only thing keeping you alive. When slo-mo is depleted this most often ended my run. It's limited and only replenishes partly when taking out enemies and enemies are best taken out with firepower which uses ammo. When ammo is depleted and you got no other gun near this is also a critical situation which ended some runs. So during these intense firefights you also gotta have a look on your ammo and your slo-mo gauge and make sure to refill those healthily. This encourages an aggressive gameplay style because you gotta take out enemies to refill both resources. Playing cautiously is possible, but not intended and not as fun as diving into chaos!A BIG and UNIQUE plus goes out to Severed Steel: this is the first FPS I know of that is able to turn the aim beyond your feet! You can literally do a somersault by just turning your aim while in-air. You can jump over an enemy and all the while track him without being bothered with the usual 0° wall FPSs have. Severed Steel manages to do this no limits aim and you will be tilting in-air like crazy flying upside down getting 4x multiplier for that, but when you hit the floor again the view will reset to normal. FULLY DESTRUCTABLE environment! Every shot does different amounts of damage to walls, also the shots from the enemies. Some enemies have grenade launchers which lets them or you tear holes in everything in no time!You get a literal environment destroyer gun which will bomb spheric holes in everything you want! Always good for a shortcut to the goal or an escape method. It's very convenient that the mission goals are marked with a red outline and visible through walls, so you always know where to head to. Speaking of convenience, there is a convenient quit to operating system button right from the in-game menu. I appreciate it! 100% achievements possible in  37 hours since the challenges, Rogue mode and Firefight 2.0 updates more than doubled that time.Very very good gameplay flow, I like it a lot!

_childDocuments_.review: It took me a minute to really get use to all the systems at play, but once you do, this game is out of this world in terms movement and shooting. _childDocuments_.review: A fast-paced FPS game that makes you feel like a total badass+ The gameplay is FANTASTIC and feels like a mix between dishonored and hotline miami+ The game has a simplistic and futuristic look which works well, and it runs well on my fairly weak PC.+ The music is amazing and really fits the explosive action of the game+ The enemies are somewhat varied but they're all fun to fight, especially the enemies with shields+ The weapons feel good to use even though there's not too much variation and the arm cannon combined with the destructable surfaces adds a bit of depth to the fights- The story, well... There isn't much of a story. Which is fine, honestly- I finished the campaign in 111 minutes for a game that I paid 20£ish for. I'm going to finish the campaign several more times and I'll also try out the other gamemodes so those numbers are going way up. For some people this is going to be a big deal, for me it's not.------------------------All in all I think you should buy this game, it's pretty damn awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: I heard of this game through GmanLives and now that it's out, I thought I'd check it out. Overall, it's a very fun and unique shooting game. I don't think I've ever played a first-person shooter game that lets you manually do flips and blast a goon in the face with a shotgun while doing so. The shooting feels good, and like any game with this feature, the addition of bullet time makes it a lot more enjoyable and crisp. It kind of reminds me a lot of F.E.A.R. in many ways, so if you're a fan of the shooting in that game, with the addition of some extra movement options, you'll definitely love this game. The sound design is good too. I especially like the little sound prompts when you kill an enemy or when you're fighting an armored enemy and chip off a piece of their armor. It really makes me feel like I'm doing actual damage and not just shooting a bullet eating sponge.The only negative that I'd note is definitely that feeling of being a bit overwhelmed by the visuals. The game looks very good, but it's definitely not a game I'd recommend you play while sleepy or tired or if you're an epileptic (obviously). I'd imagine that the movement may cause some motion sickness too if you're sensitive to that, not that there's anything that can be done about that. The only other thing I'd like to note is length, not that that's a real issue for me, there's definitely a lot of room for a DLC or some additional maps in the campaign. The level editor is great, but I'd imagine it not being very active if the fandom doesn't grow or remain active enough to push out any levels. With that said, the game overall is good. I picked it up now because I'm bored, and I reckon you guys can too, or wait for a sale. Either or is fine - this game is definitely worth playing for first-person shooter fans. It's a very good game for short to long periods of play, and offers a lot of room for "pick up" and "drop" gaming like Hotline Miami, which I think is good. Overall, yes, this game is work picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good game. It's like FEAR but on crack and slow mo is a necessity in the core combat and not just a optional feature.So many movement tech like slide, wall run, double jump, double jump kick jump to scale higher wall, and even dive. This is the first FPS game I see a dive implemented (like dodge roll in Dark Souls) but can be quite disorienting in first tries. The only con I can say is the checkpoints in Campaign is very inconsistent at times. most of the times its  forgiving but there are handful of times its very punishing throwing you back to previous encounter in same level.There are some modes that unlock weapons and upgrades which can be carried on when repeating Campaign. Another mode to unlock skins and collectibles. Great value for your money

_childDocuments_.review: The first 30mn of the game were very difficult because of how fast the gameplay is. I almost gave up on the game, but after 1h, it finally hooked me. The campaign is short but very nice to go through, the gameplay is very fun once you get used to it and is very rewarding by doing cool stunts.Would recommend, but on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something that has been worked on by a group of devs who truely care about their craft. While overall it is a very straightforward run, jump shoot, kind of game. It mixes things up with its stylish slow-motion, wall running action. It harkens back to a time when the Matrix was popular and we all wished we had this kind of gameplay in our games. While we came close back then, Severed Steel really nails it. Add in the variety of weapons and custom levels and you have a game that is just a solid all around, pick up and play good time.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This game is quite tough to review, it's very pretty, the gameplay is tidy, and the mechanics all work well (other than the kick) but the ideas built on the core gameplay loop are quite shallow. It feels a little unpolished all round, some levels are a joy to navigate and like water you almost fall into a path from start to finish, some feel unnatural and you're left walking around an empty killing floor trying to find the exit. Some levels nail the difficulty, then the next one comes with a high difficulty spike only for the next three to be too easy.Overall it feels a little bit like a rough extended tech demo or a bunch of concept levels.I bought this game in a sale and whilst I couldn't recommend it at full price, I would at a 50%+ discount and it did enough to warrant its purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an hour in and having a great time.  This game has a lot of levels and a lot of different ways to approach it, much like other fps games like it, like SUPERHOT for example.  The movement feels good and I'd say for 5 dollars on sale, this was absolutely worth it.  Full price I might even say is worth it because there is a lot of replay value here.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute gem of a game.Severed Steel is basically stealing the movement from Titanfall 2, the slow motion gimmick from [insert game of your choice here, I'll go with SUPERHOT but on a button press instead of when standing still] and the gameplay pacing from Doom Eternal. But the thing is, it does so . None of these elements feel wonky or half-baked. Wall running, leaping over enemies, sliding under objects feels incredibly good and works flawlessly 99% of the time. The slow motion gimmick works off a meter that refills on kills and is otherwise 'free' during stunt actions, which flows really nicely with the combat - you're never entirely out, but you can also build a comfortable buffer by playing aggressively. Also worth noting that unlike in other 'parkour shooters', your aiming direction is not restricted at 180° up and down - you can do literal front and back flips, which are insanely fun to pull off. And all of it looks fantastic too, with that slick, minimalistic TRON like visual style.Steel is one armed, which is another cool design decision. The first thing I wondered when I saw this was 'how is she gonna reload, then?', and the answer is simple: She doesn't. Gun's empty? Throw it at a guy, grab his offhand out of his holster, shoot him in the face with it. You're constantly changing guns and constantly meant to adapt to your currently available tools. There's 22 different guns covering your regular suspects, and they're almost all very good at their particular niche. I've only found myself ditching 2 specific ones out of the full arsenal as fast as I could get an alternative. And then there's the (minor spoiler?) arm cannon you get after a short while, that allows you to install convenient, creative new pathways into the level architecture. Level architecture is mostly fantastic and encourages using your full parkour kit for fun and stylish killing (and also to avoid getting shot).The campaign is over in a blaze. Takes about 2 hours to burn through on standard difficulty and at your average, casual skill level (and I don't usually play many twitch shooters). It's got a nice variety of different objectives and most of them are fun - again I could name 2 levels I really didn't care for, but that's 2 out of thirty, and they're all rather short. Some of the other missions aren't bad, they work as a one off campaign mission, but I wouldn't want to replay them over and over. Like the one where you have to set a certain amount of the level on fire. Luckily the other game mode puts ALL of these levels into the context of pure KILL THEM ALL combat. There IS a story, but it's not very elaborate and even the cutscenes are rather minimalistic. I don't mind minimalistic world building, but some sort of (optional) lore would have been nice. Afterwards the game has its 'firefight' mode to keep you entertained, which is all 30 campaign levels turned into arcadey KILL THEM ALL missions with optional modifiers, challenges, your preferred starting weapon and the games 5 difficulty levels, as well as workshop support right out of the box. Firefight mode is great and absolutely remedies my small, personal issues with the campaign, as these use all the really well made levels and offer the greatest asset the game has, undiluted by some of the less awesome story mechanics - it's fantastic movement and combat experience.  Though a very subjective matter, I'll mention that the soundtrack is pretty damn hot, if dark electronica be thine jam. Also worth noting that there's a lot of accessibility options, that kinda stuff is always really appreciated.All in all I absolutely love this game. It's much better than it has any right to be, mostly because the components it took from other games have been grafted together very competently, and put into a rather unique context. It's easily one of the most satisfying FPS experiences I've ever had. In terms of fun and quality, Severed Steel is easily playing in the same leagues as Titanfall 2 and Doom Eternal, and even if the quantity of its content is a bit lacking, the pure joy of its gameplay experience is SO worth it. Though to be fair, if the idea of replaying the campaign levels in firefight mode, with challenges and modifiers (but no story) doesn't sound appealing to you, there's probably not enough game to make it worth your while.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is a little in the air for me. I played it back when it released and revisited one day out of the blue and felt as though I wanted to write something about it.Now I play a handful of games like this namely Fear, Ultrakill, Dusk, Quake, Doom yada yada. Severed Steel does stand out on its own and its fun but there are some things to note.For one the campaign is very short. On what I think is regular difficulty I finished in about 2 hours and the same went for my second playthrough. It depends on how long you want to keep going in the carnage.The game is very past paced, and enjoyable in that too. But I can't stress this enough, the controls man, the CONTROLS. They aren't poor or anything, but there is a weird feel to the game locomotion I had to get used to. Its like every step you take your floating over a bed of slippery marshmellows, dunno why but thats about the best I can put it. I often find myself doing very strange actions I hadn't intended but they work out.As for everything else, I couldn't really read into it. Stories are told by the missions and cutscenes between acts, but its worth noting the missions can really take you out of it sometimes. I often lost sight of what I was doing because the game feels more like a museum of arenas more than an objective. For instance (maybe spoilers),  The game ain't going for immersion, but I didn't mind, I've had similar experiences with games like Doom 2016. I don't think this game really needs to try to tell a story, as I see it your just a badass gunslinger with one arm who is insanely lucky ruining someones stuff, presumably the fulla that took your arm. With whats going on constantly, I suspect the intention was to give the story little time to breathe almost like the inverse of Katana Zero.Its a genuine treat. But it won't last long unless you like the Arena mode. Do with that what you will.Oh and for the record, the OST is sex.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the PERFECT balance of brutal difficulty and cakewalk. essentially, you get a slowmo mechanic that refills on kill, and in slowmo you can pretty easily just shoot the enemies and keep going on that slowmo chain, but if you're out of slowmo you get killed almost instantly, your have 5 "luck" witch is just health, and it also refills on kill, so you get this constant high of just going nuts and killing every soldier in your path, and to heighten this john wick esc crazy mode you have to constantly be in to avoid your demise, you get a seemingly simple set of movement abilities that, in truth are simple, yet has a skill ceiling that can be mastered, and when mastered allows for you to make every combat scenario you encounter act as a movie scene where you run around blasting everybody to high hell, and thats a feeling i cannot get enough of. not perfect, but holy hell is this game fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Super Hot but with parkour and fully destructible environments. Very compelling gameplay and satisfying level based high score system after you beat the campaign. The only downside is how short it is for its price, 3 hours of gameplay to 100% achievements for 25 bucks is a little much. Worth buying on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best shooters in a while. While Severed Steel doesn't have a massive budget or team behind it, it absolutely makes up for that unique gameplay that perfectly strikes the balance between brutally fast and instantly accessible, which most indie shooters fail at. The comparisons to SUPERHOT are accurate, but as someone who isn't a fan of SUPERHOT, don't let that discourage you. This is next level.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on sale for ~$20 and finished it in only 3.5 hours. Despite the extremely short campaign, I am fully confident that this game was worth it. Those 3.5 hours we're some of the most fun I've had playing a game in a long time. This is not including that the game has a workshop and level builder for even more maps and campaigns to play on, thus extending that playtime. I can only hope that the main game receives further expansions in the future because this was a thrill from start to finish. If you're a fan of games like Titanfall and Overkill, this game is definitely worth your consideration.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: I especially like the AIs in this game. Enemies can be stunned by explosions or when hit, they can drop weapons and then try to find another one, also they don't magically know player's position and can lose track of player.Also the destructive environment is a very nice addition to the game. There are many creative ways to use it, like making holes on the floor under enemies, or creating an alternative passage in the level.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: fluid movement shooter with bullet time and voxel destruction, although sometimes feeling gimmicky. features a great breakcore(?) soundtrack to accompany the action in-game. bullet time makes the game a lot more peaceful and can be easy to abuse, as its infinite while doing certain movements, but self-aware restraint can make it more difficult if the built-in difficulties arent desired.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: this game saved my life.I am 27.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ing minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: It's been a long time since a game made me feel this absolutely overpowered.There's nothing better than blowing a hole in the floor, dropping down, kicking a guy in the face and against a wall, grabbing his sawed-off shotgun to kill his 2 buddies and then throwing the empty gun in his face before your feet even touch the ground again.There might not be a lot of story (and what is there is pretty vague, to be honest) and the game might be a little on the short side (finished the campaign in under 4 hours, if I remember correctly), but it's just pure fun wallrunning and kick-diving all over the place and headshotting everyone in slow-motion.My only "gripe" with the game, is that the Rogue Steel mode has a very small map pool. You keep playing the same handful of maps over and over again. There should be an option to allow community made maps into the rotation or something like that.Other than that, it's an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: I recently bought a PC and this is one of the first games I've played on it after having been on console since the age of 12. I had a blast playing this game.The gameplay is simple but not in a way that feels repetitive or boring, the movement and gunplay are both incredibly satisfying - the bullet time ability never gets old.I played on Severed steel difficulty and am looking forward to playing again on its hardest.All I would say negatively is that it is maybe just a tiny bit expensive for that length of campaign (I complete it in about 2.5 - 3 hours, I have no idea what the average completion time is) even with the other gamemodes but not so much so that I regret my purchase in the slightest.So if you're looking for a solidly built, fluid and satisfying parkour shooter, I would absolutely recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: So, the gameplay is fun, sound design and music are great, graphics are pretty (though sometimes there can be a sort of information overload at times, especially if you don't use slow-mo and try to do a lot of movement). However, I beat the campaign in about an hour and 30 minutes on its recommended difficulty, which in my opinion is way too short, but that does make it easily replayable, so speedrunners will love this game. Speedrunners will especially love the firefight mode, though it doesn't do much for me honestly. What I'd really love is a round/wave based style mode where you try to live for as long as you can, though sadly the game doesn't have that, and I don't know if it ever will.I didn't mess with the custom level editor at all, but I did try a custom level that was basically a recreation of dust_2 from Counter Strike that was pretty fun, but again it's only for Firefight mode where there's a set number of enemies. Overall, if you love fast paced movement shooters where you try to rack up high scores with style points, you'll like it. I'd definitely play this game more if it had a sort of "Endless" mode, but for me, I think I'm already done with it, having only played 2 hours of it. I've pretty much seen most of what there is to see, I feel, and for this price, I'm not sure I can really recommend it until they add other modes.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: game is an actual masterpiece, movement is smooth and responsive from wall running sliding diving it all just feels great. All the guns are cool and satisfying to use, you're always excited to see what cool new gun your gonna pick up. enemies are varies too, regular grunts, shielders, cloakers, heavies. Level design is awesome, so many different ideas throughout the campaign. Replayability is insane in this game, there's the campaign which is pretty good, then new game plus, a daily run mode, a rogue like mode with modifiers that make the game even crazier, a survival mode, a level editor, just endless fun. Highly recommend if you're i to games like Quake/Doom and movement based games like Mirror's Edge/Shady Knight. Also it goes without saying but every single song on this OST is a banger. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit from the future: I'm going to switch my final verdict from negative to positive. Once you figure out what this game is asking you to do, it can be a lot of fun for a couple hours at a time. I'm going to leave my initial review below, because that was my genuine first impression in the first couple of hours. Most of the gripes there can be overcome and adjusted to after a little while, ie the clunkiness, wall stickiness, etc. Slides still kinda suck as an attack, but they're good movement tec. Overall, especially given the low price tag, I feel pretty good recommending this game....I stand by my comments about the dive mechanic, though. ♥♥♥♥'s ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ass. First Impression: Massive potential here, ruined by clunky controls and poor player-action feedback. The dive mechanic is  one of the worst things I've ever experienced in a movement shooter. The "stickiness" of wall running is an unreliable crap shoot. The hit box for slide kicks is about one pixel wide. I really wanted to like this game and rave about it like everyone else. But, IMO, the aspects of the game that try to stand out from the pack all fall flat and feel terrible.

_childDocuments_.review: wow the music is amazing, and the music kicks in and you have yourself a game that one can describe asghostrunner met mirrors edge, and mirrors edge met titanfall, and titanfall met john wick, and john wick met superhot, and was baked in the oven, you get yourself a nice game that blends everything just nicely.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, first thing to touch on is the . Wonderful tracks. Has the same feel as GITS:SAC on PS2 did, which will keep you pumped without getting old. So crank your speakers for sure.Second, the  are fantastic. Not too frenetic, but just frenetic enough to really mesh well with the action of the game and the cyberpunk/retropunk setting.Third, the  is so fluid and wonderful. Controls are very responsive. _childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: The game feels like it wants to be a cool combo of SUPERHOT and Mirror's Edge. Slide around emptying clips into bad guys and swiping their guns. I tried to play it that way for the first few minutes, but found it too hard to control. It's really easy to get stuck sliding on a wall when you don't want to. I eventually just ended up playing it more like a standard FPS. In that sense it's not too bad, but nothing inspired. The shooting holes in the wall mechanic is pretty fun though. Maybe pick it up on sale if it looks interesting, but not full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: You can read the store page and other reviews to learn about the specific features. I want to tell anyone reading this that this game has been bug, glitch & crash free; the gameplay proves slick with a fluid movement system that's very fun; and the cornucopia of options and mutators available to the player keeps the experience feeling fresh time and time again. I don't know anything about the developers but their passion for the game is evident in the craftsmanship on display, and in the fact that the game continues to be updated with new features and content even a couple of years after release. On top of all this, you have the workshop with community content to further expand the game with. Basically, what I'm trying to say is, Severed Steel rules and is worth the asking price. These are the kinds of games worth supporting.(a multiplayer mode with the likes of deathmatch and ctf would compliment this game like pb&j, tho)
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: As far as I'm concerned, this is "it". The apotheosis of this type of game. Beautiful, buttery smooth, great soundtrack, and the destruction? Oh, don't get me started.Story is pretty good too, if extremely subtle. Think SUPERHOT. The gameplay is the focus.I can't wait to see what happens when Steel returns...
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting for the day I would get my hands (metaphorically) and play the full version of "Severed Steel" after I played a satisfying demo. It is perfect and everyone shall play it.The story can be summarized with one single word: revenge. Seeing the eyes of Steel in the first comic cinematic the only word pop-up in my head. I was right. I will admit in some later scenes *name* had been drawn weird, like she is an old person.So why do I love it? Like always, controls is the king. "Severed Steel" the king of cosmos. It just feels good doing all kinds of stunts to kill your enemies. Obviously you still can run around and start shooting like on a classic FPS. However, don't you think it is way cooler to knock a shielded soldier and shoot his back while sliding to the floor? Do a backflip in the air and blast an enemy group with your laser blast? Run to a wall and headshot an annoying sniper? Can you do something crazier? You can!But with so many awesome moves you need the suitable feedback. A+. It is pure pleasure seeing everything around you getting destroyed and the poor fools flying all over the place from the waves of lead you kindly deliver. With that said the soldiers aren't pushovers. They will fight for their (short) survival. They use rifles, shotguns, shields, grenade launchers, missiles, EVERYTHING TO ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ STOP YOU! They start yelling all the time trying to find you and put you down. The same goes when you hear their agonizing screams when you shoot them in the face. Music to my ears.So you think that you just reach a new level and just kill everything that is breathing? Yes…but before that you need to do other small tasks like to destroy computers, collect legendary artifact (awesome level), burn a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ house and much more!And there is more! After you finish the story campaign, you can start playing arena mode in which you start from the beginning and you slowly unlock new levels, weapons and cheats! CHEATS! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!Perfect. This game is perfect! You shall truly go and buy the game if you didn't already.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is incredibly uncomplicated. Jump, dive, wall run, and shoot your way through loads of bad guys. Unfortunately for the main character, they don't have any pockets for ammo. Once the gun you're holding runs out then you best pick up a new one or you're going to be stuck getting physical. You can kick and punch but it's far less effective. Every enemy drops their gun and you can even pull one off of them if you're close enough.Now, there are two things that make Severed Steel unique.The first one is crazy acrobatics. You move quickly! The developers gave the character a sense of speed while diving and wall running. I'm sure glad they added slow motion to give you time to enjoy everything. Flying over a shielded enemy's head is a great way to get around them. And it's a lot of fun. You gotta keep moving to stay alive too. The movement system is my favorite part of the game.The second thing that makes Severed Steel unique is the destructible environments. Smashing face-first through a glass window firing a gun is fun every time I do it. But it's not only the glass that breaks but all the walls in the game.Overall, Severed Steel is a blast. The few bugs and small graphical issues don't ruin the fast-paced raw action. I really enjoyed the movement system. I agree with all the other reviews and it makes you FEEL like an action star.Full video review,

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed it fantastic movement shooter, music and general feel are awesome but i completed the campaign in about an hour and a half with distractions on the difficulty its meant to be played on according to the devs. There seems to be a weird click delay/recognition in that i can click or spam click for 20 seconds with a fully loaded gun stand there like a tool and get gunned down. I also feel the firefight won't retain my attention nearly long enough to justify the asking price of £22.99 without a sale. Honestly really fun but probably wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: A short but fun fast paced first person shooter. If you just want straight to the point action, then this game is for you. There are a couple of annoyances, like your slowmo ability only recharging with kills (and you're basically defenseless without it) and some long levels with no checkpoints, but other than that it's fun.The story is meh. I know its not a major thing in the game but still. There is a cutscene after every chapter, and even then I don't really know what was going on. Other games similiar to this have had much better implementations.This game is IMO pretty much Max Payne in first person and it's a lot of fun. However it is less than 4 hours long and the "Firefight" game mode just reuses the campaign levels with really slow progression. The colors and flashing lights in the game could also be a problem for some people.I'd recommend this game, when it's price drops a little.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Severed Steel is the hypest game i have played in a long timePicture this, you load into a level you kick in a door dive towards an enemy kick him in the chest, steal his gun to kill him then front flip over a shielded enemy to shoot him in the back of the head, then knowing enemies are upstairs you use your mega buster to destroy the floor under another pair of enemies before effortlessly shooting them in the face. then you proceeded to double jump into that same hole and lay down a cacophony of vengeance before exiting the level.The game is short on normal difficulty I beat it in about 3 hours including unlocking the levels but the game is meant to be replayed over and over again. For 22 bucks at the time of this post its more than worth it and I cannot wait for more content from the creators.
_childDocuments_.name: Severed Steel

_childDocuments_.review: Underrated, Adrenaline fueled gem with a rewarding, fun and fluid gameplayloop which leaves room for personal expression by allowing users to finish levels they way they want to, got a problem? blow it up? chasing the highscore? Headshots.The Campaign can be finished within less than 2 hours easily, the meat is in the firefight mode which is like oldschool arcade fps gameplaytype. If you let it be, this game is alot of fun and the gameplay is only as clunky as your imagination.
