_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR You might get 8-10 hours of enjoyment from your $25, if that's enough for your then go ahead and get it, but If you're looking for a game of better overall value, or longer playtime, then this probably isn't it. The game would need a few significant mechanical changes to have any kind of longer term value.The game's genre is sort of awkward, and it really doesn't hit any sort of traditional tower defense vibe. It's really more of a "defend your tower" game.The defensive towers that you get have some strange pacing early in the game. Some of them are good, and some of them are objectively trash. But that doesn't really matter because even the good ones are only good for a little while. The damage of your towers doesn't scale at all, and the only upgrades that you can get for them are different forms of health upgrades.Your towers will continue to do more and more damage as you play the game, but only because you are collecting more and more of them. Eventually you max out your available tower slots and their effectiveness flatlines. At this point your main cannon takes over and winds up being the vast majority of the actual gameplay, turning the game more into a point and click shooter.This doesn't feel especially good because the main cannon doesn't seem to have been designed for high intensity gameplay at all. There are a few main cannon variants that do slightly different things, but they all have miserable reload times and very little ammo between reloads, so you spend a lot of time watching your rubberband-gun turrets whittling things down. And there's not a lot of interesting gameplay to be had otherwise. The enemies don't do anything interesting, they're really never difficult to click on, they don't have any special interactions with eachother, it's just slightly more and more powerful versions of generic baddies, and the most interesting that the point and click gameplay ever gets is limited to basic decisions about which is the biggest enemy that you should be clicking on.There's nothing especially interesting about the main cannon or the turrets either. For a game essentially called "Tower" I would've expected more interesting towers. Instead all you get is your basic stuff. Auto turret, mortar turret, frost ray, a couple of anti air turrets, nothing you haven't seen before. You do get some units that you can add to your army, but you can't control them at all, and they don't seem to be any more meaningful than just a basic tower anyway. Same sort of story with the main cannon. You get a literal cannon, a beam, a shotgun, a mortar, a missle, just nothing very interesting at all.Overall I could see some real fun in this game if you could rearrange and customize your defenses for the mission that you're on. But you can't. You just can't. The only way to replace a tower with another tower is to destroy it, but then that destroyed slot can't be used until the next mission, and so your stuck with whatever tower setup you already had at the start. This leads to you designing your defenses as a very generic "do everything" defense with a few towers for any enemy that you might fight in later missions. Combined with the generic feel of the towers themselves this leads to a sort of samey feeling to every mission, with only a slight power ramp mechanic that takes of form of "your main cannon does more damage" between missions to keep things interesting.There's also not many missions. Only 4 actually. those 4 missions are sort of mildly randomized by "difficulty" which is really just the number of enemies that will appear. And the map selection, which is also very samey. Not that missions could get much more varied or specific because that might require specialized tower defenses, which you're not capable of building.

_childDocuments_.review: My first impression video for the TL;DR -  , one thing to implement in a hurry rn would be great - Time 1x, 2x, 3x, etc function, i.e fast forward! Refreshing spin on the TD genre. Fleshy combat.Great environment.Destruction is good and fleshy too. Good early progression.Good graphics. (Poly type in level)The Not-So-Good bits:-Late progression is a literal grind loop.[1]Weapon upgrade slot machine(called 'forge') mechanic is RNG despite not needing to be. Only a few builds are viable. Research tree is a bit small.Mission variety is not much[2]No tutorial levels, complicated design.[1] - I got to the Overlord at Day 50 first time and tried to beat it. I failed. Then I got him very late and in that time I had upgraded everything on my tower like 20 days earlier and had to literally do the same few things over and over again to get the much feared Overlord again. To make this point really, really clear. I would just start the level and watch something else on my 2nd monitor with no sound on the game because mostly my units alone were able to clear 90% of the levels, I just had to sit and watch and upgrade stuff that was not necessary in my research tree. [2] There's like 5 - 6 types of missions that you do and you can choose which type most of the time after the first couple of missions but this does get repetitive a bit. It's not like its not different its just that what you get at day 15 vs day 20 on the same 'type' is just 'more of that type yo'. And the problem with this is that this is not even like Bloons which is quick progress. There's a lot of waiting and unskippable anims and reasearch that cannot be actively done within the level or upgrades. Everything is very locked in and committed which makes it a lot slower and very waiting room to finish-y. Wave times are very delayed and such. If there was a feature to fast forward time I would have finished this game in a third of the time. ----------------------------------------------- because the goods very much outweigh the bad at the moment and I would like to see this game develop into a much better game. Hell, I give 9 on potential alone if its realised.

_childDocuments_.review: Through the first 0-1 hours i had a LOT of fun, every enemy bot shot by my towers felt like an acomplishment.... until it didn't. I started unlocking towers, abilities, turrets, shields, etc. That was the point that it started to get boring. The difficulty in this game dissapears almost immediately. After day 15 or so I started to get shields. The game turned from a struggle for survival to "How many aircrafts can I fit in one map" simulator. The only things i started putting down are the jets, shields, defenders and rangers. Why? Because that was the optimal play of course. Since then the game became a grind to get every ability and upgrade you can. The game suprised me at lvl 20 with the air raid with 30 or more jets, but after that i got used to it. Maybe buy this game at 50% off if you can, otherwise i would stay clear unless the devs add more difficulty options, mutators, or pretty much anything to make the game more interesting+ Great low polly art+ Variety of skills and towers- Heavy grind at the endgame (and by that i mean ~day 20/1.5 Hours)- Low enemy variety- Reloading takes way too long- Too easy

_childDocuments_.review: While I do think Taur may benefit from a difficulty setting (you have to play for quite a while to get into anything of any real challenge) I don't think that's nearly so much of an issue as it would be were the rest of the game not just so much fun to play. The sound effects are satisfying, the physics make scoring a hit feel real and meaningful outside of just chipping away at an HP bar (though you do need to do that, too.) Taur isn't going to be a huge challenge for veteran tower defense genre players, at least not for the first 100 or so levels, but that doesn't mean it isn't a hell of a lot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: (Based on v1.31, 12.9h playtime and nearly 100% completion of the game, played on "Easy" difficulty)Taur is a very good "reverse" TD game which keeps the player heavily engaged in most missions. Impressively elaborate skill and tech trees, a satisfying number of different maps and enemy types.Ressources won through missions and trade create a great internal and coherent economy.All in all a very well designed TD game with a few minor flaws, but once you've found your rhytm, the gameplay loop is highly satisfying.+ Visual and aural spectacle in the later game+ Unique central grid and diverse types of towers allow for both active and reactive playstyles+ Elaborate skill trees, "Rebels" and "Sentinels" systems for micromanaging small individual army+ 6 different abilities and primary weapons, combined with specific enemy threats keeping the player engaged in every mission+ "Trade" system creating an organic economy and keeping all ressources relevant throughout the entire game- Progression system and missions  result in a frustrating loop of multiple defeats, if towers were researched in sub optimal order- Primary weapon upgrades are heavily RNG based and ranking up may very well  the actual damage- A number of user-unfriendly UI and gameplay elements (white crosshair virtually not visible in massive skirmishes, no active notification/warning for destroyed towers, rebels not dismissable unless part of a squad)- Small technical issues (mouse acceleration, mouse not usable when having USB-plugged controller (?), game freezes when using Exit from main menu

_childDocuments_.review: I had 1.2hrs into this game, and 2 campaign runs so far. The visual design of this game is simple yet stunning, I enjoyed the low poly style, what I really dislike is the gameplay and UI.1. The Resource Icons.They are just over-simplified, and their meanings are poorly conveyed to players. It's unclear what kind of resources you want to get until you're forced to notice it -- when you have insufficient amount of them. But it's often too late to start aiming for the ones you actually needed because this game is kinda unforgiving to new players. This could've been made so much easier by making them unique like 'Power Cells', 'Control Circuits', 'Energy Crystal', 'Energy Matrices', 'AI Cores'. Instead they're separated into 2 categories and made into 3 tier each, which made it really confusing.2. The Tutorial.There's really not much to say about it. Maybe devs think the game is so simple that it doesn't need a proper tutorial, or even a working one. The fact that you have to reach for 'Enter' key to mark the game tip as read is like the worst design choice in this game, not to mention that it won't go away until you hit enter or escape  ( escape make the tip go away but back again the next time you enter the menu or jump into a game), and it covers the most important resource indicator of this game in menu so.. Have you really tested your game??3. The Aiming system.I'll be straight forward, it's just not fun imho. It's weird and it's not really rewarding and satisfying enough to compensate your frustration when you miss a shot, because the problem is clearly not your aim but the poor design of the game.4. Maybe add save and load slots to the game, or just a prompt that ask you to confirm when starting a new game which overrides your last save file.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited when I saw this pop up on an ad and I was thinking about it all day on release day. Just couldn't wait to get home from work to play it. Game just isn't fun.... The gameplay loop is thin and the core of the game just doesn't have enough meet there to keep me playing. Plus the tech tree feels forced like there is one or 2 correct builds and your main cannon is a joke. You shoot at the max of 5 nerf darts until you gotta reload. You can barely handle 10 units by yourself and I get that its a tower defense game and I'm suppose to build towers to help me handle the swarms but when your main cannon with 0 accuracy has to 2 shot each minion with a starter mag of 3 nerf darts you're going to have a terrible time. Oh and you can land a perfect artillery shot literally putting the shell down the minions throat and it still won't kill them, its basically small splash damage across the board. Game should say Early Access. The game itself and concept is super cool but it needs more and the balancing needs work. I'm sorry to have to give this game a bad review.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, I really enjoy what Taur can sometimes be, DESPITE what it normally is. The first 4 hours are boring as brick, it takes forever for the game to actually give you equipment, let alone an interesting fight. You are really terribly weak, and that never really changes outside a few abilities and end game weapons. And the rest of the game is only really great in these rare gem moments of full battle where you claw desperately to win a tough fight. But most of it is either, crush the enemy, or get steamrolled by a force you had no hope of winning.As a game itself, wow is it slow and annoying. Takes like 2-4 hours before the game starts letting you have fun blowing up some enemies. Even then, I feel like a stick smacking a steel knight most of the time. The game will suddenly swarm you with hundreds of enemies, while you the PRIME CANNON are basically only good in a 1v1 against boss enemies. You CANNOT fight swarms, and that is 80% of what the game sends at you. You are "SUPPOSED" to beat this with towers and units but the game is frustratingly stingy with handing out basic resources to you to actually build anything.So like, look. Play it if you have the stamina to sit through crap until you get moments of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game.Taur is, in my opinion, one of the most original and well realized game of the genre.The graphisms are absolutely gorgeous, and the sheer scale the battles can reach makes for a memorable experience.However, the game does have quite some challenge to it, with the difficulty spiking pretty roughly in the first few levels.This can easily filter out players who haven't figured out what works and what to prioritize in terms of towers and upgrades, but once you find what works, the difficulty becomes much more manageable, while still achieving victory by the skin of my teeth in brutal in multiple occasions.overall, this game is absolute spectacle and well worth the money in my opinion.P.S: Most of the negative reviews on this game stem from either skill issue or a flat out inability to read (like players complaining that losing a tower makes you lose all the material when it is refunded to you at the end of the battle, which is litteraly written down at some point)

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay loop is fine but overall flow ultimately fails. What I look for in Tower Defense games is simplicity, experimentation and progression with each incoming 'wave' testing my strategy to see what worked and what didn't. Plan, execute, watch and observe... that's the fun of it.In Taur you'll bounce in and out of missions that last from 30 seconds to a few minutes not really knowing what was effective or not. This completely breaks the flow. After each victory instead of accomplishment I found only disappointment. Commitment to this game than is survival on a broader scope of a planetary war which may work for many. After 90 minutes of play time roughly 25 missions, the game remained a frenzied action shooter and simply not for me.

_childDocuments_.review: Taur is a game where you have a central point that must be defended against hordes of enemies. : The game has fantastic visuals and sound design. It feels good to shoot the tower and witness the explosions around the battlefield. The difficulty is engaging while not being too overwhelming (you are refunded for destroyed towers, allowing you to completely rebuild at the start of every mission). My biggest gripe is that there is not enough planning. You cannot plan your base with your current resources  a mission. Instead, you must build in the mission which, if you do not memorize all resources, technology costs, grid costs, and turret placements, you are left unable to prioritize and strategize your path forward. Taur is a captivating game yet a frustrating one. The graphics and audio are clean, immersive, and beautiful. Shockwaves erupt from the impact of your base landing on the terrain, while wisps of smoke fade away like lingering specters of gorgeous explosions. The pacing is even and good, and the game slowly teaches you about all the units will you encounter over the course of your campaign. I see other people complaining about a "death spiral," but I have not been in a death spiral after losing even three times in a row. The missions are randomly generated and vary. Every tower that is destroyed has either a partial or total refund on its resources, allowing you, at the start of the next mission, to hold "R" to restore your base. . The ultimate goal of the game is to beat the boss -- a massive warship with enormous health, armor, shields, and the ability to spawn hordes upon hordes of enemies. Due to the RNG element of the missions, there is a good amount of re-playability, although this will indubitably also cause frustration.Missions vary in type, location, opponents, resources, and length. The main category of missions are: Invasion missions are where all enemy types (infantry, tanks, air) merge together in an assault on your base. They are typically the longest as waves can spawn of varying strength and composition as you progress further in the campaign. Sky fall is an infantry-only mission, where hordes of units fall in close-quarters all around your base and you must fend off the constant swarm of infantry until the mission ends. The infantry are primarily regular grunts, grunts with armor, and grunts with rocket launchers.Air raid is an air-only mission, where hordes of aircraft attack your base (starting from the edge of the map) until you defeat them or are defeated by them. The aircraft are fighters, bombers, and gunships.  Siege is a tank-only mission, where hordes of tanks (brought in by aircraft that can be destroyed, killing both), attack your base until you eradicate them or are eradicated by them. Tanks come in a few variants: Tanks with shields, tanks with a lot of armor, and tanks with rocket launchers. I don't remember what this mission is called (Hellkron?), but you must fight an enormous boss which spawns all types of enemies while attacking your base. It is difficult but thoroughly engaging to fight. My biggest complaint is that there are no mini-bosses before fighting the final boss, and that the boss fight will always be the exact same with no variation in phases, movement, level, etc. Beat the boss, win the game.Except for the final boss level, all missions take place in a wide variety of terrains. These include - forest, jungle, desert, crystal fields, mountain, coast, lake, tundra, cliffs, etc. Upon completion, each mission will reward you certain resources. The  is by completing the mission. Missions also have two factors pertaining to your faction: Defeat score and an incomplete score. You can often choose from three missions, but any that are not chosen will have a number (1 - 18ish, maybe more) that will influence the total Taurian-Imperion counter at the top. This means you may find certain missions with crucial resources needed, but have to choose a different mission to prevent Imperion from reaching 100, ending the game with your defeat. All of this information is presented rather well, and prioritizing Taurian influence with resources results in more complex decision making than selecting a level. In fact, you may know your base handles tanks poorly at the moment, so you choose a Sky fall mission knowing the total increase to Imperion score will be greater than the rewards to Taurian score for completing the mission. You can't change or plan your base outside of a mission! If you want to change your turrets you must destroy them in a mission, preventing you from building on that spot until the start of the next mission. But you do not know what the next mission will be, and if other towers are destroyed . I just want to know what I will be able to do in the future. Right now, here is the scenario you will find yourself in, what I will call a "Indecisive Loop" (different from a death-spiral so many others complain about). Let's say I complete a mission -- my core tower survives but some of my other towers are destroyed. I have resources at the bottom of the screen showing my current inventory. Resources are refunded for your destroyed towers, but I do not know which towers were destroyed (there are a lot and they all kinda look the same). In addition, I am now also supposed to make decisions to use resources for technology. I can use the resources from my destroyed towers (which are in my inventory), thus preventing me from rebuilding at the start of the next mission, or I can try the next mission by rebuilding my current base at the start and re-using all the destroyed turrets resources to rebuild those turrets. Unless you reach a point where you have an enormous benefit of resources, you will probably be rebuilding your base first instead of trying something new and figuring out your future plan. Why can't I look at my current base and repair it in space? Why can't I use my resources before a mission to plan how to expand my base? And, if I realize I have too many/too few of a certain turret, to replace it without waiting to start a mission and destroy the turret in the middle of the fighting? Then I can see exactly how many resources I have, exactly how many resources my expansion will cost, and then I can choose expansion of my base vs. acquisition of technology. This way I can strategize my base and composition and not rely entirely on RNG of missions, resources, enemy composition, and maps to determine how I want to build my base. As it stands, I cannot recommend because there is no way to plan without memorizing the structure of your base, towers available/lost every mission, resources, etc.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: After finishing the game in its (near) entirety, I had to un-recommend the game due to a couple factors: Bear in mind that I DID factor in the fact that this game is developed by only 1 person and thus is reasonably lacking in certain aspects. 1. The game has a very interesting premise but soon fell flat by day 10, from which point on you already forgot about the premise. The ending was unsatisfying and there was exactly 3 lines of storytelling in the entire span of the campaign. If we even had a little bit more narrative at the end and somewhere in the middle, the story wouldn't have been this lacking. 2. The game has practically zero replayability and scalability. With just basic understanding of how TD/Idle games work in general, you can completely destroy this game with very little resistance. Defeats don't even set you back in resources, but a pointless point system which you can easily turn back -- and given how 80%+ of the deployments are incredibly easy, it's practically impossible to screw up. 3. Going back on point 2, the end boss is very unsatisfying to play against. It had 3 phases that requires very little strategic adjustment on your part, and it is very reminiscent of a street gang fight of raw firepower. You also have practically no hope to succeed on the first encounter, and some slight odds to win (with very careful planning and decent strokes of luck with reforging) by the second, but the Boss is practically powerless against your reinforced shields and overpowering firepower by the third encounter -- again, very unsatisfying since for 99% of the players it'll be impossible to ever end up in a even match against the boss. 4. Progression is very linear with few player choice. There's too few structures and since every map has the exact same tower set-up, your entire battlestation will be static throughout the game bar some major adjustments to lineup vs the final boss's phase 2 (where I put most of my turrets on the west/north and support units on the east/south, away from the frontline)5. This is probably the most important pseudo-complaint: This game IS very fun to play, the good mechanics are there, the Prime Cannon mechanics is very well-integrated and the game strikes a great balance between numerous factors that make similar-genre games repetitive and difficult. However, the price-tag is very much on the expensive end for what it has to offer. A reasonable price would be 8$ (on the high end) or more suitably 3$, unless the developer rectifies these major downfalls plaguing the game at this moment.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I will say that this game has  a lot of potential and could become very fun with some adjustments, ALSO if I've missed something or misread something please let me know, i'd love to be wrong here.I love tower defense games very much, they are my go to for almost any mood. I have games for intense, hardcore, make one wrong move and your dead TD games, and relaxing, no way to lose TD games, and everything in-between. This game, I'm sorry to say, ends up in the "good idea, executed poorly" pile which is sad.The research tree is a absolutely engaging idea, the premise is intriguing if a little odd, the combat style is enjoyable in that you have control of the primary tower, and the researched towers are very powerful in their own right. So why the thumbs down? Because all of this is executed on a very poorly engineered platform.Lets start with the premise: The idea is an AI 2 is invading AI 1, AI 1 is losing so they hire an "organic" to win it for them. Now if you lose a battle you just move on in the "campaign" which says to me you are controlling these towers from elsewhere. NOW if this is true then at mission select you should be able to deploy a response to each of the available missions instead of having to pick one and lose the others by default. Moving onto game design: You control the primary tower and add additional towers by unlocking the slot then buying the tower, but only the towers you've researched. Problem here is the unlocking the slot and buying the tower require the same resource which is WAY TO RARE so you VERY quickly end up at a point where you need more OR better towers. MORE towers is locked by the aforementioned resource, better... well see belowUpgrading or "forging" your towers: This is a "random" system where you spend resources and get a random chance at a better weapon... OR a worse one and the chances seem to be stacked in the "bad' one. In a game that relays on you having sufficient towers of acceptable power and armor this game goes OUT OF ITS WAY to make getting there beyond maddening. I really would like to know why the developers thought including a random system in a critical factor of the game so heavily dependent on strategy was a good idea? blows the whole "tactical strategy" aspect right out of the water and makes this a "luck" game, meaning if you don't get the right draw... you lose REGARDLESS of your strategy, almost seems like it was setup to be a micro-transaction system "Aww you got a poor outcome for X dollars you can try again"If the "random" system is removed and the resource drops are increased (Slightly, like 1 or 2) this could be a truly challenging and rewarding game, on par with Elemental TD 2, elemental TD (Android), 2112 TD (Android) and the like. But for now is it, sadly, not worth its price point, even at $5 this isn't worth it. Which is sad because you can really see the effort and energy that went into this and I think those 2 changes I mentioned would instantly make this a $30 maybe even $40 game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first review on Steam. I decided to write a review about this game because it gave me a lot of enjoyment for the sub 10 hours I played it.Taur is a mechanically simple but somewhat strategy tower defense game. Playing it, my first thought was "wow, this takes me back to playing Crimsonland!" You start with a single main gun and over the course of play upgrade your base with more weaponry and defenses, fine tune your main gun through an RNG process and decide which path you'd ultimately like your base to go into.The game plays very well. The graphics are spectacular in all of their textureless glory. The audio feedback from the game is extremely solid. Firing weapons feels right. The mass and weight of everything seems proper. Controlling the Prime Cannon is a treat, and the game conveys all the minutiae of what's going on in realtime without confusion.The stages are divided up into a few varying types, such as Air Raid (aircraft only), Siege (massive tanks with shielding and big guns), Invasion (waves of mixed enemies) and Skyfall (instant infantry overload). My personal favorite is Siege because the games are very fast and there is nothing quite like blasting holes into larger tanks.Here's where the issues start, however. The game starts off fairly innocuous, with only a smattering of enemies here and there. As you play, you find which weapons are fairly easy to use and what defenses and abilities carry you. Once you've gotten into that easy-mode of gameplay, the difficulty of overwhelming enemies seems nigh insignificant. I have gone through Skyfalls and Invasions where I didn't even have to fire my Prime Cannon because my defenses are doing such a good job of prioritizing and destroying the enemies that the game almost plays itself.The learning curve of the game takes time, though, and I believe that is a plus for the game. At day 50 the final boss appears. And I got smashed. 25 days later, the boss spawns again, and I held myself better but didn't really understand what was going on until it was too late. Finally at day 100 I was able to defeat the final boss. Granted, it only took me 100 days to defeat the final boss, so it was more of a patient grind from 75 to 100 once I realized what I had to do. But that grind had no variety or true difficulty to it, and I felt sort of like I had already beaten the game. Once I finally did beat the boss, I realized I had seen almost all there was to see.The game is great, don't get me wrong. Was it worth $25? Eh, 10 hours of solid and engaging entertainment is probably worth that. But the game has limited replayability and I will probably only ever see it again to show it to my friends who I enjoyed playing Total Annihilation and Crimsonland with. :)8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this for a tower-defense-like experience, where you maybe have to strategize about what weapons to use for which map, where using abilities at the right time is vital, etc.But while the game feels quite polished a bug free, I quickly relized that while all the turrets you can call in add to the overall damage you will cause, exchanging a few towers here and there hardly makes a difference in the big picture.The main-turret-weapons also seem kinda strangely balanced. Most of them are simply a worse choice than the upgraded basic weapon. Even specialized weapons that e.g. are especially good for draining shields, are inferior over all, since they do not recharge while you bring down the no-longer-shielded target with another weapon.The AA-rocket does an okay job, but it is super boring locking a plane, firing, locking another, firing, ... wait ~10s for reload and repeat.You cannot even switch to a different weapon during the reload, since then the reload just stops or even starts over.Anyway, I played through the campaign, and while the overall volume of enemies increases somewhat, the last missions didn't really feel any more difficult than e.g. the 10th, with the exception of the boss-ships that comes every 25 levels, which to me seems to be intentionally unwinnable at level 25, 50, maybe 75.If you are looking for something you can fire up quickly and spend 10 minutes or so shooting stuff up, then sure, this might be a fun little game, but if you were hoping for something with more depth or difficulty, I'd pick something else.

_childDocuments_.review: So, first did i recommend the game? It's a big yes. But  there is some little thing that need to be said. First, in respone with every player saying "it's an endless lose spiral" no, look a little bit at the game and you will see that when a tower get destroyed, IT'S ENTIRELY REFUND. Second, if you die on the first few day... You're not ready for the days after 80. You can't blame a game cause you're bad. It's remind me of something... A yes, Git Gud Scrubs. Third, the dmg of the tower. I see some people complaining about the dmg of the tower being unfair, that it's ridiculous. To that i have to say that i didn't get any problem on this side on my first run. The first tower you get is insane with some upgrade, it OS every little infantery ennemy, and you destroy ennemy tank quickly. So yes, the game is hard, but not impossible. You need to prioritize some upgrade, when you see a precise ennemy, focus it, etc... there is some kind of aim assist too, so aiming is not THAT hard. I love all the effect of explosion, it was soooo good. The graphisms are good too, and i love to see all the little infantery fly when i nuke them. It's hard, but not impossible. Now, even if i defended the game until now,there are downside, and some of them are BIG. First, balancing. In the early wave, flying rounds are unbeatable. In the late wave, Tanks wave are unbeatable ( 40-50 tank is wayyyyy too much), skyfall is a joke from beginning to the end, weapon switch take SO MUCH TIME it's useless to switch to a precise weapon to beat a precise ennemy (like a shielded one) cause the time you spend switching is so long you better just keep firing with the weapon you have, cause the switch time is the time you take to take down the special layer you were switching for. Ressources are SO BADLY GIVEN. I have no Tech Ressources, but i have 100 big construction ressources, 80 medium, and 0 small. The Missile launcher SUCK SO HARD, it's useless AF. Better just machinegun the aircraft, it's way better. The missile launcher OS ennemy when upgraded a little, that's cool... But if you OS an ennemy with 50 hp left, and you do 250, that's a bit useless. It take to much time to reload, to much time to lock(even fully upgrade) you can take down 5 aircraft with a full clip of missile, but you can take down 10-15 with a machinegun(when it's upgraded  Of course) What else... Some towers are useless, like the little laser one, Some weapons are useless, like the shotgun and the missile launcher ( the big one). I had to restart from 0, cause after wave 100, it's hard, to hard. The boss is so difficult, it's so hard, i inflict him 150000 out of his 200000 hp, and the last phase is "timed" cause he launch an attack every X time, and you can't tank it more than 4-5 time.I think i said everything i needed to say. So if you want to play, go, it's worth, and fun. But it's hard, you're maybe gonna die, again and again, but hey, it's a part of the game.For some improvement, i think a level editor would be SO MUCH FUN, maybe some kind of speed challenge on given map, i've see a coop idea, but i think a pvp one where you send ennemy on your ennemy and gain ressources to build your defenses could be quite good too.Finally, I hope the developpers are not gonna let the game die and are gonna listen to the community and improve there game, because the potential is HUGE.gonna update the comment the more i play, so it's maybe gonna changeAnd if you read until here, ty for you're time ;)

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to give this one a middle mark.As the game itself feels rather nice. Aesthetically pleasing, rather dynamic for TD sort of game.Some neat systems like resources and research tech to keep you busy between the stages.Even threat management in form of point based tug-of-war with enemy.However, there are two glaring elements, that presence of which I fail to comprehend.1. Weapon enchanting. And they did it like in old mmo. You can make gear better, but with few outcomes, of various degrees. So for same amount of precious resources invested, your gun might get a whooping 1dmg per shot more. As opposed to lets say 5 in best case.Why would they do that to players..? This ain't mmo, nor even some crappy parasitic mobile game.Let the people have normal steady progress.2. Another thing, I mentioned scoring system for threat, right?You clear the mission, you get + points. You fail, and you'll get into negative.Makes sense? Should..but devs came up with idea of giving you up to 3 "mission" prompts.Each with slightly different reward and score you can get/lose.Problem? They plastered penalty score for "abandoning" prompt. So you pick one, and remaining two give you cumulative negative score anyway. Not as big as losing them, granted... but here's the catch:Mission A: Win: 20 Failure: -20 Abandoning: -15Mission B: Win: 15 Failure: -15 Abandoning: -4Mission C: Win: 10 Failure: -10  Abandoning: -3And of course, mission A is the hardest. In this sense, game doesn't give you any real choice, especially if you're close to defeat and trying to get back up. Because penalty for ditching this one is bigger than other two missions combined.That is just poorly planned.Either way, up to you lads, whatever you'll play this or not.

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure if "Tower Defense" is the right term for this, but whatever. You have a tower at the center of the map that you control. Over the course of the game you can research more weapons for it, as well as an assortment of turrets and summoning buildings that will act on their own. A bit of a downside is that there isn't much freedom in what you should research and build. Some weapons, turrets and summons are just much better than others and you can't really win the game without them.I'm slightly disappointed that the boss enemy doesn't reappear after you've defeated it and entered endless mode. It would be nice to be able to face it again with all the upgrades and your ultimate tower setup.Despite these shortcomings the game is very enjoyable. There are few things as satisfying as seeing one of your Destroyer missiles blowing a hole into the enemy hordes and watching them scatter into polygons.The game is currently missing the feature to delete save games, unless you want to delete all of them and your game settings with them, by finding and deleting the save file. From a technical perspective I have no complaints. I haven't encountered any bugs and the game runs very stable, it only crashed once when I tried to exit the game (progress was saved though) and I had only slight lag when there was an exorbitant amount of enemies on the screen (I have a GTX 1060). Mind you, I mean an extreme amount of enemies for this game, since normal battles in this game are already quite large. It was far from unplayable even then though.

You can not change the mouse cursor. Which is a real problem, as in the later levels there is so much going on that's almost white, it becomes impossible to see your (also white) cursor.2. You cannot remove or rearrange rebels that are not in a squad. This just seems spiteful, as you can do both in the squads themselves.3. There is no way to place buildings outside of missions.4. There is no way to tell how much you'll need to spend for repairs outside of missions - so it's perfectly possible to spend more in-between missions than you should.

_childDocuments_.review: reloading simulator 2020. You spend more time reloading your weapon then anything else. even with full upgrades you barely get to do any damage before you have to go through the excessively long reloading count down. This looks like it could be a fun game but needs a major major balancing pass. If you lose a battle you lose your defense and more or less need to build it over from scratch.  If you have some crystals saved up you might be able to rebuild some of it. But it;'s a losing battle. I went to day 55 (that's 55 battles) before giving up. _childDocuments_.review: Despite some QoL (Quality of Life) improvements that could be made, I enjoyed the game a lot and kinda wish we saw more of these "literal tower defense" games. Taur is beautiful, has great visual effects, and offers a lot of freedom in how to play the game. Whether you wish to reforge your main weapons and fight the waves yourself, summon armies of mechanical phalanxes to guard you as I did, or sit back and watch as your pilots rain death from above, there's a playstyle for everyone it seemed and a lot of replayability. This would be especially true if they add some QoL improvements as I mentioned, like perhaps a speed-up or the ability to instantly spawn coming waves to reduce the slow campaign start. The game could also do with being more challenging or offering difficulty options. It has an X-COM mission style where you're offered 3 different missions, can only do 1, and suffer abandonment penalties for the others. After completing a mission, you get resources and a certain score and lose score from the abandoned missions. You lose the campaign once the score drops to 0. For me, it was easy to build the score up to 100 (starts at 50) by just always choosing the biggest reward and once I reached it, it was rare that I ever dropped below 100 by taking whichever mission had the biggest abandonment penalty or making sure the mission's score gain is more than the others' score loss. Looking forward to playing more and seeing if the difficulty starts to creep, but for now, the beginning does feel too slow and too easy.Overall - I must say I'm surprised by the price and not sure if I would've bought it had I not been given a press code, but I did enjoy it and think it has a lot to offer and potential for some to be even better with some simple updates, so I'd recommend it (:

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal indie game!  I haven't played a tower defense shooter in a long time, but this game brought me back into the genre.  I like the way the campaign is set up, and there is a lot of options to upgrade everything. There's some replayability with the upgrades and what you can choose to do, maybe a run with just air defenses, or ground defenses, or units, etc.  The tech tree adds a lot.A few cons: it got too grindy to upgrade weapons later on when you had to start using building cores, so I just focused on towers upgrades at that point.  Could use a few more enemies, a few more tower types, a few more upgrades, a few more mission types.  I wish I could upgrade the damage of rangers and shield guys.That said, this was just released and I am sure there will be content updates. I had a lot of fun playing one campaign and got through nearly all the upgrades.  Campaign skirmish matches are the perfect length to not get bored.  The artstyle is well done.  The music fits, but is just kinda there.  The ability to rain frost arrows is incredibly powerful.  I do not want to say overpowered because I would rather other abilities and tower damage get some buff and only see a slight debuff to the arrow ability.  Felt like I was doing all my damage with that, especially with the last boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent.  Maybe even outstanding.  Good unit/weapon options, great research curve that fits the increasing difficulty as the game progresses. _childDocuments_.review: [UPDATE 3] Developer just added a content update which appears to be substantial. Glad to see they didn't abandon it. Still feel they have a little more to go regarding some mechanics of the game and content, but it's now beyond the demo point IMO. The RNG parts of the game still need a rework.[UPDATE 2] Sadly, the developer hasn't touched the game for awhile now. Shame. Still needs more content for the price point. Worth around 7-10 euros IMOP.[UPDATE 1] Finally had a chunky patch delivered and it's going in the right direction. Sadly, the developer has been rather silent, but at least it appears they are still working on the balancing issues. What I mention below still stands, as the game needs more content/game modes, not just a few more maps.I recommend this game when it's on 50%+ discount in it's current state.The game is not worth 20 Euros. Why? Because of a lack of content. You'll pretty much be doing the same thing over and over again, albeit a few different strategies on different mission types. As so many people have said before me, the game is hard, not because you might not be good enough or there's things you need to learn, but because of the RNG. RNG for resources and RNG for Main gun upgrades. There are times when you cannot build anything new or research anything for a good 5-10 missions because the choice of missions you get can randomly just not provide you with the resources you need.It's probably the most polished game I've ever played, and encountered only one bug in my entire play through (2 enemies got stuck below a cliff and it took me a good 10 minutes to get a luck bomb shot on them to end the mission).Originally I stated  that "Other than that, the developer has made some alterations and listened so far to player feedback." However, the dev has only done one balance update. It has a long way to go yet to be balanced.Let's see where the developer takes it. If there's been no content update for a couple of months, I'll change my review to a negative, because as lovely as the game is, at the price it's at now it feels like a cash and grab.

_childDocuments_.review: Good Things About Taur: Taur has such a clean and satisfying visual, control, and audio. This game to me is more of a way to relax myself by blowing up enemies with style. With the large arsenal of buildings and turrets to choose from, I really like the way we can customize our base defense load-out to the way we please. Very satisfying to play.___Down-Side for Taur:[Gameplay] When I won the campaign and transition into post-game situation, I felt that there was no incentive to keep on playing. The rounds felt repetitive, and there was nothing to use the large stockpile of resources for.[Weapons] Some weapons felt overly under powered.- The Shotgun's long cooldown and low mag-size made is very very weak and I felt that it was the most useless weapon in the game (even for defending hoard at close range, it lacks damage).- The starting cannon was fairly weak, lacking the damage to pick off units later in the stage.- The Lock-On missile weapon felt extremely unpractical since everyone would just use the Mini-gun to deal with Air-Raid, the Siege's transport aircraft AND the Boss. There was no middle-ground tanky enough enemy aircraft to really use this weapon on.___Comments & Suggestions:The game felt like there's only 'weak' enemy and 'hardcore' enemy. Both the infantry and tank (siege rounds) are fairly "weak", but then all of the sudden we run into the Boss, which was "extreme," power wise. The enemy aircraft were so-so but still weak.- Add Mini Boss (Each for enemy Infantry, Tanks, Aircraft)  - [] Less enemy, but make them strongerThe game felt like it need a little more upgrade option or even "special upgrade" for the Buildings and Units.- More Upgrades for Everything! (Ex: Units attack faster, Building can rebuild 1/2/3 units etc.)- Special Upgrade for everything (very very expensive, but you can stack the upgrade) Ex: Turret (Raptor) fires additional arounds, Bombers drop larger bomb, etc.__Overall, very nice game with great potential, I would really like to see this game grow!

_childDocuments_.review: Taur is a tower defense game that initially appears very promising in the store, but unfortunately fails to live up to expectations. As many other reviews have pointed out, the game is rather average and lacks the excitement and innovation that other tower defense games offer.While the graphics and sound design are decent, the gameplay itself is lackluster and fails to engage the player in a meaningful way. The tower defense mechanics are standard and the game lacks the strategic depth and variety that players might expect.Overall, I can only recommend Taur to those who are able to purchase it on a steep discount. There are many other tower defense games out there that offer a more satisfying experience, and players may want to consider those instead.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great start but lacks replayability. Pick it up on sale or wait for some updates.Taur is a sleek looking tower defense game with some nice twists to the genre. Your base travels with you between maps so upgrades stay and get stronger the further you are into the campaign. Another intersting twist is the top down shooter element of the one tower the player controls. The UI is well designed, simple, and intuitive. I ignored 90% of the tutorial messages outside of the three main control buttons, space, tab, and shift. Or at least I tried to because the damn messages kept popping back up even after marking as read. Sound is simple but it does the job.The technology tree is at the same time robust and lacking in depth. There's a lot of options standard to tower defense from ground and air units, to turrets, and global powers. There's a nice variety and for about half of that, there's some depth with upgrades from adding more units spawning for ground units to a global power up specific for the rangers. The global power ups have upgrades ranging from longer duration, shorter cooldown, to stronger power effect. The weapon upgrades range from faster reload to armor piercing and extra magazine sizes. It's enough to make the upgrades feel impactful. And then there's the tower upgrades and air units. Health upgrades. That. is. it. It's boring, and uneventful. Does it make a difference? Sure, sometimes, maybe, I guess? You certainly don't feel it as much as a frickin extra shot of pew pew or extra units spawning.The core gameplay loop is interesting enough. Pick a map based on what resources you need/how difficult of a mission you can handle, build towers, kill stuff till waves end, get rewards, spend on tech tree/towers, repeat. Simple, and quite enjoyable. The game is setup -almost- akin to a rogue-like. But it's not and it makes all the sad pandas. If there were commanders/units/upgrades/mutator unlocks for each run it would make Taur much more enjoyable for multiple playthroughs. As it stands now, it's a 'figure it out and beat it once' type of game. One and done for the most part. Sad pands.What's there is a great start. It's so close to being great but falls a short with lack of modes for replayability. I hope the dev adds that little extra because the core is fun.As it is now, I cannot recommend picking it up unless it's on a hefty sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Important details that may not be obvious: This is a snowball game. You play it in series of battles with an overall tug of war score with the enemy. If you win the bar moves in your favor and vice versa. Once you complete a battle you get some resources. Those resources are used for BOTH researching things available to build IN BATTLE and for the stuff you build in battle. So you shoot your wad on research, you can't build. You don't research, you don't have anything to build. The PROBLEM is if you lose something in a battle, it's gone. You have to spend the same resources to build again next battle. If you don't lose it, its just there next battle. Again, snowball: Once you start losing, you basically can't recover. In my view that is the game's main flaw. You have learn by repeated failure (not even on the harder difficulties) what kinds of things you need to prioritize early. Even then, RNG may screw you b/c you don't get enough of the right kind of resources after a battle. In short its one of those games that LOOKS like you have lot's of paths to victory, but in fact, you need to 'crack the code' and figure out the 'right way' to spend resources or you will invest time and choices in a run that starts failing and you may as well quit... because now you don't get as much from each battle which means the levels get harder but you are spending everything on rebuilding to where you were when you lost at an easier level. The problem is, the game is designed as if you can take a loss, make changes and recover. But because resources are shared with research and building AND buildings lost have to be rebuilt, it is more than brutal when you lose one battle. Game mechanics don't match gameplay design.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, what a fun tower defense! I am very glad I waited so long to play this because I feel that the Rebels and Sentinels are an essential part of the gameplay. I think this would've been way more boring without them.I am honestly so tired of maze-builder/path TDs. They haven't really evolved in the decade or so that they've been around. This game dumps mazes altogether in favor of a central base approach. As a TD vet, this is like a nightmare scenario for building defenses. Having to cover 360 degrees is a worst case scenario, but in Taur, it's handled impeccably. It makes you feel like the leader of Future Sparta as you and your drone warriors, mercs, capital ships, and towers hold off endless onslaughts of space Persians. The gameplay never feels stale and the strategy was not immediately apparent to me on my first playthrough, which ended up making me lose my first run on Hard by like day 30. I won my second playthrough by day 75. The final boss was super uniquely challenging and I almost had it the first time, I absolutely massacred it the second. I think beating this by day 50 is the true testament to your strategy, so aim to do that.I highly recommend Taur. It's easily one of the best TDs out there. It's super simple and extremely deep, doesn't try to do too much but also doesn't do too little, is perfectly challenging, and extremely engaging the entire time. 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun only for an exceedingly short time, and largely only a single playthrough. The early game is arduous and utterly dismal, requiring an excessive amount of time plinking away at individual enemy infantry units with POS pop guns, with no variety at all possible since there's no option except pushing out Guardian bots and going for the Aegis shield, which will, if you know to beeline it, probably only be possible AFTER the first mandatory Siege mission that is pretty much guaranteed to kill you.It can be fun to get it going and build a tower that can win for the first time, but after that it's pointless because most of the towers are of little value. The entire aerial tree is pointless because attack planes are slow to reposition and not even particularly effective. Just get guns. The SAM weapons are pointless because they're not doing anything guns can't do. Just get guns. Guardians are not optional, must have 100. No other bot variety or strategy, spend four slots on Rangers if you really want. Then just get guns. And getting the guns? Small towers.....just get plasma to attack ground and air. Chimera and Cryo towers have no particularly increased efficacy for their limitations, and the former reload one every ice age. Just get plasma. Missile interceptors? Dead stuff doesn't shoot. Just get plasma. Large towers? SAM is inefficient, you can't waste space on specialist air-only weapons that aren't really that much more effective. Just get Tri-Barrel plasma. Massive towers? There's so many enemies on screen that weapons need to be able to switch to new targets and maintain fire.....so just get minigun plasma.This is an action-strategy game that gives you a frustratingly ineffective big gun for the action, which makes the action boring for a long, long time (also serving as an early game trap...waste resources upgrading it, and you'll die), and the strategy is so poorly balanced that it's effectively a linear puzzle game of working out what your initial steps need to be until you get 60-90 minutes in and can possibly consider different ways in which to gimp yourself by deviating from Maximum Gun. And when your strategy works the action is still boring, since you may finally have been able to upgrade and reforge your weapon to be.....kinda meh. It's another stream of lights in the lightshow of melting enemies. I guess you get to press the 'big missile' button now and then.11 hours.....I'm done. Uninstalling it. The game just annoys me with its deceptive linearity crushing all strategy, and the earlier periods of the game where you have to lean on the action side of things is horrendously boring because your gun isn't any kind of efficacious or spectacular. It's a pretty game that looks good when your favourite YouTuber plays it, but is just irritating and rote when actually played for yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: I was disappointed.  I like to know what the objectives of the game are, and what weapons my side has.  Then we get on with the game instead of trying to figure out how the game should be played. Only the very basic steps are explained, the rest is for you to figure out wasting time when you could be making progress at getting further in the game while actually doing battle.  Another aspect is that it appears to be a very simple game.  You just keep fighting with the same "grand cannon" or whatever they call it.   It's not that there is no strategy, it just isn't intuitive and interesting because you don't know how to build you capabilities and what they are.  Sound confusing?  It is.  I have played thousands of hours of games from Steam, and most of them were tower defense game.  This one is not close to the best.  That's just me.  someone else may like it more, but I can't recommend it to tower defense fans.For those who are still thinking of buying it - The game has a tower that is placed on the map for you.  Various enemies come towards it to destroy it.  You control a cannon of increasing sophistication that will destroy the enemies in a point and shoot confrontation.  If you kill all of them before your tower is destroyed, you win, and go to the next map.  Otherwise you are set back.  A score is kept.  If setbacks are too many you are defeated.  That's about it.

_childDocuments_.review: Once you get the basic tactics down, there's basically very little to do. They've not handled player power creep well enough, and it turns into a never ending grind for resources. If you fail the ending boss, which is basically inevitable the first time, you're forced to do another 25 matches (minimum 5+minutes each), till you get another chance. Fail again, another 25 matches. Make a single tactical error in the boss fight, be forced to play for 250-500 more minutes -- 2 to 4 hours to get another run at the boss because you clicked the wrong button, or hadn't laid your towers out *perfectly* ahead of the boss fight. The basic mechanics are fine, but it truly does turn into a grindfest in the endgame. Do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: There are entertaining aspects, but there are a few bugs. For starters, a cursor bug, where the system cursor is not deactivated when first launching the game. To fix this, the only thing that works is changing the resolution of the game. No other settings seemed to help. Once you see the cursor disappear, change the res back to whatever. The other bug is that the game does not clean-exit. If you get a crash or an ALT+F4 you will still need to open task manager and kill the window. Then there is a massive balance issue. For starters, a handful of missions have you with basically nothing, and a mammoth tower flies in within 3 feet of your main tower and effectively two-shots it in about 5 seconds. Nothing you can do but die. Then you have the issue where missions "expecting light resistance" are zerg fests, over and over I got swarmed and wiped out on light missions, even while maxing out upgrades, resistance forces, etc. 3 runs in a row I ran into the same kind of balance issues. Getting destroyed by the first unit on the 3rd mission is rage-inducing. IF this game is designed to troll the player into wanting to stop playing the game entirely within a few hours of play, mission accomplished. I'm going to give this a few days for a balance update... but if it doesn't improve, I'm probably going to ask for a refund. I want to love this game. I like so much about it, but the balance issue makes it less of a skill issue, and more of a luck of the draw issue. If I'm SUPER lucky the first couple of towers I place will be on the side the mammoth drops in on. But even then, it's got so much armor, literally just tanks anything I can do with a day 5 or 10 tower. I was super lucky my first run, made it to day 40 but this kept happening. Even with rebel forces, spending all currencies to max out as much research as I could, upgrading main cannon, etc. Nothing helped.  Feelsbad man.

_childDocuments_.review: An arcade tower-shooter with fantastic low-poly aesthetics. Not a tower defense. Research technologies and improve weapons in planet view, and then deploy to farm materials.Build assisting towers for infantry of sorts, shields, cannons or even fighter / gunship / bomber hangars which are autonomous like everything else than your main cannon.Efficiency requires pin-point accuracy shooting, not a problem for me. Rinse and repeat. _childDocuments_.review: + Graphics are v. good - clean, colourful (but not garish) voxel style+ Audio effects are nice+ The central cannon is always under your manual control, which is a nice way of letting you prioritise certain enemies and gives you something to do- Can't remap any controls- The mouse feels very floaty and/or sluggish- No markers for spawned enemies that are off-screen- The game isn't especially clear about why you can't build certain turrets that you've just researched (it's because they fit on a larger hex (which you can't unlock because it takes a different kind of resource (which the research screen doesn't tell you about)))- The central cannon can't be set to Automatic, so you HAVE to always use it. _childDocuments_.review: * Game's controls are not very good. The manual aiming for your prime weapon clashes with the weird 3D environment & makes it difficult to aim for what you're actually trying to aim for.* You start off INCREDIBLY weak; all you have is a primary and secondary prime weapon, and both are TERRIBLE. Your primary gun has only 3 shots before it takes its sweet time to reload, and since you'll be missing a lot (see above) this is super frustrating. And your secondary gun is a mortar that takes FOREVER to get to its destination, rendering it almost entirely useless.* The early battles are balanced against you having virtually no offense, but this just means they're incredibly boring. Very few enemies that take forever to get to you.* In order to build ANYTHING in this game, you have to spend resources to research it, THEN spend resources to unlock the building slot for it, THEN spend resources to build the structure for it! Which means you won't be building much of anything. (On top of this, there are multiple different types of resources, so often times you just don't have the RIGHT kind of power core or whatever to get what you need. It feels very artificial, subtracting from gameplay as opposed to adding to gameplay.)There's more I'm probably forgetting; the game just got a new update that added some new mechanics, but they are explained even more poorly than some of the base game mechanics, and they seem complicated for the sake of being complicated.Overall, this game has some interesting ideas it fumbles horribly; the result is it misses the spirit of what makes tower defense-style games fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The trailer makes the game look like a super fun laser flinging power trip and I was super hyped to blast waves upon waves of enemies! _childDocuments_.review: This game can be immensely fun at first. The tutorial is short and easy; and the tech tree is fairly intuitive, though it takes a few hours to be able to explore enough to find out what is effective or not. However, the biggest issue is the mismatch between the expected forces of "light", "medium", "heavy", "massive", or "extreme" and what you actually get. I had FAR too many "light" or "medium" battles with two massive airships dropping dozens of infantry each and completely overwhleming my reasonably formidable defenses. This forces a reset on your defenses and you never really manage to recover, making the game effectively unbeatable outside of RNGesus. Without the player agency that is critical to the strategy game genre, I give this game a whopping 2.5/10. If you could actually predict the opposition and make your choice of battle meaningful, I'd give this game a 7/10. However, some flaws are just too influential to play around.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not buy this game. Do not get suckered in by the visuals and sound design, and it's promises of “strategy” lest you end up like me; horribly disappointed by the actual gameplay. There are two key design issues with the game that make it more frustrating than anything else, the aiming system and randomness-as-padding.The aiming system is unforgivable. Your turret aims aims at the cursor in only the vaguest definition of the word. Because of the game's visuals and terrain depth, this means that your turret aims at where it thinks the cursor is. This means that any weapon with travel time are only barely useful against ground units, as aiming against air units causes your aim to snap to the supposed ground instead. If you are familiar with UE4's innate issues with third-person based camera aiming, this is a classic example of it. In addition, you can't rotate your view for a better perspective and firing angle. In addition, since your main gun itself is the tallest object in the game, you can't see anything at all “behind” your turret once you start building. You best hope nothing important is back there. To make the aiming system worse, your two basic weapons, the ones you will be using the most, have innate spread. This means that when you absolutely need to hit a target, you're now fighting the terrain, aiming system, and randomness at the same time. If there is a ranged enemy unit next to a cliff, you simply can't hit it; your reticule won't move the right position, and your artillery shots have too much spread to reliably hit it anyway.To make the aiming system even worse, you have to reload your weapon after a period of time, and that environmental objects like trees will always block at least one shot. Seeing how it takes you a few seconds to reload, you have weapon spread, and you have to wiggle your aim around terrain, this becomes unbelievably frustrating and unrewarding very quickly. If you want to take the game “seriously” and still have the tactical advantage, you're forced to rush to a beam weapon so you can carve down the landscape for better firing angles. The rest of the tech tree doesn't matter.As for the actual gameplay loop, I couldn't care to play any more than a few levels. There is no content other than the same few maps, with different spawn points and different enemy compositions. Since all missions are randomly generated, there's no pacing, no unique challenges. Picking missions is a matter of juggling numbers for what you want in upgrades and such. The enemy composition is very slow to mix it up. Somehow, this approach makes the content feel thinner than most other Early Access Roguelikes out there. There's a boss fight in here somewhere, but after 20 missions of the same drab gameplay, I couldn't care less.The AI of your turrets and deployables is questionable. Aircraft will crash into trees and rocks and destroy themselves, your defender bots will line up on the wrong side of your base because they operate off of net distance rather than actual travel distance, and so on. Turrets aim somewhere, but are so small in comparison that its hard to see their impact and whether you made the right purchase.The worst part is that I don't see a way to salvage this game, without drastic changes to how the game works. Don't buy this game at all, not even on sale. It's a aesthetically pleasing, but mechanically vapid game.  There's other better tower defense games like X-Morph that deserve your time more.

_childDocuments_.review: wanted to like this so much, the core idea and aesthetic are really cool, but there are three massive fundamental issues with this in my view, that are really making me want to chuck this and never play again:Aiming/power of primary weapon; Aiming your prime cannon is awful - projectiles do not go where you aim them, and given point 2 below, this is a massive issue. even on easy difficulties, the most basic enemy take nearly a full magazine to kill, which makes for incredibly unsatisfying game-play when you empty a full clip into the weakest enemy in the game, and they dont die... This goes for your secondary mortar weapon aswell, you get a nice bunch of enemys, hit them with the mortar, and it barely effects them...Not tower defence; your turrets and units are very weak and even when upgraded, die very easily and barely deal with a single enemy unit. WHICH WOULD BE FINE, if you were able to deal with lots of enemy's yourself, but the aim and power off your primary weapons are terrible! What is the game trying to be?? if  the turrets and units were abit more effective, it would help compensate for the weakness of your primary weapon, but currently both are ♥♥♥♥...difficulty curve: Not sure if its intentionally very difficult, or just poorly thought through, but the game throws waves at enemy's at you very early on that you have no hope of defeating given the weakness of your weapons. I had a boss tank that killed my tower with a  single shot at level 7 or something silly.... What makes this worse, is when you loose your towers / units (which you will as even upgraded they are very weak) they're lost forever, along with the resource investment it took to build!  so once you loose once, you might aswell give up and start again.Very frustrating as this has the potential to be a fantastic game, but currently the core gameplay/fun proposition is broken, as its a bad 'shooter', with awful aim and unsatisfying/untactful player controlled shooting, but also a bad tower defence, with turrets and units that are very weak and cant be relied upon for anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Im not gonna lie, after over 100 hours on this game, i would give it a 9.5/10. Reason being: 1. It can run on pretty much anything unless your playing on a pc with a RTX negative 650 (This is cause ive brought my old ahh laptop to lots of places and played this game a ton) 2. This game is also REALLY fun. I love gunning down hundreds of tanks, special units, and grunts all in one battle. 3. The graphics and designs are really good for a game of this caliber, its somewhat calming in way. From red and blue lasers flying across my screen, to enemy designs, to your little guardians getting massacred by Praetorians and brutes. Its just cool.4. Its easy to pull up, play, and leave after a little while, i have also had this game up for 26 hours at the time of this review, no issues after coming back. Also doesnt close automatically which is a big plus.5. The only reason this game is 9.5 and not 10/10 is because of its price. Personally, i think its a tad bit high while not on sale. However, i do think that with my current knowledge of the game, and having played it for so long, i think it is worth this price. For what it gives, (See points above) i think its a 25 dollar game. "Cons"These are not really cons, just stuff that isnt added that i would like to see :thumbsup:1. We need more variations of pretty much everything. More types of tauron units, more enemies (There are plenty right now, but still) I would love to see more bosses, more types of "mini" ones. Such as a tank like the paladin, give it all the max upgrades of the paladin, then you have the perfect boss.  2. I would love to see more towers. One i could think of would be a base repair station, that deploys drones 24/7, like the ability, but less powerful. Another would be more types of offensive towers, more basic turrets. Such as an autocannon, a turret firing a high caliber round in quick succession. A minigun turret, that has LOTS of ammo and shoots REALLY fast. 3. More tauron bosses (Paladin and avenger, i forgot what the type was called)TL:DR This game is really good, lots of content, a fairly good campaign, good progression, and a decent price. If i knew what i would be in for while playing this game, i would definitely buy this game at its full price.

_childDocuments_.review: I got about 8 hours worth of fun out of this. If you like Tower Defense games I think this is well worth $10 or less. At full price I'm not sure if it's worth it, compared to other TD games. The game doesn't live up to it's full potential, unfortunately. The bones are here, it gets a lot of things right, just doesn't go quite far enough.The gameplay loop is simple you - just play mission after mission trying to gather resources to advance a tech tree and try to power yourself up. Your base and setup persists through missions, which feels good until it doesn't. Once you find out what works there isn't much reason to deviate your build throughout your run. I won't spoil it here, because figuring out how the Units and Towers interact is basically the entire game. You can't easily rework your build to react to the level or what's going on. Which means that level you're on and mission type are essentially meaningless. It turns the game into a resource grind to advance the tech tree, which is less than it could be. Once maxed out the towers I cared about using, i don't really feel the need to play through it again. It feels like you're playing a fun mode that was tacked on to a better game.

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game, I enjoyed it quite a lot. I'll do a pro/con list:PROS-Great graphics-Many units and upgrades giving you the option to complement troops with main gun, 23 hours in and I am still missing tech-Gorgeous animations and battles - troops engaging in melee have very fluid motions, each shot feels meaty(except for laser but that is a given cos... laser)-Intense battles, not a TD where you can just rest on one arm and play with the other. Heavy and massive battles require you to be able to use abilities, change weapons, replenish lost units/tower. Trying to snipe bombers, suiciders or other bigger threats covered by swarms of other enemies is tense.CONS-lackluster interface in certain sections - took me quite a while to realise when I actually have reinforcements in the battle. And very often I would take troops that should have rested to heal. Maybe mercs/supertroops selection could be done prior in a separate screen prior to the battle. -no TwinTaur to enjoy the mayhem with a friend. I'm certain it could be done. -A big one for me - most weapons feel like they need to many upgrades to become useful. I often try to use the best weapon for a scenario - blobs - select cannon/shotgun/minigun/mortar/rocket, Air? switch to cannon/AAmissiles, huge elite - go cannon/laser and rocket. Thing is, you can do just fine in most situations with the default cannon, especially after a few upgrades. The mortar can be easily replaced by the heavy rocket, only situation where it is better to have it is on mountain maps to overcome cover. It feels like the animation to switch a weapon is too long, sometimes as long as the reload time for the main cannon so it doesn't feel worth it. Or just make it that the reload occurs in the background while the weapons if offline (it won't reload unless selected, and for some weapons is it quite a while). Switching to a new weapon only to find it is not reloaded seems like a huge miss for me. Couldn't there be tiny robots in the Taur to do a reload?- No mech super unit - I mean, eye candy speaking, the only thing missing is a mecha slugging it with another in melee while pushin all nearby units to the side so the big boys can play.
