_childDocuments_.review: tbh I had more frustration than fun with this game (+constant crashes). But if you consider "catching your attention long enough to finish the game" as a positive thing, then I'd recommend.I was able to beat boss on day 50 on normal. Just spam Time Warp and use upgraded Punisher + Cleaver. I didn't even have 12 slots filled yet. Instead rushed Striker x5, which gave ranged damage boost. "Predicting" my inevitable defeat, I didn't even use my Colonel Rebel Specialists (good idea to include 1 Scout with Expose Weakness tech). Turns out you can easily kill the boss before he hides behind his shield (during the first phase).I also used 2 Interceptors in hopes that they will reduce his movement speed (-50%). Didn't feel like it had any effect. Probably another terribly designed part of the game (there are a lot), with scripted movement of the boss.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Great take on tower defense. Very addictive and challenging. Just when you think you have your taur perfectly set up you hit a new level and new enemies that decimate your turrets. This continually changing environment provides the right learning curve while maintaining the challenge throughout the levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Well if you are looking for a a good game loop with "1 more mission" u got the right game. I started 3 loops - all on hard - and everytime i learned more about the game. I want to beat it and it has a good feedback loop.ConsThe tech tree is not really balanced. You have to learn what you really need for a successful run.The game sometimes dont close and tab out of the game is buggy.You will see your game cursor and your windows cursor wich kind of sucks but i got used to it really fast.I give a 8/10 if u like rts tower defense like games. Worth the 20 bucks imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, the mechanics work well and the graphics are also very well executed, difficulty is fair but you finished it in 6 hours and unless you like starting over fresh and doing it all again you won't get more then 10 hours of gameplay out of it really. Still, good game just could have used some more "story line" type of content to keep it engaging maybe for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: As it turns out, I don't want to sit through hours of boring early game in which no strategy is required (or allowed, all you can really do is place a couple starter towers) in order to get to the more interesting features of a game.  Please make your next game with the understanding that the early portion of a game should include a hook to secure player interest, and not just a dry lecture on the basics of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the campaign in 100 rounds which took about 12 hours. I'm sure if you're really into tower defense games or play really tactically you could beat it faster. I just loaded it up and started playing. The graphics are surprisingly good and when you start being able to intervene less and less and automate defenses more and more it's a lot of fun to watch the chaos ensure.Only downside is that it took about 15 minutes worth of playing with the resolution to get the double cursor problem to go away. Once it was gone though it didn't come back. Overall, I give the game a 7/10. Satisfying graphics, runs very well, and is easy to pick up and just play. Negatives are that once you're done you just play until infinity or start a new campaign, and I find the camera a little bit wonky.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: It is a Very Good Tower Defense game. It has the right amount of Micro Management with the 'Prime' cannon. The Towers dont disappoint outright like other TDs. As you unlock more Tech, the game gets progressively more difficult. The Concept of gathering different resources is interesting, however could be more rewarding once you get into the later waves (Day 20+). Bringing your previous wave's towers with you to the next wave is a nice idea. The tech tree is...a little confusing as first, but not overbearing. All in all, 8.5/10 could use some polishing, maybe some different modes. Price is a lil much for the 10-20+ hours you will likely get out of it. But if you like Tower Defense games, add it to your wishlist and pick it up on sale around $15-$20
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those "just one more turn and then I'll go back to something productive" game where you end up spending an extra hour without realising it. It's a fairly challenging and very interesting tower defence game with a wide selection of enemy and friendly units. At first the battles might seem a bit stale, but once you reach the 30 days mark your screen will light up with projectiles and explosions. Surprisingly, it doesn't make the game slow down one bit. In fact, the entire game seems to be bug free. If you are a fan of the genre, I highly recommend Taur. It might be a bit pricey though so I would recommend to buy it on sales.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: An engaging,but difficult,game. Taur is not for the easily frustrated. Did I mention it becomes more difficult...rapidly. You will find yourself focusing the turret fire on some incoming badies,but one or two have already made your inner perimeterand are thrashing your rebel troops to bits.  another scenario,bad guys are incoming in groups and you start to engage them,but here comes a couple of support aircraft and you are forced to focus fire on them alone. 'Well',you think,'my guys will be okay,they have some firepower.' And,they _did_ have firepower. But now half of them are dead,and you realize you were expected to multitask wildly,somehow supporting your guys while switching to air-attack mode and back with your turret(then _waiting_ for that gun to reload...).  Did I mention it might be frustrating?  Overall,a nice looking game for the dogged tactician with good shooting skills. You'll be plugging-away at this one for awhile.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been very fun and the visuals are fantastic. On the other hand, the game was pretty short and now that I've completed normal mode I can either restart or play the endless mode and try to min/max my setup, neither of those options is currently appealing to me so I will return if more is added.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: I really started to enjoy this after I got used to the unresponsive controls but once you hit day 20 the difficulty just spikes and you have no chance of beating levels that have even medium enemy forces. You're just not given the time or resources to build up before it starts hammering you. Made worse by the condescending message if you lose.This is on the easiest difficulty too. Add that to the fact your aiming cursor is white and is near impossible to see on the snow levels and the tendency for enemies to hide behind your tower so you can't see them really makes for some frustrating moments, Another thing is it gives you a choice of missions but if you don't pick a particular one then the enemy will just take a huge chunk of control, so whats the point in being given the option? It's far too unforgiving to be enjoyable. There's a good game in here but stupid difficulty spikes have spoiled to for me. Waste of my money.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This game is certainly weird. In a good way.On one hand, the game implements some great mechanics, is epic, has great music and decent visuals. On the other hand, optimisation is still terrible as lowering the graphic settings does not change anything absolutely. As such, the game requires a significantly better graphics card (and CPU) than what is stated in the System Requirements.Update 1.4 was great, loved it! Keep it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Tower defense. You play as the center tower that enemies want to approach and destroy. From an overhead perspective, click on any spot around the map to send a laser bolt to that location. Build automatic turrets in a tight cluster around you to help deal with waves of enemies. It's fun to spend your rewards from each round on a variety of smaller towers and their upgrades. The game is stable and controls well, even with a screen full of hundreds of enemies and high speed laser bolts. Amusing and captivating.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This review will hinge on the caveat that you will like the never ending mode after the main story. TLDR:The game is quite straight forward, it is a tower defence game with shooter mechanics. There are several very interesting tech options that in my opinion gets pushed back because of the lack of a longer story line. And there are strategic choices regarding resources and trade that can make you think deeper about your future plans and game play. The main issue here for my personally is that the story and campaign is quite underwhelming in the sense that you only get the actual game play. Obviously this is a good part of the game that could have been enriched by some sort of storytelling and buildup towards the boss. Yes, boss, there is only one. It shows up at day 50 and then you die, unless you are strategically clever and lucky... which then means the game is over. If not then it will come back at wave 75 and then you will very much win against it. Abruptly you are presented with a message that you are now going into the "never ending" part of the game, which quite frankly is a very disappointing way to end a game with an interesting introduction. Minimalistic is not the word here... lazy is. The tech! The lovely tech that you will never get to enjoy through a story driven campaign  is never finished. The many guns, rebels and super units are never done unless you just... keep playing. But this is what is so very unsatisfying with this game. The game play as previously mentioned is straightforward and easy. Perhaps you will die a couple of times, but the strategy is quite easy if you want to beat the game early... Focus on the basics first, get towers and units out on the map with ranged focus first, and then just get the bigger towers when you get the resources... there you go. Throw in a little skill with the gun you use and presto you are a winner. What i would have liked to see, as you can probably guess, is that there needs to be an actual story... more bosses that encourages you to actually play the game more. The last update of this game was great, or it would have been, had it not given you something that would have made sense IF... you guessed it, built upon the story further! So there you go, if you like the "never ending" aspect, then go right ahead, if not... this is a very short game frankly.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: I went back and forth on how I felt about this game. The very beginning is very boring as you are just plinking away with a cannon but as your base begins the game gets very fun. It then turns into a grind again for most of the end part of the game where you are just running through missions for resources.The style is really striking to look at and it was a fun take on a tower defense base builder so I am giving it a thumbs up despite some major problems mostly in the RNG area. Mission difficulty is all over the place. The ratings on enemy difficulty make no sense as you can breeze through Massive or Extreme missions and then get absolutely clobbered on a Medium wave, especially on harder difficulties. The weapon upgrades were also too risky to be an enjoyable experience since you might just downgrade your weapon and get unlucky enough to get a decent one again with the resources available. Also, some of the prime weapons are just objectively the right choice. The beam weapon was basically worthless, the primary gun and the shotgun are the correct decision for almost every enemy and encounter which really added to the tediousness of the game. All in all I enjoyed it but doubt I will be coming back to it much, would recommend on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This by far has been one of the best active tower defense games I have ever played. The game to me is perfectly balanced and for me at least i really took the time to consider my upgrades and strategy for each battle to the point my time spent between battles considering my strategy far out lasted the time in battles themselves later in the game. I highly recommend this game as after you beat the mission you can continue in an infinite war mode, up the difficulty and start again or even play a mode that you will most likely never win but you can try to actively beat your previous best days survived.Update: I have beaten the game in Normal and Hard Difficulty
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This is quite possibly the most underated game evermhmHOWEVER there is a lack of content that i would say as a person who has completed the game 5 times is kinda boring at times that some may say is not worth 25$ and i agree its a bit much but the devs are trying their best and i want this game to be updated so just wait for a year or so
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Super fun little game. Don´t think I would spent hundreds of hours with it. But 10-20 sounds like a really good time :) Love the visual style, the different types of buildings and units are fun and just looking at the chaos on screen praying that in the end your main tower will still stand ... awesome :)
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah , it's a good and fun game. Very casual while offering a decent array of strategy, although kinda lacking in that respect (you don't need to do anything fancy to win on Hard , on Normal it's dead easy). It is pretty original for a TD , so I would highly recommend it for strategy players looking for something casual.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: There's a learning curve, and the difficulty spikes in a specific way at a specific point during campaign meaning you have to have certain buildings and researches at that point. Builds are a lot less flexible than you would expect. That said the core gameplay is very fun, and once you hit a certain point you can fiddle around with your setup more. There's not much replay value sadly. Overall I'd say grab it since $25 isn't a lot and you get your money's worth, be be aware there's a few shortcomings.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun good system of progression great visuals large scale battles top tier tower defense game. My only issue is that after completing the main story line there isn't another chance to fight the big boss unless you restart. putting in an escalating boss mission would add some much needed replay-ability. But thats just my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: While the Tower Defense Style and all the different Upgrades are fun, this game is short, buggy and unbalanced.I finished it within 8h, having seen everything this game has to offer after 4.And while there are rarely any game-breaking glitches or bugs, i had often that enemies fell below the geometry (only to be hit by splash damage at this point), destroyed buildings not refunding the ressources and once where the last enemy/last wave not spawning at all. The difficulty is entirely arbitrary with air-strikes being laughable easy (even if the enemy is sending a massive force) vs the chaotic drop of enemies which will overrun you quickly, even if you only expect a "light force" Some game-mechanics are just plain weird. As example the game lets you upgrade your main weapon ("Reforging") up to lv 10 which extends the possible damage the specific weapon, but will also randomly pick the actual damage from the damage-range. If you're unlucky, the cannon becomes very weak. Reforging on high levels is also one of the most expensive things to do. And why can't i change my base-setup outside of battle? This game focuses quite heavily on strategic placement of your towers, yet i have no time to carefully plan my build as on the battleground the time will only be slowed down in build mode. Explosions looks great though.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game. Started with Hard difficulty for my first play-through and finished it in under 6 hours on stream. Then i moved to playing brutal for the challenge. Brutal complete in 7 hrs. Doing Day 100+ as a bit of fun until i decide to restart and do it all over again. I like tower defence games like this. I did read some of the other reviews, but a lot of changes have come to the game. I can recommend this game to those who like tower defence.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Taur is an interesting take on Tower Defense.  I think it's more of an RTS even than Tower Defense, because of how plays out and it is a lot of fun.  It has a pretty in-depth research tree, and a lot of configuration options as well as troop management, etc.  I dont have a lot of time into it, but I'm sure I'm going to rack hours on this until I beat it.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very fun and unique game. I wouldn't yet call it a gem yet, and development is slow, but oh is it worth it. With each update the Developer brings forth grand things. They are always quality and bring tons of fun into the game. So, if your into wave defense games, or futuristic warfare then this is a game I would highly recommend to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, it was a lot of fun and I enjoyed it enough to play it through all 3 difficulty levels to brutal. Got wiped in my first game but once I had the upgrade order figured out it was fine - and pretty addictive. I love TD in that it's such a relaxing time-wasting genre - like solving a little puzzle.Graphics and weapons are great and satisfying - particularly enjoyed the ballistic missile at the end of the weapon tree.Rebels and Giant tank / Airship also very cool additions - though they take a lot of resources to be useful.After 27 hrs - there's not much more to do which I thought was more than fair for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: The other reviews echo my view. It takes many days to get to a point the battles are ferocious, so stick with it because they end up very action packed. You will probably restart a couple times asbad purchases will price you out of winning. The battles get intense eventually and the sheer amount of different weapons is fun and lets you mix it up. My only grievance - no lengevity. Youll love it while getting there in the game and getting to the top. But once there, nowhere else to go, just fight win rinse repeat. needs a non campaign sandbox mode. let us players get stupid with it!
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Taur is a very good base defense game.Pros:   * Looks great. I really appreciate the spectacle of combat.   * Well paced and compelling gameplay loop   * Tons of meaningful upgrades to choose from   * Variety of build choices   * Normal mode is moderately challenging. I like that you don't lose everything after a defeat.   * The player-controlled weapons and short battles keep the combat engaging.   * Decent variety of maps.Cons:   * (Version 1.3) The late game can drag on. I almost beat the end boss on day 50, and it was took a couple of hours to get to wave 75 before I could face it again. (Version 1.31 update) I haven't replayed the campaign since the update, but this may have been addressed.   * A bit expensive for 8-10 hours of gameplay.(Version 1.3) One minor critique I have is that while the two superweapon vehicles are cool, even fully upgraded they feel overshadowed by the towers. Damage to the superweapons carries over between rounds. Superweapons only repair ~5-25% of their health for each round where you don't use them, and you need to purchase multiple levels of the repair upgrade to see any significant effect. As a result, the superweapons feel fragile. Instead of enjoying the destructive power that I invested so much resources into, I was mostly worried that they would take damage.(Version 1.31 Update) The superweapons received a huge buff. Base damage of their weapons increased by 100-300%. Prices of their upgrades were reduced. HP repair increased by 60-100%. I am very happy with the update and the dev's balance work.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Decent little game probably not worth the 24.99. It has very little content and is very easy. Once you you your tower and defense setup the game becomes pretty meaningless and after 75 days nothing has even come close to killing me. Need more difficulty options and more weapons choices, more of everything. Good start.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little tower defense kind of game, recent updates added some new flavor to the game but it is still just something you will play for a few hours and then be done until you come back to it.  Good for short segments as maps can be rather quick and it doesn't require significant amounts of time per play session.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Absolute blast to play this game. The game starts out slow but you eventually start getting more and more chaotic battles. The tech trees feel a bit overwhelming at first so it's best that you stick with upgrading stuff one at a time for a bit until you start getting resources more easily. The challenge is absolutely fair. I had to restart my campaign twice trying to get a feel for the game but third time was a charm and after 75 in game days the final boss was defeated. This is definitely something I can see playing on Twitch and is something I've always wanted in a Tower Defense game, you get to take part in the battle, you don't just place down towers and wait for enemies to die or wait in vain for the level to end when you figure out your towers aren't strong enough. Not 100% sure about the $20 USD price tag but if the devs keep adding stuff, I'd say that will be well deserved.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game, though i think for beginners, when you pass 30 days it gets a bit difficult, i think that more additions like for example barricades and a more simplified tech tree would be good, or an evolving tech tree, where in easy mode it's less to chose from, but the more difficult the gamemode is the more you can choose within the tech tree, i also think you should be able to build your tower setup from the tech tree screen.overall i do love the game with both pros and cons, and i recommend this game for thse who like this style of gameplay!
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This is a laid-back sort of game that's more about visual spectacle than engaging gameplay. Even on the hardest setting, you'll eventually get to a point where you don't really have to do anything during a battle other than hit a few buttons. That said, it is very cool to watch. There's a wealth of progression options to choose from over the course of the campaign and they all lead to different and satisfying ways of blowing apart the invading armies.My only gripe is that it gets a bit stale by the time you're done with your first campaign. The developer just added a massive update to the game which is a step in the right direction. I hope more content and balance changes will follow.tldr great cookie clicker game, give me more
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Great RTS tower defense hybrid, with the new update 1.3 the game is much better. Progression is satisfying, especially with creating rebel army platoons which you can upgrade and customise as there are around 5 different units to implement into the army platoons. You can also make a big investment into superunits which will take resources away from the many other sinks like the main upgrade tree and rebel army upgrade tree. The difficulty curve can be wibbly wobbly but it makes the game all the more fun. But it has been greatly improved and seems to get harder the better you are doing and easier in some ways when you take a big L. The developer is dedicated and has created a fantastic niche game.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game, wish it was replayable and had more variety. While the game itself if fun, its very repetitive by the end.  Each level is basically the same.  Either an all out air attack, all ground attack or a mix.  That's it.  There needs to be more variety. Upgrade interface is a mess. Overly complicated for no reason.  Same with the Forge feature (pointless) and main campaign screen, also pointless.  Once you figure it out, it's fine, just poorly designed.Resources are not balanced.  Some you'll have way too much of, other's you'll be empty the whole game.  Just makes it frustrating.  A resource exchange feature would be nice.Very little strategy because you have the same towers on every level.  You either overwhelm the attackers or they overwhelm you.  I played 101 levels, lost 6 maybe.You'll beat the game before upgrading everything or filling all tower slots.  That's the only reason to play after beating the game is to see what the other upgrades do and this'll provide about another 1-2 hours of gameplay.  A decent tower defense game with potential, so I'm recommending it.  Suggestions: 1) On the build interface screen add a counter for each tower so we know how many we have.  2) Add a build phase at the start of each level. Instead all towers in the middle, make the maps more unique and allow some towers to be placed in different locations of the map to add more strategy to the game.3) More boss levels, not just 1.  That was fun level.. Make a lot more boss levels. Every 10 levels or something would be great.  4) Resource exchange ability and the ability to sell your towers for some resources back.

_childDocuments_.review: Taur is a very fun game if you like the idea of "Base Defense," what I like to call it. It was semi-prominent in Flash Games, where you get a single point to defend yourself for increasingly large waves, with varying degrees of emphasis on your involvement or your preparation, i.e, what you can click on to make go boom, and what you buy to do it for you, and I think the fundamental gameplay here gets a very good balance in that regard...with some caveats.Let's start with the pros:1. You get a very large area to fight in, with a lot of enemies involved. If your system can handle it, and mine handles it fairly well, it's a spectacle to see and engage with. Waves start off small, and progressively get much larger. 2. The scale.. You really are taking on whole armies in this game, and your tower likewise outputs enough firepower to take that all on, and it's fun to make a defense which can survive these onslaughts, or even survive them with very minimal to almost no damage to your towers. It's very flashy and nice to witness occur on screen.3. The level of personal involvement. You get a prime tower, and multiple abilities to use in the middle of battle, with multiple weapons to switch between in the middle of the fight. In fact, you can even rearrange the towers in the middle of the fight to suit your needs (with the required resources, that is). I found that the level of involvement was very balanced, with both your involvement and the automated defenses pulling roughly their fair share of work at any given moment.4. The music. It's not the greatest, but it's quite nice to listen to. It's a bit of a shame it doesn't play during battles. No music offers its own benefits--the battles are quite crunchy--but perhaps the option to have music in the battles would have been nice.5. The campaign. Every day, you get a battle. You can choose from 3, and occasionally 2 or even 1, but almost always 3. Each one provides its own benefit in one area compared to another. One battle might let you occupy more ground, but not give you all the resources you necessarily want. Same for resources, some give out more resources than others. However, what type of battle it is may be different, along with the difficulty of the mission. You can go for the better resources, but slog through more enemies; better have a defense you know works. I like these kinds of decisions. Problems, and things that could be done better:1. All this stuff. there's so much stuff at some point that it's hard to know where I'm pointing, because the targeting reticle and laser-sight eventually is hard to see in the mess. And I'd find myself shooting at nothing, because I'd lose track amid the chaos. A more distinguishable targeting reticle would have been appreciated. Perhaps a choice to choose which color it is besides white, to help make it stick out. It also started causing some performance issues later on in the game, though not too much so.2. The flow of the campaign. At some point, it's just about picking the resources you don't have at the moment. By day 70, it didn't really matter if I picked one battle type over the other, though some were harder than others, even when some were more difficult and hard to manage than others, such as sky fall in the late game and air raid, which feature a ridiculous amount of enemies in a complete cluster-truck bum rush, with no rhyme or reason. These are, unfortunately, the weaker battles of the game, as there isn't as much creativity in the flow of battle or in on-the-fly decision making, like in the invasion battle type by comparison. In addition, there isn't really that much of a penalty for losing. The resources you spent you get back, and can just re-set up the tower using them, which you can do instantly by pressing R. Some harder penalties would make for more interesting decision-making, and really make it feel like you're taking a risk choosing the harder mission for your preferred resource type. More campaign battle variety would have also been nice. For example, the enemy sieges me, but what if I occasionally need to siege the enemy myself? That would have been a nice way to spice things up. Or, add in mission types solely with very, very large units, but in smaller quantities than the siege battles; titans to kill, requiring particular ways to optimally defeat them.3. Enemy variety. It starts off providing a variety of enemies. The first 20 days are the days with the most new enemies being introduced. It eventually tapers off by day 50, in which no new enemies are introduced. It would have been nice to see a greater variety of enemies, especially in ways to spice up how you use your weapons. As I found myself only really needing three out of the eight weapons by day 60 or so, even though all of them were meant to have their own strengths and weaknesses, it just didn't largely show because there weren't enough situations to really warrant using that weapon again. For example, the very last primary weapon is by far the best in terms of dealing with all of the missions that become available, and you'll only need 2 of the 4 secondary weapons by this time. But on the boss, I felt the need to use 5 of all the weapons, 3 primaries, 2 secondaries, to optimally beat the boss. Speaking of the boss, it'd be a much better game if there were more actual bosses.4. Lack of various modes. You get a campaign. And beating the boss awards you with, effectively, just more of the same game. I like that, as I can finish upgrading everything to be even more awesome. But it's not the best reward. Skirmish mode, or multiplayer, would both be good ways to increase the longevity of the game. Even more modes would be appreciated. As it stands, all that you have left is a higher difficulty, but it doesn't seem like that will really solve the fundamental problems present. And more enemies, at day 74, isn't really that hard to deal with, if nothing else is different, according to the menu-description.5. Some of the constraints. You get infantry units to defend your tower, but are limited in how many can be on the field. They are an integral part of your tower. I do somewhat understand, but because this game is quite keen to flood the screen with a ginormous amount of enemies, it would have been nice if I wasn't constrained to only 100 of my own infantry units. The ability to make air-towers spawn more air units than just 1 per tower, also would have been neat. 6. Variety in turret types. There's a total of 15 different tower types, across the three tower sizes. 10 normal sized, 3 large sized, 2 massive sized. While the present variety of turret types is nice, especially with the (mostly) free reign to plop down any arrangement of towers that you so please--if you want 50 artillery turrets, you can have 50 artillery turrets, though it probably won't last very long in an air raid--you can. This confers some replayability, but only so far. i would have liked either the ability to considerably modify the towers to do different things--branch off into variants with different strengths and weaknesses compared to other variants--or more tower types would spice up the game. For example, a tower that spawns vehicles to roam the battlefield, yes, even though air power also has full-range on the battlefield. Or an MLRS tower/tower variant.7. Editing your towers. You can only do this in the middle of the battle. A way to do so outsides of battle would have been a QOL feature. Editing on the fly can still be a thing, but this would remove some of the pressure of finding a setup knowing enemies are gonna be attacking in the next minute or so.I think this game is very nice. And I still feel like I have a lot left I can--and want--to do with the game. But there's a lot that can be done to really make it a *great* game.I would recommend getting this game on sale below 20 or 15 dollars.

_childDocuments_.review: Fun tower defence with some interesting strategic aspects.  Many of these can combine to make gameplay extremely frustrating at times e.g. not being able to plan ahead for types of enemy faced, not being able to reconfigure defences easily (sold resources not available until next mission) and the bottleneck on cores.Late game this can repeatedly force you into spiralling, unwinnable scenarios from which there is no recovery - you cannot attempt missions with the desired rewards due to enemy strength/abandonment costs, you are then unable to unlock/build the needed turret counters in subsequent missions, then you are unable survive long enough to get resources to recover, etcPros:- Pretty visuals and fun physics- Good map and unit variety- Huge tech treeCons:- Rapid difficult spike in midgame without matching rewards- Frequent post game crashes in later missions- Frustrating, overly punishing resource system- Limited replayability - Reforging RNG is garbageSuggestions:- Make tile unlocks cost only energy. The additional cost in cores means it's frustratingly common to be unable to place more turrets when needed due to the chronic resource constraints- Remove the one-sided negative stats on reforging. There is nothing fun about spending rare resources to get a strictly worse main weapon with nothing meaningful to compensates- Allow forecasting of enemies compositions for planning or refund at least cores immediately to allow some adaption instead of constantly being forced into missions constantly with sub-optimal setups on top of having to forgo ones with desired resource types (e.g. due to enemy army size and/or abandonment costs) - Make at least standard cores more plentiful and/or scale rewards to increase with mission difficulty

_childDocuments_.review: If you like playing tower defense games, but might be looking for something with a little twist to them, THIS IS IT! This game is one of the most unique tower defense games I've ever played and it's just as challenging, if not more challenging than regular tower defenses. Literally every single choice you make, everything you do, has to be tactical or you just might not make it in the long run. you have resources that you have to use wisely to aid you and you only get resources by completing rounds. You can only select 1 out of 3 rounds each wave, so choosing what resources you want to fight for poorly will surely see you to an early grave. The gameplay might be a bit repetitive, but the challenge that increases after every match due to increasing numbers of enemies and their strength, the harder the decisions get between what resources you want to fight for each wave and etc. almost completely eliminate the feeling of repetitivity. The games giant tech tree that allows you to unlock more buildings, weapons, turrets and etc. from said resources, that aid you in your defenses each round also, blow the reptitivity feeling out of the water because it always leaves you wondering what's going to happen next. I've only been playing normal mode for about 3+ hours now and just when I was starting to get the steamroller and reach critical mass with my defenses, the endgame boss rolls around and absolutely obliterates me because I was still unprepared with some of the poor tech decisions I made and now I'm set back planning again until I have the chance to fight him again. The end game boss is also NO joke, he'll rip you to pieces if you don't plan and play right.On the easiest difficulty, this game might be a pretty laid back/chill game to play, but if you want a tower defense challenge that will leave you in deep thought each round on what to do next, yea, this is the game. Highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: very good and fancy looking tower defense, but lacking in many very simple things.- you cannot see the current status of your base outside of missions and cannot edit it. so if you lose a turret and dont save up some ressources to rebuild it within a mission, you pretty much lose.- infinte mode doesnt scale. as soon as you beat the end boss, difficulty stays the same all the time. it only gets easier because you will have the chance to research and upgrade even more.- game offers many turrets, of which all but three are completely obsolete. simply the basic turret turrets (small, medium, big) will carry you through an infinite number of matches without the need to press any buttons besides "start mission". (and believe me there are quite a lot of buttons to press, which are all.. useless)- the game can get you stuck in progress because you can only chose between three missions all the time and the rewards are randomly generated. if you are unlucky (like me) you will end up with hundreds of everything but 0 of the ressource you need or want. at least if you care to bring some variety into your base and not just spam the basic turret. but it really doesnt matter in the end.- big part of the game is an upgrade mechanic (to increase your main weapons damage) that completely relies on RNG, eats up a ton of ressources and can easily cripple your performance, especially early game.- there's only one boss fight mission that will never reapper if you beat it.- you cannot zoom out, but for whatever reason, zoom in so far that it's more confusing than anything.so, for me, as a veteran strategy gamer and tower defense fan since it was invented: this game game me absolutely no challange at the highest difficulty. essentially, i beat the whole game within 4 hours, did never fail a mission and only kept playing because i wanted to see if there's anything interesting to happen after the boss fight. sadly, no. not even achievements. i'd suggest pick it up for 5 bucks or lower. game appears to be a mobile game but for whatever reason it's for 20 bucks on steam. i had fun tho

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely awesome. Only your tower is an "active" unit. Everything else functions passively on its own so there is no micromanagement during each round. All of the visuals and sounds are phenomenal, and the reactions from every weapon feel right. It's super satisfying when your mortar turrets saturate an enemy wave into oblivion. I haven't ran into any bugs in 8 hours of playing it.Between each battle, you have an economic phase where you can do upgrades and plan for your next battle. The upgrades could use more balancing, but it's a solid system. Before you start each battle, you get a choice of what you want to fight against (ground invasion, air invasion, tanks, etc) and each one provides their own rewards so if you need a certain resource to upgrade your weapons or unlock something, you might want to select that option, or plan ahead for a different resource. During most battles there are 3 rounds that aren't over until you kill the last enemy of the round, and you can see the estimated difficulty when you choose which battle to fight. Easy battles are really easy, but the harder fights are a real challenge without being impossible to a new player. The game ends when you either kill the boss (first chance is at 50 battles, and every 50 after that if you don't kill it) or lose enough battles. Losing a building during a battle doesn't cost you anything, and in fact, refunds all the resources used to build your structures as they are destroyed, so you could have another plot unlocked to rebuild the tower immediately on. Once you fill all the plots, it's just optimizing during each battle.Pros:-Looks amazing-Feels great-No bugs -New style of Tower Defense-Losing once isn't the end of everything-It's only as challenging as the battles you choose. -Fast battles Cons:Upgrade system could use more tweaking, but devs have actually balanced and improved. I'm sure this won't be an issue in the future. Everything will get repetitive quickly if you don't kill the boss at day 50, as your next opportunity is day 100, 150,etc. TL;DR:I would recommend this to anyone that wants to experience a fresh type of tower defense game. Solid 9.5/10. If you're on the fence about the price for 6-8 hours of content, pick it up on sale and you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this kind of game, and it does some interesting things, but it is not polished enough for me to recommend. It especially doesn't make sense when it tells you before you go into combat what to expect, but you can't really do anything to avoid it if its not suited to your current loadout, other than picking a different mission - if that is an option. You also can't rebind the controls, which was frustrating for me. I also felt like the progression was too slow. Unlock a sweet new tower in your research and want to drop it in your next combat? _childDocuments_.review: Recent updates have improved the game quite a bit in both replayability and later levels not taking such a long time.  The price point for what you get might still be a little high -- maybe check on pricing or sale history. Before the update I was on the verge of downvoting the game, but I'm glad to see improvements in the update.I hated that, previously, most towers couldn't even hit the final challenge.  I haven't tested all new specialized builds yet, but the possibility seems there at least.  And a high DPS build can beat normal difficulty in only ~2-3 hours now (I believe it was around 4-5+ before due to simply waiting for the slow influx of invaders past day 40, which was quite boring in old patches).  Though I still think the main weapons seem VERY lackluster aside from splash damage (your towers handle huge waves while your main weapon can barely take out a few single units), it still seemed somewhat important for taking out high priority targets/tanks.  I'm interested in coming back every few days in the near future to try out a new strategy and/or difficulty when I have a few hours to spare, including focusing on main weapons more to see if I'm wrong about that part.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, nice game for sure. Good mix of tower defense, invasion/horde game, and even some element of cookie-clicker game.The large battles, once you upgraded a lot, are amazing. Great system for allowing us to choose which battles to pic, to either get to the end boss as soon as possible or to keep on fighting to upgrade your towers further - feels rewarding.Very satisfying to see how a bunch of mortars strike an area. Super fun to see at the start of a battle how your entire tower defense descends onto the field.A good game to do a little match here and there. But one will come to the final boss quickly. Overall variation in fights is missing. The map cycle is short. Would have preferred to have some more options on how the camera is controlled instead of it forced to the mouse. There is not much beyond building up towards the boss fight or maybe completing the entire upgrade tree. What might help to improve this game is to add additional choices/conflicts. For example: picking which battles you fight also influence the factions or it will effect what kind of battles you can choose in the future - something else to give the choices more consequences. And maybe something similar for during the battles - saving certain spots on the battle fields to gain additional tower slots beyond what you can normally buy, etc. Overall, it is still a great game that I enjoyed playing, but it is quite simple and basic with its game systems. It relies heavy on replayability but it lacks in variation that allows for different type of playthroughs each time, and thus becomes stale a bit too quickly. I was a bit sad when I reached the boss because I knew that after this, there wasn't really anything keeping me from playing this more.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely unbalanced garbage, the resource system is SO BAD even on easy you need to go on numerous missions just to get the resources needed to research, then unlock, then construct, each individual component to your base... and then you hit Siege mode, wherein your tiny little painstakingly-assembled base, with its 100 hp towers and 20 damage per shot weapons, that can barely hold up against a couple too many light units, gets swarm assaulted by massive tanks with thousands of health that do like 90 damage a shot, which wade through everything you throw at them and then one-shot your tower. _childDocuments_.review: I stopped playing just to review this game. It was exactly what a was looking for; a unique, modern, epic tower defence with a twist. Exceeded my expectations, quite fun. I suppose some people complained about the price, however between the soundtrack, the sound effects, the skill tree, and the variety of maps to play on, I feel like they worked hard on this game and it shows.Edit: I've now beaten the game and simply want more. There IS an endless mode and also the option to restart on a harder difficulty, however I am craving more content in general. The main missions seem to cycle, different types of attacks between the same couple maps and such.. it does get a little old. Hope these developers make some content additions or a sequel. Looking back, for only 24 hours played so far, I could agree the price is a little high for what is actually here. The gameplay loop gets old with no way to modify or alter the experience other than your tower build.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting tower defense game where you have to protect one single structure that provides both the offense and defense. You upgrade this structure by surrounding it with other smaller towers, that also may be offensive or defensive in nature. Enemies attack form all sides and you must resist to the end to win.You get more resources to upgrade when you win a battle. Thing is, there are 6 main resources and you may only gain two per battle, so you have to pick carefully which battles you want to fight.Campaign mode can be beaten on normal difficulty in just under 3 hours, so it's relatively short and easy. I found the campaign to be rather repetitive, with little enemy variety and the scenarios making little to no difference on the overall gameplay. However, the game offers enough upgrade options for your tower to make the experience diverse.It's rather gorgeous to look at, sound and music are excellent, gameplay and controls are okay.I think it's a good enough game to justify it's price tag, and a decent TD. Not spectacular, but deserves a recommendation. Play it if you are interested in a simple, minimalist game without too much depth in strategy, resources management or base-building. If you want a challenging and super in depth tower defense game, search somewhere else.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best SFX, VFX and shader work I've ever seen from a solo-dev. Honestly outstanding attention to detail and richness to the art. Taur is a undeniably gorgeous game, especially in the heat of combat. The UI is also fantastic and functional. It's an incredibly well polished game, clearly made by a talented artist.Campaign Completion: 5hrsUnlocked Everything: 6hrsMax'd Research: 8hrsFavorite weapons: Tempest, Punisher, Destroyer.Best moments: Massing Chimera's, every double Tempest shot, Shotgunning enemy aircraft, Knocking Helios' out of the air before they drop payloads, watching Guardians and Rangers form a line.However, the balancing misses the mark for me - it feels massively incomplete. My main gripes are:- The pacing was so slow. It felt like a point and click defender for the first few hours, rather than a tower management / defense game.- Once I entered mid-game, I was frustrated at the lack of variety and novel experiences. Repetitiveness kicked in fast.- Losing the mouse when lots of explosions happen.- The Prime Weapons are frustrating to use due to inaccuracy, ammo capacity and reload balance. Honestly, I was expecting an aim-assisted weapon to replace the Railgun because it got way too much. - The environment blocks line of sight. It's a novel idea, but massively over-used IMHO and leads to odd and annoying AI behaviour.- The maps are also very small, making enemy density way too high to be coherent, especially late game. Honestly, the game would feel better just by making the maps 2x larger, with more open ground.- The Research tree is huge, but unlocking new stuff doesn't feel very impactful as it's mostly incremental stat boosts. I want to feel the effects of my purchases. Also, some items (Aegis) are orders of magnitude better than others (SAM Site).- Seven(!) currencies is too abstract, and makes the mission RNG extremely frustrating. Switching to "Energy, Towers, Research, Forging" currencies may work very well.- The abilities are single-use per mission until late in the campaign due to cooldowns.- Mines are area denial tools, but this mine ability functions almost identically to the Tempest Mortar.- The Ranger Volley is useless until late.- My shield was depleting constantly, but the screen was so cluttered I often had no idea who was hurting me. Damage direction with damage quantity indicators would be appreciated. Enemy weapon VFX should scale with damage output (e.g. enemy attacks that do more damage should be more easy to notice).- Some HUD displaying number of allied units and turrets remaining would be appreciated, with more UI events for turrets getting destroyed. - The Forge is also quite frustrating, given that the benefits are incremental, and the bad outcomes are RNG.- Giving enemies more distinct roles would be good (e.g. by playing with range and how the enemy targets). Summary: Gorgeous game, and recommended based on strong confidence that the gameplay will be improved over time, given the caliber of what I've seen. Great polish and execution, but some ideas need to be re-worked, as the game lacks variety and coherence.

_childDocuments_.review: If you  want a tower defense game that requires some resource management and a bit of base building then this is a game for you! Great replay value too since you can try different strategies and base layouts. I really liked having control of a tower. Its a very unique mechanic in the tower defense/RTS genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Just so ya know I've played this game for 8 hours so far (most of it is offline)Taur is by far the best tower defense game I have ever played.I have not played every tower defense game, but Taur by FAR is the best looking and most interesting tower defense game I've ever seen or played.The beginning is a bit slow, but about an hour in is when your gameplay starts to look like whats in the store trailers, it does take patience, but once you get to the mid game and endgame, it is absolutely INSANE.To start off with, the optimization is fantastic for the level of graphics, and I absolutely adore the sound effects and the way enemies die and fall apart.When you first start you'll simply be shooting little rolling balls with a sniper tower, and then you'll be buying defense turrets to help you take care of the small hordes that will attack your tower, and then it starts to get insane when you buy guardians, which are basically holeless-donuts on their sides with lances, which will further help you defend against the small hordes of attackers. and then once you start getting gunships, fighters, bombers, and archers, that's when you start facing an absolute insane amount of enemies.for game mechanics Taur has a decently complicated rock paper scissors system, which you will use to take enemies ranging from, gunships, armored gunships, tanks, armored tanks, armored shielded tanks, and large groups of rollers (that's what I call the basic ground enemy)I don't know what else to say except if you enjoy tower defense and watching things go BOOM and youhave some spare time on your hands Taur is the game for you! I will definitely keep playing it off and on even though I already beat it.(oh yea it only took me 8 hours to beat it, but the game has a endless mode for those wanting more boom and ka-boom)I give Taur a solid 10/10 the only flaw is that there's only 1 boss and a little lack of enemy air variety.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Tower defense isn't my thing, so I refunded it. Great game for those who are into this genre though, plays like a Flash tower defense game in some ways but has great production values. Graphics look clean, sound design is top notch, though personally I think it should be $20 as I feel that would be a fairer price for what you're getting. I would love to have this game on the Switch, as it seems like it would be a great way to kill a few minutes during your commute and/or lunch break.

_childDocuments_.review: Good example of a game that does one thing well. It's pretty short (~5 hours) and the replayability is pretty bad because, well, there's no difficulty setting and it's not very deep strategically, but it's fun for what it is.+ I enjoy the basic gameplay loop. It's fun.+ It's satisfying blowing stuff apart+ Intuitive controls and menus- Main points: lack of meaningful choices: shallow strategy. Also, too easy. Most of the points below are tied to that.- Upgrade stuff => build stuff => shoot stuff is the game, in sequence. Would like it if for example there was an alternative game mode where you would build and upgrade your base during battles, forcing you to choose between spending time shooting or building, giving you more decisions to make as to where you would spend your attention.- Somewhat boring upgrade trees - most are incremental, numerical increases (+ health, - cooldown...) that don't really show during game. Would love upgrades that change the way the weapons work. For example, the beam weapon could have a choice between wider or more narrow beam, allowing you to specialize it.- No sense of risk - it's easy to keep your "control" over the planet at max or close to max and you get resources even if you win or lose, and every building that gets destroyed refunds its cost.

_childDocuments_.review: It could use a lot of improvement but generally I found it pretty enjoyable. My favourite part of Starcraft was always base defence, and this feels similar to what I've been looking for. Positives: -Nice visuals-Sound design is mostly great (aside from the starting secondary weapon's silly cymbal crashes), which makes everything feel great to useNeutral:-Research tree has good and bad elements to it, some of them are really fun and some are grindy minor health upgrades-The repetition is kind of balanced for me by the assault variants, and the overwhelming numbers you face later onNegative:-The Forge is awful. Huge expensive resource dump to gamble on upgrades, in most cases I ended up downgrading my gun after spending expensive resources I had to grind a while to get. Feels bad, especially at endgame.-Rewards don't seem balanced. Early on I ended up having masses of the higher tier resources and not enough medium or lower, at endgame I had none of the highest tier after the lower ones became nearly useless.-There is a major repetitive grind-I can't see myself starting over to replay it, once I had everything unlocked it will be a fun game to go back to infrequently, like a Starcraft / Wc3 custom game would be-Didn't meet my $1 per 1hour of fun measure, but it definitely would once it goes on sale

_childDocuments_.review: Played through the recent updates and I gotta say, Taur is turning into one of my favorite tower defense games.It's not endlessly replayable, but I see myself coming back to this every few months-years and having a good time. That's value that a lot of popular games don't give me.There's nothing quite like it on the market, and I love the new systems being added. In many ways the game became objectively harder with more difficult enemies, but new systems added in place give you plenty of tools to tackle that challenge.The difficulty is at a point now where I find it very hard to left click my way to victory, and so this has become a much more strategy focused game than a shooter.I hope it continues in that direction, and I hope more updates change up the game as much as the last.

_childDocuments_.review: JUST ONE MORE ROUNDJust to start off: this is not a tower defense game. At all. It's a mix of old time arcade shoot'em up and stonewall defense.This is a good little game, which also happens to be stupid addictive. Slaughtering all those little bots with your railgun is extremely satisfying. Nuking the hordes with your plasma bombs is also extremely satisfying. All the tiny bots' pieces flying everywhere. Even the entrance scene to each map is extremely satisfying with all your towers and units plopping down onto the map.The gameplay is very simple. Hold off the hordes of invading enemies with your weapons arsenal. Each map you win earns you various crystals etc. which you can use for research and upgrades. It does however require a good portion of reflexes and aim by the player. But so far after 5 hours of gameplay, I still find it quite relaxing and laid back. There's no feel of rush or stress when playing the game, not even when you're overwhelmed by enemy waves of bots.Unlock and upgrade. Fight more enemies. Repeat.You have several primary and secondary weapons to choose from - guns, missiles, anti-air, bombs, etc, and you have a good selection of various turrets as well. You have melee and ranged ground units, and some flying units such as interceptors, gunships, and bombers. All turrets and ground/air units are automated, and will move around to defend where needed. The ground units will form a defensive line against the invading hordes.The graphics are easy on the eye, and the sound design is simple. Everything looks beautiful, and the guns, bombs, and explosions all sound really good.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR Best visual explosións ever, so satisfing to watch every time, loop is fun enough.This is a "base defense" so the diference with a "Tower defense" is that you build your base in a hexagon like manner insteand of building in each map a maze like defense, but the catch is that they can be destroyed, howhever you get refunded full price so it's not punishing.This is not a hard game but the visuals are pretty enought (the explosions are the best I've ever seen) and the  game loop is fun enough, plus the liberty of how you're going to set up your base lends itself to various strategies. You can also (and will need to) upgrade your guns and interact in combat directly with shooting and skills.

_childDocuments_.review: It's smooth, straightforward, gives me varying levels of happiness from destroying robots, tanks, aircraft, and (someday soon) big, giant super cruisers. It's a manual turret-defense, manual being that you control the main turret while still landing mini turrets to defend you. Along with mini turret modules, you got unit modules that send in either foot soldiers or aircraft of your own, all automated. --I would love to have the camera to rotate left and right. Some of the maps have uneven terrain, like weirdly shaped/placed boulders, that block my shots when I least expect them to. The big bubble shields that covers us also happens to partially cover our view of what's happening behind the towers.--Since we regain a full refund from destroyed turrets and other modules, it would be nice if we could rearrange or replace these modules between missions. Right now, anyone can scrap all their modules near the end of the mission to prep for the next. It will even help out with buying new upgrades and such. I would say yes, this game is a pretty good game to get. It does have its tense moments, and some easy moments. Exploding little balls and cubes and making them fall around is satisfying to watch, and quick sniping the rocketeers from the far side of the map is a joyful tickle to my ego. It does have some things that it can improve on, but gameplay is smooth sailing for the most of it. I am still trying to find a way to get the most out of my main guns, but they feel powerful and potent that it's not much of an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Tower Defense games, you'll probably love this game like I do.Pros:~It's beautiful. Especially when you get to mid-late game and you have lasers, missiles, and bullets flying every which way as explosions are destroying the environment and planes are spiraling out of the sky. Nothing like massive destruction.~The music is great. It fits the game so well and can get you hyped to get right in the action!~Time flies. You easily start the game, play a few matches, and notice that 2-3 hours have gone in an instant. Love it.Cons:~There is no music in the actual battles. Though this is easily fixable by looking up battle music on YouTube. I would love for the music that's on the main screen to also be played while you're actually fighting. Like I said the music on the main screen is great, so it's a shame they didn't make any for the actual fighting.~The tech tree is limited. While at first glance it looks pretty big and nice, and it is. You'll soon realize that almost half of the upgrades are just to increase the health of the tower's themselves, not to increase the damage, attack speed, etc. And while it's useful, isn't a super fun thing as it adds nothing visually. ~Enemy types are limited. The first few matches you'll get excited after seeing all the different droids, vehicles, and planes the enemy throws at you, but after like 30 minutes you'll have pretty much seen every enemy type except the boss.Conclusion:Taur is a new and interesting take on the tower defense genre and personally I love it. Most of the cons I listed are easily fixable/updateable and I hope we get some kind of DLC in the future as that could easily fix most if not all the cons. Keep in mind this is the Developer's first game, and I think it's fan-flippen-tastic. While I can't honestly say I think it's worth the $25 price tag (mostly due to how quickly you get through seeing all the enemy types and the tech tree) I will say if you want to support a developer who cares about his game (He has hotfixed this game twice in 1 1/2 weeks and clearly seems to look at feedback) and hope to see more, I would say this is a game and developer worth your investments.

_childDocuments_.review: Bought the game. After two hours of play uninstalled and refunded it. The gameplay is solid, however there is a zero tutorial and no way to either re-key map or know what button does what. The aim is very pin-point so amazing at first look, completely a bad idea though when facing hordes of enemies. There is no room to experiment, it's either you already know or hope what you picks work. Though I like the idea of building while in battle, but come on, does everything need to be rushed?Overall, gameplay is repetitive, "matches" are unrewarding, resources are RNG to the point that "i'm with stupid-bat" can't numb the pain, zero story other than the intro. It's just pop you in a area, defend yourself, win, repeat. Oh yeah, one other thing, if you loose enough, there isn't really a way to get back though the game will keep trying to play a loosing battle.For the price, it's asking a lot for something feels lacking. If you can buy it cheap ($10.00 at the very least) then I could justify getting the game, but at $25 for so little, it's depressing.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool take on the tower defence genre with a persistent base that travels around to defend locations from swarms of enemies. Fight in different locations, choosing where to defend (and where not to) to choose what resources you need, or where stopping the enemy will be most valuable for your campaign.Use those resources to build up your Taur (Tower) with guns, infantry drone controllers and air powerResearch survivability upgrades, new weapons and special abilitiesEach battle is a short and intense affair and destroyed parts cannot be rebuilt until the next deployment, although losses are refunded 100% so your overall progression can't be set back by the enemy. You lose the campaign by losing control of the planet, but campaign difficulty is pretty forgiving in the current patch so you'd have to be Videogame Journalist level bad at games or totally AFK for that to happen in my opinionWorth a buy, completed campaign in less than 8 hours, but infinite mode is unlocked so you can continue playing with your upgraded toys and go for 100% tech tree completion

_childDocuments_.review: Unique tower defence game with interesting style. Don't let the simplistic polygons fool you, this is a surprisingly challenging game. You will be pushed. I didn't find it too difficult, though the difficulty does ramp up, and quick, it does so at a pace that is easily in line with the player's progress in upgrading and expanding their tech and weapons.You will need to balance your weapons, find the right layout of your turrets and keep a close eye on your abilities as they cool down. Everything is needed if you want to win, especially in the later missions.On day 50 and every 25 days after, you will fight the end boss. I beat him on day 100. It isn't difficult to stay in the positive when it comes to the occupation level of the planet, which I feel might be a tad too easy, as having the enemy fill that occupation meter is how you lose the game. The game is pretty forgiving when it comes to the missions you can do. Even if you fail a mission, it is very easy to make it back up.All in all, this is a fun and somewhat challenging game, but not too challenging if you know what you are doing. Actually losing the game seems somewhat impossible, and, looking back on it, you are fairly OP compared to what you are facing once you can fully load out your base and upgrade your gear. Heck, I didn't even finish unlocking all the abilities before I beat the end boss.Despite that, the game excellently manages to keep a frantic feel to everything and, regardless of your actual overpowered nature, you always feel on the edge of losing. It strikes that precarious balance that all tower defence games seem to struggle with beautifully.Definitely can't recommend this game enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, a new take on a classic Tower Defense scheme that has seen close to nothing new in the last 10 years.This game is nothing short of excellent game play mechanics and a extremely satisfying physics system, that is at least before you begin to get hoarded with enemies. And that brings me to my biggest gripe with this game, there is almost no variety in how you play the game, it is all just leading up to a boss fight that you get to where you would be able to defeat fairly easily with all the upgrades, but even having failed the boss fight twice, it only took me 7 hours to complete the game, and for a game that cost 25 dollars, I feel like I did not quite get my money's worth out of it.While I do think that this game is a worthwhile experience, I think it needs some more variety in modes and perhaps maybe even a choice on how to arrange the towers. Otherwise the price for the game does feel extremely steep.All in all, a begrudging recommend for a game that is so close to excellent but just needs a little more.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the game in 10 hours. Nothing to do after that, unless you want to continue to play endlessly. But you can't play endlessly because most likely you have used all the spaces for towers. You can continue to grind and upgrade your weapons, but it is pretty much randomised and not worth the time and resources.Overall, the game has one sound strategy, which is unlocking all the abilities and filling tower board with a mix of towers. There is only way to win this game and it is to use your shield ability and that archer skill. It is very primitive in its gameplay. No provoking of deep thinking, should i build this tower in front or beside this tower. If you have played tower defense you would know that there are towers that boost other towers. In this game, there is none, it is basically survive, use the resource to build more towers and that's it. This could be a mobile game for all I know. Ultimately, very disappointed. Could have been more. Saying that this game has more updates to come is inexcusable. I bought a released game, I am reviewing the experience of a released game, not a game that has potential to be better (or worse) in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: A bit on the high side for price on a casual gamer type of tower defense. Great graphics, decent game-play. Could honestly work on bettering the pacing, but somehow currently feels accomplishing with how I'm playing it right now.  To each their own, except you should try it when you have a good amount of free time.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: For all those who dig up tower defense games, I have to say that this one is truly an interesting take on the genre (at least in my knowledge). At first you're presented with a bit too much information perhaps, but as you play you get used to it and just realized the similarities to all the other games of this genre. It has its unique quirks, which took me by surprise. A pleasant surprise.I've went past the 80+ mark in the campaign and I can say the difficulty is very balanced, assuming you are smart in upgrading your tower. A few losses here and there are to be expected, and the fact you get for free all the resources feels a bit like a cheat to me (each battle literally ensures you get the resources mentioned, either you win or lose, and that's a bit of a minus imo, but it's fine overall cause difficulty keeps increasing regardless) but overall the game feels well balanced in every aspect.After encountering the "final boss" a couple times I can already feel the satisfaction it will bring when I'm done with him ahahahah.Again, highly suggested if you want a peculiar take on the tower defense genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy Taur so far. It's a great blend of strategy and action. The weapons feel powerful (especially when upgraded) and it's satisfying to watch the destruction unfold. I recommend Taur to people who enjoy tower defense games but who may be bored with the traditional lane-focused gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Taur is a tower defense game focussed upon a singular, central defensive structure, whose capacities you persistently unlock and upgrade as you wish via research, reforging of available weaponry, and unlocking/construction of modules. Much like the GemCraft series, the more you play the more capable you can get, which is terrifically engaging. Your mouse controls your targetting cursor, the primary interface for your gun structure; much of your buildable assets can act on their own, so you do not need a million hands and fifty brains to keep up or merely play.The trailers for the game show Taur at its busiest - no worries, as the play curve seems very amenable. The developer does not throw you into the deep end to watch you flail.  :)   Definitely recommended. Solid engine & animation... like a tower defense wargame version of Tempest. Of course, the biggest factor here is that Taur is genuinely fun. Its upgrade/unlock systems promise that such fun will last for a lengthy period of time, and for a quite reasonable asking $price$. A great game seemingly from out of nowhere.EDIT/UPDATE: Wow! The additions of Rebels, Trading (& Trading Factions), and Sentinels add entirely new dimensions to Taur. Revisited and re-enjoying. Awesome updates! Difficult, but worthy... even more worthy than it was before.

If you are just starting out, i would recommend investing points into troops for a solid line, then going for turrets into air. My one recommendation for the devs is to add more story. _childDocuments_.review: It's an OK game. I found the micromanagement of manually shooting your central tower weapons to be quite annoying and against the spirit of the tower defense genre. The amount of resource types also struck me as unnecessarily complicated. Just make the higher tiers of technology and buildings cost large amounts of one resource. Other than that, I liked the meaty feeling of explosions and other effects, and the melee phalanx your deployed droids make. Not quite the mindlessly satisfying time sink a la Creeper World or Bloons I wanted it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the concept of this game :)Nice to have an interactive TD with intresting progression system- Base is persistent (you can sell and buy your towers at no loss)- Research system to unlock towers and increase their potential- Research abilities that you can activate at an cool down each missionThe resource management is also fun, you need to make choices when you defend a place, each place gives other resources and sometimes you need to consider the score loss of not defending a specific one over maybe the resources you may find in a other sessionYou cannot change the dificulty of the game. I personaly noticed it was easy until wave 50 was hit, at that point it got more intyresting in my opionThe missions / mobs are to similar would be fun to have more intresting mobs and hordesI do like that you are in control of the main tower keeping you engaged during a mission.

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this type of tower defense, It's much different from others. I recommend focusing on one specific defensive strat in the beginning, this will make things a bit easier since getting materials can be a grind. I enjoy the challenge during the first 50 days or so. Once you get to the point in building the bigger structures then the game gets drastically easier.  For my strat I focused on towers at the start, once I got the Striker towers the game got noticeably easier. It's a balancing act on what resources to spend and save to spend. Overall for a tower defense game I'll give it a strong 8/10.  Couple things I wish could have been different but it still was well done!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good simple game, it starts out a bit rough and you build your base slowly.But i must say after getting a few buildings and powers it gets really easy fast.
