_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in 8,6 hours. The core gameplay is good, but it gets repetitive very quickly. The mechanics are nice and the graphics are pretty. It feels rewarding playing with the considerable powerhouse that is your base. If anyone reading this ever played supreme commander and remembers how much fun it was having fully upgraded commander, and the power that came with, you can experience the same satisfaction here, but with more customization options. You have your autonomous turrets  and airplanes and whatnot, and you can use your considerable arsenal manually. Rewarding powerful laser beams and tactical missiles, and so on. The resource missions you get can be very uneven, making artificial bottlenecks to the progress. For example I had a shield generator researched and building area ready, just needed the material for the construction. I think I ended up waiting over 7 turns in game before even seeing a mission with said needed resource. I had to wait even longer to get enough of those missions to have the resources to build it. This can get annoying in long run when you have mountains of all the other resources piling up, but the one you need for research or upgrade the game is arbitrary scarce with. I hope they would later introduce some sort of conversion system, if further development is planned. Game has only one last boss you encounter first time at day 50. Losing to it for the first time is not punishing, I don't think you are expected to beat it in the first run. Personally I managed it at day 101. ( could have been faster without those annoying bottlenecks I mentioned earlier).  The difficulty curve ramps up fast, but it is manageable. Even if you lose a conflict, you are still awarded the resources, so there is no problem with losing too many fights in the campaign leading into this losing spiral. Ofcourse you cannot lose too much or you,,, well, lose. All in all good game, especially for it's price, but few things to nag about.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for tower defense games and this scratched that itch.  I love the graphics, sound, and the depth of strategy needed to win.  If you like tower defense games, it'd be easy to sink 8 fun hours into this.  But you wouldn't put +20 in.My feedback to the developer:  The whole tower system is very passive.  I would like a lot more tactical control of turrets.  For example: restricting their field of view, changing their target priority (closest, largest, flying, etc), or having some that would aim at your cursor.  The left click gun is also very underwhelming.  For both land and air, the secondary guns are way more effective.  It starts you out thinking it's a shooter-type tower defense, focused on your main gun and precise aim.  But that quickly falls off and resources devoted to the gun (of any type) are wasted.  I really like that the strategy to beat regular levels differs so greatly from the strategy needed to beat the boss.  It makes for a great learning curve and challenge to squeeze through air raid levels (for example) and beat the boss 2 days later.  But what I don't like is that everything effective was passive.  Optimal strategy is to hold down F and cycle spells.  Even if they were more effective, the reload times on all the best guns are punishing and unfun.  I felt like the property manager of the tower system rather than the pilot or gunner.  An overhaul of the primary weapons and changes to turret options would turn this from a 7 to a 10.  Thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: Review based on 3 hours of gameplay so far.Taur is a bit different from other TD's. Here you control the main turret and build other turrets which has automatic functions. You also can use "skills" or "spells" to help you get control of the situation.I'm really enjoying the game so far, I'm currently at my first run (day 48), the learning curve can be a bit difficult for those who don't pay attention to upgrades and types of map you choose to deploy your defense.Whats i like in the game:- It has THAT X FACTOR: you feel satisfied with the action and results of your action.- Sound FX is amazing, helps the satisfaction thing to get better. (shooting sounds really good)- The challenge is fair yet some maps can be a nightmare... so far- Graphics are exactly what the game needs.- Straight gameplay (you upgrade your stuff and go beat the enemies, there's not much more than this).- Good set of weapons and turrets, i still didn't unlocked everything though.What i don't like or think would be improved for now:- Maps seems to be a bit repetitive, there are a few ones.- It could have more enemy variations too.- The system to reforge the main weapon is too random, i'm still not sure i like it.I may change this review in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of fun, but very limited play time as the game is right now.I'm on day 29 on my first play through and the game has become somewhat repetitive. It constantly says 'massive army' on the days but the army sizes doesn't change much, nor their compositions. I want enormous battles with 300+ enemies with several tanks and miles of dudes - leave out the planes, they don't do much other than take away from the beauty of leaning back and seeing your towers slaughter the cannon fodder running towards you. At most you just change weapon and blow them away.You also very quickly max out the tech tree, or at least get to where the things you want are and then max those out.As is, you get 2-3 solid hours out of it before it gets too repetitive. But those hours are a lot of fun - though a bit pricy game for that amount of time but w/eCrossing my fingers for updates on:-a primary weapon that also goes boom-nerfing the shield - got it on day 26 and all of a sudden i became immortal-make defeating the enemy mean something - just having a bar move between 80-100% doesn't tell me anything-the 6-8 maps or so gets very repetitive, make moving around mean something - give some maps advantages to specific things or make specific units for each terrain (droids drilling under the sand fx).
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky one.I am a huge fan of the TD genre. I love it. You will find a ton of innovation here. You can almost say this is almost not TD. Your 'base' is saved across maps, so its not about matching specific build patterns to specific levels. More about robustness. You also control a main tower with primary/secondary weapon to help defense, for me this isn't ideal and not that rewarding. It also detracts from the TD experience and makes it more arcade. The resource-system is a over-complicated. There are 6 types of resources for various actions. Hopefully this will get re-worked. The tech-tree could also use some work, it takes some work to get into it. Not easily clear what towers do what, though I appreciate the minimalistic icon design its not easy to understand what each tower does from it. So why am I recommending this? I see so much promise here. The devs clearly love this game. So I am hanging on and waiting. All the best devs! <3

_childDocuments_.review: After giving it some years, the game is nearly perfect. And is still absolutely great and worth buying in 2024. You can now buy and sell ressources, (with some strategies into it) and that solves one of the main issues we had. You also can use more units of your own (a big tank, an enormous spacecraft, and some rebels that will help you in some more specific ways than the old and great guardians and rangers).The only small issue that I still have is not being able to build towers between matches. It forces you to take some screenshots to remind of the prices of things and act pretty fast when in battle, but it's not awfull. This game is the pinnacle of tower defenses games. It's still very fresh, and way less frustrating than before while being way more challenging ! Really, good job dev.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is hella fun. It's a really simple premise. You build a tower with shooty bang bangs on it, and you have to kill the enemies before they kill you. Each level lasts 1-3 minutes early on, and then 3-10 minutes in the mid-late game. That's it. That's every level of the entire game until you win, lose, or quit. The graphics look fantastic in motion. It's a very simplistic style, but it works -very- well. Lasers have sufficient pew pew, explosions feel meaty, and as levels escalate it becomes a kaleidoscope of booms. The audio is also great, though for some reason there's no music during levels (other than the final boss). This is a bit disappointing because the music is actually good.The variety of turrets and toys to play with are good. There's a decent selection of primary and secondary weapons, and there's (some) reasons to use them all. Spreading out defences feels good, and the base area looks cool as heck when it gets crowded with all the structures and units you've deployed.There's a meta campaign alongside the tower defence action. This is pretty shallow, and basically boils down to picking the missions which give the best resources, then using those resources to buy/upgrade your shooty bang bangs. There's not much more to it. You can 'lose' the game if you have a string of losses in missions, but otherwise the campaign will continue until you win or quit.There's a few things I don't like: The early game levels are too quiet, some of the techs feel pointless, and primary guns get randomised upgrades. The game also gets a bit repetitive in the late-game, as there's only four mission types other than the boss. The escalation of missions makes them feel different though, especially 'invasion' which drastically changes once aircraft + tanks join the fray.It would've been great to get more bosses or unique encounters, as the -one- boss is easily the best level in the game. A different unique boss every 5 levels would take this game from good to phenomenal, even if it was the only change made.Overall: it's good, I enjoyed it, but it's also a bit overpriced. Watch the videos. The videos contain the entire gameplay loop after the first hour of play. If you're happy with that spread over 6-10 hours then it's worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Taur

_childDocuments_.review: I have always been a huge fan of Tower Defense games, so picking up Taur was a no brainer. I am not very creative, so instead of writing long sensible paragraphs, I'll do pros and cons.PROS:- Graphics: Game looks absolute fantastic, I love the art style. The explosions are just beautiful, and there is a lot of them.- Difficulty: Game is actually genuinely hard in the beginning. The boss that happens on day 50/75/100 demolished me the first 2 times(I won the 3rd!) Some waves are extremely random and hard to predict which adds to the the difficulty.- Gameplay loop: It's fun, it's engaging, there is a lot of upgrading and researching between rounds.- Skills: Fairly large skill tree, most of the upgrades are kinda dull and unintuitive, but it kinda works.CONS:- Sound: There is literally no music apart from when you're in the campaign menu. The gun/explosion/tower sounds are fine, but I had to play my own epic space battle music to add to the experience.- Content: Or lack of. There is at most 10-12 hours of content in the game at the moment(I stretched it because I enjoyed streaming it) There is a so much room to grow in this game, I feel like this is more of an "early access/beta" kind of thing where you get the shell of a game. - Heavy RNG: You can get royally screwed by continuously getting the wrong resources from missions. Some missions are also just straight up very very difficult, and sometimes all 3 options end in defeat.- Severe lack of strategic options: This is a pretty big one, there is much room to grow here. You can basically SELL/DEMOLISH ANY structure on the field for 100% refund. Downside to this is that the tile becomes UNAVAILABLE for the remainder of combat. So you can't make a strategic decision on the fly, you just gotta play with the cards you dealt yourself on the campaign screen.- Poor balance: Prime weapons are terrible. Atleast until you manage to upgrade the destroyer. Some waves are just insanely hard and ridiculous on some maps. Skill tree gives you 0 options to increase tower damage/speed etc. So your only options are massing more structures that you can't change on the fly.- Air waves: These are absolute butthole, sorry. They're just annoying, tedious and way too long. The anti air weapons for the prime are garbage to say the least :( Even with 8 SAM sites, using beefed HAVOC these waves still take like 5-10 minutes.OVERALL:I enjoyed the game. It's fun, is it worth the 20.99€ price tag at the moment? Probably not. If you're a huge TD fan? I'd pick it up and hope it gets updated soon. Because of my personal bias towards the genre and because the game looks f*in sweet I'll give it a positive review.I will probably come back and edit this review at some point in the near future, It's a little rushed and there is some typos here and there.Might stream it more in the future at  (Shameless self promotion PogChamp)

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Tower Defense games then be sure to check this one out.  The graphics and style is great and it's a lot of fun, and something new too.  It's not perfect but I got a solid 10 hours out of it.  More content is promised, so that may go up.Beware that it's a Rogue style game, you can easily fail a campaign and start over.  The learning curve is brutal, read the forums for hints and tips if you don't want to experience figuring it out by trial and error.  The game itself isn't hard once you learn the mechanics and figure out what everything does, but learning all that IS hard when you think you're fine and then get murdered on the next wave.  But stick with it.Overall, a mostly positive experience. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game, it's quite fun and very active for a tower defender, there's always something to shoot. I do recommend it, but would also say maybe wait for it to be on sale. Overall what content there is is fun, but it's relatively shallow and there isn't enough variety for me to want to replay or do the 'infinity war' endgame after beating the final boss. _childDocuments_.review: Won at wave 100 after 8 hours of playtime. Its not a bad game but gets a little repetitive. Probably not worth the $20 I paid.Each wave you usually get to pick which of 3 different fights to do for their listed rewards. These rewards usually don't match the fight difficulty. Often you'll pick an easy fight because it will pay the resources you need. While these easy fights are quick, its not going to produce any excitement or fun.There are many nodes in the research tree which unlock new weapon towers, new unit towers or base weapons. Not all of them will turn out to be useful in battle as some just perform poorly. Some balance issues there.

_childDocuments_.review: The game has very attractive graphics, particle effects and nice feeling shooting gameplay & hitting feedback. One thing is the tower fall punishment is a bit too harsh, especially on chapters rolled with large group of enemies, didnt have enough resources to upgrade any significant update and my game ended on day 9. _childDocuments_.review: I had a good reason to change this.The Dev's heard the people and acted accordingly, granted i actually don't agree with some of the changes but they did fix the main issue I had with this game in the past and have removed any real chance of the death spiral happening unless you're just really bad at the game now.I really hope the devs plan on adding more to this game it has potential for more if they choose to seek it.Pros-fun concept-Visuals are solid and pretty to look at-Game just works, hardly any bugs to speak of or none at all- balanced gameplay is done really well-Easy to learn-great time wasterCons-Some resources don't drop at good rates making some upgrades hard-can sometimes feel like your units are paper-repetitive but hey its a tower defenseTL:DR Dev's Listened and fixed many issues initial gameplay had making this a very enjoyable experience, which it now is. definitely a game to pickup if you like tower defense with a unique twist on it.

_childDocuments_.review: I like the game, it is fun and I would recommend it, however the resource management is annoying as ♥♥♥♥ and thus the game can't be recommended in its current state or at it's current price. Reforging a weapon 5 times in a row and getting less damage out of it every single time makes you basically useless for a literal real world hour at least. Then, now that your weapon does no damage, you have to save all of your crystals you get from missions to recoup your weapon damage, which means you spent an hour not upgrading your base, not to mention you can absolutely play 4-5 games in a row not getting the crystals you need. By that point, the game has gotten harder which means your base gets heavily damaged because now you have your weapon damage back, but your base has crap for defense. Seems like an endless cycle of you or your base not being able to do ♥♥♥♥, with rare instances of each being on par.I don't understand how people are barely getting to level 5 with issues, if that is the case, you are just really bad at these types of games.I've made it to level 57 so far and I have only lost once. I can not stress enough how much the resource management needs to be fixed. The game has just become a game of diminishing returns because the more you play, the more resources required to build things, the resource growth does not appear to scale at all, and you eventually run out of space to put your little towers, that don't appear to do much anyways.None of this would be a problem if the "Reforge" system wasn't so absolutely garbage and a massive drain on resources.

It can give you contact outlets to journalists or simply let you put up a press release.  I think once this has proper visibility and people see that you are actually listening the game will do well.

_childDocuments_.review: To say Taur is addictive is an understatement.The challenge in this game lies in learning when and what to research and upgrade. Sometimes it will be immediately obvious that you're losing, and other times it will be 30+ days later in-game when the AI begins overpowering you. New players will be sent back to the drawing board and restarting their campaigns.There are lots of different upgrade 'builds' to experiment with, and combat is very engaging and fun.With that all in mind, the game is slightly overpriced. If you really enjoyed old school TD games, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: So this game is basically "What if the group you're playing as in the tower defense has no army to counter attack with."There is no way to when(yet i don't know if they will ever add one). It's a single planet verses a galaxy wide empire. This is not some fairytale or kids movie. You don't stand a chance. All you can do is make them bleed for ever inch of ground they take.You WILL die. You won't survive. But you won't go quietly into the night.In simpler terms: You are Cadia from Warhammer 40k and there are no reinforcement to help fight off the enemy.

_childDocuments_.review: At the beginning I need to say that I'm not a big fan o tower defence style games, but Taur is something more than just another tower defence title. Taur is more interactive kind of game, player need to aim and shoot to enemies by yourself (which is very entertaining and hard). You can ofcourse unlock a lot of upgrades and build automatic towers and drons/droids to help you automatically but the most important are player aim skills and strategy. Taur is hybrid of tower defense and RTS game. If you are looking for more challenging and fun (with all that slow motion effects) tower defence game then Taur is something for you!

detailed_description: An artifact from the past returns in Bartlow's Dread Machine, a long-forgotten game from the dawn of the Electric Age. Dread Machine is a dual stick arcade shooter with single player and couch co-op modes, six scintillating game worlds and a cast of improbable monsters and historical characters. ​ Teddy Roosevelt has been kidnapped! Your mission: Pursue his abductors from New York, across the Great Plains to San Francisco, the high seas and beyond using trains, ships and even a newfangled automobile. Master an arsenal of futuristic Edwardian weapons as you fight otherworldly creatures to free the Commander in Chief. Coming Summer of 2020!

_childDocuments_.review: If this game looks at all interesting to you, give it a try.  If you enjoy twin-stick shooters and/or classic arcade games definitely give it a try.  Even in Early Access they have totally crushed this unique style to deliver a one-of-a-kind inspired game (cripes, that really sounds douche-y, but it's the truth, so whatever).
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: A unique addition to any twin-stick shooter fan's library, the art style is gorgeous and there's a surprising amount of variety involved.  There seems to be a constant 30 FPS lock (since there's no v-sync options in game, only resolution change) and while that's not great, it doesn't seem like a dealbreaker for once, simply due to what this game is.  Seems a bit low on reviews overall so I wanted to do my part but there's a good time to be had here for sure.  I don't think I own nearly enough games where anarcho-Satanists kidnap Roosevelt.  edit: just noticed it's the same devs as Voodoo Vince, and everyone knows that game is great so give this one a shot too.edit 2: so for some reason I needed almost another 3 years to finish the game after starting it, but that's more of a comment on my obscene backlog than it is on the quality of this title.  The 30 fps lock seems to have been patched out long ago and that's good since 60 is almost necessary for this somewhat bullet hell / on rails (of sorts) twin stick shooter.   The game has an odd difficulty spike in the middle I thought but it was fun to work through.  Would love to see more from these devs one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a hidden gem, the music is amazing some of the best in years composed by the same guy who made the song in beep's previous game Voodoo Vince. The aiming in this game can be a bit dodgy at times and I would like to see some sort of laser upgrade or something to show where you are actually shooting. Sometimes you'll aim directly at an enemy but you'll shoot a bit to far to the left or right. You can only shoot in a 2D plane when the game is in 3D but apart from that the game is great.Highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a fun twist on the classic twin stick shooter genre that won’t break the bank. Story is pretty minimal but the dialogue can be fun and the old time’y Americana fits well. Some of the enemy placement can feel a bit cheap at times but stages are 5-10min long for the most part.EDIT: Forgot to mention that this is currently flagged as unsupported on Steam Deck but you can play it from start to finish with no issues by manually setting one of the other Proton versions.
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I love co-op games, especially unique ones with interesting mechanics to give me opportunity to try out something new! Bartlow's does exactly that. The movement system is pretty interesting and gives a unique take on twin stick shooters. The classic strategies still work, but moving on a grid opens up some new ones too! I give props to any game trying something out so unique with high polish and a consistent well designed world.
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Check out the full written review: Bartlow’s Dread Machine takes us back to the simpler times when arcade machines were more mechanical filled with gears, pulleys and levers. This twin stick shooter injects a small dose of style and imagery which we quite welcomed. While not perfect, Bartlow’s Dread Machine does hold our attention long enough, taking us through a story filled with mystery, intrigue and suspense.The twin stick shooter has been around for awhile, but Tribetoy and Beep Games have presented it in a new stylish package. The details of the moving mechanical gears and parts to the old time amusement park music, Bartlow’s Dread Machine is a refreshing entry in the gaming market place. This game is simple, but also throws you into the gauntlet which puts a smile on your face when you make it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: I'm generally not a fan of Early Access, so this was the first time I'd ever bought a game early. From the second I saw a trailer, I knew I had to have it. Months ago, I enjoyed the first few worlds. Today, there's some good and bad within the full product. There are a few difficulty spikes in the later half of the game, and the unfavorable lives system causes some frustration. And sometimes the environments are a bit too dark to really get a good grip on things. But outside of those few gripes, this is a twin stick shooter unlike any other I've ever played. The one hundred year old style is really cool, reminding me a lot of pinball. The way the levels shift, the way everything is attached to metal rods, and the way the characters automate are all really delightful. Going all-in on that presentation reminds me a lot of Puppeteer (PS3) which I find is extremely underrated. There's a lot of love that went into fully realizing what a turn-of-the-20th-century game would look, sound, and feel like. I wasn't initially sure how the traversal would feel, but moving around the slotted tracks as you blast the various types of foes is both satisfying and fun. Fans of serviceable gameplay, who really love games with rich, unique atmospheres should find plenty to enjoy.
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: New idea and cool concept until the devs decided that this is mainly a shooter game and absolutely demolished the creativity that's in the game.Controls are horrendous because your cross-hair can only go up, down, left and right on the screen but the character aims inwards and outwards of the screen.You have auto-aim but sometimes that can screw you instead of helping you.Because the movement is limited in this game which I'm alright with I don't think it was a good idea to make this game heavily depend on movement and trying to get to a good position.

_childDocuments_.review: Bartlow's Dread Machine offers a blast to the past while giving a unique experience that stands out from most modern games. Every aspect of the game is designed in such a way that immerses you in that time period. There's also plenty of customization to support an addicting gameplay loop. It has so much going for it, marred only by the camera being much weaker than it could be. If you're a fan of twin-stick shooters, or even just want something unique, Bartlow's Dread Machine is a game you'll have troubles putting down.Score: 4/5If you'd like to read the rest of this review and more like it, check out . Thank you to Beep Games for providing a review copy.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a great style but the shooting and camera angles are not good.So the developers had a great idea but the execution feels half baked. First, if you are going to create a shooter while moving on tracks you better get the camera angles right, this game has awful camera angles. The problem is that this game plays like a standard  top down shooter but Bartlow's Dread Machine isn't a standard top down shooter. I don't mind getting shot when I can't see an enemy in Hotline Miami but if I am moving on rails that becomes a problem.There are almost no PC options and no accessibility options of course.Look, I know this game is not for me but the camera angles and no accessibility options are facts. Good idea but poor execution. Can't recommend this one.

_childDocuments_.review: i personally didn't enjoy this type of game, but i don't think i'm the target audience.i really wish i could abstain from a "recommend" or "not recommend", so i'm giving it a qualified "Yes" on merit alone.i think it has a lot of charm, a well-executed style, and cool gameplay if it's the kind of gameplay you like. for me, the shooting mechanic felt really challenging given the limited movement, and once enemies were able to shoot BACK at me, the pressure to dodge, parry, shoot in 360 degrees, while moving on a grid fried my little tiny brain.i hope you big brain shootercels can enjoy it though

_childDocuments_.review: Well done twin-stick shooter. It is unique in this landscape of games for its art direction, but the most interesting aspect is the way the movement was done here. Not allowing for full analog movement across the level made for an interesting gamestyle. Thanks to making the playing field always rectangular and movement only four directional, it allowed for the perspective to not hinder the player while he is shooting enemies. It takes a moment to get used to it, but the point is to line the shots on the railing you are on, and then intuitively calculate the angles to shot at, very pleasing to do. Enemy variety is good as well as the difficulty overall is well balanced. It could only use some better effects when hitting bosses to understand that you are doing damage. For the interesting approach to this genre of games and very approachable base price it is an easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: While checking out Bartlow's Dread Machine, for once, I didn't even bother reading the reviews first. The art looked so great and the on rails aspect looked so fun that I just hit purchase. Then I checked it out for a few levels and all my joy turned sour.While I do enjoy the old school characteristics of the movement, it just doesn't work because the controls are too slow to react to your inputs. Meanwhile, the melee enemies will close in on you FAST while the others shoot at your general direction. This means taking your time, losing the money since it disappears, and hoping your placement is correct or you'll die.Speaking of money, you will get a few dollars after each map to purchase unlockables, but nowhere near enough to gain anything impactful. Expect grind. A lot of it.Also, the control scheme is just terrible. Ammo being (quite) limited, keeping your finger on the trigger will not result in shots being done in succession. You have to release the trigger, and then shoot again. Which means dodging is a tad complicated since you gotta move, keep your concentration to shoot, and then aim at the same time. Said issues can be fixed by editing the control scheme in Big Picture and using a controller with a turbo function, but if you gotta use external tools to fix the gameplay, there's a problem.Now, there are a few cool things in the game but as an example, I love chocolate, cheese and red meat. Make me a soup with both of those and I'm absolutely certain to vomit after the first spoon. This is what the game feels like. Individually, I don't feel like the gameplay aspects are really an issue, but mixed together, they just don't work. Great concept, great looks, but poor execution. Sad!
_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: Nice game with automata look and great music. The art style is unique and to the last detail - super! Regarding game mechanics it is a twinstick shooter with the twist that you move on rails which limits you quite a bit when you try to evade the hundreds of bullets and enemies. The game is tough, I beat it on normal in single-player and it took me countless tries. But maybe I am just not good at it, On the positive I was motivated to finish the game and kept playing. There are two difficulty levels below normal and you can switch anytime during the game to avoid frustration.  Mouse and keyboard worked fine for me. It is a very good game if you like the mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: I realised I have 1100+ games in my Steam library and I was going to die before I played them all.So thought I'd spend a bit of time on each one, a new one every night, and leave a short initial review.This is a real surprise, and unknown gem of a game.It's a stylised almost steampunk like retro type arcade machine that is a mechanical twin stick shooter if such a thing could be invented.Great art style, graphics, sound, story, humour, action with twin stick shooting from unusual changing angles and a little bit of Pac man thrown in for good measure. The more you play the better the weapons and I had to drag myself away to play something else. I may even come back later and try and finish it. I hope it runs on Steam Deck!HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!

_childDocuments_.review: Great concept, style, art and music. The mechanical theatre setting and implementation is very cool, granting a very unique approach on the genre, and is very entertaining and fun to play. Also the story and dialogues are nice and well written for the purpose. The mini-games (or alternate game modes, if you will) help add variation and showcase other aspects of the mechanical theater idea. I've played it in couch coop mode and it worked very well, except in a particular (and unique) mini-game. It may use some minor improvements to navigation, at times (especially with a controller, the possibility to move using the d-pad would be a great help), but overall is a very good experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Bartlow’s Dread Machine is a unique game with a wonderful art style. It is a twin-stick shooter with lovely animations, a half-interesting story and a fun gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: Bartlow's Dread Machine is visually beautiful bullet-hell shooter but has a few short-comings within it that are worth taking notice.1. In-game items cost too much/ player don't get enough money during playthroughTo be honest, I could not afford of buying new clothes to my character because I had to save so much money on secondary weapons which have more ammunition and boy do they cost a lot.2. Inaccurate weapon descriptionsTowards end of the campaign I wanted to buy a weapon with as big magazine as possible. Two side-weapons had vague description in style of "this should installed into a ship". I just had to assume the latter one would be with a bigger magazine since it was the most expansive gun to be able purchase but instead it was 20 round magazine.If you are into bullet-hell shooters Bartlow's Dread Machine is a game I recommend to grab on sale. And also worth pointing out that game supports two (2) player co-op and I could imagine this being more fun with a friend.

_childDocuments_.name: Bartlow's Dread Machine

_childDocuments_.review: This game blows me away. I love a good twin stick shooter, and Bartlow's Dread Machine combines great shoot 'em up action with a thoroughly unique gameplay mechanic, and an amazing aesthetic, hearkening back to turn-of-the-twentieth-century gear and slot driven arcade machines.There are other "on rail" shooters, but in this one, you are LITERALLY on rails. Slide your mechanical hero through brilliant, gorgeous, retro-themed levels to rescue Teddy Roosevelt from the clutches of the "anarcho-Satanists".Graphics and music are absolutely fantastic. Remember how much we all loved the style of Cuphead? Bartlow's Dread Machine borrows from roughly the same time period and aesthetic of Bioshock Infinite in American history. The piano driven score is especially good, and the visual design is just breathtaking.Some minor complaints - aiming can be difficult, and the difficulty can be extremely daunting at all but the very lowest levels. An aiming system to show what you're trying to hit would be welcome, even as a gear upgrade. Food for thought for the dev team, who - amazingly! - have been updating this regularly to incorporate user feedback.What a labor of love this game is. And if gamers want to encourage more creativity among software companies, try (and support!) games like this. I got it on sale for a song ($5!) which is the steal of a lifetime in a world of $60 AAA titles loaded with ads and microtransactions. Even at full price, it's a steal. Check this game out.

name: Chained Echoes
detailed_description: Chained Echoes is a story-driven JRPG where a group of heroes travel around the vast continent of Valandis to bring an end to the war between its three kingdoms. In the course of their journey, they will travel through a wide array of diverse landscapes spanning from wind-tanned plateaus and exotic archipelagos to sunken cities and forgotten dungeons. Take up your sword, channel your magic or board your Mech. Chained Echoes is a 16-bit SNES style RPG set in a fantasy world where dragons are as common as piloted mechanical suits. Follow a group of heroes as they explore a land filled to the brim with charming characters, fantastic landscapes and vicious foes. Can you bring peace to a continent where war has been waged for generations and betrayal lurks around every corner? Key Features: 30 - 40 hours of play time Fast paced turn-based battles No random encounters; enemies can be seen running around Tons of items to be looted, stolen or crafted Complex skill and equipment system Customize your own airship Travel and fight by foot or in your Mech 16-bit SNES style graphics Music inspired by PSX RPGs

_childDocuments_.review: Chained Echoes is a game I feel very protective about.  I backed it thinking that it looked pretty cool, but it was going to be developed by a single person and they weren't even asking for that much.  I'm sure they meant well, but I've seen a lot of developers try to pull off a full scale RPG and miss the mark in a variety of ways.  I was just hoping for something interesting and fun.What Matthias Linda has accomplished here is nothing short of incredible.  He demonstrates intricate genre literacy, and has clearly thought very hard about the pros and cons of various systems in RPGs over the years.  The result is something that is rock solid - damn near bulletproof, and every little thing that I've ever thought was an annoyance in the countless other RPGs I've played has been avoided.  The result is something that could only come from examining hundreds of other games, seeing what didn't work, or almost worked, and tweaking until the final product shines.I love the way that each area has a relatively small number of encounters, and each one (on the default difficulty settings) balanced to make you make heavy use of your toolkit.  In exchange, you are fully healed after each battle.  Being able to exercise my full knowledge of my characters' abilities often rather than having my time wasted by hundreds of weak enemies feels excellent.  The addition of the overdrive gauge brings everything together: each attack raises the overdrive gauge, while swapping characters, defending, and using highlighted abilities lowers it, with your goal being to keep your position in the sweet spot to keep incoming damage minimized and your TP costs lowered.  It just feels great. The sky armor combat extends the idea of the regular combat system, but plays with the way the overdrive gauge works in a way that is really interesting and fun.Speaking of difficulty settings, the game does have three separate settings in the options menu to tweak.  "Enemy stats" low/normal/high, "enemy aggressiveness" low/normal/high, and overdrive gauge sweet spot size.  The default is to put everything on normal, and as I mentioned above, it feels absolutely perfect to me.  But if you are having trouble, you have the ability  to adjust to your needs.The side quests in the game are all meaningful and relate directly to the story.  There is not a single fetch quest in the game.  I really enjoyed this.  They have nice little subplots and satisfying encounters.  All completely worth doing, and it ties in well with the in-game reward board which is a checklist of tasks that gives you boosts on money and other resources.I also feel the need to praise the soundtrack. Eddie Marianukroh did a  job here, and the game truly would not be what it is without his work.There's a lot more I would love to talk about here, including entire systems that I really enjoyed, but I strongly feel that at least some of them should not be spoiled for the player.  They're just that cool.  Ultimately, I think that anyone who is a fan of SNES and PSX era RPGs owes it to themselves to check this out.  It really is one of the best RPGs I've played in a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Chained Echoes

_childDocuments_.review: Set in a war-torn land, Chained Echoes places you in a nation who hasn’t known peace for many generations’ lives. You start out playing as a mercenary Glen who’s supposed to go on a quick in and out mission. This sets in motion the events of the game which involve a weapon of mass destruction, angry petty gods, and reincarnation. This gives way for many points of intrigue in the story. All of this is engaging until the last bits of the game which seem to throw the player for a loop completely. Sometimes instances like these capture the player, I was not one of those players. The game ends with a cliff hanger considering the main issue doesn’t get solved. When credits rolled, I sat back and just thought to myself that it ended weaker than I expected.  What Chained Echoes does to stray away from the classic turn based is introduce an overdrive gauge. This gauge moves with every action taken. Split into orange, green and red, the overdrive gauge brings strategy into how the player chooses their actions. Each special skill is classified and using a skill that matches your overdrive gauge will move the cursor inside. The objective is to stay in the green for added advantages such as extra damage and reduced skill cost. If the overdrive reaches the red, enemies do more damage and skills cost more. Bosses take advantage of this gauge by using moves that mix out the normal order of the overdrive gauge. Later, the game introduces (badass) mechs that players can pilot that add an extra dimension to area traversal and discovery. These mechs do substantial amount of damage and change the overdrive movement by linking it to “gears” of your mech. Having your mech in a certain gear will move the gauge in a given direction. This change alone keeps the game from just mashing the skill that does the most damage. Sometimes you’ll have to sacrifice a few turns to make sure you don’t go in the red and suffer the penalties.   Chained echoes side missions are not hard to miss, which I love! At a point in the game, you will be able to go off and adventure in your sky ship straight Cid style. Looking at your map you will be able to discern the side missions that you can do and points where to go next. As a person who doesn’t have as much time as I used to play video games, this streamlines everything for me. The content of each side mission varies, but for the most part they hit. There are some heavy hitting side stories and others are pretty lighthearted. In classic RPG form there are secret boss fights that test the build of your group. There are also special beast hunts that only occur if special conditions to make them appear are met. Both of these task do reward you with special equipment and weapons for your troubles.  The game employs the classic 16-bit sprite art concept along with full bodied adventure JRPG soundtrack.  There were some definite bangers in there for me such as Rohlan fields. It does a good job of making a high fantasy sound track that tickles your nostalgia bone.
_childDocuments_.name: Chained Echoes

_childDocuments_.review: It's a modernized-retro JRPG styled game. For starters there are no random battles and you're automatically healed after each battle without the need of items.During battle, the overdrive system keeps you on your toes and prevents spamming one move with a bar on the top left that has yellow-green-red colors. Green is where you want to keep it at for extra damage and defense. You have to strategize according icon shown at the top box in order to lower or rise that bar. If you go to overheat [red zone] you'll suffer by taking additional damage. Unlike many RPGs, debuffs actually WORK on all bosses and can be vital to your strategy towards victory. My only minor complaints here is that enemies can move your overdrive forward when they attack you. Which can be problematic in certain situations but it's nothing too complicated. Also, some skills have minor improvements [like 5 less TP use.] The only things you can grind for are SP, crystals, upgrade materials and money.Money is easier since you find item bubbles scattered around the world which can respawn anytime you leave an area and come back. Or farm enemy drops. They also unlock deals at shops.Crystal are used to upgrade and customize your characters however you likeMy approach was Agility, Attack\Magic and HP drain which was very effective.Crystals also respawn but after a set time. Skyarmor battles function a bit differently. You manage 3 gears which can affect you attack power and defense depending on what gear you are on. Skyarmor levels are gained through a proficiency system [for both ranged and melee weapons] so make sure your characters are proficient at everything since the stats gained are permanent. There is a nice variety of equipment and attachment which you can switch around to your needs. Also you can select from a nice variety of predetermined colors for your mechs.Once you first unlock skyarmors it's like a breath of fresh air! Levels\skillpoints are gained by fighting bosses [to get Grimoire Shards] or filling up the reward board with many challenges to take on.SP is gained in every battle which is used to level up your skills. {you gain SP twice one is automatically applied the other is stored for you to Lv up whatever you like.Grimoire Shards are your level up currency which you can use to unlock new skills or stat buffs. You also get stat bonuses when you unlock these skill [After every certain numbers of unlocks]. Reward board also offers some of these upgrade shards.Class emblems are scattered around Valandis. Once found and equipped they give you bonus stats + two skills and two passives. They can be permenant once you master them] so you can switch them around once mastered. You have to go through a group of enemies as a test in order to get each emblem.There are 12 characters to select from. 8 can be used in battle and switched according to your formation mid battle [without losing a turn]2 for each of the 4 slot.Each character come with their set of skills that are mostly unique and fun to play with. Some characters involve finishing a side-quest in order to be unlocked.Each character has a unique finisher but they share 1 finisher bar [AKA ultra bar]. Finishers are built up during the battle or by using unique skills.The Soundtracks are fun to listen to and they capture the mood perfectly.Overall It's a solid RPG which has a lot to offer. The weakest link in my opinion was the story. It sets up for a potential sequel, but it's by no means boring. In fact, it can be emotional at times.Fun gameplay and skillsets to play around with. It's one of those games you think about when you go to bed.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Chained Echoes is my GOTY. After finishing the game 100%, it has successfully reignited my passion for turn-based RPGs and all the charm that goes with them. To say that I feel like I got my money's worth from this game is a huge understatement because, throughout 50+ hours sunk into Valandis and this beautiful story, I was in a constant state of wonder that never even bordered the realm of tedium.To start off, the combat is what you make it. There is enough customization in difficulty to tailor the game to how you want your experience to be. The crystals are an interesting mechanic, but it is something that I believe has a lot more potential that can be unlocked.I personally turned my focus toward exploration and the story because I wanted to keep a good pace while writing guides for this game. As a result, I found so many subtle but thoughtful changes that occurred from act to act. Upon noticing how the NPCs evolved as the story progressed, I felt invested in the smaller yet just as meaningful stories they had to tell. I found myself determined to talk to every NPC from Act II onwards because the flavor text definitely turned out to not just be for show. What happens in this world affects all citizens, and it's small details like this that really solidified my interest in the game/story.As far as collectibles go, I really enjoyed exploring every nook and cranny of the game. I felt that the developer did a great job of encouraging exploration by inserting just the right amount of feedback to point players in the right direction (a yellow orb here and there to alert you of a hidden path, NPC subtext to teach you about an area's mechanics, etc.). I enjoyed the gradual expansion of most areas due to unlocks tied to story progression. It reminded me of how Darksiders encouraged revisiting areas after you unlocked exploration tools to reveal more of the map. Overall, nabbing as many collectibles as I could (chests/caves/buried treasures) was a truly satisfying experience. It felt just right and was never tedious/frustrating.This review would not be complete without me mentioning the fantastic soundtrack! After visiting a certain village, I had a skip in my step and kept singing Wa Wa, WaWaWA! Unless you are speedrunning this game, I strongly suggest taking your time in each area because there's a lot of fantastic ambiance to take in that's only complemented by such a well-placed sountrack. Huge props to the artist(s)!Thank you Matthias Linda, the rest of the team, and the publisher for making sure I can end this year with a masterpiece of a game! After such a beautiful experience trying to 100% this game, I feel confident supporting any future titles from this brilliant developer.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely don't know where to start, this is an absolute masterpiece. This is absolutely, without hyperbole, the indie and RPG GOTY 2022.*Spectacular pixel art, highly detailed for both sprites and backgrounds, yet perfectly nostalgic for the classic 16bit era of jRPGs. This would have been comfortable on the SNES and lauded for its visuals to boot. There was a definite missed opportunity for implementing a lovely scanline or CRT shader, that would have just amped the nostalgia factor \o/*Orchestral soundtrack that was a genuine delight in every single track, melancholic and happy in equal measure.. fabulously composed.*Probably the best classic-style battle system I've seen in a jRPG in a long, long time. Conditional turn-based like in FFX, and even has the same "swap party members in and out on the fly" mechanics too. Being able to swap your characters at will adds enormous layers of strategy and enjoyment. One of my favourite parts of the combat system was how ailments and buffs work, having a departure from the usual "immune to everything" enemy roster -- you can impart buffs and debuffs on any enemy or boss, adding more strategy.Everything about the game just oozes charm, class, style, and absolute talent from the developers. The story is engrossing, mature yet not bleak or overly gritty for the sake of it, just a joy to get wrapped up in - dealing with weighty subjects with characters whose emotions and motivations feel real. Combat is enjoyable, the game pacing is brisk but not rushed, tons of equipment and items, a fabulous "deals" system that has you selling loot in order to acquire rare gear and materials, and even a thoroughly enjoyable "Grid" that rewards exploration and combat prowess.My singular lament is the Gem System, something that had the potential to be truly powerful and enjoyable, a way of customising your characters statistic, allowing you to create and find gems to slot into your weapons/armour. Gems have "purity" and "size" and "rank" - and you have to combine gems in order to unlock stat changes. In reality it just becomes a chore trying to juggle clunky game mechanics and frustrating "purity" or "fake crystals" which can't be merged. So I largely just ignored it.It's fair to say I loved every moment of this (gems notwithstanding, lol) and had I played this prior The Game Awards, or Valve's own Steam Awards, I'd have *happily* rated this RPG GOTY and my own personal GOTY to boot. Fabulous start to finish, a pure delight, and I urge any and all jRPG fans to NOT SLEEP ON THIS.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I've 100% the game, I can give it a fair review. It took around 45 hours to 100% it, ignore the 62 hours (I fell asleep twice playing the game, this is normal for me and not a comment on the state of the game).There are very few games released in the past 10 years or so that I hold with a very high regard. Games that I went into with a high expectation and still came out blown away. Chained Echoes is one of them joining the ranks of other greats like Cross Code and Symphony of War: The Nephilim Saga. You'll notice they're also indie games. The story isn't anything spectacular. It's there, it's well told, it's cohesive. That alone puts it above average. If I had to guess, the dev had multiple ideas of things he wanted to do and tried to mash them all together. For the most part, he did a great job. The story follows a "who to trust?" format. Friends become villains. Villains become anti-heroes. Etc. That said, most of the twists and turns are expected, but how they're often delivered isn't. Most of the characters are fully realized with their motivations well defined. Character personalities are mostly tropey, but not a degree that detracts from the game. For example, you have the steadfast princess, the lost main character, the average bard without the womanizing, and so on. However, quite a few of the sub plot characters just trail off without a true conclusion. I think a lot of this was planned with future content in mind. Being a solo dev is a hard job. Hitting a 7 with as many ideas as the dev was able to fit into this game is really good. Let me itemize a list.Each character plays differently than the rest, giving you a lot of varietyEach character is functional in the way they should be (no character is useless, but a few are a bit better than the rest)I was expecting a lot of monster reskins to pad enemy variety. There's very little.Finding unique monsters is funThe environments are diverse and fun to traverseThe crystal system is one such example. I 100% the game, with ease without ever using them. The Sky Armor system, it's just not thought out and feels 'extra' more like a plot convenience than a game play assetDifficulty. This game is entirely too easy. I've seen a few people post that the game is too hard, but I think that they're just not thinking. They're just trying to out dps stuff. In this game, status and buffs are king. I enjoy that, but I'd like to see the enemies take advantage of that too. An example is with the super boss, I just laid down dots and used paralyze over and over and laughed my way to an easy win. I know the dev is working on NG+, I hope he adds a hard mode or something similar to Cross Code. While every character is viable, character balance and stat balance are atrocious. AGI reigns king over all other stats. It caps at 50, but once you hit about 46-47 you're taking 2 turns to the enemies (even the super boss).Skill balance. Some characters skills are laughably broken. Heroic Ode? Break All? Bee Sting? Completely busted.Passive skill balance is just a bad. There are tons of them, but only a handful as even worth taking. The class system. I'm not sure why this is in the game. It feels largely pointless and just tacked on. I like the idea but not the implementation.Much like the story, the sound design, It just works. I don't have cant think of any memorable tracks or sounds.The art though? It's damn good. Everything from the characters, to the portraits (even the big nose guy), to the back grounds. They're all exceptionally well done. I'd give it a 10 if I didn't hate the rear designs to the Sky Armors (should have just put capes on all of them).I just want to restate how impressed I am with each level's design. Not only that, but the world map design as well. I want to state this clearly, Chained Echoes is my game of the year for 2022. You might look at 31/40 and ask how could I rate it like that. I'm highly critical of games. Anything above of 30 is phenomenal. Especially when I rate many of the games from AAA studios in the low 20s. I highly recommend Chained Echoes for any who enjoys a good turn-based jrpg romp. One final thing. I've seen many say this is a Chrono Trigger (which only rates at 33 for me) successor. It's not. It clearly takes some inspiration, but they both take very different approaches to just about everything.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  is done and dusted. This  is an epic JRPG adventure with a sweeping story where your party tries to prevent an apocalypse while also trying to stop a civil war, helping civilians and solving other mysteries along the way. There is soooo much content, and yet somehow, the download is only 800mb lol. Anyway, it took me about fourty three hours to complete the story and the majority of content.You will have four active characters at a time, but you'll have quite a few unique and fully fleshed out party members by the end of the game. Additionally, at some point, you'll earn a base, where your party members can chill, and where you will also invite a variety of NPCs that provide passive boosts, extra items, storefronts, and so on. And, you'll also be given an airship at that point, making travel around the world much easier and giving you access to new areas. Prior to that, you have to rely exclusively on a fast travel system with teleport points opening up as you find waypoint crystals.This is a loot heavy RPG, and so you'll be leveling up your party members (who thankfully all level up together), unlocking new abilities and buffs. You'll also earn SP, which is used to level up the abilities you know. You will also level up your weapons and armor via use of anvils and materials found or purchased, and can use special crystals found throughout the game to buff your weapons and armor with a variety of abilities and stat boosts.Additionally, you can find secret locations throughout the world that, after proving yourself in battle at these locations, can each offer what is essentially an equip-able secondary class with special abilities and boosts.Battles are turn based, and there are thankfully no random encounters. You might trigger an encounter by entering an area, but for the most part, you can see exactly what you're going to fight ahead of time.Early on, you'll join an Adventurers Guild, and via a rewards board, you earn cash and other stuff by meeting benchmarks, such as finding a certain amount of chests, defeating "x" amount of an enemy type, etc...and will also be rewarded for killing unique monsters that inhabit the world and are functionally optional boss fights.So, with some gameplay specifics out of the way, and as mentioned earlier, this story is truly epic in my opinion. Navigating political intrigue while also dealing with day to day life and several types of apocalypses is a lot to keep track of and this game never loses focus, never forgets where it is, and never writes itself into narrative corners. It was very impressive. The title is also a reflection of the central story premise, but it won't be obvious prior to certain story reveals.The sights and sounds in this game are no less impressive. There are numerous unique locations, impressive representations of abilities and spells in combat, cool music catering to the moments in the game, and just overall vibrancy and life breathed into the setting both graphically and from an audio perspective.It was a fairly seamless experience on the Steam Deck out of the box, and generous with battery life running at about four hours for me. There were instances where the game seemed like it was wanting to lag or stutter, but never quite did. It's kind of weird seeing a game almost bug out and is difficult to describe this better than that. You can just tell when it's on the cusp of lagging. But, like I say, it never quite slipped into bugginess.Recency bias aside, this might genuinely be one of the greatest JRPGs ever made, and certainly the top one in recent memory, which includes contemporaries such as . This was given to me as a gift, but there is no question it earns its asking price. And did I mention that this game was the vision of one person and the majority of work on it seems to have been handled by like three people? Impressive. Give it a look for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: (No spoilers, keeping things out deliberately. Get used to the word pacing, as it is at the heart of the game's design. Read other reviews if you want more, I actually want you to enjoy the game yourself.)Where do I even begin? There exist a lot of Western JRPGs out there that are a fun little journey on their own, but never really go beyond their shell of inspiration. You attack, you level up, you gain stronger attacks, and now you have no use for older attacks as some are plain worse, throw in some references, rinse and repeat. It is rare that a game shows up that makes me not even consider for a second if it's good or bad; I just need it no matter what. The first screenshot and description to "board your mech" were all I needed, and I didn't know what I was even in for. In the troves of western JRPGs that are, for a lack of a better word,  in its delivery but honest in its execution, Chained Echoes is more than that and drags me into its maelstrom to make me feel like I was a kid again who just discovered their first JRPG. While there is a sincere attempt at the love and nostalgia we used to feel while playing these types of games whenever one gets made; Chained Echoes goes above and beyond with thoughtful design and terrific delivery. It wears its inspirations and references on its sleeves and rather than becoming a crutch like so many other games; it fully becomes an identity of its own.Come on, sleepyhead! Wake up! From its opening, you immediately get dragged into the game's coy nature, and your expectations are set right away only to be immediately subverted. Get used to this feeling, since "one more hour" will make you feel like a time traveler after several hours have passed.The plot follows a very well-paced and familiar story, you are a young mercenary who is placed in the middle of a war that has ravaged the world for generations. You are followed by 7 companions in your journey, each united with different sets of goals, all of who contribute to the main plot of the story. There are an additional 4 that can be found that are optional but aren't that engaged in the main plot, except for one which you will know as the plot unfolds.Whenever I became smug and thought I was predicting the plot, it would surprise me and make me awed at how it was all unfolding. Like the previous point about inspiration; the game does so in a very nuanced way that will make anyone familiar with it smile, and it is extremely rare to get a pacing that is this well done as it becomes its own entity. I want more, and the game is fully aware of what it is that I want out of it.Honestly, this game should be in a masterclass education on how to properly pace a game and how to organically meld new gameplay elements along your journey. I'll say it right away, but this game is a natural evolution of how the turn-based JRPG formula should be made, and it isn't afraid to destroy the old to create something truly new and amazing.The tutorial is excellent at introducing you to its Overdrive system, which is the core gameplay loop at its heart and will organically introduce newer elements outside of this system in time, and it has quickly become my favorite system of the genre by far. Simply put; it's a system that requires you to have a balancing act on the abilities you use, and requires a more varied moveset for your party- Use too much of the same ability and the cost goes up across the board and your entire party takes more damage, and it rotates and tells you what you have to use. It breaks down the traditional elements of spamming and stops you from the monotony that haunts the genre.Bringing the best from some other game, such as swapping party members without losing a turn, and then melding that as a core part of its gameplay, is something you'll get used to quickly. Encounters aren't random, a very welcome addition which just adds more to the game's wonderful pacing and the story. This allows me to pick my fights where I want them rather than 30-50 fights before the next story, only to be introduced to yet another welcome addition; full HP/TP recovery after each fight- which forgoes the annoyance of stocking up fully on items or spamming 'attack' to conserve TP. This is needed since the sprite art is amazing, and I always want to see my party do their flashy abilities.The game doesn't follow a conventional leveling system either, instead opting for a split between unlocking points for exploring/doing tasks and following the story. It doesn't use this as an annoying stopgap either, you will never feel like you are held back for a lack of points as long as you play the game right. This ties right into its skill system, with a wide variety of abilities, passives, and stat bonuses to unlock, and while there are no respecs, you do get enough points to unlock everything eventually. All characters might have their intended or traditional role that is familiar to you, but you are allowed to explore other possibilities or use them for other purposes as the game naturally progresses, so a lack of variety isn't a worry either.And then we have the mechas. Oh boy, the mechas. I love me some mechas, pull my Gundams and Xenogears trigger because HOT DAMN. You are better off discovering this part on your own, but it follows the Overdrive a little bit differently while being extremely cool (The mechas, that is).Each soundtrack is beautifully crafted in this game, each song masterfully placed precisely where and when each should be played at any moment. There are some extremely clever uses of transitions, from what themes to use at any given area to what battle theme gets used in any specific environment, to making you invested in any series of events unfolding. Honestly, the main point that it's inspired by SNES and PSX RPGs isn't even a joke, it's like a combination of Breath of Fire 4 meets WildArms in its use of thematics; I keep thinking "man this place had that amazing unique tune" or "damn this boss fight is hype". If the soundtrack wasn't as good as it was to supplement the rest of the game, the game itself would have felt quite in the middle and short of perfect (since a lot of other games tend to have average OSTs).The art style is beautiful, the game keeps introducing new things to look at, and the details placed around the world are mindblowing. Whenever I thought the game was going to get lazy, it instead throws me for a loop and shows me something new in its environmental designs, it honestly baffles me and every new sequence feels completely fresh every single time. I can't fathom how long all of this took, and the style is consistent and beautiful. Enemies range from cute to bizarre, and boss sprites are treated with the respect they deserve for their intended purposes and are always a joy to look at. There are so many design decisions in this game that are just great, the feeling of nostalgia and something new never leaves. Everything from the smallest detail to the most mundane adds up to a level of quality you expected from the old SNES/PSX era JRPGs while pushing beyond that to really captivate a fan of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Chained Echoes

_childDocuments_.review: takes place in war-torn Valandis and narrates the story of a group of individuals of different backgrounds and skills on a quest to stop the atrocities of war and, in a truly heroic fashion, save the world. Mathias Linda, the sole developer of the game successfully created a love letter for old RPGs. In Chained Echoes, you play as Glenn, the main protagonist and de facto leader of a group of mercenaries on a mission to destroy a weapon of mass destruction, restore peace and fight your way through tyrants, monsters, religion and tremendous magic powers.Without spoiling anything, the game’s storytelling is extremely well done, and a lot of effort was put into building a cohesive universe. The lore, deities, places, Matthias Linda really thought of everything. Furthermore, this story is exceptionally well-paced and surprised me at times; expecting a classic scenario, some unexpected plot twist drastically changed the course of the story and this down to the very end.Furthermore, you will be able to play the game with a cast of 12 characters, each with their reason for joining the band and their backstory influencing the main storyline. Sadly, dialogues sometimes feel forced and extended for no reason. While it is great to have a variety of playable characters for a turn-based RPG such as this, their late arrival in the game and their limited use make the character development extremely uneven. Quite frankly, I didn’t try most of them in actual fights. I am sure it was also the case for most players. The Mechanics of the game work well together but can sometimes be frustrating. Beyond the story and the act of “beating” the game, there is much optional content. Including and not limited to a reward board that will push the challenge further for full completion. Chained Echoes has an astonishing amount of content for you to explore, loot, fight etc.In the middle of the story, you will unlock Sky Armour (Mechs), which allows you to fly, discover, and reach new areas of the map previously blocked off. You will also be able to fight with them; it is super fun but eventually becomes a tad tedious as only the same characters can enter mechs. The fighting strategies are extremely limited to a few that shine and many that aren’t useful.But the same can be said for combat in general; turn-based and not very innovative until the overdrive system makes its entry. Imagine a bar that buffs you, while you keep it in the green, granting you better defence and less TP (mana) used for skills and pushing it further into the red zone will do the opposite. To raise or lower your overdrive, you need to use specific actions as requested by the game. I was using the strategy at the right time to facilitate my progression until I completely forgot about this system, ignored it entirely, and wasn’t punished at all (except at 2 specific boss fights).Similarly, you are fighting on foot, and agility is the most important stat to grow for your characters. Defence doesn’t seem to have an impact, and while there are so many variations of builds you can do, some shine, while most of them are not helpful.On the bright side, all your characters level up simultaneously, and you can max out all their skills and talent tree by simply playing, not limiting you in any way should you have made less desirable decisions early on.An interesting mechanic is that each character can be assigned a backup that you can switch out at any time in battle to adjust your strategy. Exciting concept, beneficial at times. On top of that, you also have an Ultra Bar, a super skill that builds up with every attack and is available at every boss fight.Finally, the difficulty will randomly spike, making you wonder what just happened; thankfully, you get to retry battles should you die, which will happen.Chained Echoes won’t let you grind levels and overpower the game; you can only acquire new stats or skills each time you kill a boss. Thus, leaving you at the same level as what was first intended by the game. I greatly appreciated that aspect. Chained Echoes has a pretty big map allowing you to explore every little bit of it, and what a beauty. Pixel games are pretty en vogue and have been for quite a couple of years, but this game doesn't pale compared to some bigger names in the genre. Distinguishing itself with magnificent art, locations, buildings, fauna and flora so rich and diverse with such attention to detail that it all truly comes to life.The Graphics are fantastic, with great animations that are all just contributing to create a general ambience that is to die for.The score of the game and its different track were also fantastic and reminiscent of some of the classic RPG I played a long time ago. Very well done.Chained Echoes was a surprise; I wasn't expecting too much and was blown away by the story and general quality of the game. It is an exceptional game to play, even more so considering that only one person made it. This game is a must play.Game ran great, experienced a few glitches here and there but nothing ground breaking.If you liked this review, you can check my curating page for other games you may like..

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a work of art.  I grew up with FF4, Chrono Trigger, FF6, FF7 etc and since then it's been very hard for me to get into RPGs.  The overall story is incredible and the writing sticks out to me.  While I enjoyed games like Triangle Strategy and DQ11 recently, going into this game all I could think about was how much better the writing is.  It's shockingly good.  Bit of humour in as well had me laughing many times too. The gameplay has additional depth beyond Chrono Trigger and FF6, and it's the modern touches that I really really enjoy.  Makes me think of how Path of Exile did alot of improvements to the Diablo 2 template. Choosing/upgrading skills, the quest rewards, the loot system, slotting equipment/gems etc add tons of customizability/depth but it's not overwhelming.  The music is good, but not great.  Some tracks are super catchy and could land in a Chrono Trigger/FF6, but there is a solid 1/2 of them that are just ok.  That's honestly the major difference for this game vs FF6 and Chrono Trigger in which all tracks are godlike.  TLDR: Great story, gameplay of Chrono Trigger/FF6 with nice modern touches, but the lack of godlike music makes this a solid 9/10 instead of a 10/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Chained Echoes

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best RPGs I've ever played in my life; a definitive tribute to the 90's JRPGs.Chained Echoes is 90's JRPG nostalgia as a game. The best way I can describe the whole experience is: what if Chrono Trigger, Xenogears, Suikoden, Octopath Traveler, SaGa Frontier, Final Fantasy Tactics, Breath of Fire and Legend of Zelda were mashed together by this one brilliant German developer?Easily one of the best RPGs of the year; or rather, of the past decades. It's amazing how  this game feels, managing to capture the essence of 90's RPG but still giving its own spin to the genre. The story and characters are so well written I've actually cried in a couple of moments that really hit the emotional core.Character progress is very different in that you don't actually level up in a traditional way. Instead, you get skill points (called Grimoire Shards) upon defeating bosses or completing certain activities, and said points are used to unlock new abilities, passive skills or straight-up improving stats. You get enough points through the whole game to max out all the characters so there is nothing to worry about it. Killing enemies and completing side-quests nets you SP points, which you spend to upgrade your abilities and passive skills.✅ Very charming and incredibly detailed pixel art.✅ The soundtrack is absolutely mesmerizing. I adore its versatility and how themes have this very "PS1 era music" vibes you'd hear from games like Star Ocean 2, Chrono Cross and Xenogears. Eddie Marianukroh is a brilliant composer and deserves all the praise for giving this game's music such immersion.✅ Combat system is fundamentally simple at its core, yet very engaging and filled with a lot depth. It revolves around the constant use of abilities and swapping between party members.✅ The story is very reminiscent of Final Fantasy Tactics and Xenogears. There is a lot of political tension, backstabbing and surprising twists and revelations.✅ The game has a lot of accessibility options that allow the player to tailor their experience. One notable option is that rather than having an actual difficulty setting, you can adjust the enemy stats and their aggression (how often they use abilities) separately.✅ Exploration feels great, especially after you unlock the Sky Armors (flying giant robots) later down the road. You also get Fast Travel pretty much right off the bat, making sections that require backtracking less draining.✅ A lot of side activities, such as sidequests, hunting unique monsters, completing specific tasks and farming for materials to upgrade equipment.✅ As of May 28th 2023, the game got an update that added New Game+, which, on top of giving the player the option to restart the game while retaining all their equipment and skills, also has an option for an additional much harder difficulty setting, as well a randomizer option for treasure chests.❌ Even with the accessibility options the difficulty is a bit in the extremes: it's either too easy, where enemies hit you like wet noodle, or absurdly hard, where a single hit shaves over half of your HP. There is no in-between.❌ The lack of a proper level up system can make character progression feel a bit slow. The player cannot refund skill points once spent, also.❌>✅ The Crystal Crafting system is interesting on paper, but very convoluted in practice, relying too much on RNG. Luckily, you can play the entire game without touching it once and still finish without many issues. Edit: Matthias said he plans on reworking the system on a future patch. Edit 2: he reworked it!❌>✅ There isn't an option to access past tutorials. Edit: there is now!Even with the very few weaknesses the game is a fantastic experience and nearly flawless. It is outstanding how this was spearheaded by a single individual, aided by some very talented people.  truly is a labor of love and passion for the JRPG genre as a whole, and it shows in every single aspect.Honestly, I'm hoping this game gets a DLC or even a sequel. It's way too good and I'd love to see more of the lore and unravel more of the mysteries.

There are only a couple mechanics that don't quite work but they are very minor stains on a near perfect game.
