_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: I feel really, really bad for not feeling able to recommend this game. It feels like there was a lot of love and care put into making it and the presentation is lovely...But it just kept feeling worst and worst to play. ---I want to start off with the positives. The music was good and enjoyable to listen to, the sound design is great, the spritework was lovely, with the backgrounds being a standout. The atmosphere presented by the many different locales and given to the various cutscenes and other events were fantastic. And I don't think I've encountered a single bug in my 32 hours of playtime. For what I've heard was a solo dev, that's pretty awesome!Also, the game introduces a mechanic I've always had a soft spot for in Act 2--base building!The decision to give a full heal after every battle is a nice little quality of life feature, letting me focus on in-battle tactics and skip fiddling with consumables. (The game *is* balanced around doing so!) And how many games let you both fight with your trusty sword and spells AND a mech?... But. But...First: The combat system.The Overdrive bar, at first, seemed like a cool mechanic to introduce, but by the time I got to act 2, there had only been one fight that tried to make it any more engaging than the basic "stay in the green zone." On top of that, there's a harsh penalty you get for letting your Overdrive bar get too high, and the mechanics seem determined to try and force you into that state whenever it can. What you need to bring the Overdrive bar down with is correlated to RNG. Enemy actions also raise the Overdrive bar. There are bosses who get to act twice, both actions raising the Overdrive bar. The only saving grace is having items that could be used to fulfill the requirement to bring it down... While you're on foot. In Sky Armors, the mechanic tied to the Overdrive bar makes it even harder to manage, AND you don't even have items to force it anywhere!As a result, many major fights ended up feeling either like easy and unengaging, or annoyingly swingy and overwhelming. Even then, that wouldn't have been insurmountable if not for one thing:The game balance itself feels horrendous, with it being simultaneously easy while also constantly putting you at the precipice of a failure spiral.The enemies you fight are generally tanky as hell, and their damage was rarely balanced to account for AoE abilities and multi-hitting attacks. Since most "at-level" enemies deal roughly around 25%-40% of someone's base HP in damage, some enemy compositions can end up just KOing a party member from full health if you have poor RNG. Generally, an annoyance when you face regular enemies.... But it's an absolute pain when it comes to boss fights. If you needed that party member for a part of your strategy, the only thing you can do is hope the RNG would be merciful on you as you try to revive them.Then, when their too-high numbers is combined with the penalty for taking more damage if you don't manage your Overdrive bar, it feels like many boss fights constantly put you a string of bad RNG away from a spiraling fail state.The bosses themselves also, at the end of the day, give very little room to strategize with them. Sure, you could apply status effects on them, and sure, you could debuff their own stats, but that was the extent of it. For most bosses, every ability they seem to get access to has an equal chance of being used at all times--with no way to manipulate what they do. This in of itself isn't a problem... If not for the aforementioned problem where enemy stats just seemed too high for their own good. However, all this wouldn't have been a problem if not for the fact that *the majority of characters were plain just uninteresting.* Except Sienna. Sienna is the best of all the characters I've met, 32 hours in. (And I'm especially critical about having seen cuts of wood with more charisma than Glenn, seeing as he's the protagonist and stole a moment so thoroughly from Sienna, I thought her textbox was given to the wrong character. *huff*) Unfortunately, the game often falls into the trap of *telling* us things about the characters, rather than *showing* us those things, which is why I suspect the characters are falling flat for me. I remember one scene where Lenne's brother is wondering why she was so cold with him, vs the party member he saw her talking to... Which isn't something that was shown at all between them. A lot of the dialogue also felt stilted or forced.  The plot also... While just enough of the events in it were intriguing enough to keep me going for a while, as a whole I can't say the plot engaged me enough that I want to keep going on top of everything else.Everyone else seemed to have already talked about the crystal system, so I don't think I really need to go into that.Last and honestly the least of the problems, the exploration. While the sights are nice and the varied teleport locations are helpful, the scale of things compared to the camera feel a little too close at times, making it easy to miss some paths and chests.  The places that have a map don't have them labeled, even though there are dozens of sites of interest around them. And worst of all are the hidden treasures, where you're supposed to just spam the search button in a radius where two arrows *might* be pointing to--not exactly easy to tell, considering it's all offscreen.All in all, while I'm admittedly being fairly harsh in my review, I also... Just feel like I'm not having fun playing it at this point, and these are my reasons why.For anyone who does pick this game up, I hope you have fun and enjoy yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Trigger aesthetic with a Final Fantasy 6 story and Final Fantasy 10's combat system (with a dash of Xenogears combat). Pretty much sums up what Chained Echos is. Cute throwback RPG but overall combat is probably the most intuitive and best part of the game. Enemy variety could use a lot more work and the Sky Armor inclusion seems like a fun and interesting idea but the SA combat takes away from the much better regular character combat. Characters are okay as well I found 2-3 party members really interesting while MC and the others are meh. (Also IMO the more interesting party members are met half way through the story). Story is okay as well. Wish it could of been more compelling or captivating, but it's a RPG inspired by so many other SNES RPG's of it's time it's not surprising the story also is not as inspired or has it's own way of uniquely special.

_childDocuments_.review: Art: 10/10Music/Sound: 10/10Writing: 10/10Combat system: 8/10Can pet the doggos: 10/10If you have any interest in the genre, play this game. This is easily the best JRPG to have been released in a very, very long time. The story & writing especially is among the best I've seen in any game, period, regardless of genre.HOWEVER...There are some smaller issues, like the gear & crafting system just being WAAAAYYY too grind & luck dependent or the characters being really quite uneven in how useful they are and some are introduced so late you'll have a perfectly oiled party machine already and have no use for them or the game mechanics not being explained at all, forcing you to browse wikis to understand what's going on.And there is one big drawback, at least if you are looking for a fair and balanced challenge:On "easy" (aka low enemy stats in the options), the game is most likely just story mode. Whatever...On "normal" (normal enemy stats), the game is still just way too easy and you can make mistake after mistake and will win any combat just fine anyway.On "hard" (high enemy stats), the majority of the game will actually be adequate in challenge and requires mastery of its systems to a degree. But every now and again, the game throws non-optional stuff in your way that is far and beyond the rest in challenge and even with perfect equipment will still put you in "reload until RNG goes in your favor" territory - that's not true difficulty, that's just bollocks. This holds especially true for the first quarter of the game where you just don't have the means yet to adjust strategies at all and later on in quite a lot of sky armor battles where some enemies will suddenly just entirely overpower you unless you get very lucky RNG-wise.

_childDocuments_.review: Think of every JRPG you've ever played. Chained Echoes somehow manages to hit all of those beats without falling into their same pitfalls.Its like they did a quality of life pass on the last 20 years of JRPGS and created the perfect dish, sprinkled with a dusting of homage and reference to what came before.Story: greatCharacters: interestingBattle system: engaging and difficult without being punishing.Upgrade system, complex without being confusing.If you've EVER enjoyed a JRPG you owe it to yourself to play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not one to write reviews but this game had to be an exception.I bought this game on a whim after seeing a few videos in my recommended saying how good the game was and how under the radar it was flying, and boy were they right.Chained Echoes is extraordinary from start to finish. If you even remotely like turn based rpgs PLEASE at least give this one a try. IT WAS ALSO DEVELOPED BY 1 GUY WHICH IS INSANEEvery piece of this game combines together to become a masterpiece.The art is beautiful and detailed, despite being 16 bit everything feels so alive with detail and personality, Enemy design, attack effects, environments, all of it is beautiful. The music throughout the game does a great job capturing the atmosphere and vibe of the events and surroundings The story is complex and rich and I was left with shock and desire to learn more as layers and connections between characters and events were unveiled The gameplay is satisfying and requires genuine strategy for every encounter, even basic enemies will put a hurt on you if you dont properly manager resources and elements. It evolves more as you get deeper into the game, unlocking more members for your party, learning new attacks, encountering new types of enemiesI dont really have any negatives to say about the game other than maybe some parts of the story are kinda hard to follow, but that could very much just be me.PLEASE give this game your time and money, it deserves every hour and every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: as an avid gamer since i was 3 years old growing up on the SNES ; i have experienced my fair share of RPG's and JRPGS i have to say this game is remarkable and exceeds even the bests IMO.As someone with ADD i usually don't care or can't follow the story or RPGS but with this game i actually care and understand the story along with each characters story/backstory and was so impressed with how unique all the stories were considering how hard it is to be original in fantasy. You will not be let down with any of the story aspects if you try to understand.The combat system is so unique and fun and makes the old style of just spending mana to cast spells feel so outdated.It also incentivizes you to use different characters/and moves to prevent you from just spamming your best move. You eventually are rotating in up to 8 characters as opposed to these other games that give you casts of 8 to 10 characters.. but only lets you use 3 or 4 of them max!It really just seems like this one creator just played all the classic RPGS and thought of every possible quality of life change to make them all better.-Using 8 chars instead of 3-4-Beautiful music and art-Clan Upgrades-Customize characters through armor/gems-Dialogue box's so you know who you need to speak to-Clear maps/fast travels-the few sidequests in the game are meaningful and fun-achievements give in game bonuses-game eventually lets you know where items you need drop from

_childDocuments_.review: The best way I can summarize this game is to say that it is long... which turned out to be almost equally good and bad because the game had good offerings but didn't always put its best foot forward.In general, there is so much going on. While things regarding the main plot do get eventually explained, it gets gummed up by the many sidequests. There is also so many different characters which do make the world building more colorful but kind of diffuse the focus, and this sometimes leads to not knowing what you should be remembering or taking note of which might be vital later. The main plot at it's core, however, does have a pretty cool concept generally speaking although some ideas such as  are not very fleshed out or get breezed over . Complex relationships get established which is good for tension but they are not tactfully resolved such as the odd choice of . Another odd/awkward interaction throughout the game was A side note about side quests, why are they detracting? While they attempt to work on character building, the dialogue ends up getting in the way, being too verbose and trying to tie a moral bow on every action as if it's a present, forgiving characters for their weakness and such. While the message is good, these fetch quests are often all about topics such as:-unholy backtracking-find a ton of npcs to talk to and you have to check every path and room or you can't progressIn addition, the rewards are usually not that good.As I said in my side note about quests, the dialogue always has this charge to it towards proving that every character is righteous and . I guess games and fantasy stories are meant to have happy endings but... well while the writing certainly is not offensive, it's just not well-crafted. The way things are explained and set up leaves so much to be desired. Other reviewers were critical on this point saying "they should have hired a writer to edit and fix it all" but I think that is also symptomatic of the way the plot is structured. You can't simply alter the writing without altering some of the plot decisions. Sure some parts are cringy and I personally did not like the ending (didn't hate it either) but when you construct a world which is of this magnitude you have to eventually start cutting off ends. When designing a game it's always difficult to manage the scope and scale, especially when you are very passionate about the content, wanting to squeeze every last drop and give as much as you can. That being said, I'm not apologizing on behalf of the game for anything but saying that I can understand the troubles of managing such a large world.Here comes one of my biggest complaints: the world is too big. There's too many redundant paths, too many mazelike areas, boring and tedious puzzles . Overall, it just gives a feeling of great impatience because it feels like you're such a small character but there's so much ground to cover. Many items/weapons/etc. are hidden away in secrets too. So you need to check every path to get everything. The worst is when you're trying to find things in your . Even with maps and fast travel... it doesn't help much. Speaking of the maps, as I recall they don't show the details of the place you are, just only exit points. Also there are certain puzzles  which for me just added nothing to my experience other than to annoy me...I actually really like the combat, and while I know others are critical of the overdrive system, well at least it tried something new. However, sometimes it really sticks you in battle when you can do nothing to get out of the red and get wiped because you take extra damage. I don't consider this game hard but that's because I went through and meticulously found every bit of loot and did the crystal system crafting thing which is just honesty too much, basically an inferior materia system. And with that, you can in fact battle in the red all day and still win (just not on higher difficulties). The beginning is a bit of a slog as you have pretty low killing power and no good way to power up so every battle seems to take forever. The hits and moves are fun to watch and feel cathartic on impact, with some very minor exceptions. Two things that really bug me about battling though are: 1. You can't run from a battle? (at least I never found a way to do it or bothered to look it up) It's not made obvious in the battle menu. 2. You can't turn off battle animations? or again, maybe there is.. I don't know but it wasn't obvious from what I could find.Let's get this out of the way: The artwork is great. Everything has a lot of detail, and it's really some of the best pixel art you can find in many regards. The ambience was usually well-constructed and detailed but as I said before just too big and too much. You can only emphasize the point of a hallway so much before the player goes "lucky me, another hallway with nothing in it that I have to run through". That said, I have great respect for the artwork here.The music gives me such torn feelings. On one hand, if you go listen to the OST, you'll find many great tracks: the sound quality being very good and with live recorded instruments the whole way (or at least mostly) as the ending credits allude to. By the way, the ending credits music is simply astounding as a piece of music even outside of video game compositions, very beautiful. And yet, with all this talented work comes the biggest flop from music, that they picked like two or three tracks to heavily reuse. I'd rather mute my game than listen to the Hermit Island theme one more time. That and the battle theme. They could have had other themes for battle (besides times of boss battles) and they could have at least done a variation on the Hermit Island theme because every time you do something the game drags you back to that hell on the island to force you to listen to that music again while you mash through the pages of dialogue. Now, objectively speaking, it's a good piece of music but come on man, you can't feed me that the entire game for hundreds of hours then give me really bomb stuff in the credits... that's not fair.While I might sound like I hate this game, I did have a decent time playing it. I think it could stand to be an overall shorter experience - cut down the map sizes, cut down the dialogue, don't put in time wasting side quests. In the end, this project was overly ambitious. Maybe the designers spent years making this game and know every part of it so well, but normal people will spend .. maybe 90 hours? Especially since the game is so long, getting busy with life and coming back to it and having no idea where in the hell you are or what you need to do next (yes I hear you, the quest log) is disorienting. Also, just some feedback here, please stop doing so many red and white screen flashes, it hurts my eyes.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't quite finished the game yet, but if you like RPGs cozier than a mug of hot chocolate on the perfect snow day when school got canceled and it was a video game marathon in your childhood bedroom (RIDICULOUSLY COZY), then buy this one on site because it's worth at least five bucks more than what they are charging for it at full price I would say.  Graphics are super basic but not offensive on the eyes.  Super unique take on turn based combat that is actually quite challenging as long as you don't fiddle with that difficulty slider and set the enemies stats on "Low" and make them less aggressive with yet another slider for making the game accessible.  Trust me on this:  if you leave the difficulty exactly where it is at by default you can expect a tough time at different moments in the story.  Almost without question be prepared for some wipes even during the games first Act (it's kinda long....).  8.75 // 10 = just give them your money already

_childDocuments_.review: Picked this game up on a whim. I knew nothing about it, but I was craving an old-school RPG. Reminds me a bit of Chrono Trigger. Beautiful art direction, fun combat system and interesting and different enemies. It also allows you to explore without feeling like you're just getting hammered with random encounters as the enemies are one and done. You don't need to grind to level as your skills/levels are tied to bosses. This game seems to respect your time, which is great as I don't have nearly as much time nowadays.My only complaint so far is that your active character is incredibly fast for some reason. It's like you're running to every location at 2x speed. I'm glad I don't have to turn on auto run, but it just feels too fast.Plays well on the steam deck although I have noticed tiny bits of slow down randomly that I assume will be smoothed out with a patch.

_childDocuments_.review: ---- I WAS IN THE EARLY ALPHA RELEASE ----TL;DR THIS GAME IS THE BEST JRPG IN RECENT YEARS IF YOU DO NOT BUY THIS GAME, SLEEP WITH ONE EYE OPEN IM KIDDING JUST BUY THE BLODDY GAME10/10Since the day i backed this game on kickstarter i had really high hopes for it. A pixel art, turned based, class based rpg with a deep story, it was my dream game and boy has it turned into one. Once the alpha released i was playing none stop with no breaks in between. The way all the characters, battle systems, writing and the world building is just perfect.The games combat opens as a traditional turn based party rpg which seems boring to some but this game does something that makes genuinely all the battles in this game engaging, challenging and new. This mechanic is called the  if i went into this mechanic here, This would probably take up your entire screen but just know it is a really good mechanic that makes turn based combat make you think about your abilities carefully no matter where you are in the game.The story and its characters are also a sight to behold, there's the standard jrpg protag who becomes a lot more than just the protrag, the nerd, missfit, elder who has infinite knowledge. All those classic tropes are present in the characters but are barely seen in their writing after spending a few hours with the whole cast. And if you think its gonna be like any other jrpg where u breeze through the game with the same team you had in the beginning you are dead wrong. Not only are characters you gain later just better than others, some are also a lot better in late game than early game and the games challenges and bosses will force you to swap your team formation or at-least make you think of a different strategy. The whole cast is able to shine multiple times throughout the game in both their character and their battle power.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: For me this game was 10/10 for 95% of my playtime, but the ending was written pretty horribly. Very sad, with some better writing in the final act this would've been on the same tier as 90s snes JRPGs. Especially disappointing since a lot of this game was written very well up until the last bit. I understand what the game was trying to go for themetically but it just didn't work, at least not for me. Bummed out I have to leave this game with a sour feeling, man...For a first game this is incredible though and I still had an insane amount of fun playing through the game. It does A LOT of things right and I thought the ensemble cast were all pretty decent. It seems like Mathias is setting up a sequel but I would actually prefer seeing him work on a different IP for his next game because of my feelings towards the ending.Either way I'd still definitely recommend a playthrough if you're a fan of JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: The game was going great. It was everything I'd want from this style of RPG. Then I completed Act 1 and Sky Armors became a part of the game. At first this seemed like a good thing, but actually it changed the entire dynamic of the gameplay.Sky Armors have their own combat. Compared to the normal combat it is INCREDIBLY tedious. Thanks to the Gears system, every battle is as drawn out as a boss fight but with none of the hype. And god help you if you accidentally enter combat sans Sky Armors with enemies intended to be fought via Sky Armors. It's game over, and it's easy to stumble into if you're just trying to explore the area.  Speaking of exploring the area....Sky Armors change what you can do and where you can go in any given area. Sweet, so I can fly my way into previously inaccessible areas and find new gear, etc. Sounds great! But it also turns every single zone of every single area into an amazingly boring and tedious GRID SEARCH. Gotta make sure you covered every inch of ground that's only accessible in your Sky Armors otherwise who knows what you could miss besides more painfully long and boring battles with enemies you could have avoided if the camera kept up. And in areas with water: If you're in hover mode moving over large areas of water it's impossible to tell if you're going to exit into another zone until it's too late.I was loving the game up to this point, but after two hours with the Sky Armors... I'm done.

Take up your sword, channel your magic or board your Mech. Chained Echoes is a 16-bit SNES style RPG set in a fantasy world where dragons are as common as piloted mechanical suits. Can you bring peace to a continent where war has been waged for generations and betrayal lurks around every corner?

Chained Echoes is a story-driven game where a group of heroes travel around the vast continent of Valandis to bring an end to the war between its three kingdoms. _childDocuments_.review: Everhood is an unconventional, rhythm battle based rpg with themes of psychedelic spirituality and philosophy at the core of its narrative. it does get a lot of comparison to Undertale, and it's easy to see why. it has a lot of the same spirit/personality, but i feel like the intensity is turned up a few notches. there was nothing particularly 'inappropriate' in the subject matter that i recall, but it felt very much aimed at a more mature audience, particularly those interested in deeper thinking and philosophy. i went into the game essentially blind, and have played through once as of writing this. it was a wild ride, a pensive experience - and it is clear that there is still more left for me to go back to experience if i like, which is really exciting. i get why some people argue that it's not a 'true' rhythm game, but i don't exactly agree. i'd still call it a rhythm game - it just approaches how rhythm is woven into the game mechanics differently. instead of moving 'on beat' or 'with' the music like in a conventional rhythm game, it is more like you are dodging the sounds, in an abstract sense. i found it really interesting and satisfying to play, and in my opinion, the soundtrack is really phenomenal, with a good range of genres and styles represented. as a massive bonus, it also has a great range of difficulty settings that you can change at ANY point during your playthrough, which makes it accessible for gamers of a wide range of experience and skill levels. if that sounds cool to you at all, i beg of you, just play it, and for the best experience, with as little prior knowledge as you can.

_childDocuments_.review: So I beat the game in roughly 9 hours give or take given breaks with just leaving the thing open.  Let me start by saying this, when the game says seizure warning, it's not joking, be warned.  Let me follow up by saying this is one of the most stress inducing nightmares of a game I have ever played.  Don't get me wrong not, it is incredibly fun but it honestly does make me question constantly what I'm actually doing.  This is, at it's core, a beat game.  It functions on the same line as guitar hero, DDR, and many other I've played in the past, but at the same time, it is nothing like any other beat game I've ever encountered.  Each "battle" is a unique experience with visuals that will make you question which pill you actually took.  The graphics in this game are beautifully crafted and it carries a likeness to Undertale, both visually and in story telling. _childDocuments_.review: This game isn’t long, and it doesn’t cost much either, but it sure gives a lot to the player. Everhood is such an experience.Firstly, the soundtrack and sound design is outstanding and one of the largest and best put together I’ve seen. The narrative is full of charming characters you meet, which all have wonderful wacky designs by the way, and it gives you a lot to think about by the end. There are 6 endings in total, which are all great, although some require more willpower to complete than others. Another factor of praise is the actual gameplay itself. Everhood has several bosses and they are all so fun and unique from one another. The music-based dodging, weaving, and attack-absorbing never get old and provides something I haven’t really seen before in a game. Playing this game is exciting and can be challenging, however you have the ability to change the difficulty if you so choose. The game’s visuals can also be spectacular, enhancing the gameplay significantly, but I would stay away if you are highly photosensitive. Lastly, I want to touch on replayability. Everhood is more of a one-and-done type of game, but you can, if you wish, re-fight any boss or play the game again on a higher difficulty. Like I said earlier, there are multiple endings you could do as well, not even to mention the vast list of achievements you can hunt for.Anyhow, you would love Everhood if you are a big fan of games such as UNDERTALE (yeah I had to mention it). Absolutely one of my favorite games to release this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Easily a "Game of the Year" contender for me so far this year, personally. Go in blind if you can -- watch the trailer, and if you like what you see and hear, go for it. It hasn't been since Undertale that a game has finished rolling the credits and left me feeling numb and thinking about some heavy stuff, in a good way. Yet here I stand. Undertale is the obvious comparison but you would do yourself a disservice to dismiss it as such. There's something really special here, and for ten bucks, it's worth experiencing.Everhood draws you in with its style and vibes, stringing you from event to event with almost no real rhyme or reason, before turning around and asking you to get serious, to think about what you're doing and why you're here. That's what the game meant to -me-, anyway.  I didn't expect a game that drew me in via art style, good jams, and some cute character designs to really make me think about games and experiences, and then to stir in some existentialism along the way. Other players might not see it as such, and I think that's part of the appeal -- it doesn't have to be serious, it may just be a game to the player, and that's a-okay.Plenty of difficulty settings, and yet even at its lowest (and you may need to turn it down that far for some fights!), it provides a challenge. Color-blind and photo-sensitivity options are highly appreciated for players who need them. Great little story that leaves enough wiggle room to take from it what you want, maybe even what you need, in the moment. Fantastic visuals; quick, simple, empty yet purposefully so, and yet just enough to paint a picture along with some breathtaking in-fight effects. Charming moments with a colorful cast, whom I only wish could get more screen time and depth. A few "post-game" little secrets and exploration. Lots of "No Hit" achievements for completionists that, uh, whoof, yeah, I'm definitely not good enough to get...!! (Respect to those who can, especially some of the big bosses!)Everhood truly deserves your attention. Please give it if you can. My only big complaint is that I'm left wanting more from these Foreign Gnomes. This was a joy from start to finish.

_childDocuments_.review: This is absolutely one of the best and most engaging games I've ever played. This game is a 10/10 without any argument. I don't do serious reviews, ever, but this is a game that deserves a real review.Let's go over the combat/gameplay itself, ignoring the story for now.-The game has a simple/relatively linear overworld with a hub to different parts of the map. (Being vague to avoid spoilers)-The overworld is very simple, tiles that comprise the environment are very minimal, however the illustrations for the backgrounds and sprites are incredible and full of inspiration. (This is where the Undertale comparisons come in, yes they are visually very similar. Story and gameplay wise, they are both very diverse and unique.)-You engage in "combat" by interacting with other characters on the map, there are little to 0 random encounters.-The combat itself is a pseudo dance battle where you have to dodge attacks summoned on time to the music-IMPORTANT: I see many other reviews going over how you have to dodge "off-beat." These reviewers have either never heard of triplets and articulation, or were just very upset during their review. The minimal times you may have to dodge "off-beat", are simply just 16th and 32nd notes, or other decorations in the track. You can see and hear every single attack that comes at you. Get good.-The difficulty in this game ramps up PERFECTLY. I have never felt better after beating a hard boss only to find out there's another that builds on the mechanics the last one did amazingly. Everhood teaches you slowly how to play, while dropping mechanics on you suddenly that change the game ENTIRELY.---SOME STORY SPOILERS BELOW. I TRIED TO HOLD BACK, BUT YOU WERE WARNED---Moving on from the actual gameplay, which is amazing, the story itself is really what captivated me. I don't even like rhythm games, but this game moved me to complete nearly every ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ impossible challenge it had. The Absolute Truths the game's narrator/deity tells you have so much meaning within the game, and in real life. It feels as if the developers are trying to reach out to you, for all the hard work you put into 100%ing their game. The initial facade of having Gold Pig be the enemy, only to turn out he was protecting everyone from, well, you. Getting your arm and realizing what had to be done (Killing the characters you've befriended so far) left me in shock for a solid 5-10 minutes. Denying that "destiny" and battling Frog's Wrath took me forever, and once I had done it I went back to finish the game the right way. And then I did it again all the way through to experience the NG+. Then I went back and I am doing it again hitless. This game has left me obsessed. I want nothing more than for the developers to know that they have made a masterpiece of a game and that this experience will never leave my mind. Thank you Everhood, for changing the way I think.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not another undertale clone, an undertale like as many may think. It is also not a rythm game which I have heard many times too, which is easy to assume from the videos on the store page. This game is its own beast, an anti rythm game were you fight the beat and a story that goes its own route and doesn't mimic other more popular games. This game is hard, it will test your skills of dodging and other things, it will push you to furstration if you seek optional bosses that is has in spades, but in the end it is all worthwhile.The story does its own thing and takes awhile to get going. You spend part of the game in darkness wondering what is going on. Wandering through world and character building before things suddenly hit the gas and you are taken on a wild roller coaster ride. This is not undertale, do not expect the same thing but you can expect emotional moments and heart questions. While not all the characters get enough development they get enough to matter to the story and your heart.The battle system works well even if difficult and each battle is unique in both musical themes and patterns. Learning each song and how to beat each foe is actually worthwhile even if you may pull hairs out at some of the more difficult battles. The story is well worth every moment, the post game and super bosses are a wonderful set of fights and challenges, and the soundtrack will stick with you for ages!The only downsides to the game I found were instances of dropping inputs and lag during some really intense battles, but these only reared their head on two super bosses and mostly only caused trouble in one in particular. They did cause trouble for me on my no hit 100% run, but unless you intend to go for that crazy challenge you have nothing to worry about. Some characters needing more time in the light is also something I wish but it wasn't a major issue in the end.What this game has in its challenge is something I haven't found since beating star ocean 2 hard stuff, or when I beat I want to be the Guy. Beating the optional bosses, going full no hits is a satisfying feeling that few games manage to hit. Many games are hard but leave you wanting, this game leaves you feeling like you want to throw a party after you finally beat that one crazy boss, get through that one intense song no hit, and even watching the credits roll on a normal playthrough. Do not pass this game up, its worth the praise and your time, you won't forget it in a long while.

_childDocuments_.review: Pinniochio in Psychedelic Purgatory: the Rock Opera Adventure. OR: I walked backwards into hell, and felt euphoria as I became privvy to the Divine TruthsFirst, I want to say to the developers and anyone else that this has quickly become one of my all time favorite games. Currently writing I have personally never felt a greater emotional attachment to an experience with a piece of software. Perhaps it is the extreme idiosyncratic nature of it, perhaps it is the deeply intriguing storyline, mostly however it is a combination of those in addition to some of the most outstanding psychedelic visuals I have ever seen, particularly in the finale sequence, and a killer soundtrack that combines many genres but focuses mostly to being as bangers as possible. I will be upfront and say this game comes with a boatload of trigger warnings, and thus the aforementioned idiosyncratic nature of it may not appeal to everyone, however I feel it nessecary to indicate potential content warnings here as I would hate for people to be triggered: epilepsy is the big one, I myself have mild stutter based epilepsy and it didn't cause health problems or anything but my case is not universal. Anyway. That is a hard warning on epilepsy. I do it because The Incredibles 2 did not, lmao (that's an example of the kind of visuals that trigger me personally. An aside ) Other things include (spoilers): aracnaphobia, misophonia (screeches, unsettling sounds), themes of death, immortality, suicide. Some game mechanics are not immediately intuitive and puzzles require some pretty clever but sometimes obtuse solutions. Direction is not always super clear either. People have complained of performance issues but I am leaving this review after playing the switch port, which played smoothly other than some awkwardly long loading times here and there. What I have played of PC so far runs smooth but as of writing, performance for me was fine (my pc is a lowend budget build). There is a difficulty to it. Even playing on easier modes, it can be quite unforgiving. If you're a fan of hard games (I am but I suck at them) and rhythm games (this is, uh, Not? That? Almost functions as half walking sim, half rhythm Game, dodgy shoot em up kinda feels. Truly unique gameplay I think. Constantly switches things up, too. But yes I also adore rhythm games, and yes i also do suck at those too.), half of it is that. The devs troll you with puzzles. It's truly a wild experience as it advertises, one of a kind. And yet, however....This game wears, much like its heart,, its references, on its sleeve. If you are not into that kind of thing, you will probably be annoyed by this game. It also loves to delv into meta, as many puzzles and interactions are references to the UI of the game itself. Personally, I'm not wild about meta but I appreciate the ernestness here, so I'm willing to roll with whatever this game throws at me because every turn feels unexpected, fresh, funky, somber, and wildly intelligent, with boldly sincere ludonarrative choices, script and art direction. If you like Geno from super Mario Brothers, which, guess what, narrator here LOVES Geno from Super Mario Brothers, this is functionally the game you've always wanted that Nintendo could never make because Square has held Geno hostage in some kind of underground torture facility since 1995. Turns out they were rather right to do so, because when that puppet is out serving a higher authroity, he can be quite dangerous. Narrarively it borrows much from its sources but I would argue there's proof the writers have spent time thinking about the implications of their source materials worlds, and that reflection casts itself back to create this, experience that is wholly unique even if we know Red is Geno and "Gaster" (who was based on Uboa from Yume Nikki or princess mononokes forest spirits), and some kind of disco Marceline character who changes their identity frequently, skeleton brothers- well undead brothers, really -We have to remember in the creation and consumption of media sometimes, influences and archetypes are ever present and Everhood almost itself is a realm that would indulge in the idea of self referential material. It makes for this very Jungian experience of friendly archetypes we're familiar with, which works well with this setting of an immortal realm. Thats not to say the personalities we do meet aren't expounded upon - they are, heavily, and become uniquely their own.(Spoiler) if my theory is to be believed this world is a purgatory where people have made their own artificial vessels and as time has made them bored (though some seem to be having a good time) while typical strains of the Pinocchio myth are thrown in about questions of identity and death - and probably even more so towards Timothy Learys concept of the Ego Death, or the return to the collective soup of unconcious being. Undertale will probably always be a reccomendation even by its own reference to it so comparisons to it will be littered through here. It feels like the developers were emboldened by Toby Foxs spirit in game development (his creative energy is rather infectious) and shared many similar ideas, but this feels far more aimed towards a maturer audience (references to the things I mentioned in the trigger warning list) and focused on achieving this feeling that its predecesors have as well. Yume nikki. Lisa. Earthbound. Toby's games. super Mario rpg in its humor, Cat Soup in its psychedellic depressive vibes, all this cool indie cult classicy kinda mash up soup.  bizarre antics and then these characters who have surprising depth the further you go. It has been 6 years since Undertale came out, and the developers for Everhood have called a lot of the "what ifs" that fans of that game ask, an answer in their own game. (What if No Mercy was forced, for example? What if going against destiny is the wrong thing to do? Why is Death such a Bad Thing? etc!)And the further along you progress, the smarter the story gets, the more complex the narrative threads and characters. This game knows how to write compelling literature and that wasn't an element I expecting but god am I so glad for it. Literally my pea brain saw Red's design flipping around some frets on a streamers videocapture (shoutout to based fellow tampa native Charles White, thank you for being witty and having good taste and your Floridian comisery.) one night and went "oh i like." But the experience I got in exchange was, so, so much more than that (but the tetris effect won't let that image disappear from my eyelids quite yet haha.)I hear there are multiple endings and one requires a 3 hour long trek. I'm not done with the game at the time of reviewing. You bet your sweet ass I am going to find out the Ultimate Truth. I found a way to deal with some of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in other games, I may not be great at games but I want to see whatever imagery these guys put on screen so it compels me to seek out all the alternative routes. I am going to be following these developers projects very closely. If this is their debut, their next project will be ... ... I would hate to force expectations, like if you just made a magnum opus like this it'd be perfectly alright to retire, but I just once again want to say thank you to the developers for putting your heart on display for the world to see. I see it. I have dealt with struggles similar to the ones in the stories this game articulates about anxiety and depression, existentialism and dread, dissociation and all the heavy themes that were risky to include narratively - I'm certaintly glad you took the risks you did. May update this review as I get further along the story but yeah. Tl;dr: haha pinocchio myth done well make brain go brrr.edit i beat the game on the switch version and the ending made me cry and the last time i cried from an ending to a videogame was when i originally played mother 3 and this made me cry like a LOT 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.So this was a game I fully expected to enjoy. I love games breaking the fourth wall, meta-jokes, and clever writing, and it certainly seemed like this game had all of that. So I grabbed it on a sale and booted it up.To start off, I was a little annoyed about the prompt that requires you to "abandon your humanity." In my opinion, it's a bit of a lazy way to introduce the idea of player character-player dissonance. In a slight protest, I wrote a ten line bot that just auto-played the game by pressing semi-random keys from main menu to first scene, then I took over after the bot had played through the bit I refused to.Then... the battles. Now, I'm not great at the fights. I took my sweet time through a bunch of deaths on probably easy encounters, retrying the Incinerator a bunch, and talking to everyone, but in two hours, I only really found one of the first four fights somewhat enjoyable. The others were... tedious. The music was sometimes good, but the game seems to frontload the fights and backload the characterization. That's fine in a game like Undertale, but when every one of the first few fights is scripted and lasts a minimum of X minutes, I found myself wondering why I should care about any of them when I didn't know who any of these people (entities?) were.And then... there's the Incinerator. Now, this was actually the fight I enjoyed the most; it was slightly unconventional, with a soundtrack that had more traditional battle music than the more techno-y backgrounds of the other songs (from what I recall; I'm writing this review a few months later). The thing is... .When the game decided to have random cosmic entities attack the avatar without explanation and to have gnomes explode all over the screen with technicolor lights, I realized this game prioritized its odd aestheitc over storytelling or characterization, so I uninstalled it.If you find yourself enjoying the fights, and if you go in liking the game for its aesthetics and not just its promises of forth wall breaking, then go for it. Otherwise, you're better off not buying this game, or taking "Purple Mage's" advice and refunding the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Someone tell me why this game isn't a cultural phenomenon. I mean that without any irony. This game is just... it's art. You NEED to go in with as little info as possible. The difficulty can be a bit wonky at times, but it's not terrible. You might struggle with one battle, then blow the next ten out of the water. I played it though on hard to start, so maybe that was my own fault. Hard is the mode the game defaults to, so that's what I went with.The story... This game makes you ask some interesting questions. I'm not talking about main narrative either. There is an A story that has heavy philosophy, but there's also a B story. That B story comments on video games and your perspective as the hero. I'm not spoiling too much here, because it goes WAY deeper than that, but that story made me question things about games that I take for granted. Some games have come close to this in examining the role of a player in a game world, but this one manages to really put a spotlight on it, and... man, I almost don't want to play another game... It's just... It's good. Buy it.PS. This game was DEFINITELY brought to us by hard drugs. There's just no way that some of this stuff came from a completely lucid mind. I'm personally against drugs. I don't have a problem if that's what you choose to do, but I wouldn't do them, and I wouldn't want my loved ones to get involved with it. That said... I don't think I've ever been thankful for the existence of drugs. This game makes me question that as well....

_childDocuments_.review: I want to emphasise that I think Everhood is a quality effort and I feel a bit bad for this verdict but ultimately if someone asked me "should I spend $10 on this" I'd make a vague non-committal grunting noise rather than a confident "Yes".I have a laundry list of complaints from minor to moderate that ultimately keep the game from being Great, which is a shame because it has strong core mechanics and the soundtrack to back it up.- Weird lack of resolution options. Fullscreen changes between 16:9 in menus and 4:3 in gameplay. Windowed mode is like, 480p with no option for window resizing making it impractical to play on.- The connective tissue of the narrative is in general really weak and the game lacks the strong worldbuilding I think it wants to have? Stuff just kind of happens and I walked through the game and its characters not really getting a sense of a cohesive narrative and not really engaging with the questions I think it wants to ask players.- Further to that, the script is littered with typographical errors. A lot! I was finding them very regularly. Missing words, wrong words, incorrect spellings, apostrophe use, the whole nine yards. Script could do with another editing pass.- Halfway through the game it introduces a "parry/reflect" mechanic, but the delay on how often you can perform this action is inexplicably tied to the difficulty setting. So the controls become less responsive the higher your difficulty is? This sure is a choice! I understand the balance concern since you don't want people spamming it to trivialise patterns, but making it less responsive isn't striking a good middle groundSuggested: successful parries cut recovery time down, maybe by half or something. Punishes mis-times but successful parries are rewarded. Not sure how that would actually play out, but I'm not crazy about the current system.- The reflect move also has a deadzone directly on top of the player where you can fire a projectile back at the enemy while a projectile is almost on top of you, you'll get the projectile off successfully, but you'll also eat a hit that you probably didn't expect to since the reflected projectile usually destroys incoming bullets.- In order to successfully reflect, you need to parry two bullets of the same colour. But getting hit will erase your current charge. I don't really know what this adds and I just found it frustrating. I don't have a suggested fix here, I just found this made me press Reflect expecting to fire a projectile only to get nothing because I hit something in the last fraction of a second and my charge was taken away as a result. Personal, yes, but I did mostly just find that irritating.- a lot of the environments are visually simplistic and sometimes go on for too long. sometimes the style is really charming and strong, but all too often it's "single colour path in a black void". Occasionally feels like padding.- game does a fakeout ending thing like four times which makes the actual conclusion feel incredibly exhausting and not in a good way- THIS ONE IS ACTUALLY A PRETTY LARGE SPOILER: the pixel art Buddha at the end is hysterically funny and I don't think it's meant to be. The other elements weren't going to add up to a conclusion that had a large emotional impact regardless, but this blunt rendition of just deadass The Actual Buddha took it to a level where it caused me to break into a full on laughing fit. I do not think this was the intent.- The music is technically proficient but lacks much emotional resonance which kinda ties back into the "narrative is weak" thing. This makes battles all kind of blend together somewhat.- the difficulty settings don't tug on the right parameters. Projectile patterns never change, just enemy/player health and how easy it is to spam the parry when you get it. This doesn't really give a good experience to people who aren't proficient at not being where bullet is. I know it's hard to chart all the patterns per difficulty but I think consistent mechanics with different patterns is a stronger solution here, however conventional that may be.Despite this, it's not a game that I think lacks heart. It has many positive qualities, the jokes occasionally land well, the music in fights is scored well and patterns feel appropriate for their music. Many of the fight gimmicks are also disarming and fun to muddle through. But a quality effort doesn't inherently equate to a quality game.

_childDocuments_.review: It drives me insane when it comes to talking about these sorts of games since it always feels like a total minefield about how much I can say before I get into some pretty serious spoiler territory. It's especially the case when it comes to a game I find as cool as this one because it makes me all the more determined to insist on not contributing to the endless sea of spoilers that is the internet. With that said though, wow, what a great game, one that manages to walk that line perfectly between representing its influences prominently while also going for a style and approach that's wholly distinct and its own. It's a game that not only represents the inherent flaws in calling a game inspired by something else a "[blank] clone", but is also able to demonstrate the sheer versatility of games as an artform with how much variety and incredibly distinct characteristic there can be in even the most similar looking experience. I'd say that it also conveys that games shouldn't be so inherently opposed to stylistically following in the footsteps of others if they have something unique of their own to bring to the table, and this definitely has a lot of interesting stuff to say.While one of the most popular summaries I've seen of this game falls somewhere along the line of "Undertale meets rhythm games", I'd argue that this is only true on the most superficial level both thematically and mechanically. In terms of mechanics, while there's clearly a rhythm game aesthetic that's intrinsically tied to this, with the enemies summoning obstacles in accordance to the music along with the arena you fight everyone in being reminiscent of a Guitar Hero chart, this is far closer to a bullet hell than it is a true rhythm game. This goes all the way to the point where there are some section that feel as if the player's actions are totally disconnected to the music going on, and while those who expected a proper rhythm game would probably find this an odd or downright terrible decision, it's something that becomes much easier to appreciate if you're able to take it as a very stylish bullet hell that's intrinsically linked to the soundtrack. It also helps that the combat itself feels so fun, with your character's movement being largely fast and very responsive, which is a must for a game that gets as chaotic and fast paced as this one. The way it's able to better represent the characters themselves and bring forth a lot of interesting mechanical challenges is also really neat.Rarely does it feel as if two fights can be approached in a similar way, whether it's because of certain patterns forcing the player to act in a certain way, a type of obstacle unique to a certain fight, or even just in the more nuanced areas of how the player needs to respond to any given situation in front of them, almost every battle feels wholly unique and entertaining. The exception to this is when a certain element gets introduced about halfway into the game and throws some of the difficulty balancing a bit off, almost going against the core gameplay loop in the process, but fortunately the times which this additional element reveals its more negative connotations are relatively uncommon and are able to actually add to some of the best moments in the game. Overall, this element is a bit of a double edged sword but mostly works out well, so the bad points it brings to the table are largely an acceptable tradeoff. I also am a big fan of the way this game handles difficulty for the most part as well, having a really smooth difficulty curve at the start and getting absolutely brutal by the end, but also feeling as if it can get pretty interesting with things to further solidify the narrative side of things. Occasionally you'll just get put up against something that feels far beyond what everything else is, or uncharacteristically easy, but it always feels fitting from a narrative perspective and serves to strengthen the relationship between these combat sections and the overworld, reinforcing the way that these are 2 parts of the same world and not separate entities that only coexist for the sake of providing some more cohesion to the experience. At the same time, the devs also understand that putting in some optional superbosses is a really fun time and one that is able to transcend any semblance of such a difficulty curve to create some moments of pure insanity for those who are looking for the game's mechanics to be pushed to their absolute limits.Cohesion on the whole is something that this game has a ton of in ways similar to this, which is surprising given how abstract and psychedelic it can often get. You have a bunch of these moments that go completely off the rails visually and yet, once you begin to better understand the game and its world, none of this ever feels entirely out of nowhere, it all has a reason to exist and is all integral to how the game functions. Being able to craft multiple encounters that reach incredible levels of flashiness and creativity in the way that this game does, all without sacrificing any part of its identity or feeling superfluous is one of its strongest characteristics from where I stand.The abstract nature of Everhood's presentation is also very strong in the way it contributes to its surreal atmosphere along with some of its deeper narrative themes. The world feels so sparse, yet full of colour in a way that you never feel able to get a full grasp on the situation. It's hard to tell how happy a lot of these characters really are and how much they're merely trying to pass time in the endless expanse of nothingness that they live in. The more atmospheric approach to the world design here often also feels more reminiscent of games like Yume Nikki beyond anything else, which is a massive plus in my eyes, especially one that understands how to use the surreal, often nonsensical composition of the world to its benefit. Beyond the artstyle and vibe of some of the comedy, I really cannot say in good faith that this is an Undertale clone either, especially from a thematic standpoint and the way that while Undertale focused on the concept of humanising fictional entities and the player's relationship with their protagonist character, Everhood instead uses the medium to ponder more abstract concepts relating to the nature of existence itself. I was surprised with the way that this game would often reflect a lot of Buddhist ideologies about what life truly is, and what it means to exist, using an interactive medium to allow the audience to become further immersed in the world that was created in an attempt to allow them to more strongly question what the game was telling them. This also served to strengthen the moral dilemma that the player is then faced with, as while there is a "true ending" so to speak, it's not particularly black and white in what is considered the morally correct option, which can be seen both as a way to make the game feel less didactic on the whole, and also could be seen as representing the endlessly complex and nuanced nature of life itself.Overall, Everhood is a game that subverts so many expectations and does so in a constantly engaging way. What might seem like something that wears its influences a bit too heavily on its sleeve to begin with quickly evolves into something wholly unique. There are so many idiosyncrasies present here, ranging from the intentionally sparse overworld being contrasted by these high octane, sensory overload inducing combat sequences, to the way that the game keeps itself so vague without feeling as if it's being contrived about it. Everhood is a careful balancing act that feels as if it could easily have fallen apart at every step of the way, yet rarely does so, and it's truly an amazing experience that I would recommend wholeheartedly. Don't be deterred by the game's surface level appearance, there's so much more to it.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wild ride, of ups and downs. A two act game that takes you places where you never thought you would go and routes you didn't want to but needed to go down. Death comes for us all, we're human. But as humans we get to live through the chaos of the world and take it all one. Say, if we were timeless. Never died, never aged, what's there to see? What's there to experience? The zeal and lust of life fades when there's nothing to live for, nothing to live through. No expiration date nothing to do. Yes, death is scary and inevitable. Some feel regret, sadness, anger, joy, and content. But mortality is something taken for granted of. Nothing is forever, but even then there may not always be an end.

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty easy, characters are forgettable, story is pretentious with no real payoff.Also I HATE to compare it to Undertale, this game does take it's own creative risks which I think does separate it from Undertale. However, in regards to meta-analysis, Undertale does a better job than this game while also creating a story with payoff. Sometimes, this game gets so meta it makes my eyes roll, as if the developers want you to know how clever and meta they are while having you aimlessly walk around the world killing shallow characters.Learning the battle system is fun; however, once you understand the mechanics there is no development, making battle become stale VERY quickly.The only good thing I have to say about this game is that the soundtrack bops. I found that the only thing keeping me going in this boring game is to find out what the next song sounds like.Tbh, I came into the game hoping it would scratch the same itch Undertale did; that is the tragedy with this game. Maybe if I didn't think that way I would have enjoyed the game more for its own merits. However, as an experience separate from Undertale, I cannot ignore the lack of interesting game design and character writing. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: An Absolute Indie gem, Wasn't expecting too much in the beginning, but after the first 20 or-so minutes the game really starts getting incredible, The awesome gameplay, the mind-blowing visuals, the characters and locations, the beyond incredible music, and a really interesting story. I couldn't recommend this game more 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: excellent gameplay, excellent music, excellent characters, and excellent writingcombats are challenging on Expert difficulty, but theyre fair. the movement is so precise that it doesnt need to rely on cheap tricks or ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ note patterns. to quote the Angry Video Game Nerd, "The difficulty isn't all about stiff controls and cheap deaths, but [...] in genuine, fair challenge." and the game isnt afraid to mix things up either. not every fight is dodging notes. some fights may require you to shoot back, others are an endurance test, and the racing minigame is a lot of fun too. every victory, especially with how challenging some of the fights can be, is satisfyingthis leads into the music. as a rhythm based game, music is arguably the most important part. so while I had to hear the intro to each song several, several times while trying to get the various no-hit achievements, I never get tired of hearing any of the songs. there was A LOT of passion put into every piece, and it shows speaking of passion, the character design and writing have lots of that behind them too. no two characters look a like, not even the literal twin slime brothers, nor the various mage characters you will meet. each character's design and personality are unique and unforgettable. i wont touch on the story much because its best experienced yourself with as few spoilers as possibleits criminal that this game is ONLY $9.99, they could have charged $20 for it and itd still be an amazing deal for how much game is in this game. Everhood is an example of the ideal indie game: a small team of people and artists who want a game to be made for a good experience. not to say AAA titles are objectively worse in every way, but they're made with significantly less soul and passion as games like this are
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: A definite must-play for any fan of an RPG with challenging battles front-to-cover and an absolutely STELLAR music track, as well as deep lore and many endings and routes to choose from with great characters. Easy-to-access user customization allows for the player's own battles to come to life, and an assortment of custom options to choose from make this game's replayability extremely high. If you enjoy a challenging but rewarding game with a deep story that comes with it's fair share of big twists and amazing characters, all tied up in a grand bow of an unexpected yet great plot, this game is for you. My only problem with this game are it's visuals, they can cause some eye strain with how psychedelic they are, especially if you get stuck on a fight. But alas, this just makes the game look even better. 9/10, an experience and a half.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: Everhood was a great experience.It's short but packed with non-stop combat whice is quite nice.Most of the characters you meet are great and a blast to meet. but due to the games short lifespan of about 4-6 hours you don't really get to know them to well.The story was meh, a solid 4 out of 10?The soundtrack is a banger tho so I highly recommend it!Overall I would give Everhood a solid 7/10 rating.It's short but packs a punch. :)Also Blue is the best character and I will not be told otherwise!
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is *obviously* heavily influenced by Undertale. The goofy humor. The vivid and bizarre characters. The minimalist 8-bit pixel art. The non-violent, bullet-hell-like RPG battles. But Everhood also is its own beautiful, unique snowflake. It covers surprisingly spiritual themes and has *something worthwhile to say* in a way few games do. Visually it is absolutely STUNNING in many places, ranging from the achingly elegant & minimalist pixel art in the overworld in some places, to the mind-bendingly psychedelic and maximalist visuals during the most intense fight sequences. If THC is legal where you live, Everhood is one of the most compelling games to play stoned EVER.It's also pleasingly difficult, authentically hilarious, and even a tear-jerker. PLAY THIS GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: You know how in music/rhythm games you are supposed to hit the notes in time to the beat? Well instead of trying to hit the notes you are trying to dodge them; add some psychedelic visual effects, a fantastic OST, a engaging story, and you got Everhood! Its a great experience with some unforgettable moments, that may leave you questioning your existence. I highly recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: Steam reviews need a neutral option. here's my two cents.PROS:There's a lot of heart put into this game. i'd say play it if you're not looking for rhythm stuff, because it looks quite interesting. the art is great, the story seems like it could get interesting, and the music is FANTASTIC.  I may actually finish this some day.CONS:THIS IS NOT A RHYTHM GAME.I got this hoping it was a rhythm game where you play to the beat and get lost in the genuinely awesome music.you do not. the beat is on enemy attack, and there's a delay to when you react, so it's completely off-beat. you have to actively ignore the beat to play. IMO that's just not fun at all, and it's the core of the whole game.Overall, I don't hate this, I just don't enjoy it. I think it has tons of potential, but the battle system is so disappointing to make that I just can't recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: An instant classic.Amazing gameplay, great and deep story, lovable characters, fire soundtrack, funny writing, I could go on. Gameplay stands out and stays fresh with the way every battle looks and sounds so different. Every song slaps and some of the segments are super trippy. The game's description isn't lying when it says you're in for a ride. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: The negligence of 'no hit part two' seriously soured my outlook on the game, and made me view other parts of the game with jaded eyes, but taking some distance I'll say the game is overall really awesome. Particularly I hit a groove with its use of visual effects and music, which shone the most.The characters are quite surface depth, in that you do not get to see anything much more to them beyond the first impression or see them develop, but they didn't necessarily need to be something else so long as they still had some sense of personality, which they did. The world of Everhood itself is consisting of a lot of emptyness and long stretches of sparsity, but while I would have appreciated if more was put into it in some way, the design does also feel tasteful, and it does seem a world made with some intent.The battles are the highlight of the game, and what everything else props up. It's where the majority of time will be spent. I had a more enjoyable time on somewhat lower difficulties, as the latter battles paired with a high difficulty meant very long stretches of pure memorization and trial and error. They work better for me when I can feel a natural flow together with the music, like an actual clashing of character, and me experiencing their personhood in the style of the music battle. With long tedious memorization that powerful effect no longer applies. I think that because players experience the personality of the characters through their music battles, this is part of why they can still connect with them emotionally despite the simplistic characterization otherwise.I look forward to the next game, and hope it has no equivalent of the 'no hit part 2'.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: (SPOILER FREE FREVIEW)I was excited to play this game and really wanted to like it, but even though I did enjoy the rhythm-ish fights at least half as much as I thought I would, that's about where my fun ended.Too much of the game is spent incredibly slowly, tediously walking around, with almost all of the map laid out in an unnecessarily maze-like way with way too many invisible walls and rocks to stop you from getting where you want to be in a timely fashion.The story is... unpleasant. It's frustratingly vague at first and then quickly turns into a downer that feels like it's pushing really specific and questionable morals onto you, despite having almost no choices the entire game through. It feels like you're supposed to care about the characters for it to land well, but none of them feel developed, so I only liked characters based on how cute they looked and whether their voice was bearable (the character that talks the most in the first half of the game has a really painfully grating voice). The devs chose a particularly difficult theme to write for, though, and I think it'd be really difficult to keep it from feeling pretentiously nihilistic even with more skilled writing and more time and reason to get attached to the characters in game.In summary, the fights are fun, but the rest of the gameplay is incredibly tedious and boring, and the story is depressing, hardly in a deep or thought provoking way. If slowly walking around a mostly black screen for hours isn't your thing, then I'm pretty sure you can select "Replay Battles" at the main menu without needing to spend time on a story save.I'd give this a neutral recommendation if I could, it's clearly a work of love and I'd probably want to play future games made by the same devs.also, sorry-not-sorry if any Gamers™ disagree with this, but i love that all characters are referred to with gender neutral pronouns regardless of their appearance. me likey :3 thank u devs
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: I can not for the life of me understand, why this got 'overwhelmingly positive' reviews.What exactly is here? It's not a rythm-game like the trailer suggests, you just dodge attacks more, often without regard of the actual beat. The trailer is heavily misleading.And is there supposed to be a story?The characters only seem to be "quirky" for the sake of it and have nothing interesting about them that you not already have seen in other indie-rpgs.There are some sparks about deep philosophical stuff, which I usually like, but this is too abstract to allow me to relate to anything in here.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: An underrated gem. A quirky psychedelic 2D/3D RPG with rhythm battles and a soundtrack that absolutely slaps. Draws lovingly from Undertale while standing proudly on its own as a JRPG with a focus on great music and character design. The story is interesting, the pacing is great, each battle throws something new at you, and the selectable difficulty ranges between mildly challenging and tough-as-nails. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is crazy fun, I love the ideas mixed in this game, the music feels like it was made for the game, and not a lot of video games musics feel that way. The story is confusing but I like that since it makes you think. The gameplay is really simple that most of the game can be played on one hand. and the way the game work is like "easy to use, hard to master". There is also a mode for custom combat that is still in beta but I am interested to see what the community will be able to make with it. There is achievements for literally all the boss when you beat them without getting hit, that add a reason to become better and better at the game to get all of them. Again about the story it is confusing but makes sense when you have the whole picture when you reach the end. _childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: If you have to get any game this year, make sure it's this one. There is a surprising amount of replay-ability to this game, getting the achievements are far more satisfying than any other game i have played recently considering the effort you have to put in for some of them, the dopamine rush is amazing.There are multiple endings and even after 40 hours of gameplay i'm still discovering things in the game that i hadn't previously run into, on one of my runs of the game i was transported to another area where i was the pink character but in a town-like area after being struck by a car. _childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game is polished, has unique combat, and some engaging gags. The overarching plot is also enjoyable, with plenty of twists. However, I did not find any of the characters interesting or compelling. They are generally flat and underdeveloped given the time you spend with them, and are generally either goofy or trying to do something that I won't spoil. There was only a single character (whom you spend the entire beginning of the game with) that hit me with a really heavy emotional moment- all the other characters felt like generic (if unique looking) video game characters. This game is probably still worth a buy for most people. But if you expect the characters, not just the premise, in a story driven game to be interesting, this might not be for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: This game blew me away the amount of mind tricks it plays on you, how fun some moments can be as well as how sad they can be its really a blast to play that is almost impossible to put into words the songs are one of if not the best part of the game the way you bond with all the npc's is just amazing and you may be able to finish the game fast sure but it's a lot better to just take you're time doing it all me with a little more than a day of play time have beat the game twice and still haven't seen it all so much dialog to choose from now i think that having the second game come out early 2025 is perfect and i can't wait overall the game is a must play 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been a huge comfort of mine since I've first played it. It got me to look back and rethink on a lot of my views in life. _childDocuments_.name: Everhood

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, EverHood...I had an amazing little time with this indie title. I bought it because i saw it on sale and read all the positive word of mouth and critics reviews on the product. Its sitting pretty at 84% on metacritic. Granted i am not the targeted fan base. Im in my 30s, I dont care for most rhythym games out today...BUT im a sucker for a good story, And man was this story Bizarre in such a weird and wonderful way. The graphics are definetly Retro and have a nice asthetic especially when the colors pop up in the later fight sections. Wonderful soundtrack, But just such an amazing story. So much love went into making this game, Its just hard to reccomend as great as it is. Its one of those titles that either captures you in the first 20 minutes or completely baffles your mind. I say give it a shot if youre into indy rpgs and are looking for a nice soul searching story. The game isnt easy but theres 6 difficulties so everyone can have a shot at it. Its rare that i give a game a perfect 10, I always find flaws. But this game gets a 10 from me....Its not free from all flaws hoever...I felt that the final 2 hours of the game in regards to backtracking (For the TRUE ending, As there are several) Got a bit monotomous and just when i thought it was going to end more and more kept happening. But by the last scene i felt truly accomplished and that i helped Red and his crew as much as i possibly could. Buy it for the RPG and music, Stay for the characters and story. All in All....A rare perfect 10. Dont miss it!
