_childDocuments_.review: Disc Room is a greatly challenging game and intern rewarding, most importantly it's fair, every mistake feels like your own, every half second feels like progress. I would recommend beating the game all the way through to completion of hard mode, however getting 100% is what I would call a cluster♥♥♥♥ of RNG and combines the worst elements of the game. There are small issues that become big problems with 100% completing,  but beyond that, I have no real complaints. Disc Room is unique and surprisingly fair for having so many elements that could have gone wrong. A good time all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable little game, what seems easy at first quickly turns to insanity. Surviving 20 seconds in all rooms is a pain specifically because of one singular room that's basically luck on getting to 20 seconds, if you've played this game you know which room this is. Other than that one room the game is a a kiss from an disc-angel
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good at what it's doing. TORTURING YOU. But it does it in a very interesting, fun and rewarding way. Sometimes you need luck to win, yes, but most of the time you need skill! What I especially like about this game is it's way of unlocking new levels. If you're good enough, you can pass. If you're a godlike creature, you can find extra levels to play. Sadly, I'm not a godlike creature, and I'm stuck on the last level of hard mode. But hey, you can keep dying trying!...the story is a little confusing tho.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I have 3 hours on Steam and about 20ish hours on Switch for Disc Room. It's one addicting game that I have found to be one of my most favorite games for speedrunning.**Edit at playing around 15 hours on Steam and 20ish on Switch: After playing this game on both Steam and Switch, using Joycons, a Pro Controller, a PS4 Controller, an Arcade Stick, Keyboard and Mouse, after speed running this game so many times just to get a 15 minute speedrun, getting 300% in the game completing both Normal and Hard mode, and getting all Steam Achievements, I officially call this one of the best games ever.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I wish this had been a little harder without being as insanely hard as some of the (non-achivement) challenges. The RNG on a couple of the rooms (especially the ones where you need to pick up the orbs) can also be kind of annoying. Aside from those minor complaints, the game is great! There is a lot more "stuff" in here than you might expect. Lots of types of discs, rooms, and puzzles along with a fun pokedex. I think that the art and music are great.The demo does a pretty good job of showing what the rest of the game will be like, although your scores aren't carried over from there to the main game.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: If i can beat the final boss of a game in 3 and a half hours on my first go and still leave it a positive review, that not only says something about how well-crafted the game is but 100% confirms the saying, "Quality trumps quantity." Plus, "beating" the game gets you nowhere in terms of 100% completion. So, if you enjoy arcadey, bullet hell type games and happen to be a completionist, I would gladly recommend this game to you.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big fan of Devolver Digital so this may be a biased review. However, I have attempted to review this like every other game and to look at as unbiased as possible.Going into Disc Room, I had seen a few gameplay clips but hadn't looked into the game. It looked like a simple game where you had to dodge discs. I didn't expect much so brought it in the Steam sale when it had gone down in price.Upon playing the game, I was greatly surprised. The game is full of many different levels with different types of discs. It starts off quite simple to let you learn the basic mechanics of the game. This also slowly introduces you to the idea that different types of disc move in different ways. The difficult soon ramps up but it always satisfied me to complete the objective after dying multiple times on the level.The main mechanic in the game that I liked was that the longer time you took to complete an objective, the more discs that would spawn. This means that playing the game slow was not an option. If you played the game slow there would be nowhere to go and it would make the game a lot harder. When completing levels as fast as possible, it would mean that you had more options of where to stand but would make the game more intense as the timer ticks up. At some points, I would start to shake if I was unbearably close to the objective and was running out of places I could stand.Some power-ups would help a lot in difficult situations. These would give you a chance to think. I think the sprint was the best power-up out of the five I have unlocked (six in total). I feel like the other abilities were worthless compared to the sprit. Some of the other abilities could have been better. In the aspect of things, this is a very minor point.In conclusion, I have enjoyed the game so far. This somewhat simple idea comes with a lot of replayability and is guaranteed to make your adrenaline pump. I would highly recommend this game as it is exciting and after completing every objective you get a sense of satisfaction. I have completed the normal mode to find that there is a hard mode which I am not sure if I will be able to make it through but I am sure that I will enjoy as well as the normal mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I had avoided buying this initially because I figured it was gonna be like Meatboy, where most of its sauce is spent on difficulty and punishing challenges. I picked this up after I heard someone describe this as "purely focused on movement", and I think that's accurate. It's a simple game with a lot of tiny flourishes. It's good - but not quite great.The core gameplay loop of dodging, bobbing, and weaving is strong. The first few hours are challenging but not frustrating. You don't have to survive that long on any stage, and the timing/spacing on everything is more forgiving than you might expect - it feels just right. Each stage has its own gimmick to keep things fresh. If you don't like the gimmick, you can skip ahead and come back later. Whatever stage you spend time on, you'll be improving at the whole game since it's all about the same thing - movement and tracking. Awesome art direction and sound design keeps it pleasantly entertaining the whole way through.What holds this back from greatness is the tuning and randomness. No stage is deterministic - which is totally fine for some stages, but quickly devolves into chaos on harder stages. It's a frustrating experience to go from one stage where you generally feel responsible for your successes and failures, to another where you're basically grinding it out until you get a nice pattern. The overall design of this game is so tight! I really wanted to dump more hours into this to set record times on every stage, but eventually decided the process would feel less like mastery and more like grinding.There's also a missed opportunity with the abilities. They're all excellent twists on the gameplay, but most of them have significant drawbacks that make them difficult to rely on - they're slow, costly, and sometimes unpredictable. I was initially excited to unlock these and experiment, but usually found myself leaning on the basic dash since it's so reliable. And it's a good dash! I just wish I didn't have to choose between such an important movement mechanic and other more experimental options.It's great fun and I recommend this to anyone who enjoys tight movement - you'll get 4-6 hours of proper fun. The ingredients are here for a timeless game that could eat up hundreds of hours of a perfectionist's playtime, but it needs some mechanical tuning to simplify the stages and give the player more control over their fate.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty solid game where all you do is just dodge saw blades. The difficulty curve is rather fair, with new areas introducing small new mechanics that are required to either progress your timer or defeat bosses. Each room also has challenges associated with the neighboring room that help unlock them with a handful of them requiring a bit more thought than just outright survival.There's also a fair few bonus rooms that'll usually require you to use certain abilities to clear them, and  two small sets of puzzles to access some achievements.If you've got a few hours to kill, it's a pretty good time, it never gets overly frustrating with just two or three rooms that really can push you to the limit if you're aiming for a full 300% and all achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Good game! It's a "bullet-hell" dodger with some clever ideas. I love the artwork and there are many well-done details. I think I found the puzzle elements ("how is this level even possible?") to be my favorite part of the game.One gripe: The difficulty is all over the map, and some of the challenges are just really grindy because you basically have to get lucky AND be good. This wasn't a problem for the regular ending, and rarely a problem for the hard ending, but I didn't do the 20-seconds-in-every-room challenge because some of them just seemed unfairly hard. I think it would have been more fun if the levels were deterministic so that you could practice a route.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Solid disc-based carnage to test your twitch reflexes.Casual players will probably find it to be a bit too short - I completed all of the main levels and beat the final boss in about 3 hours - but for those masochists who like being chopped in half hundreds of times, there is some post-game progress to strive towards, as well as secrets to unlock. The game also has some light puzzling of various sorts that I found satisfying, but I wish it had leaned harder in that direction, with more objectives that followed a pattern besides "survive for N seconds".I've seen other reviews compare it to Super Meat Boy and other such games - I think that is a great comparison. If you like replaying the same level 100 times as you hone your skills, then finally beating it and feeling that SMB-like catharsis, this is the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy how challenging this game is and how fundamentally simple the concept of surviving a room full of obstacles is. The way they keep innovating on this concept and the skill curve it presents is really satisfying. I would recommend this to anyone who likes to challenge themselves with difficult games.Edit: after beating the game 100% and getting all achievements I can say that is probably one of the most gamiest games I've ever played. I'm not sure how I would describe what that means, but It was a super enjoyable time.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: This game is not easy, but it respects the one thing some hard games don't: your time. Restarting is instant. What would or could be head smashingly annoying levels are just another "one more try" thanks to this. Helps that the gameplay loop is fun as hell, I mean, I completely lost track of time and beat it twice and still kept playing for more. Awesome game. I was looking forward to it from reveal and it came out great. One of the best of 2020.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Disk Room300% CompletedSuper Meat Boy meets Smash TV, a simple concept, run around rooms of various disks with different properties for different chunks of time, similar to other games in its genre its a one trick pony, but it does that trick really really well, or at least well enough that you always feel challenged.In traditional fashion Disk Room does have numerous secrets to find throughout its square levels, its not Super Meat Boy dense, but a decent amount that you always feel theirs something hidden behind each wall. In the game are 4 golden rooms with esoteric puzzles to solve, and padded among those rooms are a few "????" rooms with amped-up challenges or beefy survival requirements. Hidden in a few rooms are golden disks that will appear past the time limit of some rooms or when a boss is defeated, some golden disks even require specific patterns to find. I would consider this part of the game and Hard Mode to be the core of the main game. The first few levels are a warm-up.Big issues include its short length, non existent story, and somewhat useless abilities (outside of a few instances).I would recommend this game for someone who:Is a fan of games in this style.Achievement hunters.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Cool little game! With the good amount of challenge, tight controls and a bunch of mysteries to solve, the mix is almost perfect! I would regret the lack of content, as I have 195% completed in about 4 hours (and I don't really want to grind all the achievements), also some of the UI if a bit confusing (objectives are unclear, the next thing to do is never indicated properly etc...), plus the game doesn't give you any advice or tips (not even explaining some of the UI stuff), and the tutorial is barely existent. You may want to wait for a price under $10, except if you really like the devs (Minit was truly awesome!).
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Great bullet-hell challenge game. Lots of secrets and exploration. Its tight and snappy and feels good to play. It feels so satisfying when you beat a high score or get further than you were planning in a room.Quick play sessions too (or can be). Perfect game for playing a few rooms for 5-10 minutes when taking a break from something else, but be careful you might get caught up in it and spend an hour.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: This game has the best feeling movement since Pac-man. If Super Meat Boy innovated as the merciless Mario successor, this does the same for the top-down Zelda formula. It is a simultaneously thrilling and zen experience that encourages risky moves with a razor-thin margin of error. This game is why the analog stick was invented.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Disc Room is one of those "frustration games," like Super Meat Boy or The End is Nigh, where you dodge sawblade discs for as long as you can, and dying over and over again and keeping cool through your frustration is the core of the game. The level design in Disc Room keeps things fresh by introducing new discs and mechanics at a decent pace, and the 20 second survival challenges for each room ensures that you'll rarely get bored or fully complete a room on the first try. Sometimes a disc will spawn right next to you and kill you before you had time to react to it, but hey, it wouldn't be a frustration game if it wasn't frustrating right?
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: This game is mad fun while it lasts, but it doesen't last too long. I especially liked that it is not simply about avoiding death, but dying tactically... and the missions and enemy variety is suprisingly large for a game about buzzsaws. Precise controls and interesting abilities make for some fun fast paced hours, but I was done with most of it after 4 hours but ended up expecting a bit more content than I got. If the devs would release a second part of same scope or paid dlc I would definetly be up for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game, it's so simple yet so addictive. Fast paced action and you can get back into the game easily and when you finish the regular game you get to start hard mode which is beating my ass lmao. My one complaint is that in the higher difficulty rooms it can sometimes feel like complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ just because of the sheer amount of discs but other than that the game is great.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: The game is relatively easy (very fun, addicting) apart from getting 20 "seconds" on 1 single level. The name escapes me but its part of the fleshy area, you will know what I'm talking about when you get there. Probably took me 5 hours to 100% the game apart from the built in challenges, and 1 single room took me 225 attempts (~ 2-3 hours) of pain and misery just to pick up 20 dumb golden balls in 1 life without changing the difficulty of the game (disc speed, ect...). Which when I think about it. I should have tried to make the game easier to get that achievement. Just didn't want to believe the developers would keep the achievements enabled with these modifiers tampered with. Otherwise it's a lot of fun. They should definitely nerf that room for the "I AM THE ZONE" achievement though :)
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite "dodge" game!You have to dodge discs to avoid deathEvery level is a room, a different one and with different discsRooms are linked between each otherOnce you finish the game you can still return in rooms to unlock secrets and hidden roomsYou have challenges to complete too!The best thing i can tell about this game is that : its feel so smoothGameplay, musics, art, everything ...
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 mostly recommend, except for the abilities, puzzles, and dark rooms.Pros: amazing art, catchy music, some rooms can be super fun.- The boss rooms were my favorite, especially the Carniverous Gatekeeper! It's so satisfying grabbing all those yellow orbs, dashing around like a maniac. - Fun to watch friends play.- The objectives are fun little goals, but might get too frustrating if you're a completionist.- Art is 10/10 and was my main draw. I would love a Disc Room poster for sure.Cons: confusing puzzles, underused abilities, some really annoying rooms.- I *hate* the dark rooms. The Perfect Dark is the absolute worst. As my friend described it, "sometimes you gotta just luck out to complete the room." I didn't feel in control at all and they feel very unfair. The dark rooms also make up a fourth of the map, which were a slog to get through. There are also non-dark rooms that also feel very luck-based.- All but 2 of the abilities were used once or twice as gimmicks. A bit of a let down.- Most puzzles are really obscure. I tried to throw myself and my abilities against the discs (like we've been taught, to gain abilities) and nothing's worked yet. So I can't help but feel we weren't given the tools to solve the puzzles.I mean, a lot of this is personal preference. I don't usually play bullet hells (though I really love Enter the Gungeon) so maybe I'm not it's target audience? Still lots of fun though, try it out!
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: This game throws me back to the days of slacking off in middle school on Armor Games or Kongregate. It has that high-octane arcade energy in every room, with a crazy variety of obstacles and win conditions for such a simple premise. Coupled with endgame content, numerous secrets, an absolutely darling art style, and creative mechanics, it's one of those titles that's been shaved of useless fluff down to a meaty, pulsating pile of pure, unadulterated fun -- a 4-6 hour game worth its weight in coin.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Arcade action at its finest. Playable in bite size chunks. Always just enough wiggle room to make impossible things doable. Deceptively clever. Disc Room is very good, and that's not even taking into account its vibrant art style and amazing soundtrack. Would recommend for any fan of action or time attack type games.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Ok I know I don't have much play time, but you don't need much to know this is a really cool game. I'm just busy, I'll play more later I swear! This game is basically what it looks like, you dodge discs, but the way it constantly has interesting mechanical twists on that premise is fascinating! It WILL surprise you with interesting goals, abilities and layouts. If it looks even remotely fun you should get it, it will be better than you think
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Very very simple concept. Only the stick and one button (plus fast forward). Jesus christ does it have a lot going on though. Rooms have their own saw blade patterns with a many unique types of rooms. A LOOOT of scecrets , some levels are a little to obtuse for me. Overall I didn't think such a simple concept could be so polished and have so much to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following JW and Doseone for a while now, so when it was announced they were working on this together, my expectations were high, but this meets them and more. First of all, design by Terri Vellmann is beautiful. He is quickly becoming one of my favourite visual artists for games after this and his amazing work on sludge life earlier this year (which I would recommend you check out for free on epic). This look also pairs really well with Doseone's once again fantastic soundtrack. But now onto the gameplay end of things. For a game with very limited mechanics, it manages to throw enough things at you that you will struggle to get bored. Hell, I've been stuck on the same boss for about 2 hours and it still doesn't feel stale or boring. I was at first worried that this game would be too short, but after seeing the achievements and the growing difficulty curve, I think I've got a lot more play time left in it. the whole team did such a great job on everything about this.tl;dr - looks great, sounds great, lots of fun. this game is as great as expected from this team and you should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing little game. It takes the very basic concept of dodging stuff, much like many old school flash games, and runs with it. The core gameplay here is nothing new and has been done to death, but the presentation and smoothness of the whole experience makes it worthwhile.It has a surprising amount of "enemy" (Sawblade) variety and different ways in which it changes up the gameplay from area to area. There even are some puzzle elements and a bunch of secrets to uncover, which was quite the surprise!Combine the smooth and fun gameplay with a great soundtrack, great visuals and a fun little story and you have a solid game in your hands.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Disc Room is elegant perfection. It hands you a concept, surviving in a room full of bouncy blades, then keeps refreshing and building on the idea that you'll always be amazed at what it pulls next. Combine that with how quick and easy it is to throw yourself in for challenge after challenge and before long you're hooked, each second on the clock feels like a hard won victory as you and the discs dance a dance of death and adrenaline.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review: Really, really hard, but it's pretty fair and never really so hard that it makes you want to quit forever.  It's like eating some good spicy food, little chunks of pain that are enough to give you some good heat but not enough to give you the 2am spicy Taco Bell regret because there was too much of it.  The game expects and wants you to die often and in new and interesting ways, so it doesn't really ever feel like you're smashing your head against a wall because you have nowhere else you can go.And then you unlock hard mode and you REALLY start to feel the pain.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

_childDocuments_.review:
The year is 2089, and a giant disc has appeared in orbit of Jupiter. A crew of international scientists is formed in a desperate attempt to understand the mysterious secrets contained within. Step into the oversized space suit of a brave but reluctant scientist and explore this sprawling slaughterhouse from outer space. Attempt to discover the method behind its madness as you are relentlessly chased down by intelligent alien saw blades amid a seemingly endless labyrinth of interconnected death chambers. Stay sharp in order to navigate this murderous maze, as the seemingly straightforward slaughter unfurls into far more puzzling complexity. But, what kills you only makes you stronger. Absorb extraordinary abilities from the very discs that dice you into pieces. Invincibly dash, bend time, even clone yourself as you become one with the disc. Persistent punishment quickly solidifies into razor-sharp survival skills, as our scientist dies their way toward the deeper more devastating purpose of the disc.

    In Disc Room, the only way out is through Death.
_childDocuments_.name: Disc Room

name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder
detailed_description: More Great Games! About the Game Join Aletheia and a vibrant cast of characters as they race to discover the secrets of the Steam City of Canaan. Clobber armies of Clockwork golems and hunt horrors that slither through depths once forgotten. Thwart the twisted schemes of Canaan’s corrupt overseers, the nefarious Comitium. Fight for mankind’s survival and reveal the dark and dangerous truths riveted into the very foundations of the Steam City. Step into the shoes of Aletheia and tread the path of the Soldner, an elite mercenary of Irkalla who lives one job at a time. Take up the sword and gun, combining a slew of melee combos and deadly gunplay in staggering feats of skill that will leave your enemies reeling. Chase down a frenzied mutant charging through the grimy stalls of the Irkallan Black Market, leap across the molten pools blazing in the eternal furnace of Fornax, and fight off hordes of blood-drunk Raiders that prowl the fathomless depths of the Scrap Sea in search of their malignant god. Canaan is vast, and inside its swirling steam lie innumerable mysteries waiting to be unraveled. After a routine job goes awry, Aletheia sets out on an epic journey to uncover ancient enigmas threatening the very foundations of the Steam City. Challenge powerful new rivals and catch up with old friends as you carve your path through Canaan. Take on side jobs to earn a bit of extra scrap and delve into a history lost to the vagaries of time. Or maybe you’d just like to wash down your worries at Vincent’s Pub and listen for a rumor or two… Dash, dodge, and double-jump to keep out of harm’s way and stay in one piece. Wield a furious and fearsome array of abilities and grow stronger with each foe you defeat. Spend experience points to unlock new skills and trade scrap for accessories to customize your build and go toe-to-toe with some of the most formidable creatures to ever lumber beneath the copper sky. Hear that? The clang of a hammer stinging blood-red steel… The sinister murmur of heresies rushing through ancient pipes… Riddles echoing through vaulted halls of marble and madness. Sounds like fate has a job in store for you, Soldner—it’s time to earn your scrap. “Thine trembling works of Reason naught but ingots gleaming darkly by the light of a cindered heart—for what art thine flesh before the mother’s touch of flame?” - Dreams of the Steam Saint Anais, XXXIV, iii

short_description: Inspired by 16 and 32-bit classics, Gestalt: Steam & Cinder fuses tight 2D platforming and exhilarating combat with an engrossing, twist-laden narrative in a stunningly handcrafted steampunk world.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game but EXTREMELY short, it took 8 hour for 100% completion.Positives:+ Skill tree is great+ Movement is extremely fluid and responsive.+ Combat is excellent+ Plenty of accessories to choose from, do you want to focus on guns, swords, defense, a little of both, etc...+ Once you unlock fast travel, getting around is easy+ As you progress and explore the game you get items that make it easier to find things you missed early on.Neutral:+/- This game is VERY story heavy, I personally like storyline, however if a ton of text bothers you, this game is going to piss you off.+/- The map style is not my favorite, I prefer Classic metroidvania maps (each room = 1 square) or Ori-style detailed maps.  This game unfortunately uses massive blank squares and rectangles with no landmarks, which is my most hated map style for games like this.Negatives:- EXTREMELY short, 8 hours for 100% completion- Game is VERY easy, and bosses only get easier as you progress.  I was killing mid game bosses in 20-60 seconds.- The story feels incomplete, at the end of the game certain plot points are wrapped up, but there are a TON of loose ends.  It feels like part 1 of a story...
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend it if you are just wanting to play an indie Metroidvania and you're digging the style from the videos and trailer. However, the ending is quite unsatisfying and clearly they are leaving it open ended enough for a sequel or maybe a DLC? It's fine. It's not too expensive, but it's short at 9-10 hours for a 100% completion.I've heard some folks complain about it being wordy. It's really not that much text. Everything isn't Call of Duty multiplayer or Fortnite. Sometimes games have a story that you follow along with.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was keeping tabs on Gestalt: Steam & Cinder for a few years now, when I was captivated by its wonderful pixel art and mechanized steampunk setting. The announcement trailer left me full of uncertainty and anticipation, and it was a pleasant surprise to finally see its release date. Now that I could play it, I must say that it left me unsatisfied, and wanting for more, for better or worse; but a good game at the end of the day. It is a metroidvania that puts the main focus on its story, with a gameplay that although it does not reinvent the genre, is entertaining and has its own particular touches. Add to that a beautiful and detailed pixel art, with songs very much in line with the setting, and it becomes a game worth checking out.The story of Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is presented first with a brief glimpse into the past. At a certain point in time, a calamitous event took place; the sky split in two, and a portal opened into the unknown. Horrifying creatures emerged from this dimension, unleashing chaos in the kingdom. In a last desperate attempt, mankind was forced to cross the threshold in search of something with which to confront the sudden threat.Seizing the very power of the demons, they created armor of steel and steam, giving up their humanity in the process, but succeeding in accomplishing their task. It's a fairly complete prologue, and one from which I'll omit certain details that I think are more enjoyable in the game than reading it here. We follow the story of Aletheia, a sort of mercenary who will be immersed in a series of enigmatic events linked to the world beyond the portal, her own origin, and what the kingdom has planned with respect to what happened in the past. As I mentioned before, Gestalt: Steam & Cinder puts a special emphasis on the narrative, and in addition to Aletheia's adventures, we will also get a glimpse of what is happening with other specific characters as the plot progresses.The narrative aspect was what hooked me the most about the game, in case it wasn't clear. It has some pretty interesting twists, and a world building that I would have liked to explore even more; though, without giving spoilers, maybe I'll get my wish granted sometime.Then we have the gameplay, which has its ups and downs. Starting with exploration, it's a fairly linear metroidvania. There are no secondary or secret areas, but it has the typical objects or collectibles that we can not get until we acquire a particular skill. By the way, the collectibles here are corgis scattered around the map, curious, isn't it? There are also side quests, and in certain places there are boards with more generic tasks such as “kill X of this enemy”. And the truth is that the latter felt like a somewhat lacking addition.For the combat theme, we have only two weapons at our disposal; a sword for melee, and a revolver to attack from a distance. The latter is what I found most interesting, as the bullets we can load are limited, and are usually regenerated by attacking enemies. Eventually the ammunition can be upgraded, and serve to break the “posture” of the enemies (basically stun them) more effectively than with just sword hits, and also for some puzzles. The combat itself felt a bit monotonous to me at first. However, that feeling was alleviated as I progressed, thanks to the stats and accessory systems, and the typical metroidvania skills such as double jumping. With regards to enemies and bosses, some are a bit more challenging than others, but overall they're fine. The poise bar and stuns are key against some of them, which gives it some more dynamism.In Gestalt: Steam & Cinder our progress is represented by a skill tree that revolves around our weapons and movements, and a repertoire of accessories that give us passive bonuses and parameter improvements.On the skill side, we have points to distribute through the aforementioned tree, and in general we can choose which stats to upgrade or which move to unlock as we wish. The curious thing about the system is that the points can be obtained in several ways, such as leveling up, finding certain spheres that will give us points when we destroy them, or tethering with save points and fast travel portals.Accessories go hand in hand with the previous system, as they grant us passive bonuses that increase our stats, and some can even be combined in a blacksmith to improve their effectiveness.The game's mechanics fit very well together, leaving aside the reward board, which, while not a bad thing, I didn't see as necessary. Its artistic section also caught me completely, with great animations, and very detailed models and backgrounds.Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is a game that left me wanting for more, as it took me about twelve hours to platinum it; but this is not necessarily bad, of course. Maybe I also had very high expectations, but that's my problem and not the game's! It captured me with that fantastic steampunk setting, and I just didn't want to let go. Overall, it really was a pleasant experience, and I recommend it to those looking for a petit metroidvania for a fun weekend.

_childDocuments_.review: So, following my first impressions review a couple of days ago, this is now my full review of Gestalt: Steam & Cinder!As always, a video review has been created, which you can watch below: For those who do not wish to watch the video:My Playtime: 8 hours and 14 minutesCompletion Rate: 100%Pros:- Excellent story presentation and lore that goes deep, with an awesome mystery at its center that keeps you engaged.- Well-realized characters with their own personalities and motivations, all of them shaped by their past experiences which now guided their actions for what each one considers to be the greater good.- Wonderful combat that encourages the use of, both, melee and ranged strategies to overcome your enemies. Melee wise, you are equipped with a powerful sword that allows you to get close and personal and make mincemeat out of your enemies, while your ranged attacks are carried out with a gun which has a limited amount of ammo that can be restocked by drawing energy either by attacking enemies or finding certain Tesla coils on the map.- Well-implemented RPG character upgrade system. Essentially you gain experience by killing enemies in order to level-up and gain ability points, which you then use to purchase upgrade nodes across a skill tree which contains, both, passive as well as active benefits.- Beautiful art-style that depicts an amazingly envisioned Steampunk world with disturbing horror elements.- A variety of secrets to uncover, with certain merchants selling you maps that will place markers for said secrets on your overview map.- Nice fast travel system, which unlocks about two and a half hours into the game.- Bounty side-quest system that gives more incentive to take down enemies.- Aside from bounty side-quests, you also have the more traditional side-quests that require of you to seek out items and return them to NPCs, adding some extra incentive to exploration.- Sublime music (the story intro soundtrack still haunts me).- Amazingly detailed biomes that tell an environmental story of their own.- Likeable protagonist.- Nice healing system that borrows from the soulsborne genre, meaning you get vials that can be used to replenish your health, and whose number resets at save points. The number of said vials can also be upgraded via a merchant.- Very fun bosses with a good range of move-sets (though also check one of the cons below).Cons:- The occasional typo and/or missing word when it comes to dialogue (though very rare and by no means detrimental to the plot).- I noticed that certain shops in the game hadn't yet had their titles translated (for example, I will come across a shop that says "Machinist" above it, and then I will find another whose name is in Japanese, if I'm not mistaken. Not sure if this is on purpose).- Difficulty is very much on the easy side. I was kind of disappointed to find out that the game became progressively easier the more I continued my playthrough, until, eventually, it had become nearly impossible for me to die, and I ended up completely obliterating enemies and bosses alike, almost without a sweat. The only boss that took me a bit of time to finish off was one in the latter parts of the game, whose fight was simply tedious since damage played no importance and it was all about positioning and repeating an attack pattern that took him down quite slowly, with said boss fight also being the sourest part of the gameplay experience for me. There are also no difficulty settings to make the game harder, meaning the default challenge is the one you will have to play with, something I consider a missed opportunity.- I'd have liked to see a bit more variety in the side-quests. As they stand now, they are just bounties that want you to kill X number of enemies and get a reward, or fetch quests. The bounties are useful, since you would kill those enemies anyway, but feel a bit like an afterthought.- The game can be considered linear for a good part of it. Though backtracking is very much necessary for you to go for 100% completion and there are certain biomes that can demonstrate some complexity, such as the forest one with its vertical sections and platforming challenges, others can feel more straightforward, with the story essentially leading you from one area to the next.- Platforming could have also benefited from some extra difficulty since, even though there are a few sections that require some acrobatic skill, for the most part these trials were easy to overcome.- Finally, I’ll admit than I didn’t really find much use for the items I found inside basic chests, with the exception of the antidote, which came in quite handy.That's it! Overall, I pretty much loved my time with the game and couldn't leave it down until I got 100%!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game a masterpiece? No, but it is good and there can never be enough good metroidvanias. It aims to offer exactly what has made the genre so popular. For example, we can jump, dash, double-jump, leap back and forth between two walls, strike with our sword, shoot with our pistol, roll and quickly dodge backwards. However, some of these abilities - and a few more - have to be unlocked first. Bosses in particular are always a good source of useful new rewards. Backtracking is necessary, but not on a massive scale and especially if you get lost again despite the automap, or if you are looking for hidden rooms.We take on the role of Aletheia, a young woman working as a mercenary who sets off into the depths of the steampunk city of Canaan in search of Simon, a missing young man. However, after she soon finds him, she does not bring him back to the safe surface, but is persuaded by him to descend with him further into the depths of the underground labyrinths beneath the city in order to find a supposedly infinitely powerful relic. Of course, the way down is not so easy. There are robots running around everywhere, and most of them obviously no longer work as intended and attack us immediately on sight. The environment isn't exactly inviting either - locked doors, moving platforms, blocked entrances. So we fight our way forward in the tried and tested metroidvania manner - killing enemies, opening doors, lowering ladders to set up shortcuts... whereby we don't progress in a linear fashion, but have to visit previously explored areas again and again to complete quests, buy equipment or even just save the game state at one of the save points. We are also fully healed each time we save. Enemies reappear as soon as we have left their area, allowing us to kill them again and collect some scrap (=money) in return. We keep coming across friendly humans or robots who have also ended up in the underground tunnels for various reasons. Many of them help us or send us on small quests, with the game automatically documenting our quests on a separate page.One-time consumable items such as healing potions, beer or coffee improve our strength in the short term or heal poisoning, for example. Our energy pistol can only fire a single shot at first, but if we injure enemies in close combat, the energy is regenerated. Of course, we soon find ways to store a little more energy for our pistol. In the character screen, we can see our values such as hit points, energy and resistance, as well as our level, the chance of landing critical hits and a little more. However, this cannot keep up with a full-blown role-playing game. The skill tree, where we can invest points gained after leveling up in useful skills, is much more complex. There are dozens of upgrades to choose from here - provided you have the points to purchase them, and nodes in the skill tree must be unlocked during the course of the game in order to access new areas. So you can't collect experience forever in the first level and eventually unlock all the skills... Of course, we can also find items to improve Aletheia, although initially only a single slot is unlocked for additional equipment. As a bonus, you can find hidden dogs in the levels.The game automatically draws a map. However, the map is weak. You can zoom and move it, you can even add different icons yourself, but the map is still poor. It only shows huge rooms and their exits, which makes it difficult to find your way around. Imagine that the map of an anthill is just a large rectangle... the map doesn't tell you exactly what's inside the rectangle and which paths you can take. The automap is better than nothing, but not extremely helpful. X-Box Controller and DS 4 PlayStation Controller work perfectly. With an ultrawide monitor (21:9) it is playable without any problems, but with black bars on both sides. Cloud saves are created automatically.Classic 2D Metroidvania, massively inspired by the 16- and 32-bit classics of the genre. Melee fighting, jumping, exploring large non-linear levels, defeating bosses and continuously upgrading your character with new abilities and items is the gameplay essence of the game. There are also slightly longer conversations than usual, but this does not make the game a visual novel.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's start this off by saying that, to be fair, the mechanics of the game are fine. It's a solidly competent Metroidvania title throughout. If you're someone who doesn't care at all about plot or writing, then this... will probably bore you to death with the endless dialogue. Because it's as much a narrative game as it is an action platformer. The story is woven throughout the whole game, and is just as much a focus as the gameplay. Which is why, when the story is taken out back behind the shed and shot in the last 90 seconds, it devalues the entire rest of the game.Mass Effect 3 wishes it could kill a story this well.

_childDocuments_.review: Had this game in my wishlist for a while, so i was really hoping to love it.Gonna say immediately, the style and art is on point, theres no arguing that.Combat and exploration tho, leaves a lot to desire:-First of all the most annoying thing you get to find out a bit later, the light attack combo increase in the skill tree is useless, completely.theres no point in upgrading it, every enemy wont allow you to attack more than twice before you're forced to either dodge or trade damage. there's no hitstun either so even less of a reason to want to chain more than two attacks in a row.-Another thing is the gun, outside of stunning enemies with shields or bosses, its use is rather lacking.Aiming is only for 4 directions, (fully up, diagonal up, forward and diagonal down) and you can only use the gun if you're standing perfectly still, so unless the enemy is right in front of you, dont bother.-Boss fights have been very meh. You have some very simple bosses that just make you wait for attacks that leave them vulnerable so you can try stun them or just spam any strong attacks you have, and then you have whatever disgusting thing that gank fight in the underground lab was, where you're stuck in a small arena fighting 4 of the same enemy spamming the same 2 attacks over and over until you kill them all (i know theres a machine in the middle that automatically stuns them every few seconds if you hit it, but thats just a bandaid fix for a fight that sucks even when you use it)-enemy placement after a while becomes a colossal spam of projectile throwing damage sponges whose only objective is to fill your screen with as much clutter as possible, and sometimes theyre also flying enemies, or poisonous, or both!-exploration becomes very bothersome, the different regions look very pretty, but the rooms you explore are nothing more than a way to contain enemies for you to fight and treasures to find.-it'd be very nice to either have some sort of super armor for heavier attacks, or even just a bit of hitstun or stronger knockback on basic combo hit, because otherwise the combat is very barebones: just hit hit and dodge-at the time im writing this review i reached a breaking point with this game, im in a forest, every enemy i meet is poisonous, has projectiles and some of them either fly or go underground so theyre invulnerable. i dont want to deal with this, my fighting options are very limited, the enemies attacks are relentless, and the poison is too long lasting and effective for something that can only be healed with a consumable resource i have to go back and buy.-also theres some spelling mistakes in the dialogues but nothing unfixable or that mind boggling, just check the dialogues a bit better.-also if i have to hear that damn king talk about how he'll find a better way, the brutal fights in the past and all that stuff one more time i swear to god, that guy says the same things every cutscene, I GET IT.-Either make the stamina bar charge faster or make it so it can have one more charge or even that it doesnt deplete if not in combat.Despite all of this, i really enjoyed the game, but it definitely feels clunkier the longer you play it, and i dont know if i can get myself to finish it or recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't recommend this game because I found it to be all flash and no substance.The visual presentation is gorgeous. Sprite work on the main character and backgrounds capture a steampunk environment beautifully. This is the selling point of the game and it nails it perfectly.I personally tuned out of the story because the cut scenes continually got in the way of gameplay and no character presented any compelling narrative. There are a lot of cut scenes and it pulled you into a narrative beet that I felt conflicted with the gameplay flow. A few of the story beats had me doing double take, especially when I fought an enemy and then see him in town acting like nothing happened between us a few minutes ago.Gameplay wise there are a few things that really disappoint me. The level system is disappointing. When you go back to the starting zone at a higher level and fight lower level enemies, it will take a near equal amount of hits to kill enemies 10+ levels below you. Why have a level system at all if enemies scale with you throughout the game? The main character having levels is good, but enemies should not have their levels displayed as it presents a game system that gameplay fails to deliver on. The upgrade tree, and in particular the light combo upgrades disappoint me because of a lack of enemy hitstun. It is not worth upgrading the light combo system because you only get the baseline two to three  hits on an enemy rather than your fully upgraded attack amount before an enemy can counterattack you. Combo hits in general are limited to the light attacks only. I really wish you could combo into a heavy sword or a gun attack as a finisher.The fast travel system and its implementation confused me. The game says fast travel is available, yet provides you no portal to travel to despite the system becoming available. At this point in the game you have visited two portals, but you have to revisit the first portal to be able to travel to it. Why introduce a fast travel if you are not immediately able to use it? Enable the player to use a system once they get it.Items in the game require you to go into the menu to see their effects. When picking up an item you should be able to see what it does and decide it you want to pause gameplay to equip the item. There is a popup declaring what the name of the item is. Provide additional information on what the item is at this point.I do plan to finish the game, and I hope above can be addressed to make others experiences better.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think this game is horrible, but I did find it pretty mid.I think calling this game a "metroidvania" is a bit of a stretch, like it technically checks all the boxes, but it's extremely linear, and the "exploration" is mostly just backtracking with abilities you got later. The rewards for backtracking aren't even that exciting, the main exciting things to get are accessories and corgis, but most accessories are bland and just give you small numbers buffs, and the corgis don't give you any exciting rewards until you get all of them.There's also a lot of empty space in this game, in the main city most of the buildings you either can't enter, or if you can, there's literally nothing inside, not even an npc with some background dialogue. These buildings DID take up space though, and you really felt it when you were backtracking for quests and were slowly running past a lot of buildings that served no purpose.It's very weird because the core of the game, the movement and how your character feels to use, was pretty darn solid, albeit with some weirdness with the keybinds. I did find it a bit weird that the forward dash and the backdash were not on correlated buttons, so moving forwards vs backwards didn't feel natural at all. Honestly I think if they removed the ability to aim the gun but let you shoot it in the air, the controls could have felt much tighter.This strong control is not utilized super well though, since the maps felt pretty large without enough stuff to do besides extremely basic platforming, and without much to collect besides some consumables and the corgis. The enemies are extremely basic, once you know how to fight one, it becomes a complete non-threat because it always does the same thing and the response is always the same. Enemies also had enough hp that they'd take a little bit to beat as you go, so eventually I just started skipping enemies because of how uninteresting it was.This is ignoring the story, which I found pretty lackluster. Despite cutting out from gameplay to show cutscenes every once in a while, the dialogue really fails to compel me in any way. One of the most pivotal scenes in the game involved a character that previously had like 2 lines of dialogue at the real start of the game. It was impossible to really feel the connection because that character just wasn't part of the story for 99% of my playtime up to that point.In general, I think the story was pretty poor, the characters weren't particularily interesting, and the ending was clearly a setup for a future game. Unfortunately that means that the ending was pretty darn weak for the existing story. I don't even think the journey to that ending was particularily interesting since the characters just didn't feel very strong. There was a lot of potential in the first area of the game, and there was a pretty reasonable setup, but it lost steam pretty hard as the game went along.This all comes to a head with the fact that the game was honestly pretty short, I completed most of the content in about 4 hours, and the content I haven't done for 100% felt tedious enough that I don't feel like going back for it. I definitely don't think this game is worth the full price of $20, if you are interestd in picking it up, I'd wait for it to go on sale.Overall, while I see what the devs vision for this game was, their execution just didn't follow through. The amazing pixel art and animations definitely draw you in to picking it up, but past that, the game feels so lacking that the gameplay is honestly forgettable. It's really sad because deep in there, there are the bones of a good game, but the map and combat are the meat and potatoes of a metroidvania and this game did not deliver on that front.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder presents a visually stunning adventure with its gorgeous pixel art and very catchy music. The fast-paced plot and overall gameplay create a smooth and relaxing experience, rarely inducing frustration. Combat is generally good, though it can feel stiff at times due to attack lock-ins. The game’s skill tree, which can be easily refunded, adds some layer of flexibility to character development, altrough by the end of the game, you will have almost everything unlocked. Despite its relatively short length, the story is densely packed, almost overwhelming with its rich lore and numerous terms that could fit into a 50-hour jRPG, yet it remains engaging throughout. However despite the heavy handed story, the reward for paying attention to it is an abrupt anticlimactic ending.For a metroidvania Gestalt is very linear, with zero alternative routes and everything being ability or quest-locked (similiar to Iconoclasts). Exploration feels unrewarding, as many chests contain consumables that could simply be bought from vendors, and there is a lot of backtracking required to fully complete the game. Side quests, mainly consisting of dull "kill X of Y" tasks, add little to the experience. While the difficulty is on the easier side, the combat still holds up, though some encounters, particularly boss fights, are annoyingly tedious with bosses having few attack patterns but excessively long fights.Despite these shortcomings, the length of Gestalt: Steam & Cinder felt perfect, leaving me wanting more. A DLC or sequel would be a welcome addition to this indie metroidvania. However, the lack of replayability is a downside, as there are no bonuses or new game plus options. I've sadly encontuered a hard crash, that resulted in my 5hr savegame being wiped out.Solid 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really, really solid game with a MASSIVE catch that I'll list at the bottom of the review. is ultimately a fantastic feeling Metroidvania wrapped around a story that was too high-concept for the writing team to execute gracefully. That isn't to say the writing is *bad* - it's frequently very good - but I'll get into that in a second. On game feel: the controls in this game are fantastic, for the most part. The main character animates beautifully (as does most everything in ,) and everything from moving to attacking feels responsive and smooth. Getting a hang of the game's movement is a delight - it feels like there's enough here for speedrunners to chew on for weeks, fine tuning routes and perfecting short hops and dashes. The movement feels good even at a basic level but has the nuance and fine tuning potential to offer a lot of depth. The movement is  good and in some places better. The same can't necessarily be said for the combat. It's a swooshy affair with a range of basic attacks, heavy attacks that require some of your revolver meter (basically a super move gauge,) and some ranged attacks that also require your revolver meter. Where the combat has lots to unlock and master, the depth suffers when it comes time to actually put all those moves into practice. Don't get me wrong, the fighting is pretty fun but the basic enemy types don't demand much from you. There was one section of the game where I felt legitimately threatened by the enemies and there it often felt like the tactics the game encouraged weren't especially useful (i.e. i-framing an enemy shot by rolling only to get clocked by a backwards shot as part of the overly long animation.) At that point I felt frustrated rather than challenged - what I wanted was to be pushed into using more combat options, not feeling as though I had no safe approach. Boss fights are fun, but fairly easy and prone to cheesing with some of the more powerful techniques. All in all, combat felt  but it felt good despite the enemies, not because of them. The music is another standout. There's a range of Western-esque strings over some heavy drums and symphonic shenanigans, and it all works - every single track is great. It's absolutely gorgeous and will be the fastest Spotify stream of my life if it ever ends up on the service. I know the devs are working on getting it put out as DLC; I'd recommend you purchase that instantly. Now: the writing. I should note that I'm hyper-critical of writing (perhaps hypocritically so, as this review might evidence,) and by and large  's writing team did better than a lot of folks would have with this whole concept. But that's because the concept itself is anime as hell. In short: there's an apocalypse by way of a strange dimensional energy, there's people using that energy to slay the demons the energy itself produced, there's a schism between the normal people and the people corrupted by aforementioned energy, and then the story begins as the latter have been banished from the last remaining city, powered by vaguely defined 'steam.' There's proper nouns everywhere, constant exposition dumps abound, and characters routinely descend into ellipses-filled dramatics at the barest sight of a plot twist. None of it was game ruining - mostly - but it was a distraction every time a cutscene played. It's a shame the writing isn't stellar, because the character designs are fantastic and when the writing sings it really sings. But to have all that exposition and then have glaring plot holes is almost a step too far.The  step too far is a major spoiler for the structure of the end of the game. I won't be spoiling the story, but I will tell you what very nearly made me thumbs-down the game, and I will put that behind spoiler tags.With that massive caveat in place, I still recommend the game. For casual players, the moment to moment story, gorgeous art, incredible music and great controls will make for a really great weekender title you can blaze through and be (mostly) satisfied with in a couple solid sessions. For speedrunning types and completionists, the movement system here is a joy to use and I feel like if the game picks up a solid community we'll be seeing speedruns for months to come. It's a recommend, but to the devs: for the love of god don't pull that trick again.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Kinda goofy, kinda silly, really overdramatic.The opening of the game barrages you with Proper Nouns and Ominous Names and Secret Meetings, it's not hard to follow, but it's pretty standard stuff. The plot is pretty straightforward Chosen One(s) stuff, with a series of last minute twists that are hilariously generic. I loved it, but not in a serious way.The gameplay itself is pretty solid, she's got that Belmont Swagger, enemies require moderate finesse and timing, the gun is easy to use and has a satisfying kick, the sword combos are flashy and satisfying. Most enemies can be obliterated without touching any of the skill node moves, which is fine. They're cool and it's fun to figure out places to use them. The platforming segments are also solid, with snappy controls, a variety of platforming obstacles and options, and tight but not overly precise platforming puzzles and mazes to navigate. Using the platforming skills to navigate the game world is so satisfying that I opted to just Double Jump, Air Dash and Dodge Roll through the world instead of using fast travel. It's a pretty solid game, it's not going to stick in my mind nor is it going to be actively forgotten.

_childDocuments_.review: I have a lot of thoughts on this game, but I'll keep this short. Yes I recommend it, but there are a lot of criticisms I have. Overall, I enjoyed this game for sure and it was fun to play but I want to note a few opinions I have.The elephant in the room when talking about this game I feel is the story. I don't think it's necessarily bad or anything, but I was not very interested in it during my playthrough. I feel like the political drama presented with the opposing kingdoms and interrogation of prisoners and everything would be more at home in a different game, as it paused the action of the game to deliver minutes-long monologues where it would shower me with proper nouns and names that I kind of recognized but didn't remember the character associated with it. It made for a confusing and rushed introduction to what I think is centuries of history with the setting and characters, which is ironic because whenever the cutscenes or monologues happened I always thought they were WAY too long. There are a lot of ways to get around this, but I'll leave it at that. If you enjoyed the story that's awesome, I probably would have too if it was in a different game or presented differently.Combat is fun, but there is seldom time between enemy attacks to get a full combo in or use the fancy moves you unlock, so either I was playing wrong or sometimes they feel a little useless.The map is also expansive for a game that isn't incredibly long, with each area feeling interesting and unique. My only issue with it was due to lack of labeling and notation I got lost a lot, and I feel like that might be an issue a lot of player have. I understand games like this can have this quality where you get lost while playing, and while that works for other games like this one, I didn't feel any joy or satisfaction of adventure and discovery when I got lost in this game, just frustration.Those are my thoughts, maybe these things weren't an issue for you and that's good! Like I said, I enjoyed this game, but wanted to voice my thoughts on some things I thought could be improved. I'd recommend it and would be interested in seeing more games from this team in the future! They certainly have talent, so I'd love to see what they do with it next.

_childDocuments_.review: Good grief I love the idea of this game. Steampunk magic, nifty traversal, well designed sprites. The combat is wrecking me. Not because it's difficult, but because it goes on for a full 2 cycles too long. It's the same for every enemy, two hits, dodge through, two hits, dodge through. And its boring. Plus the fact that every enemy is a damage sponge means you get in this cycle repeating continuously doing the same thing over and over again. Take 25% of all enemy health off to lessen the tedium!

_childDocuments_.review: Yes and no.    The writing  fine.. but it wasn't voice acted and I quickly lost interest and skipped through 95% of it.It takes  (I had it running longer whilst AFK).  I finished at 99% map explored &  all of the collectables and was happy to leave it at that.The , though I think I had to buy some items from a shop to fully enable this.  You can also pin markers on your map.  Before the final battle I got to do some map cleanup and went backtracking to find all of the marked treasure chests and skill point containers.Unfortunately   It would introduce a new biome, you would explore that biome and then the story would progress and you'd then start on another biome.  The way the game opens up reminded me a bit of how  did it.  So it's not like a typical metroidvania where you are exploring into many different areas all the time.  That said, these areas were fun to explore when you aren't being interrupted by the dialogue.  The final biome perhaps shows the game at its best, where paths would frequently weave in and out of a large main room as you climb/fight/explore your way to the top. and they are stock standard ones.To attack you have a directional slash and a button for heavy attacks.  You also have a gun, but can only fire it after hitting an enemy a few times to build up its charge meter.To get out of harms way there is a back-dash and a regular dash which only work when standing on the ground.     I don't think I died to any of them and by the time I got to the last few fights I just mashed attack + heavy attack and barely bothered to try and avoid the bosses attacks. The game has a skill tree which is mostly passives, and works a bit like a mini version of the one in  that you might have seen in ,  and the like.The pixel art style reminded me of Souldiers and Blasphemous.  The music was pretty decent.As a game, Gestalt is pretty solid & fun, despite leaving me wanting in a lot of areas. _childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty good metroidvania in terms of controls and visuals.  The story so far wasn't terribly interesting, but that's not what I bought the game for anyway.  What gets the thumbs down for me is the enemy and boss design.  For bosses, you have to stun them using bullets to do any real damage to them.  In order to get bullets, you have to hit them.  Here's the problem: if you don't stun the boss in one go, they recover their stun meter.  With one of the bosses, the max amount of bullets you have at the time isn't enough to stun them and they have an invincibility phase as well where they can just undo all the stun you just did.  It's tedious.  Normal enemies are also tedious and really spongey.  There are none that you don't have to completely halt your progress for to deal with in the exact manner in which it has to be dealt with.  Once in a while you'll have the ammo to stun one of them, which is nice, but relief from the tedium every few enemies is really not something that's a selling point.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really wanted to like this. Story was interesting, gameplay had potential, but in the end, game was really short(less than 9 hours for 100%), and story is just incomplete?(I don't know if ending is a set up for eventual sequel, or planned to continue on updates, but not getting conclusion felt very anti climatic).
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: In all honesty this is a GREAT game..but there is just SO MUCH exposition. The gameplay is fun as all hell and the attacks and abilities are flashy but not obnoxious. Most movement feels good and smooth too, but the only problem is that every single conversation feels like 10 hours of exposition. It got to the point where I dreaded going back to complete a mission cause I was afraid of being locked down for another  "As you know...". It got to the point where I just started skipping dialogue and I don't think this game deserves that. A lot of love was put into this game, and I understand that some people might really like the lore dumps, but when I play a Metroidvania I'm there for gameplay, not a visual novel. I love a great story, but many of the conversations could have been cut down and put into a codex entry. Just too much all at once. I haven't finished the game and i don't think I will, unfortunately.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game with lacking gameplay when compared to the visuals. Combat isn't engaging, and the rpg leveling system makes you overpowered ridiculously quickly. This isn't reflected in normal gameplay as enemies scale with you and often do not allow you to use any of your cool new tricks because they die too quickly when you'd have the opportunity to. Bosses let you use your cool things, but die in 15-20 seconds after the first or second boss so it's short lived. Platforming isn't engaging and two sections in particular are absolutely mind-numbing. Other mechanics are not well thought out enough to warrant use or are so vital to general gameplay there is no reason to use anything else under any circumstances. Shorter than you'd think and no better for it. Story begins with lots of exposition and ends with somehow more exposition that tells you even less. Cutscenes are plentiful and rarely important enough to disrupt gameplay flow as they always do. Characters are universally one-note but pretend to not be, despite in every cutscene having essentially the same conversation as the last four in a row. It is hard to care about anything going on in the story. Pacing is thrown out of the window towards the end and the main villain is pulled out of the collective asses of every character you've met. The main character is the most important character to the story and has almost zero agency, as well she is not involved in 95% of story cutscene conversations. She isn't even present. Gestalt is unpolished and unfinished. The game is like a freshly baked loaf of artisanal bread with an absolutely stunning crust, but when you cut into it, the dough inside is still raw and bubbling.TLDR: Gorgeous game with not-well thought out mechanics that was clearly rushed to completion.If you enjoy it, that's wonderful.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: went into this game completely blind after i saw the thumbnail in a fireborn video. absolutely no regrets. it's a steampunk fantasy metroidvania with a hot lady PC and i am gay.while as a metroidvania it's not exactly revolutionary in its mechanics, it succeeds well in what i think is the most important aspect of a game: the aesthetic. gestalt knows exactly what its look is and absolutely nails it. background art is phenomenal, and makes excellent use of dramatic setpieces that stand out and really mark the different locations (my personal favorite was the scrap sea area). continuing from the aesthetic, i cant stress enough how delightful the vibe and art direction are. the double jump is you shooting your supercharged revolver downwards and jumping from the recoil, just to name one thing. the gun and sword combo ends up having a swashbuckly piratey feel and when you unlock special moves for the sword they have just the perfect amount of rule-of-cool flourish the music was a highlight too, each track feels at home in the environment but shares certain motifs between areas. i especially liked the foundry area music, it had a cool twangy string instrument that reminded me a bit of a shovel guitar, which feels like the kind of instrument a foundry worker would play. i look forward to owning the soundtrack!it's not an especially long game, i got just under 9 hours of playtime in it, but it's intensely intriguing and just fun to play. there's enough depth in the combat system to allow for some really cool options without ending up with some moves that never get used. upgrades never felt like they were coming too fast or slow, with a few minor upgrades (attack damage +5% etc) required to unlock the major upgrades (new attack in attack chain, new special, gun inflicts poison). bosses weren't terribly difficult (except for one which i think is a semi-scripted loss because it lets you pass without defeating it if you die 3 times) but most were extremely visually impactful. the final boss is a hell of a setpiece but i had unlocked every single upgrade so i kinda steamrolled it. i never had any problem with attacks that felt unfair or super fast. overall it may be a bit of a tough sell at 2 dollars per hour of playtime (at the price i paid) but i still highly recommend it. it's a game that knows exactly what it's trying to be and leans hard into its most defining feature to great effect. it perfectly scratched the steampunk fantasy media itch for me, being exactly what i wanted from a steampunk metroidvania, and if that sounds good to you then i dont know if you'll find a better game for it
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful metroidvania with an interesting story, easily-readable and pretty pixel graphics, and a good soundtrack.  Plus, you get to pet dogs as a challenge! What's not to love? (I think it's a pity the demo isn't still available, since it did a really good job of communicating the quality of the game and its vibe.)It's not Dead Cells: there's dialogue between characters and a story unfolding. For me that's a positive thing, and given it's tagged as "Story Rich" I wouldn't have thought it'd be a surprise, but apparently it's worth flagging.  Reminds me of the Castlevania games in a good way.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A great experience, for its wonderful animations, music, worldbuilding and combat. This is the type of ambitious Metroidvania that I want to support with my wallet. It's perfect on Steam Deck too.  I only regret that the intricate steampunk world was difficult to get into since the heavy exposition can also be quite wordy and obscure. Hoping for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I remember a time when Metroidvania games used to mean you were getting a game that was light on story, but heavy on action platforming. Gestalt is entirely the opposite. Outside of an RPG, I can't ever recall having to wade through so many tedious dialogues to progress. It becomes unbelievably frustrating, and trying to skip through them with a button mash often results in the inadvertent pressing of a speech option. It is also somewhat ironic when you consider that the entire MV genre is built, primarily, upon two seminal games that contained very few NPC interactions with next to no dialogue (Metroid and SotN).Aside from that gripe, Gestalt is decent enough. The game looks good, the gameplay is decent, and the controls are reasonably fluid, but can lag a bit. The only problem is the narrative driven nature of it. If you like narrative heavy games, you'll love this. If you don't like the action being constantly interrupted by long meaningless waffle sections, I'd give it a miss.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game because I love Metroidvanias, and it's a serviceable one.  But it's short and the difficulty starts high and peters out around halfway through.  Paired with how it ends, this is a half to one third of a great game.  If you could get it for about 50% off, it was be a great game that I would recommend, but unless more gets added, this is not worth its full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is gorgeous with an excellent soundtrack and tight controls. Unfortunately, it is let down by its constant overbearing and terribly mediocre dialogue. This is the game's greatest flaw, but there are others that dulled the experience for me: the map layouts are uninteresting and fairly straightforward for this type of game, and the combat is very one-note (and becomes trivial as the game progresses).I did not feel that I wasted my time playing Gestalt to completion, but I also find it hard to recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer:  Good game.  Want more.  Good buy if A) it's your first Metroidvania, B) you must try any and all Metroidvanias, or C) it's on sale.Points:             + Beautiful sprite work and animation                        + Solid gameplay and controls.  Couple of moves are finicky, but otherwise good.                        + Good music                        + Easy to understand mechanics                        0 Not very challenging to longtime genre fans                        0 Scope is very tight.   No wasted mechanics or padded / unfinished zones                        0 Excess resources, so you'll max out most of everything even doing the bare minimum.                        - Story is functional.  Twist is predictable and is only withheld because the antagonist doesn't interact                                directly with the MC till the very end                        - Zero replay value.   If you 100% everything on your first play through, which isn't that hard, there's no                                 reason to come back.                        - World feels under developed.
