_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for a long time, and finally played the full release after playing the demo a few months before. Let's get the obvious stuff out of the way: the game looks absolutely gorgeous, the steampunk aesthetic is nailed perfectly, the pixel art is fantastic, character designs are very nice, backgrounds are colorful and different areas of the game are easily identifiable and memorable. The soundtrack is also phenomenal, full of epic orchestral pieces accompanying boss battles.Gameplay works in typical metroidvania fashion: the player must traverse the game's world looking for upgrades and new abilities that open new paths to explore. Controls are quick and responsive and there are a lot of special moves making the combat varied and enjoyable, even if the regular enemies are somewhat spongy specially at the beginning of the game. The player has access to ranged attacks, though bullets are very scarce because they depend on an energy meter that has to be refilled either by using melee attacks or by finding energy generators scattered through the map. Enemies have a "break meter" in addition to HP meter, and will be stunned momentarily when such meter is depleted. Some enemies are very resistant to physical attacks until their break meter is depleted so a combination of regular attacks and break attacks (mostly by using special bullets) is required, which adds to the variety. Health can be recovered by using healing flasks, which are refilled at save points and can be increased in quantity by finding certain resources. There are also accessories providing different stat boosts and an skill tree which allows to unlock more stat boosts, new attacks, accessory slots and additional bullets. There is an experience system which main function is to provide additional skill points to be used in the skill tree. Different areas of the skill tree are unlocked progressively through the game each time a key ability is acquired. Overall the game is on the easier side, including the several boss battles which display patterns that are easy to learn resulting in short but fun battles. The game can still be challenging to impatient or inexpert players but it's not as grueling as other titles in the genre. The map works in a way that rooms are connected to other adjacent rooms by lines, like a flowchart, instead of being grid-based or otherwise representative of the real geography of each area. This can be confusing at first but it works well enough and rooms are usually easy enough to navigate without getting lost. Some rooms however are quite large and have multiple exits, requiring to be traversed several times through different entry points or revisited after getting a new traversal ability, and shortcuts can be opened in order to facilitate navigation. Other areas have multiple "depth" layers representing indoors and outdoors locations and can be harder to navigate. Special markers can be added later on in the game to point to the location of collectibles. The game is fairly linear both between different regions and inside each region, but there are NPCs that provide additional quests which usually entail defeating a certain number of a certain enemy type or finding a certain item. Fast travel is also unlocked later in the game, and every area of the game can be revisited for missing collectibles.And now the controversial stuff: the story. The setup is very good and it plays well to the strengths of the steampunk genre, there is some exposition in the initial cutscene about the previous history, the current state of the world and such. There is an underlying political intrigue and references to a possible catastrophe that are alluded to in the numerous cutscenes scattered through the game. The thing is that there are a lot of cutscenes, which is not common in the genre, and some of these cutscenes do not feature the main character nor have anything to do with the events occurring at the time during gameplay, and they feel like they belong in an RPG rather than a metroidvania. I don't mind the abundance of cutscenes, it was quite surprising, but these can be annoying to players looking for an action game with less text or interruptions, or to players not interested in the game plot. That being said the characters and the general plot are interesting enough and at times it is not clear who is friend and who is foe, who the true antagonists are or what are their intentions. I heard that cutscenes cannot be skipped but they can be sped up, personally I haven't tried to do either as I was genuinely invested in the plot. Dialogue can be a little melodramatic and/or poetic, which is fine by me, and there are some spelling errors here and there but nothing too serious to detract from the experience. HOWEVER, and I must say this, I was very disappointed by the game's ending for several reasons, the main of which is that the story doesn't really end, it rather just stops, leaving me hanging with a horrible cliffhanger that may or may not be resolved. I'd like to see more of the game world and a conclusion to the story via a DLC or something but for now this is all we have. Some other points of the plot seem a little rushed, and at times there are huge dumps of exposition or revelations that suddenly take place. The story is truly the weakest point of the game, but honestly I think it isn't usually the main strength of this kind of games anyways. It is such a shame that the effort put into the game's narrative didn't result in a better outcome but it is what it is and the rest of the game is good enough for me to overlook this weakness. I appreciate however the effort made in conveying a narrative through dialogue instead of obscure, cryptic and mostly optional lore references like other games in the genre like to do.Overall Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is very good, I had a lot of fun playing it and the positives are enough for me to outweigh the negatives I found. It's not groundbreaking or anything but it is certainly an enjoyable, shorter, easier and relaxing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A good but not great metroidvania. Its not terribly long but not aggressively short. Progress is quite linear with backtracking for collectibles in the form of health refill upgrades, and equipment. There's a leveling system which unlocks new abilities and increases power. There's a bit of a balance issue in that the game appears to get easier the further you get. Especially if you are playing a somewhat completionist manner.Art is good, music is atmospheric. The story is fairly engaging though you see the plot twist near the end coming a mile away. Ending includes a rather... abrupt development that doesn't seem to contribute much but i think is set-up for a sequelFairly limited key rebinding, which is a bit annoying, you can't bind mouse buttons at all without a external program. If i were to point to the biggest flaw is that the game doesn't appear to excell in any one particular aspect. Everything is good or competent. Nothing is brilliant.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good but has some critical flaws. First of all, it is easy (I died 4 times in the entire game). Second boss fights are not good, especially the final one. third enemy-level system is completely useless, in my opinion. Fourth, I didn't get into the story, but the final cutsene left a bad taste in my mouth. It was so anticlimatic. There are some little flaws I forgot, but in the end, this is a short and fun game. I wholeheartedly believe Metamorphosis Games will learn from their mistakes and make a masterpiece in their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game! It's short and relatively easy and if you're familiar with medroidvanias, the simple map isn't too bad. Honestly the story was a bit too much up front and I kinda zoned out but that's okay. Hollow Knight literally had no story for me and that was fine. At least this game doesn't have a deathless run!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love a good metroidvania, so it's a shame this isn't one.It looks nice and the controls are LARGELY pretty solid, except for a few hiccups in the default settings that allow you to accidentally burn healing charges until you realize someone made the bafflingly common mistake of binding something to a *stick press* which is the sort of insane behavior that should get developers institutionalized. You can jump, dodge roll, "backstep"(an acrobatic backwards roll that's on a trigger button while your forward dodge roll is on one of the four main buttons, why???? and why not just have a single directional dodge instead of two distinct dodges?), slash, etc. though the dodge rolls always seem to have less I-frames than you'd expect and a slightly too long recharge time. The main star of things is being allowed to mantle though it sometimes feels a bit less fiddly that you're expected to try jumps where you can land just one pixel within the nebulous Mantling Zone(tm).By and large! The movement is fine, except to a distinct lack of a double jump which metroidvanias should be legally obligated to start you with or give you within the first hour of gameplay.Where it comes apart is the combat. You have an very short reach on your main swing, especially the non-forwards swings(i.e. up and down) that make using them fiddly, which is annoying but ultimately fine. Dead Cells had short-range weapons I loved to use. You've got an extendable light-swing combo, a pistol(bullets recharged by hitting enemies with your sword) intended to break enemy "guard" and stun them(supposedly the sword can also do this, but it does so much health damage compared to guard damage that I cannot comprehend it ever stunning an enemy before killing them), and you get various "charged" sword moves.Part of the problem there is that enemies are pretty fast, you can get in maybe one, max two, normal swings, before you need to dodge. Thus, the charge moves are useless except against stunned enemies that you could just hit instead. Simultaneously, that also means that your long combos are completely pointless because there are no "pain states" or "hit stun" on enemies, you don't slow them at all, they completely no-sell your swings, so halfway through your extended combo they just walk up and punch you in the face.But once again this is tolerable, except... the bosses. The bosses are surprisingly lame. The three bosses I put up with before quitting had only one phase, but so much health that I was expecting at least three phases out of them, which means that you very quickly "solve" them and their two or three moves and then just have to be extremely patient to whittle them down unless you slip up and take a bit of damage. The third boss had more health than the previous two and so I saw an extremely tedious pattern developing where I'd need to bring a book and a packed lunch for whenever the final boss occurred and decided to peace out. Aside from the combat, Gestalt also suffers from some very bad maps, which is very annoying considering that it's a Metroidvania that expects you to loop back with expanded abilities every now and then to collect stuff and increase numbers. But every map just tells you that there's *a room*, not what's in it, and some areas are truly fouled by "interior" maps that clog up their pathfinding miserable.Plus it also does a thing that drives me personally completely insane which is that the very first area has some parts you need later game abilities to access but immediately after finishing the very first area, you're restricted from going back there for a decently long time. Drives me completely up the wall in terms of mentally keeping track of what I need to go back for. Miserable design. All in all it's really a shame because I was very interested in seeing where things would go at the start, even if the storytelling was displaying some worrying aspects, like deus ex machina items that didn't really get any kind of introduction but were apparently always there, while feeling, story-wise, like something that the main character should pick up or comment on about halfway through the first area and THEN finding out what they're for or something. Additionally also some bugged-out textboxes with overlapping text which felt like a bizarre thing to miss, and a considerable number of typos that it feels like should've been spotted and cleared out a while ago.Can't really recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Disappointing. While the artwork is incredible, and the music is pretty decent. The gameplay feels really stiff. Also the story isn't very engaging and you are constantly assaulted by walls of text. At least they added a fast forward button. Once you reach the first town, you'll wish the character had a sprint ability or fast travel because running around takes forever. I couldn't recommend this to anyone as it feels half baked. It's a shame because it had the potential to have been something amazing.Couple other things that I forgot. The area design is awful. While the assets looks great, a lot of the areas feel copy/pasted. It lacks that finesse that a game like Hollow Knight would have. It's weird that it's like this, because the main city has so much detail painted into it. The travel map is also a mess. Just squares with some lines attaching the zones. With such a beautiful aesthetic, they really dropped the ball on including a badass steampunk map.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty straightforward metroidvania; it doesn't bring much of anything new, but it gets the movement down pretty well and from that aspect it's fun to play. The pixel art is nice, and the game looks good. The music is nice. It unfortunately doesn't get much right past that.The biggest issue is that I didn't have fun fighting any of the enemies: most of them have very few attacks, but the cadence at which they attack is very high and the only way to stagger them is with your gun, which requires you to get some distance and be grounded, and you don't always have ammunition available. So you play this hit-dodge-hit game over and over, even with some of the most basic enemies, and it's just tedious. Also flying enemies have particularly obnoxious movement, which is a common source of frustration. There wasn't a single enemy or boss that I enjoyed.You never really get to feel powered up, which makes retreading your steps take longer than you might prefer, so I didn't have much impetus to try and 100% the map. I did both finish the game, and unlock nearly all of the tech tree, but all of the more powerful moves are tied to your ammunition, which even when fully unlocked is at a premium.That said it was quite easy, which is really for the best because otherwise it would just be frustrating as hell.The game wants to exposition at you constantly. The story is serviceable enough, but has basically no pay off, and so the litany of text boxes is just completely not worth it. It feels like you're interrupted every fifth room by a cutscene: it's too much.I'd give it a "neutral" if I could; it's by no means terrible but I also wouldn't tell anyone to go out and buy it. Sorry.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Not spectacular for how long it was in development. I was stoked and had this on my wishlist for ages. Turns out a lot is weird here. The game doesn't seem to be sure what it wants to be, 2D dark souls clone, metroidvania, platformer, and it shows. It ends up being OK in all departments overall, with rather obvious problems when it comes to pacing and generally some mechanics in general, e.g. levelling. Levelling seems fairly pointless as of now, unless you unlock certain moves which are absolutely not optional for some enemy types to be beaten, so I am not sure what the hell this is even in the game for. It provides you with an illusion of choice which you very much don't have. Also, in terms of metroidvania mechanics in general? This game shines by the fact that there is zero originality to it. You have your everyday metroid standard mechanics. Doublejump, check, wallbreaker, check, etc., so really NOTHING to write home about. That being said, the lore is pretty interesting and the game looks and feels like a coherent world and looks very good in general. But that's not really an argument for me to pretend this game is better than any other generic Metroidvania. What is most worrysome is that Fireshine is an Enad Global 7 subsidiary, and I literally saw negative reviews with 30 clown awards in less than 20 hours of release while total reviews were ~80... The same review is now removed. Community mod is literally a level 0 steam account with no information, etc., etc. Quite a few red flags. The game would be meh and getting it on discount would be ok if you're severely starved to add another metroidvania to your list, but there is some shady ♥♥♥♥ going on here that's not OK. Bottom line: They sell their game as "nostalgia fueled action adventure title" and I had to chuckle a bit since it is none of these things. It's a mashup of Metroid, Castlevania SotN and 2D darksouls titles with A BARE MINIMUM of what you would expect in the first two categories. So, what exactly is nostalgia here? The game lacks everything that makes me want to replay SotN or Metroid, the pacing is stop and go with a ton of cutscenes crammend in there at weird points in time that are extremely disruptive to the flow of the game, so "action" is... arguable, and the adventure is pretty much taken out by the fact that it a very linear experience at the end of the day with a bare minimum of exploration to be done by choice of the player. Feels like you have zero agency. Add to that some questionable things going on with negative reviews and that does it for me. Literally not a single metroidvania that I have in my library checks all these negatives.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited for this game. I had tried the demo during a steamfest and really enjoyed it. Nice pixel art, nice animations, nice music. The gameplay felt a little limited but I chalked it up to it being a demo. "The final game will open more I am sure" I thought. But the final game completely and fully disappointed me.Maybe it's because I had just finished playing Astlibra before starting Gestalt, but Gestalt felt really restrictive in its gameplay, where you can only dodge as a defensive mechanic and almost all battles turn into a "do 1 hit and dodge/jump" over and over until your enemy is dead. You have melee combos that are mostly useless because the enemies don't really give you the time or opportunity to use them. You can use your gun to break enemies so you can do those combos, sure, but for a good while you only have 1 or 2 bullets so you can do that just some times as you gotta recharge your gun by hitting enemies. In the end, I found the battle system to be boring as there was little opportunity to really customize my experience.My next issue was with the fundamental design choices made within the game. Because of this type of game, and because you start getting the ability to, for example, see chests or dogs that you haven't picked up yet pop up on the map as you advance, you're gonna be running around a bit through levels you already ran through as you progress. So, as I had to run around a bit, I kept wondering why it was decided to make specific teleport rooms instead of making you teleport between save rooms. That decision ended up making me run around between levels to reach some far away room to pick a dog, or break a wall, or pick a chest more than I would have liked, increasing my annoyance. And that annoyance was further fueled by some levels not being fun to navigate.The final hit was delivered by the ending. Despite not feeling the gameplay, despite being annoyed by certain design decisions, I was still interested in the story and the characters. I was interested in seeing where this story was going, to get answers, to have a conclusion. And this game spat in my face with an ending that says nothing at all. It shows nothing at all, it resolves nothing. What did I run around for? No real answer to what the abyss is, who is the "she" mentioned toward the end, or why a character that should have died was actually alive.Now, as I said at the start, before this game I got done playing Astlibra. That game has so much meat that after you reach what you think is the end, it actually keeps going and expanding and it keeps answering questions. So playing a way shorter game that doesn't even begins to give you answers once you reach the end feels like an even bigger insult.I really wanted to like this game. I really did. I even got every achievement for it but it just ended up disappointing me on such a level that I don't know... once I reached the post credit scene I just...This game feels unfinished, story wise, as far as I am concerned. It's like a whole half of the game is missing, the half that explains things, that shows you the other side, the half with the answers to the questions raised during the exposition part.Maybe one day the developers will answer those questions through a sequel or an expansion dlc. Or maybe they wont, who knows. But for now, I just can't recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is a fairly linear, and short, Metroidvania / Search-Action game. The player takes on the role of Aletheia, a Soldner who fights the enemies of humanity by blade and gun. The world of Canaan has fallen to calamity after a brush with the terrifying power of the Abyss, and its inhabitants survive in the Steam City, the only livable place in the land, awaiting the dying gasps of a world which nears its end. A capable fighter but not willing to join the Vanguard who defends the realm, Aletheia instead goes on her own investigation. While not everything is paid off and there's a pretty clear sequel-hook (which I hope we see explored in a future game), many of the core mysteries are eventually explained. I really enjoy the world Metamorphosis Games have created.Combat is largely melee-based with your gun supplementing your attack-flow. You need to melee in order to earn ammo back for your ranged shots, which largely hold the purpose of shredding enemy Break Bars. You've seen such 'secondary' health or posture-bars in other games, by other names, for sure. Crush an enemy's break gauge and deal massively increased damage to them. Accessories offer some light buildcrafting. What do you value? Raw damage? Crit? Break-damage so you can stagger and crumple enemies faster? Your sword, or your revolver? The choices you have don't make a huge difference in playstyle, but it's nice to pick something you enjoy leaning on, and then indeed go ahead and lean. Consumables grant temporary Buffs which tend to last either 30s, 60s, or 2 Minutes. These are basically just raid-buffs, you probably want to pop them all just before fighting a boss. It's a good time. The art and animation-work go crazy in this game. The music also helps the world of Canaan convey itself. Some of the boss music, while pretty standard for the genre, is appropriately epic, so that's nice. There is a lot of dialogue in this game. It won't work for everyone, but it did for me, because I liked this universe and wanted to know more. For those who don't want to take a few minutes to read long conversations between characters after bosses, this element of Gestalt will be bothersome. Not a difficult game by any means. On my first playthrough which lasted about 8 hours (with 4 more chilling AFK and AltTabbed) I 100%ed the map and got all Achievements, only dying a single time which was due to a bug and/or getting unlucky. Because of this, it's a pretty good introduction or spicy taste of Metroidvania to newcomers who may otherwise find themselves intimidated by the genre. You're unlikely to get lost, as well, as Gestalt's worldmap marks exits and entrances quite clearly, and if you explore thoroughly you end up being able to buy Maps that display every single type of collectible (Orbs, Chests, Ability Points, Dogs, etc) I enjoyed Gestalt a lot. Short and sweet, nice music, brisk exploration. You'll probably have some idea of if it's for you if you read this.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game has a good foundation. But I would not pay for it at the price it is. The ending was a frustrating, anticlimatic mess. The bosses are far too easy to even be called bosses past the second or third one that you fight, and though the game has elements of a metroidvania, it has no real sense of exploration. In fact, there is even a place in the game, where you *should* be able to go there at any time, but there are random platforms that only spawn in once certain story criteria are met. There is so much dialogue and gameplay interruptions, and that usually doesn't bother me if a game's story is solid, but this is an example of how to *not* tell a story. In conclusion: Pay the extra $10-ish USD  for Nine Sols, you will be much, much more satisfied with your purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm recommending the game because the art direction, story, and overall presentation is pretty cool. I couldn't get past the amount of unskippable dialogue, cut scenes, and cinematics in the game. _childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I finished my playthrough with a ton of mixed emotions. I am glad I played this, and want to see what the studio has to offer next, but this game ultimately feels like an extremely ambitious project that didn't meet its own high marks. It seeks to tell an epic, lore-rich story with compelling, witty, and intelligent characters ... but the writing often falls flat, feels frankly derivative (see if you can count the number of Shakespeare references), or just insists upon itself. The game wants to TELL you that its story is worth paying attention to rather than having a story inherently worthwhile. That feels like the main problem with Gestalt: What the game thinks it is versus what it actually is. The game wants to be an RPG, but its RPG mechanics are so shallow they are basically completely ignorable. It's laughable that there is a consumable item letting you respec your skill points, because there is literally no wrong way to invest your skill points -- by the end of my playthrough I had all the nodes I cared about comfortably filled, due to progressing in level so fast throughout the game. It wants to be a Blasphemous/Hollow Knight like, and while it starts to feel like Blasphemous especially as you gain more abilities, the combat and movement ultimately lacked the necessary polish to meet the high standards set by its contemporaries. The map is confusing and barely helpful, but at the same token almost completely unnecessary unless you're going for side content, which is itself shallow. Where this game succeeds at overwhelmingly are its visuals. This game is GORGEOUS, some of the best pixel art I've seen in a long time. The backgrounds and vistas are breathtaking, and present some awesome and unique worldbuilding ideas. Unfortunately, the great ideas this game and its narrative have are let down by how half-cooked everything feels. The sound design is the best example of this -- things that often really don't need sound effects get them, while things that desperately do in a game like this, such as healing, have little or no aural feedback. I feel like this game could lead to a much-improved sequel, and I want to see what this studio does ... but I don't think this game as it stands is worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania: progression, leveling, items, backtracking map for good rewards, there's a story happening but isn't mind-blowing, bosses are just hard enough not to want to rage quit, music is really good, graphics are nostalgic, etc. Recommend to any Metroidvania fans who want to play for the experience not necessarily for a story or challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A cool metroidvania on the shorter side (10-12 hours for 100% completion)- gorgeous pixel art - cool combat and traversal- for once it manages to make the steampunk theme actually interesting. SOmehow people seem to be bothered by the story bits in between levels but I found them pretty engaging. It's a cool game very worth checking out(For French speakers, the translation is unaccurate at times I recommend switching to English)
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often leave reviews of games, but this one I loved. It IS a Metroidvania, but it's relatively linear, but I really enjoyed the little amount of backtracking for treasures there was. The music is banging, you can really feel the emotion behind it, and the character art is superb. Also, the story was incredibly catching. Overall, 9/10, do suggest
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt is a very light Metroidvania with a Steampunk setting. What it excels at is  the fantastic movement and combat flow. The visuals(while extremely ugly on a big screen due to no resolytion options) are an absolute treat on a Handheld like the Steam Deck.The constant dry dialogue text windows popping up with not much to say break the game's neck though. I gave it a chance as I thought it was just the tutorial but the whole game keeps being interrupted by dialogues that aren't fun to read(typos, grammar issues and nonsense story). An 8/10 for gameplay, but sadly an overall 4-5/10. More gameplay, less text and this game would be among the best in the genre. I personally leave it at 2hrs and don't want to continue playing because I don't see it getting better. Even mid-story it keeps interrupting my "fun time". And a game that interrupts my "fun time" is not worth playing.Sadly cannot recommend it. The developers took a few bad choices here and may learn from it. I wish them luck on their next game though. Very nice and communicative folks in Discord.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Aw.. so if steam allowed for a more distinguishing ranking i would give this game maybe 4/10. Maybe.And i will push the not recommended button with a heavy heart.So Pros:- Graphics are great - The Story starts out good with enough mystery to keep you going and interested and- in contradiction to reviews i have read - i like the way it's presented, makes me kinda nostalgic and for everyone criticising it, Iam not sure what you want from a video game, not everything that's indie is either Hollow Knight or Celeste^^- I like the Skill System and the ambition behind it- i like that they chose the correct ingredients for a good metroidvania, it got the classic flee from lava scene and the on the train fight going so....BUT:Cons:- The Combat System is very slow, the enemies are pretty lobotomized and the skills you aquire in the skill tree largely don't matter. It's just kinda bland sadly. If you die, it's because you are too lazy to learn the most simplified attack pattern.- You can find actual gear to equip and items to use. Which is nice. NGL, you don't need it though for playing the game. I think they would have needed to crank the numbers and make it more challenging to survive from save point to save point. I fought the Final Boss while part-time having a conversation on Discord. Per Keyboard. So might be too easy.- Platforming is kind of none existing and gets introduced rather late. The controls feel a bit vague there. - While all the ingredients are there, they are very simple.- length is a thing, i finished the game in 7 hours, savestate timer says 5:xx hours playtime.  If i'd wanted to 100% maybe another hour and thirty minutes, but there is just nothing that i can actually achieve by that. I think the replayability is also zero, there no further difficulty and so on.- AND the ultimate reason: the story kept me going. it begins to wobble towards the last 3rd of the game and it makes quite the brutal crashlanding, it's literally one of the most disappointing endings in any game i have played in the last two years (about a 100 games i' guess). Summary:I really want this game to be good honestly, i have changed my mind while writing this like 3 times which recommendation to give. Overall it just doesn't cut it for the roundabout 20€, 5:xx hours is pretty darn short and effing hell there are so many games being released in that genre and segment.I had a problem with a save state not loading and requested support from the devs, they answered in very short time (10 mins) and were actually able to help me get back into the game and finish my playthrough, which i highly appreciate.I think it should have either been kept simpler or left longer in development. I think the Devs have the right idea how to do this genre right and i hope future titles will be more on the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not really one for the platform Metroidvania type games, but I'm really enjoying this title.  Great graphics and music, solid gameplay loop, and the story is engaging!  I really liked the challenge level for the bosses I've seen so far - not easy, but not so difficult that it took away from my enjoyment - very satisfying to figure out the best approach! _childDocuments_.review: A very nice metroidvania, with decent combat and plenty of customization for it through accessories and the skilltree (although, by endgame you will most probably have 85-95% percent unlocked). IMO, the story was a bit heavy and took control away from you too often, but was otherwise fine.Some issues I have found are that with some ranged enemies, if you stand too close to them, their shots will never hit your character.All in all, this wait has been worth it. Recommended for metroivania fans, 8/10 for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This may be one of the most mixed bag experiences I have had with a game. And honestly 99% of the game was fantastic with few complaints.  it was rough. Lets go over the good first...The visuals are stellar. Honestly when it comes to pixel art I'm easy to please, there are many games that I think look really good. Some have great animation with lots of personality, some are really cute, and others just have a great style, but very few fall into a tier of detail that is awe inspiring. Games like Metal Slug or Symphony of the Night have pixel art that I feel are a step above the rest... and Gestalt sits comfortably up there with them. The animations have so many little details and extra flourish that you can tell they really put their heart and soul into making this game's presentation as impressive as can be.Gameplay is also pretty solid, if a little easy. There is a simple flow of dodging through enemy attacks and attacking back during the roll cooldown. As someone who has done a bit of speedrunning in games like Symphony of the Night and Katana Zero I do wish there wasn't that cooldown on the roll and that I could do stuff like the backflip for just moving around quicker. That is such a minor nitpick though. The upgrades are cool, the animations for attacks read really clearly, and every time I unlocked something new I had to just sit and play around with it and gush about it. There's some interesting cancels and quick turns you can do with the attacks that come out of the roll/backflip too. I also really appreciated the gun mechanics, how having the gun didn't completely overpower everything and was a resource you had to think carefully on using. Luckily anywhere you needed bullets/charge attacks for had a nearby energy refill so you can't accidentally softlock yourself. Game also has one of my favorite features in a metroidvania, the ability to put your own pins on the map. It was easy to mark down where stuff I would need to revisit later with other abilities were and come back to. Navigation was a breeze and I never felt lost trying to find stuff or felt the need to resort to looking up a map online. Also, mostly a flavor thing, but I loved that the collectables were corgis. Adorable choice, 10/10 no notes. Also the reward for finding them all was  cool (even if it did kind of break the game and trivialize the last couple of boss fights). All that positive said, I did find the game a bit easy. Bosses were really interesting mechanically and I loved their attack patterns but even before the OP upgrade given by the corgis I didn't really have any fights that stood out as a real challenge which was a bit of a shame. Would have been cool to have some secret side super bosses or something to really test one's familiarity with the combat. Or at the very least some extra forms, especially for the last two fights which went way too quickly.Now for something that is going to be much more hit and miss for people... the pacing and story. Personally I enjoy a good story with plenty of cutscenes and dialog in my Metroidvanias. Some of my favorites in the genre are really text heavy experiences and I think that's fine. And the story here, while nothing groundbreaking or exceptionally memorable, is good enough. I enjoyed it, even if I could see half the twists and reveals coming  before they start to hint at or address them. At no point was I bored with the narrative or just wishing they would "get on with it already." That said, cutscenes popped up a tad too frequently and interrupted the flow of gameplay a bit. It would have been nice to have more time and more space to explore beyond the narrative bits. There is also an opposite issue with the side quests where very few had much narrative to them and most of them were just "kill x enemies" type stuff. Which is fine, I didn't mind them and was always excited to find a new bounty board but it would have been cool to have bounties that were more than just "farm kill 10 of this new enemy." The couple of side quests that did have some narrative to them were nice but still felt like they could do more with them. Have rolling quests with reoccurring characters that build up a questline and narrative that says something about those characters. Like the barkeep introduced early on who I expected to have more going on but basically stops being relevant past the tutorial/intro sequence.Now... about the ending... To summarize without spoilers... I see what they are going for... not sure it's gonna work/pay off... and until a potential sequel or something shows up to explain the ending sours the whole experience a bit. It leaves what would otherwise be a solid 8, maybe even 9 for me into maybe a 6/10 at best. Which leaves me in a weird place. Again I wish there was a middle ground "maybe" option for recommending a game, because while I think there is a great game here with solid gameplay and great art; I feel the ending weakens the whole thing enough that it actively worsens the whole experience. The pacing isn't great and if the story was good enough to make up for the constant interruption of gameplay it would have easily made up for it but the ending is so poorly realized and comes out of nowhere that it's hard to wholeheartedly recommend the game to people.One final nitpick I wish there was some difficulty settings or some kind of challenge mode, maybe a boss rush or something. Just something to add to the experience I think would do a lot to improve the overall package and give it some good replay value.I don't regret buying this on release and as someone who has been following and waiting on release for years I'm not really disappointed and I'm glad I got the game right away and gave it a shot. I had a lot of fun with it and think it was a gorgeous experience worth having. I just wish the ultimate payoff was a bit better. I'm interested to see what happens down the line and if there will be another game released in the series. Hopefully I won't have to wait another 4 years staring at the steam listing in my wishlist waiting for the release date to be nailed down if so.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A very nice, albeit a bit too short metroidvania. Artwork is gorgeous for the most part, and the game plays, as in movement, different attack types, most combat interactions,-almost flawlessly. I also enjoyed the worldbuilding and character writing a lot. While nothing fancy or eye-opening, the cast was likable, three-dimentional and fitting the narrative.The game overall, though, is really on the easier side. After vacuuming through most of the map my Aletheia was an unstoppable weapon of destruction that tanked everything final boss could throw at her while putting in obscene and unholy amounts of damage. The game really needs a harder difficulty option and additional modes to boost its replayabiliy and longevity.Other issue is linearity. The world of the game is huge, but it really lacks the possibility to wander around just a bit. Scale of the map does not really convert into any kind of open-ended progression. It is always a good idea to let the players "slip through thecracks" of intended path to make the game feel much wider and deeper.On the other hand there are a lot of very well done platforming sections, some devilish enough to rival those Ori jump puzzles. Also there's a nice chace sequence and a train level :3 And some nice light puzzling, though nothing that much out of ordinary. But overall the mix does not get stale at any point.So, overall, while I enjoyed the trip, the crew and the overall feeling of the journey, the game really needs some more work to become the gem it can actually be. In any case I do hope to see the sequel of this story ('cause the game does end abruptly with some uncertainty for several points of the story), as well as improvement on its current iteration.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Movement feels good. Game is gorgeous, absolutely no complaints there. But man is combat not great. Bosses aren't hard; they just have a ton of health. Regular enemies are all "hit twice then dodge away" over and over. Despite looking and feeling good to move around and play, I'm just kind of bored? For me, the story was interesting but not good enough to want to continue on. Shame 'cause this one had been on my wishlist for a long time
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I really, really want to recommend this game.  I was having a blast with it the entire time despite my primary criticism:  The game gives you a five-hit combo you'll never use past one, MAYBE two strikes, as the game's hit reactions are nonexistent-- but enemies will both hit you incredibly hard even when backtracking and stun you (with full damage) even on a one-pixel graze.The art is gorgeous, the music is nothing but bangers.  The story was pretty straightforward; I remarked to a friend that even if I could see where the plot was going I was grinning ear to ear the whole time, but... then I hit the ending.The ending ruins the game.  Everything you've done, pointless.  All the bosses, all the fights?  Doesn't matter.  There's a post-credits scene that I swear feels like it's tacked on like it's trying to smooth the ending over but does nothing.  There's no secret/true ending, there's no NG+, no challenge mode, nothing to elucidate on or expand or fix the ending, you just get stuck with "this was a really fun ride that gleefully derails itself in, literally, the final minute of the game."Bottom line:  Play it to the final boss, and then shut the game off.  You'll have a better time that way.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A very easy but good metroidvania that checks all the boxes.  I'm not a great gamer by any means and I beat the game with 0 deaths.  The story is pretty long winded and more akin to an RPG.  My biggest complaint about the story is that your character doesn't know like 80% of the story as it happens without her.  Lastly, the game just ends on a cliffhanger without tying anything up.I beat the game, 100%ing the map and leveling board, in < 10 hours.  I do not regret my time with this.  Solid B
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but it's honestly not a very good one either.  With a highly-detailed, beautiful pixel art and surprisingly good soundtrack, pretty much everything else leaves to be desired.Pros:- high-quality pixel art- soundtrack- the last two bossfights were pretty fun- the setting could've been interesting, if expanded upon in more detailCons:- game length - way too short- high focus on a story that's neither too good nor immersive - a lot of words to say not too much- way too easy - the first boss I've died to was the second to last one- not much reason to play after beating the last boss- generally feels uninspired - there's nothing unique this game has going for it - not enough enemy variety to make the whole normal/charged bullets mechanic be of any major consequence barring the enemies at the very beginning of the game- most skills in the skill tree are straight up uselessGet it on sale only when you've beaten all the good metroidvanias on the market
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty good metroidvania+I love the movement especially when you unlock Dive Kick, it made moving around the map really fun for me as you can do a little movement tech with it (by tapping jump and then immediately pressing Heavy Atk/Dive)The combat is great it reminds me a lot of the IGAvanias along with the movement (a little bit). one of the combat quirks that proved that to me is you can do a cool combat tech where you just do a short jump by only tapping then attack and immediately after landing press attack again you'll notice that there's no "lag" between the attack of when you jump and the attack of when you landed. making it seem like you can attack very fast with no lag between atk animations, I think Castlevania speedrunners call that "Land Cancelling" which I very much love because it reminded me of IGAvanias specially DoS (Dawn of Sorrow)The art style is fantastic nothing much to say about it, it's just beautiful.-I do feel that the game is short, you can complete the game in less than 10 hours or so.I didn't like the stamina mechanic but I do understand that you need to have it on this game because enemies/bosses are designed to fit the stamina mechanic otherwise it would have been a lot more easier to beat them but I personally didn't like it as I'm used to the traditional no stamina MVs.The number of bosses in the game are on the low side (about 9) and it lacks a lot of variety, you'll mostly fight humanoid bosses with the occasional big archetypes (Berserker, Brute, CK). I think there was only 1 "gigantic" archetype (MEGA M.E.S.S). The game is very linear with little backtracking.If i have to nitpick 1 mechanic on the game that I really hate which is the wall jump. I hate the way it works on this game because whenever I intend to double jump when I'm beside a wall the game seems to think that I want to wall jump which executes that move instead of double jumping, I am not actively pressing a directional key directly to the wall because I don't intend to wall jump but it does it anyway. =Great job!I am looking forward for future content updates in the game and what future changes the devs would make.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited for Gestalt but 90m in (left the game payed when I was away from my PC) but really it's not what I expected. Multiple story heavy segments that don't even involve the main character, massive exposition dump at the intro that seems to have little to do with the game so far. Enemies are damage sponges with little variety. And worst of all large in one door and out the other mazes that are a chore to navigate.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a re-edit of my initial review since I finished the game, and quite frankly this changes a lot of my initial view of the game. The game is alright for the most part but it definitely has noticeable flaws. I wont go over the numerous typos that were present/are still present despite the patch, as I believe this can be fixed in just a couple of patches in a matter of weeks. Instead I'll go over different stuff. This is your warning that SPOILERS are ahead.I'll list personal pros & cons about this game:Pros :-Extremely fluid animations & combat : The game encourages you to use your entire arsenal which I love since if all I needed to use comfortably in combat was my sword, this would've been really boring. Its also super nice that the gun has bullets that need to recharge after you hit enemies with the sword. It creates a good dynamic of combat which makes the game very unique that way.-Satisfaction over unlocks of movement abilities : This game captures really well that relieving feeling of finally getting a new ability like double jump or simply a tool to let you explore other areas you couldnt before. I know, this is standard  metroidvania behavior, but I believe they have done it in a correct manner. This couldve been horrible but it turned out great to me.-Very pleasing pixel-art : Im a sucker for pixel-art & this was what my eye first catched, and it did not disappoint with the coming areas of the game, lots of depth, detail, atmosphere, its overall really really good. -The Protagonist : Im not gonna lie with you, I just love playing a badass woman with a sword & gun, so this game already had my credit card out. Now onto the CONS of this game.Cons :-Very poor placement of dialogues : The game will throw you an absurd amount of dialogues at times & honestly it was getting really annoying after a while, so much unnecessary text to read almost as if this was a challenge for you to highlight in your head whats really important. Like key words etc as the rest was just, for the most part, meaningless chatter that brought nothing to the table except an attempt at giving characters emotions through their dead neutral faces that doesnt move regardless of the nature of the conversation that's happening. Seriously that really bothered my reading when an important & intense line is written & the characters look straight up static with only their eyes to blink to show they are alive inside.-Lack of sprites for characters, & proper cutscenes : This goes hand in hand with the dialogue problem, as the character sprites will just, so far after 9,5 hours of gametime, NEVER EVER MOVE. The only moving thing like I said is their blinking, there is no body language being shown to convey emotions or give out the feelings of the character speaking, not even a frown when something upsetting or sad has been mentioned, its just a constant slight smile and thats it. A full blown animated sprite during the dialogues isnt whats necessary here. What's necessary, is helping the player feel immersed with the emotions & personality of the characters they are witnessing & playing. This combined with the constant dialogue really killed off any desire I had to continue caring about the lore of the game. -Quests on the board : Now I dont mind at all a system like this, why not, but these quests felt a little too easy. It was just a "kill this specific enemy 10 times" & that was it, just play the game normally and your sidequest is filled automatically without having to even think about it. Would've been nice to have different quests like "get to a place in this amount of time" or "Find where that scream comes from" just different varieties of quests. Very high potential that sadly got replaced with simplicity.-Difficulty of the game : Now I am not by any means a godgamer or a super good player at video games, but the game felt way WAY too easy even for someone like me. In over 9,5 hours of game time, I died once to a standard enemy, not a single tough enemy or boss has killed me yet. I get that this was probably done on purpose as to not discourage new players who will feel intimidated with a hard game, but I think a difficulty system is really, REALLY needed at this moment, as when you make a game simple to please the players who dont want to sweat too much (which I respect), it pushes away people who are looking for a challenge in the game.-The "Story" (SPOILERS) : So, for the most part it was going pretty okay, we get to know the true identity of Aletheia (the character we play) a little bit everytime and uncover bits of lore through extensive dialogues where if you have an ounce of ADHD you will not be able to notice/care. The side characters were absolutely cosmetic in terms of depths since its REALLY hard for me to relate to any character when their facial expression remains the same stoic face despite serious dialogues going on. Now as for how the story ended :The story ended like ♥♥♥♥ pretty much. What the ♥♥♥♥ was that all about to make a side character be the actual important character in terms of lore of the game. We suddenly get this "Luke im your father" moment & then cherry on top, YOU the MAIN CHARACTER we're actually not the heroine that would have a dramatic choice no no, instead you fight a final boss to the very end without breaking a sweat, but you die of a measly blue pellet in the stomach shot by a dying old man & you're told "Actually you're not the main character, I am" by some standard NPC looking guy. If you wanna pull a move like that its fine but that was not done properly at ALL in my opinion.CONCLUSION : Honestly I did enjoy the game quite a bit, despite all my criticism I think its still a fairly enjoyable game, it just had very very bad flaws that I believe will have to get worked on for this studio's next game . If there was a thumbs middle I would put it but its not bad enough to be put in thumbs down to me. Good luck to this studio's future.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, and I want to recommend it, but I can't do so fully.  In particular, I can't recommend it without pointing out the big faults the game has.-The game is very short.  It ends with what feels like minimal exploration, and a not-insignificant amount of that time is spent backtracking.-Once you max out your upgrades the challenge disappears.  This was not only easy to do, but happened sooner in the game than it should have.  Because of this, the last two boss battles were trivial exercises with no real urgency to them.-The game ends with an abrupt cliffhanger.  It was like the game was in a desperate hurry to get its ending over with.  The plot may be YA grade, but that doesn't forgive ending with the equivalent of slamming the door in my face.  Besides, I'm not going to pretend I'm too good to enjoy a YA plot.Despite all of that, I really did enjoy this game.  I never felt frustrated or bored by the controls or the boss fights, and there was a good variety in abilities and enemies.  The characters were likable & well-written, especially Renard and Aletheia.  I'm a big sucker for that "seasoned hunter" look they used for Aletheia, and they did a good job of it with her.My recommendation is to wait and see if they ever make a sequel, then wait for both games to go on sale as a bundle.  That's a Hell of a way to recommend a game, but I can't bring myself to recommend it any other way.

_childDocuments_.review: Why make a game in such a crowded genre with absolutely no ideas?  Why do everything so poorly?  Why make it such a short and shallow game?  Why spread the puny amount of upgrades out like this?  Why make it so repetitive and basic?  Why interrupt the player so many times withe most insufferably boring dialogue?  This is one of the worst in a year loaded to the gills with great MVs.  Embarrassing for the devs.  They should be ashamed of this tripe.  Do better.  Do not buy.  Get Biogun, Biomorph, Laika, Ultros, Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown, The Last Faith, Blasphemous 2, Crypt Custodian, etc. instead of this game.  I got it for free and I feel ripped off.  A message to potential MV devs: make sure you have at least one fresh idea.  This genre is so beyond crowded right now.  If your game is this unoriginal, this uninteresting, and this poorly done then you deserve to fail as developers. _childDocuments_.review: The shrinkflation version of Iconoclasts. Same price, half the length, slightly lower quality. Just like everything in the supermarket these days.Do not buy this unless it is on a 50% or greater sale or you're burnt out from depressing soulslike metroidvanias and you've already used iconoclasts previously to cure a previous bout of burnout.Considering how similar this game is to iconoclasts I will focus purely on what differentiates them:- This game's combat is primarily melee based with the occasional gun use, total reversal of combat in iconoclasts.- This game has a lot of typos, iconoclasts has virtually none- This game is buttery smooth, even moreso than Iconoclasts. The smoothness is comparable to Hollow Knight and Rayman Legends. Some of the best C# developers in the gaming business are in the dev team.- The map is well designed, except for the fact that there's some huge rooms and no silloutette of the layout in those huge rooms. This becomes a very big problem in the sea of trash biome and the old quarter biome.- In terms of the plot, the ending for Gestalt is worse than the ending for Iconoclasts and features a terrible and unfitting anticlimax and an unwanted cliffhanger.Everything else is pretty much the same.Despite the overpricing I am going to recommend this because it is infinitely better than 8Doors, which was the previous metroidvania I played.

_childDocuments_.review: A game so in love with it's own story it never wants to shut up about it. Acts, no matter how innocuous is accompanied by a blast of some of the most stilted dialog you've ever read.  Want to talk to a quest giver NPC? Paragraph. You see a thing happen in front of you? Unnecessary explanation, and or quip. The game loves throwing names and terms at you that you have no reason to care about. If you're going to emphasize story to this degree you need an editor to look things over. It's apparent that was not done here.Gameplay is nothing special. Typical slashing metroidvania gameplay with no hook and a odd, sluggish feel. It's as if certain actions are a delay a barely perceptible half step. The wall jump also feels completely divorced from the rest of the games physics, ridiculously fast; and in a genre so well traveled there's little excuse for this mediocrity. Inpsired by "16 and 32bit classics" this might have been, but the creators should have taken a closer look as to why those games worked.

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, does it feel bitter to leave a negative review for this one. I've been eagerly awaiting Gestalt: Steam & Cinder for the past 3 years and despite the fact that some aspects and areas of the game feel unfinished, despite the relatively basic combat and AI, despite some tedious map design, I was ready to give it a positive review overall...until literally the last 30 seconds of the game.Holy hell, I think this may actually be a contender for the worst video game ending I've ever witnessed. There are bland and forgettable endings, there are tragic endings, there are happy endings and then there's...whatever the hell this is. I guess it's the "ugly" part in that infamous "the good, the bad and the ugly" trope. In short,  It sucks out all sense of accomplishment and satisfaction you may have had until that point and simply leaves you baffled. Sorry devs, not even all those Corgis are gonna save you from this debacle of an ending. If your strategy was to hook people into a potential sequel on the off chance that this game performs well-enough financially, then I honestly think you achieved the opposite effect.

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is a game that I've been looking forward to ever since I got my hands on it at a PAX South demo booth, and its full release did not disappoint!+ Smooth Controls+ Beautiful Pixel Art+ Great Music+/- Game Balance (Skews on the Easy side of things)+/- Game Length (8ish Hours)- Story- Bugs The controls in Gestalt are simply delightful. Attacks are crisp, jump height is extremely flexible, and a lot of actions can be animation cancelled into dodges or other actions. I fell in love with this game after playing only the demo of the very first level because it just felt so good to play at its core level. The extra movement options you unlock as the game goes on (double jump, divekick, airdash) is just extra icing on the cake. Combat and movement are the core of any action platformer, and here they feel great! The pixel art is gorgeous. Character designs are unique, enemy designs are clean, and the background art is beautiful. There are lots of amazing backgrounds that (for better or worse) are used simply set dressing. The Scrap Sea region in particular has several backgrounds that I took a lot of time to simply sit back and gawk at.Aletheia's animations are incredible as well! Clearly a ton of work has been put into that, from her standard swordplay to her basic movement to the flaming flourishes on her special attacks. The highpoints of the animation of the game in motion definitely meet up with the high level of detail in the background setpieces. Gestalt's music has a pretty unique feel to it - a Western twang mixed with enough other elements to give it its own identity. I'm not well versed in musical critique enough to speak on it more than that, other than to simply say that I think it's a standout accomplishment in the game worthy of praise. Gestalt intentionally skews itself on the easier side of things. If you're experienced with action platformers or metroidvanias, you'll probably breeze through it. Even if you're not skilled in this type of game, if you do all the bounty boards and sidequests and collect all the accessories, you'll likely breeze through it. The boss design is elegant in my opinion, but not overly complicated. if you're looking for a game that challenges you in difficulty, you'll likely come away disappointed. (Though I would recommend trying out a low level run or speedrun - things get significantly more difficult when you're underlevelled!)The extra abilities you can unlock in Aletheia's ability node tree are a hit or miss. Many of them feel powerful and have their own useful niche, from the divekick-esque Dropkick's aerial mobility to Ground Slams quick aerial damage to Charged Concussive's strong stun capabilities, etc. There are some that feel a little vestigial, however, mostly in that they take too long to set up and are likely to get you interrupted by enemies. Much of the back and forth of Gestalt's combat involves getting quick attacks in and dodging out of the way when your opponent swings at you and then dishing out big amounts of damage when/if you stun them. Attacks like the dodge attacks or higher number of light attack combo strings are difficult to work in against active opponents, and against stunned ones it's generally better to be using heavier hitting attacks. A bit of a shame, since dodge attacks and particularly the final light attack combo are IMO some of the coolest animations in a game that sets a really high bar for that sort of thing. Combat still comes away as being pretty satisfying in my opinion due to the responsiveness at its core, but it is a slight shame these elements don't get to shine as much as they could have. Gestalt isn't a terribly long affair. On my first playthrough, I 100%'d the game after about 8 hours of play. Your mileage may vary, of course, depending on the speed you take the game. Some might find this a little short, though I felt pretty satisfied with that overall. Gestalt is at its core a narratively driven action platformer. With that comes with lots of dialogue. If you're the sort of person who hates reading mutiple lines of unspoken dialogue, you'll probably have a bad time.I enjoyed the majority of Gestalt's story, personally. There isn't as much side detail or random people to talk to that I might have liked for this sort of narrative style, but what is there paints a pretty solid picture of Gestalt's world. While the overall story won't be winning any awards, the characters themselves all have believable personal motivations and interactions.Unfortunately, the story does not have a satisfying conclusion. If you're the sort of person that doesn't like cliffhangers, you'll likely be disappointed by the ending. The game feels like it has more story to tell than what ended up being included in this title, and I can only hope it gets expanded upon in future games. Gestalt launched in a kind of buggy state, with a bevy of minor glitches as well as some major ones. Personally I only ran into minor ones in my launch day playthrough, and I will say that despite some gamebreaking bugs being a thing at launch, the dev team has been very hard at work squashing those bugs post release. As of writing this (7/26/24) there have been six different patches released a little over a week after the game has launched. That's almost a patch every day! Members of the dev team are also very active on the game's Discord server, working directly with people who have ran into major bugs. This is noted as a negative here for posterity, but with how things are being polished up I'd be surprised if any big major or minor bugs make it past the next couple of weeks. Overall while it has its flaws and it might not be for everyone, I greatly enjoyed (and am still enjoying!) my time with Gestalt: Steam and Cinder. Come for the wonderful art and music, stay for the incredibly tight movement and combat controls.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty decent, gorgeously animated metroidvania. It's pretty fun but... it's issue make it a 6-7/10 kinda game. I found the gameplay mostly well put together. _childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free review so don't expect too much detail. TLDR: Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is a solid entry into the Metroidvania genre with a steampunk aesthetic and a bit of Bloodbonre inspiration thrown in. It is definitely worth your time. Visually Gestalt looks gorgeous, excellent pixel art and steampunk aesthetic. Animation is also on point and doesn't stutter or feel jarring when platforming. Music feels good and never out of place, not something to rock out to but it never feels bad and I was never inclined to turn it down.In terms of gameplay Gestalt is quite solid, it follows the Metroidvania template but uses its steampunk aesthetic to great effect to make it feel a bit different. Level design is quite good, I never felt lost and exploration was usually rewarded with some extra items or other rewards.Combat is based around a sword and pistol playstyle with the pistol being used to break the enemies defence while the sword deals the damage, you will need to use both as your sword strikes charge you gun and other special attacks. There are enough upgrades spread throughout the game to provide a good feel of power progression. In terms of difficulty Gestalt is not particularly difficult, I died a few times, but overall I would consider it in the low to medium difficulty range, keeping in mind I have a lot of experience with this type of game. (I will also add that the difficulty took a massive nose dive towards the end of the game, this may have been because I had cleared the entire map and got some pretty overpowered items)I like the story and setting for the most part. The characters and the world blend together seemlessly, There are no jarring moments that take you out of the world, characters are consistent and behave like people who live in the world we are presented with. However......... The ending is weak. There is a sequel bait ending that feels unsatisfying (And I hope the game gets a sequel). The final boss fight was also a bit anticlimactic, possibly due to the previously mentioned overpowered itemOther thoughts and minor issues:- Some people have complained about the length of the game, I don't find this to be an issue, The game took me 11 hours to complete and I was happy with the time I invested into it, longer is not always better if it means dragging out the story. - I don't think the game has much immediate replay value, but given the time it takes to complete I will probably go back and play it once a year.- A side objective has you finding Corgi's across the map. I don't understand the appeal of Corgis, please use Samoyed's for your next game, they are superior to Corgi's in every way.
