_childDocuments_.review: Oh man, this recommendation comes with a lot of good and then one GIANT asterisk at the end*. I wibble wobbled between recommending or not based on that one asterisk, but there is far more good than bad in the game.First lets get the obvious out of the way. This game is absolutely gorgeous. The pixel art, both the static character images and the fluid motion during gameplay are nigh on perfect. 10/10, no notes.As far as mechanics go, this game is primarily a metroid-vania, with some light rpg elements. The character does have a level, stats, and some equipment options, but for the most part as long as you're doing optional content when it pops up, you'll be getting a steady stream of experience and equipment. Far more important is the bones of the combat and platforming, both of which are excellent. It starts out relatively basic, with melee combat swings that charge your gun, and firing the gun does a bunch of damage. But this expands at a fluid pace. The game took me about 8 hours to beat doing almost everything (I appear to have missed a few points in the map with some optional collectibles) and it felt like I was getting a new ability about every 1.5 hours on average. Exploring maps was incredibly rewarding, and pretty much anything hidden is useful. Whether it be a new piece of equipment, an ability point you can spend for stat buffs, or an upgrade to your healing flask (yes this game has a healing flask).The bosses in the game are relatively few in number, but satisfying to learn and defeat. None of the encounters are particularly long (though part of that may have been due to me getting everything I could) but they were satisfying to figure out.Finally, there is the story. This game has a much greater emphasis on story than most other metroid-vania style games I've played. Usually you get some snippets of story at the beginning and at major checkpoints, but not so here. There is a wide cast of npcs, and after hitting new areas you often get a brief cutscene showing what is going on elsewhere in the world. Some people have said there is too much dialog, but in my experience it felt pretty well spaced. The world is also interesting, I actively enjoyed learning more about it and our main character. It builds up in a very real way to the ending*------------------------------------*and HERE is our major asterisk. Because after having an enjoyable 8 hours in the game, I defeated the final boss, eager to see what would happen next.In the span of only a few minutes: your final victory is undercut, a side character takes the spotlight for the final scene, credits roll as you incredulously go "what, THAT'S the end?" and then... a post credits sequence appears clearly baiting a sequel or possibly DLC.This left such a bitter taste in my mouth to the point where I almost couldn't recommend this game. However I gave myself a bit of time to cool down, and ultimately came to the conclusion that a few minutes of an unsatisfying ending does not undo 8 hours of what was, until that point, a delightful experience. So, if you are interested in this game, know that the ending will disappoint and sequel-bait. But otherwise, I can heartily recommend. And, if perhaps in future, a proper conclusion is released, then I can do away with my misgivings. But as it stands now, I've had a lovely 8 hour experience ending with one of the most sour/bitter tastes lingering I've ever known.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I dont normally write reviews, but this one I feel like I have to.  This game is so close to being awesome, but so far away from it at the same timeGraphics are a 9.9, love the fluid animation, the art style, the effort by the design team really shows talent, only really marred by the clunky menu item equipment system.  Nitpicky, yes, but a valid annoyance.Music is another 10 just great memorable sound track, all of is extremely well done and the sound effects all fit right in where they need toThe story is good, keeps me wanting to play, the dialog breaks up the pacing a bit and for some, I could see this being annoying, especially if you dont care for it?  I find it interesting.Gameplay, ok here is where it falls flat.  Big time.  The game is terribly balanced, most enemies are just the simple spam attack type but they just tank your hits, theres no stun mechanic for Alethia's weapons, and I dont count the nonsense "stun break" mechanic as part of this. Combat for most enemies revolves around hitting a couple times and dodge rolling. Making nearly EVERY SINGLE skill a pointless waste of time.  The wind up, and recovery of stronger attacks allows enemies to just hit you mid attack.  I'm not really sure what went through the dev's head for this. They just seem to want you to be punish for trying to do more than the 2 basic attacks.To make matters worse, most enemies have a lot of health so you're doing hit-dodge-hit-dodge alot for each of them.The stun break mechanic doesnt work well with the sword, if it did maybe the light combo attack increase might actually make sense???? It takes a couple of bullets from the gun for it to totally stun an enemy, but... the steel bullets even without the armor piercing ability just 1 shot all enemies, so again I have no idea what they were thinking... why would I use two-three charges of the gun to STUN an enemy and finish it with the sword when I can just 1 shot him with a regular bullet.These problems get worse towards the end of the game where enemies just seem to lack even minor openings making them something you just want to bypass, or shoot from a far or just cheese them through the ground or something.  theres just nothing enjoyable about trying to tangle with them.  Thats really the big problem overall, these things added together which form the core combat cycle of the game just arent enjoyable.   You might think I believe the game to be too hard then.  The fact of the matter is the opposite, especially towards the end of the game when the main character is just a complete brick s**thouse.The hardest boss fight in this game was the first one, after that I was able to basically face, the rest ignoring their patterns (such as they are), if I wanted to.  If you bother to learn their pattern being so simple, mistakes are trivialised due to the aforementioned high hp pool of the main character.I cant recommend the game, but I do still like it.  The story, art and music are great, the gameplay is a 4/10.  Maybe make the sword break the enemies so you can actually use combos and skills?  Maybe stun bullets should should be free?  The big attacks maybe not use the gun charges and cause the enemies to stagger? You should be punished for mistakes, not for simple engaging in combat.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the slow start let you down, Gestalt: Steam & Cinder evolves into an enjoyable Metroidvania with a focus on platforming later on. There's a little bit of challenge in the combat, but overall it's more on the easy side of games. I won't touch the ending, but there is a reasonable challenge in reaching it.Additionally, I don't think the game tells you or I missed it completely, but you can break the red orbs with a charged tesla shot. Enjoy!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A pixel-art metroidvania where you play as a badass redhead pirate/gunslinger who double jumps by shooting her big-ass revolver towards the ground, and goes around rescuing Corgis. There, I sold you on the game.In all seriousness indie metroidvanias are a dime a dozen, and as many as I've played... it's rare that I finish any of them. But I happily played Gestalt to completion and acquired every last achievement. It's perfectly sized, and has surprisingly satisfying combat and slick animations for a first-time developer. That said, the final biome of the game has enemies that all feel obnoxious to deal with, and the ending comes extremely abrupt... to the point I thought I missed something and got the faux ending. But I didn't. The game sadly just kinda ends. I still enjoyed my time playing Gestalt, and genuinely look forward to seeing whatever Metamorphosis Games create next.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Nice short metroidvania thats kinda perfect in its execution. Movement feels smooth and challenges are satisfying although bosses are kinda lackluster (I died 2 times during my whole playthrough, once during an early boss cause I still had to get accostumed to the controls and the other time cause of level hazards that im not gonna spoil). Game is fairly easy but it could be that this is my 6th metroidvania this year so I was familiar with the controls and mechanics after only a while.Exploring is fun especially with double jump and airdash (you get a lot of maps lategame so 100%ing isnt even an issue) and the dialogue between the characters is actually worth reading and sometimes got me to actually real life laugh.Only problem is the game lacks "pathos". If you've played Hollow Knight you know, that feeling that something's epic is about to happen or has happened or is happening right now as you go through the game world; well that feeling is kinda absent here as the story gets told to you almost entirely with text and you kinda know what's happening but don't really "feel" it with gameplay or anything. The fact that the OST is not that great does not help. I'd talk about the ending too but I don't wanna spoil: just know it sucks!Despite the occasional blandness the game is worth playing so give it a shot and buy it if it's on sale.Or don't, I'm not your daddy.or am I?
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it.Beautiful and detailed pixel art. Great music.Every level has it's own theme and it's own puzzles. Exploring is soo much fun.Levels are full of different enemies so never feels like you are fighting the same thing over and over again. Different strategies and attack combos is required to move foward. Only thing that I wanted in the combat was to be able to block or parry enemy attacks. Enemies will hit you no matter what if you in their general attack range. So evade, get back and hit them when they getting ready for their next attack.Equipable items offer some diversity in combat. If you find all corgis game gives you an amazing item which makes you the fastest gunslinger in the game.Every skill point spent is makes you little bit stronger. There is no skill or power trade. Which I like a lot. Makes you feel like a god at the end of the game.Boss fights are fun and they are smiply not hard. Challening in a way that you have to use all of your abilities and skills. Game does not punish you because you made a small mistake or forgot to do something.Story is mostly okay. There is some lore but as a player you only learn when some cut scene plays out. Other than that there is no way of learning about the game world or other characters motivations.There is a bar in the game and you can ask the bartender if he heard some rumors and he gives you nothing. There are some npcs you can talk to but it's just nothing burger. Could have been nice to learn about the world and the characters more. But it is what it is.Really want to see the second game in the series.Seeing the game on the Geekenders Podcast actually gave me the push to play it. And I'm glad it did.Congratualtions to the dev team and Jesse and Dodger.Can't wait for the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Despite only taking me about 9h to complete, I still recommend this game to anyone who loves a steampunk aesthetic, eldritch mystery and/or metroidvanias. It's a quick play with really satisfying moves and animations. The artstyle is gorgeous imo, and I'd say it's totally worth the 20 bucks, just for how fun this game is to play, how manageable it makes completion feel and how great the story is. At first glance, it's a really generic story but each character is really well-written, has interesting lines and clearly has their own personality. Multiple characters have a lot of development throughout the game and there's even some hints towards a sequel, so I'm all for it! Furthermore, the platforming feels very satisfying in this game. It's as fluid as I've seen in metroidvanias, on par with games like Hollow Knight in my opinion. Even though it's only a short ride, it is a very enjoyable one so please give it a shot <3Last but not least: the main collectible in the game is corgis that have ran away from home. You just HAVE to save them all! Your character even gives them all pets when she saves them!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: too much dodges for me :- hits don't knockback light enemies (no combo break, no impact feeling)- there is no guard (they can but not you)Instead you have to dodge (front/back, agressive/normal), again and again.not for me.The story seems nice, even if I don't understand some stuff:- talking with "???" carelessly,- cliche reasons for battle with R,- the nightmare-like robot torso at the forge but "don't care",- the "we know things but we ignore/hide them because... you know, master plan".I will see later with mods probably... in the absence of skill.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt is a game action fans will enjoy. It's not a complex metroidvania but if someone enjoys sidescrollers then this is worth playing, The pixel art is top notch and so is the animation.They are a highlight of the game. The ost is pretty well done as well and is worth mentioning. It really fits with the steam/mechanical theme mixed with western vibe. I personally did not have any issues with controls.If I had to nit pick I'd say the dialog will be long winded for some but you can mash through it. The game is not complicated with its equipment or systems or overly difficult. So I can easily recommend the game. Quality title that is fun to play. There you go.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful looking metroid like game without the gameplay charm to uphold multiple playthroughsIt is on the shorter side and while it does have an interesting premise it does nothing with it. The story is predictable with the story ultimately more interested in long cutscenes and in setting up for a sequel rather than a strong first outing.Difficulty is low and while that wouldn't normally be a strike against a game I do think that it makes the bosses incredibly lackluster with only two or three fights having potential to take players out. Enemies on the overworld have a better chance of killing you than the bosses due to stiff defensive options.Certain attacks are almost completely useless due to how quick enemies behave and how slow player recovery animations are. The basic attack is essentially your best tool in most cases with the gun being the most viable tool.I wanted to like this game but it is ultimately only something nice to look at rather than play.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty neat. it's really really Easy! i was rather busted at the end and defeated the last Three Bosses within seconds each! Forge is the best Area. And Drop kick can let you reach certain areas you're not meant to (even tho i reached most of those shortly after anyway.)So yeah my main con is it's really really Easy! Also the Dialogue was kinda bad. "lots of... dramatic... pauses... during dialogue..." and not to mention an abundance of typos. and one instance of repeating dialogue after the Train Part.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Time to Beat: 6.5 hoursReplay-ability: Not a lot. This is a metroidvania style story game.Achievements: Worth hunting, probably another 4 hours you go for them (guessing as I did not)The Good: This is a solid game with an ok story. The controls are pretty decent and while a lot of people complain about not being able to dodge while slashing and whatnot, I did not find that to be much of a hindrance. There is a cadence of combat you need to get used to where you get used to how long the pauses are between attacks. A number of the boss fights are quite well done and there is a combination of hack and slash as well as jump and dodge. I enjoyed the locales and the ambiance they set while exploring.The Bad: Many of the enemies get into a very typical pattern of "slash slash, dodge, slash slash, dodge" repeat. It can feel repetitive. Harder enemies really just do more damage and have more hit points, there are only a few that stand out (looking at you knife-throwing jerks). That all said, the biggest single thing that irks me and the reason I'm really writing this entire review... There is not much of a payout to the story at all. There's a glimpse of a very cool idea and it promises some crazy cool disastrous stuff but it ends before any of that comes to light.Will I give them more money for a sequel? Yes. Is it a solid game in its own right? Yes. Do I wish it had delivered on the full backstory it teased and not pull what feels kind of like a bait and switch? Also yes. If/When you jump into this game, just don't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I've had Gestalt on my wishlist since it was announced back in...2020, I think?  They kept pushing it back and back, even with tech demos to show.  In 2022, their demo showed the updated flow and combat, and I knew this would be something I'd really enjoy.And that's what it is: an enjoyable action platformer.  The Metroidvania aspect is somewhat basic; you get exactly the abilities you'd expect to get, but aside from Corgis to rescue, you don't have a ton of need to go back and retread things with your new abilities.There's a lot of worldbuilding thrown at you through text, and I found it a very enjoyable story to read based in a dying steampunk world.  If reading a lot dismays you, then be warned on that point, but it's still an enjoyable set of characters and a compelling enough story.Combat's good.  The flow of it is fun enough, you feel you're moving and rolling smoothly.  The bosses, though, can be utterly trivial.  If you do even a few side bounties or quests, you end up with gear and maxed abilities that have you blowing through almost all of the boss encounters.  I took about 8 hours to finish up (minus missing a few collectibles), so it's on the shorter end of things.It sits at 80% positive right now, and I think that's a very good place for it.  It does look like they have plans to continue on with this world and characters, so if there's a sequel in the making, I'd be interested in that as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: There's a lot of action platformers out there and this isn't one that really does anything new or interesting so far. It does feel decent, the story and characters seem to have a lot of effort put in (can't confirm, didn't care enough) but the gameplay itself just doesn't have anything going on to keep me playing. Not bad though
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It started off well, each enemy was a puzzle to solve in how you approach them and can dispatch them quickly without losing health. That felt satisfying. However, starting at the syndicate outskirts, enemies feel too spongy, and using your gun stun doesn't work well against them. The mutant brutes were even worse. Because of this, many combos you unlock aren't useful since enemy attacks don't get interrupted by your attacks. Maybe it gets better once you unlock new abilities and level up, but the syndicate and lab areas in the first few hours did not feel fun, so I stopped playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I've completed the game.This is an old-school style metroidvania, like Castlevania: SOTN on steroids. Rather short, sometimes a little bit annoying (forest, ahem), sometimes rough on the edges.But, nevertheless - it's good. Art is nothing short of AMAZING. The art director & designers are friggin geniuses. Music is good, plot is interesting, overall I'm pretty happy with the game and surely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Was really busy with the game, and literally couldn't stop playing it. Got hooked just that hard.It is true that the game is shorter than expected. It's totally possible to rush through the campaign in under 6-7 hours.There is only one level of difficulty.Please note that the demo is quite different from the release. Former doesn't have some qol like skipping dialogues and is kinda buggy. Latter has a different tree, the possibility of turning off enemies' life bars, and less bugs (I noticed only 1 bug - a couple of triggered switches still showed on the map).- Visuals and sound. Pixel art is gorgeous, music is absolutely in my taste - 9/10- Combat is quite good - 8/10- Plot is fast paced - 7/10- Overall gameplay - 8/10- Entire walkthrough is smooth af and kinda relaxing. I never felt annoyed or frustrated - 9/10- Not a soulslike, still enjoyable - 9/10- Can get all steam achievements in one run - 10/10- Passive tree can be easily refunded - 8/10.- Difficulty. There is no challenge here at all, but it's still fine because of how good the gameplay is. I still have 3 deaths, can't even remember when and where I died. Some regular monsters hit harder than bosses.- Length. It's kinda short, but not that short. I can be really upset about 2-4h games.- Dialogues. There are a lot of them, but I'm fine with this kind of storytelling. I prefer that over some notes across the world.- Zero replayability. Genuinely one and done game.- Too freaking linear. 0 alternative routes. Everything is ability or quest locked.- I have some small nitpicks to a small number of room designs.- Exploration is barely rewarding. A lot of consumables in chests that could be just bought from vendors. A lot of useless gear. A lot of backtracking required to 100% the game (literally have to backtrack 30% of the map after getting all movement upgrades).- Can become stupidly OP with the gun closer to the final boss.- Only 1 somehow good platforming area. This game is clearly not about platforming.- No true ending. 100% completion is not rewarding at all (besides korgis - reward for all is busted), so no real point to bother with it.Despite a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of subjective "don't likes''  this game to people who liked the demo. Ofc if you feel like spending 20$ for 6-8h of the decent gameplay. If not -
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Echoing other reviews, a great little game. I wish combats had a little bit more to them in terms of strategy. Story is enjoyable throughout. Some QOL negatives regarding backtracking but for the limited amount of backtracking, it could be worse. I wish the game was a longer. Look forward to any additional games/content.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's fine.To expand on that, this is a game I liked, but it was one that I really wanted to love leading up to its release. As a big-time JRPG fan, I didn't mind the dialogue, back story, and lore. I thought all that was well done for the most part. The controls are very tight, and the pixel art is beautiful -- some of the best I've seen. Add in some great character portraits (can't take that for granted!) and the steampunk setting, and it hits a lot of spots for me. It is metroidvania-ish. Gated progression, sure, but this isn't Afterimage or, heck, even Super Metroid. There's some exploration, but I'd liken it closer to Zero Mission or perhaps some of the Shantae games than to some of the other giants of the genre. Not a bad thing at all, mind you.The game is short (about 8 hours) which isn't a negative in a vacuum. The aforementioned Super Metroid is about 3-4 hours long and is basically paced perfectly. In a similar vein to Chained Echoes, there was too much lore and not enough game surrounding that lore to make the world feel comfortably whole. The analogy I'd draw is to an overpacked suitcase, where you'd stuff 2 weeks' worth of clothes for a 3 day trip.There's one other thing that I have to talk about that's a colossal negative, and it's that ending. It just stinks. I was around for Mass Effect 3's original ending, before they added the slideshow. That's the tier we're talking about here. Completely killed my desire for a replay.Overall, if you like action/adventure/platform/metroidvania-adjacent style games like Shantae or Mega Man X, then this game is an easy recommendation, terrible ending notwithstanding. If you want something like Ori, Hollow Knight, or Afterimage, then this might not scratch that itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: I didn't regret playing at all, I just wish the story was a little better given how wordy it is.I finished it which meant I enjoyed it but the story was rough around the edges for sure. For the record, I like story-heavy games and this one bombards you with words without a whole lot of worldbuilding outside of dialogue that seems to more expect you to know what's going on rather than showing you. I felt like underneath all the chatter might be something special but then the ending happened. A lot of stuff came out of left field all at once and some of it was all foreshadowed to some extent but it still felt shoehorned in. The explanation for what's going on behind the scenes and potential consequences of the story never happens but is only hinted at. It'd be fine if this was a part one but as something insinuated to be a complete experience, it kind of irked me. Also, the characters are kind of meh, if there is a sequel or DLC, I hope they work on that. My gripes out of the way, I had fun with the gameplay. As some others have said, it is kind of trivial but I found myself able to circumvent that by not wearing certain accessories and deliberately underleveling my ability points. Also, the OST is freaking great.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 so farThe game works perfectly on steam deck and is everything you'd want from a metroidvania retro / steam punk styled game. The game feels fluid in attack modes both via blade and gun. The story line has humour and the art style is just brilliant. I love how fast it feels with the rolls and ducking. It's very responsive. I'm still early into unlocking abilities so will add more to the review soon but so far i don't have any hesitations to recommend the game. No bugs encountered. Can't  to dig a little deeper into the quests. A great example of a metroidvania 2d platformer ! BRAVO
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: 9-12 hours of fantastic metroidvania-style gameplay.Beautiful art, classically influenced controls(the old sotn combo of attacking in the air right before landing to reset your swing is here and very useful), a great soundtrack, and a story that I was invested in right until I beat the final boss.I'm not sure I've ever had such a great game take such a nose dive in such a short timespan, but I'm still giving it a recommendation as to how much fun I had up until then.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It took the first 2 hours to build up enough Steam to really impress me, but now that I'm two hours in and getting some of the gear improvement and skill mechanics unlocked, I'm for sure going to play through the rest of it.I like the old school feel of the boss fights I've done so far, like an old Mega Man boss where once I learn the pattern, it's quite doable, but if you refuse to learn the pattern you'll be in trouble the whole time.Honestly, if you dig the aesthetic, and think the main character looks cool, pick it up, play it for two hours, and you'll be hooked.

_childDocuments_.review: Got nice art , nice controls , nice ost Got nice progression in the movesets and abilities you unlock that keep combat just fresh enough.I actually quite liked the exposition as it does set up for a nice overarching universe/story and justifications for what exactly you are doing this all for. ( although it sometimes could feel quite detatched from the gameplay loop)It was overall a really nice experience. The bosses couldve been a tad harder but ya cant have it allHope they make a sequel

_childDocuments_.review: I quit playing metroidvanias for years, despite Castlevania SOTN and Super Metroid being some of the first, most influential and defining video games I have ever played. I quit for a few reasons, mostly due to the obsession with copying Souls-like mechanics in games that were clearly not as thought out as the iconic games they're ripping from. Gone were the days of thoughtful pixel art, level design that leads to the urge to explore... Everything just started to feel the same, with brutal difficulty, floaty controls and "environmental storytelling" that amounts to some generic grimdark fantasy pages from the worst fanfic you've ever read. And frankly Gestalt feels even worse.This is a game that wears it's inspiration on it's ♥♥♥♥-stained sleeves. It's pretty much everything I DON'T want in a metroidvania. Let's get into that, because it's burning a hole in my brain. 1. The story is abysmal. Generic as can be. A portal opened! Demons came out! A long time ago. But some are still around? Or maybe not, and these enemies are just angry dudes. Some of them are definitely just angry dudes, you can tell because their relentless attacks clearly mean they hate you, for some reason. Now, maybe I'd know a little more about why any of this is happening if it didn't take 35 clicks through the worst dialogue imaginable to learn anything. It's not just the misspellings, of which there are plenty to see even while mashing the continue button... And this happens every few minutes in gameplay, assuming you're progressing at all and not caught in a loop due to...2. The map is ridiculous. I almost wish there wasn't one. At least if there wasn't one, they probably wouldn't have designed this thing so obtusely. The game is pretty much entirely "walk right," till halfway through when you get to nonsensical maze that is the Outskirts, which continues to grow as a theme throughout the game. But honestly, even if it had simple Ender Lillies-esque level design, this would suck. The map is giant boxes with zero context, no landmarks at all to remember anything by. Finding an old location is just miserably jumping around in circles until you see it. It's the worst map I have ever used.This is made worse by the fact that you can buy maps that sort of fill out certain items, like the lanterns to regen your health, the lanterns to regen your bullets, bullets (or "energy" lmao), or lanterns that give you experience. Naturally, these are all the same icon with the only difference being color, a slap in the face for colorblinders like me. Besides this, the icons are just floating in giant squares with zero context explaining how to get to them. Better hope it's a room that isn't too boring to remember if you're going for 100%. But even then, I've run into quite a few levers or EXP lanterns that I already hit long before circling back to check the map icon. Waste of time. Lots of chests full of cheap one time use items that will just make you pissed you spent the time getting to it. Everything significant comes through story based upgrades, besides one thing that practically makes you invincible found from locating all the hidden dogs in each level. Every game needs pet-able dogs I guess.3. Gameplay is alright. Your character is floaty, though not as bad as some of the single-developer metroidvanias that I've forced myself to finish. The controls are... not responsive, and kind of weird in general. Souls style roll on circle, backstep on left trigger? Gun is "hold RT and press another button" which has probably never been used before in history of game design. And changing the controls to something more sensible didn't seem to work at all of course. Enemies are impossible to stun unless you knock down a ridiculous bar, and you pretty much have one single move that can do that. Bosses are lame and basically become a game of "run away and get one or two hits at a time until you have bullets, then spam that, then spam melee" and repeat. Lame loop, most attacks are worthless, enemies are fast and have very little tells without trial and error. It's really just "dodge whatever direction doesn't run you into their attack, melee, dodge again." People thought Shadow of The Erdtree was too hard with too little openings. I disagreed with that, and certainly don't find this game hard in the traditional sense either. But god, is it tedious. This game has nothing for me. The vibe is weird, the characters are lame, the story is generic and nonsensical and WAY too wordy, the gameplay itself is unresponsive and your sword feels like a pool noodle while your gun/heavy attack instant kill everything. I dunno what it's even going for. The art is pretty and detailed (not as inspired as Blasphemous, but still pretty) but honestly... I'm just gonna go back to skipping this entire genre if this is the expectation nowadays.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: About 5 hours in and I haven't been disappointed. Very pretty pixel graphics -- the key to my heart. I've seen some people say that the controls are subpar, which I don't understand? The controls are just fine -- admittedly they did cram a lot of abilities into this redheaded Soldner, but the controls themselves are great, sometimes it's just hard to remember that I have other moves since there's so many. Not necessarily a bad thing, though. Combat is fun and the upgrades make it even more fun, even if it feels somewhat bloated sometimes. Having a lot of fun exploring and collecting stuff. The story and setting are interesting too, can't say I've personally played a game with a primarily steampunk setting. Cool game, really liking it so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR the game is good but it feels it needs a bit more time in the oven.Wait for a sale to buy.The pixel art is top notch and awesome.. Some male character portrait have some weird chins but otherwise it is a 10/10.The upgrade tree is just right. Not to small, not too big and complicated.No enemy contact damage. The combat feels off. I do not like the sword hit sound. It lacks impact & oomph.Enemies have no stagger animation and they attack super fast, BUT you will be staggered every time you get hit.The attack skill after a backdash is just bad. The backdash will evade the initial attack but the enemy will immediately attack again while you make your special attack and will hit you after you hit them.The attack after the dodge/roll is also useless. You have limited dodge ability and need to wait for it to recharge before you can dodge again. You only have one charge for the whole game. Therefore you do not want to use it offensively otherwise you wont have it to avoid enemy attacks. So you'll never use this attack.The light attack chain nodes are (mostly) useless. Since there is no stagger animation, the enemies will not give you enough time to pull off the whole attack chain before they attack you again. You'll get hit and interrupted if you try. The exception to this is some bosses who'll have enough of a window in between specific attacks.The poise meter is useless. Enemies have poise that if you deplete they'll get stunned and take critical damage. the meter regens if you do not hit them fast enough. The blade will never deal enough break damage to stun enemies, even with full upgrade. The only way to stun enemies is to use the gun tesla bullets. it will stun enemies in 2-3 bullets depending on how upgraded you are. Considering the shield enemies that take almost no damage from normal damage, you must break them with the tesla bullets. Invest in more bullets as early as you can. There is too much dialog exposition. It feels tedious at times. Metroidvania like this have always benefited from less talking and more doing. The story is nothing to write home about but it's not why we play these type of games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is very clunky. Every move feels like it has unnecessary end-lag, leaving you stuck for a moment after each attack. There is no way to control the distance of the dodge roll, which in a game with platforms is unfortunate.The first boss has such a basic moveset (only two attacks) that they added balls of electricity rolling endlessly across the floor, to create some kind of challenge. It was a very boring fight, and jumping over balls of electricity every 2 seconds in between attacks wasn't fun, it just felt like artificial difficulty. Between that boss and the enemies before it, I got the sense that the enemy design in this game is uninspired.Overall it would seem that the developers focused on the visuals (which are very nice) and the story but the gameplay was not given nearly as much attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: NOT WORTH YOUR TIMEI loved the idea of a steampunk Metroidvania but this was very poorly executed.The game was to damn easy. The bosses where so easy it felt like I was not even fighting them. Last boss was a joke. No challenge at all whatsoever, just a lot of HP.The accessories where 99% useless or you get them at a point in the game where you already have the best ones.Extra ability points and items you have nothing you can do with. Maybe it is like that, to remove the need to do %100 of the game to get MAX abilities and HP.But they should have at least given some sort of achievement for getting those...The writing was horrible. cool looking characters with no personality or back story at all.Having a way to long dialogue that was dumb and made little sense.A main city that is dead with almost nothing to do in it. And some of what you can do there is meaningless and a waste of time. A bunch of stores that you can't enter or do anything in them. A few NPCs you can talk with, that give you choices like they could have consequences or lead you to a mini quest in the future...but lead you to nothing and give you nothing.Lastly.  This should have just been a longer game with a proper story and a proper amount of gameplay.If they wanted to do a part 2 so much, then they should have first made a proper part 1.

_childDocuments_.review: Profoundly mediocre. After years of delays Gestalt is short, mechanically simple, and clunky to control topped off with a story that is at best akin to a grade schooler excitedly telling you about his D&D campaign. The UI for basic systems like the map or inventory constantly hitch on submenus or confirmation presses, the combat beyond rote with braindead bosses and bullet-sponge enemies, the platforming is clumsy, and the rewards for exploration never worth it.It's fitting that this game is called Gestalt because it's a bunch of parts I've seen executed with more mastery by games with higher quality. It is not the worst indie metroidvania mindlessly parroting Symphony of the Night rather than making design decisions, but that doesn't make it worth your time.

_childDocuments_.review: I prefice my Review with that i actually enjoyed my time with Gestalt: Steam and CinderThe Artwork is gorgeous, the animations are fluid and the world feels really well established. The combat feels adequad for what its trying to accomplish. The Level system has meaningfull progression, but it was outshined by the accesories that you would find throughout this game. This feels way too overtuned and is actually your main way of progression instead of it being the level system.Where the game lost me was the story, which was in my opinion lack luster and rather rushed. It felt like there should have been a least 1/3 more game than there is right now to actually tell a compelling story. The Game over all was also very short with about 6-7Hours to complete it. I havent looked at all secrets and but and didnt backtrack to the earlier areas to find all the dogs but i have most of the best gear availabe.Another big shortcoming is the difficulty of the game. It felt way too easy. Especially the boss fights. I think i only had to repeat one bossfight and firsttried everyone else including the last few. Again it felt like the progression curve is kinda whack in favour of the player. And yes there are people that like being overpowering strong because they explored every nook and cranny (me included) but i also enjoy the occational challenging bossfight to overcome. Recent examples for that for me would be difficulty spikes in the later half of Nine Sols beginning with lady butterfly ( God i loved that fight and its learning curve )All in all i have to, even if it breaks my heart, give this game a negative rating on behalf of its lackluster rushed and somewhat disconnected story, its way too easy bossfights ( especially in the later half ). And its overall short Gametime.I give the game probs for looking as beatiful as it does but that alone is not enough in this Metroidvania Renaissance we are living right now to stand atop the Absolutly great games that came out the last few years and those who are probably to come.Recommendations for other Games if you enjoyed your time with Gestalt:Steam and Cinders would be- Blashphemous and its Sequel ( For equally good pixel art ) (also the Lone Faith but story there is kinda whack)- Nine Sols for a metroidvania with a compelling and well told story ( It is quite hard to learn tho but if combat clicks it feels amazing to play )- Afterimage ( also well told story, also on the easier side imo and its really big like 20+ hours for a first playthrough big )I would recommend Gestalt Steam and Cinder tho when its on a bigger sale than as of time of this writing (17,99€)

_childDocuments_.review: Solid metroidvania style action platformer. currently going through release month bug fix constant patching, but most of the bugs are minor and the dev is active and engaged in making the game work properly.Starts with a decent number of movement and combat abilities unlocked so you don't have that feeling of being super slow at the start like you do in some games in the genre.Edit: 100% completed the game at 11hours playtime, (9.5 in game timer) game isn't too hard and is likely one that most people will play through just once, but is definitely worth wishlisting. price is in a reasonable indie tier in my region and at the launch week discounted price it feels like i got my moneys worth.

_childDocuments_.review: Cool art, super detailed and stylized, cool gameplay, fun mechanics and gimmicks. Difficulty feels just right, there's a lot to collect and explore, the plot's interesting too.The only problem I have with the game right now is that upgrading the light attacks doesn't reward you at all. There's no stun animation on enemies so you can't really combo them, it just adds more animations for you to be hit. The enemies do have a posture gauge but depleting that leaves them fully vulnerable which means you can use better, albeit slower, damaging options when they're in that type of stun.. I dunno. They just don't gel together.The equip menu is also kinda counter-intuitive but it's nothing you can't get used to.I don't know if my opinion will change as I play more of the game but I've made good progress so far. It was enough to want to offset some of the absolutely moronic reviews here.

_childDocuments_.review: An example of indie adventure games becoming more polished but also more calcified in core gameplay mechanics. The presentation and movement feels nice enough, but something's missing here. The bog standard movement upgrades don't help (double jump, air dash, attack that destroys a barrier, it's all here), and the attacks feel too elaborate and slow to risk using on enemies unless you're going to accept tanking a hit or two, and Aletheia isn't fragile in any sense of the word. It also doesn't help that the enemies have no variety in how to approach them. Hit them once or twice and then roll or jump away, the backstep isn't worth the risk. The stun meter for enemies almost never comes into effect save for a few, and for bosses it mostly devolved into me mashing them to work up enough energy to fire off all my rounds to eat away their stagger and save one for when they get stunned so the Abyss attacks really hurt.The map design is also inconvenient for the player since while there is fast travel through conduits, these conduits or often  posted at the end or the middle of areas and none of them take you back to the city itself, an unusual choice. The node system for upgrades wasn't anything special, either, it's not designed in a way to encourage a player to gear strengthening Aletheia to how they play, but just all around improvements with a few things done in the order of your choice. Could have just made these skill boosts happen directly under leveling up or completing a contract.So yeah, sorry, not a fan of this game. I don't think it's great, but I wouldn't call it disappointing, either. Just a game that illustrates the bar for what people can expect from "metroidvanias" on average.

_childDocuments_.review: The animations are super smooth and the pixel art is amazing. The story isn't best selling, but enjoyable for what it is. The game overall is a ton of platforming and metroidvania fun. However the issues are way too egregious for me to recommend it.1) The ending. The ending is awful and lame and very lazy. I also extremely dislike the implications of what it means for either a DLC follow up for the story or a sequel. 2) Not enough bosses. Bosses are extremely far and few between. I wish there were significantly more. I also wish they were harder. All the content is pretty easy after the first stint of the early game. You can scale stats way higher than you should be able to. It's a fun power fantasy but makes the game lose its charm when bosses are so easy to steam roll. 3) There aren't enough 'challenges'. Such as survival rooms and being stuck fighting a ton of enemies in one room for extended periods of time.I love the characters and the world that they made. But the execution was poorly done and not nearly challenging enough for the tools that they give us. I understand it's difficult to balance combat in video games, but at least let us have a hard or equivalent difficulty option. Challenge is what makes these games fun. And this game is lacking that and a good enough story to compensate for the lack of challenge.8/10 idea, 3/10 execution, 9/10 art direction/animations

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt has been an interesting game to follow. I came a bit later to the scene as the game has been in development for many years. The demo got me interested and my expectations were high. Now that the game is complete, I am mostly positive and think the wait has been worth it. But there are some points that disappointed me and one issue stood out more than the rest. The game follows the Metroidvania template pretty closely, there is more focus on the story and the steampunk setting is very intriguing, something we haven’t seen often. The platforming and fights using gun bullets is also a differentiating factor in a good way.Let’s start with the good stuff. The graphics are absolutely gorgeous. There were some scenes where I couldn’t believe what I was seeing in terms of details and effects. The music is phenomenal. It sounds original, so it’s a bit risky but it comes so well together. I love the characters, the world and lore. All of it was very interesting to follow and I wanted more. The progression system is great with a skill tree, lots of items to equip or consumable items to use. The bounty quests and finding dogs are neat ways of making you spend more time exploring on top of the hidden chests. The controls feel great, it makes the platforming incredibly fun and on point. I’m glad the levels are perfectly designed for platforming in an interesting way. And there are always shortcuts to minimise the backtracking once you’ve gotten further. Aletheia has some really cool moves she can use in battles, they look awesome in motion. I actually like the way the map is designed. It’s not very detailed, leaving enough room to figure things out for yourself and you can use markers to highlight areas you can’t get to yet. The achievements are excellent. They’re basically related to completing the story and do, max and find everything. It’s not as bad as it sounds because you get lots of tools to 100% the game.These are the issues frequently mentioned online: story, fights and challenge. With story, many didn’t like how there were too many cutscenes that couldn’t be skipped and the ending being a cliffhanger. It’s true that there are more cutscenes than usually expected for a Metroidvania but it’s not necessarily a bad thing (aside from not being able to skip them). It’s just something different and it’s still not anywhere close to a novel. I was more bothered by how many plot details were dropped at the beginning and the terms/characters/events mentioned throughout the game with no way to look them up. Think of FFXIII but without a bestiary to look up these terms or get more information about certain characters/events. This is a very odd omission for such a lore heavy game with many different characters involved. I’m fine with the ending provided we get a conclusion in some form, a sequel is preferred because it feels like there is too much to put in a DLC and that would be a waste. People complain about the challenge being too easy, I’m fine with that for the most part. We don’t need every game to be challenging all the time. It was nice for a change. The fighting though, this is my biggest issue with the game. It feels off and it’s all because of the way the enemies stagger and how quickly they follow up with their attacks. They don’t stagger unless you use a Tesla bullet (other means are not as affective). It might sound minor but it’s actually a big deal. A lot of moves (especially the dodge attacks costing stamina) become useless for the risk of getting hit. And bullets only have a couple of uses. You start with one and you can upgrade that with four max. The enemies have a stagger meter, you’re often going to need more than one bullet before they are staggered. This is tedious early on, later you have more means of ending fights quickly. It becomes a matter of picking one special move best suitable to finish a normal enemy right away. All of this gives the feeling of the fights not being satisfying. The boss fights look really cool but they also feel off and not as satisfying as they should. The platforming and exploration makes up for the disappointing battle system but I hope it can be improved. It feels like a few minor tweaks can make a huge difference.The game was delayed last minute for further polish. It feels like the game needed even more time in the oven or it needed more testers. But I still enjoyed it a lot and I feel positive with my experience. €20 might not be fully earned with the battle system being the way it is but I’m happy with the €14+ spent. I’m looking forward to what the developer decides next and I’m hopeful we’ll get more Gestalt content in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Underwhelming and feels unfinished.Gestalt has great presentation and the combat is fun if a bit stiff. _childDocuments_.review: It hurts me to review this game negatively as it was in my radar for a while.I wont touch anything relating to the story as i skipped all of it.This game looks really nice and plays well, but my main problems are: Enemies have a little too much HP early on and no downtime whatsoever so i would get stun locked often and die or lose a lot of my HP just trying to make my way through the map, and speaking of maps, some maps are tediously long and made to kill the player, which i understand might be enjoyable to some but it wasn't for me.Short game, took me 8hrs, i hit max level, unlocked all the abilities and passives and i tried to get as much as i could and explore a lot of the (tedious) maps.Overall rating i'd give it a solid: 6 out of 10. Tweaking enemy AI (maybe hp too) for downtime windows could bump this to a 7. I thought about refunding at the 2hr mark, but i decided to stick with it, Dont regret it but also cannot recommend for anyone unless they understand the bad points.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of my most anticipated games this year, and I've been following it since it's first trailer many years ago.On release, it has an identity crisis regarding what it wants to be, how it does it, and it's honestly going to sound odd, but the extra time in the oven was detrimental in the end.Here's a 6 hour game that makes itself 12 by level gating, in a way, having a hub world with 5 entrances that then become one, awful attack mechanics that you can't cancel out of, an outdated late 90's feel of play, and literally a worse map system than Carrion, which didn't have an actual map.Only positive is the art style which is hyper reminiscent of the 16 bit days; really looks gorgeous if that's you're thing (it's something I gravitate towards if done right!)But, it's slow, boring, and with boss fights that approach laughable as you can stand still, it's baffling how this game could go from looking amazing to a complete avoid. As others have said, the story and text is beyond insane, and the game literally has no ending, just abruptly cuts off.Praying there isn't a sequel, but if there is, I'll skip; there are 50 better middle of the road Metroidvanias out there, and EVERY one is better than this.Complete skip!

_childDocuments_.review: I'll keep my review short. I've played this game to 100% completion and feel it is a decent metoidvania (7/10). It is on the smaller side compared to most indie metroidvanias, where it took me 10.5 hrs to complete. The story is well paced and compelling. There were a few character relationships I was confused about, but that did not impact how enjoyable the story was.  I liked the graphics and character designs. Combat has its pros and cons. Pros: Combat style stands out, you are rewarded for using and managing basic/ heavy/ gun attacks, controls feel good. Cons: Dodging (in early game) seems to need adjustments. I occasionally ran into invisible walls while dodging away from an enemy (not through an enemy), causing me to roll in place. That problem disappeared mid through late game though. I felt the game bosses were extremely easy. In some cases, I defeated a boss in under 1 min.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Dev offered to resolve the issue with softlock issues of my save file, so big thumbs up to devs, they actually care and I am looking forward to their future projects.TL;DR- Did I enjoyed the game? Yes.- Is it worth the money? I would say so.- Does it have bugs? Yes. (As of release)- How long does it take to finish it? It's like 12 hours tops if you wanna 100% it.- Is the story good? Meh. Could be worse but it is fairly anticlimactic.- Is the combat good? It's ok, but it gets really easy real fast.- Music? Pretty good after the art probably the best part about the game.Review (possible spoilers but nothing major):Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is not the best game, but it is a good looking stempunkish metroidvania and it will give you enough for one or two days of play if you give it a chance. Bugs like dialogue window showing someone is saying something while it is obviously other person in the dialogue who is saying it are bit too common, There are few missed things in the text that need to be cleared like backslashes at the start of the word or missing word entirely but those are fairly rare. I am fairly sure my game bugged one entire bounty board because I couldn't get any tasks from it which was a bummer. People complained there is too much exposition and text during talking sequences, I would say it's not as bad as those people say but the story is so lukewarm and undercooked it's a valid complain. Speaking of story it strats like a cliche and continues as such and in the end the pay off is "Wait that's it?" which is kinda sad especially when one of the initial story sequences where you unlock powers shows you the past but that is never used again which I feel like is a missed opportunity to flash out past that is only talked about during the game. Characters are also very boring but it partly because there isn't that much interactions with them. That also reminds me that sometimes in this game it feels like something was planned and then scrapped but the scraps stayed like the barman in the pub has an option "have you heard any new rumours?" and he says basically no for the entire game no matter when you come back. Like fill it people with some funny rumour or that he heard that certain redhead solder hijacked a train. Stuff like that to flash out the world a bit.Combat is great if you don't like combat too much or you want easier combat in your game. There are good ideas, gun is fun and sword would be too if the moves you unlock weren't unusable half the time because everything hits fairly fast so you can't really use them without your combo being disrupted midway through by a hit. Game doesn't really explain gun/sword break mechanic too well but you eventually figure it out. That mechanic allows you to stun the enemy which is great for the said sword moves except breaking someone's posture to stun them usually isn't really worth the trouble except for some bossfights. You also get really strong really fast so you can actually facetank stuff as long as you upgrade your flask to have enough healing. If you wanna no hit bosses I gotta say the "stamina" that allows you to roll/dash sometimes feel clunky but it might be just me. Bosses pretty cookie cutter bosses for a metroidvania so don't expect anything great.Accessories could be more interesting in my opinion they were fairly bland except for a couple of them. Something with dash bar regen or more items with powerful effects and a downside would probably make it more interesting.Now for what I think is generally good about this game is art and a music. Music ranging from pretty solid ambience for the zone to really good bops. Art overall was my favorite part of the game but that's very subjective to everyone. Overall I enjoyed the game, it is pretty good value for 9-12 hours of gameplay (I haven't finished everything but I would say I have maybe like hour or two to go at best) if you don't expect something of a Hollow Knight quality this is a solid metroidvania. I wish the studio the best and I am curious about other games they might make in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the player character: she is a beautiful-looking, strong willed, badass woman. I really like her design with that beautiful red long hair, and her steampunk clothes. This shows us that female characters do not need to be sexualized to attract male players: she is attractive just the way she has been designed, and I'm sure female players will like this character as well.Unfortunately, the gameplay is not so good: I like games that have both slash and shoot mechanics, such as the Mega Man Zero / ZX series, however this game seems to be more balanced towards shooting, and having very limited ammo and the need to constantly slash your enemies in order to reload just to shoot again is no good, specially at the beginning, when fighting enemies that need to be "broken" with Tesla shots and then slashed to death. This is not the kind of gaming mechanic that I like. Slashing is also not good: most enemies require a ton of light slashes in order to be taken down, unless you break their guard first using Tesla bullets, plus you get knocked back every time the enemy hits you, almost always breaking your combos. Heavy melee attacks, on the other hand are very powerful and can quickly take your enemies down, but they also consume (your very limited supply of) energy, just like shooting., so actually they don't help too much. In general, the gameplay makes this poor lady to feel powerless, specially when compared to the gameplay in the Mega Man series mentioned avobe, despite these games being much more difficult than this one.So here is what I propose to you devs: please make a full rework of the game: make it longer, have a good and balanced gameplay (just try playing one of the Mega Man Zero / ZX series games to see what I mean, or even have a look to the indie game 30XX which is inspired by those games and have a very simillar gameplay), and avobe al else, .Considering how the game currently is, I have no choice but to write a negative review. I hope you guys make something about it so I can change my mind.

_childDocuments_.review: The Graphics: Good and detailed.  There isn't much that's really novel, but the sprite animation is serviceable, and quite good on the main character, who also has a very solid visual design.The Plot: Utterly insipid.  100% unoriginal ideas, only the barest justification of the steampunk theme, and gets painfully, obviously rushed in the second half of the game.The Gameplay: Controls are generally crisp and responsive, but a little hinky with the gun aiming.The character development tree was interesting; you can branch out in a few directions as usual, but you get a new starting point for every major upgrade, and the sub-upgrades to that are usually locked behind a junction that needs you to meet it from both the main start and the start point for the upgrade.  (There are also more than enough upgrade points to get all the upgrades regardless)The Difficulty: Could very much use a hard mode.  I'm not a roguelike tryhard, but I rarely found myself dying at all, and with minimal thought put into my build was able to face-tank and heal past the end-game challenges.  The platforming was all right in the endgame, when you needed to use your mobility tools, but it also relied very heavily on either knowing what was coming or having amazing reflexes. It's definitely accessible if you're new to the genre, but with the puddle-shallow plot that evaporates entirely by the ending, it made finishing the game a chore.The Collectables: Your Hollow Knight caterpillar-alogue are corgis.  They are cute.  There's no explanation as to how they got there or how they're going to get back, but given how reliably the NPCs teleport to where the plot wants them, I can't care that much.Total Grade: C-.  This game desperately needed a significant rewrite of the existing plot to improve the characters and not try to lore-dump on us in the rushed ending; so many lines of dialogue are just hollow nonsense that can and should be skipped over.  Once we get relationships better established in the early game, and we actually get a middle- and late-game, this would be a recommend.  Until that, there are many better roguelikes out there.

The electricity sound hurts my ears at the volume where the rest of the game feels nice, but I have to lower it not to feel like I'm going to go deaf.Also, for some reason the current main objective stays in the upper right corner? _childDocuments_.review: I recently had the pleasure of diving into Gestalt: Steam & Cinder, and I must say, it exceeded all my expectations! This game is a perfect blend of engaging storytelling, stunning visuals, and intuitive gameplay mechanics.From the moment I stepped into the beautifully crafted steampunk world, I was captivated by its rich, immersive environment. The attention to detail in the art and design is nothing short of spectacular. Each location feels unique and alive, filled with intricate machinery, atmospheric lighting, and a sense of history that draws you in.The storyline is another standout feature. It’s a well-crafted narrative that keeps you hooked from beginning to end. The characters are deeply developed, each with their own backstories and motivations that add layers of depth to the game. The dialogue is sharp, witty, and often thought-provoking, making every interaction meaningful.Gameplay-wise, Gestalt: Steam & Cinder shines with its smooth and responsive combat system. The controls are easy to pick up but offer enough complexity to keep you engaged. The variety of enemies and the strategic approach required to defeat them ensure that combat never feels repetitive. Plus, the game’s progression system allows for plenty of customization and growth, making it satisfying to see your character evolve.The soundtrack deserves special mention. It perfectly complements the game's atmosphere, with a mix of haunting melodies and epic orchestral pieces that elevate the overall experience.In conclusion, Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is a must-play for fans of the steampunk genre and anyone looking for a well-rounded, deeply engaging game. It’s clear that a lot of love and effort went into crafting this masterpiece, and it absolutely pays off. Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder offers a very nice overall gameplay experience. It comes with a fair balance of jumping puzzles, exploration in metroidvania style, a story to follow and some interesting characters to meet. The difficulty is reasonable and challenging enough to provide some fun. The soundtrack is a really pleasant surprise and contributes greatly to a dark steampunk ambiente.It's solid work but nothing is perfect:While the story keeps a player cuddled into the craddle of immersion, the ending scene is most certainly subject disappoint some players for a good reason. The main character "Alethea" and the story is interesting enough to ignite the wish to see and experience more with her. It feels like the prologue to a bigger story. A nice story to look forward to. I'd watch the TV series too, if the story or settings of Gestalt: Steam & Cinder were available.The controls are relatively smooth but a bit restrictive in some situations, Castlevania style spiced up with a bit of Metroid. The skill point system is okay. There are some unusual decisions but adjusting to that isn't a big deal. A negative point is the usefulness of quite some skills and abilities. They don't really shine because players might find themself resorting to dodging, shooting and basic attacks, most of the time. It's a missed chance to support various styles to play and that decreases replay value.Players can expect a fair diversity of content and scenes. It has good chance to meet the taste of teenagers and mature audience alike. Those 8 hours of a first casual playthrough were very enjoyable overall. Unfortunately, the game struggles some with localization issues. The german translation has some errors and problems, at least. Some languages need more space than others and that wasn't really considered. Some entries in lists and menus lose their alignment to that and that doesn't look so pretty anymore.Although there are some obvious flaws, this game can challenge highly praised past titles of the metroidvania genre. No, it doesn't beat the top 5 of most players. But I'm convinced that it can make it to the top 20 or top 10 of some people. Certainly a game to recomment for fans and friends of the steampunk and metroidvania genres.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that makes me really wish Steam had a "meh" option. There are a lot of things I do and don't like about it.Pros:+ Combat is pretty fun+ Love the pixel art style+ Music is great, it feels epic and really sells you on the idea that the entire world is at stake.Cons:- Story presentation is a bit aggressive for my tastes. Gameplay is interrupted for pages upon pages of dialogue every 5 minutes.- You start to become OP towards the end and all bosses begin to feel a bit too trivial.- Map is hard to read, and it makes exploration tedious -- rooms are spread out too far apart so you can't see enough at a glance, important landmarks are not included (you do get manual map markers, but that's not good enough), and different regions are not labeled, only color-coded (good luck remembering which color corresponds to each area)- Ending is awful. Nothing gets resolved. Calling it a cliffhanger would be an understatement; it literally feels like they ran out of time to do an ending cutscene. I got Halo 2 flashbacks. Yes, really.- I really wish they'd taken the time to record more pain grunts because your character makes the same "UGH!" sound every single time she takes damage, and it gets old really fast.Ultimately, I recommend buying this game on sale, as long as you prepare yourself for a very unsatisfying conclusion. This is one of those cases where the journey is more important than the destination.

_childDocuments_.review: Is Gestalt: Steam and Cinder worth the asking price of 20$? The answer to that is yes.   Gestalt: steam and cinder has beautiful visuals bringing a vibrant steam punk world to life. With music that fits the scenery and moods perfectly I often found myself enjoying the music as it complimented the visuals. Controls respond well and smoothly any deaths were from me screwing up and not having to fight against lag or missed inputs. The game has a fun leveling system that allows you to tailor your combat to the way you like it, and even a combo system. Side quests have meaningful rewards and do not over stay their welcome as I found myself completing them as I did the main quest. Maps are well designed if a not as expansive as other games of similar design. Finally surprisingly there is a crafting system, totally optional but taking the time to do exploring often yielded rewards for the crafting that made the effort worth it.   My two biggest gripes are that, while there is a combo system. Most combat comes down to hit 2 maybe three times then dodge roll. You can use the combo system but often it leads to unnecessary damage being taken. Second there is a lot of story. Quite often I would be getting into the grove of the game and then boom 5 minute cut scene. Not enough to kill enjoyment but enough to notice that compared to your average metroidvanyia it’s a lot of heavy dialogue and story.   Over all for 20$ this game is worth the play through and I would highly recommend for any one to give it a weekend to try. Hitting all the high points you want out of a metroidvanyia, Gestalt: Steam and Cinder provides a fun experience, with an enjoyable setting, and a well done leveling system. Plus there is a side mission to rescue corgis and who doesn’t love a good doggo rescue.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a solid 6 out of 10. It isn't bad, but does nothing particularly well. There is no challenge to be found.  I died once that wasn't on purpose for the sake of spawning at a savepoint and not having to backtrack.  Bosses are a joke.   Story is typical Metroidvania fare.  Doesn't really impact the game play much.  The biggest fail in this game imo is that as a Metroidvania, you're meant to back track as you gain power ups to get to previously inaccessible areas, however, a lot of the fighting and exploring is just not fun and left me with little desire to go back and explore.  Couple this with the fact that there is very little if anything to find when exploring save for the annoying lost Corgis and Infused Amarita which are not very exciting.  You dont find any power ups through exploration and they are very limited in the game as a hole.  Not a terrible game but entirely forgettable.  Only can recommend this if it's on sale for $10 or less.

_childDocuments_.review: Decent steampunk Metroidvania. It doesn't do anything particularly novel, but it gets all the basics right. Both the pixel art and the music are of good quality. 100% completing the game took me a bit over 17 hours, which felt like the right length for this game.Platforming difficulty was fine: there are some challenges that took a fair number of tries, but there are enough checkpoints and you don't lose a lot of life if you jump into spikes or fall out of bounds, so it's not very punishing.Enemy variety is good, with new enemies in every zone that have enough differences between them. The combat was difficult enough to keep me alert without becoming frustrating. By the end of the game though, it trended towards becoming too easy; I think the game was balanced for players who don't hunt for every pickup, while I didn't move on to the next area until I had combed out the previous one. I hit max level and full upgrades halfway the last area.The bosses felt like damage sponges until I learned to alternate light and heavy attacks, it was fine after that. It can feel like you're not making a lot of progress on the health (red) bar, but once you get the stun (green) bar down, you get the opportunity to deal a ton of damage.There are various additional attacks you can unlock in the skill tree, but I prioritized stat boosts instead and relied on mastering a smaller set of moves instead of learning a large amount of moves. I used the sword almost exclusively, only switching to the gun to solve puzzles.The story is told in short cut scenes, sometimes showing events that are happening elsewhere. It didn't grip me from the start, but as the events progressed and involved the main character more, it pulled me in. Regarding the ending, I hope this is a setup for a sequel, otherwise I'd be a bit disappointed in how open-ended it was.Despite recommending a controller, the game plays fine with keyboard as long as your keyboard registers more than 2 simultaneous key presses, as most gaming and mechanical keyboards do (N-key rollover, with N>2).
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

I hope the sequel resolves the story cleanly.

_childDocuments_.review: I was following the progress of this one for quite a while and was really looking forward to it. The early game is really fun - skill tree! melee charges ranged attacks! enemies are tough and need you to figure out their attack patterns to beat them before you die! - but by the time I got to midgame I was able to facetank basically everything and nothing was a challenge anymore. You also can't really use most of the combat skills you unlock due to not being able to hitstun anything, so the vast majority of skills you get are unusable.Platforming was fun at first each time I unlocked a new power, but the skill tree spoils everything you'll get before you get it so that was unsatisfying. There are also a bunch of unintuitive and/or obnoxious platforming sections that require precision and "hidden" uses of some of the skills.There's a lot of polish in some areas and a lack of it in others, such as a storefront with a shopkeeper inside that you can never interact with. I basically 100%'d it save for finding one last room in the map which I spent an hour on, and gave up on in the end due to the frustrating tedium.Finally, the story. Good lord, the story. I was invested at first and have great memory with names and places, and I applaud the writers for not pulling us out of the immersion by explaining everything to the PC that already knows what everything is. However, the plot beats themselves were...wretched. The overarching story was interesting but the characters were bland as hell, and the ending is one of the worst I've ever seen in media.Definitely give this one a pass.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, quite pleased with the game. Music was great, gameplay was solid, world was big enough to make exploration interesting without being obnoxious to traverse, biomes were unique with interesting challenges, platforming was hard without being impossible, combat was suitably challenging without being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Dark Souls, progression felt mostly smooth (the last 1/4 went fast, feels like the story might've gotten a bit truncated but it wasn't terrible)If I were forced to complain about something, I was a bit unhappy that both heavy attacks and ranged attacks share ammo. It limits combat options, especially considering how many different types of heavy attack. I was also frustrated that they decided, only for the last biome, to have instadeath spikes. In every other part of the game, environmental hazards resulted in knockback. Spikes do damage and reset you back to the last platform you were on. All that said, these are minor frustrations and not intrusive enough to break my opinion of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best new Metroidvanias I've played... and I've played a lot of new crappy ones.  This feels well thought out and cared for.  From the way she moves up and down a ladder, to the animations when she falls longer than normal and holds her hat, the movement set in pixel art is well done.  There's enough difficulty to not be boring and also a variety of options of moves while in combat.  Thanks for this!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10, incredible game.The pixel art was on-point, the gameplay was fluid, and I was really engaged by the story, which kind of left me... I won't say disappointed, but rather shaken, by how the final minutes of it concluded, ESPECIALLY with that double cliffhanger.Music was on-point throughout, although I will say the standout was the Fornax theme. Definitely gonna pick up the soundtrack at some point.Also, corgis. The fact Irkalla has a gang of corgis is amazing, and I would 100% play (and pay for) a corgi-based spinoff.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I give this a positive review. It got charm, great music and a structure to build upon.But the story could be built better. The combat can be tedious as you can almost never chain your attacks together. You cannot get enemies into a "stun phase" Without the gun. Bosses was decently easy, even if messed up a lot, I did not have to do much to finally manage them. The lack of an parry is also bit odd. It also builds up for a sequel. But considering some characters in the story (the bad guys), im not so sure I want to see them again. They felt pretty lackluster and presented as some kind of mastermind geniuses, yet all they did was...well nothing. The plot was forced forward by characters being idiotic.
