_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: this is a decent game that might be worth picking up at a discount. But for the fans of the genre, I'd really recommend against it.On the surface, it's a beautiful game with an engaging story and lots going for it. But after just a couple of hours of play, the shortcomings became clear to me and I played hoping it'd keep at least its current pace. I ended up reaching a disappointing non-conclusion, while running on fumes and determination to finish it just for the sake of finishing. Thankfully, the music never disappointed.In a few words, this game tries a lot of things at once and shines at none. And in case of the ending, deliberately so.The huge elephant in the room is the almost non-existent difficulty. There is no setting for it, and the only one you get ends up being  easy. Yes, bold italic underlined kind of extremely easy. There is a couple of spots where a noticeable number of enemies in a single room makes combat challenging but even so - the player character has tons of HP and accessible healing. The game forgives an unforgivable amount of errors. The levelling system (which I will further critique below) only exacerbates this problem. One would have to deliberately avoid using accessories, power-ups and abilities to force a challenge. It is not difficult to complete the game without dying once, and it'd require skill far lower than that of your average sweaty speed-runner. AS for platforming or exploration, ,making your way to valuable items rarely presents some platforming challenge either. in fact, the most challenging  (to me) dive kick trick gets you a basic consumable instead of a cool accessory upgrade. Ugh...The combat appears competent on the surface. The basic enemies have relatively unique timing and patterns. In fact, most of the challenge in the game does come from regular enemies early on. The bosses, however,  are complete pushovers. Negligible damage, cute but low threatening moves. Because of this and the indecent amount of durability that player character has, I haven't died to a single boss fight. Probably, neither will you.Combat systems are many yet underwhelming. Grounded combat is okay-ish at best. Aerial combat is shallow and boring. The aerial dash attack upgrade?  Riiiight, it does no damage and is only designed to avoid colliding with enemies or destructible projectiles. No shooting in the air. Air-to-air attacks are few and weak, they push your enemies away and deal little damage. You often end up jumping over and over to chase down and grind down an admittedly non-threatening flying enemy. Why? Good question, you probably should stick to the ground. That's where most of the fun is anyway.Special combat mechanics are break (stun gauge) and critical hits. The break encourages you to use your pistol once in a while, but this also eats into you being able to use power moves with your sword. But not to worry, they're kinda boring and some are even made obsolete by an energy-independent sword whirlwind that you get to unlock early. The combo length upgrade is also redundant as most enemies's patterns do not allow you to finish your combo before forcing you to dodge (there is no interrupt, stagger when hitting them). The critical hits do not have a dopamine-inducing sound or visual effect so you don't even notice them that often. The outcome  is not that impactful either. Yet there are 2 whole stats dedicated to them - crit damage and crit chance. There is a selection of accessories that up these and you do have to make minor choices but it never feels like you can go for a dedicated build where you could play a finesse-fuelled glass cannon. Or a gunslinger. Yeah, there is an end-game item that generates pistol energy passively, but good luck making that into an proper ranged "build". And now we segue into...The abilities map has some potential, but it ends up being just another way to sell underwhelming boring skills of which most are inconsequential (e.g. above mentioned combo length and most power skills) or boring that just make you more durable or let you hit harder. Having most of the map locked behind story-progressing main skills also detracts from actual choices the player could be making.The item acquisition tries a bit better..Here you do have to choose what crafted top-tier accessories you want to spend your rare alloys on. But even these choices are limited, because by the time the main ingredients become available as you probably have all the alloy you need if you weren't too lazy exploring.As I've said before, the game's mechanics seem to go for quantity instead of quality. There are interesting ideas yet they step on each others toes and the execution is underdeveloped and stubby. I'd rather the devs focused on fewer systems and honed them into deeper engaging ones. Instead, we have a jack of all trades that is master of none.The world is interesting, and the intro story does pretty well to engage the player. The characters have enough of a variety and would probably come to life well with some voice acting. None overstay their welcome on the screen. The dialogues are written well, except for two flaws.The first and the minor one is the explanation of the gameplay mechanics. It is subtle enough when explaining how healing works. But can be jarring or awkward  when things like AP or story-progressing abilities (like air dash) are introduced. The game still shows you a tutorial slide afterwards, why'd you hurt the immersion by an in-game character telling you about AP that he inferred from a one-of-a-kind trinket he's never seen before?The major one is the tons of exposition. It is often a necessary evil, I realise this. But there are constant cut-aways to show dialogues that the player character is not a part of. There is a cut-scene that is either flashback or glimpse into the future very early in the game. How about showing more of these instead of dragged out exposition dumps in dialogues. Thankfully, whomever wrote these dialogues did a decent jump with what they were given.The plot is engaging and had me invested, despite some triteness here and there. The finale though. Oh boy... Without spoilers, this game uses one of the worst plot-point crutches in gaming. The ending undercuts a ton of momentum that it was building for the entirety of the game. And for what...  Shame on you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm very conflicted on this game. Visually it's gorgeous. I'm a sucker for pixel art and this game is definitely art, visually at least.So why negative? TLDR: Like others have said the story is pretty uninteresting and the game as a whole is just too easy. I 100% it in a little under 11 hours which is crazy fast for a metroidvania.Long version. The story is...definitely one of the stories of all time. I can't say it's good or bad, it's just there. The things happening and what the characters are saying is interesting in context of the world but...I don't know, I can't explain it, there's just no pull, no feeling of investment or immersion. You know how when you're hanging out with friends and one of them starts telling a story which you don't care at all about but you reply with "oh cool" every now and then? That's how this game's story feels. From the start I didn't care about anything or anyone, and by the end I still didn't care about anything or anyone, in fact I hated a lot of the characters.Gameplay-wise it's alright I guess? That is when you even get the chance to play. It becomes very apparent very quickly that the design focus was definitely the story. You explore 1 to 2 areas and BAM cutscene. Seriously there are more cutscenes in this "game" than actual game. I'd go so far as to say they should've tagged it with "visual novel" it's that many cutscenes. And they talk. They talk. So. Much. I found myself thinking "christ please shut up and let me play the game" way too often. You ever played/seen/heard of Vampyr? Cool looking but 90% of the game is talking and it's never good or interesting. Gestalt gets very close to that. Whenever you actually do get to play the game it's okay. The combat is above decent, mostly carried by the lovely pixel animations. There's a skill tree system to unlock new abilities and attacks but I never found a use for the fancier combat moves mostly because they just aren't worth it. Your regular attack is fast and strong enough. And worse, some of the unlockable moves lock you in a, sometimes lengthy, animation which leaves you open to get hit whereas the regular attack is super fast in comparison and can be dodged out of at any moment. Every time I was on the brink of enjoying the combat and exploration I got hit with another cutscene which just kills the pacing and I think that's part of why the story is disliked and seemingly uninteresting. Because you're stopping me in my tracks WAY too often to shove the story in my face. Not to mention a lot of the cutscenes are the "MEANWHILE AT THE BAD GUY PLACE" type. This may be subjective, may be just me, but that type of storytelling, the "showing you the bad bads being bad" is absurdly stupid. Why show me this? The character I'm playing as isn't present, isn't eavesdropping on this, isn't using a magical mcguffin to see a vision of this, I shouldn't be seeing this. It's such a lazy way of padding story. Speaking of our main character, she is of course the super-special-magic-awesome chosen one and she has a special magical necklace which gives her super awesome power of the best and she's got long blood red hair and she's super cool and awesome and everybody knows her and most people admire her and she solves everyone's problems and her potential is infinite and her power is all of it, this is my OC please don't steal.If you want to simulate playing this game put on Super Mario Bros, the original, go through it without warping so all 8 worlds with all 3 stages per world, but after every stage stop playing and put on some random really stupid podcast like an Alpha male one, watch that for 20 minutes and then continue playing. I want to like this game, I want these devs to keep making games, but please please look through all the reviews/comments/criticism and learn from it. You want to tell a story, that's fine, go for it, but not like this.

_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Such a well constructed world with a very intriguing story. The game itself is fairly challenging early on but does eventually turn into a power fantasy, which fits the lore quite strongly. Several bits of the game's choices seem odd however with skill points being able to over cap, same with the upgrade materials for the flask system.One of my minor complaints about the game would focus specifically on the fast travel system. There's a segment of the game that restricts you away from fast travel and leaves you stuck in a specific area. It's not the biggest problem but it sort of sucks if there was something you wanted and lacked a mat or such but get enough just as you enter this area. I absolutely adored the characters in this game and loved the world building the game goes into. Admittedly wish there was more than a fast forward option for things for repeat playthroughs or revisiting. Easily recommend this to any Metroidvania fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much an 8/10 game. It's technically a metroidvania, but it feels quite linear, which is totally fine by me but might be worth knowing before buying.Art is gorgeous, music is quite nice and gameplay is serviceable. The combat feels kinda wonky, you permanently have to expose yourself to attacks since many enemies attack faster than you can dodge. Either that, or you just sneak in 1 attack every so often to conserve health, which is boring, but have to to early game as you can't heal much. Speaking of dodging, the dodge ability should be a significantly shorter dash and, either on a lower cooldown or add block +/- stamina mechanics. Final 2-3 bosses need some significant rebalance as I felt insanely overpowered (I virtually tanked everything and didn't need to heal at all, save 1 or 2 times at the final boss). One IMMENSE plus is the fact that you are able to get your hands on maps (in-game) that reveal all collectibles, which is amazing. It makes no sense to me why other games still rely on either you faceplanting on every wall (gotta love them invisible walls) or resort to internet guides. Just show me (eventually) a rough location of the damned chest and I'll find it.The setting and the story are quite amazing though. I would have *loved* some lore entries on characters, enemies, places and past events. I was hooked pretty much all the way and was able to 100% the game without guides or any struggle.PS: Make sure to pet all the Corgis, it's so worth it!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A decent metroidvania game with great art, fantastic music and good story, dog petting.However where it falls short is the part that a lot of people would be excited about - the combat.It starts lacking, the abilities you get come quite late in the game - for example: you only get the air dash 75% into the game. And you need to do a lot of backtracking to get the loot that you can only get with your new mobility, which may be offputting considering how enthralling the story can be.The skill tree is also relatively lack luster. You need to work for those skill points, and once you get through the filler +5 hp nodes, the big skill nodes end up being disappointed. An extension to your light combo does not do anything if you can never do a full combo on a basic enemy to begin with because you need to dodge to hit him which resets the combo.The gun having a charge is fine as the charges are gained by attacking, but tying the same resource to heavy attacks makes the only actually interesting abilities in the game hardly used.The game has so much potential in combat - long light combos and specials, animation canceling, 2 separate dodges with 2 separate attacks tied to it, 2 different gun attacks, multiple different heavy attacks, a dive kick. And yet you hardly use half of that arsenal simply because of how fights and enemies are designed.Overall, I think this game would've benefited a lot from a demo and some more time in the oven to polish the combat. Otherwise, getting it on sale is a pretty good deal if you just want a casual metroidvania with a good story.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a fun Metroidvania title, leaning much more in the action platformer inspiration. Combat is really fun, however, no blocking so you will have to use your roll i-frames and your jump to avoid incoming damage. You are given limited (but easily replenishing) ranged weapon ammo, which helps to balance out combat for enemies that are near impossible to deal with up close and personal.The game has an interesting story injection, where each area you progress through will play out a parallel story. It's quite a lot of text, so on my second play through, I'm extremely happy that there's the ability to hold a button to fast forward through all of the text and story stuff.Standard Metroidvania progression aspects... limited mobility and combat, but with an RPG unlocking system to open up the combat you want to focus on. It's pretty rudimentary, which is better than overcomplicated in a game like this. The movement mechanics are the key to progressing through the game as you unlock abilities like a double jump (more specifically, the ability to shoot your gun below you to gain height).Overall, this is a fun game, albeit a pretty standard Metroidvania. It doesn't really do anything too niche, but what it brings to the table, it does well. If you are a fan of action platformers or Metroidvania titles, this should be a title in your library and definitely worth a play. I travel alot, so this game is a perfect title for my Steam Deck/Legion Go... Not too graphically demanding and works when in a mobile console setup.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A relatively short and sweet metroidvania that ends at the right point to not overstay its welcome.Backtracking is limited, mainly for upgrades and collectibles. Platforming is fairly good, but the default controller map sets two consumable buttons: RB and LS press, the latter stupidly easy to trigger during fights or platforming sequences (which can result in death or losing valuable healing charges).
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a good game so far, but unless I am missing something, it's sometimes very frustrating due to rolling and backstep are not the same button with a direction, plus you can only roll once before waiting to get stamina back for ~1+ seconds while some enemies attack faster than the recharge, and we don't have block, so it feels we almost have to get hitFortunately, enemies damage is quite low so it's acceptable
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Doesn't reinvent the wheel, but then it doesn't have to. An extremely solid metroidvania, engaging if predictable story, great art and music, and a mission to find corgis that have turned up in some truly ridiculous places. What more do you want? Some developers try to insert a gimmicky new mechanic in to add something "fresh" to the formula and then the rest suffers trying to cater to the new. This game knows what it wants to do and does it well. Looking forward to what the team comes up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic visuals, music, combat and the platforming feels good too.Story was interesting, even if the ending was a bit disappointing left off with some unfinished questions.Game is also not too long, which personally I like. It took me about 12 hours to 100% it.It's not very difficult, so id difficulty is something you like keep this in mind.If you're looking for a shorter solid metroidvainia this is a good choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: For a Metroidvania its maybe a bit railroaded but i had quite a bit of fun with it. It has a lot of textboxes for the story and that can get a bit annoying at times but nothing too bad. The art is very nice. Many different biomes and the pixelanimation of some characters is excellent. The controls are smooth and responsive. The only "bad" point the game has in my oppinion is that it is very easy. Meaning the bosses were very cool but you can kill them in under one minute no problem so you barely see their entire moveset. Never the less it was a fun and short experience.So if you want a quick but fun game i would recommend this game. 20€ is a fair price in my oppionion.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: i loved it.  great metroidvania. loved the gameplay, art, music, story, story-telling, characters, corgis.  hardly any bugs.  the only downside is there is a progression loss bug that seems to only happen (to me anyways) when i use steams cloudsave function to play on multiple devices.  Its almost as if there was a problem reconciling the different saves between the device and the cloud.  If i stayed on one device and never played on others it seemed to work.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt is a -good- game with some caveats.A great art style and execution is what got my attention for this game.Gameplay and combat are a little too simple for my tastes but, serviceable.I did feel like the game was a hair too short, I was expecting another area and a half to flesh out and explore.Ending up 100% the game in under 10 hours and feel like it was juuuust short of being a full recommendation.Like finishing your plate of food but wanting just another bite of two to feel satisfied.Steam and Cinder is 7.5/10 game that feel like its only four-fifths of a game.I would recommend getting this at 20% off or more.A better game I feel than "9 Years of Shadow" (see my review on that), but as many other reviews say, it's just missing something that //really// makes it stand out.--------------------Gameplay: As a MetroidVania game it is very streamlined/simple. There's not much exploring to be done, and you can get every done in a single run so long as you go through every room/door in an area.Combat is fairly un-engaging because most of the enemies only have 1 attack and one you see them, you know what they'll do; always.Platforming is done well, the ledge grab I was hoping would be used for more secrets, but that's more of a level design issue than the ability's fault.Combat/Leveling: I put these two in the same box, primarily as I said above enemies are very one and done.Once you have a way to kill XYZ, you do that every time you see one of them. (And you don't even need all the new moves to do it.) Because of this, leveling is mostly just stat bumps on your leveling grid, as the expanded move sets dont add anything to combat other than flair. At the end of the game I had full built into sword damage/break, but somehow my gun was still outputting more damage than all the sword moves could possibly hope for. (40% defense bypass broken AF) I can only imagine how much easier bosses would be if I full built into the gun.Story/Characters: The background/opening story is interesting to me; mixing that steampunk/mystical/apocalypse vibe. It starts out strong but quickly both becomes bloated (with names and jargon) but also rushed? Things just happen and are presented as if you are part of them, but it felt more like I was along for the ride. Other characters are doing things, you just happen to be around. Mostly a well //structured// story, but was more of a rough outline than anything I'm going to hold onto.------------------Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is a game where I can see vision of everything they were going for. Simply the majority of that was not pushed to its logical end point and left me wanting more. I hope this is "first game" syndrome for the DEVs and that perhaps another 3-6 months more in the oven might have brought this game UP TO A FIRM YES at full price, rather than "pick it up on sale." As the story of the game ends I do expect a sequel and hope they can read the reviews and get that last 10% of goodness into their games.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: game is short and sweet. I really enjoyed it. 100% it in 8.5 hours.personally I thought the story was good, there were a couple areas I think it could improve on but overall it made a good hook. combat could be a bit better. I think theres potential for more but as it currently stands the combat is very easy once you get a feel for it.exploration was nice, the art and design for each area is pretty. wish the rewards from some of the chests were a bit better but overall it was alright. had fun finding all the corkis before I bought the map to find the last one.unless you dont mind spending $20 for a short experience definitely pick it up on sale. but its def worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I would strongly recommend this game to anyone wishing to discover Metroidvania games ! Yes, it is fairly easy compared to most games availabe. It took me 10 hours to 100% it, the boss fights were very easy....But the overall experience is really nice ! The graphisms are splendid, the world is a mix of Steampunk and western. _childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A short metroidvania with decent gameplay and alright story.Solid traversal mechanics, combat has a few too many bells and whistles and enemies don't seem to have *any* delay set between attacks, which makes losing health a certianty in some places.Took me ~10 hours to beat, didn't bother to 100% it. If you have a craving for a metroidvania with solid art style and traversal, I would recomend Gestalt.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a really fun "metroidvania"-style game.  Beautiful sprite work and tight controls for the most part.  I don't want to give this game a negative review because it was so enjoyable, however the ending is awful and really kills any sense of triumph from defeating the final boss.  I get that they're trying to setup a sequel, but the way they handled the main character after the final boss fight was atrocious and completely disrespectful to the entire journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game. The story grab my attention from the first.Amazing art and gameplay: a metroidvania to remember for sure.My only observation: is difficult sometimes to follow the thread to the history. I think the writting team put a lot of effort on it, so should be amazing something to review the history from the game menu or somewhere.If you enjoy 16/32bit pixel art games, good character mechanics and an amazing history, this game is for you
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Short, but enjoyable game to burn some time on. Good art and character designs, always appreciative of that in pixel-games. I wasn't too invested into the story personally, although I'd honestly just attribute that to it being fairly wordy and lacking dialogue sound effects to keep myself still focused. Despite that silly nitpick of mine, the combat asks you to be pretty on your toes as mid-to-later enemies are pretty quick between their actions. Often times you get a couple swings in before having to dodge out, which can be tedious against beefier enemies. The movement gets pretty fun to work with the further you progress which is always a bonus. The ending is a bit abrupt but that's fine. Overall pretty fun
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: So, in very much two minds about this game;It scratched the metroidvania itch, absolutely, it's not particularly difficult but the combat is good. Movement upgrades, the exploration and the secrets therein were good, while pretty linear for a metroidvania. If you're a habitual explorer, at a certain point your power scaling goes through the roof and combat becomes a cakewalk.The pixel graphics, backgrounds, character portraits etc were really well done and the music was pretty good but it didn't blow me awayThe story itself was pretty good imo, a little exposition heavy but it gelled for me. You can learn tidbits about characters from certain item pickups and the world is an interesting setting with some good shades of grey to the antagonists and their motivations. Dialogue choices also have some nice flavour implications but as far as I can tell don't actually have an impact except in one sidequest (I could be wrong about this but not planning another playthrough soon) Also, the bartender never has any rumours for you, don't know why there's an option to ask about themWithout spoiling anything, the ending was a disappointment. The spoiler text below won't technically spoil the ending but you can infer what you will from itOverall, I'd recommend it as a solid game with an interesting setting, happy with the price I paid for it and I'm looking forward to where the devs go next with the game and their future endeavours
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game years before it's release and finally had time to play it. Took me about 7 hours for a 100% completion, so it is shorter than i expected.What i liked:Beautiful artstyle and a great soundtrack. The steampunk aesthetic felt perfect.Variety in combat. There are a plentitude of skills to unlock, so no battle really feels boring.Can get all achievements in one run, there is however no replayability at all.Some gripes i have:Game is too short. While I often don't have a problem with short games, I feel like Gestalt had missed opportunities. This may just come from how enjoyable the game was in itself, but I would've liked a larger map with more character quests.It is very linear. Having played multiple metroidvanias til now, Gestalt feels lacking in the exploration aspect. There are no alternative routes as it's all locked behind main quest abilities, therefore not much incentive to 100% it.Overall, I'd give the game an 8/10 or so. Even if it is lacking in some aspects, the time I had with it was definetely enjoyable. Overall sucker for steam punk and metroidvanias, so this fell right in my alley.I highly reccomend this game for anyone interested. While I have paid more for shorter games, I recommend to wait for a sale if you are unsure about the length.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge Metroidvania fan, literally one of my favorite genres. This game leans a bit harder on the Castlevania side, and is a lot of fun. I enjoy the RPG aspect of the leveling and getting to choose how to upgrade your stats and unlock new abilities. Also the game is pretty dang gorgeous, the level design is generally pretty great, and overall, I enjoyed the game.However, there are some... drawbacks to the game.First: there are several upgrades for your light attack combo that are generally not worthwhile in the slightest. Later in the game, Whirlwind Attack is much better and more usable. And even at that, it can often be hard to use. In particular, enemies just attack too fast to make use of more than a couple of attacks at a time, unless you Break them with the gun's energy shot.Second: The accessories are very, very samey. Most of the accessories do... pretty similar things in small amounts. I would have liked them to be a bit more unique.Third: The ending is bad. The story is, for the most part, pretty dang enjoyable, right up to the very end. After completing the final battle, however, the last bit of story is just... extremely weak and it ends very unsatisfactorily.If the ending being bad doesn't bother you, I would still play this. It is genuinely fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Fun metroidvania but it runs at a break neck pace. Combat good, movement mechanics clean, enemy variety sufficient and fun to fight. My only problem with the game is the story, which can be a deal breaker for some. It is told at a break neck pace and it feels like they wanted to write so much more but ran out of time. The ending is especially insulting as they just start throwing plot points at you, at one point even randomly throwing in the "im your father" and it feels cheap. 7/10 would recommend as it is a good experience through and through just wish the story had more time to breath.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was made for me. The character is cool as ♥♥♥♥ and feels good to control, and the pixel art is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous.It's a short game, which I think works in its favour. It's certainly not a traditional metroidvania, and more of a linear platformer with metroidvania-like side areas if you want to collect everything. Skill points are given out to you very very quickly, which fits the pace of the game.Story is good. The characters are pretty simple but they get the job done nicely, and they let the main character bounce off of them.If you ever get that feeling where you need to exist in a platformer for a while, this is a fantastic game in which to do it. 10/10 look forward to replaying.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Solid experience. The combat system is simple but there are quite lot of abilities to use. The world building of the game is seriously impressing. I got hooked up with the story, the game is not too long or too short, took me 14 hours to get 100%. The pixel art is awesome, and the soundtrack too. It's not hard at all, especially in the end, the last three bosses are really easy and i was a bit disappointed. For how it ends, i suppose we are getting a story dlc or a sequel. Maybe this is what i didn't like in the end. The game is heavy on story, but the ending leaves us with a HUGE cliffhanger.Great job guys, i'm looking for a dlc or for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game follows the good ol tried and true metroidvania style map and abilities.The skill tree unlocks more abilities as you get them through progression and levels.Its got secrets and maps that allow you to find stuff that you missed instead of having to refer to a guide to find em.The best part, the collectables scattered around the whole map. After getting all of them, it pretty much says at that point "You've beaten the game through and through, have this broken overpowered item now." that makes you invincible and regenerates your powerful energy.And the fun of it? You can get this before you fight the final boss so you can just roll over it.Also, my hours reflected in this is how long it took to 100% this beautiful game~
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: it was aight. Ending kinda sucked tbh. it was a little more "Punk" Than "steam" imo, but the world was neat. WAAAAY to exposition heavy. Hard to follow sometimes with all the goofy made up ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and wacky names. Combat was fine. Kinda annoying but it also was pretty easy so whatever. Its not really a metroidvania. Solid 2d linear action combat with fun platforming. Backtracking is just for collectibles and ♥♥♥♥. You largely can just straight path through the game with little consequence. Pretty banger ost thoGrab it on sale for a solid 9-10 hour run
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! Haven't played metroidvania for a long time, I think this game brought me back to the genre. Some people complains about lots of dialogues but for me its ok and gives light on the story wich is cool. Combat, leveling, abilitys, art  everething is great, aspecially music!Hope to see some kind of a sequel (post-credits scene :) )
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Just seeing the sharp pixel art and striking main character design, I knew I had to grab this. And even beyond those factors, it did not disappoint.The story is really interesting and presents a lot of information and history without coming across as overwhelming, and this is greatly supported by the stellar writing and character interactions. Each of the main cast and side characters you meet along the way all have their own way of thinking, their own motivations and all manage to stand out as memorable. Even simple NPCs manage to stand out due to unique side quest stories or just fun dialogue. The way you unlock new abilities like fast travel and your double jump are also done in a creative way while still feeling like big moments in the story. It certainly makes exploration of older areas exciting, as you're constantly encouraged to go back to uncover every path and room. The combat and level up system are also constantly evolving, giving you plenty of options to approach each encounter, and experimenting with new combos and strategies always feels satisfying.My only real complaints would be that the music is rather forgettable and having enemies constantly respawn every time you leave a room does sometimes make backtracking a bit tedious. Other than that however, this games is an absolute treat.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty solid. A nice, well rounded vania. It took me abt 10 hours to 100%. I don't know if this is the type of game I'd return to, nothing really stuck with me when I look at the story and world presented, and all the mechanics and level design while solid and textbook, nothing stood out as an identity Gestalt could call its own. Still there's plenty of games that don't get what makes Metroidvanias so standout,  and make a product that's as cohesive to start to finish.  Just don't expect much of the plot.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt is such a great yet simple Metroidvania.Beautiful pixelated graphics mixed with solid and rewarding combat.A short yet sweet adventure that was worth 100% completion.My only major complaint would be the lack of exploration that's really available.The game is extremely linear for the genre with the only time backtracking will ever be a thing is the very first areas have one or two things you need later upgrades for, and if you missed anything.Other than that, 100% worth playing.I'll be keeping an eye on any games that come from these devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Good metroidvania, with lovely style, a interesting story, and engaging gameplay. the game felt polished and even though a bit short i appreciated my time with it! Overall  a great experience, main flaws would be around the ending that felt rushed (maybe lack of time  and the devs had to push the game out ?).
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I have several critiques of the game, first is that the game just does nothing that has not been done better in other metroidvanias, and does not iterate on any of its ideas in any meaningful way to separate it from the crowd. The power ups granted are nothing original, and the skill tree is mostly stat boosts with very little meaningful differences in gameplay besides raw numbers. After the halfway point of the game I stopped exploring for anything besides the corgis because most of the chests off the beaten path are just consumables you can get in stores. And the ending is extremely unsatisfying for everything you have gone through up to that point that it sours the experience that makes these faults in the game much worse. The game's biggest problem is its lack of originality, and its story does not save it, and in fact makes it even worse because of the interesting stuff of the lore of the game just does not really have much in gameplay that it affects and makes it seem just so unoriginal when comparing it to other metroidvanias of the genre like axiom verge, blasphemous, hollow knight, or guacamelee. Its sad to see it cause the game has a good style to it that is just let down by the gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, short and sweet, decent story, satisfying gameplay, the only issues is that most of the power is given to in a very short span, so the difficulty curve drops significantly if you're 100% every area when you get all the story upgrades, making the final boss fights trivial.Regardless, one of the best metroidvanias I've played in a while, with it's price it is a must get in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game with some caveats. It's a relatively easy metroivania, and it has good graphics and music. The combat flows well, and enemies telegraph their attacks in a manner where you can avoid them if you react quickly. Bosses are interesting and fun.The downsides are that this is a very short game, for $20 you are getting an 7-10 hour experience. I had 100% this game at 9 hours, and that was primarily due to me not noticing a door, and just randomly checking houses for the last corgi. I think it's worth that price for that amount of gameplay given the general quality but maybe that won't be true for you.The second is that there is an ongoing mystery throughout the game that is never answered, and the last 5 seconds of the game are a terrible cliffhanger. This game took 7 years of development, and who knows if any of the mysteries they raised will get any answers. The story itself is kind of eh, and gets the job done, but honestly, the end soured me on the whole thing.If you don't really care for the story, and just want a solid, pretty, relatively easy and short metroivania, this game might be for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved thed game. The lore was unique but didn't overstay explanations, also, art, GORGEOUS, loved the humor and writing. I do think the combat was a bit lacking in some parts, not a fan of the item mechanics, and I wish there were some more enemies, not a lot of enemy variety. But overall i loved the game, 8 or 9/10, will absolutely look forward to the sequel
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's quite compentently made, flows real nice and is pretty to look at. It doesn't do anything really bad, it's on the easier side of games in general and sadly a rather short game. (8h for me to 100%) The worst thing is the ending, feels like a major cop-out. While I totaly understand that scope in a game can be threatening for a small develepment team and the game had to end rather sooner than later, there is no closure whatsoever.It's still a recommend. Mind the short playtime, but it's a really fun 8 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A really good game that kept me hooked end-to-end, which in a gaming landscape full of live services yanking at your attention and daily gaming hours is no small feat to me.Combat is good and I enjoyed it. Story is nothing particularly awe-inspiring but a decent little adventure. They aren't exactly subtle that they want to do more, and I'll be there for that!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Fun game and worth your time, with caveats.+ Beautiful pixel graphics and evocative steampunk environments.+ Gameplay is smooth and traversal nearly flawless. Far better than many metroidvanias I've played.+ Many interesting monsters with varying combat-styles keep you on your toes. Not just palette swaps.+ Story is good, although it needed a bit more time in the oven.Cons (which really all boil down to a rush to market)- Game is a finished product, but artifacts of a grander scope remain. This is particularly noticeable in the town with invisible walls separating you from the Machinist, and numerous NPCs who were clearly meant to be quest-givers just moping around.- Underwhelming items and a skill tree not fully fleshed out. Characters have some personality, but not enough.- Most disappointingly, the game gets progressively easier to the point where you can face tank all bosses.Still, I enjoyed most of my time with it and would recommend picking it up on sale. Hopefully, if a sequel is greenlit the developers will be given the time they need to finish it...and the first while they're at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I personally enjoyed this game.  Some people complained about length of the game or easy-ness, but for $20 US it felt pretty right to me.It would have been nice to not have such a cliffhanger ending so suddenly, but overall everything else was good.  It's pretty much that, it's good.  I personally like several of the characters and interactions between them.  By the time you reach end game, some of the last set of bosses feel easier than the first few.If you have not played any metroidvania style games in the past, this might be a good start as it is not that difficult and not super complicated.  Like there's not too much gear or "spells" to choose between.  Minimal back tracking which is also nice, unless you want to 100% the game.If there is DLC or sequal to this game I would pick it up.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is a solid 2D action game with RPG elements that, most importantly, desires to tell a story that I think is executed well enough within the context of the game. While there are a few areas that could be improved in the overall experience, I enjoyed my time with the game and think that this is an admirable first release from Metamorphosis Games. For a more in depth review, check out my video below!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A great bite-size metroidvania with a fun pixel art style. The story is ambitious, with supporting characters that are much more fleshed out than in most games. The upgrade tree is a nice change of pace from other metroidvanias' methods of giving you power. The boss fights are challenging without being punishing. Also, what other game has you rescuing wayward dogs in additional platforming challenges?
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: After waiting for all those years it was a treat to finally play G:S&C. The main draw of the game is the beautiful pixel art reminiscent of 32 bit systems. My only gripe is that it would have been nice to see some expression variation on those beautiful portraits to better communicate emotions during story scenes.The game is basically a very linear metroidvania with some light backtracking for 100%, so don't go in expecting much exploration. Instead, the combat and the story were the main gameplay meat for the game. The combat starts a bit dull but by getting upgrades it becomes way smoother and fun. However, buying too much stats upgrades and being smart with your accessories will trivialize bosses a  bit, so some self restrain is in order if challenge is desired. The story goes in  a  way exactly were you guess it will go, but somehow it kept me glued to see if my guesses were correct. Plus steampunk settings haven't been done in quite a while and this one has enough variations to spice it up. My two main complaints are that some characters sometimes just seem to be a  bit too resolved and not shaken by some revelations, and it would have been nice if, by going back to the tavern or other city npc location, Aletheia would discuss the latest adventure to gain a bit more insight into what she was thinking. Finally the game ends on a  cliffhanger that seems to hint to a sequel/DLC, and I feel like we could have gotten some extra lines of dialogue about what happened in the aftermath.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I have 100%'d the game and its achievements. Here's my thoughts:Gameplay: 9/10. Very Metroidvania - you'll be going back and forth quite a bit in the different areas of the game. Combat is fun and the enemies are quite varied. There's a skill tree system that lets you unlock new abilities and attacks along with stat boosts and equipment slots.Story: 8/10. Enjoyable. People were whining about dialogue but I personally didn't find it intrusive or a problem at all. That said, it can be a little tough to follow the more "nuanced" moments of the story sometimes. I'll speak a little on the ending later (in spoilers of course)Graphics: 9/10. Extremely well done pixel art. Movement is ultra fluid and the backgrounds in every biome was excellent.Music: 10/10. Sometimes when playing Metroidvanias I like to watch youtube on my second monitor or something. The music in this game curbed my enthusiasm to do that. Amazing stuff, very Western/Stempunk-ish, which fits this game perfectly. I *Loved* quite a few themes, liked a few others, and disliked none of them. Great stuff. Gonna buy the soundtrack.Atmosphere: 10/10. This is due to how well everything worked together. The scenery made you feel like you were running around a steampunk city, or a molten hot furnace, or a long-since deserted scrapyard filled with mysteries, and so on. The music fit these areas superbly, and the denizens you meet in these areas also made it all feel cohesive and whole.UI: 7/10. Overall it was fine, though I swear I constantly had trouble figuring out the controls for the map. Might just be my derpy self. Equipment system was fine, but it was a little annoying having to highlight the equipment you're currently using while trying to find something to replace it with in order to see what stats each item gives. A "Comparison" button would've been nice. Small gripe, though.Game hours: As stated, I 100%'d it and it took me close to 15 hours or so. This is about right imo. Keep in mind this is an Indie Metroidvania game. Its runtime was not going to be very long, and is heavily dependent on whether or not you the player backtracks alot or gets lost. I personally never got "lost", but I didn't follow any guides to 100% the game thus once I obtained all of the movement abilities, I did alot of backtracking and searching for secrets.Achievement Hunting: As stated above, I didn't really have a need to use any guides. Certain stores within the game lets you buy maps that point you to all the collectibles, and each boss has their own achievements. Nothing seems to be truly missable. Sidenote: I highly suggest completing the "Find all the Corgis" quest asap. Granted, you won't finish until 90% of the game is completed, but the reward makes the next 10% quite easy. Also - The Cartographer's achievement. This one is to complete the map 100%. The final boss' room is included in this map. If you're at 99.3% like I was, you're finished. Just head to the final boss. If you did that already and still at 99.3%, there are houses and inn rooms that also need to be entered to hit that 100% mark. Check the town areas as well as the tavern, as it has six total inn rooms.Now, as for the ending. The only thing I'll say outside of spoilers is: It seems to be setting up for a sequel. Now spoilers: And that's my review. I highly recommend this one if you're into metroidvanias. It's not extremely hard (though enemies can mess you up if you get too confident; especially in the beginning) and overall I had a very good time. If a sequel does pop up, I do hope certain grievances are improved upon...other than the dialogue thing. Like legit I don't know why people are complaining about this game's smattering of cutscenes lol. They are not long, not THAT many, and explained what was going on both behind the scenes and up front.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed a lot of the base combat, the light, heavy and gun attacks feels great and flow together really well. Some of the attacks feel like they don't fit or have a place like the drop kick (which is fun but not really useful) and the spin attack on the hold light attack button. The dodge also feels really nice and pulls it together making for some interesting also fighting game combat feeling at times.The writing is good, the world is really interesting and the characters are pretty good. I'm nearly finished the game and it does feel like some of the later reveals around the time of the rain level are supposed to hit harder than they do. They feel like their supposed to be twists when they feel more like they play off of the earlier established stuff kind of as expected. Also there are some common mix up in how things are spelt, they change back and forth between them.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is my recommendation for anyone who has never played a Metroidvania before. It has most of what you'd expect from the modern MV, but it's quick and easy. There's plenty of optional pathways and secrets, but you're never gonna get *lost* lost (which they somehow managed to do without stupid waypoints). The price might be a bit high for how long the game takes (I got every achievement in about 10 hours), but the art and music are absolutely fantastic.And "pet all the dogs" being the collect-quest? C'mon, how is that not the best?
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: What's here is really well done, and a blast to play. It is just waaayyy too short at 5.5 hours (I accidentally left the game running when I went to sleep one night, so the playtime on my account is not accurate). The game ended at the point where the story started picking up some steam. For the amount of development time spent making it, I would have hoped to see the end being the midway point of the experience. I'm definitely hoping there'll be a sequel with less development woes, and a more complete final product.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game.  Felt like a great fast metroidvania.  Characters were good.  Story was good.  Animations on characters were engaging.  Combat was good.  I found that unlocking the specific moves didn't matter too much, but getting stronger through the unlock tree felt rewarding.  putting on different accessories felt good too because I could feel the difference things different accesories made.  Movement was excellent, getting to secrets was intuitive and fun, if anything  I thought it was underutilized.   All around great game, sad it was so short.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is a beautiful Metroidvania-style game set in a steampunk world that is struggling to survive after a costly war took place.The graphics are very detailed and quite vivid! Animations are solid and while the combat can feel a bit slower paced, it's still a fun adventure exploring through the various locations and discovering puzzles and hidden areas.The music is decent and usually fitting to the areas although nothing in particular really stood out to me.  Sound effects were also fitting for the enemies and noise of battle but it felt like some were missing or there could have been more depth to certain attack effects or reactions.As Metroidvania style games go, the exploration was fun, earning new traversal mechanics opening up new areas to explore and more secrets to backtrack to find.  While the in-game map was helpful, you needed to buy upgrades to have it automatically show where uncollected items were and the stamps you could use for notation were limited in their use.Despite it being a little rough around the edges, I could not stop playing once I started and finished the game in about 8-9 hours taking my time in completing every achievement.The only downside I would say is the ending feels a bit....sudden and kind of took the rug out from under my feet. It's not bad in setting up a possible sequel but it left me a bit puzzled despite wanting more.I would recommend the game if you're a fan of metroidvania games and want a quick easy fix! 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder exceeded my wildest expectations and then some.  With beautiful pixel art graphics that will transport many of us back to the glory days of 16 and 32 bit, an outstanding soundtrack and smooth, responsive controls, there is very little here not to like.  I felt that the storyline itself, although not the most original, was quite well done and sets us up for a sequel which I am really excited for.  I think if I had any criticism (if you can even call it one), I wish that certain aspects of the storyline were a bit more fleshed out and they elaborated a bit more about each character's past and what gives them a stake in the central storyline.  Bosses were a little on the easy side, and while I don't advocate for brutally difficult souls-style bosses, a hard or challenge mode for each boss would have been a nice addition, rewarding different outfits or other cosmetics.  Anyways, I recommend Gestalt without a second thought, you'll be really glad that yu picked it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Howdy Howdy guys, I hope everyone is doing alright. Gestalt: Steam & Cinder is no doubt a great metroidvania. It doesn't do anything new that hasn't done before and there is certainly room for improvement. It took me roughly 14 hours to 100% which isn't a terrible amount of time for the asking price. Animations feel nice and smooth, The SNES graphics are amazing, and the music is pretty solid. The Story is probably what I have the biggest gripe with. While I definitely felt invested, most people (including myself) will get to the conclusion and feel like the game wasn't finished.  It's basically gets to it's home stretch and then immediately cuts to black without any sort of meaningful resolution. Which is shame because the story was a pretty good 7.5/10 for me. I like the characters, I like suspense, and I deeply wanted to know more about the world at large.Another problem spot for people will potentially be the combat. While it is by no means bad and the moves you are give do infact look very nice there are some decisions that were made that go against the design. You have plenty of combo abilities to utilize or extend your attacks but enemies do not flinch when you attack them. So more often than not you will find your self using hit and run tactics where you run, hit the enemy, and then immediately roll behind them or dodge backwards. And then rinse and repeat until dead. You can stagger enemies so that you can combo on them but the stagger is mostly for tanky shield enemies that you often have to use hit and run tactics on as well. Bosses can also be staggered but most of the time dealing stagger damage felt like a waste of time over hitting them right out. Bosses are also waaaaay to easy and while they have fun looking abilities none of them hit particularly hard. A hard difficulty option would have gone a long way.Now, that being said, I found this game to be immensely enjoyable and minus those gripes I really did find myself wanting mroe. If you are looking a fun engaging world with metroidvania exploration and great looking animation and a fairly solid story (minus the ending) I whole heartedly recommend checking it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: the gameplay is fun, if a little stiff in some situations (try hopping over an enemy and swinging at their back for example, it's unreliable if you time it too tightly). The art is good and does what it needs to. Other than the wasps, enemy AI is decent enough. Bosses are very susceptible to post-combo punishes that can really trivialize an otherwise fun fight. The metroidvania aspects are... mediocre (earlier areas don't change at all after events that should have drastically changed them, areas are noticeably incomplete, and there's a supremely pointless quest board system that you never need to revisit in any area besides the vaults). The narrative is okay, right up until the ending, which ... look, I'm gonna put spoilers after this sentence.You beat the final boss after two phases (identical except that the second phase has way to reload your gun) of dodging lighting and chip damaging him. Bizarely he's the first enemy in the game that doesn't have a stun bar. The final cut scene starts, even though it really feels like you should be hitting the real phase 2 of the boss right about now. With the piddliest sound effect ever (I'm not even sure there was one, and I'm not going to replay that fight to relive this disappointment), the final boss one shot kills your character with a derringer. The character who has been face-tanking fireballs for the last five minutes, dead from what amounts to a papercut. No explanation, no payoff, just *pop*, your struggles are meaningless, and now suddenly mr generic narrative foil (who explicitly did not have any powers and also had no buildup in the story whatsoever) is the chosen one, fade to black.I'd refund this if I could. Oh, and then there's a generically ominous post credit sequence that proves a) your character is too stupid to tell if someone in their arms is alive or dead, and b) that the writers had no plan and no idea what was going to happen once the abyss opened.I should have clued in that this game is an incomplete mess when I got to the other side of the scrap sea, took the elevator down to Urd, and it was a single room with a ridiculously easy boss rather than ANY of the things that the story had said Urd would be. In conclusion, it gets a C. I can't recommend it, although the forest area (last real area of the game) has some fun movement puzzles, the gameplay is unexceptional enough that the sheer disrespect to my time embodied in the ending ruins thee rest of it for me. Play Hollow Knight, one of the Ori games, Pseudoregalia, Rain World, Metroid, Animal Well, Axiom Verge, Castlevania Advance Collection, Bloodstained, Blasphemous, Iconoclasts, Cave Story, Shantae or anything else like them instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly, the main word I can find for  is . Most aspects of the game start really strong, but sooner or later, issues start showing up for almost all of them.Story is intriguing at first, but a lot of questions remain unanswered, motivations of most characters remain hazy at best, and the ending is... rough.Metroidvania aspects are solid, but that's it. Aside of backtracking for missing items, there is not a lot of room for exploration - the order of locations is very linear. Almost no optional content other than backtracking and few challenge rooms where you can get upgrade materials.Combat would be solid if not for enemies poise - you cannot interrupt their attacks. Which is why most of your fights are "attack-roll-attack-roll-etc". You can't afford putting more than three hits in a row without getting hit yourself. Which is rather dumb, considering some of skills you acquire extend your combo (which you can never use).Bosses are all around the place. Some of them have very annoying attack patterns, leaving you close to no windows for attacks unless you take damage, and some die so quickly you keep asking yourself "wait, is it all?".Visuals are good, I will give the game that. Music is good, but not very memorable.So, I honestly not sure if I would recommend this game. Again, it is not horrible, but for it's price, I would expect a little bit more than 8 hours for 100%, especially compared to another games in the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Fun metroidvania but lacking in areas.Pros:-excellent music-great pixel art-snappy and responsive gameplayCons:-Exposition heavy; you will be reading dialogue very frequently and given the run time of the game I would have preferred a different approach to world building than straight forced exposition. The world they created has interesting elements which I would have loved to find out more about but there is a lack of optional dialogue, books, item descriptions, etc which allow me to engage with the world further.-Frustrating mechanical choices; Most of my issue lay in the combat of the game. Enemies attack very quickly and take no hit stun which forces you to dodge. While this isn't a problem the dodge does have a cooldown which is miliseconds slower than the enemy attack cycles forcing you to commit your dodge to just rolling. Later when abilities give you access to dodge attacks using them often lands you without a dodge and because of the enemy attack frequency taking unnecessary damage. Enemies are simple to defeat which takes away from the frustration of the dodge roll. But because you have very little interaction with them you can't fully take advantage of the break system. Player immunity/environmental respawn is questionable. There are times in the game where you will be next to a hazard which causes an environmental respawn but if you were next to an enemy they will start attacking the player immediately and there is not enough/any player immunity to reposition yourself and re-engage with the enemies.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a souls-like metroidvania I vaguely heard of once before it became available. As I remember, it looked quite interesting and fun to play, so I bought the game once I saw it was released on Steam.Having spent the past several days playing this game, sinking over ten hours into the game, I am pleased with how Gestalt: Steam and Cinder lives up to the genres of souls-like and metroidvania. The story feels like that of Dark Souls, which is the most accurate comparison I believe can be made. Similarly, Aletheia, Gestalt's main protagonist, is this game's version of Alucard from Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. I am not going to explain why the comparisons to Dark Souls and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night can be made, because that will spoil the story. However, I imagine other players can make inferences after playing Gestalt for themselves. Even though that may lead to some spoilers, the fact Gestalt is a perfect steampunk mixture of Dark Souls and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night makes it one of the best games I have ever played.Gestalt's steampunk atmosphere is also thoroughly enjoyable. Although I am not a fan of the steampunk genre per se, I found its environments well-designed and the attention to detail incredible. I think it is fascinating how Gestalt ties biblical references into its lore in a way that makes each reference feel unique and intriguing from a steampunk perspective. For example, R'lyeh, while a Lovecraftian reference to the city in which Cthulhu sleeps instead of an actual biblical story, is not at all what one might expect from the name. Rather being a complete city in which one might encounter Cthulhu or some other eldritch horror, such as another Great Old One, R'lyeh in Gestalt is actually a laboratory where experiments are run.I do have two critiques regarding Gestalt, though, one major and the other minor. My major issue with Gestalt was how underwhelming Urd was in-game. Urd is one of the locations the player can visit, supposedly, and it is built up in such a way that it feels like it should have been a proper location. Instead, Urd is way too small, and its only two purposes are to advance the game's plot and make players fight one of the game's bosses. While the boss fight itself was quite enjoyable and played an incredible track of boss music I enjoyed listening to, Urd itself had so much potential and was a place I was really looking forward to exploring before getting there. It is a shame that Urd did not live up to that potential, because it would have been really cool to explore the place.My minor concern is the lack of rumors Aletheia can hear from Vincent. Every time I went to see him in Irkalla, I always asked if there were any rumors going around to see if he had something to say. I hoped he might offer a side quest or clues that might point to one, or offer additional lore about the world of Gestalt that would have been fascinating to listen/read about. Unfortunately, Vincent always says that nothing has percolated yet, so I do not think he really has anything else to say apart from his minor involvement in the game's plot. Still, every time I find myself passing through, I always make sure to grab a drink as part of the steampunk experience. He may not have rumors to provide, but a good drink each visit is worth it after advancing the plot or exploring.Despite my criticism, Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is super fun to play and has become one of my favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. It has nice and smooth combat, It tries something fresh with its bullets and armor bars. You can fight an enemy with your sword and reserve a few of your ammo to deal with more difficult enemies later or you can spam it out. I loved the setting and the story. I was hooked on enough to read every dialogue. The game runs buttery smooth and most of the metroidvania exploration segments are good in this game as well. You unlock a new ability which allows you to to quickly revisit an area for a few additional upgrades and most of the time you don't have to backtrack too much.*There's also some negatives though: Difficulty is ''too easy''. I was able to nuke down bosses way too quickly. Being able to burst down bosses in 2 stun bars. This is to me mostly a damage number problem. Because the bosses all do have interested and variet movesets.*A lot of normal mobs you deal with either stunning them and bursting them down or you attack twice then dodge. Repeat.*The game has a major focus on combat. Which is not really bad i just would've enjoyed more platforming sections to have more variety.The game is about 10-12 hours long. Maybe a little bit more if you really wanna 100% complete it. For the price and what we get i feel like this was a great deal. One of the more fun metroidvania i played in a while. I really hope it doesn't end here. I wanna see more Gestalt: Steam & Cinders or just more from this team that has made this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish that steam allowed you to rate different aspects of a game differently. Overall good. I had fun and enjoyed looking at it. Story has issues. The presentation is fantastic, and everything FEELS very nice mechanically. Music and graphics are magnificent, and the controls are responsive and reasonably intuitive. Despite peoples' complaints, I feel like the length was about right. I wouldn't really have wanted to spend more than 10-12 hours playing a Metroidvania title. You never reach a point where you're one-shotting everything, so I was trying to pay attention to combat, but the healing became so cheap and plentiful that it was easier to just mash and heal up than to try to fight thoughtfully. The last few boss fights, including the final boss went this way. The maps are a little bare bones but they get better as you purchase the map upgrade key items. I opened all chests, collected all skill points, reached maximum level, rescued all the dogs. Rescuing the dogs gives you an accessory that trivializes the rest of the game, so use caution there. Certain things annoyed me. An important antagonist has a sprite that is clearly smoking a cigarette. His portrait is posed as though he is holding a cigarette. There is no cigarette, and it's too conspicuous to have been forgotten, so that means it was removed. In a game that involves guns, liquor, injecting drugs, and a lot of dead bodies, the removal of a cigarette is comically puritanical. Script is a little long-winded but characters don't sound like tiktok influencers. There's no "modern audiences" nonsense, no millenialisms or zoomerisms at all, which was refreshing. The story is a little bit "chosen one" but is generally well-told (up to a point) so that's forgivable. What isn't forgivable is the ending. If it turns out there are multiple endings, I'll change this review, but as far as I can tell there is only one, and it is bad. None of the setup that was laid out over the course of the game pays off and you just get some nonsense out of left field. None of the important questions get answered, and in fact, the ending itself raises even MORE questions. It feels like they had something entirely different planned and just ran out of money or time or both and just decided to push it out the door. It really reminded me of my experience with Mass Effect, where I finished the game, sped through the credits, got a vague, unsatisfying teaser afterwards, reloaded my save file to try for the 'real' ending only to get the same result, and then looked it up and got annoyed when I realised that's really all there is. What a shame to have invested myself in this story only to have the rug pulled right at the end. Puts a mouldering capstone on the whole experience.   If they had managed to pull that story together with a satisfying conclusion, this would've been an instant favourite.

_childDocuments_.review: this game is "ok". i hate saying that cause im sure a lot of hard work went into making it, but it feels kind of disappointing to play. every level has a different background track, but they all sound the same. an opportunity was missed to give each level its own identity instead of them all sounding the same. combat and movement is very responsive, but a lot of enemies can be very boring to fight. others can be extremely frustrating (the lancers, and the stupid tri-shot bees). enemy difficulty is managed by just "make enemies more annoying" than trying to get creative with enemy design. by the end of the game they resort to just "spam poison so if you dont buy enough antivenoms you kinda just die" visual design is outstanding, the levels look amazing all around, but the monotone soundtrack leaves the environment and ambience feeling less outstanding than it should given how the game looks. the story is alright, nothing really to complain about. the skill point system feels redundant, since you can pretty much unlock the whole thing, the ability to reset your points seems useless when you can just fill the entire tree with points.overall, good for the price but disappointing in that it could have been better.

_childDocuments_.review: falls into that uncanny valley where there's no particular piece of it that's obviously incomplete, but the game as a whole feels like something that suffered a sharp reduction in scope relatively late in development, and what we've got is just the pieces that happened to be finished when they decided to call it done.The signs range from a complex skill tree where half the upgrades are either pointless or actively counterproductive because enemy combat behaviour isn't sophisticated enough for them to matter (the combo extenders actually make you categorically worse in melee!); to a weirdly high cutscene density relative to the actual size of the map; to the fact that – excluding those granted during the tutorial – there are only four exploration-relevant upgrades in the entire game, two of which are acquired within five minutes of each other immediately prior to entering the endgame; to the way the game's promotional materials have a strong focus on precision platforming gameplay, yet in the actual game, precision platforming puzzles are almost entirely restricted to the final dungeon; to an ending that doesn't resolve the plot so much as simply stop, at a point which strongly feels like it was originally intended to be the end of the first act of a two-act structure.Like, don't get me wrong, there are  of the game that I had a lot of fun with, but those parts simply don't add up to a complete experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so it's one of those games when you would like to give a "hmmm maybe" rating instead of recommanding or not.I'm giving it a thumbs up because I globally enjoyed it but it has its lot of problems.Pros:* I like the character design and the global lore* It's quite a short game, I finished it under 8h. A pro for me, because I don't have the time to play all the 50+ hours games that come out so a shorter one is sometimes a welcome change. But it might be a cons if you're expecting a long game.* The various environments you visit are kinda cool honestly.* Really it's a game with its own atmosphere entirely, and I really liked it, that was one of the main reasons I finished it.* I encountered only a single bug where my character was stuck in the ground, and it only happened once. So game's quite stable.Cons:* For some reason, a npc will clumsily break the 4th wall during the tutorial telling you to open menus or whatever... I mean wtf?* Not sure if it's intentional or not but the way the story is told you can predict some of the "plot twists" long long before they happen, except when they're kinda BS.* The combat system is... weird. The only way to stagger/interrupt an enemy is to empty its green "posture" bar, which will stun it for a couple seconds. The problem is that it's really the *only* way to stop an enemy action. You learn skills, longer combos etc from the skill tree, but most enemies attack so fast that you can just throw a couple attacks before having to dodge. It's kinda annoying tbh, also the endurance bar (for dodges) is super small, so don't even hope to spam dodges.* Story wise again, the ending is *extremely* disappointing.* It looks like there are remnants of stuff that was taken out of the game. For example  you can ask one of the NPCs "any intel for me?" and he will never have anything to reply, no matter how far you're into the game. Also empty or closed buildings in the main town, or places that look like they should see far more action than what they do.So yeah... it's really hard to tell you if you should buy it or not.Then well, it's only a 20€ game and for that price it does quite OK.

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is a steampunk metroidvania that is beautifully animated and has satisfying movement as well as the smoothest 2D combat since Dead Cells. You play as Aletheia, a badass mercenary, armed with a sword and gun in addition to both a dodge roll and a backdash. The combat is where this game shines the brightest. Sword attacks are nothing particularly unique but the gun is where the combat goes from good to great. Many enemies are mechanical and have green stagger meters alongside their red health bar. The Tesla bullets from the gun can stun the enemies with a stagger meter, causing the enemy to be staggered and you can rush them with your sword. You generate more bullets by attacking enemies and quickly shift into a rhythm where you alternate between rushing in with your sword, generate bullets, shoot bullets, then rush enemy. It feels nothing short of sublime. It should be known that GSC is on the easier side. This does not bother me, but for those looking for a soulslike experience- you won't find it here. I only had a handful of deaths while playing through to 100%, most of which I used to quick travel out of far away portions of the map. If there was an accessory or ability to warp back to the last save point in the late game, my death total would be in the single digits. Bosses in general are not difficult, which is a bit of a surprise as they are oftentimes built up to be a complete badass, only for me to steamroll them without using a health flask. This is not intended to be a humblebrag (I am a veteran of the genre but by no means an expert), but a disparity between how the game builds up the bosses and how they actually come across in gameplay. Is this a power fantasy or ludonarrative dissonance? You decide. Speaking of story, it is the weakest part of this game. It is a fairly standard Chosen One narrative (which is not a problem) but the great majority of the story takes place via dialogue during which Aletheia is not actually present or anywhere near the action. As a result, I did not feel myself overly invested in the overarching plot, only what Aletheia was up to, likable badass as she is. While one would think this would even out to an average story, there is a narrative decision in the last sixty seconds of the story that made me throw up my hands in frustration. I wondered if perhaps I had missed out on an item to have gotten that ending, but no- this appears to be it. Maybe this will be retconned or expanded on with additional content, but it left a sour taste in my mouth. Ending aside, Gestalt:Steam and Cinder is a complete joy to play and I would heartily recommend it to anyone who is looking for a breezy 2D metroidvania with phenomenal combat, a likable protagonist and beautiful setting. While it is a shorter experience clocking in at just under 10 hours of playtime on my completionist run, these cinders certainly do burn bright.
