_childDocuments_.review: This recommendation is more than a little tentative.Why might I recommend this to you? Well, the gameplay, in general, is pretty solid. In a lot of ways is really feels like a classic...I would say PS1 pixelart game, both good and bad (but for an oldie like me, pretty good). The controls are tight, though perhaps a little too rigid in combat at times. Still, the combat looks great, and generally feels pretty good. The upgrades are fun, and the levels are generally pretty enjoyable to traverse as you gain movement abilities. Plus, the game just looks gorgeous. It is a solid metroidvania game...but that's where it peaks for me.Why might I recommend you steer clear? Well, how much do you hate dialogue in games like this, because holy schmoly is there a lot. Sometimes I swear you can't enter a new area without a cutscene. Rarely a cut scene involving your character, but of other characters talking about esoteric lore and nonsense. And every dialogue will last for at least 3 or 4 sentences longer than needed. Look, I like lore and story, I like a game that can draw me in to its captivating world, but this isn't it, at least not for me. There is an idea of "saying more with less" in writing, and that idea is no where to be seen here. I also should say, the difficulty has become a big of a mixed bag in the later half of the game. I either shoot enemies with some of my bullets, which kills them instantly, or if I am out of ammo, I melee them for absolutely pathetic damage while they stagger me out of my attacks, never staggered from their own. So depending on if I have ammo, fights have become either trivial or annoying. What's worse, enemies have a sort of poise meter you can break to stun them and hit them for bit damage...except it almost never comes into play except with bosses, where it is pretty much mandatory (if you don't want the fight to be painfully long). Melee attacks do almost nothing to poise, only your Telsa bullets do. Except for the vast majority of enemies, I am better off just shooting them with regular bullets, which deal so much damage as to make stunning them pointless. The only enemies you will ever want to poise break are the ones with shields, otherwise you'll probably never engage with the mechanic. My final gripe with the game is that a lot of the accessories and items just don't feel very interesting to engage with. My eyes always glaze over when some piece of equipment gives me "+5%" to something, because numbers like that feel small enough as to not really make a difference to my experience. I'm certain they do, but not enough for me to care. Stuff like that feels so token, like "Hey, video games like this require gear with bonuses" so they tossed them in. I would rather have gear that makes noticable differences like "Recharge bullets twice as fast, but take twice as much damage" or "Melee staggers enemies, but you are no longer invicible during a dodge." I dunno, I'm sure my examples aren't perfect, but there are so many more interesting options besides adding 5% more damage to an attack that is doing 10 damage...I know I said a lot more bad than good, but I would still say this game has been worth playing for me. But I'm a sucker for old-school metroidvania games and perhaps you are too. Maybe just wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Solid game with great art and music, but fails in a number of ways. Very linear world design, plot is bloated and breaks the pace, 0 challenge to be found, short playtime, no replay value, and an unsatisfying ending. Still, combat is fun, movement is smooth and satisfying, and areas are designed well. I don't regret the purchase or beating it 100%, but I expected more after it was in production for so long. 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game and the pixel art style. It's short but sweet and I would recommend to others. Gestalt: Steam and Cinder was the first game I ever wishlisted/reviewed on steam and seeing it release after all these years is awesome and I can't wait for more from the studio and publisher. The dev team is small, 3-4 people, the feats they accomplished are impressive. Thanks for reading my review.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I was very excited to play since the demo. Overall, it's a solid metroidvania. The pixel art is very pretty and the mechanics are smooth and easy to learn. It is a pretty short game and it took about 10 hours to beat. It's not that difficult so it was fun playing through it.My only complaints is that tracking missions doesn't do anything. It won't give you an indicator on the map on where to go. And some side quests are pretty vague in telling you what needs to be done. Late game I did a lot of back tracking to finish side stuff and does get tedious because all enemies will respawn once you leave and reenter rooms.The ending felt kind of underwhelming.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game does as much right as it does wrong.It is short and not particularly challenging, not the best level or combat design, and probably costs more than it's worth, but I still liked it. Gestalt has a neat story, fantastic artwork, and loads of charm. It may be a hard sell, all in all, but I wouldn't feel right not recommending this game when I loved my short time with it. Didn't struggle getting every achievement in a single playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Can't wait for the DLC's or the sequel. I'd say:++ The story and its pacing are great++ the art is fantastic++ the skill tree is cool++ the control is precise and you never want to break your screen in angerThings that could be better: maybe a little bit more difficultyMore intelligent enemies or just more enemy concentrationLove it and will get the next one :)
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Only made it through the first boss, but wanted to put a review on. Really enjoying the game and think people who like Metroidvania style games should check it out. I do agree with some of the other reviews that I'd like an easier way to animation cancel out of attacks for dodging, but perhaps I just need to stop spamming keys so much? Hard to say. Graphics are beautiful, sound is great, movement feels really clean (outside of grabbing onto ledges, but that's minor). Definitely recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

I've updated drivers, made sure the game itself is up to date but every time I try loading a save, the screen goes black and a silly pic of the Protagonist shows for a second. _childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game, the only big issue I had was that the enemies act too fast and Aletheia has to many things that slow her actions. There are several bosses or enemies that don't telegraph some action (first instance for me was the Fox slide) and the only reactions are on a timer.Apart from that the areas are much more difficult that the bosses in themAll in all I liked it, found the world interesting and will buy the next part.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Plays beautifully, music is great, art is great, and they even left themselves an open door for sequels. A short but lovely metroidvania, excited to see more of this world.My only complaint is sometimes I felt a bit lost in the story, but overall enjoyed it.Some of the later boss fights were much easier with upgrades/good accessories, but can always unequip them or remove my upgrades if I wanted a challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvania with a strong story and narrative components, kind of like Iconoclasts or Cave Story. Strong points: Good story and characters. Superb animation, pixel art, and melee combat.Weak points: Short (8-15hrs), exploration and progression are quite linear, abrupt and dissapointing ending.All things considered: Great game, even if there is nothing groundbreaking about it. Doesn't overstay its welcome and, if anything, leaves you waiting for more.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the art style, characters, world, lore, and music are all satisfying. The combat is nice because it's both melee and ranged attacks using your gun and its abilities. The music in some stages is sick, the levels vary and keep you eager to get to the next place while untangling the story and discovering what is all this noise about. The animations, and how the world is built around Steam, bullets, and mechanical stuff were cool.The game overall is enjoyable, however, it is rather short for the price they are asking for. The game starts off with drawings depicting past events and introducing the lore, we keep hearing and talking about the lore, the past events, the gate, and the abyss but it all goes nowhere. Spoilers ahead: The game just... ends at the end, nothing happens and we understand nothing much.Something is missing that I can't quite pinpoint... it's entertaining and the characters are cool but the game overall lacks depth, meaning, an emotion, something you can latch onto to feel something.All the great MetroidVanias I played had not only fantastic levels, shortcuts, and gameplay but also depth, meaning, an emotion, something I latched onto and felt. However, this isn't the case here.The game is super easy, platforming is easy and straightforward except for a very brief section in the game. The bosses are a joke in terms of difficulty. Side quests are bland fetch Z or kill X of Y. You meet some NPCs, and at first I thought wow, Soulslike NPCs quests but nope, they are just one-liner NPCs that do nothing, wasted potential big time. And in fairness, there are a few important NPCs, that have 'quests' that are self-fulfilling.Not the best, not the worst, there are many much better MetroidVanias out there. However, none of them have a gun-blazing Redhead, for that I guess it's worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, I dunno what to say. I enjoyed this game a lot. Beautiful pixel art and really good music. Combat felt good to me being a SOTN fan. What other people say is true; A bit on the easy side. The last few bosses were dead by the time I even looked up at their health bars lol. A bit underwhelming but it didn't bother me a whole lot. Lots of reading but I just button mashed through it all and it didn't ruin the experience for me. Game is on the short side. Some people prefer games to not overstay their welcome. But I'm the kind of metroidvania player that loves massive maps like Afterimage. Overall I enjoyed Gestalt a bit more than some recent-ish MVs - 9 years of shadows, Mobius machine, momodora moonlit farewell
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: It's good overall though the combat was not well thought out, and I'm currently taking a break due to the area I'm in being annoying AF.  Having no knock back or stun mechanic really hurt it.  The stun mechanic it does have only works against some enemies and bosses.  It should have been a ranged attack on a timed recharge (with multiple charges) that stuns when countering.  Would solve the attack spam from normal enemies, and made the whole thing more fluid.  A games combat system is made of 2 parts working together.  The players capabilities, and the enemies.  In this case we have a miss match of complicated player mechanics and simple enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: The story , to me at least, seems nonsensical and the pacing seems weird. The combat feels okay but if enemies scale to your level then leveling up doesn't matter at all. If they don't then leveling up doesn't give you much extra power if any. The skill tree is kinda cool though, but again, somewhat useless. The graphics and music are pretty good though.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent metroidvania style game that doesn't try to drag itself longer then it needs to, even with 100% and backtracking it never felt like it wasn't flowing well, combat and platforming all feel great and the music is top notch. That being said if you do try to complete everything the last 25% of the game give or take feels very easy as far as combat goes which is the only real negative I have to say about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game. Some people might have problems with how rushed the ending is but I loved to 100% it. The story was good and I hope there is a sequel game to continue the storyline. As far as gameplay elements go it flows really well. It might as well be the game's greatest strength. You don't need to press too many buttons to do the cool moves but you need to know how to react. And depending on what gear style you choose, it is possible to make the game easier or harder.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good game. Downright gorgeous amazing pixel art, the character art and the background/set pieces of the world are breathtakingly stunning. The soundtrack is fantastic, perfectly fits the steampunk aesthetic. The combat is fun even if some enemies are recycled just with more health/damage. The items feel like it gives you some incentive to try out different styles, gun vs blade focused. You can pet dogs as well! My biggest gripe with the game is the story, there's a heavy lore dump near the beginning the and ending...legitimately feels like it was half baked with a poor last second twist that makes it seem like there's a secret true ending, but as far as I can tell there's...nothing. It just ends on a very flat note.  I feel like the game could have been another 5 hours longer to give a more satisfying ending. Still worth the money and time spent to play, I hope there's additional story content to help wrap up a lot of the confusing ending beats.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Solid Metroidvania.The learning curve is well build with easy to grasp skills and abilities.I never felt overwhelmed by the Map, Terrain, Enemies or Bosses. This can be either positve or negative, because it also means, i never really was challenged throughout my whole run. It has some moments of "near" frustration but never so strong that i would ragequit or anything similar.I wouldn't call it per se "easy" but it certainly isn't "hard" either.I did take my time with everything and did 100% it. It took me about 20h.If you don't really care about achievments or getting all Items you definetly can finish the game a whole lot faster.The story is interesting und unravels itself in time. My problem with this kind of approach is that you get "Information Dumped" from early on. It didn't really help, in my opinion. that the Font form the dialogue looks like "Ass". But that is a minor gripe i have.I've waited for this game since it's announcement and thus really wanted to complete it.It's solid.It won't challenge you.It has a cool world.Controls are good.Story feels cramped but gets better over time.Artstyle is nice. (except that Font choice)Still a few functions that could be better and or changed.Has a good length.Nice music, but repetetive, but nice.Unfortunately doesn't feel finished.I see a lot of potential and hope they come up with DLC or a Continuation. Story has to go on ;-)Thanks
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! - Fantastic platforming, great combat. - Challenge is about right. - Art style is visually pleasing and diverse. A few gripes. - While the story is good, it's way too verbose for reading. If this characters were well voice acted, it might had added some drama, but the dialogue is too long for the format that it's in. But maybe that's just my preference.-The maps is bare bones. At the very least the general area needs to be labeled. Perhaps some art to fill it in.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Highly reccomend, excellent narrative and writing, great pixel graphics and gameplay that was just as fun at the end of the game as it was at the beginning.Movement and combat remind me greatly of megaman x/zero which i love. Map layouts felt good, none felt like they dragged on to long and most maps had ways of opening new paths making getting around quick. I liked the environmental graphics, they gave each zone a unique and appropriate feel with only very few spots leaving me questioning if it was background art or a platform.  Background music for gameplay hit the right spot so that it was never distracting or boring. Even places I got stuck in for a while the music never got annoying.General Difficulty: During the game you unlock mandatory upgrades to your character allowing for greater variety in combat and movement, like most metroidvanias. Direct character power is handled through the upgrade system and equipped accessories which are optional. This allows the player to customize their combat difficulty level based on how much they invest into upgrades and getting accessories. In addition there is a special accessory that by design overpowers you character.Main Story Difficulty: If you keep up with upgrades and equipment during the game the difficulty should remain easy to medium, on the easier side if you use consumables. Not upgrading and/or using no or weaker equipment can easily raise it to hard.Side events difficulty: Mostly like main story, but a number of side objectives are behind tricky movement sections very reminiscent of megaman x/zero. I enjoyed these sections personally.

_childDocuments_.review: this is a great little metroid vania. The story and world building are both good but it's definitely too much talking for a metroid vania and that is probably my only major criticism.The platforming is really good but doesn't really get into it's stride until the final third of the game, the combat is fun but only really shines in the boss fights. I also appreciate the aesthetic of these first few environments. I look forward to spending more time in this game and getting deeper in to the mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun to play. Its a pretty standard metroidvania approach, with the integration of RPG style leveling along with your usual equipment powerups. There is room for customization along the way, although by the time youve maxed your levels out, youve pretty much opened the entire skill tree. The game is great for newcomers to the genre and does an excellent job of explaining out game mechanics while offering decent skill based challenges that pushes the use of those mechanics to their limits. The story is very well put together, with interesting characters i wanted to learn more about. If there was one thing that really bummed me out over all is that i wanted more. I was hoping that 10 hours in to playing i would unlock a much bigger world, final fantasy style, and really begin to dig into things after having secured the core gameplay skills. This game has the kind of story that you want to see unfold on a massive, epic scale, And i would have loved to see the map and abilities scale accordingly. The game hints to a possible sequel, so maybe with a positive reception the devs might be willing to go big. Ill definitely cross my fingers.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Really astounding art style.- Fitting soundtrack.- Very responsive combat/movement system.- Good level design.- Nice ability gimmicks (Double-jump is done by shooting blank revolver shot below character, lol)- Corgi dogs.Cons:- SHORT. Very short - you can finish the game in 4-6 hours if you're not aiming 100% completion.- Too few enemy variants, combat may become repetitive, especially in the beginning.- Map - its just weird.- Dialogues - there are just tad bit too many of them. Neutral:- Bosses are somewhat easy if you're a skilled metroidvania player, but they feel just right for casual gamer.- Plot is very basic and we don't get enough lore even with all those dialogues.- Fast travel points locations are not ideal - you have to run a lot even after activating them.Solid metroidvania, would definitely recommend for its price.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really enjoyed playing this game. I had been waiting for it for about 3-4 years and the wait was mostly worth it. Te gameplay was great and had some very satisfying things about it. The story however is a different tale. The game is very story heavy which is not a bad thing. It did a decent job with its world building and had its villain and moral choice ending setup. Then in the final cutscene it ruined all of the build up and payoff it was setting up for. It is so unfortunate that the desire to setup for a sequel or dlc took precedence over a satisfying conclusion. I still would recommend this game though as it was fun in spite of its story and failed conclusion.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: If 9 Sols and Hollow Knight are fancy french meals with complex interesting flavors, Gestalt: Steam and Cinder is a burger and fries at your favorite bar and grill. It's familiar, easy to enjoy, and satisfying in a completely different way. The appreciation the dev team had for Igavanias is obvious. The game feels like a tribute to SotN in numerous ways including the fantastic pixel art and banger soundtrack. The story is interesting and enjoyable if not somewhat predictable. The combat and platforming are little to no challenge, but both feel clean. The level-up system and accessories quickly eliminate any difficulty from the enemies. A certain end-game item intentionally trivializes the last area which feels like a tribute to late game SotN items like the Crissaegrim. At ~8 hours for 100% it's definitely worth a romp.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt is a metroidvania with a great art style that uses a mixture of colours to bring their world to life through fluid animations and detailed background and characters. The combat is a bit fast with a dodge useable every 2 or so seconds and a skill tree to unlock new moves and more energy for heavy/gun attacks, unfortunately with the speed of some enemies that dodge is less useful than simply jumping and many of the new sword moves go unused either do to being weaker/slower than your combo or leaving you vulnerable to attack. Most enemies can be stunned by draining their Break Gauge allowing you to deal higher damage but unless the enemy has a shield or is a boss then they'll die before that. The story is where this game really needed the polish. Sidequests are your basic kill or collect x quests which aren't too bad but the main story loves to rear its head between areas as it cuts to black to give you a text wall of exposition. There is a lot dialogue in this game that unfortunately amounts to either lore dumps or trailer speak. As for the characters they are pretty cardboard cutouts with no real personality. Who's Aletheia? well shes a tough mercenary, thats about it. Who's Marlowe? Hes a conspiracy theorist who is onto something. Who's Renard? gruff soldier man. The characters are nothing more than whatever they initially present themselves as.All in all I think the game is still worth a play, especially if you catch it on sale, with a solid 5hr main story for a solid 7/10 game
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A solid traditional metroidvania that suffers from overwrought writing, weird pacing, and a horribly abrupt, anticlimactic ending. This game was in development for a VERY long time, so it's surprising just how...unfinished it feels.Most of this review will be complaints, but I still recommend this game overall.Don't misunderstand. It's a GOOD game. Of course, it obviously LOOKS GREAT! The pixel art is easily the best thing about it. In terms of gameplay, the mechanics are solid, the combat and platforming are fun, and the world is fun to explore. Admittedly, a lot of it is very "by the numbers" and won't really surprise you. Progression is fairly linear, upgrades are basic (double jump, wall jump, air dash, etc.), exploration mostly involves going down a short side path with a collectible at the end then going back to the critical path. It's familiar, but in a sort of comfy way. The main character feels great to control, the level design is often quite good, and the combat is crunchy and mostly satisfying.I say MOSTLY because combat is honestly a mixed bag. It feels good, but some of its features are quite awkward. It has the SUGGESTION of a complex combo system with the light and heavy attacks, but you can't combo lights into heavies. Heavy attacks use up the same resource that your gun uses, so you have to choose between using strong melee attacks or similarly strong ranged attacks. Half of the unlockable moves feel unnecessary because of the game's overall low difficulty. Enemies have "break" meters that stun the enemy if you use moves that have high break damage, but you usually end up killing most enemies before you break them, making it a very situational tactic. Enemies don't get put into hitstun when you attack them, so long combos and particularly laggy moves (such as the dodge attacks, which can't cancel into anything) end up feeling bad cause they leave you open for punishment. I only EVER used the dodge attacks and heavy attacks when I was sure the enemy would die from them because of this. But these issues, honestly, are mostly nitpicks. I still had fun with the combat after I adjusted to what moves were good and when best to use them...except when I fought the bosses. They are all...unbelievably easy. Especially near the end, when you get certain VERY overpowered upgrades that trivialize the endgame. I would literally spam one specific heavy attack to break the boss, leaving them stunned for a few seconds, then doing the flaming spin attack that just MELTS their health while they sit there doing nothing. Other than that, the gameplay was very fun. I didn't dislike actually playing the game at all (besides the bosses).The big problem is that the game often doesn't allow you to play it. I've played plenty of games with a lot of dialogue before, even metroidvanias, but this one was hard to sit through. The writing is far to obsessed with the game's lore for its own good. The vast majority of dialogue is riddled with overwrought exposition, and it ends up feeling like you're stuck sitting through a world history lecture. The names of people, places, and events of the distant past are thrown around incredibly often, as if the game expects the player to already be familiar with them. It's pretty difficult to keep track of, partly because of its abundance and partly because the game does very little to make you care about any of it. It's very much a "tell instead of show" kind of thing. Very little of it has any sort of significance to the main character's immediate situation that I just can't be bothered to care. It tries to tie all of the lore up into a big conspiratorial mystery by the end, but it could have achieved the same overall effect with a word count about HALF as long. And the ENDING? (Minor spoilers) It's honestly terrible, sorry. Not only is it HORRIBLY abrupt, it leaves you questioning whether the characters' actions were correct, or whether they inadvertently doomed all of humanity because "destiny told them to." The game even hints that you have to make an important decision near the end, as if you get to choose what ending to get, only for the main character to get knocked unconscious and SOMEONE ELSE swoops in and makes the decision for you??? AND it alludes to a sequel that is probably never gonna happen? Yeah, it leaves a bad final impression.It's funny that the game spends so much time telling you about the world, and the actual world you're able to explore is not even a fraction of what is promised. Without going into too many spoilers, the standout omission has to be the Akhaians. The game sets up these guys as the big bads, the main antagonistic force that seek to open a portal to the abyss and unleash daemons upon the world (this is explained in the opening cutscene). And yet, you NEVER fight a single Akhaian or daemon. Like, I wasn't expecting having to traverse the abyss or anything, but I at least expected a few Akhaian enemies infiltrating the city (you know, since there's a war and everything). But no, you get human enemies, dogs, robots, even PLANTS, but no Akhaians. This might seem like a nitpick, but I seriously can't overstate how much the game makes these guys out to be the antagonists and then barely every utilizes or shows them. It's emblematic of how the game in general feels unfinished, despite its loooong development time. The suggestion of a larger world outside of the one you can play in makes the whole game feel like buildup with no payoff, like it's the first act in a longer story that you don't get to see cause the game ends before it gets good....so yeah. The game has problems. But I can't say I didn't enjoy playing it. It's just another game that has way more potential than it was able to live up to. If you'd like some suggestions for games with a similar feel but much better execution (metroidvanias with good movement, combat, and exhaustive world building), I'd recommend Afterimage, Nine Sols and Phoenotopia Awakening.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: A character driven Metroidvania that consistently drip feeds you lore about its world from start to finish. The ending left me wanting, but I played 9-hours straight from morning till evening to get there. If character dialogue is your jam, Gestalt has it in abundance. Early dialogue is packed with in-world key terms you have to gradually learn, and some of them never quite fully click as well as they should. Characters are nuanced, varied, and well developed.Animations are excellent all around. Action is flashy, without overloading your screen. Everything is easy to track, with the exception of a couple enemies that can attack you from off-screen. Movement is snappy, but with just enough weight to make you think before you commit to an attack.My top highlight was the sidearm revolver. Where most games turn guns into fast projectiles with miniscule damage, Gestalt's revolver hits hard. Ammunition is limited, but you never feel reluctant to spend it. Melee attacks recharge your sidearm's ammunition, creating a true swashbuckling combat loop:Carefully dive in for melee attacks, then relish every chance this creates to fire off a shot or three.The dual weapon system feels organic, encouraging you to constantly use both weapons in a rhythm. Combat is fast, but remains thoughtful due to healthy animation lock on sword combos. I admit that I got punished a lot for thinking I should be able to dodge twice in succession.All in all, Gestalt is a fantastic game. At its worst moments, it's a bit heavy in dialogue that's dense with key terms. At its best, it's a swashbuckling adventure in a lovingly crafted steampunk world built with excellent art & animation and an abundance of characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Visually beautiful game with a pixel art style and nice music. Gameplay mechanics are polished although the combat might be a bit on the easier side. The story is kinda cliche and seems like a lot of information is dumped in text in a very short game, but it's still interesting enough to drive the plot. Wish it had a bit more replayability, hopefully it will get a dlc or second installement to progress the story, as the end leaves the plot open.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun if not a bit underwhelming. In combat enemies don't stunlock which makes sword combo upgrades worthless, and the lack of i-frames when hit can lead to some frustrating stunlocks, but nothing that will outright kill you. One thing that did really bother me is the stamina bar, which hard caps you to a single dodge every second or so and can't be upgraded/increased, and makes some bosses feel a bit slow. Movement is solid and feels really good, but the stages are too linear to be called a metroidvania, and I think the game could've worked better as just a linear platformer. The visuals are amazing, music is great and memorable, and the characters are serviceable, with a handful that show some depth but never get truly explored. The ending sucks tho, it feels like they ran out of time, and the game can be 100%ed in around 8 hours. Small nitpick, but PLEASE add an enemy log, I'm missing maybe one or two for the all enemies achievement and not knowing which is driving me insane.Overall, a solid 8/10, the standard price feels very reasonable.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable game. It's a solid Metroidvania. Gorgeous pixel art, the story was fairly straight forward but well written, responsive combat, fun platforming sections, and 25 pettable corgis. I do think some of the bosses could do with a bit more health as of the time writing this. Especially in the latter half of the game, you're so strong that they tend to go down rather quickly. However, that sort of power trip fantasy does fit in with the narrative.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I got this game on a whim cause it seemed like a pixel art metroidvania, which I like, and...I really, really enjoyed it! Now, I have to admit it's not on the level of Blasphemous or Blasphemous II, the music is okay and the spritework, while very good, isn't sublime as it was in Blasphemous (or Symphony of the Night). However, everything *is* very good. The sprites, the gameplay (which is nice, smooth, and fast-paced, incorporating guns and swordplay), and even the dialogue and story are a cut above what you'd expect from a bog-standard Metroidvania. My only critique is that its very short, I've barely started but people tell me I've already gotten through a hefty chunk of the game. Ah, well, a little pricey for 17.99 but it has enough SOVL I'm willing to pay.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Short, beautiful game.  Good music that nicely compliments the action happening on screen.  My only real criticism is that the story feels like the prologue for a more ambitious story to be told later, which left me feeling a little unfulfilled.  The world and characters are well written enough to support a much larger story and I hope the devs get the chance to tell that story.  Playtime was around 9 hours to get almost everything (I missed a shop somewhere and can't be bothered to go back and find it) and I enjoyed every minute of it.  Balance-wise, there's 1 side-quest reward that provides a wild amount of power, which largely trivializes the last 3 bosses, but story-wise this doesn't feel too wrong.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the setting and the art design is incredible! I was always excited to see what new areas I'd come across. Exploration was fun however I would have liked the map to have a bit more information on it. I spent a lot of time running around aimlessly because I couldn't tell where the map was taking me. Also didn't realize I could place pins on the map until the last area.... :)Combat was okay for the most part. I felt that thought they were strong, a lot of the abilities weren't totally useful, so I resorted to just basic slashing and shooting for most of the game. That might just be on me though. The game is also not very challenging, but that's not a bad thing. It helped me sort of relax and get into the zone while playing. My biggest complaint is the not the story itself but how it was told to the player. The dialogue seemed endless. I skipped through a lot of it because I just didn't want to read that much text. I think splitting up the story into more digestible chunks with shorter cutscenes and maybe journal entries or something is the way to go. That way players can choose when to engage deeper into the story.Last thing, the character images in the cutscenes are HUGE. Two people talk at a time and they each take up a more than a third of the screen. Plus the dialogue box at the bottom. That tied to the long cutscenes makes me feel claustrophobic and I can't escape it fast enough. Also, some character's heads are slightly cut off by the top of the screen. Shrink them down to  like half the size, maybe a little smaller. The details in the full body images are great but I can't appreciate them when they feel so close to my face.Overall, I like the game a lot! It's a chill time and I'm definitely excited to see more from the world of Gestalt and Metamorphosis Games!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: StoryThe narrative is your basic chosen one story. You're special and the only hope left for a society falling apart. It's okay, the characters are well-written and has enough twist to keep things interesting. The problem is that the game relies on information dumps to keep the story going which can break the pacing. And the ending is incredibly underwhelming with the worse sequel baiting since Halo 2. Unless this game sells chances are it'll be left unfinishedGameplayThe gameplay focuses on light Metroidvania elements combined with 2D action. There's some exploration and optional upgrades but you're given enough tools to complete the game easily using the baseline abilities. The player is granted some customization but it's basic like reduced damage, increased damage, or special traits like recovering energy or gaining more scrap. You're given a sizeable selection of abilities ranging from double jump, dashing, heavy attacks, and even special additions that add to your basic abilities in the way of the skill tree. With skill points granted by earning levels up to 50, finding save points, and locating telsa coils. The game attempts to add more content in the way of a bounty board which mainly focuses on just killing enemies and character missions consisting of gathering key items. The other main side mission is finding lost corgis.There's a fast travel system but it's limited to exact locations and for the most part the player is funneled from one open-area to the next. There's a great selection of enemies and boss fights but the final boss is very disappointing. As for the combat the best comparison I can make is Super Castlevania 4 but with a gun for ranged attacks. Don't expect anything complicated but for what it does the developers did a good job. Just really wish they made more effort on the final boss.PresentationThe biggest sell is definitely the visual and audio department. There's no voice acting but the musical score is exceptional and the graphics are amazing. The animation is absolutely stellar, even rivals AAA quality. With dynamic backgrounds, lush character models, and beautiful use of colors. The presentation alone is a 10/10.ConclusionGestalt is an okay game. The visual design is definitely striking but the gameplay and exploration elements are average at best. I wonder if the game would've been better off as a linear title rather than having open areas. Perhaps the pacing would've been better and more focused could've been placed on making the combat a bit more dynamic. Like adding a parrying system or combo mechanics. I did enjoy my time with the title and despite its shortcomings had fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Story heavy Metroidvania game which is more on the easy side.It looks gorgeous and the music is top-notch.Combat is good but nothing special. It's quite fun to collect everything and get all the achivements without any tedious partsI would love to see a sequelThe music during the last bossfight is exellent!!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Waited for this game since 2012 and it was totally worth it.First of all, i really enjoed the story driven approach to the game. It's a contrast to some other games in the genre that i've played. And the story itself is very interesting so far, so i play not only to discover more of the places but also to find out what would happen next.Steampunk setting for metroidvnia is unique for me.The pixel art is great. Real pleasure to watch the characters and places. Reminds me of a Monkey Island.The character development system through a node grid is great. Reminds me of Final Fantasy X. And i liked the battle system: the character actions and moves, additional stun bar to enemies health, accessories system, everything works together quite well.The game is very, very enjoyable. Wish high sales for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun and short metroidvania that doesn't break any new grounds but it makes good of what it have.It controls good, cool powers and is just fun.I like the lore and the characters and I would definitely play other games in the same universe, and the artwork is GREAT! BUT, like i said, it doesn't break any new grounds. It feels like a good game for people who wants to go into this genre.I completed and collected all achievements for this game in about 8-9 hours and I died twice.The rewards for collecting and searching for secrets isn't really that good EXCEPT for collecting all the corgis in the game, that made the last bosses super easy for me. If you find this on sale or if you just want some short, kinda easy but fun metroidvania-game, buy this!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty decent metroidvania.  Not going to win game of the year, but still definitely worth experiencing.  It's pretty easy to 100%, but actually, I kind of coasted through the whole game.  I was able to bet the game without ever having died.  So if you're looking for a challenge, you aren't going to find it here.  But if you are looking for a fairly casual experience, then you good.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Had a lot of fun with this game. While there wasn't anything really "unique" about it, it is still a very well done Metroidvania. The pixel-art and animation are fantastic, combat while simple was still really fun, you get enough abilities and a ranged wep to give it some variety and giving you different ways to deal with enemies/bosses. Music and sound design was well done as well, nothing exceptional but it fit the whole game very well.Doesn't really feel like a difficult game, I would say around the halfway part is the more challenging part of it all, more specifically one boss in particular; but once you get used to the combat and enemy behaviour it is not too challenging to get through the game without dying.  Pacing feels very quick and while my steam play time is longer, a 100% run took me 7 hours of "active" play time.  I thought the story was pretty good, nothing ground-breaking but still very intriguing and it had both a cliffhanger and enough unanswered question to build upon the world more in a future game if they ever do it, or even to just speculate on your own about the game world. Would give it an 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Well-made, and doesn't overstay it's welcome. Graphics are very well done, with great detail and animation. Music is really fantastic, enough that I would occasionally stop just to focus on it. Controls are tight and responsive.Difficulty wise, it was sometimes hard when entering new areas until I could level up and learn enemy timings and patterns. Not a cakewalk, but not frustratingly challenging either.Story is interesting, but can be overly verbose at times. Voice acting would have helped, i believe.The map itself is not that great, I kept wishing it had more details to it. Eventual unlocks help, but its just barely functional, probably the most annoying bit (but not that bad, I just would've liked it to be better).All in all, it's a fun romp, I'm about done at around 12 hours, taking my time, trying to find everything. Worth a play if you're into metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Metroidvanias are some of my favorite games of all time and I've played quite a few. This has got to be one of the ones that is at the top of my list. Not only for it's visually stunning looks but also for the fact that the combat is so much fun and you actually get a feeling of being overpowered by the end of the game. So there is a true power fantasy that goes along with the story very well. The backtracking isn't terrible with the fast travel system that they have. The map is very nice and open, but the visual style. The map itself is not one that I am fond of and don't really care for, but overall it wasn't too much of a drawback. Honestly, I started this game up on my steam deck and didn't stop playing it until I beat it and I recommend it very very much for anybody who likes Metroidvanias and wants to play one that looks great and feels great to play as well. So pick this up. Full price on sale. Whatever for a smooth fun flashy metroidvania that handles great and will give you hours of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Annoyed to see this gem sitting at Mostly Positive(as of this writing), especially when seeing many of the reasons for not recommending this game.  I'm about 80% through this game and I can wholeheartedly recommend this wonderful addition to the metroidvania genre!Graphics: as I think everyone has pointed out, this game is gorgeous. You can tell a lot of effort and love went into creating every nook and cranny of this world.  Additionally everything from the main character, to a boiling over pot of molten metal, to the gears on the title screen are all animated superbly. For anyone who is a fan of pixel art, this is a feast for the eyes.Sound: this goes hand in hand with the animation. Sound design is top notch. The world is very steampunk and all of the gears clicking, doors grinding open, swords whipping through the air, all have a very believable and satisfying sound to them.  Background music is also wonderful and feels at home  on this SNES style game.Story:The story is slightly generic, but the individual characters are well done and really add to the world building done in the game. The cut scenes and dialogue may not be for everyone but I enjoyed them and they really helped move the story along as well as show other things that were happening while you were on your quest.Gameplay:Mainly melee combat with a pistol that you can use sporadically.  There is a great level up system that gives you a bit of freedom in what skills you unlock and what stats you upgrade.  Utilizing the shock bullets, dodge mechanics and heavy attack system allies for a decent variety in how you attack enemies.The biggest criticisms I've seen revolve around the combat in the game.  I think the criticism is largely unfounded.  Yes the game is pretty easy for me (I'm 41), but this game would be absolutely perfect for a younger gamer(as a gateway game into harder combat systems).  Not  every game has to be a dark souls slugfest where I want to throw my controller because I didn't parry within the proper 5 millisecond window.  That doesn't make this a bad game by any means, and certainly doesn't make this "not recommended" worthy in the general sense. Sure I wouldn't recommend this game to someone looking for a boss challenge grind fest as that isn't what this game is.As a gorgeous 10 hour metroidvania, 10 year old me would have absolutely loved this game.... And 41 year old me enjoyed every minute of it as well!!If you are looking for a metroidvania that isn't too difficult, but still has its challenges and is a lot of fun, I highly recommend Gestalt: Steam & Cinder.Additionally, this game and it's difficulty(and it's red hair!) reminds me a lot of Flynn: Son of Crimson. I recommend them both and if you like one you'll certainly like the other! Pick them both up!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Gestalt has beautiful pixel art with fluid animations, fantastic music, and fun abilities to unlock. I found the story engaging, if a little predictable. The map is functional but not great, and the game is quite easy and relatively short. There aren't that many bosses, but the moment-to-moment experience of traversing the (gorgeous) areas and using your cool abilities is a lot of fun. I would have liked even more platforming challenges. Overall, I recommend Gestalt and would love to see more in this setting.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: One word: smooth.The game is incredibly smooth: controls, music, gameplay. One of the main aspect of a metrovania is the pleasure of exploring the world offered by the designers. Not only the game is beatiful but it's so pleasant to explore it too.I've finished it yesterday but I'm still exploring to have the 100% completude. Althought the end is a kind of abrupt to say the least, Gestalt is a very solid, beautiful metroidvania with an amazing score.If you played the demo and enjoyed it, go for it you won't be disappointed and if you haven't, try it. It really deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I very nearly made this a negative review. I have incredibly mixed feelings about this game. However, I feel it does enough well that it warrants being positive instead of negative, however I still don't wholeheartedly recommend it.The main reason this review was nearly negative is because it throws one of its biggest strong suits, its story out the window at the end. It's incredibly anti climatic, and just makes the player go "What?! are you serious?" The game its self has some key issues. It's very light on the metroidvania part of the game, with only a small amount of back tracking and exploration. It feels more like a 2D action game with some light metroidvania mechanics thrown in. But I never really got that sense of exploration and delving into things. The combat is iffy. It's good in theory but it winds up feeling very rough around the edged and unrefined.When it works, it works well, but when it doesn't work, it can feel very un-intuitive and clunky.However the art and soundtrack are absolutely superb. The presentation is amazing and probably the biggest strong suit critically speaking.It's quite apparent that this game feels... not unfinished, but like it was quickly wrapped up. So it winds up feeling very condensed and rushed. But even with that, it felt like the story was doing a good job of bringing things to a close, with some little loose ends that make you keep wondering about the world in a good way. But then for no reason the story does a complete arse pull on the player that will have you dumbfounded and going "HUH". With the gameplay feeling a bit clunky, the story became the reason I wanted to see this game through, and then the ending just made it feel like it was all for not, and left me incredibly disappointing.The ending does seem to hint at the potential for a sequel. And I suppose that is part of what pushed me to make this review positive. If Metamorphosis Games are able to refine this experience and give the story the space to breath that it needs, then it has the potential to be a fantastic game.As it is, if you're in the mood to play a 2D action game with gorgeous art and music, and a story which whilst anticlimactic, is fun to follow along and has a lot of cool elements, then Gestalt: Steam and Cinder might be worth picking up.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: This is a well made game with a few things holding it from being the best. It delivers on visuals and music, combat is nice, though a bit too easy, and story and characters are generally interesting. I found a couple of bugs and typos, but nothing major. The ending was kinda like "we will make a sequel if people like the game". The game kept me engaged to the end - many games fail hard at this.A few negatives to keep in mind:- linear quest: it's a metroidvania, but a largely linear one. There is some backtracking for collectibles after you get abilities. but no choices on where to go.- easy: by mid game I was destroying everything, bosses fell in 30-40s. Some well designed difficulty options will do wonders.- dialogue: Story is a bit heavy on dialogue. It was fine for me, but may be off-putting to you. Overall, if you are looking for a good platformer to have some fun with for 8-10 hours, look no further.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 4 hours or so into this game and loving it so far! as a fan of platformers, this game offers engaging and fast-pace combat, a level design that encourages and rewards returning to previously visited stages, beautiful artwork and, despite using many tropes we see in fantasy and cyber punk stories nowadays, an interesting story where the game does a good job making you as engaged and invested as the characters in piecing together the answer to the mysteries of this world. looking forward to finishing this game, and I'm heavily considering writing my very 1st video game review covering it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I like the game. The controls are tight like you want from a metroidvania and the upgrades are interesting. My only real complaint is the difficulty - it's very, very easy. I have two deaths, both of which were my fault. The game is easy enough that I generally don't pay much attention to my health. That's been the cause of my death.Other things worth noting - it's beautiful from start to finish. All the character models are interesting, and the steam punk aesthetic is a cool match for the world's lore.It's also a little short. My play time is only so long because I left the game on two nights in a row lol

_childDocuments_.review: Good story, in an 8 hour package. Some minor complaints with the combat, there were a few times I almost got stunlocked to death with melee enemies that don't have any kind of poise break from my own attacks. _childDocuments_.review: This was one of those games I was really looking forward to. I went ahead and 100%ed the game. Got Every Achievement at the time of writing.The sprite work in this game is incredibly detailed and gorgeous to look at. Both in terms of character design and the backgrounds themselves. Each area has a distinct theme and music track accompanying it.Combat is relatively simple to get to grips with, and there is some animation cancelling you can do for extra damage and movement tricks. Most of the bosses are fun and have easy to decern patterns, with only really one exception in its last phase. But the fact that I didn't really die to any of them is a good sign that they are not hard to beat. I will say that by the time I got to the last three, I steamrolled through them due to the upgrades and build I had made for myself. The controls are pretty much perfect.Level Design is also great. Not too challenging, but every area has its own gimmick and uses your core abilities to its advantage. While it looks like a Metroidvania in its map layout and overall construction, it is a more linear experience. My only "minor" gripe is that fast travel is somewhat limited to specific zones (you'll know it when you see it) and I found myself doing some movement tech to get around to certain locations. A really nice feature is that there are maps that will mark key items and collectables on your map, so if you are going to 100% it, you have that.Don't be intimidated by the upgrade tree, your core abilities are unlocked throughout the main story, and you can get upgrade orbs from leveling up (the max being 50), completing bounties, side quests, and general exploration. By the time I got to the end of the game, I had an excess amount of skill points. Not to mention there is an item you can purchase to re-spec your tree if you want to do that.Speaking of items, I didn't really find myself really using them outside of a few bosses and a couple of areas. Stocking up on healing flasks is really the only thing you need to do in my opinion. Maybe the blue vials that restore energy, and some antidotes. All of these are easy to come by. The game also provides enough upgrade materials to improve your healing flasks to its max capacity.The story itself is pretty good. Nothing too complex, and there is a good mystery element to it and some political intrigue, mostly told through other characters in the background. Our main heroine is not as involved in it at first, but that does change later on.I am not entirely sure how I feel about the ending, or if there are multiple endings. But considering I got every achievement, there doesn't seem to be an alternative ending. The dialogue choices are superficial it seems and doesn't really affect the outcome of the narrative. The last bit also tried to hype us up for a big decision, but (at least in my first playthrough) didn't really deliver. It also ends on sequel-bait, or at the very least planned DLC.That being said, the game is $20usd normally, and when I think about other kinds of games I played for that price, I think it's a tad high. $15usd is probably what I would put it at in my opinion. Personally, would wait for a minor price drop if one does happen.But it is worth your time if you are interested in playing it. I had a great time with it, and I am looking forward to what these devs do in the future, and I also want to see where the story goes.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, disappointing ending. Combat can feel very responsive though frustrating at times with how forward and backward dodging and air dashing work, very odd that they were bound to different keys and not just based on the direction the player was moving, and back-dashing when not moving at all.  Platforming is generally good, though there is a section which made my eyes roll as it really felt like aping a certain Path of Pain, which I’ll be blunt, needs to stop being a thing in platformers. Split second decision making and pattern memorization is just not engaging Enemies tend to ignore hits which never really feels good, but the stamina/stagger gauge is a fun way of getting around that and keying in the player to when an enemy is vulnerable. Balancing when to shoot and move into attack is not great (and really makes me wish I could shoot while jumping), a lot of enemies don't really telegraph all that great, with many enemies just instantly attacking when you get in range, which can feel bad, and the player can get stuck in hit-stun loops if not careful. Difficulty is not really all that high, outside of when things get chaotic on screen, which happens in a few spots, such as certain bosses or late game areas. Can be very difficult to pay attention to enemy patterns when you have stuff falling from the sky or various bullets flying about. At its worst it feels like you walked into a very different sort of game. That said difficulty vanishes the moment you get the item you receive for collecting all the corgis. My big issue though is the ending, which is a blatant and rather abrupt cliffhanger, which was very disappointing and really felt insecure in a way, like the devs begging to come back, rather than giving a satisfying conclusion to this story and leaving it open for a follow-up. All that aside however, this is a fun platformer, with some irks. As always try demos if available, watch some people play it on a stream or the like, and then make an informed decision to buy or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Is a 20 dollar/euro game. If you want to enjoy a short (11 hours for 100%) but solid metroidvania, BUY THIS GAME.I have 100% the game and I think that it is a good game considering its price. That said, I have some feedback on some of the most rough parts of the experience. Since I am recommending this game, I am going to provide the positives first and then I will complain...Positives:- The setting is cool, really cool- Visually pretty- The core mechanics of the game are solid- Almost 0 bugs (I had a minor bug with the camera but I am using a keyboard so I am expecting that to be the reason. If your camera gets lock to the left, just double tap left to fix it)- The story is engaging if you give it some attention- The Skill Tree is solid, You will get enough points for everything if you explore enough.Feedback [Warning of Minor Spoiler]- The conclusion of the story is too abrupt. Maybe a second game or a DLC, but after some much foreshadowing, it doesn't feel good. I am giving a positive review because I want this game to succeed and continue the story. I think that having one of the main characters of the story speak about hiding something too much and then not deliver on the promise on the same game will enrage some people. (I suspect what is the 'true' of the plot and the abyss, but I will have to wait a long time to see if I was right and that... frustrating and probably I will forget about my current theory)- Bosses are not very good. They have a very limited moveset that you will learn in less than a minute but the real problem is that if you have some energy regen, you can dps check any boss without interacting with the mechanics. The item for getting all 'collectable' in the game makes the last boss a joke. (I just Right + Heavy the boss to oblivion). I would hide the last 'collectible' to get the special accessory after the final boss but since there is no game+, I get why that was not possible. Some of the best parts of metroidvanias, especially after hollow knights are the bosses, they are the heart of the game. For the next game, improving the bosses will do a lot.- The stamina gauge feels weird. There is a stamina bar that is used to dodge and dash, but is the only resource in the game that can't be interacted with. Since the bar allows only for a dodge or a dash, it is more of a cooldown than a resource. Feels disconnected from the rest of the game like it was added to avoid roll spamming but no accessories or any improvement on the tree interacts with it, like it was at later in development?As you can see, I have some problems with the game but I enjoyed it enough to take 30 minutes to write this and wish for the developers to have a chance for another game and make it even better.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: If you like classic Metroidvanias you will have a blast with the  game. The boss fights are rather easy, the difficulty coming from platforming and if you are a completionist from a few tough spots. Nothing too bad though, your average player can 100% the game.Some typos here and there, a few "bad" design choices in the latter half and of course the story set up for a chance of a sequel. Overall a recommendation for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea what's going on with the story in any meaningful way but it's promising. However the gameplay has been great. The gunplay and swordplay are both a lot of fun and I have found myself just dashing and jumping and enjoying the movement mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Looks great and plays great, sadly Feels somewhat lacking compared to others in the 2D platforming Genre, somewhat on the shorter side, compact? perhaps.The Main city feels big and vibrant but also a bit hollow, doesn't feel like much going on despite the size and detail it was given.Ending was a bit lacklustre, DLC or set up for the next game? feels a little incomplete storywise.I'd still recommend it though, keep you busy for a good 6-8hrs depending on what you want out of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: So far this is the softest recommend I've ever given a game, which is hugely disappointing considering how long it's been hyped.So, the pros: the game's gorgeous. The animations slap, the music slaps. The sound effects are good. It's a really good looking game, and that's something.The bad? I don't know if the story's gonna stick the landing yet (I'm only halfway!) but the amount of exposition and dialogue that doesn't do anything is off the charts. It's not good character writing, it's not good worldbuilding, and while there's a plot going on, it really lacks early hooks. A lot of stuff seems to be happening, but characters interact in ways that feel solely in service to the plot. So it's both heavy handed and not accomplishing anything.As for how it plays, it's fine, but there's a definite lack of polish and, like, secret sauce here. The combat is fine and occasionally there's an enemy (like the Assassins!) who are tuned to your movements and are legit fun to fight, but then there's enemies like the brawlers in the second area who are just totally obnoxious to fight. The map is fine but feels pretty linear; it reminds me of the map design in Castlevania: Circle of the Moon, where there's a hub and some spokes. It's fine, but not exciting, you know? Like, this feels fine, but not really worth too much of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I had a really good time with Gestalt Steam and Cinder. The movement and combat are smooth, the pixel art is beautiful, the music is great, and for a smaller map, it is fun to explore with many things to discover. Plus you get to find corgis. It is a nice, tight experience that doesn’t overstay its welcome. Though there is too much talking.

Story, environment, and exploration really share the spot light with combat in a way not seen all that much these days, where everything's either rogue-like or souls-like.This is just the kind of game I was looking for. _childDocuments_.review: What a refreshing change of pace from the other platformers I've played lately. Normally, I'd write a witty intro, connecting some metaphor to what I think of the game. But instead of all that, I want to dive straight in. The game speaks well enough for itself so it doesn't need extra flowery speech from this peanut gallery. Anywho! The gameplay? Smooth, like skating on ice so freshly Zamboni-ed it would make a Canadian blush. The controller mappings are intuitively simple allowing you, the player, to truly appreciate the aforementioned Zamboni and its driver. The learning curve scales nicely and rewards your metaphoric attempts at ice-skating (and my desire to excessively use the word Zamboni) with a balanced difficulty that never feels unfair or too souls-like. It's balanced just right.The sound and music are layered with an almost obsessive precision, creating an ambiance that complements the gameplay and rewards the player for paying attention to the sounds of the world around them (especially when it comes to the corgis and the inevitable question of how the hell did they manage to get THERE? You'll get that reference when you play the game). You can feel the music in your bones with a perfectly struck chord between tension and immersion.Now, the story: we’re in vintage cliché territory. Bad guy wants to open the gates of hell, good guy stands in firm opposition. Predictably, it's bound to happen anyway (I haven't reached the end yet), leaving our protagonist with the seemingly Sisyphean task of saving the world.But here's where it gets intriguing. Despite the plot being more familiar than your favorite worn-out hoodie, the game weaves in enough cohesion, world-building, and character development to transform that old favorite into a retro-chic piece you'd proudly display on Fifth Ave. It’s a testament to the developers’ skill that they can take a tired narrative and infuse it with life and originality.Gestalt's only flaw is that it's short. I was able to get 100% of the achievements in about 10 hours of gameplay. But enough of my bantering. I'll end on this note: Other developers, take note! THIS! This game is a shining example of how you create an excellent Metroidvania game that not only stands out but also draws you in.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the first boss and I can already tell I am gonna like this game.The approach to Metroidvania combat is more of Deadcells  (that you have to roll through attacks). It's also really interesting that the gun attacks are more of a resource management with 2 types of attack (health or shield). It appears there may be quite a lot of customisation on the skill tree and many metroidvania moves like wall bounce are unlocked really early. The only unusual part for metroid-vanias is how much you talking there is to this game, there is a lot from the start and sometimes it feels like it's too much when i just wanna blast through stuff. I hope there is a way to skip them for replayability sake.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review: I don't feel like trying to format this in any way, so straight to the cliff notes version of my 2 cents  -- It is pretty artwork, and they start you off with nice movement abilities like dodge roll, wall jump, and backstep. -- It feels similar to Iconoclasts to me. -- There are a couple bad misspellings, but nothing too bad yet. (posssed) -- The description of stun damage implies that there could be a bit more to the game than first glance.. if so, they should have had it appear early so that you can figure out how to interact with it before you get set in your ways. -- The prologue part of the game is easy, and the boss fight is annoyingly easy.. attack, duck, attack, jump, roll, attack, duck ...hopefully the later ones are better patterns. -- I disagree that the unskippable cutscenes, are worth a negative review.. they tend to be short, and it can be updated out. I also saw one that complained about how much talking there is.. it's probably just the beginning to give background, and pad the 2 hour window. (or mebbe to lend some story to the demo) -- The attack cancelling is meh, but just something to get used to -- The skill tree seems like it will be short. You level fairly quickly, and, if that is an indication of the length of the game, that could suck. -- The gun doesn't feel particularly useful outside of stun, since you can't jump/duck and shoot, but things change.All in all, it's a fun Metroidvania that will probably be 10 to 15 hours, and seems fairly easy to get into. It's fun so far, and am excited to play after waiting through years of missed release windows.... buuut, I would say that if you feel like it costs too much, it does. This won't feel like a good bang for your buck kinda game if you're comparing it to games like Hollow Knight, Afterimage, Lone Fungus, and plenty of others I'm probably forgetting, but it might be a fun way to waste a bit of time while you wait for Silksong.
_childDocuments_.name: Gestalt: Steam & Cinder

_childDocuments_.review:
Join Aletheia and a vibrant cast of characters as they race to discover the secrets of the Steam City of Canaan.

Clobber armies of Clockwork golems and hunt horrors that slither through depths once forgotten. Thwart the twisted schemes of Canaan's corrupt overseers, the nefarious Comitium. Fight for mankind's survival and reveal the dark and dangerous truths riveted into the very foundations of the Steam City.

Inspired by 16 and 32-bit classics, Gestalt: Steam & Cinder fuses tight 2D platforming and exhilarating combat with an engrossing, twist-laden narrative in a stunningly handcrafted steampunk world.

name: Radical Rabbit Stew
detailed_description: More from Pugstorm! About the Game Get your super spoons ready and whack those crazy rabbits into saucepans to free the space chefs - but think fast or the bunnies will attack! Featuring bite-sized pick-up-and-play action, fast-paced whack-a-rabbit gameplay, scintillating puzzles, super-sized boss fights, juicy pixel graphics and a sizzling soundtrack, RADICAL RABBIT STEW is a hare-raising action-arcade game perfect for new players and 16-bit retro fans alike. Scintillating Puzzles – Sink your teeth into puzzles and challenges with a range of rabbit foes, and acquire gameplay-altering spoons that keep puzzles fresh and fun. Super-Sized Boss Fights – Face off against unique bosses, each requiring different tactics to conquer. Whether it’s using enemy rabbits as ammunition or dodging incoming trains and smacking the drivers out, be prepared to think creatively to defeat each one. Seasoned Couch Multiplayer – Hop onto the couch to face off against friends in a competitive yet light-hearted multiplayer mode. Sizzling Pick-Up-And-Play Action – Enjoy a mixture of expansive, side-scrolling levels and shorter, single-screen layouts, and have the freedom to hop in for bite-sized sessions or defeat those rascally rabbits entire worlds at a time. Sumptuous Arcade Art Style – Fun and vibrant pixel graphics that simultaneously complement and pay homage to the well-loved arcade genre.
