_childDocuments_.review: This game is easily one of my favourites to come out in the year of 2020. Radical Rabbit Stew features tricky puzzle-action gameplay, where your goal is to put all the evil bunnies away in stew pots while not succumbing to their attacks or the onslaught of other stage hazards. Each world introduces new abilities, new hazards, and new ways to get rabbits to their goal! At the end of every world, and sometimes in between, there are bosses you must face, usually by flinging bombs or smaller enemies at them. These fights take full advantage of the mechanics you've learned so far, and never feel samey, but also aren't too cryptic to figure out on your own. There's also a level editor mode, where you can create your own levels! Radical Rabbit Stew is a true gem, and everyone should play it right away!
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game since the Steam showcase thing, it was the most fun game teased and now I finally have it! It's a fun arcade action game with a bit of a puzzle to it, and a wonderful 16-bit aesthetic to it, just beautiful art, sound and music. It got harder than the demo but maybe not as challenging as I would like, then again, it's only the first world. This is the kind of game you don't really see everyday and it's definitely the kind of game you should support so more indie developers make unique and fun games that stand out, not just cash grabs.I'll update this review if my opinion changes any but honestly this is a strong 8 light 9 out of 10, one of the best surprises in a year that really could use more positivity!edit: difficulty DEFINITELY ramps up, loving it so much!
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: In a dark and uncertain world, there is one ray of sunshine and that is Radical Rabbit Stew.If you want a game that is all about making you feel good and laugh and have a good time, but also think a bit, this is for you. First of all there is the obvious, the graphics are perfect and charming beyond belief. Given my personal tastes, this is probably the best pixel art I have seen in an indie game since Cave Story. It is just bright and crunchy and the animations and designs are all as good as they could be, but at the same time it feels natural and beautiful while all being on a clear grid. Never seen anything like it work so well tbh.Then you get to the gameplay- seemed simple to me at a glance, but I still bought it mostly for the art. COME TO FIND OUT this is absolutely addictive, and deceptively simple. Every action feels satisfying, and the levels usually have multiple ways of solving them as well as a collectible I HAVE to get every time. It reminds me almost of Baba Is You, except not extremely intimidating. Like if Baba is Fun and Beautiful and Hilarious instead of Think and Hard. I'm at the point where it's getting more complicated and I have to say, the pacing is just right. It feels like they are always introducing new things or using existing mechanics to the fullest extent in the level design and I am very excited to see how it plays out. And I don't even need to mention the boss fights, you just have to try for yourself. Everything about this game is 110% quality but those in particular are really something to behold. All I can say is I hope this game gets the attention it deserves! Because it deserves a hell of a lot. This is the type of game that needs to be incentivized because it actually kind of makes the world seem like a better place.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: Quick Score 4/5Starts off painfully easy, but starts to reach an enjoyable difficulty at about the half way mark when all the mechanics are fully introduced. Takes about an hour to reach this point. However even at its peak difficulty it is still very easy as far as puzzle games go. Otherwise super polished game and pretty fun overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: What a STUNNING game!  I've been disappointed in the past with pixel-art games, being either blurry or just showing on a tiny postage-stamp-sized portion of the screen, but this game looks amazing - crisp and colourful pixel graphics, filling the ENTIRE 4K TV screen I play on with buttery-smooth gameplay... It's a total joy to play.  I spent way too long just thwacking rabbits into bumpers over and over just for fun.Soundtrack is great, has an awesome arcadey vibe that reminds me of the old Nintendo and Megadrive games of the 90s, and it plays a lot like that too but at 60fps!!!Puzzles seem simple at first but then get a lot tougher.  Each area is so beautifully designed and so unique.  The game designers have a great sense of humour and that comes across, as does their love for this genre, it's just so well crafted.In 2020 when everything seems so awful this little gem cheered me right up.  For £12 it's well worth picking up - you'll buy it for the kids and play it yourself.Definitely recommended!!
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: So far it's a charming arcadeish and puzzleish game. Each world throws a few mechanics at you, gradually. It keeps the game feeling fresh and let's the player adjust and learn. This is good game design.Pixel art looks nice. The animations are snappy and fun, not to mention that they are coupled with fitting sound effects. Hitting stuff with your spoon is just satisfying.Speaking of sound, the soundtrack is just simply AMAZING. I regret not buying the ost bundle.As you can see in my review, the game is excellent for what it is. I'm very glad I've come across the demo when that came out.  This could be the best obscure release of 2020.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and surprisingly unique (yet simple) game concept. It's got nice pixel graphics and level design that reminds me of something I'd play on my Nintendo DS. You essentially just knock rabbits into stew with a variety of different spoons. Some levels are more reaction based, while others are more puzzle based. The game is also quite short, having only 3 worlds which can be cleared in about 3-4 hours. The game is super easy at first, and you can clear the first world in under 30 minutes. But it quickly picks up the difficulty in later stages. Also huge credits to whoever made the animations whenever you obtain a new spoon, that stuff is amazing.There is one BIG gripe I have with the game though; bombs and canons. Bombs will blow up on you and have no real indicator of how far the explosion will go. I've behind walls and explosions somehow reach around and still manage to kill me. Canons will launch bombs around your location, but it's possible for one bomb to land on top of another, causing it to detonate prematurely. It's incredibly hard to see this coming and makes deaths feel super cheap. Both of these made it so that world 2 was actually more difficult than world 3.Overall; a fun experience for all ages. 3 out of 5.

You know who else is a real piece of work? The evil Rabbit Queen. Seems her tasteless, moldy veggies were becoming tiresome.  Growing jealous of the legendary Space Chefs, who serve their delicacies in an infamous space diner, she orders her evil rabbit henchmen to ransack the diner and kidnap the chefs, so she can enjoy a good meal.Want to read more? _childDocuments_.review: While I havent beaten the game yet, I would say I have gotten far enough to leave a proper review with all my thoughts on this game and ratings for a few categories General Gameplay: 8/10Easy and simple to understand, the game slowly brings you into its mechanics but doesnt hold your hand. Instead it guides you to discover it yourself and simply tells you what button you need to press.The bonus collectibles can require lots of thinking at times, such as learning the timing of a tool or solving a puzzle in the correct order. However I personally think a counter telling you how many pots of soup are left would be nice, as I find myself completing the level before getting all the collectibles sometimes.The boss fights arent too hard to understand while also not being too easy. They provide a decent challenge but however are less puzzle and more "Bash it till its over" which I was a bit upset by, but something I can overlook.Map and Level Layout: 9/10I love the way the maps and levels are, only a few times were I confused on where to go and what to do. I feel as if this map is nigh perfect in my regards as its easy to picture out the path you will go before the level is over. And the shortcuts that are provided to quicken backtracking if it is needed are loved and I have used them before. The levels sometimes have a few hiccups such as too many bombs, but it doesnt happen for too many levels.Soundtrack: 9.5/10A soundtrack is one of the main factors I take in when I am playing a game. And boy is this a great soundtrack. Hell, as I write this review I am listening to the main menu theme and having a jam. The only reason I didn't give it a 10/10 was  the fact that personally some soundtracks dont hit for me. But thats rare and entirely my own opinionHumor: 8/10I found myself laughing a lot as I played this game, especially when I was in a call with friends. The sound effects really help sell some of the humor. When I first sent a rabbit between two springs I couldnt help but laugh and keep doing it. Just watching the rabbit get faster and faster as it bounced was hilarious. If you ever get this game (Which I 100% suggest), don't be afraid to just mess around and have fun. Cause its clear thats what this game is trying to do, mess around and have fun. The puzzle solving feels like a cherry on top.Cons:This game doesn't feel good on keyboard to me. You need to play this with a controller if you have one. Dualshock, Xbox, or just anything works really. I bet you could find a way to hook up a SNES controller and it could work. Just use a controller and not the keyboardSome of the puzzle difficulty  is inconsistent at times it feels. I'll be doing a fairly hard level for a while only for the next level to be super easy. It doesn't happen too often but enough for me to have a complaint about itOther than that, I 100% suggest you get this game. Im very excited to see the future of games that Pugstorm gives us and ready for more of their glorious games.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game all the way through.  It took me 6 hours, as I wanted to get all of the coins. A fun puzzler, with good music and  a great sense of humor.  Highly funny in parts, slightly absurd.  It was a lot of fun, and reminded me of a mix of Rayman, and Lemmings, for both the puzzles, and the speed.Overall, it was good fun, a great value, and I totally enjoyed it.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: This is a seriously addictive retro feel game, it's like two games rolled into one, firstly you have the wack a rabbit fun and then you've got a head scratching puzzle to figure out. The initial puzzles aren't too hard, but they get you used to the mechanics of the game and before you know it you'll be facing your first boss Rabbit. I have really enjoyed playing the game so far and do intend of playing for much longer, it's certainly a fun, funny and addictive little game which is definitely worth the money should you be considering buying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: "Radical Rabbit Stew" is a surprisingly cute, rather comedic, pixel art puzzle/action game. The atmosphere is enjoyable, with plenty of vibrant environments and nifty character animations. The difficulty curve is fairly balanced; new obstacles and abilities are introduced at a steady pace, allowing you to learn what you need and how to best use that knowledge for future levels, while also never remaining stagnant or re-using the same puzzles over and over. However, if you're a completionist looking for a challenge, you will get your desired frustration in trying to get every single collectable, or if you want the achievement for clearing every level in a row without a single death. Also, there's some multiplayer, though I honestly haven't tried it as of writing this review. If I had to make a complaint, it's that some of the most interesting character designs (like the kidnapped chefs) don't get a lot of time in the spotlight. But overall, I thought that this experience has definitely earned a chef's kiss.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully put together with lots of personality. Straightforward and entertaining gameplay that starts easy and slowly ramps up the challenge, with great artwork and animations and sound design, and a cool soundtrack on top of it. Nice variety of levels, and fun secrets that get quite tricky to find as the game progresses if you're into that. Strongly recommend you check this one out, kind of a sleeper hit right now.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to start with saying that I wouldn't have given this game a chance if it didn't have a demo. There's tons of puzzle/retro games out there so why buy this one on release? The trailer is good and the graphics are cute, but full price...eh. Then I tried out the demo and I couldn't get enough. The puzzles are fun and love to take advantage of the various skills or 'spoons' the game provides you with. Puzzle difficulty ranges from being able to do it with your eyes closed to having to pay close attention to anything remotely unusual on the map and even randomly take your chances. This does not make the puzzles any less fun but instead it makes solving them more fun and engaging, I haven't experienced (or noticed) any bugs despite going through a few playthroughs, an unimaginable feat for a release date download.The graphics are charming and they only get better and better the more you look at them. The devs fully embrace the bunny theme and are not afraid of taking it to ridiculous lengths.  If you're on the fence about this title, just give the demo a try. You've got nothing to lose.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually go for sokoban puzzle games because i'm a dork at 'em, but this one had me playing through the whole game having fun. None of the levels are brain-breakingly hard, and there's lots of graphical throwbacks to 90s DOS games and SEGA. And it's *fun*, did I mention that? Good humor, cool music, two thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: I first played the demo on one of the Steam events and I was hooked, when the game released I was compelled to get it. Radical rabbit stew is a delicious combination of bunnies and spoons with a dash of bombs, featuring great puzzles and cute rabbits that will eat you if you're not paying attention. Bunnies, bunnies, bunnies. You play as a cleaning boy, cleaning out the pot of rabbits who have taken hostage your fellow workers. You use your trusty spoon to whack bitey rabbits into pots.Excellent mechanics, working controls and hilarious atmosphere. The puzzles aren't too difficult and encourage you to challenge yourself to try better and get the achievements. The bosses will end up making you cry both with frustration and then satisfaction after you finally defeat them.Very enjoyable!The game features a retro arcade style, feels very nice and cute. Great animations and scenery. The game is set in space, you travel through either broken chunks of land or "relax" on a nice beach, or freeze in the winter wonderland. All these different sceneries work perfectly with the core game and each provide their unique twist to the gameplay.Highly recommend trying out the demo if you're unsure if this game is not typically what you enjoy. Definitely helped me decide to get and finish the entire game and it's challenges.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly charming and fun little game that I would highly recommend. I had an ad for it come up on YouTube and the thing that hooked me immediately and made me want to buy it was the music. The soundtrack is phenomenal and suits the areas of the game well. The gameplay is simple yet fun, and they do a great job of introducing each new mechanic throughout the game. I enjoyed figuring out the various puzzles to get every coin; none of them felt too frustrating or convoluted while also not always being too easy. I haven't tried the multiplayer much yet, but it seems like it can be good for some quick frantic fun with some friends.As a warning, the game is pretty short. My first run took 2-3 hours total, which included collecting all the coins. For me this isn't an issue as I had a lot of fun playing through it several times after and going for all the achievements, and I could easily see myself coming back to this game from time to time just to chill.Overall a great game if you like the retro arcade style or just hate bunnies.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: I dont think Ive ever been as quickly turned off to a game by sound effects as I was with this one.  Game itself seems fun enough, but the abundance of grating, annoying, or stock sound effects made want to be doing anything else with my time. If I return to this one itll be with the sound low, or off.
_childDocuments_.name: Radical Rabbit Stew

_childDocuments_.review: I first saw Radical Rabbit Stew while perusing Steam's upcoming releases section in the name of digging up promising games to feature for the most popular Curator I run (Noteworthy Video Games - Upcomin)--it definitely caught my attention, and I was aware that Sold Out Software had a few other games in the works as a publisher, which can be a good sign that a game like RRS is decently funded or had a strong enough alpha/beta/whichever state it was in when Sold Out picked it up to attract a respectable publisher. late last year I picked it up, and I've had a ball with it. I'll say that it's absolutely true to its name.+ phenomenal pixel art and animations, adorable character designs which are distinct from one another (making for good visual clarity)--plus strong environmental variety.+ groovy tunes from its soundtrack. worth picking up on its own.+ satisfying sound effects, adding to the outstanding audiovisual feedback this game provides.+ fun sense of humor, between the actual writing and also just the character animations for the rabbits.+ immaculate design, does a great job of leading you along and making what you need to do feel like second nature.+ the speed with which you can hop right back into a level you flunked out of makes things so much less frustrating as your next attempt is at the press of a button.+ tight controls.+ the bosses thus far have been enjoyable to face, with a decisive difference in how each operates.+ I enjoy how it's constantly adding new abilities, new enemy types, new puzzle elements in general, etc.--keeps things feeling fresh and finely crafted, as opposed to something which feels tacked together.highly recommended, this one's a lark.

_childDocuments_.review: I played through the demo, and immediately bought the game. So definitely check that out if you're on the fence. Even if all you do for now is play the demo, it's a good chunk of fun gameplay.This is a charming 16-bit inspired light puzzle game about using a chef's wooden spoon to defeat evil rabbits who kidnapped the rest of your kitchen staff. Initially, that is. Some other abilities are introduced over time, and all of them are fun to use. From an overworld map, you complete stages where the objective is to bat these furry villains, occasionally yourself, around the map and sometimes off a series of spring-loaded plungers like Sonic the Hedgehog, to destroy obstacles and ultimately land all the rabbits in stew pots to complete the level.Boss fights shake things up a bit, but the controls and gameplay for these are consistent with the other levels, and work well when you're dodging attacks and landing some hits of your own. The levels rarely feel too easy to figure out, mostly when a new mechanic is added and it's obviously the way to move forward. And so far, they never feel like they're being overly obtuse with the solutions. The player's intuition, rather than staring at the screen, will usually reveal the next move to make.No reservations whatsoever about recommending this. One of the best retro-style games I've played on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: A thoroughly enjoyable, easy puzzle game. Don't get me wrong, it did made me use some of my brain to figure them out, especially the blue coins, but other than that, I didn't resort to any guides or tutorials and etc. The pixel art is really great (I'm a sucker for those), no music track is "bad" in my eyes, and the presentation and charm this game exudes is too great to put off. The shortcoming of it though, is that it's a bit too short, clocking in at close to, maybe, one hour and a half or less if you don't care for the blue coins, and adding an additional thirty if so.I'd say, the real enjoyment of this game are the achievements. Say in, finding one secret here or there, or maybe you like going fast? There's a cheevo for that. Maybe clearing a boss with no hits? There's a cheevo for that. Of course, you also have the stage builder, but not many people play this game anyways, so you're more likely to play them yourself. After all, it gives the game a bit more of juice for the average person to dig into. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes puzzles, bunnies, or puzzles with bunnies. Plus, fairly cheap without sales!

_childDocuments_.review: An Action Puzzler with a lot of charm, Radical Rabbit Stew feels like something that would have been right at home on the Game Boy Advance or Sega Genesis. That's definitely on the short side for $16, but you can't say it overstays its welcome. Put this one on your wishlist and wait for a steep sale - those 3 hours are quite fun 3 hours!As a bonus, the game contains a multiplayer mode that's perfect for an evening on the couch that matches the frenetic energy (though not quite the puzzly heights) of my favorite multiplayer puzzler, Chu Chu Rocket. _childDocuments_.review: Radical Rabbit Stew just oozes charm. It genuinely feels like a lost game from my childhood. The wacky setting, the gorgeous and detailed pixel artwork, the great tunes and silly sound effects, the navigation through a lovingly crafted world map and the cute designs all combine to make this feel like a forgotten classic.Its gameplay is a nice mix of puzzles and action, and most of the puzzles are optional if that's not your kinda thing. It's overall easy but the difficulty scales nicely throughout the game and there's a nice challenge to be had in the final boss fight. It doesn't overstay its welcome (with almost 4 hours for my playthrough) and introduces new mechanics at a steady pace, without ever growing boring or overwhelming.Highly recommended. _childDocuments_.review: This game was fun. It has interesting puzzles, extra puzzels if you want to collect all the hidden coins, but what this game excels at is the user experience. It is very responsive, which is rare in games nowadays. Movement is exact and quick. You never get stuck and/or irritated by the controls. Another thing that is great is the sound effects and music. The music feels like it is composed on an Amiga computer, and the sound effects feels heavily inspired by the Super Nintendo era.When talking about inspiration, many game elements are heavily inspired by nintendo game mechanics, such as the boo-ghost from super mario, or the barrel cannons in donkey kong country.Game length is perfect in my opinion. I finished it in 4 hours while collecting all hidden coins. If the game was longer it risked becoming stale instead of being fun all the way through.I highly recommend this gem of a game.

_childDocuments_.review: Intergalactic gastronomers are dismayed when a team of eclectic Space Chefs is violently captured by the nefarious Rabbit Queen and her long-eared legions.  Emerging unscathed from an overturned cauldron at the scene of the crime, a diminutive blue-bodied cleaning boy embarks on a quest to retaliate against the bucktoothed brigade.  Can he rescue his cohorts and restore fine cuisine to the cosmos?To some extent, Pugstorm's  plays like a generously caffeinated spiritual successor to Irem's ; both titles are top-down action/puzzle hybrids with an emphasis on propelling enemies and objects in order to proceed through a series of extremely brief stages.  In order to complete each level, players must fling the unruly rabbits into all of the nearby stewpots through the use of various utensils.  When the bunnies make a splash into the stew, the pots promptly launch into the air like bottle rockets - a well-deserved comeuppance for the carrot-nibbling criminals.  No-stick controls and solid hit detection make it rather satisfying to send these rascals packing.  New implements are gradually introduced which add a few twists to the level designs, and there are some decent boss battles as well.  If you have an affinity for demoscene tunes, you'll certainly savour the high-octane soundtrack; it's not easy to pick a favourite selection, but special mention must be made of the snazzy cutscene music.Unfortunately,  can be completed in less than a few hours if you don't spend time hunting down the secret coins tucked away in most of the levels; more content would have been appreciated.  Thankfully, a level editor with Steam Workshop support is on hand.  The multiplayer mode is a barebones affair, but can still be fun if you have a few enterprising cooks in your kitchen.  Overall, there is much to enjoy here.I'd like to see Pugs Bunny employed as an air traffic controller, wouldn't you?

_childDocuments_.review: is a gorgeous tranquil puzzle adventure with a golf theme and some narrative. there's a quick tutorial, but no surprises about the premise: you're trying to penetrate holes with your ball.the overworld consists of , both unlocked one by one for the most part. it's not all green and foresty, there's a moonlit garden, desert at sunset, winter forest, windy beach, and so on, and , it looks great. , the goal for each star is shown on-screen, as it should be. you can continue playing after going over par, but the level will fail when you eventually putt, so , can't progress with a no-star rating. there are occasional star checks too, at certain points you have to have enough to move on. about 200, so half, is enough to finish the game., and solving those tricksy levels reveals  that unlock . no par there but have to do all the holes in one go, and some have timing elements. 36 blue things, so a bit more than half, is enough for everything. secret stuff isn't necessarily hidden, they might just be in hard-to-reach places, and those holocubes start  with the hole as reward. a nice touch is you can restart or retry them, no need to hit the cube before every attempt, unless you leave the level. there's an overall star and collectible counter, with the current location's numbers only visible on the world map. would make more sense the other way round. mouse, keyboard and controller are all supported and  with sensitivity sliders and invert toggles. by default, wasd moves the ball from level to level in the overworld (double-tap to move faster) and holding right click lets you peek not too far around your current position.  like this, can't even easily check where a non-3-star level is, let alone get to it quickly. I'd like to pan the entire unlocked area, click an available hole and start it with another click instead of rolling all the way back. at least you can change direction, no need to wait for the ball to arrive at a hole before it can be moved again, and there's fast travel between courses.while on a level, wasd or right click to move the camera around, up/down arrows to raise/lower it, space returns to the ball, you can zoom in/out with the wheel and rotate the camera by holding the left mouse button. q/e could serve the same purpose, no such keybind though, nor can you switch left/right click functionality, which would also be nice.aim by holding left click over the ball (always zooms in), pull the mouse back to set strength (fully for a power shot), then let go when you think it's best. there's a little sway, which can be countered by focusing (holding your breath) for a short time with left shift.  left ctrl reverses the aim camera, which is useful when the goal is not clearly visible. it can be set to hold or toggle. if you want to cancel the shot, gotta decrease strength and let go of left click. I wouldn't mind if right click while aiming also did this. is also a thing, you can change hole size, turn on bounce arcs, , have unlimited focus, and  among other things, with . I honestly didn't expect undo, let alone such an elaborate help system, though it's still a puzzler in golf's clothing, so yes please. I'm clearly not cut out for (nor interested in) perfecting golf levels, putting under pressure or grabbing collectibles, the only goal was to unlock and complete as many levels as possible. passed on the crazy caverns, one bonus level, and of course a bunch of blue things and stars, and only turned off challenge timers around the halfway point and never used any other assists. good enough., really pleasant music and some ambience (birds chirping and the like), plus a . resolutions, windowed mode, v-sync, field of view, various graphics settings (depth of field, bloom, grass, anti-aliasing, etc.), separate volume settings (based on the rest I was surprised it was only music and sound, ambience could use its own for completeness' sake), control config mentioned above, you can turn off the hud, some languages, and in-game representation of achievements.it  and some seriously outdated hardware without issues and it's done really well, except for level selection and some control issues that should be easy fixes if the devs checked their email or skimmed this review for some feedback. multiple player profiles wouldn't hurt either, and cavern progress should save when you quit as well, the holes are tough enough without losing progress.while it's not cheap, there's a lot of content and it's definitely something to play at some point. , and that's from someone easily and constantly annoyed.  though, probably even with some assists, but going for good enough will still keep you busy for many hours.  and lets everybody have fun the way they want without punishing them, though the final course and a few bonus levels have a bunch of timing involved.

_childDocuments_.review: A Little Golf Journey might be selling the actual game short as far as game titles are concerned; it’s a pretty meaty game if you decide to do and collect everything you can. Now, the story on the other hand is indeed simple. All of it is told through little notes that are shown on your screen as you progress throughout the world, or by unlocking secrets. You won’t see any characters; just an overworld, the golf ball and the courses themselves. A golf game doesn’t really need a story anyway, so no harm done. Just a quick FYI.Golfing in this game is made very easy here: pull back the mouse to decide the course of the ball and pull it back even further to charge it and swing it even further. Use Control to move the camera to the opposite side of where the ball is going to land (very useful if there’s a tree or something in your trajectory) and use Shift to temporarily focus on the area where you want the ball to specifically land (otherwise, the cursor will shift left, right, up and down so you have an indication of where it will go, but not where it will *exactly* go). Both of these options will eventually be used in the game, because when the camera is swinging loosely you can sometimes get the ball to go even further, *if* you manage to time it correctly. It all sounds very complicated, but once you’ve tried and seen it the mechanic is actually quite easy to grasp. When you’re on the green you pretty much have won/finished the level as the ball then only rolls over the ground and it’s hard to miss these shots.So after finishing the tutorial you are dropped into an overworld where you can roll into one linear direction, much like Super Mario Bros. 3 (if you’ve ever played that one), with some secret pathways to be found that can be unlocked in the levels themselves. The goal of each level is to collect stars and each level has three to four stars to collect. Naturally you’ll receive the maximum number of stars the less swings you have to use to reach the hole. If you need more swings the number will reduce after a specific preset number has been reached. Normally you can easily collect as many as two stars per level, sometimes one, sometimes even three, but to get the maximum number of stars you’ll need to practice and find an ideal way to reach the hole. This can take a lot of time: to complete a hole it usually takes a minute, maybe two. But it’s fun to do and try at least several times, even if you don’t want to do them all. And sometimes you might not even have an option. You see, even though there’s a big overworld your progress will sometimes be gated by needing a minimum star limit. Meaning you need to have at least as many stars as the gate tells you to have in order to continue your journey. The developers naturally want you to actually play the game instead of rushing through it, but I personally would’ve rather seen people finish my game. Collect all stars in a level and the hole will get a yellow flag on the overworld and if you miss one or more the flag will be red so you always know where you stand if you’re looking to improve your game.Whenever you finish a level the world gets colored in. It starts off pretty barren and colorless, you see and by the time you finish a level the area around it gets color, but stuff like grass, flowers and butterflies. If you’ve ever played Flower (and you should!) you know what the effect looks like. It’s great!The levels also contain objects related to secrets. There are blue things (that’s literally the name for them) that can be collected to enter caves of skill, with holes that get increasingly more difficult. And there are transparent cubes that can be hit, which in turn will spawn blue orbs that need to be hit (sometimes with a time limit) to open up the secret hole. These secrets open up more of the levels and even some free stars that can be grabbed to quickly increase your total. Finding and collecting/finishing these secrets automatically end the level so you need to replay it if you want to collect (more) stars.There are multiple worlds to play through, with 10 levels each. This includes the secret levels. Worlds range from windy cliff sides to Japanese gardens with lanterns and even a snowy area with presents and pine trees. Plenty of variety to keep you entertained for hours.As for the stars: there are 400 to collect in total. The blue things has a total of 61. There’s no lack of content, that’s for sure.Unfortunately I did encounter a few bugs; the first being the landscapes in which the ball very, very rarely gets stuck in. So you’re forced to then reset the level, because it’s almost guaranteed you won’t be able to finish with enough stars. I encountered one issue where I wasn’t able to progress the ball at all, because it was stuck in a corner of a platform that I just couldn’t get out of. The other was a smaller issue at a forced gate. I needed to have 99 stars in order to progress, which I eventually had, but further down the road I needed 97 stars to progress, so: less. Probably a bug, a glitch or maybe even a typo (I didn’t try again with less than 99 stars), but it was very weird nevertheless.The other one isn’t a bug, more a design issue, and that’s when finishing the tutorial you’re not given the option to quit the level. You have to manually quit. So I didn’t know for sure if the game bugged out, it wanted to teach me a lesson it didn’t (yet) show or that it was just over altogether. I assumed the latter, but it’s something I took note of. Maybe the developer can explain, or just patch it out if they agree. Graphically this game is gorgeous. Lots of little details and animated objects with a great artstyle, it looks crazy beautiful for a golf game, especially when a bit of nature pops up after finishing a level. And each world also has its own style and details which adds much needed variety to a game like this where you normally only see grass, a ball and a club (the game doesn’t show any clubs, though).There is no voice acting and the sound effects are good. Nothing special, but hey, it’s a golf game. The music consists of beautiful, relaxing piano music that fits the sport I guess.A Little Golf Journey still doesn’t reinvent the golf genre – how could it, anyway? – but it does a great job at trying to keep things fresh with lots of variety in both its levels and its worlds. The golf mechanics are solid and even though I dislike gated progress I think I do understand why they ultimately made that decision. I’m not entirely sure why this name was chosen for the game as I have only collected 145 stars out of 400 at the moment of writing, with 4 hours played, but one thing’s for sure: it’s not a little journey in any way.

_childDocuments_.review: I was excited to pick up A Little Golf Journey but ended up returning it after 45 minutes. Ultimately, it wasn't fun. It's a neat concept and a cute little design but it didn't feel like a game. Maybe it gets more interesting as you progress, but I wasn't confident it was going to be worth spending the time finding out.OVERALL GAMEPLAYOn each level, you shoot the ball across a 3D map into a hole. The GUI lets you know how many strokes you need to shoot under for a full three stars. If you're super casual, I guess you might ignore this and just shoot around the map, but if you're treating this like a game you're going to go for three stars. This normally means 2-3 strokes and requires you to shortcut most of the map. For almost every level I played, that meant taking a tee shot over some trees towards the hole on Shot 1, then going right for the pin on Shot 2. Sometimes Shot 2 is close enough that you can fly it straight into the hole for a slam dunk. Other times, it's a little long and you have to hope the ball rolls across the green into the hole. It got stale quickly.BASIC MECHANICSYou click and drag from the ball to select direction and distance, and a circle appears on the ground to show you where it will land. The trajectory bounces around, adding some randomness, but you can hold a button to steady the shot. This takes all elements of timing and skill out of the game. It's less like you're shooting the ball and more like you're selecting where you want it to go. On harder levels, you might have to shoot without the steadying mechanic for a slightly further max shot for minimum strokes. But the bouncing trajectory doesn't make you feel skilled for getting the right shot so much as lucky.PUTTINGThere aren't indicators on the green telling you how it slopes. You can try to move the camera down toward the ground to get a read, but it's pretty impossible. This means that on approach shots you're doing a lot of guessing about how it will roll out. That's fine, but not when the game makes you sink those shots for full stars. Then you get annoyed when you miss, do a quick reset, and try your roll of the dice again. An indicator shows you where the ball will go on shorter puts. So basically it either takes no skill or feels like total luck.CONTROLSIt was hard to fly around the world smoothly, and I had trouble rotating the camera without the mouse going to my second monitor screen and then the next click unfocusing the game window.BONUS MODESSometimes you're tasked with finding blue blobs in the level. This is more about flying through the 3D world with the floating camera than playing golf. Once you find it, you shoot you ball at it. I didn't find it interesting. Other times, you have to hit a series of targets within a time limit. Since aiming and shooting takes no skill, the difficulty comes from how the ball rolls out based on the terrain. Where there was difficulty, it felt outside my control and therefore less fun.

_childDocuments_.review: From a satisfying little golf game on mobile to satisfying big golf game on PC. So far I have only played the first world (of nine), and it took me 45 minutes to have completed it almost 100%. I tend to get the max stars first try, and I expect that to change as the game gets harder. So I estimate the game might take me around 8-10 hours to finish, which is pretty good for the price.The levels so far have been really beautiful and well made, with good shortcuts to get below bar. The physics on the ball are really good and predictable, better than most other golf games. There are lots of graphical options, control options, and a fair few "assist" options if you want to make the game easier or harder for yourself.If you enjoyed the demo or the mobile version (OK Golf) you'll enjoy this one.

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up after seeing it at the top of Dohi64's "Best Puzzle Games of 2021" list. I often read his posts on Reddit, and he seems to play a lot of games.  After playing and loving  in 2021 (I didn't get a Switch until well after release), I thought I might be in the headspace to appreciate what  had to offer.I had fun looking for ways to unlock some of the many secret holes within each course. I remember unlocking one by placing my shot precisely in the doorway of a castle shown among the scenery. I unlocked others by placing a shot on a floating gem, and then trying to match my shot to displayed trajectories a few shots in a row.The shot mechanics are relatively simple. You'll drag your mouse back to set your shot power, and as you hold the button you'll see an arched line showing you the potential trajectories of your shot. You'll watch this arched line rotate between potential trajectories, changing slightly in distance and more notably in curve (left to right or right to left). To actually make the shot, you'll want to release your mouse button at the exact moment that the trajectory matches what you intend.While it's nice that the game uses such a simple and straightforward mechanic to make shots, I found that I tired of the experience rather quickly. Gone is the decision to club up at the expense of accuracy or club down at the expense of distance. The difficulty in the game actually comes from trying to figure out whatever strange route the game expects you to take to achieve the lowest number of shots and maximum number of stars on a hole, rather than a direct test of your shot execution. In this way, it really  more of a puzzle game than a golf game. To put it another way, the difficulty is more about figuring out what to do than it is in actually doing it. On one hole I acquired the top score through placing the ball nowhere near the fairway, instead launching it to the top of a rocky mountain so that it would roll down the other side.The courses themselves also felt pretty bland to me, and there was no real humor to speak of. Two of most compelling aspects of  were the very creative courses (a haunted country club?) and the humor on display.While I can't say that I feel any intense dislike towards , I just slowly lost interest in playing it. For weeks on end I'd see it sitting installed in my Steam library before picking something that was more engaging or satisfying to play. Finally, and still lacking any desire to continue, I decided to uninstall and put together this brief review.

_childDocuments_.review: So 'A Little Golf Journey' is a really great game. It's a chill game even though you may not be a big Golf fan like I am this is a really easy game to play and doesn't require much effort so it's a nice game to play here and there and to relax. You can maybe also listen to music or listen to a podcast or whatever you like while playing this.I completed the game 100% just now and even though I liked it for the most part there are these white blocks that are pretty hard to see and reveal themselves when you get close which I don't really get. It was so random to encounter them all of a sudden and it was a bit frustrating to see it in one of the minigolf courses.I DO recommend this game to anyone, playing it 100% was sometimes a bit of a hassle and a bit frustrating aswell to be honest. Most of the time it was pretty solid to play that way but in a few levels I felt like the amounts of shots is just 1 too short to make it more enjoyable.I DON'T recommend playing the game for 100% since I think it's way more enjoyable if you don't put that 'pressure' on you because when I collected the blue things and had all the shots in the world it was way more enjoyable to play the game so I think most people will prefer to play this way but since I am sometimes more of a completionist I played this game to 100%. The amount of shots were sometimes a bit too tight and if the developers maybe change the amount of shots needed for all stars it would make the game way more enjoyable in my opinion for most of the playerbase I assume.Again, this is a great game with easy controls where you will enjoy your time playing but just don't force yourself to 100% the game and play the game in the way you enjoy it the most because after all games are there to be enjoyed and where you can have fun!

_childDocuments_.review: I was ready to praise this game, I was ready to call it a hidden gem, I was ready to call it my favorite golf game of all time. However after a fantastic start the game kinda falls off in the middle. I still really like this game but it does have some problems.The game is very simple, you click and drag to shoot on top of that you can reverse your camera and do a focus shot. Your shot indicator moves in an ∞ motion and it is often required to shoot at the very edge of the indicator to gain extra reach.The challenge of this game comes from the star system, if you want to get the maximum amount of stars you only get a limited amount of shots for each hole. Early in the game the optimal route is usually pretty obvious, do you take the long and winded path or go for the obvious shortcut? However in later levels it isn’t always so easy, there are often multiple potential par paths and the best way to proceed is usually to just experiment. The game has a lot of tricks up its sleeve a decent amount of perfect solutions are surprising. The game also features quite a few secrets, some are just hidden holes, others require chasing a wisp around and some are even timed challenges. As the game progresses it adds more mechanics, suddenly you might be blocked by mountains or the wind starts blowing or there are moving objects. I really hate the moving objects in this game, all they do is make you wait. The issue is that you are waiting for your shot indicator to be in a good spot and the obstacle to be out of your way. It isn’t necessarily harder but it often takes forever to line up a shot correctly. The entire last world is just a huge waiting simulator and I really didn’t enjoy that. The world before that is not much better, the gimmick there is low gravity and the gameplay is basically the same as at the very start of the game it just takes longer for your ball to move. The final achievement for beating the caverns of persistence is awful, there isn’t even a shot counter for the 24 shots you get, the moving sinkhole is always in a different spot and in general the whole level but especially the ending is confusing. Another thing I dislike is the putting mechanic, it is very basic and there isn’t much to it. If you are on the green you are forced into putting mode occasionally it is better to avoid the green and finish a hole from the fairway which is way too easy.I wish the game had more mini-golf levels, they are super fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I've had more time to play this game and I wanted to expand on my review.Little Golf Journey is AWESOME!!The overall vibe from this game is just the best. It's a joy to play. The game is so much fun to play and the graphics, story and soundtrack just serve to enhance the experience. I've sunk half a dozen hours into this so far and its not an exaggeration to say I've enjoyed every second. The secrets are really well done. Hidden just enough to make it fun to find them and then you have to complete a challenge to complete them & some of the secret bonus areas are quite difficult. The early levels seem easy but the later levels really ramp up the difficulty. The final levels also transform the game into a type of retrowave/vaporwave/outrun type aesthetic which I didnt see coming and is really, really cool. I've played many arcade golf games over the years on mobile & PC like super stickman golf, golf around, golf club wasteland, ect, and a little golf journey blows them all away in my opinion. Fun game! Much to like about this one, it seems tailor made for steam deck.- Nice gameplay physics - Good graphics - Relaxing sound track - Simple, fun gameplay This is a great “pick and and play for 10 minutes” type game. The aiming and shooting system is well done, it’s intuitive with just enough difficulty that it doesn’t feel like a total gimmie (though putting is a bit too easy)Overall highly recommend for simple and fun gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: Overall verdict: A Little Golf Journey is too long and contains too much filler, incl. superfluous "blue thing" collectables. There would be a good game in here if the devs had cut 50% of playtime and a third of the levels in exchange for further polish on the remainder. But as is, I regretted playing the game. 14h is a lot of lifetime spent on something I mostly experienced moment-to-moment as a vague sense of existential dread.If you *do* decide to play this game, turn on Assist mode from the very beginning. It includes an Undo, which makes some of the stars *much* less of a chore to collect.Other comments:Ultimately I can't recommend this game, certainly not for anyone who tries to 100% games.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; An awesome and beautiful mix of the puzzle and golf genre that challenges you throughout. Completionists: Turn on Undo in the Assist menu or you’ll hate it.I’m loving this game. It’s reminiscent of Mario 64 because of the overworld map and star requirement for unlocking the next set of levels.  Each world has a theme and so do the levels themselves. They remind me of mini golf courses and are very beautiful. After you finish each level, the overworld fills in with colors like you’re painting.  It’s very rewarding.  I played the demo then immediately bought the complete game. The demo is the entire first world and progress transfers to the full game, which is great because it was not easy (assuming you complete it 100%, which I did).  The game drops you right into the action and I was so drawn in that I didn’t even pause to fiddle with the settings. I’ve played through the first two worlds now and most of the levels would have been easy if I didn’t care about maxing out the stars.  Even the swing mechanic itself was difficult to master, but after enough practice, I got the hang of it.  Now I have finished several levels with max stars on the first try (without Undo). But before figuring out the swing, there were a few moments where I almost moved on to the next level without getting max stars first.If you are like me, the type that wants to get max stars on every level before moving to the next one, this will be important. Collecting stars is done in each level using a par system.  You get max stars for hitting par.  You can restart the level if you go over, but that breaks the flow and makes mastering game mechanics really hard.  Now, I consider myself quite tenacious, but it was a slog to finish the first world. Even so, I still bought the complete game and this time, I fiddled with the settings and noticed an Undo key bind (which isn’t mentioned in the tutorial)!  A few moments later, I recalled a review that said to turn on Undo. So I went to the ‘Assist’ menu and hesitantly turned it on.  I thought using Undo would feel like cheating, but after two levels, I knew I would keep it on. It made for a much better experience, as it let me practice swinging and focus on the puzzle aspect.  It should probably be on by default because the second world was so much more fun and was still just as hard. To put it in perspective, a special level called Caverns of Skill doesn’t have a par system, so Undo basically just makes you lose progress.  The review where I learned about the Undo button talked about how hard, long and frustrating the level is.  (Thank you, mondsemmel !!!).  This was my favorite level so far, but If I hadn’t turned on Undo, I guarantee you my review would have said the same thing. I wouldn't have had the practice I needed to perfect my swing nor a smooth experience due to the constant restarting.  So, if you are a completionist like me, do yourself a favor and turn on Undo and play this amazingly awesome game the right way.

_childDocuments_.review: Golf in a miniature world which is surprisingly enjoyable. I had actually never heard of this game before, until I stumbled over it as a choice in a bundle.Graphics are good, it's a combination of simplistic and complex texture with nice lighting effects, beautiful water reflections and cozy atmosphere.The piano music is nice and relaxing, but not quite my style.There's plenty of holes to play, even if some of them may be a bit too similar.Each of the 10 courses takes place in their own very unique and different environment.You can unlock additional holes by finding secrets. Some of these can be a tiny bit frustrating to unlock, f.ex. those that require you to hit x-numbers of spheres within a certain time-limit, but you do have unlimited retries.I was at first a little worried when I read the criticism regarding the controls. Luckily, I didn't find it problematic at all. Yes, the aiming is swaying back and forth to the sides inside the aiming circle. However, you can momentarily stop this movement for a few seconds and make precise shots by holding down the focus button (SHIFT-key). Sometimes you do benefit from not using it, f.ex. if you want the power stroke to be a little more powerful or weaker.Anyway, should you have a hard time, then there's always "Assist Mode" in the settings.It's a unique, cozy and casual golf game that you can jump straight into. Each hole only takes a couple of minutes, so it's excellent for the times you want to play something but only got a few minutes to spare.On the other hand, it's not something you would be playing for hours at a time.Overall, if you're looking for a simple golf/minigolf game, I can recommend this!

This isn't a typical golf game, as there are secrets you can uncover by playing the game, and loads of courses to try your hand at. That's sadly where the goods things end.Aiming system is kind of crap for what they want you to accomplish with some of the challenges because the rocking back and forth of the line and waiting on the ball to stop eats a lot of time.The star system seems really tight with you having to cut through trees a lot of times and not really playing the level. _childDocuments_.review: Definitely a neutral but I really don't think I would've played it as completely without a Steam Deck.I've definitely given a lot of games a pass because they play well with the Steam Deck. On top of that two of my favorite video game genres are puzzles and golf. This was very much up my alley and I put my hours in getting all the "stars" and "blue things". But it really wasn't a ton of fun. At all...The golfing is very, very lackluster. The puzzles, when collecting all the stars, are paint-by-numbers at best. There's no mystery to the solutions. There's no grey area. No flexibility. No wiggle room. There's one way to get all the stars on every hole. You know exactly how many strokes it takes. You get to see exactly where all your shots are going, even with wind. There's TONS of environmental clues. It's just plain straightforward. In the last few worlds there's some timing added in, but it adds nothing really.In fact, I would argue the later worlds with their timing events highlight how tedious, tiring, and unenjoyable the game actually is. World 8 with its low gravity and shots that take 3x longer to see the result of is especially painful. And I won't even begin to speak of the finale hole. I couldn't wait that one out, I was done. I had been worn down too much and so I will uninstall and leave that last "blue thing" floating out there in the digital ether. Which speaks volumes that I'm content just walking away after 14hrs with just one collectable left.It's a pretty game though. Great visuals and styles in each world. Right down to the menus, the artists are talented and then some. But I only played as much as I did because of the Steam Deck and getting in and out. And then it still broke me in the end. I can't speak to how it would've played without going for all the collectables, so I don't outright recommend against it. But it isn't a satisfying "completionist" if you ask me.

_childDocuments_.review: I recommend this game for kids, it is a good introductory game for golfing, beautifully designed, with a lot of different and varied maps. It is a very relaxing game, with an appropriate soundtrack. Besides the regular golf courses, there are also some side-challenges, then can make the game more interesting for kids. The game is, however, not fair in the difficulty settings. While you can turn in some aiming assists, the game would made kids happier if an easier setting was present. As is, it is very difficult to finish all courses with maximum stars. Adults can also enjoy the game, but I would say it’s an 9/10 for kids and 7/10 for adults.

_childDocuments_.review: A Little Golf Journey is an enjoyable little golf/puzzle game. I didn't put much effort into trying to get every star and I finished all the levels available to me in about 3 hours. If you want to go for every star, I assume it would take significantly longer. Personally, I don't think it's worth the effort but playing through it as normal, getting the scores that I get, and completing each hole once in a few hours was still enjoyable. The only things I didn't like about the game was sometimes trees would change your ball trajectory in a way the cursor wouldn't show. It got very frustrating at times going for shortcuts. You think you have it very precise and will just land your hit perfectly only for it to hit some leaves halfway through the shot, which the game wouldn't indicate while taking the shot, and it ruins the hole for you. Also the last couple worlds have moving objects in them that can block your path. It didn't add much of a challenge, it just made you have to wait to take your shot and it got annoying. If you want to add objects in the way of shots, don't make me wait through moving objects while my cursor moves around for max power. It wasn't challenging, it was just annoying.Still, with those notes aside, it was still fun for the three hours it took me to complete all the holes once. If you want a casual golf game, I recommend this one. There's definitely a lot more value than the 3 hours it took me if you want to 100% it too!

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a great golfing game overall. Some of the game-play became repetitive once you figured out how to hit the ball the at the strongest stroke. _childDocuments_.review: It is a good game but not without some flaws. It is a relaxing game if you decide to play it that way. You could beat the game in 5 to 6 hours if you ignore secret levels, challenges and collectibles. Some of the best levels are unlocked by finding a secret. The game runs well, looks good and sounds good. There is a story but it is really nothing to write home about. You will golf your way through nice landscapes and I liked all the location except the last world. The last world is some TRON like futuristic crap and it doesn't feel right in this game and it almost ruined the whole game for me so I just rushed through it.The other complaints are all in optional time trials -  awful , caverns where you have to navigate through 5 to 6 levels and the last cavern has 0 margin for error, I had to play it again and again because at the end if you make a mistake you will go to the start and lose at least 10 minutes of hard work, it is unfair and also doesn't feel right in this kind of game.Overall a good game that can be relaxing but you can also challenge your self . I will try and forget the last world, soooo in the end I can recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Really neat golf/puzzle game with an SMB style overworld including hidden exits, bonus levels, collectibles etc. There are a bunch of accessibility options to make certain aspects of the game easier. My only gripe with this game is that some of the 3/4-star rewards can be needlessly difficult or random, and the final level is pretty annoying compared to the rest of the levels. Overall definitely worth giving a go!
_childDocuments_.name: A Little Golf Journey

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who hasn't played sports games since NBA Jam on SNES (and loathed every one since) this was actually really nice. The music, atmosphere, and clever sprinkle of puzzle gameplay had me pleasantly surprised. There are tons of stages and things to collect which is also nice, so can always come back and improve your shot if you would like.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little Golf Journey

_childDocuments_.review: A great golf game with the easiest mechanics possible (you don't need to choose your clubs, you control the aim and the power with a simple drag and drop that shows you exactly where the ball is gonna land...) that relies on the clever level design to make it engaging. Looking around and trying to find out-of-the-box ways to get to the hole in as few shots as possible is a huge part of the fun of this game, and turns it into some kind of puzzle. Plus, there are secrets hidden in some levels, so you'll want to keep an eye out for those.I usually don't care too much about exploration in games, but this one made it transparent enough to get me interested in this aspect. You can often tell from how the overworld map is designed whether there's a secret passage to discover inside a level.On top of that, it's very relaxing, supported by a soothing soundtrack.
_childDocuments_.name: A Little Golf Journey

_childDocuments_.review: When I played the demo for this a while ago, I figured it would be a neat little game I could get a few hours out of before getting bored. Well after buying it and putting over a dozen hours into it, I can safely say it's been a surprise for me. I'm not a fan of the imprecision of the shooting at times, but I found it fairly forgiving in terms of taking risks to get the ball in the hole in the least amount of shots. The level design and loading screen descriptions for levels paint pretty clear hints as to how you're supposed to solve these. Furthermore, the hidden challenge levels and secrets are fairly enjoyable.I was not expecting this to be as addicting as it is, and I enjoyed the experience immensely.

Meanwhile, the younger sister, Saki, was raised by her mother, learning to despise her father for abandoning them and taking her sister away. When her father goes missing, Aya decides to put her skills with the sword to use as an Undead-hunter. Upon her beloved mother's murder, Saki becomes consumed to the point of insanity with a desperate thirst for revenge, resorting to manipulating the Undead to achieve her goal. Aya resolves to seek out her younger sister, her only surviving relation, while Saki is determined to resurrect her mother using an ancient art passed down through the ages. This art, however, requires the heart of a blood relative to work, meaning that the younger sister must kill the elder if she is to have her sworn vengeance. And so, amidst a swirling storm of love, hate, and intrigue, the battle between the two sisters begins!

The elder sister, Aya, was raised by her father, who subjected her to rigorous training in the way of the blade. Meanwhile, the younger sister, Saki, was raised by her mother, learning to despise her father for abandoning them and taking her sister away. When her father goes missing, Aya decides to put her skills with the sword to use as an Undead-hunter. Upon her beloved mother's murder, Saki becomes consumed to the point of insanity with a desperate thirst for revenge, resorting to manipulating the Undead to achieve her goal. Aya resolves to seek out her younger sister, her only surviving relation, while Saki is determined to resurrect her mother using an ancient art passed down through the ages. This art, however, requires the heart of a blood relative to work, meaning that the younger sister must kill the elder if she is to have her sworn vengeance. And so, amidst a swirling storm of love, hate, and intrigue, the battle between the two sisters begins!
short_description: To commemorate the 15th anniversary of the sword fighting action game series Onee Chanbara, the events of THE Onee Chanbara and THE Onee Chanbara 2 have been completely remade in full HD. The evolution of this high-speed action game cannot be missed!

_childDocuments_.review: I had to put up with a lot of crap with this game. The horrendous sound issue, frame rate issues, crashes...thankfully nothing that the community, who has been a fantastic help, couldn't sort out easily. I mean, it's amazing how a few simple DIY tinkering can get this game working smoothly (which begs the question, how do you release a game so bad yet so simple to fix?).However, after taking a short break and booting it up, a big message blows up in my face - save data corrupted...which is so fitting for a game that was already giving me one headache after another be so determined to fail that it outright commits suicide when you force it to work properly. It's all the more maddening since it's not their first rodeo on PC, yet their newest game has some of the worst issues thus far. Now, the game itself is great. It's the same mindless, raunchy hack-n-slash as Z2 (sadly, without the eye-opening DLC outfits we all know and love) and the new look does give it a striking aesthetic...which makes it all the more bittersweet that it has some atrocious issues I can't say I've experience in the developer's previous work. I'm not kidding, this game's disastrous launch is almost as comical as the most notorious AAA day one blunders that's happened in the past. No doubt it'll get fixed, but for the time being I'm just too angry and worn out to give this game another round.EDIT: So, I managed to finish the game in the most technical sense - I beat the last boss. I shouldn't be surprised at all when I say that the game has managed to crash on me...during the credits, of all things. Luckily my save wasn't corrupted this time and got to plow through it again - just to have it crash after the credits this time. Again, the Steam community comes to the rescue with yet another fix (seriously, you guys are awesome!) which is just absurd at this point. I've pretty much went under this game's hood - just to get it to work, more than I've installed mods in some games. It's a strange feeling, really...I'm more relieved that I beat the game than I am satisfied with it. And in the end, I'm not even excited. I just felt like I (well, you guys) did the company's job for them without getting paid for it. You see all the achievements I unlocked for this game? They feel like purple heart medals.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, the other reviews indicate that there's some serious technical problems, so I can only speak to my own experience, which is that it's working fine on my system so far, , so buyer beware for now.That said, I've actually played this game quite a bit on PS4, and it's a lot of fun, if a bit short. You can definitely complete the main story in a single session of play. The action in game feels really good. It's not complex. You'll mostly be mashing the basic attack button and pressing dodge whenever an attack is incoming. You'll string in the "reload" button (that cleans blood off your weapons), and weave in and out of the fray with the dodge while doing so to keep moving and on the offensive. There's also a parry you'll make use of against some of the tougher enemies (one enemy type in particular calls for it), but for the most part, it's a lot easier to dodge to avoid damage and charge special attack meter.Once you've beat the storyline, there's a few DLC side-story extra missions that flesh out the characters just a little more, and an endless survival mode (not DLC, to be clear) of a looping set of 51 waves/floors of increasingly powerful enemies and bosses (they get stronger each loop). If I recall correctly, the normal way to unlock Lei is to beat floor 100, which in itself takes a couple hours of play, assuming you can even make it that far (it's pretty tough - you'll probably want to be at or near max level and stocked on recovery items).The action itself is enough for me to recommend this title, but again, it's not got a whole lot of content. Also, again, there seem to be some technical issues that other users have been experiencing, so buyer beware. It's fine for me, and I really like the game, but I can't just blindly recommend the title without noting the issues that others seem to be experiencing.On a side note, this game features  by Broken By The Scream, which introduced me to this screamo metal idol unit. That's a big plus. If you ever felt like Japanese idol pop music needed to sound a lot more like Dir En Grey, they've got you covered.

_childDocuments_.review: Posting review just to have a workaround under hand and not have to search it, if they never fix the issue. Run the game, if the sound stutters, alt-tab out of it, open Nvidia's control panel, go to manage 3D settings, then program settings tab add Onechanbara from running processes, change low latency to "Ultra" and max framerate to your display refresh rate. Apply and restart the game for the driver settings to be used. Completely fixed stutter on my RTX 3060Ti. Still rating positive despite issue with awful, stuttery sounds since the game's pretty cool and very relaxing, even if I don't necessary have will to play through it now due to covid in the family;c.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Most of this seems to have been fixed in the April 7, 2021 update. But crashes and microstutter can still happen, so the below tweaks are still recommended.Right-click on desktop -> NVIDIA Control Panel -> Manage 3D Settings -> Program Settings -> Add -> OneeChanbaraOrigin.exe, then set the following options:Low Latency Mode: UltraMax Frame Rate: 60 FPSVertical sync: FastMake sure to click "apply" when done.No known solutions.Problem: The game is not rendering at native resolution when using 4K or above display modes.Solution: Right-click on the game in your Steam library -> Properties -> Local Files -> Browse. Then right-click on OneeChanbaraOrigin.exe, Properties -> Compatibility -> Change high DPI settings -> High DPI scaling override -> Application.See this thread for more info.Problem: The mouse cursor is constantly spinning and thus impossible to hide fully.(Ghetto) Solution: Press the Windows Key on your keyboard, then click on the game's icon on the taskbar. The cursor will no longer be spinning and you can now tuck it away in a corner.Alternatively, you can also use a third party tool to hide the mouse cursor automatically, for example AutoHideMouseCursor[].Problem: Cloud saves aren't configured properly on the developer's end and in fact do not work.(Ghetto) Solution: You should periodically back up your save folder, as the game is known to corrupt saves if it crashes. The location is the same as the game folder. Right-click on the game in your Steam library -> Properties -> Local Files -> Browse. You should see a "savedata" folder.

_childDocuments_.review: I've done everything the game has to offer, such as beating the story on normal, hard, beast and berserk. All the bonus missions. Every quest including no damage taken and reaching floor 151 in survival mode. My score is a solid 10 / 10 with only a few minor gripes that don't hurt enough to subtract points.The game feels infinitely re-playable to me because it encourages you to get better at the hack and slash with the cool system. It rewards you with speed and damage for timing your attacks in a rhythm opposed to button mashing. Killing lots of enemies charges a meter for a berserk mode that increases your damage. Followed by a second form if you fully charge it again before it expires. This grants even more damage and the ability to heal yourself while attacking. In order to keep you playing aggressively, your health will drain while it's active. The more kills you get, the longer it lasts, making it especially good in survival.The graphics are outstanding, I'm glad they have finally decided on a really good looking art style. Previous games in the series have been kind of ugly in my opinion, but visuals have never stopped me from enjoying a game that plays good. I consider them to be the cherry on top of the ice cream. Voice acting is great. Sound design and music also amazing. And some of those battle songs can really get you pumped up to perfect those combos. Enemies are varied enough to make you think about certain encounters. There is a shop with lots of items to buy to give you minor boosts. From healing, revives, and even an expensive temporary invulnerability charm. One item you have to parry mud men to acquire. Which when used increases your berserk meter, but you cannot buy it. I have no problem working for in game money to buy stuff, but a lot of rings are costing 500,000 thousand to 1,000,000 million in game money when runs average low amounts. For those of you who have beat the game, I found a trick to grind money faster. Boot up level 1 on beast mode, equip the "Hits" and "Berserk" rings. Now work on doing your 300 hits quest, enemies take a ridiculously long time to die making it easy to go that high constantly. Reach stage 2 of berserk as much as you can and let it expire. Because 2 achievements require you to do this 100 times. You end up killing around 5 birds with 1 stone. About 30 minutes of this netted me over 3 million money from reaching 999 combos over and over. I assume the rings are so dreadful to obtain because most act like equip-able cheat codes. My favorite combination to use has been the Rings of Technique, Bloodsucking, and Xtasy. Play the game, you'll see what they do. My final nod goes out to the plenty of fan service. What more can you ask for? Hot girls, exceptional action and game play, lots of blood and gore. I need another entry of this franchise honestly. I haven't said anything about the story because it's not that strong. It does attempt to get you to care a bit, but ultimately it feels like the problem is presented just as fast as it's solved and not too much depth or interaction really happens. We know some basic stuff and bits of their personalities, but at the end of the day it's just a revenge trip and not much else. I don't think any of the games in this series were ever that heavily story focused, so I didn't really care that much. I was here to slash and look at eye candy, left satisfied. Little disappointing the cast was smaller and we didn't get to play as some of the human bosses with move sets on par with the player characters. But oh well. While very unlikely to happen, I still hope Eva comes as dlc one day. She was a playable character in a previous entry. Speaking of move sets, I noticed something a little strange. Aya only has 1 cool finisher, and it's good so it's not a problem. But Saki has a different animation for every enemy type. It's really cool, especially karate chopping zombie dogs in half. But I'm curious why Aya doesn't. I only have a few negatives to say. Number 1 being I hate when games give you time waster achievements. You must buy all rings, and as you've seen from before. I've beaten the story 4 times start to finish with over 20 stages and didn't even have enough money to get half of the rings. The 2nd being the camera and lock on is really bad. For whatever reason the lock on decides to randomly target some enemy far off on the other side of the map instead of the group your already fighting. And it tends to zoom in extremely high up obstructing your view against some of the bigger bosses. You can't even see yourself anymore, only hear the sounds of your character attacking when this happens. Moving camera around with the mouse does not let you turn majority of the time, you have to use the keyboard. Lastly, you can't remap all the buttons you'd like. I wish I could pause with escape like every other game and run with shift. But no, not allowed here. Overlooking these minor annoyances, I still strongly recommend playing this game.
