_childDocuments_.review: I got this in the recent Humble Bundle of D3PUBLISHER titles. I had been morbidly curious about Onee Chanbara for a while, ever since I saw it ported on the Wii as "Bikini Zombie Slayers," but the comparatively high price kept me away from the series for a long time. But, as part of a bundle with a bunch of other games, I figured it was time to finally pull the trigger.This game has a surprising amount going for it. The combat system has an impressive amount of depth and challenge to it, way more than I figured it would. Between dodging and parrying attacks, cleaning your sword of blood as needed and learning the best timing for combos, there's a good amount going on here, but it's fairly easy to get a handle on. As an action game, it's not as technical as something like Bayonetta, but nowhere near as brain-dead as a Musou game. It rests somewhere in a comfortable middle where you're still mowing down hordes of the undead, but there's enough challenge there to keep your interest. The story stages are fairly short and digestible, and thus easy to work into your schedule. And the visuals are nice and colorful, with a clean anime style.OCO certainly has its drawbacks, though. For one thing, it's not very well-optimized for the PC. If you do get this, I highly recommend looking through the Steam Community forums for pointers on how to get it running its best, at the correct resolution, and avoiding crashes. Not nearly the worst PC port I've ever played, but it's far from effortless to get running well. Hell, you'll probably have to look up info in the forums just to figure out how to switch the game's language to English, as it defaults to Japanese for some strange reason.The other major issue is that there's just not much content in the game. It's supposed to be the first two Onee Chanbara titles remade together, but even so, it's incredibly short, with the story mode (including cutscenes and having to replay the first boss several times due to a game-crashing bug that took a while to sort out) clocking in at less than ten hours. Beyond replaying those stages on higher difficulties or playing the survival mode to unlock a hidden character (assuming you don't just pay to unlock her via DLC), the only other thing to do is complete challenges of the "parry attacks X number of times with X character" variety to unlock concept art and skins. For a game that's regularly priced so high, that's a paltry amount of content. And no, the story really isn't enough to justify the price of admission, either.Bottom line, I can recommend this game, but ONLY on a steep discount. For the $4 or so it wound up being with the bundle, that's well worth it. But otherwise, I'd pass unless you're just that desperate to hack up zombies as a bikini cowgirl.

_childDocuments_.review: I've heard people describe the oneechanbara series as "Delicious junk food" and as a guilty pleasure as far as games are concerned. My take? I believe the series has ascended since its' humble roots as Origins really does weave a good story whilst fleshing out Aya,Saki,and Lei to such an extent they are likable,have layers,and are far more than tantalizing eye candy. No doubt a story about friendship,jealousy,love,and family secrets is one set within familiar  parameters we've mapped out before from similar dramas stored in our memory banks but the execution and delivery were far better than I was expecting.Let me ask you a few questions. Do you like hack n slash games that are more complex than they initially seem? Do you like attractive sword wielding vixens bound together by the bonds of sisterhood? Do you like the typical anime and manga trope of the main characters having "ultimate final forms"after they soak in the blood of their enemies for prolonged periods? Can you appreciate an awesome soundtrack whilst you slash up zombies until they gush their crimson vital fluids in all directions like active sprinklers on a golf course? Miss games like Ninja Gaiden and Onimusha? Do you like the distinct Japanese aesthetics found in games like Nioh 2 but you simply "Ain't got no time" to put over one hundred hours into yet another souls-like grind-fest of frustration? If you answered yes to most of these then Oneechanbara origins is for you.....(Or at least I think it is!)Tamsoft has been following the trend of revamping and reviving older entries in their game franchises with a fresh coat of paint. This is probably why Origins has a more cel-shaded anime look whilst its' various locales (Levels) move the action along at a brisk pace so as not to overstay their welcome.  However, like past entries in the series there are extra missions to keep you busy long after you complete the main campaign. (And there is a rpg-lite "leveling up" system via assigning attribute points between missions whilst buying items that serve every function you can think of from restoring your health all the way to making it easier to parry attacks or helping you maintain your blood enraged state over a longer duration.)Origins has its' drawbacks though.  There are less selectable characters here than in Z Chaos (Three instead of four) and dubious DLC practices. (For example,you can get Lei only by rigorously completing every bonus mission "unless" you buy her to unlock her from the start. This doesn't even touch on all the outfit dlcs or how it would be better to have them as awards for overcoming varied in-game challenges.)  It's a shame Tamsoft (Or D3 publishing) deploys these cheap tactics because to me games like Senran Kagura and Oneechanbara give anything from Tecmo/Koei a serious run for their money. In other words, it sucks to see the beloved under-dog you root for become more like their opulent and corrupt competition by the day. (D3 studios/Tamsoft seriously,people like you because you are NOT Tecmo/Koei! You are suppose to be the chosen ones!) ~Angry Obi-wan Kenobi impersonation With so many people struggling right now just to make ends meet because of inflation I sadly cannot recommend you pay "full price" for Oneechanbara origins. I was lucky enough to get it during the summer sale with a lot of its' dlc included at a reduced price point. The problem is there are some high production values here "but" the main campaign can be beaten in roughly 6 or 7 hours if you are so good you don't need to go to previous areas to grind for more orbs to buy more items. (The last boss-lady is quite the friggin nightmare unless you go in prepared!) Couple that with abhorrent dlc milking and it all does bring an otherwise wonderful very enjoyable romp down a few pegs. It is what it is and I'm not a used cars-salesmen with expertise in telling lies and half truths!"But" if you are like me and want to know where this crazy ride began along with some more lore,decent voice acting,and a much better portrayal of the Oneechanbara cast in general then yeah,it is totally worth the investment! (When there's an opportunity to buy it cheaper)Pros+Combat is as buttery smooth as always and only gets better as you unlock additional moves,techniques,and powered up states.+ The story telling and voice acting are unexpectedly good.+Great soundtrack+Varied zombie types all which have their own challenge levels and attack patterns. This is not to say you will not fight similar mobs again and again but there's just enough diversity within those mobs it never feels like a total slog.+ The cel-shaded visuals grew on me. It made the proceedings akin to watching a really good action oriented horror influenced anime from the 90's.+While the stages are bland I think that lent itself well to this kind of dystopian world where the undead have taken over and society has collapsed. +The bosses are a creative menagerie of the absurd,the terrifying,and even somewhat endearing goof balls!+While the main story itself is often solemn and tragic there's just enough humor and endearing banter between Aya,Saki,and Lei to strike a harmonious balance between the comedic and the dramatic.+There are missions to complete even after you finish the main campaign.Cons-The game's longevity is extremely short if you do not care enough to do the side missions. (That are admittedly very repetitive)-D3 publishing taking notes from Tecmo/Koei when it comes to nickle and diming their fanbase-The regular asking price is too expensive.-My game started with Japanese text and language so I had to trouble-shoot to find out how to switch everything over to english. -The game could have benefited from more weather effects. Often times rain,thunder,and lightning in a game greatly add to the ambiance and atmosphere. I still remember Onimusha 2 Samurai's Destiny as the first game I got on my PS2 because it used fog and rain to optimal effect to set the mood for the game going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I had always heard the Onee Chanbara series were janky, low-effort games, so I went into this one with no expectations beyond "Bargain Bin DMC With Boobs".I'll openly admit I don't usually play character action games, but the audiovisual feedback on hits and stagger effects actually felt really good, with my only gripe being some of the enemy telegraphs not being entirely clear when it comes to the perfect parry timer.Story-wise, the writing is actually pretty decent. It's not groundbreaking or anything, but it did make me care about the main characters. And let's be honest. this is not what most people are here for anyways.Graphics-wise, unlike the previous games in the series, ORIGIN went with a heavily stylised, almost cel-shaded anime style, with bold and bright colours. In my opinion, it looks a lot better than any attempt at photo-realism could have, especially when it comes to standing the test of time, and compliments the overall tongue-in-cheek tone of the game.As for the promise of boobs, it sure does deliver, with our main protagonist Aya's default outfit being nothing more than a bikini. Why? Who knows, but most importantly, who cares?Would I recommend buying this game? Yes. Maybe not at full price, but if you ever have the opportunity to grab it half-off, be sure to do so, and make sure it's the Deluxe Edition for all those juicy costume DLCs.

_childDocuments_.review: Onee Chanbara ORIGIN is the prequel to Oneechanbara Z2: Chaos, which was released earlier on Steam than the former oddly. Basically you play as Aya, the lingerie clad samurai girl with a cowgirl hat, slashing her way through hordes of zombies, trying to stop the source of this zombie apocalypse. Along the way you will meet some familiar faces, such as her sister Saki, and some other new characters, though you only get to use Aya, Saki and another unlockable character. Each of them uses different weapons, for example, Aya can single wield or dual wield katanas, while Saki uses her gauntlets and a nodachi as her weapon of choice. If you played Oneechanbara Z2: Chaos, you roughly know how Aya's and Saki's playstyle is like, which is how this game is played. Despite the fan service provided in this game (mainly from Aya's outfits, though there are some really skimpy outfits from a certain boss character), its quite techincal gameplay wise. There quite some focus on perfect evade, where time slows down when you do so, or perfect parry, where there will be a huge blue glare effect, which will either stun enemies temporarily (indicated by the yellow highlight around them), or heavily stun them (indicated by the red heart like indicator above them). Enemies in the latter state can potentially be finished off with a Cool Finish, which is basically your finisher move. For bosses, this finisher only appears when their HP are close to zero. Another focus is on just frames of combo strings, also known as Cool Combination. For this part, there will be a small UI with a blue bar at certain locations and varying length to indicate the timing for each string. Completing the entire string with the correct timing yields an additional string ender exclusive to performing a perfect Cool Combination string. You also get to use your Xtasy Combination, which is basically somewhat of your super moves. The more you kill, the more bloodstained your weapon will be, making it dull and unable to severe parts well. This is where the "reload" mechanic comes in, which basically cleans your weapon up. The more you get stained, the more you will enter a state of blood fueled rage known as Berserk. Getting stained even more transform you into another state known as Xtatic, where Aya and Saki will be clad in only blood, while looking more demonic. You will hit harder here, but your HP will be drained over time, thus you need to constantly kill to heal up.I kinda liked the cell shaded art, its quite unique compared to Oneechanbara Z2: Chaos realistic design. The JP VAs here do a very good job in voicing the character,s especially Aya's VA, which is none other than the Baba herself, Yoko Hikasa. Some of the combos look satisfying to look at, especially Saki's Cool Finisher, which is a powerbomb that can pretty much one shot anything except actual bosses. Did I mentioned how fanservicey Aya's design can be?Sadly, when I got this game on my older PC, I had an issue where the audio was terribly desynced. It was solved in a weird way, where I actually have to run an Android emulator in the background to rectify it. Granted, I no longer have to do this on my newer PC, but the audio feels a bit.... laggy. There's very little stuff to do after you finish the game, as the only alternative mode to play, barring DLC missions, is the survival mode. Through this mode, you get to unlock the final playable character..... or you can just buy the DLC to unlock it. Yes, this game has LOADS of DLCs, though most of it are outfits. However, in game you don't really unlock many outfits, so most of the nice outfits are pretty much DLCs only, and many of them are the same, but different colour. The DLC missions..... can be finished in 5 minutes. You heard that right, its super short! Whatever playable stuff here is actually less than what Oneechanbara Z2: Chaos offers. Even in the latter, you get to use more characters than what is offered here. For some reason, this game also does not have a Steam Cloud save (why?). Finally, some of the quests or achievements are ridiculously hard to track. For example, the Xtatic and Berserk ones, the only way to track it is by counting it yourself.... or let the Steam achievement or in game quest completed message pop up for you.Despite that, I did have some fun with it. Though in overall, I would recommend getting Oneechanbara ZD: Chaos instead, if you plan to try out the Oneechanbara series, simply because its much, much cheaper. If you do want to get this game, get it during a sales, with a heavy discount, because at its current price, it not worth it due to how little it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: Having played Bikini Samurai Squad and Z2 Chaos, I can say that Origin definitely took aspects of those games and not only incorporated them into the game, but also polished and improved upon those aspects. The art style is definitely something I enjoy. It's a simple yet dynamic and vibrant style that is appealing to the eye and makes the player feel like they're in an anime which can be enjoyable to some (like myself). It's really a matter of taste.Gameplay wise, I enjoyed the element that they incorporated from Z2 Chaos, for instance, XTatic forms and Xtasy combos. It was quite nostalgic seeing those elements again and it definitely made me want to play Z2 Chaos again. I also very much enjoy the parry system. It reminded me of Saki's counter from Z2 Chaos but much more refined, polished and improved. It gives me a DMC 4/5 Royal Guard feeling. One thing I experienced however when it comes to parries. I'm not sure if anyone else experienced it, but if you parry as Saki against the Fatmen zombies and do a cool finish either in Xtatic form or when you're about to turn beserk, the camera goes haywire and you zoom around all over the place. It does go back to normal eventually but it's a very interesting glitch. You can still attack while zooming but you have to shift the camera constantly. I currently enjoy the story. Simple, yet easy to understand and quite engaging. COOL combinations are also very cool (pun intended) to pull off. While having the technique ring to pull off COOL combinations easier is great to have, it feels more satisfying to pull them off without them. With practice mode, it gives you endless opportunities to grasp the timing of each combination. The fact that you can have the option to display the COOL combination meter in the main game instead of just training mode is also a great help.I definitely enjoyed Onechanbara Origin. While bringing back and incorporating nostalgic elements from its predecessors, it also polished and improved its own combat system. While not as well known as Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, I certainly enjoy the Onechanbara series. Hopefully, the small following that this series has will eventually grow and get bigger and more popular across the world and I hope that D3 Publisher will continue making more Onechanbara games in the future. I certainly will be looking forward to it.

Kill X amount of enemies in your berserk mode to unlock an art work.There are no cosmetic that you can unlock ingame at all. No hidden items. _childDocuments_.review: I've always been a fan of anything Tamsoft puts out. I own every Senran Kagura game on 3DS/Vita/PS4/Steam and also own the Onee Chanbara games. To fix this simply find the games .exe and click compatibility then DPI settings and force the game to use a higher DPI. With this setting ticked on the game now renders in full 4K and looks really sharp! **Onee Chanbara Origins reminds me of Senran Kagura Burst Renewal in the sense that the game feels stripped back compared to their later entries. As remakes go both Senran Kagura Burst Renewal and Onee Chanbara Origins do a fantastic job at giving a streamlined base start for newcomers as well as solid faithful remakes for fans of the series. I particularly like the counter ability as well as the dodge mechanic and the overall combat feels really solid here. If you're a fan of the series or games like it (Senran Kagura, SG/ZH, etc) or perhaps you like your games with a side of Fanservice and like the sounds of bikini wielding babes fighting zombies I think you will enjoy Onee Chanbara Origins. Highly Recommended

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR fun musuo, but your experience with the PC version will vary, ESPECIALLY with AMD GPUs.I like this game, but whoever did the port should have been fired.Onee Chanbara Origin is a third person hack n slash. You got your light and heavy attack combos, parry, dodge/dash, jump, and most of it works well. The anime cel-shading is very nice on the eyes, the levels have decent structure/pacing and bosses are straight forward fun. You can think of it as a slightly faster/more focused musou (Dynasty Warriors/Senran Kagura) with just enough interesting mechanics to not be completely mindless, with the same essential fun those games have.With that in mind, the port sucks. It stutters while the framerate flucuates around 34-55. Wanna know how to fix it with AMD graphics cards? Run an Android emulator while running Oneechanbara Origin, and it runs at around 60-66FPS. I'm sorry, but that's unacceptable.There are other things I could nit pick.  The camera easily goes to a slightly top down view too often. Enemy/level designs are uninspired. Everyone talks too much. Grinding for the rings to boost stats isn't the best. The campaign is too short for full retail price, the DLC is ludicrous....Even with all that in mind, I legit like Onee Chanbara Origin. A lot. Like, I really enjoy it.The characters are fast, fluid and user friendly. The crowd control is fun. The tag mechanics ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rock.... Even with the fan service, Onee Chanbara just wants to be a PS2 styled action musuo in the 2020s, with no set piece sections, QTEs, forced walking only sections, etc.....The designers wanted to make a fun action game, and Onee Chanbara Origin is just that. A fun action game. However, in doing so, on a budget, they skimped on port optimization when they shouldn't have. It's a shame. It's a very cautious recommend/disappointing not recommend, and even without the port it's not for everyone. But for people that it is for, like myself, Onee Chanbara Origin is a great time.

The controls are intuitive, allowing players to effortlessly execute impressive combos, slashes, and special moves. There's an undeniable satisfaction in slicing through waves of enemies with stylish flair, all while channeling the power of the game's fierce and badass heroines.The game embraces its B-movie horror aesthetic, resulting in a visually striking experience. _childDocuments_.review: This game is a loose remake (aka reboot) of the first two Onechanbara games (released on PS2 and localized as  and  in the West), it takes us all the way to the beginning and tells the origin story of the main duo, two sisters named Aya and Saki.I'm not a hardcore fan and my only frame of reference is the previous game, . Compared to it Origin is a huge improvement in most areas, be it graphics, combat depth or story presentation. The game now has proper motion captured cutscenes instead of the comic/visual novel styled ones in Z2, and the combat system was completely overhauled. Overall, the combat was slowed down considerably in an attempt to make the game play more like a spectacle fighter (aka Devil May Cry style) instead of musou (Dynasty Warriors style).There's now a proper jump (and double jump) instead of the fly-towards-the-nearest-enemy thing. Heavy and ranged attacks have been replaced by kicking (which fills up the enemy's stun bar). B/Circle is now used for parrying. Every single attack in the game can be either parried or dodged. (Yes, you can parry bullets with a katana or even just a gloved fist.) Parrying instantly fills the enemy's stun bar, while dodging gives you a second of slow-mo (for a possible counter attack) as well as a boost to your Xtasy gauge (used for specials). Dodging frames are very generous and the game has abundant cues (both visual and audio), so dodging kind of trivializes the difficulty. Parrying is harder and doesn't seem as useful, outside of one shotting mudmen. Still, it's possible to demolish a whole group of enemies by starting with one carefully timed parry and following it up with a chain of finishers.The combos are still very simple however, it's XXXXX etc, and leveling up just extends the combo. You can spice it up a bit by opening your combo with a kick or sweep or switching weapons mid-combo, but the real skill is in timing each press to execute a "cool combo" that does more damage and auto-wipes your sword. The "cool combo" training meter can now be turned on even outside the practice mode, making the mechanic a lot less obtuse. And you can also buy a ring (for a pretty reasonable price) to extend the "cool combo" frames.There are 3 playable characters, each with 2 weapons, for 6 playstyles/movesets in total. You can take 2 characters on a mission and swap between them at any time. The inactive character will be tagging along, but won't contribute to combat, outside of occasionally pulling aggro. They will regenerate their health over time, however. Worth noting, switching between characters and weapons is almost completely seamless now and can be done at almost any time, even mid-combo. Xtatic (aka Devil Trigger from Devil May Cry) forms from Z2 are back, even though it doesn't make sense story wise to have them here in the prequel.As a side note, it's interesting how the series reacted to the changing moral trends. Z2 is definitely a more sexual game with extensive fanservice, barely any story and somewhat bimbofied characters. Origin, on the other hand, is more serious (while still being sexy and featuring some gorgeous and risqué outfits), has a real story with both funny and sad moments, but what's more curious is it's also a lot more violent. For whatever reason, Saki is especially sadistic now, most of her finishers are straight up Mortal Kombat tier where she rips enemies apart with loud sounds of breaking bone and innards flying everywhere. Sex bad, violence good, I guess?The main story campaign is only about 5 hours long. There's a lot of story scenes and many boss fights, and it doesn't feel repetitive at all, but it's a bit too short. After that you unlock bonus missions (with some more story and voice acted cutscenes), harder difficulty modes (there are 4 in total, the final one is pretty cool and lets you stay in the Xtatic form indefinitely), infinite survival mode (aka Bloody Palace from Devil May Cry) and a bonus character (Lei, aka Reiko in the original games). _childDocuments_.review: This might be subjective, but I very much like the new anime art style. For one, the main character artist is Katsumi Enami, known for her artwork in recent Nihon Falcom games. The new art style, which is far from generic anime, really breathes life into Aya and Saki’s designs. One of the strengths of anime art styles is making emotions more prominent on characters’ faces, and this game is no different. You can really see the sadness in Aya’s eyes and the stubbornness in Saki’s. The world settings are a lot more vibrant as well, as are the blood and gore effects.  is a really pretty game and will no doubt age well. Also, a quick shoutout to Aya and Saki’s new Xtatic Form appearances. Their Xtatic Forms from  looked a bit strange (Saki’s looked especially ugly), but in , they’re fantastic. Although there are slight demonic features, Aya’s form is pretty damn sexy, while Saki is still very cute (must be because they maintained that adorable fringe).Surprisingly, the story is pretty decent by  standards. It isn’t  levels of storytelling quality, but the story it sets to tell is simple and straightforward, yet kind of relatable. Unlike, the first game where the story starts out with Saki killing her father and Aya going on a revenge quest (not much more detail there, except zombies), ’s story starts out with Aya on a search for her missing father and sister Saki. She eventually finds her father, but he tells her that her sister is being controlled by an evil woman and that Saki is trying to kill Aya in order to take her heart to resurrect her mother. Aya’s family being part of a cursed ancestry called the Baneful Bloodline is a major plot device for the story, but the story itself is not really serious or dark. For one, Aya’s whole family is made up of assassins adept at killing zombies. There is no fear to be had there. Also, at a later point in the story, Aya meets up with Saki and Lei, having lighthearted and humorous conservations, all whilst during gameplay and the player battling zombies. There are also a few very anime battle cutscenes as well. I really love those. My theory for why I feel that the story is pretty decent is that it takes an unoffensive, generic anime approach to storytelling. This is far from a bad thing. As a mild anime fan, I certainly enjoyed 's story. The story’s themes of reconnecting with family and sisterhood are nice as well, as is the cliched but tried-and-true theme of vengeance at the near end of the story.Simply put, this is the best  combat system to date, even better than ’s. To summarize, the streamlined but satisfying player character mechanics are paired well with well-designed enemies and bosses. Although combos are streamlined from , they are very satisfying to pull off with a weighty feeling to each swing of the sword. Cool Combinations, a series staple, are also easier to time. Throw in mid-combo dodges, Reloads, parries, combo chaining, weapon switching and character switching and you’ve got yourself a simple but satisfying combo system. In addition, player attacks seem to have taken on a new philosophy. What I mean is that nearly all player attacks have this forward momentum of attacking, moreso than previous games, even . It’s difficult to explain, but there seems to be a bit of /, minus the enemy behavior of being blown away by attacks. I suppose in a sense combat feels more realistic this way. What I think I’m trying to say is that combat this time around has a visceral feeling to its crowd combat gameplay. It feels really good to constantly move forward while slicing zombies into pieces. In a sense, Aya and Saki almost become ballet dancers of death during combat. Go into Xtatic mode, and then maybe that thought might click.Enemies and bosses are very well designed this time around. Regular enemies actually pose a challenge, and bosses are no longer unstaggerable walls of meat. Well, if you’re able to get them into a stagger state anyway. Contrary to what many people think, the Parry, a new defensive option, is not at all garbage, and is key to making bosses stagger. Learn the ins and outs of the Parry’s mechanics well and thank me later. Aside from that, bosses are fun to fight. The number of different enemy types is small, but the different enemy properties is much more important, making battles with different enemy assortments more unique.The third playable character, Lel, is fun to play as and very unique compared to Aya and Saki.This is something that must be known. It seems that in Tamsoft’s pursuit of greater polish and balance for the latest  title, the amount of story and afterstory content had to take a hit. The main story can be beaten within 5 hours, with cutscenes. There’s only one Bonus Mission, Infinite Survival, unless you purchase the 10 other DLC Bonus Missions. Extra costumes, which had historically been in-game unlockables for previous games, are now only purchasable through DLC. The only in-game unlockables now are Rings, BGMs, and artwork. I am a proponent of “Quality over Quantity”, but it’s a shame that  goes back on some series traditions.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fan service game, and one which prioritizes this over anything else.The combat is a missed opportunity. Your attacks and blocks require you to commit to them, ie. once you use them you're stuck in the animation until they finish. This leaves it with a not-too-nice feel where it isn't fluid and reactive (like let's say Fate/Extella) while also not being tactical and calculated (like let's say Dark Souls).If you mistime a block, then tough luck, you're now stuck in the animation until it finishes while the enemy keeps pummeling you. Reacting to further attacks right after the animation ends is then even worse, as the enemy attacks again just before the failed block animation ends, meaning your next block will fail again.This leaves you with the only option, a dodge, which can succeed, but often doesn't get you enough distance, meaning you just get hit again.Honestly, I could go on and on about the combat for ages (I'm rewriting this review for about the 5th time now). While it might get better if you learn the enemy patterns and dodge timings, it's still a hack'n'slash game where spamming attacks among a group of enemies is more effective anyway, and boss fights just need you to get at least some perfect blocks to be winnable (on normal difficulty).From what I've tried, beating this game on the harder difficulties seems quite challenging and could be more fun, but making even a single mistake there just snowballs into more and more frustration where I just don't even want to bother because of the annoying combat system.You probably don't go into this game for the story, and if you do, don't expect much. Or rather, don't expect anything. The story revolves around your character, your long-lost younger sister and the rest of your family. It's based in a modern time where the world is infested with zombies and that's about it.The story is there only to move you from one fight to the next, the characters are completely hollow with unrealistic interactions. The plot twists, if they can be called that are predictable and boring.Overall just an action hack'n'slash game focused mainly on fan service which lacks in every aspect I've experienced so far. Only get this if you want to suffer through the combat system to achieve mastery of the harder difficulties this game can provide, which would imo be quite commendable if you beat.Otherwise consider buying a game like Fate/Extella, Senran Kagura: Estival Versus or DEAD OR SCHOOL. They are cheaper, full of fan service, with at least somewhat coherent story and WAY better and more enjoyable gameplay

_childDocuments_.review: This game has surprisingly refined mechanics. While comparatively simplistic to other action titles such as DMC or MGRR, the kinetic feedback in this game has plenty of visual impact and is the main reason why this game is so addicting. Additionally, context sensitive defensive actions such as dodging and parrying feel extremely satisfying as there is unique animation for timing a dodge correctly. Despite the enemies being mostly zombies, they are reasonably aggressive to the point where you cannot ignore your defensive options, especially for some early bosses as well as later on in the story. While the moves list is pretty short, the game has a tag mechanic that allows you to seamlessly switch between two characters mid-combo adding flavor to a rather simplistic combat system. However, this feature is not available to the player until half-way through the main story. Additionally, there is a mechanic that rewards you for timing your strikes known as the cool-combo system. It is mainly there to reward players for not mindlessly button-mashing as executing a cool combo allows you to extend certain combo strings as well as increasing the damage output of each hit. This system is pretty hard to master without a certain ring equipped, even for an action-game veteran such as myself. This game is not without its flaws however. The lip-syncing in ENG is noticeably off and some levels are just back-tracking the same levels you have already played near the end of the game. I recommend buying the deluxe edition on sale for the bonus missions as well as outfits as the base game is pretty bare bones in terms of content and customization. If you already bought the base version and want all the DLC, unfortunately buying the deluxe edition is the cheapest way to get all the DLC, even if the purchase seems redundant. Overall, I thoroughly enjoyed this game and hope to see this series continue in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The Onee Chanbara series is a well-crafted action game franchise that boasts challenging gameplay, but suffers from cheap environmental graphics and overly sexualized character designs. Despite the suggestive costumes, the game does not contain any explicit sexual content and the story centers around the relationships and sisterhood of the main characters, with very few male characters present. The story itself is poorly written and the character dialogue is often nonsensical and unrealistic.What sets this game apart from others in the genre is its high level of complexity and difficulty. The game system reads controller input on a frame-by-frame basis, and perfect combos require precise input within 1-3 frames, or 0.0167-0.05 seconds. The strongest and most useful attacks are typically found at the end of combos, so if you fail to execute the perfect combo, you will not be able to perform these powerful moves. Additionally, the dodge and parry mechanics are challenging, requiring intense input frames, but these can be made easier with the acquisition of certain items later in the game.The newer game "Onee chanbara Origin" features simpler combo lists and items compared to "Onee chanbara Chaos Z2." The new parry feature in Origin, while riskier, allows for longer stun times on opponents.Overall, if you enjoy intensive action games, this series is worth checking out. However, if you're looking for explicit content, this game is not the right fit. A minor bug is present that can be easily fixed by adjusting settings on your graphics card control panel. Other than that, the game runs smoothly.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty neat addition to the OneeChanbara franchise. It's exactly as you expect:  a stupid-fun hacky slashy blood mess featuring strong female characters in bikinis/etc.  The anime style is pretty well done and helps it stand apart from a certain raunchy-in-a-different-way anime game from the same devs.  My greatest fear for this game was that Tamsoft might have sold-out and tried to make this game channel Senran Kagura.  Luckily that is the total Opposite of what the case actually is.  This game has its own personality and keeps true to the formula of the franchise while subjecting us to plot that seems to hold itself together and ACTUALLY makes sense!!  The main story took me about 6 hours to clear, which seems longer than the usual in the OneeChanbara series :D  You then have the usual bonus missions and activity challenges that reward you with bgm's/items/artwork/etc.  Everything is correct here.Technical: minor gripes(I'm running a 2080 super with a Ryzen 7 3700x, with a spicy 32gb of RAM)Overall I had a pretty good experience for my initial run-through, though there were a couple of mild problems with this port.The pc port seems to suffer similar issues to what Senran Kagura Burst Renewal's pc port suffered.  The game could run in the highest quality with a super computer, and the frames still seem to jitter.  (This really only seemed noticeable in cutscenes.  I've never really had an issue with this in gameplay. The actual in-game choreography and action looked buttery as ever to me, though I acknowledge that not everybody else seems to be having the same luck).  The game did not crash for me until AFTER I've beaten the story and was fooling around in the main menu after having finished a bonus mission.  Honestly, I have no idea how to gauge these crashes between how my game crashed and reading everybody else's reviews.Overall/Takeaway:  I had a really fun time re-acclimating myself to the pacing of these games while seeing what Tamsoft built for us this time!  Now we need to see what they'll do for Kagura and Saaya!  <3 If you are a fan of the previous games OR are looking for a weird-seemingly-sexual-game that actually takes itself seriously and makes barely any in-game mention to the clothing choices, Check this one out!  (Just grab a community performance patch if one exists already!)

Its a fundamentally flawed combat system that effectively punishes you for using the majority of your moveset, not helped by most stages being so short that by the time you DO enter your super-super-mode, the map is over. _childDocuments_.review: While this review will be positive I'll divide it into two segments, the game and the port, because it needs to be done due to several technical issues present at the time of this writing.OneeChanbara Origins is a remake of the first two games in the series. As a matter of fact though, it ican be considered also a partial reimagining as both storylines come into one and the overall plot has been partially rewritten to be more campy anime hack'n slash and less Japanese pseudo survival horror with hack'n slash elements. The key element here is less Japanese, more generic anime. Which can be considered bad for the purists of the series, but really good for everyone else who is just starting out with hack'n slash or wants to pick it up as an entry point to the franchise.The gameplay is very solid, rewarding, and exhilarating. The player controls 2 characters that can be swapped to be the active partner at any point during combat, the other "inactive" character will be passive after finishing the combos started by the player. The protagonist, Aya, can dodge, change weapons, jump, run, parry, and perform aerial as well as ground combos intertwined with her sister Saki to make seemingly endless chains of attacks that destabilize the opponent and put them into stun status for gory glory kills.The fighting styles of the two sisters are unique and require actual effort from the player to adapt if so desired: Aya is quick, has a huge dodging ability, and very easy combos, while Saki is slow, has a terrible dodge and heavier combos but she rewards methodical parry and precise evasion with a massive range and amazing critical potential.Both girls can equip rings that will grant them special abilities, and use items purchased via cellphone that will either heal them or increase some of their stats. It wouldnt be a slashing game without a berserk mode that changes the girl's visuals and enhances their strength. This special mode can be achieved by accumulating enough blood after killing enemies via the Stain Gauge. Since this is technically a sequel to Z2 Chaos in terms of gameplay, the dev team has implemented also the secondary berserk form and all the basic moves the two sisters could perform in the previous entries. And this is much needed as the original Oneechanbara games were absolutely terrible in this regard. Veterans of te series from the PS2 days will certainly remember the clunky animations, terrible hitboxes and atrocious level design. All of that is a thing of the past. Origins also rewrites the levels and scenarios to make them easier on the senses for the Western audience and newbies, which also means putting them in line with the arcade feeling of the newer entries. No more key hunting from random zombies in large city blocks. Yes I'm that old, I still remember.The sound design is very good, the dub is really great for the product at hand, despite some lines being recorded in different studios (the quality varies a bit from line to line) and the music, as always, fits the themes perfectly.Overall the game is fantastic. It's that guilty pleasure other anime musou cant fulfill, truly the best choice in this genre. It has enough personality and uniqueness to distinguish itself from the rest and it's a lot of fun. I'll be honest, this port is garbage. Complete utter crap. Considering how well Z2 ran, and it was a freaking emulated arcade game, there is zero excuse for the devs to be releasing a game in this state in 2020. The Japanese notoriously dont know how to make PC games (or ports in this case). Before I discovered a fix by chance on a random forum, the game had framerate issues and audio stuttering that prevented me from even going past the menu screen. Framerate drops still occur throughout the adventure, as well as audio stuttering when there's geometry streaming in between levels. Dynamic shadows have ridiculously small range, there are memory access errors crashing the game randomly and the resolution options cant be properly used. This game refuses to go Fullscreen. Borderless or nothing.Also the mouse remains on screen for some reason, and the only way to move 3D models to see the new outifts for the girls in the menus is mouse panning as the analogic sticks of the pad dont work.I didnt expect it to be this messy. Really poor job at optimizing such ancient tech, as the visuals are barely above PS3 standards and it should really run like butter on a modern PC at 200 fps minimum (Origins allows for max 60 fps though, and barely so).Tamsoft needs to fix their crap and release a patch ASAP because having such a little gem in this poor state is unforgivable.

_childDocuments_.review: Once again, I am unable to immediately get my point across with Steam's default recommendation system, because it doesn't have a meh option to choose instead of the usual "recommended" and "not recommended".Make no mistake, I actually quite enjoyed my time with Onee Chanbara Origin. Yet while the game was very fun to play and is a massive improvement over the previous installment, it does have a problematic PC port and is definitely not worth the asking price.Do note that the review was written after a complete playthrough on Normal difficulty + a few missions on hard mode to evaluate the unlockables and combat further.I have to clarify something: I don't like Onechanbara Z2: Chaos. To me, that game looked like if someone look at some gameplay footage of Dyansty Warriors and Devil May Cry, then said "Yeah, I can make my own version of those... WITH ADDED BOOBS". Onee Chanbara Origin manages to fix most of my issues with the previous game, turning it into an actually competent hack and slash and actually making me want to give the previous game another chance with the experience I've gotten playing it.For starters, the game now has a good learning curve and teaches stuff more efficiently. Instead of just throwing you in an introductory battle with no proper instructions and then teaching a lot of the mechanics in the very first level like Z2: Chaos did, this game takes its time and introduces new features whenever it feels you have mastered the previous ones.The gameplay itself is also very refined this time around, a far cry from what Z: Chaos was. On the surface, it feels like just another button mashing hack and slash game, but the more you use the different combat mechanics, you can see the action is now very fast and fun, despite being a bit mindless at times. You can dodge the enemies' attacks with a cinematic bullet time on successful ones, or you can parry them to stun enemies and leave them open to finishers. You can stick to one character and just bring in the second one whenever you start running out of health, or you can begin attacking and immediately bring the other character in to chain attacks or to prevent powered up forms from running out of time, with no cooldowns imposed on it. There are just three problems with the gameplay. To start, the unlockables don't feel rewarding. Most of the gallery contents are locked behind very grindy missions, the extra missions that you unlock after beating the game is actually one survival mode and more of the same missions you had to experience during the main game (only with more useless story context), and the extra unlockable character not only feels less fun to play than the main characters, but also gets no achievements of her own to encourage playing as her. Second problem is the low variety of enemies. The game goes on for about 4-5 hours of playtime, yet the sheer numbers of enemies it throws at you makes this issue more apparent and by the time you see the same zombie police men army for the 10th time, you will start rolling your eyes. There are only 7 types of enemies in the game, the most annoying type only appearing in one specific stage's finale, and the game's only solution to this issue is the introduction of awakened enemies; basically red aura versions of the same basic enemies that hit hard and absorb your hits like a tank, which doesn't solve this problem at all. And the last problem is that...This game's boss fights are actually the worst thing you can encounter in a hack & slash game. Not because they are broken, but because how boring and badly designed they are. All of them have two or three attacks that they spam constantly, and the only thing you have to do is to dodge or parry them, then counter attack. They might spice up stuff and do some new moves when you deplete %50 of their life bar, but you do some more damage and they go back to what they were doing anyway. None of the bosses in the game, not even the final boss, feel like an actual threat.The only boss fight that is somewhat challenging is the one that happens in middle of your first playthrough, and forces you to use one specific character in xtatic mode. That means your character's health is constantly depleting in exchange for higher damage, and you have to replenish lost health by constantly striking the enemy. Now since you have no secondary character to switch to on your first playthrough, you need to be more careful with your actions or you'll just fail the mission. That is, if you don't already have the automatic revival item to make it trivial anyway.Now comes the next very obvious improvement of this game: the graphical style. This game ditches the realistic look of Z2: Chaos in favor of a more cartoonish/anime look and as a result, gives everything a striking visual style by making them look livelier and more colorful. The only problem is that the game rarely capitalizes on its graphical style.Aside from the first two levels, most of the missions happen in levels that look incredibly bland and with drab color palettes. So much that the main characters look out of place due to how colorful their designs look. It also doesn't help that the the level layouts keep repeating and repeating and repeating. One level you are going through an area, and the next level you are going through the same area, but in reverse. The sewer levels are the worst offenders though, as they make up about one fifth of the total level count and whatever you see in middle of the game, you're gonna see again near the end of it.It's not surprising at this point, just disappointing. If there's one thing that Japanese developers cannot do properly, it's releasing a good PC port and maintaining it by listening to player feedback. And this game is no exception.Onee Chanbara Origin suffers from a very problematic PC port, marred with widespread issues that were never fixed, or fixed partially. The game starts to drop frames every once in a while for no logical reason, has major problems with AMD graphics cards, might crash randomly with %50 chance of save file corruption (forcing you to manually back up your save file), or might even start up in the wrong language. There are community fixes available to remedy the frame drops for Nvidia users, but those who use AMD graphics cards are out of luck.Was the game fun? Yes. Did I enjoy it? Also yes. But honestly, I don't think it's worth buying at full price. With some of the extra missions for the unlockable character being locked behind DLC, your best bet of getting the full game is by purchasing the Deluxe edition. And that edition of the game costs 75 USD, which is really overpriced for what you'll be getting out of this game.I'm no stranger to Japanese games and already know what a big deal it is to get a niche game like this on the global market, and for a more reasonable price rather than the hundreds of dollars you have to pay for purchase and shipping and extra stuff. But it really doesn't justify the pricing here, does it? You can get better games for the same price or less. So if you really want to try this game, get it on a really good sale.Definitely not worth it full price, but a massive improvement over the previous installment of the series and despite some shortcomings, a fun hack and slash game. A shame that the PC port is problematic.

_childDocuments_.review: Shlocky hack and slash fun. As an introduction to the Oneechanbara series, it's serviceable enough and the game packed here is great fun on its own. You'll be battling through waves of zombies and challenging several bosses as you play as Aya, fighting to avenge her family as a zombie slayer. Tons of cool moves, fast gameplay and a neat presentation should be all the more entertaining for your playthrough of the story. Check this out if you're into hack and slash games.
_childDocuments_.name: Onee Chanbara ORIGIN

_childDocuments_.review: I love this series.  It's a straight up hack and slash action with no silly puzzles or annoying collectibles to search for.  The core gameplay is excellent as always, although its previous game, Z2 Chaos, had much more robust move sets.  But what's available in this game is still good and I had a blast playing this.  Also, I'm really digging the new artstyle.  Don't expect any epic story here, as the story is always been the weak link of this series.  But very few games deliver the satisfying feeling of cutting down zombies into pieces like this one does.  Also, I'm glad Saya got her prowrestling moves back.  I missed suplexing zombies in Z2 Chaos and I was glad it came back in this game.  One warning though, a lot of people have mentioned that there is a bug that causes save data to get corrupted, so I've been diligently making back ups for it after each session.  It hasn't happened to me yet, but I suggest you would do the same if you decide to play this.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid brainless action game with sexy girls, what's more to want?Well, difficulty would be one thing. I started on hard and it was fun but challenging for a bit, but fairly quickly got to the point that you die instantly if you don't have 100% perfect execution (which is an extremely tight window). I finally gave up and tried again on normal... and you can basically just ignore the enemies completely, mashing x to win.So yea, if you want either a completely hellish challenge, or some braindead fanservice, this game is for you. Don't expect anything in between though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very straight foward game: you have the anime waifus, it's very linear, blood/gore, the music is pretty good, intense combat, is a hack & slash and it has some drama on the story which I enjoyed a lot, nice graphics and, last but not least, the story is a remake of the Onee Chanmbara 1 and 2.I bought the game with all the bundles and I don't regret any of it. The real problem is that there is a chance to lose all your progress and even Gabe Newell can't save you with his cloud system. So, if you are considering to buy this game, make as an habit to create a backup of your savegame.Another thing is that I suggest you checking on the web if your system has any problem with this game and which are the measures that you need to do to play it very smooth. I use a low end GPU and the game runs at 60 fps, but I have read that even a RTX 3060 can have problems here. Keep that in mind.If you can handle all those issues, then I recommend you playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed Onee Chanbara ORIGIN... but not without many many MANY hardships. It is a difficult game, but there was more difficulty properly setting it up. The PC version is infamous with having audio issues. The audio is delayed to the point that it messed up with my timing constantly as it is important to listen to audio cues at all times, making it somewhat unplayable for me until I fixed the issue. What I got in the end is... animu bikini princess Devil May Cry I guess. It doesn't feel like a ripoff, which is great! Soundtrack is pretty good (I'm currently looking for a decent download), and the gameplay is pretty addictive. Story is not exactly the forte, and it does get pretty goofy at times, but what did you expect? A deep narrative in a game where the main character is an animu samurai in a bikini and a cowboy hat? Of course, story is secondary (or tertiary) as the main focus is obviously on the gameplay. Is the gameplay good though? YES! Hence why I compared it to Devil May Cry or even Metal Gear Rising: Revengence as there is an emphasis on katanas. A perfect dodge system à la Bayonetta, swordplay and even a finisher system à la Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, and sibling rivalry that drives the story interlinked with surreal things happening à la Devil May Cry (additionally, one sister is red and the other is blue)... and you're a scantily clad female protagonist in a zombie setting à la Lollipop Chainsaw. Can you blame me for seeing similarities here and there? I recommend this, but it's rather difficult. I did my first run with no items whatsoever, and it's definitely doable, but I came close to dying many times. As a result, the gameplay may seem repetitive, but that's because you definitely have to improve your craft as you progress. Ultimately, it felt a lot like Metal Gear Rising to me, and I liked that game A LOT. I liked this game too definitely!

_childDocuments_.review: Onee Chanbara: Origin was an impulse buy for me, not familiar with the series other than seeing one of the earlier titles in a Gamestop years ago as a kid but after hearing about this title a few months back and seeing as its a reboot I figured now would be a good time to give it a try. And I'm glad I did!The 6 hours at time of this review was all in one sitting, once I started Story mode I just couldn't put it down. Typically hack-n-slashers grow boringly repetitive quickly (looking at you Dynasty Warriors...) but OCO didn't, despite the combo list for characters being so small, the combat doesn't really feel like a mindless button-masher. Figuring out the timing for the "cool combo" variants of your attacks is satisfying as all hell thanks to the added flair you're rewarded with which also helps keep the animations from growing stale. Mixing in your evade and blocks, combat feels all around fluid and is visually appealing (and that's without the fan-service  considered!) and each characters fighting style is unique to keep it fresh. Add in that you can switch between the 2 party members on the fly and mid-combo, and you got yourself a combo-multipliers dream! The story mode is short - I beat it in those 6 hours on Normal, but thanks to NG+ I can't really say the length is a negative. It's quick, a tad melodramatic but the main characters are endearing enough to get you invested enough to enjoy it. There are additional missions as DLC but I can't speak to their quality as of now, but will probably pick them up at a later time! Other game modes include "Practice" which is exactly what it sounds like; select which enemies you want to fight, standard grunts or even bosses, and go ham! "Survival" is fighting waves of enemies for as long as you can, and getting to Wave 101 willl unlock the 3rd playable character Rei (or you could buy the unlock DLC). I really can't say much in terms of "negatives", the only thing that I can really knock this game for is how BAD the lip-sync is in cutscene's when playing with English audio. Remember  the old martial arts movies or original Godzilla's on back in the day and the actors mouths kept flapping after the lines? Yeah, expect that along with some silent (mistimed maybe?) bodily expressions. Easy fix is just play with the native Japanese audio - though you may miss dialog during gameplay when people talk during combat but meh, nothing really all that important. Subtitles appear, but good luck reading while fighting the Undead!All in all, this game was a welcome and pleasant surprise - looking forward to this franchises future!

_childDocuments_.review: This is for the $50 version of the game.The Good:- Fun gameplay with very visceral controls- Tons of mechanics that feel natural and that are easy to pick up. - The mechanics also just feel good. Dodging or parrying a shotgun blast just feels amazing.- Super stylish- Decent music overall- Bosses are fun- Aya's transformed butt- System requirements are more lenient than advertised- A lot of the series' typical jank is gone. The Bad:- Unlocking Lei either takes insane grinding that isn't worth it or unlocking for $4. - Takes some effort to get the game running well (set VSync to "fastest")- Fairly low enemy variety. - Not as fun as Z2: Chaos, but still good (same for music).- Most environments are blandOverall:It's probably the "tightest" Onechanbara game. It's also the most mechanically complex. The dodge and parry system works extremely well. It's a lot of risk vs reward. Parries stun enemies, but are harder to execute. Dodges just look cool and help avoid damage. Also, the parry finally makes mudmen easy to deal with. The combat is slower than Z2 Chaos, but it's good in its own way.The game's look varies wildly. Sometimes it looks like a PS4 game. At other times, it looks like it's on the PS2/360 again. In general, it has great character models, but crappy environments. Everyone is cell shaded, now. It's honestly not a bad look for the series. The story is decent, and the VAs are all talented. Yu Kobayashi does great, but she always does. She steals the show. I find it weird that Aya's VA changed, but she was still in the game as another character. I suppose she was just too busy to do all of the lines. That said, no one phones it in.All of the boss fights are fun or at least decent. The one on one fights with human are really the best ones. They really let you flex those dodge and parry skills. They're also heart-pounding, even if they are a tad easy.The Bottom Line:Is it worth $50? I would say so. The campaign is ~5h long and the gameplay is fun. There's definitely some replayablilty in there. If you're looking for something somewhat short, fun, and something you can come back to, this is a good buy.

_childDocuments_.review: In the year 20XX AD, Tokyo is nothing but a dystopic wasteland overrun by living corpses known as the Undead. Here we find two sisters who descend from a long line of expert swordsmen, yet were born to different mothers. The elder sister, Aya, was raised by her father, who subjected her to rigorous training in the way of the blade. Meanwhile, the younger sister, Saki, was raised by her mother, learning to despise her father for abandoning them and taking her sister away. When her father goes missing, Aya decides to put her skills with the sword to use as an Undead-hunter. Upon her beloved mother's murder, Saki becomes consumed to the point of insanity with a desperate thirst for revenge, resorting to manipulating the Undead to achieve her goal.Aya resolves to seek out her younger sister, her only surviving relation, while Saki is determined to resurrect her mother using an ancient art passed down through the ages. This art, however, requires the heart of a blood relative to work, meaning that the younger sister must kill the elder if she is to have her sworn vengeance. And so, amidst a swirling storm of love, hate, and intrigue, the battle between the two sisters begins.

name: Paper Beast
detailed_description: Wishlist us! About the Game An adventure and exploration game about wildlife in a dreamlike universe. Somewhere in the abyssal depths of the internet, life has blossomed. You are the first human to set foot in this mysterious ecosystem. A strange force seems to weigh on its balance. Join forces with intriguing and endearing creatures to solve the puzzles of Paper Beast. GAME EXPERIENCE Explore a colorful and whimsical universe born from the imagination of Eric Chahi, creator of Another World . Two game modes: the adventure and the sandbox, an immersive playground. Explore a world populated by majestic and intelligent creatures. Grab them, help them: their behaviour adapts to your actions. Control the environment. The gameplay is based on a unique physics engine. Divert rivers, melt the ice, withstand storms to solve puzzles… And fly away! Experiment! In the sandbox, live an experience close to a god game. Terraform mountains, dig lakes, populate your ecosystem, unleash tornadoes. Have fun with the physics of the game. An original soundtrack combining the Japanese punk rock of TsuShiMaMire and the ambient style of Roly Porter.

_childDocuments_.review: This is not a simulation - this is Another World if there ever was one. This game is 10/10 and you could say Alyx-class entertainment. But this isn't just entertainment, this is VR art. And it's a celebration of life. You do have some God-like abilities, but mainly to facilitate events. Not sure if you can die - I don't think you can (at least I have not done so), and the story part of this experience may be seen as some sort of adventure game unlike anything you've ever experienced before.This may be one of the first (or best) VR games where you truly transform (part of) landscapes - and therefore polygon levels seem very high. Texture quality is great, not 4K-ish like Boneworks, Alyx and Room VR, but you usually don't get that close to the in-game animals. When you do, I was still amazed by the texture quality. Sound is awesome using Index speakers, but - maybe - most of all I enjoyed the in-game shadows. Shadows are incredibly detailed, not sure even Lone Echo or Alyx did that better. There's full locomotion and/or teleport, and snap or smooth turning.Using Index, I'm forcing res 200% and the best possible image quality, still the game performs at a close to perfect 90 fps - using a heavily oc'ed GTX 1080 and i7 7700K (16GB 3200 Mhz). That is, I mostly got 90 fps, it dips here and there, but it's not a problem. In short, performance, visuals and story content are amazing. If this experience does not blow you away, maybe not much will in life ;-) I'm thankful to the devs for creating this experience - and no, I don't know the devs and I paid the full price for this game.
