_childDocuments_.review: Paper Beast is an interesting game in that it isn't trying to tell a proper story, as much as it's simply relaying an idea that doesn't really start to show up until the last 1/3 of the game.  I found this really interesting since even when I'd play Alyx or some other god-tier VR title, I still always knew I was a dude holding two hunks of plastic in a room somewhere.  But Paper Beast was the first time I actually kinda believed that I might actually be somewhere else.  Not in a delusional way of course, but it's wild to see how far imagination on its own can teleport someone.  It's painfully gorgeous and the gameplay mechanics always hit.  There wasn't even that one particular annoying puzzle, each one was well done and even then, I spent a ton of time in the Sandbox mode that came out of nowhere to be one of my favorite things in VR.  If you want to remember why you bought a headset in the first place, buy this game immediately.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: [initial review after 1.5 hours, 2nd review after completion follows, scroll down for it...] Paper Beast is not quite like anything else, which I guess is why I'm enjoying it so much.The world is somewhat open (though the player is herded into a fairly narrow pathway through it) and feels spacious.  The low-poly graphics are almost abstract, yet well-lit enough and with good enough ambient sound support to feel convincing and provide immersion.  Lighting and sky effects are remarkably good, with dawn/sunset fx and thunderstorms over a vast desert landscape.  Water doesn't really try to be realistic, yet is remarkably wet and believable.  Occasional "special" items in the landscape cause instant teleportation to nearby spots.  It's a world of constant discoveries.  My initial experience was a delightful sense of disorientation and wonder, like walking into a strange but enjoyable dream.The fantastic Dada-esque animals are the essential feature though, and they're simply wonderful:  clearly related to familiar creatures like wolves, horses, elk, jellyfish, crabs and so on, yet weirdly different and all apparently made of paper.  Though their forms are abstract and surreal, their body language and sounds are strangely lifelike and affecting.  They convey wariness, alarm, weariness, thirst, busy purpose, confusion, a whole spectrum of moods and emotions.Best of all, (so far) I have encountered no creature that can harm me or shows any intention of harming me.  Instead, they go about their natural business and my task is to help them, sometimes rescue them, other times gently manipulate them into modifying the environment to assist my forward progress.  This increases the gentle and dreamlike quality of the gameplay;  eventually I start to feel a kinship with these creatures large and small.  I enjoy watching them and trying to figure out what they're doing.  I feel pity and sorrow and a real sense of urgency when they're in distress, and genuine satisfaction when I can rescue them.I have no idea what the overall campaign is;  so far, I've progressed slowly, savouring every moment.  I know I'll be sorry when this game is over, so I'm in no hurry.  The animal NPCs seem to have their own AI logic and respond interactively to each other and to my movements and actions;  there are no canned dialogues.  Even though I can't help noticing that I'm being herded or guided on a defined path through the scenery, the fresh and interesting behaviours of the animals make each new puzzle area entertaining.The puzzles are not terribly difficult, at least so far.  You have to learn to think in the game's logic, which is to perturb the ecosystem around you just enough to get the animals' natural behaviour to work to your advantage (think Joel Salatin of Polyface Farm explaining the "pigness of the pig" and the "chicken-ness of the chicken").  I won't say more than that because this game is too beautifully realised to spoil for any new player.  Like some of the great literature of childhood, the first "reading" (playthrough) is a truly magical experience that would be spoilt by foreknowledge.Highly recommended for animal lovers, explorers, puzzle solvers, amateur or professional naturalists, and those with a taste for the unusual and creative in game design.  So far, I would say this game is suitable for most ages, certainly 12 and up.  It might be a little scary for very young players.  (Note:  the opening sequence or intro is really weird and not representative of the rest of the game!).  I look forward to spending a few more hours in this fantastic (literally) world and know it will be over too soon...  Huge props to the developers who have achieved something very fine here, an original work of art and not "just another VR game."[additional thoughts after another 5 hours]When I got to the end of this game and realised it was the end (those are the credits scrolling upward in the starry distance) I confess for a moment I wanted to cry.  The atmosphere of the final chapter was beautiful and melancholy to start with, and then I was so damn sad that the game was over...Words cannot do justice to this amazing work of art.  It's surreal, mysterious, alien... and yet the behaviour of the various creatures is absolutely familiar.  It may be an alien ecosystem I'm observing, but I know it's an ecosystem :-)  trees bear fruit, plants grow, animals diligently work to modify their environments.  And the body language of the animals is so perfectly captured, so true to actual creatures in real life, that despite their highly stylised Daliesque construction (they are all made of "folded paper") they are completely alive and realistic.  They are realistic in a way that transcends accurate representation, and this I think is what makes this game so darned special.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I firmly believe this is the game to change the future of VR. Yes, HL: Alyx was the most well-recognised recent step into AAA VR titles, but this game shows that effort and heart can be poured into such a game without the weight of an already established intellectual property behind it. Paper Beast stands on its own and succeeds in everything it tries to achieve.There is a moment early in the story, standing in a blackened cave, hearing the wind whistle from a gap to the crisply thunderous and opaque outside world. Just the notion that you're led to this location because you can hear the DIRECTION the wind is coming from shows that this game could never have been any form of success outside of VR. It uses every aspect of the 'present' experience of VR to its advantage. And so this game curates an experience of unique curiosity; of turning your head and stepping towards a dark and windy crack in the cave wall to be met with a vast, oily, pitch-dark ocean swelling and crashing below you, lightning illuminating the twists of video-tape seaweed just below the surface through the peaks of the waves. And what can you do with it? Nothing. It's untouchable. This game takes advantage of a great irony; that modern games (particularly open worlds) have the mantra of "You see that in the distance? You can go there," whereas in reality such a notion is unrealistic and rarely the case. This game (in a medium such as VR which is designed to make as much of the experience as 'touchable' as possible) makes an effort to give you the same small, existential feeling that you might get watching fireworks, or witnessing the untouchable grandeur of crashing oceans or salmon pink skies. It uses your presence in a very tactile world to show you things entirely untouchable and yet incredibly palpable. On top of that, everything you DO interact with in the world suddenly has so much value too! I wish the story could have gone on for twice as long, but thankfully collectibles which add characters and environmental objects to the sandbox mode still draw you back to keep playing, plus the variety of puzzles and levels leave you wanting to re-experience the world anyway. Paper Beast understands VR. It's not trying to port existing genres into this field of gameplay. It's inventing its own genres.I'll say as a bit of a con against the unfathomable backdrop of pros toward this game, that the '' cliche has already been used A LOT in pop culture and particularly in VR titles and so feels a little on the nose and shallow as a metaphor for something in the game. It feels like it's trying to say something important and thoughtful but I can't put my thumb on it and so makes me feel like it was unnecessary. The game world, the design, the soundscapes, gameplay, creatures (and so on) all hugely stand up on their own and I don't think there is need to find ways to call out on rapturous, philosophical thinking points in a world you're trying to get LOST in.This game is a marvel and is an absolute must-have experience for anybody with a VR headset.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommended.  I had bought the Folded Edition first, but since I got a vr headset a week ago, I thought I might try the vr edition.  Got it in a bundle at Humble and I absolutely love it.  You really have to think and observe what's going on around you.  It's definitely unique gameplay and beautiful to look at.  I loved the vr version the best, but the Folded Edition, which is also available on Steam, is just as good.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully designed. It takes you on a Dali-sequel safari through desert lands where you interact with different animals who you enlist to help you move along the journey. The game is a light puzzler with huge payoffs when you complete a section. One in particular took my breath away and left me with a 5 minute sense of wonder. The game starts off a little slow and there are no instructions. But once you figure out how to explore and experiment, it starts making sense. This is a unique experience that you can not experience anywhere else except in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: In short, this game is entirely unique, I have never played anything like it, and I'm happy to have gone through it. It's a puzzle adventure exploration type of game, with exotic games systems.All in all, it's an absolute gem of a game, when it comes to design, systems, user experience. I cannot not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is an interesting experience.The key word being "experience". This product plays more like an interactive art piece, rather than conventional game. You progress through the narrative by solving simple physics-based environmental puzzles. There are collectables as well, but mostly you just navigate to the end of the level, where you load into another map.The whole journey is very abstract and open-ended. If you enjoy stories without real plot, lots of great art and finding meaning in art - you'll probably enjoy this game.On a more technical level, the game has both movement options, snap turning and is well optimised. In addition to the story mode, you also have a sandbox for creating your own little areas and a music visualiser type toy. Personally, I got it from a bundle and I'd recommend getting it on some sort of sale(playtime is only 2.5-3h).
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: That was  game I have played in VR yet.Do not pass this one up. The entire thing is a surreal work of art. It is stunning and beautiful. It's amazing what a small team can accomplish.It worked perfect with a Valve Index. The Japanese punk rock was a nice touch. I was not expecting that. It's short, I finished it in less than 3 hours, but I think that's perfectly fine for a game that basically functions like a living interactive art museum. For those who don't have VR, you can play it pancake, but you shouldn't, because VR is better.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend Paper Beast.There are very few games that leave you with the profound knowledge that your life just got a little richer by the power of the experience they provided. Paper Beast is one of those experiences, fuelled by an amazing animation engine that manages to give life to the abstract chartaceous creatures that accompany you in its world. While the game tells no story in the traditional sense, its scenarious are rich with emotional encounters and will leave you jaw dropped and utterly confused on several occasions. Paper Beast is, however, far more than just an impressive experience. It is also a very solid video game. In the linear campaign you solve a series of physics based environmental puzzles, you shape the terrain by shifting sand and water, you use temperature to freeze and melt, you use light and darkness to lure and to scare away. Unfortunately the game is rather short, with a playtime of under 3 hours. There are, however, achievements, collectibles and a sandbox mode that give an incentive to revisit the game after campaign completion.For a short video review see:
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: The store page classifies this as "An exploration and adventure game", which imho is way off. This is a physics based puzzler set in a trippy paranormal universe.The main gameplay loop through the levels basically consists of moving creatures and/or objects from one area to another. This is accomplished by utilizing objects that have terraforming abilities, connecting objects/creatures to others, or sometimes luring/scaring creatures in a certain direction with objects that act as bait or the opposite.Overall I found it to be quite enjoyable, but slightly janky physics and object manipulation can sometimes make you question whether you're fundamentally chasing the wrong approach, or simply losing an uphill battle against unpolished game mechanics.There are much better physics puzzlers out there, but the otherworldly presentation manages to elevate the experience quite a bit.I'll give it 69%.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is way underpriced. I just finished the main mode, which was an absolute trip, but still have so much more to do thanks to the sandbox mode and mysterious story. Paper Beast is a sitdown VR puzzle/adventure experience which revolves around you assisting the creatures of its world. You'll traverse across mesmerizing landscapes that will beg you to keep exploring. I haven't quite figured out the story behind the game, but it's surprisingly interesting and it did some things I wasn't expecting. The demo gives you the smallest glimpse of the experience, but it's worth checking out if you're on the fence. I wouldn't be though. There's a lot to see and do in Paper Beast. Tons of replayability! For the price of $20 it's an must have for anyone with a VR headset.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic and unique experience. I fell in love with all of the creatures instantly and had a hard time leaving them at the end of the story. Interacting and experimenting with the simple but cleverly built abstract ecosystems was the most fun i had in a long time. This game deserves much more attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It is killing me that people seem to just not be talking about this game?? Most VR stuff I play makes me excited for how good VR is going to be once people figure out what to do with it; this is one of a very small number of things that makes me say "VR is already good". This is amazing on a creative level, and on a technical level; they just brought it all to life so well.I could describe the gameplay, but I don't even have to -- there's a demo!! If you're this far in the review, just get the demo, what else can I possibly tell you. All you need to know is that the full game is *even better* than the demo is. Enjoy.EDIT: might as well take this opportunity to say, minor content warning for some circle-of-life kinda animal death (prey animals being caught by predators), but the creatures are abstract enough that it's not too tough to watch -- I'm sensitive to this stuff and it wasn't too bad. Also, there's absolutely some scary moments, but nothing too startling, it's not a horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: No Left Hand Support...It's nearly 6 month after release and you still can't play it as a leftie.-No option to swap the ingame buttons from right to left controller-No option to swap the "laserpointer" from right to left controller-No option to swap movemente from left to right controller-No option to swap turning from right to left controllerIs this a joke? 6 month! For controller inputs in VR games it MATTERS if you are left or right handed!John Carmack one wrote: "A number of VR developers are still small enough that they don't wind up with a left handed person continuously involved in the development process, resulting in fragile or non-existent support for left handed play. 10% of the population is left handed."
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR games I have played. Absolutely incredible interaction with the game world, with a fantastic music score and visuals to match. The physics system is the best I have seen in any VR game as well. Made me tear up a couple of times which few games have. The sandbox mode is also a welcome addition as it lets you have fun after finishing the story. Everyone at Pixel Reef deserves a pat on the back for the work they put into this piece of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I do not write many reviews but I felt compelled to write one for this game. This is a truly breathtaking experience and is very well created, it looks and feels great in VR and of the many VR titles I have played over the years this is one of the memorable  ones.The story mode is fantastic, a collection of interactive set pieces that have some of the most strange and wonderful visual art I have experienced in VR. The addition of a sandbox mode that unlocks more content to use as you progress through the main story really makes this title worth the asking price and a title that I recommend all VR enthusiasts to try. Two thumbs up
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I've been with many VR games at this point. Most are for a thrill and fun. Sure there are few that manage to captivate me with a very unique experience, But many are just a glorified experience with VR label tagging on it. Luckily Paper Beast, To me, is a few and one of a kind of VR experience.Same as many game you probably have been experience at this point, You are put in a strange world with strange landscape. Far as eye can see dune of sand, Bright blue sky that by staring too long and you can feel like it sucking you in. And strange creatures made out of paper and rock, Roaming the land.Now as I can gather, Mainly, This game is by its core a walking/puzzle  simulator kind of game. Sure there are a "God mode" where you can messing around with creating a little "Biome" to observing the AI interacting with each other, But mainly, This game is about the puzzle experience.The puzzle, To be less extravagant, are very simple. And with VR experience its does help differentiate the game from being boring.....a bit. But what really made up greatly is the environment manipulation and the scenario of each puzzle.I admit that there are certain scenario left me speechless and standing in a great awe I haven't felt since the first time I've red one certain book when I was a child. Its a great experience that probably going to happen to me just once in every while and this game manage to do just that.So yes, I recommended this game with whole heart. It is that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game, of the highest order. I think. Tbh I have no clue what's going on and nothing makes sense but hey that's the point. I think. It has some really really heartbreaking moments (I think they were heartbreaking idk music got very sad and the guy collapses soooo idk) and some really good stuff. I think. Buy it? Idk do you like looking around you going what the ♥♥♥♥ is that, that's glowing and that's paper drinking water because if you do this games for you
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Mostly a walking simulator. yeah, it has puzzles, and has a very interesting art style, but by the end of the day it just isn't for me. Still giving it a thumbs up because if you want to walk around interesting places in vr, and have a few puzzles thrown at you, then this would probably be a really good game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty okay. Just under recommendable. It's a series of surreal animal and plant based puzzles. Sometimes it's not particularly clear what you have to do.The Japanese music was an odd choice for the game but it was cool.There's a lot of downtime in the game. Even when you have the solution to a puzzle it takes time to do it due to the fact you have to wait for animals to walk or throw/move something janky. The level transitions are long balloon rides into nowhere that take like 5 minutes per time. You can steer but it makes no difference because you can't land or go anywhere unintended.It looks like it's building up to some plot at the beginning but then never mentions it again. And then it abruptly ends
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This was the peak VR experience I didn't know existed, didn't know I wanted, and became obsessed with once I tried it out. It's hard to describe; trying too hard to describe it would spoil it. But if you like the idea of a VR experience that's very puzzle-based, gives very few clues on how to solve the puzzles, yet rewards experimenting... this, get this.Wonderful soundtrack too.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Wow. Just... wow. I finished my first play-through and I'm incredibly impressed and moved by this game. The most beautiful thing I have experienced in VR to date, and it literally brought me to tears at one point. I can't wait to go through it again to get all the achievements and unlocks I missed the first time around. Definitely a world I will be returning to for both the story and the sandbox mode. I don't want to spoil anything, but I highly suggest at least giving the demo a try. If that small slice intrigues you the way it intrigued me then consider making the purchase!This is going on my list of must play VR titles for when friends need recommendations. I look forward to seeing more from these developers in the future. Really great stuff here that makes owning a Virtual Reality headset worthwhile. Pros:-Smooth Locomotion and turning options-Awesome physics simulations-Gorgeous yet simplistic visuals-Incredible soundtrack and audio design-Immersion that was off the charts for me-Post story content/incentive to replay chapters-Loveable Paper BeastsCons:-I didn't want the story to end so soonI absolutely love this game! It's a Masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Like a fair few VR games, this one is quite short and better as an experience than as a game (at least the story mode), but if you don't mind that, it's well worth putting in the few hours to experience the world of Paper Beast, which I found to be absolutely unique in terms of aesthetic and atmosphere in all the video games I've played. I can't imagine it working nearly as well in non-VR - for me, the experience was so much about being in this utterly unique, strange and beautiful place and interacting with its creatures.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Love it!  Totally surrealistic environments to explore and manipulate using the local wildlife.  Gives me vibes of From Dust in regard to how you need to change your surroundings and areas you visit, in order to progress.  No aggressive enemies to hurt you or jump scares - just fascinating sights and vistas to explore.  The most interesting stuff for me is the creature models and AI - they really act in surprisingly realistic ways sometimes (despite their appearance) and it totally helps sell the game world.  And of course there are some nifty twists in the story/world but I won't give anything away here.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even remember buying this game, but I gave it a shot, and immediately played through the whole thing.Wonderful experience, but some issues with the controls, at least on the index.If you've played From Dust, you'll have fun with this.EDIT: Well, turns out they both were created by the same person!Sandbox by default gets you to click in the tumbsticks to zoom in and out and fly around, which can negatively affect the life of them, after re-binding to use the thumbpad, I have had no problems.It'd be nice to have a left handed mode, or have the ability to use both hands to pick stuff up / interact (But I feel like that's not how the game is meant to be played, so fair enough)The puzzles were fun, and I didn't have much trouble figuring them out, even though I was stoned to ♥♥♥♥ :)This is easily one of my new VR Favourites.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere and the satisfying world shaping reminded me somewhat of an old Ubisoft game "From Dust", although the mechanics are different and you actually play in first person, which, in my opinion, makes you more immersed into the environment and feel less like a God. Accompanied with the other-worldly sound design and a story that's left for you to understand and intepret, this is one of the strongest an unique VR experiences I've had. I recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece. If 10 out of 10 is perfect, I give Paper Beast a 10 to the power of infinity, its that good. Half Life Alyx was good but this is literally god tier VR magic. From graphical design, music and audio, animation, engagement and story telling, Paper Beast beats anything I’ve ever played over the past 4 years. Paper Beast will blow your mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: wow! I just spent the last hour feeling like I was living in a completely other world.  The Immersion in this is like nothing I've ever experienced before.   Each of these creatures feels truly alive, as if they have a mind and consciousness of their own.  It is so fascinating to watch them go about their business, doing... whatever the heck it is they are doing.  But they know that I am there, which is mind blowing.   The game is gorgeous, and surprising in all of the right places.  At the heart of this game, it is a puzzler.  But figuring out how to continue moving forward using the environment and the behaviors of the creatures is such a new and enjoyable game experience.  You  gotta try this one
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Really pretty and overall nice chill VR game in which you help origami-like creatures with some tasks.It just bugs me that sometimes the process of solving the 'puzzles' (done by the creatures under your guidance) took quite a long time, much longer than finding the necessary solution itself, so it sometimes unnecessarily felt like a waiting game.Also the Walkman achievement in VR is just atrocious (took me about 50 minutes vs 10 in non-VR).I wish this and the "Folded Edition" (the non-VR version) were just a single game with 2 game modes and completely shared data (7.5GB of files on the disk) and achievements, especially that it looks like you get the "Folded Edition" for free anyway when you buy the VR version.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It started out well. Didn't understand what was going on, but its weirdness was intriguing. It just became really boring in the second half of the game instead of getting more interesting. The pacing on some levels was awful; just waiting around for the paper things to move from one end of the map to the other. Maybe I don't get it, but the weirdness didn't get explained at all. My impressions was that the developer started with an interesting, weird idea, didn't know how the "story" will develop, thought they would figure it out on the way, but never did. And then the game ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely otherwordly journey. You explore a world that truly feels alien, befriend some of the wildlife (I'll miss my tall 12-legged friend) and solve environmental puzzles. Some moments, especially the ending, gave me goosebumps.If you have VR and this looks even a little interesting to you, play it! Just don't let the first 2 minutes turn you off the game. It starts out a bit weird, but after that you'll have a fantastic time. And it isn't even that short by VR standards. Took me almost 4 hours, and after that there's a sandbox that might or might not interest you enough to play a bit more.Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I've been searching for VR games that are unique, polished, intuitive and creative. I want something that showcases VR - the scale, intensity, the emotions, the grandeur. This game meets all of those criteria. On top of all of that, the soundtrack provides the emotions I want to feel through each level.I didn't know what I was getting into with this (somewhat short) game. I thought I was just going to move around cool creatures and witness the interesting interactions between them. Well, I got that, and much much more. There were moments of urgency, intensity, calm, joy, sadness, and relief all throughout the game. I developed emotional connections with each and every Paper Beast, every one unique in its own way. Some I loved, some I had fun with, some I despised, and some carried a continual mystery as the levels progressed.Ultimately this is a physics-based puzzle game. The goal is to move creatures and/or objects from one place to another, or to find a way to move yourself to the next level. There are no guides, no words, no rules, no hints whatsoever. Every single thing is done on intuition, and more importantly, emotion and curiosity. There are no time limits, and you cannot lose. The game's pace is such that it gently presses you forward at your own pace, no matter how smart or dumb you are, and somehow it manages to do this perfectly without any rebalancing, AI changes, or retries. There are no numbers (except for interesting sky textures and particles), health meters, or level indicators. The polish is incredible for such a small developer. Though there were some moments of frustration, ultimately I found that "ah ha" moment, and got the greatest satisfaction when I figured out each puzzle, just like Valve does with their single-player puzzles. My only genuine frustration with the game was the moments where my movement actions were locked until I realized I was supposed to do something interactive ( these moments were almost entirely within the first 2% of the game).Paper Beasts is an absolute jewel of an experience, and I do not make that statement often about games. This game is up there with Valve's Portal for its ambition, uniqueness, intuition, and grand expression of the platform.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and makes you think. It's sort of a 3D World of Sand with physics for dust, water, wind, fire, ice, etc. and the emotive creatures really bring the world to life. The puzzles are clever and show off all the cool dynamic elements of the game, but also a little fiddly since no solution feels like a perfect fit. The story gives you just enough to grasp on to, but if you like things a little surreal it's absorbing. One of the most unique and stunning VR games I've ever played.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is *amazing*. It's a bit short at about 3.5 hours but it's one of the best games, puzzle games and experiences I've had in VR (and I've had a lot). The puzzle design was fantastic and organic. You don't walk into an area with levers to pull and boxes to put on switches. Instead, you have all these facets of the world itself that you have to figure out what they do and what you need to do in order to progress. None of the puzzles are particularly hard but the exploration and figuring things out is wonderful.The beasts were amazing both in their design and their AI. They all feel like different types of beasts with different personalities and some of them you get to know very well over the course of the game.The world design is beautiful, especially the skyboxes. Every area has a distinct and memorable skybox that you can just stare at for hours like you're trying to find shapes in clouds (ok, maybe not *hours* but they're pretty awesome). The world is also covered in terraformable terrain that's used for many of the puzzles which can be fun.Overall, I have no complaints. In addition to all the above, there are a number of surprises I can't spoil. Get this game, you won't regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Given the 'flat version' is due in two days at the time of this review, what better time to throw one of the best VR games out there today a review? Whilst it wouldn't be right to paint Another World, Heart of Darkness, From Dust, and Paper Beast as being solely products of the genius mind of game designer Éric Chahi (there's enough of a problematic auteur narrative in tech/games as it is), In 2011 my favourite 'god game' of all time was released. From Dust understood that the power of the elements and natural forces were scarier than anything fictional. Eric's passion for volcanology gave us From Dust's volcano eruptions, something that still struggles to find equal in how truly awe-inspiring those moments proved. Leaning on influencing the elements and environmental simulation for its mechanics, : puzzle-like manipulation of the elements, environment, and physics to your advantage; levels like meticulously-crafted diorama simulations to experiment with; and a focus on the frightening power of nature in its mini ecosystems. Only now we have better tech and the immersive power of VR that places you squarely inside these living ecosystems. Still... From Dust VR please?If From Dust had one deficit, it was its tribe AI that, in full fairness to it, had to adapt to any kind of terrain deformation you exposed them to.   What they lack in typically empathy-stirring features like eyes they more than make up for in their movements and behaviours. Simply sitting and co-existing with these creatures in their habitat as they go about their routines is worth the price of admission. More embedded in the world as you are, you're typically tasked with light physics and environmental puzzles, be it escorting certain creatures past predators, over a slippery hill, or through strong winds, etc. It's all very clever stuff,   You know you have to sand over the slippery rocks so the beasts can overcome the hill, but there's a lovely element of play between the idea of what you need to do and realising it. There's chaos in sand not quite perfectly being applied and the beasts needing that last helping hand up as you grab their feet to tug them up at the last stretch. What was made frustrating in From Dust because of punishing failure states works in Paper Beast's favour. There's a magic to sitting with and observing each one. I would just sit and throw balls for the dog-like beasts for much too long before floating away in my paper hot air balloon. Did I mention this game is magical?  On top of the 'adventure' mode is the 'immersive playground sandbox' mode. Whilst this should be all the more magical for the greater freedom and tools at your disposal, I found the lack of impetus exposed the smoke and mirrors of the game a bit too much. These creatures are living and breathing in passing, but in a sandbox wherein there's no real life cycle or in-depth simulations to their existence to speak of, it wears a little (paper-)thin.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Key points:•	Focus is narrative, puzzles, and simulation•	3-4 hours to complete the story•	Has a sandbox mode that allows you to create your own ecosystem and play god•	Beautiful aesthetic. Visuals, audio and AI perfectly marry to create a deeply moving experience•	Allows for smooth movement and teleport, works well with room scale but doesn’t require it (can be played seated)•	Almost everything is tied to the physics system which is capped to 60fps, this can cause double images when running a headset at a higher FPS (mostly noticeable when close up but not enough of an issue to ruin the experience)Paper Beast greatly succeeds in what it sets out to do. It’s a narrative driven physics puzzle game with no dialog where your understanding of this strange world and its rules are built by observing and interacting with a grabby laser pointer. You’ll interact with water and sand physics, the beasts themselves, and plants/objects. This is all you need to know in terms of gameplay without ruining the surprises.Paper Beast’s big trick is the world you’re presented with a very obviously unreal (numbers litter the landscape and many creatures lack space for organs) but the way everything interacts has you completely immersing yourself. The art direction is superb and while certain sequences can take their time the experience is like nothing else.Cannot recommend enough unless you are looking for an action game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool concept I wish I could recommend it but there just isn't much to the actual game.First impressions were rough as it somehow swapped the images for the 2 lenses on my index. Very disorienting and only corrected after a restart, which messed up calibration settings.The game itself is gorgeous, a beautiful rocky sandy backdrop that lets the plants and animals shine. The plants and animals themselves are also wonderful to look at. They are a weird abstract style of folded paper but most of them still are recognizable as to what they are. Predators have similar movement and styles to real world predators stalking and pouncing. Prey are docile and relatively simple minded. As for the gameplay goes I thought I was in a tutorial until the end credits started rolling. Every level basically introduces a new mechanic that you get to play with. This is all great and awesome except for the fact that you will never again get to use that mechanic outside of that level. What is the point of learning that the heavy beetles can be used to carry the light deer across strong winds if you are never again going to see those beetles. The ai does behave well, and as creepy or startling as some may be none of them are hostile to the player which is an interesting change of pace that lets you take things slow and relax. There are no instructions whatsoever which is fine for the type of puzzle game that it is but it doesn't explain to you that there are collectables to unlock in the sandbox mode that you have to find and grab in the story. On the topic of the sandbox mode it is likely the best part of the game letting you set up little ecosystems and watching them play out. I didn't spend a lot of time in the sandbox and while the editor seems pretty clunky it does look like a good way to relax for a while.The game does do a very good job at getting you to care for some of the creatures and there were a few points that were briefly upsetting which says a lot about the atmosphere that this game has.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Going into this, I expected a lot of 'spectacle' and creativity, what I didn't expect to find was a fully engaging game!Surreal? Sure. It puts me in mind of games like Zenoclash. It can be a bit scary sometimes, but only because of the way the game handles the player (a common issue in VR gaming, someone should write a design document to address this). The 'characters', because there are a few that you become familiar with during the game, are charming and interesting to watch. The sound design and music are great as you'd expect.What you won't expect though, is the liquid physics!!! OMG, these are the best liquid dynamics I've ever seen in a game! Water flows, erodes landscapes, freezes, thaws, squirts, pools and a couple of other things I can't even define (evades?).It's truly beautiful to look at and mess around in.I saved the sandbox mode for last, as I thought it would just be a boring "here are all the assets, have fun because the game is short" kinda deal. But the sandbox mode is actually incredible! It made me want to go back and unlock all the things in the campaign, which I will.Another incredible labour of love and another amazing showcase of what VR can do over flat-screen gaming.Highly recommend, especially for the price which is scandalously low on sale right now for £3 ish.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Simulation game / Walking Simulator. The campaign is okay. It can be a little cryptic at times, but isn't too bad. There is a lot of waiting involved. Unrelated, but I wasted over an hour trying to build a dam in one of the levels. Sandbox mode is fun. Although terrain editing options are limited, you can still influence it with weather effects. You're able to create a lot of unique interactions by experimenting with the different creatures. I don't think the games a must-have. This is for the most part just an interactive experience. I'd check out a video or two if you're unsure about buying it. Patience is required for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A truly outworldly experience.What this game lacks in content, it certainly makes up with originality. This is a visual experience and an adventure, with one of the best physics system that I've seen in a VR game so far.If you like slow paced games that won't hold your hand and force you to explore and discover you'll probably like this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: How would you start, trying to describe this experience.How do you explain the feeling of a surreal dream? I can't, except for, THIS is why i love VR, gems like this, a world in were you forget you are playing a game but rather having a full on experience. _childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.The first thing I have to say about Paper Beast is that this is not a typical "game". Don't go into it with any expectations (which is hard to do in today's culture.)There is a lot to love about Paper Beast. The game has a *ton of personality and character*, and at times can be very moving.It's hard to say that there is one thing I absolutely love about it. All of the characters seem to have their own mindset and motivations, which I think is definitely one of the most immersive elements about it.The physics and graphics implemented are also very excellent relative to the type of environment art style that is being shown within the game. Water looks like water, dirt looks like dirt, etc. Some of the effects are really stellar and enhance the style even more.There was only one map where the goal was less clear than the others, and it dragged on until I eventually found a conclusion to it. (It was the one with the predators and the prey with the seeds, the gloomy map.)I would definitely recommend people play Paper Beasts as one of their first VR experiences. There's a lot of storytelling that really transcends language and culture barriers in it and I think it can be widely appreciated by anyone with a VR setup.Great work to the team who developed and produced it. You all did an awesome job.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't sure what to expect but it was a great experience in VR with excellent sound design and a unique art style. I especially enjoyed the first parts of the story, exploring the more terrestrial environments, so I hope the developers make more projects like that.I played on a valve index, the controls seem fine.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most surreal yet beautifully artistic experiences ive ever seen in VR. I realise it was a gamble on the devs.. something new and risky, Yet the game is a complete joy to play. The way the 'paper' strips move is how you would expect. If there is (hopefully) a sequel, you can bet my money is on it again. Gave me that fresh feeling again I got when I first experienced VR in 2016. Love it to bits!  MASSIVELY recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: ok so it started out like "this is a pretty game and also kind of a fever dream"and now i can't stop thinking about these intelligent, non-water-averse despite the fact paper and water do not mix, non-HEAT-averse despite the fact paper is rather flammable, creatures, in a speculative evolution/ecological/zoological way
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the "must-have" VR games. Both adventure and sandbox modes are amazing and memorable experiences.First you are thrown into the alien world of Paper Beast to explore object interactions and solve simple environmental puzzles in a short campaign. Realistic sand/water/wind simulation, great animations and spatial sound make environments and creatures feel real, despite their surrealistic appearance. After gathering few entities in a campaign, sandbox mode opens up(but it's better to collect all the entities before trying it out). There you can design your own environments and create self-sustaining biome with a palette of plants, animals, special objects and events. World is quite small but it's very well optimized and allows smooth scaling from human to mountain size perspective. I ended up spending the most time in a created level with mountain throne in the middle, where I can sit and watch the nature below)
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: --One of the most immersive VR game I've played-----------------To the point opinion / review on this game-----------------------pros--Good artistic and immersive game play-Diverse and emotional characters I fell in love with.-Great sound quality that really kept me into the world- Nice transitional screens that felt like i was looking at something rather than the nauseating feeling of trying to  focus on void-A truly impactful decision making game- Beautiful artistic world building- New material, can't seem to pin point a precise "guess" on what will happen next!-intriguing "story"Cons and bugs--Occasional bugs on the AI where they rag-doll (though this is expected and a bit hilarious to be perfectly honest)-longing for more story-limited space in sandbox mode (only allowed to place certain amount of animals and trees in sand box)-Difficulties with "god mode" size in sand box. The button is really close to the teleport buttons (at least for HTC VIVE) and i end up teleporting everywhere just trying to adjust my height.Must admit, Paper Beast is the first game I have played in VR that had me fully intrigued and exited to play more of- It was a purely enjoyable, artistic, and immersive experience. I've never had a VR game be so immersive as this one for sure! I'd be in this game for HOURS without even realizing! I will admit, I thought there would be a bit more story then there really was with how the "story" started and strives on the idea that it was no simulation, making you feel like the very beasts and animals around you were truly alive. The AI feels very natural and intelligent. I truly feel like my decisions in the game effects them. This is a puzzle game 100% and takes pride in letting you review the level layouts, and to figure out your own direction of how to solve each stage.          I felt very attached to the creatures of this world, and really enjoyed discovering everything it had to offer! For the creatures just being paper and some sort of coral? They showed a LOT of emotion. There are points the game feels even spooky, but in an intriguingly beautiful, artistic, kind of way. I only wish for a closure outside of what was given in the ending, like, There seems to be an opposing "dark force" in this world that enters this paper world and tears it up, in which has an absolutely powerful and mortifying feeling to it! I thought for sure there would be some story where the player would have to help the paper animals rid of this odd alien force, and return it to it's natural ways. but the ending really had nothing much to do with it i suppose?  It didn't hold much satisfaction and felt more like a "and we're done but it was for nothing" kind of feeling, void, and a bit lacking. Perhaps in the future there will be more to it, I would LOVE to see more put into this game, extra puzzles, extended stories, etc. Though I know i personally favor stories over many things in games myself, so that is quite the own opinion. as for mechanics and game play i think the game is outstanding, and I 100% recommend this game to anyone who loves artistic works, puzzle games, nature, and an adventure into a whole different world! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible VR experience. I played the whole game with a Quest 2 along with VRocker. Imo VRocker is basically designed for games like this.I didn't know too much going in and am grateful for that. The art and effects really absorb you into the game. I would forget about everything around me except for when I'd trigger my Quest 2 Guardian or that my headset battery was getting low.There's no combat or a requirement for quick reflexes. This game is an experience. Some common sense, and I use that term loosely considering the world you're stepping into, is required to progress. Quite satisfying and mind blowing as you figure out the solutions. Plenty of WTF moments. If you've got a VR headset and are looking for a unique experience, this one is a no brainer, even at full price.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Surreal games are all about the experience. All-too-complex puzzles don't make sense in a surreal world (except it's an old-school adventure where moon logic/lack of any logic is customary), but a well-crafted experience is quite the something.The presentation is indeed strong with that one. The intro didn't exactly blew me away (but then, I'm not a fan of Japan pop, although the intro here is actually quite melodic) but mere moments after, mind blown. It does put VR to good use all right! And then you meet the inhabitants of that weird world, the behaviour of which is so natural, it reminds me on my real-world cat at times.Recommended, if you got a VR headset handy and are the kind of person to take in the atmosphere of a virtual world.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely incredible. If it wasn't for HLA this would have been my VR game of the year. It's extremely unique and very technically impressive. I've nearly finished the story mode, and messed around for a little bit in sandbox. It's a small game, but I feel like it's worth the price to help support the devs. Especially because they're doing some of the most unique stuff with VR I've ever seen. And I'm definitely looking forward to their future projects.There's a lot more here than just looking at the gorgeous scenery and creature design. Each creature has it's own behaviours that you can study, and then use to your advantage to solve puzzles throughout each level. There's also a fully-dynamic water and terrain manipulation system here. It's honestly mind-boggling that the game runs buttery smooth despite having all that AND being in VR. The sound design is also exceptional with 3 different dynamic range settings to best fit whatever audio equipment you may be using. All the sound effects are wonderfully crisp, and add even further to the insane amount of immersion the game has in it's presentation.Easily one of my all-time favorite VR games. Probably one of my all-time favorites in general just due to how wonderful and unique it is. I spent like 20 minutes just watching some weird bug things build their nest in a cave, it was amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best VR experiences I had. It is an intuitive physics and behavior based puzzle game in somewhat surreal setting. It is not an action game, and can seem slow paced at times, requiring patience, which in my opinion, just adds to immersion. I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys an unusual and creative setting and gameplay. If you liked games like Journey or Abzu you are likely to like this one. I will definitely be buying anything this studio does in the future.  It is one of the rare games I did not want to quit once the end credit started to roll ;) and I definitely recommend trying the sandbox after completing the main story.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the weirdest experience I've had in VR but it is definitely the weirdest VR game I've played. It's a quirky, slow-paced puzzle game with fantastic atmosphere and somehow evokes in me genuine feelings for the creatures in the game. You play a God-like role, manipulating the creatures and the landscape as you travel through the game, and various elements from the game then unlock and you can then use them in the sandbox mode. A small tip - I've actually found the sandbox useful because sometimes I solved parts of the game without fully understanding how I did it, but the sandbox explains the creatures, plants etc. and their behaviours when you select them, which should make things easier if I encounter these again, later in the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game taking you to a surreal place which you couldn't find in reality, yet one that is realistic in its environmental physics and dynamic wildlife. Use the elements to manipulate your surroundings and even terraform. Observe and interact with the wildlife. Understanding and working with the environment is the key to progressing in this game world.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I don't usually leave reviews. I normally forget to. What the hell did I just play? I think this is what VR was supposed to be. I'm not sure. My brain broken after this game and that's a good thing. I've only played an hour, but I would have paid more. This is most interesting thing I've done in a long time. It's calming but spooky. It's empowering, but really good at making you feel powerless. It unique and I'm so glad I tried it. Thank you.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely brilliant, a must have title for VR. It's like stepping into a different world that feels very much alive. It's best to go in completely blind. Eric Chahi has been one of my favorite developers since he created Out of this World back in the 90s,  and once again he's managed to exceed my expectations. Performance is really good. On a Valve Index with  a i7-8700k and a 2080 Super, I can play at 200% SS and 120hz with almost no dropped frames.   My only gripe with the game is that the physics simulation only runs at 60hz, so objects and creatures tend to stutter a bit when viewed up close.  It's a really minor issue but it's still noticeable.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is my new favourite VR game. Absolutely mesmerizing! The spacial audio is the best I've ever heard. Particle fx, water sim and geo manipulation are all top-notch and the fully procedural animation gives the creatures so much life! So glad they brought this to PC VR as well.Also hats off for providing a demo!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm fond of relaxed experimental VR games, my kids are crazy for them. So far this takes the cake with its excellent art direction, wonderful world building, and interesting gameplay. At its best an intriguing existential puzzler, at worst it's an amusing sandbox with loads of cute creatures to interact with. Most will rush through this in about 5 hours, but I probably have the most hours played in Fujii, weird flex, and I have a feeling Paper Beast will someday surpass that. Not to mention, this game is absolutely perfect for someone new to the platform or games in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Very slow and frustrating game. The game is linear but also very unclear what your next objective is. Via trial and error and often not very logical solution you painfully make your way through a desolate wasteland. You will get stuck… often since the controls are so unresponsive. Sometimes it’s just a pixel of sand that you needed to remove. The “game” is also filled with slow cut scenes that can not be skipped. I really tried to like it since there are so many positive reviews, but it just feels like an arty VR showcase.

Other gameplay mechanics include herding, and altering fluid flow. All in all a forgettable experience. Skip this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Just because it's artsy doesn't mean that it is good. The entire game is completely ambiguous which personally I hate in a game. I have no specific goal or reason to care about the world. I don't know why I'm there or what any importance of anything is. The entire game is me pressing random things until something happens. It's not very fun.Graphics are not fun. Everything looks like it's made out of paper. Very basic polygon shapes. Everything is slow and tedious. I guess it's a puzzle game where nothing about our real world makes sense in the game so you just have to figure out the game's physics and manipulate it to progress. Not intuitive at all. Mostly I'm just confused and don't understand what is going on or why I am doing what I am doing.

_childDocuments_.review: A well done artistic game.  This game wont take you long to beat.  Whatever my play time is is what I beat it in.   The game is a series of puzzles set in a very unique... uhh world I guess.  The levels are very well done.  The puzzle in each section is nothing mind blowing BUT the actions taken to solve the puzzles is where the fun comes from.  Just a fun experience for VR.  Well done devs.  No SJW garbage either.  I like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I really really want to love this game, however, it's making me sick. Something which VR titles don't normally do. And this is coming from someone that can play Boneworks with no problems at all.The issue I'm having is that character model animations appear to operate at a low frame rate and thus appear to constantly stutter despite the game running at a solid 90fps. It's very disappointing because the experience is very unique and it looks beautiful. The problem is that when anything moving appear to judder like this, even subtly, it's causing me to feel very sick looking at them. I would be interested to know if others have the same experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Don't get me wrong, the game isn't that bad. It's just honestly, if you ask me whether I recommend it or not I'll just say no.Mind you, I haven't played it that much, and within VR - which gave me even shorter tolerance for it.Now, why wouldn't I recommend it, then?For a game that seems to me mostly about the unique graphic style and experience, it didn't strike me as all that impressive, visually.It does have some cool concepts like those worms that pump the sand around (that's a first for me), but in my - admittedly short - play time I haven't encountered anything that gave me reason to keep playing.The start of the game has you standing in place without being able to move until the beast comes back to you - a very bad callback to Skyrim's opening sequence for me. I can understand the concept from TTRPG of letting people slowly get used to the controls and the world without being lost on all the options they have all at once, but it feels EXTREMELY constrictive.At least until the point I got to, the game keeps you within a narrow path and even goes further and puts you in a cave, all at the beginning of the game.Maybe it was my expectations from the game... I expected to be able to freely explore and see amazing views - waterfalls (sand/paper-falls?), canyons etc.Instead I got a dreary-looking apocalyptic experience that made me depressed.Why would you want to play this game despite all what I said? My best way to put this would be... If you're feeling like looking at the night sky and staring at the stars and galaxies. That's the kind of vibe I got.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: it's okay i guess from an artistic perspective but it's not really a 'game' .. more of an abstract experience, a journey where you float around pulling these weird paper creatures with your controllers. I found it grew boring fast..If that's your thing then cool have fun, but honestly though there are free titles like The Lab more engaging and interesting than Paper Beast
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: The game incorrectly detected my language and offered no opportunity to fix that. (No you shouldn't ever use windows locale to detect the language. You need to ask the user, or use whatever is specified by steam).According to the developer on the forums, at some point there should be an option to change the language, but "you have to finish the introduction first". Well, 20 minutes later the introduction apparently wasn't over, and the option never materialized. The game also uses comfort vignette while turning, and again, there's no option to turn it off.Those two fairly small issues completely destroyed what could've been a fun experience otherwise. Because rather than diving into the game I had to keep waiting for an opportunity to switch the language to English or disable damn vignette. The opportunity never materialized.I'll be refunding this.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty, atmospheric, but ultimately, I found it dull. It is also quite short so I find it hard to recommend at anything but a deep discount. It's not all bad, if you're not a fan of modern hand holding in games, this is one that will not do it so the less obvious puzzles will take work. It's not a bad experience, and if Steam allowed for deeper ratings I would rate it in the middle. Instead let me say if a short, beautiful and atmospheric experience is what you want, get this. If you are looking for a longer, faster paced, adventure don't.

_childDocuments_.review: did not care for this game so I will place here a recipe for huckleberry pancakes instead.Huckleberry pancakes.1 3/4 cups all purpose white flour4 tablespoons sugar1 tablespoon baking powder1/4 teaspoon salt1 1/2 cups of buttermilk5 tablespoon butter, melted2 large eggs1/2 cup HuckleberriesIn medium bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt, set aside. In small bowl combine buttermilk, butter and eggs. Add buttermilk mixture to the flour mixture, combine until mixed do not over mix (I prefer to use a whisk it does the best job). Fry at 400 degrees. Pour about 1/4 cup of batter on the griddle and sprinkle with the huckleberries.Cook on first side about 3 minutes until bubbles appear along the edge of the pancake. Flip and cook for 2 minutes more and golden brown. Serve with a big pat of butter, and some pure maple syrup ( get the real stuff it is worth it).
