_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game. If you want something ethereal and somewhat trippy to just focus in on, this is a fantastic game to play. The level of immersion in this game is also fantastic. You really feel like you've been transferred to an alien world inhabited by simple yet fascinating life-forms. The game is almost entirely systems driven and learning how you can interact with all of these complex and often large environment and creature simulations can be fascinating. The views and sky-boxes in this can were also frequently breathtaking. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt one of the most beautiful games ever made. I can even go as far as to say that it might be life changing for some. If you are imagining how good the gameplay and story will be, multiply it by 10 times. Everything feels so alive and it's like you are actually there, and it's insanely fun. This game is near perfect for VR.Lastly, the water, sand, paper physics. They are absolutely jaw-dropping. Not many games have such good ones, or even close to it.PS. You also get a non-vr version of the game!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Lovely creative puzzle game in a world you have never seen before.Not a game i would recommend for new VR players because it's such a dreamy sandbox world that you dont really grasp what you can do and what is expected of you, but if you have some experience, this game is mesmerizing. It oozes atmosphere and the paper animals make the world feel alive, the puzzles are creative and when you don't get them, you just play around for a while and usually somewhere it works. Recommended for puzzle fans, art fans and people that want to experience something new.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I found this game on accident. I wasn’t even looking for any new VR games, and didn’t even expect much from this game, but boy am I happy I found it. This is truly one of the best VR games I experienced. Not from technical or gameplay standpoint (the gameplay is “basic” fun VR stuff). But from environmental storytelling, presentation, the vibes and aesthetic. With most VR titles I’m very aware I’m person standing in a room with plastic box on their head, it feels fake, like a simulation. But in this game, I felt real. I felt like I actually could be there. The world of paper beast feels expansive, even if you travel from connected areas. The beasts are mesmerizing, and very well done. At first, I felt a bit scared getting close to them, but they are harmless towards you. The story is told without words and its done very well.I highly recommend it. This game is hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is stunning. I felt genuine emotions for the creatures and a sense of wonder unlike any game I have played. I saw on another review that it was the only game that person has played so far that has made them forget that they are playing a VR game and it really does accomplish that. Everything is so alien it really does feel like you have been transported to a strange alternate realm, and maybe you have.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actively looking for interactive entertainment media that pushes the boundaries in some never-before seen waters.. This is it...this is something that won't last a long time, play-time-wise, but will stay with you a looong time. It gives you a world with a REALLY creatively made ecosystem, where in order to progress you just have to observe, which will come by so naturally, because the interactions between the flora and fauna of the world are very interesting and well made,VR translates this close to an actual  experience really well. Had to do a few tweaks here and there on my 3080 for an optimal smooth sailing. From now on it is going to be one of my top go-to games when showing someone VR  in general- Had so many WOW and amazement factors through the whole journey and the game was just adding them on top of it. Tried to not use the word 'game', but i feel like i've played with it. Experienced it, explored it. It is certainly not a trivial game by today standards, but to me i feel like it is a  . Like portal was back then. And some other rare gems in between.Would an will return again to the world of Paper Beasts when memory fades away. Maybe a sandbox mode until then...
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe this game is 3 years old and looks so good!I jumped in yesterday, just for 5 minutes to check it out, and spent almost 3 hours in there.Visually it is stunning (don't forget to ramp the graphics up to ultra - although it still looks amazing on low) and combined with the amazing audio, it is an outstanding experience.Although there are puzzles to solve, they are not intrusive and feel like part of the experience rather than the sole objective of the game. They are pretty simple and just come naturally as you absorb the world around you.The beasts are like nothing I've seen before. They act like real animals and seem to have their own traits and mannerisms, making you want to observe and interact with them.It feels like there is a story brewing as you play, but I can't say for sure so far. It gives vibes of a realisation of the damage humanity can cause to an eco ecosystem and how it can affect the beasts that are part of it; but I could be reading too much into it. Don't worry though, it isn't pushing anything.Either way, it's simply amazing. It plays very well seated and is extremely well optimised for those using AirLink on the Quest.I think this is something that I will keep coming back to, even if it's just to chill and watch the beasts. If you are new to PCVR, or wanted to introduce someone else VR, then this is a perfect title to use; immersion happens within minutes of entering the world and even with locomotion and smooth turn, there should be very little chance of sickness (it does have snap turn and teleport).
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly nice game with simplistic-yet-beautiful style. Recommend if you tired from endless horrors and shooters, here you can find something different and worthy to be done in VR. A few hours of calm adventure through different stages, helping paper creatures of a unique sand world, where no one including predators can even attack you. Observe slightly surrealistic but not aggressive lands, mountains, lakes, caves.. and more. Interact with inhabitants and protect them from changes coming from . Don't be afraid to make a mistake, don't race against the time, don't compete with somebody else, simply enjoy this peculiar world.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Another world of the creator of Another Word, Eric Chahi. Difficulty ☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆☆ (you cannot die at all)Playable in VR and non-VR. The Folded Edition is the non-VR version. But this game is designed to be played VR, so if you have the chance to do so, go for it.The whole game is a very creative but strange exploration-puzzle-sandbox game with awesome particle and water effects (even in VR). The graphics are kept pretty simple on purpose because of the sandbox character and geotransforming the engine does.Whatever I just played? I am not sure - but I did enjoyed it! Even the sandbox kept me busy for some while. It is the unique gameplay that comes with it, especially in VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Just played through it. This game is a masterpiece. From the paper animal's design, AI, and charisma, to the dream like setting, and the amazing physics. Seriously, water and sand simulations. Amazing game.OG review: This is one of the biggest showpieces for VR. The graphics, sound, immersion, cinematic pizzazz, and interactivity is all TOP NOTCH. Good thing VR games seem to be aging well, because future players will sit and wonder why no one talked much about this when it came out.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: For $20, you get to travel through a desert full of bizarre paper creatures for about three hours, in a bizarre, dreamlike world that is probably the product of at least *some* LSD.A few of the "levels" (for want of a better term) can be a little frustrating, but the creature AI behaves incredibly well throughout and overall it's a really nice, chill experience. Probably not a bad intro to VR if you want to show off to friends and family or something - nothing here can hurt you the player, and most of the gameplay is nice and simple. Plus, there's a sandbox mode to screw around in if you're into that.In my case, it also came with the "Folded Edition" for pancake displays, but please don't waste your time with that. This unconditionally works best in VR.VR games are categorically marked incompatible with Steam Deck, but I found this title works well in Proton. There are some pretty distracting visual artifacts on the terrain from time to time though. I have yet to compare with Windows to see if that's a universal issue or not.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I got this not really knowing what to expect, and I think that's probably the best way.   All I knew was that it was something about a journey through a landscape helping the animals that inhabit it.It's very beautiful and relaxing experience - the sound design and weird beasts are very well done.   Something a bit different and Im glad I didnt sleep on it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: If you want action, this isn't for you. Paper Beast is a very gently paced (sometimes just plain slow) art game with environment/system interaction puzzles that gate progression. It has a sandbox mode but the main "story" mode is 2-4 hours of gameplay depending on how much time you spend on puzzles or just playing with interactions.The experience involves discovering and exploring a surreal ecology populated by wonderfully animated creatures and plants built like papercraft models. The puzzle elements involve altering the environment or harnessing the behaviours of the alien lifeforms to progress. While some of the puzzles will take some experimentation and a modest amount of dexterity I didn't come across any scenarios where you die or have to restart. Again, it's all very gentle.It's all very playable in a seated position and the whole gameplay experience is relaxed. Although the emotional tone wanders from melancholy through to joyful there's nothing jarring or scary so it's a light play experience that I found very enjoyable as a break from more intense VR games.  Well worth the cost of entry.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I had to retire this game unfortunately.I got stuck twice because I just couldn't figure out what to do to solve the puzzle and I still haven't finished chapter 3.The game is really pretty though and the beasts are really really impressive. The interactive part was a ton of fun from the parts I have played.Maybe someone that can figure out the puzzles would get more enjoyment out of this.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: wow.. this was truly an experience!Gave me the goosebumps; I haven't felt like this since I watched Ad Astra.I had fogotten how exciting and aweinspiring games could be. I came back to update my review after reading that the creator of another world was involved in this game too: It all makes sense - Two masterpieces!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A really beautiful, unusual and entirely unique VR puzzle game (comes with a regular screen version now). Bit short, as is usually the case with games like these, but wraps up exactly when it needs to, finishing off with something that I can only describe as some of the most bizarrely wonderful visuals I've seen in a VR game yet. Somehow it even manages to instill a sense of actual awe, without any fancy tech, mostly through its artstyle, sound design - that deserves praise on its own - and music.The game features almost no text or spoken instructions, yet manages to convey exactly what you need to do to proceed in any given scenario, which is commendable. The best kind of tutorial is one that the player is not even aware of. All you need to do to figure out the solution to basically any puzzle is to observe the environment and the titular paper beasts. All in all, it's a really solid, if short, artsy puzzle game, which I can easily recommend. It's been out for a few years, had a few deep sales and a free demo if you're still on the fence about it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished this yet, but it's just so creative. VR was made for projects like this were you can be immersed in totally different worlds to our own. You wander through a story, solving puzzles that never get too frustrating along the way with a few paper creatures giving you a hand along the way. It rewards trying stuff out as well. At one point I was feeling like everything was moving too slowly for my liking, started pulling on objects I thought might give me a response and all of a sudden I realised how to change speed and direction. Anyway, if you have VR and the idea of traveling through an imaginary world sounds appealing, I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Beast is a surreal puzzle game that works well in the VR medium. I don't think as a "flat" game the interesting designs of the animals and the uncanny feel of the world would be captured and felt as much as in VR. The story is very abstract and "artsy" which I don't care much for, but the puzzles were pretty cool - coming from someone who usually isn't a big puzzle game fan. Part of that is that most of the puzzles are rewarding, but not super obtuse, really hit that sweet spot. But I think the way that the puzzles are done is more of what made them unique. The strange animals of this world are all part of the puzzles, so you have to figure out what you can use to manipulate their behaviour in a way that helps you. You sort of have to sit back and observe and play around with things for a bit. Overall a good little experience. Only downside is that its only like 3 hours long and not very replayable, as most puzzle games are when you already know the solutions.For more thoughts, consider checking out my full review here:
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fantastic game which I would liken to "Journey" but in VR. There are some really clever puzzles that make You think & You will often need to use terrain manipulation to progress, which I love. It really takes You on an emotional roller coaster with some really nice immersive environments, great sound effects & amazing musical soundtrack. You end up feeling really attached to the creatures in the game too, they're strange alright but really nice! The graphics are really beautiful & if You have a beefy pc, cranking up the settings & resolution makes it all the more breathtaking. It's probably not for everyone as there's no shooting but if You enjoy immersive physics based puzzles with fantastic trippy art stylised graphics then this is definitely for You. There are some moments in this game which I would rank as some of the happiest moments in my life. It's that good (imho). You owe it to Yourself to experience this game, especially in VR. It's a decent length too with some good replay-ability. I absolutely love it. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Beast is a fun experience all the way through the main campaign. It was immersive, very atmospheric, and interesting the whole game. It was quite fun. I messed around in certain areas for quite a bit of time, like the underground hill with the bugs. The god mode is also quite fun to mess around in, and with unlockables from the main story for the god mode, it gives replay value to an already fun campaign. This game is definitely worth the 10$ I spent on it, as I enjoyed the campaign, and I see myself coming back to the game for both experiencing the campaign multiple times in the future, and messing around in the god mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Pixel Reef, I could kiss you. This is surely one of the most incredible and inspiring VR experiences I have had.At times Lynchian in it's delivery, with moments of terror and dread interjected with pure awe, the world of Paper Beasts isn't always pretty, but it is always beautiful. Between the physics simulations, surface deformation, interactive lighting and liquids, from a technical standpoint this game is in a league of its own and fulfills so many of the cravings I've longed to experience in VR that nothing else has been able to deliver. I'm still working my way through and there have definitely been some moments where I leapt from the overwhelming sound design or a creature sneaking up unexpectedly and there have been times where the puzzles felt a little unintuitive (only one major one so far) but I kept playing as I have been completely sucked in by the wordless narrative and design of the world. This does what only the top level VR experiences can do, allow you to experience not just actions or moments impossible in the real world, but to experience an entire new reality that couldn't exist in any other format. Pixel Reef please keep creating, you have earned a life long fan. (and I wasn't kidding about feeling like David Lynch, I bet he'd love this game get him on board with your next project haha)
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Look at the playtime on the reviews - most less than 5 hours and that's how long it takes to complete this game. Sure, it's not a game, it's an "experience", but it's very clear that even among those who greatly enjoyed playing (myself included), this is not something that most fans will play for even 10 hours total (even with the sandbox mode and replaying). After 5 hours, I have completed the game, and unlocked every achievement except one (the achievement where you have to drag an extremely cumbersome radio through the entire first level).I really enjoyed this game and I wish other VR games shared such an interesting and astonishingly beautiful setting, not to mention the superb approach to story-telling without voice or text. This game is an amazing work of art and a fantastic VR experience. It should have been twice the length at least, however. I strongly recommend this game, but I suggest buying it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable VR experience, more of a trip than a game but this is what I hope to feel in more VR games. Experimenting with the creatures and the physics of the world was a great time. The world manipulation lends itself well with the VR controls too. All in all one of my top VR experiences so far I think
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Wow.This game is just fantastic. Its such a unique game in its visuals and abstract concepts. This game is stunning, hence why I played it all in one sitting (pretty impressive for me in vr). Puzzles were understandable yet challenging, meaning I only had to look up what to do once. Only complaint is that I believe the story did have some pacing issues as well as being a little bit confusing, but apart from that it's great. For it's beauty alone it's worth it. There is also a sandbox mode included for free. Not really my thing but if you're looking for more than 2 and a half hours of game play its a great option.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Most powerful vr experience I've had in a long time. It's not a long game but I did not feel that it was too short. No section overstays its welcome and the puzzles were just the right difficulty to make you feel clever without letting you get lost. My only complaint is that I could not find the settings before the game started so I ended up playing a lot of the game at lower settings before finding that there was a pause menu. All the other reviews are true, it's beautiful and there is not much quite like it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Wierd but vivid game. This game is a vivid visual experience game. Paper Beast dwelves you into a world full of mysterious paper creatures. The game feels beautiful, yet nightmarish. I am half way through and enjoyed it so far, but I think after playing it one time, it gets even better the second time.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A surreal trip to another world where observing the alien ecosystem is your only means of survival.   Help yourself and some of the more friendly local critters flee dangerous hazards like alphanumeric storms, cave ins, and predators by terramorphing the terrain in your favor or baiting the fauna in the right direction by using their favorite snacks. VR users should definitely look into this gorgeous & engaging atmospheric puzzle experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game in a VR bundle for cheap.  Such an amazing visual game/experience!  Its a puzzle/experience simulation journey into another dimension.  The developers knocked it out of the park with this one!  Took me 4.5 hours to complete, only unlocking 4 out of 21 achievements.  If you have a VR headset, its a def must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: At one and the same time the most interesting VR game I've played and the weirdest.Inside a world of little intelligent creatures that all have a job - either to follow some shiny object, dig up sand into a ball like a dung beetle, be a heavy-weight to which to attach baby creatures in a storm, or suck sand/water from one place to another - you have to solve a little immersive puzzle using them to get to the next.  It's like Portal but on hallucinogenics.I don't think people appreciate the technical side of what's going on here, but it's great fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the byproduct of if the creators of the movie Big Fish took more LSD than usual and made a game. The story makes no sense, you do puzzles, and it's really only getting a positive review because sandbox mode is actually kind of fun and therapeutic. The game mechanics work really well too, so that's a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very beautiful and artistic game with the probably the best water, sand and melting ice simulations that you've ever seen. The game have an ecology that you can affect and sometimes it interacts with the puzzles. The beautiful scenery, the music and the effects will give you a feeling of wonder many times. It runs very well. Very recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I went into the game having a completely false expectation. I hadn't done any research, yet assumed that the game was be something of an exploration/survival game. Inevitably, I found myself disappointed to find that I had very little freedom to explore, and that the game was more of a silent story experience, with linear puzzle progression.THAT BEING SAID, when I reflect properly, I can't deny that it was a breathtaking experience. You can't help but be afflicted with a sense of awe and wonder, during every stage. It is worth mentioning that the game has a nifty little sandbox mode as well, the elements for which are collected throughout the main story.I wouldn't rate this as highly as Steam does, but I would at least recommend that anyone should play through this game once. It was a worthy experience that elevates VR as a medium.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: i didnt expect this game to be as good as it is. a weird but wonderful world with its own working ecosystemI put on my VR headset and when i came out i saw the sunrise .. oops but its just goes to show this game could retain my attention for so long - fun sandbox mode can be unlocked - good VR experience - fun physics puzzles - all hail the anime girl song
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A chilled but shockingly impressive exploration game based around using AI animals and their unique powers to help them reach what they need and in turn sending you to the next area.It's well worth a shot and the most exciting part comes when you get into the sandbox afterwards, I've barely unlocked any content and already spent more time in the sandbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Beast is one of my favourite VR games to date. I originally played it on PSVR, hence my short-ish play time on PC. I loved it so much that I decided I had to own it on PC too, so that I can return to it some time I feel like it, and also to share with others, and just to support the devs.This is a wholly unique abstract story adventure, with puzzle gameplay. It's memorable and impactful. It has great music and great visuals... great atmosphere.This is a must-play VR adventure. $20 is a great price.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: If you own a VR headset, get this game.I don't want to spoil the experience by trying to describe it, you should really just get it first-hand, all I will say is that it's the closest thing I've felt to being in a waking dream. A slight sense of awe and dread mixed with the surety that you are safe without having any idea what might happen.10/10 wish there were more experiences like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Such an artful, weird, beautiful, abstract, crazy adventure. I had no idea what was going on from the very start until the end... and I loved it!I want to call this a puzzle-, adventure-, walking simulator. The game tells a story, without telling you a story. It's more like you're an observer that has to participate. Some situations can come off as stressful but you're never in any danger so I will recommend this for people sensitive to scary games.You may get confused because the game does not explain much to you, but it doesn't really matter. It doesn't have to matter. You don't need to understand everything or do and see everything. All you have to do is come along for the journey and enjoy.Many of the puzzles and situations are solved and progressed by your actions alone. You will feel lost and puzzled, wanting to ask someone for help when you're stuck. Don't ask anyone!Non-spoiler tip: If you get stuck, just take your time and look around. Touch things, interact with everything. Observe the situation and the animals. Situational awareness and patience will get you far because this game does a great job at making solutions apparent and feel naturally available.No-spoiler description of a scenario:I found myself in a room full of crab-like creatures, playing around with items made available to me. I didn't even try to solve the puzzle because the interactions with the crabs was just fun and engaging. I'd do something and they'd react. I'd do something else and they'd react differently. I was so sucked into this playsession with the crabs that I didn't even realize there was a puzzle to solve. This rarely happens to me in games, so this is a huge compliment to this game!This is certainly not the game for someone who wants action and fast pace. This is a game for someone who wants to spend an evening or two just enjoying their time. Join these gentle creatures on their migrations and share in their pain, their happiness and curiosity. You may also enjoy the sand- and waterphysics; They're pretty good!It's also a great game to introduce someone to VR, especially if you can select your favorite scene and see how your friend copes with the weird world. I can recommend the "parade" for this, a vague description but you'll know it when you see it.Replayability is also present as there are collectibles hidden throughout the various stages of the game. Most of them seem to be tools for the sandbox-mode where you can play around with terraforming and water physics. I haven't gotten into this playmode much as the controls seemed a bit complicated (unlike the main game where controls are easy and straight forward).I got the game as part of the humblebundle VR bundle, which made this a no-brainer at a great bundle-value. If you buy the game at full price I'd say it's worth it for the experience. Just be aware that the game is a bit short. I finished it in one session and didn't rush anything, then I had a brief look at the sandbox mode.(check my playtime at time of writing the review)8/8, would confuse again
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Words do not do ANY justice for this game.Videos do BARELY any justice for this game.But playing? Playing is like stepping into a million different worlds in a million different lifetimes. Every worldly reaction is appreciated, every little detail, and every creature. This game has a much deeper meaning than what is originally on the surface, and you realize it is ultimately about our place in the universe, the insignificance we personally represent, but the significance of life in and of itself, and the significant changes we can set in motion with the touch of a single metaphorical finger.This game is an absolute beauty, and a testament to the creators outlook on the importance of life. I personally can't wait to see more of what comes.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Super creative, immersive, and a fantastic experience. There are some elements of a game with "puzzles", but the whole thing is like an art piece. It's beautiful and runs great. Unsettling at some moments, but nothing really scary happens. It really takes its time with some moments, but its very calming just watch the beasts. We need more VR games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Bizarrely, this is the most immersive VR game that i've played, truly feels like you've entered a world that you're just dipping your toe into. This is what I think of when I think VR, being transported to a new realm entirely.The 'Animals' in this world react in a manner so bizarre and yet, somehow, so true to life I couldn't help but become endeared to them within fifteen minutes of play.The environments can seem tranquil in one moment, and the next produce an event so utterly unexplainable and frightening that I found myself naturally backing away.Really gave me heart Of Darkness/Another World vibes and was very happy to discover that it was directed by the same guy!Well worth, full price the equivalent of a decent fast food burger. Wish i'd paid more.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on humble because literally Paper Beasts on photo intrigued me.At first I was totally lost what I should do, but game slowly teaches You how to interact with the world without silly tutorials, You figure it out 'Yourself'.  Graphics fitted pretty well and the 'Story' is hard to tell with words, it's more like an experience. I really liked how it's not just typical game, You don't know anything yet You are curious what awaits You. I wish more games used potential of VR immersion like this one.The ending could be a little bit better by my opinion, because I didn't felt like it was really the ending and the part was really long without interaction.But overally it's a very good game!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: i did not know what to make of this game at all, apart from i love it. Everything about it is so well done and had to be dragged off it. I am not saying anything about it, it has to be done , seen and felt.run on oculus rift cv1 on a laptop with zero issues.not many games like this one , its a one off.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review after completing the story mode. This game feels incredibly surreal. The simplistic design of the low poly paper animals, combined with the desert theme works really well together. I recommend this game to anyone who wants to mess around with wacky creature physics for a few hours, but I don't think this game is worth the 20 dollars I paid. I'd recommend waiting to buy this game until it is on sale. It's just too short for the $20 price tag.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the absolute best VR experiences there is. This is a game, which at the very end, made me shed a tear because of how beautiful it was. The world is very surreal, abstract and beautiful. The creatures feel real, even tho they are made out of paper. After spending two years with VR, this game got me fully immersed in it again, which after such a long time happens rarely. It manages to pull off everything without a word said or written. I encountered no bugs.Video games should be an creative endeavor, a journey in which you can experience the creativity of the creators. Video games don´t need to make sense or be realistic all the time. Video games are art.This is a video game.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Eric Chahi's latest game is another amazing gem. Following footsteps of excellent "From dust", this is an 3 hour long story about our place and impact on earth. A virtual reality classic, a must have for every VR game library. Even though creatures made out of paper, they are presented with impressive and lifelike animation. Vistas are interesting, effects are excellent and interaction is intuitive, natural and responsive. Coding and art is top noch.  If you played Chahi's previous game "From Dust" you will know what kind of simulation you will face here.  Simulation is particle based, water, ice, sand and wind is simulated realistically so you can modify your environment accordingly.This is a narrative puzzle game. It has several chapters, in every chapter you will need to solve a puzzle. Puzzles are generally consist of modifying your surroundings to herd your paper flock to a tree of life. Every puzzle has it's own unique mechanic, so you always need to find a new way to move through the chapters. There is also a sandbox mode to play with.tl;dr: A definite VR classic. Is it suitable for children?As this is a VR experience, some beasts look and heard really frightening especially when they first appear. But you are playing as invulnerable entity, as a shepherd. You will need to explain to your children that they are safe and that paperbeasts are all friendly. There is no blood, no violence in game,  except some wolf-like but rainbow colored paper beasts attack your herd (not you) in some chapters. Those attacks are part of a puzzle but they may be scary for under 7 years.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't think I was going to be into this game since I like more straightforward story games, but man it was REALLY cool.  It is like a puzzle game mixed with an exploration of art and physics.  Really creative, GORGEOUS visuals, the puzzles were fun and it just got you in that world.I'm sure it is still cool in non-VR, but in virtual reality it was a treat.  You just wanted to turn your head around and look at everything.  The detail in the animals  was so impressive, even their shadows were super detailed.  Great game.  Sign me up for your next games devs
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: If your a fan of puzzle adventures, this is a must have for a VR library. The atmosphere and passive story this game provides truly drives with intrigue. The physics based puzzles and environments lead one to think creatively in order to solve each challenge. While it isn't a very long game, it's a bit on the easier side when it comes to puzzle challenges. For puzzle games, much of the gameplay time is usually in trying to solve the puzzles. Many players might find a challenge here, but for a seasoned puzzle gamer, they will find it on the easier side. It's still worth checking out simply for the atmosphere and setting this game provides.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I hesitate to recommend this because while on one hand it is wildly creative, artistic, and alive, on the other hand it is... semi-lifeless and dead.For a game to try and be so immersive, the animals reacting to the player, you can pet them and they move lightly with your touch, objects move right through them with no collision and they're interaction-less.  Depends on the action.The player... YOU... are the only "creature" on the planet apparently that doesn't leave footprints in the sand of any kind.  WTF?  That's fine because you also have no footstep sounds when you're walking??   Immersionn minus minus.  So I'm here but leave no mark like the other animals?  Very disappointing and pulls you out of the "feeling" the game initially gives you which in my mind is a horrible development mistake.  You very rarely make shuffling noises if you're stopped and turn.  So why then, if you're making sounds while turning occasionally, ala friction with the world, do you not leave any trace of where you are, where you've been... and while you're walking no sound.  Awful.So you focus on the world around you and you want to be apart of it, but you're not.  You are but you're not.  The world is in contention with itself.So keep that in mind if you purchase the game and buy it on sale for sure, and ignore the fact that you're not part of the world you're traversing.  :\Its a neat experience if you enjoy art, creativity, and problem solving. As a game it kinda sucks and you just feel like a spectator instead of a visitor.  A real shame but easily fixable.  YMMV
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is an ARTWORK playable in VR! It sucked my mind into a beautiful looking paper/sand/crystal-paralleluniverse that´s exciting to explore. In every new area I can find new ways to interact with these cute paper animals and find ways to change the wolrd to progress to the next area. Everything in this game is so well composed that it feels just right. I can´t describe what it is but this game makes me feel good. I look forward to come back into it´s beautiful world. It brightens my day every time. It´s child friendly and my son loves to play it too.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Grabbed my attention right off. Brilliant graphics and interaction with the "Creatures". It's simple, but dynamic at the same time. A fun game where you interact with the environment, and solve problems along the way.In a gaming world where everything is shooting and blowing things up, it's refreshing to see something light, simple and fun.01/06/2022:Just finished.One of the finest experiences I have done in VR...
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Really incredible experience. The environments and creatures are consistently breathtaking. The creatures all feel very organic and lifelike. No mechanic overstays its welcome. It takes around 3.5-4ish hours to finish the game and every moment feels really fresh. On top of that the sandbox mode is really cool.This is one I'll be playing again in the future, I can't recommend it enough. I'm excited to see what the devs do in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is to date the most immersive VR game I've ever played. Unlike most VR games, this game does not go for typical "immersion" in that it tries to make you feel like you're a normal guy in the (mostly) normal world, with decent graphics and realistic sounds.This is a different kind of immersion. This game drops you into a different reality with its own internal rules, physical phenomena, and most importantly, its own ecosystem.Instead of trying and failing at simulating reality, this game creates its own, and just drops you in. To me, nothing is more immersive than true-blue exploration. It has an art style vaguely similar to Journey, and a similar, yet more mature tone.I'm not going to spoil anything for anyone, but let's just say that this is the first game that's ever made me feel true intimidation; not the "guy calls you out" intimidation, but the primal kind. At the same time, it's one of the few, and maybe even the first to get me to genuinely feel for a character in a game.If you have VR, you should play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it! This is very much an indie-type exploration game with lot of care for the immersion. Perfect when you want to take your time to enjoy the environment and not rush. I recommend to show it to new VR users. You can do both translation navigation and small teleportation jumps which is better to ensure no motion sickness.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Papers Beast is an awe inspiring game that fails to maintain momentum. This game starts super strong, but slows down into tedium when the player really needs a push of new exciting visuals and mechanics to want to push forward.I hate saying this about games that are already considered to be short but I think Paper Beast would have really benefited from being quite a bit shorter.I don't regret this purchase and I cannot understate how awesome this game's first few levels are.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely VR experience, in visuals and audio. Thought provoking and beautiful scenes with progress sometimes tied to environmental 'puzzles' that feel more like play. The game doesn't hand-hold and tries to minimize immersion-breaking, but the puzzles are not so difficult as to be frustrating. Very peaceful, almost meditative like a living gallery. The creatures somewhat remind me of Theo Jansen's beach walking Strandbeests. The mode that gets added after you finished took my breath away and ran so smoothly I couldn't believe all the things going on in this cute little tilt-shift world I was peeking down at.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Such games of this caliber & quality are truly rare. From the fascinating creature design & art style to the subtle movement and odd music, i found this experience (far more than a game to me) truly revolutionary for a VR title. Shooters are a dime a dozen, where as this stood in a realm all its own. I very much felt moved near the ending, and felt a sense of lost when i realized it was over. Well beyond the price they ask for. I can only pray they make more games of this nature and quality in the near future. From the intuitive Interactions, to the logic of the puzzles, to the simple beauty of the landscapes and animations, it was a massively worthy time.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: If your new to VR, This is the game to get. It almost feels like a whole different world once you get into it. The puzzles and interactions with all the paper animals are breathtaking and the puzzles aren't too hard to solve and but hard enough to allowed to be creative. Not only that, the general atmosphere and visuals is an awesome touch to the game. 10/10 would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Well now that was both an exceptional and an exceptionally odd experience. If you played From Dust then you might start off feeling quite at home. The game really has three phases.Firstly it begins as something fascinating and intriguing yet kind of hands off. It sets up the world and creates some mystery.Towards the middle you really get to start playing around with the simulation engine and get some environmental puzzle solving to sink your teeth into.And then at the end it just goes right off the rails, becomes incomprehensible and finishes with more questions than answers.I kind of feel like I do after watching a movie where they got so excited about the special effects that they forgot to write a story. I have no clue what happened but I enjoyed all of the pretty visuals. Plus, thanks to what I assume was a glitch I got to use the phrase  so that was nice.Sandbox mode shows off the simulation engine nicely but you're not going to be spending a whole lot of time in there.If you are OK picking up games for the experience then this is one that you'll remember for a bit, but not for all good reasons. I'd say it's worth picking up if you catch it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It's an absolute audiovisual feast in VR. There's an indication midway through the story that there's more to these sights and sounds than we've initially been led to believe, but either I missed critical details or that aspect of the game goes largely unexplored, but that's okay. I appreciate Paper Beast as a spiritual odyssey. Eric Chahi has a vivid imagination and I recommend this game to anyone with a VR headset who wants to be whisked away to an extraordinary new world.BUT. I actually think it's kind of a chore to play at times. Mainly because it's so labor-intensive... many of the puzzles have deceitfully simple solutions (despite the guise of parsing the "rules" of how each ecosystem operates) but often times, even once I've figured out WHAT to do, it's just a lot of work actually putting the plan into action, often involving lots and lots of that terrain-shifting stuff that Chahi toyed with in From Dust. And having to often rely on AI-controlled animals to complete tasks can be frustrating, to say the least.So it's cool and I like it overall, but I'd vastly prefer a walking simulator version of this with all of the puzzles patched out (kinda like how SOMA not has a monster-free option).
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: -Played on Index + 2080TiPositives: A very beautiful and relaxing VR game. I'm now 3hrs in and it has been a, no shooting, puzzelsolving and walk about affair. The index controls are correctly implemented, also a setup menu that is clear and works.Negatives: As with most of these games the story is more imagined by the player than told by the makers.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Paper Beast is a cross between a walking simulator and lite puzzle game, with perhaps just a splash of adventure storyline holding it all together. Enter the world of the paper beasts: a world filled with origami creatures and alphanumeric clouds. Solve terrain puzzles as you go from place to place, admire cute paper creatures, and enjoy the beautiful world of Paper Beast. I played Paper Beast as a VR game (there’s also a regular version), and I can’t recommend it enough if you have a VR headset. Paper Beast is hands-down one of the best VR games I’ve played so far. The controls feel good, the world is gorgeous, and the creatures are freaking adorable. In one of the early areas there’s a cave where you first meet the little crab creatures, and I will unabashedly admit I spent a good 20 to 30 minutes playing with them and helping them build their dirt hill. The puzzles were mostly “meh” to me, but some of them were really tricky if you were trying to complete achievements for those levels. I didn’t find any of the puzzles particularly challenging, but a few made me sit and think a bit to figure them out.I  want to be upfront about how short this game is. I completed the entire game, including earning all achievements, in a little less than 6 hours. Because it’s so short, I recommend waiting on a sale to buy it—it’s definitely worth picking up!I figure on my VR game reviews it might be nice to include a VR Game Recs list for other VR gamers who might see this and are looking for more VR games to play. Below is a list of my favorite VR games in no particular order. I’ll come back and update this review as I add more games to the list in future reviews. And here are some games I advise you to avoid:
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It's like someone let Salvador Dali make a VR experience. I've actually always wanted a surreal video game where you have to learn the rules of nature from scratch by observing your surroundings, and Paper Beast delivers beautifully. As a game per se, I'd give this a 7.5/10: it's mostly an atmospheric walking simulator, with a few nice environmental puzzles, and a fair amount of sandbox-ish interactivity, including at times the ability to reshape the landscape around you. But as an experimental art piece, or a thesis on design, rigging, and simulation, it absolutely wins full marks.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is one trippy and beautiful game. I like how the game guides you just by observing and experimenting, no real tutorial. The very beginning was confusing, but it seems to be setting the stage for whatever story is being told. It reminds me of "From Dust" (same designer, who also did "Another World" (aka "Out Of This World", a true gaming classic!) in how you change and manipulate the world via these origami entities. Can't speak for the "flat" version but being immersed in the VR world is breathtaking. Would recommend if you enjoy exploring and seeking to understand a strange world with situational puzzles.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Very pleasant world to spend time in.  Puzzles are well thought out and feel made specifically for VR unlike some other games where they are just a repackaged flat 3d game in a VR headset.  Some of the puzzles definitely feel would not work in another medium.It was a little short overall (Steam says 3 hours but I would have guessed I played for 6) but I felt good and complete at the end of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a magical experience... I took my time and it lasted almost 5 hours. The art design is wonderful, sounds are great and the puzzle part is nice (but not difficult). Highly recommended. It's well worth 20$ (what I paid). I will play it again for sure with a higher resolution headset once I get one. ;) And it's a must-show for the  wife also. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This was a pretty magical French fancy all told. Right from the off, as some interactive Japanese punk amused me while the simulation loaded, I could tell I was going to enjoy their off beats ;). You emerge into a series of sandy digital worlds, all beautifully framed, and then get led through their oddites by a range of origami companions.You do immediately notice a graphical scrubbiness to the environments, but this is soon forgiven as you realise that each puzzle zone involves some form of environmental manipulation. Sands can be sculpted, water sources steered, animals herded into making resources shrink or reappear. It's not that long, with the campaign clocking in at around 3 hours for me. But for prolonged periods I wasn't concerned with that, because each unlocked zone contained some new intrigue, and all I cared about was what the next den would hold. A couple of missions did lean on the same game mechanics in succession, but that was a rare downbeat, in what was otherwise a progression of genteel surprises.There's very little in way of instruction, you just prod things until they make sense. But I also never hit any extreme walls of difficulty. If anything I often just carried on playing with certain realms even after the solution had became clear. (Making digital mud castles can be fun alright? ;))VR just makes all of these elements more transporting. Moving amongst , sculpting the land by hand, steering between the legs of some towering paper impossibility before it peers curiously into your face. S'all good :)The bonus  is cute, and searching out the nodes that unlock it in each level is fine. But I'm not sure how much time I'll spend with it, as it's purely a 'make your own fun' affair, setting life forces in motion and watching predatory forces herd their burgeoning growth, or just throwing a local disaster into the mix. It feels like it could really do with some guided challenges to make it sing. (Add a 'get a turtle as high as the sun' level or something and I'd be in there for hours :D).
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A VR Masterpiece. The first achievement called "Another World" is a great name choice as I've been in awe like this only when I saw Eric Chahi's amazing vector based action-adventure masterpiece "Another World" at the first time in 1991. Paper Beast is a wonderful experience, like as if a Dali painting would came alive.Update: I just realized Eric Chahi is indeed the person behind this project. A genius can't hide his signature style & talent.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game! I had a sense that I was actually in another world. In some places I just wanted to sit and observe surroundings it leaves a lot of room for imagination and some places reminds me my dreams. Each creature in the game has it's own personality and sense of humor. Everything looks alive and game feels like a journey with a lot of emotions. I wish there where more games like this!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the big special games of my life. Made an immediate impact just like playing Mario, Zelda, Doom, Half-Life, X-com, for the first time.Blurs the line between a game, an experience, and art in motion (performance art?), but in such a way that they seemlessly combine into an amazing journey.This "game" is really good. It has simple logic puzzles. The world and its life forms are abstract and undefined in a way that makes the world mysterious and strange, but the paper machete style animals have incredible AI for path finding and watching them regain their balance makes them seem very real. The way they move their feet, bodies and head make them seem more real than many animals i've seen in other games with more realistic graphics. In this way the world also makes you feel as if you are witnessing something very familiar and natural.The water and sand in the game interact in a way that put me right back in my sandbox when I was 5 years old and that alone was amazing.I am a little sad that there's only 94 reviews so far. I was expecting more by now and I guess VR still needs to become more accessible and cheaper, but at the same time the impact this game makes on your senses really shows what VR is capable of besides impaling things, so I hope in time people will find this game and be able to experience it.  I think a lot of the time good games and movies take a while to sink in.My jaw dropped seeing that tear open in the sky and seeing...oh spoiler I guess...(Even better than Out of this World)
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the adventure mode--this is one of my new favorite VR games. Some might argue it's a bit too short, but the length is appropriate and justified thanks to consistently fresh ideas. Amazing atmosphere overall, with simple yet creative puzzles. While other "artsy" games may fail to offer an entertaining or unique gameplay experience, this balances its artistic vision and presentation with very engaging design. My only gripes have to do with the presence of some invisible walls, and loading transitions not being as seamless as possible. The sandbox mode seems really appealing considering the dynamic nature of the game, so I can't wait to play around with that.I'm glad I held off buying this on PSVR to play on my Index. Thank you Éric Chahi and team, I hope there are more games to come, VR or otherwise.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best visual experiences in VR ever. One of my new favourites to introduce people to VR.Puzzles are pretty good, although there were times I knew what the solution was and it was tedious to implement.Sandbox mode is fun although I am not super happy about needing to get collectibles to unlock all the components of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting game but feels half way between an art gallery and a puzzle game. I found I could play it for about an hour or so before I had enough of it. I don't like the game-play where you are forced to stay in a linear set of problems but I think that is some kind of a tutorial chain. Looking forward to trying the sandbox mode.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: A really stellar and polished game. Beautiful from beginning to end. The atmosphere is incredible. It took about 3 hours to beat and that was including getting stumped on some puzzles. The puzzles were actually quite fun to solve and the land deformation showcased was also great to experience in VR. The sandbox is a ton of fun as well and is a good peaceful time when you just wanna chill. There's really no negatives I can say about this game tbh.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: i've yet to finish Paper Beats but what i've played so far i've loved. It's weird and beautiful. Serene and intense. Thought provoking and inane. It really is the closet a game has come to art to me. Don't let that turn you off though. there really is some game here and i was surprised at how tricky some of the puzzles are. Don't miss this as it's got some of the best and most original set-pieces in VR. It's also really well optimised and polished and runs like a dream at 120fps on my Index.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Get stoned, sit back, relax and enjoy.Smooth as buttah gameplay, Visually stunning an excellent relaxing Environmental Puzzle adventure.The audio is this game is excellent! FOR SURE play this with good headphones!I am obsessed with VR games and this is for sure my top 10 games to play on VR!Dear Developers: this is amazing! Please do more!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: OMG this game Is just SOOOOOO awesome! I dont know what exactly does it for me but being a part of a seemingly real breathing world! Everything about it is satisfying! If your into puzzel, adventure, God sim this is it! Such a great game I really hope the Devs make something else like this. A REAL Sim with much larger scope. BEAUTIFUL GAME!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant art exhibition. Extremely slow-paced, which is something I don't think I get enough of in games. Go in with patience and the understanding that being confused and not really understanding what is going on is 100% part of the game and I'm pretty sure going in and reading detailed reviews or even watching too much of the trailer videos will reduce some of the experience of understanding the rules of this world, which is what it is about, as a game.It requires patience, but it doesn't feel tedious to me. The most common negative reviews seem to be from people who do find it tedious. This is in no way an action game; don't expect it to be one.I think this would still be good as a flat game but it absolutely 100% benefits from being VR.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, yet I still don't understand what the hell was going on, but I still recommend it for an amazing VR experience and atmosphere.Creature designs were interesting.  Puzzles were not too difficult except for one annoying one that involved the reel-to-reel tape player near the end.I will go back and try to find the rest of the hidden blips to unlock more creatures in sandbox mode.Recommended.Checkout my gameplay of it here
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game, its one of my favourites of 2020. The game is puzzle based & you manipulate the world & creatures. Even though the creatures are not realistic looking their behaviour, animation & sound design is exceptional & they are convincing as living creatures. I really like the way the game looks & presents a surrealistic universe where things at first don't really make sense until you start to interact. Its refreshing to see imagination used in gaming especially in VR where immersion factor can really bring you out of mundane reality. One or two minor issue i had, although the game looks great there was some not so good or convincing areas. I guess with it being out on psvr there are limitations.  Sometimes the snapping to take control of something was fiddly.The very start of the story & menu, where you are in  the real world just isn't that well done imo.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: This is a puzzle game, that's not a game. More of an 4 hour art musical ... something. Really not sure what to call it. Never played anything like it. Not sure if i understood the story, but you help some paper animals travese the landscape. They are hindered by different puzzles.Great music, great visuals. I loved it from start to finish!
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: It's a pretty nice place to escape too, and yeah it's short, it's also quite a magical/unique trip  I think at sub-20 bucks it's priced right where it should be, but if that kind of thing upsets you, might be worth waiting for the inevitable steam sale.  Another user mentioned they got motion sickness, quite surprised to hear this, I'm not able to play Boneworks for more than a few minutes before I basically have to lay down for 20-30 mins to recover, and this game has zero motion-sickness for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: An amazing game and VR experience. I spent about 4 hours playing it through, taking my time.  The negatives, not many... a few of the scenes/puzzles fell a little flat to me relative to previous ones, and the levels are not large, constrained. Not much room for exploring.  Still, these are minor quibbles.  The plus side, great art, sound, animation and AI. A compelling world with some pretty amazing scenes. Frankly, I was blown away by much of it. And though I've finished the game, I'll be going back through some of the levels and will also try the sand box playground. I've never come across anything quite like it.  Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Experience a dreamlike odyssey through a wild and simulated ecosystem. Take off on an adventure! Connect with exotic and surprising creatures. Shape the environment to solve puzzles. Or let your imagination guide you through an immersive sandbox.
_childDocuments_.name: Paper Beast

_childDocuments_.review: Recently finished the game, but I would not recommend it at its current price.SOME POINTS-A lot of the characters of the story do not have an in-game model, just a portrait, and at many points in the story you have your guys staring at a wall while this portrait is talking, not acceptable in a game of this price, very very immersive breaking.-The music tracks are good, but very few, I personally expected a couple more songs for the battle theme for example-The quests are very grindy and repetitive, if you are not into that stay away-Many times instead of getting to play the actual game, you get a narrator over pictures of the anime telling the story, even then some content was cut.-The guild upgrade system feels very lazy-You get to increase your bond with members that go in quests with you, but you can ONLY see how far they are into bond levels by adding them to your group, by the time you are at endgame with 16 characters, it can be quite a mess to find out who needs points with who, it feels like a special menu with a table of everyone with everyone would be easy to make and avoid this mess-A lot of content was only half-dubbed-A franchise well known for its eyecandy fan-service had a day 1 patch to censor every upskirt into a black void. Granted you can put every single character in a swimsuit, and some of the characters show more underboob than clothing, it leads me to question myself why that censoring was even needed, it is absolutely pointless censoring in that just the swimsuits negates it, if they were trying to "hide" something. Not to mention false advertisement as in trailers they were marketed in full view.-The battle system is fun, and probably the only good thing you can take out of this mess, unless you are a hardcore Fairy Tail fan.CONCLUSIONIt feels like they tried to add too much with too few resources, they really did cut a lot of corners with this one and it shows, it is personally my take that instead of lazily telling stories through pictures, they should have just added as much resources (character models, locations, music) as possible in a smaller single contained arc of the story, and then maybe releasing a continuation with this then newfound better quality.The game as it is will give you some fun, but better wait to get it for 20-30 bucks if you are a fan, where you can at least forgive lazy, 70-80 bucks for this is absolutely unacceptable. I am very very unhappy for having paid such ammount for a mediocre game that adds salt to wound by doing a stealth patch for pointless censoring.
_childDocuments_.name: FAIRY TAIL

_childDocuments_.review: This will be my first review on a game ever. I am only writing this to very politely say The game is fun, I enjoyed my playthrough very much. However, I purchased the Deluxe edition and for some reason... it included pointless lacrima they could've made available through maxing out your laboratory, and some costumes. And then, about a month later, they release DLC that wasn't included in the Deluxe edition?!?! Especially for things that they could've just made available on release. Again, the game is amazing I enjoyed it. But this is worse than EA. To conclude, TIL: Don't buy deluxe editions at full price if they don't include season passes because you will be very disappointed. And I am passing this information on to others who may make the same mistake that I did.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not quite sure why I bothered to put as much time into this as I ended up doing. Stubbornness? Self pity? Pure boredom? All likely.I read and disregarded the negative reviews, and really wanted to give this a chance. I had high hopes for it after hearing about it a long while before it's release, and one day it suddenly showed up again and had been released the day before. $60 down the drain.There are, outside of the actually modelled villain characters in the game a total of less than 20 enemy models in the entire game. Dark wizard/bandit (shared models, holding different weapons), giant wolf, bird, whale, monkey, mermaid,  lizard knights of maybe 2-3 varieties which is still being generous, block demons, rock monster... and honestly I can't even remember if there were any more than that. They generously recolor them in different zones to signify progression, but even grinding end-game you're just fighting clusters of these generic, borderline insultingly repetitive enemies. If you're like me and you try to do most of the "sidequests" (if you can call them that as they're literally just stuff looted off the ground and handed in) before progressing story, the fights involving the actually uniquely modelled villains from the show are few and far between. Don't even get me started on the actual models though, as many reviews will also point out they blatantly just didn't want to model many of the plot-relevant characters. There are so many visual novel-esque scenes with mugshots talking over a still shot from the show for what were mildly epic moments in the actual anime. As a fan of the show, with the game targetted almost purely at people who were fans, it just feels awkward in so many of the scenes.A laughable quote i read about the game is that the main town feels "alive" and is fully fleshed out. Guess what, it's generic alleys and a fountain, and SIX (6!) unique models walking around. Boy, girl, woman, man, old man, old woman. I stood in one spot near the guild hall and saw 7 of the same purple dressed woman standing around, or just wandering pointlessly back and forth.There is a relationship system between your unlockable characters where you get mini skits, like in the Fire Emblem series. But big shocker here, half of the characters don't even get skits for their rank ups because they couldn't even be creative enough to come up with lines for normally lesser interactive characters. Just recycled victory screen animations and you're done, rank 1 of 3 achieved. Lazy. The battle system got old so fast that I did the last half of the game with the animations turned off. Even on higher difficulties you can just blanket enemies with attacks and its over in a few seconds. Once you start getting your chains, you're forced to watch attack animations and idly click who goes next until the chain ends. At max level, you essentially just burst everything down with these chains and it feels like you've earned absolutely nothing. Final boss of the game I finished with two chains with one round of buffs in between. Fascinating. Nearly 42 hours I spent playing this. Still not sure why. I did however get 100% of the achievements, the last of which was mindlessly completing every job request in the game, which boiled down entirely to changing maps, killing 10-20 of the exact same enemies you've been fighting since level 1, teleport back to the guild, hand in. There are 50 jobs like this. I spent nearly 3 hours trying to finish that god forsaken grind out of pure spite. I'm not even going to touch the censorship issue since it's moddable anyways, and at that you're genuinely not missing out on much. Also not going to comment on the hundreds of dollars of DLC because its insulting at best. I'm only writing this review because I was alerted at the new "dungeon" DLC, laughing internally that they're very likely charging you to kill the exact same enemies just with a bit more hp.If this game were on sale 75-90%? Maybe get it, it was a time sink if I'm being generous. But I made the mistake of buying it at full price and I severely regret it.*Edited to allow comments, never noticed it wasn't allowed by default.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that does unfortunately suffer from KOEI being.... Well KOEI. The DLC is absolutely insane, but honestly I saw this coming as all you have to do is look at Dead Or Alive and you see the same thing. What makes this worse is for those who paid for the deluxe don't even get the season pass, we all paid an extra £15 for basically nothing.   It makes it hard to recommend, because I can see going forward any content that may come out for this game being heavily pay walled as well as overpriced, I mean the season pass is nearly the price of the game again.... And to be honest it's not worth it.  It sucks, because honestly the game is pretty fun. It captures the feel of the series so well. The combat animations are all well done and fun to watch through (Even if some go on a little too long, looking at you Lucy). The voice acting is alright and the story stays mostly loyal to the series arcs it follows. There are upgrades both for your guild and your characters, well sort of you can equip Lacrima to boost stats. There are plenty of side quests, even if they are on the repetitive side and can become a bit of a chore to get through. There is a good amount of dialogue and banter between the characters. A good amount of moves at your disposable and overall a good challenge if you play on a higher difficulty.For me the game runs great, I have personally had no issues with crashing or bugs or other technical problems.I like the game, I really do..... But I will admit I have a bias because I love the series so I can forgive some faults, and there are some pretty glaring ones. The main ones being just how many characters don't even get a model, or are even mentioned at all (Freed, Evergreen and Bickslow are the ones that come to mind off the top of my head). Along with that NPC models are reused WAY to much, you will see the same person over and over and over.... This is just lazy.Speaking of lazy..... As I said just now there are so many characters that don't get models so during the Grand Magic Games, for example, you will find generic mobs in the place of what should be guild members. I mean Flare is the only one in RavenTail that got a model, Ichiya the only one for Blue Pegasus, Kagura for Mermaid Heel. Now I understand that not every character needs to be in the game, but there are quite a few that should be there, that are not.And I feel I have to mention it.... The day one censoring. It does not make any sense. You block panty shots with normal clothing.... But you have no problem with having, and selling, swimsuits that... Well... Show panties. What logic is that.Ugh sounds more negative than positive doesn't it. And I won't lie It's a hard sell if you are not a fan of the series, especially at the price point. It's Fairytail, if you love it buy it... If not you can pass on it. I personally have enjoyed my time with it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a hard one to fully recommend, especially to folks not already a fan of the anime/manga series for which this was derived. On one hand, I really enjoyed my experience playing it. Sure, playing it to completion involved a bit of a grind, but I feel it was worth it, especially with how much charm there was to character interactions and faithfulness to the source material. On the other, I hate how little Koei Tecmo seemed to care about this game. Gust did a brilliant job at working with what the developers were given, but they weren't given all that much to work with.Story: We focus on the epilogue of the Tenrou Island arc, and skip 7 years ahead to the Grand Magic Games arc, soon to be followed by the Tartaros arc. Both are fun arcs, but this is way out in the middle of the series, and the lack of context will throw any newbie off course. Even casual viewers would still go in fairly confused. The game tries to alleviate this by providing an encyclopedia of past events, and occasional references during requests and character stories, but it doesn't have nearly the impact. If you're playing this game in Japan, it won't come as much of a surprise that they started where they did. Fairy Tail games going from the beginning of the series to the Tenrou Island arc have already been made in plentiful enough amounts. But none of these games were ever localized for the States, making for a lesser experience.Music: Fairy Tail's original soundtrack is one of the most recognizable parts of the original anime series. I can hear the beginning tracks and immediately pinpoint them to the show. One thing that always stood out to me is how much the soundtrack kind of resembled Atelier Rorona: The Alchemist of Arland's soundtrack, and vice-versa. In a way, this was a dream team in terms of music, and it really shows. It can have a pleasant, atmospheric feel during traversal and be notably hype during battle when it needs to be.Gameplay: I am so, so glad this was a turn-based RPG. This could have easily been just a brain dead, junk food arena brawler, but instead I get to play a Fairy Tail game with my favorite video game genre of all time, and it's fairly in-depth. The plethora of characters available have a plethora of moves available, all focusing on different ranges of attacks and attack types, fit to face opponents on a 3x3 grid. You start off with a 3-person team, which eventually grows to 5. Not bad at all, considering how many characters there are to select from. A lot of your time will be focused on bringing the Fairy Tail guild back to its former glory, and I honestly had a fun time exploring everything the gameplay had to offer.Characters: This will make or break it for some people. If your favorite characters aren't playable, why bother? Luckily, they have 16 different characters to put in your team by the end of the game. one a little too late, in my personal opinion, so there is a good chance your favorite made it in. People will miss classics like Cana/Kanna and members of the Thunder Legion (who don't even exist, according to the video game), and the characters that are there are only in Japanese, which, aside from a few characters, doesn't hold much of a candle to the much superior English dub the anime series provided. I won't blame people turned off by this. The game has Gray Fullbuster, Juvia Lockser, and Rogue Cheney playable, and I overall didn't mind playing in Japanese, so I got what I needed.Graphics: This is a point of contention for many. I can't in good taste say this looks like a PS2 game, but there are Japanese PS3 games that look better. NPC models are reused badly, monsters have palette swaps, major character models are missing, and the environments are nothing special. However, the major character models that are there look pretty faithful. I've seen people rag on the expressions in their faces, but I never saw an issue with them. For what the game is capable of doing, they look well enough. Plus, if you're mostly just focusing on the gameplay, and you're a fan of the series already, you'll enjoy the flashy special moves. Just don't expect state of the art current gen graphics.Technical: I didn't really see much in the way of technical problems on my copy. I run a pretty beefy rig, and it ran a smooth 1440p @60FPS, only experiencing the rarest of frame drops during certain multi-model enemy attacks. Others seem to have various issues, but I didn't really experience those, myself.Censorship: The fanservice show (that already censored most sections compared to the manga) censored upskirt shots. I'll be honest, I don't really care. The game doesn't offer much in the way of angles to justify censoring or uncensoring to begin with. I could see how some people can be upset with Lucy and Erza being restricted on this, considering their appeal and skimpier attire, but people are actually upset that Wendy (12) and Sherria (15) can't have their black voids removed? Pathetic.Conclusion: If you want the best experience with this game, watch the anime or read the manga up to the Tenrou Island arc first. If you like it enough, the game's worth your time. Is it worth it at $60? Well, people on the PS4 gobbled up the Final Fantasy VII Remake for $60 and called it a GOTY contender, despite being much shorter, much more bloated, and the combat replacement being more poor than what the original had to offer, so take that for what you will.
