_childDocuments_.review: + Fun combat+ Decent storytelling- Lazy story & graphical elements- Boring quest design- Wildly fluctuating difficulty- Subpar portSo we've actually gotten quite a few Fairy Tail games up to this point, but I'm pretty sure this is the first time that one has released outside of Japan, unless if you include that odd browser-based one. As someone that has seen all of the anime, I'd say it's about time. The series is perfect for a video game and I was excited to check it out.FAIRY TAIL is not only a disappointment for fans of the series, but is a disappointment for the studio. This comes from the same guys that do the excellent Atelier series, yet FAIRY TAIL never quite sticks the landing. The combat may be good and there's definitely a decent amount of effort put into giving an authentic Fairy Tail story experience, but there's so many issues along the way that it really brings down the experience. Wildly fluctuating difficulty, boring quest design, and even a subpar PC port to top it all off make this a tough sell, even to fans of the series. I'm honestly just disappointed. Fairy Tail is a massive series, we deserve better than this.Follow my  for more reviews + videos!

Despite the cons (that are listed below), as a hardcore fan...I think it's worth the buy.• You can play characters from other guilds• There is added content in interactions between characters, as well as individual characters. ex: (character interactions that the anime did not show as much). • It does include some arcs from the anime• There is more content even after the "main game", which I highly recommend you to continue to play.• It's pretty easy to play• There is content from filler episodes in the anime  • The game does not start from the beginning of the anime• Not many arcs are included in the game• You don't see all the guild members in Fairy Tail• You can't play every character in the Fairy Tail guild or in other guilds • There could've been a lot more added content/stories between characters ex: (there are bonds where sometimes if two characters have their bond increased, you'll get an interaction between them.) However, often times, there is no interactions, even among characters that in the anime did have some sort of a relationship. Even though certain characters haven't had interactions with each other in the anime, this was the time where they could've certainly explored with that.• Not many outfits than I thought there would be

_childDocuments_.review: Short version: If you like the anime and want to spend more time with the guild, then you'll like this game.If you are not a fan of the anime you most likely aren't looking this game up. It doesn't do anything new to change the JRPG genre. It does have a bit of customization for character builds which is nice. I certainly wasn't expecting that for this game. While they do a great job and staying accurate with the story, this game does not start at the beginning of the anime/manga but a little bit past the 50% mark. Be warned of some spoilers in case you were interested in later on starting the series.Graphics - Moving about the areas are nice, although townsfolk are not well designed. The real gem of the graphics is in the fighting animations, which can be turned off to speed up battles. Some scene animations are better than others, but not anything to brag about.Sound - There is no English VA, but the Japanese actors from the show do an excellent job here. Music from the series is also included which is a plus.Gameplay - The fights are fairly simple, but there is good progression. It does feel rewarding to level up your characters as they learn new abilities/power up existing moves. You can have a bit of variety with how you fight based on techniques as well as who your party contains. There are 3 options to choose from for difficulty between easy, normal and hard.If you don't have extremely high expectations, you will have fun with this game (particularly as a fan of the series). Graphics could be a bit better, but that isn't what I was looking for in this. I wanted something to enjoy to pass the time and I found it. Personally I don't think many games are worth the full price. As much as I like this I would still say wait for some type of sale.*yes they do include the beach outfits for all the characters

_childDocuments_.review: The game won't launch, some bonus items (Lacrimas) are missing, and apparently the very first patch censored stuff (pantyshots, to be precise) and performance is sub-par.I'm going to wait for patches to hopefully try it out, but this sure doesn't sound good right now.EDIT: Finally managed to launch the game thanks to black magic. I read some comments on the forums saying to plug a controller in and to close the Windows Explorer. I don't know for sure which one fixed it (probably the latter), but it allowed the game to boot again. Then I had to go and edit the settings' INI file to play in fullscreen rather than with a useless partially off-screen white window.Now that I've jumped through these hoops, I have about an hour and a half to see if the game runs well and if it's any good. Thanks Koei Tecmo.EDIT 2: Confirmed that closing the Windows Explorer + using Windows 7 compatibility mode is the key to running the game.As to how it performs... It's a mess. The game doesn't look bad in and out of itself, but some textures are pretty low-resolution and models aren't that refined either, so it should logically run fine even on computers that aren't next-gen ready. Despite that, it runs poorly at 1080p (granted, my computer is starting to be old, but it should still be enough to run this game properly) with 30-40fps on average and <10fps with some attacks, and even 720p doesn't help getting a stable 60fps target (dips to the 40fps range are frequent).In particular, particles and transparency effects seem to have a huge effect on framerate drops. Also, looking at my GPU's stats, it looks like it's close to 100% use almost all the time past the main menu, even at 720p. So I'm wondering what's going on behind the scenes. Anyway, unless you really want the early purchase bonuses Koei Tecmo are notorious for never ever re-releasing, wait for patches.EDIT 3: Bonus Lacrimas are available at last (but they aren't absolutely necessary, from what I've heard), and the second patch added tonnes of DLC with Koei Tecmo's usual awful business practices. By that, understand lots of overpriced items sold either individually or in packages, so you have to double-check not to buy stuff twice; it could have been solved by selling individual DLC also unlockable though a season pass or bundles, but no.Also edited  exactly was censored in the "original" review. I don't care much about pantyshots but it's still ridiculous to cover them up once the game is out (without any actual explanation), doubly so when trailers showed some less than one month before launch with no "game still in development, visuals and content subject to change" indication AND the game was already rated.Again, unless you really want to play the game now and/or want the bonus early purchase outfit: wait for patches, mods, and a sale. That is, if you're not discouraged by Koei Tecmo's actions so far.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Fairy Tail and I've been wanting a game for it ever since Gajeel showed up, and I always imagined it as either a action game like dmc series or any platinum game, or a warriors like one piece got, so when i heard it was a turn based rpg, the game already blew away my expections and I had high hopes for the game. I try to be as blind as I can when playing a game so I was surprised when it started me at the 7 year skip, which is fine because thats when a lot of the action kicks of and over arching story flows together really well. The game was outright lazy in all story elements and enemy avatars. one of the first missions is finding a man in a forest being harassed by some dark mage cronies, and they had some really well designed models and i thought they were going to diverge from the main story because the models seemed unique to this game. the next mission had us deal with smugglers, who looked exactly the same.What solidified my disappointment in the game is when I finally got through the tutorial, one of the worst Ive ever been through as each little mechanic needed a seperate battle encounter and cutscene/character dialouge before each one, and i could finally walk through Magnolia, I was expecting the the same feeling I got when I played Naruto Rise of a Ninja, a town that felt lived in and alive, and dont get me wrong, the town is beautiful and the detail is amazing, except for all the npcs just standing around. there are 6 models walking around the town, young boy, young girl, young man, young woman, old woman and old man. their models are spread around town so sparsely that i saw the same 3 models all at once on screen. And its not like the Trails of Cold Steel series they reuse alot of character models, but they recolor them so its not always obvious when your just running through town, FAIRY TAIL just outright copy and pasted them throughout town.I never got much farther than that because with the slogging of tutorials and the utter disappointment i felt seeing the same 6 people walking around town and the fact that they couldnt bother to atleast make a few throw away bandit type and wizard characters, the game did the minimum effort to make the game unique and alive, and if the devs didnt cut corners I imagine this game could have been so much more. If you love FAIRY TAIL like my brother loves star wars, you'll be ok with this game like he was ok with the sequels. For me the name is so much more than a texture and dialogue you can slap on a game or movie and call it good. This is a game with a Fairy Tail texture pack and thats about it, and if thats what you want, this game is for you, but it is definitly not what i would can a Fair Tail game.

_childDocuments_.review: FAIRY TAIL. This is an anime character game produced by GUST that is the dev team for the Atelier series and published by KOEI TECMO GAMES. It is based on the popular japanese manga FAIRY TAIL by Hiro Mashima. The first official news was released as surprise news ahead of the Tokyo Game Show 2019. The release was delayed, unlike the original schedule that was originally planned in March, but fortunately this game has come to us eventually! Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)In a nutshell, FAIRY TAIL GAME was even better than expected. Before experienced the game, the following two concerns have been raised by the community, according to pre-release information. One is that the game only has a story line that was in the middle of the original comics. The other is that the game has a turn-based combat, not a real-time action. Nevertheless, when you actually start playing, you will find that it is no longer a problem.Even if you don't know FAIRY TAIL, you can enjoy this game enough. To keep the story going smoothly, players are provided with some background knowledge about the stories and character info of the original manga. What's more, today's users have the ability to find what they want. If you're motivated by this game, you will experience animations and comics for the original FAIRY TAIL. It will be a great pleasure definitely.Gameplay is mainly about accepting missions in the guild and completing them. As you play to make the guild to be the top in the city, the stories are gradually opened. The gameplay time for the main story is about 20 hours, and it even takes about 30 hours to experience all achievements and events. Important cutscenes support full voice character dubbing, and the others have partial voice acting. Battle is a turn-based, but it features fast-paced magic action battles. Also the anime character modeling is pretty good, and the extreme magic combo with the familiar is so cool. FAIRY TAIL. This is a pretty fun anime character game. Most anime character games focus too much on characters, so there are quite a few broken gameplays, but this game is different. The gameplay itself is fun really. In particular, the fast-paced battle action and special moves of characters make players more immersed in the game. Honestly, it gives the first impression that the full price is a bit expensive. However, given the great event scenes with full voice acting, and nice anime character modeling, it's worth trying. It is a great pleasure to be able to experience a well-made anime character game. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: tldr: Fairy Tail fans can enjoy this simple JRPG if you find it for under 25$ (I wouldn't pay the full costs for anything, aside from maybe ONE costume for your ultimate waifu/husbando), no DLC needed (but DD is nice), and it's mostly bonus fan service costumes.The Story does not start from the beginning of the Anime/Manga, rather around the point of a time-skip (Tenrou Island), and goes to Tartaros. That said, if you've seen the show in it's entirety, it sometimes feels like an abridged version of a select amount of the full story, but YOU get to punch those that harm your friends and family, with Natsu, Lucy, or even Ichiya!It does have points where it doesn't show models for many characters that don't NEED one, seeming like it's cutting corners or just not wasting resources, though voice lines exist. But of the playable characters, and some more useful or more often seen ones, they look FANTASTIC. Most generic enemies use the same handful of models, often recolored.This game made me want to play more JRPG style games, so if you are a veteran to JRPGs, but don't know Fairy Tail, you may find this mediocre. I found it to be a good gateway and introduction, as the closest to any other JRPG I've played is the mainline Pokémon games.I got 100% achievements in the 62.7 hours I played, and it CAN be done faster, or enjoyed much slower. DLC is not needed for 100%, and are mostly just alternative costumes, on top of the 2-4+ the characters have in the base game. 4 Characters can also be obtained via DLC, being Lyon, Levy, Lisanna, and Elfman, and none are required for the Super Strong late game, so you aren't missing out unless one of them happens to be your favorite character.

_childDocuments_.review: I would not recommend this game to anyone other than those who are fans of anime or manga. The main reason is that it isn't a good JRPG in my opinion, so I don't see the point of playing it unless you are a fan. Some points I want to mention about it:The combat system does not fit the game. The system works on a 3x3 square, where the different attack moves are in different shapes, which is decent when fighting multiple enemies. The problem is that most of the boss fights are a single enemy in one grid, never moving, spawn new enemies, or interracts with the combat system. So the fighting is mostly based on whether you want to use the move that does 4 damage or the move that does 5 damage, which makes combat in the big boss fights so boring.After finishing an arc you can unlock new characters from that arc. The problem there is that there are about 5-6 different character stories 3 stories each. When you complete one, the game reminds you that you can play the character stories by showing you 2 of the starting cutscenes right after each other. It is just bombarding for people like me who take it one story at a time.My problem with the game is mostly just the combat, but the other point just makes me like it less, so overall I don't recommend it unless you already like Fairy Tail.

_childDocuments_.review: When I saw that a Fairy Tail game was coming to the West, I was excited since I grew up on the anime and manga.  I decided to support the franchise and pre-ordered the deluxe version of the game.  On launch I had a small issue, but everything worked out and I was able to start playing.The game play is super fun with the magic spells and leveling up.  All great, especially how your magic spells level up and grow with you (though they eventually stop after your first time limit breaking).  The cast of characters are all really fun, especially because I got to play with all my personal favorites.  However, there is quite a lacking number of characters, that even if they weren't playable, are not present or are only a 2D image.  It was quite lackluster doing the Second Origin scene with Ultear and Jellal with 3D models and Meredy as a 2D image that popped up when she spoke.Storywise there was a lot cut out, which I get, you need to make the story shorter so that it can fit the game.  However, it did skip over quite a few scenes that were quite important to the arcs that were portrayed.  Overall I want to say that the game was good for what it was, however, that all disappeared when I saw the recently added DLC.  I bought the Deluxe, but now $160 of costumes have been added as well as a $60 Season Pass, the same price as the base game, that has far less content than the already pared down main game.  I don't know about other people, but this is just outrageous greed.  Half of these costumes should have been added to the base game, just as several of Lucy's Star Dresses were added as well as Erza's armors once a certain point in the game was reached.  Let alone that $57 of the costumes are just recolors/retextures of costumes already in the game.  The Season Pass is not worth the same amount as the base game for what you get, as well as the fact that the Season Pass should have been included in the Deluxe Edition even if the initial price should've gone up.  Just to add, Code Vein (another game I Pre-ordered the deluxe edition of), was about $80 and that included Base Game, Pre-Order bonuses, AND the Season Pass.  So yeah, I can't recommend this game anymore, even if you are a hardcore fan because they went from making a game to making a cash grab.

But it's incredibly fun to play through if you're a Fairy Tail fan and it's finally an RPG. Finally an anime adaptation that's not another cloned fighting game.It's a very straightforward JRPG and it's got some great quality of life features. Almost all skills have fully featured animations, for every playable character. They look amazing and make every fight fun and worth it AND you can turn them off once you've had enough eye candy and just want fights to go by faster. There's even an auto feature so you don't need to manually kill every single small mob for a quest, the AI will choose the most appropriate attack or heal and take care of everything for you. Grinding is fast and fun as you can summon up to 99 monsters to fight all at once, or as Erza would call it, training warm up.Probably one of the biggest letdowns. They've included two major arcs: Grand Magic Games and Tartaros. Sounded great in the trailers until you play the game and notice they didn't even bother animating most characters, there's cutscenes with characters literally talking to the air and we're left to guess what happens with them. These are just some of the characters that are missing from the Grand Magic Games arc alone, some of them get mentioned and have a few dialogue lines but no actual in game model:The cutscenes don't help either as instead of a massive event with evenly matched competitors, it feels like you're fighting in the back alley with whoever managed to show up. The Tartaros arc is cut even shorter. The cut content doesn't even make that much sense as they seemingly had the time to animate and model a swimsuit scene in between the fights. And speaking of the swimsuit scene, somehow the same company that chose to add bikinis over plot has also pushed a censorship patch day one to prevent upskirts. A great priority when the Steam discussion board is full of people who STILL can't even open the game. The game was clearly not intended for a PC release, keyboard/mouse controls are a bad joke and there's not way to remap them without editing the game files yourself - ofcourse the publisher claims it's a bug and totally not a neglect for the Steam release. On the same note you better give up on any hopes of 4k or widescreen support, at most you can edit your game files manually to get a custom resolution and even that isn't guaranteed to work. There's a total of 16 playable characters available in the game. All characters get at least 3 costumes: default, swimsuit and alternative color. Alternative color is the best joke out of them as it's literally just that, the same costume you already have with slightly different colors, nothing actually new. Lucy and Erza benefit from having a bunch of extra costumes compared to others - mostly due to the same models being used in combat animations - but otherwise your choices are extremely limited. Juvia and Jellal have the ground breaking feature of having two identical costumes where the only difference is in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hat.I'm sure this will be corrected with massively overpriced DLC though. As is tradition for KOEI games.Despite all the negative things that I've mentioned I've had a blast playing through the game. If you're a Fairy Tail fan you're likely to enjoy the hell out of this game because it's fun and true to the source material. If it's the first time you're hearing about Fairy Tail you'd be better off checking the manga/anime first.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is okay. But just okay. For a £50+ game I had expected more which is why I am giving it a negative review.Essentially, the game is quite lazy. Within about an hour of starting, you'll have encountered all the major mechanics of the game and realise that this is all there is to it. The writing is excellent, in that, if you have read the manga or watched the anime, you'll feel like this is very close to home, with the characters having dialogue that fits and the world generally feeling like Earthland, I mean, I love the anime and I'm not even a big anime lover and I feel so bad about writing a negative review about it. The animation is pretty well done, the combat system is is fairly basic but workable. The voice acting is done by the original Japanese voice actors and delivered well (as far as I can tell as I can't speak Japanese.)But alas, the game is just quite lazy. The maps are quite small with a lot of repeated NPC models. The requests (or jobs) you get from the guild are essentially just "Go here, kill x amount of y" and then get teleported back. With such a great plethora of characters the game has and it only lets you play around 16? Not too great. There are deliberate skips in terms of the animations, Lucy's summons for example do not appear in game, you just get a little picture of them flash up on the screen when she casts it, and then the attack lands.Another, more minor complaint is where in Fairy Tail the game starts. Oddly, it starts, the prologue anyway, during the final battle with Hades in the Tenrou island arc. During this time you are basically just hitting A or X as the game demands, limiting you to only being able to make one choice during the prologue, before the game progresses to the main story. This means it has skipped a lot of earlier arcs, including the Tower of Heaven! It makes sense, because you then need to build the guild up from scratch again, but it does also mean you skip a lot of Fairy Tail. And as a final, somewhat petty point; no cutscenes or clips from the anime are included as far as I can tell. This means you are basically stuck with the in game graphics through out which isn't bad, but a lot of similar games will make use of the material they are based on to help set the scene. There's nothing particular bad or wrong about the game, it just feels lazy and drastically over priced. I'll maybe pick it up some day in the future when it is cheaper.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a little split on this decision, but I'll give it a passing mark, .  It's like a 55/45 than a 70/30 like to dislike ratio for me, mostly from the issues that stem from the controls on PC.I'll start with the glaring problems I see from a technical standpoint first before speaking about the rest of the game.While this isn't the only game to do this, I'm still disappointed that this game only shows controller prompts, even if you're using keyboard.  This is a $60+ game, the least they could do is accommodate for keyboard users as well.Second keyboard-related issue while we're on the subject, there's no way to rebind your keys from the settings menu.  Despite the fact that there are key bindings, you can't actually rebind your keys from settings.Third  REALLY bizarre key binds. Like WASD for movement is normal and sure, I've used JKLI before... for attacks in fighter games (L is your default jump key bind btw) along with WASD movement, but TYUG are used for camera angle movement...  Like I have a mouse and we don't really need to use it for camera angle movement during times where we need to select something specific onscreen anyways, why couldn't camera angle movement be mouse movement bound?This next one is tutorial specific, but when I tried using my mouse for A and B when first applying a Lacrima, it didn't work.  Then I opened the equipment menu when not in the tutorial, on the same screen and it worked... I really don't know why it works like that...  Same with certain scenarios as well, the mouse will just cease all functionality, so you need to use the corresponding keyboard bind for it instead.If there's any controller issues, I'll leave that for the controller people to rip 'em a new one if there's issues on that end.... I don't really like leaving this section on a sour note so I'll give them some credit in the technical section.  They at least have SOME advanced menu options, which is better than just "Quality: Low/Med/High" with that being the only option.  It's not saying much, but I've seen worse.You can see the character models and some attacks in the trailer and they're nice.I love the fact they brought the magic circles back for some of the attacks and it looks good.  Kinda missed some of the first season aesthetics and it was nice they incorporated some of those into this game.There was a point where I noticed some transitions with anime images and it felt a bit... cheap, otherwise I don't think I see an outstanding problem that's worth discussing.For gameplay, you have to fight enemies on a 3x3 grid and certain spells have different ways to hit the board.  For example, there's a spell that can hit in an X shape where it ignores the cardinal spaces from the center square.  It's fun if you're really craving that turn-based JRPG battle system.You also walk around maps and battle enemies and complete side quests.  It seems fairly standard, up to the part I got to.Voices.It's Japanese only for voices, but English text is shown.  I don't mind it, but some people do take issue that the voices aren't dubbed over.  You may notice sometimes the voices cut off toward the end of a cutscene, but it's pretty negligible all things considered.Normally, the characters only say a word or two, referencing the general mood of what they're gonna say or a specific thing they're talking about, kind of like Fire Emblem: Awakening.  This being a full cost PC game though can make it seem a little lazy.  There are also some characters unvoiced or not modeled.Aside from a few words that I heard that didn't entirely match the English translation here 'n there, I didn't see any glaring issues with it, but I also cannot fully speak Japanese so there may have been some things I didn't hear right.Honestly, I can see reasons to either get this game or not.  If they do fix the key binding issues on PC, I'd say this is a definite buy if you like Fairy Tail or JRPGs, but as it stands, if you're really looking for some Fairy Tail gameplay and can't afford a controller at the moment, I'd suggest waiting for a sale or until the issues are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: IntroductionFAIRY TAIL, developed by Gust Co. Ltd. and published by Koei Tecmo, is a turn-based role-playing game (RPG) based on the popular manga and anime series by Hiro Mashima. Released in 2020, the game aims to bring the magical adventures of Natsu Dragneel and the Fairy Tail guild to life. However, it falls short in several areas, leaving fans with a mixed experience.Story and SettingThe game attempts to follow key story arcs from the anime, beginning with the Tenrou Island arc and progressing through the Grand Magic Games and Tartaros arcs. Unfortunately, the adaptation feels lackluster and more like fan-made content rather than a polished, official product. Key moments from the anime do not translate well into the game, and the storytelling often feels disjointed and uninspired.GameplayFAIRY TAIL features traditional turn-based combat with a few unique twists. Players can form a party from a roster of over a dozen characters, each with their own special abilities and magical attacks. While there are multiple attacks available for each character, players often find themselves relying on the same few moves repeatedly, making the combat feel monotonous over time.Graphics and PresentationThe game boasts vibrant, cel-shaded graphics that capture the aesthetic of the anime. Character models are detailed and expressive, and the magical effects during combat are visually impressive. However, the environments are often repetitive and lack variety, detracting from the overall visual appeal.Content and ReplayabilityWhile the game offers a variety of side quests, character missions, and guild management activities, these elements quickly become repetitive. Trying to clear 100% of the game involves long and tedious hours of collecting items and defeating enemies repeatedly. Leveling up characters to the maximum level can take around 50 hours, further extending the grind and reducing enjoyment.Pros:Voice Acting: Original anime cast reprising their roles adds authenticity.Cons:Poor Story Adaptation: The game fails to use the anime’s story effectively, feeling more like fan-made content.Monotonous Combat: Limited effective attacks lead to repetitive combat.Repetitive Gameplay: The game quickly becomes a grind, especially when trying to clear 100%.Long and Tedious Leveling: Reaching the max level for all characters can take 50 hours, diminishing the fun.Not Worth the Time or Money: Overall, the game does not provide a rewarding experience for the time and money invested.ConclusionFAIRY TAIL attempts to bring the beloved anime to life in a video game format but falls short in many areas. The poor adaptation of the story, repetitive gameplay, and tedious leveling make it a disappointing experience. Fans of the series may enjoy the initial nostalgia, but the game ultimately feels like a missed opportunity. Given the significant time investment required for a less-than-rewarding experience, FAIRY TAIL is not worth the time or money.

Then what made me dislike the game a lot was the inconsistency of dialogue, character models and subtitles. There are several scenes that lack these randomly throughout the game. Then as you move on the characters stopped talking and we're just humming while the subtitles went on. _childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is a huge disappointment. For an action-packed anime like fairy tail, the JRPG formula was a bad idea. The moves are flashy but in a turn-based setting it feels sluggish and slow.There are maybe like 10 models (excluding characters) so its quite common to see the exact same NPC  several times in the same area.Switching in and out of the turn setting is very very sluggish and slow. So in areas where you need to combat many many creatures it feels very tedious.My biggest gripe with the game is how little player Agency you have. There are a lot of times where you get "guest" characters on your team. These characters will operate on their own and often fill the empty places in your team. Then you will get the prompt to change your team, which you can't because the main character is locked and can't be changed. Thus being a useless prompt. More often than not you are forced to use a certain characters.Between that and the 80% cutscenes that make up the game. You're better off just watching the anime.Personally I feel like a Legend of Zelda, or Warrior style combat system would better suit the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could split the review but here's the TL:DR This game is thumbs up if... You really like Fairy Tail -and- you own a controller. It's pretty faithful to the show, gameplay is simple but fun. It captures a lot of the heart and spirit of the show. Would recommend. However I would not recommend generally because Keyboard and Mouse support is non existent, it's essentially unplayable without a controller. All the prompts are using controller buttons, you can't rebind keys. It's a very halfassed PC adaptation. The story is nonsensical if you haven't seen the show. They introduce literally 20 characters to you in the very opening scene. It's in the most confusing part of the FT storyline (Everyone was time locked away for 7 years and now they're back doing a wizard S test but somehow a giant demon dragon shows up and there's a dark magic dude who is obsessed with another dark magic dude and then 30 seconds later it drops into dad drama about a character who secretly knew who were father was for the last decade but didn't speak up and then have an emotional reunion that another character who we also don't know sets up and spies on them. Gameplay is also not great, but not horrible, but if you have no investment in the show or characters you should just play other titles. It's a pretty generic RPG, grind up levels, etc. There are many many better title to play in the RPG space though. This also does not feel like a $60 AAA title. I would expect it in the 30-35$ realm. Buy it on sale if you must but avoid full price for sure.There is also some nonsense about censoring panty shots, etc. Please don't let that be the reason you don't buy this game. There are plenty of valid reasons to not recommend this game I wish people would stop focusing on that element.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I'll say I have little to no history with the Fairy Tail series. This game can be summed up in one word: RUSHED. The game starts you off assuming you know every detail about the series (I do not) and makes no attempt to explain whats happening or who anybody is. The story is the biggest example of the game being rushed, through 2/3 of the game the story is pretty decently laid out with lots of gameplay mixed in but, when it gets to the last 1/3 after the Grand Magic Games the game starts telling you whats going on through slideshows instead of letting you play leaving a very empty feeling when the plot is progressing so much with no input from the player. If a character doesn't appear in a battle they have no in game model they just get a little portrait and that's it. The combat is fun to look at...the first couple times, then you start getting these mid to late game spells some of which have unskippable animations that are at times 15+ SECONDS LONG for sometimes little damage. Some characters in the game are too weak some characters are too strong some are Lucy and do nothing. This game is just not worth your time and the ending is one of the biggest sequel/DLC baits I've ever seen a piece of media do. If you want something that's similar to how this game is structured but done better I recommend the Trials of Mana Remake that came out earlier this year, It's cheaper and is a better game overall.

_childDocuments_.review: From what I've seen in the trailers and what I've been promised falls short of what I paid for when I purchased the Deluxe Edition of Fairy Tail. I have to say that this release of the game took me from anger, sadness to simple and complete utter disappointment. I am disappointed in Koei Tecmo and it is sad, in fact it breaks my heart to see such a beautiful and popular franchise being destroyed in this manner, it just breaks my heart.It is saddening to see that death by DLC is suddenly the norm, in fact it was not present at all BEFORE release, the game itself is already missing core content and they have the gall to add over 50 overpriced DLC items that should have been part of the original deluxe edition purchase in my view.And yes I know about the day one censorship patch. It doesn't adversely affect how I play the game but the very reason they even did this is enough to upset me...it was simply pointless to do what they just did and I don't support such nonsense.This is a wonderful game, it's characters are wonderful, the battles are wonderful...but unfortunately that is where it ends, lazy game design, missing voice overs and sometimes completely missing whole characters by replacing them with Portraits and Portrait cutscene about as bad as what happened in Soul Calibur 6. You cannot do such shoddy work for such a potentially huge and promising game!I am an avid fan of Fairy Tail I've watched every episode, every movie, even Fairy Tail Zero, and quite frankly I was excited at the prospect of playing a Fairy Tail game!There is a lot of things that was done right in this game including battles but unfortunately lazy game design incomplete scenes where your characters are talking to portraits and in my opinion there should be a lot more voiced scenes in the game itself especially in the in-game scenes (outside of the "voiced" scenes) where significant interactions between two characters should have been voiced or dubbed.This was a wonderful idea but unfortunately a host of issues and missing content makes this release of Fairy Tail a very poorly executed game and quite frankly a huge ripoff as suddenly a lot of DLC is suddenly present AFTER the release and a worse yet day one censorship patch that really did not need to be there in the first place.It is with a broken heart filled with utter disappointment that Koei Tecmo would betray my trust so badly, that I do not recommend this half baked release of Fairy Tail, your money is better spent elsewhere. I'm done supporting cash grab stunts like this and I'm done with Koei Tecmo.

_childDocuments_.review: CAUTION, BE SURE YOU HAVE A CONTROLLER.I am not usually one to review games, but felt compelled to do so this time.  Between the extreme of thumbs up or down, I choose thumbs up, because however you slice it, I did enjoy myself.  However, there are some real problems with the game. I am not generally a RPG or JRPG player, so my views may be outside the normal viewpoint, or understanding of development and general features of these games.  It took me, according to Steam, 38.1 hours to complete the main story through the end.  It took 52.2 hours to reach the end of content, including all achievements, though some quests can be infinitely replayed beyond this point.  I would not say I speed played, but I didn't go as slow as possible either.Cons.1. There are control issues, and serious problems for people who want to play with a keyboard and mouse.  The game should warn people that a controller is not just strongly suggested, but practically necessary.  Lucky for me, I have a steam controller.  Even with the controller, and it may just be my Steam controller, the camera feels clunky.2. You can play the game and gain enough insight to generally understand the story, but there's going to be a whole lot of things you don't quite get if you are not already familiar with the story of Fairy Tail outside this game.  The game starts about halfway through the series story.  This is apparently because various games on various platforms in the past have already covered all the previous story arcs even though this game is not  a sequel to those games.3.  Important characters to the story are missing, or just assumed to be around.  You might just get a picture with text for many characters who don't appear.  While she's not a main Character, I suspect the Siren mermaid monsters use a head that was originally intended to be the character Bisca Connel, née Mulan.  Original story details are also changed or missing to make things quicker and easier.  4. The price is high.  Generally I would not pay so much for a game like this, but if I had it to do over, I probably would.  However, I am already a fan of the Fairy Tail universe outside this game.5.  Grinding.  The game can get a bit grindy, though I don't think it's as big a problem as some people say.  The game has an option to turn off the combat animations if you get tired of them, which makes combat much faster.Pros.  1.  Usually feels like the characters and world it's supposed to represent.2 Combat is fun, and properly represents the characters.  Inclusion of concepts like Unison Raids was cleverly implemented.3 Inclusion of certain details, like Lucy's House, and the exploration of locations is even more fun for those familiar with the story.4 I like the soundtrack.  Obviously they didn't pay to get the rights to the show soundtrack, which would have been much better, but it's enough in the same spirit to usually feel pretty close.Side issuesCensorship did not bother me at all, especially since overabundant fan service is actually something I don't like about Fairy Tail, but I can understand people who paid for something which was expected having it  changed after purchase.  For future buyers this should not be an issue since you know what to expect.  DLC content.  I agree it's a bit crazy, but it's also not even remotely necessary for the game.  It's really just pointless costume frills.  Just buy the game and don't worry about a bunch of overpriced costume sets.  ConclusionThe game certainly has some negatives, but I really did have a good time playing, and I wanted to come back to it whenever I could.  For most people, unless this is really your thing, or you really like Fairy Tail, I would suggest waiting for a sale, but if you really like this sort of game, or really like Fairy Tail, and you have a compatible controller, buy it and just ignore all the DLCs (as of the time of this post).

_childDocuments_.review: After 50 hours, I finished the game and got all achievements. The game doesn’t have much replay value when you finish the story and all quests (other than starting a new play through on harder difficulty).This game starts in the middle of a long sequence of battles that take place during the anime, with little to no context. As a fan of the anime, it was no problem as I knew why everything was happening. If someone who hadn’t watched the anime played this game, it’s fair to say they will have trouble following and having an interest in the story. It’s also worth noting that if you haven’t finished the anime there are major spoilers in this game.Regular requests become pretty boring after a while, there is no dialog or cut scenes just go kill x amount of y. I also think the added DLC pricing is a bit ridiculous. $55 (NZD) for outfits is a bit crazy, seems like they’re just trying to make some quick money from die-hard fans.The combat system is very well done, and the animations are very cool where all the characters have abilities/attacks they used in the anime.Performance wise some people have been complaining about issues, but for me it ran perfectly and I never had a problem.Other than a few negatives, I really enjoyed this game and found the story quite fun to play through, and I would highly recommend it to any fans of the show.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally i was excited to see this title appear and i did get a fair bit of enjoyment out of it but there are some serious issues and there will be some spoilers here to elaborate on.So lets start with what the game does well:From a JRPG element it does deliver the content that fits the genre well in some regards but there will be those that would have preferred a more action based game, the graphics do fit the style of how the anime was portrayed so is visually accurate.The game areas are quite well designed with some different map mechanics that allow for the destruction of obstructions from battle providing you did enough damage in 1 combo which is probably quite fitting for how much destruction Fairy Tail are known for.Other mechanic i haven't seen personally since playing The Last Remnant was the ability you unlock further into this game called link battle which makes the battles a bit more difficult by fighting more enemies at once to get more rewards and experience.So what does the game do so badly that i cant recommend the game?Unfortunately the big one for me is that not all the characters have a model rendered in for them and are replaced with portraits making some of the scenes a bit weird and disjointed missing characters such as - Romeo, Macao, the royal family of the Fiores' the list goes on.Worse than this other guilds members have been literally erased from the game altogether which breaks the immersion you would expect from a title such as this and i would deem to be a very poor shortcut to take.The story start point was not a bad one to start from but would certainly alienate those who have little to no knowledge of the anime or the manga which excludes those players from the immersion you expect to get from a title like this. However what i can't forgive is the ending point it's a whole season short you currently don't battle Zeref and the Alvarez nation or Acnalogia which no doubt will be some paid DLC at some point for the remaining part of the story which is a very bad way to run a JRPG title.The game didn't really offer me any challenge on hard mode i have 1 achievement left to do before i get the last one automatically and thats the game complete in what will likely be 34-35 hours and for a JRPG that is not a great sign especially for the price tag that you are paying these days. you look at the classic games in the same genre and you are getting double those numbers easily for less money.Overall i can only give the game 4/10 for a title that promised much and under delivered quite badly which is the crying shame we as a gaming community have put up with for far too long.

_childDocuments_.review: Just completed the game and got 100% achievements.  As a big fan of the series, I really want to like the game, but i have massive issues with the end product.  They did really well for the parts that were promised in the trailer which saves the game to some extent, but everything else about the game amounts to an uncooked potato.  There are a handful of hidden gems in the game, but you have to go through a lot bland, redundant quests to find them.  I can only recommend this game if they bring the price waaaayyyy down, if you are a huge fan of the series, and you don't mind a game that is mainly about grinding with story elements.  I am hoping this game does not end up being a blatant cash grab at the expense of the franchise, which it appears to be at the moment, and they patch atleast some of these issues.Pros:The combat system is easily the best part of the game:  - It is intricate but still easy to use- Most spells are visually appealing - Allows for fun combinations- Reduces some of the grind later in the game by chaining battlesFor parts that have voice acting, the voice acting is goodCharacter models look pretty good for the ones that were actually madeMaps are fairly detailed, but rather smallThere are a couple of unique quests that are actually rather fun/funny (most super redundant though)Unique character interactions can be funny, though not all characters have unique interactions with one anotherCons:So many corners were cut that its hard to figure out where to begin- Devs had no sense of story telling. First 10 secs of the game you are thrown into a fight with Hades with no introduction or explanation.  It only gets mildly better in the later parts of the game, but rather than animate a lot of parts, Lucy skims over events.- There are about 10 quest giving NPCs/ villagers in the entire game.  Those models are copy/pasted across towns, so you will see spots were there is the same model 5 times.  These models make up all non-guild characters in the game- Unless the character had a roll in battle or function as a vendor, they were not given a character model.- Character models for some of Lucy's summons appear to have been intended for the game, but were not added.  Summon Capricorn looks like a weird floating ball that flies at enemies which I'm assuming was supposed to be his fist- Game amounts to: go to this location, get cutscene, quest complete or go to this location, get cutscene, fight something, get another cut scene, quest complete.- Guild building mechanic is not really a feature as it happens rather naturally as you progress the game- Cut scene audio de-syncs from the cut scene (this might be related to a bug that the developers are looking into)- Most cut scenes have characters just talking to a wall or to the same villager/enemy model that you have seen about 80 times before- Parts of the story were modified in the later part of the game so that the dev team would not have to put much effort in animating

_childDocuments_.review: Summary: Fun for fans of the anime, but not worth paying a AAA price for and current Steam release in need of fixes/optimizations at time of review.Full dislosure: I originally purchased this on Steam and then returned it, and ended up purchasing on the Switch (and have now logged 15-20 hours). This review isn't about the differences between them, except some of the drivers behind the return.I think this may be one of the first negative recommendations I've provided on Steam, largely because I know the type of games I like and carefully research before I buy (most of the time).The actual Fairy Tail game is a mixed bag. Fans of the anime (such as myself) will enjoy playing through many story arcs as well as the side quests/interactions. The combat animations look great (for the playable characters), and combat moves quickly with a lot of options in abilities, effects, and strategy. The character dialogue is funny, even if the lack of diversity in character facial expressions leads to a mismatch between words and expression.The actual game play outside of the combat is just a slog - most of the game is fetch quests and jumping between location and location. One of the "core" systems is upgrading the guild hall, which amounts to layers of fetch quests and grinding to level up stores and services that vary between important and potentially essential (depending on the amount of level grinding you do). The "cutting corners" aspect of this game is so glaringly obvious, with a very small % of characters receiving an actual in-game model, and worse, a massive re-use of NPC models. In one fetch quest, I was given something to hand out to a few other NPCs in-town, and the third character I had to interact with was the EXACT SAME NPC MODEL as the NPC who started the quest. No difference in face, expression, hair, or even a different colored shirt. Specific to the PC release, I was tremendously disappointed with the quality of the port and what seems to be the lack of material progress in fixing/optimizing it ~2 weeks later. The problems with initial loading, missing configuration options and sub-par overall performance seems to highlight a team that doesn't have PC ports are a core competency.Closing this out, even though I've enjoyed the game (on the Switch), I don't think it warrants a $60 price tag. This isn't a AAA release by any means and the cost cutting measures noting above and in many other reviews points to a game made on the cheap. For $20-$30 I would pick this up as a fan of Fairy Tail and have enjoyed it for what it is. Right now I can only advise to wait for a price drop and more importantly for some additional patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never seen the anime, so this will only be dealing with what I have seen in the game. Also, I was ready to give this game an 11/10 before I even played it and hyped it up because I was sure it was going to be awesome, partially because I love JRPGs and partially because it was supposed to go back to old school JRPG gameplay. It is with great reluctance I have to make this a not recommended. If I could find any excuse at all to recommend it I would, but I just can't.This game falsely seems like it is going back to old school JRPG style, which would be awesome if it actually did. The problem is that once you start the game, you realize it isn't. The game is holding your hand even at max difficulty, which just seems like normal for any other game. On top of that, you start the game feeling strong already with a party full of characters and they all have magic/skills that you want to be using instead of basic attacks. Yes, you START the game using ONLY MAGIC, instead of any other JRPG where you have to start with basic fighting and as your characters grow/progress/learn, they gain more battle prowess, in this game everyone starts at a point that you ONLY WANT TO BE USING MAGIC, or as most other games would call it, mid to late game. Because of this, combat  is very boring when you don't really have any meaningful decisions to make or any thought needed ever.The game is visually appealing, but  that really is not enough to hold interest. Starting with relatively high health, high mana, a bunch of skills per character, then having linear progression on characters with no choices makes for a very easy and boring game.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm going to be straight with you, the game does a lot right, it's really darn good in fact and I had no problem getting through all of the game and I even still have the last segment to go through so I'm going to give a quick summary for people who don't want to read a huge wall of text, it's a great game worth $40/£40 at most for what you are getting, I am a huge fan of Fairy Tail so I'll take the full price hit but you can feel the budget at points which is reflected in the price I suggest waiting for it to go down to dood.Okay the long stuff then, the gameplay is good, it's flashy just like you'd want from a Fairy Tail game, the attacks are nice and varied and you have a total of 16 characters by the end to play with, sounds good so far right? the issue is enemy types are severely limited, in fact using 3-4 versions of the exact same monster with just palette changes or very slight body variation you won't notice if you aren't looking for it making you feel like you are fighting the exact same monsters over and over and over and *dizzily falls down* ahem yeah, the enemy types become tedious real fast with the only real threat being a particular enemy type that get's to attack twice in a row and has such a high speed stat that chances are even a decent amount of levels above them they will attack first, it has some tough boss fights for sure which is nice and that's where the game shines but even then for the most part they are easy and don't let you show off the mechanics of the game unless you avidly try to intentionally dood. The story covers a few arcs of the actual story and that shows a big chunk of the budget limitations I find, although sure you don't want to show too much off of the story so people will watch the anime it led to scene's not having as much impact, it somewhat makes up for this with the story guild quests and conversations surrounding them which are mostly brilliant if not too short and also suffer from the lack of enemy types, I'm a dub man and although that is sorely missed the voice Japanese VA's are as on point as you'd expect, music is also perfect having that Fairy Tail style to it I'm sure a lot of fans were hoping for, albeit not entirely, you can feel that Hiro Mashima wanted to put a lot more effort in with the writing and some scenes that felt right out of the series and his usual little nod to past series like rave master with a certain article of clothing which although the DLC is...a tad much I admit the game isn't lacking for outfits and they aren't just your average Alternate colours, in fact a few labelled as such are right out different costumes so even without the DLC you have a lot to play with dood.This brings me to a major gripe to finish up and it's to do with the DLC's, I'm not a lover of them sure but I also believe it's a persons choice to spend what they want on things like extra outfits and the like, characters however? not so much, in fact I am a little bit insulted even as there are sections of the game where you use three characters in your team who aren't playable and one of them is DLC, they are selling us a character who is already playable in the game, I have no idea who made that decision but I'm honestly disgusted, it's bad enough selling characters on disc/already in the data but this took it a step further by not only showing them as fully playable with a whole moveset but then putting them up for sale "eventually" is just...spit in our faces why don't you, do note this has no bearing on Hiro Mashima or the devs so don't give them any gripes for sure but still and then two of those characters aren't even DLC!? they are in the game too but look like they will never be available and all for an additional £40 in the season pass, how kind, I'm not even going to go into the issue of Elfman that will be obvious how much of a con DLC he will be when you see him play VS how the monster designs are dood.To end I just want to say thank you for reading and also to say as much as you can feel the budget on this game it is still a fun game, it could have been so much more with the right amount of polish too, more than worth it's full price tag but sadly as it stands I do say wait for a sale, as beautiful as travelling through the world of Fairy Tail is as small as it ended up being on a grand scale, it just didn't have enough as a whole to be worth more than $40/£40 doodDLC Edit!!Okay so played the DLC it's... *sighs* I mean it has it's perks but they reaaaally lazily made this, even going as far as calling it randomly generated dungeon in game as I find the exact same pattern multiple times, a dungeon that albeit pretty looking is filled with generic enemies and bar a colour change and the boss room, I say room because there is only one boss room the dungeon looks exactly the same throughout dood.What we have here really is what should have been freeLC, this is a post game dungeon that should have been in the game from the start, especially seeing as much like the rest of the DLC the character models were either already in there or even used in game, if you are just starting the game the DLC has some training and Lacrima benefits I guess and fighting that final boss is cool but if you've beaten the game already you're gonna find yourself steam rolling it and feeling robbed of the money you spent on it dood.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, first things first:1. Current playtime 12h.2. If you're a Fairy Tail fan stop reading and buy, you won't get another game anytime soon! But how's the game for everyone else?PRO:The game really delivers in it's core aspects - Story and Characters are well done and can easily immerse you into the world of Fairy Tail. The game chooses an interesting point in the timeline to kick things of. After some sort of reset you start from scratch and build your guild from almost zero. Over time the game does introduce you all of its characters explaining their background to some degree. Enough for the avarge player to understand their motivations. The Gameplay is also on point. Choosing from a large variety of different skills and powerups you fight in high paced battles (compared to other entries in the genere) against monsters and heroes from the Fairy Tail universe. AoE if very important aspect of the game and you quickly and intuitivly learn to use your skills in the best way possible. A neat gimmick of the game is it's automatic targeting. Whenever you choose a Spell the game way more often than not already targets the area you want to use it on which further increases pace and makes combat feel really fluent and entertaining even if you just clear some low level monsters to clear a quest.Custmization/Crafting feels good and allows you tweak your prefered characters the way you want to. *Edit: Oh dear silly me I almost forgot the most important thing: KT-Music depatment X Fairy Tail Soundtrack. That's a combination made in heaven! The music in this game is as incredible as you'd expect from a Fairy Tail game and I cannot wait to hear more of it! CON:Unfortunately game is not without issues. While anything core is well done as stated above you will run into cut corners in the enviroment, these issues are clear budget decisions in a game made my developers who otherwise really care about the original show. Monster recolors are quite frequent, townsfolk variety is reather small (you will run past the girl 2-3 times in the same city). Exploring the maps is fun and rewarding but they're quite limited in size. Side characters are not given a model and only appear off-screen. The later is my biggest Issue as a fan of the show but won't affect others to much. Although there are situations that feel rather goofy because of it. Also the visual fidelity is good where it needs to be but you do run into some wierd textures every now and then. _childDocuments_.review: Firstly yes you will need a controller to play this game on PC. I tried without right away and I was unable to get pass the tutorial so i got my controller out and finished it. Pro's:- Animations are really well done- As a fan of Fairy Tail you're playing as characters from Fairy Tail and you can mix up the characters and form your dream team. - Addicting combat. (for a while) I enjoyed just doing requests and just trying to pick a fight with tougher monsters. Later on though I started doing auto battle. -Graphics also look really well for an anime game. Con's:-DLC is so expensive for a fully priced game!!! Just to get every character you need to spend another $60 which is stupid. Especially if I just wanted Levy. Then outfits are an additional $3.50 each if you waned a different swimsuit for each character. - Story is NOT friendly to new people. If you watched or read the anime/manga you should be good but from scratch there are too many references to earlier in the story from where it starts off at. (starts after the S rank exam)-Very repetitive. Requests can be killing certain monsters and then the follow up quest is go back and kill more of the same monsters but 30 this time.-A LOT of the story character models are non-existent. During cut scenes you will see the characters talk to no one but they are talking to the main antagonist but they have no model for that character and because they have some random NPC models and not all it of them it just really makes the game feel unfinished. -Auto-battle system feels bad at times. There will be one monster left and my team will be spamming their most powerful spells for aoe damage rather than single target which felt like a MASSIVE waste of MP. -Monsters in the wild don't really change. Their colors do and their HP/damage do but its still the same model. -S rank quests for the 10 year quests and the 100 year quests were rather disappointing due to the lore behind them. The 10 year and 100 year quests were just the bosses you fought through the story and they only appeared at that time so making it a request that hasn't been completed for 10/100 years doesn't make any sense.- One of the biggest cons this game has is that Levy was not available at the launch. She is my favorite character in Fairy Tail along with Gajeel but I only had access to half of that team. Other characters that you have as guests never ended up joining your team like Lyon didn't join your team when Sherria did. Or the 2 dragon slayers from Sabertooth (sting and rouge) join your team after being a guest but Minerva stays on the sidelines. - The map didn't have a lot of places to go either so the game just felt rather small. -Lacrima becomes non important as your characters can easily get to 999 on every stat through link hunting. -A lot of the story is just summarized through Lucy talking and they just show pictures of the anime rather than a 3D cut scene or even a playable event. Keep in mind I am a fan of Fairy Tail. I played through the entire game and I have gotten every achievement on it. I can't recommend it at its current state. it honestly just felt unfinished even after it was delayed. Now if they added more characters, a few more locations rather than what seemed like 3 zones, more NPC models to make the story feel better to sit through, and different bosses for the S rank quests 10/100 year requests I would have probably recommended it. If you have watched fairy tail and kept up with the story it may be good for you but a new player will be lost VERY quickly and it doesn't really have a backstory. So i have to give it a negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Fairy Tail, I loved this game.As a fan of games, I hate this game.The game stays true to the story of the anime/manga, even has some of the filler episodes as part of some quests, which is kinda sad as they also cut out massive amounts of story and doesn't even bother to "voice" a lot of the side characters.. while still using the sounds/voices from the actual anime.First start, takes eternity to load. Crashed quite a few times before it finally loaded the game.The discussion board is full of people not even able to open it. FPS doesn't go high at all. I had issues even in the cut scenes, I had to click away from the game for it to play normally, what kind of issue is that even? I have an SSD, so can't be that it's not loading properly.The look and feel of the game are pretty good, the 3D style is really pleasant to look at as well.Which makes it even sadder when they waste their beautiful visuals and use literal screenshots from the anime... Not even using the video from the anime, they're literally using just screenshots in a lot of so called important dialogues. A lot of characters are not modelled or even voiced. At least Milliana got a ominous dark blob, counts right?There's literal fight scenes, where a character hits the air and you kind of fill in the gap that they defeated the enemy. Well done /sThe story lasts from the Grand Games till after the Tartaros arc and a tiny cameo from the Avatar arc. A lot of parts were just brushed over, with a tiny bit ot retelling from Lucy in the form of a picture book. Other than the skips, the story can almost fully be followed from the anime/manga. Watching the anime parts of this is beneficial as it will help fill in the missing bits that were skipped over or not rendered.Gameplay is fine, standard RPG. Go around do fetch quests, kill mobs and gather resources. It's got a great grind mechanism for late game, you just spam link hunt when you're higher levelled and you'll easily be gain even more. Jewels are easily obtainable the same way as well. So by far, my personal best experience grinding in a game.The annoying bit, is when it brings up a cutscene which pumps you up, then you get a few seconds where you walk to the target, then you get the pleasure pressing ready and then see another cutscene and maybe you'll get the honour of actually figthing something.

_childDocuments_.review: (I have come back after giving a positive review to this game to instead criticise it heavily) Right so where to begin. The game overall i found generally fun to play and to a degree nostalgic being a long time fan of the series. There were factors i enjoyed and others i didn't which i will list below. In regards to this Day 1 censorship i will dedicate a separate part at the end for that. I have added a part past that to discuss the DLC prices.Liked* I liked the graphics as they felt crisp and flowing (i am aware there were issues with this for others but i didn't experience this so i can't comment on that)* The combat was fun and getting to use characters iconic attacks like Erza's Heavens Wheel armour was a feel good moment* I liked some of the interactions between characters during their bond cutscenes, some providing a laugh here and there.* I liked the visual changes to the guild hall the more you upgraded it.* The soundtracks for the game are very much a highlight of the game just as they are for the anime.Neutral point (when i can't say its a pro or con)- The game if you don't do all the side stuff like helping random folks, bonds and upgrading the guild hall is short as it only has the Grand Magic Games and the Tartaros Arc. However if you do everything else there is a good amount of content. Disliked* If you are like me and like to just do request after request for ages instead of doing the main story you'll find when you do decide to do the story and later side quests they will be heavily one sided for you proving minimal challenge.* There are points where you are made to play as certain characters meaning the team you usually use is not allowed. It doesn't state this so be sure to level all characters evenly to avoid 1 character being severely under levelled compared to the rest.* In terms of character movesets there is a little continuity as some characters have moves that they shouldn't have at that point in the story at all like Juvia's "Blood Rain" move which is supposed to be the ability she only gets in a much later arc (Alvarez).* Due to where the game starts (being a good way through the entire series) if you are new to Fairy Tail then i don't suggest playing this until you are at least past the Tartaros ArcOK DAY 1 CENSORSHIP For me it does not have an impact on how i enjoy the game as i for one never actually found myself looking to see if was able to see a pantie shot during attacks etc. However from a point of principle i can see why some may be annoyed and by playing the game i couldn't help but question the decision. The trailer showed no censorship to this but yet it was patched the moment of release. I guess this could be considered false advertising to a degree. My two main point however is that during one cutscene ONLY the girls of Fairy Tail go to the swimming pool and mess about. After this the player is allowed to change all characters into said swimsuits that would then allow you to be able to run around and fight in them. The second of these points is based around Wendy. During a fair many cutscenes she is often feeling the odd one out due to her *sigh* breast size to which the game will exaggerate this point with a close up of one of these more endowed characters chest, This may be a point that is brought up in anime and manga often but in the case of what was censored yet these two things were left in was confusing in that regard. Overall however i do recommend the game if you are a fan of Fairy Tail in general but as i said in my points "if you are new to Fairy Tail then i don't suggest playing this until you are at least past the Tartaros Arc"Ok so the DLC prices are just simply extortionate. I pay in £s but regardless this will still be pricey for any currency. The season pass costs £49.99, $65.83 and 55.54 Euro. There is then 3 costume DLC packs, 16 costumes per pack at £32.99, $43.44 and 36.64 Euro. That is beyond a joke.

_childDocuments_.review: So I was looking for an RPG to sink some time into, and I like Fairy Tail's story from what I watched of the anime so I figured it's something I'd actually invest in. Sure I'm only three hours in but for an RPG  it's very hand hold-y. You're pushed to use certain characters more than anything at the start. I would probably say this was meant for a younger generation or RPG players to sink their teeth into with mechanics that are easy to understand. Fighting in this game is weird. You'll be given missions that are below your level but you'll find monsters that are up to 10 levels ahead of you, but you're kind of stuck doing the low level missions because the higher ranked missions are tough for you too. You can cheese this a little if your "special meter" is full and just spam that until enemies are dead. Erza seemingly only uses one of her armors in the game, which is kind of disappointing. I never did any crafting because the items for it haven't started dropping for me yet.  So while this game could be mindless fun, if you're looking for something a little more in depth mechanics wise while also enjoying your favorite anime characters, this game isn't for you. I'll probably still try to finish it but I wouldn't buy this game full price like i did. At least 50% off before you consider it.

_childDocuments_.review: This is clearly a love letter to the fans. Based on some decisions made, the shoestring budget shows, but I found nothing game breaking. There is a lot of fun to be had based on the included cast of playable characters, which are not limited to Fairy Tail members. Only 1-2 characters I felt were missing from the playable roster, but 16 is still nothing to scoff at for any JRPG. One note, there are two sections that are not obvious they would be in the game. First is what I call "post-credits", this section goes way further than I expected in the story, but stops just short of needing new character models and feels very rushed. The next section is "post-game" which is about what you would expect from a budget JRPG, it's a fun addition, but nothing earth-shattering.TLDR: If you are a fan on the anime and love turn based JRPGs, it's an easy recommendation. If you are just a fan of the anime or just a fan of turn based JRPGs, do your research first and you'll know whether it's for you.

Kill this many of this, go talk to this person then come back and sometimes a mixture of the two. Also for someone who just likes jrpgs and knows nothing about fairy tail the story was pretty confusing at first as the game doesn't start at the beginning. And then it was pretty whatever.But I have kept playing it despite all this because it has redeeming qualities. The combat is enjoyable and putting enemies on a 3x3 grid makes the standard turn based rpg combat more interesting. In addition the character designs are very well done. I know this isn't really saying anything about the game devs but I really like how all the characters look and the combat animations are good enough that I haven't started turning them off yet, which is rare for me. I'm usually all about speed and just turn animations off. Additionally the base building is what kept me playing. I love that stuff so it took me a good long while to get over grinding the repetitive quests for boosts to my base.But beyond that its very standard, sub standard in fact, jrpg fair so far. Nothing that makes this worth a full $60.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairy Tail, a JRPG that starts from the Tenrou Island arc up until the first few episodes of the Finale series. This takes away a number of battles between the arcs. - Requests, least the repetitive ones got old quickly. Go to X Area to kill X enemies. Sadly the Link mechanic didn't work which made this incredibly tedious. - Too much story content was excluded, for an example OverallWhile I did greatly enjoy the game, I would only recommend you the game should you absolutely love Fairy Tail and have at least finished the anime/manga. _childDocuments_.review: Fairy Tail (the game) is a turn-based RPG-lite. It takes place starting about halfway through the actual anime/manga series on a return from Tenrou Island and carries you through the Grand Magic Games and the Tartaros arcs. You can create a team of up to 5 characters from a medium sized roster of Fairy Tale & other guild members. Gameplay: You fight monsters, and level up while progressing through Edolas (the world of Fairy Tale) and fight a few of the major baddies from the series. Rinse & repeat. There is not much depth here nor a great variety of enemies, with most areas using the same old enemies but slightly different color palette. As you fight you also gain link levels with other characters that make them slightly better in combat. With that said, there's only a few moves you learn as you level up all the way from Level 1 to Level 99, with those abilities learned by about level 50 or so. This whole game is a grind, and designed to be such. It is fun to launch a few Fire Dragon Roars and such but is not engaging enough to last. In addition, you are encouraged to string together combos and hit certain damage levels in certain areas of the world. This mechanic has you draw out battles to continue launching attacks even after the enemies are dead just in order to hit that damage # and break through the barrier you're nearby. It was not enjoyable at all. I would only think fans of the series would enjoy this game, and others would best be served by skipping this game and watching the anime. 3/5 rating for me.Story: This lifts material straight from the manga starting from the end of the Tenrou Island arc all the way to the end of the Tartaros arc with some minor post-Tartaros stuff. While I am a HUGE fan of the Fairy Tale anime and story the emotions and humor just doesn't translate well in this game. I found myself skipping a lot of the dialogue, and was disappointed in the bond leveling system as half the characters don't even have any dialogue scenes, a missed opportunity to give some interesting character interactions and depth. Only those who enjoy the anime will enjoy the story, and it's a watered down version. 3/5 rating.Graphics: I was disappointed in the graphics here. Natsu looked like One Piece Luffy in a lot of scenes and the character models were really poorly done IMO. They could have done with more variety in environments and enemies as well, as the entire world feels rather lackluster. 2/5 rating.Music: While they had some pretty good takes on the Fairy Tail Celtic rock vibes, the soundtrack was pretty repetitive and didn't borrow the best music from the anime. I was listening to iTunes after the first couple of hours. 3/5 rating.Fun-factor: Is this addictive? No. It was a grind to get through and only because I'm a HUGE Fairy Tail fan did I keep going through the entire game. This is probably the only chance I'll have to play as my favorite characters and so I took advantage of that, but the fun was not to be found here. 2/5 if you're not a Fairy Tail fan, and 3/5 if you are.Overall: If you are not a fan of Fairy Tail or don't know what it is, do yourself a favor and go watch the anime, it's a great Shonen anime with a great sense of humor and emotion. Skip this game at all costs. If you are a fan of the anime/manga and want a chance to hear Natsu yelling out attacks or crush enemies with Gildarts, this is worth playing, only on sale and really is not worth playing through all the way. 3/5 overall.

_childDocuments_.review: I never post reviews so here I go:For people who aren't really invested into the actual anime or manga itself, I would not recommend the game.
