Unfortunately, many of the complaints you see are true: story-line is rushed (meant to be a recap-ish for fans really, trying to cram 3 seasons worth of story in there is difficult so some characters may seem random and scenes may seem random, but it's meant to compliment the anime and manga, not meant to be followed alone) Another thing is some characters just don't have 3D models. I found it awkward when the 7 year gap happened and Natsu was talking to Romeo when really.... there wasn't anyone there. I also don't care much about whether we have censorship or not, so I don't think you should dismiss the game just for that. There also isn't too many costumes available without buying. That being said...If you are a fan of Fairytail then yes I recommend it. It may be a little over-priced, but this will eventually go down as time goes by. The animations are cute and music is amazing (as expected since the anime itself has amazing music as well) and the flaws I feel are superficial so personally, I don't care and I don't think you should go comparing this game to big title games out there. I always found anime games to be a light-hearted extra to the actual franchise. I wouldn't take it too seriously, it's just what people say it is: a fun game you can enjoy and put your hours in while reminiscing about the series, nothing more and nothing less. :)

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game so much. I really did, but frankly this game was NOT WORTH $60. Right off the bat you'll notice the lackluster visuals. I have a very powerful gaming computer and even with everything on max settings it looks like a PS3 game at best. I understand they probably wanted that generic anime artstyle that a lot of JRPG's use, but this seems pretty shoddy for how much time the game was in development and for the price point. I'm noticing a lot of STUTTERING and frame drops. It's not constant, but it happens enough where you'll notice it and it'll annoy you. I'm only a couple hours in, so I can't judge the entire game, but I can tell you the beginning of the game is very repetitive. You're doing a lot of kill quest missions and combat itself is also pretty repetitive. Of course you'll unlock more moves as you level up, but combat just feels a bit boring to me. The attack animations are actually quite nice, so I will at least give the game credit for attack animations. The game has 16 playable characters, but you will have to unlock each one of them to use them and if there are certain characters you want on your team, well, you'll have to wait till you progress far enough in the story to unlock them. Certain quests require certain party members/comps as well, so you can't just do every mission with your own custom team. For example, I really don't care to use Wendy or Lucy, but you'll have to for some missions and characters like Laxus, Sting, and Rogue won't be unlocked till further in the story. I might update this review after I've beaten the game or played some more, but as it stands right now I can't recommend this game at a $60 price point. The game needs a patch, at least to fix the stuttering and frame rate drops, at least that'd be a good starting point. I've noticed lots of people complaining about the poor support for KB+M, though that doesn't bother me since I play with a controller on most games anyway. This review is focusing more on the game itself and not for the lack of support for certain resolutions and KB+M, though those are relevant complaints to have. I feel like people will want to know more about how the game plays and if it's worth their money. And now on to something else I forgot to mention. Are you a big fan of the Fairy Tail anime? If so then great! You can  probably overlook a lot of my personal complaints if you just enjoy the anime at least. I loved Fairy Tail, and even read the manga series as well. My own love for the series is somewhat overriding some of my grievances with the game, though not all of them. Am I enjoying the game? I actually am, but do I think it was worth $60? No, it wasn't. I'm having fun, but I'd only suggest buying the game if you really enjoy Fairy Tail as a series and can overlook the issues I've pointed out. Also I'd suggest watching some gameplay videos as well before buying.Edit: A lot of the budget went into Lucy's boobs as well. You can tell the developers priorities were focused more on the sex appeal of the girls, more so than anything. I'm not saying this offends me or anything like that. It's just I wish they had put the same amount of effort into other aspects of the game .

_childDocuments_.review: I am willing to recommend this game for two reasons.  (Please keep in mind that I bought this while it was on sale during pre-order and I do not recommend paying full price for this game.) This review was also made without recent DLC in mind. The first being that I want to see more Fairy Tale games being made. The second is that for the most part I did enjoy myself while playing.Another point is that I only quit enjoying the game when I tried to 100% complete it. If your playing it to have a good time you can. Once you start trying to beat the game with 100% of the achievements it gets frustrating.For a more in-depth review:FYI the remainder of this review will contain spoilers of some sort primarily about game mechanics. If you want to experience the story proper go watch the anime or read the manga. I will start with what I am happy with.  The graphics are decent. They are not the best. Most games that Gust helps with or makes have a baseline level of quality that they reached, but they did not really reach above and beyond to be impressive.I did not have any major issues with load times once the game got started. The game took awhile to start for me but once it was going the load times were few and far between during gameplay. The loading screen within the game I never saw until a recent update. Happy can take a fish and hit the Now Loading that crosses your screen which is fun. After this update the game started faster but had slightly longer load times during gameplay. I think the longest one I had was about 7 seconds.They gave enough moving character models in the city to make it feel like an actual city. However, when doing side quests for some of the residents you will notice that many of the models are the same. If you stick to only the plot you probably will not notice.I do not know where or if this is explained but you can remove the fight animations during combat and change it to auto combat. I only noticed it because I was observing the combat screen for a while about part way through the game. If this did not exist, I would have been bored doing all the monster slayer quests the game has for you to do. Speaking of.The fights in this game are turned based. I think this was mainly a Gust influence since their Atelier games seem to be primarily turn based. Given how combat worked in the show… turn based combat kind of made sense. Anime characters tend to attack, then be attacked, then attack again. There are not many occasions where a character gets completely steamrolled and has no way to fight back or to run.Now we are going to get into some of my favorite stuff but also the stuff that I do not like about the game:My favorite part but also the part that disappointed me the most by the end of the game was the bond system. Bonds between the main fairy tale cast have dialogue that lets people learn their backstories and helps us grow attached to the characters. The disappointing bit for me is that if they are not in the main group, they do not have dialogue with each other at all. Your main characters will have one or two at most that they can have dialogue with that are not a part of the fairy tale guild.In relation to that there are key story moments that characters will have dialogue but not have a character model, so they will not be shown on screen.There are also key story moments that feel off because I feel like they just took a screenshot from the anime and put it there. There are a few moments when they have the in-game models do the scenes and generally do quite well at it. However, because this does not happen often, I can only say I am disappointed by the missed opportunities.There are graphical issues during combat, I don’t recall the term used in game but you are linking one attack to the next, to the next, to the next, and so on until you reach the upper limit and use a finisher or they fail to link attacks. The final attack during this link does not appear correct for me. The most descriptive I can be is looking at a pixelated negative color explosion. It was like the game could not render the explosion correctly. The game never crashed, and the weird colors were only of the explosion everything else was fine.There are a few mechanics that I do not think get explained very well. They tell you what it is and what it does when you meet the requirements for it to happen but the actual process of allowing those mechanics to happen were not clear. For example, Unison Raids. If they explained how to do this than I missed it. I figured it out on accident while doing back to back quests. All I remember of the in-game description is that there were special requirements to use it. Not helpful if you do not tell me the requirements.My biggest annoyance with the game is they did not start at the beginning which was disappointing for me.  They forced a boss battle at the beginning to teach you the mechanics. If they had started at the beginning of the story teaching the battle mechanics would be more fluid and less forced. You have a full team for your tutorial and then must go back and unlock the team slots after this fight. Many of the abilities you display you cannot use until you learn how to do them in game later. Once again if you start at the beginning of the story the progress would work better and it would also reflect when they came about in the source material.Now that I am thinking about it the game does not end where the anime/manga does either. There is a missing arc or two. Granted the arc they ended on was a good one. A lot of fans probably would have liked it to end there anyway.The last bit that got on my nerves to the point where I stopped playing just before 100% the game was the quests. The quest board is rather boring.  Most of them are go to this area and kill these monsters. Which by itself would be fine. However, they introduce a mechanic where you can fight many enemies at a time. If you use this mechanic, it does not count towards the request. Which means you are running through levels on autopilot looking for the right monsters to fight over and over and over and over and over and over and you get the idea. If the mechanic would work for the monster hunter requests, I would have no complaints about this.All in all, I would say buy it if you’re a fan of Fairy Tail.  I recommend doing so while it is on sale. I do not think it is worth the full price, I am able to recommend it because I bought it discounted down over the summer on pre-order. I am also ignoring overpriced DLC BS when recommending it. If you liked the game well enough than the DLC can give you additional stuff to play with. However, if you are not enjoying your time do not by the DLC it does not help with gameplay at all. It is all cosmetic and potentially additional characters.

_childDocuments_.review: Controls:After playing through this game for an incredibly short time, I have already ran into many problems. Firstly, if you do not have a controller, I would discourage purchasing this game due to its dreadful PC port, where you have to use complicated and awkward controls to control your character (imagine using R, T, F, G to control your vision and at the same time having to use WASD for your movements). Since there are no ways to alter (or even view!) the controls as well as being incapable of changing the controller prompts to that of the keyboard, you will be fumbling around wondering the exact function of each key on your keyboard.Graphics:The graphics are something that you would expect out of a JRPG, it is not that to the extent of a triple A game but it is still acceptable for modern times. The main problem is with the significant drops in fps during attack animations and movements within the open world. I'm personally using a pretty average GeForce Driver to run the game on the lowest settings and resolution at full screen, yet at many point it can barely maintain the 30 fps cap and constantly drops far below it.Gameplay:The turn-based combat is straightforward and plain that anyone can easily grasp. Even though the use of different status effects and placements of the enemies acts as a way to give us a great variety of options, yet ultimately it still falls under the same trap that most turn-based combat games would as you devolve into spamming only one particular spell from each character. Even though I have not played much of the game yet, but I can already foresee the "mission" system becoming repetitive and boring rather quickly.Overall, in the current state of this game I would definitely only recommend this game if it is on a deep sale as it is certainly not worth purchasing at full price even for a huge fairy tail fan. A purchase when it has a light sale is only a possibility if the problems regarding significant fps drops and better PC porting have been addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Fairy Tale is oversaturated with bright vibrant color and pizzazz. It's like that gorgeous girl from your high school that everyone had a crush on, but when she opens her mouth everyone sees that she's got no personality and her head is empty. The level design feels like it is very much on rails. The maps aren't very big, or interesting to explore. You'll see the same half dozen models repeated endlessly one on top of another around town. For some reason they turn transparent and you can walk through them. I guess they're ghosts? There are no stores to go into, or interesting characters to meet outside the guild. As a result, the game feels hollow and shallow. I feel like I've walked into a movie that is 3/4 through. I have no clue who these people are, why they have the powers they do, or why I should care about them. I'm not engaged. I'm bored and confused. Maybe I would like it better if I had seen the Anime first, but alas, I have not. The combat is fun and like the other game systems shows promise, but isn't realized. It's just shallow and low budget. There are models missing for characters, which makes certain scenes very confusing, as you may find yourself talking to 1 or more invisible people at once. How they thought this would be acceptable I haven't clue. On top of this, the day 1 patch apparently censers the game. WHY? I want to like this game, but I can't. It's colorful world is shallow and boring. This isn't how you do a proper JRPG. If you want me to care about this world and this guild and these characters, give me reasons to care. Right now, this game does not. There are too many cut corners. Stay away and if you must buy it, wait for a sale. This isn't worth full price.

_childDocuments_.review: My review was originally a negative one based on the absolute bare-bones status of the game's port to PC, focusing on the abysmal keyboard/mouse controls.  I said I might swing back and review it again if the devs fixed the KB/M controls, and now, after they did so and I got to the endgame, I have changed my review to a positive one.  Make no mistake, this game still has it's faults: no mouse look, absurdly priced DLC, and characters who only appear as still face shots.  But the base game itself is a decently made RPG, and that's ultimately what made me change my review.The core gameplay loop is simple: you grab a team of characters, you go out and do a job, you get paid.  Pretty standard fare.  But there's tons of stuff to upgrade and build on.  Your characters' relationships improve as they continue to work together, unlocking little scenes of them interacting and gameplay bonuses like improved chain attacks (where everyone on your team basically piles in on the enemy and attacks out of turn) and the occasional ability to retry a failed chain (very handy on some of the postgame bosses who are serious damage sponges and hit like trucks, so you want to burn them down sooner than later).  You can improve their wizard level, which is seperate from their character level and which improves their abilities, unlocks new outfits, and gives them bonuses under certain conditions.  For example, Lucy and Wendy have a bonus that gives a chance to boost your team's speed at the beginning of a battle.  You can also upgrade guild facilities and get bonuses and extra stuff from that as well, ranging from a store to buy consumables to a lab where you can make stat-boosting gems called lacrima, up to and including a bar where you can buy drinks to get stat bonuses.  There is a difference between upgrading and remodeling the guild facilities: upgrading the job board, for example, gives you access to higher-ranked jobs, but remodelling it boosts the amount you are paid per job.The story more or less coasts along the storyline from the series, with no real deviations until you reach the postgame.  A few notable things are changed, but I'll leave spoilers out of this review.  One big change I will cover, however, is you can take a special trial so that your favorite team can take S-rank jobs, which are the toughest.  The main crew with the exception of Erza never got to take those jobs in the series, so that's a refreshing change of pace considering all the crap they went through without the rank.  Makarov even lampshades the fact the cast have earned the distinction, now they just need to prove it.Overall, I'll recommend this one as FT is a 'verse I'm fond of, the gameplay itself is solid, and I haven't encountered any significant bugs or glitches since I started playing again.  Good job, Gust, on turning this one around.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: A Day One patch was released to censor fan service in the PC version of the game. I am unaware as to why this has happened, but I've been told that Sony may have had a hand in the choice. That being said, censorship is censorship. Unless this is reversed (which it never will be) I will never recommend buying this game. Niche Japanese titles have a niche audience for a reason, we are the hardcore JRPG fans that have been around for decades, by removing fan service (from a universe like Fairy Tail) will not encourage more people to try the game and instead will convince more people to avoid buying the game. Fairy Tail is a JRPG that I wish I could enjoy more. It is developed by GUST, who are one of the best developers of niche JRPG's on the market today, and it has all the stylings of an Atelier game. However, in a world of wizard guilds and fantasy, I feel like Fairy Tail lacks the magic spark that makes the Atelier games so special. For this review, I want to break this game down into several categories: Gameplay, Story, Sound, and Graphics.If you are familiar with the Atelier games, you will find yourself right at home here in Fairy Tail because, this is an Atelier game with a Fairy Tail coat of paint. Everything from the hub worlds, monster filled forests, and quests feel like they have been taken straight out of an Atelier game for your enjoyment. So if you are already a fan of this style of game, you will have no problem diving right into this game. You will start out in a new Fairy Tail guild at rank 150, and have to complete requests to rank up the guild in order to, once again, become the best guild in the world. Along the way you will run into familiar characters, side quests, citizen requests, and main story missions that progress the actual plot along. Because I have already played my fairshare of Atelier, I was a little disappointed when I realized that GUST were not willing to take a risk and try to create something new, rather than just creating the same game again. I don't want to compare GUST to other, larger developers, but if one were to look at a game like Kakarot, or One Piece World Seekers, those games are a breath of fresh air because they took a risk and tried to create something unique and different. Even if were to look at another one of Koei Tecmo's developers, Omega-Force, they were able create a better adaptation with Attack on Titan (which was my game of show at E3 2016 when I attended). GUST played it safe and because they did, I feel like this game suffers heavily because of that.I'm going to leave this part short because, I will just be honest, I have never read or watched a single piece of Fairy Tail media before I started playing this game. However, I feel like that isn't a bad thing because it allowed me to approach this game with an open and unbias point of view. I am a massive fan of Shonen as a genre (still an unapologetic Naruto fanboy in 2020, Believe it) and that alone got me interested in Fairy Tail. As I played the game I quickly began to understand the characters and really enjoyed them for who they were, which is helped by some amazing voice acting. But, because I was feeling lost most of the time I played the game, I don't feel it is my place to critique this aspect of the game.  This is where the presentation of Fairy Tail really shines, the voice acting in this game is amazing, mainly due to the voice cast all reprising their roles. They have an amazing talent to express themselves from the smallest details to the most ridiculous, and over the top scenes. If there every was a moment in the game where I felt myself becoming absorbed with the Fairy Tail universe, it was almost solely due to the amazing cast of actors and actresses behind the microphones. The music in the game is lacking in any originality or stand out performances though and I quickly found myself growing bored of it and I eventually just muted it and started listening to my own music. If I were a more cynical person, I would wager that Fairy Tail's background music was largely left over Atelier tracks that were never used in the actual titles.Here is where I feel most conflicted. On one hand, I feel like the 2D to 3D conversion of Fairy Tail from an anime/manga to a video game is incredible. I always love seeing a studio try their best to bring a vivid and unique artstyle to life, and GUST did an okay job. But, much like every other piece of praise I have given this game there is a caveat. The actual presentation of these graphics ranges from bad to terrible in most cases. There are entire scenes of dialogue where two characters stare, blank faced at each other and talk about a wide variety of issues. This leads to the voice actors having to put in extra effort to try to bring these stiff animations to life and is completely takes me out of the scene.The opening battle sequence is one of the most egregious examples of the lack of animation polish in the game. When the villain uses an attack to throw Natsu into the air, there is no completion of the animation, he is just knocked up, the camera cuts, and when it cuts back Natsu is just standing right where he was left off at. Would it have cost so much more money to finish creating that animation? I don't think so.While there is not enough in Fairy Tail for ME personally, I am still hesitant to call the game bad. If you're a die hard fan of either Atelier or Fairy Tail, I am sure you will find more enjoyment in this game than I have. Do I recommend this game? At its current price, I do not, and knowing Koei Tecmo, it will not going on sale for a LONG time. If this game were 30 or 40 dollars, I could see spending the money to get some more JRPG's in your life, but as it stands, I feel like there are better games out there for your to sink your time into. I mean, as I write this, Atelier Ryza is on sale and that's a much better game. Score: 5/10 (mediocre)

_childDocuments_.review: The controls are absolutely outrageously bad... Look at this ♥♥♥♥: There doesn't even seem to be a way to remap them... Seriously, what the ♥♥♥♥?All shortcuts on the screen are shown for a controller, which of course, like so many others, do not have.That aside, the visual, animations and voice acting are very good, but if you do not have a controller, avoid like the plague, this is once again, a poorly thought out console port, like devs don't even know what a pc is or something.Newflash devs, a large chunk of the pc community uses mouse and keyboard, and doesn't own a controller on pc.The review will be swapped if the controls get changed, and mouse support for the camera is added, I mean seriously, it's 2020, surely, you've heard of the device called a mouse?After finishing the main parts of the game, here's the edit/add to the review:A large chunk of the dialogues later on in the game, are no longer voiced.The friendship level thing, is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ painful, for no bloody reason. It takes forever and ever to do with all characters.Characters have been "removed", many characters are not even present in the game, and not playable either... The game was sold to us as "make the team of your dream"... Well, that's quite difficult to do with only a fraction of the characters present isn't it?Most of the characters will be available, AFTER you complete the main quest, which is completely stupid in my opinion. You're basically restricted to using a select few for the largest part of the game.The graphics are fairly subpar for the terrain/ground, I feel like I'm playing on a console here :SA huge amount of characters and story, are just gone, vanished... Every single scene with nudity or torture, has been toned down, or completely removed. If you expect something as dark as the anime, forget it, this is a carebear game.Entire chunk of the the arc, are gone, and replaced with a very sub standard version instead. The garou exterminators are not even mentioned for example.About half of the magic game, are just summarised by text, and are not playable either.There are only about 20 enemies or so, the most annoying one being the generic dark guild everywhere... They did not even bother to try and make enemies per say, just copy and paste the same ones over and over.It is the same with the monsters, there are only but a few monsters in the game, their stats change, but that"s about it.The final fight, is ridiculously long. I was overlevelled and overupgraded for it, and yet, it took forever. It was not difficult at all, but just a massively long bullet sponge. Same with the "S" exam, the mob simply takes way too long to kill, it's not difficult at all, but it's just long, very very very long, for no reason. Taking a long time to kill, doesn't make it difficult, but it does make it very boring.Once you get in the epilogue however, things turn around. The mobs are a lot more difficult (first time I actually lost a couple of fights in my entire playthrough.)I think the budget (or efforts) made into this game, have been way too low.It certainly is not worth the full price, and this is NOT a AAA game. The game is closer to a visual novel with combat than anything else.If it was sold as a 20€ visual novel with RPG element, sure, that'd be ok, but this is hardly the case.Then, there are the side quests for upgrades. They'll be asking some kind of materials, and some cash. Thing is, the materials are only a few, they just change the names, that's it. There are no visual differences, because...,? That's right, you do NOT even see drops/loot/objects... In the world, you only see a small column of light, that is it. Nothing else. I think we got a mobile phone port here, even consoles have games slightly more evolved than this...Even if they fix the mouse/keyboard issues (you can not rotate the camera with the mouse, at all, ever), I will not change the review, the game is just of a too poor quality for that price.Instead of playing this, watch the anime, it's a whole lot better.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 31.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game too many times, or play nearly as long as some of you. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

_childDocuments_.review: ---{Graphics}---Ur classical anime JRPG graphic---{Gameplay}---This game is your turn-based JRPG. There's roaming, grind a bit repetitive but its not bad since Link Hunt make it quicker. Character learns and upgrade skills through leveling. It has team synergies just like in ur classic final fantasy mechanic where all round dmg dealer, debuff and buff unit, tank, etc. Skills has its own area of effect attack like horizontal, cross, T , J, etc, to put this more interesting way, some attacks can make enemy retreat backward for 1 grid, great to repositioning enemy. There are few upgrade as well, your facilities, star upgrade, and bonds between your characters which can take some times to max them out. Some bosses are pretty fun, the grand magic tourney is enjoyable but the overboost(only in grand magic) kinda kill my masochist vibe. The unison raid (ur combo attack) is dope, i love it. There are few who has its unique combo, props to that.---{Audio}---Its alright but wish we hv the original soundtrack, the one with voices. I would love this to play during boss fight---{Audience}---Teens and adults. Kids. Gramps???!!---{PC Requirements}---Even potato PC can run this---{Difficulity}---Easy but end game bosses can give u hardtime since they hv large health pool---{Grind}---Not bad, link hunt helps. Your characters levels up pretty quickly once u unlocked link hunt---{Story}---Pretty much from the anime, until the epilogue of final season. Its okay if u have not watch/not bothered to watch the anime, the story itself pretty enjoyable, dialogues has its funny moment as well. ---{Game Time}---Dont mind my playtime, i have ick on grinding games. A bit miss a point where the dragon force awakening doesnt change their looks like in the anime (dragon scale skin) Anywayyyyyy, here are some of my opinion for each characters1. Natsu = good offensive unit, good aoe skills, has attack boost with health above 50% (upgrade through star), would recommend him in ur team2. Gray = great aoe skills, early debuff unit, early defence buff unit, has chances to take off his shirt when attacked which speeds up his turn, would recommend him in ur team but can change to better unit later on3. Wendy = ur main support unit, she heals she buffs, she revives. Downside low attack but has good aoe, would recommend in ur team6. Gajeel = pretty much ur debuff unit, good aoe, good attack. Juvia = Has odd aoe skills, can revive unit to full HP with a cost of leaving her HP to 1, has attack boost if Gray in ur team, u decide whether to put her in ur team8. Sherria = Same with wendy, would recommend in ur team11. Lyon = Good aoe, good attack, would recommend in ur team12. _childDocuments_.review: Besides the excellent story and the adorable characters, you'll also have the possibility to participate in exciting quests to earn money and raise your guild level. Apart from the characters that you'll meet at the beginning of the game, as the story progresses you'll meet new characters that you'll be able to befriend and then play with yourself. You can choose your own team and level them up. With each playable character you can follow individual storylines and increase your character bond level, which unlocks various abilities.Fairy Tail has an ingenious traveling system and offers countless places to explore and unlock. Regions outside the main cities are hostile and contain monsters that you can fight. Depending on the region, they can be strong and challenging, giving you the incentive to improve and strengthen your team.You'll have the option to expand your guild and upgrade facilities. To craft and upgrade stuff, you'll have to find items. You can either kill specific monsters to get the loot you need, or you can walk around the areas to find it by yourself.I don't want to give too much away, but I can really recommend this game to anyone who enjoys this kind of genre and is a fan of the franchise. Fairy Tail gets an 8.5/10 from me.  Feel free to like this review, if it was helpful to you, and add me if you want! ❤️ 🧡 💛 💚 💙 💜

My second and by far largest problem with the game so far is that a good number of important characters that received numerous voice lines throughout the game did not receive the curtesy of an in-game character model.

_childDocuments_.name: FAIRY TAIL

_childDocuments_.review: For its price? Not worth it. Even on sale you have to be a serious fan of Fairy Tail for it to be a worthwhile purchase. The game is lacking in soul and only reeks of a cash grab. Nearly $450 USD for all the DLCS and the game? Most of the DLCs are cosmetic outfits and go for a few dollars. Modders have made their own outfits and they do it for free out of passion for the series.For the game itself, it is not bad at all but it is really only an average JRPG. Gameplay is simple and even on hard difficulty the game will be easy to breeze through. The main story quest will be the main source of entertainment in the game. Side quests and jobs are just chores. Boss fights are somewhat fun. There is not too much depth to the game and you don't really need to do any grinding to progress in the game. The game could have done something with the gameplay of the characters. Imagine a requip mechanic for Erza. Or perhaps one for the dragons slayers. One of the greatest things in the anime is all the cool types of magic every character has. Instead all the game has to offer is abilities and all the playable characters play similarly. You will have to have watched the anime or read the manga to understand the story of the game. It will not make sense and the story will be lacklustre. The game does sometimes manage to capture glimpses of the humour and spirit of the anime, but it is the exception rather than the case. The game cuts out a good portion from the anime, which the developers probably thought wasn't anything of substance. But when you cut out moments like the 2nd day of the Grand Magic Games, Laxus's fights, Lucy's fight wth Minerva, Garou Knights and Abyss Palace, etc. you miss out on some of the iconic and most exciting scenes and fights in the anime. I've have only started the Eclipse part of the Grand Magic Games as of writing, so I have yet to see what they cut out in the Tartaros Arc. For its shallow coverage of the Grand Magic Games, which is one of the longest arcs in the story, the game could have at least covered more story arcs than just the GMG and Tartaros arcs. Much of the missing content stems from having no animated avatars for many characters. It is lucky if a character even gets a drawn sprite in the game. Considering how the publishers charges exorbitant prices for DLC cosmetics, it leaves one to wonder why they couldn't spare any effort to animating the side characters that would have made the game feel less empty. Crime Sorciere without Meredy? Laxus without his Thunder God Tribe? You can't help but notice them missing. Don't even get me started on the participants of the Grand Magic Games. Overall, the game can be and is enjoyable. But in comparison to the Fairy Tail anime? A whole lot of missed opportunities and disappointment. Only consider getting the game if it's discounted at least 50% off. Your money is better spent elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: Not a huge fan of the show, but did watch around 300 episodes. There were things I liked about the show, and somethings I didn't.  I like the animation style, some of story elements. I found some appeal through some character relationships.  Only thing that really bothered me is when they starting forcing the drama.  After hitting around episode 200 everyone started getting a bit to cheesy.  The power of friendship it's constantly thrown at you. To the point where like I get it.Now to the game, I think it's worth every penny. I'm over 40 hours in and still seems like I have tons to do. There is actually a point where it seemed like they could of just ended it.  Yet the game opens up with even more.  I liked some of the story, I liked the combat methods used. I thought the character animations and designs were pretty good and accurate.  The combat is interesting, since there lots of opportunities with in the combat. All Controlled with button prompts in battle. Which is usually just one button, or one button at a time.  It's not very complicated and should become second nature after a while.  Some examples of actions you take with button prompts. is to counter attack, to defend, to counter after another ally attacks an enemy. Can use the up arrow on controller to quickly boost yourself.  When on the brink of death or when sustaining alot of damage.  There is also a devastating attack you can do with chain attacks. So after a while you can feel a bit OP, even if some enemies can still destroy you.  Though as I said there can be alot opportunities. Along with some characters being able to heal and the use of items. Which really shouldn't make this a difficult game for anyone when just playing on easy or normal.  Given they are somewhat familiar on how to use a controller and play a video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Reading all this would give you enough info to form your own opinion, but I've added a TL;DR at the end.I've watched the anime and gotten platinum in the game and I'll share my thoughts about how I felt the game was. Some minor spoilers ahead, nothing that actually spoils your experience though. The game starts right before the 7 years time-skip and goes on through the story till the Tartaros arc. There's an Epilogue where you have access to characters after the final time skip and that's where the game actually ends. It'll take about 33 hours to finish the main story if you play casually. Overall the game should last you about 15 days, give or take a few... if you try and get every achievement. You can play as Ichiya, that should be enough but i'll add more anyway.The story is quite similar to the anime with very slight changes to it. The OST is pretty good as well. The thing that I enjoyed the most were the various events with the characters, lots of new conversations that weren't in the anime. But you know that they happened off screen sometime. They represent how a casual conversation between various characters would go. This itself was done wonderfully and makes me recommend this game.Then there are quests that require certain characters, they're more like short stories since you get lots of new scenarios. For example, how would Ichiya and Laxus tackle a quest together? Well the game shows how that would go. The combat is quite fun especially in the beginning, I'll elaborate why it isn't as fun in the late game in the cons section. Overall the combat system is fun and has various power-ups and methods you can use to defeat the enemy.The voice acting was amazing as always, it brings the characters to life.You need a controller to play the game, but I'm used to it since Fairy tail is just Atelier Lucy in some ways and you always get a better experience with a controller in Atelier games.Various attacks suffer from fps drops, but that might just be my PC. Although from my experience with the Atelier games, it's also about optimization. The thing that I disliked the most, even more than the fps drops during the battle is that there's no button to skip most of the attack animations. It feels really good in the beginning and I enjoyed them a lot since they looked cool, but when there are sooo many battles and you can't skip the 15 second long attack animations, it starts to get frustrating. Lucy's urano metria for example takes a looong time to cast and although it does decent damage, I almost never used it because it took too damn long for a battle that I could end in less than 8 seconds total. Of course I just might be an idiot that didn't find a way to skip the animations. I know that some special attacks have the skip option but not the regular ones. The regular quests can get boring after a while where you simply need to kill monster A or monster B because there is a lot of repetition involved. There are about 11-12 areas total two of which are cities. It seems a lot but doing regular quests just feels a bit boring. I can't say that for special quests that required various characters however, they were always fun to do. And you have to do the regular quests if you want all the achievements, if not then it shouldn't bother you at all since you can play the game without bothering to do that many of them since they don't add to the story, just a fun in moderate doses kind of thing.There's also the high prices, nothing more I can add here that others haven't already. But it's a shame that so many costumes that could be in the game initially, cost extra. And by so many, I especially mean the post 1 year time-skip costumes because it's actually added in the game as the epilogue. And you see the Natsu after the final time skip in his old costume and that feels weird. So perhaps the swimsuits were not necessary, but this is like an actual part of the story imo.Then there's the censorship, I personally didn't mind that since I don't care about such a small thing when there are actual swimsuits and characters like Cana wearing their underwear as normal wear all the time. So there's definitely not much missing if your favorite character's pantsu is censored. But I'm putting this here anyway since in the end if their trailer showed something different, although not the final footage, some people still only buy the game because of that so either they should mention that it's not a part of the game or add it in.I recommend the game if you are a fan of the series and want more of the characters, like me. However, If you just wanna play a JRPG and this seems to be the one you might like, buy it for full price if you can afford it or wait for a sale, I recommend the latter. The DLC is another story however. I would recommend buying the DLC in a sale at least since some of that (post 1 year time-skip costumes) was 100% part of the endgame. Or just don't buy them, your choice.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclosure, i have only seen the first 4 episodes of the anime. With that being said, here are my two cents; *****Over all rating 7.5****** Although i purchased full price, in hindsight i should have waited for the sale.  The Main story itself is very short, it only took a total of 24 hrs to beat the main story. I played this game on normal and at no time did it ever feel challenging, I was super OP just by doing all the request board missions and upgrading the guild. Missions and fighting task become repetitive quick.  Animation cut scenes are high quality but become tedious (I do believe there is an option to skip them that i did not notice until late in the game) As someone who has not seen the anime, fans of the anime may enjoy game play more. As an JRPG fan the story was not as intriguing as i'd hoped it to be. There quite a few mundane cut scenes i choose to skip. What i most thoroughly enjoyed was the post game content. Once you beat the game you have the option to continue leveling your guild, you also have the option to become an S class member and take on the S class missions. These missions were a little more challenging but at the same time never really had an issue with them. To be honest it just felt like the monster HP pool was just higher as some fights lasted as long as 20-25 minutes.  Lvl cap is 99 and after reaching that level if you have stuck around for all the extra stuff you will be given the chance to go "beyond that" there's a catch but i wont spoil that. While iv'e not "Fully" completed the game - There is no additional story line. if you want to get all the trophies there will be some additional things to keep you busy post game. Overall i didn't hate the game and i would think a huge Fairy Tail ( Anime ) fan would enjoy it more. Lots of backlash on the censorship that i did not care much for but i'm sure there will be a mod for that down the line.  Enjoy - and as a reminder i would wait for a sale on this game as price is to steep for content.

_childDocuments_.review: Based on the knowledge currently available to me, I understand that this game had a decently low budget. Thus, the expectation is that the whole game is mediocre or that certain aspects of the game are fully fleshed-out and others are lackluster. This game took the second route by means of having their character models looking great and having the fighting system look and feel great! Meanwhile, not every character that has a speaking line has an in-game model and some of the environmental textures aren't appealing. The game is easy to understand, has fun gameplay, and is an excellent first Fairy Tail game to come to the West on modern platforms. If you're a fan of the franchise, purchase the game. If you're a fan of RPGs and want something new, purchase this game. If you're a quality snob that doesn't sacrifice anything because you're a PC gamer and your PC is powerful for a reason, purchase it when it's on sale.Edit: After beating the game, I can't recommend this game enough to fans of Fairy Tail. This game made the epic moments feel epic and made the emotional moments incredibly captivating. I truly can't express how much joy this game has brought me as a fan of the series, and I hope there's another game to come!

_childDocuments_.review: After 46 Hours of gameplay, I finally finished everything except some Social/Bond Links.Here is my basic review of the base game.Story:The story follows the anime content closely with references from past events (Haven't read the manga so I can't comment about that). Some scenes were skipped probably since it did not involve major fights in Fairy Tail.The game covers Grand Magic Games Arc until Tartaros and dabs a bit on some Final Season stuff,Graphics:Very well made, and the Skill Animations are top notch, some animations take longer than most but you can turn off the animation if you feel like rushing the dungeons for some basic quests.Gameplay:Very basic RPG in my opinion, it does get grindy on some parts but its so rare you won't notice it that much.There's only 2 main cities and little to no NPC interaction aside from your Guild Mates.The request board is your main source of quests and income. They are all fairly simple fetch em/ beat em quests.The Bond Links is a nice addition especially how some characters reference previous events in their talks, not everyone has a dialogue cut scene though.The encounters walk around the map so they are easily avoidable. Music:The Fairy Tail vibe is here, Wouldn't mind for more Summar:Get it if you're a fan of the series or have at least knowledge of it. The steep price for the content is not worth for those looking for an rpg experience but who am I to judge. I had fun and would probably buy the season pass soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, after doing a full playthrough I feel as if I'm ready to talk about my thoughts on the game.A couple things to clear up first. 1: If you where expecting this to be some AAA scale game much like Dragonball Z: Kakarot, this is sadly not the game you're looking for. It's clear in many places that this game was made on a strict budget, and this mainly shows in the games cutscenes and a number of the development shortcuts used. 2: This is not a 100% faithful telling of the Grand Magic Games, and Tartarus arcs of the series. Instead it is an abridged retelling with some sections either reworked slightly or outright cut out.Pros:A fun combat system that feels rewarding to get good at. A good selection of characters each with their own unique strengths that work well with the game combat.Enjoyable interactions between the characters, some of which we don't get to see much of in the show. Plenty of side content, with a number of references to the source material as well as some filler episodes.While certainly no replacement for watching the show itself, the game's abridged retelling still hits all the important beats well, and keeps a good pace throughout.Cons:As mentioned earlier, the game is clearly low budget. Certain environment textures such as walls tend to appear rather low quality, especially if you pay attention to them. Some important characters to the arcs don't have character models that appear on screen, instead just being off screen with just a text box with their picture next to it. Some don't even have any voice acting to go with itNo English voice acting. I know dubs aren't every anime fan's cup of tea, but it would have been nice to get the english voice cast on board.Practically no keyboard support. You pretty much need an Xbox controller as the command prompts default to that set up.Conclusion:While certainly rough around the edges, Fairy Tail is a decent RPG to sink your teeth into if you're a fan of the source material. However I would not recommend it to those who haven't at least watched the anime for themselves yet.

I'm not going to address the pc port issue as I was told that it will be fixed in the very near future. Where this game really shines is in the combat gameplay. So why else do you expect from a classic JPRG game? A car racing?gun shooting element? or puzzle solving? Do you even know the what does 'GRIND" means? Yes you are welcome to abandon this RPG if u dislike, instead of insulting it being "repetitive" while the game does nothing wrong itself.Yes. it's a slow pace RPG. You play as the members of fairy tail, you get the chance to enjoy their leisured daily life, doing some side quests together to build up the friendship. Don't you like Fairy Tail? If you do, why don't you have the patient to do their favorite character normal life, why are you so DESPERATE TO FIGHT EVERY SINGLE MAJOR BOSSES IN THE MAIN STORY AND END THE GAME ASAP. _childDocuments_.review:
Fight for Your Guild with Powerful Magical Abilities in FAIRY TAIL. FAIRY TAIL, based on Hiro Mashima's best-selling manga and anime series of the same name, follows the spell-binding plot from "The Grand Magic Games" story arc -- enabling gamers to re-live, or experience for the first time, the exciting episodes of this fan-favorite storyline. Not only will they be able to experience stories previously told in the manga and anime, but they will even be able to enjoy never before seen story and quest elements.

Throughout their journey, players will be able to form a party from a selection of over ten iconic characters, including: the fire dragon slayer, Natsu Dragneel; the celestial mage, Lucy Heartfilia; the ice-make mage, Gray Fullbuster; the fairy queen 'Titania', Erza Scarlet; and the young sky dragon slayer, Wendy Marvell. With a wealth of guild members to recruit to their party, players can form their own dream team even including an unlikely group of allies for their own unique adventure.

The fiery and intense magical battles from the series are breathtakingly brought to life in FAIRY TAIL's environment; with a diverse range of magic available for the extraordinary characters to wield. Renowned moves from the series light up the screen, with some characters such as Natsu being able to take advantage of mode changes like utilizing the eye-popping Lightning Fire Dragon Mode. In addition, some guild members will be available to support in battle; including the Fairy Tail Guild Master, Makarov Dreyar, who can be called in to provide powerful aid on the battlefield.

In FAIRY TAIL, completing battles and quests will not only level up party members, it will lead to character bonding scenarios, provide options to upgrade the guild, and eventually raise the 'Guild Rank' enabling players to take on more challenging missions in their quest to become the greatest guild in Fiore.

_childDocuments_.review: YEA!-Decent ROGUELITE gameplay loop, in that rare decent Focus published Warhammer title-Usually quick turn based battles-Pretty good amount of unit customization options-There are 3 campaigns difficulty levels per faction, so there is plenty of game thereMEH!-Few factions available at the start, I am missing my orks...-Could use quick turn options-Unit customization will come down to farming cards...-Multiplayer seems like the place to be, but right now the wait to get in a game is too long, possibly will be fixed as the game gets inot more hands on all platformsBLEH!-When a unit is on the bottom of a map you sometimes after zoom in to select them and see the surrounding area as the camera will not pan down enough when fully zoomed out.-Longterm AI difficulty could be iffy, as I can already spot some easy cheesing strats-Some bugs where I need to click a unit multiple times to either use its skill or select it so it will move.How it Runs:While the graphic options are basically bare, it does offer uncapped framerates. The game also is running quite well with no issues or crashes. I did lower the settings off Max to high as my GPU temps were hitting the 80s, doing so dropper em back down to the mid 60s and I did not notice any graphical downgrade.specs: 3800x/32gb/3080/m2 drive loadedThe Gist:This is a fun hex turn based game with a rogueite loop added on. You pick your faction and go through a randomized campaign earning new units/items/skills and spells. Your units earn experience as they go out and earn kills/victories increasing there customization abilities. IF you lose a run you have to restart but you get to keep any earned ability and experience but lose the units you earned and have to re-earn them on the campaign map. Skirimish mode came off as basically riskless campaign mode where you can try some builds out without the worry of losing your units.*Usually when you see a Focus published Warhammer game, its a flip of the coin if it is going to be decent or just bad. This is one the times it comes out better than expected, and can see myself playing this a bunch.

_childDocuments_.review: As of release:It's a solid game. Not great, not terrible, just a cozy enjoyable middle. I'd recommend buying it, on sale or otherwise, if you enjoy TBS games/roguelites.The Good:- The foundation of the game (mechanics, progression, campaign) is solid enough that you could build a really great niche game out of it. I hope the game is successful enough to enable that.- The faction-exclusive mechanics are fluffy and fun - e.g.; the Maggotkin terraform the map with nurglings, spreading corruption that debuffs enemies and buffs themselves, allowing them to slowly snowball in power until they're unreasonably deadly. - It's hard as nails, as roguelites should be. You gain various permanent unlocks over time, though, so I imagine it will get easier the longer I play - until a new difficulty is unlocked.  - Every faction has a randomly-generated campaign that includes a bit of story, some side-quests (also randomized) and a solid variety of scenarios to play through. It keeps it reliably fresh each run. - The Nighthaunt gheists are constantly wailing about how they want to die and don't have a choice in the matter which is both fluffy AF and really enjoyable. As a Nighthaunt fanboy it's incredibly enjoyable. - Mechanics from Age of Sigmar are often emulated, albeit obliquely, rather than directly translated. Then they threw on a slew of new concepts on top of it which are pretty fun, so far. Everything is pretty fluffy and faithful. Also Stardrakes are terrifying.The Bad: - Lack of polish. Not unexpected, but if that sort of thing bothers you it can be irritating. There are a few bugs I've encountered (including one awkward run-ending one when I tried to stop a Castigator from spawning in and she just became an immortal, invisible monstrosity beneath my insect boi), and the death animations take long enough that it's a little aggravating since you can't do anything until they're done. Oh, also, every unit spouts a line of dialogue at every opportunity, resulting in a lot of overlapping voices and some silly situations. - Some elements of gameplay, even in the tutorial, aren't super clearly explained. You catch on quickly enough, though. - You can't play the other factions until you go through 3 tutorial missions as Stormcast Eternals. Apparently this is a dealbreaker for some, but i can't fathom why. It's annoying, but hardly a big deal. - You can't access the DLC weapons for Nighthaunt and Maggotkin until you've completed their initial campaigns, AFAIK. It sucks a bit because the Stormcast get access to it straight off the bat.All in all my complaints are all stuff that are easily fixed in patches, so I'm not too concerned about them. It's just a matter of time before the game is polished enough to prevent any distractions from the fun-having.

_childDocuments_.review: Look, this just isn't a good game. It's extremely buggy on multiple levels. I have to constantly go out and come back into the screen where I edit my team because sometimes weapons, skills and the like don't show up where they are supposed to. I'll have to do this two or three times to get the right aspect to appear. No, i'm in skills, why are you showing me weapons? No I want to look at what powers I have equipped to my troops, not my weapons. No, now I actually want to see weapons and it says there is nothing there despite being in the right troop type and having three weapons for them. The game crashes not regularly, but enough that just when you start to think a build is stable, guess what? IT CRASHES.  There are multiple bugs with troops types in each Roster, ranging from movement issues to powers not working.The roguelike aspect actually is a negative here and this is coming from someone who loved way too many games in that genre, from Azure Dreams to Pokemon Mystery Dungeon. Because of the Roguelike nature with this game, you can end up with something but say, banshees as your troop type. Lots and lots of banshees. I've been there. Then you could end up with Chainghasts who just let you kill indiscriminately from afar as you figure out how and what triggers AI movement. I put Harvester on my Chainghasts and just let them get the final blow in and the damage they would do would just go up nicely.  There's no middle ground with the game - just frustratingly easy or way too hard for the troops you managed to generate. Five hours in and I'm just so bored, I'm going to stop. This is not worth $40. Especially in the condition the game is in a month after launch. it's not even a 10-15 dollar game. Look, I'm a guy who has been playing Warhammer for decades. I've got a ton of AOS armies. I finished a Sylvaneth army earlier this year and am 60 figures into a Ogors army (yes, I'm painting two this year.) as well. I would like to think I know how a good AoS game goes. This is not a good Age of Sigmar game. it's not a good Warhammer game. It's not a good game, period.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I'm Not going to mince any words here, I am a Warhammer40k/Old World/AoS Fan (I'm Willing to give any universe a fair shake), And I'm going to not mince around on this review. So Here's the Pros/ConsPros:The Art Direction is Fantastic, This game truly has done it's best to stay true to Age of Sigmar's Aesthetic for the factions displayed herein.Gameplay is a welcome Mix of Positioning and Clever useage of Abilities and Units, Even the lower Point cost units are extremely invaluable in one's battle plans.Sound Effects and Animation are Very Crisp.Every Faction Feels distinct in gameplay Style and Abilities available.Unfortunately That's All I have to say For the Pros, Here's the Cons:This game has a VERY sporadic amount of updates, And Unfortunately There is little evidence to believe this game will be updated in the future, as the development team (Whether for fear of backlash or simply aren't allowed to by their publishers) has given almost no announcement of future plans or that they are working on releasing any future updates (Their official twitter's last post was when stormgrounds was released. And I doubt any newsletter subscribers have seen any word)Gameplay is rather imbalanced, with Stormcast players Favoring using knockback and chain lightning to stackwipe most of your warband, or using Armor stacking to make an invincible beefstack that will take no damage. But not even them or nurgle's stacking debuffs and guaranteed one damage via infesting a tile using a nurgling is as agregious, as the Nighthaunt Hordes who have a basic unit that can essentially render armor useless. This leads to situations where nighthaunt players will regularly ignore the enemy army in favor of simply leader sniping (As if the leader dies you lose the game). This has resulted in storm ground being more or less a cheesefest, with the biggest cheese being equipping your most powerful weapons, and traits onto your leader unit who you will get for free every match (with no penalties at all).The Game was plagued with server connectivity issues at the start (They have admittedly done work to rectify this).Most Updates have not had much impact on the meta (Chainrasp Hordes are still incredibly useful for debuffing after all more then for combat), and have more or less been quality of life changes and balance tweaks (Which while welcome will not fix the biggest changes.)Player Level Locked Arsenal, While I can appreciate the fact lvl 1 gear is useful even later on as is lvl 1 units, I find it questionable and strange that you have so grindy a method for a turn based strategy game where matches could last for an hour and then some. Especially as this means that to experience fully AoS Factions, requires a significant time expense, and can lead to imbalanced matches as you're faced off against someone with a beatstick hero or likewise highly powerful units.Conclusion: It's not worth your money really, Focus Home Interactive has abandoned this game it seems (If I'm given evidence to the contrary I'll gladly change my Opinion Accordingly to what i'm told), which is a shame as it had good potential as a turn based strategy game, so I recommend not bothering with this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Please fix this game.On initial launch, I had an absolute blast playing this game (easily a 9/10). There was enough challenge to keep me coming back after each death so that I could learn from my mistakes and adapt my playstyle. Keyword: adapt. I managed to complete Freya's campaign on Extremis and, even after a few crashes, I was looking forward to the Nighthaunt campaign. And that's where it all went wrong...I've had MULTIPLE, back-to-back crashes for specific maps and when summoning specific units. _childDocuments_.review: Ultimately the game isn't "terrible", but it's a typical case of "what if". Also, it's buggy, unoptimized, laggy and just makes some weird design decisions (in my opinion).What you get is a hex based "pseudo Xcom" with 3 very distinct factions. There's the Stormcast Eternals, your regular humans in plate, who rely primarily on defense, knockbacks and melee combat. They can summon their units around their commander, i.e. basically anywhere you need them...Then there's the Nighthaunt, who are more about debuffing and shock attacks. Their units have high attack, but low defense. And they can summon their units even more liberally than the Stormcast, yet with some drawbacks, too.Last, but not least, are the Maggotkin of Nurgle, who are all about plagues, indirect damage and ranged attacks, as well as turning the battlefield into a disease ridden area, where they can summon their armies.So far, so good. Now, as anyone who knows anything about Warhammer is aware of: These 3 factions are just a tiny fraction of all the available ones. There are no elves, no other Chaos factions, no dwarves, no Skaven, etc. There's a plethora to choose from, but honestly this game isn't good enough to deserve the "endless faction DLC" treatment like some other Warhammer games.What you get is essentially a small campaign for each faction with a unique boss fight and some nice voice acting, but no discernible story, to be honest. Then, once you beat that, you can only play the campaigns again on 2 higher difficulties, which makes them tougher and longer, and gives you more opportunity to build up your forces and get good gear for them.Since this is the "meat" of the game: Levelling up your hero and equipping him or her with better gear.There's also a skirmish mode and a multiplayer mode. The former is pointless, since there are no rewards attached to it. The latter is dead, which was to be expected from such an obscure game. I honestly have no idea why so many of these niche games focus on MP. They end up dead a few days or maybe weeks later, because there's just not enough of an audience!The campaigns are "decent" enough, but honestly, you can see again that the game was designed for MP, instead of being a rogue-lite experience. The best gear is found on the highest difficulty, of course. But that difficulty only allows you to bring one of your veteran squads. So what's the point, really? You can't even take any of your acquired weapons with you, unless you equip them on that ONE squad you can bring along. Everything else you have to acquire in the run itself. You end up with tons of units and gear, which you will never once use again in a future run... For the most part. Nurgle for instance relies heavily on spreading corruption. But the only unit that can reliably do that are the Nurglings. So you're stuck taking them with you every run, despite your faction relying very heavily on the hard hitters later on, since Nurglings are almost useless in direct combat.Funnily enough you CAN bring all your acquired skills (modifiers for units, but not weapons) with you. I'm so confused...For the other factions you can take your stronger units with you and just let your hero solo the first few fights. The way combat works is that you have to fight several enemies, usually all tougher than your units, at once, while slowly being able to summon more and more of your own each turn. But summoning means you don't get any points for casting spells early on, so it's a give or take (the game loves to do that, as I'll explain momentarily). That means you have to have a very strong hero. Too bad if you just don't get any gear for them.Outfitting your heroes and units IS fun and rewarding, since a lot of gear can fundamentally change the way you play or even almost break the game (like the legendary summoning pyre for the Nighthaunt that just keeps on spawning units and basically makes it almost impossible to lose), but not being able to keep any actual gear to at least outfit newly acquired units in each run is bollocks. In my last Nurgle run I just didn't get a single weapon upgrade for any of my units, and the difference is so stark when your 2 damage units go up against 5 damage ones ... and yet I still beat the run, because the AI in this game is bloody stupid.So, let's talk about that for a moment. I'd like to be able to strategize in such games. That means making informed decisions about what the enemy is most likely going to do, yet in this game the AI seems to be coded to just be erratic. One moment they will attack you immediately, the next they will run away and do nothing, although they could kill you. They seem to be magically attracted to Nurgle traps though ... the game also is slow af, the UI is broken in parts, somtimes your units can't be selected and used, because they stood on a tile where an enemy unit just spawned in (unavoidable if it happens after your move), while the enemy can move. One time the game just stopped working. It didn't crash or anything, but it was unable to apparently calculate something and so I was just stuck with "Waiting" in game. Had to restart the fight. Such ♥♥♥♥ is annoying. Funnily enough, even if you lose you just have to quit the game immediately and you're fine ... There are just so many little things that I'm not even that salty about the big things like replayability, fun factor or balancing (it's not fun having to fight a boss with endlessly respawning minions...just turns it into a timed fight) or variety (there's just "kill" or "defend" missions). Or the lack of explanations in game. What is "pestilence"? Oh, better check every window to find an explanation, but only out of combat, of course. Have fun trying to find what you're looking for...Or getting a really cool spell, but being unable to ever use it, because it costs 10 mana, which takes several turns to acquire if you don't summon any units... if you do it takes even longer ... and takes another 3 turns to channel, by which point you've either won or lost anyway. So what's the point?Once you get into the game it CAN be fun. But by then it's already over, and I see no reason to play the Nurgle faction's final difficulty if I just don't get anything for my hero to get stronger in several hours of gameplay to be able to even attempt that challenge. TLDR: Buggy, messy proof of concept game that COULD have been quite good, but ends up just being mediocre at best.

_childDocuments_.review: Short review.Pretty solid game so far. Played all the factions (of the 3) a bit. Storm guard seem ok. Plague is amazing and OP in comparison and Haunt is eeehhhh - my opinion. Lot of little pros/cons but by far the reason for this review and the negative is the game crashing bug of "waiting". When you or the enemy does anything you'll see "waiting" as it doesn't want you to essentially try to queue up commands becasue it needs to wait for the action to finish to process your next action - thats fine albeit a bit slow and I could see it annoying a lot of people. More to the heart of the matter is that frequently enough I will be halfway into a tough map in which I am clearly winning - and possibly had difficulty getting to this point - only to perform some action and see "waiting" forever. Literally. Forever. There is no save/re-enter as "Save and quit" takes you to the campaign map / restarting the mission entirely. As does alt-f4 or any other varition.So with no checkpoints mid-battle or any quick save or anything of that kind it is a real kick to the ♥♥♥♥ to have this rather common bug. It's definitely not my system and while it may only happen every 5 battles... I've had it happen multiple times on the same stage and again if it was a tough map (like a boss battle) you are not happy to have to re-do that battle again and again and again because of a game freezing bug.If this was fixed I'd definitely turn this positive but this is a deal breaker.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as a turn-based strategy games go, and Warhammer for that matter, it is actually a decent game which i am rather enjoying thus far. It has issues beyond a doubt, and content wise it seems a little bare bones. But all in all it is one of the more enjoyable warhammer games i have played.Positive+-Huge play-style customization ability - you are free to change and tinker with equipment, cards and units to tailor the way you want to play through the game.- Significant difference between factions - There are currently three factions. Stormcasts, Maggotkin and Nighthaunt. All of which play vastly differently from each other.- Play at your own pace - What i love about turn-based, is the ability to play the game at your own speed and leisure, which is great in my busy work week, to be able to multitask between playing and doing necessary chores outside of work.Negative-- Where is the design customization? - In the trailers they show units with changeable looks, but after playing for nearly 15 hours i am yet to discover any sort of customisable armour outside of the main hero in the Stormcasts, Freya. Which is somewhat of a bummer because i love to get that personal touch to my armies.- Only three factions - Sure the factions are well thought out considering the overall feel of the game. But i can't help but wish for at least 2-3 more factions to play with. Greenskins, Lumineth, Seraphon or even Daughters of Khaine i think all could make for some interesting factions in the game, and more.- Buggy as hell - Nothing game breaking thus far. but there is a literal gobbo horde of visual glitches in the game.- Balancing issues - Like all strategy games.- Weird card system - After 15 hours of gameplay i am yet to figure out completely how the card system works. sometimes when i unlock a new card, i can't equip it, or it is limited to maybe only one-two units, which sometimes makes sense, but other times, not so much. And it gets rather difficult to know which cards you are currently using, have in stock or not.Overall. I do enjoy the game, and i have every intention to finish it. But it needs work, love, time and care to reach its full potential.Potato ranking - undercooked potato - still edible, but could be better.

_childDocuments_.review: The pull here is in the nicely done models and scenery, the vibe of the music and the voiceovers. There's a very basic army painter in here too.Problem is that this plays in the very limited and restricted ways you'd imagine it to from the small maps and the absence of any really thought through skill combinations. Knock a flying an enemy off an edge, it's dead. Knock them into a trap you've just built, it ignores it. And that's kind of where it's at with synergies and just a feel of a game which feels like it should be a part of something bigger. It's Endless Legend or Age of Wonder scope of combat without the layer above.The card system is quite nice to introduce new models and skills and upgrades, and the unit progression is quite sweet - if punishing for losing units. Without the roguelite mechanisms there though this wouldn't be too much of a challenge I suspect.edit: heh, well over time for refund so own fault.TL:DR Perfectly adequate game if you want AoS fluff, you'll not be playing this solely for the gameplay. It's a typical Focus Warhammer release and so I'll be refunding here as I've other indie games of similar type to play which appeal more to me.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good. Its not easy, but the learning curve is there. There are many different strategies to the game, and it is satisfying to master them. I like turn based games, and this one is reminiscent in difficulty of Into the Breach. There are some bugs, both visual and game breaking. I was playing with the Stormcast faction on the extremis difficulty when I encountered a bug on the capture point mission. There were no enemies present on the map. I proceeded to capture the point, whereupon the game demanded I kill the remaining enemies. Which, sadly, there were none. So after twenty turns, and quite a bit of progress into the campaign, I lost the run to the bug. The multiplayer aspect is somewhat limited in scope as there aren't many people playing it. I played one game, and after turn five my opponent quit, which was unsatisfying. I didn't play another. Is it worth the money I paid for it? Probably not, at least not until the developers can fix some of the more critical bugs in the game. I did manage to spend some decent time on the game, and I do like it. If you liked Into the Breach, this game is definitely for you. Hopefully the bug issues will be resolved in a timely manner, if not I will change my review to not recommended. Thanks for the read.

_childDocuments_.review: A turn-based strategy game with a "roguelike" single player mode where you get new units and gear through random drops, along with a multiplayer skirmish mode. When you die in the single player campaign, you restart but keep your wargear and units, and can bring a handful of your existing units with you when you make another attempt. For battles, you spawn into a map with a single leader unit and have mana which you can use for abilities or to summon more units.  The combat allows for some strategic use of abilities but mostly it seems to be about positioning and trying to focus down enemies so you can outdamage the opponent.  It's not terrible but I found the battles to be repetitive which, when I'm expected to do multiple runs over and over until I beat it, makes the game a drag.
