At the beginning of every campaign the game would explain you who your hero is and why are you fighting, during the combat units will exchange some insults, while at the end of the run the game will show you a victory message and tell you to go for “a greater challenge”. Which, I think, was supposed to inspire you to go for the higher difficulty, but guess what? When you finish the game on the highest difficulty... It shows you the same exact “Onwards to greater challenges!” message. Ba-dum-tss...So yeah. That's  for you. Should I say that I can't recommend it? And it's another sad thing, you know? I mean, this here is not really that bad of a game. It looks decent (nothing special, not nearly as good as the fake screenshots from the store page want us to believe, but still, game has decent visuals powered by ), there's nothing especially terrible about it and I can instantly name tons and tons of turn-based games that feel way worse than this. The problem with  is not that it's terrible. The problem with it is that it's “just a big, resounding meh”. Slow, limited and very repetitive. Back in the days? With not enough choice? I'd still play it. Nowadays? With so many other titles to choose from and only one life to live? It's an easy pass. There's nothing in this game that makes it worth it to you. If you happened to pick this game up on sale with, like, 90% off, just because it was cheap, and then found yourself with no other unfinished games in your library and no money on your card? Like I said, there's nothing terrible here. Therefore – go for it. There's even multiplayer to make things a bit more exciting. But willingly choosing this game over the others? Forget 'bout it. Doesn't worth it. Dixi.

_childDocuments_.review: Given the attention to the source material and the lore snippets and the artwork, you can tell the developers are fond of Warhammer. But the positives end there.This is a boring and monotonous game that seems more inspired by mobile/console games than anything else. The entire premise is centred on a deliberately disadvantaged player who cannot summon in units, has limited unit choices, no items and no buffs. You start with a very limited pool and then have to develop everything over the course of a campaign. To give an idea of how disadvantaged, my last mission: hero spawns in, I move her 2 steps forward, AI turn, 5 AI units spam me from range leaving me with 1 health bar. Next turn I summon my 2nd unit, AI turn I'm dead instantly... absolutely f---king garbage 'design'. How is that even competitive let alone fun?When you lose a mission, even hours in, game over. You have to replay the entire campaign again and again and again repeating the process ad infinitum. The game is deliberately rigged to ensure you MUST do this a few times over before you can even complete the first campaign. Playing the 2nd campaign requires you to repeat the first even though you just won.And that's only one faction... speaking of factions, it appears there won't be any others added or any new content for that matter. The developers have vanished.Once again we're left with another one of Games Workshop's officially licenced games. They love to throw this licence at any developer and hope something sticks. It's why the name Warhammer has such terribly mixed results in computer games. After a couple of hours of playing the first campaign over and over, I am done because "the definition of insanity is repeating the same task over and over and hoping for a different outcome". Even with all the repetition I still have no idea what the story is supposed to be. Some random Stormhost seeking revenge or something? Age of Sigmar isn't terribly accessible to non-tabletop players as it is...

_childDocuments_.review: Got into the closed beta for this game and knew it was a product worth my time and money since then. Its the devs first game, though the team does have a few noted veterans from Relic and classic games like dawn of war, but still "gasket games" first time working together on a full project and i'd say it turned out as a great little skirmish turn based strat game. The roguelike elements ensure some nice replayability and there is genuine difficulty to the how the scenarios play out and i've enjoyed the multiplayer so far for the one match I've played of it, though i do very much appreciate the inclusion of an army painter. This is the first AoS game that feels like a true video game, something the IP has sorely needed.The unit models are fairly decent to look at, though i'd personally like to say that whoever did the environmental art for this game should get a big fat bonus in their paycheck, the arenas are dripping with personality despite the playing field itself being simple hexbased tiles. Sound design is also serviceable. There is something to be said about the voice acting however, I can't say its overly impressive or even very good, but it almost has the campy charm that i'd associate the dawn of war 1 games with fondly, you can tell the VA's were having some fun with it and thats fine by me.One of the biggest complaints from the closed beta from many, me included, was the lack clarity in the UI of the game. They seemingly took the few weeks they had between the closed beta and release to iron out things like tooltips and menu navigation and its far nicer now then it was in the beta, though i would still say it can be a tad clunky in places i suspect that has to do with concessions made for console players.Overall this was worth the purchase for me, people shouldn't go into this expecting triple A refined quality but regardless im sure i'll be putting many hours into this game and keeping my fingers crossed that it does well enough to see it supported further by the dev with extra DLC down the line.Praise Sigmar!

_childDocuments_.review: I saw this game a while ago on Youtube when it came out in 2021 and thought it looked kinda cool, so I bought it. Also, before I start this: this game is a roguelike. It doesn't explicitly tell you this, but it is. Keep this in mind before buying it. It's a hex-based skirmish-strategy game with three factions. You have a rising energy bar like in Hearthstone, which allows you to develop the board early with your cheap units before bringing in the big guns. Unused energy becomes half a mana point, which you need for spells. Units that died in battle can be resurrected between missions for miracles, that you get either very rarely or shoved up your butt. If you play it cautiously though you might not need them at all.Let's start with the pros:-the abilities of some units are really cool. Pulling in enemies with your Blightkings tongue, puking on enemies with your Plague Sorcerors, the whole "sacrifice Nurglings to get more Nurglings"-mechanic... and you can eventually summon a Great Unclean One or a Stadrake (I've mainly played Nurgle for now though, as you might tell).-every faction feels unique. The Stormcast are heavy (and heavily armoured) hitters with defense/attack buffs when near each other, which befits them constantly having to fight back to back against larger groups of enemies. The Nighthaunt are the most numerous but also the most cheap. You can quickly fill the battlefield with screaming ghosts and debilitate enemy units with plenty of debuffs before swarming the enemy. The Maggotkin are imo the most interesting. You slowly corrupt the ground around you, allowing you to buff/heal your own units while debuffing the enemy. Plus your abilities get additional effects if they target a corrupted hex, but erase the corruption.-the voice acting for characters and lore blurps is really good. -the surroundings on the maps are pretty enough. The game captures the Mortal Realms quite well, even if only three of them.-you can customize your own forces, not only cosmetically, but also their abilities, which gives a good amount of depth to the game.Sadly, as this is a Warhammer game, it's far from perfect and lacks polish. Some of this might be pretty nitpicky, but the amount of annoyances is what leads players to leave the game in the end.-some voicelines get old very quick. Especially the Nighthaunt ones, as, while acted well, the wailing in your ear gets exhausting after a bit. Same goes for certain sounds, like the whooshing of the charged ability at range for the Chainghasts.-the graphics are not the best. Especially not for 2021. At range it's ok, but if you zoom in, it's not that pretty.-the arenas are... just that. They're arenas with little bits of repeating terrain. There's no story here, just kill the enemies and move on to the next forgettable arena.-the world maps are also just in the style of Slay the Spire. There's no overarching strategy to be found here. Go from A to B, do not draw 400€, rinse and repeat.-zero replayability. Except designing a campaign is haAaAaArd, so you have three difficulty modes for each faction, the first playing in one realm, the second in two and the third in (I assume) three. Except you have to repeat the previous difficulty mode to get to the new content. So you finish one run and have to do the entire thing again, minus the voice acting, before you get to the fancy new stuff. So by the time you finish the game you won't WANT to replay it.-boy is this game buggy. It's not even funny at times. Sometimes the tooltip showing the damage you will deal and receive in kind straight up malfunctions, which sucks when you're literally using it to plan your next moves. Or how about you kill an overwatching unit, but their target still gets tossed around the map when they move AFTER the overwatching unit is long dead? This doesn't happen often, but when it does, it essentially removes the unit from the rest of the match.-you get all your unit upgrades/new units from random lootboxes (you can't buy them with real money, which is something at least). But it kind of sucks when your main character is a caster, but he can't get upgraded because you keep getting upgrades for everything BUT casters.-if your faction leader dies, the run is over. Now I get where they're coming from, but why can't I revive that person with the seven miracles left in my bank? Why can I only use those on my other units? I guess the leaders are not so chosen-by-their-deity after all I guess.-and lastly, the loading times. Now starting the game up and going to and returning from arenas goes smooth. The issue is IN the arenas. After every action you take you get to wait for the game to finish processing. Admittedly, my CPU is a potato, but having to wait five to ten seconds just to be able to actually do something after the start of my turn? Bruh. And it gets worse. Sometimes... it just doesn't stop processing.  Your only option is to restart the mission by going back to the menu or to forfeit your run. Now this has "only" happened twice to me as of writing this, but that is two times too much.Tl:dr this game had some potential to be a solid hex-skirmisher. I'd even say it's better than Underworlds. But it needs a lot more work before it can truly shine. Sadly, as this is a Warhammer game, that is not going to happen. Maybe buy it on sale if you're really craving some AoS.

_childDocuments_.review: It is an awful mess. It is emberassing that this game has a publisher with money yet it is in EVERY way MUCH worse than any small team indie game rogue like that is available. - It doesnt has an undo move button- The game is SLOW. Animations are slow and after every action it takes up to 3 seconds until you can give the next action. - It often doesn't show the correct outcome of an action. Like it tells you that your unit or an enemy is going to die if you attack but they survive. Or you're going to lose health even though your armor did block all of the damage.- It's boring like really boring. This is because it lacks a LOT. If you win a battle you can chose 1 of three items. Those items can be a talent, gear, exp or a 1 time use spell. The exp and 1 time use spells are just pure trash rewards.Most of the talents and  gear is going to be the same. The first campaign is fighting easy enemies until nearly the end where you get 2 rare battles and 1 boss and then the campaign ends.The 2nd campaign is the same but after you kill the first boss it just starts again. WHY would you reset the difficulty. There is NO point in doing the 2nd campaign, over just doing the first campaign 2 times as the difficulty resets after defeating the first boss. In a roguelike the difficulty is supposed to keep going and NOT reset after a boss has been defeated. So there is no 2nd campaign. It just resets 1 time so you have to fight against easy enemies again. the 3rd campaign is the same as the second campaign just that they make most of the stuff you've unlocked unavaiable. So what was the point of the roguelike mechanics and the whole loot system if they just make it unavailable in the 3rd campaign? Imagine Darkest Dungeon where the last Dungeon was just any dungeon but you can't enter it with gear and with only 1 hero.-What is the point of having a Slay The Spire like map if there are no real options to pick?In Slay The Spire or other rogue likes you have options like battle, elite battle, resting place, upgrades, shops, random event, etc...Here you haveOption A: Kill all enemies. Difficulty 1 skull. Rewards ???Option B: Kill all enemies. Difficulty 1 skull. Rewards ???So the random loot determines if you win, you can't use most of your earned gear in chapter 3 and the rewards are shown as ??? so you don't know what you get. So if you win chapter 3  or not is LITRALLY rng.The other option is just to grind until your hero becomes an immortal god so he can finish the game single-handedly.-They charge 40 € for this. It is clearly an unfinished early access game which is worse than any other roguelike available. It is a desperate try of a soulless company trying to burrow it fingers in a market that is dominated by passionate small poor teams with a dream. It's a 20 €  game which is again in every way inferior to every other roguelike that is also too proud to label itself as early access. The only thing this has going for it is that it's "WaRhAmMeR" and fans are going to throw their money at it. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR:- Gameplay - 8/10 - Good tactical depth with unit customisation. Good multiplayer and a bit tedious roguelike campaign. -Graphics - 7/10  - Give off a vibe that its for mobile but has good graphics and special fx makes it stand out.- Sound - 7/10 - Great voice acting, soundtrack is okay.So I  played 8 hrs into the game and played both campaign and multiplayer as of this review. I am a warhammer AoS fan so will try to view it as someone who is not familiar with Warhammer or Age of Sigmar and describe it as is. If anyone is interested please read through the review to get my opinion on the gameGraphics -  7/10---------------------Good, not triple A quality, but good all the same and its very much separates it from mobile quality despite how some people feel its like a mobile game. The animations and special effects are great (espcially for stormcast death aninamtions as it reminds me of starcraft zealots death). The 3d renders of the maps and units are unique and detailed. You can customise your warband's colors and some units visual models via cosmetic cards you get in game.Sound - 7/10--------------------The music is ok not as catchy but captures a good mood of whats in the game.The voice acting is great and really capture the emotions. From the heroic stormcast, tormented ghostly nighthaunts, and the disgusting maggotkins that sounds like you farting a unit into existence. The only thing that bugs me is the overlapping voices of some units especially the nighthaunts (Same as them, I am being tormented with a variety of ghostly wails and complaints of suffering in overlapping voice overs whenever I start moving the units around but I guess that part of their charm)Gameplay - 8/10--------------------I am fond of tactical games and can say that this has a good tactical depth to it. Gameplay is a turn-based and hex-board strategy. You summon units to the battlefield to complete objectives and defeat your opponents. Units are represented in cards with their stats and abilities and can be customized. Each unit has a level (cap to 3) which expands their skill slots but not their stats. Summoning cost increases/decreases depending on each customization cards (items and abilities) you equip that unit with. Each faction has its own play style and the variety of unit customization makes it also unique to make your own strategies. Units are unique for each faction and there are no similar units crossing over to each so your definitely playing different styles and you just have to find out which one suits you more. Each unit is important so better take care of them and sacrifice as necessary. The maps also offers some nice bonuses like height advantages/bonuses and terrain hazards which you can use to your strategy. Maps are also randomly generated so battlefields are completely different on each campaign (For multiplayer, its even on both sides for balance). For starters its going to be a slight steep learning curve learning some of the abilities and faction playstyle but if you push through and learn you'll get the flow eventually.Campaign  - 7/10--------------------------This is as everyone says a rogue-lite/like experience. There are 3 sets of campaign difficulties each unlocking sa you complete 1 set. You create a small warband, steadily growing as you complete missions and collecting items. Once you faill a misison, all your progress will restart BUT Hero levels, unit cards and their levels, and items and ability cards you have are maintained. However at the start of the campaign, you can only pick 2 units and an ability card and you start growing your warband again. I can say the campaign ain't a walk in the park either, you need to be strategic and play carefully if you want to reach to the harder missions with a well prepared warband. Overall, I had fun doing the campaign and was very much rewarded with a completion of a set. Other than that I think some people will find it tedious and boring (I experienced it after doing my 4th try) and I understand that as well especially when you built up a good warband. I can say for those who don't like the experience is to keep going and eventually you will be rewarded in the end.TAKE NOTE: Your progress in the campaign is not tied to multiplayer so any units, items, ability cards you have will not carry over to multiplayer. Speaking of mulitplayer....Multiplayer - 7/10------------------------Mulitplayer has a player rank and faction rank which determines the matchmaking. If you are fighting against someone with higher player rank than yours expect some extra passive and active ability effect on their units. If you see he has a higher faction rank expect a powerful unit he has on his deck as well as other bonuses he gets. Currently there are only a few players so matchmaking can be a bit unbalanced (rank 1 vs rank 3) but overall it depends on the strategy your doing.Overall the gameplay is much the same in the campaign with a very good tactical depth to it but your fighting against a smarter opponent. The map is even on both sides with some occasional difference in terrain effect/hazards so you need to know what to do and learn the battlefield. Know your factions strengths and weaknesses, make use of unit abilities, and try to control the map to gain an advantage. One thing that bothers me is that I think there is a time limit for each player turn? It was frustrating that it move to the next opponent turn when I was not finished with activating all units. There was no indication of a timer or any warning, so this is a negative point for me in this mode.TAKE NOTE: Same as campaign progression, Multiplayer is separate and so any cards you have wont carry over to campaignOverall - 7/10------------------------Not the best of games and definitely not the worst. Gameplay was fun and challenging for a strategy game with 3 factions to master and play with. Campaign can be tedious but rewarding in the end. Here's hoping they add more factions and units especially Destruction Alliance which was not present in initial release. To the developers who might read this:It could really use a LOT of  quality of life fixes, like quick tooltips, card sorter and custom naming, and maybe a change in the warband customization UI as it is very confusing. I do not know which unit is equipped with an item/ability and sometimes end up swapping which was not my intention,I highly suggest the developers create a detailed tutorial as the campaign plunges you into the story but does not go into the specifics and just a quick glance to the the warband setup UI for example. Please also add a Turn timer if there is such mechanic in multiplayer as this keeps happening to me. Please also add in a chat function so that at least we can talk to our opponentsI recommend to revamp the UI and add in a quick tool tip for unit cards. I had no idea what the symbols on the unit cards are until I started getting ability cards to know that they were health/ attack/ movement stats.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Pretty game, but not a good rogue-like. The game is to slow and not rewarding enough to keep you interested. There are dozens of Rogue-likes out there that cost way less then this and are much better, go play those games. Pros:* Good production value* Good representation of army units from the Source Material* Makes good use of core-mechanics (turn based combat of dudes on a board)Cons:* Core rogue-like mechanics seem weak or poorly implemented.* Extremely repetitive and grindy* Story is not engaging/compelling* Loops don't feel rewarding and take to long* Unit management utilizes a very clunky interfaceMy take on this game: Storm Ground has good production value and looks very good visually, much like an early 2000 teen-pop-star music video, but there isn't much substance to it, also much like the aforementioned early 2000 teen-pop-star music video. The game is basically the Heroes of Might and Magic (HMM) series battle system, with the twist that your Hero participates in the battle as a unit too. For those who don't know what I am talking about, the game takes the old-school turn based combat grid system of units on a board fighting each other and tries to make an entire game around just that. The game makes a good effort to embrace the dudes on a board beating each-other up as well as HMM did: there's terrain features, there's high-ground, there's ranged and melee units, there's special abilities, and even spell-like effects you can throw around the battlefield. However, where a battle in HMM would take 5-15 minutes, these go on for 30-90 minutes each (most are closer to 30-40 minutes, but they can become drawn out affairs), which makes the game feel like a repetitive. In an interview with the developer, he said that each campaign should take about 10-12 hours to complete. As far as I can tell this is primarily down to the animations taking forever and the actual game play being a grind. The actual content of these campaigns appears to be about 3 hours worth, and its padded out to be 3-4 times that with bad pacing mechanics. There is some content beyond the initial campaigns but I didn't play long enough to see it, and I doubt the time investment is worth getting to it as it is likely more of the same based on my research.Why I can't recommend this game:You get to play one of three factions each with a campaign. Each "campaign" is a randomized series of mission to battle through towards a final battle to complete the story, which is the primary driver for you to keep playing. The story itself is kinda weak and doesn't really seem to matter, so the primary drive to continue the story isn't really there for me. You get upgrades as you go, but it's a convoluted mess that is very clunky to manage, especially after you restart after dying. Those two issues alone probably wouldn't put compel me to not recommend this game, but they were worth bringing up as issues I had with the game. My biggest complaint with the game, and why I can't recommend it, came down to the levels taking to long to get through and the basic game not feeling rewarding enough to keep my attention; which makes the whole thing feel like a slog, so playing the rogue-like loop just looses its momentum. For a rogue-like game to work there needs to be a sense that there is a point to what you're doing, and in Storm Ground there didn't feel to be a persistent reward for each run, they all just felt samey and not worth the time or money investment.

_childDocuments_.review: Been playing since the Beta, most of the complaints are about the bugs and the fact that it feels like we only got half of a a game. While I do agree with many of these complaints I will say that the half of a game we did get is actually pretty good. Presentation and Graphics are pretty spot on, all things considered this looks like an Age of Sigmar game. Voice acting is actually really well done with its over the top nature kind of reminding me of those old dawn of war games. The Soundtrack leaves a bit to be desired which is disappointing when considering the music that they used for the trailers was great. The Core tactical game-play is quite fun when it works, though the AI can be very dumb sometimes. That combined with the smaller maps means that this isn't going to be the deepest turn based game you've played, but there's still plenty of room for strategies and build variety.The Rouge-like nature and high difficulty of the campaigns keeps them fresh for multiple play throughs though I would be lying if I said you could sink hundreds of hours into them like you can in other Rouge-likes. The Characters are interesting to me and I think they represent each of their respective factions very well. The narrative itself is also neat but it certainly feels a little half baked, with that being said this game has the best audio logs i've ever heard in a game before hands down, and can see myself playing the game more just to collect them. Multiplayer has some issues but I do still enjoy it for the most part. The Maps and Factions are well designed with each feeling distinct and different. Full cross play is supported so you should pretty much always be able to find a game in a few minutes. There are of course balance issues but that's expected for any newly launched game nowadays. The Main issue for me is the progression, where the over the top powers of a rougelike game awkwardly clash with a competitive multiplayer mode. Players who have more time in the game simply unlock better gear and abilities so new players are going to struggle to catch up; plus the insane amount of gear you can unlock honestly makes this game a balancing nightmare. In my opinion they should just create a ranked mode with set loadouts making the game easier to balance and more fair to new players, though I'm not a developer so maybe that would be easier said than done. Overall this is a fun somewhat casual multiplayer mode that I plan to play more of, just keep in mind that you're going to lose your first handful of matches to catch up to the other players.This was Gaskett games first project and I would say they did a great job, unfortunatley Focus is infamous for pushing out their games far too early and Storm Ground has suffered from that. I'd say this game is a 7/10 maybe a 6/10 if you hate AoS or TB Games and I could easily see this become an 8/10 once the ui and bugs are sorted out. I've enjoyed this game alot and can give it a solid recommend as we aren't going to get any more AoS games for awhile and this is definatley the best one we've gotten thus far, If you're unsure It's more than fair to wait for a sale on this one as chances are the game will get patched in that time as well. I hope Gaskett are able to support this one for a long time as Storm Ground is a solid start for their studio and I'm eager to see what they decide to add to it in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think it's necessarily a bad game but I do think it's a mediocre one and something that really just isn't for me.I'll preface by saying that I don't care about Age of Sigmar at all. I loved the old world and all this means nothing to me. I only picked it up because I loved the idea of a new rogue-like that would have hero progression and such. Learning the game wasn't too difficult but the strategies take a bit to figure out without doing research. However, the longer I play and the more I understand about the game the less I really enjoy it. The rogue-like elements don't really feel all that rewarding on the harder difficulties. Instead it feels more like bashing your head against a wall until you get lucky with the loot drops you need to make progress. The progression is, well, very lacking since leveling up a unit only gives it more slots for skills. Heroes want to slap on all the skills they can but basic troops really get punished by equipping skills for the fact that it makes them cost more to summon for each skill applied. Add to the fact that most skills seem to suck in my opinion and you generally end up tossing the same things on every unit you can, it's rather boring. The rouge-like elements feel like they are there to waste your time rather than reward you for playing. I didn't delve into PvP and I never will, so I can't attest to how fun that is or isn't, and I will likely play this a bit more to try and feel like I got my money's worth out of it. That said, I don't recommend it at this time. Maybe in the future they can expand some of the mechanics and add more content but, at the moment, it feels really bland and shallow.EDIT - Also yeah, like others are saying, the Nighthaunt voice overs for their units are just aggravatingly bad. It's tempting for me to mute the game when they are around.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Storm Ground

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay and depth of the game is pretty solid and the diversity in both the unit rosters as well as the faction mechanics is really good which makes up for the fact there's only 3 factions in the base game.However. This game is not ready for release. It is absolutely full to the brim of serious bugs. Crashes constantly. A multiplayer that is barely even usage - I've only had 3 games that have gone past 15 turns and every single one of them has resulted in me "disconnecting" and getting a defeat. And my internet is perfectly fine and I'm still connected to steam, so the game is broken somehow.I've crashed multiple times in the campaign. Had numerous instances where I'd get a guaranteed crash upon picking up bonus loot in a level - since this is a roguelike being forced to not get extra loot is really bad so I had to revert to an earlier checkpoint.There are graphical bugs in which units still appear on the battlefield even though their tile is empty and they are dead. Numerous UI bugs.Bugs. Bugs. Bugs.This game is not ready for full release and I recommend getting it in 6months or so, when hopefully the bugs are fixed.Aside from the bugs the game is well worth the AA price.
_childDocuments_.name: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Storm Ground

_childDocuments_.review: There is a solid base here, but this is clearly set up to serve as a platform for selling DLC. The primary problem coming with that is the obvious lack of content. Only three factions with a hand full of units each will not keep me playing the multiplayer, which is clearly the (intended) centerpiece here, since the campaigns are very basic and repetitive.The strength of this lies in the unit customization which offers quite a lot of tactical flexibility and variety already, as well as the solid turn based tactics core gameplay loop.Aside from the lack of content, the second most pressing issue here are the UI and UX in a wider sense. Its very off-putting. Many tool tips arent where youd expect them to be and a lot of things happen in fights that will just leave you wondering what the hell interaction or effect just happened. Youll wonder that, wonder whihc slot some equipment thing you found goes to, which submenu it disappeared in, wonder what the hell "tribute XP is" or what "Aethyr" actually does, wonder what the units in a mission preview are, since hovering over there image doesnt open a tooltip, etc. etc. etc. This game needs to become much better at communicating information to the player, streamline the UI and support the decent core gameplay with an itnerface that doesnt contantly get in the way and obscure stuff.The StS groundwork of the SP runs seems pretty weak and the "story" is laughable, although laudably voice-acted.At some point, this will be an enjoyable, deep and varied PvP tactics game. But it isnt that yet. My recommendation is wait until this has a few more factions and buy it at a bundle sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this one if you enjoy tactical games in general. The roguelike campaigns and multiplayer feel pretty good.  There are bugs, but i would expect those to be ironed out over time. I havent run into any bugs that are game ending, only graphical and audio based bugs. My biggest gripe is that we have to wait for the animations to finish before choosing out next action. This sometimes causes you to run out of time during multiplayer, even when constantly doing things. At the moment, the playerbase is a bit small, but i can see it increasing if more factions are added and more features added for each mode. The roguelike mode is very light on the roguelike aspects. in essence, every unit you get you keep equipment and all. and you choose your initial loadout at the beginning of each run. So really its about balancing your loadout between function and cost. Example - i had maxed out nurglings with 3 skills on them. which increase their cost from 2 mana to 5 mana. which made them very hard to use. they were more useful when their cheaper. I also think that the nurgle faction is the most mechanically dense faction, but also the most powerful. They may need to be nerfed a bit for multiplayer. I also think they need some readability changes. They have 4 forms of corruption, but they all look identical which is confusing. Multiplayer makes that situation worse, since you can't tell whose corruption is whose. The faction i want to see the most in the game is Bonesplitters. would be a good destruction faction, and would be very diff from whats in the game so far.

_childDocuments_.review: There's quite a lot of hate for this game but I highly suspect those reviews are being generated by Warhammer fans whom are not also Yu-Gi-Oh fans.To understand what makes AoS interesting and unique to many other Gamesworkshop titlesis the anticipation of looting new and highly useful cards; especially those exclusively equipped by new units which you've also procured.AoS's progress is very similar to most rogue-likes where you will play over and over again making only marginal progress each time while ramming your face into an impenetrable wall.As each playthrough finishes you receive XP to distribute to your new army members to make them stronger and all sorts of new cards to apply 'n' try to your units.What I personally enjoy about AoS, which is much different from some other tactics games that I have played recently, is that you're not repeating efforts to try and discover the approach which the developer's intended (ie; Gothic Armada series)Instead your repeated plays are allowing you to finally discover a loadout of units and card equips which gels with YOUR personal approach.

_childDocuments_.review: Turn based tactics, rogue-like with some shades of HoMM.  You start a campaign and if you fail, you're game is over.  You can acquire characters (they can die, but can be revived) and gear that are perma unlocked as well.  Took me a couple of hours to understand what the heck was going on though.Things to note:You can stop enemies from spawning by standing on their spawn.There is no map rotation (I find this annoying).When you attack an enemy and kill it (with a normal melee attack), you move to their tile (another annoyance).There's no initiative, your team acts in whatever manner you want.You can't draw a specific path to move.There is no "back", meaning if you move or act, it's locked.There's no confirm to end your turn, so DO NOT PRESS E unless you want to immediately end your turn.  When it's your turn, it always starts by saying "end your turn'.No 32:9 ultrawide support, so I play windowed at 1080p. *FIXEDWhat you see is what you get, no hidden RNG (besides loot).High ground matters.Even with a lot of not so great implementations, so far I'd recommend it.  As with most games, some QoL changes for some of the things above would greatly help.

_childDocuments_.review: Storm Ground is a turned-based tactical battle skirmish game that clearly draws inspiration from similar tabletop games, and injects a few roguelike elements for good measure. Despite the limited faction roster, I've been impressed with the variety of units and how different combinations in my Warband can change how a scenario plays out. Even in the early game I've found it quite challenging, which I appreciate. (I even lost the first mission during the tutorial!)  I especially like that the skirmishes aren't too long, making it a perfect game to drop in and out of casually if you don't have a lot of spare time for gaming. I've spent the entirety of 5 hours so far only playing the campaign, so I can't comment on the multiplayer; Look to other reviews for info about that. However, be warned that I have encountered a number of gameplay bugs; Mainly certain ability interactions not working as expected, a unit that went unresponsive, and a showstopper that required me to force-quit the game. If you don't have the patience for that sort of thing I'd suggest waiting until a patch or two have been released, but I'm confident it will improve over time.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only 5 hours in so far and i've barely scratched the surface and that's just with the Nurgle side of things, yes you can appease the grandpappi himself and play as a champion of Nurgle as well as 2 others. I love Warhammer, and i've played a lot of different Warhammer games but this is one that I keep wanting to come back to. Here's what I like and dislike about my experience so far: Like: 1) Character models and overall graphics are super gorgeous and the devs have really captured the twisted, disgusting appearances of the Nurgle tribe as well as the other champions (who I have yet to fully play). 2) The voice acting is great, and I am really liking how the champion interacts with others. 3) Refreshing rogue-lite element to it, you keep your gear from the previous run and 2 units but start from the beginning. This may sound OP but the game is very challenging and not in a way that will leave you frustrated but wanting to adapt and learn each time, like how every good rogue-lite came should do. 4) NURGLE! One of my absolute favourite things about the Warhammer universe is Nurgle and his children and this game has finally successfully showcased that and has a interested game mechanic to go along with it. Negative: 1) Clicking units and clicking to move them can be a little slow but overall it's not a huge negative. 2) It just needs some general polish that will come with patches and is to be expected of a new game. It's nothing game breaking just general fixes. Do I recommend? If you're a fan of strategy? Yes! If you're a fan of Warhammer? Yes! If you're a fan of rogue-lite? Yes! Do you enjoy bursting nurglings out of an infected and boil ridden land? YES!

_childDocuments_.review: The core of the game is fun. You perform runs that consist of a chain of battles that ends with a boss battle. During a run you find loot and units that you can add to your warband and when you win or lose a run, all the loot you've found remains with you. You can then select two customised units and your hero for your next run.I find that way of doing a roguelite to be quite fun, you always gain something and it prevents you from becoming too overpowered for new runs.Excess items and units can be sold for XP that you can use to boost your units and hero.I also enjoy the battles themselves. They are challenging and varied enough, even though you're facing a limited number of factions. The units of these factions are also diverse in their abilities and can be upgraded themselves as well, just like your own units.During a battle you would do well to make use of the terrain and push enemies into danger zones to kill them off quickly as there tends to be a lot of them.There are a few things I don't like:1) Voice acting is a mixed bag. Some units sound good, others sound unconvincing. They also tend to keep talking all the time, so the bad voice acting starts to grate quickly2) The UI is bad. In some places you have to left-click to open unit details and in other places you have to click right. Most icons are not explained and require guess-work, It is also not explained that you apparently need to stand still for your archers to be able to shoot. Trial and error there during my first run.3) Age of Sigmar lore is stupid and pretentious. Although I do like collecting lore bits in the game, I can't help but roll my eyes at Games Workshops' worst decision since their founding.4) One of the promo videos talked about players enjoying viewing the models and being able to zoom in and look at them. I agree! But then WHY ISN'T THAT IN THE GAME!? The models are lovely, but I can't turn them around in the warband screen and I can't zoom in far enough on the battle maps.5) Only 3 factions :(The negative points don't detract from the enjoyment I get from the battles, but they do sting a bit. Some of them can be fixed though, and I'm hoping DLC will bring in more factions as the core game is very solid.In all: Recommended!Edit: After playing this game for a dozen hours or so more, my recommendation gets a bit flaky. The core of the game is still fun, but the lack of content really starts to bore me. I'm going to put the game on pause for a bit and wait until they release new stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Nvm, game is dead.Okay so, this game basically is a turn based rogue like game with heavy emphasis on multiplayer pvp.SINGLE PLAYERThere are three campaigns, one for each faction, you can only have one campaign active at the time (so if you are playing spooky guys, you can't play plague guys unless you scrap your spooky guys campaign first).Campaigns have scenarios, each scenario has its own objective, like killing a specific target, or killing a certain amount of enemies. Usually you will have multiple scenario choices at the time, each one with different objectives, difficulty and rewards.Rewards can be new units, items, gear, skills, etc. You can use those rewards between scenarios to customize and improve your squad. Here is the thing: if units die in a scenario, you have to spend “miracles” to revive them, and miracles are limited, so you have to take care of your units.Units can also level up, so the more time they survive, the stronger the become.You fail a campaign if your main hero dies, or you fail to accomplish the scenario objective. You can, of course, try again, but you have to start from zero (you lose everything, units, items, etc). There is where the rogue like element lies.MULTIPLAYER.It's cool. You have to build your own small army, and there is a lot of customization just like in single player. Items in multiplayer are, of course, completely separate from single player.I still have to play more multiplayer games to give a better opinion about.CONCLUSIONAll in all, it is a pretty cool game. It's kind of hard due to the rogue like elements, and the game does quite a bad job at telling you stuff (What each stat means, and you can't see units abilities and skills in the army builder, only while in a scenario, which makes no sense).

_childDocuments_.review: A decent tactical roguelike, but a hard one to recommend.The Good Stuff:- The game is quite pretty, and the environments and character models do a great job capturing the metal-album-cover insanity of Age of Sigmar.- It scratches the Jagged Alliance itch. Character upgrades and loadouts are meaningful, attacks don't miss, and every action has consequences. I love XCOM, but I get sick of every isometric tactical game trying to be XCOM, especially the parts of XCOM I don't like, so this is actually pretty refreshing (especially since there hasn't been a good Jagged Alliance game in decades...)- The three factions are all fun to play and have a unique playstyle. Stormcast play high-mobility offense with aura buffs and high armor, Nighthaunt have expendable swarm units with easy access to healing, and Maggotkin play area control/denial.- The voice actors are chewing so much scenery that you can tell they were all having a blast on set. The Maggotkin hero Ichorian Cankerscorn, for example, sounds like a deranged demonic-possessed version of Homer Simpson.- The roguelite aspect is justified in the game lore and is fairly satisfying to play through, though it is a bit limited after a good number of runs.The Rough Stuff:- Buff auras can stack, making spammy Stormcast lists a nightmare to play against. Many are the times where I abandoned a run rather than chew through the armor on 4-5 units of Stormcast liberators.- The game uses hexes instead of grid. Yuck.- The hex map can sometimes fade into the background, which makes for good screenshots but also makes it not terribly clear which kinds of terrain are safe and which ones are blocking/hazards.- As of this review, there are only three playable factions and each has a fairly limited unit roster, so once you've finished a run or two with each one you've pretty much seen all there is to offer.- The game bugged out at many important moments for me, forcing me to restart several missions (including boss battles)- The AI is usually decent, but every now and then it will make a move out of the blue that makes you scratch your head...Honestly, it's pretty good, but it's a bit too pricey for what you're getting right now. I'd recommend waiting a while until some more content gets added and the bugs and AI get smoothed out a bit.

Drawing new units with each run ends up with you having tons and tons of the same unit available to choose at the start of a new run, and I believe that the equipment on these units is not added to your pool if you do not select them, likely providing an answer to my abovementioned issue. Having a way to combine units of the same kind would also be excellent, as I don't need 8 Glaivewraith stalkers (of which I can only ever use 5 or 6, if I wanted to even run a pure glavewraith stalker build). _childDocuments_.review: Fight, Die, Reforge and Fight AgainBLUF: There is not enough unit variety or depth to combat to make this game worth 30 dollars. It quickly becomes reminiscent of the movie "Groundhog's day", fighting the same missions repeatedly with subtle differences. You will find yourself failing missions not for lack of a plan but not having enough time to sink into the game yet to compete.The Good: Spell effects, Environments and UnitsProps to the development team to be the first to bring the Mortal Realms and the toy soldiers that are known and loved to life in a digital form. I believe you can tell they cared to bring something as abstract as Age of Sigmar to life and it's seen in the spells and death effects. The Bad: The card and level up systemBeing able to customize your units from their abilities to their look is excellent. It being gated behind RNG drops that must be acquired during a campaign is not. This method of progression artificially extends its playtime as some missions have a kit requirement.The Ugly: The combat and paceThe combat is shallow and begins to feel repetitive at roughly 3 hours in. Worse, there isn't much unit variety to spice it up. It may have been a "less is more" approach, but the game doesn't encourage you to experiment. A player simply stumbles upon what works. Further, any experiment you the player undertake is paid for in the greatest resource of all - time.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------The Review Part 2 - Electric BungalooAfter about 16 hours in I finished the Stormcast Campaign - grinding through the same levels with minor differences on Extremis difficulty.Extremis Difficulty - Spoiler: You start nearly bare bones. Invest in skills and your hero. As you'll have to build a warband from scratch. While I was pretty miffed that all* the things I had collected so far was meaningless, it did provide a meaningful challenge and test my knowledge of units. A bit tedious but price of failure in this mode made it moderately suspenseful. Thankfully the AI is pretty simple and enabled me to play very defensive until the final rumble with the Great Unclean one where I took it down in several risky moves.What do you get for besting Extremis mode and liberating the mortal realms?Nothing. No cool cinematic. No special unit skins. You get the same ending as normal mode. I got a hero skin that I can't even use in Multiplayer to show my inclination for bad decision making and willingness to grind to give a game a chance. Sigmar be praised.Multiplayer- Don't bother. You'll sit through a wait timer only to matched up against someone who has more experience than you. (Again, its more about time invested vs. testing your skills) You get really nothing for playing comp stomp either. If your looking for a good multiplayer experience I suggest looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: A solid turn based rougelite game. There's some nice depth to the gameplay and the way units can interact with each other. Units can level up and be equipped with different gear and skills that can benefit your play style. Want to buff other units' armour, but also heal? Equip your Stormcast Liberators with a healing ability that triggers when their auto-protect activates. Your commander now has a bonus to their armour and recovered some health. Hell, if you have found enough skills and gear, equip the same skills and items to multiple units of Liberators, spawn them all next to each other, and now you have a self-healing shield wall. Now give them the Healing Warhammer, use the hammer slam ability to knock back enemies, and heal all adjacent units.The game looks good, units having been converted from the tabletop to in-game models pretty nicely. The different environments and maps look good. Special tiles on certain maps force you to think about how to manoeuvre and place your units (those damn planks have caught me out more than once when I wasn't paying attention to unit placement). Sounds are decent, music is pretty good. Overall, if you like AoS, you'll probably enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cant play anymore since, well, bugs.Edit: They patched up the bugs and made the UI looks and work better. It is still ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ though - Health/Armour of units gets hidden unnecessarily, making it hard to plan ahead; some icons do not have a hover over text, it does not show which items are equipped on which unit (it becomes a chore to customise the loadout); and there are a lot of ambiguity on how the potential move will affect the units.There are three factions to play as, each are different from each other forcing different ways of playing it. The customisation of units is a nice touch to change how your units are utilised in the battlefield. There is some complexity to the stuff happening on the screen, so you get your dopamine shot once you pull off a badass move.Fundamentally, three fixes will bring this game to actually fun to play:1. Improve the damn AI - right now it does incredibly dumb moves, and wins by overwhelming you with its units.2. Improve the UI so it is not painful to look at and is more user friendly.3. Improve the drop of the items so the rogue-lite elements actually work well - right now it is really hard in the beginning, and really easy in the end game. You also will miss entire unit types/weapon types that fundamentally change the way you play the game.A really good bonus would be if a free-to-play only multiplayer version of the game would be available for everyone - the multiplayer has that sweet sweet progression that could hook many for days to come, but currently is dead.I do actually like the game, but as such i do not recommend buying it at the full price. They fix the stuff mentioned up there, and you got yourself a decent tactical rogue lite experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played a Warhammer game before, as they all looked sucky or were published in gaming genres that I do not enjoy.  This game is a very welcome exception!The single player campaign fights are randomly generated, although they become rather familiar after several runs.  The point is to gain and level units while amassing skills and gear, a portion of which you are able to bring to each attempt you make to win 7 fights (on level 1) in a row and defeat the endboss.    What you don’t wish to keep, you can reduce to Tribute, which you can use to level units instantly.  If your hero dies during the run, it resets, but you keep everything you found.  Pretty typical roguelike mechanics, not sure why so many people are whining about them.Although the variety of units is small, the same unit with different gear and skills can function completely differently and you only get to use 1 hero and 5 units in your squad anyhow.It took me 13 hours to beat level 1 of the first human campaign.  There are 3 campaigns with 3 levels each, so plenty of game to keep hacking away at.  Besides the humans, there is a Slime-Goblin playable faction and also an Undead one.  I look forward to playing around with their units as well.I can’t speak to the Multiplayer, but it definitely looks like it could use more players.This game is badly in need of tooltips!But, once you figure out what does what, it is quite fun and immersive.

_childDocuments_.review: Age of Sigmar Storm Ground is a Turn Based Strategy game based upon the Warhammer World of Sigmar. This game starts you off by playing as the Sigmar army as a Tutorial.  You will learn their army style of play and once you finish the 3 missions, thats when you are able to play as the other two factions available or continue the Rogue Like Campaign.  The AI will give you a challenge from the start especially since you will be playing to unlock new units, weapons, abilities etc.  The three factions play out with different ways to enjoy the game.  You will be playing each time as a rogue like campaign to go as far as you can , since your units will die during each run but they will end up being unlocked for the next run should you finish or die from the game.  It is a fun game if you like to unlock things to help you progress further by having more available units as well as unlocked weapons etc to help your run.  I especially enjoy the play style of the Nurgle Maggot kin army since you get to spawn little nurglings over time and slowly try to surround the enemy to whittle them down. If you like Turn based games as well as Warhammer Age of Sigmar theme, I think you will enjoy this game.  I look forward to newer armies to release as well and hopefully soon. I do want to play an Orc army in this theme.

Even the campaigns are "Go push the enemy fortress and kill them all" - Ok, but do it 1 tiny map at a time and have every map take 15 minutes because of the 3 minute breaks for talking? XCOM has large maps and variety of units, etc, I don't need to explain it to people who know the genre. Same with Fire Emblem which has the similar "Your hero has died, game over" campaign mechanic. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a really big fan of Age of Sigmar and enjoy the tabletop version of the game. I became a fan of the tabletop game about 3 years ago and paint the models, read the books, and play the RPG/wargame, etc... This is the first real PC game associated with Warhammer AoS to my knowledge. There have been a few phone games which felt okay. Warhammer video games don't really set the bar very high. Total War Warhammer is probably the best example of the IP being used with love. Vermintide is also a great example of Warhammer being done with love and attention. Unfortunately, I think there's games like Chaosbane or Dawn of War III that completely miss the mark. Stormground seems to me to occupy a space like Dawn of War II or Space Marine. It's a well-done video game in general. It's fun, the gameplay loop is enjoyable, and the developers seem to genuinely care about the setting in a way where the used it in an interesting way. It felt like Age of Sigmar and I wanted to keep doing just one more mission. If you're a fan of AoS, I think this would be a great game to buy. _childDocuments_.review: The game is a series of turn-based matches set on a small hex grid with your troops versus the enemy. It's a bit like heroes of might and magic battles, but much less interesting. That's the gameplay. The game is too simple and also too slow - animations take quite a while to finish every time you or the enemy does anything. This is a typical problem for such games, and other games will offer a way to speed up animations. Not this game. So you'll be waiting a lot.The game is also one of those games where you power up a bit for every playthrough, whether your win or lose. This is also true in e.g. Hades, but Hades is skill-based and you can win the game with no powerups. This isn't possible in this game because it's turn-based and there isn't that much going on, so it's just a repetitive grind of running into matches you can't win no matter what you do until eventually you can win after enough powering up. That's not great.The Age of Sigmar setting is a slight flavoring for the game but the storytelling and characters are poorly done, especially the hero you are forced to play at first.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a perfectly mediocre game. The biggest issue I ran into was the difficulty was absurdly high for single player. Though it's assumed that's because it's also a rogue like as well in the sense that every campaign attempt you get a few new items to help your next run(s). Problem is that doesn't make for a fun experience when you're constantly in a situation where you're completely unable to win, and the expectation is that you just have to fail another 10 times. In most rogue likes, the idea is that you 'can' win in any run regardless of what items you have, it's just difficult. The idea is supposed to be that each subsequent run makes the game just slightly easier due to unlocks and progression.This game doesn't do that. You just have to keep playing over and over looking for items. Let your units die, and once you get the item just forfeit the game. You won't win anyway, so save your time and reset now that you have the item to make the next run slightly more playable.That's the biggest issue with this game. Bugs can be fixed assuming they bother to do it. But this game you aren't progressing to win, you're progressing to make the game playable.

_childDocuments_.review: Unless you're big into Warhammer stuff, I'd steer clear for now. so far my experience has been pretty meh. Currently maybe worth... 20 bucks-ish?Main ProsNice, chunky turn-based/hex-based combat, once I understood most of it.Animations/GFX in combat are pretty sweet. In general, the art dept. did a fantastic job.Main ConsUX/UI is not very clear, or at least obtuse in how they present information. I was struggling to find out exact details of what icons meant, if I could attack or use abilities after performing different actions, or the actual effects of certain abilities/buffs/etc. That's a bad thing to happen in a game of this genre.Units have perma-death, but you sometimes/somehow earn "Miracles" to bring them back. You can also apparently just start a new campaign and keep what you earned in a previous one (tried this to redo the tutorial, didn't work). This whole perma-death-but-not system is pretty jenk.ComplaintsHoly cow do the enemy undead units love to blabber on one after another. Tone down unit audio lines.The pre-combat screen where you equip units/gear/etc is very clunky. There's no need for the massive size of the unit cards. When equipping gear, there's a left-right arrow for scrolling through gear, only showing one gargantuan card at a time. Why?I leveled up a Castigator (archer unit), and as far as I can tell all it did was make it cost one more mana to play out. Am I wrong on this? I didn't see any other change other than an extra skill slot, even though I only had one skill available for them. I played through the first tutorial mission in my first session, then spent this most recent second session playing through about 5-6 missions (so this one may be on me forgetting things). More UX/UI confusion. How do I tell if I can attack after a move of a given range? Are the little blue energy looking balls under my mana representing how many skill points I have to use? Why do I sometimes gain four of those a turn, or more/less? How exactly does armor work? Is it a chance to deflect an attack entirely, does it reduce damage, or both? TLDR; I don't see this game doing anything new in the genre, and what it does do isn't fantastic. Again, if you aren't huge into Warhammer, Watch some let's plays, or skip (unless the developers put some shine on the game, or it goes on $20ish dollar sale).

_childDocuments_.review: I like the campaign system and I love the art style. I love that they went through and voice acted it all (even though I am not a fan of some of the voices, I am very glad that they are not silent or just speech bubbles). The multiplayer is okay but really needs a few small changes. It is not a buggy unplayable mess like many other Warhammer games.The campaign functions by doing runs where you collect gear and items so that future runs will be more successful. The system is quite fun, especially early on as you discover new equipment, scenarios and enemies. There are three factions (Stormcast Eternals, Nighthaunt, and Nurgle) and three difficulties for each faction that you unlock by completing the previous difficulty. At the time of writing this review, I have reached the third difficulty for the Stormcast Eternals, with a bit of time spent in multiplayer and a trial run as the Nighthaunt. There is a lot replayability and you can certainly get your money's worth from the campaign. My only wish is to have the cosmetics for the troops appear more often, or to be able to equip a cosmetic for a troop type to each unit of that troop type.The game also has multiplayer, but it is . In multiplayer you have a player level and a faction level for each of the three factions. As you level up each one you get gear and units for each faction. There are not many people playing that multiplayer (each time I have played, the total players in it is sub 100), but since it is only 1v1 the queue times are not too bad. The main issue I have with it is that you level up quite slowly, and since there are not many players, sometimes your opponent might have a much more geared out team. They also need to make some improvements to the HUD and UI, as there is no turn timer and it isn't very clear as to the order that your reinforcements arrive or what they are equipped with.Thus far I have only experienced some visual and audio bugs that did not greatly affect the gameplay.

I think the combination of a turn-based hex-grid game with rogue-lite elements is brilliant; add in the warhammer 40k inspired theme / lore and you have a game bursting with potential. I think, unfortunately, that the  game suffers from bad UI/UX, fun-killing bugs, and a few other things mentioned below that make this a 6/10.Pros:* difficulty feels about right* voice acting is great  -- it's way over the top but works* map art is really great as is the high resolution version of until you see pre-battleCons:* buggy - i've encountered several run ending bugs or bugs that make me repeat the map* user interface is pretty clunky -- the rewards all take the form of cards in the UI and it's a pain to sort though once you have a lot* for me it can be hard to tell unit apart on the battle field* the interface and user experience for trying to read what an enemy does is awful* slow - once you've got some experience with the game the long enemy turns become a bit painful. _childDocuments_.review: Overall I enjoy this game and can recommend it, especially if you're looking for an Age of Sigmar game. However there are some problems with it, though most seem to be fixable with updates. - The campaign seems to lose the story element after the first one for each faction, take with at least some salt as I've only reached the second campaigns.- Restarting can be annoying as you lose access to many of the units you had as you only have a few to choose from every campaign run and have to rely on random drops.- The random card drops often result in many duplicates of cards, though they can be turned into experience points. However this becomes irrelevant when your units reach max level. A good note is that there's no loot box style "pay for better cards" system.- The UI can be buggy at times and the animations can be a bit glitchy, though for me personally I haven't experienced them too often. The same goes for the crashes.- The voice acting can be hit and miss, personally I don't care for the stormcast voices as many seem to be trying too hard and some of the lore cards have awkward editing. The other voices, at least the one's I've encountered, I have liked.Overall I think after a few updates the game will be great, and if you can get passed those things I recommend it.

It's almost like playing a card game like hearthstone/shadowverse in the way you select and play your units, (how much power they cost to play, and every skill you tack on adds to that cost. If you have leftover power points, it turns into resource for casting abilities, so you want to also think about preserving some of it)The combat itself plays out almost like fire emblem, or a tactical strategy turn based rpg if you haven't played a fire emblem game before. _childDocuments_.review: Its a roguelite game, it takes alittle bit of time to get used to and doesn't explain alot to well. Part of the gameplay is each section, you have a chance of a lore urn or a warchest that spawns.From there, everytime you "die" you get to keep afew things from your previous runs to take into your next run. You then start at square 1 and have to do it again, but the cutscenes don't play out again, its only that first time your through (at least from what I've seen) however once you get further than where you died, it continues the cutscenes.Without spoiling much, as Nurgle, I got to the end of (what I think is the first area?) and died. But I got to keep all my good stuff so I was able to get back there alittle quicker next time.The stuff thats permanent though is the lore scrolls, which I believe gives the overall story and lore of the factions.Each faction plays very unique, like actually surprisingly unique. Stormcast are all about clumping up and the liberators and your lord castelant gives each other guard bonuses, I've gotten my HQ up to a 67% block chance with a massive armor bonus, so she could never take any damage. Nurgle is all about using your nurglings to sow seeds of corruption, which creates different tiles, which give your units bonuses from healing, to bonus damage, etc. I haven't played the Nighthaunts yet, so I can't say alot.The only complaints I have, is that I wish they had a experimentation field so you could test out different warband builds. I also wish they had a library that showed all the wargear you've seen so far. All in all, I just wish they had a library or glossary to be able to look at everything.But holy jesus is the game customizable. Game is completely worth it if its on sale, as it currently stands unless your a massive AoS fan, the game is not worth the full price as the time currently stands.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a gem here, so it will get a postive review here. It was as so many games nowadays not long enough in the oven (with focus games this seems be the norm) and still needs a lot of love.There are almost no tooltips, you have to find out almost everything by clicking around and hoping for the best (how to one equip skills, units, wargear etc.) And very little is explained in game at all. There are a lot of  things missing which one would expect nowadays - no possiblity (that i know of - but see above..) to sort your gear in equipped or unequipped if you want to fit out your units, you have to click through evertyhing, you have to find out yourself what the colours on the items stand for and so forth.Nevertheless if you overcome all this, there is a nice tactical game hidden under all this and if focus would for once give the devs time to amend this and other rough edges (who was making the ui and didn't see the standard cursor trashing the immersion, work on the responsiveness and so on, this might be a great game, even so it is enjoyable if you grit your teeth and soldier through.If this goes the way like most focus published games and they sell only the already made dlc for different factions and patch the bare minimum i would give it a neutral - which is not possible.If this really happens i return at a later stage and change it to negative (which in reality it hasn't earned even yet), but so is the way of the binary world nowadays - there is only yes or no (black and white) anymore, no place for the greys or neutrals.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Warhammer 40K + AoS, and I love turn based games (Xcom, Divinity, etc) but this game doesn't really "do it" for me.Unit Graphics & animations are pretty good and I want to like it but I find it more frustrating than enjoyable.Firstly, the maps are way too small and fairly dull looking/boring.When fighting Nurgle it wasn't long before the centre of the map was fully corrupted, so much that I couldn't reach enemies without having to run through it - and without any way to remove the corruption.  Compared to Xcom and Divinity you don't have much scope to use the environment much (climbing, cover, jumping). Second, not being able to save between missions is very annoying.Every decent turn based game lets you save as often as you like but not this.I'm not a fan of losing all my progress because of a couple of punishing turns in a boss battle.I suspect this was done to extend the longevity of the game.  Third, you need to spend miracle tokens to resurrect fallen units after combat.If you don't have enough miracle tokens you have to restart the campaign or go into combat with too few units.I really don't like this mechanic at all.  It seems unnecessary and the units are very squishy.i.e. 2 units of chain rasps can kill one of your units in just one turn - even if they've been buffed.Fourth, hero's don't feel very powerful.  Aside more health they don't do much more damage than regular units.Early on you can easily lose Freya to 3/4 units of weak enemies - I didn't feel she was worthy of 'hero' status.Granted you can power your hero's up with items, but again they feel weak early on.Fifth, the randomness of obtaining extra units can hinder you greatly.I really needed more melee units so Freya didn't have to tank so much but I kept getting ranged units.Like other turn based games I like to pick my own units & customise them.Units gain in level & become slightly stronger with experience so you don't want to keep getting the same units, I prefer to stick with the ones I'm levelling.  Also when you restart the campaign you can only keep 2 of your levelled units.Six, there is no difficulty slider.Some people will struggle, while others will want a greater challenge.As a casual gamer I'm not too fussed with the difficulty as long as I can save between missions.Seven, you can only place one unit on the board each turn.  What the...Your enemy will spawn with 3-5 units immediately whilst you have to slowly place one unit each turn, and they can't attack or take an action until the next turn.  This really hurt me against Nurgle who spawned 5 units against Freya, and by the time I had a full unit roster half the map was corrupted.  I don't mind a challenge but this just annoying.In summary with a few tweaks this could be a much better game.Bigger maps, ability to save at will, and better unit management would make a big difference.As it stands I don't think its worth the price but if you like a difficult turn based game give it a go.Just don't expect Xcom.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game. Might be overpriced but if you're a fan of Warhammer AOS this is an amazing world that accurately depicts a lot of the different warriors for the Stormborn, Nurgle, and the Nighthaunts. It's amazing to see them come alive and fight finally.Gameplay wise this is a great combination. Rougelite Dungeon Crawler with almost deckbuilding aspects (albiet the cards are warriors and upgraded weapons, skills, etc for them). Choose between three aforementioned factions to go through a randomly ordered set of dungeons that branch out into different scenarios to choose from and see how far you can get your run. Unique mechanics, amazing world. Definitely one of my favorite Warhammer games. Reminds me of games like Slay the Spire.Each faction has some unique mechanics which open up a lot of strategic play for your runs. Nurgle has almost a creep like mechanic.

Given the pickup and go sort of play, I kinda regret not buying it on Switch. Not bad for $30 though.

_childDocuments_.review: Update, I just don't like how this game is tied into everything, as it pertains to SP and MP. 95% of the content is constantly walled off to the player, your campaign units don't carry over to SP skirmish mode, MP requires its own unlocks and such. AOS-SG will die a horrible early death because of the developers design decisions, they've catered to a few and not the majority of their fan-base. This game is intended to be a grind, in every aspect, I'm not even going to get into all of it, many have made it clear in the forums already. I've enjoyed my time so far with AOS-SG, three very unique and distinct factions, a lot of unlocks and unique skills and units to acquire. The army painter was a very pleasant surprise, didn't expect that. I find the campaign overly difficult at times, you're completely outnumbered often to the point of near impossible odds, often times you are. I don't like how you can lose a unit permanently until you can get another card, I guess it makes sense to a degree, though lose one key unit and it can completely derail you the next mission. I would like to see map diversity in skirmish, the campaign has some great maps, why aren't they part of skirmish mode. Overall, I find this to be fantastic game, though a lot of things that still need updating, AI looking at you and depth of field should be an option to turn on or off.

name: Kandagawa Jet Girls
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition Includes Digital Soundtrack + 2 Costumes + Base Game About the Game From the creators of SENRAN KAGURA, experience a fresh, colorful racing extravaganza with Kandagawa Jet Girls! Welcome to near-future Tokyo, where the hottest new athletes race high-tech jet machines through urban waterways for thrills and glory! Choose from seven teams of two Jet Racers, each with their own story. Each team has a Jetter, who steers through each course's gauntlet of obstacles, and a Shooter, who uses a variety of water weapons to blast your team's opponents off the track. Coordinate between them to perform speed-boosting maneuvers and pinpoint-accurate trick shots. Of course, every other team has a Shooter too, so watch your back and keep your shields up! Tackle the River Alone or Compete Online Experience the game’s robust Story Mode with each of the seven two-girl teams having their own unique multi-episode arc totaling 64 episodes of lighthearted racing drama, or go online for multiplayer mayhem against up to three opponents in casual or ranked matches. Upload your best times in Time Attack mode and compete against the records of the best players in the world. Go Under the Hood and Customize Winning races and challenges will unlock hundreds of customization options, from the girls’ swimsuits and hairstyles to the jet machines’ skins, decals, and special effects. The inside of the jet machine is as customizable as the outside, allowing players to fine tune its performance to best match their driving style. Shinobi Surprise! Includes playable characters Ryōna and Ryōbi from the SENRAN KAGURA series as a special bonus for all players! Eight other shinobi from the busty brawler franchise will also make appearances as premium DLC.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun blend of Wave Race, Senran Kagura and Mario Kart Double Dash. Kandagawa Jet Girls has a bevy of game modes from Online play to Time attack, mini games and of course the story mode. The game also has an extensive set of customizations for both your Jet ski and for each character. The story mode is packed with content and each level has objectives that will unlock items to buy in the in game shop. I've always been a big fan of aquatic racing games between Wave Race, Hydro Thunder, Splashdown, etc so when I heard of a new Jet ski game from the creators of Senran Kagura (a series I've been fond of since the Vita) I was instantly excited. Thankfully the full game was exactly what I was expecting! This is a relaxing and fun summer getaway with a side of fan service. Highly Recommended
