_childDocuments_.review: NO this game is not worth the price of admission, be aware! (also dont even bother trying mouse/keyboard on this one)Ugh this game should had been amazing, and while I did enjoy my 15 hours with it (thats how long it took to me to get all achievements and get best rank on each stage 0_0 )and do recommend it to some people, it has some HUGE FLAWS that you need to be aware of before you decide to buy it.1)Sony completely censored and butchered this game, just watch one episode of the anime adaptation and you will notice a huge difference, this was meant to have a ton of fan service and nudity, instead its basically family friendly. Censorship like this lead to the producer of this and Senran Kagura games to resign... this is a huge loss to ecchi games as he made a ton of great games.2)Because of the previous point, it seems devs kinda just abandoned the game, all missions are EXTREMELY easy, you need to actually play as terrible as possible to loose, aside from the beginning stage for each arc, as you cant equip too many upgrades until you beat a level or two... but once you do, you will be running laps around your enemies. It seems devs just forgot to add a difficulty setting. They try to add artificial challenge by giving you missions to do for each stage, but alot of them are really dumb, for example "Shoot a weapon 4 times" or "Shoot every opponent once", I literally had to hang back or park my jet while I waited for my opponents... until you figure out there is a "trick" you can do to easily get em done, then I was max ranking/getting all missions done in a single run... I did not feel like I was being challenged at all, it just felt like some lazy addition.3)The rewards for actually doing missions are just ... lame, half of them felt like they were just a variation of the same boring swimsuit, where is all the risque outfits? I did not feel like I was being "rewarded" at all4)The customisation overall felt very lacking, everything was a colour variation of the outfits from the main cast, or the boring mission rewards... you literally have to buy the Senran Kagura DLC to get any decent outfits. As for your vehicle, you can buy upgrades for them that add stats, and once you buy them, you can equip them on any of the vehicles for any character (provided you advanced far enough in their arc), every vehicle will end up with the same upgrades that are not reflected visually... aside from that, you can change their color and stickers, but thats it. Funnily enough, the way to make money to buy items is not actually through racing,  instead you can do any of the 4 easy mini games for a ton of currency (easily x10 what you would make on a race), I enjoyed this as it was a nice change of pace... but shouldn't the main game be giving you more rewards? 5)As I mentioned I completely finished everything possible to do and got max rank on everything by the 15 hour mark, but I can imagine someone who is a decent player, speed reads the dialogue (most of it is repetitive and boring), and doesn't give a **** about doing missions could easily beat it in under 8 hours.This is really shameful, as I am a huge fan of anything Honey Parade makes, but this game feels more like a "proof of concept" than a full release, considering they are already turning this franchise into a sh*** mobile gacha game that will only come out in japan... the franchise is already dead :( You definitely want to get this one on sale only, and as I mentioned, watch the anime to see what this game was actually supposed to be...and shed a tear for what we could have had if not for evil Sony...

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to enjoy this, but I really cant. I never thought that the difficulty being too easy would ruin enjoyment, but it does. There is no difficulty setting for the story mode aspect of the game, though in free mode there is. Which doesn't make much of a difference anyway. Almost lapping AI as well as finishing anywhere from 30sec to a minute ahead of 2nd place. Rarely do you need to shoot others and the only times I would is to do a challenge and deliberately let the AI take off form the starting line and get a few seconds ahead, even then, a 10sec head start, by the end of the 1st lap, you are already in 1st place with a 10sec lead.The game play is decent, and has that Xseed aesthetic we love. The maps are not too elaborate and there could've been more variations or even shortcuts etc. You can customize outfits, rider variations, and Jet ski decals/tuning but require in-game currency or unlocks via races. I tried finding an Online match with no success, even on ranked. You'll need to find a friend or someone in the community who still plays to race against, at least they may provide a much more thrilling experience then the AI.Overall a below average game that could've been so much more. A game that you may pick up just to play here and there and move on after an hour. Dare I say they could've made it much more lewd like SK PBS or at the very least made the AI a bit more punishing, but it fell into the Sony censorship being first released on the playstation4 and then ported to PC, that butchered the Xseed style we love. I finished the first school and it was 12 missions of the same stuff and rather not do it all over again for each school. The AI doesn't get any stronger either with each passing mission. Get the game on sale, or just pass it all together. It isn't going to be like a SK experience. It plays like an arcade game (which could be cool riding a jet ski in an arcade). You'll get more enjoyment out of the anime.
_childDocuments_.name: Kandagawa Jet Girls

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is an enormous fan of Marvelous/HPG and the Senran Kagura franchise it truly pains me to give this a thumbs down review. The AI is just so insanely easy, broken, and terrible that I never even get a chance to use weapons or any of the fun mechanics during the races because I'm too far ahead of everyone. The game could probably be a lot of fun if the opponents were at all engaging, but coming in first feels like I'm watching paint dry for 3/4 min. If you've ever played Mario Kart in your life, this will be frustratingly easy to you. Side note, I think the mini games are a fantastic idea. They're entertaining, and offer a great way to grind money compared to SK titles in the past where you just had to repeat missions over & over to buy out the shop.The story is lighthearted and passable, but severely lacks a lot of charm compared to SK. Not too big of a gripe. It's relaxing and mindless in the way SK is but to me the cast isn't nearly as entertaining.Lastly the fanservice aspect of this game is also severely lacking. They didn't even just reuse the translucent wet clothes system from PBS, I dunno seems like that would've been pretty free to implement. I mean sure not every game has to be on Senran Kagura levels, and I'm fine with that honestly. However if we're going to skimp on the fanservice can we at least get the game to play better? If the gameplay is lacking and the fanservice aspect is lacking we aren't left with much in redeeming qualities.This game just falls short in too many areas for me to recommend it. At least I certainly can't recommend it for $50 which I paid. Great concept, bad execution. In a perfect world this would've been a great Mario Kart clone with sexy girls but it's just boring and that's pretty sad. If you are interested in games like this I'd recommend any Senran Kagura game instead.

_childDocuments_.review: Kandagawa Jet Girls is booba jet racing and it's rather well made. It may be made in the unity engine, but fear not my friends, for somewhat actually justifies its price tag. I'll start off by saying I recommend this game to someone who knows what they are getting into, but much like the precedent set by the Senran Kagura series (which is what brought me here), certain flaws hold it back from being more than a niche booba game. At first sight upon install and boot up, I have to say this game looks amazing. Everything is very shiny and incandescent, which some might not like, but I dug it. The graphics, lighting, texture, and especially the you-know-whats ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°) look better than before. I truly wish the Senran games looked this great and had these proportions ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°). It ran at 120fps perfectly (although there is no true ultrawide 3440p option, it just stretches the screen, so I played bordered).Next up is gameplay. It is comprised of two elements, much like booby and booty, you have the vroomy and shooty. You eventually can go pretty fast on the courses here, and it can get pretty difficult if you don't take full advantage of the mechanics of the jet racer - which was also another nice surprise. For someone who knows nothing of jet racing, it felt logical the way you control it. You can take advantage of drifting, lifting the vehicle's nose up or down to go faster or turn better (respectively), and an acceleration that coincides with the trigger of a controller. Being a PS4 game as I understand it, this definitely feels made to be played with one so I would recommend that as well. You also have a boost gauge, shields, and shootable obstacles that can reward you for destroying them. As far as the shooting goes, if you played Senran Kagura Peach Beach Splash, this game makes sense as a successor as most of the weapons are the same for the most part. Using the weapons is pretty simple, and there are "?" boxes around the maps that give you heftier/random weapons which you can directly control. For example, you can choose to fire in front of you or behind you. Shooting behind you will put an AI in control of driving your jet racer so you can aim. The AI most of the time keeps you avoiding obstacles but I noticed that my speed always decreased when I did it. Not just my teammate's AI but the AI all around - the AI is very weak.This is what I don't get. Babies don't play games like this because of booba - big gamer boys like myself play booba games. And this particular booba racing game appealed to a cultured gamer in his 20's, and that gamer is me. So why does the difficulty feel like it was made for babies? I, no joke, finished EVERY race in 1st place. The only reason I replayed races was to go complete missions that I didn't the first time due to silly reasons (such as being too fast for the AI). This game has a starting boost, and if you time it correctly with the countdown, EVERYTIME you perform this without fail you will speed ahead of the CPUs and stay in front the entire race (unless you get hit by a rocket, or another weapon, and your shield is broken... but you just reverse the cards immediately after). For the free races, there is difficulty options - but I didn't even play those because I had my fill by the time I completed the story. You'll spend maybe 20 hours in the story mode... why can't the story races have a difficulty too. Even the Senran Kagura games had difficulty for the story. While driving the jet racer IS INDEED FUN, you never take advantage of the shooting because the CPUs are never anywhere close to you because you are so far ahead. There are even some mission challenges like "overtake 2 opponents without being passed" and "shoot every team at least once" -  you cannot complete these challenges unless you just sit still at the start of the race, wait for the others to get in front you or handicap yourself some other way. This was disappointing, because it is a pretty dang good time, but I would have had substantial amounts of more fun if there was an element of challenge to the game's story mode. It seriously gets lonely when you never seen anyone else in a 5 minute race.That aside, the story mode can be a bit monotonous, basically written to put you into races with a cycling roster of protagonists. But they are all likable, voice acted, and have cool outfits.There is online play as well, but according to the leaderboards and steam charts no one really plays this, so don't expect that to be alive.I spent a little while playing time attack mode, even after getting the achievements, because it's fun racing against "ghosts" of players or yourself. For instance, you can download ghosts of the top 10 players of the leaderboards and race against a carbon-copy of another cultured gamer. It's moments like those where you really see how biffing a drift, hitting a wall, not shooting an obstacle, not having fast enough acceleration, etc. can take a good race split and turn it sour. And then you want to play again to shave some seconds off. But then you don't want to play a dead game so you change your mind.Character customization is decent, not a ton of outfits to choose from, but at least everything that is there has plenty of detail. Jet racer upgrades can eventually be abused to constantly giving yourself maxed out boosts. Not that it even matters though, because you can complete the main meat of the game without upgrading whatsoever. But there is a limit on how much stuff you can equip your jet racer with, so there is some fine tuning to be done if you are wanting to shave seconds off your splits or customize according to the courses. Last thing I might add is that I got the deluxe edition for the soundtrack, which is killer - lots of bangers here, so if that suits your fancy, you probably won't be disappointed. Overall, I am content with my purchase and had a good time. As far as I reckon, this game is somewhat unique with all the ideas it meshes together. It is just seriously too bad the AI/CPU/whatever is not better. I read a lot of the reviews here as well, and most of them touched on that as well. I didn't underestimate them though, I figured, "yeah, this might be easy but surely the end of the story will get pretty rough". No the lack of difficulty surpassed my expectations. If the developers are still working on this to any extent, PLEASE patch in some sort of difficulty for the story. I don't even care if it is artificial buffs that just make the jet racer stats higher... actually that would be a great idea! Let me choose to have my CPU opponents use their jet racers with the upgrades I gave it and set the CPU AI to galaxy brain mode and give me a tough time. Ryona's in the base game too, but there is no punishment to be found here, y'all let her down... For now, not sure if I would revisit this game though unless that happens.

_childDocuments_.review: is a very pretty and polished game with great graphics, voice acting and soundtrack. It's made and produced by the same people as the  series, and it's rife with nods and refences to it, e.g. the game features all the weapons from , Kafuru's dolphin (Nami-kun) is sort of a mascot here, and there are even 10 Senran Kagura girls (as guest characters, no story missions). But the extremely poor opponent AI and lacking fanservice (likely due to Sony's policies) ultimately mar the experience.The gameplay mechanics are actually pretty interesting. You can tilt the jet forward or backward for more control or speed, there's drifting, boosting, trick jumps on ramps, and the girl in the back can shoot at other racers with a pretty large selection of water guns (directly taken from Peach Beach Splash). The problem is, none of this really matters in the story mode. You overtake the AI in 5 seconds and never see them again for the rest of the race. And there are no difficulty options. I've never seen a racing game with such broken AI. You're going to win 3:30 races by 40 seconds and more. The player moves much faster and the AI keeps bumping into everything. It's literally almost impossible to lose a race. I've no idea if this kind of difficulty was intentional and they thought 40 year old salarymen who have never seen a racing game before were their audience. But more likely they just couldn't figure out how to code a reasonable AI for a racing game, as this was their first. But still, just upping the AI speed and adding some kind of a catch up mechanic would've been very welcome. Because as it is, you're watching paint dry for 3-4 minutes at a time and just goofing around with trick jumps and drifting to amuse yourself. There's a multiplayer mode too, but it's of course dead since the game bombed hard.Story wise, there are 7 teams each consisting of two girls. The protagonist duo are your generic high school girls, a genki and a tsundere, there's nothing special about them. Then you have an idol duo, a gyaru duo, a shrine maiden duo. There's a haughty rich girl with a giantess bodyguard (shamelessly borrowed from , but the game pretends it's a new character), there's a pair of American weebs obsessed with samurai/ninja stuff. The loli idols are the most interesting characters in my opinion, but for whatever inane reason their names got changed in the localization, from Tsui & Tina to Ziyu & Dina. This is strange because the localization is otherwise mostly fine and even keeps the honorifics (unlike the more liberal Senran Kagura localizations). There are over 60 story missions with a cutscene before and after the race. The writing is very safe and inoffensive, mostly just banter with some power of friendship and believe in yourself moments. It's reminiscent of late Senran Kagura games such as Estival Versus and Peach Beach Splash (when they switched from narrative heavy to just comedy and gags), but even more toothless and generic. Voice actors hard carry the whole thing.There was an  made to promote the game, it had full nudity and some very risqué moments bordering on porn. Is there anything like this in the actual game? No, nothing. Not a single nipple, no clothes tearing, not even the translucent wet clothes mechanic from Peach Beach Splash. There aren't even any finishers with god rays like in every single Senran Kagura game. There are reports saying that the clothes tearing mechanic was supposed to be in the game (it's heavily featured in the anime) and there are left overs of it in the game's files but it's believed that it didn't pass Sony's censor and had to be cut. On the upside, the character models are more detailed than in Senran Kagura and the outfits are still very sexy. More over, there's a high quality nude mod made by a certain famous Japanese modder (no links here, just google it). It has fully modeled naughty bits and stays true to the game's cel-shaded anime art style, giving it a very official look. It largely saves this game's otherwise lackluster fanservice. PC wins again, baby!Overall, worth grabbing on a deep sale (60% off + generous regional pricing made me take the plunge) if you're a Marvelous fan and want to see beautifully rendered anime girls riding jet skis (optionally nude modded). Oh, and the 10 Senran Kagura girls are lots of fun to play as, they recorded new lines and quips for all their actions.

_childDocuments_.review: Kandagawa Jet Girls. It is a new media mix anime character game launched by the creators of Senran Kagura. It's hard to argue right now whether this new project will succeed, but at least what it means is that the anime character game full of fan service has come to the PC! Kandagawa Jet Girls is the action sports genre combined the shooter element in racing. Is that a pretty unusual attempt? What about the actual gameplay? Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Kandagawa Jet Girls is definitely a game with Senran Kagura in mind. Such traces can be found throughout the gameplay. Despite such a great goal, the road to it was designed rather ambiguous. As you may know, this project also aired its anime series to promote the game as part of the media mix. This may be the result of being overly conscious of any other pressure or censorship, but this game lacks fan service content compared to the Senran Kagura series. Don't get me wrong. Fan service content is better than other anime character games. However, given the identity of this game maker, it is somewhat lacking.If so, what about the gameplay itself? Fortunately it keeps the basic core fun well. As a water jet racer, you can run cool with anime girls. Racing games generally require proficient skills, but this game is designed to be enjoyable even for beginners. Moreover, shooting elements have been added, it makes your racing exciting. These attempts are somewhat novel, but there is no deep play. After all, the essence of this game is the anime girls and their stories. Story mode is the best content you can enjoy. It will take about 10 hours or more to fully enjoy the entire gameplay content. It's good enough as an anime character game, but it's better not to expect too much gameplay. Nevertheless, if you are a fan of anime character games, it is worth a try.Kandagawa Jet Girls. It is an exciting anime character game with new characters. Water racing and shooting elements are combined in this game. The challenging attempt was interesting, but the shooter balance is a bit broken. Fortunately, the racing gameplay is fine. Besides, nice customization features to create your own racing machine with charming anime characters, and various game modes make this game even more valuable. In particular, don't miss the collaboration content with Senran Kagura friends. Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Edit (21 Feb 2021): There's no real update on the game as of now. As for a fan service game I'd say it's already dead in the water and I won't recommend you if you want that aspect of the game. Buy the Senran Kagura games instead if you want fanservices. It is still ok as a racing game so you can stick around for the racing.Expectations told me this is a fanservice game with little gameplay. But the gameplay turns out to be really good and solid despite some flaws. This game is a fun mario kart type racing game in a jet ski format, sprinkled with "good" amount of fanservice and good character.I'll be spewing a lot of info into this review all from my experience. I'll start with the flaws.Enemy AI(s) are terribly easy. This game had solid speeding and maneuvering system, in fact that aspect is perfect. But AI problem comes from the weapons and customization. With a lot of performance customization choices for your vehicle, it is a problem when your enemy don't have the ability to do the same. You can handicap yourself by not using those performance customization to make it challenging, but what's the point of the customization if that's the case. To put it simply, you can go fast but your enemies can't. There are missions including weapons as well. The problem is the weapon can't be used "manually". Weapons can only be shot automatically after you locked your target, which would suck when you need to do weapon missions and your enemies are way behind you.Design and performance customization favorites are not character specific or jet machine specific. At times I only want to favorite my costumes so that each team had matching costumes, but the favorites also saves hair style so I would have to change the hairstyle again every time I had to load that costume. It is also the same with the jet machines where the jet machine suddenly turns black (2nd jet color) rather than the normal orange blue color (1st jet color) when loading favorites.Character costumes are quite lacking. I was hoping to get quite a variety of costumes after I finished the game. There are quite a lot of it but as a fanservice game, I think the amount is not satisfying enough. I hope we can get additional costumes to get.If you're fine with these flaws, this game is really fun to play. The jet machine handles really well. Speeding and maneuvering with the jet machine feels really good and fun. Speeding with fully customized jet machine also feels rewarding, since they are pretty expensive (using in-game currency). All I can say is the racing gameplay is the best part of the game. Characters are fine, personally I like the dynamic of each teams. I can't really comment on this cause at the end of the day these are preferences.There are minigames as well as an alternative to getting your in-game currency. They're fun and innovative and I hope the dev would expand on this aspect as well.And of course, the fanservice. Unfortunately, the fanservice is only skimpy clothes. There are no "clothes break" unlike the Senran Kagura games and what they've teased from the anime. Yeah blame Sony for that.In conclusion, this game has very good racing gameplay and characters, okay dressing character "gameplay" and fanservice. I would love it if the devs would go out of their way to fix some of those issues I've listed. But even with those issues at hand, this game is still solid and fun.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: An alright racing game that you should try out when on sale and have money to spare. Unique and fun racing controls for a laughably easy game. Gunplay feels bad and can usually just be ignored. The game was made during Sony's shift to strict censorship, so fanservice is minimal and nothing compared to Senran Kagura. Characters are the typical moe mixed bag, so you'll likely find a girl to like. Story does exist, but at the lowest level possible.After completing the game and getting all of the achievements I'd say that it's alright, but definitely wait until it is on sale. The jetski controls were really unique and fun to play with, however it isn't able to shine due to the pathetically easy AI and no option to change difficulty. Furthermore, the gunplay feels clunky and can easily be ignored unless actively trying to complete side-challenges. Besides the iconic jiggle physics and somewhat revealing clothes fanservice is very minimal due to the strict Sony censorship around this time, so don't come into this game expecting something on the levels of Senran Kagura. Speaking of, I don't recommend buying the Senran Kagura DLC as they don't receive any missions so they are locked to time-trials, CPU racing, and (the dead) online racing. The characters in this game are a collection of moe girls, so you're likely to find a few girls you love and a few you hate (for me personally I loved the foreign team, especially Jennifer Peach, but dreaded Kuromaru Manpuku due to her ending every sentence with "Nanoda"). Almost forgot to mention story as there really isn't much to say. This is post-Shinovi Versus, so team stories conflicting with each other but not explicitly declaring what's cannon is a given. The last team's plot seems like an attempt at bringing back a more serious plot akin to early Senran Kagura games. However, due to these characters only appearing at the very end just to explain their backstory for most of the time made it feel very out of nowhere and laughable.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of talk about all the bewbs for what is in actuality a very tame game. Sure it has anime girls in big bewbs but there's not particularly oversexualised compared to other games nor is the story (at least the beginning) any indication of it being anything more than innocence personified. That's not a criticism of the game however. It looks good. It's more a criticism of how fans talk about this game and create wrong expectations.There's not much of a story here. You'll get a lot of visual novel style reading but it's everything you've seen before from other slice of life visual novels. All the clichés are here. Not bad by those standards but nothing to write home about either. It does give the game it's own identity though. It's a mario kart like game but with anime style story bits and visuals that distinguish themselves from other anime games by being very shiny for some reason. As mentioned this game is mario kart style, or crash team racing, or sonic racing, or whatever other kart game you may have played as a kid (or as an adult for that matter). The focus is more on the racing though, much less on the weapons. The weapons are kind of tame but there's a surprising depth to the racing mechanics. You can actually much the nose of your jet machine up or down to either go faster or have better handling. There's also stunts to perform to get some boosts.However, all of that doesn't matter because the game doesn't provide anything worthwhile to actually use those mechanics. The focus is on the single player campaign but even if you get stuck behind walls, hit anything in sight, or get turned around, you'll still leave anyone else in the dust. I did all of that (the controls really do get some getting used to) and still didn't see any competitor even get close to me. On top of that there are no offline multiplayer option whatsoever. Yes you heard me (read me?), a kart game with no couch gaming option at all.You might be thinking I've only played 45 minutes and you are correct. But there are no difficulty options and some extensive google searching tells me the game doesn't get any more challenging later on so instead I asked for a refund.

Where you have superficial talk before gameplay and they rinse and repeat that over and over until the end. There are mini games separate from the story to help change things up if you want. Doing the mini games give you points you can spend in the in game shop (with in game currency only) where you can upgrade your jets, get new outfits, accessories, etc. The mini games consist of washing your jet! jogging... mopping the floor........ etc.... You WILL have to play the mini games to buy things from the shop. And as you want to upgrade your jet to win faster you'll have to do the mini games. Sometimes GRIND the mini games. _childDocuments_.review: This game was an enjoyment for me, like the ski mechanics were there and that you got to shoot your opponents with your water guns, and of course got to see the jiggly fan service in the club room as you get to customize each girl to your liking.  Regardless of those tidbits, once you have completed the story modes of each girl, making them number one in each category, there's not much left to do afterwards.  When I want to race, I want to race with people with skill and not AI that's easy to pass and you lingering in first place for 2 minutes. There are some challenges that force you to drift back a bit, to either hit all racers with your gun or pass 2 racers before reaching first place, but they're not as challenging as the word implies.It would be great if this game offered a local play or split screen like they do in Mario Kart, but unfortunately this game didn't get much of the attention it would need to have matches online, so it's basically solo play.  If the base game went for a lower price and more people were into this style of racing, I bet it would kick off, especially if events or competitions came into play. But let's get real, the fan service of jigglying butts and boobs are the high point here and being able to race your favorite race tracks (which for me is the sewer that you get 18-20 hours into the game).I recommend this game solely for your solo pleasure and on a steam sale for less than $20 (also don't bother with the DLC)

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun playing it.  It may not revolutionize racing genre or anything, but it's still a pretty well made racing game with cute visuals.  Some people complained about speed, but just like every other racing games, the starting vehicles are always going to be slow.  It's after unlocking various upgrade when these vehicles start to get faster and handle better.  With that said though, the game was too easy in the beginning.  I'm only slightly above average when it comes to racing games, but I still find myself ahead AI opponents by nearly a whole lap on most of the races.  Eventually, the AI opponents provide decent challenge, but by then the game was about 90% done.  Another thing I'd like to mention is that every games, including this one that were produced by Takaki have these story sequences where the characters always face towards the camera while doing various gestures.  I get that this is to imitate visual novel style, probably to cut costs, but I really find this style uninteresting.  Especially in this game, it feels like a waste of opportunity since the character models look so good.Still, if you liked the anime like I did, this game is still worth having.  It was a nice game to play during summer.  Especially if you know where to find certain mods.

_childDocuments_.review: There is more to racing than increase your speed. A story of girls devoting their youth to jet races, with character designs by Hanaharu Naruko. The girls make friends and form bonds through their shared love of jet racing in this ensemble coming-of-age story. Jet races are contested by teams of two, offering accessible strategic action that anyone can enjoy! A range of weapons and jet machines is at your disposal in these exhilarating races through a fictional near-future Tokyo. In a world where jet racing has become a major sport, teams of Jetters and Shooters know how to make a splash. The Jetter pilots the jet machine, while the offensive Shooter attacks opponents with water guns. Enter Rin Namiki, a young lady whose mother was once a legendary Jetter. She dreams of becoming a jet racer herself, leaving her home island and setting out to Asakusa, Tokyo. She encounters the aloof and beautiful Misa Aoi, and the two become partners. Little by little, the two deepen their bond as they race against their rivals.

detailed_description: A Bloodless Coup: Lead the incomparable Valvatorez, a vampire bound by promises, and the ramshackle cast of werewolves, angels, failed Final Bosses and more in a story of love, loss and...Presidential politics!? Disgaea now, Disgaea FOREVER: - Level to 9,999? Make it happen. Custom maps? Build your own! Barge into other players games on a flying pirate ship*? WHY NOT!? And That's Not All (!?): Everything to ever grace Disgaea 4 is here! With over 30 unlockable characters, extra story campaigns, and modern flourishes to the Disgaea formula, Disgaea 4 Complete+ offers as deep and smooth of an SRPG experience as there has ever been. Story When the Corrupternment threatens to disrupt the way of life in Hades, Valvatorez finds himself at the helm of a fiery revolution. The former tyrant will need to call upon new allies, recruit a formidable army, and learn a thing or two about political unrest if he hopes to take down the corrupt regime and bring salvation to all Prinny-kind! Dive into a tale of revolution and redemption, woven throughout a dark and hilarious realm of vampires, werewolves, and other devilish denizens. Engage in immersive and in-depth tactics-based gameplay brimming with over-the-top destructive action, and unload a horde of special features to take your Netherworldly adventures to another level. Brace your belt pouches and grab your sardines; the ultimate HD Disgaea game has arrived, dood!

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Best Disgaea to start if you want to enter in the franchise's world.This is a Strategy RPG. You have story, characters and all that RPG jazz, but the combat plays like chess. Well, over-the-top anime-flavored chess with huge numbers showing on your screen to represent damage and your stats to be more specific. The Disgaea franchise has 3 characteristics that can define the entire franchise:- A wacky story that has a slight serious tone to keep things going. The massacre of the fourth wall and the ridicule of anime tropes are expected.- Absurd numbers in things like lvl cap (9999), damage output (trillions) and stats (99999999 ATK).- The absurd level of customization. For example: you can slightly change the colors of the skin and clothes of all your units, the appearance of the units' equipment and their names, the names of the healing items and you can even boost their effectiveness, the skills and passive abilities of your characters, the list just goes on.Most of the music score of the franchise is good to listen to and 4's score is among the best in the franchise. The franchise's aesthetics are nice and colorful but among the Steam releases, only Disgaea 4 and 5 features HD sprites. In regards to content, you can easily break the 100+ hours in all games if you are just trying to kill the strongest bosses and go to 300+ if you plan to get everything possible and make multiple powerful characters.This franchise is in a abusive relationship with Ms. Grinding and Ms. RNG, but i daresay that Disgaea 4 Complete + is the one that has both reduced in a significant amount if you compare it with the other Disgaea 4 versions and the other installements of the franchise. This is all thanks to the streamlining of the necessary steps to make an ultimate team and the multiple ways to speed up both character movement and animations. This, aligned with the HD sprites and the franchise's typical features, is why i recommend 4 to people interested in the franchise.For the first time in the franchise, a number of online features were implemented on this installement, the player now has acess to a level editor that allows the creation of maps (with slight limitations in order to prevent the creation of obscene images with the level's structure) and upload them to the internet so that other people can play them. It's also possible to upload characters for multiple purposes:- Serve as a senator that can help other people unlock stuff at the Cam-Pain HQ's hearings.- Serve as support unit to help clear maps when a certain item is used by a player.- Help other people win the Netherbattle Tournament if it is played in online mode.- Battle other players on a Ai-controlled match or a tournament that only the enemy is controlled by the AI.- Invade people's Item World (the randomly-generated dungeon that you use to level up items) as support or to be their enemies. If the Dark Souls trauma is already kicking in, be mindful that players can turn off or restrict this specific online interaction before initiating any journey in the Item World.Also, a new feature was added on this Complete + version that the previous Disgaea 4 versions don't have. There's a weekly competition now where players must complete certain tasks and, by uploading your results on the Ranking Shop at the end of the week,  earn points. These points can be traded for items and weapons. Nothing out of the ordinary except for some "never-seen-before" food items that were created on Disgaea 5.I guess that's it for the review... ah yes, i guess i need to talk about something as well. You saw those microtransactions, didn't you? YOU. DO. NOT. NEED. THEM. I don't know why NIS/NISA implemented these. You can easily beat the game and go all the way to 100% without them. Use your money elsewhere. Buy something nice for yourself, magical money for that gacha that you play or commission some cultured fan art of the best girl of the season. I don't know. Just don't buy Disgaea 4 microtransactions.Best Disgaea so far in my opinion. Buy it. It doesn't matter if it's on sale or not. It will be worth it. DO. EET.This is a re-release of the PS VITA version with some newer config options to make attack animations and character movement quicker than before. There's also a Ranking Shop now that gives you points for doing weekly tasks such as killing enemies or clearing Item World floors. These points can be traded for Rank 38 equipment, serums, snacks, Disgaea 5 food and even innocents. A fair number of things were modified or even introduced to the PS VITA version, here's some of them:- Cutscenes after Asagi's map aren't voiced anymore.- You get all the game's PS3 DLC plus a new story, new characters to use, new weapon skills, new tier of magic, new rank 41 equipment and now every generic unit has unique skills like in the Vita version of Disgaea 3.- Pre-order-only Fallen Angel Flonne and the Dengeki-exclusive swimsuit for Meaver, your dimensional guide, are included in the game now.- The Netherbattle Tournament has muted cutscenes now as well BUT you can now play the tournament offline.- Valvatorez is now suffering of DID if you use english voices. He's voiced by 2 VAs now. You can also hear some new lines from the other members of the Disgaea 4 cast.- Good bugs like the Item Shop Dupe and the glitch that allowed you to cause 184 quadrillion damage were fixed while you still have some colorful stuff happening on your game like the inability of creating Sniper innocents through the Mediator event and certain skills losing their boost enhancements if you unequip them.- You can't capture Item Gods anymore....- Geo Effects on the Level Editor's shop don't cost millions of points anymore, just thousands. Also, you don't need to sell your organs to buy Promotionhell Tickets, BGMs and Color Palletes anymore.- You have a Cheat Shop like Disgaea D2 now. You can increase EXP/Mana/HL gains, adjust enemy strength, auto-heal all characters after every map clear and choose which pirate has a bigger chance to find you in the item world. Pirate hunting isn't a pain in the ass anymore.- Meowkin Pirates can now appear on floor 20+ in the Item World instead of the previous 90+. - You can now restart a map without the need of going back to the main menu and losing your progress. Getting that Legendary Yoshitsuna or Arcadia couldn't be easier.- You can now buy Mr. Gency Exits after you beat Baal. Grinding on Chara World for those is a thing of the past now.- Inventory and Warehouse size were increased.- You have a Innocent Warehouse now. No more you need multiple crappy legendary weapons to store important innocents.- You can now pass bills with HL, trivializing the whole dynamic of the Dark Assembly.- The promotion system from Disgaea D2 is now on this version. No need to reincarnate a character 5 times to grab the Tier 6 version of a class, just promote the character.- You can now modify how a weapon looks like and its name on the normal Cam-Pain HQ. No need to go to Innocent Town.If you like to buy and play the same game again, go ahead. I'm not stopping you. Well...there's the new Ranking Shop where you can complete weekly tasks to earn points to grab innocents and serums...it's also quicker to grind now thanks to the new animation speed up features...and you can play with Stella and Rutille without the need of having a Disgaea 3 Vita savefile on your system...So, if you see one of them as your waifu or even both of them...go ahead and buy the game?...SARDINES!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea 4 Complete+. This game is an anime SRPG produced by Nippon Ichi Software and published by NIS America. The original work is a console title released in 2011(2014) as 'Disgaea 4: A Promise Unforgotten(Revisited)'. The Disgaea series is a well-made anime RPG that has received metacritic score 80 to 85. Disgaea 4, released on Steam PC this time, is a complete edition that includes all the DLC and additional stories from the console version. Moreover, the Disgaea series has never disappointed me so far. Really? Let's take a look at it with Nyanco-chan! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)These days you can meet remake or remaster games more easily than before, and even those that were console exclusive titles have started porting to PC. Of course, this game trend has both good and bad points. Developers can predict their popularity and success to some extent through their previous proven titles, and players can enjoy fun those games to suit today's game environment. Moreover, it can lead to an influx of new users to the series, and it can re-stimulate pleasant memories for users who have already experienced it before. However, not all of these opportunities lead to good results and can be very disappointing. Fortunately, Disgaea 4 Complete+ is pretty good stuff.Disgaea 4 Complete+ is still valid for today's gaming trends, and the game has returned nicely to us. It is designed to have fun not only for beginners but also for old fans by adding new elements while inheriting the original system. For example, Magi-Change, Monster Fusion, Geo Blocks, Linkage, Combo, Tower Attacks, Prisoner punishment, and so on. The game features a unique grinding system. Basically, the flow of gameplay is 'Story -> Base -> Battle'. Despite being somewhat repetitive, the process is quite fun and allows you to play the game as long as you like. There are scenarios full of delightful humor and battle content where you can unfold various strategies. Some users even rate Disgaea 4 as the best in the Disgaea series. The game experience overall is pretty good.Disgaea 4 Complete+. This is a pretty good anime SRPG where you can play as long as you like. Maybe the whole story, from the prologue to the ending, is a tutorial, and the end game content is the real start. It has a pleasant and humorous vibe, and the storyline is also interesting. Each of the game characters is attractive and supports good voice acting. In short, this game is rich in entertainment. Of course it's a bit repetitive, but players can grow their characters according to their desired concept, set challenges, and enjoy the game. The Disgaea series is definitely the best anime SRPG you can ever experience on Steam, so don't miss Disgaea 4 Complete+ as well. Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: The Disgaea series is arguably the best Japanese strategy RPGs ever made, at least in terms of gameplay.  There's so many deep game mechanics to delve into, and they're designed for a long end-game, grinding up level 9999, and beyond.  It may sound like a boring grindfest, but the part I like about their endgame is that they're all designed around the idea of exponential growth.  If you're just mindlessly fighting the same map ad infinitum, you're doing it wrong.  This game is all about coming up with schemes for levelling up as efficiently as possible.  Or you can skip the endgame and just play it as a very solid strategy JRPG.  If you ignore the endgame, you can make it through with minimal grinding, though the fights could get fairly challenging by the end.Generally with Disgaea, each installment is an improvement on the last.  Disgaea 4 is my personal favorite so far for being the first with some pretty key features that make it hard to go back to earlier installments, like this is the first Disgaea in which monsters are actually useful units thanks to the new magichange mechanics, plus it has one of the better stories, at least in my opinion.  To be perfectly honest, the Disgaea series generally doesn't have a stellar story, instead relying on its whacky sense of humor to keep the audience interested.  Usually they have a basic but serviceable A plot featuring the set of characters you like, and an extremely meh B plot with all the characters you don't care about.  Disgaea 4 is better than most for both the A and B being similarly enjoyable, or at least that's what I think, since I know plenty of other players are of a different opinion.As with all Disgaea games thus far, don't expect too much graphically.  It still features 2D sprites in a somewhat fixed perspective 3D world.  Sometimes you'll have trouble seeing what's going on due to the somewhat fixed camera.  Cutscenes are mostly still images of the characters talking.  What's there is pretty basic, though it looks appealing enough if you're into the cute anime character aesthetic.As for this port in particular, unfortunately, there's the usual problems with bugs, stability, and crashes, so beware that you might have issues with how it runs.  When I first tried it, it crashed about every five minutes until I downgraded the video settings.  Also, once again, since it's a port, they've done only a serviceable job in making it work with a keyboard and mouse.  There's no option for mapping the various functions that were so obviously mapped to the "O" button on the original Playstation version to different keys, for example, while in your base and in certain item world areas, "O" makes you jump, but in most other contexts, it's cancel.  It'd be super logical for cancel to be on the escape key, but having jump on escape is just awful.  The one other irksome thing about this port is that there are microtransactions added in, though these are completely ignorable (and quite frankly, I don't see why anyone would bother with them, as they're mostly power up items that become inconsequential if you get into the endgame.)Lastly, I wanted to note that this is a port of Disgaea 4 complete+, which means it has all the DLC, plus some additional features that did not appear in the original game, such as the cheat shop, which should be familiar to players of Disgaea 5.  I can't really think of a reason players of the original version would turn up their noses at these additions, though.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played all 4 of the Disgaea PC ports in the order that they were released on PC (so 1,2,5 then 4) and this has become one of my all time favorite series.Not sure if it's because I've played a few other Disgaea games before this one and I've gotten better at playing them, but I feel like they really nailed the progression from the story into the post game on this one. This is the first Disgaea where I've been able to play most of the post game content without feeling like I need to spend ridiculous amounts of time grinding. In the first 2 games, even the early post game was just too intimidating, so I stopped playing shortly after finishing the story. It is much better in Disgaea 4 & 5 with the addition of the cheat shop and other features, and with this one in particular they really nailed it.My only gripe is that the attack animations are not quite up to par with other games in the series (This is particularly noticeable with animations for characters from previous games, looking at you Vulcan Blaze)Otherwise, this has everything fans of the series will love in spades, and is absolutely worth checking out if you have never played Disgaea before.One last thing, the music in the Disgaea series is really really good Dood, inject White Tiger straight into my veins all day! Please release a soundtrack for all the games!

_childDocuments_.review: It's Disgaea, which means it's more or less an automatic recommend from me.Not the best game in the series (although not the worst, either) with some quality of life improvements over 1/2/3 - particularly the ability to "Promote" characters rather than Reincarnate from level 1 all the time. The Chara world continues to frustrate; I really preferred the boardgame style of the Chara world in Disgaea 5.The menu and "hub" music are two of my favourite songs in any of the Disgaea games... and you'll hear them  .It's stable (at least on my system) and runs smoothly 99.99% of the time. I have seen one stutter after a massive full-speed infinite combo chain in the Item world, where the audio popped for a fraction of a second - presumably because it was trying to play too many things at once. When I first booted it up, it wouldn't list 3840x2160 as an available resolution on a 4K monitor - it capped out at 2560x1440. I didn't worry too much at the time, and when I fired it up the next day 3840x2160 was listed; since choosing that, it has remained set.Even with the launch 25% off, this is still quite expensive, so frankly while I want to say give NIS your money so they think continuing to port Disgaea games is a good idea, at the same time I'd recommend waiting unless you really want more SRPG goodness . The Digital Artbook is fairly decent if you're after that sort of thing. Contains a few bits of art from Japan-exclusive pre-order bonuses I'd not seen before.

_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea 3 changed how learning abilities and magic inheritance worked, making it more time-consuming than it was worth to make an-all purpose mage, something I really enjoyed doing for a completely broken killing machine. I had hoped they would be made back to the way they were in 1 and 2. Unfortunately, they were not. However something about it didn't feel nearly as offensive this time. It took 4 games to get there, but I could actually tolerate the item world this time. The characters are much more lively and better developed than those in D3, I find. After two games in a row (Disgaea 2, and to a lesser extent 3) where the final boss was a complete joke, I'm happy to say D4's final chapter gave me a run for my money on multiple occasions. I have one more mainline Disgaea game until I'm ready for the release of Disgaea 6 this June. At the moment, Disgaea 1 and 4 are tied for my favorite game in the series thus far. Will Disgaea 5 turn out among their ranks? We shall see. See y'all in about a week while I play Disgaea 5.

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game. If you've played any Disgaea game you know what you're in for.There are stages of completion that I would recommend that you re-assess at each point to see whether or not you continue playing:1st cycle: 40 to 60hrs2nd cycle: if you've leveled up a fair bit in the 1st cycle then this should take a couple hoursDLC: about 10hrsX-Dimension: depends on how big brained you are, lets say 5 to 10 hoursDefeating a certain big bad overlord: didn't take note how long but you'll be grinding for a while (under statement)100% Achievements: took me 355hrs (305hrs save file), A lot of reading and watching, I also left game on when doing irl things100% the game: just because you've got all the achievements does not mean that you have 100% the game. I didn't do this. This game already sucked enough of my life away.On the topic of research...Due to this game having a few different iterations before hitting the PC as well as localisation, there are numerous changes to the way things are done/activated/attained/read (item/character name changes). This means that there are multiple different sources of information which clash with each other as well as guides having a mix of information. This will lead to quite a few moments where you swear you are doing the right thing in order to do or get something but because the information hasn't been updated or changed before being applied to newer guides, you will be left doubting yourself and having to do further research. If you're getting all achievements then have fun with that....and the freakin RNG...On top of this the end game content isn't explained in a well enough manner so I strongly recommend reading how to access this content. I know you wont reach  without doing so. So stupid.The only other negative thing I have to say is that I hate characters that self-reference them themselves in dialogue. So if there was a character named Billy, for example, billy would say "Billy likes ice cream so Billy will go get some". Drives me crazy. It's cringe.Apart from that. I like the game play style, most characters, the music is charming as always, the story...well it was alright nothing that's going to blow your socks off. Lets face it; you're here for the grind, making those numbers go up and up and up.I recommend this game if you're already a disgaea fan. If you want to dip your toes into the series maybe start with a newer one like 5 or 7 (I haven't played these yet but from what I've read it looks like new comers to the series will have a better time here). Or you could go the opposite direction like me and start at 1 and work your way up the series (I love 1, 2 is pretty good as well).I regret getting 100% of the achievements. Seriously think over if you want to sink that much time into this game or spend that time elsewhere playing another game. Like another Disgaea game.

_childDocuments_.review: is a tactical JRPG that contains the original PS3 game and all of the improvements it received in subsequent versions, now in FHD and available on PC.The story is quite absurd and contains some hilarious writing. The game takes place in Hades, the underworld, and follows Lord Valvatorez, a vampire who no longer drinks human blood because of an oath that could not be fulfilled. So he swears by sardines (yes, the fish). Human souls are transformed into Prinnies in Hades, but the president of Hades wants to exterminate all of the Prinnies. Not wanting to see this happen, Valvatorez goes to war with the aid of his trusted sidekick werewolf Fenrich.Most of the gameplay will be from battle to battle that is heavily reliant on strategy. Like most Japanese strategy RPGs, this will be on a grid-based map. You will recruit characters and make your own from several available classes for your team. You can choose how many teammates you want to be in the battle at the start, and you can add more later on as well.Your teammates can combo with one another, so there are a lot of strategies involved with really flashy over-the-top abilities. You can even use fellow monsters as a weapon. You can actually pick up and and throw just about anything. There are a lot of options available to try out. There are environmental blocks that will help you or the enemy, so it's a good idea to check what each one does.Sometimes you will need to grind a bit to level up or to get enough mana to continue. There's a level cap, but it's 9999, so expect flashy and high damage numbers to show up the more you grind.Aside from the normal battles, there are also things to do on the world map, such as taking on an item dungeon, talking to various people, etc. The item dungeon is interesting, as you are heading into the randomized world within the items. Here, you can grind levels for your characters and to improve the items.This port looks really good. I like the art style, and everything looks great in FHD, especially the characters.The music is all right. The voice overs are quite well done and bring the story alive.The game can be played with either a controller or a mouse and keyboard. Both works fine, in my opinion.I think this game is fairly priced, given the amount of content within. I spent around 6 hours going through the first of 9 chapters.It's a very nice launch-week 25% off, so people can dive in right away with a good sale price.I am really happy how many classics from consoles are arriving on PC, I look forward to seeing more to come. This is a great addition to the turn-based genre of games available on PC. If you like strategy games and JRPGs this is a must buy.Rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game from Disgaea series.This game's main feature is story in my opinion. I find it rather hilarious and unusual. I am surprised with its progression the same way as I was surprised when playing Disgaea 1, my first game in the series. D2 and D5 somehow lacked in this department. Few characters from previous games make an "appearance" in main story (Axel, Vulcanus) which felt rather nostalgic. There is also post game content that should be interesting too but I am still on my way to it.Weakpoints of this game are lack of QOL features that D5 had, like throwing unrestricted by direction, better character, item and innocent management. But that was to be expected when we go back to previous versions.I also don't like some focus on network features, it seems like it has no place in this series and just added for no special reason. Theoretically (after they activate them) you can encounter pirates from other players and can capture them to skip all progressions that you have to do otherwise. Or you can build your own map for farming instead of looking for the default ones and trying to maximize your efficiency with what you get, not with what you build yourself. But these are my personal issues with networking features, I guess some people may like them.They also tried to add microtransactions in this game, but those seems like a trap for a person inexperienced with Disgaea series who is playing the game just to read the story and stops after finishing it, not for all the content that comes after the story where all those things that are being sold become useless. Story also can be completed without touching microtransactions and there is not really a large wall that you hit anywhere in it as long as you use your extra options, like item world.Overall the game is great and I certainly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea is a series where you they let you start as level 1 but allows you to grind your character to level 9999 and deal a lotta damage! (like 1239280 total dmg)While that, you enjoy their light-hearted, comedic stories that has a hidden layer of sadness and drama with compelling characters, and Disgaea 4 is no exception.This time, our main character is Valvatorez, a former vampiric overlord, now Prinny instructor, overthrowing the Government after seeing how it has fallen from its glory. With a loyal yet cunning werewolf butler by his side, Valvatorez forms his own party and battle against the President! Of course, it won't be that simple, there will be demons who are against us.Although the story isn't as deep compared to other Disgaea games, I found it the most enjoyable story in the series. The cast here is pretty fun too and their chemistry together surprisingly works well. The voice acting here (both english and japanese) is done quite well, I love most of the cast's voices, especially Valvatorez and Fenrich. The OST is balanced for me, it has a mixture of classical and rock elements.The gameplay is here is more of an improvement from Disgaea 3. There's also a lot of mechanics like transforming your monster units in giant monsters or weapons, customising your base, passing skills from other classes and more. There's a lot of customisation and play-style. This game has multiple endings too if you're into that, (but most of them are joke endings)Overall, it's a fun game, I rate it as a Sardine out of 10, (8/10)Good game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you play TRPGs like FF Tactics as much for the characters, world and story than for the mechanics, D4 and D1 on PC are probably the highpoints of the series. I played the PS3 version for about 80 hours and I'll gladly do it again with this version!If you run this in Steam Proton on Linux, there are a few steps to get it running nicely: 1. install Protontricks and type "protontricks 1233880 winecfg" in the terminal2. go to Libraries and add the following modules (if they are not in the lower list): d3dcompiler_47, wmp, xaudio2_9(you may not need all of them, but since my config works, I never tried to change it)3. go to the game's properties in the Steam client and set these as your launch options (all one line):PROTON_FORCE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1 PROTON_NO_ESYNC=1 PULSE_LATENCY_MSEC=60 %command%4. start the game and hammer your B or Circle button on the controller or your keyboard equivalent to skip the intro cutscene and go to the main menu(since the original was a ♥♥♥ PS3 game, Circle/ B = OK and X / A = Cancel)The intro cutscene must be enabled and skipped by button mashing, otherwise you won't have any in-game sound (yes really, I was surprised too!). I also recommend turning off Anti-Aliasing and turning on Vsync, to avoid rare cases of the game crashing.Good luck and happy grinding! Highly recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: Disgaea is a tactical RPG series that excels at what is usually one of the least popular features of the genre: grinding. By doing so, it does the impossible and succeeds at making it surprisingly fun and addicting even while being less impressive in the narrative department.My experience with Disgaea 4 Complete+ is based on a somewhat limited breadth of knowledge of the series as I’ve only played the first two titles at this point. Though I never found myself able to get past the twenty-hour mark in the second game, I played the first for upwards of two hundred hours. Whether it was timing or something that just didn’t resonate with me in the sequel, I’m happy to say that the fourth title is one that I’ve found myself hooked on thanks to a handful of new and improved features.As far as the elements that tactical RPGs are classically known for, Disgaea doesn’t stand out. The story isn’t particularly exceptional in any way and the dialogue is decent as long as you’re alright with it being heavily flavored by humor. Character progression doesn’t have huge class trees and there aren’t long lists of abilities to choose from for each of them. However, its pinpoint focus on grinding ends up providing many features that make leveling up your roster a deep and reward experience all the same.Characters are divided up into two categories, humanoids and monsters, and there’s quite a bit of difference between the two by this entry in the series. Humanoids are capable of making use of just about any piece of equipment that you get your hands on (from swords to guns to axes), while monsters are only capable of equipping two specific types, one that focuses on raw physical damage and one that’s more well-rounded. Both categories can equip the wide variety of armor and accessories that you’ll be picking up along the way though. However, humanoids do have weapons that they specialize in based on their class, often with abilities that are paired with them, so you’ll likely be restricted to two to three classifications of gear if you’re going for peak efficiency.As far as capabilities outside of equipment go, both categories of characters gain new abilities as they level up, primarily via spending mana. Mana is another character-based currency, like experience, that can be used to improve characters, most notably via unlocking new classes, learning new skills, improving skills they already have, and reincarnation. Though the rest are self-explanatory for anyone with even a basic knowledge of RPGs, reincarnation is a far more unique feature that allows a character to be reduced to level one, though the more mana that is used in the process allows for that character to retain an increasingly significant amount of the attributes and skills that they’d gained prior. Think of it like prestiging but with far more useful benefits.Of all of the tactical RPGs that I’ve played, the monsters of Disgaea 4 have proven to be the best designed that I’ve ever seen (honorable mention to Fell Seal: Arbiter’s Mark for having a solid system for them as well). The real key to my heart here was the addition of the fusion and magichange aspects. Fusion allows two monsters to bond together to create one giant-sized one while magichange allows a monster to turn into a weapon that a humanoid character can wield. These abilities are great as they allow for not only significantly increased character efficiency but also allow both characters involved to gain experience at the same rate as if they were solo.Everything in Disgaea 4 is designed with the grind in mind. A story exists that offers enough insight into the setting and characters to make it worthwhile for some players, depending on their tastes, though its primary purpose is to unlock new, unchanging maps that can be used to provide steady grinding areas for gaining experience and mana. The Item World, on the other hand, is randomly generated madness where each completed map increases the stats of any item in your possession, whether you killed off all of the enemies or escaped through the portal. Yes, you will literally be diving into everything from household knives to demonic axes to pieces of cake. There’s an additional benefit here though, not only does it make the item itself more powerful, you will also have the opportunity to subdue residents. Residents are enemies within the item that grant it stat boosts beyond its predetermined state and they can be transferred freely between your items once they have been defeated. The value of this can’t be overstated as these residents can drastically improve how efficient a piece of equipment is.Disgaea 4 Complete+ is a far more entertaining game than its sales pitch would make you believe. It may be almost entirely devoted to the grind, but that grind has been distilled to an excellent experience that will keep you coming back for more. I highly recommend that any tactical RPG fan that gets a rush when their units level up or gain new abilities to give it a shot, I doubt you’ll be disappointed as long as you don’t mind or can get past the bizarre humor and heavy anime feel of it. Some of the humor tickled me the right way and the story was good enough to have me mildly interested in it, but the glorious grind kept me invested. Best of all, if you enjoy the grind that’s provided, you’ll have a title that you can play for many, many more hours than its peers.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this franchise may have peaked with Disgaea 2. I've wanted to play D2, since it's supposed to be a direct sequel to the first title, which was also pretty good, but I'm starting to suspect it's better left alone, if this and what I've played of 5 is anything to go by.4 starts off simple, if stupid, but not necessarily in a bad way. However, it never gets better. The entire game seems to be something of a commentary on government corruption, some of which is amusing in concept. There's propaganda, false flags, general incompetence, etc. Unfortunately, the oppressive air of irreverence plaguing the game, makes it impossible to appreciate in a genuine way. Humor has always been part of Disgaea, but this one didn't hit the mark.Furthermore, the story goes on for too long, ultimately becoming an incoherent mess, introducing aliens (a commentary on bureaucracy), and then finally "god" activating a self-destruct for planet Earth, which you have to fight off.I wasn't able to care about any of the new characters. It was very disappointing. I didn't even like  Flonne's appearance.The gameplay isn't very good either, in my opinion. It doesn't stray from the general system of the first two games, but it does over-complicate things for no reason. You no longer learn weapon skills, but have to purchase them from an NPC using mana. In my experience, it has locked me out of setting characters up the way I want to, because skills for weapons the character is not proficient in have simply never shown up for me. _childDocuments_.review: Sardine and pilchard are common names for various species of small, oily forage fish in the herring suborder Clupeoidei. The term 'sardine' was first used in English during the early 15th century; a somewhat dubious etymology says it comes from the Italian island of Sardinia, around which sardines were once supposedly abundant.The terms 'sardine' and 'pilchard' are not precise, and what is meant depends on the region. The United Kingdom's Sea Fish Industry Authority, for example, classifies sardines as young pilchards. One criterion suggests fish shorter in length than 15 cm (6 in) are sardines, and larger fish are pilchards.The FAO/WHO Codex standard for canned sardines cites 21 species that may be classed as sardines. FishBase, a database of information about fish, calls at least six species pilchards, over a dozen just sardines, and many more with the two basic names qualified by various adjectives.EtymologyThe word 'sardine' first appeared in English in the 15th century, a loanword from French sardine, derived from Latin sardina, from Ancient Greek σαρδίνη (sardínē) or σαρδῖνος (sardĩnos), possibly from the Greek Σαρδώ (Sardō) 'Sardinia'. Athenaios quotes a fragmentary passage from Aristotle mentioning the fish σαρδῖνος (sardĩnos), referring to the sardine or pilchard. However, Sardinia is over 1000 km from Athens, so it seems "hardly probable that the Greeks would have obtained fish from so far as Sardinia at a time relatively so early as that of Aristotle."The flesh of some sardines or pilchards is a reddish-brown colour similar to some varieties of red sardonyx or sardine stone; this word derives from σαρδῖον (sardĩon) with a root meaning 'red' and possibly cognate with Sardis, the capital of ancient Lydia (now western Turkey) where it was obtained. However, the name may refer to the reddish-pink colour of the gemstone sard (or carnelian) known to the ancients.The phrase "packed like sardines" (in a tin) is recorded from 1911. The phrase "packed up like sardines" appears in The Mirror of Literature, Amusement, and Instruction from 1841, and is a translation of "encaissés comme des sardines", which appears in La Femme, le mari, et l'amant from 1829. Other early appearances of the idiom are "packed together ... like sardines in a tin-box" (1845), and "packed ... like sardines in a can" (1854).

_childDocuments_.review: + Fun, in-depth tactical gameplay+ Nearly infinite customization possibilities+ Tons of content to play through+ Solid PC port- Tedious equipment management- Annoying geo block mechanic- Subpar storyline- MicrotransactionsNearly a year after its initial release on PlayStation 4 and Nintendo Switch, Disgaea 4 Complete+ has now finally made its way over to PC, on Steam and Game Pass at that. It takes all previous Disgaea 4 releases and combines everything into one nice little package, perfect for those that never got the opportunity to play it beforehand, myself included.Although not quite as good as Disgaea 5, Disgaea 4 Complete+ is still a solid game and worth a look for fans of the series. _childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: I received this product for no cost for the purpose of reviewing. However, this does not affect my views and opinions of the game.Disgaea 4 Complete+ is a turn-based tactics strategy RPG; with very heavy item and character management elements. The mechanics are very deep with plenty to do. The game follows a fallen tyrant vampire named Valvatorez and the insane adventures that follow. Despite this, It almost feels like the game is about becoming as powerful as you possibly can and doing as much as you can to make the best version of your characters/items.--------The game's graphic style hasn't really changed through the previous iterations of the game, and for good reason, it works, and looks pretty damn good. Not only are the anime-style sequences good; the character design, quality of art assets, and animations are well done. The actual game-play pixel-style graphics are also well done, albeit can feel a little crowded at times. The special skills, combos and effects are stunning and there are just so many characters, maps, backgrounds and over all designs to see and choose from. --------There are so many sound effects within the game. They all sound pretty good, even when some of them don't really make much sense in certain situations. The music is good and also very well done. The biggest strength when it comes to the game's audio; is that the game is almost fully voiced in English and Japanese, with the voice actors doing a wonderful job.  --------There are so many mechanics involved in this title, it is very hard to pick a place to begin. There are classic turn-based tactics in which commands can be executed before ending your turn. There are combo attacks, team-attacks, and even attacks involving stacking teammates on top of each other, as well as throwing teammates. Teammates can become weapons for your other characters, and even fuse with each-other mid-battle, there are just so many ways to fight. There is a very deep item system where items can level up, obtain abilities, move abilities to different items, and even play an endless dungeon based on the item selected, in order to level up the item further. Characters have abilities that can be purchased or unlocked, and characters can also be reincarnated for added benefits. A party can consist of different classes and races that can be captured or recruited. Each race has unique abilities. There is so much to do, so much to grind, and so much elements of this game to get lost in. It is a huge time sink, and although that may be it's biggest strength, it's also one of it's weaknesses (although not a very big one). There is no way to explain everything in-depth in a short review like this, but it really has a lot to offer.  --------Thanks to the developer for giving me the opportunity to review the title, as well as anyone who took this review into consideration, I hope it helped.
