_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a Disgaea game.  That sounds like simply stating the obvious but most of the core elements are here - levelling up your characters, reincarnation, monster classes, item world to grind - there's even consistency in a lot of item names.  It's also a Disgaea game in that there's a mix of crazy characters and crazy plot with occasionally some more genuine feeling.  Some major caveats: -  1)  Disgaea has always played fast and loose with Christian mythos but here it flirts with outright blasphemy.  Four centuries ago mere possession of this game would have led to your death in most of Europe and probably a few Islamic countries today.  Not for the devout.  2)  Most of the attack animations are exciting or funny but one of the gun animations has the graphic violence of a Sniper Elite or Mortal Kombat.  3)  Probably because I used English voiceovers the game felt far more sweary than usual - nothing very top end but many characters' legitimacy is questioned.  For long time Disgaea players (if you've never played the series before get 1 and 2 first [see my reviews]) the key changes are: -  1)  Movement can only be extended if characters then travel only in a straight line - useless on most maps.  Thus Skulls and Armour Knights remain ridiculously slow throughout the game.  2)  Upgrades to abilities have to be bought using mana but upgrades also increase SP cost.  For skulls in particular who do increased damage but for much higher SP costs any upgrade must be carefully considered.  Unlike Disgaea 5 where use of the skill rapidly brought down the points costs Disgaea 4 either does it slowly or not at all.  3)  You can't "learn" other characters' abilities.  This meant I kept my medic bow armed and far weaker as a medic throughout and choosing wand for the Shamen makes them virtually unpromotable.  But this is a fun game.  The characters are fun and the interplay between them is amusing unlike Disgaea 5's more dour and simplistic revenge story.  In Disgaea 1 a real tragedy was resolved with genuine sensitivity.  In Disgaea 4 an even bleaker tragedy isn't dealt with as effectively.  Generally item world grinding isn't essential until the final chapter (10) but I made it a policy not to equip a silver or gold item unless it had been through item world once giving the lucky recipient a hefty boost.  This meant that the back end of the game was far easier but in the Disgaea tradition the final battle is a doozy - I beat it first attempt but suffered significant casualties.  I relied heavily on my two lead characters, my first three freebie followers, my completing blue and green skulls, and one story character who looks, and originally sounds, like a wuss but by the end of the game was seriously living up to his name, as well as my gun man and thief - who never stole once  but whose gun skills were very good.  The game offers you a chance at promotion rather than reincarnation but this comes with significant expense in mana and a significant loss in bonus points.  Reincarnate and grind the opening levels to get the characters back up to level 20 and then use coups de grace and experience bonuses in item world to get them back towards full strength.  The characters I reincarnated three or four times became real toughies.  If you like Disgaea you'll like Disgaea 4 and it's best taken in sequence rather than as I did come back from 5 (which released earlier on PC).  Item world has shrunk which makes it more time manageable but the secret rooms are nowhere near as good as they are in 5.  If you like crazy chess like battle games you'll love this game and bought on sale you'll definitely get your money's worth before abandoning it.S.x.PS.  And this is a post script.  It's about the 100+ hours I've put into Disgaea 4 since completing the story.  Minor spoilers for the main game and very minor spoilers for the after game.  So there is narrative afterwards.  The biggest downturn is this.  There's an entire armada of DLC characters to unlock at the end game.  This goes old school where you have to beat a level 100 character to recruit them to your team.  Since by the end of the playthrough my best characters were level 100 plus and the battles are 10 - 1 in your favour this is a walk in the park.  It's tougher and better in Disgaea 5.  The major downer is that in one of my two post game escapades I'd recruited every monster class available which means with half the DLC characters still unlocked I've run out of space for them.  Bad planning by the devs.   There's such a lot of duplication.  Fenrich is a fist based hard case which means my fist based super hero, my fist based bouncer, Axell, and Adell all effectively duplicate his role.  Go guns for self generated characters you say - but my thief, my gunman, Artina, and Rozalin all use guns.  As well as my Professor.  Bows ?  My healer, my archer, my Beast tamer.  You get the point.  There's two main post game stories.  One involves starting a new game led by story characters who were minor on my roster and losing my big three characters.  This was a huge wrench because my killing power went back to my fighter and my three skulls - a major loss.  About the fourth level in there's an utterly murderous encounter with a character you've met before which was just unwinnable with my team.  The second involves a trip to the past and effectively removes all story characters save one.  This is manageable up to the end two levels which place you on an extremely unfavourable map and on the final level against a boss that does 36,000+ damage.  Bearing in mind at this time Valvatorez (not usable) had 13K hit points and my strongest others (Fenrich and my warrior) roughly 10k this wasn't a match I could win.  There's also the Mount of Ordeals which requires 7000 mana, using all your mobile phones, and item and money bribes to open.  First level is okay but second level involves taking on wizards on super high inaccessible squares with hefty bonuses.  Couldn't be bothered working it out.  So I've spent most time grinding silver and gold equipment to get better equipment and higher stats.  This has suited me ATM, but it's not everyone's bag.  I've enjoyed post game better than D5 anyway.

It took me quite a long time over 10 hours just to get about 25 percent done the game. I could of disabled the cheat shop but i read it's a part of the disgaea games and even without the cheat shop you can still grind over and over again to get to whatever level you need to defeat whatever level you are stuck at. A tedious process that the cheat shop does shorten the grind but difficulty feels off as result. Great retro sprites and art but they look only like 720 or 1080p remastered and they didn't look good in 4k almost as if they put a quick hd upscale filter on it, not a true remaster and lazy re-release. I didn't experience any crashing with steam deck or pc but i did encounter buggy issues with setting the resolution beyond 720p for 4k on pc and had to toggle back and forth repeatedly for no reason the full screen or borderlesss option back and forth multiple times before it would let me change the resolution. Online features also had trouble connecting and were slow and barely worked or not at all. Overall there are some interesting ideas and systems with senate hearing to recruit new members, an evolution of the final fantasy tactics formula. Despite the great presentation, I wished they kept the gameplay mechanics balanced and saved the grind for the post game as it ruins the campaign experience. Overall not a bad game for the time but has not aged well, and the newer games never evolved much past this and disgaea 5, for me to be interested disgaea 7, they would need an open world like divinity orignal sin or baldur's gate 3  with a more modern open world design and switch to turn based for the battles, and keep enemies dead after you kill them. I think an open world disgaea would be amazing, sadly they just don't have the budget and are more keen to just repeating the same formula over and over again only satisfying the dedicated few from the past. A slog of a game with a steep learning curve and very little pay off no sense of accomplishment when all you have to do is grind to beat the game and you can't avoid the grind because it's integrated into the core game system and leveling design. Overall 4/10

_childDocuments_.review: Title: The Searing Symphony of Strategy: Disgaea 4 Complete+ Bared by a Tormented Bear"In the heart of my ruffled existence, in the midst of the tempest of depression and anxiety, I, a bear of former majesty, find an uncanny refuge within the labyrinthine folds of Disgaea 4 Complete+. It stands as an enigma, its essence imbued with a familiarity that sends shivers down my spine - a mirror reflecting the disarray that my life has descended into, due to a merciless divorce and a disgraceful addiction to shoe cleaner.Disgaea 4 Complete+, at its core, is a cruel ballet of strategy and charm, akin to the agonizing dance of love and loss I was ensnared in with her - my estranged wife. Each battle, a complex tapestry of tactics, echoes the internal strife that gnaws at my soul daily. The promise of transformation held by the leveling system is a stark reminder of my own metamorphosis - from a bear of dignity and might to a creature ensnared by anger and addiction.Yet, the cruel twist of fate does not end there. From the corners of my life's stage, a new character emerges in her life, a bear of formidable presence and intimidating endowment. His prowess, a stark contrast to my own diminished state, serves as a painful reminder of what I've lost, of the gaping void that has replaced my place in her life.However, in spite of the torment, Disgaea 4 Complete+ truly excels in its narrative. A tale woven with humor, sentiment, and unexpected twists, it is a haunting reflection of my past life. The graphics and soundtrack, beautifully crafted, manage to capture a fleeting glimpse of the beauty that once graced my existence. Thus, despite my resentment, I find myself begrudgingly commending Disgaea 4 Complete+ for its strategic gameplay and captivating storytelling, as it serves as a stark memento of what I once was, and what I have painfully lost."

_childDocuments_.review: Online is here.The gap between 5 and 4 is pretty large so some of the newer changes from 5 are not there but it has classes not found in 5. If you like obsessing over the perfect setup, this game has another level of it with evil symbols. It's like the gun system in end of eternity. The story of this game is semi serious comedy, like the other games prior to this one. In the middle chapters, the game frequently repeats itself which might be an issue for people but it eventually stops. Might be irritating if rushing through the story but is helpful for people playing the game when the mood strikes them. The systems particular to -this- game are centered a political theme (as of 2011) and there are obscure references to politics when recruiting a character which I did not all get. You set your characters on a grid and assign them to "buildings" which give special abilities and affects surrounding character's stats. You can also set characters in political posts which affect their stat growth and Those characters will show up online in other's people's games to help or hinder.. There are a ton of systems in disgaea and going through every system is more suited for a guide but the one you immediately need to know if you are new to the series is that leveling up certain generics unlocks more generics and that your stat growth are influenced by your -base- stats. The difference over 9999 levels in putting 1 point in atk when creating a character versus 3 points is pretty big in the end. The game rewards you for trying different things with unlocks as well. It might feel a little jarring in the beginning to lose QOL functions from 5 but if you've played other games in the series you'll be fine. I think it's definitely fun and I am looking forward to the online functions when they come. Please check out Japanese games on steam for more Japanese games on pc.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR, it's a really solid port of Disgaea 4: A Promise Unforgotten for the PS3 and a good place to start for newcomers to the series.    The textures and artwork are cleaned up a bit, and it supports mouse input, but I've always found it a bit fussy.  If the Disgaea 1 frustrated you with its PS2 port jankiness, this is a decent place to start.  The stories aren't connected, so you won't be lost for what's going on.  On the flip side, this one has a fun but goofy story you'll enjoy. All the main characters are charming, and the English voice acting is surprisingly good; Nippon Ichi has always been good about that.  When it comes to gameplay, it's superior to all of the entries before it, though if you've played 5, you'll miss out on a few of its quality of life features. The tutorial walks new players through how the game works with the understanding that you've never played a Disgaea game before, but you can also largely skip through it if you know what you're doing.  Menus are snappy and easy to navigate, and there are lots of fun little mechanics to mess around with in-game.    All in all, it's a great game and I'm glad I picked up a copy and I totally recommend it to anyone that likes strategy RPGs, or even if you don't, it's not a bad one to start with.

If you want you can just play through the main story and end it there if you dont feel like putting in a ton of time into it, which will run you about 30 hours to finish the main story but after you do that, then the real game opens up in post.You get a ton of things to do plus you have multiple endings to the game so you can run through it again.After you finish the game you have tons of extra characters to unlock, the chara world, The land of carnage, The ♥♥♥♥ and Desco show, Fenrichs back story, Reverse pirating, some insane high level boss fights, and more to do. As far as Disgaea games go and Ive played them all this one would be my second favorite in the series.I like Valvatorez as the Main character he amuses me and can be funnyThe story is decent though Disgaea games have never had great stories but they have always been decent. They do how ever do a really good job on the characters and I enjoy the Voice acting as well. As far as the bad, not much to complain  my 60+ hours I havent had any crashes I have noticed in a few parts for what ever reason they use a different voice actor for Valvatorez, I dont know what thats about and in combat as well.The game will freeze every so often for about 2 seconds and resume again this normally would be more of a issue in a lot of games but since Disgaea is a turn based game it wont effect you outside of maybe annoying you a bit.and i did have one issue where my save got corrupt and the game would crash when i tried to load my game but thankfully this game has autosave and i didnt lose more then a few minutes. other then that really love the game.worth picking up if you like stratagy RPG'sNow hopefully they Bring Disgaea 3 and D2 to PC next.

_childDocuments_.review: I have played all of the Disgaea games. Most of them I beat the main story and grind another 1 or 200 levels then get bored. I played this one on PSP Vita and made it to level 4000. The PC port is so far great! Much better than the Disgaea 1 port and has most of the QOL improvements from Disgaea 5.Edit: I remember why I made it so far with this one. I absolutely hate the whole mana being used to purchase skills and level them up that has been with the series since Disgaea 3. However, if we have to suffer this system Disgaea 4 is probably the best version of it. I don't remember how it was in Disgaea 3 but in Disgaea 5 it takes 80 mana to hit 2 people with a fire spell and also 80 mana to hit 2 people with a giga fire spell. When your whole team is level 10 getting 80 mana takes forever and by the time you do get it you have already unlocked the next tier. With Disgaea 4 it scales like it should have in 5. So low tier spells are cheaper. As an added bonus it increases power as well so its just a 1 time purchase of mana and you get boosted power and range. I like the evil symbol system better than the squad system in 5 because people can be placed in multiple groups at the same time. Magic Change is very powerful in this game. In Disgaea 5 you get a ridiculously small boost to stats and only 3 turns to use it. In Disgaea 5 you get a pretty large boost to stats and 5 turns which makes the whole reincarnation process 20 times easier.You don't have to fight stuff in the item world to level up your gear. A popular strategy is making a flying runner equipped with 3 pairs of boots and just skipping levels all together which is great when you are level 50 and go into a level 2 item or just really don't want to grind out them levels. The geo system is way better in my opinion but I think they use it way to much in this game. I'll just leave it at that for now I could probably ramble on about another 10 reasons why this game is better than the rest but its definitely worth the money to check it out if you are a fan of Disgaea games.

name: AeternoBlade
detailed_description: AeternoBlade is a hack-and-slash fast-paced action game featuring with World Exploration, RPG elements, Time-manipulation abilities to solve puzzles and to defeat your foes. Long ago, when the world was ruled by darkness. Alwesia region, a cruel continent where humans must fight and struggle in order to survive, stood Beladim, Lord of the Mist, Commander of the Army of Darkness. It has been said that Beladim cannot be killed by any means. Those who oppose and challenge this immortal all become a feast for him and his heartless army. He has razed and destroyed everything he set foot upon. Freyja, the girl who had her village, Ridgerode destroyed, travels with an unknown weapon called the 'AeternoBlade'. Freyja looks to take revenge on Beladim. Her vengeance is aided by Vernia, a mysterious witch. Vernia taught Freya about the potential of the AeternoBlade. Freyja obtained the true power of the AeternoBlade with the advice of 'Bernard', the man who had been imprisoned in the Everlasting Void. With that, she can travel back in time before Beladim destroyed her village to save it and have her vengeance once and for all. aeternoblade Of Past's Ability Time Travel: Everything except Freyja will be played back. Some green flashing objects called timeless objects, however, cannot be played back by this ability. Time Warp: Place the marker at Freyja's current position, After that, when pressing the button again Freya will be warped back to the marker to solve the puzzles and avoid the attack in battle. Time Reverse: Everything Played Back If You Die. status Upgrade This is the most basic upgrade for Freyja. In exchange for yellow orbs, the player can enhance Freyja's basic stat. They can upgrade her Health, Mana, Attack damage or increase her Mind (which increased the speed her ultimate gauge fill up). upgrade and Relics On her epic adventure, Freyja will encounter powerful enemies, each one stronger than the one before. In order to defeat them, Freyja too must become stronger. We will explain how the upgrade systems work in AeternoBlade. master Your Art! the Move Set A power’s hidden deep within all of us. We only have to unlock it with yellow orbs! Freyja can upgrade her basic attack into a more deadly attack. Each move can be upgraded twice until it was maxing out. Each upgraded move will not only provide more damaging attack but it opens an alternate option to an extended combo that wasn’t available before. Power From the past! the Relic The items which can be installed into Freyja’s AeternoBlade to enhance her abilities. You collect relics from hidden places or from enemies. You also use Upgrade Relic to improve the ability of the Relic you are installed in the AeternoBlade. Continue to the new journey in AeternoBlade II: Director's Rewind

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say? I didn't expect to get that much invested in AeternoBlade. To be fair, I'm not much into console games so I naturally never heard of this game before — Well until it hit Steam. Although AeternoBlade is a few years old and got released back in 2014, I'm glad it made the jump to PC, and I cannot imagine what hidden gem I would have missed if I didn't get the chance to play it. Anyway, despite usually not being into Metroidvania games, I just felt like AeternoBlade was a special game, at first glance, which turned out to be quite accurate in the end.AeternoBlade revolves around a girl called Freyja whose village, Ridgerode, got destroyed by the Lord of the Mist, Beladim. You see, the world is ruled by darkness and humans struggle to survive. Anyway, driven by anger, Freyja decides to take revenge on Beladim. The only problem here is that Beladim cannot be killed. However, when Freyja meets Vernia, a mysterious witch, she teaches her about the abilities of her AeternoBlade which can manipulate the time and is the key to destroying Beladim. Vernia seems oddly cooperative, but hey, any ally against the fight of Beladim is convenient.First of all, let's start with the plot. In all honesty, I didn't expect a lot of this game when it comes to the storyline as Freyja's only goal is to defeat Beladim. However, after defeating a couple of bosses it turns out there is more to the story than I anticipated at first. Twists and turns I didn't see coming were getting introduced and I was impressed at the reveals. I even felt like a fool for not noticing the hints the game throws its player in between that this tale is much more than just a simple revenge one.However, the story takes its time to pick up in AeternoBlade. Most of the time the player only fights their way through multiple stages with short cutscenes in between that might have a greater meaning later on. Anyway, AeternoBlade reveals its colors in the last part of the game but feels like a generic JRPG at first. Regardless, it's worth it to go through AeternoBlade just for the story. As a piece of side information, the story is linear and there is only one possible end the player can reach.While the first stage is not very challenging, AeternoBlade gets harder with each stage. I needed a few tries to be able to defeat a boss, although it took a while at times. Although there is no difficulty setting available per se, the player has the option to set the difficulty lower for bosses they didn't manage to defeat after the fourth try. However, it's important to mention that this only applies to the final bosses of each stage and normal enemies or bosses that appear in the middle of a stage are not affected at all. That setting is entirely optional, yet, I found it a shame that it was only present for the very last bosses.Gameplay-wise, AeternoBlade works like a typical sidescroller hack and slash. Throughout the playthrough, Freyja gains new abilities which will help her reach new places. In total, there are seven stages available the player can explore, and whilst it's not mandatory to investigate every corner of each stage for the main story, there are still hidden relicts that give Freyja passive advantages such as increasing the maximum health bar.Sometimes, the relicts are not that easy to reach as they are hidden in secret rooms. To have access to the rooms, the player has to solve puzzles as well. However, they're not regular puzzles but the player has to work with the abilities of the AeternoBlade to reach their goal. Nonetheless, these skills are very helpful even during the battles.So, let's move to the special features of the AeternoBlade. As aforementioned, the player can manipulate the time with it, although they cannot go back for more than ten seconds. In addition to that, there is a mana bar that indicates for how long the player can use the time-manipulation skills. Anyway, the useful thing is that only the environment gets manipulated but Freyja herself is not affected. In that sense, she can foresee attacks from the enemies and go back in time to avoid them. Plus, it can save the player from death too in a few cases or help them with advancing while solving puzzles.Another feature is that the player can teleport to any place they previously marked. This feature is mandatory for a few puzzles and special attacks of certain bosses. I loved the variety of skills and combos in AeternoBlade and when reaching a checkpoint, the player can upgrade their stats as well as unlock or upgrade combo attacks. The required currency for that can be obtained after defeating enemies.The mana gets slowly filled when Freyja is not using the AeternoBlade's abilities, although it's possible for enemies to drop mana or health as well. In addition to that, when reaching a checkpoint, the player doesn't only have the opportunity to save their game but the health and mana also get fully recharged. There is also a green bar available, that gets filled up with each successful attack. When it's full, Freyja can launch a powerful meteor attack. However, the green bar doesn't get recharged when reaching a checkpoint.Well, graphic-wise it's evident that AeternoBlade is not a newly released game. However, I still found the graphics decent, and especially the design of the bosses was well-done, although there was a good variety of enemies available as well. Of course, the enemies are getting reused quite often here, however, it didn't bother me a lot. Sadly, the characters are lacking any emotional expressions during the cutscenes which made them feel less lively to me. Anyway, when launching the game the player can decide between the old sprites or anime ones, which I found was a nice touch. Although the old sprites match the style of the cutscenes, I still preferred the anime ones much more.AeternoBlade offers such refreshing gameplay with unique abilities. It was a joy for me to go through each stage, although I have to admit that I struggled at one or another boss as the game is quite hard. Luckily, I managed to get the gist of the boss' mechanics and could beat them after a few retries, however, the option to lower the difficulty helped me a lot. Anyway, the thing that truly shines here is the storytelling and I was utterly surprised at the plot twists. AeternoBlade is a hidden gem and implements such a well-executed plot and fun gameplay… So, do you even need more reasons to give this game a try?

_childDocuments_.review: AeternoBlade is an enjoyable mashup of both classic and modern Castlevania, with some Megaman X throw in for good measure. And also puzzles that involve turning back time, and teleportation!Our heroine, Freyja sets out to seek revenge on the baddie that burned her village, and along the way she meets people that help her out. The plot eventually diverges in a way I didn't expect, and while it's nothing groundbreaking, it did surprise me and it's enjoyable, if a little campy.The game focuses more on combat than your regular metroidvanias. At first the combat starts off slow and button mash-y, with only a single combo available to you. This tends to make most players stick to this one combo, even most professional reviews did not try to explore their other options.As you finish stages, more moves become available to purchase. Your up attack is great against single foes and lifts enemies off the ground, your forward attacks are good for a high combo count, and your down attacks deal high damage. You also gain the ability to do a charged attack late in the game, and this is an addition that makes the game a lot more fun. Unfortunately you get this ability very late, and at first it appears weak and useless. It only becomes useful when you can charge it multiple levels. The game does a really bad job of teaching you to try out your moves. Locking this and many other abilities away from the player for so long is one of its bigger flaws.Some of your movement upgrades are also locked away to equip-able relics, making you waste valuable equipment slots just to be able to jump a little higher or for the ability to break open walls. The game does have passive upgrades like the double jump, so I'm not sure why these aren't used this way. These equipment slots can grant you lots of useful enhancements like added explosion effects, reduced mana costs, or self-healing. It's disappointing to always have some slots lost to mandatory movement options.While you find most of these relics in the open, some are dropped by enemies. The drops have a fairly low chance, if you're collecting them it can be a pain. You do get an item that increases drop chance, but only at the very end of the game. Most of these will be useless by then, barring the few exceptionally good ones.Another issue is that you need to beat the game twice to unlock every area, with your second time offering some different enemies along the way, and a very slightly different story, along with one expanded stage. But the rest of the stages, puzzles, and platforming just stay the same. Luckily you can get to the expanded area very quickly, and can simply choose to ignore the rest of the 2nd playthrough. Not if you want full completion though.The game is also prone to freeze, so save often! Mostly when enemies spawn or when going to a new area. Had several freezes and lost game time, but the PC version is still more stable than the PS4 release. PS4 freezed on me once an hour, PC version freezed 5 times total in 28 hours.Controller input is also slightly broken in the PC version, you cannot charge your attack and jump at the same time, because for some strange reason the Xbox A and Playstation X confirm buttons - which normally functions as the jump button - will always make you do an attack while the attack button is held down. This is not intentional, and can be fixed by changing the jump button to any other one, but it's quite annoying. Console and 3DS versions don't have this issue....so with all these flaws, why do I still recommend the game? Because despite these setbacks ! The low poly art is pleasing, the music is banger, the combat is very fun once you have all your moves, and the relics add a ton of customization and build options.Want to constantly freeze time and become immune to damage? You can do it!Want to teleport around while creating explosions everywhere? That's also possible!Want the charge attack to charge instantly and deal massive amounts of damage? Yep, that's a good one!The puzzles range from brain dead simple to mind bending. Most of the harder ones being locked to the extra area at the 2nd run. Most of them have many ways to solve them, always felt like I'm not doing them the "intended" way, relic customization allows you to be creative!The game took me nearly 28 hours to fully complete, it's a long adventure. If you can look past its flaws, it's definitely one I'd recommend, especially at the low sale price it goes for quite often.It has a ton of charm and you can really tell the developers poured their heart and soul into it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not give off a great first impression, but it's actually a bit more complex and interesting than it at first may seem, both thematically and in terms of game play. I can see how this could be considered a niche title, since it's only somewhat a Metroidvania, and more of an action puzzle game. Basically, you play as a girl who can alter time with her constantly upgrading sword. This game makes a lot more sense if you consider the fact that was originally a DS game, which explains the overly simplistic combat and emphasis on completing each area section by section. Essentially, her town is burned down by a generic devil-looking villain and she has to seek revenge. That's pretty much it... or is it? The first playthrough of the game takes only about seven hours, as among the seven stages only about three of them take more than an hour to complete. The combat in this game is very simplistic. You can do sword swings and she has one Final Fantasy-style meteor attack. But there is a little bit more to it, at least in terms of tweaking your character. You collect yellow orbs that you can use to power her up like in Devil May Cry, and even though she doesn't level up, you have a lot of options on how to set your character's stats. First off, you can use the orbs to by stat points. You can upgrade her sword swings, but this doesn't really matter that much since the game is so easy that you don't really need to both with any specialized attacks. The relics are the best part of the combat. These can dramatically alter the game play , as you find these on the map and equip the ones you prefer. There's like 75 unique relics, and you can equip three at a time. By the end of the game I had tweaked it to where my character was almost invincible, as one relic was draining her health but another was allowing her to heal whenever she used the time altering ability. The relics are the best part of the combat and I'm glad they're in there because otherwise just mindlessly hacking away at enemies would get boring quick.Then there's the puzzles. See, in this game you can reverse time, which is both game-breaking, at times hilarious, and mostly just a novelty that never really gets repetitive but never really gets very exciting either. For example, if you jump on a platform as it's moving toward you and reverse time, it will start moving in the other direction. You can also warp by placing an icon on the map. So, for example, if you see a switch you need to jump to that's over a pit of spikes you can set a warp point, jump and hit the switch, and warp to it at any time. It's simple and intuitive, yet I got stuck so many times not realizing I could just warp through a wall as it was moving past me or something to that effect. The puzzles in this game are great, they aren't hard by any means, the only difficult one is totally optional, but if you compare this to a game like Metroid or Castlevania, there's no comparison. The puzzles are just more complicated and interesting than breaking a suspicious looking wall for the 100th time, but they aren't something where you get instant satisfaction, so I can see how people would like this game less because of that.The other really, really bad thing about this game is the repetition in the combat. The boss fights are cool, not too complex but when you consider this was a DS game they work fine. There's this huge plant with a human skull that looks so cool the first time you fight it, but gets extremely irritating the tenth time you fight it, especially since it's the exact same battle and you're just hacking away at it. It's funny that you can reverse and set time in motion while hacking away at enemies, it almost feels like the whole game is cheating, but you have a mana bar that drains so there is some limitation on this. Certain enemies and items will blink green, indicating that they are invulnerable to time manipulation.Where I really came to like this game was in how much extra content is stuffed in by the time you reach the last level. The final level is a fairly large labyrinth of a castle with about 100 rooms. On top of this, another level in the game, the void is only half explored. Once you beat the game, depending on if you got a certain item earlier on, you can continue, otherwise you are set back at the beginning because the game is an endless time loop in purgatory. This is where the game really gets interesting and surreal, as you get about an extra ten hours of game play completing this 100%. The more complex and interesting areas of the game are in the New Game+, along with some new enemy types and reskinned bosses. It's really weird, since probably only about 5% of players would even play to this point, and since this game isn't that popular, it feels more surreal seeing all this extra content stuffed in a game that no one else is playing.And there are some twists in the story, which, while simplistic and cliched, is honestly kind of cool. The music is also seriously mixed, with some excellent tunes, like this one rock track that sounds like a Buckethead guitar solo, and then some other horrible electronic songs. If you can get past the graphics, I think this game is probably an underrated gem, something that you can't really appreciate unless you play it all the way through.

_childDocuments_.review: is an action platformer. Half of the game is fighting, the other half solving small, sometimes heavily skill-based puzzles.You take the role of Freyja, who is the sole survivor of a devastating attack from Beladim, the lord of the mist. Swearing revenge for his terrible deed, she sets out on a journey to bring him to justice.The game is divided into stages, represented by medium-sized maps consisting of smaller and bigger rooms. If you explore each of the areas thoroughly, you can acquire different items, such as relics, to strengthen your character, though you won't be able to get to all places at the beginning of the game. It is therefore worthwhile to come back to previous stages and look what you can uncover with new abilities which you gain during the course of the game (e.g. double jump to reach higher places). At the end of each stage, you'll have to fight a boss before you can move on to the next. The unique selling point of the game is the various time manipulation abilities, which are needed to mainly progress at the aforementioned puzzles or get an edge in battle. You’ll gain access to more of them as you progress.I very much enjoyed the so-called "Memorandum", which offers additional information about the characters, enemies and items and aids world building. It is also cool to try out different relic setups and develop your own strategies as well as play styles.  Unfortunately, the developers didn't consider it necessary to indicate connections to other rooms on the map. This makes it much more difficult to fully explore the area, since you are forced to comb the whole stage again for new routes. Additionally, I sometimes have the feeling that my attacks don’t connect with the enemy when they definitely should. Falling down a pit or taking unnecessary hits are frequent results of this and can lead to moments of frustration. Finally, I witnessed some errors (orthographical and grammatical) both in dialogues and GUI text. These don't make understanding the meaning outright impossible, but are nevertheless a minor nuisance. Overall, the game is nothing groundbreaking, but nonetheless fun and entertaining. As long as you approach  with moderate expectations, you ought to be satisfied. Wait for a sale if you are unsure.

name: Ad Infinitum
detailed_description: Trapped between the walls of your family home and the trenches of World War I, you try to piece together your past and take back control of your life. BREAK THE CYCLE Will the nightmare of the war ever end? Will you find inner peace one day? In Ad Infinitum, you play as a German soldier haunted by the horrors of the Great War. While your mind grapples with memories of your family home and the trenches on the front, you try to break the endless cycle of suffering. BETWEEN A DREAM AND REALITY You wake up in your bedroom, unchanged from your teenage years, in a run-down and deserted manor house. Suddenly and inexplicably, you are transported to the trenches where the horrors of war are overshadowed by vile and even more terrifying creatures. Unable to distinguish between reality and nightmare, you must fight to regain control of your life's narrative. NIGHTMARES THAT BECOME REAL Unspeakable nightmares come to life in the recesses of your mind. To escape the death traps and terrifying creatures, you must understand the source and motivation of each monster and solve the puzzles that stand in your way. From blind demons who can hear your softest footsteps to hideous disjointed puppets who move in the dark, horror is around every corner. A FAMILY TORN APART The fallout of the war is felt far from the front. Peel back the shroud that hides the secrets of your family, torn apart by the Great War, and try to remember your past. Through exploration and by solving riddles and puzzles between the walls of your home and the barbed wire of No Man’s Land, you ultimately reveal a chapter in the story of a German family torn apart by war.

short_description: When reality is a nightmare, nightmares become real. In this psychological horror game, you fight the terrifying creatures invading your mind. Can you save your sanity?

_childDocuments_.review: I've waited for this since 2015, and it was worth it. Don't be going into this game thinking it's something like NecroVision, or even something like 1916: Der Unbekannte Krieg. Playing this is more like a hysterical psychosis from shell shock. The atmosphere is either cold or disgusting, while the characters are representations to ideology or trauma. If it's something you're looking for too, you actually play as a German. A German with a name and family. I feel like this game and Valiant Hearts: The Great War pay respectful tribute to the first World War in very different artistic ways. As a side note the developers really care about their creation here, it's like their baby. There was a man who works for them that kept me updated for issues I had involving my graphics card, which was obviously out of his hands.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: After 7 years of development, finally the boys at Hekate (Berlin) released Ad Infinitum. Well, it's very polished, no need of further patches after release, that's very appreciated and so rare nowadays. Graphics, sounds and animations are top notch. Interactions and mechanics could be better, but it's an indie production, so it's ok. Acting is quite good.You're adviced: it isn't an action game where you shoot and fight monsters, not at all! It is a pacifist game, against war and violence, so it's the negation of the usual war games. Sometimes they put a shotgun in your hands that apparently gives you more security but very soon you find that it's useless in front of the war horrors. A clear message from the developers.It's no survival horror, it isn't the usual horror game that makes you jump or scare; It's a psychological dark drama with horror nuances. At most it has something of Layers of Fear. When not competent reviewers cannot understand what they are playing, they use the term "walking simulator" that means nothing. It's an interactive experience like What Remains of Edith Finch, Firewatch, Gone Home, Dear Esther, The Town of Light and so onAd Infinitum puts you in the shoes of a veteran traumatized by the horrors of war and gives a glimpse on his problematic family. You experience in first person the nightmarish memories of a traumatized mind where the horrors of war mix with family drama. The game gives its best in depicting the tragedy of First World War: the inhuman fight in the trenches, the chemical weapons, the sufference of mutilated soldiers, the air alerts, the suicide missions, the insensitivity and narrow-mindedness of the commanders, etc. A senseless war supported by patriotic fanaticism and laughable sense of superiority of the German people, forerunner of Nazism.I appreciated the criticism of the ideology of the strong and heroic german man, without physical defects, tireless, ready to sacrifice himself for his country; an ideology leading to the contempt for those who are disabled, for other ethnic groups considered inferior.Not everything is good. Story is a bit disjointed, too many narrative elements that are hard to manage and blend, especially concerning the family drama. Too many documents as main narrative mechanic. Some puzzles are dissonant with storytelling. A few interactive mechanics can be frustrating. You can see some naivety,  it's the first work by talented but young developers, especially 7 years ago!Not at all a masterpiece as Edith Finch or Firewatch, however the experience does not leave you indifferent; some surreal representations of horrors of war are very effective, some scenes have the right atmosphere, they remain imprinted in your memory, they touch you deeply and make you think. You can see it's a work of passion; the young authors have something deep and meaningful to tell through the game experience. Don't miss their message, play Ad Infinitum; games are not just to have easy fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: A horror game that isn't scary for the majority of it's run, but has it's moments. The gameplay is boring, at the best of times, and tedious at the worst. But, it is a wonderful story telling experience that represents the trauma of war, and how it effects everyone differently, and it's beautiful. I hope no one who ever reads this has to go through the horrible experience of warfare. Or in their families.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This game has three endings, bad, neutral, and good.  If they are played through from bad>Neutral>good, the game is an incredible journey of feelings towards these characters that evolves over their course.  That said, you have to be willing to devote the time to three playthroughs.  So you need to be pretty tolerant of the gameplay which is that of a horror game, not a survival horror game.  This isn't Resident Evil.  It's not even Silent Hill.  It's a series of puzzles, stealth sections, and balls out runs to safety.  Come for the story and atmosphere or don't come at all.  An exploration of war, PTSD, masculinity, legacy and family that I have never seen so fully and completely explored in a game.  You're going to fu**ing cry.  Just let it happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I find it very odd there's no surround sound. Made some segments feel like a lesser experience than they could've been. In a game like this with a good atmosphere it's unfortunate. Overall as a complete package it's a decent indie horror title.My one huge problem with the game that I cannot ignore. Tinnitus. Devs (not just the devs of this game) you all need to stop. Seriously. There isn't a single person who enjoys tinnitus sound effects and I can tell you right now I have suffered with tinnitus every second of every day for over a year now it adds nothing to the game and only annoys the player. Thanks soldier!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: What can be said about Ad Infinitum?While certainly clunky and buggy on the gameplay side I'm not here to talk about this but rather its extraordinary atmosphere. Many games try to capture the sheer tragedy and senselessness of the First World War and this is probably what feels the closest to its dread and unpredictability, with the dirty, flooded trenches, agonizing men hanging from the barbed wire, the constant rain of bullets, letters that will never reach their destination, fanaticism, patriotism, responsibilities.Centred around a disastrous family you shall rebuild your own story and maybe even change your destiny, challenging yourself to see a life outside of the war and your ancestors' oppressive expectations.Can't wait to see what other stories the developers will deliver us!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game, but it got so painful I just ended up hating it. All boss battles are identical. Run, turn on a switch, run, turn on a switch. The game is beautiful graphics-wise, and the music was pretty. Everything else was just.. flat.Not worth the full price, unless you really like hide and seek/sneak/walking simulators that go on for hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This game should get an award for the most useless flashlight in a game.They focused on the story so much that they ignored everything else:You can sprint for about 20 meters before you need a 15 second break to catch your breath (aparently the protagonist smokes 10 packs a day).Every animation and dialogue is excruciatingly slow. The jumpscares are cheap (there is a pigeon jumpscare...) and almost always predictable .The QTEs are so unnecessary it feels like they were added just to annoy you and to "raise the stakes" (you can actually die from a wire if you fail a QTE.....).And for the worst part of the game.. whoever thought it was a clever idea to have a flashlight in the game, that takes 3 seconds to charge and lasts for 6 seconds (I am not exaggerating), really needs a medal. I can't tell what they where thinking, it's so frustrating to use I ended up maxing the display gamma just so I can see something.The story is ok.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Once again a game is falsely labeled as "Survival Horror" on Steam. Ad Infinitum is a linear, narrative driven horror game about the, well, horrors of the first world war. It's mostly a walking simulator with simple puzzles, that does provide a good atmosphere, as well as supernatural elements.Points of criticism are the following:- The game doesn't save its monitor resolution over a restart and returns to 1080p the next time- There's lots of "wtf do I go" type of walking around- The objective log doesn't update as often as it should, getting stuck on already accomplished tasksIf you want to check out some gameplay, or maybe watch the whole Let's Play, where I professionally ruin the atmosphere between heart attacks, look no further:
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Very good WW1 psychological horror game. Took me about 9 hours on a very slow and deliberate playthrough. There are three different endings depending on choices you make at critical points, so there is some built-in replayability (and a second playthrough would probably also help to more fully understand the story anyway).The story was very good if a bit confusing at times (what's going on, what's real, even who am I), but it works with the whole nightmare/trauma aspect of it. The actual gameplay is pretty linear with avoiding monsters and using a few tools (flashlight, gas mask, and bolt cutters) to overcome environmental obstacles. There are some minor puzzles to work through that aren't very difficult but still fit in to game relatively well. While there are a few jump-scares, the game is less scary and more psychological with gore and disturbing creatures, which I think lent well to the sobering WW1 theme. The best part of the game was just the overall atmosphere of the trenches, the old German manor, and the history.All in all, I'll rate it 8/10, a solidly good game. $35 might be a tad steep with the relatively short length of the game, but the sale price of $14 seems well worth it for the love the developers poured into it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: A masterful piece of storytelling that delves deep into the murky waters of PTSD, the unquenchable thirst of power and the uncompromising expectations of following in your families footsteps. Set around the events of the first world war, the story focuses on a German brother who has returned from war in a mind that is different to the one he left with. As he walks through the halls of his family home, it becomes clear that the things that he is seeing aren't necessarily what he should be seeing. Initially presumed dead during combat, the story unravels events that detail his life both before and during his military service as well as the fate of his other family members namely his brother, father and grandfather. His mother is wracked with melancholy and whilst you never see her, you hear her distorted cries in various parts of the mansion, almost as if she is in the room with you and yet your psyche just cannot manifest or process the image. As the protagonists grasp of reality becomes less certain, you begin to experience flashbacks to the trenches and no man's land of Flanders Field. Again, these memories present themselves as real as possible at first but slowly become more and more twisted as you progress through the story and you have to face twisted nightmarish manifestations that reflect the emotional state of the protagonist as they stalk you through the nightmarish hellscape that he has conjured. The emotions and feelings covered are hunger, rage, mayhem, despair, corruption and pain. Much of the storytelling is done through reading letters that you find on your journey, and occasionally you will get some narration after interacting with an object as your character remembers a specific situation. There are a number of puzzles throughout the game too, though nothing too taxing. It is usually the standard work out a code for this door, reroute power to this gate or mix these chemicals type of thing. There are three endings that you can obtain during play, though I have currently only seen one but it has left me with a desire to see the other endings too. Graphically the game is beautiful and I managed to play it on epic quality with no issues on a PC that is almost 10 years old at this point.  I have seen some people comment on discussions and other reviews about the flashlight/torch being useless and yet personally I liked the fact that they opted to use a technology that was actually used during the Great War. the flashlight is a kinetic one that requires winding up before use, and the light it produces lasts around 5-10 seconds at most. Honestly, it is more than enough light for all aspects of the game and adds to the tension that the environment tries to create. They wouldn't have had constant portable light back then, and so it makes a lot of sense to not have it in this game. All in all, I have really enjoyed the experience and I am looking forward to playing it again at some point. If I have one criticism of the game, it is purely that having some sort of map when in the house would have proved helpful purely because each time you go to the house different doors are open or locked and so it can be easy to get lost when trying to find your way around. That being said though, it was by no means a large frustration of any sort. I really do recommend playing this game if you enjoy history, puzzle games or horror walking simulators. I do think though that it is fair to warn you that it deals heavily with the subject of PTSD and poor mental health as well as some other mental health conditions like melancholia and sociopathy. If any of those are triggering for you then it would likely be wise to avoid the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Ad Infinitum is a horror drama game, set in WW1. You witness how the war affected the lives of the members of a prominent German family, its relationships and dynamics.It's a decently-crafted game, putting emphasis on the story and the characters, which you come to learn about through letters and notes you find scattered all over the stages of the game. The story goes back-n-forth between the family's household in Germany and the western front in France during WW1. It tries to show you not only the horrors of war, but also the horrors of a dysfunctional family with a dark past, a dark present and dark skeletons in its closet.Gameplay-wise, the game offers a mixture of puzzle solving, stealth and note collecting. The puzzles are not that challenging, but I wouldn't say dead-easy either. Oftentimes it seems there's not an awful lot to do but walk around too much, and a few areas/stages do feel like they outstay their welcome. Overall, it gives you stuff to do, but it tries to not burden you, more than it tries to keep you engaged.The game looks and sounds good. It's well-modelled, atmospherically textured and lit, with good sound design and music that fits the sombre and sad theme. There are instances were the models look kind of cheap, but I don't think it takes too much away from everything else.Some spooks and jumpscares are there, but it's mostly the overall atmosphere and the story that are meant to be horrific. I truly believe this is one of the most OK-iest games out there. The downsides are not that detrimental, and it never really hits any extreme highs. It's an alright experience, one I would recommend generally, but I wouldn't push anyone into grabbing immediately.

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you....Hekate & Nacon....Truly thank youThis has been one of the most anticipated releases of my life. The reason I started Content Creation.The reason I am here. 13 years ago...it was announced.They showed a short gameplay trailer that looked spooky and scary as hellBut what it became was something much much moreHekate and Nacon have outdone themselves truly!This is one of those games that needs to be explored, that needs to be talked about, that needs to be played for years and yearsAnd after finishing it 4 times, finding all the clues and mysteries and darker moments thought hidden, this is definitely not for the faint of heart.Taking into account the horrors faced, the psychological trauma experienced, the jump scares and the overarching themes...that only scratches the surface. This is a tale of true horror, the horrors we face in our world today after over a 100 years we still fight for. The reason we live is overshadowed by the reason we are told to do so. _childDocuments_.review: this is a really expensive game for being absolutely nothing at all. I like the setting, the story, etc. but there's just nothing here. It isn't scary or very interactive, nothing really happens, it is by definition a walking sim. Except, there ARE enemies and mechanics like hiding in dugouts which give you the impression that it's eventually turn into a real game, but then it just doesn't. the enemies are placed around the map like traffic cones and then they just stand there, they have no idle behavior or move around the map searching for the player or anything. it feels extremely low effort and lazy, this game should be like 5 bucks for how little the devs seemed to care about their product. and luckily, i only paid about 3 dollars for this. if you paid full price and didn't refund before the 2 hour mark then i genuinely feel sorry for you.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most boring games I've played in recent years. At it's best, it's interesting. If felt like 20 minutes of actual gameplay in my 5 hour playthrough (including puzzles, nearby enemies, boss fights, and "platforming"), the rest was reading a book or walking around and cutting through barbed wire. The monsters were cool but totally underutilized. The story was okay. The "Action" genre is very misleading, there's almost nothing that I would consider action in this game. Sorry for sounding like a hater, but this has way too many positive reviews and people need to know what they're getting into.

_childDocuments_.review: I'd like to clarify that I had no idea this game existed until a few days before release, when it popped on my recommendations shortly after finishing Amnesia: The Bunker. So, I haven't been following, nor did I have any idea about this project and I mostly went in blind.First of all, like other reviews point out, this game isn't a shooter, a survival horror or anything of the short. This game is much closer from my experience to a walking simulator, and a very lineal one. Gameplay mechanics are fairly limited and mostly consist of simple puzzles like finding items, codes or interacting with some of the environment. Additionally you might be dealing with a few monsters in different ways, cutting wires, breaking obstacles or using a flashlight or a gas mask to move through darkness or clouds of gas. All of these are very simple mechanics and they're definitely not what the game is going for. This game's main attraction is its story, which of course I won't spoil, but I'll give my thoughts on it since that's the main pillar of the game. It is a very personal and psychological story which doesn’t focus exclusively on the war experience itself, but on the consequences it had on people involved in it directly or indirectly. One thing which I found remarkable is how this game doesn't solely go over the scars and wounds that the war has caused in our protagonist, but in how it affected his own family as well. It is a story with a wide angle on the suffering and destruction that an event such as WW1 brought not only to those in the front, but also to those back at home. The game is filled with symbolism in the shape of creatures, objects and scenes, some of which I found very beautiful, haunting and brilliant. It also includes different choices that affect the ending, although I haven't been able to see all of them yet since I just completed my first playthrough. Aside from this, I didn't find any major bugs, although my first impression of this game was somewhat mixed due to a glitch that prevented me from advancing, but was solved after reloading a checkpoint. The music is quite good, very orchestral and used to a big degree in important moments of the game, although I encountered a few audio glitches or moments where music or background noises would stop playing for a moment. I would also add that I didn’t like the music much at first, not because it was bad, but because it felt quite out of place to me, especially at the beginning. However, as the game progressed it started to make much sense and I could find myself finding it fitting. That’s also one piece of advice: Do not judge the game or how it handles the setting until you’ve been playing through a good chunk of the game. Overall, I liked it a lot but it's definitely not a game for everyone. So, if anything of what you read in my review sounded like you would be interested in it, consider giving it a try. If you're intrigued by the story but can't afford it you can always watch it somewhere. I'd definitely keep an eye out for other projects of this team.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Every horror fan should experience the flooded trenches stage. One of the most unnerving designs of the year.It starts slow but eventually it gets quite endearing. I strogly recommend giving the game its sweet time to develop because it gets better. However, as a horror fan and walking sim aficionado, I've got the feeling I've already played this one several times before. It's like an Amnesia or Bloober game but without their puzzles or imagination. "In sound mind", which also deals with mental health, is more adventurous than this and more successful. One of the main problems with "Ad Infinitium" is that for long periods of time doesn't happen anything at all, you just walk and walk without any music, tension, mission or fear. That's a big con when it comes to horror or mystery games. It takes ages for the story and the atmosphere to get your attention. Moreover, the gameplay is way too easy, too straightforward. Some of the monsters are similar to those funny little jungle zombies from the early 00s sequel of "The Mummy", and the whole Mother of Sorrows thing reminds me of Dario Argento's universe. All of them pretty awesome references and maybe inspirations, but in "Ad Infinitum" they lack punch.  I expected more, to be honest. The occasional bug (I got stuck in the mansion's front door, after the "ball" appearance, or the trenches changing lights and aspect in Chapter 2 or 3) doesn't help either. It's an adventure akin to "The Beast Inside", very far from your Vintages, Madisons, Amnesias o Evil Withins.

_childDocuments_.review: I really like Ad Infinitum.It has a strong story and eerie atmosphere.There are puzzles to solve, but also enemies and chase sequences.The sounds are great and do the best for a tense feeling.Some reviews say "wandering around and not knowing what to do". Not true.You get notes with hints and you can see your next goal by pushing TAB -> mission.If you like horror, intense stories, heavy atmosphere and uncertainty about what is real - this is for you =)

_childDocuments_.review: After playing for 3,5 hours I decided to give up this exhausting experience and to leave a review for this game. I will give the pros and cons and ultimately tell you why I wouldn't recommend this game.Pros:Very polished gameGreat atmosphereGreat soundtrack and overall sound designAmazing storyVery unique creature designsCons:Nonexistent  gameplaySenseless level designControls when opening doors, gates etc. are extremely wonkyEasy nonsensical puzzlesHorrible pacing and lore experiencingWhile I appreciate the work that they put into this game, it's one of the worst walking simulators I've experienced. The navigating and exploring is absolutely annoying, due to the fact that they put in dead ends after every second corner. While the story is great from what I've gathered so far, it is very exhausting to experience it, since a lot of the lore comes from notes scattered through the world. This reaches a point where you might as well read a book instead and have a better experience, which is what I suggest you to do instead of playing this game.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10 | Incredible Story | Stunning Graphics | Unique Twists.I absolutely loved this game for the STORY side of things. I really became more interested as the game progressed and had an urge to continue to discover what REALLY happens towards the ending. Whilst this story was captivating I do believe that some of the "puzzle elements" were slightly pointless and a bit of a shame. I personally would have been fine with a walking simulator in all honesty as I felt like the "puzzles" weren't really necessary and the game/story/graphics/detail etc was more than enough. However I did enjoy this game and I am very happy I got a chance to play it. I recommend this for anyone who's interested in a world war related story that's quite heavy. I wouldn't worry too much about the horror elements but there is a few to say the least. Nothing majorly scary however.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been looking forward to this one for a while and the game was everything I hoped for and more. The horror atmosphere is quite immersive  and the visuals nice and crisp. I love the attention to controller support for the PC version as I physically can’t use mouse and keyboard and many modern games neglect proper controller support if any.I am glad that I waited until the discount went away because I wanted to pay for the full supporter edition cost because I appreciate all the developers have done to make a refreshingly unique horror game and want to show my appreciation somehow. I have also seen some reviews elsewhere that have complaints about the game, but everything works fine and the game plays well. Thank you guys for putting out a good game from the jump without needing a ton of bug fixes like many games these days. Very satisfied with my purchase and recommend it for anyone who likes horror games. So far 9/10 can’t wait to see what’s in store for the rest of my playthrough!

The trailer has literally all the cool, spooky and action stuff from the entire game. The game itself is a drag to get through, quite boring, scares are very predictable and overall very confusing story, but then again if you're into piecing stories together yourself from notes n such, fair game. If you can get this game on a HUGE discount or a gift then that's a maybe. I'd say a 4/10 but if I squint my eyes enough I'ts juuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuuust about 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Im going to agree with some others, this is not a survival horror game, its a puzzle walking simulator, great atmosphere but not very interesting. I feel like the game suits people that like puzzles and not survival. A game needs to grip me in the first hour or I will leave it, life is too short and there is so many games out there.Steam needs to make it clear this is not a survival horror.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: The tags are 90% incorrect stating the game is survival horror or action related, it is a walking simulator. The music at certain parts is inappropriate and ruins all tension if there ever was any. The house segments are probably the worst part of the game, with few if any horror elements and bland puzzles and notes. I encountered quite a few bugs where i get launched into the air across the map or the sound of the final boss being completely absent during the cutscene events. Some locked doors can even be randomly actually opened. The story is full of the same old tropes of modern horror walking sim games: mental illness, abuse, and exaggerated depth. The graphics are actually very nice, lots of detail with good lighting and it doesn't run too poorly. The gameplay is pretty lacking with just puzzles and walking around. The enemies can be pretty much ran by most the time and there's no real inventory to manage at all. The most compelling thing about this game would be the design of the monsters, they're very unique and detailed I like them a lot. Overall, I think this game is another victim of the current wave of horror that supports little mechanical depth and psychological horror themes that boil down to mental illness stereotypes and shock value drama.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a little bit of a mixed bag; it compares unfavorably to Amnesia: the Bunker, but I think it still stands on its own as long as you don't go in with the wrong expectations.  From appearances, I expected a game about the horrors of war with some action; instead, I got nearly a walking simulator, focused on the trauma and tragedy suffered by a family - although centered around the Great War, it's still much tighter and more intimate.  There are barely any characters in the whole game beyond the main character.With those expectations, it's got some fantastic enemy designs, interesting ideas, and enjoyable set-pieces.  I just wish it had been more of a game and less of a walk around making choices simulation.

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic experience that was worth going through, but out of fear and the strong emotions this game made me feel, I will not be playing it again.Very well made and the attention to detail in every environment is incredible. Some areas were not as optimized as others and would lag a little, but it didn't affect my experience much as I got through those areas quickly.I managed to get a good ending, I would not have been able to handle anything worse.I highly recommend this experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I do understand that some people are fed up with walking simulators, which this game very much is, and if you're one of those you probably won't enjoy this game. This game is definitely not perfect. I think a bunch of notes could've just been comments played at particular sections instead of picking up and reading them (there were a bit too many notes tbh, although some were really interesting to read). The voice acting was not the best for some characters.The puzzles were fun enough to me, don't need them to be more difficult to figure out. The graphics and overall sound effects were great... I didn't find the game too scary, but I don't really mind that personally. Thought the story was it's strongest point and really, really enjoyed it. BUT, lots of TW with regards to the story which people might want to keep in mind. One of the bosses was also truly just annoying and did tug down my impression of the game. Overall I truly enjoyed it though and would recommend it for people that enjoy this type of game. It's not unique by any means, but an interesting story and take on what the WW1 could mean for a soldier.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Glad I got this in a sale as it is quite short, though multiple endings could merit multiple playthroughs. That being said this is a pretty good game, a little light on the scares/horror and some elements felt like they were not really followed through on or utilised to their fullest extent. _childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I am a HUGE fan of the survival horror genre, and Ad Infinitum was probably one of the best ones I have ever played. The story was hard hitting and emotional, it really captures the effect WW1 had on families at the time. Highly recommend for survival horror fans, especially if you're a fan of the WW1 era of history.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Masterpiece... simply put. This game was a wonderful experience. The story kept me enthralled the entire way through. The visuals are beautiful... and the game play is very fun. This is like a Triple A studio title from an indie developer. It's completely worth every penny they're asking... and I can't wait to see what they release in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this is interesting. This game is far from perfect but it still manages to impress me. I went into it blindly, without even watching a trailer or using a walkthrough in the first playthrough. I didn't know where to go and what awaits around the next corner. It certainly is no Resident Evil or Silent Hill, but still I was frightened just the same at some points in the story. It builds an atmosphere. One of the reasons is, that you can't really defend yourself. There's no combat at all, but a lot of stealth elements and all of the boss fights are purely mechanical. I can see that this won't appeal to everyone and I expected something else, but it worked.If you give it a chance, then sit it through until the end. The game is worth experiencing. Also, there are three endings to get.What I would improve though, is adding a chapter select with a collector's mode as to find the missing collectibles or portraits and not having to collect them all over again in a whole new playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game by a young and emerging indie-development team from Berlin. I always liked the combination of a horror game set during the backdrop of WW1 and there are not so many games out there like that. The game's graphics and environment is good-looking and believable, the soundtrack and audio design draws you right into the world. There is a stylistic emphasis on the surreal and traumatic/psychological which fits nicely with the reality of war and it's effects on a family. Gameplay-wise the game is rather simple and repetitive (one could argue walking simulator), nevertheless I can still safely recommend it to all fans of Horror (Amnesia, Layers of Fear) or WW1.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: World War I was a horrific time in the world. The creation of mustard gas and the deaths of 20 million people are just a couple of things that came from that war. You play Paul von Schmidt, a German man who returned from the war. Paul and his brother Johannes are raised by their father, who is a wartime cripple. Over the course of the game, you explore Paul’s mind and how he feels and represents the events of his childhood and the trauma from the war. Sadly, most of this is only pieced together by letters found throughout the game, as the cut scenes themselves explain little and just muddle the otherwise generic feeling of the story.The game is broken up into two gameplay styles. An adventure/walking simulator-style mansion exploration where you solve puzzles. This part of the game is rather dull and uninteresting. Many other games do house explorations better (Layers of Fear, Gone Home, What Remains of Edith Finch) as the game slowly opens the house to you, but the key is to find objects to solve puzzles and find something that triggers a dive into Paul’s mind and thoughts. Each chapter (there are three) consists of one of his family members represented as a horrific monster. You can either choose to kill them or let them live to get different endings. Most of these “boss fights” require you to flip switches and run away for the most part, but they are rather intense, so I didn’t mind them.The second part of the game is the trenches gameplay, in which the horror part sets in. You need to run around solving the occasional puzzle while also hiding from enemies. There is no combat in this game, so you have to sneak around and find your way through the dark in various environments. The creature designs are awesome, but this is probably the most exciting part of the game. It was intense sneaking past enemies, and thankfully there’s only one small section in each chapter, but the horror elements that are actually good can be counted on one hand. There are moments in which each main monster is introduced, and these scenes are fairly creepy, and outside of weird sound effects and haunting ambience, there’s not much else here. The game does portray the gruesome horrors of the war, with bodies spread everywhere, the barbaric medical practices, and the overall brutal nature of everything people endured during that time.With the game being as linear as it is, there isn’t a lot of room for exploration outside of finding dog tags, and this only grants an achievement. There are a few extra gameplay items you can find, such as a pickaxe to break down walls, a dynamo flashlight, a gas mask, and wire cutters to cut down barbed wire, which is actually quite annoying. The barbed wire moves and is related to the story (I won’t spoil why), and you have to cut the non-moving wire or it will grab you, and that will trigger a quick-time event. This could have been done better. To be completely honest, all of these items don’t really add anything to the game. The gas mask is used a few times to get through corridors with some gas, and it lasts a few seconds. The flashlight is annoying to use, as it only lights up for a few seconds before needing to be charged again. The game overall isn’t very exciting. The horror elements fall flat, and the walking simulator-style gameplay is void of almost any gameplay. The story itself is convoluted and difficult to figure out if you don’t read the papers spread throughout the game. The visuals are at least good, if not necessarily unique or interesting, because of the monster designs. There are nice lighting effects, but the character models are something to be desired. The mansion areas are also a chore to play through, and it just feels like mindless wandering through rooms to find objects.Overall, Ad Infinitum doesn’t do anything particularly well or is interesting enough to not be forgettable. There are some good horror moments, but they aren’t anything special, and the game overall lacks a cohesive story or a way to tell it. There are many games out there that are similar and do a better job of everything listed.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a phenomenal game. A glorious blend of the atmospheres caught in games like Amnesia and Silent Hill, Exquisite aesthetics, storyline and soundscapes, beautifully telling the tale of WWI trauma, PTSD, Biggotry, classism, and family toxicity, all while manifesting the horrors of the war in such a way that seemed extremely respectful to those that lost their lives on both sides of the conflicts.Strongly Recommend
