_childDocuments_.review: Honestly not sure where the good reviews are coming from. This game doesn't provide anything interesting. It's just empty space. The first 3 hours are simply boring. If this is a horror game, there's 1 hour of walking between any marginal scare in that time. One of the tags is 'action' which it absolutely is not. 'Survival Horror'? No.Visuals are middling. The story and setting have potential but nothing to draw you in! I'm fairly certain the only exciting moments of this game are in the trailer, but I quit after 3-4 hours because there was nothing to keep me playing.  I do think sound design is good (when things are actually happening), and the voice acting is well done, but mostly all you hear is footsteps and you read a lot of notes.I really wanted to like this because I play a lot of games similar to this, and maybe that's the problem. It may be a labor of love as I've seen other people say, but it offers nothing new or unique. And if the first 3-4 hours of gameplay only contain 2-3 interesting moments, those moments need to be spectacular or the tension needs to be building the entire time, but that's not the case at all.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Ad Infinitum is a walking simulator, with a good sound story. Allthough it takes you some real reading, to learn the story. Gameplay wise it is very simple. And sadly sometimes frustrating because of failing gameplay mechanics/little bugs. It's not very scary at all, but the story, graphics and especially the music have enough atmosphere. The ending caught me with a little tear, that saved this review ;-)
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Ad Infinitum is a very atmospheric horror walking sim that intelligently deals with the trauma suffered by the soldiers of the Great War, the game feels like Otto Dix paintings come to life. The set pieces look very nice and each have their unique gameplay elements, it never feels like you are always doing the same thing for the 5 or so hours the game lasts. It is a bit rough around the edges, notably when it comes to movement and some animations but nothing too annoying. As for the story, I will simply say that it is touching, you'll consistently find yourself wanting to know what happens next. I heavily recommend playing the game with the German audio.If you're looking to immerse yourself into the trenches of WW1 from the perspective of a mentally broken veteran, Ad Infinitum will provide you with the experience you're looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: Full gameplay: All Endings and Boss Fights: This game is well designed, it has a great and touching story, great visuals, runs pretty well and has a good combination of boss fights and endings. Although it is not perfect but as an overall package I recommend this game to anyone who is interested in horror games with good story telling.Graphics and Visuals (4/5):Game visuals are pretty good, areas are pretty well designed and captures the overall game tone. Enemies are very unique and grotesque in a way but they fit pretty good to the story and why they designed this way. The only thing that could’ve been better I think is character animations and lip syncing when they talk, I wish for character actions there were some appropriate animations related to that action in the game. One other thing that was a little annoying was the darkness of some areas in the game, even with flashlight I could hardly see around myself, trying to change game gamma but didn't help.Gameplay and Mechanics (3/5):This game is a combination of walking simulator like most of the other indie horror games and some basic combat elements, although combat is not a right word but there are boss fights that you have to do some actions and use environment to beat them, there is no gun fight. It was an interesting combination in my opinion and add a layer of engagement on top of basic walking sims. One thing that felt little weird to me was that you get a gun in this game but you almost never use it, I feel that they added because of game theme but felt little awkward when you get a gun but don’t get a chance to use it.Other thing which personally irritated me a little was the amount of walking in each section, I feel this game could’ve been little shorter and wouldn’t lose much of its atmosphere and storytelling, each section is unique and has interesting design but you walk a lot which sometimes makes it little boring. Like for example there are some areas that you climb a ladder for about 30 seconds, or walk on a path for a long time to get to next point. Storyline and Immersion (4/5): I think this is where the game shines, it tries to tell a very important story about war and its influence on people. It’s very powerful and touching when you go through the things that happened to this family by gathering documents, I highly recommend to try to interact with all of them since it’s very important part of the game. You will be immersed in this story pretty well, they captured the war atmosphere and its affects on this family pretty good.The enemies and bosses as I said have a very unique design which fit perfectly with the story and situation they are trying to depict. You can understand the pain and feelings that they had through this journey. Sound and Music (3/5): Overall sound and music of the game is really good. Sound effects are really well designed too. But unfortunately the implementation was not very good, there were many moments that I felt the music and sound effects were out of place and were not playing based on situation, sometimes the music was too loud or didn’t play in some cases, there were some overlaps with conversations too.Performance and Bugs (4/5):This game runs pretty well on my machine, 1440p 12900K and 3090. I tried to run with DLSS Quality and lock framerate on 120 and most of the time got 120fps. But after a while I felt the implantation of DLSS was not very good and noticed the ghosting a lot. Disabled it and to my surprise game was still running smoothly at highest quality without DLSS.I encountered couple of bugs during my gameplay, game crashed for 4-5 times randomly and had to restart the game.Replayability (2/5): There is a replayability value to this game, but unfortunately the way that they implemented is really bad. There is only one save slot in this game and you don’t have any control over it. You can only restart the chapter you are in or reload last checkpoint. Game has multiple endings and multiple endings to each boss fight, in order to get them all you have to play from beginning of the game each time and go through everything again. I am not sure why they designed it this way but I really don’t like this approach, at least they should’ve saved each chapter separately and let users replay each one again if they wanted.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Very fantastic game!I'm absolutely fascinated with anything WW1 based, and this positively surprised me. While I first assumed it would be more "NecroVision" that doesn't take itself serious, it's more like The Great War as far as story goes, with a dash of horror.There's no combat, scenes where you avoid monsters are also a bit sparse, just so you know.I found myself really not that scared by the monsters but more moved and awed by the story and the reality of this terrible war that I think this game does a good job of depicting.Maybe it's just the novelty of finally finding a story told from the German side. It can make you realize every soldier is human, and those who are thrust right to the meat grinder that is the frontline are never the ones that WANTED the war.There seems to be some variety in endings. I got a pretty ending and it moved me close to tears.The puzzles are.. there.. they're not too annoying and not really hard. I do prefer it that way. (Look, if I can figure it out, anyone can, let's put it like that.)Voice acting is serviceable.I have to add though that perhaps this game speaks to me on a level it might not to everyone since I have done a couple years of military service, by my own wish of course.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: WWI is a setting full of horrors before you even begin to add psychological monstrosities into the mix. Trench warfare, mustard gas, ptsd, rudimentary and ill-equipped wartime hospitals already paint a bleak picture. Ad Infinitum seeks to take this setting and amp it up to 11 while carefully telling a tale that can do these complex issues justice. Surprisingly, it handles the topics of war pretty well and I'd actually say the story itself is the strongest aspect of the game alongside the monster design. Unfortunately, general clunkiness and lackluster gameplay bring down the experience as a whole.The game is split in essentially 3 sections each beginning with a part in the protagonist's family mansion and the 2nd half in and around the trenches on the western front. The game makes it apparent early on that there are no actual enemies during the mansion sections so there is a somewhat lack of tension during them. You will instead be solving puzzles and piecing together your family's history/story. The war time sequences, where the actual horror elements of the game are, are a mixed bag. Each of the 3 sections has it own unique boss enemy and non-boss enemy. Enemy designs across the board are excellent and quite unsettling, however, the execution, especially of the first 2 chapters' non-boss enemies, feels underbaked.You have the first enemy type that is essentially blind requiring you to navigate around them in stealth, avoiding traps and debris that would alert them OR in some cases using objects to divert them from blocking your path by alerting them. Their AI is pretty terrible to say the least and while the rest of the sound design was great, I found them to sound closer to a pack of monkeys rather than anything actually worthy of horror. The other enemy type is a single large entity that pursues the player in a select few sections of the trenches. The player must duck into these alcoves and wait for it to pass. It does not matter if you duck in literal feet in front of the enemy, it will not pull you out. The area it pursues you in is so big that I only had to wait once before completing my objective. It just felt disappointing considering how cool the concept was.The 3rd non-boss enemy type, however, is genuinely scary and utilized well. They function similarly to weeping angels where instead of the player's gaze halting them it is light or more importantly, the player's WW1 dynamo flashlight. These enemies move in an unnerving fashion and their screeches and groans echo across the dark halls of the military hospital they are encountered in.Boss fights in miss the mark in most  horror games, and the ones in Ad infinitum are kind of par for the course. The last 2 are OK, but the first one has the baffling idea to make the boss ONLY pursue you in a specific section that is crossed when moving between the objects you have to interact with. Meaning you essentially don't really interact with the boss at all during the fight if you just beeline from one object to another. The boss does at least have a decent chase sequence prior that is admittedly tense.I'm of mixed opinion on the game's visuals. As I said, the design of the creatures as well as the small selection of NPCs is fantastic, and the mansion itself has character with each room feeling unique. The problem is that making WW1 trenches an interesting location to navigate is HARD and this game proves that in spades. Unsurprisingly the 3rd act taking place in a military hospital is the most interesting of the wartime sequences as the rest are spent wandering around the same looking brown/grey, muddy environments.Voice acting is solid across the board and the story is well done, though it does take a little bit to get moving at first. Music was good, though nothing particularly stood out to me, and as I previously mentioned sound design was great besides the weird monkey like enemies. I encountered a couple crashes in the 3rd act and the game just had an overall clunky feel to it. It's really noticeable in the couple spots that the game gives you a rifle with some of the worse shooting mechanics I've ever seen in my life. Luckily this seems to be for show more than anything since you never actually use it for anything.This review was quite a lot of negatives, but I will say that I do think my experience was worthwhile in the end. If you can grab the game on a sale, I'd recommend that, but keep in mind that issues I've laid out and whether or not an interesting premise, compelling story, and handful of decent gameplay sections are enough to balance out the bad.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Amazing design of the world during the Great War depicting the dirtiness and toughness of trenches in the best possible way. Incorporating illusions and imaginary elements it creates a dark, surreal atmosphere that gets the player immersed right from the beginning. Some sceneries are imposing. The manor is gorgeous and so interesting to explore. - Beautiful graphics with lots of details, great lighting conditions and atmospheric elements like fogs and volume lights.- Great concept. It doesn't need heavy action to give you understand how war works. After all people have used gunshots and deaths in movies and games. It chooses to focus on struggle, fears and dilemmas of people via allegories by cleverly inserting paranormal phenomena and imaginary creatures. A great example of magical realism.- Awesome horror approach. It doesn't use jump scares or other worn, cheap tricks. It offers subtle, creepy events especially at the manor that can deeply affect the player creating a calm nightmare that doesn't rush anything.- Great story with political meanings that shows the drama of a family during the war. Storytelling is even better as is masterfully takes you back and forth in time revealing gradually parts of the plot and letting you know one by one the members of the family. It makes you understand the psychosynthesis of Germans during the war and how older generations, their pride and visions have affected younger generations.- Very good direction and photography. Pacing and framing are great. Some scenes look like a piece of art.- Phenomenal voice acting performances full of emotions. They give you to understand the personality of each character even though you never really meet most of them. - Outstanding music that fits perfectly to each moment enhancing even more the atmosphere.- Rich audio design with convincing environmental sounds and a lot of creepy others.- Interesting creatures. They're well designed and pretty frightening. Bosses are gorgeous visually although their battles are a little bit shallow.- It offers some decent puzzles. They're not difficult or innovative by any means but they're interesting enough to add another dimension to the gameplay. Encounters against enemies look like puzzles too, although the mechanics needed some more polishing.- Well written texts and dialogues that you never get bored of reading. Some of them are kind of poetic.The bad- Some gameplay elements are mediocre and needed more work. Stealth mechanics are shallow and sequences that enemies are chasing you needed some more polishing. Also, some elements look unbalanced. Despite giving emphasis on explanation of some mechanics, eventually they're not used enough, while others like the axe are overused without actually adding much to the experience.- Sometimes, mainly at the manor, you're not sure what to do next so you have to read the objectives menu. That's mediocre level design. It should give you a few more in game clues to guide you.- Controls have some issues, mainly when interacting with objects. Opening doors or turning valves is the most annoying.- You have to make some moral decisions that heavily affect the plot. The problem is that it doesn't give you enough information so you cannot imagine a possible outcome or maintain some kind of logic behind your actions.- The last part of the game is a little bit underwhelming. For about an hour there's almost no real gameplay. You just walk inside some surreal places, collecting memories that reveal the full story.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Really lovely horror game, does not lean heavily on the "classic"  formula, but that does not mean it does NOT do that, it does, but only enough for that to not be a nuisance.The game is very well paced, with a mansion section where you focus on solving puzzles, then on the... memories? subconscious? I don't know how to describe it, but you solve some other puzzles over there while avoiding enemies (or using them to solve puzzles  on the first three chapters, with each one featuring a different type of hazard, a tool to deal with it and it culminates with you using those tools interchangeably later in the game to progress, making every mechanic not a one use gimmick.Storywise this is also really well written, but I will not spoil you that for y'all.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I've been putting off this review for a while because I worried that I could in any way hurt the initial sales of this game. I think this developer has potential, but I think they have a lot to learn from "Ad Infinitum" and its failings. If they go under, they'll never do anything again, and that's not my goal. "Ad Infinitum" is flawed, flawed to the point where I found it frustrating, and I'm on the fence whether it was actually worth the trouble. But it is not worthless, and the potential was there.To be specific, I think the monster designs were very good, the music and some of the audio design were great (though uneven), and I kind of liked the plot... to a point. There are great moments in this game, like the seance scene, and some fun foreshadowing, like the mirror in the main character's bedroom. The main themes are taken seriously and explored through visual metaphors. It's not hard to decifer, as long as you read the optional notes, which I think is good; there's no need to make something interesting unnecessarily obscure. What ruins the story for me is the binary nature of the choices, where one choice is good (green) and one is bad (red). It's dumb. It does not fit a story with such heavy themes. The good ending felt unearned to the point where I questioned whether it was supposed to be real, and not just a figment of main character's imagination. Everything else - graphics and gameplay - is just overall meh.Other than that, "Ad Infinitum" is let down by its lack of polish and optimization. It stutters on a machine that should easily run it. It is riddled with glitches, big and small. Were it a fantastic game otherwise, I'd be willing to forgive the poor release state. But it's merely an OK game, reaching maybe 20% of its potential, and so it's hard to overlook all the minor frustrations. I know they've been patching it, so I started it up for a few minutes a few days ago, and I didn't see significant improvements to performance. At this point, I don't care if it's fixed. I'd rather see the dev try again. I think they can do good stuff, if they're given the opportunity.

_childDocuments_.review: Ad Infinitum is a well made first person adventure with a horror/war theme.   All the elements of decent game design come together here to make an immersive and engrossing story. From a technical perspective, every box is checked, every "t" crossed and every "i" dotted, with 4K support and a slew of graphics and control customisations, DLSS and AMD's equivalent.  The game delivers the mandatory AAA tier professional delivery, it's well optimised, runs and plays well. The game is narrative rich but doesn't fall into the trap of turning into an E-book or a Youtube video, you get the story delivered by playing the game, as it should be. It's seriously overpriced, however, so this should only be considered on a steep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly I had been worried when the game was taking so long to release, but I am so so happy with the result. I enjoyed the experience so much that I dove right back in to play again to get one of the other endings immediately after finishing the first play-through. The enemy/creature design is just top notch eye candy for those of us that love our scary monsters. Every creature/enemy looked vastly different and had story driven reasoning behind their appearance. I adore when designers do this so it's not just a scary monster for scary sake. The soundtrack is absolutely gorgeous too. If you're looking for an action filled horror game, this isn't really that. This isn't the kind of horror game where you're saving the world from some impending doom by killing monsters. This is an emotional journey for our character and given the subject matter for the game it feels appropriate that you experience the game's story in a more narrative fashion as opposed to fighting enemies to reach an end goal. I'd compare this more along the lines of Layers of Fear mixed with "action" that's more focused on discovering certain mechanics that allow you to beat the bosses or enemies you face. Again, you're not really fighting enemies in this game, but you are taking steps to avoid death and to beat bosses.  Actions you take do obviously effect the ending you get, but I also noticed a couple little easy to miss differences in item/note descriptions as well as dialogue you end up getting throughout the game. It would have been nice to have this fleshed out a little more often and more noticeably, but I still appreciated that it wasn't just boss scenes or your end cutscene that was different. There are some quirks and bugs in the game. Some item hit box interaction points being finicky. Some potential background/dialogue or music triggers getting missed and therefore not playing. As well as at least one boss phase 2 mechanic that IMO was more vague than it should be and was a bit of a Pain to get through (Pain is a keyword here that'll mean something to those who have played while still being vague enough to not give away spoilers). Overall though, these were minor for me and didn't take away from the overall experience and I'm confident that bugs will be sorted out as they're found and updates get released.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, the positive reviews that look like were made by bots that barely play video games and the game trailer give too much credit for what the game is actually worth.This game is NOT worth 35$, but it would be an okay game for like, 10$, its a ridiculous price for a game that ended up being pretty disappointing compared to the trailer. This game is pretty much a budget half-baked game with surprisingly clunky mechanics that takes Layers of Fear and Amnesia: The Bunker, mixed into one. If you don't like puzzles, I also don't recommend just because its as simple as it is described from what i quote from another "is mainly just trying to find ♥♥♥♥ a to stick into butt b". The puzzles take too much away from the gameplay and story, so most of the time, you are just wandering around, trying to find ♥♥♥♥, and googling where to find things. Due to a random bug in the game that ended up breaking my save for no reason whatsoever, I would have to restart everything from the beginning, and I already watched a gameplay video of what most of the gameplay looks like, and continues to be pretty underwhelming. The mansion is too unnecessarily gigantic and 90% of everything in the mansion is just locked anyways. Objectives are linear, but trying to complete the objectives are extremely non-linear.The only thing I'll give credit for this game is the trailer, the story, and the music production.. but even when playing the game, the music seems very.. out of place. _childDocuments_.review: Be warned, if you pick up this game expect a horror walking sim, with a few action scenes and puzzles scattered in it. In a matter of fact, the “action” tag really is a stretch for this game. The only action you will get is with bosses, and even that is meh… For normal monsters you just run pass them, for bosses, you just run around them and interact with 4 objects. I think you can see the problem here. So, the action feels like a chore, it is placed in the game to just drag out game time, but what about the rest?Well, I give it a thumbs up. It builds up horror great through the environment, sounds (too bad it aint surround), effects and art style, etc . The story, despite the fact that you should pick up notes to fully grasp, it is nonetheless an emotional roller coaster.As a note, this is a 7/10. However, for anyone looking to pick it up, just expect a lot of walking and exploration to find those notes (and even more of those if you plan on getting all endings). Might be boring for some, heck I was getting bored too, after experiencing those dreadful action scenes, where the bosses mechanics of just hitting 4 switches kept on repeating for all bosses.Also, this game has one of the most useless flashlights mechanics I encountered. It is sort of like Metro, where you wind it up to charge the battery, but here lasts like 5 seconds before needing a wind-up again.

_childDocuments_.review: I must admit, I'm not usually a fan of horror games, but this one truly caught me by surprise! This World War I horror-themed game has left me utterly captivated and impressed.First and foremost, the game's atmosphere is an absolute triumph. The meticulous attention to detail in recreating the grim backdrop of World War I is commendable. The graphics and sound design work in harmony to immerse you in an eerie, unsettling world that feels as real as it is terrifying.The storyline is a gripping descent into the horrors of war, with a supernatural twist that keeps you on the edge of your seat. The narrative is masterfully crafted, drawing you in with its mysteries and gradually unfolding a dark and compelling tale.As for the gameplay, the tension and fear are palpable. The challenging puzzles and the relentless enemies make for an adrenaline-pumping experience.In summary, if you're a fan of horror or simply enjoy a heart-pounding experience, this WWI horror game is a must-play. Its immersive atmosphere, captivating story, and nerve-wracking gameplay combine to deliver an unforgettable adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing the first trailer for Ad Infinitum 8 years ago...It gave a weird, creepy vibe, and a setting that wasn't all that common in gaming; a WWI horror based experience. The trailer vibe was exciting, and left a lot to imagination...8 years later, I finally played it and...I can't hide my disappointment. This, because, 8 years later, many games came out, that paved the way for Ad Infinitum to become a copy, instead of something to be inspired by. Amnesia, Resident Evil, and so on, were supposed to be side by side with it, but, unfortunately, it didn't happen. War and it's traumas certainly aren't things to be taken lightly, and they aren't, in this case, but that is how deep the game goes into it. History aside, the gameplay is a slog, the notes are all, and I mean all, read with the most dramatic pauses possible, and you'll have notes, plenty of them...I can't recommend it, sadly.Asides from it, it runs pretty well on Steam Deck, with shadows on Low as you can check by pressing the link below:

_childDocuments_.review: A game tagged as Horror shouldn't be this painfully boring.I get that this game probably has a slow-burn narrative that really delves into interesting topics, but I can't stomach pushing myself through to learn it by playing a walking sim 'horror' game like this.What sealed it for me was the 'climactic encounter' in Chapter 1. The chase segment broke twice and sent me flying out of bounds, and the 'fight' segment broke twice after I trotted through painfully dull chases to hit three record players, only for the control panel to do nothing both times.Also, the entire segment had its atmosphere completely neutered by this wildly bombastic, high-energy track that took me even further out of the experience than I already was.I'm sure the game has merits, but for me, I really, really cannot say I enjoyed this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Another good concept ruined by DEI and woke ideology.Throughout the whole story (which is mostly told through notes) they always portray french as the victims and germans as devils on earth, instead of showcasing that both nations back in the days were capable of good and evil, that most soldiers were forced into this war, listened to lies and false promises and how it traumatized everyone on the field by the sheer horror the great war brought to all sides.Lot of potential missed here.I know they wanted to make a horror game, but why does barely anyone in this war has a gun?You only get a rifle 2 times in the game, in situations where it never matters.And every dead solider on the field is unarmed as well, not even sidearms next to their bodies.What kind of war is that?With that there is so much potential missed that could have been possible for a WW1 horror game.Like to make the end of the story depend on how often you used your firearms, how many lives you spared, how many good deeds you have done.Instead they let you decide on boss battles to choose up or down and left or right.They didn't wanted to tell a war story, but a family drama.Only positive things to mention are the beautiful graphics, excellent sound design and well designed and accurate scenarios like trenches, fields and bunkers.

_childDocuments_.review: Only on chapter 2, but the game is great in what it's trying to give you as an experience. So far, the puzzles are fun and not overly complicated, evenly spaced and don't slow the pacing down. The soundtrack is absolutely incredible, and the sound design is wonderful. Monster design is symbolic, creepy, and impactful, especially if you read the little notes scattered around their areas. These give you some insight into the symbolism behind their designs. You aren't going to get Outlast style gameplay out of this, which is a good thing. The horror elements from this game come from the atmosphere and stories themselves, the monsters are simply the icing on top and provide for some memorable scenes and encounters. Its worth a buy at base price for sure, in my opinion. Story is obviously very well crafted, and there are a lot of little details and things to find throughout. You are rewarded for exploring the world. Nice job to the developers!

This review might change if the ending can manage to capture the snore I have.The atmosphere is alright, but the prologue felt very "Not so war like". You start off the game picking up a rifle in which you have no real chance to use on the French. And where are the french fighters? No where to be seen, only a couple German infantry firing off into nothing. On top of that the games secondary NPCs (Or things that are considered filler detail that requires small amount of animation time) animations aren't all that flushed out.Can't appreciate the music as it throws off much of the "spooky" vibe it's trying to give off so I ended up turning it off. It realistically needed some obscure ambiance tracks.As I was venturing, much of chapter 1 felt extremely bare, I expected some amount of small surrealism while exploring the trenches and bunks, but it's more of just a walking sim with nothing really going on but a few creatures here and there with some notes sprinkled around for story.I would recommend putting German voice language on over the British English dialogue. Whomever did the German voice acting did a pretty outstanding job, especially the mothers performance. I understand this is an indie developer and I won't lie, I have high expectations. It's far from a terrible game, but much of my immersion is killed by the lack of attention to detail while progressing through the levels, which is something I crave a load in story driven games.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good: + Great atmosphere + Well done monster designs + Top shelf soundtrack + An interesting and harrowing story of family and war delivered in horror formatThe Bad: - Progression can be confusing sometimes- To really understand the story you more-or-less have to find and read all the notes/letters- Minor, but consistent, technical issues- A bit too long for this style of game The Bottom Line: You wouldn’t be alone in not knowing, but Ad Infinitum was first announced by a different studio with a teaser trailer all the way back in 2017. Not much information was given about the game, but it looked to be some kind of survival horror game where monsters or demons terrorized soldiers in the trenches of WWI. Its unknown how much this early version of the game resembled the one which released in 2023, but one things for certain: Ad Infinitum is one hell of a ride. With a fantastic atmosphere supported by great use of light/shadow and a soundtrack fit for a feature length film, the environments the player moves through are haunting and anxiety inducing and the well designed creatures you encounter are nothing less than terrifying to behold. Gameplay-wise, Ad Infinitum can be compared to other titles like Still Wakes the Deep, Visage, and MADiSON. There is no combat, and no constant running and hiding (like Outlast). Instead, the player must traverse areas, avoid infrequent threats, and solve basic puzzles in order to progress. Along the way, you’ll find many notes, letters, and other objects that slowly fill you in on the story of the von Schmidt family and the impact the Great War had on them. At its core, this story is one of trauma and psychosis - specifically relating to the horrors and devastation brought on by the terrible conditions and experiences shared by both soldiers and civilians during this early 20th century conflict. While much has been written about or inspired by the terribleness of the Great War, Ad Infinitum stands as one of the few forms of media that takes this and turns it into a full-blown horror story. It’s unique and works very well. The only true criticisms I have of this game is that there do seem to be a number of technical issues that have remained unaddressed, and the game’s length. The technical issues are rather minor annoyances, but some require you to reload to the last checkpoint or restart the area. These include but are not limited to things such as the player getting stuck on pieces of the environment, unusual dips in frame rate, locked doors to inaccessible areas half opening, and being unable to disengage from an interactable object. As far as the game’s length goes: it’s too long for what it is. The average length for most people seems to be around 10 hours, and while that’s nothing compared to the 100+ hour behemoths we’re being served on a regular basis - 10 hours felt like too much for what is essentially a horror-themed walking simulator. The multiple trips through the trench network and certain areas like the lead up to the finale felt unnecessarily drawn out and void of enough interactivity to make them feel worth the time spent. In fact, I would argue that the game would’ve benefitted from being a few hours shorter - if for no other reason than making replaying it to experience the consequences of different choices a more attractive and less time consuming endeavor. All in all though, Ad Infinitum is a hidden gem among the more recent horror games - undeservedly forgotten almost as soon as it released. It’s rather unique, has a heart-breaking story of war and familial bonds, and features a finely crafted atmosphere that’s bleak and terrible but beautiful in its own horrific ways. Final Verdict = 8 out of 10 Kaisers

_childDocuments_.review: 4/5 This game is a thrilling and immersive journey into the horrors of war, masterfully blending psychological horror with a rich narrative experience. Set in the eerie, haunting trenches of World War I, this game brilliantly captures the feeling of being trapped in a nightmare that blurs the line between reality and the supernatural.The atmosphere of this game stands out. The game's graphics are stunning, with meticulously detailed environments that pull you into its dark, oppressive world. Every creak, whisper, and shadow is meticulously crafted to create a palpable sense of dread and tension. The sound design is equally impressive, amplifying the unsettling ambiance with every step you take.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This game offers a gripping psychological horror experience set in a hauntingly detailed world. With its unsettling atmosphere and immersive storytelling, it pulls you into a tense narrative that keeps you on edge. The eerie environments and chilling moments make for a compelling horror adventure. Ideal for players who enjoy a deep, atmospheric experience with plenty of suspense.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Very good horror game that is driven by a narrative that kept me hooked. was refreshing to play a game where i could slowly figure out what was going on story wise, as i progressed through the game.Game mechanics are pretty basic but they are this way so it doesn't take away from the main focus of the game. I will say that this game can be pretty buggy sometimes. I had to reload checkpoints a fair few times as objectives weren't loading and doors would be shut/locked when they shouldn't be which prevented me from progressing. Overall definitely worth playing if you like horrors narratives
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

Okay story, a little better and more focused than some of these type of games. Ultimately, kind of boring and repetitive, somewhat satisfying while in the house segments. I get why they didn't, as it fleshes out gameplay, pads runtime, adds more scariness and tension to be at war, more varied locale and scenario. But for the story told and all the pomp and circumstance, I pined for the home sections and I guess that was the point. The horror was found at home as well, which translated nicely and was also the point. 5.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: finished it in about 6 hours. got the good ending. will honestly say i thoroughly enjoyed this game. the boss fights were simple, the enemies were all gimicky, but the story was amazing, the ending i got was very pleasing and emotionally compelling. i will say i got this game on sale for $14 and it was worth every penny. personally would not pay full price. but overall a good game and a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Tad bit janky, but overall a fantastic horror game.  8/10Story: 10/10Graphics: 10/10Audio: 7/10Overall Quality: 7/10Pros:* Compelling storyline* its use of high quality textures make for insanely good graphical fidelity* I was scared and creeped out a lotCons:* Unity engine isn't nearly as performant as other engines for this level of graphical fidelity, so I suspect DLSS might be necessary for satisfactory performance with 4k resolution* This could be my configuration, but when I enabled DLSS I noticed that super finely detailed textures (IE the corduroy patterned wallpaper that is present everywhere in the mansion) sometimes "sparkle" when the player pans the view from left to right, and it totally breaks immersion.  Turning off DLSS eliminated the issue for me.  If you need to, reduce your native resolution instead of enabling DLSS if at all possible.* Sometimes I felt like I wasn't hearing the full audio when playing.  Certain cutscenes that introduce monsters have suspenseful music and a creepy background ambience, but the monster doesn't seem to have an audio track at all.  YMMV.QC Issues that could be fixed by the developers:1. Traversal mechanics can potentially break the game:Issue: In the trenches, I found it impossible to traverse through doorways with steps to the threshold when moving forward.  It was impossible to move up stairways, or traverse the apex of the hill after completing the ammunition depot story arc.Impact: it took me 45 minutes of circling the map and returning to the hill 4-5 times before I found that it was a bug, leaving me angry and frustrated that I wasted so much time trying to traverse that hill.  I finally overcame the bug by walking backward up the hill.  Identifying the workaround made it easy to overcome blocked doorways and stairs later on.2. Locked "jail-cell" style doors fly open half-way when clickedIssue: Jail doors seem to glitch out when clicked if they aren't ever meant to be opened at all by the player.  The open half way and it's super glitchy.Impact: Immersion-breaking
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a very well made game, the story isn't too special but has heart and depth to it. The stories told through letter and memories in this game give you a real look into the horrors and insanity of people who went through hell in the war. The gameplay is lacking but there's obvious effort put into it. Not the best horror games I've ever played but it's one I can recommend and place high up there. I'd give it a 7/10 made me feel horrible and spooked but in a good way. Worth about 20-25 dollars
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Anyone who didn't like the game because you had to read and barely encountered anything dangerous, well that was the point. It's a story game not a full fledged horror game. It's story rich with bits and pieces of horror to keep you on your toes. If anyone loves a good story and doesn't despise solving puzzles and piecing stories together, this game is for you. If you're looking for a game like Outlast, this ain't for you. Probably the best psychological horror game I've played in a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Setting, story, sound and visuals are great, but sadly gameplay lacks heavily. After all it's just a glorified walking simulator with your run-of-the-mill "gameplay" elements to make it more interactive or less boring. But most of those gameplay elements utterly fail. A slow walking character that can't run more than a few meters, simple riddles (if you can even call them that) and stupid mechanics like barbed wire cutting. And ultimately none of the horror elements worked for me, so it also lacked atmosphere (I wonder when devs will stop doing scare jumps).
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This is honesty a good game, the story, the fact you can either pick a good or bad ending is a big plus. I loved playing this game so much, knowing nothing going into it other than that this was gonna be a horror game. I was scared honestly ._. those mayhem guys know how to really give ya a heart attack. Just really an amazing game and the good ending made me cry like a little baby honestly. 1000/10 worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I don't typically review games but I immensely enjoyed this game. I've played many story driven psychological horror games and I genuinely feel like this is easily in my top 5 games of that category. This game's story is based around World War I and how it affected many people. The game has very similar aspects to Layers of Fear, in terms of story telling and the build up of suspense. It allows for a more immersive feeling into the game.The graphics are very well done. I didn't have any issues except it had frame rate drops in a few areas. The puzzle's in the game aren't that challenging. The game is forgiving in terms of enemy presence.If you're looking for a powerfully written story game, I highly recommend giving this game a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game. It is very story driven, which I prefer over mindless run and gun games. Graphically it looks great,  every room of the house i wanted to take my time and explore every nook and cranny. The puzzles were simple for the most part and the enemies were not too difficult. This all worked out fine for me as I was more engaged in my surroundings in the game and learning more of the story. Its not perfect but I didn't run into any glitches or bugs, the game played smoothly throughout. It is slower paced, you will find many notes to read, but all of that is to flesh out the story. The WWI setting was great as well. I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a well polished, story driven game with horror elements. If you are looking for jump scares or tons of combat this isn't the game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Story-rich game with interesting setting in World War I. The graphics are superb, the sound/music is amazing. Very interesting enemy design and good voice actors. The puzzles are very simple and although some jumpscares are included, the game is more about the story and the environment than about being scared.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly cannot understand how this game at the moment has "very positive" reviews while so many other deserving games might have "very negative" or "mixed".Anyway, I am really not new to independent games. I liked the vibes the trailer, plot and screenshots were giving so I jumped in and got the game.I really tried to like it but there are so many small things that made me stop. First of all, the sound is not surround (playing on 5.1.2 system) and that really breaks immersion, especially because during the story you had to follow certain sounds and were horribly placed in the game sound design. Other little things like breaking walls, crouching, rattle cans seem to be placed to just make the game slower (longer). Climbing down the ladder at the rat's nest didn't work (I could not leave the ladder). The whole hunger monsters were a chore...not scary, not tense, with a very repetitive sound that became annoying after a few seconds (sound pattern). It's just so many little things that in the end add up and bother.Too bad because I really liked the setting and the voice acting (german) but it felt horribly repetitive, diluted and slow on purpose (slow in a negative sense - because I can love "slow" games).
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I liked the game , most puzzle are simple and enjoyable  and  i felt like main story of this game is understanding every character's  which.. there is lot of reading  but nice thing is some letter find are read to you. i would recommend picking this game up on Sale if you like walking sim and a bit of stealth crouch walking  with puzzle's.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game. A very good game even. But I can totally see why it never took off, and I am surprised why no one during the developement cycle pointed those glaring flaws out. What almost ruined the game for me was the combinaton ofa) level designb) setting the current goalc) sense of progressionAbout any game that does one of these well get's away with it, but Ad Infinitum has:a) confusing and branching level design without clear cluesb) the goals are super abstract - my favourite: find paintings" in a house full random paintingsc) you never really understand why the game wants you to do somethingThe result? You're walking around with a big fat ? on your mind.Beyond this flaw there is a absolutely stellar produced game - the best german voice acting I've ever heard, a gripping and deep story (♥♥♥♥ war) and some absolutely haunting enemies and locations. Also it has one of the most believable and skin crawling sounddesign I've seen.The point that it was about 30 € at release and came along with the design flaw mentioned above I can totally see why this game landed in humble bundle.I give this game a strong thumbs up but beware of the weird level design - you'll walk back and forth a lot! Yet somehow the game gets you back on track again.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This is ultimately another walking simulator but it conveys an interesting story of a family torn apart by World War I, with just enough ambiguity for you to wonder how much is real and how much is the hallucinations of a madman. _childDocuments_.review: Very good horror game where the focus is on the story. That story is particularly good and at times gripping. Written with great respect for the millions of people who lost their lives during World War I. That you view the story from the German point of view is all the more unique. Tip: use German rather than English voice acting to become even more deeply immersed. The puzzles are very doable without being too easy. Only downside is the performance, which is very weak at times. 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't expect too much of it and are okay with that you will have pretty much figured out the plot of the game in the first half an hour, then it's pretty good. An accurate representation of how ww1 effected german soldiers, their families and society at large (or rather how the conditions of said society contributed to the reasons why the war happened.)
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: A great piece of psychological horror focused on the trauma of WW1 that really makes an argument for why games should be considered art and enjoy the status of high culture. It is an accurate historiographic study of the conditions of soldiers during WW1, of the horror of the trenches, of the suffering inflicted on the survivors, as well as the endless threat of being killed or maimed.It is very story-driven, so you must be willing to read a lot of documents and listen to a lot of dialogues between characters. It can feel somewhat slow at times, especially since some of the environments in the trenches are very similar to one another. But I guess that can be considered part of the narrative the game is trying to portray rather than as a flow.Other than that, it has all the typical elements of indie/AA horror games: lots of puzzles, monsters that can kill you, stealth sequences, QTEs, choices that alter the ending (there are three endings available). There is some inspiration from franchises such as Silent Hill, particularly in the themes and some of the design of the environments. Overall, I would say this is the most immersive and referential portrayal of WW1 in video games, in a year that also saw Amnesia: The Bunker release.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible story, visuals that remind me of Amnesia & Outlast, symbolism & more <3My only issue was the glitches that occurred during puzzles for some reason, they made completing puzzles impossible & keys seemed to never get used even though I had them *shrug* A few checkpoint reloads seemed to get things back on track but a fix would've been better.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: While I understand the criticism regarding the repetitive gameplay, I cannot help but be entranced by the visual components as well as the sound design and music. The horrors of the Great War being represented by literal monstrosities is nothing new, however I greatly appreciate that the focus of the story always returned to the devastating effects on the human characters experiencing this horrific period. The ending of the game (good ending) moved me to tears. In my opinion, it was a beautifully arranged drama about an individual’s and a family’s trauma based on one of history’s most horrendous events.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I am a long time horror game enjoyer, I am only through the first chapter of this game and it is hands down the scariest game I have ever played. Based off of the first hour alone I would recommend this game to anyone who enjoys horror games. Play in the dark, headphones on, sound up... and then good luck sleeping later.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic artstyle and sound design, the atmosphere is spot on!!Gameplay is similar to other games of this genre. I think Layers of Fear is a good comparison, - although Ad Infinitum has more engaging puzzles and more actual enemy encounters and bossfights.Difficulty is just right in my opinion: it's never too easy and never too hard. You need to use your head for some of the puzzles, but never to the point were you feel lost without a guide. Enemies are rare and when you are face them, they never get too frustrating, - you might die once or twice, but you figure out very quickly how to deal with them and the checkpoints are usually not too far apart in the sections where you might actually die. That being said, I'd still prefer games of this type to at least have an optional "safe mode", - if SOMA can do it, you can too.All in all this game was an amazing experience and even more so if you are interested in World War 1 and German society, culture and military mindset during the Kaiserreich, - the devs have really done their homework nailing this period in German history!!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is fairly simple, the fighting elements don't need much effort and it's not too hard.  The puzzles are quite fun though I kinda wish there were more of them, I enjoyed the ones that are there a lot. However, where the game shines is the story and music/sounds. The story is told very nicely and you can feel the horrors people went through during WW1. The music is probably underrated and I like it a lot, they put a lot of effort into it as well as all the sounds and I do really appreciate it. I had no issues with it besides a few minor visual glitches and, which's not the devs' fault since it's usually the players who make it, there's no guide for finding collectibles so it bothers me slightly that I can't get all the achievements that easily. Overall a great game worth a try imo
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: IMMERSIVE - 5/5 GreatHORROR-  5/5 GreatMUSIC-  5/5 GreatSOUND/FX-  5/5 GreatVOICE / ACTORS-  5/5 GreatGRAPHICS-  4/5 GoodSTORY-  4/5 GoodEXECUTION-  4/5 GoodQUALITY-  4/5 GoodSUMMARY- Solid horror, psychological game. _childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I am so unbelievably terrified right now and it's great. As someone who scares easily I can't play this for prolonged amounts of time, but Ad Infinitum truly succeeds in terrifying the crap out anyone who plays it in a very clever way. The music, the map, the atmosphere are very well done. Can't wait to finish it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Psychological horror fans, you must experience this game! Incredible monster design, wonderful symbolism, and creative puzzles. I bought this game because of the quality of design both in environments and monsters, but I was not prepared for the impact story that came with it.If you enjoy the thrill of being vulnerable to all things malicious while chasing the truth in a story full of heart, I could easily recommend Ad Infinitum.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I had no prior experience to the game coming into it other than it was set in WW1 and followed the horrors of a recovering German soldier. What the game delivers is way more than that in all levels. It is incredibly gripping and truly keeps you engaged during the entire course of the game's narrative. Some people say that the game feels like a walking simulator with the odd puzzle or scare, but I really do feel like that's what was intended for the game and it sells it even more IMO. It really allows you to feel immersed in the horrors that were the trenches of WW1 and it does this perfectly by just allowing you to explore them in what feels like a hellscape as there is no life present. That gameplay style really allowed me to feel just how mentally draining it would've been for soldiers during the course of the war and really helps you feel for the main character during the story.In short, if you're looking for a traditional horror game (jumpscares, chases, intense action, etc) this isn't the game for you, but if what you're looking for an immersive story into the mind of a soldier after returning home from the trenches and dealing with his experiences (you decide whether he makes peace with his demons or not) then this is the game for you. If you know what style of game this is when coming it, it executes it phenomenally!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game overall. It mixed many different aspects within the horror genre into one game without diving very deep into any one in particular. Don't expect a ton of jumpscares, scary atmosphere, chase scenes, gore, etc, but rather, you will have a mix of it all. The very best parts in my experience were the puzzles, psychological horror bits, and the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely breathtaking horror! A captivating & emotional story with amazing atmosphere & environments. The game is visually stunning. The gameplay itself is very fun & immersive. Ad Infinitum deserves much more recognition than it has. I was blown away during my play through and will definitely revisit the game at some point. My only issue is one fight in particular, with a certain bird guy, was quite frustrating and felt quite clunky, but other than that I cannot recommend this game enough. Its beautiful in a tragic, spooky way!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I would like to thank the developers and creators for making an excellent, one of the best, narrative stories about very real human experiences. To anyone that ends up reading this review. This is a journey into the soul of humanity if you let it be. It has some excellent suspense and isn't trying to hard to trick you. It just wants you to feel and understand. 10/10 Would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played the first 2 hours of the game so far but honestly have got to say that i reckon it's awesome so far for a horror game. Jump scares, but definitely separated enough in a creepy enough environment to go from whoa! to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!!! I particularly liked the way the game points out the effects of the war on not only the individual but the family and the relationships. The music also does a terrific job of enforcing the environment and maintaining the creepy vibes without sounding out of place. If i got this from two hours worth of gameplay I'd love to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This game isn't quite what I thought it was going to end up being but I did truly enjoy it.Pros:- The overall story was very good, and dealt with the topic of the war well.- There was more then one way to kill each boss- The beast design was so great, even the pancake lady (You'll understand when you meet her)Cons:- The story relies a bit too much on found documents and not all are voiced- The puzzles can feel almost a little too simple for my liking (But I love horror puzzles so I know I'm picky)- Some of the choices can feel a bit too simplified and would have loved a bit less obvious good or bad choices.I think it's a super solid game, even though it has a short run time I'm already tempted to replay and get one of the alternate endings. I think that while this game is good, this studio has the potential to make some of the greatest horror games of our time if they keep this trajectory. I give it 4/5 dysfunctional family members.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Great psychological horror/walking sim. Story, ambiance, environment, spookiness, music, theme, everything is there. Runs pretty well and its super pretty. Also great to shine a light on WW1 as its often overshadowed, and shows a German soldier as a human being and not just a savage monster.Has a few classic frustrations of the genre - unclear puzzles/navigation, enemies that you are helpless against, but overall I recommend strongly.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I loved my time with this game. I'll admit, it did kinda start off slow, but once all the pieces begin to fall together the story and gameplay ramp up more and more until the end. The story, sound design, and atmosphere are subpar, and this has some of the most tense and horrifying moments I've ever had in a video game. I HIGHLY recommend this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fell in love with this game, only abit into it but I'm so blown away!The story gets you hooked straight away, and the puzzles are just the right amount of challenging without breaking immersion Definitely recommend this game highly, even to those who wouldn't be massive horror fans just to enjoy the story alone
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I don't often make reviews for games on steam. However for this game I feel like I have to. The first trailer came out in 2015. I had it in the back of my mine for 8 years. Last week I saw it out and bought it as soon as I saw it. I am gonna get the stuff y'all care about out of the way first. The game play is fun, puzzles are not to hard but some require you to think, the soundtrack IS AMAZING, the monster design is really cool and reminds me a built of Silent Hill, and story is outstanding. Now I want to talk about this game on a personal level. This game means a lot to me. I served in the U.S Army and was sent to the middle east and came back home with trauma and scars. Not many games really touched on the family aspect of that. When I got home my mom said I did not seem right and lost a lot of my cheeriness. For awhile it was hard to maintain friendships and relationships. Over the course of time I learned to regain my hope, personality, and love back. These are aspects of PTSD that this game touches on. This game may be about a war over 100 years ago but the message is still the same all these years later. I look forward to coming back to play this game again later when I want to 100% it. Until then I recommend this game and want to thank Hekate for making this game and writing a story that means a lot to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Ad Infinitum was definitely an experience and story that I wasn't expecting! This game did a great job at bringing this story to life and showing the trauma that affected the entire family, not just our character! I expected a game that just brought some good jumpscares and scary beings that we will encounter which there are still moments like that in this game, but there is so much more! I really enjoyed the depth you can explore into this game! Worth giving a try if you're looking for a game that goes beyond just some jumpscares and a bit of story to it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Bloody, horrifying & bone-chilling.Ad Infinitum is an exploration/story-telling game with horror elements and enemies you will have to avoid, as well as puzzles you need to solve. It takes place during World War I, and even though it's one of those games i'd call a walking simulator (You walk around a lot and just take in the scenery), it wasn't that bad. It plays similarly to Amnesia: The Bunker.Game length is about 5 hours if you're taking your time and count in a few restarts/deaths on the way.It has some interesting boss designs and overall I had a fun experience playing this through and i'd recommend it for any horror game fans out there.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game quite a bit.  It's quite clear from the beginning that it will be speaking to the horrors of war, and what affect it has on the young soldiers who had to fight.  I also greatly appreciated the empathy we "allied" nation gamers are made to feel towards German soldiers - who, much like so many armies, don't particularly want to be there, or to hurt anybody.  There is a particular note left by a soldier that mentions how it was common practice upon command to fire for soldiers to intentionally miss, which is a true historical fact I very much appreciated.The best way for me to describe this game is a cross between the Amnesia series, and "In Sound Mind."  Considering the games, it should be no surprise that this is meant as a compliment.  Truly, at its core, this is a game about understanding people, empathizing, and forgiving.  Don't get me wrong, the horror is there, and there are parts that are truly chilling, but the heart is strong with this one too.You've also heard me complain about scores in other games before - but good lord not with this one.  What an astounding score - perfectly thought provoking, eloquently written, and the serious but inspiring tone this game needed.  As for the rest of the sound, the design is great, but I do feel like there were a few moments when I found myself frustrated by a stereo mix rather than binaural.  A phone would ring that sounded right next to me, but after searching for a few minutes, I'd realize that it was a floor above me, with no dampening, or subtle changes to the acoustics to indicate as much.  There were several moments like this, and while they didn't ruin my experience even by a long shot, it was still something that took me out of the experience.Now, speaking of taking me out of the experience, as of now, the game REQUIRES you to use subtitles if you want to also be able to read the contextual (eyeball icon) information that our character thinks about objects.  In my opinion, that the two are tied together is absolutely absurd.  I hate subtitles in games (immersion breaking) but naturally, if you want to use them, use them.  But to pair the two very separate game mechanics together like that is just silly.  I kept hoping for a patch that would separate the two, but when it didn't come, I bit the bullet and played with subtitles.  I would have enjoyed this game 10x more without them.  I hope the devs make this change for future players.All in all, though, a great game with some thought-provoking things to say.  Exactly what I'm looking for out of an adult horror game!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: I really like it, but the only problems I have had are:Can't walk over 1 inch floor board, have to look to the side.Animation not working properly.Music way too loud had to turn it down to (30%).I do really like it, the story is interesting but sometimes it is very difficult to know what your doing, so maybe include a map and a better hint system.But in any other way its great loving it so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Is it the best designed game? Not at all. It plays like a game from 2010 and has a myriad of glitches. Is there a really good message in it? Yeah. I feel like it's often overlooked just how awful WW1 was and the psychological and physical damage it did to people. Does this game show that well? I think it did at least
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: This horror game delivers a spine-tingling experience with its intense atmosphere, cinematic soundtrack, and clever use of lighting. The detailed monsters and heart-wrenching story make it a must-play for any horror fan who's ready to dive in. Yes, it could be mistaken for a "walking simulator," but that would totally miss the point of the game, which aims to immerse you in the horrific traumas of war. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Personally, I love this game.The atmosphere is great, and the story, although hard to wrap your head around, is by the end of the game somewhat easy to understand witch is very good for games of this genre. The graphics are amazing (I can’t say much because I had to have my graphics at a minimum setting to run at a decent frame rate, so take that with a grain of salt). The symbolism is spectacular, as well as the art behind the symbolism like the body horror. Overall it’s a great game if your looking for a fun, single-player physiological horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Insane visuals, impressively creative monster designs, great voice acting.I can tell it got some inspirations from the Amnesia series, which is a good choice, but even so, this game has its very own charm and style to it.Personally, these kinds of games aren't really my thing but I wanted to try this one, since Bunker hooked me.I encountered some bugs along the way, nothing game breaking, but I'll write them down :- The first time we enter the sort of.. dorms in the trenches? Like a sort of lobby or something, the metal doors that are supposed to be locked open anyway, but luckily invisible walls prevent us from entering any of the rooms, and one of these rooms have.. 2 metal doors inside each other?- When we get the rifle given by the Officer on our first encounter with Pain, I somehow got my rifle animations to bug out, when I was aiming, the animation wasn't playing, even the muzzle flash was a little messed up, maybe due to the flashlight still being usable?- The cutscene before fighting the final boss, I don't think it is intentional but there seems to be missing sounds?I think these are the only ones I encountered, but still. it's a great experience that I'd recommend, the story is truly impacting when you realize what's been going on.
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Now that I finished the game, I want to give my FULL opinion on Ad Infinitum:I thoroughly love this game! At the beginning, I was interested in it because of the WW1 aspect. I am a WW1 buff, so this game piqued my interest back when it was first being developed. While that's what got me to purchase this game, the story and soundtrack made me fully engrossed. All the characters were extremely interesting! Reading, listening, and watching the family drama unfold had me itching to delve more into their minds. What really sticks out, in comparison to most horror games and movies, is that I REALLY CARED for all the family members in Ad Infinitum. They weren't vessels to move the story along, and I really appreciate that. (Also, change the voice language to German. While the English VA's did a great job, I felt that the British accents made me lose immersion. It also syncs better to the lip movement)The soundtrack is incredible; especially for an indie title. It's not always "creepy horror music". Instead the score gave me feelings of whimsical adventure and bombastic power! I'm so glad I downloaded it so I can listen to the tracks of the boss battles.Ad Infinitum is really pretty and grotesque in all the right places. There was a lot of detail in the mansion, trenches, and monsters. Even though I had a few stutters around the flames, it never broke the immersion. Gameplay was ok. Basically Layers of Fear or Amnesia. Most puzzles were good, but there were 1 or 2 that were a bit ridiculous to find the answers. Exploring the mansion and the trenches was fun.  Spooky factor was just my cup of tea. Since I don't get scared that easily, I'm glad the developers went head-on in making me feel tense and creeped-out, instead of relying on jumpscares. While there are jumpscares, there are only a few of them. Yes, they did get me.  Overall, I'm pleasantly surprised in the direction Ad Infinitum went. Good ending left me very satisfied. Great work!8.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Ad Infinitum

_childDocuments_.review: Ad Infinitum is a first-person survival horror game with a focus on atmosphere and story. Experience the great war from the perspective of a German soldier. In this surreal war-torn nightmare, you must overcome pain, despair and corruption while fighting for your life and sanity. Can you escape the horrors of war?

name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends
detailed_description: MAKE SUSHI, MAKE FRIENDS As a state-of-the-art Sushi Bot, you’ve always dreamed of becoming a world-renowned chef and making your creators proud. As luck would have it, the friendly residents of Rolling Hills are looking for a rising star to take over the local sushi shop—presenting a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity for a one-of-a-kind robot to show the world what you’re made of. Build your recipe repertoire, purchase the perfect ingredients, and help turn a cozy town into a can’t-miss culinary destination in Rolling Hills, a wholesome blend of life sim and restaurant management game about serving up life’s simple pleasures. Let’s roll! Make Irresistible Sushi Collect new recipes to suit the townfolks’ tastes, source fresh ingredients from the local market to improve your creations’ flavor and quality, and become a master sushi chef. Make Fabulous New Friends Build relationships with the residents of Rolling Hills over a cup of coffee, and help them with their own day-to-day needs. Together, you can make life better for everyone in town! Make Your Restaurant Dreams Come True Dive into the hustle and bustle as you serve customers to earn coins and stellar reviews. Customize your restaurant with decorations that grant bonuses and express your style.

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to VERY CAUTIOUSLY recommend this game.For starters, it is very cute ^_^ love his little robot face, the art style and the upbeat music. It has enjoyable concepts like buying decorations, ingredients and side quests. Runs very smoothly, polished in that regard. Story seems a bit predictable but I am willing to see where it goes.Now for the parts that make me CAUTIOUS to recommend...The game so far seems ridiculously easy. To the point where during the active restaurant service time, I am often sitting around doing nothing. Adding to this...I was very surprised to learn that you are not actively involved in making sushi. You simply press a button and the dishes appear on a conveyor belt to be served. The customer movement is painfully slow and that includes ordering, adding to the boredom. So while it is not that I dislike it, I was just hoping for a bit more of a cozy challenge. Almost seems childlike and brainless in its approach. I think it is important to be aware that there is no cooking or meal prep in this game. You just buy special ingredients to add perks and level up dishes you unlock. Still going to play it and see where it goes. Hoping for more variety in the restaurant management end as the game and story progresses. Give it a shot if you enjoy sushi. I am learning a lot about different varieties and the descriptions are helpful and creative.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I feel awful for saying this, but the game is really boring.The map is disappointingly small, and the NPCs barely have anything interesting to say. My main reason for not recommending the game is the actual sushi preparation part. All you do is wait for customers to slowly walk to a table, pick up the sushi from the conveyor belt, and serve them the correct dish. That’s it. I was under the impression that the game would introduce more engaging elements, but after roughly 10 minutes, you've seen everything it has to offer.I also felt a little misled by the "Make sushi, make friends" slogan, as you aren't really making sushi, and as for friends, even after serving the same person several times, your relationship with them never seems to increase or improve, making things feel meaningless.I also felt that the fisherman at the beginning was unnecessarily rude. After I mentioned that I would make sushi for friends, he rudly told me to just do my job, which is just rude.Overall, the game feels too shallow for the asking price of £13. The gameplay loop consists of buying furniture and ingredients, and moving left and right along a conveyor belt. None of the characters were particularly compelling. I was hoping for elements like farming, more customisation options, and mini-quests, but sadly, there’s none of that. Spending 10 minutes waiting for the NPCs to sit down became tedious very quickly.

_childDocuments_.review: If there's one thing I hate, it's seeing negative reviews from people who haven't even invested an hour in playing a game. This game is the work of a small studio, created by two brothers. While I understand it might not be to everyone's taste, the least we can do is give it a fair chance before leaving a negative review after less than half an hour of gameplay.Yes, it is slightly boring at the start, and you do spend a lot of time waiting around. However, I'm now at a stage where I sometimes struggle to keep up with the need of my customers Anyway, here's my personal take after over 10 hours of playing.Overall, it's a great little game to kill time while having fun (and it has a ton of potential for future updates and improvements). The devs have been very responsive to the players and have already released a patch to address and fix some issues.
