_childDocuments_.review: In  you play as a friendly robot chef who makes friends while making sushi in the little town of Rolling Hills! You are a state-of-the-art Sushi Bot and you dream of becoming the next Jiro Ono in the robot world! You move into Rolling Hills and take over a sushi shop. Build your shop as you build friendships in this mashup of life sim meets time management. The tutorial is great and gets you familiar fast with the game mechanics which are pretty easy to learn. As you level up you gain new recipes and money you can use to purchase new items and upgrades. Also you can collect adorable hats for your Robot to wear. I do find the furniture a tad on the expensive side to be honest. There is a lot to spend your hard earned cash on and none of it is cheap (except the odd ingredient to upgrade your recipes). So the game does have that element of grind to it. * Treat the residents to coffee to level them up (at $100 an outing they have expensive taste)! * This game is best played with a controller.* Pick up cans to recycle them (gets you a bit of cash and eventually an achievement). * Look around, every now and then a present will spawn  This game is vibrant, fun and wholesome. A game everyone can play. Yes there is some grind to it and it will take some time to earn all 51 recipes and upgrade them. But the gameplay is never too overwhelming when it comes to the time management portion. The game does not have a difficulty setting and is best played with a controller.Despite having a lot of fun with the game I am also now craving sushi…🍙
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Will I keep playing it? Yes. Do I recommend it? No. As a lover of sushi, robots, restaurant sims, and time management games, I was VERY excited for this. So much so that my cheap a$$ paid full price for it. Sadly, it did not live up to my expectations.***Mild spoilers ahead for game play mechanics and progression***The game is really simple. Too simple. I love a cozy game and I don't need things to be overly complex or difficult, but there are times when you play something that feels like a mobile game because nothing really matters - that's this game. And for how simple it is, it isn't very polished. The robot that you play is too big for the space they put you in and has a hard time navigating around tables. Serving is sketchy - sometimes it doesn't take and it's often hard to select the right at a table person to serve when you're trying to hurry.As you progress you gain more and more recipes but you can't manage your menu so you have to serve ALL the recipes you've unlocked, which mean you have to continue to serve weak recipes that drag you down. The recipes are made randomly, five at a time, by a machine and there's no strategy really in what you serve - you can just hit "reload" on the machine once it's recharged, which happens pretty quickly, to conjure up a new random batch of food. When I saw the recipe types had different colors, I got excited thinking that maybe there would be a Diner Dash style mechanic to, say, using the same color dishes to gain bonuses. But no. People sit, they order three random items, they leave. That's it. There's dirty table and customers falling asleep mechanics to add a bit of challenge, but these are just annoying. You buy ingredients to upgrade your recipes. but the ingredients just level up the recipes which sometimes improves the quality and special feature of a dish, if it has one, but doesn't change the dish in interesting ways. It doesn't even seem to add more to the price of the dish. You are forced to level up dishes to keep up with the quality-demand of the customers, which is where having to continue to serve low-quality dishes is a huge pain. I don't want to spend the time to grind to gain money to buy ingredients to level up these sucky dishes. It just adds unnecessary time to the game.Everything you do in the game is a very similar sort of grind. Everything costs money so you just have to keep playing day after day to get things that don't feel satisfying or make an impact on the gameplay.Anyway, I'm a hypocrite because this caught me in a brainless mood after work and so I just kept playing. I went back and forth with myself if I should return it and wait for it to go on sale and I really should have but I said eff it and kept playing, knowing that I was not getting a good value for my dollar. I'm not trying to be harsh but I don't understand why it's so hard to find decent games in this genre. Again, the original Diner Dash came out like a million years ago and it was awesome. So simple yet so addictive and satisfying. I feel like people spend a lot of time making something cute so people will buy it and no time making it actually fun or thoughtful. I would happily pay $25 for the game I thought I was getting, if someone would just make that game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a cute, cozy game with a good challenge to it. There is a lot that makes this cute and fun, but I'm hoping some quality of life updates happen. Based on the pictures it does look like you get to change the look of your restaurant eventually, so I'm looking forward to that. That being said, some changes that could improve gameplay include: - Your sushi bar refilling after you completely empty it instead of having to manually do that- Upgrading your bot to move faster - the dash action is nice but an extra step instead of a base movement speed increase.- Upgrading your sushi bar to show you what colors are coming next- Upgrading your sushi bar to hold more dishes- A minimap to show where things are- Being able to upgrade multiple times with the same veggie if you have more than one.- A timer or daytime cycle to show how close you are to closing would be great. As it is right now there is no way to tell the passage of time so you're guessing how close you are.It is very frustrating that when you stand still for half a second, your challenges and tasks pop up and the only way to get rid of them is to move. I don't need them popping up every time I'm waiting for customers.It would be nice to either be able to hide them or at least make the boxes behind them more see-through so they're not taking up almost a quarter of my screen for no reason.Overall this game is currently 3/5 very fun and enjoyable, I do recommend this game and will tell friends about it, but a few things could be improved to make it so much better.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this charming game and recommend it. It took me around eleven hours to complete the story, and I have one pesky achievement left which may take some time.Within the first two hours or so, I was debating putting it down as I wasn't as engaged as I'd have expected to be in a restaurant simulator game. However, I highly encourage continuing on if you feel this; different mechanics are added with progression, alongside friendship bonuses etc, which I felt provided some interesting changes to the main game loop. The side quests also progressed into something I actively looked forward to completing, rather than something to get through just to progress. I found myself getting hooked on it the more I played! Something that was somewhat off-putting to me was that characters are almost cookie-cutter with very surface-level personality traits. With time, however, I found myself enjoying learning a bit more about their qualms and dreams. Where the game lacks strong character development or writing, it sure does make up for it with charm! The ending was very sweet, also.A lovely game that's well-worth a full play through. Now I need to go and sort out my sushi craving!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: 17 hours 1/10 1 You don't need a guide No No Yes, getting all the recipes requires you to get to restaurant level 20, which is a grind No No No No No difficulty settings but you can't fail, the game is very forgiving NoWhat an adorable main character and what a beautiful game! Rolling Hills is a game in which you run a restaurant. I want to make it clear that it is not a cooking game, there is no cooking involved. It is mostly a time management game where you have to bring the customer the right order. In your restaurant, there is this machine that makes the sushi automatically, and you have to deliver the food to the customer. There are 4 color types and they have a level as well, the customer wants the right color and a specific level or higher. If the right one isn't on the conveyor belt, then you can refresh the section that is available on the conveyor belt. There is a short period between the possibility to refresh, but if you upgrade your recipes, you'll be able to find the right sushi dish within the current section or the refreshed section 99% of the time. Between sessions of serving customers, you can run around in Rolling Hills, which is a small town. The better your restaurant gets the more people move to this small town. This also means that if you have space in your restaurant for them to sit, more customers will come to visit your restaurant as well. You will befriend a few and with how better you know them the more positive effects it has on your restaurant. For example, if you befriend the man of the grocery store, the more luxurious items he will have in stock, which will help you upgrade the recipes faster. One of the things that will help out a lot is the store where they sell furniture. The furniture will have different effects, for example, there is an effect that will give you money for every customer that enters your store, and another that will give you restaurant experience, but there is also an effect for customers to be more patient. Of every effect there is, there is also a "super" variant which is just better than the regular one. With those items, you can customize your playstyle.What I loved the most is that the game gave daily challenges. You can ignore them but they give points for which you can buy extra recipes and hats. Most of them are quite easy to do, so it doesn't take much time but helps you out in the long run. I thought this was an awesome addition to spice things up a little bit. The only thing I struggled with was if 2 customers sat at the same table, sometimes I gave the food to the wrong person while trying to give it to the right person. I know the devs are looking into making it more clear which customer you've highlighted, but what worked for me right now is standing behind the customer and then giving the food. Not intuitive but it worked like a charm.  A small thing I didn't notice until the dev pointed it out is that the achievements give bonuses, but to get those you have to go to the achievement menu in the game and click on the unlocked achievements. I only learned about this after missing a few recipes while very close to the maximum restaurant level. About the achievements, Rolling Hills has no missable achievements. most of them you just unlock for playing the game. I recommend picking up every soda can you find, but maybe wait with the recycling part until you have the daily challenge for doing so.  There is an achievement for recycling 100 soda cans, but you'll find those easily if you just pick them up while doing the rest. Another thing to keep in mind is that you want to get every friendship to level 5 but if you get more experience than is needed for the current level, that experience is lost. So for level 1 you need 100 exp and for level 2 200, level 3 300 and so on. The amount of gold the activity costs is the amount of experience it gives. So you can plan the right activities to not waste money. The achievement that will take the longest is getting all the recipes. You get a lot by just playing and befriending the people in Rolling Hills. There will also be a few available by the NPC that tell you about challenges a little later on in the game. The traveling merchant also has a bunch of recipes as well, so make sure you keep a bit of money for when she is in town to be able to buy a recipe. For this achievement, I would highly highly recommend stacking up on furniture with the charming stats, or even better the super charming stat, so you already get a bunch of exp for them to walk into the restaurant. For the last 2 hours, I just opened up my restaurant and let people in but didn't serve them, with quite a lot of tables but otherwise just a bunch of furniture with the charming stats. I didn't serve them so that the little helpers would just keep fiddling with the items that gave charming and keep giving a bunch of experience that way. I'm unsure if this was the fastest way to do it, but it was the most effortless way for sure. I did this on my Steam Deck because on PC it has to be the active screen for the game to run. A really helpful thing for this strategy is that the music chances if the day ends, so I grinded the last 2,5 levels this way while doing some work on my pc. I give Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends 4 out of 5 stars.

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute game with cute decor, I would hesitantly compare this game to a Delicious game without the point and click aspect. _childDocuments_.review: I pretty much never leave reviews for a game, but for this one, I think I could offer some suggestions that could really contribute to the game if considered; it sorely needs it.I went into this game with no expectations outside of something cute and casual, so there weren’t any assumptions about what the gameplay experience would be outside of that. Unfortunately, the game-loop is painfully boring. It’s as if someone took Diner Dash and stretched out the core mechanics with an experience bar that was FFXIV levels of brutal level 15+. Initially, the game-loop feels pretty satisfying. Serve customers, decorate your little restaurant, talk to the people, get ingredients, admire the look of the sushi recipes and how cute/colorful they are… and then you realize you’re looping the same thing over and over and over and over again meting out progress at a snail’s pace. The end-game is the exact same as the game before the ending, except worse in the fact that, without any cutscenes or sidequests of any nature, you are expected to do nothing but grind experience (and I mean a TON of experience) in order to get those levels for the all recipes learned achievement.The NPCs don’t have much character and are entirely forgettable, but I wasn’t expecting anything super intense or emotionally moving in a game like this, so I think this is about the expectation. Just cute little interactions and nothing more, and that’s just fine.Something that would make the overall game a little less painful would be the following:1)	Add a dialogue to Arman’s menu that allows you to buy the entire stock at one time. Please. It would be so nice.2)	Add a way to buy the mysterious potions that add a level of quality to your sushi. There is no way to get these outside of the painful RNG of Coggie’s fishing. Maybe convert Min’s shop into something that sells the potions (and maybe ingredients too?) so that the challenge points don’t just accumulate into the thousands since there is literally nothing to do with them after you buy out the shop.3)	Add the option to Wren to switch out the furniture. It would be a blessing, especially when you have more money than you know what to do with.4)	Add a sort feature to the décor. Right now, I have no idea how it’s sorted and it’s a cluttered mess trying to sort through it. It feels like there’s no rhyme or reason to it at all. A sort filter would be even better; sort by Relaxing, Charming, Profitable, etc.5)	Add a visible grid to the restaurant that you can toggle on or off if you want to when placing décor. Please. I just want to set things parallel to each other, but eyeballing that is a huge pain.6)	Please, please, please add a hat that is the imitation crab. The fact that there isn’t one is baffling.7)	Before the shift starts, be able to assign the little helper robots to cleaning a particular type of décor to focus on—again, Relaxing, Charming, Profitable, etc. I have so much money that Sushi-Bot could buy Rolling Hills twice over, but those little helpers just keep polishing away at the Profitable décor. I’d put more Charming décor in the restaurant, but Wren seems to refuse to sell any of it to me. If only I could have her rotate her selection…I think adding in even just a few of those suggestions would help the tedium that the game becomes. Grinding all the way to level 20 is just painful and the only reason that I’m doing so is to get the whole $15 bucks worth out of this game.I only recommend this game if you’ve got a Steam Deck and you use it as a way to waste time between travel. It’s just too boring for long-term play. It will be a relief to finish this game and never pick it up again.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy the game so far for what it is, and while some people might not like the braindead aspect, I can appreciate it personally. It's cute, cozy and an all around decent game to play when you don't have much energy and just want to relax without thinking too hard. I am looking forward to seeing where this game goes from here, but for now it's basically exactly what I was hoping for in a cozy game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Sorry to say, but I don't think it is fun. You are not "making sushi". There is no cooking. The food literally comes out of a machine on a conveyor belt and you just serve it to the customer 3 meters away. What's the point? Your role is just squeezed in. Why even take orders? You know there are actual sushi restaurants where the guests just take what they want. If it was more complex than you would have a purpose. The fact that it's sushi or that you are a robot is incidental and interchangable. And the upgrade system makes no sense. When you add more ingridients to something, it changes the recipe, not get better. And you are not making friends from what I can tell. There are contacts that involve themselves into your business, which is pretty much completely premade. The guests have no names and say the same stuff over and over. It may look nice, but it feels very empty and uninspired.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Its nice being a robot and serving sushi to random people even if the gameplay loop can be a little repetitive in between the story. Later on you get a little robot that supposed to help cleaning tables but it feels very bad cause it is very slow and running around randomly and only help if its near a dirty table. The game is worth its price.Edit: The helper robot feel fine now after last update. Still sometimes wanders around were you dont have any tables but thats a just a very small thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I'm actually addicted to this game. It's a mix of Overcooked (in terms of serving customers fast) and Animal Crossing (going around town, buying things, upgrading, decorating shop). It's a simple story and simple game play but it's charming in its own way. I recommend it if you like more chill, simple games with only a bit of challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Humble Games sent me a review code for . The full review is , but here is an excerpt: "Truthfully, the gameplay in  is exceedingly simple, but that’s kind of nice. However, it’s also the game’s primary flaw. It can get a little boring to repeatedly complete daily tasks and serve sushi as you try to rank up to get more story, which is ostensibly the goal of the game. I played  for much longer than I expected, not because I had a difficult time managing my resources or time, but because the popularity goals increase fast and the progression rate remains relatively slow." is a complete game, which is more than can be said of many new releases in the live-update era. It’s short and sweet and has its lulls, but it also has a lovely story and beautiful art. Sushibot is adorable and his movements are reflective of his design as a one-wheeled, square robot designed to serve sushi. The townspeople and visitors in Rolling Hills represent a range of skin tones, hair types, styles, and interests. Unfortunately, there’s no body diversity aside from the non-human characters, which is disappointing. The art style is so cute and I’d love to see more body types represented in it."The actual sushi is also stunning. Each roll or dish is unique and detailed, ranging from realistic sushi that immediately makes me crave inari, to silly, gamified sushi with playful elements like UFOs, rice cows, and clown rolls with magical properties. ... Although the map of  is small, I actually prefer it that way. The tight focus of the game clearly allowed for more creativity and detail work, which makes it feel worth playing even when the story stalls out a little bit. I love the bright colors, the array of quests, the collecting aspect, the medium-paced restaurant management. Getting lost here feels lovely in the moment, and as such, I'm genuinely pleased with my overall experience in . Other cozy games could take a page from its book, pare down, and focus on beautiful art with a solid story centered in a relatively small area rather than trying to sprawl when they don’t need to."
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Giving this a tentative yes. Buy it on a deep discount and accept that you'll have a mindless time. Otherwise, buy another game. There's no cooking involved, and you're serving dishes to the guests. I love the customization options in this game, and I believe that's the best part about this game. Since the game is so easy though, I don't feel any incentive to reach the end as the relationships are all superficial and to continue upgrading my ingredients. For that reason, my journey ends here with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best games ever made. It is absolutely the best restaurant manager I have found. Anything I disliked about the gameplay, which was not much, got fixed along the way. The design nails it, going on retro-futurism. There is advanced technology, but it's rounded, cute and seems like the type to go 'kerrr-chunk' - great. The robot also feels very smooth when moving, which is difficult to get right. THE NUMBER OF TABLES DOES NOT MATTER! Only place as many as you can manage at once, it does not affect how many customers come in.THE DAYS ARE NOT COUNTED! You can take your time. The seasons do change, but only the grass color is affected.The other characters are also charming and have their own personality and short quests. Friendship is advanced through coffee dates. What I like most about this game is that it is straightforward. It succeeds at being a cozy game by holding your hand, arguably the only genre of game where this is a good thing. The soda can collection, for example, is done organically, I was done with it well before the end. There are no other mandatory collectibles. You can collect costumes and honks, but they are not tracked and involve a weird kind of gameplay you encounter only there, which I stayed away from. The recipes are all unlocked through regular progression - yes, even the challenge ones, I had more points than I had things to buy without giving a thought to the challenges.The gameplay loop makes the grind feel like it's not even there, though the reputation for the last 5 levels could stand to go a bit faster and the option to hide the challenges once there are no rewards left to buy would be welcome. OVERALL, a fantastic game, absolutely give it a roll!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This has become one of my absolute favorite cozy games! I’ve been stuck on it since the release and for the price you can not beat it. The game allows you to go at your own pace while still having a story line with tasks to complete. The graphics are amazingly adorable and runs perfect on my steam deck. I really hope they bring updates or DLC to the game but regardless it has a high replay ability to me.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends was an experience that worked really well for a Steam Deck game/game to mindlessly play to kill time. It is very much a cozy game in which you build a town reputation as you grow your restaurant; as you get busier, the furniture you buy works as buffs for your shop. Overall, a really fun game, even though getting to level 20 for the last achievement was a little tedious. Solid 7/10 game!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This is a vary charming game, I found myself wanting to play more as soon as I put it down. From the lovely characters that help you along your journey to the actual way you run your restaurant I found this game relaxing and chill. I was never stressed while serving customers and loved being able to customize my restaurant and purchase ingredients to upgrade my recipe quality. I recommend this game if you enjoy life sim / management games.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: So much fun, I'm addicted to making sushi. Just wish there was a timer to let me know when the day was over/how many customers were left in the day. Just beat the game, I wish there was more to it. I beat it in 10hrs. I don't think the replay value is good enough to start over again. The story won't change.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: So far enjoying the game, you can tell it is was created with passion. A fantastic game for relaxing and serving us some delicious sushi to the cute townspeople. Highly recommend to anyone looking for a peaceful, laid back sushi restaurant sim game. Not as fast paced as say, Overcooked, but the game offers unique challenges, like avoiding flashes from cameras, waking patrons and cleaning messes. Seems to have a decent variety of both sushi recipes and decorations that offer the ability to create the perfect custom small town sushi shop with the atmosphere that is just right for your robot chef!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fairly casual game. It's fun to play and I think it's worth the price paid, but there's not much substance to it. You don't actually make the sushi, you hit a button and random sushi rolls out for you to serve. There's a simple puzzle aspect to it -- you have to match the quality and the flavor to the customer -- but that's about it. As for making friends, the social aspect is limited to cafe dates. You level up your friendship and get items or skills that help you become a better restaurant owner. I'd give it a solid 7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Rolling Hills is adorable. You play as a robot called Sushi Bot and run a restaurant serving sushi to people in town. As the story progresses, you unlock more recipes, townsfolk, furniture, and customer types. The story is simple, but interesting. And the gameplay is a more relaxing version of Overcooked, Plateup!, Coffee Caravan and Cuisineer. You just roll around on your robot wheel and serve people. It's pretty fun and easy to get into the flow of things. Not to mention, I love customizing my little restaurant. My dream of having an entire room filled with vending machines and gachapon has been fulfilled. There are some UX issues such as the tasks keep popping up on the right side of the screen randomly, and some bugs such as the crab daily challenge not being completed when you find the crab. However, those are pretty minor and doesn't block progression or gameplay so I can ignore them.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I've now played this game for over 10 hours and I love it! It's cozy and wholesome, as expected, but contrary to  a couple of reviewer opinions, there is a ton of hidden depth and an addictive gameplay loop if you love upgrading games.Some of the depth I'm talking about *being vague to avoid spoilers...• You can upgrade recipes with special effects tailored to your play style by buying specific ingredients.• You can buy furniture with special effects and decorate your restaurant with items that boost the numbers you want to increase (XP, money, etc.)• Making friends gives you upgrades too. More on this below.• These upgradables are available from the start of the game for you to discover and experiment with.The difficulty ramps up and you can influence it too...• As the game progresses it gets more difficult to keep customers satisfied.• The customers have hidden stats that make each one unique if you want to dig that deep.• Customizing with the right decor and upgrading the right recipes let's you take it easy or set up services to yield more rewards at the risk of having more dissatisfied customers.Making friends...• I don't want to spoil it, but each character has their own story and you see the resolution of each story as you max out your friendships.• You'll also get EXTREMELY valuable upgrades for increasing friendships and you have to strategically choose friends that will give you the upgrades you want.• As the game story progresses, you'll have opportunities to meet new friends with new story lines and new upgrades.Branching gameplay...• As the game progresses you will have to choose what you want to pursue. Advancing the game story, making your restaurant more profitable, advancing friend stories, getting upgrades, and even little micro tasks like collecting trash and finding fishing spots.A lot of stuff is packed into this game and the fact that it seems simple on the surface is part of its genius...• There are a lot of fun easter eggs: references to famous characters, other games and even other game genres• As the story progresses you get surprising new abilities that give you even more gameplay options.I hope this review is helpful. I've had a hard time putting my controller down while playing Rolling Hills. It really has that just-one-more-game aspect down. I'm also 10+ hours in and haven't finished it. A real accomplishment for a two person development team.If you're on the fence about buying it, just do it. It's well worth the price. GREAT game!!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Have to leave a review because it’s launch day and it by far exceeded my expectations. It says it’s from a two man dev team and I’m seriously impressed at the labor of love that went into this game. It’s seriously one of the cutest games I’ve ever played and once I started I didn’t want to put it down. I don’t eat seafood or sushi but I wanted to try it because it still looked fun and I was right in doing so because I’ve had a blast playing this cute game. It’s not even a cooking game which I thought it was but it’s more like a serving game with decorating upgrading quests and friendships. The game deserves more recognition as it seems to have flew under the radar by a lot of people but if you need a sign to try this game this is it. It’s a fantastic cozy game that is wildly addicting and you will have a ton of fun playing it if you like this genre of game.I also will add that I played it on my Steam Deck and it plays better than any other game I’ve tried on Steam deck. Like it was seriously made for it. (It will work fine on regular pc too but a lot of games just don’t work that well on steam deck it feels clunky but this was perfect for it.) Overall 10/10 I can’t wait to see future updates for the game. Need pink robot customization too.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Im a little robot rolling around serving sushi, what more could I want?The animations are great (im in love with Sushi Bot's idle animation), the art is great, the story and the characters are a lot of fun.The game play is repetitive but I enjoy that (and ive lost hours to this, looking at the clock going wow its been 3 hours where did the time go.)The decorations are adorable, I love that we can edit based on what we are trying to boost and there are so many options and different colors for items.Cozy little game to lose hours in, def recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO ADORABLE. I have absolutely loved playing it. But then they added a clown to the game. A clown just walked into my restaurant when I leveled up to level 12. I am afraid of clowns. A lot of people are afraid of clowns, I don't know why they would add that. I'm so disappointed. I was having so much fun with this adorable game, but now my experience is ruined and I don't want to play anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: It´s a nice little game that is good for short bursts.You are a sushi"cooking" robot in a small town.Your objective is to make the town more famousand draw new people to it.Over time, more people start to live there.All of them have a different job and as you growyour friendship level you get more abilities.Out of the story, all of them have little dialog,so interacting with them gets old pretty quick.The town itself is nicely craftet and it´s fun tostroll around in a couple of times and there arelittle things to find.The main gameplay mode is the resturant.You can put furniture whereever you want, whichgive you a bonus. In order to get the most of it,you have to jampack your room full of them,which makes it hard to make it look nice.I put them all in on side of the resturant and leftthe tables for themself. Otherwise you would have to get around the furniture every time you deliver anorder.It´s not hard or complicated.All in all it´s a fun little game and with new qol featureslike fast buy it got a little better.If you are searching for a little fun distraction and don´twant to think, this is a pretty good game.If you want deep game mechanics or thought out relationship system look elswhere.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: You can decorate your cafe, improve your dishes, build friendships to unlock cool stuff and take a break with side quests and 'daily' activities. (day resets after you close your restaurant)  As you progress, it gets a little more challenging, but never to the point that it's not still super laid back. You can control how easy/laid back serving your food is by how many tables you place in your restaurant too. The game-play is relatively simple & easy ~ there's enough story and new things you unlock through story progression that keeps it feeling fresh *but* it can feel a tiny bit monotonous and grindy in some aspects.The controls are simple, the animations are fluid and interactions are very clean. I have encountered one bug in the game that slightly slows progression -
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: A really cute game about a robot who makes sushi in his own little restaurant in an equally small town. You get to learn about the unique characters who live there, and level up your skills every time you open the restaurant. The restaurant is yours to decorate how you wish (and decorations give different bonuses as well) and you can even give your little robot different hats to wear.Definitely give this cute little game a chance if you want a quaint game about making sushi.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Super cute and wholesome restaurant management game. It's not as stressfull as some other games in the genre can be , where you are just swamped with customers and there is never enough time (take that as a positive or negative depending on what you want to get out of the game). This makes it a pretty chill game, bordering on very easy. Love my time with the game so far, just don't expect a game where you have to prepare every single order, all the dishes are made automatically and you just have to serve the right type of order of the right quality depending on the customers order.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game to drop for YEARS now. I got on the other day just to check and saw it was released earlier this month, AND the price is incredible.I will say its nothing like what I originally thought, like for one I had NO idea you were not gonna get to create your own character and you're automatically a male robot...I'd say out of all the cons that was the biggest one for me, because even if you have us being a robot, at least let us pick our gender, anyways I was under the impression that it was gonna be a lot more like Harvest Moon and Animal Crossing, and while it definitely has those traits, the main aspect of the game gives me Diner Dash which is an old school PC game I absolutely ADORED, and feel like I haven't found a game really like it since this one. I will say sometimes the customers not ordering the same meal at the same table is difficult because sometimes you don't move your robot enough to the right and it gives the food to the customers on the left of the table instead, but that's minor and doesn't bother me enough to feel negatively about the game.I'd say my biggest craving for this game would be to add in more cut scenes, like when Coggie goes fishing for you, I WISH we could actually see a cut scene of it happening, but the screen is just pitch black.I also believe there might be a small glitch in the game within the cafe, I've noticed that during the cut scenes the screen is also black, and then I have to hit A multiple times before the screen leaves the black screen and goes to you and whoever you're having coffee with are sitting. (not sure if that made any sense)All In all this game is still a 10/10, I find myself turning on my laptop just to play it, and I haven't had a game like that in a loooong time, I can't wait to play more and see what else this game has in store, and I hope the devs keep adding upgrades and eventually do add cute cut away scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I'm addicted to this game!I've been looking for something cozy to play ever since playing Animal Crossing and this was the perfect game to fill that spot. It's cute and simple but with still so much to do.I love collecting all of the different furniture and customizing my sushi shop. There's also plenty achievements to work on.At first the sushi service is slowed down to allow you to learn and get the hang of it but after awhile it can start to get pretty hectic and challenging until you work on upgrades. Overall it's still mostly just a relaxing game to play with no pressure.There are lots of different kinds of sushi and they look so good, I actually had to stop playing and go get some myself.I would recommend this game to anyone who needs something relaxing and wholesome to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: an adorable, chunky robot gets tricked into opening a sushi bar in a small town. gives the game that quirky animal crossing feel. i LOVE yeti's character design.the game claims it's best played on a controller, but i get by with WASD just fine. DESPERATELY needs key rebinding tho. took me a while to figure out how best to comfortably speed boost while still moving.each day has two distinct phases: out-about-town and restaurant. during OAT: you pick up litter (to unlock a lovely looking butterfly roll), hunt down the daily present, talk to people, buy ingredients to upgrade your recipes, drool over all the cute furniture, and invite your friends over to the cafe.why are kappa and yeti not available as friends to hang out with in the cafe??? you do all these rituals to summon them and they don't count as friends in a game literally called "Make Friends".during the restaurant phase, you activate your conveyor belt to churn out sushi for your customers. this is not a cooking game, which i appreciate. managing customers and managing food? especially without any assistants / sous chefs / servers to speak of? no thank you! it IS a little weird that the sushi-making bot isn't actually making the sushi, but it cuts down on the chores i need to do, so i'm fine with that bit of story and gameplay segregation.i'm bringing up all these nitpicks because i really like the game. if the devs end up reading this, i want to leave them a couple things to think about.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game. It’s like, Animal Crossing but with more to do. It’s involved enough that it keeps my attention but simple enough that I can come home and play it after work and not have to focus too hard. Also I get to buy hats for my robot and like, that right there was enough to sell me. I’ve had this game on my wishlist since March 2021 and honestly thought it was never going to come out, and now that it has, I can definitely say it was worth the wait.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely adore this game! It is simple yet fun and completely chill, I loved the game so much that I did all 12 achievements 100%ing the game. I would recommend this game to anyone who loves farming/cooking/cosy games. You do not build the sushi and cook it yourself, it comes onto a conveyor belt and you serve it to customers. There are also friendships to build up and other things you do on a daily basis which gain you recipes. The story has elements of humour in it and is fun. I would give it a solid 9/10 only because it can be a little repetitive once the story is complete, however, I did decide to get all the achievements so that is also my choice too! ♥♥♥
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly so cute and alot of fun to play after a stressful day at work. I really like how you can upgrade the different sushi options which then make customers enjoy them even more! The only I don't like so far is when you honk to wake up a guest and they leave and throw trash next to the door.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Cute game! I recommend it for a relaxing vibe but it does get a little bland. I wish some of the things were available for the Robot to do like the garden or fishing so it would add a little variety to the game. There also needs to be a few more options for decorating. I don't feel the items are expensive. Most are in the 100-300 range and you can easily make 600 gold in a shift after getting to level 6 which happens pretty fast. I also like others wish there were some preparation involved in the food making. If these things were implemented, this would be a really awesome game as the base is solid and well done.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: This is really an adorable game. I assume anyone who said it’s boring or too simple isn’t a fan of this niche. To me, it hits the same sweet spot as Animal Crossing or Stardew Valley. It’s not a high-pressure cooking game, or a min/max kind of thing — it’s an extremely chill time with a cute robot and their sushi. Rolling Hills fits immediately into the rotation of games I play while having my morning coffee, or listening to an audiobook, or while “watching” TV. Rolling around and doing engaging tasks that aren’t a mental strain is a genre of game I appreciate. And sassy little hats for my robot? Sign me up. If you like the low stress tasks and collecting of Animal Crossing, you’ll probably like this game. It’s sweet and simple and you’ll upgrade and unlock items as you progress. Oh, and it plays beautifully on the Steam Deck. I’m sure it’ll be Steam Deck Verified soon because it’s a perfect handheld game.
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I was looking forward to this game, and so far--8 hours in--I really enjoy it! I think there can be a few quality of life tweaks, however; like having the decor cursor move a hair faster. So far, the only problems I've had is just my input to advance the dialogue sometimes doesn't respond right away (I'm using a PS5 controller btw). And my Imitation Crab hasn't shown up once, but I heard that may have been fixed in a recent patch! Anyhow, I really enjoy the style of this game, and the serving aspect of the game play as well. I also enjoy the lack of a timer outside of shifts, how the tasks connect to one another to advance the plot pretty organically, and I enjoy the mechanics used for upgrading my sushi and friendships~ Looking forward to playing more!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: I have loved playing this adorable lil game! Here are a few things about the game for anyone who is deciding whether to buy! I believe this game is 100% worth the money. ✨💖 You serve adorable sushi dishes to townspeople - As you progress more through the game you unlock more recipes, and I must say, they are so cute, the little details are awesome! 🍣💖 You can visit the market every day to get new food items to upgrade recipes - I recommend doing this every day as the better the recipes the more XP/money they award! Once you progress the story line you'll also be able to restock the shop which is really nice! 🐟💖 The storyline is really sweet. I have loved learning about each of their journey to Rolling Hills. They all have their own stories and I find them quite relatable! I can tell the devs put a lot of thought into the storylines which I appreciate! 👪💖 You can buy furniture items for your sushi store - Again, the items are so adorable! Cat lights, plants, vending machines, teddy bears (which I have collected many off including all colour variants). 🧸💖 I absolutely recommend visiting the coffee shop daily (or twice daily) to progress your friendships! The perks you get are great! (I won't spoil it but later in the game you get some adorable helpers!!) ☕💖 The side quests are really cool also! Finding the crab, mystery boxes, collecting cans to recycle - Adds something a bit different to the game which I enjoy! 🦀Overall it's a very charming, cosy game that I have loved playing! So much so I have 100% the game, because I think it deserves all the attention it can get! I would absolutely recommend this game to anyone who loves cosy, chilled, single player games! 🥰⭐
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

_childDocuments_.review: Serve up sushi as a robot chef in Rolling Hills, a life sim about running your own restaurant in a cozy village. Make new friends, purchase ingredients, enhance your shop, and improve the lives of your neighbors as you perfect your craft!
_childDocuments_.name: Rolling Hills: Make Sushi, Make Friends

name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon
detailed_description: Feature List Feature List About the Game Yakuza: Like a Dragon’s Hero Edition includes a selection of the game’s DLC, Job Set, and Management Mode Set. Yakuza: Like a Dragon’s Legendary Hero Edition adds a wide variety of in-game bonus content, including the Job Set, which unlocks the ‘Devil Rocker’ and ‘Matriarch’ Jobs, as well as the Management Mode Set, Crafting Set, Karaoke Set, Ultimate Costume Set, and Stat Boost Set. RISE LIKE A DRAGON Ichiban Kasuga, a low-ranking grunt of a low-ranking yakuza family in Tokyo, faces an 18-year prison sentence after taking the fall for a crime he didn't commit. Never losing faith, he loyally serves his time and returns to society to discover that no one was waiting for him on the outside, and his clan has been destroyed by the man he respected most. Ichiban sets out to discover the truth behind his family's betrayal and take his life back, drawing a ragtag group of society’s outcasts to his side: Adachi, a rogue cop, Nanba, a homeless ex-nurse, and Saeko, a hostess on a mission. Together, they are drawn into a conflict brewing beneath the surface in Yokohama and must rise to become the heroes they never expected to be. LEVEL UP FROM UNDERDOG TO DRAGON IN DYNAMIC RPG COMBAT Experience dynamic RPG combat like none other. Switch between 19 unique Jobs ranging from Bodyguard to Musician, using the battlefield as your weapon. Take up bats, umbrellas, bikes, signs, and everything else at your disposal to clean up the streets! ENTER THE UNDERWORLD PLAYGROUND When you're not busy bashing heads, relax by hitting up the local arcade for some classic SEGA games, compete with locals in a no holds barred go-kart race around Yokohama, complete 50 unique substories, or just take in the scenery of a modern-day Japanese city. There’s always something new around the corner.
about_the_game: Yakuza: Like a Dragon’s Hero Edition includes a selection of the game’s DLC, Job Set, and Management Mode Set. Yakuza: Like a Dragon’s Legendary Hero Edition adds a wide variety of in-game bonus content, including the Job Set, which unlocks the ‘Devil Rocker’ and ‘Matriarch’ Jobs, as well as the Management Mode Set, Crafting Set, Karaoke Set, Ultimate Costume Set, and Stat Boost Set. RISE LIKE A DRAGON Ichiban Kasuga, a low-ranking grunt of a low-ranking yakuza family in Tokyo, faces an 18-year prison sentence after taking the fall for a crime he didn't commit. Never losing faith, he loyally serves his time and returns to society to discover that no one was waiting for him on the outside, and his clan has been destroyed by the man he respected most. Ichiban sets out to discover the truth behind his family's betrayal and take his life back, drawing a ragtag group of society’s outcasts to his side: Adachi, a rogue cop, Nanba, a homeless ex-nurse, and Saeko, a hostess on a mission. Together, they are drawn into a conflict brewing beneath the surface in Yokohama and must rise to become the heroes they never expected to be. LEVEL UP FROM UNDERDOG TO DRAGON IN DYNAMIC RPG COMBAT Experience dynamic RPG combat like none other. Switch between 19 unique Jobs ranging from Bodyguard to Musician, using the battlefield as your weapon. Take up bats, umbrellas, bikes, signs, and everything else at your disposal to clean up the streets! _childDocuments_.review: I've been with the Yakuza series ever since the very first entry back on the PlayStation 2. When first learning about Yakuza: Like a Dragon changing up the gameplay and introducing JRPG elements such as turn-based combat, I'll admit to thinking that this sounded like a terrible idea.When I finally tried the game out for myself, it didn't really click with me at first. I decided however to push on and give it a chance, and I'm glad I did, because a couple of chapters into the game I was hooked! The turn-based combat is a lot of fun, and the game commits fully to the JRPG idea, even going so far as to have the characters in the game reference actual JRPGs such as Dragon Quest.The changes in gameplay isn't all that's new in Like a Dragon. We also get a brand new protagonist in Ichiban Kasuga, who turns out to be quite different from the previous series protagonist Kazuma Kiryu. Where Kiryu is more stoic, Kasuga is a lot more outspoken and wears his heart on his sleeve. This is a very welcome change that makes for far more interesting character interactions throughout the story of the game, which mainly takes place in Isezaki Ijincho, a location based on the Yokohama district of Isezakichō. As someone who lived in Yokohama for a time, it's a great to explore a location that feels familiar. Beyond that, Isezaki Ijincho is a lot more open and sprawling compared to some of the locations we've seen before in the series, like the mainstay Kamurocho which feels a lot more dense and claustrophobic by comparison.All of these changes make Like a Dragon feel a bit like a fresh start for the series, and a lot less daunting for someone who's not familiar with the series but that would like to get into it. The previous games certainly aren't forgotten about, and throughout the story we do end up seeing several familiar faces from the past. However, Like a Dragon does stand on its own feet and should work very well as someone's first Yakuza game.The game certainly isn't without its flaws, one of the most egregious being an incredibly steep difficulty curve in the later part of the game. Essentially, Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio, the developer of Like a Dragon has designed the game with the intention of having the player do a lot of the sidequests found throughout the game. In a lot of games, these kind of sidequests tend to be more of an optional thing that can mostly be ignored if one prefers to just follow the main story. Here however they are pretty much mandatory for being able to defeat some of the enemies and bosses towards the end of the game.While I'm not personally a fan of this approach to things, it helps that many of the sidequests in Like a Dragon end up being a lot of fun. There are also various mini-games that can be enjoyed, such as a trash collecting mini-game which has Kasuga riding around on a special bike collecting cans, and a property management mini-game which turns out to be essential for earning money. There's even a Mario Kart knock-off mini-game called Dragon Kart. In true Yakuza fashion, it's also possible to stop by gaming arcades to enjoy classic Sega games such as OutRun, Space Harrier and Virtua Fighter.Like a Dragon ends up being a very lengthy game which will likely take most players around 60-70 hours to complete. Of course, a big reason for this is due to the previously mentioned approach that the developer decided to take, more or less forcing the players to engage with all of the content that's available in the game. I imagine this can be a big turnoff for some, but, if one is able to look past this, then there's a lot of fun to be had with Like a Dragon, and I would highly recommend giving it a chance.

_childDocuments_.review: The first turn-based JRPG I've ever beaten on my own, which is saying something. I've tried Final Fantasy  to Chrono Trigger to Mario RPG to Earthbound and I've never beaten them, despite getting more than halfway through some of them. This game was the one to do it, though not because of its RPG gameplay.I knew the entire story going in to this one, and yet I loved experiencing it for myself. Ichiban as a character is a really likeable protagonist, and it's compelling to see him rise up through the city and have people join his ranks. The ending confrontation is really well done, though a bit undercut by the ridiculousness of a certain sequence.The core gameplay is serviceable, but the systems themselves aren't very notable. The presentation is what makes it interesting. Framing each battle as a dynamic street brawl or high stakes gangster showdown contrasts other, more traditional JRPGs with static portraits/models. The accompanying animations for each attack, and wacky enemy designs keep you entertained during battle, but the auto-battle is a nice alternative if you aren't. Side games/missions are just as good if not better than the main game. Sidequests can range from heartwarming, to sobering, to hilarious to absolute degeneracy. Sometimes all that and more. Side activities are nice distractions, but fall in to the same vein of the main gameplay, not much depth but polished and outlandish visuals, barring IRL games like Shogi, BlackJack etc. The one exception being business managent, which can suck you in for hours.As a first time experience with a Yakuza game, it left me extremely entertained, and excited for the next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Kiryu is one of the greatest video game characters of all time. But 7 games is quite a lot for one protagonist, especially if he's getting older as each game comes along (he can only be ageless for so long).Y4 and Y5 managed to keep things fresh, because they introduced well written playable characters like Akiyama, Saejima, and Sawada for added variety. But still, it really was about time to feature a new hero that wasn't just either stoic or angry all the time. Plus, 7 games of continuous story has also inhibited new players from getting into the series.And so comes along the hero of Yakuza LAD: Kasuga Ichiban, who in stark contrast to Kiryu, wears his heart on his sleeve, and happily accepts support from his friends. Because friendship plays such a major factor in LAD's narrative, the new JRPG system makes perfect sense. Without this new combat system, the narrative just wouldn't quite work.I get why Yakuza purists would be pissed at something so drastically different, but the Yakuza series is first and foremost driven by its narrative. Because of that, using the old combat system in lieu of turn-based JRPG just wouldn't quite carry the same feeling of friendship and cooperation that is so central to the story.Fortunately, the turn based combat system is very enjoyable. It features prominently the QTE mechanics previously seen from previous games, and utilises it for a large number of abilities. A lot of the "essence" and "summon" moves have fantastic short cinematics when using them, and is very satisfying to watch.However, there are 2 main annoyances with this new combat system: One, the turn based combat system is also simultaneously "real-time". Enemies constantly move and shuffle around the field, and because of that, many AOE attacks can be a challenge to land.Two, the devs decided to include awkward environmental interactions. If your characters are near chairs/tables etc, they will sometimes pick them up or kick them. Kicking them is usually a miss, and more often than not, damages your own party members for whatever stupid reason. Another thing is that your characters can stupidly miss enemies with bullets. because they decided to stand behind walls while firing for whatever reason.But considering this is a JRPG where combat can sometimes feel repetitive, I never really felt that way with this game. You can skip animations and escape random encounters pretty easily, and that really mitigates that JRPG exhaustion.Many players have also complained about the necessity of grinding, but I never found any need to do so. I can only surmise that these players forgot about the workshop. I regularly upgraded my weapons there, and because of that, never really encountered any real difficulty until much later in the game. There is also a section of the game that requires a large sum of money in order to progress, but is easily attainable by playing one of the mini-games.Fun JRPG system. Excellent main and sub-story narratives. So many fun side activities. Fantastic soundtrack. Memorable and well developed characters. Great entry point for those who've yet to play a Yakuza game.And finally, Ichiban has all the makings of a new legendary character, and is well worthy as successor to the Dragon of Dojima.PS for veteran players: After 7 games, Tauriners finally have a use!

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza: Like a Dragon shakes things up by introducing us to a new hero, Ichiban Kasuga. He's a bit different from the usual main character we're used to, but his unique humor and upbeat personality quickly won me over. Ichiban's adventure starts in Tokyo but takes a dramatic turn, landing him homeless in Yokohama. The game is all about his fight to put his life back together.At its core, Like a Dragon has everything fans love about Yakuza games: a deep story filled with both serious moments and silly fun, interesting characters, and lots of side activities. But there's a big twist: the fighting is now turn-based, like in classic RPGs. This new style changes how battles feel, making them more about strategy but also slowing down the action a bit.While exploring Yokohama, you might find there's a bit too much fighting, which can interrupt the flow of the game. The story also has its ups and downs, lacking the punch of the best games in the series. However, there's still a lot to love, from hanging out with your party members to battling imaginative enemies that come straight out of Ichiban's RPG-loving brain.Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a mix of old and new. It captures the spirit of the series with its engaging world and quirky characters but tries something different with its combat. It might not be the best starting point for new players, but it's still a fun ride with plenty of memorable moments.

I so badly wanted to like this game because the story, substories, and characters are genuinely interesting but I can’t bring myself to fight one more boss who’s health bar is so big you’d think you’re fighting against the Colossal Titan. If you’re looking for a good JRPG, just play Persona 5 instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: This is not the standard Yakuza game. It retained the quirkiness and seriousness of the Ryu Ga Gotoku series but with a new twist. Moving from the action and almost beat'em up genre it was before to a turned base RPG like Dragon Quest (that they obviously are inspired from)Story wise, it is a lot simpler than most Yakuza entries, but it is still deep and interesting with fun and diverse cast of characters. Along with serious and intense moments but also with goofy, silly and lighthearted times that are mostly in during the side missions.Gameplay is nice and what expected from a RPG. but grounded in reality as some of the classes and characters action are from the imagination of the protagonist. Fun over the top skills and weapons as well as bosses and enemies make a fun combination to experience.Sound and music is standard to the Yakuza franchise. Fun, serious, heartwarming  and more. The score compliments the moment well though sometime it might get a bit repetitive with the heartwarming moment theme. Sound effect are on point and make you feel the effect and force of the action taken, especially when a lot can be happening on screen when fighting a bulldozer with a electric baton and throwing heart beams at it.Graphics is also a standard for the serie. Well rendered characters, you are able to see the skin texture on them. Facial expression and movement is a big improvement though it is still a little bit robotic sometimes. but overall the characters are beautiful and the city where the action take place is well rendered and detailed.The game will take you a good 60-80 hours depending on how you are used to RPGs or not. a lot more if you are a completionist due to its massive amount of side missions, side dungeon and optional minigames. Karaoke, darts, baseball, mahjong, casino and more, all optional, but well worth if you indulge in them as they can net you some really nice rewards.A game for avid turned base RPG lovers and also for Ryu Ga Gotoku fans. Lots of unforgettable moments and silly over the top fun to be had. Careful for younger audience as it is an adult story that involve murder, death, sex, violence and baseball bat to the face.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: My first Yakuza game. It was everything the franchise sells itself on. Wacky humor, compelling drama, hours and hours of sidequests, noble gangsters.New to this game is an RPG system, which I appreciate, even though it's not well balanced. Some of the earliest, cheapest abilities I got  were simply never surpassed by the late game abilities.There's a couple random difficulty spikes with late game bosses (and a few have way too much hp for how little threat they pose), and at one time they block your ability to progress based on having a large sum of money (3 million yen). Also, some of the mini game tutorials (important ones) do a pretty bad job of explaining important mechanics. You might need to look up a guide or two online.All in all it was a good, fun time though. A good entry point in the series if you don't want to start with Zero.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game that needs more notoriety. This is not only a well done game, you can feel the passion that developers put in the game in every small detail you can find in it.The Main story is simply incredible, the voice acting (only played in japanese), especially for Ichiban, is godlike (you will see in the ending).The gameplay is refreshing, I personally preferred the old combat style, especially for boss fights, but this new turn based combat has its perks too.Can't wait to see what awaits us in Yakuza 8!
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: I've been following this series for a few years now and I love it. To be honest though I was a bit skeptical about how well this one would be considering it has turn-based combat rather than the beat em up gameplay we know and love. I have to say though I was pleasantly surprised with the game. The gameplay still manages to be lots of fun in it's own unique way, that still manages to capture the charm of the Yakuza series. The new protagonist also happens to be pretty cool too. I recommend this game if you're a fan of the Yakuza series. I'd even recommend it if you haven't played any of the other games before. (You may be a bit confused story-wise though if you haven't). All in all I'd say it's a solid game. Do I miss the beat em up style? At times.. but this game is definitely its own unique experience and hours of fun in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: Different from the other games from Yakuza series in terms of gameplay, but the story still has the same feeling of an Yakuza game. However, the gameplay is still fun and engaging, very easy at times to be honest, but it can be pretty challenging at times, especially boss fights. Overall, I recommend this game for any Yakuza fan, old or new.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember that feeling you had playing Final Fantasy XII for the first time?  Do you remember going to bed after playing the first few hours of the Witcher 3 and think wow?  Do you remember the first time you heard a fart you weren't supposed to hear and laughed?  It's all those things all at once.   I've been a gamer since 1985 and I am just now playing these Yakuza games.  What a waste of time and energy I've had playing anything else.  I wish it cost more so I could feel like I wasn't ripping Sega off.  10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: Ok. So, ... I played all the remake Yakuza games on PS4 (don't own a PS4 anymore, nor a new gen console) and PC. Love the games.At first it's a bit ridiculous ... because it's suddenly a turn based RPG game with grown men XD ... and when Arakawa starts talking to Kasuga about Dragon Quest ...it kind broke all immersion for me. I thought: "Ok. That's it... idk. Should just get a refund?" IDK why, but at that point I was one hair away from refunding. ... I mean. The family's patriarch Masumi Arakawa talks about Dragon Quest ... o_O ... ... no chance in hell.Luckily I didn't because the game is actually really good... I'll not spoil anything. Just letting you know: Don't refund after Dragon Quest gate ^^ ...
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: My only experience with the Yakuza games is Yakuza 0, which I greatly enjoyed. I never really tried the remakes of 1 and 2 because I felt satisfied after the end of Yakuza 0. Like A Dragon provided the chance to go back into this world and style of game, but with a new combat system. I was unsure how a turn based RPG would work in this series, but they pulled it off well. The game is full of the usual Yakuza humor and charm, as well as plenty of mini-games and activities.I was also unsure about going from a character like Kiryu to Ichi, but Ichi is a likable idiot and a fun protagonist. I can recommend the game to people who are fans of the Yakuza series or are curious to try it. I also recommend Yakuza 0 as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: Sense of humor is unique, but does not lose it's charm. A good example is one side-quest where you are tasked with stopping a public urination. Throughout the quest all dialogue is essentially one joke about peeing into another. It's not just a humorous affair. The game has a story which has an excellent setup and it's fair share of payoffs. Ichiban Kasuga is a joy to follow and each member of your party baring one feels like a meaningful addition. Amid much criticism from fan regulars I'll just describe Ichiban and let you make your own judgment. Ichiban is a foremost a kind and trusting person. It's his trusting nature drives much of the plot forward. In combat Ichi hallucinates and imagines his allies/enemies as video game characters - for gameplay purposes this is awesome, for lore it might mean our protagonist is a schizophrenic.Regardless of your feelings the departure Yakuza 7 takes from the series it is wonderful standalone title with compelling game play and a captivating story.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not a avid gamer, but damn, this is good writing. 2 hours in, and I've decided I need to play the whole series. I was looking for a more interactive experience, but the story line is worth the watch in my opinion. I can't enphasize enough that i'm 2 hours in, and its mostly dialog, but I'm absolutely invested to this story now. Greatness in my opinion.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical that they'd be able to pull off an RPG from the Yakuza series, but this game turned out great.  Continues the tradition of serious main story, but silly side missions.  Ichiban is a great new character to the series and his team are all well voice acted japanese or english.  If you've put off the series because brawlers don't interest you, but took notice of this one due to it being an RPG, 7 is mostly standalone.  There are references to previous games, but nothing important for you to be able to follow along.  The difficulty for most of the game is pretty low but does get tougher in the last third of the game.If you're looking for a good rpg with a good story, Like A Dragon is a good pick.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: At first I was leery. Where's my Kiryu? And what is this turn-based combat doing in my Yakuza game?!After getting used to Ichiban (which took five minutes) and the combat system (eh, a bit longer than five minutes), I fell in love w the game. Fun characters, silly sidequests, emotional storytelling. It's all here.
_childDocuments_.name: Yakuza: Like a Dragon

_childDocuments_.review: What a damn good game, as someone who has played all the yakuza games that have come out for ps4 yes including the remasters and the spin-off beast judgement. I’m really glad I picked this one up I was kinda skeptical since it didn’t have free combat like previous entries instead opting for a turn based system in its stead but ryu ga gotoku yet again surprises what a game. It feels new with improved graphics and lighting but has that old dragons quest feel to it. The story is written very well not only showing you but letting the main character express so much emotion and just being a wholesome hero to the story ichi is not only a great character to follow with his struggles in the story feel really the feel like something that someone who lives his life could go through. This game is a ride I can’t recommended it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: As a person who played all of the Yakuza main-line titles, as well as Judgement, I can safely say that Yakuza: Like a Dragon is, by far, my favorite game in the series. I was put off by the drastic genre switch from a beat-em up rpg to a turn-based one; it was a blessing in disguise. It is everything people love about JRPGs, beautiful narrative-driven games, and a lovable cast of characters that will make you feel emotions that were never thought possible. The gameplay, music, presentation, and atmosphere were beautifully created out of love and care for this series. Don't take my word for it, play it and see for yourself. If you do play it, thank you for giving it a chance, you will not regret it.
