_childDocuments_.review: This is without a doubt one of the best RPGs I played ever.Classic turn-based battles are very enjoyable. In a single run Kasuga can be switched between all available classes for him, and so do all your party members, which allows you to build different party and use different strategies, I live for these types of games. Not to mention that everything in this game is funny and absurd, so for example your mage class in this universe is a HOBO, and his fire spell looks like him drinking strong alcohol and setting on fire his alcoholic fumes. And I mean it, everything in this game is made this way. You see the modern Tokyo life through Kasuga's eyes, and Kasuga is an optimistic schizophrenic. In my opinion he is one of the most likable characters from videogames overall, not just the Yakuza series.The main plot is very dramatic, Kasuga tends to sacrifice his own comfort and life for the sake of loyalty to his clan and clan-leader, for the western point of view this could be very weird to be this selfless (to the point of self-destruction). Main story ends bittersweet, but it can be perceived as good ending I guess. However the main sad story is very well blurred with unbeliveable funny side-stories of all sorts, and after finishing everything there is no heavy feeling whatsoever. Still can't beat the very last  millenium tower's boss, every other bosses in the game are way more easier. So don't waste any resurrection and self-resurrection items before you try to beat him! You also probably will need the lighting resist for all your party.Minigames deserve another full review tbh, I would quote the meme phrase from the gaming journals: there is something for everyone. My personal favourite is a manager simulator when you need to lead the cookie shop. In conclusion, this game is an absolute must! Buy a controller and play this game!

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best JRPG games of all time. The characters resonate, each party member has well written dialogue and an interesting back-story. Compared to other Yakuza games the cast is very fleshed out, the villains have goals that make sense (from a certain point of view) and there are shocking twists involving them, as well. Combat is fantastic, job system is both fun and hilarious. You will want to unlock every move.The main location of Yokohama is very well planned both in sound design and graphical excellence. The city is filled with secrets and items to pick up. You can grow your own food to make into Bento (Get your seeds and healing items from searching/growing and save a TON of Yen) bug catching and farming for materials is addicting and feel like their own separate mini-games. Side-stories are more meaningful and sentimental than ever. There are just as many serious themes as there is humor and ridiculousness. The summoning system is amazing and the animations during battle are the very top of the turn based genre. The characters and beasts you will summon are varied, from little kittens to South Korean actors, even crayfish and Sumo Wrestlers...Don't worry there are serious ones mixed in with the comedy.Mini-Games includeKart RacingBusiness requisition and re-saleDartsMovie Theater game where you attempt to stay awake with sheep-people wave their arms at you.Batting CagesKaraokePart-Time-Hero (Way to make good money early on)Casino games both from Japan and the westand more...I can't recommend this game enough, it has quite literally rekindled my love for Turn Based RPG games. I haven't enjoyed one this much since Chrono Trigger and Legend of Dragoon, it is just that good. You won't want this game to end.

Ice mage skill is pouring ice bucket.Lots of fun minigames (collecting rubbish cans, SEGA arcade games,UFO catchers, Racing game...) and ridiculous side quests.Main storyline is at times funny to serious and even emotional near the end.Definitely a game that you won't regret buying even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily personal favourite game of 2020 for somehow making that departure of satisfying beat em up action with RPG elements. RGG Studio, you do another Yakuza game like this, hook that up to my veins, music was TIIIIIGHT, the RPG system, while probably barebones compared to many others like it, still was engaging, Story was a great journey, the English dub is pretty damn good, opinions may vary, but oh well, I liked it, Ichiban is a great new protagonist, a charming idiot who carried enough with his party to let the pain of not playing as Kiryu in this game, but good things must come to an end. Only nitpicks, the game can get repetitive after a while, especially the dungeon crawling, more variety would've been great, or at least more options of dungeons, while the few blocks of Yokohama feel big considering sidequests and the amount of mini-games to do, it's not traditional RPG big, makes grinding a bit of a slog, even if the jobs system buffers that a bit, it's not perfect, yet none of this were deal breakers, everything else easily made me enjoy Like A Dragon immensely, so if you like a serious yet goofy RPG set on the streets on Japan, the idea would sound ridiculous, but totally worth the money.

_childDocuments_.review: I find myself slightly conflicted here. First off, this is an amazing game. What started off as an April Fool's Joke turned into a fantastic way for the torch to be passed on from the Dragon of Dojima to the Rock Bottom Dragon. So why am I conflicted? Denuvo. I recommend this game, no question, however, the Steam version has Denuvo, while the GoG version does not. This has got to be one of the best modern/urban fantasy games I've played, which is admittedly not many, but the way the combat uses things like a baseball bat, tweezers, an umbrella, playing cards, everyday items, is done wonderfully. The way that this game juggles the absolutely insane antics of previous Yakuza games into its core gameplay, while also managing to keep things serious when they need to be is great! Kasuga is a fantastic new torch bearer for the Yakuza/Like a Dragon series, and the supporting cast are all very interesting with their own stories to tell. The story overall is also a very well done, gripping story, with a few twists thrown in that I was not expecting.  This game has been an absolute pleasure to play. It is a Yakuza game through and through, and I eagerly look forward to the upcoming games.

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably the most well-polished Yakuza game to date. Everything from the interface to the mini-games clearly has a lot of effort put into it.New city is big and distinct. Story is the usual dark affair with a lot of plot twists (some dumber than others). New minigames are fun (aside from the management, which is the worst it's ever been). Characters are very likeable and the new protagonist is a significant step away from Kiryu's stoic quietness and it all works very well together, with a great party dynamic. Graphics are top-notch and so is the soundtrack. Humor and sidequests are more ridiculous than ever and had me chuckling at multiple occasions.All that said, I cannot stress enough how much I HATE THE NEW COMBAT SYSTEM. It is the standard JRPG grindfest, where big number = victory in combat. It especially becomes painfully apparent during the final third of the game, where you don't stand a chance without grinding out both levels and the materials for the best weapons in the game, after which all boss fights turn into "spam your strongest moves in between heals and repeat for 20 turns" as bosses are just damage sponges that can soak up a huge amount of your special moves while one-shotting your party members if you're not leveled up enough.The zaniness of jobs and special moves is very funny and entertaining for the first 10 hours of the game, after which it just becomes a nuisance that undercuts the very dark tone of the story. Like in previous games, boss fights carry an emotional weight to them and a story significance to the main character, which is thrown out the window as soon as the fight starts and the S&M queen whip-spanks the boss while a Host sprays him with champagne. It's a complete tonal whiplash. Not to mention that the turn-based system ruins any sort of momentum, while the characters do spectacular moves and exchange blows in the cutscenes, only for everything to halt, as the fighters awkwardly shuffle in place, waiting for their turn.I appreciate the RGG Team trying out new stuff, but I have never been this torn on a series I love this much. I have thoroughly enjoyed every aspect of this game except the combat and I sincerely hope the series won't continue in this direction.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played every mainline Yakuza that wasn't the original releases of 1 and 2 on the PS2. Since this year started I have played and completed 3,4,5, Judgement, and now 7 (or Like A Dragon). I played every other main title previously (0, Kiwami 1&2, 6)I was initially skeptical about the switch to turn based combat but I've played my fair share of the genre so i accepted it pretty quickly. The new game play being how Ichiban sees combat was also a neat little explanation for it. The combat while being a turn based RPG with four party members and an MP system still manages to (at least to me) stay fresh with its positional mechanics. Which can be wonky at times but they'll just teleport characters as a fail safe. Yakuza stories are always kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ insane. That's the best way for me to describe it. It's the way they execute scenes despite how dumb some of the writing is that pulls me in. You know how a lot of the time when some one is reviewing something they'll say "It's a good idea, just executed poorly" I think of the opposite with this series "That idea was horrible, but it was executed amazingly." And Like A Dragon is a bit different as after finishing I can't really think of story example like that. By Yakuza standards it's pretty tame in the wacky plot writing. I also ended up liking the new protagonist a lot more than I had initially expected.I sort of just wrote this for the steam awards thing but didn't want to just throw some half hearted meme review for it. The game is genuinely great and is a pretty good starting point for the series (0 or kiwami 1 is still better imo, but this works)Please Sega port the rest of the games (including judgement)

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely amazing. Truly one of my favorite games of all time. However, it's not for everyone. If you solely enjoy the Yakuza franchise because of the Action combat than you might be disappointed with the fact that Yakuza 7 uses "out-dated" turn-based combat. That's totally fine, but I think people need to separate this entry from the previous games in the series, and while the turn-based RPG genre as a whole may be "out-dated", this game adds such a vast amount of customization and fun to pretty much everything you do. I may be a bit biased because I am a fan of turn-based JRPGs while also being a big fan of Yakuza, so seeing them both mixed together is a treat.The story is fantastic, I personally really enjoyed it, but there are definitely some issues, especially near the last couple of chapters. But, all in all the story is gripping and in my opinion one of the best in the series next to Yakuza Zero. The characters are 100% the strength of this game, all the party members are incredibly likable and have a lot of great moments as well as amazing chemistry. The interactions at the bar are great and give you a lot of insight into their character and motivations.The substories are also really solid, they're fun and memorable and remind me a lot of Yakuza Zero. So if you liked Zero's substories, you'll love Y7's as well. There are some issues with the game however. The main one I can think of is the difficulty. The game starts off fairly difficult, there's a lot challenging fights and even random thugs in the street can mess you up pretty badly, but it progressively gets easier and easier. I did not go out of my way to even grind or optimally build classes and I never really encountered any issues. And then suddenly, around two-thirds in I would say there is a HUGE difficulty spike. This particular fight is notoriously difficult if you go in unprepared, which is the case for most people. Narrative-wise, this fight is amazing and makes sense to be difficult, though it makes the gameplay quite tedious. There's a bunch of people on YouTube who've beaten the fight incredibly under-leveled and managed to win, so it's definitely not impossible and you'll probably be able to beat it after a try or two in your casual playthrough, but a lot of people take issue with that level of difficulty spikes.Furthermore, Hard Mode and Legend difficulty are awfully balanced. They're intended for New Game+ but even then, Legend is time consuming as if you don't prepare beforehand you'll get curbstomped by the early game. Again, people have beaten it with minimal prep and underleveling and it is possible, just incredibly tedious. With all that said, this game is fantastic, I loved every second of it. I spent almost 100 hours on my first playthrough alone just because I loved the game that much. And writing this made me want to replay it again, so I'll probably add another 100 in the near future.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a totally recommended.Story is pretty solid.Ichiban is amazing and wholesome. Now I just want another game with Ichiban because he's really emotional and he's not cold-blooded.The fighting system is so amazing, the summoning system is hilarious, and the abilities are just so good that every single fight I was laughing, no matter how long into the game I was.Substories are also up there with the main story, they're just not some single secundary quest that you do to get some XP or money. They have a really good plot.Minigames are fantastic, I probably spent over 10 hours playing just the minigames (they're addicting)Job system is wonderful and really complete, and some of the skills are just so good.It has Bakamitai.It took me over 100 hours to beat the game, and this is not 100% or post content game. Just what it took me to finish the game after doing all the main story and all the substories.This game should have been clearly game of the year. 13/10

In fact, I've quit this game twice because of their questionable design choices. It seems like they really want you to grind and spend time on this game.1. I personally do not like the turn based combat system. It gets boring and it just doesn't feel as satisfying as actually getting to punch the enemies.2. You are limited by in game currency. So basically you are forced to play this mini business game or else you won't be able to progress through the main story. Which is fine since I had some fun playing it, but still a little frustrating when I'm so eager to know what'll happen next. It unnecessarily interrupts the flow of the game. 3. You are limited by level too! I'm stuck at Omi Alliance HQ when I'm barely Lv. 40 and the bosses are Lv. 50! Now I have to somehow grind out 10 more levels or I'm not making any progress! It's just boring, and again interrupts the flow of the game! It's boring and ruins the experience!

_childDocuments_.review: I thought I'd leave a review, but rather then praising what the game does good, I'd address the general (rather stupid) negative complaints people are making. (Playing on Normal, updated as I progressed throughout the game).Firstly, if I see ONE more idiot complain about how Kiryu is not the main character, I might scream. Get this right, that 6th game, you know that one that was the end to Kiryu's story, was in fact, the end to Kiryu's story. Crazy! Some of y'all didn't actually play the series and it shows when you sook about him not being the MC. Ichiban is here to stay, it's been confirmed he is the main character for now.Secondly, the game is turn based, yes. If you have experienced all of the series, you would know how they had to keep trying to spruce up combat because it gets stale faster and faster each game. This combat is a good shake up to the game that needed to happen. Judgement is now taking the brawler combat so look for Judgement 2, whilst LaD is moving towards an RPG as that is how it goes.And thirdly, The game is centrally a DRAMA. Yakuza has always been a cutscene filled series that has a lot of betrayal, mystery and DRAMA going on. It's what the game wants to be and the story it wants to lead. Yakuza has it fair share of dud plot points, and huge plot points, this game is not going to be an exception to it.This game is a masterpiece, it's serious and heavy in the main plot whilst being light and fun where it needs to be. The game is quirky, and brings in a turn based system that provides a shakeup to the dull combat. The game also features an isolated story, making knowledge of previous games not necessary, but has enough throws to them that if you do know, you'll be pleased. Highly recommended as an entry to one of the best crime drama series out there, the other option being Yakuza 0 to enter the series.Edit: I am now much further in than the initial hours of this review. I feel it needs to be discussed so I am tacking it on here as the game does have issues and I feel people need to be aware of them as few people seem willingly to mention the negatives.Firstly, Levelling up becomes a chore, fights in the street (and in general) rapidly become spam use of AoE techniques that clear the field, while major bosses are a chore because they drag on and on. They have large health pools, deal absurd damage (which is bearable) and just feel like a time waster. It gets particularly bad towards the later chapters of the story.Secondly, I mentioned dud plot points. I have no idea why people are praising this story as some huge game changer. It simply is not, after the initial 3 chapters the plot becomes garbage. It's pacing slows right down, it becomes borderline gibberish as it establishes these players who one second hate you and next are all chum chum. The lack of a consistent plot at this point significantly hurts it. Followed by arguably so many predictable plot points that will make previous games duds look smart to this. It seriously becomes so predictable and borderline stupid that I am now rushing through these final chapters as I simply don't care. You will be sucked in at first, but once you get to later you honestly will be like 'Come on, really that's where you want the plot to go?'. I like the characters and the attempt to have motives, I just hate the direction they chose to go in, it almost feels like a bad novel for the major plot points of this game. I feel they wrote them down and then had to establish a way to get to them and took the easiest path.I think this is a great game, that becomes dull past the first 30 hours. Grinding in a JRPG is never a surprise but it's rare it is this boring. There is a lot to like about this game, but there is also a lot to dislike. I still believe it is worth purchasing for both new and old players, but I think there are some large issues that sabotage the game and they are not fixable.Minor spoilers but the English Karaoke is a sin against everything. The english voice actor for Kiryu is also so wrong and ill fitting. I am sure he tried his hardest, but when Kiryu talked I burst out laughing and that's not good for one of my favourite characters (in the english dub).Also, Yakuza 6 dealt with the ages of characters catching up to them in the starting chapter(s), this is also done away with because of reasons? I honestly don't know but 6 felt very grounded in trying to wrap up the series and 7 wants to be its own thing but relies so heavily on the previous titles. It is locked in by the ghosts of the past and repeats past mistakes.Final edit: (Upon finishing the game)Ultimately, I am changing now to a negative review for a plethora of reasons. The story is an absolute mess with some of the worst writing I have experienced, starting very strong and falling apart. The gameplay is fun at the start and then has no idea what it is doing and falls apart. The minigames are varied and fun until they become grindfests. Notice the theme yet? It starts strong until it stumbles and fails.I'm going to really beef up this review because this game is plagued with STUPID decisions that ultimately ruin the game. In no world should this be as highly regarded as it is.Lets dive into the major complaint and arguably where I think the game shows it has no idea what its doing. The gameplay is just so misbalanced and unravels itself so quickly. The gameplay is basically babies first JRPG, its simple, fun and straightforward at first. Then enters the mid-point where all of sudden some enemies suddenly take 5 minutes to fight while dealing next to no damage, but alas some also just suddenly start one hitting members. There is no consistency within it, some enemies at your level stomp you, some don't. Minibosses deal little damage but have huge resistance and health pool so you spend ages fighting them. Bosses become a mess where they drag ON and on, while almost one hitting your party. It becomes the most boring, grindy and unfun JRPG I have ever played. To be CLEAR the underlying mechanics are fine, the game itself has ideas that work, what it needs is number tweaks and an overhaul of bosses and minibosses. Stats are largely irrelevant as good luck guessing (and yes I mean guessing) what they actually do.The story is gibberish, it becomes so predictable that you lose that ability to care. It crumples as it feels like ijincho was just thrown in randomly so they have to build all the lore up to start it, which would be fine if it didnt degrade back into Tojo and Omi at the end. Characters become dull as they just flip on a dime and go 'Nah ichiban is cool' and DONT EVEN GET ME STARTED ON *THAT* CHARACTER who is arguably the worst thing introduced to the plot since rubberbullets. It's a shame, it hits some highs and some lows, and has a great send off but its ultimately so messy with largely 6 chapters being really irrelevant bar introducing a faction of ijincho who ultimately doesnt mean much.This game is a good game, it is 100% not worth the asking price however. It is 60 hours wherein the first 20 are good, the next 20 are tolerable and the last 20 are horrible. It's a fun combat system until it just suddenly isn't because each fight with a main character drags on for 40 minutes (even when overleveled). I think the series will move forward in a better way for the combat change, I however think this needed so MUCH more QA and playtesting before being released in this state. It needs a lot of fine tuning, a lot more actual GAME content as well. It's loaded on wacky minigames but the combat itself is largely stuck into 2 dungeons and a battle arena for actual levelling. It's a mess of a game and should NOT be regarded so highly.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza: Like a Dragon was a refreshing entry into the Yakuza series. It's a great entry point for newcomers to Yakuza game tropes/style and a new injection of life for series vets. As an RPG it is a good first attempt, you can clearly see some strong bones in the design of this game.I am excited for another similar entry or at least more involving the main protagonist Ichiban and his misfit party. I think this studio could easily continue to develop down the RPG path making some tweaks for balance, some enemy changes to ensure classes are better used (and balanced), and some changes to the dungeons. Otherwise, the only thing I think I would request in a sequel is simply more - more gear, more crafting, more quests, more classes.An easy contender for GOTY 2020 on PC.

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza: Like a Dragon marks a bold departure from the traditional beat-'em-up formula of the series, introducing a turn-based combat system that adds a fresh dynamic while still retaining the franchise's signature storytelling and humor. The game follows the journey of Ichiban Kasuga, a lovable and relatable protagonist whose earnestness and quirky personality make him an excellent addition to the series. The narrative is both heartfelt and humorous, tackling themes of friendship, loyalty, and redemption, while the richly detailed environments of Yokohama invite exploration through a wealth of engaging side activities, including mini-games and character-building elements. However, some players may miss the real-time combat of previous titles, and certain battles can feel drawn out. Despite this, Yakuza: Like a Dragon is highly recommended for both longtime fans and newcomers, offering a unique blend of RPG mechanics and classic Yakuza storytelling that revitalizes the franchise in an exciting way.

_childDocuments_.review: (No spoilers will be mentioned) I myself am a diehard Kiryu fan, I've played Yakuza 0-6, Ishin, Kenzan, and both Judgement games. Only exception being Dead Souls.Keep in mind I will not cover other aspects of the game in detail, but here's a summary:✨: 7/10✨📖 : *chef's kiss* 🎵 : 100% the best music in the whole Yakuza series🧍‍♂️ : Absolutely insufferable until he grows the hell up in second half of the game. After which he transforms into an amazing main character.⚔️ : Too basic and no synergy between skills, making it incredibly boring and a pain. It straight up sucks.---------------------------------------------I'll go a little deeper into the 2 elephants in the room: the  and the . If you want a quick summary of both points from the perspective of a Yakuza veteran, here it is:: Annoying and unlikable in the first half of the game, but quickly his character develops and matures really well in the second half. For his first game, he is shaping up to be a worthy successor to Kiryu, but at the moment he is just a koi fish. You will feel the same way to Ichiban by the end of the game like how you felt towards Kiryu a the end of Yakuza 0, aka intrigued by their potential and curious to see more.: If you are looking for the "rush", you won't find it here. (R.I.P satisfaction from executing Tiger Drop or Parry). The combat system is unique, but I feel it is ridiculously basic and didn't need much critical thinking. Personally I hated the turn-based system and prefer the real-time combat of past games. That is not to say that I hate turn-based in general, I've played plenty of turn-based combat games before. However for this game, I got so bored I almost fell asleep multiple times. I had to pay attention for only 3 of the major boss fights, the rest felt like a slog. This is probably the only reason why I would only give this game a 7/10 at best.You can read below if you want even more details in this review.At the start, I found Ichiban absolutely insufferable. He was a cocky, loud, and overly emotional man who liked charging into things without using simple logic. At times I would think "damn is he really that dumb not to put 2 and 2 together..." I almost dropped the game because I couldn't take his personality anymore, but I powered through the first half of the game because I saw that the reviews were great. I found myself often thinking "if only Kiryu was here" or "Kiryu would do so and so instead".However, in the second half of the game, his character growth came in by leaps and bounds. While Ichiban still retains the core of his personality, he matures a lot due to his experiences with certain people. He pauses to think before he acts, he's quieter but definitely not subdued.  I came to realise that one should not compare Ichiban with Kiryu. They are both on opposite ends of the personality spectrum, but they are also 2 different people with their own way of handling things. Ichiban is also weak. Hell, he gets winded fighting like 10 guys, can barely stand after he fights 1 boss, and that's even while being in a full party of friends to back him up. At first I hated it, especially after tasting the power fantasy that is Y0-Y6. However that IS the point. Ichiban is weak, but he has friends around him to make up for it. He's not a lone wolf like Kiryu, that's just not in his personality all. The people around him support him both mentally and physically, and because of that he manages to get through his hardships. He's not an emotional rock wall like Kiryu who powers through his despair and ignores the trauma. This is a weak man, and it's quite refreshing.That being said, I can definitely tell that his combat potential is there. But for the time being, he's just a little baby koi fish trying to become a dragon, but still has a long way to go. For a "debut" game for Ichiban, this lays out a solid foundation for him.TLDR: He does have character development in the second half of the game, and keep in mind that Ichiban and Kiryu are 2 very different people and try not to compare between the two.Personally, I still prefer the real-time combat system as I like my blood pumping. However if the turn-based combat is well made, I usually go along with it. However, there's virtually no synergy between different character skills, ultimately the combat is basically summed up to:1. Find the enemy's weakest damage type. 2. Swap in characters that do that damage. 3. Spam the most powerful skill that exploits that damage type. 4. Use heals and debuffs/buffs as necessary. The combat system isn't , but it still sucks. It's functional in a very basic way, but it feels very bare bones. I literally almost fell asleep multiple times doing the combat encounters. The fights posed no challenge at all and I had a very low opinion of the combat system until I hit nearing the very end of the game.As I mentioned before, I still prefer the real-time combat of Y0-Y6 games because it feels like my wins are because of my fast reflexes, it gives me a huge sense of accomplishment dodging out of a boss' attack or doing Tiger Drop. I guess this is another gripe I have of the game. The combat doesn't give me the same rush as before due to the turn-based nature. In this game, if you hit a boss fight and you are underleveled, that means you get one-shot, no questions asked. Then it's back to grinding for levels at the arena like a classic JRPG, and let me tell you that it is not fun. I had to spend 3-4 hours mindlessly grinding 20 levels just so I won't get insta-killed and progress the story because at one point in the game, the level scaling is scuffed. This is in contrast with the real-time combat system of previous games where if you have the skill to dodge or counter, you can still win. On the contrary, I enjoyed myself immensely playing games like Fire Emblem, Persona, and Dragon Age. However in those games, the combat system is well fleshed-out and complex enough that you feel great after winning a battle. This game still has a ways to go before reaching that level.TLDR: Adrenaline junkies like me probably wouldn't like the combat system due to the turn-based nature. Combat system is unique, but too basic and needs almost no critical thinking except for maybe 3 fights. Combat encounters are braindead easy for 90% of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Discovering Yakuza Like a Dragon was an absolute blessing, I already played a few of the Yakuza games and finished them all but no game hooked me as much as Like a Dragon did, the story, the characters, the music, the minigames, the voice acting, everything just clicked for me. I discovered it the day it was announced, I remember being super pissed because they changed the main formula of the game, it went from a beat em up game to a JRPG (Japanese Role Playing Game) and I did not like that one single bit. (after watching some of it when it came out in Japan I changed my opinion of it but alas!) But then the release of the game happened, a special someone gifted it to me as an early birthday present and I tried it out for myself, and I gotta say I absolute love it.Game is about Ichiban Kasuga, a Yakuza that works with the Arakawa family, a subsidiary of the Tojo clan, who gets sent to prison to cover up one of his superiors. 18 Years later,  Ichiban gets out of prison just to find out his patriarch Arakawa is called a traitor and that he betrayed the Tojo clan, which eventually led to the doom of the latter organization. In hopes of finding answers, Ichiban tries to talk to his former boss only to get shot, after that he gets thrown in Izezaki Ijincho, a city in Yokohama. Now Ichiban Kasuga has to search for answers such as; why did Arakawa shoot him? Why betray the Tojo clan? Is it all just part of a bigger plan? While in the way, meeting new friends and striving to become a hero, just like in Dragon Quest.Overall a really inspiring game, Ichiban ends up finding comfort in his new friends and his persistence of becoming a hero is truly beautiful. Ichiban Kasuga, while being a Yakuza, demonstrated to me that, just because you have the title of a bad guy, doesn't mean you have to be, he is really optimistic, cheerful and friendly.My favorite Yakuza game by far. The gameplay is really addicting and a good replacement for the beat em up although i hope they go back to the original formula of it.

_childDocuments_.review: As much as I'd want it to be perfect, it's not. There's some slight points in the plotline that make the writing weaker than what it could have been, either with needless twist which don't offer much to the story or pacing issues by bringing up some points at a wrong time.Gameplay-wise, the system is a lot more basic than what it looks like, the buffs/debuffs are pretty lacking, and the afflictions aren't effective against bosses, and you won't be needing them for most trash mobs, making, around 30/40 hours in, the gameplay a pretty mindless button masher since you'll know what's the most efficient way to dispose of people, and doing that repetitively.In a general sense, pacing-wise, the game halts you for a bit chapter 12 in a pretty poorly introduced grinding area, while up to that point the game was going pretty well.All and all, is that a bad game ? No, it's actually fantastic. The story, while I find some slight issues with, is overall pretty good, and definitely has its moments. The gameplay, while basic and not very deep, conveys quite a lot of the comedy of the game, whether it's the ridiculous attacks, or the even more ridiculous enemies. The side-content is nothing short of amazing. While I did not try the pachislot because I just don't like slots, there's a lot to do mini-game wise, probably more than the previous games in the series (Judgement and Kiwami 2). Is it the best Yakuza game ? Probably not. Is it a pretty damn good game ? Yes.

_childDocuments_.review: The Good - How the battles work(as the enemies are constantly moving around that spells can only hit them if they are lined up and you can only run away if your character runs without hitting a wall)- How you are basically fighting 99% of the enemies human and yet most of them are unique- The summon system was really coolThe Bad- How you can't know if you had already upgraded a weapon or if you already had that equipment if it is repeated- The bond system that is just a way to give the same exp to the whole party and spam "special moves"(I could easily say that after the 5 level bond you would need to fill the bond bar to use special moves on a fill and use to fill again and use again)- The Progression as the game gives you multiple jobs but the only places that gives exp are only 3 or Main Story battles meaning that you either grind very late in game or stick to one job the whole game....The Ugly - The main minigame( the main minigame is a recurring thing in Yakuza as you will be presented a minigame that has a story by itself and you can waste a few hours or do it for a few minutes) Yet again it is something that starts fun and turns boring and repetitive because you need to do it hundreds of times Overall it is a great game even more for a studio that is doing a turn based game for the first time for me a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Yakuza Like a dragon is a wild game with things going well for it and others that aren't going so well for it but in short I would not recommend this game for the full review please read onThe Pros: Yokohama is a beautiful city to run around in, it is alive with people constantly walking, talking and driving around, the city is densely packed with minigames and side stories hidden around that will have you laughing or genuinely invested in what is going on.Ichiban Kasuga as a protagonist is a lot of fun to follow, he follows through with what he sets out to do and manages to mesh well with his crew as well as the other inhabitants of Yokohama from allies to random people to even his enemies, Ichiban is just a big ball of personality, humour and fun. The soundtrack for this game like every other Yakuza is so catchy to listen to when beating up thugs you fins in the street or bosses you meet it just always makes you want to dance even if your too busy beating a guy's face in.The story is one full of intrigue and mystery surrounding Yokohama, Masumi Arakawa and Ichiban's inclusion within the city limits.The Cons:The turn based fighting in this game was amazing and refreshing at first, however it started to get boring by chapter 6 when the game forces you into a long dungeon for the whole chapter, I soon realised part way through that I wasn't having any fun being pulled into fight after fight doing similar moves over and over again, you could argue that you do the same in other Yakuza games however what makes those different to LAD is that in those street fights I could mix up my attacks with heat moves, items in the environment or by going ham on your enemies, but with LAD the fight just starts to drag on or become repetitive depending on the level of Ichiban and his party and the level of the enemy. I became so bored of fighting in LAD that I just started avoiding street fights, I just prefer to run away and not fight at all since it just started to drain on my enjoyment of the game, so much so that I find it harder and harder to want to push myself to finish the game at this point, the story would normally be enough but the gameplay in this instance is just so boring that I don't even want to actively see how the story ends anymore, however after this review is posted I will finish the game but as of right now with 28.5 hours in the game I'm just bored now. The DLC available for this game is terrible, I don't think any of it should exist at it's current price as they are all cosmetic and only one of them really affects the how the game is played and even then it should not be a DLC if Sega and RGG keep the monetisation of Yakuza in this way then I hope more and more players stop purchasing the DLC.Yakuza like a dragon a crazy, zany turn based RPG with an unforgettable main character set in a wonderful new city that as much as it upsets me to say I really don't like the gameplay. If Yakuza stays as a turn based RPG as sad as I am to say it but I will stop playing the games, I truly hope that the next instalment is back to the third person brawler style and if not then I wish the devs all the best in their endeavours and that the players who enjoy this continue to enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played a couple of Yakuza games at this point, and Yakuza: Like a Dragon has become one of my favorites. I don't play a lot of turn-based JRPGs these days, so I wasn't sure if I would enjoy the gameplay switch, but the humor in this game and the cool combat effects made Like a Dragon more enjoyable than the South Park RPGs I liked.  Since I played Final Fantasy V many years ago, I've always loved job systems and this game doesn't disappoint.  Most of the jobs have at least one useful skill that's worth learning, though some jobs like the Fortuneteller are enormously helpful.  This game also has some of the funniest and most memorable substories of all the Yakuza games I've played so far.  I especially love "The Miracle of Spice" and "Fifty Shades Of Play", and there are a lot more great ones.    The minigames are good and I enjoyed all of them.  The business side game can get grindy, but fortunately you don't have to rely on that entirely as a moneymaker unlike the fishing game in Yakuza 6.  Dragon Kart is lots of fun, especially if you like Mario Kart.  The karaoke is hilarious and fairly challenging compared to the other games.  It's easier to 100% this game since you don't have to fill out the completion list.  The dungeons are okay but they could have added one in a different setting instead of two sewer-themed ones.  The Sotenbori Battle Arena is my favorite, and though it's considered to be optional, the difficulty spike once you get to Sotenbori will make you want to run through it at least once to collect item upgrades.  The True Final Milennium Tower is a great challenge that I enjoyed, though you have to do a lot of grinding to prepare for it.  If you just play through the game and do enough of the side activities, you shouldn't have to grind too much otherwise.  The best part of the game is the characters.  Ichiban is basically the opposite of Kiryu but I found him to be the most likable and relatable character in the series so far.  The companions you get are also very interesting, especially Adachi and Nanba.  The relationship-building quests give them a lot of depth and you share many funny and poignant moments with them.  The story is still a crazy soap opera with unlikely plot twists like the other Yakuza games, but I thought it was one of the better ones since it deals more with personal conflicts than some overarching secret government plot.  Yakuza: Like a Dragon is a fantastic game and a worthy entry in the Yakuza series.

_childDocuments_.review: I thought Cyberpunk was game of the year. This hit me out of nowhere and I'm telling ya... if a game makes you cry three times, and ROFL about 30, it's bloody game of the year. Story: Oh Em Gee... the story. It's like watching the Iron Chef mix Dragon Age and Godfathers into a salad and then serve it in Japanese. But be warned though... half the game is literally cinematics. Yeah, you can skip it but then it's like skipping the main of a 15-course meal and wondering why you only remember the taste of macha ice cream. Watch it. Savour it. It's ICHIBAN! (Hahaha. I can't help it. I have post-game withdrawal symptoms).Gameplay: It starts slow... I'd grant the critics that. But then you start fighting hordes mid-game. You have 6 companions, each with a myriad of jobs/classes that they can change in and out of, and with bedazzling cinematic super skills. You almost feel the need to spend the next 10 hours levelling up a different class JUST so you can see how PIGEONS can annihilate a clan of Yakuzas. You heard me... pigeons - and the Hitchcock version. Oh, not enough? Did I mention Kung-Fu lobsters? Independence Day satellite lasers? How about... a psychopathic chicken? I love you Ryu Ga Gotoku. Mechanics: It's turn-based. Very rare for an RPG game like this. And you'd think it's gonna be a slow, painful grind up the ladder. Not if you have pigeons! One AOE and it's next! Of course, as the difficulty goes up, you might need to mount your pigeon on a satellite. But the entire play-through was smooth as butter and never did I ever feel that the turn-based mechanics slowed it down. If anything, it made the game richer because now you can take your time to choose a skill and just watch it massacre the Flasher. No, not the fast dude with tights. It's the one that opens up the trench coat and wiggles his bits at ya. Surprise!Overall Verdict: Take my Visa!! You want a liver too?? Use it wisely!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the Yakuza games since Yakuza 0. A very common starting place for a lot of the current fanbase right now.  I thought initially I'd be uninterested in the turn based combat and lack of main man Kiryu Kazama who we all know and love. But here's the thing this game is a reset for the franchise.CHARACTERS: Ichiban Kasuga is a great protagonist and very well played character, he is exactly the opposite of what Kiryu Kazama is. Hot headed, enthusiastic and very lovable in his own right. Kazama has very little character development in his first game, which RGG remedied in Yakuza 0. This game showcases how Kasuga grows and develops as a character with all the other party members. Where Kazama will typically go solo, Kasuga eventually learns that its okay to rely on others and places his trust in his party members. By the time you are done with this game, Ichiban will likely be as lovable as Kiryu or Majima.GAMEPLAYThis game plays a lot like Paper Mario in my opinion. Press B/O to guard attacks, press Y/Triangle or X/Square to do more damage with skills. I'd like to say tho the actual strategic depth of combat is fairly weak until the endgame. The biggest difficulty spike is when you fight the Ornstein and Smough of the game. Compared to everything else you have fought so far they have a level hike that is pretty considerable at this point in the game. However there is a Colosseum at this point in the game that will help cross the gap before the fight and by its own right a very fun side quest. For folks that do not like turn-based combat I'd say give this one a chance as I think this is a good entry point to JRPG games in general, especially turn-based ones. If you miss the Virtua Fighter-esque combat, go play Judgement or Lost Judgement instead. Graphics/PC Port/Etc:This game is very good looking overall. It's PC port is very good overall. RGG and SEGA can make PC games which is important to note in the growing market. However my one gripe is that Discord streams will make this game crash on systems with AMD GPU's. I can't confirm this with NVIDIA systems but I think the issue is still there. Other than that, this version is solid and looks great.Final Thoughts:This game is fun overall, I'd recommend it to fans of Yakuza games of course as well as fans of JRPGs.If you don't like turn-based combat, I'd point to the other great Yakuza games on steam. RGG is a great development team and I can't wait to see what they put out next, even in a post-Nagoshi era.

_childDocuments_.review: [Initial Review @ ~2h game-time]At 10pm tonight, I'd never played a Yakuza game before.  Always seemed interesting to me, though.It's now 12am, and in a mere 2 hours, I've already realized why people love the franchise so much, and the game's  almost made me cry once.I'm not sure if any of the others work like turn-based RPGs, but I'm all over this one so far.  Thank you for this new gaming experience. :)[Updated Review @ ~7h game-time]This game just gets better and better.  The story and dialogues are really well done (lots of drama/excitement and some somber parts too, along with comedic relief), even for just small side-quests.  One thing to keep in mind is the game starts out a little slow, but you'll be unlocking more "features" as you progress, and the game opens up a lot more around Chapter 3 (takes a couple hours to get there - think of Chapter 1-2 as a sort of story-filled tutorial).I've enjoyed every moment of this game so far, and I already knew it was one big Dragon Quest reference (or just JRPGs in general), but I was not expecting the really over-the-top Pokemon reference at all, made me laugh out loud several times.As I mentioned before, I've never played a Yakuza game, but I do enjoy turn-based RPGs and JRPGs, and this game is honestly fantastic.  If you're still debating on getting this game, I highly recommend it.  I plan on doing another review edit later on, but at this point, if the game continues being this enthralling, it will probably end up being one of my all-time favorite games.[Updated Review after finishing the game, though it took me a few years to go back to it because I'm easily distracted]Absolutely incredible.  Insane plot twists, incredible writing and characters, super fun gameplay and lots of activities.  One of my favorite games for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the best games of 2020. Yakuza series is already quite unique and pretty engaging, but this one, ho...Story is just, excuse for my bluntness, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing. It's a story about friendship and a beautiful one at that. New cast of characters  - I couldn't have asked for a better one to be honest. I won't spoil anything, but man oh man, that was a wild ride. A bit slow in the beginning tho, but it's okay. Turn-based combat turned out (huh) much better than I anticipated. Most importantly - it fits. Yakuza is already kinda crazy and over the top, so it's okay to have something like summoning army of lobsters. I certainly would like turn-based combat to return at some point in the future. Tons of optional content is always nice. Substories are wacky and wholesome. I don't really enjoy mini-games like cards, but it's here too, as always. Soundtrack is very good, I really like it, especially some of the unique themes for bosses. Default battle theme is an absolute ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blast to listen every single time. Pacing of the game is fine. There is one big difficulty spike tho. It's not that bad, just grind a bit, the game gives you options to do it rather fast and painless. Everything in this game is on point. I wholeheartedly recommend you to buy it and play it. Worth a full price if you ask me. You can also punch an excavator. What are you waiting for? Go on, play the game.

_childDocuments_.review: I can say that this is, without a doubt, my favourite Yakuza game. I'm going to most likely be talking a lot, but I'll post a TL;DR to start. There are also MAJOR unmarked spoilers in this review. So be warned!TL;DR:Pros:- The characters- The story- The combat- Amazing English dub performances- Some of the music was dopeCons:- The story dungeons- Lack of variety in music- Optional DLC - while optional - are a little on the pricy side for what little they add to the game.------------------------ SPOILER ZONE ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Let me first start off by saying that quite frankly, I thought the mid-series Yakuza games were... not very good. Starting from 0, anything past 2 I just thought was completely dreadful for the most part in terms of pacing and plot and characters, with the exemption of some chapters in 5 and I did enjoy 6 quite a bit. Needless to say, I was completely burnt out on the series as a whole by the time I picked this game up.My god, is this game a complete breath of fresh air. Let me first start off by saying, EVERY character in this game was memorable. Their personality, their characterisation, their own personal conflicts and story, they all completely shined through in amazing ways. Ichiban is insanely inspiring to me. He's such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ idiot, but he keeps getting back up and fighting with the extreme optimism that he has instilled in him. He's naturally such a good guy who always has a smile on his face, but at the same time, being a complete hotheaded dummy who gets angry at the little things, aaa I love him lmao.The other main character members, Nanba, Adachi, Saeko, Joon-gi, Zhao are also all memorable characters with funny dialogue, chemistry with one another and interesting 'social links' that delve deeper into the type of people they are, and Ichiban is the one who gets them all to open up. I wish I got to have more time with Zhao, as he's a very late game party member and it feels unfair to say but he was probably the one I feel attached to the least. The music in this game was great if not repetitive sadly. There were times where I found myself tuning the music out, but there were some tracks that were just like "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this rules." Mainly the fights against Mabuchi, the final boss battle or the social link battle theme (which is a homage to a Dragon Quest battle theme).The main villain is probably the most memorable out of the series, in my opinion. Ryo Aoki/Masato Arakawa is amazingly written, and amazingly performed. His relationship with Ichiban, and the final scene with the two had me in absolute bawling tears. I really wish he got to stick around after it all, but such as the way in this game series. I played the game with English dubbing, and I was a bit sceptical at first, don't get me wrong. But I think everyone absolutely did an amazing job. Especially in the more emotional scenes.Now on to my least favourite part: the mini-dungeons that you needed to go through to progress in the story at points.There were no variety to them, all being underground levels with the same looking environment with just... constant similar enemies that felt like they went on forever. Which just kinda wasn't fun. Thankfully there wasn't many of them, but they were rough to get through to say the least.And also, there's a point around half-way throughout the game, there's a bit of a difficulty spike at one point where you face off against Majima and Saejima at the same time. I was around level 39 or 40 at this point, while they were level 50 and well, I got swamped. I could have absolutely avoided this, though. But my god was it out of nowhere, so be prepared! Take the warning to train at the arena seriously!Overall, this game was fun. Again, the most fun I've had with a Yakuza game for a really long time. I laughed, I cried, I was pulled in by the twists and turns. This game absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rules lmao

_childDocuments_.review: This might be the best Yakuza yet. It's certainly up there with 0 for me. The new RPG combat system feels like a natural evolution of the series' gameplay, maintaining the fast pace of prior entrance while adding a new layer of strategy. The story is deeply personal and engaging, and the acting performances, both Japanese and English, are very impressive. Ichiban is so wildly different from Kiryu, but I think I might end up liking him even more. He's just so earnest, kind and driven to do right by the people he cares for, be they his friends or the downtrodden, and he develops such a strong bond with his party over the course of the game. It's impossible to dislike him. This is easily a high point for RGG Studio, and I can't wait to see where they take the series next.

_childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly I prefer the turn base combat this release, as it has a bit more to it to keep you active and easy fights go by real fast.  You can time blocking/dodging by pressing a button at the right time,  if targeting distant enemy you have to look at enemy position (unless using a skilled attack), if fast you can attack a downed enemy for extra damage.   The combat is well animated and fun to watch, the characters even constantly walk around while you pick your move.    The story and characters are strong, especially difficult as there are numerous characters.  The story arcs add the needed extra pushing you forward.I wouldn't recommend this for those that dislike cut scenes as they are as numerous as the gameplay and I think if skipped would greatly lessen the game.  The numerous cut scenes (they are even pausable) and turn based combat make this a relaxing game to play versus the frantic past entries.On the negative side the way they handled DLC is a bit trash like showing enterable buildings that when entered bring up a purchase this DLC.  Then many of the DLC feel like things that in past would be included in a base game, especially when the base game isn't offered at a large discount.  The only pro of the dlc is much of it isn't worth much so you aren't missing a ton not having it, but the way it's done day 1 and intertwined in the base game leave a nasty impression on an otherwise amazing game.

_childDocuments_.review: I really hate to say this because it's so radically different from all the other Yakuza games (disregarding Dead Souls..nvm) but this is shaping up to be one of my favorite entries from the series.  I was unsure at first how I was going to feel about a brand new protagonist and a completely different set of supporting characters but it's been incredibly refreshing and Ichiban can stand on his own. He doesn't fill Kiryu's shoes, he wears his own and has a strong supporting cast to push him forward. The combat system felt weird at first, you get used to it very fast. People claiming it's just Yakuza Persona aren't being honest, the system is familiar yet unique for the series and the Job change mechanic gives you endless possibilities on how you engage enemies. The whole equipment/outfit aesthetics is still at heart Yakuza, additionally enemy variety is great and ranges from hilarious to downright bizarre. You get more of the traditional drama from a traditional Yakuza entry, more wacky substories and familiar faces, and some high quality level grinding. I think my biggest gripe is how we shifted to Yokohoma rather than Kamurocho. The city is so new and different, I think I've gotten way too comfortable in the last 7 entries it feels so different, even moreso than Ishin imo. This will probably change as the game progresses. I just kinda miss the neon nightlife of Kamurocho, but Chinatown is a sight to behold at night and the game has some rather impressive visuals at specific points of the game. It's not the best looking game in the world but it doesn't need to be. Overall I'm having a blast with Like a Dragon. It's a great entry that stands by it's own and is great for someone new and not able to play 3,4,5,6 (seriously Sega please just port them already). It's a great direction and the naysayers questioning why Yakuza went turn based are missing out, it fits the characters and I hope they continue to try new things in the future. Sega I gave you $90. Please port the other main games. Better yet, please localize Ishin. Thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: I can't remember the last time I played an RPG this good, in every respect.  If I had to compare how it felt to play it, oddly enough I would say it feels like Earthbound.  The game takes place in modern-day Japan, has random thugs wandering the streets that will start fights with you, and all of the enemies in the game are weird and quirky, just like the game as a whole.Sidequests range from normal to absurd in their content, with many of them being well-written self-contained stories in their own right, and the game is littered with fun minigames.  The combat system remains simple in its concept, but diverse and speedy in its execution.  You can do perfect guards in the same vein as the Paper Mario games to reduce incoming damage from any attack, many attacks can knock enemies to the ground which opens them up to the next party member being able to attack them while they're down for double damage, not counting a possible critical on top of that, and random objects in the area can wind up being used as weapons for extra damage as well.The story is stellar.  Top-notch.  I've never played a Yakuza game before this, only watched others play them, but I'm very glad I played this one.  Everything from the writing to the animations to the voice acting really makes the game stand out, and keep in mind I'm talking about the dub, not the original Japanese.  I played the game entirely in English and never felt like it was lacking.  A lot of people genuinely cared about what they were doing, and it shows.Also, the music?  I mean...do I need to say anything here?  The game has such a variety, including (of course) Baka Mitai, complete with English versions of said songs, but that's just talking about the karaoke minigame songs.  No, when I mean the music is varied and wonderful, I'm talking about ALL of it.  Can't think of a single track that sounded out of place.  On the contrary, every song complimented every scene, and the boss music for just about every single encounter is a treat for your ears.Overall, I strongly recommend this game.  It's game-of-the-year material, and I hope a lot of people get to pick it up and give it a shot.  It might help to know that nothing that happens in the story of this game explicitly requires any knowledge of the previous games.  Knowing who's who from previous games might give you some insider knowledge, but not much beyond that.

_childDocuments_.review: I've still got a lot of the game to play right now, but so far it's been absolutely great. When I saw the download size I was worried, since the last time I got a game that big with high quality graphics it ran like trash on my computer, but this game runs perfectly on my PC even when a lot's going on without any drop in quality.As for the game itself, the plot is incredibly fun and well-written; I'd only seen the sillier side stuff online before buying it and the more serious cutscenes hit like a smack to the face at first. Yakuza does a great job of balancing serious moments with more light-hearted or downright ridiculous ones, so that I very quickly got invested in not just the main character but the surrounding characters as well. I like the turn-based fighting since I'm not very good at realtime fighting, and I enjoy how it's framed like the main character is imagining himself in an RPG; I've read some people didn't like this, but it's my first game in the series and I have no frame of reference, so I thought it worked. The weeb in me also likes having the option to set audio to Japanese while subtitles are English.The only downpoint I can think of is that the cutscenes are ridiculously long at times. I don't mind usually since the plot is interesting, but my wireless controller keeps shutting itself off halfway through and I don't notice until the cutscene ends and I can't move. _childDocuments_.review: Like most Yakuza games, the story is quite convoluted (not that that's a bad thing) and entertaining to follow. Ichiban himself is a hoot of a character and never boring to watch, and the companions are similarly interesting to investigate. The scope of the game is quite large; I'm nearing 40 hours and am only somewhere around halfway through. Graphically, it looks about the same as Yakuza 6, which is pretty nice in my book, and I'm pleased that the thing does in fact run on Windows 7 and doesn't require that you install spyware OS to run it.Unfortunately, Like a Dragon falls flat on its face in two key areas: the fact that it's turn based combat and its pacing. Both of these feed into each other to make it deeply unpleasant to actually play the game in between cutscenes. Yakuza games have always had a problem with pacing in my eyes because they're rife with side content that doesn't jive with the overall narrative being told. There's nothing wrong with side stories and side content, but when you're presented with a riveting story that seems like time is always a fact and that the protagonists need to get things done quickly, it's jarring to take multiple hours out of your playtime go do side content while a critical character is waiting for you to save them from imminent death, or something similar. In past games, I've always elected to do side content after the main story is complete, or right before the final showdown if I didn't feel like playing Premium Adventure modes. That isn't an option here, because side content is no longer optional. It's required. The fact that Like a Dragon is essentially a turn based RPG means that all skill in playing it is thrown out the window. In no place is this demonstrated more than in the bosses. The bosses are -insanely- difficult, and almost every one is accompanied by a gigantic spike in enemy level and difficulty. If you're like me and don't want to do side content until later, you'll quickly run into quite a lot of roadblocks where you simply do not have a high enough leveled party to beat the bosses. Worse, most of them are at the end of dungeons that, while challenging, are manageable; so you can get stuck there, endlessly halving your money on retries for a fight that it's mathematically impossible to win, unable to escape from the vicious cycle unless you have a previous save. And if you do, it's often hours ago, because the game does not let you save in its story areas. You might be saying that I'm just not playing right. You're wrong. Bosses are, by and large, immune to status effects. I did manage to poison one or two, but you'll never land a stun, paralyze, or fear on one. On top of the fact that they often have two or even three turns in a row, you'll quickly find that they instantly K.O. your party members one by one, and there is -nothing- you can do to stop it besides reload an earlier save and grind for -HOURS- to get higher levels just to have a chance to beat the ridiculously difficult bosses. Every boss past Sawashiro, I ended up having to use Cheat Engine and freeze my party member's health to basically activate godmode. Even then it's like chopping down a tree with a butter knife because of the hugely inflated health pools that bosses have. At first, I thought that it was an endurance test; so I reworked my party to have a lot of sustain. Ichiban's group heal, Nanba, buffs for defense and so on. It doesn't matter. The bosses will plow right through it, because if you have to spend every single turn healing someone or they'll get K.O.'d because their numbers are too low, then you don't get anywhere. No, perfect block does not help. It reduces damage by something like 20%. In my entire time playing, perfect blocking never made any difference in whether I won or lost a fight. I'd have won or lost whether or not I bothered to. In past games, which were brawlers, the bosses were difficult but the games relied on your -SKILL-. Yes, you had levels and upgrades and so on; but even with minimal levels and items, you could study the boss's patterns and block, evade or counter his attacks in almost all situations. The nature of a JRPG takes that away from you, forcing you rely only on the numbers that you've farmed. If you don't have enough numbers, you lose. The huge difficulty spikes force farming at many points in the game if you want to have a chance against the bosses; and god help you if you don't want to do that or don't know that before hand, because then you'll be stuck reload an hours old save. That's where Like a Dragon fails. And that's why I can't recommend it to anyone, even though I like it's story, it looks nice, the characters are interesting, and everything else about the game shines. If it were just a brawler like the previous entries, it'd be a solid and worthwhile addition. But JRPG and pacing problems creating impassable road blocks that require grinding or cheating to get past can honestly F right off.

_childDocuments_.review: Press A to skip - The GameYakuza games have always been heavy on exposition and developing characters but Like a Dragon goes a fair bit further than the older games. There are points in this game where you might see 20-40 mins of consecutive storytelling as a mix of text boxes, in game cutscenes, and cinematics. I don't mean that as a bad thing but do be prepared for the sheer length of the campaign.The combat takes a significant departure from the old games and transitions to a full turn based system, granted it does so in the over the top Yakuza style. There's a certain level of depth and I found that surprising as I wasn't expecting much. If you're on the fence and/or a huge Yakuza fan, you will probably be happy with what it is. If you loathe turn based games then this is probably not going to do much for you.LaD has the most side games I've seen since 0 and a considerable amount of substories (side quests) as well. The Ichiban Confectionary and Dragon Kart side games have their own mini-stories and could take up a few additional hours on their own. The substories are also well done and feel a little bit longer than in previous titles, so you can tack on a considerable amount of time there. I haven't touched the other things like arcade games and Part Time Hero but suffice it to say, LaD is packed with fun things to do.The characters are well done as with most if not all Yakuza games. The transition to a turn based RPG also brought the introduction of social bonds (akin to social links in the Persona games). It's actually quite fun and there's little stories and missions to follow along with for each party member. Ichiban Kasuga is the protagonist moving forward as Kiryu has been retired from the role after 7 games. Fundamentally they're both Yakuza/ex-Yakuza with their hearts in the right place but Ichiban is a loudmouthed individual who relies on his friends while Kiryu is much more stoic. Ichiban is a great character and I look forward to seeing more but he is a bit of a blockhead sometimes.The story is riveting so far but I have yet to finish the game so I will reserve judgement until then. It also is very long if my review hasn't made it clear yet. There is also an English dub where they've apparently synced up lip movements and made considerable effort. I haven't tried it out yet but look forward to doing so in New Game +. The Japanese voice acting is great as always. I honestly have no trouble recommending this at MSRP; I think most people will get their money's worth out of this massive game. The only reasons I wouldn't recommend this is if you hate turn based RPGs or you like a linear story experience. Even at points in the story where you would expect the game to shoehorn you into the narrative, you are allowed to do what you want. At one of the more pressing points halfway through the game, I decided I would collect recyclable cans for a homeless guy for a while before moving forward. I love that kind of freedom but some people might get so distracted as to forget what the main point of the story was to begin with.

_childDocuments_.review: Went into this game having low expectations due to the shift towards JRPG game play, but it ended up being one of my favorite RGG games to date. Like a Dragon is Ryu Ga Gotoku's first attempt at a JRPG, and while it can definitely show in certain aspects of the game I would say overall they executed the shift in game play/concept extremely well. I love all the references to various video games throughout the game, especially the completion music which gives me Legend of Zelda vibes. Not really related to anything else in the review but the explanation for why everything looks so wacky being that all the battle transformations/effects are  was a neat detail.Game play: If you are a fan of JRPG style of games then I think you would enjoy this game, if you are coming from the previous Yakuza games then you could certainly give it a try but I know that the shift in game play is a huge turn off for many people. They definitely took inspiration from other JRPGs as the battle system is pretty standard turn-based combat. While I think the multiple job system is definitely interesting, I personally didn't bother trying every single job there was, mainly focusing on the ones that I needed specific stats/skills from. While a certain  skill may make the game extremely easy, you are in no way forced to acquire this skill and can still enjoy a perfectly fine level of difficulty throughout the game. I really like the additional party members you can get throughout the story, but by the end game some party members are definitely more useful than others. All the battle animations and essence of: skills fit right in with how crazy the series is known to be, and although they don't have the same 'oomph' or impact of the heat actions and combat from the beat-em-up games they are still satisfying. Story/Characters: Actually up there with Judgment in terms of having a solid story that got me tearing up at the end. IMO there weren't any real RGG signature ass-pulls that are usually used throughout most of their games. Kind of reminiscent of Yakuza 0 in that it is essentially an origin story for the new face of Like a Dragon. Speaking of, I went in being prepared to hate Kasuga after playing through the entire series with Kiryu as the main protagonist, but his character is just too lovable to hate for me. Although he is somewhat similar to Kiryu in morals, they are fundamentally different characters. Kasuga is extremely reckless, hot-headed, passionate, and in-experienced but I love how expressive he is with his voice and expressions unlike Kiryu who has a stoic demeanor (not to say he isn't also all of those things mentioned, he is definitely one of the kindest, softest human beings on the inside but they often don't let him express it). The supporting cast/characters are all pretty fleshed out and I would say I'm hoping to see many of them return in Like a Dragon 8. Also props to this game for being the first game so far to have playable female characters that actually fight. Fan-Service: Seeing some of the OG characters from the Yakuza games was so hype after playing through all of them to this game. The  fight made me tingle everywhere. The Poundmate moves for all the OGs show off their character so well that even though it's all supposedly in Kasuga's imagination, it's not too far-fetched to say they didn't actually happen. Mini-games: They definitely went ham with all the plethora of mini-games that are available. While the classics like karaoke and  make a return there are lots of other mini-games to try out while you're taking a break from the main story. Sub-stories: I think the sub-stories in this one are solid; I would probably put them right behind Judgment in terms of memorability/enjoyment. Dungeons: The dungeons are very bland in terms of layout/design aside from smash-able walls and are basically just run forward and kill enemies, not necessarily a 'bad' thing but I think it would be fun if they added some sort of puzzle aspect or putting more love into the dungeon layout/design to make them more interesting/engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a new-ish take on the Yakuza games. On the one hand, it shares the setting with the previous ones. Many iconic characters appear in this game, and even the plot seems very similar to the other installments in the series. The main story is still a criminal drama with many twists, and the side quests are still crazy and emotional. And there are, of course, tons of minigames.On the other hand, this is a party-based JRPG with all the good things (e.g. spectacular fights, original classes, etc.) and the bad things (e.g. grind) that come with the territory. It even had dungeons. And though "real yakuza use a gamepad", keyboard+mouse controls work much better here than they did in other Yakuza games.All-in-all, it is a very enjoyable product that would fit both fans of the franchise and the newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: Not perfect by any means but a pretty good time for people who love story-based games and JRPGs. Overall I had a positive impression of the game, but this review is going to sound really negative because I wanted to talk about it's issues.The story was satisfying in the end but felt a bit hit-or-miss at times, with the middle of the game especially feeling like it was lacking. There is a LOT of exposition in the game and a lot of events frustratingly happen off-screen. You get introduced to the three main powers of Yokohama who... don't really matter. They're just window-dressing. The party members are likeable enough but unfortunately are not very well integrated into the story, especially the final two. They join the party and then mostly just follow Kasuga around without doing anything for the rest of the game. Saeko was a really disappointing character because she just exists to be "the girl," and is barely involved in the story. Especially disappointing because there is another lady you meet later who is FAR more interesting, but does not join the group despite being considered their friend by the end. There are also a lot of fights that SHOULD be one-on-one narratively, but because it's a JRPG your party members have to tag along making a lot of moments that would be cool, less so.The battle system is competent, but really grows tiring once you settle on your preferred party set-up as there isn't a lot of variety and the game is constantly throwing mooks at you. The streets are WAY too littered with enemies which makes traversing around Yokohama annoying, and to make matters worse the enemies you fight on the street really don't give you enough EXP to be worth it so you'll eventually spend most of your time avoiding them. The "dungeons" in the game are really lazy, made up of empty rooms connecting fights together with nothing in-between. For some reason you can't save in the middle of a dungeon either, which is just unneccesary and annoying. The one saving grace is the boss fights, that are always fun with varied mechanics and interlaced with cinematics similar to previous Yakuza games.The side content is kinda meh, running your business isn't as fun as say the Cabaret Club in Yakuza 0 but better than Kiryu's Real Estate. The mini-games are all there, minus bowling, with some new ones that are alright. There are a lot of funny side stories, and the writing is great, but everything ties back to the combat so after a while it gets tiring.I wasn't expecting a "romance" mechanic in this game but the one they implemented was so bad I had to mention it. You'll meet a girl and have to level up your social skills to talk to her. Sure. But once you do, do you get anything for working towards it? Nope. No story, no items, not even a cutscene. You just get a text box asking you to get more stuff for her. This continues several times until you max out your social skill and dump a ton of money/items into her, and THEN you finally get a cutscene... and the ability to hire her for your business. Which you'll probably have already maxed out by the time you can actually complete a romance. What a waste of time, it makes you wonder why they bothered including it at all if they were going to half-, no, quarter-ass it.With all that said, I still enjoyed the game, if you like Yakuza games by all means go for it. But if you're on the fence, maybe wait for a discount.
