_childDocuments_.review: Pros and Cons (completely subjective): The traditional Yakuza formula, albeit with a main primary protagonist that isn't Kiryu...but changed from action-adventure to action-JRPG.  It works, but if you're coming from other mainline Yakuza games, you may or may not like it (or you may be ambivalent to it).Disclaimer: I have only played the Japanese language, English-subbed version thus far, so the review only reflects that where applicable.Pros:Fantastic voice acting, as is the standard.-Traditional Yakuza formula in terms of story, though I think some of the ending twists are more creative than some of the prior titles. (Corrupt politicians, nefarious dealings usually to do with grabbing land or control of land or properties, Yakuza and figures of authority intermingling, mass hysteria)-Running in the newer engine (started with Yakuza 6 I think).-A plethora of minigames, most familiar to other Yakuza games (saves coding time, obviously), some new.Primarily set in a new map for the most part, though there are visits to maps from earlier games.-A person new to the series can play this one and lose very little due to not knowing Yakuza lore or backstory due to the new protagonist and .Cons:-Like many JRPGS (and this is subjective and my opinion) the encounters can be tiresome.  This isn't to say that in the earlier beat-'em-up format they weren't also annoying on occasion, just that they're annoying in a new way.  The one item that really seems to drag battles into the annoying category are with two scenarios:1) You're so OP that you button mash or set the battle to auto because it feels like a complete waste of time.2) The battle occurs over a wide area and every single turn you watch the party characters run back and forth across the battle map and the camera goes back and forth repeatedly.-side note, the pathing where it's straight linear in terms of traversing obstacles, or random kicking of obstacles (I LOVE it when I bean my other party members with a randomly kicked object) is strange, and very basic.  The battle behavior doesn't exactly lend itself in making one believe the characters are rational or perceptive.Bonus Pro: You can summon a crawfish to battle with you.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone out here singing Persona 5's praises saying it taught them to go out and make friends and changed their hearts and lives, when this game is the most relatable thing I have a ever played. A Yakuza, a Homeless Man/Nurse, a Detective and an Intelligent Business Woman who have all fallen on hard times, Join together. In a city known for being the place for people who have nowhere else to go, most of them without money have to build themselves up from scratch and look out for each other as they confront their demons and face those that have wronged them, they grow together and form a friendship that makes them inseparable.The best part about this game and the characters is the message of it "never being too late to chase your dreams and to better yourself". I love the fact that the characters are regular people who are also adults, there really aren't many self improvement/positive inclusive games for adults, it's normally reserved for teens and coming of age stories. The game is set in a city and the enemies are real people with exaggerated elements of fantasy, that are grounded in a believable reality. It's just the most honest and wholesome game and for the first Turn Based RPG game that Ryu Ga Gotaku  studios have done, I like it more than any other RPG that I have played.   9/10

I did understand for the Legend Difficulty of the previous Yakuza games doing this with you dying causing you to go back to the beginning and try again. It made sense and was an option. Not mandatory. The first road block probably screw me over the most. As it ended up being me having to spend several hours of grinding to get back to where the fight was viable. It wasn't based on my skill as a player that I lost but because of game being overwhelming to deal just because you didn't put enough time into grinding your chars. It's even worse when you lose and run out of money you have to go back to your save and go through the gauntlet of easy to defeat enemies again. I just feel like the balancing went into all of the bosses and not enough into the journey to get you to the bosses. This was not a problem in previous Yakuza games where I just play the game normally and if I died on a boss I would get bumped back to the start of the boss fight again and there was option to send you back to the beginning if you wanted to do so. I just wanna say that this game is 100% worth it! I'll be honest and immediately say that I still think the combat in this game is severely half baked, especially seeing the combat in the sequel and how much it evolved. Another, tho smaller gripe I have, is the fact that you can only change "jobs" once you reach Chapter 5, which takes quite a while, and its what made me drop the game before. With these gripes out of the way, I can safely say that Yakuza: Like a Dragon is easily one of the best Yakuza games. It has one of the best RGGS narratives, the music goes HARD, the cast is stellar, and the new protagonist, Kasuga Ichiban, already has my heart. I heavily recommend this game to both older RGGS fans who are more into the classic brawler combat, and also newcomers given that you don't need to play any of the other games in the franchise to enjoy this one. _childDocuments_.review: I'm hooked and I love it. Yakuza: Like A Dragon is bold for the series in several ways, most notably for taking a turn into becooming Dragon Quest-inspired turn-based JRPG. In spite of this dramatic shift, make no mistake: this is an authentic Yakuza experience through and through and serves as an excellent starting-point for newcomers to the series while giving fans everything they could want. After 7 seven games of beat 'em up gameplay and following longtime series protagonist Kazuma Kiryu, Like A Dragon follows newcomer protagonist Ichiban Kasuga and I gotta say, he's awesome and almost instantly lovable. Granted I've only played the first five hours but he embodies everything I want to play as in a Yakuza game and a few of the members that have joined the party are all interesting, likable and engaging in their own right. Battles are just as quick, if not more so, than the street encounters of previous entries and the abundance of hilarious and heartfelt side-quests along with a fleshed-out compact overworld with a wealth of seriously entertaining activities and side operations already have made this one of the strongest entries in the long-running series.  So far the only technical issue I faced was an early cutscene pausing midway briefly to load. Other than that, I've had nothing but a pleasant experience playing through and through. Granted, I am a huge Yakuza fan going so far as to buy the Japanese copies to have them in my collection but I'm a fan for many reasons and the most important ones can be found in this game. I recommend this game to anyone even remotely curious. You won't be sorry and you'll be wrapped up in one of the most entertaining and engaging soap operas you've ever experienced.

_childDocuments_.review: Who would have thought that a series that primarily plays like a brawler could transition so well into the turn-based RPG genre? Actually, I think it makes a lot of sense once you take a step back and look at the bigger picture. I am a relatively new fan of Yakuza, having gotten into it a couple years ago with 0. I fell in love with the series and its unique ability to achieve tonal dissonance without skipping a beat and feeling unpleasantly jarring, expertly weaving in between genuinely impactful, mature storylines and silly, outrageous detours in many forms. They tend to be on the lengthy side, especially for the kind of genre it plays as, so really it already had the groundwork for a great RPG game, barring actual RPG mechanics. With that in mind, Yakuza's tendency to last long and burn slow is a perfect fit for a JRPG. Like most of the games in the series, the beginning is very slow, almost to a fault, what with its need to establish the many characters and motivations that will take place throughout the game. You might get frustrated at the pace, you might even feel like quitting. However, like most of the games, when the story gets going, it REALLY gets going. Many people consider 0 to have the best story in the game; in my opinion, Like A Dragon's story is as good if not better than 0's, and that's high praise for sure. There is also, for the first time since the first Yakuza game, an English dub for the main characters (though weirdly enough, not for a lot of NPCs, creating a strange dissonance), and the voices are well-cast and acted, though I personally prefer the Japanese dub. The characters are a joy, and new protagonist Ichiban Kasuga will win your heart, if you give him a chance. He starts off brutish and a little dim, but he quickly shows his soft side and fierce sense of loyalty for his friends and comrades, and feels very different from previous protagonists. His party members, including Nanba, Adachi, and Saeko, are also all generally well-rounded and fun characters, and the group's unlikely bond is a treat to watch play out as you play. The gameplay, meanwhile, is pretty fun and interesting. Though the shift from beat-em-up to turn-based fighting might seem like two complete opposites, there are enough real-time elements of battle to make it feel more involved and engaging. There are a wealth of jobs (classes) to pick per character to help shape the perfect team for the situation, and experimenting between them makes for a deep, fulfilling battle system. Plus, the game proudly keeps the off-kilter sense of humor that the series is known for alive, and a lot of your attacks and the situations you find yourself in will almost absolutely make you smile, if not laugh out loud. If there are any faults to bring up, I must say that inventory management is fairly clunky, with no option to sort items manually in different ways. There is also a somewhat sudden difficulty spike several chapters in, which heavily encourages grinding and can jeopardize the pacing of the story. Speaking of the story, there's a point where the story is muddled with convoluted reveals and head-scratching elements that may leave you disappointed. Finally, as of the writing of this review on December 29th, 2020, a number of games in the arcades simply do not start up, rendering parts of the game completely unplayable. Still, despite its flaws, I feel like Yakuza: Like A Dragon is an incredible game that is well-worth your time, especially if you are a fan of Yakuza, JPRGs, super-silly humor, and stories with heart and strong character. The genre-shift was risky, and ultimately paid off brilliantly. TL;DR: this game is extremely good pls play it

_childDocuments_.review: Through loyalty, sacrifice, redemption, kindness and a lot of humor, Ichiban Kasuga, a low-ranking Yakuza grunt, makes his way from underdog to dragon in a quest to uncover reasons for his betrayal by his former Yakuza patriarch. This is a sequel that made a big change from the previous entries in Yakuza series by shifting from real-time action brawling to a turn-based JRPG. The eighth main release in the Yakuza series (and the first without Kiryu or Majima as main heroes), Like a Dragon is a must-play for any fan of the Yakuza series. Best buy if on sale.- This review is a PERSONAL opinion. Try the game for yourself.- Game was played on max graphics setting and ultrawide resolution.- The plot starts in Tokyo (Kamuroho district) in the 2000 New Year's Eve and continues in Yokohama (Isezaki Ijincho district) and Osaka up to 2020. Story is getting better around chapter 4.- The game features a couple of nice encounters with iconic protagonists of the Yakuza game series.- The game's main theme (called Ichibanka) was performed by the same band that underscored the main theme in Yakuza 0, the "Shonan no Kaze" band and DJ Yasutaka Nakata.- To best capture the flavor of a Yakuza game, use the original (Japanese) voice-acting with English subtitles.- Be aware that the auto-battle feature automatically consumes recovery items from your inventory when required, starting with the best. Auto-battle is efficient on "adaptable" setting, but during boss fights you may want to switch on manual control.- Leveling character and jobs, getting best gear and being able to face certain bosses will involve a fair share of grinding.- Use often the ATM deposit feature, this way you won't lose half the money if you lost a fight. Save some money for chapter 12, you will need 3 million to progress the story. Best way to grind levels, money and gear is to repeat the dungeon and the arena over and over again.- Map is huge, the biggest so far in Yakuza series, so make often use of cabs (taxi routes must be activated first by interacting with them).- Try raising the bond early with your party members (unlock at Survive bar), in this way they will get more exp (including characters not in the party while you are in combat).- You should play at least Yakuza Zero before this one, because the great connections to the series.- The ending is a bit abrupt before credits, so make sure you watch the 20 minutes set of cutscenes AFTER credits.- A good and very long, emotional story along 15 chapters. While the game starts at slow pace it will catch wind by chapter 4 and will see epicness from chapter 11 to 15. The more you play, the better it becomes. And it has manual save.- Good graphics, decent soundtrack, good voice acting (both Japanese and English).- Combat mechanics may seem a bit more complicated than in the previous games, but are very interesting, using both turn-based combat and QTEs (Quick-Time Events). Unless you use auto-battle, it may feel odd compared to what previous Yakuza games offered.- The map is three times bigger than was Kamurocho in the previous Yakuza games.- Map directions are better and there are no quests to let you confused about where and how like in the previous games.- Special combat skill are cinematic and beautiful (max level cap for character and jobs rank is 99).- Plenty of side activities: arcade mini-games, a business to run, side-quests and collectibles for completionists, two dungeons that change mob types everytime you enter and an arena with 30 floors and a large variety of enemies. And the usual "New Game +".- Partial ultrawide support (cutscenes are pre-rendered in 16:9 thus pillarboxed).- Several skippable dialogues were way too long. The game has a tendency to go to great lengths into explaining through dialogues even the most obvious details. Compared to Yakuza Zero, we have fewer emotional cutscenes to properly develop the narrative but more static dialogue fillers, at least in the first half of the game.- Auto-battle is fun, but time consuming, you can end faster on manual attack.- Kasuga is obsessed with "Dragon Quest" video game so he sees everything through ancient magic hero eyes. While fun for a while, it will become annoying (you would expect someone grow-up a bit after 18 years in prison and with a Yakuza pin for his job description).

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very poggers.Pros:- The story is really good and is pretty consistent in quality throughout, so it doesn't ever feel like a slog.- The characters are cool. Both the protagonists and antagonists have interesting back stories that are woven together well. The performances by the voice actors are amazing (I had the Japanese voices because I'm a weeb).- The minigames and side quests are a lot of fun to do. There's a large variety so they always feel fresh. They range from just talking to people to mario kart, so that's pretty cool.- The combat is pretty fun for a JRPG. The game uses normal turn based combat, but a lot of your moves require these mini quick time events and you can block enemy moves if you time a button press correctly so it isn't just menuing the entire time. Also the special moves and helpers that you can use are cool to discover. Finally, characters interact with the combat area during the fight. For example, characeters can pick up traffic cones and hit each other with them or you can get hit by a car during the fight. It's essentially exactly like Jojo's and so that's cool.Cons- There's a massive level jump during the last quarter of the game, so you pretty much have to grind even if you do all the side quests and that is cringe.- The enemy spawns are wack. Sometimes you'll kill an enemy and one will spawn right beside you. You get an item near the end of the game that stops these spawns, but by then it's kind of pointless.- The job system is kind of weird. You can change each characters job (class) as they grow in level, but for most characters, their starting job is their best one so you don't really even need to change the job. Also sometimes jobs are straight up trash, so your kind of punished for switching to them.- Using AoEs is also weirdchamp in this game. Enemies are constantly moving around, including during animations, so you never really know what enemies an AoE is going to hit unless it's guaranteed to hit all enemies. On the one hand, it's interesting because you have to learn it yourself for each move, but on the other hand it often put me on tilt. - Selecting characters in combat is annoying. When you use a move that targets someone, you use the D-pad to select the character. Pressing left and right doesn't always cycle through all the characters depending on how they are standing. You have to press down and up sometimes. It's really weird and often hard to tell what you need to press. Reading this, you probably think I'm stupid. I am, but I promise this is true.Overall, the game is a lot of fun. My complaints are pretty much nitpicks that I hope are fixed for a sequel, but this game is goated.

_childDocuments_.review: A good first RPG entry for the series.The story is comparable to the quality of Yakuza 0. Each chapter you go, the layers of the story peel off to reveal something different but not necessarily predictable.There are some cliches here and there but not something to pull you out of the immersion.Substories are great and suit the personality of the new protagonist super energetic outlook on life.There are so many systems and mini games to enjoy that it is a lived in world.Yokohama is a good fourth area that has been created.Notes:Of course here are the footnotes of what is a bit annoying to deal with.First issue is the leveling.The base leveling should be slower but the job leveling should be significantly faster to promote diversity of trying most of the jobs.  Most people will get their base level up to max before they even max out there first job.  It really should promote a mix of jobs to max out during the course of the story. The problem shows up in the end game when there is a handful of means to get the levels and stats necessary to stand a chance for the True Final Millennium Tower.The Kamurocho Dungeon for fast levelingFinal Millennium Tower for moneySotenbori for materials.Most players are going to need at least 20+ hours to get the job levels necessary in order to stand a chance.That's monotonous.  The devs gotta to tighten that up somewhere so grinding is kept down.Combat:Movement is randomly done by the teams and the enemies.So there are moves that are supposed to hit areas but you will have to time how these enemies move together. Even by luck, players will likely only line up two enemies at once which doesn't incentivize its use.  It's simply better to use the "All enemies" that ignores that aspect.For LAD 8, I'm halfway expecting a positional grid as a means of making it more predictable and tactical.One of biggest mechanics from the action side of the series is counters... well why do we only have a block instead?  Even Amon and Kiryu were able to counter someone when they got too close or did a regular attack against them.   Also the equipment system: no existing armor sets to make that interesting.It's just base stats and that's it.  For the protagonists wild imagination, the lack of interesting equipment stands out.

_childDocuments_.review: Good albeit very flawed game. Story/characters, mini-games, side stories are all great. One of the best in the series. But everything tied to RPG elements is either half-baked, half-assed or simply lazily made. Or it could simply be, as commonly known, JRPG. It's my first one and I might say I'm extremely impressed with the sheer idiocy of many of the RPG elements.Combat.The game is constantly straight up lying and deceiving the players. All these Medium/Heavy/Extreme damage values of skills are one giant BS. There are a lot of Medium skills that deal high levels of damage due to the way how animations work and scaling from Attack/Magic attributes.Status effect skills are useless. Completely and utterly. Why bother with casting something and then risking the chance of missing/losing your turn when you can simply deal damage or debuff the enemy or heal/use an item? DoT builds do not exist here and bosses are pretty much immune to nearly every type of status effect. At least debuffs do work on all enemies.After playing a lot of Western RPGs and especially Grim Dawn, Yakuza like a Dragon is pretty bad when it comes to build variety and itemization. Some of the jobs are pretty much useless. Higher difficulties make this too much apparent. The only purpose they might serve are passive bonuses and some of the skills which you share on your character regardless of the current job/class.Probably 90% of the weapons might as well be deleted from the game. Even on normal, after Chapter 9-10 their damage and bonuses make fighing trash mobs/bosses an extremely painful experience. There is no way to upgrade them, no illusion system to at least make some use of all these weapons that are just sitting there in your inventory.There is no item scaling. Enemies have insane HP values and you pretty much stuck with items which have values from normal diffculty. The only exception is one upgradeable weapon for each job/class.Bullet-sponges galore, hidden values/penalties on skills or on trash mobs, make playing Like a Dragon a chore. On Legend, even if you have max level character some piece of trash level 10 mob is going to dodge not only your attacks but also your skills. Who the hell designed, coded and then playtested this?Some of your attributes are also useless. Agility? A lot of mobs will go before you even if you have it in 600-700 range. Dexterity? I didn't notice any value in this attribute too. Critical hits are extremely rare and don't really add much damage. The best ones are HP, defense and magical damage. And of course, resistances. These are essential if you don't want to get one shot by some of the (mini-)bosses.Speaking of bosses, their design is atrocious. Probably the worst in the whole series, considering all the idiotic design choices made by the devs. On higher difficulties they will dodge a lot of your melee attacks/skills, so you are forced to use the same ranged skills over, and over, and over again for 10-30 minutes straight (depending your upgrades/magical damage). Some trash mobs found in two last dungeons can one-shot your characters and then wipe the whole party in 2 turns (and, no. I'm not talking about melee mobs). Ask me how I know.Last boss can one shot Ichiban regardless of resistances, poundmates or defence rating/HP, he just does. This is not a brawler, this is a turn-based RPG. And if you missed the window to use a skill from Hero job, called Peerless Resolve, go and pray to all RNG Gods you know that this abomination of a game design will not focus you two-three times IN A ROW. That's right. He can also go several times before you. And there are no checkpoints, if you die you have to pay money to retry. "And what if I don't have enough money?" Well, sucks to be you lol This was probabbly the devs line of thinking when they decided to design many of the boss fights this way. What's the point of autosave?Movement during combat is pretty terrible with camera constant dancing around your characters and zooming in/out or getting stuck somewhere and you can't see anything. If you suffer from motion sickness DO NOT BUY THIS GAME. "Heat" skills which constantly require you to skip their animations manually. Blinding, white screens before some of them (Genshin Impact loading screen says hello). Just brilliant design choices.If you think that's all, you are mistaken. RPGs are built on several pillars. Dungeons, epic loot (+crafting) and quests, combat and build variety. Well, LAD fails nearly in every single category.Dungeons on Legend difficulty have the same loot than on Normal. Same garbage hats that you can buy for 10k yen in some Pawn shop are dropping from Silver and Gold safes. Crafting materials? Well, take this x1 piece of plastic (when you need hundreds of them to upgrade your many weapons). And the best part, enemies have 3-5 times more HP but your items don't scale. Is this an RPG or what? Where are my Legendary Soiled Trousers with max stats, devs?The level design is also the most boring, lazy one you could ever think of. No secrets, no rare bosses which drop some great gear, no high payouts or tons of experience. Exception to this are some of the late game dungeons which, by the way, only small minority of players can even beat not even farm consistently. Great design strikes again.Quests do not give epic loot or experience which you might expect from an RPG. The only way to level up your characters is to fight all kinds of mobs. The problem is that to level up after 40-50 you need a lot of experience. And there is only ONE place in the whole game that allows to do it. 400-450k of experience per certain fight, 4 fight in total. With experience giving trinkets it's slightly faster but not when you need to do it dozens, potentialy hundreds (yes, you heard me right) of times. My record was 8 minutes per run. Do the math. Or, you can be a smart fella and visit Nexus mods for some goodies that might help you with this ♥♥♥♥♥♥ grind. You still need to waste a certain amoung of time to level up but it is nowhere near the amount needed when doing it the "people who like to waste their time" way.Performance issues, pretty bad GUI for a game with dozens upon dozens of skills and visual artifacts are also present. At least the game doesn't crash. One thing that all Yakuza games have, they are extremely stable. I don't remember a single crash in any of the games I played."So, why the hell do you still recommend the game?". If you play on normal difficulty many of the things I mentioned can be (extremely) annoying, yes, but the enemy health and some of the idiotic design choices have some workarounds. If you treat the game like a visual novel, Yakuza like a dragon is pretty good. If you treat it like an RPG, everything falls apart. It's as if the game was made by someone who read about RPGs on Wiki and never played or seen them personally.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 3.9 out of 10Yakuza Like a Dragon is a game from a series I've never truly explored before. Despite my initial enthusiasm, I found it challenging to invest in this 45 hour JRPG, barely clocking 17.4 hours, struggling to push myself further.The game's cinematics, while impressive, had an odd inconsistency, ranging from fully motion-captured sequences with stellar voice acting to awkward scenes with static characters and minimal movement. Despite this, I found charm in the weird side stories and quests, like employing a chicken in my company or facing off against mafia members in baby outfits. However, these bright moments couldn't dispel the fatigue brought on by repetitive gameplay mechanics and pacing issues.One undeniable strength of Yakuza Like a Dragon lies in its depiction of Yokohama. From the well-detailed signs and street posters to the alluring cafes, even the meticulously crafted architecture of the buildings, the attention to detail immersed me into the atmosphere of the city, giving me a refreshing take on open world games, at a time where most of them take place in the US.Initially, the turn-based combat system offered some enjoyment, but its sluggishness and lack of depth became apparent after a few hours. The novelty wore off quickly, leaving me with a sense of monotony, especially in the "dungeon" sections with their endless battles. While side activities provided some respite, such as having various fully-developed games inside the arcade section,  they felt like missed opportunities given the game's budget and potential for improvement in other areas, especially the cinematics.Despite its flaws, the game boasts a beautifully detailed world and a colorful cast of characters. I think Ichiban is amazing, I liked the voice acting, I didn't take him too seriously cause i knew he was not supposed to be taken as such. He's not the most in-depth character but it was always fun having him on screen. I also liked Nanba and Koichi and I think there was a great chemistry between all 3 of them. Despite that, when Saeko was added to the crew, i felt it was a bit odd that one of her power moves was applying makeup... But basic Japanese sexism aside, a great crew none the less. I did want to see where their story goes ,but again the game's pace bored me so much that I might never have the chance to do so.While Yakuza Like a Dragon may appeal to fans of the genre, it failed to capture my interest beyond the initial excitement. Its disjointed cinematics, repetitive gameplay, and pacing issues overshadowed its potential, leaving me with a bad taste in my mouth. As someone unfamiliar with JRPGs, I had hoped for a more engaging introduction to the genre, but unfortunately, this game fell short of my expectations. With that in mind, I stand by my rating of 3.9 out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Yay!  I finally finished the game... what a relief, since I almost gave up.The Good:-----------Great graphics.The world building was fantastic.  I actually felt that I was walking around these locations.Lots of different things to do via the mini games.Business mini game was intriguing and enjoyable.Fast paced (for the most part, see below for more details).Diverse set of party members.Not a total button masher.The meh:----------Lackluster romance options.Collect cans mini game.Dragon Kart mini game.The bad:----------The story was very good to start with but devolved to completely terrible by the end.Boss mob fights were totally ridiculous.Chapters 12-15.Overlong cut scenes and dialogue.Poor save game system.Far too much grinding required.Lack of in game information; had to rely way too much on internet searches.Honk honk spawns.Cockroach spawns.Kasuga really is a nut job, he overreacts to everything.Slow Job advancement.Although there is a wide variety of equipment with which to outfit your party, they are shown with their default outfits when out of combat, and with their chosen job outfits when in combat.  I would have preferred that they be shown with their equipped gear instead.Summary:-----------If this game had ended after Chapter 11, I would rank it as one of the best games I've ever played.  Unfortunately, Chapters 12-15 were so atrocious that they completely changed my opinion of the game.  They were nothing more than a grind fest, slow moving, and boring.All the goodwill that was built up during the first chapters was completely lost because of the need to grind, grind, grind.Based on how few people received the later achievements (only about 30% finished the game), I suspect that most of the positive reviews were done by folks who quit playing before they reached chapter 12.I'm glad I finished and deleted this from my hard drive.

_childDocuments_.review: I laughed when I heard the next Yakuza game was going to be a turn-based RPG, and only decided to pick this game up when it was on sale....and here I am at the end of it: ~100 hours committed, every achievement earned (only game I've wanted to do this for, so far), all characters maxed, and saddened that the journey has come to an end.The story is utterly crazy, as per Yakuza tradition, but honestly, I loved it. It's so off-the-wall, I simply couldn't look away. I wanted to see how Ichiban and his band of freaks would get out of whatever insane predicament they got themselves into.  (For my fellow millennials out there, I'd compare this story to one of the 'Golden Age' episodes of 'The Simpsons': wacky as hell, but has a great message and a lot of heart under it all.). Be warned, though, while  the story is insane, you should also know that the plot armor for the main characters is THICC AF, so if you're the type of person that can't handle over-the-top contrivances in the name of progressing the story, you may have a hard time with this one. For me, I'm used to this nonsense from the older games, so I saw it more as seeing how the writers plan to outdo themselves from the previous storylines.Also, I was skeptical of Ichiban 'Afro Ninja' Kasuga being the new face of the series, but hot damn, was I wrong. He's essentially an adderall-infused version of Kiryu, and that's not a bad thing at all. I've also read others mention that he's the inverse of Kiryu, which is reflected in their outfits. Kiryu's default white coat (cool/calm exterior) with his red shirt (intense underlying personality), while Ichiban wears a red jacket (hot-headed exterior) and a white shirt underneath it (good heart under it all). In any case, you grow to love the character, as well as everyone around him does. His supporting cast is very memorable too (with the exception of one I'll allude to later), so you won't get bored.For the long-term fans of the series, the fan-service is real in this game, but I don't think its to the game's detriment. In fact, this game feel like its the 'quintessential passing of the torch' game. You will see heavy usage of this theme throughout the story, and, in this regard, I feel like the fan service is warranted.The side-quests/mini-games are are awesome too. I think I only need to type out one phrase to sum up the awesomeness: "Shareholders Meeting Mini-Game". Some minor gripes though: the battle system is a bit wonky. For example, when casting AOE spells, sometimes it will take the caster a few seconds to get into position, and, by that time, the enemies might have dispersed out of the effective range. Speaking of AOE, sometimes it's a bit unclear as to what the effective AOE range is. There have been so many times I thought multiple enemies were in the effective range for splash damage (literally shoulder-to-shoulder!) only to see they'd not take any splash damage at all. This is primarily why I defaulted to the 'all enemies' spells as opposed to AOE when I could. Also, while positioning for an attack, characters might get caught behind obstacles/debris that they are programmed to kick and hit an enemy with, but I'd say that, more often than not, they'd kick debris with no enemy within an effective range. This further exacerbates my first point, and just looked silly. With all that said, be prepared to wait ~3000 years for your hobo companion to catch up to your squad and start his turn, because he seemed to be most affected by these nuances. I also didn't like that you always have to run back to the job center (that's only in ONE town!) to change jobs. I would have liked to see a job center in each city, or at least develop a way to change jobs through your phone. I know they wanted to keep it confined to the job center for 'immersion' purposes, I just feel like there was a better way to find a balance. Also, I kinda of wish there were more dungeons. I did like the 'true' final dungeon -- I just wish there were more instances of it that provided that level of difficulty. Finally, it was weird that one character you can recruit kind of just 'tags along' in terms of the story, and doesn't contribute much, while every other recruit-able character does influence the story significantly in some way. Not that huge of a deal, just felt like a missed opportunity for more character development. No matter how you cut it though: this is one of the best RPGs I've ever played, and is easily my GOTY for 2020 (sorry, Ghostrunner!) I literally enjoyed every minute of the grind (RIP Invested Vagabonds)-- and that says a lot!The Yakuza series never fails to entertain and has easily become one of my favorite game series. Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio: please make a sequel ASAP!

_childDocuments_.review: This is my first Yakuza Game. The absurdity of life is seldom written compellingly while allowing for suspension of disbelief. This game captures that in a way that I can't do justice. Buy the game if that sounds in any way appealing.I don't usually recommend, or even play turn-based RPGs. This one, though, is a wild ride that will keep you more than occupied. It has a small world, but deep slices of life that make it feel incredibly alive. The story is gripping, and it switches up faster than one can keep up with it; influence from the Godfather and Sopranos, along with classic samurai cinema is more than evident. I won't talk about the story itself, but prepare for meta commentary and be prepared to question yourself. The gameplay is where this title shines. The story keeps you motivated, but at any time, you can find yourself taking part in a real time, multi-day process of: bug collecting, corporation management, throwing darts, racing, mah jongg, poker, company recruiting, golfing, arcade gaming, karaoke, photography, grinding for crafting material, purchasing lingerie, collecting recycling, gardening, or even dungeon crawling. You cannot explore every single facet of the environment, but those that you can offer unexpected depth. Every character comes full circle, and every scenario has you questioning the reality of what you experience. The storytelling is beyond ridiculous at times, but always heartfelt. I haven't even finished the game yet, but I am not looking forward to it. There is so much to do, and the writing outdoes itself with every new mission or encounter. To fans of RPGs, mob movies, comedy, doujin manga, and this series, I strongly recommend this game. This game, and its whole team, seriously did a good job.

detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game Supernatural creatures are stalking the pop culture mecca of Akihabara—and you know that because they've turned you into one of them. Their only weakness, and yours, is sunlight, which means there's only one way to stop them: call them out on the streets, knock their clothes off, and expose their skin before they can do it to you. Arm yourself with a rolled-up poster, a guitar, a laptop, a magical girl wand, or (if you insist) an actual weapon, then hit Akihabara's colorful streets. Browse recreations of real-life shops circa 2011, mingle with Akiba's residents and tourists, and discover the town's many secrets. Will you work with the secret paranormal-hunting agency, give the creatures a fair shake (hey, some of them seem all right), or just look out for your otaku friends? Choose your side, choose your missions, and enjoy a freewheeling adventure with AKIBA'S TRIP: Hellbound & Debriefed. Key Features Playful Reimagining of Japan’s Electronics Mecca Take a virtual tour of 2011’s Akihabara district recreated in painstaking detail, complete with accurate street layouts and shops based on real businesses operating at the time. Fight Like a Nerd Wield an arsenal of replicas, collectibles, and other amusing objects as you humiliate vampires into submission in this playful twist on the 3D beat 'em up genre, all while wearing a stylish array of customizable clothes and costumes. Your Choices Matter Choose which faction to support in the fight for Akihabara and watch as your decisions affect the course of the story, culminating in one of several different endings. Full Dual Audio Enjoy hours of voiced-over banter in your choice of English or the original Japanese.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't ask for HIS measurements!Onto a more serious review. I wish there was a neutral recommendation but, since there isn't, I cannot recommend this game at full price.To preface this review, I played the original version and the plus version on a psp years ago.I love that Aquire has translated this game into English and ported it to pc. It makes it easier preserve such a great series.However, if you are coming in from Undead & Undressed, you may be disappointed.While it does say HD update, the graphics does not look great when it is up-scaled to 1080p and above. Also, the voice recordings sound compressed. This is to be expected when you port a psp game to pc. Story wise, it is interesting, albeit darker than U&U; it is the high point of the game. Like its successor, your choices can have consequences, whether it is picking which faction you support or dying in the first 10 minutes of the game. As for the world itself, while there are areas different than U&U, you do feel more boxed-in than U&U. Unlike in U&U, you are forced to go back to the map after leaving an area. It doesn't feel like you are exploring a world, rather you are exploring different levels.The biggest difference is in the combat. In U&U, they really polished it up and made it fun but, here, it just feels clunky. This is especially noticeable on Otaku and Holic difficulty. The game goes from a beat em' up style combat to rock paper scissors combat.If they block, you use unblockable attacks.If they use unblockable attacks, you use regular attacks.If they use regular attacks, you block and parry.This wouldn't be a problem if they mixed up what the AI does. However, if all the AI does is block for 5 seconds, attacks, and repeats, the fighting becomes very stale.Also some other quality of life mechanics weren't added yet. One of which is being able to leave the map with you weapon drawn. At first, this seems like a good thing but, it also means an enemy can knock you back to the map screen, thus losing any progress you had with an enemy, or any items on the ground.Healing is also a pain since you have put away your weapon mid-combat to heal and re-equip it again to fight.One of the most annoying parts of the game is where npcs would flee from a scene, whether it be from your bad reputation or you recently stripped a human. Sometimes, they would run into you and cause you to stagger. During that time, you can't really do anything until the npc gets passed you, which can be a 1 second or 10.If you do buy it, you can only save and change equips on the map screen, took myself a bit to figure that out.I will gladly change my review if the devs plan to something about the quality, mechanically or graphically. Anything really. If they aren't, at least make the price more reasonable.TLDR: The age of the game shows but, if you really like the Akiba's Trip series, by all means get it but, not at full price. If this will be your first Akiba's Trip game, go with Undead & Undressed.

_childDocuments_.review: After a little over 80 hours, I've finally got the platinum badge. Now, I would like to mention that platinum isn't the same as 100% I am not even close to getting 100%, there's still so much clothes and weapons and nicknames and other stuff to collect. I just managed to get all of the Steam achievements, but that's good enough for me! And now that I've gotten platinum, I figured I might as well write a review.So as you already know, this game was originally released in 2011 for the PSP, and now in 2021 they decided to release a PC HD remake. Now, I've never played the original PSP game, but I am certain that they have made good improvements, and it's also a very nice port. The Good (ranked in order from most important to least important):1. The story. I haven't played the 2nd game in like 3 years, but the story for this game is phenomenal. I love it, and I think it might be even better than the 2nd game. Maybe. Again, it's been a while so my brain is fuzzy.2. The (JP) VA. I've never touched the EN voice acting because I don't use EN. I'm a sub only kind of person. But it's actually really high quality, something I wasn't expecting from a 2011 niche game.(These two points, the story and VA, are so good that you could legit just play this on easy and treat it as a Visual Novel if you wanted to, albeit a pretty pricey VN)3. Replayability. With 5 difficulties, tons of unlockables and achievements, and a multitude of side quests and endings, there's some big replayability in this game which is great. It does start getting grindy if you're gunning for platinum but that's just how platinum typically goes.4. Stripping. Of course, going along with the name, stripping is part of the gameplay. If you enjoyed stripping people in the 2nd game, you'll love it all over again in this one. 5. Amazing English translation. I've played this game for 80 hours. I don't think I've seen a single grammar or spelling mistake. Acquire has some amazing translators, that I'll say.6, Fantastic port. The game is smooth and the movement is fairly tight with no input delay. I never dipped below 144 fps.The bad (ranked in order from the most frustrating to the least):1. The combat. Oh boy... it's just bad. It's just terrible. I hate to say it but I just can't get over the combat, and anyone who's played this game on Gamer+ difficulty can probably agree. There's no manual tab target so you can't choose your enemy, the camera is actively working against you, the combo system is just weird and doesn't work half the time, and the enemy cheats by being able to do things you can't do. 2. Unfair fights. This kind of goes hand-in-hand with the bad combat. Because of how difficulty scales in this game, in Holic all enemies can 1-2 shot you, even if you're in max clothing with food buffs. Basically, all enemies are mini-bosses. And there are some nasty fights where you're forced to fight multiple people. If you try to fight them the normal way, you just lose. There's just no way you can fight 5 people who are all able to 1shot you, dodge all your attacks, and block and surround you. It's just impossible.3. Camera. I touched on this a little in the combat section but the camera is just bad. It's just bad, nothing more to say. It gets really annoying when you're fighting in tight spaces like the final fight in UD+. It feels like you're forced to fight not only the enemy, but the camera.Mixed opinion:UV Sunscreen cheese: you know how I said that there's no way to win fights on Holic if you're outnumbered? That's only the normal way. Here comes UV Sunscreen cheese to save the say, which is an item that makes you invincible for 30 seconds. And there's no cooldown or nothing so you can just keep spamming it in fights all you want. Oh, and you carry 99 of them wherever you go so they never run out. So yup, basically there's an item built into the game that lets you be invincible. This is a good and a bad thing. It's good because it lets you actually make it past the incredibly unfair 1v5 fights in this game. It's bad because it's cheesy and it really shouldn't be in the game in the first place. But ultimately I'm glad it is in the game since beating Holic would be next to impossible without it.____All in all, I would recommend this game, but only if it's on sale or you're a huge Akiba's Trip nerd like I am. It's just... not a good game by today's standard. It's a fantastic port, but it's a port of a 2011 game in 2021. So what kind of person would buy this game then? If either you:a. loved Akiba's Trip Undead and Undressed and want moreb. love games where you collect a bunch of stuff (there's so much to collect. Holy hell, there might be too many things to collect in this game)tl;dr play Undead and Undressed first since that game won't make you yank your hair out because it actually has decent gameplay. If you want more, then think about buying this game. If you didn't enjoy U&U, then obviously you won't enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The story, setting and music make this game really worth playing, although you may struggle to keep interest because of the combat.Akiba's Trip: Hellbound & Debriefed is a remaster of a PSP game made 10 years ago. What your playing now is how I assume it was originally played way back then. Some things will definitely frustrate you at times (I'm playing on hard mode to start with so it may be a bit different for others) but combat is definitely not as easy and fluid as it was in Undead and Undressed. The buttons don't seem to line up exactly in time when you push them and the camera can be all over the place at times. It feels very tough to control and, if just starting out, it's going to make you just want to shut off the game and never look at it again. If you also manage to accidentally stumble upon a crowd of enemies near the beginning of the game, you're going to wish you hadn't even bothered in the first place.That being said, once you start upgrading your gear and start getting a feel of how things are timed, it is going to feel a bit easier. It's a PSP game with slightly updated visuals and not much else, so don't go expecting to be playing a top of the range product. Areas are smaller than they were in Undead and Undressed and you can't just shove past NPCs either, which adds to the claustrophobic feel to the environments.So I guess you're probably wondering why I've thumbs upped this game when I have so many bad things to say about it.The game really shines in its story telling and music. Honestly, I'm surprised with how likeable all the characters are and how the music fits with each situation. It sets up an interesting premise of vampires doing their typical vampire things, only this time you're ripping off their clothes to expose them to sunlight rather than doing the regular stab through the heart with a wooden stake thing or covering them in garlic (I assume). NPCs also react differently depending on how you play. If you attack too many vampires in your playthrough, they'll become more hostile towards you and attack on sight. While if you attack to many innocent bystanders, they'll flee and not want to interact with you in anyway. When the game description said that my choices mattered, I didn't think it would go this in depth (especially given the kind of game that it is).Each character is voiced very well (at least in English, I don't know what the Japanese version is like) and all the conversations flow naturally and keep you engaged as you follow along with the plot. People react and behave as you would expect them to in this weird situation they've been forced into and nothing feels forced. I'm only about 4 hours in but I'm already feeling like I want to know more and find out what will happen by the end of the game. The quality is somewhat compressed however. I think this was to put it in line with the original Japanese voices, so it doesn't feel too different between the two. Given how this was a Japanese only title to begin with they can't just go back and make the quality of the original voice files better so, as a compromise, they just decreased the English voice lines' quality.The music in this game is also very well composed. Each scene has the right track playing to help set up the tone of the moment, The battle themes are much heavier sounding in this game, in comparison to Undead and Undressed which has a more light-hearted, upbeat tone. I guess that was to fit with the more serious nature of the story, but they're still great to listen to.The graphics however are noticeably aged and makes you think you're playing a PS2 game. It's not as clean and sharp as it's sequel, but it's somewhat darker colour scheme and lessened bloom effects does make it look a bit better due to it's darker story. There's only so much you can do with a 10 year old game so, if you're more into more complex and advanced systems, this probably won't be the game for you. But if you're looking for a niche title, with some pretty interesting elements and a cool little story hidden within, give it a try. Final verdict: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I have been meaning to play ever since it was released on the PSP. Even my friends recommended it to me back then. For some reason, it has remained in my backlog until now.       Well, this game was originally released on the PSP, so the graphics are from that era. But to be honest, it could have been better. On top of that, it's an indie budget title. There are a lot of .png files of real-life photos used as in-game environments. For me, it's charming, but I have to mention that it's better suited for the PSP rather than the PC or PS4 port due to the low resolution. Some of the character 2D sprites don't scale well either. But other than that, I think the graphics are pretty good. I'm a sucker for old games, but I grew up with them. The 3D character models are also reused throughout the game, so they look totally different from the character 2D sprites. When my friends and I streamed this game on Discord, we always joked to keep our eyes at the bottom right of the screen where the character portrait is. By the way, the 2D art is really good! It's expressive, cute, cool, and sketchy, just the way I like it. It's far better than the 2nd game.        The world of the game is a highlight though! Even though I said the graphics are flawed, the world itself, the miracle holy city of Akibahabara, is faithfully created. Even the placement of people is accurate. It's built based on the real Akiba in 2010-2011. I had the chance to visit Akiba in 2018, and I remember the feeling of the city. I can say that it's still a match in the game. It's nostalgic to see 2011 Akiba in this game, even though I wasn't there at that time. There's a box of PS3 slim stacked in the case, posters, and culture from around cute and moe anime (thanks, 2007). It's something I've experienced even though I wasn't there myself. That's the power of subculture. The platonic ideal of a culture from around the city, the freedom to express a thought of oneself, a dream, the spark of youth, is well captured in the game setting. It's done so well, in my opinion.         Now about the gameplay. Let me tell you this: since many reviews here talk about how they can't pull out a combo or input a move, it works just fine for me. Just use the d-pad! I played the whole game with the d-pad and pressing the R button to turn the camera (yup, I'm an OG PSP player). I have no issues pulling off any combo or input command in this game. The game is built like a 3D-type tank control, so you have to respect that. But I have to admit that it could have been done a lot better, considering this is an HD port version. For the combat itself, it's just a beat 'em up that focuses on guarding and counter-attacking. Nothing fancy here, although you need to strip your opponent to defeat them, which is something interesting. Overall, it's fun enough for me.        The plot of this game is so stupidly crazy, but the developers commit to it so seriously that it ends up being pretty good! Throughout my 28-hour playthrough of the game, I really enjoyed it so much. For me, there was no downtime in the story, and every side quest was pretty fun to play through with all the funny and geeky dialogue. The heart of the story revolves around the culture and people of AKIBAHABARA, and I have to say it's well-written. It captures an ideal and a way of seeing things through the eyes of people who really love it there. You're not going to see this often in AAA+++ games. It feels like you're listening to a friend talk about their passion, ideas, and dreams. This is not just a fictional story, but it's mixed with the voices of people who created it. There's a scene where a character tries to explain why schoolgirl uniforms are special, and you will feel like it came from the heart of someone who's really into it. It's not forced or even feel weird. It's just people telling a story about what they love to someone. And the characters... oh my. They're pretty good! There are all the tropes of characters you think you're going to find in anime here. The main female character, Rui, is even voiced by one of the legendary SEIYUU, Hikasa Yoko! And yes, the voice acting is amazing (although the English dub sucks balls). Like I said, the characters are written so well. Even hard topics about real-life issues are written in a subtle enough way in the game. The boys Nobu and Gon are the best! I'll try not to mention the story since it's better to go in blind, but you can treat it as a 12-episode seasonal anime :D        The music is good, and you know it will be good because they got Dreamin by ClariS as an OP, and there are lots of additional songs in the game, such as a song by Mirin Furukawa and LAZY GUNG. The sounds you hear in the city are real sounds captured in the 2010s. It holds something so special there! "MOE MOE MOE CUTE"        In short, the whole game is a time capsule of a decade passed. Playing through the game feels like a fleeting dream. Now I understand why my friend recommended this game to me 11 years ago...

_childDocuments_.review: We already got the second and third games in this series released in the West, so it is about time we got the first – even if 10 years late.So this game is a bit unique. It feels like a collection of interesting ideas all thrown into one little package. Some of these work, some of them do not. The combat is a prime example of this. It revolves around this “strip” mechanic, where enemies are defeated only after you strip their clothing off. This also applies to you though, so a lot of fights end up becoming this tug of war mashing fiesta. It sounds kinda out there, but this was actually a very cool mechanic, as there’s this entire other layer on top of it in the form of equipment.Not only can you strip enemy clothes, but if you have the required skill for a given article of clothing, you are able to strip it off entirely without tearing it and pocket it in your own inventory. This allows you to then equip it in-between areas and benefit from its stats or other effects. It was really cool how the combat tied directly into your own equipment like this and was easily one of my favorite things about the game.However, the good points do not really go much further. Sure, the Akihabara level design is kinda neat, but the overall feel I got from this game was more so just “clunk”. Combat, for example, is not polished in the slightest. The strip mechanic is cool, but the actual act of attacking and dodging is oftentimes a pain. The camera is constantly working against you and because your dodging direction is tied to it, this leads to several instances where you will dodge left or right instead of back or sometimes even right into enemies.Then there’s the fact that attacks don’t always hit the way the animation looks and stun-locking is way more common than it needs to be. The overall movement and combat just does not feel right and offered more annoyance than it did enjoyment.When you are not duking it out with randoms on the street, you are going through the main storyline, which should not take any longer than 10 hours to beat. It’s not necessarily a bad main story, it’s just not something I am going to remember in maybe a month or so. The characters hardly receive any development and it is more so focused on cheap laughs than actually getting you involved with some deep plot or anything. That approach can work, but only when the core gameplay is strong enough to carry it and unfortunately that is not the case here.The game runs flawlessly at 1440p unlimited FPS on my 1070 Ti and even offers a launcher to change some basic graphical settings. Controls are great on an Xbox controller, but the default bindings for keyboard (just keyboard, no mouse) make the game practically unplayable for me. I could not find a way to rebind those controls.There are some good ideas here, but the incredibly clunky combat and mediocre storyline pretty much killed any sort of enjoyment I had with it. Maybe if you’re a fan of the other two in the series and want to complete your playthrough of it, but otherwise this one is an easy passFollow my  for more reviews + videos!

_childDocuments_.review: Let's get the bad out of the way first.1. It's rather overpriced for what it is. Get it on sale. This is a handheld game from 2011 with few touch-ups being done. It's especially weird that it is more expensive than its sequel which improves upon it in almost every way.2. Audio quality varies in the dub, I think some lines had to be recorded from home due to COVID restrictions. It's jarring at first but I forgot about the issue entirely after a while.3. Due to it being a PSP game from 2011, and hardly remastered at that, the graphics are pretty chunky. I personally have no issue with the graphics, I'm well used to playing retro games and I think it looks fine enough to enjoy. But it seems to be a dealbreaker for a lot of people.4. The combat is CLUNKY. The camera sometimes works against you, movement is stilted, and any situation where you're fighting multiple enemies is stunlock city. I recommend avoiding harder difficulties. If you play on Normal or Easy difficulties you can get strong gear to make up for the unfair parts and tank all the damage you'll inevitably receive. So with all of these negatives, especially some damning ones, why would I recommend this game?Well, to be honest, I'm just willing to put up with certain negatives if I find the overall experience fun. And I do here. Much like its sequel, the Strip mechanic allows for a fun sandbox where any NPC can become a combatant and any outfit you see anyone wearing can be yours to collect. While the combat is clunky, I don't find it completely unacceptable— it still does its job of making the dopamine in my brain go brr when I beat people up. The things I liked most about the sequel are here, but honestly that alone isn't why I'd recommend it. That'd just make me recommend the sequel instead, which in the vast majority of ways is the much better game.No, I recommend this game strictly for the story and characters. All the other elements are "passable", but the only real reason I'd suggest someone play this instead of U&U is because the characters and music really resonated with me in this game. It's been a long time since I played U&U so I may need to refresh myself on that one, but I think I like the cast and story of this one more. There's 5ish endings in the game and I'm working on the last one now. If you can stomach the flaws with this game, I really do think the characters make it worthwhile. And if you haven't played the sequel yet and find you enjoy this game, I think that'll let you appreciate the advancements the sequel made all the more.Last note: It might be worth picking up the deluxe edition for the artbook alone. This game is fairly obscure to the point that it's hard to find art and stuff for the game online. The art in the artbook more or less can't be found anywhere else. But more importantly, this game came out to celebrate the 10 year anniversary of the original PSP release. So the artbook includes a story in there from the perspective of Rui, telling us what things have been like for everyone in the 10 years since the events of the game's true ending. If you become attached to the characters the way I did, this story is really really cool to read and makes you feel nostalgic for them as though it really had been 10 years, even though you just played the game a few days ago. That alone makes the deluxe edition worth it, for me.

Great customization with hundreds of loot items, replayability with multiple endings and secrets — just love it! _childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Undead and Undressed a lot. The ridiculous premise is fun and the silliness of the fighting made up for it's shortcomings. This game is inferior to U&U in every way. Not that this was unexpected. U&U was the sequel afterall, but I was still hoping for a good experience. This is an utter slog.The combat in U&U wasn't good, but it was tolerable. The combat in this is ATROCIOUS. It commits every possible sin it can. Fighting one person is inoffensive at best but as soon as someone else joins the fray it's a button mashing stunlock nightmare. Your control on who your targeting is non-existant and you'll often have people hitting you in the back with no way to defend yourself. You have crowds of moronic NPCs bystandards that run into the middle of the fray and then blame you for getting punched in the face. You'll have cops come in and arrest quest targets, preventing you from completing them unless you leave and re-enter the area or attack the cop. Cops will arrest you through some arbitrary means of blowing a whistle and locking your character in place. The camera swings everywhere and gets stuck on walls staring at some fence or grafitti in the foreground. I struggle to recall a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat experience in my 30 or so years of gaming. I'm getting annoyed again just typing about it.The rest of what the game does it does well enough, but the combat is basically the only real gameplay there is. A re-release could have been an opportune time to fix some of it but this game comes warts and all, and the combat makes it a leper.Don't get it unles you REALLY REALLY REALLY liked U&U and need more.

_childDocuments_.review: Yeah, I can't recommend this one.Now hold on a minute. Even though I don't like this one, I do like the first one in the series (Even though this is technically the first one 🤣).The game play for this game was fun, don't get me wrong, but the story didn't pull me in.-How the Characters WereThe characters are the reason I have to tell you to skip this title, and just play the first one. Now I can't say that I hated the characters, but they were just so generic! Yeah, they were generic and boring. I feel like they wanted the friend group to be as strong as the friend groups in the persona series, but they ended up not achieving that...They were trying SO HARD to make the friend group have that persona friend group feel, but you can't achieve that with characters this lame! They were so generic. 🙁I did like the fact that they were a group of outcast otakus, but it wasn't executed well enough for me to like them. I wish they would have been more likable. The reason I am being EXTREMELY hard on the characters is because it's an RPG. If it were any other genre, I would have been a little less cruel. RPGs are so story-focused that if you don't like the characters you're doomed, because you will have to cut through hours of dialog from characters you don't care about. Don't know if this counts as a spoiler, but  Even though the Akiba Trip game series is a series that doesn't take itself seriously, I still wanted to like the characters a little more than they were. I'm not gonna go down the line for each character, but please know that they are pretty generic and boring.-Game PlayOkay, wow! The game play is not bad! 😃However, it is a little different than the first one. And please know that when I say game play, I'm refering to the combat system. Yeah, because there is so much boring dialog, you barely get to fight anyone. Why would there barely be any battles? 🤨It doesn't make any since! I understand it's an RPG, but the other one let you fight a little more than this one. I don't understand why! The battles are different than the other Akiba game, because you have to put more thought into your moves. I feel like the block button is a bit more useful in this game. However, I didn't play all the different game modes, so I can't say if one game was harder than the other. But they battle system is different. I think the other one was a bit better battle-wise. I feel that first time players will be disappointed if they just played the other Akiba game. If you are hoping for the same amount of battles like the first one, you'll be disappointed! 😃 Combat is just different. I have mixed feelings about it, but I know that these mixed feelings are because I played the other one, and expected this title to be the same.-MissionsYes, I feel like this deserves its own special section. They are kind of tedious... I feel like missions just made the game more boring than it should have been. Why? Because the game kind of forces you to do missions for money in a way. How do they do this, you ask? Well, missions are the only real way to get money if you don't want to have a bad reputation. If your reputation gets bad enough, people will start to attack you! It's bad enough that if you attack too many people by accident, you could get people to start coming for you, but if you attack random people on purpose... Man, that just makes the game SO MUCH HARDER! 😟And that's why players are burdened into doing missions for extra money. Yeah, you read that right. We are '... burdened' with the challenge of completing missions for cash. It wouldn't be so bad if they were fun. We only do it because we don't wanna get attacked the entire time we're playing the game! 😫Edit: Oh yeah, one more thing about missions. You only have a limited amount of missions to cut through. Once that's over, it's a wrap.-Just WAY to Long!The only real reason my play time on this game is so high is because it's a long game.This game is VERY time consuming. It took me over 40 hours just to complete one ending! I'm not sure if I even want to play the other ones. If anything, I'd rather play the endings for the other Akiba game. I just don't understand how a game this boring can have this many endings!What's left? 🤨What could we want to be left? 😟Am I really going to waste more of my life to find out? 🙁I'm not sure. -GraphicsYeah, it looks pretty bad.But I'm not going to go in on it, because it's just an import. The original version (as we all may know) was for PSP, and because its original release date (2011) it looks old. It did not age well (and that's just pointing out the obvious). But if you actually bought this game, you didn't buy it for the graphics. You most likely bought it because you liked the other game. So bashing this game's dated graphics doesn't feel morally right, because I know what I signed up for! 🤣But this only applies to the graphics. Yeah, I only knew what I was getting into graphic-wise.Though it's not the worst, I can't help but to get Custom Robo feels, which is a series that Nintendo should have rights to (I only think they have the rights to Custom Robo because that's the platform they are released on). And to be honest, I kind of like Custom Robo's graphics! This is gonna sound messed up, but I'm old. And back in my day, the graphics were SO bad that players had to use their imagination to make up for it. Game developers back in my day would create sprites, for the main characters, to give you some kind of an idea of what they were going for. So I'm only giving the graphics an 8 out of 10, because it's pretty nostalgic, which may not be a fair thing to do because it IS OLD, and not a modern game doing it on purpose.Either way, I like the graphics. But only because I'm old. 🤣-Control SupportUh.. for whatever reason, I had some what of a hard time trying to get my PS4 controller to work with this game. I was able to make it work while my controller is hooked up to a usb port, but it just doesn't work well with Bluetooth. I don't think this is a problem on my end though, because all of my other Steam games work well with a controller via Bluetooth connection. I would definitely tell you guys to really think about this before buying the game.-Over All Review.*Sigh*With bad control support, boring main characters, completely different game play (bitter sweet); graphics only good because I might be a hipster/and or old, and a story that is just SO BORING! With all of that in mind, I would tell you just to skip it. The only reason I would not try to use a teleport machine to be all like, "Dude, don't buy that game! you'll waste money," is if you are one of those people that loves this franchise so much that you have to have everything in your collection. I'll say this, I'm not a die hard fan of the franchise, but I do like the first one. So I'm not compelled to own it because it's there, and I liked the first one. But I know some people are! 😃For everyone else though, just play the other one.

_childDocuments_.review: I went into this game to see where the "Akiba's Trip" franchise started and I leave very disappointed. With this being the first game in the series, I understand that it will not be as polished or have the quality of life features the second game has, but wow. It's mind blowing how much better "Undead and Undressed" is compared to this one. The combat is the worst thing about this game. It is clunky and has serious collusion detection issues. Since you, apparently, can't lock on to enemies, you have to line yourself up with them and attack. If this were a one on one fighting game, that would be fine. As this is a beat-em up, the player being able to freely move and attack their opponents should be a priority in design. Once you have to fight more than one person at once, it becomes incredibly frustrating.  On the real, I'm glad this game exists. If it didn't, the developer never would have created the superior sequel. If you are even a casual fan of this series, do yourself a favor and stick with "Undead and Undressed".

_childDocuments_.review: This was so PAINFUL to play, I got the first game as a joke for valentines day 3 years ago and honestly I managed to fall in love with it, just the simple beat 'em up mechanics were so good, not to mention the world building, you could enter so many shops and half of them sold items you would never really need, then there's the clothing customization I loved, the silly sidequests, the diverse story, the absurd plot that tried to take itself seriously. My hope's weren't high for the remaster of the PSP game but it fell flat on it's face.when I think of a remaster i think of improving the game and fixing any issues with it, but my god this thing ages TERRIBLY and none of the issues were even glanced at.1.) This game doesn't have any skill curve, it's a skill cliff, that starts the moment you start. you aren't playing a game, you are dragging your face along the concrete wall of the game until you beat it.2.) Stun mechanics. you get stun locked a lot, like a lot a lot, like if you're fighting 2 enemies or more at once they can easily combo you out of existence, like when fighting the final boss before I could even move he managed to do 4000 damage to me. and that's not to mention the ACTUAL stuns, where you get stunned for 2 seconds if someone does enough damage to an unarmored part of your body. The only way i was able to beat some parts of this game where you get attacked by 3 or more people was by running around until the enemies accidentally attacked someone else and got in a fight with them.3.) the jokes, oh god the "jokes" aged horribly, some of the lesser ones are usually about a dude being abused by his girlfriend because of his hobbies, transgender people sounding very masculine for no reason, having to go buy "special items" for a sex addicted maniac, having to have your sister beat you up so a pervert can imagine what it tastes like. but the BIGGEST offender is that one of their re-occoring jokes is one particular agent continually being "forced upon and a borderline non-consensual way" by that sex addicted maniac. Just horrible, I spent most of the time playing this game giving a disapproving frown.4.) no locking on to enemies. I mean like it seems like it wouldn't be that much of an issue, but when you're fighting by the skin of your teeth preparing a power attack only for you character to decide they are gonna strike about 5 feet to the left of the guy then you just lost, purely because why not. It gets worse because sometimes you can miss by a few inches, at least trice i did an attack that literally had my arms faze through my opponent.5.) No quality of life improvements. There is no way to change your character's gear unless you go on the map screen. to get on the map screen you have to walk out of the zone you're standing in, so it takes an extra 30 seconds to change gear compared to you just using your phone like in Undead and Undressed. same with saving, you have to be on the map screen, and side quests, you have to go to a specific person on the map, and just getting certain clothes you have to buy books that can sometimes cost 100k. And god forbid you don't get those books by the time you beat the game, because for some reason in New Game+ you lose all you coins because you "donated it to charity", speaking of which.6.) You will have random people constantly come up to you for no important reason. You'll have kids come up to you and demand money, then try to fight you. You will have charity workers demand money. You'll have random band members just fight you for no reason. If you go into debt there will be a loan shark to fight you in every zone. It destroys the flow of the game.Honestly I can't think of any reason to recommend this game over Undead and Undressed, just get that one instead, and if you liked that game then MAYBE you'll leave this game with only a slight sour taste in your mouth.Edit: I got all 4 endings and it doesn't get any better, higher difficulties just means enemies an combo you easier.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun. I really enjoyed replaying it to get the other endings and I might even play on holic(though it depends whether I'm masochistic enough to do so). The combat... Well, it's definitely not the best. You can't lock on enemies so you end up missing attacks. There were times I missed an attack and the enemy hit me from behind. I had to buy a controller because playing on keyboard and mouse was a pain. While NG+ lets you keep items and clothes, money and levels don't carry over so that is something you need to look out for.The reason I kept playing despite combat being a main point in the game is because i absolutely love the setting and the characters. I fell in love with the writing and the music. I just can't get enough of it really. Though, some characters are not fleshed out as the others, I played with the Japanese dub first then switched to English on my 2nd playthrough. While the EN dub isn't bad, you can really tell who has a bad mic, though that may just have been because this game is a port, but I haven't played the OG on PSP yet so I don't know exactly. If the quality bothers you then I'd recommend the Japanese dub as I haven't encountered problems with it so far.While this game has its problems, it has its charms too. I'd definitely recommend this game on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: AKIBA’S TRIP: Hellbound & Debriefed is the precursor to AKIBA’S TRIP: Undead & Undressed, the smash hit that introduced a Western audience to the seedy underworld lurking in the shadows of the haven of “otaku” culture in the Akihabara district of Tokyo. Released as AKIBA’S TRIP Plus in Japan, players explore a rich setting based on the famous “Akiba” district circa 2011, hunting vampiric foes and tearing off their clothes to expose them to sunlight. This remaster brings the game up to modern HD graphical standards, all while retaining the charm of the original classic that sparked a cult hit series.
