name: Sonic Frontiers
detailed_description: Feature List Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game Experience Sonic like never before! Worlds are colliding in Sonic the Hedgehog’s newest high-speed adventure! In search of the missing Chaos emeralds, Sonic becomes stranded on an ancient island teeming with unusual creatures. Battle hordes of powerful enemies as you explore a breathtaking world of action, adventure, and mystery. Accelerate to new heights and experience the thrill of high-velocity, open-zone platforming freedom as you race across the five massive Starfall Islands. Jump into adventure, wield the power of the Ancients, and fight to stop these new mysterious foes. Welcome to the evolution of Sonic games! Please install “Adventurer's Treasure Box” and “Explorer's Treasure Box” before starting A NEW GAME. Please note that the contents will not be validated if it's installed AFTER COMPLETING THE TUTORIAL. Please ensure that the most recent patch is installed before installing DLC. The Digital Deluxe Edition comes with the Explorer's Treasure Box, which contains useful items for your adventure: Amy's Memory Tokens, a Portal Gear, Chaos Emerald Vault Keys, Additional Gloves & Shoes for Sonic, and a Digital Art Book with a 25-track Digital Mini Soundtrack. Experience All-New Open Zone Platforming Race across five massive overworld islands, each with their own unique action-platforming challenges and hidden secrets to uncover. Experience All-New Open Zone Platforming Race across five massive overworld islands brimming with dense forests, overflowing waterfalls, and sizzling desert landscapes, each with their own unique action-platforming challenges and hidden secrets to uncover. Unparalleled High-Speed Freedom Adventure across the Starfall Islands and see what each has to offer at the speed only Sonic can deliver. Blaze a trail as you see fit and discover side quests, solve puzzles, scale enormous structures, go fishing, and encounter a friendly face or two along the way… Challenge Yourself In Cyber Space Discover portals scattered across the island and venture into Cyber Space levels through portals scattered across the islands featuring signature 3D platforming at Sonic speeds, packed with challenges to put your skills to the test. Cyber-Powered Combat The Starfall Islands are home to strange creatures Sonic has never encountered before. Use the all-new battle system and skill tree upgrades to fight strategically, combining moves such as dodges, parries, counters, combos, and the new Cyloop ability to take down mysterious foes and colossal titans. A New Adventure Full of Mystery and Intrigue Become Sonic and journey to uncover the mysteries of the remains of an ancient civilization plagued by robotic hordes. With nothing but a handful of questions and a disembodied voice to guide you, set out to save your friends and the enigmatic inhabitants of the Starfall Islands from a colossal, mechanized threat. This game may be updated over time, and have paid for and free additional content released for it. Please be aware that this may increase the minimum requirements for running the game above the specification stated below.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly an enigma for me. As many flaws as I can critically acknowledge about it, the game is stupid fun, and for  reason I can only depart from it with a positive opinion- The game is super easy (the difficulty option feels like a placebo), with the combat, overworld challenges, and platforming being nothing to sweat at.- The progression loop of fight Guardians (for the Gears)->do Cyber Space level (for the Vault Keys)->collect Emeralds can be completely skipped by the fishing minigame of all things (I guess it's good for accessibility? but I feel there's more involved ways to do that than "here's a side game that can easily nullify the main game"), regular combat encounters and running in a circle with Cyloop can also net progression items for some reason.- Cyber Space levels reuse layouts from past games (which I'm fine with) but kinda bastardize the original theming and make them all feel the same by only having 4 (5?) level themes/backdrops- Sonic in the open world will fly 10 football fields because he tripped on a rock but you can almost never replicate it intentionally on a full ramp- Making upgrades so granular (it goes from Level 1 to 99) makes little sense for things like ring capacity & speed (which are both coincidentally the ones you have to level one at a time)- The bulk of the cutscenes are either just "character talking to/around Sonic" or "Eggman and Sage in Cyber Space discussing things"- The act of going "Every Game is Canon™" is okay at best and questionable at worst when there's not that much time spent on building any connective tissue/timeline across games outside of "they happened"- There's an interesting plot point/issue introduced pretty early on that gets completely solved in one cutscene when it starts to actually get interesting- The existence of the Side Story bits (where you use Memory Tokens to get a cutscene for extra Lore™ and not progress the main story) kind of limits character development wholesale and even as it is can already have continuity issues (I had a moment where Sonic and Sage were talking about a Titan as if it hadn't already bitten the dust 6 hours ago in my playthrough)- and plenty more issuesand yet...- Sonic Just Works™ in an open world, surprised they never really tried it before given how seamless it feels- Trying to S-rank 1-2 is some of the most fun I've had in a game in recent memory, I'm down to 47.31 seconds at the time of writing- The character writing is really good as much as the cutscene direction is so-so- The soundtrack is pretty amazing (having each level get its own song kinda rules, there's only a few songs I'm a bit meh on)- The combat, while stale at times (who decided that parrying should have zero timing even on Hard??), looks nice & flashy to compensate, and the Guardian fights (that don't lock you in a cutscene anyway) still managed to be fun even when nearing the end - Sonic flying 10 football fields is honestly kinda fun when you can find consistent spots to do it- The Super Sonic battles are lightly interactive cutscenes for sure, but man do they get me hyped! Fantastic animation and accompanying songsOverall, I'm having a cognitive dissonance moment where I know intuitively that the game is "bad" but I don't at all regret paying full price for it, and I would even recommend it to people who may've been jaded by Sonic's last couple of entries. I'll definitely be keeping a close eye on the series now, that's for sure

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game I enjoyed it and would wholly recommend to anyone who likes exploration and exploiting high speeds to do things you aren't supposed to.On the other hand though the game has a very low render distance for platforms and rails which is where the majority of collectables are so you might find say a memory shard on a platform but see no way to reach it because the rails are too far away to load this isn't a failing of your system or anything like that the game itself just isn't set to load the thing until you get closer and moving as fast as you're gonna be you will be back tracking alot, the open world stages are more like theme parks in that sense that you'll spend most of your time looking for the start of "rides" as I like to call them where you hop on and sonic is either transitioned to a 2D format until you reach the collectable or just sent hurtling towards it and because the start of these rides can be outside of the render distance from the collectable it's best to just hop on every "ride" you find as opposed to going direct to the collectable.Next we got to talk about the game's overall design you'll notice that there are lots of things that are just not linked at all you'll get the sense that they had all these things they had to put in because "Japanese company" and new things are scary but not keeping up with trends is bad this game pretty much embodies a problem with gaming I refer to as "exception to the rule", using momentum as an example you aren't supposed to have it in vast amounts of the game in the open zones you're more or less magnetized to the floor even when going over a ledge (that isn't intended to be scale able) you'll often stay attached to the surface with god like traction rather than rocket in the direction you were going notice I used the word "often" because sometimes you do rocket off and get serious air and it's really fun, you might be thinking to yourself "that sounds like a bug" to which I say nay because it seems to be tied to the way they sectioned the map you can perform these feats of momentum consistently at the same places most notably places near "tower" enemies but as to not let us have too much fun these are pretty much only otherwise found in places on the map that aren't populated with "rides" or enemies.You will get the sense that you're punished for creativity that you are made to do things a certain way, this is most obvious when you find a better way to get to a "ride" and the camera just doesn't co operate because you didn't start at the beginning of the ride a mistake that suggests the real struggle they have with open world formats and really highlights the fact we don't have momentum based exploration anymore  they want to put you on rails all the time and it feels like the reasoning is "you can't handle the speed" to which I would say then give us a way to control the speed rather than Walk->Run->Boost, speaking on the boost for a moment it's bound by default on the controller (please play this game on a controller it's so much better) to the trigger, an anolog input! just give us variability in the boost on that trigger and we'd be golden! (but I remember this game had to be on switch)so in conclusion while the game is good it is only good because there's a bit of everything for everyone but outside of the sections you enjoy you'll find yourself kinda bored and the lack of cohesion from all these different gameplay elements can be super jarring

_childDocuments_.review: It has been years since I've sat down to play a modern era Sonic game, and genuinely got glued to it. I was born into the Adventure Era of Sonic games (98-04), and this game is a beautiful blend of it. Personally I wish the story was a little bit more intense and as edgy as those games, but I'll take the quality of the story over recent ones any day of the week. While this game made me feel like I was playing other titles with open worlds, this blue hedgehog had it's perfect twist. The spin dash for me will be missed(unless Im missing the controls), but the boost button with cyloop is just break neck speeds in the islands. The only downside I've had so far is the cutscene's aren't pre-rendered like the ones used in Unleashed, but everything else blows it out of the water. As others have said the First major boss, is pure redemption for this brand. Sega, please use this game as a gateway to remaster the Adventure games, become daring in level design, and putting edge back in hedgehog. This game is an easy 8/10 for me!

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Sonic franchise, I was pleasantly surprised while playing the game. With the regular Sonic gameplay style integrated into an open world, I felt that this format really immersed me more in the world and storyline presented to me. The game even added a bit more variety in what I can do. Especially as a person who generally "sucks but tries" at games, it was challenging yet forgiving enough for me to not drop the game. But most of all I enjoyed the portrayal of my beloved childhood characters as they kept the humor tasteful and true to their character. There hasn't been any issue I've had as of yet except some graphics not loading, but that's to my old GPU to blame. Nonetheless would definitely recommend this game who wants to try this new spin on Sonic games!

_childDocuments_.review: What an experience.. I've officially 100%'ed Sonic Frontiers, and I have a lot of things to talk about. I really like this game, but there's some glaring issues that keep it from quite reaching the same level as some of the greats of Sonic history. I've got a lot to say, so I'm gonna go through this category by category.Aesthetics & Presentation: This game is one of the best looking sonic games so far. I absolutely love the technicolor edges and bright colors of the cyberspace levels, and I love the wide open and realistic views of the open world. However, I think this game's lighting could use a little bit of work to make it look just a little bit better. The voice acting is top notch for Sonic, and I like Roger Craig Smith's performance as Sonic. The more serious tone he gives the character in this game works pretty well all things considered. It was a high note for his Sonic performance to end on. The supporting cast is also played well. However, in many of the cutscenes, the characters seem quite static, and don't show much expression through body language or facial expressions. Overall, the aesthetics and presentation of this game are very high up for a Sonic game, but with a little bit of polish, they could have been some of the greatest we've seen so far.Story *SPOILER WARNING, SKIP TO NEXT PARAGRAPH IF YOU DON'T WANT SPOILERS*: The story for this game has its ups and downs. On one hand, I like the lore implications of the Chaos Emeralds not being from Earth, and the Ancients being related to Chaos; the God of Destruction. I like the way that Cyberspace and Koco are implemented into the story, and I love Sonic's interactions with Amy, Knuckles and Tails. I especially love the way the game talks about Tails' insecurities about his past mistakes. It was very clear to me that the game was fixing the mistakes of the past, (Sonic Forces) and returning Tails to his former glory. I like Sage and Eggman's interactions, and I love the idea of Eggman growing into a bit of a father figure for Sage. However, once again the problems with the presentation make it a bit more difficult to get invested in the themes and emotions of the story, meaning that when Sage dies, it may be hard for some to feel any significant emotions about the event. Overall though, the story in Frontiers is one of the best Sonic has had in years, possibly being the best since Sonic Unleashed back in 2008.Music: Damn this game's music is good. The themes for the open worlds are very nice and relaxing, and the cyberspace levels have some pretty good tracks. However, easily the highlights of this game's soundtrack are the boss battle themes, and the credits themes. "Undefeatable", "Break Through it All", "Find Your Flame", and "I'm Here" are absolutely amazing tracks that really get you invested in the intense battle. "Dear Father" is a nice send off for Sage in the end credits, and "One Way Dream" and "Vandalize" are both excellent finales for the game. I honestly don't have anything negative to say about this game's soundtrack, and I'm honestly disappointed it wasn't nominated for best soundtrack of the year.Gameplay: The actual gameplay of Sonic Frontiers is absolutely golden. I cannot tell you how fun it was running around in the open world and getting combos on basic enemies and guardians. I enjoyed searching for memory tokens, and playing minigames to clear more of the map. The Cyberspace levels are more akin to the boost stages of Sonic Unleashed, Colors, Generations, and Forces, and though they are fun, they don't reach the same level as most of the boost games. They're better than Forces, but below all the others. They don't overstay their welcome though, as most hardly last more than 2 minutes. However, some are fun to run again and again in order to get the best possible time. The fishing levels with Big the Cat are very relaxing, and even incredibly rewarding, as you can get some amazing stuff from the minigame, including power seeds, defense seeds, lost Koco, memory tokens, gate keys, portal gears, and even Eggman logs. This is the third game I've ever 100%'ed on Steam, and I had an amazing time doing it from beginning to end. It was really fun.Bosses: While the mini-bosses aren't anything to write home about in this game, the Super Sonic boss fights are absolutely spectacular, with the exception of Supreme and the End. Giganto is an amazing first boss, and serves as an excellent introduction to Super Sonic, who hasn't made an appearance in a mainline 3D Sonic game boss fight since 2011. Wyvern acts as another excellent boss fight, and though in my opinion it's not quite as spectacular as Giganto, it still serves as an excellent boss battle. The Knight is arguably the best of them all, with the most unique and interesting moveset and mechanics. Supreme is a step down from the first 3 bosses, but is still a fun, if short boss fight. However, if you play the game on hard mode, you get to fight The End, which is essentially a more difficult version of the hacking minigames you play throughout the game. While it is fun, and even somewhat challenging, it's a massive step down from the other Super Sonic boss fights. While it's fun, it's just not a satisfying final boss.Ending: Despite the disappointing final boss, the ending to Sonic Frontiers does have some value to it, though it's still not the game's greatest strength. It tries to pull at your emotions with the death of Sage, and while it partially succeeds, it doesn't have the full effect that I think it was trying to go for. It's not terrible by any means, but it isn't the greatest either. Conclusion: Sonic Frontiers is a game that brings a lot to the table. It has an excellent overworld, amazing combat, a wonderful soundtrack, and a nice story. The game looks very good, however some of the presentation could use some work. While most of the bosses are incredibly fun, the final boss and ending of the game do have some disappointing features. Overall, Sonic Frontiers has some of the best qualities of any Sonic game in history, but its flaws just barely keep it from reaching the same level as the greats of Sonic history. With a bit of polish, it could have rivaled games like Sonic Mania, 3&K, Adventure 2, and Generations as one of the greatest Sonic games of all time. With that being said, I think its strong points massively outweigh its flaws. I'm very excited to hear that this game will serve as the template for future Sonic games. I definitely recommend you give Sonic Frontiers a try, especially if you're a Sonic fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine being in the right mood and someone gives you a bag of chips that for whatever reason hits, so now that chip is your favorite you get whenever you go out.Sonic frontiers is by all means the best 3D sonic game we've gotten lately. The open world sections are fun and easy to mess around in, no area feels like a void of emptiness. the new combat is fresh and exciting. Lastly, the fishing minigame is a nice break from everything you experience up to this point.I hope we get further games to tweak and refines these features.First the story:This has by all means been the most elaborate and continuity indulgent game in the since shadow the hedgehog. You'll have tons of call backs to previous games, some of which are bit more impactful in the moment than others. Which is something the series has been starved of for the last decade. I don't returning to old stages or memorabilia like in Generations or Mania, but instead characters talking about events and factions that have been dormant for a while.The tone the story sets for this makes a lot of the relationships between characters feel so cared for as for the last few years everyone who when they would show up, boiled down to their one quirk they were known for and that was it.Knuckles feels like sonics rival again, tails feels like his own person again, amy is showing her backbone again. If you're a fan of the series, especially if you're the guy who loves sonic in its entirety this has been what we've been waiting for.Quick side note for this, without being spoilery, this game does mention the IDW comics. If you haven't been reading those, nows probably the best time to get on it. As it leaves me excited for whats to come next.action stages:for the most part the action stages are serviceable. they might not have the newest aesthetics or original levels, but they do the job they need to in order to break up the gameplay. the 3D stages are usually from the adventure games, or generations, possibly one or two from colors im failing to recall. I loved being able to run through these again, especially since you can use sonics new movement options to get around (not combat moves though, lets not get crazy now).the 2.5D stage felt great, I hope more modern games try this is if the next game doesn't do full 3D anymore. The feeling of going around corkscrews that would ledge you around mountains in the foreground and background is always a nice feel as though you're not truly on a "go right only" track.The 2D stage are fine. I never felt movement was wonky there, but I often thought they were too short. not all of them. there were a couple annoying ones however, especially a couple mid game stage that relied on gimmicks that had weird hit boxes to use the little launchers that give you a timer to hit a button prompt in a small maze like fashion. It was stupid, it was slow, if you messed up at any point you had to start over, it sucked.Cons:there were only 3 main issues I found with the game in my time of 100% completion.-In the hub world, you can sometimes shift into 2D as you're running around. Normally this feel fun and you think nothing of it because its typically what you wanted to do. However, if you step on something that slips you into 2D in the open world, unless you either finish the path your now on, you're stuck there. meaning, say your running through the grass, you accidentally hit a boost panel that puts you into 2D, you can't run into the foreground or background to quickly get out of it. Whatever you were trying to is interrupted until you either finish that path or jump behind the boost panel that put you there. some of which have enough boxes in the way you can't to do this. This is especially apparent in the Chaos world as many open world sections thrust you into 2D when stepping in the right spot. Its not a glitch, but its annoying by the lack of an easy fix. I hope sonic team patches the game to give you the ability to walk out of these 2D sections when you want to. it gets frustrating.-Theres an easy glitch to trigger when you die to the 3rd boss. In a certain phase it'll rotate to the left or right, the camera will try to keep up with it. if you die, proceed to  beat the boss, then save, if you press up or down on the left stick, the camera will proceed to rotate to the left or right respectively, endlessly. I managed to fix this by turning my pc on and off again, but was worried I was stuck with an endlessly rotating camera for the rest of my run.-this ones not as bad, but confusing, there's an island mystery icon on the world map for the Chaos world that doesn't disappear when you get it. doing it for the story alters the map slightly. chances are you'll forget you've been there based off these changes, Me and friends kept going back thinking there was some crazy post game challenge earned for completion. only to learn it was nothing.off hand comment, the sounds slaps. sonic games usually knock it out of the park, this one is just that.final verdict:9/10TL:DR world 3 is frustrating but otherwise sonic is doing great

_childDocuments_.review: One of the better sonic games in recent times, although it has a bunch of questionable decisions that make it feel like Sonic Team hasn't actually learned from their past mistakes and instead made a decent game by accident by throwing as many random ideas into it as possible.The bulk of the game is still really good, but the final boss and hard mode final boss are extremely anticlimactic and leave a sour taste, especially after how awesome all of the other bosses are. It gives the impression that there was originally supposed to be a completely different final boss, but the game got rushed. Badly. A lot of the cyberspace levels have reused designs from Generations, so if you've played that game they could feel samey. At least the designs themselves are fine.There's also a fishing minigame, so that's neat.The "open zone" areas are okay. Enemies are varied and interesting and the combat system is simple but really fun. I hope Sonic continues to be allowed to kick things. The parkour system feels way more at home here than whatever Lost World was trying to do. The floating obstacle courses that cover the landscape provide something to do while running around an otherwise empty map, but their pop-in is really noticeable and there's not an option to turn up the LOD distance.The soundtrack is phenomenal and full of absolute bangers. Visuals, not quite as much but still okay. The environments look cool, the enemy designs in particular are really cool, but Sonic himself looks out of place since he's not in the same artstyle.The story is solid throughout with the characters being far better written than in Forces, having better voice direction too, and there are loads of references to earlier entries in the series, canon be damned. Ian Flynn did a great job.Overall it is definitely a good game...But.If you're a Sonic fan, you probably will get a lot of enjoyment out of it, but all of its weird issues, as well as its ending, will probably leave you conflicted and frustrated.If you're not a Sonic fan, why are you reading this?I guess we'll see what Sonic Team has learned in another half decade.

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 7.5 / 10 A really phenomenal return to form from Sonic Team after years of misses. I really hope they can keep up the momentum and produce more work of this quality in the future. The UI definitely needs some fine tuning though, as most interactions with vendors, or even in the pause menu, can feel a little clunky and sluggish.  Pause > Select which option you want > Select restart level > Hit yes to restart level. If you make a mistake on a traditional level in this game, it can be more worthwhile to die sometimes and auto respawn hopefully before you made the mistake then it is to restart the level, if the time score isn't a factor.Overall fantastic game, and a major stepping stone for the Sonic Team in terms of quality. The movement, combat, puzzles, they all give Sonic a fresh new feel that I haven't really seen since playing older sonic games from my childhood. The boss fights are also some of the best in a long time, although the last boss' pacing was kind of subverted while playing on hard mode, giving me a separate section that would have normally been a Quick Time Event after the main boss fight itself. It came with some extra dialogue / lore, but overall, I feel like the main pacing kind of stumbled because of it, and it should've been something you did leading up to the final fight.The levels are all varied, although some mini bosses do repeat themselves, bringing a new area to sprint through, and many, many collectibles to find. The game is very packed with lore about this world and the story itself, but not spoon feeding it to you, allowing you to find it at your own pace, or not at all.My biggest complaint overall, is the UI can feel ridiculously slow in comparison to the game itself. If I finish a cyber level, get a bad time, or miss an objective. I have to wait several seconds before I even get the option to restart it, then go through the loading screen after that. Leveling up can also take ages. I was thinking about maxing out the levels for Sonic just to get the achievements, but leveling up his speed or ring capacity once takes almost 10 seconds each to complete, and doing that 196 more times to fully max out the levels did not seem appealing in the slightest. Which makes that whole process feel very sluggish for a game that you are so fast in. Especially in comparison to another vendor that takes the resources required, and just applies them to the levels in bulk, not requiring multiple interactions.

_childDocuments_.review: I originally listed this review as negative because of the DRM. I've decided to relent though, because I think this game truly deserves a positive review. It's not going to be for everyone, but if you like going fast then you'll probably have a good time.From start to finish I enjoyed every minute of it. The soundtrack was on point, the story was simple but good, the combat system was fairly engaging, and the open zone movement felt fantastic. The fishing minigame is very relaxing and gives you a way to bypass the more tedious parts of grinding if you want to.That being said, it still has plenty of the usual Sega jank:- I noticed that a few pre-rendered cutscenes were very low-quality. I'm talking like double-digit render samples and no denoising kind of bad (if you've used Blender's Cycles rendering engine or something similar, you'll know what I mean). And why does Sega need to use low-poly assets for pre-rendered cutscenes? This is 2022, not 2008 lol- Some of the character movements are a bit stiff in cutscenes and gameplay. This didn't happen enough to drag me out of the experience, as most of the animation is good, but I still felt this was worth mentioning.- The 2D gameplay segments can be pretty awkward to navigate.- Some performance hiccups here and there, probably because of Denuvo. These were a bit annoying, but not enough so to spoil the fun.TL;DR If you're into rolling around at the speed of sound, it's a good place to go now to follow your rainbow. If the lack of polish has you on the fence, I might recommend you wait for a sale and/or watch some reviews before purchasing.

_childDocuments_.review: Glorious step into the right direction for Sonic games. The game is very fun, but not suitable for prolonged sessions because some of the ingame systems are repetitive. _childDocuments_.review: Gameplay: Sonic Frontiers as you know is comprised of two main gameplay styles: open zone, and the more traditional cyberspace stages. Starting with the open zone gameplay is actually pretty fun, the little traversal challenges that are littered throughout the open world can be pretty satisfying to run through. Although later into the game it switches to mostly 2D which was probably the lowest point for the open zone as well as the physics being a bit janky at times. Otherwise, I think this format works well for sonic and is overall just a blast to run around in.As for the combat  I think its serviceable and serves as a good blueprint for a gameplay style that can be improved upon in later titles assuming they don’t just throw it all away in the next title.Now onto the cyberspace stages which in my opinion, is the worst of the two styles although that doesn’t mean its complete trash. Most of the level design is taken from previous sonic games with some working better in this style then others but what really brings down the experience is my main problem with cyberspace: the physics, it really feels like a boost game with the speed of 06. That doesn’t stop some of the cyberspace stages from being enjoyable, I had a fun time with them and trying to guess what sonic game it was from was pretty fun too (although it was almost always very obvious).Story:As to avoid spoiling the story I will make this very brief, I enjoyed the story pretty much up until the end where I have mixed feelings with some of the choices made. Overall, the story is leagues better than what we were getting in earlier titles.Music:Sonic music is always pretty good, and this game doesn’t disappoint, pretty banger soundtrack that had me bopping my head throughout most of the game.Graphics:For a sonic game, the graphics are ok although I wish the islands had more unique designs or at least looked more interesting. The animations look ok and the combat animations look pretty good although they can be robotic at times.P.S. while i do recommend this game, I don't think it's worth the $60 unless you're a big enough sonic fan for that not to matter.

Oh and the soundtrack is probably one of my favorite of all time. It has such nice variety going on yet it's still really consistent in what it tries to deliver at each given point throughout the game. Can't wait to see what direction the franchise will take from here. 8/10 would replay and recommend

_childDocuments_.review: Between this, the second movie, the Netflix series, and... at least the animations for , Sonic the Hedgehog fans ate well in 2022.I will admit that I was skeptical when I first heard it's following the open-world trend. Like, if SEGA somehow can't even get linear levels right anymore, how was a fully explorable world supposed to work? My hopes went up as I saw it wasn't going to be bargain bin price right off the bat, then went down with a bad gameplay trailer, and then back up again once a better one came out a few days later on Nintendo's YouTube channel of all places.My point is, the anticipation for this game was quite the ride.But, let's get down to brass tacks: I loved this game.Is it perfect? No. There's a bit of a lack of polish here and there probably due to getting this out for the holiday season, but this is the best Sonic game we've seen in a long time, and not just by Sonic standards. I'm debating whether or not this dethrones my previous favorite entry in the series.The open-world is where this game shines the most. Running around freely as Sonic feels very satisfying. The controls are surprisingly tight; I think this may be the best control over Sonic and gives the player the best feel for what it would be like to be Sonic than any of the games have ever had. Regaining control after missing a jump or running the wrong way was almost always easy. I did find myself shot off a cliff either due to weird physics or missed rail detection, but even then I often was able to steer myself around and make my way back onto land. Combat is pretty fun, and there are plenty of enemies and moves to learn to make each fight feel different. Admittedly, the RPG elements are a grind. You have to collect items to boost Sonic's power, defense, speed, and ring capacity, and upgrading those latter two takes forever due to the nature of boosting them.The cyberspace Zones are... okay. Apparently some people don't like them at all, and they are definitely the weakest part of the game, but I don't think there are any I truly hated. If I had a rough time with one, I often found myself picking up the rhythm after finishing it once. Unfortunately, each of the zones are only based off of four previous levels in Sonic history: "Green Hill" (because of course "Green Hill" is here), "Chemical Plant," "Sky Sanctuary," and "City Escape," so the look of each level does get samey. Thankfully, each zone has its own song and gimmick, so it never gets too repetitive. Unfortunately, S Ranks are now only based on time, and hitting enemies actually slows you down, so to get said rank, your best bet is to ignore them altogether. It feels wrong. Not that any are hard to get. Well, except for  level. You'll know it when you see it.The boss fights are amazing and satisfying. I don't want to give these away. Go into them blind if you can.The music isn't quite what you'd expect from the series, but I don't think there are any songs I would truly call bad, just different. There weren't any I didn't at least enjoy to an extent.Finally, the plot and characters are much better than we've been getting. It feels more like the  era in terms of story, and the dialogue was written by Ian Flynn from the comic series. Characters are actually acting like themselves again; Amy is the heart of the group (without being summarized as "likes Sonic"), Tails's techno-babble nonsense has been replaced with a more advanced vocabulary (AKA: actual words), Knuckles feels like he has a rivalry with Sonic again (something Shadow seems to have taken away since he was introduced in ), and Sonic isn't spouting cringey, undeserved one-liners every time he opens his mouth.Overall,  is one of the best experiences with the series I've had in a long time. If you're on the fence or don't like paying full price for a short game, maybe wait for it to go on sale, but you're doing yourself a disservice if you sleep on this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some performance issues on the Deck, Frontiers is a decent open-world game and a pretty solid Sonic game.Compared to classic 2D Sonic:- Levels are shorter, but there are 8+ per zone- Mechanics favor Sonic Adventure over 2D titles- Easier, even on Hard and Fast (so far)Compared to Adventure:- Sonic controls even better! Movements can be combined in ways we haven't seen before, and when done properly, you never have to stop boosting. - Levels have the same if not even greater sense of speed - Open world areas are obviously a greater focus this time around, with hundreds of little collectibles and good design. For sure worth it as a Sonic fan, if you are on the fence as a non-Sonic fan I can still recommend it, but wait for sale.*Play with Japanese voices.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, so, finished the game collecting everything, only two achievements I don't have are "Phantom Rush combo triggered 50 times" and "fight with every guardian there is", which I don't see the need to do.In short, 7/10 game, could be improved a lot, right now it feels more of a framework. But I did have fun, collectathon gameplay does make me feel pretty happy, thoguh it might not be for everyone.+ If you wanna control Sonic in a somewhat open area, try this.+ If you wanna hear banger songs during bosses and see some of the best spectacles in Sonic's history, try this.+ If you want very well characterised characters from the Sonic franchise, try this.+ If you just want a decent Sonic game, regardless of the formula, try this. I had fun, you can have fun too.+ Environments are very pretty in the right weather. Ares is especially beautiful at night.+ Interesting variants of mini-bosses/guardians - massive beasts, sand-sharks, flying platforms/grind-rails, ninjas, tornado-makers... I recommend trying each one at least once.+ Spectacle moments are spectacular, cinematic camera angles are pretty well done.+ Plot, however basic, has actions, consequences and stakes - game is not "just another wacky 'comedy' adventure of Sonic and his unimportant sidekicks".+ Sage is pretty cool - the idea of her and Eggman's relationship could be toned down a little, but I like her character.+ Koco are pretty cute.+ Robot designs are pretty cool.+ Cosmetics for Sonic are a good idea...underdeveloped, but good.+ Game is running at 60 FPS almost all the time with High settings (only Low shadows, but I found they do not make that big of a difference when compared with High shadows), very commendable.+ Pre-rendered and hand-animated cutscenes are pretty cool - characters use their ears and body language to express emotions (could use a bit more emphasis on the ears and tails though, the characters are based on animals after all).+ UI is easy to understanda and navigate.+ Some experimentation is a welcome change from Sonic Team.+ Fishing is relaxing AND useful+ Quite addicting lol+ Got me a little emotional at the end - Plot is very basic, likely a start for something more. - There is no mind-blowingly fast Sonic - Sonic is very fast here, but enough so that you can control him in the Open Zone, not to break the sound barrier (be sure to use boost though, otherwise Sonic will move slower - which allows for more precise platforming).- Shallow combat mechanics and abundance of level-up materials make sthe game very easy. (Not enough skills, not enough places to use them in, you can get all skills at the start of the second island).- Second-to-last island is not a full area, in fact, it isn't even a new island, last island's theme is the same as the first - seems like there wasn't enough time to properly conceptualize the last island and its obstacles (or maybe its inclusion was towards the end of development).- Menus take a bit too long to respond.- Elder Koco's incremental style of leveling up is torturously slow.- Way too much air-positioned challenges - so many rails and springs, but not enough stuff on the surface or on the ground. In other words, the world could use a bit more of that cartoony Sonic style structures (loops, cliffs, built structures), as of now, it is a bit too realistic. This does HELP you when running around, but every challenge must be somewhere in the air then.- Final bosses are way too easy and in general, the endgame feels like it is running out of steam.- Character animations in the non-story cutscenes feel dead and liek puppets.- References to the past games were happening at a bit too fast rate.- Cyberspace levels are way too easy (except 1-2, that one is something else).- A lot of talking-only cutscenes, not enough action in some (mainly Eggman).- No indicator for completion when fishing with Big.- Some surfaces can be ran on, some cannot, but the logic sense is not always there.- Cannot replay bosses (literally the coolest part of the game).- In spite of appearance changing options, there are no collectibles for this.- One time a pinball game is introduced and it is blocking story, that is just bad design.- Lighting issues (the ground can reflect a lot of sunlight, though dirt and grass aren't exactly mirror material, are they).- High shadows cause random lags (but everything else on High settings is working smoothly).- Tutorial screens should be toggleable, yet they pop up whenever they feel like it.- No reward for collecting every memory token or clearing every single cyber space level  on the map (or in the whole game) - why not, you could give me some special outifts or something for that (Amy's dress or clothes inspired by it for Sonic, Treasure Hunter hat of Knuckles, flying goggles and hat of Tails, cyber corrupted look of Sage - so many possibilites, NONE exist).- Physics can be wonky when you don't need it.- The pop-in is not that bad, but it is a hinderance when looking for a way to a collectible.- Could use more minigames (racing with something on a strict track, aforementioned pinball, style-point minigame...)- Night-only challenges are not the best idea how to make the player have some variety in gameply - they just demand you wait, which should not happen in a Sonic game.- The core gameplay loop might make you fatigued.It might look like there are more negatives than positives, but many are just what I'd like to see, not what is there in reality. And for me, the positives are good enough.Don't try this expecting open world like Breath of the Wild - it is not as open or varied (as of the time of the review). Open World really isn't the right way to desribe this, you are still limited in your actions, abilities and environment. Open Worlds incite discovery, this Open Zone style more likely wants you to try every gimmick or mini-platform challenges it has.I really hope Sonic Team is listening and updates the game accordingly/improves upon the Open Zone formula by the next game. (AlsoTheyCouldIncludeShadowCuzHeCoolHaha).

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 7.2/10 (vanilla) | 8.4/10 (with mods)Pros:+Open world works surprisingly well with Sonic and it's the best part of the game from a game play point. +Titan boss battles are really well done and great set pieces.+Excellent soundtrack (why this game was not nominated for Best Soundtrack of 2022 is absolutely criminal).+Combat is pretty good and does not make the game worse.+Story is decent.+While most new characters in 3D Sonic games are bad and take away from the series, Sage is a very welcoming addition.Cons:-While not game breaking, the pop-in is as bad as everyone says it is.-Physics in Cyberspace are a downgrade from previous Sonic titles, such as Colors.-Cyberspace levels are, for the majority, reused assets from previous 3D Sonic games. Not only that, but there's only 4 different kinds.-Not enough variety in the biomes among the different islands (two out of the five islands are identical in appearance as the first).-Puzzles are piss easy and offer almost no challenge.-Camera can get annoying when you enter a 2D section in the open world-Final secret boss.-Capped frame rate at 60 FPS.I've been pretty pessimistic towards the Sonic franchise for most of the last decade outside of Sonic Mania and Sonic Generations (although I thought the latter was no more than a 7.5/10). So my expectations towards this game were quite low from the get go. I waited to play this game because of my usual skepticism towards recent Sonic titles. Once I started playing Frontiers, I found myself enjoying it. At no point did I ever find myself regretting my purchase.The game clearly has its flaws, undoubtedly. No doubt that this game was held back due to parity with the Nintendo Switch. It also could have used a little more time in the oven and given new concepts and ideas for Cyberspace level themes rather than resorting to using assets dating all the way back to the decade-old Sonic Generations. As a template moving forward, however, I see great potential for the Sonic franchise.I played the game halfway in its original form and the second half using mods via the the Hedge Mod Manager, from Game Banana. I recommend using mods for this game as it will make the experience noticeably better. The mods I recommend are: Improved Physics, Open Zone Physics in Cyberspace, Showin's Momentum Tweaks, Tracker's Physics Tweaks and Elder Koco Fixed.Overall, it is one of the better Sonic 3D games and I hope Sega/Sonic Team can perfect this formula.

_childDocuments_.review: Best 3D Sonic game in forever, probably my new favorite. The open world zones flow so well as each platforming challenge will tend to lead to a new one. The combat is simple and can be button mashy, but as you unlock new combos the fights can be really flashy and fun as your bouncing between enemies with awesome looking moves. Boss fights in the open world are also generally pretty good, the majority of them have unique mechanics to differentiate them but i found most of them to be pretty easy. The main story boss fights, however, are straight banger after banger. The music furring these fights are incredible, they're super flashy and some of them where even a little difficult. Cyberspace was a bit of a mixed bag for me, for some reason the great open world physics do not translate to cyberspace and it took me a while to get used to. I don't like how Sonic controls in these segments very much, but the design of the levels and the music in them made them a lot of fun regardless. Lastly, I enjoyed the story and voice acting a lot, such a step up from the previous 3D Sonic games. Having lore connecting the games (mainly the adventure titles, that ♥♥♥♥ made me real happy to see) had me pretty interested to see where things where going next. My biggest complaint in regards of the story where the cut scenes. They where not animated that well, and consisted of two characters standing around and talking as the camera panned around different angles. I think Frontiers is an incredible Sonic game and also a great game in general. I really hope Sega keeps this new direction and fleshes it out even more.

_childDocuments_.review: This game received a lot of hype and when it released there was a lot of waxing from the sonic community. This game is unfortunately overrated for what it is. At most, it is fun to run around as sonic for a bit, but that should be true in many other games as well, so it's not even a unique benefit. The game feels grindy, slow, the bosses aren't always interesting and reuse assets, the big (interesting) boss fights are one and done, the story is there but it isn't exactly a masterpiece, just a little different than what was done before. I like the variety in fighting, but there's not a single opponent in the game besides the first ninja you fight that actually challenges you to the point that you feel like you have to fight with skill. The game had decent ideas, but bad execution. It didn't do enough to bring sonic to the modern age.  An ok game. Free DLC is good though, but I don't think even that could save this game from its base. More games like Sonic Mania and The Murder of Sonic the Hedgehog please... but those were fan games. At this point, we probably need to accept that sonic just can't do 3D if the character remains under similar management. I hope I'm wrong.

_childDocuments_.review: Wait for a sale like I should've.- Two-thirds of the cyberspace levels are just re-skinned levels or level segments from previous games.- The islands are pretty underwhelming to explore and to look at with floating grind rails and platforms everywhere that will pop in and out of sight as you go.- The controls caused me some grief, mainly because some of the commands are not where the previous games have conditioned me to expect them to be. I did end up swapping Light Speed Dash and Lock-on with each other on the controller.- What I thought was a parry counter that sold me on this game is way too easy to execute and not even changing the difficulty made it satisfying to use.- The enemy attacks have lousy visual and aural tells and they will often attack from off-screen.- A lot of Sonic's attack animations are so long I ended up feeling like a spectator instead of an active participant.- The enemy variety was okay but the bosses were more a mixed bag with Knight being the best one. The final boss was a joke.- The tone is ill-fitting for Sonic. This is the most miserable adventure I've ever seen the Blue Blur and his friends undertake. The only times Sonic himself seems to be having any fun is when he catches something goofy at the fishing spot or when helping the Koco yields a Chaos Emerald. Even the voice actors sound listless.- The plot spins its wheels until the fourth island (or the northern part of the first island) dumps most of it at once on the player and then promptly runs out of steam afterwards when it's time to take on the final island.- This is the most newbie unfriendly Sonic game when it comes to the contents of its overwritten script and I feel bad for the kids for whom this is their first game in the series.Edit: As for update 3 -  the level design is spiteful, the enemies are damage sponges and the writing is still awful. On the plus side Amy and Tails are fun to play (Knuckles isn't) and the series sound director Tomoya Ohtani remains the undisputed MVP of this franchise that, frankly, doesn't deserve him.

_childDocuments_.review: The bones of a good game are here, the combat (when it works) has fantastic juice and really spices up the typical Sonic gameplay, but the open world is barren, the tasks that are there are simplistic and mind-numbing, and after the first two hours you've experienced everything the game has to offer. It just loops the same handful of tasks over and over again. Navigating the world is a nightmare because the areas are connected by random springs and grind rails that LOOK like they might take you in the direction you want, but often send you in the complete opposite direction, and lock the camera off to a 2D view that you can't leave until you've finished the mini platform section and end up even further from where you wanted to go. A Sonic open world game should not have me wishing for fast travel, the main character is LITERALLY FAST TRAVEL PERSONIFIED.  While the combat with basic enemies is fun, the larger enemies / mini bosses are often let down by the janky mechanics that sometimes just stop working, certain special attacks don't trigger, lots of enemy attacks have no tells which results in unpredictable damage, and certain special attacks have cinematic animations that trigger, but these don't have any invincibility frames, so you can get hit from off screen during an animation you have no control over. Actually controlling Sonic is a nightmare, especially during the cyber stages and platforming sections, due to the weird floatly at times, sticky at others physics that feel like a MASSIVE regression from even something like SA2, and are NOT anything like you'd expect from a modern platformer. I know there have been mods made to address this and I plan to try them, but I am literally baffled as to why the character controller in this game functions as it does. It feels incredibly unintuitive.  The only good things about this game are the hype moments during the Super Sonic fights and the boss themes. Literally everything else is like pulling teeth. I hope they iterate on this design and improve it, but absolutely not worth a $60 buy. Hell, not even worth a $30 buy. Just listen to the OST on YouTube.

_childDocuments_.review: There's been a lot of fretting and jeering out there over this game's "Overwhelmingly Positive" rating. People  that it's just blindly supportive fanboys with "low standards." Apparently, these people are just as upset when a Sonic game is called good as Sonic fans are when its called bad.Well, the crybabies can rest easy. Sonic Frontiers is a game riddled with flaws and anyone nominating it for GOTY can be roundly and freely mocked. This is simply a case of everyone agreeing that the good outweighs the bad. Actually, playing this game has been rather vindicating for me. For one, I've been saying for years that (3D) Sonic should be open-world; those stupid on-rails levels they've been stuck on for 20 years just make the character's key strength (speed) into a liability (limited reaction time). With freedom of movement and plenty of things to do and collect, this game actually had me reminiscing on the early days of Spyro. A "collectathon" with story sprinkled throughout. The format works and it works well.Sadly, the game is still lightly peppered with "portal stages" that mimic past Sonic games, so you can relive questions like "Why the hell does every stage take place over a bottomless pit?" and "If you're going to start me back at the beginning of the stage anyway, why not reset the timer, instead of forcing me to do it manually?" Seems like they were, ahem, hedging their bets on the new gameplay.And for point of vindication number two: from the moment they announced the release date, I predicted they were rushing this thing out the door, likely due to its less-than-favorable public reception. And seeing how many issues it has, and how much of it screams "good enough," I'd say I nailed it. In fact, as many reviewers have echoed in so many words, there's a distinct lack of attention to detail just about everywhere, right on down to the menus. (I thought there was something wrong with my controller; turns out you need to select "Options"  the Options menu to select the "submenus.")(And, yes, I realize this is Sega, and Sonic, and so it could just as easily have been rushed out the door because it was a stupid decision, but let me have this.)But now that they've seen such a startlingly positive reception, looks like they're actually going to commit to this one. They've even got a "roadmap" for additional content. It's looking increasingly likely this is just the first open-world game in the series. Might even delay the series getting "rebooted" again for another a year or two.

I don't wanna spoil it but, I'm just gonna say, play it! The game starts out kinda slow, because ya know, open world, but it goes from 0 to 100 VERY QUICKLY!!! Not just in terms of level themes (Green Hill, Chemical Plant, ect.), but also in terms of level design. This is a new low for SEGA in terms of rehashing. Fortunately, they're only like 5% of the game, but it's still kinda annoying. I guess the era of good Boost gameplay is gone. Also, the collision in the open world leaves a lot to be desired. It's not frustrating bullcrap, like, say, Wave Ocean in Sonic 06', but be prepared to go up down and all around.But, on some positives, the game looks great! I really like the graphics, and the characters have never looked so detailed before. Also, the combat is surprisingly fun! I admitedly wasn't too fond of the idea of Sonic having a skill tree before, but now I can say that I'm a fan. The islands are surprisingly big and expansive, and are a treat to explore.So in short, go play this if you haven't already! I'm excited and can't wait to play more! _childDocuments_.review: (Note: The jester awards are from an earlier review of the game where I harped on Linux support. It seems people aren't familiar with how Linux as a whole works. I still think my thoughts are valid and I'll take the Steam points - just keep that in mind.)This is the best game we've gotten since Generations. It's not as good as that game, but it is up there.I will preface this review by saying that Linux support could have had a bit more focus. The game runs fine, but shadows flicker REALLY badly if you don't run at 30 FPS, to the point where you might hurt your eyes, or worse... so we likely have to wait for a Proton update to resolve this and make the game playable at 60 FPS on Steam Deck and other Linux devices. Oh, well. I just hope later titles focus on it more, now that we are in a post-Steam Deck world. If you are one of the folks that only buy games with Linux support (which is understandable, I've thought about that a few times myself), I'd steer away from this game for the time being. Granted, the game is perfectly playable from start to finish at 30 FPS - that's how I played it because of this.In terms of controls and physics, I'd say this is the best Sonic has controlled with the boost gameplay , especially in the open zones where you're free to go wherever after the initial segment on the first island. It's really smooth, and you have a ton of control over what Sonic can do and where he can go.It's not perfect, though - Sonic really likes to stick to the ground a lot. You would think this to be a good thing, but going down cliffs feels very unnatural a lot of the time. He doesn't fly off of them into the air, or slide down them, he just... runs down them, as if they were solid ground. Very odd.In Cyberspace, it's very noticeably different for whatever the reason, but not bad by any means... except for in the 2D segments, which overall feel far too sluggish and feel like they could have used some more tweaking, which is especially bad on the third island as it is filled with them.Boost is bound to right trigger, which will definitely mess with your muscle memory from other boost games like Generations and Forces, but feels... really natural, at the same time. You get used to it relatively quickly. And boosting with a max ring cap feels really satisfying.Combat is accessible, which is nice, but consequently is missing depth I would have preferred to have. Parrying is not reliant on timing, which I'm unsure if I like or dislike - on one hand, it means that anyone can play the game without being walled by it, but on the other hand, I feel like it isn't as enjoyable for those seeking a challenge.I feel like the special moves you unlock should have been given a cooldown of some sort. As it stands now, you can just spam them without punishment, so combat doesn't feel challenging at all. Sometimes enemies will be immune to some moves, in which case I use other ones. I'm sometimes left wondering if enough thought was put into the combat system as it stands now.The writing is great and easily the best we've had in over a decade - although, given it's written by Ian Flynn, and not Pontac and Graff, are we really surprised?Character interactions feel really refreshing compared to what we've had in Forces and Lost World. Sonic joking around with Knuckles is something I hyperfixated on for a little while, I'll admit.I will say almost nothing on the plot and lore, play the game for yourself or look it up if you would like to see it. One particular retcon you are revealed to in the game's climax, , is one I'm still a bit mixed on, but think is cool nonetheless.A few more complaints that I had with the overall package:As a Sonic fan, I do recommend this game for those who are invested in the series. There are many surprises that I think they'll enjoy!I'd also look forward to the upcoming additional content that will release in 2023, as it looks to be really promising, at least in concept. More playable characters and additional story is something that if you told me we'd get sometime in the past decade, I'd be intrigued, but incredulous. Additional content for an already existing game is already unheard of in itself. I welcome it with open arms.

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10To start off this review quickly,Open zone is Sonic's own version of an open world setting. This is a core part of the games identity, and I'd say it's done fairly well. There's quite of bit of exploration and platforming to be done, though it can be a bit annoying to travel as it can be difficult to travel from section of the map to another without it getting boring.When it comes to challenges, I think there's a good amount of fun to be had. Various enemies and even mini bosses are around the islands and are great to fight against. The combat is well done enough to keep me interested and I had a gone time trying out fighting up against the bosses. This last one is more than likely a hot take, but I weirdly enough had a good time with the little tasks surrounding the map. None of them ever really get difficult but there was little moments of satisfaction when I realized what thing I needed to do... Even if it was once again just the cyloop. Cyberspace is the usual, fast paced platform levels you see in most current sonic games. Simply put, Cyberspace is better than it has been for a while. I've enjoyed playing these stages, and though I know some are straight up copies of previous levels in older games, there are what seem to be unique ones that show how much the team has improved from the last game. Unfortunately the design is bogged down a bit by physics, especially in 2d areas. When it worked though, it was fun. This is going to be a hot take, but I feel like it needs to be addressed. The story here is way better then anything we've gotten in the past few years, but it tries to reference back to previous games beyond what should be usual. I do understand this is probably because they wanted to reintroduce the core parts of what make sonic good, but I feel it should be addressed in future games.As for characterization, it's done well here. Personally not my interpretations of what the characters are, but I'm happy with how it came out. The only character I'd say is written a little off is Eggman. In addition the mad doctor really doesn't get any major plot point beyond (insert spoilers here).These overall were a load of fun. Each one felt near the level of Sonic Adventure 2's final boss, even surpassing it in ways. By far my favorite was the second one, with it's dynamic camera angles and movement I felt real pumped to kick that Titan out of the sky. Best Sonic game in ages. I recommend playing it if you're a fan of the series. As for newcomers be aware there are references to older games that might fly over your head, but I think you'll enjoy the experience as well.To clarify, a mediocre for me is 5 or less. This game is far beyond that, and is great.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of what needs to be said about this game has been, but I still wanted to get my thoughts out there, just in case anyone reads this. I'll just give my pros and cons, and elaborate when needed.Pros:- Nice looking. Graphics are solid, if a little repetitive at times.- Movement is really great (for the most part). Sonic feels fast and there's lots of space to run around.- Story is a big step in the right direction. Fixed a lot of very weak characters, and the few new ones are solid too.- Open zones were fun to explore, and didn't overstay their welcome.- Kick ass boss fights (except the final boss).- Absolute slammer of a soundtrack all the way through.Cons:- Pop-in is atrocious. Even on max settings the pop-in is absolutely ridiculous.- Islands can feel the same a lot of the time. (especially islands 1,4 and 5.)- Some Cyber-space levels are good, but a majority of them are tedious and jank af.- Final boss was super boring. Cool dialogue and story stuff, but gameplay sucked.- Cutscenes are locked to 30FPS, which really took me out of my immersion.- No way to replay the sick af boss fights.Overall, Sonic Frontiers has some really solid framework. The bossfights and combat were badass, the open-zones were a great move for Sonic, and the story is a huge step forward from previous games. A year or 2 more in development would have made this game near perfect, and it far exceeded my expectations. Definitely worth the pick up if it's on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably one of the better, if not one of the best 3D Sonic experiences so far in the series. Here is why:It is undeniable that the story hits a darker, more mature tone. Even though Sonic himself does not lose his identifying character traits, the story tackles serious topics such as fear, family and friends relations and the struggle to survive. As someone who has played all Sonic entries with stories worth mentioning, Frontiers is up there at the top. However, it is not without its obvious, grievous flaws. Somewhat unpolished, somewhat rushed, somehow not thought through til the end. But altogether, the characters play out nicely and a feeling of coherency stands out in the end (if you know you know lol).Experimental, refreshing, different, and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ clunky sometimes. Running around in the open world is a revelation - so much fun and so many things to do, to discover. It actually never got boring and I even loved the different island aspects (despite one, I'll let you guess). But here as well, the gameplay is not without flaws. Cyberspace levels are, well, to be frank, they are nothing more than an existing part of the game. They might add to the lore of the game but gameplay wise, they feel unpolished, Sonic Forces-esque and only a few of them stood out as being fun or engaging in any sense. They are forgettable and quite short, but no deal breaker, honestly.This might not come as a surprise to anyone who has played a Sonic game before but the music is beyond mind-blowing. It is the existential aspect of the game that elevates it from "hm-okay-yeah-playable" to "cinematic masterpiece". The island themes are calm, relaxing and never bother or distract, so they are absolutely fine, a nice change regarding past Sonic entries even. But many of the Cyberspace themes and especially, and I emphasise it here once more, ESPECIALLY the boss themes hit the mark so hard that they have not left my personal music mix for several months now. They are not only outstanding songs regarding their quality, but their implementation during the fights and the emotional roller coaster during the scenes close to the ending of the game left a lasting impression and make this game more than simply any other 3D Sonic game, at least for me. The music is a clear vibe, sprouts with passion, and embodies the experimental approach this whole game takes.If I had to rate this game, I would fluctuate between a 7 and 8. The potential of Sonic Frontiers is inspiring, admiring, and noteworthy. Despite its distinct flaws, the positives outshine the negatives without a doubt. Especially regarding its presentation, this game qualifies itself as a true contender to one of the best Sonic game ever made. Even though the gameplay often appears unpolished (I have not even tackled the fighting system, I'll leave it at that) and the story could have used more time in development, the overall impression left by the game is as the general public has received it - very positive. I have had a great time and I even felt motivated enough to go for all the achievements. If this is the future of Sonic the Hedgehog, then this future is bright, and there is no end in sight (there I go, I did it again).Enjoy this game and thank you for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Frontiers is the latest addition to the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise, and as a long-time fan who has experienced previous titles like Sonic Adventure 1, 2, Heroes, Forces, and Generations, I must say that this game is a great addition to the series.One of the standout features of Sonic Frontiers is the decently-sized maps that the player can explore, although they can sometimes feel a bit repetitive and barren. However, the game makes up for it by allowing the player to upgrade their abilities through skill trees, which gives them more flexibility in how they approach their journey.Another feature that I appreciate is the freedom the game provides, allowing players to switch between the main story and various side quests at any time they wish. This adds a layer of immersion and depth to the game that I found quite enjoyable.While I played the game on my Nintendo Switch, and the graphics weren't as good as the PC version, I still found myself admiring the vastness of the map while enjoying the beautiful, syncopated tracks playing in the background. The sound direction in the game is top-notch, and the vocal tracks are home runs from SEGA and the crew.Overall, I think Sonic Frontiers is a great game that would serve most casual Sonic fans a fantastic experience if purchased for $30-$40. However, I personally wouldn't buy it at full price unless you're a die-hard Sonic fan or it's the only game you want to play. Sega has built a decent formula that can be expanded into more challenging levels, bosses, and with other environments thrown in for added diversity and replayability in future Sonic titles.In conclusion, I would give Sonic Frontiers a rating of 7.5/10.

It still has some unfortunate technical hang ups and issues with control at times, but those don't out weigh the pure fun of the open zone, epic boss battles, chill fishing, OST that goes so hard, and great character writing.  Not a 10/10 Perfect game by a long shot but the fun is real, and the potential that this brings the Sonic Franchise is through the roof.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR A much needed return to form for the series but not without its drawbacks. 7/10This game feels like it could have been so much more but Sonic Team was unfortunately held back by the potato that is the Nintendo Switch. Alot of Pop-In and overall graphical fidelity (or lack there of) is definitely due to the game being optimized for a literal cell phone processor. The gameplay is surprisingly chill and unlike a lot of new games that railroad you into a specific playstyle, this lets you learn the game mechanics and engine quirks and abuse them to your leisure which is a massive breath of fresh air. And, being able to customize how you move is a huge step up for the series. When it comes to the story, its okay but the villain should've been a bit more fleshed out. Eggman taking more of a passive role rather than being the "big bad comic relief funny man" is also welcome to be back in the series, kind of like the adventure days. I'm really just glad we're getting a story that is confident in taking itself seriously rather than forcing us to sit through hours of self awareness and self deprecation like the past few installments. Also, as a part of the .0001% of people who ENJOYED Sonic 06, I can see a bit of the good aspects of that game shining through here, as much of a mess as 06 was at times, running around in open world levels was fun, Solianna was an interesting location and exploring it was great. I think that if this formula continues with returning to and refining that open world exploration, we could finally get the sonic game we were promised almost 2 decades ago in 06, but fully realized. With fan projects such as Project 06, its obvious that we're wanting something like that again, just properly executed. Oh and the OST for this game is godly.As for the cons?Definitely need more characters, I get that sonic is the main character but I'm sick of playing as him when I know that there's other characters in this universe. I ACHE for the Sonic X era of characters to make a comeback with the unapologetic cheesiness of story and fun characters. The game can force you into some on rail segments but when you are able to identify them, they can be pretty easy to avoid. The option to bail from them would be nice though.Overall I love that sega is coming out of thier shell to experiment with the series again. Hopefully that turns into something truly great in the future because for the first time in years, im excited for the future of sonic.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Frontiers

_childDocuments_.review: It's not perfect but dammit this is a very good Sonic game. Playing this brought back a lot of memories, nostalgia, happiness, and care for this franchise. No, there's no Chao Garden, but the gameplay is incredible, the graphics are gorgeous, the characters are fun and compelling, the story and setting are cool, and the music is high quality. Speaking of which, since the soundtracks of Sonic games have always left such an impression, I have to say I really appreciate the influence of dance/electronic music on this soundtrack as well as the rock influences. I am also impressed by the incidental music during freeroam sections and while menuing, watching cutscenes, etc. In addition to just the music, the overall sound design is very nice, from the environmental noises to even the sounds upon completing a level or collecting an item. Plus, there's plenty of the classic sound effects in there. I also liked the voice acting, as for the most part it fit the tone of the game well.Critiques- Camera clunkiness: between the forced 2D sections within the 3D freeroam areas, and the enemies that lock the camera even as you zoom by them, it's not the most polished, but it doesn't usually break the game.- Momentum: There are areas where Sonic's speed doesn't shine like I expect, particularly in portal levels. Acceleration and momentum conservation can feel almost nonexistent and can make Sonic feel weighed down whenever you're not boosting. I can understand that this may be for balance purposes, but I think there's a lot of potential for more momentum-based gameplay within the Sonic franchise.- The rare glitch or two: I noticed a couple places where I ended up noclipping through the ground and respawning already underground again. This put me in a loop where I kept dying until I intervened through menus.- Puzzles: There were some puzzles I found a bit repetitious and either lacking in challenge or lacking in novelty.- Music: I know how this sounds, I just said the soundtrack is fantastic, and I will be listening to it a lot -- however I would personally like to hear more jazz and hip hop influences represented. They play a huge role in the sound of classic Sonic games.Overall this game balances elements of all my favorite Sonic games while remaining a novel experience. It made me so happy to see Sonic and friends all glowed up like this, and this entry will always be close to my heart. I'm a little sad to have finished the main story, though I still have plenty to do from a completionist standpoint and I'm glad there will be more content for it in the future. And I'm hopeful that Sonic devs will take the positive fan response to this game to heart and keep it in mind when creating new Sonic games moving forward. Oh and while I'm here, I want to say I would like to see some love for the Chao Garden fans because I've spent hundreds of hours in SA2B just for them. This is not the most comprehensive review and may be somewhat a way to cope with just finishing it, but I'm really happy this exists. If you're on the fence, get it!

_childDocuments_.review: Even as a lifelong Sonic fan, I had major reservations about the first "open-world" game of the franchise. I can say without a doubt, this is the best 3D Sonic game in a long time, possibly ever. It feels so much fun to zoom around the landscapes at full boost, and the puzzle/platform traversal to get around the islands is very enjoyable. One thing that a lot of recent 3D Sonic games get wrong is the sense of speed and how its always halted for the sake of obstacles that can't be seen when going full tilt. Sonic Frontiers lets you go as fast as you want and rarely breaks momentum, and it properly uses ALL of Sonic's moves from wall-jumps, bounces, drop-dashes, homing attacks, grinding, etc.In addition to the open world islands, the Cyber Space levels are pure Sonic speed and fun. There isn't a ton of them, but Sega definitely went for quality over quantity. In fact, I'd say the vast majority of this game is a huge labor of love. This wasn't some product that they rushed out the door haphazardly. This really feels like a momentum shift for the Sonic franchise going forward. I really hope this isn't a one-hit wonder.As for the negative bits, well there really isn't much. If you've seen any of the review footage, most publications have probably mentioned the excessive pop-ins to the environment. While this does happen quite often, it honestly isn't that distracting once you get into the groove of the game. Hopefully Sega will better optimize for the future, but there is nothing majorly broken. Another nitpick would be the puzzles that expand the map being a little too simple to solve. I was also disappointed that there isn't currently any post-game content which feels like a missed opportunity. I was incredibly surprised to find that the OST has 150 tracks! Once again, Sonic games remain close to the top when it comes to video game music. Tomoya Ohtani absolutely killed it.Don't listen to the memes that say "Sonic Frontiers is a 7/10 game which means its a 10/10 for Sonic Fans". This game legitimately is great and stands on its own.

_childDocuments_.review: One heck of an improvement from Forces, I finished every nook and cranny of the game. Even if there wasn't an achievement with the task.Pros+ Really good story for a change, having Ian Flynn directing the story is a great change from the traditional happy go lucky or try hard at being eddy Sonic stories.+ Great music as always, brings me back to my days of a high school student if you listen to the Titan Boss themes.+ Looks solid, sure i'm not the biggest graphics hog, but i see some issues but it's still solid.+ I enjoyed the somber and moody atmosphere the game provides+ Nice variety of bosses and enemies to fight, while simple, you can craft some fun fights with what you got.+ It's pretty meaty for a Sonic game, if you want to 100% the game it can take 20 or more hours. Most Sonic games are no where close to that.+ You can fish in a Sonic game.Cons- Graphical pop-in as people have shown, makes finding collectibles a pain in the butt sometimes cause you cant find where the course starts to get memory tokens.- Cyberspace levels are underwhelming, Sonic's abilities are different in the levels so it's jarring, especially since you will be in the worlds more than Cyberspace, although you can play your cards right and never touch Cyberspace.- The game likes to jump between 2D and 3D depending on the course, and it can really be frustrating to get around when your shoved into a 2D section. Island 3 is full of this nonsense.- The secret final boss is underwhelming, especially since you had 3 prior final bosses of an island that were epic as heck.
