_childDocuments_.review: There's kind of a lot to unpack here. In short, I was expecting to give it a 3/10 due to previewed information, but I'll give it a 4/10 all in all. I would LOVE to take the simple approach of pros and cons, but it just isn't that simple.The control layout is odd but does overall feel more concise and smooth than past titles in the franchise. The gameplay altogether feels like a halfway point between the day and night stages of Sonic Unleashed with some mild inclusion of Sonic Lost World's parkour mechanics. Moving around feels decent, but also mildly janky.It's hard to determine whether or not the platforming was meant to be susceptible to shortcuts when it has other routes clearly meant to get to certain areas, especially because they don't stop you from taking shortcuts most of the time (but they do still have some preventative measures on occasion).The fighting gets very button-mashy. It's a good reminder that the game is first and foremost meant for kids. The game expects the player to spend lots of time rotating the camera, and it doesn't help that the lock-on feature isn't especially consistent. There's also a parrying feature which can be rewarding to use, but only when it wants to be effective. It does require the player to stop in place after any other actions' animations have ended, so it feels like an additional task on its own despite being incredibly simple to actually use.All in all, the feel and concepts of the gameplay are cute, simple, mostly satisfying, but quite janky. By a wide margin, it's the best thing about the game. Wouldn't say it feels as good as Sonic Unleashed or the Adventure titles, but it isn't TOO far behind.There are some additional tasks pretending to be minigames that really aren't necessary. They're not just unamusing, they're work. There's a crane machine, a pinball machine, a Galaga knockoff, several puzzles too simple to be difficult that throw a wrench in your efforts to make it stupid.. Every second not spent either exploring or fighting is just extra work for the sake of extra work, and since some of it has no clear indication of success, you can expect to be confused and staggered to the point of restarting that extra work."Cyber space" stages are also work. They're slow, forceful, ugly, and have the worst part of the OST. It's ACTUALLY a downgrade to the stages in Sonic Forces!One of the weirdest downsides to the game is its obnoxious love for compressed cutscenes. Get 400 rings? 720p cutscene. Parry an attack during a boss fight? 720p cutscene. Walk up to certain mini-bosses, 720p cutscene. Forget to pause when you go to answer the door? No joke, 720p cutscene.Put nicely, the OST is dynamic. At its best, it's snooze music, and at worst, it's a good reason to mute BGM. Accompanying the hub worlds (which occupy roughly 90% of your playtime) are mellow, sadness-focused tracks. Because yeah, that's why Sonic's smiling and moving at a high speed on a sunny day in the game's promo artwork. Unfortunately, that's the best aspect of the soundtrack. The "cyber space" stages feature the same misery brought forth in Sonic Forces. It's like listening to a cat slowly pander around on a synthesizer. To top it off, some boss fights in the game feature a specific song that's an entirely mixed bag and does not fit in with the rest of the soundtrack in any way, save only the terrible voicing and weightless, over-dramatic lyrics. When those voices do shut up, the song is actually invigorating, and it does a fantastic job of setting a tone for the fight. The half-assing is truly unfortunate.I've found it best to play the game borderless with a media player and three playlists ready: something that feels adventurous, mild, and upbeat (like the Sonic Runners OST or just general soundtracks from past games) for the hub worlds, something with a bit more energy (perhaps past main game OSTs like Sonic Adventure 2 or Shadow the Hedgehog) for the digital dimension stages, and, really, for the tone they wanted and didn't have the balls to aim for, get yourself a DOOM Eternal playlist for those Super Sonic boss fights.What surprised me the most about the game is that the crew that's been voicing the characters since 2010 did a decent job of keeping the voices organic, and the way the characters are written in absolutely helps the flow of every situation with very few exceptions. I was expecting the voices to absolutely flop on their own and fail twice as hard with some over-dramatic writing (which, really, the previewed OST seemed to confirm), but no, almost none of that at all.Speaking of writing, the story is pretty engaging half of the time, and that's another area I was expecting it to fall incredibly short._The voices and writing that are hardest to appreciate are Eggman and the virtual emololi, "Sage". Talk about dramatic naming. She's pretty much a passive, docile rework of Sonic Forces' "infinite" (because, yeah, we needed more of that horse $#!+). She's ultimately there to doubt Sonic for the sake of building him up as a magnificent character while everyone else just kinda behaves normally. It feels much like the total fustercluck of a story Halo: Infinite has where the not-Cortana AI (who turns out to be "good Cortana") is just there to make Master Chief sound like some kind of unstoppable force, and you can't help but wince and force yourself not to skip scenes.Eggman does not help. In the atrociously bad excuses for storytelling we've gotten post-2009, Eggman was the one character that really didn't see or need any changes. His anger can and has always shifted between immediate frustration, cute comedy, and actual menace. Here? He's never angry. He's mildly grumpy twice and otherwise grossly content and tame.The story is perhaps the most dynamic aspect of the game in terms of quality. On one hand, there's absolutely none of that wince-inducing "sense of humor" we've been force-fed since 2010. The concepts explored throughout the game often relate to information in past games in the franchise. On top of that, the more you find out, the more answers you want.The storytelling does have two unfortunate catches, however, and most of it is at the end (which matches the sudden drop in gameplay and soundtrack quality). Eggman starts to talk like Sage is his daughter, which comes from  the hell out of nowhere, and Sage decides to call him her father. The end credits give you some "I love my dad" song, by the way. That's what the game was about all along.The final boss fight has two phases in the higher difficulty: the weakest, jankiest, most inconsistent Super Sonic fight in the game (of four), and then a ten-minute Galaga hardmode stage. The "true final boss" has about as much personality as a blank sheet of paper blown around on a street in the middle of nowhere. It's called "the end." That's it. That's the name. I'd go on about it, but it's just such a flat, stupid, half-assed item. It's like they put a ton of effort into the majority of the game and ran out of steam on finale development day or something._Again, all in all, 4/10. It's kinda decent to play, and it's nice to see some of the characters actually act and sound like characters for the first time in forever, but the bad soundtrack, additional tasks that aren't fun, disappointing shortage of answers, janky and mildly buggy gameplay, disgusting ending, and absence of replayability are very taxing.Par for Sonic titles in the last decade - save Mania, of course - I'm never going to play this for more than twenty minutes a year in the future. I seldom meet people as stubborn as I am, but this game serves as the final nail in the coffin for my 28-year run as a Sonic fan. It's been too embarrassing for too long, and the fact that people act like it's Sonic's "long-awaited triumphant return" is utterly humiliating.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Frontiers is a rough game but a step in the right direction for the Blue Blur, (if they don't abandon the concept that is). The game is plagued by nasty pop-in, random junk placed haphazardly all over the place, bland Ubisoft-style open-world design, and a whole slew of nitpicks. But despite all that, I had a really good time. I think the concept of Sonic finally being able to stretch his legs in big open spaces is what distracted me from the issues that plague this game. I hope Sonic Team sticks with the concept and greatly expand upon it to get a truly great 3D Sonic game. I hesitantly recommend this if you think you think the open-zone design will be enough to keep you entertained.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is overall very good. You feel very fast roaming around the huge world which is something I was a worried about as SEGA has never made this type of open world game with Sonic before. The story is also pretty good, it is not Final Fantasy-esk but it's serviceable. I only have a few minor annoyances and complaints which caused me some grief throughout my playthrough. One gripe which is inexcusable is the way you level up your speed and ring capacity. For whatever reason, you can only level up once at a time for those stats even if you have enough koco to reach max level. This means that you need to press level up 98 times to reach the max level and read the same increasingly irritating response that the elder koco gives, "No such thing as too fast, right?" (like it literally took me like 15 minutes to max out my speed and ring count). The thing that I don't understand is that for some reason this is not a problem for leveling up your defense and power. Anyways the other thing that kinda bothers me is that there is practically no post-game content even if you 100%. Since this is an open world game you would expect there to be some sort of encouragement for exploration but no you can practically just get the minimal amount of items needed to progress and get the same experience. Despite these small problems I do still recommend this game as it is far better then forces and honestly maybe even better than generations depending on if you like open world games. There still are traditional style levels in the game found in cyber space so I think this game will be fun for virtually everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Before this game came out I considered it an insult to game designers as a whole, with glaring issues that simply looked embarassing for developers. But even after post-release feeling disgust towards this game I ended up giving it a try.I have NO clue how they even handled the marketing, because the game is more polished than 90% of triple A titles right now. Most issues felt like they were balance-wise more than anything. On a Sonic game. Can you even believe it? After countless entries a Sonic game that is polished, well thought out and well made.It's actually a shame this game didn't make it to the Game Awards (as rigged and boring as they are), because this game excels at many of the aspects they tend to bring out in games.The music? 10/10 easily, I'm not that big into rock but even I can enjoy a well composed song, and this game does that and even more: the synths are unreal, probably my favorite in any game period, and I've played so many games you wouldn't believe it.Graphics? They looked absolute ass even on launch trailers, but as of November 2022? Areas of the game I thought for sure would look horrible look gorgeous the third and last island have some beautiful scenery (I'm being serious about the third, you'd need to play it to see it), and while the pop-in is vomit-inducing, I feel like that was something that Sonic Team tried their best to improve. It's a shame it looks as bad as it does on launch, but hopefully post-launch they'll improve it.Sound design is top tier for Sonic game standards, what more can I say. Voice acting? Great, love the new Knuckles voice actor, I've gotten used to him pretty quickly.Overall, this game might be on top 3 best Sonic games, near Adventure 1 and Unleashed.One last thing I'd like to mention: It's not major, probably half of people didn't realize this, so I wouldn't really consider this even a spoiler but... This game is so obviously setting up Adventure 3. If you haven't played it yet you should definitively see for yourself the actions of all the characters and their motives while the story evolves, huge potential for a follow-up.So yeah, don't watch any videos, don't look up any trailers, they show the worst side of the game... I don't even know how. Go play it yourself.

_childDocuments_.review: Finishing the game took me 21 hoursWhen playing I felt that the team cared more for the quality and the whole vibe of the game. I had a great time playing Sonic Frontiers. As everyone says, this game delivers for the fans a nice more serious story, engaging battles and a feeling of speed. However, I feel the developers where cautious when implementing open world gameplay into this game. Because I sometimes felt locked from building momentum and using it as a reward for being aware of the space. They did add some features of reward like the rail jumping. More of that would let players experiment more. In addition, the core design of levels being formed from mostly flying platforms is a bit weird. It could have took a bit of thinking to make it more natural and believable in the context of the sonic world. I do love running in the map and trying to do all the puzzles. All the cutscenes are amazing and the characters and story are well putted together.In conclusion, the game is fantastic. This is a good direction for the modern sonic franchise, trying new and exiting thinks, and always delivering with the awasome music OMG THE MUSIC IS SO GOOD YES SEGA I NEED IT!hope the dlc is good. Of cource this game is miles better than forces, they really outdid there level design here.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, HOOO boy. Ok.Gameplay - This game was above average, no doubt. The concept of an open world game where sonic can break free from his linear 2D game style was Sega's selling point that deemed ambitious. I enjoyed the overall presentation this game had to offer from start to finish. The developers put more care and detail to Sonic, his abilities, and his power/speed.Combat - Outstanding, far exceedingly proven to be exciting and fun to play Sonic with his move set. At first, I was worried that the skill tree wouldn't convince me, thinking that Sonic would only spin dash his enemies. I was proven wrong with a good variety of moves that showcase Sonic's flashy and cocky style to fight. It may even par with basic combat in other action games, which is what I had hoped for in the first place. The only complaint I have is how you upgrade your ring capacity and Speed through Kokos without a number limit. This forces you to upgrade each ability once at a time. The soundtrack: Can we uh... can, can we take a moment to talk about the audi- IT'S TIME TO FACE. YOUR. FEEEEEEEAAAAAAAAAAAThe characters: You will find that the characters have more personality than some games, like Sonic Adventure 2 for example. The story draws emotion from the characters as you progress in the story.The story: The story was satisfactory, the game does mention lore and history from both Sonic Adventure's 1 & 2 found in Eggman's Dialogue Tracks (Also, watch the prologue on YouTube, you will see why). The game answers a lot of questions, focusing on the origins of the Chaos Emeralds & the Master Emerald.My rating for this game is a 7.9/10. For players who have completed this game may already understand this rating. For new players, don't keep your hopes up in the end.

_childDocuments_.review: After 100% the entire game I have come to the conclusion that Sonic Frontiers is a huge step in the right direction but, there are a few things that need to be addressed if SEGA intends to use this game as a basis for future titles.- The open-zones are great and traversing them with Sonic is a lot of fun and for the first time in years, Sonic doesn't feel like a tank with a jet engine up in his butt.- Storywise, the characters are finally being taken seriously and not making jokes out of everything.SEGA, do yourself a favor, never hire the Pontaff duo ever again.The plot itself is, let's face it, it's not Nier Automata, but its much much better from what we’ve got in the last decade.- In terms of gameplay, Sonic has quite an arsenal of actions and attacks which presents Sonic as an acrobatic and fast fighter.Performing the attacks is a lot of fun.There are also enemies that need to use a certain strategy and not just press the attack button.- The titan boss fights are the best thing in the game. Period!- In terms of graphics, we finally found a game that surpasses Sonic Unleashed.- the music, as always, excellent, especially in the titan boss fights.- Let's start with the obvious, the pop-in, they are everywhere and they’re noticeable.I really hope SEGA will fix this annoying problem asap.- The cyberspace stages feel quite unnecessary or at least something that was thought of at the last second to appease boost-to-win fans.The stages themselves aren't terrible but they’re very short and Sonic, unlike in the open world, controls horribly in them.But hey at least the music in them is good.PSA: I highly recommend downloading the Improved Physics mod from Gamebanana, you will have much more fun with more momentum and air time.- If we are talking about momentum then no, there is no momentum in the game and the only time it apparent is when you perform drop dash downhill.It is a shame because the game could really benefit a lot with momentum/Pinball Physics.- The 3rd island, Chaos Island is riddled with fixed 2.5D camera and side scrolling sections. - After a while the game feels repetitive a little, doing the same challenges and objectives, collecting the Chaos Emeralds, over and over again. It becomes noticeable from the third island.Spoiler Warning: - The game on the Hard difficulty is relatively easy to finish, also the parry in the game is really simple and you don’t need to time it at all, just holding the buttons until the enemy attacks.-When a titan boss throws me to the side, the camera pans towards Super Sonic front and not towards the titan, which is a bit annoying during a boss fight.Also it's a bummer that you can't go back to the titan bosses because they're really fun!The Prologues comic and video “Convergence” and "Divergence" should have been part of the game and not as separate media, I understand its for marketing purposes but I don't need to rely on external content in order to understand the plot.Spoiler warning: If you look at the whole picture, it seems that SEGA has finally found the most suitable formula for Sonic but there is still room for an improvement.If I had to give the game a score I’d probably give it a 7.5 or 8 out of 10.
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Frontiers

_childDocuments_.review: They finally made Super Sonic feel fast and strong, unbelievable. This game had almost no issues, but those I did have were: the slower pace Sonic moves at; the popping in of the rails and memory token skill checks (I felt like they were too many, however I found it rewarding to "skip" a challenge by checking the map or going from the end of an elevated parkour to the middle of another); the stiffness at times such as getting sucked into 2d areas; the lack of design put into Cyber Space (looking at you, Unleashed stages); the final boss (makes sense with the starfall and all that but a purple moon? What?) and the seemingly useless difficulty button (100%'d on Hard, toughest things were the space invaders minigames). Oh, and also a round of applause for whoever created the torture machine that is the pinball game.It felt pretty good running around the islands, even if it was sometimes frustrating having to navigate through the "Chaos Galapagos". Didn't like the Elder Koco's way of leveling, I did see some mods which fixed this though (haven't tried them). I'd recommend whoever tries this game not to level attack nor ring cap, as one makes it too easy to beat guardians before they get to change phases, and the other only makes it harder to get power boost.Overall this game's story was much better than pretty much anything from last decade, and finally we had a serious tone that didn't go over to STH levels of edginess. Having the emeralds be from outer space is weird, haven't found if I like the idea or not, even if the Master Emerald can be "confirmed" to be from earth (being the reason the Ancients were drawn there to begin with). Really looking forward to what happens next, seeing as the other 3 main characters are going on a Sonic hiatus and Sage is coming back, loved the character she got out of Eggman.Oh, one last thing. Add a NG+, I liked the idea of guardians getting tougher after first beating them (only after they respawn from a starfall though), and would like to see that on a full game scale.

_childDocuments_.review: As a lifelong Sonic the Hedgehog fan, I can say that this game definitely surpassed my expectations. It definitely isn't perfect but it has a lot of good with it.I'll start with the things I like about the game. The open world is a great gameplay element for Sonic. It's fun to just run around and traverse. It controls great, it has tons of fun platforming bits in the open world. It has a good story (something that we haven't had since 2008 with Unleashed). The characters' personalities are back, which is something I think has been missing for a while. The killer soundtrack as always. The combat works great for Sonic, which is something I was a little worried would be not fun. Sonic has a lot of expression in some of these cutscenes which I love to see. Voice acting is pretty solid. The options to adjust how Sonic controls in the open world is huge.There are some things I didn't like however. The cyberspace stages are all reused themes that can get repetitive and they mostly use layouts from previous Sonic levels. There are a couple that are original ones but that's about it. I do appreciate the variety of games they took the layouts from however. I do have a couple complaints with the story but I won't get into that too much to avoid spoilers. The animations in the cutscenes look a little off but it's not too bad. They advertise 5 islands but the last 2 are just reused from the first.I understand they are continuing with this formula for at least the next decade, so some things I would like to see in the future are smoother animations, maybe some level design that can be used for momentum in the open world, and some more original level design for the cyberspace levels (whatever they'll be called in the futureOverall, Sonic Frontiers really impressed me. Definitely one of my top Sonic games. 8.5/10

But if you can get past those, you'll have a blast. Highly recommended

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic is BACK! Combat and movement feel really really good, especially in the open zone areas. Cyberspace stages are surprisingly good breaks between running around the open zones. Wish there was more skills to unlock, a few more islands to run around, and more titan fights, but overall a solid first entry into a new open-world style of gameplay. It's very much a collect-a-thon, but I think for a first attempt it works well. I got 17 hours out of it in my first play through and still need to go back and get some of the achievements and complete challenges, but depending on if you just rush after the objectives or take time to explore your mileage may vary. _childDocuments_.review: Well it's been a long time coming, and I almost lost my faith in Sega, but from everything they have been saying, and all the passion that I could sens going into this games development, I had a feeling that it would be something worth following. I've been a fan of Sonic since I was 3 or 4 years old, and now that I'm 28, seeing the series from it's golden age and then through it's bad times and rough patches, I can proudly say that this has to be Sonic Teams greatest Sonic game yet. I came into playing this with no set expectations, and a fresh clean mind on what it will be like. It's by no means perfect, the pop in is kinda odd, but you get used to it, the frame rate is a bit choppy here and there, but not too distracting, and the controls in the cyber space stages can be a bit challenging at times, as well as certain major boss fights, when it can get a bit confusing on what to do. With all that said, those can possibly be ironed out with patches, and they don't impede on the enjoyment and sheer HYPE and sense of wonder that the game has going for it. It's extremely vast and explorative, the narrative itself is fantastic and very interesting, music is absolutely BUMPIN', and it's just an all around fun, addictive, and entertaining experience. My advice to you is to not buy into those big name yadda yadda reviewers and youtubers trying to trash the game or exaggerate certain flaws of this game. Play this game yourself, completely unbiased, and see how you feel about it. I definitely feel like this is the direction Sonic Team must go in going forward, this is the way Sonic should be, minus the few flaws here and there.

_childDocuments_.review: There are a lot of questionable game design decisions that feel straight out of the early 2000s. For example: There are some short, classic 3d style levels in this game. They're designed well enough, but if you want to retry the level while playing it, you have to wait 2-3 seconds at a minimum before GETTING to watching a short cutscene that leads into the level, usually another 2-3 seconds. If you want to retry the level after you've finished it, you have to wait for a 5 second series of animations showing your score to go by before seeing that same 2-3 intro cutscene again.Bosses drop gears that are necessary to progressing the story. You have to manually walk over to pick them up. There are items in the game that already automatically pick themselves up once you unearth them, or activate a switch, or whatever. Why don't the gears do that?you can change your starting speed and maximum speed in the menu. Why??? Why didn't the game designers design the world and levels around one, satisfying to use speed?These decisions damper the experience, but they're not the thing which makes want to drop the game. That thing is the fact that Sonic doesn't feel good to control.

_childDocuments_.review: Bottom line: If you really need a sonic game, get it on sale. Frontiers isn't great, but it's trying some interesting things that I'm hoping they do better next time. I find it particularly frustrating because I think in the things that are most important, everything this game does poorly a previous sonic game has done better. Somewhere, deep down, there is a good game inside Sonic Frontiers, but the good is buried in tedious and the bad is an unnecessary regression from previous titles.I feel really bad that the sonic fanbase is so demoralized that they're rallying around this game as some kind of second coming. Sonic Generations was great! Oh...that was 12 years ago? Oh dear. Nevermind. I don't mind the open world - it makes sense for a character whose whole deal is moving fast from place to place in a way that's fun. The most fun I had was in the the open world sections, definitely better than the cyberspace levels. It's a shame there's almost no real incentive to explore it.I don't mind the oddly opaque and melancholic story. It's potentially interesting to see these bright and colorful characters interact with that environment. There is some weird tonal whiplash with some of the minigames, though.I don't mind the sky rails - I just wish the draw distance was far enough for me to actually see how to get up there. I don't mind the superfluous RPG mechanics - they had to have some sort of incentive for exploration. It's weird how the ring capacity upgrade forces you to trade making the speed boost you get from having full rings more inaccessible in exchange for making you having a slightly longer time limit to kill the handful of area bosses? Also, trading in Kocos for speed/ring upgrades involves a 10-second unskippable cutscene and you need to get every upgrade individually. If you leveled both those stats all the way up to 100 for some reason, it'd take ~33 minutes watching what amounts to a static model and a popup. Why does any developer still do this?While every one of these things is flawed, I don't think they're bad on their own; I think they're executed at maybe a 6/10, which is pretty good by the standards of a sonic game.What I dislike about Sonic Frontiers is that it fails pretty badly at the one thing a sonic game is supposed to try to do well - make you feel like you're moving fast and stylishly. Sonic in the cyberspace levels feels like he's wading through molasses. I hate how jumping kills your momentum, how springs are often slower than running. I hate how the homing attack brings sonic to a dead stop - I never want to hear another complaint about SA1 and 2 - the boost flings me off platforms more than the SA homing attack ever did anyway. You also can't boost out of it if you've boosted already, so using it will slow you down even further and might be instant death. Nitpick: sometimes you have to light speed dash as part of the level. It's never this optional tricky thing you can do to get an edge in speed or cool shortcut. Previous sonic games have used this really effectively and this just makes the mechanic feel tacked on. Also, like everything else you have a weird pause after using it, making it pretty much useless except in cases you have to use it. The result of all of this is that other than cheesing the homing attack with a dash-cancel, the optimal way to play the cyberspace levels involves using none of sonic's abilities other than the boost. Stay on the ground, don't touch anything, try not to run into enemies as the camera jerks around. Doing this, I S-ranked most cyberspace levels within 5 minutes or so (other than the perplexingly draconian level 1-2?) and never once did I feel like I was going particularly fast, mastering some special route, or anything. The levels are also so short that none of them ever feel like much of an accomplishment.Nitpick about the open world - it's almost entirely pointless. I made the mistake of grabbing every collectible on the first area map. It was a waste of time. There's no reason to pursue any of the collectibles in the open world. You get piles of memory tokens thrown at you, and can even get vault keys (the only reason to actually do the cyberspace levels) in random enemy encounters. The moment you beat an area, your gears, vault keys, and memory tokens reset back to zero. I had like 40 extra keys, 10 extra gears, and 80 extra hearts, all pointless.This is also a shame because some of the platforming and railgrinding puzzles to get the hearts marked on the map (again, a negligible number compared to those dropped by monsters or dug up with the cyloop) is one of the few parts of the game I actually enjoyed.So the optimal way to play the bits that resemble conventional sonic gameplay, the cyberspace levels, is to play as boring as possible. The optimal way to play the overarching bits is to ignore most of it, including those cyberspace levels. The reward you get for doing those things anyway is some lackluster platforming and maybe if you're lucky sonic will run over a loop or something.Bonus frustration: Why does the starfall mechanic exist? Why would I want these powerful enemies I killed to just resurrect and pollute my map? I already have more of the collectibles they drop than I can possibly use. What purpose does this slot machine serve other than blocking my screen while I try to platform? To give me more fishing coins? I already have 104 of the damned things. It looks kinda cool and I like the idea of an occasional event, but everything about this is more annoying than engaging. Guess I'll leave my game unpaused and do something else until daybreak so I can see what I'm doing.Edit: I think part of my frustration is that I can see a better game in here with very specific changes:1) Quick and snappy homing attack, at least in the cyberspace missions. Sonic hits and bounces off. That's it. If you need that second-long pause for the combo system, keep the current homing attack exclusive to the overworld. Honestly, I'd gladly strip down the combat system back to SA2: spin dash (I know it's kinda superfluous with the boost, but it feels good and is classic sonic), homing attack, stomp/bounce attack. Keep the cyloop. Keep sonic moving. All the current system does is make fighting an ordinary enemy take a minute of button mashing. There was one enemy where the ranged rapid-fire attack was useful, but other than that all of the other abilities seemed to just be a question of which maximizes DPS.2) Jumps preserve your speed at the time of jumping.3) Get rid of the one boost per jump restriction, or at the very least let a successfully landed homing attack, spring, etc. reset this counter so that you can boost -> homing attack -> boost. You don't always know what's on the other end of a chain of enemies and it's very frustrating to boost into a homing attack, then helplessly fall to your death because you didn't know you'd need that boost.4) Tighten sonic's mid-air turning radius. Sometimes you come out of a spring or something facing a weird direction and have to wait or die while Sonic slowly wheels his way around.5) Make the chests you dig up only give stat boost upgrades. Not keys or memory tokens because that takes away any incentive to do the overworld platforming puzzles and cyberspace missions, which are supposed to be the most interesting part. Players will follow optimal strategy even if it is less fun. If you force them to do the less fun parts and rely on them to seek out the fun parts, they'll have a bad time. It's weird that those are optional when the Koco minigames (which are hit or miss at best and the biggest source of tonal whiplash) are absolutely mandatory.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I didn't have to pick whether I recommend this game or not, because neither fits perfectly with my thoughts. It's rather middle down the road, but I'm leaning on the positive side.The game has an extremely rocky start that takes a lot of getting used to. It does not at all have the polish it demands. The controls are inconsistent and often work against the player. The momentum is especially bad in the Cyberspace stages, in which it feels like Sonic randomly fluctuates in speed, particularly in the 2D sections. Same as the seemingly arbitrary way certain actions reset your controls. For example, why does going through a purple ring give me back my double jump, but not my air boost or stomp? The environments aren't helping either, feeling rather uninspired with disconnected platforming segments that, while fun to traverse, look very cheap. On top of that, the ending comes very abruptly and leaves you rather deflated and unsatisifedAll that said, I cannot say I didn't have fun after the first island. For the first time in years I'm watching a Sonic game's story unfold that feels like it has actual stakes and emotional weight to it. The iconic characters finally feel like themselves again, rather than child friendly carricatures of the cast. That is not to say that the game is edgy now, but there's a certain earnest maturity in the way characters talk to eachother that I've been missing for over a decade. In addition to the story, the open zone system, if more refined, is a promising direction for the series, not to mention the way this game approaches boss fights, minus the two last ones.Now, I realize this doesn't sound like it in any way justifies my criticisms from the first paragraph, however I can feel the heart that was put into this game to not only take Sonic into a new gameplay direction, but also revitalize the writing, and I absolutely appreciate that. Also the game is simply fun to control, when it works. I'd like to see them take this direction further, ideally with more time and budget, because these two things are absolutely the reason I cannot give this game a hard recommendation, unless you are crazy about Sonic already.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't kept up with Sonic games too religiously, but I actually had a lot of fun with Sonic Frontiers. It does have some issues though.Cons:-Lacks Polish compared to games like Mario Odyssey and Zelda BotW which this game is obviously heavily inspired by.-Game can get repetitive in long play sessions due to similar requirements between sections/islands. I found shorter play session helped my enjoyment quite a bit.-Pop-in actually harms gameplay, especially on the third island where you have a ton of rails you have to travel that you can't see until you're up close.-"Another Story" DLC seems like a knee-jerk reaction to screeching Souls-like fans. It's overly hard and frustrating, especially for a Sonic game. Not that Sonic shouldn't be hard sometimes, but I feel they're pandering to the wrong part of the audience with this DLC just because the final boss should've scaled somewhat with level so it wasn't brainlessly easy for most players (likely due to lack of polish mentioned above). Pros:-Story is actually pretty good...for a Sonic game. This isn't RDR2 or anything, but it does a great job with what it has. Like the lore/characters/themes/tone of most Sonic games? This is a better version of that. -Characters are all likable. A lot of the writing feels like they were course-correcting a bit on past choices, but I feel it works in this case and they (accidentally?) made Eggman the most interesting character even though he isn't in the game that much. If you're going to take from BotW/Odyssey, Sega, then I want to see an Eggman game where he makes inventions similar to Tears of the Kingdom! That would be amazing. -Sonic's speed feels great. I feel open world does a better job showcasing this element of Sonic which has always been defining to his character, but rarely felt genuine in his more linear games. -Combat is overall enjoyable. It definitely has holes due to lack of polish (some moves/combos are pointless and some enemies are just tedious), but combat actually feels pretty satisfying! Most of the sub-bosses have unique requirements for defeat that helps the combat system sing when its at its best. -Music is great. I missed out on a lot of Sonic games over the years, but the ones I have played always have great music and this one doesn't disappoint either. It also has a cool "jukebox" feature that lets you play songs from previous games during gameplay once found as a collectible. Neat! So if a Mario Odyssey/BotW inspired Sonic (with less polish) sounds fun to you, then definitely jump on board. I'm not even a hardcore Sonic fan and I enjoyed it. I've seen people say it's 7/10 and I agree, but not in a derisive, gaming-journalist-bloated-score sense. It's a very fun 7/10. I can't tell you how many "10/10" games I've played recently that aren't really all that fun. Sonic Frontiers dares to have disappointing elements while blazing forward without shame in celebration of the good elements. I can respect that.

_childDocuments_.review: This game certainly grew on me one personally. It might be my second favorite Sonic game (Heroes is my most beloved *gets shot*)(Spoiler warning)On the one hand, I despise the cyberspace stages(forces looking good fr) with their terrible controls, physics and design(even if some are mildly enjoyable) the mini games like the pinball one(screw that one in particular, even if I had tons of practice and consider myself decently skilled at irl and videogame pinball), the fact that you cant replay the amazing super sonic fights(literally my biggest gripe with the game), the waiting time for the short elder koko to upgrade your abilities, the missing proper final boss(that atrocity true final boss is terrible and should not exist), the popular opinion I share about the third island sucking a lot, the wonky climbing mechanics on Azura, the weird canyon like structure of the second island that makes it weird to reach high grounds at times and finally the pop in and the starting speed for sonic.So, after all this, what is there that I enjoy about the gameplay? I enjoy the combat, and im the least knowledgeable guy in terms of good video game combat, i don't know anything about good combat in the most well known games, I haven't played them since their not my taste. Yet, In one of my few combat experiences I had in gaming, I found myself, while getting hit plenty of times, having a blast. The mini bosses in this game are so fun. The chase ones are great, the combat pure ones are great, even the ones I least like such as shark, are enjoyable at worst. The combat system might be simple, especially with people complaining about the parry being so easy to do, but personally since im not big on combat games im not mad at that(lucky me). And for the second thing I like in the open zone, are the mini challenges everywhere, the 3d and the 2d memory token areas, the rails, the climbing and underground passages, towers, bridges and structures in general. They always felt immersive and kind of having goofy simple fun, not the greatest in terms of design or structure, yet I still had fun finding each little area to find the memory tokens.Also big's fishing mini-game is nice, great for grinding stuff you want to get, plus the egg memos, which ill get later on on this review.I must admit, the first 14 hours of the game I played, left a strange, almost bad taste in my mouth. I completed the game at 15 and a half hours. Even after remembering the bad taste and rage I had due to not knowing what to do in super sonic bosses, the emptiness I felt at times, and yet, I still came back to the game and got all 40 achievements(pretty easy if you ask me compared to other games). This game didn't leave a great taste or a bad taste in me at the end. Seeing for once sonic fans be, for the majority, happy about a sonic game left a strange feeling in me.And then comes my second play through. Boom, now I know what I'm doing. Beat the game in 2 days. Super Sonic fights now became fun, I knew how to traverse the terrain and obtain shortcuts by completing challenges(long rails), I knew where to go in certain parts of the game, especially in Chaos Island now it became much more enjoyable. I genuinely cant tell (If someone is reading this at all) If I enjoyed the game or not in my first play through. But looking how I got all 40 achievements in such few days, something called me back to this game and the last hours I have been playing felt good. I must have liked this game to come back to it, at least I figure. And then of course the second play through desire meant I was craving more(probably).Do I recommend this game? Yes, its worth a shot, even for its price. Non sonic fans and sonic fans alike have something to enjoy out of this game. I've seen many different opinions on it. Its a stupid but simple argument, if so many people love it, then maybe you will love it too, or at least like it, or recommend it to others like me. However I must admit I don't recommend this game for absolutely everyone, if you don't feel like buying it, don't, but if you do want it, even just a little bit and are unsure whether or not to buy it, Id say go for it. This game is quite the experience.Outside of the gameplay, the story was the best sonic story in over a decade. The characters felt real, likable, with many layers and true to their nature that made them so beloved before they got ruined near the 2010s and going forward. Even some surpassed earlier interpretations, such as Amy. She does not give a damn about Sonic romantically and treats him like a friend, not some romantic obsession. Tails was amazing, his verdict and short arc in frontiers really moves the character in a way that has never been seen before since the adventure games. And Knuckles is great, also has a short arc of his own. The voice direction also helps the game by a ton. By far the best Roger Sonic voice Ive ever heard. Knuckles and Amy too are improved by their new voice direction.  I haven't even gotten to the lore and actual story of the game. While it may seem simple first hand, the lore of the ancients was great as well as their connection to the sonic lore, the character of Sage and her evolution thought the game, the references to past games that aren't nostalgia bait but actually relevant, Eggmans relationship with Sage was the most emotional part of the game, Sonic games hadn't had a moment that felt like that since Unleashed. Truly emotional that ending was. Eggman himself is best portrayed through the final act and his egg memos. The best his characters been in a while. Much like the others. Although I will say he isn't that present in the plot which mildly annoys me, but his ups outweigh that one down by a ton.I love Sage. Greatest new character in a while. Emotional, real and deep. Well at least for a Sonic game. But its deep enough to cut through your heart at the end of the game.The OST is phenomenal as usual.And now to end this review on a weird stupid nitpick I have. I personally don't think this is MY ideal sonic game. But its the best we got and damn Ill take it. I miss other charterers being playable and having their own stories. I miss Shadow, Team Dark, Silver and Blaze. I miss having actually good, re-playable stages like in sonic adventure, heroes and even 06 if you know how to handle your way around it.The two things I would like in the next game are: Good "stages"(Generations/Sa1 design, Sa2 ranking, heroes themes and more than 2 and a half minutes in length) that aren't already done to death like the "classic" green hill, chemical plant and sky sanctuary and the next thing I would like is for other characters to be playable or present(Shadow, Rouge, Omega, Silver, Blaze)in the game, aside from the already present 4 characters, also bring back Sage shes great. This is the end of this review (nobody read this lol)

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best Sonic game in over 10 years. Unlike its predecessor, Sonic Forces, it actually builds upon the foundation of boost gameplay as well as Sonic gameplay overall. That being said, it is important to note that a majority of the game takes place within the open zone island areas, so if you're expecting the straightforward get-to-the-goal design philosophy, then this game might not be for you. Some of that is in here, but there's hardly any to make that a major selling point of the game. In terms of gameplay, it is still very much a boost title. However, Sonic is more maneuverable in comparison to previous boost games in order to compensate for the overall openness of the islands. It is even possible to modify the turning speed in the options page. Boosting has also been tweaked to reflect the game's open design, as the boost gauge now replenishes automatically as if it were a stamina meter. Personally, this is a welcomed change and just makes sense given the context of an open ended environment. If you aren't a fan of it though, there's always mods that can change that for you. Additionally, the game introduces a new ability, the cyloop, which essentially breaks Sonic power scaling and grants Sonic the ability to do things he previously hasn't been seen doing so freely. This includes casually lifting rocket-sized ammunition, creating portals to teleport objects, transforming objects into other objects, creating important collectibles (like rings) from nothing, and much more, simply through the act of running in a circle. If used to create the infinite symbol, the cyloop will also give Sonic infinite boosting for a generous period of time. Aside from borrowing from the boost style games, this game also borrows from other Sonic games of the past, primarily games like Sonic Heroes and Sonic 06. Not to mean that in a bad way either; there's more of an emphasis on combat in this title, something Heroes and 06 tried to do. As far as combat goes in this game, it is surprisingly fun and engaging for such a simple implementation, giving hope for further improvements in future titles. Similar to 06, or even the Storybook titles, there's an ability upgrade system, one which is much more fleshed out here. Sonic Team hasn't really tried their hand at an in-depth upgrade system since these titles, so even if it's a little simple, it's refreshing to see it implemented well in this game. Even the aesthetics of the game are closest to 06 in terms of the more realistic environment they were going for.Speaking of which, the aesthetics of this game admittedly grow repetitive as you play. Of the 5 islands you visit, only 2 of them differ in their overall look, which even then is a stretch because they look quite similar to each other. Given that the game involves cyberspace, I was expecting they would at least include an open zone that took place within cyberspace itself, but I guess that was expecting too much out of them when Sega was trying to rush this title out. On the topic of cyberspace, these stages also suffer from the same problem. The game once again relies on shoehorning in Green Hill and Chemical Plant, but this time as whole backdrops for a number of stages. Sky Sanctuary and a new city highway aesthetic are also used. With only 4 different styles for these stages, they too get repetitive but they're more excusable since they only take up a tiny percentage of play time. It isn't even mandatory to play through most of them. When it comes to the story, that's a little more subjective. I am thankful they put in the effort to make it more serious in tone, similar to SA2 or 06, and happy to see more Sonic lore being introduced. However, I personally found the story to be a little more boring than those previous games, at least presentation wise. The concept and lore are interesting, but presented in a way that would put me to sleep.One minor complaint before entering spoiler territory, when upgrading your speed and ring capacity, you have to talk to an elder on the island. This elder only lets you upgrade one point at a time and has an annoying animation that plays for it, followed by a pause for some reason before you can upgrade again. Each stat has 99 points max, so if you want to upgrade to max for both stats, you will have to endure the torture of repeatedly waiting for the animation to end, and for the in-between pause to end as well. This could have easily been avoided if they let you allocate how many upgrades you wanted for each stat, but this some how passed through quality assurance so it's unlikely they'll implement a patch for it. If someone else doesn't make a mod that fixes this issue, I'll feel inclined to do it myself at some point.Spoilers below:Overall I would say this an 8.5/10 fast action platforming game, but a 7/10 Sonic game given my spoiler complaints. Perhaps my score will go up when I inevitably replay it, especially now that I know what to expect, but I doubt my opinion would change all that much. I also still recommend this game, purely because this is as good as Sonic has been since Generations. Hopefully they learned a lot from this game and continue to improve for the next one.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:-- Quite a refreshing take on the formula.-- Feeling of emptyness on each of dead and deserted island is passed nicely with both audio and visual design.-- Gameplay in open spaces is interesting. It's always fun to traverse given landscapes and finding some special places even though there is no reward for finding them. The world and big amount of goals kept me going from one thing till another. "One more tower and I will go" ended up in sessions till 3-4am for a couple of days.-- Music is great, as always.-- Even though dialogues are quite... simple of nature, you can finally feel they were written by people who actually know the franchise. And characters finally talk with dialogues instead of jumping around after every single word. That being said...Cons:-- I wish characters in dialogues did at least something. During most of the cutscenes they just stand there and blink while talking.-- Virtual Worlds (regular levels) have different physics. Controls there are stiff and you feel really slow. Every move or attacks stops you in your tracks. I've ended up just jumping and boosting over everything just to make it on time. Feels especially terrible after playing with (kinda) good physics in open world.-- Third Island is freaking awful. It's a volcano with a lot of small stones, ice and lava everywhere. Boosting here will send you flying upwards 99% of the time. It's hard to cyloop due to debree. Almost everything you touch turns gameplay into a 2D section with platforming even if you didn't want to go there. You're constantly sent in those and it's hard to escape them. And since some keys are not functional in those 2D sections they may stop working even in 3D just because you touched any 2D section. First two islands were great to explore. The third island takes your exploration freedom and forces you into platforming. Also final boss is the easiest one on this island.-- Terrible menus and UI. They are slow. My hardware is top notch but when menu appears you cannot interact with it for 2 seconds. When you hit Pause (the P key, since you neither Esc, nor Enter, nor Tab can be bind to menu or map) you need to use jump button to select the menu tab before you can interact within it (even though the game uses mouse as a default input). Can't change any setting before you choose it's category and then the setting itself. Smells like a cheap console port.-- Impossibly slow Koco progression. There are a lot of small fellas hidden in the world, but you need way too much of them. You need 20 Kocos to level up a single time... out of 99 for both rings and speed. And you do it one level at a time. Also, due to slow menus the upgrade process is really tedious. ["What do you want to upgrade?"] [2s pause] [Select "Speed"] ["Okay I will upgrade speed"] [Upgrading animation] [Giant text "Speed Upgraded 17lvl -> 18lvl" sits there for 5 seconds] ["I have upgraded your speed"] ["Do you want another upgrade?"] [2s pause] etc. And you need to do this 196 times. Thanks, but no.Concl: I'm still having fun in the open world. Kind of sad that these issues are here but you can complete the entire game without upgrading or playing virtual stages to 100%. I am still doing this cause I hate myself, but you can just skip all of that. Except for the third island. Screw the third island.

_childDocuments_.review: My favourite 3D Sonic game since Generations (might like it even more than that tbh). Some elements including the story and how the level objects integrated in to the world felt a little under-cooked, but the sum of all its parts is a really fun action platformer with an enjoyable gameplay loop of doing different tasks to collect different items to progress forward. The music is amazing in this game by the way and the soundtrack is one of the best in the series, being so varied with melancholic orchestral pieces for the open zone, melodic synth music for boss encounters, heavy metal and other intense rock genres for the Titan bosses and many different edm genres used for cyberspace.The most fun things to collect for me were the vault keys found in cyberspace and the memory tokens from the obstacle courses scattered throughout the world. There were also collectables like seeds of power and defence as well as the islands inhabitants called kocos to upgrade Sonic's power, defence, wall running and climbing speed and ring capacity. You can also collect these items in a fishing mini-game accessible through a purple portal in the open zone, and costs fishing tokens to play that are scattered around the islands. Fishing, though calming and amusing, wasn't very involved and just required pressing a button at the right times. The rewards were reason enough to stick with it though, even having extra story memos available.Some of the cyberspace stages even though having re-used level themes (3 of the 4 themes being re-used assets of Green Hill, Chemical Plant and Sky Sanctuary) and some segments just replicated from older titles, regardless were all pretty fun.Most feeling like a speedy bonus stage to speedrun through with some exceptions where the levels were honestly the best level design the series has had in a long time (although a lot of that felt due to mimicing SA2 design). They were fun to replay a few times and complete all the 4 objectives. The controls were different from the customisable ones on the island though which were perfect, which lead to cyberspace feeling a little worse by comparison. The controls were still good but felt stiffer and slower, though this was to fit the stage design I presume.Also the visuals in all the cyberspace stages were really nice and had a very cyber aesthetic as their name would imply.The islands had some nice visuals too, a little unfitting for a Sonic title, especially when you have the contrast of the cyberspace stages, but I got used to the more realistic approach quickly, also kind of justified since this is an unexplored territory that used to home an ancient civilisation, I thought if it looks weird that's maybe the point in a way.It was always a fun time exploring though and had enough things to do so never felt empty, but also gave the right amount of space to run around.The islands were so fun to explore and probably the strongest aspect of the game, however I couldn't shake the feeling of the terrain being made to look good first and have Sonic's movement in mind as an afterthought, though the obstacle courses were there to lend help to that. The obstacle courses themselves although always engaging and fun to do, didn't feel tied in to the world at all with very few exceptions.There was also one activity on the islands that would happen randomly and distrupt the game for a few seconds showing stars falling from the sky, then after that small cutscene have this slot machine in your face for like 5 minutes while you collect the stars to activate it, you can receive some fishing tokens during this, but the problem was that even if you didn't collect stars or want to partake in it and are busy platforming, you'll have the slot machine taking up a decent portion of the screen which was just so frustrating since you couldn't stop it if you weren't interested, this event respawns the enemies on the island meaning you can endlessly fight the bosses, which was nice if you wanted to revisit some.Story wasn't great but I wouldn't say bad, it was intriguing at first but suddenly changed towards the end and felt unnatural. I really appreciated its more serious tone, the world building and liked the characters more than I have in any Sonic game to date. Not every activity on the island was enjoyable, but they were passable, probably the game's weakest aspect. Though I never got bored or frustrated with them, they just felt very simple and like they could be in any game for the most part.Combat was also a more prominent inclusion to this game than in others minus Unleashed, and it's nothing special but I feel if it was more complex it would detract from the speedy style of Sonic.Parrying however is broken, the way it works is just holding both dodge buttons and you can just keep that held until an enemy attacks to create an opening for dealing damage, you're even able to do it mid-air and it looks very silly floating motionless in a pose. I hope that is fixed because it's ridiculous that you can just hold a combination of buttons to deflect almost every attack in the game (I tried to use parrying as little as possible or to only use it reactively just to give myself more of a challenge).The combat although a little underdeveloped and without much strategy involved besides the cyloop ability and some other techniques were required for certain enemies. It was still cool especially in terms of visuals, the cyloop did add some depth to it and overall the combat made the enemies more engaging than they have been in past Sonic games. The mini bosses were a bit of a mixed bag with some being very fun more standard fights, others having a unique gimmick that was sometimes enjoyable but 1 or 2 of them either grew tiresome or frustrating. The Titan bosses though were really fun, sometimes having a camera issue that would make the next attack unclear, but otherwise were awesome, both thematically and gameplay wise.I'm definitely going to be replaying this game a lot and overall was a very fun time. It met my expectations, even while being rough around the edges and having a pretty weak story. It's quickly become one of my favourites in the series and I'd recommend it highly to any Sonic fan.Sonic Team needed and wanted more time to make this truly special though and I can't speak for how the average gamer would feel on it, maybe give it a shot if it's on sale. I really hope that they continue this kind of formula in future though as it works incredibly well for Sonic, especially for a first attempt.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this for ₹3,499 (launch price) but considering other latest games that you can get for this, I would recommend getting this on a sale. Apart from the price though :[+] Great and varied soundtrack. Includes calm atmospheric piano, lo-fi, metalcore, rock, EDM, DnB, etc..[+] High speed platforming with multiple routes to take through the islands.[+] Great boss presentations[+] Fun movement, even just running around with no specific goal in mind is fun.[+] With update 1 and 2, adds a lot of extra challenges and collectibles to find.[+] Fast and fluid combat that (almost) never feels pace breaking. The material rewards for combat do become  unnecessary quickly though.[-] Cyberspace aesthetic themes are repetitive and level quality is not consistent across the cyberspace.[-] The pop-in is very noticeable. It is also problematic here more than other open games since you run so fast. Objects can really jump out at you. And it can be sometimes confusing getting an item just because the relevant objects didn't load in.[-] Along with the updates, no new Achievements have been added. Some difficult challenges only reward you with a crown on the title screen.[-] The last (story) act is not satisfying, but the free Update 3 is speculated to fix that.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been a Sonic the Hedgehog fan since I played the original hit game on Sega Genesis at my cousins house when it came out. I spent a lot of time in my youth playing games at my cousins house as I only had a PC. I've played almost every release of Sonic the Hedgehog games excluding Sonic and the black knight including uncommon ones like Sonic R, 3D Blast, Sonic CD. Sonic Shuffle, SNES Sonic rom. Sonic Frontiers isn't just the best Sonic game in 3D, it's the best Sonic game. Sonic has come a long way since the 90s and I'm happy that the game got to grow and evolve over time. I still think the boss battle from Sonic Adventure 2 is the best and my personal favorite. You have the freedom to get crazy strong (the game has RPG like stat upgrades that are mostly optional and increase your speed, Ring Capacity, attack strength and defense).This is the fastest sonic has ever been and the control of his speed is excellent. Almost all boss battles and mini boss battles are over the top fun spectacles that has Sonic doing what he does best and that is run. It's not just a homing attack in different boss stages although that element is there too. Sonic also seems to have all his skills from previous games including the spin dash which I don't think was in a 3D Sonic game since Sonic Adventure. You even have the light speed dash. Speaking of which the game feels like a love letter to Sonic fans by mentioning previous bits of story and lore. Most reviewers would tell you the characters are well written for once, I'd say most Sonic games has more 2D character design and development but I never minded because I'm such a Sonic fan but even though you don't play as any other characters , the characters all feel thought out and expressed in ways I've never seen before in previous Sonic games. It felt great later on Knuckles being grateful but showing his competitive side just after Super Sonic defeated a boss and Knuckles was like that was good but we both know I'd beat him faster as Hyper Kunckles. Made me smile, lots of nods to previous Sonic games like Sonic 3 and Knuckles where Knuckles was able to transform to hyper form. The game is set up in an open world where most of the platforming and adventure and story happens. To progress the story you play Cyberspace levels that are digitally created from Sonic's memories meaning they are all levels inspired by previous Sonic games with some original ones too. Most of them are fairly short between a minute to 4 minutes on average with some taking longer. You won't be able to run through them once and move on, the game will require you to "get good" and use those Red Ring finding skills as you won't get the required keys (needed to progress the story) unless you 1. Reach the goal 2. Finish fast under a set time 3. Attain certain amount of Rings 4. Find ALL red rings. You won't need to complete all objectives but you will need to complete some in order to progress. To even access the cyberspace levels you will need defeat mini bosses on the main world. This might sound tedious on paper but most of the game you can play organically and only sometimes will you need to farm vault keys or gears. There's a lot of cyberspace levels I didn't even know existed when I finished the game with a 100% Achievement on Steam. They're all fun to run through. The only downside is that they control like previous Sonic Games and have their speed. This isn't a problem as those games were just fine but Sonic doesn't feel as good as he feels on the overworld map, thankfully this is where almost all of the game takes place. Graphics are great, a lot of inspiration from Breath of the Wild even some sound effects that I would have thought were from BoTW. Performance is pretty good but without mods you can't go above 60 fps which is a bummer. Sound is great , music is just awesome as you've probably seen memes of Sonic's boss fights already. The new Sights and sounds updates adds a ton of iconic music from previous Sonic titles ranging from remixed Sonic classics to Sonic Heroes to Sonic Adventure, that you can set on the over world easily. There's more to find and do and mini boss battles are just so much fun ranging from chasing high speed enemies to grinding rails in the sky to follow a flying boss, to a wrestling like caged fight where you have to bounce off walls and much more. While you can mostly homing attack there are regular enemies that destroy you if you do that, you will have to punch and kick and you unlock projectile attacks too. You even get a block with the ability to counterattack and it works wonders and looks very cool. Sonic has all his popular attacks from previous games and even powered up versions of them if you buy them with skill points. The new cycloop stuff exclusive to Sonic Frontiers is great and while simple adds a solid element to both fighting and puzzle solving and even just exploration. If you remotely like Sonic The hedgehog get this game at any price. It's a fantastic experience and if it's your first Sonic game you'll love it too but I'd at least watch some videos online of previous Sonic games or watch one of the shows like Sonic X or the new Sonic prime just to get a feel for the characters and atmosphere.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm gonna be real with you, I did not expect to like this game. After Forces and the disastrous reveal of this game, I was ready to write it off. But man, this game is FUN. It's definitely not polished in the slightest, very typical of Sonic Team, but when it works, it really works. The open world feels jam packed with content, and very unique. No Ubisoft towers here. The regular Sonic levels are good fun too, but they seem a bit more glitchy than the open world stuff, and Sonic doesn't control nearly as well as he does in Unleashed or Generations. Once you get used to it, though, it's good fun trying to beat all the challenges.The story is pretty good in my opinion. It doesn't suffer from open world-itis where you don't really give a rat's ass about the characters or environment by the end of it (looking at you, Breath of the Wild), and it gives you a good motivation to keep going. Now, I will say that I'm slightly biased because it's very contingent on you having played and enjoyed previous Sonic games, which I do. If you're not a big Sonic fan, the story will probably be a little nonsensical.In conclusion, Sonic Frontiers is a surprisingly decent game. Definitely not game of the year material, but definitely a good time and a good launching point for future Sonic games to build on. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the newest form of Sonic, I didn't think open a open world would work but it does and I never realized till now how much since it makes! Looking out to somewhere like a waterfall or a tower and going, "Let's head that way" and actually getting there at super speeds feels amazing! And if you run into a boss fight but just feel like exploring, you can just leave the boss fight. Straight up run past them. And the new abilities Sonic can get adds so much and different kinds of thinking, what used to be a simple homing attack can now be much more of an epic battle of taking away shields, digging up rings, destroying parts of enemies or even the enemy themselves and finding collectible items. AND THAT'S ONLY ONE POWER! There's still more where you can dish out all kinds of attacks like multiple sonic booms, move fast enough to appear in multiple places and you can get an upgrade to get skill points from air tricks! This isn't, "Oh it's another new type of Sonic game..." This is if you took the character Sonic and said, "How do we make him OP as heck, and how do we get players to use such abilities?" Even more so, when you do scale up a tower or a set of platforms high up, it feels so good and mastering things like climbing a tower is like playing through a scene from Sonic CD where he climbs up a rocky mountain in the opening cut-scene, except with more toys  like wall climb/running sections, homing attacks, rails, springs and cables. Would a new person to the Sonic franchise have a bit of a rough go trying to figure out how Sonic works? I will admit, it would be rough. But for long term fans, or just anyone who has played or is aware of how the latest 3D games work, they will have a great time! Oh, and they put in the drop dash, and you can maintain the spin dash form if going downhill! Not only did Sega came up with a new boost system for this game, but the spin dash is back! It's not just for classic Sonic!

_childDocuments_.review: The only way I can describe my experience with this game is a wild, breathtaking adventure. Obviously, I have some bias due to me being a Sonic fan. But I genuinely can recommend this  to anyone who wants to get into Sonic. Unlike most games in the series as of late, I can actually relate to the characters as the writing for this game is a massive improvement to previous installments. Tails is no longer that guy who stays on the sidelines and wants to stand up for himself. I also really enjoyed Knuckles and Sonic’s dynamic in the second island.The way Sonic controls in the open-zone is probably the most fluid he’s felt since Sonic Adventure. I’m not even kidding. They even added speed sliders in the settings so you can adjust how you want Sonic to feel. I never get bored of just running around on the islands and seeing what new pathways and puzzles I can find.Don’t even get me started on the boss fights. Those titan fights are beyond cinematic. The music complements it perfectly and I never would’ve expected to hear screaming in a Sonic game. I just wish that you could use Super Sonic in the open-zone once you beat the game. That would’ve been so fun to play.The only real complaint I could make about this game is Cyber Space. Basically, you defeat enemies or mini bosses on the map and receive “Portal Gears” which can be used to enter Cyber Space portals. They’re basically just bite-sized stages based on games like Generations and Forces. The problem is that it’s possible to complete every single level in under one minute. Way too short for what they are and Sonic doesn’t even control the way he does in the open-zone. They’re unfortunately my least favorite part about Sonic Frontiers.Overall, I really had a fun time playing this game. It was a very intriguing experience and definitely and has a very unique style compared to any other Sonic game released yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I have literally zero gripes with this game. But I'm gonna make this a short review.The last Sonic game that I played AND invested time in was Sonic Adventure 2 BATTLE for the GameCube. I loved every bit of that one, and this one takes the cake.Let's talk:It's a Sonic game.Jesus LORD ALMIGHTY THERE IS NOT ONE TRACK ON THIS OST THAT IS NOT A BOP. Hands down one of the greatest OSTs I've heard of all time. Everything meshes well together with the scene that accompanies each track and what it represents. Not once did I dread any location in this VIDEO GAME because of the amazing soundtrack. It carried the mood whenever I felt like I was running in an empty, lonely void.There are only two moments where I felt like things were being recycled, and it was negligible: Enemy types and overall theme of the cyberspace choices.Past those two, EVERYTHING ELSE felt like a breath of  fresh air. Each boss, minigame, zone, track, loops, felt new and innovative to the game.There are two modes you are able to choose from at the beginning of the game (and edit through the options later on if you change your mind):  and . The Sonic Team recommends the latter for veteran Sonic players and the former for newcomers.Everything feels incredibly  as you progress through the game - powering up your stats of Power, Defense, Speed, and Ring Capacity.By default, the tutorial is your loading screen so you're never staring at nothing; there's always something to do.There's fishing that DOESN'T feel tedious, isn't that great?Sonic Frontiers has everything - and more - that you thought you needed in a Sonic game.The fact that they tie the continuity of the stories of the PAST GAMES into Frontiers will make all Sonic fans want to be even more involved. Frontiers really brings everything together and even provides some comedic quips regarding characters and events that are not featured in the game.It's pretty mysterious, and you will have questions..and you will buy Sonic Frontiers to answer those questions.If you love the aesthetic/feel of TLoZ: Breath of The Wild (all emptiness included), the intense music of DMC, and the action and speed of Sonic, then Sonic Frontiers is a fantastic pick.It's more than a "Sonic game."It's a labor of love.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic game.Soundtrack is unbelievable, story is wonderful, gameplay loop is great, game mechanics are excellent, and the movement is awesome in the overworld.The levels are okaaaay, The "gameplay corridors" are good, they're very fun to play through. But i really don't like the homing attack delay on enemies, the slow boost speed, the one boost per jump limit, and the repeated use of only four level themes where the background design is both bland and cluttered. I expected the late game to have some "sonic frontiers" levels, but i was disappointed to see it was more repeats. The menu is also unbearably slow.Although my con section is longer than my pro section, i'm still blown away by this game.I am proud to say i'm a sonic fan again.

Preheat oven to 350°F (177°C). Grease two 9-inch cake pans, line with parchment paper, then grease the parchment paper. Parchment paper helps the cakes seamlessly release from the pans.2. In a medium bowl, whisk together flour, cornstarch, cocoa powder, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.3. In a large mixing bowl using a handheld or stand mixer fitted with a whisk or paddle attachment, beat butter on high speed until smooth and creamy - about 1 minute. Add granulated sugar and beat on high speed for 2 minutes until creamed together fairly well. Scrape down the sides and up the bottom of the bowl with a rubber spatula as needed.4. On medium-high speed, add oil to the butter/sugar mixture in a slow steady stream until fully combined and creamy - about 2 minutes. Beat egg whites and vinegar together in a medium bowl using a handheld or stand mixer fitted with a whisk attachment or whisk vigorously by hand until thick and foamy - about 3 minutes. _childDocuments_.review: Its been awhile since we've gotten this good of a sonic game. The 3D movement feels good, the story's actually alright with decent character development with added lore and plenty of references for all Sonic fans. The combat is a bit jank and it's barely even used. You unlock all your abilities by the 2nd island which is very disappointing. The pop in gets pretty annoying which does interfere with exploring a bit. The 2D sections control pretty bad and there's alot of them so be ready for that. Cyberspace levels are very much hit or miss. You'll love them or hate em. The music is really good which comes as no surprise. The boss fights are really good and are varied in both combat and design. My main issue with this game is that it is very repetitive. You will experience just about everything the game has to offer by the second island. With that being said, this game gets my recommendation. I hope SEGA continues and improves on this formula going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't normally write reviews but I felt like I absolutely had to for this one. As an avid Sonic fan for years since the early 2000's. This game is definitely a love letter to fans. Sega poured their heart and soul into this title. Is it a perfect game?? No. Is it a perfect SONIC game?? A resounding yes. This is how Sonic should feel. There are so many aspects that outshine the flaws. It legitimately makes me feel like a kid again running around in the Mystic Ruins from SA1. The combat is enjoyable and beating enemies and bosses is satisfying. It makes you feel empowered. The story takes itself seriously and has charm, but also there is alot of lore for fans of early generations of the franchise to enjoy. Exploring the islands never felt like it was a chore. There are plenty of things to keep you moving at top speed, from grind rails, and springs etc. In conclusion what Sega has here for Sonic is a very good blueprint. I hope to see them expand on this idea more and give fans what they deserve. They definitely delivered this time around after many many dark years. Sonic is back again and he is better than ever before! Cheers to another 30 years and beyond!
