_childDocuments_.review: Sonic is back! The last time I was excited for a Sonic game was Sonic Adventure on the Dreamcast, which was over 20 years ago. Sonic Frontiers delivers! It's everything you'd want in an evolution of the Sonic formula that grew stale a long time ago. They don't call this Sonic Adventure 3, but it may as well be. The world is massive. There is so much to do and explore. You can truly get lost in it. The sound track is one of the best I've ever heard and perfectly accentuates the mood. You have everything from calm soothing orchestral tracks for the overworld, to more gamey videogame music that you'd expect for the virtual levels, to metal for the boss fights. Speaking of the boss fights, they're out of this world! I don't want to spoil anything, but you are in for a treat, especially that first boss.Sonic has a host of new abilities to deal with these big bads and new foes. He can jump into the air and send out shock waves. He can smash the ground and boost around enemies to damage them to name a few. You unlock these new attacks via a talent tree using currency that you collect by solving puzzles and doing things around the map. I'm not sold on the talent tree, but the abilities themselves are fun and change it up a bit from what you'd expect. The world is made up of different islands. Each island is a giant open map for you to explore as you see fit. You primarily navigate the map via a system of grind rails. Solve puzzles you find around the map to get more grind rails to better traverse the map and expose more of it on your map. It's very reminiscent of Zelda: Breath of the Wild. When you solve a puzzle there is even a little chime that plays that sounds very similar to the one in Breath of the Wild. It works though and is a very enjoyable experience. The virtual levels you find littered around the maps are like mini levels that are exactly what you'd expect from a Sonic game based on previous titles. You have to complete the different objectives in these to unlock their keys, which are needed to get the chaos emeralds. You need the chaos emeralds to beat the bosses of each island. It's a repetitive gameplay loop, but it works.Sonic Frontiers isn't all sunshine and rainbows though. On the technical side, this game leaves something to be desired. I've played the Switch version, as well as the Steam release, and I can say the Steam version is definitely the better one. It still suffers from pop in though, which is an issue that seems to get worse the faster you make Sonic's speed. The engine just can't keep up. It's not a little pop in either. It's entire objects and geometry in places and definitely detracts from the experience. On PC, I play with an RTX 3080 in 1440p Ultrawide and Sonic Frontiers seemed stable enough, though I wish it wasn't locked to 60fps and had more options in the PC version. It's a console port and it shows.Overall, Sonic Frontiers is an excellent game. It's the first Sonic game that has gotten me excited about Sonic in over 20 years. It tries a lot of new things, and while it doesn't deliver on all of them, it's a blast all around to play. If this is the blue print for Sonic going forward, I am very excited to see how it will continue to evolve over time. This is a title I easily recommend. If you're a Sonic fan, you'll love it. If you're new to Sonic, or if you're like me and haven't played a Sonic game in a long time, you'll enjoy it. BUY THIS GAME!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Frontiers is a right step in the direction of where Sonic games need to go. Open-world style just feels right for the blue hedgehog, since now he can run around wherever, being unrestricted by linear level design. The game has a great control scheme, pretty graphics, runs very smooth, and the boost formula has been fixed, for the most part. The game has an unbelievably amazing soundtrack, which is normal for Sonic games. The Cyber-Space levels are little levels that you can enter to collect items crucial for game progression, and they contain throwbacks to prior Sonic games, with amazing music, platforming, and a good challenge. Some issues i have with the game are that the world design isn't perfect, so the world gets repetitive sometimes, and the terrain can sometimes cause Sonic to clip into objects and glitch the world around him. Some Cyber-Space levels are too difficult for their placement in the games' progression stages, and cut-scene facial muscle animation is lagged and difficult to follow. Some text UI is low-poly. These errors are few and far between, though. And with expansion coming in 2023, like new game modes, challenges, features, and a new story, the blue hedgehog isn't done yet. Great job, Sonic Team! Sonic is making a comeback :)

_childDocuments_.review: It's a Sonic power fantasy game in a sandbox with hundreds of platforming puzzles. The outsides of the sandbox have too many invisible walls, but inside the sandbox you can finagle your momentum to break puzzles to your heart's content. You sometimes play a modern stage with emphasis on exploration, collecting and keeping rings, and speedrunning (personally I wish S rank times were harder).The dialogue isn't bad, especially so for a Sonic game. Characters break out of their pigeon-holes that Sega previously stuffed them in.Combat exists, it's not very hard; maybe parries need to have a timing window, maybe the ranged attack and some of the combo attacks should eat chunks of your boost gauge so you can't spam them endlessly. Fishing.

The open zone, the addition of EDM music for the cyberspace levels, the Titan bosses and themes (the first 3 mainly, the 4th is a rehash of the games theme which sounded pretty anticlimatic for me) and even the island themes caught my attention; from the soothiness and melancholy inducing to the most fiery and blood rushing tracks. If it werent for the Titan bosses i think the game wouldnt have aged that well. The first two updates have left a very good impression on me, but the last is the one I am most excited for. I mean, its incredible how they didnt charge anything for the second-half story overhaul, (which was obviously rushed and under-developed) and 3 playable characters! It is a shame that SEGA was rushing them and simultaneously glad the game was delayed for 1 year , though the devs could have achieved more into utilizing their whole vision. All in all, I hope the team continues to grow and evolve, knowing the director himself listened to a lot of feedback and SEGA finally giving them a proper budget and time (not 100% sure about that) to work on their next big project. Its really freeing to be honest for us sonic fans! Thank you SEGA for the W's you currently giving us! Excited for update 3! Well then; to another 100 years of sonic greatness!

_childDocuments_.review: The game was very fun, very nice story compared to the past couple of games. The game-play was fun, but I will describe prior to update 2 and after update 2 game-play just to give an idea of how much update 2 changed things:Before Update 1:The game was fun, the platforming, challenges, and enemies are very easy. I liked the story's depth. The ending feels like it was done on a weekend so it brings the score down a lot. It barely had any momentum and physics, you could get around that by rail jumping but there wasn't an easy way to go fast aside from power boosting. All challenges had to be completed the way they were designed, so the game-play loop was very one dimensional. There wasn't much to be done after beating the game.Overall the game for me was a 6.5/10Before Update 2:The game was pretty fun, after beating the game, you can collect the music notes. There was also the battle-rush, and the cyberspace challenges-which wasn't part of the main game, they are side modes. So post-game is lacking still. Extreme mode is very fun, but it removes like half of the side stuff you can do like leveling up so it's literally just for beating the story again but harder.Overall the game for me was a 7/10After Update 2:Man what an update, the game is so much more fun now. The new Kokos added into the game make it so much fun to complete their challenges as they are much harder than the normal challenges, there's also the boost gauge upgrades it offers so it incentives you to go for them. I wish there were more unique challenges like these, they remind me of Sonic Unleashed difficulty and level design which was very high quality. There's been added open world challenges added that are kind of difficult, so it's fun, beating them unlocks the spin-dash. THE SPINDASH IS BROKEN IN THE BEST WAY POSSIBLE. I understand why you would need to unlock it but it was so much fun 100% the game using it. The challenges now can be beaten by using slope physics and momentum instead of doing them the normal way. Normal players can beat them normally, but experienced players looking for a faster and more challenging method can launch off a ramp and beat them that way. So fun. The birthday stuff was also fun for a day or 2 but I'm done feeling like I'm on LSD after a day or 2. NG+ is fun on extreme mode with the spin-dash and carrying over your updates, it makes you feel less under-powered. I wish the boost gauge would also carry over, but it's not a big deal.This update has increased the games quality by a lot. I can't wait for update 3.BOOSTS THE GAME UP TO A 8.5/10Criticism 1:The game is still very easy, it would be nice to implement some level scaling for the enemies, it's ridiculous that you can kill each titan in 2 minutes by abusing the power moves. I'm not saying make levels irrelevent, just make it so they slightly scale as the player scales, something like:* Sonic lvl 1: Titan boss lvl 10.* Sonic lvl 50: Titan boss lvl 35.* Sonic lvl 99: Titan boss lvl 60.So as Sonic gets stronger, the titans scale up, but at a smaller rate, so it's still possible to be overpowered, but also not possible to one punch titans like SUPREME.Criticism 2:SUPREME should get his bad-ass wings back, how are they only in the cut-scene. The entire boss needs to be refactored, he doesn't have any unique moves and when you're maxed out you can 1 punch him. He doesn't use his gun  outside of one QTE event.Criticism 3:THE END still sucks, hopefully Update 3 addresses this. The game shouldn't turn into a space shooter for the final boss.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Team tried their best with this one, they pulled all the scripted sequences, all the 2D sections, they even  dumbed down the boost formula even further, but despite their best effort to make a mediocre-at-best game like Forces was, this is one of the good ones. So Sonic Frontiers is essentially a collectathon, you wander around open levels, clear platform challenges, solve puzzles and defeat enemies to get McGuffins that allow you to face more of the aforementioned challenges, to get even more McGuffins and so on. The difference this time is that you're Sonic, so you're really fast and, because of that, said open levels have to be really big, more akin to open world (dubbed Open Zone) areas rather then levels from a platformer. The reason I'm saying that they tried their best to make a mediocre game and failed is that despite the egregious amount of scripting in a game genre about freedom of action, because of the same nature of that genre (and Sonic's insane mobility), said scripting can be easily bypassed. The result is a game that is good for the same reason some of the best 3d platformer are good (please don't read this as if I said that this game is as good as super Mario 64, that's a completely different sentence).What I'm talking about is the freedom of action and the sheer amount of cool stuff you can pull off.You see, one of the main collectibles needed to progress the story are these "memory tokens", you can find these floating above far above your head, supposedly only reachable through really ugly platforms that are just lying around with no artistic cohesion whatsoever, giving this game its signature "SEGA hired this man" vibe. This platforming challenges are, per se, fine, but what really sets this game apart is how easy to break this are, yes, you can follow the standard path and run through loops and jump on springs, OR you can boost jump from a grind rail on the other side of the world, gain an insane amount of air and try to aim yourself to get the collectible. And the whole game is like this, you just need a ramp or an enemy and you can do whatever, not unlike super Mario 64's BLJ. And that's the biggest strength of the game, once you complete a few missions in the map, the (again, very ugly) rails used as fast travel start collecting together, with enough finesse you can chain rails, platforms and attacks on enemies to travel the world without touching the ground, it's a similar feeling to chaining tricks in a Tony hawk game and can get really satisfying, even though it's not the main focus of the game but just a side effect.  And for these reasons my favorite open zone was the third one, despite being the worst design wise (full of 2D sections) simply because it was pushing me to find ways to go around them.I ended up collection ALL memory tokens in the game, and i can't stress enough how much is not needed to do so for finishing the game, you just need a fraction of those (and it's you don't want to get them the intended way you can still farm them for a couple of minutes in the fishing mini game (yeah there's a fishing mini game, it's pretty innocuous, you only have to play it is you want to read Eggman's diary)), you don't even need them to COMPLETE the game, you don't even get bragging rights from them, i just did it because i was having fun doing so.The story is also an improvement from most Sonic games actually but ESPECIALLY Forces, where, instead of being edgy for the sake of looking important (but ultimately feeling shallow), has a much simpler story with a deeper meaning. We actually have a THEME in the story this time. The story in Frontiers is about facing the inevitable and the game explore how every character reacts to it, most importantly Sage, the series' new entry, who is so sure about what's going to happen that doesn't even bother explaining it to Sonic and instead is openly hostile to him who instead is still hopeful and it's going to fight no matter what. The writing also helps, for the first time in way too long we have actual character development, to the point where even missteps like force have payoff.All secondary characters have their substory connected to the main events of the game. Amy for the first time in the main series menages to feel like Amy, always thinking about love, without being annoying; Knuckles and Sonic's rivalry and friendship is felt through their dialogs and Tails is trying to grow up after Forces. The rest of the game is fine:So the game is good, but what worries me is how is SEGA going to evolve the formula, despite how wonky the game physics may be, the biggest problem of the game is that they're not broken ENOUGH, hopefully for the next game Sonic won't abruptly stop every time he jumps, but how i said, since the best aspects of the game happened by accident, I can just hope.  EDIT:Jesus Christ i just re-read this, it's like twice as long as I thought, why nobody told me?           ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ editing the review made it lose the formatting and now it's unreadable, thanks steam

_childDocuments_.review: FOR THE LOVE OF GOD PLAY THIS GAME! I just finished the first island, 100% of it, and fought the first major boss. This is the first time in over a decade that I've fully submerged myself into a sonic game and I'm loving every bit of it. The story is something we haven't seen in a sonic game be this serious in such a long time, the characters actually have character! (no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way) and the voice acting is actually pretty damn good. Gameplay wise this is nothing short of a blast to play. If you're a fan of the 3D sonic games such as Generations, Unleashed, and Colors, this game takes the good and makes it better. I won't go into spoiler territory but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game has the best soundtrack that I've ever heard from a game in years! if you like Devil May Cry, Metal Gear Rising or any other game that pumps out thunderous metal tracks while you fight then this is the game for you. The open world is massive yet not overwhelming at the same time, giving players an easy time figuring out the layout of the map while giving you plenty of room to boost around and practice your free running. Hunting down items never feels tedious but instead feels innovative and clever, having to figure out how to get from point A to point B in the most efficient way possible to collect all the little trinkets and doo-dads that are sprinkled around the map. The combat feels fluid and fun to control, however not perfect. I've experienced a couple little bugs but it's honestly not a big deal in the grand scheme of things. So yeah, if you're a bit on the fence with this game and weren't 100% sure if you wanted to commit, I so strongly recommend this game especially if you're a Sonic fan (AHEM and a fan of Metal tracks in your video games) Sonic is back!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- open zone idea with different islands is great and traversal generally works pretty well- the story is a welcome change in the series and it works well both on its own as well as in the context of earlier titles- the things floating around the world doesn't actually feel of if you fix pop in and the story even provides some sort of an explanation- they keep updating the game and the introduction of momentum for example made it quite a bit better after launch, although it obviously can't work perfectly well in every situation since they designed most of the worlds without it in mind- the soundtrack is fantastic including both great new tracks as well as previous bangers from the seriesCons:- they entirely based it around the weakest platform (Switch) and did not bother to properly optimize it for the stronger consoles and PC -> pop in and LOD are atrocious and you should use mods to not be constantly distracted by technical shortcomings- the fact that you need a mod/code to unlock the frame rate in a 2022 game is a joke- they started building the worlds and everything within them on the basis of lacking game physics and while they're showing that they can significantly improve it (momentum update) the level design is mostly not based around it- they wanted a little too much in too little time, some things just feel rushed and do not always work resulting in deaths or having to climb up things from the bottom againConclusion:It's not perfect by any means, but you can partly fix it yourself with mods/codes and if you can live with some minor frustrations with some passages not always working quite as intended you'll have a fantastic time with it. It also lays a very good foundation for the next game and if they can directly start building upon that (incl. momentum etc.) and release the next one in a more polished state. Frontiers is good, but the successor could be the game we're all waiting for if continue to push it in the right direction.

_childDocuments_.review: -- INTRODUCTION --Sonic Frontiers is not just a improvement over Sonic Forces but it succeeds to beat the liking of most of the Boost area games from the last decade.The good boost games, only regarding the base boost machanic, like Unleashed, Colours and Generation have a better overall feel for what they were designed for and are far superior to the Cyberspace levels in any way possible but they are either way too short or highly inconsistent like Colours and Unleashed.Sonic Frontiers succeeds at staying consistent but is not affraid to try out new ideas like puzzles, tiny 2D sections in the open world and the very dumb but amazingly fun fishing game.-- NEGATIVE -- (nothing insulting, just opinions and facts but keep reading, the positive stuff is overwhelming)**Development and Bugs**Knowing that Sega always pushes out their games even before they are done makes this game even more of a miracle, I mean 5 years of development! - that is highly unusual. Though, Sega being Sega, they still pushed out the game with many bugs, nothing game breaking but just tiny annoyences like loading erros, objects just appearing(pop in), frame drops, collision errors etc.**Gameplay**It is quite hard to know where you are on the island since every part looks pretty much the same, even while using the map you get disorianted easily.The fourth island felt a little lazy and was part of the first island, so nothing new which was a little dissapointing, other than that, Cyberspace was a fun distraction but controlled poorly and I kept boosting of stage when trying to correct myself, the same applies while gliding down from the sky, it sucked to control.Titan fights were awesome but very easy to break in a way where you just knew you were fighting a 3D model with animations and some code.I was very enraged by tiny stone plates on the ground which cancled out my Cyloop and made Sonic flicker/jitter around.**Story**!!PLAY WITH SUBTITLES, I MISSED THE WHOLE ANCIENT PLOT!!There were quite a few story inconsistencies towards the end, but I doubt that this was writer Ian Flynn's fault but more so what he was given by Sonic Team. Every island has these Story moments when you collect memory tokens but the last one could've given Sage and Sonic more moments together which was the weakest island story beat wise, Sage had a great development all the way trough but got cut off a little at the end. (Also I never knew that this giant moon thing was coming and I was a little confused by the whole end sequence and we never found out who the speaking voice was for Sonic or I probably just missed it, either way, something that could've been improved.)-- POSITIVE --**Gameplay**Sonic Frontiers, like the Adventure Series, has tiny games everywhere (not talking about the puzzles).From Pinball to collecting Scraps, Gardening or Fishing, it's all here! Of course, games that use Sonic's character controller do suffer from the same issues like other parts of the game but it all feels consistent which is the most important thing.Running trough the open world felt great, having these tiny gameplay functions like infinite boost or the very fast boost felt awesome, need to go somewhere quick? Fill up your rings with cyloop and you are good to go!Puzzles were a great way to update your map, I even prefer it over the towers in BotW. Sidestep puzzles, run from A to B and so much more, it felt awesome!The combat was not as button mashy as I expected, it actually felt like something I had to think about the further I progressed and required skill for certain mini boss type enemies which, trust me, were not easy but not in a unfair way but rather in a way that intrigued me to keep trying and not give up!Running on these Green/Blue/Rainbowish walls is just *chefs kiss*, that was the only part I enjoyed about Lost World back then but it is truly made for this game to move around the enviroment.The Super Sonic sections felt nice, maybe a little too easy but still quite nice. They were beautifully composed with visual flair and made you not just feel but know that you are about to whoop this Titan's ass.I have more to say but let us move on.**Visuals**Beautiful, I was so worried back in Summer 2022 about the visuals but Sonic Team proved us that they knew what they were doing. They are using the Quixel libary, which are scans of realworld textures. Making something look nice using Quixel is quite hard since it still depends on good lighting, Sonic Team put in 110% to get the best out of lighting to make the textures feel integrated and it really worked out for them. Day and night cycles work great, the new character designs are also breathtaking.Particle and VFX are also a great improvement to what came before.There is more to be said but I will leave it as is for now.*Story*Finally! Sonic is not a jerkward anymore, he is back to being a occasionally joking but yet a well meaning friend like in Sonic06 and Unleashed. If Sonic would have to leave someone behind for a greater purpose, Sonic wouldn't care, he would go trough all the trouble in the world, saving/helping each and everyone because this is what he knows is right, he fights against all odds, no matter what.Sonic's relationship with Knuckles is great, they respect each other and apreciate what both did in the past, jokingly testing who is better at starring to then break out in laughter. Sonic even stops Knuckles from attacking Sage but instead of Knuckles getting angry, he trusts Sonic to know what he is doing.For once they don't fall back to, Tails - Scared but Smart, Amy - THE Sonic Fangirl, Knuckles - Brain AFK/Agressive and Eggman - acting so smart yet so stupid, all of them grow far beyond from what they were the last 12 years and this is great.Sage is very. and I mean very well written, that is all I will say since I don't want to spoil anyone.From occasional references to past games, locations and characters, Sonic Frontiers has it all, it even attempts to make the overall lore of the games coherent.Great job Ian, great job!-- What now? --Sega, if you see this, please keep giving your team the time and for god sake, keep Ian Flynn, he knows what he is doing. Make your games and make them make sense, make them longer again like now, keep game testing, it really helps you guys and trust me, we Sonic fans are able to wait another five years and are willing to wait even longer if needed.This game is a 8/10 for me.It has issues and bugs but even now, Sonic Team is still gathering and working to fix them.100% recommended even if you don't care about Sonic.

_childDocuments_.review: This installment to the Sonic franchise is a good step in the right direction. There are a few graphical errors currently with some of the shaders, as well as a few spots in the game where the controls are a little sloppy, but this is far from holding the game back and should not deter you from enjoying a Sonic title that has been a long time coming for most fans of the series. Frontiers is a different approach for Sonic, bringing him into the open-world exploration scene. The game delivers on keeping the flow, as Sonic moves from one obstacle to the next. However, this is all done with little effort. The unfortunate feeling I was left with after the first few hours of gameplay was there was a lot of these puzzles and rail systems to "do" but no a ton to gain from any of it. Moreover, some of the obstacles just seemed to chain together in a way that almost seemed like scripted events. This left everything to feel like filler in an otherwise open map; all while you completed the main story objectives or looked for actual levels to complete. A giant missed opportunity would have been collecting upgrades around the islands, similar to the upgrades from Sonic Adventure 1's overworld sections.The boss battles will most likely leave you wanting more unfortunately, as the game failed to deliver some innovative ideas for combat sequences within the game. Most combat scenarios during your playthrough will consist of you pressing the same button over and over until the enemy is dead. Enemy has a shield? Press one additional button to take away the shield before continuing to spamming attack button.I wanted to be honest in this review, which is why I wanted to include my two thoughts above. Overall, I think Sonic Frontiers breathes life into what seemed like a dying franchise. I'm hoping that the next Sonic title(s) might take the work they have in Frontiers, improve upon it and take out some of the stuff that didn't work out this time around. I don't think this is the game that saves Sonic, but I would say this is a "Good" Sonic game.8/10(18.6 hours on a single playthrough, Near 100% total completion on the Hard/Speedster difficulty setting for playtime expectancy)((It did not seem like the game had much to offer in terms of replay-ability or additional challenges after completing the game))

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I do recommend this game, but much like how Cyber Space levels put an asterisk on your time if you use the Homing Dash, my recommendation comes with an asterisk as well.The primary gameplay loop is a surprising breath of fresh air. Aside from a forced tutorial section, you're mostly free to explore and progress as you see fit. Don't want to do all the Cyber Space levels (not that I'd blame you for that)? No problem, there are plenty of ways to get the collectibles you need. Don't want to repeatedly fight more progressively time-consuming Guardians? Pay a visit to Big's Fishing Spots or randomly find more Portal Gears while exploring. Don't want to hoover up all the Memory Tokens that litter each map? You get more than enough from exploring the islands, and mercifully there isn't even an achievement attached (though I still did that simply because I could).So what did I like about this game, you may be asking? Well, boosting and jumping around large open zones, for starters. Especially after tuning Sonic's speed and maneuverability to my liking, I found it such a joy to run around that even after unlocking fast travel options I'd mostly just stick to running around to my heart's content because it's simply more fun to do so.While most Sonic games tend to not have worthwhile narratives, Frontiers manages to actually have a somewhat compelling narrative centered around a sparser cast of characters exploring the ruins of an ancient civilization. Sonic, Tails, Knuckles, Amy, Sage, even Dr. Eggman felt like believable characters with actual depth to them. Frontiers as a whole offers a more somber tone, while not being over the top edgy like certain past entries. Every story beat got me even more invested and wanting to see more.Circling back to gameplay for a moment, this game NAILED the boss fights, by which I mean the Titans that you face at the end of each island. The songs accompanying these fights were an audible treat for my ears, and the actual gameplay of them felt strangely reminiscent of Metal Gear Rising, of all games. If I had to say one negative thing about the Titans, it's that I wish there were more of them.Comparatively speaking, I wasn't entirely sold on fighting Guardians, essentially minibosses that you find scattered around each island. From the second island onward, most of them were just timesinks that took far longer to even get a chance to hit than they had any right to. It got to the point where after fighting them once for the achievement for fighting all of them, I would go out of my way to avoid them because I had other things to do.Sonic Frontiers offers a very solid foundation for future entries to build upon. What worries me most is the very real possibility that Sonic Team will fall back into bad habits again. But considering how much I enjoyed this game, I'd prefer to be cautiously optimistic. The future is bright for the Sonic franchise. One can only hope that Sonic Team has truly learned from their past mistakes this time around.

_childDocuments_.review: I've 100% the game. Better than all others in the modern times by far. Super Sonic and the combat system really sets this game apart from the rest in the series. Although, it was short and very easy to trivialize; by spinning in a circle, you can get rings, exp, memory tokens, and even power/defense seeds. this made it so that exploring was kinda an option; a less efficient option. If the game made you explore and fight bosses, it would be forcing you to have more fun, rather than spinning in a circle using cyloop. You don't have to go into cyberspace at all, or fight any boss; if you fish, you get emerald keys. It's a really good game and I recommend it a lot, but if cyloop and fishing weren't broken, it would have made players have fun fighting mini bosses, and exploring the vast island before blasting through it with super sonic. Another thing I wanted more with this game was super sonic; I wanted to fly across the land with super sonic, to be able to freely move and fight guardians with super sonic's unrivaled might, or even travel to other islands without having open the map would have been a blast! However, the 'open world' aspect of the game is limited due to the linear story progression and separate maps. That is to say, I will definitely be replaying the wyvern fight and listening to the ost when it is fully released. And here's hoping for some lore explanations and maybe hyper sonic because they hinted at the master emerald like twice

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving the game thumbs up but with reservations. It's a considerably flawed game. After the abysmal Forces I had no expectations at all for Frontiers so at least the game exceeded my expectations. I'm not done with it yet, I just finished Chaos Island which was way too long. Of course it's not a bad thing that the game is long, but in Frontiers things tend to get very redundant, especially after the first island which is my favorite because it's not too big and it's well designed. The next two islands are VERY large and sometimes I was just wondering how to get to the next objective which is far away and you have to go through absurdly long and repetitive platforming sections to get there. It's frustrating to get way up in the sky to talk to Tails only to find out that you don't have enough tokens so you have to get back down. There's WAY too many of these tokens to collect.Another major flaw of Frontiers is the simulator levels (I think we can all agree on that) which are all badly designed and have lousy music, and to make things worse the physics are altered in those levels and Sonic's movement is slow and sluggish. I'm glad these levels are short. Last flaw I want to point out are all the mini games and quests. There's too many of those and many of them are frustrating  and completely pointless (like the pinball game). I hope SEGA removes those completely in the next Sonic game and no one will miss them. Now for the fighting part, I have to say I was pleasantly surprised with many of the bosses, and especially how they look. But it's still too much button mashing and again it gets redundant, and the final bosses (which are huge) take too many hits before being defeated. But for the most part I'd say the boss fights are okay. That leaves us with a very long and very flawed game that I don't think I'll ever play again after I finish it. I'd say roughly 40% of the game content is unnecessary and has no place there at all.

_childDocuments_.review: I was gifted this game (I think I need to check the received for free for that), and I'll start with the short version.This is a pretty okay game, maybe even good. It has ups and downs. As a whole I had fun with it! I did 100% it in the end.Of all the sonic games I've played, I think this is the one I've enjoyed the most. It is my sincere desire that they continue to try to polish the sonic franchise in this direction.Now for a bunch of rambling.The gameplay loop was fairly satisfying. Run around exploring a zone to get used to it, and in doing so find a bunch of trinkets and bits. Use those to progress the story and level your character up, and also occasionally take the time to fish (I am very biased towards fishing minigames, even when they're on the simple side like this one), use fishing points for more lore/level up tokens, and repeat on each new area.That said, this game is not without its faults, and boy does it have them. The camera in several areas is really, really annoying. This is compounded when you get shoehorned into a 2D section while exploring a 3D environment. I can not stress how extremely awful this felt 9/10 times it happened. The 3rd island is *especially* bad about this, and often when you get shoehorned into one you cannot simply choose to leave it or not do it, as the beginning is often a boost forward.Speaking of the third world, that brings up another major negative for me in this game. A lot of the world design is. Very bad to be honest. While the constant floating grinding rails and other typical sonic things are annoying, at least at first they're all fun. Once it starts hiding 2D sections behind every other fun thing (the 3rd island was ESPECIALLY bad about this), I found myself avoiding all the fun sonic stuff to avoid potentially getting sucked into another forceful 2D section. I can not stress how annoying these sections are when exploring.THAT SAID, the 2D sections are perfectly fine when it's stuff like. Moving upwards/climbing towers and so forth, because one thing a 3D environment is typically pretty bad at is upward platforming. So then it works pretty well! That said, I *really* wish they did something like, say, mario 64, where sonic's shadow is always directly below him. It's very easy to misunderstand sonic's relation to the world, especially when the 3D camera angles are poor, and completely whiff a platform.Another thing I don't see a lot of people mention is the sound design for this game is, extremely good? All the sounds feel, grounded and well thought out. I don't know exactly how to explain this? With one exception, being the coin get/spending noise in fishing. On it's own it's fine, but the problem is you *almost never* hear the sound once. Especially if you're buying things in rapid succession or catch a fish worth quite a bit? Prepare to have your ears blown out with a sound they clearly only listened to/tested as a single noise.So yeah, this game is full of faults, and honestly the negatives stick out harder in my mind than the positives do! But despite that I just. Had fun with it? The music was good (except the random dubstep song, lmao what the heck was that), the gameplay loop was satisfying, getting 100% as I went was fun. Running around in open fields instead of your typical cramped feeling stages feels a lot better to me? In most sonic games you couldn't ever really go fast for all that long, and having room to just mindlessly run was fun.At the end of the day, I do recommend this game and I really hope sonic team considers continuing to polish the series in this direction. That said, I'd probably still wait for a sale for this one.

_childDocuments_.review: Just 100% Completed Sonic Frontiers, And It's A Very Good Sonic Game. This Game Completely Wipes The Floor On Sonic Forces Which, Personally, I REALLY Didn't Like. The Pros: The Game Runs Well, Soundtrack's GOATED, Sage Is ALSO GOATED, The Combat Is Fun, Enemy Designs Are Awesome, The Story Is One Of The Best In The Series And Even Makes References To Past Games Like Sonic Unleashed For Sonic Fans Who Like Sonic Lore, Voice Acting Is Great And Characters Are Expressive, And The Graphics Look Nice, The Exploration Of The Islands Is Fun, And The Sonic Controls The Best He's Probably Ever Has. Now, The Cons: Combat Is Quite Janky But It's Not A "Bad" Kinda Janky, The Combat Also Gets Repetitive Quite Fast Because Sonic Also Doesn't Have A Broad Moveset Either Which  (I Already Had Like 1/2 Of The Moveset Unlocked On The First Island), The Cyber Space Levels (For The Most Part) REUSE Old Level Designs From PAST Games Which I Find Very Lazy But Could Probably Be Fixed In Sonic Team's Next Game Or In Future DLC They've Planned, In Cyber Space Sonic Controls Worse Than He Does On The Islands For Some Reason Which Made It A Tad Bit Harder To Control And Platform, The Puzzles Are Not Hard To Only A Select Few MAYBE, Game Was Quite Easy Aswell I Was Playing On The Hardest Difficulty... Which Would Be "Hard" Mode, Pop-In Is Bad Not Even Like A Fade-In Pop-in Effect Which Gets Distracting, And The Enemy Types/Variety Get Reused With Just Different Colors And Names. Now Probably The Maybe's/Nitpicks: No TRUE Momentum The Game Has A "Speedometer" But It's Use Isn't Really Put Into Full Effect Which Means Sonic Doesn't Lose Or Gain Speed That Much (It's SO Slight And VERY Insignificant) Going Up Hill Or Down Hill, I Think Sonic's Animations In Gameplay Are Very Stiff And Janky-Looking Compared To Previous Games Like Sonic Generations/Unleashed Which Had WAY Better Animations (This Game Uses Sonic's "Sonic Forces" Model, So They Just Ripped That With The Animations To.) Well, That Should Be It For This Review, ENJOY THE GAME!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Sonic Frontiers

_childDocuments_.review: IF YOU ARE A SONIC FAN, YOU WILL ENJOY THIS GAME!! I have played for 5 hours and only just now beat the first island, skipping only a few items and collecting just about everything else, and here are my first impressionsGraphics: Absolutely Beautifulpros: -Beautiful models-Scenic levels and island-Day/Night cycle (with occasional weather cycle too)cons:-Occasional clip ins (Nothing too jarring, just an occasional rock)Gameplay: Incredibly fun and with lots of room for skill buildingpros:- A handful of skills allowing for mixing in combos- The dodge mechanic makes speedy in/out fights really fun and in Sonic's style- Boss fights feel a lot more engaging cons:- Occasionally a bit stiff- Super fast gameplay is sometimes hard to keep up with (good or bad is opinion based, I think its cool)Story: So far, really frickin interesting. It not only includes the new big villain, but brings back the personalities and genuine character growth of the characters we missed from old games. The writers for this game did well staying true to the material.Overall, the game isn't perfect, but man it is INCREDIBLY REFRESHING, as it feels the innovation and speed of Sonic is back, and that this franchise is on its way to achieve big things, with this being its starting piece. Again, the game does have a few little nitpicks, but nothing game changing, and overall is super enjoyable. Fans of the series will be happy to see something nice after the long wait.Oh, and you can level up your speed, and there's a mechanic where at max rings your boost is essentially mach speed and makes island travel as Sonic a blast. You're welcome.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's a 6/10 being lifted up by some amazing music and let down by... quite honestly everything else.They decided to take an open world approach with Frontiers as opposed to just a bog-standard level select progression. The good side of this is you get to experience Sonic not bound by normal level conventions. The downside is it's an open world, and they squeeze everything out of the open world as much as they possibly can.The story's serviceable, if you're gonna buy the game, buy it for the spectacle of them (even if some are annoying as hell), and play the game on Hard mode if you want to experience all the boss-fights, because I don't believe the game tells you this, but if you play on normal, like I did, the game just skips the literal final boss of the game, a boss that monologues that I would've very much liked to hear, and then congratulates you for beating the big bad of the game....WITHOUT... GIVING YOU AN OPTION... TO REPLAY BOSSFIGHTS (officially)...I was actually willing to give this game a positive rating, but I legit thought the game just bugged me through the final boss, it was so abrupt, and learning that the fight it starts hyping up is only available on Hard mode without telling me is, quite honestly, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the story and the lore. The graphics were amazing to look at as well. I definitely give Sega credit for originality. The open zone format is a lot of fun to explore. Sonic gets a lot of cool upgrades as well. It's like he evolves in the game, and that's an interesting aesthetic for him. I hope they implement that idea in future games.The one thing I'd want them to improve on is gameplay.It would have been nice if Knuckles, Tails and Amy had been playable from the beginning, similar to how they were back in the Adventure era. But it is nice that they get to be playable in "Another story."But it's refreshing to see some backstory behind the Chaos Emeralds. Over all it's a lot of fun and addicting.As always, probably one of the best parts of the game is the music. The rockin' tunes definitely set the tone for the epic boss fights.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, all you need to know is that this is the first truly good 3d Sonic game in a very, very long time. It is worth it if you are a long time fan, by far. The writing is good, the game-play is good, and Sonic Team has outright said that they plan on vastly improving the template they've made. With new playable characters on the way as well, this is shaping up to be the start of a new golden age of Sonic games.(WARNING)The free update DLC is a bit odd. It feels very frustrating, and the other characters are not very good to play. They cannot combo well at all, so fighting bosses and enemies become incredibly frustrating, feeling more like a war of attrition. I feel I may be able to get them to work after I play a little longer, however. Since the free content update is optional, I wouldn't factor it into making a decision on whether or not you buy Frontiers. The base game is still really good.

_childDocuments_.review: Upon getting this game, I was enamoured by how good it felt at the time. I loved it for the same reasons anybody else did. Easy to understand gameplay which felt like it did a better job at exhibiting how platforming can change completely when the character can run super fast and jump really high. A more seriously toned story and villains/antagonists that actually feel somewhat threatening. Although I understand doing open zone puzzles can feel repetitive to some, it was fun enough for me at the time. Back in 2022, I had to reset my PC. Upon getting everything reinstalled and booting up SF, everything was wiped down to my settings. Fast forward to now and this actually happens any time that I use another PC to run the game, no matter what Steam Cloud settings I have on. I've looked online for almost a week to find if even a single user has had the same thing happen upon reinstalling, but either no one has reinstalled the game since it came out or I'm the only one who has this problem.I figured out this glitch way too late; too many hours to refund now. In the future I'm gonna have to choose between keeping a really old PC for this one game or reducing Sonic Frontiers to a $70 unused game slot in my Steam Library.Even without this very devastating bug that may be a possibility for anyone, I feel that this game doesn't have enough going for it to say it's a good purchase. To get a bit nit-picky:- Story honestly feels weird. (I haven't been able to beat the game yet, I didn't understand the fact that the game wipes it's save anytime I reinstall so I've lost my progress about 4 times now. It got spoiled to me by now, but obviously I'm going to hear about it the game's been out for 2 years) It always feels like the Sonic franchise gets hit by the Cosmic Reset Button from the comics anytime a new game comes out and there's new/old characters just slapped in that I'm supposed to care about.           - The references that sonic makes in his monologues (callbacks to old titles i.e. comparing Ares island              to Shamar, talking about Zavok, etc) are fun, but I would like to actually see something from earlier              stories show itself in some subsequent game for once.- Music is too mellow and calm. Things only get hype in boss battles, and the only hype music available in Open Zone are said boss battle tracks. Honestly same goes for Cyberspace tracks imo. Feels like cheap EDM versions of Generations remixes.And may God himself be with anyone who plays this game vanilla. I have a mod for just about any facet of the game and then some. Only then does the game not feel like a tedious nightmare chalk full of glitches and severely nerfed platforming where you have to do things exactly how the game intends without any room for nuance.I have ~300 hours on this game, either steam or SF is so bugged that it can't even tell how long I've been playing .

_childDocuments_.review: MAJOR Spoilers below!!! You have been warnedTerrible formatting alert!Overall, Sonic Frontiers is a great game, sonic feels smooth and there were no problems during any of my time playing the game. The main gameplay loop consists of beating challenges to unlock the map, collecting keys (which unlock vaults that have the chaos emeralds in them) from cyberspace stages that you need gears to unlock (which are obtained by beating special mini-bosses) and memory fragments around the island. The amount of these that you need is low enough that its not pace breaking, and even if you need more the game gives you a good way to farm them VIA Big's fishing minigame.Theres lots of content in the game with the 5 islands taking you 14-20 hours to beat depending on if you like taking your time or just blasting through as fast as you can. Regardless of how fast you are, the game will take you some time to beatIn addition to the 5 islands there are 50-ish cyberspace stages. These are your more traditional stages, and there are even some call backs to older sonic games such as rail canyon or radical highway from SA2. Theyre all short never taking you more than 3 minutes to complete one.Next, theres the aformentioned fishing minigame, here you can get things that you need by using trade tokens obtained by catching fish, you can get memory tokens, keys or level gears. Overall its executed very well and offers a quick way to progress the story if the player is bored of searching for memory fragments one at a time (or if the player wants an absolutely MONSTEROUS catch)Lastly, the game offers an expansive combat system. You get skill points to unlock 10-ish special skills that you can use during combat. The only problem with this is that you'll only be using your skills against mini-bosses and bosses. Every other enemy dies to 1-2 homing attacks. In addition to the 10 skills you also have the ability to parry, this will open up spots to attack bosses/mini-bosses and deflects projectiles. My biggest gripe with this is that you can endlessly hold down the parry button to parry indefinitely so that you dont actually have to time your parries. Which makes no sense since its more of a guard than a parry.The story of the game is... alright. Its nothing special by any means but you shouldnt be expecting an amazing story from a sonic game.The soundtrack is your average 11/10 soundtrack since sonic games just dont miss on that department.The enemy variety is quite nice and the mini-bosses take a bit but are fun to do (but unfortunately can be skipped entirely thanks to fishing)But HOLY HELL the main boss fights are SUPER ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ BADASS. The first 3 (Ill touch on the final 2 in my complaints) are super cool and require you to pull off some crazy stunts as super sonic even if all youre doing is mashing your mouse to attack. Every one of them is loaded with an amazing song to go with to make you feel like you're the strongest man out there and you're about to rough their ♥♥♥♥ up!Although heres where my complaints start.During the final 2 islands everything youve done over the course of the game gets thrown out the window for no good reason, like at ALL.The 4th island (i forgot its name) has you climbing 6 towers instead of getting 6 emeralds, this would be cool but theres 0 memory tokens, 0 cyberspace stages and 0 mapping challenges. But the biggest sin is that theres barely any enemies and no boss at the end. This island just feels like filler that SEGA added so that they could do a lore dump on you without killing the pace, and they failed at doing that.The final island, unlike the 4th is more normal, although you need lots of keys from cyber space and a metric ♥♥♥♥ ton of memory fragments. Like im talking 25+ keys and 200-ish memory fragments, its genuinely insane and if you dont fish for fragments and gears like i did, have fun beating the mini-bosses and grinding for them so that you can progress 2 inches forward (ironic in a sonic game).And what do you get after you finally get all the emeralds? A JOKE OF A BOSS FIGHT. Despite the name "Supreme" hes absurdly squishy and can be beaten by mindless button mashing unlike the other bosses which taught you how to actually use the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ parry system.Well you may be thinking that Supreme is just one bad boss fight but unfortunately hes the 4th boss of the game. The final boss "The End" is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bullet hell. Like straight up Touhou except its Sonic the Hedgehog, there is no Finalhazard, Neo Metal, hell even sonic 06 got the final boss formula down. It makes ZERO sense as to why the final boss is a bullet hell and even the actual fight is kinda meh. Its a really good way to ruin an otherwise amazing game.Also this last point might be a personal one, but Sage is totally just Shadow if he was a 10 year old girl lets not lie to ourselves.Overall Id rate the first half of Sonic Frontiers 10/10 but the second half just ruins it so badly its a 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: After playing 24 hours and having played since day 1 till completion(Only one achievement left, the 50 times max combo one), I can safely say this is a pretty good Sonic game. That's it, it is a good game.I got a bit angry right aroud the end though... May contain spoilers later.I never imagined how the combat would feel on a Sonic game, but gotta say I'm not disappointed. It's not the best and feels quite janky, but it's a nice addition and it works as expected. Also the final fight of each island makes you feel badass. The speed part it's where I'm having most trouble though. You'd think that having Sonic in an open world would have to feel like pure freedom. Well it's not. I get that you have to put some limits for the sake of gameplay, but thanks to that come some troubles; Sometimes Sonic bumps into a mountain wall and stop inmediatly because it's a boundary, and trying to jump over it won't avail othing since it will reduce your jump height whenever you go fast when close to a mountain... or a cliff. You don't know how many times I died to a fall because of Sonic deciding to jump 2 cm in the air. Again, only happens around elevations and pits.The Portal levels are good and do feel like Sonic, though sometimes you'll feel like you're slow as hell.Still, you'll learn to dominate those flaws and whenever you get around lvl40 speed you'll start to get places crazy fast.Now, plot-wise... IT'S THE BEST SONIC HAS GOT IN YEARS they bring up themes and plot points from other games and give sense to those, and the characters get so much personality... If only Eggman and Sage would get a bit more time on camera to develop...Sonic Frontiers is a fun game and I totally recommend you as a Sonic fan, since I think there's a lot of steps forward... But be wary of some let-downs.Allright allright, PLOT AND ENDGAME SPOILERS AHEAD:They give meaning to the Chaos Emeralds and the Ancestors and stuff... And then drop it COMPLETELY at the end for some reason. They give you all that story and plot for nothing. And then there's the final fight...The last fight of the game... Are you serious? I'm so mad. It's literally 3 quick time events- fade to cutscene- roll credits.How can you butcher a good tale like that?! It's nowhere near as spectacular as it should. And I mean it since the other 3 bosses felt quite good to fight against. Especially Giganto with it's badass theme. Such a hype moment.I swear if it did the ending right it'd be a 9/10 or close.Again, good game, if you can't decide whether or not to play it, I'd tell you to try it, you may be surprised.I give this game a final score of "Sonic amogus drawing simulator/10" (now seriously, solid  7.5/10)

_childDocuments_.review: Oh how I wish Steam would let me rate a game beyond "yes game good" or "no game bad".I do think Frontiers is a good game... but it needed so much more work. Towards the end you can just feel how Sonic Team was forced to wrap development up. It's unpolished, full of half done ideas, and when it was over it felt lacking like there was so much more game that was supposed to be here.However. This game gets two REALLY important things right:1) It feels so good to play as Sonic. Running around the islands, which is the main portion of the gameplay, is an absolute blast. I never got bored of grinding rails, timing jumps just right to hit springs, and zipping through the landscape.2) The writing. Praise be to Ian Flynn! The dialogue in this game is S tier, this is characterization done right. There's actual story and lore! The big "villain" was a bit underwhelming but everything else was a joy.This game has passion. The people behind it clearly cared about what they were making and wanted to do more but weren't given the time. The foundation for an amazing 3D Sonic game is here. Just... please SEGA... Listen to the fans, listen to the developers. Don't throw this away.Also, give us the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ chao garden back.

They go through a journey and face challenges, while expanding on the Sonic Lore.The game has a lot of content and it`s just a blast

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a pretty alright time but it seriously lacks alot of polish and feels super clunky in a ton of areas.  Overall I think it serves it's purpose of healing the hearts of people who like sonic but I still can't look past the games pretty large problems, atleast for me.The draw distance in this game is terrible and it has pop in like no tomorrow, something that is downright impossible to ignore due to the amount of grind rails , springs and other stuff that just APPEARS a few feet infront of you.Cyberspace can be fun if you get a grip on how sonic controls but theres no denying it's clunkier then something like generations where sonic controlled extremely smoothly which is strange since I think this is the part that'd be the best since they've done it right already. _childDocuments_.review: Just what the series needed.The gameplay is a huge improvement from Forces but could be something truly great in a future title with a good base structure around momentum-based platforming. The open worlds are really good as they are with the weakest of them being chaos island, which I believe with momentum-based physics would have made it one of the most fun to play through as you could use the terrain to cross the gaps and have a satisfying way to traverse the map.Cyberspace leaves me in a weird spot as I don't hate it but I also don't love it. The controls being different to the open world isn't the best and with most of them reusing level layouts from previous games doesn't fully help that as well as having the level themes be from green hill, sky sanctuary, and chemical plant. These for me make the stages lack an iconic feel like you could with previous stages in the series. The city design is nice because it acts as an amalgamation of all the previous city levels mashed into one, This type of design could have made having older themes done with a unique twist making them more refreshing to see. some examples of this could be: Green hill mixed with seaside hill and emerald hill zone. chemical plant mixed with Eggman land and metropolis zone. sky sanctuary mixed with Babylon garden and sky road.The story being pinned by Ian Flynn leads to the characters being characterized as they should be since (for sonic at least) Sonic and the Black Knight, which was in 2009. The extra depth to weave elements from different games through the dialog was nice to see with references to games like S3&K SA1, SA2, Heroes, Shadow the hedgehog, Unleashed, Colours, Lost World, Forces, sonic riders team sonic racing, even one line to reference the idw comics which is nice to see.Overall, the game is not perfect but it does show a lot of promise for the future and on its own was a really fun time to play all the way through despite some jank that occurred throughout the game and the pop-in issues.Just like with Generations, I'm excited to see what the community does with mods and custom stages to fully test the capabilities of the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has everything us Sonic fans have been waiting for quite some time now. Ever since the newgrounds and the era where Sonic flash animations/games were dominant, sonic fans have somewhat envisioned JRock being incorporated into a sonic game, take for example Sonic Advance Z which already had ONE OK ROCK in its animations, and even back then fans roared for something like that in an actual sonic game. Even far beyond that, back in 2017 when fans wanted the franchise to return back to a serious tone for the story, you can see that SEGA somewhat tried to do that with infinite, and his theme, but it was overshadowed by the terrible writing that whatever serious story they were trying to tell, was drowned out by mediocrity. Though with SEGA also featuring artists such Sleeping with Sirens, it shows how serious they were it came to this game, you wanted serious and edgy, well you sure as heck got it. Same goes for having NateWantsToBattle in the soundtrack, SEGA is nailing the mark on so many things that fans have wanted over the years, and not only at one point having fans make a great game for them, but they're also now allowing the fans to make music for the games (obviously besides Tee Lopes) For the game the first of its kind when ti comes to Sonic, it does it really well, yes of course it could be quite a bit better, but for Sonic's first outing in this type of game, they built a really solid foundation for anything  to come after. They have the base for a great gameplay style, and also including boost formula stages in the game shows that they're still willing to cater to the old fans, even though the cyberspace stages could be better (nowhere near the level of generations good) theyre still really fun to play when you consider them as special stages, obviously they need to tweak the physics, and still make the levels a little bit longer, but overall, they're good for what they are, since they are not the main focus of this game. The Open Zone in the game is amazing, sure it does get repetitive, but that's only if you do all the side challenges as intended, the momentum you get in the game jumping off rails, and boosting off edges changes how you approach the game entirely, you can boost from one rail section to an entirely different one, not even related to the previous one that you were doing, and it seems as if it almost fits, to me that was the best part of the open zone. The environments, the sound design, ost, graphics, story, and even the animations when it comes to the camera angles that the game likes to pull off to seem more cinematic is all breathtaking. I would sincerely give this game a try, come into it blind, don't try to rush through it, experience it, you'll definitely like what's here.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want my quick overall thoughts, skip to the last paragraph.Growing up, Sonic was right up there with Pokémon as one of my favorite game series. The Genesis games, Adventure and Adventure 2, Heroes, Shadow, '06– you name it, I played it. As time went on, the series' quality wavered, and many people wondered if Sonic Team had it in them to deliver a great 3D Sonic game again, especially after Forces. Sonic Frontiers is proof that they absolutely do.The open world gameplay takes an approach that reminds me of Mirror Edge: Catalyst, in that it's one big platforming playground. Exploring the world is fun, because the simple act of playing the game - jumping from platform to platform, rail to rail, shooting high in the air from springs, boosting, etc. - is fun, and each of the environments have these Sonic-y segments sprinkled all over them, making them engaging to zip through. You're incentivized with items that grant stat upgrades (speed, attack, etc.), while you will also need to collect certain items to unlock new conversations with characters (which you will want to do— more on that in a bit), and I feel that between the two, you're given plenty of reason to explore— but again, it really helps that the gameplay is just so darn fun.If you want a more traditional Sonic experience though, you'll get that here too. The game has thirty different "cyberspace" stages that you unlock over the course of the game, and each one plays like a traditional 3D Sonic level. In fact, most (if not all) of them are taken from other Sonic games, albeit with different visuals. You've got the usual suspects - Green Hill, Chemical Plant, Sky Sanctuary, and so on - but there are also some fairly deep cuts here that, once I realized what level I was playing, made me smile like an idiot. My only major complaint with them is that despite each level coming from a different past stage, most of them are themed after the three zones I just mentioned, so you won't see much variety from a visual standpoint. That said, the most important thing is that these are fun to play, which they are: each stage lasts around 2-3 minutes on average, never outstaying its welcome, and going back to replay them and complete missions or just whittle your time down is a lot of fun. And just like the open zone, you're incentivized to perfect these stages— completing missions nets you extra keys to unlock Chaos Emeralds for the story.The soundtrack, as expected, is fantastic. Tomoya Ohtani's team have delivered another great soundtrack with a decent but of variety in it— while many of the open zone themes are subdued and reminiscent of games like Breath of the Wild with how piano-driven they are, the cyberspace stages are often full-on techno and trance, while the game's boss battles consist of the sort of vocal-led rock themes that feel straight out of Sonic Adventure 2 or Sonic '06. All throughout, the music stays catchy and enjoyable to listen to, and the rock tracks in particular really help elevate the boss encounters and get you pumped.Narratively, this is Sonic at its best since the Dreamcast days. While the overarching story may not be anything unique, there are some very big lore revelations here that longtime fans will appreciate, as well as a lot of calbacks to previous games (even somewhat obscure ones) that feel meaningful rather than simply being nostalgia bait. But the thing that truly makes the story great, for me, is the characterization.In most modern Sonic games, Sonic and friends have largely been written as if they were Saturday morning cartoon characters: all jokes, little depth, etc., but Frontiers changes that and reminds me of how they used to be written before Colors and Generations. Characters still made jokes and quips - it wouldn't be a Sonic game without them - but they also show moments of doubt, playful teasing with one another and getting under each other's skin, regret over things they did in previous stories, and genuine character development. And in all of this, each character still feels like themselves— Sonic is still your arrogant-with-a-heart-of-gold protagonist, Tails is the younger brother trying to find his own way out of Sonic's shadow, Knuckles is still the hot-headed rival, and so on. This game has Sonic's crew written the best they have been in a very long time, largely thanks to Sonic comic writer Ian Flynn's involvement, and it's a large part of why I enjoyed this game so much.Overall, this is hands-down my favorite Sonic game since the Dreamcast era, and more than that, I think it may end up being my favorite one *period* after I think on it some more— maybe it won't be, but the fact that I'm even considering it should tell you how much I loved this game. As a longtime Sonic fan, this game is almost exactly what I've wanted from the series for a long time, and it feels like a true return to form for a gaming icon that has often fallen by the wayside. If you like (or liked) Sonic and are debating getting this game… Just do it. I have a feeling you won't be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a rollercoaster of emotions for me. On one hand, it's a mess with its fair share of frustrations. But on the other hand, it's undeniably fun in its own chaotic way.The story starts with a bang as Dr. Eggman and Sonic's pals get sucked into a portal. As Sonic, your mission is to free your friends, help some smiley rock creatures called Kocos, and stop Dr. Eggman's evil plans. Simple, right?You'll navigate through open zones, not quite an open world like Breath of the Wild, but more like Mario Odyssey. These zones are vast and filled with fog of war that you gradually uncover as you explore. It's a collectathon, and there's a certain joy in gathering tokens and skill shards while zipping around on rails and listening to the excellent drum and bass tracks.But here's the catch: the game can be seriously directionless. The rails and platforming bits often send you flying in all sorts of directions, leaving you a bit disoriented. And when you need to reach specific places, it can be quite the challenge to get there without being flung off course.The Cyberspace levels provide a more traditional Sonic experience, and they're a mixed bag. They showcase the game's janky nature but are still a lot of fun, especially with their catchy music.Boss fights, however, are a necessary evil. They highlight the game's flaws, and Sonic's lack of precision becomes apparent when combat is mixed with fast platforming.Despite its quirks and repetition, Sonic Frontiers has potential. It's a fun foundation for a sequel that just needs some fine-tuning to reach its full superpower. So, if you're up for some scrappy fun and can handle a bit of frustration, Sonic Frontiers might just be the wild ride you're looking for.

I enjoyed the slightly more mature dialogue that what we've typically seen in past Sonic games, and it was refreshing to see the character development in old and new characters alike as this story progressed. Sage is such a charming character, and I hope to see her show up on a regular basis.The cyber space levels were exciting as I recognized the past games they pointed to, and while I would have liked to have some of the cyber space levels be longer than they were, they served their purpose as to break up the open zone format with the typical "sonic stage" feel. The fishing was an amazing addition, and I found myself spending more time there than I honestly expected to.I would love to see future Sonic games keep this style, but we'll see what they choose moving forward. This game is definitely worth picking up.

The game will render platforms, springs and over objects right in front of Sonic which makes it horrible to the point it impacts platforming.-World design is very generic, none of the environments aside from cyberspace have anything unique or interesting to look at aside from some of the boss encounters.-Game itself looks very dated in the open world. I actively avoided fighting any enemies unless I needed gears to unlock Cyberspace levels.- The upgrade system destroys any semblance of challenge even on hard mode. _childDocuments_.review: PEAK FICTIONEdit for real review (THIS WILL HAVE SPOILERS):Sonic Frontiers is a great game, it's now even my favorite Sonic game beating out Sonic Generations. With that said, the game does fall short in some areas and may or may not affect your enjoyment.Let's start with the pros:-Open World controls are GREAT, rarely did I feel like I couldn't do something or get somewhere because I was fighting with the controls.-Combat, while not as flashy as Devil May Cry, or as complicated as some other Hack-n-Slash games, does feel good to use and game DOES give you decent progression with getting new attacks.-Enemies are generally extremely fair to fight. I can't think of a single enemy type that felt like it had too much health or super obnoxious mechanics. Some enemies can be annoying but that mostly came down to me being dumb rather than the game itself.-Cyloop is a great and interesting addition to the gameplay with the different applications it has. From providing a knockup on some enemies to being used in puzzles to even letting you get infinite boost for a period of time. I sincerely hope this gets used in future games (assuming they do an open world/semi open world format again)-The vast majority of the boss fights are my favorites in the series, the combination of how the fights play out visually combined with the music of the fights made me giddy the entirety of the fights.-The story is pretty good, not 10/10 masterpiece writing but actually has the characters show CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT and not be dumb downed stereotypes that they have been for the past 10 years. Thank you Ian Flynn.-Visually, I think the game looks great. There is a caveat to this which will be in the cons but the game looks great.-MOST minigames (and I do mean MOST) are fine breaks from the general gameplay and don't overstay their welcome. There is also a caveat to this that will be in cons.Before the cons, I'm gonna do some indifferences I had with some things in the game.-Cyberspace levels are in general hit or miss in my opinion. Both in terms of gameplay or music. Some levels are very fun, and some of the songs are great as well but some levels are outright not fun to play for 1 reason or another and some of the songs aren't bad but feel more like background noise than anything else. The themes of the levels are also largely strange as there's really only 4 level themes (Those being Green Hill, Chemical Plant, Sky Sanctuary, and a more city and military theme similar to City Escape or Speed Highway but unique in its own right) and don't really do much for the game itself.-The game isn't hard even on the hardest difficulty, this doesn't really mean much at all in the grand scheme of things but do keep it in mind-Some later enemies in the game are largely just reskins of previous enemies, but most if not all have more attacks so they don't just feel like "the same enemy but he's red now and thus has more health"Now for the cons:-The first one you come across will be the Cyberspace controls. I praised the open world controls and feel bu Cyberspace feels off. I got used to it as time went on but Sonic just didn't feel exactly right. I get why it works different since open world gives you too much freedom in movement for confined levels and would work against you as well but it feels TOO stiff.-The pop in. While this does not bother me largely at all, this WILL be a point of fault for many people. Many set pieces will just appear in the open world with no fade in whatsoever. As far as I could tell this only happened with the Sonicy level pieces and not enemies or the grass.-The last island. Now don't get me wrong, the gameplay and everything is the same so it's not inherently the island itself but a combination of things. This will be HEAVY SPOILERS:The final island wants you to do the same beats as the first 3, but the issue comes in with collecting the Sage hearts. For whatever reason you either need to collect EVERY heart on the island or at the very least the VAST majority to actually finish all the dialogue to progress to the final boss. This is where Big's fishing minigame came in, and why I haven't talked about it until now as it's both a pro and con. With the finishing, it allows you to purchase things like keys, gears, and that island's NPC token (hearts, medals, or wrenches) along with Lost Kocos and Attack/Defense seeds. You could very likely skip most of the open world grind by doing JUST the fishing, which is what I did for the final island with the hearts.-The TRUE final boss. Hope you like the hacking bullet hell minigame. This is skippable by playing on Normal but is easily the worst final boss solely because it's not Sonic at all and this gameplay style only comes up in the later half of the game, and only about 3 times.With all that said, I still firmly believe this is a solid 8.5/10, 9/10 if you don't count the optional true final boss.
