_childDocuments_.review: There is a lot to like about Sonic’s latest 3D adventure and also a lot of frustrating issues that hold it back from being great. It’s miles better than the previous three 3D Sonic games (Forces, Boom, and Lost World) but the game is so close to being in that elite tier of Sonic games it almost left me disappointed. 	Sonic Frontiers is the closest thing to what most people would consider Open World and while I initially thought that was going to be a terrible idea for the most part I think it works great and is a refreshing change to the traditional Sonic formula. The longer I got in the game the more I realized the best part was just running around and doing to mini platform puzzles and collecting the “Memories of Tails, Amy, Knuckles, and Sage” (Yes I know that sounds weird but that’s what the game calls them). You get in a really fun game play loop and mixed with the pretty good music played in the 5 islands (the open world is split in between 5 islands) it’s a rather relaxing experience too. That’s to say there isn’t faults in this open world though. I lot of odd invisible walls, poor clipping on the rock sides of the island, terrible pop in that would have a N64 jealous, and overall generic environments hold it back. The game also features challenges that you have to complete to unlock parts of the map and for the most part these are incredibly easy and have very little substance. Throughout the map you’ll find giant bosses that can provide a fun challenge and really show off the new “combat” system. Unfortunately it involves a lot of button mashing but you do get abilities that are noticeably better. Beating these bosses unlocks “Portal Gears” that can be used to unlock traditional Zone Levels. This is in my opinion the worst part of the game. Nearly all of these levels are just former zones (Green Hill, Chemical Plant, Etc) with a ugly Cyber Space theme and bad music. The 4 “Missions” are incredibly easy to get and in some cases I cleared all 4 on my first run through of the level on “Hard mode”. Also something about the physics in these zones feels off and makes it even less fun. Anyways clearing these unlocks Vault Keys which allow you to get Chaos Emeralds. When you get all 5 you can fight one of 4 Titans as Super Sonic. These fights are incredibly button mashy but the music is great even though it doesn’t fit the tone of the game very well. It’s definitely more spectacle than gameplay. Repeat that 4 times (1 of the island is just climbing massive towers 7 times) and then you get to the final boss which I wont spoil but it’s one of the worst in Sonic history. 	The voice acting and story is actually pretty good. The story takes itself serious for the most part and covers some dark topics for a Sonic game and for the most part pulls it off. Eggmans new AI named Sage can be pretty annoying and generic though. Learning the values of friendship which is a trope modern Sonic games have done for over a decade now. There is a hilarious “emotional” scene featuring Sage’s friendship/family revelation where cutscenes are replayed with a tint filter and Sage humming a terribly out of tune song (some of the cutscenes happened 10 minutes prior and are not emotional at all). The voice acting is solid but I still am not a fan of Roger Craig Smiths Sonic voice. However the writing isn’t really as cringy as it has been in part games so that helps a ton.	The music is very hit or miss. The over world music is solid and fits the tone well. The Titan music is great despite not fitting the games tone well. The music in these Titan Boss fights just goes so hard it's awesome and they're genuinely good songs. The Zone music almost all sucks and would rather never hear it again. The credits music was also very good (Shoutout to NateWantsToBattle). So it’s a mixed bad soundtrack that is held back by the Zone music.	Lastly graphically this game is just ok. At times it looks really good but the rain effect is bad and certain textures like grass and rocks look straight up terrible. The pop in is also straight up terrible and can even pop in when Sonic is 2 feet away from it which just doesn’t look good.	Overall I enjoyed Sonic Frontiers and am optimistic about the groundwork is layed down. A lot of the issues it has are very fixable too (Pop In being the biggest) and really make me excited for another game that build off Frontiers foundation. Not nearly as good as Generations but miles better than Force and Boom. 14-15 hour campaign too making it the longest Sonic campaign is quite a while (maybe Unleashed) so you get a lot of content for your money (including Fishing with Big the Cat). Would recommend if you like Sonic game or 3D platformers. 7.7/10

Having to level speed and ring capacity one at a time kinda sucks, but it's not like it's a deal breaker. The music is amazing all the way through, the cyperspace levels are some of the best sonic stages there are, and the story fixes everything that was wrong with forces. _childDocuments_.review: Miraculous fresh start for the series. Moving around the open world feels natural, fun, and most importantly, fast. Combat nails the feel of being a league above all your enemies, but only in terms of speed, so the challenge comes in choosing when to attack with Sonic's new much more varied moveset. As always in Sonic the music  and animation is incredible, but for the first time in a long time the gameplay quality catches up. Bringing Ian Flynn on as the writer for a game is a godsend. The characters feel fleshed out and real, the story is more interesting than it's been since Unleashed at least, but possibly ever.Lastly, though perhaps most critically, everything functions and the game is polished. No 06 flashbacks here.Overall, 9/10, very few complaints. Sonic might be running in the right direction again.

_childDocuments_.review: This is easily the best Sonic game released in over a decade, hell it might even be a contender for best 3D Sonic game ever made. The story and characterization are easily some of the best they've ever done, the soundtrack is an amazing mix of the Adventure era rock songs with the Modern era's EDM with this game going way farther in both directions (heavy metal and straight rave music), and the gameplay is super fluid with you easily being able to go from speeding through the world, straight into combat, and doing puzzles.Unlike past "good" games, there's no massive flaw that detracts from an otherwise amazing experience (Adventure titles being early 3D so they don't hold up well today, Generations having a lackluster story, Unleashed's Warehog levels, etc.). It's just a solid experience all around, definitely not "best game ever"/"game of the year" quality but easily up there for a Sonic title so all the 7/10's this game is getting makes sense.The only complaints I got are fairly minor:1. The graphics settings for a PC port are kinda lacking. No Ultrawide monitor support and locked 60 FPS sucks (but that is to be expected from past Sonic titles and has already been modded in)  2. Cyberspace reusing the same 3 general level themes and older game layouts (it's "okay" since the rest of the game is so good and it's not the main focus of the game but definitely something they should improve on next game)3. They really need to patch the Elder to allow redeeming multiple at once, having to click through 1 by 1 all the way up to 99 is absurd.

_childDocuments_.review: Frontiers feels fast, dynamic and frankly fantastic to play, with great lines of springs, ramps, loops and obstacles, fun combat, occasionally challenging mini-bosses, epic boss fights and worlds that invite the player to explore them.The open zones have a "checklist map" nature to them, but the game is forgiving with its currencies and not only does not require the player to gather every single thing, but it also provides multiple sources for them, including a fishing minigame that features Big the Cat. As fun as they are to traverse in search for activities, the islands themselves lack personality and suffer from dull visuals, while also appearing a little empty and disjointed.The action stages, although rich in number, are rather short, but intense. Frankly, the difficulty for clearing their extra objectives is mostly easy, but the times for S ranks can be a bit inconsistent, with a few that are particularly difficult compared to the rest. They're much more interesting than the overworld in terms of visuals and style, but for some reason they only come in 4 themes based on stages from past titles that feel a little overdone by now.Like most modern videogames, Frontiers also features an RPG-like system that allows Sonic to gain new moves and improve his stats. The moveset can feel a bit unnecessarily bloated at one point, although fun to play around with, but improving the stats too much sort of messes up the game's balance.From a technical standpoint, the game lacks high-end graphical options and could benefit from higher draw distance, which can become a real issue when looking for the start of a line that leads to a token that is too far up. In traditional 3D Sonic fashion, the camera can prove a little difficult as well, locking both itself and Sonic into a specific position when certain platforming objects are interacted with.Every pro seems to have its con and yet, the overall experience was very positive to me. Despite its faults, Frontiers is a lot of fun to play and tells an enjoyable, light-hearted story that shows awareness of the events of past titles and expands the lore in a way that might pay off in the near future. In short, this may be one of the strongest titles in the franchise, even with the almost experimental feeling it evokes.On a personal note, I wish Sonic Team could focus on their successes and what makes Sonic, the gang and their universe truly great and unique without feeling like recurring to nostalgic stages is a must. Regardless, I have high expectations for what's to come and would like to congratulate the team on their hard work.

_childDocuments_.review: No amount of jank can take away from what this game accomplishes, both as a fun action platformer and as a Sonic game.The Open Zones are fun to explore throughout multiple playthroughs with tons of fun platforming sequences and level geometry to speed through. The combat is simple but fun and varied, and new puzzles and enemies are thrown at you on the regular to keep things fresh. Helping with this sense of exploration is the beautiful atmosphere and eclectic soundtrack, which I feel would alone make the game worth it if the gameplay wasn't already fantastic.I personally find the Cyberspace levels quite fun, and a massive improvement over Sonic Forces' levels because of how tightly Sonic controls in this game, on top of his new mobility options and generous homing attack range. The controls lack the same fluidity of Unleashed and Generations, but that's really all that's needed if this iteration of Sonic Team wants to continue working on traditional Sonic levels. It also helps that completing Cyberspace levels helps you progress through the Open Zones; it's like if in Sonic Adventure, doing better in levels would help you progress through the world map.I'm not as critical of Sonic's storytelling as other fans can be but there's no denying Ian Flynn's script really brings these beloved characters to life; many of the cutscenes are characters just talking about their feelings, which we haven't gotten in a while. The script is so good, I go out of my way to collect all the Tokens to see all the optional dialogue on an island, even if there's no in-game reward for doing so.I can't really say anything that hasn't been said already. A great new foundation for future Sonic games has been established here, but it's also a great game on its own. Please pick it up and show Sega and Sonic Team your support and constructive criticism.And don't be a jerk about it! This fandom needs to lighten up!

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I'll try to stay off the topic of mods, but let it be known, most of my play time is from modded Sonic Frontiers. Below I have some points of interest I'd like to speak of...First off, gotta get it off of my chest, most of the music is forgettable. Mainly the Cyberspace themes. 2010, anyone?Second off, Physics. They're alright. From my knowledge, Sonic Forces' controller was based off Lost World's and Frontiers' Controller based off of Forces. I'd suggest completely rewriting it. If you're gonna do open zone, it is inarguable that we need momentum. While most physics mods are GREAT, they don't flow with the game all too well because the game wasn't designed with it in mind. I think it's time for the boost to go and for us to let the spindash shine again. I'm aware the spindash was added in update 2, obtained from S ranking all the action chain challenges (for those of you claiming its difficult, it really isn't), but that's just a boost that does damage, is slightly faster, and has floaty physics.Third, open zone design. This is... lazy. I'll give ya slack, this was your first try. But next time, the platforming needs to be built in. And not just visually (but definitely do that), but game play wise. It's kinda weird to just have bits and pieces of a stage split apart across an entire island. I think the design needs to be baked into the terrain. Like, have islands have 4-5 major areas where important plot things happen, in unique and fun locations, and have entertaining terrain between them. Imagine spindashing down a slope, to be shot back up, and homing attacking a tree's branch to swing around and jump off like those poles. That'd be awesome! Also, please fix the model, you massacred my boi's spikes.Fourth of all, Combat. I haven't played Unleashed, but from what people say, this is a lot better than that. But it's a bit too flashy. Sure, it LOOKS like Sonic, but it doesn't FEEL like it. I think you shouldn't lock onto enemies, but have 7-8 free-flowing attacks you have to manually hit the enemy with. It might be cumbersome, but you can simply add an aim assist option. I think that would make Sonic FEEL a lot nicer. High skill ceiling and whatnot. Oh, and make the Parry able to be held forever, but you having to time when to release the parry, corresponding with when the enemy is about to hit Sonic. That feels a lot more balanced than the standard and perfect parry.Fifth, Story. All in all, pretty darn good. Just don't drop the ball at the end, and then replace it with a difficulty spike a year later, okay? I'm not a story writer so I couldn't tell you how to improve it. That being said, how will the next game go? Tails is going his own way, Amy is "sharing her love with the world" and yada yada yada... oh, and she name-dropped frigging STICKS.Paid 60 bucks for it, all in all a total win. I definitely recommend trying some modding. I've even dipped my fingers into some HMM. Anyways, its a great package. I'd recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing to think this game looked so bad when it was first shown.In what feels like a true return to form of the 3D Sonic franchise, Sonic Frontiers stands as a fresh new take in the Sonic universe. Sure, it borrows HEAVILY from Breath of the Wild, but it does so in an entertaining way. I thoroughly enjoyed this, and hope this means 3D Sonic will get many new exciting titles.The best parts were definitely the Cyber Space worlds, they had just the right amount of fast-paced, nostalgia-packed action, while staying short and sweet.Not without it's frustrations and some clunkiness here and there, but very enjoyable as a whole.Finished 100% Hard mode in 26hrs, so do with that information what you will.8/10 in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: The level of quality is on par with Sonic Generations and Colors again. I thought that Sonic's speed and control for traversal through the open world is done pretty well. I never really felt like I couldn't control Sonic when running around, but if you do you can also stop on a dime by letting go of the stick.The actual levels are all pretty short, and mostly callbacks like Sonic Generations. They're definitely designed like shrines from Breath of the Wild. Overall short and not too hard to S rank besides Stage 1-2.Super Sonic fights being plentiful is the highlight of the game, with amazing music (with meaningful lyrics),  action set pieces, and power scale showing off Sonic at his best. I personally don't like collectathons, and being somewhat forced to do it to progress did wear on me at times. I found myself rushing through areas just to get to the next Super Sonic fight tbh.Overall I recommend it, as it's the once in a decade good Sonic game.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, my first serious review, because this needs to be said.I'm gonna preface this by saying, i am a longtime, hardcore Sonic fan, i literally could not hate him if i tried, my first game, the very thing the got me playing games, was Sonic Colors for the Wii, and the blue blur has stuck with me ever since.Despite everything: the flaws with this game, Sonic teams past failures, and Sega rushing them to put out content, this game is still a freaking masterpiece in my opinion. Really, i believe the reason Forces and Lost World were crap was because they were rushed, and not by themselves. Sega Sammy (mostly the latter) are the ones that put sonic team on a short time limit, and the fact they were able to make something playable at all is impressive given the circumstances they had to work within.Frontiers however, i have heard rumors that reps at sonic team begged and pleaded for more development time, and the game was STILL forcibly rushed by about a year, which is most likely what made the lategame subpar in most peoples opinions, it shows how little Sega cares and how much Sonic Team does.Still, that extra time paid off, as this game is the most fun I have had with sonic in over 7 years, its not too graphically impressive, but still managed to look and feel unique and beautiful, The gameplay, mostly the combat system, is among some of the best sonic has to offer. Level design is meh (simply because Cyberspace isn't the most fun part of the game to put it simply) but manages to get the job done and not feel unfair constantly. The music? do i even need to say anything? go listen to any of the 3 boss themes or the main theme, the very thing i have on repeat to keep me focused while writing this. Its literally the same concept that one Circletoons animation about this game had, it being "mid" is still a perfect 10, and that is SOLELY becuase of how impressive it is given the working enviroment. Sonic Team wanted to give us something with their passion poured into it. something sonic fans will play and think "man, they do care about our words". In my humble opinion, they did it."They said we'd break, they said we'd lose, but here we are, what else is new?""You and me we're built on trust, thats why we can always get up..."Two of my favorite lines from One Way Dream, a song in the game that is confirmed to be a message from Sonic team to the sonic community, as a love letter to the fans, and a big fat middle finger to the haters.He's here, reach far across these new frontiers, and he has the ones he loves in his hands.Sonic is back.For those wondering why i returned it, its simply because my computer is nearly 8 years old at this point and lags from watching discord streams, it could never hope to run this game. I did however beat this game on Switch, making this review valid.

SEGA DID IT!!!, don't listen to any negative reviews or negative critics, they don't know what they are talking about, I highly recommend anyone to play this. _childDocuments_.review: To be clear, I've left this game in the background for days at a time, hence my time-card, but in actuality I'm right near the end of the game and I've maybe invested 4 hours? Could've been a lot less if I knew the fishing spots could grant me chaos emerald vaults from the beginning. Anyway, onto the review, and this has to be the laziest, most pointless game Sega has ever spat out. In the 6 months since the release Sega have seemingly made no attempt to improve ANY of the glaring faults in this game. I'm going to break this review down into categories:Level design:There are two sections to this, the open-world islands, and the "cyberspace" levels. Let's tackle the "cyberspace" levels first. What are "cyberspace" levels exactly? Dotted around the open-world islands are gates, these gates transport Sonic to more traditional 3D Sonic stages (think Generations/Colors type gameplay), but the trouble is these "cyberspace" levels typically only last from 30 seconds to a minute and a half, and literally ALL of them utilise one of four basic texture packs, Green Hill, Chemical Plant, Sky Sanctuary, and what appears to be Unleashed's Empire City.Yes, that's right, you'll only be seeing these 4 places, crudely reorganised over and over with basic track design ripped from earlier games. I hope you're ready for more Green Hill Zone, because it appears in this game a staggering NINE times. Things don't get better as you'll also be revisiting Chemical Plant Zone seven times, and Sky Sanctuary six times. Yes, recycling assets is a hallmark of Sonic games, but this is ridiculous. Cyberspace levels are supposed to be a homage to previous Sonic games, but instead they feel like a free-trial version of Sonic Generations, a game released over a decade ago that already depended heavily on retreading worn ground, but at least Generations had more than double the variety for level texturing.Now onto the open-world islands, and these really are horrifying. 6 months after release and the game still suffers from the worst and most frequent pop-in rendering issues that I've ever seen in my entire life. Rails, platforms, springs, they all appear out of nowhere once you get within proximity. Every island feels like a disjointed mash, as though someone started a Unity project last night and just started dumping assets wherever.This random mashing together of elements has other issues too. You can be locked into a 2D perspective improperly if you cross within some defined platforming areas, and the colouration of these islands makes identifying Koco (one of an endless number of collectables) difficult. Seriously, why task me with finding things the colour and texture of stone, in places filled with stone? It's pretty obvious the reason these Koco creatures dance around so much is to counterbalance this obvious oversight.  Enemy AI:What AI? You won't find any here. Whether it's little robots that fall apart with one hit or gigantic bosses that take time, they all follow a disturbingly rigid fixed pattern. Have you walked 30ft away from the enemy? Good news, the enemy has no memory of ever seeing you. Are you standing behind a fence that comes up to Sonic's knees? Might as well be an impenetrable moat because god only knows how the robots will take 2 steps to the left to walk around and get you, such logic is well beyond their capabilities. Progression:The game has a system of skill points and collectables governing Sonic's speed, defence, attack, and ring capacity. Ring capacity is essentially worthless because you start with 400, and can easily leech rings out of the ground itself with nothing more than a quick spin. I maxed out Speed too but found no noticeable difference.Some parameters such as defence and attack points can only be increased by trading collectable fruits (usually obtained by completing side missions) with an NPC, whereas other parameters such as ring capacity and speed can only be increased by trading Koco (the aforementioned stone creatures) with another NPC. This progression system sounds familiar enough, but the actual collecting is redundant. The game features a fishing component where each fish caught contributes some amount of tokens, which can be traded for fruit, Koco, even the vault keys used to get chaos emeralds and progress the primary storyline.The fishing is a miserably simple quicktime affair. You throw out the line with the space bar, you wait for the bait to be taken, you hit the space bar again when the bait moves, then you hit it a 3rd time at the correct moment (illustrated by a growing circle within a ring, you must stop the growing circle so that it falls within the ring's boundaries). 3 presses of the space-bar, that's all it is, and you get a fish, a fish that can be worth (and often is) as much as 48 tokens, or enough to buy 3 chaos emerald vault keys, more than 300 Koco or 16 fruit.So therein lies the problem, what motivates me to find anything or complete these dull side-missions when I can get all the collectables I want about two-hundred times faster with a few presses of the space bar? There's no point in me scouring the land for Koco and fruit for hours if I can spend literally just TWO minutes fishing and amass enough keys and tokens to completely finish an island.Storyline:It's awful, but that's nothing new. Sonic games have never been all that good at the story element. This game does go a bit further by inserting more dialogue and attempting (however poorly) to flesh out the characters, but it just doesn't work. They attempt to capitalise on callbacks to canonical events in older games, but it feels like a cheap cameo, a quick off-hand remark to induce nostalgia.Sonic characters in previous games haven't often dwelt on anything that has occurred in other games of the series. They mostly walk around in a perpetual fugue-state, with only the subjects and topics of their current adventure ever on their mind. What happened the week before their current adventure or the week before that may as well be erased from the timeline. To see characters making cheap callbacks to other games feels off. I appreciate the attempt to give Sonic and friends some sense of continuity, but the writing of the dialogue suggests they were looking to cram in nostalgia references more so than they were looking to the past for relevant lessons or knowledge they can apply to the characters' current situation.Conclusion:Sega really just need to shut down for good. I like Sonic games but I'd rather the franchise die than continue to put out these half-baked clumsy games. Sonic Frontiers is the epitome of programmer-shortcuts, the prime example of what happens when a middle-manager imposes a deadline on a team of software developers without a real plan, and so the developers are left to throw together some disjointed patchwork of incomplete ideas and faulty concepts. It's a repetitive slog through levels we've seen too many times with a plot you can't care about and a totally broken progression system. My advice, don't buy this game, wait until it's 99p, or free.

_childDocuments_.review: Yo, so like I never thought I'd make a review on another game but man, I have been blown away by this game.. at first I started it off skeptical, and I was trolling it and laughing at how buggy it started off (horrible performance issues, software issue, not hardware) and how I was just gonna refund it.. I played like 20 mins after, and the lag stopped completely, it was so fluid and beautiful and I had just the most fun ever literally exploring every single area to get 100% on the maps..I was literally in love with the first titan of this game, playing as super sonic was so unbelievably amazing and it was so genuinely exciting to feel powerful.. Imma be fr, this game is amazing, I would DEFINITELY consider buying this, it has its bugs, but they aren't gamebreaking or haltering in any shape.. yes, there is pop in, but it loads up so quickly that it's but a few seconds (or a few half seconds in most cases) for everything to render in properly, which is fine by me.. fighting is kinda interesting, as you progress you can pull of some sick combos and never hit the ground again, which I love so much. The fluidity and speed of sonic is what completes this game for me, as of now I'm only just finishing the 3rd island and I've been enjoying it so far..but one bad thing is like, the main story, since there's a lot of collecting items, but whilst collecting said items (memory tokens), you can also find Kocos to increase your speed, and the two other seed things to get more def and attack, at level 6 in speed my guy sonic is blitzing across the map in like 30 seconds, can't wait to get that to 100 lmao.. so yeah, if you like sonic (or even if you DONT), i genuinely suggest getting this game, it is genuine fun, havent had this much fun in a game since sonic rush or unleashed (generations to but blehhh), JUST BUY THE GAME :SOB:edit: 11/15/2022Just finished this game, and I am honestly starstruck.. I haven't had this much fun playing anything in literal years. Sonic Frontiers managed to become my FAVORITE game in just a span of a few days, from the absolutely amazing and well thought out lore, to the god tier boss battles, this game is literally what sonic is: true speed combined with skill. I finally got everything to 100%, leveled up everything and even did every single quest and cyberspace mission. This game is so much more than you think, you will get sucked into this game and play it for so long without you even noticing. Open Zone is amazing, and I finally understand WHY its named the way it is, each part of the map has so many sonic elements that flows so well together that it feels like an actual complete stage once you get enough speed, you can go to each part of the world so quickly by just following springs and boostpads (which usually bring you into a 2D section, which controls BEAUTIFULLY), this is literally what I needed from sonic.I can wholeheartedly say that I, a major sonic fan, am extremely excited for more games to follow this 'open-zone' formula. PLEASE SEGA MAKE MORE. I BEG. I NEED.

_childDocuments_.review: Controls will feel weird if you're very used to Sonic Generations and Sonic Unleashed day-time Sonic controls, Sonic can feel very stiff and slow, whether this is enjoyable or not depends on how good you think the Sonic Generations/Unleashed controls are, and whether you think boosting is too strong or not in that game. Other than the controls, everything else is mostly good! The characters in the game are not written to only be comprehensible by children, they actually have depth! The story is somewhat cliché but it's not too predictable. Regarding the "open world" concept, it's fun to explore and roam around the world, however, a mini map would be nice to have because you can easily get lost when trying to reach the objective. Nevertheless, it's still fun roaming around the world, the enemies and mini bosses are fun to fight against, and the objects like springs and rails are fun to interact with. There's never a dull moment in the game.smol tip: you can easily get max rings by spending 4-10 seconds doing mini Cyloops, getting max rings will grant a huge speed increase when boosting which make travelling around quicker, it also feels more awesome zooming around :)

_childDocuments_.review: I have no idea who is writing these positive reviews. The game's hardware performance is atrocious. It struggles to hit 40-50 FPS and the weird high-poly photorealism is jarring in contrast with Sonic as the main character. Even for a game that's been in development hell since 2017 (Sonic Team admits this) the texture quality and render distance are really lacking. The camera work is blatantly unfinished, causing gameplay issues with locking on to enemies and epilepsy warnings every time a collectible spawns. Unsurprisingly, it's visually similar to Breath of the Wild, a 6-year-old game for a very underpowered console, but that level of fidelity doesn't make the grade on PC or PS5 in 2023.The voice-acting and """""plot""""" are the worst. If you're buying this game for Sonic characters, don't. They managed to make Mike Pollock's Eggman sound dull and lifeless which is a once-in-a-lifetime achievement. I don't know what happened to Cindy Robinson's Amy but I do know that she said she was retiring from the project and her quick return is very obvious from Amy's voice lines, words slurred together in a pitch that's too low for the character. The intro cutscene is ninety seconds long so the game can hit you with 30 minutes of tutorial text boxes (unanimated, unvoiced, flat, lifeless text boxes! As a tutorial for your 2022 PLATFORMER!) that contain *grammar and syntax errors*. Even the name "Cyber Space" feels like a syntax error every time I look at it. Is that really the best worldbuilding they could have come up with? "Cyber Space"? The world of Sonic Frontiers feels like a shoddy rip-off of Code Lyoko and that's an insult to Code Lyoko.Every single non-Sonic thing in this game feels like a straight asset rip from a canceled open-world game that Sega just happened to have rotting in a storeroom hard drive. Nothing about the game feels like Sonic except for a couple of cheesy Green Hill textures for fanservice. Even the Saturday-Morning-Cartoon-y voice acting and animation, basically the only reason people continue to put up with this franchise, is missing. The generic 'creepy robot' enemies, a mishmash of tropes from the last few 3D Zelda games, fit exceptionally poorly into the world of Sonic. Hilariously, though, they look very similar to the robot enemies in Sonic '06. I don't know how Sonic Team remains this blissfully unaware of how inconsistent their own product is. They keep putting out half-baked ideas on half-baked code and expecting a full paycheck.Maybe Sonic should've stayed in the 90s 'til Sega were ready to put him in something finished and polished. At least Crash Bandicoot still has his dignity.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Frontiers is an upcoming game that promises to take players on a high-speed adventure through various zones and environments. However, one major issue with this game is the unrealistic portrayal of hedgehogs running at supersonic speeds. This depiction goes against what is known about the biology and behavior of hedgehogs in real life.Hedgehogs are small, nocturnal mammals that are known for their slow and steady movements. They are not capable of running at supersonic speeds or performing the outrageous stunts and maneuvers depicted in Sonic Frontiers. This lack of realism takes away from the game's immersion and makes it difficult for players to connect with the game's mechanics on a believable level.Furthermore, the game's insistence on portraying hedgehogs as super-fast runners could also be seen as potentially harmful to the perception and treatment of real-life hedgehogs. By presenting an unrealistic and exaggerated image of hedgehogs, the game could perpetuate harmful stereotypes and misconceptions about these animals.In conclusion, Sonic Frontiers' unrealistic portrayal of hedgehogs running at supersonic speeds is a major flaw that detracts from the game's immersion and believability. By going against what is known about hedgehogs in real life, the game presents an exaggerated and potentially harmful image of these animals. If you're someone who values realism and accuracy in games, then Sonic Frontiers is not the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Full disclaimer I am a huge sonic fan and have played and finished most of the mainline games. But as for Sonic Frontiers---yeah it was ok, most of my issues with this game were from a technical side and lack of polish. Like the pop in didn't ruin the game for me, but it is  and you will notice it throughout your time spent with this game. It is fun to control Sonic in these big environments, you can finally turn while boosting and it gets even better at top speed, launching yourself off rails and flying across the map. And kudos to the devs for allowing you to fine tune the controls (honestly reminds me of tuning a car in a racing game) however it is also janky, stiff and inconsistent. Sometimes Sonic will launch himself off a ramp just fine other times it feels like the earth's gravity is just got 20x stronger.The Cyberspace levels and the Combat in this game are just fine. The levels themselves borrow a lot of assets  and layouts from previous titles. They are better than any Sonic Forces levels by a long mile in my opinion.Plotwise I'd also say it's just fine. The writing and voice acting is the best this series has gotten over the past decade really and it is without a doubt because of Ian Flyns writing and direction. There are a lot of  callbacks and references to past titles and even some nods to more obscure characters in the Sonic lore. But if you're not a huge Sonic nerd like me I think a lot of these will fly over your head, but I'd say that the plot was just fine because the references were a little heavy handed and losses the game some identity of its own when you're constantly referring to the past. The game's structure itself does not lead to the best storytelling if you ask me, there are only so many different ways you can spin going to a new island saving your friend and defeating the big boss and move on to the next.So overall would I recommend this game?  Well if you're a Sonic fan you probably already got it in your collection. But if you're on the fence or curious I'd say wait for a sale,  by then modders may have fixed some of the rougher edges with this game. I am curious how Sonic Team will follow this up, I’d be down for a more polished content rich version of frontiers, Hopefully this game does well so they can be more ambitions for the next title

_childDocuments_.review: 3D Sonic is known for being inconsistent in quality and style. With Forces running of the Boost formula into the ground, we all knew that for the next entry to be worth its asking price, it'd have to deliver on something wildly different. Sure, taking your game Open World in a Post-Breath of the Wild industry isn't a shocking or original twist, but it's far from the worst direction Sonic could choose to go, and Sonic Team finally delivered on a game that justifies its premise.The individual open zones are all large and dense enough to justify breaking down the boarders, and the construction of 'traditional levels' throughout both in the world with floating platforms and separate from it in the Cyberspace Stages makes sure that the game keeps its boost formula roots while also balancing it with the open world. There's some jank in the physics, you can't run loops without using provided boost pads, and the controls don't seem to be as good as previous titles (Generations, Unleashed), but all told, this game works, and its works much better than l could have expected it to going in. The structure, the design, the gameplay, the story, the characters, and the sheer fun of Sonic are all here in ways that previous 3D entries failed to grasp. If you're on the fence, haven't liked 3D Sonic since Adventure 2, or have never played a 3D Sonic, this game is a solid recommendation. Tweak the controls a bit though, side stepping (R1) while boosting (R2) is hard in the default mapping.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great sonic game! There's so much freedom on the islands, it almost makes it feel like an old school Tony Hawk game (with all the grind rails and tricks and such). The boss fights are suitably epic (some of the best I can remember), and the story is pretty good for a game about an anthropomorphic cartoon hedgehog and his animal friends!I'd still probably put this below the Sonic Adventure series as far as replayability goes, but it's a very good game. I have three potential complaints:1) It's a little slow to get started. You've got to give it maybe 2-3 hours to get into it, get used to the controls, and get a bearing on what you're supposed to be doing.2) The cyberspace levels are not great. They're not very memorable and seem like a grind. I'd much rather the team had put their time into something else. Or maybe like 10 epic cyberspace levels as opposed to 28 meh ones.3) I'm probably going to 100% this in about 30 hours of gameplay. Seems kinda short compared to the Sonic Adventure series? Wish there was some more to do.

_childDocuments_.review: Team Sonic nailed it! This exactly what the franchise was needing, the feeling of speed and the freedom of the map it's similar to swinging around on Spider-Man, you never get tired of it and you feel good doing it. The combat is fun but can be quite boring since enemies die too fast (even on hard difficulty). If you're looking to complete the story and get all achievements, you shouldn't need more than 30 hours, but it's gonna be 30 hours of awesomeness and pretty good OSTs.Now, as a Sonic game, it was disappointing not being able to replay the boss battle (not the mini-bosses, those you can), the battles were AMAZING and I would love to do them without making a new save. Keep in mind, this game has 5 bosses, one being only available on hard difficulty right after the 4th boss. If you finish the game and load back your auto save, you're going to be able to replay the 4th and 5th boss, but for the other 3, you will need to save before the fight and there's only 3 save slots, which was disappointing, especially after knowing how many things I would like to redo in that game. In addiction, there is no new game+, so you will have to max all your stats in a playthrough to get all the achievements, thanksfully, there is fishing as a side thing and that can reward you all the materials you need.Overall the game was pretty good and worth buying, looking forward to see what Sonic Team brings next.

_childDocuments_.review: I just played through a H2H game where my WR2 was switched with my Guard in nearly every single play's formation for the majority of the game, eventually causing immediate fumbled snaps that either went to the other team or forced my QB to scramble upon getting the ball, despite it being a pass play. Without a doubt, this is the single buggiest Madden launch I have EVER seen to date, and EA hardly seems to care. A dev was literally caught on twitter calling the people with valid criticisms on this trash ass game "clowns". EDIT: The more I play this game the more I want to invest in a punching bag. The gameplay is so incredibly unbalanced between offense and defense that every game becomes a shootout because the defense runs as if their shoes are filled with rocks. Defensive players are so unbearably slow every down that running backs can get through gaps and into the secondary within seconds functionally unopposed every time they get the ball. Stretch runs are still broken, and dives are only stopped *some* of the time; runs up the middle can still 50/50 beat an engage 8 blitz as if they were running against a dime set. None of the new features added to this game even remotely fit the description of this game, which primarily is SUPPOSED to be a sim experience, replicating "what you see on Sundays". The main marketed modes of this game this year are (once again) MUT and The Yard - neither of which have ever been even close to realistic. The Yard is a backyard football experience with very little strategy other than "throw the ball to whichever corner/wheel route in the designed play opens first", and MUT is...well, it's the same thing.So what about Face of the Franchise? That's a sim mode; it's in franchise! Don't get me started on this trash. As if last year's product wasn't already cliche, this year's FOTF is another cameo-ridden cesspool of writing that a middle schooler could have come up with, full of pre-set scenarios that put all players along the same path or branch of paths that becomes stale within an hour, maybe two if you're lucky. You can only play as one of three offensive positions, and the story is always the same for all players, giving no pretense for replayability. As for actual franchise, likely the gamemode with the most passionate community that is asking the most for new features, EA gave us...patch notes. And when we complained, the response we got was along the lines of "no promises, but we are DISCUSSING these features to be added into the game". Fast forward, the new update announcement as of August 31st was an announcement for an announcement for potential franchise features by a potential timeline. All of this at the same time as the aforementioned clown remarks on twitter by devs. The degree to which EA does not give a damn about their consumer base - or, the degree to which EA is blatantly anti-consumer - other than for their money is frankly appalling. I'm a junior in college just starting to take his actual marketing major courses, and I probably know more about consumerism than the entire collective EA does. Do not give EA your money.

_childDocuments_.review: A Great Experience So FarFor context, I've been a Madden player since 2002 (PC)Madden is back on PC and I can't find much to complain about.  I've played Madden on and off for quite some time, growing up I had a copy of the latest game almost every year.   Madden is finally back on PC and back on Steam, WITH achievements even...so honestly I don't have a lot to complain about.In recent years, I've pretty much stuck to a purchasing the game every other year type of strategy.  Like many of the negative reviews state, not a lot changes each year apart from a roster update.I played a bit of Madden 19 on Origin last year while I had their subscription and it was a decent game, but not much changed from 18.  Same is true for 21.  I consider myself to be a Franchise mode only type of player, however shockingly my hours in game spent so far have been spent playing MULTIPLAYER. On a whim I decided to try a head 2 head match and since then I have been able to find games at a consistent rate.  With there being NO crossplay, I expected multiplayer to be dead, but I've already played over 20 H2H games with an only 40s-1.5m wait time in between games.  I'm impressed!  I've played MUT occasionally throughout the years but I got Madden21 late so there's not much point in me starting put time into building a team now.  I have the deluxe edition so I opened up a few packs and tried to find a multiplayer game.  Found one in seconds so it looks like the PC community for MUT is still strong. All in all, I am having a ton of fun playing these H2H quick play matches, and when the community finally dies out I'm sure I'll have fun in Franchise mode. Not a lot has changed, but so far it's been easy to find games in Multiplayer and Madden is on Steam so I can't complain.  YES Franchise mode needs some much needed improvements, but hey...at least I can see a players history now.  (The teams they used to play for and their stats) .  This was a much needed feature and if I recall correctly, it was NOT in Madden 19 so I'm happy with being able to sign a new player and see his previous stats.Madden 21 is a BUY for me.

_childDocuments_.review: So I got EA Play to check this game out, and I gotta say, it seemed really fun at first. The Face of the Franchise mode is really the only part I dove deep on, and I gotta say, what a disappointment.  I thought this was going to be a fun and interesting little mode where I could build my career, play for a decade and a half, and build a legendary story with my character.  What I actually got was, repetitive cutscenes, "rpg style" gameplay (reporters asking you questions, and you picking an answer based on what skill you get from the answer), and coaching decisions that made absolutely 0 sense.Long story short, I played as a QB.  I wanted to reshape the Bears and lead them to championships as their new legendary QB.  Made it to the super bowl my first year and lost on a doink FG (maybe this was meant to be), won the superbowl the following two years.  The following year, I sustained an injury (no context btw, didn't even know wtf my injury was, but I was out the whole damn season).  The following season, my player returned, we went undefeated and won a superbowl.  Then the part that really makes the story, I was cut the next season after a practice where I received a silver rating.  Listen, I'm all about pushing a story, but when you tell people they can shape their own legacy, I'd much rather not feel like I'm stuck inside of some EA devs box.The "dream team" storyline is a joke.  I signed onto the Texans randomly, and sure, we got a good HB, and one good WR, but the rest of the talent on the team was long gone before I arrived.  The next best rated player we had at any position other than WR, HB or QB was our punter at 85.  Dream team material right there.Another thing, why the hell do I have to simulate about 85% of my FOTF career if I want anything to count for my progression?  The mode starts you in HS, you play a game or two, you're in college, you play a game or two, and then boom you made it to the NFL - where, you guessed it, you play maybe IF YOU'RE lucky, 4-5 games a season.Another gripe, the announcers.  Who programmed these conversations? I picked a response in my FOTF press conference that was a modest "winning is a team effort", and the very next game ALL the announcers could talk about was how I came out and said I would put the team on my back with my talent.  Not to mention all the cringey references to madden and it being a video game "who cares man, work those thumbs"... smh. Overall, I'd give this like a 2/10.  I had fun for the first few games, quickly grew to realize this is just yet another rapid release sports game. Maybe next year they'll be able to compete with 2k's career modes.

I figured there might be SOME sort of big change from Madden 19 two years ago, there isnt. They added one thing about player abilities that overall dont drastically or even noticably change anything. At that point missions are frustratingly difficult for players just starting out, theres hardly any that can easily be knocked out if your team is below an 80 overall, and even if you want do go through a dark-souls-esque guantlet of failed missions voer and over again, THERES NO REAL GOOD OPTIONS TO BUY WITH YOUR COINS. I really like how the ball trajectory is finally altered by hitting the QB. Also the LBs feel more responsive when tackling and actually tackling instead of diving at air in front of the ball carrier because it didn't trigger the animation.Now for a quick re-review:post-patch - they addressed ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, but hey more MUT content you can pay for just to have it be worthless next year! joy!-AI clock management is atrocious. Every since they added the automatic time run off in no huddle, 9/10 the AI wont call a timeout until AFTER the 10-15 second run off. Already had 3 close games end by the AI letting the time run out before calling a timeout, very anti-climactic.-The new d-line started out fun until i realized if i get double teamed as a DT i can literally move 2 OL players like the 3 of us are on a plate because they move any direction i turn when engaged. Looks straight up goofy as ♥♥♥♥.-the AI blocking is still ♥♥♥♥, still so many run plays where a blocker is just running full speed ahead into outer space passing 3 blockers on his way to run out of bounds and through the stadium wall. The way AI blocking works needs to be rebuilt, there is no targeting, the AI just runs to a spot and blocks anyone that runs into him, all while taking an angle no self respecting player would ever take to cut off a runner.-Still getting sucked into tackles and blocks after i ran past like they're a black hole with wonky animations.-Scenarios in franchise mode don't ever correlate to what happened on the field, ie. sit a player to rest a week before the playoffs and it doesn't register that he didn't start even though I went in and made sure he wasn't on the depth chart that week, then get a negative modifier because i didn't target a player, said player gets injured early and you still get negative modifier and no one acknowledges the injury being the reason.-The gameplan practices are extemely buggy and sound levels are way off, hearing clacking of pads 10x louder than the coach talking and the gameplan practices are just funny because some of their concepts only apply to madden and not real football.-Impossible to turn off soundtrack during practice and the yard even with music at 0. It makes me want to bash my head into a wall. Literally the worst soundtrack of any game i've played. -The UI is still a laggy mess, even on an NVMe m.2 drive-SB celebration still the same 5 years running-Still so heavily animation based that you're just hoping for the right animations as opposed to actual skill-HDR looks like ♥♥♥♥ during rain games, way too dark-They threw in Kaep to combat the #NFLDropEA-They gave away copies to try and stop #NFLDropEA================================================================Below was previous review week of launch================================================================Review from someone that's played Madden since '97:Let's start off with The Bad first:-Despite MUT being the money maker they still continue to have the slowest and clunkiest menus in gaming; could be fixed by a patch, but i wont hold my breath with EA, some bugs are never fixed and ignored-Franchise mode is copy and paste from previous years. The added presentation is just music playing pregame with the stadium announcer saying the team names then it's back to the same tired introduction lines from the announcers.-The writing for Face of the Franchise is some of the worst I've seen, makes nba 2k mycareer stories look like oscar winning movies in comparison. Also you almost always get drafted by the Bears. - The yard is basically a less fun blitz with yet more microtransactions-defenders tend to get sucked into blocks more than previous years-blocking AI is somehow worse ex: on kick returns i regularly see the outside blocker run past everyone and not attempt to turn inside to block; screen passes you still regularly see lineman run past corners and safties as if oblivious to them-Kicking meter is too bright and they use a white dial, contrast on it sucks too-Some UI changes just to say they changed it--------------------------------------------------------------------------------Now the Good:-Gameplay: it's leaps and bounds better than 21 in terms of animation flow, animations happen faster and there are more of them resulting in a much smoother experience overall and less madden moments of wtf-The yard ability load outs; it's a good idea for head to head matches to have different abilities to level up and experiment with, makes replay value higher-streamlined some MUT; now when doing a specific set of challenges you can flow from objective to objective without having to go all the way back and select it again, still too many menu transfers in MUT IMO-more coaching adjustments; I love the addition of being able to set depth on zone drops, helps a lot when trying to cover certain parts of the field like in goalline or defending the deep pass.-devs acknowledging and giving a timeline for improvement; just hope they don't ignore 21 and still give us something to chew on in the form of a big update or something til next edition-community files; custom draft classes and sliders can change the feel of franchise mode too-on steam finally; get a much bigger audience to PC and also the modding community; lots of potential for creative modders---------------------------------------------------------------Score: 7.5/10Gameplay is great, the yard is kinda fun, franchise mode is stale as old bread. Here's hoping next gen they deliver on their promises. Soundtrack is annoying, but that's just me.======================================================================Above is previous review week of release======================================================================

_childDocuments_.review: If you don't own any other madden games, then buy this on sale. It is identical in almost every way to the last several madden games, except with updated rosters, server support, and it is riddled with bugs. They added an avatar for you on the main screen which so far does nothing else except stand there, and in the clothing choices they add basic clothing for every team, except they straight up forgot to add patriots pants. That one doesn't really matter, but theres just an endless supply of bugs or missing content like that. In the face of the franchise mode my character suddenly changed race, name, gear, and everything halfway through a college football game. I attempted to play my way through it, and then suddenly my character gained the ability to fly, and the game broke. I was never able to do anything else in face of the franchise mode. The stories of missing content or bugs in face of the franchise mode are hilarious and endless, and it seems the game mode doesn't even work, as the vast majority of people will never actually finish college. One of the brightsides is that they have finally fixed fantasy drafting, which is one of my favorite things to do in madden. Now the cpu drafts like a real person would, so you don't have 99 ovr christian mccaffery getting drafted in the 15th round every time. All in all the game is worth it contingent on you not having any madden from the past 5 years or so, not caring about any mode except connected franchise, and the game being on a 50+% off sale. If those don't all apply, then its probably not worth it for you.

_childDocuments_.review: As you have seen in other reviews, this year is not much different than past years.  If you go in knowing what to expect, then that is on you. For the past three years, there has been a bug that makes it so you can not see your stats, rank or your previous opponent's stats in regular online head to head play.  This makes playing competitively useless if you can not see how you stack up against the competition. This has been discussed so much that we had a 52 page thread on the EA website where EA (EA Barry) would occasionally come in and say they were working on it.   This has to be one of the easiest things in the world to fix, but there is a growing belief that they do this to push people to play Ultimate Team (the ultimate cash grab) - where you can clearly see your online stats, hmmmm.    The game-play is scripted, animation based garbage.  Does not take skill to win, just luck of the draw on which animation you will receive.  I am a 20 year Madden vet and can tell you that the game play is as frustrating as ever.  The Face of the Franchise is a cringe inducing mess. 5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't played a Madden game since 2018, already this feels like the biggest rinse and repeat they've had. It also felt super phoned in and I wouldn't have bought it if I wasn't a football fan in general. Below I will breakdown the few things that bugged me about Madden 21Face of the franchise: The story line is recycled and boring. you have your main skill set that can be upgraded but there are attributes that are gained by how you respond in cutscenes and "press conferences". The responses don't have audio recording nor do most of the questions in the news conference, it's just terribly worded text. Also character creation is that of " the Sims 2", my character looks like I cut someone's face off and put it on my face... You get to play a few years of college for a school you probably aren't a fan of if you live out side of the south or west coast. But it's the closest to NCAA you'll ever get. ( pay the players)Franchise Mode: There are legit players missing or they don't even look like the players on the actual team. It's the same franchise style: you play, you win or lose, you get draft slots, rinse and repeat. When you win the super bowl it's the same animation celebration they've had since 2015. Also coaches are always angry for some reason, and players are complaining to other position players if they are doing poorly. If the makers of Madden knew anything about football, you would never see a RB go up to a LB saying, " What's the problem, why do you suck so bad?" Franchise doesn't give you that epic feeling of winning a game, doesn't build tension for rivalries, if you make a big play it's the same dance since 2018. NO real excitement other than to just win games.The new game mode THE YARD: It's supposed to feel like you are really cool playing a type of "backyard" style football. There are some aspects that are cool. The plays are fun, but messy. The CPU is so horrible it doesn't prepare you for real players. You can pick a skills set based off of current players that need to be upgraded when you win, this unfortunately causes mismatches with real players because they are obviously just better upgraded players you play against and have no chance. the jukes and spins are the same as the normal game mode but they have you put the ball behind your back or something pointless to make you feel like it's "cooler". You are able to play the mode with friends who have the game which probably makes it a lot more fun, but I don't have friends.Ultimate team: it is what it has always been for as long as it's existed.OVERALL: this game tickles the fancy of whomever is an NFL fan. You play as the your team with the big name players. You can live out your dream as an individual player on your favorite team or forge your own destiny. I down vote because if you have last years game It's not worth the money. This feels phoned in and Madden tends to get away with selling because new content will be available every year in the form of new players. I don't see myself buying another one until there is a major overhaul in Franchise mode and Face of the Franchise. I am hoping someday we can hire agents, select contracts, be influenced by teams. SUPER bowls feel SUPER. Design superbowl ring for the team, retire jerseys, move cities, make a new team, do the probowl minigames, become a star where you can see your stock rise in jersey sales, sports cards, do commercials. There's litteraly endless things that could be added and changed. Madden shouldn't just be relying on a new draft class every year to make anew game, they should want to innovate the players experience.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a time not that long ago when Madden was something more than an overpriced roster update ushered forth by a lazy publisher. Once upon a time Madden NFL was a fun game with innovative features, that of course was before EA shareholders decided that all the money wasn't enough money, and before gamers lost their pride and accepted Diminishing Returns the Game (Madden NFL). As recently as the Playstation 3 era Madden was a game with roster integration that allowed you to bring in the latest college classes from NCAA Football. You could actually update your own rosters without having to buy a new game every year! Going back to the PS2 version of Madden we had Create a Formation, which let you create actual formation and design plays from those formations. You could act like an actual NFL head coach and put players in positions to wreak havoc on their opponents. It was a truly glorious feature that has yet to be replaced. On Super Nintendo Madden had a Create a Player function that wasn't just a bunch of sliders. The feature was a series of mini-games that allowed you to cultivate the skills of your player by actually playing the game. There was a forty yard dash, passing drills, running back drills, wide reciever drills and so on. Again it was glorious, and again it has not been replaced.  This game has gotten so lazy that you can't even make a proper create a team. We used to be able to make our own uniforms, but no more. Modern versions of Madden don't even allow you to properly create a team, instead users are fed low effort design predetermined by the development team and stuffed to the gills with as much boring as possible. Madden NFL is like a small under-attended dog that barks at the wind, I just want it to stop and you should to.

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR: Not worth the money at all. If you're like me and just love football (and don't have any of the other Madden games), then it's a good game it get despite being overpriced. I don't care for the ultimate team (I see it as a huge money grab that's just not fun to play), nor do I have any interest in the Yard. I only play the Franchise mode (which is honestly only fun if you go to the league settings and turn off full field control so you only control your player) and then exhibition games. I enjoy these modes for the most part, but I'd say that they alone are 100% not worth spending $60 on.The Face of the Franchise is boring and the story line is stupid. Not to mention that the commentators saying "QB 2" throughout the entire story (I'm assuming, since it got so boring that I just stopped playing after hitting college) is annoying and unrealistic, and signifies that minimal effort went into the game mode. This would be fine if the game wasn't so expensive and the goal wasn't for it to be as realistic as possible. It would be nice if they had a list of preset names/nicknames that the commentators actually say during games, like they had in Fifa (I think, the last Fifa I played was Fifa 12 and they had the option to choose a nickname for that the commentators would actually announce. If they had it in 2012 you'd think they would have it now). There are also a number of small glitches and bugs in the game, and small details that are annoying. For example, in franchise mode if you play as an elusive running back, there's a practice that has you run through precision moves. This would be fine, except they got rid of precision moves completely this year (making the practice impossible to complete) and it's clearly a copy and paste of the code from last year's Madden. This brings up my main issue with this game: all of these small things wouldn't annoy me as much if this game wasn't so expensive. But when you spend $60 on a game, you expect much better. This is what happens when a company has a monopoly on a game with no competition: they can charge whatever they want and make the game suck. EA, let someone else make these games!

_childDocuments_.review: Madden NFL 21 offers many ways to play the game.  You can play a season, exhibition game, create a player whose career you follow, control the management of the team, draft, and more.  You can play single player or multiplayer.  During the main season you can use the season's calendar to play the actual games being played, which is always fun.Overall, I really enjoyed the game.  Though I say this from someone who has not played Madden since 1996 on the SNES.  I definitely would not buy this game annually as the only real changes that you would get is an updated roster, and maybe some additional enhancements.  Multiplayer is really tough, be prepared for some really good opponents.  I prefer to play simulation on single player where the game is more realistic, difficult, and gives me a good challenge without the frustrations that multiplayer brings.The graphics are pretty amazing, especially in comparison to my last Madden experience, and they run well on my system and really work well in the game.  There are some clips here and there, but mostly the graphics compliments the game real well.  The ball is caught in the player's hands, they trip over players, and the tackles are good too.  It's fun experience to play the game, but also to watch it.The sounds are good, though the ball being dropped makes a weird stuttering sound when it bounces around and then drops.  The commentators will definitely repeat themselves eventually, but they are good at really bringing up points about what is happening in the game.  For example, reminding you that in the previous drive you had an explosive touchdown.  They are good background noise to add to the cinematic experience of the game.The gameplay is fluid, it's easy to play and maneuver your player through the field.  Though at times, especially on defense, the movement can seem pretty stiff, but maybe that's cause I suck at defense.  It's easy to spin, stiff arm, and truck through the defense.I've been enjoying this game since I got and highly recommend you take it for a ride if you're interested.  Not sure if Madden 22 is any better or not, and not sure how much better Madden 21 is to Madden 20.  Either way, get yourself some Madden and play a game with your favorite team.  You won't regret it whether you enjoy arcade sports game or a simulation, this game allows you to create the type of sports game that you want to play and it does it well enough to definitely keep you entertained.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Madden. It's fun when it works.The game is deep and a lot of fun, but it has a lot of quirks right now. You can power through them and enjoy the game in spurts, or you can wait a while until the updates roll through and fix everything. Here some examples of issues I personally have seen since unlocking the game 3 days early on Aug 25th. - Weird commentary glitches where they call your Face of the Franchise high school team the Panthers (they are selected as my favorite team so it could be a glitch where it names your favorite team) and say "you're watching the NFL" when you play your college games.- Black screens. A couple times the screen has just completely blacked out. You can still see the scoreboard and your players x factor logo on the ground, but everything else is black. I have had this randomly happen when opening a new menu as well.- Complete crashes. I have had franchise games crash at crucial moments, particularly late in the game or right after half time. Yesterday, I was playing a game online and it crashed at half time. Sorry SLOWGLXY, I promise I didn't bail because I was losing.When the game actually works, it is great. There is a lot of depth and customization and it is quite satisfying. Exhibition, online, MUT, franchise, face of the franchise (story mode), playbook editing, player editing, and a lot more will keep you busy all season and you'll have fun doing it... as long as it works. I can't truly give this game a positive or negative review just yet. I only am because the review process forces me to. If everything worked flawlessly, the game would certainly be a 100% recommendation. Until then, I must heed warning.

_childDocuments_.review: While I don't recommend this game, there ARE things to do in it that are genuinely fun, and if it weren't a full $60, I'd probably recommend it. There is a good time to be had in here, just not a $60, full-price AAA good time.PROS:-Madden on PC. I don't really think this needs explaining.-MUT is addictive, in a fun way. If you like football and TCGs, you'll enjoy Ultimate Team. ...Well, the single-player part of it.-If you, like me, haven't bought a Madden game in a decade, there are a lot of new features. This one needs a HUGE asterisk, because from everything I've read, it's basically identical to Madden 20, and only very slightly different from Madden 19. If you've bought any recent games, you're not going to notice anything that special. On the other hand if you're like me and haven't bought a Madden game since 2010 because of how notorious EA is for charging $60 for a roster update, a decade of crawling has created a worthwhile update. Plus Russell Wilson actually exists on this one!-It is still football. Despite its many issues, the core mechanics and gameplay of a game of football are still fun. If you enjoy football, there is a good time to be had in this game. Whether it's a good time worth its pricetag is another matter.CONS:-Microtransactions everywhere. As if EA taking full price for the minor tweaks wasn't enough, the game is full of bait to try and get you to shell out money for ingame currency. You can play and have fun without it, but it's obvious that nothing was getting added to the game they couldn't monetize. A good experience and quality take a very clear backseat.-Online is a headache. Matchmaking is either terrible or nonexistent. God help you if you're playing MUT multiplayer, because the pay-to-win microtransactions mixed with the terrible matching system means your starter-pack 70 OVR team is going to get mauled by a bunch of 90+ OVR teams.-The physics engine makes no sense. Every single pass play has the potential to become The Immaculate Reception. I've had a ball batted in the air stay bouncing for ten full seconds. Hitboxes for linemen on running plays are as weird and inconsistent as ever, sometimes a blocked defender's hand will extend ten feet from his body and tackle you down, sometimes you can run right into them, make a sharp right turn to get away, and lose zero momentum. Receivers and defenders seem to occasionally phase through each other on passing plays.-As always, there are a bunch of plays that are useless. There are certain running plays that take so long to develop they will never be useful. Same for some passing plays that just flat-out do not work with the broken physics engine. You can throw out about 70% of any given playbook. This is not ideal for a game that wants to sell itself as a realistic football simulation.-As always, there are a bunch of plays that are broken. Singleback slot 01 Trap always works against AI opponents. Always. I don't think I've run it for negative yards, even on max difficulty. It almost always gains at least seven yards, even on, again, max difficulty. There are a couple dozen plays that are effective if you use them right, but there are maybe five or six that are so consistently effective that running anything else is waving a white flag, especially in multiplayer. The game gives you a hundred things you can do, but only about 20 of them are worth doing, and five of those 20 are so broken that doing anything else is silly. Again, not ideal for a game that wants to sell itself on realism.VERDICT:DO BUY IF:-You haven't bought a Madden since Andrew Luck was at Stanford and want a game that isn't older than most of the league.-You have the money/patience/etc. to not be bothered by all the microtransactions and pay-to-win elements.-You're a Ravens fan like me and dig seeing Lamar Jackson everywhere. Big Truss.-You're an EA employee being blackmailed by your boss to drive up sales.DON'T BUY IF:-You have a copy of Tecmo Bowl handy.-You have a copy of any of the NCAA football games handy. (Yeah it's college, but they're somehow still better almost a decade later)-You have an actual football and three friends handy.-You don't want to spend $60 on a meh time-killer, which is what this game ultimately is. It doesn't have the polish and depth to be more than that, and Steam is full of time-killers that cost less than a third of this pricetag.It's a damn shame EA has its exclusive license. Madden was better when 2K gave them competition. But hey, Bo Jackson is more fun in 8-bit anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: haven't played a Madden game since '14, but needed the sweet release of football in this dumpster fire of a year.While this iteration feels like the evolution of the franchise in terms of added features, there are numerous issues that frequently disappoint.From graphics issues that cause a complete freeze for anywhere from 5 seconds to a minute (every 3-4 games), to obvious bugs among menu options, the biggest issue is the commentating. I've heard the commentators mentioning the QB needing to protect the ball better, since the last drive ended in an interception - but I had run for a touchdown on the last drive. The stats commentating is even worse, though not *quite* broken: I've heard the commentators choosing to comment on how often a QB was sacked in a previous game (twice) rather than speaking to the single-season sack record that was just broken. These issues are everywhere - break the 200 yard rushing mark in a game? Let's talk about how surprised you are that a run play was called on 3rd down. These disconnects happen multiple times in every game, and it seems like a simple issue to solve. This one's for free, EA Sports: map your commentating lines to some impact value (career record > season record > game record > specifics about a big play > etc), and choose whichever line is related to the biggest thing that happened. If there's a tie, (multiple single-game records in a single play, for example), then apply the random selection you seem to have chosen. I can recommend the game if you don't expect to notice or care about these issues, but I can't say that it's worth the cost otherwise.
