_childDocuments_.review: Recently came back to multiplayer hoping the game was in a better state than release... I was sorely disappointed.If you want a good and functional Halo multiplayer experience, save yourself the headache and get MCC. It's still infinitely better in almost every possible comparison than Halo Infinite. Better season progression, better customization, less desync, far less bugs or CTD's, better playlists (seriously, who asked for EVERY SINGLE semi-auto gun to be in the Tactical Slayer playlist???)...Not to mention that MCC has Firefight, and Campaign and Firefight still counts towards season progression in MCC.The game is still playable, but honestly it's just insane to me that MCC, a collection of several games all over a decade old, is a better experience. 343 really dropped the ball with this one.EDIT: -- Update as of 30 March 2024 --MCC multiplayer population is waning which is why I thought I'd give this game a second try. I disliked it immediately upon coming back to it but decided I would do the full 20 unlocks on the battle pass (operation) before making up my mind.Multicore is nice. The game looks great and the gunplay is decent. Movement is fluid for the most part outside of desync issues. The new Firefight is boring (and easy). The playlists are in somewhat of a better state but now the core issue is with the maps. Most new maps in rotation are either poorly designed or have poorly optimized spawns (usually both). There is un-ironically a map in which you can go almost 2 full minutes of game time without there being a first blood, and this is in Tac Slayer where the TTK is 1 second.This game is barely playable in 2024. The amount of monetization in this game is genuinely off-putting for how poorly it functions after 3 years. Absurd amount of desync (ironically after a patch that was meant to fix the desync issues), UI errors and other bugs, and I have to choose between some of the worst screen tearing I have ever come across, or enabling VSync and feeling like my character is walking through gelatin at a 1 second delay and constantly teleporting around.Honestly: not having a Halo multiplayer experience at all is still a genuinely better option than Halo Infinite's multiplayer experience. Uninstalled.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, Halo Infinite feels like a mixed bag of nostalgia and missed opportunities. The gameplay has that classic Halo charm, but the 'Games as a Service' model is dragging it down. It’s frustrating to see a game that could be so great suffer from a lack of proper progression systems—why do I have to rely on challenges for XP instead of just enjoying the matches?After investing countless hours, it's hard to overlook the repetitive maps and the bugs that seem to multiply with every patch. I get that the campaign had its moments, and fighting against the Banished brought back some of that old-school fun, but the multiplayer experience often feels like a chore. The mechanics are solid—who doesn't love the thrill of a well-timed grapple or a perfectly executed energy sword kill? But when grenades disappear or I get 'back-smacked' through my shield, it breaks immersion completely.The potential here is massive, and yet, it feels like 343 is playing catch-up instead of leading the charge. With so many promises left unfulfilled and a steady decline in player numbers, it’s hard not to feel let down. Maybe in a few years, we’ll see this title reach its full potential, but for now, it feels like a shadow of what Halo could be. Here’s to hoping for a brighter future in the Halo universe! 🚀

_childDocuments_.review: First off, the gameplay is insanely solid and intuitive, the movement feels great, the weapon sandbox is pretty nice, the only problem might be the lack of punch in some weapons, and the vehicles feels super lightweight. The 10 maps included are nice for the most part, but having 3 of the 4 BTB maps being set in daylight forest kinda blends em' together. It definitely needs more distinct maps.The progression system is awful. XP is only given by challenges and playing the game good won't make any difference. I played 6 Hours and I'm barely level 2. 343 however has stated that they were aware of these issues and are working on it.Playlist wise, we need more control for what we queue for, like in MCC where you could pretty much opt out of any gamemode you didn't wanna play. Dedicated Slayer playlist and Objective playlist would be nice. FFA is a must have too for solo queue players who don't always wanna have to rely on a whole team to win.The customisation is a mixed bag, on paper it looks amazing, the assets are really well made, but in practice, more than 70% of the content is locked behind the premium battle pass. Coatings and Visors are locked between armor cores too, which severely cripples the Spartan customisation when it comes to colors.Overall it is a pretty fun game, but coming out of MCC, it kinda feels lackluster in content. I hope the actual launch on December 8 will correct most of these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking for a genuine halo experience l recommend looking else where. In the current stage there are way too many issue with the game politically and technically. The Biggest Problem! We live in a world where developers heart and passion come second. Games used to be made with more of the consumer in mind. Everything was on whether or not the game launched successfully! Now, the community (not just halo but all gaming) has lowered our standards and expectations to allow the launch of an unfinished product. Big AAA and IP games are now owned by big coroporations who only want to cash in on the monetizations. The community has been only given lots of PR. Things any Halo game should have- Forge- Functional ranking systems (not being tested in beta 1 year later)- Fully functional theater mode- Custom games (it exists but is untouched without forge) and custom game server browser - Sustainable online multiplayer content (maps, weapons, game modes (Infection/FUN ONES) etc.-Anticheat (plenty of hackers on the higher level ranks) You will find yourself only playing this game to sweat on any casual game list. They changed how aim assist work on controllers. If you are not a sweaty FPS keyboard user already, you will find most people can out shoot you. You can switch to only mouse/keyboard but you will wait longer for games and play with the same people even more in matchmaking. GENERAL HALO EXPERIENCE: The game has some aspects correct and done much better than halo 4 and 5. General armor styles, weapon design and sounds look great. Overall, the game feels  more competative  and flows more like a fast paced point and click shooter. The customization is super restrictive and nothing like how anyone wants it. The progression system is very unfulfilling making you feel no sense of achievement. The whole aim assist is BROKEN and rewards anyone for simply strafe matching. The skill bar has been lowered and muddied down. So much of your aim is done for you by only using the left thumb stick on controllers! You had to actually aim in the past halo games. Broken as all hell. The Politics:There have been many promises made, we were told we were being listened to and big updates were coming.  Season one lasted many months too long. Season two is going to last even longer based off of the road map planning with very minimal updates or with things that should have already been in the game. Now that the Bonny left 343 maybe things will change but there is no guarantee. 343 has lost majority of their player base loyalty and no one really believes in them and it is very apparent anywhere you look on social media. In general, we the consumers were being thought of second. Nothing was fixed or updated properly and the predatory progression system which induces you to spend your money is still not gone and restricts the great customization everyone knows and loves (which should be unlocked and rewarded to you by completing in games tasks, achievements and events.) In short its is a good game to pass time but nothing more.

Running around trying to get an ammo refill with a boss after me, running faster than me and one-shotting me on loop isn't fun. The most painful ones are any brute bosses wielding hammers: if you can't find an elevated platform to cheese'em out, you're in for some time. And the hunters whose design was brutally murdered on this version: just get a vehicle, preferably a wasp or a scorpion and just kill them from a safe distance, they have the exact same problem as most of the bosses. I'm at the Escharum fight, I wanted to be patient but it just gave my patience its final blow. _childDocuments_.review: Wow. What a thrill. Halo Infinite really hits different. Honestly there is little reason not to play and try it yourself (unless you cannot run it). That being said.... There are multiple complaints about Halo Infinite that I cannot say are fair or true, though this game deserves criticism.First, progression. Many say that the progression is too slow, and honestly I slightly agree. Actively challenges is the only way to progress reasonably through the Battle Pass, but it is a fun challenge and goal to have while playing, adding a dynamic variety of playstyles which end up being fun (after replacing some of the more annoying challenges). Unfortunately, it can take +10 hours to get 5 tiers through the Battle Pass, so even slightly more reward would be nice. On another note, I think that EXP and levels should exist in some capacity, especially as the Skill Based Matchmaking (SBMM) very much exists. This system of matchmaking can be annoying after a while as the playerpool can get too hard, very quickly, especially if you are an above-average player. Some complain that there is select progression. What I mean is that the progression is non-existent if you wish to play this game for free, while everything gameplay wise stays the same. I have no idea why people think this is unfair; this is a free-to-play title. Additionally, you can always access these $10 Battle Passes as they never expire, meaning players can take their time with completing them. Sounds great, right? Because it is! C'mon, there are just so many bad opinions out there about the microtransactions that have been known for MONTHS pre-release. None of this is news, and I would be inclined to say that most of these types of reviews are trolls but it is what it is.And the next popular critique that I take issue with: vehicles. For some reason people are complaining that vehicles are pointless or being on foot is "objectively better?" Sorry, but what? How a team uses their Warthogs and even Mongooses can ABSOLUTELY alter a whole match, whether focusing objective or going straight into the fray. And anyone saying that the Wasp or Scorpion aren't fun or viable just aren't playing the game right. If anything, a great Wasp or Banshee pilot can easily rack a Killing Spree before being shot down (fly fast and focus targets!). The Razorback has a different but equally as important role as its cousin, the Warthog, and it offers a great battle dynamic (at least in Big Team Battles). And regardless of all of that, who can hate the feel and sound of the Warthog? Craziness. If anything the issue with vehicles come in the spawning of them and how enemy teams can memorize where Pelicans land and steal your teams equipment (e.g. Warthog, Ghost, Scorpion). While that is annoying, it really doesn't happen often and when it does you're losing anyways.  And lastly, there is some talk about the "imbalance" that the new weapons create with the old ones. Admittedly the new weapons can be quite strong, and in one case take the role of a previous-iteration of a gun (e.g. the Plasma Pistol), but I would say that some are also pretty weak (shocking, I know). But that is really disingenuous as arguably any gun has a "place." My two complaints are the Plasma Pistol lacking any real utility, and even the Shock Pistol lacks common use over the Sidekick and a good Sticky Grenade. The Stalker Rifle is a pleasant treat too as it stands and feels like a Brute version of the UNSC's DMR. Great fun when at medium range. Oh, and the Commando? Fun and balanced, IMHO! Oftentimes I find myself beating it in a close-ranged fight with something like the Assault Rifle, but in short-medium range it is something to fear (albeit aim is a must). Love the re-balance they did on it. And on the topic of weapons, I would say that many weapons from previous titles get far more spotlight than ever before. The Assault Rifle? Damn does that thing do some work, more than any other Halo I can recall outside Halo: CE (excluding the other titles that shall not be named, of course). Complaints about old guns not being included (e.g. Classic Shotty, Magnum, DMR) are slightly ignorant as 343 already mentioned that these weapons will eventually find their way into Infinite (much like many other features, i.e. assassinations).~So is it worth it? Play it and find out. Worst case scenario, you waste an hour. Best case scenario, you love it. I think it is absolutely amazing what these developers can do with all their work and love for the series, and seeing 343 slowly redeem themselves is something I once never thought possible. What a time to be alive, and I highly encourage anyone who can run in (especially with friends!!!) to pick this up and see for yourself.Alright time to play some more and excitedly await the many updates that are to come.EDIT 11/5/22:So, Halo Infinite is finally getting Forge in a few days... Well, anything I say here about the issues with updates and content has already been stated over 1000 times by everyone and their grandmothers. Regardless of all its faults, it really does seem like Infinite is finally getting the necessary tools and content for longevity. Will it deliver? Will it be enough to garner back all those fans that came within the first couple weeks? Guess we'll see...

Season 1 of multiplayer was an instant cash grab, the majority of cosmetics were locked behind paywalls, limited game modes, terrible connections, and the campaign felt very lacking and somewhat unfinished. Alot of people defended it due to how 343 lost alot of time with having major backlash on the graphics but that just gos to show how they were willing to put out an even more half assed version with more than likely the same amount of paywalls. The base gameplay felt pretty solid when it worked but it was held back by terrible connection issues and some guns just feeling drastically more weak compared to other weapons. I left a little after halfway through season 1 because i already finished the campaign and just feeling defeated when playing a multiplayer where i felt like i was earning anything. after hearing about season 2 i jumped back on and the only thing i can say is its just more depressing to play than before, FPS feels way worse (could just be my bad gamer chair), heavy latency issues, those of you who play destiny it feels like D2 multiplayer when dudes are shooting u from behind walls. CONSTANT disconnection from the server (I do actually have incredible internet so its very jarring when im getting invalid shots on players and lag is constantly a problem. Also i dont want to start the whole MnK VS Controller debate but from my experience MnK is good for quick movement and being able to snap onto someone flanking you or just being more precise with you movement, and the latter being better for holding lanes. But for this game Controllers Aim assist literally boosts my KD every time i switch to it, having such a strong aim assist to do 70% of the work that it requires to kill someone just feels drastically superior over MnK (might just be my bad gaming chair)Only time i play this game is with friends because some funny stuff can happen. _childDocuments_.review: This review is with regard to the campaign. For the beginning half of the campaign I was on board but it lost me as it went on. I'm first going to talk about the good stuff then the bad stuff *Warning Spoilers Ahead*The good stuff:It's halo it always feels good to be Master Chief again. The first mission I think is really good for story telling. You're on a banished ship trying to free the pelican. Solid story building and classic campaign level. I liked the dramatic ending to that level too. Then you head to the ring and you go through your classic forerunner level running through hallways and retrieve the *weapon* aka new your new AI. I'll get into her later. After you're out of that mission you have free reign on the ring free roaming and doing missions. At first its really fun doing the side missions. You have a lot of different ways of setting up how you're gonna tackle these missions, like what weapons you're gonna bring etc. This doesn't last however. Another thing I liked was fighting the banished it was nice tackling covenant 2.0 rather than prometheans is a definite improvement. The valor system is alright, it gets really good when you unlock the scorpion and you finally have a good weapon for dealing with all the outposts. Another improvement was the boss fights, man they are tough and give you an actually feeling of accomplishment when you beat them. The new armor upgrades are great the grappling hook is essential for getting around and dodging attacks the sensor is also a welcomed upgrade, but the evade and drop shield are not really used at all they're just not really useful. That's really all I have to say about the good stuff.Now for the bad:The dialogue between the characters is off at times and wrong at others. There are too many times where they try to make jokes but they're all bad, but not cringe worthy but a roll your eye type. The real problem is that isnt halo to me. Your new AI which says these bad jokes all the time and kills the mood. She's overly optimistic and cheery barely has seriousness, but I liked it when Cortana was serious and made sarcastic jokes. Old Cortana gave seriousness when it was need and would crack a wise one when appropriate. Honestly the new AI doesn't add any gravity to the situation when it should be like damn we lost Earth, Cortana, the Infinty, all the Spartan, the Navy now we gotta rebuild and be a badass. Seriously she kills the mood for me. The entire campaign when chief plugs her into a terminal its the same conversation, she says something like "this is so easy" but then it turn out to not be and Chief says the same line 10 times "Is there a problem?" and its a 50/50 everything is alright or its not but its the same conversation. Also the pilot is also kinda annoying he's not great but I have less problems with him since hes more of side character.Next is the open world. At first its nice and refreshing but then turns into far cry real quick. Its the same exact outpost/mission every time, no nuance no cool mechanics your plain and dry open world experience. Other than you can at least unlock the wasp and fly around and decimate every mission from afar so at least you're not spending a ton of time at each. Honestly they should've focused on the campaign more. The campaign is not terrible but not good either. I get they were trying to show Chief's Humanity through a simple story but halo isn't a simple story. Halo 2 you go from Space to Earth to Halo to High Charity. You're saving the galaxy but this story doesn't have any of that. YOU PLAY THE EXACT SAME LEVEL OVER AND OVER. If you like playing through forerunner hallways and then walk into a big open room with enemies then you'll love this. You play that over and over it's half the campaign. Other half is fighting the banished and fighting through their buildings or in the open world which isnt much better. I get staying on the ring is the deal but come on. They copied and pasted the levels with little thought behind them. Why not sneak onto another Banished ship, maybe find the wreckage of Infinity on the ring god I wish the campaign levels were more interesting but they're not. Another terrible mechanic about the levels is that they make you do this stupid grab the power core and go plug it in to open a door over and over, that is just bad game design.Lastly the story. The entire time I was really missing Cortana, I was like this new AI sucks, maybe someway they will bring Cortana back or maybe the new one will turn into Cortana and be more normal and less cheerful and happy all the time. Surprise surprise she is a copy of Cortana and doesn't change. The story also confused me a bit. I really thought we would see the flood again, seeing as they mentioned the flood was on the ring. Nope no flood instead something worse. The endless? Which they never explained what they are. Just they're reviving them and we need to stop them. The only good parts are killing Escharum and the Harbinger because they're the only good antagonists. Its also such a short campaign plays more like a dlc than a full campaign. Its better than 5 for sure, but still a let down for sure. This is all my opinion tho so do with that what you will.

_childDocuments_.review: Look I'll be straight forward, only reason I'd recommend it is because it's free so why not. That's it. This game has countless bugs and glitches even today, being able to shoot through walls, bullet delay, random fps drops, which, aren't too bad in the long run. The worst part is Gameplay and Content. Every single previous Halo game in the past decade has had a plethora of game modes, Swat, Grifball, Forge, BTB, Warzone, Warzone Firefight, Breakout, Fiesta, I could go on forever. Halo Infinite, has quite literally...the bare minimum. BTB, Slayer, Fiesta and Tactical Slayer (Swat). Not only is the gameplay aspect lacking, but the key reason for playing so often in previous games was to earn points or credits to buy packs for Spartan Armor or just buy Spartan Armor. Earning your armor is literally, Impossible in this game. Not to mention, even if you feel so inclined to spend, let's say, 15 USD on an armor bundle, chances are it's either going to be a crappier rendition of old Halo Reach Armor, or an ugly new part for the MK 7 armor. Just to add up the ridiculousness of this game, not only did I have to spend 15$ just for the Hazop helmet, but I also have to pay an extra 10$ just for the helmet attachment I want. Instead of just going and painting my Spartan red in like other Halo games, I now have to spend 5$ just for the color red which not only does it color certain parts of the armor wrong, but I also have to wait weeks just for it to pop up in the store.It's a pathetic attempt by 343 in every way. And dont even get me started on the Campaign..

_childDocuments_.review: I actually do recommend this game to people all the time,  I will split this into two parts; Campaign and Multiplayer.Campaign (no spoilers):Campaign is one of the best in Halo. Listing them off in no particular order, the useless vehicles because grappleshot, the inability for marines to drive, bullet spongey brutes, grappleshot being the only useful utility outside of a few niche times, the monotone environment of the ring surface and repetitive layout of the interior areas, but the gameplay is dynamic, combat dialogue is hilarious, the soundtrack is next to Halo 2 in my favorites, and the storyline is great. Well worth the $60, especially as a long-time halo game and lore follower.Multiplayer:Multiplayer is where I get a bit sour. The base gameplay loop is fun, and for a free game it is fine. If this multiplayer was a separate franchise or debut series I would love it. Issue is that it’s Halo. People were on top of this game and giving it an unnecessary amount of praise on initial release because it was a major step up from the dumpster fires of 4 and 5, but the limited gamemode selection, map selection, awful desync, lack of forge, and emphasis on buyable cosmetics is not very good. YouTubers like Ascend Hyperion and the Act Man (among others) emphasize on all of these points.I will continue to play Infinite and I recommend you check it out if you haven’t.. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying the gameplay is very fun, and due to issues with my hands I can't game competitively on key board and this is really the only game with PvP I dont feel disadventaged  for using controller. However, the microtransaction system is complete garbage. And this is coming from a girl who sent over $1000 on Warframe on my PS4.For example. In this Halo, there are different types of armor cores, which have their own sets of different attachments. (Shoulder pads, helmets, chest pieces, etc) Okay, I can buy into that being because of clipping issues, I guess? But stylistically, the two primary cores Mark V and Mark VII arent that different. But you have to buy the season pass in order to get the Mark V, which Mark VII armor coats can't even be applied to. (Paint jobs. So you have to buy the $10 battle pass for the *opportunity* to spend $20 for ported armor and paint coatings they forced into the game for no reason other than a meaningless cash grab. Even armor coatings are exclusive to the specific armor cores. Which is crazy. I'm left with just the impression that Microsoft sees this as a cash grab opportunity and they need to fix it if they want a concurrent player base.

_childDocuments_.review: Im trying really hard to like this because im a long time Halo fan but I just cannot. I will try my best to list the things I like about it and dont like. Keep in mind that although it might be a good game on its own (separately from the Halo license) it is still a Halo game and so will be held to the same high standard that Halo set when it was at its peek. I believe that highest peek to be Halo 3 so it will be the one for reference.Visuals-Visually this game is beautiful, I am beyond happy that they have finally decided to ditch the awful visual design of Halo 4 and Halo 5: Guardians and have returned to the more traditional (simple but detailed) design of the original Halo games. The Spartan characters look awesome and the maps and vehicles look great. The guns are futuristic but far more believable and realistic. Although Halo is a SyFi game it has always been rooted in a realistic design to its militaries and their equipment/weapons. Halo Infinite appears to return to that classic design philosophy and does it well. The only issues I have with the visuals is the HUD in game. It is cluttered and stuffed into the bottom corners of the screen and is a bit hard to read in a intense situation. My other issue is.. WHY CAN I NOT SEE MY FEET??? Every Halo since Halo 2 has had visible feet/legs when you look down but for some reason this one does not, inexcusable and unacceptable. Needs to be fixed.Sound Design-Unfortunately the visuals is really the only thing that Halo Infinite really has going for it. Although it has returned to the classic visual design of the original Halo games, the same cannot be said for the sound design and most of the music. Although the sound design is crisp and of high quality it lacks the iconic sounds that Halo set in its lifetime. All of the sounds in this game are highly realistic and believable but for me that is part of the problem. It feels like they were so focused on making the sounds realistic that they forgot how iconic and recognizable all of the weapons, vehicles and equipment sounded. Throughout my time playing this game I have had an extremely hard time telling weapons apart in terms of sound. Even the Needler, which has one of the most recognizable sounds of any game weapon, is difficult to distinguish from the other weapons being fired in a firefight. Even in a controlled environment the weapons lack the distinguishing sound that allowed a player to figure out who has what weapon just by hearing it. I played the sound difference for a few friends who are also long time Halo fans and they couldn't even tell what weapon it was until I had to tell them. The same can be said for the vehicles, the Warthog went from its original vehicle sounds to a generic gun-truck sound, from the engine to the horn and the turret on the back. The plasma weapons also all sounded very similar and indistinguishable from one another. That's the best way I can describe the sounds in this game, generic. The weapons, vehicles and environment all sound like they could come from any COD or Battlefield generic shooter game. The AI voices, although a unique choice, gave me a heavy feeling of playing something like Destiny more than Halo. Most of the notifications from the in-game announcer have now been replaced by your Spartan AI companion, for me this was off putting and as stated before made me feel more like I was playing Destiny rather than Halo. Gameplay - The gameplay falls behind its predecessors. I honestly am not sure where to start with this one. Everything from the gunplay to the movement and player/vehicle physics seems like it was rushed through with little thought. The guns feel as if they have little impact or power behind them and are more akin to toy weapons. The player movement is floaty and light, Halo has had some floaty gameplay before however as a player I felt very light and as if I had almost no weight to me. The vehicles are the same way, one turn too strong or a grenade can easily flip your Warthog and send you rolling into a wall. For some God forsaken reason they still have to have sprint implemented into the game. I have never been a fan of sprint in Halo but this has to be the worst rendition of it. This version of sprint gives you a barely noticeable speed boost, im sure most of us have seen the comparison videos between normal running and sprint in Halo Infinite. After playing it is definitely obvious that sprint does not give a big speed boost at all, that makes me wonder however. Why even have it in the game then? For me it feels more like they are trying to keep it to appeal to audiences coming from games like COD or Battlefield while also appealing to Halo fans. This ultimately makes sprint almost useless and unnecessary to have in the game. Time to Kill is odd and inconsistent , when attacking enemies they seem to be fairly durable and their shields hold up well. When being attacked however (even by a pistol) the shields seem to fail quickly and health beyond that is almost non-existent. The same can also be said in reverse, where I have sometimes felt fairly tanky while enemies will melt quickly. Many times I have felt more like I was playing COD rather than Halo just because of TTK. Music - So far from what I have heard, the music barely shows homage to the original titles. When you load up the game it opens up to a beautiful classic Halo theme and plays through the choir, though after the choir has sung their part of the Halo theme it quickly goes into some new music. This inst necessarily bad on its own, but the music that it transitions to is lack luster. There is not much that the new music contains to separate it from other generic SyFi game/movie/show sound tracks. Coming back to those iconic sounds the original Halo games had, Halo Infinite just drops the ball. Customization/Battle PassI will be lumping these two together because VERY unfortunately 343 has decided to lock ALL of the customization options behind the beyond awful battle pass. Not only is a battle pass a terrible thing to have in Halo but it has to be the worst battle pass I have ever seen. All customization options are locked behind it. Colors? Locked, you now cannot customize your own colors, you have to unlock an armor paint/skin/camo from the battle pass and equip it, you cannot even change the color tint of any piece of armor. Armor? Locked, there is no legitimate in game way to unlock any pieces of armor. It is now all locked in the battle pass, all of the iconic classic armor pieces and new cool armor pieces arent even free, you are forced to pay for the battle pass if you want any of the awesome armor that you customized your previous Spartans with in Halo before. Emblems? Locked, not only are emblems locked behind the battle pass the same as everything else, but now you cant edit them aside from a specific set of color patterns for an emblem. No more picking what emblem you have, no more unique emblem colors, no more custom emblem backrounds, no more cool emblem combos such as Cowboy Chief, Dead Cowboy, Hidden Elite Emblem or any other cool combinations anyone could create. Now they are all preset in design and in color. The battle pass is beyond disgusting and unforgivable and having the Infinite Multiplayer be free to play is nothing more than a pathetic excuse to suck more money out of loyal Halo fans and forcing us to pay for features we already had in previous Halo titles. I would rather pay full price for a Halo game that has everything up front. I will leave all of this here as I plan to continue playing Halo Infinite, I will return to edit any changes or additions that I might have but for now this is my take on Halo Infinite. As it stands Halo Infinite in my eyes is a 3/10. Long time Halo fans looking for Halo to finally make its comeback, im sorry but 343 has failed once again. I wish they hadnt but for some reason they just cannot grasp what makes Halo unique and fun to play. Rating - 3/10

_childDocuments_.review: Revision January 28th 2024 : So, as of today, there have been numerous new updates in season 4 and season 5 that bump my score up to a 7/10. Game has been vastly improved in terms of it's multiplayer offering and I am having a really fun time with this game. Too little too late, I understand. But, they have added a wealth of content that makes me give this game a 7/10. If you're looking for a fun multiplayer experience for free, there's pretty good value here. Halo Infinite. What can I say about this game? Quite a lot. But I will keep it brief. A few disclaimers first. I am not a die hard halo fan. I played through the Masterchief collection back in 2021 which I felt was dated but was a great package for those new to the Halo franchise. I was looking forward to playing the next instalment in the franchise in that year. I'm a fan of first person shooters and especially science fiction futuristic type of shooters. I played this game first on a 1650Ti laptop through game  pass and then eventually, when it went on sale for about $49.99 I outright purchased it as I had a new 6750XT desktop system to run it at higher settings. I played through the campaign and have over 100 hours on the game total at the time of this review. For multiplayer, I don't care about forge and I also don't buy any battle passes. I also never played coop.The good : The campaign. It's a good story. Not extravagant. Not out of the world. Not going to shatter any records or break any new ground. It's just good with an open world to explore and some excellent cutscenes. Voice acting is very good and it's a joy playing as the masterchief. Could it have been better? Absolutely and it really should have been for a franchise this old. Weapons : The guns feel and look and sound good. Good variety of vehicles to use in the campaign to get around. The grapple hook, to me, counts as a weapon and that is an excellent addition to this franchise and is perfect for the masterchief's arsenal. I personally think the AR is the best version of it out of all of the Halo games. Upgrading : You can upgrade your suit which is nice. You have a nice tac map to access upgrades and find your way around the map. Game play : The core gun play, animations, traversal, and the way the game generally plays in it's combat and manoeuvring is really well done here and definitely one of the high points. It's more advanced than the prior Halo games but just modern enough to please old and new fans. Soundtrack : Soundtrack is very good. Stays faithful to the original games music but also brings out a more modern flair. I have some of the tracks on my spotify just like the old games. I would say the old games music was better, but that's because those are timeless classics that are very hard to top. The Bad : Graphics : This was a very tough call to make. There are many moments where this game is absolutely beautiful. Such as when you stare at the Zeta Halo ring with the sun setting behind it, or the sun rising behind it. The lighting is gorgeous, some of the environments look very nice...but it's all very surface level. There are no different biomes. Some pop in occurs, things in the distance look grey, dull, and unrendered. Zooming in reveals some unfinished textures. Trees look great from a distance, but once you get close you realize some of the details are off. The night time in this game is beautiful. Masterchief and cortana looks very good. Enemies look good. Overall, it looks and feels like halo....but not 2021 Halo. It looks like a mid range 2015 Xbox One release...not a next generation Xbox Series X release like it should. Maybe Horizon Forbidden West spoiled me, but that's no excuse. Some of the environments in previous Halo games like Halo 4 and 5 look better here. I can still forgive some of these things if it weren't for the performance issues at these rather "very average graphics with some stand out moments."Performance : So on my 1650Ti laptop the performance was not the best but I could still get a fairly steady 60fps average at medium to high settings at 1080p. On my 6750XT I was getting about 90 - 120FPS on maxed out settings at 1080p. This is absolutely garbage performance for a game that has very average looking graphics. I think this is due to the slip space engine. I have riva tuner, vsync, freesync, and graphics and frame rate caps adjusted to give me a smooth near stutter/tear free experience today, but at stock settings without much fiddling around, this game had many micro and macro stutters that I feel are inexcusable for a game of this calibre and history. Not much else to say here besides the overall performance of this game is disappointing.Side Quests : I don't think there are any side quests. You kill some "most wanted" style enemies which are fun to find and kill. Some boss battles are quite interesting and fun but nothing too grandiose. You do have some collectibles scattered throughout the map. You also have random enemy encounters and bases to complete. You also have trapped fellow marines to rescue. Other than the standard open world offering, there isn't much else. Fairly standard here. Once it's done, it's done. I think you can still replay some high value targets but not much else to do.Multipayer : Fun to play at launch but that was OK because it played really well, was still in beta, was free to play for everyone, and the other games were trash such as BF2042 and Vanguard. Performance was average but the core gun play and game play was there and was a very nice treat for old and new fans. However, the multiplayer was missing tons of features at launch like being able to select just specific modes such as slayer or team slayer. You also didn't have any skills tracking or a ranking mode to track your progress. Everything was tied to the battle pass system which wasn't too bad because it never expires and it was only about $9.99 CAD. However, it was the only form of progression and that was a huge disappointment for me. I don't care much about forge but that wasn't in the launch game. Lack of content like maps and being able to customise your spartan like you could in prior games was also a big loss. The store was also disappointing as lots of the items were locked away and you had to buy it separately for ridiculous prices. Long story short, the multiplayer was not pay to win by any means, but it was riddled with micro transactions and overall lack of content once the game was released. Today at the time of this review, lots of these issues are resolved but it's too little too late. Verdict : Not a bad game but not great. I rate it a 6/10 overall. There are some fun moments. Campaign is fun to play through once. Once you finish all the side missions on the map (there aren't that many to do), there isn't much else to do besides explore around and fight the same enemies over and over again. If you want to buy this game, It's hard to recommend it any price point above $49.99 CAD. There are many games out there that are just plain better to play.

_childDocuments_.review: It might surprise you to hear that Halo Infinite does not remind me of “the good old days”. As someone who has been playing Halo for their entire life and has even written a series of reviews on each of the games, I find that I take a mostly nostalgic stance. Halo Infinite feels like more of an evolution in some ways, and utter regression in others. It’s a game with a fresh but familiar face; the fundamentals are all here. Everything surrounding those fundamentals, however, is rushed, cut down, or otherwise not present at launch.As scaffolding, as a structure for 343i to build upon, Halo Infinite is a massive success. The art direction is a masterful blend of the new and the nostalgic. The sound design is crisp and envelops the ear in immersive ambience. The core gameplay loop is a nearly perfect innovation upon the Bungie-era sandbox. Reworked armor abilities such as the grappling hook and repulsor fit neatly into the physics-driven sandbox that Halo has always thrived in. This is Halo gameplay at its best, both in the multiplayer and in the campaign.So, what’s the issue? 343i created an excellent platform for the game, and that’s about where they stopped. The campaign’s level design, world design, and storytelling are all created in service to the core gameplay at the cost of fidelity, variety, and meaning. Halo Infinite’s multiplayer utterly lacks gamemode diversity and will for months after launch. The progression system is utterly parasitic; it tugs at your wallet and your frustrations more than your desire to play.Halo Infinite as a live service platform was a poisoned chalice from the start. Locking cosmetics behind a paywall is one thing, but advertising the cosmetics as “obtainable for free” at E3 and then slapping those same cosmetics in a $20 bundle is another thing entirely. I’m not sure what everyone expected when they said the multiplayer would be free to play; with games like Planetside 2 and Destiny 2 as its peers, Halo Infinite was sure to be rigged.As someone with a fervent love of the earlier titles, I find Halo Infinite to be disappointing. Halo Infinite’s campaign is written to be an apology for Halo 5 above all else, and that denudes the game of any sort of self-contained finale to Master Chief’s story. So much time is spent on the Banished and their control over the ring, but very little of that time is spent actually explaining what happened in the story.You know a game’s story is bad when the final cutscene of the game mentions that there are many mysteries that we still don’t understand. To clarify, I’m not opposed to open-ended storytelling; I’m opposed to spending an entire game teasing mysteries that are then aggressively not solved by the time the credits roll. Halo Infinite will absolutely get single player expansion content, because what’s on offer now does not offer any closure, or even much story at all. Chief is sad about Cortana still, there’s a guy who wants to leave the ring, and the Banished are all over the ring. Almost nothing in that initial pitch changes by the time the credits roll.I don’t want a Halo game that treats me like a baby and answers every question instantly. I want a Halo game that is self-contained like the previous games and has an actual story arc. Halo Infinite fails to tell its story in the broad strokes, so it relies on individual moments which can vary in effectiveness. The new characters are, for the most part, welcome and provide roles new to Halo storytelling. This seemingly came at the cost of creating something with an unbroken, self-contained story arc.Perhaps the arc of the ring itself is what matters more anyways. When it comes to Zeta Halo, what you see is what you get. It’s rolling green hills and mountains, with some points on the map to do silly little tasks. The moment-to-moment gameplay is, again, the most dynamic in the series, but I thought that we as a gaming collective had moved on from Far Cry 3 checklist design. The world design is utterly soulless; open the open world map, clear the fort, pick up collectibles and move on. There isn’t any identity to the forts you clear, squads you save, or bosses you kill because they all use the same tilesets. There is a stunning lack of diversity in the open world. I kept saying to myself, “I can’t wait until I’m in a desert, or in a snow biome, or a swamp” all the way until the credits rolled and that didn’t happen.The open world often funnels the player into self-contained missions similar to the structure of the original games. These missions reminded me a lot of Warframe; I ran down some gray hallways, shot a lot of dudes, had fun, and instantly forgot about the level once I got out. There is no living memory to the endless Forerunner halls in my brain because 343i did not diversify these levels in any meaningful way. Some are a bit more red, some have lasers and big hallways, and sometimes they are blue. As someone who treasures the levels of previous games, even some in 343i’s catalog, I am left wanting more.In fairness, to reiterate, the fundamentals are all here. The AI is shockingly smart and fun to fight. Animation work on The Banished is nothing short of an achievement; so much life was breathed into the grunts, elites, and the brutes that I’m left staggered. The weapons, new and old, are solid to use and retain their own utility. New armor abilities like the grappling hook allow the player to manipulate the environment in ways that capture that spartan power fantasy we all know and love. It’s a strong foundation, but everything around that foundation is weaker than previous titles.If the campaign doesn’t land for you like it didn’t for me, you can always play the multiplayer. Thankfully, 343i have crafted an utterly unmatched sandbox in Halo Infinite’s multiplayer. It’s an almost nonstop highlight reel of vehicle collisions, grappling hook plays, and long-range snipes. The maps and gamemodes were clearly designed to cut down on monotony, with objectives that move throughout the map and points of interest (such as power weapon spawns). This results in a gameplay rhythm that feels different from match-to-match, and moments of victory and defeat that feel truly earned. 343i clearly designed the multiplayer with a delicate hand, and their hard work was worthwhile. It’s a shame about the game modes though.One facet of the multiplayer’s design that leaves a lot to be desired is the use of vehicles. Vehicles are now dropped in via airship at points of interest and at team spawns, but heavier vehicles like tanks are only dropped on rare occasions. I’ve played around 40 hours of the multiplayer, and I think I’ve seen a tank 2 times. Something in these back-end dials needs to be adjusted, because there really needs to be more heavy vehicles to create that “Big Team Battle” vibe.The multiplayer arrived weeks ago, but it feels stale to me already due to a lack of map variety and gamemode variety at launch. This criticism will ultimately become meaningless as time goes on, since 343i has clearly stated that more content is on the way, but it’s worth noting that the game launched with a middling number of maps and a tiny pool of game modes to choose from.A solid metric for defining a game’s subjective value is the duration that a game remains in your memory. Halo Infinite was one of my biggest excitements of the year before launch, and after rolling the credits on the campaign I’ve all but forgotten about it. Halo fans are still in that masturbatory “a new halo game released” phase, but I feel that with time people will see Halo Infinite’s faults more clearly. It’s a game that’s fun, but I ultimately did not love it. The campaign is not worth $60, and the multiplayer will be more worth playing as time goes on and when the progression system is inevitably fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: The Halo Infinite Multiplayer has absolutely taken the gaming world by storm and for good reason. Between Call of Duty Vanguard and Battlefield 2042’s awful or mediocre launches Halo Infinite comes right out of the gate swinging.The multiplayer is a mix of both the OG Halo Arena Shooter formula that made Halo amazing back in the day and fresh and polished new tweaks, weapons, abilities, gear, and more that truly create a modern Halo experience.And the first thing I want to talk about is just core Arena Shooter experience because a lot of people either aren’t super familiar with it or they only know it from halo but Arena Shooters are absolutely one of my favorite type of fps game of all time.It pretty much means that everyone starts a match with the same exact weapons, and a big part of the experience is about map control. And the reason it’s all about map control is because crazy powerful weapons and abilities will spawn every so often on a timer so if you know the maps and know where the weapons spawn you can consistently try to make sure you are the one getting to use the powerful weapons. So when I’m playing on a map where powerful sniper rifles spawn you bet you I’m going to try and grab them as soon as they spawn and then absolutely decimate the opponents with them.And another huge thing about the core halo infinite experience is the high time to kill. A lot of people complain about this but it makes it so much fun to actually have the back and forth battles where someone doesn’t die in 2 seconds. Don’t get me wrong I like super fast paced arcade shooters like COD but being in these super intense firefights with opponents and then meleeing them to finish them off is the most satisfying feeling on the planet.And meleeing is a huge part about this game so if you want a easy beginners tip to do well, always shoot at the enemy a bit and then if you are close enough try to finish them off with a melee. It’s the most fun thing on the planet and its the optimal thing to do haha.And so overall, if you’ve played the previous games in the Halo franchise, and by that I mean the older ones not Halo 4 or 5 and you enjoyed them you are going to have a blast in this game. The gameplay is so freaking solid, the game itself is the most polished triple A game I think I have ever played recently, I am very happy the game got delayed a couple times, and it just feels so much fun to play and that's the most important thing ever.The main things you can do in multiplayer is que for a 4v4 quick match which shuffles all of the base game modes which is nice but it also means that if you don't like a certain game mode sucks for you. So as an example I don't know why but in every game I’ve ever played I hate capture the flag. Don’t know why I just do, so I would love if you could deselect any game modes you want. Also there is no way to just play slayer which is just TDM and I personally like objective based game modes but there are a lot of people that clearly just want a slayer or team swat mode based on how many randoms don't play the objective. All the gamemodes that are in the game are unique tho and what you would expect from Halo.You also have big team battle which can have 24 players in these gigantic large scale battles with tons of vehicles, weapons, and more and it’s just such a fun large scale way to mess around in. Definitely gives me battlefield vibes with the increase in players in this version.And you also have your stereotypical ranked mode for everyone wanting to climb the MMR ladder and stuff like that. And with the game being free to play, which frankly is absolutely amazing I just want to say, there is a battle pass system to get the armor customization you would expect from a Halo game. And at launch it was extremely grindy and there where a lot of complaints about it so they made it a bit better with some changes but it is still on the grindy side. And I would say that was the worst thing on the planet but 343 is doing something that I truly think needs to be the future of battle passes. The battle pass will never ever expire and even if you don't buy it but in a year you want to buy it you can buy any previous battle pass and complete it.So it still gives you something to work towards but you don't feel like you need to make the game your second job and get super stressed that you wont be able to get everything in time which I think is a huge freaking plus.And so overall I just have to say that Halo Infinite is one of the best multiplayer fps games I have played in a longgggg time. I have been waiting for the perfect fps game to come out to make me feel like a kid again and it is 100% this game. I don’t normally play the campaign in my fps games but if the campaign’s quality is anything like its multiplayer I may have to check it out.And if you liked this review then follow my   for more stuff like this!

_childDocuments_.review: As 343i make delay for season roadmap, they totally screwed themselves up that they need more time to make improvements right. Limited mode's in the Multiplayer is also a bit of an issue right now. The modes need to be consolidated a bit more, especially since the challenges require some certain game types to be played. Even though the season last until may, the whole appeal to halo is a relaxed shooter with all the customization. Unfortunately, obtaining anything threw the season pass is slow, and is separated between two armor sets, and soon a third. Which limits what little customization there is already.Ultimately, the game is fun, i've enjoyed countless hours on it already with friends, with a little balancing of the pass, and some changes to how the flow of the game works it'll be even better. =)

And things began to look a lot brighter. By no means was the game perfect, but the future seemed to hold a lot of promise. The developers were much more open with their shortcomings, much more public and transparent about what they were working on behind the scenes. Flash forward to today, Season 5's launch day. It's a night and day difference. Everything looks, plays, and feels so much better. There are things to work for, reasons to keep coming back, and the community has never been stronger. If you can think of a gamemode, odds are it's been made and is populated in Forge. And if it isn't, you can probably make it yourself with relative ease. Season Five marks a New Golden Age (hopefully) for the Halo franchise and 343i. If you've made it this far into the review, please install (or re-install!) this game and give it another try.

_childDocuments_.review: A title that I so desperately wanted to be great. One that I would be playing for years and years on end. That did not come to be though as the game went through development hell and 343 seemingly becoming worse and worse at making Halo titles. The campaign's narrative was very weak and incredibly generic, and frankly making the campaign open world did nothing but screw with the pacing and smother me with monotonous busy work. I feel like mission design for campaign missions as well was hampered by having to work or be apart of the open world, and that nothing about the environment in the open world is varied or interesting. I will say on the upside though I found the AI in general in this game to be fantastic, and if there was one team worth keeping in 343 it would be those behind the AI. It felt like 343 finally did something better than Bungie did with their games. As well as during those curated story missions they did have, I felt like they had great enemy placement and pacing that just felt "right". The core gameplay loop of Halo is here, and it feels the most "Halo" out of all 343 entries but it flubs everything else besides that. I also want to touch on music real quick, because Halo has been known for its soundtrack, and I find it to be an important aspect of Halo. The music in this game is just one big nothing burger, no tracks stood out or enhanced my experience and are just a much weaker derivative of the original series score. Which is really disappointing to see because 343 has made a great soundtrack before in Halo 4, it was very different from Marty's scores, but it had an identity of its own and elicited a sense of mystery and felt much more alien than any track that could be found in the originals. To see 343 going so safe with the soundtrack was really disappointing and left it feeling unmemorable.Multiplayer, I would say the heart and soul of Halo, in every single mode in Halo you could play it with a friend. Except this one, Co-op campaign didn't release alongside the game but was instead delayed. It wasn't a short delay either it was delayed for almost a full year, and even then they cancelled local Co-op, something they said they would never do. I wish that was the only thing missing, but Forge, Firefight, and many multiplayer gamemodes were absent from the games release, but with the "promise" that they would be coming "later". But given that it took them multiple weeks to get slayer added as a sole matchmaking option, it hasn't inspired confidence that we would get those features and modes in a time frame where the game would still be relevant. Its been 2 years and many of these features have not yet returned. I have enjoyed the multiplayer that is here and there is alot of room for skill expression and truly feels like an evolution in moment to moment combat, but that doesn't change the fact that there is no meat on these bones.Customization/Monetization is clearly where 343 put most of their time into, as it was the main recurring revenue driver. This game unless you are willing to shell out hundreds of dollars is the halo game with the weakest customization to date, most of the cool cosmetics are locked behind battle passes and Infinite's in-game shop, but even then they cycle out the in-game shop every week making you have to come back every week to the game in order to have the chance of purchasing the cosmetic you've been eyeing. There were very few campaign cosmetics, none of which were tied to achievements or difficulty and not a single one was armor piece. They were only camos and victory poses, all of which paled in comparison to the ones that could be found in the battle passes and in-game shop. Even with their premium offerings I can't recreate the colors that my spartan has been using for decades in all the prior titles.343 should just take the L and start over. Just don't get this game, its not worth your time, and frankly its not worth 343's time.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; Awesome gameplay and visuals but there is nearly no individuality when it comes to customization so don't expect to get anything without paying and even then don't expect to get much for a fair price. There is no longer merit based earning and anyone young or poor won't fully be able experience to the game and will be left out. I've already heard people insulting others for wearing defaults. This will only slow the growth of the fan base and leave poor impressions on both the game and the community. Your in game appearance no longer shows the effort and time spent in the game but instead only shows how much money you have and are willing to spend.I love the game. It fells good to play and looks beautiful. It has its bugs and needs some rebalancing but none of that bothers me. In time the game will be even better I'm sure. Already it's better than 4 and 5 to me. However I can't recommend it with a clear conscious because it is extremely money hungry. It's frankly disgusting especially compared to any of the previous games which has little to no in game purchases. It's even worse because of the dishonesty about customization before launch. It's all presets and almost all paid for and almost none of it is interchangeable. Some items such as visors and colors are nearly identical.An example for how money hungry they are is you have to pay $15 for one armor piece and 4 of the exact same emblem. The armor piece cant be used on any other armor core or armor kit and the emblems are duplicates because you can't use one on multiple items, it is unlocked for one vehicle, weapon or armor core only. So basically $15 for 2 items than can only be using in specific circumstances. None of those items also can be bought separately to lower the cost of the one item you actually want.Also it takes about roughly 2000 games at 50xp each to max out the battle pass or you can pay about $400 USD for XP Boosters or $328 if you bought the premium battle pass. (If my math is correct)On the battle pass Identical left and right armor pieces are separate and unlockable at different levels to give the illusion you're unlocking more. If you do the free battle pass then almost all you'll be able to unlock is challenge swaps which are only useful to gain more XP for faster battle pass progression which gets you more swaps because you aren't paying so really you're unlocking practically nothing without paying. The only positive things I can say about the battle pass/progression/customization system (since they are all practically the same thing sadly) is the base battle pass cost is $10 and I think that's a good price for a battle pass as well as the supposed ability to unlock previous battle passes and their times after the new seasons have started with no deadline.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game for too long now and have finally uninstalled. The game play itself is incredible, by far my favourite modern FPS game, way less cringe than COD, better movement than CSGO, more technical gunfights than pretty much anything else on the market. Most of the maps have a very distinct style. The weapons and power ups are well-balanced, and you can do creative ♥♥♥♥ like repulsing rockets and grenades, sticking someone with a plasma and repulsing them off the map, grapplehooking to the top of the map and sniping enemies from the air... and I could go on, there really are a huge amount of possibilities, and I've had so many great memories and exhilirating moments in Infinite. Pulling off sick shots with the S7 sniper is the most dopamine I've ever gotten from a video game, period.But the game is also a broken piece of ♥♥♥♥. The campaign is awful, with a tedious plot, poorly written dialogue, and almost no variation across environments. If you are playing outside of the US or Europe the servers are absolute garbage, even if you do find a game you will load in and then the match will just immediately end (and it's only a bit better within the US and Europe). The monetization of the shop reflects the very worst instincts of modern AAA studios. It took the devs two years to get the game to the point it should have been at at launch, and now the population is pretty much dead and nobody cares. 343 reneged on its promise of seasonality, taking it from a traditional paid game, to a live service, to a game that barely gets any new content. The matchmaking is horrible, you will be punished with unwinnable games and then handed cheap victories. If you get good at the game your teammates will be so useless, especially in 4 v 4s, that you have to solo carry if you want a chance of winning. The more time and effort you put into the game, the more it will punish and disappoint you.Although they mostly get the blame, I don't think any of this is really 343s fault: Microsoft is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ corporation headed by a relentless ♥♥♥♥: they bought up the Halo franchise, drove it into the ground through sheer mismanagement, squeezed as much money as they could out of its corpse, and then turned their attention to the next game, which I'm almost certain will release unfinished and with a very expensive shop attached. They've been buying up and destroying studios across the map, setting a precedent for malpractice that Sony have only been happy to follow. In short, Infinite represents the very best and worst of modern AAA gaming. The technology and the mechanics are excellent, showcasing the kind of complex interactions that you can get from contemporary game design. But these developments in design are unfortunately tied to selfish, greedy corporations who don't care about creating a sustainable franchise that people will want to return to for decades; all they care about is squeezing as much money out of the player base as quickly as possible. This isn't the kind of game, or the kind of game company, that I want to support with my money or attention anymore.

_childDocuments_.review: At first the hype for this game was real. As a Halo veteran, first playing Halo:CE on the XBOX on release, I was looking forward to the first 'proper' Halo game in over a decade. When the beta came out early, me and all of my friends were spamming the download button, restarting Steam every 5 minutes when the servers weren't letting us download, and when it finally was working, we stared at the downloads screen until it hit 100%. And then we got in game. Hours we played. So much fun was had, crazy across the map snipes, shooting grenades on the ground to kill the enemies standing beside them, all that sweet Halo sandbox goodness. It was such a good base to build the game off of! The gameplay was fun and we were looking forward to what came next when the game released!Flash forward 4 months and the game hasn't changed at all. The biggest change they made was to remove the reticle going red when you're looking at an enemy. Why? Because of the hackers that riddle this game due to the fact there is absolutely no anti-cheat whatsoever. Did removing the reticle work? Not in the slightest, hackers are still in 25% of the lobbies you'll be in...The micro-transactions are egregious and massively overpriced (£8 for a helmet from a 12 year old game?! £5 for the colour blue?! What the actual f***.). The absence of classic Halo game modes is glaring as currently there are only about 6 to choose from (and you can't even choose exactly what game mode you want to play!). The custom games are completely broken and unusable as the games don't even start, the theatre mode works maybe 5% of the time, and forge isn't even there for the community to prop-up the piece-of-crap game the devs have released and done literally nothing to fix or supply with meaningful updates.The campaign is decent. It's fun flying around with the grapple hook, but it's just like every other generic open world game. Go here do this menial task, go there do that menial task, find the collectable, unlock 'upgrades' that are kind of pointless, etc, etc... They should have kept to the level-by-level formula of previous Halo games. The open world really ruins the pacing of the narrative. Speaking of the narrative, the writers did an okay job rectifying the awful stories of 4 and 5 but resort to exposition from a red hologram BBEG that you only see in-the-flesh one time at the end of the game and offers no threat unlike the 'LEGENDARY' Atriox who's, more-or-less, entirely absent from the game. Unfortunately they continue to try to peddle Cortana off as some kind of sci-fi waifu to the Chief which is just the most ridiculous decision ever made for this franchise.Another thing that 343 Industries gets wrong is the tone and feel of the setting. The art direction, honestly, is fantastic. Area variation is unfortunately lacking, however. Halo has always been a game of various settings. One mission you'll be in the bowels of a spaceship, the next you're in a tundra, the next you're in a desert, another you'll be in a snowy setting or a swamp, etc. This game rotates between green forest, silver interiors, and black/red interiors. The locations get stale very quickly.Another thing they seem to get wrong are the Covenant you will be sharing the world with. They almost feels like a caricature of the classic Halo games. The grunts have always been funny little weirdos that you just one-tap in the head in every Halo game, but in this game they feel a little too silly? They went from lovable cowards to straight up cartoon characters. The Brutes look far more humanoid now and less bestial, unfortunately, and because of that they've lost a lot of their original identity. The Elites are at their best since Halo: ODST yet still move sluggishly as if they're from Halo 4 and 5. The Hunters are back to being oppressive mini-bosses, and the brute chieftains often have cool arenas to fight in and are a genuine challenge on Legendary (which is probably the easiest Legendary of all the games except maybe 4).The marines are... Okay? First off, it's so good to have lovable, quippy, friendly AI marines back to accompany you on your journeys. But their AI can't drive vehicles anymore? And they remain glued to your ass constantly and don't move through an area without you? Both of which they've been able to do since Halo 2? Are these more limitations that forcing an open-world setting caused the game to have? Massively disappointing. Feels like you're babysitting most of the time... Loading them up into the Razorback with the OP upgraded skewer is very fun though. Makes Legendary an absolute cake walk.Honestly, the overall feel of the gameplay loop hearkens back to the classic, glory days of Halo. But, unfortunately, thanks to poor design choices, unenthusiastic (and probably overworked) game developers, outsourcing devs, along with predatory monetisation schemes that only take away from the Halo experience, it doesn't just fall short of its potential to be great, it absolutely nose-dives into failure.On a scale of 1 - 10, I give this a Not Good.

As for the campaign, while good, really struggles to capture the moment to moment magic of Bungie's Halo. They clearly felt more inspired here and there are some good elements at play. _childDocuments_.review: XP Progression needs to be fixed. Badly. Its insane they thought this was fine.I blew off two games to chase challenges, ignored my team and the objective just to get the challenge done. There's literally no incentive to not do this. It actually rewards better and encourages it. It doesn't matter if we win, lose, or if you're first or last on your team. At the end of the match, if you didn't complete your challenges, you get 0XP. Finish a match 25:0, top of the board, absolutely dominate, but fail to kill someone with a shock rifle? That's 0XP for you. Finish a match 1:25, bottom of the board, literally had no idea what game mode you were playing, but got that shock rifle challenge? Good, have 250XP. All it encourages is players logging in, chasing their daily challenge, regardless of the game, and logging out. Half your team will eventually just be completely detached from the match, because they've got no reason to want to help you at all. Its clear the decision was made to encourage you to use the $2 PER LEVEL "Boost" system, so I don't expect it will be going away since they need to farm those micro-transactions. Until they change the system to actually account for in-game score and things like kill-streaks and victory, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I can not in good faith recommend this game in its current state. Hit registration is some of the worst I've seen in a Halo game to date, monetisation is extremely predatory and insulting, updates are slow and content is non-existent. Especially with the new changes to server selection which have essentially ruined the game for non-American players. If you want a good Halo experience, go play MCC, it is in *infinitely* a much better state and is way more deserving of your time.The one feeling I had throughout my experience with the campaign was "eh". I guess its fine, but Halo hasn't seemed to make the transition from linear storytelling to open world unscathed. Missions feel much less cohesive and the pace has taken a huge hit in order to allow you to explore the world of Zeta Halo. It is an absolute shame that this world doesn't have more than 1 biome. The question I ask myself was "Why?". Halo has worked perfectly fine as a linear story experience for decades, and shifting to an open world has only hurt it.

_childDocuments_.review: Microtransactions and focus on the cash shop still stunt the potential of expressing yourself / customization.  Hope to see a turn around.  The spartan cores really contribute more to the stunt of this growth than the microtransactions yourself, think of it as a extra layer of greed.   Desync has been vastly improved since the games launch, however its still a issue here and there, but not as big as it once was.  Lag / server lag seems to be more common than desync now.   Xbox aim assist and PC is still noticeable and irritating but not game breaking.  Weapon Balance is a lot better than it used to be but still needs worked.  I know I mentioned lag before, but the first few months was really bad but its been mostly cleaned up.   There is now 11 game modes instead of like the original 3 so thats a vast improvement, but classics like Firefight, Infection, and Griffball are still not here if you're looking for those.  Personal opinion time:  Most of the maps are fine but there is a couple maps i just really hate, the original maps that launched with the game seem better designed but to small for 4v4 as spawning in can be a issue, but for the new maps that released from launch that isn't a issue anymore yet seem to lack good design.  Design being how much cover you can without someone from the other side of the map shooting you / how open you are, to how many paths you can take to get from point a to point b.   Though size isn't an issue anymore as i said before.  Really hoping for a focus on bettering customization, staying away from spartan cores and bringing cash items into future battlepasses.  Fomo doesn't suit Halo.  Hoping to have the 3 game modes listed above brought in preferably Warzone firefight without the cash aspect of it.  Assassination animations are still missing those were really cool. TLDR: Still rating a wouldn't recommend due to previous halo installations have been. This game could be so much better but it isn't.  But if customization, microtransactions, and lack of unique game modes from previous halo game modes don't bother you, than you'll probably enjoy the game.  But it is a lot better than what the game was at during launch.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is largely for the single-player portion of Halo Infinite:Infinite feels more like groundwork to a better game, which is an odd thing to say considering I saw credits on it and generally enjoyed myself. But there are huge swaths of missing narrative, characters who seem more important than they actually end up being, and a strangely truncated feel to the whole of the story, as well as a feeling of repetitiveness to its level design. It also can't quite justify the open-world in this outing, but you can see the makings of something great in that regard if the developers can come up with something more interesting than "take this fortified position" and "shoot this tower." The skill progresssion is also about as vanilla as they get, with none of the upgrades feeling particularly exciting.If you can get past that open world tedium, there's really something here under the surface. The grappling hook is one of the best additions to the series. The shooting feels bang-on, and I found a lot of different weapons I liked (though upgradeable ammo belts in the future would go a long way towards making me care about tracking down those special weapons). Without spoiling anything, the core story is a great way to reset things for the series while still keeping the familiarity of the universe intact.I'm not sure Infinite is going to be for everybody, especially if bland open worlds don't interest you. But when Infinite shines, it really shines, and I think that, in the end, outweighs its glaring troubles and lack of creative focus.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a story that every Halo fan is familiar with. 343 Industries, a studio spun up by Microsoft to be the stewards of the Halo IP going in the future, took over the franchise in 2011 after the departure of series creators Bungie. They then proceeded to drag the franchise and its fans through two sequels which, while not awful in totality, were proof that 343i had no clue what made Halo so special in an aesthetic nor a gameplay sense.  was seemingly meant to be the course correction for the Halo series in the modern era. It had the Bungie era aesthetics, music evocative of Marty O'Donnell's amazing scores, and a gameplay loop that brought the focus back to the sandbox. Weapons, vehicles, power ups, and equipment placed on the maps, equal starting loadouts, and a set of base abilities that blended old and new felt refreshing in an age of gaming where this kind of arena design was dead in the mainstream. Despite a solid foundation however, 343i's attempt at creating a live service ecosystem around what they had built was doomed from the start because of just how bare bones the launch game was.Critical features like campaign co-op, the custom game browser, and Forge mode did not ship at launch, split-screen co-op didn't launch at all, and the features that were initially included were half-baked or broken. The content updates were extremely slow to come out, utterly failing to keep the core community engaged as new maps trickled out at the slowest rate they had in the series history. The free 2 play cash shop and the battle pass system being the only meaningful ways to earn cosmetic items critically damaged the experience of the average player, a problem only made worse by a horrible armor coating system which disallowed players to change their armor colors as they saw fit. This combination of failures and downgrades made much of the community write off Infinite for good, seeing every update as too little, too late.Despite the general attitudes around the game, a hiring freeze that prevented new developers from coming onto the game to help fix it up, and a huge management shakeup that led to the previous studio heads departing from the company, 343i kept on working diligently to fix the game's issues. Pierre Hintze, the man who led the Master Chief Collection's amazing overhaul, taking over as the head of 343i has led to an incredible shift in priorities from the developers: building up on top of the solid foundation they already had by giving the community what they want.Halo Infinite is officially in comeback mode.The new developer-made maps are a huge improvement over the stock maps, finally allowing the arena game design to shine. The playlist rotations keep things fresh every week. Free events happen all the time, finally letting free players collect some great looking gear on a regular basis. Custom games are lively and full of tons of creativity. Forge mode is astoundingly powerful, with some forged maps looking indistinguishable from developer made maps. They've even started to implement the best of the community's maps directly into the matchmaking system, in both competitive and casual playlists. Shoutouts to the Squad Battle playlist.It's amazing to see how much better Halo Infinite actually is right now. Even in a gaming landscape where games launch broken and then somehow get even worse though post-launch updates, there are many reasons to be optimistic for the future of this game due to the dedication 343i has shown in the last several months. I hope that people will be able to give it a chance again, because if 343i stays the course, this could be one of the best Halo games of all time.
