_childDocuments_.review: One of the biggest disappointments in gaming. If anyone at Xbox had any sense, they'd hand the Halo franchise off to a different company. After 10 years of this crap, it's clear that 343i isn't going to change.Pros:> Campaign is decent. Not terrible, not amazing. It's repetitive, but it's a big improvement from whatever the heck Halo 5 was supposed to be.> When it works, the game is actually great fun to play. Movement feels good, shooting feels good. The fundamentals are solid and this is the only thing saving Halo Infinite from being a total dumpster fire. That said...Cons:> Less map variety than Halo: Combat Evolved from 2001. Numerous Halo staples are just flat out missing.> Worse overall gameplay experience than Halo 2 from 2004 due to horrendous desync. It has been 6+ months and this issue still hasn't been fully resolved.> No stats page.> Lackluster to nonexistent social features.> Launched without Forge. Was supposed to be added shortly after launch but keeps getting delayed. This has been a series staple since Halo 3 in 2007.> Customization is an insult. The devs flat out lied about being able to earn most cosmetics through playing the game. In reality, almost nothing is unlockable by playing. Everything is either in the store bundles or the battle pass.> Even after numerous price cuts, store items are still way too expensive.> Battle pass progression is horrible. _childDocuments_.review: The first game I ever remember playing when I was younger was Halo 3, so needless to say I am a big fan of classic Halo. But, I have to say Infinite has a very strong gameplay flow. I never find myself frustrated with sprint or mantle, I think the movement in particular has been executed very well. I find myself missing some of the old weapons (covenant and human), but I think all of the weapons have a place in the sandbox and I enjoy using most of them. Going back to the classic art style probably saved the franchise, and I am very happy with the looks of the weapons and the armor, (a few of the armor cores are a bit ridiculous). The sheer amount of armor customization was a breath of fresh air after Halo 5, and the only thing holding it back at this point is the lack of cross core customization. The progression system, haunts me in my sleep. Going with the battlepass style progression system is very lazy, and I find incredibly unrewarding. I find it hard to believe that any Halo game after Reach has looked even remotely different where unlocking armor and such is concerned, I don't have any suggestions other than follow what Reach did, it is universally loved. As much as I dislike the idea of spending real money on in-game cosmetics, I like the idea of a rotating item shop. But, I do not like the fact that half of the items I do not have unlocked, might come back to the store one day, and I might be online that week if I happen to catch it when it does, maybe??? Something needs to be done about that. The challenge based XP is so very frustrating to me. I like the idea of challenges, I always have, but they should be in addition to earning XP through simply playing matches and earning metals. If you get an overkill, or a killing spree during a match, you get XP based off each metal and it's difficulty/rarity to obtain. You should be rewarded for playing well. I have had an absolute blast with custom games thus far. Forge is undoubtedly the best of any Halo game to date, and I see room for it to grow and become even greater. If we can create out own content, this game will be in an amazing place. The lack of a pre-game and post-game lobby is very sad to me, it feels pretty much impossible to meet people and make friends without it. I know 343 worries about bad interactions with less than sanitary characters, but it certainly doesn't help the community, grow either way. Finally, the goofiest issue this game has, only because of how incredibly fixable it is, is the menu for selecting a mode in multiplayer. It absolutely blows my mind that they didn't take inspiration for the MCC, it is literally perfect in every way. The current one we have in Halo Infinite doesn't display everything at once, and it commits the biggest sin of them all, it's so incredibly boring. This game's menus need more character, and if you need help with that 343, look at Halo CE through Reach.I have very mixed feelings about this game as it currently stands, but there is no denying it's is in a far better spot than when it launched. If this is what the game is like after a year and then some, I believe it will be in a great spot in another year. I just hope 343 has their priorities straight, the wrongs need to be right before they keep adding content. Overall I think this game has fantastic potential.

_childDocuments_.review: I have never written a review for a game, but I'm making an exception here to try and warn people about the huge disappointment and cash grab this game is.If you are looking for you typical Halo experience, DON'T buy this game. While the game showed great promise, I believe it became absolutely disappointing taking into account the following:CAMPAIGN:-It promised instead of the linear story-line progression through different levels, an open world exploration. What you actually get is an empty world, with random scattered weapons, enemies and bases, where the story progression is thinned out throughout the world and consists of "go to far off base , kill all enemies defending base, kill bullet sponge boss, press button, get cut-scene, repeat", which makes you feeling less engaged with the game, and more bothered on how long it will take to drive to where you have to go.-There's no current co-op mode for the campaign, which is a HUGE aspect of the Halo franchise and makes absolutely no sense on a full released game.-The story is the most inconsequential so far, and even without considering how thin-spread it is all over the map, it really lacks much progression and ends up becoming pretty much just a dialogue without any significant event like in previous games.-The game glitches constantly, which shows poor polish in general.MULTIPLAYER:-Due to the lack of different levels on the campaign, or just lazy design, the multiplayer maps are barely different in design and end up pretty much looking the same, leaving out the multiple level designs that showed various alien worlds and aesthetics that were present in previous Halo games.-Battle pass... basically paying to be able to unlock armors in the game, which even then is a long grind to get, despite of performance during matches, basically unrewarding any attempt at being good at the game, and more rewarding on how much money and time are you willing to waste in game.FORGE:-No forge on release... The only good thing that I can say of this game, is that combat mechanics are fluid and graphics are great.So, to summarize, this game ends up leaving behind the dense story rich campaign, the various alien worlds and levels, the co-operative experience of fighting aliens with friends, and basically all that characterized the Halo experience... for what is a "barely" existing story and empty world campaign at a full AAA game price, and a blatant cash grab of a multiplayer that doesn't reward performance in any way.Just play the previous games. I'm only truly angry that I cannot ask for a refund because I wanted to give the game a chance. Don't make my mistake...

_childDocuments_.review: **Edited Review: The gameplay for this is fantastic, and while it is in a better state now, than a couple months after launch, if you were playing from the point of release, you know as well as I that the live-service aspect of this game has been poorly managed and frustrating to say the least. There are many game modes still missing from multiplayer, and it can feel "grindy" at times, but is better than it was. So while I can recommend this to others now, I think everyone should be aware of why people are upset with the management of this game, and that it doesn't take much to be better than rock bottom. If the gameplay wasn't so good, I would probably give this a HARD pass. FAR better to play with friends than alone.**Original ReviewI am a long-time Halo fan. I've loved this game series since it's inception on the original Xbox. Hell, I remember playing a demo of Halo: Combat Evolved at a Best Buy before it came out. However, I just can't recommend this. I've played this game for 8 hours on Steam, and I've played through the Campaign as well as some multiplayer on the Xbox Series X (about 30-40 hours at least). I found that the more I played, the more I realized the soul of what made Halo great is quickly disappearing. I'll admit, I'm not a pro, or a competitive player, but the multiplayer is just not fun. With the battle passes and challenges, it saps the fun people would normally have by just hopping on and playing a few random matches. They make it feel like work, and I feel guilty because I have bought 2 season passes I want to unlock, but the grind of completing specific challenges and playing modes I don't want to play just takes me out of the experience. The gameplay is good, it all plays like a Halo game should, but the rest of the experience makes you feel exploited at every turn and forced to play something that looks and feels like Halo, but just isn't. I'm going back to the Master Chief Collection because this new direction just isn't fun.

_childDocuments_.review: So, the Halo Infinite multiplayer beta has been out for almost a week and I could play only 7 hours because of life in general (work/gym/got sick/other stuff), but I have kept a close eye to what the community has been saying and I want to get out of the system a few things about this beta, even if I played only 7 hours (with 4 of those played today).First off, the game is really fun. Runs well, definitely better than the closed beta, has the classic Halo gameplay and... that's it really. Luckly, unlike Battlefield 2042 or Call of Duty, they are still true to what Halo is as a game. I really like it and cannot wait to play it this weekend.But I'm leaving a bad review, ain't I ? That's because I think the progression of this game is... bad. I get it, F2P gets more money than standard AAA multiplayer games, look at Warzone how much money is making, why don't we make our most popular FPS into a F2P ? And I'm ok with that, I would have paid 60€ for this, but ok, better for me, for you and everyone else, no ?  So, they added a battlepass as a way to progress in the game. And ok, nothing wrong with this either, we have seen it a lot and, if done correctly, could be a nice way to progress into the game. Problem is, they didn't make a good way to progress it nor they did a good battlepass. First off, there's no levelling system outside of the battlepass. No ranks (except for the ranked mode if you're into that), no nothing. You can only progress this battlepass which is 1000 exp per level and "unlocks" stuff each level. "Unlocks" because a lot of the cosmetics are behind paywall, at a price of 10€. Which I'm fine with it, being a F2P game and all that, but, both the quality of these cosmetics and the slowness with which you progress it, really puts me off from buying it.The progression is made only with a daily and weekly challenges (as of the time of writing, the daily is simply "play a game" which gives 50 exp for every match played). So, you win, you lose, you play like god, you play like ♥♥♥♥, you will progress like the other players. Unless you do the weekly too, which involve things from killing enemies with a weapon (and I'm not a long time Halo player, I don't know the name of the weapons and where to find them, so I can easly mistake the "battle rifle" for the default rifle. Also, remember that Halo is an Arena Shooter. I need to camp a weapon spawnpoint and wait for it to spawn if it's not there if I want to use it) to playing a game mode a few times (but you can't queue that game mode. You need to hope that, when you start the matchmaking, you will get that game mode. I like big team battles, but I need to play 3 oddballs, so I will queue for quickmatch and get to play elimination, CTF etc.. until I finally find and play a match of oddball. And this 3 times.). There are/were other weekly that are harder, but I don't remember now. Just an example of what happened to me a few hours ago: I unlocked a challenge, complete 3 Strongholds matches. Easy enough, time to start the quickplay, cross my finger and play the game. After 97 minutes of playing the game, how many matches of Strongholds I completed ? The answer is . What a fun and challeging progression system. Honestly, I don't know what to say. I mean, it's a really fun game, but they really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up the monetization and the progression. The store is atrocious, classic F2P with these "microtransactions", where an armor is 20€ or a skin bundle for the vehicles is 15€. Should be called "macrotransaction". And the progression... well, feels like you are never progressing. I would have bought the game at 60€ if it was a classic game (so, without F2P ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥). I like the game and I will probably continue to play it, but I really hope 343i will change this system for the better, because like this, I doubt I will be spending money and continue to play the game on the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: Let's begin with the multiplayer suite, since that released twenty-eight or so days before the campaign. It was, to be frank, a barebones but solid experience for quite a lengthy period of time. Now, however, it's enjoying regular content updates and lots of community love through Forge maps. Nevertheless, I enjoyed it from the start, and for me it was a massive step up from the previous game in terms of connection quality. I was constantly being kicked out of games with no warning and sometimes with matchmaking penalties in Halo 5: Guardians. Thankfully, there's been virtually none of that match ejection nonsense in my experience playing Halo Infinite PvP. Moving on to something more positive! This game has, in my opinion, the best sandbox in the series so far. The weapons sound good, yes, but they play well too. The Battle Rifle is trusty, the Commando is useful for those who prefer more control over their utility weapon, and the Sidekick is just that—a faithful companion to whip out in close quarters combat. The new Banished weapons don't just fill the same basic roles as their human counterparts; they each have something unique to offer and don't make the sandbox feel overcrowded or homogeneous. The Pulse Carbine is great for softening opponents' shields, or going for a show-off kill (it's challenging to land all the shots in two pulses to kill an opponent). The Ravager is good for area denial, and the Mangler echoes the original M6D pistol from Halo 1, but with a more balanced set of traits, namely a smaller ammunition capacity, bullet drop, and slower rate of fire. The new equipment items are fantastic map pickups and they enhance the flow of multiplayer matches, such as the Repulsor, which you can use to ascend levels or push enemies into walls or over map boundaries to their doom. The Drop Wall is a way to briefly fortify a position, but can't be used to break the flow of matches in the same way as the bubble shield from Halo 3, since it can be destroyed from the front. And the Grappleshot? Oh, this is so. much. fun. You can grab weapons, pull yourself to opponents, and swing like Spider-Man across structures. It feels good to use and it looks so stylish when you pull off a counter-play with it. There's a lot more weapons, equipment, and vehicles I could talk about, but I don't want to make this review tooo long.  The only thing keeping this multiplayer suite from being a 10/10 for me is probably the lack of true offline play, which is crazy since this is the first Halo to officially feature multiplayer bot players. If they add offline capability, it would definitely be a 10/10. Now, for the campaign... I loved it. So, so much. I grew up reading the Halo novels—in fact, I read The Fall of Reach as a kid before I played through any of the games (my parents couldn't afford a game console at the time). That book shaped my perception and biases toward the Halo universe, and it defines the Master Chief for me. He's not an empty husk for the player to inhabit, he's a person with distinct traits and his own character, to which I personally can relate, at least on some level. Thankfully, I didn't have to go through kidnapping and physical augmentation. I've read most of the novels in the series, and played through almost all of the games, and there's been a remarkable consistency in the writing for the Master Chief. Halo Infinite is no exception.This campaign is a character study of the Master Chief, and it shows that beautifully. The open world is fun, and as others have pointed out, it's essentially an expanded version of the original level Halo from the titular game. The enemy AI for the Banished is amusing, intelligent, and challenging. It makes them seem extremely competent, and certainly more deadly than the Covenant (except Halo 2's Jackal Snipers, of course). The Grappleshot enhances just about everything because of its versatility, and the combat is satisfying. I won't go into spoiler territory anymore than I already have, but suffice it to say that this is my favorite modern Halo campaign. It's absolutely stellar.

_childDocuments_.review: I must say I’m glad to see Microsoft finally release a modern Halo game on PC, the master race after waiting for a couple of decades. Sure, you have the Master Chief Collection, but how long did it take for those titles to be released for PC? Maybe they realized that computers are a thing and we also enjoy a good Halo game? Enough of my ramblings! This review will be revolved around my experience that is multiplayer.   I haven’t played a Halo title since Halo: CE for PC many years ago. I never bothered with MCC which I always told myself I’d give a try. Whatever the reasoning, I never did. When I tried the beta for this edition, I was not disappointed – in the gameplay. The controls are fluid; the Spartans move with dignity and reassurance that they will overcome all the odds against an array of players and a diverse selection of weaponry. When I hold onto that battle rifle, spray n’ pray on that enemy player, I feel in control of the weapon. I did not experience any hiccups, delays, or disappointment when shooting at someone, unlike other modern shooters. When I shot at the enemy, the hit registry was on point. I have a purpose in winning because not only is the gunplay solid, but moving around is solid too. I’m glad to see that Halo still lives in strafing rather than bunny hopping, eating grass while in the prone position, and other garbage that has accumulated over the years. From firing off my rifle to moving around the map, I feel they did an excellent job producing this title. The UI is clean, efficient, and gives only details as needed. The information doesn’t clutter up your screen, which will offer you more screen coverage on those pesky Spartans. A few of the modes that are currently in the game are: Capture The Flag, Oddball, Team Deathmatch, and a few other ones that show up within the events.  A few of the guns require pruning in their damage, but they’re the weapons that spawn on the map. Knowing the environment, where they generate, having the high ground, placing yourself in ideal situations are all key to not being one-shot. CTF still feels significant compared to the original Halo. The maps weren’t too big and felt just big enough for 4v4 or big team battles. They did a lot of playtesting to see what works and it shows. They do offer Cross-Play for PC players to go up against console players. If you have friends still living in the Dark Age and want to show off your superiority, then this is the best option in the industry. You can play against controllers in ranked matches, but be aware that their aim-assist is ridiculously on point. I have seen plenty of live streamers complain about how well it is compared to using the mouse and keyboard.  Graphically and audibly this game looks, feels, and sounds incredible. 343 did put some effort into making this game majestic. Though some of the issues are not around gunplay, gameplay, or the creative aspect of the title, but the paywall they added to this product. Vivid Halo players are saying fewer weapons and maps – which I could agree that there should be more maps, but we’re in Beta testing. They may have more maps on release. Honestly, I’d rather pay for multiplayer than deal with this cringe-worthy ATM that will take my money. I shouldn’t have to pay $10 to $15 USD to pick up a skin that is more or less a re-skin! Oh, that visor? $20 dollars! Do you want a sticker with your Warthog? Make it $9.99 for an installment plan of 12 months. This is some of the worst micro-transactions I’ve seen in a video game; Call of Duty was pretty bad at it too, but at least you were getting something from theirs – to an extent. A lot of the content for the price is bare bones. Not only that, but they went the Activision route of doing Battle Pass, charging for every skin, calling card, sticker, re-color, vehicle decals, and so forth. I understand that the multiplayer is for free, but even playing it for free, I feel like I’m being robbed even for not buying anything. To even rank up with relative ease – as there is no XP from killing players, kill assists, acquiring the objective, or anything of that nature – you’d have to buy the Battle Pass to get XP cards so you can get more XP when you WIN or LOSE a match. You’ll also get XP for finishing a challenge, but even some of them are limited in regards to completion. The XP grind in here is absolutely disgusting. The customization is also limited because of the troll at the toll bridge. Fee fi fo fum I want your money. You’re provided a few colors, can change the AI, add some decals, and one or two armor pieces. You can unlock more of these options via the levels you gain throughout your matches and completion of challenges. Those XP cards and having the Battle Pass versus not having either of them will make this a horrible grind to unlock your seasonal armor pieces, color variations, and other accessories. However, you can purchase multiple skins, decals, etc. from their online store and support some of the competing teams within the Halo community. My sentiment towards supporting your community teams is a plus, granted they get the monetary funds. Some skins do look a lot better than most of the pieces you’d acquire from leveling up in the current season. The cherry on the top! If you unlocked the item via leveling up, you're required to purchase a Battle Pass to use it. It comes down to the color or armor piece applicable for seasonal use only. This business model is toxic - I’m not surprised. If anything, I’m disappointed.  GPU: EVGA FTW3 GeForce RTX 3070 TiCPU:  Intel Core i9-10900KOS: Windows 10Ram: 64GBStorage: Evo 870 4TB (SSD) I did not notice any lag, stutter, or crashes. Everything looks so crisp and clean. From the bullets piercing my head to the footsteps coming behind me to butt the back of my head, it sounds astounding. What you call this is top quality in terms of visual and audible concepts. I enjoyed the gameplay as it felt like I was a kid again playing Halo: CE for the PC decades ago. It felt genuine with a sense of purpose to prove that Halo isn’t dead on the PC, but alive and kicking to their rivalries. My only gripe with this title is that humongous paywall. It’s why I’ve stopped playing a lot of modern shooters because most of them go this approach as its toxic behavior towards the consumer. I’ll be playing this title regardless because the gunplay is astonishing compared to similar titles. 343 will just need to discuss with Microsoft how to be more customer-friendly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game will become my next abusive relationship. Let's talk about it:The Good:Looks excellent. Art design is greatThe Campaign is ultimately worth a play. That alone gets this game a recommended from meThe movement and shooting is very well done and constructed. I have basically no issues with how you move.Each weapon feels unique and has its own place in the sandbox, to a fault almost.Plenty of customization options, from helmets and chest plates to weapon attachments and armor effects. Infinite has everything.Battle Pass and XP progression as of 12/23/21 is very fair and has some flexibility without being too punishing. Challenge Swaps are abundant.Crossplay and Cross Progression.Multiplayer is free. Try before you buy.Sound design is REALLY goodGrappleshot is easily the biggest innovation this series has had in awhile and forced almost all the maps in the game to have real verticality that hasn't been seen since Halo 2.Graphics options are plentiful.Ranked settings are the best they've ever been and the only way to play multiplayer properly.Events are frequent and the rewards are now pretty solid for doing so little. They're also free.The Bad:No Forge, no Co-Op Campaign. Custom Games are broken.Keyboard and Mouse is unviable competitively solely because of how easy the BR is to use.DX12 and unoptimized. No fullscreen mode. You can barely take advantage of DX12 as is.Competitive Ranking system is a joke.Store is bland and overpriced. Don't buy unless you have a gift card with nothing else to spend it on.Lack of free options in the Battle Pass and customization (Spending $10 is truthfully worth it here). You get like 4 helmets, one of which is your starting helmet. Questionable balancing decisions revolving around the niches weapons provide. Everything is useful, but only in specific scenarios, with some being too rare to where the weapon gets any use (Hydra and Pulse Carbine are particularly pretty bad, and Ravager is the only useless weapon a la Halo CE Needler or Halo 3/Reach Spiker). You will become very frustrated at higher levels because all the weapons are pretty limiting with little flexibility in their use.Lack of content. 10 maps sounds like a lot, but 5 are 4v4 maps of medium size, 2 are larger 4v4 maps with vehicles, and 3 are 12v12 monstrosities of "maps". There's only 7 or so gamemodes too, not including variants like Fiesta or SWAT.Vehicles are paper thin and have too many counters, yet most of the old ways to counter vehicles have been replaced by equipment and the Shock weapon type.Netcode is straight up horrendous. Has major desync issues.Playlists were non existent until the 14th of December, 2021, and new playlists are just event playlists made available year round. Gamemodes are straight up missing. No Multi Team variants, no Infection, no King of the Hill (Strongholds is better for structured teamplay but for FFA/Casuals King of the Hill is much appreciated).As of 12/23/21, BTB playlist is broken and cannot consistently get players into matches.No earnable Master Chief armor. Only thing is Mark VI prototype from Halo Reach. No Mark V either.Overall: 6/10 experience that drives me absolutely bonkers. Give this game a try and see if you like it. If you are on the fence, run far far away until a year or so passes.

_childDocuments_.review: Halo: Infinite has some great elements, but as a whole, it was incredibly disappointing. Both the gameplay and the story. Starting with the story… The Banished were given an enormous amount of potential via HW2 and third-party content. But in Halo: Infinite, almost everything is dropped. The idea of Atriox trying to turn his band of rebels and mercenaries into a galactic superpower is dropped entirely, and their conflict with the Spirit of Fire is gone with no explanation. There are huge gaps in the story (not because of h5) that cause major issues. The Banished had some interesting ideas, but now all the characters associated with them are monologuing cliché villains with minimal depth. Watch Atriox’s introduction in HW2, then watch Escharum’s introduction in Infinite. There's a huge difference in quality. The damage to the Halo universe extends way beyond this. Every single faction, setting, conflict, and character (except the chief) we’re supposed to care about has been written out. It honestly sucks, I was invested in these ideas and wanted to see what the writers would do with them. Now it’s all gone, for no reason. There are countless additional issues I could go over, meanwhile the writers spend 3 conversations trying to explain that Zeta Halo was turned into a living thing for some reason. Nothing in this story makes any sense, and it all feels so lazy and disrespectful.The gameplay also has major issues. Almost all the weapons and power abilities are extremely poorly designed. To name a couple… The Ravager is a grenade launcher with low damage and almost no explosive damage. The Shotgun trades half or more of its damage output for additional range (CQC is literally the point of the shotgun...) The Gravity Hammer’s lunge gets you next to your target, then hits you with an enormous delay in which you can be melee’d to death. The Shield Wall absorbs a couple shots and then that segment breaks. On top this, the Cloak and Grapple hook break the game. I’m seeing people use cloak to stroll right through the middle of an active firefight with no repercussions. It’s not supposed to be foolproof. It’s not fun losing that neat vehicle or weapon you found to an enemy you can’t see or fight. The Grapple Hook has the same issue, you can use it to board something with a massive distance between the two targets, and I’m not even sure there’s a way to counter this. Basically, every single weapon and power-up is either useless, or simply takes away the fun from other players, which is not something I can say for any Halo game to this extent.The art style is also a big problem. It’s nice to see Chief and the Elites getting their classic designs back, but everything else has issues. A lot of the weapons and armor look really blocky, out of place, and poorly textured, even after the updates since the Tech Preview. On top of this, 343 seems to mistake quality for quantity by cramming tons of particle effects onto the screen for no reason. It actually feels irritating to get kills, not only because there’s tons of visual noise when doing so, but because the kill sound is like 3 different sound effects spliced together. How am I supposed to enjoy the gameplay when it’s constantly throwing crap on the screen to distract me? This is something people have criticized H4 and 5 for, so I know I’m not alone in this.I could go on like this for much longer, but you get my point. The core elements of the gameplay are really poorly designed, and many of the positives are incredibly minor elements that don’t have much impact on the game. The story is extremely incoherent with major gaps and dialogue that makes no sense, and drops all the potential established by prior stories, or third-party content. I can excuse a lot of this, but 343 has had twice the amount of time and has produced an extremely poor-quality product with less content, that compounds countless issues from previous games. I’m sure a dedicated team of experienced developers could fix this, but… it’s 343.

_childDocuments_.review: To be real, this game has its moments and the core of the shooting is great, but jesus christ does everything else fall flat on its face, wtf was 343 doing for 6 years???not only it is super bare bones for a triple a game with 6 years of experience but a lot is just not working for instance melee doesnt work at all, big team battle straight up doesnt work, nor does custom games (at time of review) most of the cosmetics are in the shop and they arent all great the armor coating system is a downgrade, same with the emblem, most cores are missing a lot of content e.g. mark 5b having very little coatings, mark 7 having very little wrist utility ect and the yokia core or whatever it was called has like 2 helmets and 2 pads.By making the game only progress by challenges is frustrating as i don't really want to win 3 games of oddball or use the pulse carbine it also doesn't help when the game decides it doesn't want to track the challenges as well, halo for example mcc had perfect progression with your medals being used as xp and the ability to do challenges if you want to also most games have a season pass every month or two but this first season pass is lasting I think 6 months, 6 months! after that period of time the player base will most likely harshly die down, like halo 5, due to the lack of content.Triple a studios Tend hire an assisting studio with large live service games to keep content coming, examples like warzone having 2 teams on it and fortnite i think hire extra help for its update, As the game is free they gain money from mirco transactions and i think if they get additional support for the micro transactions while 343 works on the main game that would get a lot more done.The new trend of releasing half arsed games and then slowly updating them into a decent game is a trend among large studios, The sad fact is when the game is finally good no one want to play because of the bad first impression, this exact thing happened to battlefront 2, will halo infinite be a great game in 2-3 years time, most likely but in the current state it is in rn i foresee a lot of people hopping off the game. I love halo always been a fan, i was put off the series by halo 5 and came back with high hopes, issues: limited customisation, poor connection on pc, big team finna dont work, progression system flawed, challenges often not counting, vehicles dont feel right (super tanky against ars br ect but super squish agains  snipers and hardlight), barebones playlists, systems like armor cores and armor coatings being very scummy, having to unlock each shoulder pad separately as well as skins and stickers, red reticle issues, unbalanced spawns (ghost on one side tank on other, or ravanger on one side and shock rifle on other), weapon pad tiers being unbalanced(mangler is way better than distrupter/plas pistol, br over commando, battlepass pretty bad (you cant unlock all of noble teams armor unless you use a kit which is very restrictive this is by no means a complete list but these are some of the main ones,The balancing for the most part is very very good, most weapons are usable, there are a few outliers like the plasma pistol and ravager, and I should talk about how the commando is a little underwhelming but not bad, weapons like the hydra, distruptor and pulse carbine seemed crap at the start of this games lifecycle but now know how to use them better. Like I said in the list there a few issues with weapon pads balance, to give a run down weapon pads have tiers you will have rifles on one snipers(non power) on one shotguns ect, there is some issues with the spawns as the mangler which is regarded as the same tier as plasma pistol and distruptor spawns too quick for how strong it is, but apart from that and the br > commando the other 2 pads are pretty balanced (heatwave = bulldog and shockrifle = stalkerrifle). One last issue with balance is there are some sandbox elements missing or nerfed. for example a power shotgun is really needed as swords and hammer feel very strong, spartan lasers replacement, the skewer, feels a lot weaker in the fact it requires 2 shots for anything tankier than a mongoose and tanks require like 5 shots, cindershot is good against vehicles but the weapon in all over the place and at times you can get a weird bouncy shot, the sniper is the best vehicle destroyer which it should not as the sniper is already a very powerful anti spartan weapon.i would give this game a 6/10 (multi-player) and a meh review but steam only allowed yes or no, I would still recommend this game to halo fans and people new as it is fun but be warned as there is a lot of issues as i listed above

_childDocuments_.review: I've attempted to enjoy this game over the span of it's release, and it's gameplay is alright, but that's just about it.  Every time I do play it though, I can't get over how 343 basically killed the titan that was Halo slowly but surely.  It's not like it isn't an improvement to their other titles (except 5's multiplayer, which was surprisingly enjoyable) but it just lacks the soul of what made Halo what it is. Back in the day when I was growing up playing Halo 3 during it's prime, everyone wanted the sword, Hyabusa armor, rouge armor, EOD armor, etc. Why? Because having them meant you accomplished something. In 343's Halo, everything can be bought with money, there's no accomplishment. When you see someone with something cool like that, you immediately don't care because you know that they could have just paid for it, additionally, there's a lack of incentives to accomplish any kind of challenge at all. Your gameplay in multiplayer doesn't matter either, just their ridiculous challenges that you are forced to do if you want to make any substantial progress in leveling up their paid season pass. The campaign launched at 60 dollars by itself (A ridiculous change of form considering Halo has always been a full package. Admittedly, it was a good campaign) but completely detached from the "free" unfinished multiplayer aside from a few red skins. Consider for a moment if Halo Reach, the insanely successful  conclusion to Bungie's time with Halo launched this way with all it's promotion and hype. Back then, they would have been laughed off the stage the next time they did anything. Instead, they delivered what is probably the most consistently fun Halo ever created. We shouldn't accept now what we wouldn't then, 343 is a joke and doesn't deserve to squander the name of Halo any longer. They had the greatest opportunity to bring Halo back to a golden age considering both COD and BF where bad at the time of release, but they wasted it regardless. What a tragedy.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been putting a review off for this game for a long time, because Halo is one of the most important game franchises to me as it helped formally introduce me to the FPS genre, the awesome story of Master Chief and the war against the covenant, as well as help me grow closer to relatives and make new friends, whether it was being in a LAN party trying to be the best player and rubbing it in each other's faces, or sit on the couch with everyone and just screw around with the physics and share some laughs. So after 343 Industries took over the role as main developers after Bungie left Microsoft and made the disappointment that was Halo 4 and the absolute dumpster fire that was Halo 5, Halo Infinite to me looked like it was going to be the one to bring the franchise back to its former glory, and it almost did with it's artstyle, gameplay, new equipment such as the grappleshot, and it's reasonably good campaign as opposed to Halo 4 and 5. But as it succeeded in those things, the game and 343 Industries pretty much failed in everything else, in some cases, more than even Halo 5 did. With the game being too competitive to play casually with friends, discouraging player interaction without having pre-game and post-game lobbies as well as voice chat being off by default, having little content even 10 months after launch, restricting player customization through the armor core system and locking certain cosmetics behind a paywall, poor optimization on pcs, and features and gamemodes that should've been there on day one being pushed back or, recently in splitscreen co-op's case, straight up canceled, it made me understand something I've understood for a long time even more: 343i has been ruining this IP ever since they acquired it when Bungie left.They gave us a lackluster remaster of Halo CE, the game that started it all, changed the artstyle and gameplay with Halo 4 and doubled down on their decision with Halo 5 as well as giving us the worst Halo campaign to date, and released the Master Chief Collection in a broken state and didn't finish fixing it until several years later. They've also been chasing trends instead of making them by making Halo 4 play like Call of Duty, Halo 5 play like Titanfall, and Infinite play something along the lines of Apex Legends, especially with it's "live service," which is a major reason why Halo Infinite is failing. With little content being added with each occasional update, Forge and Network Co-op being delayed multiple times, a bunch of cosmetics being locked behind a paywall with inflated prices, seasons lasting more than 3 months, and now needing a BETA for MATCH XP, it makes games like Battlefield 2042 and Destiny 2 look like better games.In the new roadmap, 343 announced that campaign splitscreen co-op, a feature that was in ALL Halos prior (with the exeption of Halo 5) and was one of the staple features that made Halo so revolutionary, would not be coming to the game. There's a glitch going on that actually let's you play splitscreen, and it works pretty much perfectly! And it only makes 343's decision to cancel it look worse on them. Also, fun fact: After the backlash Halo 5 got for not having splitscreen on launch, Bonnie Ross, CEO of 343i, PROMISED that ALL Halo titles moving forward would officially have splitscreen co-op on launch, and now that statement has aged like milk.Another thing, the idea that Halo at is core is competitive, is completely false and is another major reason that Halo Infinite is failing, in my opinion. Marcus Lehto, the lead developer of Halo CE, said that his intention for the Halo multiplayer experience was that it would be a social party game with shooter mechanics and that it was meant to be more accessible for casual players, and actually didn't like the competitive scene all that much. And that's how it was from CE to Reach. 343i, on the other hand, is the complete opposite. All they seemed to care about for a long time now is the competitive scene and have tweaked their games to be catered towards them and not players who want a FUN experience. Huge emphasis on fun. When I'm playing matches in this game, I'm playing against sweats who don't think about anything other than just winning the match. Which leads me to this game's skill based matchmaking. 343 has made it so that you have an average 50% win/lose rate; the better you are at the game, the better opponents you'll face, and the worse teammates you'll be given, and vice versa. BS!!! That is not fun! Not for the player OR their teammates! I can't tell you how many times players, myself included, have lost matches because they got stuck with teammates who act like it was their first ever match and/or opponents who play like their lives will be ruined if they don't win the match.Although I can't be too pessimistic, because MCC has been through somewhat similar circumstances. The game was a mess at launch, but 343 managed to get it together, fix the bugs that were impacting matchmaking, and add LOADS of new content to the games (plus they're all (except Halo 4) Bungie's Halos so ofc they were still good). And the games are still being updated today, fixing more bugs, adding new content and features, and even getting modding support. But while all this is really good and will preserve the games for years to come, they haven't gone through what Infinite is going through right now.I could talk about all the problems the game currently has because of 343i, but I think you get the point, so I'll just be as frank as possible: I firmly believe that if this franchise is going to be successful again and will have a chance at being at the top of the gaming charts like it's supposed to, 343i either needs to leave and never work on Halo again and get replaced by a company that knows and respects the franchise like Certain Affinity, or get a full restructure, specifically for the upper management, because Bonnie Ross and the rest of her team in charge of what happens with the game, are all incompetent and clearly don't care about Xbox's biggest IP that made them successful from the very beginning. Xbox CEO Phil Spencer said it himself: "If we lose our way with Halo, we lose our way with Xbox."I'm sure Joseph Staten, ex-Bungie dev who worked on Halo and current Head of Creative at 343, did his best to get the game to be the best when it came to gameplay and the campaign and genuinely didn't want any of this to happen to Halo nor did the other devs who worked on this game. Which made it so infuriating that they made him deliver the bad news in the September 1 roadmap as well as other bad news previously, especially considering his reputation and passion with the IP. I'm sure the poor guy felt like crying when he announced the cancellation of splitscreen "couch co-op." It wasn't his fault Halo Infinite's in the state it's in, nor is it all of the other devs', it was the head management at 343i and Microsoft.I'm tired of missed deadlines. I'm tired of broken promises. I'm tired of being lied to. I'm tired of 343 Industries."Don't make a girl a promise, if you know you can't keep it."

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having promised ten years of Halo Infinite, it looks like 343 are throwing in the towel barely after the two year mark. This marks the second time they've outright lied about the game's development, following Bonnie Ross' first official statement on Halo Infinite, before we even knew its title, that it would in fact have split screen co-op. If Halo still had the fanbase it did in 2001-2010, there would have been multiple class action lawsuits for these lies. Unfortunately, no one cares anymore.After confirming they've just reached seasonality, they're pulling the rug and only doing small updates with no more future seasons, starting with the upcoming "CU29" update. This update will only consist of cosmetics and one developer made map. The majority of the update's file size will surely be drip fed, rotational, fomo premium cosmetics, as ever. The rest being forge items, or map cosmetics, for the community to do their job for them in making maps people actually like playing that aren't outsourced to Russian studios, who sand away every interesting detail in the process to make the most generic and boring, competitive friendly maps imaginable.They started their livestream’s gameplay by showing off an assault rifle skin made to look like the classic CE/3 AR, which looks more like the 4/5 variant than anything. Despite the weapon sandbox not having any meaningful updates in over two years (two DMR variants, i.e. more precision weapons we don't need, are not meaningful additions to the sandbox), they used the opportunity to create a purely cosmetic variant, and not a 60 round variant to celebrate the franchise’s legacy and give its ever dwindling player base something fun to use. Knowing people will want the skin regardless, they locked it behind the $5 premium tier of the event pass.Given seasons are gone now, it seems like the 100 tier battle passes are gone as well. Now we can count on the 20 tier event passes, which will be loaded up with filler items, to contain the one item people really want in its $5 premium tier. Event passes expire while battle passes don't, the latter being promised in their initial multiplayer showcase video. However, if you buy the event pass premium tier you unlock its use forever. This is their means of getting around their prior commitments in service to pure greed.This especially stings knowing that season 2's battle pass and every subsequent one had in its 100 tiers enough premium credits to buy the following pass. No credits are returned for the premium event pass. They also made sure to rename the event passes to try and cover their tracks. Yet another measure to milk fans of every dollar they have.All of this comes directly off the heels of daring to ask the few dedicated who can only now expect to play fan made maps with an over bloated premium dress up shop, to please buy a $20 Halo CE Mark V skin. Now, I've always played CE as a white spartan since small kid time, playing against my buddies on xbox on blood gulch. On my 22+ year old copy of CE, I can still do this for free with all of the game's original content and functionality in tact. I can even play the campaign cooperatively using local split screen on my TV at home without having to buy a second console/pc and copy of the game, believe it or not.Now if I want that same pvp experience today, I'm expected to spend $40. $20 for the Mark V skin which can barely be customized because it's an armor kit and not pieces of an existing armor core, and $20 for a bundle filled with crap I don't want just to get the color white, a color freely chosen by the player in every prior Halo to date. And to play blood gulch I'm supposed to play on a player made variant because the actual developers couldn't be bothered.Not to mention the litany of issues since launch and lack of features 2001-2010 Halos had at launch:It was made clear in their stream they're slowing down development to work on the next Halo, which may well be another shell of a game which disappoints everyone, and over monetizes its storefront to the few who stick around to "recoup", despite being funded by the infinite money well that is Microsoft. They won't make an effort, unlike Battlefront 2, to win back its playerbase by not focusing solely on money for every single decision.The sad reality is no matter any petty arguments about sprint, clamber, weapon sandbox, monetization, etc., 343 isn't equipped to make Halo.Bungie always upped not only their own game, but tested everyone in the industry around them, by holding themselves and the industry to an ever increasing standard of player fun oriented gameplay, story, feature suites and mechanics. This resulted from them being scrappy upstarts who were bought by Microsoft after they were proven. They could fight back against mindless corporate profit seeking and shareholder pleasing, while arguing for things like theater mode and forge which would by no means fly today.343 on the other hand was created by and works directly under Microsoft. If they weren't established already, theater mode wouldn't be slopped out with every release in a broken state and left to rot, and forge wouldn’t have been dreamt of. Forge only gets the treatment it does because they want fans to do their job for them.TLDR: 343 is giving up and continuing to fail to make good on their promises, to likely focus on developing an upcoming Halo. Future updates will be slow, inconsistent nothingburgers with fan made maps and overpriced cosmetics that were free well over a decade ago. 343 are inherently unable to create Halo games which are satisfying to general audiences because Halo was never just about "green man in suit with blue waifu and multiplayer with cool dirt bike helmets", but an ever increasing standard of quality and quantity Bungie held themselves to by fighting back against Microsoft's corporate ignorance, always striving for player fun and not player's wallets.EDIT: Context and spelling errors.Also, the vast majority of the update’s new armor, which easily could’ve filled a battle pass, is locked behind somehow even more heavily priced bundles in the shop in the midst of a cost of living crisis. Not surprising in the least, sadly. Halo is not for the player anymore. Support games by smaller studios which are player fun oriented, like Deep Rock Galactic or Tower Unite.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time fan of the Halo series, and someone who was excited for this release, it pains me to not recommend the multiplayer, or at least recommend spending your money on any multiplayer item, including the battle pass. While the core gameplay is great and the art style is the best it has been since 3, the progression and monetization has damaged the reputation of the game.For starters, items promised as free unlocks in the battle bass were presumably cut out and sold separately for real currency after the release. Not only has 343 cut items from the pass that have been promised as being a part of it (and instead charging real currency for it, excluding the price of the battle pass), they have encouraged wasting money on so-called "challenge swaps" as a faux-reward to swap out annoying challenges. Speaking of the challenges, often-times they are tedious or downright asinine, and being that they are the main method of acquiring XP. Leveling up can be extremely frustrating if you are dealt an unlucky had with these terrible challenges (again you can use a "challenge swap", but this doesn't fix the problem, only exacerbates it by encouraging players to spend money to gamble on getting an even worse challenge). There are of course easier challenges, such as to complete "x" amount of CTF, Oddball, etc. matches, but even these simple challenges can be tedious as well as there are no separate playlists for game modes (a match composer system like MCC would be even better, allowing you to select specific game modes and team sizes), but even a basic separation of slayer v. objectives, which has been a staple of every past Halo game, is not present.I should mention the lack of content at launch, especially given that the game has been in development for six years (for reference, that is longer than the time between the releases of Halo 2 and Reach). There are only three big team battle maps, which means the playlist gets very stale after less than 20 hours of playtime. There is a little more map variety in the 4v4 playlists (Quick Play and Ranked Arena) but, as there are not many game modes available, that too gets stale quickly.I could go on and on about some minor nitpicks that I have (like the Ravager being a useless weapon, or being unable to disable crossplay for Ranked Arena), but overall, despite the solid gameplay and art design, everything else about this game leaves much to be desired. If you don't mind going for challenges or ranking up, then by all means do play this game, as the core gameplay is fantastic and is the best in the series since 3. If you do care about doing these things, then I would not recommend investing too much time or any money into the multiplayer. I am hoping that with time and adjustments to the progression, playlists, and microtransactions that my opinion will change for the better.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like Halo Infinite. I tried incredibly hard to stick with this game and enjoy it! It's an incredibly fun game when it works, but there's so many hurdles thrown in your way constantly to remove as much fun as possible in the spirit of monetization.- The multiplayer challenge system is awful and is designed to encourage the player to drop real money for challenge swaps. You will constantly receive challenges that are difficult to complete, or force you into gamemodes you don't want to play or dislike. Progress is incredibly slow as a result, and XP is not rewarded based on performance in games.- Multiplayer customization is limited to armour cores (and arbitrarily limited, as shown by simple modding) and player armour colour is very limited in order to encourage players to spend real money on coatings.- Season 1's battlepass has been extended long beyond its intended end-date, meaning new content has so far not reached the game. There are very few maps, and a limited selection of weapons and vehicles. Seeing all the same maps over and over grows old quite quickly.- Matchmaking isn't great, and frequently results in steamrolling rather than fun, balanced matches. Playing against bots also affects your MMR for matchmaking which is just absolutely insane.- There's still tons of desync and lag issues, meaning sometimes you will just have rockets disappear after firing, solid hits won't land on enemies, you'll be killed well after entering cover, and etc.- The campaign, while fun, very much shows that it had a significant amount of content cut.I think this game may bounce back someday, but the state it's in a few months after launch is sad, and frankly makes it difficult to recommend unless you really want to play the campaign. You're better off playing the Master Chief Collection with your friends... they've probably all gone back to it anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: It kind of sucks to see just how terribly Halo Infinite turned out to be. Only 343 and Microsoft could have dropped this franchise in the toilet and flushed it. Halo was probably the very first game I touched that also turned into my childhood. I spent countless hours on Halo: CE on both Xbox and the old PC port. I was not even apart of the lucky few who did LAN parties and had tons of laughs and beautiful memories. I spent most all of my time from Halos 1-3 playing the campaign over and over with the games never faltering to amuse me. I didn't have Xbox Live up until Halo 3 and the little I did play online was fun whilst I was a kid getting called out over voice chat... good times.A lot of people on here seem to form the popular opinion that 343i has progressively gotten worse with the franchise. In my opinion, they were not nearly great with any of their releases since Bungie left. Halo 4 was not particularly great but I was excited to see a Halo continuation nonetheless. Halo 4: As a huge fan of the Forge feature, I was ecstatic about the expansions and overhauls Halo 4 brought. The campaign was pretty mediocre in every way. Multiplayer was alright although the progression system was pretty neat. Not Halo: Reach, but different.Halo 5:I spent hours having too many laughs with friends with the silly yet harmless glitches Forge had brought. The custom games browser was incredible and helped me re-experience what was like Halo: Reach customs but I did not have to invite 100 previous players to get a lobby going. Warzone introduced higher player lobby population and a new concept I fell in love with, especially the firefight version. Personally, I thought Halo 5 was quite an improvement in many ways.Halo Wars 2:It took me a while to adjust to just how different this was from Halo Wars 1. I loved Halo Wars 1 and after some dedicated time, I grew to enjoy HW2. I despised their Blitz game-mode. It did not fit the game at all.Halo Infinite:343i wiped the slate clean for the worst. Rather than reach higher and greater than before, they did almost every wrong you could think of. They really messed up with their cross-platform balancing. It was almost pointless including cross-play with how horrifically it was handled. They spent what felt like four times longer on the development on Halo Infinite compared to almost every other Halo combined. I overlooked it as they brought it on a new game engine which I thought was great. The idea of Halo finally getting a brand new engine could mean really good things and open up to so many modern possibilities. Oh... I thought SO wrong. Here's just a list of things they did that no one wanted except for the gullible few..- Live Service- Micro-transaction Store- Super-inflated prices on products- Scummy premium currency packages when compared to product prices- Campaign sold separately from multiplayer- An over-priced "DLC" that doesn't meet a $60 price tag- The company selling out to trashy modern standards and practices- A battle pass. HOWEVER, they did allow players to complete past seasons at any point... which is how it SHOULD BE in other games. -1 for battle pass, +1 for having a brain. Cancels out... still sucks.- Premium battle pass- Removing all user creativity/expression by forcing prefabricated color packages as a method to armor customization.- Game-play and gun-play that somehow feels as if affected by censorship.You should also know, fellow reader, that the game is basically cancelled now. Microsoft did a big wave of layoffs that affected further development of Halo Infinite and so now the game has essentially flopped, only sometimes receiving community updates. The custom engine has been taken off the board and further major updates have been terminated. That's right! That cliff hanger you are left on is NO LONGER getting a follow up. You're going to have to wait for the next new release carried by the Unreal Engine.If you grew up with Halo as I did, I'm sorry that your favorite franchise is going to be only playable through a book at this point. 343i AND Microsoft have really killed off Halo fans. The only people who play now are Battle-pass addicts and people who are spoiled enough to buy everything in the game and refuse to put a foot down against modern day company cretins who are ruining the gaming industry. Enjoy gaming while you still can. Enjoy your favorite titles. Microsoft owns them ALL. They will snap them out of existence and you'll NEVER be able to go back and have a laugh with your friends.

_childDocuments_.review: PERSONAL HISTORY WITH THE FRANCHISE:I've been a day one Halo fan, my uncle worked for Microsoft from 1995 to 2005 and would always tell our family (who love Halo and would play 4-way split-screen all the time) when a Halo game started development. Halo:CE through Halo:Reach was at least in my opinion the pinnacle of a gaming Era. Once H4 released I'm not gonna lie I wasn't a fan of 343i and was on the fence about Halo as a franchise. But since it was a Halo game I played it. And same with H5. I didn't like how they changed it so much and went away from the core Halo feel. With Halo Infinite, or at least with the multi-player I feel like 343i is taking the steps back in the right direction. PROS/THOUGHTS:Classic guns have returned, new ones are finding their place. The art design of the Spartans remind me of Halo Reach along with the customization for your Spartan. The graphics I feel are the best in recent years. The equipment is refreshing and different. About 90% of the weapon sounds are amazing! Love the idea of how the season pass itself works.CONS/THOUGHTS:Not the biggest fan on how the xp and Challenges work. I get that they have it the way they do to encourage the purchase of credits to either buy levels for the pass or to get swaps or xp. I feel like there should be xp after every game. For example, you gain 100xp for doing ok and 200xp for placing well on top of if you complete a challenge cause then you'd slowly progress through the pass instead of having to grind all day for a few levels. The second thing is optimization. I feel like they need to work on that as a priority first and foremost. I have an RTX 2060 with a Ryzen 7 2700, and 32GB of DDR4 and it struggles with medium and high settings. And lastly is the crashing of the game. I've only had two crashes, but friends I've played with who have similar specs if not better are having far too many crashes. And I could be wrong on this next statement...but it seems like there could be a memory leak upon launch that should be looked into. If they can at least focus on true game breaking issues 343i will have a very solid game for old and new Halo fans.So far with what I've played that's where I'm at with the game. Time will tell what else I or others come across. At this point I give the online portion of Infinite a 7.5 to 8 points out of 10. If 343i listens to their fans and community and work on what needs to be done I'll most definitely give a 10 outta 10. But I do recommend this game to others....plus you can't beat free.

_childDocuments_.review: Honeymoon phase is over. The game is still fun, but the problem is that it feels like they're forgetting key components of what makes a Halo game. The event pass has 30 tiers and only 13 of them have any sort of customization rewards-- keep in mind that's counting Emblems. Every other armor piece, armor paintjob (which you have to earn now for some reason), visor color, etc. is all stuck into the shop in these horrible """"bundles"""" that give you the one thing you care about plus 4 emblems or something else you don't care about in order to make it feel justifiable to charge people $15 - $20. The only way to look unique in this game will be to spend money. There will not be enough customization options for free players or players who buy the battlepass to make their Spartans look truly different from other people's unless they buy multiple $15 - $20 bundles to get armor options that other people won't have simply because they don't want to spend the money. At this point, I would have just preferred them to make this game cost money.Don't even bother playing the game yet until 343 either makes the game cost money and makes the battlepass a progression pass like what the Master Chief Collection has, or stops being so scummy with their monetization choices. The game is fun, but its not fun enough to deal with the clear malicious business practices 343i has implemented into the game thus far.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was gifted to me as I refused to buy it. Especially before co-op came. This is a co-op only review and I am on legendary.Every 30 minutes is met with either a crash opening the map or your equipment bugs and can't be changed for ~5 minutes. Marines won't follow other players in the game, only the host. Players can't be over 300m from each other; while that is fine if everyone is doing one objective, if you want to split up and try and get map completion you won't be able to do that. Vehicles? Don't bother. A few shots of anything will destroy them. Early-mid game UNSC weapons are utter garbage on shields. This game feels like they removed Tilt just so they can have it enabled at all times. Late game once you have the modified weapons they actually feel like they did in previous Halo games.There's no assassinations. Not just no animations, you can't even one-shot enemies with shields by back hits.Rocket hog? Scorpion? No, forget those. Troop hog. Get marines, give them snipers/rockets, and carry them around with you. They can shred bosses in literal seconds on Legendary. They can kill a Phantom with basic guns while it takes you four rockets. Their damage is absolutely insane. Oh, did they die? GOOD! Now you can pick up the six rocket launchers you gave them and blow all that ammo.I was psyched to do LASO with my bois, especially without Iron. Except now you have forced unlimited ammo and equipment usage, so I don't know why this is an achievement anymore. It'll be about as easy as... well, easy. Thunderstorm seems a bit more extreme than it used to be, but being able to have friends with max profiles brought in and with unlimited ammo, kinda breaks the game. I do enjoy the equipment and world exploration. Grappling is a lot of fun and still useful for shocking even on legendary. A decent amount of points are hidden in caves and not just layed out in the middle of the world. The map tells you exactly how many of each collectable are in a given area and how many you have found. Skulls and towers don't appear on the map until you find them personally and then they stay after you completed it which is a nice touch.

The progression system is terrible, the xp gain is tied to challenges. You don't get xp automatically for winning or playing matches, it's strictly tied to challenges. The worst part is that the xp gain from the challenges feel damn small. Felt like it took 2 hours just to get to level 1. It hurts even more when they sell you xp boosters. 3. This game doesn't offer enough armor cosmetic unlockables for me to go back and to replay because all the armor cosmetics as of now you have to pay for. And even if you can get them for free, because of the progression system the grind to get them isn't worth it in my eyes. *As OF 8/10/22*:I can't recommend this game still. 1. The only positives is that they finally implemented playlists. 2. The progression system got updated but it's still poor. Skins and other content is still tied to battle pass and you have buy the pass to get said content, and it still feels like a chore to grind. 3. This game has massive content drought and it still not properly being addressed. Gameplay is fun, but if you're using the same maps its gets quite repetitive. 4. _childDocuments_.review: Think a lot of the reviews on here are very nit picky, which isn't surprising in the gaming community. The guns feel great (haven't used them all, the bulldog shotgun felt a bit flimsy) but the rest I did manage to get my hands on were awesome. I've forgotten how satisfying landing headshots with a sniper rifle is in Halo. Good variety of game modes with different team sizes. Had a lot of fun playing Big Team Total Control, which ended up being way more chaotic than other game modes (in the best possible way). Really pleased with what I've played so far, and it's really cool we're able to play it early. Haven't experienced any real concerning issues with bugs or other technical problems. Playing the game on medium settings with a 3600x and a 2080 Super. Performance could be better, especially when compared to Modern Warfare / Warzone or Apex Legends for example which perform excellently, but it's not exactly unplayable. Hitting 80fps on average at 1440p which is fine for me - gameplay still feels super smooth and fast as previously mentioned. All in all a fun first session and hopefully will have many more over the coming months and years. Happy 20th anniversary, Spartans.

_childDocuments_.review: A great game wrapped in horrible technical issues.Halo Infinite is fun but I wouldn't recommend you buy it just yet, especially if you're on PC.  I've only been able to play the first two levels of the game so far, and here's a summary of my experience."Why does this game look so pixelated and crappy at 1080p rendering?""Okay, don't touch any buttons if the game decides to load...  Also, why do they just freeze in the middle of a loading section""Cool, I beat that boss.  Time for the open part of the game...  wait, why did my framerate drop below 20fps?"Yeah, you heard that right.  On my RX6700xt, I cannot get more than 20 frames per second on the "outdoor" parts of the game.  What an incredible way to ruin this game for me.  I was having fun in a new Halo game for the first time in a decade and the game itself is literally unplayable.  For some context, and without spoiling too much, your first view of the open world has you facing down something like a hundred Banished enemies right away, something that feels nearly impossible at 1/4th time thanks to the absolute crash in framerate.UPDATE: There appears to be a hidden, optional update for the drivers for my card that restored some performance.  I will have to do some additional testing to see if its playable or not, or if further issues arise later on.  If that smooths things out, I'll probably retract this review, but I don't have hope from my experience so far343i and Microsoft need to be applauded for delivering exactly the experience we were promised back at E3 2020; a title that gets the Halo game play right, but is so technically disappointing and buggy we might as well stick with a game from 2007.  Good job guys.  Good job.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, this is one of the best  Halo multiplayer games I've ever seen. It's like a combination of Halo CE's old-school arcade tankiness with Reach's armor abilities (as pickups on the map) and modernizations. Every shot missed feels like my fault and nearly all the guns feel genuinely useful, solid and impactful. Even the starting AR and pistol which I only ever found useful in CE are pretty damn killer in this one.However, I can't give this a positive review because of the sheer ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that is the progression system, namely the battle pass. The battle pass not only gives very,  little progress for completing challenges, doesn't seem to give anything at all as a reward to players who don't pay for it like other f2p games do, but also has its challenges broken and poorly designed. Many challenges require you to use a specific weapon or play a specific mode, neither of which you are guaranteed to roll in a random match. And even if you do get the weapon you need for the "kill x enemies with weapon y" challenge, it only counts one kill per I do not believe for a second that any of this is an accident or a bug; we've seen them already do better with the Master Chief collection in the past, so they know exactly what they're doing. This isn't just the worst progression system in Halo, it's flat out the worst battle pass in gaming, full stop. Expect the battle pass to be marginally improved by release, call it "fixed," and bring online progression in gaming to a new, crappier normal soon.Update: Apparently you actually keep any battle pass you purchase, and you can even buy earlier passes that have long expired. IF THIS IS TRUE, this is a marked improvement for battle passes in general. All my main issues still stand, ofc, but still.
