_childDocuments_.review: General recap of my experience with Halo Infinite. There's a lot to go over, so I'll start with the cons. Game Modes :That game modes are fun, but you are entirely unable to filter game modes for quick play. Odd ball, CTF, and Slayer are all classics, but I quickly found that I don't enjoy playing Odd ball like I used to. Not only are you not able to filter game modes, you can't filter maps, which is a huge issue due to the current map design. This is a given, please add a game mode filter. Map design & size: The maps in 4v4 can be summarized as follows; Way too open or way too many choke points. Some maps suffer from being way too small with only choke points to fight in, other maps have numerous funnel points with massive clearings in the center. This wouldn't be a massive issue if 2 things were in play, Custom Loadouts & grenade spam. I personally think the maps need major redesigns in the 4v4 game mode, but that could be due to the lack of custom loadouts. Loadouts vs Weapons Spawns :Back in the day, you were able to select a set of weapons in spawn with (in some game modes), and a perk. I am mainly referring to Reach here, Halo Reach is my personal fave. When you spawn, you always spawn with the same 2 weapons.(referring to 4v4 quick play and big team battle) The assault rifle, and the magnum. This locks you into a more medium range and close to medium range build until you pick other weapons up, which can only be found at certain locations on the map and periodically spawn. Yes, the magnum is very good at range, cqb, mid range, and literally any other situation you put it in. But, if you were to run the magnum at long range vs a battle rifle, unless the other player is trash, you're going to lose (as it probably should be). Some maps have severely unbalanced weapon spawns, grenade spawns, heavy spawns, etc. That goes back into map design, which if you are playing on a more open map but don't have any good sniper or long range/mid to long range weapons, you are immediately playing at a severe disadvantage within the first few seconds of a round. God forbid you are playing Oddball and the people you are fighting win the first team fight and lock themselves down in a corner for a massive point lead, just to jump off the map once they finally start to lose control of their corner. Most team fights are decided by two major things; who had better nades and who team shot better. The ladder isn't a major issue, and is extremely common in high TTK games like halo, but is just something to quickly note. Please re-add the ability to spawn with your set builds, or primary weapon at the very least.Nades: Every time you die, you spawn with 2 grenades. When you spawn, you usually spawn near or basically on top of a nade pickup. If said pickup is the stock nade, then you don't get anything out of it. But, if you spawn on any other nade (sticky, spike, or dynamo), you now have 4 nades to chuck to your hearts content. Stock grenades 2 shot, stickies and spikes can one shot, and the dynamo does a massive amount of damage after slowly ticking down someones shields. This is fine, but every single time you die this cycle repeats. And, with how high the TTK is, most players tend to rely on team mates or grenades in a direct 1v1 with stock weapons. Spawning with 1 nade would lessen this, I honestly think spawning with 0 nades would be fine. It would put more emphasis on gun skill vs last ditch nades to win 1v1's or team nade spam. Team shooting : This is a given, the TTK is extremely high for the base spawn weapons, and barely goes down on a few pickups. (i.e the needler, energy pistol, bulldog, commander, and battle rifle) Most fights with leave you with a fully emptied, or mostly emptied mag on your primary. This is not opportune in a 4v4 game mode on extremely small maps, with 4-6 second spawn times, comparatively high mobility. (which can be made faster with perks like the grapple or thruster pack) This breeds a very odd combat cycle that often depends on spawn locations. Many team fights can be completely won within seconds, just to have the enemy team spawn a 4 second sprint away and immediately wipe your team. Which, if the spawns don't favor you and you are playing oddball, you have effectively lost a minimum of 20 points against a group of players with more than 50 brain cells. Most team fights devolve into nade spam (as said), or team shooting. (which makes sense) Whichever team is prioritizing targets wins, as it should be. But, because the game feels so heavily balanced around out numbering or out nading your enemy, 1v1's can be a bit messy against an evenly skilled player. Most CQB fights turn into a melee trade, long range fights just end up in a disengage, and mid range fights can easily end up in a trade via nade, projectile, rarely hitscan, or can be interrupted completely by another player getting involved and swaying the duel.This isn't to say you can't 1v1, that's definitely not the case, but it feels weird to due to the high TTK and comparatively low mag size. Time to kill (TTK): I already summarized my main issue with the TTK, but I will comment further on how shields function below. For now, the TTK is wacky high with the base weapons and majority of pick ups. The assault rifle takes at least half a mag, magnum takes at least 6 shots, battle rifle takes 4 full bursts, commander needs nearly half a mag, needler leaves few rounds to spare. This is why people rely on melee's more often than not in a CQB fight. But the issue is, Melee hitreg sucks. It is completely common to have two players flop bodies together and both die from melee (basically always been a thing), to lunch forward and hit the other player but not do any damage (also extremely common), or for you to literally not move at all but they lunge and kill you and vice versa. Personally, a 25% to 30% TTK reduction would be wonderful IMO, but I know people like that high TTK for team fights. This could be done by lowering shield cap, increasing damage for most (semi)automatic and burst weapons. Or, by allowing head shot multipliers to apply to shields. Shields : My completely subjective view on shields, is that they are cringe as hell. In a 1v1 where I land all head shots and the other player lands all body shots, the TTK is nearly identical, save a few milliseconds. Technically, I would win if I landed 1 head shot and they landed 1 body shot, but with how high a lot of the RPM's are, you are really pushing it. Not only does it do the same amount of damage, its a smaller (kind of projectile inconsistent) hit box, that can be moved way more than center mass by crouching, strafing, or jumping. I genuinely believe that head shots should reward skilled players, and body shots should lose to someone who is cracked and landing head shots vs body shots. Crossplay & aim assist : Speaking of skilled players, never have I seen such a cesspool of contradicting statements about console players. I have directly seen the same player say "If they remove aim assist, controller players won't be able to play the game" while also saying "PC players are just trash, they blame aim assist because they actually suck at the game" I have no idea those two statements can leave the same persons mouth. If I had a quarter for each time I have seen it, i'd have a surprising amount of quarters. God forbid all the times I haven't seen people spout such nonsense. First hand, the aim assist is over kill beyond compare. Well, its is comparable. It's similar to playing with an aim bot that uses a thresh hold scrip vs map wide script. The kind that can make it seem like you're just flicking to enemies near your cross hair. It is absolutely, 100%, entirely over tuned. If it makes bad players good, and good players great, its an issue. My Fiance (admittedly is not that good at FPS games) had a noticeable increase in accuracy, total kills, and 1v1's won. Hit the character cap.-.

_childDocuments_.review: Halo fan since 2001, love the franchise and the one thing I want most is for the game to be good. And at its core, it is.  However, customization is a crap shoot and the progression is the worst system i have ever seen in any game ever.  They have removed things that used to be free in other halos and made them paid, and made it incredibly difficult to progress through a battle-pass that is paid!  DO NOT buy anything in this game, it does not respect your money or your time and it is downright malicious.  It has fallen into the classic tropes of other big AAA games where all it does is try to get you to grind and play the game more and more, and it is BAD.  The current in-game event has challenges to unlock things, however they are MIXED IN WITH THE REGULAR CHALLENGES! So you won't even always have any event challenges while you play meaning you cannot progress! This system is terrible.There are also a lot of game-play issues as well, melee is broken, likely due in part to the lack of player collision so you go through the enemy when fighting and then cant even find them again before they hit you in the back.  Many weapons with high skill ceilings due not reward you spending the time to get acquainted.  The heatwave for example is a bit tough to get used to but even when you do it takes A LOT of shots to kill, a high skill ceiling weapon like that should be more rewarding to those willing to put in the time.  Overall I'm very disappointed as a long time Halo fan.Play a few rounds if you want to check it out, but don't plan on investing any real time or money here until these terrible practices are addressed.  MS has been silent on the issues other than "we're working on it" and given no idea of what that really means.  The lack of communication is abysmal.  As heartbreaking as it is, I cannot recommend Halo: Infinite in its current state.  Yes, I realize its a beta, and anyone who thinks any real changes are coming in the next couple of weeks is kidding themselves. _childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: Halo Infinite is a broken mess. If you want to play an Arena Shooter with Mouse and Keyboard you shouldn’t play Infinite. In view of the fact that you are almost always at a disadvantage and will lose your 1 on 1's to aim assist. Furthermore the game is very poorly optimized and runs very badly, even on high end hardware. ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------First of all I'm a big Halo fan and I played the original trilogy for thousands of hours.Halo 4 and Halo 5 are in my opinion the worst Halo games to ever exist until Halo Infinite launched.Infinite launched in a completely unacceptable state. No campaign coop, no forge, broken custom games, very poor netcode with strong desync, almost no customization and only with a small selection of playlists and gametypes. Because 343's plan was to drip feed the content slowly.The campaign is extremely boring, repetitive and tedious.Halo Infinite's Multiplayer is at its core a good and fun game. But what need do you have for a brilliant core, if the rest of the game is just plain frustrating.I played over 1 thousand games of Halo Infinite since launch and almost nothing changed. 343 released a live service game with zero live service. The only part of Infinite getting new content is the store. Every other aspect of the game gets ignored.Furthermore if you want to play on mouse and keyboard, just play any other game. Halo Infinite is made for controllers and the aim assist is insane. You have to be in the Top 10% of MnK players to be able to compete with the average controller player.The game has no server selection. Which means if you are from Europe, you will play most of your games on US Servers with an average ping over 100ms.Another big negative point of Halo Infinite is the lack of customization compared to the old Halo games. If you want to customize your Spartan, be ready to get your wallet and pay for it.They even monetized colors as coatings and want you to pay for basic color combinations.You cannot use a basic palette of colors compared to the old games. 343 wants you to pay for customization, no matter what. Except if you like the color grey. Grey is free.Halo Infinite has a lot of FOMO (fear of missing out), be ready for it. Sure you can buy a season pass and complete it whenever you want. But you also have to constantly play missable and time gated events to unlock free armor (beware you still only get a part of the event content for free, the rest is in the shop).The weekly ultimate rewards are one time only and if you miss them you are out of luck.The game gets almost no new content or patches. You have to wait months for bug fixes and if 343 release a patch it will break something else in the game.In my honest opinion nobody should play Halo Infinite until they released all the basic content in 2 years. Till then you should buy The Master Chief Collection and play the old Halo games. You get more content, better gameplay and a great story.

_childDocuments_.review: 343 has it all; time, money, and an established fanbase. They have had control of the Halo IP for as long as Bungie did and in all that time they have nothing to show for it but mediocre entries and an erosion of trust with their fans.Halo Infinite at its core is a great game, it runs well, it's art style is a return to form, and the gameplay is tight. However it's underlying issues weigh it down too much for it to strive. Desync has been a problem for months and has barely been addressed,this is especially infuriating as it is such as common occurrence and its been prevalent for months.Lack of content with the game being 9 months old at the time of this review we have received only 2 seasons and a handful of gamemodes (that aren't even new and should've been in the game from launch). To put the nail in the coffin 343 cannot even keep to their word and keep delaying features (again should've been in the game from the start) mainly forge and co-op, "oh co-op splitscreen is cancelled btw" 343 1 day after it was meant to launch. Communication is abysmal for such a large company and "live service game". Custom game options are lack luster. Infinite is still missing forge, co-op, firefight, the ability to replay missions, and a custom games browser all of that on top of having the most development time out of any Halo game and a year long delay.While the gameplay is great it is ruined by the challenge system, which forces you to use weapons and play game modes you don't want. This would be okay if it wasn't the only way to progress and earn rewards at all, because of the lack of a traditional progression system. If you get a challenge for a weapon that sucks and doesn't even spawn good luck if you don't have a challenge swap.The campaign is not worth the $90 I paid for it. The story was great and I enjoyed the more smaller scale of the narrative. But after playing it once nothing really stood out to me in terms of missions. Halo has always had amazing set pieces for their missions and epic moments (ie. The Covenant mission H3) which I think this campaign was lacking. Furthermore there is no real reward for completing the game outside of some stances and armor coatings(which were free in every Halo prior). The story also brushes off most of Halo 5's campaign with very little payoff rather than being a cohesive narrative.All in all this game is worth it to try but don't waste your time getting attached things aren't getting better anytime soon, get the campaign on gamepass and don't spend a dime on anything.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok let's get right into it and I'm not going to sugar coat anything. As a preface, I am a long time, 20-year Halo fan who's been positively impacted by Halo and all the experiences that came from it.  I've done it all, split screen and LAN parties all night to finally getting internet to play Halo 3 online when that came out. I absolutely love Halo and everything about it. Therefore, it saddens me greatly to see the current state of Halo (and gaming in general). 343 had 6 years to get this game right, 6 YEARS and they still mostly flopped. By wanting to "reach a broader audience" they watered down and ruined the identity of Halo. This is nothing more than a theft of a beloved IP, using its name to steal money from the consumers. 343 AND Microsoft (yes, we can't only blame 343 because this is Microsofts flagship IP, afterall) ruined this franchise.The only positive things about this game are that the gameplay and campaign are actually pretty decent. Other than that, we don't have Forge and we have no idea when or if that's going to happen, no split screen or co-op campaign, no progressions system, customization is in shambles and locked behind paywalls. It's garbage. They claim that the multiplayer is free to play but is it really? We all know that most of us got the campaign when it came out which was $60. That's the typical price for a game with both single and multiplayer. So really, this "free to play" multiplayer seems like an excuse for Microsoft and 343 to have their atrocious online store and battle pass systems. Absolutely pathetic and disgraceful.Really the whole AAA gaming industry is pathetic and disgraceful. How many more Cyberpunks, GTA Onlines (the current and upcoming plans for it, anyways), Battlefield 2042's, Call of Duty's, and Halo: Infinite's are we going to take before something changes? I don't care if 343 gets this game to a completed state NEXT YEAR because this should have been completed on release. Not having forge, customization, a progression system, theater, split-screen, co-op campaign, etc. is the Battlefield 2042 equivalent of calling a scoreboard and voice-chat "legacy features".Do not recommend and never will until 343/Microsoft/the gaming industry, have finally and truly learned their lesson.**Update** 9/7/22Split-Screen Co-op is no longer in development with no plans to add it. 343 Confirmed via Joseph Staten. _childDocuments_.review: The campaign of Halo Infinite is very fun and interesting with good gameplay as well as a good story. _childDocuments_.review: The Halo Infinite multiplayer is, in my eyes, a marvellous addition to the franchise, encapsulating the core enjoyment that the original games had with balanced armour pickups reminiscent of Halo 3 gadgets, awesome customisation as seen in Halo: Reach. Fortunately, all of it has been understood in Infinite - with a unique set of pick ups like the grapple-shot and the repulsor, as well as custom prosthetic pieces. Additionally, I am enjoying the subdued movement mechanics from Halo 5 e.g. slide and clamber which fit the pacing of each map well.The art style is incredible, taking on a subdued approach to scenery, structures, armour pieces and weapons while still looking visually impressive and interesting. Vehicles look refreshing with the Banished theme being painted over prior covenant themes - which follows the current direction of the campaign.The vehicle and weapon sandbox has been crafted brilliantly with the addition of unique and purposeful weapons like the area of effect and entry denying 'ravager', as well as the spartan laser replacement called the 'skewer', each one being distinct and filling their own role.There is a healthy amount of maps at the moment - 7 arena style maps and 3 BTB maps each one painstakingly detailed (map events will trigger when the objective is completed on BTB maps and arena maps have lots of charm packed into them) and complement the use of the armour pickups and vehicles. I wish that more are added in the future - ensuring that they are unique and play wellThe game has been vastly optimised for me since the preview - I can achieve a consistent 60fps @ 1080p @ medium settings on my RX580 whereas it was barely reaching 30fps @ 1080p @ medium settings a few months ago. The state of the progression system needs to be changed - it is too tedious and unrewarding for how much effort is put in (I could spend a week playing and only receive a few less than desirable items from the battle-pass). Additionally, the challenge based XP system needs to be reworked (or be complemented with a match performance based XP system) to not force players into completing the same challenge over and over... Which becomes monotonous over time.Lastly, the current choice of game-modes seems constrictive at the moment with oddball and slayer being common-place in rotation - would love to see action-sack, infection and swat on release with an option to play specific modes.This addition to the Halo franchise is looking promising in terms of game-play features and overall multiplayer features. If 343 industries can fix the issues surrounding the progression system, this will be stellar game.  If I could give it a review out of 10 at the moment, I would rate it an  (knocking points off at the moment because of the state of the progression system at the moment). I would definitely recommend that you pick it even if you are sceptical as it is free to play right now. I'm anticipating the campaign to be incredible after seeing the variety of weapons, vehicles, environments etc. It has always been my favourite part of Halo.Thanks for reading!

_childDocuments_.review: To be clear: I love the gameplay. This has been the most fun I have had playing a Halo game for a long time.However, I cannot recommend it until some serious work is done on the battlepass progression system. It is the worst battlepass I have ever seen. The issue is that it only gives xp progress through completed challenges, not through playing the game. Medals, wins, and kills mean nothing in this system, and they do not affect your progression at all. The only way to get xp is to do the daily challenge and weekly challenges. These weekly challenges are annoyingly specific and tedious, here's some examples:"Get 5 kills with the BR""Get 5 kills with the shade turret""Kill an enemy that is carrying your flag""Kill an enemy with the Mangler"The daily challenge is "Play multiplayer games" and it requires more games to be played every time you complete the challenge.The daily challenge gives 100xp and the weekly challenges give 200xp. Each level in the battlepass is 1000xp. There are 100 levels, requiring 100,000xp to progress through season one.I found myself doing very well in games and leaving with no xp reward because I didn't complete any of the very specific challenges. The games where I got the most xp are where I was a selfish player and went hunting to find specific weapons the challenges required and played very conservative to get kills. People don't care about the objective because it literally means nothing. You get nothing from playing the objective. You're better off running to the BR spawn, getting 5 kills from across the map, and doing nothing for the rest of the match. Not to mention that many of these require vehicles, and vehicles are only available on certain maps. There is no way to choose which maps to play on nor is there a way to choose what game mode you will be playing other than standard or big team battle. I played for roughly three hours and only managed to get to level 2 in the progression, and that was done while focusing on the weekly challenges. There is no incentive to actually play the game and it shows, as teammates couldn't care less about the objective of the game. There needs to be passive progression of the battle pass, if not, casual interest of this game will die within weeks.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game-to-game gunplay feels very crisp, and the classic utilitarian halo art style is back, the whole game has clearly been designed from the ground up to vacuum money out of players.There is a battlepass system, but you don't even get experience towards it for completing matches. You *have* to complete daily/weekly challenges to get any experience, but even then that's only 100xp per completion, while even trying to get the first level up requires 1000xp. I played for roughly an hour and a half and wasn't able to get past a single level up.On top of that, the game is packed with all manner of cosmetics that can be bought, from armour colour schemes, AI buddies, armour pieces, vehicle colour schemes, cosmetic effects (such as fire), and so on and so on and so on. It's clear that the store is going to be completely packed, and with a single armour bundle costing £16 / $20 (roughly double what it costs to have a full armour ornament set in Destiny 2), it's very clear that the game is free because it allows them to set these prices, rather than having these prices because the game is free.

_childDocuments_.review: While Halo Infinite has certainly improved since its infamously under delivered launch, there are still core issues which persist to the extent that I cannot recommend this game to anyone other than an already devoted Halo fan.These issues include:- Poor optimization for lower end (but still past minimum specs) PCs.- Terrible netcode which severely harms the multiplayer.- Excessively overpriced cosmetics and unfulfilled promises related to them.- Overtuned Skill Based Match Making in nearly every gamemode which either makes every game a sweatfest, or a poor team balance in which one player is expected to carry the rest.Halo is a marvelous multiplayer on paper that turns into a nightmare with these issues where other less fine-tuned games would not suffer as heavily. Where skill and accuracy are vital to succeed, there is nothing more frustrating than a game which will handicap you at every chance.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game on release and it took me a year to actually want to finish it. I honestly find it heartbreaking what 343 has done to the Halo franchise. The fact that we look at Halo Infinite as "one of their better if the not best title " is an actual embarrassment. Halo Infinite is an empty shell of a game with lacklustre gameplay, a boring story and no direction. Mirroring the studio and its direction. This game lacks split-screen something the original had 21 years ago, it lacks dual wielding that Halo 2 had 18 years ago and it missing theatre, forge and playable elites that halo 3 had 15 years ago. Infinite is missing so much even a year later. The only positive I can find in infinite is the art style. The artists (for the landscape of halo and the modelling) tried really hard, and achieved in my opinion, to revisit and retain some of the golden era halo designs with the elites, banished and world. I feel so bad for the people in 343 that try to give halo life when the leading figures are so absent and uncaring towards the franchise. Revisit any documentary on Halo during the days of Bungie the team were passionate, they constantly improved upon the game and they made a satisfying trilogy. I wasn't happy with Halo 4 but thought I'd stick with it. I felt burnt with Halo 5, which is all but forgotten. And I feel like an absolute moron for giving these guys another chance and buying infinite. I've run out of patience and given 343 so many chances but they have wiped out any love I had for Halo. I know whenever they pull together the next mess they call halo I'll still hold a little hope it isn't like this but I'm done. I will never buy another halo game and wholeheartedly encourage everyone to follow suit. Halo is dead.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know if i should recommend the game or not cause of plenty of reasons.First of the gameplay feels very good, feels like an old school halo game.Gunplay is superb just like in older games.However here come my major complaints about the game.The battlepass being something that locks you to do challenges every game makes it feel very unrewarding to actually play the game. Sure they made the challanges easier and added more (if i understand it right) but the challenge system as a whole needs to go.. I want exp from every match not a match where i kill 2 people with a granade. And when you're done with all the challenges you feel a lack to continue playing unless it is to grind ranked. Why they even thought about gatekeeping people like this i have no clue. The tickrate of the servers has to be 24 or worse, i feel like i get shot behind walls constantly when i'm not even in sight of the enemy, this has also been something i've experianced as i kill an enemy where they run behind a wall but die like a second later when they're behind cover. The customization being a bunch of differant armor sets with individual visors/shoulders etc feels like a scam to just resell 3-4 red visors for differant armorsets instead of actually just getting the red visor and being able to use whatever helmet/shoulder/visor etc on a base character. I also feel like this being a "beta" is just something they say aswell. If a game has a functional store with microtransactions it's not a beta.The Matchmaking system where you can't choose a single gamemode you want to play is very strange and feels horrible. Sometime i don't want to capture the flag but is forced to, this is also a big reason alot of teammates leave and makes the game worse for everyone. And people not being punished for leaving games, especially ranked is a joke, i've had 2 games in a row in plat/diamond where the enemy team just all left or 1 player was left behind to fight us 4. Makes the game feel unrewarding for getting a high rank.  After all this i realise that i have way more negative things to type but the gameplay itself carries this into a game i actually recommend. That is if you're not to worried about cosmetics and just want to have some casual fun. For someone who likes customization and likes being competetive i'd recommend against it.*Edit* Removing it from recommended cause after this latest update with the event i just kept crashing and crashing, never happened before. _childDocuments_.review: Before reading, please take note that I am a long time Halo fan, and am biased towards the old games. This has impacted my review in some aspects. I am aware that this game had a rocky development, but the choice to make it a live service free to play game has forced the developers to take business decisions that negatively impact the game as a whole.Upon launch I would have given this game a positive review. It tried to go back to the glory days with the old art style. Initially for me it was enjoyable, however the constant additions to the sandbox and the need to keep the game updated with new content due to it being a live service has disrupted the original sandbox of the game. This for me has changed the game too much and has made some content feel out of place in the Halo setting. I hope that the next Halo game is able to recapture the essence of Halo.Let's break things down.Pros- Great sound design- Beautiful visuals- Decent variety of game modes- Enjoyable campaign with interesting and likeable characters (although it's paid)Cons- Multiplayer sandbox weapon balancing issues, with new weapons often having issues finding their place- FOMO armour customisation and requires an obscene amount of grinding to get the free stuff- Obscenely long loading time (5 mins plus)- Overpriced Microtransations- Ridiculous method of armour colour that requires players to grind or spend money to change the colour- The armour customisation options look ridiculous. Doesn't feel like the grit of Halo, but like a child's game.

name: KeyWe
detailed_description: MORE GREAT FIRESHINE GAMES About the Game KeyWe is a cute, co-operative postal puzzler starring Jeff and Debra, two small kiwi birds working in a whimsical post office. With no hands to help them, they must jump, flap, peck and butt-slam their way across an interactive landscape of levers, bells and buttons to get those messages delivered on time. Encounter perilous postal environments and navigate seasonal hazards while waddling through the Telepost’s various mail rooms, and partner up with a pal to help these adorable kiwis complete their tasks, whatever the weather. Unlock new accessories to customise your kiwi and become the best-dressed mail bird in Bungalow Basin. Take on the role of a postal-working kiwi bird and partner up with a friend to type out telegrams, send urgent messages, ship packages and keep the mail flowing. Buddy up on the couch or flock online. Control both kiwi birds on a single controller to venture out on a solo mail service adventure. Navigate post office desks and shipping rooms to become a master of the mail service. Encounter hazards caused by wintery weather, autumnal thunderstorms and more on the way to becoming postal pros. Change the color of your kiwi’s feathers and unlock new accessories – because kiwi birds look cute in little hats!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fantastic.My boyfriend and I played through the first 32 stages and had an absolute blast with it.  We were also very impressed with the love, care and attention to detail the game exudes as we played.  We also loved how original the game and its game play were.  Nothing about it felt cookie cutter/samey from what we've really seen before and we play games all the time.There are four different types of stages that constantly repeat, each time with new layouts and added/new gimmicks.  Take the second type of stage for example.In these stages, you have to put together notes by picking up different words that have been cut out of a magazine or something and stick them to a piece of paper.  Sometimes words will be whole but other times you take multiple separate parts of words and combine them as a word you're looking for.  The next time, some words could only be made by taking certain whole words, cutting them in two pieces then using them in your combinations.  And the the time after that, you had to shine the words with UV lights to make the words appear.All in all, I definitely cannot recommend this game enough, at least for co-op.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! Me and my boyfriend got it to play cause we were going long distance shortly and we wanted some fun and cutesy games to play. _childDocuments_.review: Having owned and hosted a lot of couch and online co-op games, this has become an often requested game by many of my friends.There's a lot of variety even within the game modes, and the levels themselves. It's undeniably adorable, and well made. I only see one downside, and it's a compliment to the game itself. All my friends want to play, but it's only two player! _childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: This is the ideal game to play with that special person that might not be as skillful as you are when it comes to games.I been trying every type of coop game in steam, and I can tell you with confidence that there’s non other KeyWe, here are some of my reasonsIt feels responsive, jumping moving hopping around It encourages the right amount of synchronicity, by this I mean having to do tasks requiring two players but also giving the option to split tasks and sort of multitasking with 2 brains.The game has simple controls that enable for a lot of interactions. There’s a Peck button, Butt slam button, Chirp button. These drive interaction such as stamping stamps on the packages, writing by butt slamming into the keys, chirping to scare off enemies or to break fights.The visuals are very cute stylized art with a great sense of humour and goofiness.Outside of the campaign which includes 4 seasons you get challenger, hidden trophies, and a sort of task to earn more tickets which are more challenging and new levels Onto the Bad stuffThe camera is not always great in certain level, you might need to move occasionally towards your partner to get both in frameThere are some depth perception specially on the octopus levels which are a minor annoyance.The boxes that you can push around are a bit arbitrary, sometimes you are able to push by just moving other times it requires pecking Some interactions are very tight window time, like tying the saddle ,it barely gives you time.Dash is not used at all which is a shame, I feel if they would move it to the B key on the controller it would be better as well as give it some gameplay purpose other than mobility like pushing boxes, and a better animation to give it some weight.As you can see this is me being too picky. The game is super fun and an easy recommendation for me.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, really quick turnaround time on making a game about the current state of the USPS.They had me at Kiwi. I'm a simple man child, I see a game about kiwis, I buy it immediately. Truth is I love Kiwi birds. I even wrote a paper on them in the 4th grade. The very fact that there's a videogame based on these little creatures makes me SUPER HAPPY!Man this game is a hidden gem and a half. It's kind of like Overcooked and Moving Out in that you work together with other players to achieve a common goal but there's a lot of creativity and unpredictability in the level designs here, like the walking little robots, hazardous plant life, and flying around. It can feel like a fever dream at times, but trust me it starts making sense after ten beers. It’s a fantastic game to play with your wife’s boyfriend or significant other.The level objectives are fun, the hazards are varied, the scattered story scenes are super cute, the cosmetic unlocks are worthy rewards, and the mini-games are meaningful enough to keep coming back to. Overall the game is gold and very cute, it's funny, silly and quite hectic. Just a cute little game where you typewrite with birds, deliver mail, and AVOID SINGULARITIES.If you’re remotely interested I cannot recommend it enough, it is absolutely fantastic, specially if like me you can't afford Mario party....8/10
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: A great game for me and my girlfriend. uses teamwork mechanics well but doesn't force you to use them too often making the natural flow feel just right, with you being able to manage switching between solo tasks and co op tasks seamlessly. This is very important for her and I. With a lot of co op games it seems one person ends up doing all the problem solving while the other awaits instruction or else the problems that make the game fun are too difficult to overcome. Usually leading to frustration and in her and I's case infighting. But not this game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: It's honestly such a cute and cozy game. Perfect to play with your significant other, best friend, sibling... Anyone really. The funniest part of it all though was that my mom, who hates the concept of videogames and lectures me day in day out about how bad videogames are, actually expressed a desire to Watch me play this if not, at the very least Play with me. _childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: KeyWe is so good i really recommend anyone that likes interesting and thoughtful co-op experiences to give this a try, it's a truly unique experience. Even though it stands on its own if i had to compare KeyWe to anything I would say the closest gameplay loop is that of Overcooked where you're trying to complete a common objective and need to work together in order to achieve it. various things need to be done in order to reach that goal and you'll have to decide quickly who is doing what tasks. If you work well with the person you're playing with this obviously makes things a lot easier to manage.That being said if you want to complete every level with the best times you're in for a real challenge here, balanced very well for my taste but maybe overkill for some. I really liked replaying levels to get better scores, but if you're after a more casual experience i think KeyWe caters to that too.I honestly hope KeyWe earns enough in sales so that the devs can either make more KeyWe content or maybe a new project. _childDocuments_.review: Really fun game!Played the co-op campaign. If you like a fun 2 player game this is really fun as 2 cute kiwis have to work together through a variety of levels. Aside from the main campaign, which slowly increases in difficulty, there are also "overtime" challenges which are fun mini-games with lots of variety, as well as a tournament DLC.Really enjoyed playing through all the levels and seeing what new cool gameplay and cute level design we'd find next!To use Overcooked as a benchmark - this game is a bit easier than Overcooked, but could still be challenging if you want to go for the highest scores. It's less chaotic, but the design really focuses on co-op so it's really fun. There is a built in 1 person mode but I can't comment on that since I didn't use it.Highly recommend for people wanting to play a cute co-op game!
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: My GF and I loved playing this game! We had a really good time. The kiwis are super cute, there's lots of cute and silly cosmetic options to select and unlock. _childDocuments_.review: ------- New ------After changing the option so there is no timer, the game is much better, I almost wish it was off by default and mentioned to turn it on for more of a challenge.  This game is a challenge of wits/smarts and you don't have to go alone.Graphics -  are pleasant and colourful.Music - is cute, but after a few games I turned it off.Gameplay - is a little repetitive in a good way, but changes up depending on the map you play.Fun - is great with family or friends.Price - is a little high for a casual game, maybe wait for a special.If we take too long it keeps going now and it's great with friends, even if you mess up your not forced to endure the map with replays.I would highly recommend this game (timer off) with a friend to laugh and have good fun, each season brings something new, love it, and the developer is actively helping out people in the reviews.------- Original Message -------Good game and fun, but I don't like that your on a timer that ends the game instantly with a loss, if you fail you don't get anything for trying.  So if you or your friend are not very good then you will get stuck and never get any incentive to keep trying the level, and no you can't skip levels.If they just allowed you to keep playing after the timer and gave you bottom score it would be more fun to just solve the puzzles and see all the content with my friends. _childDocuments_.review: This was a really fun co-op experience that I highly recommend! I played this with my boyfriend and had a blast!There are several mission types and each type has little variations that build upon each other, so it never feels too repetitive and keeps you on your toes. The missions are not too challenging for anyone familiar with video games. It typically took only two attempts to get a gold mark on a mission, though some were more challenging than others. At no point did it feel frustrating or unfair. The cosmetics are easy to unlock as I found myself drowning in tickets, and the kiwis are so cute!!!The game can be a bit finicky at times, particularly with the platforming and packages. There were many situations where a jump appeared doable but wasn't, or we attempted to move a package and it wouldn't budge (especially with the convener belts). But I never experienced anything game breaking. On rare occasion the mission mechanics were a little unclear, but nothing a quick restart won't fix after you give it a go and figure it out.It took roughly 10 hours to go through all the story missions and obtain gold marks on all of them. I really loved this game and only wish it was a bit longer!

_childDocuments_.review: A fun puzzle game that's entertaining to play with long-distance friends!The puzzles aren't too difficult, and while they have 4 basic premises, each level that repeats has a new gimmick added to switch things up and keep you on your toes. _childDocuments_.review: KeyWe has to be one of the most underrated games I've ever played. It's a cute little co-op game that's equal parts challenging, thought-provoking, and adorable. Pretty much everything about this game feels perfectly balanced—the length, the difficulty, the challenges and rewards—and there wasn't a second when I felt like the game was unfair. It's great that there are also a number of ways to play with others or alone; the game supports local co-op, Remote Play Together, and even has multiple control options for playing solo (if you want to learn Dual-Wield controls, it's quite difficult but very rewarding!). I played through the main storyline with a friend and then went back for the side challenges and achievements by myself, and both ways of playing were equally enjoyable. I also highly recommend getting the Telepost Tournament DLC; it's a great add-on that feels true to the spirit of the main game while also adding content that feels fresh and new. Overall, KeyWe is certainly a hidden gem of a game, and it's absolutely worth playing either alone or with a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

ESPECIALLY if it's on sale. It's one of the cutest coop games I've played in awhile, I really hope there's dlc or a second game, all I want is more because it's so good!! :3
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: It's so nice to be hyped about a game for a year and then it comes out and it's even better than you anticipated. In the sea of disappointing games that have been coming out in recent years, KeyWe shines in perfecting the formula of cooperative madness that you'll find in games like overcooked or moving out. The game's difficulty scales with the progressing seasons, none of the concepts are too difficult to understand but the moving parts can be overwhelming at times. Some of the times to achieve gold medals seem slightly unreasonable considering you may need a partner that you have a semi-psychic link with so you can juggle your half of the load while they equally do their share with minimal verbal communication, but it's all part of the fun.The overtime shift minigames are unique and give a nice change of pace from the rotating 4-5 mission types you typically see in the story. They all are pretty fun to me even if I'm mainly incentivized to play then during bonus pay events or to unlock custom clothing. There are some bugs. Sometimes I've gotten stuck in a wall, but it's very rare and once it happens to you it's generally easy to avoid that particular spot so it doesn't happen again. This game can be played single player, but it's very difficult. I haven't tried the option if controlling both kiwis at the same time with each half of the controller, but I imagine that is just as difficult, if not more, than swapping between kiwi's using a button.If I could change anything, it would be changing the mechanics where both players have to press buttons at the same time in the respective mission types that they're present in. It can kill a gold medal run by a few seconds and input lag introduced while playing this on parsec doesn't help.TL;DR: KeyWe is charming and fun all the way through. I'd recommend it to anyone who has a friend willing to play with them. If you liked overcooked or moving out, you will probably love this game too

_childDocuments_.review: This is such an adorable, clever, and engaging game! Currently playing through it with my brother and it quickly won us over as a new favorite in the same vein as Overcooked and Moving Out. _childDocuments_.review: A wonderful 2P (or 1P if you are willing to multi-task) coop game with a very wide variety of levelsThere's the campaign ("seasons" of sets of 4 levels of 3 main categories, each with a twist) and "overtime" levels, which are intended for cosmetic unlocks but have even more variety (featuring things like a rhythm challenge and trying to steer a cassowary on a race track together) all while being Extra Intense.Speaking of comsetic unlocks, the game has a  of them - with numerous hats, glasses, backpacks, and plumages you can customize your bird a whole lot.Of downsides, online multiplayer can be  buggy (had moving platforms get out of sync on a halloween level due to lag), but nothing show-stopping (have successfully played through every level that there is).

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game instantly. It's cute, it's immediately comprehensible, it offers a reasonable challenge curve, and its core gameplay loop of fluid, cooperative platforming makes it superb for co-op. It might be described as a little like "Overcooked," but a lot less frantic and without its deliberate obstacles to prevent you from getting into a flow. It might not be quite as rewarding in single player, but at least if you have a second player, I heartily recommend it. It does for some reason require room codes rather than letting you just invite via Steam, but it's a trivial obstacle.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: There's about five hours of couch co-op in here that is way more varied than the previews give it credit for. There's three seasons, each with 20-or so levels in them, and they're all substantially different enough from each other that there's always at least a little tiny something new.  There's some silly ones -- like the Halloween-themed one.  There's some annoying and frustrating ones -- like the summer fly invasions or the plumbing one.  There are some that are puzzling -- I don't think we ever would have figured out how to give a hammer to the octopus without seeing five seconds on video.  The only problems I had were the few times I had absolutely no idea what I was doing, as I was unaware I was supposed to be doing a pixel hunt or something.  The other problem was when I mixed up my character with the other player's character.  You're only different in the subtle shade of brown, so I recommend playing around with the seemingly pointless costumes earlier rather than later -- you'll find it easier to tell your characters apart if they're dyed fluorescent colors.  But overall, it's just nice.  There's nothing too stressful about it, there's nothing too difficult about it, it's just a nicely assembled, fun little game. I recommend a purchase, and I think it might be worth its asking price.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: KeyWe is a delightfully fun co-op experience.  Lots of variety and creativity in the levels.  Really nice increase in difficulty, and optimization challenges + achievements as well.  Cool mini-games to boot.  Little bit grindy to get all achievements, though, so be warned about that.  Overall, definitely get it to have some chaotic bird fun for you and a friend.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: God, this game is fun. My friend and I played it together for the first time today and we both agreed it's probably the best co-op game either of us has played. The most stressed you get is rushing around, trying to figure out what you're supposed to do, or what word you need, that sort of thing, but it's never hard on pressure or abuse. The overall aesthetic is charming and being able to customize your kiwi is so much fun. Even the little secrets you have to find to unlock some things are cool - the friendship rock one was a lot of fun, even though it took us a second to figure out what to do. We played through to about the first week, week and a half of Fall, and I'm looking forward to playing it again. Seriously considering getting some of the DLC. This game could easily be worth a cold $40 for the content and quality involved. The ONLY issue we ran into the entire time we were playing was some lag, which my friend said was likely their internet. Seriously, if you love cute games, you love playing with a friend, get it. If you want a more challenging game, try playing solo; if you can speed run on solo, you are definitely a beast. I love being a lil' kiwi running my rural outback post office.

_childDocuments_.review: KeyWe is a lot of fun to play with a friend! The maps change based on season and have new challenges to overcome. The expansion pack is worth it for the challenges and extra items to wear. I would recommend this game to any cozy-core gaming list.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE this game! I played it with my boyfriend, so I haven't experimented with single player yet, but it has been so fun! _childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cute and so wholesome. Each level is diverse and different and really gets the brain juices flowing. Me and my co-op friend alternate frequently between cooing and awwing over the kiwis and just falling over laughing at the game itself because it's so much fun. Definitely requires a lot of coordination but you have so much fun deciding how you'll do things and what jobs you prefer! The hidden collectible challenges are a great addition too. The customisations are adorable and excellent and we've spent just a little while going through various dress ups. Excellent wee game that I thoroughly enjoy playing thank you for making it!!
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: Do you have what it takes to be a fully-fledged post office worker? It's really fun to play with others (I personally play it with someone that lives across the world from me) and it works really well doing that with. There will be shouting and frustrations because just missing a mark or time running out, but as a whole it's all good fun. Also the stages are for the most part filled with neat little hidden things, which makes the whole game feel like a treasure hunt!When it comes to the smal bugs I've encountered, I think they're mostly due to playing with someone from another country. The bugs have been things not loading, and have been easily fixable and nothing game breaking at all. Timing things you should do at the same time can some one be a pain in the butt (because you'll butt slam over and over again).So if you like cute and funky animals, to play games with friends where you have to work together, and puzzle games... _childDocuments_.review: KeyWe is a very fun game for everyone. You control two Kiwis working at the post office. There are a few activities to complete which get progressively more difficult as the game goes on, however, the level hazards keep them fresh and enjoyable. The game runs smooth and looks very good but some more graphical options would be nice. Unfortunately KeyWe is not without flaws. IMO the biggest flaw is how the online play has been implemented... In order to play online a room must be created, once it is set up there's a name generated for it, a guest has to type in that name in order to join. So online is invite only, no online lobbies to play with randoms or matchmaking of any kind. However there is an option to play locally on one machine BUT for some reason the game will only recognise 1 xbox controller, so if You have 2 xbox controllers hooked up, then only one will work correctly. PS4 dualshock 4 and Xbox controllers connected to the same PC work as they should, even showing the correct buttons for PS4 dualshock 4, which is nice. Playing the game solo is an option and You can control both Kiwis using one gamepad by simply switching Kiwis one at a time or by controlling them both at the same time by splitting the controlls (left stick and d-pad and LB LT for one Kiwi, right stick face buttons and RB,RT for the other Kiwi) which is a challenge in itself, making the gold reward almost impossible to get especially later in the game. Kiwi would even go and say that PLAYING WITH ANOTHER PERSON IS A MUST. All in all Kiwi likes the game and will play it later for sure.TL;DR version:Probably the 1st game with Kiwis :3Yes, the game is funYes, it's worth the priceBUTYou need another person to play this locally or via online.Online game is invite only, and there are no lobbies to play it with random people.No microtransaction BS :3for more detailed info read the whole review...yiss...

_childDocuments_.review: I have a weird history with Kiwi birds. I put off getting this game for that reason, but I'm so glad that I did give it a try in the end. I had so much fun playing with my partner that by the time we finished getting all achievements we were saddened to uninstall as there was nothing more that we could do. The game can be completed in about 6 hours if you're really good at it, but for us it was closer to 28 just to get every achievement. It has a really nice difficulty curve that isn't too punishing if you like more relaxed gameplay, and it gives a pretty good amount of time in the first three seasons for you to comfortably beat each level if you're not going for high scores. (If you are having trouble getting gold in some levels, just have patience and be willing to try again. I swear its possible!) when Winter hits, they introduce a time constraint on the levels, however my partner and I found that even that was relatively simple to navigate and we only ended up losing to the timer Once due to encountering a bug (more on that later). There are also cosmetics in the base game for you to unlock, so even if you don't get gold on a particular level, you can still use the reward for silver/bronze to purchase cute skins or wearables, or even unlock them by finding secret collectables throughout the seasons.Now for the bad, the list is short.There are a few bugs throughout the levels, where some are more prone to bugs than others, one in particular was famous for breaking on us. It is a level where you need to type out messages on a holiday themed typewriter, but all the keys are on a carousel and constantly swapping places. While admittedly one of my favorite levels due to this gimmick, it is not without its flaws. Most notably, the keyboard occasionally forgets a random letter. We had to end countless runs while trying to get gold because the letter M refused to spawn in, (M is just an example, it happened for other keys). This is only one bug, of which there are a handful, they thankfully weren't too obtrusive aside from the missing keys, and usually only set us back a few seconds. If you encounter a bug, resetting the level will usually do the trick. On one instance though, I had a massive loss in framerate in one particular level (the overtime sorting mail level) which couldn't be fixed by resetting. I had to close the game entirely, and reopen it, and I never saw it happen again.My one other complaint is, if you purchase the tournaments, and activate all challenges. Its, well, challenging. A little startlingly difficult compared to the rest of the game. in addition to a few of its own bugs, there were many instances of resetting and hair-pulling because the mechanics of the tournaments would occasionally just be TOO much. Perhaps some people like it that way, but as for me, it was my least favorite part of the game.Well, thats about all I have to say about this, TLDR is I'm really glad I decided to pick this up, it ended up becoming one of my favorite coop games probably ever and was a really fun experience that brought me and my partner closer in a really stressful time of our lives. Thank you for reading, and, if you haven't already,TRY THIS GAME! :)

_childDocuments_.review: So my wife and I are super addicted to co-op games and as soon as I saw cute little Kiwi birds I knew we had to try it :)That being said, we had a pretty good time playing KeyWe. As of now, her and I have 7 hours invested and the main story is all done. That is, of course, the time it took us to play through all the levels just trying not to fail them and perfecting every level by any means. Dunno if you'd call 36 levels and 7 hours short, but take that however you want. Getting gold on the levels is hard as ♥♥♥♥. Neither me nor my love have the patience to do that LOLI will just say that the game has a couple of weird things with it that are worth mentioning if you're reading reviews before buying, so i'll put them here:1. Check the collectibles!! My wife and I totally forgot about them until after we beat it. (the game won't tell you about it.) Doing the collectible tasks give you, in my opinion, the cooler cosmetics than what the game originally allows you to buy with your tickets. They are worth doing.2. The Overtime shifts are extra content for you and your duo to play if you want, so very much optional content. However, they also hold some of the cooler cosmetics you can earn. They are grindy as hell though and even with my wife and I playing them 1-2 times every time we opened the game to play, we never unlocked a single one. (they really should be a smidge easier to earn)3. A big selling point of KeyWe is that the game functions a lot like a "do order and get point" game (like Overcooked or Moving Out) but every level is so different you really don't notice the repetition. You learn how to send letters in one level and the next level you need to send letters while the entire room is full of sand or frozen over. I wanted to point this out because that means almost every level you play, you will have to read some sort of tutorial. The controls will always be the same, but get comfortable with things spinning, swapping places, or flying around the room for the rest of the game! :DOverall, I'd recommend giving KeyWe a go if you enjoy an ever changing, somewhat challenging, cooperative experience that also includes being a silly little bird that can wear a top hat :)

_childDocuments_.review: A coop-based game, in which you’re tasked with controlling two kiwis running various tasks in a post office.This game is in essence a collection of timed platforming challenges, in which you control the titular flightless birds who, in addition to jumping and running of course, can dash and interact with objects by pushing, pulling and carrying them as well as squeak and butt-stomp to activate certain mechanisms. While it’s recommended to grab a friend to get the most out of KeyWe, you can also choose to play solo, with the option of either controlling both characters at once or switching between them at the press of a button. With the latter options, the game adjusts any time and score requirements, meaning you’re not at a disadvantage.KeyWe’s main content is found in 3 different challenge types, tasking you with transcribing telegrams, assembling letters and sorting mail. While these start off being rather basic, the game introduces a bunch of modifiers to these basic premisses, changing their layouts, implementing stage hazards and adding more and more complexity to the tasks you’ll have to perform. Through this, the game creates a total of 36 genuinely unique-feeling levels making up a campaign divided into 3 seasons.Each level has a time limit and requires a certain number of tasks to be fulfilled, requiring a decent level of coordination and quick thinking from both kiwis, which can oftentimes become quite frantic, especially when playing with a friend. The time limit certainly isn’t too strict, giving you plenty of room to mess up but also providing quite a challenge if you want to go for the top times. The latter is incentivized, as better performance is rewarded with a larger amount of currency, which you can spend on various cosmetics, ranging from colourations and plumage styles to hats, backpacks and more.Additional stamps can also be earned by completing various mini-games which become available as you progress through the campaign and reward you stamps based on the score you manage to rack up in a limited time. Additionally, there are a number of hidden collectibles spread throughout the game’s main levels, giving you some neat optional challenges and rewarding you with different exclusive cosmetics.There’s a notable DLC, being “The 100th Grand Ol' Telepost Tournament”, which introduces three racing challenges. These task you with completing a string of tasks and reaching a finish line as quickly as possible. All of the tasks feel rather unique, either putting new spins on existing activities or introducing completely new mechanics for you to manage. Each race also allows you to add certain modifiers, handing you more tasks to keep track off but also giving you a decent head-start. Overall, this does a lot to shake up the regular gameplay and offers some good additional challenges while remaining quite fun.As for presentation, KeyWe oozes charm, constructing a wonderfully wacky world around its basic premise that manages to feel quite cozy. Cosmetics and the set dressing for the various levels have a lot of love put into them, resulting a playful and frankly fun atmosphere. All of this is complemented by the rather neat and inviting art style and some charming flavour text spread throughout. While the game’s controls can be a bit wonky at times, this rarely resulted in frustration for me.Overall, I had a great time with KeyWe and can only recommend grabbing a friend and giving the game a shot.Note: I was pleasantly surprised to see a lot of effort being put into the game’s localization. I used the German version, which impressively features non-trivial gameplay adjustments, such as adding additional buttons for letters not present in the English alphabet.

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to like this game. I did enjoy the initial play-through of this game. I cannot recommend this game. KeyWe's issue is consistency or the lack there of. Routinely, there are actions that both players need to do at the same time. The game is not consistent with what "at the same time is," sometimes a countdown works, sometimes it doesn't. Maybe this is a server lag issue, but for a multiplayer game there needs to be something that corrects for that to be fun.A key issue with this lack of consistency is the challenge system. There are three levels of completion for each level that you get for beating the level in under a certain time. As a completionist, I think this is a great idea! It adds replayability and makes you real master the systems. Having almost no extra time for the highest level, that is also a fun thing, makes you REALLY master the level. Loosing that timing because of inconsistent inputs so you just miss the target time, not fun.The straw that broke the cassowary's back was the new challenges. There are so many little pieces of randomness that some of the challenges just feel like luck to beat. One that requires memorising labels, that is fun and challenging. "Don't let the red or purple mayflies steal anything," then have those flies b-line to the player and grab them out of the air when there is nothing to be done, not fun.Thanks for reading my rant, and I hope the devs find a way to reduce the random in the game. _childDocuments_.review: An absolutely  co-op affair where two kiwis join forces to take over a postal office. Yes, you read that right. It’s as challenging, chaotic, and adorable as it sounds.Challenges cover what you’d expect to be doing at an old timey postal office. That is, typical tasks done in highly atypical ways by operating makeshift contraptions. Mostly, it’s about mastering the art of language. For example, one challenge has you packing boxes, using a flimsy telegram to infer where it needs to go and what labels to stick on it. Another challenge has you chopping up words into syllables to form new messages that need to be transcribed. The amount of content here is pretty amazing. Some games throw vanilla puzzles at you and up the difficulty in pretty predictable ways as you go along. KeyWe transforms its initial puzzles, theming them around distinct seasons, holidays and weather conditions, introducing whole new mechanics into the mix. A thunderstorm charges your character and restricts what mechanisms can and can’t be tampered with. During halloween, trick-or-treaters throw wrenches in the machinery if you don’t feed them candy. All that’s on top of what you’ve already grown accustomed to doing.It’s one of those games that’s just a joy to take part in. It’s fatiguing in a way few games are -- in a good way. It requires some brain power, and that brain power runs out surprisingly quickly. Sort of like in Overcooked, when you’ve played too long and the basics start to slip; when you start making silly mistakes, dragging your friend down with you in pure laughter.Highly recommended if you enjoy goofy slap-stick in your co-op games with great challenge levels to reach for and a pretty wide range of content.

_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very cute and very fun! Played it with my fiance and we both love this game. I highly recommend this game, especially if you have someone to play it with! _childDocuments_.review: This game is an absolute blast! I was browsing co-op games to find a new title for my wife and I to play when I stumbled across this one. When viewing screenshots, I had a hard time judging what type of game it was. Is it a typing simulator? A word/puzzle game?Then I saw a review that mentioned Overcooked/Movin' Out and I was sold. Indeed, it is very much in line with Overcooked. This game will have you and your partner/friend/online stranger(?) rushing about, pecking, chirping, and butt-slamming buttons, stamps, stickers, and labels to send off messages, mail, and packages. There are four distinct level types, and the game progressively adds new challenges and twists to those. In some levels you and your partner will be doing the same tasks (i.e. the typerwriter-style level) but in other levels you'll find distinctly different tasks that may be better suited to a particular player (i.e. the mail/package sorting level). In addition to the levels, there are "Overtime Shifts" which include an assortment of arcade-style levels you can complete for extra tickets. We have unlocked eight of these currently, which include silly-fun levels like popping bubblewrap, feeding ostrich-like birds, and playing music.For extra fun, you get to use the tickets you earn to spruce up your lil' KeyWe bird with new colors, feathercuts (haircuts), backpacks, spectacles, and hats.This game does not have enough love. Buy it now. Review it. Share it with your friends.P.S. This is the first game I've tried through the Remote Play Together and it works wonderfully.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: Only played a few hours but it's fun as heck! It's basically many mini games that require team work and a bit of co ordination. Each season has several "work weeks" at the post office, there's bonus rounds and you have opportunities of trying to beat your highscore. Highscores mean stamps. Stamps also mean outfits! ;_; it's too cute!You can play solo or with someone else. Honestly it's great co-op game and there is an official Discord for people to find KeyWe mates :)
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: While the game is advertised for coop, I decided to try out the game because it was really cute and looked like a lot of fun. Even though I am still able to play this game on low graphics, it will be important to note that I am not using a gaming computer so some things that might run smooth for others are still doable for me. With that in mind, I'll give my perspective.Usually I don't really write reviews but I do feel like it's important to give this game a review because it mentions that solo play is also possible. It is possible; you just need to be really coordinated or have some kind of strategy in mind if you play alone. It has two different options: hot swap and dual play. Hot swap is basically switching in between both kiwis. It's doable and easy when you're simply swapping in between kiwis, but takes some getting used to. The controls are a bit hard to be exact when using a keyboard and the controller was a lot easier for me to use. It was do able to keep swapping... until I got to level 8, which was the mail room with vines.The game is already difficult to navigate with two characters and the tutorial mentions that having two kiwis pull the package out of the vines makes it easier. However, I was only controlling one character and trying to pull it out of the vines. You eventually pull it out, but it makes things a little more difficult when several things could be happening like vines snatching the other kiwi or vines snatching the other mail. I decided to see if I could try the dual play option.Dual play was also doable, but it takes a lot to get used to when you start changing sides with particular kiwis. However, I ran into a bug of sorts - that being from the introduction of bugs. While I was replaying of the levels with the controller, one kiwis got snatched and I had to free them. Spamming the left trigger was a bit difficult, but then the controls suddenly changed from left trigger to square (I was using a PS4 controller). When I got free, I ended up controller both kiwis with the left stick and the square button. I couldn't control the other kiwi with the right stick. I ended up scrambling the controls at some point after I left that level and I tried to replay the mailroom with vines, which changed controls as one kiwi being controller and the other being the keyboard.While it is a fun game, I don't know how viable solo play is despite only playing for less than 3 hours. The hardest aspect is that most games allow you to change the controls; in this game, there's pretty much only one set up you could pick with specific keys. There is no way to change them.TLDR: You're better off playing coop than solo because some weird bugs can pop up when you play solo.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: A new contender for the most adorable game on Steam. Simple but unique gameplay except the only problem is that you really need a buddy to play it with for the full experience.I've also been told by my Aussie friend that this is 100% historically accurate on how Australia works, or New Zealand, I don't know it's still in my backlog of to-read fantasy novels.
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: Tested on Pop_os 21.04: once some bugs within the general game were fixed, it was all smooth sailing. Linux players rejoice!Absolutely lovely co-op game. It starts out mellow and easy enough but good luck getting all gold in Winter: it requires really tight teamwork with no room for slip-ups.Besides some small clipping issues getting you stuck in places where you shouldn't be from time to time everything worked great. Never had any problems in local co-op with 2 wireless Steam controllers.I can't comment on online/remote play but if you're looking for a fun local co-op game, you can't go wrong with this one!
_childDocuments_.name: KeyWe

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed this game a lot, I purchased it to play with my long distance boyfriend. It was a lot of fun even if we both got frustrated with eachother sometimes. There are no Spring levels which is extremely odd as the rest of the seasons are in the game and when you are done with those there isn't much to do.
