_childDocuments_.review: More than 2 years since launch, All You Can Eat is still littered with critical bugs, whether it be connection errors or gameplay bugs, All You Can Eat is an inconsistent experience. You would expect a well polished game, it being a repackaging and remaster of previously released content, but this isn't the case. Apparently Team17 and Ghost Town missed the memo that their product is a co-op game where most players will be playing with others over the internet, yet the game's online infrastructure has zero stability and missing critical features. You can't mix players from public matchmaking with invitees, so enjoy manually hunting for partners all over the internet if you're looking for players to fill empty slots. The major campaigns are mostly bug free but all the side content suffers from match ruining bugs and constant disconnections. 4 player games are as stable as a critical nuclear reactor and in every session is an inevitability that your game will ♥♥♥♥ itself at some point. My absolute favorite part is being unable to connect to Team17's servers for multiple days straight ruining an entire weekend that was meant for playing with friends. What I find most insulting is that these problems are as old as the game itself and the developers have not made any effort in squashing these critical bugs.All You Can Eat's technical failures are saddening because there is a genuinely great game beneath the bugs.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Good game if you never bought the previous two games, multiplayer issues galore even for 2 devices using the same gigabit internet, feels like an intentional monetary roadblock on those who cant afford to buy the game a third time and could easily be solved by allowing crossplay with the previous versions.Overall it is a good game, but it has its issues. Multiplayer can be a bit laggy(even when both of the players have gig internet) a good example of this is when my wife and i play on our separate PCs using the same connection, we should not have any latency issues specially on google fiber but we do. Second issue with this is the lack of crossplay support when it comes to those who own previous copies of the Overcook 1&2, it isnt fair to have had to purchase the games separately only to have to rebuy an "HD update with a dozen or so new levels" at full price, I am aware that there was a discounted price when the game released for those who had the previous versions but it still isnt fair for those folks who are on a budget and cant afford to rebuy the same game. Let alone be roadblocked by the developer not affording a bit more time to enable crossplay with the other versions of the game with other players. This huge issue basically blocked a good chunk of friends who had the other two games to not being able to play with us. _childDocuments_.review: I'm a major Overcooked fan. I have every level in 1, 2, and all DLCs 3-starred, and I enjoy them immensely. I've been looking forward to this game for months, and the day it came out, I paid $40 for a game that includes 7 actual new levels, and the chance to play the original Overcooked without having to rely on how horrible steam remote play is. I was immediately disappointed with the lack of consistency of development, as they neglected their keyboard and mouse users by making it impossible to bind mouse buttons to any of the controls. They've since fixed this, but because I have 200 hours using either a switch controller (which I still think doesn't work) and keyboard and mouse, i didn't want to relearn the controls to complete the same exact levels. I reinstalled after the original hotfix, and to my delight, not a single online function works on my computer! I'll give their support team props for trying to help me, but their public discord shows dozens of other people struggling with the same issues I've had since the game's release. Overall, it feels extremely buggy, unfinished, and overpriced for something with major online functionality problems, less control support than its predecessors, and very little actual new content. I'm likely refunding again if I can't play a couch co-op online.
_childDocuments_.name: Overcooked! All You Can Eat

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game ever. I LOVE the Overcooked! series and own every title multiple times over. I bought the AYCE version on sale and it's been totally awesome. I love the added accessibility features, mainly the lack of camera motion on the Overcooked! 1 content. It would be nice to have these improvements pushed as an update to the older games though. The new levels in AYCE are super fun. The game runs and looks great. I would very much recommend buying this game to anyone. The reason for my negative review is that one of the biggest advertised features of AYCE is the online functionality. This has not worked well at all for me. Matchmaking options are practically nonexistent and the gameplay is unacceptably laggy. Specifically, it takes way too long to register interacting with objects when you're not the host. Also there's weird rubber banding when dashing. This makes harder levels feel outright unplayable. It shouldn't be too hard to just trust all of the clients game states completely? It's not the end of the world if an item gets duplicated? This is arguably significantly worse. I love the franchise, this has to be one of my favorite games of all time. I primarily play with friends locally, and for that this edition of the game is basically perfect. I'm just a bit disappointed in the online functionality. If you plan to play alone or with other people physically with you, BUY THIS GAME IT'S AWESOME. If you're buying it for the online functionality, don't.TLDR-- Awesome game for playing with people locally or alone, I consider the online mode to be unplayable though

_childDocuments_.review: YOU ABSOLUTE DONUTReal talk. The game is Overcooked 1 and 2 with all the DLC repackaged. Some visual optimizations have been done but it's not all that different of an experience from the other games. If you already own the other two, it's likely not worth the purchase. The ONLY reason I'm purchasing this game is because of the inclusion of cross-platform multiplayer: I have a niche case where netplay options like Steam Remote Play Together and Parsec aren't viable. In my view, there isn't anything else here at launch that would convince me to buy.Don't get me wrong, it's a good game. It doesn't give much value beyond the original games, but if you haven't played Overcooked before, this is a fantastic bundle. _childDocuments_.review: Claims to be the ultimate Overcooked! experience and more or less delivers on that for me so far. It has everything the first two games contained plus a smattering of new levels, and for the first time in the series offers crossplay between consoles and PC.The remastering of the levels from Overcooked 1 to bring them visually in-line with 2 is pretty much perfect. They look great and the new graphical flourishes do nothing to interfere with the gameplay, couldn't really ask for it to be done any better. I've seen some complaints they don't go a step further and add in gameplay changes from the sequel, namely throwing items around, but playing it for a half hour will pretty quickly make it apparent that doing so would break the balance as a lot of the levels are built entirely around the players not having a simple way to pass ingredients or objects to eachother across any sort of obstacles/distance. Have yet to dig into 2's levels beyond a quick glance to see how it looked versus the first games' ones, and haven't gotten to the new ones yet either - but looking forward to tackling both after I'm done 3-starring everything in 1 with my friends. The crossplay is the one point of contention I've had so far with this remaster collection. While it isn't anywhere near broken for me as others have reported it to be for them, I and my friends are playing with a mixture of Switch and PC players and have had one or two odd issues so far where a loading screen before returning to the main menu will seemingly get stuck and require a restart. I'm not sure if this is an issue with the multiplayer specifically or some other issue with one of our connections that catches everyone else in the party when it happens, but I didn't see it while I was tooling around with the game solo. Overall though it's been reasonably stable and smooth once we're all in a game together - so I can deal with the odd hiccup that might not even be down to the game specifically. Strongly recommend this for anyone who wants a prettier version of Overcooked! 1, a compilation of 2 with all the dlc, and a way to play Overcooked with their friends on consoles.

Game won't tell you what you did wrong, game won't tell you how you should be doing it. And there is no tutorial (a tutorial for playing with an already connected controller.. like come on).Here is how it works for me, in case anyone struggles as well:I use an old XBOX360 controller from like 10 years ago with one of those adapters and one of those later versions of the PS4 controller. Both controllers connected correctly with Steam, I know because I could navigate Steam Big Picture with either of them. I was able to start the game but only the XBOX controller was able to get past the start (Press A/Spacear) screen. PS4 just would not work and google search gave me the answer eventually (after way to much time spent on this, which should not be a problem in the first place). Solution: Plug it in via USB. Who would have thought, that this might be a problem in the year 2021. Would have refunded the moment I relized that but since my gf loves the game I'll keep it and play it with her. Shame on every developer that is unable to include a proper Controller on PC feature. Oh an also: No Playstation controller symbols? I know both is used... how about include them both like A/X or B/O. Since.. you know.. / are a thing and people can distinguish what's used for what. And no, it is not about "just memorize, can't be that hard". It is about accessibility and people who barely ever have a controller in their hands.What a mess.

_childDocuments_.review: Overcooked! is the first game that comes to mind when i think of the quintessential co-op experience, i've played Overcooked! with my friends and girlfriend going for highscores to playing with my parents and trying to scrape through each level teaching them the game while laughing as the kitchen burns down amongst the chaos. I think the trailer does a good job of showcasing what the game is about so i won't go in depth here, the basics are working together with your group to cook and deliver various meals to customers, This starts out simple but toward the end will really test your co-ordination and teamwork skills if you're looking to get the maximum star rank on each level. The game offers a gigantic variety of recipes and stages to play on with new mechanics or hazards to consider. If you like the gameplayloop you won't be disappointed with the huge amount of content on offer here. I really could sit there all day making ramen in the giant woksWhile the game certainly won't click for everyone i feel Overcooked! appeals to a wide range of ages and skill levels, i've played the series with different people trying to achieve very different goals but the common factor is that it has always been a fun time. A must buy for any co-op fans library

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR Definitely get this game if you want to play Overcooked online, even if you own the previous games. Controller issues have been resolved.This is the best online Overcooked experience. What it feels like is they switched to using a dedicated server instead of having one host (in Overcooked 2), which was a nightmare of latency for anyone who wasn't hosting. While the new setup does introduce some weirdness from time to time, overall it's a far better experience than Overcooked 2. What's more, crossplay works flawlessly (I've been playing with friends who have the Switch version). While there were some issues initially upon launch (unable to crossplay, broken controller support), both have since been resolved, and it's been a great experience so far. It's a shame that some of the old music was replaced, but the gameplay has definitely been refined (Overcooked 2 engine, which means you can pick up cooked hamburger patties with just a bun instead of needing a plate, for example; this was impossible in Overcooked 1)

_childDocuments_.review: Overcooked! All You Can Eat is an absolute riot! This game is hands down one of the most entertaining experiences I've had. Sure, you might run into the occasional bug, but they're minor blips in an otherwise fantastic game. What truly sets it apart is the sheer amount of content it packs in, combining all the levels and kitchens from both Overcooked games. This means you're in for a ton of gameplay, and that's always a good thing.However, what makes this game truly shine is the chaotic fun it delivers when you play with friends. It's not just about cooking; it's about laughter, frustration, and the challenge of working together seamlessly. Your friendships will be put to the test, and it's a brilliant way to see just how well you and your buddies can coordinate under the pressure of a busy kitchen. Overcooked! All You Can Eat is not just a game; it's a friendship forge. I can't recommend it enough for anyone looking for an unforgettable time with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Overcooked is what made couch co-op games big again. Overcooked! All You Can Eat brings you the first, the second, and all its DLCs in one game.Everyone reading this probably knows what Overcooked is about but if not: You and up to three friends need to work together to cook as fast as possible. There are dozens of different receipts and several machines to use. You need to take care of cutting vegetables, cooking, deep fry, baking, dish out the food, wash the dishes, and a lot more at the same time or shortly one after another.is everything since you won't have a lot of it. Costumers will get angry quickly which means, if you need too much time, you will lose points. To advance in the story (and unlock new levels) you need a certain amount of stars (similar to games like Crash Bandicoot).Well, I said time is everything but in fact, communication is everything. If you can't communicate well enough, you won't be successful as a team. Overcooked is what games like UNO and Monopoly were before. You will scream at each other and get angry but the main difference is: If you are successful in the end: All of this will be forgotten. If you aren't successful, this could be the last time you saw your friend. There are over 200 levels and over 80 different cooks (they just differ in looks). With a playtime of around 20 hours (More if you want four stars in every level or play against each other), there is enough to do. They are also adding more free content such as cooks and levels (the next update will be in August). You can play online with friends or strangers on different consoles, together on your couch, invite friends through remote play (they don't need to own the game), and use keyboards, all kinds of controllers, or the steam remote app. You can even decide to share ONE controller with a friend. This way, everything gets even more confusing. I did try to play online but found no other players. I also read several times now that there is a bug and you can't even play online. I can't say for sure but you should know before buying it (especially if you intend to play online!). A higher resolution, more FPS, the graphics got updates (especially the first game), new cooks, and a few new levels. That's about it. Overcooked! All You Can Eat is everything you're looking for if you want a couch co-op game. It has a lot of content, still gets free updates, is playable in different ways, and is just fun overall. It's the best of its genre. A masterpiece. But be careful: If you want to play online with a friend on a different console wait for more updates as it seems that this is bugged right now. If you want to play online via steam, you can use the remote play feature instead of the online lobby. Also, if you already own the base games, there is really no need to buy this one.Otherwise, I definitely recommend getting this if you're looking for a couch co-op game. It regularly gets on sale!

_childDocuments_.review: Will preface by saying I love this franchise, and have bought each game and DLC prior on both PS4 and Steam. So, bias laid bare, to the review:If you've never played Overcooked before, this is an incredible deal at $40 for all the content. Over 200 levels, with couch or online co-op for up to 4 players, as well as crossplay with other platforms. It's quite fun for both casual party play, and the more hardcore competitive end has a scene as well. overcooked.greeny.dev tracks high scores, and the Overcooked League Discord hosts no-stakes tournaments to test your skill against other teams in a somewhat live sense.If you HAVE played every Overcooked game and DLC prior to this, it may be hard to justify the price tag. What you add is online play for OC1 levels, more chefs to play as, 7 brand new levels, somewhat better load times, and having everything in one package. I got a 15% dicount for owning all prior content. While not much, with how much play time I've gotten out of the series thus far, I was happy to support the dev more. So use your best judgement if the moderate convenience improvement is worth it to you.There ARE currently some bugs that need working out with connectivity, though my personal experience hasn't been a dealbreaker. Hopefully these will be fixed in the future.Another issue I hear of is bad controller support. I personally run 8bitdo with my PS4 controller emulated as a 360 controller, and have no issues with that. I'd do some research on it depending on your setup.Overall, while there's some launch issues, I still highly recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: So content-wise I love Overcooked 1&2, I have played both games with friends and am always looking forward to content updates. This game unfortunately is NOT optimized for PC controller play. I have never had this issue with Overcooked 2 so when it felt like my character was moving through sand on screen, I was really disappointed. My character will slide without me moving it, glitches all over the screen, and just in general has zero accuracy when trying to place/chop/throw anything. I am so confused as to how this came after Overcooked 2 which has just been a fantastic experience. I understand it is basically a combination of the two games, but clearly something was done RIGHT with OC2 that was just not implemented in All you can eat. It needs to be fixed, because this is an absolute chore to play with friends.Edit 10/15/2022:So this game has gotten better since it's first launch although it has never played as smoothly as OC2 did which still baffles me. This recent update (world food festival) really feels like it was not properly played through before release. I don't play solo so all my experiences come from both hosting as well as joining my friend's game (we tested both to see if the issues were lag-related or game related). We played through all levels once to 3 star and then again to 4 star and the issues were consistent through each playthrough. This update has ridiculous bugs that I have never experiences on any other level.1. Our characters frequently dropping or throwing food without prompt, and I MEAN frequently2. In 1-2 specifically the amount of times items were dropped or thrown was ridiculous, thought it might have something to do with the stairs3. Collision with other characters as well as fire was ridiculously exaggerated, simply bumping into a player would throw them off the map and cause a re-spawn, even if we were nowhere near an area on the map we could fall (1-2 get kicked from the sink area to the water, 1-3 from multiple areas)4. On 3-1 & 3-2 the score system and stars are screwed, show 0 and what you score doesn't matter, you get 3 or 4 stars without actually getting a high score (tested), does not show you what score you have to get to reach each star at the start of the level either5. On 3-4 specifically the delivery guy is just stuck, doesn't move, and his box is not reachable. We tried throwing the items into the box to get something to happen but the box looked bugged too so we gave up and played around the delivery guy6. This is minor compared to everything else but emoting was bugged and players couldn't hear their own character emote 1/2 the timeI look forward to every update because I genuinely enjoy this game and the games that have come before it. These kinds of bugs make playing very hard to enjoy though, and I honestly expect OC2 level gameplay given it clearly worked well.

But at least you don't have to bear higher price if you buy this game nowOne thing though, I noticed that this game causes my laptop to overheat easily. The first time I played this game (2 months ago), my laptop overheated like crazy, it went shut down by itself, with a weird sound of charge. I reckon that variable FPS during gameplay is one of the factors of this issue]I really hope that the devs do something about this overheating issue. To the devs, make sure that this game really worth the high price Pros:-Better graphics and UI-You don't have to buy DLCs from OC and OC2 to play them-The camera doesn't zoom in even if you play solo (a huge problem in original OC)Cons:-Crossplay and matchmaking doesn't work (not that you'll mind if you play solo lol)-You won't get certain achievements if you play solo :(-Overheating issueTL;DR: If you support Overcooked, usually plays solo and have decent gaming computer, go for it! May not worth it for now, but it will in the futureUpdate: I have just bought myself a gaming PC, and I have enjoyed this game a lot. Of course, I play other games as well, but I really enjoyed the latest birthday update. Sure, the last level is quite frustrating to get 4 stars, but it is supposed to be challengingTbh, I feel sorry for Overcooked team because of the recent backlash, especially from Twitter. Sure, the damage has been done, but I still have faith in this game. I really hope that the dev team will make things right and bring this game back to its glory days, just like how my other favourite game () were used to fall in popularity last year, before giving great comeback with great updates this year

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game at half price during Team17's publisher sale. Before this purchase, I owned Overcooked! 2 without any DLCs on the Nintendo Switch. This game is great fun with friends, definitely, just like the other Overcooked! games. The assist mode is a very welcome addition, especially because not all of my friends game a lot or are familiar with controller games. It prevents everyone from getting frustrated on a nice afternoon. It also makes playing with younger kids much easier, as the game gets much harder further into the story. I would recommend getting AYCE to anyone who hasn't previously purchased one of the games and want to have some (chaotic) fun with friends. I personally don't regret buying AYCE on Steam mostly because OC!2 on my switch can serve as a more portable method of playing as I could bring it to someone else's, and for the price of the original Overcooked! plus a bit more, I get to play the original AND all DLCs (in addition to the OC!2 I already have) on my PC, which I think is better than on a switch. However, if it wasn't on sale, I might be a bit more hesitant when it comes to this purchase. I probably will not recommend this game, especially when bought at full price, to someone who already has at least one previous game (OC!1 or OC!2) and on the same platform. Unless you intend to play with someone online and cross-platform often, or just want to collect them all, you could probably just stick to what you have right now, especially if you've bought DLCs before.

_childDocuments_.review: This one looks better, has more content than Overcooked 2 and has crossplay support. It includes Overcooked 2, Overcooked 1, all DLCs and a few exclusive levels. Furthermore you can play with friends around the globe without worrying about finding a host that doesn't lag. There will be lag and glitches still but it seems to be very likely that it isn't unplayable anymore when your friend is on the other side of the continent since this is server based instead of peer to peer. If your friend is near your city and you got a good connection already you might experience more glitches with All You Can Eat compared to Overcooked 2 though. However I would say it is still better than Remote Play Together. Currently it seems to be harder to find players in arcade mode than in Overcooked 2 but that might change in the future.The game doesn't feel polished yet especially when a patch fixes issues but introduces new game braking bugs for other players. Considering the slow update rate (1 week to fix controllers partially) maybe the devs should think about taking advantage of the beta release option to further test their updates after QA is done with their tests.

_childDocuments_.review: "Overcooked! All You Can Eat" is a fantastic party game, perfect for playing with friends either locally or online. The game's simple mechanics are ideal for a party setting, yet they lead to some of the most chaotic and hilarious moments I've ever experienced in a team-based family game. The shouting, laughing, and memories created while playing this game are truly outstanding.However, the game's patches for common issues leave much to be desired. On my old PC, my controller wouldn't work with this game, and I found many others had the same issue online, with no available fix. It wasn't until I got a completely new PC that the game finally worked with my controller. The support for the game could definitely be improved.Despite this, I've had a tremendous amount of fun with "Overcooked! All You Can Eat" and continue to do so. The content is bursting at the seams with numerous levels and varying difficulties, offering a nice break from the more challenging stages when needed.Overall, I'd rate it 9/10 based on enjoyment and experience. It's so good that I even bought it for my Switch!

First, the tracking on tiles could be improved. The magnetizing nature of things like the frying pans and rice pots could be better, as there were a couple times when, instead of grabbing them, I'd accidentally grab the item behind me, that was still highlighted even though I was turned away from it.And the other thing, it's minor, but punctuation in dialogue sequences should be revised. I would understand if it was a stylistic choice, but throughout the game, it seemed inconsistent; some sentences would end with a full stop, some wouldn't. Again, super minor, but I think it could still be improved.Other than that, great game! I loved playing the first game with my partner, and I'm looking forward to the throwing mechanics and whatnot in the second one.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouse/keyboard controls are badly implemented. The game doesn't always display the correct prompt for a custom keybind, and you might get stuck with duplicate keys because the menus seem to use some of the defaults + some of the ones you set. This is all on top of simply not having an analog stick for better directional control.Single player is iffy at best. You don't *have* to get great scores to progress, but it's frustrating trying to get the right rhythm.  It almost feels like you'd be better off trying to control each chef individually, simultaneously, by using a pair of separate one-handed fighting game or flight simulator sticks. The game's tile-based interactables (food, plates, everything) are *very* touchy, and being trapped in a clunky isometric-view chef character makes even the simplest tasks require a lot of precision, although this could be mostly due to using keyboard controls.

_childDocuments_.review: ================================== The Only Review You Will Need ================================================================= Warning Long Read, but full context review ============================================================= Game is being Review Bombed, Negatively ================================I'm a long time player of this franchise. I'm a huge fan of the series. Why am I putting this out there? 2 Reasons. First and foremost my review will be biased. Secondly, I have seen the changes and improvements over time and can speak to the mess that's happening here.  That being said, Overcooked 1 was a great game, it was probably the first game in a long time I can remember that was coop, that had me frantically running around screaming, but having fun without actual combat. I mean, I genuinely replayed levels to get higher scores and for sheer fun factor, not just to beat the game. I enjoyed it enough I set up a portable PC to share the experience with family, and later picked up a copy on the Nintendo switch. There were certain features and ingredients everyone wished we had in the first one. Mainly ONLINE play, (not be limited to LOCAL Coop, meaning stuck on the same couch / device) Going back to the drawing board the developers did just that, they gave us everything we wanted and more with Overcooked 2, different ingredients, processing methods, more chef's, and finally online COOP. So it was a big success. They even added DLC, both free and paid. Then they made Overcooked 1 free periodically. To be honest if you have a steam copy at that point you could play remotely via steam remote play, so it was less an issue, but still it's better to have the functionality in the game. Me personally, I wanted even more complex foods, and an endless mode, but the game more than delivered. I also picked up a copy of Overcooked 2 on switch just for convenience and to support the developers.Moving on to the present. No one asked for Overcooked: All You Can Eat, but it was a nice surprise. Here we have Overcooked 1 + 2, plus additional content, and more DLC down the road. The loyalty discount was only 15% and limited to a short period after release, plus if you didn't know about it you missed out on really cool twitch rivals skins to boot. So the timing and the price point really hurt. The game itself is phenomenal. The developers have outdone themselves again despite no one asking them to do it. I know they have to be compensated for their work, but the problem is no one asked for this, and there's not enough new content at launch, the loyalty discount was a bust. The promise of future DLC being free is great, but with no pay incentive, we know how that could end up, as it has with many games. No money, no time, no content. Not saying the developers would abandon the game, but you can't blame a gamer for worrying about it. So I with they would have waited and had more content at launch or provided a better discount. Problem is most people who would enjoy this game already purchased and played Overcooked 1 and 2, or at least one of them and this is a steep asking price. Those who aren't interested probably aren't interested. If you fit into that small category of people who thinks this looks interesting or already played a friends copy and enjoyed it. Pick this game up and have a blast. Ignore the negative reviews, this game is being review bombed for the reasons listed above. If you already own 1 and 2, or 2. I would probably hold out for steam sale unless you want to support the developers. Where do I stand on all this. I still love the series. I hope you understand this game is great and is only receiving negative reviews because of the reasons listed above. It's a great game and deserves better. Me, personally, I was on the fence with this one. I almost purchased it, out of loyalty, but I struggled with the asking price. I'm also bummed out about the missed twitch rivals skins as I like to have a whole game, so I'm really bummed. I'm a content creator, so I lucked out and got a free copy. I was not required to create content with the game or leave a review, but out of love for the series I felt I must. I will eventually probably snag a copy on the switch when it goes on sale. This is the definitive version of the game. It's the most amazing version of the game no one asked for with a steep cost for previous  owners. I can't tell you the memories I have of playing this game and the joy. Now you can do all that in ultra high resolutions and buttery smooth frame rates, online coop, and have all your chefs and levels in one place. All that aside, if you somehow haven't played this game before, you a missing out. The puzzles will keep you on your feet. This game will teach you teamwork and strategy. It will get you working well together like a well oiled unit, or you will have a crazy kitchen. It will have you being innovative. This should be used as one of those in classroom exercises to demonstrate synergy. This game is best played with friends in coop online or local. You can play solo, but i strongly advise against it unless you are a masochist and into torturing yourself. I would imagine some levels might even be not passable solo. When playing solo you have to switch between 2 independent characters and keep them both busy at the same time. I've done it on some of the simpler levels and it has some sense of rewarding feeling to have that going on, but it's not worth the trouble and most importantly frustration. It's not the way the game was really meant to be played. It's best enjoyed with friends. If you are on the fence, find a friend who has it and play remotely, watch some videos, or seek out a cheap copy or free copy of the first one. By that point you will know if you like it. You will be craving more or know it's not for you. If you have questions about the game or want to discuss the review you can swing over to my steam profile and comment or message me, or stop by my stream  . I only ask if you come by to not be disruptive or rude.When I say this game is being review bombed to clarify, Most of the negative review are to hurt the game and the developers because of the pricing and the anger of this game mainly being recycled content, and overlooking the additional content, added features, having it all under one roof for now and all upcoming updates. I can't say all, but most are knocking the game because of the situation not the game. It's like when someone orders a top of the line TV, and it shows up 2 days late in a beat up box. Does it make it a bad TV? No. It means the TV was shipped poorly and abused. Reviews are meant to rate the product. I can understand why this is happening though. Just take this in mind when reading the other reviews.Note to developers: please add throwing to Overcooked 1 levels, please provide a detailed road-map of future content if you haven't already. Please consider a new loyalty discount or lower asking price. (At this point the damage is done, I would hate to say it but probably 50% off or more to get people to budge) Please consider selling twitch drop skins. Many people missed them and others play on multiple platform but only use one twitch account and we want a complete game. Lot's of missed opportunities and dropped balls, but great job and great game. The biggest problem is in it's current state, a large part of the player-base is sectioned off on Overcooked 2, and it's hurting this title. Please consider dropping the price. It's hurting the game and the franchise. Thanks for making this masterpiece, bringing me and my friends joy.================================== The Only Review You Will Need ================================================================= Warning Long Read, but full context review ============================================================= Game is being Review Bombed, Negatively ================================

_childDocuments_.review: I previously bought Overcooked! and Overcooked! 2 a WHILE ago, and I loved both of them. They were great experiences, but they weren't so fun singleplayer. Way better multiplayer and way funner. Although it's pretty much impossible to matchmake with real players in the online mode, if you've got friends to play this with and like party games, get this game immediately. It's easily the best deal if you want the full Overcooked experience, as it includes a remaster of both Overcooked 1 & 2, all extra DLCs plus new ones, fully integrated online with new features such as voice chat, and even has enhanced 4K graphics with 60 FPS in it, which is even better than Overcooked! 2 graphics. This is a real game changer, and is extremely fun to play with friends. Couch co-op  is the best for this game in my opinion, and is EXTREMELY fun. The original Overcooked games weren't too replayable, but this one definitely is as it has SO much content in it. It has ALL overcooked content and costs less than buying both overcooked 1 and 2 and is easily the best option if you're looking to buy all there is to overcooked. It's a great and amazingly fun experience, and I cannot stress enough how much of a great time I had playing this game with my family. 10/10 for me, I haven't played a game this fun in a long time, and in my opinion, it's one of the best options out there if you're looking to buy a party game. Singleplayer isn't as fun to be honest, but multiplayer is on a different level of fun. Amazing game. If you have a chance, I HIGHLY recommend buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I have honestly never played a game that infuriated me more than this game.I got this game to play with two other friends, and coming from a game called PlateUp, I thought that with a similar premise, we were going to have a lot of fun. It initially did start off as a fun, challenging game. However, over the course of the game, that challenged turned into absurd difficulty and it started getting ridiculous.Some of the levels the game throws at you are really difficult to wrap around, but imagine trying to get multiple people to understand it and figure out how to optimally work with each other. We had to take several attempts to barely understand the levels, combine it with some minor bugs in this game, and other minor details, the game knows how to infuriate you. And I hate how this is the default difficulty of the game. The fact that the game has ways to make it easier through "Assist Settings" is condescending and makes you feel like you are not good enough for the game.Getting 3 stars on a level honestly isn't possible unless you and your friends completely sweat with the dashes and get good RNG with the recipes. It was through this that we got a few close calls to 3 stars, but only falling a few points short. But the game deliberately times you to where if you don't get it within the second, the customer gets impatient and fails you. I know PlateUp has some finnicky controls, but it is much worse in this game. Sometimes whenever I place an ingredient in a pot or trying to pick up a pot/pan before the meat burns, the game oftentimes misunderstood where I was facing and decides to place what I'm holding on the completely wrong tile, or it picks up an item I'm not even looking at. It's almost as if the developers didn't do enough playtesting to iron out these seemingly minor issues that can make or break an attempt.Also, don't bother playing this on singleplayer. On singleplayer, you have to control two people and it is difficult to manage, especially if you are playing with a controller. If you ever choose to play this game, at least get it with a friend so it becomes more bearable. Get a good friend, so that when the both of you get upset trying to do some of the levels, you can forget it.The plot is cheesy, but I can overlook it. I like the look of the game, it's nice and refreshing. The soundtrack is pretty nice. But that's all the positives that I can say about this game. Unless you're willing to sweat or you can hold your rage, don't buy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Got this game a while ago and I've been really trying my best to get into it. Let me preface this by saying that I work actual food service. I find cooking to be quite enjoyable and a little bit of micromanagement, especially in a real world setting, is absolutely no problem to me at all. When I played this game for the first time, my experience was a bit akward and uncomfortable, much like how you'd feel at your first day in a real job. This feeling didn't go away however. I initially wrote it off as just me being bad, however the more patient I try to be with this game, the more frustrated I get, and I think I should get my views on this game out just to validate the feelings of those in the same predicament as me, since I really didn't see anybody acknowledging this in the reviews. Maybe this is just me and my play style, but this game is FAR too gimmicky for me to play. The base gameplay which consists of prepping food and serving it has virtually no depth to it, making a good 90% of this game pointless, impractical, micromanagement due to all the pointless and nonsensical gimmicks in the game. If there's anything I know from my experiences with games, it's that difficulty is no substitute for gameplay, and this game is practically the reason I believe that. Sometimes you'll be prepping food and the entire kitchen starts moving away from you (WTF??!) or the kitchen will have an infestation of super rats that can locate and acquire food as soon as it's dropped. My personal favorite is that level where people are just casually walking through the kitchen. That kind of stupidity and spatial unawareness makes me absolutely livid. If somebody walked through the kitchen at work we'd literally just kick them the ♥♥♥♥ out. So why the hell should I take that ♥♥♥♥ in a game? Every level there's a dumber, more bizarre obstacle that holds dominion over the kitchen that you just happen to be working in. I understand that this is a video game, but this is a game about cooking. Why the hell am I forced to play in these levels that are were so obviously not designed to be cooked in? The level choices are creative, but frustrating and practically designed against you, which I have to hold against the game since it's just so unrealistic for a food service environment. There's a way to make your game difficult without making it this ridiculously frustrating. Take a game like Touhou 6 or Crash Bandicoot for example. Those levels are clearly designed for you to play them, and the difficulty is based on skill, where as in Overcooked it's more about management. You can't just make a game super overwhelming and substitute that in for difficulty. I'm a bit of a perfectionist so I found it hard to even get started on most levels let alone get a good flow going, and that's basically why I'm writing this review. In my opinion, it feels like the player has very little control over the game, and instead of actually introducing skills that let players thrive in that environment, the game focuses more on just putting the player somewhere and forcing them to just deal with it. If I wanted to deal with annoying customers, I'd go back to work and actually get paid for it. This game is really cute and has a lot of accessibility features, but it feels like you're trying to do a job while a group of mentally disabled children running amok and wreaking havoc on your workspace. To give you a better example, this game is like a Mario game where all the levels are water levels, and instead of making them harder as they went on they just added ridiculous spams of enemies. Cute game, not worth the stress at all imo. This is the only game where I can be bored of the gameplay while still stressing out about the levels. Not fun for me, 6/10.

Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. _childDocuments_.review: I love this game. It is a super cute game, thats lots of fun to play with your friends or family. Very fast and communicative. I also admire how many different, genius levels are included that keep the game interesting. However I would not recommend buying it. Because they make it as hard as possible for you to play online with your friends. The first part is not online playable at all. The second one theoretically could be played in online multiplayer BUT both of the players need to have the same version of Overcooked 2 on the same plattform. I can't play Overcooked 2 with my friends online, because I have the "All you can eat"-Version and they have the normal Overcooked 2 version, which sucks a lot. I also can not play it with friends who have the game on a different platform because there's no ID/friend list system inside the game itself. Additionally, even though in local coop up to 4 players could play, you can only invite one more player when playing online coop. Which means the amount of players is reduced to maximum 2 online. That is pretty low for a multiplayer coop game nowadays, because as much as I wish I  could've had my friends and family over to play local, most of us playing games together nowadays happens online. This is why I can not recommend buying it, unless you have somebody at home to play regularly. Or you have exactly one friend online who owns the exact version of Overcooked 2 on the same platform as you do.

_childDocuments_.review: Overcooked! All You Can Eat is a complete edition consisting of both Overcooked! games, all DLC, & some additional stages to entice owners of the previous titles.  The games still have that goofy charm to them with their silly plot & irreverent stages.  The controls are tight & fluid, leaving little room for error outside of human control.  The variety of stages & dishes is still just as nice as ever, with different mechanics unique to each stage.  The soundtrack is equally as charming, with the overworld theme being the easiest to stick in one's memory.  Finally, the co-op is just as fun as ever, making the stages both easier to complete & more chaotic to run about, as well as increasing the star required score due to the number of chefs running about. Overcooked! 1 feels slightly out of place, the lack of a throw food option making the game feel a bit slower.  Where the stages are varied, some can be quite annoying due to the individual level features, such as ice physics in the ice world.  The largest con for fans of the series would be the game's status.  As a complete edition of both titles, this is not a bundle, meaning players who already own both games will already have about 90% of this in their collection already. This is actually an easier list than the original titles this was based off of.  The removal of the heavier grind achievements have been replaced with ones requiring multiple chefs to be specific chefs.  This needs to be done online, or locally using a controller & keyboard/second controller.  There really isn't too much difficulty here, other than completing the main campaigns if one finds them difficult.  One doesn't even need to finish a majority of the DLC to clear the list either. Overcooked! All You Can Eat is a fun bundle of two fast paced, enjoyable games with some extra DLC added for those who want more.  It's colorful style & frenetic gameplay creates a wonderful experience, be it solo, couch co-op, or online.  Though owners of the titles would be much better off waiting for a sale, newcomers should jump on this first rather than start with the earlier games.  A solid recommendation for anyone interested.

The array of assist options are great, from simply upping a couple timers to being able to skip annoying levels entirely.My only complaints are: -the DLCs (extra trimmings) are more prone to lag and glitches with crossplay, as well as any levels with portals-World food festival has a level that randomly stopped allowing me to plate dishes even while playing solo. -Some arcade versus levels have no sink to wash dishesAll this to say:-This game is everything I want from overcooked, 1 and 2 are reliable games, the DLCs have their issues but all in all are enjoyable and playable. -If you like overcooked and want to be able to crossplay with a friend, it is playable and works well the majority of the time (In my experience for steam+xbox with only 2 players total). -If you want to play overcooked but you were turned away by the difficulty of later levels, the assist options are incredible for making the game as easy as you need it to be.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.Ingredients:1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter2. 1/2 cup white sugar3. 1/2 cup brown sugar4. 1/4 cup water5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon6. 1 pinch salt7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced8. 1 pastry for double-crust pieDirections:1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

name: Sword of the Necromancer
detailed_description: What would you do to bring back someone you love? Sword of the Necromancer is a dungeon-crawler action RPG with Rogue-like elements where you can revive your defeated enemies to make them fight alongside you. Turn your foes into allies using the forbidden powers of the Sword of the Necromancer and help Tama reach the dungeon's depths in order to gain enough power to bring Koko back from the dead . Gather a little army of monsters, equip yourself with weapons and relics and level up to take on the guardians that stand between you and your objective. Turn your foes into allies: use the Sword of the Necromancer to revive defeated monsters and make them fight alongside you. Gather weapons and relics: each weapon is different from the others thanks to the procedural weapon generation system, which gives them various effects and attributes. Fight with all your might: defeat your enemies using a variety of weapons and objects and dominating the fluid head-to-head battle system. Level up: enhance your character by fighting enemies and upgrade your stats. Improve your summoned monsters by fighting alongside them. Death is not the end: Each try gets you closer to the Necromancer. You will lose all your equipped weapons and monsters, but you will retain half the level you achieved in your run. Learn the truth: Discover Tama and Koko's past as you advance through the dungeon. Local co-op play: Use the Flask of Homunculus to create a copy of the playable character and play with a friend in local co-op game. ' Legend says that, deep within these mountains, a heretic decided to violate the will of the gods in order to achieve eternal life. The heretic succeeded in this aberrant attempt, and created a tool for forbidden rituals that could grant immortality… and even bring back the dead. Over the years and centuries many have tried to get that power for themselves, but all they found in the Necromancer’s crypt was their demise. They say that the tool the Necromancer created is also a weapon… The Sword of the Necromancer ” Tama is a former rogue that is tasked to escort the priestess Koko in her pilgrimage around the continent. During their travel Koko dies , and Tama carries the corpse to the Necromancer's crypt, where legends say there dwells a power that may resurrect the dead . Filled with despair, Tama will enter the dungeon with the aim of obtaining the forbidden power of necromancy , ignoring the dangers that lurk in the shadows. Languages Voices: English, Japanese Texts: English, Spanish, Catalan, Galician, Basque, French, German, Italian, Japanese

name: Sea of Stars
detailed_description: Promising the Sabotage touch in every system, Sea of Stars aims to modernize the classic RPG in terms of turn-based combat, storytelling, exploration and interactions with the environment, while still offering a hearty slice of nostalgia and good old, simple fun. Pressing the action button in sync with the animations increases damage output while reducing incoming damage. Along with timed hits, combat features multi-character combo attacks, boosting, and a strategic 'locks' system offering options to play with different damage types in order to hinder enemies while they are channeling powerful attacks or spells, all in an immersive take on the genre; no random encounters, no transitions to separate battlefields, and no grinding. Swim, climb, vault, jump off or hoist up ledges as you traverse seamlessly through the world with a navigation system based on platformer expertise that breaks free from the classic bound-to-the-grid tileset movement. Our custom-made render pipeline allows the creation of a breathtaking world coming to life by pushing the limits of 2D pixel-art games. Dozens of original characters and story arcs will take you on a captivating journey. Sometimes epic, sometimes silly, and other times emotional, Sea of Stars does its RPG duty of exploring classic themes of adventure and friendship, while also being chock-full of the unexpected twists and events you’d expect from a Sabotage production. There are many ways to hang out in the world of Sea of Stars if you feel the need for a change of pace in your adventures. Sailing, cooking, fishing, stopping by a tavern to listen to a song or play the infamous tabletop game known as 'Wheels'.....every system has been designed to deliver an experience that pays respect to retro classics, while rethinking in some areas to offer a smooth and modernized experience.

short_description: Sea of Stars is a turn-based RPG inspired by the classics. It tells the story of two Children of the Solstice who will combine the powers of the sun and moon to perform Eclipse Magic, the only force capable of fending off the monstrous creations of the evil alchemist known as The Fleshmancer.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr I give it an 8/10. Standalone Wheels when???Sometimes the writing was weird and the decisions the characters made left me scratching my head, but it was fun and took the old RPG tropes and innovated with a fun spin. The game is visually impressive, sometimes turning the usual pixel graphics on their head and surprising you out of left field.The mini game "Wheels" was super fun. I normally don't care that much about mini games, but this was rad. The clockwork sound effects while playing was very satisfying. If the studio released a game that was just Wheels, I'd play it for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine a game where Golden Sun Puzzles + Chrono Trigger storytelling and combat + Mario RPG timed attacks all met up and had a baby.The Devs of this game made an amazing love letter to classic turn based JRPGS that you love and it's not even at the full price of garbage triple A gamesThe writing at times is a little weird but there's also references here and there of classic tropes and they come out pretty good as I got an unexpected chuckle here and there.The combat is also super fun and timed attacks keep you on your toes and make combat a little more interesting. Combat also doesn't last super long as well. One complaint I do have however is I feel like the bosses are a little too easy.Besides that, this game is definitely worth your time and when you pick it up, you will definitely feel the charm and energy the devs put in.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:- Audiovisually it's a fantastic experience. The pixel art and the music are beautiful- Combat mechanics are pretty cool; boosting and lock breaking gives it a strategic feelCons:- Not enough depth to combat and equipment systems. Each character gets like 3 skills; this also makes the combat feel very repetitive because you're using the exact same skills in every encounter from the beginning of the game until the end. Additionally, combat feels dragged out because some skills like moonarang, which is super useful so you use it in every encounter, take very long to execute. When it comes to equipment almost all of them are straight stat boosts with no interesting qualities whatsoever.- The world-building is very poor and often doesn't make much sense. For example, there's the port town, Brisk. Visually, the town screams that it's a trading hub. Except if you progress far enough into the game to see the world map you'll find out they have no one to actually trade with! The other settlements either don't have ports or are otherwise inaccessible. The game is just filled with all these elements that don't really coexist with anything else in the same world and kind of do their own thing.- The story, the characters, the writing in general. They're awful. There's no other way to describe it. The dialogue is boring, the jokes are painful, too many of the characters are bland and none of the interesting characters get any meaningful screentime. The story is pretty generic, save for one or two interesting moments it just falls flat. The pacing is awful, there's a part where you'll just spend hours trudging through these seemingly neverending dungeons just to get to another dungeon so the story can continue. There's a sign near the beginning of the game that reads "This way to the GOAT boat" that made me want to alt f4 immediately.- But far and away my biggest gripe with this whole game is: Garl. ♥♥♥♥ this guy. He's supposed to be Joe Everyman, the guy with no special powers. So why does this sidekick best friend character get so much of the spotlight? He hogs every moment for himself; every bit of story-important dialogue is delivered by Garl, every important interaction with an elder or council or whatever it's Garl that does the talking. When the two chosen one main characters save some people, the people cheer for Garl. It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ridiculous. And the worst part is all the characters love Garl. The entire main cast, all the side characters, just can't stop talking about how good of a guy he is. Hell the villians are probably categorised as evil in this world because they DON'T love Garl. The two main characters especially are so obsessed with Garl that he is all they talk about. When he's not there all they say is: "Oh how I miss Garl","I wish Garl was here","Garl would know what to do!","Remember that thing we did with Garl, best time of my life". And when he is there they go: "What would we do without you Garl?", "You're the best Garl!", "You're so right Garl", "Thank Garl you're here Garl". I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick of it. I was convinced partway through that Garl was going to turn out to be the evil wizard final boss, that he's been emitting spores or something to make everyone fall in love with him. All so he could manipulate the heroes and take their moments of growth away from them, so they could never grow powerful enough to defeat him. But no, he's just genuinely a Gary Stu that can do no wrong and everybody loves him because he's the best. ♥♥♥♥ you Garl.I'm gonna go wash the taste of Garl's ♥♥♥♥ out of my mouth, and I suggest the writers do the same.5/10 too much Garl

_childDocuments_.review: Edit 2: You can fasttravel later in the game. Sooo...if you want to avoid to walk through areas again and again just wait till that point where you're able to get everywhere and do the most backtracking at this point.Edit 1: 19h in and still not sure if i reach the end in the next 5h, game has definitly a great length. However, there are some negatives i should meantion that are not BAD in like being a reason to not buy the game but more something that could be bit annoying1. Fast travel, maybe i'm stupid but atm it's just not possible to skip an area in case of backtracking. Sometimes you have to run multiple areas to reach a destination to collect an item you're now able to reach with new abilities or stuff. It's fine doing it sometimes but always having to go through most areas before actually being in the place to collect chests is getting a bit annoying.2. You can only have 10 cooked meals. Nothing i actually need or is necessary but i can't deny that it feels a bit unsatisfying that the number isn't increasing once the whole game so far. Make it a relict or something you can buy to upgrade the amount you can store so it would still be optional.3. Sometimes enemies have similar attacks. Recycling is still recycling, can't judge but still pointing it out.As said, nothing special, not really something to hate on, especially 2 & 3 but i would say number 1 is still something that could be annoying for many that would like to backtrack and go back to past areas, collecting stuff they couldn't get before.Edit EndLove it already, just buy it, beautiful art, great combat system similar like Mario RPG and the game should run smooth af on every computer.(The Price is more than fair, if people complain about it than those are the same who play f2p games and invest thousand of dollars in skins and gacha)if you were able to buy a console or pc or laptop you are able to afford that game as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is a fancy JRPG combined with some kind of a rythm game, which makes the core gameplay a bit more alive and entertaining. In contrast to Messenger, this game contains significantly less meta-humor and is pretty much story based. If you're not gonna go for a completionist run, you'd probably be dissatisfied with the finale, coz it just sucks. It is literally most obvious way to finish the game which doesn't make ANY sense. Messenger set standards and the default ending just doesn't even try to meet these. True Ending is something you NEED to unlock to get something special from the game. Events featured in additional scenes are 100% worth watching and without them the story would be a total failure. Along the story we have absolutely fantastic visuals, background music and SFX. Still not perfect but very VERY good, 8/10P.S. Don't let the 1.5 HOUR LONG INTRODUCTION scare you away (afterwards it was worth it for me) and enjoy this wonderful world.P.P.S. Default run ~30 hoursTrue ending ~35 hours (even faster if you are following guidelines)All achievements ~50 hours

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a lot of positives. Unfortunately, some of the writing isn't great and some of the dialogue is absolutely awful.  After 5 and a half hours one character broke this game for me. Yolanda, in the town of Brisk just starts spewing tropes from RPGs out of nowhere, completely breaking immersion in the game. The double eye patch pirate with them has a dumb back story too, completely unnecessary. They don't take their own story serious enough and after 5 hours it's already a parody of itself.  What an absolute shame, so much wasted potential.  I've never done this before on Steam, but I'm going to try to get a refund if I can .  If they can't take their own story serious, I'm not going to waste my time getting to know it.Edit: Looks like I can't get a refund because it's after 2 hours.  Wish the writers would have been up-front with their game and that they weren't going to be serious about it from the onset.Sabotage studio is right, they sabotaged their own game.Positives -Visually appealingInteresting combat mechanicsClassic RPG puzzlesEnemy/character scaling seems good so farNegatives-Bad dialogueImmersion breaking characters

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Sea of Stars! The graphics and world-building are incredible with delightful details that always caught me by surprise all the way to the end. Usually I struggle to finish games because I lose interest, but this one I explored to the max. The graphics are lovely and the lighting and dimension are a triumph.I will admit that the two main characters don't have a character arc, but it honestly didn't bother me. Grinding for exp is difficult, but grinding actually isn't needed since you'll be on good footing by the end just by picking up better gear on the way and leveling up naturally. I enjoyed the fights up until the final boss battle for the true ending which just left me frustrated and exhausted, but I did get past it and victory was sweet.All in all, I'm going to gift Sea of Stars to my loved ones and hope that it'll bring them as much joy as it did me.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a wonderful game in old JRPG style and gameplay, it has some flaws(most of them due to the bad battle system) but overall I enjoyed it. Thanks to my friend Alexinus who gave it to me. So in nutshell here pros and cons:+ Beautiful visual part with well-done pixel art and animations+ Nice and kind story with some drama and heartbreaking moments+ Great OST+ Funny dialogues and anime like comedy moments+ Good level design for most part of game except some areas that have no shortcuts+ Bunch of interesting gameplay mechanics such as cooking, minigames, etc+ Relic system is awesome - because you can freely adjust your difficulty from very hard to easy+ Exp raise to all party members so no need for lots of grind for each hero you don’t play previously+ You can change heroes in battle at any moment which is very interesting mechanic+- Lots of puzzle games(but at the end i start hate some of them due to similarity)-Battle system may be debatable, but for me it's bad so if you don’t have fast reaction then without “relics easy mode” it will be hard and every encounter become so long and boring- Lack of info about dmg your skills and combos do, in pair that some of them just useless but cost same amount as more profitable- Less amount of skills and possible actions - every hero has only 3 skills, 1 default attack and some combos(count increase with more heroes unlocked) and no other options to change it for your playstyle- Leveling system seems to give you options but at the end you will just take all stats early or later, no much difference. So you definitely have to take mana point first and then all to dmg stats. It could be done much better and interestingWhole game is awesome and I felt a lot of nostalgia for games like Chorno Trigger, Legend of Mana, games from SquareEnix and all others old JRPG. Kind and fairy story with the power of friendship, self sacrificing and making some good stuff for the world and people there. We lack the personality of the main heroes so I feel that truly the main hero is only  and you just help him to make the world better. I love the visual part so much that playing on a big TV was very satisfying. I don’t feel that high tech graphics from recent AAA games are much better than this pixel game. Devs made a really big work to make not a common indie pixel game but a really masterpiece in the style of old JRPG. Great and relaxing OST, lot’s of funny dialogues and anime style moments that fans will truly appreciate. Big number of enemies with its unique art design and their animations of skills. If you like puzzles there are a lot of them on every step but at some point i feel bored of them. Nice idea of npc that will tell you more stories to fulfill your knowledge of the world. Great minigame but really sad there so less tournaments for earning some extra rewards.    - use guides like  and  because you will lose a big amount of time for returning and searching for missed items and 1 achievement -  can’t be done in one game if you start doing it too late after all side quests and need to be done in NG+So the only aspect i was disappointed is battle system - because all main aspect is your reaction to make timed block and attack without it you will struggle in fight to block enemies actions and deal at least normal amount of damage and survive without use healing items and rest every 2-3 encounters. In that case your only option is to use relics for activating “easy mode”, because grinding level will be so long and boring without well timed actions. Also no sense of using some skills or combos, because combos cost the same amount but have a really huge difference in dmg and versatility, each hero has 1 skill that will be used at 80% of game and others mostly to counter enemies actions. Due to the fast cd of enemies actions, it’s very hard to make a cool wombo combo, you have to use some “right” tactic without any imagination for most part of the encounters. Minigame at Final Boss in  at first glance interesting but how my ass was burning before i finally killed him.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played for a while.  Super charming, great visuals, cool story, interesting characters, awesome battle system, great soundtrack.  I like my jrpgs to be challenging so I'd recommend putting the rune on I think 'tactician's mettle'; but even the concept of runes is a really cool idea, instead of the normal 'easy, normal or hard' mode, as it lets you cater to your own liking of challenge and gameplay.  Love how the story progresses as well, and takes a u-turn (won't spoil).  I've heard people negatively critique that there is a lack of skills and spells in the first portion of the game, but I never found that (may have to do with having the tactician mettle rune on, which always made it challenging and I had to use skills at specific times to win battles.  The game is obviously an jrpg at heart, but I found that it felt kind of action-ey and arcade-y in the best ways possible as well, with nice design choices of timing buttons with different enemy attacks and so forth.The only negative I found with the game was that the final dungeon felt a little too undaunting when finishing the game.  I didn't get the 'true ending' as I couldn't be bothered going back and finding all the conches, so I didn't fight the real end boss; but still the end dungeon I felt could've been bolstered a tad more.But other than that; highly recommend the game.  I wouldn't be surprised if I still counted it as one of the best games I've ever played in years to come.  Now if only that art book didn't have such a costly shipping price haha.

_childDocuments_.review: As Illusion of Gaia and Chrono Trigger are my favourites of the decade in the 90's, Dragon Quest 8 & Zelda Majoras Mask + OOT are mine of the 2000's and Undertale & Persona 5 of 2010's decade, this game just got into the same hall of legends in my heart! _childDocuments_.review: StoryThis game is brimming with love and passion.  It's a shame the director/writer's approach to storytelling is so shallow.  He has some great premises for characters and plots, but that's all they really are.  B'st is an ancient spirit brought to life through living glass, and that's it.  If you read 99% of his dialogue without knowing his backstory, you could easily imagine him as a generic villager NPC.  That pretty much applies to every character, you could describe them and say "oh that sounds like an interesting character" but their actual dialogue and writing could be swapped out for any generic NPC and you'd hardly notice a difference.  There's not a single real character arc anywhere in this entire game, except maybe that little wind mole guy who is only there for like 3 scenes.  He's probably the best character.GameplayThe gameplay is fun but too easy, and the hard mode items are a massive overcompensation that make it a nightmare.  All that needs to be done is to give every boss in the game about double the health they have currently.  That would solve half the combat's problems.  It feels weird to recommend damage sponging but really it's a valid prescription in this case.  The puzzles are also too easy, except the optional endgame puzzles were pretty decent.  The whole game should have had puzzles on the level of the endgame puzzles.  The traversal mechanics are nice and better than nothing but I really think they could have taken it a step further and just made it have actual platforming.  It wouldn't even need to have drastic changes either.  Just allow the player to fall off ledges, and add a jump button in place of all the contextual jumping.  It would be nice to have revamped traversal design with additional platforming elements but honestly even if they just did those two things it would make it way more fun.  The level design feels as if it is designed to be a light platformer but they just replaced all the jumping with contextual jumping and put invisible guard rails everywhere.  Also I think combo attacks should just cost MP for each character involved, and breaking locks should just give ultimate charge instead.  ALSO, where are the 3 man combo attacks???  This is supposed to be chrono trigger inspired, how are you gonna have combo moves but only duos???Level Design The game is too linear.  I don't need it to be a metroidvania with a million different paths with locked doors to backtrack to, but it needed more optional paths sprinkled in with some side content and at the end they loop you back so you can pick right up where you left off on the critical path.  Also the dungeons were too short.  I liked their design and what's their is enjoyable but there's just not enough.  The final dungeon has really just 2 segments to it with a boss each and each segment takes like 5 minutes.  The whole final dungeon probably took me 20 minutes including cutscenes.  MusicI loved the music but there were only a handful of memorable tracks.  It suffers from being a bit too safe and generic just like the rest of the game.  There are lots of little details with the music that are impressive, like how the academy has one central motif but different accompaniment in each wing.  The music is a great microcosm of the game itself, competent and charming, filled with love and passion, and too safe and risk adverse.  Visuals I really have very little criticism for the visuals.  They are gorgeous.  The character design is definitely very tumblry but it is charming still.  The art is beautiful and was my favorite part of the experience.  Overall I recommend the game, it was well worth the money and I hope they make more games in this series  and more RPGs specifically (though I imagine their next project will probably jump genre as well.  Though with their little extended universe's lore and track record I could easily see them doing a game that jumped between genres, which would be cool.)   I just hope the director is humble enough to let someone else write the characters and dialogue moving forward.  He can still design the overarching story and character/event premises, just let someone else do the dirty work.  The director is a great ideals guy, just not so great at the fleshing out ideas part.  Maybe that's why the bad guy is called the fleshmancer.

_childDocuments_.review: Good, but not great.Honestly, I wanted to like it more than I did.It has some really good things going for it:  * The graphics are gorgeous and it has a number of musical compositions from Mitsuda. * The combat system had a few good Mario RPG tricks and combo techs.  * The ability to control the sun/moonlight in real time over pixel graphics is rad and a real technical feat.* The relic system allows you to tailor the difficulty level to your own desires, and since you earn them through gameplay it never feels like cheating.* Plays really well on Steam Deck and doesn't eat the batteries too quickly.The bad:   * The main characters might as well have been silent considering how little development and personality they have.* Garl is NOT Samwise Gamgee and having him be the one to always butt in and do everything of note is annoying.* Most of the characters are just kind of bland despite efforts by the game to tell you how special they are supposed to be.* It lacks the "feels" that make for a classic RPG.  It tries so hard, to force the feels, but the story and characters come short.* Part of the end game content to get the true ending involves the game's collect-a-thon quest.   Save yourself the time and misery and just use a guide for these as you play through the game.It gets more right than it does wrong, and it certainly scratches an itch.  But I had likely over-hyped myself into thinking this could somehow be another Chrono Trigger... will there ever be another Chrono Trigger?

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is a game that seems somewhat divisive in JRPG communities. Many people seemed to have hyped up their expectations and gotten disappointed, luckily I just thought it looked good, and wasn't too excited because frankly, I don't play many JRPGs myself. Maybe that's why Sea of Stars really got me, but it isn't perfect. The story suffers in a way I feel a lot of longer stories do, you feel like you're approaching the end, only for the game and story to expand, often in completely insane ways to prolong itself. This isn't too egregious in Sea of Stars, but I definitely had a "what the heck?" section of the game. Aside from that, the writing is often brought up, it isn't bad but the main characters could use some more dialogue, and the combat is also brought up, which is definitely on the simple but more engaging end of games like this, with only a few skills but a timing element to them which I found fine even if you do it hundreds of times.Now let's get around to what is essentially the obvious part. The art and music are unparalleled. Hearing familiar tunes to The Messenger and plenty of tracks from Yasunori Mitsuda is an absolute treat and together with the visual feasts that are the game's environments they almost make you want to cry. It feels like a new bar for pixel art in a way that makes it harder to play other pixel art games without thinking about it.If you're like me and rarely play these types of games, I would totally give it a shot, it definitely gave me more than I hoped for. If you already play tons of JRPGs, then manage your expectations, it probably won't be the best JRPG you've played, but it's a good game and there's no denying that.
