_childDocuments_.review: You have no idea how excited I was for this game when it was announced. I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ adore Chrono Trigger; it's a game deserving of the accolades it gets. That's why it pains me to say Sea of Stars is the most disappointing game I've ever played. **I want to preface the rest of this by saying Sea of Stars is not a bad game, not remotely. Hell, I'm aware I'm in the minority here and I'm happy for the people who enjoy this game. I wish I could.**My first point of contention is the core gameplay. The battle system is very well put together, and I like that the game forces you to diverisfy your attacks between normal attacks (to regen MP and build up Live Mana) and special attacks. The game is mechanically solid, no doubt. The issue is... the lack of attacks really. All that praise I had to having to diversify your attacks is almost entirely undone by just how few special attacks you get. You'll be using stuff Sunball and Moonerang almost exclusive for far too much of the game. Buffs and Debuffs are almost entirely absent, and this game I feel sorely needed them. Combat becomes pretty mind-numbing because of the overly simple movesets. After playing the demo, I was concerned that bosses would regularly be HP sponges. This is somewhat the case, the aforementioned limited movesets compounds this, but it never got to an unbearable point admittedly. You also go a huge chunk of the game with the same 3-4 party members, and I know I'm a broken record, but the lack of variety in attack effects makes some of them feel alike. Combos are also horribly underutilized, you'll be using Zale and Valere's Solstice Strike for most of the game because the other Combos take too long to build up in normal encounters, and this one is just so practical since they both regen MP from it (they both perform a normal attack simultaneously). Every character combination should've had a a Normal Attack Combo like this imo. Rq, felt I should mention the only Game Over I suffered was this one point in the game's latter half where the part gets split up into 3 groups, and the enemy numbers in following area kinda just tore my ass inside out. The only part of the game I thought was remotely cheap.The Relic system is the one thing I don't get. The only one I used was the one to make a star appear when timing an attack correctly (though sometimes the sweet spot felt really vague for certain moves). So, most of these seem to be Easy Mode modifications. Alright, doesn't bug me since I can just leave them off. What I don't get is that you have to buy them... Why? Also iirc Rainbow Conchs are only used for purchasing more of these, so if you want to play mostly vanilla then any time your reward for exploring is a Rainbow Conch, it's entirely unsatisfying. But yeah, why are these, again what I presume to be Easy Mode Modifications, something you have to buy. I don't see how that remotely benefits people looking for an easier time. And you toggle Relics on or off, not equip them to a specific party member. This system makes no sense to me.A quick positive, this game is absolutely breathtaking visually. Genuinely, one of the best looking games I've ever played. The sprite quality is absolutely phenomenal, characters are well animated, and there's a real sense of scope.The soundtrack is also very good, Eric W. Brown did a solid job. I'm not certain to the extent of Yasunori Mitsuda's contributions to the OST (I tried looking up lists and get some conflicting reports), with exception to Coral Cascades since the demo flat out said he composed it. This game is also dripping with attention to detail. I got big, dumb grin on my face listening to the Pirate versions of the OST, but also seeing that each player in the band would start and stop playing in accordance to if they had a part in the track or if you spoke to them. I don't need these little details to enjoy a game, but I'm always pleased to see them.I cannot give much praise to the writing, this game's story is a big load of *nothing*. The story is a lot of "Go here, do this, suddenly a boss fight against a dude we'll never see again". The characters are far too basic, though not insufferably bad at least. What we're left is some characters who clearly have potential, but are beyond underused and left undercooked. I think I liked Garl the most, if only because of how positive he is. There's also a point where he basically tells the main villain to ♥♥♥♥ off and I thought that was pretty funny. To give some credit, the game does have some decently funny moments. But they're just that, moments. Without spoiling to much, this game does have a True Ending and I just could not be bothered to see it through. I looked it up and yeah I don't feel like I missed a damn thing. It also ruins one story moment I thought was genuinely good, like damn I thought the devs were really going through with a certain story moment but nope. Anyway another reason I didn't bother was because I felt the final portion of the game was just completely necessary and flat out bad. Like, I didn't care about the story yeah, but all the ♥♥♥♥ aside from the final dungeon was stuff I'd classify as "jumping the shark", it was that intrusive to me.One last minor positive I have is that I think the game's dungeon design is overall better than most other RPGs's dungeon design. Hell, there was one dungeon that reminded me straight up of a Zelda Water Temple (Great Bay specifically). Anyway, I'm done complaining. I wanted to love this game, genuinely, but just couldn't. I see the passion, I really do, but the game just feels like a proof of concept for me. Something a sequel could improve upon big time. I think the best case scenario is you haven't played Chrono Trigger, or are just a casual turn based RPG enjoyer. I do want to say that this game doesn't feel derivative of Chrono Trigger, it absolutely stands out. I just feel the game underutilized its battle system. This isn't like Bravely Default II scenario for me, a game I feel is just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mess design wise (not to mention not remotely holding a candle in comparison to its predecessors, but I'm getting off topic. Ngl I just wanted an excuse to bash BD2 real quick). Sea of Stars is mechanically solid, I just feel it doesn't use those mechanics anywhere close to their full potential. I'm starting to repeat myself so I'll wrap this up. This game only took me about 25 hours, but the lack of variety, and my distaste for the finale, made it feel so much longer. Very much a one and done game for me.I know I just spent like 20 minutes writing a review bashing the game, but I genuinely wish Sabotage Studio the best in their next endeavor. And again, more power to the people who do like this game. I'm glad y'all find enjoyment in this game.

_childDocuments_.review: As I write this review I'm at hour 82 of this little piece of liquid joy, and I'm still on "act 2." I can't sing enough praises for this game, all I'll say, and I'm totally going there, is that while Baldur's Gate 3 was made with "big boy money" and may be bigger and prettier, Sea of Stars beats it in writing, world building, and soul... which to me, are all that matters in an RPG. Sea of Stars is a love letter to the JRPGs of yore, a longing to simpler times, times more innocent for the industry... much like the fantasy genre itself, and it shows in the colorful pixel art, music that takes after OG Yasunori Mitsuda, and world building that fills you with wonder every step of the way.As per the old high fantasy formula, Sea Of Stars is a zero-to-hero story of two kids who happen to be the latest generation of Solstice Warriors, an ancestral order created with the mission of exterminating monsters called "dwellers" which, unlike other monsters, not only don't age, also keep growing as long as they keep eating, so it's Solstice Warriors' duty to exterminate them before any of them grows into a World Eater (TL;DR, kids fated to save the world)... in this case, though, they're at least young adults... and against formula (and much to the delight of anyone tired of alocentric carp being shoved down our throats), the protagonists not only , also  (sorry, horndogs... but about time we got some aro representation in here, don't you think?).Graphics-wise, the game goes for old SNES looks... if some disgruntled Nintendo engineer had shoved all the extra-chips of a 16bit arcade board on a SNES. It pushes 16bit paradigm close to its limits of all you could visualize on said paradigm, providing rich vistas just at the right time and surprising "mock cut-scenes" for Ultimate Attacks, only one step from reaching Monsterboy's "perfect pixel" level (not quite there, but almost). In addition, key moments of the story enjoy fully-animated sequences in reminiscence of Playstation's old remakes of Lunar: Silver Star Story and Blue Star Story (granted, Sabotage couldn't grab a hold of Kadokawa Animation like old Game Arts did for Lunar, but it's still a most decent job).Music wise, if you're old enough to have enjoyed Chrono Trigger, you know what to expect, and the music blends with the art style to perfection to create an atmosphere of pure magic for old Gen-X gamers like me.What really takes the cake, though, is the world building... and again, I'm going THERE: Sure, Baldur's Gate benefitted from half a century of accumulated dnd lore, but  is exactly why I have so much more respect for Sea of Stars... SoS , no borrowed settings and no more help than the shoulders of giants they stood on to see farther than most. As a matter of fact, if I had to compare, I feel . It's not more of the same, it's not another Johnny Come Lately. In addition, and something I hope becomes SoS' contribution to the RPG genre, is : Rather than just hoarding text snippets with all bits of world building the devs couldn't manage to fit into the game's active narrative and that you have to remove yourself from said narrative (see, opening the menus) in order to read, SoS ads a "travelling magical historian" NPC for your party, and every time you come across a "codex entry," the historian (who happens to be disarmingly adorable) acquires a new tale to tell you when the party sets camp... and Teaks is an AWESOME storyteller.Again, nothing against Baldur's Gate 3, in fact it's still a game I want. Sea of Stars just happened to be the game I .

_childDocuments_.review: It doesnt need a game of BG3-scale to be great. No MX, SeasonPass or other BS. Just a complete game, aiming to cheer on beloved SNES titles, self-published by a small dev with only one game (really good, buy Messenger!!!) on prior record.  + content is more than enough, especially with side gigs+ had 1 bug(only visual) after 24hrs+ the world opens more while you progress, revisiting locations with new skills gives new loot       + you'll get more and more skills/tools to navigate faster in the world  - the more you         progress+ story is cute and well crafted - Mystery, Sci-Fi and Fantasy well packed       + many side stuff going on if you are eager to search for it or talk with your mates+ the soundtrack is so nice, all alone worth 30€+ graphics SNES-like but more detailed and with much love (lighting is OP)+ combat is responsive, good timing is valuable (basic attacks, magic, combos and some more)+ puzzles fit good, getting "harder" but not unfair+ loot comes after 1st location(bosses drop loot, random crates hidden in world, fishing etc.)+ cooking and fishing works great+ gamepad controls(xbox) work good - but jumping off cliffs still clunky+ you can choose perks after level up+ german translation good, found 2 typos after 10 hrs+ if you want there are relics available to ease up difficulty(loser)+ cute drawn short cutscenes (no voiceover) - no questlog or journal to track what you got to do- no mini map (frustrating when navigating cities, POIs are hard to find)- keyboard controls are clunky(play with gamepad[XBOX or PS])

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars was an outstanding game that I totally got my money's worth out of. I went into this game having played and 100%-ed The Messenger, so I very much enjoyed every single call back or reference to that game that Sea of Stars offered. But apart from the overlapping story and universe of these two completely different games, Sea of Stars blew me out of the water. Each area, mechanic, enemy, and story twist that the game offered only made me enjoy this game more and more. The only downsides I really have about this game is that the battle system does not get overly complex later into the story and I wish there was just a little more story explanation for The Messenger. For me, I enjoyed almost every second the battle system and thought that they expanded on it well over time. However, I have heard complaints that it may not be for everyone if you are more attuned to complex turn-based games. And with me wanting more Messenger stuff, I do wish that there was more explanation for why The Messenger took place, but maybe I will have to wait longer to see more of that (maybe in another game, or in some other parts of Sea of Stars that I haven't fully explored yet) Even with that, I still highly recommend this game.You don't need any prior story knowledge from The Messenger to enjoy this game, the game stands firmly on its own. I haven't even mentioned the outstanding soundtrack either! With everything being said, this is a game you should totally pick up and play without spoiling yourself about anything the game has to offer. Sabotage Studio outdid themselves once again.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a real throwback to JRPGs on consoles like Gameboy Advance. It reminded me a lot of Golden Sun which is one of my favourite GBA games of all time. I have yet to finish the game but I'm 10 hours in and I'm really enjoying the art, music, story and atmosphere of the game. The combat is turn-based, but extra elements have been added to make it a bit more engaging which I think is a great addition. I think the only downside for me is I'm finding it hard to connect with the main characters. They're likeable, but beyond that I don't feel invested in their story as much as I would like. I might feel different as I continue progressing through the game but that's just my opinion right now having spent the time I have thus far. With all that being said I couldn't recommend this game enough. It's a lot of fun to play and I appreciate the nostalgic feeling it gives me when I dive in. One other point I will raise is around the relic system. In the game you can obtain relics which change the way the game is played, such as making enemies harder, or allowing you to fully heal after each battle encounter. I think it's a really neat way to tailor the gaming experience for those who want a bit more of a challenge or simply want to enjoy the story and have things a bit easier for them. Buy this game, you won't regret it. It's worth it, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: A very intimate and beautiful experience that outshines the game's flaws. Sabotage studio continues to impress with their retro style game design, following The Messenger. As a gamer that enjoyed past titles that are now considered retro, I fully believe they managed to capture the same charm to bring out the nostalgic notes in me.The positives:- Unreal visual style, unlike anything I've seen for a pixel art game.- The amount of detail you notice when paying attention proves how much developers loved making the game.- Music is complimentory to the visuals and very distinct from one another.- Story has some twists to keep it spicy- The game is running super efficiently on Steam Deck. Barely lost any battery when playing. Major plus from my side.The negatives:- Character development is tricky. It's there, but it might not make the most sense.- Combat can get repetitive after a whileI highly recommend trying this game out. It's very special in my opinion and absolutely deserving of the awards it will get this year.

_childDocuments_.review: Not just one of the best indie games in recent years. Not just one of the best RPGs in a long while. Not just the single most visually stunning pixel art in any video game ever made. _childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is a combination of CT and BoF IIIWARNING - THIS REVIEW HAS BIG SPOILERSI just finished the game and I want to discuss it. By the way, CT is Chrono Trigger and BoF III is Breath of Fire III, two of my favorite JRPGs. So how SoS does compared to them? Not very well, specially taking into consideration that SoS borrows A LOT from these (90s) masterpieces. So, even standing on the shoulders of giants SoS doesn't reach the sky. But first I want to talk about...WHAT THE GAME DOES RIGHTThe art. SoS is gorgeous. I loved every place/environment that I visited, which was enhanced by the level design and how vertically the game is. You can climb, jump down, swim. Its amazing. The level design was also spot on on how many fights you are suppose to encounter in a given place. BoF III can get tiresome with its random battles, but not SoS. The transition to the fights is also very smooth. I also like how the enemies match the place you find them. It helps with the world building, which leads me to...WHAT THE GAME DOES WRONGSoS's main flaw is the writing - the characters, the story and the world building.CharactersA lot of people complained about how bland Valere and Zale are. They are still an improvement over the Silent Protagonist found in many JRPGs, but, yes, they are bland. You can defend them saying that their blandness fit their backstory, but that doesn't make them any less... bland. They are the protagonists, they need to be interesting! I'm not saying that they need to be deep like a Planescape Torment character, but they do need to have some defining qualities and flaws. It could have been tied to their stories and elements (Sun and Moon), like Zuko and Katara from The Last Airbender, for example. I think their blandness made the writer pour "personality" on Garl, which made an otherwise fine character into a really annoying one. The game tried to make me like Garl so much that I ended up disliking him. His death was so drawn out that by the time he died I was glad that its was over with. And then he got resurrected for the true ending! I think its lazy writing to kill a character just to make people feel anything... and its even worse when he comes back. Some people say that Garl seems like the true protagonist of the story and they are not wrong. He has more agency than the Zale and Valere, but he's a bad protagonist because everybody just loves him and he can get anything done. The other characters are not bad, they are just too shallow. Personality wise you can barely tell them apart. For example, lets compare how SoS and BoF III do the small talk at Camp. In SoS the character's dialogue is usually really dry and a direct remark of the story's current objective. But BoF III uses the Camp to show the personality of its characters. For example, Momo is an inventor that's says the first thing that comes to her mind. When Ryu, the protagonist, meets her, he is traveling with Nina, the princess of Wyndia. The first time you Camp with Momo in the party she says something like "Ryu, you know that traveling with a princess doesn't make you a prince, right?". That's funny and showcases Momo's personality. SoS doesn't have dialogue like this.Story and WorldbuildingThe story and the worldbuilding have a big problem of scope and scale. In other words, the story and the world don't fit the game's length, so everything feels shallow and rushed. Teaks doesn't fix this. You need actual playing time for the world, characters and journey to sink in. When I reached and crossed the Sea of Stars I didn't feel like I was in middle of an amazing journey. I barely felt at home in the "home world". But in BoF III (SPOILER ALERT), when I crossed the ocean and found a futuristic city with advanced and emotionless inhabitants and then went through the Desert of Death to fight a Goddess in a Sky Fortress, it felt like I was in a new world, far from home, because the game spent time to build that journey. It felt earned. Also, the lack of normalcy doesn't help. Everywhere except for Brisk and Mirth looks like a fantasy theme park, which leads me to the tone problem. When I fought Malkomud and found out that he was causing problems because he was bullied it felt so... childish. It felt like a kid's show. And then we have something like the Fleshmancer, that builds beings out of corrupted flesh. Its such a tonal clash. It reminded me of a show called Bravest Warriors. Its really hard to pull this kind of clash off. Bravest Warriors does it, but SoS doesn't.Another thing that the games does wrong is the Rainbow Conch and locking the true ending behind it. Guys, collectibles like this are lazy game content. It's there just to make the game feel longer than actually is. Locking the true ending behind them is such a low blow.Quick points about other elements:The animated scenes were pointless and a waste of resources imo. The storytelling the game did with still images after Garl died was much better than the animated scenes.Fishing was shallow and pointless. BoF III did it much, much better.The battle mechanics were ok, but lacked progression and skills.Some characters sprites were overdesigned, like Erlina, Brugraves and Hortence.For such a beautiful game, all the Ultimates were quite ugly.In the end, I think it is an average game that has great art and bad writing and ends up being worse than every game that it borrows from.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people think this game is the most chrono trigger game to be released since that masterpiece, but to me I feel like this game is the sequel to golden sun we never got. Sea of Stars is a beautiful game, but lacks in certain areas that older games perfected. Characterisation finds it's strength in characters outside the main characters, leaving the main characters to fill a silent protagonist role almost. There is no real love shown to the main characters, with both sort of being bland with 0 character growth, whilst Garl and Serai benefit from stellar character work. The art style of this game surpasses the likes of Chrono trigger with every shred of art in this game being filled with love and devotion. Amazing graphics that you will love.Battle is simplistic but fun. There's no real depth to it, more a case of strategic approach and determining which character you need for any one scenario.Story is not structured in a clever way, it's sort of faux linear with distractions, but also with an "Open world" filled with very little actual substance or things to do outside of your main objective or the mandated funny side mini game "Wheels" which I enjoyed.You'll enjoy this game if you were a fan of old gameboy RPGs or enjoy an actually well made sprite rpg. Don't expect this to reach the heights of Chrono trigger or Persona 4 but it is definetly a worthwhile use of your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing throwback to oldschool jrpgs while managing to have it's own identity. The story is great and the characters are fun and interesting. The combat is a solid 8/10, maybe 9/10 for novelty. If you're looking for challenging gameplay I recommend using the in game difficulty enhancers. Without them battles are engaging but not hard, and there's virtually no need to ever stop barreling forward.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed my time with this. Loved the art and pixel graphics the story was fine and the music was pleasant. There were only a handful of songs I'd listen to in my personal time, Songshroom Marsh being one of them. That being said, I really loved how each area had a day and night theme and how Val and Zale glowed blue and orange respectively in dark areas. The sound design was also great! Was totally grossed out stepping on the fleshy floors and enjoyed hearing the 'tink tink' of our resident glass man as he stomped across the ground. Serai ended up being one of my favorite characters(sucker for assassins who dual wield) and I loved her portal animation, it's fluid and gorgeous. It obviously took a long time to make because any time it can be used, it probably will be. I will say while I know the combat can get repetitive I personally enjoyed it. What I didn't enjoy was having to fight weaker enemies whenever I had to backtrack. Wish they would've just avoided me.As much fun as I did have, I really didn't like how Zale and Val kind of take a back seat to Garl. I adore Garl but it's advertised as a Valere and Zale story but without Garl it feels like there wouldn't BE a story. Maybe he should have been the main character instead. Another thing that bothered me a lot is that Serai caused a major incident that could have been avoided and no one calls her out on it. They just accept what happened and move on. Could've been great for some character conflict. I also wasn't a fan of having to do the final fight twice to get the true ending. By the time I reached the end of the game I already had everything I needed for the true ending done but it wouldn't let me go for it until I had the final confrontation once. It does drop you off right before the final confrontation once you get through the credits but it felt pointless considering who the the first 'final' boss was. Brugaves and Erlina also don't face any consequences for their actions in the true ending either they just get to live out their lives 'peacefully' which is a little unfair all things considered. I really did have a great time despite all my misgivings. Honestly didn't realize I had this many problems with it until I started typing(i'm sure it's fairly obvious I don't write these often). Managed to get 41/42 achievements on a first play through which is nice. I'll parrot another review I saw that said don't backtrack until you get air travel. I didn't know about that and a lot of my time was wasted running back and forth for things I couldn't do/access yet and trying to avoid weak enemies.

The storytelling, the graphics, the music, everything was well done! Definitely give this game a try! I'm going to sleep now. Goodnight everyone! - JNORJT

_childDocuments_.review: This is a decent game. It's not great and it's not bad - it's decent. The whole game screams "decent" in my opinion. I would recommend this game if it's on sale, to people that are itching for a new turn based rpg. In hindsight, I would not buy it for full price (34 euro here). This game also feels like a good introduction to the turn based rpg genre, as it is easy to learn the combat. However, the story might not be best suited for children since it can be rather dark at times. Completing the main story and some side quests took me 25-30 hours.Combat- Easy- New/unused mechanics- Small skill pool in beginning, making it feel like you aren't really progressing as you level upPuzzles- Very easyStory- Has a very slow pace- Decent overall, feels like they have the ingredients to make it much betterMusic- Varied. Sometimes okay, sometimes greatTLDR: If you want to try out a decent turn based rpg, buy it on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, Sea of Stars is 100% complete. With up to 40 hours of content at a reasonable price, Sea of Stars is very much a very good RPG in 2023 (and hey, it fits my taste too). Is it the best and unrivaled RPG that has come in recent years? Not for me because unfortunately, I tried Octopath Traveler II before this game.If I were to convert everything above into a score like other game journalists in their media, I would give Sea of Stars 85/100 or 8.5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me go through the stages of grief. I followed it since The Messenger and was unbelievably excited for it. If you love Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy, Super Mario RPG, or any other classic 16 bit RPG, then I'm afraid you might be disappointed. The game feels like its plot was generated by AI. Allegedly it gets better, but I'm almost 12 hours in and it is inconsistent, basic, and above all boring.The combat is okay. It's very very repetitive. What starts off as fun mini games of proper button timing devolves into chores very quickly. The game never realizes the power fantasy of an RPG. You never have great passive power where you can one shot a group of enemies without thinking. You always have to get your timings right with attacking and defending.The music is fine. I firmly believe that a games soundtrack resonates much stronger when linked with core memories of what was happening during it. Undertale is a prime example of the songs taking on a life of their own because of this. Sea of farts didn't get there during my time playing.Art work is pretty good! The pixel art needed a little extra love in certain spots, especially the outlines. Hard black lines mixed randomly thrown around some but not all things makes for a jarring contrast. Definitely needed an art director and not just artists.I'm heart broken that the game is such a chore to play and leaves me screaming at the screen with the plot. The Messenger was so good. But this might retroactively sour that too.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, who loves this type of combat. Story is simple, yet just enough to keep you going, to keep you invested in it. Combat has cute addition to classical turn based combat, the timing stuff maybe got tedious at some point, but still point to developers for trying to "spice up the combat". No, honestly, good game. The only downside what I really can think of, is that leveling part. You just don't get enough of levels in this game. The system is great, you get some stats automatically raised, and you can choose in addition what to increase more. But I ended the game being something like level 24 I think. Which is just too low. Yes I did not just go around kill stuff for fun, but I would expect to be at least level 35-45 playing for more than 34 hours. So improving the level system can be done in future!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars I heard was a successor to Chrono Trigger. I have not done all the side quest, but I believe I have a solid enough opinion to form my review of this game… no this gem. Because I am going to call this game exactly what it is. First off, a successor to Chrono Trigger, that’s still out there so I’ll hold off on if it is or not, but it does pay respect to it and in all the right ways. Story, Humor, Characters, and yes combat. However, I don’t think it’s a successor because the game is just too damn good and unique. Sea of Star steps up to the plate of a classic SNES JRPG and holds its own. It then looks at you says hold my beer, everything from sprites, graphics, music, combat, and story. It is solid with no frame rate issues and easy to use and very rewarding combat. It then looks at you and says just wait, you haven’t even seen anything yet. It takes advantage of the story and blows you away. The music for this game is too damn good. But when you have such a legend helping you compose music, what can you say but hell yes. 	My favorite part of this game is the music, the story is both compelling and will make you feel things. I won’t say what but your be in for a treat. It also has the guts to be as bold as it was and bravo! I want more, I would very much love to see more Sea of Star Games. My only regret was not backing such a S tier game on kick starter because I learn it was on there to late.I would also love to see more games with Eric W. Brown and Yasunori Mitsuda doing music because yeah. Just wait, that moment above your know it when it hits. I highly recommend this gem.Edit: As of 11/9/2023 I have done the stuff needed to answer the chrono trigger successor remark. Its definitely inspired by it but no its not. Its as I said earlier its to unique and just to damn good. That game is a gem and all I’ll say is, hot dayum what I just fought took me an hour. And that felt good.  The main Antagonist is definitely in my top ten villain list. As for those going for the you know what… good luck, your need it. However I would be fine if this took Chrono’s mantal. I feel confident enough in the development team that they could do that, and that’s saying something.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a product of love and dedication. I strongly recommend it to everyone who enjoyed the SNES style RPGs (Mario RPG and Chrono Trigger). That sentiment isn't exactly unfamiliar to anyone who has heard of this game before, but I reiterate it here because of how accurate it is. I was cautiously anticipating this game's release, as video game hype tends to lead to disappointment.My only disappointment is that the game is over :/

_childDocuments_.review: The kind of SMRPG nostalgia trip this gives me with timed hits is impeccable. Story?                          Linear. But that's not a bad thing. Progression of areas?  Linear. But that's not a bad thing.Obtaining items           Linear. But that's not a bad thing.and abilities?A lot of the ways this game handles how you interact with it is fairly linear, but introduces segments where you're (somewhat) free to explore each and every map, but must do the objective in a straight line. This isn't necessarily a bad thing. It streamlines things for the player; it makes a lot of abilities, key items, ingredients very easy to find, and it's an enjoyable romp from start to (almost) finish.I will say, the ending does feel a bit like a cop-out for a boss fight. I won't spoil, but it could have been done with a bit more of a bombastic finish. If they plan to make a sequel, I'd gladly support it.

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolutely awesome game.Right off the bat, you get immediate Chrono Trigger Vibes.  Map layouts are all similar to CT, but yet it has a...new, uniqueness feel to it, that just feels right.  Combat and moving all feel fluid.  You can tell the developers spent lots of time making homage to games of yesteryear, but creating a new masterpiece for a new generation along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The art and music of this game are second to none.  Hearing Yasunori Mitsuda's compositions in this RPG love-letter was nothing short of beautiful.  The game takes a lot of inspiration from Breath of Fire III, Chrono Trigger, and Illusion of Gaia (as well as many other old school RPGs).  The combat system is simple, but fun.  You need to use certain kinds of attacks to break the attacks of the enemies and disrupt their moves.  Leveling was never grindy, and the game is fairly easy overall.  There are settings within the Relic system of the game make it even easier, but I don't recommend using most of those because they take away any semblance of challenge that the game might have had.  The biggest criticisms I have about the game are the story and the writing especially.  The story is simplistic, and that would almost be forgivable since most old school RPGs had fairly shallow stories.  But the writing is really bad.  The main characters have almost no personalities and far too many of the characters respond with predictable tropes, one-liners, or "Hahaha!"  That said, even with the poor writing, the game is still fun.  If you you grew up playing games like Chrono Trigger/Cross, the Final Fantasy series, Breath of Fire, Illusion of Gaia, or other classic RPGs, you'll find something to like about Sea of Stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game. It is a solid RPG that focuses more on the story than grinding, leveling, min-maxing. I never had any problem going into fights where I felt I was fighting an uphill battle. The game gave me the same feeling that the older mario RPGs on the Gameboy and the DS had with the leveling system and combat.The game is not long in comparison of other RPGs that I have played and could probably be beat in around 10-15 hrs or even less if the person playing it just did the main story and did not explore.I did like the relic system that allows the player to increase or decrease the relative difficulty of the game if they wanted to.One of my few gripes with the game was that the player barely would barely find any gold so you had to be sparse with your spending especially in the latter portion of the game when stuff gets on the more expensive side. This being said I did not need to buy the best gear/items to progress it was just sometimes frustrating when you get to a new store and you are only a few gold short even after selling some other items.All in all I would definitely recommend this game to anyone that enjoys RPGs that seem to focus more on the story or have played similar type RPGs like I stated above.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Game would rank 3 out of 5 stars if that was an option. Worth the time to explore around the environments and engage in the mechanics if you are a fan of these types of games.  The reason this isn't one to remember in the genre isn't because they make genre meta comments within the game (blacksmiths keep getting better the further you go..., etc.) but rather they do the genre a disservice in their nonexistant character writing. Characters, including the villians, are all one note. There are several late-game animated scenes suggesting we feel about these characters fates without noticing there hasn't been an arc or any character development in the first place.The second comment worth mentioning is the combat. It's a unique focus for a game within the genre. The player can equip relics that function as an easy or hard mode and they can be adjusted at any time during the playthrough. The combat functions around the ability to block and critical hit, which is based on timing. So, if you learn to one-time your way through enemy and character animations, you can master the combat. Some enemies go to Elden Ring levels of delayed attacks (I'm gonna getcha,,, in a moment.. gonna getcha... swing) to keep the player guessing. It's a mixed bag, but overall not very engaging.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying that, in my eyes, this is a good game and I really wish there was a neutral review rating. I heard this game was heavily inspired by Chrono Trigger. Having not only loved the Messenger (The dev's previous title), but numerous JRPGs as well, I quickly wanted to play this game. After playing it for the time I have, it just doesn't add up to much. Many people complain of the dialogue being rampantly present, but that never really bothered me.What got in my head is when I started to compare this to Chrono Trigger. Numerous questions popped in my head; "Why does a game with little character to character dialogue have far more character fleshing than a game with plenty of it?", "Why does this game feel boring compared to Chrono Trigger?" and more questions similar to it. I came to realize that this game does certain things that make the game slowly erode the atmosphere it developed, all while keeping the player on a linear track. The opening of Chrono Trigger allows you to explore an entire content before you progress the main story, you hardly get an additional area in Sea of Stars; the most you get is a fishing pond. The next thing is how the areas in Chrono Trigger seemed to flow much better. In Sea of Stars it makes plenty of sense to find  in or perhaps finding a  in a  It just doesn't fit into the world as cleanly as it might like. The puzzles are decent but there just a matter of using the concept you just got and following an A to B to C sort of method to solve. I understand you can't make games too hard because it might push the casual crowd away, but I find it really annoying to find myself treated as if I have the intelligence of a child. I did not finish the game, nor get to a point in which the map opens up, but from the other reviews I read, this hardly opens the map but acts as a vessel to continue the linear story. Overall, this game is a fine game, but hardly approached the quality presented by Chrono Trigger. More than anything, listing this as a love letter to the game made me compare it to Chrono Trigger in the first place, and it just make the experience lacking and unremarkable.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I should preface this by saying that I've never played any traditional JRPGs like Chrono Trigger and I tend to dislike turn based RPGs however this game does something that I think other turn based rpgs fail at which is... makes combat fun. As for characters, I haven't played much of the game but as of the 1.2 hour mark I have loved them all. The main cast really feels like a group of 3 friends going on an adventure. Is this game perfect? No. But I see it as a very good entry into a genre that I normally wouldn't care about. I heavily recommend this game to anyone looking to get into this certain genre of games over something more dated.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the best elements from so many classic rpgs and puts them all together cohesively.  The games greatest strength is that it looks beautiful, There is also a ton to do with collecting chests and doing side quests and finding the rainbow conches.Combat is pretty straightforward and becomes a bit more strategic when the locks (which if unlocked before the enemies turn could cancel their move and save your party from taking some big damage). start coming into play in fights which will keep you on your toes if you already grow accustomed to the games combat system which borrows heavily from Mario RPG with timed inputs for additional damage and reduction. The only thing that moved a bit slow for me was the story it was difficult to stay into initially, but if you ride it out it does get better the further in you get. good game overall i definitely recommend it

_childDocuments_.review: only got 15 hours so far and i'm enjoying this game to the maximum level, the plot is good with few twists that you might not expect.there's a lot of stuff to explore and enjoy specially the mini game within, that's alone i spent 2 hours into.graphic and sound both are amazing and on point.been waiting for this game since it came out on kickstarter in 2020 and it did deliver more than expected, thankfully I avoided any spoiler as i didn't watch the trailer or playing the demo, can't wait to finish it .the only con of this game, that the fight sometimes is repetitive but i can look past that with what the game provided me with.

_childDocuments_.review: Saw it on steam on the day it came out and I liked how it looked so I bought it, not expecting it to be such a good game. It has a very good flowing story and the game play is quite fun. Systems and mechanics are introduced to the player via the story and it's engaging you to look for places where you can use them.  It has that 90's aesthetic with graphics and sound which is just the right amount- not making you feel like you are playing a super old game.You have to read through the story, there is no voice acting which I really enjoyed (not sure if this is common for games like this).The total time it took me was around 40 hours, without me rushing and grinding, so it's pretty good for a game of its price. Then I went back to grind for the achievements which in total brought my game-play to 72 hrs.There was only one issue that I encountered: - one of the characters did not load properly on screen and the game just stopped the progression when it came to their dialog box. The way I fixed it was by loading the last saved game up 2-3 times and it fixed it.Other than that, I would say it's a pretty solid game and I would highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: If you like solid mechanics, story and characters. Grab this.This game was charming and months after playing still sits in my heart. A personal test I hold for whether a games is "great" is whether the story and characters resonate enough that they follow me in life in a sense. In comparison I recently played Assassin Creed mirage 100% days after release and I recall nothing from that game aside from the lady doing the little rascals Froggy voice... _childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, AMAZING GAME. It was a great, hypnotizing experience. I really recommend you play it.But now, a more thorough personal review.The gameplay was quite impressive. The combat style seems based on the Chrono Trigger formula (which was already very satisfying back then), but it goes further with some improvements that make it more dynamic and engaging. I was really excited for every boss fight, even the hardest ones. Also, I really hate grinding in games, and here I had to do none of it. Let me state this clearly. ZERO. GRINDING. Thank you, developers.When it comes to the graphics, my satisfaction was equally great. They don't just remind you of Super Nintendo classics (Chrono Trigger above all else, naturally), but they are really fascinating. I never thought I'd play this kind of RPG around such beautiful scenarios, special effects and character designs. Special praise to the Port Town of Brisk, a vibrant and full of life location that I never wanted to leave. If they did a spin-off based only in the town, I'd buy it.Speaking now of the characters, they were quite captivating as well. The developers ditch the old concept of the silent protagonist, and just go with two very expressive leads. And every relevant character here has a variety of visual expressions, which makes them much relatable to, and the dialogues even more interesting.When it comes to the story, I must say that I really liked the pace of it, not feeling dull at any time. It was creative and compelling, and felt quite original. I confess I was wary that they would go the easy way and try to Force Awaken it, creating a story that relied on parallels with Chrono Trigger, but they delivered something worthy. Make no mistakes, there are some parallels, but they didn't seem central to the narrative at all, but rather a nostalgic wave to an inspirational game.I do think the narrative could be improved in some points, though. Some concepts or characters seemed to receive little explanation, leaving me confused for a while before finally putting the pieces together - that's nice when done on purpose, but my comment here is about stuff that I don't think was supposed to be that way. Still, it was a great story, and I could follow it well despite those minor flaws.By the way, I was a little bit frustrated at some points, because the cutscenes seemed too long for me. It is good to have the story well told, but some of them seemed to me like they could be interlapsed with some action, or at least some "stop and save" moments. I wanted to read all the dialogues, but sometimes I had to get out of the game, and couldn't finish all the scenes, but I also didn't want to go all the way back.One complaint must be filed here. Some of the side quests can only be completed AFTER finishing the main story. I wish that was hinted at in the game itself, so I didn't waste some hours backtracking to find missing pieces that were unavailable at that moment. Eventually, I gave up and searched the internet for answers, realizing there was nothing to be done yet.But on the brightside, it was nice to have that amount of side stuff to unravel, and exploring that world was really pleasing.When it comes to the music, I really enjoyed the overall production. There are many cool songs in this game, and I liked the match between them and the scenarios/occasions. But even though Yasunori Mitsuda was involved, and did a great work, I feel like a game that is inspired on Chrono Trigger has to draw the comparison to that work. And here, you might feel like it doesn't measure up, but just because the soundtrack in CT was simply a masterpiece. If you played that game, I bet you can easily remember at least one of its songs, if not a handful. That is an unfairly high bar, so this is not a negative comment on Sea of Stars, just something I couldn't help but bring it out.Before I finish, let me just state something. There is a mini-game inside the game. It's called Wheels. I loved it. I wanna play it against human beings. I was addicted to a mini-game inside the game that I was already addicted to. Please, tell me there's an Wheels app coming on soon.In conclusion, I think this game lived up to the hype. Despite the few negatives described above, it was worth every penny I spent to play it on launch.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Loved this game. Instant classic. Turn on the relics to make it less frustrating if you're having trouble with battle and timings, it's not going to short change your experience at all. The people who say the story was weak weren't paying attention. Tons of fun side quests and collectables and the true ending is a must. The easter egg's added are a lot of fun too.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer: I backed this on Kickstarter. Take that as you will.I'm a couple hours in and this is definitely giving me those good JRPG vibes. A lot of people are saying it's like Chrono Trigger, and I think it's apt enough of a comparison, but I'd say that moment to moment (combat especially) it reminds me of Super Mario RPG. You have pure turn based combat with timed hits and blocks, and spells have little timing bits to get you some extra oomph. Mana in this game is a variable resource, you'll be spending it and getting it back very often. The Combo system, that lets you do Chrono Trigger-style dual tech type moves, is a use-it-or-lose-it system so when you get the meter it means you have full license to go full throttle instead of saving it for another fight. Gear is a pretty simple affair so far, there aren't a zillion different types of armor slots. There's a lock system for interrupting enemy spells, and basically it asks for you to hit an enemy with the attacks shown and as of now it's interesting. Not having enough MP to have access to all your moves to break locks feels really punishing, so learning to conserve your MP feels important.The story has been nice so far, though I'm only a couple hours in like I said. Garl is a real homie, I like him. I'm not really buying into the main villain being called "The Fleshmancer", it kinda sounds silly to me. It's on-the-nose and not very foreboding. If the game has a creepy tonal shift when him or his goons are on screen, maybe I'll lighten up.Overall really enjoying my time so far. I'm hoping to update this review as time goes on. So far, very positive impression.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars was a game I was looking forward to for years and it exceeded my expectations dramatically! Amazing engaging turn based combat, honoring old school RPGs while not keeping the bad parts. Fantastic soundtrack. Great story but not overwhelming. The mini table top game is so much fun too! :)

_childDocuments_.review: 100% one of the best games of 2023! A total JOY to play from start to finish! If you're at all a fan for the turn based genre then this game will be one of your favorites especially if you loved Chrono Trigger! The normal ending had me wondering why? And then I learned there was a TRUE ending and that instantly made this game a 10/10 for me. Please play this game and you will not regret it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful and visually detailed game, but that's all it had going for it for the 3-ish hours I spent playing it. The characters were as deep as a puddle and the story was the platonic form of generic. The English translation was pretty bad - or was it the writing broadly? It's difficult to care about the characters when the game itself doesn't. Traumatic things happen to apparently main characters and the game just moves on, immediately, as if nothing's happened.And yet, it's hard to believe how undefined the characters are given how much time they spend talking.Anyway, there are plenty of good-faith critical reviews of this game, and they seem to agree on the main points of where it goes wrong. _childDocuments_.review: not 100% because screw the last achievement. I'm not restarting the game just to fight 10 bosses with a single specific relic turned on.I do want to point out that this game is not perfect. And frankly, it doesn't need to be. It plays out just fine, has its boring moments that are balanced out by its interesting and fun moments. There's just enough world-building and the cast is relatively lovable. The character development is barely there, but the story is cliche enough to not need a lot of it. Weirdly enough, lack of character development would be a huge negative for me, but in this game I ended up appreciating other things besides the characters a lot more so it distracted from the cast where it needed to.There's a good amount of positives. While yes, the game could have improved in some aspects, it's fine the way it is as I mentioned earlier. This game carried itself well.1.	Story: Very straightforward and simple story. Can't go too wrong here especially if the game was designed to be the studio's love letter to older games. I won't mention any of it here because it's best for you to experience it yourself. You work with your band of friends to defeat the evildoers and find out the real strength were your unwavering beliefs and bonds you made along the way.2.	Combat: it is simple, but fun. It follows the standard turn-based features, but expands on how turn orders function as well as turn manipulation. Since you have different party members later on, you get to choose whether you want to focus on just your favorite characters, or mix and match different combinations to have different approaches to fights.3.	Art: it is GORGEOUS. From the backgrounds, to character sprites, to the animations and colors, it's all masterfully chosen and drawn. The devs went all out on the art and it shows with every step you take in each area.4.	Music: wonderfully composed. The soundtracks are amazing and fits every area and encounter very well. I found myself even pausing at times just to listen before moving on.5.	Customization: there isn't a whole lot, but for what the game is, it's enough. Every time you level up, you get to choose which stat you want to invest in. This will allow you to build each of your characters differently even if they had a default path. It's not very impactful as you'll realize the best level-up option to get would be your MP, but you don't necessarily have to depending on your playstyle.There's a few things to address in this game.1.	A lot of the core gameplay is very repetitive and some fights are either way too easy or way too hard. If you're not someone who likes sticking to one style, you might end up defaulting to a very "meta" playstyle like I did. The reason this isn't a major issue is because you can augment how your fights go very easily with the relics they give you from the start on top of having food to heal when needed.2.	Lack of flexibility in character skills becomes noticeable the more you play. As some others may have meme-d it, this game is very much 75% Moonerang and Moonerang only. The game makes up for this by having enemies be vulnerable to different elements, so you don't cast Moonerang every round, it's just every other round instead. Jokes aside, only two characters have meaningful skill sets (no it's not both protagonists, just Ms. Moonerang), everyone else does not have anything truly useful. I wish the devs implemented skill trees because that would not only add customization, it would add different depths to how characters can be utilized.Here’s where I think they just had questionable administrative calls on the game.1.	Some enemies don't give you any time to react or to cancel their attacks and it can really screw you over. Because of this, you might end up having to play in a fashion just to survive or straight up bully them. 2.	The villains feel very low-effort. None of them were very impactful and the few that were, were ultimately wiped from the story less than halfway through the game. Fights just end up becoming mob farming simulator without feeling like beating the different bosses accomplished something. The final bosses were the only bosses that felt fulfilling to fight because they actually carried lore weight.3.	So...I had mentioned the story as a positive for being very simple; however, it's also right at that point where it's a negative as well. At certain parts of the story without spoilers, the transitions are very poorly done and it comes off as if story didn't even matter. Some things are never thoroughly explained and left as plot holes while others are brushed off as a character's attitude when it really diminishes the value of the cut-scene at that moment.Conclusion: good game, it ticks off all the boxes it needs to. Could it have been better? Absolutely, but it is fun just the way it is. Even if you don't plan on playing this anytime soon, it deserves a spot on your wishlist if you like RPG's. Unless of course, my major issues speak volumes to you.

_childDocuments_.review: I appreciate the devs for trying to make a game of this style, but overall I think this game falls super flat.  Hopefully they will learn from the negative feedback instead of just dismissing it all due to the obvious success of this game.Pros-Very, VERY pretty game.  One of the best looking 2D RPG's I've ever played pretty easily and I've just about played them all.-Dungeon design is actually very solid.  This was probably one of the parts of the game that most felt like it understood those older games.  The dungeons are varied and mostly designed in a way where you are always doing something, or solving some kind of minor puzzles.  I think that because of the absurd amount of dungeons in the game and bad pacing though you get pretty heavy dungeon fatigue in the end.Cons-Game is laughably easy.  This point puzzles me as this is such a niche genre at this point who is this being dumbed down for?  For reference all I really ask is that the game expects me to engage in it's systems in order to win.  I don't need the thing to be SMT or anything.  Anyways it's absurdly, roll your face on the keyboard easy and that is super unfortunate.  They give you items to make the game harder, but the onus of game balance should not be on the player.  That's like the self checkout of game design.  In my experience I did end up equipping the stuff that makes the game harder to try to actually enjoy the game and it was fine up until a moment deeper int he game where the difficulty spikes to such an absurd level I turned it off and then got very upset the game was way too damned easy again...-Lack of pacing, lack of freedom.  The game seems to think the only thing RPG's are is dungeons and combat.  At some point you realize you are just running from one dungeon to the next constantly with nothing to break it up in between.  There is a gorgeous world map (I miss world maps so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much in RPG's) and it's kind of all for naught.  I dropped the game pretty close to the end, but as far as I was (30 hours) the game never opens up.  Not once.  And the few times it tries to act like it does you just go directly to where you have to go because you can't do anything at any of the other locations until the game wants you to.  This is an incredibly scripted go from x to y to z design philosophy and even then whenever you have to go anywhere the game just flat out says: hey go right here, exactly.  Oftentimes "right here exactly" is: walk out of dungeon you are in, your characters appear on the world map, walk left or right 10 paces, start new dungeon.- Itemization is incredibly bland and boring.  Itemization is pretty terrible outside of some decent ideas for trinkets, and most of the things you find in the dungeons has been so QoL'ed that you start to just know what the loot will be.  New weapon for a character who doesn't have a new weapon yet, collectible stuff for side quests, ingredients for cooking.  The design feels way too safe and uninteresting.-Great idea's in the battle system, but it's executed pretty poorly.  For a game genre designed around character growth and dripfeed game mechanics it is wild to me they chose to only give each character 3 skills.  This helps to kill the pacing as well because you are just running through 3000 dungeons using the same moves constantly.  I love the Mario RPG esque timing mechanics, but you realize pretty quick that there are generally like 2 types of timing moves.  you press the timing when the move finishes, or you hit the button to a specific timing ala Mario's super jumps in Mario RPG.  I am exxagerating here a little, but only slightly.  The lock system is actually really cool and I love the idea behind it, but it is implemented so rigidly that it's more like a puzzle game at times where it almost forces you to use X character with X attack and god forbid you don't have the mana.  The lock system also matters so much less if you are just playing the regular difficulty and ends up being trivial for the most part anyways outside of boss fights when the lock attacks do negligible damage and you can just burst down enemies anyways.-Story kind of falls off a cliff.  From reading some of these other reviews I think people expected a lot more of the story from this game than I did.  I WANT to expect these games to have plots and characters on the level of Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy 6/7/8/9, Xenogears, ect.  But I think it's a little ludicrous to expect that, especially in the modern game landscape.  That said I found the story and characters pretty enjoyable up to a point, I just think it kind of gets way too uninteresting and detached by the point I got to.  Which, to be honest is way more about the games pacing issues than the story.  I think If I wasn't so sure every single plot point would be followed by 3 dungeons to get to the next plot point I wouldn't mind it as much.  It does have a lot of deus ex machina and such just based on the story they were going for, and I don't think it was all inherently bad, but I do think they could have done a better job making me give a damn about the second half of the game as if it felt earned I think a lot of the craziness in the second half could be pretty cool.Overall I really wanted to like this game, but it was pretty apparent to me right out the gate with the absurdly easy difficulty that it was going to be an uphill battle.  I got almost to the end and never finished the game,  I lost interest at about 20-25 hours in and tried to power through but it just kept going and going with the dungeons.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: If you loved Chrono Trigger and don't go into this thinking it'll be Chrono Trigger 2, and you'll love this game. Itches the exact same JRPG scratch. Otherwise:Strongly recommend the game. If you're on the fence because the comparisons to Chrono Trigger seem over-stated, they're not. It has a lot of its own character, mechanics and design, but there's a clear emulation through admiration here. The music's great,  the characters all have their own personality/backstory and don't feel like filler, the core plot feels substantial and worth completing, it's not predictable though it's not obtuse either, the graphics are exactly what you'd want in an homage to Chrono Trigger, and the combat mechanics are pretty engaging.There're push-your-luck, puzzle and reflex mechanics with every turn of combat. For example, an enemy will drop a powerful move in 2 turns, and you need to hit them with a combination of effects before then to cancel it. You have only 2 turns, and a combination of moves, combos, elements, etc. all need to be considered to cancel the move. And they're not at all obvious sometimes. It keeps you thinking through what may've just been an encounter. It's not as simplistic as Chrono Trigger was, but it absolutely feels good and it retained the team member combo move mechanics.I've also heard comment that it's not as open-world as Chrono Trigger, but that's false. The game does have a very linear plot up to a point in the story, but after that you're free to explore the world and complete side-quests. Worth reminding folks Chrono Trigger was also very linear until you got to the time machine in the Keeper's Dome, which isn't for a while into the main plot.I think the only things I would bring up in caution about the game is that equipment doesn't play much of a role. It didn't in Chrono Trigger either, really, but it did feel more important then. In SoS you get regularly stronger items, at regularly paced chests, or regularly met merchants. You do find the occasional 'rare' piece in some random chest, but it's not often enough to say it makes item-finding more interesting. There is a mechanic called 'relics' that are basically game-state options made into collectible items. You can use them or not, but they'll make the game easier or harder. For example, there's a relic that makes many of your attack counters auto-successful. I don't use it myself, but someone who wants a more story-focused experience? Good relic to find. Also Garl as a character is the embodiment of 'toxic positivity', to the point where sometimes you want him to shut up and be somber for like, two minutes. So other than Garl's overly-optimistic personality, no other issues.As a note: the game is oddly dark with the default brightness. I recommend cranking it up a bit to really appreciate some of the pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is truly a mixed bag.On the one hand, it has fantastic art direction, beautiful character, asset and background designs, creative map and level layouts, and pleasant music.On the other hand, it suffers from an uninspired good vs. evil story, bland characters with no actual personality, dull dialogues, and a mediocre combat system. Combat:Very creative enemy designs with cool moves. Unfortunately, the art direction and visuals are where the positives end for me. The strategic element is shallow and offers little depth. Characters cannot be specialized, classes don't exist, weapons and items offer no diversity or notable differences. The amount of attacks and combinations that can be used in regular fights is limited and you hardly every get to use the interesting combo-attacks and ultimates outside of boss-battles. Instead, strategic depth is replaced by a quick time event type system, where you have to press a button during an attack to either boost your own damage or reduce the enemies damage. Fights quickly become extremely repetitive and require very little thinking as long as you manage to hit most of the frame perfect quick time events.Story and dialogues: There isn't much to say. Simple stories can work well but require strong characters to carry them. Sea of Stars' characters have hardly any recognizable personality traits, with the two protagonists being indistinguishable from each other. No interesting conversations, no conflicts, no banter. Everyone agrees with each other on everything. Art:This is where the game really shines. Everyone who worked on the art did a fantastic job. Maps and levels are creatively designed and don't get boring. Characters, monsters, and backgrounds look beautiful. The music fits whats seen on screen. Sound design is also great. Nothing to complain. One of the prettiest pixel based game out there.Overall, the game is an okay-ish experience but I wouldn't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were really into games like Chrono Trigger, you'll like this game. It definitely has the feel of an old SNES era JRPG. There is a lot of extra exploring if you choose to do it. There's a lot of honing timing for extra attacks and blocks. The story isn't revolutionary (OMG Save the world!)- and while the two main characters strike me as a little flat, the other characters in the game more than make up for that. They're not silent protagonists, but I wonder if that wasn't kind of what they're trying to pull off, so that they're easier to put yourself into the game through them. Either way, I'm 7 hours in and am really enjoying myself. The animations and environments are all beautiful, and have lovely touches of details that make them more enjoyable and interesting. The music is fantastic, new but still somehow... nostalgic. I love this game. I foresee a new game in my top 10, which has been stagnant for a very long time.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of these reviews come from people who have nostalgic memories of playing classics like Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy, etc. Unfortunately, I did not get to play/experience these as a child, so I am coming at this game without the nostalgia filter. And....it is absolutely fantastic. The characters grabbed me and drew me in, the pixel graphics are a treat for the eyes, the music....there are parts of this game where I just idled so I could listen to the soundtrack. And the story - 1000/10. I don't cry super frequently in games, but this game made me weep. The gameplay is very fun, with the combat being simple on the surface, but taking time to master (there are still parts I haven't timed correctly after 48 hours' worth of playtime.) And there are plenty of secrets to be discovered!Go in blind, avoid spoilers as if your life depended on it, and go enjoy an absolute beautiful example of a passion project game. I am already excited for what Sabotage has for us next!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to 100% the game first before giving a review, but last achievement is complete bullsh*t, so screw thatSo, what can I say about Sea of Stars? It ain't Chrono Trigger, despite it desperately trying to be, not even close. But it is still a decent and enjoyable game.Presentation of the game is great: graphics are just gorgeous, animated cutscenes are just breathtaking, music is great, locations are vibrant and memorable, level and puzzle design is fun. Minigames and sidequests are neat, I actually enjoyed Wheels, and fishing.Battle system.... is okay. It starts really promising and fun, but then it just doesn't deliver on the promise. It stops evolving way too quickly, about 50% into the game you already seen almost everything game can show you in that regard. Each character has only three skills, and also  combos with each other, and one Ultimate each - and honestly, that's not enough for variety and synergy. Not the worst, but not really something to write home aboutAnd for writing... Uuh... Yet again, starts promising, but the more you play, the more issues you notice. Bar few exceptions, characters are pretty bland, story relies on prophesies, visions and emotional power ups a bit too much, some plot threads are outright abandoned, ending is not really satisfying, and I think there might be even some plot holes, but I might be wrong on that one.But on the other hand, while lows are eeeeh, highs are freakin' high. This game both made me cry and also say "Holy sh*t" multiple times. And that enough is worth it. It ain't Chrono Trigger, but so are most of the games ever. Despite flaws, it is still fun and emotional game, that has some tricks up its sleeveP.S. Garl best boy

_childDocuments_.review: Edit at completion: Wow! Just, WOW! This game was everything I hoped for and more. A++++ for Sabotage on a game very well done.Reviewed at ~5 hours game play..This game looks stunning within the confines of the style it uses. It's like the 16 bit era on speed.The controls, I used a XBox One controller, are silky smooth and everything responds as you would expect.The combat system is simple, some would say too simple, but I wouldn't, It has what it needs and it handles it perfectly.The few dungeons I've done so far have been nice, typical early game stuff with the obligatory hand holding tasks for new abilities etc.Music - Oh Boy! There is a lot of the usual stuff you would expect from a JRPG style game, emotional damage tracks, victory fanfares boss bangers, and it's all crisp and a delight to listen to. *****BEWARE*****When you first hear Dance of 1000 Suns, the one I have dubbed Garl's Theme, make sure to set your volume high and set aside a good ten minutes while you drop all game play and bop away to this instant classic.The main characters I have met so far are your generic good guys so nothing much to write about there, but it's still early yet so that could change.Some of the support cast I've encountered up to now are great, even getting some little laughs at the naming and characteristics of some (not gonna spoil here).Overall:My first impressions of this game are outstanding. I really do like it. It's not perfect, but it's a damned solid instalment into the modern retro 2D/3D JRPG library.My fingers are crossed that the rest of the game is as enjoyable for me as the first 5 hours have been.
