_childDocuments_.review: RPGs are complex games and they are difficult to make. RPG fans, like me, are unusually very demanding. The classic, turn-based formulas were slowly abandoned by bigger developers in search of a wider audience. The torch is figuratively passed to smaller teams with lesser demand for ROIs. The resurgence of the classic JRPG has brought us many excellent games and one of them would be Sea of Stars. At least that was what I thought when I saw this game for the first time. In August 2023, Studio Sabotage entered into the foray of the RPG world with this game, and it was received with such an overwhelmingly positive reception. My experience, however contrast the general reception of the game. here is whyThe players begin by choosing Zale or Valere as the main controllable characters. This is a purely inconsequential choice, as they can be used interchangeably a few hours into the game.Zale and Valere are Solstice Warriors, born respectively at the zenith of the sun and the moon solstices. They wield the sole magic that can destroy maleficent creations of the evil Fleshmancer called Dwellers, which have plagued their world for eons.After extensive training since childhood, both warriors are ready to graduate as full-fledged warriors. This serves as the initiation for the players as well, and the first dungeon teaches us how to overcome obstacles in this world. Upon regaining control after a lengthy cutscene, the effort Sabotage put  becomes apparent, starting with the movement. It is unbelievably dynamic yet straightforward, and each character is animated with such life and personality. For instance, when crossing a tightrope, Valere balances calmly without losing her posture, while Zale sways slightly left and right. I appreciate these subtle ways of conveying the characters' temperament. They can also jump, fall down, and mantle ledges, emphasizing the vertical and layered level design even in the tutorial dungeon.Enemies roam throughout the dungeon floor, and touching them initiates combat without transitioning to another screen. Sea of Stars employs a timing-based combat system. Pressing the prompted button at the right moment strengthens your attack and weakens the blows you receive from enemies. Regular attacks restore your MP, allowing characters to use various skills with different button prompts for extra oomph. For example, Zale’s fireball can be held until it reaches the optimal size and then released for extra splash damage.Damage dealt and received will charge a combo meter. When filled, two characters or more can unleash powerful combos that deal multiple damage types at once. The game cleverly uses these attack types and elements beyond the usual rock-paper-scissors formula. When enemies start their big attacks, “locks” appear above their heads.This system integrates seamlessly with the active timing combat. This means you can break the locks in just one turn with the right skill and timing. This is where the game’s core mechanic lies: rationing MP, managing the combo meter, health, and using abilities at the right time are the rules of the game’s engagement.So, what’s the problem then? The issues arise later in the game, where I feel like the combat hasn’t evolved beyond the basics. Sure, the party will grow, and you will gain new skills, but the activities with those skills and combos aren’t that interesting for two dozen hours. There are no buffs, status effects, or synergies. In the end, you’re just attacking and healing. The lock and interrupt system get barely more complex because while there are more elements and attack types, the basics stay the same throughout 50 hours of playtime. There are also random elements where, when the battle begins, you will get some complex locks where you won’t have enough combo meter to cancel enemies' attacks. In the end, there is only one sure way to “get good” at this game: mastering the block timing of enemies' attacks. Maybe this is the intended way to play it, and there are various kinds of attacks and enemy types, each quite different from another. The problem, at least for me personally, is the lack of tactical depth I want from turn-based RPGs. Combined with the lack of an option for running away from battles, and some combat encounters are difficult to avoid makes the mid to late game especially frustrating.Character growth is another problematic element of the game. Every level up, you have the option to raise a stat point on top of predetermined stat growth. That means later on, each character will have their specialization in the party, yet it never happened. For example, you want to make Garl a tank because of his high base HP and defense. Yet you cannot pick to increase his HP every level up; instead, the game roulettes four stats out of eight (whether this is random or predetermined, I don't know), so there’s no truly specializing by consistently increasing a certain stat on a character. It just results in a frustrating illusion of choices.I feel the same way about the storytelling of this game. The true dullness hides behind the facade of a promising hook and beginning. Without saying too much, the most obvious example of bad writing is how the plot progresses using multiple, very specific prophecies given to the team in early to mid-game. Prophecies are a tricky plot device that requires finesse so it doesn't turn out cheap. The writers definitely lack the finesse required.What frustrates me the most is the ending, AND the true ending of the game. To access the true ending, one needs a few extra boring hours of tracking a few dozen collectibles that require backtracking and, to my disappointment, it doesn't really add a meaningful layer to the story, just adds extra frustration on top of everything.The game is very polished. No problems at all, at least not ones I noticed. It runs well on both my main PC and potato laptop.This is the aspect where Sea of Stars truly excels. Oh god. The pixel art. The animation. Everything is just beautifully made. I have never seen modern shaders and lighting features put into pixel art so well. During sunset, the light effect would paint the terrain bright, orange hues, and buildings, trees, and rocks cast proper shadows that dynamically move with the sun and moon’s position. There is an insane amount of effort in animation too, especially the bosses where some of them would look progressively more wounded as the battle drags on. The locales and dungeons are varied, each populated by unique monsters. This is the aspect where the game truly shines.There is a similar amount of care put into the soundscape of Sea of Stars. The music is quite varied enough, and they are enjoyable to listen to. The sound effect of spells, enemies, and their various movements and attacks are very well done to accompany their excellent animation.It’s very difficult to judge this game. It is not a straight-up bad game; I know Sabotage truly put everything into this game, and their passion and care show in multiple aspects of the game. It is just playing through this that frustrates me greatly because of the design and narrative choices they managed to put in the game. This is just the perspective of an old grognard though. I can see why the game is hugely popular and glad it achieved this success. What I hope is they use this opportunity to iterate on some of the weaker aspects of the game in future projects.Would I personally recommend buying this game? Not at full price. Not if you think my complaints are valid for you, but at a discount? If you think the critiques don’t bother you much, yes.

_childDocuments_.review: I cant say enough. This game is so incredible. The music is fantastic, the battle is simple and easy to understand but has depth, the art is really amazing with many wow moments so far. The story seems interesting with lots of hidden stuff going on. The dialogue is funny. Really one of the best games I have played in the last 15 years of gaming. _childDocuments_.review: All reviews pretty much will tell you the same thing, which is good, because all that you need to know is that you should get this game. This easily became one of my favorite RPGs, taking inspiration from the good ♥♥♥♥, while also doing its own thing.The presentation is already some of the best I've seen out of a 2D RPG. I like the way Sea of Stars handles its pixel art and lighting than both Octopath Traveler games. You don't get bombarded with effects, and the game is still very colorful. The music makes every single thing in this game 10x better, just because of how good it is. During my first playthrough, I would keep the game running sometimes to keep the music on. I wouldn't want to leave the area I'm in because of how much I love the soundtrack.The relic system, while not the first game to have this type of thing, is great for people who like to adjust how they play on the spot. I think that the game is pretty easy, even with the difficulty raising relics (save for the one you get near the end of the game, which forces you to play near perfectly and save your resources for the right moment).The story, while not as deep as some other RPGs, was still very engaging, with the characters being one of the best parts about the game. The fact that this takes place way before The Messenger, another great game, makes all of the little things you notice even more special.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Graphics and Art (Score: 10/10)The game's pixel art and sprite animation are undeniably stunning, evoking nostalgia for the 8/16-bit era. The attention to detail in the visuals is commendable and adds to the overall charm of the game. The art direction is a clear highlight.Story and Character Development (Score: 6/10)While the game's story has potential, it feels rushed and lacking in depth. A 35-hour playtime isn't enough to fully develop the narrative and characters. More time should have been devoted to fleshing out the story and providing greater context for the characters, especially the area bosses. This lack of development leaves players feeling like something is missing from the experience.World Building and Lore (Score: 7/10)The game introduces unique and interesting enemies, which is a positive aspect. However, they could benefit from more background story and context which would make the world feel more immersive. A deeper exploration of the game's lore could have added more depth to the overall experience.Combat System (Score: 5.5/10)The combat system offers interesting choices, but it tends to become repetitive, even with the lock system in place. The challenge level is also lacking unless players acquire a few specific items. Adding more variety and depth to combat could enhance the overall gameplay experience.Overall Enjoyment (Score: 7.5/10)Despite its shortcomings, the game provides enjoyable and emotional moments, especially for players who have a fondness for JRPGs from the 8/16-bit era. While it may not be a flawless experience, it still offers enough to entertain fans of the genre.Final ThoughtsIn summary, the game excels in its visual presentation and nostalgic appeal. However, it falls short in terms of story development, character depth, and combat variety. With more attention to these areas, it could have been even more of a standout title for fans of classic JRPGs and gamers in general. Unless you are a hardcore fan i would either play it on gamepass or wait for a discount sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend! The real game of the year! Everything is done at the highest level. The graphics are very nice, well done down to the smallest detail. Unique visual style and technical implementation, very cool and pleasing to the eye. The music is just super! Pleasant melodies enhance the atmosphere of each location and game situation. I haven’t felt this much interest in a story for a long time. I won't spoil it, play it and enjoy it. The gameplay is, oddly enough, very diverse, with a lot of interesting and unexpected moments. Lots of humorous moments and references. Many thanks to the authors for the fun hours spent playing the game. I haven't felt such a thrill from a game for a long time.

_childDocuments_.review: The first 10-12 hours are quite boring. Everything feels very trivial and there isn't really any mechanical progression. The story is fine, and you get to like most of the characters at least. I am playing without any of the relics that make the game easier, except for the one that lets you know when you time things correctly. The music is great throughout, and the game is always visually appealing.Around 15 hours the combat actually started to make me think, although I didn't party wipe until much, much later. As new characters join the party, there's actual tactics to do, which is fun. The plot and environment also gets much more to my liking and feels less generic.Thoughts on equipment (spoiler just in case you want some mystery): There's a lot of secrets, but I never really feel compelled to go back and do them except for the achievement and maybe some minor unlockables for... more achievements I guess.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game fails in everything but aesthetics. I don't often come across games that I would consider juvenile but this is one of them. This year I've been graced with playing a lot of wonderful games among those was Chained Echoes. A somewhat flawed but largely brilliant approach on the JRPG method that had depth in story and in combat. It also boasted similar aesthetics to this game (and used all of these things better). Now Sea of Stars both fails to be enjoyable or inspired. The naming conventions used in this game are dreadful. 'The Fleshmancer' 'The Dweller of Woe' 'The Necromancer', 'The Solstice Warriors'. The names chosen are SO painfully generic, especially in a fantasy setting. It's like they didn't hire a writer and just decided that generic enemy names would work great as titles in a long form RPG. Characters are flat and perhaps that's even being too kind. Neither of the Solstice Warriors boast any form of meaningful growth or attitude, their responses to virtually every situation are trite and predictable. Garl while initially lovable quickly becomes tiresome. NPC's and side characters are past the point of being uninteresting and well into the real of actively abrasive (Looking and you, Yolande and crew. Yes I hate you).The combat is bumbling in the extreme. A handful of well thought out mechanics are hamstrung by overtaxed action economy, which leaves the player with a handful of potential moves but the answer you need is almost always just attack. Enemy breaks in most cases are either outright impossible or a mad rush with how quick action counters run down. I wish I had enough words to detail all the ways the combat kept running into itself.Just go play Chained Echoes instead, its better in all regards.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A solid 5.5 game.Combat is the same an hour in as it is at the end of the game. 3 skills per person with 2 or in some cases 1 being useful per character is inexcusable.Story is bland, characters are hollow and provide 0 personal growth. No conflict between members with different ideologies, and the 2 main characters are just gender swapped identicals. The music outside of the Mitsuda tracks are annoying at worst and average at best.If you're looking to get your nostalgia RPG fill, go play Chained Echoes.

_childDocuments_.review: Really a throw-back to the Super NES golden age of JRPGs. Battle system is very simple and adds an element of interaction that will keep most people involved in each encounter. There's a ton to do if you are looking to complete the true ending and the story is very rewarding (beware the mid-game SUPER sad moment). Not much replay after you get the true ending, but nonetheless a good 40 hours for a game that pays homage to an era of games that probably is the reason many of us are JRPG fans nowadays.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this one - and it's not a *bad* game strictly speaking, it's just... shallow. The art direction is wonderful, I love how colorful and rich the world is, and there were some hints at story elements that intrigued me (like the Vespertine story). Sadly, that's it.While playing the tutorial, I thought the combat system was promising, because each special ability has its own quicktime minigame you play in order to increase damage / hit multiple enemies / multiple times / etc; also, every time an enemy is hitting you, if you click at the right moment you will negate some damage. I thought they could do a lot of interesting stuff with this, but apparently they didn't. I didn't see any increase in depth after the tutorial (and i'm playing with the highest difficulty settings that are available to me): after 3 bosses (and some 8 hours I think - I played offline with my Steam Deck so not all of them are being counted) my characters still have the same skills they had in the tutorial. There are no status ailments, and every enemy, bosses included, just makes attacks that are either damage on a single target or damage on multiple targets or healing, and that's it. I have never had to think of a new strategy with different enemies, I just try to eliminate them in the most efficient way given which random icon combination they have upon them (if you manage to hit them with attacks of the icons' kind, you stagger them and they can't perform their strong attack).The main characters seem to lack personality, some kind of struggle, narrative arc, anything.Puzzles are quite linear at the moment, not particularly exciting.If you just want some easy and lighthearted story with intriguing bits lore-wise but no character depth, and you don't want a challenging and deep system, then you might like this. Otherwise, I suggest Chained Echoes over this, they are trying to cover the same niche but Chained Echoes is on an entirely different tier.What a wasted occasion :( (and I loved their other game, The Messenger).
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid turn based game. It is more simplistic compared to chained echoes. The level up system here is pretty alright, I initially thought we could hyper focus on a stat, but its mostly just to set which stat you want earlier. Skills are kinda limited, not much strategy at play here just mostly timing what skills you use. Skills and attacks require to time it right similar to Super Mario RPGS or Virgo Versus the Zodiac. It does it well, but only at the end I realized you could also time attacks like:  crescent moon, abberage, etc. They should have put a notice for it.The story was pretty simple, have some parts where I questioned some of the character's decision at the end. I won't delve too much, but it was still very enjoyable. I enjoyed how much the main duo was able to grow stronger and the relationship between the mage and fleshmancer.I also really hated having to pick up 60 conches. At least have them be trackable through the minimap.Overall, it is still a very good turn based game still would reach to my top 20s for turn based games. I was really expecting to be able to build my characters in any way i wanted. Maybe something similar to virgo vs zodiac. The pixel art was legit really good, I loved the design on places. 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: I'll change my review if this changes, but so far, this might be my personal game of the year.  That's mostly because I really adore this vibe.  It's really just addicting to play.  Exploring feels good.  Combat feels good.  The characters are lovable (so far (only 5 hours in)).  I'm invested. _childDocuments_.review: this game is GOOD but i gotta say, i've got some complaints. namely, relics. they're a confusing implementation of accessibility/difficulty settings that feel messy and not very thought out. i don't use many of the relics that make the game easier, but as someone who uses all the relics that make the game harder: it doesn't feel good to have to spend gold for the purpose of making the game harder with no additional benefits - aside from an achievement for using one of the more gimmicky relics.also, forgot to mention, the game is piss easy. if you do not stack on every difficulty modifier the game allows you to, i do not imagine anyone would die in this game. and if you do die? you get all of your health and mp refilled. this turns every first attempt at a fight into a "test run" as, unless you saw the fight coming, it will be your only attempt where you do not have full health/mp to start. in a game with a hundred modifiers that make the game easier and like 5 that make the game harder, i really really wish the base difficulty of the game was higher. overall, i'm still really enjoying this game. but these two things just make the game feel cheaper than it needs to be.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm doing an immediate review right after i finished this game to give my thoughts.This game does so many things so right and it will be the perfect game for you if you do it right.And yet i don't know if i can recommend it or not, there is sadly no inbetween option.Pros:- Characters are fleshed out and have or will have motivation down the line- Combat is awesome fluid and rewards patience and reflexes- Worldbuilding is fantasticly vibrant and creative without breaking boundaries- Music is composed beautifully- Fishing- Minigame is addictive (although 1 combo of figurines is broken beyond belief)Cons:- Sometimes in combat abilites with timed button presses leave the screen which makes it very hard to hit them- Music variety is not big enough (but that might be more of a budget thing)- Combat could be a tiny bit harder or at least a relic that allows for a harder fight- And last but not least ... THE ENDING IS ABSOLUTE GIGA ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ... no payoff, no satisfactory final fight, no lesson learned, no (proper) reconsiliation, 1 Character is just gone from the ending (no buts, where is he?), and not only that they make a mockery of it even more by adding a bullet hell at the end, seriously?! bullet hell in addition to a unsatisfactory ending?btw alternate ending is still not good ... better but not good.All i can say is, play about 36-40 Hours until the final confrontation, with some sidemissions and secret bosses and make the ending up for yourselves.Hope this helps.Cya

_childDocuments_.review: I can say for absolute certain that this is the best game I've played this year. Hands down on of the best RPG games I've played in a long time. The story is fantastic with a bunch of great turns and twists and it is fairly easy to follow. The combat is a bit basic but I enjoyed it that way. It wasn't hard to understand and fairly engaging and made me think for some boss fights. Nothing blocks you from getting 100% the further you progress which is fantastic. Also the game rewards you greatly when you do optional stuff which I appreciate.Also, I strongly encourage everyone to at least activate those mysterious pillars that show up when you beat the game. The best thing ever is waiting to you and it is so worth the grind.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this review by saying this game is very much meant to be a nostalgia bomb. I don't believe it's enough like any previous RPG to nail one specific game next to its name. Lots of people comparing to Chrono Trigger but I found it's more like Breath of Fire 3 and Mario RPG mixed together. Maybe the combos? Maybe the art? It's definitely not Chrono Trigger. Don't fall for nostalgic poison and over enthusiastic lovers of the genre. I wouldn't recommend it at it's current price or current build (if the devs ever patch things based on what's written below).Next I will say at about the playtime of this review, you will either love this game or hate it. The first two hours will be wasted with a tutorial and reading a lot of dialogue. About 10 hours in you will realize the story isn't immersive enough or maybe interesting enough OR the combat is tedious and unbalanced. I fell to the combat and didn't really care for the writing to effect me one way or another. The story is there... just not doing much.Let's talk about the combat. The devs will lie to you about needing to use the interactive combat system effectively. It is do it or suffer a long drawn out battle. I'm not talking about the more fun and interesting bosses you will face, I'm simply talking about the various minions you'll fight getting there. The devs took no liberty on balancing fight to fight and put the limitations based on the "Relics" you can find in the game. Most relics will make the game easier or accessible which actually works against it. There doesn't seem to be reason for most of them from what I could tell. Most could have been eliminated through better balancing, better visual feedback and queues, and a less tedious combat system mashing A. I would suggest turning some of them on but I'm not sure if it would be enough for some or too much for many. One relic even takes control over the visual feedback that this kind of combat system absolutely needs. Some odd development choices in my opinion.Without relics, enemies will have too much health and may cause you to be stuck in infinite combat. Healing is almost too dangerous to do fighting regular enemies as you can lose that health the very next enemy turn. Breaking all spells during combat is impossible at times. You do not have any of these problems during the boss fights however. Very weird to have to struggle getting to the boss and having to use campfires so much to help replenish HP and MP.The game isn't all bad. The music, art, and even the idea of the story is great. The dialogue definitely needs work but I didn't find it any more bloated than other games of today. Puzzles are pretty simple and the overall world is charming. Sadly, it's just plagued by some heavy distractions and tedious combat. I'd buy this game on discount for sure but the current price seems a bit inflated for what has been delivered. I give it an overall score of 7.5/10 for what I played. Don't know if I will return to finish sadly.

_childDocuments_.review: This game blew me away.  It's charming as hell, has a captivating story, and a simple, yet very engaging combat system.  It hits some of the best notes of great old school RPGs like Chrono Trigger, but cleaned up with the comforts of modern game design.  It is unbelievable to me how many aspects of this game Sabotage nailed.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I was really looking forward to this game but it ultimately left me disappointed. Everything here feels really well polished, looks and sounds amazing, but the story and dialogue fall flat very hard for me. It's enough to put me off and as of now, I don't know if I want to play it through. Story is very important, especially for these kind of games, and it happens to be the lowest quality of the game. Some say it gets better around the 20 hour mark, but I don't know if I have it in me to push through. It feels like the targeted audience is for children, and if you are one then perhaps it will be an enjoyable experience for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an amazing game.  The throwback (tag) is spot on, it feels like the past.  When games fealt good.However, even a game nigh close to perfect has its faults.Combat becomes fairly repetative, with few real choices (do you take damage or knock out the puzzle).The story, while fairly good, is entirely focused on... (I'd have to say a side character).  Beyond that I've read multiple theories and 'plot holes' type content, but I feel overall the narative is solid.The soundtrack is second to none.  There are at least a half dozen tracks here I just loop sometimes, because of their (amazingness) (so much so that I bought the ost for them cause I was outta my mind in bliss).Afterthought, looking back, it isn't a game where you find.... power.  You aren't gonna find a hugely noice weapon or armor thatll last until forever, its standard.... a - b - c.  Coupled with the.... (I'm severely tempted to call it a puzzle combat) system, Gear takes a severe backseat.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a charming turn based RPG with a lot of heart, beautiful spritework and homages to the 16-bit era, but I don't think it reaches the greatness of its contemporaries. Its plot and characters are pretty basic, the combat suffers from repetition due to the limited amount of skills available for each party member and there were some pretty notable pacing issues halfway through that bogged the experience down. I also have no idea how there doesn't seem to be an active escape command from battles? An oddity given how most of the game is a breeze otherwise, Fear and Hunger with all its intended unfairness still allows the player to attempt avoiding battles.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Just to clarify, Sea of Stars is by no means a bad game, it is in fact very well made and the love that the developers have poured into making it is admirable. That being said, I cannot recommend this game. This is a very linear adventure with little to no customization, leveling is set at a pace that you cannot get overpowered if you wanted to, combat is way too simple for it to be engaging in the long run, characters are bland and one-dimensional. The story switches up here and there with twists but because the characters are so uninteresting, I ended up just not caring at all. This is all such a shame because the graphics, presentation, and music are all excellent.In conclusion, if you are looking for a casual experience that pays homage to classic JRPGs then by all means, this game is for you. If you want an RPG with likable characters, an engaging story, interesting combat mechanics and customization, look elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a love letter to classic RPGs.Nice visuals combined with great soundtrack and creative combat system that will teleport you back to the golden era of RPGs.In the first hours of gameplay, you will see inspirtation from many classics like Super Mario RPG, Golden Sun and Chrono Trigger to name a few.If you enjoyed SNES titles of the genre this game will blow your mind.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've been looking for an old school 90's RPG that give strong Chrono Trigger vibes with a little extra humor this is the game. Chrono Trigger is probably still my favorite game of all time but Sea of Stars tops it several areas. The combat is way more refined and interesting, they added small puzzles to the game whiich mix up the pacing nicely. Honestly this game is so good I'd recommend it to people who don't normally play RPG's.

_childDocuments_.review: Just... Ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh. Pure RPG comfort food, playing this game is so refreshing. It's complete, it's fun, the story is passable even if not exceptional, and everything just ticks all of the boxes that I've been yearning for.The Gameplay is sublime, the timings felt good, even map traversal felt good with the grappling hook. The characters are fun, even if not exceptional, there were concepts that I found to be exceedingly interesting, the way that the story is told in the part of the game is interesting too, with that man telling the story as though it were history. The art, I wish I had more words synonymous with magnificent in my vocabulary because the pixel art in this game is so freaking gorgeous. I would die happy if every single game I played was done in this style with this quality, everything is so smooth and charming.The music. It starts out with the classic retro style, but as the game goes on it steadily sheds that styling and moves towards being its own thing, and I loved the entire thing. I hum the songs at times and I'm unashamed.If you have any love for RPGs, old or new, play this game, it's so fun.

The story may be what one would expect from a RPG, but the characters are well developed and I didn't mind the RPG clichés, which are even pointed out by characters .The game doesn't overstay its welcome, no "arc" or "chapter" dragged on for too long. _childDocuments_.review: Oh boy, where to start.I really REALLY wanted to like this game. After Octopath 2 I've been dying for a good JRPG, and this one... this one isn't it.The story is made for children... and I mean, it's really soft. From consequences of messing up to fighting a boss, telling him, hey, u do you, and then him turing his whole life around, it's just so bland. There's no consequences for any action. The story feels like it was written for one of those little kid shows, it's really bad.Then the combat is just odd. At first, it feels good, but level ups and upgrades are extremely underwhelming. Say u have an armor of 10 and u get an upgrade that puts it at 36. Enemies that where dealing before 19 damage are now dealing... 17? Why? I upgraded my armor by 26 points and that took off 2 point of damage?? In level ups, u get 3 points (six if u bonus upgrade) so if 26 takes away 2 points, 6 is useless. This is the same with attack moves, where the timing is just stupidly forgiving (very easy) and the spells are incredibly easy to pull off.Overall, the game is just easy and bland. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing character designs and gorgeous environments. This alone is worth the game price. Perfect.  This story went from a nicely written, somewhat simple, RPG about solstice siblings coming of age, to what seemed to be a random word generator creating a story. The story just gets wildly out of control and seems to have no real purpose or goal. It felt so grounded at the start and then it just shot off into outer space.  The gameplay is good, but I feel like it could have done so much more with the mechanics that it grabbed from the other games I mentioned above. There should be a penalty for continually pressing the timed block button before it actually works. I found that if I just spam it I block about 80% of the incoming hits and it was actually easier to time with a multi-hit enemy attacks. I think something like this would have been a better idea:Pressing the block button early once: -20% effectiveness against successful timed blockPressing the block button early twice: -40% effectiveness against successful timed blockPressing the block button early three times: -50% effectiveness against successful timed blockThis would have advanced the mechanic a bit more and brought it into current times more than just simply using the same mechanic from the old Super Mario RPG days.UPDATE: There's been a new 'Combat 2.0' update, so I am hoping they have fixed the things I'm complaining about here. Some of the "exploration" feels a bit tedious and without purpose. Just running down a corridor and vaulting up and down ledges. It isn't hard and it doesn't add anything to the gameplay and/or story. I love the environments, but it just takes time and doesn't actually involve anything challenging. Something else that bothered me was that there are so many opportunities to click on parts of the environment for some juicy lore or information and most of the time it just says the same thing for different objects:"This place hasn't been cleaned in a while.""This place hasn't been cleaned in a while.""This place hasn't been cleaned in a while."There is seriously nothing else to write about this awesome  area?A beautiful RPG that I am glad that I played, but I will never play again.---

_childDocuments_.review: It is a game about powerful people being nothing without the great friends/family supporting them.Whatever you may think about this game, at least it’s better than the other “star” game that released in the same week as this one!!This game did exactly what I hoped for; it made me feel a little bit like I did when I was 7 and playing Chrono Trigger or FFVI or Illusion of Gaia. Just... warm again.In 1998, aged seven, I played Chrono Trigger for the first time. I couldn't play well yet because I was too young and didn't understand English but the experience left an impression on me: the Millennial Fair games, the fight against the robot Gato (this is my kindest memory), the dramatic problem involving Lucca's teleportation machine, the battle system and beautiful graphics. That style of game became a passion, and then I learned it had a name: "RPG". Around the same time, l also discovered Super Mario RPG at a local videogame store, and that was another game which really marked my childhood.Sea of Stars comes as a great celebration of this style that marked an era and consecrated itself as immortal. It's great to see that there is a community that still appreciates it and that there are talented people drawing inspiration from it and developing new games. Da Vinci is to Renaissance art what Square is to RPG, and Sabotage Studio proves itself as a virtuous new team following the steps of the Masters.Sea of Stars is a look back at the world as it used to be in the ancient past, when the world was a brighter place. The theme is hope for a better future. In terms of the world, it is not trying to be Chrono Trigger. Gameplay-wise yes in a lot of ways.Sea of Stars is AMAZING - but it's also not trying to be some grand epic. The story is simple by design and it leaves room for the game to be a more light hearted adventure. There are a few "stakes are high" moments, with a couple of major plot twists and consequences, but even those are handled in a way that allows for more charm than chaos. I will say though that it is not conveyed in grandiose storytelling.  Most dialogue is brief and the plot points come quickly.  This isn't to say that it is bad, but I think people are confusing brevity for lack of depth. The game has plenty of depth, but it is also simple in how it presents it. If you look back at the SNES, there were grand epic stories like Chrono Trigger and FFVI, but there were other excellent games with a much more basic story that focused more on adventure like Secret of Mana and Mario RPG. SoS is the latter, for better or worse, and if you are okay with that, you'll love it.I actually think the story becomes quite enjoyable the further you advance into the game, and if you have the patience to do the true ending, it’s amazing! The problem with the narrative is that the stakes take a little time to build up, so there's not much going on for the first half of the game. Halfway through, the stakes rise dramatically and everything becomes a poignant moment, and the story does its best to keep you off balance and always guessing what will happen next. It's a really beautiful game. The game rewards you for patience and sticking around, if you can make it through the subpar first half. It does what it set out to do. And for me at least, it dredged up those fleeting and distant memories of the warm places of childhood.This is one of the most beautiful looking games I've seen in a long time. Personally, I will take art direction and design over graphical powerhouses any day. The music alone makes this game amazing, but then you add in the visuals, the characters, the gameplay and the simple but charming story and it is one heck of an experience. The little touch's are what grabbed me, the wind blowing with the sprite art gently wafting in the wind, the shadow work, the water splash. The dungeon exploration is also really amazing, it reminded me of old school RPG’s like Wild arms 1 and Breath of Fire 3.I know that I talked about the music already, but seriously it legit made me emotional. Garl is a delightful character and his relationship with Valere and Zale is so wholesome. One of the best parts about Sea Of Stars is that while Valere and Zale are clearly the chosen ones - being enormously talented at magic - Garl is the hero. The normal dude who fights with a freaking pot lid as a weapon. Just like where Samwise was the true hero that got sh*t done and Frodo just carried a ring around and whined about it.While it does have an issue or two (our leads are kind of uninteresting at times, for example) it is quite fun to spin the JRPG formula and have the everyman hero be the one who joins in later on, with you seeing the perspective of the slightly more plot relevant characters who would typically be thrown in much later into the story to convey that stakes are real now. I think it's a nice way to both have the conventional genre tropes we're all used to and would maybe actually miss if they were gone, without having it be so paint by numbers that the game eliminates its worth by being 100 things you've already seen beforeIt has flaws and isn’t a 10/10 game, but they did a great job of making a game that would feel at home on the SNES. It does what it was made to do. Which is be a mostly lighthearted mostly simple story with fun characters and a colorful, fun world. It’s beautiful for sure, the music is good and battles always felt interesting. Ultimately if you go into it knowing that it’s a souped up SNES game then you get what you want. If you come in looking for some AAA story that’s like Red Dead level stuff you’ll not get it and maybe that’s off-putting. To me it was more than worth it. I highly recommend it.8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could return this game. The three most important things for me in an rpg are:1. Combat2. Story3. ExplorationI can accept simple combat or a generic story or a boring world if one of the three is at least pretty good. While I do think Sea of Stars manages a fairly unique take on all of these I can't say that it does any of them really all that well. So let's get into it then.Combat: my initial impressions were that the combat systems would offer me some amount of tactical freedom to the decisions I make and how I play. However it very quickly just became a checklist of doing certain things in the order that makes the most sense and it is both disengaging and feels as though most of the agency I've been granted isn't necessarily taken away but doesn't exactly matter at all. Boss fights have mostly been uninteresting and have on more than one occasion proven easier, if longer, than regular combat in the areas leading up to them.Story: I am only about halfway through the game as of this review so I cannot comment on the story as a whole. However right now the story (with specific regard to the writing/direction) is the thing making me least interested in actually trying to finish this game. At best it's uninteresting. I just don't find myself invested in it. The twists and turns have so far been predictable. I do like the way that symbolism and archetypal characters are represented within the world and I appreciate the worldbuilding. However the reason I'm absolutely turned off by this game right now is in the first moment that captivated me, that felt dramatic and that gave me some sort of catharthis I got "[insert funny internet joke]" and as of right now that's all that I will be able to take away from this game.Exploration: I like the pseudo platforming mechanics and the fact that most areas aren't totally on rails and have things to discover. Unfortunately however, it still feels pretty stiff. Also something I find inconvenient is that most encounters seem to be unavoidable which kinda sucks when the enemies are visible in the overworld since typically rpgs with on-screen enemies give you that option. At least the encounters are not typically grouped close together so you have a small respite if you need a break or just to heal up a bit. Speaking of needing a break thank god I'm playing this on steam deck because while save points are given to us pretty generously there's no quicksave option for when I have to stop or when I'm just feeling drained and need to go do something else. I am aware there's an autosave feature but I can't check if it's autosaved recently and refuse to risk any of my progress to chance it.Which actually does lead me to the things I like: it runs well on the steam deck, the game really is beautiful, the tavern minigame is fun, the dialogue doesn't feel stilted or unnatural, and despite all my negative comments I have still felt engaged enough to play through a fair amount of it until an unfortunately misplaced joke soured me on it when I felt like it was gaining momentum.In summation (tl;dr), this game both takes cues from its predecessors and treads new ground but a few missteps make it a truly mixed bag. Not exactly disappointing but not great either.I'm a person who usually struggles to finish games and I told myself I would commit to finishing this. Unfortunately right now I have no interest anymore but I would like to mean the things I say so if I do finish this game I will come back and edit this to reflect my thoughts about it then.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: Got the true ending. Cribbing so much from other JRPGs, it does get significantly better later on. I wrote the below right before the game popped off. That said, I do think it's still more or less true, but as the game goes on, you get a lot more boss fights and they're really cool. Meduso is basically what I described below of a battle that's just the Lock mechanic used ad infinitum. It has this neat effect of "If you don't solve this puzzle, you will take a ton of damage and die. If you do solve it, you will be granted a stream of combo points and ultimate abilities which you will need to solve this next puzzle, and on and on". Those fights where you're just chaining from one combo into the next are where the game really shines, and they're basically the entire back half.Original at 10hr:Gonna be upfront and say that this style of game is catnip for me. I do really like it, but as I'm playing it, I often feel like I like it more because of the technical aspects than any "fun" I'm getting out of it. There are RPGS with better combat, better pixel art, better music, better writing, etc. This game has never seen a swing it didn't want to take though, and that means you get music where you're often like "meh", and then you fight the first boss and the song Encounter Elite doesn't leave your head for 2 days. Literally hearing the hook while I'm typing this. The combat is similarly a mixed bag. Most turns are boring and strategically shallow which is pretty bad for a game like this, but I like the Locks. They force you to switch into this mode like, "OK, this character will do this which will set up this character to do this, which will give me a combo, which will break the Lock". But the combat isn't defined by that and it's weaker for it (in fact, if you get good enough with the "repeat" abilities, you can safely skip any strategy. I've been told this changes as the game goes on, but like I'm 10 hours in).The lore and aesthetic are spectacular. There's no qualifier there, it's just very good and cultivates this idea that you're in a world fundamentally shaped by magic and that you are a legend in a world of legends. My fic brain spun up so fast and hard, which is honestly a good enough reason in itself to play a game.So, ya. There's a bunch of cool ideas in here. There's also a lot of cruft. I'm enjoying the things I'm taking out of it more than the game itself. If that's something you think you'd like, you'll have a great time. If not, wait for the sequel 'cause I betcha it'll be incredible.*Also, some of the stuff is Canadian references I don't get. Which isn't a complaint; it's not in the way or anything. More like if you're Canadian that's another potential positive for you.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is obviously incredibly pretty. The polish is also incredible.But the substance is lacking. The characters are one-note at best, non-characters at worst. The story has potential, but can never actually execute an interesting and unique perspective on any of its ideas and themes. This game succeeded at being aesthetically amazing. It feels great to play. But once you get past that, there's not much there. And in a game with so much story, so much emphasis on characters, and so many puzzles: for those to be anemic is not great.As a first foray into the jrpg genre, this is a absolutely incredible effort. I hope this team continues to make games in this genre. However, there must be more creativity.

_childDocuments_.review: Review changed after playing more. There was no feeling of progression in this game at all besides the minor stat choices on level up. The lack of variety of skills and gear put a hamper on my enjoyment, especially when battles end up being sloggy at many points. Then there is just how on-rails the game is. Its modeled after Chrono Trigger, in which they do a great job of providing the illusion of non-linearity by giving the player different locations they can visit. While they may not be able to advance in each section because they arent in the story yet, you can sometimes find an item or two early, or something.There wasnt even an attempt to hide the linearity of this game. When combined with the lack of character progression, it just made me put the game down. I loved the first couple hours, but then as I kept waiting for the "real game" to start, I realized I was already in it.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good game that has very few ideas that haven't been done before, but does none of them poorly. You will either be fondly reminded of things you like, or feel like its derivative of better titles. Gameplay is very good but has a couple of minor annoyances where some moves feel frustrating to time.Music is never distracting but a good chunk of it is forgettable ("stars align on the assembly line" goes super hard though)Story is solid but annoyingly requires knowledge of the dev's previous game to fully follow and lacks a lot of depth in the main characters.Visuals are basically the only thing I have no grievances with. This game is pretty as hell.Easy recommend, but I can understand why people have issues with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game and I really tried hard to like it. I have played RPG's like ff1-3, golden sun, and "I am setsuna". The last title in that list is what I was comparing Sea of Stars to.Music: Firstly, the music in Sea of Stars is just not good. It's incredibly repetitive and it does something in my brain that makes me want to toss a table. I think it's the key signature or maybe the timing? Hard to explain, but hopefully the visual helps.Pace: Agonizingly slow. BuT RpG's HaVe PuRpOsElY sLoW pAcE yOu JuSt HaVe tO gIvE iT tImE. No, it was already painful enough listening to the music that it made the dialogue more distracting and I ended up skipping through a lot of dialogue.Saving: Alright, I get it. The developers really wanted to engage with its consumers to have an authentic and original RPG experience. This means that customers are going to have to search for a floating book on a pedestal in order to save their game. Auto save has become such a commonplace and expected thing that I absolutely overlooked this and shut off the game before arriving to a save point. This then provided me with the wonderful experience of painfully starting the game again. This included going through the monologue of the archivist which is an unskippable cut scene.Unskippable monster fights: Unskippable monster fights. You cannot flee. Annoying feature. Art Style: One of the things that got me really excited about this game was the art style. There's absolutely no doubt that the artistic style of this game is beautiful. It is. For the select few places that I visited early in the game, the landscape, artwork, character cut scenes, town, and archivist were all beautiful. That being said, all aforementioned overshadowed this gorgeous looking game. I am pleased that others are finding the game to be enjoyable and I wish them all the best in their journey. Perhaps my taste will change in the future but as of the time of writing, it just simply was not the right game for me. In the end, I received a refund for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is now my new favorite video game.There are so many things to love about this game. I absolutely love the personalities and art styles of the characters, as well as the design of the levels and bosses. The story, while a little confusing at times, is extremely captivating and all falls into place in its own time. Discovering the new parts of the map and unlocking different abilities and powers kept the game interesting and it never felt "grindy" at any point, especially since the level ups always felt to happen at just the right times. Even the mini games like wheels, fishing, and going around finding all the extras to complete the achievements was still a good time and didn't feel too tedious. This game made me feel genuine emotions of all kinds, whether it be happy, sad, suspense, excitement and everything in between and that's what I loved the most about it. All in all an absolutely wonderful experience that I highly recommend to anyone. 10/10 about to go play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A charming retro-rpg that replicates the feeling of playing a 90's JRPG so perfectly,  I found myself hoping for a snow day so I could stay inside and beat it. The story is simple but pleasingly wholesome, the combat is engaging without being punishing, and the music and art direction are compelling every step of the way. A refreshing interlude between heavier games like Baldurs Gate 3 and Starfield.If you're looking for a fun RPG without a complicated narrative or hours of grinding I wholeheartedly recommend Sea of Stars.

Not gonna talk about the story other than "It's good" I recommend playing The Messenger first only cause there's some callbacks to it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun. I haven't played many jrpgs before, but this has opened me up to the genre. The story, art, music, and gameplay consistently show how much effort and passion was put into this game. I did not expect to care about the story as much as I did, and the game achieved this through clever and funny dialogue and generally good writing overall. As far as gameplay is concerned, what initially drew me to want to play this game is the interactive timed button presses in combat that increase your damage dealt and decrease damage taken. The combat and movement are repetitive but never boring due to the diversity of enemies and attacks, as well as your ever-increasing move pool for your own party. In an attempt to not make this review a whole novel, I'll just say that if you even think you might like this game, pick it up and play it. This has been one of the best games I've played recently, and you owe it to yourself to have fun with this one.

_childDocuments_.review: So... How can I describe this game, so that you can understand.. _childDocuments_.review: Visuals? Top notch. The lighting in particular is where it's at. Never seen the 16 bit style graphics look so wonderful before.Music? Oh mannn. Sooooooo good. About 10 tracks stand out to me and I will ALWAYS love listening to them.Game play? Very good. And I say this as someone who hates turn based rpg game play but they did this really well. 4 things to master. Button timing, the lock system, the magic system, the combo system. Learn all 4 and it becomes clear that this is a very balanced way to approach combat. Mindlessly spamming your best attacks will get you killed in this game. Sorry guys but thinking is very important with this one lol. The other part of the gameplay is puzzle solving and platforming which is my fav part of the game play. There's also some side stuff like a silly board game and fishing which is a nice touch to spend a few hours on : )Story? It's really good. My fav part of the game honestly. It starts off pretty by the numbers... But make no mistake. They are setting you up for a emotional rollercoaster once the fleshmancer villain character finally makes a appearance. And yes, he's a horrible monster person. A very sick character. A true villain. And a certain character who you would not think would be so important, turns out to be the most lovable character there is. It's not a story about super heros rising up to stop a villain. That's too simple. It's about the super heros friends. How they can matter just as much if not more than the main heros of this story. And that's just a wonderful message for anyone. Have you ever felt like you were not good enough? That you wish you could do more but can't for whatever reason? This game says that YOU CAN be good enough : )I got next to nothing to say about this game that's negative. If you want the true ending you gotta find all these 60 hidden items throughout the game world and they can be a pain in the azzz to find. That was kind of dumb fetch questy stuff and the creators clearly wanted you to go back and see all the wonderful world that they created so that's fair. Still a chore though so I thought that part of the game was a lil lame. Luckily I play on pc and used we mod to cheat that part of the game haha. So I guess this part of the game isn't a issue for me haha.No game is perfect so you wont see me drop a 10 out of 10. But it's a high af 9 that's for sure!One thing I'm effing tired of seeing though is people hating the two mains being bland. Bro... That's on purpose! The mains being fairly blank slates is so you can easily imprint yourself onto them. That way whenever emotional story parts happen, it feels like it's happening to you. YOU! The human playing the game! You're the one losing friends in battle. You're the one becoming depressed and sad that you got screwed over! The story telling hits harder this way. Halo, half life, gta3 etc etc. This is by design so you get sucked into the character and BECOME the character. These fools will praise chrono trigger but hate this game which makes NO SENSE. I think some a holes just like to be elitist and act like any games from the past are the best, and new games all suck. Which is mostly true but not in this case haha. Just wish those idiots would get the obvious point here...

_childDocuments_.review: I only review games that really wow me.I kickstarted this back in 2020 and have been eagerly awaiting it ever since I heard Yasunori Mitsuda was going to be on the soundtrack.  Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy III, and Super Mario RPG were some of my absolute favorite games as a kid, and this game is a beautiful love letter to all of them.The characters are likable and cute, the story is engaging and keeps coaxing you forward through the game.  The pacing is wonderful.  I've never felt overwhelmed, rushed, bored, or let down by anything - its all been very comfortable and enjoyable.I'm about 60% of the way through the game if the chapter guides in the online walkthroughs I've peaked at are any indication, and honestly I'm pretty sad that I'm already that far through the game.  Makes me want to slow down and really savor it.The game also introduces a game-within-the-game called "Wheel."  I absolutely love it.  I'll be doing all of the championship matches before I'm done playing, for sure.  If you're a fan of all the JRPG mini games like Blizball, Gwent, Triple Triad, and whatever other wacky games developers have shoved into their titles, I definitely wouldn't pass up Wheel.The game has a "difficulty setting" for every kind of player.  The base game with no relics is actually quite challenging, but if you're looking to just experience and enjoy the story -- there are plenty of little switches you can flip to make the game as easy as you'd like it to be.  I have a few turned on, but not all of them.  I want to still feel like I'm battling through the game, but I'm just not interested in having to attempt the same boss 6 times, or backtrack through an area 6 times because I keep dying.  The game allows me to play that way, which is nice.The soundtrack is incredible, particularly the "Trials on the Wind" track, you can find it on YouTube if you'd like to check it out.  I also very much enjoyed the BGM in the water temple area.  I'm excited to hear all the wonderful tracks I have yet to discover.I love the puzzles, I love the little tools you get that offer you additional ways to interact with your surroundings.  I love fishing, I love gathering food, I love cooking, I love all the little systems they've implemented to make the game more interactive and engaging - I have yet to find a system in the game that feels like a chore or a slog.  They all seem very approachable and useful, except for setting up camp.  I haven't really found a part of the game where I was like "Man I should set up camp here instead of just resting at this bonfire - I really am in the mood to go to a whole other screen to accomplish the exact same thing I can do by -not- going to that other screen."  Idk seems weird...  Not sure why the camp system is even in the game to be honest, but maybe some people like it.That's it.  That's really my only complaint.  There's one screen in the game that's pretty much useless - and you never have to interact with it if you don't want to.So I'd say its pretty damn good.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of stars is a visually stunning game developed by the studio behind the messenger. That's about all that wowed me about the game. Not to say that it's bad, the game as a whole is really well made, but it feels lacking in many areas. Starting with gameplay the combat is a very simplistic turn based combat system with very little depth. While you do have active moments when it comes to just timing your attacks or blocks, the lack of variety in moves and ways to customize your play style made it so that battles often boiled down to building up boosts for your attacks, sustaining your characters, and very little else. The lack of move variety also ended up making the moves that were there end up feeling stale after you've seen them for the 20th, 30th, 50th time. There are some parts of the combat system I like such as moonerang and by extension soonerang which are very active moves that reward proficiency, but that is the exception not the norm. Moving on from combat, other aspects of the game play were fairly good. Fishing was the most entertaining part of the game to me and traversal of levels was fun for the most part. The story of the game often times reflects the quality of the systems, it is good but not outstanding. In addition there are issues with pacing with the game starting out very slowly only picking up after about 9 hours in. If you're looking for something with a little more complexity to it's systems I would recommend Octopath Traveller 2. But if you're looking for an indie RPG with a fantastic story I'd recommend Chained Echoes.While this game doesn't excel at what it tries to do, it is a good package overall and I would recommend it if you are interested in it, just don't expect a 10/10 indie masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was pretty much everything I hoped for when I was waiting for it in anticipation last Fall. The music, art, and combat are amazing, with the music and art definitely being up there with some of the best I've experienced in a hot minute with a video game. I think the story is fine, I didn't necessarily love it, but for reviews saying the story is really bad I can't say I agree with that opinion. Additionally, another opinion you might see in a lot of reviews is that the characters don't really have a lot of character or progression. Without getting too much into spoilers I think this opinion might come from either the reviewer not beating the game to completion or not going out of their way to set up camps throughout the game to talk with each character individually. I will say none of the characters are groundbreaking, this game isn't a character study, but I think a few of them are really well fleshed out, while some of the others aren't. Unfortunately, I think media literacy is pretty much non-existent in most people who play video games, and the concept of static characters just doesn't exist in their minds. The two main characters of this game are static characters (just because a character doesn't change from the beginning of the story to the end of the story doesn't mean they aren't a character). This complaint about the two main characters was in pretty much every negative review that I read through for this game, to which I cannot agree. Either way I think this game is an easy 4-4.5/5 for any rpg fan, and a great first jrpg for anyone who has never played one before. I cannot wait to see what Sabotage Studios has in-store for us next.Also, play The Messenger if you haven't already, it'll make your Sea of Stars experience 2x more fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm 10 hours into the game as of writing this review.Do you want the brunt of it? Real honesty? Sea of Stars just isn't it, chief. I played the messenger, which if you are unaware, is an astounding testament to what proper nostalgia / genuine brilliant writing can do for this medium of visual storytelling, and was the first experience I had with Sabotage Studio.If that was the pinnacle of what the Sabotage studio is capable of, then Sea of Stars is the sheer cliffside on that expansive plateau.  If you are looking for a narrative as great as the one in The Messenger, perhaps Chrono Trigger, or anything remotely similar to a gripping storyline, then this isn't going to fulfill your wishes.The characters are one dimensional, there are multiple instances where rooms are just empty without anything to interact with, and the world itself is very linear in nature. I just beat one of the major bosses and due to a design decision that was harmless and genuinely an interesting take for the game's genre for the first 10 hours of the game:  I couldn't tell if I was actually doing anything substantial to the boss at all. It dragged on for that long.If you told me that all of the budget for the game went into the art direction, music, and animation, I'd believe it! All of that is incredible, and should not be understated here in my review. The music and art carry this game heavily since everything else lacks polish.I refuse to believe this was play-tested beyond the first island. It's like someone played The Messenger, said, "I could make a game like that!" and proceeded to NOT do that. Also, was there a writers strike or something? The clever humor has been replaced by genuinely fourth wall breaking muck that doesn't add anything to the player experience and is especially bad characterization for a specific npc you meet relatively early on in your adventure.Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying different is bad. It's an entirely different genre of game, so my expectations are already tempered enough. Though, when the first line of your steam store page directly contradicts itself "Promising the Sabotage touch in every system", I believe it's fair for me to say it was a disappointment.If you want to enjoy this game, go into it without expectations; because ultimately it doesn't fulfill any of them.TL;DR Pretty visuals amazing music, bad story, lackluster exploration; tedious.I doubt my opinion will change much as I play more, but I would be overjoyed to be proven wrong. I want it to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: is a heartfelt tribute to classic JRPGs, blending nostalgic elements with modern updates. It follows two Children of the Solstice, whose unique powers are needed to fight an ancient evil, and their non-magical friend Garl, who brings warmth and a sense of grounded realism to their journey. The game combines strategic combat, exploration, and puzzle-solving, with a notable feature being the ability to shift between day and night, which plays into the game's puzzles and world design in meaningful ways. This mechanic not only adds variety to gameplay but also evokes the same sense of wonder in players as it does in the characters.Though the storyline can feel simple and a bit naïve, with its clear-cut good-versus-evil framework,  excels in creating a captivating world. The lush visuals, smooth mechanics, and an atmospheric soundtrack, including music from  composer , elevate the experience.Whether you're a fan of the genre or new to it,  offers a fresh yet familiar journey that balances classic JRPG appeal with modern sensibilities.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A serviceable, jack-of-all-trades, yet charming, turn-based RPG that suffers from trying to be everything, including a prequel.  The archetypal 7/10.  Worth a try on sale, but not at full price.I'm honestly not sure as I write this whether I'm going to click thumbs-up or thumbs-down at the end, that's how conflicted I am about this game.  Serving as a prequel to Sabotage's prior platformer, The Messenger (which is definitely worth a look if you haven't played it), Sea of Stars serves as the origin story for several elements and characters of The Messenger.And this is the first of its problems.Several times in Sea of Stars, plot-lines are established and then left hanging until the realisation that the resolution is simply "and this is how *this* enemy in The Messenger came to be".  And even that is only if you are able to realise the particular connection which the game relies on you to make itself (and I can't tell if that's a good thing or not).  What should have been a hook for a late-game encounter becomes merely a 'member-berry for what was, at the time, an otherwise throwaway encounter in an entirely different game.  At best, maybe those who play this game before The Messenger may (and I stress *may*) have a marginally more profound experience in some places for having played SoS first, but...really?....The fact that this is a prequel also puts a dent on your attachment to the world, and even the protagonists given the connection to The Messenger.  I'm trying to not spoil here (and I'm sure I'm failing miserably), but I'm hoping that the True Ending of SoS represents a divergence of sorts in the timeline.Putting aside it's status as a prequel, as a standalone RPG it ticks all the boxes, but only in the box-ticking sense:- Turn-based combat? Check!- Special powers that use Mana Points? Check!- Combos and Ultimates that you have to charge up? Check!- Strangely ubiquitous side mini-game? Check!- Equipment upgrades? Check!- Cooking? Check!- Fishing? Check!- 'Save the universe' plot? Check!- Ensemble of characters? Check!It has almost everything you would expect, and it all works, but none of it "Wow!"s.  Each character's skill list is very short, and you'll almost never use many of them.  There are almost as many combo's as there are skills, but in practice you'll use even less of those.  The ultimates are hilariously underpowered and are mostly useful for lock-breaking (much like combos).Equipment upgrades are almost entirely linear stat-sticks, some of the few exceptions are basic QoL upgrades that shouldn't be equippable items at all (I shouldn't have to spend an item slot just to be able to see non-boss HP gauges).  Cooking effects are only restorative, indeed the only status effects in the game are specific boss-mechanics.The characters are often under-developed.  The two main leads are usually empty vessels, never really having any kind of inner struggle regarding the position they find themselves in or the stakes they are facing.  While the rest of the protags are usually more interesting, most of their story hooks are just dropped the second they no longer serve the main plot.  Captain Klee'Shae for example has not one, but two true-identity reveals, and even after finishing the game, I'm still not entirely clear if her crew are even aware of *either*.  Headmaster Moraine's crisis of confidence at the end of Act 1 is one of the better character moments of the game, but he plays essentially no part of the rest of the narrative, and even if you specifically go talk to him, he has no reaction to several key events, as if the devs kinda forgot he existed.  After one particular lore-drop early in Act 3, one member of your party mumbles something about "This changes everything" then ups and leaves nothing but a *literal* empty shell, and has no dialogue for the rest of the game!  And while the concept of B'st is interesting, we don't get enough time to really demonstrate the 'sheer will' concept of his character, instead relying on some limited exposition about the nature of his physical form.So.......lots of problems........and yet.....It's a cohesive enough package that in many respects all the individual criticisms can feel like nitpicks.  In the moment, the game experience is fun enough that I was always interested in seeing what happened next, and moving on to the next challenge.  The Boost and lock-breaking mechanics in combat brought something new to the table.  And I was, ultimately, charmed by the world and am interested to see how the lore that Sabotage have created develops.In many ways, I think this might be a decent game for someone who wants to dip their toe in to story-driven RPGs.  The mechanics are usually well-enough explained, and it contains many of the common tropes of the genre (usually played straight), with enough in-the-moment whimsy to have it's own identity.  I don't think it's a big issue if you play this without first playing The Messenger, although you may find some jokes make no sense.Die-hard RPG fans are likely to see a lot of rough-edges, but depending on your tolerance level for those rough-edges there's a perfectly decent, if uninspiring RPG-experience available for those looking for their next dose of RPG goodness.I initially published this review with a thumbs-up, but after sitting on it for a couple of hours I've decided to change my mind.  Why?  Firstly, the price.  I'd forgotten about it because I was an original Kickstarter Backer (I'm in the credits and everything! :-) ).  There's a significant enough chance you actually won't like this game that $35 feels like too much to spend to find out.Finally, and admittedly this is purely personal, there are some implications to the ending that leave a sour taste in my mouth, in stark contrast to how the game itself plays it as heartwarming.  If it's a happy ending, I want a happy ending, dagnammit.  Don't leave me with existential-dread-by-proxy...
