_childDocuments_.review: Dropping this after 12 hours.The story is bland, bland, bland. The main characters are lifeless husks with no personality who only exist to say whatever lines are needed to progress the shallow plot. The dialogue is also technically flawed, with lots of comma splices or missing commas throughout. I could forgive the lackluster writing if the gameplay was any good, but it isn't. Party members have very few skills, so battles quickly become repetitive due to a lack of options.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, the game offers some exciting retro fun, very much inspired by Chrono Trigger.  Mechanics are simple and straight forward.  Objectives are cleared, and a decent storyline.  My only issue is some of the outdated special effects.  I played through 15 hours, and still haven't gotten any combos or skills that wowed me with effects.  While I understand the nostalgic retro graphics, we are still in 2023.  Certain upgrades are warranted and overdue at this point for any game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I see a lot of comparisons to Chrono Trigger and others, for obvious reasons. Sea of Stars proudly wears its inspiration on its sleeve, like The Messenger before it, but you'd be selling it short to stop there. This game perfectly engaged all of my SNES-era nostalgia without exploiting it. It has an identity all it's own that's intriguing, heartfelt, funny, and, perhaps most importantly... just plain fun to play!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: By far one of the top 10 games I have played in the past 23 years.This game plays homage to all turn based JRPG games that were released on the Super Nintendo and Playstation 1. The game is rewarding, challenging in some areas and FUN. The multiple endings are satisfying unlike alot of games today. This game didn't waste my time at all. Every minute was worth it and I wanted more.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I was very reassured that the playable characters were not the barely speaking monoliths the demo showed. Each and every one of them is a colorful living being (Garl best boy!)The combat mechanics are quite simple. There is no customization whatsoever, but the difficulty manages to be quite balanced. Until the final bosses, too easy. This kinda felt like a let down (like the low level 20-ish at which you arrive to end the adventure). Still, it felt great, intense, diverse.Thanks for your words and world, Shopkeeper, and Sabotage!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:+ Great soundtrack+ Turn-based combat with timed button presses+ Gorgeous backgrounds. Some of the best 2D backgrounds I've ever seen, along with gorgeous spritework.+ Not obnoxiously melodramaticCons:- If you want to collect everything, there's some frustrating backtracking- Limited replay value for now; might change with DLC- The characters aren't compelling for me; they're neither fun enough nor flawed enough to draw me in- Left me with a weird hollow feeling after I finished it, like I had eaten dessert for breakfast or somethingVerdict:Good game. It's not an all-time great, but its presentation is outstanding, and the combat was just fun enough to keep me going until the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not typically a fan of JRPGs, but Sea of Stars introduces a timing element to combat that makes otherwise drawn out encounters feel more interactive. The music, storytelling and ambiance are all incredible -- I found myself actually crying during this game because I had become so emotionally invested in the characters. Without a doubt, this is my game of the year for 2023.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Final Fantasy 7 to the latest, Chrono Cross, All the Tales series games, Breath of Fire series, Xenogears, The Mana series, and probably too many more JRPGs that I can no longer remember...But Sea of Stars definitely has the best story out of all of them, and I highly suggest *SPOILER ALERT* to get the true ending of the game.Sadly, it was a bit to boring in the beginning, it takes too long for an animation to execute after you've decided on an action. I get that it's to cater to newer players of the genre, but damn, I fell asleep on the first few levels of the game. I wish it had the same game-feel and quickness such as modern JRPGs like Yakuza: LIke A Dragon, or even DragonQuest.But not even that could hinder the poured effort on game level, world-building, lore, and story.There's a goddmaned reason why this game is 2023 Indie Game of the Year. And boy does it deserve it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game was great. Very good pixel art. Story starts a bit dull, but it picks up quickly and then its non stop insane stuff going on. Dont listen to the reviews saying the true ending is not worth it. The true ending was WAYYY better than the standard ending, a much more difficult end boss fight, and the story bits before and after were much more satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: For starters, yes this is a decent game. I can see why it won Indie Game of The Year and its certainly a game thats worth playing, but I wouldnt suggest it to someone at full price. While I had an ok time with the game there are some pretty fatal flaws I have with the game that stop me from giving it a thumbs up.Overall, I can see why it gets a large amount of praise. The game is reasonably short, looks fantastic and is easy enough for a majority to complete if they actively try (although less than 30% have completed the base game per steam achievements). Its certainly not a terrible game by any stretch, especially when you consider all the shovelware RPGMaker games that flood Steam weekly. However, given the issues I have with the games core experience (story, progression, and difficulty) I cant in good faith give it a positive review. My verdict is this, if you like JRPG's, pick this up at a discount. It doesnt even need to be a massive discount, 30-40% or more and I think its worth a shot. Full price however for  me is a no go.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this game for people that enjoyed Secret of Mana/Evermore, and Chrono Trigger. There's even a strong reference to CT in the game that I loved. Combat is roughly turn-based, but slightly in the fashion of FFX where you can get an idea of who's going next enemy-wise and can switch to other party members if they haven't attacked yet.I'm only 7 hours in, just left Lucent. But I'm enjoying the story so far, kinda getting vibes hinting at betrayal but nothing concrete and I refuse to look it up and ruin the story.I would prefer faster leveling but as long as I can keep up with the enemies I suppose we're good, I do have a tendency to over level when possible until I can take out the enemies and bosses as easily as breathing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: good 1st half, but  falls apart in the 2nd half with poor, rushed and lazy game play/puzzles and writing, the 2nd half almost feels like an absolute joke compared to the first and i cant understand at all how this game received such high praise and awards when its simply a poorly made and written game hiding behind beautiful art hopes no one will notice (for reference i didn't play this game after seeing the hype, i actually followed its development and was incredibly excited to play it, not tryna hate, just being honest cos no one else seems to be)Sea of stars was the single most disappointing game I've ever played. I followed its development from the very start and was so excited at the beauty and promise this game showed. this game is visually beautiful, both the pixel and 2d artists for the advertising/splash art did an incredible job, in fact they entirely carried this game on their back and I hope to god they were paid handsomely for it. because the actual gameplay and story of sea of stars sucks absolute ass, it is an absolute joke that this game won any awards, and I say that as someone who has literally purposefully taken my time to wait to review this game even tho i finished it some time ago, in hopes my review would be less angry than how i felt when i initially got to the end of this game. I truly believe the only reason this game is reviewed so highly is because people reviewed it far too early and because a majority of reviewers were sponsors of the inital kickstarter and were paid a wonderful homage at the end of the game. I cannot fathom any other reason people would rate this game highly. AND I WANTED TO ENJOY IT AND I TRIED SO HARD. the issue is its so easy to tell the creators absolutely gave up halfway through development, I dont know if the money ran out or they had a deadline, but the absolute laziness and mockery of itself it makes after the halfway point is so frustrating. the initial story is great,  starts a lil slow but the visuals are gorgeous and traversing feels alot more involved than traditional rpg's which made me happy, one of my favourite things in the first half was the difficulty of the puzzles and having to actually really think for an answer, where as at the end they completely through any care for those once enjoyable puzzle's out the window making you do simple match ups that aren't even randomised you just.. match one tile to the one above it.. its.. a joke. story wise half the game builds up some huge secret a character has, but spends so much time reminding you again and again that this secret exists that you just dont care anymore, and when its finally revealed its the worst, stupidest twist ever, which you then have to spend the second half of the game trudging through desperately trying to find anything good about it before the game ends anticlimactically. the twist also means you spend half the game in a horrible ugly location that ignores all the actual cool initial world building and places that were visually enjoyable. this game could have been great, but it wasn't, writing quickly gets lazy, puzzles get lazy, twists get lazy, even the visuals get lazy and you're left feeling like scratching nails on the chalk board til the credits. i think the most enjoyable thing about the game was the little board game you could play in taverns, that about my 1 positive take away aside from the main world visuals and advertising art being incredible. it was also incredibly jarring seeing the massive face of some random youtuber in the final town who was just there permanently and randomly until they removed him because it turned out he stole from charity which was for the best anyway cos his portrait was so weirdly large and jarring and his presence was so annoying and weird that i couldn't write this review without mentioning it. anyway i can't rate this game more than a 1 honestly, i wouldn't wish playing through this game on my worst enemy. I hope they do better in future, but i for now i feel so sorry for all the other amazing indie games robbed of awards while people blindly frothed this rushed lacklustre game

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game. I completed it out of obligation but looking back, my enjoyment of the game steadily declined after 10ish hours.This game starts out strong, but after a few hours you've seen pretty much all this game has to offer. After 4ish hours, pretty much all of your combat options are unlocked.Combat becomes a chore, with new skills coming very rarely, and battles rarely offering any challenge. Boss fights were mostly straightforward affairs as well. I rarely felt threatened or had to use an item.There's basically no ability to customize your characters either, with most equipment just offering basic stats.The story is fine, nothing special. Your main characters are pretty bland.The soundtrack is fine but largely forgettable.Recommendation - Play Chrono Trigger, Super Mario RPG, or Golden Sun instead.

The combat is extremely satisfying and always feels fresh, the art of the game is breathtakingly beautiful, and the story is fun. Can't wait for the Free DLC coming next year.If you're a fan of JRPGs you'll love this game, a must buy.

The story telling and general development between characters in conversations makes it feel very lifely. The lifely atmosphere really helps with it, Im only 3h deep into this game as it stands but have little doubt much is wrong with the game.It overall has a very pleasing scenery and really great sound tracks to go along with it. _childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game in the line of old school JRPGs. It does not just copy them but takes them to the next logical iteration. The combat is fun and engaging with light manipulation of timed button presses, but the game never requires it and has multiple ways to play around that feature. It has an active map that is fun to interact with and really well done art. The story is just like that of those types of games, I don't anything that will blow you away with the depth, but is very much good enough to keep you into it. It does poke fun and winks at the player a decent amount, but I don't feel that it rises to the level of distraction, although I could see some finding that less palatable. Art and sound are top notch. Fluid gameplay that allows you to manipulate combat without being overwhelmed and forgiving health/mana systems that keep the game flowing without making it brainless. This does not replace any of the great RPGs of old, but it a great entry in that line and is extremely fun to play. If you enjoy the FF IV/VI and Chrono Trigger era/style of JRPG, then this is a easy must.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still midway through the game, but this is seriously one of the most special RPG experiences I've ever had since playing Chrono Trigger and Earthbound. Sea of Stars is just brimming with life and only gets richer as you dive in deeper. Not to mention, the environment art is just unreal! I find myself stopping quite often to take in swaying grass or water lapping at a cliff's edge. I can't recommend this one enough!Btw wheels is insanely addictive LMAO
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve seen reviews compare this game to Chrono Trigger, and I don’t actually see that other than the attempt to be a well-written story (which it does have). The writing is wholesome and interesting and complimented well by fantastic art and music. It’s a little slow to get going, whereas Chrono Trigger gripped me in the first 10 minutes, but after about an hour you’re settled in. It reminds me more of a Golden Sun / Super Mario RPG combination than Chrono Trigger. Overall, I highly recommend this game. It’s beautiful and fun and I’ve been thinking about it all day at work excited to be able to play some more later. Been playing it on my Steam Deck without issue for those whom that matters.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This is a worthy star to sit in the sea of nostalgic RPGs, and it wears its influences proudly. This is also just a fantastically balanced game. At no point did I ever truly need to put my nose to the grindstone, though my compunction to do so got the better of me at least twice (what can I say? I enjoy having an active hand in how my party members improve when they level up). Not just that, but the amount of customization you have towards your own gaming experience with the use of relics puts even triple A games to shame. The music on display here truly runs the gamut of somber and heartbreaking, to triumphant and powerful. The attention to detail is just as incredible, even with the limited feedback that the art-style can convey. I would consider myself a veteran at these sorts of games, and I was stunned into speechlessness by the sheer spectacle twice, reduced to tears once, and surprised at the escalation of the story many more times besides. I truly wish I had known about this game much sooner than I did, as everyone who contributed to this project was honored, and this is a finished product that deserves the recognition. In a year of already stacked releases, Sea of Stars shines towards the very front of the pack, and will surely take its place as a modern classic that is held up as the correct way to develop a game, a studio, and a fanbase. Bravo.

(Moonerang goes brrrrrr... )The story is OK, but some of plot choices and progression did not sit right with me. Without spoilers, the game's tone is all over the place: there are austere story sections with comedic moments that sometimes aren't put well together. For me that wasn't a deal-breaker, but to others it might be.Also, the game's soundtrack is phenomenal!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I'm gonna fire off the main points of my review and then explain.-The game looks beautiful.-The soundtrack is a bop.-The game feels exceptionally good to play.The game is stylized is the most beautiful way. All of the settings that I've been to in just under 15 hours have been breathtaking at best and aesthetically pleasing at worst. The areas have such care put into every aspect of them. Level design, secrets/treasure placement, overall cohesiveness, these are all things that stick out if nearly every area I've been to so far.The composer is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Yasunori Mitsuda. I shouldn't have to say more about the score, but I will anyways. The level scores are just great. That sounds bad, but when the worst aspect of a score is deemed great, it should speak to what the music serves to the game. The boss themes are catchy and climatic, filled with great variation for the environment you find yourself in. And then I also just unlocked the ability to listen to the songs in the tavern? Chef's kiss.The game rewards good gameplay. Which is good because there's no shortage of it. Timing is rewarded, strategy is rewarded, and variation is expected. Some of the attacks are easy to figure the timing to get that second attack or block. Some aren't so much so you're forced to adapt and learn when to get that bonus. I've had some skills for quite a while now and I still haven't mastered yet.I've skipped over a lot of the small details (such as upgrade progression, backtracking, general feeling of learning) as well, because firstly, I couldn't possibly cover them all in this short review, and secondly I'd wholeheartedly recommend this game to someone and want them to get the experience that I'm having with this game. This game is amazing.Update: This game is still amazing.

_childDocuments_.review: Hailed by a lot of people as a spiritual successor to Chrono Trigger, this game fails to measure up to its predecessor. Combat is easy and filled with button tapping mini-games that quickly become boring and repetitive. Boss fights feel like a joke, especially with no functional debuff and buff management. The lock system feels like it could have been fun but falls short of the promise it might have shown due to either being overly easy to break or so tedious to break that it isn't worth attempting. Not that it matters with how easily you can trivialize the damage enemies deal through massive healing.Moving around the world feels slow with "puzzles" that take almost no thought to complete. Ultimately it's a linear turn based RPG with tedious combat that fails to challenge and over world puzzles that also fall short. The only positive with this game is it is one of the most beautiful sprite graphic games you can find.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game on switch and bought it here to give a review. I'm 10 hours in and this is just not it.They probably took the first draft they made of almost every single element in the game and just went with it. From the combat mechanics to the dungeon map designs and the pacing. There are some basic elements found in every modern and even some old JRPGs straight up missing here, like how is there not a map? Why is there no option to run away from battles?Some elements like the pixel art are beautiful to the point where they are overdone. And then you look at the Menu GUI and it ruins your whole immersion. You can't tell me they made such beautiful environments and locations for one moment of gameplay, but the menu GUI where you'll be spending a lot of time during the adventure looks like some RPG Maker XP preset. When I first started equipping items, I genuinely thought the game was bugged because every single weapon, armor or ring has the exact same graphic. This is something old JRPGs did to save memory, not because it looks good! Even a game as old as Secret of Mana had different sprites for their items.Then the combat. In a vacuum, I love the combat. I’m a huge fan of Paper Mario, The Mario&Luigi series and QTEs in Turn Based Battles generally speak to me. This game however will just not give you any new attacks and using the ones you already have for the 40th time in a row gets old quick. I was 2 hours in, and my characters still only have the 2 spells which I had at the beginning of the game. And now I'm 5 hours in and I'm still using the same 2 spells from each character, only difference is I've gotten some mildly useful combo attacks which won't be much of use in a normal battle anyway since the enemies are dead by the point, I have 2 combo points. I'm 10 hours into the game at this abandoned lab and my characters are still only having 2 spells. This is ridiculous. They try to sell you the idea that the magic droplets thing spices up the battles when they have a negligible effect on the outcome of the battle. Enemies themself are hard to avoid if you want to explore the surrounding area thoroughly and getting into a battle always just made me sigh that I must be going through another slow battle. If there was an option to run away it wouldn't be half as bad. Then the dialogue. It's incredible how much these characters have to say in a conversation and how little was said. None of the characters have any real personality at this point and all feel the same besides Garl who is annoyingly happy. It's always such a back and forth of generic chatting which resolves to the obvious plot point being told in the end. Also, side note: In my opinion this is not a game where any 4th wall side breaking has a place. The whole scene at the first town felt like a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mod. This game tries way too hard with its self-aware humor and it ruins the immersion immensely. The dungeon design so far feels extremely basic and linear. This game has a classic case of "putting the key next to the door" phenomenon. You are introduced to a problem just to find the solution to it in the very same room 5 seconds away from your problem. What is the point of introducing these challenges if they are resolved in the blink of an eye? It also doesn't help that the puzzle types have been done a million times before and a million times better. Moving an icy block along a path, how unique. This could have been the chance to make something interesting, like have Valere shoot her moon bounce attack around the room and try to light some torches in an angle, or have Zale blast his Sunburst against a surface and make it splatter correctly against something behind.All in all, this game just feels like an overdone prototype with inspirations taken from older JRPGs at the wrong places.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased this game to play with my 5 year old daughter, she loves this game and was able to play it from start to finish with some guidance from me and with me reading the story to her, and using some in game "Relics" (optional game modifiers) that basically make it easy mode.Reviewing the game from this perspective it is a wonderful game, exactly what I was looking for, something simple and linear enough for my daughter to play, it was her first game she has played (completely, not just messing around with the controller). It required no grinding, and there was always a clear direct path to take.reviewing from the perspective of an adult gamer, I would still say it is fun albeit very linear, the puzzles are very simple so not much challenge there. The combat is similar, although it could be more difficult with certain relics that add difficulty if you want a real challenge. overall a fun experience with great pixel art.This game has the classic bunch of optional "side quests" you can do before the final boss, which include puzzles that are a bit more difficult than the main game and bosses that are more difficult than the main game boss as well. through the entire main game I could for the most part direct my daughter how to complete it, but some optional puzzles I had to take over and actually think about for a bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game received Best Indie in the Game Awards 2023 yesterday and it damn deserved it.Sea of Stars is beautiful. The pixel art is gorgeous, each character has so many animations in and out of battle and all of the fantasy environments are well-designed to transport you in this wonderful world.The music is reminiscent of some of the early Final Fantasy titles (which means amazing) with a plethora of tracks to adapt to each location of the world.The gameplay reminds me of those Mario & Luigi games. It's a turn-based combat system but when you're performing any kind of action, if you press the action button at the right moment, you're are going to amplify the effects of that action (for example, more damage dealt, more healing, less damage when being attacked etc). I really like this mechanic as it adds a nice bit of spice to the turn-based system. You can also adjust the difficulty, making it easier or harder, and find that sweet spot in difficulty that you prefer.The only thing I think could have been better is the story. Don't get me wrong, I'm not saying that it's bad. It's a really wholesome story that introduces you to an epic world with legends and gods and so on. I just think I'm more into a dark tale than a happy colorful one. Still, some of the plot twists really left me with my jaw dropped.The last thing I want to talk about is the quality of life in this game which I really appreciate as a completionist. It is never hard to backtrack in any area with tons of shortcuts you can unlock. There is a damn ping parrot that you can talk to in the world map and it will inform about the areas in which you've missed a chest. In every fishing pond there is a sign of every fish you can catch in that pond that also shows which ones you've caught. Without spoiling anything, towards the endgame you have the ability of travelling wherever you want on the world map without having to get through an area in order to get to another one. It also has a big amount of optional/post-game content so all of the above really help to complete this game.Overall, this game is excellent. It's beautiful, it's unique,it's nostalgic, it's entertaining and the list goes on.  Really deserved Indie of the year and I'm glad I played it.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game was my Game of the Year for 2023! I was super excited about this game when it was first announced and the trailer was released, and despite my already high expectations, it was still so much better than I could have imagined! The game is a modern take on the classic SNES-era JRPGs, primarily Super Mario RPG and Chrono Trigger (at least from how it felt to me), and you could really feel the passion of the developers throughout the game.First, the visuals. This game is absolutely gorgeous! It has pixel graphics, but they have modern aesthetics (e.g. trees swaying in the wind, modern lighting, etc.), in some ways like Octopath Traveler. The colors, the art, everything was so beautiful, and I found myself constantly snapping screenshots because of how mesmerized I was by the terrain.Second, the music. The songs were extremely catchy, and each location had its own unique feeling because of how well the music matched. I also really enjoyed the day-night cycle of music (e.g. in the daytime, the instruments are a bit stronger, and at night time, the music is a bit muted), which added to how alive the world felt. It really felt like a classic JRPG with respect to the soundtrack.Third, the gameplay. The controls are pretty straightforward (up, down, left, and right in an isometric view), but they are a bit modernized (e.g. diagonal movement, the ability to climb and jump down the terrain, etc.). The battle system is turn-based, and it feels most inspired by Super Mario RPG: turn-based, the male protagonist's first magic attack is clearly inspired by Geno Beam, the female protagonist's first magic attack is clearly inspired by Ultra Jump, and the combat has timed hits/guarding just like in Super Mario RPG. It also has the charged hits breaking by certain attack types game mechanic that Octopath Traveler has. I felt that the combination of these two (timed hits/guard + type breaking) made the combat feel very immersive and fun, not super repetitive like Final Fantasy games can start to feel by end game (e.g. every new enemy provided a new challenge for learning its attack patterns to master blocking).Lastly, the story. I really enjoyed the plot: the characters were lovable (especially Garl!), and I really felt attached to them as I progressed through the story. It's a fairly standard classic JRPG plot: some big baddie is trying to destroy the world, the protagonists are special chosen ones that need to defeat it, and along their way, they meet new friends (and help their friends with their own side plots), and then they defeat a god-like being with the power of friendship. It was light-hearted and didn't take itself too seriously, and I really enjoyed it!Overall, I highly recommend this game, even at full price. If you're a fan of classic SNES-era JRPGs, you absolutely must play this game!

_childDocuments_.review: I backed the Kickstarter for Sea of Stars, and I'm glad I did.  At this point, I'm still very early in the game, just barely out of the starting area.  But, so far I'm really enjoying things.  They did an amazing job of recapturing the 16-bit era and SNES magic of classic RPG.  I don't know why, but that first boss size and animation caught me a little off guard.  The detail of the bosses was slightly spoiled by the last trailer, but it was just great to see that the bosses wan't just a bigger enemy.  It managed to strike the right balance of using limitless storage and the styling of a 16-bit game.  The one aspect to the game I'm mixed on is the stats upgrade.  It's hard to know if you're making a poor choice. Hopefully there will be an option to redo it if you find it's not quite working.  But, it's possible that the delta is not large enough to make a huge difference at the end.  Min-max can be a pain if you let it.  I'm sure someone will have a video out about best combos soon.Something I want to say about the combat.  The combat has a little more depth than you might realize. I haven't gotten the relic that allows for a harder mode (I assume there is one), and I can tell the combat is really geared to equip for that.  In the beginning, the game very much tells you don't be afraid to use your MP and abilities.  Normally in Sq/En JPRG you kinda hoard your abilities unless you want to grind.  Here, since you can regen your MP during combat, the game seems like it wants you to be more aggressive in your play style.   That's a change from the norm, and so far it seems like overkill.  You have to really understand the battle and how to time/align your regen with breaking the enemy to min/max you MP usage and regen.  But, unless there is a hard mode, this seems like it's overkill. If there is a hard mode where the mobs have higher HP I could see this being more of a thing and you'd have to think about combat a little more.  This would dispel some of the monotony I see other reviews talking about.  So, here's hoping there is a hard mode later and that's why the combat is designed this way.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely without a doubt would recommend this game to anyone who likes traditional RPGs, and also to anyone who's just interested. Even if you don't care for some of the typical elements of RPGs, this game has you covered. Tons of variability in difficulty settings, progression that's balanced to basically eliminate grinding, and fun combat that makes it easy to get in the flow of every battle. Music is phenomenal and there's tons of attention to detail in the world they've made. You can truly have whatever experience you want with this game, and I'm sure you'd enjoy it.Only things I'd note is that the story and gameplay can feel a bit slow to get going, and if you're jumping in for a Final Fantasy level adventure, you won't find it here. But that's not a huge deal because the game is short compared to your average RPG, and everything I mentioned before makes up for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Do you remember how you felt the first time you played through Chrono Trigger?Did you enjoy solving environment puzzles in Zelda games? (not the water temple, F that place)Did you ogle the art style of Illusion of Gaia and laugh at the tongue-in-cheek self-awareness of Secret of Evermore?I've been chasing those highs since the 90's and this game is about as close as I've ever gotten to that  feeling of a play-through.Sea of Stars was kickstarted as a love letter to classic RPGs of the 90s.It feels familiar and brand new at the same time.Traversal of the world feels really good and only improves as you go.Puzzles are pleasantly challenging but never frustratingly so. (I'm looking at you Water Temple)You have a lot of choice in how you level your characters.Each character's abilities feel unique and useful if not outright epic.You can pick ingredients and choose what food to make for healing/mp items or you can just sell all of the ingredients and buy whatever items you want pre-cooked when they're available. There are fishing and battler mini-games that are fun to learn and master. You can perform timed attacks and blocks for bonus damage or damage reduction.It's as if they took your favorite games from the 90's and gently, lovingly massaged in quality of life improvements and all of the fun, unique aspects of other games that have come before and since.Enhancing replayability is the Bastion/Hades style toggles in the form of relics.Want to make the game extra smooth or are you dying a lot? There's a relic for that.Do you want bad guys to hit harder or take less damage? There's a relic for that.Are you a completionist like me who wants to find every treasure in the game? There's a relic for that.Are you a try-hard who deletes their save file when they die?... Seek professional help. There's also a New Game + feature which I'm also super excited about trying after I finish my first playthrough.To the best of my knowledge, you can't permanently "Miss" anything in the game. Most items are fairly straightforward to find (So far no digging in unlit corners of the map to find some hidden item for later)If you listen to the soundtracks of Final Fantasy games in the car and at the gym(or wherever)This soundtrack will be on your rotation. I kickstarted the game and was a bit hesitant to buy the vinyl without hearing any of it. Now I'm super excited to get mine. For the snarky negative reviewers, I don't know who hurt you but unfortunately the one thing this game can't do is heal whatever childhood trauma made you unable to have fun and enjoy something like a wide-eyed kid again.Like I said, this is like playing Chrono Trigger or similar again for the first time. Inject that ♥♥♥♥ into my veins. Do you understand how hard that is to pull off without being just a full-on clone? It's a razor's edge, edgelord...Meanwhile, I'll be over here criss-cross apple sauce on the carpet gaming until four in the morning when they have to call a paramedic to get me up off the floor because I'm old and can't get back up.   If my nieces and nephew don't play the original Chrono Trigger, Secret Of Mana, Secret Of Evermore, A Link to the Past, etc. I would be just as happy if this was their "it" game for them. I will be introducing them to it as soon as they're old enough to hold a controller. They will be solstice warriors.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the prettiest games I've ever played. I like the combat system, it reminds me of Legend of Dragoon's input responsive turn based combat system but  in my opinion it works a lot better here in a 16 bit pixel art setting. Everything is animated smoothly, the characters have a cute, old school RPG charm and fit the setting well. I wish there was more depth to the combat, there's a serious lack of diversity when it comes to skills. I believe there are only 4 unique to each character and 4 combos (might be wrong, haven't beaten it yet but I'm pretty well into the game). However it's got a lot going for it and I genuinely hope to see more from this dev in this style. Wasn't expecting a quirky indie retro-core RPG to impress me as much as this game did. If you like old school Japanese RPG games, especially ones like Secret of Mana or Chrono Trigger, definitely check this game out.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is the most beautiful lazy river ride you'll ever take.The high point for the game is oddly the background art, which is -- without hyperbole -- the best pixel art backgrounds I have ever seen. Period. The character animations and art are also superb, running a close second behind the gorgeous backgrounds. Definitely an odd thing to have as a high-point, but it is quite high.The low point is the characters and their dialogue, which leaves each character as either too weak in personality to describe, or too strong in a single personality quirk that borders annoyance. The story is not offensive, but it's run-of-the-mill at best.Everything in-between is a fine experience. Nothing in the game will wall you with a challenge, you'll meander right through it. The combat can be interesting when it's not frustrating (though it's never difficult). Thankfully, there is little need to grind! The game also demonstrates a 2D platforming / obstacle course design in all of it's maps. This can be engaging your first time through a map, but becomes tedious if backtracking.Overall, Sea of Stars is a good entry-level RPG that echoes traditional values from the 90's. It took roughly 40 hours to get a 100% completion (barring a few achievements) with very, very light guide usage, so very playable! It felt like the right length for the content.There's not a strict and enduring charm to Sea of Stars. It probably won't stick with you, but it's easy to beat and engaging enough to warrant a play-through if you enjoyed the JRPGs of yore.

_childDocuments_.review: I backed this game in 2020 because the idea of a modern-day Chrono Trigger (CT) excited me so much. Loads of JRPG fans, myself included, hold CT as the pinnacle of JRPGs. Whenever I was reminded of Sea of Stars through the backer emails over the years, I would always feel a sense of excitement and anticipation. I couldn't wait to get my hands on this game. You'll read lots of reviews about how this game is a "love letter to classic JRPGs" and "if you loved CT, you'll love this game!!!!!!!" I completed the entire game (including side content), and my time with the game bothered me so much that I decided to write this review to gather my thoughts.  When I watched the credits roll, I finally figured out what I was feeling: it was disappointment. I had been waiting YEARS for this game, and I felt like I was let down.  This game is not really that comparable to CT in terms of quality. Sure, they both share similar music and art style I guess, and hey, when you engage in combat, you don't transition into a generic battle area! You fight where you engaged the enemies! Like in CT! And there are character combo attacks too! You know, in that game everyone loves?! If you liked THAT game, SURELY you'll like this game! But the dialogue, the story, the characters-- the things that I love about JRPGs and make me want to keep playing, and the things that CT excelled at-- are so laughably bad in this game that they really, I mean REALLY, detract from the overall experience from the game. The blatant grammatical mistakes are only a very small fraction of what's wrong with this game. Zale and Valere are self-insert protagonists that can be interchangeable at any given moment. I cannot tell you a single thing that differentiates the two personality-wise. The only standout feature of their personalities is that they really cherish their friend Garl, the warrior cook, who's very wholesome and friendly and everyone loves him DON'T YOU LOVE HIM TOO LOVE HIM HE IS VERY WHOLESOME AND FRIENDLY WHY IS THIS GAME NOT CALLED BIG GARL'S BIG ADVENTURE. The other characters are there too, I guess. The dialogue can be read with your eyes and lets you know what to do and where to go. It's not enjoyable to read, and at times it was grating for me because of certain side characters who have funny quirks, like making fourth-wall-breaking jokes that are so funny and make me laugh every time I read them. I loved it! At a campfire, you can sit down and listen to a story about cool things that happened in the past. Some things are only elaborated on when you listen to these stories at a campfire, but in my opinion, it feels very artificial and boring to be told about past events and characters through this way. It doesn't help that the delivery is very bland and boring.I don't want to talk too much about story, but I will say that I was very unimpressed. I had joked about why isn't this game called "Big Garl's Big Adventure," but I feel like there's some truth to it. It feels like Sabotage Studios put more love and effort into Garl, so much so that it feels like he's the actual protagonist whereas Valere and Zale are the deuteragonists, despite their massive significance to the plot, at times. Some plot points personally made no sense to me, and other times I wanted to know more about certain things but they're never followed up on. I saw loads of potential in the story but it never came to fruition, and that's a shame in my opinion. Like I said, I beat the main game and side content on normal difficultly so my characters were fully decked out and had all their skills. Throughout the game, I didn't feel like I was progressing that much; I felt the same as I did at the final boss as I did in the middle of the game. The REAL challenge of combat was fighting normal enemies that felt like they were poorly balanced. Bosses? Easiest battles of my life. 2v4 with mobs that deal lots of damage via normal attacks and have a special attack that hits the entire party (only two of you by the way)? Probably the worst fights of the game. It bothers me that the devs tell you in the beginning of the game that you don't have to be perfect by blocking every single hit that comes your way, and yet they make some mobs regularly dish out absurd amounts of damage which makes you feel like you're being destroyed regardless of whether or not you're blocking properly. I normally play on normal difficulty for games, but I was tempted to put on the storyteller mode just so I could get through the painful fights more easily. Skill issue? Maybe. But how am I able to defeat big scary bosses easily when I get beat up by normal mobs so badly? Shouldn't it be the other way around? Conclusion/TLDR:+ I thought about Chrono Trigger while playing this game so go play CT if you haven't already+ Art style is beautiful + Music is pretty good imo - Characters are very bland and one-dimensional- Story and world had potential but didn't capitalize on it - Combat is okay in the beginning but becomes tedious; you'll feel like you're scraping by in normal fights almost all the time but boss battles are a joke If you really want to play this game, I recommend buying it on a discount. Otherwise, I would recommend looking elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game for quite some time now, and it definitely delivered in a lot of places but fell surprisingly short in some others. Before anything else I'd like to state I definitely enjoyed the game and found it well wort the $35, however, there were definitely a couple of glaring issues I'd like to comment on as they definitely bring down the game as a whole. **SPOILER'S AHEAD**- The characters:This represents both a positive and one major negative for the game. Most of the characters, while at times somewhat one dimensional, were very fun to play and watch. Resh'an, B'st, and Serai all have very cool and unique character designs that are just a ton of fun to watch, especially with their cool abilities in comabt. Garl is definitely the developer's favorite character in the way he kind of forces the story along, but he is pretty awesome for the most part (he tame's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ dragon) aside from being one dimensionally positive at times. The biggest problem here is the main characters... While having a single main character be bland is ok for the most part, as to serve as a self insert for the player, having TWO main characters be bland is a bit too much. Valere and Zale consistently have completely useless and uninteresting dialogue, no personality whatsoever, and also bland visual character designs save for some colored glowing hair. I find myself just wanting to skip through their dialouge half of the time, but having to stop myself due to the occasional story-relevant sentence hidden among all the "..."s and "hahahahaha"s. The focus throughout the story and combat is clearly placed on Valere and Zale but I find myself having trouble caring as I really just don't care for them at all. It's extra confusing too, given that the studio can clearly make good characters as evidenced by the rest of the party and even the other evil solstice warriors that have far more interesting character designs and motives than the main characters. There is also a lack of character development throughout the story leading to characters feeling one dimensional even though their designs are cool. They try to develop resh'an's character for a bit, but then he just leaves out of nowhere??? And instead of building on his mental conflict between Aephorul being his good friend but also evil at the same time, he kinda just pops back in at the end of the game and just... sends you off? In the true ending he also doesn't do anything interesting, as he just takes Aephorul away and doesn't demonstrate any semblance of a result from his time he to "think about things". At least have him somewhat hesitate to take Aephoruls hand or something to show the mental conflict and develop the character. Also don't just leave us with a husk of one of the best characters for the entire end game, it's just pointless and they don't even do anything with his return at the end. Overall, the characters weren't phenomenal, but save for the main characters they were definitely enjoyable and memorable and I liked seeing them in the story and in combat.-The plot:As many reviews touch on, the intro is definitely slow. I feel like there was some need for developing the main characters here, but it really just pins them as "I like pushups" and "I like sittups". Past the intro the story kicks it into high gear and is definitely really good. The transition to the sea of stars was awesome and Serai's twist was super cool. The story was one of the best parts of this game and is what kept me playing for so long. The ending is definitely where it kinda fell flat though, as aside from some fun fan service in the true ending (which definitely shouldn't be optional by the way and hidden behind 60 entire conch shells), the ending kinda sucked. Both version of the final boss were super anti-climactic, resh'an's roll in the end was useless, and the boss kinda just gtes whisked away before getting downplayed by a bigger badder threat and the main characters kinda just leave out of nowhere. It's hard to feel sad about due to the suddenness, and i don't think I really would've cared even if the main characters were interesting. The scenes in the credits are definitely fun to watch though, and bring it back enough so that the ending is not a complete disappointment (especially the true ending (which definitely shouldn't be optional****)). Overall, the story was definitely one to be remembered, save for a bit of time spent in the intro and the ending overshadowing it a bit. - The world, graphics, and sound:This is definitely the one part of the game I couldn't find anything to criticize about. The world is super fun and engaging with plenty of not too hard to find but not too easy to find secrets hidden about. Every place you go to is unique and fun to walk through and explore. The incredible graphics only add to this, with this being the best looking pixelated game i've ever played. The lighting, 3D depth, and texture quality are all superb and make the game just that much more immersive. The sound too is awesome, with great SFX and also a  pretty good soundtrack to boot (maybe a bit repetitive at times if I had to pry). Overall, this part was great.-Gameplay:In my opinion, the combat was actually really enjoyable. The timing help reduce how repetitive the combat felt and even added some reward for learning moves and their timing. This is a place where a ton of other rpgs tend to fall flat, as timing out each move makes it much more engaging than just hitting x on fire blast and watching the same animation do the same amount of damage every time. The only issue I found with this, however, was that it made certain moves just take way too long and made the combat feel very lengthy at times, which gets annoying when you fail to dodge multiple small fights in a row. *cough* *cough* moonerang *cough*. The lock system for blocking spells was very unique and fun in my opinion and added a fun bit of strategy when it came to figuring out which combination of moves could block each attack. Once again this made fights less repetitive, but had some isues in the fact that a poorly timed spell could leave you locked out of a character that could otherwise block the attack, certain spells were just blatantly impossible to block, and multiple spells going at once quickly overwhelmed any ability to block them all, which is good at times, but also leaves the player feeling forced to attack instead of healing and just leaving one of the characters to die. (Nothing felt worse than seeing a sun lock in the arena when Zale literally wasn't even on my team). I thought the auto revive KO system was very nice and took some stress off of constantly healing all the time and left more time to attack which is a problem in a lot of other RPGs (as I mentioned before though, sometimes there was too much emphasis on just attack). Overall the combat was much more engaging than most other turn based rpgs, and I think most criticism on this combat doesn't view it from the scope of a turn based rpg.-And for the games mot fatal flaw, the bosses:The bosses. The design for the bosses were cool and all, but holy crap did some of them just need to die already. There were so many bosses that started off fun and interesting, but after mellowing out once their henchmen died, just kinda of sat there and absorbed damage for 30 minutes.  SO many times the bosses had waaaaaaaaaay too much health, or at least just didn't do anything interesting enough to warrant taking so much time. A couple of second phases here and there could've buffed this issue out, but this was almost never the case. Lack of second phases,  lack of  move sets, and also lack of boss characterization, left many bosses feeling incredibly anti-climactic. This was also true, FOR THE FINAL BOSS (both of them). Need less health.-Yolande:Who's oc is this? >: (  Horrible character, needed to stop talking. Broke immersion.- B'st ultGive the designer a raise : D

_childDocuments_.review: IT SLAPS, IT SLAPS, IT SLAPS. I genuinely love everything about this game. The battle system's a great callback to classics like Chrono Trigger and Super Mario RPG, the visuals and music are some of the best I've seen and heard, the characters are great (Zale and Valere are kinda boring, but the supporting cast carries), the writing knows how to be witty and serious, and the story had me no-lifing the game for days on end just to see where it all went. It does lose steam a bit in terms of pacing toward the end, which is one of the few complaints I've seen others have that I agree with, but beyond that, nothing overstays its welcome and I got just enough of everything I wanted out of the game. It's not perfect, but it simply ticks all my boxes. Another absolute banger from the lads behind The Messenger.

_childDocuments_.review: Having beaten the story (non-100%) a couple days back (10/18), I can easily say this game is definitely one of my gaming highlights of this year. Compelling combat system (similar to Paper Mario, plus boost and lock mechanics), great cast of characters and an amazing soundtrack (one of its boss themes still playing rent-free in my head to this day). Looking at other reviews, I can kinda understand why the story may be regarded as overall divisive (especially how I thought the final boss and ending felt rather abrupt), but personally I enjoyed it, especially how it tossed in a few surprises I wasn't quite expecting.Big mention to its difficulty and accessibility options. From pretty early on in the game, you'll be able to enable various Relics which help tailor the difficulty to your liking; ranging from automatically timing combat actions like double-attacks and blocks, to taking more damage and not being allowed to use healing food items in battle. Myself, I stuck with the default difficulty (the only relic I had enabled is one that just provides visual feedback on timing combat actions correctly) which felt just right; providing enough challenge and no boss ever felt frustrating.Combat and other mechanics are explained pretty well via their tutorials (and if you forget, you can access 'How to Play' from the pause menu at any time), which therefore confused me as to why there was no automatic tutorial for fishing and Wheels (tabletop minigame), the latter which took me a good while to understand and therefore appreciate (even if Wheels is still a little slow-paced for my liking).I also wished there was a bit more variety to puzzle solving; most puzzles featured either 'push this block to X' or 'find the X object that can interact with Y switch' - in particular, I would like to have seen a bit more creativity with the 'time changing' mechanic.But those nitpicks aside, Sea of Stars has perhaps become one of my favourite turn-based RPGs in recent memory, and a definite recommend from me (though best to get this on sale, given its rather steep asking price).

_childDocuments_.review: Nearly 20 hours in thus far and the only major complaint is how linear the story has been thus far - avoiding spoilers I think it is just now opening up more, so hopefully that will change.It's not overly difficult, save points are abundant. My main advice so far is to always keep empty slots in your food inventory (you can sadly only carry 10 meals); I've only ever even used a meal once, but you find them all over the place and if your meal inventory is full you can't pick them up. So just sell off some so you always have space.The relics allow you to tweak the game experience (mostly to make it easier) so I haven't made use of them and it's still not very challenging thus far; aside from when a bunch of monsters all use "lock" abilities on round 1 and you can't interrupt them all - that's the only time it gets a little hairy.Overall it's an interesting game, hopefully it becomes more challenging and less linear as I enter the next "chapter".EDIT: Now up to 33 hours in - it remained unfortunately linear, but the story had a few decent notes. Though now that I've hit the  chapter it kind of... accelerated unrealistically? Avoiding spoilers but the group encounters some things that really should have been more than just set pieces and aren't explained at all how they are so nonchalant - or even how they know what they are talking about when none of it has been mentioned before.An unfortunate turn- but we'll see how things progress.==================================================EDIT2: Well - that was even more unexpected and another tonal shift - .TLDR: This game seems like they came up with some really interesting set pieces and had no idea how to connect them in a true narrative - the first half of the game (up to spoiler one) does a good job, but then at that point it takes a rapid shift like they suddenly lost track of development time or funding and decided they needed to very rapidly shift to a whole new disconnected area  That's not to say I'm not enjoying the game - but it's definitely nothing like what I expected, and unfortunately I don't mean that in the good way...==================================================EDIT3: 49.5 hours in, all side content that can be done before the "end" completed.A lot of spoilers below - but the short version is: the ending feels extremely rushed, and doesn't bother to resolve anything hardly - it doesn't leave you feeling any sense of accomplishment at all.This game had a lot of potential, but the story is just an absolute mess; it's fun, but disappointing that it could have (and should have) been so much more.I believe there's a handful of things that can be done after the "end" of the game, so I'll be going through those, but I seriously doubt it can make up for the disappointment of the last half of the game, and especially the last fifth or so.==================================================EDIT4:As a parting piece of advice - there are two moves that are extremely useful in the game, especially when it gives you normally unbreakable combos of locks: Serai's "Disorient" (give her a lot of mana, it costs 7 base); and the Great Alchemist's Ultimate move. Strategic use of these two allows you to overcome things like "5 Suns" or "Sword, Hammer, Poison, Moon, Sun" when they show up with only 1 turn to interrupt them in.========================================EDIT5: Unexpected continuation.========================================EDIT6: Tedium...This is going to be tedious; not because it is hard, but because New Game + is not scaled, at all... enemies die in one hit, and I wasn't over-leveled from the first playthough; I didn't use the xp boost relic, and only really did required combats...========================================EDIT 7:Made it to Brisk; thus far the only enemies who have survived more than one hit have been bosses .

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is beautiful, and its level design and aesthetics in every respect are a love letter to older RPGs from the SNES era. The developers removed a lot of the tedium involved from back then -- you won't spend a night or two just wandering around for random encounters so you can grind your way up to survive in the next area -- and that's great.. but the issue now is there's no challenge present.You will see a lot of negative reviews talking about the RNG of the 'interrupt this special' combo system, or the dialogue or flat characterisation, but ultimately all these things can -- or at least in theory, COULD -- be looked over if the mechanics were tighter, and they're just... not.They've done what they can to make the structure of combat interesting, and they've toned down on random encounters, but there is no challenge to anything the game presents at all. None. There *are* items that you can purchase and turn on to make things harder, little optional artifacts you acquire along the way that give no benefit but do make things more difficult, but personally, I don't think that's how a game should be made. Provide variable difficulty levels if you want, provide optional toggles or sliders, but don't simply dump all the tools in my lap unsorted and tell me, "I don't know, you balance it :)" I don't want to balance it. I want you to balance it; you're the developer. This is your job. Balancing games is a non-trivial task, and if I wanted to meticulously tinker with things to get the difficulty-fun-reward ratio *just right*, I'd be making my own game or working for hire with someone on theirs, I would not be paying to play yours.It's a lovely game, clearly made by people passionate about the era of gaming it emulates and iterates upon, but the complete and utter lack of difficulty means I may as well just be watching a slideshow or Let's Play.

At the beginnig I dreaded the combat, because I sucked, but I got better. Learned to absolutely abuse the hell out of our two magically inclined main characters, and slowly but surely learned to like the combat system. But the strenght is the exploration. The world itself. _childDocuments_.review: I recommend. It's a very good game. I'd score it 8/10 after doing about 95% what games has to offer in a little above 30 hours. The game is visually astonishing, story is very good, characters too. There's good amount of exploration and there's interesting minigame built in the game.The one thing that is problematic in my opinion is combat - especially in a first few hours after leaving starting island. There is a lot of RNG that can often make opponents' casting impossible to interrupt and groups of normal enemies deal A LOT of damage. There's a combo system that provides powerful skills done by 2 characters. Due to issues i mentioned, the only viable option in early game is healing what makes combat quite irritating and boring (at least for me). After a few hours player get access to a character able to delay actions of enemies what finally makes player be able to deal with unfortunate RNG. Later on, you get another 2 characters who make combat more and more interesting with options and combos which each of them provides.I didn't use it myself, but there's an option (that happen relatively quickly) to buy a relic for a low price that decreases amount damage dealt by enemies by 30%. I don't recommend using it on bosses because I think they are well balanced. I'm writing about it because I had few moments in the beginning that i wanted to just stop playing. Now, after beating this game, I would regret not playing it. So if you happen to feel like that during your playthrough, there's an option to make it more fair.There's also one relic you get from the start. It provides autohealing after each combat and doubles your Hp, but i think this one depletes any difficulty from the game. But that's also an option to make it through unbalanced parts of the game, just to have fun with the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is a really nice old school JRPG, made with heart and love, that's for sure. Yet it has flaws.Yes, the combat gets boring by the middle of the story as there are too few skills and yet the the lock system and the gimmicks of late game bosses bring back some flavour to it.Yes, the two main characters are your generic heroes with non-existent personalities but several side characters or party members had great stories and funny interactions, and I am not talking about Garl, as I felt I was being force-fed into liking him, but rather of Cael, Teaks, Seraï or even B'st.Yes, it feels like it's built like any other JRPG, the story feels bland at first, then by the time you get to the second world, things start getting interesting as you get invested and secrets unveil in front of you. Nothing too crazy though but it's alright.But it also has strengths, and boy oh boy they are something. The pixel art is top tier, you won't find another game using pixel art as beautiful to look at that than this one. The music is awesome the whole game, from day and night variants, to alternative themes in the second world, I was head-banging all along.All in all, Sea of Stars is a great experience, I've probably played too many games like these hence why I was expecting more depth on every aspect, but I still enjoyed my time.Oh and don't listen to the hipsters trying to figure out which one is better between Chained Echoes and Sea of Stars, do yourself a favour and just play them both.

_childDocuments_.review: When I was growing up as a kid, my dad spent time with me in a way different way than most dads. He would watch me play video games. We grew up with him watching me play countless RPGs. His favorite of all time (and one of my favorites) was Chrono Trigger. He loved the characters, the music, the story, the combat, everything about it and I loved it as well.About 5 years ago my dad died of brain cancer. As he was dying, he slowly forgot more and more of himself and those he knew over time. The last game I played in front of him was a replaythrough of Chrono Trigger since I knew it was his favorite game of all time. He would always light up, even if he was having trouble remembering things when I would play it in front of him again. I left a copy of the game on his grave when he passed away.Why am I saying all of this? This game brings back those old memories of what it was like to experience Chrono Trigger for the first time. The characters, atmosphere, combat, so much of it is truly amazing. I haven't felt like I have since then in a long long time. There are so many great things I could start listing about this, but there are other great gamers on here who have made great reviews to talk about all of those. I know wherever my father is now, he was watching me play this game just like when I used to play Chrono Trigger, and he was having the best time of his life.Thank you for making this amazing gem Sabotage. We are lucky to get to experience it.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for 34 hours, I definitely plan to replay it again. This is without a doubt one of the most enjoyable experiences I've ever had in an rpg. The artwork is simply fantastic. The expressions are well drawn, and the environment feels extremely immersive, despite it being a little too linear at times. The music is also superb, and since its a turn based rpg I would just sit there and listen to the music for a solid few minutes prior to actually doing a fight lmao. Additionally, the open world is really fun to explore, especially post-game. Theres a lot to do after being the main story. My only complaint would be the writing. Granted, I don't know how to read french, and I had to rely on the english version of the game. I can understand if there was some translation errors, but even then I feel as if the writing was murky. Sometimes it was stellar, and other times it fell short. If this was a translation issue, I wish it was resolved earlier during the proof reading. Regardless I wish the quality of the writing wasn't so spotted. The characters also aren't as developed as I would've liked. Valare and Zale are fairly one note. Serai and Garl, and the other two party members (which I won't say as I don't wanna risk spoiling), feel somewhat developed, the main characters fall short in this category. I really wish they added scenes of the group bonding and getting to know each other. This could've been added in the campfires, and I feel as if it was a missed opportunity.Another thing I didn't like was the side quests. There is no way to really check your objectives apart from going to the campfire, which, can honestly be annoying at times. It would've been nice to have a quest tab. Also, the backtracking was a real chore sometimes, but I didn't mind it too much as I loved exploring and re-exploring areas. Now, heres where I get into the part I disliked the most. Warning, there WILL be spoilers.The story had a lot of holes near the end. For example, while I thought it was clever for B'st to take Garl's place and save him from being killed, how did B'st know exactly what happened leading up to his death? Yes, we can argue that when he visited garl's grave at Mooncradle with Valare (If I remember right, it was either valare or zale) that he was told about the events and was able to replicate them to not break the timestream. However, it would've been nice to actually see this dialogue so we understand how he was able to replicate Garl's actions. Also, why the ♥♥♥♥ did we see pretty much nothing happen to Erlina and Brugraves? Theres a cutscene in the true ending that shows Brugraves as a demon..thats it? I really wanted to see the two more on screen since Valare and Zale clearly saw them as a mentor figure, and were heartbroken at their betrayal. Also, Erlina was pretty underwhelming as the final boss. I expected her to be more challenging, but it was a cakewalk. Even if this was just the normal ending, I really wanted to have a really good fight with her, because she was one of those characters that I got pissed at and wanted to thrash. And thrash I did, but it isn't fun when there is no struggle lol. All in all, the fight was underwhelming. Also, and this is personally my biggest gripe..I wish there was more post-game content. The sea of stars was such an interesting concept, and I loved traversing between the home world and serai's world. Plus actually sailing in space was really cool. I wish there was more worlds I could explore, or if I could keep doing that sequence between the two worlds. I didn't like that it was just turned into a loading zone after going through that cutscene once. . I hope the developers make a dlc or just add more content, allowing us to explore more than just one world. All in all, this is an amazing game. I highly recommend that you check out this masterpiece. It isn't perfect, but its pretty damn close!

_childDocuments_.review: Good game with interesting story and great endings (especialy from the perspective of the Messenger player), but just OK'ish gameplay as pretty much every aspect here is pretty simple and while there are no bad mechanics, they all lack something more, more skills, buffs/debuffs, not to mention shmup parts that are present on 3 different occasions which on one hand adds variety to otherwise simple fights but on the other it just looks bizzare and doesn't really add any valueFights are based partially around your reflexes and mostly around puzzles, as you have to figure out which locks to break in which order or how to use combos and attacks to break more of them. It's nice that swapping characters doesn't cost anything and you can move each and every one of them all the time throughout the main story, but on the other hand it slightly takes away from the whole planning your party for the encounter or preparing for specific encounter that a lot of classic JRPGs have... but I wouldn't say its a straight flaw either, I just kinda liked that aspect in other gamesSide quest and "character stories" are pretty well made and even if you can finish most of them without having the campsite talk and just after get the dialogue prompting you to start it, there isn't really a thing to complain on as each of the 7 side activities is slightly different and each has its own reward, not to mention the connected reward after completing them all and unlocking the 8th side quest and somewhat emotional cutscene. The only thing to actually complain about is how true ending ends, how there is pretty big empty space for what Rash'an was doing in the meantime and while I belive it may be explained in another sequel/prequel/paraquel or w/e they come up with, I'd like to not be left on a cliffhanger for another 5 yearsLeveling up is kinda funny cos it's rng based but at the same time everyone at max level which is 30 would have same stats cos you can only take each stat 5 times, but everyone knows that first dmg, than armor and by the end you are invincible anywayItems and shopping feels lacking, but as the game is more focused on the fights and environmental puzzles, it doesn't really matter and is fine as isSecrets doesn't really exist beside few little things (or I missed them all secret secrets)Music and sounds which I usually don't care for, this time were a big part of why I enjoyed the game as much, some tunes from Messenger were nice touch, most of the new things fitted nicelyGraphics are 10/10, I loved each location, each pixel and every character design... beside the cartoon like cutscenesStrong recommendation for everyone who enjoyed the The Messenger story or likes the metroidvania approach of revisiting old locations with new tools for more loot as after the true ending it's 9.5/10 imobut for people who love the turn based combat and are looking for some challanges in this end... it's 6 at best

_childDocuments_.review: After getting all achievements my opinion is this: a very fun game with a good story and music, with some replayability, something I feel most games these days lack. Overall, I think it's fantastic and more people should give it a shot. It's not Chrono Trigger, nor should it be compared to as such. It offers so much in a minimalistic way I would never have expected from a JRPG from the pixel style to how animations and sprites are used. My only complaint is that it is not quite optimized for PC in the last sections of the game, giving me brief moments of lag. Otherwise, it's a wonderful adventure filled to the brim with story and gameplay that is by far very engaging for a turn based RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pleasantly surprised with the duration of the main narrative and the layered approach to it. The game doesn't really lay out, in an obvious way at least, the "main goal" of the entire campaign right out of the gate. This allows for you to achieve major milestones and begin to understand how that accomplishment leads you to the next necessary step. I also really appreciated the relic system letting you sort of "tweak" your difficulty in specific ways which is appreciated more than a "easy normal hard" approach, and this also flowed into rewarding players with more skill in timing things during turn based combat. I hadn't really experienced much of that previously and felt this to be a big boon.Overall I would have to say I recommend this game, especially on sale. You can comfortably clock 25-30 hours with a normal playthrough that includes minimal "collection" activities. Pros:*Pleasant artwork and music*Rewarding and substantive narrative*Minigame (wheels) is a nice way to change of pace, if at times frustrating*Skill rewarded during combat*Nuanced reveals, some more obvious than others, that feel satisfyingCons*Fishing minigame adds little*"True Ending" hidden behind some pretty boring time-wasting activities*Cooking/food adds little. Could have been managed differently but did tie in narratively well. *Combat lock RNG sometimes frustrating*Trial and error necessary to learn proper timings of abilities, even with help of relic

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely DELIGHTFUL.I'd backed Sea of Stars (on Kickstarter) ages ago, mostly on a whim: I don't do a lot of crowdfunding, and frankly, I haven't played many JRPG-style games. (The original FF7 is probably the last one I've actually committed to and finished, way back in the late 90s. Since then, I'd muddled through many, or tried, always losing my focus and moving on.) But something about Sea of Stars called to me - trust in the Sabotage team, maybe? - and here we are.Bottom line, it's terrific, and if (by chance) you're like me - you've got a nostalgic interest in the genre, but you haven't been able fully engage these games as a grown-up - this might grab you, like it grabbed me. On one hand, it feels breezily accessible: many JRPGs lean so hard into arcane world-building and exposition that they tend to leave me bewildered and bored from the outset. The world and atmosphere of Sea of Stars is INCREDIBLY charming and it feels rich, but there aren't too many moving parts to juggle. Dialog is informative but not overwhelming; conversations flow speedily along, and the early phase of the game isn't cluttered with unnecessary details.At the same time, it quickly becomes clear that Sea of Stars seeks to balance streamlined features with ones that give the experience depth. The combat system, for example, plays out in the usual old-school JRPG fashion: cycle your party member, select an action, select a target, etc. Turns are true - ie, there's no real-time initiative system permitting the CPU to jump turns if you snooze. (And if you're a working parent, snoozing is a real issue). At the same time, Sea of Stars introduces neat little "timing" features with executed actions: players are invited to attempt blocks or critical hits by hitting keys at certain moments while animations play out. The game assures us that these features are there for the taking and can enhance the action, but they aren't necessary.All in all, the game feels like a perfect balance: it's fresh yet nostalgic; it's relaxed but exciting. It's also beautiful, and it boasts a great musical score to boot.I won't give a numerical score until I've finished or gotten further, but in terms of recommendations, Sea of Stars is an easy pick. Grab it and support this terrific team.

_childDocuments_.review: So I wanted to try a JRPG... and I could do a lot worse than Sea of Stars! The story is engaging enough, the grind is not unbearable, the characters are likable, and the pixel graphics is great. I happily followed the story even though it's a straightforward coming of age cliche full of standard tropes with only a couple of twists and very few jokes (Yolanda tried, A for effort, but that's not enough). In general, this was a great success for me.On the other hand, it's still a JRPG, and it proved to be not really my genre. The gameplay is very repetitive; I didn't use any amulets to keep the experience as intended by the devs, and I really don't understand how anyone could ever want to replay this game. I wanted to get the true ending, and while almost all quests were easy and straightforward, the grind for rainbow conches was suddenly way too much: it required combing over basically all locations in the game again while adding zero new fun or challenge. Thanks for the parrot, it's really useful, but I still did it with a guide to save time, and I don't regret this decision; it still took several tedious hours to collect all conches, even with a guide!
