_childDocuments_.review: A great JRPG style game with bopping music.I'm of the generation that lived though the golden age of JRPGs, Chrono Trigger, Final Fantasy 4-7, Breath of Fire 1-3, etc. The fact that pretty much all of them got sequels is a testament to their popularity and quality, but the first one in that list has always mysteriously been lacking one aside from the, imho, lackluster Crono Cross (that was so different it might as well have been a completely different series).Sea of Stars is a proper successor to Chrono Trigger, though it doesn't quite hit the mark in terms of story quality. It's alright, but it doesn't feel that personal. The devs have spent a lot of effort trying to make us care about the people in this world, but honestly... it didn't really click for me. It may have something to do with the two main protagonists being larger-than-life chosen ones from the get-go, rather than roles they grew into. The many antagonists you meet really aren't that special either in terms of character development, not even the final bosses of the game (that despite the true ending leave several giant plotholes behind).What the game DOES have, though, are really awesome boss battles and kickass music. Composer Eric W. Brown has gone above and beyond to make the the combat tunes real head boppers, and in each dungeon I always look forward to what cool boss will they let me rave out to next. The animations are something to behold, with sway and motion perfectly accompanied by the beats of the music, making each encounter a treat (despite some unskippable attack cinematics slowing things down, having watched them a bajillion times already).There's plenty to of collectibles to find, a fishing minigame (because all JRPGs must have them by law), a steampunk:esque boardgame and gorgeous environments to discover.It's not a flawless game by any means, but well worth the asking price if you're into JPRG-style games. Do keep in mind, however, that it's a _very_ slow starter. It'll take quite some time before the action kicks off, and even longer before it really gets into gear.

_childDocuments_.review: The pixel art in this game is among the most beautiful I've seen this year with great lighting effects to showcase the cool glowing auras of the characters and the glowing visual effects for the attacks and skills. The music seems basic at first, but as you progress in the game and the story it becomes increasingly fun. It may also be nostalgic for SNES rpg fans.    The combat is super interactive and unique and allows you to affect how much damage a move does or which targets it affects depending on where you use it by pressing certain button inputs during a move or at the right time a spell hits, etc. sort of like the mario and luigi series. In this game there are also combos and ultimate attacks, which are both special moves that you can perform in battle by building up a meter throughout. These moves typically involve performing a skill with another party member and unleashing your ultimate signature move to deal tons of damage, respectively. Mechanics like these in combat is what makes sea of stars very fun and memorable and prevents it from becoming repetitive. As you unlock new party members, progress the story, and explore new areas, you will unlock new ultimate attacks and combos to use in battle. The combat also takes place in real time rather than entering a loading screen or some flashy animation to start combat. When you engage a target, or vice versa, the characters hop into place and immediately are ready for battle. It's practically seamless and is another reason why the combat doesn't get stale, unlike some rpgs like Pokemon with its extremely repetitive and long intro random encounters.    Another cool feature is that you can cook meals in this game. Instead of your standard elixirs and potions you would normally find in other rpgs, this game allows you to cook meals at rest spots like bonfires or stoves with ingredients you have collected along the way or bought from a merchant. each meal even has amazing pixel art in the menu as you cook them, and of course their own healing and mana restoration effects. You can tell a lot of love was put into the art of this game! Little deviations like the aforementioned, from the standard formula of an rpg is what makes Sea of Stars such a breath of fresh air in the genre.    The story is really cool from the start, but picks up even further around halfway through the game to tell an epic story of all the characters you will meet. I don't want to spoil anything because it's so good, so I won't say more on it, but if you're looking for a more story-driven rpg, I 100% would recommend this game. All of the different aspects I have mentioned as well as the story cement this game as my 2023 GOTY for sure. Buy it!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a child of the SNES. And this game has all the flavours of the SNES, it's all glorious. Art, Sound, Story, Gameplay.You are about to get a very good old JRPG experience. And more. Even animated cutscenes will blow your mind.They hired Yasunori Mitsuda, the composer of Chrono Trigger, for some tunes. Speaking of it, Sea of Stars is very much influenced from the gameplay of Chrono Trigger aswell. You can do combo attacks with different characters and swap them in the same battle. There are optional quick time events for attacking and blocking that increase/decrease your damage.There are so many refreshing minor changes in the classic turn based combat system, it feels dynamic and never tedious.For example, you don't need to resurrect knocked out party members. If you can hold on long enough, they will stand up again, with decent amount of HP and are able to act instantly, before anyone can knock them out again without any chance (which is quite annoying and common in a classic RPG battle system). You are able to break enemy turns with the right combination of attacks and spells. Normal attacks are no "button mashing". Every normal hit drops "boosts" that can be collected by any character for more powerful attacks, and also regenerates your mana. The boosts are visualized beautifully, every fight is just so satisfying to watch, even if there are not that many spells and perks in the game.Sabotage nailed this game. If you have any love for pixelart, buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Sea of Stars is good from afar, but far from good.Absolutely S-tier graphics and nostalgiavibes are an excellent foundation that the game design team completely fumbled. It is full of baffling and unfun gameplay decisions, and not in a "at least they tried something new," kind of way.Level design is complex just to be complex, but not to serve any function (other than, at best, padding your hours played). For example: There will be a door to another zone, and a chest. To get to the chest, you go through a one-way drop, which serves no function other than requiring a 30 second trip the long way around to get back to the door. This happens frequently enough to be overtly intentional, and makes me silently swear at the level designer (Philippe Dionne, apparently) every time. The lock breaking system, coupled with shallow HP/MP pools offset by active MP regen makes combat a total slog that is nothing but reactive gameplay. If the game had been released in 1996, sure, maybe no one knew better at the time, but there are hundreds of case studies on how to do Chrono Trigger But Better. Similar to level design, the combat "innovations" add complexity without considering if that complexity is fun. (They aren't. They just make combat run longer.)Finally, the dialogue/storytelling also has an awkwardly padded feel. Rather than give the characters personality, they just talk 30% more than they should. Examples of this are all too spoilery to go into specifics, but it reminds me of Hallmark Christmas movie that is 2 hours long, when they clearly only needed 90 minutes to tell their story.Overall, if you really just want to scratch that nostalgia itch, and don't mind a game that has a lot of style and very little substance, picking this up for half off isn't the worst decision you can make.

_childDocuments_.review: Super Solid game.  Just like with The Messenger, developers have made a game based on old time classics with their own spin on things.  There are elements of classic RPGs from the Super Nintendo era like Chrono Trigger and Super Mario RPG while still bringing their own game play elements and quality of life.  If this game had come out around that same era of gaming, this would have easily become every bit the classic that those and others like Secret of Evermore and Seiken Densetsu have become.Story was pretty good.  There were quite a few twists that, while not unexpected, were well executed.  The only sort of gripe that stuck out to me is that this story is only tangential about the two "main characters" Zale and Valere.  This story is actually all about the third character Garl.  He pushes what feels like 90% of the story, talks the vast majority of the time, while having a large amount of the events revolve around him.  Zale and Valere show some personality early in the story, but turn into one line brick automatons (All Zale pretty much says near the end is "Hahaha"), very quickly relinquishing the story to Garl.  This is sort of fine, it just feels kind of odd how Zale and Valere have so little personality.  It is like how Tidus is the obvious main character in FFX despite the story technically revolving around Yuna's journey as a summoner, except in this case it is like if Yuna had zero meaningful dialogue.Music was pretty serviceable.  Good tunes for the most part with a few outstanding ones.  Somewhat of a lack of unique boss fight music.  Some bosses and fights get amazing ones, while others get stuck with the generic fight music.  Art is self explanatory.  It is excellently made, with plenty of different locations.  Given the Sun and Moon motif, the lighting is also quite good.Length was pretty good.  Full run takes about 30 hours to complete almost everything while exploring everywhere, with another few hours to complete absolutely everything.  Decent in-game tools telling you where you might be missing things.  Difficulty of fights was on the lower side.  Puzzles were also on the easier side.  I have tried quite a few different things and have run into absolutely ZERO bugs.  There were a few minor gameplay elements that I wish were modified a bit.  Backtracking in locations can be a pain with no quick option to leave other than walking out.  Figuring out the timings for the attacks can be a little awkward with few indicators of what the timing is aside from the few attacks that get actual prompts telling you the timing.

_childDocuments_.review: Lackluster gameplay and characters hamper on what could have been an enjoyable experience if anyone on the development team had asked is this mechanically fun and what can we do to change it.After seeing the launch trailer for Sea of Stars I wasn't too big on the art direction, but it thoroughly surprised me as I played through the game. Every area in the game (especially the latter half) are nothing short of breathtaking and I can't imagine how much time and effort went into creating such detailed art. All of these areas are only enhanced by the beautiful boss artwork and the exceptional soundtrack. Unfortunately these are the only good things I can say about the game as we move into the gameplay territory.The main mechanic of the gameplay in Sea of Stars is that it has a "timed hit" in battle akin to Super Mario RPG where you press the A button in this case to empower your own attack to do extra damage or increase your defence during an opposing enemy attack. While basic enough the window for blocking opposing enemy varies wildly due to how different enemy attack animations are in the game. Some enemies shoot a slow ball at you that may do 10% of your overall life and others have incredibly fast melee swings which due to the animations they have results in you having to delay your block for a microsecond else your block animation would run out and you would take the full hit. Not exactly fun how tight the your execution needs to be when a ton of later animations have a severe delay to them where the animation may be over your characters but the hitbox isn't active yet.Another major part of the battle system is Spells or Spell locks where you must break enemy spell locks by using the appropriate action command such as Slashing, Hammer, Poison or Solstice Magic. The spell lock system is engaging enough and is also the main source of frustration many newer players will have towards the first and second act of the game because you have next to no resources at these points in the game. Mana pools are pitiful and your party is nowhere near complete resulting in random monsters sometimes all having spell locks at the start of battle. This all results in unavoidable party wide damage which depletes your very small healing pool of spells or food. Many of the resources you will have to counteract all of this are only acquired during the final act of the game when the majority of combat may as well be over with because...Grinding is a nono in this game. Monsters in your area don't drop gold, and their exp rates for how much effort that needs to be put in for each monster pack is not worth it when monsters in the next area give 10x more exp. The only thing of value that monsters can potentially drop is cooking ingredients.. yay. At some point during the end of act 1 I felt punished for even bothering to engage with monsters in dungeons for these reasons. Their overly long attack animations, constant consumption of my materials to keep up with all the mana/hp that was lost per battle and so on all for a few hundred exp when the monsters in the area proceeding would be giving me 1500-2000 exp per pack. And the next area after that 3500-4000 and so on until the very end of the game.The final mechanics of the battle system include Live Mana and Combo Points where each spell lock broken or turn taken increases your CP gauge. Combo Points can be spent between two party members and holding a maximum of three combo points to preform stronger joint attacks that require 0 MP to use. Great but this is never expanded upon. There is no Trio combo attack in the game and what you learn is fed to you throughout the game so until you reach a certain point in the story you're stuck with basic joint attacks until the end of the game. These joint attacks can also be used to break spell locks in fewer turns as they will be using affinities between both characters such as poison, sun, luna etc.Live Mana on the other hand is handed out in battle after auto attacking an enemy monster up to a maximum of three Live Mana on the field. Boosting with Live Mana enhances the players attacks and gives their autoattacks one hit of their respective element such as Sun/Luna/Poison to help in breaking locks. If you preemptively strike a monster you gain access to a single Live Mana ball at the start of battle but the ability to consistently strike an enemy is only given to the player a few hours into the game in an odd choice by the developers. Prior to this the player has to walk within a pixel of a monster and tap the A button to hit them which is finicky as all hell. Again as with Combo Points this is the extent of the Live Mana system and it is never expanded upon.What you see within the first hour or two of gameplay is what you will be seeing for the next 25 hours. Incredibly slow animations that make Final Fantasy 9 blush, horrendous random Spell lock on dungeon monsters where all of them may have spell locks or there might be 1 instead. Combo Points and Live Mana that are never saved between battles meaning you will always have to work towards something in every battle. If you got two combo points in the previous fight and were hoping to have an incredibly high damage opener or party wide heal on your party at the start of the next battle you're out of luck. You'll forever be struggling in the opening of new encounters.The only upside of this battle system is that the boss battles are the highlight of the game. They aren't exactly hard, but they are engaging enough to be fun.... and finally the characters and story. The characters are written with a good foundation. But thats all they have going to them. Anything interesting that could happen to any of the characters never comes into play. Nobody is expanded upon. What you see during their introductions is all they will ever be. Zale is introduced as a speedster but this never comes into play during the story. Valere is the strong one of the two but this never comes into play in the story. This is a thing with every single member of the cast be it your future party members, or villains of the game. The devs write a line or two about them or hint at things regarding and none of this is used within the games story. Many of these characters are simply dropped in the games story with no conclusion to their respective arcs with the exception of one reveal late into the game. All in all as I finish the game I have 1000 questions that may never be answered because the developers conveniently dropped them all without a proper conclusion.As a backer of this kickstarter I can't say I regretted dropping cash on it. The boss battles were fantastic, the soundtrack was phenomenal and the sprite work is impressive. Unfortunately that's all there is. Everything else the game has to offer is an unfun inconvenience at best.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game with a fairly straightforward story, interesting characters and a fun innovative gameplay loop. I don't normally play JRPGs but I did enjoy this game. I did find some of the forced meta-humor to be kind of annoying..I get the feeling it was meant to be quirky tongue-in-cheek humor but it was overdone and a major eye-roller. The pirate dialog is the worst about this and luckily takes up a relatively small portion of the game. I enjoy the occasional nod towards meta jokes..not being beat about the head with them.The interactive combat is an interesting take on things and makes it a lot more interactive of a game than other JRPGs. (I say this meaning my prior experience is older Final Fantasy games). This being one of it's major strengths is also one of its weaknesses, in that it does feel like it can get to be a bit repetitive when doing combat in the later game when trying to time blocks. While it's said in the tutorial that hitting combos isn't necessary for success but rather a nice bonus to help you along..it does feel like some areas would require you to hit these skill-shots in order to actually succeed.Lastly the artifact system is quite smart. It allows you to purchase various "upgrades" that can be toggled to alter your gameplay experience to something that is more agreeable to you. They essentially work as settings options, and I think all of them are designed to make the game a bit easier to play. It's a very slick system that lets people tailor the game experience to suit them while providing an immersive and interactive way of doing so. Largely I think this is a game worth playing if you like JRPGs or are JRPG-curious. It's time well spent and there are plenty of secrets to explore. I'm inspired to find most of the collectibles which I normally don't do in games once finishing them. Overall a solid 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: What an incredible game. I am rather sad to be at the end of this game because it brought me so much happiness in the 90 hours i played it. One of the main things that really stood out for me in this game was the absolute STUNNING soundtrack that was imbued into different scenery's and different vital moments in the game. I am IN LOVE with the soundtrack, from daytime, to nighttime, to boss fights, to different locations. It was so remarkable, so very astonishing. One of the tracks i really love is The oracle of tides. What a masterpiece between the others.I really started to love the characters, especially Garl. He was such an inspirational character, so fierce and brave. It really created a special place in my heart for him. I truly do love Zale and Valere, though i feel like there was no actual development to their characters, they had little spots where I could really envision what their character would be like, but most of their character is bland and really doesn't feel as real as Garls character. It feels like there was no plot to them, plot to who they are, there was no character IN these characters. But that was really all that bothered me about it, was just that zale and valere absolutely needed more work done to their characters. I do still love them though :3Scenery was gorgeous, the side characters were amazing, especially the pirate crew, i loved them. The combat was really fun and new for me and i thoroughly enjoyed this type of game play. This game leaves a really warm feeling in my heart. It was such a great game to experience. Through the laughs, through the tears, through the fights, I loved every bit. <3 Thank you for such a breathtaking game developers, i am excited for more future work!

_childDocuments_.review: Now that was incredible. I love all the references- especially music wise- to The Messenger. The game definitely hits the mark in terms of a quality RPG. Lots of content, great storytelling, and fun combat. I see a lot of gripes about the lock system and while I can see how some people might get bored of it, I found it very interesting because it turns the combat into more of a puzzle than just picking what does the most damage. Really wish that in late-game, earlier enemies could be ignored or more easily steamrolled, but that's the only real issue I see with the game. Absolutely astounding, 9/10 for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and, unfortunately, my initial review still holds true.The game works best when you are exploring, searching for secrets, solving puzzles, fighting monsters, immersing yourself in the world and letting your imagination fill in the blanks. This is when it really reminds me of the JRPG games of the 90s.The writing isn't all bad. I enjoyed the stories that Teaks tells. However, the dialogs ruined any kind of atmosphere that the game had going for it. This was the most frustrating part for me.The images tell such an amazing story full of happiness, mystery, darkness, sadness, hope, friendship, betrayal. This game truly could have been a masterpiece.The graphics are fantastic! There are some really neat visual effects. The music and sound design is good. I enjoy the combat mechanics and the puzzles. The gameplay is solid. I like the fantasy world and its lore. The story has all the trademarks of a good RPG!What really bothers me, is that everything is written so bland. The characters look interesting, as if there might be something more to them, but there isn't. The enemies look intriguing at first, but then they seem nice and friendly. I know that there is conflict in the story because I can see it on the screen, but when all characters act so happy-go-lucky, or mildly inconvenienced by what is happening around them, I don't feel it. What's at stake here?Things happen, characters deal with it. There are a few interesting bits here and there but they are resolved rather quickly and unceremoniously, instead of leaning into them, like a real adventure would. It just seems so inconsequential.Maybe that's the point. Maybe the bad guys aren't the bad guys. Maybe what the good guys are doing is pointless. But if that's the case, why am I playing this game?If you are looking for a light-hearted and easy game to fill some time, Sea of Stars does a fantastic job! Otherwise, you might be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars, the long-awaited RPG from Sabotage Studio, takes players on an enchanting voyage through a beautifully crafted universe. Released in 2022, this game has been a highly anticipated addition to the genre, and it does not disappoint.Visually stunning, Sea of Stars boasts a breathtaking 2D pixel art style that pays homage to the classics while adding a modern flair. The attention to detail in the game's environments, character designs, and spell effects is truly remarkable, immersing players in a world that feels both familiar and fresh.One of the game's standout features is its deep and engaging storyline. Set in a world threatened by the malevolent forces of an ancient entity, players take on the roles of two young heroes, Valere and Zale, who possess unique celestial powers. The narrative unfolds gradually, drawing players into a richly developed lore and a memorable cast of characters. The bond between the two protagonists adds emotional depth to the story, and their interactions are filled with charm and wit.Gameplay in Sea of Stars combines classic turn-based combat with a unique twist. The Celestial System allows players to harness the power of the stars, adding a strategic layer to battles. This system encourages experimentation and creativity, making each encounter feel both challenging and rewarding.Exploration is a joy in Sea of Stars. The game offers a vast, interconnected world filled with secrets, puzzles, and hidden treasures. The attention to world-building is evident, as every nook and cranny feels purposeful and thoughtfully designed.The soundtrack, composed by Yasunori Mitsuda, is a masterpiece in its own right. It complements the game's atmosphere perfectly, enhancing the emotional impact of key moments and immersing players even further into the game's enchanting universe.However, it's worth noting that while Sea of Stars excels in many areas, it does have its share of minor flaws. Some players may find the difficulty level a bit uneven at times, and there are occasional performance issues on certain platforms.In conclusion, Sea of Stars is a delightful addition to the RPG genre, blending nostalgia with modern gaming sensibilities. Its captivating story, stunning visuals, and innovative gameplay mechanics make it a must-play for fans of the genre. Despite a few minor hiccups, the journey through the Sea of Stars is a celestial adventure that shouldn't be missed.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is better than 95% of the games released today, even surpassing many AAA and AAAA titles. :')All the nostalgic elements from a bygone era are here and the quality of this game far exceeds the junk that some developers are releasing in 2024.Visually the game is stunning. The atmosphere and ambiance are incredibly well-crafted across all biomes and areas. The real-time lighting work is particularly impressive and is tied directly to the gameplay, as our two protagonists control day and night as the Children of the Solstice.The difficulty curve is well-balanced with several in-game options that allow players to customize their experience to the fullest.The story and dialogue are well-written. The characters are vibrant and memorable, with a special mention to Garl, who brings genuine emotional depth to the narrative. Even the antagonists will make you smile at times, thanks to the clever references sprinkled throughout.The gameplay is excellent, with plenty of new spells, combos, characters and evolving strategies as the story progresses. This keeps the experience fresh and engaging, preventing the game from feeling too repetitive—though it can feel a bit overloaded with boss fights towards the end.The puzzles are also well-designed, with some that will really make you think. I can't count the number of well-thought-out features designed purely to enhance the player's experience. Honestly, this game is a banger—huge kudos to the development team.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, it's a pretty good game. I decided to go for it after reading other reviewers comparing it to Golden Sun; well, as much as I liked it, Golden Sun this is definitely not.Main criticism you can find about the game is:- game is too easy: quite true, combat is hardly a challenge and puzzle are almost always pretty straightforward (both are toned down a lot compared to GS). That didn't prevent me from enjoying it, but if you're looking for a challenge you may want to look elsewhere.- main characters are shallow: also true, they are basically a placeholder but I think it's intended and at least for me it worked (just like in GS).- the story is bad: while the writing isn't always top notch, I respectfully disagree. Most of what happens in the second half of the game kept me more than interested and entertained (even if some things may feel a bit rushed).- Garl is a forced character: yes and no. He's obviously over the top (and I too found him cringey at first), but he seriously grew on me and from a certain point it becomes clear he's the real star of the show, and maybe the thing I loved the most about the game.The art, on the other hand, is breathtaking. Plus, endgame quests are pretty good and the reward is so damn wholesome it made it all worth it.TL;DR: the game has its flaws, and it's not hardcore as fans of Golden Sun or other games could expect, but I spent 30 very happy hours playing it and it was enough for me.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game that reminds me a lot of old school RPGs like the Breath of Fire series, with a variety of minigames/features, such as fishing, hometown building and cooking.The graphics in this game is gorgeous, probably the best pixel art out there. I’m really surprised by how much pixel art the artist created for this game, especially at the place showing backer statues. The combat is quite unique, there are only a few skills for each character but each skill has purpose, particularly in satisfying the conditions for stunning enemies before they use their big moves. Some people might find this limiting, but I personally never got bored of the combat in this game. I wish sometimes you can escape battles though. The story overall is good, though very slow at the beginning. I can see that the writer wanted to use the first hour to establish just how different the life style between the two main characters and their mentors are as they grow up, which lead to them making different decisions, but the kids section was too long and could have been handled differently. Luckily as the adventure progresses the story gets more and more interesting with some surprising twists. There’s even a point in the game where it gave me the World of Ruin vibe from Final Fantasy 6, which is great. In terms of characters, most of the main cast are quite generic, but two do stand out for having quite good story/lore elements and reveals. The supporting NPCs are fun to have around and the final villain is quite interesting in his demeanor and motives.  Lastly, I would also like to give praise to Sea of Star’s minigame Wheels. I feel a lot of thoughts have been put into creating this minigame, and even though it has its RNG elements, I just can’t help but feel addicted to it 😊.

_childDocuments_.review: Although it falls short of the timeless excellence of classic RPGs that inspired it, Sea of Stars is an incredibly enjoyable standalone experience for someone who wants to lose themselves in that familiar and ever-desired RPG adventure. Though the main characters are only a few steps removed from being silent and featureless, the world they inhabit is anything but that. Before I get to my criticims, I'll say that the thing which stood out most to me in Sea of Stars was the art direction, as it was consistent eye candy that was accompanied by a strong world-building. The map is delightfully interactive, and gameplay is seamlessly intertwined with it (aside from a few secrets that I felt were unfair). The "modernization" of that aspect of the Classic RPG experience was excecuted incredibly well, and that was most of what kept me engaged throughout my playthrough. As far as the other aspects of "modernization," the game frequently does less with more in terms of combat.        As someone with experience in classic RPGs, I offer that there was a lack of difficulty in the entirety of the storyline evidenced by the fact that I have never once seen the game over screen throughout a complete playthrough, side content and all. In my opinion, that should be an experience reserved for people who play through the game with its provided accessibility toggles on, not the standard RPG enjoyer that the game seems made for. With the exception of a a few end-game bosses which I can likely count on one hand, it seemed to me like you had to try to game over, especially considering that you're given so many straightforward tools for success in combat the further you proceed into the game. A ways into the game, something like the combo meter becomes less of a reward for playing well and more of a tool for the player to prevent enemy encounters from ever becoming too long to be challenging. This is an example of what I meant by "doing less with more", I would have much more enjoyed the combat if I had to game over a few times in order to formulate a strategy to win against enemies or an area.        Though some would say such design is unfair, it ultimately causes the player to let go of the hand they were holding and begin to adopt their own strategies towards victory, which always feels more earned. The last thing any of the classic RPGs did was hand over easy wins to players past the tutorial stages. Even Chrono Trigger, a game that paced itself so that the player would never have to grind in order to beat the game, was far from being a game that played itself. Sea of Stars isn't egregious in its lack of difficulty, but the player never has to grind OR give much thought to how they're playing the game for the vast majority of the experience. Within a few turns of each fight, after having seen every enemy's attacks once, the choices the player needs to make are obvious. Players have and will wing it on every single fight in this game from beginning to end and beat the entire game without ever experiencing a game over like I have.         Though I have never played anything else by Sabotage, it seems like their execution of this approach to difficulty was a little cleaner in The Messenger, where mistakes arising from unfamiliarity with new mechanics could actually lead to failure. Of course, The Messenger plays much faster than Sea of Stars, but that is another reason why the approach to difficulty should be scaled up in the enemy and boss design of this game.        Difficulty aside, the other thing I felt like took a step back from classic RPGs were the characters. To be clear, I do not think the characters are bad. Not every RPG needs super quirky or layered characters on the level of narrative-driven games. There have certainly been successes in the RPG space that I suspect have spoiled people in this game's reviews, but a good RPG doesn't need super great characters. Storytelling and character writing are two very different things, and I think sabotage delivered on the storytelling front. Sabotage never needed to "modernize" the characters, but they could have taken more risks in writing the main cast, as three of main cast seem to be completely two-dimensional in the sense that they lack any flaws or motivations that go beyond their surface-level traits. These choices result in characters that are likable and sometimes very enjoyable, but not as memorable as those in RPGs that took those risks.        Those things aside, I would definitely recommend RPG newbies and veterans alike to give Sea of Stars a shot. The soundtrack for this game is exactly what players will want out of a full-length RPG, with a battle theme that never grows old and music for every occasion and mood. This game rewards the player's engagement with it and respects your time. Get Sea of Stars to take in the sights and sounds of an adventure with plenty of surprises in store. Longer-than-expected review for The Steam Awards over.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really feels like a love letter to the heart and soul of what made Chrono Trigger such an amazing game of the SNES era. The story is so much fun and enjoys poking fun at the usual game tropes. The tactical aspect of the combat keeps you on your toes and rewards you for figuring out the right sequence of attacks. Additionally, the clever ways you're allowed to adjust the difficulty is much more refreshing than selecting Easy/Normal/Hard.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute masterpiece of a game! This game scratched an itch that i thought would never be scratched as an older gamer that grew up with the earliest JRPGS.The music is amazing and on point and adds an extra layer to the great combat system and mini-game. The story sucks you right in to this fantasy world and keeps you firmly anchored wanting to know more.There were some great surprises in how this game evolved mid-game and end-game that brought a big smile to my face and sometimes a tear to my eye. The characters are well thought out and i just wanted to play them all which is hard to get right in these games. I normally just play a few and stick to those.The only minus points i can think of came from the fact that some areas where quite dark which on a Steamdeck outside on max brightness was still hard to see for a set of older eyes.All in all an absolute blast of a game and worth every cent. This game answered a question i had as a kid. "How awesome would games like this be in the future when there is way more technology available?"

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing turn-based RPGs for years and they're probably my favorite genre. This is one of the best turn-based RPGs I've played in the last decade. If you're a fan of old school RPGs like Chrono Trigger, Mario RPG, or Final Fantasy X, this is a must play game. Amazing gameplay, beautiful soundtrack, gorgeous artwork, and a very solid story. At the very least, try the demo and see what it has to offer. You will not be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: You can tell that the game is designed with lots of love. _childDocuments_.review: Amazing RPG in the style of Chrono Trigger. Game just oozes quality, from the art to the animation, to the music (which even has the composer for Chrono Trigger on a few tracks). Remember when RPGs had minigames? This game does! And the game they cooked up in this game is a joy to play. Can't recommend this enough if you enjoyed RPGs back in the 16 bit days.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is an incredible love letter to old RPG's like Chrono Trigger. I was impressed the whole time from start to finish.The gameplay is really cool and I never was bored of the turn based combat thanks of the optional timed attacks and blocking. Even more thanks to the variety of abilities you can have.The graphics are beautiful and so are the animations. The world is filled with high diversity of environments and I was always wondering where we would go next.The story is amazing, very rich and surprising, and it makes me want to see more of what they can do storywise. The characters are all also incredible and have very unique designs, I loved every one of them.I think I even don't have to speak about the music which is over incredible ( I know I say incredible a lot but it's true ). Every track is amazing.As for the duration, it took me 36 hours to get to the end and there are a lot of interesting and fun things to do on the side and I still have some left that I have to finish.All things said, I honestly haven't felt that for an RPG in a long time, I really loved it and I would very much like to see more of all that world they created. Thank you for making this game !

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is an exhilarating turn-based RPG that successfully captures the essence of classic JRPGs while offering a refreshing and engaging experience. Its captivating story, endearing characters, and innovative combat system will keep you hooked from start to finish. Sea of Stars is a love letter to the golden age of JRPGs, and a must-play for any fan of the genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm writing this having just finished the game with the standard ending. I think the game has strong characters and the writing for the most part is fantastic. I enjoyed the combat a BUNCH. For me its the highlight of turn based RPGs and this game definitely delivers. The soundtrack is fantastic really bringing the whole game to life in a way that it couldn't through the art alone. Frankly its so good that I'm considering buying the soundtrack separately just to have the files to listen to while doing other things. The wheels mini game is fantastic and like any proper RPG you can fish in it.The one major criticism I have with this game is the ending. Scrolling through comments I'm getting the impression that there's some more content I need to do in order to get the 'true' ending, but as it stands the initial ending feels even more lackluster than hollow knights initial ending. The final boss does not feel like the final boss. I went into the final dungeon expecting it to be like, the second to final boss cause its  I imagine the 'actual' ending will be much more satisfying, once again comparing to hollow knight and fighting the radiance and not just the hollow knight, another very underwhelming final boss if you only fight him. I plan on updating my review once i properly 'finish' but I figured people who might not ant to play the post-game should know what they're getting into. As of now I'd give a cautious recommendation.Edit: Finished the proper ending. Much more satisfactory. You fight who the game has been teasing you with the entire time and its MUCH more satisfying. After having finished it all the one complaint I have now is that collecting the rainbow conchs without a guide is incredibly difficult (which is needed to get the true ending), but luckily there's a few insane folks who've already gone and documented where you can find every one. Final verdict: 7.8/10 (this means its good and worth your time its just not an insane masterpiece play it but its not like, best game of all time level)

_childDocuments_.review: I don't take the time to review games very often, but I backed this game on a whim on kickstarter back in.. I think 2019? Four years later and it delivered. I almost never get 100% achievements in video games, especially on PC, but I wanted to finish every last thing this game had to offer. If you're a fan of old school RPGs, this is a must-play.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is great, but not perfect.One thing I noticed so far that I'm not too fond of is how far apart level ups are in terms of the experience points you casually get. The way it currently is, it feels almost as if every player will likely end up being at the same level at whichever point they are in the story, if they were to play the game in parallel.If I were to make my own RPG, I would normally have the bosses be harder and, for compensation, have levels be easier to grind. Like that if you die, you could at least go train and level up a bit, which, for variety, would have you fight bosses either at a higher or lower level than intended.I'm only almost 5 hours into the game, so maybe that aspect will change later.I also wish the writing was a bit better in terms of character interactions.-- Spoilers --You eventually meet a travelling historian that reads a story to your party at camp, and after the story, your party members end up not giving their input or opinions on what they thought of it when you talk to them. Another aspect I noticed is how that same historian, when she travels with you, doesn't show any reaction to the main character''s power to manipulate time after she tags along. These are some of the nitpicks that I have that I wish were less noticeable, but at least it doesn't ruin the experience for me all that much as I really enjoy everything else such as the combat, the music, and the ambience. Everything else is really good so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Great RPG. The combat is fine, the graphics are good, the music is great and while the story is ... well, the classic RPG story, the lore of the world is rather pleasant (and easily accessible).Overall I would recommends it.(By the way, while NG+ is overly easy with most early enemies being killed in one hit (assuming that you took your time in the first run), the "Artfull Gambit" Relic does make it interesting.)
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this so far - excels in art and really good in basically every other area. English localization hasn't bothered me at all, though I do see what people are saying about lack of commas and a few typos. For me it was never enough to be distracting.BUT - there are some game-breaking bugs still left it would seem. I just hit one 17 hours in where I'm locked in a battle and nothing will happen nor can I do anything but force quit the game from Steam. Granted that's 17 hours in and its the first one I've found, just a shame that I'll either have to cheese my way around this issue or wait for the bug to be fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: this is like dating someone so beautiful it takes a while for you to notice how boring their stories are, how dull and uninteresting are their conversations and how bland their overall presence is ... this game is ridiculously beautiful, but I could not go through the boring story, bland characters with child like dialogue that makes most events lacking importance ... kinda feels like harry potter without the good plot ... and sometimes you will imagine how cooler it would be if the main characters would die in a terrible death to make things at least a bit more serious and .. exciting ... but no, too many hours with no excitement besides the overly beautiful art of it all.The combat also does not help ... kinda satisfying in the beginning but then you notice it does not change much and look like more of the same like forever ...when the plot twists happen you will be already to bored oh the music is awesome as well ... so ... well, like on a bad date, maybe its me, so maybe you will learn to enjoy it

_childDocuments_.review: What a perfect game. Sea of Stars originally caught my eye because of the art style and game play, but I wasn't prepared for the many other reasons that kept me engaged and enthralled. It's as if every single inch of this game was meticulously curated and thought through to ensure a highly polished finished result. The flow of game play felt intuitive and that you were always just good enough to progress without hitting any brick walls. I loved how the dialogue was written to be concise and not time consuming to engage with, from NPCs to story-line, progress moving moments. There were some moments in combat that I think could use work (Serai's venom fury to be exact) but otherwise I always felt in control and ready to solve the combat puzzles. Although I couldn't quite get through the Gold Rank in the Arena...maybe next time. A joy all the way through.OMG and WHEELS...WHEELS!! Why did I spend hours just playing a mini-game?! I sincerely hope they build out an online function for this to play with other real-world players in the future. So much fun10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The writing and story ranges from weak to abrasive. Sometimes venturing further into the realm of seemingly disliking the common elements of the game's genre when it becomes 'meta' in an unpalatable way.The art is pretty good, and is what sold me on buying the game hoping it would live up to its polished aesthetic.Gameplay wise, the game would be fun if they didn't ruin the Paper Mario combat by not paying attention to what they were doing.To explain, the variety of 'attack minigames' is incredibly low considering it's a derivative system. They disinclude obvious easy alternatives seeing as they have a solid background of games to draw from.Considering this, the fact that there are more than a few 'repeat' minigames within the character's incredibly small skillsets, and further that these repeats are on moves that are used so often, as they are the default bread and butter attacks, is even more egregious.Compounding this and maybe the most damning, is the lack of understanding that these minigames need to work with the flow of combat as opposed to interrupting it for long periods of time. In a more polished game all combat minigames except ults should resolve in at most 5 seconds, usually less.The result of this lack of attention is that nearly every turn of every combat, you will spend 20 seconds playing the timing bounce minigame as the blue hair woman, then when the ninja girls turn shows up, you will spend 20 more seconds playing her exactly equivalent timing bounce minigame. Every fight, large and small, becomes a chore because this move is costed/balanced around being your basic all the time use magic attack. The game seems spot playtested instead of runthrough playtested, otherwise they would have realized something this abrasive was a problem immediately.Regardless, outside of them increasing the pace/limiting the duration, changing the mechanic or scaling & cost and expected use case of some of these minigames; this in addition to throwing in at least one or two varieties of mashing games, short memorization games, stick-flick timing games etc. there will remain a game ruining problem.I can't recommend the game because of just how obvious this problem is, how easy it is to solve, and how bad it is for the game experience.The gameplay becomes unfun near immediately, this because even the most pathetic weeny fight takes ages of watching yourself time A presses. These moves are so important that avoiding them would be a challenge run, and doing so would be limiting further the already miniscule pool of actions and combat minigames present.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Wholesome, joyful, sad and beautiful. Love it so much.Edit after completing the game at 100%: Sea of Stars is a beautiful pixelated adventure full of humor and love that actually made me tear up a few times.I did find the combat too easy (I only ever lost when not paying attention), and some mechanics can be exploited to make any fight a joke. I'm usually the kind of player who will discard a game that is not challenging enough, but not here.The music, the characters, the sound effects, the pixel art... Everything is so enjoyable. Easy combat does not hinder the game, especially because it offers options to render it harder as you progress, though I would have liked a general difficulty option nonetheless.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed this game for the most part, but I will say that I was ready to be done with it at around the 30 hour mark. I went out of my way to get the true ending, which requires completing one of the collect-a-thon style quests and this took way longer than I would have liked. "Get 60 rainbow conches" doesn't sound that bad on paper, but you'll probably need to do a lot of backtracking to find them all, and god help you if you don't use a walkthrough.Generally speaking, the combat system isn't the most complex thing in the world, but it's just satisfying enough to determine which party member should take the next turn, what they should do, who they should target, and so on. Additionally, I played with the Tactician's Mettle relic enabled (the game's equivalent of a hard mode). This made combat much more interesting than I'm sure it would have been otherwise, although I still didn't find it to be particularly challenging. The only times I ever lost a fight and had to reload from a save point were when I forgot to top off my party's health after a previous fight. My biggest criticism of the combat is that once you've figured it out, there's basically nothing new to be challenged by. Boss fights become more like slogs with ensured outcomes rather than tense, imposing challenges. It suffers from the classic problem of games with turn-based combat as a puzzle, meaning that the combat can be "solved."The last major criticism I have is one that's been repeated many times, and it's regarding the game's story. It's nothing offensive, but it's absolutely nothing special either. It essentially boils down to: "We have to go to A place to get B thing, so that we can then go to C place and get D thing, so that we can then go to E place..." and this is pretty much the entire game. There's a great piece of writing advice that suggests using "So Then" to bridge different parts of a plot together, instead of "And Then." Sea of Stars feels like an "And Then" story in disguise as a "So Then."Despite all of the above, as I said, I really enjoyed the game for the most part. The art style, music, animations, character designs, and cutesy dialogue really carried it for me. And it does genuinely feel like I went on a huge, epic journey with these characters. I don't feel sad that it's over, but I'm still glad to have been part of it. This game reminds me of something I would have played to death as a child, and it makes me happy to imagine other children (and adults) out there who will consider Sea of Stars to be their favorite game for many years to come.7/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The best RPG released in the last 5 years.  the visuals are gorgeous and have quickly become the background not only on my personal computer, but my work one too.  Every animation pops with personality, every island is teeming with life, every pixel feels alive.  The combat is fluid, easy to understand and fun to master, with plenty of ways to modify it for the sake of accessibility witch I find great.  The story is just as convoluted as you would expect from a pixel art JRPG, and I love it! But, by far the *Best* aspect of sea of stars is it's characters! everyone our protagonists meet is so multi-faceted and human, they all sport unique and distinguishable styles of speech and silhouettes, making every random NPC you encounter feel so much more real.  My only real gripe with the game is that the main characters - Valarie and Zale - are a little white bread when it comes to personality, it can get a bit jarring to see all of our party members - just Breathing personality and uniqueness - and then there's just valarie and Zale sitting there like "let's save the world cuz it's the right thing to do!" y'know?  Although there is a part of the game that tries to humanise them by adding a bit of tradgedy to their lives, but they don't dwell in the character's head space after that event for it to be anywhere near impactful as a character moment for Val and Zale as I feel it should've.  Sabotage Studio, you definately have created a marvelous piece of art out of pure passion for the industry and genre, and it was a welcome breath of fresh air, I can't wait to see what other marvellous projects you have in store for us next!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Was waiting for this one for a long time and am a fan of both The Messenger (A good game that went a bit odd later on) and Chrono Trigger (Still my favourite 2D RPG experience by a long way) So how does this hold up after finally getting True Ending? Pretty well in fact. It is beautiful that is for sure, and the soundtrack, much like The Messenger is amazing, even better in fact, truly top tier stuff. It is completely imitating much of Chrono Trigger, so bare that in mind as you go, but in my case that is certainly not a bad thing, though the end game 'Fated Hour' sequence doesn't remotely compare to CT. I Do have some issues. The 'Active' combat element are hit an miss. Valerie's Moonerang is fine, but hitting the correct moments for many other characters is very difficult, and Serai's Venom Flurry sucks to manage - the game either needed a proper training area or drop that mechanic completely. Some of the post game stuff is questionable also - the Conch hunting is awful, worst part of the game without a doubt and I had to resort to a guide for it. However perhaps the most disappointing thing for me was the story - not overall, it is a perfectly fine RPG story. However it felt...lightweight? It never really delved into the meat of the matter. Everything felt very superficial on the surface. Case in point is two characters (Erlina and Burgraves) whose ultimate true ending fate is a 5 second no text cut scene in the credits with no elaboration. Similarly many characters are very little more than cardboard cutouts with no real depth. As such the Story lets the game down somewhat for me, giving me a Cyberpunk vibe of not really caring at the end too much which is a shame. However I did enjoy playing it overall and much of the game is very enjoyable. Perhaps an 8/10 for the experience, but a 6/10 for any actual investment in the aftermath unless there is a sequel/dlc that actually delves into the rather thin story.Overall, Good, mostly fun to play, looks great, story is distinctly average.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is an absolute gem of a game that takes me back to the golden age of JRPGs, particularly the timeless classic, Chrono Trigger. As a long-time fan of the genre, I couldn't be more thrilled to dive into this enchanting world, and I'm ecstatic to share my thoughts on this masterpiece.First and foremost, Sea of Stars' visual aesthetics are breathtaking. The hand-drawn pixel art style is a love letter to the 16-bit era, capturing the essence of that era's greatness while elevating it to a whole new level. Every frame of this game is a work of art, and the attention to detail in character design, environments, and animations is nothing short of phenomenal. The game's vibrant and colorful world is a joy to explore, and it truly feels like a living, breathing canvas.Now, let's talk about the gameplay. Sea of Stars adopts the classic turn-based combat system reminiscent of Chrono Trigger, and it nails it beautifully. Battles are not only strategic but also incredibly engaging, thanks to the well-balanced mechanics and the ability to combine character skills for devastating combo attacks. The encounter system is also a breath of fresh air, offering players the option to avoid battles or engage as they see fit, which adds an extra layer of depth to the exploration aspect.One of the standout features of Sea of Stars is its captivating story. The game's narrative weaves a rich and immersive tale of magic, destiny, and adventure. The characters are well-developed, each with their unique personalities and motivations, and the dialogue is witty and well-written. It's evident that the developers poured their hearts and souls into crafting a story that resonates with players, much like the timeless epic of Chrono Trigger.The soundtrack deserves special mention as well. The music in Sea of Stars is an absolute masterpiece, evoking strong emotions and enhancing the overall experience. The melodies are reminiscent of the iconic tracks from Chrono Trigger, and they do an exceptional job of setting the mood for different parts of the game.As for the exploration aspect, Sea of Stars doesn't disappoint. The world is filled with hidden treasures, secret areas, and memorable NPCs, making exploration a rewarding and delightful experience. The map design is ingenious, offering a perfect balance of challenge and intrigue.In conclusion, Sea of Stars is a lovingly crafted homage to the golden age of JRPGs, and it succeeds in capturing the spirit of Chrono Trigger while forging its own unique identity. From the stunning visuals and captivating story to the strategic combat and enchanting soundtrack, this game is a must-play for both fans of the genre and newcomers alike. Sea of Stars is a shining example of how nostalgia and innovation can come together to create something truly extraordinary. Don't miss out on this modern classic that will undoubtedly stand the test of time.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars, like The Messenger before it, is doing an homage to a specific genre in a specific era and does it very well. Sea of Stars is a retro 2D turn-based RPG. You travel around a beautifully detailed world, fighting monsters, solving puzzles, and collecting items and resources. The game looks excellent, everything is colorful and animated immaculately. It's hard to explain that something so old-school still feels epic when you pull off a special move in a fight, but once you get the different character's ultimates, every one of them goes absolutely bananas. Over time, the combat can get a little repetitive and there isn't as much customization as some big fans of turn-based RPGs might like, but it never really gets too old or tedious to the point of frustration.The overall story is a little strange at points but the core friendship of Valere, Zale, and Garl anchors the whole thing. The world you travel around has a lot of unique locales, peoples, and lore, that feel different than most standard fantasy worlds. All the characters are fun and somehow feel old-school but also modern. Garl was definitely my favorite, which surprised me given my initial impressions. He really gets to grow and go places throughout the course of this game.There is a lot of good balancing between nostalgia and modern sensibilities in Sea of Stars, it's a real magic trick sometimes. Traversing the levels is a great example of this. I played a lot of old RPGs and the fact that many don't have the quality of life updates we've come to expect, something as simple as a run button, makes me very reluctant to go back to them. In Sea of Stars, you don't have a run button, but hear me out! Even without that, you're climbing, jumping over gaps, zipping across platforms, it takes the roughest part of old-school RPGs and makes it great. That being said traveling around the overworld can be a little slow but it does get better as the game goes along.The last big thing I have to mention is the music. The music in this game is incredible, similar to The Messenger. And as a bonus, every track has an alternate version played by a band in every inn you enter.Overall, I think Sea of Stars will be most appealing to people who already have an affinity for this type of game, but it also would serve as a good intro to people who haven't played turn-based RPGs before since it sands down a lot of the rough edges in the genre and makes everything else very pleasant. I'm definitely excited for what these developers do next, whatever it is.

_childDocuments_.review: You can probably already tell from screenshots and trailers but the pixel art is fantastic, and the soundtrack is great. However, the game kind falls flat when it comes to the story, and it uses the combat as a crutch by having you doing fights more than anything else. The combat itself is fine but not exactly fun enough to repeat it over and over again. Exploration and any other game mechanics take a back seat. You'll see some puzzles and mini-games but they're nothing special. It's a passable experience with great art behind it. I'd get it on sale. Still some impressive work from a studio with only one other game. What's here is very polished and tightly designed, even if I didn't enjoy every aspect of it.

_childDocuments_.review: -NON-SPOILER REVIEW-I just finished playing this game then 100%ing it and all I would like to say is... please give the game a shot.Sea of Stars is a JRPG heavily inspired by old school JRPGs from the 90s and early 2000s. If you're familiar with games like Chrono Trigger/Chrono Cross, Golden Sun, and Secret of Mana then you should feel right at home. It's a love letter to the genre and the price to time spent playing makes this worth your while.-THE GOOD-Storytelling: This is a story with high fantasy elements and environments. As a quick summary, your two starting characters are known as Solstice Warriors, guardians who's goal is to protect and eradicate the world of Dwellers, world ending monsters. You'll have obstacles and characters who you'll meet along the way, learn new moves, defeat monsters, etc. Usual JRPG formulas. The plot is engaging even during side quests and the characters you meet have a wide variety of personalities that really make you feel attached to them. It's an overall charming and enticing world and each area feels like it's own. Gameplay: -The maps and overworld serve their purposes well. Inside maps, your movement is pretty smooth and unrestricted (you don't move in a grid) while you can climb walls, hop ledges, swim, and move objects. You will also get upgrades that enhance and compliment these map elements which will be needed to progress further. -Battle System is easy to understand with some added depth that rewards the player for executing it well. Pressing a button during specific timings will give you extra damage and perks if done correctly much like Super Mario RPG or Paper Mario. There will also be times where an enemy will begin "casting" an ability and you have to perform specific types of attacks or elements to interrupt it or risk taking bigger damage. There is a toggle you can enable to let you know when you time these correctly to help build muscle memory as well.-For the collection aficionado, there are tons of treasures and hidden items to find in maps ranging from valuables to equipment upgrades.Art: Very fluid and animated pixel art helps make the world pop out. Just from running around with your party, you can see fluid limps, hair bouncing, fabric moving. Buildings and environments are heavily detailed keeping you immersed wherever you are. This becomes especially apparent when you fight huge bosses with loads of particles and animations and you start seeing so many details put into the animation and sprite work.Music: Renowned Composer Yasunori Mitsuda and Eric W. Brown were in charge of the music for the game. One big thing you have to have in a JRPG is a catchy and memorable battle theme as its likely going to be the song you hear the most in the game. They absolute met this goal. The music fit the environments and themes when needed and certain songs just stay stuck in your head.Side Content:-Outside of the main plot, the side content and plotlines easily add an extra 10-15 hours. They put in quite a bit of extra content for people to focus on if they wanted to take a break.-There is a lot of things to collect as mentioned above, ranging from fishing to food ingredients for cooking.-Wheels. Whats a JRPG if it doesn't have its own built in minigame? This is a table game popular throughout the world of Sea of Stars with easy to understand rules that make it fun to play and keep on going back for rematches. -THE NOT-SO GOOD-Storytelling: The plot while engaging and the characters are charming, it unfortunately at times falls into JRPG Trope Pitfalls. Certain decisions are questionable, certain plot points are either forgotten or tossed aside for the sake of progression and certain times, the story will really take an unexpected turn that feels out of place. but nothing that I personally feels takes away from the overall experience. Gameplay: -With the battle system and puzzles mentioned above in mind, the difficulty is minimal to none. You need basic common sense to beat the battles, but these really revolve around "hit X first, not Y and block correctly". The game has an overall death counter and I only died once in the beginning of the game. The abilities you learn and the stats you gain are heavily balanced in favor of the player so you feel somewhat overpowered especially by the end of the game. This isn't a bad thing! This was likely an intended design choice but I personally never felt like I had a difficult time with the base difficulty. -I mention base difficulty because you get key items very early on that essentially toggle an easy mode/hard mode (more/less damage taken/dealt, passive healing, etc). The problem I personally had was that the "hard" toggles felt brutally unforgiving and was difficult for the sake of being difficult, not actually challenging. I don't have a problem with the easy toggles since certain players just want to enjoy the ride. -The puzzles were very simple to solve outside of a select few that had me racking my brain for a couple of minutes. It's very trial and error based, usually involving pressing a switch or moving an object from point A or point B. Again, this was likely an intended design choice for people who just want to enjoy the ride of the story. Certain obstacles aren't really puzzles as the answer is given to you either by talking to an NPC or your party figuring it out for you.Side Content:-Sometimes there might be TOO much collecting. I'm not joking when I say this is a collector's dream game, to where it sometimes feels like a slog since certain items are simply fluff to sell or you found something already better.-Wheels. It's fun, terribly balanced though. The games and pieces look to be designed with a Rock/Paper/Scissors system in mind but certain units simply bypass that system through their passive abilities. Not enough units either.Overall, the game is phenomenal, but it doesn't go without its flaws. These flaws do not take away from the overall experience and the game's music/art/battle system is still very enjoyable and I consider this one of my favorite JRPGs to date.

_childDocuments_.review: sea of stars is the most okay game iv'e played this year. the combat system, the story, the world, it all just feels so bland. there's like one fun fight and one good character, and absolutely nothing remarkable in between them. i can't think of better way to describe my problems with the plot than "things just kinda happen". your'e told go somewhere, and then something mildly interesting but usually unimportant happens, and your'e told to go to next place. i also feel like the game just can't decide what tone it's going for. if you've played the messenger, the previous game by sabotage, sea of stars is like that just often enough to prevent any sort of serious tone from emerging. the writing is also very bland, which for the most part prevents you from getting any sort of emotional attachment. the protagonists don't have any personality whatsoever besides the typical "hero" traits. but then occasionally, they'll talk about something that had happened in the past where they acted totally differently, but you just feel really confused because as previously stated, they haven't been characterised to have any personality at all in the actual events of the game! on to the combat system, each character only has about five different thing they can do in battle, and although there's technically a bunch of different combo moves, you barely ever actually get to use them. there is no synergy, no builds, and barely any strategy to battle. again, if you've played the messenger, you'll remember the quite frankly brilliant way that game was structured. well, sea of stars is completely linear. how 88% percent (as of the writing of this review) of players enjoyed this game will forever remain a mystery to me. i wouldn't buy sea of stars for 10 bucks, let alone the 34 they're charging. if a jrpg is what you're looking for, please try octopath traveler 2 instead.

_childDocuments_.review: You can feel Chrono Trigger all over this game. A little bit of Golden Sun as well. The visuals are incredible, the combat is simple but satisfying, and the puzzles are rewarding (speaking as someone who is genuinely bad at puzzles). The story is pretty standard, the pacing feels pretty good as well, but the true star of the show are the characters. Especially Garl. I recommend this to anyone looking to feel the nostalgia of older turn based RPGs of this style. You will feel right at home.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars in general was a great game as someone who is a big fan of these turn based RPGs. The art and music are beautiful and there were key moments where the story got me feeling emotional (won't spoil). However the ending fell a bit flat for me and took that 10/10 experience to more of an 8/10. I still recommend the game but the end was disappointing story wise and in difficulty. I also think character development was shallow in our heroes and that side characters had a lot more personality. I appreciate the ties to The Messenger and I'm sure it was exciting for fans who played both games. But for myself it was disappointing that some loose ends do not get tied up if you do not know about The Messenger and that it wasn't just a few easter eggs connecting them. So as someone who played just Sea of Stars I was confused on what happened to some characters. I still love the game and it gave me a wonderful sense of nostalgia and absolute joy that I haven't felt in a long time playing games. I just wish it gave more at the end. I never wrote a game review before but I felt really strongly about this one.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game's a good time. The relic system is great if you want to play either story mode or a challenging but rewarding combat mode. Levels and puzzles are quick to navigate/get through and the story just makes you feel like a kid again. It's fun and heart warming! The one in-game achievement that's worth getting (if achievements ain't your thing) is collecting all the rainbow conches to unlock the true ending.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is one of those games that banks on a saturated 90’s JRPG nostalgia market but it sets itself apart from others pretty damn well in terms of quality.Gameplay is not as groundbreaking in terms of innovation but it makes up for it through engaging story, beautiful artwork and amazing music.Overall, I enjoyed my time with Sea of Stars just like how I enjoyed the JRPG’s of old like Chrono Trigger, FF3, and Golden Sun.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Nice collection of mechanics and tropes, taking me back to so many great games I've played: Chrono Trigger & Chrono Cross for sure, but there's also a Suikoden mood in the visuals, and a very generic feel to the story in general. Great humor and some very clever use of environments, nice and organic level design and puzzle design.I love the nice touches like the cooking mechanic being about an experience instead of a tedious "mini-game". I prefer an approach like this, where I'm repeatedly going through nice moments brought by the quality of the experience itself, not just grinding my teeth on difficulty to prove my worth. When it's time to fight, combat mechanics are fluid and responsive, if somewhat repetitive even after a few hours. Difficulty is well-balanced in my opinion and some fights are quite exciting! Not sure if I will go through the whole game yet, since it's VERY reminiscent of the source material it takes its inspiration from. Don't get me wrong: it feels like a good experience! But after playing a whole lot of JRPGs my entire life, this particular game doesn't stand out from others and seems to stay very close to them, almost to a fault. My main problems are the repetitive nature of combat and the seriously stupid plot and story. Without spoiling anything, the arrival to Brisk for example is really just ridiculous and would not even be a good plot point in a kids' game. Even Suikoden IV was more believable than that, for those who pushed themselves through this particular ordeal at some point in their gamer life. So Sea of Stars IS an enjoyable JRPG, very true to its roots and also improving on key mechanics in fresh and satisfying ways! It is very repetitive and not well written, but If someone is looking for an introduction to turn-based JRPGs, this could be a good entry point in the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This is by far the best game I have played this year, a year of great releases.  It scratches the itch of playful nostalgia and a need of a comfy kick back and de-stress game.  The story has been fantastic, the music and colors of the pixel art are a joy to be withheld.  I'm glad this game exists, we need more of them.  If you love games like Mario RPG, Chrono Trigger, etc you will very much enjoy this title.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: If Breath of Fire III and Mario & Luigi had a baby, this game would approximately be what is made out of it.By far its best quality has to be the gameplay, with options for so many different things to change your experience (either easier or harder difficulties) and though there is an achievement related to one of these settings, all in all it doesn't seem exactly balanced to have those turned on from the start unless you're willing to spend quite a few hours in the beginning stages grinding (since levels are so hard to come by in this game). But it still manages to be fun, all up until the final boss where for some reason they decide to make a bullet hell segment which doesn't really fit thematically into anything and is just kind of...there.The animated cutscenes are hit and miss, they start off pretty weak but as the game goes on definitely raise their quality. As with the writing as well, but the story gives a completly different feeling. While it definitely got better around the third island, I noticed most of the beginning story was actually better on a second playthrough and leaves a lot of context lacking on the first playthrough. Which is rather strange to say the least, but thankfully the latter three quarters of the game is good enough to be actually worth it even if you're not willing to replay the game anytime soon.The two main characters are kind of just there, and what we're really playing is Garl's story for the most part. Usually when people say a character grows on you, I never actually expect it to happen. So when Garl did grow on me, it was the strangest feeling. A good one, though, since I really enjoyed most of his scenes later on (and even more so the second time through). Not sure I'll ever like the pirates though, aside from Keenathan.As for less specific criticisms, some mechanics do feel like they've been put into the game but simplified a lot to the point where what it actually does just pales in comparison to their original counterparts. The fishing is very basic, the town building isn't actually a minigame like older RPGs tended to have, and most of the levelling/character building is incredibly simplistic and more relies on specific accessories and relics equipped rather than the stats you chose on level-up.The game is at least very enjoyable by most accounts, but not quite on the level of its predecessors -- though it is clear the direction they wanted to take was this one. A shorter experience made to remind you of 90's-era RPGs that doesn't drag on for too long or overstay its welcome. With enough characters in it to make at least something about it unique, having many elements of "I tangentially recognise where this idea probably comes from" meshed inbetween.For the price, I'd recommend it if that is something you're looking for.
