_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is a love letter to 90s JRPGs. Conveniently, the Super Mario RPG remake also came out in 2023 and is a good reference point, though the biggest influence here is clearly Chrono Trigger. The visual design is as close as you could reasonably get without bringing on Akira Toriyama to do the character designs. And they actually got composer Yasunori Mitsuda to do some guest tracks. That said, under the nostalgic veneer the game has clearly availed itself of modern amounts of disk space as it's packed full of custom sprite work and far more music than those old JRPGs could ever have hoped to fit in a SNES cartridge.Mechanically, the game does preserve a couple of Chrono Trigger conventions, but ultimately seems to take most of its lessons from Square-Enix's more recent efforts in the genre, particularly Bravely Default and the HD-2D series. They then inject a few of its own ideas into the mix and the result eventually settles into a fun rhythm, though I wish they'd shaken things up a little in the late game as the rhythm had become just a little too comfortable by then. Or perhaps I should've tried tightening the difficulty options.Story-wise, I found Sea of Stars to be most effective for me when it was ushering its protagonists between memorable set-piece fights and surprising plot twists while foreshadowing more to come. Having so much more room for art and music than those old JRPGs really helps here, as the game can leverage them to make each place feel new and unique. This helps bring atmosphere to individual dungeons and those boss fights set pieces, and the contrast between them as we switch from place to place builds a strong sense of forward momentum.Conversely, I felt the story was at its weakest when it didn't have that momentum. It takes a little while to build up from the start of the game, and the side-quests in the endgame feel very much like side-content and removed that sense of momentum. After them, the final dungeon isn't long enough to re-build that momentum before hurling you into an ending that can feel a little abrupt. That said, given the light adventure tone the game strikes there's only so much you can expect.Overall, it's a fun JRPG with some great set-pieces that generally moves at a good clip. Genre fans will almost certainly enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Good Stuff-Great visuals: The environments looked great and the sprites were really well animated.-Music: Loved the soundtrack.Neutral Stuff-Story: The story was okay for the most part but it definitely borrows a lot from games like Chrono Trigger for some of its twists. It also takes a while to really get going.-Exploration and Dungeons: The movement in the game feels really good and I really like the grappling hook you get later in the game. Unfortunately, the dungeons are very linear and are lacking in secrets to find. There are some puzzles to do but they are stupidly easy. Thankfully you move through it so quick that it didn't bother me too much.The Not so Good Stuff-Characters: The two main characters have zero personality. They are basically cardboard that talks. Their friend Garl is annoyingly positive and upbeat. The other party members you get along the way are better but it doesn't make up for the first three being so bad. NPC characters are hit or miss. There was one that frequently broke the fourth wall and I really hated it.-Combat: The combat system is okay for the most part but I have a few issues with it. After the first few hours where you learn how to play, the combat really stagnates and doesn't change much for a really long time. Each of your characters starts with two skills and you don't get new ones for a long time. There are these combo attacks where two characters team up to perform a more powerful attack. Most of the new stuff you get during this stagnate period are combo moves. A lot of them aren't very useful and I never used half of the ones I found. When you do finally start getting more skills, you get a few special moves that are easy to exploit and they make boss fights pretty trivial. I beat the final boss and only had to heal twice.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of ​​Stars is a “retro-inspired turn-based RPG,” as Sabotage Studios presents it. As I will show below, it has beautiful pixel art, mechanics that refresh the genre and a story that captivates you. Not in vain has it won the award for best Indie game of the year at the Game Awards.In a JRPG, movement is not the most important factor, but the level design -which I will talk about later- makes it very dynamic. As seems to be dictated by the rules of the genre, we will also have a couple of vehicles as the plot progresses that will facilitate our passage and access to new areas. Some jumps that give a touch of platforms (although automated).The camera is static, a traditional top view in the style of Final Fantasy or classic Pokémon. The most interesting point is that there is no transition between free play and combat, making it more dynamic.The game, outside of combat, does not use UI to let the artistic section shine with its own light. The combat menus are very intuitive. In addition, there are some sections that are introduced into the narrative, such as orbs to enhance attacks, in true Dead Space style. The pause menu is also very intuitive and clear, making it easy to navigate.Sea of ​​Stars draws on the mechanics of previous games like Mario RPG or Chrono Trigger. He does not hide when doing so, he recognizes it and refreshes and improves them by adapting them to our time. It also introduces -again following the instruction manual of good JRPGs- a very elaborate minigame.The navigation at a narrative level is excellent, revealing elements on the map that you cannot use and for which you will have to return later, giving the player the possibility of going to optional areas and with very elaborate maps.The enemy design is very good. The area bosses present certain puzzles and strategies that, although simple to understand, complicate the game a little. On an artistic level they are fantastic, with the most careful designs, from the first monster you face to the final boss (the first one and the one in the postgame).This is perhaps one of the negative points of the game. Getting gold is more complicated than in real life. The only way to get money fast is to play spinner and it's not really that fast. The monsters only drop ten gold coins at most and in the end the player feels like they fall a little short. In my case, I have farmed a lot and even then I have had to spend hours fishing to get one or two gold coins per fish.This is one of the points in which Sea of ​​Stars and, actually, the work of Sabotage Studios stands out. Each level presents several paths, some optional, others that open after completing certain tasks. In general its levels are a master class on how it should always be done.JRPGs are not particularly replayable except, perhaps, Pokémon. However, this video game has a system of relics that can greatly transform the mechanics and ultimately the video game being played. Therefore, it could be replayed several times trying different relics.The game performance is quite good. Without being too demanding, sometimes many elements are put on the screen and, in general, it runs quite smoothly. Only on one occasion did it drop below 60fps.The only bug I have found is already fixed in the new update. It was in the sea of ​​​​nightmare, that the game could crash and you could not continue the adventure.The blocking and critical system is a delight. Everything is very well measured. Some enemies and abilities are difficult to catch but it always feels fair because there is always the possibility of finding when the right moment is.Regarding the difficulty, I must say that it is not very demanding, but it also allows itself to be a challenge at times. Not even the optional postgame bosses are a big problem.Regarding the soundtrack, Yasunori Mitsuda has simply participated. They create incredible themes with variations depending on the time of day the protagonists are. In addition, they remastered some songs from The Messenger and it looks great. 10/10. Another high point of the video game: the art design of the stage, that of the characters, the animations, the skills, the combat. There's not much to say when what you do is simply excellent.The plot is very good. It has certain twists that the player does not expect. Others that are expected but are treated with such grace that they look very good. The characters are wonderful and you manage to empathize a lot with them, especially with some like Garl or Seraï. They all have a lot of charisma.The Spanish translation (which is the one I played) is not particularly good, and has quite big errors such as calling Cunaluna fish pie “pie de pescado de Cunaluna”. There are many translation errors that hinder the enjoyment of such a brilliant game.This game is literally based on taking RPG tropes and twisting them, parodying them or emulating them, as the writer feels like it. It is noticeable that before writing the game they have dusted off their old JRPGs to play them and give us the best possible experience, with many breaks of the fourth wall. Literally. In conclusion, Sea of ​​Stars is a very good game that, if you are a JRPG lover, you should take a look at. Everything he does he does well, and in some things he even excels. The small mistakes it has do not even make a shadow in the light of its successes.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games of the year, here's why.The gameplay is an ode to some of the best back in the days RPG's like Chrono Trigger and Final Fantasy.The soundtrack is some of the best, I sometimes found my heart pumping while in a boss battle and suddenly THAT beat drops. The music sets the tone perfectly for what you are doing at that specific moment.The combat introduces a fresh puzzle-like take on the old turn-based formula. Feels like your choices matter and you get rewarded for perfecting your timed skills with extra-damage or less damage received.The story is amazing so far. Twists and turns. Characters that you love and root for. Characters that disappoint you. Characters that surprise you. Backstabbing, support and heartfelt emotion.Graphics are what you would expect. Pixelized beauty with super attention to details. You can even see some reactions in the characters faces. There's different biomes like florests, towns, bad guys lairs and even some sea travelling!Pros:- Innovative formula while fighting in a turn-based game;- The OST is so so good that I will need to add it to my Spotify;- The story is immersive and you find yourself rooting so much for the main characters;- Travelling through the world while unlocking traversing skills is so satisfying, climbing, jumping, discovering secret chests etc.- The mini-puzzles around the world are so original and make you really think about the stuff you need to do! Cons:- Levelling doesn't seem to impact too much the fighting experience, and I sometimes would find myself trying to decide on which stat to level;- Cooking takes a lot longer than it should, feeling like a chore for no reason at all;Conclusion: Sea of Stars is one of the best games I've played this year. It totally deserves all the praises it's been getting. It leaves me wanting more of the same. I rate it a solid 9,5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good game. Fun spirit, great exploration (traversal was always fun, and the animations are so well done for every different thing you do), and the combat.... Ooooo, the combat. So much more than your standard "select attack, watch animation". Timing is everything, and perfecting it is oh-so-satisfying. When you land that perfect hit, reflect your 30th Moonerang, block that crucial attack or you would have gone down... The game flat out lies when it says you don't need to learn to do the timing, unless you're using the relics to ease up on the difficulty a little. Which, I loved. Maybe one night you're playing, and you just wanna have fun without worrying, click them on for a while and pop them back off later. Or, in one particularly... Questionable portion of the game... You'll know. -_-While it wasn't as long as some of the JRPG's of yore, I think the game length was perfect for it's story. There's a few tidbits you'll notice if you know the studio's other game, which were nice. I think if they continue making games in the same "universe" and spice in some more crossover info, that'd be really neat.Being a completionist can add a fair bit of time, especially without looking up a guide for some of the stuff, cuz... I definitely never would have found some stuff without it the first time through.All in all, if you want a fun, mostly laid back game with a few twists and turns, and some potentially thrilling combat if you're into it, 1000% would pick this up.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Hey, I fully completed this game back in September and Steam Awards needs us to support our favorite games.  This is me telling you to go buy this and complete it.  It is such a beautiful game that brings a bunch of your favorite JRPG mechanics from years past into one seamless package.  While you are at it, make sure to show your support on the nominations page.  They've put their hat in the ring with the, "Outstanding Visual Style Award," but you can add them to any category you'd like by manually searching it.I'll see you... in the Sea of Stars.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: It was a tough call whether to recommend this game or not because I really WANTED to recommend. I WANTED iit to be something i could talk about with my friends and significant other. Rather than just disappointment lol.  After 100 percenting the game, and unlocking all secrets, Hoping for some sort of reason to push me over the edge on whether to recommend it.Pros:- Pretty- Music is pretty good- Combos are funCons:- Just WOW bad storytelling, it was so bad it was cringe-Zero character development, zero personality-Puzzles a 3 year old could put together- Once you unlock the barrage combo and sarais interupt attack plus rashans ultimate, you just stunlock bossesEven on the final boss im pretty sure i used like 2 heals? and that was it....- What is even an endingWhat it comes down to is its pretty to look at and pretty to listen to, but thats it. Nothing else.Zero immersion .Sabotage studios, please hire a storyteller to give you at least the basics next time. Lots of game studios are doing it now, 100 percent would not play again lol. BUT i prob will listen to boss soundtrack. Because that was fire.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Comparing this to Chained Echoes, I am just going to say Chained Echoes was the better game. Theres 3 major flaws with this game. Collecting the Conchs for the True Ending, the back tracking is a slog with the linear levels, and the lack of combat options. Every single fight is the exact same end game. The True Ending boss was way too easy as with most this game. The + side of this game is its amazing pixel art for the attack animations and a godly soundtrack, but it does fall short it terms of exploring and combat. 6.5-7/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time playing this game. I picked it up after watching some streamers play it, and it reminded me a lot of Golden Sun, one of my favourite game series to play growing up.The storytelling is fantastic. The main plot stays serious and meaningful, the character interactions and side content provide levity to break up the mood and add a lot of charm.The combat system is really fun! I enjoy the team member swapping, the strategy around breaking enemy locks to nullify big attacks, and the revival system. The difficulty level is not high, but the fights are still engaging.Loved the various side content sprinkled throughout the game. I always had my eye out for loot chests as I explored, the Wheels mini-game was super compelling, and it was awesome building your own little town.Big recommend if you are nostalgic for old era RPG's.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I can't say I have many original thoughts that have not been spoken already in the reviews, but... this game would be a 10/10 if I cared about the main characters in the slightest. They always agree upon everything, there's no conflict between the two of them, everything just happens to them as a pair.I didn't grow up with Chrono Trigger as a millennial, but I DID grow up with Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga, which has a very similar play style. If I may compare the two to strictly story, I'd rather take completely silent Italian plumbers over anything these two have to say, really.I think fans of the glorious Chrono Trigger will be disappointed - but fans of Mario & Luigi might be in for a treat.That being said, I thoroughly enjoy the gameplay, the combat, the puzzles, Wheels, everything else! I think that those aspects will help me to see the game through.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of stars has a ton of things to like. The music is fantastic, the gameplay is very entertaining, the art never gets old, the over arching plot remains overall fairly interesting. BUUUUUTTT, there is a huuuuuuuge issue i have with this game, the dialogue and characters. My god, the characters are a CHORE to listen to despite there being no voice acting. The dialogue is the most one dimensional I have probably ever seen. I still definitely recommend this game, but for some people the dialogue will be a deal breaker so keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Do give this a try, the 25-40 hour journey is worth it, especially if you like Golden sun exploration wise. Combat is more like Mario and Luigi RPG and starts off a bit slow but it makes sense considering the mobs' attack pattern later into the game. Everything clicks more pacing wise around the 5-6 hr mark imo. Loved the writing for the characters too. Probably will play on NG+ with the ardent amulet cause the gameplay grew on me.Easily one of my top 5 RPGs now.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A huge adventure, that's both comfy  and saddening , with boss battles that are equally fun and challenging , the wheels mini-game , having you challenge different players as you discover the world, and the amazing short animated cut-scenes you encounter occasionally throughout the story.Having some nice and convenient travelling mechanics allowing you to easily back track and travel through the world as you're closing in to the end of the adventure. This made me feel like I was a kid again , uncovering quests by talking to ever character in the game and absorbing all the details in the game, and in aww with the amazing pixel art that brings each area alive and little easter eggs? Well some amazing fun spontaneous events that happened through the game , that pleasantly surprised me each step of the way, making me want more and more, along with that, some soothing music and a camping mechanic to take a break and save for another day. It was quite the adventure for me, and has me looking for another experience like it :D .
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I'm a sucker for well done pixel graphics. And this game doesn't disappoint.From funny character quirks and jokes that last even till the end of the game, to the feel of old school Mario and Luigi RPG games combat, moves and combos, this had me hooked from the start and kept me there my entire play through.I bought, played and 100%ed the game within 2 weeks across 55 hours. (4 hours a day)Music is a bop at times and I will definitely listen to it casually.Story can be a bit dragging but its not as bad a others make it out to be. Its a heart-warming story with lovable characters.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best RPG's available. i would recommend buying at full price to support the devs. I bought into this because of the pixel artwork initially. but the story and battle system really took me. It doesn't take long to get into the story, but it takes a little bit to get into the battle system. The choices you make in battle might be repetitive, but the enemy's make it interesting. Although you might think there's a lack of skills/combos, there is a perfect selection between the characters abilities/swap option to make you think and counter your enemy. I wasn't too satisfied with the end, but looking forward to the second game,
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The more I play this, the less I enjoy it.  It's been 20 hours of absolute linear exploring so far. Even when you're finally given access to "explore" the world, you either can't enter any area other than the single area you're meant to go to, or you can enter it and do absolutely nothing past the first screen since you're not meant to go there yet.Along with what many others have posted, the writing is awful. It's not even average, or passable. It's very, very sub-par. I think I may lose my mind if I see one more "Hahaha!" It's worse than the "..." ones.Combat sucks too. You're gradually given more ways to act in battle and more to deal with, but none of them are fun.  They're basically much worse versions of the games they're borrowed from.Wheels also sucks by the way.  I love minigames, and spent probably equal if not more time playing Triple Triad than the actual game (FF8).  But even if the CPU didn't absolutely CHEAT, there's no meaningful rewards to playing a single game in each tavern.  By the way, yes, it absolutely cheats.  It consistently gets a triple+exp roll, sometimes even a couple per turn... and I've never even seen a single one of those in my reel. Total trash.Where are the side quests by the way??Next Chrono Trigger, lol.  The closest this comes to CT is the line "Mountains're nice" which they put in the game verrrrry early on to try and trick you into believing it's a good game. But it's not.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Combat +Soundtrack ++Level Design +++Sea of Stars is throwing me back to the good ol' days of Chrono Trigger, Super Mario RPG, and Paper Mario! The maps look and feel fantastic to explore with lots of secrets and reasons to backtrack later. The combat is fast paced but very interactive, and I even feel pressured during many of fights against regular enemies - yet the option to ease combat IS there for people who don't enjoy the challenge as much.The writing and story are hard to judge at this point as I'm still just getting into the meat of the game, but I've had quite a few good laughs so far and can't wait to see what happens next!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: It feels like pass the torch moment from Chrono Trigger-SupermarioRPG to current generation, respecting the OG but still create their own magic.The developer got it right in terms of focusing what's important in this type of game.We may left wonder what to be improved in this kind of genre, what can make a better improvement, or what feature could be added, but in this current design, this game just done it.Story wise, art direction wise, and gameplay wise, they just delivered all the promise.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars could very well be a title that re-ignites the JRPG passion for many people.It is a one-of-a-kind experience, and the closest game that resembles it, is the legendary SNES title and masterpiece, Chrono Trigger.I've enjoyed the demo and was lucky to have access to a press release prior to launch, thx to a friend of mine.After around 40–50 hours of gametime, I can confidently say that Sea of Stars is a MUST-PLAY title for every JRPG lover and anyone who wants to get into this genre.Pros:+ Serves as great entry title into the JRPG genre.+ Battles feel fresh and engaging, even after tens of hours.+ The graphics are awesome, it has a charming and unique art style.+ Does not force you to grind for endless amounts of hours to overcome difficult confrontations.+ The game has its very own charming character, which sets it apart from generic titles with no identity.Cons:- The only minor con that comes to mind is that Sabotage Studio might have overdone themselves by trying to capture the magic of the 90's JRPG's too much. Some NPC's you encounter have only a few words to say, this makes them unfortunately appear shallow at times.I can't wait to have multiple playthroughs and go for 100% achievements on Steam.Thanks, Sabotage Studio, for this outstandingly amazing game! <333
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Loved it, comfortable and smooth playing experience. Not extraordinarily difficult, but options to increase difficulty come up later in the game. Wheels is my favourite minigame ever, possibly, and I hope it goes standalone. Music is a vibe, silly dialogue is enjoyable, and references to the Messenger throughout were really pleasant. Early on I was not enthused by the story, but found I really loved it by the end (especially the true end). Worth the play, without a doubt.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: + Amazing OST.+ Combat feels nice and dynamic, with each character bringing something unique to the fight.+ High quality pixelated artstyle and animations (but this one is up to personal preference).+ Loads of variety (enemies, their attacks, environments, ...).+ Relics (settings that are toggable) adjusting gameplay, making it easier/harder for those who want to adjust their challenge.+ The story is amazing. Very silly at times, but often also very serious. I both laughed and cried. The story was also way longer than I expected it to be, which was a nice surprise.+ The achievements make sense. You earn almost all achievements by 100% completing the game.- There is a single achievement which requires quite a bit of skill in timing hits and blocks, which makes 100% completing the achievements quite hard.- The hint system for missed treasures tells you which zone a treasure is in, but at times it might be nice to have a more precise location because some zones are quite big.- Travelling back to previous zones can be quite tiresome, since you have to go through other zones if those are on the only path to the zone you are trying to reach. This game exceeded all my expectations. From the moment I started playing I was hooked on the story, the characters, the artstyle, the OST, ... . It took me about 45 hours to do a 100% playthrough of the game. Even when not playing the game, I now find myself sometimes whistling some of the songs from the game. Definitely worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The combat is boring. Too simple, not engaging. It's not about killing enemies; it's about using attacks with specific traits to 'prevent' enemy attacks, and killing them as a result along the way. It feels very tedious, like I'm not able to actually use strategy, but rather I just select the correct attacks to check the little boxes above enemy heads. Combat with enemies is using the new "Fight them in the environment gimmick", and encounters are pre-ordained in terms of their enemy compositions. An over-correction to random map encounters. It takes away the thrill of navigating the world. You just see a few enemies walking around some small area that you are being funneled into, and see the battle coming from a mile away. Combined with the boring combat system, the core gameplay element of all RPGs is turned into an obligatory task to complete to get to the next scene. It is TOO measured and controlled.The world design is quite beautiful, but the character design is meh. Looks far too "Modern day cartoon" to be truly enjoyable. One trade off of an intricately designed world is the huge lack of interactivity. Sure, the world is gorgeous and detailed, but you can't really DO anything with it except look at it. It's just a big pretty set piece to walk through to get to your next developer ordained enemy encounter. A lot of old RPGs that relied on tile based maps had a lot of things you could interact with, for little blurbs or perhaps a bit of worldbuilding.The opening 'tutorial' was over very quickly, showcasing the combat basics. Then straight into what was essentially just a big flashback cutscene that served more as an introduction to the two/three main characters. It took way too long to get through. Too much dialogue with unproven characters in a game you aren't even sure you're going to like yet because you haven't had the opportunity to sink your teeth into its gameplay loop.Concerning the characters and story, boring again. You start the game with the two 'chosen one' characters going on a quest to stop a 'potentially' dangerous thing, and they have to do it because they are the 'chosen ones'. Their weird normie friend wants to come along too. Honestly it has been a couple months since I played, and I can't remember the personalities of the two main characters, and the friend is just 'quirky' (never seen that before, have ya?). They don't have any true character flaws. They are all just so friendly and 'happy to be here'. Bland and generic.Yes, this is my impression of them out of the gate with only a few hours in the game. It doesn't matter if all of these things improve later on. If the entire game is good, then the beginning should also be good. If you are going to have an RPG with combat gimmicks, then those gimmicks need to be fun and engaging right out of the gate to keep the player interested. Same thing with story and character development. The beginning of an RPG needs to be firing on all cylinders. Likable but obviously flawed characters, concise dialogue that only serves to provide the player with the ESSENTIAL knowledge (with optional dialogue available through chatting with NPCs, bookshelves, etc.) with a clear and present threat that makes itself known VERY early in the game, and a strong PERSONAL motivation by the main characters to overcome that threat. Sea of Stars doesn't have any of this. A very environmentally pretty mediocre at best RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral option, I would have picked it, but I decided to err on the positive side of a game that I feel is incredibly lacking, one that I cannot understand at all the effusive praise it received.I'll start with the negatives, which will sound weird, but I feel this game lacks in every major element important to an RPG. The story is poor, both overall and in terms of the amount of time it takes to see anything remotely compelling happen. The characters leave a lot to be desired. There is very little character development or characters that make you care about them whatsoever. And, finally, the combat is quite boring and repetitive. There is the foundation of something nice in the combat, but overall it is just not very developed. There are very few skills, combos, etc. Part of the joy of older turn based RPGs was leveling up, acquiring more powerful skill and spells, and, for a game like Chrono Trigger, seeing the interactions of techniques between party members, and this game just lags behind in that way. I don't mind the game being on the easier side (it is very easy), but I do mind it being overly simple. So if I think the game is lacking in all the major elements of the RPG, why does it get a thumbs up? Well, it does all the little things well. Even though all the major characters are not remotely compelling, the minor characters are endearing and have some amusing dialogue. I don't think it's good that the characters that are scarcely a part of the game are my favorite characters, but I do appreciate that they do exist. As an adult, I DO appreciate that the game is not a grind fest, so there is that going for it. The artwork is excellent. I did very much enjoy the level traversal since the game is very beautiful to look at. The soundtrack is absolutely excellent, my favorite part of the game. The little side things to do in the game, whether it's fishing, collecting, or the game "Wheels" that you play in taverns are all fun additions to the game. There were times I asked myself why I kept playing, and it was the cumulative effect of all the little things. The funny dialogue from one of the characters in particular, the music in a new area, finding a new collectible, and the fact that it is an easy play, made it a relaxing experience, one that I have enjoyed enough to deem the game a thumbs up despite the major glaring flaws.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A masterpiece. Quibble all you want about things here and there - nothing is perfect, after all, and everyone has their own preferences, and that's valid - but there is not one actual substantial flaw in this game.The battle mechanics are both simple (to be inviting and accessible) and still have voluntary complexity (to add depth and challenge).The story is a modern take on all the classic video game epics' stories. And what a delightfully refreshing take to have the main characters be a blue-haired woman, a brown-skinned guy, and an overweight dude with a disability. Absolutely love the representation.The pacing shows the devs respect player's time.The art - all of it - is a game changer. This game's visuals and audio are the new standard, as far as I'm concerned. Even if you don't want to play the game because turn-based RPGs aren't your thing, get the soundtrack. You won't regret it.There's no other way to say it. Sea of Stars is a masterpiece. From the bottom of my heart, thank you to everyone who helped bring this to life.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The game has great presentation with fantastic visuals and extensive OST. The story is not complicated, but it's cute and has a few surprises. Game's setting is full of creative ideas and worldbuilding that comes back as the plot unfolds. The game starts slow, but it picks up eventually.The gameplay is turn-based combat, suplemented by simple environmental puzzles and seemless exploration. The combat has interesting ideas. Lock-breaking disables enemy attacks, which adds an interesting tactical layer when combined with many different types of resources to manage (mana, living mana, combo and ultimate meters). At least, that would be in theory, however in practice combat is easy to an extent where these ideas aren't fully utilized. Lack of status effects meant that after a certain point all enemy attacks were variants of "I do damage", which is a shame, but attacks were still differentiated due to having different block timings. Boss fights are cool as a show-off stages, but they are nonthreatening unless you play with hardmode Relics equipped. Speaking of, relics are a really good system for not only setting the right difficulty level, but also for enabling QoL and generally alter the gameplay to your liking.This game is a prequel to The Messenger and a segment full of references to that game, but knowledge of the previous game isn't necessary for this one.Grinding XP not required and many fights can be skipped. There are also no random encounters.Overall I recommend it. There is a lot to like, and the worst parts of the game were still decent.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Chrono Trigger this game is not. There are some absolutely good things going on here but I am just not enjoying this game and it seems unlikely to change. It is already obvious that this game just has too many things going on in combination such that I'm not going to enjoy this. Specifically, I take issue with the following:1. Quick time event combat. I don't typically enjoy this mechanic in other RPGs (Shadow Hearts Covenant being the sole exception due to how well it was implemented) and here it isn't particularly well done. There just isn't any indication of how you are supposed to time things and it just comes off as fairly random. The game tries to tell you that you don't really need to worry about it but that isn't true as the battles are very clearly designed around your being able to hit the timings on both offense and defense so this alone is enough to kill my enjoyment of the game. The only feedback you get is after you have already failed or succeeded at the timing which, to me, feels backwards.2. Dialogue, this is personal preference but I'm really not feeling the writing. It comes off as very modern, internet casual feeling (for lack of a better way to describe it) and it is just taking me out of the experience. I suspect that It is going to age about as poorly as Working Designs infamous translations from the 90s. Also they took the annoying feature from Golden Sun where everyone speaks in sort of a nonsense babble while the text is being output. It isn't a big deal but I wasn't wild about it there and am not wild about it here.3. Pacing. This is killing me. I'm two hours in and nothing of any interest has happened yet. Compare to Chrono Trigger (which I only bring up because everyone seems to think this game is Chrono Trigger's second coming) which had you neck deep in action within 10 to 15 minutes if you wanted to breeze through the Millennial Fair. Based on other reviews I've read this doesn't seem to improve as the game goes on.4. Character customization/growth. Pretty minimal stuff.  You get some basic equipment options and a stat perk to choose from upon leveling and that is about it. The available skills  and options seem quite shallow.On the positive side, the game absolutely looks gorgeous and I wish more modern games would take 2D artwork this seriously. There are some really great visual effects going on in the world despite the game being 2D and it really does come together nicely. The soundtrack is nice too and I am particularly excited to listen to it more given that they were even able to get Yasunori Mitsuda on board for some of the tracks (probably the only area where I think comparing it to Chrono Trigger actually works).I will probably force myself to play through this some more since I bought it and don't have anything else I'd rather play at the moment but so far this game is a big miss for me. No doubt this review will be drowned out by the mass of positive reviews comparing it to Chrono Trigger but hopefully this will at least provide at least a bit of counterbalance to those for anyone who is on the fence about this.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Wanted to experience crosscode again, was somewhat dissapointed. The story is the most lukewarm klee'shae thing, but it does have a nice spin after you beat the game. The characters are alright, all of them have some kind of gimmick (most of all the side characters), and the haha's were plentiful.The combat is where the game shines - every encounter is fresh, on account of the lock system, plus the paper mario-esque timing attacks/blocks has a good feeling once you get used to every ability/enemy attack pattern. The game's pretty aware of itself when it comes to re-skins of the same enemies/bosses, so I won't rag on it too much. Even if it's a re-skin, most of the enemies/bosses have at least one new attack pattern that you have to learn or face mucho damage-o. Yeah, the game looks great, but some locations feel barren, others are so stuffed or geometrically insane that I can't tell which way is up, which way is down at times. I very much like that for every boss there's an indicator for how much health there is left, so there's a bonus motivator for you to keep pushing, use everything you have etc. etc. One thing I disliked is the imbalance of different combo skill costs - most of them cost 2 combo points, which I feel is a bit too much, as early game, you will basically only have the zale+valere combo move and then a couple of 2-point combo skills (granted, if you find them, since most of them are hidden away in treasure chests)Speaking of treasure, I love how much exploration there is. At first you just kind of have to push through the main story, to unlock some new traversal/utility abilities, but the late game is where the exploration aspect really peaks. I adored finding all of the little secrets, seeing where some random doohikey fits, so I could unlock some hidden boss battle and then post-main story content unlocks, where you can go for the true ending - it warms my soul.Soundtrack is 10/10, especially the autumn hills track.All in all, I went into this game, thinking that it's gonna be crosscode 2. I was dissapointed by the story and very much pleased with everything else. Get it,  play it, you will not be let down.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Not as good as classics from the SNES era, but a great addition to that type of lineup.Garl could have probably been written better, even the most positive people have fears, and in his case he definitely should have had that depth. Took me out of a lot of the scenes which hampered the experience a little.Solid 8/10 though
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: So disappointing.  I was very much looking forward to this, but there is nothing of Chrono Trigger in it.- The plot is incredibly bland.- The combat is nonsensical and repetitive.- The art is nice, but repetitive.  All the best visuals are in the trailer.- The music is unmemorable.- The world is tiny.DNF'ed at what feels like probably 80% or so.  There's just no reason to keep playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: You know, some games take a time before they kick off, go tickle your nostalgia, if it's that kind of game, or get interesting in either story or gameplay.Sea Stars is almost immediately great. You unlock things with time, for sure, but the base is so good that you'll already fall in love with it before the 2 hours mark.I said it, and I'll keep saying it: Sea of Stars set its sights on reminding older gamers of their childhoods, and showing a good modern take on said classics to the younger generation. Not just in its style, not just its genre, but the story itself. Typically, I can understand why one wouldn't really wanna play a group of kids... But these kids, they bring it home and remind you of the amazing days when everything was an adventure.To get technical though, it's very tactical, with a lot of gameplay mechanics past your typical "attack, magic, items." There are really fun choices to make, whether it's to counter an enemy's mechanics or simply to heal yourself efficiently through the dungeon.I love this game. A true homage to quality RPGs.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I wrote a long, unedited, spoiler-filled rant to a friend of mine and copy posted it on the forum. If you've already played the game and want to know the gritty details of why I'm giving this a thumbs down, then check it out here:The spoiler free version of my rant is that I went into Sea of Stars coming from The Messenger, and my high expectations were disappointed.The production values, especially the music, are great.The combat, while really tightly designed, lacks variety. This starts to hurt as you approach the mid point of the game.Most disappointing though is that the story is trite and full of narrative shortcuts. The potential seeps from the wound this creates like pus, and it's unceremoniously wiped away and discarded. It's an entertaining game, and usually I would give a thumbs up for that, but it fails the standard that Sabotage set up for themselves with their previous game. With a bit more planning, this could have stood tall with the classics that it clearly draws inspiration from. Sadly it ended up being yet another derivative indie game, and as a result no amount of production value is going to prevent it from fading into the void of the forgotten.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a very nostalgic trip for the old 90s JRPGS.Things I like:- Combat. It's pretty enjoyable. It feels very similar to Octopath Traveler. You also get to swap party members on the fly without it being a turn for more advantageous combos.- Traversal. It's not a combat slog the whole way. There's stuff to interact with the world in a style reminiscent of platforming.- Story. It's not deep and profound, but it is satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Game notes 8 hours of play, but spent somewhere around 1~2 hours playing and then being interrupted to take care of children through holidays. Bought game for plot and it's poorly written from what I have seen and all posts I dug into online clearly talk about lack of plot through entire game.Besides a boring plot the mechanics are not the smoothest for a game with timing intensive mechanics. Bad enough that the developer even slapped in a special graphical option you can turn on to show you when you successfully made a combo or not but seem to have a disdain for the setting as the graphics for it are very annoying.

_childDocuments_.review: Lifeless soulless RPG. At least it looks good.Characters dont have personalities outside of Garl.Level ups and gear don't matter. Youll be hitting enemies basically just as hard 1 hour in as you will 15 hours in.Youll be using the same abilities the entire game.Very very overrated game, and this is coming from someone who kickstarted it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game I have been compelled to review, mostly in confusion as to the general tone of awe that the community has towards this game. This game is absolutely beautiful, to be sure. The environments are breathtaking, and the majority of the boss encounters are spectacles of the highest order. This game falls critically short in two areas, however - the character development and the combat. Many other reviewers have nailed that the two main characters are basically Mary Sue chosen one stand ins with no progression whatsoever throughout the entire game. The developers also clearly push Garl as the favorite character, but it is hard to maintain empathy for a character who calls an evil immortal a "loser" to his face just for the game to have a cool moment and set off one of the dumbest and most predictable story beats in this game. All of which pales in comparison to the true ending. I haven't been this mad at an ending since I finished reading the Mistborn series. We bait out the big bad, we beat the pozz out of him, and the Alchemist rescues him and smiles! The End! What the actual chocolate fudge?The second giant elephant is the combat. Often, enemy locks will require uses of moves that require timing like Moonerang. I grew to dread moon locks because they would drag combat out a massive amount, and with food I never lost a single combat throughout the entire game except for a single arena encounter for the true ending. All of this combines to mean that I finished this game thoroughly underwhelmed. Setting up a true ending after a lot of optional content sets the aftertaste for the game, and this game was completely ruined by its ending. I do not recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: To be brief: I spent 40 hours playing this game to nearly 100% completion on stream. If I didn't have an audience and a co-pilot to goof with, that time would have been mostly boring slog. Sea of Stars paints a beautiful world with delicious sound design, and it absolutely nails the nostalgia-bait aesthetic it's going for, but aesthetic is pretty much all it has. The combat system is paper thin and falls apart pretty early; in the second half of the game, most of the bosses never got an action, even with all of the hardest difficulty options available enabled, and there's basically no mechanical meat to interact with. The dialogue is vapid (behold a storm of "..." and "!" and "!?") and most of the characters never develop a personality (Garl's fine, though- he's the real protagonist, anyway). The overall narrative is pretty uninspired and absolutely loaded with references to The Messenger that feel really, really intrusive.If you've got Game Pass or can nab it on a deep discount and know what you're getting yourself into, you might have a good enough time, but you really need to temper your expectations. If you're looking to play something like Chrono Trigger or Super Mario RPG, you'll have more fun re-playing those games instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I have not played post game so review may change laterI was debating on whether or not to recommend this game but I did find this game enjoyable with some charm. The music and graphics are nice and I did like the concept of the plot.If you like standard rpg games you would like this but prefer more complex story and characters than I don't think you would like this.My main criticisms are the lack of development from the characters and the lost potential they had with the plot. It is an interesting concept to have solstice warriors desperate to find their own path after being forced into the role they are in, but they do nothing with it except use it as motivation for what happened later. Overall I thought the story was fine but left more to be desired.While I did like a few of the characters, I found the main ones to be generic hero ones, others annoying at times and even come into the story more randomly like it was rushed. There is zero development and not much dynamic except being friends and working as a team. Only one of them was interesting and even then he leaves later (and probably comes back post game but haven't played that yet)
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Do I recommend this game?  Yes, but on sale only.(+)Music, Visuals, Battle were all excellent.  f you enjoyed the music from The Messenger, I'd say about a solid third of the music in this game sounds like it was ripped from that sound track; which makes sense.  The rest of the track is at worst "good" and at best ABSOLUTELY SLAMIN'.  Songshroom Marsh gets a special callout for the background singing along with the BGM, nice touch!Visuals are pixel graphics, well done and with shading... "NeoPixel" basically.  Combat is different than most RPGs.  You only get 4 abilities per person, with one of them being an Ultimate that you can only use sometimes.  It's up to you to use the right ability in the right situation, while managing your mana.  You gradually build up Combo points as well, which involve two people and use no MP for various effects.  Surprisingly, this game has no buffing or debuffing what-so-ever.  The lock system was an enjoyable spin on combat.  Lastly, for those that have no faith in their ability to manage the timings or other systems, there are relics which reduce the challenge of combat, with no penalty.(-)So why "on sale"?  Because the story and characterization are awful, atrociously, and aggressively bad.  Without spoiling anything, the circumstances surrounding the third person joining your party made me first say "no, no, don't do it, don't you effing do it" as I realized what was about to happen, then it did and I facepalmed.  I was _completely_ disappointed.  Were they just waiting there for _LITERAL HOURS_ so they could jump out of the bush at that specific time?  If the designers had had even a second of foresight to have them come from _behind_ the party instead of up the mountain path, it wouldn't have been nearly so bad.  This is to say nothing of the cringe pirates, or, uhg, Wentworth... everything about Wentworth was outlandish and stupid.  No decision about Wentworth was sane, no action he took made sense.  Bread?  REALLY?!  Oh, and Malkumud!  Slight spoilers here.  He's a minor villain early on, performing actions that everyone agrees that, if successful, would result in EVERYONE DYING.  His justifcation?  He was made fun of.  But everyone's okay with this, and just lets him off the hook after a battle with a pep talk.  ?!?!?!?!!????!  There's more, but you get the idea.It's a solid game, the pros outweight the cons (barely) but I'd wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars harkens back to the golden age of the genre while still providing a modern, polished experience. It's an homage to old school RPGs (Chrono Trigger) that also stands on its own as a must-play title. If you grew up with the classics, it will feel comfortingly familiar. Even the side stories featuring supporting characters shone the spotlight on moving backstories.I can't recommend Sea of Stars enough. It brings out all the feelings with its poignant storytelling and satisfying gameplay. This is an adventure that stays with you long after the credits roll. Pick it up and enjoy the journey.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: **I'll break down the good and the bad of the game:****The Good:**- Simple and linear gameplay, like an RPG for children; you won't waste time getting lost.- Great characters with unique personalities.- Plenty of bosses and enemies with reasonably varied mechanics.- Fantastic animation and visuals that are easy on the eyes.- A large roster of characters to play with.- Strategy is well-balanced—not too complex, not too easy; it leans towards simplicity.- By the end, you'll feel like a total badass.- Puzzles are straightforward and not too difficult.**The Bad:**- The true ending requires collecting too many objects, which becomes tedious. It’s a shame because the true ending is excellent, but most players might miss it due to the grind.- Early in the game, characters have limited skills and powers, making the start a bit boring. However, it picks up once you have the full cast. I think adding more skills and powers to the main characters would be better, but they might also complicate the mechanics, so it's a tricky balance for the developers.- The game loop could use more surprises; it felt a bit repetitive. Although there were surprises, adding a few more would’ve made it more fun.**Conclusion:**This is a perfect game if you want to play an RPG but don't have much time to spare, or if you're a child. It's probably one of the simpler turn-based RPGs out there, ideal for casual gaming. There aren't tons of superpowers, skills, mechanics, or story twists, but there's a healthy amount of everything. The game is very satisfying, especially towards the end.However, if you're looking for something more challenging and complex (less casual), you might be disappointed. I recommend trying it on Microsoft Game Pass to see if it's worth it for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: (Full disclosure, I haven't finished the game yet. If something dramatic happens plot or gameplay-wise, I will eat my words and change my review.)I can't recommend this game at full price. If there is a sale, go for it.I was super excited for this game. Based on other reviews, I thought this game would deliver some of the heart or character or fun of a classic 90's RPG. It does not. There is obviously a lot of love in this game, but it falls short of the games it emulates. There is so much more they could have done with the story progression. Because this is an homage to 90's rpgs, I would have hoped they would subvert a trope or two, or at least make the story more interesting. Instead, they deliver imitation that feels like a items ticked off a checklist. An ensemble cast, a navigable map, collectables, needy npcs, mcguffins, elemental attacks, etc. Everything is very linear. The levels are very same-y and a pain to navigate. Exploration is a chore, not fun. Some of the levels are too dark visually to see, which might just be that I'm getting old because I feel like I'm complaining about that a lot... It might be a me problem. The plot suffers from "we're in a hurry, time is of the essence... oh, hang on, I need you to run this errand for me so I know you're worthy."Combat animations get repetitive. Also, I might have recommended this game if the ship's controls weren't the worst.

_childDocuments_.review: Simple, fun and well made. An excellent jrpg that is beautiful to look at and easy to just play and enjoy and includes difficulty sliders to make it more or less hard as it pleases the individual. The soundtrack is easily one of my top 5 for the year of its release and keeps the game feeling incredibly atmospheric at all time. 10/10. do the thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Everyone would agree this is an homage to the JRPG genre of the late nineties and early 2000s, but what it does differently, what it does especially well, is bringing all the best elements of those classics into a beautiful and touching story and melding it with satisfying combat and movement mechanics that allow for a type of constant puzzling. For those discovering the genre there is lots to love and adore. For those whose focus is on the story, there is a story mode. And finally, for those who want a bit of a challenge and tight timing, there's a 'hard mode.' Even if you don't have fond memories of Chrono Trigger, Super Mario RPG, Final Fantasy, etc. there is something for you to love.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like it was made for me. It's an unapologectic love letter to turn-based RPGs, and more generally games from the 90s and early 00s. It's beautiful, the music is banging, and it's really quite fun. The game isn't very difficult but it's full of good ideas that keep it engaging.The story isn't very good, or subtle in any way, but I don't think that's the point. It's a good bit of fun, it has a few effective emotional moments. and it's an excuse to have a really grand adventure across a pretty impressive variety of environments.It's good ! If you like turn-based RPGs in any way you'll probably like it. Just don't take the story too seriously

Combat gets stale fast since you’ll use many of the same attacks throughout the entire game. Story and characters are forgettable. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful art and sountrack couples with a magnificient and wonderful experience that can tug at the heart strings, Sea of Stars is a well worthy candidate for Indie game of the year! _childDocuments_.review: Went through and 100%'ed the game in about 35 hours.It's fun, and can be made more challenging with relics.For the "default" difficulty, some of the later bosses were more of a patience challenge rather than anything else because you have so many methods of restoring yourself, so it boils down to patiently waiting out the health drop.The platforming never ends up being complicated, and generally always boils down to "what's the only thing I can do now".Other than those little gripes, no complaints here. The art style is great, with a lot of flourishes to it that add to the fun character designs.The game ended up being 20h longer than I initially thought it'd be after reaching the first "end" zone, the clockwork castle. The combat gameplay with the "optional" timed aspects is fun, though I was never a fan of the mystery locks (though those can be disabled if you really hate them, I ended up keeping them in).
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is pretty great but go with the adequate mindset into it. This game does pretty much everything it tries to do very well, and I mean very well. However, due to games such as Baldur's Gate 3 showing the gaming community that player agency and expression and how the world reacts to it is very important, people might expect something like this from Sea of Stars. This isn't that type of experience. Everything is crafted in a very streamlined manner. Progression can be very linear and there isn't many room for creativity in this game. It's a great overall experience with plenty of content (and some great hidden content as well), just don't expect it to innovate any front or be a playground. It's a great tribute to older turn-based JRPGs and it does a surprisingly great job at it, despite a few hiccups. If you hop into this game expecting exactly that, you're going to have a great time probably. A very solid 7.5/10 game.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Beware, this game has a really weak start and it takes a few hours before it finally starts getting interesting! Overall, I think Sea of Stars is totally worth it. The combat is on the weak side and remains as such for the entire game, but the story was really good in the end and there is a good amount of varied and enjoyable content. What I especially liked about the game is the vast variety of environments, some great nods to The Messenger and also the fact that the game feels like a complete package when you finish it. There is some replay value in NG+, nothing stellar though. Once you've seen everything and opened every treasure, the game offers little variety. Expect around 40-50 hrs to 100%
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I started my RPG career with Final Fantasy ! and in my nearly 35 years of experience with playing them, I think if it came down to it, I would probably vote Sea of Stars as the best one I have ever played. Maybe not my favorite, that would have to go to Final Fantasy IV, or 6.. or Chrono Trigger... But more love and care and attention to detail definitely went into Sea of Stars. And that makes it the best!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: This game handles better than the games of old and, while somewhat predictable if you're used to some common tropes, the story just feels so good. Also, have to give some credit for a unique battle system that still reminds me of some of the stuff from classics. Give it a try with the demo if you're unsure, but I'd absolutely recommend this.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: So, you like Chrono Trigger, don't you? You're the kind of JRPG enjoyer that's in it for character focused storytelling, strategic combat and the kind of plot twist that make you realise that this isn't actually a final boss (twice)? Well, hop on!Sea of Stars is... well, calling it a "Chrono Trigger spiritual successor" would actually do it a disservice. It's not a wrong statement in itself: CT was clearly the main inspiration there, but the developers' goal wasn't to simply recreate the 1995 original (damn, it's already been that long). No, they're also breaking a lot of new grounds in the JRPG space.The real draw here, besides the absolutely breathtaking pixel art (which I will go so far as claim is the best I've ever seen) and the absolutely banging soundtrack, is the combat system. Fighting any enemy is a puzzle into itself, figuring out the best order of operation to interrupt enemy actions and put the tempo on your side. You will feel very smart fighting bosses, let me tell you. It is somewhat on the easy side, however, but since then is that a bad thing?The narrative is... serviceable. Since the developers couldn't decide which of the twin solstice warriors of Zale and Valere would be the "JRPG party leader", they share the role, which means they don't really have much of a personality. Chrono was a blank slate for you to project yourself into, after all. As such, the story has to force their childhood friend Garl into doing most of the emotional heavy lifting. If you feel like the whole plot revolves around Garl like he's the writer's pet character, well, that's because someone has to talk during the cutscenes.Another point is that (and that's not really a spoiler) this game is technically a prequel to the Messenger. You don't need to have played that game (I sure didn't, but now I guess I'll have to) to understand what's going on, but there's a few moments that I'm told have much more impact if you know what they lead up to.Also, this game is very long? I went for the true ending (oh, yeah, there's two endings in this game) and that took me a while. Just like Chrono Trigger, just when you feel you're done, surprise, there's a whole new game behind it.Anyway, it's very good.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: A fun RPG, reviving the spirit of the SNES and PS1 era RPGs.  The timed attack boosts and element-based breaks are a fun new layer (borrowing from several earlier games).  The story is cute and fun.  As a gamer with a severe neuromuscular  disease, this game was easy to get into, whether playing with keyboard or adaptive controllers, and the timing element was reasonable, and did not make/break the battles (e.g. missing a timed block didn't result in party-wipe).
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: this was one of the best turn based rpg's i think i've ever played. from the interactive combat to the incredibly well written story it was so much fun. there were so many times when i thought i was about to finish the game and a big event happen and it just kept going in the best way. so worth the cash. 30 hours felt like 5 and I didn't even do everything. if you like turned based games or interesting fantasy worlds this is a must buy.

_childDocuments_.review: Sea of Stars is one of the best indie games I have played in my life. There isnt a single aspect about this game that isnt incredible. I smiled, I laughed, I teared up, and finishing the game left such a grand feeling.Every area is expertly hand crafted and very distinctly different and none of them over stay their welcome, this include the actual look of the area, the enemies you fight and GOOD LORD THE SOUNDTRACK FOR THIS GAME.Do yourself a favor and if you like old school turn based rpg games, just buy this. Dont even second guess it.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Love the timing aspect of the game. Really breaks the routine of how fights go in your usual RPG. Story not overly complicated. Puzzles are all really fun and challenging. _childDocuments_.review: Long story short: try the demo. If it makes you happy and nostalgic, you will probably enjoy the full game. If you played a ton of SNES era JRPGs in your formative gaming years, you will probably love this game. I absolutely couldn't put it down. It felt like I was a teenager again, staying up late with snacks and working my way through a colorful, magical world. I swear I was smiling the whole game -- every new system, movement tech, character, everything was a joy. I don't think it's trying to be something dramatically new or different, but rather a very well thought out homage to everything that came before it. The game feels instantly comfortable and familiar, almost like I opened a box of a bunch of my old favorites and they somehow got melded into a single, amazingly polished work.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game - felt like i'm playing chrono trigger mixed with other elements of rpg , the story gets interesting the more you progress and the amount of secrets are amazing - sound tracks ara amazing ofc cause the same soundtracks creator from chrono trigger . got 41/42 achievements and finished everything in the game like 99 percent . so i can say it's worth it and it's a gem -   every guy who love jrpg classic turn based must play this . i never bothered to write a review about anything but the team behind this game deserve it .

_childDocuments_.review: This game is absolutely captivating. The Music amazing and great to listen to. Game play and story elements reminds me very much of classic and belonged RPGs such Chrono Trigger and Lunar. Other than a somewhat forced opening chapter the story flows nicely and the art is memorable. Hands down one of the best new RPG's iv played in a long while.

_childDocuments_.review: Had this on my wishlist for a while now!Brings back that nostalgic vibe of games like Legend of Dragoon, Final Fantasy, and Golden Sun.The active combat mechanics make for an engaging experience.If you're feeling that RPG nostalgia trip with a modern twist, great art and a great story-line this is a game you won't want to miss out on!
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: The love and passion poured into this project drips off every pixel, tune and line of dialog. The best looking pixel art I have ever seen. The writing is charming. The level design is fun.The music is great. The sound FX are prefect and a treat to the ears. This studio deserves all the love coming its way.Both this and Chained Echoes are an incredible gift to us who are 40+ and want to re-experience playing a great SNES RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: Received game as a gift due to my love of JRPGs and Chrono Trigger specifically.  The aesthetic is beautiful, the music even more so, and the residual love the devs have for old school JRPGs shines through in all the best ways.  I'm 13-14 hours in with no idea how long of a game it is and still just as invested as I was the first 30 minutes.EDIT:  Just finished the game around 35 hours.  Not 100% completed yet and i will be chasing some achievements.  this game is so so so so so good.  HUGE kudos to the dev team, and i hope there's more in store from them.
_childDocuments_.name: Sea of Stars

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend Sea of Stars.The game looks amazing, and it has some really good music.  It even has some decent ideas for its turn-based combat.  None of that saves the story and characters., which fall flat at nearly every chance given.Play Chrono Trigger.  Play the original Final Fantasy 6 on SNES.  The games that inspired this one still stand the test of time today, and are better investments of your money and effort.

_childDocuments_.review: The only tiring part of the game? Going for achievement #42 which requires players to spend an extra 5 hours on NG+, even though nothing is missable in the first playthrough.Otherwise, a near-perfect experience for anyone looking to scratch the old-school, pixelised-style JRPG itch which focuses on storytelling and a linear progression experience that veterans such as those from Camelot ("Golden Sun") and SQEX ("Chrono Trigger") would be proud of. Players wanting a more difficult, or easier combat experience can simply toggle on/off specific "relics", which to a great extent helps with managing the overall difficulty in combat.A deep soundtrack ("Encounter Elite!" is a banger of a boss battle theme), a simple and fun minigame with a strong RNG element (would actually buy a "Wheels" tabletop if they want my money), and also a top 10 saddest deaths in video games moment. Nothing more I could ask for

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively mid. The budget's obvious to see and the presentation is breathtaking, but the gameplay gets repetitive fast due to the lack of variety in character skills beyond combos. The lack of indication of when you are supposed to press for the timed hits mechanic also disincentivizes trying new moves beyond a certain point and instead just repeat the moves you already know the timing for, further limiting gameplay variety.However, while flawed, the gameplay is relatively solid on its own. The main sticking point for this game is the story, which is weak and at the same time over and underwritten, with some plot points having 5-10 minutes of exposition where a line would have sufficed, and others having no introduction or elaboration despite never having been mentioned beforehand. Many of its writing issues were already there in the dev's earlier game, The Messenger, but the lighter tone and immediate leaning on the fourth wall gave the writing a cheeky flair that it could get away with, which this game does not have, as it generally tries to take itself more seriously.In general, this game explicitly compares itself to other games like Chrono Trigger or Paper Mario/Mario & Luigi (by lifting many plot points and visual elements from CT and gameplay mechanics from Mario RPGs), but then is stuck in the position of having forced itself into a comparison that does it absolutely no favors. You need to be very confident if you want to be compared with Chrono Trigger of all things, and this game just doesn't measure up.Is it a bad game? No, but it is terribly overrated and, imo, not long or good enough to justify its price tag. Pick it up on sale if you want, but there are RPGs to chose from, indie or otherwise.

_childDocuments_.review: All of the aspects of old styled jrpgs wrapped with a bow of gorgeous graphics. I enjoyed so much about this game, although the writing was lacking in some departments it's something i could look past due to how amazing the combat system is. All attacks characters use can be timed for more damage or health which i found fun to master. Each of the party members had charming designs and fun abilities, it was nice to see that combo attacks were implemented into the game although i would've liked to see a trio attack the amount of combos there are makes up for it. If you love games like chrono trigger and paper mario for sure check this game out you won't regret it! 4.5/5
