_childDocuments_.review: Frontier delivered solid work with Jurassic World Evolution 2. As with its predecessor, the visuals of the dinosaurs are simply beautiful, with great animations. The game improved some gameplay mechanics over the first part and offers different terrains to build you park in - a refreshing change from the tropical islands setting in JWE1.The most fun mode in the new game is Chaos Theory, which lets you construct the original Jurassic Park, as well Jurassic Park San Diego, which was only alluded to in the Lost World movie - and this time, you can do it better and fulfill John Hammond's dream without a pesky fat guy sabotaging it. Same goes for Masrani's Jurassic World.The soundtrack with music from the Jurassic Park and Jurassic World movies make this a well-rounded experience.I was experiencing some minor bugs during my playthroughs so far, though. None are gamebreaking and can be fixed by reloading the game. The most annoying bug was that sometimes dinosaurs just stop following their daily routines and stop drinking and eating. After a while you get the message that they have below 50% health.I'm sure that Frontier will adress those bugs with patches soon.

_childDocuments_.review: Want to play a game for hours and hours and hours, forced with as many dependencies along way, all while doing the MAXIMUM amount of micro and macro management to add to your frustrations?!Then this is the game for YOU!Pushing the amount of tedious extra task to reach a virtual "difficulty" does not make for a fun experience...Lazy mechanics...Let's just call ALL the workers "scientists", because Engineers, Managers, etc don't seem to exist right? And lets just throw all of those scientist skills into ONLY 3 categories like Logistics, Genetics and Welfare... like seriously What the actual fudge is that even?!?!Imagine having to TELL people to go rest and pay them for it, and after a forced amount of 5 ticks non the less, or you get a forced disgruntled employee (oh hey, they are scientists?) which can cause you problems. Every single thing has to be done by you... Imagine the CEO of Amazon, Jeff Bezoz filling the gas tank of every Amazon delivery driver's truck and then also giving them the directions on where to deliver their packages... for ... every .... single... employee.... There is ranger outposts that can have "some" automation, but it's also quite tedious and then takes up what is called TASK queue spots, which can make doing all the other manual stuff even harder to manage as you have to try switch between rangers, which is also tedious within itself... If you were not TOO busy frantically managing every little thing and managed to do a save, reload that save before the above storm, lose a bit of progress when you load the save and experience a new storm... you might get a storm that is like light breeze the next time, indicating literal lazy RNGesus BullShaait right there.Realistically you would think a bit of debt to fix some fences and buildings and move some escaped dinos back would make some bit of sense..er... NO NOT IN THIS GAME! Just like the real world, if you showed some success and then get HIT, you have "NOPE BRUH", insurance or anything is for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. It's not like I'm new to the game, I have played the previous one for HOURS, and I restarted the first Chaos story twice just to get a feel for the new mechanics, but no, I guess we just have to fail and ignore the countless issues...There is plenty of graphical glitches too, like this weird tearing effect, not screen tearing, but the tearing of certain things that seem to fall out of some render LOD "block"... like shadows, some foliage and lights at night. Tested with other games, it's definitely JWE2 causing the hard crashes.I'm honestly really disappointed...again. the only reason I got these is because I love JP (the og ones, not World).

_childDocuments_.review: It’s 10:00 at night on Isla Nublar and I’ve just finished repairing the storm damage. It’s fine; the power stayed on, none of the animals escaped, and the park guests emerged from their shelters a little bit irritated but alive and well. Nothing that a hot chocolate from one of Jurassic Park’s many fine concession stands, or perhaps a new t-shirt or two, can’t fix.Chaos was averted. In your face, Dr Malcolm!Mind you, it did mean reworking Dr Hammond’s original plans quite extensively. A proper power grid, backup generators and decent, dinosaur-grade fences for the raptor paddock for example. Not to mention keeping the park tour well away from the T-Rex. Oh – and giving the staff decent wages and paid holiday leave helped to keep everything running smoothly too. John Hammond – peerless at the vision thing; beyond hopeless at line management.I’m playing the first of Jurassic World Evolution II’s Chaos Theory maps and I’m having a blast. Although, in fairness, I was pretty much hooked from early on in the Campaign when I emerged from the treeline in my Jeep and came face to face with a trio of Brachiosaurs just living their best life by a nearby lake. It was the video game equivalent of that famous opening scene from Jurassic Park and I couldn’t stop smiling.I’m a bit further on now. I’ve finished all five Chaos Theory maps and I’ve made a start on the first Challenge map, so I figured I’d seen enough of the game to write a review. Full disclosure - I haven’t played the original Jurassic World Evolution, or any other theme park sims, so this is pretty much coming from a newbie to the genre. Make of that what you will.At the moment, JWE2 is very much a park management and problem solving game. Of the four game modes on offer, the Campaign feels like a tutorial with a short story attached and the Sandbox currently only lets you play with stuff that you’ve unlocked from elsewhere in the game. As a new player, I found the Campaign very welcome to get me into the basics of paddock building and dinosaur care. Plus, as I may have already said, it had some genuinely awesome moments!I haven’t tried the Sandbox yet but right now, if you’re the kind of player who prefers to play freestyle with a big box of customisable toys and spend your gaming time getting them all set them all up *just* right, then JWE2 may not be the game for you, simply because unlocking all those toys means spending a lot of time doing other stuff first. There’s already been plenty of player feedback on that point though, so I’d definitely come back in a few weeks and and see if anything’s changed.At the moment, the meat of the game is in the Chaos Theory and Challenge maps, both of which are (with a few exceptions) squarely focused on building a smoothly running dinosaur park that can also deal with the various challenges the game throws its way. Building that smoothly running park requires juggling quite a few game mechanics, not all of which are explained in the Campaign missions. Fortunately the well laid out UI does a good job of making them discoverable in-game. It’s quite a lot to get your head around to begin with but it all gets a lot easier once you’ve built your first park and had a chance to explore the tech tree, play around with the various buildings, and get a better idea of how everything fits together.As other reviews have noted, there’s also quite a lot of micromanagement to begin with but once you dig a bit deeper into the game mechanics there’s almost always a way of reorganising your park to reduce the amount of clicking required. I’ve come to think of the micromanagement as kind of a gameplay backup generator; when a problem happens, its a quick fix to keep things running whilst you figure out what the long term solution is. There’s plenty of time to unwind by the paddocks whilst you’re thinking though and to watch your dinosaurs going about their daily, gorgeously animated, lives.And there’s nothing quite as satisfying as finding those long-term solutions, leaving things to take care of themselves for a while, and hopping on your very own park tour. To be driven through those iconic torchlit gates, and given an up close, first person view of the dinosaurs from the comfort of one of your Land Cruisers. Naturally, each Land Cruiser comes with a built in state-of-the-then-art CD-ROM drive and voice acted tour guide!It turns out that a Brachiosaurus is no less awesome for being penned up in a safari park rather than roaming free. Especially when there’s a handful of Gallimimus playing around its feet and a herd of Parasaurolophus looking at you from the other side of the track.Readers. My dear patient readers. Welcome… to Jurassic Park.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing this game reminded me of my fond memories playing  on my chunky laptop. Games like , , and  were childhood favourites growing up, but it's been a long time since I really played a business sim.  was a welcome surprise for me, rediscovering the fantasy of building my own dinosaur theme park. The graphics are great, capturing those picturesque moments that photo modes in video games were made for. The dinosaurs are extremely detailed, looking exactly like their movie counterparts, and have realistic AI and animations. It feels good when everything is in equilibrium, dinos are happy, profits are up, and research/genetics enables new structures and dinosaurs.The main campaign is more accurately a tutorial of the basics of park management with enclosures, research, amenities, etc. and are more geared towards scripted sequences of capturing wild dinosaurs and managing a national park, leading into the story of  in June. What I enjoyed more was the Chaos Theory scenarios, where you can take on alt-history scenarios of building successful Jurassic Parks on Isla Nublar and San Diego, or following heavily scripted sequences of creating a natural preserve out of the ruins of Jurassic World which I thought was nice and lived up to the major themes of the franchise, reminding me of the ending of . I would like to see a free update with a new Chaos Theory focused on .However, I do have some issues with the game. Amenities are too simplistic and require very little thinking on the part of the player. The management view tells you exactly where to put them, and deciding which products and modules to implement only requires staring at the profit number and making it go up, without much consideration towards target audiences and guest appeal. Micromanagement in a business is expected and tolerable to an extent. But, as others have pointed out, it can be a pain in the butt to heal a dinosaur. First, you have to send out a ranger team to scan their condition, a MVU to heal/medicate them, and/or a helicopter to tranquilize and deliver the dino to the medical bay. You have to manually assign ranger teams to conduct critical repairs after a storm, otherwise they will still be doing their routine patrols or idling in the parking lots while dinosaurs are rampaging through the park.All in all, though, I really enjoyed  for reigniting that childhood love of dinosaurs and bringing me back to the business sim genre.

_childDocuments_.review: This game (Jurassic world evolution 2) is a real improvement over Jurassic world Evolution 1. Improved management, Improved creativity, Improved dinosaurs, Improved maps, Improved graphics, Improved everthing! Although I wish they would bring back slow motion from the first game for capture mode.Frontier have really reviewed the lacking features of Jurassic World evolution 1 and decided to improve them. The Introduction of the scientists into the game really makes the game feel well rounded and boosts the management. You must make sure that your staff is not overworked or undertrained or you will be sabotaged and tasks cannot be carried out. It adds that new layer of management that we have been sorely lacking in Jurassic world Evolution 1.The dinosaurs also feel way more alive. The problem with Jurassic world evolution 1 is that the dinosaurs feel don't have that feeling of having a soul. Interactions between each other are just standing in cult circles and that was about it. But now in Jurassic world evolution 2 we can get unique social animations! With some being utterly adorable. Even the T-rex gets a social animation which kind of remind me of two dogs rubbing and playing with each other!There are also pack hunting and the fighting system has been slightly improved, but perhaps not as much as we would have liked. The dinosaurs still square up to each other, butthey can perform random unique attacks while fighting. For example:When a Rex and Spino are fighting, there will be a chance that they will perform a unique animation where both dinosaurs will leap over do a elegant swirl, snap at each other and the result is that they have switched sides. That there will be the normal biting animation. This does improve the fighting system but I wish they could implement ambush attacks.Perhaps when a spino isn't watching and sits down next to a forest, the T - Rex could sneak up on the Spino and land a surprise attack.The last major improvement is the creativity and customisation. We get so much new decorations in jurassic world evolution 2. From planters and fountains to sheds and lights. it really allows us to decorate the empty spaces within our park and really make it interesting to look at. Contrast this to the first game and you will really see the difference.Not only that but you can change the looks of some amenity buildings such as shops and guest attractions. You can change the signage, roof styles, ground decorations, colour of the lights of the building and the colour of the building itself.All these show that Jurassic World Evolution 2 is leaps and bounds better than Jurassic world evolution 1.But no game is perfect, and Jurassic world evolution does need to implement certain improvements in some areas.Such as new dinosaur attractions.We have viewing galleries, towers, tours and monorails, but that is about it.We need more attractions!Real theme parks have uncountable amounts of different attractions that will give guests unique experiences, and that is something that we sorely lack in Jurassic world evolution 2. The dinosaur roster is big enough, we don't need new dinosaurs, we need more attractions!For me I will give this game a solid 8.5/10.It is really fun and an absolute blast of a experience. I really want this game to reach a solid 9.5 out of ten! Of course no game will ever reach 10/10.I recommend this game to any jurassic fans and also to the previous fans of jurassic world evolution 1.Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: I honestly thought about leaving just a series of four letter words as my review because, seriously, **** this game. I've played 72 hours -- I still don't have sandbox unlocked and I'm losing my patience. Had this game not been in a bundle I'd be livid. I really enjoyed the first one but this is such a step down in player satisfaction that I don't understand who this game is for. It's not difficult in concept or by being challenging in a satisfactory way -- it's just annoyingly tedious. The main reason for this is because too much of the game is a bad (horrendously, frustratingly bad) jeep and helicopter simulator where you steer garbage handling vehicles and try to shoot dinos that have way more maneuverability than frickin modern vehicles. A TRex can turn on a dime but your vehicles respond like something out of a 2000's escort mission. The way the game makes you swap between perspectives to chase down dinos that need 3 darts before they pass out is one of the most bewilderingly stupid design choices I've seen in ages. It makes any "hunting" aspect utterly unsatisfying. I am on the last of the "Chaos" scenarios where they deliberately don't give you helicopters so you have to use the ridiculously clunky and tedious "herding" commands which -- I swear to goth -- need to die in fire. Apparently once I finish this garbage I'm still going to need to do the challenges to get the sandbox open. Which is all I want -- as opposed to this worthless time wasting garbage. This is a perfect example of a development team that were instructed to put their (I'm sure) tremendous efforts and talents into something half the audience of the series didn't ask for. There is zero reason to gatekeep so much content behind garbage missions with vehicle nonsense. If you were so insecure about players not wanting to engage in your badly designed missions and campaigns you could have put in hidden achievements or whatever for the masochists who need to 100% things. I'm not sure if I'll make it to sandbox mode, but should I do so, it will be not via an enjoyable, satisfying into or campaign, but though a deeply frustrating and unsatisfying dumpster fire of unnecessary hoops.Seriously -- **** this game.

They don't breed, you can't interact with them, and they are just there.  The park building aspect looks nice but again, it's simplistic when compared with other builder sims. _childDocuments_.review: I thought long and hard about whether to up or down vote this game. After 30 hours I thought I'd be sure but there are some bits to like and a lot to hate.I liked the first one and completed it several times. This one feels like they just wanted every nod to the films as possible, expecting peoples nostalgia to carry the game.The mechanics of this game vs the first are a little bizarre. There were some clear decisions to pad gameplay out by adding extra pointless steps. There are tonnes of crazy economic decisions (such as filling up a backup generator) which can cost more than sending 3 specialist scientists around the globe, dig up fossils and extract DNA. But a few cans of fuel for a generator and your park is bankrupt! Hell, electric grid power has free consumption and 100% coverage of my park, but my backup generators STILL are running out of fuel? What?! But I digress.Some improvements were welcome. The guests needs being contained within a single building was nice, as was catering to different clientele with the customisations of said buildings. The frustration comes where you don't need anything beyond the tier 1 of this building to get a 5 star park makes zero sense, so the research becomes irrelevant. The worst function of this game is the addition of aviaries and lagoons. These had HUGE implications to park variety, dino variety, different management and setup of parks. Except they feel barely designed. The grid system for them is awful. An enclosure and fences are all designed by you to match the map, your design, etc. The aviaries and lagoons snap to grid, require huge spaces, often quibble over terrain for no reason and are just downright horrible to use. Equally rangers and med vans frequently get "stuck" in drone mode trying manage these locations, and what's worse is that the areas are almost pointless. The aviary has flying dinosaurs all sitting on the viewing platform, because they apparently refuse to land anywhere else, despite DEMANDING rocks to sit on, or trees to land upon. Lagoons are worse with zero design or interactivity. Both areas have 4 dinos that can go in them. It legitimately felt like the worst area of the game.All in all, the game does deliver on the basic premise of a park sim. There's a tiny amount of management, a tiny bit of park design (which feels very dumbed down), but as a sequel it really doesn't improve on anything.It feels like rather than finishing the game the devs wanted, they cut a bunch of features and forced time sinks to extend gameplay out.It's both satisfying and not at the same time, which is frustrating because a game with dinosaurs doesn't need a lot to get it over the line...

_childDocuments_.review: If you´re looking for a sandbox experience like Planet Zoo or Planet Coaster do not buy this game. Jurassic World Evolution 2 inhibts the players creativity in various ways:1. The pathing tool is quite wonky. Creating symetrical paths and plazas is a mess. Vertical building options like stairs and bridges are not a thing at all.  Additionaly the low amount of different path types is ridiculous. 2. Terraforming gives you no freedom at all! Water always has the same depth, cliffs and ravines are impossible to create and foliage can only be placed via imprecisely brushes. The amoint of foliage, rocks and undeground is extremely limited.3. Decorations. The game offers two types of table with chairs, 2 types of lamps, 4 banners (same model, different colors) and 7 types of planters, all of them using almost the same model. That is it. No benches, lamps, fences or whatever. 4. Creating habitats is boring af, The games lets you chose between two(!) different types of fences. Once you created the outer fences  you´ve got the aforementioned trees and rocks to fill the habitats with "life". Of course you can add the additional feeder that is nothing more than a hatch in the ground. Enjoy! (Not even gonna start talking about lagoons. Oof ...)Of course the dinosaurs are fun and the graphics are awesome. Unfortunately that is pretty much it. In the end all parks created in this game will look pretty much alike. Life outside the habitats is boring and sterile. Actually, life inside the habitats is not that fun either. Sadly Frontier can do way better than this. If the coming DLCs address the issues mentioned above this could become an awesome experience. At the moment its a pretty big lackluster for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted so badly to like this game... When I heard this sequel to the original Jurassic World: Evolution game was coming out, I was so excited! I pre-ordered and everything, all I had to do was sit back and wait for the release day. Release day comes: I played for an hour, and I was completely underwhelmed. This sequel had a huge chance to give players a much bigger area in which to build dinosaur enclosures, but NO! Thanks to the need for a "wild area", and not to mention most of these dinosaurs needing a ridiculous amount of space for one enclosure, you're lucky if you can fit 3-5 different species on one map. What is the point of boasting brand new, 75+ species total in-game if you can't fit more than 2 Carnotaurus and an Allosaurus in the Washington map?? Campaign honestly felt rushed and had very little substance to it, something I enjoyed in the previous version. Of course if you want some of the "cool, awesome" dinos you have to complete challenges first to gain access. And even then, where are we supposed to put them?! Sandbox mode you say? Forget it. Unless you play through the challenges first, you won't have access to the dinosaurs you want or the fences you'll need to contain them! I will say I did like the new behaviors and graphics displayed in this game, but they fall short to the obvious issues this sequel has. I wasted $70.00 on this, just to play for under 4 hours total and lose complete interest, going back to the original game. Definitely would not recommend this to anyone, unless you're game for a ton of disappointment! Devs ramped us up on so many new dinos, only to fall flat on their faces with what feels like a half-finished delivery. I wish I could get my money back... -.-

Wanna go drive around like a maniac in one of your unassigned Ranger vehicles? (yeah, you can assign them to stuff. its really handy.)TOO BAD! NO DO THING! ONLY WATCH!That and some of the AI is composed of sweet summer children with short term memory loss learning how to walk every 10 minutes.DON'T GET ME WRONG!! when the games is running like its supposed to and those ai are giving it their damnedest, the game is everything you could want out of it and more! Good difficulty spike, more dinos, tons of stuff to do, AND you have to manage Fuel now! also, storms suck.Out of 5, i'd personally give it a 3. _childDocuments_.review: The complaints about this game are valid. It is more like a $40 DLC on the original than a separate, standalone game, and it seemingly does things worse in (almost) every regard. Yes, it's nice having some color to the atmosphere of the game, whereas previously we were in a sea of green. It is a bit weird, however, to be painting sand over a snow-covered landscape so that your warm-weather dino can feel at home in that whiteout blizzard...on his patch of desert while that snowstorm ostensibly rages around him.Yes, the new dinosaurs and mannerisms are nice to see, even if most of the things in this game are recycled from the last. Yes, the new buildings are a welcome addition...but no, the 'added layers of complexity' they included here aren't meaningfully complex, nor what anyone was thinking when they wanted a bit more involved gameplay. * Adding a fuel requirement to everything - that must be done manually - isn't an added layer of complexity to gameplay - it's a lesson in mediocre tedium. * Separating out game mechanics, such as making a veterinary style building, isn't an added layer of complexity. It's something that was already in the game that you just created another layer of UI to get through to get it done. It functions the same as it did previously (select building, have vehicle drive to dino, shoot dino with dart), so why even introduce this?* Hiring scientists would be interesting (is there a solitary white person from the US that went to school to be a scientist in this universe?) if it didn't come with the additional burden of having to 'rest' them, manually, so that they don't sabotage your park. Why this is in the game, or why sabotage is still a thing is a bit beyond me. If you didn't have to do this weird mini-game of abilities with each of them to do...basically everything in the park, it might be less frustrating. Research? Assign scientists. Expeditions? Scientists. Veterinary problems? Scientists. Why? * Pathing for the AI is somehow worse than the previous version. They will routinely bug out while going to an assigned mission, not be able to find paths while one is very clearly available which forces you to manually control them in order to get the job done. They will routinely bug out while being attacked by dinosaurs and become unable to respond or just teleport across a paddock.* Why, on earth, did anyone think ranger outposts/dinosaur statuses would be a good addition to this game? It is, again, something that already existed (dinosaur status) now locked behind another layer of mediocrity. * There is still, apparently, no latent 'viewing cone' option while placing buildings or otherwise - so you consistently have to go through menus to see where possible overlap or non-coverage is while building viewing platforms. One of the most basic quality of life upgrades, for some reason, still hasn't been implemented. * Why did the game not add features that would've been some sort of net benefit on park  a game about managing a dinosaur park? Why not have some sort of janitorial service, not unlike the Planet Coaster/zoo games? Why not implement basic, you would think, park management aspects. You have basic services down, such as the food/toiletry/drink/entertainment needs of your park, why not diversify this more? Instead of having five restaurants serving the same dish, give a bonus/decrement for diversifying/not diversifying this across the park. Have high-end hotels and lower-end ones. Give bonuses for things that can readily view dinosaurs, all of these things. * Why are you still locking features of sandbox mode behind star ratings in other play styles some people may not want to do? I don't mind the challenge maps, but I can't see why you'd lock so much content behind them. The campaign is a bland 2-4 hours long and does nothing. The previous game had a more interesting and involved campaign over several DLCs..it was half the fun of the franchise and really served as the main vehicle of the game - different islands, different problems that needed different solutions. This just serves as a vehicle to get into a sandbox mode that's locked behind challenges.Edit: An update to this review leaves it the same - assigning scientists and 'juggling scientists!1 so much to do11!' has got to be the most annoying 'new' mechanic to this game. It's tedious, it's obnoxious, it's unnecessary 'gameplay mechanics' that introduce nothing worthwhile to the game but an enormous amount of additional clicks and wasted time on the worst aspect of what this game is supposed to be.

_childDocuments_.review: (EDIT: Unstable, unplayable, only works on teeny tiny maps with low populations. Not worth)This is another one of those games that released way too early. Now, with all the additional DLC, it's actually a very entertaining experience. Except, it still has one common problem in the development philosophy: Quantity Over Quality. Many of the new features and dinos are great, but often feel like slapstick after thoughts when the bugs start crawling out of the woodwork. Weather it be territory needs awareness, ranger teams that won't do their job, or the very spotty collision detection system which sends cars flying hundreds of feet in the air or causes dinos to phase and clip into the ground when coming out of a hatchery, which is supposed to be the cherry on top for animations in this game. At least the flying ranger cars are  h i l a r i o u s. I would chalk this game up as a very, very well dressed puzzle game. There's no RPG or forked-path decision making elements. You have to obey a set of "challenges" which often have you restarting almost from the beginning of research on every new chapter. Personally for me, this is a buzzkill, but it's still a relaxing way to discover the graphical treats the game has to offer. I would much rather have a real campaign mode with persistent progress which cause player choices to actually matter; the current 'campaigns' are just static levels which get reset on every chapter, if there's multiple chapters. Example: Just maxed out biosyn sanctuary research and genome, and made your park perfect? You did too much. You were supposed to meet the bare minimums for the chapter goals, then you get kicked out of the park and all your work resets. Being a completionist and park design enthusiast, I lost way more hours than I ever would have intended with this game, simply due to a lack of transparency. Sure, you could do your research to prepare yourself for this before getting into the game, but the point is that, this is a very unusual, highly lackluster progression model. In fact, it's a lack of progression. The only progress is unlocking maps for the sandbox mode, and the features of the game don't allow for any meaningful sandbox experience unless you like gardening with reptiles. I won't judge, you do you, but I need mods to run proper Site B / Lost World simulations. This game could best be described as the elbow of the arm in a series of games dictated solely by planned obsolescence. The first game was the shoulder, and the third game will be the hand of perfection. I remember lots of development buzzwords being thrown around between the release of the first and second game, and it's frankly just loads of excuses. The technology/software has been available for 10+ years, so let's not pretend this new engine is revolutionizing park management games. It's reinventing the wheel for the sake of funding project longevity. This is a career series, not for us, but for the people making it. Good on them for finding their niche market, but I won't ignore the fact that this series is deliberately punching way under its own weight class.It's still a fun game, I'm going to finish all the chapters and enjoy modified sandbox here and there... but it definitely misses the mark for "spectacle games". Once you've seen damn near any part of the game in action (an animation, 3D model or dino interaction), you've seen the height of the spectacle. Spectacle or awe loses its value if it's always hanging the same spectacle views in your face with little to no change. It hits right the first time, but only the first time. After that, it's all just visual clutter. Honestly, the game is best *played* in the 2D map view, for too many reasons to list here, but that sounds immensely wrong for a graphical spectacle game like this doesn't it? That's because it is. There's hardly a balance between mechanics, gameplay and visual fidelity, to a point that one must shift between "management mode" in the sky and "relaxation mode", when you come down from the sky to inspect things.3.5 / 5 Pros:- Mindless Relaxation (your hand couldn't be held more, unless playing an Andkon property manager flash game)- Visually pleasing for JP fansCons: - Intentionally under developed- Unjustifiable DLC cost to flesh out the base game- The voice acting, plot and 'character conversations' are SO pretentious and self righteous that it ruins the whole story and setting if you think too much about it. The worst part is that these audio logs can't be skipped, and fluff up about 30% of actual required playtime if intending to complete chapters in record time. - Whoever wrote these characters and dialogue had or has no idea what attracted the fanbase to the original trilogy. It wasn't just spectacle, it was also about philosophy. The philosophy in the new series and games are so incredibly ass-backwards that it has to be rationalized as an alternate timeline. - In a nutshell: JP had a tried and true formula to follow... self-righteous zealot characters are the antagonists; life, particularly humanity, is chaos; passionate, educated professionals are the protagonists; everyone who survives the experience becomes humbled (almost). Claire and basically every other character would literally be the antagonists in any authentic JP setting due to their immense disillusionment, selfishness and grossly misguided 'passion'. It makes their dialogue down right disgusting to listen to, like being in a PETA convention attended only by radical Scientologists. And the worst part is, they finally took Maldoon's advice... you're locked in and have to wait out the ride. There is no escape. You may not be eaten alive, but there's still no escape. I genuinely don't even want to talk about it any more.Anyways, fun game, horrible development decisions. Get it on a steep sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game better than the first one? The short answer is yes. The dinosaurs look better and the animations are phenomenal. The addition of flying and marine dinosaurs is great and really adds to the park building experience. I have over 40 hours in the game and I am having a blast so far, but my major gripe is that for a park builder it kind of feels "gimped." I find it odd that you cannot really customize guest amenities past the modules and positioning of the entrances. Considering the depth of this mechanic in Planet Zoo and Planet Coaster this really does rub me the wrong way. I also really wish that you could customize the aviaries and lagoons further than you can now, but it is what it is. The campaign is short, about 5-6 hours, and is fun for what it is. I do think that they had to cut some content due to the delay of Dominion and you can be sure that they will re-add this down the road in the form of paid DLC's. Chaos Theory mode is great as you get to do a number of what if scenarios throughout the franchise, although they did do the Spino from JP3 dirty. The main complaint I am seeing online is that you have to play the campaign/chaos theory mode to unlock all the dinosaurs for sandbox mode. I do understand where this is coming from, but I don't agree with this whatsoever. Having to play the game for all the content? That's a plus. I miss the days of having to grind out unlocks without predatory microtransactions in the background tempting you to skip said grind. It's refreshing. To keep this short, if you are a huge fan of the franchise or just a fan of dinosaurs, this game is for you. Even though it is missing a bit of content you will get your money's worth. If you are a fan of park builders and the dinosaurs are just window dressing, I would stay away for the time being as IMO the game is not fully fleshed out. Overall I would say this game is a solid 7, bordering on an 8. I enjoy it, and if you are a dinosaur/JP fan you will as well. Otherwise hold off and wait for the game to be fleshed out further.

_childDocuments_.review: After spending nearly 200 hours with Jurassic World Evolution 2, I can confidently say that this game has been an absolute blast. As a fan of both the Jurassic Park franchise and management simulation games, this title has delivered everything I was hoping for—and then some.Gameplay & Design: The core gameplay loop of building and managing a dinosaur theme park is addictive, and the way it balances creativity with resource management is impressive. The campaign mode is engaging, offering a mix of story-driven missions that keep things fresh while gradually introducing new mechanics. The addition of new biomes, dinosaur species, and gameplay modes like Challenge Mode and Sandbox have kept me coming back for more.The dinosaurs are the stars of the show, and Jurassic World Evolution 2 brings them to life in a stunning way. From their behavior and social interactions to the way they respond to the environment, there’s a level of detail that I find absolutely captivating. Watching a T. rex roar, or seeing a herd of Brachiosaurus wander through a beautifully landscaped park, never gets old. The AI has come a long way from the first game, and it's been a joy to watch the dinosaurs interact with one another and their surroundings in dynamic ways.Graphics & Sound: Graphically, the game looks incredible. The environments are gorgeous, and the attention to detail in the park’s design makes each one feel unique. The dinosaurs themselves look fantastic—each species is meticulously crafted, and the animations are smooth and lifelike. The lighting effects, especially during dawn and dusk, add a cinematic quality that makes the game even more immersive.The sound design is also top-notch. The roars, calls, and ambient sounds of the park create a truly immersive experience. The music, which blends the iconic Jurassic Park theme with new compositions, is another highlight that adds to the sense of adventure.Depth & Replayability: This is where Jurassic World Evolution 2 really shines. There’s so much to do and see that no two parks feel the same. Whether you're focusing on creating a peaceful sanctuary for your dinosaurs or pushing the limits by constructing massive attractions and managing complex ecosystems, there’s a lot of flexibility in how you approach each scenario. The sandbox mode allows for total creative freedom, and with the wide range of dinosaurs, buildings, and park elements, I never run out of ideas for new projects.The addition of the new species and the deeper management systems has made the game even more rewarding. I’ve spent hours tweaking genetic modifications, researching new technologies, and optimizing park operations to boost both dinosaur happiness and guest satisfaction. It’s the kind of game that’s always presenting new challenges, keeping things engaging even after hundreds of hours.Challenges & Community: While the game is generally accessible, it does offer a good challenge for those who want it. The difficulty ramps up nicely in the later campaign missions, and the sandbox mode allows you to push yourself to build the ultimate park under various conditions. The game also features a number of user-generated content options, and I've found some fantastic custom scenarios and mods that really extend the replayability.Conclusion: Jurassic World Evolution 2 is a fantastic follow-up to the first game, offering more depth, more dinosaurs, and more ways to build and manage your own Jurassic park. After 200 hours, I'm still discovering new things and enjoying the endless creative possibilities. Whether you're a fan of the movies, a lover of simulation games, or just someone who wants to experience the thrill of managing your own dinosaur park, this game has something for everyone. If you're on the fence, I highly recommend diving in—you won’t be disappointed!

tranquilize manually or via task (sedative on 100% but dinosaur never going down) and this causes them to not eat / drink and waste MUV time or just simply waste your money- had a save during a storm where I would load back in the next day, wait for storm to pass, you close the shelters and all your guests are gone. Where only close park & then open park would resolve it leaving you with a massive debt on high star maps and resulting you having to restart the mission because you would lose millions in seconds.- a few crashes occurred during building park tours normally or daisy chaining > meaning area 1 park tour towards area 2 then repeat area 2 to area 3 etc etc- medium carnivores with having enough live prey spread out of the enclosure but still don't eat the goats resulting them rampaging or starvingVerdict----------If you like the dinosaur nostalgic feeling aspect and basic park building mechanics then I would recommend you to buy this game when its on sale (base game only), I would not endorse paying full price of 60 bucks for this game, it is absolutely not worth it.Luckily for you its often on 70~75% sale or if you patient 90% like previous Steam Summer Sale.Avoid DLCs unless you have copious amount of money to spent

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very true successor to the first game. While the campaign seems lacking right now (probably because of the swapped release dates between the game and the Dominion movie to avoid spoilers? More may come out in a DLC after the movie release) the chaos theory mode is actually really fun, like a campaign bonus. The little easter eggs are a nostalgic nod to the movies that I love.My only current complaint, and it might just be my luck, is how easy it is to go from a stable park with multiple millions of funds to work with and have one storm roll through and drop you into the negatives to an irrecoverable point that forces you to restart a park you've spent 5-6 hours on for the chaos mode. I've redone jurassic world 4 times now, once because my rex died of TB right at the beginning, and 3 times because ive had a tornado roll through and knock out my main service buildings and the innovation center right around the stage where you're making a mosasaur. a little frustrating, but still fun up to that moment lol. But like i said, it may just be my luck :P
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: I'm addicted, I lose track of time playing this game trying to keep up with managing the parks.I loved the original Jurassic World Evolution, and in some ways I liked that one a little bit better, but this one is great too, with the Chaos Theory modes revisiting the settings of each of the movies.A couple of the things I liked better about the first game were how you got to build parks on each of the 5 islands, and the research carried as you moved between them, but in JWE2, with each story mode and challenge mode, you start from scratch each and every time. As far as game play, 1 had amenities that counted for multiple ratings, like a bar that counted more for drinks but also gave some food and entertainment ratings, but JWE2 has dedicated amenities, so food amenities only counts for food, etc. I also liked the story of JWE1, how it carried from start to finish, and the dynamic of balancing the entertainment, security, and science divisions in keeping them all happy or else risking the neglected one sabotaging you. JWE2 had sabotage, but you just have to rest your scientists after a number of tasks to keep them happy.One thing I'm glad they implemented for JWE2 is the ability to run faster than "normal" speed, going back to 1 felt like watching paint dry at times. I also like the genetic modification interface better than 1's. And the amenities in 1 felt like I had to micromanage everything (what to sell, for how much, how many workers to hire), but 2 feels a lot more streamlined.But I hate that they've split the game up into multiple micro transactions to hide some of the coolest content. There are 2 content expansion packs, Malta and Biosyn, that offer new challenge modes and maps to play, as well as a few new dinosaurs in each of them. Then there are 9 more animal packs that contain a few new dinosaurs each and maybe a new skin for dinosaurs or amenities or for your ranger or vet vehicles.  I can understand there being an expansion for Jurassic World Dominion's release, or even a smaller one for the Camp Cretaceous fans, but this is crazy.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: Using this to play with my kid that is fond of camp cretaceous. Really good with the according extension, and how excited my son is when sees "the real one" like in his show makes the purchase worth it on a hefty discount. He asks to play it almost every evening these days !Overall, the game is fairly made, and really chill in creative, so great for kids. There is some difficulty to be had in challenges, so one shouldn't get bored too quick.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: A tad bit too much micromanaging for my taste. The aquatic reptiles can't do much and there's little customization for lagoons, but aviary enclosures are great. Electricity can be managed much better in this game than the first one, there's a ton more customization in terms of buildings and how they look. More ways to change the environment then before. Dinosaur models look better, and there's tons of dinos to choose from. Overall, I'd say it isn't better than the previous installment, but it sure isn't worse. If you liked the first one, you'll enjoy this one. It's basically the first game with slightly different managing mechanics, different maps, different campaign/story, and new dinos.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: A really strong title for designing a great park with a lot of new features over Jurassic Park - thank you for the hatchery air-lift! But in exchange extra micro-management has been put in which adds frustration - status checks being less micro-managed and better AI on the vehicles really needs to be put in just for quality of life improvements. Anyone who wants to build a great dinosaur park should definitely play this, but if you're after a challenging builder where you can fail due to the game being hard then I wouldn't recommend this - it's for building and enjoyment not for the challenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: You have to mirco manage everything! Oh dinosaurs are fighting be prepared to spend half your time healing them only to return them to need to be healed again. This game you lose hours and it filled with bugs in which make it really fun for the first hour or two but then they start to hit and you can't do a damn thing but wait another minute or two for funds because you can't break past 3.4 stars. Then get ♥♥♥♥♥♥ over by some natural disaster. I hate this game, I really wanted to like it but there is just so many things that make me just want to punch my screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for quite a while for a huge discount on the Premium Edition, luckily, seems like Humble Bundle fulfilled that wish of mine.Back in the day, I used to play Operation Genesis a lot, so seeing its descendants brings me nostalgia and joy, to see that it lives on.Now, let's talk about the game.For a zoo management game, it's pretty damn good, well, maybe not as good as Planet Zoo, but for someone who's also a dinosaur nerd, like me, this is more right up my alley.Gameplay itself is very well-polished, but can also be pretty complex at times, but that's actually one of the pros, since it leaves you with more room for creativity. And the graphics, holy cow, they look and behave so realistically, like how they do in their movies. So yeah, you're guaranteed to be overloaded with immersion. That is, if you don't mind occasional bugs that can ruin your moments sometimes.To summarize this, if you love dinosaurs and you're a big fan of either Jurassic Park or World, just grab this.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of the "improvements" just add busy work. A good example of this is with assigning rangers to check out a dinosaurs status instead of being able to just see it. I get trying to add realism to sim games can be important, but not when it becomes tedious.The fact that they have a big button on the main menu that says "UPGRADE TO DELUXE EDITION" after I just spent $60 isn't exactly giving me a lot of confidence. I expected there was going to be DLC eventually, but day 1 DLC is disgusting.Overall it's okay, if you liked the first game you'll probably like this one, my advice is wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: After playing this game for couple hours i think im ready to give it a honest review. So lets start.Pros:-Better animations when compared to jwe1-Better textures and models when compared to jwe1-Marine reptiles (yay)-Multiple improvements in terms of gameplay (time acceleration, more in depth management, -More customizable buildings)-Better dino ai when compared to jwe1-Egg incubation reworked which makes more sense considering jurassic park lore than the system we had in jwe1.-Chaos theory gamemode, In my opinion its the true campaign of the game-New skin and pattern systemNow lets move onto the consCons:-Animations and models glitching quite frequently-Sometimes ranger team pathfinding is awful-Micromanagement (i will go more in depth later)-Sandbox mode needs a LOT of grinding in order to have everything unlocked-Ranger outposts.... just why frontier-Campaign is really short. Although the chaos theory mode more than makes up for itNow i will clarify on that micromanagement point. Yes the scientists are generally a good addition but it can get really tedious, especially in late game.  But i think that some tasks should be automated. Like healing a injured dino or excavating fossils. Also there is a fact that sandbox mode still has scientists which is pretty dumb in my opinion.Conclusion:Would i recommend this game right now?If you really like dinosaurs then yes, otherwise i would wait a couple weeks. But its by no means a bad game and is definitely an improvement when compared to the first one

_childDocuments_.review: After beating the campaign, chaos theory modes, and all the challenges on the hardest difficulty, I can confidently say I like this game lol. This game is marred with bugs, glitches, Frontier's iconic bizarre design choices, and every so often you just have to restart hours of progress. But, if you are willing to research and learn to work with the game's mechanics instead of blunt-force making a park, you will find this is the best and most complete dinosaur zoo-making experience there is. I have every hope that Frontier will work past their strange decisions and make this game the most perfect Jurassic World Simulator there is.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't feel this game was worth the price I paid for it so far, having gone through campaign and working on challenges now. I say that entirely because I also own the first game. While there are some  improvements to the game from the first one, core issues still remain and they've managed to add new ones! The amount of new content seems low for the price and the campaign is choppy - feels rushed and unfinished.  My main complaints thus far:- Terrain issues still persist from the last game. - At least one map has been reused.... with different foliage.- They COMPLETELY failed to fix the issues with not being able to build anything around the edges of the map, even when level. Often there's enough space for an entire building where you aren't allowed to place things.- Still can't fully utilize said space with enclosures because you get the error that you're trying to build fences outside of the map when you very clearly are not- You now can't drive vehicles through anything that looks slightly bushy. Even if there are no trees directly in front of you. It's not frustrating at all :)- Ranger vehicles still still sit there and state the have no clear path to do something (cough, check on welfare posts, cough) even though they do have a path.- Expeditions are crazy expensive now WITH NO WAY TO SELL FOSSILS WITHOUT FIRST PAYING A PREMIUM THAT USUALLY EATS AWAY MOST OF THE PROFIT, literally WHY WOULD Y'ALL DO THAT- Did you accidentally train a Scientist in the wrong skill when you needed a different one? Well too bad you can't undo  that, your only option is to fire someone. - Changing the type of amenity between shopping/food/drink takes way too long. When you click on an amentiy to build, there should be a sub menu to select which kind so you don't have to go through the process of changing it for every store you put down.- Campaign mode is pretty much lifeless and extremely short, still with terrible dialogue. Feels choppy and unfinished, as stated before. The only time there seemed to be a plot cooking in the last one, there was no resolution... just ended.- Also INCREDIBLY FRUSTRATING. In one mission a dinosaur can't have anything else in the enclosure.... BUT THERE ARE WILD COMPYS everywhere WITH NO WAY TO SEE THEM ON THE MAP!!!!!!! No indication of how to fix the issue!- Some research tasks cost an exorbitant amount of money for no reason. Who thought it made sense for SCIENTISTS to need to RESEARCH how to build a main walkway for $500,000??? Why is that at the end of the research tiers, when you need to plan spacing and have no way to properly do that without being able to create a walkway? Come on!- Flying dinosaurs get stuck in the flying animation constantly.... you can't fly the drones manually or do anything, so the only option you have is to tranq them. Then.... THEN, you can't "reset" them by putting them in the same aviary. Only a different aviary.  Only real option is to restart the game. - The color/pattern idea looked cool but seems very limited. - Speaking of, why do you have to research a bunch of genetic traits before skin stuff? Would it not make more sense for simple things to be at a lower tier? The highlights:- Live capture events are cool- Random events are an amazing addition- Social interactions are much better, big props to the team for a job well done- animations in general are better- A lot of models look nicer- weather looks better too- Manifestation of traits is cool- Finally, aquatics- Dinosaurs

_childDocuments_.review: This game breaks even on the £1 an hour entertainment point at this stage and I'm not done with it. I've enjoyed it and would recommend it. It's not perfect and I hope my review might be read and the recommendations considered for a future version.So I think most can visualise the theme park type RTS this is, to concentrate on its high points as follows:The DInosaurs are very well done, especially the animations, variety, sounds and complexity of this main feature. All too often a game centered on one thing can miss a mark and this one puts the love and effort in where it counts. I think all that could be missing is baby dinos. I think that would change the game entirely and needs a lot of work, but if I was a project manager I'd know it sold copies if the nurturing stage of a dinos life was added to the game. This game should concentrate less on the tedious parts of park building like the electrical grid and more onto the micromanaging of the dinos to keep people looking at the great graphics.After 19 hrs I had completed the campaign stories, which are more like tutorials and ventured directly to the sandbox. I realised that there was missing preparation here. You have never been taught about transport systems, attractions, amenities and shops, economics, fossils, hatchery or even the seas creature segment! A huge part missing it seems in the story mode.During the sandbox mode I could see some balancing in the main game that is required.Firstly; the electric grid for power is the most annoying feature ever. I can see why its part of the game with electric fences but only a storm seems to affect it and otherwise it makes your park look ridiculous. No one likes that. The days of pylons are over and it doesnt fit with a themepark.The scientist bottleneck took hold quite early when I realised that once you have a couple of dinos up and running and making money, you really should be racing your scientists and research hard but ultimately almost the game is over as your threats will not touch your park. I didn't mind so much, but it seemed to be a waste of time throwing research effort into new species or even avian and underwater dinos, i was a multi millionaire with a few big carnivores.Lastly, there was nothing that really caused me to experiment beyond the basic box pen of dinos and not mixing them. There's a stat that increases photos with more going on and more species, but I never for example felt like introducing a single T rex into the herbivore paddock was going to be a money spinner. I'd show up for that... a viewed dino fight should be newspaper material and encourage economic growth. Personally I think the park should decay if its not revamped more, has more interesting changes over time and thus has a economic decline to force the player to reinvent themself.Overall pretty good, could be much better. Picked it up in the sale, YMMV.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is clearly designed for people who are familiar with the previous version. If you're new to Jurassic World Evolution (as I am), expect to face a very steep learning curve (as I did). I have played almost twelve hours, and have spent as much time searching the internet for information on how to play as I have playing the game.The game is very good at telling you what needs to be done, and very poor at telling you how to do it. That's really rough on a game as complex as this.But the graphics are amazing, the dinosaurs are amazing, the voice acting and scripting are... well, not amazing. Just be prepared to spend a lot of time being confused as you try and join in the fun.

_childDocuments_.review: To be honest, this game is average at best, considering the price of 60$ for the entire game, it feels like a rip off. I got it on a steam sale, but i still feel robbed. I had my go in the Capmain and the Challenge mod...and sandbox Let's start with the good things: Dinos (main purchase argument tbh) Nice and crisp visuals Modable (no direct mod support) First person driving and flyingNow strap yourself in for the bad stuff:Building:In tight spaces, building stuff is a nightmare; most buildings need enormous spaces around them and beware of tiny ass bumbs and hills because this will lead to the message, that there is a terrain constraint. However building things in mere cliff-like inclines works like charm tho. Whenever you place a building the terain gets flattened, nothing wrong with that but it will make your roads and pathways look like a ninja warrior track, just without the fun obstacles. Pathways, tours and monorails lack the option of tunnels, bridges, ramps, stairs and physics in general. The monorail, due to its elevation is kinda allright tho. The roads and tours just stick to terrain no matter what, no matter the incline or slope, your NPCs will happily walk everywhere. These things look just wrong. To fix the constraints, there is a mod, which I highly recomend, called: Free build (No 1 on Nexus (surprise) (not really tbh))Weather: The Tornados are as much fun as fixing the blade of lawnmower, while it's running at full tilt. You will end up fixing your park a lot. Dino lifespan: Realy short...you will burn through some dinos as fast as Charlie Sheen burn through an ounce of Columbian snow. Park Rarting: Looks very random, it is, but mainly the visitors are suckers for big teeth dinos, the other 40-odd dinos could die and rot and your rating of the park won't move an inch, but it goes all south when the T-rex bites the dust. Visitors:Picky eaters, just fyiAnd as lazy as Dice when they have to make a Battlefield Game...walk for 10 Minutes? what a wild concept..they will demand transport, then walk anyway.  Over and underexplanation:Something a lot of games suffer; they take you by the hand like a toddler, telling you to look around and click and double click....and after that they throw 30 more mechanics in your face without bother telling you, leaves nothing but google to help you (Thx Google) Map Size: While the Maps are nice and come with enough varity, they are tiny...and not in a convenient shape (that's not a negative point, I kinda enjoyed that one) But if you are too generous with the cage sizes in the story mode, good luck reorganizing the entire park, or just restart. Also there is a Mod "Expanded Parks" on Nexus to enjoy a bit more area to build in the sandbox mode. Sandbox mode:Usually Sandbox modes are there just to have fun, make the perfect game, get the eyes on high lvl stuff or fool around, usually everything is doable, adjustable and playable. I open with that because as it seems the devs. have no idea what a sandbox mode is, since you need to unlock everything in other modes to use in sandbox (R+D is disabled). Since you can't R+D Dinos and go on expeditions in Sandbox, it's utterly pointless to play if you have less than everything unlocked. Worst Sandbox ever. Here there is another mod, called the "100% savefile" just to enjoy the sandboxMicrowave:The game features a lot of buildings, that sounds good, but some of them are in there 3 times over, just in a different skin, this is unneccesary since you are able to customize buildings in the game (Restaurants and shops) to fulfill a different function, it would have been great to customize some of the buildings like the Dino-Doc, the response Team, the arrival point as well. Customized Restaurants, Bars and shops:On the surface, this is a good idea, but renders itself pointless in advanced stages of the game, since the same upgrades will do the same things over and over again, you end up picking the same 5-10 upgrades every. single. time. great fun, many change. Terrain editing:Not too bad, the only thing that's annoying is the tree brush that seems very unmotivated to do its job. Story: Well I've told there is one, but tbh it's not any good, you are basically a disaster response team that builds cages in 5 different places. Dialoge: My recomenadtion: Subtitles on and sound off Agro-Saurus:Herbivores, attack each other...luckly theres a mod for that as well.Ninja Dinos, and dumb as ♥♥♥♥ dinos:Either your dinos will find a 0.0003 Inch gap in the fence, where they will squeeze through and "break out" or they will ignore the food, water and open gate around them...there is no in between. Those dangerous gentle creatures: Every dino, not husked by a fence will be a "threat", makes sence for the T-rex, but it also counts for those dinos who move slower than slugs and eat leaves......we got petting zoos with tigeres in real life....just to compare. No reproduction: Why do the dinos lack the need to reproduce? The lack of shagging and baby dinos is just wasted potential, like an EA game without microtrasactions.  Staff:Lazy ass stuff, works 5 times, then needs some rest for the low low price of 15k a minute....my boss would so fire me: "Sorry chief, i made these 5 mails, se ya tmw" Value: For a 60$ you get 15 maps, 117 buildings (some of them multiple times, therefore it doesn't count) 8 Water Dinos, 8 Flappy bois, and 57 Land Dinos, 4 Game modes, an add to subscribe to something, that will probably just fill your spam folder, nice graphics, Jeff Goldblums voice, T̶o̶u̶r̶e̶t̶t̶e̶s̶ Tornados and the least fun Sandbox mode apart from real life. TL;DR Playable with mods, wait for a steam sale to buy it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played the first game, buy this. If you have played the first game, do not buy this. There simply isn't enough new content to justify charging for a whole new game. The aquatic and flying creatures are cool, however, the novelty wears off rather quickly and you're left with what feels like the same game as the first (in fact worse in some ways). The lack of individually placeable trees is gone and some of the decorations from the Return To Jurassic Park DLC is missing. Not to mention the absolute GRIND you have to go through to gain access to all of the dinosaurs and unlock all of the buildings. As someone who wants to play this game for sandbox alone, it's kind of a drag that I have to put in the hours into Chaos Theory and Challenge mode when I have little to no interest in playing them. There are some items that have the wrong names and some settings that are also labeled wrong. To add insult to injury, not even one month after release, they release a DLC pack. Come on, Frontier... Simply put, it's unpolished and a hollow version of what I know it could have been. The idea of this game is fantastic, and the fact it is made by Frontier still gives me some false hope that this game can be updated and turned into something a little deeper and a little more fleshed out, however deadlines and pressure caused by what I assume to be Universal, making creative decisions and limiting the developers on what they can and can not put in the game. This is simply not the game that I was hoping for.

_childDocuments_.review: Game's pretty lame.As a construction and management sim, it's perfunctory at best. I mean, it does everything just in the most boring and bland way possible.There is no challenge. No variety. Every game is going to play out exactly the same. The game's basic loop is dreary and dull. Build some facilities, send scientists out to gather dinos and research, repeat. Occasionally deal with a sick dino or a breakout which shouldn't happen if you're doing everything right, which is easy. Occasionally there's a storm that makes you have to go around clicking on all the buildings and fences because pointless busywork is fun I guess.The campaign is particularly lame. The number of missions doesn't extend past the single digits. Half of them are preschool levels of "difficulty." The rest of them are grade school levels of difficulty.The settings are weird too. Like I had my first sandbox set to have a high rate of dinosaur collection opportunities. I was getting them every six minutes. So then I set it to low and I never received any dino collection mission. At all. So apparently the low setting is the same as the off setting?Pleasing your guests is simple. Guests have individual needs but none of them are difficult to fulfill. Dinosaur behavior... exists. Although there isn't a great deal of interaction beyond what you'd expect. Provide their needs, don't mix dinos that don't like each other unless you want them to fight and break out. It can be fun to pit dinos against each other but the novelty wears off and it's ultimately not worth it. Every dino has an appeal rating but your guests don't really care about it. One dino's as good as any other, I suppose.You've got your basic smattering of rides and attractions, but nothing beyond what you'd expect. None of them are particularly interesting. Messing around with dino DNA isn't the novelty you'd expect it to be. It's largely if not entirely irrelevant except to eliminate bad traits that can affect certain dino species. You aren't going to be frakensteining mind blowing genetic super freaks of nature or anything.Graphically the game looks alright, which is as much as can be said for it. Dinos look good. Buildings are nice. Terrain looks okay. I guess that's good enough.The game also functions... so it's got that going for it. I mean, when you tell it to do a thing it does it without fussing or bugging out. So that's nice. Vehicles can get pretty janky though. I didn't know dilops could throw Jeeps 40 feet into the air. JWE2 doesn't do anything new and it doesn't do anything well. I got it for $15 on discount and I still feel like I paid too much. I'm tempted to try for a refund, even though I'm past the play time.

_childDocuments_.review: Look... I do hate to keep thumbs downing otherwise pretty decent games for things that aren't directly to the game itself, but, this is a necessity, especially with this game. Why?2 reasons: The Premium edition does not operate like a Season Pass. So, if you, like I, bought the Ultimate edition or Premium edition previously which contained all the DLC, and then come back to the game months later, and new DLC is added to the game... those DLC are not part of the bundle you bought, and you'll have to buy them directly; Yet, the Premium Edition Bundle that's on offer for people buying the game now includes those DLC that you did not get when you bought the Premium Edition Bundle. So, not only is the Premium Edition a money sink that doesn't ensure that you'll be getting future DLC that gets added to that very same bundle, but, others will be paying for the exact same bundle as you but be getting the added DLC.I have never seen a Premium or Definitive Edition bundle on Steam operate like this. Of all the games I've bought that had either moniker, those other games by default added the extra DLC directly to my account without requiring an extra purchase, so, either there's a bug on Steam that only effects this particular game, or, more likely, the dev is selling those Bundles, deleting the Bundles and re-releasing the Bundles with the added DLC to avoid current owners of the previous bundle with the same name getting the added content. I'm pretty sure it's not a Steam bug since this issue has been around for a while with this specific game, and ONLY this game. I think the idea of Season Passes is inherently anti-consumer because that's a dev asking you to pay a separate price for DLC that they haven't made yet, and, in some cases will never make for whatever reason. That said, if the dev behind the game has a proven track record of doing as they say they will, it's more excusable. That said, it's far more ethical for those DLC to be released on a Season Pass than it is for a dev to Sell a Premium/Ultimate/Definitive Edition, and then delete those bundles specifically to add a new bundle which has the extra DLC for new customers, but forcing the current owning customers to have to buy that DLC separately. Sure, there's another bundle that has these recent expansions put together that's separate from the Premium Edition, however, at the same time, that's still an added price tag for a game I already paid a premium for to get the Premium edition. _childDocuments_.review: You guys surely outdid yourselves, Frontier. Let's break it down:GRAPHICS:Graphics are really nice. Well designed dinos, environments and objects. Love the designs in this game.SOUND:Same outstanding quality as JWE1, dinos sound really nice and environment sounds like snowstorms and windstorms are done quite well. Voice acting is also on point, both in english and portuguese(my mother language), with classic voice actors reprising their roles in this game(specially the Cabot Finch VA, whose jokes return in this game).GAMEPLAY:In this game, you are a jurassic park/world owner, much like the previous game and the old Operation Genesis. Researching technologies that speed up incubation, bringing dinosaurs to life from genomes and ensuring that the park runs well without accidents.There is A LOT of different modes to play. JWE2 has the usual modes like Campaign and Sandbox, challenge mode from PlanCo and PlanZoo, etc. But, also brought Chaos Theory, one of the most fun modes to play in this game. Reliving the scenarios from the movies was a brilliant experience from what I played. Also lots of different things to do, the new veterinarian feature dealing with diseases(rangers used to treat diseases in the first game) brings more complexity to it; addition of sea dinos, flying dinos and lots of others...Dinos also fight and they are quite fun to watch when fighting. I did put a tricera in a velociraptor pen to watch the fight and dang, the tricera hits quite hard. Seriously, it's way too fun to watch the fights.Also, now you can have a central incubator(hatchery) and transport incubated dinos to other enclosures, which saves a lot of money. The dino release button is back. And you can get from 2 to 5 eggs when incubating and you can release them all in the same pen or select which ones to release and which ones to move to other enclosures.And, we got Aquatic DINOSAURS!!!CONTENT:There is a LOT of content in this game, lots of dinos, utilities, modes and other things. I was surprised when I saw the number of dinosaurs that came with this game by looking at the game's dinopedia.Overall, I do recommend this game if you want to cool off building a dinosaur park, want to put dinosaurs to fight and watch them or relive the scenarios from the movies.Thank you, Frontier!

_childDocuments_.review: To sum the game up, it's JWE but better in its own way. There's new dinosaurs, dynamic new enclosures like the aviary or the lagoon with corresponding dinosaurs to inhabit those. Better graphics, better audio and better tools for decorating your park as you see fit, however.The thing's I'll complain about:I miss the individual sectors buildings, like the science building or the security building etc. Those extra buildings just helped really spice up the look of your parks so they aren't just all the same buildings copy pasted every now and then along your paths, they forced you to find a designated spot for these very specific buildings (if you even wanted them in the first place).This also goes for the storm defense buildings, yes there are building upgrades that adds storm defense to that specific building in this game, but I personally don't like that and often find myself using that upgrade slot for something far more useful. I also liked having that storm defense building to have to construct if I wanted my buildings protected and honestly it was a really good system, get a high range with low protection or short range with high protection. Also like the specific sector buildings, the storm defense buildings also helped spice up the look of your park.Now onto the pathways, I like all the paths they are just as nice as in the first game my only complaint about them is that they don't have those automatic Jurassic World banners on the larger paths anymore, if you want those you'd have to manually place them down one by one which honestly is way more trouble than its worth. I'd love to just have it as another path option to have banners going down the center, or to choose the alt version same size without banners.Now to the campaigns, I love them I truly do and there are a heck of a lot more levels to play on which are each equally just as enjoyable and unique. My 1 complaint is, in most of those missions I never felt as connected and invested in my parks as the missions usually didn't last longer than an hour or 2. While in the first game each "mission" was an entire level where you had to meet specific requirements to progress in the story and to progress to the next level, HOWEVER you always had the option to stay on that specific level to continue building it and upgrading buildings which would stack with other levels building upgrades, so by the end you'd have super upgraded systems and research. There is none of that in this game, yes there are more levels yes there are more campaigns, but no you won't feel invested in your park as it will just disappear as you leave the level to start a new one (yes you can save the game and go back to it at any point, but without upgrades or any incentive to actually fully develop a park, why would you?).Despite all the negative things I've had to say so far about this game, I still think it's wonderful and definitely worth a try at least. I will refrain from calling this game "better" than the original JWE, it definitely is better in some parts, but is certainly worse in others. This game is great, but so is JWE 1, I highly recommend both games. (and no I wont be adding things I like about the game other than I just LOVE it, just cause I don't wanna write a review as long as the dictionary)

_childDocuments_.review: I'd mostly recommend this game especially if you enjoyed the last one and really love dinosaurs (OMFG I LOVE DINOSAURS!!!) but there's plenty i hate as well. At first i hated how there are individual scientist mechanics but i grew to appreciate that they were basically characters that i had to take care of the same way you had to take care of dinosaurs...but im not so much a fan of how they need to rest so often even after not working, more so how i need to pay 75k to let them rest. JUST GET IN BED! ITS FREE I DO IT EVERY NIGHT!I also felt like the technology and required buildings were a little bit overwhelming...first time playing it i must have spent hours scouring through the tech tree trying to figure out what i needed next. Im not a fan of how you need to research dinos before digging them up like the bones are all ready there why do i need to know what they are before hand? It doesn't make any sense unless you flip the two mechanics around. It makes more sense to dig up bones and then research them and then scan them...better off just removing the dino research function its self. I also experience crashes at least once every 12 hours, probably a fault on my end but still frustrating. I've experienced numerous glitches including helicopters crashing and remaining permanent eye sores for the rest of the play through, and its even worst if they were carrying a dinosaur. Occasionally guests wont appear on screen, there are times where guests wont use amenities, etc etc. Despite the glitches its still 100% playable. There are no shortage of maps and modes to play on unlike the last game, there's a decent variety of dinosaurs, the character dialogue is mostly enjoyable. Theres sh** tons of DLC if you somehow get bored or complete everything, I only wish there were more variety when it comes to non-dinosaur creatures.
