_childDocuments_.review: Loved the first Jurassic World game and was excited to see all the new features in the sequel with aquatic and aviary animals, as well as the dinosaur "hunt" mechanic. But upon starting the game you are treated to one of the worst campaign modes, and when finished with that you can go to the original Movie Locations to do more missions. These, maybe even worse as they last around an hour and seem to have nothing to do with the original movies. The challenge mode feels like how the game should be the only problem is its all timed and you have to do everything to get the max park rating, so it takes away any creativity you have. Sandbox is fine besides not having everything unlocked unless you play everything else and win (including challenge mode), it gets boring quickly as you have no objectives or tasks to complete. The foundations are good, the graphics and dinos are great but once you start playing you quickly run out of meaningful things to do and are left with boring hand holdy extra mods, a flat 4 hour campaign, and a bunch of time trials.

_childDocuments_.review: It adds new things to do while idling, and more ways to play than the original, while still maintaining (mostly through DLC) the classic challenges and Frontier game modes you may expect..The Story is extremely lacking, and essentially just one long tutorial. It is disappointing in scope, scale, and execution compared to the previous game. The best additions are new gameplay loop elements and the ability to travel beyond the borders of your park with Ranger teams to take photographs and capture Dinosaurs you can then transport back to the park. At first, I was extremely disappointed in the title because the Story mode feels like an afterthought.However, through the classic scenarios of the films, bonus DLC, and additional gameplay elements they have added, I can fully say this game is a more diverse, open, and involved Jurassic Park/World game than the previous title, and certainly the better game of the two.I have seen some people note performance issues/crashing..but on my PC it ran like a dream, never had any issues with performance, crashing or load times, and while it isn't the greatest visually, it is one of the best Frontier games I have played visually, and much more diverse in settings than the first game.Overall, the more I play this game the more I realize it is simply more than the first, and if you are a fan of other Frontier games, Dinosaurs, and/or management games, this one is pretty solid especially considering the films associated with it. I can highly recommend it myself, as a fan of games like it, and having now seen the breadth of options available to the player compared to the previous title. If you want a deep management  game you might want to look elsewhere, but this one has just enough action and depth to keep me truly invested

_childDocuments_.review: Jurassic World Evolution 2 is definitely a game that I recommend any Jurassic Park or World fans as well as just general dinosaur lovers buy. There are so many more aspects that the developers have added to the game such as amenity modules and ranger posts to really make it a true park development game. The variety of dinosaurs that this game has to offer is insane. Without any DLCs, you should be more than occupied trying to fit all the dinosaurs into 1 map. The Story mode gives you a great taste of what the other modes such as Sandbox and Challenge modes will offer you. I'm yet to complete the Chaos theory but have very high hopes from playing basically every other mode. There is still some touching up that needs to be done to a couple of things. I hope that the developers are looking into fixing a couple of the dinosaur roaming issues such as them doing a full revolution on the spot to change direction, or doing a weird-side stepping thing to start the hunting animation. Also, the game would just be made that little bit better if they made it so the dinosaurs couldn't just walk straight through each other. I suggest maybe adding an animation where one dinosaur gets angry at the other for the contact by the other. All in all, the developers have definitely taken a big step up from Jurassic World Evolution 1. From playing this game, I can definitely tell you that the step up was very much so worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I have decided to delete my review and start over because my opinion has changed since my last review. At that point i had done 35 hours with the game and now i'm 75+ hours into it and my opinion has changed. I can no longer recommend this game and i will get into why but right now i just want to say i wanted to hope everything we wanted in the last game would be here and the issues we had would be fixed but while some were fixed others remained and a lot of the good from the last game didn't even make it into this one. I have completely stopped playing this and until mods fix the issues in the game (cause we know frontier won't) i will continue to not play it. It is not worth the money they are charging for it, they could have done a massive update for the first game and it would have sufficed but no this obviously is just another cash grab. The reason i say this is it's exactly like the first game, just new features. Everything else is the same. As Ian Malcolm once famously said, "That is one big pile of sh*t". Look when i first played this i wanted so bad for it to be good that it blinded me to the issues that were staring right in front of me. There is a lot Frontier got right, from the scientists to the dinosaurs but they fell hard on a ton of things. The biggest issues I have with Evolution 2 is the maps. This was on my last review but now having unlocked everything i see how truly awful it really is. They are so unbelievably small it's not even funny. Maps here are even smaller than the first game if you can believe it. Even the ones that are labeled "large" are too small to do anything. I'm sick of it. D*mn it frontier i know you can make a decently sized map. You have every opportunity to do so and yet you still refuse to to do it. "We want players to be able to be creative" You can't be creative when you have no room to do anything. When you have this many dinosaur species you can't give us these maps. All you have to do is make an island creator like in Jurassic Park Operation Genesis. You do that and the issue is resolved and you have more than enough types of maps to do it. I can not and will not play until this is fixed. Once you play a map once you have pretty much done everything you can and replaying them has become ungodly repetitive. There's also a ton of features from the first game that aren't in this one and items missing. Decorations for example no longer have single tress which is a huge missed opportunity. The guest side of the game too is again majorly lacking. Is there improvements to amenities, yes, but the way you guys did this isn't really user friendly. You should just have each type of amenity in the side menu like you did the last game. Nobody has liked having to manually go in to change the type of amenity. If JPOG can do better in 2003, you can do better. Not only that but visitors yet again are the same bland uninteresting aspect they were the last game. JPOG did amazing at this because they made each guest feel unique. They had a menu that popped up after selecting a guest and you could see where they were from, what type of guest they were, what they wanted to see/have seen, and what they thought of your park. That seriously is nice and i have missed it so much. It adds a really good aspect to the game and offers more content. JPOG also had many other things that were really nice additions like garbage cans, benches, rest areas, and cleaner stations that would have cleaner workers go out and clean the park. The cleaning station would at least be something else to add to the game to actually keep people's attentions. They also had the hot air balloon that went around the park. Something like that in this game would be next level. The fact the Operation Genesis could do that in 2003 but this triple A game can't do it in 2021 is a huge let down. Everyone has already expressed how the campaign is a let down. If the rest of it is going to be released when Dominion comes out then this game should not have released until the movie released. If this is it for the campaign you guys really failed so hard. I hope that it is just because of the movie because if it isn't i don't think i'll ever buy a game from you again. In the end it's the maps that are the biggest let down. I didn't like how small they were in the first game but i accepted it and in this one you went back no forward. It has made me not want to play this game. It is exactly like the first game albeit different maps (which aren't improvements but a step backward), updates to the dinosaurs (which really haven't changed other than the features added to them), buildings, JP era stuff at the start, adding the vets, and removing contracts for scientists. This legit could have been a DLC and it would have worked. Seeing that i realize this was nothing but a cash grab. The initial awe this game has worn off and i'm back to the same point i was with the first. Oh and that laughing stock of a first DLC should have been an update, it wasn't worth 7.99$. After careful consideration i have decided not to endorse your park. Peace out.

_childDocuments_.review: A lot of people tend to say a lot of negative things about this game. While some it is justified, this game is not like other games mad by frontier. Due to their agreement with Universal, their is only so much that they can add and do with the game. Just understand that- here is my reviewProsJurassic world evolution 2 greatly expands from its previous predecessor in multiple ways. This comes in the shape of -- More custmisobilty, from decorations to the shops themselves. - Improved skins system, much more cusmosible then jwe1- Option to use time speed which greatly reduces the time it takes to complete tasks- Much more fluent and natural animations- Improved dinosaur behavior that makes your dinos feel alive- Improved Dino needs- Territory system that allows dinos to claim land essentially- Plant system for the herbivores- Improved dinosaur needs, the dinos will need a certain terrain or water, etc.- Aquatic and flying species- aviary and lagoons- Medical team for the dinos- Multiple eras with associated buildings- Almost full dinosaur roster from the last game- New biomes and maps- New weather types- Chaos Theory Mode- Decent UI- Beautiful GraphicsNeutralThere are several things that I don't personally mind, but could use some fixes- Scientist system, its great, but could use to adjustments- Dinosaur aggressiveness, frontier work on this with their latest patch- Medical system, its alright but could use some improvements.- pack hunting, this feature could use some tuning up.ConsJurassic world evolution 2 has very few cons, but the ones that are is substantial.- Not enough decorations. While the ones they added improve the game a lot, they just need more.- Not enough attractions. There are only a few such as park tour or the guest attraction. Where are the baloon tours, the domes, the submarine tour. Just ass more attractions.- They removed placeable trees- Not too many new dinos were added to the roster. In all you might have about five new dinos, and like seven flying and aquatic reptiles.- Short campaign- ranger and medical teams can't go through tour gates anymore- No submarine tours, wait i already said that.Final reviewThe game itself is good if you enjoyed the last game or just keen on playing a simple park builder. If you are looking for a much more complex park builder like planet zoo or planet coaster, you are not going to find that amount of depth and complexity here. So if you liked the last one, grab it. If you prefer complex builders or your not a hardcore dino nerd like me, grab it on sale or come back and check on the game in four years! Otherwise I recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Recommending with some caveats. First, and this is the most important one. As of the time of this review, the latest Nvidia driver will BREAK the game. It will become unplayable and you will have to revert to an old driver before you can play it again.Secondly, I was getting frequent crashes for no discernible reason. My best guess is that the game was crashing under the weight of its own settings. Once I set it back to "High" preset everything was fine. I have a relatively high-end system, (i7-7700k, 3060, 32GB RAM) so it wasn't a compatibility issue on my end. Now onto the game. It's overall pretty good. It mostly improves on everything from the first game, and has more biomes and animals. However, they added WAY too much micromanagement into the game.For some reason they have you manually re-fueling generators and re-filling the food supply of the response team instead of having this be automated and simply deducting it from your budget. The wellness check system is also just bad. They have you putting these little nodes in all the different cages that the AI goes to and then checks on all the dinosaurs in order to see their status. This means when you get a new dino, you won't know what they need in their pin and will be racing their anger meter to put everything in that it needs before it breaks out and eats people. Just tell us what the animal needs like the first game.You also have to micromanage scientists. Instead of clicking on an upgrade and that's it, you now have to assign scientists that you hire and level up in order to purchase upgrades. These same scientists also help with getting new dinos. If they are busy with upgrades you can't get more dinos. They also have to rest, so you will have a lot of downtime for really no reason.You can get used to all these new systems, and it's really not as bad as it sounds, but if you have an eye for good design, you will quickly become annoyed by irrelevant and redundant things they have going on.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited Review:As a Jurassic FAN I have to say, after all the hype of Marketing and PR since this game was announced, I was very much looking forward to the release: Jurassic World Evolution 2!Now brace yourself for some Jurassic reading...After downloading the game and subsequently loading it, it basically just looked familiar and not at all surprising which somewhat is what I was looking for in a sequel game, to be blown away in one way or another. At least something that was going to leave me jaw dropped when I first opened the game.Still, excitedly, I launch the main Campaign Mode. It was, again, simply familiar and I must say that personally it under delivered.Moving on... I finish the first mission within the campaign mode and BOOM... game crashes when loading the second mission!I kept trying to reload the game and carry on from where it stopped me in my tracks but sadly after 3 more crashes I gave up and instantly left a bad review to the game out of frustration.The next day I validated the games files and tried again and it worked... this was to become a very much needed constant action whenever I want to play the game.Important Lesson Learned: before launching the game verify files or a crash is imminent after loading.After over 20 hours playing the various aspects of the game (Campaign, Challenge and Chaos Modes)... Here is a non-extensive list of the main likes and dislikes...Likes:- Mechanics are smoother- Graphics are improved- Storylines are OK but not mind blowing but the Chaos Mode is definitely a welcomed and enjoyable glossy tutorial- Visuals of content are definitely improvedDislikes:- Sandbox is still locked on the idea that you must complete all the tutorials (or Modes) of the game to actually be able to use the Sandbox mode!I mean if I don't want to complete the whole game in one go, why on earth are you making me do all the tutorials (Modes)  before I can freely build the park of my dreams... this actually puts me off from playing the game to be honest. I am paying a premium for something I can't actually enjoy playing! FRONTIER PLEASE STOP IMPLEMENTING THIS silly silly roadblock!- Constant game crashes- Constant having to verify files- Pretty much an open game for lathering us with an addition of DLCs in future years to come (especially as more movies get released of course)- Underwhelming voice acting for such a game but then again the scripting is pretty basic- Where is the deluxe content at?!?From everything that Frontier has learned from the first game... It's sad they decided to pick only a handful of things to improve and implement in a much anticipated sequel!Aside from the Chaos Mode, the smoother mechanics and visual updates, this game is most certainly not (in my most humble opinion) a full Triple A game worthy release.So no I am not recommending this game until you can buy it for cheap by which point DLCs would have been released and therefore the vicious circle starts...Frontier please get a grip and unlock the sandbox mode with all the game content available... This is my biggest peeve after the unstable performance and no, I do not have Jurassic components in my PC that would explain such bad performance before you all come for me!Well done for managing to get through this and thanks for reading.If it warrants future edits they shall come along...Original Review:For a game of this calibre to be constantly crashing when finishing the 1st Mission... I would have to start by saying the game is not worth the price, especially the Deluxe Version!Looks great and from the first mission the mechanics seem much better than the original from 2018!However I am still left wondering if at launch, this game is really worth it's cost, even if the game worked past the first mission!Will edit this review if and when appropriate.

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR: Not recommended at full price. If you want to play JWE, play the first one and the DLCs (and I recommend getting mods as well).I played the first game earlier this year with all DLCs, so I played it as polished as it would get. I didn't get into modding but heard many good things about them. The game felt complete by then, with a good variety of mechanics, good quantity of dinosaurs. What JWE needed was updates to AI, additions of aquatic and flying dinosaurs, variety in the "stores" system. As I am a huge dinosaur fan, I LOVED the first game and was very excited with the announcement for a sequel.So yesterday I played the Campaign and the first Chaos Theory Map. The game feels as unpolished as the first one in release day, before all the patches and DLCs. It's baffling how they decided to change every - I mean, every - mechanic, even the ones that worked really good, just for the sake of "not being the same as the first one". But they forgot about making them fun, I guess...I basically decided I will finish Chaos Theory mode, uninstall and probably go back to it in about 2 years when they announce the game will not be getting any more updates.Some examples:- The narration in the campain. It was fine, but they basically transformed Owen Grady into Andy Dwyer? Maybe it was the same in the first game but in this game it bothered me.- Scientists. I get the whole "crazy scientist" vibes they wanted to bring with the profiles and stuff but really, did we reaaally need to manage how "tired" they get after doing the tasks? Did we need to MANUALLY tell the scientist to go rest? I mean, I have been playing park games since Sim Theme Park and never had to tell a janitor to go to sleep...- Synthesis % incubation. Did I really need to assign a scientist to synthesize eggs and another one to incubate and hatch the dinosaurs EVERY TIME? I like that each scientist has their own attributes and modifiers, but why can't I assign them ONCE as "chief scientist officer" or something like that and from then on, when you do the process they use their stats?- Dinosaur injuries. Yes, we wanted more 'personality' to our dinosaurs, but really, did we want to have them CONSTANTLY fighting, even among their own species? I mean, yeah, we did, but we did NOT want to have to use a ranger to do a check-up of EACH DINOSAUR (mostly manually because the AI is really bad for this), then use a vet (again, manually) to check what the condition is, then use a helicopter (manually, but since it flies you don't need to actually pilot) to take it to the 'hospital' and then take it back? (oh yeah don't forget to ASSIGN THE SCIENTIST to heal your dino because the vets only have a degree in IDENTIFYING injuries/diseases, not treating them)- Power supply. It's very bad that the game teaches you to use BACKUP GENERATORS as the main source of energy. It's in the name that it's a BACKUP, but you - for some reason I CAN'T understand - have it unlocked by default and have to manually research the "normal" power.SOME PROS OF THE GAME:- Dinosaur behaviour and animation upgrades. Even if it's buggy at launch, the animals look and feel real, and this is the main focus of the game.- Guest personalities. I like that they wanted to make the "needs" system more challenging than just "reach max coverage". I haven't had the chance to play too much around this but I like it for now.- Building varieties/customization. That is something the first game needed SO MUCH and they delivered (I still think they went overboard when allowing us to customize almost non-visible stuff like wood color in the door for a building, but won't complain).- Graphics! The game is GORGEOUS to look at, from looking at the scenery, to looking at the dinosaurs up close, etc.WHAT THIS GAME NEEDS:- Rename Campaign to "Tutorial Campaign" and/or expand it. We need it at least to present aquatic animals.- Transfer EVERYTHING JWE had into JWE2. Go the L4D2 way of making the first one irrelevant because it's playable in the sequel. It's the same engine. Dinosaurs, buildings, even TREES, everything.- Add automation. Ranger Posts are nice (when they work). Add ranger pathing so you can control the route the ranger goes to check on their dinosaurs (increase range for check-ups, please, they have binoculars). Add vet automation (and make the vets act like vets).- Rework the scientist system. I know it's a gameplay choice, but it's BAD. As a suggestion, I would recommend Frontier to take a look at freaking Football Manager: you want a new staff, you look up the staff with the attributes/characterics you want, you offer them a job, you TELL THEM what to do (like assign training routines, etc), and THEY DO IT. You don't have to click once every 10 sec to tell them what to do.- Skin varieties when hatching new dinosaurs. My take on it: instead of going the JWE1 system but hatching 5x of each skins per batch, use a skin "theme" for the batch. I mean, if I choose "Alpine" for my batch, have the dinosaurs come in different tones of the skin (you added color palette to the game, use it). Maybe one dinosaur of the batch will have stripes, some will be darker, etc. If you want to take it to the next level: taller/longer, fatter/slimmer, stronger/weaker (defined abs), etc.- Addition to the path system. Add bridges to go over rivers/lakes. Add lookout areas. We don't need to go deep into Planet Zoo/Tycoon mode but it would be nice to actually plan out a park infrastructure like that.- Automatically remove Forest when placing Water (vice-versa). Also a QOL change, but it bugs me a lot when I place a new water source and the forest stays there.- Different colored helicopters/helipads! I mean, maybe this happened only with me, but during my playthrough, I tend to automatically click in the wrong helicopter in the world view when I need to select my Rescue teams.

_childDocuments_.review: Wait for a sale, Still buggy af------------------- CAMPAIGN REVIEW (3.3hrs)----------------Compared to the 1st one, it's vastly different. Not in a good way. There is no "amusement park". Just compounds, where you make pens for the dinos and cater to their weird needs; then bounce to the next location to do the same thing. You literally paint the ground with sand to make the carnotaurus content... paint is their description, not mine. Not even basic research is carried over from one location to the next.The main campaign is very short, I completed it in my 1st sitting. But don't worry, You will spend most of your time in chaos theory and challenge mode at this point.------------------- Chaos theory and challenge mode ---------This is where you will spend mode of your time. Classic park builder levels where you play out the 'what if' scenario; as to how you would handle managing all the parks from the previous films and game.challenges which unlock various vanity content. Neither of the two are a picnic, it is hard. Money is a killer. You will be restarting the levels a lot.------------------- Good, bad and not so ugly? ------------------Good: The graphics still look on point. Close details feel a little better than JWE1. The dino animations have been spruced up. Changes such as the response facility; it's both the ranger and ACU center as one building doing both fubctions. This great, genius; make a mod of it for the first game.Bad: New additions like the aquarium and aviary (which should have been in the 1st game tbh) however cool; feel unfinished and basic. Thumbnails, preview pics and index entries don't look as nice. More like looking at pics rather than 3d models.To me, the game still feels unfinished. If the final base game version for release was 1.0... this is close to a 0.8 early access instead. There is a difference between a new game with bugs and an incomplete game with issues. It really feels like they just phoned it in. Ugly: The poorly implemented ranger 'status check' system is more annoying and chaotic than anything.  This just creates unnecessary busy work to micromanage a function that was automatic in the 1st game. Just why? There is a good number of bugs, crashes, odd A.I behaviour and clunky menus; where it looks like a solid portion of game play is missing, unbalanced and just plain broken at times. All this leads me to believe this is a early release to meet a deadline n' cash in quick now, then fill in the blanks with "dlc" in the coming months. Final thoughts:I am trying my hardest to enjoy a game that is clearly half-baked. Restarting because of game breaking bugs and economy issues is the deal breaker for me.Will happily change this review once the game and it's asking price, reflect it's value.

_childDocuments_.review: #98 JWE 2So, i'm a bit torn on this.  I just finished the campaign.  My time says 7 hrs, but its more like 5.  Maybe less.  I have a habit of pausing and walking away for an extended period.  It has like 5 or 6 levels to the campaign, so it averages to about 1 hr per level.  Its short, and had paid full price i would feel ripped off.  But wait!  It has several other modes, like a sandbox, and a chaos theory mode.  Sure, ok.  I guess what i'm saying on this, the campaign was definitely second thought.  They wanted you to get outside the park, get in the vehicles, drive/fly around, then you're done.  I felt that was the worst part of the 1st game.  Getting in a Jeep or helicopter, driving around and fix this, take a picture of that, cure a  beast.  It was mundane, and it was made worse by poor driving mechanics.  This no different.  You're relegated to making holding pens for the dinos you catch.  The targets  you have to reach are small and honestly worthless.  In the first you had ratings of 10k+ to reach, in this, the highest was 3300.  So, it goes by shockingly fast.  The deluxe add-on adds nothing to the core game.  It gives you dinos and vehicle skins i never had access to, and the economy is non-existent.  You get money no matter what.  At one point, i was down to 750k, two minutes later i was at 10 mil.  So what did i like?  Its polished, it has a sandbox mode and you can hire and fire scientists.  Some of the mechanics in the employee range are different.  Like, you can overwork them.  The more tired they are, the less effective they are.  It costs money to let them rest.  The aviary level was slick, especially in how you crafted the aviary.  Oh, and Jeff Goldblum is back, so it has that going for it. Bottom line:  Get it at a steep discount, and only of the drive mechanics didn't p!ZZ you off.  Don't go into it expecting a major break through in the genre. 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: If you already played the first one, are interested in dinosaurs, and get a kick out of micro-management and park planning, this is a great (pardon the usage) evolution in the series!     Before I get in to what I think about the game-play, this game's graphics apparently are a huge step up from the 1st game. So, if you think to yourself, "I loved this first one, I'll go ahead and get this, too," be careful! I did that, and quickly noticed that where the first one ran at max graphics settings, this new one ran at absolute minimum and looked pretty gnarly, until I upgraded my (bought an expensive, new, RTX) GPU.     The main campaign serves more as a tutorial. It was a really gorgeous and engaging, albeit short, tale. (Which, I'm guessing was meant to walk hand-in-hand with the delayed 3rd JW movie entry.) I quickly moved on to where the true meat of the package showed up, and things really got challenging: Chaos Mode & Challenge Mode.     Chaos & Challenge Modes are probably where you'll spend most of your time, and have most of your fun. Here's what I am currently taking away from my experience with those parts of the game, so far:<>Managing staff stress levels and assigning appropriate crew to appropriate jobs is a big new addition that at first seemed tedious, but now I really enjoy! They put a lot of care in to the staff bios, and sometimes I find myself just reading about all the candidates' fake lives.<>Dinosaurs are way more wily, in my opinion, compared to the first. I felt like, in 1, once you hit your stride, have your shtuff all locked down, it was easy to afk and just build income. This game has way more random wrenches it will throw at you, making for a much more engagement-demanding dinosaur park sim. As it should be, imo.<>The dino models and animations are positively masterful. I fricking love JP dinos more than any childhood love, and to get to build their homes and see them strutting about with their pals, (or frenemies,) in their habitats is a delight I wish the 8-year-old-me could have lived!<>Challenge Mode has some really great 'tough choice' events that pop up sporadically and can really help or hurt your progress through some tough maps with fun rules built in! I am currently loving Challenge Mode, and it's a fun way to unlock some of my favorite aspects of the game: Dino Skins & Patterns!    It's a big time-investment if you want to do it all, but like all of the great sandbox games, it's meant to be played for a long, long time. If you just want a bite-sized thing, this isn't going to be that. However, if you are a dino-nerd with a penchant for building and design, you're likely to adore this well-made gem!

_childDocuments_.review: It's very rare that I'll actually review a game. And this game is an exception. It's not... amazing. It's a solid good game. But with a concession. It relies way *way* too much on RNG mechanics. Everything from the severity of common colds and pneumonia to the volatility of your animals. Even with an understanding of the Dominance system fight can and will still occur. Based on my experiences? I recommend the game. But some things need to change, as detailed belowPositives:+ The game is earnestly fun when it cooperates. It's one of the best park sims I've played, though that sample size is miniscule so sampling bias is very real. + The graphics are good, the designs for some animals are another story+ The Campaign is really good. It's fun and not overtly annoying like the first game+ The gameplay changes are largely positive, but with a major caveatNegatives: - There is no progression. The game advertises a proper gameplay cycle, but there's no difference between managing a 1 star park and a 5 star park. - There is little automation. Vets and Scientists are all manually assigned and rested, the game could be improved drastically with some automation tied to upgrades (which are themselves tied to higher star levels and numbers of scientists) - The variance within this game is INSANE, I've had friends who've earnestly lost their minds over the RNG ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this game peddles as difficulty. While I've been mostly lucky. I've seen it creeping in as games go on longer and longer. Especially in Challenge mode. Overall: I honestly do recommend this game. At its current price? No. After a couple updates that may change, but definitely. If you're curious. Or if you love Dinosaurs. Wait for the game to come on a large sale and pick it up. While I've had a lot of fun and I'm eager for more. Your experience may differ drastically.

_childDocuments_.review: I have really enjoyed this game so far, but there are so many little things that stack up and make it feel like playing is a chore. For context: I grew up with the original Jurassic Park trilogy, my favourite film was Jurassic Park 3, i loved the idea of all the dinosaurs adapting to the island and forming herds, while carnivores could be lurking around any corner ready to attack, the most exciting part of it all was how random it was, nothing set in stone, on an island filled with wild dinosaurs chaos will ensue. I understand Jurassic World Evolution 2 is primarily a park building simulator, but i think you misunderstand what the fans are really here for, the dinosaurs. Personally i enjoy creating hundreds of dinosaurs and letting them run wild in large open areas, but that becomes very tedious with all the park simulating and management tasks, along with all the wait times, especially in sandbox with the hatchery's taking forever to airlift several batches of dinosaurs. I am not very good at conveying what i am thinking into text/writing, and it becomes especially hard when there are lots of little things throughout the game that i dislike, so i will just point out somethings that stick out in my mind. 1# its very hard to be immersed in the game, aside from how stunning the dinosaurs look, there are lots of odd things that occur especially if you try to become a guest, dinosaurs attack vehicles all the time, but its so boring to witness, they lose a car door or the front end gets dented, why couldn't actual animations be implemented, in my 33.1 hours of game time so far i haven't seen any vehicle/destruction based animations from the dinosaurs, it makes it feel so fake. 2# Where are the hybrid dinosaurs? let me guess, cut content to be sold back to us in a few months down the line? i miss my spinoraptors. 3# the ranger patrol feature is good, allowing the jeeps to go check on dinosaurs for you is great and takes out some of the tediousness from the game, but what is annoying is that now my free range dinosaur parks are interrupted by random vehicles if i want to get a status check to see the dinosaurs stats/environmental/social information, this is dumb! 4# Texture flickering and other graphical issues constantly blind me when i am playing, please fix this! There are lots of of other little things, but i don't want to site here to type them out any longer, getting quite bored, honestly. I really do like the game, that is the reason i made this review, I have hope the game will improve with time and feel more complete than it currently does, but I am reviewing the game on how it is at the moment, and right now it doesn't feel like a big enough upgrade over the first game.6/10
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr: a decently put together, easy and relaxing game at it's core, worth about $45 if you haven't played the first one and like what you see, $30 or less if you have played and really liked the first one, do not buy if you felt the first game was mediocre. Avian and marine dinos should have easily been a part of the first game but the other core changes to gameplay I somewhat agree with having a new game for, essentially this is JWE 1.5.I have very mixed feelings about this game, firstly, I did acquire a totally normal copy outside of steam and explore some of the systems without worrying about the 2 hour limit. This actually managed to change my mind about one of my two main issues I had with a 'sequel' instead of further updates to the first. I realized that no, I don't think they could have updated the first game with a lot of the differences to core systems, so a new redux of the game made sense if they needed to change or tweak the engine for it. Secondly which was proven correct is there is not enough new content and changes here to warrant a full $60 price, the changes are nice but only worth about $30 (what finally pushed me to buy it) or less to anyone who's played the first game. What I believe should have happened was a half off coupon for those who had bought the first game for a week or so after 2's release, this would have lessened any "cash-grab" accusations. The only truly positive thing I have to say about frontier is to my knowledge they aren't scum enough to go egs exclusive, a low bar but it's at least something.As it stands with the above point and the dlc practices (as well as denuvo inclusion) frontier seems to employ, I doubt I will ever trust a frontier game without TotallyLegallyAcquiringItElsewhere first for a judgement and I would suggest others do the same if they can, I feel like the devs do really want to make a good game with what they're given but the corporate greed side will constantly be an issue for them.As for the game itself it's a fairly easy park management game, main pull being dinosaurs of course and there is some fun to be had with it, both campaign and chaos theory is mostly redundant nothing-stories and are mostly there to tutorialize. challenges are what I'd consider to be the standard mode but even on the hardest difficulty the only struggle is in the setup. past an hour or two into each map the cashflow should be way too overwhelmingly high to bother you much, I do respect that they made an attempt to apply more money-sinks in certain events and setting up automation is a little more intensive than the first game but even so it's a fairly easy overall experience, much like the first game, a management-lite if you will. I would heavily suggest against purchasing any of the dlcs, they offer very little.Addendum: after having completed the first challenge I was pleasantly surprised that challenges are actually just that this time around, having some unique conditions past the first one and the highest difficulty actually has enough economic balancing that money can become a real issue with the time constraint.

_childDocuments_.review: Very CALM and RELAXING game. Nothing too stressful and nothing too exciting. I'm more of a play-as-the-dinosaur type of gamer, but this isn't so bad, DLC's aren't too expensive if you buy them one at a time every couple months or so. It CAN be challenging at times but given enough thought and planning this game will become a piece of cake. JWE2 is also compatible with community mods, look online for JWE2 mods to add to the game if you've seen it all and want to spice things up a bit. If your more into intense action games, this ISN'T the game for you. If your all about spectating and controlling, this IS the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. I love the diversity of the dinosaur species, the improved graphics to the last game, as well as the ability to go into first person mode and control the rangers. There are however, some things I really would love the developers to add OR open up the game to Steam Workshop so fans can add these things so we can continue celebrating this franchise.1) I would love there to be more decorations. I really enjoy decorating my parks in the downtime of waiting for my  income to increase. Especially when playing the Jurassic World level, I'm trying to remake that feel of that park. More decorations and perhaps flowers would help this. I'm not sure if there are more that I'm just not seeing because I'm in Chaos Theory, but even so, I think the amount of decorations currently available is too sparse.2) I think buildings like shops and things could have more diversity? Being able to change the colors helps a little but I think this could be improved on as well. 3) Baby dinosaurs? I think its a missed opportunity to not have a separate building where people can see/pet baby dinosaurs.4) This could be me not understanding the graphic settings but I have toggled quite a few, and the game is still quite intensive. I think the campaign could really be improved on as well? It sort of just starts and ends. It also took me quite a while to figure out I had to configure my shops by adding modules to increase my revenue which would increase my star level. I think the game does a bad job communicating that to the player. Honestly this is a great game and it has so much potential. Thats why I really hope the developers open this up on Steam workshop, as I think the fanbase can really help this game blossom. The DLC adds quite a few dinosaurs but does little to improve the decorations of the game, so it can seem bland at times despite the interesting dinosaurs. With the addition of more decorations, flowers, perhaps even children park goers, I think this game could be even better.

_childDocuments_.review: Not gunna lie, very disappointed with this game. The amount of Micromanagement is absolutely insane, worse than JWE honestly. They fixed things that didn't need to be fixed and made everything more complicated than it needed to be. Plus, on top of all of this, the game just feels like a massive DLC to the original game.... Refunded.

_childDocuments_.review: Now I've heard lots of people complaining about the missions and guest comfort and that sort of stuff, but, in all honesty, to me those things don't matter. The detail of the creature models are good enough to look realistic up close. Although almost everything is locked in sandbox from the start, I did not mind the campaign. I also played 4 of the Chaos theories to unlock more stuff, then went onto challenge to unlock the rest. I did not mind the time it took to unlock things in sandbox and rather enjoyed every mode. I feel that the addition of pterosaurs and marine reptiles was much needed, and allows more variety in your park. I used to have a keen interest in palaeontology, and this game has reignited this. I hope that later DLCs will bring about the prehistoric life that I feel is missing. In the 60 odd hours I have played, I would strongly recommend this, even to people who aren't really into the Jurassic Park franchise. The game has some complexity, but not an excess that would scare off new players. The game is rewarding, although at times the progression can feel somewhat slow.Some slight bugs and slightly buggy AI are at times a nuisance, but in most cases by no means render the game unplayable.My overall rating for this game would be 8.5/10.EDIT: You can now have everything unlocked in sandbox from the beginning

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so steam doesn't give me the meh option.  Tldr: cool concept but an overall lazy design, Also game is INCREDIBLY expensive for its total content unless you're an average sim player so only buy on a salePros- You get to build a literal Jurassic Park of your dreams  Fun(ish) sim-like qualities and gameplay buffers to give a challenging aspect while still not being too difficult  Different game-modes including a campaign that sorta rein-visions some aspects of the story, as well as cool challenge game-modes that take the older movies and does a what if scenario where things didn't go haywire and what those parks would have looked likeCons- Very little cohesion with the world building aspect that this game could have  Somewhat buggy (at least from my experience) system for placing structures and somethings just stop working like the expedition center (normally pretty easy fix but still to keep in mind)  Limiting content outside of the sandbox mode in terms of freedom and decision making when building and laying out your parks  Voice dialogue that no matter how many times you hear it, cant be skipped aside from the few cut-scenes  The most egregious sin this game makes is not allowing for multiple saves in the sandbox mode especially given the 9 different locations you can build your parks. Even from a real world prospective, there would be multiple parks in real life if not that would be the biggest wasted opportunity in the world. As somebody who doesn't play sim games from the occasional boot up of sim city when I'm hanging out irl with friends and we get bored and wanna mess with the sims, the total amount of replay value drops instantly for somebody like me. A fairly steep price range IF you want all the game has to offer plus a few nitpicks but not deal breaking, (no option to turn off auto-save, The need for a decent amount of ram just to make sure things run smoothly once the park starts growing in size (tho this is purely because of it being a sim game), The fact that I put this game on an m.2 and it still takes a hot second to load a save file even at a relatively small size park with few dinos.)

They get stuck in mid-air and die of starvation. This has been a known bug for some time now.

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyable builder that has a conservationist twist to it, giving the player more things to do than just pure profits and amusement rides. I love all the little touches like getting to ride along with your guests in the cars as they go through the park. It instantly gave me the feel of being in the movies and the magic of it all again.
_childDocuments_.name: Jurassic World Evolution 2

_childDocuments_.review: 100 hours in, I think I have played enough now to give it a decent review.Firstly, this is much better than the original base game. Far more playable with far more scenarios and things to do... but it's not perfect.Why on earth isn't there a proper tutorial? Nothing is explained in detail - if at all - and everything is left for the player to figure out. Shops don't make sense, even after 100 hours and yet without balancing these perfectly, you won't get 5 stars.The stories are broken up into bite-size chunks rather than having one, flowing story - which is something I don't agree with but understand this is what the newer generation wants as they feel overwhelmed otherwise. Doesn't mean I have to agree it's the best way of doing things though.We finally get flying and swimming dinosaurs in the base game, but these are a little disappointing. Why aren't there lights in the lagoons so we can actually see the dinosaurs in there?And why can we not simply undo something when placing an item or deleting one by mistake?Chaos Theory is HARD (well, apart from Site B for some reason) so do everything else before you get there, so you know how to beat the challenges.It does feel a little rushed in places, there are minor glitches and bugs which hopefully will be ironed out soon and when the new patch landed, I had A LOT of crashes, but they seem to have stopped now.But even with all the negatives, these are minor compared to the hours and hours of fun I've had playing JWE2. I wanted to keep coming back and playing every day. I looked forward to beating the challenges and discovering more dinosaurs. It would REALLY help with a proper tutorial to guide you through how everything works, but at least now there is info online if you do get stuck.If you enjoyed the first game, you will love this one!

_childDocuments_.review:
Jurassic World Evolution 2 is the sequel to Frontier’s Jurassic World Evolution, building upon the 2018 management simulation. It introduces a compelling, new narrative campaign, incredible new features, and awe-inspiring new dinosaurs brought to life with captivating authenticity. Together with expanded construction and more customisation options, the result is an even bigger, better and authentic Jurassic World game.  

FEATURES

An Original Jurassic Story
Immerse yourself in a compelling and original Jurassic World narrative set after the Earth-shattering events of Jurassic World: Fallen Kingdom. Lead efforts to control, conserve and contain dinosaurs as you work alongside iconic characters from the films, including Dr. Ian Malcolm (Jeff Goldblum) and Claire Dearing (Bryce Dallas Howard). 

Create your own Jurassic World
Take control with deeper management tools and creative options. Construct and customise new buildings and flex your managerial muscle across never-before-seen locations ranging from dense forests to rocky deserts. Rescue and bioengineer more than 75 prehistoric species, including highly requested flying and marine reptiles , and watch them seek territory, fight and interact with staggering realism. 

Play with Chaos Theory
Chaos Theory mode lets you play through key moments of your favourite films - with a twist. Experience "what-if" scenarios from iconic Jurassic World and Jurassic Park films, with each level set across eras and locations from all five movies. Immerse yourself at the heart of the Jurassic World franchise and see how things turn out when you are put at the helm of managing new challenges with unpredictable outcomes.

Rash, Zitz and Pimple are returning at last to smash-hit their way through an all-new action-packed adventure of choreographed chaos, and couch co-op may never be the same again. 1-3 players will take control of the Battletoads and team up to storm through wild and unpredictable stages with only one rule – expect the unexpected. Teamwork makes the dream work in a drop-in, drop-out gameplay blast, filled with over-the-top gameplay moments that anyone can enjoy, but only a True ‘Toad’ can master. With a unique hand-animated cartoon style and packed with memorable characters and locations, the Battletoads are back for a larger-than-life brawl across the universe that promises to be fun alone, and unforgettable together.

_childDocuments_.review: Before getting the game I looked at reviews and found that the most prevalent issues among the negative reviews were that the game is "repetitive" and that it is not a classic beat 'em up. Decided to check it out anyways - I thought the addition of other game genres like platformer levels could be interesting and didn't see how the game could be "repetitive" if it tries new things.After finishing the game I understand why it got so many negative reviews and decided to write my own review to help others see what I missed. The main issue for me is not that the game is "repetitive", rather that it is lazy and uninspired.  The game goes something like this:Battletoads: Here is a tedious mini-game you will have to complete as part of the campaign.Me: Not particularly my cup of tea, but I appreciate you are trying something new. Done, can we do something else now?BT: Lol, no. Here is the same exact mini-game another 5 times.Me: -_-
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not going to lie, the game isn't bad at all, it's actually a very good game but I was still hoping for a slightly more classic experience,there is certainly a lot of variation in the game in terms of levels and type of gameplay and you will notice this quickly stage after stage, but if the game had been finished with a slightly lower cartoon content, I might have been able to experience it closer to the classic battletoad games places.Watch a snippet of gameplay here: Battletoads does a lot of things visually well and then it doesn't, but the game is therefore very accessible for all ages. As a result, the game is not too difficult and easily digestible, but the game will still feel very repetitive after long play sessions and it is therefore advisable to play the game in short bursts. Battletoads is therefore a nice game, even if only for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Apparently I'm one of the few people that grew up with the original battletoads AND loves this game.  The way I see it is we either could have gotten A) a poor attempt at recreating what the original had, with no real dialogue, endless combat that is the same punches and kicks over and over, with an even poorer attempt at the humor.  Or B) Something that is unique, very beautiful graphically, a variety of combat moves that is quite fun to witness, a variety of mini-games much like the first one, real voice acting that shows some real money went into it, and something that showed the developers were actually trying to make something for the fans.So what if they messed up on some things such as the queen.  I'll gladly take a few mess-ups over an entire pile of crap any day.  And to complain at a $20 price tag when we have so many $60 games that make you spend hundreds just to get cosmetics?  Some gamers just make me lose hope in humanity...
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Boring GameplayCringeworthy HumorDisgusting VisualsHorribly OverpricedBattletoads went from a dark and stylized TMNT inspired franchise... to an overpriced CalArts flash game. An NES game that has a reputation for being one of the toughest to beat... has been reduced to a series of minigames. Add to this some of the worst attempts at humor you'll ever encounter in the entire video game industry... and you have a recipe for disaster. The biggest crime of all though is how they massacred The Dark Queen. They beat her unconscious with the woke stick. She went from Heavy Metal Bombshell to Tumblr fanart. Gone is her sultry and villainous ways... she now resorts to schoolyard insults and rude gestures. But at least she isn't wearing revealing clothes, right? I've survived both cancer and corona... but this was pretty painful to endure.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: This game NEEDS online co-op. Split screen/couch co-op is just not enough. Besides we're living during a pandemic, we aren't supposed to have friends over.But it is a lot of fun. Steam Remote Play works. But we end up having to play on everyone's stream so they get the achievements. (if you care about those things)It mixes different game modes like the original games had. Challenging, but not too hard. I like that they have different difficulties so you can challenge yourself.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, the brawler sections are sadly the least fun. The developers made a bad choice in character design when it comes to enemies. They’re not clear in shape and therefore they don’t read. It’s hard to catch their tells, because they have so much unnecessary details that are more distracting then helpful when studying their movements. The more I kept playing I was convinced that the devs lack experience in the brawler genre. To me, the last turbo-bike section was the only one that does justice to the battletoads series. I do like the design style they went with, although I’m missing the term Queen in dark queen.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: This is the Teen Titans Go of video games. Teen Titans Go took a cool show and turned it into a derpy comedy. Same with this game!I'm glad I waited 26 years only to have the Battletoads no longer be cool, get jobs, see Rash crap himself in a diaper, cringey jokes, and preachy messages.The combat is actually really cool and well thought out. It just takes me out of it to see the toads no longer having most of there cool moves. Rash's axe kick and giant boot have been replaced with a chicken hand, nasty foot, and dead fish... So lame. Also to be stopped by puzzles every few minutes if not entire sections of the game is really annoying. I understand Battletoads isn't all beat'em up levels and that is fine and even a puzzle here and there I would be ok with but this many? Naw son. many of the bad guys are super lame too.The only way I was able to get through this game was because I was playing with my oldest friend that I grew up playing all the Battletoads games with.. Oh did I mention there is NO ONLINE CO-OP built in?  We had to do it through the steam thing. I'll tell you what doing a turbo bike level with lag is about as fun as stopping all progress in a game to smash your face into a wall. also when we played many of the levels we aren't even a Battletoad! We played those puzzle levels as the two stupid aliens that are with the Dark Queen. They couldn't even let me play as the Toads?! I know in single player that might be different. Just like Teen Titans Go has some funny moments and you can tell the team is trying. Same here.I wouldn't say it is a horrible game though. The animation (not the art style) is great.  Some of the jokes are funny. and the combat the short time you get to do it is fun. If those things I mentioned wouldn't bother you then I think you might enjoy it. I was fine going in that it was going to be a little different. I just didn't know it was going to be so lame.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting a "Battletoads and Double Dragon" or "Battletoads Arcade" experience. You'll be very disappointed. While the animation is decent and jokes are somewhat amusing, I found the game very lack luster. It starts out decent enough saying "Hey. We're beat-em up." but then afterwards devolves into a quick time event stage. It has a couple of turbo bike stages. Acts One and Two were decent enough and had beat-em up stages. Act three is basically the "Shoot em up and platforming non beat-em up." act. I get they were going for something there, but this is BATTLETOADS! BATTLE MOTHER FLIPPING TOADS!Act four was okay but I was hoping for more since they were basically fighting gods. lolAnyway, I don't recommend this game. I would recommend it as a tv pilot though.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the nuts and bolts of battletoads. The style is completely different from the originals that it's no wonder why people hate this game so much. But as a standalone game it's actually pretty good, the issue seems to be that people were waiting for a sequel of sorts in a modern style, but they rebooted it completely instead to the point of angering a lot of classic fans, however it's actually a good game on it's own just like how nuts and bolts would have been if it wasn't a banjo game.tldr: it's not what people expected, however it's still pretty good.

_childDocuments_.review: When I purchased this game, I was expecting a beat em up.  A game where you beat the living crap out of enemies with satisfaction.  This was not what I was expecting, you only play as the Battle Toads during the beginning, and the end...  That's it...  Everything in between is a cluster of frustrating and tedious puzzle games, mixed with a space shooter.  I can't even imagine playing this with friends.  This game had great potential, the animations and cut scenes were sensational!  Lot's of funny adult humor, and good colorful graphics.  The only time I was enjoying this game was when you play as the toads, which is only about 20% of the whole game...  The game is very short too,  I played it on Toad difficulty (normal) and it only took me 4 hours to complete.  I do not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: The biggest problem about this game, besides the fact it isn't a full-on beat em up but a genre free loader, is that it doesn't know when it overstay it's welcome. Your level of enjoyment will decline instantly once you get into that spaceship, run for your ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ life when you get to Act lll - The Pimples Joy of Life. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Divisive visuals but solid gameplay. Different doesn't mean bad. No online play option. Battletoads. A popular TMNT clone with a series of games in the 90's by Rare. Primarily a beat 'em up with platforming, it did mixup the gameplay throughout the various stages with different genres.  An iconic drumbeat would play when the game was paused.  It was famously difficult and is still considered one of the hardest games of all time.After a few cameos in recent years (KI and Shovel Knight cameos are both great) the Battletoads finally get their own game again. The end result is a good game but not without issues. Let's start with the art-style. The Battletoads and the Dark Queen (who used to look like Jessica Rabbit) have been redesigned with a modern, simplified look which I'm not a fan of (mostly DQ) but that's subjective. Remember we all had similar reactions to Wind Waker until playing it. Animation is a high-point. The characters animate very fluidly (easier to do with the simplified designs) so screenshots won't do it justice. Backgrounds look good too. Visually it looks very colourful, like a cartoon. It's a shame that no shaders were used to cast shadows and lighting on characters like other modern games to rid it of that Flash-look. The game has multiple difficulty settings and you can choose any completed level to start from. It is still far more fair than the original games even on the hardest setting.The soundtrack has some remixed classic tracks along with some original tracks. A couple of them are catchy but most made me miss David Wise. They're not inherently bad, just not memorable. I did notice in the beat 'em up stages that the music would be very soft, then a heavy track would kick in when enemies appeared, followed by that track fading out when they are defeated and then back to a subdued track. I get what they are trying to do, to make the soundtrack dynamic so that it goes with the action but I think the execution needed work. Perhaps if they didn't make the shift so drastic so that it blended and sounded like a single track that changes with the on-screen action. This could have been accomplished by the music subtly changing as you pass certain checkpoints and gradually crescendo with more instruments until enemies appeared, then go all out with the heaviest parts of the track. The sound fx are adequate and voice-acting is hit and miss but overall goes with the aesthetic. The Topians and Dark Queen performances being the stand-outs. Story has been fleshed out far more than previous games. Whilst I'm not a fan of the direction they went with the story (the jokes fell-flat more than they landed), it was refreshing to see the characters get some development for a change. The gameplay itself is a mix of various genres.  Beat 'em up sections feel more scarce then in most prior games. They've revamped the combat mechanics so that it feels unique yet still really good. There's a ranking system depending on how well you perform where you can achieve up to S rank similar to Bayonetta. Each Toad has their advantages with varying speed and power. The tongue-pull is a fantastic addition and lets you zip around the screen by pulling yourself into enemies or pulling them into you. Smash Hits are back, where the Toads limbs will morph into large feet, fists or random objects like an anvil. New Smash Hits are fine but how could they leave out Big Bad Boot? Stank Foot is not the same and makes no sense!I do feel like the combat feels SLIGHTLY off but is great fun if you're willing to learn it. Switching Toads during combos is almost a must for those S ranks. When switching, your Toad will enter with an attack that can be used to extend your combos. They were aiming for Bayonetta-style mechanics but I think they missed the mark (forgivable as it's still great). Combat stands out as something that a lot of thought went into and if they do a sequel they have a strong base here. I do wish combat intricacies and S ranks were explained more in-depth in-game. Note: Button-mashing will hamper your enjoyment!Some startup frames take a long time before the active hitboxes come out so you'll be hit out of it unless you cancel. Juggling enemies and zipping around screen with your tongue during combos feels great once you get it down. Toads can go between the foreground & background similar to DKC. Also characters will visibly change size on-screen depending on how close they are to the foreground which is a nice touch. Boss fights in the older games were always a weak point. Boss designs aren't as memorable here as the originals but fights are more interesting due to bosses having a wider array of attacks.In co-op there is a participation trophy awarded to the player playing the "worst". This system is poorly executed as my friend would spam jumping B with Pimple and as Zitz I would get the trophy despite pulling off long combos. All because Pimple hits harder. The speeder bikes are back but from a 3D perspective. Still challenging, still fun and one of the highlights of the game. They appear twice in the game but are nicely spaced apart. There are some DKC-style platforming levels that have no enemies but have stage hazards and simple puzzles to solve. In-between these are 3 shmup levels with a minigame at the end to repair the ship which itself is made up of numerous minigames. It's not too long but it's not enjoyable either.There are LOTS of minigames and if they ever do a sequel I hope they reduce them. There is diversity but most are so basic, not fun to play and hurt the pacing. There is a rock paper scissors minigame for instance that is short but you have to play it multiple times, almost back-to-back and it feels repetitive. There are some where you have to try and hack open doors which again whilst brief, aren't fun. I think Spider-Man PS4 has something similar but that game is huge.  I think that's a big part of my problem with Battletoads. They went for a genre mashup but needed to rein it in a little with those minigames. Also the DKC-style stages and the shmup stages would have been fine if they were spaced-out more across the different acts of the game. Battletoads Double Dragon had a shmup stage but it was one level so it broke up the gameplay and worked. In this game I found the shmup stages were quite fun, but they decided to reuse the concept multiple times in quick-succession. The chase levels in this game (Mis-treatied and Gut Reaction) got this right as they only appear once and are enjoyable.I admire that the devs tried to be ambitious (whereas Battlemaniacs was merely a fun rehash minus most vehicle levels). It felt different but I can also see that putting off some older fans. SoR4 was a more successful relaunch IMHO as its instantly gratifying. It still felt old-school, yet evolved.  For older fans it would feel like our nostalgia remembered it was like. Battletoads feels very different to the classics and in-turn doesn't feel instantly recognisable for series vets. It feels good but with more of a learning curve so I didn't have an instant appreciation for it. Series newcomers may be more accepting though. There are collectibles which are fun to collect but upon completion you only get an achievement. No unlockable alternate ending/art gallery. Nothing.An old-school mode with limited continues would have been nice too.Despite my gripes, I think the gameplay variety will help with replayability in the long-run. I found in 1-player, Battletoads started off average but got better after learning the intricacies of combat and replaying on hard (whilst going for all S ranks). Co-op is fun so if you have people to play with (why no online option devs?!) then co-op is how it should be played. Don't go into this expecting the Battletoads of old. Try not to let the art-style put you off, give it a chance and it's an enjoyable game.It's good to have the Battletoads back!

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads is a fun game. I've beat it solo and look forward to trying it on the hardest difficulty as well as playing co-op (which, if anything like its predecessors, should make the game harder.) I own Battletoads (NES), Battletoads in Battlemaniacs (SNES), Battletoads and Double Dragon (SNES) and the arcade game. I've beaten the SNES titles and arcade game, but not the NES game, which I think is the hardest of the bunch in a series that is defined by being difficult, muscle-memory based games. I say this to establish some credibility; I've enjoyed this series for a long time, but until I beat Battlemaniacs, I never really knew what this series was. See, most people never made it past level 3, the Turbo Tunnel, in the NES and main SNES game. If I had to guess, I'd say at least 95% of people who have played Battletoads have only ever experienced the first 3 levels of the game unless they used a game genie, which is kind of missing out on the real experience anyway.What I'm trying to get at is this: most reviewers who are trying to make some appeal to nostalgia should face some scrutiny; how many have experienced the original games in their entirety, or even close to their entirety? The series has always been an absurdist Saw-like meat grinder with an obnoxious difficulty level, and Rare made a new Battletoads game that sports an obnoxious (but wonderful) sense of humor. This game is most everything you ought to expect from a Battletoads sequel in 2020 and does a pretty good job honoring its past.Battletoads 2020 is arguably the most beat-em-up oriented the series has ever been (not counting the arcade and Double Dragon spin-off) and it's still not a beat-em-up. Battletoads has always been a variety game that offers a buffet of different level types. This entry includes side-scroller levels with several races like the old Turbo Tunnel and Intruder Excluder levels, and new additions, like bullet hell and platforming levels. There are also a bunch of fun and silly mini-games.The story never takes itself seriously, but the games have never had much of a story until now, so the cut scenes and dialogue are suitably ridiculous. The controls are solid and the graphics are crisp and clean, obviously taking note from current cartoon art styles. It can feel a little bit of a stimulus overload, but so much of the older games were built around stimulus overloads anyway that I think it is keeping with its heritage. Plus, it works artistically and the player gets the hang of it after the first or second level. My only minor criticisms actually revolve around the difficulty level and some characterization. A game that has the type of difficulty Battletoads featured on the NES just isn't going to sell super well anymore, but this game is a shade easier than the old titles. It gets pretty difficult in the later stages, which is good because. well, most players in the 90's only ever experienced 15 minutes of Battletoads content. A more gradual increase in difficulty is better. But I wish it spiked a little harder at the end.And as for the characterization issue, it's really just an art choice. Battlemaniacs (SNES) and the arcade game developed unique style for all the Toads' signature smash moves that you can see in the trailer. Zitz transformed his body into machinery, Pimple into blunt force objects like hammers and bricks, and Rash into more elegant bladed and medieval weapons. Zitz and Pimple are pretty spot on, but Rash now uses rubber chickens and fish and unkempt feet. It doesn't feel like it has the same unifying theme, and I miss that. Plus his old axe kick was rad. Oh, and they need to bring back the ability to smash enemies literally into the ground.Anyway, that's my meandering gate-keeper review. Battletoads 2020 is a fun and silly game. I think it has a particular audience, maybe one that is capable of laughing at how damn hard it is trying at such a silly game, but if you're in that group, hopefully with a buddy or two, then this is a good one.

_childDocuments_.review: It's cool to see these dudes back. Unfortunately, while it's clear a lot of work went into it, it kinda falls into its old games' traps... be good at exactly nothing. The beat-em up stuff is alright, but mostly just timing dodges and smashing buttons until things die, making sure you pick the right time to use a smash attack or else you'll probably get nailed by something interrupting the animations. The non-beat-em-up stuff is just so-so too. Art is alright on the whole. Good animation and a style that kinda feels like Alien Hominid or Castle Crashers in all their Newgrounds-era floatiness. A bizarre plot, tons of self-referential "jokes", and bad writing supplements it. It's Dane Cook; it's Deadpool 2; it's going to force feed you dumb jokes and make sure you got them. Go back and watch an episode of Street Sharks, 80s TMNT, Biker Mice. That irreverence was kinda charming for its time, but it doesn't quite feel the same here, didn't hit that feeling.So in the end you're left with a divisive art style (that I like), mediocre and samey gameplay, and a soulless writing style. Just watch some videos to understand what's going on here, then look up Fight'n Rage and the Capcom Beat'Em Up Collection. Maybe hunt down a PS TV and buy Dragon's Crown, Odin Sphere, and Muramasa. There are easily a dozen beat-em-ups I would recommend over this. I just asked for a refund... and might swing back if I see some significant updates, or it hits 5 bucks during a sale.

It takes a little while to pick up speed, but is actually downright hilarious at times in its self-aware assessment of a series that hasn't seen a release in two and a half decades. The combat isn't quite as fleshed out or as satisfying as it good be, but the game is primarily a series of varied minigames, so nothing overstays its welcome. Likewise, there are generous checkpoints/autosave positions and other such mechanisms to keep things from getting too repetitive and frustrating. It's an entertaining trip down memory lane for those who enjoyed (or suffered through?) the original games.

_childDocuments_.review: I really had a lot of fun with this game!  This is a bit of a "variety" game, with lots of different types of levels. From the classic combat and turbo bike levels Battletoads is known for, to some brand new puzzle platforming areas, a space shooter, and even a few minigames thrown in for comedic effect. I actually liked the art style, too. The original Battletoads was more of a 90s cartoon inspired romp, so it makes sense for the reboot to take inspiration from newer cartoons. The animation on the moves were pretty fun. It reminded me of how the original would do cartoony transformations as attacks, but going even further with it, a lot of the moves transforming the frogs into sharks, vehicles, weapons, and more.The sense of humour and story of this game is probably it's most polarizing aspect, but I would not say it's like anything on Cartoon Network. This game has swearing, violence, and references to cults. It's really not meant to be a kids' game at all. The meta humour really is a "your mileage may very" situation, but it didn't bother me at all. I also don't think the message of the game was that the Battletoads "suck", as the only characters who say this are some random gossipers by a water cooler who we aren't supposed to care for in a job Zitz is miserable at, and the game's main villains. I see the story of the game as a few heroes who are down on their luck, struggling to find their place in the world, then getting back on their feet and being awesome again!If there's one major issue I had with this game, it's the lack of a proper online multiplayer mode. I hope this could be added in a future update, as it was teased that there will be more content in the future. That being said, the Battletoads 2020 reboot is surprisingly fun, and if you give it a chance you might like it!
