_childDocuments_.review: When the E3 2018 trailer for this game dropped I took the opportunity to play the original 4 games and eventually beat all of them individually without using continues.  While I don't have the pleasure of growing up with these games I still became a big fan of each game, boss, and their characters.  One of the main reasons why these games are still remembered to this day is their notorious difficulty.  Throughout the experience it's up to the player to play each level near-perfectly with limited lives & continues as a Game-Over sends you right back to the beginning.  An often overlooked but critical aspect is that most of the difficulty is memory based and not skill based.  In most circumstances, a skilled player that has no experience won't perform as well as a moderately skilled player that has memorized the game.  This is largely the result of many beginners traps like objects / projectiles quickly reaching the player with no room for reaction time and off-screen obstacles being completely unknown until the player either or collides into them or gets lucky enough to avoid one of many.  The games demand accuracy and perfection but the aforementioned issues mar the experience as many retro games suffer from.  Aside from difficulty the Battletoads is also known for the gameplay variety, satisfying "smash-hits" where the toads transform their limbs into comically large objects with "freak-out" animations to match, and attitude which is heavily inspired by the 90's era it was born into.  The games were well aware of what the experience was and constantly mocks the player throughout.  While characteristically insulting, they offer light-hearted humor and encourage the player to prove themselves capable despite the insults.  Even the game's guide "Professor T Bird" berates and belittles players when only congratulating you once at the ending.  The game's bosses were quite a unique bunch with gross-out greats such as Big Blag who gets bigger in each game and Robo-Manus with a downright terrifying character design with dialogue to match.  Rare did an excellent job with the Dark Queen in that she's equal parts hated as she is intimidating.  This design principle would eventually influence other great characters like Gruntilda from Banjo Kazooie.  Overall I really enjoyed my time with the originals and they leave this new entry with a lot of room for creativity in smash-hits and the genre-swapping gameplay approach.When the game was revealed in E3 2019 it was met with a lot of criticism for it's tone, art direction, and gameplay speed.  While they've made the game feel very fast and fluid the tone and art direction were too integral to change so late into development.  People will oftentimes point to other commercial products like the Sonic The Hedgehog movie and ask the Battletoads team to do the same.  I believe these people fail to realize how in Sonic's case it was gripes with a model whereas with Battletoads the "issue" is with something so inherently fundamental that you'd have to scrap thousands of hours of progress to properly remedy (not impossible but CONSIDERABLY more difficult and wasteful).  I played the game on singleplayer with Battletoad difficulty.  If I could sum up my experience with one word it'd be chaotic, both in a good and bad sense.  Inspired by Battletoads Arcade the game's combat is fast and fluid and you can repeatedly attack enemies even when they've fallen onto the ground.  There's a tools at your disposal and it's welcoming to fans of the original's more simplistic gameplay with button-mashing being completely legitimate tactic aside from the occasional charge attack to break an enemy block.  It also allows a skilled player to dash around the arena with the tap of a button, use their tongue to grab or dash to enemies, and juggle enemies midair with a variety of different options with each toad.  My only issue is that some combat encounters from the singleplayer experience felt unbalanced.  For the most part this isn't a huge issue but sections with several projectiles makes it quite difficult as enemies no longer stop when you're in the middle of attacking like in the original games.  This is partially remedied by dashing which intuitively cancels any of your current attacks and being able to stun enemies from a distance but can still prove overwhelming on your first playthrough.  Overall though it feels incredibly satisfying to attack enemies which is a big reason why people enjoy the series and I'm sure fans will enjoy it.  The game feels more reaction based than the originals which is a much more enjoyable difficulty in my opinion but I hope they're also able to implement a continue / life / game over system that's unlocked after finishing the game. In addition, the music is stellar and you'll hear a variety of re-creations of classic tracks like the original theme and turbo tunnel plus brand new tracks that fit the glove perfectly.  David Housden hit the ball out of the park on this one and it was one of my favorite features by far.  The only caveat being that the classic pause theme from the original game only makes a brief return at the beginning and isn't present when pausing.  I do hope they consider adding it in as an optional setting.  Battletoads (2020) also takes inspiration from Battletoads (1991) and Battlemaniacs in it's genre-swapping gameplay.  None of it feels ridiculously jarring with short tutorials for the more radical shifts and control well. Excluding two sections I was able to pick up and enjoy them rather quickly.  It helps accompany the comedic tone, story, and makes gameplay exciting as you never know what the next level has in store for you.  The writing feels very self-aware taking the toad's 26 year absence as a major plot point while occasionally breaking the 4th wall like mocking the game's age rating.  If you're a fan of cartoons you'll find a good number of laughs with it's crazed cast of characters, they don't all land but there are some winners.  I was surprised to find how short the experience ended up being as I reached the game's credit screen saying I took 4hr 45m of in-game time to complete.  There's still plenty of achievements and collectibles left to unlock for replayability but those only interested in one / two playthroughs may feel a bit underwhelmed given the game's price tag.  The game's A rank challenge for 100% completion is particularly challenging on Battletoad difficulty but also incredibly fun when you use your full knowledge to finish each combat encounter flawlessly and achieve S ranks in various arenas.  For Ranking, you're required to use a variety of different attacks with the toad mugshots at the top of the screen corresponding to a stylish combo or not.  My only complaint is how there's no way of telling how long a particular arena will last as some feature multiple waves of enemies and if you finish with a low Rank there's no way to retry the fight instead of restarting the entire stage entirely.  While the tone, art direction, and lack of returning characters is a huge departure from the original games there's still plenty of features that harken back to the series' past while providing a brand new experience that remains faithful gameplay-wise.  While I would've loved to see a more faithful reboot overall, the Rare & Dlala team have done the best with the card they decided to play and I hope to see more of the Battletoads + other classic Rare franchises in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads 2020 is the prime example of not looking at a book by its cover, or even one of its pages. While many have seen the artwork that can a bit weird at times, or an out of context screenshot indicating that the developer doesn't like the “old fans”, this game is probably one of the games that captures the spirit of the original game, better then most others of the genre. It understands how to evolve the game with more up to date references and still keeping the humor like you'd expect from the cartoon show, but also understands the focus on difficulty in gameplay by not just throwing more things at you, but being smart about it. The tag in mechanism for single player with the cooldown time is great, and adds a level of complexity with the ability to control tag ins and even using that to keep combos going. There's a great emphasis on forcing the player in to new situations while keeping the basics consistent, which is a great sign that the gameplay holds up for the entire run. The game's pacing from going from a slow to fast section is good too, keeping you on your toes while not shoving ACTION ACTION ACTION down your throat. The presentation does have some good exagerration and some cool imagery,  especially in the environments. The animations however feel like they are missing key frames in the middle, which leads to a weird effect when watching the toad punch at the air. Story elements are a mixture of hit and miss: I found myself laughing at certain jokes and snickering and a few, but when a joke misses (especially in visual storytelling), it misses hard. Quite frankly, what I love about Battletoads 2020 is that it took risks. It was willing to deviate in a lot of places that people may have not liked (difficulty system, story, presentation), but it did that while still honoring the past. It captures those moments of ooh and awe when changing genres, it captures those difficulty spikes while still making them doable, and most of all captures the spirit of the battletoads themselves. A solid buy. list]

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads for Nes is my favorite game and I never really expected this game to be anything like it, I was kinda expecting something more akin to the arcade game.Honestly I don't think that the original Battletoads is really a product people want however I think this game still misses the mark in the spirit of the games and just on its own in a bubble.I don't have much experience with other beat em ups but I find the Animations in this game so incredibly slow. This on top of the large enemy hp pools and the sheer amount of enemies on top of level lengths makes the game just feel like a slog. On higher difficulties this problem is amplified a lot more. Not to mention the level design of these fighting areas are just plain boring. They can be summed up as a series of boxes with different looking backgrounds. The only thing close to making it interesting is you can fling to the background to fight different enemies but this feels more like 2 boxes stacked on top of each other. It really pales in comparison to a game like Battletoads and Double Dragon (the mash up game for nes, not both of these 2 games) where the first level level is this cool space ship that you can cling onto the side of and knock off other guys clinging to the side.Next the non beat em up levels.The turbo tunnel is ok. It lacks a lot of variety which is why I really liked the original game. But overall I'd say it was the most enjoyable part of the game. Almost every other section is mediocre at best or annoying at worst. There's a lot of press the button when the prompt tells you mini-game and they're cute sometimes but other times I just want to move on to the next thing.A lack of focus is something Battletoads gets grilled for a lot but I've always like how the games played around with the concept of genre. Game genre generally boils down to mechanical differences (ie Platformer, Shooter) while Battletoads I'd generally call an Action game in the same way movie genres are more about emotions and pacing. Battletoads before was about going fast and facing impossible odds. You'd never really see a puzzle in Battletoads because that isn't action, it wouldn't fit the theme. This game has puzzles which means while it doesn't hold a mechanical genre it also doesn't seem attached to the Action genre of previous games.Honestly I wish there was more platforming levels with enemies. Those were some of the best Battletoads levels. The 3-4 platforming levels they have don't have combat. Also there was only Turbo Tunnel hover bikes for vehicle levels which is sad.This game feels like if its trying to tackle a genre the genre is comedy, which is fine except I don't think it ties the comedy into the game play very well. I wouldn't really call any of the attack animations funny. Rash (sunglasses) has a move where his arm turns into a giant fish and he spins around and slaps people with it and that should be funny I guess but its so slow and its kinda lame. It doesn't have anything on the level of how the arcade let you grab an enemy by the balls and punch them, which wouldn't even be off brand for this game since it has people using the middle finger and cussing (both censored but the tone carries with them.) The levels that differ the most from the old toad games like the platforming puzzle section with no enemies and the fix a ship console command section (which I hated btw) weren't really funny in concept or the way the game executes them. The ship console fixing part doesnt even have visuals of the characters of them talking during it making quips, you just have a screen with buttons and they groan when the ship malfunctions. It's such a soulless section that feels like it should've been cut.The comedy itself is ok. Often times it feels like a B grade cartoon network show. Some jokes land well a lot don't and you can always just watch the game on Youtube so I don't think that should be a deciding factor if you don't like the game play.Overall I think it fails both as a sequel and a stand alone product, I know there's some people who swear by the comedy of the game and would be okay with how much the game stalls during the gameplay portions but that ain't me chief, I'd love to see a new game that captures the heart of the toads without the difficulty though.3/10 Not enough snakes.

_childDocuments_.review: I have to say that I used to be a mild fan of Battletoads as a kid because I had Battletoads/Double Dragon on SNES, and it was a fun game! I was excited to hear that Battletoads would get a modern sequel the same way Streets of Rage 4 did because the updated art style and mechanics are always nice to revive a series with, and although I may compare this game a lot to SOR4, even by its own merit, this new Battletoads does not stand on its own two feet really well.It's unfortunate because in comparison to SOR4, the toads actually have way more helpful mobility options that let them dash and tongue grab their way around a screen of baddies and they control very well. The beat em up aspect of this game, as it should, are SOLID. The new mechanics are weird at first as there are too many commands, but then I got used to them.Sadly though, the beat em up aspect of the game doesn't get to shine because it seems like they shoehorned too many NON beat em up elements into the game that break the flow too much for me. Like after the first level, what the hell was the point of those QTE's of the toads  It was nicely animated and sequenced but wholly unnecessary. While it's awesome that this game also has hand drawn animated cut scenes with full voice over work, it's a shame that the writing isn't good enough to justify the need for them. The humour is more miss than hit as its very juvenile and degenerate, and this is coming from a guy who watches South Park. But at least South Park has social commentary and some philosophical wisdom hidden beneath the poop and fart jokes. This is just pure dirty humour with nothing to back it up.I will give this game a pass for now and wait for a sale. I still want to like it and I still want to play it, but at full price it's hard to pay for because I KNOW the developers wanted to do a lot with this game, but they ended up doing TOO MUCH for it. They forgot what made classic beat em ups fun back in the day, and that was non-stop action in between levels with maybe a few change ups to alter the pace a little bit. Here they seem to change the pace too much. Like damn I was already bored within the first hour because of the tunnel and motorcycle sequence seemed to drag on forever.I was momentarily impressed by how you can use a tongue grab to switch between the foreground and background of a level, I thought that looked cool and stylish. Not to mention the super expressive animations for the attacks are nice and stylish as well. But this game gets horribly killed for me due to the unfunny humour and non beat em up elements.You are better off playing Streets of Rage 4 if you want something more straight forward that appeases the nostalgia needs while throwing some new elements in the table. This game takes too many liberties in NOT being a beat em up that it ends up suffering and makes the game more stale than it was meant to be full of variety.

Passing whatever you can may confuse your opponents but mostly, you are unlikely to win.And that is what I feel about the game: Confusing.It starts with beating them up arcade game and actually doing okay. Even the enemies are uninteresting so are the backgrounds setting, no weapon to pick up, at least the special attacks with interesting poses are good and you can switch characters smoothly. Toads using their tongues to switch roads seems promising. However, the gameplay changed into airplane games with several identical levels. _childDocuments_.review: After over twenty years of retirement and having been reduced to nothing, the Battletoads re-emerge from their self-pity, and enlist outside help for a frantic crusade to become relevant once again and fight a monolithic, oppressive regime. That line tells you everything you need to know about  Battletoads.Getting this out of the way right away: The gameplay is good, and it can be as punishing as old NES' Battletoads if you play it on the top difficulty AND actively strive for all the collectibles (). And yes, it IS multi-genre because guess what?  (not that journos would know). In fact, part of the difficulty is due to the fact that you're bound to run into a stage of a genre you suck at.Everything from the aesthetics to the humor is a self-aware love letter to the whimsy of the 90s. The re-imagined designs take a page from the Neptunia series in that the full cast have both a competent side and a stupid side that keeps everyone well-rounded and funny (and yes, for obvious reasons, in this day and age you just  have sexy dark queen, get over it, it's either this redesign or nothing... also, this queen rocks)... and those who complain about the art style clearly weren't alive back in the nineties as to remember that was the time when western animation stopped trying to compete with Japan in the "looking pretty" area and instead took shelter in "hyper ugliness" (see Aeon Flux, Phantom 2040, Ren&Stimpy, etc.)).Finally, the music is full of rock with the occasional synthy tune here and there, and they start on full throttle giving you two fan favorite tunes right at the beginning of the game.You don't have to be an old fan of Battletoads to enjoy this game, but you must have been alive in the nineties to actually get it (or at least, you know, document yourself on the matter, unlike journos).Give this game a try.P.S: Just like Killet Instinct, this game was also outsourced (thanks, DLala Studios!) because, let's be honest, all of Rare's talent escaped years ago to greener pastures, there's nothing left of rare.

_childDocuments_.review: As a long-time Battletoads fan, I was very excited about this game. In the end, I can say it's not exactly what I was hoping for, but it did enough things right to earn a recommendation.I'll get the negative out of the way first: I'm not a fan of the graphic style. It's not that I don't think the Battletoads would work as hand-drawn animation, it's just that I don't particularly like the character design. I don't like the Toads' eyes or their lanky limbs, and the Dark Queen looks wrong to me (I'm fine with her no longer being sexualized, but her hands look terrible, she often has a muppet head, and despite this game taking place long after the original, she looks like a child most of the time).Then there's the game's humor, which emphasizes random silliness and wacky jokes. I can easily see how the writing and presentation might turn a lot of people off, but after a while it grew on me. Not all the jokes landed, but I did chuckle a few times and I don't disagree with the decision to not treat the Battletoads franchise too seriously.One of the most unique features of the original Battletoads games was how the gameplay could change dramatically from level to level, switching between brawling, racing, rappelling, etc. They were a series of set pieces designed to keep you on your toes and prevent you from getting complacent. This game takes that concept and really runs with it, and I think it works to the game's benefit. There is a large variety of activities you will find yourself engaging in, from standard brawling to platforming to twin-stick shooting to minigames (lots of minigames). I think this approach to game design suits the Battletoads very well, especially since it allows the devs to get imaginative with their off-the-wall integration of story and gameplay. For example, at the end of the first level you find out the Battletoads have been trapped in a simulation for 25 years. Discovering they are irrelevant, they spend the second level doing menial jobs in the form of quick minigames. Instead of being a jarring and awkward change in gameplay, it uses gameplay to suit the (silly) narrative, which I found delightful.As for the brawling itself (arguably the focus of the gameplay), it definitely takes a bit of getting used to but I ultimately found it clever and challenging. Fighting is very different than it was in classic BT (no more running attacks or picking up weapons) and is a lot more tactical and demanding. While you can get through the first couple of fights with punches alone, the game gradually introduces elements that demand your attention: Enemies that block regular attacks and require charged attacks, enemies that fire projectiles that need to be dodged, enemies that electrocute wet parts of the floor, enemies that need to be immobilized by spitting gum at them, etc. Individually, none of these elements is particularly difficult to handle, but when you have to deal with several of them at a time, you quickly find you need to be attentive of what's going on all over the screen instead of just at the end of your fist. It actually seemed a bit overwhelming at first, but looking at the game as a puzzle-brawler instead of a straight action game helped me get a better handle on it.It took me almost 5 hours to beat the game in "Toad" difficulty (the equivalent of "normal"). Besides a harder difficulty to challenge, the game also features lots of hidden collectibles (some of which can only be earned by beating levels under certain times or achieving "A" rankings in all your fights) so if you enjoy the game there are reasons to replay it. I had a good time with Battletoads, and while it didn't entirely satisfy my desire to see a new Battletoads that more closely follows the classic template of the originals, it did what it did very well and I'm glad it was made.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a mixed bag.Its been awhile since we last saw the toads in action, and this game unapologetically reminds you of that quite frequently. We've all missed them, the quirky & cool characters, the absolutely rockin music, and the ball-busting difficulty we've come to know and love of the toads. And while Dlala Studios rendition of the Battletoads tries its hardest to incorporate the best of what the toads have always had to offer, it tends to do so in an...overabundance...to the point of exhaustion. There's a lot going on here in Battletoads 2020, some good, some bad, and some just annoying af. Want the toads in their classic beat em up fashion? You got it. What about as a platformer? Sure! Would you like some puzzles in that? Uh...o-okay. What about a shoot em up!? I-I mean I guess that alri... WE GOT MINI GAMES TOO! I'm not really that into thos...AND INTERACTIVE CUT-SCENES!!! S-STOP IT!!!This is kind of the experience one has when throwing on Battletoads 2020 for the first time. Its a game with quite a few positives, such as beautiful animation, gorgeous colors, and a rockin soundtrack. And had this been a 2 hour animated special, then Battletoads 2020 (aside from its...less than favorable character designs) would have been just fine. But this is not a cartoon, its a GAME, and a games bread in butter lie in the gameplay, to which Battletoads 2020 falls a bit short. Don't get me wrong, this games got variety, perhaps TOO MUCH variety. Battletoads 2020 will have you sampling several different genres while you are on your adventure, none of which are particularly fleshed out or interesting. You'll go from beat em up, to platformer, to puzzles, to puzzle platforming, to mini games, to interactive cut-scenes, and even shoot em ups, all of which function and aren't offensive per-say...but tend to overstay their welcome or outright break up any semblance of a flow. There is no rhythm to catch in Battletoads 2020 because it has none, it just tosses a bunch of ♥♥♥♥ your way and hopes you like it. And while that can certainly be seen as admirable, it more so comes off as a lack of faith in the sustainability of the games core mechanics. Battletoads 2020 feels like it gives you a lot of different things to do because it doesn't think any of the things it does are fun or interesting enough to sustain the players interest for more than a few minutes. This in my opinion is what hurts Battletoads 2020 the most. Had it took its time and stuck to mastering 1 or 2 genres for the toads return it could have fleshed out the battle mechanics further, add more variety to the combat and platforming, and cleaned up the cumbersome and over-engineered control scheme. Instead, Battletoads 2020 chooses to do all, and masters none, leading to a more chaotic yet less fun experience.That being said, I don't think Battletoads 2020 is a bad game. Its got an identity crisis and a lack of depth in its combat that stop it from being as good as it wants to be. But it also has a few highlights that make it stand out just enough for you to pay it a visit if you are a big enough toad fan. Just be aware this is not the Battletoads you remember, either in gameplay or style. And if you can accept all that along with its oddball new sense of humor, you might find some enjoyment here. Id wait for a discount though.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to say Battletoads and Double Dragon was one of my favorite SNES games when I was a kid, and the Battletoad games are actually pretty difficult. So, I've played them a lot over the years without getting bored. This game truly brings to light how a 90s game can be brought back to life and made relevant again at least in the first part of the game. Dlala Studios has done a wonderful job making you really appreciate how much fun these types of games can be. However, they've also proven how agitating these 80s and 90s arcade style games can be.   Pros* Story, voice acting and dialogue -boy, this in my opinion is the highlight of the game. I can't wait to see what's next, I find myself laughing and enjoying the silliness. It kind of reminds me if the Three Stooges were super heroes, lol. * The artistic style they used in this game really fits perfectly with Battletoads, sometimes when these types of games are brought back from the 80s and 90s they take themselves too seriously and they just come off as forced and not crowd pleasing  * The game isn't just stupid hard until you get towards the end of the game (there is actually less fighting and more mini games)* Fighting is fun and there are a variety of combos and attacks using all three toads (There is a tag system, where you can readily tag in another toad in combat, I'm assuming you can only do this in single player though)* There small puzzles and breaks in combat that really change up the pace nicely in the game (until act III, then it's all mini games) * Some of the levels are just funny and not combat oriented -you'll see what I mean very early in the game* Multiplayer (I have not tried it yet, but I'm betting it's just as fun as single player)* Controller supportCons* I'm not sure what in the world happened but starting in act III it's as if the developers completely abandon the fighting portion of the game. Until I got there, I was really having a lot of fun. Now it's stupid mini games over and over again, or you play a platformer as character that I'm not even for sure why it's in the game.   Honestly, until I got in to act III I would have said hands down buy this game, but now I'm pretty much hating it. It's just frustrating tasks (Like fixing the ship) you'll see what I mean if you make it that far. Some of the levels aren't even fun, they are just boring as hell and obnoxious. After getting towards the end, I'm gonna have to completely do a one eighty on my review and switch it to a thumbs down.

_childDocuments_.review: This is why I really wish a middle option for game reviews on Steam, with a third option being in the middle. I'm very mixed on this game, which is accurate since it reminds me of a lot of my feelings for the original Battletoads, but for different reasons. The original game was just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ hard in terms of difficulty, we know this. Over 20 years later and this reboot shows up. Much like a lot of others, I took a double take when looking at the art style. Still, I wanted to support and try the game out for myself. I've played through the game twice on normal difficulty, and plan on playing through on the Battletoad difficulty. So far I'm definitely liking it, but the other half of me isn't a fan. Let's talk about itBattletoads over the years has been known for many reasons. It's a beat-em-up with toads that somehow can shift their limbs and body parts to do over the top finishers and attacks. The first game was all over the place, with the sequels like Battletoads & Double Dragon and the Battletoads Arcade game being the best at representing the Battletoads as a beat-em-up series, with slight gameplay variation from here and there. Battletoads 2020 has 4 acts in total, having a couple stages in them. Gameplay styles shift depending on where the stories go, so I'll give you the short run down on the best to worst gameplay styles in the game. 1. Beat-em-up gameplay: It's not the most deep combat system, but it feels so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. Having a clever idea to use the morphing abilities the toads have in a dynasty warriors like fashion with the B button. The set pieces from areas to enemies are...strange to say the least (yes I'll get to the art style down below) but there's a lot of variety there. It can get annoying with the amount of enemies that not only spawn, but certain enemies you need to take out with a charge attack or wait for them to charge at you to stun themselves. It's a bit hectic, but I've played plenty of these kinds of games that have this kind of issue. Also this game's vibration feedback on the control is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ GODLIKE. Your controller will respond to punches, kicks, and other little details outside of combat. The only thing that's missing is...well, the weapons! That was a missed opportunity, that and the level design is more typical of a belt scroller, there are elements of the background and foreground switching, along with collectables, but that's it. Still, really good stuff2. Turbobikes and that one 2D Sled segment: There's two turbobike segments and the 2D one in the trailer you have seen. Battletoads has gotten so famous for the bikes with how brutal they are. They're no where near as difficult here, but they still require effort and quick reflexes to get through. Plus with collectables to gather and finishing it under fast times without hitting a wall can give extra challenge. A fun diversion3. The Mini Games: I won't go into too much detail on these minigames for now since they're tied into story. Every time they're used, it gives me a chuckle and they are pretty entertaining to boot. They aren't too long, and it's impressive that all of the mini games (along with the whole game for that matter) is three players. Not much to say or complain there4. The Shoot em up style: Okay...I like the shooter segments in the game. Shooting ships in space with power ups while avoiding getting hit too many times is fun. What's the issue here? There's three of these stages in total and they're fairly long, mostly cause of the enemies you face are like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bullet sponges. They take a lot of hits, so it goes a bit too long. 5. The 2D Platforming style: Hands down the worst part of the game (With the exception with the Dark Queen in Act 4, that one is fast paced and really fun. Act 3 with Pimple's 2D Platforming is what I'm talking about here). It doesn't control bad and the level design isn't terrible, it's just really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring. I forget where but I saw somewhere that these parts of the game were similar to Celeste. To that I say, no they ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ aren't. The platforming here has no brawling (there is a story reason behind it, but I think there could have been a way to implement the beat em up style here) and the level design itself is just so boring. If you played any 2D platformer with puzzles and avoiding basic obstacles, then you'll get through them in no time. There's one very short part in these stages where you learn the Donkey Kong Country roll, and have to use it to go faster to avoid falling traps that are going to land on you. WE COULD HAVE USED MORE OF THAT, that's the one part of the 2D platforming where I wasn't bored. The first 2 acts of the game are honestly really good, it's the later half that just completely ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed. The 3rd act having the worst gameplay segments in them unfortunately. Act 4 is better, but feels undercooked. From 2D Platforming segment with the Dark Queen that is pretty entertaining, a beat em up stage that isn't really a stage as much as it is an arena and it doesn't last nearly as long. Another turbobike segment with the final boss of the game, and then the final boss. Feels like another one or two more stages of a beat em up was supposed to be here, like after the arena area I mentioned before. Now let's talk about presentation for a moment. The audio is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ excellent, the soundtrack is badass and is a great listen. The animation quality is stellar, very smooth and looks great. As for the art style itself...well, the best I can say is that I like the designs for the Toads. The Dark Queen really got screwed over with her design sadly. Nothing resembling her original design. The rest of the game is going for more of a cartoony look. Reminds me when DiC animated a pilot for a cartoon series. It never happened of course because it was awful, straight up awful. Battletoads is definitely over the top in some areas, but I prefer the badass look in enemies, environments, and etc. That's what made Battletoads unique and different compared to TMNTAs for the story, I enjoyed myself. The humor doesn't always hit the mark, but the majority of the game did make me laugh. Having the Dark Queen and the Toads team up to regain their fame and glory is a great set up. Of course there's nods, references, and even a little tease with something Battletoads fans will immediately recognize at the end of the game that hints at a sequel if this does well. For me the stand out moments of the story are of course the interactions between the Main Trio, they're great here. Props to the voice actors for really making an entertaining performance. It's definitely funnier than the DiC pilotConclusion: I really want to recommend this game, I did legit have a fun time here. Yet with the later half of the game with the last two acts, it completely ♥♥♥♥♥ the bed. I have a couple of solutions though if you are interested, but don't want to buy just yet. If you want a Beat-em-up that's more consistent and has online, go play Streets of Rage 4. If you want to play the Battletoads games, I recommend getting the Rare Replay Collection if you can since it has the original and Arcade game. The rewind feature is great for beginners in using with the original battletoads, and the arcade game has infinite lives so go nuts, it's hectic as hell and it's a gem on that collection. Unfortunately Battletoads & Double Dragon isn't on Rare Replay, so you'll probably have to use an emulator or purchase an original copy of whichever version you want to play since it was on NES, SNES, Genesis and etc. TLDR: Story was entertaining and the new designs for the toads are great but the Dark queen's design is unrecognizable, the first two acts of the game are fun but the later half of the game really takes a dip in quality. Go play Streets of Rage 4 for a more consistent beat em up in high quality, or play the original Battletoads games on Rare Replay or on an emulator (especially for Battletoads & Double Dragon)

_childDocuments_.review: If you’re looking for a game that makes you laugh—mostly out of frustration—look no further than Battletoads! It’s like the developers took a good idea, dropped it in a blender, and then threw the pieces into an active volcano.First off, let’s talk about difficulty. The game clearly missed the memo about "fun challenges." Instead, it cranks the difficulty up to eleven and then laughs maniacally as you crash into walls like a blindfolded raccoon on roller skates. Seriously, I’m pretty sure that turbo bike level was designed by someone with a vendetta against joy.And the graphics? They look like a vibrant fever dream that forgot to take its meds. One moment, you’re in a beautifully drawn scene, and the next, it’s like someone spilled paint everywhere and called it “art.” I half expected a character to pop out and say, “Surprise! You’re in an art project gone wrong!”As for the story? Let’s just say it’s as memorable as a soggy piece of toast. I played through hours of this madness, and I’m still not sure what’s happening. Do the toads even have a goal? Is it just to make us suffer?In conclusion, if you want a game that will have you questioning your life choices while simultaneously entertaining your friends with your epic fails, Battletoads is your ticket to hilarity! Just be prepared for a wild ride filled with rage and confusion. Grab a snack, because you’ll need it—if only to throw at the screen!

_childDocuments_.review: The Battletoads reboot is a mixed bag, but ultimately boils down to this - it isn't very fun. It's a beat-em-up that's ruined by some awful mini-games.The old games were a mixed style of beat-em-up gameplay with a lot of variety, like racing levels, platforming, etc. They had a unique feel that had some notorious difficulty. And while this game tries its best to capture all of what the old games offered, unfortunately it doesn't do any of it very well.The best part about it is the beat-em-up portions, but those sections surprisingly only take up about 1/4th of the game, and even then, other current reboots of the genre (like Streets of Rage 4) do it far better. They are decent enough though, but they get interrupted a lot by a lot of mini-games, which is by far the worst part of the game.The mini-games are a mix between mind numbingly easy, boring, frustrating as all hell, or simply make no sense. Sometimes they pop up out of nowhere and before you know what's happening, you've failed it and have to try again. The game is littered with them and they suck. I found myself saying "why is this in the game?" a lot.The artstyle and story are designed like a modern day cartoon show for kids ages 8-12, and the humor matches that demographic. I will say the animations are superb in that regard (whether you love or hate the style is up to you), but the game thinks it's way funnier than it actually is. I love the original games, so naturally was excited for this one. I was open to the new look and some gameplay updates. Unfortunately, for every step forward, it takes two steps backward. I can only recommend it at a deep discount ($5 or less). Also, there's NO online coop! Seriously?! It's only offline, couch co-op (which I'm glad is included, but why not online too??). In this day and age for this type of game, that's ridiculous.On the plus side, if you're an achievement junkie and have an Xbox account, the game does unlock on both Steam and Xbox if you sign in with your Microsoft account, so there's that.Ultimately though, I thought the game kinda sucked. 5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads is a 4th wall breaking co-op beat-em-up that’s in line with the series very random level progression, tough as hell gameplay and wacky humour. I thought it was ok solo, but much more fun with friends. I recommended picking it up when it’s on sale. If there was a neutral option I would likely place the score on that.The game continues directly after the events of the last game in the series (no previous knowledge is required), but starts with the Toads finding out they aren’t the intergalactic heroes they thought they were (I loved the way it explained away 26 years of no new games in the series), and are left with the prospect working humble jobs and fading away into obscurity. They jump at the chance to reclaim their glory, and basically go from bad situation (of their own making) to worse. The story can at times be quite juvenile in its humour, but it grew on me and I thought ended up at a good place.Gameplay really depends on what difficulty you play on, as the difficulty is fixed for that save once selected and really changes how the game is played. On tadpole(easy), most fights are over in seconds, you get options to respawn on jetbike courses and generally any challenge the game would provide has been removed. I rarely say this but other than using it to clean up achievements you would be doing yourself a disservice playing on this difficulty. However, on the hardest difficulty (Battletoads) the game reminds me the original NES game, being frustratingly difficult (especially solo with jet bikes or sled), but giving you that sense of achievement when you do reach a respawn point or clear a mission. Seriously consider turning off steam notifications to make your life easier.Actual missions follow the first games footsteps, changing between a beat em up, side scrolling and timed descending platformer, space invader/bullet hell style shooter, jet bike/sled sections, and a host of other timed mini games that need to be completed. The puzzle sections aren’t hard to figure out, and most of the beat em up stages have you going in one direction and slightly interacting with the environment to progress. Some missions are very random (like the Olympics mini games, Toadshambo, or the computer restart mission, but serve to allow you great bragging rights for whose best when playing with friends). On hard, each stage becomes a mission in muscle memory (especially the space invaders and jet bike stages where obstacle and enemy placement doesn’t change and you can only take 3 hits). This game isn’t for those who only want to experience a certain style of play, and if playing multiplayer you need to remember you are rewarded for living on the edge (any non-beat em up stage rewards you for avoiding obstacles at the last second).Each Toad plays differently, falling into the generic quicker movement/weaker attacks, average across all & slow but powerhouse attacker that you can sub between at any time (you can sub to non-controlled toads when playing multiplayer). Each toad subs in a different way, so depending on where enemies are picking a different character to sub in can be quite beneficial. The combat move sets are fairly limited, but as a brawler a large combination isn’t needed as it’s the enemies move sets you need to learn. You are ranked at the end of each fight (getting hit resets the combo counter), however to get the best ranking it seems you have to switch Toads often. Each enemy has its own move set, and remembering this is the key to surviving (on easy just mash the buttons). It’s good that each enemy type is unique and aren’t reskinned so this is easier than it sounds, and each has a tell the lets you know when an attack is coming. Bosses function as unique enemies that have multiple phases (with move sets getting introduced as the fight progresses).The game played flawlessly for me, with no issues, crashes or problems being found and achievements seem to track correctly. You can play on a keyboard, but I would heavily recommended playing on a controller. The game does support local 3 player co-op, as well as remote play so there should be options of getting others to join you.I thought the graphics were very detailed in the beat em up parts in that cartoony way. Each Toad has tons of morphing attack animation, as do the enemies. The stages (while being basically a straight line) were colourful and vibrant, and had plenty of things happening in them. If anything the detail can be distracting as the additional movements can make you take your eyes off what you need to be focusing on. The platforming stages were less detailed, but since you are racing through these its forgivable as you don’t have time to really look. The jet bike stages (and sled) I found were the hardest, as taking your eyes off the track for split seconds leads to death.  Space battles become bullet hell dodge games however there aren’t any cheap shots (all enemies enter from the top), and each attack is clearly visible. There are plenty of movie scenes that break up the gameplay, but only at the start/end of stages and these were animated well, though an option to skip would have been nice.The soundtrack is surprisingly good, with all of the songs featuring heavy electric guitar and drum work. At some points I could have sworn there were heavily reworked versions of previous songs in there. I loved how even when you die and are at the reload screen the music continues for a few seconds and the tracks don’t restart but continue playing. Many of the songs loop, however I never remember hearing the point where it restarts with its good mixing. It’s a shame the soundtrack isn’t offered as a DLC download, as it would have been worth it. I found the voice work to be good (Pimple and the Dark Queen were stand outs), though the enemies speech in the first stage sounds a little forced. Some of the dialogue is childish, and yet without swearing can be very mature and dark.If aiming for 100% achievements then its feasible, but you require 2 friends to help (there’s lots of 3 player co-op achievements), and a few playthroughs. None of the achievements are impossible, but the toughest will be completing the game on the hardest difficulty.For more reviews please visit

_childDocuments_.review: As a preface: I only picked this game up for the sea of thieves bonus.That being said, the game really isn't very good. As a mindless button-mashing beat-'em-up, it accomplishes just that. There is little to no thought required to succeed in combat. Combos consists of mashing the light attack button over and over again, and sometimes trying to fit a heavy attack in somewhere. That is, if you can even get said heavy attack in. The animations for the "morph attacks" are incredibly drawn out and offer no sort of armored state while using them, often resulting in the player taking damage upon the first frame of the animation, canceling the attack outright. The grab works fine enough, pulling the enemy into attack range, however, it then returns the player to the aforementioned, lackluster combat.The non-combat minigames don't fare much better. The turbo-bike section is overlong and laughably easy; the rock-paper-scissors while straightforward in theory, are presents in a very strange and occasionally confusing manner; and the smaller, gag sections just end up feeling tedious after dragging on for too long.Saying Battletoads' story is lackluster would imply it's something one should try to stomach at all. Tonally, the game stumbles back and forth from trying to cash-in on the original game's 90s roots and ham-fisting self-depreciating jokes about the game's painfully average gameplay and presentation. I lost all interest in the game the moment it resorted to a diaper joke within the first hour, which it then dragged out for almost five minutes.

_childDocuments_.review: At first, I was horrified by the visuals. I'm used to old console games and their classic designs. It's not that the situation changed much after an hour of gameplay, and I'm still not thrilled with the design of the toads themselves, but the backgrounds aren't the worst, with layers, parallax, and so on. I thought the game would suffer mainly in its art style, but it turned out that the gameplay itself is just terrible. I've played enough of the original Battletoads to be amazed at how developers 30 years ago managed to create fun combat, whereas now, under the same brand, we get this mess. Even the bike levels, which I honestly hated in the original, have become a boring, monotonous, long stretch, during which you're entertained by the most idiotic dialogues.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I finished this on hard mode. Never played this on normal. So I don't know how the difficulty is balanced on normal. So take this with a grain of saltI had some fun with this. The beat em up combat itself is varied and satisfying. But it is kinda weird that death isn't consistent. At least you can use steam input to change that.1) But I don't want to talk about the combat too much. Since that's only half of it. _childDocuments_.review: A quick thought, months after release and my beating it: Battletoads (2020) is tough to review, as I'm not sure who the audience is. It seems interested in clutching for new life among younger fans, but is seemingly haunted by the original NES game and feels it must appease those die-hard fans as well (of which I number myself).To the specifics: its attempts at nostalgia sometimes fall flat and its new-Saturday-morning-cartoon-but-also-Rick-and-Morty humor very,  often misses the mark. That said, aesthetically, it's a pleasure to look at and the sound direction is quite nice with several old tunes remixed along the way. Determining the genre of Battletoads (NES) and Battletoads (2020) has always been a fun conversation to have, as they both switch seamlessly from platformer, to brawler, to shoot-em-up, to many further uncharted territories in the reboot. Without delving into spoilers, I will say that most of these new genres are a lot of fun! Unfortunately, the 'brawler' genre,, of which most people come to expect in a Battletoads game, is the weakest - it's bland, repetitive, and overlong.Ultimately, . For fans of the old-school original, it simply isn't challenging enough though there is some fun to be had along the way with nostalgia bombs and remixes to old songs. For potentially new fans, it might be easier to recommend in that it does so much more than other modern games in terms of different styles of gameplay,, except that at best some feel unpolished and 'incomplete' and at worst others are downright frustrating and a drag to play through.

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I rolled my eyes at some of the earlier footage shown off. Wasn't the biggest fan of the style direction, nor was I willing to accept the fact that the toads are going a more child-friendly route. I was excited to see my favorite characters in action, and I was inclined to subside my first initial reactions until I finally got my hands on the game.With that being said, this game-for the price it's going for is well worth purchasing. The game is solid as hell, and loads of fun especially when your playing with friends. Beating the hell out of baddies feels satisfying, and put up a nice challenge at certain parts of the game. I found myself enjoying the turbo bike sections, as well as the space-galaga type mini games that were incredibly addicting. My gripes with the game fall along with these unique puzzle sections that felt more of a hassle than a actual enduring challenge. The game simply did not need to have puzzles that halt the flow of this action packed beat-em up. One thing that I did miss from the Arcade version of battletoads, was being able to pick up weapons, as well as being allowed to throw enemies. These features are completely missing, and would have made a massive difference in variety if they were to be included. One thing I will say is that I can actually play this game through in and through out, unlike its very first iteration on the NES, in which most levels are completely impossible without memorizing every possible nook and cranny. Although the original Battletoads is very well received, we must remember that the difficulty for that game is what put it on the map in the first place. It wasn't because it was necessarily amazing, it was challenging and felt great to play. Now with this new title, it would be fair to say that it retains this difficulty as long as you turn it up to be that way, which I completely recommend. Playing on any difficulty other than it's highest makes it a cakewalk. All in all, this game deserves its criticisms- and it also deserves to be loved for what it brings to the table.

_childDocuments_.review: I was skeptical when they went this route for its presentation. I can safely say that my concerns were unfounded, and the new Battletoads game is some pulse pounding fun and mayham.Like the original Battletoads and its sequel, Battlemaniacs, there are levels that change up the gameplay that keeps it from being a straight beat-em-up title that many may affiliate this game as. Turbo bikes are back, there are puzzles to solve, and much more you should discover for yourself.I played this game from beginning to end on Toad difficulty with three-player coop. The coop mode offers a unique experience where each player are designated different roles in the unique sections of the game, where cooperation is a must, otherwise prepare to reload from checkpoint again, and again, and again. It's going to be a very frustrating experience. Thankfully, the game can be merciful and allow you to simply become invincible if you struggle for too long. Like the original Battletoads, it's actually easier to play alone since each Toad acts as their own life-point, which does respawn in some sections if you stay alive long enough or reach a checkpoint. Battletoad difficulty is a commitment, and I can only recommend it if you know what you're getting yourself into, or if you had beaten the game already.Overall, very pleasantly surprised. The presentation grew onto me, along with the new characterizations, with single player and multiplayer being pretty unique to each other, and it is a fun-filled ride from beginning to end. For the budget price of $20, you cannot go wrong.

I better controller scheme would had made the game easy to just pickup and play. And some levels are rather confusing. Maybe an expansion in the future will remedy the shortcomings. _childDocuments_.review: When Rare left Nintendo, it was the saddest time for the gaming world. The adventures of a mighty king on his island put on hiatus, the future of a hillbilly adventurer and his feathery gal-pal left uncertain and their parting gift is one of the most desired waifus in the Furry Fandom to date...Who hasn't seen much action since her most recent appearance in that particular series.Now, with that depressing soliloquy out of my system, let's talk 'Toads! That's right, Pimple, the big guy, Rash, the poster boy and Zits, the leader...Who got himself kidnapped that one time are back in an all-new epic adventure! Without giving too much away, I enjoyed this so much from being able to actually play a Battletoads game to the story. I'm sure die-hards who have followed the franchise from its genesis as a TMNT wannabe are a little miffed over the Dark Queen's understandable redesign, but, as someone who rented Battlemaniacs once as a kid (Never got past the tree level) and has seen the animated pilot, I went into this with a fresh perspective. Visually stunning and just as entertaining up to the final boss(es), this band of brothers (Or whatever) have definately regained their place in the gaming world in MY book!In conclusion, it's worth every penny.

_childDocuments_.review: Tried to like it. Big Battle Toad fan from the old days. Combat feels good at first, but the game spams way to many ranged unit swarms for a game that has little to no ranged attacks, making the game difficult to play when in single player mode. Though a tough and somewhat tedious beat-em up isn't a bad thing by itself... the rest of the game is... kind of annoying.Love the animated cut scenes but the humor is mostly meta and the purpose of the cut scenes feel meaningless. The mini-games are the same, shoved in between every chapter and do nothing to influence any change in the story. The worst part is, it's hard to route for the Battle Toads as heroes when they're kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and are causing half the problems themselves. I guess the 'destructive' hero trope is a thing and it can work, but we're just not given enough time with these new toad personas to really appreciate this.I will say this, even if you don't like the Dark Queen's redesign, Siobhan Hewlett, her voice actor just sells that performance so well. Never seen or heard her in other roles, but damn is she great here. She really brings Dark Queen to life. You just feel the Queen's pain as she is forced to deal with these idiotic ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Her presence and performance is the one shiny light that never dulls in this game. Dev team has my money so I know they don't care what I think or feel, but I implore you if you ever decided to try to reboot Battle Toads as a cartoon (which is feels like thats what you really wanted to do with this project, it felt like you wanted to make a cartoon and not a game) please hire Siobhan Hewlett again as Dark Queen's voice actor. _childDocuments_.review: Game's pretty alright for the price. It's not so much a beat-em-up as it is a genre blender; there's bullet hell levels, sidescrolling levels (with the last one being a clear reference to the infamous Rat Race level from the first game), two high-speed biking levels that are a lot of fun, and there's even a level full of puzzles akin to the bomb-defusing game Keep Talking And Nobody Explodes. I'd call it faithful as the original Battletoads on the NES was also a genre-blender, but unfortunately video games are a whole different production behemoth compared to over 30 years ago (the original came out in 1991!) and it shows in this long-awaited sequel with how some aspects of the genre-blending are half-baked compared to others.As for the writing, some of it landed for me while some of it didn't. There were a few jokes and gags that were funny but nothing amazing particularly stood out. It's not really the kind of game that would have a deep witty story, though, so it's no big deal.To summarize, Battletoads is a good bit of fun for a few hours. There's enough callbacks and nostalgia to please fans of the original, and the gameplay remains fun enough for the runtime. A solid 6/10.

_childDocuments_.review: “Battletoads 2020 Review”I’m sorry to say this, folks. But I had to get a refund for this game after playing for an hour and half. Do you know why? Because this is NOT a Battletoads game.This game was destined to fail as soon as I saw the trailer. And after reading the reviews, I couldn’t have been more right. But let’s delve deeper into this pile, shall we?The story was crap. Quite literally, all you’d have to do was do a retelling of their origin from the Battletoads comic from the old Nintendo Power magazine (Y’know, the one where our three heroes were originally human game testers Morgan Ziegler, Dave Shar & George Pie before being sucked into another dimension and turning into the ‘Toads) and you’d have the ultimate revival. Instead, we get our three heroes trying to regain their fame and recognition. That’s it.I have played the original Battletoads games via Rare Replay. Heck, I’ve even played the awesome Battletoads Double Dragon SNES game as a teenager. And each game was a painfully tough, yet replay-able adventure with simplistic controls. To beat up an enemy, you can press the attack button repeatedly until they get knocked out, do a dash attack, or perform certain attacks with precise timing. This reboot? Well, screw it. Let’s throw in some light, medium and heavy attacks and have the player perform certain attack button combinations to take out the enemy. Gameplay like this gets boring very quickly. Don’t believe me? Play DMC: Devil May Cry for an hour or two.The platforming levels are poor Donkey Kong Country ripoffs. Yeah, the other Battletoads games had platforming levels, but at least they kept the combat the same. The only good thing I liked were the Turbo Bike levels. While the animations is good, the overall designs are horrendously bad. What is up with the ‘Toads’ new look? They look nothing like they did back in the day. The ‘Toads themselves look like their heads were shaved with a grease-cutting kitchen razor and their eyes like rectangular bricks (aka Xbox 360s). The enemies are no longer the muscled-up tough guys and instead just some scrawny looking minions ripped out of a flash animated cartoon. And the Dark Queen? Brace yourselves, folks. The developers (who are most likely PC) have taken an old female villain, who was basically a sexy latex supermodel in a royal cape who taunted you during each stage or if you used cheat codes to beat the game, and turned her into another generic Marvel Cinematic Universe villain in a lab coat. The characters from the ‘90s Battletoads cartoon pilot had better designs that this game.And the multiplayer? Yeah... Why is that this game has only local multiplayer and NO online multiplayer while other beat ‘em ups like the superb Streets of Rage 4 has both options available for playing with friends online and/or offline? Seems counter-productive to me.Final thoughtsBattletoads 2020 is the WORST attempt at reviving a beloved game franchise and sits up there with the likes of Bomberman Zero and DMC: Devil May Cry. With boring gameplay, bad plot and awful art designs, it’s now obvious at this point that the Rare that brought us such classics as Donkey Kong Country and Killer Instinct before they joined the Microsoft posse is now a shell of its former self. And if this is a hint of what’s to come for Bethesda now that Microsoft owns them, I weep for any and all future game developers who get swept up by them.So do I recommend Battletoads 2020? Hell, no. Go buy Streets of Rage 4 instead and leave this game where it truly belongs. In a frog blender from an old Joe Cartoon flash animation.1 flying insect that acts as an health item out of 5.Rest In Peace, Rare.

I dont even want the drugs, id flush them and not worry about the cost. A few fanservice references here and there, good enough right?  HELL NO. (Professor T. Bird or the Princess doesnt show up either) Its someones idea of a stand up routine that just happens to have nostalgia attached to it and the humor just doesnt cut it.  The game tries self aware jokes but it really needed to take itself more seriously, it feels more like a Newgrounds Flash parody.  Oh it was made in Unity?  Close enough.Excluding the art (which in of itself should have tanked this game, I cant understand why it has any positive reviews) its very middle of the road to me like its music and action (and mini games? WHY???) its dull and monotonous. _childDocuments_.review: (I'm reviewing from a single-player, "I'm here for the story" perspective. I've never played a Battletoads game before. Your experience may vary!)PROS* This game is BEAUTIFUL!!! I especially like the new, creative designs for enemies and NPCs; they're appealing and funny. I wish we could see more of them or talk to them in the environment. Aside from that, I also enjoyed the retooling of the existing designs - yes, even the new Dark Queen, but especially the new Battletoads. (The old designs looked odd to me, personally) Everyone is expressive and the in-game animation is polished and creative, with each enemy and character having many frames of movement. The animators really went the extra mile in giving the playable characters oodles of personality through their motion.The cutscenes, unlike the in-game graphics, are Flash-animated. However, don't let this put you off; they also looks quite good, with their crisp quality and strong art direction. Fantastic job overall!* Some of the jokes made me laugh, and I appreciated how creative and unique the characters and setting were. I wanted to explore some of the characters and places more in-depth, in terms of interesting locations, character origins, motivations, etc.* The game has adjustable difficulty and doesn't mock you for playing on easy (which is what I did) but tries to ensure you have the experience you're looking for. It also includes features like temporary invincibility and ample checkpoints to make sure you don't have to replay sections you already finished (a common time waster in older games in general).* Full voice acting is a major plus. The actors do a good job and fit their characters well.* That graphic design is sleeeeek. Microsoft does a far better job designing game interfaces than operating systems, lol.CONS - Story* I really wanted to enjoy this game's story, and while it had intriguing ideas - the characters are mutant shapeshifting toads,  - it lacked heart.For a game supposed to be celebrating Battletoads, I was surprised that it took a weirdly cynical, occasionally depressing tone.  Overall, the game's sometimes sour sense of humor left a strange taste in my mouth.* The gameplay and story are clearly separated, so you don't often get bits of characterization while you're actually playing. I didn't feel like I got to know the characters super well or explore their world. I would have liked if the developers had integrated the two parts more to use the game's short runtime wisely.* The plot went in some weird directions and sometimes things didn't make sense. But instead of adjusting the story in some very simple way to make a bit  sense, the characters just point out the nonsense...it's a funny idea on paper, but it didn't really work for me.CONS - GameplayMy brother asked me how the game was as I was nearing the end. I found myself replying, "Irritating." In general, the various gameplay styles are...okay. But they each could use more polish, and they're usually repeated too many times at once and overstay their welcome.* The combat is fun at first. Trying to get higher ranks is enjoyable. But it soon became a chore. Run into room. Stop to fight enemies. Clumsily attempt to eat flies with LT and Y (???). Maybe solve a puzzle. Repeat. I found myself running into a room and thinking, "Bleh, gotta fight even moooore enemies to get to the next story beat. Sigh." Maybe it's a sign that this kind of gameplay isn't my cup of tea, but I also feel the design could be a bit more interesting - perhaps if the fighting mechanics were given some more hidden depths a la Super Smash Bros. (I don't think increasing the difficulty would have helped me enjoy this more, as it'd likely only make these fights . Haven't tried it, though.)* While the difficulty settings are appreciated, you have to choose one before you've even begun playing and you can't change it without starting over. I chose easy because I pictured myself getting annoyed at a battle that began to feel like a chore, giving up, and then letting the game languish in my Steam library. If I loved the gameplay more, I'd gladly try a harder level.It'd be awesome to see more mechanics that allow you to shape your own level of difficulty by making decisions in realtime as you play. (The invincibility is an example of this, since you can use it or ignore it, though sometimes I  to use it.)* The mini games are sometimes difficult to understand at first. I remember saying stuff like "OH. Wow. Okay...what am I supposed to do???" multiple times. * Finally, this game is surprisingly short. To be clear, , as long as they have a high "awesome per second" factor. With this game, though, I often felt like I was doing boring or repetitive stuff in order to get to the story, but in the end, I found the story itself to be underwhelming. What really pushed this review into "Not Recommended" territory was the fact that I was actually glad the game was over, since I'd really just wanted to experience it to the end. I didn't feel like I enjoyed enough of my time to give it a thumbs up.CONCLUSIONI was really excited for Battletoads 2020. I wanted an experience akin to playing a cartoon (in a narrative way), but it was not as heartfelt or funny as I'd hoped, and the gameplay didn't grab me. Of course, I don't hate it - it's like a "meh, okay" for me. But I enjoyed the gorgeous animation and art, and I wish the developers all the best in their next project!STRAY OBSERVATIONS* Sometimes this game feels like it was written to be more raunchy, and then edited down to an E10 rating. That would explain the weird tone and a few euphemism-filled sentences like "Suck my friggin' butt."* Rash's foot attack makes me uncomfortable. :P

_childDocuments_.review: This game left me with mixed reactions. I don't feel like it's a bad game, however if I'm answering the question of whether or not I would recommend this game, most of the time the answer would be no. I think the game looks pretty good, I like the animation and the voice work as well. What really made me struggle to play this was the gameplay. I am not an expert on the Battletoads games, but from what I understand this one is a different entry in the series when it comes to the gameplay. Every level seems like it changes game genres, an interesting idea that if well executed would make for quite the unique experience. The thing about that is it really feels like that would be difficult to pull off because for it to work every (or almost every) genre presented needs to be done well, and unfortunately I don't feel like this game does most of the things it tries to do well. Not only that, but it led to me having to replay levels or do some trial and error to figure out what I was trying to even accomplish sometimes. Some of the writing and jokes made me laugh, some of them did not. I think it was a pretty mixed bag in that department. Overall, I don't want to call this game bad or anything, I definitely think it is something that some people out there could enjoy, however it feels like in order to enjoy it you really have to like very specific writing, and be very into this specific sort of game. Not an arcade-style beat 'em up, but whatever you can call this game (I'm not sure how to even categorize it haha). If you really think you'll be interested, give it a shot. But if you're looking for something to play or another beat 'em up or something, I unfortunately have to say I believe there are some better options out there.

_childDocuments_.review: 2 Things I'll just address before actually sharing my thoughts on the game.1) I love the soundtrack, it's probably the only thing I really like about the game.2) The Dark Queen's look gained a lot of negative attention, I'm not much of a fan of the overall art style but this game takes place after 26 years and her character literally has aged and put on pants.  There you go.  That's literally it.  If I was a woman in her 60's who spent a better portion of almost 30 years in an abandoned creepy amusement park (for whatever reason) I would probably put on pants too.  Even though apparently that's one of the last things she did before running into the Toads... go figure.  If this is your main reason for hating the game, I'm just going to say you are coming off as a bit of a mouth breather.  Not saying you are, but just saying that's what you look like.OK So the actual game. -------------------------I really wanted to like this game, but it's just really hard for me to ignore the gaping problems with it.1) Brawling - The Main focus of the game has been "Updated" but ultimately feels like a generic beat em up - you got your regular attack, your power move, your charging smash attack, you dodge, your tonguelike grapple that isn't as useful as it seems (Not completely worthless, just not exactly the most practical and is kinda spotty on the execution) and you basically find yourself shift dodging and building up the combo meter each fight...which ends up feeling more tedious than anything else.  You walk into an area, guys come out in waves - you beat up the waves, more guys come in waves... you beat up more guys... and that's it.   You have the same 5 guys reskinned for each level who do the following things.A) Enemy who walks around and does a power attackB) Enemy who blocks constantly and does a power attackC) Enemy who will posture around, charge at you and is stunned if they miss.D) Enemy who wanders around and hits you with a ranged attackE) Enemy who is Stationary and hits you with a ranged attack.Some fights have gimmicks which is cool, I guess... like electrifying water areas which adds a little bit to some fights but ultimately there isn't enough of that to save you from the tedium.  Why is it Tedious? Because even on single player - if you die you tag out and switch Toads while the recently dead have a cooldown for 20ish seconds.  This means, you literally can't die in most cases if you are seriously not trying to.  The game responds with this mechanic by just cramming the screen full of enemies that just becomes a real chore when tracking.I wouldn't have much of a problem with this, but if you ever played the more classic games - every enemy has a method and animation that takes them out.  Part of the fun in the strategy in fighting enemies was knowing which enemy to go after and with their animations use that to help crowd control other surrounding enemies.  There was also a "Knock Down" style health system that you can survive undamaged so long as you don't let enemies complete combos on your (or your friend bails you out) .... it's a lot easier to witness than to explain honestly.  The enemies were varied to the point where the gameplay never seemed too repetitive and like the classic titles you also had to mind the scrolling of the level.  This latest incarnation just only really spawns enemies at what seems like "Arena Sections" and the levels feel like you're just watching from one Arena Section to the Next.I never thought that the Brawling aspect of a Battletoads game would be my least favorite part.2) The Minigames - This is tricky, because Battletoads titles love to crossover into other areas whether it be a Turbo Tunnel esque level or spaceship combat.  This does both, and they are... OK.  The Day job minigame was hilarious at first... and the security puzzles are... ok.  The Sled part was aiight for a line runner.  The Platformer area was...dumb.Honestly I would have loved to see more done with the main gameplay, I think "Battletoads And Doubledragon" REALLY demonstrated how well you can incorporate all these features together.  Which in this case... an attempt was made but ultimately feels shallow.3) The Writing - At first - it was funny...but by the time you were nearing the end of the Jeff Arc it derailed so badly that it just felt like the never ending tirade of that person who tells you "OMG THAT IS SO RANDOM, I'M SO RANDOM... LOOK AT ME WEAR THIS CHIHUAHUA AS A HAT!" with the Toads being replaced by absolute glory hounding sociopaths and the Dark Queen... well honestly felt a little more fleshed out and actually kinda fun to watch.  The Antics though almost get tiresome like watching back to back of the worst episodes of Teen Titan's Go... or at least the ones that aren't nearly as funny as other episodes.  It's almost like it just crosses the line of cheeky fun nonsense to a never ending "Blinking guy" Meme.  You know the one.To top everything off writing wise, aside from the Toads, the Dark Queen and the first couple of levels... nothing from the original games made it to this parody sequel in terms of look/feel/lore.  Which is sad, because there was a lot of potential here.  Hell I would have gladly accepted this as a lovable parody game had it actually feel like a Battle Toads game.4) I could go and say something about the Animation style in general but... eh, I've grown to accept that people love the most modern form of the Cal Art's aesthetic.  I mean there has been worse things done to the Toads (look up the 90's TV Pilot) - But I will say the enemy Animations are harder to track than usual. Also...the Dark Queen's hands, they literally just seem to be as long as her arms and they end up looking like flippers when shes waving them around.  It's inconsistent too, like one moment they are fine and look like they would fit her in the cartoon style she's in, and the next they look so massive it's a little off putting.  So there you have it, I won't really recommend playing this - I mean if you need it for your collection get it on discount.

_childDocuments_.review: The humor of the game is something inbetween juvenile and adult humor. It can be charming or cringe at times. The story is fine enough and the gameplay is like a classic fun beat em up. The main thing about this game is that it doesn't just stay a beat em up game. For some reason there's sections that randomly change into different game styles, mostly for the worse. It'll switch from a bullet hell to a racing game to other mini games. It really halts the pace of the game because these sections go on for way too long. I played this co-op with a friend and we both were so tired of the really slow sections and forced ourselves to play the rest of the game. Overall, you'd get the same experience just watching the cutscenes instead of actually playing the game.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very conditional 'yes' review since the execution of the title had some warts. If you're hoping for a pure brawler, this is not the title for you. If you want brawling with platforming sections, Geometry Wars and Warioware-style minigames, then this game is for you.The biggest design issue is that the brawling mechanics are very fleshed out, yet it feels as though whole major sections of the game don't even have you throw a punch. There's a section that plays like Lost Vikings interspliced with a shmup series of levels that ends on chaining button presses to progress. A XBOX controller is a necessity because one of the minigames near the end requires pressure-sensitive shoulder buttons and my initial controller, a Switch Pro Controller, lacked that feature.There's definitely the core to elements of a proper Battletoads revival, so I'll say I'm cautiously optimistic for more along these lines. If you're on the fence, wait until a 50% off or more sale. I waited until 33% off.
