_childDocuments_.review: Look at these negative reviews... my brother and I really dont get it (this is a multiplayer review).  This is simply a perfect reboot. A perfect game? No, of course not, but a strong reboot of Battletoads? Absolutely.  I simply cant imagine a better modern interpretation of the property. The mixed reviews led me to expect a battletoad-esk experience that was cringy and lame but maybe with enough good content to keep me interested. What I got was an innovated, fun, and sometimes laugh out loud funny ("pink mouth?" comment got me) romp in the Battletoads universe. I didnt expect that decent animated cartoon cutscenes, good voice acting, and strong writing in a Battletoads game - but we got it.  The gameplay was fun and often novel, example: one level is a schmup/twin stick shooter where one player controls the ship and the other controls the guns. This leads to the gunner having expectations of where the ship will turn and for a millisecond it almost gives you vertigo that you are not predicting the proper path. Novel and fun. Many levels are unique and are just fun to try  to figure out without being annoyingly difficult. Do us all a favor and buy this. Relax, grab a friend, and play it on your couch and have a blast.  RARE gave us exactly what a Battletoads remake should be and we gave it mixed reviews.  This is why we get cookie-cutter, bland IP reboots where nobody in the development has even played the original.  Its a shame. **HOWEVER** In my opinion, this is a local multiplayer title. If you are booting this up by yourself, theres surely fun to be had, but I think it excels in the coop multiplayer on the first time play though. Discovering the mechanics of each level with a friend is a blast. Doing this as a single player maybe not as much fun and Im not sure how much repeatability there is for this type of game. Perpective - old battletoads fan from the NES, beat it for the first time in probably 2014. It can be brutal but its amazing what innovative levels they crammed into that NES cart.

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads 2020 is an absolute mess. That's basically the gist of this review, but if you want to understand my frustration with this game and with this series, read on.Back in 1991, a little company called Rare made a little beat em up game for the NES system called Battletoads. It was basically the younger and slightly zanier cousin of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles with a more cartoony approach. It was notoriously difficult, which has earned its reputation as one of the hardest games ever made. The game was a massive success, some people calling it one of the greatest video games of all time. Personally, I wouldn't go that far, but the game had a unique charm to it with some of the zaniest, trippiest video game design ever seen in the 90s.Unfortuantly, there weren't a lot of sequels, and the ones that are out varied in quality. While Battletoads in Battlemaniacs was a worthwhile sequel and brought the series to the 16-bit era, it paled in comparison to the original's quirkiness. It wasn't a bad game, but it wasn't great either.Then there was the very strange Battletoads/Double Dragon crossover, which while an interesting idea on paper, left a lot to be desired. It looked bland and played blander. The arcade game Battletoads Arcade, while arguably the best one in the series, bombed badly and the series laid dormant for 26 years. Which is where Battletoads 2020 comes in.Right off the bat, the game reminds you that it's been 26 years since we had a new Battletoads game. Boy, they sure like to tell you that. Over and over and over again. The plot is just plain moronic. Our heroes have been in a fantasy simulation bunker for 26 years, to which they finally awaken and realize.....hey! We aren't relevant anymore! Yes, the plot is basically a cartoon toad version of How Stella Got Her Groove Back.Honestly, the plot is just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stupid and pointless it feels like I barely need to talk about it. This is the best we could come up with? Some "aging boomer game" tropes? Also, the writing....my GOD, the writing. Every single plot point in this game, they try to shove some Venture Bros esque humor down your throat but NOT. ONCE. DO. THE. JOKES. LAND. It is painfully unfunny and cringe, with some of the worst "jokes" I've ever heard in a video game. I get that Battletoads was supposed to be zany, but this is just bad. After a while, I just pressed whatever button I could to skip these obnoxious scenes. Not since Orcs Must Die 2 have I wanted all the characters to just shut the hell up.But you probably want me to talk about the gameplay, right? That's what we're here for. Well, congratulations, fellow gamers, welcome to THROW THINGS AT THE WALL AND SEE WHAT STICKS THEATER! We got some of the most convoluted, random assortment of gameplay I've ever experienced in a video game. Boring beat em up? Check. A tunnel sequence that kinda resembles the tunnel sequence from the first game? Check. A weird Mario-esque platforming section with some of the most confusing puzzles of all time? Check. An absolutely baffling ship repair sequence that's poorly explained? You betcha. At one point there is a part where a strange purple alien chops down a tree with a timer going down. It's just  This game feels more like a Warioware game than the beat em up it was known for.Also, the decision to not make this online baffles me. In this day and age with every successful multiplayer game being online, you're just gonna resort to couch co-op? Are you mad?Simply put, Battletoads 2020 is a terrible game. Hell, Rare didn't even make it, it was Diala Studios, a no-name studio that had two games under it's belt. Why Rare wasn't involved with this disaster is beyond me. Maybe they would've made it worse?Avoid at all costs.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit I never spent a lot of time with Battletoads before I played this game. It's basically no secret that they're thinly veiled ripoffs of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. For a long time while they remained in obscurity some people only knew them as the subject of prank calls to video game stores. I've played some of the older games in the past and really enjoyed the SNES crossover with Double Dragon, but this new iteration charmed the hell out of me. It's short and sweet, very well drawn and animated, and fun to play, with hilarious writing and voice acting. Most of it is the classic beat-em-up formula with some interesting changes here and there interspersed with mini games, quick time events, and other stuff. The classic mega hard difficulty is there is you want to choose it but you don't have to. It's just too bad there's no online multiplayer, that feels like a hugely missed opportunity. Otherwise I have a hard time finding anything bad to say about this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads 2020 is the long awaited return of the classic NES beat em up franchise that since day one has left people divided. From my personal point of  view and as someone that's played every  game in the franchise - from the original NES game to the 1994 arcade title - I find myself on the positive side of things.I feel the need to clarify my opinion due to the mixed reception it has received from fans and because this is naturally a review. The first thing I want to cover is the art style, as from the get go this was the most negatively received aspect to the game that when we first saw our gameplay footage, put me off as well. However as I kept playing the game I found that the designs for the Toads and Dark Queen started to grow on me and helped heighten the comedy - it's definitely helped by the fact that the actual in game animations are high quality hand drawn that look both full of life and over the top which while different does manage to stay true to the cartoony nature the original games  had. Examples would include the characters having a jaw dropping expression when going up against bosses, sadly the fmv cutscenes dont do a good job highlighting how gorgeous these in game visuals are as they feel more stilted and tweened, easily comparible to a cheap flash animated show you'd catch on TV. What saves these sequences however is the writing, as while the animation doesnt live up to the task, the game's comedy is spot on and throughout the experience I found myself laughing at how much the game was delving into the madness brought upon by the world it created.While some may argue that the charm to the original was the fact it took itself seriously while churning out ridiculous concepts and having appalling dialogue (check all the Dark Queen's taunts in every single one of the original titles) , I say the 2020 game while it knows its ridiculous, it too also takes its humor seriously as if what's going is really important to the cast which often leads to the joke hitting harder - an example that comes to mind is how Pimple has an arc about giving up violence, which is played for laughs but because the character takes it so seriously, it winds up becoming hilarious when he eventually loses his cool and we're welcomed with a surprisingly fun minigame.That brings up the gameplay, Battletoads does what its NES counterpart did, in that while you did have a beat 'em up, it was jumbled in with a ton of different sections - the infamous turbo tunnel, platforming, worm riding and even space shooting elements. I personally never liked the jumbled mess that is the original NES game + the SNES title as while we had those different sections, the general gameplay and control would maintain that of the beat 'em up, meaning that when it came to say platforming intensive sequences (such as the worm ride and the ice level after turbo tunnel) the game would fall apart as the Toads default controls were always on the more slippery side. This is a detriment when a game suddenly wants to throw in platformer elements and demands that you do very precise movements. While the 2020 title does mix mash different genres in a similar manner the originals did, it does it far better as with each segment the controls do change to match the different genre designs.While I do prefer my games to have a proper focus on what type of gameplay/genre it is, Battletoads 2020 does pull it off really well for the most part. The 2020 game also has its "definitive hard moment", which comes in the form of a bullet hell shooter sequence that arrives in the penultimate act - this will really test your patience as it's the one time in the game where the difficulty matches the originals, however unlike the originals it feels as if my skills are properly being tested rather than just throwing them in my face and the bullet hell sequences do make a comeback as opposed to being once off frustrating challenges that  just disappear after one level never to be seen again.  For the most part the minigames are also enjoyable, however there are two in particular that really wore out their welcome quickly , one being the Olympic styled one where it would jump from one task to another, whether it's shooting an arrow into an object, jumping high in the air to pose  - which really drags out and doesnt feel like it gives you the proper amount of time to do the proper pose. The other mini game is the final title that wraps up the bullet hell act where you need to press buttons in the proper sequence to repair the spaceship. As with the olympic section it feels like there isn't a proper amount of time to both register what the correct symbols are you need to configure (as they change on each round) and  it drags on, a weirdly appropriate ending to the 3rd act of the game as a whole due to how long it can feel due to the difficulty , even on tadpole - for the record, I played the game on the normal difficulty and only revisted some areas on tadpole.With the beat em up aspect of the game, it feels fast and satisfying, allowing for the action to flow nicely and keep the adrenaline going as you rack up the combos, another new aspect the game introduces not seen in previous games is charging up an attack to deal serious damage to stronger enemies and one hit kill weaker ones. In the beat em up aspect it lives up to what the arcade game put forth and adds some more to it, once again leaving Battlemaniacs in the dust with its sluggish movements and beat em up gameplay - a concern I had when I saw the initial gameplay reveal and was glad to see rectified upon release.There is a platformer section that pops up in the 3rd act of the game that spaces out the bullet hell sequences where you control Pimple  as he solves puzzles to find enlightment at the top of a mountain - these puzzles are nicely done and at points do require a bit of thinking to get past and provide a good breather from the aforementioned bullet hell moments and helps set up for the penultimate section where you control the Dark Queen who's outrunning stomach acid - If those sentences didnt prove my earlier point about how crazy things can get then nothing will (should I mention the bit where you use an ambassador's body as a bodyboard?).In another improvement over both the NES game and Battlemaniacs, the turbo bikes make a return and like the Double Dragon crossover, actually manage to not be a headache this time around  - in a weird change of events they actually prove to be the highlight of the game with their fast paced obstacle dodging gameplay. As far as the series is concerned, this is the best the turbo tunnel levels have ever been.In conclusion, Battletoads 2020 is a fun romp that manages to keep itself from ever feeling like a repetive or mundane beat 'em up. While the variety may feel a bit much at times (as the game at times can feel overstuffed with so many other random elements, again a common problem that plagued both the NES game and Battlemaniacs) they never turn out to be a detriment to the overall experience, leaving me wanting to continue and work towards finishing it up.I hope we do get another sequel that can ideally streamline a few things. Of the non beat em up section I would keep in the mob chase, the turbo bikes and platforming sections as those were the best minigame additions included that added more to the typical beat 'em up experience.With good comedic writing to boot, I find myself recommending the title to people that want to have a fun crazy time that can only really be expected from the Battletoads series. It's also the perfect introduction to anyone that wants to play these games, despite in my personal opinion, merely being the second best in the franchise - but when you're number 2 to a really great, underrated arcade beat em up, that itself is a good honor, especially for a comeback.

_childDocuments_.review: Video Review: It would be disingenuous to recommend this game based on one simple problem.Way too much of this game has nothing to do with Battletoads. It is chock full of insanely frustrating and stupid mini-games that seem to have been designed by 14-year-olds on NewGrounds and repurposed into the most annoying, infuriating wastes of time Diala could possibly conjure up.  It isn't an exaggeration to say countless hours of the game aren't Battletoads - they are a bullet hell space shooter. They are a puzzle platformer. They are Sonic. They are Geometry Wars. It's like they had a conference room meeting and an executive deciced "No one is going to play a modern game of just straight level after level beating enemies up." and so they forced this developer to throw darts at a board full of game genres, and make a sampler platter of the four they hit until they hit exactly four.I have no problem with the art style, it's great. I have no problem either with the redesign of the Dark queen to look more like DeeDee from Dexter's Lab or something, who doesn't matter anyway because she played almost no role in the originals. I could forgive the stupid dialog and tweeked out storyline. What I can't forgive about this game is that they took a simple game from the late 80s/early 90s that I loved, and they inserted all this needless content into the game as if they had some mandate that they couldn't just release a relatively short arcade game with a cheaper price tag - or that the price wouldn't be justified as it is right now without needless content. The 30% of the game that IS a Battletoads game - that part is great. They introduced a lot of game mechanics and complexity to the combat that goes far beyond the simplistic single-button cheesing strategies from the original 4 games. The soundtrack is excellent and the Toads each play differently enough to make it interesting, despite most of the iconic animations not coming back.It also has no built in online multiplayer. The only way to play online is to use Remote Play Together, which works amazingly (to its credit.)I can't stress enough that unless your reaction time is faster than the average human being to begin with then you inhaled caffeine, you will get to a point of the game and get stuck there and you will hate the entire game because of it. Maybe when this is dirt cheap, give it a try, or if you subscribe to Game Pass, play it there.

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing a revival of a long-forgotten franchise is always a blessing, especially when the source material is very fondly, in some cases not so fondly, known for being one of the defining works of its generation. The original game, “Battletoads,” developed by Rare Ltd and published in 1991 is often remembered as one of the hardest beat-em’-ups of all time and set a new industry standard for the difficulty in games. The recent iteration of this, simply titled, “Battletoads,” developed by Dlala Studios and Rare Ltd, still offers ample challenge while being far more accessible to new audiences supplying a thoroughly enjoyable experience throughout most of its short duration. The first word I would use to describe this game is stylish. Inspired by 20th-century Saturday-morning cartoons, “Battletoads,” has a robust, yet self-aware and outlandish, story with plenty of slap-stick comedy to briefly distract from the consistent heart-pumping action. The main characters Zitz, Rash, and Pimple have dynamic qualities reminiscent of the classic, “Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles,” which works far better than it should and leaves so much potential for more. These three toads are on a journey to achieve fame once again after 22 years which is a fine story with plenty of other charming characters to support it. The gameplay itself is good, if not slightly simplistic, for a side-scrolling beat-em’-up. Each of the three characters is unique from the other with Zitz pushing fast combos of moves, Pimple dealing hard-hitting attacks, and Rash being a harmony between the two. The star of the show, when it comes to gameplay, happens not to be the combat itself, yet rather the wide variety of minigames sprinkled generously throughout the game. At its heart “Battletoads” is a beat-em’-up, yet I couldn’t help but be very pleased to play through a bullet-hell shooter here or a WarioWare style, Simon Says minigame there. While most of the minigames are a blast, there are a few that could use some tweaking, as the fast-paced surfing minigame and the third-person rail surfer games felt frustrating at times among others. Collectibles are scattered well in each of the levels with a few exceptions which offer replay value and can be good challenges to find. The visuals themselves serve the game well, as the cartoon style goes will with the crafted environments of the game. Good use of the Unity Engine’s resources makes the colors and backgrounds pop with exceptional quality. My biggest problem with, “Battletoads,” is its length. I was left wanting more by the end of my roughly 4-hour playthrough and the story could benefit from a little more pacing. This game is made so much better playing with a friend, yet there’s no online co-op play which only leaves local co-op available. Overall, I had a very good experience with this new iteration of 1991’s, “Battletoads,” and I’m excited to see what else Rare Ltd and Dlala Studios can do with this property. Disappointing only in its length and some frustrating hiccups, “Battletoads,” makes a superb experience catered to a modern audience and is a strong multiplayer game to tackle with a friend. 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn’t sure what to expect from the reboot of Battletoads.Going on previous outings and the little snippets of gameplay released here and there, I knew that it would have some kind of side-scrolling beat ’em up element, and that was enough to get me interested. And then there was the sumptuous art style; some will turn their nose up at it, sure, but present to me any game that looks like it could actually be a cartoon in motion and I’m happy.The truth is, I don’t think anyone is really prepared for what Battletoads has in store for them. It’s a three-or-so hour roller coaster ride full of combat, puzzles, minigames, platforming, zany humour, and so much more. More impressively, it manages to combine all these things with great finesse; nothing feels out of place or shoehorned in. Every aspect of the game is polished, and though it’s wholly enjoyable when played alone, get a couple of friends or family members in on the act and it’s an absolute riot.“A THREE-OR-SO HOUR ROLLER COASTER RIDE FULL OF COMBAT, PUZZLES, MINIGAMES, PLATFORMING, ZANY HUMOUR, AND SO MUCH MORE”Presented via wonderfully animated and voiced cutscenes that could easily be mistaken for a TV show, Battletoads‘ story is genuinely entertaining. It’s also extremely funny, leaving you chuckling in between bouts of its varied action. Reunited with Rash, Pimple and Zitz once more, you’ll find them coming to the realisation that they’ve been locked away for 26 years, and now everyone has forgot about them. Needless to say, they’re determined to make themselves celebrities again.The adventure starts off with some some old-fashioned side-scrolling fisticuffs, as you’d expect. Each character has their own characteristics – Pimple is the largest of the Battletoads, for example, and so he moves slower, is a bigger target, and hits the hardest – but they all control the same. One button performs a standard attack that forms the basis of combos, another launches enemies up into the air, and to break an opponent’s guard or simply cause a world of pain, another button can be held to charge up a powerful attack.“BATTLETOADS‘ SIDE-SCROLLING BEAT ’EM UP SEQUENCES ARE UNDOUBTEDLY THE HIGHLIGHT OF THE GAME”On top of that, each Battletoad can jump, dash out of the way of incoming damage, and use their tongues in a myriad of helpful ways. Flies can be snatched up from a distance, healing a small amount of health, bubblegum can be spat at enemies to keep them held in place for a brief period of time, and hooks can be grappled to move you in and out of the background. Your tongue can even by used to pull enemies towards you, or you towards them, much like Nero’s demonic arm does in the Devil May Cry series.Battletoads‘ side-scrolling beat ’em up sequences are undoubtedly the highlight of the game, with the action getting pleasingly chaotic at times. You’re rarely just moving right and pummelling your enemies into submission; you’re conditioned to watch out for collectibles lurking in the background that you can grab with your tongue, or targets that you can shoot. And there’s also the occasional puzzle to complete, as well as a hacking minigame.“BATTLETOADS IS HUGE AMOUNTS OF FUN WHEN PLAYED ALONE, BUT IT REALLY COMES INTO ITS OWN WHEN PLAYED IN CO-OP”Sometimes the side-scrolling beat ’em up action is put on the back-burner for extended periods of time, however. You might find yourself carrying out a menial job, playing the odd game of Toadshambo, or racing a hoverbike through an assault course. One of the game’s four acts is even pretty much comprised of just platforming and twin-stick shooter segments. The pace of the game suffers slightly as a result, but everything is put together so well that you’ll still be glued to the screen.As mentioned previously, Battletoads is huge amounts of fun when played alone, but it really comes into its own when played in co-op. Only local co-op is supported unfortunately, but it’s of the drop-in drop-out kind, so additional players can come and go as they please without causing a disruption. Players will need to work together to succeed, effectively communicating with each other in certain activities, for example, or picking each other up when they’re down in side-scrolling beat ’em up sections. It simply makes everything more involving and enjoyable.“THERE’S BEEN A LOT OF GREAT GAMES RELEASED THIS YEAR, BUT BATTLETOADS WILL SURELY PROVE TO BE ONE OF THE MOST MEMORABLE”Battletoads continues to make the series more accessible, too. Multiple difficulty levels are available, and while you can’t change it mid-game, well-placed checkpoints ensure it’s always possible to proceed with sheer determination. And if you die often enough, the game will throw you a lifeline in the form of invincibility. You can, of course, turn that feature off if you wish. Basically, you can make Battletoads as easy or hard as you like.It’s hard to play Battletoads and not be mightily impressed with what it achieves. It mixes so many genres and does it so, so well. Then there’s the humour, which is a hard thing to get right, especially in the world of video games. Dlala Studios and Rare have a done a grand job of bringing the Battletoads into the 21st century, and I really hope we get to see more of them. There’s been a lot of great games released this year, but Battletoads will surely prove to be one of the most memorable.

_childDocuments_.review: It’s here guys! It is hard to believe that after the Arcade adaptation in 1994, it’s been 26 years that fans have waited for a new entry in the franchise of the world’s most famous Toads. Without boring you with ancient history, the original NES game was created to rival the success of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, which by 1991 was enjoying a lot of success based on the Animated Series from 1987, the year I was born! As a Beat Em Up, the controllers were a nightmare and the game became infamous for its tremendous difficulty when in reality it played as a memory game where knowing what challenge comes next made things a little bit easier. Even if the controls were basic and unpolished, the game had that “” that is missing in so many games today. The three amphibian brothers () were so cool and the world around them was original and interesting that made the game special for all of us 30 something’s.  Even though with the release of its sequel for SNES the game was more polished and better in every other way, people hoped that Battletoads was brought back with the treatment and care it deserved. Very similar to the situation that another famous Beat Em Up experienced this year, . So know that it is here, was it worth the wait? Hell yeah.Street of Rage 4 gave you the game you remembered with today’s technology and that felt safe but tremendously successful. Battletoads is doing the opposite. Even though the game is a sequel, it gave the Toads a 180 degrees spin and if you ask me, it works. There is a strong influence from games like Cuphead or the "new" Rayman games where the art style is vibrant and with a lot of charisma and it feels like it could belong into a TV Show and we know Cuphead is headed that way but I can definitely see this for Battletoads as well. Actually, the game was written by people who worked on TV Shows before and you can tell by the personas in these characters and their dialogue, which is genuinely funny and not forced. I will talk about the gameplay in a minute, but I really wish the game could have been longer. I had a TON of fun but the world and the characters are so rich that you end up wanting a lot more. I hope this sells a LOT of copies so we can get DLC with more content. And as I mentioned, I understand that there is definitely a TV Show being done from this and you can see that  so I guess this game is just the first step into taking Battletoads to the next level. Oh, please keep all the voice actors for the TV show. Specially the Dark Queen, that woman is talented and awesome!As I said, the graphics are amazing. I can’t believe that I loved the animation and how fluid the combat works. Kudos to  for the  amount of work they had to put on this game to change it from the lackluster demo shown to us last year. They definitely outdid themselves. The music is simply amazing.  and you will realize that there are a bunch of classic songs remade as metal head bangers () and some new tunes that go hand in hand with the attitude of this game. The gameplay is solid, accessible and with no complications, allowing you to perform 70 hits combos no problem and allows you to keep juggling opponents in the air with those ridiculous but classic over the top morph attacks that the Battletoads have. And just like the original sequel, Battletoads in Battlemaniacs, to make sure that the  mechanic doesn't become a chore, several mini games were included in between stages only this time they are a lot more fun and definitely less frustrating; from a shoot em up ship scene, to the classic speed bikes (now from a different angle, ) to a massage session. Yeah, really. The boss fights mechanics are fun and they definitely look great on screen, often being huge and merciless with some really cool and original designs.On the down side, , there is no online co-op, I would have loved some more enemy variety and the design of certain classic characters are a little doubtful and definitely more story content would have been much appreciated but on the bright side of these minor complains, the game plays like a charm, there are no bugs or anything that messes up with the experienced and based on playing it on PC, so far I can say the game runs smoothly and responsive with my Xbox One controller. Battletoads looks great, is a blast to play and is here to stay! It treats the fans of the franchise with respect and its wonderful world full of charisma and creativity opens the door to new fans and mainstream media alike, which hopefully gives us a sequel that doesn’t take 26 years to come! Now we just need Arc System Works to resurrect Double Dragon and we might have one of the most unexpected but successful crossovers of all time kicking ass once again! One can only hope...

_childDocuments_.review: Well hate to do this but I'm going to have to say a pass on old Battletoads. Why? Well for several reason.The premise of Battletoads is a good old fashion arcade beat'em up like what most of us would remember from the 90's. In a way it is that though a very watered down version. Rather than just beat up folks in some zany and crazy ways the game's combat system is very simplified. It consist of a light attack that can be stringed along with inter mixing of hard attacks to create some powerful effects. Each toad has their own way of doing this but you can guess what it is. Zitz is the light weight that is quick, Pimple is the bruiser, and Rash is the balanced. While though it is fun it does get old to a point. Unlike the prior Battletoad games where you would have a multitude of ways to fight that made it interesting and challenging, this does not. All of the fights will simply be go to a small enclosed space and duke it out, move on to next space, rinse and repeat. Some of the boss fights and enemies are memorable and well designed but again their AI is simplistic to figure out that you will easily guess their attack patterns even on the hardest setting of the game.The art style of the game is very reminiscent to something like Alien Hominid or flash games of the early 2000's. As well the character designs themselves for our heroes and villains is essentially ripping off Earthworm Jim. It is bright and colorful and I will say that stage designs for the themes were done nicely.As to the overall story well the writing is just bad. The game tries to poke fun at itself with the use of jokes that just don't land the laugh. There is also other forms of humor that I also just did not get. For example, there is one boss fight where after you defeat the guy he begs you not to send him to the hospital on account that his roommate keeps ketchup packs in his car, opened, and it will get all over his pants. How is this suppose to be funny? There are many things like this and worse. Though the one thing I cannot understand is why mini games were included. Between each act you are forced to participate in a mini game akin to something like from Warioware. Thing is there really isn't any point to these nor do you have the option to just fail them and move on. In that, they are also just not that fun anyways being more tedious. I really wanted to give this a liking but I just can't and I am already past the point of getting a refund. If you are looking to buy this even for the nostalgia of Battletoads from back in the day, I would advise not to. Or if you must, wait until it goes on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: (To be clear, I have plenty of playtime on the GamePass version)80% of the people that think this game is bad have not played it.10% of the people that think this game is bad,bought the game and played it for less than 2 hours to make sure they put in a bad review.And the other 10% are people that legitimately did not like this game.Now, let me be honest with you: Battletoads 2020 is nowhere near a perfect game.But you know what game is nowhere near perfect, the original Battletoads.Yes, that is right, take off the nostalgia goggles kids. The original Battletoads was a janky beat-em-up with horrendous difficulty spikes. It had a very strange style, that only strikes now with nostalgia; but at its time, it really was a TMNT rip-off.Sorry, we need to get this out of the way to ensure my review lands.This game is not by any means a loyal remake of the original Battletoads; the manchildren crying about it are 100% right.Let's address those complaints to tell you how that is a GOOD thing:This game is not insanely difficult, it is APPROPRIATELY difficult. Yes, you can play the game in the highest difficulty and still beat it just fine; but it takes legitimate skill and timing to get all the perfect rankings. You, the player, can tailor the difficulty to your playstyle.This game does not have the same art-style as the original game. That is 100% correct, and that is a GREAT thing. The hand drawn art-style of this game is terrific, making the characters DROWN in charm. Rash, Zitz, and Pimple are actually distinguishable characters now with strengths and flaws in their personalities, and it makes me happy to say it.I keep hearing the complaint that this looks and feels like a Cartoon Network cartoon... and I have yet to get a valid argument on how that makes it a bad thing? That is unarguably the best thing about this game and the one reason to get it. This game feels like a saturday morning cartoon that I grew up with in the 90s, and that is nostalgia at its finest.The combat is probably the weakest part of this game, and ironically that is the thing most similar to the original game.The combat is very basic, with one or two combos being the most optimal to go for each character.  It is still very satisfying to play, especially with a controller; just very basic at its core.In conclusion, please give this game a try if you want to play a new battletoads game.I think its a legitimate argument to those "angry" at this game to kindly ask them to go back to playing the originals. I keep hearing "we want to play legit revival of the old games" but reviving the old games would be a mistake; those games were just a product of their time, get over it. A fresh new coat of paint was the way to go, and I am extremely glad Microsoft and Rare stuck with their instincts alongisde with Dlala and did not listen to the loud minority that dislike this game superficially.

_childDocuments_.review: I got this on sale for 5 bucks. Normal difficulty took under 5 hours. Con: This game is Steam Link Multiplayer only but has 3 Player/Multiplayer achievements.Con: The story AND art style come off like a cheap children cartoon. Con: Game play is nothing special. Difficulty during Single-player feels inconsistent. Con: Boss fights seem really uninspired, and one of the fights is an overload of chaotic mess that the mechanics of the game don't really support fighting against.Con: The mini-game sections start with a timer, and without giving you the controls/explanation guaranteeing you fail it once before you understand it.Con: No Professor T-Bird nor Princess Angelica... No cameo, and no mention.Con: They tried to make a new name logo, and it's terrible. A lot of the music falls flat as well. They brought back some of the old music but it's used extremely briefly...Con: Large lack of extra features even post-game.Con: One of the mini-games uses pressure sensitive triggers so if you aren't using a controller similar to an Xbox controller you need to get lucky, or fail until you do.Con: Game is extremely short.Con: Uninspired, and a shell of it's former self. Remember the originals? Remember picking up a broken piece of an enemy, and using it? Remember beating up an enemy, and riding it? Remember picking up an enemy, and throwing them at another enemy? This game somehow made the combat more basic than the NES originals... Think about that for a second.Con: Character design is pretty bad. Dark Queen suffers the most as she is now a mad scientist for some reason, and with the exception of her hair color really doesn't look anything like the original character. Remember those bad ass spiked belts, and spiked gear the Toads had? Gone. Their designs are very basic in this. Even the enemies of the game are very basic, and uninspired. Pro: I liked the personality of the Dark Queen. She's sarcastic, and witty. Overall it was a neat choice what her role ended up being in this game. Pro: Some of the jokes land, and when they do it's actually pretty clever. Sadly I had to flip a coin to list this as a pro, or con because some of the jokes are just really bad... Plus this list needed more pro...Pro: The classic symbolic 3 spiked logo was kept. They re-did it so it looks worse than the original but at least they didn't throw it away completely like they did with the other classic name logo.If you don't mind the con's then I say buy this game when it's on sale for 5 bucks, or less if possible.Otherwise I suggest just watching a review on YouTube so you can see what it would be like if you wanted to waste your money.

gamestop. it was my first ever job in a management position and i was enjoying it for what it was. sure the pay was crap, but i got to talk about the video games i love and inform customers about new games and information that i always had on hand. this was before i really dove into the deepest darkest parts of the internet, before i was really familiar with "memes" and 4chan. looking back now, i was pretty naive and oblivious to the problems the internet posed to people. anyways, i was working one night with a fellow employee named jack. it was around seven and the shift had gone on without incident. the store was dead at the moment since people are at home or out eating dinner around this time. i was sorting games and worked when the phone rang. now, usually a phone ringing didn’t mean anything. little did i know that that one phone call would change my perception of the world. i promptly answered the phone, greeting nonchalantly “thanks for calling gamestop, where we buy and sell used games, this is <redacted>. how can i help you?”“do you have a game called battletoads?”now, i was familiar with battletoads, and i knew this was a trolling phone call. i rolled my eyes and hung up the line, shrugging and going about my work. and then another phone call.“do you have battletoads?”and then another. and another. for the next two hours, the phone didn’t stop ringing. my associate and i spent the next two hours answering each of these calls, our work completely disrupted. and with each phone call, the callers became more and more vapid, violent, and vehement. there were calls where people played porn noise over the phone, calls asking for my picture with time stamp on /b/, loud obnoxious roaring noises, and so on and so forth. it was one of the longest two hours i’ve ever experienced. when i got home, i cried. yes, dear readers, a full grown man went home and shed tears because of phone calls. in retrospect, i think i overreacted, but i was really upset. how could people i didn’t even know hate me so much when they didn’t even know me? however, i got over it pretty quick after a couple minutes and promptly passed out, pushing the troubling thoughts out of my mind, figuring that things would blow over.nope.for the next two months, i received these phone calls, with people specifically asking for me, <redacted>, threatening me and the store that i worked at that the calls won’t stop until i posted on 4chan my name with my photo and time stamp on /b/.  it got so bad that i was forced to relocate stores. and yet the calls continued to follow me at the new store that i worked at. the phone number for the store that i worked at was posted on encyclopedia dramatica, and the harassing calls would not stop. even to this day, after my two year tenure at gamestop, those stores that i worked at still received the odd phone call here and there, asking for a <redacted> and battletoads. was i upset? yes. reasonably so? probably not in hindsight, but at _childDocuments_.review: It's games like this where I wish I could select "maybe" instead of a hard Like/Dislike on Steam recommendations, because this one certainly is a mixed bag despite me leaning towards liking it, but being frustrated with it. Also I never played the original Battletoads, and I do not this game is quite different which means purists will most likely dislike the changes.As far as graphics and presentation go, the game is slick and pleasing to look at, I have no qualms about how it looks, but it does remind me of a Saturday morning cartoon I would wake up to. The music is also pretty top tier, there's alot of tracks in this game that I really love and get pumped up for, especially that crunchy intro and battle music.As for story and characters, it deviates quite alot from the original game as far as I'm away. Personally I find it a bit pretentious at times, but I still enjoyed it, there's alot of character from both the toads and the enemies. It oozes personality.Now the gameplay is where it's a really mixed bag for me, the side scrolling, 2D beat em up combat is fun and satisfying enough for me, and it's reasonably challenging, although you can tell it was designed for multiplayer. Single players will find it a bit harder to keep track of everything going on while simultaneously dodging and attacking. I do dislike how multiple functions are assigned to the same button with a combination of presses. Do we really need to a similar, yet separate button combination to collect health pickups, spit gum and pull/push enemies/myself closer? I think it should have been just walk over health pickups to use them like you would in alot of other beat em-ups, it's too much to press the right button combination while dodging large swarms or enemies and attacking at the same time. Each Toad felt distinctively different in combat and it doesn't take long to work out their gameplay style/quirks. Unfortunately the enemy isn't great, it's basically the same 3 or 4 enemies re-skinned for each new section of the game. I generally like and enjoy the combat,The other major thorn in my side about this game is the mini-games at each interval to break up the gameplay, I like mini-games and breaking up the gameplay, but it is not well thought out here. In my first encounter, I didn't even know it was a mini-game, I thought it was a cutscene and I wasn't given much explanation or instruction on how to play it. This issue becomes more frequent as they throw multiple different mini-games at you, some are more poorly implemented than others. The "reboot the computer" mini-game has you doing multiple actions to complete it, but shows EVERY possible button combination and action on screen at the same time. However, there is no explanation on how to play, you don't even know what button presses and combinations to use each retry as it randomises the mini game each time. Some feed back on which combination I needed to use each time would have helped, whether they highlighted the section that was currently in play or had it flash or messaged you at the top/bottom of the screen would have greatly improved the mini-game and made it less frustrating (spending a minute or two to work out which section is in play 3 times and complete it before the time runs out is really cruel). Often, this mini-games are significantly more difficult than the beat em-up sections, they're also necessary to complete before progressing the story. They also become much more frequent towards the end while abandoning the original gameplay, playing 5 or 6 minigames before the next beat em-up section felt bizarre for this genre. Although, a couple of these games while punishingly challenging, were also really fun, I mainly enjoyed the bullet hell sections, and the sled one with the fast button changes was fun too.Overall, I feel like if you aren't a purist who wants to stick closely to the original, and you can handle the lack of feedback in some mini-games, and other bizarre game mechanic flaws and short shortsightedness, you might enjoy Battletoads quite alot. But I would still recommend buying this game on discount instead of full price, it's a really mixed bag overall.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: The game is fun with good banter. But it tries to do a lot of things and not excel at any one of them. From beat em up to bullet hell to platformer. Some better than the others but often times after such a sudden shift the difficulty spikes and it takes a while to get adjusted to the new mechanic you are suddenly introduced to halfway through the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Actually a very solid game. Nostalgic people seem to forget that the hardest part of the OG game is that you had limited lives and when it was game over you had to start over from the beginning- in terms of actual gameplay challenge there are some very intense moments that not only rival, but at times surpass the original. The variety of gameplay is something I see other reviews complain about, but it was an aspect of the original I loved- the only real difference is some of the levels are more of a minigame style as opposed to various platformer/brawler mechanics, but they can still be challenging
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: (Completed on Xbox One, first time playing on Steam) I don't know why people hate this game so much. It's a fun self aware mix of gameplay styles and that's not a bad thing. The beat em up levels are fun, the hoverbike levels are alright and the quick time levels are fun too. People say the art style is bad and I don't really see why. It's unique, unique doesn't equal bad. The story is good, the writing is hilarious and overall, I think it's a really fun time. I think the price point is also a key factor. For $20 you're getting more than what you paid for.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Mixed. Best experienced in Co-op. Looks fantastic. Presentation is fitting for a prime Saturday morning cartoon. I kind of like the old school challenge to some levels. Overall for gameplay, difficulty and collision detection feels very off at times and the player is hammered over the head with variety for level types (Beat'em up, racing/dodging, platforming, etc). The game's sense of identity is best derived from the cutscenes and art style. Again, mixed. Where's that neutral rating? I'm honestly not sure if this should be a thumbs up or down. Maybe a thumbs up for some of the throwback levels.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Of course, this is different that the original NES/SNES games, but it is an experience that will remind you on the original in plenty of levels. The only downsides are (besides the Disney-like Dark Queen) that there are too many space shooter levels and the Pimple levels in Act III are also not very appealing.In total, definitely get it if you liked the original series - but don't except the very same experience. Due to the plenty checkpoints, you can easily beat it - compared to the original, which was entirely based on building up the levels in your muscle memory.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun beat em up mixed with space shooting and puzzle levels. Though I think they over did it with the space shooting and the puzzle modes. I feel like 1 section of each would of sufficed instead of just throwing all these "extra" levels at you for no reason. It felt like it just dragged the game out and it took so long for them to get back to the beat em up style. Those levels just felt like fillers and they probably over did it just to make the game longer. I really enjoyed the cut scenes in the game and loved the humor behind them. To me they were some of the best content in the game. If you are a fan of Battletoads I would say get it but wait for a sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: This game is sick as hell. The only part of this game that I didn't like was the chapter: The Pimple Joys of life, which is so slow and way way WAY too peaceful compared to the rest of the game. It honestly feels like the devs needed an excuse to say that this game was for kids, so they just threw in a super cutesy peaceful chapter for the heck of it. But other than that, this game is amazing. 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Adored my time with battletoads! Its certainly not for eveyone but none of the mini games over stayed there welcome and i enjoyed the variety there was of them!! The story is very funny and well done too in my opinion!! I do wish there was more fighting in the middle section of the game and it was longer in general but thats probably because i enjoyed it so much!
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a lot of fun, but the second half really drags on and the mini games become especially annoying at that point, music is absolutely fantastic and the animation during game play is really well done. The plot while it did have some funny jokes, the characters  and story were low key kind of lame.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the identity Battletoads has and doubles it.While it's pretty disappointing that there's not a friendly fire option, it pays a ton of respect to the game and the era. It has VERY hardcore Saturday morning cartoon vibes in hilarious ways. And, of course, local multiplayer is always a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads is a fantastic beat em up where you play as 1 of 3 main characters. It is not just a beat em up though. It changes up the core gameplay multiple times and you play through multiple genres of very well crafted games. It's so surprising that how well every game genre was made and played. A lot of them such as the shoot em up part was so good that it could've been its own game by itself. The story was quite decent and was really quirky and fun which i really enjoyed. Music and the artstyle both are fantastic and really suits the formula of Battletoads. Characters are really charming and sometimes very funny. Everything feels solid and very polished. This was my first Battletoads game so i can't comment on the changes from the original formula but this game made me want more out of the franchise so i will be turning back to play the other games. It gets dirt cheap on sale and is a definite must buy for all the fans of the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit, this wasn't the revival of the Battletoads we were all hoping for.  The way the characters talked and behaved felts like how they went from Teen Titans to Teen Titans Go and some of the story felt like it didn't make any sense at all.  However, I'd be lying if I said I didn't enjoy the levels where you beat up the badies in the classic "Beat'em Up" style.  And hey, call me a sucker for the "Beat'em Up" games since I grew up with those games back in the 90's.  Could be better, but also could've gotten worse.  And I would suggest stick more to the "Beat'em Up" style levels and a more mature story if they make another game.  But I'd say it's ok if you're fan of the Battletoads and/or side scrolling beat'em up games.  Not great, but just ok.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed the game in general, but it was an uneven experience. The beatemup levels where challenging and entertaining, but some of the platforming level where mediocre at best. I liked the character designs and voice acting and the animations where funny, like one of those Saturday morning cartoons. If you play the game in the hardest difficulty, is as challenging as the SNES version, but in no way as hard as the original NES game. I enjoyed the game overall and I would like to play a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: If you still have a dying need for beat em ups with deep, freeflowing combos after finishing Streets of Rage 4, this will quench your need and more. Style rankings, combos, constant genre switching, the works. Perfect for your average Devil May Cry player. Character designs and the art style will probably need some getting used to especially if you are coming here from the original Battletoads for the NES. The writing is like a modern kids cartoon, whether that's good or bad is up to you but I personally adore it. It could do without the Rash wearing a diaper scene and the Dark Queen spreading her cheeks to the far corners of the Earth, but I'm sure you can look past those no problem. I know I had to but I digress, Lots of callbacks to the original as well as great voice acting and a pretty engaging story. Animation is also a high point with this game, it's very fluid and does a great job of amplifying the wacky, exaggerated animations of the original. Expect a lot of 4th wall breaks idk some people think that's a problem so just a heads up lolbut yeah one year later, this game still holds up. it's really fun, I personally love that beat em ups are finally opening up like this in terms of how the gameplay is designed and as of me writing this, it's on sale for $5. and even without the discount, it's still fairly cheap. No reason not to give it a shot, right?
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Such a good old school type of game, I played on Games Pass and thought it was so good I bought here as well.  Funny goofy characters like I remember them from my childhood from their first game. Cool levels with a variation on the level design. Controls are a bit clunky, here and there. Hope to some one run this on Games Done Quick one day :)Recommend for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: The game itself is a wonderful throwback to everything the old Battletoads game was.  The cartoon graphics feels like a hearken back to 90's era style, and the full story gameplay is just filled with lots of little tidbits here and there regarding the franchise that old school gamers like myself love.  Even the start of the game has that wonderfully iconic "pause beat" that the original game had.   To go over every little detail of nostalgia would make this review too long, so all I can say if you like beat-em-ups, and you're familiar with the old Nintendo version of this, or played the lesser known Battletoads & Double Dragon crossover, you're likely to love this game.  It's much easier than the original, and should bring many fun hours of gameplay, and likely replay-ability.  HOWEVER.....While this is a wonder nostalgic throwback, I do find one... major.... glaring problem with it.That would be the lack of online co-op gameplay.  Keeping true to the 1991 series, this game can only be played either by yourself, or if you have a friend in your general vicinity that is interested (if you do, you're truly blessed).  That being said, in 2021, games such as these NEED to be online co-op, to play with friends across cities, states, and countries; and for such a game to not have such capabilities is doing the fans that wish to buy and play with their friends, a huge disservice.  If I was to rate this game as a single player game alone, I would give it 5 full stars (out of 5) with all the nostalgia brought into it.  It is obvious the creators truly understood the spirit of the game, and wanted to make a good timeline story after such a long absence of anything Battletoads related.  The game as it currently stand right now, I can't give anything better than a 3 out of 5, purely because it is obvious the game SHOULD BE co-op online, like so many other beat-em-up games before it, but fails to deliver on this much needed premise.  I really want to be able to recommend this game, so that a new generation may be able to enjoy it as I once did, but the lack of co-op severely hurts it.  I hope the developers can create an online co-op system in time, and put it in an update.  If they do, I'll be glad to go back and review this again.So, overall 3 out of 5 stars,Devs, please make an online co-op system.You deserve 5 stars for all this game is, but not without proper co-op play.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: A classic beaten up reborn! The game is a lot of fun but just like the original can get extremely hard in some areas. Since you get no extra lives you really have to smash that didge button.When I saw trailers for the game I wasn't thrilled about the art style but after playing the game in person and seeing all the unique hand drawn animations I came a fan and was really impressed.The story is wacky Saturday morning cartoon stuff which isn't a bad thing. I has entertained and there are hit ND misses with the humor.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Overall:  Super fun experience that doesn't try to take itself too seriously.Music - It does a nice job remixing David Wise's music and integrating new tracks into the mix.  Starting off with Pause music (NES) and Khaos Mountain was a nice ease into the new musics.Gameplay is solid and responsive.  The tag-out system is nice to try and fight monotony that can come with beat 'em ups.  Even if that doesn't work, there is a LOT of variety in the gameplay (turbo bike sections, bullet hells, puzzle platforming).Art style is nice and bright.  The art style on the Toads especially allows them to have their personality shine through.  There is a lot popping colors and nice animations to signal attacks and whatnot.Humor is very much on the absurdist side.  This will not be for everybody.  It is also a little on the self-depreciating side, but in a fun way.  Already been said, but it does NOT take itself too seriously and this works in the game's favor.No matter how you feel about the humor, there is no doubt that the voice actors for this game were outstanding.  I hope they had a blast making with the VA work, because it was super enjoyable listening to.  Some sections can be tough, but the conveniences of modern gaming (checkpoints, save points, no lives/ continues system) makes thing nice and fair.Overall, I would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: In the first two months after release, Battletoads attracted over a million users - this number includes both game buyers and Xbox Game Pass subscribers (“Battletoads” became part of the service’s library from day one). During this period, gamers were responsible for 42 million accidents on a turbobike and defeated the boss Porkshank one and a half million times. The most popular toad was Rush, and the least popular was Zitz! And it seems bright and dynamic, but... JERKING OFF THE SAME MOBS JUST DRIVES YOU CRAZY, and quickly gets boring...
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I had the original for NES so I figured I would check this reboot out. Not as insanely difficult as the original, but it's a pretty good beat em up. However, the weird puzzle minigame crap with the blue alien lady "Bratty" climbing the mountain of enlightenment or whatever is AWFUL. Really. Bad. The rest of the game is fun, but that whole tedious sequence should be skippable.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about Battletoads? I didn't come to this game because I played the originals - because I didn't. I guess I was interested because I like a good beat em up and this seemed to fit the bill. The beat em up aspect of this game was well done, nice assortment of different moves, each toad has a different move set, decent variety of enemies, interesting boss encounters. However, mixed in with these beat em up levels are random other levels such as platforming levels, fast bike driving levels, flying bullet hell shooting levels and mini-game levels. It was definately surprising. I like the platforming levels. The fast bike and flying bullet hell levels were hard but decent as well. I was not a fan of the mini-game levels, probably the only thing about this game that I disliked. The story was interesting and entertaining - like a Saturday morning cartoon. The controls were good, I used an XBox 1 controller without any issues. I completed the game on Toad difficulty and that was a decent challenge. Overall, I judge a game based on how well it keeps me engaged and whether I am enjoying progressing thru the game and this game kept me wanting to continue and move on to the next level. Looking forward to the next Battletoads game - hopefully it wont take another 25 years for them to make one!
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: This game might be more geared towards kids, but I would still call it a decent remake. It is nothing like the original, so if you have that expectation, get rid of it. I don't care that it's different, but it plays out more like you're watching a cartoon episode of "Teen titans go" with the same type of quirky random cuts and comments. The action does have some challenge to it so it's not all straight boring side scroller. They mix it up with a little bit of comedy tasks here and there which is appreciated. I probably wouldn't recommend this to my adult friends who are looking for a relive of the nostalgia from the 90's version, but it's still a fun and quirky game.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Three things worth noting:1. Got this on sale for $5.2. Played on tadpole difficulty since I'm the type that usually plays on easier difficulties so I don't get as stressed.3. This is my first Battletoads game.Ok lol, so I know I was playing on easy, but I did not expect to beat the game at around 2 hours XD. That being said, I say it's definitely worth it! I don't even think I would have been upset had I payed $20. I love the animated cut-scenes and the sprite work, and I also found the raunchy sense of humor pretty funny (it won't be for everyone, though). I went in knowing full well that it has varying game play styles, but I ended up really liking the package as a whole! The beat'em up sections would have ended up feeling too repetitive without the variations, in my opinion. If you're the type who prefers a certain level of consistency when it comes to games while also not being too fond of immature/self-referential humor, you aren't going to like this at all. But if you enjoy experimental games and don't have the slightest care in the world over their metacritic scores being in the yellow, then this just might be something you find enjoyable!
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I purchased the game when it was on sale for $5 and having low expectations for a $5 game I was still disappointed. The admittedly fun arcade brawling was frequently interrupted by annoying and frustrating mini-games. The story was bizarre, childish, and I've got to think insulting to long time fans of Battletoads.Save your money!
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Remember 1991? No?You might not appreciate this game the way you should if you haven't played the original. You also might hate this game if you're a long time fan. Don't go into it expecting anything other than a reboot that mmmmmaybe isn't as good as previous entries, and you'll be good. It's supposed to be a beat-em-up, and it is, with a WHOLE bunch of other stuff wrapped around it. It's a platformer, it's a bullet-hell shooter, it's got a handful of QTE, it's got some puzzle stuff, and even generalized minigames. It's not at all the Battletoads that I expected, and at times, it was even a little dull. The story doesn't seem to really be all "there", it feels like it was edited by someone with severe ADHD. It's also got some parts that you just have to guess a whole bunch until you get lucky and figure it all out, REALLY bad explanations as to what exactly you're supposed to be doing.BUT, all that by the wayside (because really, it's not THAT bad), it's a fun game with a TON of nostalgia, hysterical moments, and charm for miles. Could it have been better? Yeah, absolutely, but it's a nice start to a great take on Battletoads for a modern audience. I think standard price is $20, I got it on sale for $5. Money well spent, but really.... wait for a sale. I don't think I'd be so forgiving for the full $20.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of beat-em-ups with varying gameplay segments in between levels then this is definitely a must-have.  The story is genuinely funny and feels like a cartoon pilot, the beat-em-up segments are fun and challenging, and the old school challenge is definitely there. My only complaint is that some of the mandatory minigame segments can get a little tiring but they usually don't overstay their welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Disclaimer:  I never played the original NES version of Battletoads.  Well, maybe I did, but that would have been 30 years ago so I don't remember.This game STANDS ON ITS OWN as a lightheated, fun experience.  Sure, there are only SOME beat-em-up fighting levels.  There are plenty of different kinds of levels with different challenges.  It's kind of like having a lot of games in one. And hey, variety is the spice of life.Even if green wasn't my favorite color, I would still give this game a thumbs up.  We've been doing multiplayer and each of us is controlling a different fro...I mean Toad.  Sorry guys!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game on Toad difficulty... I will not attempt this on Battletoad difficulty.... People would have complained had it been a NES copy of the original - so the devs decided to bring something completely new - graphics, gameplay, style - even plot twist! I, personally, commend them for changing the recipe. Battletoads have had a few sequels on older generation consoles - so why not something new? Gameplay wise - it is not an easy brawler. Heck, it's not just a brawler! Platform elements - Bike rides - Galaga-style shoot'em ups - mini-games (which I hated) - etc. The humour is just a inch under the belt - no complaints - and the cartoon network style is pleasing to the eyes. I would recommend it - play it solo. My next run will be co-op on Toad difficulty... it really is not an easy game.

_childDocuments_.review: I had a good time playing through on easy difficulty. Gave me a few good laughs and smiles. Nothing in it feels very deep but the gameplay keeps changing fast enough to keep from getting bored. (Not sure if I'd feel that way if I played it on higher difficulty.)I'm a huge fan of the NES and GB games. _childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I can only recommend this game if it's on sale and you have a mate to play it with.Humour & story in the game are mediocre at best. After about an hour or so the story started going places and I just stopped paying attention to it. It just felt like it was made for much younger folks, so if you're in your late 20s-30s, the best you'll get is a chuckle or two out of it (though this is subjective, of course).Gameplay was OK. The way controls that we were shown while playing (on the joystick) were confusing and my mate and I were trying to figure out what buttons we had to press to do this or that. Beat 'em up levels were OK but fairly simple. Where the game shined for me were the mini-games as they were most fun for two players. The variety of those mini-games I think is what saved Battletoads from being very boring and stale. When I played alone through some of the levels though, I didn't have all that much fun. Also, the game is short- it would take you 4-5 hours to beat it.Music - nothing stood out to me.I played the OG Battletoads back in early 2000s and absolutely loved the game. It was one of my favourites on the SEGA console. Sadly, this one didn't win me over but I must say I did have some fun with the game when playing with friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Good stuff. Turbo tunnel is just as frustrating now as it was as a child. Bonus though, this time you don't have to start over at level 1 when you mess up, so you can relive your frustration instantly. Over, and over, and over, and over again. Beating the turbo bike level had level of satisfaction of beating a level of "I Wanna Be the Boshy"10/10, would wreck a speed bike again.
_childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: Oh hell yeah, this was a nice break.Battletoads is one of those games that despite being an nes classic and being left dormant for years on end, didn't take itself too seriously. What you got here is a game meant to be played with friends, and have some lighthearted laughs along the way.To get it out of the way, playing the game by yourself on normal mode, its just under 5 hours. Not the longest game in the world, but whats there has enough love and care put into it that it doesn't feel half-hearted.The arcade beat em up style changes if you play with friends or not. With friends, its what you'd expect. Each player has a character, you and punch, chime in to keep combos up, then have some goofy add in's like the ability to high five each other.By yourself, is interesting. None of the characters have full tool sets like in traditional beat em ups, the co-op wants friends to help you. Whereas singleplayer. its like a 3-man tag team sort of combat. like if you have fighterz, or marvel vs. capcom 3 and made a beat em up out of that. Mid-combo, your expected to tag in and flip between the other toads to keep it. Which on one had I was thrown off a bit since I tend to prefer single characters that can do everything, But it got me in the mindset of recalling what all three characters can do, thus the overall game became a lot easier when it game to the beat em up segments. That said, I tended to prefer the other gameplay types presented since a large portion of the difficulty came from enemies who were faster than you would just run away and hit you from a far. When this is happening theres typically a mix of enemies who approach you and hold up their block. Which while you could break, the amount of time it takes to charge up an attack capable of break these blocks, there would usually be another guy slap you just before its ready right behind them, if not another enemy far away shoot you from a distance.I'll say this, if you're thinking about this game as your next big beat em up, you're going to be disappointed. Get something like streets of rage 4 if your looking for a traditional experience, since the game will spend a good portion of its time with other play styles.You've got bullet hell segments, platforming, puzzles, quick time events, and so on. None of these segment are necessarily bad, I found a number of them really fun, while others the explanation was minimal and it just sort of said "go" before you really knew what was happening. They'll certainly take you out of it if you expected to fight and nothing else.The art style for the game is perfect for what its going for. Something cartoony, but still easy to distinct whats what for a video game. I will said as a draw back, despite being able to tell "thats an enemy", "that's something I can interact with", or "I can walk there." I found myself making poor decisions in the beat em up portions of the game from time to time since the animations for the villains attacks are just as stretchy and cartoony as the playable characters. Its not unmanageable however I did find myself a number of times thinking I was far enough from an enemy to avoid an attack only to get hit cause I underestimated the enemies range.the soundtrack is nice, though sad to say, with the time I spent with the game, I couldn't really tell any of the tracks apart from one another. It all just kind of blended together that I'd have to listen to the soundtrack for a little bit to tell them apart.The writing is decent, I tend to not think of the story when it comes to games that are gameplay first, however the emphasis on it is worth mentioning. It plays out like a down to earth cartoon with a well aware sense of what the battletoads IP has become. It knows people aren't here to take it very seriously and the guys who are willing to give the game a try can crack a smile with some humor just enough over a kids head but still has a couple jokes only kids would find funny. Not everything is gonna have you off your seat in hysteria but there's a couple jokes that got me.In the end its a pretty short and sweet game, if you got a couple buddies to gather around, or you just need to burn a couple hours, give it a try.8/10TL:DR, its not gonna be your next big fighter. But a solid game to play on the side.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly fun co-op brawler. The various genres and modes in the story keep the game varied and the new battle mechanics are great. Gameplay is definitely deeper than the new Streets of Rage, especially if you are familiar with traditional fighting games which can give you a feel for some nifty combo extensions and cancels. To the reviewer who said the combat was lacking, I'm not sure what to tell you. Maybe try exploring more instead of pressing the same stuff over and over? It's more than fine and more than I expected from this game to be honest.Soundtrack is amazing as well, definitely got my vote in the Steam Awards for OST of the Year. Plenty of great new tracks that sound awesome and are very reminiscent of Donkey Kong Country, which makes sense considering Rare made them and Battletoads. Lots of old tracks got remixes as well that will stand out while you play and make you stop just to jam out a little.Many people who played the original Battletoads games may be concerned with the difficulty but I can assure you it is completely fine here. There are multiple difficulties to choose from so you can play on easy, normal, or classic hard Battletoads difficulty if you want. The hover bike levels have also returned and are completely redesigned to be less frustrating and are actually really fun now.In regards to the art direction of the game, I disliked it at first but it grew enough on me that I am pretty neutral about it. I would prefer if they went with a more detailed 3D style like how Rash appeared in Killer Instinct as that matches the feel of the rockin' 90's Battletoads everyone knows more but the Saturday morning cartoon look works surprisingly well. The writing for the game complements the art direction and watching the cutscenes really feels like being a kid watching cartoons again. That is not to say that the writing is childish, it has plenty of enjoyable adult humor. It is also understandable when you consider they may not have wanted to go all in with some crazy 3D Battletoads game when they were just testing the waters with revitalizing a franchise that hasn't had a game in 20 years.I played through the entire game in full 3 player co-op with friends and we found ourselves laughing out loud quite a few times at the jokes or character decisions. Some other reviewers left negative reviews because of the lack of online play but that is a bit ridiculous when Steam Remote Play and Parsec exist in this day and age. Sure it kinda sucks but it is a minor inconvenience AT BEST and only 1 person has to buy the game anymore so what are you even complaining about? We also played through all the previous mainline Battletoads games to prepare for this one and the unanimous conclusion amongst my friend group was, "The Battletoads did not deserve a sequel this good."I may be biased because I was a big fan of the older Battletoads games and happy to see the franchise return but I think this game was really great. We beat the game in about 5 hours while playing on normal difficulty so it was a short but sweet experience. It was probably the best co-op experience I've had in a long time, which I'm thankful for considering the current state of the world, and it only cost me $20. Overall, I'd rate the game an 8/10.Bottom line is if you were a fan of the Battletoads and have nostalgia for them, are looking for a fun co-op experience, or have any interest in the Battletoads as characters(or at all really) then you should get this game. Show your support and maybe we can get that full 3D rockin' Battletoads game after all.P.S. Battletoads for Smash
