_childDocuments_.review: Battetoads in name only.  I'm a huge fan of the nes original, and this game is a disappointing followup.  I am glad it exists, and honestly, I'll throw money at any new battletoads game, but nonetheless, I'm disappointed.Ultimately, the game just doesn't seem to know it's audience.  It has no reverence to the source material, and on it's own, it's a fairly uninspired beatemup that pales in comparison to Castle Crashers.The game, in itself, isn't that terrible.  The style is beautiful, the animation is slick, and the gameplay is adequate - not great, but adequate.The problem is, it's a sequel to a 30 year old franchise.  Most of the design decisions look like they were made by someone who'd at best seen a poster of the original:-the original game had a variety of levels; nearly every one was unique in design and gameplay.  The new one is pretty much just a repetitive brawler beat-em up that lacks variety.  There's some minigames thrown in for sport, but most of them are annoying, unintuitive side quests that detract more than they add.  One of them is Rock Paper Scissors.  I'm not sure if that's lazy design, or just tone deaf?-what little plot was in the original was at least entertaining.   They traveled through space into some weird organic sort of world fighting the dark queen.  In this game, they've been locked away for 26 years, now escaping on a quest to be famous.  The dark queen joins them about a third of the way in.  Her originally cool, sorta goth, bombshell character is now reduced an annoying sideshow prissy idiot wannabe.-it's a beatemup, but instead of just button mashing, there are button combos that you have to learn in order to do certain things and beat certain characters.  I get what they're going for; this requires some strategy.  You have to decide which characters to fight first, and which to temporarily freeze by shooting bubble gum at them.  The problem is, it's just not that much fun.  A game like this, I just want to mash buttons and get through to the next thing to beat up, and this can be fairly joyless and frustrating.-the controls seem unnecessarily complicated, and somewhat nonsensical.  With your tongue, you can pick up flies, pull enemies toward you, and lasso yourself to other parts of the screen.  Each of these use a trigger button and a unique button, and sometimes require joystick to aim.  It can be frustrating to remember which combo is which.Similarly, the attack button combos are complicated, and hard to remember.  Again, just mashing buttons would honestly be more fun.  -the visuals are fantastic.  I'd opt for a different style, being a battletoads sequel, but I can forgive that.  The style is bright and colorful, the animation is pretty solid.  My only qualm is that it can be easy to lose your character.  There's often a lot going on, and the characters can get lost in the backgrounds sometimes.  A little better use of dark contrasting colors and outlines probably would have solved this.  Minor gripe, but still can be annoying.-The story is awful.  I play with my kid, and he's into it, but I'd skip cutscenes if he'd let me.  On that note, the game seems like it was designed for a toddler youtube generation.  Again, I'm not opposed to that, but fans of the originals are going to be in their 30's and 40's by now.  I'd have made it a little more racy, not as cartoony.  It's kinda cool to be able to play with your kids, like a Lego game, but then it's a little to complicated for them to control.  A couple hours in, my kid won't play anymore because we die too often and don't make progress.-I've read reviews praising the dialogue, but I find it pretty terrible.  There's bad puns, and then there's baaaad puns, and the jokes can be mildly amusing at best.  Mostly, they're stupid and out of character with what you'd expect.  The turtles all have different character types, but here, they're all three just kinda stupid, trying too hard to make jokes that don't land.-the controls for the toads each behave a little differently.  It's sorta cool to have different play styles, but the end result is you just bash enemies differently. The devs obviously put some effort in to make the game more than just a beatemup, requiring strategy, and adding minigames and side quests.  Big swing and a miss here - they naturally could have incorporated more  strategy and gameplay in by giving them unique abilities.  Say one could unlock electronic locks, one could jump higher to access platforms, one could sneak, etc, etc.  Instead, it's just kinda monotonous, joyless repetition.  Glad to have a new toads game, just hoped it had more reverence to the source material, or would have expanded on the old without throwing it all away with a reboot that pales in comparison to other beat em ups.

_childDocuments_.review: Battletoads is a bit of a mixed bag. I really like the humor, the varied gameplay, the smooth animations and rocking music. Combat design has some cool tools to play around with (namely a version of Nero's arm from DMC4). But the game is held back by few very glaring issues:-There's a huge problem with readability of the action. There’s too many enemies on the screen, they have elaborate idle animations and they (and some of the projectiles) blend too well with the backgrounds. There were some fights I could only beat by constantly dashing around, fighting in the air and throwing one or two punches at a time, because I just couldn't follow the action. Human eye can track only 5-7 objects at the time, and the more erratically they move, the harder it gets to track them. This is some game design rules 101, they are there for a reason. -Hiboxes and hurtboxes are reaaaaaaly terrible. There were so many times when I was sure that the enemy attack was nowhere near me and still got hurt. If I had to guess, Id's say they are either too rigid, and go outside the character sprites in some of the animations instead of scaling back if necessary, or they are too precise (it's a rule of thumb to make character hitboxes a bit smaller than their models/sprites, it just feels better). And enemies should really telegraph when they are dangerous better, maybe highlight them in red/white or something, their idle animations are so bouncy that attack animations don’t stand out enough. -The difficult ramps up too much. What I mean by that, is the last 10% of most stages is just too hard. I'm a competent gamer, and I like hard games. But when I'm clearing stages/bosses with 0 hits until the last 10%, when suddenly I die a dozen times, it gets frustrating. Especially in the platforming and bullet hell sections, first of which I had to memories, because margin for error was too small, second of which I just had to get lucky to pass, because there were soo many moving objects with too little room to maneuver for comfort. It really sucks, because most of the stages felt fantastic at first, but got frustrating because of those unreasonably hard sections at the end. All in all, it’s a fun game. It’s just frustrating, because it’s so close to being great.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game with high hopes and I wish I could say I enjoy it. It's terrible. It tries to be funny, it doesn't know what type of game it wants to be. It's absolute garbage. They should have just given us RARE replay, with arcade battletoads and classic BT. I have gotten as far as where you ride the dead guy down the hill-but I absolutely detest just about every element of this game. Some genius thought it would be a fantastic idea to put a speed bike level on the THIRD stage-if you can forgive the crappy controls and mechanics-you might actually find something about this game to enjoy. The controls, however-are like a wet noodle in a wind tunnel. Than there are the stupid mini games like the Olympics or going to work and don't forget: about the security puzzles, which are timed. I wish I hadn't purchased this. I'd rather have my eyelids forced open and have to watch the 90's Battletoads cartoon pilot then be subjected to anymore of this crap. _childDocuments_.review: Possibly the best hybrid brawler-racing-puzzle platformer-bullet hell-side scroller game on the market right now.Pros:-Caters to nostalgia with a lot of in game references to the original.  Only old school players will understand the ending.-Old school Battletoads challenge is still there, but HIGHLY mitigated by an infinite life + checkpoint system.- Various game modes for different levels, so you wont get bored from just punching things. - Co op can be done on steam for PC players with remote playCons:  -No built in on line co-op.  Steam remote play or couch co-op only.- Some may not like the vastly different game modes for levels. (It does tend to kill the tempo of the game).- Quick time events vary from quirky to annoying.  Full QTE levels vary from irritating to infuriating and need to be KILLED WITH FIRE. (Whoever designed the ship maintenance level should be fired immediately.  Imagine a timed chain of quick time events of varying difficulty and time to complete chosen from a random pool of events, and having to figure out which qte you are playing by matching the symbol from a group of 12 on the screen at once.  Then imagine having to start over if you run out of time getting a new random selection.  Since some of these take more time than others and they are of varying difficulty AND you are graded by how fast you complete them, this level is more luck than anything.)-My childhood has been ruined by the removal of the Dark Queens "assets".

_childDocuments_.review: While the gameplay and art style have definitely been changed, you still get some nostalgic kicks out of it. It's honestly pretty funny. _childDocuments_.name: Battletoads

_childDocuments_.review: I beat the game on toad (normal) difficulty. Man, what a great arcade experience this was! The game as a whole is very challenging and at select few times quite hard, but it always feels motivating to keep playing with satisfying gameplay, great music, and a fun presentation.In most beat-em-up games, the goal is to walk up to an enemy and punch them till they fall. This game has a diverse cast of enemies that make for challenging encounters when multiple types work in tandem with another. The enemies aren't defeated when they lose all their health; they have to be put into a special stunned state and then be blown away by a powerful attack. Combat is very engaging and satisfying! And it helps that the toads have great attack animations. It's morphin' time.But on top of this fun beat-em-up, we get tons of different minigames. There's quite the variety of them, and they are very fun and, honestly, quite humourous. You'll have to see for yourself. There are the funny minigames, but then there are also the ones that require a bit of effort like the turbo bikes and the space ship. These two are also incredibly fun and involved.This was a simple review for a simple game. I definitely recommend it. I actually played it solo. I am very interested in playing multiplayer using Steam remote play. Also, RELEASE THE SOUNDTRACK PLEASE.

_childDocuments_.review: The Battletoads are Back. Rash, Zitz and Pimple are returning at last to Morph Attack their way through an all-new action-packed adventure of choreographed chaos, and couch co-op may never be the same again. 1-3 players take control of the Battletoads and team up to storm through wild and unpredictable stages with only one rule expect the unexpected. Teamwork makes the dream work in a drop-in, drop-out gameplay blast, filled with over-the-top combat that anyone can enjoy, but only a True 'Toad can master. With a unique hand-animated cartoon style and packed with memorable characters and locations, the Battletoads are back for a larger-than-life brawl across the universe that promises to be fun alone, and unforgettable together.

name: Roots of Pacha
detailed_description: Fall in love with Roots of Pacha, where every moment is a pleasant surprise! Roots of Pacha offers a relaxed and fresh take on the classic farming sim genre. Set in an ancient era, you’ll gather, farm, and explore the enchanting world of Pacha. Befriend animals, craft tools, and customize your character, home, and farm. Expand your village while forging deep community bonds. Thrive and evolve together with your clan through the seasons, and shape your own story at a calm and peaceful pace. Meet your Clan, delve into the biomes, and discover charming surprises wherever you go. From new flora and fauna to mini-games and cave mysteries. Unearth a long-forgotten world. ‎‎‎‏‏‎ Manage crops, gather resources, fish, and discover ways to process and preserve food. Domesticate and breed animals either for goods or as cute pets. Develop tools, items, and buildings to shape your society. ‎‎‎‏‏ You are not alone in Roots of Pacha, strength comes through cooperation. Contribute to your Clan to progress as new ideas arise and see your village grow. Play single-player or co-op with friends. ‎‎‎‏‏‎ Attend festivals and develop friendships, tame your dream pet, and find that special one to start a family with. Customize your character, home and farm to tell your unique story. ‎‎‎‏‏‎‏‎ Make your way at your own pace; the world of Roots of Pacha is a relaxing haven to explore and play in peace. There is no need to rush, as all ideas and prophecies can be completed in any season.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely breathtaking, "Roots of Pacha" delivers a charmingly captivating experience that manages to transcend the genre of life and farming simulators. Set in the dawn of civilization, the game presents a wonderfully vibrant world that feels alive, brimming with exciting potential at every nook and cranny. The characters are charming, quirky, and wonderfully fleshed out, injecting a sense of vitality and depth into the player's interactions. Its unique take on farming, where you gradually learn and progress from simple stick and stone tools to the dawn of agriculture, is incredibly rewarding and paves the way for a palpable sense of progression. The crafting system is intuitive and satisfying, while the environment is meticulously designed, striking a beautiful balance between realism and artistic style. The creators have also poured heart into the intricacies of their game mechanics, ensuring that every action has a meaningful impact on the game world. "Roots of Pacha" isn't just a game, it's an exploration into the birth of human ingenuity and community, a deeply immersive experience that deserves to be savored.

_childDocuments_.review: Please keep in mind I played this game as it was originally released. Over time modifications might be included by the developers which may make parts of this review obsolete.My overall impression is that it's all rather tedious.As you all know by know, this game is a Stardew clone. And there is a mountain to climb when one aims to follow in ConcernedApe's footsteps.Pacha copies a lot of the mechanics but everything taken into consideration, it just isn't that much fun.You start the game as a member of a displaced gang which relocates on an island between two rivers, bit like old Paris. Even though you're just adopted by an elderly couple, you somehow have half of the island at your disposal, the other half will be gradually cluttered by the rest of the tribe with mostly useless constructions.The first year ingame is like a permanent race to get the necessary contribution points to be able to release building which will allow you to improve your yield in other fields of activity.  You can exchange stuff for extra contribution but you also need those resources to execute upgrades or to give to other npcs to improve their friendship level. Npcs participate to the overall contribution so you yourself don't really need to: the tally will raise by itself over time. Which is part of the reason I never really could get to care about the others characters in the game at all.Eventually you will be able to build your own hut and move out of your granpas, but I am still not sure why I bothered. Sure you can have a pet when you do and it can follow you around, but that's a rather meager bonus. And if you place your newly acquired house in an inconvenient site, you can't move it anymore at a later stage. I did, unfortunately, so now I'm married, have a stage-3 villa with 3 pets (no pool) and still live with the granpas cause it's closer to my fields and I don't want to waste 1 hour of the day just running from one part of the island to the other just for the sake of it (tip: place your house and Acre's toolshop as close as possible to Field2, don't bother with the other buildings).The higher the contribution level, the more ideas are freed up in the game, the more you progress. If you manage to keep up with the insane rythm, by the time year 2 starts there will be nothing much left to do. The only thing that makes me go for another 4 seasons is the will to get all the achievements, which is not a very good reason anyways. You get the watermill and irrigation rather late in the game, but those will allow you to up your production rate from a wee peasant to a more organised farmer. If you managed to hoard enough hardwood that is. One third of the island, up north, looks covered with hardwood trees, but the whole area is off limit for some reason. So hardwood becomes a painfully limiting factor to your development.And then there are a number of time wasting features that really put a drag on it all. I read earlier a claim by the developers that there is a lot of content, but not all of it adds to the game. For instance, why does every farming item come with 5 degrees of quality: wild tomatoes, tomatoes, good tomatoes, better tomatoes, best tomatoes, who cares?Plus, who needs all these tools? I feel I am constantly hitting the E key to rotate between the can, the flute, the hoe and all the other tools. And beware if you enter a field with your axe selected: I lost track of the number of plants I chopped up unwillingly.The fishing mini-game is another of my eye sorrows: start it using your harpoon in a puddle, minigame pops up on the screen, wait for it, hit the fish, minigame closes. Rinse and repeat if you would like to fish a second one. And as dry fish is one of the main sources of contribution the first year, fishing for 12 fishes a day feels like going to work irl.And don't get me started of the caves map, which looks like it comes straight from a 1980's game of D&D.All by all, this games feels to me like the developers had plenty of ideas, implemented them, tried them out once or twice to make sure the code worked, and then moved on to the next item, but did not take the time to check how it all turned out in the long run.In it's current state, I guess this game will get you busy for about 50h, and another 50h if you are going for the full achievement shebang. But that's rather light compared to the original Stardew this game wants to emulate.Plus, it's expensive. So if you haven't already, buy yourself Stardew Valley instead.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is such a breath of fresh air in the farming sim genre. It brings a sense of discovery that fits so well with the setting: A lot of tech needs to be invented by you and your people first because it doesn't exist yet. I'm always curious to see what kind of ideas the community comes up with :)These are some aspects I think this game brings to the table that make it stand out among others of its genre:* Discovering crops in the wild makes it fun to explore the lands (later you can buy seeds)* Befriending & taming wild animals (later breeding to improve traits)* Clan mates play an active role in advancing the settlement* Puzzles to advance in the mines instead of aimlessly digging for stairs* Unique and gorgeous festivals* NPC dialogue is quite diverse (I like talking to everyone daily and it took quite a while for dialogue to repeat; also they react to accomplishments, relationship advancements, and more)* NPCs actually use new infrastructure (I'm looking at you, community center in SDV), which is a minor but lovely touch that motivates to advance the settlement* Somewhat novel currency & trading system (there is no money in the game and some items you only get through trading)* Baby mammothIn other farming games, I feel the need to industrialize the farm for profit and efficiency. But in Roots of Pacha, I really enjoy a much slower farming life, with some days dedicated to foraging, fishing, mining, or cooking up a storm with all the produce I'm hoarding. Still, you can go for the "big-scale-farm" if you prefer.Overall, I'm eager to see where this game is headed (some features & locations shown on Kickstarter are yet to be implemented) but I can recommend this game even at this current state to anyone who is a lover of farming sims.

_childDocuments_.review: Played it both solo and then with a couple friends. I'm huge on the farming sim genre, long before Stardew I was a Harvest Moon kid and I don't think a year's gone by where I haven't tried out a new game in the genre (to varying results). Having said all that, I really enjoyed this game! It does enough to stand out while also staying familiar, simple, and addictive.The game's primary unique focus is on that of the community. Everything you do in the game not only contributes to your own personal income but also to the tribe as a whole. You'll be taking smoke signals (quests) from NPCs regularly to brainstorm up new technologies to increase your productivity. When you earn contribution (money) in this game it gets added to a pool (you still get to keep your currency for spending) that boosts the rate of the tribe upgrading the village with new features and structures over time. It's a lovely feature that feeds into itself well and kept me motivated while I played.The farming itself is satisfying with nice QoL features to keep it from getting tedious. Day-to-day farming isn't much different from other farming games. Till, plant, water daily, harvest, ship. You have limited stamina to begin with but as you advance you will receive better tools from advancing in the mines to reduce the time spent on each task, upgrades to your stamina bar, access to recipes to refill the stamina bar, and even technologies to automate processes. As you continuously harvest crops your knowledge of them will increase and they will become domesticated which blew my mind. Seeds are taken from the wild and are stored in a separate inventory and never take up space in your bag which is so nice when you're a gremlin hoarder like me. I should mention though, that while some processes can be automated to save time in the late game you will never have full automation since this is the stone age and all. This is especially true of processing which is your main money maker.Animals are from the wild and can be bred to increase their productivity and speed. Farm animals take themselves outside on days when it is not raining and feed on grown grass automatically, and all of them (save pets) can be mounted. They can be set free and found in the wild again (for a limited time) if you are running low on space, and a new feature allows you send them to the village hunter if you are in need of meat but it is entirely optional. All meat recipes in this game allow the use of plant meat as a substitute but animal meat can also be purchased from the village hunter or obtained from traps without sending your animals to him.In multiplayer your seed bags and contribution are shared between all players. At first the shared seed bag was a problem for us but since seeds can be purchased for cheap after a few weeks it became a non-issue after a month or so in-game. The same was true for contribution, where we had to communicate what we were buying and whose turn it was get their bag/house upgrades but it eventually became a non-issue as we were all making more money working together than a single person could anyway.Characters are good. Likable, with cutscenes that you progressively unlock as you befriend them that allow you to get to know them better. They're a nice touch and I'm glad they opted for this over only using character dialogue to indicate relationship progression, and some are very well written (I really enjoyed Jag's). Unfortunately the game's art style for its portraits is not for me but there are a few portrait mods out there as alternatives even if they're pretty limited. I also think that there could be more progressive character dialogue (it took over a month for my character's partner to give any kind of dating-specific dialogue instead of generic lines), as well as more dialogue from other npcs acknowledging your partner/family. Edit: My points about progressive dialogue being lacking might have been addressed as of 1.2, though I haven't checked myself yet!There's more I didn't really talk about such as the mines (fun, there are no enemies, can be a little stressful though) but I've typed a lot here already. Basically it's a really good game and I highly recommend it if you're looking for a solid farming sim. Multiplayer is excellent also if that's what you're looking for (and you can marry other players!). I hope to see more updates in the future that add even more content to the game's core systems, because they work really really well and I'll always take more of a good thing. :)

_childDocuments_.review: This is a wonderful new spin on the farming sim genre. The communal approach to gathering "currency" and upgrading the tribe/buildings is very refreshing - usually I'm very much a minmaxer, but here it feels like I can just relax and let go of the grind, as things progress naturally and there's not as much pressure to amass as much money as possible. The controls are smooth and I love the way the inventory and tools are divided up, makes for a very pleasant gameplay experience. I just wish there was a way to customize key bindings, I hope this is something that will be implemented in future updates. I find the minigames for fishing and taming animals quite innovative too, although they do get a bit repetetive at times, but with the game being so relaxed overall I don't mind skipping them entirely for a couple ingame days if I don't feel like it. I also like the building system - having preset locations for the buildings gives you just enough freedom without being overwhelmed by choice and wanting to have everything set up perfectly, as is the case with a lot of other farming sim games. And finally, the graphics are so pleasant to look at, especially the tilesets/maps feel very organic, and the character portraits are simply beautiful. The only issue I currently see with the game is that it might not be as intuitive for players not already familiar with the genre, as the mechanics for e.g. farming or foraging aren't really explained (it took me a while to figure out you could actually shake trees to get pinecones lol)Can't wait to explore the game in multiplayer, and hopefully see some mod support in the future!

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good prehistory-ish fantasy-ish Stardew Valley-like. The only real complaints I have are that the relationship with people can decline if you don't talk to them regularly, making it a huge chore if you want to keep it up with everyone, and that the spawning of rare animal variants is extremely obtuse and you pretty much require a guide to even know about how it works. _childDocuments_.review: This game is frustrating to play, with completely messed up controls.- Designed for controllers, so on keyboard/mouse you are getting a middle finger. Have an entirely empty quickbar? Here are 3 sets of radial buttons to tab through to slowly and painfully switch tools every 1-2 steps to try clear your land with mixed debris.- Overlaying interactions all condensed to a left click. Want to water your plants? Let me repeatedly open the animal menu for the animal touching the square. Want to harvest? Let me toss a water bucket, then another, and another. Want to actually pet the animal? Let me till and un-till the land behind him on loop. It's horrible.- Economy has no balance. Seed purchase costs as much as the produce grown from it over several days. Cooked food is worth a fraction (in some cases 1/6th) of the grown produce that went into it. The energy restored by the food is less than you wasted growing the damn thing to make the food. The best strategy is to just not grow stuff. Go fish, they are worth a fortune for a fraction of the energy and no daily maintenance needed.- You know how Stardew sprinkles a light amount of debris over your land on season change? This game does it daily. Floods of it. I'm getting like 30+ per day. It's not just grass, but also wood and rocks, like the whole village sleepwalks and throws crap on my land on purpose. I have nowhere near the energy to clear it.- 1.5 season in, I'm still manually watering everything. No sign of any irrigation upgrade. 75% of daily energy goes into basic watering.- Walking is painfully slow, even while mounted. I had to get a mod for walking speed to be able to do anything in the day.- Quick stashing to chests does not exist. You'll have a ton of small capacity chests to go through, manually depositing one item at a time. You can't drag drop it. You also can't just click on it. For some reason you have to do it in multiple steps.- Fishing in the pond shows outlines of all the fish. No matter your fishing experience, they all look identical until you have your mouse on them for a while to progress fishing. The problem is, the moment you mouse over 1 of them, the mouse hard snaps and won't let go for a long time so you can't quickly go through them all to find the fish you want. Again, all ruined by controller users who apparently can't follow the fish. There needs to be a toggle to disable the snapping.This game has not heard of QoL. They took the good features of similar games and tossed them out the window. Don't get me wrong, the game is pretty. It just plays horribly.

The music is lovely & playful.  It matches the vibe that is going for- a small, pre-industrial community making beats with simple, melodic instruments.  There is crafting, farming, foraging, fishing-all the things you would expect in a Harvest Moon-like game.  I love that this game has dancing and a lot more interaction with the animals (pets, taming,riding)  I am excited to see how the story develops between the different tribes and with the spiritual elements.  The game is both relaxing and exciting somehow, so I enjoy playing in the evening after work.  The graphics are nice, especially if you appreciate the aesthetic of games like The Survivalists and Stardew, which I really do.  And with the recent update, you can adjust the pacing of the day, which is wonderful, because my one complaint was that the day felt like it moved a little too quickly for me. _childDocuments_.review: I went into this game thinking it'd be a breezy simplified take on Stardew Valley.  What I found was a game with a wheelbarrow of fresh ideas within its genre and enough polished content to rival Stardew Valley at release.  Nothing in this game feels tacked on.  tldr; Roots of Pacha is very good.  Its a game that starts out small, but masterfully unveils itself to be one of the most well thought out games in it's genre.  + Ranching is a full discipline in it's own right with animal husbandry, stats, rarity in appearance, and racing.  + Cooking requires almost no investment to start, which lets it be a more important part of your play throughout the game.  It'll still take a lot of investment if you want to be able to do everything, but the flexibility means almost every recipe is worth keeping in mind, rather than just the 1-3 most powerful ones.+ Farming in this game has a completely different flow to other farming games.  You cannot buy seeds and there are no sprinklers.  You have to forage for seeds from wild crops each season, turning the first few days of each season into an almost easter egg hunt.  Later in the game you'll have other ways to water crops and get seeds, but their implementation is immaculately tied to your efforts from earlier years.  I have never played a farming game that made me so eager to find and plant as many of every plant my stamina can manage.+ Artisan goods can be made as well, and though mostly it's just a way to make crops worth more money, the different mechanics of each crafting station, and the existence of multi stage crafting systems for the most valuable types of artisan good is my new gold standard.+ Mining did not copy Stardew Valley's homework.  There isn't much I want to say about it other than appreciating that they didn't feel the need to add combat and monsters to it.  Mining with combat is fine, but without it they can focus on the exploration and puzzle solving aspect to it, which is a breath of fresh air.+/- Relationships are maybe the one area where I feel not enough is done.  Living in a close knit community like this I find it strange that there aren't more ways to feel connected to that community.  Seasonal festivals are nice, and I love the ability to invite people to dance (Though with how long the animation is, it's not really worth doing with someone you're not trying to romance), but something like occasional celebrations around the fire, or small birthday parties would give the wider cast more opportunity to show off their honestly excellent character writing.  Rainy/snowy days where almost everyone huddles up in a couple buildings feels like a gesture toward that, but still only serves as a chance to give a lot of gifts.  Child rearing is a welcome addition and feels like it has the care and attention of the team, but your spouse has the same dead end problem almost all games with this kind of system fall into.  - My one negative is that it's not clear how valuable buffs actually are.  They have a number associated, and a tooltip explaining what exactly each buff means, but not how the number is actually applied.  For walking speed it seems like its #% movement speed increase, which makes food that gives walking speed 1 feel more like a joke than an actual benefit.  For how short these buffs last, and with a buff that just increases how long other buffs last, it seems weird to me that they don't feel all that impactful.  The accessory system is a really interesting alternative to having just regular skill progression, and I wanted to believe it was worth investing the massive amounts of time and resources, changing them out as my goals shifted, but until the very end it was hard to see any real effect.

_childDocuments_.review: Solid farming sim. The systems for seeds and upgrades are innovative and an improvement over other games in the genre.  Instead of buying seeds from a merchant (which in other games would force you to focus exclusively on profit for early growth), you forage to find seeds and then plant them in your farm. This gives the game a relaxed pace.Instead of having to grind skill or donate random bundles of items to unlock new content, your clan members will occasionally let you know that they are working on a discovery and you can donate related items to make this happen. (The builder will ask for construction materials, the herbalist will ask for herbs, etc.)The setting is more vibrant and interesting than the description suggests. If you are looking for a slightly alternative take on the farming sim genre, then this would be a very good pick.

Now, I don't know exactly the other sorts of games the devs worked on. With the comment on being part of the family friendly bundle, I'm going to take a gander they're extremely nonviolence.For a game about cavemen and tribals, this makes no sense. I wanted to hunt the mammoths. Have real adventures and such. Have a reason to transverse the map other than occasionally needing an item that spawns in the EXACT SAME LOCATION each time.The village even has a hunter so it makes even less sense.Yes, it's a farming sim. But that feels really sidelined and time consuming. IF they hadn't released the update to change the clock, this game would not be worth touching. The village growing means they've decided to carefully lock off areas, meaning you can't place crops wherever which means that placement of player house is redundant.The game is extremely handholdy for the first in game week. It's annoying and made a friend I pointed this game out to- before release- put it down. They also bought it due to the exact imagery of Stardew. If the caves hadn't had so much effort put into them, there wouldn't be much dynamic to keep longterm interest. They take too long to pick up even then. There's a point where all your doing is waiting on things for the cave.The npcs just aren't as interesting as they could be. They grew on me, but I really struggled to remember their name until one of their cutscenes eventually put something of note to attach it to. Again, without the clock enhancement you'd pick either farming, caving, or getting to know them. I think being more true to the era attempted would have given them all a more interesting backstory.-also, only romanceable people have cutscenes.edit- The biggest problem I had with it was optimization. They released patches to better this, but it's still not really smooth butter. -end editPROSNow, there is clearly a lot of work put into the game and some love. The player's children are very cute, and interactable.  There's a nanny system, good feel to actually being a part of a tribal family, farm animals are actually useful (tho there are still more upgrades that could be done here), and much more. TONS of unique dialog- tho everyday dialog does cycle a bit much eventually it's still more than other games put effort into.Farming is dynamic.They're trying new things, playing around with some mechanics both of which are good.Ultimately, if this was a game for children it would absolutely feel like a 1.0 release. As it stands, still seems like they're finishing up and it seems it'll take another year to feel complete.It has charm. It does not have the entirely strategic, near perfect formulae of Stardew level of charm.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Stardew, but every other "clone" has fell short for you... this is FINALLY the game for you. _childDocuments_.review: first of all: I would give this game a mixed review if i couldIts basically Stone-Era Stardew Valley. It plays like stardew valley, feels like stardew valley, and in its core is propably heavily inspired by it. It does have some QoL Features over SV however, like a Map that shows you where people are (unless you modded SV which you definitely should)My main gripe is that the pacing cant keep up with the content. After 25-30 hours you have seen everything the game has to offer gameplay-wise. However, there's still new stuff coming that you have to do in order to progress the story. That leads to a gameplayloop where you wake up, tend to your farm and animals and if theres nothing to do at that day, go back to bed. While i enjoy the minigames this game offers, the puzzles in the dungeon (especially the last one) are absolutely dreadful. Which is a shame, because the dungeon puts SDVs Mine to shame. But those puzzles completely destroyed the pacing at which one was going for 5-20 Minutes, depending on the puzzle. What i enjoyed most, was how new stuff was developed. Unlike other Farming Sims, where you just get new recipes, in this game your village has an idea and you provide them with materials so they can turn it into reality. Its a nice take on the Farming-Sims Idea, especially since it adds realism to the stone-age setting.Last but not least i would have liked some automation-features towards the lategame. I havent finished the game yet, but i cant see them coming tbh. And even if they came, with the problem mentioned earlier, it would lead to the players having even less to do. So in addition, i would like more content in upcoming updates (if there are any coming)Overall i give the game a solid 7/10. It's a nice take on the farming-sim formula, it does it a lot better than other games and its perfect if you want to play a relaxing kind of farming sim.Also, other game devs, take note: Farming sims dont need some kind of ♥♥♥♥♥♥ combat system to be playable

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun and everything I've been looking for in the post-Stardew world. You can tell that great care and thought was given in the production of this game! The creators also thought outside of the box, so to speak, and have presented a great work of art!I love that Roots of Pacha takes place in a different era, where you work as a community to advance everyone's knowledge and make life easier to live. Advancement depends on your contributions (donating goods) and other discoveries in the game over different seasons, making this game a go at your own pace, truly relaxing adventure that never seems confusing or overwhelming and will surely put you in a good mood. You will like this game if you like customizing your environment like your character and their clothing, the location of your home as well as upgrading and decorating it, the location of all other amenities, deciding how to use your garden/animal space (there's a LOT of space!) and I'm sure there's more I haven't even discovered yet after 19 hours of playing. There are many characters to get to know and eventually marry if that is what you wish to do. While this game does have similar elements to other games in this genre, I must say that the thing I like the most about this game so far is that fishing is actually relaxing! I play with a keyboard and mouse, so I am not sure how the controller experience is, but I am so happy that fishing won't make me want to rage quit in my pursuit of perfection and steam awards!Overall, I think this game is absolutely worth the buy. It is a perfect example of what this genre can be and what it can do to advance this cozy/farming/life genre. CHEERS!

_childDocuments_.review: The following review is strictly about the single player mode of Roots of Pacha.This farming sim set from the stone age to the bronze age has a lot of features that make it stand out:+ A real sense of community, as everyone contributes to the clan. You get a real sense that your tribe is advancing across the ages, as they actively improve their village with a lot of projects.+ The locations of NPCs and your mount can be tracked on the map.+ The in-game journal mentions who each NPC is, what they do and the relationships with other NPCs.+ No combat. Instead, cave levels have fun puzzles to solve.+ A lot of fun minigames at the festivals.+ The fishing minigame is much easier and much less annoying than that in Stardew Valley.+ Farm animals are obtained by finding them in the wild and playing your flute for them.+ You can breed farm animals to make them more productive and move faster.+ The real-time length of in-game days can be made longer if you find it too hectic.+ Child rearing is a bit more involved.However, there are a few annoyances and problems with the game:- In game menus are not very responsive; stutters occur when you move around too quickly.- Unlike Stardew Valley, you can't hold down left mouse button to pet all animals in a shed or put a bunch of stuff into processors. You have to left click each time for these actions.- Opening the in-game menu pauses the game in single player; however, NPCs don't stop moving.Overall, this is a unique and fun take on the farming sim genre.

_childDocuments_.review: In most regards, Roots of Pacha is a highly functional but closely matched Stardew Valley clone, set in the Stone Age. If you're burned out on Stardew, Roots of Pacha will recharge your battery for a play-through or two, but the field-clearing, crop-raising, villager-courting, fish-catching rhythms are remarkably similar. The lack of any sort of monster slaying / loot mechanic also makes the game feel a little bit flatter than Stardew by comparison.That said, Roots of Pacha has plenty of its own charm. The graphics are lively and colorful, the music cheerful, the farming system effective and elegant, and there are some unique twists - my favorite might well be irrigation, which lets you build a customized system to flood your fields each morning to save you the back-breaking work of hauling around a bucket of water. Also new and entertaining is your ability to sally forth into the world and use your flute to charm various animals as pets or producers of milk / fur / eggs / etc.  Gathering wild seeds is also a step beyond Stardew, and there's something satisfying about putting together a field from scratch without have to spend on seeds.Characters in Pacha are skillfully illustrated, but their personalities and arcs tend toward the generic - Stardew managed to make all of its villagers feel like three-dimensional people, while the clanspeople of Pacha also seem sort of generally cheerful without much backstory or personal complexity. That Pacha falls short of Stardew Valley isn't anything to be ashamed of - Stardew is a remarkably deep and well-developed game, and Pacha is relatively new. It's generally a joy to play, and with the lack of even monster-induced unconsciousness to worry about, it's even easier going than the game that inspired it. It's a charming game and well worth the asking price.

_childDocuments_.review: disregard the 14 hours. i play mostly offline and steam doesn't count that.. got the game Dec 30th completed the last 2 achievements on January 25th ( summer of year 3 in game). triggers that might make it upsetting to some are same gender partners (two females married in game), the ability to date all dateable npc's even if married (once the friendship gets high enough they will ask you to date them even if you're married), idol worship (well tree and totems), to have a child you ask a idol thingy in your upgraded home.other than that it's mostly repetition. there's the starting area, a small beach area, a path through a forest area, a large Savannah that's mostly grass, and a cave system (best part) that has hidden locations/secrets as well as puzzles that must be completed to continue farther in. the last in game location is the jungle but not much there til late game and even then there's not much.you can decorate your home with items bought with contribution points from a npc. fishing mini game is different then any other game i've tried before. items have 4 different qualities normal, good, better, best. there's no combat in game, animals are tamed by playing a flute to them for a few days (varies by animal type). there's 7 normal colors, 2 rares, and a legendary color. there's also pet animals but other than the cuteness of them when you pet them, they just get in your way around you home/garden. you can send a tamed animal off to be butchered by Grob one a day or release unwanted ones back into the wild. each type of animal gives an item every couple days (3 - 9 i believe it was). you can breed a male and female animal of the same type to make a baby animal that will have slightly increased stats (stats being - quality of harvest item, time until next harvest, and mount speed). there are 2 races each season that you can enter. there are events every season. there's a few npc's you only see during events sadly you can't do anything with them other than speak to them during the event. which include two of the more attractive npcs which aren't dateable. items give more contribution when crafted up, hair to yarn, fruits and some veggies to juice then wine and so on. cooking food does not give more contribution. other than the cook all types of food achievement, only make food for energy refills/boosts.

_childDocuments_.review: I Tried to like it but found the pacing too dull. Just lots of busywork and overwhelming amount of chores without enough agency or creative freedom. Preferred stardew and even starbound by comparison. Other Notes:- Pacha forces you to engage with the various NPCs more than stardew but none of them struck me as particularily interesting.- Multiplayer suffers from pacing issues, such as needing to gather all players in one spot for any sort of minor event or story progression.  - Even with three of us playing it often felt like a bit too much busywork to unlock most things.- The days are fairly short and you spend most of them walking around to reach distant work sites so you can smash rocks all day, rinse and repeat.- The cave quests are terribly boring, you need to smash rooms full of rocks before the door will open and allow you to progress. It takes a long time to reach the place you left off and you drain stamina super fast. You practically need to have one player dedicated to mining the caves while the others supply that person with food to keep their stamina up. When you finally find a place of interest, all other players need to drop everything in order to progress past a cutscene or puzzle in order to continue. _childDocuments_.review: Yes. Just... yes. This game delivers on the tried-and-tested recipe set in stone by games such as Harvest Moon, developed on further by games like Stardew Valley, and further expands upon this recipe to create a genuinely amazing experience.The world is set up beautifully. A new, budding tribe's development in new, strange lands. Tribes, each with their own twists of culture, traditions, and philosophies working together. A plethora of colourful individuals, each with their own stories to tell. A very healthy mix of activities to fill the day with, and a marvellously set up research tree that slowly gives you more and more to play with, to further boost your contribution to the tribe's growth and well-being.There is no combat in the game. And I am glad for this. While I did definitely enjoy it in Stardew, I don't think much is lost by taking it out of the cocktail - a cocktail that already is very rich and detailed in its texture. Resource gathering is largely done in the overworld, and a series of caves. The caves themselves are a pleasant, if not at times welcome, alternative to the already busy days you'll be playing through. They come with their own little challenges, and a series of in-game 'puzzles' and tests that grant you additional utility to further delve into the unknowns of the cave system.It features mounts, pets, husbandry, butchery, and fishing, helping establish the atmosphere of this tribe: One who lives alongside nature, who benefits from the boons of mother nature, praises Her in reverence. It just adds a little bit of flavour, and it fits the theme perfectly.Can't recommend this game enough. Its coop functionality is also splendid. It's very easy to play solo or multiplayer, without even needing to have you set up a new world/save file to switch between the two styles of play.  What more to ask in a game like this - I am, honestly, not sure. I haven't checked too deeply in further plans, though with them having continued support and adding new features, I can only see this game reaching an even higher state of greatness.TLDR; Beautiful, wholesame, enjoyable farm-sim with a great focus on building up not as a lone farmer, but a whole tribe, a whole community and the nature around you. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Prehistoric Stardew Valley with a bunch of quality of life features like:- Separate slots for your tools and seeds which are always available - Ability to simply un-till the earth by clicking it again- Ability to just pick up and relocate any furniture/workstation without expending any stamina or using a specific tool - No stamina expended when accidentally swinging your tool at nothing, it's only used if you actually mine/harvest/water something with itThere is also so much to do in this game:- Animal farming & husbandry- Crop farming- Brewing - Cooking- Mining- Fishing- Romance- Friendship- FestivalsAnd so many different areas too. There's the village, a beach, a forest, a jungle, a savanna, the mines (which has several different areas that you unlock through puzzles). And they each have their own background music.A very fun game I would recommend if you like Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I can feel that the devs cared a lot about this game.Mechanically the game plays a lot like your typical farming sim, that said it also integrates and sometimes even expands a lot of mechanics that got introduced in the genre. _childDocuments_.review: People are calling this a prehistoric Stardew Valley, but I don't think that is accurate or fair. The similarities are clear: farming sim, fishing, crafting, mining, socializing. But this game combines those things with a civilization tech tree mechanic that distinguishes it from other farming sims. It also makes extensive use of original mini-games to accomplish things like taming animals, catching fish (no rods), and exploring the mines. There are other unique mechanics/problems that promise to make for some very interesting game play. One of the things I have enjoyed so far is the quest system; you often work with others to accomplish a quest, and they make strong contributions.All in all, so far, I really like this game, and would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a must play if - you suffer from insomnia. I'm a fan of farming sims but boy this game is one of the most boring out of all the ones I've played. The only good thing I love about this game is the fantastic controller support. The seeds, tools and inventory mechanics are very well designed which makes swapping stuff seamless and quick. This is indeed a commendable feature that beats not just Stardew, but most farming sims by a mile. Now the points that put me to sleep, literally:- Graphic and animation are revolting. I don't mind pixel or retro artstyle but somehow I cannot vibe with this game. Everything just felt.. off. NPC sprites are uncanny; animal sprites looks like deformed abominations from lab experiments; walking animation are just.. weird.- BGM are garbage. Literally the same few notes on loop. Add this on top of the monotonous gameplay, snoozefest!- The quests designs are extremely repetitive and dull - go talk to this NPC > gather something > talk to that NPC again > wait a few days > tada you have achieve something! At first I thought yeah perhaps this's some tutorial stuff. Nope. 3 hours into the game and I am getting hit with the same quest pattern every single day.- The mini games are interesting for the first 5 seconds, thereafter they become a chore. Fishing, attuning with animals etc probably will be fun for a kid's standard. - NPCs are incredibly monotonous and one dimensions. The only reason I talk to NPCs is because I want to progress the stupid storyline, not because I give a crap on their background stories or personalities. For some reason I find them really unlikable and I wish that there is a mod to let me burn down the village along with whoever the hell is Pacha.Conclusion:- Roots of Pacha isn't completely a bad game. I would have given a thumbs up if it doesn't try to put me to sleep every single time I pick up my controller. - Despite that, I tried to love the game but to no avail. Everything about this game just seems so bland. I would probably have more fun talking to a wall than to bore myself to death with Roots of Pacha.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fine Stardew Valley clone, but it isn't and never will be a Stardew Valley replacement. Like, that's the nicest thing I can say about it. Play this is you have extracted every bit of fun out of Stardew Valley that you possibly can, otherwise, just play Stardew Valley. It is functionally the same videogame just a little bit worse.Pacha has the same problem that a few SV clones have for whatever reason (Graveyard Keeper is the biggest offender), in that it introduces its own form of gating on top of SV's resource gates. You can't just get a bigger watering can with your resources or money, you need to wait until a villager gets the idea for a bigger watering can then use your resources or money to buy it. And this happens.... idk, whenever Pacha feels like it :)Most progression paths have this gate. It only exists to punish players who have their ♥♥♥♥ together.Also, annoyingly for a time management game, the punishment for staying out all night is laughably lax. You get a little less stamina the next day, which you can just recover by eating a sandwich. Why manage my time at all if a single food item renders an entire mechanic pointless lol. Also, please make the NPC's stop walking when the game is paused. Not only is that exploitable, but it is really, really annoying that I need to get up from my computer and the NPC I was right next to has just walked off into a totally different map square.Yes, I'm going to keep playing it, but only because as mentioned above, I have already sucked all the fun out of Stardew Valley lol.

_childDocuments_.review: What really, really sold me was hearing the height of "Sun" from the soundtrack for the first time, in the trailer. _childDocuments_.review: Short version: Stardew Valley if it took place in the Stone / Early Bronze Age. Long version: Yeah pretty much like Stardew, but instead of the big bad being some corporation, it's just trying to uncover and resolve a wrong that was done some time ago. You learn the land, befriend and care for your livestock, contribute to your clan so they in turn build the things you need, make friends with the villagers and other clans, raise a family, uncover the secrets of the caves, and progress the clan's knowledge & technology. There's also a dash of collecting things. Seeds, fish, fruit trees, even the animals and their rarer variants. (Tip: Grandpa Igrork operates a seed shop once the relevant idea is complete. When you buy out his seed stock, he'll restock the next day and have roughly double that seed available than the day before. You just have to find the first seeds in the wild. ) The game is very peaceful and relaxing, especially when you can change the day length to the maximum of 20 minutes. There's no combat or direct hunting, but you can set traps in a specific location or send off your animals in exchange for meat. There are also alternate ways of getting "meat", such as using beans. You can also make Almond or Coconut milk, and by extension, their respective cheeses. I didn't even know those were things irl, but apparently they are! Now, for some reason, some people are having a hissy fit about "how dare you put in vegan options?1?!" and the rest of us are like.. dude.. People are gonna look for the best ways to use the resources they have. Like if someone grinds up some beans, cooks em, and goes "wow, this kinda tastes like meat," don't you think they'd use it as a substitute when meat gets scarce? It's not about veganism, it's about utilizing your limited resources in a clever manner. And, ya know, relaxing in a damn video game.

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is one of the “just one more day” and 10 days pass in game and it’s going to be hard getting up for work tomorrow. it take lots of the good things form the farm sim games, add some new flavors and we end up with a relaxing beautiful game, as of this om over 65h and are in year 2 fall. Just being a part of the clan and help with building up the village, expand you farmland, explore the lands and find new seeds, tame animals to bring home. All of this add a good atmospheric game. Like the ide system when clan help with new discovers, I just wish it was more of them spread out over a longer time. Animals can be improved over generations, to get faster products and better quality. Fishing is a nice mini game for ones. Join the festivals with competitions and races, cook some food for stamina, and upgrade accessories for helpful stats boosts like more wood or faster grow speed, but it’s a bit confusing how helpful they are, + 7 wood yield what dos it men… Experimenting timeLearn to know the people and find a partner have kid or just hide in the mines it’s all up to youIt’s a slow expanding in the start but after you unlock new things it can be large scale, spend less time tending to farm and try to unlock the puzzles or just enjoy the story.I did kickstart this game and happy that it turned out this goodNow I have to stop here, for my clan needs me. _childDocuments_.review: Fun, addictive and relaxing game! Imbued with gorgeous art and music. If you are familiar with pixelated farming sims then it should come as no surprise that you will find yourself farming, mining, fishing, crafting and so on. A big difference here is that the game takes you waaay back in time. You know back in the day when we made fire with sticks and stones :> And it is super fun! Compared to other similar games such as "Stardew Valley" I do like how "Roots of Pacha" puts even greater focus on community. You are not just building yourself a fabulous farm, but you are also actively helping your tribe to grow and flourish! Which really shows as you progress through the game. The whole village feels alive, and I like that. There is however no combat. Which is totally fine for me and for this game I actually welcome the abscence of it. There is so much else to do and so many goals to work towards... And it does take time and effort, which I really appreciate.With that said you should of course expect a lot of "rinse and repeat" which is quite usual when it comes to these type of games. But I do feel there is a good enough variety of things to do so that it doesn't become too boring. And who knows what the future holds. Judging from the official roadmap, there is more content planned and with that comes also a great opportunity to further improve and polish this gem. A big thumbs up from me! ^.^

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a gem for the price and finally a life sim that's complete at launch!Pros (compared to similar titles)- animal breeding is rewarded- Unique animals and pets- good pacing/ gradually unlock upgrades and features- Fun and unique prehistoric aesthetic- NPCs actually contribute to the story progression- Fishing mini game that isn't annoying- Puzzle solving instead of combat- Solid character customization- You can chose to concentrate in farming, animal raising, or fishing without being punished by the game- Festival mini games are fun- Very few bugsNegatives- NPC dialogue/ interactions could be better- NPC friendship difficult to earn- Takes a while to get decent farming tools- No sense of urgency to "completing" the game- Festival rewards aren't great- Text is a bit small- Soundtrack is okay but could be better imo
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is my current ADHD hyperfixation dopamine fix. If you're a chronic game hopper like me and you're looking for something new with that old nostalgic cozy farming sim lay out, this is amazing. It also has themes of unity and togetherness, and working together in small communities that touch my heart in this current existence we've all been facing.Playing co-op I expected bugs, as many other games have had, but have not run into any that I can tell. So far, 16 hours of gameplay since it released 2 days ago... And they've been very quick with patches and patch notes!  Yay! And yes it is similar to other farming sims (because its the same genre?) but it has some unique mini-games and features that make it novel and interesting. I think it stands out among other popular farm/cozy games as its own unique play experience without confusing players by removing some of the staple features of the genre.It's worth noting that fishing (a common point of contention for many fans in these game styles) in Roots of Pacha has a unique twist and a mini-game for fish catching that's actually kind of peaceful (provided you're not racing the clock). There's also animal taming with on-beat minigames, races, puzzles, all sorts of stuff to discover and find. Finally, if you stay up past the time you're supposed to sleep, its not incredibly punishing. You lose a little bit of stamina but that's it. Which is nice... the pass out penalty in some games can be very stressful and detract from The Cozy (tm)A+
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoy this game. It has a wonderful premise that builds on while also differentiating itself from Stardew Valley. I like the ideas mechanic, and the artisan/farming is just as rewarding as SDV in my opinion. The caves are an important parallel to your developments on the farm and elsewhere, and I enjoyed the pace of progression. I will say I found the puzzles to be pretty hard once you get further in, and the final puzzle was more than I could handle on my own. This game also does relationships really well, although in a way that's very similar to others in the genre (esp SDV, but that's not a bad thing). My favorite part, though, is that unlike some other games in the genre, there's never any harm or damage done to you at any point. You can stay up too late away from home and all that happens is you wake up with a little less stamina. If you want to cozy farming sim without the risk of death/loss of items, this is a great option. It's a little sparse on endgame content right now but I am super excited about the new content to come later this year.

_childDocuments_.review: A perfect game for those who love beautiful aesthetics, want the freedom to do whatever they want and don't want to subscribe to a toxic grindset mentality. And a really nice reminder of a world outside capitalism, revealing that there is plenty of motivation to do work in a socialist/communist environment, even (especially) if everyone shares everything equally in the end regardless of contribution. Basically it's Stardew without the rampant capitalism, which is amazing. Dislikes: not many, except for how the game captures 'progress' in the form of agriculture and technology as a positive. The anthropology nerd in me wishes it were a bit more true to history, where those advancements actually paved the way towards the modern dystopia we live in today. So as I play, each step away from the hunter-gatherer lifestyle and towards agriculture and manipulation of the environment feels like a slide towards a terrible world. I would have loved a game that emphasised how to preserve the natural environment and our harmony with it, and made a priority out of preserving their lifestyle rather than 'advancing' it.

What you can find in the game:  Farming, exploring, puzzles, relationship building, animal taming, fishing,  cooking, village building/improvingIf you are looking for combat, this game doesn't have it.  If you are looking for a peaceful farming sim, this game is worth a try.  Yes, the price point seems a little high, but remember, this is an indie game, and ALL games are luxuries.  A lot of work went into this game, with a very small team.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface this review, I'm basing this off my single player experience, and . This review is based off my initial 40 hours of playtime, and as someone who has a variety of experience playing similar games in the farming simulator genre.I will try to keep this review somewhat spoiler free.Roots of Pacha starts out with an interesting plot point, and as a result of said plot point, you have to make a decision that jumpstarts your playthrough.  After that, its up to you and your clan to settle down in these strange lands and figure out the strange mystery that brought you here.The plot for RoP is pretty interesting with the theme of the stone age. Although at some points, it may feel a bit cliche or too similar to some other farm sim mechanics, but overall not a bad story. I do enjoy the player's introduction into the clan and how the game makes great use of its NPCs, not just to serve as the player's utilities, but makes it really like it is a clan that works together.For your standard 2D pixel indie farm sim, RoP looks fantastic. For something based in the Stone Age, this game and its world is nothing bland. Lands are full of color, scenery is lush and full, and there is lots of detail that really sets the game. I really felt like I was sent back to the prehistoric ages as I traveled around.First off, the character creation, although not perfect, does offer plenty of options such as skin tone shades, different hair options, color variety and marking options.Some things that would be desirable for more inclusive options: more body options, few more starting options for the clothes and footwear.I mainly used keyboard and mouse for my playthrough, but browsing through the options, there is controller support available, which is nice.Something that threw me off, but took some getting used to was having my tools, seeds, and inventory be separated into 3 parts. Your seeds and tools can also be brought up via a wheel for quicker selection access.There is the option to start the game with the choice of speed, by walking or running, holding also allows for the reverse of whichever option you picked.The tutorials are helpful to some degree when you first start out, but there are some parts and points where things aren't fully explained or feel obvious unless you pay close attention. Even as I got stuck at one point, looking up some guides didn't give me any real solutions until I figured it out myself.Core gameplay is repetitive, but that's a farming sim for you.   Instead, you'll navigate some puzzles and solve a few mysteries.Currently in its current state, the game also goes by a bit faster than most farm sim games. , but it feels shorter than that sometimes. .Unlike other farm sims, I found myself grinding out a lot more in RoP, for the basis of trying to establish some kind of progress. You're mainly working on a somewhat linear quest line, but really trying to build "", which is the game's form of overall progress. There is no money system, but instead utilizing a system called "". As the name implies, you are contributing to your clan's survival and evolution, by dropping off goods and items to be "sold" at the end of the day. Contribution is used to purchase items and buildings, and you can only gain contribution through the set bins placed, and that contribution is only accounted for at the end of the day/night once you go to bed. Contribution is added to Prosperity, and the clan also naturally generates their own Contribution as well. "" are the form of crafting unlocks that will naturally spark based on what you're focusing on or as time goes by. You'll get a notification an NPC has an Idea they want to share with you, and it's up to you, whether or not you want to proceed with it. There is no skill system, so there is no inherent need to level skills to reach desired perks, instead you'll do as you please, and the game will try to suggest ideas or advancements based off what you're doing. For example, spending time in the mines providing better tool upgrades as an idea for me. There are also accessories that you can unlock as you advance through the game and it's story that can enhance some of your passive skills. Fishing is really simple, but can feel a tad slow, but that can be improved over time as you play.I do like the idea of mounts being available. Mounts help out with navigating the different lands, getting to places and back home faster, and the variety of different mounts and , make this game much more lively. The taming mechanic is much like a rhythm game, and pretty straightforward to use, and makes me feel more personal with the animals I'm meeting. Also the babies and pets are very cute!The festivals and events were also very fun and enjoyable as well. + Interesting Stone Age setting+ Easy fishing+ No skill tree/advancement, play as you like+ Lots of character creation options aside from limited body types+ Mount system+ Fun interactive events+ NPCs are not just for dialogue/utility. They are also adding to your progress.+ No harsh penalty for missing curfew+You can pet the dog (and other pets).-No combat. (Not a game breaker for me, but can be for others.)-In game days goes by a bit too fast. 15 mins real time = 1 in game day-Can be a bit grindy to get advancements.-Lack of body types (not a dealbreaker but more so representation lacking)-Linear plot events can impede or throw off gameplay-You cannot gain the game's form of currency at any other time besides the end of the day/when you go to sleep/save.-Traversal without a mount, makes exploration feel limited with the time constriction.-Some frames drop during some interactive events, and playing the game too long can lead to random stutters that require a restart.-Some upgrades don't feel worth it/not noticeable, which can be taxing on your stamina bar.-Map doesn't allow scrolling/moving around. So it can be a pain to have to physically move your character to see parts of the map.-Price doesn't feel like it justifies current game state at its price point.Overall, this game does a good job of making prehistoric farming pretty fun. Its such an interesting take and the lack of automation and other mechanics we're so used to in other games, makes one really appreciate the time and effort to make survival optimal. There are a few things that could use improvement for better quality of life, but there's nothing too bad that would leave my playthrough less than desirable. One thing I noticed people are debating,is the price, and I will say,

_childDocuments_.review: I have had this game on my wishlist for what feels like forever!So I was surprised and happy to see that it released today, and not even into early access but a full, real 1.0 release which is rare nowadays.I adore farming/life sims and Stardew, Rune Factory, etc are some of my favorite games.I have only played a bit over 2 hours, and I don't write a lot of reviews, but I am here to say that if you like this genre, then this game is a *must play*.  It's basically a stone age version of Stardew or Story of Seasons.  Everything you know and love is here - farming, fishing, mining, exploring, foraging, relationships, upgrading - this game is the full package.  The graphics are cute and a different 2D artstyle than other games in this genre but I feel like it works well and it's charming. The music is A+++ calming and perfect vibes.  The NPCs seem varied and interesting so far - with hot guys and gals available for your pursuing :)It's got that magical, one-more-day, perfect loop that very few games in this genre have managed to get. I had to pull myself away tonight to get some sleep.There seems to be some new, different gameplay systems here as well.  There is a whole tab in the inventory for "Prophecies" which I have yet to even have mentioned in the game.  There are quests you get from NPCs as you play, that expand your capabilities while playing.  Someone might have an idea on how to make water easier to get, or someone may say they know a way you can get closer to the wild animals that dot the landscape.  There's a lot going on here, but instead of being overwhelming, I just feel relaxed and great playing this.So while my playtime is low, my best sell for this game is that: very few games have made me feel this way since the first time I played Stardew Valley. I do not know what higher praise I can give a game in this genre.  If you are at all interested in these kinds of games then I *highly* recommend Roots of Pacha.  It's an easy 9/10 so far for me!

_childDocuments_.review: Edited to add: This is the first "like Stardew Valley but" that I genuinely, honestly believe is BETTER than Stardew Valley. That's the highest praise I could ever give a game in this genre. -♥-I've been looking forward to this game ever since we found and backed the Kickstarter and I'm so happy to finally play it. Everything is gorgeous, the Kickstarter bonus item is adorkable, the fishing mini-game is the cutest I've ever played and THE RABBITS ARE APLENTY. ♥ Lots of love for this one!After playing some more, I lost count of the amount of times my husband and I went "oooh this is pretty" or "oh wow I love that". The details in this game are astonishing, the general feeling of community and belonging, like every single Pacha is doing their best to contribute to the community, is really on point. You can tell a lot of love and passion went into this game. If you're still on the fence, I'm pushing you over. Get the game, you won't regret it!

_childDocuments_.review: I really really enjoyed Roots of Pacha. As other's have said, it scratches the Stardew Valley itch without being so similar as to feel like a copy. The setting is unique and imaginative, and feels very well constructed and fleshed out  (with the beginnings of some lore etc.) Content-wise it is not nearly as expansive as Stardew, but it still has a satisfying amount to do, and it seems like the devs have plans for expanding it which I'm excited about. Controls are intuitive and work well, with some features that I now miss when playing Stardew (especially being able to summon your mount!)I especially liked the variety of crops (many of which are not plants that often appear in farming sims) and the animal interactions. The NPCs are a diverse bunch with distinct characters and relationships, and there's a decent selection of romance options (though not much scope if you want to play as an older character). The fact that there is no combat is a plus for me, though some will likely disagree. The cave quests made a very welcome and enjoyable change from the usual monster fights.The soundtrack is especially good - definitely one to play with the sound on!Overall I'd highly recommend for anyone looking for a Stardew-style farming sim with a twist.
