_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a game that captivated me with its boundless creativity, a true testament to the passion and dedication of its developers. From the moment I embarked on my virtual journey, I was enthralled by the plethora of ideas and the meticulous attention to detail that makes this game truly remarkable.One of the most striking aspects of Roots of Pacha is its sheer creativity. The game presents a unique blend of farming simulation, village management, and exploration, creating an immersive experience that constantly keeps you engaged. The seamless integration of these gameplay elements showcases the developers' commitment to delivering a fresh and innovative gaming experience.The world of Roots of Pacha is brimming with diversity, both in terms of its characters and the gameplay mechanics. The range of customizable options for your character allows for personalization and the opportunity to create a truly unique avatar. As you interact with the various inhabitants of the village, each with their own stories and quests, you'll be drawn into a rich tapestry of cultures and traditions.What truly sets Roots of Pacha apart is the extraordinary attention to detail. The game world is meticulously crafted, with lush environments, vibrant colors, and atmospheric sound design. Whether you're tending to your crops, exploring hidden caves, or participating in community events, every aspect of the game exudes a sense of authenticity and care.Additionally, the progression system in Roots of Pacha is well-balanced, rewarding players for their efforts and encouraging exploration. The gradual unlocking of new tools, crops, and areas keeps the gameplay fresh and exciting, ensuring there's always something new to discover and accomplish.Overall, Roots of Pacha is a testament to the developers' commitment to their craft. Its remarkable creativity, diverse ideas, and meticulous attention to detail make it a standout game in the genre. If you're seeking a truly immersive and rewarding gaming experience that celebrates the love for creativity, Roots of Pacha is an absolute must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I like the game - you can farm crops and animals, there’s puzzles, fishing, foraging, and building relationships with NPCs. _childDocuments_.review: The only reason I am writing a review is to tell new gullible players (like myself) that the game even though 1.0 released it isn't a full game (I personally don't think the core mechanics were thought out). If you design a game on the PC can you please make it more mouse/keyboard friendly. Personally speaking I've run my course with "Early Access". There's way too many developers ruining the platform with little to zero or incredibly slow updates. Slow updates are fine but have a clear Roadmap on Steam. I prefer to "support" on what I see NOT on potential. If I'm going to waste my time, I'd sooner it was closer to completion. It's a pretty blank canvas yet and there's little to no tutorial. I feel like I've played enough games over my lifetime if I don't feel a certain vibe going forward or if it feels like a browser game (which it does) it's a big turn off at that $30+ asking price. I don't feel Kickstart games should be asking so much starting out. Have a lower price for the first year and once you build updates then you can increase. It just appears to be very greedy on little content. There's also many games that are way more fun than this. I'd rather play clicker AdventureQuest at least there's something to do. If you're making a game in this genre a day clock is needed. I don't know what time it is I'm going to bed and I could end up wasting in-game hours. Graveyard Keeper was a definite favourite (Stardew Valley kinda meh, only because of the short Day/Night, but honestly if that's all your only complaint it's not bad). But this doesn't even come close to the benchmark of a $30+ game. And music is very similar to other "farming sim titles". There is literally currently 10x the content in competing titles and at half it's price.Sorry for my long rant I'm just disappointed and little disgusted with what I've seen so far. I like text boxes that are quick and it seems like they just want to turn this into a choose-your-own story game with no choices and a farming sim on the side. I don't know what sim game I can compare this too because I haven't seen anything quite as bad as this except maybe a Harvest Moon. I don't buy games solely on graphics and sadly I guess that's the route most games are heading here. Lookin' at you Starbound. If it's cute it sells, right? Even if gameplay is poor or non-existent. TBH there are better mobile games than this. I can't see giving an uptick, not in my lifetime. If you're interested in this genre try a different one otherwise you've been warned.

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a fun, relaxing life sim that definitely evokes that feeling of "pre-human history", or at least, pre-RECORDED-human history" even as it lets you paint on cave walls during a community celebration. The characters are all interesting, they all have their own little quirks and idiosyncrasies you can either speak to them to learn OR to the other villagers. I really like the fact we can go out and tame certain animals with music and those animals can both be a mount (one at a time!) and give the ingredients and such you need. You can even breed them for adorable babies! (with better stats - gotta go fast!)I HIGHLY recommend playing with a friend as the fun is that much more amplified, but this game works well for single player too. Haven't finish the game yet, but I'll hop back on after the holidays. :D

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is "Great Value Stardew", but also it's very much its own thing.  It's clear the developers set out not to copy but to innovate, and in most aspects they succeeded.[Summary review at bottom]== Basic Gameplay ==For anyone familiar with Stardew Valley, the basic game loop and mechanics are clear: collect environmental resources, construct systems to leverage them, use gains to improve and streamline those systems for better efficiency, and engage with the local community both socially and commercially while you do it.  All the genre trappings are there and take a form you expect them to.The UI was also a bit clunky.  The choice to have seeds permanently bound to 1 and tools permanently bound to 2 meant that not only was the inventory toolbar shorter than players are accustomed to, but the muscle memory of "first item in toolbar is 1" requires some retraining to recondition it to being 3.  This also meant that cycling between different tools and seeds is clumsier than it needs to be.  Some other control issues existed in the UI, such as all menus being nested and the ESC key simply backing out one layer instead of closing the menu entirely, increasing the number of keypresses needed once you've obtained the information you need.  These issues didn't significantly impact gameplay, but did introduce frustration that had tangible impact on the experience.There are some broad game mechanic issues the game doesn't really do a good job of explaining, nor does it provide any glossary.  Stats aren't clearly defined, buffs aren't explained, and some feedback is nebulous at times.  For example, an accessory that gives +15 to a given stat doesn't have any indication of what tangible change the player should expect to experience.  Animals can experience maladies, but there doesn't seem to be any rhyme or reason to why they do.  One idea requires "pots", but doesn't clearly indicate this is something purchased from a single NPC and cannot be made or found, unlike every other resource requirement.  None of these are gamebreakers, but they feel like something which could be polished up to improve the experience, and likely could be patched without any significant change to the game design.== Audio/Visual Design ==The visual design is vibrant and detailed.  Characters had interesting designs, which complemented their personalities.  Maps were varied and well fleshed out, and each environment felt rich.  Nothing about the design or layout of the areas felt inorganic or lazy, and exploring the same handful of areas never got tiresome as small aspects would vary on a daily basis.  There were some visual glitches in places, but nothing that meaningfully impacted gameplay.Sound design was... good.  At times, it felt a little too Stardew-y, with some sound cues and music choices feeling like they were even using the same soundfont, but that dooesn't mean it didn't feel pleasant or appropriate.  Just too appropriate.  Still, it all came together nicely.  Dynamic sound mixing incorporated environmental aspects to change the audio in a manner that made the world feel fuller.The one major grievance I have on visual design is that crops can be problematic.  Plants can obscure the soil beneath, making it hard to tell if a given grid point has been watered, and the positioning of plant sprites on the grid makes targetting crops for harvesting and watering difficult.  This could be easily resolved with a simple cleanup of spritework either by devs or through a mod.== Narrative ==The game's narrative is a bit odd.  The opening splash indicates it's not representative of any one culture or time period, and that becomes truer as the game goes on.  Several technological advancements clash with each other, resulting in an end-game civilization that has developed metallurgy and low-grade mechanization, but still wears pelt robes and paints on rocks.  However, if you ignore the more absurd anachronisms (which isn't hard once you get into the flow), all the small advancements serve to create a fun progression.  My one real complaint here is that if you're doing particularly well - which I'd imagine most familiar with the genre trappings would - the technological progression tends to be heavily front-loaded, leaving the later seasons somewhat sparse.  Fortunately, as you'll tend to be preoccupied with the relative complexity of your operation by that point, it's easy to forgive that.The characters all feel distinct and meaningful.  Their roles in the tribes and their behaviour come through and produce a lively tableau of a small community.  Some of the characters are more lowkey than others, but even the less remarkable NPCs still serve a meaningful role in padding out the cast to give a sense of community.The story itself is fairly by the numbers.  It's gradually unveiled as you meet progression milestones, however the foreshadowing isn't shy about where it's going.  The story's end doesn't feel especially monumental, but it is an end that gets to where you expected it to go.== Overall ==All in all, Roots of Pacha is a solid, robust entry in the genre that anyone interested in should check out sooner than later.  Some design choices work against itself, but nothing that impedes the foundational goals of the game or the expectations of the player.  It's not better than Stardew Valley, but it's somewhat unfair to forcibly compare it to a game that's had a decade and millions in funding to perfect.Pacha is its own game that strikes that balance of "I want more of what I'm used to, but completely different from what I've seen", and if that sentiment sounds familiar to you then this is the answer.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall the game is colorful, atmospheric and fun. I love the cute aesthetic and all the different options you have, as well as the variety of NPCs.However, I wish the story was more engaging and rich, and that each character could feel more personal. In addition, and more importantly, I wish there was more where to progress to in the later game, by the time I've unlocked irrigation and automation I've already had an endless amount of money and nothing to do with it, nowhere I'd like to put it into aside from more expansion, but it felt that there was no point for more expansion cause I've already had an endless amount of money. It's really too bad, cause I don't wanna get out of the lovely world of Pacha, but after a bit more than one year I don't really see where to go..All in all, I've had a great time in this adorable world. I was just done wish a super stressful period and really needed something to relax and have fun with, and this game delivered beautifully.

I'm only on Summer of Year 1 but I am thoroughly enjoying it so far!!

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely the best farming sim I've played since Stardew Valley. Has everything you could want in a cozy farming game - tons of crops, recipes, and animals; a town that feels alive with a huge variety of villagers and cute cutscenes for those villagers; decor for your house with a surprising amount of flexibility (including the ability to custom-paint plant pots!); steady progression with rewards that are visible in the town. Has a huge "just one more day" pull - I wish there were more hours in a real life day to play this. 11/10

_childDocuments_.review: While Stardew Valley is my first love, I feel like this game is everything I wish SDV was. Or maybe its that I have over 300 hours in SDV and having a new spin on the genera is refreshing. Having a structured story and set of goals really helps keep my motivation for this game. The NPCs are deep and have good dialog. This game is a must have if you like cozy games or cute animals. I can't wait to see what the developers have in store for the future!

_childDocuments_.review: You can play the flute to animals and make friends with them, what more could you want in a game!!I started Roots of Pacha a few weeks ago and I am really enjoying it so far. Finding new seeds, new animals, watching the Clan grow and thrive as they gain more prosperity is great. I like that this game doesn't hold your hand at all, here this is what you have to do now go do it, I get to makes mistakes on my own and that I love. Oh and you also get to buy and wear a White Wolf outfit that gives you a strange affinity to the name Geralt and I am working to that outfit so I too can have an affinity with Geralt.This game has everything you need and want in a Farming Life sim and so much more. _childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I love this even more than Stardew Valley, the game is that good!* Taming Animals* Growing Crops* You have to find new crop seeds out in the Forest, Savannah, Jungle, Beach, or in your village, or buy them from a clanmate* Tool upgrades - flint, obsidian, copper, and (haven't gotten this yet surprisingly) bronze* Lots of romanceable characters, and a chance to lose them to someone else* Can have two kids* Can tame a mammoth, wolf, bunny, or even a cave lion cub for a pet (& can have up to 3!)* Cook lots of dishes with a wide variety of foods* Ferment, make cheese, sour cream, brew drinks, and make grain so a large variety of ingredients for cooking and contributing to the clan* Wild foods to find & use immediately (just tree fruits, like almond, pine cones, coconut, ect)* Puzzle in the caves make you think & the hints are very clearMy only issues are:* it feels like there isn't enough stamina, especially starting out. Yes, you can eat food but it still feels like there's too little for everything that's available during the day.* Daytime goes by very quickly, it doesn't need to be super slow but slower would be nice* Riding tamed animals is barely faster than walking
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Do you think Stardew Valley feels lonely? Are you disappointed by the lack of meaningful story in most cozy farming games? Do you like farming games with an abundance of non-farming things to do? Do you like taming cute animals? Do you want to have the option to date 10+ people at once with no story consequences? If you've answered 'YES' to any of these questions (or if you just like good games) then you NEED to buy this game. The thing that initially sold me on this game was the seamless multiplayer integration, since you can have friends drop in or out of your saves with no problems or complications. As soon as I started playing though, I knew that I was in trouble and that this game would dominate my attention span for the foreseeable future. As it stands, this game is PHENOMENAL, but the best part is that the devs are still actively working on it and adding content regularly. Roots of Pacha is going in my personal hall of fame and it's certainly worth a try for anyone who likes cozy games.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I play a lot of farming sims, but usually not for the reasons advertised.I don't usually care about making friends with my neighbors, and when I do get attached to characters it is usually only one or two of them.Usually heart meters are just another part of 100% completion.My favorite farming sim is RF4, because I find repetitive tasks and making numbers go up relaxing.By all accounts, I should have been severely disappointed by this game.But I wasn't.If you play farming sims because you like the actual gameplay of them, this game is not for you - it is for the people who like to spend time in virtual communities and enjoy a friendly neighborhood.However, it might be worth giving the game a try anyway.Lord knows I hate socializing. In real life and games alike, I am usually a loner and an introvert.Something about this game, though - and *only* this game... it makes me run up to everyone and talk to them every single day. Just to say hi.The friendship meter filling up is just a bonus.So, yeah. I recommend it.There's no real reason it's good, not a one. No, its flaws have reasons... but what makes it good is more subtle, woven in between all the things that you can see and hear.You can tell this game was made by people who just wanted to share something "nice" with everyone.

_childDocuments_.review: If I could give a "meh" or neutral recommendation, I would. This game is not bad, but it has so little of interest to it for me, that I did not care for playing it. I played it co-op with my wife as I do most of these sorts of games. From the beginning, this game is so easy and feels like the target audience is for new gamers, or people around the age of 10 or so, and if that's the case, I really should not have purchased this game.Right off, I noticed the options are very minimal, which basically nothing to help with accessibility. Because I have wrist tendonitis (due to programming way too much, yep, all my fault), I always try to remap controls in games so I can use a special keyboard, the Wolf King, that puts as many keys as possible right around my left hand without requiring a lot of movement. There is no option to remap keys in this game, just options for QWERTY, QWERTZ, and AZERTY. Even with the QWERTY configuration, some odd keypresses like Alt (to rotate objects) and Control (hide/show some things in some menus) are still used, but common keys like inventory and the map are way out of the way, as I and M.There is no proper Steam integration. You have to tell your co-op partner a random 6-character code for them to find your server. You cannot password protect the server either, so I guess if someone randomly came on your server, all you could do is shut down and restart to deal with that. Just like Stardew Valley, it only saves after the end of the day report.At its roots (haha), this is a Stardew Valley clone that strips out a lot of the personality of that game, removes combat, adds in a frustrating multi-tiered menu system (you have to press Esc 3 times for most menus), and puts in a pseudo-stone-age story that is just all over the place. The story moves along completely without you, and I cannot figure out how your characters are supposed to fit into anything in the game at all. You are complete nobodies that were picked up on the way to a new location, and aside from getting a unique totem at the beginning of the game, nothing in this game cares about your existence at all. Instead of selling products, you contribute to a tribe-wide total score that occasionally causes the other characters to build something new that you generally couldn't care less about. If you do absolutely nothing, the game carries on without you. I cannot emphasize how worthless and unnecessary I feel in this game world, and I feel completely disconnected with anybody in it other than the building maker and the tool maker that we have to interact with regularly.In Stardew, occasionally other characters come to your farm, tell you stories about your grandfather that used to own it, talk about things they have done in their lives, mail you items, or ask for you to help them. None of this exists in this game, and if it weren't for the NPCs getting random ideas (that YOU unlock) that you have to give them items to actually complete, you wouldn't need to interact with much of anybody in this game. The characters all have unique, strange names with Igrork and To and Mana and so on as examples of names, but it also makes it hard to figure out who is who. The first time you talk to characters, you see a brief family tree, and it also struck me as so strange that this stone-age tribe looked so disparate, with just about every family having a range of different-looking people that don't appear to have anything to do with each other. When you find a couple other tribes, they're just as varied, and it makes everybody indistinguishable. Racial intermixing is great in most games, but it makes no sense in a stone age game where people could not travel across the world to support such a thing.The game itself gives very little choice for what you do. You can farm, but nobody cares much, and there isn't a lot of a point until you can cook. You can fish, and once you get the sun-drying racks, it's the best way to get contribution points. And you can go into the mines...The basics of farming are nearly identical to Stardew, except that aiming is a lot better in this game. But you are very limited on the amount of seeds you can get, which you have to forage for by wandering around every few days. After a while, you can at least buy more seeds, again in limited quantities, but it does give you a little more options. Over time, your crops will progress from wild to non-wild since you level up every individual crop type. You will then have a total of 5 different qualities that the game designates as wilted-looking (the wild variants), normal looking, and with a circle, triangle, or star. The only problem is that just about all of the crops are not worth much to contribute, and even after you unlock all of the recipes, almost nothing really stands out. Lots of the food give meaningless boosts like "+1 Ore Gathering" that I never noticed make any difference at all, and the buffs only last 60 seconds or so, so why even bother aside from gaining stamina from the food?There's the fishing mini-game which is so much less involved than other fishing mini-games where you literally just point your mouse cursor at them and wait for bars to fill out, but occasionally they are alerted and you move your cursor away for a few seconds, then continue. Repeat until it says you can catch the fish. Some fish get alerted easier and/or have more bars to fill... and you level up in fishing each fish, which only seems to decrease the number of bars by 1 once you reach level 3. It's really mindless.And then there are the mines which are very, very slow to get through. To begin with, they are in a remote location, so you have to do a lot of walking every time to reach them. You do not know when the next teleport point will be as you travel through them. The arrangement of the rooms feels fairly random, and the "map" you get only shows you where each room is. And each room is either completely straight-forward, has one of the four mini-games you have to do to get more progression, or is a huge time-sucking frustrating darkness room because your character cannot possibly use two hands at once or put their torch on the floor so they can break rocks in their path. It takes so much stamina that some days I'd go through 8 entire stamina bars while digging to get around, and aside from needing the ores to get better tools and buildings, it's not particularly rewarding either. You end up getting an ability to turn into a bird, then a monkey, at designated circles that let you switch back and forth, and eventually gain the ability to use bear claws to break rocks in a 4x3 area, or special bear-breaking-only rocks. It takes nearly constant, dedicated time to get through it, though I suppose without the mines, there wouldn't be much to do in the game.You can also tame animals with a simple "click when the circles reach the middle in time to music" mini game. All you get from them is dropped resources (or milk once you unlock the milking pan), or riding some of them (there is no advantage to riding any one animal over another), or having one hang out at your home for cuteness' sake I guess. Eventually you are required to have some of those resources to make part of the water canals or give a cheese to get the bear power. Oh, and there's breeding to try to get the three attributes up to 4 points each I guess. It's all serviceable, but feels like a missed opportunity for much else.In any case, the game is serviceable, and stops with that. It is too easy, too mindless, and after just a few days, I'm very bored with it. For $25, $10 more than Stardew Valley, I was expecting there to be more to this. I'd give it a 5/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is your usual Harvest Moon type game (though nowaways the reference is usually Stardew Valley). It does a few things very well, namely the cozy atmosphere, the sense of progression and the constant things to look forward to as the village upgrades. Although after the first year you will probably already have made every discovery and you will likewise already have explored the whole cave system.Considering I got 65 hours out of the game at this point I feel good about recommending it for the game mechanics. Plus it features multiplayer which is probably pretty awesome for nice hours with friends and family.However there is also a downside as far as I am concerned. As can be expected the game feels very "progressive". An unhealthy amount of hippie villagers, diversity around every corner, a lesbian couple (also hippies), overused modern day themes ("tradition is bad", etc), a lot of man/woman role reversal (prime example: son and daughter of the chieftain - one likes cooking and runs away from duty and confrontations while the other is a brave tomboy adventurer), most characters have some sort of childhood trauma that you need to help them overcome, and so on.Well what can I say? The mechanics are too good to pass this game up though. Just roll your eyes like I did.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The best in its genre so far. The era and set up makes so much sense and the concept of ideas could not have been better. Multiplayer is super interesting as we progress together and quests / quest rewards are given to all. we are really invested in the story and cannot stop playing. There was a lot of love put into this game it shows in all aspects of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Tip: Go into main menu settings and increase day cycle to maxFor fans of Stardew, Graveyard Keeper, and other pixel life/farming sims, this is definitely worth a playthrough...with one caveat.  This is not as deep as most in the genre.  Im nearing Winter of Year 1, and already have 29 hours, yet I've found that there is not a lot of variety to money making like their is in Stardew or Graveyard Keeper or My Time at Portia.  For this game, just fish a bunch and dry them.  What this game does have going for it is its style and its world, cause there is a bit to explore.  Hopefully they do add a few more zones that are mentioned in the Kickstarter stretch goals, as year 2 looks like it my start to drag a tad.  I loved the characters, and this is similar to the usual give everyone their favored gift mechanic.  What I do like is that npc's will randomly share a favored gift of someones, a thing i wish most games had.   The story at this point is a bit barebones, especially the "conflict" between two neighboring tribes that isn't entirely clear, but maybe the story and conflict will have more depth near endgame.  I will most likely spend around 50 hours in this game when all is said and done, and that money well spent for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is the best cozy game I played last year. It has the best progression system I've seen in any cozy game - including Stardew Valley - it's incredibly engaging to just run that cozy game loop. That said, the social stuff is a bit lacking, I don't care about these characters - and neither did anyone else I've talked to or seen reviews by. This also effects the festivals because while they are incredibly inventive if you don't care about the characters, they lack the impact. I also feel that since the game lacks any kind of quests that are not based around new technologies - the devs might struggle to support the game with new content going forward and once you're done with the questline, there isn't much to keep you around. That SAID, I enormously enjoyed my playthrough with the game and I'm certain I'll revisit the game in the future for other playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Was a Kickstarter backerPlayed 46 hours of the betaHad some of my suggestion implemented into the gameSquashed some bugs/misspelling dialog lines, etcThe duo developers are so warm, listened to feedback and fostered a family of backers in DiscordNow can't wait for my friends to experience the joy of exploring Pacha!So you can bet my turnip ass it's a recommended from me=quick TLDR review=It's basically akin to a modded out SDV with a prehistoric theme, but I say that in a good & positive way (there's nothing wrong with that, even SDV was inspired by Harvest Moon and  Rune Factory series, and all farming sims bear similarity one way or another)RoP has it's own unique gameplay features and charm, all the quality of life you get via mods in SDV are here, makes life very easy to do and I find the non aggresive no combat decision to be a delight. If you want meat, you can still get them (no spoilers) so there will be meat based dishes for your carnivorous culinary disposition.What I like the most about RoP is how you're really building a new home for your clan, the community pitches in and grows with your farm together, unlocking new stuffs as time goes.PS: for you anglers out there, the fishing mini game here (which is usually hard to get right for most farming sims) has a pretty interesting mechanic and very much in line with the theme of spear fishing during prehistoric age. The devs have listened to frustrating feedback of early beta fishing and tweaked it
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an incredible amount of charm and really brings something fun and unique to the genre. Recently a lot of farming sims have felt kind of repetitive and unoriginal, but you can definitely feel the love the devs have for this game in every aspect of it. While there are some improvements I would love to see, Roots of Pacha is a charming and rewarding farming sim with a diverse and unique cast of characters (I still haven't gotten married yet because it's so hard to choose!)Pros:-Unique story progression that intimately connects the storyline with gameplay. Developing ideas with the villagers allows for improvements to crop growing, fishing, tool enhancement and more. This makes the gameplay super immersive which I feel has been lacking in a lot of games in this genre recently.-Unique improvement systems on everything from fishing, to fruit tree growing, to crops that goes beyond just "use better bait" or "use fertilizer". -Game runs smoothly, doesn't crash or stutter.-Diverse cast of townsfolk and marriageable characters with their own character development and storylines.Cons-This game does have a bit of a problem with lots of debris spawning in the editable areas of the farm. Debris tends to respawn every few days, especially on the southern field. I tend to like my fields to be cleared so this was a pain point for me. You can build flooring and stuff to cover it up but thats a time consuming process in itself, plus it makes traversing that part of the map annoying. Considering how many other places there are to gather basic resources this felt a bit heavy handed.-Can't see animals stats from the animal menu, you have to investigate each animal individually. I have three barns of animals so it would be really nice to be able to see more info about the animals individually from the menus, especially when deciding which animals to breed.-It was a little unclear when I was able to purchase fruit tree saplings, turns out it was a separate menu tab you can access when purchasing seeds. The tutorial doesn't address this and the character didn't mention it either, so I didn't start growing fruit trees till year two. Granted trees grow pretty quick so it isn't as painful as it could be, but still felt it deserved a mention.Overall even with the cons I felt this was an extraordinarily well tailored game and I plan to continue playing even 93 hours in. (Really need to get married at some point huh). I haven't been this immersed in a farming sim since probably Pumpkin Days or Stardew Valley, both of which I have hundreds of hours played. Give this game a try, even with the cons its well worth the money!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I am in love with this game so much that I just yeeted it at two friends. I've only had it for a few days but I'm eight hours in. It's just perfection- calm fishing, farming, speedy access to pets and mounts, so much exploring to do and a knowledge system that makes your efforts rewarding- I can't think of better. The game being combat free is approached in the perfect way;  you have mining trials and can set traps for meat instead of having to do direct combat. A major bonus for a scardy-cat like me who is still scared of minecraft mobs and stardew mining! Thank you so much for making this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I definitely recommend this game, if you like Stardew Valley, you will like this game, however IMO it does have some pacing issues. The first spring is overwhelming with new ideas and unlocks almost every day. I completely missed the beach and Savannah zones for a long time because after meeting the new tribes, I didn't think there was more to that cutscene/unlock and I was so overwhelmed with everything else. After the first spring it does settle down, however, I was able to complete the main plotline and all the "idea" unlocks by the first week of the second year, without using guides (and missing 2 zones for a long time!) After that there are some more community unlocks but they're just aesthetic and I completed those by early summer year 2. As is always an issue with games of this type, the inventory is far too limited, only 24 slots when fully upgraded. Each crop can grow 5 different quality levels which makes harvesting a massive pain, even if you clear out your inventory, you might still need multiple trips to processing/storage areas on harvest days.Tools don't take up inventory space which is nice but you start off with a simple hand tool that chops wood, smashes rocks, clears foliage, dig and fishes - its great, especially for clearing the farm land . But then when you upgrade, you get individual tools for each job and have to tab through them to find the one you want. Later in the game you get a better hand tool but its not as good as the individual tools so I only used it for clearing fields. Then you have your shearing tool and your milking bucket, which you only need for a short period of time as when the sheds are fully upgraded, that's all taken care of automatically but I could see no way to ditch those toolsSame issue with the seeds, there are about 30 crops and your seed bag is a separate menu rather than inventory space but it show all the seeds you know, not just the ones that can be planted so its an arduous task rotating through them all to get the one you wanted. Later in the game there's an area where you can plant any crop at any time but that just means that the seed shop now sells all the seeds all the time too, which IMO was not an improvement. Maybe if there was a way to filter them, that would have been better. The do show which season they can be planted on the seed but you still have to look at each one to find the seasonsEnd-game content is pretty much just completionist stuff, getting 5 in every crop and fish, cooking every dish etc. There are some end-game item purchases available that are very expensive and there's a whole animal breeding/rarity thing that I've barely scratched the surface of so there's a good many hours still to play but IMO it would have been better if the main plot wasn't so front-loaded and took maybe 2 years to complete for a beginner with no idea what they're doing
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A fun prehistoric farming simulator that has all the coziness you'd want. Unlike many games in this genre, I found that Roots of Pacha nailed the feeling you want games of this type to elicit. I found myself wanting to keep playing the game to see what the next day and the next season would bring.While I played the game solo and have enjoyed it immensely, I think the game may be even better multiplayer. If you have a friend (or three) that likes farming simulators, I would heartily recommend you try this out.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in love!This is the perfect cozy game, simple enough to be a pleasant experience but with so much detail I can't get enough of it. Different from the most classic farming games, but with all the things we love about them. The art is beautiful, the activities fun, mini-games that don't make you want to cry in frustration. You can decorate, paint, combine... SO MANY POSSIBILITIES! And the characters! Charming and with amazing personalities. Ata has a hammer pet! With its own bed! *dies of excitement*
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game has a really enjoyable progression and the animal sprites are so cute and well designed. Because it is quite similar to Stardew Valley I can't help comparing the two games, and I'd have to say this game does not induce the same level of obsession that SV did - you have to put a little more effort into finding and remembering all the things you can do, but it's still a game I'll happily play for a few hours straight.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: If you loved Stardew Valley, you'll love this game.  It very obviously was inspired by it, and it is one of the few games since Stardew Valley that feels like can measure up.  Almost the exact same relaxing and one more day vibe.  It has no combat but excels in other areas.  If you've never played Stardew Valley, then you don't really have a point of reference.  This is a relaxing prehistoric village development simulator.  You help your village grow by contributing through farming and animal husbandry.  It has a story/campaign so you are not just playing for score.   You improve little by little each day and each season, and small changes occur as the village grows.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Like many others, I got this game in attempt to "scratch that Stardew Valley itch." Not only did it succeed in doing so, but I've found it equally satisfying in a slightly different way. It's an even chiller game than SDV. I know others are disappointed by the lack of combat, but I really don't miss it - cave combat was my least favorite part of that game, anyway. Wandering around the world collecting, farming, befriending and breeding animals, and improving the village in a community that values nature and each other is a welcome respite from the current world.I have 140 hours in right now and am on my second play-through, where I'm still discovering some things I missed the first time. The developers are still working to add content, which I'm really excited about and think will greatly enhance the appeal of replaying of the game."Is it worth $25?" Everyone is looking for something different in a game and so this is a highly subjective question, but for me personally, the answer is yes. It's a chill (i.e., certainly idealistic but satisfyingly cozy) way to spend hours of enjoyment. There's no rage-quitting or spam saving. Very much like SDV, it may not be a game that I sink thousands of hours into; however, it's one I'll come back to periodically throughout the year and binge for a month at a time whenever I need to quiet my mind. That makes it worth the money for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A fun and engaging farming RPG. Very relaxed, not difficult with interesting mechanics. Instead of only building your farm, you also have to take care of technological development of farming and the development of your tribe.Recommended for everyone who:-is interested in farming simsand -don't mind a different take on it-likes prehistory
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: It's kind of like an acient Stardew valley, but a tad more forgiving. There are more days in a season, and fishing doesn't make me want to throw my pc into a lake like Stardew valley's fishing does, in fact, i'd say fishing is my favorite minigame in this game.Also the NPCs are written to be believable and fun, they have character traits that make them up, not just one defining thing. Plus NPCs aren't constantly at your beck and call, you need to go out of your way to find them, and sometimes, they're just gone for a day.Also i love that you can dance with the NPCs :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Primitive Stardew is the easiest quick description to give it. However it does a good job of carving out it's own identity instead of just another story of seasons/stardew clone. From your humble beginnings you start with no more than a mere handaxe and no knowledge of the world around you. As you explore you come across seeds you can forage to plant in your farm, as you do so you gain more knowledge about the seeds in question (for example you won't know how many days a seed takes to grow initially). As your village gains prosperity villagers begin coming up with ideas for advancements of science you can help out with such as a sundial for more precise timekeeping (until then your "clock" is just a rough position of the sun), etc. The game is very casual friendly, no combat to die in, and you can run your stamina to the ground without worrying about collapsing and losing currency. Same if you stay up too late, you don't have to worry about losing currency the only consequence is reduced stamina the next day. long as you keep a mind out for it stamina isn't too large an issue as you can easily spear up a fish and cook it for cheap effective stamina among other options.There's plenty more that could be gotten into such as the animal taming/breeding and the community driven nature of the game, but I'm not quite far enough to cover everything. If a fresh take on the farming sim genre is what you're looking for you can't go wrong with Roots of Pacha
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Like Stardew Valley, I loved the game :) Especially I liked that I could play flute to animals, each have their own melody to play.I don't really get it that you don't get any seeds from the plants you grow on your own field. When you are out of seeds you either have to go gather them in the wilds or buy them from the old geezer. Not a big problem, but it bothered me a little.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The personalities of the characters are very deep. I loved being friends with everyone and discovering who everyone really is. I also loved how challenging the progression in the game was. Money isn't snowballing, you actually have to work for it. Also, I loved how the cave exploring is like a mini-puzzle game. It is so different from classic combat-type gameplay for this kind of genre. The art and music also are so cute. I could easily say this game is in my all-time top 3 and I haven't finished it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I thought the game was in early access due to the low amount of content there is.Pretty expensive for the amount of content it had.Price and content aside, it was a fun and easy game, simple mechanics but there really isn't a lot to do. Because it is simple, you won't need to consult the wikis to enjoy the game and discover everything.I'm only on year 2 but there really isn't much more to do that I hadn't done in year 1.SDV had more content when it was first released, and definitely has way more content in its current form. Hopefully ROP will follow in their footsteps.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is the most unique of the farming Sims I've played. Its has beautiful Pixle graphics and a complex and wonderful game play system that require cooperation from your clan, exploration, and innovation! There a ton of way you can customize your clan and home, multiple pets and mounts to choose from and a vast (sometimes frustrating) cave system. Give the game a try! Its worth it! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just crazy cute and relaxing all over! I can't get enough of the animals, I want them all!The theme of contributing and working together to progress is very refreshing, and the people also have very cute interactions! I do actually want to talk to them everyday and, better yet, you can DANCE with them! (once you have enough friendship points, otherwise they just stare at you in silent judgement XD)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game. It's so different than usual farming sims. I like the fact that you go out and find/gather crop seeds. As you grow and harvest them, your knowledge of them grows. This will give you the chance to start buying the seeds, and it'll make your crop quality increase. I also love that you go out and tame animals. You have to have a barn built first, but it's a nice change than just buying cows and sheep and chickens. You can also release the animals at any point. You tame pets the same way, but they stay in your house. There are a ton of things to do and upgrade and explore. House decorations can be bought; plus you can customize some of them a little bit. I have a pot that I was able to paint whatever color I wanted. There were also different plant options to be in that pot. It's the little things that can really make a game stand out. You can also change how long a day lasts. Overall, this game is super fun, and I cannot wait to see more developments.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game up until Spring of Year 2 over the course of a long holiday weekend. I absolutely love Roots of Pacha and can't wait for future updates!! I will say you can progress very quickly if you're a min-maxer, but I appreciate the more laid back attitude of things like the mines and the fact that there are no penalties (aside from stamina) for passing out.The animals are adorable. NPC characters are all very fun to interact with. The recipes are wonderfully rendered, and the soundtrack is great. I am going to be starting a new save for 1.2 as soon as its out!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely fantastic addition to the farming sim line up! It really feels like a community game, with a really interesting approach to learning new techniques in a way that rewards giving back and helping your clan members without being too grindy. I like that information is always recorded to go back and review, and at 6 hours in, I have naturally increased the things I can do without it feeling overwhelming, and there's clearly so much more to go! I also love the mini games, which remind me very much of Spiritfarer. The game very naturally rewards experimenting and giving things a go, as there is so far always something unlocked or new waiting on the other side. There is clearly a lot of love and attention to detail that went into this game, and I definitely recommend giving it a go and a fair chance :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: If your looking for a hard game go elsewhere, this game is calm easy and relaxing. No combat, low risk from running out of energy or time and no need to worry about a time limit for interactions. This is a game to play after a hard day at work so that you can just breathe out and relax. Catharsis and relaxation. I personally play it on 15 minute days and early on you will have a bit of a time crunch if you go too big too early but the upcoming update seems to be looking to help with that. Late game is looking fun so back to it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much fun. _childDocuments_.review: I put off purchasing Roots of Pacha for quite a while, thinking it just another Stardew Valley clone.  However, it does a great job of iterating on the Stardew style of gameplay by adding quality of life features and thematic aspects that help set it apart.One of my favorite parts is the "idea" system, which results in you building up the village with additional capabilities (and also getting to choose where the new buildings go).  The caves are a lot of fun, with staged progression (via fun puzzles) and well-placed fast-travel spots (so you don't have to backtrack through multiple screens).I also like how plants level up as you progress with farming, and there's a visual difference in how the crops look.  Again, really nice touches that show the level of care that went into the game.If you enjoy games like Stardew Valley, I definitely recommend giving Roots of Pacha a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very good game in the mold of Stardew Valley, but with the twist that you are a member of a small tribe of prehistoric humans. End game is a bit sparse, but the developers seem to still be working on adding features. Unlike many games in this genre, there is no combat, which I thought was a plus.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a delightful and immersive farming and life simulation game that truly stands out in the genre. As a player, I found myself captivated by its unique blend of community building, exploration, and engaging gameplay mechanics.Exploring the world is a joy, with caves to discover and puzzles to solve that connect you with totem spirits. This spiritual quest adds depth to the gameplay and keeps things interesting as you progress. The game also features a variety of flora and fauna, making every exploration feel rewarding and full of potential.

_childDocuments_.review: It gets stale very fast.It says it's the Stardew Valley in Stone Age and I can't agree.Stardew Valley has a fight system that is interesting, it has reasons to always want to go bigger and better, this game gets stale very fast.Stardew has interesting puzzles, this game puts you in front of a door with vanes before it and instead of saying, hey figure it out, there is a small pet near it that tells you what to do and additional there is a picture of an axe near it.Also, I don't feel that I really have anything to do, the since points are coming in without me doing anything, so there will always be a small progression but the progression feels so empty like torches at night on the houses of the villagers or that I can buy seeds but don't need to because they are everywhere and I can't really do anything with the end product except sell it for since points that are same as the villagers get without me.I think only the first 5 days I used up my endurance, otherwise I end days with half of it because other than water my plant I don't need it for anything.Also, there are other people that are bland and late there are other tribes that do nothing.I have to say, that I am not the type that likes to talk to NPCs and give them gifts, so I don't know if that would change something but till now, they do nothing interesting.The new regions are nice, but especially the beach is uninteresting.Maybe after some additional content this game gets better, Stardew wasn't as it is today from day one but if I had not played longer than 2 hours I would refund.

_childDocuments_.review: People looking for their new farming sim, look no further. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game! Very unique. I love all the different things and ideas they did here, and all of them work and make this different and memorable from the million other farming sims.Here are the things that I loved: - The big one, which is the contribution system. Brilliant, I absolutely love the idea, and the implementation, making it the 'currency'. It actually removes the grind that typically comes with these games, I really feel more relaxed in this game than others. - Taming animals instead of buying, and the mini game is excellent. I love also that you are able to ride them.- Fishing mini game is good, and I am actually glad someone did something new and good with it.- Quite a few qol implementations that make the game all around better, only missing two things for me. One is being able to craft immediately from a box (you can only do that in Kitchen lvl 2 house and only from the near pantry). And second one is an option to move all same items you have in a chest from your inventory, instead of clicking one by one. - A separate 'pocket' for tools and another one for seeds, and you get seeds from the game world.- The game doesn't take your tools when you upgrade them. Imagine a game that wants you to keep playing normally and not inconvenience you!! - The idea system is really good, only thing is that some ideas take a little too long to start, I think they are season bound.Absolutely recommend this to lovers of the genre, what a fun and different experience this has been for me so far.

_childDocuments_.review: Really good farming and time management sim. It's Stardew, but in the Neolithic Era of civilizations. I sank about 50 hours until the final day that I just dinked around and played with my pets in game. I was stuck to my computer for those 50 hours, though. This review offers minor spoilers as examples to be reviewed, but otherwise no characters, events, names, or pronouns are used to avoid spoiling a beautiful game.Good•Game is very easy to pick up and understand what to do•In the rare moments that you don't have an objective, the game does not ever have "wasted days"•Wonderfully written characters that have a very plausible and beautiful connection to the world and your character•The story is simple and very wholesome•Very inclusive and artistic vision of characters•It's very beautiful to see the village upgrade and inspires you to want to continue to contribute•Tons of customizable options for your house, character, and clothes•No combat! (which may actually be a downside for some players)•Very grounded and realistic styles of early-civ peoples' tools, styles of preservation, and interesting interpretations of production - there's some things I'm STILL finding out about in the tools and crafting•Lots of Quality of Life improvements if you are used to vanilla Stardew Valley•Absolutely gorgeous pixels and sprites•Full Co-Op!Bad•The game has some brief stuttering issues once you've really upgraded the village: this is not very impactful until you have some minor rhythm-based minigames•There is a long wait for automation•Even though there is no "perfect" spot for your buildings, some spots definitely seem more coveted than others and some seem worthy of decoration at best: this could be a damning "meta" usage that will show every core player using the same layout for a lot of their villages•It is WAY too easy to achieve all of the village plans and makes the game seem like it's on a very finite track - it is also VERY easy to make money which may not be a downside depending on how you like to play•Tons to discover that could be discovered way too late without much tutorial or explanation•Unfortunately falls into the algorithmic formula basis of: certain items are just worth more, so you should always focus on them - this is seen in Stardew with Pumpkins or Harvest Moon with Eggplants•Not a lot of customizable settings for graphics or screen size besides the res and vsync, which can be an issue if you're playing this on a functional potato like I wasThings to Come and Why You May Want to Wait•Not a ton of locations to explore, but it was revealed SodaDen is working on more areas in a 1.2 patch•The End Game is as close to nothing as you can achieve: once your village and the world is in harmony, you really are just farming and raising a family•Nothing to do with the World's economy in your leather pouch besides decorate some spots around town or build infinite farms•So many beautiful and useful buildings that don't come into play until the last section of the gameConclusion and Arbitrary Score: 9/10•The game is an extremely friendly farming sim that can be enjoyed by Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley lovers, or by new players to the genre who have an itch to grow some prehistoric cabbage and squash•Some players may see the gameplay as very stale if they are used to Stardew, but there is a fair amount that is dissimilar enough that you should be able to enjoy the gameplay loop on a different spectrum•I bought this on sale, but it is easily worth $40. There is more content in development, but also a major push to move this to consoles as well if you would prefer it there.

_childDocuments_.review: This game typically is compared to Stardew Valley. I agree with comparison, given both the minute to minute gameplay, but also the longer term gameplay. However, essentially every aspect of this game is an evolution and improvement on Stardew Valley.Everything from the fishing mechanics, which is the best i have tried in any game, to the fertilizer system and domestication system of the crop growing, to the way technology is developed, which is also some of the best tech mechanic i have ever tried in a game, to the massive upgrade to the cave gameplay. And then the general purpose of the game, helping your settlement prosper, also just makes what you do feel purposeful and connected to the actual gameplay.It also feels like Roots Of Pacha has taken many lessons from Stardew Valley and made huge improvements to the quality of life of the player. A lot of small annoyances are removed, and stuff has been made more convenient.TLDR; If you liked Stardew Valley, or any other games from this genre, this game is an absolute MUST!

_childDocuments_.review: Lets start off by saying Life/Farming Sim games are a staple for me; I've been on board since Harvest Moon 64, and while a lot of people roll their eyes at all the 'Stardew Clones' these days (as ppl call it, I don't feel this way personally, Roots of Pacha is unique enough I don't feel it's a clone at all!) I've been living in my own form of game heaven for the past few years. Still having fun and playing in Sun Haven, I was excited for Roots of Pacha and had been hyped for it for months leading up to the release - so I may be a biased party here.Pros:+ The art style is beautiful! Both portraits for characters, pixels, and UI menus.+ It feels super fresh to go out and discover new seeds, learn more about them. I'm not just reading from the shop description 'carrots take 4 days', I have to learn that over time by farming enough carrots to learn about them.+ Taming animals feels super cute and fun! I have a pet wolf and a boar I ride around!+ Customization of both my village and plot layout is already high, and I'm only up to Summer+ I really like seeing the village grow around me, and sometimes without me. The village will learn technologies and make the village home with upgrades (both useful and cosmetic), and it isn't totally dependent on me! I feel like the village actually cares about things getting better.+ I was gonna put 'stamina drains too fast' as a con, but I'm seeing accessories already that will buff that, and there are a lot of options for restoring stamina pretty easily - like Vegetable Stew and Fish.+ Congrats on making a fishing mini game I actually like, while there's nothing wrong with them I wasn't a huge fan of Story of Seasons, Stardew, or Sun Haven's 'bar that goes back and forth' game, and usually modded them to a one click catch.+ And more!! I'm still early in the game so there's lots left, I've read there's domestication of animals?? I have a quest for breeding I haven't finished yet, and other things.Cons:- Time goes way too fast, but since I'm still early game I'm giving it the benefit of the doubt for the moment; I don't want to burn through all the stuff to do, and get burnt out.- I learned Animal Medicine before I had the ability to make Oil, so I had a sick Ipex just sitting there for a week or more until I felt guilty enough that I released it.- The savanna is so big, why is it so big, I'm lost, aaaaa- ... wait, is that it?? Uh-- wow. Okay.Other notes; my one favorite thing in these games is having kids and seeing them grow, so I did get excited to see that a future patch may add more life stages. As it is, what I've read said this version (1.0) does have marriage and 2 kids that grow to infancy, so that's awesome!

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, let's get this out of the way: this is a Stardew Valley game. By that, I mean that it shares the same beats that make SV the ultimate farming life-sim:- seasonal farming with basic agriculture staples (various tool levels, fertilizer, animal husbandry, etc)- an assortment of people you can discover and/or romance- gifts and newer tools gated behind community milestones and friendship levels- a semi supernatural story that asks you to follow a checklist of deliverables and events in order to offer endgame rewards (and an "ending" of sorts)Where Pacha differs is in its approach to the system: you are at the very beginning of humanity and things that seem regular for most farm-sims have yet to be invented. You'll learn how to develop agriculture from finding seeds in the wilds (the game only unlocks seeds for purchase once you found them and unlocked a seed store), learn to domesticate animals, discover irrigation, etc. Tiers in farm sims is a necessary evil, even if it often takes you out of the gameplay due to how misaligned it is with what you're doing. Pacha here solves this by gating things behind actions that make sense: of course domesticating animals will lead to learning to ride animals. Of course gathering animal fur will lead to inventing a spindle whorl. New solutions bring new problems which in turn lead to new solutions.But you're not doing the solving yourself: the community does. Pacha believes in collaboration and it has based its in-game economy on this. You don't accumulate currency: instead, whatever you contribute to your clan raises the clan's prosperity and awards you contribution points, a unit you can use to barter with other people. It makes it so that it's not just about getting rich, it's about pushing the community to reach milestones from which new ideas are sprung. It's an effective way to handle what would otherwise be a weird disconnect where you're a cave person but also a capitalist somehow? Here, it makes sense.Add to this the various traditional mini-games like fishing, mining, discovering magic things, solving puzzles, etc and it's a serious contender for a SV spiritual successor (or... ancestor? Get it?).Unfortunately, like most farm sims, it starts to stall once you're nearing the end. Most discoveries have rendered the menial work so efficient that you run out of things to do quickly. And what's left is heavily gated behind scarce materials that you should always strive to find any time possible (seriously, hoard any hardwood you find and plant Beech trees ASAP). A bit of a shame because it really feels like a wall whose only purpose is to slow down gameplay while you continue grinding friendship. Speaking of, friendship decays FAST here and does not ever stop decaying so keep talking and dancing with everyone every day...What else is there to say... Music is excellent, art style is definitely unique, the message is super positive and the writing, while a bit simple at times, carries that message extremely well. We are indeed better together. Speaking of which, coop exists here.So if you're looking for a SV replacement that isn't too dissimilar, same vibes with a bit of history lessons thrown in a very hands-on way, look no further!

_childDocuments_.review: After sinking roughly 10hrs into Roots of Pacha already, and having played some during the kickstarter beta, I am amazed at how this game has turned out. The music alone gives the game a very laid back feeling, and with the lack of combat I would say it's more relaxed than Stardew Valley. In my opinion I would not say Roots of Pacha is better than Stardew, I would say it stands equal to it. The animal breeding and crop domesticating mechanics are a nice twist as I've enjoyed watching the crop and animal sprites change from their wild counterparts. The festivals and events have been fun.
