_childDocuments_.review: I was really surprised by how much I enjoyed this game. I was looking for a game that had the same farmer, mining, relationship building thing that Stardew has and this one was the best by far. After playing, I feel bad for comparing it to Stardew because this game stands great on its own, adding a new spin on the story and game mechanics that makes it stand out from other games while still excelling in aspects that we've all come to expect from a farming RPG. I'd also say that it's even more relaxing than Stardew.I've played about 40 hours and I've about reached the end of the game. The story and gameplay itself was very entertaining and I like the time that it took to "complete" the game (at least the story part). There wasn't any grinding, and the game does a good job pacing the progression of the story with the town contributions, ideas, and mine abilities so it's not boring or rushed. It was just 40 hours of fun gaming and constant, steady progress. I appreciated that there also fast travel introduced early in the game to also cut down on the walking. Diving into the mines was the highlight of the game for me. It's not just a linear path, that you have to break rocks constantly to go down a deeper floor or farm for ore, but a maze of different rooms where you can choose which direction to go down. The totem mechanics and puzzles make it interesting as well, giving hints that the player may return to the room after some time in order to gain access to it. The puzzles themselves aren't challenging, but I appreciate their existence and place in the story. I like how the mine itself comes with a story and that's why I was always looking forward to going and progressing, instead of it being like a chore. I also appreciate not having to fight monsters through clicks.Roots of Pacha really hit it out of the park with the NPCs and how to build relationships with them. The dialogue was never stale: everyday the characters had new little tidbits to share which made it fun to talk to them. I really liked that a lot of times NPCs would share information about what other NPCs liked or disliked as gifts - I just find it so annoying to have to look up what to gift an NPC and putting it in dialogue further made talking to them more meaningful. There's also a good amount of cutscenes for all of the characters. NPC relationships is a common aspect that I feel like a lot of games don't complete to satisfaction, so it's really great to see the devs put focus and effort here to make the world seem more alive. The whole game is about exploration and the devs do a great job in making exploring engaging and fun without being frustrating. The maps are done well where you can see where all the things you've already discovered are and the different areas you can explore are different and big enough where exploring to find new seeds or gatherables is satisfying. Even the dialogues kind of cater to the exploration, since they give hints on facts about the NPCs. I also like that they did a different mechanic to the fishing game, where you follow the fish instead of the whole "click when it's in the green bar" thing, At first I was a little put off, because the game kind of walks the line of being relaxing or just being boring with the lack of challenge, but I appreciated it more as faster fish were discovered. Its still not challenging, but I like that: it fits in with the whole relaxing vibe. The other kind of minigame would just frustrate me. I don't have any complaints about the game. It was well worth the price and the 40+ hours was well paced and filled with story and fun. If I had to give a critique, it would be the whole farming thing seems a bit unbalanced to me. Now that I'm towards the end there's been a little bit of grinding, just because I think I may have invested a lot of time in diving into the mines (because they were amazing), and a little less time in producing stuff to gain contribution for the village, so now I need to catch up to buy the things I need to move forward. The fishing game isn't challenging, so it's not really something I look forward doing for the whole day. Farming takes up time and the different ways to process food items is cool, but at this point when I can only focus on building upgrades and getting max stats on the animals, a lot of the big stuff like getting a large house, barn, or even furnishing the house each takes 10,000+ contributions when daily I only get 1-2,000.  To be fair, this could be by design or because of how I played the game with focusing on the mines. I know the devs already made some QoL changes to it, but I still think there may be room for improvement. I'm very excited to see the bigger updates adding content and expanding the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Stardew Valley, but Pre-historic. The game is super neat, and very fun, with likable NPCS, plenty of things to grow and animals to befriend. My favourite part being the "Ideas" mechanic, since you're basically the first farmer/rancher ever, you have to invent new tools, and buildings to make farming/ranching easier, with the help of your fellow clan members. Great game that deserves to be played if you enjoy Life-Sim or Farm-Sim games. All this needs is Stardew level mod support and it'll be a 11/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is a super great, cozy, cute game very similar to Stardew Valley but in a paleolithic era. However there are plenty of features that make it different, I love how as time passes the clan and your player character make discoveries that can make your life easier. One being the idea of calendars and clocks. As you grow plants you domesticate them and you have to tame wild animals in order to have animal products. You also have an influence over where clan buildings are placed which allows you to arrange certain buildings around your home if you don't want to go running across the land to find what you need.The other villagers have so many details and stories to learn about with their own relationships. You also get to witness many fun traditions, festivals, and religious views. Pacha is a fictional god that your clan follows, but later on you meet other clans that follow other gods which creates tension between them. Not to mention there is a ton of different looks between the villagers and yourself. I recommend if you're in search of something like Stardew Valley or Animal Crossing.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The beginning feels like a very fun and laid laid back Stardew Valley. I particularly liked the somewhat limited amount of foraging and exploration.Up to a certain point the village feels extremely immersive and unique.  Further into the game it feels like a slog, since you've seen and heard everything before.It's feels like it lacks content towards the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a solid farming game. It includes all aspects you'd expect from a farming game and does them well. There is ranching, mining, quests, fishing, marriage (union), and crafting. All the characters look cool and represent a broad range of ancient cultures. I didn't pay too much attention to their dialogue or backstory, though. None of the mechanics are groundbreaking or too complicated, but some are kind of tedious. As another reviewer said, you have to click each individual fermenter/keg/etc to obtain your product. When you have a ton of those processors, it is very time consuming to load and unload them. That said, I didn't personally see any glaring issues with this game that prevented me from enjoying it. Did I love it? No, but I definitely enjoyed it. I don't know if I'd give it a second playthrough - I think once is enough and you've experienced it all. I think I finished the main story around 40-50 hours in, then the rest was just getting 100% completion. Another thing that stood out to me was a lack of end-game content. To my knowledge, there is no extra stuff to do in the cave, more expensive stuff to buy, or any further challenges. Once you complete all prophecies and unlock the tree, that's about it unless you want to go for 100%. You go from having new quests every couple days to having absolutely none. For anyone wanting to get all achievements, I highly recommend using the guides available on Steam. Many of the pages I found on the Roots of Pacha Wiki were out of date and/or flat out wrong. For example, the Wiki said I had to get substantial flowers (friendship points) with like 15+ villagers to get cooking recipes. I'm not sure if that was true in past versions, but, I believe only one Pachan villager gives a recipe from friendship points (Era). There are six recipes from the other two tribes. All other cooking recipes are learned automatically when you buy kitchen upgrades.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't find the game engaging. There are a lot of characters but they're not distinctive enough to be memorable, and they barely have any interesting dialogue and there no conversations like in Stardew Valley. Someone might say it's unfair to compare RoP to Stardew Valley but Stardew was created by one guy.Roots of Pacha does have some neat ideas. There's a research system of sorts. A tribesmember will come up with an idea like a sundial. You give them resources to experiment with their idea then you have the sundial built which gives you a more accurate clock. Great idea.There's a fishing mini-game. I like it better than Stardew's. Basically you equip your stone tool (I forget its exact name) and start fishing. You see a couple of fish swimming around and you keep your cursor above the fish. A charging bar of sorts fills up and when it's full you click to catch the fish. Unlike Stardew time passes while all this is happening which I suppose makes sense but I think time should stop.You can tame wild animals via a mini-game. You get a bone flute, go up to a wild animal and start the mini-game. A series of tunes play and you have to click on the beat. As someone with little musical skill I had no issue with timings. My only complaint is that this flute somehow has charges to it, you can only tame four animals a day.As expected there is no money per se but there is a currency in the form of tribal contributions. Cooked fish seems to be the most valuable items to contribute for points. You then use these points to buy some items like seeds and backpack upgrades.There are areas you can visit. You start out with the forest enabled then later you get access to the savanna, the jungle and the beach. Some of these areas are inhabited by other small tribes that are completely forgettable.  These tribes mention another tribe that are allegedly dangerous but there doesn't seem to be any combat so I don't know what's up with that.There's mining but it's not as interesting as Stardew's mines. There's magical creatures (sound familiar?) that help you navigate the mines but that's about it.There is no skill progression. You can't specialize in ranching, farming or angling so your character doesn't grow as a person.Roots of Pacha is by no means a bad game but it lacks a soul, something to make it truly standout outside of the shadow of Stardew Valley.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Great piece of art. Labor of love. Good for people like me who just want to relax while playing. There is (so far) no combat, and only mini-games based on timing to perform tasks. Excellent pacing as features are unlocked by time and earned by discovery. Everything is earned: better seeds, new tools, animal friends, faster travel, even time. I hope this gets added to and improved upon for years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Stardew Valley and hoped I would love this the same. I did for the first while but the more I played the more the sheen rubbed off. This game is so close to being up there with Stardew but a bunch of small issues for me ended up piling into making it not fun enough to stick with:- The characters just aren’t as interesting- While I can’t quite put my finger on why, the repetitive tasks in this game felt so much more tedious than in Stardew- The Economy seems broken with fishing being more valuable than just about anything else
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Got this to play co-op and some of the design choices are just strange.  Money and seeds are shared and so are some tools, but others aren't.  Some quests require everyone to be be present, so we'd all have to stop what we were doing or plan our day around them.  Other quests are first come, first serve, with no way for the other players to see what was said.  It just feels really off.  It's cute and probably a fine single player game, but after the first 90 minutes we just felt like we were constantly having our fun interrupted.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a Blast with friends. Currently doing a 'Not a Date Night' play through with a friend and its been so much fun. The art is so wonderful, The music you can't help but bop to as you run around. Riding the animals is a blast. Game feels amazing on a high refresh rate monitor @ 144hz as well as still feel amazing and responsive @ 60hz. All in all a 10/10 in my book Definitely will be a staple comfy couples game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The game never manages to feel compelling. Its systems are competently made, but they lack soul and there is no real driver to what you do in the game. There’s a distinct lack of rewards in the game that act as a carrot on a stick for the player to follow. Despite having all the hallmarks of the genre, like: building and decorating a home, marriage and family, friendships, and exploration, it just never really builds to anything substantive. And the currency for getting those rewards makes it feel like a ton of work with little to show for it.The progression just feels broken for some reason. It isn’t just the fact that progression happens outside of the player’s input, which I actually kind of like. It is that this progression is very stilted and the rewards never feel meaningful and they are completely enshrouded. You never really know what you are capable of building towards because it relies on an “Idea” system whereby discoveries are made by your fellow tribe members, but it isn’t like there is a roadmap for you to follow. With something like Stardew, you know what to expect and what you could potentially build towards. And worse than all of that is that the contribution points you need for getting those rewards are so arbitrary in their value that certain activities feel largely pointless and others give massive rewards, but are incredibly tedious, like fishing. The NPCs are nice and there are various pleasant scenes involving them, but they just never really stood out too much to me. They can be charming, but I don’t feel like I’ll ever recall anything special about them.The game could definitely be described as cozy, but perhaps too much. I try to play the game and put time into it, but I generally end up feeling so bored after a day or two in-game that I have to put it down. I sometimes forget I’ve even been playing the game and then I see it in my Steam list and think “Oh! I was playing that.” There are a lot of people that really like the game and find it quite compelling, so your opinion could differ quite a lot from mine. My takeaway is that the game is just okay. It is something to pass the time with, but when I end up feeling even more bored after playing it than I did before playing it….well, that’s not exactly high praise. And I’m so conflicted on giving it a positive or negative review review. The game, at best, is a 5/10 erring slightly above the 5, I’d hazard. And no more. And with how boring it is, I just can't in good conscience rate it positively.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, so fun. A bit more on-the-rails than Stardew Valley with the storyline you pretty much have to follow so you can unlock areas and tech. Lots of choices and ways to focus your character (i.e. focus more on farming, fishing, gathering, or fishing) depending on how you spend your limited time. Very polished gameplay and beautiful art. Definitely recommend, if you like farming sims.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: 8/10A refreshing take on the farming sim genre. I loved the feeling of progressing through the learning system, it was a easy way to get into all of the systems without being overwhelmed all at once. The relationships were pretty shallow (although, I have not played since release). The big winner is the aesthetic of the game, very cute and cozy! My only complaint was that I felt like I was finishing the game too quickly, which led me to stop playing because I hate ending things, haha.Definitely recommend for any cozy game enjoyers!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: My absolute favourite Game in a long time!So this Game is just a GEM in the world of farming sims!It's developed by only a few people and it's full of love, I don't know if i will  be able to list all of the amazing stuff this game has to offer, but i will talk about a few things that made this game so amazing for me! <3The pixelart in this game is just outstanding, all the little animations the animals and characters have, i can't praise it enough! ( i mean, the wolves nibbling on their bones? The little piglets wobbling their nose while sleeping? THATS JUST SO ADORABLE!)The Game has a LOT to discover in forms of the world, find new places, exploring the caves and mine there, find new crops, animals, fish, ways of working and so much more! And yes, it can be overwhelming for some people that there is just SO MUCH content to discover for the fact, that it is "only a little pixel art game", but it is just really going nuts on longterm content and thats just so amazing! It does take some time to play fully through the game but tbh, isn't that what we want from a farming game? Taking your time to play through a cozy game, it's just the best feeling to still discover new things after already +130hours into this game.Just don't get scared that you won't speedrun this game in 24 hours. It is a really cozy longterm game and you have all time in the world to discover everything this game has to offer, there is no rush at all, you can do EVERYTHING in your own pace, just enjoy, relax and notice how the world around you slowly changes!  <3The characters in this game are so lovely, it takes a whole lot of time until the phrases they say start to repeat, if im being honest, i haven't dicovered that time yet even tho im in the second year ingame. Just so much love from the writers, i love it!! There's so much more to say about this game but it's just too much. Im even more involved in this game then in stardew valley, just because i like the way the game treats their animals, crops and late game romance content. It's just so much content and original ideas, i just wish i could live in this world for real!Also the music is outstanding! It even fits the circle of the day in every world so you can recognize through the music how late it is, thats just pure love for detail right there!!So yeah, I don't even know how to express all my love for this little studio that made this game, i just hope that they know that they made at least one person out there the happiest one alive with their game! <3Definitly buy if you want a game, that you can spend just as much hours in like in Stradew Valley :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I don’t normally write reviews, but intentionally went into this game with plans to write one after so I could do  my small part in helping spread awareness of this game and help others in making an informed decision on whether or not they should purchase it.  I enjoyed my time with this game and definitely think it’s worth purchasing despite my handful of complaints- but it does have some issues that need to be worked out at some point in the future.-Everything about the game, from the artwork to the music, is beautiful. Seriously, so well made. I’d say more about it but honestly other reviews have worded my thoughts about this particular point much better than I could.-The characters are beyond charming, and as I progressed through the game and got to know them, I genuinely began to feel as if I was part of a community that saw each other as one big family. Something other farming/life sim games often lack. In Pacha, characters aren’t just vendors who exist for your convenience- they each have their own lives and opinions of one another. I also appreciate how quickly your relationships progress with them as well. In other games it usually takes a while to build your relationship with a character, but you can earn 1 or 2 hearts a week in this game through the various interactions you can have with them. -The story is simple but enjoyable. I loved how much the village grows and changes as you continue to contribute to your little village. It’s a visual reminder of how much your contribution to your community helps it.-I enjoy the variety of tamable animals (which each have multiple color swatches) found throughout the game. Animal breeding to try and get perfect stats was also entertaining.-”Money-making” as it currently stands is widely unbalanced. For example, the profit you earn from farming and animals, which SHOULD be the primary way you earn “money” in this game, pale in comparison to what you make from fishing. And while I enjoyed the fishing mini-game a lot when I first started my play through, it quickly became tedious when I was forced to play it for hours because it was the only viable way to make the “money” I needed to achieve my goals in game. Needs a rework for sure. Did confirm you get more the higher the level the crop! :)-If you’re like me and were hoping to adopt a sabertooth as a pet as soon as you found out they were in game, you’ll be disappointed to hear that you can only adopt the babies as pets and they never grow up. This makes sense for animals like Mammoths- who realistically wouldn’t be able to fit inside your house. But adult sabertooth’s don’t have that same problem. Not a deal breaker, but it was a bit of a let down. -The rate of debris respawn across your fields at the end of the month/season is honestly tragic. Even with food to replenish stamina, it took me from late fall to mid winter to clear out the largest field in the game. Every few days, debris would respawn and cover large chunks of it, which was annoying, but manageable. But then when year 2 began, I was horrified to discover that ALL the work I spent in the previous seasons was rendered completely pointless--- because the ENTIRE field was covered from top and bottom again and completely unusable. It looked exactly like it did at the very beginning of the game and I was so disheartened I closed the game immediately. I’m hoping it’s just a bug and it’ll be patched eventually.-I think the character customization at the beginning of the game is super well done- but I was a little disappointed that hair came in every color of the rainbow EXCEPT pink. There’s red, magenta, light purple- but no pink. This is a much more superficial complaint that has no impact on anyone besides me and a handful of others who are equally obsessed with this color- I just wish I had the aesthetic cherry on top of my ice cream sundae.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game if you are looking for a cozy relaxing farming sim. if you had a hard time with the fishing mechanic in stardew valley then you will have an easier time with this game, ontop of that there are lots of cute little rhythm games to play and the animal raising is alot more in depth then stardew. just a little note of warning to new players, the game doesn't make this very clear but you shouldn't spend too much time gardening in your first year. Automatic watering systems aren't available until later on and if you are like me you will think making the biggest profit possible year one is a great idea but I accidentally ended up upgrading/unlocking everything except irrigation in my first year and now do not have much to spend my currency on. Other then finishing catching every fish, maybe decorating my farm/the village and getting the rare coloured animals theres not much else to do in the game for late game content. It feels like there is the intention of possibly adding more content later on? either way if you decide to play, for your first play through I really recommend exploring first and getting to know the villagers before you start large scale farming.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Wasn't so sure about it when it first came out but the devs have steadily been making this project a real stand-out game in a massively over-saturated market. The most recent 1.2 release and the upcoming 1.3 means it's never been a better time to start playing it!I find the new addition of the wolf mounts to be awesome.The much needed Q.O.L upgrades, such as transferring matching items from inventory to storage & the early game sprinkler system have made this game so much better too!I also just found out they previously added a day-speed option, which currently maxes at 20 mins per in-game day, giving us ample time to do our daily tasks.Going forward I would love a craft from storage option, especially for cooking.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game. Definitely draws inspiration from Harvest Moon and Stardew Valley, but has its own voice, style, and merits. I only played single player, so I can't comment on the multiplayer experience, but I have really enjoyed the single player experience.I absolutely love how alive the clan feels. It's a big family, everyone working together, coming up with new ideas, improving the village together. I like that the NPCs will periodically do things on their own to improve things without your involvement, making it feel less like "I am the main character" and more like "I am a part of something bigger".I was impressed by how many different lines of dialogue each character has, to where I feel like I rarely have encountered repeated lines outside of specific scenarios (e.g. asking someone about an idea they're currently working on). I'm happy with the variety of romantic interests, and that same sex relationships are a thing even among the NPCs. The music is great. The art style is cute (though more clothing options would be nice).My only real complaint is that the farming is tedious and time consuming at the beginning, but it sounds like they're going to be improving that in a future update. The fact that they are still pushing out updates and improvements is promising. I feel comfortable giving this one a recommend even at full price. I've had a lot of fun with it and I can see myself returning to it for subsequent play-throughs, which isn't something I do with a lot of games. Wonderful game; I'm excited to see what these devs do in the future..
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I have never played such a complete game that isn't even done updating itself yet. Most games that come out of Alpha are unable to do what they've promised, but this one? A whole different story for the better. I'm glad to have backed this kickstarter and I hope that this game continues to thrive. It truly can be as big as Stardew Valley as long as the consistency in quality stays in place.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I adore this game!!! For a really long time I've been grieving playing Stardew Valley for the first time (I wish I could wipe my memory clean and play it again - it was the first real computer game I ever played and helped me through a v tough time), and I couldn't find any game that came remotely close (apart from maybe Dinkum but I did get bored because I binge played it in beta mode). Roots of Pacha has filled the hole of the game I was craving. I love it so much, I LOVE the animal breeding and the exploring different landscapes and finding new seeds. It brings me so much joy! Thank you :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Game really has a lot of potential.. but I can't in good faith recommend it. In one word, overwhelming. Didn't feel like I had a proper tutorial to introduce me to various game mechanics, and instead was thrown into the vast open world where it seemed like I was unlocking more and more without being guided on what to do. The debris in the field even respawned wayyy too fast overnight. There's a singular tool for pretty much everything, with the upgrades not really worth much in my opinion since I can't break grass or fish without the first tool (handaxe) after five hours into the game? With all that said, the game is beautifully made, especially the cutscenes, maps & pixel art style which is gorgeous. Will be keeping an eye on this one as it's hopefully going to be updated in the future!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having so much fun in this game. :) It brings enough new elements to the farming sim genre that it feels fresh and different from most of the formulaic farming sims I've played (i.e. you've been left this plot of land, grow crops and make money and restore the farm). I especially love the animal taming/mini rhythm game, the fact that you can forage seeds for free so there's no inherent need to make "money" really, the variety of animals, the fishing mechanic (since there aren't fishing rods!!!) the community/working together as a clan & ~contributing to a greater whole~ thing, and lastly how the music never gets annoying (imo). The pixel art is charming and the character profile pixel portraits are really nice. The story also has great pacing and has cutscenes appear quite often so you never find yourself stuck or at a loss for what to do. It's a breath of fresh air from some of the farming/cozy games I've played lately. I love it! tldr;If you like farming sims and want something that feels different, this game rocks. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game recently from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Such a great game! Has a lot of familiar features from other farming games like Harvest Moon/Stardew Valley, but also has a LOT of cool innovative features. I was a Kickstarter alpha backer and it was awesome to see this game grow - I had over 67 hours played before release, and just sunk in another 4 today! The characters are fun, dialogue is fresh, and it's just a cool take on one of my most loved game genres.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A very fresh take on the Stardew Valley-type farming sim but with a lot of great ideas and mechanics that make this game imminently playable! I love the tribal lifestyle and all of the accurate flora and fauna you can start planting and raising and eventually domesticating. I love all of the interesting tribal lore that you learn piece by piece through storytelling and cave paintings to keep you engaged. I like that you can mine for useful rocks and minerals such as flint and various gemstones that you can have a tribal craftsman fashion into  jewelry that gives you stat boosts. I love that you can create your own paintings a la cave-style to decorate your tent, which is upgradeable. I like the idea system that has your fellow tribesman coming up with ways to advance in knowledge adding useful technology to your farm such as irrigation, much to the benefit of you and the tribe. On top of that, there's just a ton of QoL improvements from other games in the genre and it's clear this a big labor of love from devs who are clearly game players. A game that honors its Stardew roots but branches off in its own, unique direction. If you like the genre of pixelated farming sims, you owe it to yourself to pickup and try Roots of Pacha.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A feature-rich full game release with no EA purgatory that brings something fun and new to an overly saturated genre?? In this economy???It's no secret that the farming sim market is saturated, and to my bank account's chagrin, I've bought and played them all. Most feel derivative, either just remakes of old games that rely on nostalgia goggles or cash grabs by half-baked studios that push out unfinished glop after years in EA. There's still a mad dash as studios try to fumble their way into Stardew Valley-esque success by making minor visual adjustments while copy/pasting the same formula.Thankfully, Roots of Pacha is NOT that. RoP sets itself apart with intention, and brings to light just how repetitive and monotonous the other farming sim titles truly are. It feels fresh and engaging, and is just *fun*. I have so much trouble tearing myself away - the world and mechanics are fascinating, I genuinely love my clan, and I FINALLY feel those early-days Stardew vibes of giddy curiosity again.There's a real sense of progression as you watch your village develop. There's always a new idea or event right around the corner that break up what can be a one-note gameplay loop. The village feels alive, and the villagers take an active role in community building rather than just waiting for you to fix everything. The characters so far all have unique traits and engaging personalities, and the cutscenes I've seen so far were wonderful for adding even more context to their behavior. My one bit of advice would be: people who don't love mini-games, you might struggle with this one, because they are frequent. I love them and the way they break up the rest of the gameplay, but it's worth pointing out.To me, this is the only new farming sim worth playing. Buy it, you need it. It deserves WAY more attention than it's getting.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A great game, honestly.Similar to  the titan and current leader of the genre of cozy farming sims, however it puts a good twist on things, plus its not even finished! Devs want to add loads of more content for which I am excited!-Progression is buttery smooth, there is no lapse in tempo, nothing to slow down the game to a crawl it keeps going and going and going and--Early on you get the option to tame and ride animals. Any animal. I ride on top of a boar for most of the time and it looks cool. Also your first tool is a multitool used on everything from fishing to mining, very cool!-Inventory: by FAR the BEST inventory system I have seen for these games and its not even close! Seeds? separate inventory with infinite slots with a . Tools? Yep, separate tool bar which is completely customizable as well. Normal inventory? Three separate hotbars you can cycle through with TAB. MASTERFULY DONE. I cant praise the inventory and UI of this game enough it really is a -NPCs show on maps! Need to gift someone anything on their birthday? Look on the map and you will find them instantly no problem.-As much as I like to praise it there are a couple of things that diminish the experience quite a bit.-Friendship decay: for some reason, there is friendship decay in this game, meaning, if you dont speak to an NPC for multiple days in a row their friendship will slowly decay and you have to regain it. (This issue is fixed by installing a simple mod from nexusmods!)-Polygamy: Honestly? Not a con for most for sure but it is simply strange. I get it, ooga booga caveman days and all that but really? it gets weird. (you can date every npc simultaneously while being married as well lol)-Animal taming system: It needs more clarity. In the game there are legendary animals that spawn after a certain ammount of that animal was  by you, which actually means-> taming the animal-> INVITING the animal to live with you. Not enough clarity so if you dont research this before hand you could waste a lot of time.Fun game with unique aspects, i left out most of them cause its more fun to actually experience them. Unique game with lots of replayability and my god, the UI is too good. Also soundtrack is a bop.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I played this multiplayer on nights where I was tired but wanted some wholesome entertainment. It was perfect for just that.The negative reviews of this game largely make complaints about the nature of it ; it is a low energy, slow burn,  very low stakes survival game set in a primitive universe. You can make plenty of meaningful, fulfilling progress in the game while enjoying everything it has to offer. You will not enjoy this game if you are unable to appreciate pacing that is slightly slower to that of Stardew Valley.While it is similar to Stardew Valley, Roots of Pacha is distinctly different in multiple ways, including the gift economy present in the game. Your choices strengthen and/or weaken the social contract you have with you tribe, and you are not punished for making mistakes. There is no "electively" homeless Linus or poverty stricken Pam to worry about, everybody has a home, a meal and whatever they need in this universe. There is something comforting about this, which provides a sense of ease not found in Stardew Valley.Also, bonus points for queer and polyamorous options, historically fitting *and* inclusive for the modern world. If you like cosy games and/or you are some flavour of queer and/or communist then you should get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I really wanted to love Roots of Pacha. I was excited for It for a while and bought It eagerly within the hour of It releasing. It was looking so hopeful, the game's customisation Is great, the art style Is GORGEOUS, the sprites and map and everything look amazing, the music Is great and It controls just fine! However a big Issue with the game Is just boring. I always get so addicted to farming games and find myself entranced for hours, always having new plans I want to achieve and things I want to do, but In this game, I just felt like I never knew what to do. It feels really lame In a way, like there's these cool areas of the map to unlock and explore, but you don't get to contribute to any of that at all, It's just automatically done for you, within a REALLY short timespan of the game too, like you don't feel like you're ever contributing to anything important that's ever going on In the world, and It feels like It takes away HUGE motives to keep playing the game. I feel like you'd really want to keep playing to discover new things, but that's removed from you within a week or 2 of In game time.It also feels SLOW, like you're forced Into playing a slow playstyle for no reason. You get quests to give people Items In order to unlock things, but then they have a community point requirement on top of that In order to unlock It. Why? Why not give the quest when you have those points first, or why have the requirement at all? It feels like It's only there to slow your game to a crawl or pointlessly pad out game time and make It even more boring. That makes things take forever, then you have to wait 2 days to unlock the object, and even then you might need to wait several more days to unlock the items you need off the object you just built and just ugh.. It's exhausting.I don't personally find any of the characters Interesting personality wise, and dating feels boring, I don't think any of the characters are that good looking, but that might just be a personal preference. I never really got too far Into dating though so I can't comment on It too much. It's just another system that feels dragged out Into feeling like It's taking FOREVER. I talk to my interest and gift them whenever I can, and barely had any heart progression.Days feel like they fly past sometimes, like you get your basic farm care done, but If you're exploring caves, It always feels like the day has gone half-way by, by the time you get In them, then you have no time to explore when you're there. The caves feel so long and confusing and maze like, and are just WAY too complicated for their own good, not to mention some of the back tracking you're expected to do, I couldn't even remember or figure out where to go by the time I unlocked what I needed for an earlier segment. You also run out of stamina EXTREMELY fast and It's just a slog to get through, restoring stamina Is clunky too, you have to right click food, but It only works If you're stood and facing a certain angle for some reason? Also upgrading tools feels sorta like.. bad? It's like you upgrade a tool to do double power, but It also takes double stamina from you, so you kinda feel weaker when you upgrade things, Idk If this Is a bug but It's really weird If It's intentional. Caves are so confusing though, and when It's time to go home, a lot of time you'll be exploring and It'd be so zig-zaggy and long to go back to your last checkpoint to leave that sometimes you feel like you need to progress forward to find a new one, and you never know when that can be, It's just way too convoluted. Shrine transformation animations always take FOREVER and getting to any of the 3 cave entrances are also taking forever, they are all SO far away from your home.Farming In this game felt pointless. Animals AND crops. Aside from being a mount, I didn't really get the point of animals, and crops felt like a waste of time. They make barely any money at all and just never felt like they served a purpose. The only way me and my co-op friend made money basically was from fishing and cooking them, then selling them, which Is extremely boring, the fishing mini game sucks a lot In this game.TLDR: There's a lot of little Issues In this game, I'm probably forgetting a lot more right now, but I'll leave It at that. This game Is definitely for someone out there. If you like slow drawn out farming games, where you just chill and do menial tasks, and don't care too much about progressing quickly, you will probably enjoy the game. It has gorgeous graphics, music and environment. I think the devs did put a lot of heart Into the game, It just doesn't seem like MY type of farming game.If you hate really slow and forced dragged out gameplay, that's It really. There's many problems, the main one just being It's BORING. It's unfortunate, I wanted to love the game, and I do still appreciate my time with It and that I gave It a go, I just wish there was some changes to It that took away all these barriers that slow the gameplay to a crawl, and I think I could like the game a lot more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I am a big Harvest Moon / Stardew Valley fan. This game feels unique yet familiar at the same time. I really enjoy the sense of community and township! The ideas / requests / quests that the other villagers provide you are fulfilling and keep the game going. You feel like you are always working towards a goal to build the community and not just make a ton of "money". Also... no money. You donate items to the clan and depending on what the items is "worth" you get clan points to spend / trade / upgrade. This is an amazing concept because you are also helping the community thrive with the points you provide. The clan will build, upgrade and get bigger as times goes on. Also... A ton of different crops and a BUNCH of animals. You can breed the animals to get specific trait increase from the parents such as speed or productivity. it keeps track of generations. I absolutely adore this title. The music, atmosphere, ambiance and graphics are perfect. If someone in the tribe starts playing a flute... you can hear it going along with the background music. If you like Stardew Valley / Harvest Moon this will amaze and please you. I can't want to try multiplayer!!! This will definitely be a title that I will play, follow and watch as it grows. I hope for updates!!! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: It's absolutely delightful- One of the few things I've ever kickstarter backed, and I'm so glad I did. The gameplay is fun, and the vibes are comfy.Inspiration from other games in the genre show through in a unique way that doesn't make it feel derivative, rather adds onto base expectations for the genre in a fun way.The music is enjoyable, and while there's a little less freedom for placing buildings than I'd prefer, the pre-set locations are solid and it's not a big deal.The devs also care, and are quick to respond to questions in their discord, and I'm looking forward to seeing where the game goes from here!Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Love it.Love the fact that you have to tame animals instead of buying, so you can just tame adult animals instead of waiting for them to grow from a baby and have the items faster.Love how there are other little clans out there, which make the festivals and events pretty fun to do (and man, those events are hella unique).Thought it was hella funny that you fish by hitting them with a rock.Really love the trading system. Like, actual trade item for item and not money (which makes sense since cavemen).Theres a lot more that I love.Also, since I kinda made my little character kinda look like my stardew one, i have a little headcanon that this clan is the ancestor to the stardew villagers.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful pixel art, gorgeous music, well-written characters and a great progression system! _childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: 60+ hours into the game, I think I can safely say that I love it and that it's a great game. I am usually not that into pixel art, but I make an exception for exeptional games like Stardew Valley and Roots of Pacha. I hope I have a lot left to discover, because it is absolutely charming and very addictive.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is everything you'd ever want out of a farming sim, especially if you're getting bored with other games. Every detail is a refreshing new take on the genre. Best of all, you can't accidentally knock yourself out by swinging your tools at people! (unless you connect with an object that uses that tool)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing farming sim game, I got it originally because I've pretty much exhausted everything there is to do in Stardew Valley, and waiting for Haunted Chocolatier to come out, I needed something to hold me over until then... While this is Stardew Valley-esque, it is absolutely not a carbon copy of the game. It very much has its own identity, its own mechanics, and own original story. Came for a Stardew Valley copy to hold me over until the next game releases, but found something way better than I expected instead. Absolutely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The story begins with you living in a cave with your adopted parents and suddenly they reach the decision for you to start living your own life while helping the village you reside in. Foraging for plants, taming animals, farming,  discovering forgotten lands and meeting new people all while helping your village grow and expand.The graphics resemble those of typical cozy indie games (Stardew Valley, Potion Permit, Graveyard Keeper, etc.) but also it's own as well. The music and sound effects are also similar to typical cozy games.I recommend this to anyone who loves cozy games in general and aren't bothered by simple graphic designs.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Reminds me of Stardew Valley and Pokemon Arceus.  Stardew with the farming aspect, building relationships and going around the area, but Arceus in the sense of needing to learn about your products and learning everything you can to grow better items and do more stuff.  It's been a great game so far, and always something to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't expect to fall in love with this game - it's been such a wonderful experience. I think it's a disservice to compare the game to a certain popular farming sim as Roots of Pacha can stand on its own.I love the community aspect - how you don't really "grind" for money, but help to contribute. The ideas system is also really cool because you feel like you're really working with your clan.The characters are fantastic. The cutscenes can be emotional or really funny, depending on what's happening. I'm really motivated to socialise with everyone.There's animals to tame, plants to learn, mini games (traps, fishing, festivals, etc.), a trading system (later on), and more!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A very welcome entry into the Farming Sim genre, with a setting and premise that sets itself apart from the rest.   With not even a week into Spring,  I can tell this game will be a mainstay in my library right alongside Stardew Valley. _childDocuments_.review: Very nice and chill, I'm enjoying it. But what's a surprising amount of stress is that the days feel a bit too short, especially compared to Stardew, and this is particularly true when I'm scouting the savanna. 15 minute days don't break the game but I think two extra minutes would give you time to take care of the home front and then go fully explore a zone without having to always wait for rainy days.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVE this game.I'm usually super picky about most games, especially when it comes to artwork and controls.This game has me addicted with it's story line, artwork, characters, music, puzzles and progression.I like who you unlock things overtime and you're able to practically decorate and place objects down anywhere. This way I can organise the heck out of everything anywhere.It's nice that you can play with friends (still gotta get hubby to play with me at some point...) or just solo and still have a blast. It'd be nice if you could unlock little outfits for your pets/farm animals like flowers or paint to make it feel more immersive (since this is exactly what I'd do if I were able).Anyways, 10/10 would recommend this game to anyone looking for a cute casual game they can play with or without friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I'm around 40 hours in the game; I believe Roots of Pacha is rather overrated - this is my main reason for giving it a bad review, to balance the actual score of what this game deserves; I saw a good rating and I thought it would be great, it wasn't.I've played better video games of the same genre with cheaper prices and superior quality of everything.Let me say it again, I haven't finished the entire game yet, I will eventually but right now I feel forced to keep on going and I have felt this way from the very beginning, it's not fun nor is it relaxing, the main parts you usually meet in this category of gameplay; you play for the sake of playing.Once I finish everything, if somehow I change my mind I will give a good review.My main issue with this game is that you don't have much diversity of activities and the tasks that you do have are as boring as they can be.* The prophecies system is not complicated though it's not fulfilling either.* Events are lacking in the personality department and usually there isn't much to do on the event days.* Same can be said about the characters, they're not too interesting, they're simply there, they're fine but not memorable at all, this is not a big deal however in this category of entertainment, it's half of what it has and the main portion of what makes the world surrounding you be perceived as being alive.* There is no leveling system for your character in anything.* I also think they could have improved on the graphic design, yes, it looks cute but it also resembles a browser game.Typically you have enough time in one day to get done whatever you would like getting done if you change the game time mechanic to longest (which should be the standard from the get go if you ask me), albeit, once more, playing through the entire day it's dissatisfying. Don't get me wrong, they have good elements in the game such as the fact that you have different inventory slots for tools, seeds and another inventory for the rest of your items.The leveling system of the plants from wild to domesticated plants can be categorized as a positive.I like how you bring wild animals to your farm, how you very slowly build up relationships with them, this structure can be improved but all and all it's all right.While playing I haven't encountered any bugs at all.It has potential yet it seems incomplete, you need more depth until you have a proper game with a charming personality, not only with a gimmick that becomes bland rapidly.One background song for every season? Come on, you can do better than that.6/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: As soon as I got this game installed, I was totally immersed. I was so into this game that I ended up losing track of time. I mean I played 13 hours straight and kinda forgot to go to bed! So far I haven't encountered any game bugs at all. Greatly enjoying this game so far! If you're looking for a cozy game to vibe to, I highly recommend "Roots of Pacha"! It has a great soundtrack, adorable animals, nice villagers, and beautiful artwork all bundled up in a wonderfully crafted story!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Quite a lovely farming sim that inherits some ideas from Stardew Valley and brings something brand new to the table.It has (among all the rest of core features):- minigames- animal taming and mounts- quite unique setting It could have: - tasks given by your tribe members for rewards (I think that would make the game more interesting and kinda break the routine)- better balance (the game encourages you to sell/donate produce to gain contribution points, at some point you discover that the economy is based on weird stuff. For example complex meal made of processed ingredients produces less points than smoked fish or fermented tomatoes)- better endgame progression (there's a secondary (?) goal to explore a vast cave system and unveil it's mysteries. Once you do that - the game becomes kinda bland to my taste. You just skip days, so your tribe gains enough prosperity and gives you final tasks). Summary: great variation of a farming sim that hits the sweet spots just right and does most of the things just right. Definitely recommend for all the genre fans.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game has been hands down game of the year for me, if not my favorite game of all time! I love how the community evolves with the idea system and taming animals being the way you obtain them instead of just buying them somewhere. _childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a cute, sweet game. It's very Stardew Valley-esque but in prehistoric times. There's so much to do in the game and yet it doesn't feel overwhelming (like Stardew sometimes does). Also, the characters in the clan all have such great personalities. It's really fun getting to know them while playing through the game. I like the character customization options, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Stardew Valley, get ready to go ENCINO MAN!!! In Roots of Pacha you are a native Pachan, a tribe that follows their goddess the Pacha in the form of the Pacha Tree. You have been told by the tribes Shaman that Pacha wants you to find a new land. So your tribe and you journey forth. Eventually you settle in a new land after a great Earthquake, a Pacha Tree, hidden is now rediscovered and your tribe settle down. Soon YOU are tasked to lead the tribe to find innovations, clearing the land, befriending animals, and encountering the other tribes.This is an AMAZING game, having played countless hours of Stardew Valley this game is a glorious successor. Farming, Animal Husbandry, Inventory Management, and all the fun side events of building friendships and relationships that Stardew Valley gave us continue on. Solve puzzles in the caves to grant you access to further materials and raise your tribes technological advances!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I've been an avid enjoyer of the farming sim genre (played Harvest Moon [now known as Story of Seasons], Rune Factory, Stardew Valley, Harvestella, Sun Haven, etc.) and I really like how Roots of Pacha does its own twist on the farming sim genre. For me, Roots of Pacha is especially unique in its prehistorical setting and how integrated you feel in the community; some games make me feel like I'm the only one contributing, but here, it really feels like everyone plays a part in contributing towards the clan.I'm also a huge fan of the UI and the tool + seed bar! Although it seems overwhelming at first, I quickly got used to it and I really appreciate the little details that ties back to the prehistorical setting of the game. I also really love the torch and how you're able to smoothly switch between tools while moving.It's evident that the devs have poured a lot of love into this game. For example, during multiplayer, each player gets their own color, both on the map and in the cave. I also like how each player can make their own choice during a cutscene (although it's funny seeing the other party only respond to one of the choices if you choose a different one).Other features I really enjoyed are the confirmation button before gifting, the easily accessible calendar and map, the ability to see if there's a cutscene with a specific NPC or not, and being able to date someone or hangout together after turning them down. For the minigames, I really enjoyed the racing, fishing, and befriending animals minigames. I also love the festivals and the puzzle-based cave challenges!During multiplayer, some aspects are shared that, although they don't bother me, might bother others. The seeds, quests, animal taming progression/animal affection, and several cutscenes are shared. NPC cutscenes where they invite you aren't shared, but the ones that you stumble into are shared. For NPC-based cutscenes, only one player needs to trigger them and the others get teleported into the cutscene; for story cutscenes, festivals, races, and cave challenges, everyone needs to be present. Overall, I had a lot of fun both playing solo and with multiple players- I'd definitely recommend it to anyone interested in farming sims!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Very chill cozy game with a prehistoric theme.  Has all the elements that most  cozy games do, like mining, fishing, farming, relationships, etc.  There is no combat, so if that's you're favorite part of cozy games, you won't find that here. If your favorite part is relationships, you can romance every available bachelor at the same time. You can also have 2 children, and they actually grow up from baby to toddler, with interactions changing as they age. The fishing mini game is annoying, but honestly - what fishing mini game ISN'T, lol.  Lots of fun ranching, with rare animals to find and "collect," if you're into that. Cooking gives you different buffs. It's not super complicated or in-depth, which is good for folks who want to just chill and relax. There are fun secrets to discover, and the villagers all actually have storylines and backstories. It's definitely entertaining, and if you like chill farming sims, I recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: this game is great. i started with playing around 20 hours on switch, before developing nintendo thumb, because you have to click 'A' heaps to do anything : (. i wanted to play it on computer bc i tend to have better posture playing on computer and also was hoping that i could use my left hand more, and not as much of my right hand. the game is really great on mac and similair to switch i've had little to no issues. you can click spacebar to do most stuff, and i can play my with left hand mostly on mac, which has been great. i love this game - its like stardew in some ways, but in many ways its unique. when i first fell in love with stardew i watched heaps of videos, played all the time etc. and it quickly became a grind (i tend to play games like this). with roots of pacha, i have done some of this, but it seems to have a great inbuilt resistance to my perfectionism. easy to enter a flow state, and the environment supports immersion really well.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if ConcernedApe and Primitive Technology collaborated on a farming/life sim game and you got Roots of Pacha.  This game is just excellent. I've put in 32 hours almost non-stop over the weekend and have plenty of stuff left to accomplish/achieve. I just unlocked the keg+casket processing equivalent from SDV and am so stoked to cover the town in machines!There's lots of details that I love about this game, including how you don't acquire a currency that measures your wealth but instead recognition of your contribution to help the tribe that garners exchange of goods and services. "You helped out with those gemstones -- how about I upgrade your hammer?" Really wholesome and rewarding.The character portraits are gorgeous, there's plenty of thirst traps to potentially romance. I even got to adopt a wolf to live in my home! I think you can choose a baby woolly mammoth to live in your home, too. Your adopted grandfather tells dad jokes and the tools maker's daughter talks to her hammer.It's comfy, it's relaxing. The only combat in this game is the one that takes place internally when considering who to romance and I even read online that you can romance everyone if you like (but only "marry" one person). Harem enjoyers, rejoice!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I held my review until I felt I was able to get well into the heart of the game.  I'm at a little over 20 hours, and I can say that it's definitely a farming sim you'll get your money's worth out of.  In terms of familiar features, if you're familiar with titles like Stardew Valley, you'll notice an energy system, till, plant, water, harvest cycles, and mounts.  Some of the more hidden gems that I've found so far is a mastery system associated with each plant type, fish, and tree.  It seems as you get to a higher level, your chances for better quality harvest increases.Now... let's get the ugly bad over with.  The mini games are atrocious.  Seriously, I'd love the game immensely more if I wasn't forced through the same fishing mini game or pet taming ritual each and every time.  Second - while the teasers show irrigation, don't expect to get it early on.  Again 20+ hours and it's still eluding me.  Albeit, you do get the same tool upgrade cycle as with other farming sims, but at a much slower pace in Roots of Pacha.Despite the horrid mini-games, the game is worth it, and if you can get past them you'll have a great time.  A huge recommendation to the devs.. please give a 'disable mini game' option to make them go away.  I'd rather insta cast with fail % for wasted energy than having to keep going through the fishing cycle.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Do I like the game - yesWill you like this game - maybe... depends if you like the retro style genreWhy then am I giving it a no?The game is NOT a 92/100 gameThe game for its genre to fans of the genre is a 72/100 (not quite a B)The game on its face to regular gamers is a 58/100Hence meta score noOne of those times where I dislike steams yes or no rating then giving a % on the game review base...Well one of the complaints I see a lot is a lack of combat... but then how many of this type of game have actual good combat?  Stardew valley was mediocre, My time at Portia/Sandrock is mediocre, sun haven is mediocre, coral island is mediocre... this genre isn't known for decent combat... it is nice to see yes, but really its never well doneMy complaints?  -Animal meat can only be bought, no slaughtering animals for their goods-Days are very fast (which now has a fix in a settings option to increase day time)-'ideas' (game progression) requirements are extremely vague, doing it blind means you'll miss a LOT for a long time-some unnecessary and slow minigames occur just to slow things down-things get 'stuck' like animal types-story is mediocre-basically NO RPG elements in this game... you have some equipment, but no leveling of your character occurs-UI isn't intuitive and oftentimes clunky (no auto sort in inventory/chests, tools get strewn around your bar, seeds are chaotic too)-LOTS of things essential to progress the game are unexplained in their entirety or hidden in unexpected npc vendor tabs-The mines bear mission doesn't explain bear claw use leading to a hammering slow time-Might have hidden values for 'sale prices' of things-Game suffers from a by the time you can get it you don't need it syndrome... aka by the time you can farm enough to get 'reputation' (money) you no longer need it-Farm animals are largely useless only needed for a couple story progression things (which is typical of these games)Pros?-Farming has a lot of different levels of plants represented visually from wild to tamed a couple varieties for each-Fishing is a different but slow method than most games-The mines are well done, progress through them is better than most other games in the genre with acceptable if easy puzzles-Controls work about as you'd expect
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Stardew Valley, this builds on that formula and makes it better. The UI is slightly better, the crop growing is more interesting, the animal collecting is definitely more interesting, and some of the harder edges of SV (losing money if you didn't make it to bed, combat) are sanded off. Really, any flaws with this game are that sometimes it's just too much the same as Stardew Valley, and a minor complaint that sometimes it doesn't explain itself or its menus well. But again - if you liked SV and want more of it, this is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Basically a farming sim with a few new mechanics. The gorgeous pixel art style convinced me to get this (not a fan of the Stardew Valley looks), and the game itself didn't disappoint. Lots of things to do, lovely details, quite customizable, many ways to make "money", a tiny bit tricky in some places, if you don't turn to the internet for solutions. The more time you spend on it, the easier your daily tasks become because of developments in the clan, which is pretty rewarding. Definitely worth the money for me, haven't had a farming sim this fun in a LONG time.A few things I'd note (after almost 100 hours): A LOT happened in the very beginning. Nearly every day there was a new cutscene for me, they could've stretched it out a bit IMO, so that the player's not that quick to complete the main story. I also hope for an update that let kids grow past the toddler state and maybe even introduce rival events, cause currently there are very little cutscenes with only some of the NPC's. Other than that, I still have a lot left to complete after my many hours, so I'm definitely not done playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is of a kind with Stardew Valley but very much is its own thing. "Stone Age" setting, multiple NPCs to interact with, well-done graphics, fun (!) mini-games. Yes, of course there is farming. And fishing. No hunting, though, I mean, you can befriend ALL THE ANIMALS so of course there is no hunting. (There are one or two hunter NPCs, and you can if you wish trade with them for meat, but you do not have to.) The socio-economic model is based on communal living, rather than capitalism. There is a huge emphasis placed on collaborating with others being the way to survival and happiness and the favour of the clan's guiding spirit (Pacha). No currency per se, and the player's contributions to the clan's larder is measured in what amounts to 'likes'. The player can use those contribution points to trade with other clan members for things like clothing and household goods and tools. Also new buildings, like a shed so your animal friends have a place to sleep in your village. (Your especial animal friends stay with you in your own tent/hutch/yurt.) Tech advances and knowledge are gained via working with clan members to realize the "Ideas" they have. No one asks you to fetch this or that random item; instead, they ask your help on a project they want to work on. I am enjoying it very much.

I can’t recommend this game enough, if you’re a cozy gamer, this is a perfect edition to your library!

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is an incredibly polished game made by two brothers, a labor of love and a fresh take on the farming sim genre. The first things that stuck out to me were the clean, intuitive user interface and incredible controller support. Every other system in the game is unique yet familiar and intuitive. No combat in the game, it is purely a chill and relax farm sim.The cave system is not a bottomless slog of levels, instead it is a fun, exploratory area with puzzles and secrets that are rewarding while not feeling super mandatory for progression. Farming, husbandry, and fishing are all engaging with an interesting progression system that rewards specialization in each area. I have not done much with the relationship and romancing yet, but have heard it is forgiving and allows you to romance multiple villagers without repercussion. Holidays and recurring events are also super cute and endearing so far (only year 1 summer as of this review).My favorite part is the core progression system and how it revolves around your tribe contributing to increase "prosperity", which allow you to reach milestones that allow for the unlocking of technology and other features with the help of villagers. I can't recall a similar game in the genre with a system as cool as this one.All in all this game is great and engaging so far. WAY better than Sunhaven and actually feels like a finished game (what a crazy concept for a non-EA game). The devs will be releasing kickstarter stretch goal content in the coming months as well that fleshes out other parts of the game.

The story is interesting enough for me. Honestly, I hope they come out with more content for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is, to me, an extraordinary game that has truly captured my heart. As an avid fan of farming simulators like Stardew Valley, I was eagerly looking for a game that could deliver a similar experience while also offering something fresh and unique. Roots of Pacha did that, and slightly exceeded my expectations by delivering a delightful farming simulation set in prehistoric time with lovely pixel graphics and art style that made a visually captivating environment from the picturesque landscapes to the adorable animal and good looking character designs.What sets Roots of Pacha apart is its depth of gameplay. It seamlessly combines classic farming mechanics with an immersive storytelling experience, along with other cool hidden gameplay. I found myself completely engrossed in the game's narritive, which beautifully explores themes of community, nature, and the harmonious coexistence between humans and animals.The farming mechanics, reminiscent of other beloved titles in the genre, are refined and highly enjoyable with it's own tweaks and tool/seed organization. Tending to my crops, raising animals can be addictive to some. Fishing could be easier and less finicky, but even it's mechanics are easier than other games, which thank goodness. The game also offers a wide variety of activities beyond farming such as exploring ancient caves, interacting with a pretty large diverse cast of characters living within your valley, trying to find and catch rare animals, and doing tasks to uncover the lore/past of the land. The abundance of content ensures there's always something to do.Another thing I enjoy, even though I haven't put my toes into it yet, is that it has a multiplayer feature. So if I want to play this with friends in the future, I can. So this just adds an extra layer of enjoyment to an already captivating game by working together to build, explore, and prosper.As a whole, Roots of Pacha is an enchanting adventure that combines the best elements of farming simulation with a rich prehistoric setting. It has become my top go-to recommendation for fellow farming simulator fans and those seeking a game that offers relaxation and engaging narrative. I wholeheartedly recommend Roots of Pacha to anyone who appreciates the farming simulation game genre and yearns for a carefully crafted game that blends charm, storytelling, and addictive gameplay. It's a true gem in my book that deserves to be celebrated and cherished. Happy farming my fellow pacha adventures and clan members!Hearing about big update of this game excites me
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This feels a lot like Stardew Valley with a different graphic style. The whole setting is very well done and sets the atmosphere masterfully. The only thing I don't outright love is the taming of wild animals minigame, which feels a bit too childish like for me. But it's rare and quick enough that I don't get annoyed at it. On that note: this game is very kidfriendly. If you're looking for a game for young kids or just enjoy a wholesome, peaceful playing experience yourself I can absolutely recommend this game! :)

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a stone age game in the vein of Stardew Valley. Play that one first if you haven't.While initially the game got me interested, it turned into a bit more of a grind and a slow slog than Stardew Valley ever was.In this game you grow crops, forage for resources, build buildings, explore a cave, domesticate animals and grow your community.However, taking care of any moderately sized field early on just eats all of your stamina (that you can barely upgrade). Sure, at some point you can do irrigation, but until then I have to dump all of my stamina into watering every tile. Sure, you can eat your crops to gain back energy, but that's tied to a slow animation and you don't get that much back in comparison to how much effort it took to grow the crops in the first place. Even clearing out your field to expand it can eat a good chunk of your stamina so you're not feeling like you can neatly separate the crops...Exploring the cave seems to be an important quest, but you will be limited by your stamina too. Plus getting to it takes a bit of effort.And you better hope you grow your correct crops and find the right items to progress the game. I didn't save enough grain in the first season to unlock grain milling which is required to progress in the caves so I was locked out of it for two more weeks before the new harvest would come in.Your community accrues culture points over time. You contribute to that by donating items to the community bin. It's meant to show more of a communal spirit in a society without money, but it ends up just being replacement for money. Which items you donate don't matter, just their points value, and you spend those points bartering...The tribe culture points are also a gatekeeping method for progressing with your tech. A lot of new ideas you want to develop have a minimum culture point requirement, meaning you sometimes have to wait a few days for your ungas to grind that number up. Your contributions (probably) matter, but the numbers for your community as a whole are so much bigger you are just a drop in the bucket.Your tribe is forgettable. They have names, but you will only care about them based on their profession - the tool lady, the shaman, the building builder, etc. The festivals they throw also don't feel like they have much personality or sometimes even point to them.While the game has some interesting additions to the Stardew Formula (watering system, more rideable animals, breeding animals, plant knowledge), it feels a bit like a chore to play rather than something you can't put down.
