_childDocuments_.review: I played this game from start to finish, and I still can't recommend it. It has a great look and style, and some great mechanics. But the pacing is an absolute mess. The most useful technologies came so late into the game I didn't need them anymore. And I don't think it was clear how closely I was to pay attention to the prophecies. I spent half my game time doing nothing and waiting for more events to happen, only to realize I needed to somehow interpret the prophecies into meeting some vague checkpoints. Also I didn't like the cave puzzles at all. I was looking for a cozy little tribal farming sim, and while it did have those elements and they were excellent, everything else kind of got in the way or wasn't fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't enjoyed a farming sim game like this since Stardew Valley. This is exactly what I wish Sunhaven was. If you loved Stardew Valley I would highly recommend this game! I also loved the tribal lifestyle which is such a fresh new feel for farming sims. Explore multiple different locations, gather materials, help your clan with projects so it can grow, interact with animals by playing a charming flute, grow your own farm, and raising a family are just a few things you can do in this game. There is also lots of enjoyable events and celebrations, which my favorite was the racing day event every 2 weeks. It also has one of the most interactive parenting mechanics in a farming sim game that I have ever experienced. Which isn't saying much since all the other games you practically leave the baby alone for hours as if it was a rock. The only issues I had with the game was that there were some mechanics I didn't realize until much later that would have made things easier. So they could do a little bit of a better job pointing them out. Nonetheless 9.5/10 really great farm sim!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game that feels like a breath of fresh air in a genre that has been over-saturated in recent years. This game raises the standard for farming sims games like Stardew Valley did before it, and I consider this game an equal to SV. I have 100% in this game as of this review, and I plan to keep up with that with each subsequent update because this game is just that enjoyable to come back to. Needless to say, I strongly recommend this game!THE GOOD- The soundtrack is great and perfectly fits the vibe of the game.- The pixel art in this game is top notch, fantastic job to the artists because this game looks incredible.- The Pachans & Co. are enjoyable characters and actually feel like a village in that every person is connected to each other and they each have their own opinions of each other, whether they be good or bad. It is hard to find two pachans that don't have some sort of meaningful relationship, I'm sure there may be one or two pairs that don't but the vast majority of them actually have some sort of relationship or opinion of each other.- SO MANY CHOICES for romancable NPCs, and you can romance multiple characters at once with no repercussions if you want to see everything they all have to offer. Every couple can have children regardless of gender. My only complaint in this department is that Nokk is still not romancable, let me marry this big softie please I'm begging you.- Children will grow up through life stages! Currently only the baby and toddler stage are in the game, but Child is being added in the next update in July and more stages will likely be added from there!- The animals feel worthwhile not only to tame, but to breed. Breeding good animals gives you a chance at a baby with improved skills, which gives a lot more longevity and depth to the husbandry aspect of this game. Unlocking and taming all the secret color variants for each animal is also fun and can be quite the task. - After you release an animal, you can occasionally see it chilling in the wild. It's a nice touch, it's good to see old friends every so often. You can re-invite them to your farm if you choose to as well!- A unique take on the crop system where you can domesticate crops over time to increase their value, it is a passive system but it works really well in my opinion because it's not too much of a hassle while also requiring you to put a good bit of work in to max each plant species.- the game world is big enough for the scope of this game, with a large hub area, 4 biomes of various size and caves, but there are more areas that are planned to be added. - The fishing minigame in this game is good! Doesn't take long, doesn't require lots of clicking or keyboard inputs, and is easy to pick up.- The devs have so far delivered on their promises for this game, as well as taken community feedback into account and added in and plan to add in features that were not originally planned.- The seeds have their own inventory separate from tools and other items, and each of them show what seasons to plant them in when you scroll over them and go to plant them. You can also move the seeds around to organize them if you want. It is great and all farming sims should do this going forward.- YOU CAN DANCE WITH THE NPCS TO INCREASE FRIENDSHIP AND THEY EACH HAVE THEIR OWN UNIQUE DANCE AND IT'S GREAT HANDS DOWN BEST FEATURE, OPA GARREK STYLE EVERYONE.THE MEH- I mean...I guess it's still actively receiving updates and such, so if you want a 100% completed game, come back later I guess?- Watering in the early game can be very time consuming, making crops more trouble than they are worth until the late game when you have a few upgrades under your belt. HOWEVER, they are adding a new feature that will act as a early-mid game watering option that will cut the time spent watering crops to hold players over until you get those late game upgrades. So this point will soon be addressed. -  Currently the pet animals don't feel as valuable as farm animals, in the sense that they don't really do anything. It is cute for them to follow you around and you can pet them but that's about it. HOWEVER, more interactions with pets are being added in the upcoming update. Pets will be able to fetch items for you and several of them are confirmed to become new mounts.  So this point will soon be addressed.THE BAD- I have honestly tried to think of something but I got nothing to put here tbh.OTHER-I do not play multiplayer, my experience is exclusively in single player, so I have no idea how good the multiplayer experience is.

_childDocuments_.review: The multiplayer is very frustrating. _childDocuments_.review: What I love most about the game is how chill and laid back it is. You get to explore, farm, fish, tame animals and play in peace. The day clock is a sun slowly going over the horizon, so no ticking clock. If you don't go to bed by the time the sun gets to the bottom, all that happens to you is lower stamina for the next day. No penalties or anything like that. It also slowly fades into the night in a relaxing way. And all you need to do to boost your stamina is eat something. The controls are simple and easy to figure out. There is lots of foraging and exploring to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Very recommended for fans of Stardew Valley. The comparison between the two is natural.It adds a few Quality of Life improvements over SDV though, such as seeds and tools not being taking up space on the inventory / hot bar which I never realised I wanted until I had them. Among many other small QoL changes that add up to a very pleasant and frustration-free experience.It replaced the usual combat area / mine with a cave that you explore and complete little puzzles in instead. Don't find myself missing the SDV mine at all!I also liked the fact that getting into the animal husbandry side of things had a low bar for entry, needing to tame the animals rather than save up a load of money to buy. Feeding them plant fibres instead of needing to buy / make fodder, etc etc.For a person that has played Stardew (or any of the old Harvest Moon games) this is going to be a very familiar, very simple, but very addictive game. My current 17 hours played is 2 play sessions.

_childDocuments_.review: Check the Article for the full review: After only 3 hours of playing the game, I'm plotting how fast I can finish homework and other responsibilities in order to squeeze in as much time in the game as possible during this next week. I want to play it and I'm the type that if you have my attention after 3 hours, you've succeeded. Will update once I'm further in.Roots of Pacha puts a unique spin on the "Harvest Moon"-style game, which really helps it flesh out into its own game. Rather than being solely about being a farmer, you're now a core contributor to a clan of primitive people -- each of whom contribute to the clan as well. _childDocuments_.review: Honestly having a great time with this. Pick this up if you're a stardew valley, rune factory, or harvest moon fan as its very good for a farming/life sim game, and if you're curious about the genre id say this is an even better one to start with as unlike the other games this one feels a lot more low stakes and relaxing then the others do. And it's got a nice gimmick that adds a fresh coat of paint to the genre, which has become a little cliche at this point. No more "nondescript grandpa died and you got his farm in a small town because reasons." Instead you are part of a tribal village that has just migrated to a new, vibrant region to call home. Kind of gives similar vibes to the plot of "The Land Before Time" if you're old enough to remember that movie.Some positives: The setting is actually really nice. "Prehistoric" is something i've really never played anything in and i wasnt sure it would be for me but i think it does a pretty good job at making that setting interesting and approachable. If you want a historically accurate game it definitely is not, but historical accuracy wouldnt really fit in a lighthearted game like this and I think most players would prefer it this way.Whether this is a positive or not depends on you (for me it is a positive) but the days are alot shorter than other games, which I personally like as it can take an irl week or two just to get through one season in games like harvest moon, and i appreciate the faster pace. A very diverse approach to player gender! Your character is never referred to with pronouns and you basically just are whatever you envision yourself as. You can even be nonbinary if you wish to be, and the character creator allows for androgynous looking characters. Since the player's gender isn't acknowledged by the game you can romance any of the options as well.Pretty good, diverse, and interesting cast with designs I really liked. It's also quite large which is really nice in games like these. Stardew valley always felt like it didn't have enough people populating the town, whereas this one has plenty of people around, as well as 2 neighboring villages to interact with as well. (They don't have nearly as many members as your tribe does, however)LOTS of animals to choose from! And tons of places to explore! The only farming sim with more exploration then this I can think of is rune factory, definitely much larger than stardew and harvest moon ever has.A pretty satisfying character creator.Some negatives:Its a little disappointing that there are alot of characters who probably *should* be romanceable but aren't. A few make sense, such as a young couple that have already gotten together, the village children and elders, and the parents of certain characters, but I was surprised by how many younger characters that seemed like they'd be romanceable weren't. Im only one season into the game so it's possible this is for a reason, such as maybe they pair up with someone else, but I see no other reason that they shouldn't expand the romance options a bit. Not that there's not enough but if you went to all the trouble of designing these characters why make them single and not an option? I have a feeling a mod will eventually be made that addresses this, though.Part of the main quest is exploring a cave and there really isn't enough time in the day to do this without passing out at 2am, while also watering your crops and whatnot. I would personally suggest making it so that at 2am if you havent made it into a bed you still get the energy penalty but the day doesnt immediately end then.The character creator is actually really nice but there are very few clothing options, with only TWO available initially and only a handful being available later. I definitely think this needs to be expanded on. DLC would be great for this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A chill farming life simulator, similar to Stardew Valley in some ways, yet with it's own details and ideas. It is set in a pseudo - stone age, but to be clear, don't expect some realistic representation of the era - there'll be some technologies / ideas, buildings, phrases, and other things not originating in the time period. There are some fantastic elements in the game, too, like totem spirits and magical creatures and the like.You have several activities you can partake in, most of them typical for the genre, such as farming (duh), animal taming and husbandry, fishing, trapping (upcoming at the time of the review), creating different produce, gathering, cave-exploring and mining, socializing with other npcs, having pets, decorating your home... And no combat whatsoever. I know this is important to some players, so, if you want more peaceful game, or don't care for fighting, this will be right up your alley, otherwise might be a turn off. Some of the activities are in form of mostly easy minigames.The game is relaxing and for most part, there's really no need to rush anything. You can select day length ( 15, 17.5 or 20 min), which can sometimes feel short if you're trying to do everything (would love the 30 min day, but that's me), but not a big problem if you don't overextent yourself with things to do. You also have quite large inventory with separate tabs for items, tools and seeds, which makes inventory managment less of a hassle. Some things might still feel a bit grindy for some players, but overall it's nothing drastic.Npcs are varied and interesting, with different personalities and histories, and you have a nice selection of romanceable characters. Main story is nice, and there are some puzzles, but it's nothing too demanding. Art is cute, and music is very good, although some songs tend to repeat a bit at the end of a day, but it's still great at rounding the experience.The game is also quite inclusive and open-minded, as many games today are, but I don't feel it is expressly forced upon you or anything like that. There are same sex relationships and marriages, which you can also be a part of. There are also vegetarian and vegan recipes for different food, and any type of hunting that will or might be in game will be optional.And important to note, the game is still being worked on, so there'll be even more options for many aspects of the game.In short, fun and very chill game, deffinetly worth checking out,
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Yes. Yes. YES! I have played so many farming sim games after putting in 500+ hours into Stardew Valley and none of them lived up to the hype except this one! Its similar to stardew in many ways (farming mechanics, caves, relationships) but it has its very own story that seems very fleshed out as well as the time period in which it takes place is super fun (stoneage). I love befriending the animals, and i love the conversations with the townsfolk. I also love how frequently they have updates and how involved the DEV team is, they really seem to be listening to what suggestions are provided to them. I never feel like I am doing monotanous or grindy work either, and the caves are so fun because rather than killing enemies you are supposed to solve puzzles.  I love the lore and anytime there are cut scenes. my only recommendations for the future are MORE cut scenes between characters please,  and more romanceable characters.

_childDocuments_.review: I never played Stardew or Harvest Moon, but a friend suggested we try Pacha. It has a way of sort of chilling you out or zoning you out. It makes hours drift by with ease. The games that recently hit this note for me were HL Alyx, Raft, Valhiem and FTL, but they're not comparable. Maybe a key for last used item, or options for things like showing item labels, and auto-depositing like-items into storage. It doesn't seem to be optimized for a controller but that's fine with me.

_childDocuments_.review: Singeplayer Review OnlyAt first glance Roots of Pacha is a Stardew Valley clone set in the stone age. But the deeper you look into it, the more you realise that it's not actually that at all but something else - and that is a good thing.Everyone in your clan has a role and purpose. Yours is to manage the farm. First you got to find seeds in the wild, then grow the crops, and learn more about them. You will see plenty of wild life, which you'll later learn how to befriend, tame, and eventually breed. You will stumble upon a mine inhabitated by the spirits and solve their puzzles to gain their powers and find better minerals - all of this completely peaceful. And in between you help your clan inventing better tools and techniques until you slowly crawl forwards through prehistory.Here are some features and thoughts on the game:Graphics and UI:- the UI und controls feel clean- if you're a friend of pixel graphics, it's very cute to look at. If not, why are you even looking at this game?Gameplay:- you don't faint with no energy left or lose energy when you hit nothing (eg. by accidently using your tool)- you can paint much of your furniture, giving your home your own touch- there is no combat in any way- the festivals have actual competitions in the form of mini games or puzzles- fisihing and taming animals comes with mini games- the price for seeds is quite high compared to the profit- some crops you cannot grow but have to trade with other clansStory and Characters:- the story is well designed without feeling overbearing or annoying- every character has their own daily rhythm depending on season, weather, and time- you can talk, dance, and meet up with every character depending on your friendship level- there is no locking in or out of relationships. the only point of no return is marriage.Fazit:If you enjoy farming games like Harvest Moon or Stardew Valley, you should defintely give this one a try. Roots of Pacha is the first farming game to capture me in this way in a long time. All I hope for now is that they give us more of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: If you like Stardew Valley and games similar to it, then you'll love Roots of Pacha too.I wanted to wait with my review until I reached year 2 and finished a whole year first, but I can already say that this is a lovely, cosy and relaxing game.You can farm, tame animals, grow the clan and have challenges in the caves, which are enormous and offer loads to explore. There's plenty of characters to get to know, each with their own little side stories and some of them are also roman-cable. I don't know as of yet if it has any benefits having one of the Pachans moving in with you, but it's still a cute little extra.Sometimes days feel a little stretched, but on the other hand, some days can't have enough time. I think all in all the time is managed pretty well and Roots of Pacha offers plenty of things to do throughout the days. It's a great game if you want to take off your mind for a while and just have some fun in a virtual nature-related environment.

_childDocuments_.review: As of this review I am only just entering Fall with my fiancée, so it's possible that some opinions will change, but I find it hard to believe my opinion could become negative.This is a very relaxed entry into the farming life-sim genre with a very unique setting due to it being in ancient times. Unlike a lot of other games in this style there is no combat, which to people like myself is a blessing as I've always considered that to be one of the weaker parts of Stardew, for instance. There is a large emphasis on community and character relationships, even more than most others, as you are always situated with the community rather than being separated from them in a different zone, and interactions with characters are cute and fun. You can also date everyone at once until you finally settle down for marriage, which lets you see lots of the dialogue in the game without limitations, though there's no penalty for monogamy either.The evolution of the tribe and unlocking new tools, stations and ideas is one of the most interesting parts of the game by far, as it feels like you, the player, are not the only one participating in life with the clan. NPC's will spark ideas on their own and ask for your help and contribution towards some new ideas will happen without your input each day. Even if it's all just scripted to happen it feels like you aren't just the center of the world, and it's always fun to see new ideas unfold and unlock new stuff to help you or even just get new decorations around the clan.The game was also built from the ground up with multiplayer in mind and it shows. Non-romantic interactions with NPC's will have all players see them and participate in them together, and even the opening cutscene includes all players starting the game together. It feels very nice to play, even with very long distance such as US to AUS, with no noticeable lag or latency. Most developments are shared between players, too, aside from their personal tool belt which requires them to have their own tools created. It's been a very positive multiplayer experience.There's very little in the way of negatives in this game, as they have been very quick to fix bugs so far, so if you like these kinds of games (Stardew Valley, Harvest Moon, Story of Seasons, etc.) and don't mind the lack of combat I think it's a no-brainer to pick this up.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game. What a breath of fresh air. I am an avid fan of 'farming sim', 'life sim' type games, i.e. harvest moon, stardew valley, story of seasons, animal crossing etc. Pros: This game gave me the same obsessive feeling once I started playing for the first time in a long time. This game is so unique and creative. I love the way they introduce the different mechanics, how resources and 'currency' work in the game, and all the things 'to do' through the game. The music and pixel art is amazing! Also, the story is cute and engaging.Cons: The only thing that I was kind of let down on was the replay-ability of this game. For instance, in stardew you can focus on plants vs. animals, community center vs. joja, and all the different personal stat upgrades. But for roots of pacha, once I finished the game and got 100% on achievements, there was nothing I could have done differently in a new game (other than romance someone else, but you could do that in one game). Sad, because if there were those type of elements, I would put so many hours into this game, and it would shoot to the top of my favorite games. Other than that, I highly highly recommend this game to those of you out there looking for your next fix in the 'farming sim' game world. I thoroughly enjoyed all 100 hours, and will be excited to see future updates from Soda Den.

_childDocuments_.review: Just got through Summer and now in the middle of Fall, All I can say is, this game is well worth the wait, and there will be more down the line.  Like I said, there is much more to come. There were a multitude of stretch goals for this game's Kickstrater, and they were all crushed by the end of the campaign. However, the team made the decision not to fully implement all the stretch goals into the game so that we players won't have to wait even longer for this game after the release had been pushed back from December 2022 to April 25th this year. So instead, there will be hints in the game for the larger stretch goals to come down the line, and the team will fully implement the stretch goals in a way as not to break the immersion of the game as it is and make them seem natural in the timeline of the game. With this in mind, I feel that all the wait was well worth it, after winning Beta access in September 2022, DMed Creb this note, and he sent me a game key, and now, I'm enjoying the experience so far with all the improvements, and am super excited for the major content updates down the line. _childDocuments_.review: Hold onto your loincloths, folks, because Roots of Patcha is here to transport you to a prehistoric farm-tastic adventure like no other! With its incredibly satisfying gameplay, stunning pixel art graphics, and captivating nature, this game will have you shouting "Yabba-dabba-doo!" and spending more time on it than you ever thought possible.Let's start by admiring the visual feast that is Roots of Patcha. Prepare to be dazzled by the gorgeous pixel art that takes you back to a time when mammoths roamed the Earth (and you didn't have to worry about your Wi-Fi connection). The attention to detail is so mesmerizing that you might just forget to milk your virtual mammoth.But enough about the visuals, let's dig into the gameplay. Roots of Patcha isn't just another Stardew Valley wannabe. Oh no, it's a farm sim life with its own unique, well-thought-out mechanics. While there are similarities to other games in the genre, this one sets itself apart by letting you step into the furry shoes of a prehistoric tribe member. Who needs carrots when you can ride a wild boar or raise your very own bison? It's a primal joy that leaves you grinning from ear to ear.While the story might not be the next epic tale of heroism and destiny, that's absolutely irrelevant in this caveman wonderland. The focus here is on the sheer delight of living a simpler life and embracing the quirks of a bygone era. Who needs prophecies when you have a virtual stone ax to upgrade?Now, I must confess that there's one little quirk that might make you go "Uggh!" in both frustration and amusement. Forget about using your trusty WSAD keys to navigate the map. In this game, you have to unleash your inner caveman instincts and use your cursor to edge your way around. It's like playing a never-ending game of tag with your mouse, and boy, does it keep you on your toes!In conclusion, Roots of Patcha is a wild and woolly farming adventure that will have you laughing, grunting, and shouting with joy. With its enchanting pixel art, clever gameplay mechanics, and the satisfaction of taming prehistoric creatures, this game is an absolute blast. So, grab your virtual club, put on your best fur loincloth, and prepare for a prehistoric farming extravaganza!Get ready to plow, sow, and harvest your way through the ages. Roots of Patcha doesn't just offer a farming experience; it's a time-traveling escapade that will leave you in stitches and longing for more. Happy farming, my fellow cavemen and cavewomen!

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is part of a genre I like to call 'pixel farming sims', alongside the early Harvest Moon games and the infamous Stardew Valley, and not only does it sit comfortably among them, it brings some Quality Of Life enhancements that I am going to sorely miss when I return to those games. First off; I love the unique premise of setting the game in prehistory during the birth of farming. It turns a lot of preconceived notions on their heads, such as having to domesticate farm animals first, as well as the plants, displaying what well-known farm produce used to look like in the wild, such as purple carrots, wrinkly strawberries and even some odd looking squashes. Seeing them morph from their wild shapes to something more familiar as your planet knowledge level rises is always fascinating.The setting also allows you a sense of progression; first you start off with just your stone handaxe multi-tool and a pitcher for water that only waters one tiles at a time. As you progress, exploring the Land and talking to the tribe, Ideas will occur that, when their prerequisites are met, will give you enhancements. Sometimes it's as humble as knowing exactly what time it is in a day. Sometimes it's as essential as taming animals. Ideas range from giving you the ability to make wine or cheese or even sour cream, to increasing and upgrading your tools.Okay, I might as well talk about QOL enhancements, since there's a lot and I love them, so this'll be the focus of my review. 1st: seeds live in their own little sack separate from your inventory. This means you can forage wild seeds constantly and never have to worry about running out of space. When planting, you can hold 'E' on keyboard to bring up the radial menu so you can switch seeds or assign them on the fly. Each seed has a little symbol next to them denoting the season(s) they can be planted in, so you can tell if you can plant them straight away at a glance.2nd, branching off that, every tooltip for items is very informative, giving you all the details straight up. This is especially useful with cooking and Ideas, as you can quickly see what each plant is considered as ingame very quickly, and even politely informs you that yes, tomatoes are technically fruit, but they will be treated as vegetables. The only slightly marring thing was that I was never exactly sure what was treated as 'Fat' though. I think it's milk/cheese, but the game was a little coy in that regard as it doesn't say. That said, the highest compliment I can give to this game is I did not have to look for a guide for something until several hours deep in, as the game had been so forthcoming about its information.3rd: back to radial menus, your tools can be assigned to a radial too, and they also don't take up inventory space. At the start this is moot, since you just have the handaxe multi-tool that serves as hoe, axe etc. and your wand pitcher, but as you develop tool upgrades that create the specialised tools like the sickle, hammer, axe, they can be assigned to the radial to be easily selected. And they'll be glad they stay separated from your normal inventory.4th: this game respects your time. If you need a reminder for something, the menus have you covered. The biggest is in the 'Smoke Signals' section: this will chart any Ideas that are available to progress, what clan contribution is being worked on if any, whether a race is going on, if a festival is happening all the way down to 'hey your new tool is ready' or 'hey the new animal shed is built'. So very useful, especially to someone as forgetful as me. It also keeps track of what things you require for Ideas, if you've spoken to the person to get it started. It'll even tell you at a glance if you've got the items in your inventory. There isn't as much information for the animals as I'd like, however. If you need to get an animal's stats beyond its happiness towards you, you need to go interact with the animal itself, which can be a faff if you're looking to breed for the best stats.5th: best map everyone go home. Ok, maybe slightly hyperbolic, but it's still an example of a game that respects your time. It has a list of all the tribe members, shows you what role they play (whether you can 'buy' meat from them, get them to construct things, upgrade your tools, etc.), and shows you where they are at the time, or even if they're moving at the moment (the tribes-people will move even though the game is 'paused', which is odd but nothing close to an issue), so you can always find where they are very quickly. Seed origins and animal locations are also marked on the map once you find them, making it very easy to see 'oh I need some more wheat seeds, I'll just head over there to get some'.6th: it's chill. There's no rush to do anything by, and the game is more than happy if you want to neglect farming for a while to go delving into the caves and their puzzles. You will miss some Ideas by not interacting with all aspects of the game, but the game is content to let you get there when you get there. To add to this, in a not-so recent update, the devs have added three options for how long you'd like your day to be, just in case you feel the default option is a bit quick. I use the 'Long' option myself, and can see an argument for 'extra long', but definitely experiment for yourself. You'll need to start a new day for this to take effect, AFAIK.7th: the caves fill in their own map as you explore, show doors you haven't explored yet and after a certain point you unlock fast-travel points that let you get back to where you were in the cave very easily. A recommendation from me to you, potential player: go back to the fast-travel point 'Flight Simulator' when you've gained the required ability, there's some neat stuff you can find in there.8th: Running out of stamina doesn't make you fall flat and wake up at home with money/items gone - you just get a 'no stamina - go rest or eat something' box come up. Anticlimatic maybe, but it fits the chill vibe of the game that it doesn't punish you for overextending.The only issue I have with this game is it can be a little fiddly with the controls, especially when using hotkeys to swap tools around, and navigating some menus. Bizarrely, coming out the 'Smoke Signals' menu really wants you to use 'Esc' to leave it, clicking the button won't do it. It also has that behaviour when selecting places to building things - you have to use the keys to cycle through the areas. DON'T click the button to cycle, as it'll take it as a 'I want to build this here' command, and only the 'are you sure?' dialog box will save you. It can also be fiddly to harvest a plant if you've got a water bucket selected as the commands get confused, and I've had issues trying to do something around an animal, as the commands will change depending on the pixel selected. Luckily the game shows you the command in the bottom right on the screen, but it can still be a nuisance.All in all, a very HEARTY recommend! If you love Stardew Valley and other pixel farming sims, this is absolutely a gem to get now it's back on Steam. I have barely scratched the surface of what this game has to offer, since I've focused on the QOL stuff that this game brings to the table. Honestly, it's a great chill game, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: A nice little neolithic Stardew Valley, more or less.This game is 100% peaceful, no combat of any kind. Instead, caves have puzzles.*TL;DR*: Great way to get a new flavour of Stardew Valley in like 20-40 hoursL;R:*Story + time to complete:*Main story is pretty simple, can be completed within the first year, but it took me a bit over a year because I didn't notice a couple key parts to completing the story until the 2nd spring (~40hrs in). After you tick all the boxes for the story to wrap up, the game makes you wait about 3-4 extra days before actually ending. Those were the most boring part of the game. since there was no way to make real progress in the game anymore. If you're the sort of person that like to 100% games, this can keep you busy much longer. You can start a family, master all crops, find all the animals, etc. If you like those, cool! I'm only interested as long as I can progress (get new tools, build new stuff, etc) so I stopped when the main story finished.*Farming isn't quite as useful as expected*This isn't a farming sim the way I expected. Fish is worth WAY more than crops, especially once you unlock smoking fish. You can farm, of course, but now that I've finished the game I realize that only real reasons to farm are:- Cooking food for mines (since mines are super energy-consuming)- Making alcohol/pickled stuff/spiced wine in the waaaaay late game- If you want to 100% stuffSo, if you're not interested in 100%-ing the game, you can honestly skip farming everything but grain + fruit(for wine). Cooked foods sell for basically nothing, so no point in cooking once you clear the mines (doable by winter)*Progression is cool*I like how you start by finding your own seeds and taming wild plants. It's neat how you can breed animals to improve their produce quality/quantity. _childDocuments_.review: This long-winded review spoils a few really interesting concepts of the game, so be warned if you want to go in blind. TL;DR: This game is fantastic, and I highly recommend trying it out.This game is more than just "something to fill the void" between Stardew Valley and Haunted Chocolatier, as some people might claim. This game innovates on the townsim/farmingsim genre in ways that few other games of its kind dare to experiment with. What separates Roots of Pacha from its peers is its setting, and the numerous ways in which it utilizes its setting to its fullest potential in terms of the world's lore and game mechanics. I'll break down each of the game's components and review them individually.I've always found the progression system in other farming/townsim games like Stardew Valley... strange. You upgrade your tools from one metal to the next, build bigger crop fields, get more animals, marry whoever you want, complete whatever big collection bundle you have to do, buy new crops from the crop seller each season, etc. Roots of Pacha makes you feel like you're actually making brand new, fresh discoveries.The basic way that you improve your farm and settlement is through a progression system called 'ideas.' Ideas come up when certain requirements or conditions are met, such as the prosperity of the village needing to be a certain number, a specific crop/tool/produce needs to be obtained, etc. You'll need to develop ideas to progress your village through the ages, such as the ability to domesticate animals, develop beekeeping, creating the first cheese cloth, and so forth. For example, at the beginning of the game, you and your tribe don't know how to keep track of time, and thusly, you have no way of knowing what precise time it is outside of the general lighting (day, evening, etc.). It isn't until you've developed the idea of a sundial that you're able to tell exactly what time it is.Additionally, the way the game progresses your "farming ability" is different than other games of the genre. For comparison, improving your faming skill in Stardew Valley unlocks recipes to create various recipes, like stone fences, sprinklers, mayo machines, etc. Pretty boring, and not really indicative of your skill actually improving. In Roots of Pacha, you first need to find seeds in the wild to bring back to your farm to plant and care for. You can then harvest these crops, but they'll usually be 'wild' versions of these crops. As your knowledge of a crop increases, you'll begin to see domesticated versions of this crop instead. And as your knowledge  increases, you'll start to see higher quality crops. It feels rewarding to specifically plant these crops, like you've developed a natural affinity for them, and it feels like these crops sort of become your "specialty." There's also an animal progression system beyond just being their friend (though that certainly helps). There are various different types and colors of animals that you can find, including rare and legendary skins. You can breed animals to create new generations of animals that produce higher quality goods or produce them more quickly. Optimization!Aside from progression of the farm, the game also has a cave system that the player can explore for metals, rare gems, and a few other interesting things. What I appreciate most about the cave system is that it isn't randomly generated, but a fully fleshed-out map that feels deliberately designed. The cave itself almost feels like a mini metroidvania that you can play while in the game, giving the player puzzles to solve and new routes to explore whenever you obtain a new "power-up" via the totem animals. This is so much better than other cave systems in similar games because you actively engage with the system rather than hack and slash away at monsters or slimes or rocks (though you do have to hack away at rocks from time to time, I at least never found it to be too much). The cave system is also how you obtain the metals required to upgrade your tools, and I was pleasantly surprised by how thought-out the tool progression was as well. Instead of a weird progression ending with gold or a made-up metal or something radioactive, the best tools in the game are bronze, which fits with the timeline progression of Stone Age to Bronze Age.The village of your tribe serves as the "town" through which you can conduct your townly activities, including talking to people, giving them gifts, dancing with them, or dating/hanging out with them. Like all other farmsims, villagers follow schedules that take them to various places throughout the day, including leaving the village for other areas of the map. The townsim half is just as important as the farmsim half, as it is where you'll be spending the majority of your time when you aren't farming or exploring. The "dance" action is refreshing, as it gives the player a new way to interact with townsfolk that isn't just talking to them. And each villager has their own unique little dance animation, giving them so much personality. In order to buy things from the villagers, you'll have to "contribute" to the village through putting any of your products into a contribution box. It's essentially just selling your goods for cold hard cash, but they give it a different name.I haven't been able to go through every character's relationship events, but what I have gone through is interesting. Each character seems to have their own individual flaw/problem that the relationship events focus on, making the characters feel alive and realistic, but not boring. You even get glimpses of these characters' personalities, history, etc. through speaking with other members of the village. It feels rewarding to speak to Villager B, who talks about Villager A in a way that tells you something new about Villager A, that adds depth to their character. Now, I don't know exactly how common or frequent these happenstances are, but it was frequent enough for me to comment on, at least.Another fun thing is, with the addition of children, you have to actually care for your children. Can't just make a baby and leave it alone at home all day. Assign it a babysitter and nurse it/change its diapers.There are several different maps outside of the village that you can explore, each with their own seeds (depending on the season) and animals to tame. At first, you'll only have access to one area, but your options will pretty quickly expand. Because each season provides different seeds, you'll want to explore every biome in every season. The areas are beautiful and provide a sense of the area where a Stone Age tribe might settle. The music for each of these areas, seasons, and times of day is also top notch. You can also meet and trade with other tribes, though you can't visit them.- Animal breeding is fun, but far too time-consuming compared to domesticating crops. It can take 6 or 7 generations to get a "perfect" animal, and you need to get both animals to relationship level 6 in order to breed them, meaning it takes foooooreeeever to breed animals.- Children don't attend festivals. Your spouse won't bring your child to the festivals and you can't take them either, they simply disappear on festival days.- Spouses won't help take care of children, even if they're standing in the room while they're crying.- Map diversity is a bit poor. There's 4 different biomes to explore, only 1 of which is large enough to feel expansive.- Some methods of turning a profit with your produce seem inferior, such as fermenting vs pickling vs aging. It could use a bit more balance.- Needs the ability to meet with other tribes in their villages.Overall, I'm excited to see where updates take this game, and I would highly recommend anyone who enjoys farming sims gives this game a try.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really really chill farming game, I highly recommend it for any fan of the genre.My biggest joy: Maybe I'm the odd one out but I have never liked the forced aspect of combat in farming sims, usually in the mine sections. If I wanted to fight, I'd play another genre, or Rune Factory. But every other farming sim on the market (except maybe Song of the Prairie) insists on adding at least some fighting involved in the mines or in the case of Dinkum, even overworld. I'm not sure why, and I've never liked it. Especially when it's an aspect of the game you are forced to engage with in order to advance. Not so in Roots of Pacha, the game is peaceful, and to make the mines interesting they instead add story advancement and small easy puzzles to the mine section, with cute npcs, and fantastic music. It's such a breath of fresh air and so peaceful and calm, even if that was the only thing RoP did different to other farming sims, I'd already be very on board. But that's really not the end of it.Other things I love in no particular order: absolutely fantastic and enjoyable. the music mechanic is just cute but the little tunes also really bring to mind the animals themselves, really clever and fun. I mentioned this above but they are a charming part of the aesthetic. you can ride boars! Or other things, if you really want. instead of trying to become the most capitalist farmer out there, your currency is how much you contribute to the clan, and every day you see that other members also contribute, it really gives a peaceful sense of community. it's very endearing and has such a sweet message and feel.   Instead of the traditional fishing mechanic, they mix it up. I absolutely love the item progression. Sure it's the same as usual mechanically, but that you go from flint to obsidian and so on, up to items that in other games would be tier one but in this one are endgame, is just really charming.Negative: why is this so hard to come by? Even with the max upgraded hardwood ring, if you want a lot of casks you are going to spend hours chopping trees. Now casks aren't an essential way to make lots of contribution, fishing is a really valid strategy, but I like the traditional make an aged wine empire route, but the hardwood involved in this is intense the supply is incredibly limited. Though I have pretty much nothing else I would complain about regarding the gameplay loop, setting, music, or mechanics, there are some performance issues on both PC and steam deck when you leave the game running for a while. The game noticeably lags and stutters, becoming increasingly unplayable until you close it out and restart. Since you have to go to sleep/end a day to save, this becomes more of an inconvenience because you have to finish a day cycle before fixing the issue if you don't want to lose that day's activities.

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is a game that will inevitably draw comparisons to Stardew Valley and many other farming games. However, Pacha has plenty of unique ideas that keeps it from being a clone and might inspire a few imitators of its own.Roots of Pacha is highly community-oriented, both in its story and its gameplay. Instead of building and upgrading things to become the most prosperous individual in town, you're doing those things to help your entire village. The more you help out, the more your fellow villagers will pitch in, too: as you explore, discover and gain friendship, the other clan members will come up with their own ideas that will in turn aid you. One clever example is that at the beginning, you can only rely on the sun's position in the sky to keep track of time. Once your villagers invent the calendar, you gain access to an in-game clock. You will not be able to do and invent everything on your own, you need your clan members. This allows Pacha to maintain a sense of discovery into late-game. (Speaking of time; the default day length is a little on the short side. I found myself enjoying the game more after increasing day length in settings to max.)The game is more pacifist than Stardew: there is no combat, but the game replaces this with clever and charming puzzles. You'll still be mining for minerals, but you'll also gain animal powers that help you progress in the caves.Another fun interactive element is the ability to customize the furniture you "buy" from villagers. The game allows you to make each pot, vase and jug unique by painting anything you like on them. You can also hang your little drawings on the walls of your home.The festivals are varied and unique, again focusing mainly on community. No trying to win the title of Farmer of the Year here - instead you'll be joining snowball fights, playing in a band, tug of war with your teammates, and more.The game has a few rhythm- and music-based features, including taming animals with your flute. The taming itself is fun, but gets grindy if you try to catalogue every single variant and breed legendary animals.The control scheme is a little unintuitive. Instead of having one inventory for everything, you have three separate ones: a seedbag for seeds, a toolbag for tools and a "general" inventory for everything else. Sometimes you have to manually assign seeds in order to have them show up in the inventory wheel, which gets unwieldy considering each season has a slew of different crops.Roots of Pacha is still a developing game with many more features planned. It's already well worth its price at this stage, having plenty of content to keep you busy. I'm pleasantly surprised to have found a game that sets itself apart from many other farming sims out there, and looking forward to future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been really enjoying this game. If you’re a fan of the harvest moon/stardew valley genre then this game is a fun twist on that idea. If you’ve already beaten stardew valley and you need a new way to get that fix, I would pick this up. Some of my favorite aspects:Foraging seeds: it’s fun on the first day of the season in your first year running around and finding the plants around each of the maps to get seeds from. It gives you a good excuse to explore and I appreciate that you can play a lot of the early game without any “money” at all. Tech advancement independent of you: your clanmates come up with ideas, contribute to the clan, and create things independently of you. This gives me a feeling of forward advancement that helps the middle of the game feel like less of a grind and helps the clan feel like an entity that exists without my help. Even on days when I don’t contribute at all, the clan projects move forward. The setup of the other locations all being located off the main farm/clan area so no area is too far from the central location. This helps with setting up your day, you can start in your main area and then pop off to one outer location a day and be back by bedtime The painting! You can paint and decorate things in your house and it’s actually very detailed. There are dozens of colors and you can go pixel by pixel to make really nice art. Things I like less:Characters feel a little one dimensional at first. The one that cooks, the one that fishes. It’s all they talk about. Their dialogue can feel a little one note. As your relationship with them advances this gets better and there have been some cool days when multiple characters daily dialogue play off each other and tell a mini story. Still no pausing inside! I guess this isn’t a popular mechanic, but I wish the game paused inside buildings so you can “take a break” Everyone is thirsty. This isn’t a full criticism but there have been hilarious moments when a character has asked me to date them while I am standing next to their own brother that I am in a relationship with. At least they all take no for an answer!

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot overemphasize how much I love Roots of Pacha. I am a hardcore Stardew Valley lover, but since I downloaded Roots of Pacha in the spring, I haven’t touched Stardew! The soundtrack is beautiful, the graphics and character designs are adorable, and the story is just delightful. You don’t just buy animals, but tame them and intentionally breed them to increase their stats. You can also ride animals and tame some to keep as pets. You progress through the caves by solving puzzles, your crops evolve as you continue to farm, and the fishing mini game is actually chill, so fishing doesn’t feel like a burden. Not to mention the festivals are SO much fun. All of that being said, my absolute favorite part of Roots of Pacha is the characters. I unequivocally love every single character, their dialogue, their events, and the journeys they go on. I especially love that characters actually romance you back instead of you being the one to initiate everything!I don’t want to only compare Roots of Pacha to Stardew Valley because Roots of Pacha is absolutely its own interesting and unique farming sim with a really exciting premise and features, but it’s like the devs took everything I didn’t love about dating, romance, and NPCs in general from Stardew and made it better! Dating feels more natural, your spouse still does much of what they did before your union, and having a baby leads to new game mechanics that actually have consequences. I could go on, but basically, if you like farming sims, I cannot recommend Roots of Pacha enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Helping my clan, farming, fishing, exploring new areas and investigating all kinds of mysteries! _childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: It is by far my favorite farming cozy game, surpassing Stardew Valley. What I love about this game:- The pixel art is GORGEOUS, I love it so much- The amount of details and care put into the world + in the cut scenes is just lovely- Every person you interact with is unique in so many ways, without being an AH- Lovely stories of healing and growth- There is no combat- You can choose daylight speed (fast, normal, or slow)- Healthy, loving relationships- View into what thoughts or difficulties might have inspired certain technological developments (which I found FASCINATING each time)- The romance options are 10/10, so many interesting people to choose from- Farming is optional, but is fun and rewarding- You can tame all sorts of animals with provide a huge variety of products (no killing if you don't want to)- You can tame pets, which will live in your house- The fun holidays and events are so engaging and an absolute delight to interact with If you are on the fence, I really recommend this game. Please give it a try if you are into cozy games. And Devs, thank you for making this game - it is such a wonderful experience playing it. It's clear that so much love has been put into it, with even more content coming up on the roadmap. An overall amazing experience. I rarely post comments on games but this one was worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The quinoa-munching tree-hugging peacenik cavemen totally lost me.Gameplay wise, this is Stardew Valley on , so I can understand why so many people love this, and I recommend sim-farmers at least give it a go. Of especial note is the way the clan as a whole comes up with ideas and accomplishments, so you don't feel like the only person on the planet who actually gets ♥♥♥♥ done. So yeah, good game, but be aware of one major flaw: like so many SDV clones, the setting and characters are so ridiculously bland! Devs, please get this! The reason so many people liked SDV was because the small-town-failing-economy bcakdrop was realistic, and the NPCs were very human, with complicated relationships, secrets, real life issues and problems that were not one-note for the most part. This lot?? ARGH! I'm a raging liberal and even I find them almost too 'woke' for my taste! Their so-called problems would be considered too wishy-washy for a kibbutz! Oh, my, this character tries too hard and tires herself out, she needs to learn to slow down and accept her clan's help. Oh no, this other character has so many good ideas but is not organised or ambitious enough to carry them out, will the player and his clan ever help him take that step forward? The anguish!(If anyone thinks I'm exaggerating, compare any SDV character's page - which you usually have to scroll down several times to get to the end of -  to Pacha's wiki where each character is described in essentially one paragraph. A small paragraph at that.)Now this is something that annoys me in a lot of SDV clones, but what really got my goat in Roots is that there is so much great gameplay here and so much promise in the premise. Oh, I laugh sardonically every time I see the we-cover-our-butts text from the devs at the start of the game, 'this is not based on any actual culture in history', duh. Though there may have been tribes somewhere in time or space that were this peaceful and pleasant and nature loving and so open minded and accepting they'd give an entire hippy commune a collective toothache, we all know that people like that would have gotten wiped out by their neighbours in short order, and probably eaten, too. This is the dawn of civilisation! This is the mills of a non-benevolent god that ground humanity into something mean and keen that didn't want to live in harmony with their environment so much as dominate and eradicate it, because in real life, wolves don't become pets that easily, lions are not effing vegetarians you can tame with a song, and nothing makes you hate mother nature more than having grandma eaten by a sabertooth tiger! We invented agriculture because hunter-gatherers are always at the verge of starvation! We coined fire and weapons because nature was rife with claws and fangs, and we were tasty bags of protein! Early man did not build f#""$$# arts and crafts stations!!! He (most likely) evolved art to teach and understand and give his growing brain a narrative that would explain why everything out there seemed designed to *simmers down*I know why the devs didn't want to go with the Red In Tooth And Claw approach, because that would have turned Roots into a survival game and gotten pretty darn bleak very fast. I feel keenly the waste of an awesome premise, but I'm okay with a farm sim in final, just give it a bit more of an edge, please. I tried, I really tried, I forced myself back again and again to play it, because the gameplay rocks and baby mammoths are the absolutely cutest things that were ever created, but I had no attachment to the pixelated people running around, no immersion into the game, no real goal in mind, and finally I just gave up. I'm waiting for the game Grave Seasons now, an SDV clone with a serial killer on the loose, surely that won't leave me in a diabetic coma...

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent modeling of the progression of human civilization in a very personal experience. Beautiful art, good music, and such a massive cast of well developed characters. The writing has gone very deep, with a lot of interactions, character arcs, and cutscenes that really bring the world to life and create engaging relationships. I'm particularly impressed with how the devs handled irrigation. It's not just the end of the tech tree, it's a massive achievement and a whole new game mechanic, really bringing home the impact this development had on human agriculture. I'll be streaming this in the near future, now that I feel like I have an understanding of all the options.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll preface this by saying when I first caught wind of this game on Kickstarter, I backed it immediately. I love the Harvest Moon - SDV type games and Roots of Pacha felt like it would be a fun twist on the genre.  I also played both a multiplayer game with ONE other person and a single player game. I also play with zero mods to get the full experience first time round. Also I wish there was a more neutral recommendation because that's what I'd give. I'll start with the good.The first couple of hours were a lot of fun.  The tutorial for each new skill / action were helpful.  Time period / SettingI love the fact that we are in that prehistoric like time period where things really feel new and novel. Getting a bucket for watering felt really awesome for that reason alone. When I would progress with new tools etc, it felt more impactful. Art styleColors are vibrant and very much in line with Stardew Valley.  Clearly being set in the stone age or whatever shakes this up. Different animals, clothing style, etc. doesnt take away from this at all. If anything they did it very well. Music/Ambiance The soundtrack slaps hard. It really keeps with the theme of the game and I added the OST to my VGM playlist the second I heard some of the songs (Savanna in the summer is a true banger and don't get me started on the last part of the caves music ♥️♥️♥️)MechanicsI loved how RoP approached fishing in this game.  I also enjoyed needing to go out and "tame" your own animals . Mining, chopping down trees, farming are very much in line with the look and feel of games like SDV. MountsI like the option of having a choice of mounts in both species and colors. Also you can get one really early on which helps with the traversing different areas. The Negative Story Length / Completion In my multiplayer game, we completed all the prophesies by Winter 1. We weren't even trying to speed through the game or anything. Relationships For starters, I am one of those peple that enjoys achievement hunting if it's worth it. I stopped playing when I had to gain favor with everyone. It felt like everyone was so... bland. They also kind of all felt similar.  Im not looking for Baldurs Gate 3 level of character development but just something that made me go "I want to see what this person is about. "  The other thing is friendship decay. I can understand this in most games but these people are my clansmen. I can't imagine why affection would diminish if I don't keep up appearances.  I just think it's silly but there is a mod that exists that can circumvent this situation.Mounts Another issue would be mount collision.  Just let me walk through my mount, please. It's such a small thing but when I'm trying to get that coconut at 1am and I get off my osteriche the wrong way it just really grinds my beans. The other issue is finding my mount. Yes they give you horns everywhere, however why not just let my flute double as a whistle to call it over. When I'm taming animals it'll sometimes walk off and it's just stupid to not be able to have it stay put, so a whistle would be a nice change. Animals / TamingRare and Legendary animals having no real benefit other than looking pretty. At least make it give me like 3 eggs or shiny poop or something. The payoff for grinding these animals was just not worth it in the end. I decided to just send all of them to Grob, turn them into glue and be done with it. I did put the taming in the positive side, but after taming so many animals, it's becomes a chore more than anything. Like fishing, the more I tame an animal, my skill for said animal should increase to the point where maybe the song is shorter and shorter.  Side note: some of the legendary skins for the animals are weak, I'm looking at you Ibex. It would've been a cool feature to go on a "hunting party".  Maybe once a month you give Grob some materials and then over night you wake up with meat in the mailbox if the hunt was successful. It kind of sucks to tame an animal just to slaughter it when I invite it to live with me. Yes there is trapping but it I think going to the main hunter would've just felt cooler. Money makingMoney making is also kind of sad. The best money is in fishing and only fishing. imo.  Now I love fishing and I think the fishing in this game is done well, but for anyone who hates it, it kinda of sucks for them. They need to up the numbers for some of the means of contribution making to make it worth while. MechanicsThe totem powers are interesting, but become absolutely tedious (especially monkey form) when in trying to farm for specific things. Also I wish fishing had more "map" options. It's the same look throughout each biome. A little variation would've just felt really good. Irrigation was good in theory but I hated it in practice. Its awesome that they give you a spinkler type system but there was no great way I could set up the farm I wanted while using it. It was also clunky when it came to connecting certain points. Building placementsOn one hand it gives you nice options to place buildings in different places. However, I can't see why anyone would want to move their house away from the left side of the map, especially in the later game. Keybinds/ MenuLet me hit M to close my map. Why is this not a thing? Why do I have to hit escape? The menu also feels very clunky. Especially in a multiplayer game where time doesn't pause, needing to menu over to find something can be painful. A search feature in recipes would have gone a long way. Because the animal menu doesn't give enough information, I need to name my animals their color so I can know which variation I'm missing. Why it doesn't tell you the variation makes no sense. Multiplayer HousingI wish it gave the option to just use ONE house. RoP gives the option to let you keep playing a multiplayer game as a single player. The issue is, when that person isn't on and their DOG is in the doorway and I can't get out of their house... It's an issue.  Either let me control their animals to follow as well or let us share a single house as one. Yes we don't have to build multiple houses, but if we both want pets it's absolutely necessary.   If I were to come back I'd probably just forgo getting pets and animals for the most part. SummaryI know more content is supposed to be released in the future if they are sticking to their roadmap.  I will come back for the update and if they tweak anything in the meantime, I'll update my review accordingly.  As of right now, this just made me excited to play the new SDV content when it's released. TBF SDV is a very polished game, and has been out for a bit. But entering this genre, certain things should be way more polished. Luckily I only ran into ONE big. I was going to butcher an animal and it froze me on the dialogue. It was painful because the other person in the game just farmed a TON of high quality fish and because I didn't just pass out, enabling the option to save, I had to restart the entire day. Considering it only happened once, it's not the end of the world, but it really took the wind out of our sails. I don't recommend this title simply because there are better titles out there right now that do it better. Unless you really love this time period,  it doesn't really change enough up in meaningful ways. There are not enough mods to fix things that I wish I could change. If I grabbed any of the few, it would be the one to stop friendship decay.  By no means is this a "BAD GAME".  I just feel once you hit a certain point, the game is no longer fun. But before that the game is awesome.  If give it a solid 6.5/10. Decent game currently with plenty of room for improvement.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game from start to finish. If you love Stardew valley and are looking for something new to scratch that itch, this is the game for you. The farming is pretty standard for these type of games, but the fact that your plants evolve into more modern forms as they increase in quality is a nice touch. The same goes for your animals that you domesticate. As they become higher quality, they begin to resemble modern livestock. This game's irrigation system is also a delight to see in action. It's so unique compared to things like sprinklers from Stardew Valley, where you set it and forget. Every day you have to prime the irrigation system, but that one pump could water your entire field if you let it, allowing for lovely decorative patterns to form in the field as you plant more crops and dig more ditches.

The seeds, tools, and item pouch are all separate but require shifting through multiple items to get to the one you want unless you pull up the item selection wheel. Having to hit, 1-3, then E or Tab just doesn't feel natural to me of course I prefer controllers. I tried using a controller but the LT,RT, and RB/LB just doesn't feel fluid enough.
