_childDocuments_.review: I'm a sucker for cozy farming sims, but Roots of Pacha stands out as one of the best since Stardew Valley.The elements that it has in common with kindred games are executed extremely well, but it stands out because of its uniqueness:* You and your vibrant little tribe are actually discovering agriculture and technology bit by bit -- your character isn't being artificially forced to reinvent the wheel or personally source crafting materials that should be commercially available; you're creating things that have never been seen before in the game's world. * Things like animal taming and fishing are performed through minigames, but unlike every other farming sim, these are actually fun and engaging. * The characters are all likable in their own way, with distinct and absorbing stories, interesting relationships with other characters, relatable circumstances, and a sense of importance in the community. They tell you things you actually want to know about each other. Their preferred gifts actually make sense: a child will have many of the same tastes as their parent, the woman who lives with wolves will like herbs that repel fleas, etc. The heart events are well executed, feeling significant, appropriate to your level of familiarity with the character, and giving you insight into them. Best of all, they don't feel like one-off skits, because they're talked about by other relevant characters afterwards.* There's no formal currency, just a measure of your contribution to the tribe. Whether or not you contribute, though, the tribe still advances, so there's not the ridiculous feeling that the fate of the community rests solely on the shoulders of your character.All in all, it's an entertaining and cozy look at prehistoric times, with a wonderful cast of characters and some truly unique features.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: In the prehistoric times, a human tribe invents socialism. Soon the tribe of Pashans get to experience first hand how it failed. The premise seemed quite brilliant to the elders. The idea made them wonder why nobody came up with such a solution to the tribe's struggle before. Instead of everyone learning how to sustain themselves and their families, they would get guaranteed income in the form of food, shelter and services. Each member of the tribe has to contribute in the role they have chosen and that role only. This way they can specialize and excel in their profession and others will benefit from it. You have been adopted by the Pashans and accepted into the clan when you were a child. Perhaps not being born and bred into it makes you question the principles. It is the day of your coming to age and soon comes the ritual where you choose your role. Your adoptive grandpa is a master farmer although retired now. You wish to follow in his footsteps. Slowly you learn how to till soil, plant seeds and yield crops. This is the way you choose. Now you can finally start to contribute to the tribe.Quickly you realize how flawed the system is. Simple math tells you that there is 28 members of the tribe yet the average of contribution per capita is ridiculously low. So low that if you'd want to contribute on the average level it would be somewhere around two tomatoes a day. The elders say that everyone in the tribe has their role and provides services. For example Croll builds houses, sheds and all kinds of structures. He doesn't need to do any other task. He doesn't need to dance like Daari, who's role is a dancer. He doesn't need to sit at the lake all day, contemplating, like Garrek whose role is thinker. Super fair system based on equal distribution of responsibilities.As you hone your farming skills you also learn why the contribution levels are so pitiful. It's not because only part of the tribe specializes in providing food. The Pashans glorify laziness. One day you witness one of your fellow peers, the adept healer Illoe, being scolded by one of the elders for doing something that wasn't her task. The wisdom coming from the older lady was that by doing more than you must you wear out your body unnecessarily. Really?Days pass and you meet two other tribes. They bring with them something you haven't heard before. Trade. It appears that they don't contribute to a one big chest and instead barter items they have for stuff they would want in return. Exchange for something of equal worth. What a weird concept to the Pashans.Pashans who shirk even their own duties, like the guy who taught you how to fish because he thought that maybe you'll fill in his spot for catching them and was ecstatic to learn that there is another person who can provide fish now. You are different, though. You learn different skills and ways to obtain sustenance. You don't hunt but learn how to set traps. You don't build but learn how to craft contraptions. The plants you grow increase in numbers and quality as you gain experience with farming. Soon you realize that you're the only actual farmer in the tribe. There is a huge field not far away south from yours, that's several times as big, yet nobody uses it. Strange. Why do so many Pashans choose to be dancers, musicians or clothes cleaners when they could farm and have a full stomache every day? Like you.The Pasha tribe has better things to do, though. Their favorite pastime is coming up with ideas that would make their easy tasks even easier. They share them with you, the tribe's number one provider, knowing that you'll be able to obtain the resources needed to experiment. Then you get the result of their inquiry. One of them is a way to turn your veggies into juice. Another is to turn that juice into a fermented something that makes you feel weird. You soon realize that a lot of Pashans are very keen to this liquid. So much that the more potent the liquid in making your head spin, the more it is worth in trade or as a contribution.A game changer arrives when Garruk, perhaps under the influence of the fermented juice, comes up with the first actually decent idea in his life. An irrigation system that lets you water your crops with a directed stream of underground water. Pure brilliance. You clear all the debris from the huge unused field and work daily to make the aqueduct ready when the next season comes. It works amazingly. Now you don't need to spend half the day watering your crops. Aside from that, your yield is now massive. You decide to turn your kales and carrots into juice. Then you pour the juice into the array of fermenters you've conveniently lined up. The Pashans get addicted to your fermented juice. Business is booming. The outlanders have a word for it. Wealth. Now you can afford any service your fellow tribe members provide. Any item from the traders seems silly cheap now. A bunch of bottles tossed into the chest in front of the elder's hut equals more contribution points for you than the whole tribe's contribution combined. You learn that the housing market is a joke in Pasha's tribe. Poor Croll is obliged to build you a mansion, a massive warehouse, even the barns for your domesticated animals are now upgraded into a level unatainable even by the tribe members whose role is to domesticate animals. You still provide more than the others combined so nobody bats an eye at your wealth. Monday morning. You wake up next to your beautiful wife. The Morgani huntress who dreamed of dropping out of her keeper apprenticeship and not needing to hunt. By your side she can choose a job that she enjoys, or simply slack off all day like all the Pashans do. She fell for you instantly when she realized how crafty you are. That and you showered her with gifts. She currently has no role in the community other than being your partner. Nobody seems to care. Correction, nobody DARES to care. You check the mailbox and browse through the gifts you receive. Funny thing, when you have more than you need other people tend to give you even more. You step into the brewery grounds. You pour the juice into the fermenters, knowing that only one other person in the settlement knows how to do it but Ron lacks the ingredients to provide a refined product like this. He is content with making "just enough" beer for himself and to cover his part of the clan's contribution. Gin is the leader of the pack but everyone knows who runs things here and it's not Gin. Maybe I should name my new beverage after him to somehow honor how he allows all of this to happen. Would a different man try to stop me? Would he try to contest me? I'm overthinking again. I should leave thinking to Garrek. That's his role, not mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is a pretty great farming sim. I've enjoyed the main storyline and the progression system, it's an interesting choice to not have any sort of fighting in the game, but it seems to work. I only wish the automation/better tools would come not as close to the finish line as they did, but maybe if there are more content updates coming, this will be less of an issue. Could be interesting to try this in a multiplayer.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game on and off for some time. Always nice to return.Definitely more fun since the update that allows you to stretch the days a bit.Also more fun in Co-Op.Really feels different enough from other indie stardew-likes.Your own progression and the automatic progression of the tribe make sure, that there's always something new around the corner. You can still go at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I was waiting 2-3 years for this game to release and closely followed development. I have to say this is truly one of my favorite releases this year! You could make the comparison to Stardew Valley because of the core mechanics but i feel like Roots of Pacha is much more. Im excited to continue playing and exploring the rest of this game There's so much story for each character and lots to experience! Highly recommended if you enjoyed Stardew Valley or Harvest Moon type games very similar with a massive prehistoric twist
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, so I played the game for the last week. Haven't finished it but I have experienced the gameplay to an extent that, in my opinion, allows me to express my opinion about it.Good things first:+ It does feel like a cozy game. To people like me, who play to relax but can't get over minmaxing everything and ultimately spoiling the game with sweaty behaviour and ruining the "relaxing" part -> It's even less stressing than Stardew Valley. The days seem longer but (and maybe because of this) it feels like you have less energy, you can do less in a day. Never have I felt like going to sleep earlier or with full energy was a waste.+ The progression is satisfying. Particularly when you get better tools or get more animals, or when you fulfill ideas. I personally like the "crop knowledge" mechanic the most satisfying.+ The graphics are very well crafted, however devs could work on hitboxes a little more, because it feels off when in a game with such high resolution you run into invisible barriers/hitboxes.+ The soundtrack is immersive.+ The fishing mechanics are stressless and DON'T feel like a chore.+ Cool map design.+ The UI is really great and I love it.+ You can have a mount very early into the game.Now the cons:- The value you get for processing produce you want to contribute (sell) is a joke. Especially in the early game, it feels like a scam and you don't get any meaningful introduction to those mechanics at all.- I don't mind the fact that there's no combat, but even with the puzzles in the mining areas, the entire cave adventure is simply boring and unrewarding.- I know its very subjective, but there should be an option to enable pausing the day when you look at the map.All things considered, a pretty solid game, but given the hype we've been served I expected a more polished experience. Looking forward to future updates and to playing more of Roots of Pacha.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha is clearly a game with a lot of love and time put into it! The world's unique culture is very immersive. The festivals, characters, clothing, seed gathering mechanics, and animal taming all reflect this. I love living in this world. My current favorite update added children aging and going to school! The kiddo's all have different personalities and it's so cute. So many farm sims treat kids like boring objects. This game captures the feelings of family, which for me, is a must in my farming games. If you've been unsure, I highly recommend playing this game! I don't think you'll be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I like that this plays like other cozy farming sims, and yet has it's own unique way of doing it. I absolutely love the way new ideas are introduce to help the player progress in the game. The animals are cute, and in my opinion they grow up quick. The mini games have ranged from fairly easy to difficult, but I find that to be on par with similar games. The different furniture themes are fun as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Roots of Pacha takes the tried-and-true farming/social sim formula and strips all of the urgency and stress away; leaving a core game play loop that is still addictive and entertaining without the "always in a rush" feeling I get from it's peers.  It's exactly the game I need right now as I tend to not have much time to play so I pick it up and after a couple in game days I can walk away without feeling bad about it.  I know my little village, animals, crops and my buddies in my tribe will be waiting for me there for me when I get back.  The world is big enough for the relatively short in-game day cycle (even when set to max in the settings which is basically mandatory to get anything done) but not too small either.  The in game menu and maps are full of great information and is a masterclass in great organization.  The villagers are a little hard to get to know with all the other things you do each day but after awhile they grow on you.The music is really good and the game looks incredible.The only real gripes I have are: -The tool/seed selector is awkward as heck to use.  I like hotkeys.-The different qualities of so many types items that do not stack with each other is annoying as they fill up your limited inventory even more quickly (yes, after getting the biggest inventory belts available)-Once you max friendship with an animal they should shorten the mini-game for collecting more of that species by 75% that mini-game gets old fast T_T-Weeds/Rocks respawn so fast after clearing them! I get that you may desire this sometimes for collecting animal feed but there could be a progression to making better animal food (via farming) that feeds them longer and improves your relationships/animal stats.-The fully upgraded hammer/axe should get a hold-down charge attack to clear more rocks/trees/branches.  It feels like the max upgrade isn't all that satisfying for the work put into upgrading them.-When you walk behind a building the building should fade away so you can see what is in the ground behind it. Is it a rock or a branch that is keeping you from walking? I'll never tell tee heeReally just QoL stuff, the game is a solid 9/10 for me as is!  I love Roots of Pacha!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I love this game. I have been waiting for it to come out for quite some time.I bought it on the day it came out and have been playing every single day since.I have seen some reviews that say that there is not much to do, which I cant understand. I stay up past midnight during in game days cus there is so much to do!The characters are great and show events in which u find out more about them.The festivals are fun and finally different from other, similar games. You can paint the flower pots that you purchase, whichever way you would like.You can form a "union" and have children, who will have their naming ritual. And ofc, u can tame wild animals, some of which are legendary and rare ones.In order to progress, you will have to "discover" ideas and research them. For example a keg or riding on animals.Overall, I can honestly say that you should buy this game and try it out yourself. If you loved Harvest Moon, Stardew Valley, etc. You will love this one
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: As farming games go, this game is great. It reminds me of Stardew Valley. I enjoyed it very much and would recommend it to anybody who enjoys exploration, farming, puzzles, and crafting. If there is combat, I didn't find it. I got a little bored with the repetition at times, and wished that the game had some combat -- which is probably the one area that Stardew does better at.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A lovely farming sim with it's own unique twists and w/o combat. I really enjoy this. I've played both solo and with a friend. There are some things about multiplayer that are a bit annoying (like needing both characters to check in before starting a trial). However, these do not happen often enough to be a really big hassle. Do note, this isn't really a game that you can enjoy multiplayer without communicating with your farming partner.The fishing takes some getting used to as it's based more on snatching fish from the water without using a fishing pole. It's more of a game of patience that will not be for everyone. I did like it. It does get easier with practice and the right tools. My favorite part of the game has to be the animals and getting to know the people of the clan. Unlike most games of this genre, there is more than just petting the animals and collecting products from them. They can be bred to increase specific attributes (I don't want to spoil, so will not say more). You can use them as mounts. You can even get pets that will follow you about. As you get to know your clan more, they will open up with little stories. On top of that, each clan member has their own unique dance that is quite wonderful to discover.Finally, the caves. The caves have a wonderful mix of exploration and puzzles that all feel unique. I'm not sure how much replayability the caves have as once you are familiar with the puzzle, it seems like something that'd be easy to duplicate with a later save. With my multiplayer save, I've basically refused to visit the mines unless my farming partner needs me for a trial, trying to give them as fresh an experience as possible. Overall, I'd definitely recommend this game. It's a great addition in the farming sim collection that doesn't feel like it's trying to copy-paste other titles in this genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game let’s me pretend I have everything I want in life: Stable income, a wife, and a pet mammoth.It’s a game about being closer to nature and your neighbors, but is highly addictive and is keeping me indoors and alone. The irony is not lost on me.If you’re looking for a wholesome game that destroys your IRL health bar, look no further. The regularly satisfying hits of dopamine will cause addiction. You’ll lose sleep due to the “Just one more day” factor. You’ll strain your eyes. Your most visited website will change. The existential crisis that will awaken in you for enjoying a pixelated, 2-D world more than your reality will send you down a path of reflection and, in most cases, enlightenment. Probably.This game is is so incredibly comfy. I love the way they do the cave paintings as cut scenes. The early game flow is very pleasant, and the minigames are just really nice to play. The fishing minigame is so relaxing compared to other similar games. It feels familiar to the traditional Stardew/Harvest Moon farming mechanics but also feels different enough to not feel like a knockoff. As you explore and find things, you get quests from the other tribe members who will unlock stuff. It will be like, give this guy sticks and rocks and he will take a day to research and teach you how to make a drying rack.Most importantly, the village feels ALIVE and active! They don't just wait around for the farmer to solve everything, they take initiative and start projects on their own (like clearing a rock slide) etc.Even though it’s another farming game, which is commonly found everywhere, Roots of Pacha is original with its own spins. Similar to Stardew, it’s extremely difficult to find a game that has such a captivating message that’s been developed so well as this game.Roots of Pacha is the game-equivalent to a long-time best friend for introverts. You may have some questions at first, may have doubts, but the more time you spend with it, the more you attach yourself, the more it becomes a part of you and part of the things you cherish. It’s the game you always come back to; the game that helps you relax when you get anxious; the game that is there with open arms when you are ready.Do yourself a favor: get this game. Just trust me.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Get ready to build a community! Roots of Pacha is all about your clan, and your place within it. With beautiful pixel portraits and a charming art style, Roots of Pacha is one comfy game that has you playing within a friendly clan.In just my few hours playing, I've done a ton so far. There is farming, crafting, and helping out your fellow clans-folk.Pros:The style is adorable, and the gameplay so far is charming!The storyline is very engaging, with multiple cutscenes and story beats happening in the first season.Roots of Pacha has hands down the best fishing mini-game I've ever played. I love it, and I really think it captures spear-fishing. I'm not a huge fan of fishing mini-games, but I spent so much time just fishing!An adorable taming mini-game comes in the form of a musical mini-game as well.The art, the music, and the style are absolutely refreshing and a treat to play.Cons:I have a hard time getting things done in a day. Time does seem to go rather quick, and it takes awhile just to get places and I already feel like I have to head back to sleep. This doesn't really detract from my playtime really, as it means I space things out over multiple days.I am way too used to E being used to interact with things, so the controls took awhile for me to adapt to. This is just because similar games have used E for talking/interacting, but I'm sure I'll get used to this particular style in no time.All in all, my first impressions of Roots of Pacha are that it is definitely worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful farming sim! It clearly draws inspiration from the games that came before it like stardew valley and harvest moon/story of season, and while still having a ton of unique elements that make it stand out.I love that there aren't shops, you have to go and find the villager who makes tools if you want an upgrade, or go all the way to the forest to buy new clothes sometimes. Irrigation in place of sprinklers (which obviously wouldn't make sense in this time period) is also very fun. It takes a while to unlock it, but that makes it even more rewarding when you do. The cave system is an interesting mix of mining and puzzles, with no combat at all if that isn't something you enjoy. Opening more rooms feels more rewarding to me than simply descending another level. I do wish the in game map for the caves was more detailed, as it's hard to remember where some special points of interest were, and some rooms have very confusing layouts that would be nice to see on the map.The pixel art is all gorgeous and charming. I love the design of the animals and the building interiors especially. If the game lacks anything right now, I would say I wish there were more clothing options. But it's a minor inconvenience, and they could always potentially add more.The villagers all have a lot of life and character, and they aren't all perfect and nice either. There are misunderstandings and hurt feelings in the cut scenes, which adds a lot of depth. And the romance options are very diverse, so there's sure to be someone for everyone (I'm having a hard time picking between a couple options).I've sunk almost 30 hours into the game without even realizing time was passing. If you like farming sims and you want something that feels fresh and exciting I couldn't recommend this game more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Be warned before purchasing. After playing to completion, it's simply 'OK'. The puzzles are way more difficult than the game play is and that might turn off a lot of players. A good indicator of this is taking a look at the global stats for achievements, and  seeing how fast people are dropping off and giving up once the game takes a weird turn. If I wanted a game with tough puzzles and lots of hard to figure out hidden clues, I would have bought something else than what was advertised here. A lot of the challenges aren't even close to slightly obvious on how to figure them out and/or not enough clues are presented in the game. So nice on the surface, but not at all relaxing or cosy as you get deeper into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: It's an absolutely lovely farm sim, Stardew Valley gone to the Stone Ages. You don't start out with your basic tools as they have not been invented yet! You'll need to complete tasks from the villagers to advance gameplay mechanics - very fetch quest heavy which I don't personally mine.There is no combat and the caves require puzzles to progress - not too challenging i feel and I had a lot of fun in the caves.  Having just played Fields of Mistria the NPCs feel boring in comparison, with a lot of repeated dialogue but polygamy is allowed if that's to your liking. Raising in-game children is quite a commitment for 2 game weeks so wouldn't advised until you're well advance into the game.The music is *chef kiss* amazing! Festivals are fun and I love the game lore and story telling. Worth the full price imho.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I'm thoroughly enjoying playing the game and I'm happy I bought it. I'm a fan of Stardew Valley and I think Roots of Pacha improves upon some of it's features, and adds content I like better in some cases.One being that fishing isn't as much of a high blood pressure inducing headache😅😹I've even started the game over a few times, looking for a smoother and more efficient way to play.I highly recommend this game for lovers of cozy life sims💙😻
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Frankly I love it. It hits all the same winning notes as Stardew but is different enough that it doesn't feel like another Stardew clone. I especially enjoy the songs you play in order to befriend animals. On the minus side, some of the cave exploration and accompanying puzzles can feel a little tedious. The exploration is useful, but not ever forced, so you can do it at your own pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A fun spin on the farming/life sim genre. If you like Stardew Valley, you'll probably like this. And plus, it's a full complete experience with no feelings of Early Access-ness. I've read that they plan to continue updating the game with their Kickstarter stretch goals, which seem to be more areas and other villages to explore. But right now I don't feel like the game is missing those things, and if they're coming later as free updates, great!The only 2 negatives I have is that the UI can be a bit awkward and it took me a good long while to figure out I can buy things from the other villagers. The other negative is that I don't enjoy the fishing minigame but I'm a weirdo who enjoys Stardew Valley fishing. If you're looking for another farming/life sim to sink hours and hours into, Roots of Pacha is a good one to try.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game. It reminded me of stardew valley, but the farming and contributions to the clan felt way more accomplishing (it feels like you're actually helping the clan). Liked the characters in the game as well, they had nice developments and background as you got to know them. Definitely a nice cozy game, can't wait to be playing more.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to recommend this game and it has some good points I would give it a resounding "meh" Super short review version. This is twice the price of Stardew Valley for less than half the content. And feels weirdly jankier, like if someone told me this was the proto Stardew valley or the prequel that SV improved on in almost every way I would have believed them.Longer reviewPro's its a clone of Stardew Valley (though not as good) and has improved the map, and taming animals (and breeding them for improved stats).Now for the things it does worse.1 No combat, hardly necessary and certainly not for all players but weird (esp when both your neighbours are tribes that hate each other and believe the others are monsters)2 Caveman game but no hunting, you can fish, but while you will need meat etc for recipes you have to buy that from the hunter which seems weird, esp since for the first chunk of the game he doesn't hunt, and not just hunting you can't kill your animals to get meat either, so you need meat but you can't get meat, your pet cat appears to hunt, you can't.3 No ranged Combat at least as far as I have gotten (about 18 hours in will edit if I find any)4 Everything feels more aimless, hard to explain why but you don't feel like you're running a farm (like SV) you feel like the only hard working person in the tribe. A tribe member has an idea (a fetch quest every time....) you bring them stuff they make it.5 Watering your crops feels like it takes more time and more stamina than SV. 6. In place of combat is cave exploration, which if you played SV you remember the parts of the mines that required constantly pickaxing your way through slowly, well it's that plus glowing cartoony animal spirits and "puzzles" that are politely described as less than challenging assuming a non lead based paint diet.7. Frequent bugs some minor and some gamebreaking, minor include winning a competition but not getting the reward, major include the game locking up when using the inventory and not letting you close it, meaning the only option is to quit out and restart the day from scratch.8. One thing now I think of it, the fishing is worse than stardew valley, it's legitimately the worst fishing mini game I've played and I've seen people praising it and I can't understand why. Here is how it works, when you fish (its the same pond graphic every time whether your fishing in a river or a beach the only change is there will be orange leaves or snowflakes in the air during autmn or winter...no snow or leaves on the ground always the same) you see the shadow of a fish in the water, you move your cursor over it and as the fish very slowly moves around you keep your cursor over it while a bar fills, once in a while with harder to catch fish you have to move the cursor away to stop an 'alert' bar filling then you go right back to it, it's mind numbing and almost impossible to fail. To put this in perspective I ate lunch with one hand while watching a youtube video and fishing, didn't fail a single fish, I'm really not bragging it's just its that easy, I would imagine that an average 2 year old or similarly mechanically privileged dachshund would have an equally significant success rate. 9 The more I've played it the more it feels like a lazy cash grab, of the 5 areas (excluding the cave for obv. reasons) only 2 appear noticably different in winter (when 2 are covered in snow and the others are just fine, despite being only 5 mins away)For 'fun' I just did nothing for a few days, you don't need to eat or drink and there was no problem that I didn't contribute to the tribe for a week. The progress the tribe makes are almost, if not all, cosmetic "upgrades" to your home land, which translates as clutter to get in the way of you riding across the map.I'm putting time into the game to see if there is more but here are the lands - The "land" your home plus the town Jungle nothing but the community centre from SVBeach, a few trees (some have fruit), water to fish and entrance to the cave systemSavannah grasslands nice array of animals and some plants, entrance to cave system.Forest tree, couple of species of animals, some plants first entrance to cave systemThats it you can explore everything besides the cave in 15 mins (though it takes a couple of hours in game to unlock them, that was my first run of the game so not like I was speed running it) In terms of map size I think all 5 lands combined are probably smaller (and certainly with less to do) than SV farm and town map alone.The cave is just the annoying parts of the mine (constantly smacking rocks to get anywhere) but without the combat or items, also all the transmutations to animals to progress through the cave (sounds awesome, isn't) take several seconds and feel weirdly stiff and dumb, the owl flies but can't fly over rocks. The monkey jumps but can only jump on the set rock pedistals so they are all literally just ways to cross gaps, you can't explore the cave or do anything with them beyond got to monkey platform, become monkey jump across the pedistals (each button press is a single jump that goes to the next platform again 0 skill required) it's like playing frogger but you can't lose, then at the end tranform back to the only functioning cave person in the tribe, and continue.In short if you are completely done with Stardew Valley and are looking for similar this is about as close as you can get, minus my above statements. (I discovered more in the first 5 hours of stardew than this game has in total)That said the current price (£22 is about 40% more than I think it's worth even for a SV fan) get it on sale, if what I've said appeals, but between the lower content, the fact this game has no fail state, even being caught outside after 2am when you pass out didn't seem to have a negative impact, there is simply 0 challenge in this game, it's a mindless time sink and nothing more.Closing thoughts I suspect you can 100% this game in a week and it has all the challenge of an audiobook.

_childDocuments_.review: The game plays alright. In the beginning it can be overwhelming with everything there is to do and the day can feel short. Luckily you can adjust how long a day is now so that helps. Lots to do and lots to explore.Endgame comes a bit too fast for my liking (reached it in year 2 already). The community functions without your help and will grow on its own. Sometimes I feel like I don't know what my place in the town is as a player. _childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Wow I remember how excited I was when I first found out about this game a few years ago! It was always at the top of my “Most Wanted Games” list. Now that it’s FINALLY HERE, 😁 I have to say that I am very impressed! The music is very addictive and I often find myself humming the tunes after taking a break from playing. It is so refreshing to see something different in the farming genre and this ISN’T just a farming life simulation game! I do get a sense of the community involvement from my clan members as ideas are formed and evolved  - which I absolutely love. There is no combat which is also refreshing- I don’t feel stressed while playing but instead very CHILL. There are puzzles to solve in caves, and all the animals are friendly so no need to worry about any danger while exploring! The only thing to watch out for is your stamina which can easily be replenished with food. Thankfully you will not pass out when stamina is at 0 and the game is not punishing if you don’t go to bed by 2:00 a.m. (will just lose some stamina the next day). If playing on the Steam Deck - recommend bumping the Frame Rate from 30 to 60, this solved the stutter issue I encountered while walking/riding on an animal. Other than that, no issues!So far I’m quite enjoying Roots of Pacha especially since I could play at my own relaxed pace. As far as I know, there are no time limits to complete tasks, requests from Clan Members or main quests which is also nice for a change. The developers did a great job on this one. I cannot wait to see the next wave of updates from the kickstarter page which you should definitely check out what they have planned in the future! Combat-Free, plenty to discover and I just made it to Summer! I haven’t even unlocked the other biomes yet either, and I don’t feel rushed to do so.Did I mention you can have a pet baby Mammoth? _childDocuments_.review: I've never purchased a game faster after watching someone else play. Roots of Pacha scratches an itch I didn't even know that I had. While it does share similarities with Stardew Valley, It has enough differences and quality of life improvements that it is distinct (and arguably better) based on more than just the fun prehistory coat of paint. Roots of Pacha is kind enough not to penalize you for mis-clicking and swinging your ax at your spouse. If swigging your tools doesn't accomplish something, then the game generally won't take your stamina for that action. The only exception that I've noticed is with fishing. Probably because you still take a stab even if you exit the mini-game without a catch. Reasonable exception. Roots of Pacha gives you a completely separate inventory for seeds, tools, jewelry, and clothes. Never again will you have to leave valuable tools at home in order to free up some extra space in your pockets! Instead of giving you levels in farming or fishing, Roots of Pacha gives you a "knowledge" system for each crop and fish. (Mining is only progress locked behind tools and there is no combat in this game, so there's not a real equivalent for those skills from SV.) Gaining higher levels of knowledge for a crop can develop them from wild goods to domestic goods. As your knowledge level continues to rise (which happens when you harvest each crop) it will also benefit the quality of the crops harvested even before adding fertilizer. the knowledge levels for fish have a less obvious impact, but still help out. Higher knowledge levels seem to allow you to identify the type of fish a bit faster before catching and reaching level 3 knowledge of a fish makes them easier to catch by removing one of the bars that you are required to fill for a successful catch. The community center equivalent in Roots of Pacha doesn't require you to sacrifice your first grown crops in order to restore it. Instead, this games internal achievements and progression through ideas track your progress through the pyramid in order to heal the land and those living in it. This is a system I prefer since it still allows me to keep/sell all of the fruits of my labor. Breeding animals in SV doesn't do much for you other than give you "free" animals. Roots of Pacha gives their animals a stats system which can be improved through breeding. Each barn animal has three stats: production, quality, and speed. Production allows the animals to produce their good faster, quality improves the base quality of good produced, and speed allows that animal to be a faster mount (most, but not all, barn animals can also be ridden). Everything about the festivals is so well-put-together that i'm genuinely excited to keep encountering them year after year. Some of my personal favorites are the cave painting festival (you are given actual blank cave walls to paint!), the clan gathering/cooking festival (let's me live out my dreams of being a culinary Sherlock Holmes), and the carnival festival (reminds me why I so rarely play Guitar Hero).  While I do enjoy having Elliot lurking around my home as a lawn ornament, he will always be the male counterpart to Leah, the only other "creative" person in town. While making similar characters have a male and female counterpart covers your bases well in terms of satisfying a players romantic desire regardless of their orientation, it also makes the love interests feel less unique. Roots of Pacha seems to steer clear of that (with only one notable exception coming to mind). As i learn more about the characters I may discover more exceptions, but, as of the time of writing this review, the love interests are much more lovable and individualized than in SV. As someone who doesn't want to upset the pixel person who I am trying to romance, this matters a lot to me. I want to see everything that the developers worked hard to make. Having already put 50 hours into my first play through, though, i'm not terribly inclined to create several new games just to see a different set of love interest lore. This helps to soothe my burning desire to 100% games without taking up the next several months of my life. You are sometimes called to care for your newborn by a "your baby is crying!" prompt. Returning to your child while this prompt is active allows you to bottle nurse and change your baby's diaper as an interaction to calm them back down. Pretty standard newborn stuff. Once your baby becomes a toddler, though, you can show them items, dance with them, talk to them with their toddler gibberish, and even choose what they call you as their parent. Incredibly wholesome and much more enjoyable and fulfilling than the moving furniture you're offered in SV. The pets in Roots of Pacha are varied and beautiful, but they are forever locked as babies! This is totally understandable with something like the , but the the wolf pups, bunny kits, , and  could absolutely grow into adults without issue. Something I hope that they implement in the future is the ability for the smaller pets to become adults under your care.Immeasurably charming game full of heart and mechanics that just make sense with the theme. I can hardly imagine a game like this being done better. Easy five stars. Definitely worth the purchase if you are into farming/life sims.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game is fun!You start as a clan of primitive people and by finding new products of nature that you eventually give to your clan they find new ways to process things like food, materials cause they see it and get "Ideas" where you have to give more of the stuff they need to fulfill their idea which gives you more opportunities to advance as people and clan.It's done in a very fun pixel style with Stardew like gameplay which I'm a fan of!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Ranked along Stardew Valley and My Time at Portia,  Roots of Pacha is a very addictive, farming simulator and LifeSim game that keeps you engaged for hours. The mechanics of the game is easy and not too grindy (compared to SOS: A Wonderful Life, HM: Light of Hope).There is farming, ranching and growing of honey. You unlock seeds whenever you find them in the wild. The taming of animals is quite fun since it is a music beat game. I only needed help with the growing of honey since there was very little explanation on the mechanic of growing them. (Spoiler)It helps that the world slowly expands as you advance in the game so that there will always be new things to explore.There are mini games to try for every season, including two races. These games are quite refreshing and intuitive, which breaks the boredom of sticking to the routine of farming and ranching. There are several race course which means that if you participated for all the race course in the first year, they would be different each time.The exploring of cave requires solving puzzles to advance. The powers unlocked by every totem adds to the dynamic of the game. The puzzles are not that difficult that you require a guide but you might need to spend a little time on it. It is good that if you are working on the puzzles, the timer of the day stops, so you don't have to worry about wasting time. The game revolves around the protagonist who is adopted by the tribe and they try to establish themselves in this new land. The characters in the story is fascinating and you might be surprised by little backstory between the NPC themselves when you have a higher relationship with them.Other than the bugs of being stuck in the cave due to walking too close to the edge (which can be resolved), it is a game that I would recommend to players who like this genre and is looking for causal fun
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Very enjoyable! Seems quite polished so far; similar mechanics to Stardew Valley but somewhat different vibe... more teamwork, less buying affection from strangers. I'm very curious to see how the relationships with your tribe members develop. The paleo/neolithic setting is very interesting. Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is certainly going to be one of my all time favorite cozy/farming games. Every time I think I can't say how impressed I am with the game something new happens and dang I'm impressed again! There is so much to do, the game is very unique and playing co op has been a blast. This game seems to have really listened to what gamers in this genre really wanted and just nailed it all. Can't recommend this game highly enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Loving it so far - If you are looking for a cozy, relaxing music farm sim I don't think you can go wrong here. There is no combat so it's just purely focused on the farm and relationship building aspects of the game. I like the time period being the brink of agriculture and civilization, it makes progression feel more immersive and rewarding to see your improvements affect the "wildness" of your plants and domestication of your animals. Like any farm sim, it's going to be repetitive, but I like the cute mini games for things like taming animals which use music and rhythm in them. The relationships you build with your fellow Pachans lead to lots of cute little scenes and conversations. You can tame a cave lion for a pet and really that's all this game needed to win me over. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Stardew Valley with Mammoths!What can I say more? This game is cute and fun and has a lot to offer:+ Farming, Livestocks, Fishing, (the fishing mini game is less finicky than in most other games)+ Use Based Leveling & Learning. (The more you harvest of a specific plant, the more you learn about it, the game doesn't just give you all Info like when to grow a plant. You have to harvest them and figure it out)+ A prehistorical Community Center (of some sorts) to "rebuild"+ Already a lot of Community Events with your Clan which offer more fun Mini Games which can be done but most not be "mastered" to gain rewards. Some are difficult to master but participating is enough.+ A nice little story I havent even barely finished after 20h of gameplay+ Relationships and a Special form of trading+ Really adorable Spirit Animals (This little guys are so cute and neon)+++ BABY MAMMOTHS & and much more! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A quirky prehistoric version of Stardew in some ways with lots of exploring and unlocking of secrets in the cave system.  My only complaint would be a more comprehensive guide page as several things aren't clear when unlocking recipes or achievements and looking around online for answers seems to be your best bet.

_childDocuments_.review: Its ok but way worse than stardew valley. whats the point of making a game that is not as good as something that already exists? its missing the skill tree, the endgame, the fighting system, the fishing game is ♥♥♥♥, the seed gathering is annoying and the system of domesticating plants isnt used to its full potential at all. the production of refined produce feels clunky and the tools you use to make them just take up way too much space. this game would have been better if they had just copied stardew valley one to one and added their ideas like the animal music thingy with the mounting and the stone age skin. im giving it a thumbs up because its not a bad game but if you are making a clone atleast improve upon it like stardew valley improved upon harvest moon or make it more unique like my time at portia/sandrock.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: It's a good game for farm sim fans out there.Most of all I like the prehistoric twist on everything: - you don't sell stuff, you contribute to your tribe's development.- you don't mine copper, silver and gold, you mine flint, obsidian and copper (although gold and silver are present in the game, they serve a different purpose).- you don't have sprinklers, you have ollas which you fill with water and they leak overnight.- you don't have to buy seeds and animals, you can find them in the wild and take home. Then you breed animals for better stats and plants change their quality as your knowledge of them increases.Gameplay-wise:- there is no fighting in the caves, just a few puzzles here and there. This is pleasant, as fighting can be annoying in farm sims.- fishing is not a QTE or a "mash the button to keep the bobble in the green radius" thing. It's very simple.- if family aspect is important to you, you can start a family in this game and have children who will grow up and develop their personalities.All in all the gameplay loop here is very pleasant but here's what I didn't like about the game:1) The progression here is not evenly linear, if that makes sense. For the first 1-1.5 seasons you scrape by, selling whatever you can find, then when you invent brewing, you suddenly make a lot of money and can afford basically anything, and then suddenly it grinds to a halt and unless you like setting your own goals, like catching all rare-colored animals or earning 100k contribution for an achievement, you may find that there's nothing else to do, because:2) some of the things (for example, certain plants and animals) only unlock once you build certain tiers of the pyramid. It could be compared to raising your town rank in other games, but I personally found it to be a bit tedious. Especially because one of the prophecies needed for raising the pyramid requires cooking and I personally don't like cooking in farm sims (also I didn't really feel the need to cook in this game, because your fellow tribespeople give you food sometimes and you can also earn it from races and events, and for me that was more than enough).3) Another minor issue is that there are a couple vendors in this game who have their goods in categories, and it's not immediately obvious. I was looking forward to buying decor and furniture for my hut, but all I could see in the vendor's inventory is pots. I thought it was the only available type of decor, but it turned out all other items were in different categories, which are not highlighted in any way.All in all I can recommend this game because I thoroughly enjoyed my 30 hours in it (got bored by Winter, 1 and won't continue playing). However for me personally it doesn't have much gameplay value unless there is a big update that adds lots of stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty similar to SDV, a very good game to relax playing it... I just miss the combat sometimes, but you will not remember that all the time. All characters have personality, i have so much fun times with the dialogs of them. Farming and Livestock is the same of SDV, but farming especially, cost so much time, because, here the irrigation only unlock after gathing tin in the caves, so i get the system pretty late in my run, so if you dont habe the irrigation, small fields is better, to save stamina for all other contents.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I love Roots of Pacha. The graphics is cute and some bits of the game I find endearing. It's quite nice that I live with my family at the start of the game. I really like the crops mechanic too, they evolve! Everything actually starts out quite primitive. Then the tribe improves along with the player unlocking upgrades. This was something that was nice to experience. Later when you've raised the affection levels of the villagers a bit, you get some scenes where you get to know them and some dialogue changes. The gossip in game is actually quite entertaining lol. Best perk though is they give you items.Other bits of the game that I really like- The selection of animals and the mounts! I enjoyed breeding my animals for speed.  The weekend races are also something I look forward to in-game.- Dancing, festivals, pots and painting!I haven't unlocked everything yet. Looking forward to future updates!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Although smaller in scope, Roots of Pacha for me, in terms of art, beats Stardew Valley, game that I have over 4000 hours of playing. I absolute hate the Fall songs in SV but I love RoP music, and when I play SV, I play RoP OST as background music on loop, specially the Spring Theme. The crops are beautiful, the character portraits are stunning, the animal sprites are well drawn, I love them all. RoP also stepped up a notch with the Tool and Seed Wheels. I think they are better than the carrying system in SV. RoP also excels in festivals. While in SV festivals are days that I'll waste because I can't enter the shops to buy supplies, I'm eager to festival days in RoP, because they are lots of fun. Many, many mini games, I love the Saturday running copetitions and drawing Pixelart in cave walls. I've drawn Sonic, Mario, Luigi, Bomberman and anything my creativity allows. The game also gives you the opportunity of training the minigames before going to the real match.I also love anthropology, so I absolutely love domesticating new crops, new animals and discovering new technologies to improve everyone's lives. For me, Roots of Pacha is a must have for anyone who loves Stardew Valley and Stone Age stuff.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This game presents a truly charming 2D pixel art style, and it was the visuals themselves that captivated me the most. The game is clearly geared toward children, as it lacks any violent elements. Moreover, it avoids any negative, pessimistic, or objectionable behaviors. It is a game intended for individuals who would like to play with their young children without exposing them to such situations. I highly recommend it; this game provided me with incredible entertainment, and I invested a significant amount of time in it.Funny thing, I discovered how inclusive the game aimed to be even on the code level, although terms like "gender" don't quite apply to an ostrich or a mammoth :)

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the game when I first bought it. It reminded me of Harvest Moon/Story of Seasons but with a twist! I had to pause for a bit after it felt a bit repetitive. _childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoy a lot of the content in this game, and personally prefer some systems to other games - specifically the animals. My personal preference would be for a more complex farming system compared to Stardew Valley, which I feel is a direction the game could go in, but would perhaps impact the chill, low-stakes nature of farming sims in general.Everything is just a bit more complicated, which is fine for what it is, but means I'm usually reaching for Stardew Valley first. I feel that if the game is set up to be very amenable to replayability, and I see potential in the evolution system to allow for different styles of gameplay and very different farms/camps each playthrough, which hasn't quite come through in the 100 or so hours I played - after not-quite finishing once, I didn't feel the desire to replay as I did Stardew Valley.I feel that the static camp and set slots to build contribute to the lack of replayability pretty significantly, and also reduce the amount of thought you can put into your setup. Having said that, there is clearly a lot to like - the 100 hours I spent in it were very much enjoyed, I liked the fresh take on the genre and particularly enjoyed the sense of community from the style they went for, and would overall recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: You wouldn't have thought that a game well into patch 1.2 would be so damn boring. The game progression being tied to prosperity (how much money you made) just feels like going from one buzzkill to another. Ugh... i gotta wait another 2/3 days for what's his/her face to Einstein-up their wacko idea, like... like an art station... Reese... baby girl… are you just wanting the tax payer to foot the bill for your bigger workshop? And how come Ata, a freaking 9 years old who wants to move out the house because there was a spider in her bed, comes up with idea for bronze metal working. Dude, make her chief, we'll be living in luxury condos with robot butlers in no time. All the other NPCs are weirdos anyways, asking me to give them 50 flint for a breeding pen: what!? Tetih, can I just give you 100 stone instead? Flint, is kinda like a luxury at the moment.Anyways, you'll be like,... man... I'm tired of fishing: fishing sucks, it's so boring and unrewarding. Oh! i know, I’ll go cave diving (this game equivalent of the mines in Stardew except lamer). Psyche! you can't progress further until your prosperity is high enough until Yosemite Sam think of this great idea called getting drunk (making beer/wine)! Why... why does the farmer need alcohol...? because a pile of rocks in shape of bear said it needed wine. What? Maybe the farmer needs to lay off the shrooms before picking up another vice. (By the way, pretty sure the red mushroom is toxic in real life.)AND the bear rock want honey too; DO YOU KNOW HOW LONG IT TAKES TO MAKE HONEY? And, the bear locks up any further progression in the cave. Not only do you have grow four sunflower (and god forbid, if you didn't know it ahead of time that you needed four sunflower to obtain honey; you'll be waiting an extra 5 days or more). You need four sunflower because once you hit 55k prosperity (really?!... for honey? it bearly [pun intended] sells for jack), Zeda will ask for it... so she can come up with this totally disrupted tech called a beehive; which by way, took her two days to cook up.Is the farmer stupid or apathetic? And don't tell me the player's character ain't a farmer, I don't see anyone else growing food. Dude, our character been growing the whole village's food supply and never comes up with anything? How come everyone in the game is cooking up a fierce storm of ideas, but our character can't even come up with an idea. Instead, they choose to stand by the press and make juice from morning to night. For the love of Pacha, our character should just lookup some primitive technology videos and get inspired /sSeriously though, the heck was the dev thinking... is watching your character juice up 40 carrots fun? It's boring as !@#; and then the waterwheel is lockup at 300K prosperity. Really? That's anti-fun; that's called being grindy for the sake of being grindy. Give me some in between tech, yeesh. Do you know how much energy exploring the caves takes? Here's an unlockable, the juicer, that's supposed to convert your harvest into a decent source of energy... but, oh wait, it consumes a bunch of time (and there's no way to speed it up): back to fishing, I guess, because cooking fish takes zero time (even if it's 20 fish) and you didn’t waste a crop that took 4/6/8/(w/e) days to grow.And what's with the focus on fishing being the primary source of income in the early game, was nothing learn from Stardew? That's like one of the flaws of Stardew (early game fishing being the only reliable money maker; it just drawfs everything else). They need to take a page from Fields of Mistria: buy and go play it; they could use some inspiration like the farmer by watching primitive technology! (But seriously, Fields of Mistria does have some great ideas, particularly the mines).Anyways, back to the honey. You gotta grow four sunflower (5 days + another 5 days if you didn't know Zeda would ask for it), Zeda takes another 2 days to research the beehive, then you have to place the beehive and wait another 6/7/8/(who the heck knows; even the wiki doesn't know) days. And by the way, Zeda isn't always available (there are days in which you cannot talk to her; she's not visiting Pacha), so if you're unlucky enough; her research may take 2 additional days. That's freaking brutal; just to be quickly buzzkill by the bronze watering can (you have to wait 3 days for Ata to research bronze metal working, then you have to wait 2 days(?) for the station to be upgraded, and then you have to wait 2 days for Acre to make you the bronze watering can. And, the cherry on top, 120K prosperity requirement). Worst part is that the cave is a terrible source of income (heck, it's probably an income sink).The progression is annoying. It wouldn't be so bad if there was something else to do instead while you’re waiting... that's not, you know... fishing (which is !@# boring). What else is there? Foraging for manure in the savannah? Dude, let me let me fight a lion or a mammoth with nothing but my handstone --- I think I’m up for it. Fine, fine, at least have a community-center-like quest line. And no, the pyramid thing doesn't count; you were going to do that stuff anyways. What? Did the dev think when Yosemite Sam hands you the brewer you weren’t gonna see if Al Capone was your spirit animal?Yosemite Sam: Hey, I just came up with this great idea: BEER!	Player: Uhh... I don't drink bud.Yosemite Sam: You what!?Player: Yeah, I don't drink... I do SHroOms!Laughs (maybe) aside, kind of a disappointing game; especially given the price tag (and that it's out of early access) relative to its competition in terms on value per dollar. I guess if you exhausted all of the "good" stardew-esque games on steam; this one is okay-ish and worth trying (just don't come in thinking it's Coral Island, Dinkum, Sun Haven, My Time at Sandrock, or something). 6.75/10
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. It's extremely well polished and the characters are all pretty charming. The farming aspect is fantastic and I can't wait for the future updates the kickstarter promised. I am completely in love with the idea of domesticating crops and I can't wait for the domesticated animal update. The building upgrades are also fun to work towards and contain plenty of QoL functions other farming sims lack, so that's a big plus. Auto animal harvest, feeding, and being able to cook from storage after a certain period to name a few.That being said, the game does have some issues for me. For one, there isn't much to do after the first year. I somehow managed to complete everything by spring year 2 after trying my best to play as slowly as I could tolerate. There also isn't much to do with your money after you buy all the upgrades other than to spend it on seeds. I'm also sitting on a ton of ores that I wish I could find some other use for. Maybe make it so you need money plus the ores and other materials to buy furniture. The characters, while charming, feel kind of flat. They have one dialogue per day and they repeat eventually. There's also not much happening after you marry them. Your spouse kind of just exists. Massive FPS drops. I'd be working around my farm and notice my FPS tank. From max FPS to 20 or lower and it's killer on my eyes. So if you're photophobic like I am, I'd play the game with caution because I'd be vibin' and next thing I know I'm lying back in my chair feeling extremely sick. And the worst offence of all, in my book... the arches can't be rotated. They gave us these beautiful arches, but I can't use them on the side of my farms. An absolute tragedy.  All in all, this is a fantastic game. I cannot wait for the future updates; this game has a bright future ahead of it. My only real wish, other than some superficial additions like more crops and ways to spend money/materials, is that they fix the FPS drops because this issue makes the game almost unplayable for me sometimes.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lot of fun so far! Definitely in a similar vein as Stardew, minus combat (which honestly... thank goodness, I like to keep my farming sims and shoot 'em ups separate, tyvm). I also love the setting, it feels very unique, even if gameplay-wise it's very standard for the genre! I think my only nitpick is that sometimes the directions for certain things (items needed for tasks for example) are sometimes a bit vague and take a little head scratching to figure out; but honestly give it a couple of days and there will be enough guides online that that won't be a problem either.  Overall a solid 9/10 from me, definitely recommend if you've sunk hundreds of hours into Stardew like I have.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Love it! It's a lovely farm life sim with an enjoyable twist. The characters and world are vibrant, and I love that there's always something to do. The prehistoric/stone age theme is a really nice touch without feeling too cliche, and the underlying motif of discovery and innovation, that everything in the world is new, always makes me want to see how much more there is to learn. I'm not all that good at writing reviews lol, so to summarize: Neolithic Stardew Valley Prequel= :D
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing take on the common farm sim. Too early to tell if it'll be the next 'Stardew', but its a promising start. I wonder what the modding community will do with it. If you like games like 'Stardew valley', 'Coral island', 'Travellers Rest', 'My time in Portia/Sandrock' and other cosy chill-out games where the game play loop is generally doing tasks for NPCs and exploring the world without any stress, and you like more of an Indie pixel art-style, I think It's definitely worth a good look in my humble opinion. Although these games are getting more popular the good ones are few and far between. This one looks like it could hold it's own and scratch that itch for a lot of people. At the very least it'll be something to fill the void until 'The Haunted Chocolatier' or chucklefish's 'Witchbrook' comes out.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only in summer of my first year, but I've very much enjoyed experiencing the gradual evolution as my community discovers new ideas to improve lives for their community, watching my foraged plants grow slowly to better quality, domesticated plants, and so forth. It can be a bit hard to balance the necessary mining with your other "duties", but so far, the game has been delightful. I love discovering new seeds and animals in each season, in each biosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting take on the genre. I find I spend as much time on this as I did on the original stardew valley, which says a lot. It has some uniqueness, especially around how you develop new technologies by doing stuff in the world and by donating stuff to make your village prosper. I highly recommend this to those who enjoy the genre.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I really appreciate that Roots of Pacha even exists. There is no other game that I can create an orchard of almond trees, watch them grow over the days, harvest the almonds and turn them into almond milk which I can then turn into almond milk cheese. Lastly adding rosemary to the cheese to make herb milk cheese. Thank goodness. I enjoy trotting around on a horse through the orchard, slowing down and enjoying the abundance of time. There is always another day.I really appreciate that there is no combat because games are supposed to be fun and fighting a living being or pretending to fight is not fun. The characters in Roots of Pacha are enjoying life. We can dance with each other. I can play my flute, which is suppose to be for befriending animals, but I can just use it for fun. In multiplayer we can play hide and seek in the forest and try to find each other. It's fun. I get to laugh and smile.It was a surprise when characters started giving gifts back, I really appreciate that the friendships aren't one way, they are caring for each other. The contribution system of giving to the community works really well. I'm grateful that I don't need to think how much currency or what the dollar value of something is. Money is dumb and made up and I'm glad it doesn't exist in this game.I'll end by saying I know this game isn't for everyone, it isn't mainstream, but this game has helped me enjoy life more and my life is better for it. Thanks
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: A fun (and pretty) new take on the farm sim genre! I'm at the end of my 2nd Spring but I haven't actually started exploring romance properly yet so I can't speak much on that aspect. I will say there's a good variety of characters and personalities available to romance (though some of my favourites are non-romanceable). The character portraits are well done and emotive. The dialogue is well written and doesn't feel as repetitive as other farming sims I've played.  Characters will often give clues to their friends and family members favourite gifts and I wish these were perhaps recorded in the characters' tab as they're discovered instead of having to write my own notes. It would also encourage and reward the player to make more connections in town regularly from the start of the game instead of just foraging, fishing and watering crops all day.Really enjoy the concept of working together with the clan to develop 'ideas' and contributing towards the clan rather than having a monetary system. It's also really lovely seeing the clan working together to build up and decorate the area over time rather than your sim being the sole contributor. Not to mention how the characters' schedules change to interact with these spaces. All these little things make their lives and the world feel more dynamic. There's a variety of decor you can purchase for your home (and to place in your field and around town) which I'm only just starting to explore. For the first few seasons I didn't even realise some of the "shops" have multiple tabs of goods to purchase so I've only just started planting my orchard in year 2! Some of the objects are able to be rotated but the arches don't appear to be which is a shame as I'd like to place a few around my field.The cave system provided a good level of challenge. Many times I couldn't get to a "portal" in time to get home before 2am I was so absorbed in trying to progress and get to the next room. The cooking system is good and there's a decent amount of dishes (considering the stone age setting) but I wish the kitchen had a bit more food storage or recipes can take from chests within your home. The fishing mini-game is easy to pick up but a little slow, and time doesn't stop during so it's easy to lose hours of time trying to catch a few rarer fish. I also wish the smoker was a bit more lucrative because it doesn't really seem worth having when drying fish/meat on the solar dryer has better returns.Farming takes up a lot of time the first few seasons but speeds up dramatically as you learn and upgrade ideas and tools. I unlocked the irrigation system during my 1st Winter and it has made such a difference to my day. There's also a great number of crops to grow in Winter unlike many other farm sims I've played so the season doesn't slow down or feel like a grind as much. Changing tools is easy enough (press tab to cycle through) but I do wish there was a way to jump backwards to the previous tool (i.e. shift+tab) instead of opening the wheel to choose. It would speed up clearing the fields of rocks, branches and grass.Animal husbandry is quite good and similar to other farm sims though there's not a brush tool (at least from what I've played). The flute rhythm mini-game to build friendships with the wild animals is easy to pick up. You can play your flute nearby a herd and see how individuals respond to quickly recall which ones you were trying to build relationships with as some have identical patterns. There's a variety of different animals to domesticate and of each a variety of colours and types so it's fun to try and "catch" them all, and breed newer generations that are faster and have better production. Though that's something you won't be able to do without releasing older generations to make room, unless you focus on building lots of barns instead of growing crops. The fortnightly race mini-game is also some good fun and the food prizes make it worthwhile as they make good gifts or can help provide a much needed stamina boost with spelunking through caves, clearing your fields, gathering materials etc. Aside from that it provides a good break from the regular day-to-day schedule.It's a solid game and a great addition to the genre. Apologies to the team if any of my suggestions are already in game and I just haven't realised/unlocked it yet. This review is by no means exhaustive as I'm learning more about the game all the time!  But I'm very much enjoying it and would recommend to anyone who enjoys a cosy farming sim and wants something a little different from the same old.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't review games at all. in fact I think I may have only 1 or 2 other reviews that I have honestly given in the past.  This game however has entranced me and brought me back to the feelings of Harvest Moon: Back to Nature or a Wonderful Life. This game was originally recommended to me by my Wife and I thought "Oh it's like Stardew Valley I suppose I could try it and refund it" How wrong I was. I didn't refund it, in fact I am recommending it to the greatest extent possible.  The graphic style may be reminiscent to Stardew but the game play, the sprites, and the overall pacing have been a joy to play. One thing that normally irks me in these types of games is the art style. I am a stickler when it comes to art style and this game was a breath of fresh air. No one had weird noses, no one had weird walking styles, and there hasn't been a time where I thought "Why did they think it was a good idea to do that?". The art is clean and, I think, appropriate for the feeling the game is trying to create. As I played I think what got me most of all is the Music. I am a giant sucker for music in video games and I think they knocked it out of the park. The music creates such a chill atmosphere and each area of the game has different versions of the main season music that plays that it compliments the game play overall. It really does a good job of differentiating each area so you don't get tired of looping music and really makes each area feel unique and special.I've only scratched the surface of this game but I am enjoying it immensely. It may not be for everyone but it certainly is for me. I hope you give it a try.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally something refreshing and unique among all those farming sims. Usually it only takes me a few hours or days to get bored easily due to repetitive tasks or stiff conversations with villagers. Roots of Pacha has so many things to discover, you're getting hooked into the story and little puzzles and the pixel art offers so many beautiful details in the characters and landscapes. Sometimes I have to stop playing for a while, just to take some time to absorb everything with my eyes. Looking forward to more gaming hours - really addicting and fun!
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: I can't believe that I haven't heard more about this cozy game; it is really great!  Roots of Pacha adds polish on the farming formulas which has roots in Harvest Moon, but exploded into the mainstream with Stardew Valley.  Roots of Pacha is pumping new life into the genre by making familiar things like animal products and mounts available much earlier in the game, and de-emphasizing crop farming as the central way of making 'money'.  Also, the technology/unlocks rely a bit more on the townspeople, so it feels like less of a chore to leave the farm and visit with them, giving a much greater sense of meaning to the interactions.  I can't wait to find out what secrets the game still holds, so I expect this review at just under 12 hours will be relatively early in my eventual playtime.

_childDocuments_.review: As a stardew fan for many years, this fresh take on the farm sim has me intrigued and involved in what there is to discover in the exploration of the new characters and play style. The characters are interesting and the dialogue they have is enticing, giving the game a feel that you really are living off the land. I enjoy the concept that you learn things as you go, e.g. how long different crops grow. The community based structure of the town (or clan) has me wanting to progress in the game and see what is next to come as far as the advancement of the efficiency of tasks.5 hours in and many more to come, I recommend this game to anyone who has played stardew valley or (throwback) harvest moon. _childDocuments_.review: Wow! I am blown away. The attuning feature is incredibly fun and unique. Simple and complex at the same time with nods to more modern farming sims like SDV - I give it a 10/10 so far. I also heard a rumor that there may be a rival "marriage" feature in this game, which is very exciting for an OG Harvest Moon fan! _childDocuments_.review: 8/10 A cute and fun farming game with no combat.Nice music, cute graphics, a unique world setting (for a farming game), and lots to do makes Roots of Pacha a solidly engaging experience. The seasonal events and associated mini-games are lots of fun, the story is enjoyable without being overly complicated, and the friendship/romance system is a carbon copy of Stardew Valley. The pets and mounts are nicely varied, as are the cave exploration puzzles.The downsides are few but important. First, most of the NPCs are fairly bland, making it hard to remember (or care) who's who. The village progression/quests are very undemanding, meaning that MOST of the crops you can grow are not necessary for the game's progression. Finally, the daily routine can get very grinding after a few hours, making the game over-stay its welcome once you're done exploring the caves.That said, if you're looking for a fun farming game in a unique setting, Roots of Pacha is a good place to be.
