_childDocuments_.review: This game is quickly becoming my favorite game of 2023. The stone age setting is great, the visuals are really charming, the storyline and progression are quite nice. The caves are really cool, the only thing is that it might be a bit too hand-holdy. Especially the repeated picture of "you need an axe to cut this vine" like, yeah i saw it the first time and it makes sense that i need to do the same thing again, please let me figure this out for myself. We also don't need dialog explaining every cave painting, the whole point is that we can see what you mean by having eyes. The farming is pretty basic, but i like it. The fishing mechanic is great.And what i really, really like is how they make you choose where the important buildings go. It really helps with making you feel like you have an impact on how this primitive village develops. What i also like is that, while you are a great influence, the village will actually continue to develop on its own, slowly but surely. For example, they will find better ways to do the laundry, barricade the rivers so kids don't drown and build torches so people can see at night. All this, while sped up by your progress, basically without player interference. It really helps with the immersion, making you feel like an actual part of the village instead of just "the main character that everyone is helpless without".

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty good, entertaining, chill and beautiful Stardew Valley-like game. The prehistoric setting is nicely represented (with many understandable and obvious inaccuracies), with a secondary touch of fantasy and cute visuals. Gameplay is similar to the games of the like, but feels unique enough through the prehistoric setting and some nice touches. It has its kinda grindy part, but it's one of the less annoying grinds I've encountered in the genre (unless you want to 100% the achievements playing solo, in that case brace yourselves), and I had a good time with it, especially playing co-op.Find seeds in the nature, learn about them and grow them as an agriculture pioneer. Fish everywhere. Tame wild animals and bring them to your primitive farm. Have a little mammoth or a purple fluffy spider as pets. Befriend the townsfolk, romance someone, have kids. Solve the caverns mysteries using the sacred beasts powers. Develop the village and raise the mysterious jungle structure.If you are looking for a chill and cute game with plenty to do, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could recommend this game, as it has so much potential, and clearly the developer put a lot of love and care into the product.  However, it has balance problems that make much of the game unrewarding.1. The most lucrative way to earn "money"/contribution points is fishing, by a long shot.  You can can easily make thousands per day just "selling" dried fish.  Unfortunately the fishing minigame is extremely dull and simple.2. The progression path is all about farming and raising animals.  However, neither of these will earn enough to make the activities worthwhile.  We kept waiting for the next machine to process foods or animal products that would pay off, but it never happened.  It takes the majority of an entire day to process, for example, a fruit wine that will sell for 19 points.  Yet we can sell a single dried fish for hundreds.3.  There's no risk.  You basically can't do anything wrong.  There are no aspects of the game that introduce even the slightest tension.  I understand the theme that the game is going for, and that's fine, but it's not for me.  4.  Sharing "money" and seeds in coop mode is a real turn off for us.  I understand that this is part of the theme of the game, but there's nothing really to collectively work towards.  You work collectively because you have to, not because there is a compelling reason to do so.  Thus, nobody really wants to spend on frivolous things like decorations that could make the game a little more fun.5.  There's little charm to the characters, and I suspect it's because there are just too many.  I ended up dreading cutscenes, and while some of the festivals were amusing, many of them were simply tedious.After >15 hours I find myself irritated and mad at the game.  I'm running around busting my buns for the clan, but the rest of the clansfolk lounge around dancing and playing flutes, and all for no significant feeling of reward.  It's intended to be a positive nod to humanity working together, but feels more like a subtle criticism of communism.This is a game for people who simply like to build a farm and interact with NPCs.  I'm not trying to dis people who like it, to each there own.  But if you're approaching this thinking that it might scratch a Stardew itch, it's not that.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't want to compare this game to Stardew Valley, so I try not to.I just LOVE this game. I'm now in my second year of the game. You start in Pacha with your (adopted) grandparents. They greet you and give you simple tasks like weed this en chop that. It's a really nice way to understand the basics. You have a tool belt with three sections: seeds, tools and inventory. You can buy seeds from your grandfather after you obtained the plant nursery, but you can find seeds that are in season on the lands. With knowledge the plants get better quality and with better quality your food gets better. Just a great and logical concept. You also get a lot of space to build on. So no worries about that. Another thing that stands out is the currency. The currency is contribution. You can donate food or supplies to the clan and you get rewarded with clan prosper. With enough clan prosper you get ideas from the clan members and this is a major mechanic for progression. You can make new items, resources and tools if you have enough progession. It really feels like you belong there and that you're needed. I love that idea.Another thing are the animals. All over Pacha are wild animals that you can tame by playing the flute. After you tamed them, you can invite them on your land if you have a shed. Then they give you resourses like milk and fur. But the nice thing is that each animal has a quality, production and speed. You'll learn what those mean in game. Breeding is vital to improving an animal's stats. Animals part of a second generation will often yield higher stats than their parents. So you just want to have the best animals. The ones you don't want anymore? You can release them or chop them for meat. Well.. not really. Someone does that for you.At this point my focus lays on the plants and the animals, so I don't have great releationships with the clan. At certain friendship points you get cutscenes and they are really well put and give you insight in the characters. I can't wait to get closer to each clan member and see a romance blossem at some point.With certain things you really have to think and I love that in a farming game. I have so many more things to say that I love about this game, but you just have to buy it to see it. I can't think of something I really don't like about it. At first I was sceptic, because Stardew Valley is in my heart and no game can top that, but this game is really great. I would recommend it 100%.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The gameplay is solid, the atmosphere nice. Do like how technology is unlocked in a somewhat organic and believable manner from several different characters on a context driven manner. Love how you can locate NPC's and track them in real time something I wished other similar games did before. I do enjoy this game. So why the thumbs down? The game heavily implies a hunting system that doesn't exist. Your initial cooking recipes call for meat. There are multiple hunter characters. And yes the simple fact they're all cavemen. The only way to obtain meat in the game is to talk to one particular NPC and ask him for meat. That's it. To contrast it, there is a Dedicated fisher kinda like the dedicated hunter. Your able to fish personally. You fish initially with a hand axe implying your stabbing the fish. Then unlock a fishing spear later for spear fishing.. Yet hunting Animals doesn't appear to be an option at all. This has marred my experience as I've been actively looking to hunt since day 1 of spring 1. I'm now into my first week of summer and no closer to hunting. I mean it's a silly thing sure but as I said. The game heavily implies hunting as an activity. Feels as off as a Wild West Game with no guns.

_childDocuments_.review: I have one minor complaint and I'm going to just get it out of the way first: The UI is slightly janky. On mouse and keyboard, it feels like my inputs are getting eaten when I try to navigate certain menus. On controller, cycling through the different ring menus feels really clunky.That minor thing aside, I'm enjoying this. The game uses the stone age setting well. I really like that it depicts early humans having less information but the same intelligence as we do today. A lot of the game's progression is NPCs discovering something new or noticing something unexpected happening, then going, "How can we replicate/use this?" I also like that the game gives you some options to say "no" on some game mechanics. If you don't care about romance options you can just turn them off. If you don't want to kill your animals, you can tell the butcher you won't be sending him any and the option stops showing up in the menu. You can replace meat in (most?) situations with processed legumes. I'm not doing any of those things, but I really like seeing the option.Anyway, money well spent.

You can not only shear and milk them, but also use them as mounts. The racing is unique and well done as well. There's also this mysterious cave that has a lot of puzzles to solve. _childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever review games, but this one deserves a lot more love! It is a very fresh take on the Farming/Life Sim genre. I thought that the story and characters were well written, the setting is interesting to explore, and the game is super addicting. I thought that the puzzles and mini games were well thought out and challenging, whereas in other games in this genre they are usually a forgettable afterthought. I am thoroughly hooked! Anyone who likes the Harvest Moon franchise or Stardew Valley should 100 % play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Stardew Valley, you'll find yourself right at home with Roots of Pacha. It has lovely pixel art, relaxing music, and a perfectly simple and intuitive user interface. It's just a really nice laid back, peaceful experience. What the game could use more of is work on its dialogue. At its best it isn't good, and at its worst we get generic, placeholder responses to receiving a gift like "This is okay [name]" or simply "Thanks." These seemed fine in Early Access, but I hope the developers can change these to add more flavor to the game and help develop the characters better.My only other minor complain is that the red mushrooms that look like fly agaric are edible when they are in fact poisonous. I'm not saying they should kill you, but they shouldn't be edible, at least not consumed raw.
_childDocuments_.name: Roots of Pacha

_childDocuments_.review: The change in setting is a breath of fresh air in this saturated genre. The sense of progression is evident when it comes to upgrading your tools, unlocking new town facilities and technologies, and how your plants are slowly changing into their modern equivalents and more. Quest lists are neatly arranged with quest givers easily found on the map.Although, while the first few days are slow, eventually you'll have so much to do that the in game day is too short (around 20 minutes). Hopefully the devs will allow players to tweak the day length in a future update as they promised in a Steam thread discussion.When it comes to exploration, the caves have puzzle based obstacles that'll allow you to open up new rooms and acquire uncommon materials. The huge areas outside of town really lends itself to exploration as you discover wild varieties of plants and animals which are tracked on your map once discovered.When it comes to befriending the townsfolk and romanceables, you can only give them gifts once a day twice a week. All the gifts you've given will have a like and disliked list within their profile along with their family relationships.Taming animals is easy and I've heard that there is a breeding system. Getting a rideable animal helps you in travelling the huge maps.I haven't tried multiplayer and I didn't bought this game for this feature but according to reviews in Youtube, you have to make a new character when joining someone else's world which means starting from 0 when it comes to tools. It'll be quite inconvenient for those who want a casual drop in and play session so if you want to play with a friend, play together from day 1. I also hope that the devs will allow players to use their existing characters in multiplayer.That's all for now. If those two issues are fixed then this game will be close to perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting a long time for a game on par with Stardew Valley, but I was honestly delighted because this game in many ways surpasses it.  Pros:-As much as characters can be that you talk to every day, I think these are delightful. There are idiosyncrasies and character flaws to some characters, but many of the characters are self-aware, which you learn through cutscenes.-I love that the characters have somewhat varied dialogue. I love that you can learn what gifts certain characters prefer from their family member or neighbor. This beats looking things up for me, because I'd much rather find things out organically in the game!-The taming and breeding mechanism keeps my long-term interest in the game. The Stone Age animal types breathe a bit of life into the typical ranch archetypes.-The variety of mounts is a nice touch, and the biweekly races are a nice way to encourage regularly interacting with the community.-I loved the story line and the idea of neighboring clans that you can trade with.-I know it isn't for everyone, but I personally thought the cave was really fun! I really liked that it was a puzzle rather than a dungeon! I loved the introduction of the totems and their abilities.-Cooking is fun, and I like that you can make dishes using other dishes you've made.-The celebrations are unique and wholesome.-You can make the day longer!!!!-I love that the team continues to work to add value to the game. I think having a game set in the Stone Age gives a lot of room for the game to grow, and I'm really looking for to future updates and expansions!-Also, what's your favorite character and why is it Igrork?Things I haven't thoroughly explored:-I haven't had a Union or a child yet - I'm waiting to acquire all the character cutscenes and choose from there.-I haven't really delved into fishing - it takes a lot of time from the day, and I feel like it's a lower-value way to spend time.-Rare and legendary forms - I'll probably pursue this after I start getting perfect-stat animals.-Multiplayer - soon!Not Pros:-Maybe a future update could include nomadic clans or neighboring clans that cause some discomfort? The game is currently entirely wholesome.-I'd love for the personal pets to be able to grow up into their mature forms! I was disappointed that I couldn't  have a mature cave lion or mammoth (this one makes sense tbf) as a pet.-I'd like to be able to interact with the community buildings - I think it would make me feel more a part of the community.-Something that I would have liked was making the story more challenging to progress, i.e. making it dependent on multiple factors rather than based on the total community contributions.-I'm...surprised? that in a Stone Age game, you can't cull your own animals or wild animals for meat. You have to go through another character for meat acquisition.As I said, I'm excited to see more from this game. I hope this helps other people to decide if they might be interested in giving it a try!

_childDocuments_.review: !!!FOR EVERYONE LOOKING FOR A GOOD AND FUN CO OP GAME!!!I bought this for my sister to celebrate her purchase of her first gaming rig. From the menu screen you select that you're going to be playing this as multi-player and you both will go through character creation separate before it tosses you in together. These are my thoughts after 4 hours playing together. We are having SO much fun. The characters are great, both in-game design and the close up portraits that farming sims always use during dialogue. There's not too many where it's overwhelming but enough that you've got decent variety. There's a lot of romanceable options and everyone likes that. A big selling point for me is that we have separate inventories and *we can be in different parts of the map*. You can be doing one thing and talking to someone or turning in a quest while your partner is off farming materials or mining or fishing. You guys do share a quest log, so you have to communicate about if you unlock new upgrades or whatever otherwise you'll be like me and using crappy tools while your partner is slapping trees down with tools made outta the same stuff they build spaceships with. The "money" is also shared but it doesn't feel grindy so far to get more. The pacing so far has been relaxing but interesting. Music is great and the animals are SOOO CUTE. There's an adorable music mini game you have to play to charm the animals and finding new ones is exciting. You can name them and breed them and there are pelt variations and little quirks (I found an ostrich that had a single feather sticking straight up from his head) which really gives a fun splash of diversity to the animal rearing part of the game. And you can ride a fair share of the animals. Plus you can own as many doggos as you want. Like, c'mon. ENDORPHINS people! We've only encountered one big puzzle so far that took both of us coordinating to solve but it wasn't stressful or confusing and we had it figured out in less than 10 minutes. No combat system so far so if that's important to you then you may wanna check out Sun Haven instead. Crafting is a little different but seems to have a fair amount of variety. Lots of decor options so if you're huge on decorating this game will cater to that and definitely has lots of space to grow with future updates. Fishing has a new type of minigame to accomplish which isn't my favorite but again - isn't stressful. I find some of the dialogue to be a bit silly when it pertains to the whole concept of "cavement" creating and discovering stuff, but hey, it's all whimsical and I LOVE the break from modern day farming sims. Nothing wrong with that theme at all, I'm a huge fan of the overall genre, but this is so fun being back in time. I literally squealed when I saw my first mammoth. So yeah, I'll update if there's anything else eye catching. But as someone who is always on the lookout for games that play well together with others whether family, friends, or partners. This one is good. Def worth the buy. We are really enjoying it and have laughed a lot together.

_childDocuments_.review: When it's sunny I water my plans, greet my animals then go talk to the villagers and help them with their ideas. If I have energy left, I work on clearing out a bit more of the giganting farm or go fishing. When I don't have energy or food, I explore to find more seeds, decorate the farm, or run around to give gifts to everyone and find out what they love.But my favorite days are when it's raining and I can just go spend the day in the cave, trying to figure out what the statues want, unlock more rooms or find new ores.Although I love farming casual games, I usually get bored after a while because it gets way to repetitive and becomes a chore more than a game. This is not the experience I'm having with this game. Between the villagers inventing new stuff often, the various activities, all the customisation and the long term objectives being hinted at, there's always something new to do and no 2 days feel the same.

_childDocuments_.review:
An upcoming co-op farming and life simulation game set in the stone age 

You have roamed the primal wilds. Now, it is time for you to build a village that will stand for generations. Join up with your friends to create a thriving community.

Features: 

Tune into Nature
Discover, gather, and farm vegetables and herbs. Explore the surrounding wilderness to find animals to befriend and domesticate; fish the shallow and deep waters to see what lies in their depths; and mine the darkest caves filled with mysteries and secret powers. 

Get to know the Clan
A tight-knit community of people will ensure your village's survival, each with their own fears and dreams. Develop friendships and overcome hardships together. Grow your village by inviting people from other clans to live with you. Participate in primitive festivals and rituals to Pacha, mother nature, and her elements. And when the time comes, find your true love. 

Evolve
Begin your journey of discovery as you develop the tools and ideas that reshaped the primitive world. Learn to process and preserve food (meat, vegetarian, and vegan options), begin metalworking, create beautiful pottery and art, unlock your clan's spirituality, and invent new buildings to expand your village any way you want. 

Play with Friends
The game was developed from scratch with multiplayer support in mind. Live together with friends and share your talents and resources to help the clan evolve. Compete in fishing, have fun at festivals, and participate in milestone multiplayer cutscenes. 

Make it Yours
Customize your character's appearance with the best cosmetics the stone age has to offer. When you're done working on your face, work on creating the most amazing farm around. Don't stop there! Design, place, and decorate your own unique home to return to after a hard day's work.

name: ELDEN RING
detailed_description: ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree Edition ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree Edition includes: ELDEN RING ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree expansion ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree Deluxe Edition ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree Deluxe Edition includes: ELDEN RING ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree expansion ELDEN RING Digital Artbook & Original Soundtrack ELDEN RING Shadow of the Erdtree Artbook & Soundtrack About the Game THE CRITICALLY ACCLAIMED FANTASY ACTION RPG Rise, Tarnished, and be guided by grace to brandish the power of the Elden Ring. • A Breathtaking World Full of Excitement and Mystery The Lands Between are part of a vast continent where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex and three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you. Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses or lead invading players into traps. • Defeat Challenging Foes in Intense Combat Combat in ELDEN RING is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of mastery. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking and avoiding damage, use a wide variety of weapons, spells, & summons, and perfect your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses. • Create and Build Your Own Character In addition to customizing the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armor, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style. No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices. • An Epic Drama Born from a Myth Created by George R.R. Martin The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways, depending on your interventions. • Play Alongside a Massive Worldwide Community The Tarnished community is massive and active. Your friends may already be among them. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members. There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

_childDocuments_.review: I am a 45 yo father, probably one of the oldest people playing this game. I am a single father to my Son, who is 14 now. My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my son, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: Now that things are calming down I can only hope that Fromsoft fixes this game despite the generally positive reception that it seems to be receiving on steam now.I still can't seem to get this game to use my graphics card despite designating it in the Nvidia control panel and the Window graphics settings. So the game runs at an unplayable framerate (around 15-30fps) in the overworld and even stutters a bit in dungeons and the totally isolated and enclosed hub area. Then there is still the more major stuttering that occurs from time to time while the game seems to be loading in new assets or shaders, even though I have everything on an SSD. The only graphics setting that seems to make any difference to performance is the SSAO which needs to be turned off completely lest the game run even slower, 5-10fps. I was also experiencing some controller problems but I haven't played for long enough recently to know if those are still an issue. So in short the game exists in an unplayable state for me despite meeting the recommended system specs. This is a game that I would love to jump into but this performance makes playing it completely intolerable and I can only hope that it is fixed over the next few months. Fromsoft is a very successful studio now and releasing ports in this state really is unacceptable at this stage. It's a bad sign when people who pirate your game in order to play without the Easy anti cheat software actually end up having a better experience than those of us who attempted to support the developer and this series.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the best souls game. Hell, this is the best game. Git gud.Edit: If you are a veteran invader you will probably not like this game. This is much more focused around the open world exploration and co-op aspects of the game than it is the PvP. With that being said, this game also has the absolute worst camera angle I have seen in any title by Fromsoft, which makes some of the main story bosses incredibly unpleasant to fight. All of the "build diversity" really goes away in PvP, when you need to use bloodhound step to survive almost any situation that involves more than one opponent. No true combos means its crazy hard to turn and burn and get a reset if you are getting chased by multiple opponents. I don't see the longevity in the Invasion scene in this game. Really sad for someone who has put countless hours into PvP in both DS2 and DS3. 1v1 duels will most likely be more popular than ever before.The auto camera recovery has to be broken cause even with the setting off it bounces off walls all the time. When you lock onto a boss, and it does an animation where it is moving quickly, your camera will go nuts. I personally felt as if I was fighting the camera more than the boss half the time. All that being said a single main story play-through still netted me around 100 hours and thats pretty killer compared to most releases in general. If you have not played a souls game you will probably love this game as co-op has been much more streamlined than before, and it is definitely at its best.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, visually it is amazing, everything in the game you can actually visit which creates a whole new level of exploration. The main bosses are all fun, and if you are not good at Souls games, you can steal beat them with the usage of summons/magic. Every castle/cave/area gives you a reason to explore it, with usually a unique boss at the end resulting in just spending hours exploring and gaining new resources. I am 35 hours into my save file, and I am still only past the first boss. This is because I have spent all my time exploring all the different locations and not really caring about the actual progression of the game. Unlike many other games, Elden Ring is actually worth 50 pounds, it has hundreds of hours of content and potentially DLCs coming in the future. Elden Ring is incredibly rewarding as a player, spending hours trying to beat a boss only to ultimately beat it feels amazing. My only complaint is the FPS drops which doesn't happen during the gameplay in my scenario, only during the shop menus/inventory. I also do not enjoy fighting large enemies as it makes it really hard to see the thing you want to hit, but that is personal preference.Overall, this game is amazing. A true masterpiece.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is a masterpiece of dark fantasy and action role-playing, created by the collaboration of Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R. R. Martin. The game takes place in the Lands Between, a vast and richly detailed world that was shattered by the breaking of the Elden Ring, a mysterious force that gave order and harmony to the realm. As a Tarnished, an exile who lost the grace of the golden Erdtree, you must rise from the ashes and claim the power of the Elden Ring to become the new Elden Lord.The game offers an unprecedented level of freedom and exploration, as you can traverse the six regions of the Lands Between on foot or on your steed Torrent, encountering various enemies, allies, secrets, and surprises along the way. You can also enter hidden dungeons that offer more linear and challenging experiences, where you can find valuable items and lore. The game’s world is dynamic and responsive, changing according to the time of day, weather, and your actions.The combat system is deep and satisfying, allowing you to customize your character with various weapons, skills, magic, and runes. You can also use stealth, environmental interactions, and summoning mechanics to gain an edge over your foes. The game’s difficulty is balanced and fair, rewarding skill and strategy over brute force. The game also features a robust online multiplayer mode, where you can cooperate or compete with other players in various ways.The game’s story is rich and complex, weaving together the lore and history of the Lands Between, the motivations and personalities of the demigods who rule over each region, and your own role as the chosen Tarnished. The game’s narrative is delivered through environmental storytelling, dialogue, item descriptions, and cutscenes, leaving room for interpretation and discovery. The game also has multiple endings depending on your choices and actions throughout the game.Elden Ring is a game that will keep you hooked for hours, as you explore its vast and beautiful world, engage in thrilling and rewarding combat, and uncover its secrets and mysteries. It is a game that will challenge you, inspire you, and immerse you in its dark and captivating fantasy. It is a game that deserves to be played by anyone who loves video games. It is a game that deserves a perfect score: 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Game deserve praise but only for its first half and scenery. Late game and combat is a massive disappointment.Lot of enemies are just reskins using same moveset just with higher numbers, hell some enemies are just copy pasta from Dark souls 3. Enemies just feel like they are non-stop pressing attack button and never gas out. There very few enemies that get staggered or can have their endless combos interrupted while you can staggered to death by anything, even things like poison clouds make your character look like it has seizure. The fact that lot of enemies have delayed attacks to catch players rolling too early doesn't help make fights any better, lot of times it looks very unnatural and downright goofy. Frankly some enemies just slowly winding up their attacks for few seconds and holding weapon over their head but then being able swing at blinding speed just looks funny. I get that they are trying to make player pay attention to when attack is going to connect react rather than roll when enemy twitches but frankly make enemy wind up for long time and then swing in a instant is a cheap way to go. Its also painfully obvious that lot of enemies have input-read scripts for when you attack or heal just to punish you for pressing a button, again this feels like very cheap and degenerate design. Perfect 360 tracking of attacks just adds to feel of cheapness, massive enemies that can do 180 mid swing and even mid air is just hilarious. It feels like i'm playing this slowpoke of a character with few attacks while enemies can attack endlessly and jump around at the speed you can only dream of.Frankly most fights devolve into playing defensive and rolling around for 10-20s just to get one hit in, unless boss jumps away or decides to go straight into another combo. Its tedious and boring design.Another problem when you get past certain point is just massively bloated health bars and damage numbers of enemies, dying to 2 hits on 60 vigor sucks and not just from bosses but also regular enemies, hell I even got one-shot few times by regular assassins in royal capital. Massive enemy health bars just make you feel like you are forced into few builds which sucks because there is so many weapons, spells and skills in game but 95% is useless later into game.I had lot of fun with DS3, replaying the game with different builds and play-styles. There was this distinct feeling when dying a lot and then finally beating bosses in DS3 like "Damn I should have dogded that, nvm I'll get better" and "Wow, this was hard but nice fight" when you finally win. In Elden Ring its more feeling of "lmao what a cheap ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" and "Glad this ♥♥♥♥ is over" when you get past the enemies. This game has the worst bosses and combat from souls games and is definetly not worth replaying.

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is a souls-like action RPG by the legendary FromSoftware (the developers of the Dark Souls series) where the main goal is to expand the genre by allowing you full access to an open world environment. Players will have treacherous traps to bypass, devious bosses to decimate, and epic distances to travel on their path to becoming an Elden Lord.In Elden Ring, you assume the role of a warrior, derogatorily known as a "Tarnished". A being whose existence is an affront in this land, where gold and power rule all. You soon find out that this world has been torn apart by countless wars, and that very little of its once noble kingdoms remain.You must use sites of grace (Elden Ring's bonfire replacement) to guide you across these lands and seek out the great rune bearers with the hope that you can eventually restore the Elden Ring itself and assume the mantle of Elden Lord. But this is no simple task, as over time these great beings have become lost and confused in a power-fuelled madness, and they will do anything to ensure the runes remain in their grasp.Elden Ring's story is mostly masked in fog and intrigue, and to truly understand it in its entirety, you will likely need several playthroughs and to explore every inch of its world to unravel it. What is explained to you, however, is beautifully written, and flows exceptionally well for the entirety of the game.The heart of all souls-like games is inevitably the combat, where prowess and skill determine whether you are victorious or suffer a crushing defeat. Elden Ring is the same for the most part, combat is more forgiving than previous FromSoftware entries, especially compared to their previous title, Sekiro, where even minor mistakes could cost you a dozen hours. Despite its fairer scenarios, you will still require some finesse to progress. Combat is smooth and for the most part pretty fair, although there are some cases where it can feel clunky or just plain broken.You have far more freedom here to build your character exactly how you want to, with limited respec's available to your character, as well as a plethora of weapons and armour to choose from. Combine all of this with both, the new and improved ashes system, where you can enchant a  non-unique weapon with a specific skill and a completely rebalanced magic and ranged system, you have a fairly dynamic gameplay experience.There is also a newly implemented crafting mechanic. While I didn't use it to its full potential, I can see it being useful to the player who wants an edge for boss fights or difficult encounters. Most crafting materials are freely available in either the open-world or as drops from specific enemies.This is the best analogy I can give to the game's open-world experience. In truth the scope feels extraordinary, with every visible location in the distance being a place worth investigating. It saddens me that this falls short of expectation as the game’s format doesn’t fit this kind of experience, it feels like a flattened and rolled-out version of the original Dark Souls formula without updating it all to compensate for the vast distances. This is made more evident in the latter portion of the game, where it’s riddled with recycled content. Bosses and enemies you have already fought will return to the fray, with slightly more health or a higher damage output, which honestly is just lazy game design, and it entirely detracts from the atmosphere intended.Veterans of the genre will be glad to see the vast quantity of bosses and enemies this game has to offer, from monstrous dragons to overwhelming giants. This game has it all. So it disappoints me greatly to play through the entire campaign, completely unimpressed by the lack of boss mechanics, tactics and overall strategy. There are obviously exceptions to the rule, but the overall experience fighting most of them felt uninteresting and stale. The side content isn’t much better, where you are literally just riding around looking for copy-paste dungeons or crafting materials to bolster you against the next boss fight.There can be no denying this game is stunning. A real treat for the eyes in nearly every aspect of its design. The world is gorgeous, the vistas are cinematic and the bosses are heavily detailed, in a way telling you a story about themselves by just standing before you. My only major concern is the sheer amount of golden visuals that encompass your vision no matter where you look. The audio falls into the same boat, with most of it being recycled from previous games, it immediately feels a little stale. There is a notion of nostalgia here for sure, but I think an entirely fresh experience would have done wonders. To contrast this perfectly, the soundtrack is just something to behold, absolutely one of my favourite soundtracks ever orchestrated, with each boss and zone bringing entirely new compositions to the fold and elevating the overall atmosphere. With settings set as high as they could go, I’ve had only minor fluctuations in frame rates with my current build below. Game launch had an astronomical amount of issues, some of which were heavily performance based, most of these have since been rectified.🟧 Volumes of bugs and crashes experienced in under 100 hours of gameplay.🟨 Some texture tearing and clipping issues were present.RAM: 32GB (Under Load Usage: 39%)CPU: i9 10900KA 3.70GHz (Under Load Usage: 42%)GPU: MSI Ventus RTX 3080 (Under Load Usage: 49.4%)Elden Ring is a well-written and gorgeous adventure that also proves without a shadow of a doubt that you can’t simply take an existing linear formula and force it into a new open-world shape, without it losing some integrity. A vast array of new and improved mechanics, as well as the large catalogue of weapons and armours you can choose from, basically ensures that no challenge is insurmountable and will keep you “build crafting” for many hours. There were quite a lot of bugs and performance issues at launch, but these have been rectified for the most part. Overall a decent game, and one that definitely caters to a larger audience than ever before. I can recommend this game in its current state, but if you havent been a fan of the genre in the past, perhaps wait for a sale.

This game is for die hard soulsborne fans and newcomers to the series alike. (and yes, this is a souls game I don't care what any elitist fan has to say.) The world of Elden Ring is a world filled with grandiose beauty, mystery around every corner, and a lore with a depth so unfathomable and secretive it at times shook me to my very core. The combat is so well done and polished, the weapon and armor designs were badass, and the character customization is the best it has ever been in a from software game. While riding Torrent, your mount, you will experience some of the best mounted combat which had echos of legendary open world title Shadow of the Colossus and the final boss of Twilight Princess on Epona. Now, onto the difficulty. I know this has been a topic of debate among fans but I will give you my honest opinion having sunk hundreds of hours into the soulsborne titles: this is the most difficult soulsborne game to date and has undoubtedly two of the hardest boss battles I have ever faced in my 25 years of gaming. The gratification gained for sticking it to some of the bosses in this game was immense and full of a mix of overwhelming emotions. With all this being said, please, pick up this game, believe the hype, it is a masterwork for Miyazaki and the From Software team.

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is essentially a culmination of everything FromSoftware has refined over the years in their previous titles, wrapped in a vast open world that invites exploration and discovery. If I could describe Elden Ring in one word, it would be "Lost." Like other FromSoftware games, this one is filled with moments where you’re not entirely sure what you’re doing, who the enemies are that you’re fighting, why they’re there, where you should go, or what the correct path is. Yet, that sense of being lost isn’t frustrating; it’s a driving force that pushes you to keep going. There’s something magnetic that urges you to press forward, to explore every corner of the map in search of an NPC, an item, or any clue that might give you some direction. But as you progress, things only become more convoluted. When you finally defeat an enemy, a tougher one appears. When you think you’ve grasped a part of the lore, new information emerges that forces you to rethink everything. The game constantly keeps you in a state of uncertainty, wondering whether you’ve taken the right path or strayed into a dangerous detour.The only clear indicators of progress in Elden Ring are the boss fights, a few scattered dialogues, and some of the graces placed across the map. The sense of accomplishment from defeating a boss is unparalleled, it serves as a reminder that despite the confusion and challenges, you are making progress.One of the standout aspects of Elden Ring is the sheer size and richness of its world. In open-world games, I’ve always enjoyed exploring every last corner of each zone, and this title was no exception. The world’s vastness, both visually and in terms of content, is impressive. The thrill of discovering a new area or finding a well-hidden secret is what drives me to keep playing. However, as I explored, I encountered one of the game’s most criticized aspects: repeated bosses. While it’s a common practice in some games, I expected FromSoftware to maintain their unique touch of originality. Perhaps the decision to reuse bosses was driven by the ambition to make the world as large as possible in their first attempt at an open-world game. Personally, I wouldn’t mind it as much if these bosses became increasingly challenging or had new attack patterns, but in most cases, the fights feel nearly identical. Despite this shortcoming, the overall experience wasn’t “tarnished” (xD), I thoroughly enjoyed every battle, striving to improve with each encounter.The Erdtree expansion brings new mechanics and a narrative focus that complements the base experience of Elden Ring. When I first accessed the expansion, I thought it would be similar to the DLCs in the studio’s other games: having a high level would be enough… I was wrong. Erdtree introduces a unique mechanic that intertwines with the game’s lore. If you choose to ignore that detail, be prepared to suffer like never before. What’s fascinating is how this expansion not only adds content but also manages to maintain the essence of what makes Elden Ring special while expanding its world in a way that feels natural. Despite all the new content, both Elden Ring and Erdtree are, in my opinion, the most accessible and, to some extent, the easiest experiences FromSoftware has developed. That’s not to say they lack challenge, but the open-world design, with its emphasis on exploration and freedom, somewhat softens the experience.In conclusion, I can confidently say that Elden Ring is the best game they’ve created in terms of ambition, design, and execution. However, interestingly, it’s not my favorite. Despite everything I’ve mentioned, I don’t feel the desire to replay it, cause it feels like a one-time experience. This contrasts with Bloodborne, my favorite game from the studio, which I could play over and over again. Despite being technically inferior in several ways, Bloodborne has an atmosphere and design that I find more appealing and invites me to a better "dream".

_childDocuments_.review: Now that Elden Ring has been out for a while, a good number of players have had enough time to complete their first playthroughs. While I’ve seen many discussions about the PvP meta, the fairness of gank fights, and the tendency for Elden Beast to run away like it owes me child support, I have seen a resounding lack of conversation around topics like whether or not my beloved Mimic Tear is capable of reproduction, though we may have to wait for VaatiVidya for that one.Anyways, since “Maidenless behavior” is quite popular these days, I figured it was time for somebody to review Elden Ring in a new lens. So here I am - I’ll be giving my own personal opinion on the fappability of the Elden Ring characters. Keep in mind that many things will be left off of this list, as development time was running too long and we had to cut some questlines lackluster entries.Character Creation - 8/10 Starting the review, the sensible thing to look at is the character creator. It’s largely similar to its Dark Souls 3 counterpart, but manages to output fairly human-looking characters if you use it just right. For the more adventurous, monstrosities are still very easy to make. A lack of boob sliders takes some points away, but overall, it’s a great iteration in the soulsbornekiroring series, definitely something memorable for those looking for a more personalized experience, but don’t expect modded Skyrim.NPCs -10/10 Elden Ring may or may not have the pinnacle of memorable NPCs in the series. The first Dark Souls still contends its spot on the throne in this category for characters such as Sunbro Solaire, Blacksmith Andre, Amazing Chest Gwynevere, and the connoisseur’s Gwyndolin. Elden Ring is far from lacking, however. The game starts off slightly weaker, with Varré and Kalé being the first NPCs you meet. Many players will agree that it picks up speed once you encounter Melina and the witch Renna. Melina, permanently winking, offers to act as your maiden, a shining ray of kindness in an unforgiving world. Renna, later known additionally as Ranni, is a mysterious character with a fantastic questline for those who are looking for a mistress to serve, or simply want to see what those 4 hands could do. In Roundtable Hold we will see more fantastic appearances, such as Fia, who will attempt to numb the pain of being as lonely as your average Strength user, Roderika, a sweet girl who I can’t bring myself to sexualize for this stupid ass review, Hewg, who I can, Nepheli Loux, who I’d let beat me up any day, and the Two Fingers, whose political views I find rather abhorrent but don’t detract from their innate sexuality. There’s also Blaidd and Alexander, for those with more particular tastes (well, Blaidd’s pretty handsome I guess…). There are also some honorable mentions, such as the Dung Eater, for those of you who I’d rather not talk to, Lady Tanith, a great match for lonely Tarnished who need to sate their bloodlust by spamming Moonveil invasions, Sellen, for those with a teacher fetish, and the noble Goldmask, who will give about as much interaction to you as most women.Minor Enemies - 3/10 There are too many enemies in Elden Ring to fit in this review, but I’ll go over the highlights. Nothing here matches up to DS2’s desert pyromancers, and overall the minor encounters feel a bit disappointing. The Iron Virgins are there for anyone who likes being… grabbed… and eaten… yeah, forget that one. Nox Swordstresses will happily whip you, so get going to Noxstella if you’d like that. Caelid has some… no, Caelid doesn’t have anything. Don’t talk about the dogs and the birds in Caelid. The second-generation Albinaurics look quite adorable with their frog-alien heads, and they’re actually quite agile. In the Dragonbarrow, you can take on several dragons at once (you know who you are). I really regret doing this. The Pillsbury Dough Trumpet Onions will blow your mind with their curves! This is terrible. Do you like Royal RevenaBosses - 8/10 From the withering failure that is the minor enemies, Fromsoft brings it back in the bosses category, making sure everyone’s Fromhard. I’m sorry. Margit the Fell Omen is a fairly weak start, but Godrick the Grafted’s many hands more than make up for it. Leonine Misbegotten is a fun addition for the furries out there. We see Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon, who strangely enough wants to give birth to you, so I guess… uh… Radahn is an absolute chad who don’t need no maidens. While his size might look appealing, he remains sadly out of reach of us lowly Tarnished. The Ulcerated Tree Spirit Godskin Noble is big and most certainly beautiful, and excels at thrusting attacks. Godskin Apostle on the other hand is great if you like yourself a contortionist, and who doesn’t? Tibia Mariner is a pinnacle of game design and I would let them bash their boat in my head in again. Morgott makes his return under a new name and… stinks up the thrones at the Erdtree? Mimic Tear gives us some much-needed spice with the cultured selfcest option, a personal favorite. Astel, Naturalborn of the Void is quite honestly one of the prettiest ladies I have ever set my eyes upon. And let’s not forget about Godfrey/Hoarah Loux - for those into being stomped on, he’s a perfect match. Radagon is as close as we’ll get to the Queen Marikussy, but it’s good enough. Elden Beast is always there if you want to ♥♥♥♥ a cosmic tardigrade god. And probably the greatest of the bosses, Malenia, Blade of Miquella and Goddess of Rot, has captivated the souls community with her scarlet rotussy. I hate everything.Overall - 8.5/10 Elden Ring holds up as a great game to play alone at night. It’s certain that Miyazaki’s vision is upheld, with an unparalleled amount of bare feet and messages reading “try fingers but hole” and “still no head?” Above all, while there are definite gaps in fappable content, there is so much that this game is worth getting for its price tag. Let me know of any great characters or enemies that you would have put on this list!

_childDocuments_.review: Here's an interesting ordeal about Elden Ring: The Souls Formula? It's very much there! Entertaining gameplay? Very much there. Cool bosses? Very much there! Unfortunately, for a title that really does have all the potential to be -the- game of the half-decade, it falls short in the QA, testing, and QOL department. How? Let me give you a list of reasons.-For some reason FromSoft decided that certain things, such as having a check that'll have the game basically insult you for 'not closing it correctly' was more important than fixing crashes. Guess what causes that check that makes the game insult you for not closing it correctly? Crashes! Guess what Elden Ring likes to do? Crash!-Crashing can also corrupt your savefile and if you're not lucky enough that Steam made a cloud backup you're permanently screwed over and have to restart from scratch. Say goodbye to your 100+ hour character!-Did you know that players can place a message at the bottom of a ladder and grief you by making it next to impossible to climb? They can do that! Same thing for the top of the ladder. I certainly hope you didn't fall down a pit in a certain mine and were scrambling to try and find a way up while a giant iron maiden with saws for hands was trying to murder you, because you'll get to it, be unable to climb it, and pressing the interact button will just bring up a message from some moron that reads 'try fingers, but hole!' as the giant 10' fullmetal killing machine grabs you from behind and kills you instantly. Why did they not pick up on this in QA testing again? Oh, by the way, you'll find this at nearly every ladder where something will be trying to kill you while you're climbing it, because people are morons.-Fall damage is terminally inconsistent. There are sections where you can fall ten stories and survive without a scratch, like in some towers! There are others where you'll jump off a five foot high drop, freeze, then die upon hitting the ground.-Stutters! I run this on a computer that could theoretically be taken from NASA's server farm and I still get random times where it'll freeze for five seconds or drop to 1-5 frames for several seconds. Guess when this likes to happen? During boss fights and times where things are trying to murder me.-Were you a victim of dark bead mage twinking in DS3? Guess what they didn't solve? Twinking! You better be ready to get invaded by glass cannons that've dedicated their entire build to INT for using Moonveil or STR and ARC in order to wield the pair of swords that create an instakilling gravity nuke that has an AOE the size of a debate hall. Are you not ready for them? Guess you're never playing multiplayer, then! Because they're the most common invader types you'll run into, and they're literally everywhere.-Looking for build variety in PVP? Sorry! Everyone's either using bleed proc weapons or the gravity nuke swords, you will occasionally find a person with a normal build, otherwise it's going to be pain and suffering all the way down. They're using bleed proc because bleed proc is one of the few ways to compensate for boss absurdity, by the way.-If you're co-oping with buddies whatsoever you're agreeing to being invaded, and as you may see from the 'They didn't fix twinking' up above, take my advice: You should get to the next boss fight fast, because every second you linger is a second closer to another glass cannon invading and oneshotting you and your friends.-The grind to level up is horrendous after you clear level 30! Hope you're alright with having to farm in excess of 10,000 runes for a single level and losing all of them to an invader or an enemy or boss you weren't ready for. By the way, there's a guy in a certain castle that'll just straight up steal a massive chunk of your runes every time you die and you have to kill him to make it stop. Does the game tell you this? No! So...Even if you get them back you're losing progress. Also, he's apparently bugged to the point where his rune stealing will happen -anywhere- you die on the map, have fun with that.-Also on the topic of the grind, looking to play legitimately? Sucks to be you, pal! You're going to be getting invaded by glass cannons, twinks, and people who are nonstop running rune farms left, right, and center...Which means you'll have to run rune farms to stay competitive, which means you'll be spending more time farming than actually playing the game.-Expecting bosses that have attack patterns that make sense? Sorry! One of the first ones you fight is literally a twelve foot tall guy with superheavy attacks that moves like a ballerina and won't stop faking out or hesitating on his attacks which makes learning his patterns infuriatingly difficult. This will happen a lot.-There are multiple spots in the world where you'll just be minding your business and FromSoft will happily drop an enemy far beyond your level and equipment rating atop you as a boss.-Get ready for a lot of "It's about skill, not gear." while you're fighting enemies with an instantly casting hitscan spell that drives your character to madness and kills them instantly! Also get ready for deathblight, a thing that exists solely to kill you instantly, and all the people running deathblight invasion builds for this exact reason.-Really, people are incredibly fond of saying 'skill issue' when FromSoft casually drops what is effectively an ancient deity of chaos and madness on you in the overworld when you're sixty levels below where you should be to fight it.-By the way, on the topic of that 'skill issue', a heavily upgraded regular sword can take upwards of 50 successful hits to kill the first major boss while a slightly upgraded katana can do it in around ten swings and two bleed procs. Still about skill? It never was! Equip bleed and watch a quarter of the health of a boss or 3/4ths the health of a PVP invader vanish once that procs.It's a great game with plenty of merit! Clearly it has something to it, because I've played 43 hours at the moment of writing this review and I'm still coming back, but the problem is that there is so much rough around the edges, missed bugfixing, worn spots that need polish, and rust that needs to be buffered out which FromSoft have either accidentally or willfully overlooked. Maybe you'll take it like everybody else and say it's your game of the year! I have to disagree. I'm having fun playing it, but that fun is directly tied to whether or not me and my friends can go 30 seconds without being invaded by another Moonveil twink who has found the most optimal route to instantly kill three people with one use of its special attack the second they exit bonfire range.

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is, without a doubt, one of the best open-world games ever released, and among the gaming "Hall of Fame" of the past decade - among the likes of Skyrim, Witcher 3, Red Dead Redemption 2, God of War, and Breath of the Wild.The best features, among many, have to be its unique and refined artistic style and direction, detailed world and lore, mysterious yet alluring characters, incredible bosses and visual effects, and the wide array of weapons and magic at your disposal.The biggest area to nitpick is the graphical fidelity, which, for this time, is outdated. However, as mentioned before, it has an unparalleled artistic design, with a look and feel that more than makes up for its shortcomings in texture quality. The way the color palettes blend and contrast with the beautiful lighting, along with the sheer grandiosity of The Lands Between, culminate into a remarkable masterpiece.The difficulty is punishing. Let me be clear - I am not a fan of such types of games. But as an RPG and open-world lover, with a penchant for medieval fantasy settings and huge swords, Elden Ring hits every other spot for me. A tremendous title for the ages.

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of my favorite games I have ever played, it has grabbed my attention and held it with an iron grip. Anytime I figure out what I wanna do, it's very hard to resist the siren call of ELDEN RING.The exploration in this game is absolutely a treat, it really feels like discoveries can be made in every little nook and cranny. With some boldness and knowledge of how far you can fall without dying, there are very few places you can't get to, and usually will be rewarded for taking the time to explore it all.The combat is extremely polished, every playstyle is viable and can have a ton of fun variety within those styles. Most enemies and bosses are incredibly awesome to just LOOK at, let alone actually fight and overcome. Not all of them can be winners, but with the sheer volume and variety already on display, I believe that's fully excusable. From the replayability and ridiculous amount of content here, I believe that anyone who isn't afraid of some level of difficulty should give this a shot and be delighted by what it offers.

_childDocuments_.review: After 3 years of wait, I can say that I am satisfied and happy with the game.In short, Elden Ring is a better and refined version of Dark Souls, which offers more content, more freedom and has way less tedious and annoying tasks to deal with. Unlike Dark Souls and Sekiro, there is no clear path. It is a true open world game, where you are free to go where ever you want. One of the strong points of Elden Ring is, that it reduces frustration and tedious tasks to a minimum. There is almost always a bonfire (checkpoint) after difficult sections or at least a shortcut to an already visited bonfire. Small but significant adjustments like infusion, changing your weapon art and leveling up are doable at the bonfire. The only time where you are forced to go to your hub, is when you want to upgrade your gear or when you want to learn new skills.Another major point which drastically reduces frustration is, that you don't have to walk all the way back to the boss any longer. There will always be a 'Stake of Marika' (which you don't have to interact with) near the boss room, where you will respawn after dying to the boss.The amount of freedom together with the amount of content you get can be overwhelming to newcomers and Souls-Veteran alike. Thankfully, the bonfires will most of the times, show you the way where you have to go next (to follow the main story) and if you forget something about an important mechanic of the game, you can always look it up in your inventory.The gameplay and combat in Elden Ring is comparable to Dark Souls 3 gameplay. There are no longer any rough or strange feeling gameplay mechanics and the game is now open to sorcerers and melee fighters aswell. The jumping mechanic from Sekiro, Powerstance from Dark Souls 2 and the new horse advances the combat in a new way. None of the new mechanics feel out of place or badly implemented and the world is designed around having these new mechanics.After having a blast with the bosses of Dark Souls 3 and Sekiro, I thought it would go the same way in Elden Ring. Sadly, that was not really the case this time. There are a lot of boss fights in this game, and almost all of the are technically way better than the previous titles, but the fun factor has gone down for me. Bosses are way to agile and most of them are masters of all. That means they can run and move around like crazy regardless if they are a giant stone figure and they can damage you from almost all distances. It is especially frustrating as a Greatsword (or Colossal Weapon) wielder, because as a slow but hard hitting player, you will miss a lot of strikes since they instantly adapt to the situation.That does not mean that there are not great boss fights in this game. For example:  And there are countless more great bossfights in this game, but proportionally the amount of good boss fights have gone down.Last but not least, the optimization... In short, it sucks. There is no excuse for such a bad optimization. Stuttering, 60 FPS lock (even though the game runs perfectly fine at 144 FPS), you name it. After Sekiro's acceptable optimization, I had my hope high, but that was a slap in the face.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if you're looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.Ingredients:1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter2. 1/2 cup white sugar3. 1/2 cup brown sugar4. 1/4 cup water5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon6. 1 pinch salt7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced8. 1 pastry for double-crust pieDirections:1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a rare 10/10 game. Perfect in almost all aspects. Here are some key features of Elden Ring to consider:It's not an easy game, like any other Souls game.It makes you learn enemy patterns, boss mechanics and most importantly what your character is capable of. Each boss is designed to punish certain player behaviors (one boss will punish for playing melee only, another boss will punish for constant movement, and so on). Some of the mobs are tougher than bosses. Environment will often be dangerous too.Yet it will greatly reward you for overcoming those challenges and reaching a certain goal.Are you tired of other open-world games published recently, such as latest Assassin's Creed or Horizon or Far Cry? Where it feels like enemy camps were just copy-pasted all over the world just to artificially prolong the playtime?Well this game is different. Each area is unique, mobs are different, not just visually but also have different mechanics. The exploration is real in Elden Ring, you might revisit a low level area later in the game and find something new, something useful.This is probably the biggest achievement of Elden Ring and I hope other game studios will take a note here, because this is the future of open-world games.While graphics are not the best (UE5 is better), this is one of the most beautiful games i've ever played.The art team has made an incredible job. All these epic models, various biomes, beautiful sky, ambient music, and so on and so forth. You can tell that this game was created by people who actually care for the game. Every small detail was considered.It's hard to pass the feeling when you go underground and find a peaceful river with artificial stars on top of it, or when you descent to burning lava cave or reaching the top of snowy mountains with giants.GRRM did a great job here. It's not that Dark Souls series had bad stories. But Elden Ring is on a completely different level. I wish he puts the same amount of effort in finishing Winds of Winter.And it's not just lore, but also the way the story is being told, it doesn't just push cinematics or walls of text over your face. But rather each NPC gives out portions of the story over time. Sometimes you won't even pay attention to what this NPC said but later will figure out how important that small piece of information was.This is another aspect I have to mention. Most of the time there's little to no interface on your screen. You're actually playing a 3D game without tons of 2D elements/text on your screen. In combat it'll show minimum amount of information necessary for the fight. You don't have a special journal with arrows and map markers for your quests, but rather have to rely on your memory and decide on your own where to head next.It really helps with the immersion, i think FromSoftware has proven that this approach of minimalistic UI is more than functional in an open-world game.- Some minor things like the confirmation popup to summon dead horse while fighting a deadly dragon... this popup needs to be removed.- Controls are not easy to learn for newcomers.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are like me and hate the Souls games for being overly difficult and for always working against and not for the player, do give Elden Ring a try, you might end up loving it as much as I did.Before getting into the review I'd like to give my opinions some merit by saying that I played over 50 hours of Demon's Souls in 2010 on PS3, made decent progress too, then I played Lords of the Fallen on Steam(Not a From Soft game) and gave Sekiro a try and hated it. I also played a bit of the PS5 Demon's Souls remake.I have also tried other games with Souls mechanics and did not care for them one bit with the exception of Star Wars Jedi Fallen Order which had multiple difficulties and I loved from beginning to end.With that in mind, let's get into my Elden Ring review.Elden Ring is the single, best action RPG I have ever played bar none. I even took the time to "Platinum" the game which I pretty much never do. Sure it had its shortcomings but the overall experience was simply unmatched by anything.In order to keep it clean and easy to understand I will post pros and cons of the gamePros:- STUNNING Art Direction, the game looks like a moving painting at every turn. I was in awe from beginning to end- Even though the game has a rather sparse and vague storytelling, if you stick to quest lines you're actually going to relate to the characters and that's very sweet. They all have very little dialogue yet it's well written and acted enough to make the player care about them.- The game is full of AMAZING Random moments you wouldn't even think could occur- Incredible, epic, amazing boss fights- Fantastic gameplay that works FOR and not against the player unlike other Souls games which do everything they can to screw the player over- Essentially infinite healing items that only increase and get stronger as you explore the world- Weapons and armor don't break! Maintaining your equipment ruined so many games for me including Demon's Souls and even Breath of the Wild (I still finished BotW at least)- Very frequent checkpoints, a checkpoint before every major encounter- Specifically dedicated Farm Zones that make leveling up a breeze, they also have checkpoints right next to them- The world is full of content yet never once felt overwhelming or boring much less like some kind of a checklistSense of discovery like no other game before it, I was genuinely happy and excited to discover new dungeons, places, items, characters, vistas, everything is just so well put together it's incredible.- Brilliant eerie somber music and ambience that fit the world perfectly- Satisfying sound effects, from the sounds the main character makes as they walk or roll around to weapon clashes, hits, everything it's just perfect. With headphones on the game's sound helps with gameplay too.- Elden Ring lets the player make mistakes, experiment with fights, take risks without punishing them by wasting their time which is something other souls games doCons:- Quest lines could and should have been clearly outlined IMO, unless you follow a quest guide you have pretty much no chance of discovering or progressing through these quest lines- Some bosses were idiotic, mainly the 2nd form of the final boss and 2nd form of that one other boss tho her I dealt with by summoning two other players to help withMaking it complicated to get all three endings on a single file for console users, fortunately I was on PC so it was a nonissue for me- TERRIBLE CLUNKY MOVEMENT AND JUMPING which sadly comes into play in 2 optional areasMost spells, armors, items and weapons are fairly useless and only a few are worth using, so that's pretty disappointing- Unable to respec an unlimited number of times, you need respec items, I had 10 and used two I believe, but it would've been so much more fun if I could infinitely play with my build. You also need to find these items tho I seem to have found them without trying so there's thatMy final rating - 10/10An absolutely amazing experience, only marred by the final boss' 2nd phase for me----------------------------I still strongly dislike Souls Games for the following reasons, none of which are present as much in Elden Ring:- Even the slightest mistake can and will mess up your run in other Souls games, but not in Elden Ring- HP and MP healing items cost souls, souls take time to farm up, it's not your choice to farm, the game essentially makes you- Dying sets you back to the beginning of a level, if you opened up shortcuts cool but some levels don't have them, fighting the same damn enemies over and over is tedious when it is NOT your choice to do so. Meaning you are either perfect or you mess up, end up wasting healing items and what not just to die at the end of the segment and try again and again to no end.I play plenty of retro games, they give you far more room for mistake than the average Souls game.- Demon's Souls for example LOVES putting the player in small, narrow spaces with enemies. If you're melee good luck becuase your sword will bounce off walls, if the camera decides to mess up and it will, it's even worse. Elden Ring very rarely did this. Tho there were some camera issues in Elden Ring as well here and there but nothing major. - IIRC the more you die in Demon's Souls for example, the more difficult the game becomes, something about world tendency getting darker but I can't confirm this for sure, Elden Ring does none of this stuff.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is frankly weak. Let me start with the cons that outweigh the pros: the open world feels empty, and it copies mobs from Dark Souls, even though this is a new universe and game. It's very difficult to follow the path planned by the developers because if you find the boss later, you'll be too strong for him and will kill him on the first try. An open world is not suitable for this genre. The quests, as always in the games from this studio, are rubbish. In Dark Souls, they could be completed intuitively, but here, maybe 0.1% of players will finish them without guides. You practically need to get into Miyazaki's head to figure out where the quest character is standing this time.There are few good bosses  8 come to mind, and it's even funny to call the rest "bosses." There's a lack of a coherent local plot, and instead, we get more vague, global nonsense about gods and aliens.Now for the advantages of the game: the beautiful locations, a sea of interesting weapons and spells, and the 8 good bosses. I especially liked the capital, though sadly, it was the only location that truly impressed me.
