_childDocuments_.review: This is basically a negative review for people, who like soulslikes and all previous souls and sekiro games. If it's your first game it might be fine for you (albeit very hard on the main bosses). I've played for 13 hours, beaten about 2-3 major and 4-6 minor bosses and I want to say, that it's honestly underwhelming. Firstly, as usual, it recycles a LOT of previous enemies and bosses from dev's games. However, what NEW it adds, makes very little sense and does not feel thought out at all at times. As if this game was composed by ubisoft. So, now we have crafting. What it does it do? You can craft arrows and some consumables after hunting down some animals and searching for plants. Is hunting animals fun, you ask? No. Is looting plants fun? No. In previous games you simply bought all the stuff but honestly you usually didn't bother at all, because consumables aren't required for progress. Then, there's "open world". It's basically same as crafting, as in I have no idea why they added it. Now there's maps, there's monster camps of sorts and there's dungeons (we get on this one later). Maps are aquired very easily and only reveal landscape. Even without it there's no difficulty in navigating, but the problem is, once again, there's no real fun to be had. Interesting encounters are almost non-existent, and there's nearly no good loot to be found (and even if there was, you can't tell if your search will provide you something useful). I must say, the dungeons are obscenely bad. All dungeons are structured similarly and their bosses often are very halfassed. There's next to none story or interesting feel to the dungeon, usually it's just some random caves or crypt with cruelly placed enemies and single obscure item in the end. Other than that, this is basically a Ubisoft game which was built over the stronger DS3 base. You want more of DS 3? Then you can get this. You want something closer to sekiro or something more original? Better get nioh 2, it's way more fun. Honestly, I'm surprsied Miyazaki did such a poor job on the new mechanics he decided to implement, but I also have some faith that latter parts of the game will be better than what I saw so far.Edit after ~60 hours:So, as I'm closing to the finale of the game I have a better grasp of its problems. Basically, the closest comparison I'm willing to give, it's a Dark Souls 2 all over again, some parts are better, some worse, but it's basically underwhelming to the premise. The core problem of the game is that it tried to go 'open world' and adapted the worst parts of it without addressing the ingame issues which make this awkward. Many of those aren't seen intially but become apparent the more you play.This is not true openworld. ER has no quests (as in visible, trackable quests you can do for fun), no activities, barely any feel of exploration. Worst of all, the areas are VERY restricted at where you can go. There's also no cool movement stuff like glider, graphook or really anything but basic horse. I'd not really like to present this as an issue (except for people who genuinely wanted an open world game), but as ER was advertised as such, the intention has clearly failed. Worse even, by trying to go 'open world', the game plays very awkward after you progress a bit and go into areas which clearly were planned to be progressed earlier. And there's a LOT of those. The game has astonishing amount of repeating enemies and bosses. There's probably like 10 dragon fights which have same model and similar movesets. There's about 6 (or more) golden knights. It's actually easier to name a boss which wasn't reused multiple time through the game. The enemies aren't very different either. Remember how every skyrim dungeon had draugers? This is it, same stuff different hp and damage everywhere. Before I finish, I want to name some more issues, which really should've been fixed but didn't. Why not every boss has a respawn point by it? Just look at Sekiro.Why you introduced new respawn points which are terribly hard to see in a murky pallete? Why not make it glowing?Why weight system wasn't reworked so player would not have to juggle stuff like bows and torches out of their inventory? Just look at Nioh 1/2.Why not make souls autopickup when entering boss room (which also does not alloiw you simple escape anymore to save it). Just look at Nioh 1/2. Why not allow us to use runes/items at the campfire/shop? Why close the inventory after you've used 1? Why weapon damage system wasn't reworked? The problem with DS weapon system is that you can't realistically know how good is the weapon later on without upgrading it and having stats for it, so more often you end up with a weapon you've started with or planned to play with. You can't switch weapons most of the time because anything you find will be unupgraded. This is simply bad design for an open world game with a variety of cool weapons. Just look at Nioh 1/2. I'd also like to critic the combat system but I'm willing to accept that it's a dark souls 3 system and they are unwilling to change (even though I believe sekiro is vastly superior), but at least fix the management systems. Speaking of some stuff I quite enjoyed and welcome:Summons are kinda cool concept even though it's very stupid you can only summon them at specific points. Like, why?Talisman pouches/memory slots is a good concept (even though they were already existing in like hollow knight)Weapon arts are really cool, albeit fairly imbalanced. Also the ability to change your weapon enchant for free for your current situation at the camp site is great.Similarly, buffing potion is good, albeit pretty weak.

_childDocuments_.review: Performance issues notwithstanding, Elden Ring is an amazingly well designed game with some interesting additions to its signature combat system and a large and engaging open world. The story (as seen so far) is pretty good too. In my 20+ hours of gameplay, I have encountered little to no performance issues/crashes. I'm playing the game on my laptop with an Intel i7 11800H, RTX 3060 and 16 GB RAM. Elden Ring at its heart is Dark Souls by another name, but it is also a lot more than that. The player character is a tarnished (referred to as the dead who yet live) who has been set on a course to reunite the shards of the titular Elden Ring and become the Elden Lord. The game starts in a chapel where the player can walk around for a bit until a min-boss promptly slaps them into the training dungeon, a true souls game welcome.The game is set in a open world where the player starts off with a blank map and has to acquire fragments to reveal the actual map. The bonfires (Sites of Grace) are present with a reasonable frequency and certain sites point to the next site in order to progress the story. Fast travel between the sites is enabled from the get go. The map has several dungeons which the player is free to explore and defeating the dungeon bosses grant powerful rewards to the player. Elden Ring does not thrust the open world on the player and Fromsoft has not simply slapped an open world on to Dark Souls and called it a new game. The Lands Between and the landmarks found in it work as scenery story elements and of course, fight arenas. branching paths the player can take to move from one region to another enhances the non-linear gameplay of Elden Ring. In the open world, the music gradually transitions from the ambient music to the boss fight/combat music, the sound design is general is stellar. In typical Fromsoft style there are traps in game that leverage the open world design. The day/night cycle and the weather events also change the world state and there are some NPCs and enemies that appear on the maps only at a certain point in the day. The very first site of grace in the open world is within spitting distance of a boss on horseback and a dragon in a lake that are best fought on a mount which is provided to the player at a place beyond the horseback guy. It is also not possible to level up until the player acquires their mount. Fromsoft mitigates these immediate challenges by allowing players to sneak past enemies in the open world and has also implemented a system of stealth attacks similar to  Stealth and an improved traversal with jumping/crouching on foot and the mount based combat makes traveling in the open world a really smooth affair.The combat is essentially the tried and tested souls formula and there are some new additions like the posture/guard breaking mechanic and guard-counters where a successful block can be followed up by a heavy attack that breaks the guard of most normal enemies. There are also spirits that can be summoned in certain point in the map and can aid the player in combat; the poison spewing jellyfish is really helpful against bosses. Mounted combat allows the use of melee, ranged and magic weapon while mounted and this allows the player to come up a variety of strategies to deal with enemies and bosses in the open world.Finally, it seems that several users are experiencing performance issues with the game, I have personally encountered a handful of frame drops and no crashes and the game ran at close to 60 fps even while streaming. The game also starts with the Xbox controller prompts by default but there is a setting in the game menu to switch to keyboard and mouse prompts. Fromsoft has acknowledged the presence of these issues and has promised fixes for the same, I'm inclined to believe them especially considering the number of copies of the PC version that have sold. In conclusion, Elden Ring seems to be a very competently designed game that moves the Souls game formula forward in many meaningful directions while retaining its own signature features.

_childDocuments_.review: Hooo boy where to even begin with this. This game is big, like, really big. My first playthrough as a relatively completionist player clocked in at just over 100 hours (and im certain i still missed stuff), and I've just finished respeccing to give my second playthrough a go. As has been said countless times before, those of you who have played DS3 will notice a lot of similarities in mechanics, abilities, and movement in Elden Ring, with a few things added in from Sekiro. I did have some performance issues with basically minimum specs (rare unexplained framerate drops/freezes in the open world) and had a few crashes in the midgame, However after progressing past the midgame (or due to the patches From had been putting out at the time) crashes were quite uncommon. Unless an absolutely amazing game comes out this year it will easily, easily be my GoTY, and is certainly in the running for my favourite game of all time. This is the open world fantasy game as far as I'm concerned, highly highly recommend.Now for those of you who want a little more detail in your reviews than a general recommendation: Yuka Kitamura does a brilliant job as always, ER has many tracks that are on par with or better than the likes of Maria, Gehrman, Ludwig, SoC and Gael. The ambient music in some areas is absolutely beautiful too, especially a couple later game zones. Imo this is overall the best OST Fromsoft has blessed us with yet, as well as the largest.  I was cautiously optimistic when I heard Elden Ring would be open world, fearing it would feel formulaic as a lot of the other open world games these days do, tending to leave me burnt out halfway through and rushing to finish them. Fortunately that was not the experience I had with Elden Ring, the world is vast but distinct and exploration is most often rewarding (of course there are times you get baited by arteria leaves and get sad) but there are some very cool and interesting items and weapons you can find off the beaten path, as well as beginning or continuing hands down the best questlines From has ever made. The addition of the Guidance of Grace was also very freeing, as I personally tend to go whichever way is not the main progression path first to try not to miss optional stuff, so knowing which way was the main path was very welcome. Crafting was very rarely used by me on my playthrough, reserved exclusively for occasionally making poison arrows, and the poison/rot curing items. There are more status effects here that in any other Fromsoft game, bringing over terror from Sekiro (because that was fun) and revamping frenzy from Bloodborne (because that was also fun) on top of more familiar ones from previous Souls games (and op DS1 bleed). Torrent (your horse) and horseback combat feel pretty good and much better than I expected them to upon finding out about them, while horseback combat was never my first choice when picking an engagement, more due to habit than it being bad, there were certainly enemies and even bosses where it was obviously the no brainer choice over regular old ground melee. The addition of a revamped posture system makes defense playstyles especially much more effective, along with the introduction of guard counters, I cannot speak too much on how different those playstyles feel since I played as a 2h Dex user who relied on dodging and at times parrying for defense, but from the little I tried they seem  powerful. Likewise I never really delved into ash summons aside from a few interactions in the open world for items/etc, but they seem quite powerful and effective when used correctly. This is the point that i am most conflicted about honestly, and where most of my grievances with the game are. The vast majority of bosses in ER have two phases with a few exceptions that are usually limited to open world/caves, and a lot of them change very drastically between phases. Early on i genuinely have nothing but positives to say about the bosses, they remix some of the tropes from previous Fromsoft games and are overwhelmingly very aesthetic and well designed. When you get to the lategame however, it feels like a lot of the designers were designing bosses around the players ability to use magic (can't complain too much because TBH the poor magicbois have had a rough time with DS3, BB and Sekiro), however it ends up making some bosses feel very melee-unfriendly, with very large aoe/ground effects that at times combo together with very long chains or sweeping delayed attacks, and a lot of bosses have vertical/very fast movement. Some hitboxes also seem to be a bit wonky on explosion attacks (especially a  boss I won't name) with me being hit by them despite being to the side of the boss.Before you say anything, yes I fought  boss, that everyone complains and whinges about, I died to them for about 6 hours, and honestly I can say I enjoyed all of those 6 hours, and no, they are by no means unfair, they do however require a higher level of skill than most every other boss in the game (which is something I'm perfectly okay with, given the difficulty of finding them and the fact they are optional). Unfortunately the excessively melee-unfriendly bosses aren't the only issue I take with some of Elden Ring's bosses, I'm just gonna say it, the devs created too many gank fights, there are far too many instances of a boss fight just being two of the same enemy you fought earlier, not even two enemies that do different things, just two of the same enemies (they may use different weapons but aside from that no major differences), which leads me to my BY FAR most disliked boss in the game. It is one of those gank fights and it appears From tried to marry together two of their better gank fights from previous games (Bell Gargoyles and Demon Prince P1). However due to how gosh darn big they are, combined with their propensity to rapidly move to the other side of you, it creates a fight that isn't necessarily hard but is very frustrating and unfun, where it's at times impossible to keep both in LoS, regardless of how good your positioning is. Enough about them though, i could probably write two whole pages on why they don't work and Demon Prince P1 does, that example was more to illustrate a point. Those types of fights are more common than I would like, and a lot of bosses are just too big to actually see what theyre doing, leaving you just spam rolling hoping to avoid whatever that sound he's making means.That being said, the overwhelming majority of the main bosses are phenomenal, ranging from the best kind of classic From bosses to the best and coolest caster boss they've ever made, the second last boss is probably my favourite of the game, with the first phase of the last boss being a close second. Somehow From managed to make the second phase of the final boss worse than Nashandra/Moon Presence though, which was kind of a letdown.GRRM's influence in the story and world is apparent but make no mistake this is still Miyazaki's vague, high fantasy, up to interpretation story. However, the overarching story is portrayed a lot more clearly in Elden Ring than in previous Fromsoft games, thanks primarily to the abundance of cutscenes From has implemented, which is a not unwelcomed change. The depth to characters is still there and as mentioned before ER has hands down the best character questlines in any From game, there's so much intrigue and mystery to their lines that end up paying dividends big time. There do seem to be one or two that kind of just stop rather abruptly but the game has only been out for 2 weeks so theres a good chance I just don't know what secret location/item I have to go to/get to continue them.The game is good, get it, play it, its worth every cent and more.

_childDocuments_.review: After 70.2 Hours, I've finally completed Elden Ring.There's so much I want to say. I ran the game with an intel i7 10700KF and a GTX 1070. The game ran at a smooth 60 Frames per second for most of the game and the few crashes I have ever experienced were attributed to summoning another player, or when trying to invade someone, which were few and far between.The game's utterly massive, every single time I thought the game had peaked, there was a new surprise waiting around the next corner. Everything you could have possibly thought of are waiting around the next corner.I have played every souls game, Bloodborne, Sekiro, and from a real place of love, this is absolutely the greatest game among them, and probably the best game I have ever played.This game is brutal, it's designed to reward, and challenge soul veterans while giving new players so many chances and tools at their disposal.Persevere, try, and be excited. I was skeptical of an open world but when I realized all of the possibilities the game had waiting for me and things I COULD do at my OWN pace, it created an experience like no other.Every time I played the game with my friends, we'd tell each other of something we found unique to our playthrough and share it, there was never a time when we wouldn't be able to surprise each other, and the way we explored the world and went about it was completely unique to each other.I can't believe this game got made. It is baffling how good it is. If you're still playing it, you know what I'm talking about.If you've played a souls game and you don't have it, you are missing out. (I know hardware limitations and PC issues are still rampant, and I'm truly sorry.)And if you have NEVER played a souls game, this game will eclipse all of them in quality, despite how great they all are.Don't give up on Elden Ring, and it will be one of the most unforgettable experiences you will ever have.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write Steam Reviews frequently - far from it. Nine years ago, when I was a mere two dozen hours into playing Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition, I wrote of the game's quality, the need to fix the port's issues through modding, and concluded that it was a Top 10 game for me.From there, across the hundreds of hours subsequently played, I only grew to further appreciate Dark Souls 1 and it jockeyed among my all time favorites, such as EarthBound. Even as new fantastic titles came out, such as Undertale, even as the Souls series entered the public zeitgeist and expanded upward and outward to DS3, Bloodborne, and Sekiro - Dark Souls 1 had continued to hold a special place to me.The interwoven level design of DS1 was untouchable by other games in the Souls series, even as gameplay became more fluid and refined. Nothing could compare to that moment in Undead Burg when I kicked the ladder, or when I realized how Darkroot linked together, or when I stumbled into Ash Lake, or that first time walking steps meant for gods in Anor Londo. The compulsion to make new characters, try out new items, and challenge the game in new ways was never as forceful as DS1, and the fun of cooperatively playing through with wacky character builds never had the same appeal as DS1.Now, at only a few dozen hours into Elden Ring, it's clear to me that this game is hitting me in the same way as Dark Souls: Prepare to Die Edition did, nearly a decade ago. The incredibly interwoven routing in Stormveil has managed to capture the incredible vertical level design of my favorite DS1 locales: such as Undead Burg, Duke's Archives, Blighttown and Sen's Fortress. Stumbling blindly into Siofr River elicits the sense of wonder and beauty of Ash Lake. Jolly Cooperation is more approachable, freeform, and glorious than ever before.Running cross-country with a friend across the fields of Limgrave feels better than any modding I've managed in The Elder Scrolls, with a cooperative element unseen elsewhere. Ashes of War encourage the player to experiment with weaponry and develop a unique playstyle without material cost. The story is rich, gameplay is tight, and the visuals are spectacular.At last, I have what I have sought to recapture from DS1 - and what I aspired to mod into games such as Skyrim. I hope that Elden Ring will capture me for hundreds of hours, across a dozen different characters, for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: DISCLAIMER: There are no spoilers in this review!Elden Ring! It is for sure the pinnacle of the souls-like series of FromSoftware. And although I find the game a masterpiece, it has its problems. But let's get something out of the way: I strongly recommend this game for everyone, even those with the famous phrase "Souls-like it isn't for me".You could stop reading there if you like, but for those who want a more in-depth review, I'll talk about every aspect of the game...Gameplay & Game Design: 10/10I chose to start with Gameplay because it is, undoubtedly, what makes this game so good. It's addicting in every way that I can think of, the combat, the exploration, and the puzzles (although there aren't many). I found the game entertaining even when I had to farm for an item or a crafting material.The boss fights and enemy encounters are well-designed. There were times that I just kept watching some enemies fight among themselves, or had to change my approach to conquer a zone, or even had to outsmart a boss. The terrain also plays an important role in how you approach your enemies, using it to your advantage is not only recommended but at many times, necessary.The combat is awesome! You feel good defeating a difficult enemy, or an invader player that played well. Every time that I god invaded some player would present a different challenge for me since the game has so many weapons and they are so different from each other. And although my current build does not use a lot of magic skills, so I can't talk too much about them, I already want to do a skill-based character, like a mage or a cleric. And talking about builds, the amount of builds possible seems huge (I didn't play that much to say that for sure, and only the future meta will tell about the viability of them, but so far they seem pretty vast).So about the Open World, I liked how they incorporated the aspects of it inside a souls-like game, all the mechanics that surround the Open World part were well designed, but the multiplayer (more on that later). The exploration, how you get your "Estus Flask", the dungeons, and the world itself is well-designed. Sure there are some dungeons and places that are copied and pasted from each other, but overall they did a great job of creating different challenges. What I found most valuable was how different every area was from each other, not only the color pallet but the enemies and challenges even the insides of some areas, you can tell just by looking at the screen in which area some player is.Multiplayer: 2/10 I saw an article saying that multiplayer is outdated and gimmicks, and sadly, I agree. The souls-like games that came before had similar Multiplayer mechanics, I know. But that doesn't mean that those mechanics are fun nor do they indeed add something to the game, on the contrary, they add unnecessary complexity and a laborious way to play with your friend that does not fit in an Open World game. I'm talking about all the tedious process of summoning your friend every time you kill a boss, or even the game BLOCKING you for exploring certain areas when you have a friend in your world. For me, that is unacceptable in a game where exploration plays a major role in it.With that said I found very few issues when it comes to multiplayer connections, I mainly played with my friend and we had just 2 disconnects with more than 100 summons, and as we are in the first week of the game, so I find it acceptable. One issue that kept occurring to me and my friend though, was the red stains stopped working, they just didn't show how that character died.Music & Sound Effects: 9/10The music is beyond great, they are a masterpiece on their own. Even the menu music awakens your inner fighter and just makes you wanna play more. Something that I enjoyed is how the music seamlessly translates the situations that you are in, for instance, when you start combat with an invader the combat music starts to play, that is so cool! The sound effects are also good, nothing out of this world like the music, but they get the job done in making your immersion more vivid.Graphics: 8/10Elden Ring is not a new-gen game in terms of graphics, don't get me wrong, the landscapes and the scenarios are beautiful, and for an old engine is impressive what FromSoftware did. But still, we have games today that surpass Elden Ring in graphics in so many ways. Again, this isn't a factor that would make you give up on the game, because the graphics are still great, but it's worth saying that there are games with better graphics out there.Open World: -/-I've already talked about it, but I felt it deserves a separate topic to talk about more in-depth. The world is huge! I'm not saying that is huge compared to other games, I'm pretty sure that in a few days someone will do the maths and find out that there are a lot of games that have far more ground than Elden Ring does. But I'm talking about the content inside the world and the density of events that composes it. We have a mount named Torrent to travel the vast world but were very occasionally that I summoned it to travel. Mostly I used it for combat. I didn't summon it a lot, not because the controls are bad, they were pretty good. Not because the mount wasn't fast enough, because it is indeed faster than your character, but because I had so much to explore that staying in the mount, just wasn't worth it. I spent my first 20 hours or so just in the first area of the game (Limgrave), and I still came back to do more stuff that I forgot or even hadn't checked out yet!Story & Characters: 9/10Demon Souls, and the Dark Souls series had their way of telling a story, it's definitively not a conventional way, it has its own weird and ambiguous way to tell what the f*ck is going on. Elden ring shares a lot of that, but it has more ways to tell its story. Now you find documents and paintings that you can read about them in a new menu that adds a lot to the story of characters or the world itself. Talking about the characters... I've always found that those were the main part of the story, all of them are well written and most of them will awaken a strong feeling, either hate or love, even disgust, and sympathy.Overall: 9/10Although the maths gives a score of 7.6/10, I can't use this score just because I hated the multiplayer mechanics, I agree more with the 9/10. This game is by far the best souls-like game made by FromSoftware and I already enjoyed 90 hours of it, I'm pretty sure that I didn't scratch the surface, nor reach a tenth of what the game truly has to offer. Play the game I'm sure you'll enjoy it as much or even more than I am now!

_childDocuments_.review: From Software has taken the lessons of the open world game trend and showed pretty much everyone how amateurish they are compared to a master. Elden Ring is an amazing mixture of the open world adventuring of Breath of the Wild, the deep and flexible combat system of Souls games, and a dark fantasy aesthetic that feels like the culmination of years of their game design. It is, without a doubt, a masterpiece.Now, about the elephant in the room: performance. I will admit that my gaming PC is definitely above and beyond the requirements (Ryzen 7 5800X, Geforce 3080Ti, 32GB RAM and installed onto an NVMe). I have not had many performance concerns at all, with the game running stably at 60fps probably 90-95% of the time. There are some occasional fps slowdowns but they don't seem to sink lower than 50ish fps, and only for a few moments. I have had a freezing hitch or two, but in my estimation they're no longer than 100-200ms and they're only happening once every so often - rare enough for me not to keep track. All that said, I can't deny evidence that's plainly visible in other people's streams and videos, and for whatever reason there are lots of people that have performance troubles even though they also go above and beyond the required and recommended specs. However, I just want to relay my personal experience to say that the performance problems are not an absolute certainty. Hopefully these issues are resolved soon, because as it stands it's a basically flawless game slightly marred by the technical issues.

_childDocuments_.review: For the first time, I am doing a revised review for a game. Originally, I had given this game a negative review because I felt the cons outweighed the pros. But after patch 1.03 and continuing to play the game, I feel Elden Ring deserves a revised review which I will be giving it a positive score. However, I do have plenty of cons to mention regardless.Game is breathtaking to look at. So many moments of me wanting to take a screenshot and enjoy the scenery of it all. Even the 'worst' of places in Elden Ring still looks great, and the visuals are top notch. Out of all the From Software games, they really made this game incredible on the eyes. Absolutely jaw dropping to say the least.Soul games have always been linear and well designed, so I was afraid of how From Software would handle an open world. Gotta say, they did a very excellent job. You can pretty much almost go anywhere you'd like with a few exceptions, and Elden Ring took all previous games before it and placed them all into this one, the best traits anyways. So much variety of builds to go with, a lot of ways to fight, Ashes of War are incredible since they truly spice up combat and the fact you can fight while on horseback is so fun overall. Also every part of the world is filled with something- not a single place is empty. So many secrets, discoveries, unique bosses, and hidden lore that it is brimming. I'm very impressed to say the least.Also which ever employee came up with Spirit Summons, give them a raise. They're a super fun concept and the best solution if you somehow can't (or unwilling) to play online. Fantastic concept and well executed for sure.It's a Souls like, it is going to be hard. While I would even say Elden Ring is the hardest Souls yet, the devs have given people so many ways in approaching a fight. The game rewards players for exploring, getting stronger, finding better weapons or loot, and coming back to a boss to overcome it. While some builds are far superior depending on what you optimize, every build is good enough and so long as you're experienced and patient, the game can be beaten even with a lvl 1 character. It's all about how you go about a fight and learn from your mistakes.Perhaps the most depth of any previous Souls game as well, since there's so many NPCs to interact with, telling a story, having quests, and these ones actually move around the world which impacts the story. Some will be more of a fan favorite than others, but each NPC is well written and I definitely loved their dynamics, including the fact some outright help you in fights you would of otherwise struggled with. Doing and completing their quest lines not only rewards you with loot, but can even lead to changes and some secrets that wouldn't be possible otherwise.So ... despite Elden Ring is a very good game, great even- there are a lot of issues I have with the game even after patch 1.03 which fixed or improved the problems I had beforehand.To explain, the game gives little to no hints on how to progress certain NPC quests, what they'll do next, where to go at times (apart from main mandatory bosses), key items, very essential items, and so forth. I understand Souls games in the past have held back secrets but because they were linear, it was easy to check every corner and not miss too much. Here? The game is open world and the devs went out of their way to hide a lot of stuff, to the point you WILL need a guide or go into NG+. While I get they want you to replay their game and invest, it isn't properly executed. I know fans will say it rewards players for discovering stuff on their own, but the fact there's no quest markers, completion entries, or anything to let you know who's gone where, it takes me out of the game by a lot since I hate missing stuff.So this is a big one. I can't seem to co-op with friends, much at all. I can help strangers but if I use a password, game often disconnects me or downright crashes. Then you have people who are cheating often in PvP, using the most meta stuff that makes you die instantly (bleed builds ...) and honestly it doesn't feel like the devs balanced it well at all. The game is amazing in PvE, but PvP? Very unstable and not exactly good. Only plus side is helping those struggling with a boss but that's if the game lets me do so. No other game in my library has this issue with me doing multiplayer.Game will at times crash or stutter hard. It is at random, and nothing fixes it. I am not too upset due to the fact it isn't often, but when it does happen- it is quite terrible to experience. My graphics card is up to date, newer version, and again no other game in my library (besides infamous Skyrim) has this problem. I personally think they need to do more patches to fix this since so many are facing this issue still.This game is obsessed with certain builds, as they're very strong and can make the fight trivial even. If you do a bleed build or hyper magic build, you will destroy both PvE and PvP. If you do a strength build, you are hindering yourself sadly as so many enemies are fast, hit harder, and can tank against your heavy hits. Also some Ashes of War are outright broken. Also the meta for this game is very off putting- rather than earning your stuff, you can easily run around collecting upgrades and get your weapon to +9 or even 10 before killing a single boss. I know you don't have to do this, but knowing it's possible makes me wonder why handicap myself and struggle when I can just be overpowered off the start. I'd rather struggle and be forced to like previous games, even if there was cheese-like methods this game has too many opportunities to make you feel you need to be meta to just keep up in PvE and PvP.Game is great, very good I would say. A lot of downsides, with mostly it hiding important information and key items from you, forcing you to scout and possibly become overpowered to just win early. Not exactly the best, but for those who like to do whatever- it does benefit those people since they can just get to level 45, 10+ weapon before fighting the first boss (after the tutorial boss). Game's balance is questionable, and a lot of issues with multiplayer with meta and disconnections / crashes. But otherwise, game is very fun, engaging, has so much content, awesome bosses, and so much variety to the builds if you don't want to be meta. I am giving this a positive score but it was close to still being negative like the first review I did.Still hoping DLC comes out for this game i'm waiting with baited breath!

_childDocuments_.review: Wish I could give a more mixed review for the game. When the game was initially announced to be "open world with crafting" I expected the worst from the game, but as it turns out, this might be the first game since Morrowind where the open world manages to justify itself.I wasn't sold on the concept in the first two or so hours of the game, but once I had Stormveil Castle fully explored and been to a few other areas, I kept being amazed at the visuals, scale, and sheer amount of optional content hidden away. Optional areas would open up into branching paths with other optional areas, and it was a lot like stumbling onto Ash Lake for the first time over and over again.The honeymoon period wore off once I got to the end of the game, though. After trekking through a massive area for the upteenth time I was getting nostalgic for when a relatively small area like the Upper Cathedral in Bloodborne could be immensely satisfying to find and explore, while everything in Elden Ring is massive, sprawling, and probably only offers Gravel (I never found crafting to be remotely worth interacting with), Butterflies, or some runes. Eventually you've successfully gawked at all the - admittedly incredible - sights and just want to get to the meat of the game, and that's where its a big step down from the previous games.I've beaten every major boss of the game to my knowledge, and overall it's a fairly weak collection of bosses. A few stand out for their bombast or coolness (Rykard was probably the most impressive boss of his 'type'), and the game certainly has the most impressive visuals to accompany them, but the majority of bosses suffer from the fact that this is, essentially, Dark Souls 4. After Demon's Souls and DkS1 just about any type of boss the basic gameplay loop can handle has been thoroughly explored (and breaks down into either a Gimmick, some very large thing that makes the camera spazz out, or a big guy with a sword). The only real way to challenge the player after 100000 hours in these types of games is, ultimately, to just crank everything about the fights up to a bazillion. Which ultimately makes most of the bosses in the game just feel like something you've seen a million times before, but potentially tougher. Extra disappointing when you then walk into a boss you've just defeated in a random dungeon, or see repeats of the same bosses (or regular enemies with inflated stats and a named healthbar) with cranked up values. This is a very far cry from Bloodborne and Sekiro managing to feel very fresh by giving you a new set of mechanics to explore (and also being much more focused on a specific type of playstyle, which is going to lend itself to much more focused boss design).The final straw for me, though, was one of the optional bosses - the probably most significant fight in the game, hyped up all game long, and probably the biggest challenge in the game. Which would have been a very cool fight if not for the fact they have an attack that is undodgeable(!), heals them a massive amount, and can very quickly immediately kill you from full. I refused to believe that they'd let something like that slip into the game and tried out different approaches, but after not coming up with anything I checked with what the No Damage Run psychos were doing and - turns out the solution is to be a STR build and just block through it with a greatshield and watch them heal. Or hope they just never use that particular attack. At that point I broke my personal rule and just used the mimic ashes to turn the fight into a joke and felt extremely deflated as the game patted me on the back telling me "wow you beat the ultimate challenge" while the boss spent two minutes unsure whether to attack me or the mimic (which is really a problem with the phantom ashes in general - bosses in these games NEVER manage to deal with there being more than one opponent, is this item really something you want to balance the game around???)  while being ganged up on and destroyed. At that point I just wanted the game over with.Ultimately, I still have to recommend the game - I enjoyed it for most of the 60~ hours it took me to play through, there was a ton to discover, and it's probably in many ways one of the most impressive games I've ever seen. Personally, though, I'd much rather have gotten DLC for Sekiro, or something different that doesn't adhere so closely to a by now tired Dark Souls formula for combat, and I hope to god they never make an Open World game like this again.

_childDocuments_.review: Where do I even begin, everything about this game is simply amazing. I'm not a big souls game fan nor have I play a lot of them but man after playing this masterpiece I'm a big fan of them especially games from the likes of FromSoftware. Don't get me wrong, the game isn't perfect by all means but man after completing it, I felt that it definitely deserves the Game of the Year award. Before continuing, the game is basically about you trying to find out the pieces of the shattered Elden Ring to put them together once again so that you can become the Elden Lord. Well that is the gist of the game but there is deeper lore on it which I'm not going to touch.Elden Ring, is an action role-playing game which takes place a fantasy world setting written by both Hidetaka Miyazaki and George R. R. Martin. The game plays pretty similar to Dark Souls but now the open world is much more massive as oppose to it's predecessor. The game allows you to choose a starting class that you would like to start with or an entirely blank sheet where you can build the character however you like it. Elden Ring definitely offers you more freedom on how you want to play it and in terms of its difficulty, I would say that it is much easier compare to other titles from FromSoftware prior to this as they allow you to use Ashen Summoning during boss fights and in some cases NPC Summoning as well. One thing I really like about this game is that it doesn't force feed you any instructions and allows you to explore the world at your own pace, you may stumble across overwhelmingly strong enemy at start without knowing you can just skip right through it. In terms of its content, I think it is plentiful and as for the side quests, some of them might be miss-able if you progress too far into the story as you need to manually keep track of it or you may refer to online walkthrough. Although the open world is really massive, it doesn't feel empty. From its unique NPC interaction  all the way to dungeons, it definitely allows its place to take their sweet time to explore. There multiple dungeons that are fun and although it may seem similar at first glance, most of the are rather unique. Although it is completely optional, I definitely would encourage you to explore all of them. The open world definitely entices its player to explore them and in some cases the NPC or Boss only spawn in certain time as there's natural Day/Night cycle in the game which really adds to the sense of realism. Now to avoid getting tedious of travelling across the massive world of Lands Between, they have added a horse mechanic which greatly reduces the time you need to travel between one location to the other and in some case you are also allow to fight bosses on horseback. I will admit it isn't the best but it works fine without any issue and that is what's most important. The game also have a lot of checkpoints littered throughout the whole map which is really convenient as the map is really massive and it is called "Grace" which are essentially what you call Sculptor's Idols in Sekiro or Bonfire in their Dark Souls series. The side quests are really engaging as well, some of them are really interesting and I honestly wish it could've ended differently. Such as  & .In terms of combat, it feels much more fluid and refine with various play styles to go for depending on your build. It really does offer its player the most freedom when it comes to building their character, you can dual wield shields, katana or even spam with sorcery if you so wish to. You can level up your character's stats with "runes" which is what you get after killing the enemy. Although do beware that you will lose all of the runes if you die unless you equip Sacrifical Twig or make a Flask Of Wondrous Physick using Twiggy Cracked Tear. I can't emphasise enough on how fun their combat mechanic is and how it plays an important role in elevating the game to its current status. Elden Ring has also included their now more polished "Weapon Arts" which are called Ashes of War in this game which essentially allows you to replace your weapon skills. This is a fun aspect and allows you to customize your weapon to suit your play style but on some weapons the Ashe of War is fixed and are unable to be changed. Speaking of weapons, the game also have a ton of weapon waiting to be discovered, remember earlier when I mentioned that if you are planning to play this game, you should definitely explore the dungeons? This is why. Most of the weapons or unique ashe of war can be found in the dungeons around the Lands Between. Let's not forget about the armor sets. There's also abundant of them throughout the game with each set providing different status buff and some are just for the looks more than anything.In terms of the game's graphics, it is easily one of the best work by FromSoftware. From the music all the way to the details of the environment and the characters it is really beautiful. Yes it isn't ground breaking by any means but both of this elements match each other so well it is hard not to give credit to team working behind it. Each region in the game felt so unique and the dungeons are not too complex but at the same time looks spooky enough as it should be. Sadly the game caps at 60 FPS for PC and I personally have some FPS stutter issue during the cutscenes, this isn't really game breaking and isn't as bad as some people made it out to be. Other than that, I have literally no bad experience with the game and I don't think during my entire 100+ hours of gameplay that I encountered any bugs or glitches. Kudos to the FromSoftware team for releasing patches and making it more and more stable for the PC release.In conclusion, I definitely think that this game is worth to play if you are a big fan of souls like games or just trying to start your journey into the souls like game genre. I would definitely recommend this as starting point as it allows you to use summoning which in turn reduces the difficulty of the game. I can definitely understand why this game got the Game of the Year award. It is a masterpiece, all the way from the presentation of its story up till the gameplay and even its graphics and music. They have done it wonderfully. I'm personally really excited for their expansion DLC so that I can suffer more in the Lands Between. Definitely one of the best game on our current generation and would recommend it to anyone looking for some challenge.PS: Malenia is the Blade of Miquella (In case you didn't know)

_childDocuments_.review: OOOooohhhh Elden Ring Elden Ring is a game developed by the folks over at From Software, and directed by Hidetaka Miyazaki, a man who started taking more pictures of himself rubbing his chin and looking thoughtfully into the distance after Dark Souls came out.And also Yui Tanimura, but the joke doesn't work if I mentioned them as well. You play as the Tarnished, someone who had lost grace with the Erdtree and banished from the Lands Between. But now everything has gone to the toilet so now you're being beckoned back to fix everything because of course you are. And so you embark on an adventure to become the Elden Lord, and put everyone who stands in your way into the dirt.Elden Ring, also known as Big Dark Souls, is an action RPG with combat and themes similar to previous Fromsoftware games from 2009 onward. Not Armored Core, though, you don't get a new one of those. I don't know how I can explain combat outside of you try to not die and smack things with a sword/axe/spear/club or light them on fire, or turn their bones to dust, or hit them with an arrow or crossbow bolt. You got a lot of options for murder via self defense in this game. Unlike previous games, Elden Ring is flat out an open world instead of a larger, connected one. You spend a lot of time hoofing it on foot or via mount to get to where you want to go. The main theme is exploration here, since the game doesn't tell you where you have to go.It just SHOWS you where you have to go. With large, noticeable landmarks and even a little arrow created by the Grace that says “This way, stupid.” There are no check markers or anything like that, but you can manually mark areas on your map so you don't lose your way. Area's are distinct and unique from one another, and the draw distance goes so far that you can see and keep track of landmarks from great distances.What I'm trying to say is you have to actively be trying to not know where to go. Bosses go anywhere from a total blast to a complete slog, though I'm pretty sure it changes depending on what build you're going for. There are bosses I had to cave and summon a friend for, but most of them you can probably just fight through if you're willing to adapt. But its always funny to just be minding your own business when some regular dude with a sword shows up specifically to start problems. Elden Ring is kind of the perfect Dirk simulator, as in you wander in random directions and pick fights with strangers. I liked -most- of the areas I had to go through, and finding catacombs was also fun for the time I was actively seeking them out. There are some things I don't like, though.For one, it feels like the enemies are pulling some fighting game crap and reading my buttons sometimes, although I don't know how true that actually is or if its just me being paranoid. There's also a gross reuse of certain bosses, forcing you to fight the same dude a couple of times. But sometimes their stronger! OR THERE ARE TWO! Either way, it can be disappointing. Also, this might just be a Dirk thing, but I was hoping all the underground stuff would be longer. Once I found the ant hill that led to a ruined city I was hooked. It does that thing where the deeper you go the more messed up everything gets, especially with the implications and other horrid ♥♥♥♥ you can find down there.Elden Ring, in a sense, was the Dark Souls game I wanted. Big world, lots of stuff to hit with a sword, and random dungeons I can just explore and rob. Its probably not my favorite game of 2022, but its up there. Oh my god, its 2022. There's nothing I can say about this game that hasn't been said before. I wish it wouldn't randomly stutter at times, and From really needs to work on its online exploits and balances. Its fun to explore, fight, and its fun to play with friends, so if those are all your check boxes, then hey, good to go!Elden Ring gets 9 Names that are too similar out of 10.Special, big boy hugs and kisses thanks to ViceVerscant for gifting me Elden Ring while I was picking through garbage to find Burger King Coupons. Hey man, you're the best.Octopuses have three hearts.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really good game. I rate 8.5/10 hats.The combat is stellar and the landscape is beautiful with excellent (not perfect, but excellent) verticality... I've had a couple performance issues, janky hit-boxes for attacks (which is only noticeable because of otherwise flawless hit-boxes) and a few crashes but nothing major. Enemy attack timings feel very fair, and there always feels like there are multiple ways to tackle fights, in no small part due to the massive customisation options, from weapons to weapon arts to spells and equipment. Downside is the scaling, which can get a bit weird due to the mid-late game area very close to the starting area - I've found myself badly failing at some areas and bosses very suddenly due to the level gap, and sometimes I explore an entire dungeon killing things in one hit, bosses included.I also didn't activate a certain mission and missed out on a plot hook which was very annoying as it locked me out of progressing until I searched for the result but otherwise the NPCs have the usual Dark Souls vagueness and hinting at where to next find them which feels very smooth.

_childDocuments_.review: Well, I thought, when I played this game solo, it was one of the best games I have ever played, then I took a look at the multiplayer and just changed my mind.Pros:+ Really large world that feels filled and makes exploring it a pleasure.+ Difficult but rewarding combat where you have tons of build options and different ways you can play the game. It also adds to the replayability of the game.+ Game is well paced and world map opens step by step, always keeping you eager to see what might be around the next corner.+ Some bosses in this game can become such spectacles that you can outright feel the adrenaline rush like you are in the game.+ Impressive music that compliments the atmosphere.+ Good graphics and decent environment design.+ Starscourge RadahnCons:- I do not really like that some bosses are recycled, some boss encounters that show up in later parts of the game are just bosses from early game with some stat tweaks or they put two of them together against you.- I  do not really like that some dungeons are recycled. Catacombs while layout wise being unique, use exact same textures and identical final boss arenas. - Some of the late game bosses scale a bit questionably. Even heavy armor tanky builds get one-shot and some builds like strength (yes despite the buffs) remain weak for the entirety of the last quarter of the game. It mostly feels like you are railroaded towards overpowered builds like bleed or frost. Not a major issues though, all bosses (except Malenia perhaps) are completely possible even with weaker builds.- I ABSOLUTELY ABHOR MULTIPLAYER. Here's why:--P2P servers-- P2P in 2022, really? Seriously? I think it would be better if they did not put multiplayer in there at all. I spent days troubleshooting everything from firewall settings to port forwarding, I still automatically disconnect always. Upload and download speeds wise I have a good connection and never have I experienced connectivity issues with other online games but this game literally is unplayable.--P2P servers-- While invasions are a cool mechanic and they are there to balance coop as you have 2 people or more to face those bosses but game already scales cooperators down and scales mobs and bosses up in cooperative play. I think they could have given the option to turn invasions off but, it is fine. What makes invasions actually bad is my point above, with lag bananza how am I supposed to protect my precious host of fingers?--P2P servers--P2P servers-- You have to buy or craft a certain consumable to initiate coop, which is a bit silly. Item is not even difficult to craft, so why? It does not make the coop harder to initiate just annoying, please get rid of it. Please make it a non-consumable item.--P2P serversOVERALL: 6.5/10 (9/10 FOR SOLO PLAYERS)

_childDocuments_.review: Best souls game ever released.Unique open world is really well done combined with some typical stuff from dark souls. _childDocuments_.review: You know that time when you hit it up with the girl you've known for quite a while and don't see anything out of ordinary, but when it comes to the sweet time, you undress her and all of a sudden she be packing a ? Well, this game is exactly that, first couple of hours seem quite familiar, it's the good ol' Dark Souls, except for a couple of quirks, but as you move on, you keep discovering and discovering. Ripping off the latest Legend of Zelda was a good move - that, Red Dead Redemption 2 and this are the games that justified having the open world. It's filled with mysteries, secrets, quests, mobs and bosses, secret bosses, too!The combat seems a bit more refined than in the previous installments, you can actually stagger fools this time around. The  is back! Unfortunately for me, however, I accidentally made an overpowered build, so from mid-game and on, I beat pretty much every boss, except for the final one, on my first try and that's not because I'm good or bosses are easy. With that being said, I immediately started a new run with an entirely different build, and the game remains interesting. Speaking of builds, from what I've seen, there is much variety in what you can do and mage builds seem actually fun, they got rid off of some unnecessary skills, so whenever you level up, you don't get lost in what you need to upgrade.What about story? How has famous author George R.R. Martin influenced the plot, the storytelling, the beats, the set pieces? Well, I don't know, 'cause most players will still have to look up some explanation on YouTube, so I imagine Martin's involvement was almost purely a marketing stunt. Save for some The Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones references, I really didn't get what else he was responsible for. A bonfire? Well, no it's a grace. Souls? Runes is where it's at, baby. Try fingers? But hole. The visual part for me is on par with . In that you had such a fitting world for the story: the design, music, everything seemed to be meticulously crafted to a dot. In  it's the world full of variety that mixes and blends together so well, you don't give it a second thought, and it's the world you actually want to explore just to see how it all looks.Speaking of looks, the performance is still pretty bad a month after the release. There is literally no rig in the world right now that could run this game perfectly smooth, so it actually comes down to the optimization and not necessarily your PC. Sometimes it's locked 60 FPS of smooth goodness (though, frame cap is ridiculous), sometimes it's a miserable nightmare of 30-45 frames with huge hiccups, stutters, downright freezes. It's embarrassing that such a great game is held down with the problem that has been plaguing all of FromSoftware games since the original Dark Souls. The only exception being Dark Souls II, it was quite good in that respect.Big mood on this one, big recommendation, big world to explore, big swords, big dudes, big . However, I found the lack of Among Us references to be disappointing, so 2/5.

_childDocuments_.review: I actually died to the first boss on its first attack because the game stuttered through whatever happened. Apparently you die in two hits, and I died in none. Considering that I'm still playing after my initial review, I feel obliged to "  recommend" despite my experiences:   All in all: fun game, would recommend  After launch, they've added lower mouse sensitivity--prior to the update it was absurdly fast at the lowest sensitivity, forcing me to use 400 dpi . Unfortunately, a few other issues  gameplay annoying:1. Auto-camera: 2.  3. Putting multiple movement actions on one button is just stupid(backstep, dodge, & sprint). At some point it will perform the wrong input. It feels like the game sometimes "eats up" dodge inputs, but I suspect it occasionally considers them a sprint instead--at least when not during a stutter. 4. Not all actions appear in the keybinds list. Some actions are not bindable to mouse buttons. 5. Even with motion blur off, turning in this game feels particularly awful. My brain adjusted after a few hours but not before dealing with headaches and discomfort. The camera smoothness  from the following:1. stutters (uses avg. <30% cpu and <50% gpu at max settings, 3 year old pc) 2. 60 fps and below 3. fighting auto camera with camera input causes additional shaking 4. high sens mouse camera--fixed5. lock-on --The game is very pretty with beautiful scenery and great effects. I've had a great time exploring the map and fighting enemies. The world feels full and has good variation in verticality. Bosses are varied as are their movesets. Many have mechanics designed to increase suffering, but that is to be expected.The story is not "handed to you". If you have any interest in understanding any of what is going on, you have to be quite active. Many open world games use a "main storyline/sidequest" strategy which sometimes have boring/useless sidequests, but since you generally cannot discern which is which here, everything explored feels like it has some significance. There are rewards for doing all manner of things, allowing you to journey however you like. You may frequently find yourself in higher level areas, allowing you the decision of turning back to explore more of what was behind or to forge onward towards more difficult battles. While it IS a good and playable game, I find it important to be harsh about the disappointing performance and the blatant lack of certain features. I will happily change my review to positive when I experience a day with smooth fps and no crashes with other issues fixed. The game has literally crashed every session. One error even caused me to expect save corruption.

_childDocuments_.review: The story of Elden Ring makes you crave more if you're a lore seeker. I believe many things are up for interpretation, making the game more exciting. Upon completing the game, especially if you attempt 100% of every location possible, you feel exhilarated yet wonder if there's still more to Elden Ring.Combat is clunky with the auto-aim camera style, especially if you are a caster, as there is no reticle system, but it is a game mechanic that needs getting used to. Otherwise, the combat is very satisfying, especially after you beat up a challenging encounter. Without the currently pointless Ray Tracing implementation, the game is graphically gorgeous, and each environment you encounter is immersive.The biggest downside of Elden Ring would be the 60 FPS lock. This game is undoubtedly made for controllers, but I managed through and through with a keyboard + mouse. For those who have an UltraWide monitor, as of this review, FromSoftware has yet to implement support for it.I won't hold my breath, but here's hoping FromSoftware unlocks the FPS, implements all that Ray Tracing offers, UltraWide support and upscaling.

My son got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his uncle, so we installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my Son for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my Son since my wife had died. This game has ever since brought me and my son closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my Son many happy memories.

_childDocuments_.review: the entire lategame actually sucks serious ass. Even with 60 vigor and 40% physical absorption enemies will still 2 or 3 shot you, it's way too overtuned to the point it's not even fun to play, just outright frustrating. It feels like trying to play Nioh 2 NG+, if you know, you know.I'm almost certain that they had accidentally tuned certain areas to be in some NG+ cycles already in your first playthrough. There's absolutely 0 sense in a crippled woman shooting arrows stuck in place to be doing 300+ damage per shot (after defences) and having 4k HP. If you think that's not too bad then that's not even all of it as there's always multiple of them sniping at you.Try to have fun in the game, but if you start getting frustrated with areas and just feel like the power scaling in enemies starts to curve a bit too much then know I completely agree with you. I'd say that this steep curve of power creeping in enemies starts around just before you enter Leyndell proper, at the Draconic Tree Sentinel. One of the worst things From could've done is to re-add dogs (not wolves, different moveset), rats and thralls animations. If you know these enemies from DS3, then you're gonna have a  experience with this game :).Poise is back, but only somewhat, kinda like that  cousin you know. The reason for that is because almost every weapon deals insane amounts of poise damage except daggers, whips and er, something else. For example a One-handed scythe does ~92 poise damage. The only way you can achieve this amount of poise is to equip very heavy armour AND use a talisman to boost it further. It's just weird.I would rather DS3's hyper armour back than this half-baked mechanic. I say that because it seems the trade off for having this dumbed down version of poise is infinite stunlocking and even getting stunned from bleeds and frostbites out of rolls. Remember in DS3 how after getting hit twice you were given a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ away, even amongst a blender of phantoms swinging at you? Well now you don't have that anymore, welcome to the blenderzone b#tch!Bleed is broken, and not just bleed damage, like the actual mechanic is just outright broken in an exploitative kind of way. No matter how much robustness you stack on, Corpse Piler will still bleed you in 2 hits. Dual wielding two bleed infused weapons (which had innate bleed before infusion), apparently cause you to instantly bleed (exploit?). So basically if you see someone wearing a white mask with a hood, and they are wielding either two katanas or naginata's just finger out, it's a waste of time bothering with them.Colossal weapons jump attacks are pretty broken, they deal insane amounts of damage. I was instantly killed by a host who was dual wielding colossal hammers despite my 2.1k hp, 141 flat defence and 35% physical absorption, which means the jumping L1 had to have done more than 3000 damage without defence values lmfao? (which is more damage than HP you can even get in this game even with 99 vigor and HP boosting talismans LMFAO) Makes sense for them to be so overtly broken with their jumping attacks though because their normal movesets are garbage. Though I think this might be for only some colossal weapons, because I've noticed this only with some weapons.

_childDocuments_.review: A Masterpiece.Just like Souls is an industry standard for games of the same genre;FromSoftware managed to re-invent the formula into an open-wolrd setting that will also become a standard (no doubt).-A gigantic world to explore with various gorgeous sceneries-Freedom to do so with a nice mount; just go have an adventure in any direction you want-A fantasy setting with the best of many inspirations (one of the obvious ones being Berserk but not limited to)-Tons of armors, weapons, spells to suit your style-Tons of Customizable weapon skills to build a completely unique character and adapt to any situation or fight.-The map always has enough rewards for you to feel interested in exploring a ruin you saw in the distance. So at the very least while travelling you are never really bored as there is always something to look for or note on your map for later.-No one to hold your hand: sure that can scare a lot of people. But know that if you are really lost, you can always find either helpful messages (mostly^^) in game to help guide you, or there is tons of info built by the community to help you online. There is no shame in looking up some help.-About the difficulty: One of the general pre-conceived ideas of Souls is that it's "too hard". it's false. It is challenging, but 99% of your problems are caused by you either being too impatient and not having leveled up or you not willing to either learn a bit of the boss patterns or even adapt your way of playing for the fight.Take your time. Try other things. in Souls games I personnaly never finish the game with the weapon I started with or thought I was going to use. Everyone has that one boss that was the hardest for them and in general it's never the same for everyone. There is a reason why. And the game offers you a way of respeccing your stats.Allow yourself to be surprised. Give yourself the time and means to "Git Gud" : )-The NPCs are really interesting with personnality and purpose (you can tell that RR Martin worked on at least some of them) which is a nice improvement from the previous games.-The bosses are varied in their styles and behavior and some of them are already becoming fan favorites just by how silly/awesome they are.-There are several endings and the game encourages you to go on additionnal runs (NG+, NG++) to try other things-The soundtrack is incredible and is, at the very least, always adapted to the moment or the place you find yourself in.As I write this I am still not over the shock of how good the whole experience is.I was expecting something OKish that we would jokingly call Dark Souls4I was vastly unprepared. Bravo FromSoftware and everyone who worked on it.A Masterpiece.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive Dark Souls fan, I was really excited for this game, even more when I heard that G.G. Martin, creator of A Song of Ice and Fire helped with writting lore of this game. Since the game is from the creators of Dark Souls series, naturally I am planning to compare this game to it, since it has ton of similarities.  I really enjoyed gameplay in this game. For the most of the game it's easier than rest of the souls games that I've played, and that was a bit refreshing, since I could focus more on exploring, and it was pretty chill game at first. Gameplay is pretty smooth and there are ton of fun weapons. I mostly used ultra greatsword, which I rarely use in these games, but it looks so cool and it was so fun to use. Overall it's pretty similar to previous souls games, you have weapons, shields, armors, magic, miracles, you have to worry about your equip load so you don't fat roll, you have standard stamina bar, you can fast travel and rest on sites of grace, which are checkpoints here, so same as always. Most important new gameplay mechanic are ashes, horse and you can jump (mind boggling). Ashes are basically different ghosts that you can summon to fight for you in areas where blue door icon apears. Ashes icon is almost always available in bossfights, and after finding  ashes, if you upgrade it to max and plan to use it, it will make most bosses pretty easy, since upgraded ashes are stronger than you and have more HP. This is why I didn't use ashes in bossfights, I only used ashes while fighting multiple enemies. I had a rule, if boss calls a friend, I will call it too, otherwise I played fair. As for horse since the game is so big, it would take ages to travel it on foot, so that's why horse is here, and if you've ever played Darksiders 2, it works exactly like that. You can summon it almost everywhere in open areas and decide when it will dissappear. It's also easier fighting some enemies on the horse. You are also able to craft items in this game, and you are basically finding crafting materials everywhere in the world, all the time. It felt like flower picking simulator at first. There is also good tutorial in beginning of the game. Overall pretty solid gameplay, but I feel like ashes made the game way easier, and sometimes it's tempting not to use it.Lore is pretty interesting, definitelly one of my favorite lores of the souls games. As always in souls games, you are supposed to investigate a lot, talk with npcs, write down/screenshot dialogues, read item descriptions, and then put all pieces together and make the story. Problem is cause the game is so big, it's really easy to miss the clues if you are not willing to explore every single corner of the game. I did explore a lot, but I definitelly missed important stuff, so I used wiki to collect all important lore pieces and after reading everything I think that the lore is good, and not that complicated compared to Bloodborne, which is still confusing to me. World design quallity is mixed for me. When we first enter the world, it looks so big and beautiful, but after exploring for a while you realise how empty this world is. It's supposed to be open world game, and open world means that you can do different stuff, but it's just bigger Dark Souls. All you can do is fight enemies, talk with npcs, loot items, craft stuff and explore this world to get more loot and understand lore better. But you could do all that before in previous souls games, it's nothing new (aside from crafting which is irrelevant). There are bunch of catacombs that you can explore, and they are all so similar. At the end of every catacomb is boss, and they are fun at first, but then they get boring. They don't help almost at all with understanding lore of the game, and don't bring you much souls. I would say it's worth doing few of them, just to try them out, and then using guides to found out in which ones are hidden achievements items. World is extremly big for a souls game, and it's really big overall. There are even whole undeground cities which I honestly enjoyed. While all this is great, I am personally fan of more interactive worlds, and there is ton of aimless wandering around here. In conclusion, while you can explore a lot, you can't actually do much, so I wouldn't call this game an open world.Boss design. This is connected to the world design. Since the game is so big, there are ton of reskinned bosses. I've fought so many dragons, that have almost identical moveset. A lot of others optional bosses also repeat many times. There are total of 235 bosses in the game, and I can't say that I really really enjoyed more than 10-15 of them. Even some of the main bosses repeat later on. Even though I didn't enjoy much boss design in this game, there are some really good ones. There are around 30 quests in this game, and there are few good ones, but it's really easy to miss the clues on where to go if you are not careful, since the world is so big, and some ncps don't always give you clear clues. Some of these quests are tied to the endings of the game. There are few endings, and all except one are pretty much similar, and I didn't find any of them good tbh. After everything I would say doing side quests just to see the different endings is a waste of time if you don't care much about lore. Performances were terrible for me at first and a lot of other people, but then few patches came out, and I upgraded my PC, so it works good now, however I still had to lower some settings even though I got great setup. I am not sure how it's for other people. It took me 145 hours to get all achievements, however I restarted the game first time after 60h, so it took me 85h to complete it for the second time from scratch. - Really interesting and good lore, one of my favorite in souls games- Pretty fun gameplay, a lot of cool weapons- Main bosses are mostlly great- Traveling with horse is fun cause you can just rush through boring areas if you want- World design could be better, a lot of empty space, and looks kinda similar; you have green area, water area, sand area, snow area etc.But I guess this was intended, to represent empty world, it just can get boring sometimes.- While some bossfights are great, there are a lot of reskinned bosses- Performances problems for a lot of people at release, fixed a lot of issues in meantime, and now it works decent for me - Some good quests, and a lot of mediocre- Ashes are fun, but make the game way easier- I didn't like the endings I think that Elden Ring is a pretty good game, but I don't think it's anything new or groundbreaking, it's just a really big souls game. While the gameplay is fun, and lore is pretty good, world is extremly big, but empty and and a lot of bosses are reskinned, so the game can feel like work sometimes. I played multiplayer only 3, 4 times, so I can't comment on that. Overall I still enjoyed a game, and I am recommending it, but with the warning to expect just a big Dark Souls game.

_childDocuments_.review: After having played Elden ring a lot, having the platinum achievement, I feel like I can finally write a serious review as a customer for the game...If you've played previous Souls game, you will find yourself at home, Elden ring takes everything from its predecessors and elevates it to new heights!The open world is very compact full of things to do and fight, there's dozen of things you discover and can explore all packed in one area and it feels endless, the builds and weapon arts feel so refreshing and you can really have tons of variationsThe bosses (the shardbearers) are some of the hardest in the From Software's universe, and they are all unique and amazing...There are thousands of things to say about the game and they are all positive things, so I will just focus and explain the major cons, these cons are in the game, rest assured, the game is still a masterpiece:-There's too much to explore, most caves and dungeon might look similar even if they are not the same, some enemies in these dungeons are other enemies with a bar and 2 more special moves, while this is completely normal for an open world game, I see many complain about it, it's not too oppressive and it's not literally every dungeon, plus every dungeon gives you an unique reward, I just felt like I had to state this...-The open world gives the player too much advantage, in previous souls game you had to fight that one hard boss and you could get stucked for hours, in this game it's very easy to overlevel yourself and you are kinda required to overlevel yourself if you find a "wall" of a boss-Some ashes are way too strong, while I'm not one of those players that will insult other players just because they play with summons or other things (everyone should play the game as they want), I feel like some ashes need to be balanced, you can sit in a corner of a major bossfight and let some ashes do the work for you, it's a bit too much...-PVP right now it's only bleed builds and Frenzy flame builds, with so many amazing weapon arts it feels sad that people are only using these two things and they should be nerfed a bit to be on pair with other spellsOverall the game's a complete masterpiece, even people that didn't enjoy previous From games for their difficulty are appreciating Elden ring, and one of the cons I said, which was the fact that you can explore and become stronger, is technically also a pro thing about the game for new comersIn short it's worth every single penny, and From has won once again the hearts of its fans
