_childDocuments_.review: I haven't yet completed the game, but I'm posting a review now because people need to know.The game itself is great but has issues not related to gameplay which degrade the experience so much that I honestly can't recommend this in it's current state.This unlike earlier From Software games, uses EasyAntiCheat which has been causing issues for many players, including myself. More often than not, the EAC popup shows but after that the game window never shows up. The only somewhat reliable workaround is to delete the EasyAntiCheat folder from inside the game's files (and the game's compatdata directory if using Linux) and then verifying the game's local files. Steam will then re-download the correct EAC files and the game should be able to launch.Other users have been experiencing different problems with EAC, such as crashes, getting stuck at a white/black screen and "inappropriate activity detected" errors etc without any good reason.If you are able to get the game started, you're faced with the second major issue, performance.Afaik, this is an issue on the PC version only, but nevertheless a major issue which needs to be fixed.Even on high-end hardware, the game fails to maintain a steady 60fps, especially in open areas. Sometimes the framerate drops down to 20-30fps in the worst cases. Only in some closed areas a steady 60fps is possible currently.This game deserves a thumbs up, but I can't give it before these issues are solved...EDIT: Seems like my savefile just got deleted. When I started the game I was only presented with a "NEW GAME" option in the main menu. No "CONTINUE" or "LOAD GAME" option in sight. So apparently that's a thing too...EDIT 2: Most of the game's performance issues have been solved, but not all and EAC is still causing the same problems as before.

_childDocuments_.review: Fromsoft innovates their souls formula with a refreshing style of open world game where you are really free to explore instead of being guided throughout like most other modern open worlds. It's an enormous game that never seems to end.All the locations are unique and gorgeous, their aging engine masked by stunning art direction. Most of the issues present in Dark Souls 3 were corrected making for a much more varied and replayable experience, with a plethora of unique items and possible build variations. Unfortunately thanks to the bigger scope, some aspects of the game fell short compared to prior titles, most notable the boss fights aren't as well balanced and finely tuned as previously with most boss attacks consisting of randomly flailing around or executing 10 hit combos that directly lead to another combo with no breathing room. It can become really tedious especially when you have to fight the same copy pasted bosses multiple times.Overall it's still an outstanding achievement that will hopefully lead to other developers making open worlds where you are encouraged to explore instead of handing you a checklist to grind through.There's a reason why this was the only game in 2022 people talked about for more than a week

_childDocuments_.review: Dark Souls 4....err I mean Elden Ring is a culmination of all Dark Souls games placed in one package and settled in one big open-world map but is it as amazing as many claim it is? Not really. 👍 +One of the best open-world designs.+The soundtrack+The combat👎-Technically it's garbage.-Nothing new in regards to, almost everything it offers.-Story was some pointless obtuse garbage.What the f did George R. R. Martin even write in this game? There's no difference in the way the lore/story or whatever this nonsense you want to call offers versus what we previously had in souls games. I was hoping at the very least something more detailed, something with a bit more depth, fleshed-out characters, anything really but sadly none of that is in the game. So what's the story about? Well, you can literally swap any mention of the word ring with flame and you have the Dark Souls 3 story. At its core, it is the same sh*t we received plenty of times already. You're some weak-ass dude and you have to become the lord of cinder...oh sorry I meant rings by slaying the previous lords. You get some side-quests here and there, without any kind of information, randomly showing up, and if you do them, you might get a different 10-second ending that talks about nonsense and nothing you care about. I did the entire Ranni quest and I would advise everyone to do it as well because while it feels and acts as a secondary it's probably the only one that makes some sense out of all and feels like a main quest besides the fact that it takes you in a ton of places you will miss, which compose practically 30% of the game.I wished and hoped with Elden Ring that they'd learn from previous games, that story is just as important in games but how could they learn when critics and ignorant fans blindly overrate the series? At the end of the day, if you don't care about luls and memes, there won't be any characters to care about and no good coherent emotional/amazing story. It has lore and some random words and that's it. Even the item/world-build lore took a nose-dive. Not a fan.Story rating: 6/10So let's talk about the bread and butter of FromSoftware games, the gameplay. Straight to the point, if this is your first game in the series then I wish I was in your place cause you'll be in one hell of a ride, literally and figurately. If you're not new and have played any of the previous games or all of them as I did, well, there's nothing new in the game, besides a cool double-jumping horse. That being said, this review is from someone who has played the games and how I feel about it, not how the game is as a stand-alone/unique experience. The core of Elden Ring is as I mentioned the combat, the gameplay, the exploration, the items, and the boss fights. The combat is exactly the same as all the other Dark Souls, with nothing new added to the mix. All the items, all the bosses, all the enemies are just variations of previous ones. It's shocking how From gets away with re-using stuff while other companies get destroyed for it. It gets worse, as the game moved on to an open-world design, naturally it suffers from repetitiveness and will get tedious if you bother doing all the game has to offer. I'll talk more in the tech aspect of the game about the world itself but suffice to say, you'll be fighting the same bosses a lot of times, visiting the same places over and over with little variation. Basically, most of the secondary stuff with a few exceptions are boring as hell. Actually, most of the areas except the main ones are just filler sh*t. The game did not need to be open-world but enough about that for now. To counter the criticism about its difficulty, From made the game easier by adding a summon mechanic, which I also used. You obviously don't have to but don't let anyone persuade you that it's "wrong" to do it. These people are the same ones playing Sorc class that two-shot bosses from afar or use overpowered stats/weapons that the series are known for so just ignore these idiots and play as you wish. They designed the later bosses with summoning in mind anyway. So yeah, the game is now less of a niche and more of a welcoming party but don't get me wrong, it is still Dark Souls but with a different skin, and as such there's going to be a ton of obscure and hard challenges ahead. The weapons, the armors are all great as was always the case, tho some are better than the others. Combat is still incredibly satisfying though not even close to Sekiro. You have the freedom to approach the zone and enemies any way you want and at the very least I do have to commend From for inventing this great combat formula. I just wish they'd improve it more and more instead of just re-using it. As always some bosses are well designed some are not and overall there's really not much else to say from a "fans" point of view in regards to its gameplay. It's samey but still good but I wish it did more. The horse is cool but fighting from it is not. Gameplay rating: 8/10Not much to say here, except that the soundtrack is still similar to the other games with epic orchestra in fights and sublime chilling everywhere else. It's great but again, exactly the same as previous games. The voice acting is bad. They have not improved an ounce in this regard and as for all the other sound effects, such as combat and atmospheric ones they are straight out of Dark Souls so take that as you will. Audio rating: 7.5/10And now onto the second most important thing in a Dark Souls game, the atmosphere, level design that FromSoftware is known for. Let me be real here, whoever designs their levels in the team, needs a ♥♥♥♥♥ statue. Yes, as I mentioned in the gameplay aspect, there are a lot of repetitive areas and a lot of imported and changed locations from previous games but the way they are connected to one another and how the world is just so overwhelmingly well designed and intricate with huge labyrinth-like cities and underground zones is still freaking insane. Incredible use of inter-connected main areas and verticality. Bravo to the level designers. Sadly it's not all perfect and as with all open-world games, FromSoftware can not escape the tedious/repetitiveness that comes with the territory and you will have to go through a lot of repetitive mines and catacombs and boring secondary areas. Artistically the game is beautiful and there are a lot of incredibly looking zones but when it comes to its actual technical stuff, the game is a piece of garbage. It feels stuck 10 years in the past, textures are ugly, characters are ugly, very weak lighting and shadowing, and on top of all that the game is unable to maintain 60 fps on any kind of system. I'm shocked everything is holding together and not taking fire. There are a ton of frame drops especially in boss fights when they use special effects, loads of stutters, loads of crashes, it's just very bad. The level design is all that keeps the game together on a technical level and if I would've rated the game based on just that it would be a 9 but sadly I do have to add that 5 from the technical stuff so you can do the math. Graphics, performance and tech analysis score: 7/10The tl;dr of it is, if you've played previous souls games, lower your expectations if you have common sense and not just a blind consumer that drinks critic score cool-aid. It's a good game but it's just more Dark Souls. If you're new, then you will most likely love the game a lot more. As for both parties, be wary of the technical issues and frame-drops that will never get fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Finished the game after 60 or so hours, including the secret areas. I've skipped some optional ruins and minor dungeons. Gonna leave the original review below for reference. Again, this review won't talk about performance and optimization issues, widely acknowledged by everyone and still (hopefully) to be patched sooner or later.First, the good: it's always nice to be back to Souls games. The formula behind these games is a winning one: addicting, charming, challenging. They are good games and, with the right mindset, very enjoyable ones. Elden Ring is no different in that sense it manages to deliver the same engrossing experience we all came to love during these years. For the record, I've been playing souls games since Demon's Soul, which remains still one of my favorites.Now, let's tackle the issues I've got with Elden Ring.- The gameplay formula is my main gripe here. There are other problems I will address later but this here is the true source of my frustration, which inevitably spoiled most of the enjoyment I had. People say that it all started with DS3, but personally I believe it was a slow process of "memification" of the Souls genre gameplay. The git gud mentality behind it all which steered all design decisions towards what I consider now a pure CBT and ultimately unfun experience. The perfect summary I've read around is: "it feels you're playing Dark Souls while every enemy is playing Bloodborne".Slow, uncancellable animations are sometimes so annoying it feels you're playing with 500 ping all the time. Most of the bosses (and even enemies) are hysterical, aoe spamming madlads with perfect hit tracking, inconceivable hitboxes and so many AOE moves that sometimes they feel copypasted. Imagine Pontiff Sulyvahn on crack. Not enough? Ok now imagine zoning AOE bosses, sorta like Laurence of crack. That's 90% of how I felt my experience with Elden Ring.And it makes me sad to think about bosses like Rennala (it felt like i was fighting a real witch) , the Fire Giant (aoe monster but slow and earth shattering) or even the stupid Mimic. How unique and interesting they felt. Even Radahn had an incredible concept but holy mother of god in the end it became spam Y to summon meat puppets and dodge the oneshot hits.I'm not gonna talk about Malenia.I'm not gonna do it.Too soon.- Said that, the other (secondary but still quite perceivable) issue I've got here is the amount of recycled content and how derivative most if the world feels. Is the "open world" empty? Not really. But I believe they've chosen quantity over quality. The more I played the more I felt diminishing returns in exploration and boss fighting enjoyment.Some bosses appear again and again during the game, sometimes as minibosses, sometimes as slightly reskinned new bosses, sometimes OH WAIT THERE'S TWO NOW! Areas start repeating themselves very soon and biomes only offer some respite in the creeping familiarity that inevitably kicks in after a while.The most jarring example of this is the Siofra River area and boss. Design: absolutely incredible. Gameplay of the area: not really a fan of aimbot snipers but hey, it's easily rushable so whatever. Boss: simple, fascinating, one of the most memorable music track in the game. They basically copypasted everything, from lightning the beacons to unlock the boss fight to the boss fight itself (with a couple of added gimmick moves). Why? Not only it feels cheap but it manages to take out the beauty and uniqueness of the area you encountered the first time.So yeah, I confirm my suspicions of my early review: Elden Ring feels like a step back for From Software compared to a Bloodborne or a Sekiro. Not only it's their comfort zone, it's the festering Blight Town comfort zone where the Souls franchise is now sitting in semi-stagnation. Open world and jumping are not enough to call it "the most daring" Souls ever made.Good game? Yes.Mediocre Souls? Also yes.---Original review:Elden Ring is a classic Souls game, exactly what you'd expect, which is why I find it disappointing. I find the raving reviews talking about the most "daring" and "ambitious" souls game ever misleading. Compared to the Dark Souls franchise's gameplay, Elden Ring doesn't feel much different: i-frame rolls, parries, critical attacks (jump attacks are just another way to trigger them), poke and repeat. Bloodborne, a game from 2015, tried to innovate the formula in a more meaningful way and it felt different, at least a tiny bit. Sekiro, released before Elden Ring, completely revolutionized the formula and soaked it in crystal meth. How can you say that Elden Ring is the most ambitious souls game when older souls game tried so much harder to shake things up? Sadly to me, Elden Ring feels like a step back.The open world aspect feels gimmicky, a way to follow nowadays trend where every game should have a crafting system and a faraway mountain you can go to. The world so far has felt empty, just a bland grassland linking together various areas and dungeons, some of which are truly wondrous (Siofra River anyone?) but most got me saying "I've been here before".All souls game feel like rites of passage: with sweat and pain you git gud and when you git gud you are able to delve deeper in a mysterious world, or enjoy a gorgeous new scenery, or have the chance to wreck a new abomination's ass. This time, the suffering is starting to feel a bit more pointless, which is a shame.Is it a good game? Yes.Is it a good souls game? No, so far I've found it uninspired and bland. One of the weakest of the franchise.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright. A lot of contention surrounding this game right now because of the technical issues. Here's my take:-GOOD-Absolutely gorgeously crafted game. The word is incredibly engrossing and beautiful in its own dark FROM SOFT twisted way. The gameplay is good. An improvement from previous Souls titles while maintaining a similar feel.-BAD-Definitely some optimization works needs to be done. Everyone is talking about that, no biggy. I'm sure it'll get patched. What's frustrating for me as a PC KB+M user is that the game only shows controller keybinds for prompts. This is confusing, and I struggled a good deal to figure out what a lot of the keybinds are. Furthermore, the keybind customization leaves out some important options like the map key. I had to Google how to pull up the map as it is not shown as a prompt (because the game only cares about representing controllers) and it did not appear in the options menu as a rebindable key. Very very sloppy.Would I recommend this game?As a work of art? 10/10 absolutely recommend.As a technically sound cross platform game? 6/10 some very basic functionality and smoothing of the rough edges needs to be done.Overall a recommend, but she needs some work.

_childDocuments_.review: Truly a beautiful game. The world is so deadly and magnificent all at once. The enemies are all unique, and the fighting styles displayed are eloquent. Every boss is a treat to fight, and the variety in them and the dungeons/areas they reside in are truly a treat to behold. PC launch issues aside, it has lived up to what it was meant to be.The combat is fluent, and the different special abilities you can apply to different weapon types really bring out one's playstyle. Each enemy provides a unique pattern and challenge, while each different area does the same. Some areas feel easy, while others provide frustration in difficulty.On that note, you can always go somewhere else, anywhere else...whenever you want. You find anything from death to beautiful treasure and sometimes both intertwined in a beautiful dance of craftsmanship. I could say more...but just try it yourself.TLDR; Launch issues aside, it's a beautiful game well worth the praise with some wonderful changes to the Souls-Like formula we know and love.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has restored my faith in the video game industry. Polished, complete, original and ambitious. Superior to anything that has been released in recent years.I have played so many games in my 22 years of life that I thought nothing could fix my endorphin overdose, but this game... This game held me hostage in my chair like games only did when I was a little kid, every inch you walk is a jaw-dropping surprise, a challenge to overcome. "How tf am I going to beat this?" is what you will think about most while playing.In the end, Elden Ring is just like life: however simple thou are as a Tarnished, scream like the barbarian Hoarah Loux, fight like Malenia, endure like Radahn (and love like he loved his horse Leonard), think like Miquella, give it all like Rykard, graft your way to power like Godrick, seize the throne like Morgott, try the impossible like Mohg and die like Godwyn. Never give up!I can already imagine The Game Awards... "And the game of the year is... ELDEN RING!"Orchestra: PAN PAAAAAAANNN!!!! *menu theme*I look forward to it.Edit: Looks like I was right. Exactly as I imagined.

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is an open world game set in a world ruled by demigods and populated with beautiful environments and structures, allowing for players to traverse the Lands Between, discovering secrets, engaging in battles, and mayhap get some maidens.There are some problems with the low fps being capped at 60 for PC users but there are solutions on the internet that can help rectify this issue, in addition there is also some fps stuttering at times, it can be annoying but other than that the game is still very much playable. But with that said let us get into what I think is great and what I dislike about Elden Ring.The bosses are fantastic looking and have some fantastic flashy move sets, however most of the main bosses have attacks that are too fast to be dodged, insanely long combos, always have some sort of AOE attack, and always keep moving making them hard to hit with melee weapons. Malekith the black blade fits in most of these points vie stated, having ranged abilities, difficult to dodge attacks due to his wide range of attack also making it hard to run away to heal, and a DOT (damage over time) after being hit with his blade. And this trend continues for most of the bosses, making them quite unfun.Giant bosses are also quite hard to battle against, it's hard to see when they are going to attack IF you’re using melee due to you needing to be up-close to the boss.Duo bosses are not too fun to fight, considering that they can kill you within 2-4 hits and you now must focus your attention on 2 enemies which considerably increases the difficulty in a cheap way.The enemies in this game are fantastic with a wide variety of epic designs making the world feel populated, however some of them are made to be quite annoying, the Rotten Stray constantly staggering you, the Lesser Kindred of Rot with their spammable ranged attack, the Bladed Talon Eagle being hard to hit for melee users and so on.The dungeons are fun areas to explore, containing resources that can help the player out by giving them better weapons or useful materials. However, some of the dungeons have bosses that are too large for the area it is placed in, mostly referring to the Tree Spirit enemies. Fighting in these small rooms is extremely difficult due to the combination of your third person camera, a large boss and a small room, making it quite a challenge to know what is going on, not to mention the AOE attacks this boss has that basically reach the entire room.Bosses are too quick with too many AOE attacks to avoid, a handful of enemies are annoying to fight against, duo bosses are hard to fight without summons but possible, hard to keep track of when giant boss will attack, small areas with big bosses are hard to fight against.The world of Elden Ring is fantastic, not needing to always rush head in towards a boss first, you can always explore and grind levels, get better equipment before trying to battle the bosses, in addition to better equipment, you can also use summons which dramatically makes the fight easier.The combat in this game is decent, having many different attacks, light attack, heavy attack, rolling light, rolling heavy, jump light, jump heavy, sprinting heavy, sprinting light, guard counter, block, parry, and unique weapon skills that can be applied to each weapon. You can also switch between two handing and one handing weapons as well as dual wielding weapons of the same type as well as mounted combat. There is also the introduction of the stance/posture system. If you are familiar with Sekiro, it is like the posture system. After hitting the enemies enough, it will cause them to stance break and leave them susceptible to critical hits, this is also applicable for bosses too. Some attacks will cause more stance damage than others such as jumping heavy attacks, counter hits and charged heavy attacks.Rolling is a little different in this game, rather than rolling on pressing the button, you roll when the button is released.Runes from bosses and enemies are a little low. The rune scaling also does not improve much for enemies when you progress to more difficult areas, but bosses do drop more runes. And the runes you get from bosses and enemies are increased permanently after NG+ as well.But aside from all these issues this game is exceptional, one of the best Maiden Pick up simulators I've ever played, a solid 9/10, definitely would recommend to anyone who wants to get into the Souls-like franchise or anyone who is a masochist.

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is hard ? bosses are dying simply by smelling my breaths, and ho you gotta believe me, it smells so bad their internal organs get rotten to death. i mean, i'm happy from the victory but it's kinda an insult, like if they're saying i rather die than be near you or something.aside from the half joke above ( rotten breath is op, be sure to grab it )the game feels like skyrim, fewer npcs but more dungeons and more spells and weapon variety. if you liked dark souls or skyrim, or anything similar, you will enjoy this.if you want to get better at it, you need to know your weapons and spells, ashes and summons, consumables, wondrous  physic and so on. don't rely on basic knowledge as you will regret later on, the game throws a lot of mechanics at you and expects you to use them all.easier than dark souls, better than dark souls, and the netcode is way better than dark souls.harder for invaders, as solo online players don't get invaded unless they use a specific reusable item designed for summoning invaders, hunt me babe <3 , co-op sessions are always open for invades, which makes invades mostly a 2v1 or even worse, 3v1. they deserve it if you ask me.almost no bugs, those that happened for me were enemy spawn bugs and i'm grateful XDoptimization is not great, but the port itself is a well done PC port, all graphical and control binding and so on.Elden Ring is not that hard like everyone's saying, respec is pretty easy, open after completing 1/4 of the game, and character re-customization is open and free anytime you want. sadly there's no transmog, you either wear a big armor or weak, beautiful light dresses.it has a lot of copy paste bosses/mini-bosses but since you need at least 200h to complete every dungeon and open area boss and puzzles/locations in-between, it's fine imoi recommend this game to the point i think $60 is a steal for it. remember those old games that had 3x more content than modern games ? Elden Ring is like that.every moment of the game was blast for me, even the moments i got blasted to death,they're technically blast moments, right ?comment if you have any question around the game, if you're angry that i ended up enjoying the game, don't comment.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I could have ever wanted, and more. In a stagnating AAA industry of copy paste third person action adventure open world games, Elden Ring is simply built different. Most notably with its revolutionary open world design philosophy of actually having interesting stuff in it, as opposed to a massive yet effectively empty space, with the same content spanning the entire map. Granted, now that iv'e had more time with the game I am willing to critique it. I enjoy the small dungeons throughout the map but the bosses did begin to repeat a fair bit more then id like, and dungeon rewards can be useless depending on the build ya run. I also began to notice that most enemys one or two shot ya later on, which was a bit wacky, and despite the massive amount of weapons you can only really effectively use a select few due to the upgrade system. Still these complaints are r e l a t i v e l y  minor.

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay:It feels like a extended version of DS3, just like you would expect from the trailers. The combat feels just like dark souls 3 with just a few minor changes. It offers so much space to explore, optional bosses and areas, as well as a more balanced version of magic than in the last dark souls games. The bosses I have encountered yet were unique and offered a good mild to good challenge, depending on the type of boss.The RIDING COMBAT feels way better then expected. It fits really great into the whole, makes traveling easier, faster and much more fun.Technical:I was affraid to buy this game at first after I saw so many reviews reporting the game to lag even on high end computers.BUT I didn't encounter a single lag, great frame drop, game crash or what ever during my game. Since I dont even meet the recommended specs I feel like most of the players that reach the minimal requirements will be able to enjoy Elden Ring if they can accept to not always run on 60 FPS and low graphics.My Setup:Ryzen 5 5600GNvidea GTX 1060 6GB16 GB RAM |  213 MHzAnd I play on 2k resolution with medium settings and still run constantly on 50-60 FPS!

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to take the plunge despite bouncing off Dark Souls and the like and hearing how hard Elden Ring was. Well, don't let that put you off. It wasn't a cakewalk, but just doing everything in the game without grinding levelled me sufficiently that nothing caused me too much trouble. 140 hours I think I saw everything (no appetite for New Game+), I'm sure I never actually "got good", but I did at least learn a little patience instead of button mashing constantly.The game was very good, but I won't go so far as to say it's personal GOTY material, nor one of the best open world games I've played. It was sufficiently different to keep me interested. There is lore there, if you're willing to hunt for it. Much like the game's systems, there is a distinct lack of explanation or direction. Life's too short: I used a wiki. :P

_childDocuments_.review: I’m a veteran player (I’ve been playing for over 20 years) and I can’t praise too much how good it feels to play a game that doesn’t underestimate the player. It is exciting to explore an open world. Which succeeds in a mysterious atmosphere. Which serves a demanding but satisfying fights. Which serves one of the finest open worlds ever.Which serves the freedom to search and develop the character at your own pace if the challenge is too demanding. Depending on the style of play, the game is either very challenging, or easier if you focus on developing the character. This happens as if by itself as you explore the fascinating world. The PC version technically didn’t always keep the fps steady, but this didn’t ruin the experience. This will probably improve over time with updates.Elden Ring is one of the best games of all time, I can't add anything that hasn't been said by others. Buy and Play it already!

There is lots of NPC quests, items, skills and equipment to find, and also various different secret locations to discover only to greeted with an another one. Elden Ring has it all. _childDocuments_.review: Stepping into a new "branch," we encounter a map that is both old and new. Once known as Limgrave, it is now a land of shadows, tinged with an unsettling hue influenced by the Erdtree, which emanates an energy far from positive. The monster scaling mechanics are merciless, and the bosses are masterfully designed and highly unpredictable. Following in the footsteps of Miquella, the journey unfolds across a relatively small map, yet brimming with layers upon layers of FromSoftware's intricate design.Everything is executed to near perfection. However, a few elements prevent this expansion from surpassing the side content of previous FromSoftware titles and earning the moniker of "Greatest Expansion Ever." These include the super boss known as Prime Radahn (akin to a community-created boss mod), the erratic performance of the latest update, and the slightly hollow feeling after unraveling Miquella's story and motives.I give this expansion an 8/10. In my heart, it stands as the winner of "Best Ongoing Game 2024" and "Best Expansion of the Year 2024."-SHADOW OF THE ERDTREE-

_childDocuments_.review: In many ways, the work of a critic is easy. We risk very little, yet enjoy a position over those who offer up their work and their selves to our judgment. We thrive on negative criticism, which is fun to write and to read. But the bitter truth we critics must face, is that in the grand scheme of things, the average piece of junk is probably more meaningful than our criticism designating it so. But there are times when a critic truly risks something, and that is in the discovery and defense of the *new*. The world is often unkind to new talent, new creations. Last week, I experienced something *magical* an extraordinary game from an amazing company. To say that both the game and its maker's have challenged my preconceptions about fine gaming is a huge understatement. They have rocked me to my core. Not every game can become great, but a great game can come from anywhere. It is difficult to imagine more humble origins than those of the geniuses working at FromSoft, who are, in this critic's opinion, nothing less than the finest game devs known since 5th of February 2009. I will be returning to Elden Ring soon, Yearning for more-Greloks The Masochist

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made just for me... There are some complaints to be spoken about, but for the beginning I will say 10 out of 10.  This feels like a perfect game if they are able to fix some of issues we are all having at the moment.  For perspective, I am about 45 hours in on my first playthrough.A dark fantasy world where the best word to describe it would be Epic!  The sense of scale is something that will really make you stare open jawed that they were able to make something so awesome.  The geometry of the world is weird... if you could see the world from the side the amount of verticality would most likely be amazing.  It reminds of the sense of being dwarfed like in Shadow of the Colossus.  There is so much to do, the game really opens up like a flower... the more you explore the more you find stuff to do.  This world puts an elder scrolls game to shame, they wish they could have this much to do.  The only thing I can think about regarding this is I cannot imagine FromSoft being able to top this game(it would be a mighty tall order to do). The controls are tight just like a 2D fighter game.  The more I play the more the combat makes me think of Devil May Cry games.  The controls are very precise and they demand you to be as well.  Like any "Souls" games  there is a lot of difficulty here to get frustrated about.  There is no shortage of bosses to fight.  The way that you can build your character makes different ways to fight the bosses.  I cannot wait to play this a second time(and more) and see how different it feels.The cons are few, but they are there.  The game has issues with stuttering due to the game loading shaders.  This will cause the game to freeze on screen for split seconds at times but the game will continue which will cause you get hit by all sorts of attacks or spells or whatever.  There are also some UI elements that could use the be changed or optionally removed.  Such as the game popping up an are you sure window when you attempt to revive Torrent when they die in combat which can be possibly be dangerous if you are in combat and you need to move.  These things could be changed so this paragraph might be removed later(hopefully) as things get updated.This is the best iteration of the Souls game formula and I was worried how it would all turn out at attempting an open world game... It came out better than could have been hoped for!  I love everything about this game... I did not think it could be improved upon... but thankfully I was wrong in that regard.  If you can stomach the endless dying that will occur throughout a playthrough you will really find something special here.

_childDocuments_.review: FromSoftware took the risk of creating an open world and they succeeded. They moved away from the “corridor” approach, giving the player the opportunity to choose their own pace of passage: leisurely exploring or rushing to collect key demigod bosses to advance in the plot. The abundance of content turns the first playthrough into a 100+ hour adventure.The world of Elden Ring is tragic and beautiful. George R.R. Martin helped develop the characters' stories, although, as he himself said in an interview, he contributed only a small part to Miyazaki's large-scale ideas. The comedy component lies in the names being similar to each other. Without a doubt, J. R. R. Martin had a hand here, so that in addition to “You died”, players thought about who they talked to and who gave the task (Malenia, Miquella, Marika, Mohg, Morgott, Margit, Melina, Maliketh, Miriam , Maleigh Marais, Miriel, Millicent, Mary, Maureen, Moongrum, Radahn, Radagon, Renna, Ranni, Rennala, Rykard, Rogier, Roderika, Rileigh, Gideon, Godfrey, Godrick, Godwyn, Gostoc, Gowry, Ghiza).The game was adjusted so that you could complete all the quests in one playthrough. Neither quest line interferes with another. In DS it was impossible to have all or almost all endings immediately available. It was necessary to carefully complete the quests in order to reach a certain ending. But this is done to attract new blood, so that nothing is “screwed up” or missed. In principle, this is a good solution, since it takes a lot of time to master most of the content. That is, few people will replay it again for an additional portion of achievements.Unfortunately, I didn’t like that the easy walkthrough was aimed at magicians. If, as usual (as in DS), you pump up health + strength + agility + endurance, then it doesn’t really work. I saw how players with pumped up intelligence and a set of spells passed bosses. So, the host calls me and the second assistant, we go to the boss, the magician stands in the middle and activates Comet Azur. All. The boss was blown away.Otherwise, a lot of fun comes from silent communication with random players. Everyone is different, everyone is interesting, that’s why I really love the community. Polite bows when summoned, “Thank you” after killing a boss, synchronized snapping of fingers. She helped other players countless times, and she also helped me many times.I liked the idea of summoning ghosts. Wide choice of companions, I liked the wolves. I ran like Princess Mononoke (: While the wolves are gnawing off my sides, I do the bulk of the damage. I expected more from the False Tear, but I found it after a couple of patches, when the AI intelligence was cut. I found out that my Tear really likes to eat turtle necks. If they don’t beat me - need to chew.The most chilling boss was... the secret one. Dragonlord Placidusax. I drank a lot of blood. In some places he couldn’t calm down and launched special attacks without a break. The relief of winning was phenomenal. Elden's Beast is in second place, the brightness hurt me.I also liked Malenia as a boss. My respect seems to be the same type as the incipient attacks, from which it was not always possible to dodge. The battle with Renalla was aesthetically beautiful, both the first and second phases were delight and pleasure.You can write a lot of good things about Elden Ring, because the game deserves it. I wish you victory in the “Game of the Year” nomination and that more people can experience the beauty.I recommended, recommend and will recommend for purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: If anyone is going to do a soulslike and do it right, it may as well be the folks responsible for Demon's Souls and Dark Souls. Much like Demon's Souls connection to Dark Souls, Elden Ring is not a continuation of either series, yet the game borrows a lot of elements all the same, from combat to the overall tone and look while adding in its own unique flair to make it still seem like something original with new enemies, a new story, and a completely new way to explore this massive new world. Elden Ring takes place in a world called The Lands Between. A really big world brimming with both life and death at every corner. I won't go into story really to give away any spoilers, but rather say where Dark Souls is overly dark and dreary, a lot of Elden Ring feels sort of the opposite. Full of light and wonderment. That is not to say though that a bit of Elden Ring will not bring you the same dark morbid uneasiness found in a Dark Souls game. Oh, it will. But you will also find areas lush with life. and I mean wildlife too. This is a world that seems to have a mixture of both hope and dread at the same time. One minute you'll be in a magical forest with twinkling lights and cute and fuzzy critters and beautiful floral scenery, and the next you might find yourself in a dark gothic hellish landscape with half rotted corpses, crumbling buildings, and doom at every corner. It's wonderful how well Elden Ring connects these themes in its world filled with massive castles, poisonous swamps, huge open battlefields, mystical forests and more. It would be hard to explore everything in one playthrough given how many nooks and crannies are scattered about. There are tons of dungeons, hidden bosses, secret areas, and some avenues completely locked off unless you meet certain quest requirements. But as big as the world is, and as non linear the path is, you'll be hard pressed to find yourself not finding some new discovery each time you boot the game up. I'm personally at around 100 hours so far and still plenty to discover, and am still finding new things on current plays. Even revisiting old areas I thought I fully explored before. Since Elden Ring is as big as it is, the game does include a map, which at first will reveal itself to be rather small, despite the opening area being so massive. As you explore more areas, the map will grow in size. And each site of grace (essentially the new Bonfires) will allow for fast travel between them. One thing Elden Ring does not do like you find in most open world games is hold your hand when it comes to quest progression. Most open world games usually have a logbook with all of your quests. Elden Ring does not. It does not usually point you in the right direction on side quests other than through conversations with NPCs or treasure maps. It's up to you to figure out where to go. That said though the sites of grace usually clue you in on where to go for the bigger picture, being the main quest. But it's not so fun to just focus on those directions. The game offers so much more that you will find it more enjoyable to go off the beaten path and do your own thing. This is one the areas where Elden Ring is going to feel the most familiar. Combat. You have most of the same mechanics introduced in Demon's and Dark Souls, with only a few omissions, but some new tricks added to take the place of those. Combat varies based on your left and right hand load out, where your right hand is usually the dominant for weapons. The usual layout would be a weapon in the right hand, and some type of shield in the left. But you can mix things up any way you want, and a lot of the weapons even allow for dual fisting for different and sometimes more powerful attacks, at the expense of less defense. You can also equip ranged weapons such as bows and cannons (Yes, cannons), and also magical staffs and amulets for a wide variety of attacks, buffs, heals and more. Of course much like previous souls games, the items you wield come at a cost, which is based on the stats you have. So managing how you spend your skill allotment with each level gained is crucial. Luckily later in the game you can respec in case you have any regrets. But these skills mixed with the loadout you use can make for a wide variety of playstyles. If you want to be a pure bruiser, you can. If you wish to play a more stealthy ranged attacker? You can. If you want to play an all powerful battlemage? You can do that too. While you are given a limited number of themed starting characters, ultimately you can switch it up to any playstyle you wish as you progress. Some of the new things added to Elden Ring for combat really make for a much more interesting dynamic. For starters, you can now crouch. This allows you to add in a sense of stealth, which is perfect for things like backstabs, or just to survey an unfamiliar room. you can also jump! Well technically you could jump in Dark Souls, but it was a little convoluted and mostly ended up being used for navigating and not so much in combat. In Elden Ring you have an actual dedicated jump button that you can mix with attacks to get an aerial advantage. A great maneuver for catching enemies off guard. On top of all of this, a majority of the game's open world will be playable on horseback, and with your trusty steed Torrent you will also be able to have attacks while mounted. There are a lot of different ways to utilize the combat. Something for everyone. So when you feel one approach might he too difficult you might want to take a step back and figure out a different approach. Luckily Elden Ring has you covered on options. Elden Ring may feel unforgiving at first for those not familiar with From Software's other works (mainly Dark Souls) first hand. But for those who are, this will be a delight. To put it bluntly, this is not Dark Souls. But at the same time this is best experienced if you know Dark Souls. The DNA of the Dark Souls franchise is baked into Elden Ring in a way that will make it familiar and wholly accessible to fans of the series while still giving you a completely fresh and original experience. While this may not be Dark Souls, it is safe to say this is something better.

_childDocuments_.review: Probably the best game out there right now. Actual open world with stuff to do. Not a filler open world like any other open world. Do you like Dark Souls? You will love this! Did you like Sekiro? You will love this! Did you ever want a DS/Sekiro mix with the bets of both worlds? You will love this! Did you ever wonder how DS could be further improved? You will love this!Edit: 22.04.2022I have done several PvP Builds now (Invasions, no duels) and it is alright. It had been better in previous souls game because you can appearantly no longer solo invade hosts unless they specifically ask for it. Thus you pretty much always end up getting ganked by tons of "Blues" as they get spawned in pretty much all the time to fill up the players. Thus it is quite different and at times unenjoyable when three enemies spam meta weapons, however, when timed properly and spaced well, you still can win these and it feels even more rewarding. That's why I actually do enjoy the PvP aspects of the game very much and the latest Patchnotes showed quite the effort for PvP balance (even though some aspects were not fixed, but it is definetly a good way it is taking)!Furthermore, the Host's Phantoms (i.e. White/Yellow Summons in DS) can for whatever reason seemingly be way overleveled or the souls dropped is glitched sometimes. At RL50 Invasions I had gotten RL150 Phantoms on a RL60 Host, but their Vigor actually was that low that I am unsure whether they actually were that high level or if the runes dropped is just glitched.  Either way I guess it is more of a (somewhat unfair?) challenge that kind of adds to the charm as they game itself is probably easier than most Soulsborne Games.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR version: excellent early game, polished combat and fun exploration brought down by badly designed late game ripe with blatant reuse and encounters made frustrating on purpose unless you're using a broken build or using the new "spirit ashes" system to summon your own adds to the fights. Would've been an easy thumbs up if it was half as long with half as much content being reused and BS mechanics toned down.Currently this feels like a 6-7/10 title or a "maybe", with early game at 8-9/10, mid-game at 7/10 and late game at 3-4/10.Full version:Elden RIng is hard to review. It's both the hardest and easiest game in the series, and simultaneously the most fun and the most frustrating entry in From's catalogue.The first half of the game (~40-60 hours) is very good. Stormveil castle is a very fun dungeon, among the best in all Souls games. Early bosses are great, too: difficult but fair, and the game gives you a lot of choice in how to approach them. Multiple optional areas are available for players who want to improve their characters before tackling the "main story" bosses. Even the optional bosses, found in various side dungeons and open world of the game, are well-designed and don't feel unfair despite their difficulty. Lots of fun weapon choices are present, as well (some much stronger than others, balance of the game is still being worked on, as clearly shown by the recent 1.03 update). A few shortcuts (which, for newer players, may feel like deadly traps) exist to circumvent the natural order of progression and get some powerful upgrades and experience boosts early on, which is cool for repeated playthroughs and challenge runs.It also just feels nice to play: both traversal and combat feel great now that you're able to jump, resulting in a proper "3D" feel. Going back to older From games right after this one really makes you realize how stiff they feel.So why the negative review, then?It all goes south in the second half of the game, when you get hit by the full extent of content reuse and silly inflation in numbers. You'll start feeling it by the time you reach Atlus Plateau, and it only gets worse from there.Someone else did the math and there are 8 (eight) - ok, 11 (eleven) if you count the drastic phase changes - non-reused bosses in the whole game. Now consider that there are more than 100 bosses in Elden Ring, meaning 90% of your playtime is tackling reused content in some form. Some of these also make absolutely no sense at all, too: even the main story, "shardbearer" bosses, and final bosses of long quest chains spanning almost the whole game, get reused as "optional" content. What's worse, From pulls their "early bosses as trash mobs" card on an unprecedented scale. Without any exaggeration, every single boss enemy you encounter in early game dungeons later gets encountered as a regular enemy or, sometimes, as a duo gank-type boss fights. Some of the bosses you will fight 4-5 times throughout the game, with gradually increasing HP and damage, but nary a change to their moveset.Surely, at least the non-repeated bosses must be great and spectacular, yeah? Well, about that: - One mid-game boss, the epitome of macho brute force spectacle, was nerfed in 1.03 update and was lauded as one of the worst fights in Souls series before that because of long and very damaging combos and some 1HKO moves with insane tracking which are made hard to read because of the bosses' size relative to the player. - One late game boss is fought in an arena with multiple pillars that you'd expect are there to help break line of sight. Unfortunately, that doesn't stop the boss from attacking and at least one of the moves he has ignores line of sight completely and will hit you from behind a pillar.- Another late game boss has, according to a dialogue line, "has never known defeat", and therefore comes with an "I win" move which can only be consistently avoided using a specific Ash or being far enough away from the boss to be able to outrun the ability when it's used. Otherwise, if you're too close your survival is up to RNG. The boss can and will use this ability multiple times during the fight at seemingly random points in time. The boss will additionally heal a couple of hundred HP when landing any hit, even if blocked with a shield.- Yet another late game boss comes with guaranteed 3-hit attack which can either be healed through (-3 uses of Estus flask) or ignored completely if using a special item obtained in a completely unrelated area of the game, and usually either several hours before or several hours after first fighting this boss. Additionally, these 3 hits heal the boss for 30-40% of its HP, regardless of whether the mechanic is ignored using the item or not.- One more late game boss will use a homing missile type of ability that persists for ~15 seconds, continously following the player and dealing small but almost unavoidable damage. The boss will continue using its normal moves at the same time, so have fun multitasking.FInally, many bosses in this game are obnoxious in their love to delay their attacks and input read the player to punish dodging and healing. In some cases, the delay is so bad (3 or 4 seconds, you can roll 3 times and the attack will still be charging) that you'll start doubting whether the animations are being artifically stretched - and then they're followed by a sped-up hit which is usually too fast to avoid reactively. These same bosses also have plenty of normal fast attacks, too, so I can only assume that the ridiculous delays were added specifically to throw off the player's sense of timing and rhythm. It's ok in theory and has been used cleverly in other From games, but never overused to the extent they are here. Get ready to face patterns that look like ATTACK - ATTACK --------------------------------------------  ATTACK ------ ATTACK - ATTACK, in one combo, followed by a one second opening until the boss switches to the next combo.All of this is, of course, easily ignored if summoning Spirit Ashes, which gives you a (sometimes, very powerful and almost capable of soloing the boss on its own) extra in the fight at no penalty (unlike normal coop summons which raise the bosses' HP). Some overpowered builds are also available to let you easily break the game, but those are gradually being nerfed judging by 1.03 changes. Seeing how at least one of the bosses who had obnoxious and unfair mechanics was also nerfed, maybe we're all playing a beta test and the game will be in a much better shape after a few months? Not sure that I'll have another hundred of hours to test that, though. But at least in the current state, Elden Ring's lategame as a solo melee character not using Spirit Ashes is an exercise in frustration (and I stayed away from using Spirit Ashes for a very long time, only using the ability on three bosses in the game).Exploration, which starts off very strong, also becomes almost unexistant by the end: locations feel increasingly more empty the closer you are to the end of the game.On the technical side of things, after the initial performance issues were fixed in the first couple of patches, the game ran smooth as butter at 1440p@60 fps on my 9700K/3070 rig. The game crashed a few times when invading other players in the first week since release, but I haven't experienced any crashes since then.Overall, Elden Ring feels amazing early on and is definitely a huge step forward for the series. Alas, in its second part, the game overstays its welcome and, instead of providing organic challenges, attempts to frustrate on purpose with unfair difficulty and encounters that are simply not fun to play against, bringing the overall experience down and making it hard for me to recommend in its current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing. As my first soulslike game, I had an absolute blast getting my ass kicked over and over. I think this game is absolutely worth a play, however it is not without its flaws.Pros:Graphics. This game is absolutely stunning almost all of the time. It is hard to find an area in this game that doesn't look so good that you want to take a screenshot.Soundtrack. Whether your in the middle of the starting area listening to that calming violin, or hearing the bosses beginning 15 seconds of their theme for the 50th time, this game's ost slaps.Combat. I had no idea what I was missing having not played soulslike combat before. Not once have I played a game where I so consistently blamed my own skill as the player rather than the challenge presented before me. The first boss breaks you down and builds you back up, until you come out the other end a more skilled and accomplished player. No feeling compares.Cons:The framerate. Capped 60fps is a huge bummer for a modern pc port, and considering this game will have the occasional frame drop and stutter regardless of what you run it on, I can kind of see why.Diffiuculty scaling. A lot of the late game bosses and areas can feel extremely difficult if you are just following your way through the story, and it can feel limiting to have to grind certain areas or look up a new build guide in order to simply have a chance in some cases. Bosses with large AOE attacks that make melee play extremely difficult can be frustrating to go against depending on your build, especially if you are not playing with summons.NPC questlines. Having to use a piece of paper and a pen to keep track of your progress throughout a quest, or have the wiki open on your second monitor, sucks. I ran into quite a few cases where I had softlocked a quest line due to some other quest I had partially progressed and forgot about. I don't think the addition of a journal or something that keeps track of what quests you are doing would be immersion breaking, certainly not as much as having the wiki open on your second monitor.Conclusion:I think anyone can find a certain amount of enjoyment out of this game. The open world nature makes it easy to take a break from your challenges and come back stronger. Even with my gripes, this game is still amazing and I can't recommend it enough. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Update: this is my vote for Game of the Year.Elden Ring is an emotional roller coaster, that is both challenging and rewarding. The game was mostly problem free of technical issues, and nothing game breaking. Beating the game was a joy, but there is a great deal of content that can be missed with only that in mind. The story is not in the main boss fights alone, but in every element, behind ever hidden wall, in every item description, and in the choices that you make. Elden Ring is an epic that your character lives through; and not just a series of cinematics and narrations. The graphics are fantastic. While they are not cutting edge realistic like some games, they are complete, artistic and beautiful. Elden Ring is a masterpiece of art, as can be seen throughout the Elden world and all that resides within. There is a clear passion seen in the many spells/incantations, as well as the combat actions and poses. The controls are fantastic, and yet a little frustrating. There is a learning curve to the controls, due to a small delay to input and character reaction. This is due to the way that the core of the game operates. It is not a long delay, but if you have fast reflexes, you will find it impact how you play. You will have to train yourself to be more patient, and treat combat with a slightly different approach. Once this is mastered, the combat is very fun. There is a great diversity with numerous weapons having their own style, timing and bonuses (many hidden). My favorite aspect of Elden Ring is the story. The story is simply beautiful and something that I believe reflects well the history of humanity. Maybe even the present. Possibly the future as well. I will not spoil the story, but it is worth experiencing, and very well done. There are many characters to be introduced, but they have decent depth, and the voice acting is done very well. My one dismay is the soundtrack. I found it to be lackluster, and some of the songs to be headache inducing. Overall, it is mostly neutral, and you can just as easily forget it is on. Except for the few that have a constant high pitch tone that just repeats. In short, Elden Ring is a must play. While still early in the year, Elden Ring is the game to beat for Game of the Year, and I am doubting anything will come close.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece but literally nobody is mentioning the sheer amount of reused/recycled bosses, and how similar a lot of the optional areas are.    The bosses themselves are great but expect to fight the same ones over and over and over again, almost every boss you see is used again and again in other locations in the game, just with more health, and if you're lucky maybe they have a different weapon or magic type.     Exploring the world is amazing, especially when you first start playing, but after around 30 or so hours you will learn how the world is structured and it gets somewhat predictable (caves, catacombs, ruins etc) and alot of them are pretty similar.      But with that aside this game is masterfully made, although I think it's a little too big for its own good. It's a perfect balance between letting you figure things out for yourself like Dark Souls but also not being overly cryptic. The graphics are very good with lots of breathtaking locations and there's plenty of new features and gimmicks that make it stand out from other From Software games, which is all this game really needed to be great.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface, I am not a Dark Souls or Bloodborne purist and haven't even put that many hours into any From  Software game before Elden Ring.  That being said, I now want to go back and play the Dark Souls trilogy from start to finish just to experience the story and see how it plays into the Elden Ring universe since it has been eluded that it could or may.Elden Ring is the best RPG I've played in years.  The game starts with a sharp learning curve that is both unforgiving and not completely clear in the direction you should work through the game in even with the grace items that give you clues, but that is, in part, a portion of the appeal and fascinating evolution of how the game draws you in.  Above all else, the underlying story and characters are engaging and make you want to continue pushing on even as your patience and temper are tested throughout.  The difficulty of the game can be overcome through trial and error, but can also be supplemented with grinding out more levels and learning the crafting system to strengthen and enhance your weapons.Having not spent long hours in From Software games before Elden Ring I had to learn the timings and overall strategy that you must apply in every fight as this game does not forgive any type of button mashing and will punish you for each mistake you make when fighting enemies that could be 5, 10 or 50 times the size of your character.  You learn what "iframes" are and how some animations will prevent you from taking damage, you learn how the longer you hold the button for your "strong" attacks, the more likely you are to get hit, but the greater the damage potential.  You learn that parrying and counters are an essential play mechanic and that you cannot brute strength your way through the game and you must apply a level of finesse that is frustratingly cruel at times, but amazingly rewarding when you finally complete the mission or fell the boss at hand.Having played many other 1st & 3rd person RPGs, Elden Ring is the game I wish so many before it actually were.  Specifically, I've indulged in the entire Elder Scrolls series except for the very first game, Arena, so I have thousands of hours in the series.  As great as the evolution of the series is, story-wise, the gameplay actually declined over the course of the series rather than improved, even with the deployment of newer technologies and engines.  In fact, the latest installment was, in many ways, a disappointment in terms of the play difficulty, story telling and the lack of time spent on developing the NPCs and driving factors.  When you compare this to what Elden Ring is it's clear that From Software is extremely talented in staying focused on what matters and developing the gameplay and story to craft a universe that you not only want to be a part of, but also want to continue learning and digging through.With all that being said, Elden Ring is not a perfect game and there is definitely room for improvement; the lack of cut scenes and the reusing of them at key points in the game was disappointing.  The game could have been greatly enhanced by adding more meaningful cinematics and not leaving so much up to the imagination. There definitely are pros and cons with this approach, but for a game of this caliber I would expect a more complete cinematic element, particularly at key points in the game where you overcome main bosses, make discoveries about characters that can come as a huge surprise and develop the story to your own path that makes the story all your own.  The only other part of the game I find is lacking other than the cinematics is the focus on developing the story nearly exclusively through item descriptions.  Although this is fairly unique in how you learn the more obscure details, the fact that you basically have to grind out for items with an extremely tiny drop rate to find those complementary tidbits, I wish there were other ways that the story was elaborated upon similar to other RPGs where lore is weaved throughout and doesn't just appear in an item drop.The only other criticism I have found within the game is that there is no truly enjoyable way to play as a physical ranged character and that the lack of ranged weapons tends to leave the game in a balance between magic & melee, which itself leaves a huge amount of content choices for any character development, but with only really a "2 pronged" weapon/class choice balancing act it does narrow down the way you play the game.  Regardless this is minor in my eyes and is something that could be shored up in a DLC/expansion or in a sequel that makes the weapon choices slightly more dynamic between melee, magic and ranged.Overall I would say that even if you never played a Dark Souls title, Bloodborne, Demonsouls or any other From Software title, but want a challenging, infinitely fun and dynamic RPG that focuses on true gameplay and a story, then I would profoundly recommend Elden Ring.  With the historical elements of the lore developed with the help of George R. R. Martin (Game of Thrones), the intertwining paths of the characters and their fates was amazingly interesting, creepy, diabolical, sad, enraging, thoughtful and yet still left room for even more emotions depending on what you discover on your first play through.  The fact that you can then choose to play the main story again, and again, and again, evolving the difficulty to your own desire is a great complement that allows you to relive the ups and downs to your own expectations without needing to start a brand new character.TL;DR, it's the best action RPG of a human generation and there won't be another game that comes close to it until From Software teams up with a company like BioWare to integrate a more dynamic end game experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Insane game. Dark Souls in its core - but more.Let me tell you that - at first - the open world thing really made me hate it a bit. Then again - in a way Dark Souls has always been, well, a tiny bit open world. You were able to choose your path most of the time and go for a couple of different areas. For the first couple of hours of me playing the game i honestly felt like it's yet another "forced open world" empty grasslands game but the more i kept playing, the more i realized that it's actually full of lots of precious content.Sure, some side-bosses felt a little rushed - or a little too easy, and some catacombs felt like they were short and empty. But in the end all of them are rewarding you as a player with interesting items. And don't you be worried - there are very challenging bosses coming up, too. It also greatly depends on your build. Some things just work better for certain bosses.The crafting system was yet another thing i really disliked at the start, but at this point i appreciate the option to just quickly craft my buff items when i need them, instead of painstakingly farming them in certain spots or finding just a couple limited resources before i have to hit NG+.The atmosphere is insane, dark - as always. The ambient-sad-dark-ish music is great and does its job fully immersing you into Elden Rings long lost world.Playing the game with a controller on PC is definitely recommend it for any From Software game. They're just not made for KB+M most of the time. Of course you can get used to it, and in the end its yet another input method people might prefer, but its just not as fleshed out as the controller support.Performance is fine for me, didn't face many issues or stutters (none that ever killed me anyways, never had stutters fighting bosses or any enemies). GPU driver is Up2Date so that might actually help with some of the issues other people are facing."Why is it always dog?"

_childDocuments_.review: Elden Ring is a challenging Souls-game RPG game.I will preface this review by mentioning I've actually played the game solely using keyboard & mouse, so yes I will definitely mention that the controls and attacks were very wonky at times. The learning curve of the game is very high, the game has so many mechanics, attacks and items to use that it quickly becomes overwhelming. It is a progressive experience where you first learn the basics, then slowly integrate more strategies as time goes on. Thankfully, all you  lose on death are runes, so you can spend your runes on level ups and equipment without being penalised by dying repetitively to an hard enemy or an hard boss.Elden Ring has a ton of main quests and side quests alike, with a cast of interesting characters and bosses. Everything follows the same theme, but each of them are very unique nonetheless. The monster design of Elden Ring is THE BEST I've ever seen in any games ever, considering I love grim and terrifying-looking creatures. The story is pretty good, but while it is probably an unpopular opinion, I think it could've been better. I felt attached to some of the characters and some parts are very intense, but I did feel detached to the story as a whole for some reason.My favorite thing about Elden Ring is the everlasting feeling of constant progression whenever you unlock a new site of grace (fast travel waypoints) and after beating major encounters you have to work hard for to learn the mechanics of the bosses. My second favorite thing about Elden Ring is the hundreds of different weapons, armors, spells, incantations and different builds you can come up with.The graphics are amongst the best of any games I've ever played, the cutscenes are super well made and the background are even more beautiful. Some of the animations while moving are a bit wonky, but the scenery is a breathtaking experience every single times. The spell effects are also top notch and the variety of backgrounds/dungeons/castles/shacks/etc is simply put crazy.The soundtrack of this game is absolutely amazing, but it's mostly atmospheric or intense. It doesn't really have any memorable songs from what I could tell, but it is a very pleasurable auditory experience.As far as the controls and overall mechanics of the game, I obviously think that a ton of things are overtuned or wonky. The platforming is very bad in some parts of the game and some bosses really feel like they hit outside of their hitbox. It also happened to me a countless amount of time I swing my weapon an inch too far from the boss and then get punished by almost dying due to missing my hit and trying to recover from it. That made most of the gameplay super frustrating and I definitely loss a ton of time to bosses and certain enemies due to that.Also, the requirements for this game are quite high. Yes, the graphics are amazing, but my 2070 struggled with a lot of the game on the highest settings. I had only 1 crash thankfully, but I had hundreds of slowdowns when there are big explosions or a lot of smoke or whatever.As for the expected playtime, it really is honestly almost endless. If you go for different builds, different routes, different choices, collecting everything and going up to NG+7 (or higher), you will have a few hundreds of hours in this game easily.Overall, if you are willing to put a ton of efforts into learning a deep, complex and hard game, it is worth and it is worth the full price. Just keep in mind it is a really hard game and unless you use summons and the best setups, you will need a lot of practice to beat the first few bosses and even more to beat the harder bosses.

_childDocuments_.review: “Wow this game is amazing”, that's what i actually thought to myself several times while roaming the world of Elden Ring. This game is truly a masterpiece and exceeds all expectations. The world of Elden Ring is lush with life and feels like a complete world. _childDocuments_.review: 10/10 GOTY 2022Best RPG and genuinely fun game in a long time. There is no hand holding and that's what makes the game so rewarding. The difficulty of Souls games but a bit forgiving if you decide to roam around and get stronger before taking on main bosses. The addition of a mount and jumping has also taken the Souls games to the next level, making vertical exploration possible (some places can only be reached by jumping with the mount for example). Fast travel is extremely accessible and abundant. Playing with friends is also easier as the item needed is craftable using easily found mats from the open world. The open world puts you in control of the adventure and difficulty. You can rush through the main story or take your time and explore the dungeons and take on mini bosses. Exploration and discovery can be found in every corner and the world has unique zones and mobs. There are mystery elements in that the story is told not only via cutscenes but also through notes that you find and NPCs that you speak with (which aren't always in the same place or time of day).The bosses are all unique and have their own movesets to learn. You can choose to take them on just you or you can bring in spirit summons/NPC summons/co op or even use cheese methods (which are plentiful) to beat the bosses. The music is phenomenal as well and really sets the mood for the fights.

_childDocuments_.review: After years of waiting, Elden Ring does not disappoint representing the culmination of all the things FromSoft has learned over the recent decades, taking and refining previous ideas to perfection. Elden Ring possesses an unparalleled level of exploration, gorgeous terrain, well hidden secrets and incredible boss fights making it one of the most compelling open worlds ever. Aside from some reused content and poor balancing of certain aspects of the PvP and PvE, this game remains a masterpiece of both RPGs and open world games alike.

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATED REVIEW: This could be the best game I've ever played. There's nothing like your first time experience Dark Souls...Until now. Elden Ring is everything I loved about the original Dark Souls, filled with so much more wonder. It's the culmination of a decade's worth of game design, splashed with devious surprises that ask you to discard what you thought you knew about the franchise. By leaving the "Dark Souls" name behind, Elden Ring is free to build new lore and present a wholly unique dark fantasy world. Despite this, the state of the PC port is still unacceptable. I've never had a game run so poorly on my system, with regular frame drops, controller issues, and hitching every time I discover a new area. The game is playable for me, but only barely. It took a lot of work on my end, tinkering with various settings in and out of the game (Nvidea control panel, CPU processes etc.) to see Elden Ring running anywhere close to 60FPS. It's not quite as bad as Bloodborne on PS4 in terms of performance, but it's certainly my closest comparison. Be warned. PREVIOUS REVIEW: This game suffers from terrible stuttering and poor performance. I should be used to sloppy PC ports by now, but genuinely thought From would have nailed this one. I have no doubt the game is fantastic, but the performance is so inconsistent that I do not recommend buying this for PC in it's current state.

_childDocuments_.review: This is as big a mechanical and technological leap over Dark Souls 3 as Demon's Souls was over Shadow Tower: Abyss on the PS2. Absolutely staggering. Prettiest open world I've seen to date. Very, very dense, tons and tons of enemy variety, SO many bosses. I played it 10 hours straight two days in a row, and I just finished a 4-hour session on day 3. I only have 3 out of 42 achievements, even though I've beaten like ten bosses that were all quite different, none felt like repeats/reskins of the others.I haven't beaten Elden Ring yet, but oh my gosh, it's so good. I can't recommend it highly enough, best game I've played since Doom Eternal hit in 2020. I don't like most open-world games, but this is more like Breath of the Wild instead of Ubisoft titles like Assassin's Creed or Far Cry. Might be From Software's best game yet, but I'm reserving judgement until I beat it; I'm quite partial to Demon's Souls PS3. It feels like From is trying to make the best game ever made, they're quite ambitious but it feels like they may've actually delivered.As for performance issues, they're very real but I've gotten used to them, kinda like the framerate drops of Souls games on PS3. Really hoping they issue a patch to improve performance, but expect to potentially run into big framerate drops. I'm rocking a 6800 XT, a 5900X and 32GB of RAM, and the game periodically dips to 22FPS at 1440p max settings, similar 22FPS-dip issue at high but not as often. Game's limited to a maximum of 60FPS and I've heard it doesn't support ultrawide. Runs at like 30-40FPS on the Steam Deck without messing too much with settings, solid 60FPS seems likely with FSR. A friend who uses Linux didn't experience any performance issues at all.Edit: I have the game installed on a speedy PCIE 4.0 NVME drive. They released a small patch on day three, and the framerate dips are significantly less common but they still occur. I'm pretty sure we'll get more patches like this soon, should be smooth as heck in no time.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played Dark Souls 1 and Dark Souls 3 but never completed them. Elden Ring is my first FromSoft game I have gone far in and even defeated Melania. This game is fun but the boss designs are disrespectfully poorly designed. Like utter garbage when you compare it to Sekiro or Souls bosses. In previous games they were difficult yes, but they were fair. I felt accomplished when overcoming hurdles and felt rewarded. In Elden Ring when you defeat something you are just glad it's over. Sad really. Only bosses I felt was amazing was Godfrey, Radahn and Melania. It might sound like I hate this game but I love it, it's healthy to criticize games you love. I realized why it feels more RNG and why the bosses just feel like they have too many cheese. It's because I refused to use the tools that are available. I beat Melania without a summon and with a pure Dex katana build out of pride that "I have to beat her without a summon/no magic". Elden Ring is not Dark Souls, the bosses will cheese you and it will be RNG sometimes. But use what the game gives you, level past 150, use summons, cracked pots, respec, mage, cheese builds, etc.  Be resourceful because sometimes, pure builds just get ♥♥♥♥ on with the bosses in Elden Ring. And thats okay.
