_childDocuments_.review: This is a delightfully weird and surprisingly touching game. While flying from airport to airport (all of them, you know, run by dogs) to follow your fiancee, Krista, you meet many wonderful characters. Nearly all of these characters are stock photography dogs, though you may meet some cats, humans and even a bear, and you can pet them all. They have things to say to you, and these things are funny and absurd. A dog god named Updog goads you again and again into saying "What's Updog?" He finds it hilarious. A ticket agent dog snickers when you need a ticket to Uranus.Sometimes these odd characters need your help, and often they are quite generous, offering you interesting items such as axes, shampoo, dangerous missiles, balls of yarn and many other things. One dog would like your help building a bridge that takes you underneath a waterfall of... blood?  You can also purchase supplies like toilet water, umbrellas, a cup of coffee larger than your body, and squeaky meat toys from the various airport shops. You can buy a skateboard from a dog named Chad Shakespeare. Many of these items can be used for quests or to change the speed at which you run or experience time.You'll run a lot of errands in this game, and you'll look for your departure gate, which is in an alien language and sometimes tricky to find, to go to the next airport. Drunk puppies fly your planes, and you have awkward conversations with your fellow passengers (dogs.) While the gameplay is a little bit repetitive, it is pleasurable and always funny. Each airport is charming with its colorful and simplified graphics and catchy music. At each destination you have a brief but meaningful and sweet conversation with Krista, and this guides the storyline, which is ultimately about coming to terms with a long distance relationship. The quirky tenderness of the interactions is really nice.In about 8 hours, I got all of the achievements and went on nearly all the quests (some of which were a bit tricky!), but did miss a few. So it's a substantial length, and an immersive, funky little game that I highly recommend. Go into it with an open mind and be ready to pet dogs 704 times to get the coveted "Deity of Petting" achievement!

_childDocuments_.review: You can pet all the dogs!Now if that hasn't sold you on it already; It also features a heartwarming story of a long distance relationship between the only two humans (Rodney doesn't count because he is a dog trapped in a human body), unique and funny reoccurring characters written by an award winning writer, an open-world with plenty to discover and some of the only fetch quests in games that I took joy in doing.
_childDocuments_.name: An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs

_childDocuments_.review: Very charming game that's full of plenty of dogs you can (and should!) pet as much as you want while they do and say absurd things and just generally be dogs, but at the same time as all the canine (and the occasional feline) absurdity is going on across all these different planets, there's also a very heartwarming and overarching plot focused on the difficulties of a long-distance relationship and portraying it in a very healthy light, where both characters accept these difficulties for what they are while also completely respecting each other and fighting for the relationship and understanding why it's all worth it while also in no way thinking that anyone should give up on their dreams just for the sake of the relationship either, and it's just very heartwarming and great. Just an all around pleasant experience. Would (and did!) give all of the pets. All of them.
_childDocuments_.name: An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs

_childDocuments_.review: It's only fitting that such an upbeat game is currently run by dogs, and once the tone is set by them everything else follows suit: its happy, absurd, funny writing, its beats, its playful interactions... everything is consistent so when the game chooses to throw its punches, it hurts: this is also a game about a relationship, and there may be some existential terrors lurking in the void too. This game made me laugh and made me sad in a very human way, something that, casually, usually happens with dogs. I really liked it.Oh, there MAY be cats there too, and they MAY be perfectly depicted (those lovely bastards).

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs? If you love the idea of wandering through hand-crafted alien airport terminals staffed and occupied entirely by stock images of various dogs (and maybe even ), then this game was literally made for you. _childDocuments_.review: Not sure how it will pan out by the end but the writing is incredible, hitting notes of humor, sincerity, wholesomeness, philosophy, and existentialism. _childDocuments_.review: An Airport for Aliens Currently Run by Dogs is a first-person open-world comedy adventure game with a very long name. You and your fiancée are the last two human beings left in the universe. Dogs run airports, along with the rest of society. Deal with alien logic, travel issues, and strange stock photo dogs as you attempt to stay in touch with the person you love, when you both live your lives on the go.

name: Harvest Moon: One World
detailed_description: Trek across beaches, the desert, and even a volcano in the latest entry into the long-running Harvest Moon series! The Harvest Goddess has gone missing, and it's up to you to help bring her back! Along the way, you'll come across cows, sheep, camels, and even reindeer! Dig in, because in this game, the world is literally your oyster! Before the Harvest Goddess disappeared from this world, she imbued the tiny Harvest Wisps with the knowledge of various seeds, thus ensuring the various fruits and vegetables of the world would not be lost. Using the power given to these Harvest Wisps, you'll unlock various seeds as you progress through the game! But the Harvest Wisps can be tricky to find, as they all appear at different times and places. You'll need to use your noggin to make sure to seek as many as you can of them out! • Set off on an adventure around the world to revive the Harvest Goddess! • Explore 5 unique and colorful areas: the sprawling grasslands of Calisson, the gorgeous beaches of Halo Halo, the searing desert heat of Pastilla, the cozy hills of Lebkuchen, and the snowy mountains of Salmiakki! • Play as a boy or a girl and woo one of 5 bachelors and 5 bachelorettes, each with their own unique personality and backstory! • Raise and keep animals such as cows, sheep, goats, and even reindeer! • Use your Expando-Farm to easily travel from one area to another!

_childDocuments_.review: If SHREK was a game, this would be it.This is Harvest Moon for Mom’s.Now sure, at first impression it looks like a mobile game without the pay to win features and it kind of makes Farmville look amazing in comparison, yet……Honestly, despite the jokes I don't think One World is that bad. It's not fantastic but it's also not the worst thing ever as some may claim. One World might not be the worst Harvest Moon game out there, but if you go in thinking you're about to play Story of Seasons (which are very very good), you will be disappointed. Go in expecting a dumbed down version of Harvest Moon and brace yourself for some bugs. Once you get into it, I actually quite liked the farming mechanics and the story.I liked the mutation mechanic and the concept of being able to pack the farm up and settle in a different town. Game play is fast and I like the fact I can just press the A button on fields, animals, & rocks and the game just knows what to do. I don't have to keep switching my tools. The characters have a certain charm to them that a lot of story of seasons characters have been lacking for me.. since around... animal parade? I’d go for the DLC, it adds some animals that are interesting enough for the extra cost, along with the marriage candidates.I don’t like the lack of divorce option and the hetero only option. I’m hetero and play hetero but it’s very non-inclusive. The lack of main character customization is a slight issue as well. The story is short-ish, but I've found their games are more about the gameplay than the story. They're especially good for people who enjoy farming and/or engaging in completion related goals I think.This game just needed more love and care put into it. Seemed like they had a good idea, kind of doing their own thing with the different locations and learning new crops, unfortunately it fell short of what they were trying to achieve it seems. I wouldn't recommend buying it for full price though.Now, can someone please make a Harvest Moon game that doesn't look like it was thrown together by one guy over the weekend???6/10

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10 - Damn near perfect game.While a lot of the reviews are quite negative, I can only presume that they rushed the game. Graphics: 8/10Music: 9/10Storyline: 7/10Cute animals: 11/10Variety of animals: 15/10Farming: 9/10New crops: 10/10Characters: 10/10Controls: 10/10 (i play controller so take this with stride)Really my only two biggest issues are the lack of ability to plant more than one seed at a time, and time continuing inside buildings- Even in Light of Hope and previous games, neither above issues existed. I do find this quite odd to have taken away and definitely have made a bit of an impact on your play time. The time still ticking inside makes it even more difficult to navigate and manage your time efficiently, considering it only takes 24 IRL minutes to equal a full day in the game, but you don't wake up until 6am-7am.I do find mining for new ores much more exciting, the MUCH larger array of crops and animals, and the different mutations of crops you can get via new terrains and properly using fertilizer. I've never been a big fan on fishing in real life, or in video games, but there are definitely a lot more fish added as well and even exclusive to certain areas. Your love interests all have their own personality instead of duplicated with a slight altercation. Personally, I think Shogen is the best option for bacholers and Laura for bachorelette (spelling is hard). Plenty of tasks to keep you busy and a plethora of recipes to unlock. The game can be a little grindy, but overall I would say its worth the money 100% and a great game over all. Give it a good chance and a bit of love !

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game, editing for corrections and whatever changed my mind going through. Just steamrolled the story and didn't marry yet.I can't really in good conscience review this in a vacuum, and I'm going to be comparing it strongly with its direct relatives Story of Seasons and Rune Factory, since this is essentially a Publisher offshoot of that series.This is the first time I've played a post publisher-fallout Harvest Moon game, and it's pretty good. The writing is okay, the characters are written kind of 2d (though to be fair, that is an aspect that it shares with Story of Seasons) and the art and character design is competent. Everything works as expected and looks good for what it is. Regardless of the breakoff there seems to have been staff involved that were instrumental in making great games.The central plot revolves around you moving from town to town to solve problems, and you can bring your farm with you. This means you'll be incentivized to move your farm during each story arc to be closer to where the story is, which is generally a little antithetical to how these games usually work. The farm work is just hands off enough to make this fairly straight forward, with almost everything I've seen so far growing within a six day cycle. You can grow things out of season and out of biome, but I don't think you can have it be both out of season and out of biome without fertilizer, growing in season and in biome leads to genetic offshoots of the crop you're growing, which I think is an interesting system. You cannot marry and you aren't encouraged to have a homestead until the tail end of the game, after you've completed the harvest goddess revival. This doesn't take too long if you're gunning for it, and it in some sense becomes a more traditional harvest moon game after that.The story is kind of what you'd expect for a game like this, helping harvest sprites restore the harvest goddess by fixing nature. I do think it gets a little more granular than the general rune factory/story of seasons thing of "nature good, grow good, make good things happen" One of the main story elements is about restoring fertility in a forest so the nutrients carried by the river can reach the fish and restore the fish population. I like that you have real world genetic mutations like San Marzano tomatoes (which are very region specific and require specific soil and environment to grow correctly) I thoroughly enjoyed these aspects and wish that more farming games would talk about real world environmental effects like that (without delving into full on simulator territory.)One advantage I think this has over most of the natsume published story of seasons games is they don't have weird stinted direct translated dialogue, though the Marvelous ones have fixed that up quite a bit. There may or may not be plot elements that rely on you knowing about this series, Doc Jr seems like a specific recurring character but I could be wrong.I don't like the RNG elements, or at least how finding new seeds work, all seeds are semi-random drops based on biome/season and there are way too many kinds. You can intentionally search for a specific seed after finding it once, but based on a series of luck factors you may not find a good seed for a quest until several hours later. I wish they would have went for a normal progression system where completing missions would add seeds to the shop, and seeds for offshoots were added when you first ship that offshoot, but for story reasons that can't happen because for some reason you live in a world where people don't understand what seeds are. I also wish the quests weren't as frequent, though having quests that give the exact materials needed to move the main quest forward is a nice way to give an alternative to people who don't want to spend like 15 days rearing a new sheep for some wool.Overall, I don't think this is going to outshine friends of mineral town, pioneers of olive town, or any rune factory game, but I think it's worth a shot if you like this kind of game and want a new one of these games. The 2023 game seems a lot higher rated but I do enjoy the simplistic, more cartoony art style of this and it runs well.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game worth 50$? No. at minimum i expect the controls to work with pc/controller for this price. Did I eventually get the additional DLCs anyways? Yes. The rumor this game was rushed in order to beat SOS PoOT to market feels accurate. The PC controls suck and I do recommend a controller- the controller makes it playable but it takes getting used to. TBH if you were like me and debating if you should get this or SOS PoOt- go with story of seasons. That all said, this is my favorite genre of game, and even lack luster ones are pretty enjoyable for me. I don't care about romance/npc relationships- so the critique these characters are lacking might be fair. They seem no better or worse than any other game. (Rune factory 4 is the only game i noticed with unique characters with engaging dialogue) I most look forward to the animals in these games. I LOVE the reindeer and camels. Though the travel system makes them not as useful later in the game when they become attainable. I love the chicken varieties and even without the dlcs you can tame so many wild animals! (if you have room in the limited barns). A wide selection of pets too. I think I have as many hours as I do in part because the game itself really constricts your pace. Running around depletes your health (which SUCKS) and limits your ability to complete tasks early game, and even when you get later in the game the way its balanced still takes me awhile to unlock new upgrades and the like. I have a habit of binging a game and running through the main story at least pretty quick- this one makes me keep a slower more relaxed pace- which sometimes im in the mood for. This title series can be pretty hit and miss, as can story of seasons. but the nostalgia has me in a chokehold so i'll probably keep getting suckered into overpaying.

_childDocuments_.review: Take a trip around the world in the latest entry in the long-running Harvest Moon series! You'll ride camels across the deserts of Pastilla, venture deep into the snowy mountains of Salmiakki, and even visit a volcano near the cozy mountain town of Lebkuchen! Can you imagine a world without cabbage, tomatoes, or even carrots? Believe it or not, that's the world you'll find yourself in at the beginning of Harvest Moon: One World, as the Harvest Goddess, the queen of crops herself, has vanished... However, before the Harvest Goddess disappeared from this world, she imbued the tiny Harvest Wisps with the knowledge of various seeds, thus ensuring the various fruits and vegetables of the world would not be lost. Using the power given to these Harvest Wisps, you'll unlock various seeds as you progress through the game! But the Harvest Wisps can be tricky to find, as they all appear at different times and places. You'll need to use your noggin to make sure you seek out as many of them as you can.

detailed_description: Expedition Zero — survival horror set in the anomaly zone of the northern forest. Face the dreadful forest monster and find a way to defeat it. Explore the corrupted forest and abandoned research facilities to uncover the truth about the top-secret expedition. Limited resources can be used to enhance your abilities and chances of survival in extreme conditions. Could you escape the zone or reveal the secrets it keeps? Key Features: Fight or Hide You are not alone in the forest. Face the horrifying monster in a deadly duel. How would you deal with other corrupted creatures? Run away, fight back or become prey. Survive Deadly monsters are not your only enemy. Deal with lack of resources, extreme temperatures and snowstorms. Get Strong Loot and craft useful devices and modules for your mecha-suit. Establish new safe points to have uneasy rest. It is the only help you'll get on the expedition. Explore The Unknown The former research camp is now abandoned and surrounded by a 50m high wall. Uncover the dark truth about the research expedition and top-secret experiment.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit/Update as of July 2022: So any hope I gave the team in the original review was... unfounded lol. They added one new location and fixed a few of the other game breaking bugs but this is still a really disappointing game. I'm never going to hate on someone trying to do something new, because at the least this game did try to set itself apart a bit, but pretty much on all counts this game flops as both a fun experience and a product. It's far too short, costs too much and is just really lacking. I still maintain that this shouldve been an early access project that the devs could have made with feedback because it might have had a shot then, but as it is now, all of the updates to the game have just patched the holes in the ship. It's not sinking, but its still an ugly ship that barely floats. Hard pass.For starters, I want to say that just in the first day alone the devs pushed out 4 patches fixing bugs they got feedback on, which is admirable and deserves to be noted. I consider myself part of the crew that got to play on easy mode because the regular zombies were bugged and would just stand there dancing and looking at you (they patched that one!)I would also like to say that this game has a ridiculous amount of potential. The setting, the visuals, everything in a year from now might turn this game into a must buy after some work gets done to it. That being said, they pushed those patches because this game is  buggy. I have a reputation for accidentally breaking games but there was 3 times in the 4 hours I played where both myself and the people watching me play thought I'd done something that made it so I couldn't progress. There are some big upsides to Expedition Zero, though. The enemies legitimately scared the hell out of me for the first hour or so. Constant footsteps all around you and the way they dart through the trees, I couldn't tell if I was tripping out or being stalked. The game also looks extremely good at times, but that gets hindered by textures freaking out occasionally and some of the animations being very stiff. ( Side note, the aiming in this game is toggle only :( feelsbadman )With all of that in mind, the ONLY reason I am not recommending this game is the length. If there was more to it I would say deal with the bugs and go for it, because I really did have a fun time with it, but even going at a relatively slow pace I beat the game in less than 4 hours. I had to double check I wasn't accidentally playing the demo as the credits rolled :( I wanted more and I think that speaks to some of the passion and promise that definitely shows in this one.Do yourself a favor though, and don't just pass on this game entirely. Wishlist it and keep an eye as the team updates it, there is a ton of potential here. The whole Metro/Stalker/Tarkov meets The Long Dark really does get delivered on and with some polish and time in the oven this could be something really special.

_childDocuments_.review: Clearly inspired by masterpieces such as "Roadside Picnic" and the STALKER series, Expedition Zero (EZ) proposes yet another spin to the by now well-tested "anomalous zone" narrative premise. You'll wear the heavy shoes of an unnamed explorer sent past the Wall and into the Zone - an area where the laws of nature don't apply normally. Tasked with collecting anomalous samples by the enigmatic Trader, you'll have to rely solely on your wits, orienteering and combat skills to succeed.Dark, creepy, generously dotted with spooky locations; the area inside the Wall clearly shows a well thought-out world building, with the horror feeling all the more emphasized by apt tracks, effects and a dynamic weather system. The anomalous events, alongside the stories of those who came before, contribute to giving out a constant sense of dread, hopelessness, mystery. Most exposure is given out through indirect narration and the occasional writing, to shed more light on what transpired, and the fate of the characters involved in such events. Despite numerous typos and weird English wording at times, the writing manages to involve the player regardless.With just a map, an old rifle and a few other essentials, off you go into the unknown to find the precious samples. The forest is the most extended "main" location, with several points of interest to progressively uncover, ranging from abandoned civilian structures to military outposts and anomalous zones. Using a detector, you'll be able to locate the nearest anomaly's signal, and proceed to collect the sample; easier said than done, since you'll have to fight against multiple threats constantly. Cold, poisonous gases, anomaly effects and dangerous monsters will often try to put an end to your journey. Death means reloading the last available save, with no other penalty.In order to stay up-to-par with the increasing dangers, as the Zone sends more threats after you after each anomaly is collected, you'll have to scavenge materials from broken appliances, cabinets, watchtowers, manage your inventory space wisely; afterwards, use the occasional Printer (each with unique blueprints in it) to dismantle loot and craft powerful augmentations for your suit, which give the edge you need. The survival mechanics are well-balanced and not too annoying, however, nature will definitely kill those who rush and aren't thorough in exploring - don't run out of firewood. Ammo isn't rare at all, while battery chargers to power the suit mods and healing are far less common - it's more about wits / getting the hell out of somewhere, less about shooting, generally. Trader will give you a hand after each anomaly piece is collected, by disclosing the coordinates of smaller, secondary locations you can reach with your snowmobile, a vehicle that follows you to any shelter (safe house) you decide to sleep in. These places will usually be much less dangerous than the forest (some zombies here and there, but not much else), and host a significant amount of materials, ammo and other useful things to scavenge - load everything in the vehicle's integrated storage, then back to business.As the adventure goes on, times will become progressively harsher. The Zone will send its lethal monsters, I like to call them Stalkers, to permanently hunt you as long as you're in the forest area. They can be repelled with enough bullets, but never truly defeated - they have several ranged and melee attacks, supernatural speed and great agility. Going indoors will shield you from them, but you'll have to get out sooner or later or die from frostbite. Some anomalies will also act as "boss fights" of sorts, with monsters and anomalous effects combining in a lethal mix you can overcome by destroying critical structures or activating mechanisms different for each anomaly.The thing is, there's just too much of... everything lying around (except healing - now that's plenty rare indeed). For a survival horror hell-bent on delivering a haunting, tense survival experience, there's just too much stuff for its own good. Provided you loot everything in each place - which you CAN do since the weight limit is ludicrously high - you won't ever run out of ammo or materials to make new upgrades, the choice between what to loot and what to leave behind is almost always a non-issue. This doesn't make the game a cakewalk sure, but it also makes it, well, not as challenging as it could (should?) be as far as the survival horror aspects are concerned. Combine that with unlimited, ubiquitous saves and a coarse level of polish, and there you get a game that, while decent enough, doesn't go the extra mile to be really good.

But they appear way too often. Bascially every time you move from one camp to another they will appear. They rather get annoying very soon.- Similar goes to the mini boss type enemy in the shaft. Its a huge jump scare and insane creepy the first time you see it. But its nearly impossible to kill it. It just randomly disappeared for me after like 10 retries to kill it. (maybe its just a bit buggy?)- You have to decide between different upgrades for your head. Which is pretty irrelevant since you pretty much ALWAYS need the gas mask.- Please let us equip both shooting weapons instead of 2 melee weapons that are useless since you cant use them without taking damage. The problem with only one shooting weapon is, that it takes too long to switch weapons from the inventory when you encounter an enemy. For example you have your rifle equipped but a bear encounters you. In the time you switch to your shotgun in your inventory, youre dead by the bear.- I often didnt know what to actually do. The questline always said the same thing. But I often didnt know where to search for mysterious objects or even when to go to which location. When I started the game, I thought all the different locations are connected together. But it turned out there is only one main location, where the game actually takes place. I dont really get why the farmers location was seperated from the main map but I liked it! The merchants location will be accessed for about 5 minutes in total just to talk to the merchant twice. And all the other locations arent even needed to complete the game if I remember correctly. - Please mark important objects. I accidentally recycled the tree items i needed for the sacrifice table in the farmers location.There are also a few things that are still unclear to me:- Why can I barricade some houses if there are no enemies to follow you?- Why do some of the areas like the school exist? There is basically no reason to go there, it doesnt help you progressing in the story or any sort of side quest.- What is the purpose for the sacrifice table in the farmers location? You get all three items needed as soon as you enter the area PLUS the key that you recieve for making the sacrifice! Why do I get it twice? _childDocuments_.review: The atmosphere for the game is solid but there are a grand total of three enemy types in the game and you only encounter one of them once, the second is invulnerable to damage and constantly hounds you in the main area of the game and the third is the same copy/pasted zombie model over and over again.The monsters start out creepy but the fun wears out fast due to how little there actually is to the game. _childDocuments_.review: A game about surviving infected woods full of zombies and anomalies. I love the backdrop for this. Snowy, cold environments are a great setting for these types of games. Between safety, you have to make sure not to freeze to death. Nor fall victim to the stalking horror that randomly appears -- fluttering around. The monster is actually one of the best parts of the game, because it’s still not clear to me how it operates, or even how it looks. Which is a sweet spot in terms of the horror and uncertainty it’s bringing. Especially in combination with how the aggressive weather sort of blocks your senses. _childDocuments_.review: Gonna be honest, I'm disappointed. It's not by any means a horrible game but it's not the same game we saw roughly 6+ months ago. _childDocuments_.review: Expedition Zero is a survival horror set in a mysterious anomaly zone made of creepy forests, military outposts and abandoned research facilities.  You play as an explorer who has been sent to collect artifact samples of the anomaly and understand what happened to the previous expedition team. With only a few items in your pocket, you will scout every corner looking for resources you can use to craft new items and upgrades using 3D printers placed in different locations.The premise of the story is very light and introduced through a short exchange of dialogues. There is a very weird and unpleasing stealth moment at the beginning when someone asks you to meet him, but then he shoots you on sight if spotted. It wouldn’t be that awful if you didn’t die with only two shots, so in my opinion, it’s rather annoying to introduce the story this way. The plot could have been interesting to develop further, but it’s abandoned soon after the prologue and ends up being just another set of repetitive tasks with only some documents left to read, a plot twist that doesn’t make much sense and a disappointing ending that possibly teases a sequel.While this is a survival horror game, you don’t have to eat food or drink water in order to survive. You only need to pay attention to your body temperature and your mecha-suit battery, which will be essential to your survival in the dark cold forest. Fortunately, you can find plenty of wood and use the stoves to keep you warm while also recharging the battery in the nearby stations. There are a few safe shelters where you can rest on your bed, use 3D printers to upgrade your gear or simply take a breather from the most dangerous moments.The game gets more intense as you move far away from these “comfort” zones. To find the anomaly samples you need to use your scanner, which will pinpoint the exact location as long as you walk in the correct direction of the signal. Be ready to fight though, as the creatures of the forest will do anything to protect those samples. Zombies will constantly appear, but their AI is so weak that you can take them out easily with a crowbar. The real threat is the invincible and creepy monster that hunts you through the forest and becomes more aggressive as you progress further with the samples collection. There is no way of defeating him and you will be forced to run towards the nearest safe house while defending yourself using an old rifle (or you can just reload your saved file prior to the monster appearence). Shooting isn’t great though; it’s clunky, inaccurate and doesn’t show any feedback. Paired with the clunky movements and rough animations, it makes these monsters encounters more annoying than scary.Visually the game has some good-looking locations. The forest is the main setting, but you will also explore more interiors, such as those of the abandoned research facilities. While there are not many jumpscare moments, the atmosphere is great and exploring the map feels intriguing enough but, as mentioned earlier, there isn’t much to do other than looting resources and reading documents. Optimization isn’t that great and despite being far above the recommended specs, I noticed multiple frame drops on both cinematic and high settings.It took me around 4 hours to complete the game while exploring almost every corner, including all the optional areas. You can expect to finish it in 2 to 3 hours if you only follow the story tasks, depending on how many times you die, reload your saved file etc.. I always value the quality of the experience more than its length, but in this case neither was really great and the price tag is a bit higher than I would have expected.Overall, Expedition Zero is still a decent survival horror experience. A bit rough around the edges and clearly in need of more polishing (including controller support), but the atmosphere is solid and the exploration, mixed with the looting, crafting and upgrading system, is somewhat satisfying. The amount of content probably doesn’t justify the full price though and you will have a better experience once all the major flaws are patched.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr : I wish there was a 'middle ground' for thumbs up or down, because this game fits right there, it's a 6/10 you should get on 40-50% or so discount. I'll detail why below, but there's your quick review.The basic flow of the game is that you traverse a forest finding artifact samples, while evading a monster that grows increasingly aggressive as you find more artifacts. It feels like one of the Slenderman games where you hunt down pages, but adapted and improved upon significantly. Along the way you have to manage your temperature by lighting fires, your suit battery by recharging at stations, finding materials to break down and 3D printers to make suit upgrades.The movement is clunky, but makes sense, you're in a sealed mech suit and interacting with the world is slow but deliberate. The upgrades you craft change the game to be smoother but not massively game changing, slower heat loss but higher battery drain, an exoskeleton to carry more, a better backpack, etc. The upgrades are fairly essential, but there's no real variety.Combat is limited to a Mosin Nagant, a powerful but slow rifle, and a wood chopping axe. You'll never need the axe as you're absolutely showered in ammunition, and you never fight more than 2 enemies at once. All enemies are the same, basic zombies, aside from the monster that stalks you. They're never a threat, just a bit of flavour to the world.The most interesting part is the forest you traverse in an endless snowstorm. This combined with impeccable sound design helps build tension wonderfully, and the ever present threat of the monster does generate a solid horror experience. However, once you get attacked by the monster and find it does functionally no damage the threat pretty much dissipates.Finding artifacts in the forest unlocks side areas, these just provide more resources and are completely optional and really not at all essential. They do offer some interesting side story, but again not enough is done with that story.There's about 3 hours of gameplay, I played a little more because I was streaming and I took my time, but even at your slowest and dying a few times it'd be 4 at maximum.The game overall feels like the first chapter of a larger story, and I really hope the devs do more with it. But until that's the case or the game is on discount, I can't recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm looking at the game from the perspective of a stalker fan (especially the less shooty versions) and i gotta say it straight away: WOW. I've tried quite some stalkeresque games but this one hits kinda different.You're scavaging while exploring abandoned and destroyed facilities while avoiding the few but terrifying enemies, trying to stay warm and keep your battery charged. There are some upgrades for the suit to craft, 2 weapons to find and a few gimmicks. Nothing special. The game stays very simple, which is - imho - a good thing.- Graphics are okayish, could be better, could be worse. It won't be a problem because the overall tone is dark and you want to preserve flashlight battery.- Sound design was a surprise. Normally if you hear a noise in those kind of games, it is just there to frighten you. But not in this game - if you hear something, there is something there and you should probably avoid drawing it's attention.- Story is weak, there are notes to read but they add nothing. But that's not really a downside, if you know that kind of game, you know exactly what's going on and don't need an explanation anyways.- Voice acting is okish, there is not much of it anyways- Gameplay is as already stated simple with focus on atmosphere and exploring with a tiny speck of shooting/crafting/basebuilding on the side- Time frame is about 5-6 hoursI did only encounter a single bug; some enemies haunted me with an impressive T-pose. Otherwise i didn't encounter any problems with the game. To me, the game also does not feel unfinished. Sure, it could always be better, but it feels thought through and complete. So, despite the negative reviews, i'd highly recommend it to every stalker fan and also fans of horror or exploring games. It's not a hardcore survival game or shooter, so if you're looking for that, this is not for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I like this game. The atmosphere is there, the tension, the constant dread... The flying enemies got my adrenaline flowing. The post-apocalyptic Soviet theme is becoming kind of a tired trope these days, but I'm a sucker for it, and this game has it. Mysterious derelict zone full of abandoned military gear? Check. Cold winter nights in dark woods where inhumane shrieks pierce the night? Check. Soviet-era technology, including a nuclear reactor? Check. A thin layer of Eastern Orthodox mysticism with inverted crosses and tainted holy manuscripts thrown in for good measure? Check.Crafting is OK once you get the hang of it: basically all the stuff you find can be turned into three basic resources: metal, plastic and electronics. With those you build auguments to your suit, increasing various attributes as you explore the forest. Just one weapon, though, but it only adds to the tension since you have to manually reload each bullet. Ammo is scarce so it needs not to be wasted. Stuff which regenerates HP is even rarer, so manually saving every now and then was a must for me. There's not a lot of story: some dude in a bunker wants the main character to find creepy stuff for him, from around "the zone". Once you find it all, you have to purge the area by (spoiler) blowing up a reactor.The price is a but too high for what it offers. I would play a sequel, though. The developers have released some small patches since launch, fixing some stuff and polishing some minor features - but I would like to see more content updates.

_childDocuments_.review: PROsGreat Visual DesignPresentationToneMonster DesignCONSAggressive often unfair Monster AIMany Technical ProblemsClipping Monster Attacks that ConnectGas Clouds Are Near Impossible to See in the Dark (Causes lots of Damage)Having to Hold a Key to pick up every itemExpedition Zero is an intense horror experience but can feel unfair. First off, the presentation is incredible. The developers did a great job in the visual design and lighting to convey that sense of isolation and fear that comes with being hunted by an unknown threat. Hidden collectables add to the atmosphere with mysterious logs from those within the zone attempting to survive.The survival system involves you collecting items to craft new equipment for your suit found in printing stations. Each station creates unique items and resources are not shared between them. You'll also need to keep warm by burning wood but cannot charge the heating until any other way. This goes for healing as well, you can only recover health through specific items like bandages and health pills. Beds only serve as spawn points.Since your suit uses electricity for everything you'll need to keep it charged. Fortunately these provide infinite power but the system is balanced enough that you have to properly manage how much power you're using. Since you can only equip 1 piece of gear to each slot often you'll need to swap items such as a gas mask for toxic clouds and a headlamp for seeing in dark areas. Portable batteries are available as a rare resource for mobile 1-time charging so the game doesn't leave you in the dark entirely, managing your resources is essential. I found it strange that you have to hold down a key to pick up everything, which is annoying since things like bullets should be instant.Now for the bad, the game is unfair with how aggressive the monster's AI operates. This was likely done since the only other enemy are infected who are walking targets. The monster can use its tongue for massive damage and toss toxic clouds that drain your health within seconds. The creature can also teleport, move at incredible speeds, and once you're targeted it'll remain glued to you regardless if you're in a safe zone. Even remaining outside of the zone until you come out.There's very little you can do about this other than load a save before the creature found you. You cannot outrun it due to its speed and the fact your character can only sprint for about 4 seconds before getting winded. There's also plenty of technical problems such as getting stuck in the geometry, your gun not reloading, and items failing to equip. The reason I'm leaving a positive review is that this game has potential but needs tuning and patching. In the state that it's in most will find the experience frustrating and unfair.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has so much potential but sadly it falls short for many reasons. The programming/coding.. horrific.. a game this small with somewhat poor graphics shouldn't choke your computer into submission and force you to lower graphics settings. I run MSFS 2020 which in itself is a very demanding game on most computers. I run my settings on ultra and never once has my system wanted to choke. Not the case for EZ. At this point I regret buying it due to not only the constant bugs and chunky coding but mainly the length of the game. Most indie games are short, I get that but most of them, the price vs playtime makes sense. Even with the short story mode, they could've at least added a multiplayer aspect to the game. _childDocuments_.review: ❤️I appreciate Enigmatic Machines pushing out patches very quickly, taking the time to listen and respond to their players' reviews and just generally being rad. Overall, I  enjoyed the game - but I do feel like there's a lot lacking. There is a lot of appeal to this game, the atmosphere it creates and the environment is fantastic. I also thought the plot was neat too! However, I felt like there could've been more done in ways of environmental storytelling aside from placing readable documents around the map.The enemies in the game were also quite lacking, the zombies felt a bit easy and more of an inconvenience at times. It would've also been nice to see some variations to them, rather than the same model repetitively used. The main ‘enemy’ was really cool, despite being a bit silly and not all too threatening at times. Never knowing when it would show up, or where it would be attacking you from was a fun element. I also really appreciated the design of it too. However, knowing that I could just hide under any form of shelter to escape it made it feel overall less scary as the game progressed.There is only one major gameplay mechanic I absolutely despised - it was being unable to use the flashlight while wearing the gasmask. I’m not sure if I was just playing wrong, but being unable to see whatsoever and fumbling around in the woods just felt a bit more frustrating rather than terrifying. Also, obtaining the night vision goggles at the very end also felt a bit , and I felt like the flashlight still did more while exploring the underwater area.Even with all this said and out in the open, I did enjoy the game.  The visuals were nice, I loved the environments and the overall feel of the game. The story (although quite empty) was really unique and nice, and the ending scene / cliffhanger was seriously cool!The developers have a lot of potential with this game, and with any future releases. I just personally believe they have to do better with their environmental storytelling, maintaining suspense and fear and offering a bit more variety in terms of enemies, gameplay and such. I do still recommend picking up the game if you're looking for an easier horror-survival type of experience.

_childDocuments_.review: TL:DR - This game is not really what it appeared to be and I would highly recommend you avoid this title until it's had some issues fixed or addressed.  I don't think it's for me, and even if they fix some of the issues I don't see myself playing this one for more than an hour or so, so I'm refunding it.List of issues in just the first 15 minutes or so:Music slider off before I even start playing and I hear music for almost 2 minutes.  Changing the slider doesn't affect the volume of that music.  Off means off, developers.Holding the E key for actions - I hate this in most games and when the action is 0.1 or 0.3 seconds it's pointless to make me hold the key.  There's no way to toggle this off, either.Many graphical settings are lumped into post processing effects (or some such heading) so you can't pick and choose what you want to turn down, or off.  You can only set it to low.  I'd turn most things off if I had the option.  At least they have motion blur separated from the rest and do let you shut that garbage off.  Maybe a +1 for that but it was only added after people complained it wasn't an option.  These days having separate options should be the industry standard, and they can't possibly be that hard to add.  Some things, like bloom, have to be added by developers on purpose, so it should not be hard to let players shut that stuff off.Excessive head bob.  No way to toggle it off or turn it down.  Too much inertia, meaning uncontrolled camera movement, when moving around.  I don't mind a character slowing down or speeding up gradually but the camera shouldn't be moving around uncontrollably when that's happening. The janky camera movement doesn't make it seem more realistic, it only adds to the head bob issue.Unable to jump on or climb up on low items.  Like knee height low.  You just kinda bounce off if you aren't "allowed" up on something.Speaking of which - invisible walls.  You seem to be unable to leave immediate area unless using the sled to travel to a specific set of coordinates.  You can't open the gate, or climb the fence, and go exploring in your immediate surroundings.Upon arrival at the first set of coordinates you're given, and being warned that the "lights sting" or something like that, you will find yourself shot to death in about 0.5 seconds should the light touch you at all.  After that happened unable to see my attackers nor hide from them behind cover, I stopped playing because I had already seen enough to know that I was going to be disappointed with the rest.Developers - you have roughly 20 to 60 minutes to make a VERY GOOD impression on players so you'd better make the first half hour of your game as good as you possibly can.  I shouldn't be annoyed within 30 seconds and quitting after 15 minutes because the gameplay, GUI and controls, and overall experience are so aggravating that I can't bring myself to keep playing.

_childDocuments_.review: I give this thumbs up with RESERVATION. Expedition Zero has a lot going for it. The atmosphere is spectacular, especially how the weather makes things more oppressive and uncertain. I also appreciate the attempt at deeper gameplay, as you need to pay attention to health and stamina (as usual), in addition to your body temperature and battery power. These latter two details add an interesting twist to the usual and create more tension. You can upgrade your gear to make life easier and this involves gathering various resources by scraping through trash cans and investigating abandoned houses and such. The mystery revolves around the expected biofreak cult somethingrather and takes place in northern Russia. The setting is well-designed based on that model, but the story quite typical. Regardless, as others have mentioned, the big ugh in this game is the bugs. There are still a number of them. Most are easy to ignore, such as disappearing corpses after a kill or the occasional, and hilarious, floating zombies that look like Christ crucified as they hover along the terrain. But some are rather breaking such as a case where I fast traveled to the forest only to find myself stuck in the floor of the church? How even? There are ways around these occasional problems, and generally it's enjoyable, but consider buying it with reservation or wait for more fixes or perhaps a lower price.
